# Changelog {#changelog}

## v7.1.0a — 2026-06-15 (v7.2.0-REM Program — M02.3 Runtime-Wiring Pass)

Implementation pack **M02.3** (per `Build_Execution_Strategy.md` §11) lands the runtime wiring for the spec-tree-lint subset of its assigned §M.5 gates. This is a non-destructive, additive pass on top of the v7.1.0a P0 hot-patch stamp: no engine semantics change, no acceptance criterion is invalidated, and the only Master Spec body mutations are six §M.5.4 `Runtime status` cell promotions plus the §M.5.6 / Appendix J `ci_gate_runtime_status` enumeration reconciliation. Pre-edit backup at `_versions/Sourcera_Master_Spec.v7.1.0a-pre-v72REM-M02.3-runtime-2026-06-15.md` (6,508,666 bytes; md5 `893c6b7f0c1cabd0a43e975ad3bf4aae`).

### 1. Runtime artifacts landed (`tools/spec-lint/`)

- **Reusable harness** (`tools/spec-lint/lib/`): `types.ts` (enum spine — `ci_gate_runtime_status` / `ci_gate_row_class` / `ci_gate_execution_context` mirrors), `spec_loader.ts` (heading/anchor/markdown-table parser), `overrides.ts` (§M.4.4.1 / §M.4.4.5 grammar), `emit.ts` (§M.4.5 four-destination audit emitter + §M.4.5.3 idempotency), `gate.ts` (runner + CLI + fixture mode + `makeSingletonGate` factory).
- **Eight detectors** (`tools/spec-lint/gates/<gate_id>.ts`), one per spec-tree-lint archetype, each with pass/fail CI fixtures (`tools/spec-lint/fixtures/<gate_id>/`).
- **Workflow wiring**: `.github/workflows/spec-lint.yml` step "Run M02.3 spec-tree-lint batch (runtime_active gates)"; closes the previously-dangling `audit_emit.ts` + `package.json` references; `package-lock.json` captured for `npm ci`.
- **Observability-as-code**: `tools/spec-lint/observability/` (`datadog_monitors.tf` per §M.4.5 ¶4 / §M.4.6.3; `pagerduty_rotation.tf` per §M.4.6.2 `spec-ops-oncall-rotation`). Declarative source-of-truth; applied by the Ops Terraform pipeline (no live-account mutation in this pass).

### 2. §M.5.4 rows promoted `spec_binding_pending_pack_m02_3` → `runtime_active` (8)

`appendix_anchor_slug_no_colon`, `principle_9_anchor_canonicality`, `appendix_i_internal_event_no_http_status`, `defense_view_appendix_i_pairing`, `appendix_m5_runtime_status_coverage`, `appendix_m5_header_count_parity`, `eval_starter_appendix_i_pairing`, `appendix_m5_cross_reference_resolution_completeness`. Each was verified to PASS on this Master Spec **and** to pass/fail its CI fixtures before promotion, per the §M.5.6 transition rule (a `runtime_active` gate must be green on the latest commit). The §M.5.4 runtime-composition therefore moves **3 → 11 `runtime_active`**, **118 → 110 `spec_binding_pending_pack_<id>`** (of 122 §M.5.4 rows); the 181-Gate-ID aggregate moves **3 → 11 / 177 → 169 / 1**. No catalog rows are added or removed (the `122` / `181` row-count claims are unchanged; `appendix_m5_header_count_parity` re-verified). The aggregate-count re-baseline narrative is maintained as a running delta and the full §M.5.6 re-baseline is deferred to the v7.1.1 §M.5 hygiene pass, consistent with the §M.5.18 precedent.

### 3. Gates authored but held `spec_binding_pending_pack_m02_3` (3 — honest non-promotion)

`solo_tier_numeric_single_source` (45 findings), `retention_singleton_section_40_2_canonical` (180 → **124** after this pass's detector citation-breadth fix cleared the §6.8 DSAR-deadline false positives; the residual 124 are genuine §4-entity retention literals lacking a §40.2 cite), and `section_anchor_slug_no_colon` (new Authored-Extension follow-on gate; 13 findings = the §2.2 / §10.x colon section anchors) are authored + fixture-verified but surface pre-existing findings on the live spec. A `runtime_active` stamp would be false while the spec is non-green, so all three run **advisory / non-blocking** and remain pending. Filed as D-V72REM-M023-003 (solo restatement triage), D-V72REM-M023-004 (retention; detector fixed + residual triage), D-V72REM-M023-002 (section-anchor normalization) and routed to the v7.1.1 numerical-singleton / anchor-hygiene passes. The `section_anchor_slug_no_colon` §M.5 catalog row is registered at promotion time (after the 13 anchors + their inbound links are normalized).

### 4. Scope boundary (product-codebase gates NOT touched)

The ~14 M02.3-tagged gates whose scan target is the product codebase (Convex serializers, GraphQL/REST handlers, RBAC enum declarations, MFA code paths, the DSAR cascade-walker, the EvalStarter registry) are **not** addressable in this spec repository and remain `spec_binding_pending_pack_m02_3`; they land in the product-repo M02.3 implementation pack. Full classification + build-out plan at `_integration/M02_3_RUNTIME_WIRING_PLAN.md`. Authored extensions registered as AE-V72REM-M023-01 (harness) / -02 (observability-as-code) in `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md → v7.2.0-REM Program`.

## v7.1.0 — 2026-04-28

This release closes the **Surface-Abstraction & Dual-Maya** program defined and executed in Cowork session 2026-04-26 → 2026-04-28 (Phase 14.0 → Phase 14.20). It is a programmatic, additive release on top of the v7.0.0 baseline: no entity is removed, no v7.0.0 acceptance criterion is invalidated. The program adds the codified surface/engine separation principle (Principle 9), the canonical Surface/Engine mapping registry (Appendix M and §M.4 / §M.5 CI gate catalogs), the two new top-of-funnel personas (Buyer Maya / Seller Maya) with a symmetric Solo plan tier across both consoles, the Defense View executive-defensibility surface, the per-vertical Evaluation Starter intake on the buyer side, the Hero-Moment surface polish on the seller side, and the AI-consumption-invisibility treatment that hides per-op metering from Solo and Free users while preserving outcome-based accounting beneath the surface.

The reconciliation log (`/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` → Phase 14.0 through Phase 14.20) is the authoritative line-by-line audit trail. This changelog summarizes the headline diffs only.

- Program window: 2026-04-26 → 2026-04-28.

## v7.0.0 — 2026-04-26

This release closes the 13-phase integration program defined in `Integration_Prompts.md` (2026-04-14 → 2026-04-26). It absorbs the entire `Sourcera_Master_Summary.md` (v1.1, 2026-04-17) and `KB_Engineering_Spec.md` into the Master Spec, retires the v6.0.0 token-denominated billing model in favor of an outcome-based AI consumption model, and adds the two large surfaces that v6.0.0 lacked: the Seller Knowledge Base / Managed Agent platform (§22) and the Sourcera Ops Console (§50). Both source documents are now superseded and have been moved to `/_versions/` (`Sourcera_Master_Summary.md` 2026-04-26, `KB_Engineering_Spec.md` 2026-04-26).

The reconciliation log (`/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md`, ~9,100 lines) is the authoritative line-by-line audit trail of every change; this changelog summarizes the headline diffs only.

### Major New Sections

- **§4.7 Cross-Console Bridge Entities** — buyer↔seller materialization records, cursors, and reconciliation primitives (Phase 3).
- **§4.8 Billing & AI Accounting Entities** — `AIOperation`, `AIWallet`, `AIWalletLedgerEntry`, `CommittedSpendContract`, `RateCardSnapshot`, `OutcomeAttestation`, `MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord`, `SellerOutcomeSignalConfig` (Phase 4 + Phase 4e).
- **§22.8–§22.18 Seller KB Platform** — KB MCP Server, Retrieval Engineering, Managed Agent Definitions, Custom Tool Contracts, Skills, Environments, Session Lifecycle, Event Stream Handling, Observability & Evaluation, KB Value Capture & Stake-Building (Phase 8 + Phase 11).
- **§25.5 Materialization Protocol**, **§25.6 Console Bridge Observability**, **§25.7 Internal Comments** — cross-console hardening (Phases 6, 9, 10).
- **§26.7–§26.10 Seller Public Surface** — Seller Org Pages, SellerSoftware & Software Pages, SEO Requirements, Extended Acceptance Criteria (Phase 5).
- **§27.8–§27.11 Marketplace Hardening** — Marketplace Abuse & Takedown, Seller Signals (anonymized buyer intent), Vendor Opt-Out Global Registry, Marketplace Discovery Pricing (non-AI monetization layer) (Phases 6, 7).
- **§29.7–§29.11 Notification Surface** — Failure Audit, Preference Inheritance, Support Widget, Frequency Override Rules, Full-Screen Incident Surface (Phase 6).
- **§31.6.1, §31.8, §31.9** — Payload Body-Exclusion Gates, Billing-Domain Webhook Catalog (13 events), CRM Sync (Salesforce, HubSpot, Dynamics, Pipedrive) (Phase 4b/c/d + Phase 6).
- **§32.8, §32.9** — Billing Endpoint Detail, Seller KB Export Endpoint.
- **§38.6–§38.12 Responsive & Platform** — Breakpoints, Gesture Equivalents, Mobile Feature Parity Matrix, Print Stylesheet, Reduced-Motion, RTL/Locale Mirror, Presence Avatar Stack (Phase 8 / UX track).
- **§48 PLG, Growth Mechanics & Network Effects** — entirely new; M1–M17 mechanics catalog plus the Seller Hero Moment (§48.8) (Phases 5, 11).
- **§49 Seller Onboarding — Seven-Stage Implementation Flow** — entirely new (Phase 11).
- **§50 Sourcera Ops Console** — entirely new; admin tooling, Signal Integrity Monitor, Fraud Analyst Surface (§50.1–§50.19) (Phase 11).
- **§51 Product Usage Analytics & PLG Instrumentation** — entirely new; PostHog event taxonomy, dashboard contracts (§51.1–§51.8) (Phase 11).
- **Appendix K — Glossary** (created Phase 1, canonicalized Phase 12.3; CI gate `appendix_k_glossary_canonicality` asserts Appendix K — not Appendix B — is the canonical Glossary).
- **Appendix L — Entity State Machines** (created Phase 1-Closeout 2026-04-17; consolidates state machines for InternalCommentThread, BuyerReferral, Pro Trial Seat Grant, KB Entry, KB Document, Target Account, AIOperation).

### Replaced Sections

- **§34 Plan Tiers, Billing & Entitlements** — full end-to-end rewrite (Pricing Rewrite Track, 2026-04-15). All 14 §34.X anchors preserved; ~320 lines → ~1,260 lines. Adds §34.10 AI Wallet Service, §34.11 Outcome Resolver, §34.12 Cross-Side Billing Rules, §34.13 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat (M17), §34.14 Seller Rate Card (Authoritative), §34.15 Seller Outcome Signals (Authoritative), §34.16 Marketplace Discovery Pricing (Non-AI Layer), §34.17–§34.20.
- **§22 Seller Console — Knowledge Base** — structural rewrite (Phase 22-Rewrite); KB Engineering Spec §0–§3 absorbed; §22.1–§22.7 → §22.1–§22.18; acceptance criteria expanded from 6 → 20.
- **§21.4 Agent Capability Catalog → Capability Registry** (Phase 5a 2026-04-15 rewrite).
- **§21.5 Agent Cost Budgets → Agent AI Budgets (Value-Dollars and Wallet Behavior)** — denomination shifted from tokens to value-dollars in lockstep with §34 rewrite.

### Major Extensions

- **§3 UX Standard** — §3.6–§3.12 added: Form & Input Tokens, Loading/Empty/Error State Catalog, Side Peek Dimensions & Behavior, Cursor Presence Visualization, Bulk Action Toolbar, Dark Mode Parity Rules, Presence & Unread Tracking. New pattern §3.7.12 External-Target Clipboard Confirmation Pattern (Phase 10).
- **§21 The Sourcera Agent** — Capability Registry rewrite plus AI Budgets denominated in value-dollars.
- **§22 Seller KB** — see "Replaced Sections" above; KB MCP, retrieval engineering, agents, skills, environments, sessions, observability all integrated.
- **§25 Cross-Console Mechanics** — §25.3 Disqualification formalized; §25.5 Materialization Protocol added (22 ACs); §25.6 Console Bridge Observability added (23 ACs); §25.7 Internal Comments added.
- **§26 Seller Profiles** — Seller Org Pages, Software Pages, SEO Requirements, Extended ACs (25 ACs in §26.10).
- **§27 Vendor Discovery & Marketplace** — Abuse & Takedown, Seller Signals, Opt-Out Registry, Discovery Pricing.
- **§38 Responsive Design** — see "Major New Sections" above (§38.6–§38.12).

### Breaking Changes

1. **Token-denominated billing model retired.** v6.0.0 Free / Business $499/mo / Enterprise tiers with token budgets and `$0.01 / 1K token` overage are superseded by AIOperation value/cost prices, AIWallet value-dollars, and `CommittedSpendContract`. Old enum values (`free`, `business`, `enterprise`) deprecated with successor mapping; migration path documented in §34.
2. **Three-tier plan model → five-tier per console.** v6.0.0 (Free / Business / Enterprise) → v7.0.0 (Free / Starter / Growth / Scale / Enterprise) per console (Buyer + Seller).
3. **`Organization.plan_tier` single-enum split into `buyer_plan_tier` + `seller_plan_tier`.** Migration backfills existing Orgs to `buyer_plan_tier=<old>`, `seller_plan_tier=seller_free`.
4. **Token-denominated AI budgets → value-dollar budgets.** v6.0.0 50K / 500K / 5M tokens → v7.0.0 $5 / $50 / $300 / $800 (buyer) and $5 / $30 / $200 / $600 (seller); Enterprise governed by committed spend.
5. **Per-token overage ($0.01 / 1K) → per-capability outcome rate card.** `value_price = MAX(min, cost_base × 10)`, `cost_price = MAX(min, cost_base × 1.05)`.
6. **Seat-cap plan-gate becomes informational-only.** v6.0.0 hard-gated `max_members` (Free 10 / Business 100 / Enterprise unlimited); v7.0.0 explicitly rejects per-seat charging — seat counts are observability metadata, not entitlement.
7. **Error code rename.** `agent_budget_exceeded` → `wallet_hard_capped` (HTTP 402). Old code preserved as alias through v7.x then deprecated.
8. **`sourcera_owned_cost_center` enum extended 1 → 3 values** (`customer_billed`, `sourcera_owned`, `platform_marketing`); backwards-compatible.
9. **New `billing_admin` Org-level role** added (§5.2; Appendix J role enum updated; assignment migration required).
10. **Vendor Pro Trial Seat (M17)** — new cross-Org billing primitive on Buyer Scale + Enterprise (additive; new audit events, Stripe meters, entitlement rows).
11. **§42.1 Enterprise SLA tightened from "1-hour" to "4-hour critical response"** (Phase 12.4 — narrower than v6.0.0 prose; Sales / Legal must reconcile pre-v7.0.0 contracts before v7.0.0 SLA-citing collateral ships).

### Source Document Retirement

- `Sourcera_Master_Summary.md` (v1.1, 2026-04-17) is fully absorbed into the Master Spec and is moved to `/_versions/Sourcera_Master_Summary_v1.1_retired_2026-04-26.md`. It is no longer authoritative for any topic.
- `KB_Engineering_Spec.md` is fully integrated into §22 and is moved to `/_versions/KB_Engineering_Spec_retired_2026-04-26.md`. It is no longer authoritative for any topic.

The CLAUDE.md source-of-truth hierarchy is updated accordingly: after v7.0.0, the Master Spec is the sole authoritative engineering document. Pricing strategy documents (`Sourcera_Buyer_Pricing_Strategy.md`, `Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy.md`) remain authoritative for buyer/seller pricing strategy commentary not in the Spec.

### Counts (Cumulative v6.0.0 → v7.0.0)

- ~46 new first-class entities (Phase 1: 9; Phase 2: 12; Phase 2b: 4; Phase 3: 7; Phase 4: 11; Phase 4e: 2; Phase 22-Rewrite: 5 KB entities).
- ~165 new enum blocks in Appendix J.
- ~25+ new webhook events (billing-domain 13; KB-domain 5; KB-Session 3; marketplace-monetization 5; plus §27/§29/§31/§50 additions).
- ~28 new error codes in Appendix I (marketplace-monetization, billing, KB).
- 146 new acceptance criteria authored in Phase 13.2 alone; many more inline (§34: 46; §26.10: 25; §25.5: 22; §25.6: 23; §22.17: 20).
- 52+ Authored Extensions tracked in `/_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md` awaiting human sign-off.

### Phase 13 Closure Status

**Phase 13 Final Acceptance Gate: ACCEPTED (2026-04-26 post-Phase-12.5).** All seven acceptance-gate criteria PASS. The original "Conditional Pass" disposition was lifted by the Phase 12.5 residual closure (Citation Closure Register + R-01 / R-03 / R-04 / R-05 / R-06 promotion to authoritative tables). See `_integration/PHASE13_FINAL.md → Phase 13 Final Acceptance — Closure Addendum (2026-04-26)` and `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Phase 12.5 — Cross-Reference + Numerical-Consistency Residual Closure (2026-04-26)` for the audit trail.

- **13.1 — Endpoint Authoring** (~11 customer-facing entity REST endpoint families flagged).
- **13.2 — Test-Catalog Aggregation** (146 ACs landed; aggregation index pending).
- **13.3 — Appendix H Rewrite** (Stripe Billing Model rewrite; STALE banner present in v7.0.0).

## Introduction {#introduction}

Sourcera is an enterprise software procurement operating system designed to eliminate evaluation friction, accelerate vendor selection, and provide defensible decision documentation. It serves three distinct user cohorts through a dual-console architecture: Buyers (procurement teams, evaluators, decision-makers) and Sellers (vendor representatives, account teams), with a unifying Marketplace domain. This specification defines behavior, data models, UI patterns, access controls, and integration boundaries for the complete platform. It is authoritative and supersedes all prior documentation.

## Citation Convention {#citation-convention}

To avoid ambiguity between intra-spec and inter-document cross-references, the following notation is normative across the Master Spec:

| Notation | Resolves To | Example |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `§N.M` (bare) | A section in **this Master Spec** (table-of-contents resolvable) | `§5.11` = Master Spec §5.11 Feature Access Matrix |
| `Summary §N.M` | `Sourcera_Master_Summary.md` §N.M | `Summary §6.13.4` = Master Summary §6.13.4 KB Health |
| `MS §N.M` | Equivalent shorthand for Master Summary §N.M (used in §34.14–§34.18 pricing chapters) | `MS §2.11` = Summary §2.11 |
| `BPS §N.M` | `Sourcera_Buyer_Pricing_Strategy.md` §N.M | `BPS §6` = Buyer Pricing §6 |
| `SPS §N.M` | `Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy.md` §N.M | `SPS §10` = Seller Pricing §10 |
| `KB Engineering Spec §N` | `KB_Engineering_Spec.md` §N | `KB Engineering Spec §6` |
| `Appendix X` | An appendix in **this Master Spec** (A through L) | `Appendix C` = Notification Event Catalog (this spec) |
| `Appendix C of <doc>.md` | An appendix in another corpus document | `Appendix B of Sourcera_Buyer_Pricing_Strategy.md` |
| `C.NN` (bare) | A `Sourcera_Master_Summary.md` C-numbered concept (e.g., `C.100` = SIM concept) | `C.131` = Summary's C.131 Marketplace Discovery concept |
| `U.S.C. §NNN` | United States Code citation | `17 U.S.C. §512` = DMCA |

**Authoring rule.** When a `§N.M` reference is added, the author MUST verify the target resolves intra-spec; if it does not, the citation MUST carry the appropriate prefix per the table above. CI gate `citation_intra_spec_resolution` (Phase 12.3 authored; deploy-time validator) walks every `§N.M` reference and asserts it resolves to a Master Spec heading anchor or carries a recognized inter-document prefix.

**Phase 12.3 closure note.** This convention was authored to close Phase 12.3 (Cross-Reference Integrity). Pre-existing bare `§6.x.x` and `§2.x` references that intended Master Summary targets were prefixed with `Summary §` in a Phase 12.3 perl-driven sweep across the entire Spec; remaining unresolved bare refs are itemized in `_integration/PHASE12_3_VERIFY.md` and were closed in Phase 12.5 via the *Citation Closure Register* below.

# 1\. Product Overview {#1.-product-overview}

## 1.1 Sourcera Architecture {#1.1-sourcera-architecture}

Sourcera operates as a three-domain system:

| Domain | Purpose | Primary Users | Console |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Buyer** | Procurement, evaluation, selection workflows | Procurement teams, evaluators, decision-makers, stakeholders | Buyer Console |
| **Seller** | Bid response, proposal management, relationship tracking | Vendors, account teams, solution architects | Seller Console |
| **Marketplace** | Public vendor discovery, publisher-managed catalog, Seller onboarding | All users (context-dependent access) | Marketplace (public \+ managed) |

Each console is independently deployable and maintains distinct data isolation at the workspace/bid-workspace level. Consoles share a common authentication layer (WorkOS) and a unified database (Convex). Organization-scoped entities are visible across consoles within the same org; console-scoped entities are isolated to their respective console and workspace.

**Surface-abstraction binding constraint (Principle 9).** Every architectural primitive enumerated below — the dual-console firewall, the 13-phase buyer evaluation pipeline, KB governance, AIOperation metering, Capability Declarations, Match Scoring, outcome resolution, plan-tier gating, the audit trail, marketplace inventory, and every entity in §4 — is an *engine* construct. The *surface* a user sees on either console is governed by §3.13 Principle 9 (Surface Simplicity, Engine Complexity), which is the binding constraint on all subsequent UI authoring decisions in this spec and in `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md`. The canonical contract that maps every engine concept to its allowed surface representation is Appendix M (Surface/Engine Mapping); Appendix M is the single source of truth for what the user is permitted to see, name, configure, or think about. The operational quality gate that verifies a surface obeys Principle 9 is the First-30-Seconds Test (`UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §X). Appendix M and the First-30-Seconds Test are authored in Phases 14.2 and 14.17 of the v7.1.0 integration program (`Integration_Prompts_v7.1.md`); until those phases land, Principle 9 is in force as an authoring constraint and any new surface introduced must be registerable in Appendix M when it lands.

## 1.2 Core Value Proposition {#1.2-core-value-proposition}

Sourcera solves three endemic procurement problems:

1. **Evaluation Fragmentation:** Buyers use email, spreadsheets, and ad-hoc scoring. Requirements are lost, vendor responses are scattered. Sourcera consolidates requirements, responses, and decisions into a single system of record.  
     
2. **Slow Vendor Alignment:** Sellers wait for clarity, Buyers chase vendors for information. Sourcera provides vendors structured questions, real-time response tracking, and collaborative refinement without email loops.  
     
3. **Defensibility Gaps:** Procurement cannot audit why a vendor was selected or rejected. Sourcera logs every requirement, score, comment, and decision with timestamps, user attribution, and change history.

## 1.3 Dual-Console Data Isolation Model {#1.3-dual-console-data-isolation-model}

The platform enforces strict logical isolation between Buyer and Seller operations while permitting selective collaboration through opt-in sharing mechanisms (RFI responses, Bid Workspaces, Marketplace Listings).

### 1.3.1 Org-Scoped Entities

These entities exist at the Organization level and are accessible across consoles (subject to RBAC):

- Organization  
- Organization User (Org Membership)  
- Team  
- Audit Event  
- Billing & Plan Data  
- Integrations (at org level)

### 1.3.2 Console-Scoped Entities

These entities exist within a console context (Buyer or Seller) and are NOT shared across consoles:

- **Buyer Console:** Workspace, Use Case, Requirement, Evaluation Phase, Response (vendor responses to RFI/RFP), Score, Scoring Profile, Evaluation Scenario, Intelligence Cache Entry, Evaluation Pulse Event  
- **Seller Console:** Bid Workspace, Bid Response, Capability Declaration, Seller Profile, Bid Task, Bid Schedule  
- **Marketplace (neutral domain):** Marketplace Listing, EOI (Expression of Interest), NDA Record, Marketplace Review, Marketplace Integration Hook

## 1.4 Query Scoping Requirements {#1.4-query-scoping-requirements}

**For org-scoped queries:**

- Use `org_id` parameter only  
- No `console` parameter required  
- Examples: List Organization Members, Get Team Details, Audit Event Query

**For console-scoped queries:**

- Use both `org_id` AND `console` parameter (Buyer|Seller)  
- If querying Marketplace, use `console: marketplace` or omit for public queries  
- Examples: List Workspaces (requires `org_id` \+ `console: buyer`), List Bid Workspaces (requires `org_id` \+ `console: seller`)

Data model definitions in Section 4 will explicitly label each entity as org-scoped or console-scoped.

## 1.5 Deployment & Technology Stack {#1.5-deployment-&-technology-stack}

Sourcera is deployed as a cloud-native SaaS platform with the following authoritative technology stack:

| Layer                        | Technology                                                                                 | Purpose                                                             |
| :--------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Frontend**                 | Next.js 16 (App Router), TypeScript, ShadCN/UI \+ BaseUI, Tailwind CSS                     | Multi-console UI, responsive design, real-time collaboration        |
| **Backend & Database**       | Convex                                                                                     | Serverless functions, real-time subscriptions, ACID transactions    |
| **Collaboration**            | Convex OT, Convex Presence, Convex Subscriptions                                           | Real-time document editing, live cursors, live notifications        |
| **Comments & Notifications** | Convex Comments, Unread Tracking                                                           | Threaded annotations, unread state management                       |
| **Authentication**           | WorkOS                                                                                     | Enterprise SSO, SAML/OIDC, org-level identity                       |
| **AI & LLM**                 | Claude (Anthropic) — Opus, Sonnet, Haiku                                                   | Scoring assistance, intelligent summaries, policy analysis          |
| **AI Search & RAG**          | Convex RAG, Perplexity Search API (Enterprise)                                             | Knowledge base retrieval, vendor intelligence gathering             |
| **Payments & Billing**       | Stripe                                                                                     | Subscription management, invoice handling, usage tracking           |
| **Email Delivery**           | Loops.so                                                                                   | Transactional & marketing email, template management                |
| **Analytics & Insights**     | PostHog                                                                                    | Feature adoption, user behavior, performance metrics                |
| **Web Intelligence**         | Firecrawl                                                                                  | Automated vendor website content extraction                         |
| **Hosting & CDN**            | Vercel                                                                                     | Global edge deployment, serverless functions                        |
| **Observability**            | Pino (logging), Datadog (metrics \+ APM), Sentry (error tracking), OpenTelemetry (tracing) | Platform health, incident response, debugging                       |
| **Status & Transparency**    | Statuspage.io                                                                              | Public incident communication                                       |

## 1.6 Deployment Regions {#1.6-deployment-regions}

Sourcera supports data residency constraints for enterprise customers. The `data_residency_region` field on Organization is authoritative for all entity placement.

| Region | Value | Coverage | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **US** | `us` | North America, default region | AWS us-east-1 |
| **EU** | `eu` | European Union, GDPR-certified | EU West (Ireland) |

Default: `us`. Org Owners can change region during initial setup or via Enterprise support request. Region change after workspace creation requires data migration and is not available during production evaluations.

# 2\. The Sourcera Method {#2.-the-sourcera-method}

## 2.1 Overview {#2.1-overview}

The Sourcera Method is an opinionated, repeatable procurement evaluation methodology embedded into the platform's workflows, terminology, and user guidance. Its phase-duration benchmark is owned by §10.15; this overview does not restate total elapsed time. The Method compresses ambiguity and rework by providing structure, parallelization, and decision accountability.

The Method bridges the gap between unstructured business needs and defensible vendor selection. It is not mandatory—users can adopt Buyer Console without the Method—but the platform's phases, roles, and guidance assume the Method as baseline.

## 2.2 Decomposition: Use Cases → Requirements {#2.2-decomposition:-use-cases-→-requirements}

### 2.2.1 Use Case Definition

A **Use Case** is a discrete business capability or workflow that the software must support. Each Use Case focuses on a specific job-to-be-done and involves a defined set of stakeholders.

**Examples:**

- Manage monthly close procedures (Accounting)  
- Automate invoice matching (AP)  
- Track open RFP status and deadline compliance (Procurement)

**Guideline:** Define enough Use Cases to cover the decision's distinct jobs-to-be-done without exceeding the plan-gated cap in §34.1.1 cell **Use Cases per Workspace**. §39 mirrors the cap and defines the counted rows (`UseCase.deleted_at IS NULL`). Use Case count guidance in this section is non-authoritative; create / import / materialization paths MUST validate against §34.1.1 and reject over-cap writes with HTTP 403 `plan_limit_exceeded` (Appendix I).

### 2.2.2 Requirement Definition

A **Requirement** is a measurable, scorable outcome that demonstrates whether a software feature meets a Use Case need.

**Format (required):**

\[Use Case\]: \[Requirement Statement\]

Acceptance Criteria: \[Observable, testable outcome\]

Type: \[Functional | Non-Functional | Integration | Compliance | UX\]

Granularity: \[Core | Important | Nice-to-Have\]

**Example:**

Use Case: Automate invoice matching

Requirement: System must match vendor invoice to PO and receipt within 2 seconds for 95% of invoices.

Acceptance Criteria: Latency \< 2s; accuracy ≥ 95%; no manual rekeying required.

Type: Functional \+ Performance

Granularity: Core

### 2.2.3 Requirement Granularity Guidelines

Each Requirement must result in exactly **one scorable outcome**. Avoid bundling multiple concerns into a single requirement.

**Anti-pattern (too broad):**

Requirement: The system must have strong reporting and dashboarding.

This encompasses data model, UI, export formats, scheduling—impossible to score holistically.

**Pattern (correct):**

Requirement 1: System provides real-time dashboard with current invoice aging by bucket.

Requirement 2: System exports reports to Excel with custom date range filtering.

Requirement 3: System schedules and emails automated aging reports on configurable cadence.

**Guideline:** If a requirement contains "and" or "or", decompose it. Total Requirement count is plan-gated by §34.1.1 cell **Requirements per Workspace** and mirrored in §39; create / import / materialization paths MUST validate against that source before writing Requirement rows.

### 2.2.4 Lifecycle Authority

Use Case and Requirement lifecycle rules are engine contracts, not advisory copy:

| Entity | Lifecycle authority | Status field | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Use Case (§4.3.3) | Appendix L.14 Use Case Status State Machine | §4.3.3 `status` (`use_case_status`) | Covers draft, validation, phase-lock, soft-delete, undo, and purge behavior. |
| Requirement (§4.3.4) | Appendix A Requirement Status State Machine | §4.3.4 `status` (Appendix J Requirement Statuses) | Appendix A pre-dates Appendix L and remains the canonical Requirement state-machine source. Do not author a second Requirement lifecycle in Appendix L. |

### 2.2.5 Acceptance Criteria

1. A Use Case create, import, duplicate, or EvalStarter materialization path MUST reject any write that would exceed §34.1.1 cell **Use Cases per Workspace** for the Workspace's plan-tier snapshot; the rejected response uses HTTP 403 `plan_limit_exceeded` and does not write a partial Use Case row.
2. A Requirement create, import, duplicate, generated-policy amendment publish, or EvalStarter materialization path MUST reject any write that would exceed §34.1.1 cell **Requirements per Workspace** for the Workspace's plan-tier snapshot; the rejected response uses HTTP 403 `plan_limit_exceeded` and does not write a partial Requirement row.
3. A Requirement write whose statement contains multiple independently scorable outcomes MUST be rejected by the decomposition validator before scoring setup. The rejection response MUST identify the compound conjunction span and return remediation copy instructing the author to split the Requirement.
4. Use Case transitions MUST conform to Appendix L.14; out-of-table transitions return HTTP 409 `use_case_invalid_state_transition` and leave `status` unchanged.
5. Requirement transitions MUST conform to Appendix A. Requirement writes after `status=finalized` MUST use the Phase 6 Amendment Protocol (§10.6) or return the Appendix A error path without mutating the Requirement row.
6. Deleting a Use Case that has Requirements MUST either cascade soft-delete the child Requirements in the same transaction while preserving audit history, or reject before any mutation when the Workspace phase / amendment guard does not allow the cascade. Partial parent-only delete is forbidden.

## 2.3 Scoring Calibration {#2.3-scoring-calibration}

### 2.3.1 Scoring Models

Sourcera supports three scoring models per requirement:

| Model | When to Use | Answer Type | Calibration |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **FM (Feature Match)** | Binary capability presence | Yes/No/Partial | Objective; scorer consensus is quick |
| **PM (Performance Measure)** | Quantifiable outcome | Numeric scale (1–10, 0–100) | Objective; compare vendor claims to benchmark data |
| **Expert Judgment (EJ)** | Subjective quality, fit, risk | Numeric scale (1–10) | Subjective; requires SME alignment and written rationale |

**Guideline:**

- Use FM for at least 30% of requirements (ensures defensibility).  
- Use PM for quantifiable requirements (speed, cost, capacity).  
- Use EJ sparingly; cluster EJ requirements by domain (e.g., "Implementation Risk," "Vendor Stability") to ensure consistency.  
- For EJ scoring, provide a **written scoring rubric** (e.g., "5 \= Moderate risk, 2-year relationship, regional support" vs. "3 \= High risk, startup, no local presence").

### 2.3.2 Handling Subjective Requirements

Subjective requirements (e.g., "vendor partnership quality," "ease of use") are common and necessary but must be disciplined:

**Do:**

- Define a scoring rubric with 3–5 clear levels (1–3, 1–5, 1–10).  
- Assign these to SME scorers with relevant expertise.  
- Require written comments for every score.  
- Conduct calibration session: have 2–3 evaluators score 1–2 vendors first, review scores together, agree on interpretation.

**Don't:**

- Score without a rubric.  
- Mix multiple subjective dimensions (e.g., "ease of use AND vendor stability") in one requirement.  
- Allow anonymous or comment-free scoring.

## 2.4 Vendor Shortlisting Strategy {#2.4-vendor-shortlisting-strategy}

### 2.4.1 Shortlisting Phases

The Sourcera Method recommends a two-phase vendor filtering approach:

**Phase 1: Initial Screening (Weeks 0–1)**

- Issue RFI (Request for Information) with 20–40 lightweight requirements (mostly FM).  
- Focus: Vendor capability baseline, compliance, basic fit.  
- Acceptance: \>= 80% "Yes" on Core \+ Important FM requirements, OR clear path to capability.  
- Typical outcome: 10 vendors → 5–7 vendors.

**Phase 2: Deep Evaluation (Weeks 2–6)**

- Issue RFP with full requirement set (FM \+ PM \+ EJ).  
- Conduct vendor demos, technical validation, reference calls.  
- Scoring during Phases 10–11 (see Section 10 for phase definitions).  
- Typical outcome: 5–7 vendors → 1–2 finalists → 1 selected.

### 2.4.2 Shortlisting Criteria

**Keep vendor if:**

- Covers ≥ 80% of Core requirements with FM \= Yes or Partial.  
- No critical compliance gaps (data residency, SOC 2, GDPR).  
- Total cost of ownership (TCO) within budget band (±20%).  
- Vendor stability signals OK (not pre-acquisition, not declining revenue).

**Drop vendor if:**

- \< 70% Core requirement coverage.  
- Critical compliance blocker (e.g., no US data residency when required).  
- TCO \> budget \+ 30%, AND no flexibility signaled in pricing discussion.  
- Vendor signals lack of interest (slow RFI response, no availability for demo).

## 2.5 Evaluation Timeline Benchmarks {#2.5-evaluation-timeline-benchmarks}

### 2.5.1 Recommended Phase Durations

§10.15 is the canonical source for Method phase names, per-phase benchmark durations, and total elapsed timeline. §2.5 does not restate phase groups, duration ranges, or total timeline numbers. Any surface that shows expected dates reads §10.15 and `Workspace.expected_phase_durations`, not this section.

### 2.5.2 Parallelization Opportunities

- RFI \+ RFP preparation can run in parallel during Phase 1–3 (assign separate teams).  
- Demos and scoring can overlap (Phase 10 scoring on early demos, Phase 11 score adjustments on later demos).  
- Reference calls can run during Phase 10–11 in parallel with internal scoring.

## 2.6 Cross-Departmental Alignment Patterns {#2.6-cross-departmental-alignment-patterns}

### 2.6.1 Stakeholder Cohorts

Define roles and responsibilities upfront:

| Cohort | Typical Title | Responsibilities |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Exec Sponsor** | VP Procurement, CFO, COO | Sign-off on Use Cases, phase gates, final vendor decision |
| **Evaluation Lead** | Senior Procurement Manager | Own end-to-end timeline, coordinate evaluators, interface with vendors |
| **Functional Leads** | Dept Manager (Finance, Ops, etc.) | Define Use Cases, write requirements, score FM/PM, represent department in demos |
| **Technical Evaluator** | IT/Systems Engineer | Assess integration, security, performance requirements, score technical PM/EJ |
| **SME / Evaluator** | Domain specialist, power user | Score requirements in area of expertise, provide written rationale |

**Cohorts are engine-level constructs.** The five cohort rows above are the canonical taxonomy used by the engine to bind stakeholders to permission profiles (§5), to compute SLA timers (§8.4), to drive Pulse Health Score components (§20.3), to gate phase advancement (§10.16), and to power Org Intelligence cohort analytics (§16). At invitation time the engine auto-assigns a cohort using the email-domain heuristics defined in §5.9 (functional-domain match → Functional Lead; IT/security domain match → Technical Evaluator; executive-suite domain match → Exec Sponsor; SME-tagged invitation → SME/Evaluator; the inviting user's role on the Workspace defaults to Evaluation Lead). The auto-assignment is a starting cohort; the Workspace Owner can re-assign at any time. Auto-assignment heuristics are advisory and never prevent invite acceptance — a heuristic miss falls back to the inviter's explicit cohort selection.

**Cohort surfacing depends on `evaluation_owner_mode`** (§4.3.1, §2.8). In **Team Mode** (`evaluation_owner_mode=team`), cohorts surface as role chips on every Workspace Member, drive cohort-bound Pulse cards, and gate phase advancement against per-cohort sign-off thresholds defined in §10.16 and §20.3. In **Single-Operator Mode** (`evaluation_owner_mode=solo`, authored in §2.8), cohorts remain engine-level constructs — the engine still computes them, still binds them to permission profiles, still records them on Audit Events for downstream reporting if the Workspace later transitions to Team Mode — but they do not surface as roles to the operator. The operator sees the work, not the role taxonomy. When the operator transitions a Workspace from `solo → team` (per §4.3.1) or invites the first stakeholder via the contextual one-click invite affordance authored in §2.8, the cohort rendering surfaces immediately for the newly-invited stakeholder and is back-populated on the operator's own membership row using the same auto-assignment heuristics. Appendix M row "Stakeholder Cohorts" binds the surface metaphor; the cohort enum strings (`exec_sponsor`, `evaluation_lead`, `functional_lead`, `technical_evaluator`, `sme_evaluator`) are never displayed verbatim — the user sees the title-case labels above.

### 2.6.2 Alignment Cadences

- **Kick-off (Week 0):** 1–2 hours. Present timeline, roles, Use Cases, phase gates. Collect feedback. Lock scope.  
- **Shortlist Review (Week 1–2):** 1 hour. Present RFI results, shortlist recommendation, rationale. Approve or adjust.  
- **RFP Response Review (Week 4):** 1–2 hours. Demo previews, early scoring patterns, any emerging gaps.  
- **Scoring Calibration (Week 5):** 1 hour. Review 2–3 early scores for subjective requirements; align on interpretation.  
- **Final Selection (Week 5–6):** 1–2 hours. Present recommendation with score summary, TCO, risks, next steps. Sign-off.

### 2.6.3 Escalation Pattern

If consensus cannot be reached on a requirement score:

1. Evaluation Lead facilitates 15-min discussion with scorers.  
2. If unresolved, escalate to Functional Lead (Use Case owner) for tiebreaker.  
3. If still unresolved, mark score as "Pending Vendor Clarification" and schedule follow-up demo question.  
4. Document all escalations in Evaluation Pulse (see Section 6).

## 2.7 Template Design Framework {#2.7-template-design-framework}

### 2.7.1 RFI Template Structure

**Recommended sections:**

| Section | Purpose | Typical Questions |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Vendor Background** | Qualification | Company size, years in market, customer count, funding status |
| **Compliance & Security** | Gate criteria | SOC 2, GDPR, data residency, penetration testing |
| **Product Capability (FM)** | Binary coverage | Feature existence (Yes/No/Partial/Roadmap) |
| **Pricing & Model** | Cost baseline | Pricing model, customer count, SLA, support tier options |
| **Integration & Data** | Technical fit | API availability, webhook support, data export, connector ecosystem |
| **Implementation** | Feasibility | Typical go-live timeline, onboarding model, training availability |

**RFI Guidance:**

- Keep to 40–60 questions max.  
- Expect 1–2 week vendor response window.  
- Require structured answers (yes/no, multiple choice) rather than open-ended prose.

### 2.7.2 RFP Template Structure

**Recommended sections:**

| Section | Purpose | Typical Questions |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Detailed Requirements** | FM \+ PM \+ EJ | Full 150–200 requirement set with scoring model per requirement |
| **Scenario-Based Demos** | Validation | "Walk us through Month-End Close workflow: " |
| **Pricing & Licensing** | Commercial terms | Final pricing, annual growth, bundled modules, cloud/on-premises options |
| **Implementation Plan** | Feasibility | Specific timeline, resource allocation, training, cutover strategy |
| **References** | Social proof | 3–5 reference customers in same industry/size, key contact names |
| **Appendices** | Admin | Security questionnaire, SLA template, data processing agreement |

**RFP Guidance:**

- Allow 2–4 weeks for vendor response.  
- Provide scoring rubric and weight distribution upfront.  
- Use Sourcera's Template Builder to auto-generate RFP from requirements.

## 2.8 Single-Operator Mode {#2.8-single-operator-mode}

### 2.8.1 Definition and Scope

Single-Operator Mode (also "Solo Mode") is the default surface path for first-time evaluation owners and for any Workspace whose owner is running the evaluation alone. The operator is, in engine terms, all five Stakeholder Cohorts simultaneously — Exec Sponsor, Evaluation Lead, Functional Lead, Technical Evaluator, and SME — until they explicitly invite another person. The Method itself does not change: the 13-phase pipeline (§10), the requirement decomposition discipline (§2.2), the scoring calibration (§2.3), the shortlisting strategy (§2.4), the alignment cadences (§2.6.2), and the template framework (§2.7) all run as authored. **Single-Operator Mode is a surface, not a methodology change.** The Method is invariant.

The mode is selected by the `evaluation_owner_mode` field on Workspace (§4.3.1, Appendix J `EvaluationOwnerMode`). Default-on for Buyer Free and Buyer Solo (Phase 14.6) plan tiers; default-off (i.e., default `team`) for Buyer Starter, Growth, Scale, and Enterprise plan tiers. The default is applied at Workspace create time using the Org's then-current `plan_tier` snapshot per §34.1.1; subsequent plan changes do not auto-recompute the field. The Workspace Owner can flip the mode at any time via Workspace Settings, subject to the transition guards in §4.3.1 (the `team → solo` direction is blocked when stakeholders or guests are present; the `solo → team` direction is always allowed).

### 2.8.2 Engine vs. Surface — What Compresses, What Does Not

The 13-phase pipeline runs as the engine in both modes. The Solo surface compresses the 13 phases into a 4-step user-facing progress bar — **Setup → Define → Score → Decide** — whose canonical step-to-phase mapping is authored in §3.14.1 (closed Phase 14.6) and whose component-level UI authoring (visual design, motion, mobile translation, accessibility, state catalog) lands in `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §5.2.19 PipelineSurface (closed Phase 14.6). The 4-step bar is a presentation of `pipeline_stage_id` (§4.3.1), not a replacement: every phase still advances through the Phase Advancement API (§10.16), every phase still emits the same audit events (§4.6.1), every phase still computes the same SLA timers and Pulse Health Score components (§8.4, §20.3), and the same Webhooks (§31) fire on the same triggers. The surface compression is purely a rendering decision driven by `evaluation_owner_mode`.

The mapping from engine phase to Solo surface step is fixed and is the canonical Buyer Solo step-to-phase contract. This table mirrors §3.14.1 verbatim per the §3.14.4 invariant `pipeline_surface_compression_step_to_phase_canonical`. Phase 14.6 supersedes the prior provisional mapping (which placed Phases 2–9 under Define) authored in Phase 14.4 as a placeholder; the Phase-14.6 mapping is the binding contract for engineering and QA. The §2.8 reconciliation log entry for Phase 14.6 documents the supersedence.

| Solo step | Engine phases (§10) | What the operator sees | Step-to-phase first sub-phase (click target) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Setup** | Phase 1 (Stakeholder Alignment & Discovery), Phase 2 (Requirement Definition), Phase 3 (Use Case Definition & Validation) | "Set up the evaluation" — Workspace creation, Use Case decomposition, Requirements authoring. The operator answers as the sole stakeholder; cohort auto-assignment runs in the engine. | Phase 1 |
| **Define** | Phase 4–5 (Vendor Discovery & Outreach), Phase 6 (Vendor Bidding Opens) | "Define the bid" — Vendor longlist, RFI / RFP design, vendor invites. Surfaces the Bidding-window deadline countdown (7-calendar-day minimum, §10.6). | Phase 4 |
| **Score** | Phase 7 (Vendor Response Refinement), Phase 8 (Buyer Due Diligence & Demos), Phase 9 (Final Vendor Clarifications), Phase 10 (Team Evaluation & Scoring) | "Score the vendors" — vendor responses come in, refinement and Q&A close, scoring proceeds; the operator scores all requirements as the lone evaluator and divergence detection (§13.6.2) is suppressed because there is only one scorer. | Phase 7 |
| **Decide** | Phase 11 (Score Review & Consensus), Phase 12 (Selection & Recommendation), Phase 13 (Contract & Closure) | "Decide" — Selection Record, Defense View (§13.11), post-selection close-out. Scores lock at Phase 12 entry; the Defense View augments this step with a structured "defend my decision" companion. | Phase 11 |

The 4-step progress bar surfaces only one active step at a time with the others rendered in a faded preview state. The full 13-phase chip ribbon authored in §3.3.1 and Appendix M (line "Phase X of 13 — …" chip) is suppressed in Solo Mode — it does not pass the §3.13 First-30-Seconds Test for a panicked first-timer. The full UI authoring (visual design, motion, mobile translation, accessibility, state catalog) of the four-step progress bar lands in `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §5.2.19 (PipelineSurface), authored in Phase 14.6.

### 2.8.3 Phase Gates — Soft in Solo, Hard in Team

The Phase Advancement API (§10.16) enforces phase-gate preconditions on every transition. In **Team Mode**, gates are **hard**: a missing required-field, an unsigned-off Use Case, an unaccepted vendor, or an unresolved scoring divergence blocks the API call with HTTP 422 and a structured remediation list. The user must satisfy the gate before advancing. Hard gates are the engine's enforcement mechanism for the Method's parallelization and accountability discipline — they prevent a Workspace from drifting into an unscorable or undefensible state.

In **Single-Operator Mode**, gates are **soft (skip-with-warning)**: the same gate logic runs, the same remediation list is computed, but the API call is not blocked. Instead, the operator sees a warning panel — "You haven't finished {N} setup items. Skip and come back later?" — with two affordances: "Finish them first" (returns to the open items) and "Skip for now" (advances the phase and logs a `phase_advanced_with_unmet_gates` Audit Event with the unmet-gate enum list serialized into `metadata`). The skip-with-warning behavior is encoded by a new boolean `soft_gates_enabled` on the Phase Advancement request: `soft_gates_enabled=true` is auto-applied by the server when `Workspace.evaluation_owner_mode=solo` and is rejected with HTTP 422 `phase_advancement_soft_gates_not_permitted_in_team_mode` if a client attempts to set it on a `team`-mode Workspace. The `phase_advanced_with_unmet_gates` audit event (registered in Appendix C and the §4.6.1 action namespace) carries the original gate list verbatim so a later `solo → team` transition or post-hoc audit can identify exactly which Method discipline was deferred.

A Workspace that transitions from `solo → team` after one or more soft-gate skips inherits the unmet-gate ledger: the Team-Mode UI surfaces a banner reading "{N} setup items were skipped under Solo Mode — review before advancing" listing each unmet gate with a one-click "Address" CTA. The banner does not block subsequent Team-Mode phase advancements, but new advancements in Team Mode are hard-gated as authored.

### 2.8.4 SLAs and Pulse Health — Engine On, Surface Off

SLA timers (§8.4) and Pulse Health Score components (§20.3) compute identically in both modes. The engine runs the per-cohort response-rate, agreement, and overdue-task aggregations every Workspace tick regardless of mode. The difference is the surface:

- In **Team Mode**, SLA timers surface as "Due in 2 days" pills on Pulse cards and "Overdue" red pills on breach (per Appendix M); the Pulse Health Score widget renders the composite score (e.g., "Workspace health: 87 / 100") with a per-component breakdown; the Pulse Inbox surfaces grouped notifications per cohort.
- In **Single-Operator Mode**, the operator sees a single deadline countdown — the next phase-bound deadline relevant to the operator's current step — and a "What to do this week" panel that lists the top three open items in priority order. The full Pulse Inbox, the per-component Pulse Health Score breakdown, the SLA pills, and the cohort-bound notification grouping are suppressed. The composite score is still computed and persisted on `WorkspacePulseHealth` (§20.3) for audit, dashboarding, and any future `solo → team` transition; it just does not render in the operator's UI. The Pulse Digest Email (§20.4) is suppressed by default in Solo Mode and can be opted into via Notification Preferences (§20.6).

This split is a rendering decision keyed to `Workspace.evaluation_owner_mode`. There is no second copy of the SLA or Pulse engine; the same `WorkspacePulseHealth` row is written, the same component aggregates are persisted, and the same `pulse.health_score_threshold_breached` webhook (§31) fires on threshold breach regardless of mode. A `solo → team` transition immediately exposes the previously-suppressed surfaces with their already-computed values; the operator does not start over.

### 2.8.5 Contextual Stakeholder Invites

Invitations in Single-Operator Mode are **contextual and inline** — never an upfront setup step. The operator does not see a "build your team" stage before they can begin. Instead, each natural moment surfaces a one-click invite affordance bound to the cohort whose work the operator is currently doing:

| Natural moment | Inline invite affordance | Auto-assigned cohort |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Operator is drafting the security / IT requirements section | "Invite your IT or security lead — they'll review just this section" | Technical Evaluator |
| Operator is filling in the TCO model (§15) | "Invite your finance partner — they'll see only the TCO and pricing pages" | Functional Lead (Finance) |
| Operator is composing the data-residency / compliance section | "Invite your compliance contact — they'll review only the compliance section" | Functional Lead (Compliance) or Technical Evaluator (per email-domain heuristic) |
| Operator is scheduling a demo (Phase 8) | "Invite the people who should attend this demo — Sourcera will share scoring with them" | SME / Evaluator |
| Operator is composing the Selection Report (Phase 12) | "Invite your decision-maker — they'll see the Selection Report and approve" | Exec Sponsor |
| Operator is approaching the Bidding-window minimum (7 calendar days, §10.6) | "Need a second pair of eyes on bids? Invite a reviewer." | Reviewer (workspace role; cohort = Evaluation Lead by default) |

Each invite is a single click that opens the existing Invite Stakeholder modal (§5, §38) pre-filled with: (a) the cohort selection inferred from the inline affordance, (b) the permission profile defaulted to the cohort's profile per §5.9, (c) the visibility scope defaulted to the section the operator is currently in (the invitee sees only that section unless the operator widens the scope), and (d) a contextual one-line note ("I'm inviting you to review the security section of our [vendor type] evaluation"). The first stakeholder accepted into the Workspace **does not auto-transition the Workspace from `solo → team`** — the operator can still run the evaluation themselves with a single guest reviewer. The transition fires only when (a) the operator explicitly toggles the mode in Workspace Settings, OR (b) a second non-guest Workspace Membership with role ∈ {`workspace_admin`, `use_case_lead`, `reviewer`} is accepted, at which point the surface auto-promotes to Team Mode and a one-time toast surfaces ("Switched to Team Mode — your team can see the full evaluation now"). The transition is recorded as a `workspace_evaluation_owner_mode_changed` Audit Event with `trigger_reason=automatic_team_threshold_reached`.

### 2.8.6 Cross-Console Behavior

Single-Operator Mode is a Buyer-console concept (the seller-side Bid Workspace surface compresses by default — there is no "team" version of seller-side bid response authoring). On the Buyer side, Solo Mode does not affect any cross-console firewall behavior (§4.7.1, §7.2): vendors invited to bid see the same Bid Workspace surface regardless of whether the buyer Workspace is in Solo Mode or Team Mode. The seller never learns the buyer's `evaluation_owner_mode`. The Console Bridge Event payload (§4.7.1) excludes the field; the Public Pricing API (§32, §4.8.9) excludes the field; the Marketplace Listing exposes only the buyer Workspace's `pipeline_stage_id`, never its mode.

### 2.8.7 Acceptance Criteria

1. A Workspace created by an Org on Buyer Free or Buyer Solo plan tier MUST default `evaluation_owner_mode=solo`. A Workspace created by an Org on Buyer Starter, Growth, Scale, or Enterprise tier MUST default `evaluation_owner_mode=team`. Defaults are computed from the Org's `plan_tier` snapshot at create time per §34.1.1 and never auto-recomputed on subsequent plan changes.
2. The Solo surface MUST render the four-step progress bar (Setup → Define → Score → Decide) and MUST suppress the 13-phase chip ribbon when `Workspace.evaluation_owner_mode=solo`. The mapping in §2.8.2 is canonical; the surface MUST pass the §3.13 First-30-Seconds Test for a panicked first-timer.
3. The Phase Advancement API (§10.16) MUST auto-apply `soft_gates_enabled=true` on Solo-mode Workspaces and MUST reject a client-supplied `soft_gates_enabled=true` with HTTP 422 `phase_advancement_soft_gates_not_permitted_in_team_mode` on Team-mode Workspaces. Soft-gate skip MUST emit `phase_advanced_with_unmet_gates` audit event with the unmet-gate enum list serialized into `metadata.unmet_gates[]`.
4. Soft-gate skip MUST NOT block phase advancement on a Solo-mode Workspace; the API MUST return HTTP 200 with the new `pipeline_stage_id` and the unmet-gate list in the response body's `warnings` field per §32 envelope conventions.
5. SLA timers (§8.4) and Pulse Health Score components (§20.3) MUST compute identically in both modes. The Solo surface MUST suppress SLA pills, the per-component Pulse Health breakdown widget, and the Pulse Inbox grouped notifications. The Solo surface MUST display a single deadline countdown (next phase-bound deadline) and a "What to do this week" three-item panel. The deadline countdown MUST render the deadline timestamp in `User.timezone` (falling back to `Org.timezone` when unset) and in the user's locale per the §41 (Email Deliverability) date-rendering convention; format MUST honor 24h-vs-12h locale preference; CI gate `solo_deadline_countdown_renders_in_user_timezone` (§M.5.4) asserts.
6. Pulse Digest Email (§20.4) MUST default to suppressed in Solo Mode and MUST be opt-in via Notification Preferences (§20.6).
7. Stakeholder cohorts MUST be auto-assigned on invite acceptance using the email-domain heuristics in §5.9. The auto-assignment is advisory; the inviter MAY override the cohort selection in the Invite Stakeholder modal.
8. The first contextual invite that resolves to a guest role MUST NOT trigger an auto-transition from `solo → team`. The auto-transition MUST fire only when (a) the Workspace Owner explicitly toggles the mode in Workspace Settings, OR (b) a second non-guest Workspace Membership with role ∈ {`workspace_admin`, `use_case_lead`, `reviewer`} is accepted. The latter MUST emit a `workspace_evaluation_owner_mode_changed` audit event with `trigger_reason=automatic_team_threshold_reached`.
9. A `solo → team` transition that follows one or more soft-gate skips MUST surface a Team-Mode banner listing each unmet gate with an "Address" CTA. The banner MUST NOT block subsequent Team-Mode phase advancements; new advancements in Team Mode MUST be hard-gated.
10. The `evaluation_owner_mode` field MUST NOT appear in any Console Bridge Event payload (§4.7.1), any seller-visible API response (§32), any Marketplace Listing serialization (§27), or the Public Pricing API (§4.8.9). The seller MUST NOT learn the buyer's mode under any code path.
11. Appendix M MUST contain a tightened, surface-bound row for Single-Operator Mode (the forward-reference row authored in Phase 14.2) and MUST contain explicit annotations on the Stakeholder Cohorts row, the Pulse Health Score row, the SLA Timers row, and the Pulse Inbox row indicating that the surface is suppressed when `evaluation_owner_mode=solo` while the underlying engine continues to compute and persist the corresponding values. (Phase 14.4 deliverable.)
12. The four-step progress bar UI authoring (visual design, mobile translation, motion, accessibility, state catalog) is a Phase 14.6 deliverable in `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md`. The §2.8 mapping is the engine-side contract that Phase 14.6 implements against; any divergence between Phase 14.6 UI and §2.8 mapping is a defect against §2.8.

### 2.8.8 Cross-References

- §3.13 (Principle 9 — Surface Simplicity, Engine Complexity): Single-Operator Mode is the first surface authored under Principle 9 and is bound by the First-30-Seconds Test.
- §4.3.1 (Workspace): `evaluation_owner_mode` field, indexes, transition guards.

# 3\. UX Standard — The Sourcera Constraint {#3.-ux-standard-—-the-sourcera-constraint}

## 3.1 Philosophy {#3.1-philosophy}

The **Sourcera** **Constraint** is an opinionated UI/UX principle that ensures Sourcera remains fast, predictable, and focused despite feature complexity. It codifies keyboard-first interaction on desktop and gesture-first interaction on mobile, preventing the platform from devolving into modal stacks, buried settings, and slow navigation trees.

**Core principle:** Every major workflow must be navigable and actionable via a single linear sequence (left-to-right, top-to-bottom, keyboard-driven on desktop). Discoverability and power-user features are orthogonal and accessed via secondary patterns (search, context menus, keyboard shortcuts).

## 3.2 The 8 Core Interaction Patterns {#3.2-the-8-core-interaction-patterns}

| Pattern | Desktop Primary | Mobile Equivalent | Use Case |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Sidebar Navigation** | Left-side nav panel; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+J toggles; Keyboard arrow keys to navigate | Bottom sheet or hamburger menu | Workspace/view switching, rapid context shifts |
| **Command Palette** | Cmd/Ctrl+K opens fuzzy searchable command list | Swipe-up gesture or search icon (limited command set) | Jump to any entity, trigger action, set property |
| **Inline Editing** | Click field, edit, Tab/Enter to confirm, Esc to cancel | Tap field, edit, tap checkmark to confirm | Edit requirement title, team name, score notes |
| **Keyboard Shortcuts** | Defined per-feature (see 3.3) | N/A (accessible via Command Palette instead) | Power-user acceleration, repetitive actions |
| **Optimistic Mutation** | Change applied immediately on screen, spinner indicates background sync | Same behavior | Instant feedback, perceived speed |
| **Contextual Menu (Right-Click)** | Right-click opens context menu with actions | Long-press opens context menu | Duplicate requirement, change state, delete |
| **Modal \+ Escape Hatch** | Modal dialog with Esc to close, Cmd+Enter to submit | Full-screen overlay; back gesture to close | Confirm destructive action, complex multi-step form (rare) |
| **Live Preview / Presence** | Collaborators visible in sidebar (avatars, live cursors in shared doc) | Presence indicator in collaborators list | Multi-user editing, collision avoidance |

## 3.3 Pattern-to-Feature Mapping (Authoritative) {#3.3-pattern-to-feature-mapping-(authoritative)}

This section maps all 46+ features to their primary interaction pattern and defines feature-specific keyboard shortcuts, optimistic mutation behavior, and mobile translation.

### 3.3.1 Workspace & Navigation Features

**Feature: Create Workspace**

- Primary Pattern: Modal \+ Keyboard  
- Keyboard Shortcut: (none; Modal auto-focuses input)  
- Shortcut: Cmd+Shift+N (Windows: Ctrl+Shift+N)  
- Optimistic Mutation: Workspace appears in sidebar with loading state; refresh on background sync.  
- Mobile: Full-screen form; back gesture dismisses.  
- Acceptance Criteria:  
  - Workspace name input accepts 1–100 chars.  
  - Default console (Buyer|Seller) pre-selected based on user org role.  
  - Tab navigates through form fields; Enter submits; Esc cancels.  
  - Error message displays inline under failed field within 1 second.

**Feature: Switch Workspace**

- Primary Pattern: Sidebar Navigation  
- Keyboard Shortcut: Cmd+Shift+J (jump to workspace); arrow keys to cycle; Enter to select.  
- Optimistic Mutation: UI switches to workspace immediately; data loads in background.  
- Mobile: Tap hamburger menu \> tap workspace name.  
- Acceptance Criteria:  
  - Sidebar shows max 10 recent workspaces; "View All" link shows full list in modal.  
  - Current workspace highlighted with underline.  
  - Keyboard navigation with arrow up/down; Enter confirms.  
  - Workspace switch within 500ms; loading spinner during data fetch.

**Feature: Workspace Settings**

- Primary Pattern: Sidebar Navigation \+ Inline Editing  
- Keyboard Shortcut: (accessible via Command Palette: Cmd+K, type "Settings")  
- Optimistic Mutation: Field change reflected immediately; background sync indicated by brief spinner.  
- Mobile: Gesture-first; tap settings icon \> scroll list of editable fields.  
- Acceptance Criteria:  
  - Settings accessible via gear icon in sidebar footer.  
  - Click any setting field to edit (name, description, data residency, default phase).  
  - Tab between fields; Enter confirms; Esc cancels current edit.  
  - Unsaved changes indicated by italic field label.  
  - Save all changes with Cmd+S (desktop) or tap "Save" button (mobile).

**Feature: Org Switcher**

- Primary Pattern: Sidebar Navigation  
- Keyboard Shortcut: Cmd+Shift+O (cycle org); Cmd+Shift+L (list orgs in Command Palette).  
- Optimistic Mutation: Org switches immediately; workspace list updates in background.  
- Mobile: Tap org avatar in top-left \> tap target org.  
- Acceptance Criteria:  
  - Org avatar in top-left corner with org name tooltip.  
  - Click to open org switcher dropdown (max 8 recent orgs; "View All" for full list).  
  - Keyboard navigation with arrows; Enter selects.  
  - Org switch completes within 1 second; page remains at current route context.

### 3.3.2 Use Case & Requirement Features

**Feature: Create Use Case**

- Primary Pattern: Inline Editing / Modal  
- Keyboard Shortcut: (Create from Use Case list via Cmd+N)  
- Optimistic Mutation: New Use Case appears in list with "Untitled Use Case" placeholder; immediately editable.  
- Mobile: Tap "+" button; full-screen form.  
- Acceptance Criteria:  
  - Form includes Use Case name (required, 1–200 chars), description (optional, 0–1000 chars), owner (Team or User, optional).  
  - Save via Enter (desktop) or tap checkmark (mobile); Esc cancels.  
  - Form validates non-empty name before save; error shows below field.  
  - New Use Case appears in list within 300ms; loading spinner indicates background sync.

**Feature: Edit Use Case**

- Primary Pattern: Inline Editing  
- Keyboard Shortcut: (Open Use Case, then Cmd+E to toggle edit mode for name/description)  
- Optimistic Mutation: Field change visible immediately; background sync within 2 seconds.  
- Mobile: Tap Use Case row \> tap field to edit.  
- Acceptance Criteria:  
  - Click Use Case name or description to edit inline.  
  - Tab navigates between name and description fields.  
  - Enter confirms; Esc reverts to last saved value.  
  - Concurrent edit collision detection: if another user edits same field simultaneously, resolver modal appears (Keep Mine | Keep Theirs | Manual Merge).

**Feature: Delete Use Case**

- Primary Pattern: Contextual Menu \+ Modal  
- Keyboard Shortcut: (Delete from detail view via Cmd+Delete)  
- Optimistic Mutation: Use Case disappears from list; undo button available for 10 seconds.  
- Mobile: Long-press Use Case row \> "Delete" option.  
- Acceptance Criteria:  
  - Right-click Use Case in list \> "Delete" option.  
  - Confirmation modal: "Delete \[Name\]? This cannot be undone. \[Cancel\] \[Delete\]"  
  - If Use Case has requirements (\>0), secondary confirmation: "This Use Case has N requirements. They will be deleted. \[Cancel\] \[Delete Anyway\]"  
  - Upon delete, show undo button in toast for 10 seconds.  
  - Undo restores Use Case and all associated requirements.

**Feature: Create Requirement**

- Primary Pattern: Modal / Inline Form  
- Keyboard Shortcut: (Within Use Case, press Cmd+N to create new requirement below current one)  
- Optimistic Mutation: Requirement appears in Use Case list with placeholder "Untitled Requirement"; focus auto-moves to title field for immediate editing.  
- Mobile: Tap Use Case \> "Add Requirement" button \> inline edit form.  
- Acceptance Criteria:  
  - Form fields: Requirement statement (1–500 chars, required), Acceptance Criteria (0–5000 chars), Type (dropdown: Functional|Non-Functional|Integration|Compliance|UX), Granularity (dropdown: Core|Important|Nice-to-Have), Scoring Model (dropdown: FM|PM|EJ).  
  - Tab navigates through fields; Enter confirms; Esc cancels.  
  - Validation: statement required; no save allowed if blank.  
  - New requirement appears in list within 300ms.

**Feature: Edit Requirement**

- Primary Pattern: Inline Editing / Detail Panel  
- Keyboard Shortcut: (Open requirement detail, Cmd+E toggles edit mode)  
- Optimistic Mutation: Field changes visible immediately; save on Tab or Enter.  
- Mobile: Tap requirement \> swipe left to reveal edit icon \> tap to enter edit mode.  
- Acceptance Criteria:  
  - All requirement fields editable via inline click or detail panel right-side form.  
  - Edits auto-save on field blur (Tab/click away); Esc reverts to last saved.  
  - Concurrent edit collision detection applies (same as Use Case).  
  - Requirement links (related, dependent) manageable via "Link Requirement" modal.

**Feature: Reorder Requirements**

- Primary Pattern: Keyboard Shortcuts \+ Drag  
- Keyboard Shortcut: Cmd+Up/Down to move requirement up/down within Use Case.  
- Optimistic Mutation: Requirement order changes immediately; background sync within 1 second.  
- Mobile: Long-press requirement, drag to new position, release.  
- Acceptance Criteria:  
  - Drag handle (≡ icon) visible on left side of requirement row; grab to drag.  
  - Keyboard: select requirement, Cmd+Up/Down, requirement moves and list re-indexes.  
  - Visual feedback: target position highlighted while dragging.  
  - Drop completes reorder within 500ms.

**Feature: Score Requirement (FM)**

- Primary Pattern: Inline Selector / Popover  
- Keyboard Shortcut: (Within requirement row, press Tab until focused on score cell, then arrow keys to cycle Yes|Partial|No)  
- Optimistic Mutation: Score change visible immediately; background sync within 2 seconds.  
- Mobile: Tap requirement row \> tap score button (Yes|Partial|No) to cycle.  
- Acceptance Criteria:  
  - Score options for FM: Yes (green checkmark) | Partial (yellow dash) | No (red X).  
  - Click or tap to cycle through options; keyboard arrow keys to navigate.  
  - Score cell shows current selection with background color.  
  - Notes field auto-appears if score \= Partial or No (optional, but recommended).  
  - Multiple scorers can rate same requirement independently; final score determined by averaging or voting (see Section 5).

**Feature: Score Requirement (PM)**

- Primary Pattern: Inline Number Input / Slider  
- Keyboard Shortcut: (Click score cell, type numeric value, press Enter)  
- Optimistic Mutation: Score visible immediately; validation on blur (Tab or click away).  
- Mobile: Tap score cell \> number picker or slider (0–100).  
- Acceptance Criteria:  
  - Display scale (1–10 or 0–100) pre-defined at workspace level.  
  - Click score cell to reveal inline numeric input or slider.  
  - Keyboard: type value, Enter confirms, Esc cancels.  
  - Validation: value must be within defined range; error shows below field if out of range.  
  - Notes field auto-appears (optional but recommended for PM scores \> 7 or \< 4).

**Feature: Score Requirement (EJ)**

- Primary Pattern: Inline Scale / Popover  
- Keyboard Shortcut: (Click score cell, arrow keys to select 1–10, Enter confirms)  
- Optimistic Mutation: Score visible immediately; background sync within 2 seconds.  
- Mobile: Tap score cell \> 1–10 scale picker.  
- Acceptance Criteria:  
  - Display 1–10 numeric scale with labels at bottom (e.g., "1=Poor, 5=Adequate, 10=Excellent").  
  - Scoring rubric tooltip available (? icon) showing full rubric for this requirement.  
  - Notes field REQUIRED for EJ scores (cannot save without written rationale).  
  - Keyboard: arrow keys (1–10), Enter confirms, Esc cancels.  
  - Notes field auto-expands and focuses.

**Feature: Bulk Edit Requirements**

- Primary Pattern: Checkbox Selection \+ Contextual Menu  
- Keyboard Shortcut: (Cmd+A to select all visible requirements; Cmd+Click to toggle individual selection)  
- Optimistic Mutation: Bulk changes applied immediately to all selected; individual background sync within 2 seconds per item.  
- Mobile: Swipe left on requirement to reveal checkbox; tap to select; "Bulk Actions" toolbar appears at bottom.  
- Acceptance Criteria:  
  - Checkbox appears on left side of each requirement row (hidden by default, reveals on hover or tap).  
  - Cmd+A selects all visible requirements; Cmd+Click toggles individual.  
  - "Bulk Actions" toolbar appears when selection \> 0 (desktop at top of list, mobile at bottom).  
  - Available bulk actions: Change Granularity, Change Type, Change Scoring Model, Copy to Use Case, Delete All.  
  - Confirmation required for destructive actions (Delete All).
