## 3.4 Mobile Translation of Linear Constraint {#3.4-mobile-translation-of-linear-constraint}

On mobile devices (iOS/Android, viewport \< 768px), the Linear Constraint translates keyboard-first patterns to gesture-first equivalents while preserving the "linear flow" principle:

| Desktop Pattern | Keyboard | Mobile Gesture Equivalent |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Sidebar Navigation | Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+J | Tap hamburger icon \> swipe list |
| Command Palette | Cmd/Ctrl+K | Swipe up from bottom or tap search icon \> type |
| Keyboard Shortcuts (Cmd+X) | Direct shortcut | Trigger via Command Palette or long-press on element |
| Inline Editing | Tab, Enter, Esc | Tap field \> keyboard appears \> tap checkmark or swipe down to dismiss |
| Right-Click Context Menu | Right-click | Long-press element \> swipe-up to reveal menu |
| Modal | Esc to dismiss | Swipe down to dismiss; back gesture (Android) to close |
| Keyboard Arrow Keys | Up/Down/Left/Right | Swipe up/down in list to scroll; tap to select |

**Mobile Constraint Requirements:**

- All major workflows completable within 5 taps (excluding text entry).  
- Modals default to full-screen or 80% viewport height (not center-anchored).  
- Bottom-sheet modals (over existing content) used for secondary actions.  
- Touch targets follow the §38.6.2 per-tier minimum; avoid edge-of-screen targets (swipe-back conflicts).  
- Keyboard always auto-shows when text field focused; auto-hides on blur or swipe-dismiss.  
- Horizontal scrolling avoided except for comparison views (explicitly indicated).

## 3.5 Optimistic Mutation Rollback Behavior {#3.5-optimistic-mutation-rollback-behavior}

When optimistic mutations fail in the background (network error, validation failure, concurrency conflict), the UI must provide clear recovery options:

**Pattern: Optimistic Mutation with Rollback**

1. **User Action:** User clicks "Save", field value changes, or item is deleted.  
2. **Optimistic State:** UI immediately reflects change (spinner or loading indicator brief).  
3. **Background Sync:** API request sent in background.  
4. **Success Path:** Change persists; spinner disappears within 2 seconds.  
5. **Failure Path (Validation Error):**  
   - UI reverts to last saved value.  
   - Error toast appears: "\[Field name\] could not be saved: \[reason\]. \[Retry\] \[Discard\]"  
   - If Retry: attempt save again; if Discard: revert and close toast.  
6. **Failure Path (Concurrency Conflict):**  
   - Conflict modal appears: "This field was edited by \[Other User\] at \[time\]. Resolve conflict: \[Keep Mine\] \[Keep Theirs\] \[Manual Merge\]"  
   - If Keep Mine: user's version persists.  
   - If Keep Theirs: revert to other user's version.  
   - If Manual Merge: open side-by-side editor; user manually reconciles and saves.  
7. **Failure Path (Network Error):**  
   - UI keeps optimistic change visible.  
   - Persistent banner appears at top: "Offline. Changes will sync when online. \[Retry\] \[Discard\]"  
   - If Retry: attempt save when connection restored (automatic).  
   - If Discard: revert change and remove banner.

**Feature-Specific Rollback Behavior:**

| Feature | Rollback Trigger | Recovery Option |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Create Requirement | Validation error (empty title) | Toast \+ input re-focuses; title field highlighted |
| Edit Requirement | Concurrency conflict | Conflict modal (Keep Mine / Keep Theirs / Merge) |
| Delete Requirement | (No rollback) | Undo toast for 10 seconds; click to restore |
| Score Requirement (FM) | Validation error (invalid value) | Revert to last saved score; error below cell |
| Score Requirement (PM) | Score out of range | Revert to last saved; error tooltip shows valid range |
| Add Comment | Network error | Persistent "Unsent" badge on comment; retry button; discard option |
| Submit Bid Response | Validation error (required field empty) | Modal shows missing fields; user can edit and retry |

## 3.6 Form & Input Tokens {#3.6-form-&-input-tokens}

**Purpose (C.109).** A single source-of-truth token system governs every form control rendered in either console, in Ops Console, in Marketplace authoring surfaces, and in embedded portal artifacts. The contract covers sizing, spacing, border treatment, focus, validation, label, and helper-text behavior. Every form component in §38 Component Library MUST consume these tokens — inline CSS overrides are a lint failure.

**Scope.** Tokens apply to: text input, password input, email input, phone input, numeric input, monetary input, date/time input, textarea, select (native + combobox), multi-select, tag input, toggle, checkbox, radio, segmented control, slider, stepper, file picker, search input, inline-edit cell, and rich-text editor (wrapper chrome only — interior typography owns its own tokens). Applies to Buyer Console, Seller Console, Ops Console (§50), and Marketplace authoring surfaces (SellerOrgPage edit, SoftwarePage edit, ComparisonPage Ops authoring). Excluded: the Command Palette search input (§3.2), which ships its own token set documented in §38.3; the NDA signature input, which ships Adobe Sign chrome; third-party embedded widgets (Stripe Elements, Firecrawl console).

### 3.6.1 Dimensional Tokens {#3.6.1-dimensional-tokens}

All dimensional tokens are authored as CSS custom properties and mirrored into the Figma token library via Tokens Studio. The token name, value, and usage rule are authoritative here — UX Summary §2.9 is the paired designer-facing surface and is kept in sync via the token-sync CI job (`ux_token_drift_check`, §50.17.4).

| Token | Value | Usage Rule |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `--input-height-sm` | 28px | Compact inputs — inline-edit cells, DataTable in-cell editors, dense filter chips, keyboard-driven scoring cells. MUST NOT be used for primary form fields. |
| `--input-height-md` | 36px | Default for all primary form fields — Workspace create, Requirement create, Settings, Profile, Marketplace authoring. The "canonical" input. |
| `--input-height-lg` | 44px | Prominent inputs — hero search, onboarding first-field, empty-state primary CTA embedded input, mobile text fields (WCAG touch target). |
| `--input-padding-x` | 12px | Horizontal padding for `sm` and `md`. `lg` MAY use 16px when paired with leading or trailing icon; icon-adjacent padding reduces to 8px on the icon side. |
| `--input-padding-y` | Derived from height − typography line-height | Computed, not hand-set. Prevents vertical-centering drift across typefaces. |
| `--input-radius` | `--radius-md` (6px) | Every input. Segmented controls use `--radius-md` on the outer shell and 0 internal separators. |
| `--input-border-default` | 1px solid `--color-border-default` | Resting state. |
| `--input-border-hover` | 1px solid `--color-border-strong` | Mouse hover; suppressed when `:focus-visible` is active. |
| `--input-border-focus` | 1px solid `--color-accent` | Paired with focus ring. |
| `--input-border-error` | 1px solid `--color-danger` | Paired with red helper text. Takes precedence over focus ring tint (ring stays `--color-accent` at reduced opacity; border is red). |
| `--input-border-warning` | 1px solid `--color-warning` | Soft validation (e.g., duplicate-requirement detection from Summary §9.3.8). |
| `--input-border-success` | 1px solid `--color-success` | Confirmation of async validation pass (e.g., valid domain, valid email, NDA signature captured). Auto-clears after 1500ms. |
| `--input-border-readonly` | 1px dashed `--color-border-default` | Read-only fields that are not disabled (e.g., inferred values, server-computed fields); cursor: text, selection allowed. |
| `--input-bg` | `--color-bg-tertiary` | Resting fill, both modes. |
| `--input-bg-disabled` | `--color-bg-secondary` at 50% opacity | Disabled; paired with `cursor: not-allowed`. |
| `--input-bg-readonly` | `--color-bg-primary` | Read-only (distinct from disabled — text remains selectable). |
| `--input-focus-ring-color` | `--color-accent` at 20% opacity (light) / 30% opacity (dark) | Composes with `--input-border-focus`. |
| `--input-focus-ring-width` | 3px | Outer ring, offset 0 (same-plane). |
| `--input-focus-ring-error-color` | `--color-danger` at 20% opacity (light) / 30% (dark) | Used when input is simultaneously focused and in error. |
| `--input-label-gap` | `--space-1` (4px) | Vertical gap between label and control. |
| `--input-helper-gap` | `--space-1` (4px) | Vertical gap between control and helper/error/counter text. |
| `--input-group-gap` | `--space-4` (16px) | Vertical rhythm between sibling form fields within a section. |
| `--input-group-gap-dense` | `--space-3` (12px) | Dense forms (Ops Console, SettingsTabbedPanel) and inline-edit tables. |
| `--input-icon-size` | 16px | Leading / trailing input icons (search, clear, validation glyph, unit suffix). |
| `--input-icon-gap` | `--space-2` (8px) | Gap between icon and text. |
| `--input-min-width-numeric` | 8ch | Monetary / quantity / SLA-day fields; prevents jitter as value length changes. |
| `--input-max-width-url` | 480px | URL inputs (crawl seed, webhook endpoint, IdP SSO URL). Scroll within field; wrap on overflow unsupported. |

**Cross-token invariants.** `--input-height-sm` + `Body Small` (13px) produces 28px with 7.5px vertical padding; `--input-height-md` + `Body` (14px) produces 36px with 11px vertical padding; `--input-height-lg` + `Body` (14px) produces 44px with 15px vertical padding. Typography tokens are defined in §38.1 / UX §2.1. Rendering implementations MUST use `line-height: 1` on the input element itself and rely on the outer height for vertical centering.

### 3.6.2 Focus Ring {#3.6.2-focus-ring}

Every interactive form control renders a 3px outer ring on `:focus-visible` using `--input-focus-ring-color`. The ring is suppressed on `:focus:not(:focus-visible)` to avoid showing on mouse click. Suppression rules:

- `:hover` never composes with the focus ring; hover resolves to `--input-border-hover` only when not focused.
- `:active` (mousedown/keydown in progress) dampens the ring to 2px width and 30% opacity to provide a tactile "press" signal.
- Ring color inverts to `--input-focus-ring-error-color` when the control's `aria-invalid="true"`.
- Ring is suppressed inside an open Command Palette (`z-index: 80`) because the palette owns its own focus chrome.
- Ring respects `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` by disabling the 150ms fade-in; the ring appears instantaneously.

### 3.6.3 Validation States {#3.6.3-validation-states}

The authoritative validation-state enum is `input_validation_state` (Appendix J). Every form field exposes exactly one state at a time. State precedence from lowest to highest: `default` < `focus` < `success` < `warning` < `error` < `disabled`. `read_only` is orthogonal to the above and composes with `default` or `success` only.

| State | Border | Fill | Focus Ring | Helper Text | Cursor | ARIA |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `default` | `--input-border-default` | `--input-bg` | — | Neutral (secondary text) | text | `aria-invalid="false"` |
| `focus` | `--input-border-focus` | `--input-bg` | `--input-focus-ring-color` | Unchanged | text | unchanged |
| `error` | `--input-border-error` | `--input-bg` | `--input-focus-ring-error-color` (on focus) | Red, leading error icon | text | `aria-invalid="true"`, `aria-describedby` → error-id |
| `warning` | `--input-border-warning` | `--input-bg` | `--input-focus-ring-color` | Amber, leading warning icon | text | `aria-invalid="false"`, `aria-describedby` → warning-id |
| `success` | `--input-border-success` | `--input-bg` | `--input-focus-ring-color` | Green, checkmark icon (auto-clears after 1500ms) | text | unchanged |
| `disabled` | `--input-border-default` (desaturated) | `--input-bg-disabled` | None | Tertiary text, no icon | `not-allowed` | `aria-disabled="true"`, `tabindex="-1"` |
| `read_only` | `--input-border-readonly` | `--input-bg-readonly` | `--input-focus-ring-color` (selection only) | Tertiary text, lock glyph optional | text | `aria-readonly="true"` |

**State-transition edge cases.**

- **Async validation race.** If a field is revalidated server-side while the user is still typing, the UI displays the latest server response; older in-flight results are discarded on newer request's success. During in-flight, the field shows a 12px spinner in the trailing-icon slot and retains its prior state (does not flicker to `default`).
- **Focus during error.** Border stays red; ring uses error-tinted opacity; ARIA announcement is rate-limited to once per 2s to avoid screen-reader spam while the user types corrections.
- **Disabled transition.** Disabling a field mid-interaction blurs it, clears any inline popover, and emits `input.disabled_midinteraction` telemetry (Appendix G). Focus is returned to the nearest enabled focusable sibling or form submit button.
- **Read-only + Success.** Allowed (e.g., server-computed field confirmed valid). Border is dashed; success glyph renders inside the read-only chrome.

### 3.6.4 Labels, Helper Text, and Counters {#3.6.4-labels-helper-text-counters}

**Label.** Every input MUST have a visible `<label>` element positioned above the control at `--input-label-gap`. Label typography: Caption (12px / weight 500 / `--color-text-primary`). Label wraps to two lines before truncating; truncation with ellipsis is rejected at review. Required fields append a non-breaking red asterisk (`*`, `--color-danger`) after the label text; the asterisk is `aria-hidden="true"` and the "required" semantics are carried on the input via `aria-required="true"` and an `aria-describedby` pointer to a visually hidden "required" affordance. Optional fields append "(optional)" in `--color-text-secondary` when the form surface has any required fields; otherwise the suffix is omitted (all fields optional → no suffix noise).

**Helper text.** Neutral descriptive copy — definition, format example, or scope — rendered below the control in `Body Small` (13px, `--color-text-secondary`) at `--input-helper-gap`. One line preferred; two lines maximum. Helper text MUST NOT duplicate the label or the placeholder. Helper text persists in all validation states; error/warning/success messages REPLACE helper text while the non-neutral state is active.

**Error text.** When `aria-invalid="true"`, the helper slot renders error copy in `--color-danger` with a leading 12px error glyph. Copy MUST follow the Failure / Reason / Recovery contract (§3.7.4). Screen-reader announcement fires once per distinct error message via `role="alert"` for synchronous errors (submit-time) or `aria-live="polite"` for async errors (onBlur revalidation).

**Warning text.** Non-blocking advisory; identical rendering to error text but in `--color-warning` with a warning glyph. Used for duplicate-requirement detection (§9.3.8), soft quota warnings, and signal-integrity advisories.

**Success text.** Optional confirmation after async validation pass. Auto-clears after 1500ms to reduce cognitive noise; the success border also fades to `--input-border-default`.

**Character counter.** When a field has a `maxLength` constraint from §39 Object Size Constraints, a trailing `N / MAX` counter renders in the helper slot, right-aligned. Counter turns `--color-warning` at 90% capacity and `--color-danger` at 100%. Counter uses `Caption` (12px) and is `aria-live="polite"` with a 3s debounce.

**Inline input affordances.**

- **Leading icon.** Semantic affix (e.g., magnifying glass for search, currency glyph for monetary). Icon color is `--color-text-tertiary` by default, `--color-accent` on focus.
- **Trailing icon.** Action affix (clear button, visibility toggle for password, spinner for async validation, validation glyph). The visible glyph follows component icon sizing; the interactive hit area follows the §38.6.2 per-tier touch-target minimum.
- **Prefix / suffix.** Non-interactive text affix (e.g., "https://", "USD", "@sourcera.com"). Rendered in `--color-text-secondary`; does not participate in the input's focus ring.
- **Clear button.** Appears only when the input has a non-empty value AND is focused or hovered. Keyboard accessible via Tab → Space/Enter; also bound to `Escape` when the input is focused (first Escape clears; second Escape blurs).

### 3.6.5 Grouping and Fieldsets {#3.6.5-grouping-and-fieldsets}

Forms with more than five fields MUST use `<fieldset>` elements with visible `<legend>` headings. Legend typography: Heading 2 (16px / 600 / `--color-text-primary`). Fieldsets separate with `--space-6` (24px) vertical gap; sibling fields within a fieldset use `--input-group-gap` (16px) or `--input-group-gap-dense` (12px) in Ops Console and inline-edit contexts. Conditional fields (revealed by a toggle or select) animate in at 150ms ease-out; `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` disables animation.

### 3.6.6 Accessibility Requirements {#3.6.6-accessibility-requirements}

1. Every input has a programmatic label via `<label htmlFor>` or `aria-labelledby`. Placeholder-as-label is rejected at lint (`no-placeholder-label` rule).
2. Color is never the sole carrier of state — every non-default state pairs with an icon and/or text.
3. Contrast ratios: label vs background ≥ 4.5:1; helper text vs background ≥ 4.5:1; border vs background ≥ 3:1 in all states; focus ring vs background ≥ 3:1.
4. Keyboard focus order matches DOM order, which matches visual order (left-to-right, top-to-bottom).
5. All validation messages are associated via `aria-describedby` and announced to assistive technology.
6. All interactive trailing-icon affordances have a dedicated `aria-label`.
7. Reduced-motion users experience instant state transitions.

### 3.6.7 Failure Modes (Counterfactual Pass) {#3.6.7-form-input-failure-modes}

| Failure Mode | Authored Handling |
| :---- | :---- |
| User pastes multiline content into a single-line input | Input strips `\r`, `\n`, `\t` on paste; emits toast "Line breaks removed — this field accepts a single line." for fields that were expected to be user-written rather than paste-safe (configurable per field via `accepts_multiline_paste` boolean in component spec). |
| Async validation dependency times out (>3s) | Field falls back to `default` state with spinner removed; trailing-icon slot renders a neutral info glyph; helper text: "Validation unavailable — you can submit and we'll verify on save." Server-side validation then owns the final check. |
| Concurrent edit conflict on inline-edit cell | Field reverts to server value; red border flashes for 1000ms; toast "This field was updated by [User] — your change was discarded." (see §3.5 rollback pattern). Offers "Apply mine anyway" link that re-submits with `If-Match` override. |
| Input receives characters that exceed `maxLength` during IME composition | IME composition allowed to complete; on commit, any excess is trimmed; counter re-renders; `input.max_length_trimmed_during_ime` telemetry emitted. |
| Screen reader user submits a form with pending async validation | Submit is gated until async validation completes; screen reader hears "Validating, please wait" via `aria-busy="true"` on the form; submit button re-enables on resolution. |
| Browser autofill inserts formatted data into plain fields | Inputs with server-side canonicalization (phone, date, currency) accept autofill; on blur the value is reformatted; the reformat emits a `success` transient state. |

### 3.6.8 Acceptance Criteria {#3.6.8-form-input-acceptance-criteria}

1. Every form control rendered by any console surface consumes the tokens in §3.6.1 — automated audit script `token_audit_inputs` (§50.17.4) reports zero violations against the deployed CSS bundle.
2. Focus ring renders only on `:focus-visible`; visual regression tests confirm no ring on mouse click across Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge latest.
3. `aria-invalid`, `aria-required`, `aria-readonly`, `aria-disabled`, and `aria-describedby` are present and correctly wired in 100% of DOM contract test coverage across components in the scope list above.
4. Label-vs-background contrast ratio measured at ≥ 4.5:1 in both Light and Dark modes for every tokenized input component, verified via automated Playwright + axe-core scan gated in CI.
5. Async validation with a 3s timeout falls back to `default` state plus neutral glyph plus helper "Validation unavailable…" copy; e2e test `async_validation_timeout_fallback` asserts this path.
6. Inline-edit concurrent-conflict rollback completes within 1000ms of server response; telemetry event `inline_edit_conflict_rollback` (Appendix G, §51) fires on every rollback.
7. Reduced-motion preference disables all 150ms input transitions; Playwright test with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` media emulation confirms instantaneous state changes.
8. Character counter turns red at 100% capacity; blocking submit when the value exceeds max is enforced both client-side (submit disabled) and server-side (API returns `validation_error` with `field`-specific code).
9. Paste of multiline content into a single-line input strips line breaks and emits the documented toast in 100% of e2e coverage.
10. The Figma-to-code token drift check (`ux_token_drift_check`) runs on every PR touching `app/styles/tokens.css` or the Tokens Studio export and fails on any divergence.

**Observability.** Every non-default state emits a PostHog event from the `ui_form_input` family (Appendix G): `ui_form_input_error_shown`, `ui_form_input_warning_shown`, `ui_form_input_success_shown`, `ui_form_input_disabled_midinteraction`, `ui_form_input_async_validation_timeout`, `ui_form_input_max_length_trimmed_during_ime`. All events carry `surface`, `form_id`, `field_id`, `validation_state`, `console`, `plan_tier`, and `user_role`.

## 3.7 Loading / Empty / Error State Catalog {#3.7-loading-empty-error-state-catalog}

**Purpose (C.110).** Every page surface in Sourcera renders one of five top-level states at any moment: `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `partial`, or `ready`. This section defines the catalog of state treatments per page type, the copy contract, the illustration rules, and the recovery CTA rules. Loading states use content-shaped skeletons; empty states name the next-best-action; errors follow the Failure / Reason / Recovery contract. The enum is `page_state_kind` (Appendix J).

**Scope.** Applies to: Buyer Dashboard, Buyer Workspace, Requirements Matrix, Scoring Matrix, Vendor Detail, Requirement Detail, Use Case Detail, Response Detail, Selection Report, Traceability Matrix, Seller Bid Dashboard, Bid Workspace, Bid Response Composer, Seller KB Browser, Seller KB Detail, Marketplace Listings Board, SellerOrgPage edit, SoftwarePage edit, Ops Console dashboards, Ops Console entity tables, Settings (Org, Workspace, User), Integrations, Billing, Audit Log. Page-type taxonomy: `dashboard` | `matrix` | `detail` | `settings` | `ops_console` | `knowledge_base` (enum `page_surface_kind`, Appendix J).

### 3.7.1 State Governance {#3.7.1-state-governance}

Each page component owns a state machine with transitions:

```
(mount) → loading → ready | empty | error | partial
loading → (no upward transition; loading is a leaf transient)
partial → ready | error
ready → loading (refetch) → ready
empty → loading (user action triggers data) → ready | empty
error → loading (retry) → ready | error
```

State changes are driven by the Convex subscription layer (§7.5) + a per-page state-manager hook. The state-manager hook MUST emit telemetry `ui_page_state_changed` (Appendix G, §51) on every transition, with `surface`, `page_surface_kind`, `from_state`, `to_state`, `latency_ms`, `console`. `partial` is emitted when at least one — but not all — top-level data panels have loaded; it is distinct from `ready` and must render skeletons in the not-yet-loaded panels.

**No-flash rule.** Skeletons MUST NOT render when the underlying data completes within 300ms (an "imperceptible delay"). Implementation: render skeleton via `setTimeout(show, 300)`; cancel on resolution. This prevents skeleton-flicker on warm caches.

### 3.7.2 Loading State Rules (Content-Shaped Skeletons) {#3.7.2-loading-state-rules}

1. **Shape-matching.** Skeletons mirror the geometry and information density of the resolved content. A DataTable skeleton is not a gray rectangle — it is row-skeletons with the correct number of columns, each column the correct width, with avatar bubbles where avatars will render.
2. **No spinners on primary content.** Spinners are reserved for button-internal progress (e.g., "Submitting…"), inline validation, and file-upload progress.
3. **Shimmer.** Skeletons animate a 1500ms linear gradient sweep. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` replaces shimmer with a static 15% opacity gray block.
4. **Max duration.** Each page type has a p95 loading-skeleton duration budget (see §3.7.6 catalog). Exceeding the budget escalates to `partial` or `error` with an informational banner and a manual Retry CTA.
5. **Preserve column widths.** Tables preload column widths from schema + last-viewed persisted widths (§38.7) to prevent layout shift on resolve.
6. **Progressive reveal.** Pages with independent data panels (Dashboard, Workspace Overview) render `partial` as panels resolve; do not block on the slowest panel.
7. **Cancellability.** Long-running loads (KB crawl, Policy Ingestion, Agent pre-scoring) render a Cancel CTA after 5s.

### 3.7.3 Empty State Rules (Next-Best-Action) {#3.7.3-empty-state-rules}

1. **Name the emptiness.** Headline in Display or Heading 1 (context-dependent), 1–6 words, factual ("No workspaces yet", "Your queue is clear", "No capabilities declared").
2. **Explain the next step.** Body copy, 1–2 sentences, explains what content *would* populate this surface and why.
3. **Offer the next-best-action.** Primary CTA labeled as a verb (`Create Workspace`, `Invite Teammates`, `Upload Document`, `Browse Marketplace`). The action enum `empty_state_next_best_action_kind` (Appendix J) values: `create` | `import` | `invite` | `browse` | `configure` | `contact_ops` | `none`. Every empty state MUST map to exactly one.
4. **Offer a secondary action when helpful.** Learning path (docs, demo video, template gallery). Never more than one secondary action.
5. **Illustration optional, rule-bound.** Illustrations used only when the surface is *aspirational* (marketplace-facing, onboarding). Never for routine empty states (empty queue, empty comment thread). See §3.7.5 illustration rules.
6. **No empty-state placeholders for ephemeral data.** Presence indicators, typing indicators, and live-cursor overlays do not render empty states; they simply do not render when no data exists.
7. **Permission-aware emptiness.** When the viewer lacks permission to populate the surface, the empty state substitutes the verb CTA with a `Request Access` link routed to the Org Admin via the §29 Inbox.

### 3.7.4 Error State Rules (Failure / Reason / Recovery) {#3.7.4-error-state-rules}

Every error state names three things, in order:

1. **Failure** — what happened, in plain language. NOT a technical code. ("We couldn't load this workspace.")
2. **Reason** — why, when known. If unknown, state that. ("A temporary network issue interrupted the request." | "The server returned an unexpected response; our team was notified.")
3. **Recovery** — what the user can do now. Every error MUST offer at least one recovery option from `error_recovery_kind` (Appendix J): `retry` | `reload` | `contact_support` | `change_input` | `wait` | `upgrade_plan` | `view_status` | `no_recovery`. The `no_recovery` value is reserved for terminal states (permanently deleted resource, permanently revoked permission) and always carries a "Return to [parent surface]" fallback link.

**Error copy style.**

- Second person, active voice, direct. ("You don't have permission to view this" not "Permission denied".)
- Never blame the user. Never use engineering jargon in user-facing copy.
- Always include the incident ID or request_id in a small monospace caption below the CTA for user-reported errors.
- Never expose raw stack traces or internal error names.

**Error persistence.**

- **Transient** errors (network, 5xx, rate-limit) auto-retry once on mount with exponential backoff, then surface the error card.
- **Permanent** errors (404, 403, 410) do not auto-retry.
- **Plan-gate** errors (402 / `feature_not_entitled`) are distinguished with a yellow banner (not red), primary CTA "Upgrade", secondary CTA "Request Upgrade from Billing Admin".

### 3.7.5 Illustration Rules {#3.7.5-illustration-rules}

| Context | Illustration | Weight | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Aspirational empty (Marketplace, first-run, onboarding) | Line illustration, 120×120px, `--color-accent` stroke | Sparingly | Uses the Sourcera line-art set (Ops-curated). |
| Routine empty (empty queue, empty comment thread) | None | Always | Copy-only. Prevents the UI from looking "always empty". |
| Error (404, 500, 403) | Line illustration, 96×96px, `--color-text-tertiary` stroke | Always | Single illustration per error type — do NOT vary illustrations per page type. |
| Loading | Never | — | Skeletons only. Illustrations on loading states are rejected at review. |
| Partial | Never | — | Skeletons in the not-yet-loaded panels; other panels render ready state. |
| Plan-gate | Line illustration, 96×96px, `--color-warning` stroke | Always | Paired with Upgrade CTA. |

All illustrations ship as SVG with `prefers-color-scheme` variants; the dark-mode variant re-tunes stroke color to preserve ≥ 4.5:1 contrast with the dark background (see §3.11).

### 3.7.6 Per-Surface Catalog {#3.7.6-per-surface-catalog}

For each page type, the catalog specifies the loading skeleton shape, the empty-state copy and primary CTA, and the canonical error treatments. The per-surface rows below MUST be honored by the corresponding `page_surface_kind` implementations.

#### 3.7.6.1 Dashboard Surfaces {#3.7.6.1-dashboard-surfaces}

Applies to: Buyer Dashboard, Seller Bid Dashboard, Ops Console Home.

| State | Treatment | Copy / CTA | Max Duration |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Loading | Panel-shaped skeletons: hero KPI row (4 cards), activity feed (6 rows), chart shell (280px high), queue widget (6 rows). Staggered shimmer so the first row animates first. | — | p95 800ms; 3s triggers Partial |
| Partial | Panels that have resolved render normally; pending panels keep skeletons; banner at top: "Some panels are still loading." Dismissible. | — | Indefinite; refetch via explicit user action |
| Empty (first-run, no data at all) | Hero illustration + "Welcome to Sourcera. Start your first workspace to see activity here." Primary CTA: `Create Workspace`. Secondary: `Browse Templates`. | `next_best_action = create` | — |
| Empty (data exists but filter yields none) | No illustration. Copy: "No activity matches your filters." Primary CTA: `Clear Filters`. | `next_best_action = none` | — |
| Error (5xx) | Full-page card: Failure "Your dashboard couldn't load." Reason "A temporary issue interrupted the request." Recovery: `Retry` (primary), `View Status Page` (secondary). Incident ID in caption. | `error_recovery_kind = retry` | Auto-retry once on mount |
| Error (403) | Full-page card: Failure "You don't have permission to view this dashboard." Reason "Your role was changed recently." Recovery: `Return to Home`, `Request Access`. | `error_recovery_kind = no_recovery` | — |
| Plan-gate (in-slot widget) | Per §3.7.4 plan-gate contract. Plan-gated widgets render their slot with a yellow upgrade tile (not red): headline "[Widget] is included on [tier]+", body cites §34.1 entitlement, primary CTA `Upgrade`, secondary CTA `Request Upgrade from Billing Admin` (routes a §29 Inbox item to every org member holding `billing_admin` per §5.x). Non-gated widgets render normally; the dashboard never blocks on a gated widget. Buyer Dashboard examples: Pulse health-metric drill-down widget (gated by `pulse_dashboard` entitlement per §34.8.5); Cohort Stakeholder widget (gated per §34.8.5). Solo plan suppresses gated widgets entirely per §44.6 (no upgrade tile renders on Solo; the slot is omitted). | `error_recovery_kind = upgrade_plan` | — |

| Error (410, resource permanently gone) | Same as 404 with additional line: "This resource was permanently removed on [date]. You can recover archived data from the Audit Log (§6.7)." | `error_recovery_kind = view_status` | — |

Triggered when the Convex query resolves with a `service_unavailable` / `internal_error` from Appendix I or when an Anthropic / Firecrawl / Perplexity downstream call surfaces a 5xx through a Convex action. Comment thread renders its own per-section 5xx if the body resolves but `internal_comment_thread` subscription faults. | `error_recovery_kind = retry` | Auto-retry once |
| Error (403, permission-denied) | Full-detail card replacing the body: Failure "You don't have permission to view this [requirement/vendor/use case/response/scenario]." Reason — when known — names the missing capability ("Vendor curation requires the `vendor_curator` role" / "This vendor is gated to verified buyers"). Recovery: `Return to [parent]` (primary), `Request Access` (secondary — routes a §29 Inbox item to the Workspace Owner or the Org `billing_admin` per the failure class). NEVER falls through to a 404 — the user is told the resource exists but is restricted, per §3.7.4 second-person-voice rule. | `error_recovery_kind = no_recovery` | — |
| Plan-gate (gated detail content) | In-page yellow banner replacing the gated panel slot only — the rest of the detail surface remains interactive: "[Capability] is included on [tier]+ per §34.1." Per §44.6, Solo plans suppress the gated panel entirely (no upgrade tile renders). | `error_recovery_kind = upgrade_plan` | — |

| D-SS-040 | PipelineSurface / Pipeline Step Tokens (UX §5.2.19, F-AE-030 / F-AE-031) | `dashboard` | Master Spec binds the component to Dashboard state handling; UX §5.2.19 owns the component-level skeleton, bridge-read error, retry, and per-step partial treatment; §3.14.4 invariants remain binding. |
| D-SS-041 | Solo Notification Suppression Rule (§29.3, F-AE-065) | `dashboard` / `ops_console` | Suppressed Solo notification events render no customer-visible loading, empty, or partial banner; each suppressed event writes an audit trace and an Ops-visible entry in §50 audit log; if the suppression audit write fails, the customer surface remains silent and Ops receives an error event. |

### 3.7.7 Copy Guidelines {#3.7.7-copy-guidelines}

1. **Length budget.** Empty-state headline ≤ 6 words; empty-state body ≤ 20 words; error headline ≤ 8 words; error reason ≤ 20 words; error recovery CTA labels ≤ 3 words.
2. **Verb discipline.** CTA labels are verbs or verb-noun pairs (`Retry`, `Create Workspace`, `Invite Teammates`), never vague nouns (`Options`, `Help`).
3. **No internal jargon.** Customer surfaces never say "SIM flagged", "DLQ overflow", "5xx", "token regression". Ops surfaces MAY use internal terms because the audience is Ops.
4. **Plurals.** Empty-state copy uses "No X yet" (singular subject, plural noun where grammatical), not "You have 0 X".
5. **Future-tense empties.** Empty-state body uses future tense for surfaces that will fill over time ("You'll see activity here as your team adds requirements"); present tense for always-empty-unless-configured surfaces ("Connect your CRM to see signals here").
6. **Incident IDs.** Error cards render the incident ID or `request_id` in a `Caption`-sized monospace caption, preceded by "Ref:" — e.g., "Ref: `req_01JAXM…`". Copy-to-clipboard on click.
7. **Status-page links.** Transient 5xx errors link to `https://status.sourcera.com` (or the resolved equivalent from §42.4 dependency config); link is opened in a new tab (`rel="noopener"`).

### 3.7.8 Recovery CTA Rules {#3.7.8-recovery-cta-rules}

| Recovery Kind | Default Label | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `retry` | Retry | Re-fires the failed request with the same parameters. Disabled for 1500ms after click (debounce). After three failed retries within 60s, label flips to `Contact Support` with a `contact_support` action. |
| `reload` | Refresh | Re-mounts the page / section. |
| `contact_support` | Contact Support | Opens §29.9 Support Widget (Zendesk-backed; available on every paid tier — Starter, Growth, Scale, Enterprise — per §34.1 cell **Support**). For Free tier, opens a mailto with `request_id` pre-filled. |
| `change_input` | Edit [field] | Returns focus to the offending field and scrolls into view. |
| `wait` | Check back in N minutes | Non-interactive message; paired with countdown where ETA is known (rate-limit reset, scheduled maintenance). |
| `upgrade_plan` | Upgrade | Opens the Billing → Plans surface, pre-filtered to the gating tier. |
| `view_status` | View Status | Opens the Sourcera status page in a new tab. |
| `no_recovery` | Return to [parent] | Navigates to the nearest non-error ancestor surface. |

Exactly one recovery kind is `primary` per error card; up to two `secondary` CTAs may be offered. A card MUST NOT render more than three total CTAs — if a triage requires more, the page escalates to a full-screen incident surface (§29.11).

### 3.7.9 Failure Modes (Counterfactual Pass) {#3.7.9-loading-empty-error-failure-modes}

| Failure Mode | Authored Handling |
| :---- | :---- |
| Skeleton never resolves (data source silently hangs) | Each page type has a hard timeout (per-surface catalog above). On timeout, transitions to `error` with `error_recovery_kind = retry` and Ref caption. Background telemetry `ui_page_state_timeout` emits with `page_surface_kind`, `timeout_ms`, `subscription_id`. |
| User triggers retry storm (spam-clicks Retry during outage) | Retry button debounce: 1500ms disable after click. After three retries within 60s, client caches the 5xx and prevents further retries for 60s; card updates to `Contact Support` recovery. Telemetry `ui_retry_storm_suppressed`. |
| Partial panel never resolves while others have | Page remains in `partial` with dismissible banner; after 30s, the pending panel renders its own `error` state inside the panel slot without failing the whole page. |
| Empty-state CTA is plan-gated but user clicks anyway | Click handler intercepts, emits `ui_empty_state_plan_gate_clicked`, opens the upgrade panel instead of the verb action. Prevents broken-link UX. |
| Offline-triggered empty state | When navigator.onLine = false AND the data is cache-miss, empty state is suppressed; an offline banner (§3.7.10) renders instead. Prevents misleading "No data" on a transient offline. |
| Dark-mode illustration contrast regression | CI visual regression suite tests all illustrations in both modes; any < 4.5:1 contrast fails the build. §3.11 parity rule enforcement. |
| Error copy leaks PII | Copy lint rule `no_pii_in_error_copy` scans all error-copy strings during build for email, phone, SSN patterns; fails build on match. |
| Long incident-ID caption wraps and breaks layout | Caption truncates to 12 chars + ellipsis with a tooltip showing the full ID and a copy button. |

### 3.7.10 Connectivity and Offline Signaling {#3.7.10-connectivity-offline-signaling}

When `navigator.onLine` flips to false, a sticky `--color-warning` banner renders at top of the viewport: "Offline. Changes you make will sync when you reconnect." The banner dismisses automatically on reconnect and emits a success toast: "Back online — syncing (N pending changes)." This banner is rendered by the global App Shell, not per-page, and suppresses per-page error states during the offline window.

### 3.7.11 Acceptance Criteria {#3.7.11-loading-empty-error-acceptance-criteria}

1. Every page surface documented above emits `ui_page_state_changed` on every state transition; zero missing transitions in e2e coverage.
2. Skeleton-first paint occurs in ≤ 100ms from navigation commit on all catalog surfaces; p95 measured by Real User Monitoring (RUM).
3. No-flash rule is honored: skeletons never render for loads that resolve in ≤ 300ms; Playwright + Chrome DevTools Protocol test `skeleton_no_flash_under_300ms` confirms.
4. Empty state primary CTA exists on 100% of non-permission-gated empty surfaces; audit script `empty_state_cta_coverage` reports 100%.
5. Error cards follow the Failure / Reason / Recovery contract; automated copy audit parses each error card and confirms all three present on 100% of error surfaces.
6. Every transient error auto-retries exactly once on mount before surfacing; e2e test `error_auto_retry_once` asserts this.
7. Plan-gate errors render a yellow banner (not red) with `Upgrade` primary CTA on 100% of gated surfaces.
8. Offline banner renders within 500ms of `navigator.onLine = false` and suppresses per-page error states while offline; e2e test `offline_banner_suppresses_errors` passes.
9. Dark-mode illustration contrast ratio ≥ 4.5:1 on all rendered illustrations; visual regression suite `dark_mode_illustration_contrast` passes.
10. Incident-ID captions copy-to-clipboard on click; clipboard contents exactly match the server-returned `request_id`.
11. Every Phase SS row in §3.7.6.7 has a `page_surface_kind` binding and at least one explicit clause for loading/error/retry, partial-completion, and permission / plan / Solo disposition where applicable. Verification script `phase_ss_surface_state_binding_coverage` asserts all D-SS-001 through D-SS-041 identifiers are present exactly once.

### 3.7.12 External-Target Clipboard Confirmation Pattern {#3.7.12-external-target-clipboard-confirmation-pattern}

**Authored Extension — flagged in RECONCILIATION.md (Phase 10 follow-up to §25.7.7 mobile copy-paste leakage clause).**

**Purpose.** Some surfaces render content that is firewall-restricted to a specific console or visibility scope (e.g., Internal Comment Posts §25.7, buyer-internal Selection Report drafts §10.13, internally-marked Q&A redlines). User-initiated copy-paste of such content into an external paste target is not a platform leakage by definition — the platform cannot block what the user types into the OS clipboard — but Sourcera SHOULD surface a pre-copy confirmation dialog so that the user is aware they are about to remove content from the firewall envelope. This section catalogs the confirmation dialog pattern and binds it to the firewall-protected surfaces that invoke it.

**Trigger heuristic.** The pre-copy confirmation dialog renders when **all** of the following are true at copy time:

1. The selection range is wholly contained within a firewall-protected surface (`internal_comment_post`, `selection_report_draft`, or any Convex-rendered region tagged with the `data-firewall-scope` DOM attribute set to `buyer_internal` or equivalent).
2. The detected paste target — derived from the browser's `clipboard.write` event handler against a heuristic registry — matches a known external app or non-Sourcera route. Heuristic registry includes: any URL not under `*.sourcera.com`; any seller-console route within Sourcera; any public Marketplace route; any third-party messaging or document app surfaced via the OS clipboard-target hint where available.
3. The user has not opted out of the confirmation in the same session via the dialog's "Don't ask again for this thread" checkbox (session-scoped, NOT persisted; per-thread).

**Dialog content.**

| Slot | Copy |
| :---- | :---- |
| Title | "Copy internal comment to external paste target?" |
| Body | "This content is buyer-internal. Pasting it into a non-Sourcera surface will move it outside the buyer firewall. Confirm before continuing." |
| Primary CTA | `Copy anyway` (`--color-warning`) — proceeds with the clipboard write |
| Secondary CTA | `Cancel` — aborts the copy operation |
| Tertiary control | Checkbox: "Don't ask again for this thread (this session only)" — session-scoped suppression |

**Behavior.**

1. Dialog is modal — backdrop click is a no-op (must use Cancel or Copy anyway).
2. Focus moves to `Cancel` on render (defensive default — the safer choice).
3. Escape key invokes Cancel.
4. The dialog NEVER blocks copy of non-firewall content; only the trigger heuristic above invokes it.
5. Audit event `firewall_protected_clipboard_copy_confirmed` (Appendix G) emits on Copy anyway with `surface`, `firewall_scope`, `target_heuristic_class`, `session_suppress_state`. No event emits on Cancel (avoid spamming audit on benign user reconsideration).
6. The clipboard write itself is performed by the platform — we do NOT modify or watermark the copied content. The dialog is a user-awareness affordance, not a DLP control.

**Mobile divergence.** The dialog renders as a bottom-sheet modal on mobile (per §38.6.2 mobile dialog conventions); the heuristic registry is the same; OS-level long-press copy menus that bypass the in-app handler MAY surface the dialog as a toast-with-undo if the platform clipboard event is observable post-write. If the OS does not surface a clipboard-write hook, the dialog cannot render on that surface; the audit event is omitted. This degradation is documented per §38.6.2.

**Reduced motion / High Contrast.** Inherits the §3.7.5 / §3.11.8 patterns: no animation under `prefers-reduced-motion`; bold border + 4.5:1 contrast on Copy anyway in High Contrast mode.

**Failure modes.**

| Failure Mode | Authored Handling |
| :---- | :---- |
| Browser does not expose a clipboard-write hook (Safari quirks, older WebKit) | Confirmation cannot render. Audit event is omitted. Documented in the surface's release notes. |
| Heuristic registry false-positive (paste target is a Sourcera buyer-console route mis-classified as external) | Conservative — the dialog renders; user's `Copy anyway` proceeds. Per-target false-positive rate is tracked via a Posthog-side review and tuned monthly per §50 Ops process. |
| User selects content that spans both firewall-protected and non-protected regions | Dialog renders if any portion of the selection is firewall-protected. The Copy anyway CTA copies the entire selection (we do not perform partial copies — that would silently truncate user intent). |
| User opts out via checkbox, then later targets a different external app | The session-scoped suppression is per-thread, NOT per-target. The dialog does not re-render for that thread within the session. Reset on tab-close. |

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. The dialog renders for firewall-protected surfaces (Internal Comment Post, Selection Report draft) when the paste target is heuristic-classified as external; Playwright `clipboard_external_target_dialog_renders` passes.
2. Cancel aborts the clipboard write; Copy anyway proceeds; audit event emits only on Copy anyway.
3. Session-scoped per-thread suppression honored within the same session; reset on tab-close; test `clipboard_dialog_session_suppression`.
4. Mobile bottom-sheet variant renders per §38.6.2; long-press copy that bypasses the hook gracefully omits the dialog and the audit event.
5. Dialog is keyboard-accessible: Escape cancels; default focus on Cancel; Tab order Cancel → Copy anyway → checkbox.

**Surfaces invoking this pattern.** Internal Comment Post (§25.7.7); Selection Report draft Redlines pane (§10.13); any surface tagged with `data-firewall-scope="buyer_internal"`. Future firewall-protected surfaces SHOULD declare their invocation in this catalog rather than re-author the pattern.

## 3.8 Side Peek Dimensions & Behavior {#3.8-side-peek-dimensions-and-behavior}

**Purpose (C.111).** The Side Peek is a right-anchored detail panel that opens in response to row-click or keyboard `Enter` on a parent list/table. It is the default "open detail without leaving list context" affordance across Sourcera. This section fixes the panel dimensions, open/close triggers, navigation keyboard bindings, persistence semantics, and edge-case handling.

**Scope.** Applies to every list or table surface that exposes an associated detail entity: Requirements Matrix (row → Requirement Detail), Vendor List (row → Vendor Detail), Triage Queue (row → Requirement Detail), Comment Inbox (row → Comment Thread), KB Browser (card → Entry Detail), Ops entity tables, Marketplace Listings (card → Seller/Software page preview). Excluded: the Command Palette (ships its own overlay), full-page detail surfaces accessed by URL navigation (e.g., `/buyer/workspaces/{id}/requirements/{id}` is a full page, not a Side Peek — the Side Peek is the Peek variant, URL-shareable via `?peek={requirement_id}`).

### 3.8.1 Dimensions {#3.8.1-side-peek-dimensions}

| Property | Value | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Default width | 480px | Authoritative default per C.111. Wider than UX Summary §3.1's legacy 420px; the 420px reference is superseded and flagged in RECONCILIATION.md for UX-source update. |
| Min width | 360px | Resize handle clamps at 360. Below 360, the panel auto-collapses and emits a warning toast: "Minimum 360px — peek restored to default." |
| Max width | 640px on `desktop` tier (1024 ≤ w < 1280); **720px on `desktop_xl` tier (≥ 1280)** | Resize handle clamps at the tier-appropriate upper bound. Rationale: on `desktop`, beyond 640 the parent list becomes too compressed to remain a context; on `desktop_xl` the extra horizontal budget supports a 720px Peek without list compression. Tier-appropriate bound is resolved at runtime from §38.6.2 and persisted per-tier in `UserUIPreference.side_peek_width_px_per_tier_json` (§38.6.3). |
| Resize step | 8px | Keyboard-driven resize (`Cmd+Alt+ArrowLeft` / `Cmd+Alt+ArrowRight`) adjusts in 8px increments. |
| Persisted preference | Per-user × per-surface | Stored in `UserPreferences.side_peek_widths_json` (§4.2 user-entity field); per-surface keys e.g. `requirements_matrix`, `vendor_list`. LRU cache of 30 most-recent keys; older surfaces revert to 480px default. |
| Mobile | Full-screen modal | Below 768px viewport, the Peek occupies 100% viewport width as a swipe-up modal (see §3.4 mobile translation). |
| Elevation | `shadow-3` (`--elevation-3`) | Matches Modal; distinct from Dropdown's `shadow-2`. |
| Z-index | 30 | Per UX §2.8. Below Dropdown, above Sticky and Sidebar. |
| Open animation | 200ms ease-in-out slide from right + 150ms fade | Reduced-motion disables slide; panel appears instantaneously. |
| Close animation | 150ms ease-in-out slide right + 150ms fade | Same reduced-motion rule. |

### 3.8.2 Open Triggers {#3.8.2-side-peek-open-triggers}

| Trigger | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| `Enter` on keyboard-focused row | Opens Peek for that row's entity. Focus MOVES into the Peek; first focusable element receives focus. |
| Row click | Opens Peek. Focus moves into the Peek on desktop; on touch devices, focus remains on the activated row to avoid mobile keyboard popups. |
| `Space` on keyboard-focused row | Does NOT open Peek. Space is reserved for row selection (bulk action, §3.10). |
| Cmd+Click row | Does NOT open Peek. Reserved for toggle-select in bulk-action mode. |
| `O` on keyboard-focused row | Opens Peek (alternate binding, documented in Appendix B Keyboard Shortcut Reference under "Table / List Navigation"). Cross-links to §3.8 from Appendix B. |
| Deep-link URL param `?peek={id}` | Opens Peek on page mount if the ID resolves to an entity that (a) is in the current list scope and (b) the viewer can read. Invalid IDs are silently ignored with a Toast: "That item isn't in your current view." |
| API: `openSidePeek(entityId, surface)` | Internal UI-state API called by higher-level commands (e.g., "Go to next unread comment"); same permission check as Enter/row-click. |

**First-focus rule.** On open, focus moves to the Peek's primary action (e.g., "Edit", "Score", "Respond") when one exists; otherwise to the Peek's close button. This preserves one-keystroke usability for the most common action.

### 3.8.3 Close Triggers {#3.8.3-side-peek-close-triggers}

| Trigger | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| `Escape` | Closes Peek. Focus RETURNS to the row that opened it (focus restoration). If the row was removed while Peek was open (e.g., deleted), focus returns to the parent list's primary CTA. |
| Close button click | Same as `Escape`. |
| Backdrop click | Desktop: NO backdrop (the parent list remains interactive). No effect. Mobile: backdrop click closes. |
| Navigation to another URL | Auto-closes. Peek state cleared from URL `?peek` param. |
| Browser back button | Auto-closes. Peek is a pushState entry; back pops it. |
| Row removed from underlying list (filter change, delete, phase change) | Peek remains open with a banner: "This row is no longer in the list. [Close]." Data continues to render for the still-valid entity; user decides when to close. |
| Entity deleted while Peek open | Peek transitions to its own error state per §3.7.6.3 (Detail 404). Close button remains accessible. |

### 3.8.4 Navigation Within the Peek {#3.8.4-side-peek-navigation}

The Peek supports prev / next entity navigation *without closing*. Enum `side_peek_navigation_direction` (Appendix J): `prev` | `next`.

| Binding | Direction | Scope |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `Cmd+[` (macOS) / `Ctrl+[` (Windows/Linux) | Prev | Current list's visible scope (respects filter and sort) |
| `Cmd+]` / `Ctrl+]` | Next | Same |
| UI prev/next chevron buttons in Peek header | Prev / Next | Same; buttons disabled at list bounds |
| `J` / `K` | Prev / Next inside Peek | Mirrors list-level `J`/`K` (C.114); rebinds only while Peek is focused so list-level `J`/`K` still works when the Peek is closed |

**Navigation semantics.**

- Navigation is scoped to the **filtered + sorted list** at the time of Peek open. A user sees the ordering they set.
- If the user changes the underlying list filter *while* the Peek is open, the navigation cursor rebinds to the new list; if the current entity is no longer in the new list, the cursor snaps to the nearest valid entity (by original sort position).
- At the first entity, `prev` is disabled (button grays out; `Cmd+[` no-ops with a single chirp of the system bell equivalent — a brief orange flash on the prev chevron, 200ms).
- At the last entity, `next` is disabled with the same chirp.
- Pagination: if navigation reaches the last item on the current page and a next page exists, the Peek auto-requests page N+1 and advances to its first row; a progress indicator in the Peek header shows "Loading next page…" with a cancel control.
- Permission-gated items in scope are skipped silently during navigation (e.g., a Requirement the viewer cannot read is removed from the nav cursor).

### 3.8.5 Peek Layout {#3.8.5-peek-layout}

The Peek is divided into: (1) sticky header, (2) scrollable body, (3) sticky footer.

| Region | Height | Content |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Header | 48px | Entity title (max 60 chars, truncating with tooltip), prev/next chevrons, close button (right-aligned), optional action menu (three-dot). |
| Body | Fluid | Scrollable. Contains metadata chips (assignee, status, phase, SLA), primary body (requirement text / vendor profile / response / etc.), tabbed sub-surfaces when applicable (Activity / Comments / History / Related). |
| Footer | 56px | Primary action (context-specific: Edit, Score, Respond, Resolve). Secondary action. Footer is sticky when body overflows. |

**Scroll preservation.** When the user navigates prev/next, body scroll resets to top. When the user navigates *back* to an entity previously visited in this Peek session, scroll restores to where the user left it (per-entity LRU of 10 most-recent scroll positions, session-scoped, not persisted across reloads).

**Resize.** A 4px-wide resize handle on the left edge of the Peek (hit target 8px). Hover: handle widens to 6px; cursor becomes `col-resize`. Drag resizes panel; keyboard resize via `Cmd+Alt+ArrowLeft`/`Cmd+Alt+ArrowRight` (documented in Appendix B).

**Shared URL.** On open, the URL updates to include `?peek={id}` via `pushState`. Sharing the URL opens the same Peek for a teammate with access. Sharing a URL with a Peek the recipient cannot read opens the list with a Toast: "You don't have access to that item." (Matches §3.7.6.3 detail-403 behavior.)

### 3.8.6 State Variants {#3.8.6-peek-state-variants}

| Peek State | Rendering |
| :---- | :---- |
| Loading | Per §3.7.6.3 Detail loading skeleton inside the Peek shell; header title and chevrons still render immediately from the list row's metadata. |
| Partial | Metadata and title render; body panels show panel-level skeletons. |
| Ready | Full render. |
| Empty | Peek never opens on an empty entity; an "empty" detail is an error (see next row). |
| Error (entity 404) | Peek shell remains; body renders per §3.7.6.3 404 card. Close button active; prev/next remain active so the user can skip past the missing entity. |
| Permission revoked mid-view | Peek body replaces with 403 card; header title is preserved (already-seen data); prev/next active. |

### 3.8.7 Failure Modes (Counterfactual Pass) {#3.8.7-side-peek-failure-modes}

| Failure Mode | Authored Handling |
| :---- | :---- |
| User opens Peek while list is paginating (race between Enter and next-page fetch) | Peek queues the open action; opens as soon as pagination resolves. During queue, the row is visually pressed (100ms) and a 12px spinner renders at the row's right edge. Timeout 3s → error Toast "Couldn't open. Try again." |
| User resizes Peek below 360px via keyboard auto-repeat | Panel clamps at 360 and emits a single Toast; subsequent keypresses are no-ops until value increases. |
| Peek is open when the user changes console (buyer → seller) | Peek auto-closes; console switch is a parent context change. Telemetry `ui_side_peek_auto_close_on_console_switch` emits. |
| Peek is open when the user's session expires | Peek renders §6.3 session-expired state; prev/next disabled; close returns to login with `return_to=<url-with-peek>` preserved. |
| Deep-link URL references a Peek ID that is in the list but filter hides it | URL-param handler restores the Peek AND temporarily relaxes the filter to include that ID's status (with a banner: "Showing this item outside your filter. [Restore filter]"). User can restore filter without closing Peek; restoring filter removes that row but Peek remains open with "not in list" banner (§3.8.3 row-removed behavior). |
| Two users concurrently update the same entity while Peek is open | Per §3.5 rollback pattern, the Peek body shows a banner "Updated by [User]. Refresh to see latest. [Refresh]". The user can choose to keep their local edits or refresh. |
| Peek is open and the parent list unmounts (navigation to unrelated page) | Peek auto-closes, `?peek` URL param clears, telemetry `ui_side_peek_auto_close_on_list_unmount` emits. |
| Screen reader navigation enters Peek while the parent list still reads rows | Focus-trap binding is active inside Peek; assistive technology stays in Peek until close. Aria-live polite region announces "Detail panel opened for [entity name]." |

### 3.8.8 Acceptance Criteria {#3.8.8-side-peek-acceptance-criteria}

1. Side Peek opens with default width 480px on first use; user-adjusted width persists per-surface per-user in `UserPreferences.side_peek_widths_json`.
2. Width is clamped to [360, 640]; attempts beyond either bound snap to the nearest bound and emit a single toast.
3. `Enter` and row-click both open the Peek; `Cmd+[` / `Cmd+]` navigate prev/next within the filtered-and-sorted list scope without closing the Peek.
4. `Escape` closes the Peek and returns keyboard focus to the opening row; if the row is gone, focus lands on the list's primary CTA.
5. Deep-link `?peek={id}` param opens the Peek on mount; invalid / unauthorized IDs fail gracefully with toast and no broken UI.
6. Navigation at list bounds (first/last entity) disables the respective button and emits a 200ms orange chirp on the chevron; no-op via keyboard.
7. Navigation auto-advances pages when reaching last-on-page if a next page exists; a loading indicator appears in the header during fetch.
8. Peek preserves per-entity scroll for the 10 most-recent entities this session.
9. Console switch while Peek is open auto-closes Peek; telemetry event emitted.
10. Playwright test `side_peek_prev_next_respects_filter_change` confirms cursor rebinds correctly when the parent list's filter changes.
11. Axe-core scan on open Peek yields zero WCAG 2.1 AA violations; focus-trap verified.
12. Visual regression: dark-mode Peek preserves `--elevation-3` with sufficient luminance contrast against dark background (see §3.11).

**Observability.** Events (Appendix G): `ui_side_peek_opened`, `ui_side_peek_closed`, `ui_side_peek_navigated` (with `direction`, `reached_bound: boolean`), `ui_side_peek_resized` (with `width_px`, `method: keyboard|mouse`), `ui_side_peek_auto_close_on_console_switch`, `ui_side_peek_auto_close_on_list_unmount`, `ui_side_peek_pagination_fetched`.

## 3.9 Cursor Presence Visualization {#3.9-cursor-presence-visualization}

**Purpose (C.112).** The Cursor Presence system renders live teammate cursors and editor-presence indicators on collaborative surfaces. It supports up to 8 concurrent cursors per surface, assigns distinct hues per session, fades idle cursors, and exposes off-screen teammate indicators at the viewport edges. Backed by the `PresenceRecord` entity (§4.3.14).

**Scope.** Applies to: Requirements Matrix, Scoring Matrix, Traceability Matrix, Requirement Detail body, Vendor Response editor, Comment composer, Selection Report editor, Bid Response editor, KB Entry editor (seller). Excluded: Ops Console (no cursor sharing across Ops surfaces — rationale: Ops roles work on independent tasks and cursor-share adds noise without collaboration value).

### 3.9.1 Cursor Rendering {#3.9.1-cursor-rendering}

| Property | Value | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Self cursor | Native OS cursor; no remote render | Never double-rendered. |
| Teammate cursor | 16×16 SVG pointer with 2px colored border | Rendered above content; pointer-events: none. |
| Color token | `PresenceRecord.color_token` (hue_1…hue_8) | Deterministically assigned per active session per C.112. |
| Label | Teammate initials (2 chars) in a 20×20 circular badge | Anchored bottom-right of the cursor pointer; shows on hover of cursor OR within 500ms of teammate's last mouse-move. |
| Tooltip | Full name + workspace role | Appears after 800ms hover over the cursor or initials badge. |
| Text caret (editor surfaces) | 2px vertical bar in teammate color | Anchored at the teammate's text-selection head. |
| Selection highlight | Teammate color at 20% fill alpha over their text selection | Rendered beneath content. |
| Typing indicator | "[Name] is typing…" rendered as a 12px Caption below the editor when any teammate's `PresenceRecord.typing_in_entity_ref` matches the surface's entity | Multiple typers aggregated: "Alex, Jordan +2 are typing…". Max 3 names; overflow as "+N". |

### 3.9.2 Hue Assignment and Collision Wrap {#3.9.2-hue-assignment-and-collision-wrap}

The 8-hue palette is defined in §38 Component Library / UX §2.2 as `presence_hue_1` through `presence_hue_8`. Hues are chosen for distinguishability under normal trichromatic vision AND for deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia (WCAG 1.4.1 color-not-sole-means is satisfied by pairing color with initials badges).

**Assignment algorithm.**

1. On PresenceRecord insertion, the client requests a hue assignment from the Convex Presence function.
2. The function inspects active PresenceRecords with the same `(org_id, workspace_id | bid_workspace_id)` scope and chooses the lowest-index hue not in use.
3. If all 8 hues are in use (9th or later concurrent session), the function wraps: the 9th user receives `hue_1`, the 10th `hue_2`, etc. Collision is documented in §4.3.14 `color_token` "wraps after 8 concurrent sessions." Clients render a "+N more" chip near the avatar stack when wrap is active.
4. Deassignment on session end frees the hue for the next arrival; existing users retain their hues (stable per session).

**Collision remediation.** When wrap occurs, the avatar stack (§38.12 PresenceAvatarStack) shows a "+N more" affordance; hovering reveals the full roster with hue indicators and a note: "Color palette reuses after 8 people."

### 3.9.3 Idle Fade and Disconnection {#3.9.3-idle-fade-and-disconnection}

| Trigger | Cursor Opacity | Text Caret | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `active` (< 3s since last heartbeat) | 100% | Solid | Default. |
| `active_idle` (3s ≤ heartbeat < 10s) | 80% | Solid | Near-continuous; no visible change for most users. |
| `idle` (heartbeat ≥ 10s AND < 30s) | 35% with 500ms fade transition | Hidden | Cursor dims to indicate teammate is not actively moving. |
| `disconnected` (heartbeat ≥ 30s AND < 60s) | Cursor removed | Hidden | Initials badge remains in the avatar stack at 50% opacity for up to 60s total; removed after 60s. |
| Evicted (> 60s) | Removed | Hidden | Full eviction from the avatar stack. |

Transitions animate with 500ms ease-out. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` replaces fade with immediate state change.

### 3.9.4 Off-Screen Viewport Indicators {#3.9.4-off-screen-viewport-indicators}

When a teammate's cursor is outside the current user's visible viewport, render a 24×24px indicator at the viewport edge pointing toward the teammate's position:

1. Compute the teammate's absolute position relative to the scrollable container.
2. Determine which edge (top, right, bottom, left, or corner) is nearest to the cursor.
3. Render an arrow indicator at the edge in the teammate's hue with their 2-char initials.
4. Click on the indicator scrolls the viewport to bring the cursor into view (200ms smooth scroll; reduced-motion replaces with instant jump).
5. Max 3 edge indicators per edge; overflow aggregates into a single "+N" indicator that opens a jumplist popover.

**Viewport-indicator activation rules.**

- Indicator renders only for cursors with `status = 'active'` or `active_idle`.
- Indicator suppressed while the current user is actively typing (to reduce peripheral noise); resumes within 500ms of the last keystroke.
- On a collaborative matrix, indicators are anchored to the teammate's `viewport_element_ref` (§4.3.14), not the raw cursor coordinates, when the surface is row/cell-based; this gives a more meaningful "they're looking at row 42" experience.

### 3.9.5 Mobile Divergence {#3.9.5-cursor-presence-mobile-divergence}

On mobile (`client_device_class` ∈ `{mobile_web, ios_app, android_app}`), cursors are not rendered (no mouse). Instead:

- Presence avatars render in the page header with online-status dots.
- Text carets DO render during editor sessions (shared doc), matching the desktop treatment.
- Viewport-indicator arrows are suppressed on mobile (viewports are too small for edge arrows to be useful); replaced with a bottom-sheet "Teammates" indicator that slides up on tap.

### 3.9.6 Cross-Console and Cross-Org Behavior {#3.9.6-cursor-presence-cross-console-cross-org}

1. **Buyer / Seller firewall.** PresenceRecords NEVER cross the console firewall (§7.2, §4.3.14). A buyer-console session is invisible to a seller-console session even for the same user. Cross-console leakage is a P0 defect.
2. **Guest cross-org.** A guest from Org B in an Org A workspace is visible to Org A teammates; Org A internal users are NOT visible to Org B guests (§4.3.14 Cross-Org Guest Presence rule).
3. **Console switch.** When a user switches console mid-session, their Presence record in the old console is evicted within 5s; the new console issues a new session_id and color_token.
4. **Ops impersonation.** Ops sessions impersonating an Org user do NOT render cursors in the impersonated Org's surfaces (rationale: impersonation is diagnostic, not collaborative). Instead, an "Ops reviewing this workspace" banner appears per §50.11.

### 3.9.7 Accessibility {#3.9.7-cursor-presence-accessibility}

1. Color is paired with initials; meeting WCAG 1.4.1.
2. Hue contrast against both light and dark backgrounds is audited at ≥ 3:1 for the cursor edge and ≥ 4.5:1 for the initials badge text.
3. Screen reader behavior: presence changes are announced via `aria-live="polite"` region: "Alex joined" / "Alex left". Rate-limited to one announcement per 2s to prevent spam.
4. Reduced motion disables all presence transitions.
5. Users can disable teammate-cursor rendering in User Settings → Accessibility (§37.4) via UserAccessibilityPreference.`show_teammate_cursors` (default: true). Presence avatars and typing indicators remain unless separately disabled.

### 3.9.8 Performance Budget {#3.9.8-cursor-presence-performance}

- Cursor position updates throttled at 50ms client-side and 100ms server-delivered; client interpolation smooths visually.
- Max rendered cursors per surface: 8 (matches hue palette).
- Rendering is GPU-composited (`transform: translate3d`) to avoid reflow.
- If the Convex Presence subscription exceeds 50 events/sec sustained, client degrades to update-every-250ms and emits `ui_cursor_presence_throttled` telemetry.

### 3.9.9 Failure Modes (Counterfactual Pass) {#3.9.9-cursor-presence-failure-modes}

| Failure Mode | Authored Handling |
| :---- | :---- |
| PresenceRecord heartbeat lags due to client tab backgrounding | After 10s without heartbeat, cursor transitions to `idle` fade; after 30s to `disconnected`. On tab refocus, client resumes heartbeats and cursor returns to `active`. |
| Hue palette exhausted (>8 concurrent sessions) | Wrap algorithm per §3.9.2. Avatar stack renders "+N more" with hover popover. |
| Convex Presence subscription disconnects | Client retries with exponential backoff; rendered cursors fade to `disconnected` state after 30s; banner at top of surface: "Reconnecting presence…"; reconnect within 30s is silent on success. |
| Teammate's browser crashes without clean disconnect | Same as lag → disconnected → eviction path. Eviction at 60s guarantees ghost cursors clear. |
| Cross-console firewall breach (buyer cursor leaking into seller console) | Server-side query filter on `(console, user_id)` rejects cross-console reads; client never receives the record. Defense-in-depth test `presence_firewall_isolation` runs on every PR. |
| User grants Ops impersonation and cursor renders to the impersonator's org | Impersonation sessions carry `is_ops_impersonation: true` on the PresenceRecord; client render filter excludes these records from rendered cursors; §50.11 banner replaces. |
| Reduced-motion user sees flickering presence during high-activity | Throttle to 250ms update cadence; fade transitions disabled entirely. |
| User's color hue assignment collides with the surface's semantic danger color (e.g., hue_4 too close to --color-danger) | Hue palette is curated to maintain ≥ 5 ΔE* distance from all semantic tokens; audit test `presence_hue_semantic_collision` runs on palette updates. |

### 3.9.10 Acceptance Criteria {#3.9.10-cursor-presence-acceptance-criteria}

1. Up to 8 concurrent teammate cursors render per surface; the 9th and later wrap to `hue_1` and later with "+N more" avatar stack affordance; Playwright test `presence_palette_wrap` confirms wrap semantics.
2. Hue assignment is deterministic per PresenceRecord session_id and stable across the session; unit test `presence_hue_stability` asserts.
3. Cursor fade transitions at 10s and 30s match §3.9.3 table; automated timer test asserts opacity changes at ± 200ms of the specified thresholds.
4. Off-screen viewport indicators render at the correct edge within ± 4px of the computed teammate position; visual regression asserts.
5. Console firewall test: a buyer-console session cursor is NEVER rendered in a seller-console session of the same user; Playwright `presence_console_firewall` passes.
6. Reduced-motion preference disables all cursor transitions; visual regression `presence_reduced_motion` passes.
7. Teammate-cursor rendering can be disabled in User Settings; when disabled, no cursor SVG renders and no performance overhead from presence updates (subscription remains for avatar stack + typing indicators).
8. Presence subscription disconnection renders cursors as `disconnected` within 30s; reconnect banner appears and clears within 30s on recovery.
9. Hue contrast against dark mode is ≥ 3:1 (edge), ≥ 4.5:1 (badge text); dark-mode parity test asserts.
10. Ops impersonation sessions do not render cursors in the impersonated Org's surfaces; §50.11 banner renders instead.

**Observability.** Events (Appendix G): `ui_cursor_presence_joined`, `ui_cursor_presence_left`, `ui_cursor_presence_palette_wrapped` (with `active_session_count`), `ui_cursor_presence_throttled` (with `events_per_sec`), `ui_cursor_presence_disconnected`, `ui_cursor_presence_reconnected`, `ui_cursor_presence_disabled_by_user`.
