**k-Anonymity Enforcement.** Every rendered metric carries an explicit per-metric signal count check against the §48.4.7 Market Intelligence tier / §48.6.4 M12 floor. Metrics below floor are either (a) aggregated into a coarser band until the floor is met, or (b) suppressed with placeholder text. Enforcement runs at generation time (rejects generation run if `minimum_signal_count_satisfied=false`) and at publish time (rejects publish if any rendered metric fails the audit). Runtime evaluation is additionally performed on every public render; a metric whose cohort shrunk below the floor post-publication (e.g., due to DSAR) triggers an immediate re-render with suppression and a `market_intel.k_anon_degradation` webhook.

**Residency Enforcement.** If `residency_region_scope != global`, the underlying signal cohort MUST be filtered at generation time to signals from Orgs in the specified region. A cross-region leak fails the generation run and emits `market_intel_residency_violation` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422). Reports published per-region may be discoverable globally but carry a `region:scope` hreflang meta tag.

**State Machine.** `page_publication_status`, with the added requirement that `editorial_review_status=approved` requires both Marketing and Finance sign-off timestamps non-null.

**Retention.** Published reports: platform-life, with archive after 8 quarters. Archived reports retain their URL with `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`; PDF download redirects to a "Report archived" landing page. DSAR: aggregates retain anonymized content; any PII that leaked into narrative text is subject to targeted redaction (Ops-driven) within 30 days.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Signal cohort below the §48.6.4 M12 floor at generation.** Generation aborts; Ops alerted; report skipped for the quarter (next quarter retry).
2. **DSAR reduces cohort post-publication.** `market_intel.k_anon_degradation` + re-render with coarser aggregation or suppression.
3. **Marketing and Finance reviewers disagree.** Page held in `revision_requested`; dual sign-off required before publish.
4. **Residency leak.** Generation-time check rejects; Ops paged; no report published for that region-period.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Publishing without both Marketing and Finance review timestamps MUST be rejected with `market_intel_dual_signoff_required` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409).
2. Any rendered metric with an audit row below `k_anon_floor` MUST fail the publish gate with `market_intel_k_anon_floor_not_met` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409).
3. Cross-region signal leak at generation MUST be detected and aborted; QA regression test asserts the check.
4. Reports older than 8 quarters MUST auto-transition to `archived` via nightly sweep.

### 4.4.16 HeatMapCell (Marketplace-Domain, Sourcera-Owned, Aggregated, Public) {#4.4.16-heatmapcell}

**Authoring Intent.** HeatMapCell represents a single aggregated demand cell for the Public Marketplace Heat Map per Summary C.71 / M13. Each cell is the intersection of `(category, region, industry, company_size_band, period)`. The §48.4.7 Aggregate-tier / §48.6.4 M13 k-anonymity floor is enforced. No vendor names ever appear on heat-map cells (aggregate demand only), so vendor opt-out is structurally inapplicable: HeatMapCell carries NO `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` field and the §4.4.8 `vendor_opt_out_scope_kind` enum is NOT extended with an inline sentinel value for this entity. The aggregate cell's k-anonymity floor, the `contributing_source_hash` SHA-256 redaction over contributing Workspace IDs, and the *Vendor-Identity-Free Aggregate Invariant* declared below together provide the firewall guarantee that no individual vendor identity is reconstructable from a cell. The §4.5.6 Marketplace-Domain Read/Render Contract therefore treats HeatMapCell as a vendor-identity-free render path — the Opt-Out Registry (§4.4.8) is NOT probed at render time, NOT stamped at refresh time, and NOT referenced by FK from this entity.

**D-2.2-042 remediation (v7.2.0-REM Phase 1, 2026-05-15; AE-V72REM-01).** Prior v7.1.0 wording on this entity stamped `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` "per uniform source-of-truth linkage, with a sentinel `scope_kind=not_applicable` record in the registry." That sentinel admission was structurally defective on three grounds: (1) the §4.4.8 `vendor_opt_out_scope_kind` enum is a closed set — `global | category | software | page_type | specific_page` (5 values) — and `not_applicable` is not a member; (2) admitting an inline sentinel in spec prose against a closed Appendix-J enum opens an enum-bound erosion gateway (a write-time validator coerced to admit one sentinel value can be coerced to admit arbitrary values, bypassing per-scope enforcement); (3) the field's stated purpose ("uniform source-of-truth linkage") is satisfied by the §4.4.8 entity-table reference in *Vendor Opt-Out Registry Source-of-Truth Rule* (§4.4 glossary) without a per-row stamp on aggregates that carry no vendor identity. The field is removed; the §4.4.8 enum closed-set is preserved verbatim; CI gate `enum_bound_no_inline_sentinel_admission` (§M.5 V72REM block) prohibits future re-introduction across all entities and all closed Appendix-J enums. Downstream containment: §4.7 Cross-Console Bridge `event_kind` enum (Appendix J `console_bridge_event_kind`) carries no HeatMap-domain event, so no Bridge payload-field redaction matrix row can carry the removed field; §27 Marketplace Discovery surfaces (§27.3 directory, §27.4 Match Score, §27.5 Featured slots, §27.9.x Seller Signals aggregation pipeline) consume HeatMapCell rows only via the §4.5.6 render contract that already redacts vendor identity at the cohort floor, and the §4.4.18 SellerSignal cascade (which DOES stamp `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` because CRM-Sync routing surfaces implicit vendor attribution) is unaffected — SellerSignal remains opt-out-bound and HeatMapCell does not.

**Vendor-Identity-Free Aggregate Invariant.** A spec entity is *vendor-identity-free* when (a) every public render path strips vendor identifiers prior to materialization, (b) the entity's data-model table carries no FK that resolves to a Seller Org, Seller User, SellerSoftware, SellerProfile, or any SellerOrgPage / SoftwarePage row, (c) a k-anonymity floor ≥ 5 prevents single-vendor identification by joint-distribution inversion, and (d) the §4.5.6 Marketplace-Domain Read/Render Contract registers the entity in its vendor-identity-free surface list. HeatMapCell satisfies all four predicates and is therefore exempt from Opt-Out Registry probing. Any future amendment introducing a vendor-identifying field, FK, or denormalized identifier on this entity MUST simultaneously add a `vendor_opt_out_ref_id` FK to §4.4.8 AND remove the entity from the §4.5.6 vendor-identity-free surface list AND add a §M.5 row enforcing the new opt-out coupling — the three together restore the firewall integrity. CI gate `enum_bound_no_inline_sentinel_admission` covers the inline-sentinel attack surface; the field-presence-on-vendor-identity-free-aggregate attack surface remains under §4.5.6 render contract authority.

**Scope:** Marketplace-domain, Sourcera-owned, public read.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `category_id` | UUID | FK → Marketplace Category (§4.4.7) | — |
| `region_code` | String | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 OR macro-region (`global`, `us`, `eu`, `apac`, `latam`, `mea`) | Stored as uppercase |
| `industry_code` | String | NAICS 2-digit or industry taxonomy slug | Coarse industry band to preserve k-anon |
| `company_size_band` | Enum | See Appendix J `heat_map_company_size_band`: `1-50`, `51-500`, `501-5000`, `5000+` | Coarsened size band |
| `period_start` | Date | ISO | Period inclusive |
| `period_end` | Date | ISO | Period inclusive; typical period = 14 days (matches `refresh_cadence_days`) |
| `signal_count` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Total contributing signals in the cell |
| `k_anon_floor` | Integer | §48.4.7 Aggregate tier / §48.6.4 M13 render-gate floor | Minimum signal count for Heat Map cell rendering |
| `k_anon_satisfied` | Boolean | Computed | `signal_count` meets `k_anon_floor` |
| `demand_index` | Decimal | 0.0–100.0; NULL when `k_anon_satisfied=false` | Normalized demand score |
| `demand_trend` | Enum | See Appendix J `heat_map_demand_trend`: `up`, `flat`, `down`, `insufficient_data` | Computed against prior period |
| `prior_period_signal_count` | Integer | ≥ 0; nullable | For trend computation |
| `contributing_source_hash` | String | SHA-256 hex; 64 chars | Hash of contributing Workspace IDs; used to verify derivation determinism without revealing identity |
| `last_refreshed_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | — |
| `refresh_cadence_days` | Integer | Default 14; range 7–60 | — |
| `next_scheduled_refresh_at` | Timestamp | Auto-computed | — |
| `publication_status` | Enum | `page_publication_status` (HeatMapCell subset post-D-2.2-042 remediation: `draft`, `published`, `archived` only — Heat Map has no editorial review gate; `suppressed_by_opt_out` is structurally unreachable per the Vendor-Identity-Free Aggregate Invariant authored above and is NOT a valid transition target for this entity; the shared-enum registration in the Appendix K *Page Publication Status* sub-section retains `suppressed_by_opt_out` for the seven sibling entities that DO probe the Opt-Out Registry) | Auto-published when `k_anon_satisfied=true` |
| `residency_region_scope` | Enum | `market_intel_residency_scope` | Governs which residency regions' signals contributed |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete |

**Indexes.** `(category_id, region_code, industry_code, company_size_band, period_start)` unique, `(next_scheduled_refresh_at)` partial, `(k_anon_satisfied, publication_status)`, `(residency_region_scope)`.

**Scope Isolation.** Public read. No `org_id`; no customer-side write. The heat map UI renders only cells with `k_anon_satisfied=true`; cells below floor render as "Insufficient data."

**k-Anonymity Enforcement.** At refresh, cells below the §48.4.7 Aggregate-tier / §48.6.4 M13 floor set `demand_index=null` and `demand_trend=insufficient_data`. Cells below floor remain in `published` status (for index continuity) but render suppressed on the public UI. Across-cell aggregation to next-coarser bands occurs only via a separate reporting surface; never inside this entity.

**Retention.** 24 months of cells retained in raw form. After 24 months, raw cells purged and replaced with quarterly roll-ups stored in MarketIntelligenceReport. DSAR: not applicable (no user-level data; aggregates only).

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Signal cohort shrinks below floor due to upstream opt-out cascade on contributing SellerSignals.** Cell transitions to `k_anon_satisfied=false`; `demand_index` nulled; UI renders suppressed. Note: the opt-out probe occurs at the §4.4.18 SellerSignal layer (which IS opt-out-bound and stamps `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` because CRM-Sync routing surfaces implicit vendor attribution per §4.4.18 Delivery Channel Semantics); HeatMapCell observes the cascade only as cohort-count shrinkage, never as a direct registry probe. The Vendor-Identity-Free Aggregate Invariant is preserved.
2. **Residency leakage.** Refresh worker's source filter guarantees signals are from the chosen region; anomaly detector checks cross-region leakage nightly.
3. **Stale cells (refresh worker outage).** Cells older than `2 × refresh_cadence_days` are flagged `stale=true` in a separate derived column (not in table; computed); UI shows a "data may be stale" banner.
4. **D-2.2-042 residual probe attempt.** Any future migration, backfill, or capability handler that attempts to write a `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` value (or any other vendor-identifying field) on a HeatMapCell row MUST be rejected by the entity's write-time schema validator with `heat_map_cell_vendor_identity_field_forbidden` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422) and the §M.5 CI gate `enum_bound_no_inline_sentinel_admission` MUST fail any spec PR that re-introduces an inline sentinel against the §4.4.8 `vendor_opt_out_scope_kind` closed enum. Together these close the enum-bound-erosion gateway.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. A cell with `signal_count < 10` MUST never expose `demand_index` via any public endpoint; serializer test enforces.
2. Cross-region leakage in contributing signal set MUST be detected and the refresh aborted with `heat_map_residency_violation` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).
3. Cells older than 24 months MUST be purged; nightly sweep enforces.
4. **D-2.2-042 remediation AC.** A POST or PATCH attempting to set any vendor-identifying field on a HeatMapCell row — including but not limited to `vendor_opt_out_honored_at`, `vendor_opt_out_ref_id`, `seller_org_id`, `seller_software_id`, `seller_user_id`, or any FK that resolves to a Seller-side entity — MUST be rejected with `heat_map_cell_vendor_identity_field_forbidden` (Appendix I; HTTP 422). The write-time validator is bound to a static field-allowlist generated from the §4.4.16 data-model table; allowlist drift is detected by CI gate `heat_map_cell_field_allowlist_drift_detect` (new; M02.3 wiring). QA test `heat_map_cell_vendor_identity_field_rejected` asserts.
5. **D-2.2-042 remediation AC.** The §4.4.8 `vendor_opt_out_scope_kind` Appendix-J enum closed-set MUST contain exactly the five values `global | category | software | page_type | specific_page` and MUST NOT contain `not_applicable`, `n/a`, `none`, or any other sentinel value. CI gate `enum_bound_no_inline_sentinel_admission` asserts; spec PRs that add a sentinel to the registered set or to any inline reference are blocked at lint time.

### 4.4.17 GhostBidImport (Console-Scoped, Seller) {#4.4.17-ghostbidimport}

**Authoring Intent.** GhostBidImport is the historical RFP ingestion record per Summary C.73 / M15. Sellers paste or upload historical RFP/response content to seed their Software- or Org-level KB via the `ghost_rfp_ingestion` capability. First import per Seller Org is free; subsequent imports bill as a standard AI operation per the Seller Pricing Strategy. Powers the seller's time-to-value by seeding KB content before any live bid arrives.

**Scope:** Console-scoped (Seller). Content lands in the target KB namespace as standard KB entries after parse + review.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID | FK → Organization | Seller's organization |
| `console` | Enum | `seller` (fixed) | — |
| `target_seller_software_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → SellerSoftware (§4.4.9) | Null → Org-level namespace |
| `target_kb_namespace_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → KB Namespace | Derived from target software/org |
| `import_type` | Enum | See Appendix J `ghost_bid_import_type`: `paste`, `upload_document`, `upload_zip` | — |
| `source_file_attachment_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable | Populated for upload types |
| `source_file_mime` | String | ≤ 128 chars; nullable | e.g., `application/pdf`, `application/zip` |
| `source_file_byte_size` | Integer | ≥ 0; bounded by §39 `GhostBidImport.source_file_byte_size` | Per-import file size cap |
| `raw_text` | Text | Bounded by §39 `GhostBidImport.raw_text` | Extracted raw text (pasted or OCR'd) |
| `parsed_qa_pairs_json` | JSON | Payload bounded by §39 `GhostBidImport.parsed_qa_pairs_json`; pair count bounded by §39 `GhostBidImport.parsed_qa_pairs` | Structured Q/A pairs produced by `ghost_rfp_ingestion` |
| `parsed_entry_count` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Number of KB entries produced |
| `import_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `ghost_bid_import_status`: `draft`, `parsing`, `parsed`, `review_pending`, `publishing`, `published`, `rejected`, `failed` | See state machine |
| `parse_capability_ref` | String | Enum: `ghost_rfp_ingestion` | — |
| `parse_capability_run_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → AI Operation ledger | Links to the AI operation |
| `is_first_import_free_for_org` | Boolean | Computed at creation | True iff no prior GhostBidImport in `published` state for this Org |
| `billing_ai_operation_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → AI Operation ledger | Populated on second+ import |
| `failure_reason` | String | 0–1000 chars; nullable | Populated when `import_status=failed` or `rejected` |
| `rejected_by_role` | Enum | See Appendix J `ghost_bid_import_rejected_by_role`: `seller_user`, `ops_moderation`, `content_validator`; nullable | Who rejected (if rejected) |
| `duplicate_of_import_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; self-FK | Populated when dedup sweep matches a prior import |
| `imported_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when `import_status=published` |
| `reviewed_by` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; Seller User ID | Reviewer |
| `reviewed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | — |
| `retention_tier` | Enum | `data_retention_tier`: `standard` | — |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Seller User ID | Creator |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Seller User ID | Last editor |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete |

**Indexes.** `(org_id, import_status, created_at)`, `(target_kb_namespace_id)`, `(duplicate_of_import_id)` partial, `(is_first_import_free_for_org)` partial (for Ops analytics).

**Scope Isolation.** Seller-console only. Buyer-console MUST return 404. Imports route exclusively into the owning Seller Org's KB namespaces; cross-Org namespace references rejected with `ghost_bid_import_cross_org_namespace` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).

**First-Import-Free Rule.** `is_first_import_free_for_org` is computed at creation time by checking `COUNT(*) WHERE org_id=? AND import_status='published' AND deleted_at IS NULL = 0`. If true, no AI Operation ledger entry is created; `billing_ai_operation_id` remains null. Concurrent imports racing for the first-free slot: the first to reach `published` wins; a later racing import flips `is_first_import_free_for_org=false` and creates its billing ledger entry retroactively (triggered by a post-publish reconciliation worker). Authored extension — flagged. Refund semantics follow §34.11 Outcome Resolver if the retroactive bill is disputed.

**State Machine (`import_status`).**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `draft` | Seller creates row | — | Upload/paste not yet finalized |
| `draft` | `parsing` | Seller submits for parse | `raw_text` non-empty OR `source_file_attachment_id` non-null | `ghost_rfp_ingestion` AI operation begins |
| `parsing` | `parsed` | `ghost_rfp_ingestion` returns success | `parsed_qa_pairs_json` populated; `parsed_entry_count > 0`; parsed-pair count within §39 `GhostBidImport.parsed_qa_pairs` | — |
| `parsing` | `failed` | `ghost_rfp_ingestion` returns failure | `failure_reason` populated | No billing (failure reversal per §34.11). Parser output above §39 `GhostBidImport.parsed_qa_pairs` fails with `ghost_bid_import_pair_count_exceeded`. |
| `parsed` | `review_pending` | Auto-advance | — | Seller reviewer required |
| `review_pending` | `publishing` | Reviewer approves | Reviewer holds `seller_kb_editor` role | Writes entries into KB namespace |
| `publishing` | `published` | KB write succeeds | All entries indexed | `imported_at` stamped; billing entry created if not first-import-free |
| `publishing` | `failed` | KB write fails | `failure_reason` populated | Partial writes rolled back |
| `review_pending` | `rejected` | Reviewer rejects | `rejected_by_role=seller_user` | Entries discarded |
| Any non-terminal | `rejected` | Content validator fires | `rejected_by_role=content_validator` | Per Summary §3.5 anti-spam controls |

**Retention & DSAR.**

- `raw_text` and `parsed_qa_pairs_json`: retained 90 days after `import_status=published`, then purged; KB entries produced remain for KB-entry retention (per KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4).
- Rejected or failed imports: purged 30 days after terminal state.
- DSAR: `raw_text` scanned for PII; any targeted user's PII redacted within 30 days.
- Residency: imports stored in the Seller Org's data region.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Parse fails due to malformed document.** `import_status=failed`; Outcome Resolver reverses billing; seller notified with remediation steps.
2. **Content validator flags spam/adversarial content.** `rejected_by_role=content_validator`; Org SIM (C.100) credited with a flag.
3. **Duplicate imports.** A dedup sweep (SHA-256 of normalized `raw_text`) sets `duplicate_of_import_id`; duplicates skip billing and auto-reject after 7 days if not superseded.
4. **Target namespace deleted mid-parse.** Parse job aborts; `import_status=failed` with `failure_reason='target_namespace_deleted'`.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Creating a GhostBidImport with `source_file_byte_size` above §39 `GhostBidImport.source_file_byte_size` MUST be rejected with `ghost_bid_import_file_too_large` (Appendix I; HTTP 413).
2. The first successful `published` import per Org MUST NOT produce an AI Operation billing record; second+ imports MUST.
3. Content validator rejection MUST be logged in audit with the triggering validator rule (per §3.5 anti-spam controls).
4. Duplicate dedup MUST be enforced server-side (SHA-256 of normalized `raw_text`); duplicates MUST NOT consume the first-import-free slot.
5. KB namespace write failures MUST roll back all entries atomically; partial KB state is disallowed.

### 4.4.18 SellerSignal (Platform-Scoped, Aggregated, Seller-Visible) {#4.4.18-sellersignal}

**Authoring Intent.** SellerSignal is the anonymized, aggregated buyer-intent record per Summary §6.17. Buyers opt in (off by default) to signal sharing; signals are stripped of all PII and aggregated to the §48.4.7 Signal-tier k-anonymity floor for the count gate AND a **distinctiveness gate** at `k_anon_effective_floor` (D-1.3-001 remediation, 2026-05-01) that suppresses cohorts whose joint distribution resolves to a buyer Org with probability ≥ 1/`k_anon_effective_floor`. Sellers consume signals via in-app Seller Dashboard, weekly digest, and CRM Sync. De-anonymization happens only when the buyer explicitly sends an EOI or direct invite (transitioning the signal to a one-off de-anonymization record tied to that EOI).

**Scope:** Platform-scoped (no `org_id` on the record; the aggregate is cross-Org). Distribution targets are Seller Orgs via a separate `SellerSignalDelivery` index (authored extension; deferred). Read access is gated by Seller plan entitlements (Growth tier and up); access-control check performed at the delivery layer, not on the signal rows.

| `region_code` | String | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 OR macro-region | Coarse region |
| `company_size_band` | Enum | `heat_map_company_size_band` | Reuses Heat Map bands |
| `timeline_band` | Enum | See Appendix J `seller_signal_timeline_band`: `urgent_0_30d`, `near_30_90d`, `mid_90_180d`, `long_180d_plus`, `exploratory_no_timeline` | — |

Default 10 for general-class signals; 20 for de-anonymization-related publication (`de_anonymized_eoi_id IS NOT NULL`); governed via C.97 Baseline Assumption Manager. |

Probability that the joint tuple `(industry_code, region_code, company_size_band, timeline_band, intent_strength)` resolves to a single buyer Org against the residency-region cohort population (the platform's authenticated-buyer corpus filtered to `residency_region_scope`). **Scope Isolation.** Sellers see only signals matching their Marketplace footprint (category and region configuration). Buyer identities MUST never appear in the signal row, regardless of k-anon; de-anonymization happens only via `de_anonymized_eoi_id` (which is the buyer's explicit, affirmative action). The Seller-facing API serializer excludes `signal_cohort_count` when `k_anon_satisfied=false` OR `distinctiveness_gate_satisfied=false` (returns `"insufficient_data"` marker instead). **D-1.3-001 remediation (2026-05-01):** the distinctiveness gate is enforced in series with the count gate — a row that satisfies `k_anon_floor` but fails the distinctiveness gate is suppressed at the delivery layer with `suppressed_reason=tuple_distinctiveness_threshold_exceeded` (new Appendix J value).

**Delivery Channel Semantics.**

- `in_app_dashboard`: rendered on Seller Dashboard widgets; subject to opt-out scrub at render.
- `weekly_digest`: dispatched via Loops.so weekly; per-seller aggregation respects seller's email preferences.
- `crm_sync`: pushed into the seller's CRM via Summary §6.18 CRM Sync; creates a "Prospect Category Interest" record type.

**De-Anonymization Flow.** When a buyer sends an EOI (§4.5.2) to a seller, a new row is created linking that specific buyer-Workspace-to-seller relationship. The aggregate SellerSignal row itself is NEVER mutated to reveal identity; instead, the EOI carries the buyer identity, and a pointer-only field (`de_anonymized_eoi_id` + `de_anonymized_target_seller_org_id` + `de_anonymized_at`) is populated to mark that the aggregate has now been partially disambiguated for one seller. Other sellers still see the anonymous aggregate.

**Retention & DSAR.**

- Raw aggregates retained 180 days, then anonymized further (signal_cohort_count rolled into Heat Map).
- DSAR: buyer identity was never present in the aggregate; DSAR on a contributing buyer triggers a recomputation with that buyer excluded. If the recompute drops the cell below k_anon_floor, the signal is suppressed immediately.
- Residency: aggregates computed per-region; cross-region aggregates flagged `residency_region_scope=global` and require explicit Ops approval before delivery.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Buyer revokes opt-in post-contribution.** Recompute sweep within 24 hours; signals that drop below `k_anon_floor` transition to `suppressed_reason=buyer_opt_out`.
2. **Cross-region leak.** Residency enforcement at generation; violation aborts the generation run.
3. **Stale signals delivered via weekly digest.** `expires_at` check gates delivery; expired signals not delivered.
4. **Aggregate inadvertently reveals one buyer** (cohort = 5 but geographic+industry+size bands are narrow enough to identify). **Resolved (D-1.3-001 remediation, 2026-05-01):** the *Distinctiveness Secondary Check* authored below runs on every signal generation, in series with the count gate. The check computes `tuple_distinctiveness_score` against the residency-region's authenticated-buyer corpus and suppresses cohorts whose joint distribution resolves to a single buyer Org with probability ≥ 1/`k_anon_effective_floor`. The pre-remediation deferred-Authored-Extension state is retired; the spec is now operative.

**Distinctiveness Secondary Check (D-1.3-001 remediation, 2026-05-01).**

The count gate `signal_cohort_count ≥ 5` is necessary but insufficient against re-identification. A cohort of 5 buyer Orgs in a sparse industry/region/size/timeline/intent tuple can re-identify if 4 of the 5 are publicly known to be inactive at signal time and the joint tuple is rare. This sub-block authors the secondary distinctiveness check that operates as the second gate in series with the count gate.

**Computation.** The `signal_distinctiveness_estimator_v1` job runs at signal-generation time (line `expires_at` definition computation). Inputs:

1. The aggregate's joint tuple `T = (industry_code, region_code, company_size_band, timeline_band, intent_strength)`.
2. The residency-region's authenticated-buyer corpus `B(residency_region_scope)` — the population of buyer Orgs that have ever produced authenticated activity in the relevant residency partition.
3. The signal-period buyer-Org distribution `D(T, period)` — the empirical conditional distribution of buyer Orgs producing intent matching `T` over the prior 90 days.

Output: `tuple_distinctiveness_score = max_orgi (count_orgi(T) / sum_org count_org(T))` — the maximum probability mass on any single buyer Org in the cohort. If the highest-probability buyer Org dominates the cohort, the cohort is "distinctive" and re-identifiable.

**Decision rule.**
- Compute `tuple_distinctiveness_score` on every signal at generation.
- Snapshot `distinctiveness_gate_floor_at_generation = k_anon_effective_floor` for reproducibility.
- Set `distinctiveness_gate_satisfied = (tuple_distinctiveness_score ≤ 1.0 / k_anon_effective_floor)`.
- A signal that satisfies the count gate (`k_anon_satisfied=true`) but fails the distinctiveness gate (`distinctiveness_gate_satisfied=false`) is written to the SellerSignal table with `suppressed_reason=tuple_distinctiveness_threshold_exceeded` and is **never delivered**. Sellers see no record of the suppressed cohort.
- A signal that fails both gates carries `suppressed_reason=k_anon_floor_not_met` (the count gate's reason wins under the precedence rule below).

**Suppressed-reason precedence rule.** When a signal fails multiple gates, the `suppressed_reason` enum value is selected per: `k_anon_floor_not_met` > `tuple_distinctiveness_threshold_exceeded` > `buyer_opt_out` > `residency_mismatch` > `vendor_opt_out` > `expired`. The earlier-listed reason wins. This rule prevents seller-side inference about which gate failed when a sophisticated seller could probe.

**Effective floor by signal class.** `k_anon_effective_floor` is set at row generation per the following class table (row defaults; override via C.97 Baseline Assumption Manager):

| Signal class | `k_anon_effective_floor` | Rationale |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Standard signal (`de_anonymized_eoi_id IS NULL`) | 10 | Distinctiveness gate at probability 0.10 — re-identification probability of 10% is the threshold for a privacy-respecting "noisy" signal. |
| De-anonymization-related publication (`de_anonymized_eoi_id IS NOT NULL`) | 20 | Distinctiveness gate at probability 0.05 — once a buyer has explicitly de-anonymized to one seller, the surrounding aggregate must be even less distinctive to prevent the buyer's identity leaking to other sellers via the residual aggregate. |

**Privacy-review-gated AE flag.** This remediation is registered as an Authored Extension in `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md` because the distinctiveness estimator's parameters (the corpus boundary `B(residency_region_scope)`, the prior-period window, the `k_anon_effective_floor` defaults) are operational tuning that requires Privacy Officer review before each parameter change. The CI gate `seller_signal_distinctiveness_check_active` (§M.5 — new) asserts the estimator is invoked on every signal generation; parameter changes outside the C.97 governance flow fail CI.

**Statistical-soundness contract.** The `signal_distinctiveness_estimator_v1` is governed by `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md` AE-D1.3-01. The estimator MUST satisfy: (a) recomputed on every signal generation; (b) deterministic given the same `(T, residency_region_scope, signal_period_start, signal_period_end)` inputs; (c) input populations sourced only from authenticated-buyer corpus rows; (d) output values stable to ±0.005 across re-runs within a 1-hour window; (e) periodic accuracy audit by Privacy Officer (≥ quarterly) sampling 1,000 generated rows against ground-truth manual cohort analysis with ≥ 95% agreement on suppression decisions.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. A signal below `k_anon_floor` MUST never deliver via any channel; the delivery layer enforces.
2. Buyer-identity information MUST never appear on a SellerSignal row; serializer test enforces.
3. **(D-1.3-001 remediation, 2026-05-01)** A signal with `tuple_distinctiveness_score > 1.0 / k_anon_effective_floor` MUST never deliver via any channel; the delivery layer enforces. QA test `seller_signal_distinctiveness_gate_enforced` asserts that synthetic distinctive cohorts (one dominant buyer Org) are suppressed and synthetic balanced cohorts pass.
4. **(D-1.3-001 remediation, 2026-05-01)** `distinctiveness_gate_satisfied`, `tuple_distinctiveness_score`, and `distinctiveness_gate_floor_at_generation` MUST be populated at signal generation; the `signal_distinctiveness_estimator_v1` job is invoked synchronously in the generation transaction. QA test `seller_signal_distinctiveness_estimator_invoked` asserts.
5. DSAR on a contributing buyer MUST trigger recomputation (count + distinctiveness) within 24 hours; audit event `seller_signal_recompute_dsar` emitted.
6. Cross-region signal leakage MUST abort generation and emit `seller_signal_residency_violation` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).
7. Expired signals MUST NOT be delivered; delivery attempts increment the `seller_signal_expired_delivery_blocked` metric.
8. **(D-1.3-001 remediation, 2026-05-01)** CI gate `seller_signal_distinctiveness_check_active` (§M.5 — new) asserts the estimator is invoked on every signal generation; deploy is blocked on red.
9. **(D-1.3-001 remediation, 2026-05-01)** The `suppressed_reason` precedence rule MUST be enforced when multiple gates fail; QA test `seller_signal_suppressed_reason_precedence` asserts on synthetic multi-gate-fail rows.
10. **(D-1.3-001 remediation, 2026-05-01)** Parameter changes to `k_anon_effective_floor` defaults, the corpus boundary, or the prior-period window MUST flow through C.97 Baseline Assumption Manager with Privacy Officer dual sign-off; out-of-band changes fail CI gate `seller_signal_distinctiveness_governance_flow_compliance`.

### 4.4.19 PromotedListing (Org-Scoped, Seller-Purchased, Platform-Attributed) {#4.4.19-promotedlisting}

**Authoring Intent.** PromotedListing is the keyword-targeted, category-scoped paid-placement record governed by §34.16.1 Marketplace Discovery Pricing and Appendix K `PromotedListing`. A Seller Org on the **Seller Scale** or **Seller Enterprise** plan (§34.1.2) purchases a category-capped slot that surfaces the seller's SellerSoftware (§4.4.9) at the top of `/marketplace/categories/:slug` (CategoryPage, §4.4.12) and in EOI-eligible Buyer Workspace search surfaces. Pricing is dual-metric (impression + qualified EOI acceptance) and cleared via a **second-price auction**. Inventory is accounting-isolated under the `rev_marketplace_discovery` cost center (§34.16) and MUST NOT consume AI Wallet value-dollars (§4.8.3); the billing line appears in the Admin Console Billing tab as a discrete SKU.

**Scope:** Org-scoped (`org_id` = Seller Org); cross-Org read: platform render paths only. Buyer Consoles never read the row directly — they consume a derived attribution-scrubbed projection (see *Cross-Console Projection Rule* below).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID | FK → Organization | Purchasing Seller Org |
| `console` | Enum | `seller` (fixed) | Identifies originating console |
| `seller_org_id` | UUID (FK) | Mirror of `org_id` | Retained for query ergonomics with SellerSoftware / SellerSignal joins; denormalized |
| `seller_software_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → SellerSoftware (§4.4.9); required; must belong to `seller_org_id` | The specific product promoted. Cross-Org references rejected with `promoted_listing_cross_org_software_ref` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422) |
| `category_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Marketplace Category (§4.4.7); required; state MUST be `active` at write | Category-scoped placement |
| `secondary_category_ids` | Array\[UUID\] | 0–2 entries; FK → Marketplace Category; each `active` | Optional expansion categories (still subject to per-category cap) |
| `keyword_targets` | Array\[String\] | 1–20 entries; each 2–40 chars, lowercased, `^[a-z0-9\- ]+$`; unique within array; canonicalized against `Controlled-Vocabulary Tag` (§4.5.5) where a matching tag exists | Buyer search terms that surface the listing. Free-form entries are allowed but deprecated in favor of Controlled Vocabulary |
| `placement_surfaces` | Array\[Enum\] | Subset of Appendix J `promoted_listing_placement_surface`: `category_page_top_slot`, `category_page_adjacent_rail`, `eoi_eligible_search_result`, `workspace_phase_4_vendor_discovery_surface` | Where the listing can render. The seller selects, and the auction resolves on each surface independently |

Bids above this cap return HTTP 400 `promoted_listing_bid_above_max`; the cap is not seller-configurable and has no per-category override in v7.1.1. |

**Indexes.**

- `(category_id, status, cleared_cpm_cents DESC, cleared_eoi_cents DESC)` — composite for auction render lookups.
- `(seller_org_id, billing_cycle_month, placement_mode)` — monthly-allotment enforcement.
- `(seller_org_id, status)` partial on `status IN ('active', 'paused_by_seller')` — seller analytics.
- `(category_id, status)` partial on `status = 'active'` — category cap enforcement; MUST be queried inside the eligibility-check transaction to observe current fill.
- `(vendor_opt_out_ref_id)` partial on `NOT NULL` — opt-out cascade.
- `(active_until)` partial on `active_until IS NOT NULL AND status = 'active'` — expiration sweeper.
- `(last_auction_run_at DESC)` — auction-fairness debugging.

**Scope Isolation.**

- Writes require seller-console session + role as above. Cross-Org writes rejected with HTTP 404 (non-leak) per §7.2 Dual-Console Firewall.
- Buyer-console reads return the *scrubbed projection* only: `{seller_software_id, category_id, ftc_disclosure_label, placement_surfaces[], active}`. All cost, bid, cap, and spend fields are excluded at the serializer layer. Raw reads by buyer-console sessions are rejected with `promoted_listing_cross_console_access` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 404).
- Ops Console reads are unrestricted.
- Marketplace public render paths read the scrubbed projection via the `CategoryPage` composition step; opt-out is evaluated at render time per §4.4.8 contracts.

**Eligibility Gate (Pre-Activation).**

Before `status` may transition from `draft` → `pending_eligibility_check` → `active`, the following MUST all hold. A failing check writes `eligibility_check_failed_reason` and transitions to `status = terminated_eligibility_lost`.

1. `org_id.plan_tier ∈ {seller_scale, seller_enterprise}` at snapshot time (§34.1.2).
2. `seller_software_id.claim_status = 'claim_verified'` (§4.4.9).
3. `seller_software_id`'s SoftwarePage (§4.4.11) exists with `publication_status = 'published'` OR `publication_status = 'pending_review'` with `editorial_review_status ∈ {'not_required', 'pending'}` — listings are allowed to go live against a `pending_review` page because the page is seller-authored content and the review gate is for Sourcera-owned pages only. Reviewer disagreement is handled at §4.4.11.
4. KB Health Score on the seller's Org namespace ≥ §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_kb_health_floor_default`; changes to the floor follow the §34.16.1.A governance cell.
5. At least one closed Bid Workspace (§4.4.1) in the prior 90 days with `status = 'won' OR 'lost' OR 'submitted_and_not_awarded'`.
6. `category_id.state = 'active'` (§4.4.7).
7. Current active listings in `category_id` count < §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_category_slot_cap`. If the cap is met, transition to `status = 'category_cap_exhausted'` with waitlist position recorded in `category_cap_snapshot.waitlist_position`.
8. For `placement_mode = 'included_allotment'`: `monthly_allotment_snapshot.consumed_this_month < included_this_month` at the moment of activation.
9. For `placement_mode = 'purchased_top_up'`: `monthly_allotment_snapshot.purchased_top_up_this_month` is less than the §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_purchased_top_up_hard_cap_per_month` value.
10. No active Vendor Opt-Out Record (§4.4.8) covering `(seller_org_id, category_id)` with `ops_review_status IN ('auto_honored', 'approved')`.

The eligibility check is executed transactionally against the indexes above; the composite `(category_id, status)` partial index is read with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` to prevent two concurrent activations racing past the category cap.

**Auction Mechanics (Second-Price Clearing).**

For each buyer-side render event on an eligible surface (CategoryPage, EOI-eligible search result, or Workspace Phase-3 vendor-curation surface), the platform runs a per-slot auction:

1. Filter active listings for the `(category_id, placement_surface)` tuple intersecting the buyer's query (keyword_targets ∩ buyer query tokens ≠ ∅ for keyword-gated surfaces; category match alone is sufficient for CategoryPage top-slot).
2. Exclude listings for which the buyer has hit `frequency_cap_config.max_impressions_per_buyer_per_category_per_rolling_window`.
3. Rank remaining listings by effective bid = `bid_impression_cents` (for CPM-priced surfaces) or `bid_eoi_cents` (for EOI-priced surfaces).
4. Winner = highest effective bid. **Cleared price** = second-highest effective bid + **1 cent** minimum increment. If only one qualified listing exists, cleared price = the listing's declared floor (min of `bid_impression_cents` and the auction surface's published reserve per §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_surface_reserve_cpm_cents`).
5. Cleared amount is posted at resolution time as a `MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord` (§4.8.12) with `sku='promoted_listing'`, `source_entity_type='promoted_listing'`, `source_entity_id = PromotedListing.id`, and `cost_center='rev_marketplace_discovery'`. `cleared_cpm_cents` and `cleared_eoi_cents` are updated with rolling-period medians (reported in seller analytics for price-discovery visibility).
6. If the cleared amount would cause `spend_to_date_cents + cleared_amount > daily_cap_cents`, the charge is clipped to the remaining cap and the listing transitions to `status = 'daily_cap_exhausted'` at UTC day close. Further wins the same UTC day are suppressed.
7. If the cleared amount exceeds `per_eoi_cap_cents` (for EOI-priced surfaces), the listing is skipped for that render event and the auction re-runs without it.
8. All auction decisions are logged to `PromotedListingAuctionRun` (§4.4.19.1) for fairness-audit reconstruction with `auction_run_id`, `eligible_listing_ids[]`, `winner_promoted_listing_id`, `cleared_price_cents`, `buyer_org_id_hash` (SHA-256 of buyer_org_id salted per-auction; never reverse-resolvable without Ops key material).

**k-Anonymity Enforcement (§34.16.1 / §27.11.2 requirement).**

Impression attributions written to `impression_count` MUST be buffered until the contributing buyer-cohort count reaches k=5. Before buffer flush:

- Attribution increments are staged in a Redis-backed bucket keyed by `(promoted_listing_id, hour_bucket)` with an ephemeral `buyer_org_id` set.
- When the distinct `buyer_org_id` count in the bucket reaches 5, the bucket is flushed: `impression_count += bucket_size` and the `buyer_org_id` set is hashed and discarded.
- If a bucket does not reach k=5 within **24 hours**, the unattributed observations are counted in `k_anon_failed_attribution_count` and the bucket is purged without attribution.
- Buyer-level identification MUST NEVER appear in the row or any downstream analytics; serializer tests enforce. EOI acceptance attribution is a distinct path: EOI acceptances are inherently non-anonymous between buyer and seller (that is the point of the EOI) and are attributed 1:1 under §4.5.8.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `draft` | Seller creates | Role check | All auction fields may be edited |
| `draft` | `pending_eligibility_check` | Seller requests activation | Required fields populated (keyword_targets, bids, caps) | Eligibility worker picks up |
| `pending_eligibility_check` | `active` | Eligibility gate (all 10 rules) passes | All snapshots written; category-cap `SELECT FOR UPDATE` acquired | Listing enters auction pool |
| `pending_eligibility_check` | `terminated_eligibility_lost` | Any eligibility rule fails | `eligibility_check_failed_reason` populated | Non-recoverable for this row; seller creates a new row |
| `active` | `paused_by_seller` | Seller PATCH | — | Inventory returns to category cap; billing cycle allotment debit is NOT refunded for `included_allotment` mode |
| `paused_by_seller` | `active` | Seller PATCH | Re-run eligibility gate; all rules must still pass | Allotment already debited; no double-debit |
| `active` | `paused_by_ops` | Ops action | `ops_pause_reason` required | Listing removed from auction pool |
| `paused_by_ops` | `active` | Ops action | — | — |
| `paused_by_ops` | `terminated_eligibility_lost` | Ops action | — | Terminal |
| `active` | `daily_cap_exhausted` | `spend_to_date_cents` reaches `daily_cap_cents` (day-window rolling at UTC midnight) | Auction suppression | Auto-reset at UTC midnight → `active` |
| `daily_cap_exhausted` | `active` | UTC midnight rollover | Eligibility still holds | Auto |
| `active` | `monthly_allotment_exhausted` | For `included_allotment`: allotment debit exceeds plan allowance (should not occur if pre-check is honored; defense in depth) | — | Re-evaluated on `billing_cycle_month` rollover |
| `monthly_allotment_exhausted` | `active` | Billing-cycle rollover | Eligibility still holds | Auto |
| `active` | `category_cap_exhausted` | Concurrent listing activated in same category pushing count > cap (should not occur with `SELECT FOR UPDATE`; defense in depth) | — | — |
| `active` | `frequency_cap_exhausted` | Cap configured with `0` max and immediate exhaustion — operationally rare; reserved | — | — |
| `active` | `exhausted` | `active_until` reached AND seller declines renewal | — | Terminal |
| `active` | `expired` | `active_until` reached AND no seller decision | — | Terminal |
| `active` | `terminated_eligibility_lost` | Nightly eligibility re-check fails (plan downgrade, KB health decline, closed-bid 90d window lapses, vendor opt-out cascade, category deprecation, SellerSoftware unpublished, claim revoked) | `eligibility_check_failed_reason` populated | Terminal; seller notified via `promoted_listing.eligibility_lost` webhook (§31.13 / Appendix C) |

**Cross-Console Projection Rule.**

Buyer-console reads and public-Marketplace render reads return the scrubbed projection:

```
{
  "listing_id": "<id>",
  "seller_software_id": "<id>",
  "category_id": "<id>",
  "placement_surfaces": ["category_page_top_slot"],
  "ftc_disclosure_label": "Promoted",
  "active": true
}
```

All cost, bid, cap, spend, and auction fields are excluded. A serializer unit test MUST assert that no projection of this entity ever emits any of the excluded fields to any console other than the originating Seller Console or Ops. The scrubbed projection MUST be used by CategoryPage composition at §4.4.12 and §26.7.2.

**Accounting Isolation.**

PromotedListing charges are posted to `rev_marketplace_discovery` cost center (§34.16 / §4.8.12) and MUST NOT post to AI Wallet (§4.8.3) or AIOperation (§4.8.1) ledgers. Cost-base margin analysis at §34.3.3 excludes PromotedListing revenue. Finance dashboards report `rev_marketplace_discovery` independently of AI margins.

**Retention & DSAR.**

- **Retention.** Listing rows: life of Seller Org + 7 years (financial record retention alignment per §40.2 with Buyer Referral / Pro Trial Seat precedent). Terminal-state rows read-only after 90 days. `PromotedListingAuctionRun` (§4.4.19.1): 24 months raw, then rolled into quarterly auction-fairness aggregates.
- **DSAR.** No buyer-identity fields on the row (k-anon enforcement above). Seller-side `created_by` / `updated_by` pseudonymized on seller-user deprovisioning within 30 days. Financial fields retained unaltered under the §6.8.5 financial-record retained-row classes.
- **Residency.** Listing inherits `data_residency_region` from Seller Org (§4.4.9); rendered only on surfaces matching the *buyer's* residency per §4.4.15 / §4.4.16 cross-region rules. Global (category-universal) renders honor the most restrictive of buyer and seller regions.
- **GDPR anonymization.** Not applicable at the listing level (no personal data). EOI Acceptance Records (§4.5.8) attributed to a listing carry their own DSAR path; on buyer DSAR, the acceptance's `origin_attribution_ref` is severed but the listing's `eoi_acceptance_count` is NOT decremented (counts are aggregate; breaking would enable inference).

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Two sellers race to fill the last slot in a category.** Resolution: `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the `(category_id, status)` partial index inside the activation transaction; the losing seller transitions to `category_cap_exhausted` with waitlist position. PostgreSQL's default READ COMMITTED isolation is insufficient; the activation worker runs under SERIALIZABLE.
2. **Cleared price exceeds `per_eoi_cap_cents` on a runaway auction spike.** Resolution: per-EOI cap clip at charge time; listing is skipped for the render event and auction re-runs without it; suppression logged to `PromotedListingAuctionRun` (§4.4.19.1).
3. **Impression attribution leaks buyer identity through a narrow cohort.** Resolution: k=5 bucket with 24-hour flush TTL; below-k observations counted in `k_anon_failed_attribution_count` but never attributed. Distinctiveness secondary check (as in §4.4.18) MAY be applied if a configurable narrowness threshold fires — Authored Extension deferred pending Privacy review.
4. **Mid-cycle plan downgrade.** Seller downgrades from Scale to Growth mid-month. Nightly eligibility re-check fires; active listings transition to `terminated_eligibility_lost` with `plan_tier_below_scale`. Allotment debits already applied are not refunded (pool-accounting precedent from §4.3.17 Pro Trial Seat Grant). In-flight charges within the current UTC day continue to clear through end-of-day to avoid spurious billing inversions; subsequent days are suppressed.
5. **Vendor opt-out filed mid-flight.** `vendor_opt_out.applied` webhook (§4.4.8) fires → cascading sweeper flags matching listings → listings transition to `paused_by_ops` (not `terminated_eligibility_lost`, so the seller can revoke the opt-out and resume). 15-minute SLO per §4.4.8 cache-bust rule.
6. **Second-price auction with only one bidder.** Cleared price defaults to the listing's declared floor (min of `bid_impression_cents` and published reserve). Prevents degenerate $0.00 clears.
7. **SoftwarePage unpublished after listing activation (e.g., page fails editorial review post-activation).** Nightly eligibility re-check transitions listing to `terminated_eligibility_lost`; unless the page transitions back to `published` within a 72-hour grace window, the row is terminal. The 72-hour grace is Authored Extension — flagged.
8. **Auction-run log DLQ overflow.** `PromotedListingAuctionRun` (§4.4.19.1) writes are append-only; if the primary write fails, the auction still resolves and charges but a `write_status='shadow_queued'` shadow record is logged to the secondary incident queue for retroactive reconstruction. Ops is paged if the queue depth exceeds 1,000 rows.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Creating a PromotedListing with `org_id.plan_tier ∉ {seller_scale, seller_enterprise}` MUST be rejected with error `promoted_listing_plan_tier_below_scale` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403). The error body MUST include the upgrade path.
2. Activating a PromotedListing in a category where the active-listing count already equals §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_category_slot_cap` MUST transition to `status = 'category_cap_exhausted'` and MUST write `category_cap_snapshot.waitlist_position`; the activation transaction MUST run under SERIALIZABLE isolation with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on `(category_id, status)` — asserted by a concurrency integration test that runs an oversubscribed activation batch and observes successes equal to the category-slot cap.
3. Impression attribution MUST buffer writes until the buyer-cohort count reaches k=5; serializer tests MUST assert that `impression_count` never increments below k=5 distinct buyer Orgs. Below-k observations MUST appear in `k_anon_failed_attribution_count` within the same 24h bucket TTL.
4. Buyer-console GET of a PromotedListing MUST return `promoted_listing_cross_console_access` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 404) — never a 403 — and the scrubbed projection is the only read-path available to buyer surfaces. Audit entry `firewall_violation_scope = seller_promoted_listing` (new; Appendix J) is written per §4.6.
5. Auction resolution MUST use second-price clearing with minimum increment = **$0.01**. For any auction with exactly one qualified listing, the cleared price MUST equal the listing's declared floor (≥ published reserve). A property-based test of 10,000 randomized auctions MUST show zero instances of first-price clearing.
6. The `rev_marketplace_discovery` ledger MUST post PromotedListing charges as discrete `MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord` (§4.8.12) line items keyed to the source PromotedListing via `source_entity_type='promoted_listing'` and `source_entity_id = PromotedListing.id`; no PromotedListing charge MUST EVER appear in AI Wallet (§4.8.3) or AIOperation (§4.8.1) ledgers. A nightly reconciliation job sums those rows by PromotedListing and billing cycle and compares them to `spend_to_date_cents` with zero tolerance for mismatch.
7. Vendor opt-out applied to a category MUST cause active PromotedListings for that (seller, category) tuple to transition to `paused_by_ops` within 15 minutes of the `vendor_opt_out.applied` webhook fire, observable via the `promoted_listing.eligibility_lost` or `promoted_listing.paused_by_opt_out` webhook fan-out (§31.13 / Appendix C).
8. The `ftc_disclosure_label` field value MUST render on every public surface; a DOM contract test on CategoryPage (§4.4.12) and every EOI-eligible search surface asserts the "Promoted" label is present within the rendered slot with WCAG 2.1 AA contrast on the accompanying tooltip.
9. `daily_cap_cents` enforcement MUST clip the final charge of the UTC day to exactly the remaining cap amount; overspend MUST NOT exceed **$0.00** (no tolerance). The clipping test runs at the charge path before ledger write.
10. `monthly_allotment_snapshot.purchased_top_up_this_month` exceeding §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_purchased_top_up_hard_cap_per_month` MUST be rejected with `promoted_listing_monthly_top_up_cap_exceeded` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403).
11. Every auction resolution attempt MUST write exactly one `PromotedListingAuctionRun` (§4.4.19.1) row, including no-fill, cap-skipped, and rerun outcomes. QA test `promoted_listing_auction_run_exactly_once` asserts idempotent creation by `decision_payload_hash`, and incident test `promoted_listing_auction_run_shadow_queue_reconciliation` asserts failed primary writes reconcile from `shadow_queued` to `reconciled`.

#### 4.4.19.1 PromotedListingAuctionRun (Platform-Internal, Auction-Decision Audit Log) {#4.4.19.1-promotedlistingauctionrun}

**Authoring Intent.** PromotedListingAuctionRun is the append-only, platform-internal auction-decision record for §4.4.19 PromotedListing second-price clearing. It exists so Engineering, Finance, and Ops can reconstruct why a listing won, lost, skipped, or reran without exposing buyer identity or raw bid/cost fields to buyer or seller consoles. It is not a customer-facing object and does not create revenue by itself; any charge is posted separately to `MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord` (§4.8.12).

**Scope.** Platform-internal, marketplace-domain audit row. No buyer-console read path exists. Seller-console users see only aggregate reporting derived from rolled-up auction metrics; raw eligible-list arrays, buyer hashes, and runner-up bids are Ops-only.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Also called `auction_run_id` in logs and tests |
| `console` | Enum | See Appendix J `promoted_listing_auction_run_console_scope`: `platform_internal` | Fixed scope marker; not a user console |
| `category_id` | UUID (FK) | FK -> Marketplace Category (§4.4.7); required | Auction category |
| `placement_surface` | Enum | Appendix J `promoted_listing_placement_surface`; required | Surface whose render triggered the auction |
| `auction_metric` | Enum | See Appendix J `promoted_listing_auction_metric`: `cpm`, `eoi` | Determines whether bids read `bid_impression_cents` or `bid_eoi_cents` |
| `auction_at` | Timestamp | UTC; immutable | Decision time |
| `render_context_id` | UUID | Nullable | Optional link to the marketplace render / Usage Event context; not buyer-visible |
| `buyer_org_id_hash` | String | 64 hex chars; SHA-256 of buyer Org ID salted per auction | Never stores raw buyer Org ID. Salt material is held only in Ops key material and is not persisted on this row |
| `buyer_org_hash_salt_version` | String | ≤ 40 chars | Key-version pointer for rotation/audit; not the salt |
| `eligible_listing_ids` | Array[UUID] | 0-50 entries; FK -> PromotedListing (§4.4.19); immutable | Listings considered after eligibility, frequency-cap, opt-out, and category filters |
| `eligible_listing_count` | Integer | Must equal `eligible_listing_ids.length` | Query convenience and tamper check |
| `winner_promoted_listing_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK -> PromotedListing; if non-null MUST be a member of `eligible_listing_ids` | Null for no-fill / all-skipped outcomes |
| `winner_seller_org_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK -> Organization | Denormalized from winner listing for Ops reporting |
| `runner_up_promoted_listing_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK -> PromotedListing; if non-null MUST be a member of `eligible_listing_ids` and differ from winner | Drives second-price reconstruction |
| `winning_bid_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0; nullable when no winner | Winning effective bid used by the auction engine |
| `runner_up_bid_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0; nullable when no runner-up | Second-highest effective bid; null for single-bidder floor / no-fill |
| `reserve_floor_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Reserve floor from §34.16.1.A for the surface and metric |
| `cleared_price_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0; nullable when no charge | Cleared second price, single-bidder floor, or clipped charge before daily-cap application |
| `auction_outcome` | Enum | See Appendix J `promoted_listing_auction_outcome`: `winner_selected`, `single_bidder_floor`, `no_eligible_listing`, `skipped_by_cap`, `rerun_after_cap_skip`, `shadow_recorded` | Outcome after all filters and reruns |
| `suppression_reason` | Enum | Nullable; See Appendix J `promoted_listing_auction_suppression_reason`: `daily_cap_exhausted`, `per_eoi_cap_exceeded`, `frequency_cap_exhausted`, `vendor_opt_out_active`, `category_inactive`, `no_keyword_match`, `below_k_anonymity_floor` | Populated when `auction_outcome` is not `winner_selected` or `single_bidder_floor` |
| `decision_payload_hash` | String | 64 hex chars; unique | SHA-256 over canonicalized inputs and engine version. Idempotency key for exactly-once auction-run logging |
| `auction_engine_version` | String | ≤ 40 chars; required | Semantic version or deploy SHA of the auction engine |
| `write_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `promoted_listing_auction_run_write_status`: `recorded`, `shadow_queued`, `reconciled`, `rolled_up` | State machine below |
| `secondary_incident_queue_ref` | UUID | Nullable | Required when `write_status='shadow_queued'`; links to Ops incident queue item |
| `rolled_up_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when raw row is included in the quarterly auction-fairness aggregate |
| `data_residency_region` | Enum | Appendix J `data_residency_region`: `us`, `eu`, `apac`, `custom` | Most restrictive of buyer and winning seller residency at decision time; no cross-region raw replay |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | Only `write_status`, `secondary_incident_queue_ref`, `rolled_up_at`, and `deleted_at` may change after create |
| `created_by` | UUID/String | System agent ID | Usually `system_agent_marketplace_auction_engine`; never a buyer or seller user |
| `updated_by` | UUID/String | System agent or Ops ID | Last mutator for reconciliation / rollup |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete after the §40.2 PromotedListing auction-run raw-retention window and successful quarterly rollup; aggregate row remains |

**Indexes.**

- `(auction_at DESC)` — Ops replay and retention sweep.
- `(category_id, placement_surface, auction_at DESC)` — category/surface fairness review.
- `(winner_promoted_listing_id, auction_at DESC)` partial on `winner_promoted_listing_id IS NOT NULL` — per-listing charge reconstruction.
- `(winner_seller_org_id, auction_at DESC)` partial on `winner_seller_org_id IS NOT NULL` — seller aggregate reporting.
- `(write_status, auction_at)` partial on `write_status IN ('shadow_queued', 'reconciled')` — incident-queue reconciliation.
- `(decision_payload_hash)` unique — exactly-once write guard.

**Scope Isolation.**

- Raw rows are readable only by Ops roles with marketplace-auction or finance-audit permission. Seller-console APIs never return raw `eligible_listing_ids`, `runner_up_bid_cents`, `buyer_org_id_hash`, or `decision_payload_hash`.
- Buyer-console reads are rejected with 404 non-leak semantics; buyer Org identity cannot be recovered from `buyer_org_id_hash` without Ops key material and the per-auction salt.
- Derived seller reports may expose aggregate win/loss counts and median cleared prices only after the §27.11.2 k-anonymity floor is satisfied.

**Retention & DSAR.**

- Raw rows retain for the §40.2 PromotedListing auction-run raw-retention window from `auction_at`, then roll into quarterly auction-fairness aggregates; `deleted_at` is set only after rollup succeeds.
- Aggregates retain 7 years with PromotedListing financial records per §40.2.
- DSAR for a buyer Org does not reveal or delete this row because raw buyer ID is not stored; if Ops key material is rotated or destroyed, historical hashes remain non-reversible. DSAR for a seller user pseudonymizes `updated_by` if it names an Ops user, while auction facts remain.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `recorded` | Auction engine writes canonical row | `decision_payload_hash` unique; source listings validated | Normal path |
| (init) | `shadow_queued` | Primary write fails but secondary incident queue accepts payload | `secondary_incident_queue_ref` populated | Auction may still resolve and charge; Ops alerting follows Failure Mode #8 |
| `shadow_queued` | `reconciled` | Reconciliation worker writes canonical row from incident payload | `decision_payload_hash` still unique; replay matches original payload hash | Reconstructed row is immutable after reconcile |
| `recorded` | `rolled_up` | Quarterly rollup job includes row in aggregate | Raw-retention window reached; aggregate checksum written | Raw row eligible for soft delete |
| `reconciled` | `rolled_up` | Quarterly rollup job includes reconstructed row in aggregate | Same as above | Preserves incident provenance |

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Auction resolves but canonical row write fails.** The secondary incident queue stores a `shadow_queued` record keyed by `decision_payload_hash`; Ops is paged when queue depth exceeds the §4.4.19 Failure Mode #8 threshold, and reconciliation must move the row to `reconciled`.
2. **Duplicate render retry attempts to write the same auction decision twice.** Unique `decision_payload_hash` enforces exactly-once logging; duplicate writes return the existing row ID to the caller.
3. **Buyer identity inference through repeated hashes.** Hash salt is per-auction, not per-buyer; the same buyer produces different hashes across auctions. Seller-visible reports use only k-anonymity-safe aggregates.
4. **Winner not in eligible list.** Write-side validator rejects any `winner_promoted_listing_id` or `runner_up_promoted_listing_id` not present in `eligible_listing_ids`; the auction replays before charge posting.
5. **Rollup drops incident-reconciled rows.** Quarterly aggregate checksum includes `recorded` and `reconciled` states; rollup is blocked if any eligible row remains `shadow_queued`.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Every auction decision attempt MUST create exactly one row keyed by `decision_payload_hash`; duplicate retries MUST return the existing row rather than creating a second row.
2. Any `winner_promoted_listing_id` and `runner_up_promoted_listing_id` MUST be present in `eligible_listing_ids`; mismatches reject before MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord charge posting.
3. For single-bidder auctions, `auction_outcome='single_bidder_floor'`, `runner_up_bid_cents IS NULL`, and `cleared_price_cents = reserve_floor_cents` MUST hold.
4. For no-fill auctions, `auction_outcome='no_eligible_listing'`, `winner_promoted_listing_id IS NULL`, and no MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord row may be written.
5. If primary write fails, the secondary incident queue MUST create a `shadow_queued` row within 5 seconds and reconciliation MUST transition it to `reconciled` before the quarterly rollup can run.
6. Seller-console projections MUST NOT expose `eligible_listing_ids`, `runner_up_bid_cents`, `buyer_org_id_hash`, or `decision_payload_hash`; serializer tests assert those fields are Ops-only.
7. Raw rows MUST roll up after the §40.2 PromotedListing auction-run raw-retention window and must not be soft-deleted until the aggregate checksum includes the row ID.
8. A property-based auction test with randomized bids MUST prove the `PromotedListingAuctionRun` row reconstructs the same winner and cleared price as the auction engine for 10,000 generated cases.

### 4.4.20 FeaturedPlacement (Marketplace-Domain, Ops-Curated, Public) {#4.4.20-featuredplacement}

**Authoring Intent — and Source-Document Conflict (Resolved).**

FeaturedPlacement is the editorially-curated placement record per Summary **Summary §2.10**, **C.131**, and **Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy §12.3** (all three agree: *"Strictly editorial. Not purchasable."*). Summary **Summary §6.16.6** contains older, conflicting text describing FeaturedPlacement as a **paid monthly/quarterly commitment**. The prompt invoking this entity explicitly listed "paid" language and `commitment_period` as a field. The conflict is surfaced in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Known Gaps` and resolved as follows:

- **Authoritative current behavior:** Editorial-only. Three sources (Summary §2.10, C.131, SPS §12.3) agree and the newer Appendix-C entry (C.131) supersedes §6.16.6. No seller ever pays for a Featured Placement slot under the current model.
- **Schema future-proofing:** Fields that would support a paid-commitment variant are retained but **feature-flagged OFF** at launch. The `placement_mode` enum distinguishes `editorial` (live) from `paid_commitment` (reserved; activation requires an Ops Council + Finance + Legal sign-off documented in RECONCILIATION). This preserves the Summary §6.16.6 optionality without contradicting the authoritative model.
- **Commitment period interpretation:** Under editorial mode, `commitment_period` represents the editorial featuring duration (monthly or quarterly slot). Under paid-commitment mode, it would represent a contractual commitment window. The field is authoritative across both modes.

FeaturedPlacement surfaces live in three locations per Summary §6.16.6: **CategoryPage** (M9, §4.4.12), **ComparisonPage** (M11, §4.4.14), and **HeatMapCell** (M13, §4.4.16). Featured status does not alter organic Match Scoring (Summary §6.16.4) — the "Featured" lane is visually distinct and labeled per FTC 16 CFR Part 255 disclosure requirements.

**Scope:** Marketplace-domain (platform-scoped, no `org_id` on the authoring record — the Featured *target* is a Seller Org or SellerSoftware, but the *decision* is Sourcera's). Rendered on public surfaces with FTC-compliant disclosure.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `seller_org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization; must resolve to a Seller Org | The featured seller |
| `seller_software_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → SellerSoftware (§4.4.9) | When the featuring is software-level (required for ComparisonPage; optional for CategoryPage; forbidden for HeatMapCell) |

| `target_entity_type` | Enum | See Appendix J `featured_placement_target_entity_type`: `category_page`, `comparison_page`, `heat_map_cell` | Polymorphic target kind |
| `target_entity_id` | UUID (FK, polymorphic) | Required; FK resolves per `target_entity_type` to §4.4.12, §4.4.14, or §4.4.16 | The specific page or cell this placement appears on |
| `slot_kind` | Enum | See Appendix J `featured_placement_slot_kind`: `hero_tile`, `carousel_rail`, `sidebar_strip`, `comparison_spotlight`, `heat_map_annotation_callout` | Visual treatment; drives the layout token used in the DOM |
| `slot_position` | Integer | 0–19 | Zero-indexed position within the slot kind; allows up to 20 featured entries per surface |

| `commitment_period` | Enum | See Appendix J `featured_placement_commitment_period`: `monthly`, `quarterly`, `ops_discretion_variable` | Duration of the featuring window. For `editorial` mode, usually `monthly` or `quarterly` per Marketing editorial calendar. For `paid_commitment`, reflects the contract term |
| `selected_by_ops_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Required when `placement_mode = 'editorial'`; Ops User ID | Marketing editor who authored the selection |

Enforces C.131 selection-criteria transparency |

| `invoice_ref_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Stripe Invoice (external ref) | Only for `paid_commitment` mode |
| `status` | Enum | See Appendix J `featured_placement_status`: `scheduled`, `active`, `paused_by_ops`, `expired`, `revoked`, `revoked_by_opt_out`, `revoked_by_verification_downgrade`, `revoked_by_abuse_finding` | Full state machine below |
| `revocation_reason_code` | Enum | Nullable; See Appendix J `featured_placement_revocation_reason`: `vendor_opt_out`, `verification_tier_downgrade`, `abuse_report_upheld`, `kb_health_below_floor`, `seller_org_deleted`, `seller_software_unpublished`, `editorial_discretion`, `paid_commitment_cancelled_by_seller_with_proration`, `paid_commitment_cancelled_by_ops` | Populated on any `revoked*` status |
| `vendor_opt_out_ref_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Vendor Opt-Out Record (§4.4.8) | Populated when revocation cascades from an opt-out |
