## 4.6 Audit & Logging Entities {#4.6-audit-&-logging-entities}

### 4.6.1 Audit Event (Org-Scoped, Cross-Console-Tagged, Append-Only) {#4.6.1-audit-event}

**Authoring Intent.** Audit Event is the canonical, immutable, append-only mutation-log row for every customer-Org-mutating action across both consoles plus Ops impersonation. Per §6.7 Audit Logging it is the SOC-2 / GDPR audit anchor; per §6.8.5 row-class catalog, Audit Events of audit-integrity / financial / compliance class are retention-exempt and retained 7+ years. Audit Event is hard-delete-forbidden at the application layer; DSAR right-to-erasure proceeds via field-level pseudonymization on `user_id`, `ip_address`, `user_agent`, and `notes` per §6.8.5, with `entity_type` / `entity_id` / `action` / `status` / `timestamp` / `changes` retained for audit-integrity. Soft-delete is forbidden at the application layer: the entity has no `deleted_at` field by design.

**Scope.** Org-scoped (`org_id` is required), with explicit `console` tagging that controls cross-console firewall enforcement on read projections. Audit Events are read-projected per console: a buyer-console session sees only `console = buyer` rows of its Org plus `console = ops` Ops-impersonation events targeting the Org; a seller-console session sees only `console = seller` rows plus `console = ops`. Org Owner / Org Admin / Billing Admin (per §5.2.1 Billing Admin Audit View) can read across consoles via the unified Audit Surface; the cross-console read is flagged in the audit-of-audit log with action `audit_event_cross_console_read`.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID | FK → Organization; required | Organization reference; never null |
| `console` | Enum | See Appendix J `audit_event_console`: `buyer`, `seller`, `ops`, `platform_system`; required | **Console attribution; controls cross-console firewall on read.** Set at write per the actor's session context: `buyer` for buyer-console actor, `seller` for seller-console actor, `ops` for Ops impersonation events, `platform_system` for system-actor mutations (cron jobs, webhook handlers, Outcome Resolver). (D-1V-008 remediation, 2026-04-29.) |
| `timestamp` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC; event time. Aliased to `created_at` per §4.1 Principle #2 audit-trail conformance — Audit Event is immutable so no `updated_at` / `updated_by` fields are required. |
| `user_id` | UUID (FK) | User ID; nullable for `console = platform_system` | Who performed action. NULL only when `console = platform_system` and the actor is a synthetic system identity. |
| `action` | String(48) | See Appendix J `audit_event_action_type` (controlled-vocabulary string per §4.6.1.1; bare-verb canonical set + qualified-string namespace extensions registered per Appendix J line 42617 + line 43611+) | Action type. Originally a closed enum; converted to controlled-vocabulary string in D-1V-008 remediation 2026-04-29 to accommodate the §22 / §27 / §48 / §50 / §51 extensions registered in Appendix J. |
| `entity_type` | String(48) | See Appendix J `audit_event_entity_type` (controlled-vocabulary string per §4.6.1.1; canonical registry covers every §4 entity); required | What was acted upon. **Originally enum-typed with 8 values; converted to controlled-vocabulary string in D-1V-008 / D-1V-009 remediation 2026-04-29** to cover all 70+ §4 entities (Organization, Workspace, Use Case, Requirement, Response, Score, Scenario, Team, Workspace Membership, Pulse Event, Internal Comment, Bid Workspace, Bid Response, Seller Profile, Capability Declaration, Marketplace Listing, EOI, NDA, Marketplace Abuse Report, EvalStarter, Audit Event, Attachment, OpsSession, Console Bridge Event, Vendor Disqualification Record, AIOperation, AIWallet, OutcomeContract, ContestRecord, FreeAllowanceCounter, CommittedSpendContract, PricingTableVersion, DowngradeExcessDataBucket, BillingSeatSnapshot, MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord, SellerOutcomeSignalConfig, plus all §4.4.7–§4.4.29 Marketplace + Seller surface entities — full canonical list lives at Appendix J `audit_event_entity_type`). |
| `entity_id` | UUID | Resource ID | Which entity. FK is application-validated against `entity_type` rather than database-enforced (polymorphic). |
| `changes` | JSON | Max 10000 chars | {field: {old_value, new_value}, ...} for updates. Field values are pseudonymized at write for PII-bearing fields per §6.8.4 (e.g., `email`, `name`, `phone`); pseudonyms are stable per Org, reversible only by Ops Finance under §35 audit. **Bearer-secret exclusion (D-1.5-001 remediation, 2026-05-01):** the closed forbidden-field-name registry below is enforced at write time; matching fields are dropped from the `changes` object before the row is committed. The full registry, validator, error-code, and CI-gate contract live in §4.6.1.2 below. |
| `ip_address` | String(45) | IPv4 or IPv6, optionally masked | Client IP. Masked to /24 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6) when the Org has GDPR-strict mode enabled per §6.8.7. |
| `user_agent` | String(1000) | Max 1000 chars | Browser/client info. |
| `status` | Enum | `success` | `failure` | Action outcome |
| `failure_reason` | String(500) | Max 500 chars; nullable | If failed, why. |
| `notes` | String(2000) | Max 2000 chars; nullable | **Visibility scope (D-1V-010 remediation, 2026-04-29):** Visible to Org Owner, Org Admin, and Billing Admin only via the Org's Audit Surface; never returned to standard members or guests; Ops can read all under §35 impersonation audit. The UI projection guard at the §32 audit endpoint applies the role-based filter at serialize time. |

Per §6.7.5 full-corpus integrity coverage. |
| `event_content_hash` | String(64) | sha256 hex; required | sha256 over the canonical-JSON serialization of all immutable columns of this row (excludes `prev_event_hash` and `event_content_hash` themselves; excludes DSAR-pseudonymizable PII columns to permit DSAR re-hash). Per §6.7.5. |

#### 4.6.1.1 Audit Event Indexes, Retention, DSAR & State Machine (D-1V-008 remediation block)

**Indexes.**
- `(org_id, timestamp DESC)` — primary Audit Surface query
- `(org_id, console, timestamp DESC)` — per-console projection
- `(entity_type, entity_id, timestamp DESC)` — per-entity audit trail
- `(user_id, timestamp DESC)` — per-user audit trail (DSAR support)
- `(org_id, action, timestamp DESC)` partial where `action LIKE 'billing_%'` — Billing Admin Audit View per §5.2.1.4
- `(org_id, status)` partial where `status = 'failure'` — failure-rate dashboards

**Scope Isolation (Cross-Console Firewall).**
- **Buyer-console reads:** `console ∈ {buyer, ops, platform_system}` only, scoped to `org_id = session.org_id`. `console = ops` rows surface in the buyer's Audit Surface so the Org Owner can see Ops impersonation events; `console = seller` rows are filtered out at the read projection.
- **Seller-console reads:** Symmetrically `console ∈ {seller, ops, platform_system}` only.
- **Org-Admin / Org-Owner / Billing-Admin unified reads:** Cross-console reads permitted via the unified Audit Surface; flagged in audit-of-audit log with action `audit_event_cross_console_read`. Billing Admin reads further filtered to `action LIKE 'billing_%'` per §5.2.1.4.
- **Ops reads:** All fields, all consoles, all Orgs (under §35 impersonation audit).
- **Cross-Org reads:** Always blocked; HTTP 404 `audit_event_cross_org_access` (Appendix I — new).
- **Writes:** Application-mediated only via the audit-emit handlers in §6.7. Direct POST/PUT to Audit Event is forbidden (HTTP 403 `audit_event_direct_write_forbidden`).

**State Machine.** Audit Event is **append-only and immutable**; there is no state machine. Once written, the row is frozen: only DSAR field-level pseudonymization (per §6.8.5) is permitted; all other writes return HTTP 422 `audit_event_immutable`. Soft-delete is forbidden — the entity has no `deleted_at` field by design.

**Retention (D-1V-008 remediation).**
- **Default UI retention:** Per plan tier per §40.2 (`30d / 30d / 1y / 1y / 3y / 7y` for Free / Solo / Starter / Growth / Scale / Enterprise).
- **Financial / compliance retention:** Audit Events whose `action` matches the §6.8.5 retained-row class catalog (financial actions: `billing_*`, `wallet_*`, `contest_*`, `payment_*`, `committed_spend_*`, `marketplace_discovery_revenue_*`; compliance actions: `dsar_*`, `gdpr_*`, `audit_event_export`, `audit_event_cross_console_read`, `ops_session_*`) are retained **7 years** regardless of plan-tier UI retention. The 7-year-retained rows surface in the Audit Surface even after the plan-tier UI retention has expired, displayed under a "Compliance & Financial Retention" sub-tab.
- **Residency:** Each row stored in the `org_id`'s `data_residency_region` partition; cross-region reads from customer surfaces blocked.

**DSAR Cascade (D-1V-008 remediation; D-1V3-001 / D-1V3-003 remediation 2026-05-01 — Pattern B).** When the §6.8.4 cascade walker pseudonymizes a User per right-to-erasure:
- **Pattern B applied to `user_id` (D-1V3-001 remediation, 2026-05-01).** The `user_id` UUID FK column is **preserved unchanged**; the User row pointed to by the FK is pseudonymized in-place per §6.8.4.1 Pattern B (`users.email`, `users.full_name` rewritten to canonical `anonymized_<console>_user_<base32(hash)[:16]>` per §6.8.5 line 9454; `users.deleted_at` set; PII fields hard-deleted; `users.state → tombstoned_dsar`). Joins through `Audit Event.user_id` resolve to the pseudonymized User row. The pre-remediation §4.6.1.1 v7.1.0 prescription "rewritten to `anonymized_user_<hash>`" was incorrect on a UUID column type and used a non-canonical pseudonym form — superseded by Pattern B citation per the §6.8.4.1 per-entity assignment table.
- **Pseudonymized in-place (non-FK columns):** `ip_address` (zeroed to `0.0.0.0` or `::`), `user_agent` (zeroed to `[REDACTED_DSAR]`), `notes` (filtered for subject-name occurrences and redacted to `[REDACTED_DSAR]`), `changes.<field>` PII bearers (filtered per §6.8.4 PII registry).
- **Preserved:** `id`, `org_id`, `console`, `timestamp`, `action`, `entity_type`, `entity_id`, `status`, `failure_reason`, `user_id` (per Pattern B above — the UUID resolves to the pseudonymized User row), monetary or numeric `changes.<field>` values that don't carry PII.
- **Audit-integrity exemption:** Audit Events whose `action` is in the §6.8.5 retained-row catalog inherit Pattern B by definition (the User-row pseudonymization is the single point of PII redaction; the FK column is preserved for forensic continuity). CI gate `audit_event_dsar_cascade_field_partition` asserts the exact field-set partition; CI gate `dsar_cascade_pseudonym_pattern_consistency` (§6.8.4.1) asserts Pattern B is the chosen mechanism.

**Acceptance Criteria (D-1V-008 remediation).**
1. Every customer-Org-mutating action across both consoles MUST produce exactly one Audit Event row; missing-write recovery is via the §31 transactional outbox pattern (commit-time guarantee).
2. Audit Event is append-only and immutable: post-write writes (other than DSAR field-level pseudonymization) MUST return HTTP 422 `audit_event_immutable`.
3. A read of an Audit Event by a buyer-console session whose `console` filter would expose a `console = seller` row of the same Org MUST return the row only when the requester is `org_owner` / `org_admin` / `billing_admin` and MUST emit an audit-of-audit row with action `audit_event_cross_console_read`.
4. The 7-year retention exemption MUST apply to every Audit Event whose `action` matches the §6.8.5 retained-row class catalog regardless of plan-tier UI retention; QA test `audit_event_financial_retention_exemption` asserts the row remains accessible to Org Owner / Org Admin / Billing Admin past the plan-tier UI cutoff.
5. DSAR cascade MUST pseudonymize the field set declared above and preserve the audit-integrity field set; QA test `audit_event_dsar_field_partition` asserts the exact partition.
6. Cross-Org reads MUST return HTTP 404 with `audit_event_cross_org_access`; QA test `audit_event_cross_org_isolation` asserts.
7. The `notes` field MUST be filtered out of read projections for `member` and `guest` roles; QA test `audit_event_notes_visibility_role_filter` asserts the projection.

**Failure Modes (D-1V-008 remediation).**
1. **Audit Event write fails after entity mutation succeeds.** Resolved: §31 transactional outbox pattern — the entity mutation and the Audit Event write are committed in the same database transaction; on commit failure, both roll back atomically. The Audit Event handler is part of the entity mutation handler's commit chain, not a post-commit observer.
2. **DSAR cascade pseudonymizes a `user_id` that should have been preserved for audit integrity.** Resolved: §6.8.5 row-class catalog filters retained-row classes out of the user_id pseudonymization step; CI gate `audit_event_dsar_cascade_field_partition` asserts the partition.
3. **Audit Event cardinality explodes (millions of events on a high-traffic Org).** Resolved: storage partition by `(org_id, year(timestamp))` with hot/cold tier transitions per §40.2; query layer enforces cursor pagination (default 50, max 250) per §32; Audit Surface UI default-filters to the last 30 days with explicit "Load earlier" pagination.

---

#### 4.6.1.2 Bearer-Secret Exclusion (D-1.5-001 remediation, 2026-05-01) {#4.6.1.2-bearer-secret-exclusion}

**Authoring Intent.** §4.6.1 v7.1.0 specified PII pseudonymization (`email`, `name`, `phone`) for the `changes` JSON but contained no schema-level exclusion of bearer secrets. NIST SP 800-63B §5.1.1.2 forbids credential capture in audit logs; SOC 2 CC6.1 requires the same. This sub-section authors the closed forbidden-field-name registry, the write-time validator, the error code, and the CI-gate contract that operationalize the exclusion across every audit-emit path.

**Closed forbidden-field-name registry.** The following exact-match and prefix/suffix patterns identify bearer-secret fields. Any field whose name matches the registry is dropped from the `changes` JSON pre-commit; any failed strip (write-time validator detects the field name persists) returns HTTP 422 `audit_event_secret_field_forbidden` (Appendix I — new) and aborts the audit emit. The registry is **closed** — additions require an Authored-Extension ledger row plus a Master Spec amendment.

| Pattern | Class | Match rule | Examples covered |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `*password*` | password | substring (case-insensitive) | `password`, `password_hash`, `current_password`, `new_password_hash`, `password_reset_token` |
| `*passwd*` | password | substring (case-insensitive) | `passwd`, `passwd_old`, `legacy_passwd_hash` |
| `*pwd*` | password | substring (case-insensitive) | `pwd`, `pwd_hash` |
| `mfa_seed` | MFA seed | exact (case-insensitive) | TOTP seed for §6.2 MFA enrollment |
| `mfa_secret` | MFA seed | exact (case-insensitive) | Alias of mfa_seed |
| `mfa_factor_secret` | MFA seed | exact (case-insensitive) | WorkOS factor secret payload |
| `recovery_code*` | MFA recovery | prefix (case-insensitive) | `recovery_code`, `recovery_code_hash`, `recovery_codes_array` (the array is dropped wholesale) |
| `*api_token_secret*` | API token | substring (case-insensitive) | `api_token_secret`, `legacy_api_token_secret_hash` |
| `*session_token*` | Session bearer | substring (case-insensitive) | `session_token`, `sso_session_token`, `mobile_session_token_jwt` |
| `*step_up_reauth_token*` | Step-up bearer | substring (case-insensitive) | `step_up_reauth_token`, `step_up_reauth_token_jwt` |
| `webauthn_credential_secret*` | WebAuthn | prefix (case-insensitive) | `webauthn_credential_secret`, `webauthn_credential_secret_hash`, `webauthn_credential_secret_blob` |
| `*signing_key*` | Crypto material | substring (case-insensitive) | `webhook_signing_key`, `private_signing_key`, `signing_key_id_secret` |
| `*private_key*` | Crypto material | substring (case-insensitive) | `private_key`, `tls_private_key_pem`, `kms_private_key_handle_secret` |
| `*encryption_key*` | Crypto material | substring (case-insensitive) | `encryption_key`, `data_encryption_key_blob`, `customer_supplied_encryption_key` |
| `*bearer_token*` | Generic bearer | substring (case-insensitive) | `bearer_token`, `oauth_bearer_token`, `service_account_bearer_token` |
| `*oauth_refresh_token*` | OAuth refresh | substring (case-insensitive) | `oauth_refresh_token`, `oauth_refresh_token_jwt` |
| `stripe_*_secret*` | Stripe secret | prefix + substring (case-insensitive) | `stripe_secret_key`, `stripe_signing_secret`, `stripe_webhook_secret` |
| `workos_*_secret*` | WorkOS secret | prefix + substring (case-insensitive) | `workos_api_secret`, `workos_factor_secret_blob` |
| `convex_*_secret*` | Convex secret | prefix + substring (case-insensitive) | `convex_admin_secret`, `convex_deployment_secret` |
| `posthog_personal_api_key*` | PostHog secret | prefix (case-insensitive) | `posthog_personal_api_key`, `posthog_personal_api_key_jwt` |
| `loops_*_secret*` | Loops.so secret | prefix + substring (case-insensitive) | `loops_api_secret`, `loops_signing_secret` |

**Pattern-match semantics.** Substring patterns match anywhere in the field name; prefix patterns match at the start of the field name; exact patterns require equality (case-insensitive). Hyphen, underscore, and camelCase variants are normalized to lowercase-snake before match. The validator runs in O(n × p) where n is the count of `changes` keys and p is the registry size (≈ 22 patterns); typical mutation has n ≤ 30 keys, so latency overhead is < 50µs per audit emit.

**Write-time validator.** The audit-emit middleware (§6.7) MUST run the registry pass before persisting the row. Implementation contract:

1. Walk `changes` object keys at every depth (the JSON is at most 10,000 chars by `changes` field constraint, so depth-walk is bounded).
2. For each key, normalize to lowercase-snake-case.
3. Test against every pattern in the registry; first match wins.
4. On match: drop the key-and-value from the `changes` object. Increment the `audit_event_secret_field_redacted_count` counter (per-Org, per-day, surfaced in Ops dashboards for security-incident detection).
5. Run the validator again post-strip as a defense-in-depth check; if any registry-matching key persists, abort with HTTP 422 `audit_event_secret_field_forbidden` and emit a `audit_event_secret_field_strip_failure` PostHog event. The mutation that triggered the audit emit MUST roll back per §31 transactional outbox pattern.

**New error code.** `audit_event_secret_field_forbidden` (HTTP 422; Appendix I — new). Body: `{"error_code": "audit_event_secret_field_forbidden", "field_name_pattern_matched": "<pattern>", "field_count_failed_strip": <int>, "remediation": "Submit the mutation without the listed field; if the field is required for business purposes, file a §6.7 audit-handler exception request via Ops."}`.

**New CI gate.** `audit_event_secret_field_redacted` (§M.5 — new) asserts every audit-emit handler invokes the validator before persistence. The gate inspects the call graph statically: every `auditEvent.create()` invocation MUST be reached only via a code path that calls `validateBearerSecretExclusion(changes)` first; a property test generates synthetic mutation payloads for every §4 entity type with worst-case bearer-secret content and asserts the validator strips every pattern.

**Bearer-secret-exclusion-overrides-DSAR rule.** The bearer-secret strip happens at write time; the §4.6.1.1 DSAR Cascade pseudonymization happens at retroactive DSAR fulfillment. Bearer-secret strip is therefore complete before any DSAR ever reads the row — a DSAR that nonetheless encounters a bearer-secret-shaped value (e.g., legacy rows pre-2026-05-01 deploy) MUST treat the value as if the registry had stripped it (anonymize to `[REDACTED_BEARER_SECRET]`) and emit a `audit_event_legacy_bearer_secret_dsar_redaction` event for forensic review.

**Migration of pre-deploy rows.** Audit Event rows created before the 2026-05-01 deploy MAY contain bearer-secret-shaped values in their `changes` JSON. A one-shot migration job — `audit_event_legacy_bearer_secret_strip_migration` — scans all rows by `created_at < 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z`, runs the validator, and rewrites matching keys in-place with `"[REDACTED_LEGACY_BEARER_SECRET]"` placeholder values; the migration emits a `dsar.audit_event.legacy_bearer_secret_redacted` event per row mutated for the audit-of-audit chain. The migration is idempotent and forward-recovery-only per §6.8.4 partial-failure rule.

**Acceptance Criteria (D-1.5-001 remediation).**
1. Every `changes` JSON committed via the audit-emit handler MUST pass the bearer-secret-exclusion validator before persistence; a failed strip MUST abort the mutation with HTTP 422 `audit_event_secret_field_forbidden`. QA test `audit_event_bearer_secret_strip_correctness` asserts.
2. The closed forbidden-field-name registry above MUST be the single source of truth; CI gate `audit_event_secret_field_registry_closed` asserts no inline pattern lists appear elsewhere in §4–§51.
3. Pattern matching MUST be case-insensitive after lowercase-snake normalization; QA test `audit_event_bearer_secret_pattern_normalization` asserts.
4. Successful strips MUST increment `audit_event_secret_field_redacted_count` per-Org-per-day; surfaced in §50 Ops dashboards within 5 minutes.
5. Failed-strip aborts MUST emit `audit_event_secret_field_strip_failure` PostHog event AND page `ops_security_admin` within 10 seconds; chronic failures (≥ 3 in 1 hour) trigger §42 P1 alert.
6. Legacy bearer-secret values in pre-2026-05-01 rows MUST be redacted by the one-shot migration job within 7 days of deploy; QA test `audit_event_legacy_bearer_secret_strip_migration_idempotency` asserts forward-recovery on partial failure.
7. CI gate `audit_event_secret_field_redacted` asserts the validator is invoked on every audit-emit path; static call-graph analysis MUST report 100% coverage.

**Failure Modes (D-1.5-001 remediation).**
1. **Engineer adds a new bearer-secret field name not in the registry.** Resolved: the §M.4 `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` CI gate cross-checks new field-name additions in §4 entity tables against the registry; new fields whose names match a "secret-shaped" linter heuristic (`*secret*`, `*key*`, `*token*`, `*credential*`, `*hash*` outside common-pattern allow-list) trigger a CI warning and require explicit author confirmation that either (a) the field is exempt from the registry (must be justified) or (b) the field's name is added to the registry.
2. **Pattern false-positive — legitimate field name matches a registry pattern (e.g., a Bid Workspace field named `password_recovery_workflow_status`).** Resolved: the registry maintainer adds an explicit allow-list exemption registered via Appendix J `audit_event_secret_field_registry_exemption_v1` (new enum); the validator consults the exemption list on substring-pattern hits before stripping.
3. **Performance regression — registry pass adds latency to high-frequency mutations (≥ 10K/sec at peak).** Resolved: the validator is implemented as a precompiled regex union with O(1) match cost; the validator fingerprint is hashed at deploy time; the runtime budget is enforced at 100 µs P99 per audit emit; breach raises §42 P1 alert and triggers a `audit_event_secret_field_validator_latency_breach` PostHog event.

### 4.6.2 Attachment (Polymorphic, Cross-Console) {#4.6.2-attachment}

Single-file upload record used by Internal Comment Post (§4.3.12), Q&A Post (§18.3.1), Bid Workspace deliverables (§4.4.1), Seller Profile assets (§4.4.7), and any entity permitted by plan gating to accept file uploads (§39). One row per file. Binary payload stored in S3 / R2 via presigned upload; this entity records the metadata, ownership, scan status, and FK target.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID | FK → Organization | Uploader's org |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer` \| `seller` | Uploader's console scope at upload time |
| `uploader_user_id` | UUID | FK → User | Who uploaded |
| `owner_entity_type` | Enum (Appendix J `attachment_owner_entity_type_enum`) | Not null | `internal_comment_post`, `qa_thread_post`, `bid_workspace_deliverable`, `seller_profile_asset`, `selection_report_draft`, `bid_response`, `certification_artifact`, `presigned_orphan` |
| `owner_entity_id` | UUID | Nullable (null while `presigned_orphan`) | FK target depends on `owner_entity_type`; polymorphic; validated at application layer |
| `workspace_id` | UUID | Nullable | Denormalized from owner entity when owner is workspace-scoped; used for workspace-level quota sweeps |
| `marketplace_domain_id` | UUID | Nullable | Denormalized for firewall-isolated storage path; required when `owner_entity_type ∈ {seller_profile_asset, bid_response, certification_artifact}` |
| `filename` | String(255) | Not null | Original filename (sanitized); stored exactly for user display |
| `content_type` | String(128) | Not null | IANA MIME type; validated against §18.5.2 allowlist |
| `size_bytes` | BigInt | Not null; ≥ 1; ≤ 524,288,000 (500 MB per §39) | Enforced at presigned-URL issuance |
| `storage_backend` | Enum (Appendix J `storage_backend_enum`) | Not null | `s3_us`, `s3_eu`, `r2`, `local_dev` — residency-bound |
| `storage_key` | String(512) | Not null | Object key in storage backend; includes `org_id` + `marketplace_domain_id` path segments for firewall-isolated listing |
| `storage_region` | String(32) | Not null | AWS/R2 region code (`us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, etc.); must match Org data-residency setting (§40.3) |
| `sha256_hash` | String(64) | Not null; hex-encoded | Content hash; used for dedup and integrity verification |
| `scan_status` | Enum (Appendix J `attachment_scan_status_enum`) | Not null | `pending`, `scanning`, `clean`, `infected`, `scan_failed`, `scan_timeout` — virus-scan state per §18.5.2 |
| `scan_completed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Populated on transition to `clean`/`infected`/`scan_failed`/`scan_timeout` |
| `scan_engine_version` | String(64) | Nullable | ClamAV or successor engine version that produced the verdict |
| `infection_signature` | String(256) | Nullable | Populated only when `scan_status = infected` |
| `redaction_state` | Enum (Appendix J `attachment_redaction_state_enum`) | Not null | `active`, `dsar_redacted`, `org_deleted_redacted`, `infected_quarantined` |
| `redacted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When redaction was applied |
| `redaction_reason` | Enum (Appendix J `attachment_redaction_reason_enum`) | Nullable | `dsar_request`, `org_hard_delete`, `virus_detected`, `ops_takedown`, `legal_hold_release` |
| `presigned_upload_issued_at` | Timestamp | Not null | Used for orphan sweep (presigned-orphan rows older than 24h hard-deleted) |
| `upload_completed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Populated when client confirms upload; null while `presigned_orphan` |
| `download_count` | Integer | Not null; ≥ 0 | Cumulative download counter; used for audit anomaly detection |
| `last_downloaded_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Most recent download |
| `plan_quota_counted` | Boolean | Not null; default `true` | False for system-generated or plan-exempt attachments |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Not null | |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Not null | |
| `created_by` | UUID | FK → User | = `uploader_user_id` at creation; invariant enforced at API |
| `updated_by` | UUID | FK → User | Last mutator (uploader or Ops) |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft-delete |

**Scope:** Polymorphic; scope derived from owner entity. Storage path enforces firewall: buyer-scoped attachments live under `{org_id}/buyer/{workspace_id}/...`; seller-scoped attachments live under `{org_id}/seller/{marketplace_domain_id}/{bid_workspace_id | seller_profile_id}/...`. **Cross-console access (D-1V-013 remediation, 2026-04-29):** seller cannot list or GET any Attachment whose `console = buyer` UNLESS the Attachment's `owner_entity_type ∈ {nda_record, qa_thread_post}` AND a §25 cross-console projection grants explicit access (NDA-bridge attachments are buyer-uploaded but seller-readable post-NDA-execution per §4.5.3; vendor-visible Q&A-thread attachments are buyer-uploaded but seller-readable when the buyer explicitly promotes the thread post to vendor visibility per §4.7.1 `qa_thread_post_appended` event). Bid Response attachments (`owner_entity_type = bid_response`) are seller-authored and live in the seller's storage partition; they never gate on the buyer-console rule. All other cross-console attempts return HTTP 404 (not 403) per §4.3.11 scope-isolation pattern. Buyer cannot access seller attachments except via Console Bridge-exposed sync (§25), which surfaces attachments only with explicit seller-share consent. CI gate `attachment_cross_console_carve_out_consistency` asserts the carve-out list matches the §4.5.3 NDA Execution and §4.7.1 Console Bridge Event projection contracts.

**Indexes:**
- `(org_id, owner_entity_type, owner_entity_id)` — owner enumeration
- `(workspace_id, created_at DESC)` WHERE `workspace_id IS NOT NULL` — workspace attachment list
- `(marketplace_domain_id, org_id, created_at DESC)` WHERE `marketplace_domain_id IS NOT NULL` — seller-side marketplace-scoped enumeration
- `(sha256_hash, org_id)` — dedup lookup
- `(scan_status, created_at)` WHERE `scan_status ∈ ('pending', 'scanning')` — scan-queue worker
- `(scan_status, redaction_state)` WHERE `scan_status = 'infected' AND redaction_state != 'infected_quarantined'` — infection-quarantine sweep
- `(owner_entity_type, presigned_upload_issued_at)` WHERE `owner_entity_type = 'presigned_orphan'` — orphan sweep
- `(uploader_user_id, created_at DESC)` — DSAR export and per-user audit
- `(org_id, deleted_at)` — Org-delete sweep

**State Machines:**
- Upload lifecycle: `presigned_orphan → upload_completed` (triggered by client confirm within 24h; otherwise hard-delete orphan).
- Scan lifecycle: `pending → scanning → {clean | infected | scan_failed | scan_timeout}`. Terminal: `clean`, `infected`. `scan_failed` / `scan_timeout` retry up to 3× before escalating to Ops.
- Redaction lifecycle: `active → {dsar_redacted | org_deleted_redacted | infected_quarantined}`. `infected_quarantined` is entered automatically on `scan_status = infected`.

**Retention:** Inherits owner-entity retention when linked. Orphan attachments (`owner_entity_type = 'presigned_orphan'`) hard-deleted 24h after `presigned_upload_issued_at`. Infected attachments (`scan_status = infected`) binary payload purged immediately on detection; metadata row retained 7 years in `infected_quarantined` state for forensic audit (§40.2 new row required). On Org hard-delete: binary payload purged within 30 days; metadata row set to `redaction_state = org_deleted_redacted` with `filename`, `storage_key`, `sha256_hash`, `infection_signature` zeroed to `DESTROYED_ON_ORG_DELETE` sentinel; metadata retained for audit per §6.8.5. DSAR: on subject request, `uploader_user_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by` pseudonymized; binary payload detached (hard-delete from storage backend) and `storage_key` zeroed; `redaction_state` set to `dsar_redacted`; metadata row retained for audit-integrity per §6.8.5. `filename`, `sha256_hash`, `content_type`, `size_bytes` retained (no subject PII in these fields unless filename leaks subject name — in which case filename is redacted to `[REDACTED_DSAR].{ext}`).

**Relationships:** Polymorphic child of eight possible parent entity types (see `owner_entity_type` enum). Referenced by Internal Comment Post (`attachment_ids[]`), Q&A Post, Selection Report Draft, and seller-facing entities. Uploaded via §18.5.2 upload flow; scanned via §18.5.2 scan pipeline.

**Authoring Intent:** Attachment is promoted to a §4.6 cross-console entity (rather than buried under each owner entity) because it is the single most-referenced polymorphic entity in the spec, it carries dual-console firewall enforcement at the storage layer, and it has unique retention semantics (orphan sweep, infected quarantine, per-owner inheritance, DSAR payload detachment) that differ from its owners. Consolidating into §4.6 makes the firewall contract testable and the retention matrix enumerable.

**Failure Modes:**
1. Presigned orphan never completes upload — 24h TTL sweep hard-deletes; monitored via PostHog event `attachment_orphan_swept`.
2. Infected file — auto-quarantine on scan verdict; binary purged; uploader notified via Inbox `attachment_infected`; workspace admin notified; download endpoint returns 451 Unavailable For Legal Reasons.
3. Cross-console read attempt — returns 404; logged to Audit Event with severity `high`.
4. Residency mismatch — if Org data-residency is EU but upload lands in `s3_us`, write is rejected with `E_RESIDENCY_MISMATCH` (Appendix I); worker migrates mis-routed objects during reconciliation.
5. Dedup collision with malicious hash — `sha256_hash` alone does not grant access; every access is authorized against `org_id` + `owner_entity_id`; dedup at the storage layer only saves bytes, never access.
6. DSAR on uploader of an attachment cited in a finalized Selection Report — binary detached, metadata retained; Selection Report rendering falls back to `[Attachment removed per user data deletion request]` placeholder.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. An Attachment can be accessed only by users whose scope matches the owner entity's scope; firewall-crossing read attempts return 404.
2. `scan_status` must be `clean` before any download endpoint serves the binary; `pending`, `scanning`, `scan_failed`, `scan_timeout`, `infected` all return 409 or 451 as appropriate.
3. Orphan sweeper (24h TTL) hard-deletes every `presigned_orphan` row whose `presigned_upload_issued_at < now() - 24h`.
4. DSAR right-to-erasure on uploader results in binary payload hard-deleted from storage within 72h, metadata row retained in `dsar_redacted` state, and downstream renders display the placeholder.
5. On Org hard-delete, binary payload purge completes within 30 days; metadata row retained 7 years under `org_deleted_redacted`.
6. Per-org total attachment size respects §39 object-size constraints (500 MB per attachment; Org-level aggregate enforced at owner-entity-quota level, not globally at Attachment layer).

---

### 4.6.3 OpsSession (Platform-Scoped, Ops-Bounded Impersonation Unit) {#4.6.3-opssession}

**Authoring Intent.** OpsSession is the durable audit object for every Sourcera Ops-originated impersonation of a customer Org, and, by extension, the audit anchor for every mutation an Ops user executes against customer data while that session is active. OpsSession is distinct from §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord: OpsActionRecord captures a *single discretionary Ops action* (plan downgrade for abuse, kill-switch toggle, AntiPattern exception, taxonomy-lock override, etc.); OpsSession captures the *time-bounded impersonation window* during which zero or more customer-API mutations may be executed with Ops attribution: §4.6.1 AuditEvent rows use Appendix J `audit_event_actor_type = 'ops_actor'` and §4.8.1 AIOperation rows keep Appendix J `ai_operation_actor_type = 'ops'` per §50.5. Every non-impersonation Ops action against a customer Org (e.g., a pricing table publish that affects all Orgs, a marketplace-taxonomy edit) writes an OpsActionRecord without an OpsSession. Every *per-Org* Ops mutation (impersonation read, impersonation-bound write, support-triage scoped query) writes an OpsSession AND emits Ops-tagged audit events in the customer's Audit Event ledger. The two are linked: an OpsActionRecord row written during an active impersonation MUST populate `linked_ops_session_id` (extension to §4.4.27, registered in RECONCILIATION.md — Authored Extension). Per Summary C.93 / C.98, OpsSession is the single object that proves "Ops had justification, Ops was time-boxed, Ops's window opened and closed, the customer Org Owner was notified both times."

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK, immutable | Standard. |
| `ops_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Required; → Ops User (see §5.2.2 Ops Role Registry, §50.3); `ON DELETE RESTRICT` — see tombstone-or-transfer procedure below | The Ops user who opened the session. **Cascade behavior (Authored Extension #37).** Deletion of an `ops_user` row carrying ≥ 1 historical `OpsSession` row is forbidden at the database layer and returns HTTP 409 `ops_user_delete_blocked_by_historical_ops_session` (Appendix I — new). The operational path for offboarding such an Ops user is the two-step tombstone-or-transfer procedure: (1) write a new `ops_user` row with `state='tombstoned'` (Appendix J `ops_session_ops_user_lifecycle_state` — new: `active`, `tombstoned`, `transferred`), `source_ops_user_id=<original>`, `tombstoned_at`, `tombstoned_reason_category ∈ {offboarded, role_transition, compliance_revocation, security_incident}`, preserving a public-facing forensic breadcrumb; (2) soft-delete the original `ops_user` row via `deleted_at` (NEVER hard-delete) so the PK remains live for FK resolution and every `OpsSession.ops_user_id` continues to resolve to the original identity-bearing row in a single hop. The forensic chain is therefore a one-hop FK join (`OpsSession → ops_user (deleted_at set)`, with `state='tombstoned'` on the successor row providing operator provenance). CI gate `ops_session_forensic_chain_one_hop_property_test` asserts no multi-hop chains. Hard deletion of an `ops_user` row is prohibited under all circumstances. GDPR DSAR for an Ops user is satisfied via §6.8.5 pseudonymization (`anonymized_former_ops_user_<hash>`) applied in-place on the soft-deleted row while preserving the FK target. |
| `ops_role_at_session_open` | Enum | Appendix J `ops_role_kind` (extended in §50.3 / Appendix J); required | Snapshot of the Ops user's role at session-open (role changes after open do NOT retroactively alter session's capability envelope — authored extension, flagged). |
| `org_id_impersonated` | UUID (FK) | Required; → Organization | The customer Org whose context the session operates within. |
| `console_scope` | Enum | `buyer`, `seller`, `both` (see Appendix J `ops_session_console_scope` — new); required | Which customer console surface(s) the session may access. `both` requires `ops_admin` role and dual sign-off per §50.4. |
| `impersonated_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → User | When set, session assumes the session-context of a specific customer User (their view of their own workspaces, inboxes, notifications). Null when the session operates against Org-scoped admin surfaces without assuming a specific User's session context. |
| `justification_category` | Enum | Appendix J `ops_session_justification_category` (new: `customer_support_ticket`, `fraud_investigation`, `bug_reproduction`, `data_migration`, `legal_compliance`, `enterprise_escape_hatch`, `billing_dispute`); required | High-level reason class. |
| `justification_note` | String | 80–4,000 chars; required | Free-text rationale. A linked Zendesk ticket ID, Linear issue key, or Slack thread URL SHOULD appear in the first 256 chars; a CI lint `ops_session_justification_references_source` warns (not blocks) if none of these appear. |
| `linked_support_ticket_ref` | String | 0–128 chars; nullable | Zendesk `ticket_<n>`, Linear `SRC-<n>`, or Slack canonical URL; parsed and indexed to support the Ops Cross-Reference view. |
| `requested_duration_minutes` | Integer | 5–480; required | Ops-requested time-box at session open. The default surface selection per §50.4 is 30 minutes; values ≥ 60 minutes require a written scope-expansion note and quorum sign-off (§50.4). |
| `effective_time_box_minutes` | Integer | 5–480; required | The actual time-box granted after §50.4 quorum evaluation. MAY be lower than `requested_duration_minutes` if the `ops_admin` quorum reviewer narrowed it; MUST NOT exceed `requested_duration_minutes`. |
| `quorum_signoff_user_ids` | Array[UUID] | 0–5 entries; FKs → Ops User | Populated when `effective_time_box_minutes > 60` OR `console_scope = 'both'` OR `justification_category = 'enterprise_escape_hatch'`. Quorum rules in §50.4.4. |
| `started_at` | Timestamp | Immutable; required | Session-open timestamp (UTC). |
| `ended_at` | Timestamp | Nullable; immutable once set | Session-close timestamp. Null while `session_state = 'active'`. |
| `close_reason` | Enum | Appendix J `ops_session_close_reason` (new: `ops_closed_manually`, `time_box_expired_auto_closed`, `ops_admin_force_closed`, `customer_owner_revoked`, `system_error_closed`, `residency_evacuation_closed`); nullable | Populated at `ended_at`. |
| `session_state` | Enum | Appendix J `ops_session_state` (new: `pending_quorum`, `active`, `closing`, `closed`, `force_closed`, `expired`); required | State machine per §50.4.3. |
| `actions_taken_count` | Integer | ≥ 0; default 0 | Count of Ops-tagged audit events emitted under this session's scope (see AC #8). Incremented atomically on each child audit-event write in the same Convex transaction. |
| `mutation_count` | Integer | ≥ 0; default 0 | Count of mutating (`action` ∈ {`created`, `updated`, `deleted`, `archived`, `submitted`, `approved`, `rejected`, `advanced_phase`, `reverted`, `amended`, `signed`} or any `billing_admin_action`) audit events under this session. A session with `mutation_count > 0` triggers a mandatory post-session review surface for the customer Org Owner per §50.4.5. |
| `read_count` | Integer | ≥ 0; default 0 | Count of read-only audit events under this session (where `action` is a view/read verb). |
| `customer_owner_notified_open_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Stamped when the Org Owner notification email / in-app Inbox item for session-open delivered (§50.4.5). Null until Loops.so confirms `202 Accepted`. |
| `customer_owner_notified_open_dispatch_attempts` | Integer | ≥ 0; ≤ 5; default 0 | Retry counter; §50.4.5 retry curve. |
| `customer_owner_notified_close_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Stamped when the Org Owner notification for session-close delivered. |
| `customer_owner_notified_close_dispatch_attempts` | Integer | ≥ 0; ≤ 5; default 0 | Retry counter. |
| `customer_owner_notification_failure_code` | Enum | Appendix J `ops_session_notification_failure_code` (new: `loops_dispatch_unrecoverable`, `no_owner_resolvable`, `residency_legal_hold_suppressed`, `none`); required; default `none` | Captures the terminal failure mode if either dispatch fails after 5 attempts. `no_owner_resolvable` is the residual case where an Org has no active Org Owner (pathological; §50.4.5 FM #3). |
| `residency_region_at_open` | Enum | `us`, `eu`, `uk`, `apac` (per §40.3); required | Snapshot of the customer Org's residency region at open; used to validate that the Ops user's assigned data-residency-access tier permits the session (§50.4.1). |
| `ip_address_origin` | String | Max 64 chars; required | Ops user's source IP at session-open (IPv4 / IPv6). Masked per §40.5 retention rules. |
| `user_agent_origin` | String | Max 1,000 chars; required | Ops user's browser / CLI user agent at session-open. |
| `auth_factor_evidence_json` | JSON | ≤ 4,000 chars; required | Evidence that the Ops user satisfied §50.2.2 auth requirements (WorkOS SSO + hardware-key MFA + step-up re-auth within 5 minutes of `started_at`). Fields: `sso_session_id`, `mfa_factor_id`, `step_up_reauthed_at`, `step_up_reauth_method ∈ {webauthn, yubikey_u2f}`. |
| `api_request_ids_count` | Integer | ≥ 0; default 0 | Authoritative scalar counter of `request_id` values emitted under this session (supersedes the pre-existing `api_request_ids` array document-field storage — Authored Extension #37 cascade, reconciling the §4.6.3 storage strategy to avoid unbounded Convex document growth). Incremented atomically in the same Convex transaction as the per-request middleware write (AC #8). |
| `api_request_ids_recent_100` | Array[UUID] | 0–100 entries; required; default `[]` | Rolling-window denormalized array of the 100 most-recent `request_id` values for the session, powering hot UX paths (Ops session-detail drawer, Customer-Visible Projection's "recent activity" slice) with O(1) read cost. Overwritten on each new API call (FIFO eviction at the 100-row cap). Invariant: `|api_request_ids_recent_100| == min(api_request_ids_count, 100)`. |
| `api_request_ids_table_ref` | UUID (FK) | Required; → `OpsSessionApiRequestLink` sharded link table (§4.6.4 — authored 2026-05-01 per D-1V3-002 remediation; pre-remediation stub annotation "Pending Follow-Through" retired) | FK pointer to the denormalized link table that carries the full history of `(ops_session_id, api_request_id, emitted_at, ordinal)` tuples with O(log N) seek. Reads that require the full history (forensic export, DSAR fulfillment, insider-threat investigation) join through this pointer. Writes to the link table and to `api_request_ids_recent_100` are wrapped in a single Convex mutation; invariant `ops_session_api_request_id_denorm_invariant` deploy-time test asserts that `api_request_ids_count == COUNT(OpsSessionApiRequestLink WHERE ops_session_id=<this>)` after every write. **Migration note.** Sessions created before the §50 Phase 6 Verification Remediation (2026-04-21) carry legacy `api_request_ids: Array[UUID]` document storage; the migration path backfills `api_request_ids_count = |legacy_array|`, `api_request_ids_recent_100 = last(legacy_array, 100)`, and hydrates the link table from the legacy array; the legacy field is read-shadowed for the migration window then retired. The 10,000-entry soft cap from the legacy strategy is replaced with a per-session hard cap of 100,000 link-table rows (§50.4.6 AC #9 extension) above which writes return HTTP 429 `ops_session_api_request_volume_exceeded` and page `ops_security_admin` (indicator of an abusive session). The pre-existing §42 P2 alert on 10,000 soft-cap breach is retained as a leading indicator. |
| `force_close_actor_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → Ops User OR Org Owner User | Populated when `session_state = 'force_closed'`. Ops Admin can force-close any session; Org Owner can revoke via §50.4.7 customer revocation surface. |
| `force_close_reason_note` | String | 0–2,000 chars; nullable | Required when `session_state = 'force_closed'`. |
| `parent_ops_session_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; self-reference | Populated when a new session is opened within 60 seconds of a prior session's close to continue the same investigation. Chain length capped at 10 per §50.4.6 AC #11; exceeding raises `ops_session_chain_depth_exceeded`. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by` | Standard | Immutable after creation for `created_at`, `created_by`; `updated_at`, `updated_by` follow counter updates | No `deleted_at`. OpsSession is append-only; state changes mutate `session_state`, `ended_at`, and counters only. |

**Scope.** Platform-scoped. Lives in the platform-shared Ops audit partition; no `org_id` on the row itself — `org_id_impersonated` is the customer-side identifier used for cross-reference. Read access: the Ops user who opened the session, any `ops_admin`, `ops_audit_reviewer`, and the customer Org Owner of `org_id_impersonated` (read-only, read-subset projection per §50.4.8). Write access: the Ops middleware (mutations constrained to state-machine transitions); no direct human writes. Customer-console reads by any role other than Org Owner return HTTP 404 per §7.2 Dual-Console Firewall non-leak rule; the Org Owner's read returns the `customer_visible_projection` (omits `auth_factor_evidence_json`, `ip_address_origin`, `api_request_ids_count`, `api_request_ids_recent_100`, `api_request_ids_table_ref`, `ops_user_id` replaced with opaque `ops_agent_handle` per §50.4.8).

**Required Indexes.**
- `(org_id_impersonated, started_at DESC)` — per-Org timeline; used by the customer Org Owner's read-subset view and by Ops Cross-Reference queries.
- `(ops_user_id, started_at DESC)` — per-Ops-user session history; used by Ops performance dashboards and insider-threat detection.
- `(session_state, started_at) WHERE session_state IN ('active', 'pending_quorum', 'closing')` — active-session sweeper target; queried every 15 seconds by the time-box enforcer (§50.4.2).
- `(justification_category, started_at DESC)` — justification-class rollups for Ops trend analysis.
- `(linked_support_ticket_ref, started_at DESC) WHERE linked_support_ticket_ref IS NOT NULL` — sparse; powers the Ops Cross-Reference view.
- `(residency_region_at_open, started_at DESC)` — residency-bound Ops audit review.
- `(customer_owner_notification_failure_code, started_at DESC) WHERE customer_owner_notification_failure_code != 'none'` — sparse; powers the §50.4.5 notification-failure remediation queue.

**Retention.** 7 years minimum (Ops audit + regulatory-defense horizon). Matches §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord retention. DSAR pseudonymization applies to `ops_user_id` (replaced with `anonymized_former_ops_user_<hash>` per §6.8.5) and to `impersonated_user_id` (when the impersonated customer User requests erasure); the session structure, `justification_category`, `justification_note`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `effective_time_box_minutes`, and counters are preserved under the §6.8.5 row #2 Ops-action audit-integrity retained-row class because the rows substantiate Ops-actor attribution on every mutation executed during the session — removing them would break audit integrity for the downstream mutation rows.

**Relationships.**
- 1:N → §4.6.1 Audit Event (each Ops-initiated audit event populates a new `ops_session_id` FK — §50.5.1 — pointing back to the session).
- 1:N → §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord (when an Ops user executes a discretionary action during an active session, the OpsActionRecord's `linked_ops_session_id` FK — new; Authored Extension — populates from the session).
- 1:N → §4.8.1 AIOperation (every AIOperation whose `actor_type = 'ops'` populates `ops_session_id` FK — new; extends §4.8.1 per RECONCILIATION.md Authored Extension).

**Entity-level acceptance criteria.**
1. OpsSession rows are append-only for `created_at`, `created_by`, `started_at`, `ops_user_id`, `org_id_impersonated`, `justification_category`, `justification_note`, `residency_region_at_open`, `auth_factor_evidence_json`, `console_scope`, `impersonated_user_id`. UPDATE of any of these fields returns HTTP 405 `ops_session_immutable_field_mutation` (Appendix I — new).
2. Every session open MUST satisfy §50.4.1 authentication evidence completeness; missing `auth_factor_evidence_json` fields return HTTP 422 `ops_session_auth_evidence_incomplete` (Appendix I — new).
3. Every session with `effective_time_box_minutes > 60` OR `console_scope = 'both'` OR `justification_category = 'enterprise_escape_hatch'` MUST carry ≥ 2 distinct `quorum_signoff_user_ids`; breach returns HTTP 422 `ops_session_quorum_required` (Appendix I — new).
4. `ended_at` MUST be populated within `effective_time_box_minutes + 120` seconds of `started_at` for every session whose `session_state ≠ 'active'`; the 120-second grace covers the time-box-expiry sweeper and the customer-notification dispatch window. Breach raises a §42 P1 alert and pages `ops_security_admin`.
5. `customer_owner_notified_open_at` MUST be populated within 300 seconds of `started_at` for sessions whose `customer_owner_notification_failure_code = 'none'`. Breach raises a §42 P2 alert.
6. `customer_owner_notified_close_at` MUST be populated within 300 seconds of `ended_at` for sessions whose `customer_owner_notification_failure_code = 'none'`. Breach raises a §42 P2 alert.
7. When `session_state = 'closed'` OR `'expired'` OR `'force_closed'`, the time-box sweeper MUST NOT re-open or extend the session; extension requires a new OpsSession row (chainable via `parent_ops_session_id`).
8. Every customer-API call carrying an Ops auth context (§50.2.3) MUST either (a) reference an active OpsSession whose `org_id_impersonated` matches the call's `org_id`, or (b) be rejected with HTTP 403 `ops_session_required_for_ops_actor` (Appendix I — new). The middleware MUST atomically (i) increment `actions_taken_count`, (ii) increment `mutation_count` OR `read_count` based on action kind, (iii) increment `api_request_ids_count`, append the `request_id` to `api_request_ids_recent_100` with FIFO eviction at the 100-entry cap, AND insert a row into the `OpsSessionApiRequestLink` sharded link table, (iv) emit a §4.6.1 Audit Event row with `actor_type = 'ops_actor'`, `ops_session_id` populated, in the same Convex transaction. The `ops_session_api_request_id_denorm_invariant` deploy-time test asserts `api_request_ids_count == COUNT(OpsSessionApiRequestLink WHERE ops_session_id=<this>)` at all times; violations page `ops_platform_admin`.
9. Customer-console reads of OpsSession rows by any role other than the customer Org Owner of `org_id_impersonated` MUST return HTTP 404 `ops_session_cross_console_access_denied` (Appendix I — new). The Org Owner read returns the `customer_visible_projection` ONLY.
10. Soft-delete / hard-delete of OpsSession rows is forbidden before the 7-year retention horizon; DELETE attempts return HTTP 405 `ops_session_append_only`.

**Failure modes (required ≥ 3 per §50 Counterfactual Pass — authored per project convention #17).**
1. **Ops network drop mid-session.** If the Ops user's browser loses connection after session open but before `ops_closed_manually`, the time-box sweeper (§50.4.2) auto-closes the session at `started_at + effective_time_box_minutes`. The customer notification dispatch proceeds as if Ops had clicked "End session". No Ops-side retry mechanism leaves sessions artificially open; an orphan sweep at 15-second cadence asserts invariant.
2. **Concurrent Ops session on same Org.** Two Ops users may hold concurrent active sessions on the same `org_id_impersonated` when `console_scope` and `impersonated_user_id` do not conflict. When a second session attempts to open with an overlapping `impersonated_user_id` AND `console_scope`, the write is rejected with HTTP 409 `ops_session_overlap_conflict` (Appendix I — new); the second Ops user must either request quorum-approved override or wait. Concurrent sessions that do not conflict are permitted and each populates an independent session row.
3. **Customer Org Owner notification dispatch fails 5 times.** Loops.so retry curve exhausted at attempt 5; `customer_owner_notification_failure_code` is set to `loops_dispatch_unrecoverable`; the session does NOT block on the notification — the Ops middleware continues to accept mutations, but a §42 P1 alert fires immediately and the session is flagged for `ops_security_admin` forensic review. The customer Org Owner is notified via a secondary channel (in-app Inbox item + Zendesk ticket auto-opened against the Ops user's team) per §50.4.5 fallback; the fallback is also retry-bounded with its own failure code `no_owner_resolvable` for the pathological case of an Org with no active Owner.
4. **Residency-region mismatch.** Ops user's data-residency-access tier (§50.2.2) does NOT cover the Org's `residency_region_at_open`. Session open rejected with HTTP 403 `ops_session_residency_access_denied` (Appendix I — new); no partial row is created. Known failure mode: Ops user with `us` tier attempts to open session on an EU Org mid-incident — escalation path is for an EU-residency-tier Ops user to open the session instead.
5. **Step-up re-auth elapsed.** `step_up_reauthed_at` must be within 5 minutes of `started_at`; if elapsed, session open is rejected with HTTP 403 `ops_session_step_up_reauth_stale` (Appendix I — new); Ops user redirected to re-auth.
6. **Quorum signer is the same Ops user as `ops_user_id`.** Session open rejected with HTTP 422 `ops_session_quorum_self_signoff_forbidden` (Appendix I — new). Enforces separation-of-duties.
7. **Ops Admin force-close races the time-box expiry.** Both `ops_admin_force_closed` and `time_box_expired_auto_closed` transitions target `session_state = 'closed'`; whichever acquires the Convex transaction first wins. If both writes arrive within 100 ms, the resolution rule is: force-close precedes time-box (force-close represents explicit Ops intent; time-box is advisory). The loser's action records a §42 observability note `ops_session_close_race_resolved` but is non-fatal.
8. **Customer Org Owner revokes mid-session.** `customer_owner_revoked` transition populates `force_close_actor_user_id = owner_user_id`; session state transitions to `force_closed` within 15 seconds of the revoke API call; in-flight Ops mutations that began pre-revoke but commit post-revoke are force-rolled-back via the middleware and return HTTP 409 `ops_session_closed_mid_request` (Appendix I — new) to the Ops user.
9. **Authored-extension linkage: pre-existing OpsActionRecord rows without `linked_ops_session_id`.** Historical rows from pre-§50 deploys lack the field; backfill rule: rows with `created_at < §50 deploy date` leave `linked_ops_session_id` null; a migration-complete CI gate `ops_action_record_ops_session_link_post_cutover` asserts 100% population for rows with `created_at ≥ §50 deploy date`.

**Authored Extension flag.** The new fields `ops_session_id` on §4.6.1 Audit Event, `linked_ops_session_id` on §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord, and `ops_session_id` on §4.8.1 AIOperation are authored extensions to those entities and require human sign-off. Registered in `/Sourcera/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions → §50 Ops Console (2026-04-21)`.

### 4.6.4 OpsSessionApiRequestLink (Platform-Scoped, Append-Only, Sharded Link Table) {#4.6.4-opssessionapirequestlink}

**Authoring Intent (D-1V3-002 remediation, 2026-05-01).** OpsSessionApiRequestLink is the per-API-call link record that materializes the full history referenced by §4.6.3 OpsSession line 7274 (`api_request_ids_table_ref`) and AC #8 line 7306 (the atomic-transaction contract requiring per-request middleware to "insert a row into the `OpsSessionApiRequestLink` sharded link table"). The pre-remediation §4.6.3 v7.1.0 referenced this entity as "Pending Follow-Through: full entity registration in §4.6 during the next §50 reconciliation pass" but never authored it; AC #8 was unbuildable, the deploy-time invariant `ops_session_api_request_id_denorm_invariant` had no row source, and the migration path from legacy `api_request_ids: Array[UUID]` could not run. This sub-section closes that gap.

**Scope.** Platform-scoped. Lives in the platform-shared Ops audit partition adjacent to §4.6.3 OpsSession; no `org_id` on the row itself — the join through `ops_session_id → OpsSession.org_id_impersonated` resolves to the customer Org for cross-reference queries. Read access: the Ops user who owned the parent OpsSession, any `ops_admin`, `ops_audit_reviewer`, and the customer Org Owner of the impersonated Org (read-only, redacted projection per §6.8.5 Pattern B applied to `OpsSession`). Write access: the Ops middleware in the same atomic Convex mutation that increments `OpsSession.api_request_ids_count` and appends to `OpsSession.api_request_ids_recent_100`; no direct human writes; no UPDATE / DELETE permitted (append-only).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key, immutable | Auto-generated. |
| `ops_session_id` | UUID (FK) | Required; → §4.6.3 OpsSession; `ON DELETE RESTRICT` (OpsSession is append-only and not deletable, so this is defense-in-depth) | The parent session. |
| `ordinal` | BigInt | ≥ 1; monotonically increasing within `ops_session_id`; immutable | Per-session sequence number. Combined with `ops_session_id`, this is the natural key for ordered history reconstruction. The atomic Convex mutation increments this in the same transaction as `OpsSession.api_request_ids_count`. |
| `api_request_id` | UUID | Required; immutable | The `request_id` propagated from the §32 API ingress middleware (one per HTTP request). |
| `emitted_at` | Timestamp | Immutable; required | UTC; the moment the API call commit emitted the link row. |
| `mutation_or_read` | Enum (Appendix J `ops_session_api_request_kind` — new: `mutation`, `read`) | Required | Mirrors the §4.6.3 `OpsSession.mutation_count` / `OpsSession.read_count` partition. Determines which counter incremented in the same transaction. |
| `request_action` | String(48) | Required; controlled-vocabulary string per §4.6.1.1 `audit_event_action_type` | The action string of the §4.6.1 Audit Event row written in the same transaction. Joining through `(ops_session_id, ordinal, request_action)` reconstructs the per-request audit trail in O(log N) seek time. |
| `request_entity_type` | String(48) | Required; controlled-vocabulary string per §4.6.1.1 `audit_event_entity_type` | The entity_type acted upon by the request. |
| `request_entity_id` | UUID | Nullable | The entity_id acted upon (null for read-broad operations like list endpoints). |
| `audit_event_id` | UUID (FK) | Required; → §4.6.1 Audit Event | The Audit Event row written in the same Convex transaction. Joining through this FK avoids re-reading the OpsSession-scoped Audit Event subset for forensic export. |
| `redaction_state` | Enum (Appendix J `ops_session_api_request_link_redaction_state` — new: `active`, `dsar_pseudonymized_via_ops_session`, `dsar_pseudonymized_via_customer_subject`) | Required; default `active` | Set when DSAR cascade pseudonymizes the parent OpsSession's `ops_user_id` or the customer subject's identity reference. The link row itself is never hard-deleted. |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC; equals `emitted_at` at write time. |

**Required Indexes.**
- `(ops_session_id, ordinal)` UNIQUE — the natural key; powers ordered-history reconstruction and the `ops_session_api_request_id_denorm_invariant` row-count assertion.
- `(ops_session_id, emitted_at DESC)` — powers per-session forensic export (chronological).
- `(api_request_id)` — powers reverse lookup from a §32 API request ID to the owning OpsSession.
- `(audit_event_id)` UNIQUE — assertion that exactly one link row joins to each Audit Event row written under an Ops session.
- `(emitted_at) WHERE redaction_state != 'active'` partial — DSAR audit-of-audit query path.

**Sharding Strategy.** Sharded by `(ops_session_id, ordinal)` per the §4.6.3 line 7274 contract. Each session's link rows live on a single shard; read queries that reconstruct a session's full history hit one shard. The shard map is published in §42.3 storage-scaling tables (Authored Extension flagged). At a per-session hard cap of 100,000 rows and an empirical median session of 200 API calls, the platform-wide row volume scales linearly with active OpsSession count and is bounded.

**Per-Session Hard Cap.** 100,000 link rows per `ops_session_id` per the §4.6.3 line 7274 contract. The 100,000th row's commit triggers HTTP 429 `ops_session_api_request_volume_exceeded` (Appendix I — registered at §4.6.3 line 7274) on subsequent OpsSession-bound API calls AND pages `ops_security_admin` (the soft-cap-at-10,000 alert is the leading indicator; 100,000 is the hard cap). The session itself is NOT auto-closed at hard cap — the Ops user can finish the in-flight request that caused the breach but is blocked on subsequent requests; the time-box sweeper will close the session per the standard `effective_time_box_minutes` window.

**Retention.** 7 years aligned with §4.6.3 OpsSession retention. Hard-delete forbidden at the application layer — same append-only invariant as the parent. DSAR pseudonymization applies to (a) `ops_user_id` of the parent OpsSession via §6.8.5 Pattern B (link row's `ops_session_id` FK preserved; the OpsSession row's `ops_user_id` row pseudonymizes via the User entity), and (b) the customer subject's identity reference IF the link row's `request_entity_type = user` AND `request_entity_id = subject_user_id` — in which case `redaction_state` transitions to `dsar_pseudonymized_via_customer_subject` and `request_entity_id` is rewritten to the canonical `anonymized_<console>_user_<base32(hash)[:16]>` pseudonym (note: this column type is `UUID` — see §6.8.4.1 Pattern A; the link table follows Pattern A because the column type is large enough and the User row is hard-deleted at DSAR for pure-PII rows). Cascade scope: when the customer subject is DSAR-pseudonymized, the cascade walker batches link rows in chunks of 1,000 and forward-recovers per §6.8.4 partial-failure rule; the long-tail-cascade alert at §6.8.4 fires if affected-row count exceeds 50,000.

**Relationships.**
- Many-to-one → §4.6.3 OpsSession (`ops_session_id`).
- One-to-one → §4.6.1 Audit Event (`audit_event_id`).
- Reverse-lookup target for §32 API request IDs (when an Ops user files a forensic request "what did session S do at request R?", the platform joins `OpsSessionApiRequestLink ⋈ AuditEvent ⋈ OpsSession`).

**State Machine.** Append-only; no state machine. The `redaction_state` enum is the only mutable column — a one-way transition `active → dsar_pseudonymized_*` triggered by the §6.8.4 cascade walker; no reverse transition.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Every customer-API call carrying an Ops auth context (per §4.6.3 AC #8) MUST insert exactly one OpsSessionApiRequestLink row in the same Convex transaction as the Audit Event row, the OpsSession counter increments, and the rolling-window `api_request_ids_recent_100` update. The atomic-transaction invariant `ops_session_api_request_id_denorm_invariant` (deploy-time test referenced at §4.6.3 line 7274) MUST assert that for every OpsSession, `OpsSession.api_request_ids_count == COUNT(OpsSessionApiRequestLink WHERE ops_session_id=<this>)`. CI gate `ops_session_api_request_link_atomic_transaction` (§M.5 — new) asserts.
2. The unique constraint `(ops_session_id, ordinal)` MUST prevent gap or overlap; concurrent commits resolve via Convex transaction-ordering. QA test `ops_session_api_request_link_ordinal_uniqueness` asserts.
3. Per-session hard cap of 100,000 rows MUST be enforced; the 100,001st insert MUST return HTTP 429 `ops_session_api_request_volume_exceeded` AND page `ops_security_admin` within 60 seconds. QA test `ops_session_api_request_link_hard_cap_enforcement` asserts.
4. DSAR pseudonymization on the parent OpsSession's `ops_user_id` MUST flow through Pattern B (FK preservation; User entity pseudonymized in-place); the link row's `ops_session_id` FK is unchanged and continues to resolve. CI gate `ops_session_api_request_link_dsar_cascade_pattern` asserts.
5. DSAR pseudonymization on a customer subject whose User row is referenced by `request_entity_id` MUST transition `redaction_state → dsar_pseudonymized_via_customer_subject` and rewrite `request_entity_id` to the canonical pseudonym (Pattern A). QA test `ops_session_api_request_link_subject_dsar_redaction` asserts.
6. The migration from the legacy `OpsSession.api_request_ids: Array[UUID]` storage (pre-§50 Phase 6 Verification Remediation 2026-04-21) MUST hydrate this table for every legacy session row; QA test `ops_session_api_request_link_legacy_hydration_migration` asserts the row count and ordering match the legacy array. The legacy field is read-shadowed for the migration window per §4.6.3 line 7274 then retired.
7. Hard-delete attempts on link rows MUST return HTTP 405 `ops_session_api_request_link_append_only` (Appendix I — new). UPDATE attempts on any column except `redaction_state` MUST return HTTP 405 `ops_session_api_request_link_immutable_field_mutation` (Appendix I — new).
8. Customer-Org-Owner reads MUST return only the redacted projection: `{id, ops_session_id, ordinal, emitted_at, mutation_or_read, request_action, request_entity_type, request_entity_id (only when entity_id ∈ subject's own Org's entities, otherwise null), audit_event_id (only when audit_event row is in the customer's read scope per §4.6.1.1 Cross-Console Firewall, otherwise null)}`. Ops-internal fields and cross-Org link rows MUST never appear.

**Failure Modes.**

1. **Convex transaction commits the OpsSession counter increments but fails to insert the link row.** Resolved: the transactional guarantee is atomic per the §31 transactional outbox pattern — both writes commit or both abort. A partial commit is impossible at the database layer; the deploy-time invariant test `ops_session_api_request_id_denorm_invariant` would fail at the next deploy and block the release.
2. **Engineer runs the legacy-array hydration migration twice.** Resolved: migration idempotency keyed by `(ops_session_id, ordinal)` UNIQUE — second-run inserts no-op on existing rows; the `legacy_hydration_run_id` audit-of-audit row records the second-run no-op for forensic continuity.
3. **DSAR cascade encounters a link row whose parent OpsSession was already pseudonymized but the link row's `request_entity_id` still points to the customer subject.** Resolved: cascade walker is two-pass — Pass 1 pseudonymizes parent OpsSessions via Pattern B; Pass 2 walks every link row whose `redaction_state = active` and the customer-subject FK matches, transitioning to `dsar_pseudonymized_via_customer_subject` per Pattern A. Idempotent.
4. **Per-session hard cap of 100,000 reached during a legitimately high-volume incident-response session.** Resolved: the time-box-bounded session is, by §4.6.3 design, capped at 480 minutes (8 hours); 100,000 link rows in 480 minutes is ~210 requests/minute, well above realistic Ops-tool usage. The cap is intentionally aggressive to function as an insider-threat detector. Ops Admin can request a quorum-approved high-volume override per §50.4.4 (authored extension flagged).
5. **Migration job times out on a high-volume legacy OpsSession (e.g., 50,000 legacy api_request_ids).** Resolved: migration job processes legacy rows in chunks of 1,000 link inserts per Convex transaction; per-session migration time bounded by `(legacy_array_length / 1000) * avg_chunk_time`. Forward-recovery on partial failure per §6.8.4.

**Authored Extension flag.** This entity is registered in `/Sourcera/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions → §50 Ops Console (2026-04-21)` as the AE-15 v7.1.1 follow-through to the §50 Phase 6 Verification Remediation; AE-D1V3-02 transitions `pending → ratified` on the v7.1.1 stamp.

### 4.6.5 DSARRequest (D-3.5-002 remediation, 2026-05-04) {#4.6.5-dsar-request}

**Authoring intent.** §6.8.6 references five fields (`verified_at`, `extension_reason`, `fulfilled_at`, `dsar_subject_acknowledged_at`, `dsar_partial_failure_notified_at`) on a DSARRequest entity that pre-V3 had no §4 entity table. §40.2 cited a "GDPR deletion request" row with no entity backing. This sub-section authors DSARRequest as a first-class persisted entity. Tagged Authored Extension (AE-3.5-006) — pending Privacy Officer + Engineering ratification before v7.1.1 stamp.

**Field table.**

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK; required | Entity primary key. |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | nullable; null only for cross-Org DSAR per §6.8.6.2 | FK → §4.2.1 Organization. Per-Org DSAR: scoped. Cross-Org DSAR (subject is account-holder in N Orgs): platform-scoped (null). |
| `subject_user_id` | UUID (FK) | nullable; null only for third-party DSAR per §6.8.6.1 | FK → §4.2.3 User. |
| `subject_email_hash` | String(64) | sha256 hex; required for third-party DSAR; optional otherwise | Used for non-account-holder verification at submission. |
| `request_kind` | Enum | required; values per Appendix J Phase-3V cluster `dsar_request_kind` | One of `access`, `rectification`, `erasure_anonymize`, `erasure_complete_deletion`, `restriction`, `portability`, `objection`, `automated_decision_review`. |
| `received_at` | Timestamp | required; default `now()` | DSAR submission timestamp. |
| `verified_at` | Timestamp | nullable; stamped on §6.8.6.1 successful verification | SLA clock-start trigger per §6.8.6. |
| `verification_method` | Enum | nullable; values per Appendix J Phase-3V cluster `dsar_verification_method` | One of `signed_in_session`, `magic_link_email`, `id_document_review`, `multi_factor`. |
| `verification_failure_count` | INT | default 0 | Per §6.8.6.1 cooldown sequence. |
| `state` | Enum | required; values per Appendix J Phase-3V cluster `dsar_request_state` | One of `received`, `verifying`, `verified`, `in_progress`, `extended`, `fulfilled`, `failed`, `withdrawn`, `manifestly_unfounded_rejected`. |
| `extension_reason` | Enum | nullable; values per Appendix J Phase-3V cluster `dsar_extension_reason_code` | One of `complex_high_volume`, `multi_jurisdictional`, `vendor_dependency`. Stamps the §6.8.6 +60d extension trigger. |
| `extension_granted_at` | Timestamp | nullable | Audit trail for the extension grant. |
| `fulfilled_at` | Timestamp | nullable; stamped on §6.8.6 fulfillment | SLA-clock-end. |
| `dsar_subject_acknowledged_at` | Timestamp | nullable; stamped on §6.8.6 72-hour acknowledgment | Per §6.8.6 AC #4. |
| `dsar_partial_failure_notified_at` | Timestamp | nullable; stamped on §6.8.4 partial-failure 24-hour notice | Per §6.8.6 AC #4. |
| `cascade_completed_at` | Timestamp | nullable | §6.8.4 cascade walker completion. |
| `audit_integrity_exemptions_invoked_json` | JSON | nullable; max 4,000 chars | Enumeration of §6.8.5 row classes invoked during cascade with retention-window cite. |
| `data_residency_region` | Enum (Appendix J `data_residency_region`) | required | DSAR cascade fork-key per §6.8.4.2. For account-holder DSAR, initialized from `User.home_residency_region`; for Org-admin-on-behalf DSAR, initialized from the initiating Organization.`data_residency_region`; for third-party DSAR, selected by the verified subject-evidence scope. |
| `objection_basis` | Enum | nullable; required only when `request_kind = objection`; per Phase-3V cluster `dsar_objection_basis` | One of `legitimate_interest`, `direct_marketing`, `statistical_purpose`, `automated_decision`. |
| `decision_id` | UUID (FK) | nullable; required only when `request_kind = automated_decision_review` | FK → §4.8.1 AIOperation. |
| `rejection_trigger_condition` | Enum | nullable; stamped on `manifestly_unfounded_rejected` transition; per Phase-3V cluster `dsar_rejection_trigger_condition` | One of `verification_failure_3x`, `same_kind_5x_30d`, `cross_org_20x_30d`, `ops_manual_flag`, `sim_coordinated_flood`. |
| `rejection_dual_signoff_actors` | JSON | nullable; required when `rejection_trigger_condition = ops_manual_flag` | Array of two actor IDs (Ops reviewer + Privacy Officer). |
| `rejection_subject_notified_at` | Timestamp | nullable | §6.8.6.2 72-hour subject notification stamp. |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | required; default `now()` | |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | required; auto-updated on every mutation | |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | required | Subject (account-holder path) OR system actor (third-party DSAR path). |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | required; auto-updated | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | nullable | Soft-delete timestamp. Hard-deletion forbidden — DSARRequest is itself an audit record per §6.8.5 audit-integrity exemption. |

**Indexes.**

- `(org_id, state, verified_at)` — primary cascade-worker scan index.
- `(state, verified_at)` partial WHERE `state IN ('verified', 'in_progress', 'extended')` — SLA-sweep index for the §6.8.6 30-day enforcement.
- `(subject_user_id, request_kind)` — subject's own DSAR history.
- `(subject_email_hash)` — third-party DSAR lookup.
- `(rejection_trigger_condition, received_at)` — fraud-pattern detection per §6.8.6.2.

**Scope isolation.**

- Org-scoped except for cross-Org DSAR which is platform-scoped (`org_id = null`).
- Cross-console: DSAR is universal (subject-rights are not partitioned by buyer/seller console); cascade walker per §6.8.4.2 partitions by data-residency region only.
- Buyer/Seller firewall: DSARRequest never crosses the §1.3 firewall — the cascade walker reads source rows and writes redaction outcomes, but the DSARRequest entity itself is not surfaced to the partner console.

**Retention.**

- 7 years per §6.8.5 audit-integrity exemption (DSAR fulfillment is itself an audit-integrity record).
- Residency-partitioned per `data_residency_region`.
- Hard-deletion forbidden; soft-delete via `deleted_at` only.

**State machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `received` | INSERT | DSAR submission via UI / API / public surface | `received_at` stamped. |
| `received` | `verifying` | Verification attempt initiated | Per §6.8.6.1 method | `verification_method` stamped. |
| `verifying` | `verified` | Verification succeeds | Per §6.8.6.1 success per method | `verified_at` stamped. SLA clock starts. |
| `verifying` | `manifestly_unfounded_rejected` | Verification fails 3× within 7d OR Ops manual flag OR SIM coordinated flood | Per §6.8.6.2 trigger conditions | `rejection_trigger_condition` stamped. |
| `verified` | `in_progress` | Cascade walker dispatched | Standard fulfillment path | — |
| `in_progress` | `extended` | Complex / high-volume request | `extension_reason` stamped within 30d ceiling | One-time extension up to +60d per §6.8.6. |
| `in_progress` | `fulfilled` | Cascade complete + acknowledgment delivered | Standard fulfillment | `fulfilled_at` stamped. |
| `extended` | `fulfilled` | Cascade complete within 90d ceiling | — | `fulfilled_at` stamped. |
| `verified` / `in_progress` / `extended` | `failed` | Unrecoverable cascade error | Per §6.8.4 partial-failure procedure | Subject notified via `dsar_partial_failure_notified_at`. |
| `received` / `verifying` / `verified` | `withdrawn` | Subject withdrawal | Subject UI / API request | Withdrawal is irrevocable; subject must file fresh DSAR. |
| (any) | `manifestly_unfounded_rejected` | Per §6.8.6.2 triggers | Documented rationale + dual sign-off where applicable | `rejection_subject_notified_at` stamped within 72h. |

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Every DSARRequest INSERT MUST set `state = 'received'` and stamp `received_at`. CI gate `dsar_request_initial_state_received`.
2. State transitions MUST follow the table above; out-of-table transitions return HTTP 422 `dsar_request_invalid_state_transition` (Appendix I — new). Property test `dsar_request_state_machine_completeness`.
3. Hard-deletion of DSARRequest rows MUST return HTTP 422 `dsar_request_hard_delete_forbidden` (Appendix I — new). Property test.
4. The §6.8.6 SLA clock starts at `verified_at`; `fulfilled_at - verified_at ≤ 30d` unless `extension_reason IS NOT NULL`, in which case `≤ 90d`. CI gate `dsar_request_30d_90d_sla_enforcement`.
5. DSARRequest residency partitioning per §6.8.4.2 MUST honor `data_residency_region`; cross-region cascade requires DPO approval per §6.8.4.2.
6. Indexes per "Indexes" block MUST be present. CI gate `dsar_request_indexes_present`.

**Failure modes.**

1. Subject submits, then changes legitimate circumstance before `verified_at` (e.g., subject's role change). Resolution: subject withdraws and re-submits; the original record is `withdrawn`-tagged per the state machine.
2. Cascade walker encounters a row in a §6.8.5-exempt row class. Resolution: per §6.8.4 AC #4 partial-failure procedure; emits `dsar.audit_integrity_exemption_invoked` AuditEvent and continues for non-exempt rows.
3. Cross-region cascade required (subject's `data_residency_region` was changed mid-cascade). Resolution: DPO approval required per §6.8.4.2; cascade walker resumes from prior cursor with new partition key.
4. SCIM webhook arrives mid-cascade deprovisioning the subject. Resolution: §6.9 cascade is the upstream event; DSAR cascade is the downstream consumer; idempotent on `(scim_event_id, subject_user_id)`.
