## 4.7 Cross-Console Bridge Entities {#4.7-cross-console-bridge-entities}

**Authoring Intent.** §4.7 consolidates the entities that materialize the cross-console data flow defined in §25 (Console Bridge / Firewall / Disqualification). Two entities live here: Console Bridge Event, the per-change sync unit between a Buyer Workspace and linked Seller Bid Workspaces per Summary C.116 and C.117; and Vendor Disqualification Record, the first-class audit object for the disqualification workflow per Summary C.118 and §25.3. Both entities straddle the Dual-Console Firewall by design, and both carry explicit, testable field-level redaction rules so the firewall remains intact. Authored per PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS.md Conventions #1–#10.

### 4.7.1 Console Bridge Event (Cross-Console, Firewall-Bounded Sync Unit) {#4.7.1-console-bridge-event}

**Authoring Intent.** Console Bridge Event is the authoritative materialization of a single atomic cross-console change. Every Buyer-Workspace Requirement edit, Use Case re-structure, phase advancement, Q&A post, Amendment, NDA execution, EOI acceptance, and Disqualification that must reach the linked Seller Bid Workspace(s) produces one (or, for fan-out events, N) Console Bridge Event rows. Each row is the durable record of the sync attempt; it carries the redacted payload, retry state, bounded-lag SLO metadata, conflict resolution disposition, and cross-Workspace correlation. Per Summary C.116 the bridge is the only mechanism that carries buyer data into a seller's Bid Workspace without breaching the Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2).

**Scope:** Cross-Console. The row's logical home is the Buyer Workspace (`buyer_workspace_id` primary scope) but the row is also readable by the linked Seller Org's `bid_workspace_id` for the seller-side rendering. The row itself lives in the platform-shared bridge-event storage partition with strict authoring-side isolation: seller-console reads are filtered at the serializer to the `seller_visible_projection` (see below); seller writes to this table are REJECTED uniformly (HTTP 403; `console_bridge_event_seller_write_forbidden`). Ops has full read and state-machine transition authority.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `buyer_org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | Buyer-side Org |
| `seller_org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | Seller-side Org |
| `buyer_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Workspace | Source Workspace |
| `bid_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Bid Workspace | Target Bid Workspace (1 per row; fan-out events create N rows, one per Bid Workspace) |
| `fanout_group_id` | UUID | Nullable | Correlation id for fan-out events (e.g., Amendment broadcast to N vendors) |

Forbidden-kind contract: the §M.5 CI gate `console_bridge_no_defense_view_event_kinds` (line 46544) prohibits any `defense_view.*` kind on the Console Bridge; new forbidden-kind classes are similarly added via §M.5. Every new `event_kind` value MUST be registered with (a) its field-level redaction matrix row (this section's table below) AND (b) its seller-visible projection rule AND (c) its retention class per §4.7.1.1 below; CI gate `console_bridge_event_kind_completeness` asserts. |
| `direction` | Enum | See Appendix J `console_bridge_event_direction`: `buyer_to_seller`, `seller_to_buyer` | Dataflow direction |

| `payload_schema_version` | Integer | ≥ 1 | Schema version for the kind-specific payload shape |

| `sync_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `console_bridge_event_sync_status`: `pending`, `synced`, `retrying`, `failed`, `dlq`, `superseded` | See State Machine |

| `last_attempt_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Most recent apply attempt |

D-6.1-012: renamed from the former `console_bridge_standard` label, which is retired as a webhook retry class — Bridge-domain *webhooks* use the Appendix F.1 `standard` curve. |
| `retry_count` | Integer | 0–5 | Attempts; capped at 5 before `dlq` |
| `failure_reason` | Enum | Nullable; see Appendix J `console_bridge_event_failure_reason`: `target_bid_workspace_missing`, `target_bid_workspace_disqualified`, `vendor_withdrawn`, `bid_workspace_readonly`, `schema_mismatch`, `payload_too_large`, `downstream_timeout`, `persistent_firewall_violation_suspected`, `other_transient`, `other_permanent` | Populated on every failed/retrying/dlq transition |
| `failure_note` | String | 0–2000 chars | Diagnostic note; MUST NOT contain buyer-internal content (redaction check) |
| `conflict_resolution` | Enum | Nullable; see Appendix J `console_bridge_event_conflict_resolution`: `last_write_wins`, `buyer_origin_wins`, `operation_non_idempotent_dlq`, `merge_op` | How concurrent edits on the same source were reconciled; null when no conflict |
| `superseded_by_event_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; self-ref → Console Bridge Event | For `superseded` state: newer event for the same source supersedes this one |
| `slo_bounded_lag_ms` | Integer | ≥ 0, nullable | Observed lag in milliseconds between source-write and `synced_at`; populated at transition to `synced` |
| `slo_breach_flag` | Boolean | Default false | True when `slo_bounded_lag_ms > 30000` (30-second SLO per C.117) |
| `redaction_verification_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex | Hash over canonicalized `payload_json` asserting that no forbidden field (see below) is present; verified at write and re-verified on every retry |
| `cross_console_audit_trail` | JSON | ≤ 8000 chars | Denormalized summary: who authored source, who triggered bridge, timestamps, for Ops forensics |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID (buyer-side author) or synthetic Ops/system UUID | Originator |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Last updater (typically system) |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete via Ops GDPR path only |

**Indexes.** `(buyer_workspace_id, created_at DESC)`, `(bid_workspace_id, created_at DESC)`, `(sync_status, next_retry_at)` for the retry scheduler, `(idempotency_key)` unique, `(fanout_group_id)` partial, `(slo_breach_flag, created_at)` partial where true for SLO dashboards, `(source_entity_type, source_entity_id, source_entity_version)` for ordered-application queries, `(superseded_by_event_id)` partial.

**Scope Isolation.**

- **Buyer-console reads:** `buyer_workspace_id` MUST match `session.workspace_id`; workspace RBAC applies. Returned payload is the full `payload_json` (buyer authored it). Row-level columns are returned in full to the buyer side.
- **Seller-console reads:** `bid_workspace_id` MUST match `session.bid_workspace_id`; bid-workspace RBAC applies. The seller-side projection is **row-level firewall-bounded** (D-1.6-001 remediation, 2026-05-01) — both `payload_json` AND row-level columns are filtered. See *Row-Level Seller Projection* below.
- **Ops reads:** All fields; Ops impersonation requires §35 impersonation audit (C.98).
- **Cross-Org reads:** Blocked. A buyer-console session for Org A attempting to read events for a `buyer_workspace_id` owned by Org B MUST receive HTTP 404 (not 403) with `console_bridge_event_cross_org_access` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 404). Same rule for seller cross-Org.
- **Seller writes:** Unconditionally blocked; HTTP 403 with `console_bridge_event_seller_write_forbidden`.
- **Buyer direct writes:** Not permitted through public API. Events are emitted by server-side side-effect handlers of source-entity mutations (Requirement, Use Case, Q&A Post, etc.). Direct POST to a bridge-event endpoint MUST return HTTP 403 with `console_bridge_event_direct_write_forbidden` (new; Appendix I).

**Row-Level Seller Projection (D-1.6-001 remediation, 2026-05-01).**

The pre-remediation Scope Isolation block (V1.2-era) constrained only `payload_json` via the kind-specific `seller_visible_projection`. The defense-in-depth seller serializer described below applied to `payload_json` content only — the row-level columns (`created_by`, `cross_console_audit_trail`, `failure_note`, `fanout_group_id`, `payload_content_hash`, `redaction_verification_hash`, `superseded_by_event_id`, `slo_bounded_lag_ms`, `slo_breach_flag`, `updated_by`) were returned to the seller-console reader unredacted. `cross_console_audit_trail` carries "who authored source, who triggered bridge, timestamps, for Ops forensics" and exposed buyer-internal authoring information on every seller-side read. This remediation closes the firewall gap.

**Per-row allow-list / redaction matrix.** The seller-console serializer applies the following row-level partition to every Console Bridge Event row before responding:

| Row-level column | Buyer-console read | Seller-console read | Ops read | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | full | full | full | Stable opaque identifier; not subject to redaction |
| `buyer_org_id` | full | **redacted to projection ID per §1.3.2** | full | Seller sees the platform-shared bridge counterparty handle, never the buyer Org's `org_id` |
| `seller_org_id` | **redacted to projection ID per §1.3.2** | full | full | Mirror rule on the buyer side |
| `buyer_workspace_id` | full (only own Workspace per the Buyer-console-reads rule) | **redacted to opaque `bridge_source_handle`** | full | Seller never sees the buyer's `workspace_id` directly — only an opaque handle that resolves only on the buyer side |
| `bid_workspace_id` | n/a — buyer-direction bridge events do not surface in buyer Workspace data; seller-direction events are scoped to the buyer's Workspace via the Console Bridge feed; the buyer never reads `bid_workspace_id` directly | full (only own Bid Workspace per the Seller-console-reads rule) | full | |
| `fanout_group_id` | full | **always replaced with `bridge_fanout_recipient_token = HMAC-SHA256(fanout_group_id ‖ seller_org_id, webhook_secret)`** (per-recipient deterministic pseudonym; D-V6-001 / D-6.1-001 composite remediation, 2026-05-06). The raw `fanout_group_id` is NEVER returned to the seller console regardless of single- vs multi-seller fan-out. The seller observes the same token across an arc that targets them (correlation preserved); two different sellers in the same fan-out arc observe different tokens; a seller cannot derive the underlying `fanout_group_id` and therefore cannot infer cardinality. | full | Pre-remediation rule "null when multi-seller / full when single-seller" (V1.6-era) was a binary cardinality side-channel violating §25.1.2 line 19702 ("count" never carried). The HMAC pseudonym restores the legitimate seller-side correlation use case (e.g., grouping retries of a single buyer-emitted broadcast on the seller's "Sync Health" panel) without leaking arc cardinality. CI gate `console_bridge_seller_projection_no_cardinality_leak` asserts. |
| `event_kind` | full | full | full | Required for client-side rendering on both sides |
| `direction` | full | full | full | |
| `source_entity_type` | full | full | full | |
| `source_entity_id` | full | **redacted to opaque `bridge_source_entity_handle`** | full | Seller resolves the entity through the bridge payload, not the buyer-side ID |
| `source_entity_version` | full | full | full | Required for ordered-application invariants |
| `payload_json` | full | filtered to `seller_visible_projection` per the Field-Level Redaction matrix below | full | Pre-existing payload-level partition |
| `payload_content_hash` | full | **null** | full | The hash binds the buyer-internal pre-redaction payload; exposing it would let a malicious seller cross-correlate redacted payloads against unredacted payloads if they ever obtain a leak |
| `payload_schema_version` | full | full | full | Required for client-side parsing |
| `idempotency_key` | full | **null** | full | Idempotency key encodes `(buyer_workspace_id, bid_workspace_id, event_kind, source_entity_id, source_entity_version)` — exposes buyer-internal IDs when leaked |
| `sync_status` | full | full | full | Required for Sync Health panel |
| `synced_at` | full | full | full | |
| `last_attempt_at` | full | full | full | |
| `next_retry_at` | full | full | full | Required for retry telemetry |
| `retry_count` | full | full | full | |
| `failure_reason` | full | full | full | Failure-class enum is firewall-safe |
| `failure_note` | full | **redacted via the same firewall validator that redacts `payload_json`** — strings matching `(redaction_check_violation_*, persistent_firewall_violation_suspected, …)` patterns are surfaced as the enum class only with a generic body `"Diagnostic suppressed for firewall integrity; contact Ops if your Bid Workspace is impacted."`; all other notes pass through | full | The pre-remediation field constraint at `failure_note` line 7358 — "MUST NOT contain buyer-internal content (redaction check)" — is now an enforced server-side validator, not author-side guidance |
| `conflict_resolution` | full | full | full | |
| `superseded_by_event_id` | full | **always replaced with `bridge_superseder_recipient_token = HMAC-SHA256(superseded_by_event_id ‖ seller_org_id, webhook_secret)`** when the superseder targets the same seller; **null** when the superseder targets a different seller (no observable signal that a non-self seller's event superseded this one). D-V6-001 / D-6.1-001 composite remediation, 2026-05-06; the prior cross-fanout-group conditional null was itself a cardinality-class side-channel. | full | Same per-recipient pseudonym pattern as `fanout_group_id`; seller can correlate "their own" supersede chain on the Sync Health panel without learning anything about cross-vendor supersede activity. |
| `slo_bounded_lag_ms` | full | full | full | Required for Sync Health panel; latency telemetry is firewall-safe |
| `slo_breach_flag` | full | full | full | |
| `redaction_verification_hash` | full | **null** | full | Same reasoning as `payload_content_hash` |
| `cross_console_audit_trail` | full | **redacted to seller-safe projection — only seller-side actor identities and seller-side timestamps are returned; buyer-side `who authored source` / buyer User IDs / buyer role snapshots are dropped or pseudonymized via the §6.8.5 canonical form** | full | This is the column that motivated the remediation |
| `created_at` | full | full | full | |
| `updated_at` | full | full | full | |

**Defense-in-Depth Row-Level Seller Projection (D-1.6-001 remediation, extended by D-V6-001 / D-6.1-001 / D-V6-004 composite remediation 2026-05-06).** Two property tests guard the row-level partition:

1. **`console_bridge_seller_row_level_projection_defense_in_depth`** (D-1.6-001) — enumerates every row-level column AND every Appendix J `console_bridge_event_kind` value, generates synthetic rows with worst-case buyer-internal content in every redactable column, and asserts the seller serializer emits null / opaque-handle / pseudonymized values per the table above.
2. **`console_bridge_seller_projection_no_cardinality_leak`** (NEW; D-V6-001 / D-6.1-001 composite, 2026-05-06) — for every `event_kind` in Appendix J `console_bridge_event_kind` AND every `payload_json` field in the kind's CARRIED whitelist, asserts (a) no scalar field discloses cardinality of any buyer-internal collection (Target Account list, fan-out group, affected-requirement set, vendor list); (b) no array field returned to the seller has a length tied to a buyer-internal collection size — array fields are either fully buyer-side-only OR per-recipient projected (intersection with the seller's own scope); (c) no row-level field exposes a binary or N-ary signal about the cardinality of any buyer-internal grouping (the prior `null when multi-seller / full when single-seller` rule on `fanout_group_id` is the canonical anti-pattern this test forbids); (d) the per-recipient pseudonym fields (`bridge_fanout_recipient_token`, `bridge_superseder_recipient_token`) are computed deterministically from `(buyer-internal id ‖ seller_org_id, webhook_secret)` such that two distinct sellers in the same fan-out arc observe distinct tokens.

Both CI gates `console_bridge_row_level_seller_projection_consistency` (D-1.6-001) and `console_bridge_seller_projection_no_cardinality_leak` (D-V6-001) assert; deploy is blocked on red on either.

**Forward-compatibility rule.** Every new row-level column added to §4.7.1 in a future release MUST be registered in the row-level allow-list above with explicit Buyer / Seller / Ops projections. The §M.4 `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` CI gate triggers a check against this table. New column additions without a row-level projection row fail CI.

**Field-Level Redaction Rules (Firewall Integrity).** The `payload_json` is REQUIRED to be firewall-compliant at write time. The write-layer redaction validator enforces, by kind:

| Event Kind | Fields CARRIED | Fields NEVER CARRIED |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `requirement_created` | `requirement_id`, `use_case_id`, `title`, `description`, `response_type`, `weight`, `priority`, `order`, `status`, `buyer_workspace_phase` | Internal scores, rubric definitions, scoring scenarios, internal-comment threads, selection-report drafts, intelligence-brief drafts, AI operation prompts, buyer-authored private notes, buyer Team's AgentInstructions, buyer's cost/TCO computations not part of a pricing requirement |
| `requirement_amended` | `requirement_id`, `use_case_id`, `title`, `description`, `response_type`, `weight`, `priority`, `order`, `status`, `amendment_diff_summary`, `buyer_workspace_phase` | Internal scores, full amendment rationale, rubric definitions, scoring scenarios, internal-comment threads, selection-report drafts, intelligence-brief drafts, AI operation prompts, buyer-authored private notes, buyer Team's AgentInstructions, buyer's cost/TCO computations not part of a pricing requirement |
| `requirement_reverted` | `requirement_id`, `use_case_id`, `revert_target_version`, `reverted_by_user_role_snapshot`, `reason_snippet (≤200 chars public)` | Full revert rationale, internal-comment threads around the revert, buyer User ID |
| `revert_propagated` | `requirement_id`, `use_case_id`, `revert_target_version`, `reverted_by_user_role_snapshot`, `reason_snippet (≤200 chars public)` | Full revert rationale, internal-comment threads around the revert, buyer User ID, source Workspace history beyond the reverted Requirement version |
| `requirement_locked` | `requirement_id`, `locked_at`, `locked_reason_public` | Internal rationale; who scored; Agent Pre-Scoring drafts |
| `response_locked` | `requirement_id`, `response_id`, `locked_at`, `locked_reason_public` | Internal rationale; who scored; Agent Pre-Scoring drafts; any buyer-side score or ranking context |
| `use_case_structure_changed` | `use_case_id`, `title`, `description_public`, `lead_role_kind`, `included_requirement_ids`, `order` | Lead user identity (role-only), internal-comment threads, scoring scenarios |
| `qa_thread_post_appended` | `qa_thread_id`, `post_id`, `author_role_snapshot`, `body_markdown`, `attachments_urls` (Convex Storage signed URLs) | Internal comment bodies, Internal Comment Thread ids, mention expansions for buyer-internal users, buyer-internal thread replies |
| `phase_advanced` | `workspace_id`, `from_phase`, `to_phase`, `advanced_at`, `advanced_by_role_snapshot` | User identity (only role), reasons (only phase-specific public message) |
| `nda_executed` | `nda_record_id`, `nda_type`, `executed_at`, `nda_document_url`, `signatory_email_buyer_public`, `signatory_email_seller_public`, `expires_at` | Custom terms NOT auto-redacted (terms ARE carried; NDA content is by definition cross-console); buyer-internal notes about the signatory |
| `response_submitted` | `response_id`, `requirement_id`, `vendor_org_id` (same as seller_org_id), `submitted_at`, `version`, `response_payload` (seller authored; not buyer-internal) | N/A (seller→buyer direction; same redaction rules apply in reverse for buyer-internal data) |
| `disqualification_issued` | `bid_workspace_id`, `disqualified_at`, `notification_body_to_vendor` (vendor-visible copy only; rationale withheld) | Rationale, rationale author, any internal comment context |
| `workspace_canceled` | `workspace_id`, `canceled_at`, `canceled_reason_public` (≤500 chars), `acting_role_snapshot` | Full rationale, internal-comment context, buyer User ID, cancellation impact analysis |
| `workspace_reopened_ops` | `workspace_id`, `reopened_at`, `reopen_reason_public` (≤500 chars), `acting_role_snapshot` | Full Ops rationale, internal-comment context, buyer User ID, Ops note, cross-vendor recovery count |
| `amendment_broadcast` | `amendment_id`, `diff_summary`, `affected_requirement_ids_visible_to_seller` (per-recipient projection: `intersect(amendment.affected_requirement_ids, this_bid_response.requirement_ids)` — the seller learns only which of THEIR active responses are affected; the buyer-side total scope is buyer-internal), `amended_at` | Internal rationale, buyer-internal discussion, `broadcast_to_vendor_count` (D-V6-001 remediation 2026-05-06: removed from CARRIED list — directly disclosed Target Account list cardinality in violation of §25.1.2 line 19702 invariant), the buyer-side total `affected_requirement_ids[]` array (D-V6-004 remediation 2026-05-06: replaced with the per-recipient intersection above; the buyer-side scope is buyer-internal authoring information) |
| `buyer_comment_visible_to_vendor` | `qa_thread_post_id` reference (the Q&A post that surfaced the comment) | Raw Internal Comment content (the Internal Comment Thread is NEVER carried; only the externalized Q&A post that a buyer explicitly promoted to vendor-visible is carried) |
| `eoi_acceptance_propagated` | `eoi_acceptance_seller_visible_projection` (see §4.5.8) | All other EOI Acceptance fields |
| `eoi_acceptance_reversed` | `eoi_acceptance_id`, `reversed_at`, `reversal_reason_public` (≤200 chars) | Full reversal rationale |

**Redaction Verification.** `redaction_verification_hash` is computed over a canonicalized JSON serialization of `payload_json` with the kind's whitelist applied. At write, the validator (a) confirms no forbidden field is present at any depth, (b) confirms the hash matches, (c) rejects with `console_bridge_event_firewall_violation` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422) on any mismatch. The CI gate `console_bridge_redaction_kind_completeness` asserts a one-to-one mapping between every Appendix J `console_bridge_event_kind` value and exactly one row in the Field-Level Redaction Rules table; additions to the enum without a row fail closed. Violations additionally alert Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100) — a persistent pattern of firewall-violation events from the same buyer session is a potential security incident.

**Seller-Visible Projection (Payload-Level — historical block, retained verbatim).** A secondary kind-specific whitelist is applied by the seller serializer to `payload_json`. This is a defense-in-depth layer: even if a malformed event slipped past write-time validation, the seller read layer still strips any field not in the kind's whitelist. QA test `console_bridge_seller_projection_defense_in_depth` asserts this for each event kind. **As of D-1.6-001 remediation, 2026-05-01, this payload-level projection is composed with the *Row-Level Seller Projection* defined in the Scope Isolation block above** — the seller read pipeline applies the row-level partition first, then the payload-level whitelist on the surviving `payload_json` field. CI gate `console_bridge_row_level_seller_projection_consistency` and CI gate `console_bridge_seller_projection_defense_in_depth` both assert; both must be green for deploy.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `pending` | Buyer-side mutation handler emits event | Redaction validation passed; idempotency check passed (no prior row for same idempotency_key within 24h) | Scheduler picks up within 5s |
| `pending` | `synced` | Bid Workspace applies event successfully | Apply handler returned success; `synced_at` stamped; `slo_bounded_lag_ms` computed | SLO breach flag set if `> 30000ms` |
| `pending` | `retrying` | Apply failure, retryable | `failure_reason ∈ {downstream_timeout, other_transient}`; `retry_count < 5`; `next_retry_at` scheduled per backoff curve | |
| `retrying` | `synced` | Retry succeeds | | `slo_bounded_lag_ms` may exceed 30000; `slo_breach_flag=true` |
| `retrying` | `retrying` | Retry fails, retryable, `retry_count < 5` | `retry_count++`; new `next_retry_at` | |
| `retrying` | `dlq` | 5 failed attempts | `retry_count=5`; transitions to DLQ with Ops alert | Manual re-drive from Ops Console |
| `pending` or `retrying` | `failed` | Apply failure, non-retryable | `failure_reason ∈ {target_bid_workspace_missing, target_bid_workspace_disqualified, vendor_withdrawn, bid_workspace_readonly, schema_mismatch, payload_too_large, persistent_firewall_violation_suspected, other_permanent}` | Buyer workspace surface shows bridge failure note |
| `pending` or `retrying` | `superseded` | A newer event for the same source arrives | `superseded_by_event_id` set; the newer event takes precedence per `conflict_resolution=last_write_wins` | Useful for rapid successive Requirement edits |
| `dlq` | `pending` | Ops manual re-drive | Ops resets `retry_count=0`, `failure_reason=null`, `failure_note` cleared | Re-queues |
| `failed` | `pending` | Ops manual re-drive after fixing underlying issue | Same conditions as from `dlq` | |

**Retry Curve.** Exponential backoff: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s — 5 attempts total. `next_retry_at = last_attempt_at + (2^retry_count seconds)`. Bounded-lag SLO is 30 seconds from `created_at` to `synced_at` per C.117; the 30-second SLO excludes `dlq` and `failed` terminal states (those surface in dashboards as separate anomalies). Retry curve class is the non-webhook `bridge_apply_standard` apply curve (§25.2.2; D-6.1-012 — the former `console_bridge_standard` webhook-retry-class label is retired; Bridge-domain *webhooks* use the Appendix F.1 `standard` curve per Appendix C / Appendix F).

**DLQ Handling.** DLQ-state rows are visible in (a) the buyer Workspace's "Bridge Health" panel with per-event detail, (b) the seller Bid Workspace's "Sync Health" panel with redacted detail, and (c) the Ops Console's cross-Workspace bridge dashboard. Ops one-click re-drive transitions back to `pending`; automated re-drive is NOT permitted (human approval required) to prevent infinite loops on persistent underlying failures. If a buyer-side source edit is made while an event is in DLQ, the new event supersedes (the DLQ event transitions to `superseded`, new event enters `pending`) — no duplicate apply.

**Conflict Resolution.** Concurrent buyer-side edits on the same source entity produce multiple events. The default rule is `last_write_wins` — the newer event supersedes older events in `pending`/`retrying`. For non-idempotent operations (e.g., `requirement_reverted` on a version that has since been further amended), the rule is `operation_non_idempotent_dlq` — the event is routed directly to `dlq` for Ops resolution. Amendments (`requirement_amended`) use `merge_op` — the semantic diff is recomputed against the most recent applied state and applied as a single rebased amendment. `buyer_origin_wins` is used in the rare case of bidirectional conflict (buyer amends and vendor submits response against the pre-amendment version simultaneously) — the buyer-origin event applies; the vendor's response is marked `needs_reverification` per §4.4 Response state machine.

**Daily Reconciliation.** Per §25.2, a 2am UTC job scans for stale bridge entries across all workspaces. Stale = `pending` or `retrying` > 24 hours. Stale entries are escalated to DLQ if not transient, or re-driven if the underlying infrastructure is known-healthy; the job emits the Appendix C `console_bridge.reconciliation_summary` webhook with per-workspace counts.

**Retention.** Bridge events retained for Workspace life + 7 years per §40.2 (aligned with Workspace retention). Soft-deleted only via Ops GDPR path with DPO approval; even then, the row is redacted (payload reduced to kind + timestamps + redaction_verification_hash) rather than hard-deleted, to preserve firewall audit integrity. Residency: each row lives in the buyer Workspace's residency region; reads from the seller Bid Workspace are served from the buyer region with a latency-permitting cross-region read path, with exceptions per §45 Data Privacy for EU-only residency scopes.

**Client-Cache DSAR Attestation (Phase 1.5).** Console Bridge Event payloads may be materialized into client-side caches (Convex reactive query result caches, IndexedDB write-ahead buffers, service-worker response caches) on both buyer and seller consoles. These caches are subject-data surfaces for DSAR purposes. On DSAR right-to-erasure for a subject user (`rationale_author_user_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by`), the server-side redaction pass pseudonymizes the subject fields to `ANONYMIZED_USER` and updates `redaction_verification_hash`; Convex reactive-query invalidation fans out within 60 seconds, evicting the stale rows from every connected client cache. For offline clients, a `dsar_client_cache_flush_required` event is persisted in the subject's Inbox Item Group (§4.3.22) so the next authenticated session triggers a forced cache flush. Service-worker caches are explicitly versioned against `payload_schema_version`; a schema-version bump at DSAR time forces re-fetch. IndexedDB write-ahead buffers for bridge events are bounded at 24h retention client-side; any buffered-but-not-synced bridge event older than 24h is discarded on next client boot, ensuring no stale subject data persists in client storage beyond the DSAR response window (§40.2 72h target). QA test `console_bridge_client_cache_dsar_flush` asserts cache-eviction latency across Convex, IndexedDB, and service-worker layers.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Vendor Bid Workspace disqualified mid-event.** Resolved: target check at apply time; `failure_reason=target_bid_workspace_disqualified`; event transitions to `failed` (non-retryable); buyer-side "Bridge Health" panel flags; no re-drive possible until disqualification is reversed.
2. **Vendor withdraws during a pending event.** Resolved: `failure_reason=vendor_withdrawn`; transitions to `failed`; buyer-side notification (optional based on buyer preference) that vendor withdrew.
3. **Payload exceeds 256KB (e.g., massive use-case restructure).** Resolved: write-time check rejects with `console_bridge_event_payload_too_large` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 413) and surfaces a buyer-visible "payload too large" banner that links to the §25.1 guidance on chunked updates. The mutation handler is responsible for emitting multiple smaller events (e.g., per-requirement amendments) rather than one massive batch.
4. **Firewall violation detected at write.** Resolved: `console_bridge_event_firewall_violation` + SIM alert + Ops investigation; recurring violations from the same buyer session may block bridge emission until Ops reviews (hard-block is a last resort; defaults to soft-warn + Ops escalation).
5. **Concurrent edits produce rapid-fire events.** Resolved: `last_write_wins` + supersede semantics; older events transition to `superseded` rather than being applied out of order.
6. **Seller-side apply handler is slow (downstream timeout).** Resolved: 30-second SLO; retry curve; DLQ after 5 attempts; Ops page on DLQ depth > 100.
7. **Daily reconciliation job fails to run.** Resolved: job heartbeat alert; missed-run triggers Ops page; manual re-run is idempotent (idempotency_key prevents duplicate apply).
8. **Ops re-drive of DLQ event on a disqualified vendor.** Resolved: re-drive re-evaluates target state; rejected with `console_bridge_event_cannot_redrive_disqualified` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409).

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. A Console Bridge Event MUST be written within 100ms of the source-entity mutation being committed (event emission is a Convex transaction side-effect on the source mutation).
2. Bounded-lag SLO MUST conform to §25.2.1 — `slo_breach_flag` MUST be set true for every event whose `slo_bounded_lag_ms > 30000` (the per-event flag is observational, not a hard SLO bound); the **rolling 15-minute breach rate MUST be ≤ 1% per event kind per residency region** (the percentile contract: p99 latency ≤ 30 s; p100 is a non-goal). Breach rate > 1% over a rolling 15-minute window MUST page Ops; sustained breach rate > 5% over a rolling 60-minute window escalates to the §25.6.4 Cross-Console on-call runbook with P1 severity. The `console_bridge.slo_summary` Ops dashboard observes both the per-event flag and the rolling-window breach rate. (D-6.1-014 remediation 2026-05-06: AC reconciled with §25.2.1 percentile contract.)
3. A write with `payload_json` exceeding 256KB MUST be rejected with `console_bridge_event_payload_too_large` (HTTP 413); mutation handler falls back to chunked events.
4. A write whose `redaction_verification_hash` does not match a recomputed hash over canonicalized `payload_json` MUST be rejected with `console_bridge_event_firewall_violation` (HTTP 422) and SIM-alerted.
5. A seller-console session reading a Console Bridge Event MUST receive only the `seller_visible_projection` fields for the event kind; QA test `console_bridge_seller_projection_defense_in_depth` runs against every event kind.
6. A buyer-console or seller-console session attempting cross-Org read MUST receive HTTP 404 with `console_bridge_event_cross_org_access`.
7. A DLQ transition MUST emit Appendix C `console_bridge.dlq_entered` webhook within 10 seconds and surface in the buyer and seller Health panels within 60 seconds.
8. Daily reconciliation at 2am UTC MUST emit Appendix C `console_bridge.reconciliation_summary` with per-workspace stale counts; a missed run MUST page Ops within 2 hours.
9. Ops manual re-drive MUST require the Ops user to supply a note (min 20 chars) and MUST NOT automatically cascade to other related DLQ events without explicit per-event re-drive.
10. The `idempotency_key` unique constraint MUST prevent duplicate application across restarts and retries; a duplicate write attempt MUST return HTTP 200 with the existing row's id (idempotent replay), not HTTP 409.

#### 4.7.1.1 Retention & DSAR Cascade (D-1V-012 remediation, 2026-04-29) {#4.7.1.1-retention-and-dsar-cascade}

**Authoring intent.** §4.7.1 declared scope-isolation, redaction, and seller-visible projection but was previously silent on retention TTL and DSAR right-to-erasure cascade. Without these rules, a DSAR-pseudonymized buyer User remained identifiable in seller-held bridge-event payloads — an unsatisfiable GDPR Article 17 obligation. This sub-section closes that gap. **Authored Extension AE-D1V-012 — pending ratification before v7.1.1 stamp.**

**Retention Classes.** Each Console Bridge Event row's retention class is determined by `event_kind` per the table below. The class drives the retention TTL applied by the §40.2 retention sweeper and the DSAR cascade exemption per §6.8.5.

| Retention class | TTL | Member event kinds | Rationale |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `bridge_event_financial_class` | `workspace_lifetime + 7 years` | `nda_executed`, `phase_advanced`, `response_submitted`, `response_locked`, `disqualification_issued`, `workspace_canceled`, `workspace_reopened_ops`, `eoi_acceptance_propagated`, `eoi_acceptance_reversed` | Audit-integrity / financial-record class per §6.8.5 — these events anchor the immutable audit trail of contract, signature, and selection-record formation. Aligned with §4.8.1 AIOperation 7-year retention. |
| `bridge_event_operational_class` | `workspace_lifetime + 90 days` | `requirement_created`, `requirement_amended`, `requirement_reverted`, `requirement_locked`, `revert_propagated`, `use_case_structure_changed`, `qa_thread_post_appended`, `amendment_broadcast`, `buyer_comment_visible_to_vendor` | Operational-class events that describe the evaluation flow but do not anchor financial / contractual outcomes. Retained 90 days post-Workspace-close to support late-arriving DSAR / forensic needs without indefinite storage. |

When a Console Bridge Event row's retention TTL elapses (per the class table above), the §40.2 retention sweeper hard-deletes the row at 02:00 UTC nightly. Hard-delete is permitted at retention TTL (this is not the same as DSAR-driven hard-delete, which is forbidden — see DSAR Cascade below).

**DSAR Cascade (D-1V3-001 / D-1V3-003 remediation 2026-05-01 — Pattern B).** When the §6.8.4 cascade walker pseudonymizes a User per right-to-erasure, the cascade reaches Console Bridge Event rows as follows. **The pre-remediation §4.7.1.1 v7.1.0 prescription "Rewritten to `anonymized_user_<hash>` per §6.8.4 pseudonym format. The original `user_id` is no longer recoverable from the row." was incorrect on a UUID column type and used a non-canonical pseudonym form — superseded by Pattern B per the §6.8.4.1 per-entity assignment table.**

| Field | DSAR action when subject = User identified by `user_id` |
| :---- | :---- |
| `created_by` | **Pattern B (FK preservation).** The `created_by` UUID FK is preserved unchanged; the User row pointed to by the FK is pseudonymized in-place per §6.8.4.1 Pattern B (`users.email`, `users.full_name` rewritten to canonical `anonymized_<console>_user_<base32(hash)[:16]>`; PII fields hard-deleted). Joins through `Console Bridge Event.created_by` resolve to the pseudonymized User row. |
| `updated_by` | **Pattern B (FK preservation).** Same mechanism as `created_by`. |
| `payload_json.<field>` references to subject by id | Walk the kind-specific `Fields CARRIED` list (§4.7.1 redaction matrix); for every field carrying a User reference (`reverted_by_user_role_snapshot`, `advanced_by_role_snapshot`, `acting_role_snapshot`, `signatory_email_buyer_public`, `signatory_email_seller_public`, `author_role_snapshot`, etc.), filter for occurrences where the value equals the subject's identifier (id, email, role-snapshot composite) and pseudonymize in-place. **The pseudonym embedded in `payload_json` is the canonical §6.8.5 form** `anonymized_<console>_user_<base32(hash)[:16]>` (because `payload_json` is a JSON value type, not a UUID FK column, Pattern A applies inside the JSON). The `redaction_verification_hash` is recomputed post-cascade so subsequent retries don't fail the firewall validator. |
| `cross_console_audit_trail.<field>` | Walk the denormalized JSON for `user_id`, `email`, `name` keys; pseudonymize in-place using the canonical §6.8.5 pseudonym form (Pattern A inside JSON). |
| Other fields | Preserved (audit-integrity). |

**Cascade scope: applied across all seller Orgs holding the bridge event.** A bridge event with `direction = buyer_to_seller` is held by the seller Org's read view but stored in the platform-shared bridge-event partition; the cascade walker therefore touches one canonical row per `(buyer_workspace_id, bid_workspace_id, idempotency_key)`, not N copies. Fan-out events (`fanout_group_id IS NOT NULL`) are walked once per fan-out group; the walker iterates all rows sharing the `fanout_group_id` and applies the field-level pseudonymization to each.

**Audit-integrity exemption.** For `bridge_event_financial_class` events, `created_by` retains the original `user_id` for forensic continuity per §6.8.5; the User-entity-level pseudonymization (rewriting `user.email`, `user.name`) covers the right-to-erasure obligation, while the bridge-event row's `created_by` resolves to the soft-deleted User row whose PII has been pseudonymized in-place. The `payload_json.<field>` PII bearers ARE pseudonymized inline regardless of class — the audit-integrity exemption applies only to the FK field. CI gate `bridge_event_dsar_cascade_field_partition` asserts the partition.

**SLA.** DSAR cascade on Console Bridge Event rows MUST complete within the §6.8.6 30-day fulfillment window for the subject User; the cascade walker batches rows in chunks of 1,000 with idempotent forward-recovery on partial failure (§6.8.4); the long-tail-cascade alert at §6.8.4 line 6.8.4-AC-3 fires if the affected-row count exceeds 50,000.

**Retention residency.** Each bridge-event row's retention partition follows the buyer Workspace's `data_residency_region` (the source-of-truth side); cross-residency reads from customer surfaces are blocked even within retention TTL.

**Acceptance Criteria (D-1V-012 remediation).**
1. Every Console Bridge Event row MUST resolve to exactly one retention class via `event_kind` per the class table; QA test `bridge_event_retention_class_completeness` asserts coverage of every Appendix J `console_bridge_event_kind` value.
2. The §40.2 retention sweeper MUST hard-delete bridge-event rows at retention TTL; QA test `bridge_event_retention_sweeper_ttl` asserts.
3. DSAR cascade on a User authoring N bridged Requirements MUST pseudonymize `created_by` and the kind-specific PII bearers in `payload_json` across all N rows within the §6.8.6 30-day window; QA test `bridge_event_dsar_cascade_completeness` asserts the cascade reaches every row referencing the subject.
4. Post-cascade `redaction_verification_hash` MUST be recomputed and stored; QA test `bridge_event_dsar_post_cascade_hash_consistency` asserts subsequent retries don't fail the firewall validator.
5. The audit-integrity exemption MUST preserve `created_by` on `bridge_event_financial_class` events while pseudonymizing the User entity itself; QA test `bridge_event_audit_integrity_exemption` asserts.
6. Long-tail cascades affecting > 50,000 rows MUST emit the §6.8.4 weekly progress alert; QA test `bridge_event_dsar_long_tail_alert` asserts.

### 4.7.2 Vendor Disqualification Record (Cross-Console, Buyer-Initiated, Seller-Visible-with-Redaction) {#4.7.2-vendor-disqualification-record}

**Authoring Intent.** Vendor Disqualification Record makes the disqualification workflow (§25.3, Summary C.118) a first-class entity. Today §25.3 describes the transitions as prose on Target Account and Bid Workspace state; this entity captures the disqualification as a queryable, auditable, appealable business object, supports three severities (workspace-local soft, account-level across the buyer Org's Workspaces, and Ops-imposed global ban), and binds the rationale (buyer-private) to the notification body (vendor-visible) with explicit asymmetric-visibility fields. This separation is necessary because disqualification has implications that extend beyond the originating Workspace (Organization Intelligence vendor history per §25.3; Seller Signal suppression downstream; Marketplace Listing eligibility interactions with Vendor Opt-Out; and Ops escalation paths).

**Scope:** Cross-Console. Scope anchors: `buyer_org_id` + `buyer_workspace_id` for workspace-level disqualifications; `buyer_org_id` only for account-level disqualifications; platform-scoped for Ops-imposed global bans. Seller reads are limited to the vendor-visible fields (`notification_body_to_vendor`, `disqualified_at`, and the Bid Workspace status transition) — the rationale and rationale author are NEVER exposed.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `severity` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_disqualification_severity`: `soft` (workspace-local), `account_level` (buyer Org's Workspaces, forward-looking), `global_ban` (Ops-imposed across platform) | Determines cascade scope |
| `buyer_org_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable for `severity=global_ban`; FK → Organization | Disqualifying Buyer Org |
| `buyer_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable for `severity ∈ {account_level, global_ban}`; FK → Workspace | Workspace (if soft) |
| `seller_org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | Disqualified seller |
| `bid_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable for `severity ∈ {account_level, global_ban}`; FK → Bid Workspace | Target Bid Workspace (soft) |
| `target_account_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable for `severity ∈ {account_level, global_ban}`; FK → Target Account | Target Account (soft) |
| `trigger` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_disqualification_trigger`: `workspace_owner_manual`, `automated_policy_violation`, `ops_compliance_action`, `vendor_non_responsive`, `vendor_withdrew_then_blocked`, `duplicate_bid_submission` | Why |
| `rationale_internal` | String | 10–4000 chars, required | Buyer-private rationale; audit trail; NEVER shown to vendor |
| `rationale_author_user_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → User | Who authored the rationale |
| `rationale_author_role_snapshot` | Enum | See Appendix J (workspace_roles / ops_roles) | Frozen at write |
| `notification_body_to_vendor` | String | 1–1000 chars; templated | Vendor-visible copy; defaults per severity (neutral "Your participation in '{Workspace Title}' has ended. Thank you for your interest."); editable per-disqualification by Workspace Owner |
| `notification_style` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_disqualification_notification_style`: `neutral_no_rationale` (default), `rationale_shared_with_vendor` (only if buyer explicitly opts in and Ops approves), `silent_no_vendor_notification` (global_ban Ops-only) | How the vendor is notified |
| `notification_sent_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When vendor received notification |
| `vendor_acknowledgement_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When vendor session first loaded the disqualification banner |
| `appeal_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_disqualification_appeal_status`: `not_offered`, `eligible`, `submitted`, `under_review`, `upheld`, `overturned`, `expired` | Appeal state |
| `appeal_window_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Deadline for appeal (default 14 days for `account_level`; not_offered for `soft`; 30 days for `global_ban`) |
| `appeal_narrative` | String | 0–4000 chars, nullable | Vendor's rebuttal |
| `appeal_decided_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | |
| `appeal_decision_note_internal` | String | 0–4000 chars | Ops-facing decision rationale |
| `appeal_decision_note_vendor_visible` | String | 0–2000 chars | Vendor-visible decision summary |
| `cascade_status` | Enum | `pending`, `in_progress`, `complete`, `failed` | Cascade of downstream effects (response lock, Q&A orphaning, Scoring exclusion, etc.) |
| `cascade_completed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When cascade finished |
| `cascade_actions_json` | JSON | ≤ 16000 chars | Structured record of each cascade action + timestamp + success/failure; for Ops forensics |
| `console_bridge_event_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Console Bridge Event (§4.7.1) | The bridge event of kind `disqualification_issued` that propagated the disqualification to the seller's Bid Workspace (soft severity) or to the Seller Console banner (account_level / global_ban) |
| `related_abuse_report_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Marketplace Abuse Report (§4.5.7) | Populated when disqualification is a downstream of an upheld abuse report (trigger=`ops_compliance_action`) |
| `reversed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Populated only for overturned appeals or Ops manual reversal |
| `reversed_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → User | |
| `reversal_reason` | Enum | Nullable; `appeal_overturned`, `ops_manual_reversal`, `buyer_workspace_owner_reversal_within_72h`, `system_error_rollback` | Required when `reversed_at` set |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Alias of `rationale_author_user_id` for most cases; Ops-user for `global_ban` |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft-delete only via Ops GDPR path |

**Indexes.** `(seller_org_id, created_at DESC)` — Vendor history view per §25.3, `(buyer_workspace_id, seller_org_id)` unique partial where `severity='soft'` — prevents duplicate soft-disqualifications in the same Workspace, `(buyer_org_id, seller_org_id)` unique partial where `severity='account_level'`, `(severity, reversed_at)` partial where null — for the "active disqualifications" queries, `(appeal_status, appeal_window_at)` partial for appeal-expiry scans, `(related_abuse_report_id)` partial.

**Scope Isolation.**

- **Buyer-console reads:** Workspace Owner, Workspace Admin, and Use Case Leads of the originating Workspace see all fields; Ops sees all. Other buyer Org users see a redacted projection without `rationale_internal`.
- **Seller-console reads:** Only a redacted vendor-visible projection `{id, severity, disqualified_at, notification_body_to_vendor, appeal_status, appeal_window_at, appeal_decision_note_vendor_visible, reversed_at}`. `rationale_internal`, `rationale_author_user_id`, and `cascade_actions_json` are NEVER returned.
- **Cross-Workspace seller reads:** For `severity ∈ {account_level, global_ban}`, the Seller Org sees one row in their Seller Console Account Status surface with the vendor-visible projection; `buyer_workspace_id` is null, preserving workspace-specific privacy even when account-level disqualification originated from a specific Workspace.
- **Org Intelligence surface (§25.3 vendor history):** Reads disqualification records for the buyer Org's past Workspaces; `rationale_internal` is visible only to the disqualifying Workspace Owner and to Org Admins; other viewers see "Rationale restricted to Workspace Owner".

**Cascade Actions (Soft Severity).**

1. `target_account.status → disqualified` (aligns with §25.3 and existing enum in Appendix J).
2. `bid_workspace.status → disqualified`.
3. Vendor notification dispatched via Loops.so template per `notification_style`; `notification_sent_at` stamped.
4. All vendor responses in this Bid Workspace → `locked`; vendor cannot edit or add; banner displayed on vendor side.
5. Q&A threads initiated by this vendor → orphaned (read-only for vendor; no reply capability).
6. Vendor excluded from Scoring phase; scoring matrix renders with red "Disqualified" badge.
7. Console Bridge Event of kind `disqualification_issued` emitted; `seller_visible_projection` includes only `{notification_body_to_vendor, disqualified_at}` (rationale NEVER carried).
8. SLA timer for this vendor in any open Team queue cancelled.
9. Seller Signal (§4.4.18) suppresses this buyer-vendor pair from the affected buyer Org's signals to this Seller Org for 90 days (avoids noisy post-disqualification signal).

**Cascade Actions (Account-Level Severity).** In addition to steps 1–6 for EVERY `bid_workspace` this seller is currently active in within the buyer Org's Workspaces, plus:

- All open Marketplace Listings by this buyer that this seller matches → seller is auto-excluded from future match-score calculations for this buyer for 12 months.
- Seller's future EOI submissions to any Workspace of this buyer Org → auto-rejected with reason `buyer_account_level_disqualification` (new enum value for `abuse_report_closure_disposition` is NOT appropriate; use a new enum `eoi_rejection_reason.buyer_account_level_disqualification` — authored in Phase 4 when EOI rejection reasons are added to Appendix J).
- Bridge event fans out to all affected Bid Workspaces (N events, one per active engagement).

**Cascade Actions (Global Ban, Ops-Only).** In addition to the account-level cascade for the triggering buyer Org (if applicable):

- Seller Org's Marketplace Listings → `hidden` across the platform.
- SellerOrgPage and SoftwarePage → `410 Gone` (like Vendor Opt-Out render contract).
- Seller Profile delisted from Marketplace search; Capability Declarations remain but `published=false` is forced.
- Seller Signal delivery suspended platform-wide.
- Seller's account is placed in a `banned` state (new Organization state; `organization.state=banned` — authored in Phase 4 when Organization state machine is extended).
- Notification style is MUST be `silent_no_vendor_notification` for Ops-covert investigations OR `neutral_no_rationale` with Ops leadership approval; `rationale_shared_with_vendor` is disallowed for `global_ban` (legal).

**Appeal Workflow.**

- `soft`: appeal NOT offered by default. Workspace Owner MAY reverse within 72 hours (see Reversal below). `appeal_status=not_offered`.
- `account_level`: appeal eligible for 14 days from `created_at`. Vendor receives magic-link (authenticated Seller Org Admin) appeal form; 4000-char narrative. Ops reviews within 10 business days; decision renders `upheld` or `overturned`. Appeal form displays vendor-visible projection only.
- `global_ban`: appeal eligible for 30 days. Dual sign-off by Ops leadership required for both upholding and overturning. Overturning requires a documented audit path.

**Reversal.** Soft disqualifications MAY be reversed by the Workspace Owner within 72 hours with reason `buyer_workspace_owner_reversal_within_72h`; beyond 72 hours, requires Ops with `ops_compliance_admin` role. Account-level disqualifications are reversed only through appeal-overturned or Ops manual reversal (`ops_manual_reversal`). Global bans are reversed only via Ops leadership dual-signoff. Reversal cascades (reverse of the severity's cascade): Target Account un-disqualified, Bid Workspace un-disqualified (returns to prior status, typically `active`), responses un-locked (returning to prior state, not necessarily `submitted` — §4.4 Response state machine handles this), Q&A threads reopened, scoring inclusion restored (if Scoring phase has not already concluded — see Known Gap below), vendor notification sent. Reversal emits a new Console Bridge Event of kind `disqualification_issued` with a reversal flag in the payload (not a separate kind — reversal is semantically a new disqualification-state event with `reversed=true`).

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Actor | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `active` (existence, no state field) | Buyer or Ops creates | Rationale ≥ 10 chars; seller not already in same-severity disqualification from same buyer; severity-specific preconditions | Buyer (soft), Buyer Org Admin (account_level with dual-signoff), Ops (global_ban with Ops leadership dual-signoff) | Cascade begins; bridge event emitted |
| `active` | `appeal_submitted` (appeal_status transition) | Vendor submits appeal | `appeal_status=eligible`; within `appeal_window_at` | Seller Org Admin | Ops review SLA starts |
| `appeal_submitted` | `appeal_upheld` | Ops upholds | Ops decision | Ops | Disqualification remains; vendor notified |
| `appeal_submitted` | `appeal_overturned` (reversal cascade) | Ops overturns | Ops decision; `reversed_at` set | Ops | Reversal cascade executes |
| `active` | `reversed` | Workspace Owner reverses within 72h | `severity=soft`; within 72h | Buyer Workspace Owner | Reversal cascade executes |
| `active` | `expired` (appeal_status) | Appeal window expired without submission | `appeal_window_at < now`; no appeal filed | System | Appeal no longer available |

(No top-level state field on this entity; the lifecycle is represented by the presence/absence of `reversed_at`, `appeal_status`, and the cascade state.)

**Retention.** Retention, hard-delete prohibition, and DSAR redaction behavior are governed by §40.2 **Vendor Disqualification Record (§4.7.2)** and §6.8.5 row 7. Vendor Disqualification Record rows are retained as buyer-vendor legal-defense and audit evidence; DSAR fulfillment redacts or pseudonymizes identity-bearing fields but does not erase the fact, severity, timing, or non-PII operational outcome of the disqualification.

#### 4.7.2.1 Retention & DSAR Cascade (D-1.6-004 remediation, 2026-06-22) {#4.7.2.1-retention-and-dsar-cascade}

**Authoring intent.** §4.7.2 previously stated only that PII fields are redacted, without enumerating the fields, cascade path, seller-projection behavior, or audit-hash implications. This sub-section closes D-1.6-004 by binding Vendor Disqualification Record to the §6.8.4 cascade walker, §6.8.5 row 7, and §40.2. **Authored Extension AE-V72REM-PH16-VENDOR-DISQUALIFICATION-DSAR-01 - pending ratification before v7.1.1 stamp.**

**Retention class.** Vendor Disqualification Record uses the §6.8.5 row 7 retained-row class: buyer-vendor disqualification audit and legal-defense in disputed evaluations. The row itself is not hard-deleted for DSAR. DSAR fulfillment applies Pattern B to User FKs and Pattern A/body sweep to text or JSON fields that carry subject PII, while preserving structural facts needed for audit, appeal, reversal, and seller-notice history.

| Field / projection | DSAR action when subject = User identified by the request |
| :---- | :---- |
| `rationale_author_user_id` | **Pattern B (FK preservation).** Preserve the UUID FK; pseudonymize the referenced User row in-place per §6.8.4.1 / §6.8.5 using `anonymized_<console>_user_<base32(hash)[:16]>`. |
| `created_by` | **Pattern B (FK preservation).** Same treatment as `rationale_author_user_id`; the FK remains available for audit joins and resolves to the pseudonymized User row. |
| `updated_by` | **Pattern B (FK preservation).** Same treatment as `created_by`. |
| `reversed_by_user_id` | **Pattern B (FK preservation)** when non-null. Preserve reversal authorship continuity while the referenced User row is pseudonymized in-place. |
| `rationale_author_role_snapshot` | Preserved only as a role enum snapshot. Values MUST NOT embed name, email, title string, or free-text identity. Any legacy non-enum value discovered during cascade is treated as a body field and redacted to `[REDACTED_DSAR]`. |
| `rationale_internal` | Retained for legal-defense under §6.8.5 row 7, but subject-identifying spans are redacted to `[REDACTED_DSAR]` by the §6.8.4.5 body-field sweep. Non-PII rationale structure, severity evidence, timestamps, and policy references remain. |
| `notification_body_to_vendor` | Seller-visible body field; subject-identifying spans are redacted to `[REDACTED_DSAR]`. The seller projection MUST be invalidated and re-materialized after cascade so seller reads never show stale pre-redaction buyer identity. |
| `appeal_narrative` | Seller-authored appeal body; subject-identifying spans are redacted to `[REDACTED_DSAR]`. If the DSAR subject is the appeal author, any author FK is handled by the owning seller User / AuditEvent path rather than by this free-text field. |
| `appeal_decision_note_internal` | Ops-facing body field; subject-identifying spans are redacted to `[REDACTED_DSAR]`; non-PII decision outcome and appeal disposition remain. |
| `appeal_decision_note_vendor_visible` | Seller-visible body field; subject-identifying spans are redacted to `[REDACTED_DSAR]` and the seller projection is refreshed before the next read or webhook replay. |
| `cascade_actions_json` | Walk nested `user_id`, `actor_user_id`, `email`, `name`, `display_name`, and role-snapshot keys. JSON user identifiers use the canonical §6.8.5 pseudonym form; names/emails/free-text spans are redacted to `[REDACTED_DSAR]`. Non-PII action kind, timestamp, success/failure, and downstream entity ids remain for Ops forensics. |
| `console_bridge_event_id` | Preserved. The referenced Console Bridge Event is also reached by the §4.7.1.1 / §6.8.4.7 cascade path so bridge payloads and seller-projected copies converge on the same post-redaction state. |
| `severity`, scope FKs, timestamps, appeal state, `cascade_status`, `reversal_reason`, `notification_style`, `notification_sent_at`, `vendor_acknowledgement_at`, `deleted_at` | Preserved. These are structural / operational fields and do not by themselves identify the DSAR subject. |

**Cascade invocation.** The §6.8.4 cascade planner MUST include Vendor Disqualification Record whenever the subject User appears in any field listed above or in a referenced Console Bridge Event. Rows are processed in the same batch / forward-recovery regime as §4.7.1.1: chunks of 1,000, idempotent row markers, partial-failure recovery per §6.8.4.6, and completion inside the §6.8.6 DSAR fulfillment SLA. Retained-row disclosure uses §6.8.5's `dsar.audit_integrity_exemption_invoked` AuditEvent path and names "Vendor Disqualification Record (§4.7.2)" in the requestor response.

**Seller-projection parity.** Seller-console reads of the vendor-visible projection `{id, severity, disqualified_at, notification_body_to_vendor, appeal_status, appeal_window_at, appeal_decision_note_vendor_visible, reversed_at}` MUST observe the post-cascade redacted values. Cached Convex query results, service-worker responses, and materialized seller read models follow the §4.7.1.1 client-cache DSAR invalidation pattern. A seller-visible projection that retains pre-redaction buyer identity after the buyer-side source row is redacted is a console-firewall failure.

**Audit and webhook hash treatment.** Vendor Disqualification Record does not add its own `audit_chain_hash` column. If a downstream AuditEvent, Appendix C `vendor.disqualified` / `vendor.disqualification.reversed` delivery payload, or replayable webhook projection derives `rationale_hash`, `audit_chain_hash`, or a redaction verification hash from a redacted body field, future replay/retry payloads MUST be recomputed over the post-redaction value before delivery. Historical webhook deliveries already sent to subscribers remain immutable delivery records; they are not retroactively mutated.

**Acceptance Criteria (D-1.6-004 remediation).**

1. DSAR cascade planning for a subject User referenced by `rationale_author_user_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, or `reversed_by_user_id` MUST include the Vendor Disqualification Record row and apply Pattern B to the referenced User row while preserving the FK column.
2. Body-field sweep MUST scan `rationale_internal`, `notification_body_to_vendor`, `appeal_narrative`, `appeal_decision_note_internal`, `appeal_decision_note_vendor_visible`, and identity-bearing keys in `cascade_actions_json`; detected subject-identifying spans MUST be replaced with `[REDACTED_DSAR]`.
3. The cascade MUST preserve `severity`, scope FKs, appeal/reversal state, timestamps, and non-PII cascade outcomes, and MUST NOT hard-delete the Vendor Disqualification Record row before its §40.2 retention boundary.
4. Seller-console projection reads after cascade MUST return redacted `notification_body_to_vendor` and `appeal_decision_note_vendor_visible` values; QA test `vendor_disqualification_seller_projection_dsar_parity` asserts no stale seller cache contains pre-redaction buyer identity.
5. The referenced `console_bridge_event_id` MUST be walked through §4.7.1.1 / §6.8.4.7 in the same DSAR plan, and buyer-source plus seller-projection bridge payloads MUST converge on the same redaction result.
6. Future replay or retry of Appendix C `vendor.disqualified` and `vendor.disqualification.reversed` payloads MUST recompute any derived body hash or redaction-verification hash over the post-redaction body before delivery; historical deliveries remain immutable audit records.
7. Cascade completion MUST satisfy the §6.8.6 DSAR fulfillment SLA and use §6.8.4.6 partial-failure recovery for any batch that cannot finish in a single worker run.

**Residency.** Buyer-origin disqualifications stored in buyer Workspace residency. Ops-originated global bans stored in platform-global residency. Seller reads served from their home residency with cross-region read path.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Rationale contains accidental buyer-internal content (scoring, selection-report draft excerpt).** Resolved: `rationale_internal` is explicitly buyer-private and firewall-isolated; redaction validator on Console Bridge Event ensures it does NOT cross the firewall; the vendor sees `notification_body_to_vendor` only.
2. **Concurrent disqualification and scoring phase.** Resolved: cascade includes "exclude from scoring matrix" only if phase ≤ `phase_11_scoring_review_consensus`; post-Phase-12 disqualification is allowed (emergency Ops-driven only) but does NOT rewrite the historical Selection Report — it adds a post-hoc annotation (see Known Gap below).
3. **Reversal after Scoring phase has concluded.** Known Gap: reversing a soft disqualification after Phase 11 ends is permitted but scoring cannot be retroactively reopened (per §12 Scoring semantics); the vendor is reinstated to the shortlist but not to scoring. Flagged in Authored Extensions for human review.
4. **Vendor Org deleted between disqualification and appeal.** Resolved: appeal flow disabled with `vendor_org_deleted` note; `appeal_status=not_offered`; disqualification record preserved for audit.
5. **Global ban overlaps with an open soft disqualification.** Resolved: global ban supersedes; existing soft records stay in place (audit integrity) but are annotated with `superseded_by_global_ban=true` and surfaces redacted to Ops-only.
6. **Rationale author's role changes after disqualification.** Resolved: `rationale_author_role_snapshot` is frozen at write; role change does not rewrite history.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Creating a Vendor Disqualification Record with `severity=soft` but without a `buyer_workspace_id` and `bid_workspace_id` MUST be rejected with `vendor_disqualification_soft_requires_workspace_scope` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).
2. Creating `severity=global_ban` without Ops leadership dual-signoff MUST be rejected with `vendor_disqualification_global_ban_requires_dual_signoff` (Appendix I; HTTP 422 — D-6.1-016: a missing or invalid co-signer dual-signoff token is a request-body precondition, not an RBAC denial; the pure role-denial case, where the caller is not in the Ops leadership group at all, is covered by the existing Ops-role-forbidden code set per §25.3.9).
3. Vendor notification dispatch MUST occur within 60 seconds of create; failure retries per the §41 Loops.so non-webhook `transactional_email` policy; DLQ after 5 failures with Ops alert.
4. The full cascade (Target Account, Bid Workspace, responses, Q&A, scoring exclusion, bridge event, Seller Signal suppression) MUST complete within 10 seconds for soft severity and 60 seconds for account_level (because fan-out may touch N workspaces). Completion is observable via `cascade_status=complete`.
5. Seller read of the disqualification record MUST return only the vendor-visible projection; QA test `vendor_disqualification_seller_projection_redaction` asserts this.
6. The Console Bridge Event of kind `disqualification_issued` emitted on create MUST NOT carry `rationale_internal` or `rationale_author_user_id`; QA test `vendor_disqualification_bridge_firewall` asserts this against the redaction verification hash.
7. Workspace Owner reversal within 72 hours MUST fully reverse the cascade within 10 seconds (seller-visible restoration) and MUST emit a Console Bridge Event reflecting the reversal.
8. Account-level disqualification MUST auto-reject incoming EOIs from the disqualified seller to the buyer Org for 12 months from `created_at`; the EOI rejection uses `buyer_account_level_disqualification` as reason and the seller is notified.
9. Global ban MUST force `organization.state=banned` on the seller Org (authored in Phase 4 when Organization state machine is extended) and MUST hide all Marketplace Listings, SellerOrgPages, SoftwarePages, and suspend Seller Signal delivery within 15 minutes.
10. Appeal window expiry MUST transition `appeal_status → expired` exactly at `appeal_window_at` (± 1 minute); system job runs every minute to sweep expirations.
11. A write attempt by a non-Workspace-Owner/Admin/Use-Case-Lead buyer user with `severity=soft` MUST be rejected with `vendor_disqualification_role_forbidden` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403).
12. Historical Selection Reports (§43) that reference a vendor later disqualified post-Phase-12 MUST render a banner "This vendor was subsequently disqualified on {date}" at next report access, without rewriting the report body (preserves Phase-12 immutability).
