## 4.8 Billing & AI Accounting Entities {#4.8-billing-&-ai-accounting-entities}

**Authoring Intent.** §4.8 introduces the data-model foundation for the outcome-based consumption model that will replace the current §34 plan/seat surface in a subsequent integration phase (Phase 2 of the pricing-rewrite track, distinct from the v7.0.0 entity-integration phase numbering). These eleven entities collectively hold the truth for: every billable AI invocation across both consoles (`AIOperation`); the authoritative, Ops-managed list of billable capabilities (`CapabilityRegistryEntry`) that supersedes the historic "21 capabilities" hardcoding; the org-pooled value-dollar wallet that buyer- and seller-console capabilities draw against (`AIWallet`); the per-capability machine-readable acceptance/rejection contract (`OutcomeContract`) that drives the §4.8.1 settlement state machine; the 14-day customer-initiated dispute lane (`ContestRecord`); the nightly cost-base re-derivation audit (`CostBaseRecalculationLog`); the per-capability free-operation counter (`FreeAllowanceCounter`) that powers the Free Allowance PLG lever; the Enterprise annual commit with discount bands (`CommittedSpendContract`); the publish-time snapshot that feeds the Public Pricing API (`PricingTableVersion`); the 90-day read-only preservation bucket for downgraded customers (`DowngradeExcessDataBucket`); and the periodic seat counter used for plan-gate enforcement and reporting only (`BillingSeatSnapshot` — Sourcera does not bill per seat).

These entities are authored to: (a) make every monetary movement in the platform a queryable, immutable, append-only object; (b) preserve the firewall such that a Buyer Workspace cannot read Seller-console operations and vice versa, while still allowing Org-level pooling at the wallet layer; (c) make residency-locked invoicing (§4.5.5 / §4.4.15 residency model) a first-class concept by binding every ledger row to a `legal_entity` enum; (d) make the cost_base re-derivation a documented, auditable, drift-monitored process rather than a quietly-running cron; and (e) decouple the rate card the customer sees from the cost base Sourcera observes, so an Anthropic price move does not surface as customer-visible repricing.

**Source authority.** This section materializes Summary §2 and Appendix C entries C.75–C.87, plus the Buyer and Seller Pricing Strategy v2 documents (`Sourcera_Buyer_Pricing_Strategy.md`, `Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy.md`). Where the Summary, the Pricing Strategies, and the existing Master Spec §34 conflict (§34 is the v6.0.0 token-denominated billing model; the Pricing Strategies and Summary §2 are the post-2026-04-13 outcome-based model), the Pricing Strategies win — see RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions for the conflict log. §34 will be rewritten in a subsequent integration phase to reference the entities authored here; this phase preserves §34 to avoid out-of-sequence breakage and explicitly flags the pending rewrite.

**Cross-console scope rule.** The eleven entities span scopes: `AIOperation`, `OutcomeContract`, `CapabilityRegistryEntry`, `CostBaseRecalculationLog`, `PricingTableVersion`, and `FreeAllowanceCounter` are platform-scoped or org-scoped with rigorous console-tagging; `AIWallet`, `ContestRecord`, `CommittedSpendContract`, `DowngradeExcessDataBucket`, and `BillingSeatSnapshot` are org-scoped and pool across both consoles by design (this is the explicit billing-shared/data-not-shared rule from Pricing Strategy §11). The Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2) is preserved end-to-end: a Buyer Workspace session cannot enumerate the AIOperations of a Seller Bid Workspace even though both bill against the same `AIWallet`. Console isolation is enforced at the read-projection layer, not at the wallet layer.

**Authored Extensions disclosure.** Most monetary, retention, and state-machine details below extend the source documents. Source documents define the conceptual model; this section authors the production-grade schema. Each authored extension is logged in RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions for human reviewer sign-off.

### 4.8.1 AIOperation (Org-Scoped, Cross-Console-Tagged, Append-Only Billing Unit) {#4.8.1-aioperation}

**Authoring Intent.** AIOperation is the canonical, immutable, single-row record of one billable AI invocation. Every customer-billed capability, every Sourcera-owned (Platform Marketing cost-center) operation, every Managed Agent sub-call, and every Public-Pricing-driven simulation that the API accepts produces exactly one `AIOperation` row at the moment the work begins; the row is then transitioned through the settlement state machine as the Outcome Resolver collects acceptance signals or the contest window closes. AIOperation is the single point at which all four billing-relevant facts coexist: what was billed, who consumed it, in which console, against which wallet, locked at which FX rate. Per Summary C.75 it is the single billing unit across the platform; per the Pricing Strategies §6 / §10 (buyer + seller) it is the persistent record that the Outcome Resolver acts on; per C.84 it is the row that locks the FX rate at settlement.

**Scope.** Org-scoped (`org_id` is required), with explicit `console` tagging that controls cross-console firewall enforcement. AIOperation is append-only after settlement: once `settlement_state ∈ {accepted, rejected, auto_accepted}` is set and `settlement_at` is stamped, only `contested` and `reversed` transitions are allowed (and only via §4.8.5 ContestRecord materialization), all other field updates are rejected with `ai_operation_immutable_after_settlement` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422). Soft-delete is forbidden at the application layer: AIOperation is a financial record. GDPR right-to-erasure is satisfied via field-level redaction (PII fields scrubbed; monetary, capability, and provenance fields retained for SOC-2 audit).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated; surfaces in customer Billing Ledger as the row id |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization; required | Billing anchor; never null |
| `console` | Enum | See Appendix J `ai_operation_console`: `buyer`, `seller`, `platform_marketing`, `sourcera_owned`, `ops` | Console attribution; controls cross-console firewall on read |
| `workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Workspace OR Bid Workspace (polymorphic; application-validated against `console`) | Workspace context if applicable; null for Org-level operations (e.g., KB Bootstrap on Org KB) |
| `workspace_kind` | Enum | Nullable; `buyer_workspace`, `seller_bid_workspace`, `seller_org_kb`, `buyer_org_kb`, `marketplace_domain` | Disambiguates polymorphic `workspace_id` |
| `capability_id` | String | 1–80 chars; FK → CapabilityRegistryEntry.`capability_id`; required | Joins to §4.8.2 for billing mode, model tier, and outcome contract |
| `parent_operation_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; self-ref → AIOperation | For Managed Agent sub-calls (Summary C.55); the parent is the customer-facing operation, children are sub-calls. Never null for `actor_type=managed_agent`. |
| `chain_correlation_id` | UUID | Nullable | Sourcera-side grouping key across multiple parent AIOperation rows that belong to one customer-facing journey (for example, the §22.14.4 Ghost-Bid Importer sequence `ghost_rfp_ingestion → kb_bootstrap → first_pass_responder`). NOT an Anthropic-side ID; all parent rows in the chain share the value, while child rows may inherit it for query locality. |
| `actor_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → User OR Managed Agent identity OR system identity (synthetic UUID); required | Polymorphic: see `actor_type` |
| `actor_type` | Enum | See Appendix J `ai_operation_actor_type`: `user`, `managed_agent`, `system`, `ops` | Disambiguates polymorphic `actor_id` |
| `actor_role_snapshot` | Enum | See Appendix J workspace/org roles | Frozen at write; preserves attribution if the role later changes |
| `model_tier` | Enum | See Appendix J `ai_operation_model_tier`: `haiku`, `sonnet`, `opus`, `embeddings`, `external_managed` | Source model class; `external_managed` for non-Anthropic third-party invocations (e.g., Firecrawl, Perplexity) that nonetheless bill through the AI accounting framework |
| `model_id` | String | ≤ 120 chars; nullable | Anthropic model id at invocation time (e.g., `claude-opus-4-6`); preserved for the cost-base recalc job |
| `cost_base_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Nightly-recalculated cost basis in **integer USD cents**; locked at write to the most recent published `CostBaseRecalculationLog` for `(capability_id, model_tier)` |
| `cost_base_version_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → CostBaseRecalculationLog | Which nightly recalc produced this `cost_base_cents` value |
| `value_price_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Charge to wallet on `accepted` / `auto_accepted`. Default `cost_base_cents × 10`; floor `min_value_price_cents` from CapabilityRegistryEntry |
| `cost_price_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Charge to wallet on `rejected`. Default `cost_base_cents × 1.05`; floor `min_cost_price_cents` from CapabilityRegistryEntry |
| `effective_charge_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0; nullable until settled | Final amount applied to wallet at settlement; equals `value_price_cents` for `accepted`/`auto_accepted`, equals `cost_price_cents` for `rejected`, set to `0` for `reversed`. Frozen at settlement. |
| `settlement_state` | Enum | See Appendix J `ai_operation_settlement_state`: `pending`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `auto_accepted`, `contested`, `reversed` | See state machine below |
| `settlement_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | UTC; populated on first non-`pending` transition (`accepted`, `rejected`, `auto_accepted`); preserved through `contested` and `reversed` |
| `auto_accept_after_seconds` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Snapshot of OutcomeContract.`auto_accept_after_seconds` at write time; drives `pending → auto_accepted` timer |
| `contest_window_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | UTC; equals `settlement_at + 14 days` (per Summary C.78); after this, `contested` transition is rejected |
| `contest_record_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → ContestRecord | Set on transition to `contested`; nullable until then |
| `provenance_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex | Hash over `(capability_id, prompt_template_version, input_content_hash, model_id, cost_base_version_id, billing_currency, fx_rate_locked)` — used by ContestRecord to assert a specific operation; immutable |
| `prompt_template_version` | String | ≤ 40 chars | Capability-specific prompt template version (semver-aligned); aids drift analysis |
| `input_content_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex; nullable for content-free operations | Hash of canonicalized input content; never the raw input (PII safety) |
| `output_content_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex; nullable until response received | Hash of canonicalized output; powers retention-style outcome signals |
| `tokens_input` | Integer | ≥ 0; nullable | Anthropic-reported input tokens at completion; preserved for the cost_base recalc job — NOT used for customer billing |
| `tokens_output` | Integer | ≥ 0; nullable | Same as above for output tokens |
| `compute_milliseconds` | Integer | ≥ 0; nullable | Convex-side compute attribution in ms; included in cost_base recalc |
| `external_provider` | Enum | Nullable; `firecrawl`, `perplexity`, `loops`, `posthog_ingest`, `none` | When `model_tier=external_managed`, names the third-party provider whose cost is rolled into `cost_base_cents` |
| `external_provider_op_id` | String | ≤ 200 chars; nullable | Provider-side identifier for cost reconciliation |
| `wallet_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → AIWallet; required | The wallet this operation will draw from |
| `billed_against_free_allowance` | Boolean | Default false | True when this operation consumed a unit from §4.8.7 FreeAllowanceCounter rather than the wallet (effective_charge_cents = 0) |
| `billed_against_committed_spend_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → CommittedSpendContract | Set when this operation is drawing from an Enterprise commit pool rather than the standard wallet balance |
| `billing_currency` | Enum | See Appendix J `billing_currency`: `usd`, `eur`, `gbp`, `cad`, `aud` | Customer-visible currency at write time |
| `fx_rate_locked` | Decimal(12,8) | Default 1.0 for `usd` | Exchange rate from Sourcera-internal accounting (USD) to `billing_currency`, locked at write to the daily Treasury rate per C.84; preserved through `contested` and `reversed` (a reversal credits at the same FX rate as the original charge — see Failure Modes #5) |
| `legal_entity` | Enum | See Appendix J `legal_entity_kind` (post-Phase-2V D-AJ-004 canonical 4-value set: `sourcera_us_llc`, `sourcera_eu_gmbh`, `sourcera_apac_pte`, `sourcera_custom`). The v7.1.0 pre-Phase-2V value `sourcera_uk_ltd` is retired at v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 (D-RES-004 closure 2026-05-20); UK-resident Orgs route through `sourcera_eu_gmbh` per the Glossary "Residency-Locked Invoicing" entry, OR through `sourcera_custom` keyed on a `custom_sovereign_residency_label` of `uk_crown_secure` per §4.1.1 row `custom_sovereign_residency_label` for UK-sovereign-cloud Enterprise contracts. | Locked at write per the Org's `data_residency_region` — drives invoice issuance per C.84. Mismatch with the deterministic mapping rejected with HTTP 422 `ai_operation_legal_entity_residency_mismatch` (Appendix I). |
| `cost_center` | Enum | See Appendix J `sourcera_owned_cost_center` (extended): `customer_billed`, `sourcera_owned`, `platform_marketing` | When `customer_billed`, charges hit `wallet_id`; when `sourcera_owned`/`platform_marketing`, the operation is recorded for COGS but no wallet draw occurs |
| `firewall_isolation_token` | String | 32-char base32 | Per-row token used by read-projection layer to confirm console match before deserializing payload-adjacent fields (defense-in-depth against accidental cross-console enumeration) |
| `idempotency_key` | String | 1–128 chars; unique per `(org_id, capability_id, actor_id, request_idempotency_window)` | Application-supplied; default derived from `(actor_id, capability_id, input_content_hash, request_window_minute)` |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC; the moment the AI operation began |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC; updates only allowed on settlement-state transitions before settlement freeze |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User OR system OR managed agent identity | Equals `actor_id` for `actor_type=user`; system/agent UUIDs otherwise |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User OR system | Last updater (Outcome Resolver, Contest Reviewer, Ops) |
| `redacted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | DSAR right-to-erasure stamp; presence indicates `actor_id` and `input_content_hash`/`output_content_hash` have been scrubbed; monetary fields preserved |

**Indexes.** `(org_id, created_at DESC)` for the Billing Ledger view (Summary C.82), `(wallet_id, settlement_at DESC)` partial where `settlement_at IS NOT NULL` for wallet-balance queries, `(capability_id, settlement_state, created_at)` for per-capability acceptance-rate dashboards, `(org_id, console, created_at DESC)` for per-console enumeration, `(parent_operation_id)` partial for Managed Agent sub-call tree queries, `(chain_correlation_id)` partial WHERE `chain_correlation_id IS NOT NULL` for multi-session journey reconstruction, `(settlement_state, contest_window_at)` partial where `settlement_state ∈ {accepted, auto_accepted}` for the 14-day-window expiry sweep, `(idempotency_key)` unique, `(provenance_hash)` for ContestRecord lookups, `(billed_against_committed_spend_id, settlement_at)` partial for commit-burn-down queries, `(redacted_at)` partial for DSAR audit.

**Scope Isolation.**

- **Buyer-console reads:** `console=buyer` only, `org_id = session.org_id`. Workspace-scoped operations additionally require `workspace_id = session.workspace_id` UNLESS the requester holds `org_admin` or `billing_admin` (then all `console=buyer` operations of the Org are visible).
- **Seller-console reads:** Symmetrically `console=seller` only with the same workspace gate.
- **Cross-console reads:** Blocked. A buyer-console session attempting to read a `console=seller` row of the same Org returns HTTP 404 with `ai_operation_cross_console_access` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 404 — 404 not 403 to avoid leaking existence). The same Org's `billing_admin` and `org_owner` ARE permitted cross-console reads on the Billing Ledger surface only (this is the legitimate exception necessary for unified billing reporting); these reads are flagged in audit log with action type `billing_ledger_cross_console_read`.
- **Sourcera-owned reads:** `console=platform_marketing`/`sourcera_owned` rows are NEVER returned to customer reads regardless of role; visible only to Ops with `ops_finance_admin` role.
- **Ops reads:** All fields, all consoles. Ops impersonation requires §35 impersonation audit.
- **Cross-Org reads:** Always blocked. A read attempt across orgs returns HTTP 404 with `ai_operation_cross_org_access` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 404).
- **Public API reads:** Org-scoped via the Public Pricing API (§4.8.9) is rate-card data only — never per-row AIOperation data. The Org-scoped private API (`GET /v1/billing/operations`) returns AIOperation rows scoped to the Org and the API token's console scope.
- **Writes:** Application-mediated only. Direct POST/PUT to AIOperation is forbidden (HTTP 403 `ai_operation_direct_write_forbidden`). Writes occur via the Outcome Resolver and the AI invocation handlers.

**State Machine.** Append-only after settlement; transitions enforced server-side; out-of-state writes rejected with `ai_operation_invalid_transition` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409). The authoritative transition table lives inline below; Appendix L (Entity State Machines) is now authored and covers the non-billing-entangled compendium (Internal Comment Thread, Buyer Referral, Pro Trial Seat Grant, KB Entry, KB Document). The AI Operation state machine is deliberately retained inline here because its transitions are tightly coupled to billing settlement, contest, and committed-spend semantics (§34) that live adjacent to this entity definition.

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Actor | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `pending` | AI invocation handler emits operation row | OutcomeContract for `capability_id` is `active`; FreeAllowanceCounter checked; wallet balance OR free allowance OR commit pool sufficient | System | Wallet hold (soft-reservation) placed for `value_price_cents` until settlement |
| `pending` | `accepted` | Outcome Resolver fires accepted signal per OutcomeContract within window | Signal type matches contract; signal received before `auto_accept_after_seconds` | System | `effective_charge_cents = value_price_cents`; wallet hold converted to charge; `settlement_at` stamped |
| `pending` | `rejected` | Outcome Resolver fires rejected signal | Signal type matches contract OR explicit user reject click | System / User | `effective_charge_cents = cost_price_cents`; wallet hold partially released; `settlement_at` stamped |
| `pending` | `auto_accepted` | Auto-accept timer expires with no signal | `now ≥ created_at + auto_accept_after_seconds` AND no signal received | System | Treated as accepted; `effective_charge_cents = value_price_cents`; flagged in dashboards as `auto_accepted` for product-quality monitoring (Summary §10 leading indicator: rejected-op rate per capability) |
| `accepted` / `auto_accepted` | `contested` | Billing Admin files ContestRecord within 14d | `now ≤ contest_window_at`; ContestRecord materialized; `contest_record_id` set | Billing Admin (User) | Wallet draw temporarily reversed pending Ops Finance review (soft credit) |
| `contested` | `reversed` | Ops Finance approves contest | ContestRecord.`status=approved` | Ops | `effective_charge_cents = 0`; reversal credit posted to wallet (or commit pool); audit row in Billing Ledger references both the original AIOperation and the reversal credit |
| `contested` | `accepted` | Ops Finance rejects contest, original was `accepted` | ContestRecord.`status=rejected`; original prior state preserved on ContestRecord | Ops | Soft credit reversed; original charge restored; `settlement_at` unchanged |
| `contested` | `auto_accepted` | Ops Finance rejects contest, original was `auto_accepted` | Same as above | Ops | Same as above |
| `accepted` / `auto_accepted` / `rejected` | (terminal at `contest_window_at + 1 minute`) | 14-day window expires without contest | `now > contest_window_at` | System | No state transition; downstream contest attempts return HTTP 410 `ai_operation_contest_window_expired` |
| Any settled state | `reversed` (Ops emergency path) | Ops Finance with `ops_finance_admin` invokes manual reversal | Documented note ≥ 50 chars; reason: `system_error_rollback` or `compliance_action` | Ops | Used for outcomes-resolver bugs detected after `contest_window_at`; logged with elevated audit severity |

**Settlement Freeze.** Once `settlement_state ∈ {accepted, rejected, auto_accepted, reversed}` and `contest_window_at < now`, the row is fully frozen: only `redacted_at` (DSAR) writes AND the **Ops emergency-reversal path** documented in the state-machine row at line 8166 are accepted. All other writes return `ai_operation_immutable_after_settlement` (HTTP 422). **Phase 7 V7 D-CONS-002 remediation (2026-05-07).** The Settlement Freeze rule and the state-machine row at line 8166 ("Any settled state → `reversed` (Ops emergency path)") are reconciled into a single coherent contract: post-`contest_window_at`, only two write classes are permitted — DSAR redaction (Pattern B per §6.8.4.1) and Ops emergency reversal under the §4.8.1.A Ops Emergency Reversal Protocol below. Both write classes are auditable, customer-notifiable, and event-emitting; both preserve the financial-record-integrity guarantee that no silent post-window mutation is possible. The Acceptance Criteria #3 wording is updated to enumerate the two carve-outs explicitly.

**§4.8.1.A Ops Emergency Reversal Protocol (Phase 7 V7 D-CONS-002 Remediation, 2026-05-07).**

The Ops emergency reversal at line 8166 is the platform's **last-resort** correction path for systemic outcome-resolver bugs, compliance actions, or settlement errors discovered after the 14-day contest window closes. It is materially distinct from in-window contest reversal (`contested → reversed` via §4.8.5 ContestRecord); the emergency path bypasses the customer-initiated 14-day window because the underlying defect is platform-side (e.g., a resolver bug that mis-classified 10,000 operations as `accepted` when the signal contract said `rejected`).

| Aspect | Rule |
| :---- | :---- |
| Authorization | `ops_finance_admin` role + Founder dual-signoff (per §50 Ops Console authorization matrix). Both signoffs MUST be present in the OpsActionRecord audit row before the reversal commits. |
| Permitted reasons | `system_error_rollback` (resolver bug / metering bug); `compliance_action` (legal / regulatory order); `customer_remediation_at_scale` (Sales-Ops-approved goodwill credit covering > 100 ops). Other reasons rejected with HTTP 422 `ai_operation_emergency_reversal_reason_invalid`. |
| Audit | OpsActionRecord row REQUIRED with: `actor_user_id` (Ops Finance), `cosignatory_user_id` (Founder), `decision_note ≥ 200 chars`, `reason_code`, `affected_operation_ids[]` (≤ 10,000 per single OpsActionRecord; flood ops use multiple records), `corresponding_ticket_ref` (Linear / Zendesk reference), `customer_notification_plan` (one of: per-customer email, public status-page post, in-app banner, no-notification with Counsel sign-off). |
| Customer notification | DEFAULT: per-customer email via Loops.so within 24 hours of reversal commit, citing the reversal reason in customer-comprehensible language; the email includes the reversed `effective_charge_cents` credited to the wallet. NO-NOTIFICATION exception requires Counsel sign-off documented on the OpsActionRecord. |
| Settlement state transition | Any settled state (`accepted`, `rejected`, `auto_accepted`) → `reversed` per state-machine row at line 8166. Wallet credit posted at `original_charge_cents` × `original_fx_rate_locked` per §4.8.1 Failure Mode #5 invariant. |
| Webhook | `ai_operation.emergency_reversed` (Appendix C; HMAC-SHA256 signed; idempotency via `event_id`; recipients: customer's webhook subscription + Ops Finance dashboard). Phase 7 V7 D-CONS-002 — added to Appendix C. |
| Stripe meter event | `sourcera_ai_value_emergency_reversed` (new Stripe meter event; tracks emergency reversals separately from contest-driven reversals for finance reporting clarity). |
| Settlement Freeze interaction | The Ops emergency reversal IS a permitted post-`contest_window_at` write class. The AC #3 wording explicitly enumerates this carve-out alongside DSAR redaction. |
| Volume cap | Per `(org_id, rolling 30-day window)`, an Ops emergency reversal MAY NOT exceed `max(100, 5% of accepted_ops_count_30d)` operations without **Founder + CFO + Counsel** triple-signoff (extending the dual-signoff to triple). Cap exists to prevent ops abuse. Cap breach surfaces as `ai_operation_emergency_reversal_volume_cap_exceeded` (HTTP 422) at OpsActionRecord write. |
| DSAR-vs-emergency-reversal interaction | DSAR redaction during open emergency reversal review is permitted (the redaction is a no-op against the financial fields preserved per §6.8.5; the emergency reversal targets `effective_charge_cents`, `settlement_state`, and `wallet_id` credit, none of which are DSAR-redacted). |
| Idempotency | OpsActionRecord `(actor_user_id, decision_note_hash, ai_operation_ids_hash)` unique; replay returns the existing record id. Prevents accidental double-reversal. |

The Ops emergency reversal is **not a customer-facing path**; customer-initiated reversal is the §4.8.5 ContestRecord 14-day window, full stop. The emergency path exists to correct platform-side errors that the 14-day window would have permitted but the customer didn't notice, and to discharge legal / regulatory orders. Regular use (e.g., ad-hoc credits without the dual-signoff documentation) is rejected at the `OpsActionRecord` write layer.

**FX-Locking Semantics (per C.84).** `fx_rate_locked` is set at write time to the daily Treasury rate for `(legal_entity, billing_currency)`. The FX rate is preserved through `contested` and `reversed`: a reversal credit issues at the same FX rate as the original charge so the customer's invoice nets to zero in their billing currency regardless of FX movement between charge and credit. The cost-base side (USD-denominated `cost_base_cents`) is not affected — Sourcera-internal accounting and customer-facing accounting are decoupled at the FX layer. Treasury rate source: Stripe Treasury daily snapshot at 00:00 UTC; cached for 24h; failover to ECB / IRS published rates with a 60-second cutover budget.

**Residency-Locked Invoicing (per C.84; canonical post-D-RES-004 4-value mapping, v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 2026-05-20).** `legal_entity` is locked at write to a fixed, deterministic, four-row mapping from `data_residency_region` (the canonical four-row residency registry per Appendix J `residency_region_kind` post-D-AJ-005, and §4.1.1 `data_residency_region` enum):

- `us` → `sourcera_us_llc`
- `eu` → `sourcera_eu_gmbh`
- `apac` → `sourcera_apac_pte`
- `custom` → `sourcera_custom`

The mapping is closed (exactly four rows, exactly one row per residency value); a `data_residency_region` value not in the four-row table is itself rejected at the Organization-write layer by the Appendix J `residency_region_kind` enum validator. A `custom`-residency Org's invoice line items are issued under `sourcera_custom` against the Org-specific `custom_sovereign_residency_label` (§4.1.1) which carries the Stripe Customer's billing-address jurisdiction and the underlying legal-entity sub-classification (e.g., `uk_crown_secure` → Sourcera UK-Crown-Secure-LLC operating subsidiary at the Stripe-Customer-metadata layer); the canonical `legal_entity` enum value remains `sourcera_custom` regardless of the sub-classification, preserving the four-value billing-event enumeration discipline.

The mapping is not customer-overridable. A customer changing `data_residency_region` does NOT retroactively re-issue prior invoices; subsequent operations write the new `legal_entity`. The cross-region migration *procedure* (Org Owner / Enterprise Admin / DPO authority; consent timeline; data-cutover semantics; in-flight AIOperation settlement) is an Ops procedure documented at §34.10.5.A Stripe-Customer Atomic-Binding Protocol (v7.2.0-REM Phase 5; this Master Spec) for the Stripe-side reconciliation contract, and at §1.6.1 (pending v7.1.1 stamp authoring per D-RES-007) for the full Org-side residency-change state machine. The §34.10.5.A protocol below is the canonical authority for the *billing surface* (Stripe Customer atomic-binding + new-invoice routing); §1.6.1 is the canonical authority for the *Org surface* (state-machine eligibility / consent / data migration). The two protocols compose: §1.6.1 calls §34.10.5.A at the cutover instant; §34.10.5.A is callable independently for the special case of a Stripe-side correction without a residency change (Ops emergency path; OpsActionRecord audit required).

**UK-residency historical-row migration backstop.** v7.1.0 pre-Phase-2V row state may include AIOperation / AIWallet / MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord rows with `legal_entity='sourcera_uk_ltd'` historically settled prior to the D-AJ-004 enum retirement. Such rows are immutable financial records per the §4.8.1 Settlement Freeze contract — they remain in-place under their historical enum value (which is preserved as a *historical* permissible value at the storage layer per the §40.2 retention contract for 7-year audit horizon) and are NOT mutated by the v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 reconciliation pass. New writes against the legacy value are rejected at the Convex schema-validation layer per the post-D-AJ-004 canonical 4-value `legal_entity_kind` enum. The §M.5.17 catalog block (this pass) registers `legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_test` to assert (a) no new write of `sourcera_uk_ltd` succeeds in any of the four entity homes (AIOperation, AIWallet, AIWalletLedgerEntry, MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord) and (b) historical rows with `legal_entity='sourcera_uk_ltd'` are *readable* under Ops-only / Finance-Reconciliation projections but produce no new Stripe Customer assignments. The historical Stripe Customer attached to those legacy invoices remains in place per §34.10.5.A invariant #4 (legacy invoices remain on the legacy Stripe Customer for audit fidelity).

**Retention.** AIOperation rows retained for **7 years** from `created_at` per SOC-2 audit requirements (financial records). DSAR right-to-erasure: `actor_id`, `input_content_hash`, `output_content_hash`, `prompt_template_version` are scrubbed (replaced with redaction sentinels); monetary, capability, FX, and `provenance_hash` fields preserved. Hard-delete is forbidden at the application layer. Residency: stored in the `legal_entity`'s residency region with no cross-region reads from customer surfaces (Ops Finance reads cross-region under §35 audit).

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Wallet exhausted mid-pending.** A `pending` AIOperation has a wallet hold for `value_price_cents`. If the wallet hold cannot be placed at write (insufficient balance + no commit pool + no free allowance), the operation is rejected before it begins with HTTP 402 `ai_operation_wallet_insufficient` (new; Appendix I) and no row is written. A successful write guarantees the funds are reserved; subsequent operations cannot starve a settled-pending operation.
2. **Outcome signal arrives after auto-accept timer.** Resolved: late `accepted` signals are silently ignored if `settlement_state=auto_accepted` (auto-accept holds); late `rejected` signals create a Contest Record automatically with `auto_filed_late_signal` reason — Ops Finance reviews. This prevents revenue loss to bug-late acceptance and customer overcharge to bug-late rejection.
3. **Anthropic price spike between write and Outcome Resolver settlement.** Resolved: `cost_base_cents` and `value_price_cents` / `cost_price_cents` are locked at write. A nightly recalc that re-derives a new cost_base produces a new `CostBaseRecalculationLog` row; existing pending operations continue to settle at their locked prices. The new cost_base applies only to operations created after the recalc's effective time.
4. **Managed Agent sub-call tree contains a failure mid-tree.** A parent operation can be `accepted` while a child operation is `rejected` — this is normal (Managed Agents try multiple sub-strategies; not all succeed). Per Summary C.55 the parent represents the customer-facing capability; children are sub-calls. Wallet draws hit only the customer-billed cost-center rows; sub-calls with `cost_center=sourcera_owned` are recorded for COGS without wallet impact.
5. **Reversal at a different FX rate than the original charge.** Resolved: `fx_rate_locked` is preserved on the original row through `reversed`; the reversal credit issues at the same FX rate. A 30-day FX move between charge and reversal does not produce a customer-currency residual.
6. **Contest filed at second 13-day-23-hour-59-second.** Resolved: `contest_window_at` is preserved as a strict-less-than; the system clock for the comparison is the database transaction commit time, not the API request time. This prevents off-by-one race exploits.
7. **Concurrent settlement attempts (e.g., Outcome Resolver and auto-accept timer fire within the same second).** Resolved: optimistic locking on `(id, settlement_state=pending)` predicate; second writer receives HTTP 409 `ai_operation_invalid_transition` and does not double-charge.
8. **DSAR redaction mid-contest.** Resolved: redaction is rejected during `contested` state with HTTP 423 `ai_operation_locked_for_contest` (new; Appendix I); after contest closes, redaction proceeds normally.
9. **Drift between `provenance_hash` and reconstructed hash on Contest filing.** Resolved: ContestRecord write rejects with `contest_provenance_hash_mismatch` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422); the customer must re-derive from the AIOperation row.
10. **Sourcera-owned operations leak into customer Billing Ledger.** Resolved: customer Billing Ledger query excludes `cost_center ∈ {sourcera_owned, platform_marketing}` at the query layer; QA test `billing_ledger_excludes_sourcera_owned` asserts the projection.
11. **Free-allowance race: two concurrent operations both consume the last free unit.** Resolved: §4.8.7 FreeAllowanceCounter uses an atomic decrement-and-return; the loser's operation transitions to wallet-billed with a single retry path.
12. **Anthropic returns an empty response (zero output tokens).** Resolved: the operation is written with `output_content_hash=null` and the Outcome Resolver fires `rejected` with reason `empty_response`; cost_price applies and a SIM signal raises after 5 such events on a single capability in 1 hour.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Every billable AI invocation across both consoles MUST produce exactly one AIOperation row at the moment work begins; missing-write recovery is via the §31 transactional outbox pattern (commit-time guarantee).
2. A read of an AIOperation by a session whose `console` does not match the row's `console` (excluding the `billing_admin` cross-console exception) MUST return HTTP 404 with `ai_operation_cross_console_access`; QA test `aiop_cross_console_isolation` asserts this for every console pair.
3. Once `contest_window_at < now`, all writes to the row except (a) DSAR redaction per §6.8.4.1 Pattern B, and (b) Ops emergency reversal under the §4.8.1.A Ops Emergency Reversal Protocol (with `ops_finance_admin` + Founder dual-signoff and OpsActionRecord audit), MUST return HTTP 422 `ai_operation_immutable_after_settlement`. Phase 7 V7 D-CONS-002 remediation (2026-05-07): the prior AC #3 wording reading "all writes except DSAR" silently elided the §4.8.1 line 8166 state-machine row's emergency-reversal path; this AC is now reconciled with §4.8.1.A as the single source of truth on permitted post-window writes. Deploy-time validator `settlement_freeze_carveouts_canonical` (Appendix M.5) asserts no other code path mutates a frozen AIOperation.
4. The `effective_charge_cents` MUST equal `value_price_cents` for `accepted`/`auto_accepted`, `cost_price_cents` for `rejected`, and `0` for `reversed`; any other combination MUST be rejected at the database constraint layer.
5. A reversal MUST credit the wallet (or commit pool) at the same `fx_rate_locked` and `legal_entity` as the original charge; QA test `aiop_reversal_fx_parity` asserts net-zero customer-currency residual on a charge-then-reverse round trip.
6. The 14-day contest window MUST be enforced server-side using the database transaction commit time as the comparison clock, not the API request time.
7. A successful write MUST guarantee the wallet hold; a wallet-insufficient operation MUST NOT write a row and MUST return HTTP 402 `ai_operation_wallet_insufficient`.
8. The Billing Ledger (Summary C.82) query MUST return rows in `(created_at DESC, id ASC)` order with cursor-based pagination, default 50, max 250, per §32 conventions.
9. `cost_center ∈ {sourcera_owned, platform_marketing}` rows MUST NOT appear in any customer-facing read projection; QA test `aiop_sourcera_owned_isolation` asserts this against every customer endpoint.
10. The `(idempotency_key)` unique constraint MUST cause a duplicate-write attempt to return HTTP 200 with the existing row id (idempotent replay), not HTTP 409.
11. Late-arriving outcome signals after `auto_accepted` MUST NOT mutate `settlement_state`; late-arriving `rejected` signals after `auto_accepted` MUST automatically materialize a ContestRecord with reason `auto_filed_late_signal` and notify Ops Finance within 5 minutes.
12. DSAR redaction MUST satisfy §6.8.4.1 Pattern B for `actor_id` when `actor_type = user` or `actor_type = ops`: the FK `actor_id` column itself is **preserved**; the User row pointed to by `actor_id` is pseudonymized in-place per §6.8.4.1 Pattern B. When `actor_type ∈ {managed_agent, system}` the DSAR cascade against `actor_id` is a no-op (the resolving identity is not a GDPR subject). The non-FK content-encoding columns `input_content_hash`, `output_content_hash`, `prompt_template_version` MUST be scrubbed (these are content hashes that encode subject input under the §6.8.5 row class #3 Pattern A column-rewrite treatment). The financial-fields set MUST be preserved verbatim: `cost_base_cents`, `value_price_cents`, `cost_price_cents`, `effective_charge_cents`, `fx_rate_locked`, `legal_entity`, `provenance_hash`, `settlement_state`, `settlement_at`, `created_at`. QA test `aiop_dsar_redaction_field_set` asserts the exact field partition. CI gate `dsar_cascade_pseudonym_pattern_consistency` (§6.8.4.1 AC #1) asserts AIOperation membership in the Pattern B set. **D-3.5-003 V3 remediation, 2026-05-04** — pre-remediation AC #12 prescribed scrubbing `actor_id`, contradicting §6.8.4.1 Pattern B; the contradiction is resolved in favor of Pattern B (financial-record audit FK preservation is the correct posture per §6.8.5 row class #3 financial-record exemption).
13. Managed Agent sub-call trees MUST be queryable via the `(parent_operation_id)` index with depth-first traversal returning the full subtree in a single query; the maximum tree depth is capped at 6 with `ai_operation_managed_agent_depth_exceeded` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422) on attempted insert beyond depth 6.
13a. Multi-session customer-facing journeys (including Ghost-Bid Importer §22.14.4) MUST write the same `chain_correlation_id` to every parent AIOperation in the chain before the first child operation starts; QA test `aiop_chain_correlation_id_completeness` asserts that the journey can be reconstructed without relying on Anthropic session IDs.
14. The `legal_entity` MUST equal the deterministic mapping from the Org's `data_residency_region` at write time per the canonical 4-row Residency-Locked Invoicing mapping above (`us → sourcera_us_llc`; `eu → sourcera_eu_gmbh`; `apac → sourcera_apac_pte`; `custom → sourcera_custom`); mismatch MUST be rejected with `ai_operation_legal_entity_residency_mismatch` (Appendix I; HTTP 422). The mapping function is total over the Appendix J `residency_region_kind` enum and surjective onto the Appendix J `legal_entity_kind` enum — every residency value has exactly one legal-entity target and vice versa; a `data_residency_region` value not in the four-row table is itself rejected upstream at the Organization-write layer (Appendix J enum validator), so AC #14 never fires for an unmapped residency value. **D-RES-004 V72REM Phase 5 remediation, 2026-05-20** — pre-remediation AC #14 wording cited a `legal_entity` enum at `Appendix J line 45257–45266` that diverged from the canonical post-Phase-2V `legal_entity_kind` enum at `Appendix J line 49594–49598`; the divergence permitted a `custom`-residency Org to write any AIOperation row at all (the old four-value enum had no `custom` target, so AC #14 fired with `ai_operation_legal_entity_residency_mismatch` on every write — a fail-closed regression that effectively blocked the entire `custom`-residency Enterprise / sovereign-cloud cohort from billing). The reconciliation to the post-D-AJ-004 four-value canonical set restores fail-open for the legitimate `custom` cohort while preserving fail-closed for genuine residency / legal-entity mismatches.
14a. The `legal_entity` value `sourcera_uk_ltd` MUST NOT be accepted by the Convex schema validator on a *new* AIOperation write at or after the v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 stamp (2026-05-20). The Convex schema validator enforces the canonical 4-value `legal_entity_kind` enum (`sourcera_us_llc`, `sourcera_eu_gmbh`, `sourcera_apac_pte`, `sourcera_custom`) for all new writes. Historical rows with `legal_entity='sourcera_uk_ltd'` settled prior to the v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 stamp are preserved verbatim per the §4.8.1 Settlement Freeze contract and the §40.2 7-year SOC-2 financial-records retention rule; such rows remain *readable* through Ops-Finance and Compliance projections under the existing scope-isolation roles. CI gate `legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_test` (Appendix M.5 §M.5.17) asserts the canonical 4-value write-time enforcement AND asserts the historical-row read-fidelity invariant (no new Stripe Customer assignment is keyed off a legacy `sourcera_uk_ltd` row).
14b. A residency change on an Org (`data_residency_region` mutation; e.g., `us → eu`) MUST atomically trigger the §34.10.5.A Stripe-Customer Atomic-Binding Protocol: the new `legal_entity` is computed from the canonical 4-row mapping; a new Stripe Customer is created keyed on the new `(org_id, legal_entity)` pair; the prior Stripe Customer is set to `closed_for_new_invoices` with its historical invoices preserved verbatim; in-flight `pending` AIOperations settle on the *prior* Stripe Customer to honor the §4.8.1 FX-Locking semantics (the `fx_rate_locked` and `legal_entity` snapshot at AIOperation write time bind the settlement Customer); operations created *after* the residency-change cutover write the new Customer. No Stripe Charge MAY route across the cutover boundary; the cutover is enforced via a single Convex mutation-layer transaction that updates `Organization.data_residency_region`, creates the new Stripe Customer (via Stripe API), and stamps `Organization.stripe_customer_id_active`; failure of any step rolls back the mutation. CI gate `legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_test` (Appendix M.5 §M.5.17) asserts the atomicity invariant.
15. The `settlement_state` transition graph MUST exactly match the table above; any out-of-graph transition MUST be rejected with `ai_operation_invalid_transition` (HTTP 409).

### 4.8.2 CapabilityRegistryEntry (Platform-Scoped, Ops-Managed) {#4.8.2-capabilityregistryentry}

**Authoring Intent.** CapabilityRegistryEntry is the authoritative, Ops-Console-managed list of every capability that can produce an AIOperation. It supersedes the historic v6.0.0 hardcoded "21 capabilities" reference and decouples the platform's billing surface from code deploys: a new capability is added by writing a CapabilityRegistryEntry, an OutcomeContract, and (if customer-billed) a CostBaseRecalculationLog seed — no code release needed for the billing layer to recognize the new capability. The registry is also the source of truth for plan gating (which capabilities require which plan tier), free-allowance applicability, and rate-card publication. Per Summary C.76, deprecations are soft (capability remains queryable at a `deprecated` state with successor pointer).

**Scope.** Platform-scoped (no `org_id`; global registry). All Orgs see the same registry. Read access is platform-wide for any authenticated session and for the Public Pricing API (§4.8.9) for `customer_billed` rows. Ops-only writes via `ops_finance_admin` and `ops_capability_admin` roles.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `capability_id` | String | 1–80 chars; lowercase snake_case; unique | Stable identifier referenced by AIOperation, OutcomeContract, FreeAllowanceCounter; immutable after first publish |
| `display_name` | String | 1–120 chars | Customer-visible name in Billing Ledger and Public Pricing API |
| `category` | Enum | See Appendix J Capability Categories (extended: `evaluation`, `seller_kb`, `seller_response`, `marketplace_content`, `intelligence`, `agent_orchestration`) | Rollup dimension for dashboards |
| `console_applicability` | Array[Enum] | Subset of `ai_operation_console`; ≥ 1 element | Which consoles may invoke this capability; e.g., First-Pass RFP Response is `[seller]`; Pre-Scoring is `[buyer]`; KB Suggestion is `[buyer, seller]` |
| `model_tier_default` | Enum | See Appendix J `ai_operation_model_tier` | Default model class for cost-base seeding |
| `model_id_default` | String | ≤ 120 chars | Default Anthropic model id; nightly recalc may pin the latest |
| `billing_mode` | Enum | See Appendix J `capability_registry_billing_mode`: `customer_billed`, `sourcera_owned`, `platform_marketing` | Drives wallet behavior on AIOperation; `sourcera_owned` and `platform_marketing` never draw the wallet |
| `cost_center_default` | Enum | See Appendix J `sourcera_owned_cost_center` (extended) | Cross-references `billing_mode`; populated on AIOperation.`cost_center` |
| `min_value_price_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Floor on `value_price_cents` regardless of cost_base × 10 — used for capabilities where the multiplier produces an unrealistically low price |
| `min_cost_price_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Floor on `cost_price_cents` |
| `value_multiplier` | Decimal(6,3) | Default 10.000 | Per-capability override of the standard 10× multiplier (rare; default 10.000 holds across the board) |
| `cost_multiplier` | Decimal(6,3) | Default 1.050 | Per-capability override of the 1.05× multiplier |

| `free_allowance_quantity_default` | Integer | ≥ 0; default 10 | Per Summary C.80, the default free-op count per Org per capability; overridable per Org via Ops |
| `free_allowance_resets_per_period` | Boolean | Default false | When true, the allowance resets per billing period; default false (lifetime allowance per Org per capability) |

| `requires_committed_spend` | Boolean | Default false | When true, only Orgs with an active CommittedSpendContract may invoke (Enterprise-only capabilities) |

| `state` | Enum | See Appendix J `capability_registry_status`: `alpha`, `beta`, `active`, `deprecated`, `retired` | Lifecycle |
| `successor_capability_id` | String | Nullable; FK → CapabilityRegistryEntry.`capability_id` | Required when `state=deprecated`; powers customer-facing migration messaging |

| `surface_throttling_class` | Enum | See Appendix J `surface_throttling_class`: `active_workflow`, `low_priority_background`, `never_throttle`. Default `active_workflow`. | Phase 14.10 / 14.10.1 — Solo-tier surface treatment routing per §44.6.4.1. `active_workflow` capabilities are NEVER throttled regardless of envelope state; `low_priority_background` capabilities are silently throttled at ≥ `throttling_threshold` of envelope per §44.6.4 (default 80%); `never_throttle` is reserved for billing-cycle-critical capabilities (e.g., outcome resolution, refund processing). Internal-only attribute; never surfaced. v7.1 `low_priority_background` membership: `proactive_cmd_k_marketplace_surfacing`, `weekly_kb_refresh_suggestions`, `vendor_page_enrichment_polling` — registered as §4.8.2-fidelity `CapabilityRegistryEntry` rows at **§21.4.6 Solo Throttling Membership** (v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.4 D-EM-004 closure, 2026-05-19); §21.4.6 is the canonical authority and the closed-set membership is mutation-guarded by the §M.5 meta-gate `low_priority_background_solo_throttling_membership_canonical` per §21.4.6. |

Internal-only; never surfaced; Ops-only writable via `ops_finance_admin`. Override values outside the §44.6.4 `throttling_threshold` 50–95% range are rejected with HTTP 422 `solo_envelope_throttling_threshold_out_of_range` (Appendix I). |

Reserved for "active workflow" capabilities whose mid-bid / mid-eval interruption would corrupt the operator's primary task — notably `first_pass_rfp_draft` per §22.20.5 (canonical capability_id registered at §21.4.1.E per the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.3 D-EM-003 closure; prior non-canonical alias `first_pass_rfp_response_generator` rewritten to canonical form at Phase 4.5 loose-ends closure 2026-05-19 per D-NOM-016 P2; legacy string preserved as an `aliases` array entry on the §21.4.1.E row for SDK back-compat). The flag is engine-side only; never surfaced. Schema-validation test `solo_capability_registry_field_registration` per §44.6.8 #17 asserts presence of this field. |

| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Ops user | Required `ops_capability_admin` role |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Ops user | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Always NULL | Hard-delete is forbidden; deprecation is the terminal path |

**Indexes.** `(capability_id)` unique, `(state, console_applicability)` for available-capability listings, `(billing_mode, state)` for rate-card publication, `(plan_gate_min_tier)` partial for plan-gate enforcement queries, `(successor_capability_id)` partial for migration-graph traversal.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `alpha` | Ops creates entry | Internal Ops-only invocation; not in Public Pricing API; AIOperations recorded but never customer-billed | Used during capability development |
| `alpha` | `beta` | Ops promotes | OutcomeContract present and signed off; CostBase seed exists | Limited customer rollout; customer-billed if `billing_mode=customer_billed` and customer is on the rollout list |
| `beta` | `active` | Ops promotes | 30 days in beta minimum; rejected-rate <40% sustained over the prior 7 days | GA: included in Public Pricing API |
| `active` | `deprecated` | Ops deprecates | `successor_capability_id` set; `deprecation_grace_until` set ≥ 90 days out | Customer-visible banner; rate card flags as deprecated |
| `deprecated` | `retired` | `deprecation_grace_until` passes | No new AIOperations may be created; existing rows preserve their reference | Permanent terminal state; capability removed from Public Pricing API |
| `active` | `active` | Ops adjusts (display_name, value_multiplier, cost_multiplier, plan_gate_min_tier) | Any field change of a customer-visible attribute triggers a new PricingTableVersion publish | Audit row in §6.7 audit log |

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Capability promoted to active with broken OutcomeContract.** Resolved: state-transition guard `capability_promotion_requires_active_outcome_contract` enforces `OutcomeContract.state=active` before `beta → active`.
2. **Customer attempts deprecated capability without successor migration.** Resolved: deprecated capabilities remain invokable until `deprecation_grace_until`; UI surfaces successor; AIOperation write is permitted but emits `capability.invoke.deprecated` PostHog event for monitoring.
3. **Two Ops admins write conflicting price multipliers concurrently.** Resolved: optimistic concurrency on `(id, updated_at)`; second writer rejected with HTTP 409 `capability_registry_concurrent_modification` (new; Appendix I).
4. **A `customer_billed` capability lacks a CostBase seed.** Resolved: write-time validation rejects with `capability_registry_missing_cost_base_seed` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422); Ops must seed the cost base via §4.8.6 before publishing.
5. **Removal of a referenced capability_id.** Resolved: hard-delete blocked at the application layer; deprecation is the only retirement path; existing AIOperation `capability_id` references survive deprecation.
6. **Plan gate bypass via API token created before plan downgrade.** Resolved: `plan_gate_min_tier` evaluated at AIOperation write time, not at API token creation time; the AI invocation handler queries the current plan tier (Org-scoped) before allowing the operation.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. The `capability_id` MUST be immutable once any AIOperation has referenced it.
2. A capability with `billing_mode=customer_billed` MUST have a non-null `outcome_contract_id` referencing an `active` OutcomeContract before `state=active`.
3. Deprecation MUST require `successor_capability_id` set and `deprecation_grace_until` ≥ 90 days from the deprecation timestamp.
4. The Public Pricing API (§4.8.9) MUST include exactly the `customer_billed` rows with `state ∈ {active, beta if customer is on rollout, deprecated within grace}`; QA test `pricing_api_capability_filter` asserts.
5. A field change to a customer-visible attribute (display_name, value_multiplier, cost_multiplier, unit_label, plan_gate_min_tier, free_allowance_quantity_default) MUST cause a new PricingTableVersion publish within 60 seconds.
6. Concurrent Ops writes MUST be rejected with HTTP 409 `capability_registry_concurrent_modification`.
7. A `requires_committed_spend=true` capability MUST be invokable ONLY by Orgs with an active CommittedSpendContract; non-commit Orgs MUST receive HTTP 402 `capability_requires_committed_spend` (new; Appendix I).
8. **Solo-tier surface treatment fields (Phase 14.10 / 14.10.1).** Every `CapabilityRegistryEntry` MUST carry `surface_throttling_class`, `solo_envelope_override_value_cents`, and `solo_envelope_no_block` per §44.6.4.1. Schema-validation test `solo_capability_registry_field_registration` (§M.4 catalog; §44.6.8 #17) asserts presence of each field. `surface_throttling_class` MUST be one of the three Appendix J enum values; `solo_envelope_override_value_cents`, when non-null, MUST be derived from a `throttling_threshold` integer percent in `[50, 95]` per §44.6.4. Violations rejected at write with HTTP 422 `solo_envelope_throttling_threshold_out_of_range` (Appendix I).
9. **Family-rooted sibling-split integrity (v7.2.0-REM Phase 4 D-EM-001 + Phase 4.2 D-EM-002 closures — generalized).** Every AIOperation whose `capability_id` belongs to a registered family-rooted sibling-split set MUST cite a `capability_id` from the sibling set of its `capability_family` (NEVER the family-root identifier). The three registered family splits at v7.1.0a stamp are (a) `qa_suggestion_family` → `{qa_suggestion_buyer, qa_suggestion_seller}` (per §21.4.1.B); (b) `kb_suggestion_family` → `{kb_suggestion_buyer, kb_suggestion_seller}` (per §21.4.1.D); (c) `org_intelligence_family` → `{org_intelligence_vendor_history, org_intelligence_full, org_intelligence_suggestions}` (per §21.4.1 row 16). Direct invocation of any family-root identifier MUST be rejected at the AI invocation handler with HTTP 422 `capability_rollup_root_not_invokable` per Appendix I (v7.2.0-REM Phase 4 extension). Deploy-time validators `qa_suggestion_family_cardinality` (§M.5.14) and `kb_suggestion_family_cardinality` (§M.5.15) assert per-family; `org_intelligence_family_cardinality` is registered for forward-compatibility under the same `not_permitted_capability_family_integrity` override class and lands its runtime wiring in M11.3 per AE-V72REM-PH4.2-01. New family-rooted sibling-splits added by future remediation passes MUST extend this AC by appending to the registered-family list and registering a paired `{family}_family_cardinality` gate in the §M.5 catalog; the closed-set generalization holds at every stamp boundary.

**Retention.** Life of platform. Deprecated entries retained indefinitely for FK integrity. DSAR: not applicable (Ops-authored metadata; no subject PII).

### 4.8.3 AIWallet (Org-Scoped, Pooled Across Consoles) {#4.8.3-aiwallet}

**Authoring Intent.** AIWallet is the org-scoped, console-pooled value-dollar account that every customer-billed AIOperation draws against. Per Pricing Strategy §11 the wallet is explicitly Org-scoped and pooled — an Org holding (Buyer Growth + Seller Starter) sees a single $330/mo unified budget — and the Dual-Console Firewall does not partition the wallet (billing is shared; data is not). The wallet is the single source of truth for: included monthly budget remaining, overage cap remaining, auto-topup configuration, active soft/hard cap state, residency-locked invoicing entity, and the linked Stripe customer/subscription identifiers. The wallet is also the surface where free allowances flow up to monetization (an Org consuming its 10 free Pre-Scoring runs migrates seamlessly to wallet-billed Pre-Scoring on the 11th invocation).

**Field-naming convention.** Every `*_value_dollars` field on this entity is stored as **Integer USD cents** (Convex schema → Stripe charges → pricing-engine math all operate in cents). The legacy `value_dollars` token in field names is a display-aware-naming convention preserved for Convex-schema-migration safety; storage is always cents. See Appendix K Glossary entry `value_dollars` field-naming convention (Phase V14 D-V14-005 Authored Extension) for the canonical rule and the `value_dollars_storage_convention_audit` CI gate. Refines pre-existing decision **E-1 Currency Unit Convention** per `_integration/Decisions.md` and D-DEC-001 (P1); the eventual `*_cents` rename path is driven by E-1 ratification.

**Scope.** Org-scoped; one row per Org. Reads are restricted to `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `billing_admin` (a new role authored here — see RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions); Ops with `ops_finance_admin` reads all wallets. Writes are confined to: the AI invocation handler (decrements `consumed_value_dollars`), the Stripe webhook handler (increments `budget_value_dollars` on subscription renewal, increments `overage_cap_value_dollars` on top-up success), the Outcome Resolver (issues credits on `reversed` operations), the Contest Reviewer (issues approved-contest credits), and Ops manual adjustments with mandatory note.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization; unique | One wallet per Org; cross-console pooling enforced by the absence of a `console` column |
| `wallet_state` | Enum | See Appendix J `ai_wallet_state`: `active`, `soft_warned_50`, `soft_warned_80`, `hard_capped_100`, `hard_capped_auto_topup_monthly_cap` (Phase 7 V7 D-V7-002 remediation 2026-05-07), `payment_failed_grace`, `suspended`, `closed` | See state machine below. The `hard_capped_auto_topup_monthly_cap` state is distinct from `hard_capped_100`: the former is reached when auto-topup is enabled but `auto_topup_consumed_monthly + auto_topup_increment > auto_topup_max_monthly`, even if `consumed_value_dollars + overage_consumed_value_dollars < (budget + overage_cap)` would still permit further consumption against unfunded headroom. The state preserves operator-diagnostic clarity: an Org seeing `hard_capped_auto_topup_monthly_cap` knows the binding constraint is the customer-set monthly auto-topup cap, not an infrastructural exhaustion. |
| `auto_topup_monthly_cap_exhausted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Phase 7 V7 D-V7-002 remediation. Stamped when the auto-topup state machine first attempts to fire and the projected charge would exceed `auto_topup_max_monthly_value_dollars`; cleared at billing-period rollover (when `auto_topup_consumed_monthly` resets). |

**Indexes.** `(org_id)` unique, `(wallet_state, current_period_ends_at)` for the period-rollover sweep, `(auto_topup_trigger_state, updated_at)` partial for top-up scheduler, `(payment_failed_grace_until)` partial where `wallet_state=payment_failed_grace` for grace-expiry sweep, `(committed_spend_contract_id)` partial, `(plan_tier, wallet_state, consumed_value_dollars DESC)` for the plan-tier balance-sweep cohort analysis (required to drive the plan-tier utilization histograms on the Ops Billing dashboard without full-table scans at Org volume; partial scope `WHERE wallet_state IN ('active', 'soft_cap_50', 'soft_cap_80', 'hard_capped_100')` excludes closed-Org and suspended rows).

**Scope Isolation.**

- **Buyer-console reads:** `org_id = session.org_id`; `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `billing_admin` see all fields; `member` and `guest` see HTTP 403 `wallet_role_forbidden`.
- **Seller-console reads:** Same as above (the wallet is shared).
- **Public reads:** Forbidden.
- **Ops reads:** All; `ops_finance_admin` may also write (manual adjustment).
- **Cross-Org reads:** HTTP 404 `wallet_cross_org_access`.

**Wallet State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `active` | Org first publishes a paid plan OR Free Org first invokes a customer-billed capability | Stripe customer created; `budget_value_dollars` set per plan tier | Free Orgs receive a $5/mo budget per Pricing Strategy §4 |
| `active` | `soft_warned_50` | Consumed crosses 50% of `(budget + overage_cap)` | Email + in-app notification to Org Owner + Billing Admin | One-shot; `notification_50pct_sent_at` stamped |
| `soft_warned_50` | `soft_warned_80` | Consumed crosses 80% | Same notification recipients | One-shot; auto-topup may fire here if enabled |
| `soft_warned_80` | `hard_capped_100` | Consumed crosses 100% AND auto-topup unavailable / disabled / Stripe charge fails | All subsequent customer-billed AIOperation writes return HTTP 402 `wallet_hard_capped` (Appendix I); Sourcera-owned operations continue | Customer-visible banner with one-click upgrade or top-up CTAs |
| `soft_warned_80` | `hard_capped_auto_topup_monthly_cap` | Auto-topup state machine attempts to fire AND `auto_topup_consumed_monthly + auto_topup_increment > auto_topup_max_monthly_value_dollars` | All subsequent customer-billed AIOperation writes return HTTP 402 `wallet_auto_topup_monthly_cap_exhausted` (Appendix I; new in Phase 7 V7 D-V7-002 remediation, distinct from `wallet_hard_capped`); Sourcera-owned operations continue | Phase 7 V7 D-V7-002 remediation. Customer-visible banner explicitly cites the customer-set monthly cap as the binding constraint, with deep-link to wallet config UI to raise the cap. The `auto_topup_monthly_cap_exhausted` event fires (Appendix C; HMAC-SHA256 signed; recipient: `org_owner` + `billing_admin`). |
| `hard_capped_100` | `active` | Top-up succeeds OR billing period rolls over OR plan upgrade | Wallet headroom restored | All counters relevant to current period reset only at rollover |
| `hard_capped_auto_topup_monthly_cap` | `active` | Billing period rolls over (`auto_topup_consumed_monthly` resets to 0) OR `billing_admin` raises `auto_topup_max_monthly_value_dollars` AND a subsequent top-up succeeds OR plan upgrade | Wallet headroom restored | Phase 7 V7 D-V7-002 remediation. Distinct exit-trigger set from `hard_capped_100` because the binding constraint is the customer-set monthly cap. |
| `hard_capped_auto_topup_monthly_cap` | `hard_capped_100` | Customer raises `auto_topup_max_monthly_value_dollars` but total consumption then crosses 100% before next top-up succeeds | | Phase 7 V7 D-V7-002 remediation. Allows the wallet to flow into the standard hard-cap state if the customer's headroom expansion proves insufficient. |
| `active` (or any soft_warned state) | `payment_failed_grace` | Auto-topup charge fails | `payment_failed_grace_until = now + 48h` | Wallet remains active during grace; billing admin emailed hourly |
| `payment_failed_grace` | `active` | Top-up retry succeeds | | |
| `payment_failed_grace` | `suspended` | Grace expires without successful top-up | | All customer-billed operations rejected; Ops alert |
| `suspended` | `active` | Manual Ops resolution OR customer updates payment method + retry succeeds | | |
| Any | `closed` | Org deletion OR Ops closure | `closed_at` stamped; wallet read-only afterward | Financial records (AIOperations) survive |

**§4.8.3.A Top-Up State Machine.** Encapsulates the auto-topup state machine for clarity:

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `idle` | `pending_charge` | `auto_topup_trigger_utilization_pct` reached | `auto_topup_enabled=true`; `auto_topup_consumed_monthly + auto_topup_increment ≤ auto_topup_max_monthly` | Stripe charge initiated |
| `pending_charge` | `completed` | Stripe charge succeeds | `last_topup_at` stamped; `overage_cap_value_dollars += increment`; `auto_topup_consumed_monthly += increment` | |
| `pending_charge` | `failed_retry` | Stripe charge fails (transient) | Retry per the non-webhook `auto_topup_charge` Stripe charge policy (1s, 5s, 30s, 2m, 10m; DLQ at attempt 5) | Wallet enters `payment_failed_grace` |
| `failed_retry` | `completed` | Retry succeeds | | |
| `failed_retry` | `abandoned` | DLQ at attempt 5 | Wallet enters `suspended` after grace expiry | Ops alert |
| `completed` | `idle` | Period rolls over | `auto_topup_consumed_monthly` resets | |

**Free Allowance Interaction.** When an Org invokes a customer-billed capability for which it has unconsumed FreeAllowanceCounter units, the AIOperation is written with `billed_against_free_allowance=true` and `effective_charge_cents=0`; the FreeAllowanceCounter atomically decrements. Wallet counters are NOT touched. On exhaustion, subsequent operations follow standard wallet-draw semantics.

**Committed Spend Interaction.** When `committed_spend_contract_id` is set, AIOperations preferentially burn down `commit_burn_remaining_value_dollars` before drawing `budget_value_dollars`/`overage_cap_value_dollars`. The commit is the customer's pre-paid commit pool — billing the wallet first would be an accounting error.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Currency change mid-period.** Resolved: `billing_currency` is immutable post-create except via Ops Finance with explicit migration runbook (out of scope for entity; flagged).
2. **Stripe webhook fires twice (idempotency violation).** Resolved: `stripe_invoice_lookup_token` deduplication + Stripe's `event.id` outbox dedup at the webhook handler layer.
3. **Period rollover at midnight UTC for an Org with `billing_period_anchor_day_utc=31` in February.** Resolved: month-end normalization (Feb 28 / Feb 29); `current_period_ends_at` always equals the next anchor day.
4. **Customer disables auto-topup mid-charge.** Resolved: in-flight Stripe charges complete; the disable takes effect for future triggers; UI shows "Top-up in progress; auto-topup disabled effective next period."
5. **Wallet enters `suspended` while a `pending` AIOperation is open.** Resolved: pending operations may settle normally (the wallet hold was placed at write time and is honored through settlement); only NEW operations are blocked.
6. **Org changes residency mid-period.** Resolved: `residency_locked_entity` change requires Ops with re-invoicing runbook; in-period residency changes do not retroactively reissue invoices.
7. **Free allowance and wallet both insufficient simultaneously.** Resolved: AIOperation write is rejected with HTTP 402 `wallet_hard_capped`; UI surfaces upgrade or top-up CTAs.
8. **Concurrent decrements from two AI invocations consuming the last $0.05 of headroom.** Resolved: optimistic locking on `(id, consumed_value_dollars)`; second writer retries with re-evaluation; if headroom now insufficient, the second operation receives HTTP 402.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. The wallet MUST be Org-scoped (one row per Org) regardless of console plan combinations; QA test `wallet_org_unique` asserts.
2. `consumed_value_dollars` MUST reset exactly at `current_period_ends_at`; cron-based with idempotent retry; missed run alerts Ops within 1 hour.
3. Customer-billed AIOperation writes MUST be rejected with HTTP 402 `wallet_hard_capped` when the wallet is `hard_capped_100` AND no commit pool AND no free allowance is applicable.
4. Auto-topup MUST NEVER be enabled by default; an admin action with explicit confirmation MUST be required to set `auto_topup_enabled=true`.
5. `auto_topup_increment_value_dollars` MUST be ≥ $50 and ≤ $10,000; values outside this range MUST be rejected with HTTP 422 `wallet_topup_increment_out_of_range` (new; Appendix I).
6. The 50%, 80%, and 100% notifications MUST be one-shot per period (idempotency stamps prevent duplicate emails); QA test `wallet_notifications_idempotent` asserts.
7. Free Allowance consumption MUST atomically decrement the FreeAllowanceCounter and write `billed_against_free_allowance=true` on the AIOperation; QA test `wallet_free_allowance_atomicity` asserts no double-spend.
8. Commit-pool burn-down MUST precede wallet-budget burn-down for Orgs with an active CommittedSpendContract; QA test `wallet_commit_burn_priority` asserts.
9. A wallet in `suspended` state MUST NOT block in-flight `pending` AIOperations; only new operations are blocked.
10. The wallet MUST never hold a non-USD `budget_value_dollars` value internally; presentation in the customer's `billing_currency` is via `fx_rate_locked` at presentation time only.

**Retention.** Org-life + 7 years (SOC-2 financial audit). On Org hard-delete, balance + audit fields preserved; `stripe_customer_id` and `billing_admin_user_ids[]` zeroed to `DESTROYED_ON_ORG_DELETE` sentinel. DSAR: `owner_user_id`, `billing_admin_user_ids[]` pseudonymized on subject request; financial rows retained per §6.8.5 audit-integrity exemption.

### 4.8.4 OutcomeContract (Per-Capability, Versioned, Ops-Managed) {#4.8.4-outcomecontract}

**Authoring Intent.** OutcomeContract defines, per capability, the precise, machine-readable rules under which an AIOperation transitions from `pending` to `accepted` or `rejected`. It is the canonical location for the Pricing Strategy §6 / §10 outcome-signal tables (Appendix B in the Buyer Pricing Strategy, §10 in the Seller Pricing Strategy). Because the Outcome Resolver is the single source of truth for Sourcera's margin protection, the contract is versioned: a contract change does NOT retroactively reclassify settled operations, and `pending` operations always resolve under the contract version that was active at AIOperation write time.

**Scope.** Platform-scoped; many-to-one with CapabilityRegistryEntry (a capability has one active contract version at a time but a history of prior contracts).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `capability_id` | String | FK → CapabilityRegistryEntry.`capability_id`; required | The capability this contract governs |
| `version` | Integer | ≥ 1 | Monotonic per `capability_id` |
| `accepted_signal_rule` | JSON | ≤ 8000 chars | Structured rule referencing one or more `outcome_contract_signal_type` values; supports composite (AND/OR) rules |
| `rejected_signal_rule` | JSON | ≤ 8000 chars; nullable | Optional explicit rejection rule; absence means rejection only via timeout (auto-accept fires) or explicit user reject button |
| `auto_accept_after_seconds` | Integer | ≥ 60 (1 minute floor); ≤ 7776000 (90-day ceiling) | The auto-accept timer; copied to AIOperation.`auto_accept_after_seconds` at write time |
| `contest_window_days` | Integer | Default 14 (Summary C.78); ≥ 1; ≤ 90 | Per-capability contest window override (default 14 used if not overridden); copied to AIOperation `contest_window_at` derivation |
| `signal_evaluation_grace_seconds` | Integer | Default 30 | Time after `auto_accept_after_seconds` during which a late `accepted` signal still counts (race-condition mitigation) |
| `requires_explicit_user_signal` | Boolean | Default false | When true, no auto-accept — the operation hangs in `pending` until an explicit accept/reject signal arrives or 90 days pass (then auto-rejected as `rejected_timeout_no_signal`) |
| `signal_subject_entity_kinds` | Array[Enum] | Subset of AIOperation entity kinds | Which downstream entities the resolver watches for retention/edit signals |
| `min_retention_threshold_pct` | Integer | 0–100; nullable | For "retention" signal types; e.g., "≥ 50% of draft retained in submitted bid" |
| `max_edit_threshold_pct` | Integer | 0–100; nullable | For "edit-distance" signal types; e.g., "≤ 20% edit" |
| `state` | Enum | `draft`, `active`, `superseded`, `retired` | Lifecycle |
| `superseded_by_contract_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → OutcomeContract | When state=superseded, the next-version contract |
| `effective_at` | Timestamp | UTC | When this contract version became active |
| `superseded_at` | Timestamp | Nullable; UTC | |
| `published_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Ops user with `ops_finance_admin` | |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC; only allowed in `draft` state |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Ops user | |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Ops user | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Always NULL | Hard-delete forbidden |

**Indexes.** `(capability_id, version DESC)`, `(capability_id, state)` partial where `state=active` (a capability has at most one active contract; enforced as a partial unique index), `(superseded_by_contract_id)` partial.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `draft` | Ops creates new version | `version = MAX(prior versions) + 1` | Editable in draft |
| `draft` | `active` | Ops publishes | Prior `active` (if any) transitions to `superseded`; `effective_at` stamped | Atomic swap |
| `active` | `superseded` | New version published | `superseded_at` stamped; `superseded_by_contract_id` set | Pending operations under prior contract resolve under prior contract |
| `superseded` | `retired` | After 90 days | All operations under this contract have settled or expired | Permanent terminal state |

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Contract change retroactively reclassifies settled operations.** Resolved: AIOperations record `outcome_contract_id` of the active contract at write time (denormalized via the resolver query plan); resolution always uses the original contract.
2. **`accepted_signal_rule` JSON malformed.** Resolved: write-time JSON-schema validation against `outcome_contract_rule_schema` (versioned schema in Appendix J extension); rejection with `outcome_contract_rule_invalid` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).
3. **No active contract for a customer-billed capability.** Resolved: AIOperation write rejected with HTTP 402 `capability_no_active_outcome_contract` (new; Appendix I); operation does not begin.
4. **A signal arrives during the `signal_evaluation_grace_seconds` window after auto-accept.** Resolved: late `accepted` signals are no-ops if already auto-accepted; late `rejected` signals trigger automatic ContestRecord with reason `auto_filed_late_signal`.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Exactly one OutcomeContract per `capability_id` MUST be in `state=active` at any time; partial unique index enforces.
2. AIOperation resolution MUST use the OutcomeContract version that was active at the AIOperation `created_at`, not the currently active version.
3. `auto_accept_after_seconds` MUST be ≥ 60; lower values rejected with HTTP 422 `outcome_contract_auto_accept_too_short`.
4. Contract publication MUST atomically transition the prior active contract to `superseded` (single transaction); concurrent publication attempts rejected with HTTP 409 `outcome_contract_concurrent_publish`.
5. Default-on-timeout MUST be `rejected` per Pricing Strategy §6 unless `requires_explicit_user_signal=true`; auto-accept produces `auto_accepted` (a distinct settlement_state) for product-quality dashboards.

### 4.8.5 ContestRecord (Per-AIOperation, Customer-Initiated, Ops-Reviewed) {#4.8.5-contestrecord}

**Authoring Intent.** ContestRecord materializes the 14-day customer-initiated dispute window per Summary C.78. Any settled `accepted` or `auto_accepted` AIOperation can be contested by the Org's `billing_admin` within `contest_window_at`; the contest routes to Ops Finance, which approves (and credits) or rejects (and restores). The 14-day default is overridable per capability via OutcomeContract.`contest_window_days`. Contests are also auto-filed by the system when a late outcome signal arrives after auto-accept (`auto_filed_late_signal`) — this is a margin-protection / customer-trust mechanism that catches outcome-resolver bugs without requiring the customer to notice.

**Scope.** Org-scoped; one-to-one with the contested AIOperation (a single AIOperation can be contested at most once; second contest attempts return HTTP 409 `contest_already_filed`).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization; required | Mirrors AIOperation.org_id; denormalized for query performance |
| `ai_operation_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → AIOperation; unique | The contested operation |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer`, `seller`, `system` | Mirrors AIOperation.console for cross-console firewall enforcement on read |
| `filed_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | User with `billing_admin` role; nullable for `system` (auto-filed) | |
| `filed_by_role_snapshot` | Enum | Role at file time | Frozen |
| `reason_code` | Enum | See Appendix J `contest_reason_code`: `accidental_trigger`, `outcome_resolver_bug_suspected`, `model_quality_defect`, `duplicate_operation`, `wrong_capability_invoked`, `auto_filed_late_signal`, `customer_other` | Categorical reason |
| `reason_narrative` | String | 50–4000 chars; required for non-`auto_filed_late_signal` | Customer's explanation |
| `original_settlement_state` | Enum | `accepted`, `auto_accepted` | Snapshot at file time; restored if contest rejected |
| `original_charge_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Snapshot of `effective_charge_cents` at file time |
| `provenance_hash_at_file` | String | 64-char sha256 hex | MUST match AIOperation.`provenance_hash`; mismatch rejects file with HTTP 422 `contest_provenance_hash_mismatch` |
| `status` | Enum | See Appendix J `contest_status`: `open`, `in_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, `withdrawn`, `escalated`, `abandoned` | See state machine |
| `ops_reviewer_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; Ops user with `ops_finance_admin` | Assigned via Ops queue |
| `ops_review_started_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | |
| `ops_decision_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | |
| `ops_decision_note_internal` | String | 0–4000 chars | Ops-private rationale |
| `ops_decision_note_customer_visible` | String | 0–2000 chars | Returned in API and Billing Ledger UI |
| `resolution_reason` | Enum | Nullable; see Appendix J `contest_resolution_reason`: `outcome_resolver_bug`, `model_quality_defect`, `duplicate_operation_confirmed`, `accidental_trigger_acknowledged`, `customer_education_provided_no_credit`, `ops_discretion_credit`, `ops_discretion_no_credit`, `withdrawn_by_customer` | Drives `approved` vs `rejected` interpretation |
