| `credit_amount_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0; nullable | When `status=approved`, the credit returned to wallet (typically equals `original_charge_cents`; partial credits permitted) |
| `credit_posted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | |
| `escalation_target` | Enum | Nullable; `ops_finance_lead`, `cfo`, `legal` | When status=escalated |
| `sla_breach_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when `ops_review_started_at` not set within SLA (default 5 business days from `created_at`); pages Ops Finance |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User OR system | |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User OR Ops | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Always NULL | Financial record |

**Indexes.** `(ai_operation_id)` unique, `(org_id, created_at DESC)` for customer Billing Ledger Contest tab, `(status, sla_breach_at)` partial for Ops queue, `(ops_reviewer_user_id, status)` partial.

**Scope Isolation.** Customer reads scoped per console (mirrors AIOperation); `billing_admin` and `org_admin` see all of their Org's contests. Ops sees all. Cross-Org reads return HTTP 404 `contest_cross_org_access`.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `open` | Customer files OR system auto-files | AIOperation.`settlement_state ∈ {accepted, auto_accepted}` AND `now ≤ AIOperation.contest_window_at` AND no prior ContestRecord | AIOperation transitions to `contested`; soft credit to wallet |
| `open` | `in_review` | Ops picks up from queue | `ops_reviewer_user_id` set; `ops_review_started_at` stamped | |
| `in_review` | `approved` | Ops approves credit | `resolution_reason ∈ {outcome_resolver_bug, model_quality_defect, duplicate_operation_confirmed, accidental_trigger_acknowledged, ops_discretion_credit}`; `credit_amount_cents` set | AIOperation transitions to `reversed`; final credit posted |
| `in_review` | `rejected` | Ops rejects credit | `resolution_reason ∈ {customer_education_provided_no_credit, ops_discretion_no_credit}` | AIOperation restores to `original_settlement_state`; soft credit reversed |
| `in_review` | `escalated` | Ops escalates | `escalation_target` set | Ops Finance lead picks up |
| `escalated` | `approved` / `rejected` | Escalation owner decides | | |
| `open` | `withdrawn` | Customer withdraws | Customer initiated | AIOperation restores to `original_settlement_state`; soft credit reversed |
| `open` | `abandoned` | 90-day Ops-side non-pickup sweep | Contest filed and unclaimed by any Ops reviewer for 90 days AND SLA-breach paging exhausted AND customer has made no inquiry within the 30-day re-notification window | Terminal state for stale Ops queue hygiene. AIOperation soft credit is auto-converted to a permanent credit at abandonment (customer-favorable disposition per Pricing Strategy §11 dispute bias) and `credit_posted_at` is stamped. `resolution_reason` forced to `ops_discretion_credit`. Emits `billing.contest.abandoned` webhook (§31.8.12 / Appendix C) and an Ops Finance audit record. No customer-visible change beyond credit-posted notification. |
| `in_review` | `abandoned` | 120-day Ops-side non-decision sweep | `ops_review_started_at` set but no `ops_decision_at` within 120 days AND escalation was not invoked AND assigned reviewer has been unresponsive through two escalation cycles | Terminal state protecting customer against indefinite Ops hang. Same auto-credit disposition as `open → abandoned`. |

**SLA.** Default 5 business days from `created_at` to `ops_review_started_at`; breach pages Ops Finance with `billing.contest.sla_breach` webhook (§31.8.12 / Appendix C). Default 10 business days to `ops_decision_at`; breach escalates to `ops_finance_lead`.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Contest filed past window.** Resolved: write-time check; HTTP 410 `ai_operation_contest_window_expired`.
2. **AIOperation already in `contested` state.** Resolved: HTTP 409 `contest_already_filed`.
3. **Customer files contest, then deletes wallet (Org closure).** Resolved: contest preserved as financial record; on approval, credit posts to a Stripe credit note (not the closed wallet); customer-visible note explains.
4. **Provenance hash mismatch (e.g., AIOperation re-derived after contest filed).** Resolved: write-time check; HTTP 422 `contest_provenance_hash_mismatch`.
5. **Auto-filed contest from late signal arrives during DSAR redaction.** Resolved: auto-file rejected with `contest_locked_for_dsar` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 423); Ops alerted to handle out-of-band.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. A ContestRecord MUST be filed only against an AIOperation with `settlement_state ∈ {accepted, auto_accepted}` AND `now ≤ contest_window_at`.
2. Filing MUST atomically transition the AIOperation to `contested` and place a soft credit on the wallet.
3. Approval MUST atomically transition the AIOperation to `reversed`, post the final credit, and stamp `credit_posted_at`.
4. Rejection MUST atomically restore the AIOperation to `original_settlement_state` and reverse the soft credit.
5. Auto-filed contests MUST set `filed_by_user_id=null`, `reason_code=auto_filed_late_signal`, and notify Ops Finance within 5 minutes.
6. SLA breaches MUST emit `billing.contest.sla_breach` webhook within 10 minutes of breach.

### 4.8.6 CostBaseRecalculationLog (Platform-Scoped, Nightly Audit Record) {#4.8.6-costbaserecalculationlog}

**Authoring Intent.** CostBaseRecalculationLog is the per-run audit record of the nightly job that re-derives `cost_base_cents` for every active capability from actual Anthropic billing, Convex compute attribution, and external-provider billing. Per Summary C.77 the job runs nightly; drift > 10% triggers a Finance alert; the margin floor is enforced at price-update time with explicit override audit. Per Pricing Strategy §11 the cost_base re-derivation is the mechanism that holds the customer-visible value-dollar pricing constant across underlying Anthropic price moves. The log is the authoritative trail that every cost_base value an AIOperation locks against was approved (auto or manual) at a known time with a known approver.

**Scope.** Platform-scoped; one row per recalc run per `(capability_id, model_tier)` pair. Reads gated to `ops_finance_admin`. Public Pricing API publishes a digest derived from this log (effective_at, capability_id, value_price_cents, cost_price_cents) — never the raw cost_base.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `run_batch_id` | UUID | Required | Groups all rows produced by a single nightly run |
| `capability_id` | String | FK → CapabilityRegistryEntry.`capability_id` | |
| `model_tier` | Enum | See Appendix J `ai_operation_model_tier` | |
| `prior_cost_base_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Cost basis prior to this recalc |
| `new_cost_base_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Newly computed cost basis |
| `prior_value_price_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Snapshot for diff |
| `new_value_price_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Newly published value price |
| `prior_cost_price_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | |
| `new_cost_price_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0 | |
| `drift_percent` | Decimal(8,4) | Signed | `(new - prior) / max(prior, 1) × 100`; can be negative if prices fell |
| `drift_severity` | Enum | See Appendix J `cost_base_recalc_drift_severity`: `normal` (`|drift| ≤ 5%`), `warning_5_10` (`5 < |drift| ≤ 10`), `alert_10_25` (`10 < |drift| ≤ 25`), `critical_gt_25` (`|drift| > 25`) | Drives notification routing |
| `approval_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `cost_base_recalc_approval_status`: `auto_applied`, `pending_finance_approval`, `approved`, `overridden`, `rolled_back` | See state machine |
| `auto_applied_reason` | String | ≤ 500 chars; required when `approval_status=auto_applied` | E.g., "drift within 5% threshold; auto-applied per policy" |
| `approver_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; Ops with `ops_finance_admin` | Required when `drift_severity ∈ {alert_10_25, critical_gt_25}` |
| `approver_decision_note` | String | 0–4000 chars | Required when `approval_status=overridden` |
| `effective_at` | Timestamp | UTC | When this cost_base became effective for new AIOperations |
| `rolled_back_at` | Timestamp | Nullable; UTC | Set if a subsequent run rolled back this row |
| `rollback_reason` | String | 0–4000 chars; nullable | |
| `inputs_summary_json` | JSON | ≤ 16000 chars | Snapshot of inputs used (Anthropic billing line items, Convex compute aggregates, external provider billings, sample size) |
| `model_id_at_recalc` | String | ≤ 120 chars | Anthropic model id observed during the sample period |
| `sample_size_operations` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Number of AIOperations contributing to the sample (per capability + tier) |
| `sample_window_started_at` | Timestamp | UTC | |
| `sample_window_ended_at` | Timestamp | UTC | |
| `margin_at_value_price_pct` | Decimal(6,3) | Computed | Margin floor check: must remain ≥ 88% per Pricing Strategy §2.6 |
| `margin_floor_breach` | Boolean | Default false | True if `margin_at_value_price_pct < 88` even at the new price; routes to Ops Finance for explicit override or capability deprecation |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | System (cron) OR Ops (manual recalc trigger) | |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Ops on approval | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Always NULL | |

**Indexes.** `(capability_id, model_tier, effective_at DESC)` for the AIOperation cost-base lookup, `(run_batch_id)` for run-level queries, `(approval_status, drift_severity)` partial for the Ops queue, `(margin_floor_breach)` partial where true.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `auto_applied` | Recalc run with `drift_severity ∈ {normal, warning_5_10}` AND `margin_floor_breach=false` | Auto-applied; capability rate card published in next minute | |
| (init) | `pending_finance_approval` | Recalc run with `drift_severity ∈ {alert_10_25, critical_gt_25}` OR `margin_floor_breach=true` | Approver assigned via Ops queue; AIOperations continue at prior price until approval | |
| `pending_finance_approval` | `approved` | Ops Finance approves | New price effective at approval timestamp | |
| `pending_finance_approval` | `overridden` | Ops Finance overrides (e.g., deprecates capability instead of accepting margin breach) | `approver_decision_note` required (≥ 50 chars) | |
| `auto_applied` / `approved` | `rolled_back` | Subsequent recalc detects the prior recalc was wrong (e.g., Anthropic billing data revised) | `rollback_reason` required | |

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Anthropic billing data delayed (sample window has insufficient data).** Resolved: recalc skips capabilities with `sample_size_operations < 10` for the window; logs `insufficient_sample` warning; prior cost_base remains.
2. **Margin floor breach on a critical capability.** Resolved: requires Ops Finance override OR capability deprecation; never silently accepted.
3. **Two recalc runs fire concurrently (cron + manual).** Resolved: optimistic lock on `(run_batch_id)` uniqueness; second run rejected with HTTP 409.
4. **Drift calculation on a brand-new capability with `prior_cost_base_cents=0`.** Resolved: `prior_cost_base_cents=0` produces `drift_percent=NULL` (sentinel); routed to `pending_finance_approval` regardless.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. The recalc job MUST run nightly at 03:00 UTC with idempotent retry on failure; missed run alerts Ops within 1 hour. Phase 7 V7 D-CONS-004 remediation (2026-05-07): 03:00 UTC supersedes the prior §34.3.3 row reading of 02:30 UTC; the §34.3.3 row is reconciled to cite §4.8.6 AC #1 as authoritative.
2. `drift_severity ∈ {alert_10_25, critical_gt_25}` MUST require explicit `ops_finance_admin` approval before publication. **Phase 7 V7 D-CONS-001 remediation (2026-05-07).** This AC is the canonical publish-gating rule; the §34.3.3 row "Per-capability drift threshold (auto-publish block) ≥ 25% OR margin-floor breach" is **retired** and reconciled to cite this AC's enum membership ("`drift_severity ∈ {alert_10_25, critical_gt_25}` blocks auto-publish; ≥10% drift requires Finance approval"). Deploy-time validator `cost_base_publish_gate_threshold_single_source` (Appendix M.5) asserts no inline 25% threshold remains in §34 / §4.8.x bodies.
3. A `margin_floor_breach=true` row MUST NEVER auto-apply; it MUST require explicit override or deprecation.
4. AIOperation writes MUST lock against the most recent `approved` or `auto_applied` log row for `(capability_id, model_tier)` at the time of the AIOperation `created_at`.
5. The Public Pricing API publish MUST occur within 60 seconds of any new approved/auto-applied row; QA test `cost_base_recalc_publish_latency` asserts.
6. **Phase 7 V7 D-V7-001 / D-CONS-001 composite remediation — Notice-window margin-trajectory gate.** A recalc that produces a customer-visible price increase MUST compute the projected blended-margin trajectory over the 30-day breaking-change notice window per §34.3.3.A. A trajectory breach (any day with projected blended margin < 88%) MUST hold the recalc in `pending_finance_approval` until Ops Finance commits to one of the §34.3.3.A paths (margin absorption / customer-comm price pull / capability deprecation). Deploy-time validator `cost_base_recalc_notice_window_trajectory_gate` (Appendix M.5) asserts every `auto_applied` or `approved` row carries either ≥ 88% trajectory metadata OR a paired `margin_absorption_decision` / `customer_comm_pull_published_price` / capability `deprecated` audit row.
7. **Phase 7 V7 D-CONS-005 remediation — Sample window canonicality.** The recalc job's sample window MUST be the prior 30-day rolling window (NOT 24h) of Anthropic invoice events + Convex compute allocation per `posthog_event_name`. The §34.3.3 row reconciliation is canonical. Deploy-time validator `cost_base_recalc_sample_window_30d` asserts.

**Retention.** Life of platform (audit). DSAR: not applicable.

### 4.8.7 FreeAllowanceCounter (Org-Scoped, Per-Capability) {#4.8.7-freeallowancecounter}

**Authoring Intent.** FreeAllowanceCounter implements Summary C.80: every customer-billed capability grants 10 free operations on signup as a PLG lever. The counter is per-Org per-capability with a default lifetime quota (no period reset) overridable by Ops or by capability-level settings (`free_allowance_resets_per_period=true` for capabilities where Ops has configured a per-period replenishment). Exhaustion surfaces an inline upgrade CTA with the ROI of the operations already run.

**Scope.** Org-scoped; one row per `(org_id, capability_id)` pair. Reads scoped to Org members per console rules; writes are atomic decrement-and-return via the AI invocation handler.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | |
| `capability_id` | String | FK → CapabilityRegistryEntry.`capability_id` | |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer`, `seller`, `cross_console` | When `cross_console`, the counter applies regardless of which console invokes (e.g., KB Suggestion); console-specific counters allow per-console PLG levers |
| `quota_total` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Total allowance; default 10 (Summary C.80); Ops-overridable |
| `quota_consumed` | Integer | ≥ 0; ≤ quota_total | Used count |
| `quota_remaining` | Integer | Computed (`quota_total - quota_consumed`) | Denormalized for read-path; reconciled at write |
| `resets_per_period` | Boolean | Default false | Mirrors CapabilityRegistryEntry.`free_allowance_resets_per_period` |
| `current_period_started_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | When `resets_per_period=true` |
| `current_period_ends_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | |
| `last_consumed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Last decrement |
| `last_consumed_ai_operation_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → AIOperation | |
| `exhaustion_cta_surfaced_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Stamped on first exhaustion event for ROI-on-exhaustion UI |
| `roi_value_dollars_at_exhaustion` | Integer | Nullable | Sum of `value_price_cents` of the consumed operations at exhaustion (the "ROI of free ops") |
| `status` | Enum | See Appendix J `free_allowance_counter_status`: `active`, `exhausted`, `reset` | |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | System (on first invocation of the capability by the Org) | |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | System OR Ops | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete on Org closure |

**Indexes.** `(org_id, capability_id)` unique, `(status, current_period_ends_at)` partial for period-reset sweep.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Race between two concurrent operations consuming the last free unit.** Resolved: atomic decrement (`UPDATE ... WHERE quota_remaining > 0 RETURNING quota_remaining`); loser's invocation transitions to wallet-billed without retry overhead.
2. **Ops increases `quota_total` mid-flight.** Resolved: increase takes effect immediately for future operations; in-flight operations unaffected.
3. **Counter for a deprecated capability.** Resolved: counter remains; if the capability is still invokable within deprecation grace, decrement continues.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. The first invocation of a customer-billed capability by an Org MUST atomically create a FreeAllowanceCounter row with `quota_total = CapabilityRegistryEntry.free_allowance_quantity_default`.
2. Decrement MUST be atomic and consistent: no two operations may simultaneously consume the last unit.
3. Exhaustion MUST stamp `exhaustion_cta_surfaced_at` and `roi_value_dollars_at_exhaustion` on first exhaustion only; subsequent attempts skip directly to wallet-bill flow.
4. AIOperation rows consumed against this counter MUST set `billed_against_free_allowance=true` and `effective_charge_cents=0`.

**Retention.** Org-life; hard-purge on Org hard-delete. DSAR: not applicable (only `org_id` + capability FK).

### 4.8.8 CommittedSpendContract (Org-Scoped, Enterprise) {#4.8.8-committedspendcontract}

**Authoring Intent.** CommittedSpendContract represents an Enterprise customer's annual AI value-dollar commit per Summary C.81 and Pricing Strategy §6 with discount bands authored canonically in §34.2.4 (single source — never restated inline per the `volume_discount_band_single_source` validator). The commit replaces the static Enterprise tier's token budget (v6.0.0 §34 model) with a per-Org pre-paid commit pool that AIOperations preferentially burn down before drawing the AIWallet's standard `budget_value_dollars`.

**Scope.** Org-scoped; many active contracts permitted in theory but typically one (overlapping commits handled below).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | |
| `contract_external_ref` | String | ≤ 200 chars | DocuSign / Salesforce / CRM external reference; preserved for audit |
| `commit_value_dollars` | Integer | ≥ 1200000 (per Pricing Strategy §6: $12K/yr floor) | In USD cents, integer |
| `discount_band` | Enum | See Appendix J `committed_spend_discount_band`: `none`, `band_25k_10pct`, `band_50k_15pct`, `band_100k_20pct`, `band_250k_25pct` | Derived from `commit_value_dollars` at signature; locked |
| `effective_discount_pct` | Integer | 0–25 | Mirrors `discount_band` for query convenience |
| `commit_period_start` | Timestamp | UTC | Annual contract start |
| `commit_period_end` | Timestamp | UTC | Annual contract end |
| `commit_burn_remaining_value_dollars` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Live burn-down |
| `shortfall_policy` | Enum | See Appendix J `committed_spend_shortfall_policy`: `forfeit`, `partial_credit_next_year`, `rollover_capped` | Sales-negotiated; default `forfeit` |
| `shortfall_rollover_max_pct` | Integer | 0–25 | When `shortfall_policy=rollover_capped`, max % of commit that may roll forward |
| `auto_renew` | Boolean | Default false | When true, contract auto-renews 30 days before expiry at the same band |
| `auto_renew_notice_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When the auto-renewal notice was issued |
| `status` | Enum | See Appendix J `committed_spend_status`: `pending_signature`, `active`, `expired`, `terminated`, `auto_renewed` | See state machine |
| `signed_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; user from customer side | |
| `signed_by_sourcera_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; Sourcera Sales Ops user | |
| `linked_wallet_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → AIWallet | The wallet this commit funds |
| `linked_legal_entity` | Enum | mirrors AIWallet | |
| `linked_billing_currency` | Enum | mirrors AIWallet | |
| `terminated_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | |
| `terminated_reason` | Enum | Nullable; `customer_request`, `sourcera_breach`, `customer_breach`, `acquisition`, `bankruptcy` | |
| `posthog_event_published_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Stamps `commit.signed` event publish |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Sales Ops user | |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Sales Ops or System (auto-renew) | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Always NULL | Financial record |

**Indexes.** `(org_id, status, commit_period_end DESC)`, `(linked_wallet_id, status)` partial where `status=active`, `(commit_period_end, auto_renew)` partial for the auto-renew sweep.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `pending_signature` | Sales Ops drafts | DocuSign envelope sent | |
| `pending_signature` | `active` | Both parties sign | Wallet linked; commit pool funded | AIOperations begin burn-down |
| `active` | `expired` | `commit_period_end < now` AND no auto-renew | `shortfall_policy` applied (forfeit / partial credit / rollover) | |
| `active` | `auto_renewed` | `auto_renew=true` AND 30 days before `commit_period_end` | New CommittedSpendContract row created with new period; this row transitions to `expired` on period end | |
| `active` | `terminated` | Contract terminated mid-period | `terminated_at` stamped; remaining commit handled per termination clause (typically forfeit) | |

**Overlapping Commits.** When two commits are simultaneously `active` for the same Org (rare, e.g., an early-renewal scenario), AIOperations burn down the commit with the **earlier `commit_period_end`** first; this prevents stranded balances on the expiring contract.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Customer terminates mid-period with unspent commit.** Resolved: `shortfall_policy=forfeit` is default; alternative policies require Sales Ops explicit configuration at signature.
2. **Auto-renewal with FX move.** Resolved: auto-renewal preserves the prior `linked_billing_currency`; FX is locked at the time AIOperations charge against the new commit, not at renewal.
3. **Two commits both active and AIOperation burns from one — race against contract overlap window.** Resolved: deterministic burn-priority (earlier `commit_period_end` first); single-row update with optimistic lock.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. `commit_value_dollars` MUST be ≥ $12,000 (1,200,000 cents) — per Pricing Strategy §6 Enterprise floor.
2. `discount_band` MUST be derived deterministically from `commit_value_dollars` at signature; manual override rejected with HTTP 422 `committed_spend_discount_band_mismatch` (new; Appendix I).
3. AIOperations from Orgs with an active commit MUST burn down the commit pool before drawing the wallet's `budget_value_dollars`.
4. Overlapping active commits MUST burn earlier-ending first; QA test `committed_spend_overlap_burn_priority` asserts.
5. Auto-renewal MUST issue a customer notification 30 days before `commit_period_end`; opt-out window is 7 days before renewal.

**Retention.** Org-life + 7 years (financial-audit). DSAR: `signed_by_user_id`, `account_executive_user_id` pseudonymized; contract rows retained per §6.8.5.

### 4.8.9 PricingTableVersion (Platform-Scoped, Public-API-Backing) {#4.8.9-pricingtableversion}

**Authoring Intent.** PricingTableVersion is the publish-time snapshot that backs the Public Pricing API at `api.sourcera.com/v1/pricing` per Summary C.83. Each new active CapabilityRegistryEntry change, each approved CostBaseRecalculationLog, and each plan-tier price change produces a new PricingTableVersion. The version is immutable once published; customers can pin a version for forecasting reproducibility.

**Scope.** Platform-scoped. Publicly readable (no auth) for `status=published` rows; Ops-only for drafts.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `version_label` | String | semver-like, e.g., `2026.04.15.001` | Human-readable; chronological |
| `status` | Enum | See Appendix J `pricing_table_version_status`: `draft`, `published`, `superseded`, `rolled_back` | |
| `effective_at` | Timestamp | UTC | When this version becomes the canonical Public Pricing API response |
| `superseded_by_version_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable | |
| `published_payload_json` | JSON | ≤ 1,048,576 bytes (1 MB) | Full rate card snapshot: capabilities, value_price_cents, cost_price_cents, currencies, plan tiers, free allowances, retry curves, deprecation banners |
| `published_payload_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex | For client-side change detection |
| `included_currencies` | Array[Enum] | mirrors `billing_currency` | Currencies for which conversions are precomputed |
| `included_capability_count` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Denormalized for monitoring |
| `triggering_change_summary` | String | 0–4000 chars | Free text describing what changed since prior version |
| `triggering_changes_json` | JSON | ≤ 16000 chars | Structured diff: capability_id → field → prior → new |
| `breaking_change_flag` | Boolean | Default false | True when a customer-visible price increase or capability removal occurs; triggers 30-day-advance customer notification per Pricing Strategy §11 |
| `customer_notification_sent_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Required when `breaking_change_flag=true`; sent ≥ 30 days before `effective_at` |
| `published_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | UTC; null while draft |
| `published_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Ops user with `ops_finance_admin` | |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC; only mutable in `draft` |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | System OR Ops | |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Ops | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Always NULL | Financial / audit record |

**Indexes.** `(status, effective_at DESC)`, `(version_label)` unique, `(superseded_by_version_id)` partial.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Publish race with concurrent capability change.** Resolved: publish takes a snapshot at the publish transaction commit time; subsequent changes produce a new version.
2. **Customer pins a `superseded` version then expects current behavior.** Resolved: pinning is a forecasting tool only; AIOperation pricing always uses the current `published` version, not the pinned one.
3. **`breaking_change_flag=true` without 30-day notification.** Resolved: publish rejected with HTTP 422 `pricing_table_breaking_change_requires_30d_notice` (new; Appendix I); Ops must schedule notification first.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. The Public Pricing API MUST return the `published_payload_json` of the row with the most recent `effective_at` ≤ `now` and `status=published`.
2. A new published row MUST atomically transition the prior row to `superseded`.
3. `breaking_change_flag=true` MUST require `customer_notification_sent_at ≥ effective_at - 30 days`.
4. The endpoint MUST be cacheable for 60 seconds with the `published_payload_hash` as the ETag.
5. Cursor-based pagination MUST follow §32 patterns; default 50, max 250 (rate cards may grow large).

**Retention.** Life of platform (immutable public-API artifacts; customers may pin for forecasting). DSAR: not applicable.

### 4.8.10 DowngradeExcessDataBucket (Org-Scoped, 90-Day Read-Only Preservation) {#4.8.10-downgradeexcessdatabucket}

**Authoring Intent.** Per Summary C.85 and Pricing Strategy §9 / Seller §17.4, plan downgrades preserve excess data in **read-only mode for 90 days** before archival; customers may upgrade back and restore active access without data loss. DowngradeExcessDataBucket is the per-Org-per-data-class record of what was preserved when the downgrade occurred. It is the single source of truth for "what would I lose if I let the 90-day clock run out" and powers the customer-visible preservation banner.

**Scope.** Org-scoped; one row per `(org_id, data_class)` pair per downgrade event. Cross-console: a downgrade on the seller plan creates seller-data buckets; a downgrade on the buyer plan creates buyer-data buckets; an Org with both plans downgrading independently has independent buckets.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer`, `seller` | Which console the downgrade affects |
| `data_class` | Enum | See Appendix J `downgrade_excess_data_class`: `workspaces`, `requirements_over_cap`, `kb_entries_over_cap`, `vendors_over_cap`, `capability_declarations_over_cap`, `seller_software_over_cap`, `firecrawl_sources_over_cap`, `concurrent_bids_over_cap`, `seller_signals_over_cap`, `evaluations_over_cap` | What's preserved |
| `entity_ids_preserved` | Array[UUID] | ≤ 100,000 elements | The specific entity ids made read-only |
| `entity_count_preserved` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Denormalized for UI |
| `prior_plan_tier` | Enum | See Appendix J Plan Tiers | Plan held before downgrade |
| `new_plan_tier` | Enum | See Appendix J Plan Tiers | Plan after downgrade |
| `downgrade_at` | Timestamp | UTC | When downgrade took effect |
| `preservation_until` | Timestamp | UTC | `downgrade_at + 90 days` (Summary C.85) |
| `status` | Enum | See Appendix J `downgrade_excess_bucket_status`: `active_preservation`, `notice_sent_d60`, `notice_sent_d80`, `archive_pending`, `archived`, `restored` | |
| `notice_d60_sent_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | 30-day-prior notice |
| `notice_d80_sent_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | 10-day-prior notice |
| `archived_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When entities were hard-archived |
| `archive_storage_ref` | String | ≤ 500 chars; nullable | Cold-storage pointer (S3 Glacier or equivalent); 7-year retention for legal |
| `restored_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When customer upgraded back and restored access |
| `restored_by_plan_tier` | Enum | Nullable | Which plan tier they upgraded to |
| `restoration_partial` | Boolean | Default false | True when only a subset of entities fit under the restored plan |
| `restoration_partial_kept_ids` | Array[UUID] | Nullable | Subset restored to active; remainder remain in bucket |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | System (downgrade handler) | |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | System OR Ops | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Always NULL | Audit record |

**Indexes.** `(org_id, status)`, `(preservation_until)` partial where `status IN (active_preservation, notice_sent_d60, notice_sent_d80)` for the daily sweep, `(console, data_class)` for reporting.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `active_preservation` | Downgrade handler runs | Entities transitioned to read-only; `preservation_until` stamped | Customer-visible banner |
| `active_preservation` | `notice_sent_d60` | 60 days post-downgrade (30 days remaining) | Email + in-app notification | |
| `notice_sent_d60` | `notice_sent_d80` | 80 days post-downgrade (10 days remaining) | Email + in-app | |
| `notice_sent_d80` | `archive_pending` | `preservation_until` reached | Hard-archive cron picks up next run | |
| `archive_pending` | `archived` | Cron archives entities to cold storage | `archive_storage_ref` set; entities hard-deleted from hot storage; metadata preserved | |
| `active_preservation` / `notice_sent_*` / `archive_pending` | `restored` | Customer upgrades back AND restoration eligible | Entities restored to active; `restored_at` stamped; partial restoration marked when applicable | |
| `archived` | `restored` | Customer upgrades AND requests restore-from-cold within 90 days post-archive | Cold-storage rehydration; SLA: 24 hours; Ops-assisted | Beyond 180 days post-archive: data is permanently lost (legal-retention only) |

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Customer upgrades to a tier insufficient to re-cover all preserved entities.** Resolved: `restoration_partial=true`; remaining entities stay in bucket; UI surfaces upgrade-to-cover-all CTA.
2. **Hard-archive cron crashes mid-archive.** Resolved: idempotent archiving via `archive_storage_ref` checkpoint; restart resumes at the next unarchived entity.
3. **DSAR right-to-erasure for an Org with `archived` data.** Resolved: DSAR handler purges cold-storage rows in addition to hot-storage; legal-retention exception preserved per `data_retention_tier=extended_financial` if applicable.
4. **Org deleted during preservation.** Resolved: bucket transitions to `archived` immediately on Org deletion; no preservation hold survives Org deletion.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Plan downgrade MUST transition affected entities to read-only within 5 minutes of downgrade; QA test `downgrade_readonly_latency` asserts.
2. The 60-day and 80-day notices MUST be one-shot per bucket; idempotency stamps prevent duplicates.
3. Hard-archive MUST occur exactly at `preservation_until` (± 1 hour) via daily sweep; missed sweep alerts Ops.
4. Restoration on upgrade MUST be atomic: either all eligible entities restore or none; partial restoration is a separate flow with explicit user confirmation.
5. Archive cold-storage MUST retain entities for 7 years (legal); restoration window is 90 days post-archive.

### 4.8.11 BillingSeatSnapshot (Org-Scoped, Reporting-Only, Periodic) {#4.8.11-billingseatsnapshot}

**Authoring Intent.** Per Summary C.86, Sourcera does NOT charge per seat — but the billing layer counts active seats for reporting and plan-gate enforcement (`max_members` in §4.2.1). BillingSeatSnapshot is the periodic point-in-time count of active seats per Org per console for analytics, plan-gate enforcement, and Stripe invoice line-item context (informational only — no per-seat charge). Guests and API-only identities are excluded.

**Scope.** Org-scoped; rows are immutable snapshots (one per `(org_id, console, taken_at)` tuple). Many snapshots over time; older snapshots downsampled per retention rules.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer`, `seller`, `both` | `both` for combined snapshots; per-console for plan-gate evaluations |
| `taken_at` | Timestamp | UTC; immutable | Snapshot moment |
| `trigger` | Enum | See Appendix J `billing_seat_snapshot_trigger`: `monthly_cron`, `plan_change`, `manual_audit`, `stripe_invoice_generation`, `dsar_request`, `ops_capacity_review` | Why the snapshot was taken |
| `active_seats_count` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Excludes guests, API-only identities, deleted users |
| `guest_count` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Reported separately; not billable but visible for context |
| `api_only_count` | Integer | ≥ 0 | API-only identities (token-only users); also non-billable |
| `deleted_count_30d` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Members deleted in the trailing 30 days; preserved for audit |
| `seat_breakdown_by_role_json` | JSON | ≤ 8000 chars | Per-role breakdown (e.g., `{"org_owner":1,"org_admin":3,"member":47,"guest":12}`) |
| `seat_breakdown_by_team_json` | JSON | ≤ 16000 chars | Per-team rollup for the console |
| `plan_max_members_at_snapshot` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Snapshot of `Organization.max_members` at the moment |
| `plan_gate_breach_flag` | Boolean | Default false | True when `active_seats_count > plan_max_members_at_snapshot` (a soft-gate condition that surfaces an upgrade prompt) |
| `linked_stripe_invoice_id` | String | Nullable; ≤ 200 chars | Set when `trigger=stripe_invoice_generation` |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC; equal to `taken_at` |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | System OR Ops | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Always NULL | Reporting record |

**Indexes.** `(org_id, console, taken_at DESC)` for the time-series read, `(plan_gate_breach_flag, taken_at)` partial where true for the breach-cohort dashboard, `(trigger, taken_at)` for trigger-correlated reporting.

**Retention.** Daily snapshots retained for 90 days; weekly downsamples retained for 1 year; monthly downsamples retained for 7 years. Snapshots tied to a specific `linked_stripe_invoice_id` retained as long as the invoice (7 years for SOC-2).

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Snapshot taken during a bulk-import (1,000 users in 60 seconds).** Resolved: snapshot uses the database snapshot-isolation level; a long bulk-import is captured at the snapshot moment, not as a transient mid-state.
2. **Plan downgrade between snapshot and Stripe invoice.** Resolved: `plan_max_members_at_snapshot` is the snapshot-time value; subsequent downgrade does not retroactively rewrite the snapshot.
3. **Snapshot for an Org with no `seller` console plan.** Resolved: per-console snapshots only when the Org has the corresponding plan active; `console=both` snapshots always taken.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Monthly snapshots MUST run on the 1st of each month at 02:00 UTC for every active Org.
2. Plan-change events MUST trigger an immediate snapshot within 60 seconds.
3. `active_seats_count` MUST exclude guests, API-only identities, and members with `deleted_at IS NOT NULL`.
4. `plan_gate_breach_flag` MUST be informational only — Sourcera does not block invoicing when seat counts exceed the soft cap; the breach surfaces as an upgrade prompt to `org_owner` and `billing_admin`.
5. Snapshots MUST be immutable post-creation; any update attempt rejected with HTTP 422 `billing_seat_snapshot_immutable` (new; Appendix I).
6. The Public Pricing API MUST NOT expose per-seat pricing; QA test `pricing_api_no_per_seat_pricing` asserts.

### 4.8.12 MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord (Seller-Org-Scoped, Accounting-Isolated, Non-AI Revenue Line) {#4.8.12-marketplacediscoveryrevenuerecord}

**Authoring Intent.** Per Summary §2.10 / Summary §6.16.6 / C.131 and Seller Pricing §12, Sourcera sells a narrow set of non-AI, traditional-media marketplace SKUs (promoted listings; verification-tier reserve; featured-placement reserve) that MUST be accounted for separately from both the AI Wallet ledger (`rev_ai_wallet`, ≈ 4.5% gross margin per Summary §6.16.6) and subscription revenue (`rev_subscription`, ≈ 85–90% gross margin). MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord is the authoritative line-item record for this third revenue class, which Summary §6.16.6 targets at ≈ 95%+ gross margin and requires to surface independently in every finance dashboard. The record does NOT debit AIWallet, does NOT participate in outcome resolution, and does NOT appear in the AIOperation ledger. Its existence protects Sourcera's margin-reporting integrity: mixing media revenue into AI-wallet cost-of-goods would silently inflate the AI-wallet margin and hide the operational reality that AI is thin-margin and discovery is fat-margin. See Appendix K Glossary and Appendix J `marketplace_discovery_cost_center` for the canonical single cost-center value.

**Scope.** Org-scoped (the seller Org). Accounting-isolated: `cost_center` MUST equal `rev_marketplace_discovery`; any other value rejected at write. Seller-only: the source Org MUST have an active seller-console plan at purchase time. Residency-partitioned via `legal_entity` for invoicing; residency is derived from Organization `data_residency` at invoice finalization time per §6.8 / C.84. Append-only for post-invoice states; pre-invoice void permitted only by Ops Finance.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `seller_org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization; required; Org MUST have active seller console plan at purchase | Non-seller Org writes rejected with HTTP 403 `marketplace_discovery_non_seller_org` |
| `sku` | Enum | `promoted_listing`, `verification_upgrade`, `featured_placement` | See Appendix J `marketplace_discovery_sku`. `verification_upgrade` and `featured_placement` are reserved per Summary C.131 but currently earned-free / editorial-only per Seller Pricing §12 — enum retained so future priced tiers do not require schema change |
| `sku_variant` | String | ≤ 100 chars; nullable | Category slug for `promoted_listing` (e.g., `hris`, `edr`); tier identifier for `verification_upgrade`; placement slot for `featured_placement`. Required when `sku=promoted_listing` |
| `source_entity_type` | Enum | See Appendix J `marketplace_discovery_source_entity_type`: `promoted_listing`, `verification_review_record`, `featured_placement`; required | Source entity class that generated the line item. MUST match `sku`: `promoted_listing` → `promoted_listing`; `verification_upgrade` → `verification_review_record`; `featured_placement` → `featured_placement`. Mismatch rejected with HTTP 422 `marketplace_discovery_source_entity_mismatch`. |
| `source_entity_id` | UUID | Polymorphic FK to the source row indicated by `source_entity_type`; required for every priced row | For `source_entity_type='promoted_listing'`, FK → PromotedListing (§4.4.19). For `featured_placement`, FK → FeaturedPlacement (§4.4.20) only when paid-commitment mode is enabled. For `verification_review_record`, FK → VerificationReviewRecord (§4.4.21) only if a future paid verification SKU activates. Missing source row rejected with HTTP 422 `marketplace_discovery_source_entity_required`. |
| `amount_cents` | Integer | ≥ 0; non-fractional | Integer cents per §4.8 monetary discipline; fractional values rejected with HTTP 422 `marketplace_discovery_amount_cents_fractional` |
| `billing_currency` | Enum | See Appendix J `billing_currency` (existing) | Captured at purchase time; immutable |
| `fx_rate_locked_to_usd` | Numeric(18,8) | ≥ 0 | FX rate snapshot at purchase time per C.84; all downstream USD conversion MUST use this rate, not the live rate |
| `billing_period_start` | Timestamp | UTC; immutable | Sale-window start (for `promoted_listing`, this is the week start) |
| `billing_period_end` | Timestamp | UTC; immutable; MUST be > `billing_period_start` | Sale-window end |
| `cost_center` | Enum | MUST equal `rev_marketplace_discovery`; DB CHECK enforces | See Appendix J `marketplace_discovery_cost_center`; any other value rejected with HTTP 422 `marketplace_discovery_cost_center_mismatch` |
| `legal_entity` | Enum | See Appendix J `legal_entity_kind` (canonical post-D-AJ-004 / D-RES-004 4-value set: `sourcera_us_llc`, `sourcera_eu_gmbh`, `sourcera_apac_pte`, `sourcera_custom`). The v7.1.0 pre-Phase-2V value `sourcera_uk_ltd` is retired at v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 (D-RES-004 closure 2026-05-20); UK-resident sellers route through `sourcera_eu_gmbh` per Glossary "Residency-Locked Invoicing", or through `sourcera_custom` keyed on `custom_sovereign_residency_label` for UK-sovereign-cloud Enterprise contracts. | Derived from seller Org `data_residency` at invoice finalization via the canonical 4-row Residency-Locked Invoicing mapping at §4.8.1; mismatch with Stripe-invoicing entity rejected with HTTP 422 `marketplace_discovery_legal_entity_mismatch` (Appendix I). |
| `invoice_ref` | String | ≤ 200 chars; nullable until invoiced | Stripe invoice ID; populated on state transition to `invoiced` |
| `stripe_charge_id` | String | ≤ 200 chars; nullable until paid | Stripe charge ID; populated on state transition to `paid` |
| `status` | Enum | See Appendix J `marketplace_discovery_revenue_status`: `pending`, `invoiced`, `paid`, `voided`, `refunded` | State machine below |
| `status_reason` | String | ≤ 500 chars; nullable | Free-text or enum-keyed reason (e.g., `k_anonymity_pending`, `legal_hold_void`, `ops_refund`) |
| `k_anonymity_cohort_size_at_sale` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Required for `sku=promoted_listing`; cohort size in the category at sale moment per Summary C.131 |
| `attribution_bucket_id` | UUID | Nullable | Aggregate attribution bucket for k-anonymity-safe reporting (authored extension); per-buyer attribution is NEVER stored on this row |
| `void_reason` | Enum | See Appendix J `marketplace_discovery_void_reason`: `ops_pre_charge_void`, `legal_hold_void`, `fraud_review_void`, `k_anonymity_timeout`, `plan_downgrade_void`, `customer_request_void`; nullable until voided | Populated on state transition to `voided` |
| `settled_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable until `paid` or `voided` | |
| `refund_parent_id` | UUID (FK) | Self-referencing; nullable | Populated on companion negative row created by a refund; original row retained unchanged |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC; permitted state transitions only |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Seller billing admin OR Ops | Never a buyer-side user |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Last mutator | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | ALWAYS NULL | Hard-delete forbidden for 7-year SOC-2 retention; attempts rejected with HTTP 422 `marketplace_discovery_hard_delete_forbidden` |

**Scope Isolation.**

- **Org-scope:** strict; the row is owned by `seller_org_id` and is invisible to any other Org.
- **Console-scope:** seller-only; the Dual-Console Firewall ensures buyer-side users and buyer-side queries never return marketplace-discovery rows for their own Org even when the Org is both buyer and seller (the rows are fetched only via seller-console billing endpoints).
- **Marketplace-domain-scope:** the row is marketplace-global (it records a sale made into the shared marketplace); no marketplace-domain partitioning applies at the row level.
- **Residency-scope:** `legal_entity` residency-locks the invoice per the canonical post-D-RES-004 4-row mapping at §4.8.1 Residency-Locked Invoicing: US-residency sellers invoiced under `sourcera_us_llc`; EU-residency sellers (including the legacy UK cohort and any post-Phase-2V UK assignment) under `sourcera_eu_gmbh`; APAC-residency sellers under `sourcera_apac_pte`; `custom`-residency Enterprise / sovereign-cloud sellers under `sourcera_custom` (with the Stripe-Customer-metadata sub-classification driven by `custom_sovereign_residency_label`). Mapping per §6.8 / §1.6 / C.84.
- **Source-entity scope:** `source_entity_type` / `source_entity_id` bind the financial row to the originating marketplace object. Reconciliation jobs MUST read the source row inside the seller Org boundary before comparing amounts; cross-Org source references are rejected with HTTP 422 `marketplace_discovery_source_entity_mismatch`.

**Indexes.**

- `(seller_org_id, billing_period_start DESC)` — per-seller time-series.
- `(status, billing_period_end)` — invoicing queue.
- `(sku, billing_period_start)` — SKU-level gross-margin dashboard.
- `(cost_center, billing_period_start)` — finance dashboard partition (all rows share the same cost_center; the index exists to make dashboard queries explicit in partitioning and to fail loudly if a mis-written row ever lands with a different value).
- `(invoice_ref)` PARTIAL WHERE `invoice_ref IS NOT NULL` — invoice lookup.
- `(legal_entity, billing_period_start)` — residency-partitioned finance reporting.
- `(seller_org_id, source_entity_type, source_entity_id, billing_period_start)` partial on `source_entity_id IS NOT NULL` — source-row reconciliation, especially PromotedListing `spend_to_date_cents` nightly zero-tolerance checks.
- `(sku, sku_variant, billing_period_start)` PARTIAL WHERE `sku='promoted_listing'` — category-level cohort reporting.
- `(refund_parent_id)` PARTIAL WHERE `refund_parent_id IS NOT NULL` — refund companion lookup.

**Retention.** 7 years minimum per §40.2 (SOC-2 financial record retention; see also GDPR Art. 30 record-of-processing-activities overlap). `deleted_at` MUST always be NULL. DSAR right-to-erasure (§6.8) redacts PII linkage (`created_by`, `updated_by`) to a tombstone user and nulls any free-text `status_reason` containing subject PII; monetary fields, cost_center, sku, period boundaries, and invoice refs are preserved under SOC-2 legal hold. Refunds create companion negative rows; originals are never mutated.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `pending` | Seller purchases SKU | Plan gate passes (Scale+ for `promoted_listing`); category cap passes; monthly cap passes; k-anonymity cohort recorded; `source_entity_type` / `source_entity_id` resolve inside `seller_org_id` | `amount_cents`, `billing_currency`, `fx_rate_locked_to_usd`, `source_entity_type`, and `source_entity_id` locked at this moment |
| `pending` | `invoiced` | Stripe invoice finalized | `invoice_ref` populated; Stripe `invoice.finalized` webhook received; `legal_entity` derived from residency | Webhook HMAC-SHA256 verified per §31 |
| `invoiced` | `paid` | Stripe charge succeeded | `stripe_charge_id` populated; Stripe `charge.succeeded` webhook received; `settled_at` stamped | Settlement locked |
| `pending` | `voided` | Ops void OR k-anonymity timeout (nightly `marketplace_discovery_k_anon_sweep` job at 02:00 UTC, horizon = `billing_period_start + 30d`) OR plan downgrade mid-period | Pre-invoice; reason in `void_reason` | Does not require Stripe interaction |
| `invoiced` | `voided` | Ops pre-charge void | Stripe invoice voided; `void_reason` populated | Creates no Stripe charge |
| `paid` | `refunded` | Ops-initiated refund OR legal hold requiring reversal post-payment | Stripe refund issued; companion negative row created with `refund_parent_id` set, `status='refunded'`, `amount_cents` = negative of parent, all parent fields copied (`cost_center`, `legal_entity`, `billing_currency`, `fx_rate_locked_to_usd`), `void_reason` populated on companion when origin is legal hold | Original row retained unchanged; companion row is itself immutable post-create (refund-of-refund forbidden); append-only discipline preserved |
| `pending`/`invoiced` | `voided` | Legal hold prior to payment | Requires legal approval; `void_reason=legal_hold_void` | Post-payment legal holds MUST take the `paid → refunded` path above, not this row; the `voided` terminal state is reserved for pre-payment voids to preserve SOC-2 settlement integrity |

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Cost-center drift — a code path writes `cost_center=rev_ai_wallet`.** Resolved: DB-level CHECK constraint `cost_center = 'rev_marketplace_discovery'`; write-side validator rejects with HTTP 422 `marketplace_discovery_cost_center_mismatch`. Finance dashboard partitions by cost_center and surfaces any orphan row in a monitoring alert within 5 minutes.
2. **Promoted listing purchase when seller plan downgrades below Seller Scale mid-period.** Resolved: plan gate evaluated at purchase time per §34.1.2 / §5.11 Feature Access Matrix; already-purchased period-overlapping records remain valid until `billing_period_end`; new Promoted Listing purchases are rejected with HTTP 403 `promoted_listing_plan_tier_below_scale` (Appendix I). No automatic rebate; Ops may void via `plan_downgrade_void` reason on request.
3. **Category cap breach — seller attempts 5th additional promoted listing in a calendar month.** Resolved: per-seller calendar-month counter queried pre-write against `(seller_org_id, sku='promoted_listing', count_in_month)`; rejection with HTTP 409 `marketplace_discovery_monthly_cap_exceeded`. Counter resets at UTC month boundary.
4. **Category-cap breach — >3 concurrent seller slots in one category.** Resolved: per-category concurrent-slot counter queried pre-write; rejection with HTTP 409 `marketplace_discovery_category_cap_exceeded`. Preserves Summary C.131 / Seller Pricing §12 noise-prevention invariant.
5. **K-anonymity cohort below floor of 3 at sale time.** Resolved: `k_anonymity_cohort_size_at_sale` captured; if `< 3`, record is written as `pending` with `status_reason=k_anonymity_pending`; the promoted placement does not render until cohort threshold met; if cohort not met within 30 days, Ops voids with `k_anonymity_timeout` reason and no charge.
6. **Multi-currency invoice — seller in EU buys in USD.** Resolved: `billing_currency` and `fx_rate_locked_to_usd` captured at purchase time; all USD-aggregation in finance dashboards uses the locked rate, not the live rate. Currency drift between purchase and invoice does NOT reopen the amount.
7. **Refund issued after SOC-2 7-year retention window.** Resolved: hard-delete forbidden via `deleted_at` always-NULL constraint; refunds ALWAYS create companion negative rows rather than mutating; retention clock resets on the newer row, not the original.
8. **DSAR right-to-erasure from a seller Org contact.** Resolved: PII in `created_by` / `updated_by` redacted to a tombstone user; monetary fields, cost_center, sku, period boundaries, invoice refs preserved under SOC-2 legal hold per §6.8. Redaction event logged.
9. **Accidental linkage to AIWallet.** Resolved: schema forbids an `ai_wallet_id` FK; QA test `marketplace_discovery_no_ai_wallet_linkage` asserts no such column exists. Row creation does NOT touch AIWallet balance.
10. **Buyer-console user attempts to read marketplace-discovery rows for their own dual-console Org.** Resolved: seller-console billing endpoint only; Dual-Console Firewall (§3.5) rejects with HTTP 403 `dual_console_firewall_buyer_denied` (existing).
11. **Finance dashboard accidentally UNIONs cost centers.** Resolved: QA test `finance_dashboard_cost_center_isolation` asserts no UNION across cost_center partitions; gross-margin queries SELECT with explicit `WHERE cost_center = 'rev_marketplace_discovery'` or the equivalent partitioned equivalent. Dashboard template engine refuses a cross-cost-center UNION at config-load time.
12. **Stripe invoice legal-entity mismatch — seller residency is EU but invoice is drafted under `sourcera_us_llc`.** Resolved: `legal_entity` derived from Org `data_residency` at invoice finalization; write rejected with HTTP 422 `marketplace_discovery_legal_entity_mismatch`. Ops correction requires residency transfer under §6.8 / C.84 protocol.
13. **Seller `data_residency` has no matching `legal_entity` enum value (e.g., a jurisdiction where Sourcera does not operate a local entity).** Resolved: purchase rejected at row-create time with HTTP 403 `marketplace_discovery_unsupported_residency`; the seller is directed to contact Sales-Ops. The four-entity ceiling is a business-policy decision; expansion requires an Appendix J `legal_entity` enum addition plus a Stripe-invoicing entity provisioning runbook. Documents the geographic operating scope rather than silently failing downstream at invoice finalization.
14. **DSAR right-to-erasure arrives while row is in `pending` state (pre-invoice).** Resolved: redaction applies to `created_by`/`updated_by` immediately; the monetary fields remain preserved under SOC-2 legal hold even in `pending` state because the row is a financial artifact from creation, not from invoicing. The `pending → voided` and `pending → invoiced` transitions remain permitted post-redaction; the invoicing job identifies the seller Org via `seller_org_id` (not redacted), so invoicing proceeds under a tombstoned contact on the seller side.
15. **Refund-of-refund attempted via a second companion row referencing an already-refunded parent.** Resolved: write-side validator rejects with HTTP 409 `marketplace_discovery_refund_chain_forbidden` when `refund_parent_id` points to a row whose `status='refunded'` or whose `refund_parent_id IS NOT NULL` (i.e., a companion row). Legitimate re-credit after a refund must be modeled as a new original purchase, not as a chained refund.
16. **PromotedListing revenue row cannot be reconciled to its source listing.** Resolved: every priced `sku='promoted_listing'` row MUST carry `source_entity_type='promoted_listing'` and `source_entity_id = PromotedListing.id`; the source-entity index above drives the nightly zero-tolerance comparison against §4.4.19 `spend_to_date_cents`. Missing or cross-Org source references are rejected before invoice finalization.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Every MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord MUST have `cost_center = 'rev_marketplace_discovery'`; enforced by DB CHECK constraint and write-side validator. Violations rejected with HTTP 422 `marketplace_discovery_cost_center_mismatch`.
2. MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord MUST NOT be aggregated with `rev_ai_wallet` or `rev_subscription` in any finance dashboard. QA test `finance_dashboard_cost_center_isolation` asserts gross-margin queries partition by cost_center and do not UNION across cost centers.
3. Gross margin MUST be reportable per SKU and per cost_center independently; dashboard query plan MUST include `GROUP BY cost_center, sku` on the margin view.
4. `amount_cents` MUST be stored as a non-negative integer; fractional or negative values rejected with HTTP 422 `marketplace_discovery_amount_cents_fractional`.
5. `billing_currency` and `fx_rate_locked_to_usd` MUST be captured at purchase time and immutable thereafter; all downstream USD conversion MUST use `fx_rate_locked_to_usd`, not the live rate, per C.84.
6. `legal_entity` MUST be derived from the seller Org's `data_residency` at invoice finalization and MUST match the Stripe-invoicing entity; mismatch rejected with HTTP 422 `marketplace_discovery_legal_entity_mismatch`.
7. Promoted-listing SKU purchases MUST be gated on Seller Scale or Seller Enterprise per §34.1.2 **Promoted Marketplace Placements**; non-eligible plans reject with HTTP 403 `promoted_listing_plan_tier_below_scale`. The generic `marketplace_discovery_sku_unavailable_on_plan` code is not used for PromotedListing plan-tier eligibility.
8. Promoted-listing per-seller monthly cap MUST be enforced at 4 additional add-ons per calendar month per Seller Pricing §12; breach rejected with HTTP 409 `marketplace_discovery_monthly_cap_exceeded`.
9. Promoted-listing per-category concurrent cap MUST be enforced at 3 slots per category per Summary C.131 / Seller Pricing §12; breach rejected with HTTP 409 `marketplace_discovery_category_cap_exceeded`.
10. K-anonymity cohort floor for promoted listings MUST be 3; purchases with `k_anonymity_cohort_size_at_sale < 3` MUST defer placement rendering and remain `pending` with `status_reason=k_anonymity_pending` until cohort threshold met or 30-day timeout (then voided with `k_anonymity_timeout`).
11. Records MUST be append-only post-`invoiced`; `amount_cents`, `billing_currency`, `fx_rate_locked_to_usd`, `cost_center`, `sku`, `billing_period_start`, `billing_period_end` MUST be immutable after write. Mutation attempts rejected with HTTP 422 `marketplace_discovery_field_immutable`.
12. Retention MUST be ≥ 7 years per §40.2; `deleted_at` MUST always be NULL; hard-delete attempts rejected with HTTP 422 `marketplace_discovery_hard_delete_forbidden`.
13. MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord MUST NOT reference AIWallet; no `ai_wallet_id` FK exists. QA test `marketplace_discovery_no_ai_wallet_linkage` asserts.
14. MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord MUST NOT create or mutate AIOperation rows. QA test `marketplace_discovery_no_aioperation_write` asserts.
15. Stripe webhook processing MUST follow §31 HMAC-SHA256 and idempotency semantics; duplicate webhook deliveries MUST NOT create duplicate state transitions.
16. DSAR right-to-erasure MUST redact PII linkage while preserving all financial fields per §6.8; QA test `marketplace_discovery_dsar_financial_preserved` asserts.
17. Dual-Console Firewall MUST prevent buyer-console users from reading marketplace-discovery rows for their own Org; enforced by scoping all queries to the seller-console billing endpoint. QA test `dual_console_firewall_marketplace_discovery_buyer_blocked` asserts.
18. Finance dashboard MUST surface per-cost-center gross margin independently: `rev_marketplace_discovery` target ≈ 95%+, `rev_ai_wallet` target ≈ 4.5%, `rev_subscription` target ≈ 85–90% per Summary §6.16.6.
19. Every priced PromotedListing charge MUST create a MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord with `source_entity_type='promoted_listing'`, `source_entity_id = PromotedListing.id`, and `cost_center='rev_marketplace_discovery'`; nightly reconciliation MUST compare the summed `amount_cents` for those rows against PromotedListing `spend_to_date_cents` by billing cycle with zero tolerance for mismatch. QA test `promoted_listing_revenue_source_entity_reconciliation` asserts.

### 4.8.13 SellerOutcomeSignalConfig (Platform-Scoped, Seller-Console-Only, Versioned) {#4.8.13-selleroutcomesignalconfig}

**Authoring Intent.** Per Summary §2.9 / C.130 and Seller Pricing §10, the 12 seller-side AI capabilities each have a capability-specific accepted-signal rule, evaluation window, and `timeout_default = rejected` semantics. Where §4.8.4 OutcomeContract is the platform-scoped base contract layer for the Outcome Resolver, SellerOutcomeSignalConfig is the seller-console-specific extension that binds each seller capability to its accepted-signal rule, window, and the mandatory "reject on silence" timeout default that Summary §2.9 / Seller Pricing §10 describe as the cost-protection stance. This entity exists because (a) seller signals often terminate on downstream marketplace events (e.g., "bid submission") rather than on timer expiry, which the base OutcomeContract does not natively express, and (b) k-anonymity constraints on some seller signals (e.g., `match_score`) require cohort-aware deferral logic that is cleaner to model in a seller-specific extension than to fold into OutcomeContract generically. The 12 rows MUST be seeded at migration time in one-to-one correspondence with the capabilities enumerated in Seller Pricing §10.

**Scope.** Platform-scoped (Ops-managed). `console_scope = 'seller'` enforced; buyer-side capabilities are governed by their own buyer-side rule sets and never written here. One row per `(capability_id, version)` pair; exactly one active row per capability at any time.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `capability_id` | String | FK → CapabilityRegistryEntry.`capability_id`; MUST be a value of Appendix J `seller_outcome_signal_capability`; required | Non-seller capability rejected with HTTP 422 `seller_outcome_signal_unknown_capability` |
| `version` | Integer | ≥ 1; monotonic per `capability_id` | |
| `outcome_contract_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → OutcomeContract; referenced contract MUST be in `state=active` or `state=superseded` (NOT `retired`) at publication | The base contract this config extends; bound at publication |
| `accepted_signal_rule` | JSON | ≤ 8000 chars; validated against `seller_outcome_signal_rule_schema` (versioned; Appendix J) | Structured rule; see rule_type for the signal family |
| `accepted_signal_rule_type` | Enum | See Appendix J `seller_outcome_signal_rule_type`: `retention_threshold`, `edit_distance_ceiling`, `publication_event`, `approval_ratio`, `citation_event`, `dedupe_or_approval`, `reverify_or_archive`, `ui_publication_event`, `submission_after_view`, `assignment_event`, `attachment_event` | Drives the evaluator's dispatch |
| `rejected_signal_rule` | JSON | ≤ 8000 chars; nullable | Optional explicit rejection rule; absence means rejection fires only by timeout-default (`rejected`) |
| `window_seconds` | Integer | 3600 ≤ `window_seconds` ≤ 7776000 | 1-hour floor; 90-day ceiling. Out-of-range rejected with HTTP 422 `seller_outcome_signal_window_out_of_range` |
| `window_alt_boundary` | Enum | See Appendix J `seller_outcome_signal_alt_boundary`: `none`, `bid_submission`, `eoi_submission`, `kb_publication`, `response_submission`; default `none` | Event boundary that also terminates the window (whichever fires first). Supports Seller Pricing §10 "14d or on bid submission" semantics |
| `timeout_default` | Enum | MUST equal `rejected`; DB CHECK enforces | Any other value rejected with HTTP 422 `seller_outcome_signal_timeout_default_invalid` |
| `min_retention_threshold_pct` | Integer | 0–100; nullable | Required when `accepted_signal_rule_type='retention_threshold'` (e.g., ≥ 50% for `first_pass_rfp_draft`) |
| `max_edit_threshold_pct` | Integer | 0–100; nullable | Required when `accepted_signal_rule_type='edit_distance_ceiling'` (e.g., ≤ 30% for `qa_suggestion_seller`) |
| `min_approval_ratio_pct` | Integer | 0–100; nullable | Required when `accepted_signal_rule_type='approval_ratio'` (e.g., ≥ 60% for `kb_bootstrap`) |
| `console_scope` | Enum | MUST equal `seller`; DB CHECK enforces | Buyer-side values rejected with HTTP 422 `seller_outcome_signal_console_mismatch` |
| `k_anonymity_floor` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Cohort floor for attribution-sensitive signals (e.g., `seller_match_score_numeric`); below-floor cohorts defer accepted-signal firing (which then times out to `rejected` under the default) |
| `state` | Enum | `draft`, `active`, `superseded`, `retired` | Lifecycle; mirrors OutcomeContract state machine |
| `superseded_by_config_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; self-reference | Populated when state transitions to `superseded` |
| `effective_at` | Timestamp | UTC | Publication moment |
| `superseded_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | Populated on state transition to `superseded` |
| `retired_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | Populated on state transition to `retired` |
| `published_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | MUST have Ops `ops_finance_admin` role | Non-Ops writes rejected with HTTP 403 `rbac_ops_finance_admin_required` |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC; permitted only in `draft` state |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Ops user | |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Ops user | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | ALWAYS NULL | Hard-delete forbidden; rule-definition history retained indefinitely for audit |

**Scope Isolation.**

- **Console:** seller-only; `console_scope='seller'` enforced by DB CHECK. Buyer-side rule sets live in a separate buyer-side configuration entity (to be authored in Phase 2 alongside the §34 rewrite).
- **Org:** platform-scoped; not Org-scoped. Rule definitions apply uniformly across all seller Orgs.
- **Marketplace-domain:** platform-wide.
- **Residency:** N/A; rule definitions are operational metadata, not customer data, and are not residency-partitioned. Runtime signal evaluations occur within the residency-appropriate tenant per §40.5.
- **RBAC:** writes gated by `ops_finance_admin`; reads by Ops roles and, via a sanitized projection, by seller-console users (who see a human-readable description of the accepted-signal rule, window, and timeout default, but not the raw JSON).

**Indexes.**

- `(capability_id, version DESC)` — history lookup.
- `(capability_id, state)` PARTIAL UNIQUE WHERE `state='active'` — enforces exactly-one-active per capability.
- `(outcome_contract_id)` — join to OutcomeContract.
- `(superseded_by_config_id)` PARTIAL WHERE `superseded_by_config_id IS NOT NULL`.
- `(accepted_signal_rule_type, state)` — rule-type reporting dashboard.
- `(console_scope, state)` PARTIAL WHERE `console_scope='seller' AND state='active'` — all-active-seller-rules sweep.

**Retention.** Rule definitions retained indefinitely for audit (immutable history). Superseded rules retained for at least 7 years after the last AIOperation resolved under them settles or expires. No DSAR impact (rule definitions contain no customer PII).

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `draft` | Ops creates new version | `version = MAX(prior versions) + 1` for the `capability_id`; must reference an active OR superseded OutcomeContract | Editable in draft |
| `draft` | `active` | Ops publishes | Prior active (if any) transitions to `superseded` atomically; `effective_at` stamped; partial unique index enforces single active row | Atomic swap inside a single DB transaction |
| `active` | `superseded` | New version published | `superseded_at` stamped; `superseded_by_config_id` set | AIOperations with `created_at ≤ superseded_at` continue to resolve under the prior config |
| `superseded` | `retired` | All AIOperations under this config have settled OR contest-window has expired + 90-day hold | `retired_at` stamped | Permanent terminal state; no mutation; history preserved |

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Operator sets `timeout_default = accepted` to game resolution stats.** Resolved: DB CHECK constraint `timeout_default = 'rejected'`; write-side validator; violations rejected with HTTP 422 `seller_outcome_signal_timeout_default_invalid`. QA test `seller_outcome_signal_default_rejected_12` asserts all 12 seeded rows have `timeout_default='rejected'`.
2. **Signal rule written for a non-seller capability.** Resolved: DB CHECK `console_scope='seller'`; capability_id validated against `seller_outcome_signal_capability` enum. Non-seller capability rejected with HTTP 422 `seller_outcome_signal_unknown_capability`.
3. **Config published referencing a retired OutcomeContract.** Resolved: publication checks that the referenced `outcome_contract_id` is in `state IN ('active', 'superseded')`; retired contracts rejected with HTTP 409 `seller_outcome_signal_contract_retired`.
4. **`window_seconds` out of bounds.** Resolved: range constraint 3600 ≤ `window_seconds` ≤ 7776000; violation rejected with HTTP 422 `seller_outcome_signal_window_out_of_range`.
5. **Concurrent publication of two draft versions for the same capability.** Resolved: partial unique index on `(capability_id, state)` WHERE `state='active'` enforces at most one active row. Concurrent transaction rejected with HTTP 409 `seller_outcome_signal_version_conflict`.
6. **K-anonymity violation — `match_score_numeric` accepted-signal would fire when cohort = 1 (buyer identity leak).** Resolved: evaluator consults `k_anonymity_floor` before firing; sub-floor cohorts defer accepted-signal firing, which then times out to `rejected` under the default. Deferral events counted in `seller_outcome_k_anonymity_deferred` for Ops reporting.
7. **Alt-boundary event fires before `window_seconds` elapses (e.g., bid submitted on day 3 for a 14d window).** Resolved: evaluator fires on whichever of (time window, alt boundary) comes first per Seller Pricing §10 "14d or on bid submission". Simultaneous firings at `t = window_seconds` tie-break to the alt boundary (preserves event-primary semantics).
8. **Late signal arrives after `window_seconds` has elapsed and `rejected` has already been recorded on AIOperation.** Resolved: late signals are no-ops for resolution; if the late signal is `accepted`, an automatic ContestRecord (§4.8.5) is filed with reason `auto_filed_late_signal` mirroring the OutcomeContract grace-window behavior, so the customer is protected from resolver-latency bugs.
9. **Seller attempts to read platform-scoped config rule JSON via API.** Resolved: API route scoped to Ops `ops_finance_admin`; seller-console endpoints return only a sanitized human-readable projection (signal description, window, timeout default) and never the raw JSON rule. RBAC enforced at route.
10. **Version drift — AIOperation created at t=0 under config v2, resolved at t=window under config v3.** Resolved: AIOperation resolution uses the config version active at AIOperation `created_at`, not the current active version; config FK frozen at AIOperation write time (denormalized via the resolver query plan per §4.8.4 pattern).
11. **Seed migration misses a capability (only 11 of 12 rows inserted).** Resolved: QA test `seller_outcome_signal_seed_count_12` asserts exactly 12 active rows post-migration, one per `seller_outcome_signal_capability` enum value. CI blocks deploy if assertion fails.
12. **Rule-schema version drift — a rule authored against rule_schema v1 is evaluated against v2 after a schema change.** Resolved: each SellerOutcomeSignalConfig row is locked to a rule-schema version captured at publication; evaluator consults the locked version, not the current version. Schema migrations require a new config version per capability.

**Seed Specification (MUST match Summary §2.9 / Seller Pricing §10 verbatim).**

The migration MUST seed the following 12 rows at v1 with `console_scope='seller'`, `timeout_default='rejected'`, `state='active'`, and `k_anonymity_floor=0` except where noted:

| `capability_id` | Accepted signal | `accepted_signal_rule_type` | `window_seconds` | `window_alt_boundary` | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `first_pass_rfp_draft` | ≥ 50% of draft retained in submitted bid | `retention_threshold` (min 50) | 1209600 (14d) | `bid_submission` | "14d or on bid submission" per §10. **D-1.7-001 remediation, 2026-05-01:** prefixed `seller_first_pass_rfp_draft` retired in favor of canonical Appendix J `seller_outcome_signal_capability` value. |
| `qa_suggestion_seller` | Answer sent with ≤ 30% edit | `edit_distance_ceiling` (max 30) | 604800 (7d) | `none` | **D-1.7-001 remediation, 2026-05-01:** prefixed `seller_qa_suggestion` retired; canonical name carries the `_seller` suffix to disambiguate from buyer-side `qa_suggestion` per §21.4.1 / §22.10 reconciliation note line 14521. |
| `kb_to_capability_suggestion` | Declaration published | `publication_event` | 1209600 (14d) | `kb_publication` | **D-1.7-001 remediation, 2026-05-01.** |
| `kb_bootstrap` | ≥ 60% of proposed entries approved | `approval_ratio` (min 60) | 2592000 (30d) | `none` | **D-1.7-001 remediation, 2026-05-01.** |
| `ghost_rfp_ingestion` | Resulting KB entries cited in a future bid | `citation_event` | 7776000 (90d) | `bid_submission` | **D-1.7-001 remediation, 2026-05-01.** |
| `firecrawl_crawl_dedupe` | New entry approved OR correct dedupe | `dedupe_or_approval` | 604800 (7d) | `none` | **D-1.7-001 remediation, 2026-05-01.** |
| `kb_staleness_classifier` | Flagged entry re-verified or archived | `reverify_or_archive` | 1209600 (14d) | `none` | **D-1.7-001 remediation, 2026-05-01.** |
| `seller_page_enrichment` | Seller publishes generated content | `ui_publication_event` | 1209600 (14d) | `kb_publication` | **Grandfathered.** Canonical Appendix J value retains the `seller_` prefix because it disambiguates from the parallel buyer-side surface; the `canonical_capability_id_lock` deploy-time validator carries an explicit allow-list entry. |
| `capability_declaration_suggest` | Declaration published | `publication_event` | 604800 (7d) | `kb_publication` | **D-1.7-001 remediation, 2026-05-01.** |
| `match_score_numeric` | EOI submitted after viewing score | `submission_after_view` | 1209600 (14d) | `eoi_submission` | `k_anonymity_floor=3` per Summary C.131. **D-1.7-001 remediation, 2026-05-01.** |
| `bid_task_assignment_suggest` | Task assigned as suggested | `assignment_event` | 86400 (24h) | `none` | **D-1.7-001 remediation, 2026-05-01.** |
| `document_attach_suggest` | Document attached to response | `attachment_event` | 86400 (24h) | `response_submission` | **D-1.7-001 remediation, 2026-05-01.** |

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Exactly `|seller_outcome_signal_capability|` active SellerOutcomeSignalConfig rows MUST exist at any time (v1 migration seeds 12, one per enum value; future Appendix J extensions to this enum MUST ship with a migration step that adds the corresponding active config row in the same release). QA test `seller_outcome_signal_seed_count_matches_enum_cardinality` asserts parity between active-config count and enum value count.
2. Every SellerOutcomeSignalConfig MUST have `timeout_default = 'rejected'`; DB CHECK and write-side validator enforce. Non-`rejected` values rejected with HTTP 422 `seller_outcome_signal_timeout_default_invalid`. QA test `seller_outcome_signal_default_rejected_12` asserts all 12 seeded rows.
3. Every SellerOutcomeSignalConfig MUST have `console_scope = 'seller'`; non-seller values rejected with HTTP 422 `seller_outcome_signal_console_mismatch`.
4. `window_seconds` MUST be in [3600, 7776000]; out-of-range rejected with HTTP 422 `seller_outcome_signal_window_out_of_range`.
5. Exactly one SellerOutcomeSignalConfig per `capability_id` MUST be in `state='active'`; partial unique index enforces; concurrent publication rejected with HTTP 409 `seller_outcome_signal_version_conflict`.
6. AIOperation resolution for seller capabilities MUST use the SellerOutcomeSignalConfig version active at AIOperation `created_at`, not the currently active version.
7. `accepted_signal_rule` JSON MUST validate against the locked rule-schema version captured at publication; invalid rejected with HTTP 422 `seller_outcome_signal_rule_invalid`.
8. Each SellerOutcomeSignalConfig MUST reference an OutcomeContract in `state IN ('active', 'superseded')`; retired contracts rejected with HTTP 409 `seller_outcome_signal_contract_retired`.
9. Seller-side outcome signals MUST default to `rejected` on timeout per Seller Pricing §10; QA test `seller_outcome_signal_default_rejected_12` asserts each of the 12 capabilities resolves to `rejected` when no accepted-signal event arrives within `window_seconds` AND no alt-boundary event fires.
10. K-anonymity-sensitive signals (where `k_anonymity_floor > 0`) MUST defer accepted-signal firing when cohort size is below floor; pending AIOperations remain in `pending` until cohort threshold met or window/alt-boundary terminates (then timeout-default-rejected applies). `match_score_numeric` MUST have `k_anonymity_floor >= 3` per Summary C.131. (D-1.7-001 remediation, 2026-05-01: prefixed `seller_match_score_numeric` retired.)
11. Config rows in `state='active'` MUST be immutable; only `draft` rows may be mutated. Post-activation mutation attempts rejected with HTTP 422 `seller_outcome_signal_immutable_post_activation`.
12. Writes MUST require Ops `ops_finance_admin` role; non-Ops writes rejected with HTTP 403 `rbac_ops_finance_admin_required`.
13. Seller-console GET endpoints MUST return a sanitized projection (signal description, window, timeout default), never the raw rule JSON.
14. Late-signal handling MUST mirror OutcomeContract §4.8.4 grace semantics: a late `accepted` signal arriving within OutcomeContract.`signal_evaluation_grace_seconds` MUST auto-file a ContestRecord with reason `auto_filed_late_signal` to protect the customer from resolver-latency bugs.
15. Migration MUST preserve Summary §2.9 / Seller Pricing §10 verbatim signal-definition semantics for all 12 capabilities; cross-reference QA test `seller_outcome_signal_seed_matches_summary_2_9` asserts window and accepted-signal-type parity against a frozen fixture derived from Summary §2.9.
16. **(D-1.7-001 remediation, 2026-05-01)** Every seeded `capability_id` MUST be a registered value of Appendix J `seller_outcome_signal_capability` per the canonical (unprefixed) taxonomy enumerated in the Seed Specification table above; the deploy-time validator `canonical_capability_id_lock` (§M.5) cross-checks each seeded value against the Appendix J registry and against the §22.10 / §21.4.1 Capability Registry, blocking deploy on any mismatch. The `seller_page_enrichment` row is the sole grandfathered prefixed value, allow-listed by the validator. CI gate `seller_outcome_signal_seed_canonical_capability_id` asserts the parity at deploy time.
