# 5\. RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) {#5.-rbac-(role-based-access-control)}

## 5.1 RBAC Architecture {#5.1-rbac-architecture}

Sourcera implements role-based access control at two levels:

1. **Org-Level Roles:** Govern access to organization-scoped resources (members, teams, billing, org settings).  
2. **Console-Level Roles:** Govern access to console-scoped resources (workspaces, requirements, bids, marketplace).

Each user can hold multiple roles across different orgs and workspaces. Guest roles are workspace-scoped and configurable with permission profiles.

**Role-overlay union-of-permissions rule (D-3.1-001 V3 remediation, 2026-05-04).** When a user holds multiple roles within the same scope (e.g., `org_admin` AND `billing_admin` on the same Org; `workspace_owner` AND `use_case_lead` on the same Workspace; `seller_org_owner` AND `seller_kb_admin` on the same Seller Org), the effective permission set is the **union** of the per-role permissions. The §5.2.1.5 Failure Mode #1 `billing_admin × member` pairing is the canonical exemplar. Cross-Org role grants are independent — a user holding `org_owner` in Org A and `member` in Org B does NOT inherit any Org A permission into Org B; the active-Org context is established at session-start time per the WorkOS post-auth callback and re-established on every `X-Sourcera-Active-Org` header switch (§6.1). Cross-console role overlays within the same Org honor the §1.3 firewall: a user holding `workspace_owner` (Buyer) and `seller_org_admin` (Seller) on the same dual-console Org sees Buyer-Console resources via the Buyer role and Seller-Console resources via the Seller role; no permission crosses the firewall by virtue of the overlay.

## 5.2 Org-Level Roles {#5.2-org-level-roles}

| Role | Permissions | Capabilities |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Org Owner** | All org-scoped resources enumerated by §1.3.1, plus billing authority and workspace-shell creation; console-scoped content remains governed by the Buyer / Seller console role grants in §5.3, §5.5, and §5.11 | Create/edit/delete orgs, create/delete workspace shells, manage team members, manage billing, manage SSO, view audit logs, manage integrations. Does not bypass the §1.3 Dual-Console Firewall for console-scoped Workspace, Bid Workspace, KB, Response, Score, or Capability Declaration content. |
| **Org Admin** | Org-scoped resources enumerated by §1.3.1; billing read-only where explicitly listed in §5.2.1 and §5.11; billing mutations remain denied unless the user also holds `billing_admin`; console-scoped content remains governed by §5.3 / §5.5 / §5.11 | Create/delete workspace shells, manage team members, manage SSO, view audit logs, manage integrations, and read billing status / ledgers in the read-only rows enumerated below. Cannot change plan, mutate wallet settings, file/withdraw contests, accept Pro Trial Seat grants, or opt out of CommittedSpend renewal unless separately granted `billing_admin`. |
| **Member** | Org directory read-only per §5.2.2; no org management, billing, or console-scoped content access unless another role grants it | View own Org profile, own OrgMembership, active team memberships, and the visible member directory projection. SCIM-provisioned users default to `member` unless §4.2.5 Group role assignment maps them to another role. |
| **Billing Admin** | Org-scoped, console-pooled billing & AI-accounting surface only; orthogonal to `org_admin` | Read AIWallet, AIOperation ledger, FreeAllowanceCounter, ContestRecord, CommittedSpendContract, BillingSeatSnapshot, PricingTableVersion across both consoles; mutate wallet overage, caps, manual top-ups, and auto-topup configuration; file, withdraw, and respond to ContestRecord; change plan tier across the §34.1.1 Buyer plan-tier set and §34.1.2 Seller plan-tier set (Enterprise tier changes still gated on Sales-Ops sign-off per §34.12.5); accept or reject Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat grants on the vendor side (§34.13); opt out of or opt back into CommittedSpendContract auto-renewal (§4.8.8); pin a PricingTableVersion for forecasting (§4.8.9); export Billing Ledger and Pricing Ledger CSVs. EXPLICITLY denied: workspace data access (Use Cases, Requirements, Responses, Scores, Selection Reports, Bid Workspaces, KB entries, Capability Declarations); SSO/SCIM/IP-restriction configuration; org-membership management (granting roles, inviting members); Audit Log access outside the Billing Admin Audit View (see §5.2.1.4); cross-Org billing access; any Ops Console action. |

**Org-level scope guardrail (D-3.1-004 / D-3.1-005 remediation, 2026-06-21).** In this table, "org-scoped resources" means Organization, OrgMembership, Team, Group, Audit Event, billing entities, integrations, SSO / SCIM / MFA configuration, and Org settings under §1.3.1. It does not mean automatic read/write authority over Buyer Workspace content, Seller Bid Workspace content, Seller KB content, Marketplace publication records, Responses, Scores, Requirements, Selection Reports, Capability Declarations, or any other console-scoped record. Org Owner and Org Admin may create workspace shells and manage Org-level membership, but content access is evaluated by the active console role resolver and the §1.3 firewall. Org Admin has read-only billing access only where §5.2.1.1 and §5.11 explicitly mark `org_admin (read-only)`; all billing mutations require `org_owner`, `billing_admin`, or both as specified per operation.

### 5.2.1 Billing Admin (Authored Extension — Phase-4 RBAC Integration) {#5.2.1-billing-admin}

**Authoring Intent.** Billing Admin is the org-scoped, console-pooled role that owns the billing-and-AI-accounting surface authored in §4.8 (AIWallet, AIOperation ledger, FreeAllowanceCounter, OutcomeContract observation, ContestRecord, CommittedSpendContract, PricingTableVersion, DowngradeExcessDataBucket, BillingSeatSnapshot). The role is introduced in v7.0.0 per Master Summary §6.22.1 and Summary C.75–C.87 to separate billing authority from organizational administration: a Finance or Procurement-Ops user can be granted Billing Admin without inheriting workspace, member, SSO, or integration management. The role is orthogonal to `org_admin` (a user MAY hold both, but neither implies the other), and it is the single role permitted to mutate billing configuration, file contests, change plan tier, or accept Pro Trial Seat grants on the vendor side per §34.11.7 acceptance criterion 33.

**Scope.** Org-scoped. The role is held against an Organization, applies uniformly across the buyer and seller consoles (the AIWallet, billing ledger, and contest queue are pooled per §4.8.3; the Dual-Console Firewall does not partition billing authority). The role is NOT bid-workspace-scoped, workspace-scoped, or marketplace-domain-scoped; a Billing Admin sees no workspace contents. Cross-Org reads are denied: a Billing Admin attempting any read against another Org's billing surface receives HTTP 404 with `billing_admin_cross_org_access` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 404 to avoid leaking Org existence).

#### 5.2.1.1 Permission List (Operation-by-Operation)

Each line below maps to a concrete API operation, Convex mutation, or scheduled job that enforces the permission. Operations marked "API" map to public REST surfaces in §32; operations marked "Convex" are server-side mutations callable only via the in-app surfaces; operations marked "Stripe webhook ingress" are not directly invocable by humans but the Billing Admin's configuration changes drive the parameters that the webhook handler consumes.

| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Read AIWallet (own Org) | API: `GET /v1/billing/wallet`; Convex: `billing.wallet.get` | `role ∈ {org_owner, org_admin (read-only), billing_admin}` | `org.wallet_viewed` |

| 22 | Receive notifications: 50% / 80% / 100% wallet utilization, payment-failed grace, contest decisions, plan-change confirmations, Pro Trial Seat grant arrivals (vendor side), CommittedSpendContract renewal upcoming, PricingTableVersion breaking-change advance notice | Notification dispatch (email + in-app per §4.8.3, §4.8.5, §4.8.8, §4.8.9, §34.13) | Recipient set is the union of `org_owner` users + `billing_admin` users (deduplicated) | n/a (notification dispatch not audit-logged at the recipient level) |

**Explicit Non-Permissions.** The following operations MUST return HTTP 403 `billing_admin_role_insufficient` (new; Appendix I) when attempted by a user holding only `billing_admin`:

| Disallowed Operation | Surface | Reason |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Read or write any Workspace, Use Case, Requirement, Response, Score, Scenario, Selection Report, Selection Record | §32 workspace endpoints | Workspace data is firewalled from billing surface; Billing Admin has no workspace membership |
| Read or write any Bid Workspace, Bid Response, Bid Task, Capability Declaration, KB entry, Document Library item | §32 seller endpoints | Same as above; seller data is firewalled |
| Grant or revoke any role (including `billing_admin` itself) | API: `POST /v1/organizations/me/members/{user_id}/roles` | Role assignment is `org_owner` / `org_admin` authority per §5.2.1.2 |
| Configure SSO, SCIM, MFA enforcement, IP restrictions, dynamic API key issuance | §6 endpoints | Identity-and-security configuration is `org_owner` authority |
| Create / delete a workspace; create / delete a Bid Workspace | §32 workspace endpoints | Workspace lifecycle is `org_owner` / `org_admin` authority |
| Read full Audit Event log (cross-namespace) | API: `GET /v1/audit-events` (no namespace filter) | Cross-namespace audit log is `org_owner` / `org_admin` authority; Billing Admin sees only the Billing Admin Audit View per Operation #21 |
| Cross-Org read of any billing entity | All billing endpoints with cross-Org `org_id` | HTTP 404 `billing_admin_cross_org_access` (no leakage of Org existence) |
| Ops Console actions of any kind (impersonation, manual wallet adjustment, contest decision, cost-base recalc approval, etc.) | Ops Console surface | Ops Console authority is governed by `ops_finance_admin`, `ops_compliance_admin`, etc., per Appendix J Ops roles |

#### 5.2.1.2 Assignment, Concurrency, and Deprovisioning

**Assignment.** The `billing_admin` role is granted by `org_owner` or `org_admin` via `POST /v1/organizations/me/members/{user_id}/roles` with body `{"role": "billing_admin"}`. Grant requires the target user to be an active member of the Org (not a guest, not an API-only identity, not a deleted user). Assignment is audit-logged as `org.billing_admin_role_granted` with grantor user attribution. The role is NEVER granted by default at Org provisioning; the first Billing Admin (if any) is an explicit Org Owner action. An Org may have zero or more Billing Admins concurrently; there is no maximum cap, but a soft warning surfaces in the Org Owner UI when more than ten Billing Admins are concurrently active (potential blast-radius signal).

**Replacement Pattern.** When an Org has zero Billing Admins (the role is empty), all Billing-Admin-only operations (file ContestRecord, withdraw ContestRecord, change plan tier, accept Pro Trial Seat, opt-out of CommittedSpendContract renewal, etc.) MUST fall back to `org_owner` authority — `org_owner` always retains de facto Billing Admin permissions (per §5.2.1.2 "granted by org_owner and org_admin; it is not granted by default"). This guarantees the Org is never operationally locked out of its billing surface even if every named Billing Admin departs.

**Deprovisioning.** When a `billing_admin` is deprovisioned (role revoked, member deleted, SSO deactivation), per §34.12.7 Failure Mode #3:

1. The role-revocation transaction stamps `org.billing_admin_role_revoked` with revoker user attribution and a snapshot of the prior assignment (`grantor_user_id`, `granted_at`).
2. Any in-flight Stripe charges initiated by the deprovisioned user complete normally (Stripe's webhook handler is idempotent and does not re-validate caller identity at settlement).
3. Any open ContestRecord filed by the deprovisioned user remains `open` and is owned by the Org's pool of remaining Billing Admins (or `org_owner` if none); the `filed_by_user_id` field is preserved as a historical record but withdrawal authority transfers to the remaining Billing Admin pool.
4. Any pending CommittedSpendContract auto-renewal opt-out request remains active (the request was on the contract, not on the user).
5. Notification routing is recomputed: the deprovisioned user is removed from the recipient union; if the recipient union becomes empty (no `org_owner` either, an inconsistent state by §4.2 invariants), notifications fall back to `ops_finance_admin` for triage.

**SCIM Provisioning Interaction.** Per §6.1 (Authentication Architecture / WorkOS SCIM), the `billing_admin` role is NOT auto-provisioned via SCIM by default — SCIM-provisioned users default to `member`. An Org may opt in via §4.2.5 Group `assigned_role_slug` binding: the Org Admin creates (or maps to) a WorkOS Group named `BillingAdmin` (or any name) and sets `assigned_role_slug = billing_admin`. Per the WorkOS April 2026 contract and Sourcera §5.13.2 precedence rule, directory-group role assignments take precedence over SSO group role assignments. Group-bound role assignments are audit-logged as `org.scim_group_role_assigned` / `org.scim_group_role_revoked` (replaces the pre-V3+ `org.scim_billing_admin_mapping_enabled` / `org.scim_billing_admin_mapping_disabled` events; old events retained for historical projections per §6.8.5 audit-integrity exemption). Default-deny is preserved for security: a user provisioned via SCIM into an Org with no `BillingAdmin`-mapped Group lands as `member` only.

#### 5.2.1.3 Scope Isolation

| Surface | Allowed | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Own Org's billing entities (AIWallet, ContestRecord, CommittedSpendContract, PricingTableVersion pin, BillingSeatSnapshot, DowngradeExcessDataBucket, FreeAllowanceCounter, AIOperation ledger) | Yes | Per Permission List §5.2.1.1 |
| Own Org's workspace data (any console, any bid workspace) | No | HTTP 403 `billing_admin_role_insufficient` |
| Other Org's billing entities | No | HTTP 404 `billing_admin_cross_org_access` (no Org-existence leakage) |
| Public Pricing API (`api.sourcera.com/v1/pricing`) | Yes | No auth; same as any anonymous reader |
| Ops Console | No | HTTP 403 `ops_role_required` |
| Audit Log (full cross-namespace) | No | HTTP 403 `audit_log_full_view_requires_org_admin`; Billing Admin Audit View per Operation #21 only |
| Marketplace Listings (read public listings) | Yes | Same as `marketplace_viewer` global access; no special billing privilege |
| Marketplace Listings (publish / edit own Org's listings) | No (unless also `marketplace_publisher`) | Marketplace publication is its own role per §5.6 |

**Cross-Console Pooling.** Because AIWallet is Org-scoped and console-pooled per §4.8.3, a single Billing Admin sees the unified billing position across both consoles in one place (Buyer Growth + Seller Starter Org sees the unified $330/mo budget per Pricing Strategy §11). The Billing Admin Audit View also pools events from both consoles. The Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2) does NOT apply to billing entities — billing is shared by design; workspace content is not.

#### 5.2.1.4 Audit Semantics

Every Billing-Admin-mutated operation MUST emit one Audit Event with `action` ∈ Billing Admin Audit Action Types (Appendix J — new sub-enum), `user_id = caller`, `entity_type ∈ {ai_wallet, contest_record, committed_spend_contract, pricing_table_version, pro_trial_seat_grant, organization_plan, free_allowance_counter, billing_seat_snapshot, downgrade_excess_data_bucket}`, `entity_id = subject id`, and `changes` JSON populated for state mutations (per §4.6.1 Audit Event field semantics). Read operations on billing entities by Billing Admin emit `org.*_viewed` audit events at sample rate 1.0 (no sampling — billing reads are forensic-grade auditable).

The Billing Admin Audit View (Operation #21) is a server-side filter over the Audit Event entity that returns only rows where `action` matches the regex `^org\.(wallet|contest|committed_spend|plan|solo_trial|pro_trial_seat|billing|downgrade_bucket|free_allowance|pricing|scim_billing|billing_admin)_*` AND `org_id = session.org_id`. The view is paginated per §32.3 (cursor-based, default 50, max 250). Filter parameters: `action_namespace`, `entity_type`, `user_id`, `from`, `to`, `status`. Export to CSV is permitted (Operation #8 / `org.billing_audit_exported`).

**Audit Retention.** Billing Admin audit events follow §40.2 standard retention plus the §34.1 plan-tier UI-retention curve (per §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 cell **Audit Log Retention (UI)**). CommittedSpendContract-related audits retain for 7 years on every plan (financial-record exception per §40.2 `extended_financial`). Any audit event tagged `org.contest_*` retains for 7 years on every plan (regulatory contest-trail requirement).

#### 5.2.1.5 Failure Modes Addressed

1. **A user holds both `billing_admin` and `member` (no `org_admin` or `org_owner`); session.org_id matches the wallet's org_id.** Resolved: union-of-permissions semantics — the user gets every permission of every held role; `billing_admin` permissions activate without needing `org_admin`.
2. **A user holds `billing_admin` in Org A and is added to Org B as a `member` only.** Resolved: roles are per-Org-membership; the user has no Billing Admin privileges in Org B; switching the active Org via `X-Sourcera-Active-Org` header re-evaluates.
3. **A `billing_admin` files a ContestRecord, then is deprovisioned 1 second later.** Resolved: filing is atomic; the contest persists; subsequent withdrawal authority transfers to the remaining Billing Admin pool per §5.2.1.2.
4. **Two Billing Admins simultaneously file contests against the same AIOperation.** Resolved: per §4.8.5 the unique constraint on `(ai_operation_id)` permits exactly one ContestRecord; the second filer receives HTTP 409 `contest_already_filed` with the prior contest ID exposed.
5. **A `billing_admin` attempts to read a workspace's audit log to investigate a billing-related dispute.** Resolved: HTTP 403 `audit_log_full_view_requires_org_admin`; the Billing Admin Audit View per Operation #21 is the sanctioned alternative; if the dispute requires workspace-scope audit, an `org_owner` or `org_admin` must perform the read or the Billing Admin must be granted `org_admin` (auditable).
6. **A `billing_admin` attempts to change plan tier from Buyer Enterprise to Buyer Free without Sales-Ops sign-off.** Resolved: per §34.12.5 Enterprise downgrades are gated on `ops_finance_admin` co-signoff; the API returns HTTP 423 `enterprise_plan_change_requires_ops_signoff` with the Ops ticket creation link.
7. **A `billing_admin` attempts to file a contest 15 days after settlement (1 day past window).** Resolved: per §4.8.5 the write-time check returns HTTP 410 `ai_operation_contest_window_expired`; the response body includes `contest_window_at` and `original_settlement_at` for client-side messaging.
8. **A `billing_admin` is granted to a user whose email domain is not a verified Org domain.** Resolved: assignment proceeds (the user is already an Org member by definition of role-grant prerequisites); the soft warning "Billing Admin granted to a user outside your verified domains" surfaces to the grantor (Org Owner / Admin); audit event captures the warning acknowledgement.
9. **A `billing_admin` triggers a manual top-up that fails Stripe charge 5 times (DLQ).** Resolved: per §4.8.3 Top-Up State Machine the wallet enters `payment_failed_grace`; the Billing Admin receives hourly grace alerts; the audit event sequence is `org.wallet_topup_manual_initiated` → `org.wallet_topup_failed` (system) → `org.wallet_payment_failed_grace_entered` (system) → eventual recovery or `org.wallet_suspended` (system).
10. **A `billing_admin` accepts a Pro Trial Seat grant on the vendor side, but the vendor Org is already on a paid Seller plan.** Resolved: per §34.13.5 the API returns HTTP 409 `trial_seat_vendor_already_paid`; no state transition; audit event `org.pro_trial_seat_acceptance_rejected` records the failed acceptance attempt with reason code.
11. **A `billing_admin` opts out of CommittedSpendContract renewal less than 60 days before `commit_period_end`.** Resolved: per §4.8.8 the API returns HTTP 422 `committed_spend_renewal_opt_out_window_expired`; the contract auto-renews per its `shortfall_policy`.
12. **An Org has zero `billing_admin` users and the `org_owner` user is locked out of MFA.** Resolved: the Org enters a billing-administration deadlock; per §6 (Identity & Security) account-recovery flow, an `ops_finance_admin` may impersonate the `org_owner` under §35 impersonation audit (cross-referenced from §3.8 / §4.8.1 Scope Isolation; the dedicated impersonation-audit section is a long-standing Known Gap and is preserved as the canonical reference per existing spec usage) to reset MFA; alternative: another `org_admin` may re-grant `billing_admin` to themselves and proceed.

#### 5.2.1.6 Acceptance Criteria

1. The `billing_admin` role MUST be enumerated in Appendix J Global Organization Roles; a deploy-time validator asserts the enum contains `billing_admin`.
2. Granting `billing_admin` MUST require the caller to hold `org_owner` OR `org_admin`; HTTP 403 `role_grant_requires_org_admin` otherwise.
3. Granting `billing_admin` MUST be idempotent: re-granting to a user who already holds the role returns HTTP 200 with no audit event re-emit.
4. Revoking `billing_admin` MUST emit `org.billing_admin_role_revoked`; if the revocation reduces the active Billing Admin count to zero AND there is no `org_owner` for the Org, the revocation MUST be rejected with HTTP 422 `billing_admin_revocation_would_leave_org_unmanaged`.
5. Every Permission List operation in §5.2.1.1 MUST emit its declared audit action on success; failure paths emit `<action>` with `status=failure` and `failure_reason`. QA test `billing_admin_audit_completeness` asserts no operation can succeed without a paired audit event.
6. The Billing Admin Audit View MUST exclude all non-billing audit rows; QA test `billing_admin_audit_view_isolation` asserts that workspace, response, score, KB, and capability-declaration audit rows never appear in the view regardless of filter parameters.
7. Cross-Org access attempts by a `billing_admin` MUST return HTTP 404 (not 403); QA test `billing_admin_cross_org_404` asserts.
8. Workspace-data access attempts (any of the explicit non-permissions in §5.2.1.1) MUST return HTTP 403 `billing_admin_role_insufficient`; QA test `billing_admin_workspace_403` asserts.
9. The Org Owner's de facto Billing Admin authority MUST hold even when the Org has zero `billing_admin` users; QA test `org_owner_billing_fallback` asserts.
10. The 50% / 80% / 100% wallet notifications MUST be delivered to the union of `org_owner` and `billing_admin` users; recipient deduplication MUST occur at dispatch time; QA test `wallet_notification_recipient_union` asserts.
11. The Billing Admin role MUST be assignable to a user holding `org_admin` simultaneously; the union-of-permissions principle holds; QA test `dual_role_org_admin_billing_admin` asserts both role's permissions are active.
12. The Billing Admin role MUST NOT be inherited by `org_owner` or `org_admin`; explicit assignment is required for billing-admin-ONLY operations (Operation #9 file ContestRecord, Operation #11 withdraw ContestRecord) — except that `org_owner` retains the de facto fallback per §5.2.1.2 Replacement Pattern; QA test `billing_admin_role_non_inherited` asserts the matrix.
13. Pinning a PricingTableVersion MUST stamp `org.pricing_table_version_pinned` with `version_label` in the `changes` payload; unpinning MUST emit `org.pricing_table_version_unpinned`.
14. The role MUST be removable by Org Owner or Org Admin without requiring confirmation flows (no soft-delete, no archived state — the role is an active assignment that is either present or absent); deletion is the audit event `org.billing_admin_role_revoked`.
15. SCIM mapping (when opted in) MUST follow the same audit semantics; auto-grants from SCIM MUST stamp `org.billing_admin_role_granted_via_scim` (subset of `org.billing_admin_role_granted` for filter convenience).
16. The Audit Event write-time validator at §4.6.1 MUST accept the union of the bare-verb enum and the `billing_admin_action` qualified namespace per the extension note in Appendix J → Audit Event Action Types. Writes presenting a mismatched namespace for the given `entity_type` MUST return HTTP 422 `audit_event_action_namespace_mismatch` (Appendix I). QA test `audit_event_action_enum_union_validator` asserts all three branches: (a) valid qualified action on billing `entity_type` succeeds; (b) bare verb on billing `entity_type` fails with namespace-mismatch; (c) qualified action on non-billing `entity_type` fails with namespace-mismatch.
17. The deploy-time audit-vocabulary drift validator at Appendix J MUST assert: (a) every audit action emitted by §5.2.1.1 Permission List Operations is registered in Billing Admin Audit Action Types; (b) every registry entry is emitted by at least one code path (no dead-code entries); (c) the bare-verb enum contains no dotted strings; (d) the qualified namespace contains no bare verbs. Build MUST fail on drift. QA CI job `audit_vocabulary_drift` asserts.

#### 5.2.1.7 Glossary Note

The term **Billing Admin** is added to Appendix K Glossary as: "Org-scoped role with billing-and-AI-accounting authority across both consoles. Orthogonal to `org_admin`. Required for filing ContestRecords, mutating wallet configuration, changing plan tier, and accepting Pro Trial Seat grants on the vendor side. See §5.2, §5.2.1, §4.8, §34.12.6, Appendix J Global Organization Roles." (Glossary canonicality: Appendix K is — and remains — the canonical Glossary per Phase 12.3 amendment; Appendix B is the Keyboard Shortcut Reference. CI gate `appendix_k_glossary_canonicality` asserts.)

### 5.2.2 Member Permission List (Operation-by-Operation) {#5.2.2-member-permission-list-operation-by-operation}

**Authoring intent (D-3.1-003 remediation, 2026-06-21).** The `member` role is the default low-privilege Org role, especially for SCIM-provisioned users before any §4.2.5 Group role assignment applies. It is intentionally narrower than `org_admin`, `billing_admin`, or any console role. `member` gives the user enough directory context to understand their Org membership and team assignments, but grants no billing, workspace-content, Seller Console, Marketplace publishing, security-configuration, or role-management authority by itself.

| # | Operation | Surface | RBAC Check | Audit Action |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Read own Organization summary | API: `GET /v1/organizations/me`; Convex: `org.current.get` | `role ∈ {org_owner, org_admin, billing_admin, member}` and `org_id=session.org_id` | `org.current_viewed` |
| 2 | Read own OrgMembership row | API: `GET /v1/organizations/me/membership`; Convex: `org.membership.self` | Same Org; subject user equals caller | `org.membership_self_viewed` |
| 3 | List visible Org members | API: `GET /v1/organizations/me/members`; Convex: `org.members.listVisible` | `role ∈ {org_owner, org_admin, member}`; response projection excludes billing roles, SSO attributes, SCIM raw group IDs, MFA recovery state, and deleted users | `org.member_directory_viewed` |
| 4 | Read own Team memberships | API: `GET /v1/teams/me`; Convex: `org.teams.selfList` | `role ∈ {org_owner, org_admin, member}`; returns only Teams containing caller | `org.team_membership_self_viewed` |
| 5 | List members of Teams containing caller | API: `GET /v1/teams/{team_id}/members`; Convex: `org.teams.memberList` | Caller is a member of `team_id` OR holds `org_owner` / `org_admin`; `member` projection hides role-assignment metadata | `org.team_member_directory_viewed` |
| 6 | Read own notification preferences | API: `GET /v1/notifications/preferences`; Convex: `notifications.preferences.get` | `user_id=session.user_id`; role-independent within active Org | `notification_preferences_viewed` |
| 7 | Update own notification preferences | API: `PATCH /v1/notifications/preferences`; Convex: `notifications.preferences.updateSelf` | `user_id=session.user_id`; cannot subscribe to events for surfaces not otherwise visible | `notification_preferences_updated` |
| 8 | Read personal profile fields mirrored from WorkOS | API: `GET /v1/users/me`; Convex: `users.self.get` | Subject user equals caller; excludes raw WorkOS attributes and admin-only forensic fields | `user_profile_self_viewed` |

**Explicit denials.** A user holding only `member` MUST receive HTTP 403 `member_role_permission_insufficient` on: workspace reads/writes unless the user also has a §5.3 Workspace Membership; Seller Console reads/writes unless a §5.5 Seller role grants them; any billing read/mutation; SSO / SCIM / MFA / domain governance configuration; Audit Event reads outside their own profile-level activity notifications; role grants or revocations; webhook endpoint CRUD; API token CRUD; Marketplace publisher actions; and Ops Console actions.

**SCIM default.** SCIM-provisioned users land as `member` only unless a WorkOS Group / §4.2.5 Group row maps them to another role. Group-based upgrades are additive under the §5.1 union-of-permissions rule and MUST be auditable as `org.scim_group_role_assigned`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Every operation in the Member Permission List MUST be covered by a role-check fixture in `member_role_permission_completeness`.
2. A `member` without a Workspace Membership MUST NOT read any Workspace, Use Case, Requirement, Response, Score, Selection Report, Bid Workspace, KB entry, Capability Declaration, or Seller Signal row.
3. A `member` without `billing_admin`, `org_owner`, or `org_admin` MUST NOT read AIWallet, AIOperation ledger, FreeAllowanceCounter, ContestRecord, CommittedSpendContract, BillingSeatSnapshot, PricingTableVersion pin state, or DowngradeExcessDataBucket.
4. A `member` who later receives `workspace_owner`, `workspace_admin`, `use_case_lead`, `reviewer`, or a Guest profile gains only that console-scoped role's permissions; the `member` role does not broaden the console scope.

## 5.3 Console-Level Roles (Buyer Console) {#5.3-console-level-roles-(buyer-console)}

**Role canonicality (D-3.1-006 / D-3.1-008 V3 remediation, 2026-05-04).** The §5.3 role names are normalized to the canonical Appendix J `workspace_role_kind` enum values used in §4.3.1 Workspace Membership and §5.11 Feature Access Matrix column headers. The pre-V3 names "Evaluation Lead", "Evaluator", "Scorer" are retired in favor of the canonical `workspace_admin`, `use_case_lead`, `reviewer` enums. Per-role glossary entries are landed in Appendix K Phase-3V cluster. CI gate `rbac_role_name_canonicality` (Appendix M.5 — new) asserts §5.3 / §5.5 / §5.6 row labels match Appendix J role enums.

| Role (canonical enum) | Workspace-Scoped | Responsibilities | Operation-level reference |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `workspace_owner` | Yes | Own & manage workspace, decide on vendors, final approval | §5.11 Feature Access Matrix `Workspace Owner` column. Full operation enumeration via §5.11 + per-feature §13.10 / §17.8 / §20.7 / §25.7 ACs. |
| `workspace_admin` | Yes | Oversee evaluation timeline, coordinate scorers, escalate issues; full requirement / response / score / phase mutation except `Delete workspace` and `Manage workspace team` | §5.11 `Workspace Admin` column. Pre-V3 name "Evaluation Lead" retired. |
| `use_case_lead` | Yes | Author requirements within assigned Use Cases, score (Phases 10–11), view responses, comment | §5.11 `Use Case Lead` column. Pre-V3 name "Evaluator" retired. |
| `reviewer` | Yes | Score vendor responses (Phases 10–11), provide rationale; cannot edit requirements | §5.11 `Reviewer` column. Pre-V3 name "Scorer" retired. |
| `guest` | Yes | Limited, configurable via Guest Permission Profile per §5.4 | §5.4 + §5.11 `Guest (read_only / contributor / scorer / full_participant)` columns. |

### 5.3.1 Buyer Console Role Permission Matrix (Operation-by-Operation) {#5.3.1-buyer-console-role-permission-matrix-operation-by-operation}

**Authoring intent (D-3.1-007 remediation, 2026-06-21).** This matrix turns the §5.3 Buyer Console role descriptions into operation-level grants. The §5.11 Feature Access Matrix remains the row-by-row canonical feature grid; this table is the compact build contract for role resolvers, API guards, Convex mutations, and audit actions.

| Operation | Surface | `workspace_owner` | `workspace_admin` | `use_case_lead` | `reviewer` | `guest` | Audit action |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Create Workspace shell | `POST /v1/workspaces` | n/a (Org operation; §5.2 / §5.11 governs) | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a | `workspace.created` |
| Edit Workspace settings | `PATCH /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}` | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | `workspace.settings_updated` |
| Delete / archive Workspace | `DELETE /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}` | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | `workspace.archived` |

| Transition Sourcera Method phase | `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/phase-transition` | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | `workspace.phase_transitioned` |
| Create / edit Use Case | §32 Workspace Use Case endpoints | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | `∈ profile` (`contributor`, `full_participant`) | `use_case.upserted` |
| Delete Use Case | §32 Workspace Use Case endpoints | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | `use_case.deleted` |
| Create / edit Requirement | §32 Requirement endpoints | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ (assigned Use Cases only) | ✗ | `∈ profile` (`contributor`, `full_participant`; assigned Use Cases only) | `requirement.upserted` |
| Delete Requirement | §32 Requirement endpoints | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | own authored requirement only when profile allows | `requirement.deleted` |
| View vendor Responses | §32 Response endpoints | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ (assigned Use Cases) | ✓ | `∈ profile` / assigned scope | `response.viewed` |
| Score Requirement in Phase 10-11 | §32 Scoring endpoints | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ (assigned Use Cases) | ✓ | `∈ profile` (`scorer`, `full_participant`) | `score.updated` |
| Lock / unlock score after Phase 12 | §32 Scoring endpoints | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | `score.lock_override` |
| Disqualify Target Account / vendor | §25.3 / §32 Target Account endpoints | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ (intersecting Use Cases only) | ✗ | ✗ | `target_account.disqualified` |

| Create / reply / resolve Internal Comment Thread | §25.7 / Comment Thread endpoints | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | `∈ profile` and visibility scope | `internal_comment_thread.changed` |

| View Selection Report | §13 / §35 Selection Report surfaces | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | `full_participant` only | `selection_report.viewed` |
| Export evaluation | §32 export endpoints | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | limited export for `full_participant` only | `evaluation.exported` |
| View Workspace audit log | §32 Audit Event endpoints scoped to Workspace | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | `audit_event.workspace_viewed` |
| Regenerate Defense View | §13.11 capability invocation | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | `defense_view.regenerated` |

**Guardrails.**

- `org_owner` and `org_admin` can create workspace shells per §5.2, but they do not automatically receive Workspace content access unless they also hold one of the Workspace roles above or the specific §5.11 row grants Org-level authority.
- `use_case_lead` scope is always computed from assigned Use Cases at request time. Empty assignment does not grant global workspace scope.
- `guest` grants always defer to §5.4 permission profiles and `assigned_use_case_ids`; no Guest profile can manage workspace team membership, phase transitions, audit logs, Defense View regeneration, or disqualification reversal.
- Every row above MUST be asserted by `buyer_console_role_permission_completeness`; the gate fails if §5.3 role labels, §5.11 cells, and endpoint RBAC predicates disagree.

## 5.4 Guest Role & Permission Profiles (Gap S-2) {#5.4-guest-role-&-permission-profiles-(gap-s-2)}

Guest is a **workspace-specific role** with **configurable permission profiles** assigned at invitation time. When inviting a Guest to a workspace, the Workspace Owner selects one of four permission profiles:

### 5.4.1 Guest Permission Profile: `read_only`

**Default profile. Maximum restrictions.**

| Capability | Allowed | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| View workspace name, description, phase | Yes | Read-only |
| View Use Cases (assigned only) | Yes | If in `assigned_use_case_ids` |
| View requirements (assigned only) | Yes | If Use Case assigned |
| View vendor responses | Yes | Read-only; assigned requirements only |
| View scores | Yes | Read-only summary; no individual scorer details |
| View Selection Report | No | Report access restricted to Workspace Owner only |
| Create/edit requirements | No |  |
| Delete requirements | No |  |
| Score requirements | No |  |
| Edit workspace settings | No |  |
| Manage team members | No |  |
| Export evaluation | No |  |
| View audit log | No |  |
| View/resolve comments | Yes | Can view and reply to comments; cannot delete others' comments |
| Add comments | Yes | Can comment on assigned requirements |

### 5.4.2 Guest Permission Profile: `contributor`

**Allows requirement authorship within assigned Use Cases.**

| Capability | Allowed | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (Includes all from `read_only`) | Yes |  |
| Create requirement in assigned Use Case | Yes | Must belong to assigned Use Cases |
| Edit requirement (own or any) | Yes | Within assigned Use Cases |
| Delete requirement (own only) | Yes | Within assigned Use Cases |
| View workspace configuration | Yes | Read-only |
| Score requirements | No | Use `scorer` profile for this |
| View Selection Report | No |  |
| Manage settings | No |  |

### 5.4.3 Guest Permission Profile: `scorer`

**Allows requirement scoring only; no authorship.**

| Capability | Allowed | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (Includes all from `read_only`) | Yes |  |
| Score requirements (Phases 10–11) | Yes | Cannot score before Phase 10 |
| Score requirements after Phase 11 (Phase 12\) | No | Scores locked at Phase 12 entry |
| Add score notes | Yes | Notes help explain scoring rationale |
| View score history | Yes | Limited to own scores and aggregated results |
| Create/edit requirements | No |  |
| Delete requirements | No |  |
| View Selection Report | No |  |

### 5.4.4 Guest Permission Profile: `full_participant`

**Combines contributor \+ scorer; maximum guest capability.**

| Capability | Allowed | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (Includes all from `contributor` \+ `scorer`) | Yes |  |
| View Selection Report | Yes | Can view final recommendation and rationale |
| Manage comments (own only) | Yes | Can edit/delete own comments |
| Export evaluation (limited) | Yes | Can export as PDF/CSV (not sensitive metadata) |
| (Workspace management, audit logs, etc.) | No | Still cannot manage workspace or see admin features |

### 5.4.5 Guest Scope Isolation

- **Use Case Scoping:** Guests assigned to specific Use Cases see only those Use Cases and their requirements (if assigned).  
- **Empty Assignment:** If `assigned_use_case_ids` is empty, guest can see all Use Cases and requirements (full visibility within permission profile).  
- **Workspace Isolation:** Guests cannot see other workspaces in the org; invitation is workspace-specific.  
- **Cross-Org:** Guest is always a single-org guest; cannot access other org workspaces.

**Guardrails.**

- Seller Org roles are additive under §5.1 but remain scoped to the Seller Console; they never grant Buyer Workspace content access.
- `seller_org_admin` is broad over Seller product operations but does not inherit seller billing mutation authority unless also granted `seller_billing_admin`.

- KB namespace scoping is evaluated before the role table grants mutate authority; `seller_kb_editor` may only mutate entries in assigned namespaces.
- Every row above MUST be asserted by `seller_console_role_permission_completeness`; the gate fails if §5.5, §5.11 overlays, Appendix J `seller_workspace_role`, and endpoint RBAC predicates disagree.

## 5.7 Scoring Availability (Gap 4.2, Gap 4.3) {#5.7-scoring-availability-(gap-4.2,-gap-4.3)}

**Critical Requirement:** Scoring is available in Phases 10 and 11\. Scores lock at Phase 12 entry.

| Phase | Activity | Scoring Allowed? | Score State |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1–9 (Planning, RFI, RFP, Responses, Demos) | Gathering information | No | N/A |
| **10 (Primary Scoring)** | Structured evaluation | **Yes** | Mutable; can be edited anytime in Phase 10 |
| **11 (Demo & Adjustments)** | Demo findings, score refinement | **Yes** | Mutable; can be edited anytime in Phase 11 |
| **12 (Close) onwards** | Selection, close | **No** | Immutable; locked at Phase 12 entry |

**Behavior (D-3.1-021 V3 remediation, 2026-05-04).**

- The canonical scoring-eligible roles per §5.11 row "Score requirement (Phase 10–11)" are `workspace_owner`, `workspace_admin`, `use_case_lead`, `reviewer`; the `guest` permission profiles `scorer` and `full_participant` are additionally eligible. The pre-V3 narrative names "Evaluators" and "Scorers" are retired in favor of the canonical Appendix J enum values. CI gate `rbac_role_name_canonicality` (per §5.3 V3 remediation) asserts.
- At Phase 12 entry, all scores become immutable (locked=true, read-only in UI, API enforces).  
- Attempting to edit a locked score results in: "Scores are locked in the Close phase. Unlock requires Workspace Owner approval."  
- Workspace Owner can unlock a single score (rare) but unlock triggers audit event and requires written justification.

## 5.8 Policy Ingestion Availability (Gap 4.3) {#5.8-policy-ingestion-availability-(gap-4.3)}

**Critical Requirement:** Policy Ingestion is available from Phase 1 day 1 with no prerequisites.

- Policy Ingestion (uploading knowledge base entries, compliance policies, vendor docs) can begin immediately upon workspace creation.  
- No gating on phases or prior evaluations.  
- Enables parallel preparation while other teams work on Use Cases / Requirements.

**Role gate (D-3.1-022 V3 remediation, 2026-05-04).** Policy Ingestion operations (`POST /v1/workspaces/{ws}/kb-entries`, `POST /v1/workspaces/{ws}/document-library/upload`) are restricted to `workspace_owner`, `workspace_admin`, `use_case_lead` per §5.11. `reviewer` and all guest profiles return HTTP 403 `policy_ingestion_role_insufficient`. Buyer-side Policy Ingestion is plan-gated per §34.1.1 cell **KB Document Library**; Seller-side per §22 KB authority + §34.1.2 cell **KB Document Library**.

## 5.9 Executive Sponsor (Gap S-7) {#5.9-executive-sponsor-(gap-s-7)}

**Definition:** Executive Sponsor is an **informal persona**, not an RBAC role. It is typically the Org Owner or Org Admin who receives escalation alerts via Evaluation Pulse (§20).

**Designation flow and forensic identifier (D-3.1-023 V3 remediation, 2026-05-04; extended V3+ 2026-05-04 with WorkOS `manager_id` predefined-attribute auto-derivation).** The Executive Sponsor is a **per-Workspace** designation set by the Workspace Owner at workspace creation OR via Settings → Workspace → Executive Sponsor. The designated user MUST hold `org_owner` OR `org_admin` on the same Org; designations referencing any other role return HTTP 422 `executive_sponsor_designation_role_invalid` (Appendix I Phase 3V — new).

**Auto-derivation cascade (V3+ remediation, 2026-05-04).** When no explicit Sponsor is designated, Sourcera auto-derives the Sponsor in this priority order:

1. **WorkOS `manager_id` chain** — walk the Workspace Owner's `User.manager_id` chain (per §4.2.3 V3+ predefined attribute) toward the root; the first manager whose role on the same Org is `org_owner` or `org_admin` auto-resolves as Sponsor. Manager-chain walks are bounded at 5 hops to prevent cycles in malformed directories.
2. **Most-senior Org Owner** — when (1) returns no candidate (manager chain breaks; manager has no Org membership; manager-chain depth exceeded), the most-senior (earliest `created_at`) `org_owner` of the same Org auto-resolves.
3. **Most-senior Org Admin fallback** — when the Org has zero `org_owner`s (deprovisioning race per §6.9.5), the most-senior `org_admin` auto-resolves; emits `org.executive_sponsor_org_owner_absent` Ops alert per §50 surface.

When the designated user is deprovisioned, the designation auto-falls-through to the cascade above. The forensic identifier for Pulse audit logs is `executive_sponsor_user_id_snapshot` on every Pulse event row — captured at event-emit time so historical Pulse events resolve the Sponsor identity even after subsequent designation changes. The auto-derivation source (`explicit` / `manager_chain` / `most_senior_org_owner` / `most_senior_org_admin_fallback`) is also captured in the event row for forensic clarity.

**Behavior.**

- Any `workspace_admin` (canonical name; pre-V3 "Evaluation Lead") can escalate an issue to the Executive Sponsor (see §20 Evaluation Pulse).  
- Escalation sends notification and adds Executive Sponsor to audience for that Pulse event.  
- Executive Sponsor is not a formal RBAC role in the system; governance is via audience designation on Pulse events plus the per-Workspace designation column above.

## 5.10 Active Workspace Definition (Gap S-7) {#5.10-active-workspace-definition-(gap-s-7)}

**Definition (D-3.1-024 V3 remediation, 2026-05-04).** An "Active Workspace" is one that meets BOTH criteria:

1. `Workspace.status` ∈ `{active}` per Appendix J `workspace_status` enum (Phase 3V cluster — values: `draft`, `active`, `suspended`, `closed`, `archived`); MUST NOT be `draft`, `suspended`, `closed`, or `archived`.
2. `Workspace.pipeline_phase` ∈ `{phase_1_stakeholder_alignment, phase_2_requirement_definition, phase_3_use_case_validation, phase_4_vendor_discovery, phase_5_vendor_outreach, phase_6_vendor_bidding, phase_7_response_refinement, phase_8_due_diligence, phase_9_final_clarifications, phase_10_team_scoring, phase_11_score_review, phase_12_selection, phase_13_contract_closure}` per Appendix J `pipeline_phase`; integer storage in `pipeline_stage_id` MUST resolve through the Appendix J Pipeline Phase Integer ↔ Enum Mapping table. Pre-V3 prose used the integer comparison `pipeline_stage_id < 13` and the retired pre-V4 12-phase enum, both of which silently coupled consumers to ordinal position.

**Usage:** Used in reporting (active vs. total workspaces), timeline forecasting, and Active Workspace KPI dashboards. The `workspace_status` enum is registered in Appendix J Phase 3V cluster; CI gate `workspace_status_canonical_consumer` asserts every active-workspace predicate consumes the enum, not the integer ordinal.

## 5.11 Feature Access Matrix (Comprehensive) {#5.11-feature-access-matrix-(comprehensive)}

**V3 Matrix Extension (D-3.2-001 / D-3.2-002 / D-3.2-003 / D-3.2-004 / D-3.2-005 / D-3.2-006 V3 remediation, 2026-05-04 — Authored Extensions AE-3.2-001 through AE-3.2-006, approved in the Phase 8 cluster ratification; §5.11.2 / §5.11.3 materialize the Seller and Marketplace overlays in-body).** The §5.11 matrix is extended along five structural dimensions:

1. **Min-Tier (Buyer) and Min-Tier (Seller) columns.** Every row carries a `Min Tier (Buyer)` and `Min Tier (Seller)` cell citing the canonical Appendix J `buyer_plan_tier` / `seller_plan_tier` enum value (e.g., `buyer_solo`, `business_growth`, `seller_scale`); blank cell denotes no plan-tier restriction beyond an active console plan, with `buyer_free` / `seller_free` included by default. This replaces the inline plan-tier strings tracked in the §14.9.1 27-location backlog. CI gate `appendix_j_plan_tier_inline_string_retired` (Appendix M.5 — new) asserts.
2. **Solo column (`buyer_solo` and `seller_solo`).** The pre-V3 Notes block declined to add a Solo column on the surface-compression rationale; the V3 extension adds explicit `buyer_solo` and `seller_solo` plan-tier handling to surface plan-gated entitlements (Verified eligibility, KB Bootstrap re-bootstrap, unwatermarked Selection Report, Direct Invite, etc.) that differ from `buyer_free` / `seller_free`. The `evaluation_owner_mode = solo` surface compression remains the per-Workspace driver per the existing Notes block; the new Solo column is the per-Org plan-tier dimension.
3. **Seller Console role overlay columns.** Seller Console row groups (Seller Signals, CRM Sync, Bid Workspace, KB) gain explicit columns for `seller_org_owner`, `seller_org_admin`, `seller_billing_admin`, `seller_marketing_editor`, `seller_kb_admin`, `seller_kb_editor`, `seller_kb_viewer`, `seller_bid_captain`, `seller_bid_contributor`, `seller_compliance_officer`, `seller_integrations_admin`, `seller_guest` per Appendix J Phase-3V `seller_workspace_role` enum. The pre-V3 Seller Console Role Overlay prose Note remains as the cross-reference home for the additive permission semantics.
4. **Marketplace role columns.** Marketplace row groups gain columns for `marketplace_publisher`, `marketplace_viewer`, `marketplace_public_reader` per Appendix J Phase-3V `marketplace_role` enum.
5. **Ops Console role columns.** Ops-managed row groups (M9–M13 editorial mechanics, Marketplace abuse review, Verification Tier review) gain columns for `ops_marketing_editor`, `ops_marketing_supervisor`, `ops_taxonomy_admin`, `ops_legal_takedown_admin`, `ops_marketing_finance_reviewer`, `ops_template_reviewer`, `ops_finance_admin` per Appendix J Phase-3V `ops_console_role` enum.

The body matrix below remains the canonical buyer-console role grid. The plan-tier dimension promised by AE-3.2-001 / AE-3.2-002 is materialized in-body by §5.11.4 rather than by widening the legacy role grid into thousands of cells. §5.11.4 is authoritative over stale inline display-plan wording; the CI gates `appendix_j_plan_tier_inline_string_retired` and `solo_role_grid_inclusion` assert the enum-form and Solo-inclusion contract.

**V3 Missing Rows Authored Inline (D-3.2-007 through D-3.2-023 V3 remediation, 2026-05-04 — appended below the existing row groups; Min-Tier columns cited in row labels per the V3 column extension above).**

**Acceptance-criteria coverage gate (Phase 13 inline fix F-5.1 — 2026-04-26).** Every gated row in this matrix resolves to a numbered Acceptance Criteria block in the row's owning feature section (§13.10, §14.9, §17.8, §20.7, §22.17, §25.3.13, §25.7.13, §27.4.x, §27.9.x, §31.7, §31.8, §31.9.x, §32.7, §32.8.23, §32.9.4, §33.9, §34.8.7, §34.20, §35.4, §36.4, §37.6, §38.5, §40.5, §41.5, §42.7, §43.5, §44.5, §45.4, §46.5, §47.5, §48.x AC blocks, §49.1.x AC blocks, §50.8 / §50.17 / §50.19, §51.8). Per Phase 12.3 closure (`_integration/PHASE12_3_VERIFY.md`), the cross-reference verdict is **PASS — all rows resolve**. The deploy-time validator `feature_access_to_acceptance_criteria` (Phase 13 follow-on) asserts this on every commit.

This matrix shows which roles can perform which actions across all major features. "✓" \= allowed; "✗" \= denied; "∈ scope" \= depends on assigned Use Cases or Grant; "✓ (filtered)" = scoped to a server-side filter (e.g., Billing Admin Audit View per §5.2.1.4); "✓ (read-only)" = permitted only for read operations and never for mutation; "✓ (fallback)" = held only when the Org has zero `billing_admin` users (§5.2.1.2 Replacement Pattern). Per §34.11.7 acceptance criterion 33, mutations on rows in the **Billing & AI Accounting** group are exclusive to `billing_admin` (with `org_owner` retaining the de facto fallback per §5.2.1.2). Per §5.2 and §5.2.1, `org_admin` has read-only billing visibility on the rows explicitly marked below and remains denied on every billing mutation. Member operations are not represented as a full extra column in this legacy 11-column grid; §5.2.2 is the authoritative operation-level Member overlay and `member_role_permission_completeness` verifies parity.

The default is a per-Workspace property, not a per-Org-tier permission gate; every plan tier may hold Workspaces in either mode, and the field is switchable per the row above. Plan downgrades and upgrades after Workspace creation do NOT auto-recompute this field; only the explicit `Switch Workspace evaluation_owner_mode` action does. Surface consequences (compressed pipeline UI, deadline-countdown affordance, optional stakeholder invites, suppression of multi-stakeholder SLA UI in `solo` mode; full multi-stakeholder surface in `team` mode) are authored in Phase 14.4. The literal enum string is never displayed to the user; Appendix M binds the surface metaphor.
- **Plan-tier overlay closure (Phase 3.2 residual closeout).** The prior Solo-exclusion posture is retired for plan-tier enforcement. `buyer_solo` and `seller_solo` are explicit plan-tier values in the §5.11.4 resolver, while `evaluation_owner_mode=solo` remains only the workspace-surface compression driver. Plan-tier feature access follows §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 / §34.8.5 / §39 authoritatively. Inline display-plan lists in row labels are non-authoritative citations only and MUST use Appendix J enum values when retained. CI gates `solo_role_grid_inclusion` and `appendix_j_plan_tier_inline_string_retired` assert this contract.

**Seller Console Role Overlay (§27.9, §31.9).** The 11 role columns in the table above are the Sourcera universal / Buyer Console role set. The **Seller Signals — Seller Console** and **CRM Sync — Seller Console** row groups introduce seller-console-scoped operations whose `✓` cells on `org_owner` denote the universal Org Owner role acting on a Seller-console Organization (Seller Orgs are Sourcera Organizations and therefore inherit `org_owner` as the universal top-of-tree). The Workspace / Use-Case / Guest columns are inapplicable for seller-console feature rows (shown as `n/a`) because the Seller Console does not model Bid Workspaces, Use Cases, Reviewers, or buyer-side Guest variants.

The following Seller Console sub-roles (defined in §5.2 and the enum `seller_console_role` in Appendix J) are **granted additive access on top of `org_owner`** and are enforced at the API layer via the seller-console role resolver (authored extension — requires human sign-off if §5.2 does not yet define `seller_integrations_admin`):

- `seller_org_admin` — Same access as `org_owner` on all rows in the **Seller Signals — Seller Console** and **CRM Sync — Seller Console** groups. Does NOT inherit billing rows unless also granted `billing_admin`.
- `seller_marketing_editor` — Read-only on SellerSignal Dashboard and SellerSignalDeliveryPreference; may NOT configure delivery preferences, send Direct Invites, or read SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink; may NOT mutate any CRM Sync row.
- `seller_integrations_admin` (new per §31.9.11) — Read-only on SellerSignal rows; full mutate access on all CRM Sync rows EXCEPT `seller_scale`+ customer-custom field mappings / custom routing-rule predicates (which remain `org_owner` / `seller_org_admin` only) and EXCEPT Disconnect CRMSyncConnection (which requires dual sign-off with `org_owner` or `seller_org_admin` per §31.9.11 operational safeguard). `seller_integrations_admin` MAY file Retry on failed CRMSyncActivityEvent rows and MAY Resolve Match in Review Queue.

`billing_admin` has **no** authority on any Seller Signals or CRM Sync row in this section; these are Product-Domain operations, not Billing-Domain. Plan-tier entitlement checks (`seller_scale`+ for Direct Invite; `seller_growth`+ for CRM Sync; `seller_scale`+ for customer-custom field mappings and custom routing predicates) are enforced at operation time per §34.1.2 and are **orthogonal** to the role grid: a role with `✓` may still receive a `402 plan_upgrade_required` error if the Org's Seller plan is below the required tier. Plan-tier gating is authoritatively defined in §34.1.2 Seller Plan Tiers and referenced — not restated — on the rows above.

Buyer Signal Opt-In rows (§27.9.2) are Buyer Console–scoped and use the existing Buyer Console role set. `org_owner` and `org_admin` may change org-level opt-in scope (this is an Org-wide privacy decision); `workspace_owner` may additionally pause contribution for a single workspace (scoped override). `billing_admin` has no authority on opt-in scope (not a billing operation). Guest variants are uniformly `✗` (opt-in decisions are non-delegable to guests).

## 5.12 Access Control Enforcement {#5.12-access-control-enforcement}

- **API-Level Enforcement:** All mutations and queries enforce RBAC at the Convex function level. No row-level data returned if user lacks access.  
- **UI-Level UX:** Features unavailable to role are hidden or disabled (not shown; no error message for security).  
- **Audit Logging:** All access (successful and failed) logged to Audit Event entity with user\_id, action, resource, timestamp, status.  
- **Permission Denied:** If user attempts unauthorized API call, 403 Forbidden returned (no details on reason).

## 5.13 WorkOS FGA Custom Roles & Groups Integration (V3+ remediation, 2026-05-04) {#5.13-workos-fga-custom-roles-and-groups-integration}

**Authoring intent (Authored Extension AE-3V-002 — pending Engineering + Security ratification).** WorkOS released two RBAC-relevant capabilities in April 2026 that materially affect Sourcera's authorization layer:

1. **FGA Custom Roles scoped to resource types (released 2026-04-21).** WorkOS Fine-Grained Authorization Custom Roles can now be scoped to specific resource types (e.g., `workspace`, `project`, `bid_workspace`) in addition to applying organization-wide. Refreshed dashboard UI for managing roles and permissions.
2. **Groups API (released 2026-04-22).** Named groups within an Organization that bundle Organization Memberships. Groups are first-class WorkOS-side entities with `create` / `update` / `delete` / `add_member` / `remove_member` / `list_members` / `list_groups_for_membership` endpoints. Group-based role assignment is announced as a future capability.

Sourcera's two-level RBAC model (Org-level + Console-level per §5.1) maps cleanly onto WorkOS FGA's resource-type-scoped Custom Roles. This sub-section authors the canonical mapping, the SCIM directory-group → role assignment precedence rule, and the Sourcera-side Group entity contract (per §4.2.5).

### 5.13.1 FGA Custom Role ↔ Sourcera Role Mapping

| Sourcera role enum | FGA `scope_type` | FGA scope target | Authority anchor |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `member`, `billing_admin` (§5.2) | `organization` | the Sourcera Org | Mapped 1:1 onto WorkOS Org-wide Custom Roles. |
| `workspace_owner`, `workspace_admin`, `use_case_lead`, `reviewer`, `guest` (§5.3 / §4.3.1) | `workspace` | the §4.3.1 Workspace | Mapped onto WorkOS FGA Custom Roles scoped to the `workspace` resource type. Per-Workspace assignment via §4.3.1 Workspace Membership table. |
| `seller_org_owner`, `seller_org_admin`, `seller_billing_admin`, `seller_marketing_editor`, `seller_kb_admin`, `seller_kb_editor`, `seller_kb_viewer`, `seller_compliance_officer`, `seller_integrations_admin` (§5.5) | `organization` (Seller-Org-scoped) | the Seller-side Sourcera Org | Mapped onto WorkOS Org-wide Custom Roles within Seller Orgs. |
| `seller_bid_captain`, `seller_bid_contributor`, `seller_kb_viewer` (per Bid Workspace), `seller_guest` (§5.5) | `bid_workspace` | the §4.4 Bid Workspace | Mapped onto WorkOS FGA Custom Roles scoped to the `bid_workspace` resource type. Per-Bid-Workspace assignment via the Bid Workspace Membership table (§4.4.1). |
| `marketplace_publisher` (§5.6) | `organization` (Seller-Org-scoped) | the Seller Org publishing the listing | Mapped onto WorkOS Org-wide Custom Roles. |
| `marketplace_viewer` (§5.6) | `organization` (Buyer-Org-scoped) | the Buyer Org browsing | Mapped onto WorkOS Org-wide Custom Roles within Buyer Orgs. |
| `marketplace_public_reader` (synthetic per §5.6 V3 disambiguation) | none — anonymous | none | NOT a WorkOS-managed identity; resolved at the §32.4.5 `marketplace_public_unauth` rate-limiter layer; no FGA assignment. |
| `ops_*` roles (per §50 / Phase-3V `ops_console_role` enum) | platform-wide | the Sourcera platform | Mapped onto WorkOS Org-wide Custom Roles within the internal Sourcera-Ops Org (`org_id = SOURCERA_OPS_ORG`); not visible to customer Orgs. |

CI gate `fga_custom_role_scope_canonical_consumer` (§M.5 — new) asserts every Sourcera RBAC role enum value declares an FGA `scope_type` from Appendix J Phase-3V `fga_custom_role_scope_type` enum (`organization`, `workspace`, `bid_workspace`, `marketplace`, `platform`).

### 5.13.2 SCIM Directory-Group → Role Assignment Precedence

Per the WorkOS April 2026 contract, **directory-group role assignments take precedence over SSO group role assignments** when both fire on the same Organization Membership. Sourcera honors this contract:

1. SCIM `user_created` or `user_updated` webhook fires; the user's directory groups are mirrored to §4.2.2 OrgMembership.`workos_group_ids` and §4.2.5 Group rows.
2. For every Group with a non-null `assigned_role_slug`, Sourcera applies the role to the member's OrgMembership (or to the appropriate per-Workspace / per-Bid-Workspace membership row if the role's `assigned_role_scope` is `workspace` / `bid_workspace`).
3. If the same member also has SSO-assertion-driven group claims (legacy SSO group role assignment), the SCIM directory-group role takes precedence; the SSO claim is logged but ignored.
4. CI gate `workos_directory_group_role_assignment_precedence` (§M.5 — new) asserts.

### 5.13.3 Group-Based Role Assignment (Future WorkOS Capability)

WorkOS announced group-based role assignment as a future capability in the 2026-04-22 release notes. Sourcera's §4.2.5 Group entity is designed to absorb this capability when it lands: the `assigned_role_slug` and `assigned_role_scope` fields already model the binding. When WorkOS ships the group-based assignment endpoint, Sourcera's SCIM webhook handler will auto-consume the WorkOS-side bindings and reflect them on the Sourcera-side Group row without requiring a customer-Org-managed mapping. Until then, the customer-Org Admin sets `assigned_role_slug` via Sourcera UI → WorkOS API call.

### 5.13.4 WorkOS Predefined Attributes Consumption

The April 2026 WorkOS Predefined Attributes (`display_name`, `employee_number`, `manager_name`, `manager_id`, `phone_numbers`, `organization`) are consumed by Sourcera per §4.2.3 User entity V3+ extension. Specific RBAC consequences:

- **Executive Sponsor auto-derivation (D-3.1-023 V3 cross-reference).** When no explicit Sponsor is designated and the Workspace Owner has a `manager_id` whose role on the same Org is `org_owner` or `org_admin`, the manager auto-resolves as Sponsor. The fall-through-to-most-senior-Org-Owner rule per §5.9 V3 still applies if the manager chain breaks.
- **`organization_attribute` (department) for forensic Audit Event projections.** Org Admin Audit Surface may filter audit rows by actor's `organization_attribute` to investigate "all actions by Procurement-team members in the last 90 days." Read-only at the Audit Surface; not a permission gate.
- **`employee_number`** is surfaced in the Org Admin Audit Surface only; never displayed to other consoles or Marketplace surfaces.
- **`raw_attributes` deprecation (effective 2026-04-15).** Sourcera MUST NOT consume `raw_attributes`; CI gate `workos_raw_attributes_not_consumed`. Error code `workos_raw_attributes_consumption_forbidden` (HTTP 422).

### 5.13.5 Acceptance Criteria

1. Every Sourcera RBAC role enum value MUST declare an FGA `scope_type` per §5.13.1; CI gate `fga_custom_role_scope_canonical_consumer` asserts.
2. SCIM directory-group role assignments MUST take precedence over SSO group role assignments per the WorkOS April 2026 contract; CI gate `workos_directory_group_role_assignment_precedence` asserts via property test.
3. WorkOS Groups API webhooks MUST be reflected on §4.2.5 Group rows within 60 seconds of delivery; CI gate `workos_groups_api_membership_consistency` (paired with §4.2.5 AC #1).
4. Sourcera MUST NOT consume `raw_attributes`; CI gate `workos_raw_attributes_not_consumed` asserts via static-analysis property test.
5. WorkOS Predefined Attributes (`display_name`, `employee_number`, `manager_id`, `manager_name`, `phone_numbers`, `organization`) MUST be populated on the §4.2.3 User row from the SCIM webhook handler within 60 seconds of delivery; CI gate `workos_predefined_attributes_consumed` asserts.
6. Group deletion cascade per §4.2.5 state machine MUST revoke role assignments within 60 seconds; emits `org.group_deleted` + per-member `org.role_revoked_via_group_deletion` AuditEvents.

### 5.13.6 Failure Modes

1. **WorkOS Groups API outage during SCIM-driven role provisioning.** Resolution: SCIM webhook handler buffers role assignments per the §4.2.5 Failure Mode #1; Sourcera continues to operate under cached Group state. Customer-Org Admin notified via `org.workos_groups_api_outage` (Appendix C — paired with `console_bridge.dlq_storm`-class detector at §4.2.5 v7.1.1 follow-on).
2. **Customer-Org sets `assigned_role_slug` to a value that becomes invalid after a future Sourcera RBAC enum retirement.** Resolution: HTTP 422 `group_assigned_role_slug_invalid`; Ops alert; member OrgMemberships continue under prior role until Org Admin re-binds.
3. **WorkOS-side Group renamed concurrently with Sourcera-side rename.** Resolution: WorkOS is source of truth; last-write-wins on the WorkOS side per §4.2.5 Failure Mode #3.
4. **Subject submits DSAR while a member of multiple Groups across multiple Orgs.** Resolution: §6.8.4 cascade walker iterates the subject's `workos_group_ids` and removes them from each Group via `remove_group_member` API call; Pattern B applied per §6.8.4.1; member-removal events DLQ if WorkOS API unavailable.
5. **Customer-Org grants `marketplace_publisher` to a buyer-Org Group via `assigned_role_slug` mis-binding.** Resolution: HTTP 422 `marketplace_publisher_buyer_org_grant_invalid` per §5.6 V3; member-rebinding required.
