### 6.8.4.4 Marketplace-Aggregate Cascade Trigger (D-9.2-007 V9 remediation, 2026-05-09) {#6.8.4.4-marketplace-aggregate-cascade-trigger}

**Authoring intent.** §6.8.4 fan-out Class 5 routed "aggregated signal rows" to §6.8.5 for retention treatment but did not invoke the §4.4.18 / §4.4.12 / §4.4.15 / §4.4.16 entity-level k-anon recompute paths. The 24-hour nightly sweep was the only mechanism — meaning a deprovisioned subject's signal continued to be visible on the seller-Marketplace surface for up to 24 hours after `dsar.cascade.row_redacted` fired. The 24-hour window is a **cross-firewall PII residue on a binding GDPR Art. 17 right-to-erasure obligation** — the seller console renders the buyer subject's contribution to the cohort even though the subject has been erased buyer-side. §6.8.4.4 elevates the recompute path to a synchronous cascade-trigger.

**Synchronous recompute trigger.**

The cascade walker, on resolving a Class 5 aggregate row in the cascade plan, emits `dsar.cascade.aggregate_recompute_required` once per affected cohort tuple:

```
cohort_tuple = (
  category_id,                  // §4.4.7 Marketplace Category
  region_code,                  // residency-bound: us / eu / apac / custom
  industry_code,                // §4.4.7 industry classification
  company_size_band             // §4.4.18 standard cohort dimension
)
```

The recompute target set is computed from the subject's contributing-buyer footprint:

| Entity | Contributing-buyer column | Recompute scope |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| §4.4.18 SellerSignal | `contributing_buyer_user_ids[]` (or sharded link table) | Every SellerSignal row for which the subject is in the contributing array. |
| §4.4.12 CategoryPage | Cohort-membership join on Buyer Org membership | Every CategoryPage cell for which the subject's Org contributes. |
| §4.4.15 MarketIntelligenceReport | Cohort-membership join | Every MarketIntelligenceReport cell. |
| §4.4.16 HeatMapCell | Cohort-membership join | Every HeatMapCell row in the affected cohort. |

Recompute is **synchronous** — the cascade does not advance to `dsar.cascade.row_redacted` until the per-cohort recompute completes. Synchronous SLO: P99 ≤ 60 seconds per cohort tuple (Convex serverless invocation; Convex `cohortRecompute.ts` mutation).

**Suppression on floor breach.**

For each recomputed cohort:

- If post-recompute cohort size < `k_anon_floor` (per-entity floor: §4.4.12 k=5; §4.4.16 k=10; §4.4.15 k=20; §4.4.18 k=5 / effective floor 10–20 per de-anonymization context — registered in §39 per D-9.2-008 v7.1.1 backlog), the cell transitions to `suppressed` immediately within the cascade transaction.
- The seller-side render path returns "Insufficient data" (§4.4.16 suppressed-cell pattern) on the next request after cascade-completion.
- A cascade-emitted `dsar.cascade.aggregate_recompute_completed` event carries `suppressed_cell_count` and `recomputed_cell_count` per cohort tuple.

**Retention class.**

§6.8.5 is extended with row #16 (V9 remediation; AE-V9-01) — "Marketplace and Signal Aggregates":

| # | Row Class | Retention Driver | Retention Window | Redaction Treatment |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 16 | Marketplace and Signal Aggregates (CategoryPage §4.4.12, HeatMapCell §4.4.16, MarketIntelligenceReport §4.4.15, SellerSignal §4.4.18) | Cohort-anonymized public surface; cohort recompute on every contributing-buyer DSAR | Per-entity per §40.2 (CategoryPage / GuidePage / ComparisonPage = Platform-life; MarketIntelligenceReport = Platform-life with 8-quarter auto-archive; HeatMapCell = 24m raw; SellerSignal = 180d raw) | Identity FKs already absent at row level; cascade synchronous recompute per §6.8.4.4 with cohort suppression on k-anon floor breach |

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Cascade walker MUST emit `dsar.cascade.aggregate_recompute_required` per affected cohort tuple before advancing to `dsar.cascade.row_redacted`. CI gate `dsar_cascade_aggregate_recompute_synchronous` (Appendix M.5 — new) asserts via cascade-transaction property test.
2. Per-cohort recompute MUST complete within P99 ≤ 60 seconds; SLO violation triggers Datadog alarm `dsar_cascade_aggregate_recompute_p99_breach` and routes the cascade through §6.8.4.6 partial-failure path.
3. Cohort recompute results in suppression when post-recompute cohort size < per-entity `k_anon_floor`; CI gate `dsar_cascade_aggregate_recompute_suppression_completeness` asserts via QA test.
4. Recompute failure (Convex mutation transient error, dependency outage) emits `dsar_cascade_aggregate_recompute_failed` (Appendix I — new; HTTP 503) and routes to §6.8.4.6 partial-failure path; the cascade does NOT advance to `dsar.cascade.row_redacted` on an unresolved aggregate failure.
5. The §4.4.18 / §4.4.12 / §4.4.15 / §4.4.16 nightly sweep continues to run as a defense-in-depth backstop but is no longer the primary mechanism; nightly sweep emits `dsar_cascade_aggregate_recompute_backstop_drift` Datadog metric if it finds a cohort that the synchronous trigger should already have suppressed.

### 6.8.4.5 Bridge-Event Body Text PII Sweep (D-9.2-009 V9 remediation, 2026-05-09) {#6.8.4.5-bridge-event-body-text-pii-sweep}

**Authoring intent.** §4.7.1.1 cascade walker filtered `payload_json` fields "for every field carrying a User reference … filter for occurrences where the value equals the subject's identifier (id, email, role-snapshot composite) and pseudonymize in-place." Buyer-authored free-text fields (`payload_json.body_markdown` for `qa_thread_post_appended`, `payload_json.amendment_diff_summary` for `requirement_amended`, `payload_json.reason_snippet` for `requirement_reverted`, etc.) routinely contain subject self-identification ("I'm Jane Doe at Acme — please clarify Q3"). The pre-V9 walker matched only structured FK columns and structured-equal matches against subject identifiers — unstructured prose containing the subject's name persisted on the cross-firewall surface (the seller console) post-DSAR. **§6.8.4.5 closes the cross-firewall PII residue.**

**Body-scan invocation.**

The cascade walker, on resolving a Console Bridge Event row in the cascade plan, invokes the §48.4.4 PII detector pipeline on every `payload_json` free-text field per the kind-specific `Fields CARRIED` registry at §4.7.1 (line 7889+). The PII detector is the existing `claude-haiku-4-5` content-validators pipeline used for Public Selection Reports, watermark text, and email custom messages — extended in V9 to cover bridge-event body text. The detector returns a PII-span report:

```json
{
  "spans": [
    {"start": 0, "end": 12, "kind": "person_name", "confidence": 0.98, "matched_text": "I'm Jane Doe"},
    {"start": 17, "end": 22, "kind": "org_name", "confidence": 0.95, "matched_text": "Acme"}
  ]
}
```

Detected subject-PII spans are replaced with the `[REDACTED_DSAR]` sentinel in the in-place `payload_json` mutation; the `redaction_verification_hash` is recomputed per §4.7.1.1.

**Sweep scope.**

The sweep covers every bridge-event kind whose `Fields CARRIED` list at §4.7.1 line 7889+ includes a free-text field. The seed-set at v7.1.1 (extensible via Appendix C amendment):

| Bridge event kind | Free-text fields scanned |
| :---- | :---- |
| `qa_thread_post_appended` | `body_markdown` |
| `requirement_amended` | `amendment_diff_summary` |
| `requirement_reverted` | `reason_snippet` |
| `buyer_comment_visible_to_vendor` | `body_markdown` |
| `eoi_acceptance_propagated` | `acceptance_note` |
| `amendment_broadcast` | `broadcast_note` |
| `disqualification_propagated` | `disqualification_rationale_redacted_to_seller` |

(New bridge-event kinds added in v7.1.x trigger the `bridge_event_body_pii_sweep_completeness` CI gate.)

**False-positive safeguard.**

The PII detector's confidence threshold for redaction is 0.90 (matching §48.4.4 default). Sub-threshold spans are NOT redacted; they are emitted as `dsar_cascade_bridge_body_pii_sub_threshold_finding` Datadog metrics for Ops review. Ops can elevate a sub-threshold pattern via `ops_pii_detector_confidence_override` workflow (§48.4.4 amendment). Spans matched against a known organization name in the buyer's Org Name registry are auto-elevated regardless of confidence.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Cascade walker MUST invoke §48.4.4 PII detector on every free-text field listed in §6.8.4.5 sweep scope for every bridge-event row in the cascade plan. CI gate `dsar_cascade_bridge_payload_body_pii_sweep_completeness` (Appendix M.5 — new) asserts via cascade-transaction property test.
2. Detected PII spans at confidence ≥ 0.90 MUST be replaced with `[REDACTED_DSAR]` sentinel; `redaction_verification_hash` MUST be recomputed; CI gate `dsar_cascade_bridge_redaction_hash_recompute` asserts.
3. Sub-threshold spans MUST emit `dsar_cascade_bridge_body_pii_sub_threshold_finding` Datadog metric; metric values are routed to the `dsar-ops` PagerDuty queue at SEV-3 for nightly review.
4. PII detector unavailable (Anthropic outage, §22.8 `anthropic_mcp_degraded` state) MUST route the cascade through §6.8.4.6 partial-failure path with `dsar_cascade_body_pii_sweep_failed` (Appendix I — new; HTTP 503); the cascade does NOT advance to `dsar.cascade.row_redacted` on an unresolved sweep failure.
5. New bridge-event kinds added to §4.7.1 redaction matrix MUST be evaluated for §6.8.4.5 inclusion at authoring time; CI gate `bridge_event_body_pii_sweep_completeness` (§M.5 — new) asserts every kind with a free-text field in `Fields CARRIED` appears in the §6.8.4.5 sweep-scope table OR carries an explicit "non-PII-bearing" attestation.
6. Buyer-side body-redaction sweep (§6.8.4.5) and seller-side body-redaction sweep (§22.3.1 third-party body-redaction sweep, D-3.5-012 V3 remediation) MUST produce a structurally-symmetric `redaction_state` post-cascade; QA test `bridge_payload_body_pii_sweep_buyer_seller_parity` asserts.

### 6.8.4.6 Partial-Failure Procedure (D-9.2-011 V9 remediation, 2026-05-09) {#6.8.4.6-partial-failure-procedure}

**Authoring intent.** §6.8.4 AC #4 declared partial-failure pause is forward-recovery only; §6.8.6 SLA row at line 10387 carved out the §6.8.4 partial-failure path with a phantom "§6.8.4 partial-failure procedure timeline" that did not exist. A paused cascade could exceed the 30-day GDPR Art. 12(3) statutory ceiling indefinitely. **§6.8.4.6 authors the procedure.**

**Trigger.**

The cascade walker emits `dsar.cascade.partial_failure` (Appendix C — new V9 row) on:

- Per-row pseudonymization or hard-delete failure that exceeds the standard retry curve (§6.8.4.5 / §6.8.4.4 dependency outages; Convex serializable-transaction conflict exceeds 5 retries).
- §6.8.4.4 aggregate recompute failure on more than 1% of affected cohort tuples.
- §6.8.4.5 body-PII sweep failure on more than 0.5% of bridge-event rows in the cascade plan.
- §6.8.4.2 mid-cascade residency change requiring DPO approval (the DPO approval is treated as an Ops-review event under this procedure).

**Pause and Ops-page.**

- The cascade transitions to `state = paused_partial_failure` with `pause_started_at` stamped.
- A PagerDuty page is raised on the `dsar-ops` queue at SEV-2 within 60 seconds of pause.
- The Ops responder's review SLA is **24 hours from `pause_started_at`** to `dsar.cascade.resume` OR escalation per §6.8.6 extension path.
- Failure to resume within the 24-hour SLA fires `dsar_cascade_partial_failure_sla_breach` (Appendix I — new; HTTP 503) Datadog alarm at SEV-1 and pages on the `dsar-ops-escalation` queue (Privacy Officer + Engineering Director on rotation).

**Resume protocol.**

`dsar.cascade.resume` is emitted by Ops with:

```
{
  "actor_user_id": "<ops_user_id>",
  "ops_session_id": "<ops_session_id>",
  "rationale": "<free-text remediation rationale>",
  "remediation_action": "<retry_failed_rows | skip_rows_with_documented_exemption | abort_to_extension_path>",
  "audit_event_id": "<audit_event_id>"
}
```

`actor_user_id` MUST be an `ops_dsar_admin` role (Appendix J `dsar_partial_failure_resume_actor` enum — new V9 row). Single-signoff is sufficient for `retry_failed_rows`; dual-signoff is required for `skip_rows_with_documented_exemption` (the second signer cannot be the original triage actor; same separation-of-duties rule as §6.8.6.2 manifestly-unfounded path). `abort_to_extension_path` triggers §6.8.6 +60-day extension with subject notification per Art. 12(3) controller-extension requirement.

The cascade resumes from the per-row `dsar_redacted_under_request_id` marker (§4.6.5 + per-cascade-target entity column added in this remediation pass; D-9.2-002 P1 simultaneously closed). Re-running the same plan post-resume is idempotent at the per-row level; the marker prevents double-redaction and the §6.8.4.5 hash recompute is skipped if the row's `dsar_redacted_under_request_id = $request_id` already.

**Hard ceiling — statutory-window cumulative-pause invariant.**

Cumulative pause time across all `paused_partial_failure` transitions for a given DSAR MUST NOT exceed (§6.8.6 30-day SLA + §6.8.6 +60-day extension) − active-walking time. Concretely: when cumulative pause-duration would breach the 30-day window, the cascade auto-escalates to §6.8.6 extension path; subject is notified within 72h of the auto-escalation per Art. 12(3); the extension grants up to 60 additional calendar days. When cumulative pause + active-walking time would breach 90 days from `received_at`, the cascade is **administratively closed** with a `dsar_cascade_administratively_closed` audit event, the supervisory authority notification path is opened, and the subject is informed of their lodging-with-supervisory-authority right (§6.8.6.2 line 10458 cross-link).

**Cross-link to §6.8.4.2 mid-residency-change DPO approval.**

§6.8.4.2 AC #2 (DPO approval pause for mid-cascade residency change) is governed by §6.8.4.6 procedure. DPO approval is treated as an Ops-review event with the same 24-hour SLA, the same resume protocol, and the same statutory-window cumulative-pause invariant. The DPO is mapped to the `ops_dpo_admin` role (Appendix J) and counts as a single signer for `retry_failed_rows` and as one of the two required signers for `skip_rows_with_documented_exemption`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. `dsar.cascade.partial_failure` MUST be emitted within 60 seconds of cascade pause; PagerDuty page MUST raise SEV-2 on `dsar-ops` queue. CI gate `dsar_cascade_partial_failure_pagerduty_sla` (Appendix M.5 — new) asserts via Datadog synthetic test.
2. Ops-review resume SLA is 24 hours from `pause_started_at`; SLA breach fires `dsar_cascade_partial_failure_sla_breach` Datadog alarm SEV-1 and pages `dsar-ops-escalation`. CI gate `dsar_cascade_partial_failure_resume_sla_24h` (Appendix M.5 — new) asserts.
3. `dsar.cascade.resume` MUST carry `actor_user_id`, `ops_session_id`, `rationale`, `remediation_action`, `audit_event_id`; missing fields rejected with `dsar_cascade_resume_missing_required_fields` (Appendix I — new; HTTP 422).
4. `remediation_action = skip_rows_with_documented_exemption` MUST require dual-signoff (separation of duties; second signer ≠ original triage actor); single-signoff rejected with `dsar_cascade_resume_dual_signoff_required` (Appendix I — new; HTTP 403).
5. Cumulative pause-duration breach of the 30-day SLA MUST auto-escalate to §6.8.6 extension path with subject notification within 72h; cumulative breach of 90-day statutory ceiling MUST administratively close the cascade and open the supervisory-authority notification path. CI gate `dsar_cascade_statutory_ceiling_auto_escalation` (Appendix M.5 — new) asserts via QA test.
6. Per-row idempotency marker (`dsar_redacted_under_request_id` UUID FK + `dsar_redacted_at` Timestamp) MUST be present on every cascade-target entity registered in §6.8.4.3. CI gate `dsar_cascade_per_row_idempotency_marker_completeness` (Appendix M.5 — new) asserts via static-analysis. Closes D-9.2-002 P1.
7. Salt-rotation re-pseudonymization (§6.8.5 AC #3) is governed by `pseudonym_epoch_id` semantics: cascade idempotency is bound to the active pseudonym epoch; cross-epoch re-runs are governed by §6.8.5 AC #3 re-pseudonymization workflow, NOT §6.8.4 cascade idempotency. DSARRequest (§4.6.5) carries `pseudonym_epoch_id_at_cascade`. CI gate `dsar_cascade_pseudonym_epoch_consistency` (Appendix M.5 — new) asserts. Closes D-9.2-005 P1.

### 6.8.4.7 Cross-Org and Org-Admin DSAR Fulfillment (v7.2.0-REM Phase 3.5 P1) {#6.8.4.7-cross-org-and-org-admin-dsar-fulfillment}

**Authoring intent.** The global User entity (§4.2.3) can be a member of multiple Orgs through §4.2.2 Membership rows. Pre-remediation DSAR prose described per-Org cascades but did not state whether subject-initiated erasure crossed every Org, whether Org Admins could initiate a controller-mediated request on behalf of a member, or how buyer/seller Console Bridge rows were walked. This subsection closes that operational gap.

**Cross-Org policy.**

| DSAR initiation path | Cascade scope | Controller / approval rule | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Subject signs in and requests access / rectification / portability / objection / automated-decision review | All Orgs where the User has an active or historical Membership row, plus platform-owned rows keyed directly to the User | Subject verification under §6.8.6.1 is sufficient; Org Admin approval is not required for the subject's own rights | Export partitions by Org and console inside one bundle; other-Org data is represented only where the subject is actor / author / assignee / signer. |
| Subject signs in and requests erasure / account closure | All Orgs where the User has a Membership row, except rows retained by §6.8.5 audit-integrity exemption | Subject verification under §6.8.6.1; each Org receives an Org-admin notice before Org-owned content attribution is pseudonymized | Org-owned IP remains retained under §6.8.2; identity-bearing fields are pseudonymized. |
| Org Admin initiates DSAR on behalf of a member | The initiating Org only | Org Admin must hold `org_admin` or stronger plus a DPO / Privacy Officer attestation field; subject receives notice and can object through §6.8.9 | Used when the customer Org is controller of record and Sourcera is processor under §45.1. |
| Org Admin initiates DSAR for a former member | The initiating Org only | Same as above; if the subject has no active login, notification uses last-known verified email and the §6.8.6.1 non-signed-in verification path | Does not cascade to unrelated Orgs where the User remains active. |
| Non-account-holder / third-party DSAR | Body text, attachment metadata, KB entries, verification docs, comments, Q&A, support tickets, and bridge payloads that name the verified subject | Ops-mediated `id_document_review` under §6.8.6.1 with dual sign-off | Does not pseudonymize Sourcera account-holder User rows; redacts named-person spans only. |

**Console Bridge traversal.** Cross-Org cascade walks Console Bridge Events exactly once per `(buyer_workspace_id, bid_workspace_id, subject_user_id, dsar_request_id)` tuple. Buyer-origin and seller-projected copies share the same `redaction_verification_hash`; the seller projection MUST NOT retain pre-redaction buyer identity after the buyer-side source row is pseudonymized. Duplicate bridge-event rows are idempotent on `dsar_redacted_under_request_id`.

**Org-admin fulfillment surface.** Org Admins initiate controller-mediated DSARs from Settings -> Privacy -> Member Data Request. The surface creates a DSARRequest with `created_by = <org_admin_user_id>`, `subject_user_id = <member_user_id>`, `org_id = <initiating_org_id>`, `request_origin = org_admin_on_behalf`, and `subject_notification_required = true`. The API contract is registered in §32 under `POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/dsar/initiate-on-behalf` (full endpoint authoring is tracked separately by D-3.5-020).

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Subject-initiated erasure MUST enumerate every Membership row for the User before cascade plan generation; CI gate `dsar_cross_org_membership_enumeration_complete` asserts.
2. Org-admin-on-behalf requests MUST be scoped to the initiating Org and MUST NOT mutate rows in other Orgs where the subject is also a member. Property test `dsar_org_admin_on_behalf_org_scope_isolation` asserts.
3. Every Org-admin-on-behalf request MUST notify the subject within the §6.8.6 acknowledgment window and expose objection / correction paths. QA test `dsar_org_admin_on_behalf_subject_notice` asserts.
4. Console Bridge cascade MUST process each buyer/seller tuple once and produce matching buyer-source and seller-projection redaction hashes. CI gate `dsar_console_bridge_cross_org_redaction_parity` asserts.
5. Third-party DSAR cascade MUST redact body spans and embedding references only; it MUST NOT pseudonymize account-holder User rows. Property test `dsar_third_party_cascade_account_holder_isolation` from §6.8.6.1 is extended to KB, Q&A, comments, verification docs, support tickets, and bridge payloads.

### 6.8.5 Audit-Integrity Exemption & Retention Override {#6.8.5-audit-integrity-exemption}

The §6.8 right-to-erasure regime carves out a narrow set of row classes that MUST be retained even under DSAR / right-to-erasure for audit, regulatory, financial-defense, and contract-defense purposes. The exemption is documented exhaustively here as the canonical target for the 17+ "per §6.8.5" body citations.

**Retained row classes.**

| # | Row Class | Retention Driver | Retention Window | Redaction Treatment |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | AuditEvent (§4.6.1) — all subtypes | SOC-2 audit trail; cross-namespace investigation; legal hold; subpoena response | 7 years from row create | User-attribution FKs pseudonymized to `anonymized_<console>_user_<hash>`; payload body retained verbatim |
| 2 | OpsActionRecord (§4.4.27) | Ops-action audit; impersonation history | 7 years | Same pseudonymization treatment; OpsSession ID retained |
| 3 | BillingLedgerEntry, AIOperation (§4.8.1), ContestRecord, CommittedSpendContract | SOC-2 financial controls; tax / accounting horizon; revenue-recognition restatement audit | 7 years (financial-record exception per §40.2) | Pseudonymization treatment per §6.8.4.1 Pattern B on the User-row target of: AIOperation `actor_id` (when `actor_type ∈ {user, ops}`); ContestRecord `filed_by_user_id`; CommittedSpendContract `signed_by_user_id`; BillingLedgerEntry `actor_id` / `attributed_user_id`. FK columns themselves are preserved; the resolving User rows are pseudonymized in-place per §6.8.4.1. AIOperation non-FK content-encoding columns `input_content_hash`, `output_content_hash`, `prompt_template_version` are scrubbed per §4.8.1 AC #12. Financial fields retained verbatim. **D-3.5-003 / D-3.5-016 V3 remediation, 2026-05-04** — pre-remediation row referenced the non-existent field `submitter_user_id` and ambiguous `accepter_user_id`; the canonical fields are listed verbatim above. |
| 4 | MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord (§4.8.12) | Cost-center isolation audit; FTC disclosure traceability | 7 years | Same as #3 |
| 5 | KBExportLifecycleAudit (§22.18.7) | Export-as-read invariant proof; downgrade-firewall investigation | Plan-tier retention per §40.2 (NOT the 7-year exemption) | Pseudonymization only |
| 6 | InternalCommentPost / InternalCommentMention rows linked to a finalized Selection Report or active legal hold | Buyer-Org evidentiary record; selection-rationale defense | Workspace-life + 7 years | Author pseudonymization; body retained |
| 7 | Vendor Disqualification Record (§4.7.2) and reversal rows | Buyer-vendor disqualification audit; legal-defense in disputed evaluations | 7 years | Pattern B on `rationale_author_user_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, and `reversed_by_user_id`; body-field redaction on `rationale_internal`, `notification_body_to_vendor`, `appeal_narrative`, `appeal_decision_note_internal`, `appeal_decision_note_vendor_visible`, and identity-bearing `cascade_actions_json` keys per §4.7.2.1; non-PII rationale / severity / appeal outcome retained |
| 8 | VendorOptOutRecord, VendorOptOutAuthorityAttestation (§27.10) | Opt-out authority chain; CAN-SPAM / GDPR DMA defense | Org-life + 7 years | Pseudonymization of `signed_by_user_id`, `attested_by_user_id`; attestation body retained |
| 9 | OutcomeContract (§4.8.4) — versioned snapshots | Contract-versioning provenance; settled-AIOperation classification audit | Active version + 7 years; superseded versions retained until the youngest dependent AIOperation expires retention, then +7 years | `authored_by` pseudonymized at supersession + 90 days; active-version author attribution pseudonymizes on DSAR; contract terms retained verbatim |
| 10 | SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink (§4.4.18) | EOI-or-direct-invite reveal traceability | Workspace-life + 7 years | Pseudonymization of `triggering_user_id`; cohort metadata retained |
| 11 | ReferralRecord (§4.3.16) — invite/accept history | Anti-fraud evidence; reward-recovery | Org-life | Pseudonymization of `referrer_user_id`; invite metadata retained |
| 12 | TimeSavedCredit (§4.3.19) — credit award history | Customer-billing dispute evidence | Org-life + 90d | Pseudonymization of `awarded_to_user_id`; quantity retained |
| 13 | EOIAcceptanceRecord (§4.4.18) | Marketplace consent chain; opt-out timing defense | Org-life + 7 years per §40.2 Marketplace consent / contract-defense row | Pseudonymization of `accepted_by`; intent and timing retained |
| 14 | NotificationFailureAudit (§29.5) operational rows; OpsSession customer-notification failure rows | SLA-breach investigation; Ops-Trust posture proof | NotificationFailureAudit raw rows: 90 days raw + 24 months aggregated; OpsSession customer-notification failure rows: 24 months; rows tied to classes #1-#13 inherit that retained-row class by reference | Raw rows pseudonymized; aggregates subject-redacted. Any request to retain operational failures beyond 24 months requires a documented legitimate-interest test. |
| 15 | All §31.8 billing-domain webhook delivery records | Customer accounting reconciliation; SOC-2 financial-impact-event audit | 90 days raw + 7 years aggregated | Same as #3 |

**Pseudonymization scheme.** A single deterministic hash (HMAC-SHA256 keyed by per-Org rotation salt) maps the original `user_id` to `anonymized_<console>_user_<base32(hash)[:16]>`. The hash is irreversible (the salt is rotated and the original ID destroyed). The hash is consistent across all rows for the same user / same Org / same rotation epoch — so audit chains remain navigable but the human identity is unrecoverable.

**DSAR notice obligation.** When a DSAR request encounters one or more retained rows, the cascade worker emits a `dsar.audit_integrity_exemption_invoked` AuditEvent with the row-class taxonomy hit, and the response to the requestor explicitly enumerates the exempted classes with retention windows. This satisfies GDPR Art. 17 §3(e) "necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims" disclosure.

**Reversibility.** None. The pseudonymization is irreversible by design. A subsequent court-ordered un-redaction is satisfied via OpsActionRecord trail — Sourcera CAN show "user X was active in this Org at this date" via the original AuditEvent timestamps + Org membership records (themselves pseudonymized but with retained membership row), but cannot reconstitute the original user identity.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Every retained row class above MUST have a deploy-time validator that asserts the redaction-path code matches the table's "Redaction Treatment" column. CI gate `audit_integrity_exemption_redaction_path_correctness`.
2. The DSAR worker MUST refuse to hard-delete rows in any retained class; an attempt MUST emit `dsar.audit_integrity_exemption_violation` and halt the cascade for Ops review.
3. The pseudonymization salt rotation epoch is documented in the §22.18.7 deploy-time validator catalog; rotation MUST trigger re-pseudonymization of all retained rows touching the rotated user_id within 7 days.
4. The retention windows in column 4 are authoritative; §40.2 cites this table for the financial-record exception and does NOT restate the values.

### 6.8.6 DSAR Operational SLA (Authoritative) {#6.8.6-dsar-operational-sla}

**Authoritative home for the DSAR fulfillment SLA.** Promoted from prose-distributed mentions in §6.8.1 / §6.8.2 / §6.8.3 / §33.4 in Phase 12.5 (R-01 closure). Prior to this subsection the "30-day" DSAR SLA appeared in ~15 places without a single canonical row.

| Phase of DSAR Fulfillment | SLA / Window | Source of Authority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Verified subject-request receipt → first acknowledgment to subject | \< 72 hours | GDPR Art. 12(3); CCPA §1798.130(a)(2) |
| Verified subject-request receipt → fulfillment (export OR confirmation of erasure path) | **\< 30 calendar days** | GDPR Art. 12(3); §33.4 |
| Extension trigger (complex / high-volume request) | One-time extension up to **+60 calendar days** with written reason recorded in `DSARRequest.extension_reason` | GDPR Art. 12(3); audit-eventable per §6.7 |
| Cascade fan-out completion (per §6.8.4) | \< 30 calendar days OR within the §6.8.4 partial-failure procedure timeline if `dsar.cascade.partial_failure` triggered | §6.8.4 |
| Audit-integrity-exempt rows (per §6.8.5) | Retained per §6.8.5 retention windows; pseudonymization MUST land within the 30-calendar-day SLA even though the underlying rows are not deleted | §6.8.5 |
| Subject-notification on cascade partial failure | \< 24 hours from `dsar.cascade.partial_failure` event | §6.8.4 #4 |

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. The DSAR worker MUST stamp `DSARRequest.fulfilled_at` no later than 30 calendar days from `DSARRequest.verified_at` unless `extension_reason` is non-NULL; in the latter case the ceiling is 90 calendar days. CI gate `dsar_30d_sla_observability` asserts via property test on a 10,000-record synthetic stream.
2. Every §6.8 / §33.4 mention of the 30-day window MUST cite this table by §6.8.6 reference; new inline duplications fail CI gate `dsar_sla_single_source_of_truth`.
3. PostHog event `dsar_sla_window_breached` fires when `now - verified_at > 30d AND extension_reason IS NULL AND fulfilled_at IS NULL`. P0 alert; pages Privacy Officer on-call.
4. The 72-hour acknowledgment is observable via `dsar_subject_acknowledged_at` on the DSARRequest row; the 24-hour partial-failure notification is observable via `dsar_partial_failure_notified_at`.

### 6.8.6.1 Subject Verification Protocol (D-3.5-005 remediation, 2026-05-04) {#6.8.6.1-subject-verification-protocol}

**Authoring intent.** §6.8.6 SLA clock starts at `DSARRequest.verified_at`. Pre-V3, the verification protocol was undefined: a bad actor could flood unverified DSARs (no clock starts, no abuse path); a legitimate subject locked out of their account could not start the clock at all. GDPR Art. 12(6) requires the controller to "request the provision of additional information necessary to confirm the identity of the data subject" — this sub-section authors that protocol.

**Verification methods.**

| Method | Applicability | Mechanism | SLA |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `signed_in_session` | Subject holds an active Sourcera session | Step-up reauth via TOTP / WebAuthn at the DSAR submission surface; `verified_at` stamped on successful step-up | < 60 seconds |
| `magic_link_email` | Subject does not hold an active session OR account is deprovisioned but email is recoverable | Magic link delivered via Loops.so to the subject's last-known verified email; clicking the link within 24h stamps `verified_at` | < 24 hours |
| `id_document_review` | Subject's account is deprovisioned AND email is unrecoverable; OR third-party DSAR (subject is named in customer text but holds no Sourcera account) | Subject submits identity document via Ops review surface; Ops reviewer verifies and stamps `verified_at` after dual sign-off | < 7 calendar days |
| `multi_factor` | High-risk subject (e.g., subject's account was previously compromised) | Subject completes magic-link AND TOTP / WebAuthn step-up | < 7 calendar days |

**Verification failure path.**

- 3 failed magic-link attempts within a 24-hour window → 24-hour cooldown; subject notified via email.
- After cooldown, Subject may retry; second cooldown is 72 hours.
- After third cooldown, automatic state transition to `manifestly_unfounded_rejected` per §6.8.6.2 (D-3V-003 remediation).
- Verification SLA: `verified_at` MUST be stamped within 7 calendar days of `received_at`; if not, the DSAR auto-state-transitions to `manifestly_unfounded_rejected` per §6.8.6.2.

**Third-party DSAR (subject is named in customer text but holds no Sourcera account).**

- Subject submits via the public privacy-request surface (`https://sourcera.com/privacy/request`).
- `id_document_review` is the only permitted verification method.
- Ops-mediated identity proof: Ops reviewer cross-references the document against the customer text mentioning the subject; dual sign-off required (Ops reviewer + Privacy Officer).
- Cascade is bounded — third-party-DSAR cascade does not pseudonymize Sourcera-account-holder Users (those subjects have their own DSAR path); it redacts only the body text mentions and (where applicable) embedding-vector references per §22.3.1 third-party body-redaction sweep (D-3.5-012 V3 remediation).

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Every DSARRequest INSERT MUST be in state `verifying`; `verified_at` is null until verification completes. CI gate `dsar_request_state_transition_received_to_verifying`.
2. `verified_at` MUST be stamped within 7 calendar days of `received_at` OR the request auto-transitions to `manifestly_unfounded_rejected` with subject notification. CI gate `dsar_verification_sla_7d_enforcement`.
3. `id_document_review` verification MUST require dual sign-off (Ops reviewer + Privacy Officer) audit-eventable per §6.7. Property test `dsar_id_document_review_dual_signoff`.
4. Verification failure MUST emit `dsar.verification_failed` AuditEvent with `failure_count`, `cooldown_window`, `verification_method`. Registered in Appendix J Phase-3V cluster.
5. Third-party DSAR cascade MUST NOT modify Sourcera-account-holder User rows; it operates on body text and embedding vectors only. Property test `dsar_third_party_cascade_account_holder_isolation`.

### 6.8.6.2 Manifestly-Unfounded and Excessive Requests (D-3V-003 remediation, 2026-05-04) {#6.8.6.2-manifestly-unfounded-and-excessive-requests}

**Authoring intent.** GDPR Art. 12(5) authorizes the controller to "(a) charge a reasonable fee taking into account the administrative costs of providing the information or communication or taking the action requested; or (b) refuse to act on the request" when requests are manifestly unfounded or excessive. Pre-V3, Sourcera had no spec-side authority for either action — exposing the platform to DSAR-based denial-of-service attacks. This sub-section authors the controller-side rejection authority.

**Trigger conditions for `manifestly_unfounded_rejected` state transition.**

A DSARRequest auto-transitions to `manifestly_unfounded_rejected` when ANY of the following holds:

1. Verification fails 3× within 7 calendar days per §6.8.6.1 cooldown sequence.
2. Subject submits ≥ 5 DSARRequests of the same `request_kind` against the same Org within 30 calendar days (cap reset on legitimate change of circumstance, e.g., subject's role change).
3. Subject submits ≥ 20 DSARRequests across all Orgs within 30 calendar days (platform-wide abuse pattern).
4. Ops reviewer manually flags the request as manifestly unfounded with documented rationale (audit-eventable; Privacy Officer dual sign-off required).
5. SIM detector (per §48.4.10) identifies the request as part of a coordinated DSAR-flood pattern.

**Excessive-request fee (Article 12(5)(a) authority).**

For requests that exceed the §6.8.6.2 trigger thresholds but are not yet `manifestly_unfounded_rejected`, the controller MAY charge a reasonable administrative fee per the §34 fee schedule (authored as the new §34.18.1 row "DSAR Excessive-Request Administrative Fee"). The fee is calibrated to administrative cost, not punitive; subject must be notified of the fee at acknowledgment time and given 14 days to pay or withdraw.

**Subject notification on rejection.**

The subject is notified within 72 hours of state transition via email (Appendix C `dsar.rejected_manifestly_unfounded` notification — registered in Phase-3V cluster). Notification carries:

- Reason code (one of the 5 trigger conditions above).
- Appeal path: Privacy Officer review with documented rationale; appeal must be filed within 30 calendar days.
- DPO contact information.
- Right to lodge a complaint with the supervisory authority (GDPR Art. 77).

**Retention class.**

Rejected DSARRequest rows are retained 7 years per §6.8.5 audit-integrity exemption (rejection itself is an audit record requiring proof of controller-side compliance with Article 12(5)). The rejection rationale, trigger evidence, and dual sign-off chain are part of the retained record.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. DSARRequest auto-transitions to `manifestly_unfounded_rejected` ONLY on the 5 enumerated trigger conditions; no manual ad-hoc rejection. CI gate `dsar_manifestly_unfounded_rejection_trigger_enforcement`.
2. Every rejection MUST emit `dsar.rejected_manifestly_unfounded` AuditEvent with `trigger_condition`, `rejection_rationale`, `dual_signoff_actors[]`. Registered in Appendix J Phase-3V cluster. CI gate `dsar_manifestly_unfounded_rejection_audit_emission`.
3. Subject notification MUST land within 72 hours of state transition; carries reason code, appeal path, DPO contact, supervisory-authority complaint right. CI gate `dsar_rejection_subject_notification_sla_72h`.
4. Rejection MUST NOT short-circuit the SLA-clock window for the subject's right to file a fresh DSARRequest after a documented change of circumstance.
5. The §34.18.1 administrative fee (Article 12(5)(a) excessive-request fee) MUST be calibrated to documented administrative cost per the §34 fee-schedule audit; punitive fees are forbidden.

### 6.8.7 Right to Rectification (Article 16) — Authored Extension AE-3.5-001 {#6.8.7-right-to-rectification}

**Authoring intent (AE-3.5-001 — pending Privacy Officer + legal sign-off).** GDPR Art. 16 requires the controller to rectify inaccurate personal data without undue delay. Pre-V3, §6.8 contained zero references to rectification. This sub-section authors the right.

**Surface.**

- Subject submits via Settings → Privacy → Request Data Correction (signed-in path) OR `https://sourcera.com/privacy/correction` (third-party path).
- DSARRequest entity instantiated with `request_kind = rectification`.
- Verification per §6.8.6.1.

**Rectification scope.**

- Subject's directly-controlled profile fields (name, email, avatar, preferences) are self-edited in Settings → Profile; rectification request is unnecessary for these.
- Derived data (Audit Event change records, Console Bridge Event payloads carrying frozen role-snapshots, Selection Report content quoting subject text) is in scope: rectification rewrites the affected columns AND propagates an `audit_event_post_rectification_rehash` per §6.7.5 to preserve hash-chain integrity.
- Inaccurate data attributed to the subject by another user (e.g., a Comment thread identifying the subject by an outdated role) is in scope: the offending row is annotated with a `rectification_overlay_json` field that the rendering layer applies at display time; the original row is preserved for audit but the rendered surface shows the corrected data.

**Cascade.**

- Rectification cascade walker is co-resident with the §6.8.4 erasure cascade walker; both honor the §6.8.4.2 residency partitioning rule.
- Pseudonymized rows (DSAR-pseudonymized prior to rectification) cannot be rectified — the subject's identity is no longer linked. Subject is notified of this constraint at submission time.

**SLA.** The §6.8.6 fulfillment window applies; rectification is a fulfillment outcome.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Rectification cascade MUST recompute affected `event_content_hash` per §6.7.5 to preserve chain integrity. CI gate `rectification_cascade_audit_chain_continuity`.
2. Rectification overlay MUST be visible in the rendering layer and audit-eventable. Property test `rectification_overlay_render_layer_application`.
3. Rectification request on a pseudonymized row MUST return HTTP 422 `dsar_rectification_against_pseudonymized_row_unsupported` with subject notification.

### 6.8.8 Right to Restriction of Processing (Article 18) — Authored Extension AE-3.5-002 {#6.8.8-right-to-restriction}

**Authoring intent (AE-3.5-002 — pending Privacy Officer + legal sign-off).** GDPR Art. 18 grants the subject the right to restrict processing while a dispute is pending. Pre-V3, §6.8 was silent. This sub-section authors the right.

**Restriction state on User entity.**

A new column `restricted_processing_state` is added to §4.2.3 User (registered in Phase-3V Appendix J cluster as enum `user_restricted_processing_state ∈ {none, restricted_pending_dispute, restricted_pending_rectification, restricted_legitimate_interest_objection_pending}`).

**Restriction effect.**

- AIOperation creation against a `restricted_processing_state ≠ none` User row is blocked at the §32 endpoint layer with HTTP 423 `user_processing_restricted` (Appendix I — new).
- Managed Agent retrieval against a restricted User's KB content is blocked similarly.
- Read-only access to the subject's data continues — the subject can still view their own data and Org Admins can read for compliance.
- Subject is notified at restriction-effective time; restriction lasts until the underlying dispute resolves (rectification completes, objection adjudicated, etc.).

**SLA.** The §6.8.6 fulfillment window applies; restriction MUST take effect within 72 hours of `verified_at`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. AIOperation creation against a restricted User MUST return HTTP 423; CI gate `restricted_processing_aiop_block_enforcement`.
2. Managed Agent retrieval against restricted KB content MUST return HTTP 423.
3. Restriction-effective notification MUST land within 72 hours of `verified_at`.

### 6.8.9 Right to Object (Article 21) — Authored Extension AE-3.5-003 {#6.8.9-right-to-object}

**Authoring intent (AE-3.5-003 — pending Privacy Officer + legal sign-off).** GDPR Art. 21 grants the subject the right to object to processing based on legitimate interest. Pre-V3, §6.8 was silent. This sub-section authors the right.

**Surface.**

- Subject submits via Settings → Privacy → Object to Processing (signed-in path) OR public surface (third-party path).
- DSARRequest entity instantiated with `request_kind = objection` and `objection_basis ∈ {legitimate_interest, direct_marketing, statistical_purpose, automated_decision}`.
- Subject specifies which processing activity is objected to.

**Adjudication.**

- Objections to direct marketing (Art. 21(2)) are absolute — Sourcera MUST cease the marketing activity within 24 hours of `verified_at` (no balancing test).
- Objections to legitimate-interest processing (Art. 21(1)) trigger a Privacy Officer review with the standard balancing test; outcome is `objection_upheld` or `objection_rejected_compelling_legitimate_grounds`.
- Adjudication SLA: within the §6.8.6 fulfillment window from `verified_at`.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Direct-marketing objection MUST cease the activity within 24 hours; CI gate `objection_direct_marketing_24h_cessation`.
2. Legitimate-interest objection MUST be adjudicated by Privacy Officer with documented balancing-test rationale.
3. Subject MUST be notified of adjudication outcome with appeal path.

### 6.8.10 Right to Data Portability (Article 20) — Authored Extension AE-3.5-004 {#6.8.10-right-to-data-portability}

**Authoring intent (AE-3.5-004 — pending Privacy Officer + legal sign-off).** GDPR Art. 20 requires the controller to provide the subject's personal data in a structured, commonly-used, machine-readable format AND to transmit the data to another controller upon subject request. Pre-V3, §6.8.1 partially addressed (a) but not (b). This sub-section authors the full right.

**Format guarantees.**

- Export bundle JSON Schema is published as `dsar_export_schema_v1.json` (versioned per `dsar_export_schema_version`); subject can validate the export against the schema.
- CSV alternative is offered for non-developer subjects (single ZIP containing JSON + CSV-rendered subset of human-readable sheets).
- Bundle is encrypted at rest with per-DSAR-request KMS key; download requires authenticated session OR step-up auth via TOTP / WebAuthn for the magic-link path.
- Bundle size soft-cap 5 GB; multi-part split above.

**Transmission to another controller.**

- Subject specifies receiving controller's endpoint at submission time.
- Sourcera supports the W3C Data Transfer Protocol (DTP) for direct controller-to-controller transmission where the receiving controller is DTP-compatible.
- Where DTP is unavailable, Sourcera delivers the export to the subject (signed-in download); the subject is responsible for forwarding.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Export schema MUST be published and versioned; subject can validate. CI gate `dsar_export_schema_published_versioned`.
2. CSV alternative MUST be offered alongside JSON. Property test `dsar_export_csv_alternative_offered`.
3. Bundle MUST be encrypted at rest with per-request KMS key; download MUST require authenticated session OR step-up auth.
4. DTP-compatible receiving controller transmission MUST complete within the §6.8.6 fulfillment window.

### 6.8.11 Automated-Decision Rights (Article 22) — Authored Extension AE-3.5-005 {#6.8.11-automated-decision-rights}

**Authoring intent (AE-3.5-005 — pending Privacy Officer + legal sign-off).** GDPR Art. 22 grants the subject the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing that produces legal or similarly significant effects. Sourcera's AI Scoring (§13), Match Score (§27.4), and SIM flagging (§48.4.10) are automated decisions about subjects. Pre-V3, §6.8 was silent on Article 22. This sub-section authors the right.

**Scope.**

- AI Scoring: subject is the vendor whose response is scored; scoring decisions affect Selection Report ranking which has economic significance to the seller.
- Match Score: subject is the seller whose listing is matched against buyer Use Cases; ranking affects seller's marketplace surface visibility.
- SIM flagging: subject is the user whose account is flagged for fraud / abuse review; flagging affects account-status decisions.

**Right surface.**

- Subject may request human review of any automated decision via Settings → Privacy → Request Human Review.
- DSARRequest entity instantiated with `request_kind = automated_decision_review` and `decision_id` (FK to the originating AIOperation row).
- Sourcera commits to human review within the §6.8.6 fulfillment window.

**Adjudication.**

- Human reviewer is a Privacy Officer (for SIM flagging) OR an Ops reviewer with documented qualification (for AI Scoring / Match Score).
- Reviewer applies a documented review checklist; outcome is `automated_decision_upheld`, `automated_decision_overturned`, or `automated_decision_partial_correction`.
- Subject is notified of outcome with rationale; outcome is appealable to a second reviewer (escalation path).

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Subject MUST be able to identify the automated decision being challenged via `decision_id` (FK to AIOperation). CI gate `automated_decision_review_decision_id_resolution`.
2. Human review MUST complete within the §6.8.6 fulfillment window.
3. Outcome MUST be communicated with rationale and appeal path.
4. SIM-flagging reviews require Privacy Officer (not Ops reviewer alone) per the higher-stakes posture.

### 6.8.12 Jurisdictional Subject-Rights Coverage — Authored Extension AE-V72REM-PH35-DSAR-01 {#6.8.12-jurisdictional-subject-rights-coverage}

**Authoring intent.** Pre-remediation §6.8 implemented GDPR article-rights mechanics and cited CCPA acknowledgment timing in §6.8.6, but did not map Sourcera's subject-rights surfaces to the launch jurisdiction set. This subsection is a spec-side coverage matrix, not legal advice; Legal / Compliance counter-signature remains required before the v7.1.1 stamp.

| Jurisdiction | Rights covered | Sourcera surface | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| GDPR / EEA | Access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, objection, automated-decision review | §6.8.1 through §6.8.11 | Fulfillment SLA is §6.8.6. Erasure exemptions are §6.8.5. |
| UK-GDPR | Access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, objection, automated-decision review | §6.8.1 through §6.8.11 | UK / sovereign residency routing uses §1.6 / §34 legal-entity and residency configuration where applicable. |
| CCPA / CPRA | Know / access, delete, correct, opt out of sale or sharing, limit sensitive personal information where applicable, non-discrimination | §6.8.1, §6.8.3, §6.8.7, §6.8.9, privacy choices surface | Sourcera does not sell or share personal information by default; the opt-out surface still renders, records `not_applicable_no_sale_or_share` where appropriate, and writes an AuditEvent. |
| LGPD | Confirmation / access, correction, anonymization / blocking / deletion, portability, information about sharing, review of automated decisions | §6.8.1, §6.8.7, §6.8.8, §6.8.10, §6.8.11 | Brazil requests use the same SLA unless local-counsel configuration overrides the response window. |
| Quebec Law 25 | Access, rectification, portability, de-indexing / cessation of dissemination where applicable | §6.8.1, §6.8.7, §6.8.9, §6.8.10 | Transparency / privacy-impact notices bind to §33.5 and launch compliance materials. |
| US state privacy launch set | CCPA / CPRA, VCDPA, Colorado CPA, CTDPA, UCPA | §6.8.1, §6.8.3, §6.8.7, §6.8.9, privacy choices surface | State add / remove register is owned by Legal; product mechanics must map each right to a DSARRequest `request_kind` or explicit `not_applicable` reason. |

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Every jurisdiction row above MUST map each active subject right to a DSARRequest `request_kind` or to an explicit `not_applicable` reason recorded on the request. CI gate `dsar_jurisdiction_rights_mapping_complete` asserts.
2. Subject-rights fulfillment MUST be available across all plan tiers; plan gating is forbidden for the rights-fulfillment side of DSAR. CI gate `dsar_subject_rights_plan_gating_forbidden` asserts against §5.11 / §34.1.
3. Legal MAY add or retire state-law rows through the jurisdiction register without changing §6.8.1 export mechanics, provided every new row has a `request_kind` mapping before launch.
4. Privacy-choice opt-out requests MUST write an AuditEvent even when Sourcera's default posture returns `not_applicable_no_sale_or_share`.
5. The §33.5 compliance table MUST point to this subsection for privacy-rights coverage and MUST NOT be treated as the implementation source of truth.

### 6.8.13 DSAR API Contract - Authored Extension AE-V72REM-PH35-DSAR-02 {#6.8.13-dsar-api-contract}

**Authoring intent.** Pre-remediation §6.8 defined subject-rights behavior but did not expose a §32-style API contract for request submission, verification, status, export retrieval, withdrawal, extension, or Org-admin listing. This subsection is the canonical DSAR endpoint family; §32 remains the general API style guide and envelope authority.

**Endpoint registry.**

| Method | Path | Purpose | Auth scope | Rate-limit class | Idempotency |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| POST | `/v1/dsar` | Submit a subject-rights request | Signed-in subject OR public privacy-request token | `dsar_subject_request` | Required: `Idempotency-Key` |
| POST | `/v1/dsar/{dsar_request_id}/verify` | Complete subject verification | Subject verification token OR signed-in subject step-up | `dsar_subject_request` | Required: `Idempotency-Key` |
| GET | `/v1/dsar/{dsar_request_id}` | Read request status | Subject, Org admin with scope, Privacy Officer, Ops compliance | `standard_authenticated_per_org` | n/a |
| GET | `/v1/dsar/{dsar_request_id}/export` | Retrieve signed export URL | Subject OR Privacy Officer | `standard_authenticated_per_org` | n/a |
| POST | `/v1/dsar/{dsar_request_id}/withdraw` | Withdraw a pending request | Subject OR Privacy Officer on subject instruction | `dsar_subject_request` | Required: `Idempotency-Key` |
| POST | `/v1/dsar/{dsar_request_id}/extension` | Grant a statutory extension | Privacy Officer OR Ops compliance with dual sign-off | `data_mutation` | Required: `Idempotency-Key` |
| GET | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/dsar` | Org-admin / compliance listing | `admin:ops_compliance` OR Org Admin privacy scope | `standard_authenticated_per_org` | n/a; cursor pagination |
| POST | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/dsar/initiate-on-behalf` | Org-admin assisted request initiation | Org Admin privacy scope + subject notice proof | `dsar_subject_request` | Required: `Idempotency-Key` |

**Shared endpoint rules.**

- All responses use the §32 canonical envelope. List responses use `data` + `pagination` with `cursor` and `limit` (default 50, max 250).
- Request IDs are tenant-scoped. Cross-Org reads return 404 `dsar_request_not_found` unless the caller has Ops compliance scope.
- DSAR subject-rights availability is plan-independent. Endpoint authorization MUST NOT consult plan tier except for unrelated admin analytics exports.
- Every write endpoint emits an AuditEvent; DSAR lifecycle notifications are Appendix C DSAR-Lifecycle events and PostHog mirrors in Appendix G.
- Public-token endpoints bind to the verification token and email address submitted at intake; tokens are single-use, 24-hour TTL, and residency-routed per §6.8.4.2.

**POST `/v1/dsar`.**

Request schema:

```json
{
  "request_kind": "access",
  "subject": {
    "email": "person@example.com",
    "user_id": "optional-uuid",
    "third_party_context": "optional text"
  },
  "org_id": "optional-uuid",
  "jurisdiction": "gdpr_eea",
  "delivery_preference": "json_csv_zip",
  "receiving_controller_endpoint": "optional https URL for portability",
  "reason": "optional subject-supplied explanation"
}
```

Response schema: `201` with `{dsar_request_id, state, verification_required, verification_methods[], expected_acknowledgment_at, expected_fulfillment_at}`. Errors: `dsar_subject_request_rate_limited` (429), `dsar_request_scope_forbidden` (404), `validation_error` (422), `idempotency_key_request_mismatch` (409).

**POST `/v1/dsar/{dsar_request_id}/verify`.**

Request schema: `{verification_method, verification_token, step_up_challenge_response}` where the required field set is determined by §6.8.6.1. Response schema: `{dsar_request_id, state, verified_at, expected_fulfillment_at}`. Errors: `dsar_verification_failed` (401), `dsar_request_invalid_state_transition` (422), `dsar_request_not_found` (404).

**GET `/v1/dsar/{dsar_request_id}`.**

Response schema: `{dsar_request_id, request_kind, state, received_at, verified_at, fulfilled_at, extension_reason, extension_granted_at, expected_fulfillment_at, partial_failure_status, audit_integrity_exemptions_invoked[]}`. Errors: `dsar_request_not_found` (404), `dsar_request_scope_forbidden` (404).

**GET `/v1/dsar/{dsar_request_id}/export`.**

Response schema: `{download_url, expires_at, bundle_size_bytes, schema_version, checksum_sha256}`. Returns `dsar_request_export_not_ready` (409) until `fulfilled_at` is stamped; returns `dsar_request_export_link_expired` (410) after signed URL expiry. Export downloads emit `dsar.export.downloaded` AuditEvent and PostHog mirror.

**POST `/v1/dsar/{dsar_request_id}/withdraw`.**

Request schema: `{withdrawal_reason}`. Response schema: `{dsar_request_id, state="withdrawn", withdrawn_at}`. Withdrawal is allowed only before `fulfilled_at` and before a statutory retention record has been finalized. Errors: `dsar_request_withdrawal_not_allowed` (409), `dsar_request_invalid_state_transition` (422).

**POST `/v1/dsar/{dsar_request_id}/extension`.**

Request schema: `{extension_reason, rationale, dual_signoff_actor_ids[]}`. Response schema: `{dsar_request_id, state="extended", extension_reason, extension_granted_at, expected_fulfillment_at}`. Errors: `dsar_extension_not_allowed` (409), `dsar_request_invalid_state_transition` (422), `dsar_request_not_found` (404).

**GET `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/dsar`.**

Query parameters: `cursor`, `limit`, `state`, `request_kind`, `received_after`, `received_before`. Response schema: `data[]` rows matching the GET status schema, with `subject_user_id` pseudonymized unless the caller is Privacy Officer or Ops compliance. Pagination follows §32.3.

**POST `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/dsar/initiate-on-behalf`.**

Request schema: `{subject_email, request_kind, jurisdiction, subject_notice_sent_at, subject_notice_channel, admin_rationale}`. Response schema: `{dsar_request_id, state, verification_required=true, subject_notice_sent_at}`. Errors: `dsar_org_admin_subject_notice_required` (422), `dsar_subject_request_rate_limited` (429), `dsar_request_scope_forbidden` (404).

**Examples.**

```http
POST /v1/dsar
Idempotency-Key: dsar_2026_06_22_person_access_01
Content-Type: application/json

{"request_kind":"access","subject":{"email":"person@example.com"},"jurisdiction":"gdpr_eea","delivery_preference":"json_csv_zip"}
```

```http
GET /v1/orgs/org_123/dsar?state=in_progress&limit=50
Authorization: Bearer <token with admin:ops_compliance or Org Admin privacy scope>
```

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Every DSAR endpoint above MUST emit only Appendix I-registered errors; CI gate `dsar_api_error_catalog_completeness` asserts.
2. Every endpoint-declared rate-limit class MUST resolve to §32.4.5 and Appendix J; CI gate `api_rate_limit_class_registry_consistency` covers.
3. GET listing MUST use the §32.3 canonical pagination envelope and `cursor` / `limit`; CI gate `pagination_envelope_canonical` covers.
4. Public-token access MUST be single-use, 24-hour TTL, and bound to the DSARRequest subject email; property test `dsar_public_token_single_use_bound_subject`.
5. Org-admin assisted initiation MUST provide subject-notice proof before write; otherwise return `dsar_org_admin_subject_notice_required`.

## 6.9 User Deprovisioning (D-3.5-004 remediation, 2026-05-04) {#6.9-user-deprovisioning}

**Authoring intent.** Pre-V3, three sections (§6.8.2 line 9589, §6.8.3 line 9627, §7.1.2 line 9795) cited "Section 6.9" as the canonical home for user deprovisioning rules — but §6.9 did not exist. This sub-section authors §6.9 end-to-end.

### 6.9.1 Trigger Paths

User deprovisioning is initiated via one of five trigger paths:

1. **Org Admin manual revoke.** Org Admin removes user via Settings → Members; emits `org.member_removed` AuditEvent.
2. **SCIM IdP-driven deactivation.** WorkOS SCIM webhook fires `user_deactivated` per the IdP-side membership change; Sourcera-side handler triggers deprovisioning.
3. **Account-closure subject-initiated.** Subject submits §6.8.3 complete account closure via Settings → Privacy → Close Account; deprovisioning is the prerequisite step before complete deletion (§6.8.3 30-day reflection period).
4. **Anti-fraud Ops action.** Ops reviewer with documented rationale deprovisions a user as part of fraud / abuse remediation; dual sign-off required (Ops reviewer + Privacy Officer).
5. **Role-revocation cascade.** Org dissolution / merger triggers automatic deprovisioning of all members; per-Org cascade.

### 6.9.2 Pre-Deprovisioning Ownership-Transfer

Before the user's session is invalidated, ownership of single-owner entities is transferred per the following fall-through:

| Entity owned by deprovisioning user | Transfer target |
| :---- | :---- |
| Workspace (`workspace_owner`) | Sole-Workspace-Admin → least-recent-active-Org-Admin → Org Owner |
| Use Case (`use_case_lead`) | Workspace Owner |
| Bid Workspace (`bid_workspace_owner`) | Sole-`seller_bid_captain` → `seller_org_admin` → `seller_org_owner` |
| Capability Declaration (sole `capability_owner`) | `seller_marketing_editor` → `seller_org_admin` |
| Internal Comment Thread (sole `opened_by_user_id`) | Workspace Owner |
| API Token | Hard-revoked; new owner re-issues |

Transfer is audit-eventable; emits `org.ownership_transferred` per entity.

### 6.9.3 Deprovisioning Sequence

1. **Session invalidation (immediate).** All active sessions for the user across web + mobile are revoked; emits `auth.session_revoked` per §6.7.6.
2. **WorkOS-side propagation.** SCIM `user_deactivated` reflected back to WorkOS within 60 seconds of trigger.
3. **WorkOS Groups cascade (V3+ remediation, 2026-05-04).** For every `workos_group_id` in the user's §4.2.2 OrgMembership.`workos_group_ids`, Sourcera invokes the WorkOS Groups API `remove_group_member` endpoint to detach the membership. This cascade is automatic on `user_deactivated`; explicit removal is needed only when the deprovisioning trigger is Sourcera-initiated (Org Admin manual revoke) and the WorkOS-side is not the originating actor. CI gate `workos_groups_api_membership_consistency` (per §4.2.5 AC #1) extends to assert post-deprovisioning membership consistency.
4. **Ownership transfer (≤ 24 hours).** Per §6.9.2.
5. **Pseudonymization (per §6.8.2 schedule).** Comment authorship, score authorship, audit-row attribution all pseudonymized per §6.8.4.1 Pattern B. Sourcera-side §4.2.5 Group rows transitions to `tombstoned_dsar` for any Group whose member set included the deprovisioned subject.
6. **Account-status transition.** User row `state` transitions to `tombstoned_dsar` (per §6.8.4.1) OR `deprovisioned` (per §6.8.2 if the deprovisioning is not subject-initiated).

### 6.9.4 SCIM Loop Semantics

- Sourcera-initiated deprovisioning emits a SCIM `user_deactivated` to WorkOS within 60 seconds.
- WorkOS-initiated deprovisioning (IdP-side membership change) flows in via SCIM webhook; Sourcera handler is idempotent on `(scim_event_id, user_id)`.
- Loop suppression: a SCIM webhook arriving for a user already in `tombstoned_dsar` / `deprovisioned` state is a no-op (idempotent).

### 6.9.5 Cross-Org User (Member of N Orgs)

Per-Org deprovisioning is **independent**. A user who is a member of 4 Orgs and is deprovisioned from Org A retains active membership in Orgs B / C / D. The §6.8.4 cascade at deprovisioning is scoped to Org A only.

If the user is the source of a DSAR `request_kind = erasure_complete_deletion` (§6.8.3), the cascade DOES operate cross-Org — every Org membership is deprovisioned in turn; the User row is hard-deleted only after all Org cascades complete.

### 6.9.6 Acceptance Criteria

1. Session invalidation MUST occur within 60 seconds of any §6.9.1 trigger. CI gate `deprovisioning_session_invalidation_60s_sla`.
2. Ownership transfer MUST complete within 24 hours; cascade target MUST satisfy the §6.9.2 fall-through. Property test `deprovisioning_ownership_transfer_fallthrough_correctness`.
3. SCIM loop suppression MUST be idempotent on `(scim_event_id, user_id)`. Property test `deprovisioning_scim_loop_idempotency`.
4. Cross-Org user deprovisioning MUST be Org-scoped unless triggered by §6.8.3 complete account closure. Property test `deprovisioning_cross_org_scope_correctness`.
5. Every deprovisioning event MUST emit `auth.session_revoked`, `org.member_removed` (or equivalent), `org.ownership_transferred` per affected entity, and per §6.9.3 Step 4 cascade audit events.

# 7\. Organization & Administration {#7.-organization-&-administration}

## 7.1 Organization Lifecycle {#7.1-organization-lifecycle}

An Organization represents a legal entity or business unit using Sourcera as a Buyer or Seller.

### 7.1.1 Organization Creation

- Organization is created when first user from a company signs up via Sourcera  
- System detects domain from user email (e.g., `@acme.com` → Organization name `Acme`)  
- Founder is assigned role Organization Admin  
- New Organization starts on Free plan  
- Founder receives welcome email with onboarding guide

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- Organization record created with status `active`  
- Organization Admin is assigned initial settings defaults (MFA enforcement disabled, no IP allowlist, no custom domain)  
- Organization appears in user's Organization switcher

### 7.1.2 Organization Settings

Organization Admin may modify the following Organization settings:

| Setting | Type | Default | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Name | Text (255 char) | Auto-detected from domain | May be updated anytime |
| Logo | Image (PNG/SVG, max 5MB) | Sourcera default | Used in Marketplace, emails, billing portal |
| Billing Email | Email | Founder email | Receives invoices and payment notifications |
| Primary Domain | Custom domain | None | Used for SSO/SCIM configuration (see Section 6.4) |
| SSO Connection | WorkOS Connection ID | None | SAML configuration details, enterprise only |
| SCIM Endpoint | URL | Auto-generated | Enterprise only; URL for SCIM provisioning (see Section 6.9) |
| MFA Enforcement Level | Enum (`off` / `optional` / `required`) | Plan-derived per §4.2.1 | Enterprise Orgs may set `required`; all tiers follow §6.2.2 / §34.1. |
| IP Allowlist | CIDR list | Empty | If populated, only users from these IP ranges can access Sourcera; blocks all other access |
| Default User Role | RBAC role | Reviewer | Role assigned to new users invited without explicit role |
| Audit Log Retention | Read-only | Plan-dependent | Displays current retention window (30d/1yr/7yr) |

**Audit Logging:**

- All setting changes are logged with `action=org_setting_updated` and `changes` showing before/after values  
- MFA enforcement-level changes are logged separately as `mfa_enforcement_changed`

### 7.1.3 Organization Deletion

Organization Admin may initiate Organization deletion. Deletion follows a 44-day process: 14-day grace period \+ 30-day processing.

**Phase 1: Deletion Initiation (Day 0\)**

- Admin clicks Settings → Organization → Delete Organization  
- System presents confirmation: "This action is irreversible. All data will be permanently deleted in 44 days. Your team has 14 days to cancel."  
- Admin confirms with password verification  
- Organization status changed to `deletion_scheduled`  
- `deletion_scheduled_at` timestamp recorded  
- Organization still fully functional during 14-day grace period  
- Organization remains hidden from new user invitations (existing members can still access)  
- Deletion initiation is logged as `org_deletion_initiated`

**Phase 2: Grace Period (Days 0-14)**

- All Organization functionality remains active  
- Admin may cancel deletion by visiting Settings → Organization → Cancel Deletion  
- Cancellation resets `deletion_scheduled` flag; Organization status returns to `active`  
- Cancellation is logged as `org_deletion_cancelled`  
- After Day 14 grace period expires, deletion cannot be cancelled

**Phase 3: Processing (Days 14-44)**

- Organization status changes to `deletion_in_progress` on Day 14  
- Cascade deletions execute immediately (see Section 7.2)  
- All Workspace and user data is purged  
- After 30-day processing window (Day 44), final purge of audit logs and backups occurs

### 7.2 Organization Deletion Cascade

> **Anchor disambiguation note (D-6.1-013 remediation, 2026-05-06).** A large number of body citations in this Master Spec read "Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2)" — including §4.7.1 line 7729, §25.1, §25.7.1, §31.8.1, Appendix K's "Dual-Console Firewall" entry, and ~50 other locations. Those citations are anchor-shorthand for the firewall enforcement contract; they MUST be read as resolving to **§1.3 Dual-Console Data Isolation Model** (the read/write/scope-isolation contract) and **§1.4 Query Scoping Requirements** (the runtime-enforcement contract), NOT to this section. This section (§7.2) authors only the deletion-cascade behavior when an Organization enters `deletion_in_progress`. A future v7.2.0 anchor-stability pass will rename §7.2 and propagate the canonical anchor; in the interim, every "(§7.2)" citation referencing the firewall resolves to §1.3 + §1.4.

When an Organization enters `deletion_in_progress` status, the following cascade occurs automatically:

**Marketplace Listings (Seller Side):**

- All Marketplace Listings published by any Team in the Organization are unpublished  
- Listing `status` set to `closed`  
- Sellers receiving the Listing may no longer respond to it  
- Listing remains visible in seller's historical view for 30 days, then purged

**Active Bid Workspaces in Other Organizations (Buyer Side):**

- For each Bid Workspace where the deleting Organization is the Vendor, the workspace `status` is set to `buyer_org_deleted`  
- Vendor's ability to submit new responses is blocked  
- Vendor's existing responses become read-only; vendor may view but not edit or delete  
- Buyer workspace continues normally; scoring and evaluation proceed  
- Buyer receives notification: "Vendor \[Organization Name\] has been deleted and can no longer respond. Existing responses are preserved."  
- This status persists indefinitely (even after 44-day processing); workspace remains in buyer's history

**NDA Records:**

- All NDA documents signed by users of the deleting Organization are preserved  
- NDA status remains `executed` and documents remain accessible to the other party (read-only)  
- No cascading NDA termination occurs

**Webhook Subscriptions:**

- All webhooks subscribed by the Organization are disabled immediately  
- Webhook `status` set to `disabled_org_deleted`  
- Failed event queue is purged  
- Cannot be re-enabled; must be manually recreated if Organization is recreated

**Active Users & Sessions:**

- All user sessions are invalidated immediately  
- Users receive "Organization has been deleted" message upon next access attempt  
- Users cannot sign back in; account is unusable

**Data Purge Timeline:**

- Day 14-44: Marketplace Listings, Bid Workspaces (buyer-side), active sessions purged  
- Day 44: All Requirements, Use Cases, Scenarios, Responses, Scores, Comments, audit logs, user accounts purged  
- Final backup purge occurs Day 45; no data recovery possible after this point

## 7.3 PII Handling Across Org Boundaries {#7.3-pii-handling-across-org-boundaries}

**Scope.** This subsection consolidates the PII-handling rules referenced from §4.3.16 BuyerReferral, §4.4.18 SellerSignal, §4.4.22 SellerOnboardingSession, and other entity sections that defer to "§7.3 PII handling" for the canonical cross-Org rules. The runtime authority for DSAR / right-to-erasure is §6.8.

**Rules.**

1. **Pre-signup anonymity.** A referee Org that has not yet completed signup is referenced only by an anonymized hash (`anonymized_referee_<hash>`); the referrer Org sees no identifying information until the referee completes signup AND consents to attribution.
2. **Pseudonymization on cross-Org PostHog joins.** Any PostHog event property that carries cross-Org user-attribution MUST use the deterministic per-Org pseudonymization scheme (§6.8.5); raw user IDs from the originating Org are never exposed in joined event streams.
3. **Vendor-side opt-in disclosure.** When a Seller Org de-anonymizes a SellerSignal cohort via EOI Acceptance or Direct Invite (§4.4.18, §27.9), the disclosure is limited to: the responding buyer Org name, the originating Workspace name, the requested-capability set, and the consenting buyer-user's display name. No cross-buyer-Org PII (other Org names, other buyer users) is leaked.
4. **Internal-Comment isolation.** §25.7 Internal Comment Posts NEVER cross the Buyer-Seller console firewall (§7.2). Webhook payloads omit `body` and `attachment_ids`; only metadata is delivered. PII embedded in post bodies (mentions, attached file names) is firewalled by virtue of the body itself never crossing.
5. **Marketplace projection redaction.** Public marketplace surfaces (CategoryPage, SoftwarePage, ComparisonPage, HeatMapCell) NEVER render buyer-side PII. Seller-side PII is rendered only with seller consent (verified domain ownership of the SellerOrgPage).
6. **Audit-log scoping.** Cross-namespace audit-log queries are gated to `org_owner` / `org_admin` per §6.7; Billing Admin sees the Billing Admin Audit View only (§5.2.1). Ops sees all per §50.5.
7. **DSAR redaction inheritance.** When a DSAR request anonymizes a referrer's user_id, the corresponding referee-attribution chain inherits the pseudonymization (the link survives but the originating identity does not).

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. CI gate `cross_org_pii_firewall` asserts no PostHog event property exposes raw cross-Org user IDs.
2. CI gate `referral_pre_signup_anonymity` asserts referrer-side surfaces never render referee identifying info before signup-consent completes.
3. CI gate `marketplace_buyer_pii_redaction` asserts no marketplace-public surface renders any buyer-side `user_id`, `email`, `display_name`, or `org_name` (the latter only after explicit publication consent in EOI / Direct Invite acceptance).

## 7.5 Convex Subscription / Reactivity Layer {#7.5-convex-subscription-reactivity-layer}

**Scope.** Pointer subsection. The runtime contract for Convex reactive queries — subscription registration, push-update semantics, optimistic mutation reconciliation, watcher reconciliation, and back-pressure handling — is authored at §22.4 (KB Reactivity), §25.1 (Console Bridge Event apply contract), §31.6 (Webhook Consumer Reactivity), and §44.1 (Performance Targets — p95 ≤ 500 ms reactive query latency). This subsection is the canonical anchor for body citations of "§7.5 Convex subscription layer" and provides the unified contract summary.

**Subscription contract.**

1. Every page or component that observes mutable state MUST register a Convex reactive query subscription via the `useQuery` hook (frontend) or the `runQuery` server-side primitive (worker).
2. Subscriptions are scope-isolated by `org_id` + `console` + `workspace_id` (where applicable) by default; cross-Org observation requires explicit Ops authorization per §50.2.
3. State changes are pushed via Convex's reactive layer; consumers MUST NOT poll. Polling-based watchers are a deploy-time validator failure (`convex_polling_watcher_violation`).
4. Optimistic mutations are reconciled against authoritative state via the `useMutation` hook with explicit reconciliation handlers; reconciliation conflicts are surfaced via the standard error-card UX (§3.7).
5. Reactive query latency MUST satisfy the §44.1 p95 ≤ 500 ms commit-to-observation budget. Breach triggers an Ops alert via §42.2.

### 7.5.3 Reactivity SLO {#7.5.3-reactivity-slo}

**Scope.** Pointer subsection for the §44.1 p95 ≤ 500 ms commit-to-reactive-observation latency budget. Body citations of "§7.5.3 reactivity SLO" resolve here. The authoritative latency target lives in §44.1 — this subsection is the §7.5 sub-anchor for cross-references.

**SLO statement.** Every Convex reactive query consumer observing a mutated entity MUST see the post-commit value within p95 ≤ 500 ms / p99 ≤ 1 s of the commit timestamp. Breach triggers a §42.2 alert.
