## 10.16 Phase Advancement API {#10.16-phase-advancement-api}

Phase advancement is available via REST API and UI. The §32-canonical endpoint is `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/advance` (cite §32.5); the §10.16 sub-section authors the contract that §32.5 binds to. Pre-V4 forms (`POST /workspaces/:workspaceId/advance-phase`) are retired in favor of the §32 OpenAPI form `{workspace_id}` (D-4.2-002 / D-4.2-036 closure).

### 10.16.1 API Endpoint (§32-canonical)

```
POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/advance
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
Idempotency-Key: {client-generated UUID per §32.3 idempotency convention; required on every mutation per §32 conventions}
X-Sourcera-Console: buyer
```

**Auth scope (§32 / §6.6.3 canonical scope axis):** `write:workspaces` (Workspace Owner, Workspace Admin, Use Case Lead per §5.11; Org Owner inherits). HTTP 403 `workspace_role_insufficient_for_phase_advance` on RBAC failure.

**Rate-limit class (§32.4.5):** `data_mutation` — 60 requests/minute per Org per Workspace.

**Cursor pagination:** n/a (single-resource mutation).

**Request body schema:**

```json
{
  "target_phase": "phase_2_requirement_definition",
  "soft_gates_enabled": false,
  "advance_reason": "string (≤200 chars; optional; required when soft_gates_enabled=true)"
}
```

- `target_phase` (required) — one of the 13 canonical `pipeline_phase` enum values per Appendix J Pipeline Phase Integer ↔ Enum Mapping. Server-side normalizes integer forms (`3`) and pre-V4 `phase_3`-style aliases to the canonical 13-value enum; submission of an unrecognized value returns HTTP 422 `pipeline_phase_invalid_enum_value`.
- `soft_gates_enabled` (optional; defaults to `false`) — when `true` AND `Workspace.evaluation_owner_mode = solo`, server skips hard-gate enforcement and emits `phase_advanced_with_unmet_gates` audit event with the unmet-gate list; when `true` AND `Workspace.evaluation_owner_mode = team`, server returns HTTP 422 `phase_advancement_soft_gates_not_permitted_in_team_mode` (per §2.8.7 AC #3). When omitted, the server auto-applies `soft_gates_enabled=true` for Solo-mode Workspaces.
- `advance_reason` (optional) — operator-supplied justification for the advancement; required when soft-gate skip is active per §2.8.3.

**Response (success — 200 OK):**

```json
{
  "workspace_id": "ws_01H8…",
  "current_phase": "phase_3_use_case_validation",
  "previous_phase": "phase_2_requirement_definition",
  "current_pipeline_stage_id": 3,
  "advanced_at": "2026-04-11T14:30:00Z",
  "advanced_by_user_id": "usr_…",
  "advanced_by_role_snapshot": "workspace_owner",
  "gate_validation": {
    "status": "passed",
    "checks": [
      {"check": "requirements_defined", "status": "passed"},
      {"check": "teams_assigned", "status": "passed"}
    ]
  },
  "warnings": []
}
```

**Response (idempotent no-op — 200 OK; already at target phase):**

```json
{
  "workspace_id": "ws_01H8…",
  "current_phase": "phase_3_use_case_validation",
  "current_pipeline_stage_id": 3,
  "message": "Workspace already at target phase; no state change.",
  "warnings": []
}
```

**Response (Solo soft-gate skip — 200 OK with warnings):**

```json
{
  "workspace_id": "ws_01H8…",
  "current_phase": "phase_4_vendor_discovery",
  "previous_phase": "phase_3_use_case_validation",
  "current_pipeline_stage_id": 4,
  "advanced_at": "2026-04-11T14:30:00Z",
  "warnings": [
    {
      "code": "phase_advanced_with_unmet_gates",
      "unmet_gates": ["use_case_lead_signoff_pending"],
      "message": "1 setup item was skipped under Solo Mode."
    }
  ]
}
```

**Response (Gate Failure — 422 Unprocessable Entity; team-mode hard-gate):**

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "gate_validation_failed",
    "message": "Cannot advance to Phase 3: 3 requirements are still pending review.",
    "localization_key": "error.workflow.gate_validation_failed",
    "details": {
      "current_phase": "phase_2_requirement_definition",
      "target_phase": "phase_3_use_case_validation",
      "failed_checks": [
        {
          "check": "requirements_approved",
          "status": "failed",
          "message": "3 requirements still pending review"
        }
      ]
    },
    "request_id": "req_01H8...",
    "retry_after_seconds": null
  }
}
```

**Error codes (registered in Appendix I; D-4.2-003 closure):**

| HTTP | Code | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `pipeline_phase_invalid_enum_value` | `target_phase` not in canonical 13-value `pipeline_phase` enum. |
| 401 | `unauthenticated` | Missing / invalid bearer token. |
| 403 | `workspace_role_insufficient_for_phase_advance` | Caller role lacks Workspace-write per §5.11. |
| 404 | `workspace_not_found` | `workspace_id` not visible to caller (Console firewall non-leak per §1.3). |
| 409 | `phase_advancement_concurrent_request_in_flight` | Another advance request for the same Workspace is mid-flight; client retries with the same `Idempotency-Key` after the in-flight request completes. |
| 422 | `gate_validation_failed` | Hard-gate failure (team mode); `failed_checks[]` enumerates under the §32.6 error envelope `error.details.failed_checks[]`. |
| 422 | `phase_advancement_soft_gates_not_permitted_in_team_mode` | Client supplied `soft_gates_enabled=true` on a `team`-mode Workspace per §2.8.7 AC #3. |
| 422 | `phase_6_bidding_close_below_minimum_window` | Phase 5 -> 6 advance attempted with `bidding_close_at < phase_6_entered_at + 7 calendar days` per §10.6. |
| 422 | `phase_advancement_backward_transition_forbidden` | `target_phase` < `current_phase`; backward transitions are explicitly rejected (one-directional advancement per §10.1.1). |
| 422 | `phase_advancement_terminal_phase_no_advance` | Workspace is already at `phase_13_contract_closure`; further advancement requires §10.14 cancellation or workspace soft-delete. |
| 503 | `phase_advancement_dependency_unavailable` | A required pre-commit dependency in §10.16.7 (Convex, WorkOS, local billing snapshot, or required outbox enqueue) is unavailable. Error body MUST include `error.details.dependency`; no phase mutation or side effects commit. Client retries with the same `Idempotency-Key` after `Retry-After`. |

### 10.16.2 Idempotency

The endpoint is idempotent on two axes per §32.3 idempotency convention:

1. **`Idempotency-Key` header** — required. The server caches the response keyed by `(Idempotency-Key, workspace_id, target_phase)` for 24 hours; replay returns the original response. A client retrying after a network timeout re-uses the same `Idempotency-Key` and is guaranteed to advance the Workspace at most once.
2. **Already-at-target-phase no-op** — a request whose `target_phase` equals the Workspace's current `pipeline_phase` returns 200 OK with the no-op response shape above. This second axis composes with `Idempotency-Key`: a retry with a fresh `Idempotency-Key` against an already-at-target Workspace still returns the no-op response (no audit event, no state change).

**Concurrency.** When two concurrent `advance` requests target the same Workspace with different `target_phase` values, the server serializes via Convex transaction commit-order (last-writer-wins on `pipeline_phase`) and emits HTTP 409 `phase_advancement_concurrent_request_in_flight` to the loser; the loser MUST retry. When two concurrent requests target the same `target_phase`, the second returns the no-op response (idempotent).

### 10.16.3 Phase Advancement Audit

Each advancement is logged to §4.6.1 AuditEvent:

- `action`: `phase_advanced` (canonical) or `phase_advanced_with_unmet_gates` (Solo soft-gate skip per §2.8.3)
- `resource_type`: `workspace`
- `resource_id`: Workspace ID
- `changes`: `{ "pipeline_phase": { "from": "phase_2_requirement_definition", "to": "phase_3_use_case_validation" }, "pipeline_stage_id": { "from": 2, "to": 3 } }`
- `metadata.unmet_gates[]`: array of unmet gate enum values (only on `phase_advanced_with_unmet_gates`)
- `metadata.advance_reason`: operator-supplied reason string (when provided)
- `timestamp`: ISO 8601

The audit row also emits a §4.7.1 Console Bridge Event projection `phase_advanced` (Carry list at line 7780) with `from_phase` / `to_phase` typed as `pipeline_phase` enum values.

### 10.16.4 Plan-Gating

Phase advancement itself is not plan-gated — every plan tier (Free / Solo / Starter / Growth / Scale / Enterprise) can advance a read-write Workspace through the pipeline. Soft-gate skip is plan-keyed indirectly via `evaluation_owner_mode=solo` (default for Free / Solo per §34.1.1; default Off for Starter+ per §2.8.7 AC #1). Per-phase capability access (e.g., Defense View on Phase 12 entry) is gated at the capability layer per §5.11 + §34.1, not at the §10.16 phase-advancement layer. Plan changes after Workspace creation follow the §10.17 preservation rules; a Workspace inside §34.6 read-only preservation cannot mutate or advance until restored, re-upgraded, or otherwise brought back under cap.

### 10.16.5 Webhook Emission

The `workspace.phase_advanced` webhook event (§31; Appendix C transactional events) fires on every successful phase advancement with payload schema:

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_…",
  "event_type": "workspace.phase_advanced",
  "workspace_id": "ws_…",
  "from_phase": "phase_2_requirement_definition",
  "to_phase": "phase_3_use_case_validation",
  "advanced_at": "2026-04-11T14:30:00Z",
  "advanced_by_user_id": "usr_…",
  "soft_gate_skip": false
}
```

HMAC-SHA256 signed per §31; `event_id` idempotency; exponential backoff retry; DLQ after 5 failures; payload ≤ 256 KB. Appendix G PostHog row `workspace_phase_advanced` is paired per `appendix_c_to_appendix_g_coverage` CI gate.

### 10.16.6 Acceptance Criteria

1. `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/advance` MUST be the only active Phase Advancement REST path; pre-V4 `POST /workspaces/:workspaceId/advance-phase` is historical-only and MUST NOT appear in active endpoint examples.
2. The request MUST include `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}`, required `Idempotency-Key`, and `X-Sourcera-Console: buyer` per §32.2.1; missing or contradictory console headers fail closed before mutation.
3. The request body MUST validate `target_phase` against Appendix J `pipeline_phase`, MAY include `soft_gates_enabled`, and MAY include `advance_reason`; invalid `target_phase` returns Appendix I `pipeline_phase_invalid_enum_value`.
4. Solo-mode Workspaces MUST auto-apply soft gates when omitted and MUST return HTTP 200 with `warnings[]` when unmet gates are skipped; Team-mode Workspaces MUST reject client-supplied `soft_gates_enabled=true` with Appendix I `phase_advancement_soft_gates_not_permitted_in_team_mode`.
5. Team-mode hard-gate failure MUST return the §32.6 nested error envelope with Appendix I `gate_validation_failed` and endpoint-specific fields under `error.details.failed_checks[]`.
6. The endpoint MUST deduplicate retries for 24 hours by `(Idempotency-Key, workspace_id, target_phase)` and MUST NOT double-emit audit, webhook, Console Bridge, or PostHog side effects on replay.
7. Every successful phase advancement MUST write AuditEvent `phase_advanced` or `phase_advanced_with_unmet_gates`, emit the `workspace.phase_advanced` webhook with §31 retry / DLQ semantics, and project the §4.7.1 Console Bridge Event with `from_phase` / `to_phase` typed as Appendix J `pipeline_phase`.
8. Every error code in the §10.16.1 error table MUST resolve to Appendix I with the same HTTP status.
9. Third-party outage behavior MUST follow §10.16.7: pre-commit dependency failures leave no committed mutation or side effects, while post-commit delivery failures retry from durable outbox / Console Bridge rows without rolling back the buyer Workspace phase.

### 10.16.7 Degradation and Third-Party Outage Handling

**Principle.** Phase advancement is a single buyer-side Workspace transaction over source-of-truth state. Dependencies needed to authorize, validate, or commit that transaction fail closed before mutation. Dependencies used only for summaries, delivery, analytics, or downstream projection degrade after commit through durable retry paths.

| Dependency | Used by phase advancement | Unavailable behavior | Side-effect ordering |
|---|---|---|---|
| Convex | Workspace read, gate validation inputs, optimistic concurrency, transaction commit, AuditEvent / outbox writes. | If Convex is unavailable before commit, return HTTP 503 `phase_advancement_dependency_unavailable` with `error.details.dependency = "convex"` and `Retry-After`; no Workspace mutation, AuditEvent, webhook, Console Bridge Event, PostHog event, or Loops notification is written. If the client timed out after an unknown commit result, retrying the same `Idempotency-Key` MUST recover the cached response or the already-at-target no-op without duplicate side effects. | Convex transaction writes `Workspace.pipeline_phase`, `pipeline_stage_id`, AuditEvent, Console Bridge Event, webhook outbox, PostHog outbox, and notification outbox atomically. |
| WorkOS / auth scope verification | Bearer-token validity, Org membership, Workspace role resolution, and console-axis authorization per §6.6.3 / §32.2.1. | If the request cannot be verified from a still-valid local session / claims cache and WorkOS is unavailable, fail closed before mutation with HTTP 503 `phase_advancement_dependency_unavailable`, `error.details.dependency = "workos"`, and `Retry-After`. Invalid or expired credentials still return the normal 401 / 403 codes. | No audit, webhook, Console Bridge, analytics, or notification side effect is written before authorization passes. |
| Stripe / billing snapshot | Indirect read of plan state for read-only preservation and `evaluation_owner_mode` defaults per §10.16.4 / §10.17 / §34.5 / §34.6. | Phase advancement MUST NOT make a live Stripe call in the hot path. A live Stripe outage does not block advancement when the local plan / preservation snapshot is present and fresh enough for §34.5.1 entitlement refresh rules. Missing, corrupt, or expired local billing snapshot returns HTTP 503 `phase_advancement_dependency_unavailable` with `error.details.dependency = "billing_snapshot"` before mutation. | Plan / preservation checks complete before the phase transaction opens. Stripe reconciliation happens outside the phase-advance transaction. |
| Anthropic / Maya summary | Optional Solo-mode soft-gate explanation copy for unmet gates; deterministic gate validation remains local. | Anthropic unavailability MUST NOT block Solo soft-gate advancement. The response returns HTTP 200 with deterministic `warnings[]`, omits Maya-authored summary copy, and includes `warnings[].summary_source = "deterministic_fallback"`. Audit metadata records `soft_gate_summary_source = "deterministic_fallback"`. Team-mode hard-gate behavior is unchanged. | No Anthropic request may run inside the Convex transaction. Deterministic unmet-gate results are committed with the phase advance; summary generation is best-effort. |
| Console Bridge | Seller-side projection of `phase_advanced` via §4.7.1. | The Console Bridge Event row is written in the same local transaction as the buyer phase advance. If it cannot be written, the transaction fails before commit with `error.details.dependency = "console_bridge_outbox"`. Bridge apply / downstream backlog after commit MUST NOT roll back the buyer Workspace phase; it retries under `bridge_apply_standard` and alerts / DLQs per §25.6 and Appendix C `console_bridge.dlq_storm`. | Buyer Workspace mutation and Console Bridge Event enqueue are atomic; Bridge delivery / seller projection apply are asynchronous post-commit side effects. |
| Webhooks, PostHog, Loops | External delivery of `workspace.phase_advanced`, analytics, and notification fan-out. | Delivery outage MUST NOT block a committed phase advance. Failed delivery retries from the durable outbox using §31 / Appendix F / Appendix G semantics; DLQ handling is observable through existing event pipelines. | Outbox rows are committed with the phase transaction; external sends occur after commit. |

**Commit ordering.**

1. Verify auth / console scope, read Workspace state, and resolve the local plan / preservation snapshot.
2. Validate target phase, gate rules, read-only preservation, and concurrency guard.
3. Open the Convex transaction and atomically write Workspace phase fields, AuditEvent, Console Bridge Event, webhook outbox row, PostHog outbox row, and notification outbox row.
4. Commit, then return the response from committed state.
5. Run webhook, analytics, notification, Maya-summary, and Console Bridge apply workers asynchronously; retry / DLQ failures without mutating `Workspace.pipeline_phase`.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Convex and WorkOS outage tests MUST prove HTTP 503 `phase_advancement_dependency_unavailable` returns before mutation and leaves no AuditEvent, webhook outbox, Console Bridge Event, PostHog outbox, or notification outbox row.
2. Stripe outage tests MUST prove no live Stripe call is required for phase advancement when the local billing snapshot is valid, and missing / corrupt / expired local snapshots fail before mutation with `error.details.dependency = "billing_snapshot"`.
3. Solo soft-gate tests MUST prove Anthropic outage returns HTTP 200 with deterministic unmet-gate warnings and `soft_gate_summary_source = "deterministic_fallback"` while Team-mode hard gates remain blocking.
4. Console Bridge backlog tests MUST prove committed buyer phase advancement is not rolled back when seller projection apply is delayed, retried, or DLQ'd after commit.
5. Replay tests MUST prove the same `Idempotency-Key` after a dependency failure or unknown commit result cannot double-write audit, webhook, Console Bridge, PostHog, or notification side effects.
6. The §M.5 gate `phase_advancement_third_party_outage_completeness` MUST fail if §10.16.1, §10.16.6, this dependency matrix, or Appendix I drift out of alignment.

## 10.17 Cross-Phase State Preservation Under Plan Change {#10.17-cross-phase-state-preservation-under-plan-change}

Plan changes are Org-level billing mutations owned by §32.8.15 and §34.5. This section binds those mutations to the §10 pipeline so an in-flight evaluation has deterministic behavior when the Buyer Org upgrades, downgrades, or changes console scope.

### 10.17.1 Source of Authority

| Surface | Authority | §10 binding |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Plan-change request, idempotency, and emitted billing webhooks | §32.8.15 | §10 consumes only the applied or scheduled plan-change result; it does not author a second plan-change API. |
| Upgrade carry-over | §34.5.1 | In-flight evaluations, Workspace state, RBAC assignments, audit log, and Internal Comments are preserved with no data loss. |
| Downgrade effective time and pre-effective warning | §34.5.2 / §34.5.3 | Downgrades take effect at the billing boundary; over-cap Workspaces surface in the pre-downgrade impact list before enforcement. |
| Downgrade read-only preservation | §34.6 / §4.8.10 | Excess Workspaces enter DowngradeExcessDataBucket read-only preservation; §10 phase mutation is blocked while preserved read-only. |
| Single-Operator Mode default | §2.8.1 / §4.3.1 | `evaluation_owner_mode` is computed at Workspace creation and is not auto-recomputed by later plan changes. |

### 10.17.2 Workspace Preservation Policy

| Plan-change class | Pipeline scope | Phase behavior | Capability / quota behavior | Data preservation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Upgrade to a higher Buyer plan | Any `pipeline_stage_id` including `draft`, `1-13`, `closed`, or `archived` | `pipeline_phase`, `pipeline_stage_id`, `Workspace.status`, phase locks, and existing gate-validation results are unchanged. The Workspace may continue advancing per §10.16. | Newly-unlocked capabilities become available immediately after the §34.5.1 entitlement refresh. Existing `evaluation_owner_mode` is unchanged; the Workspace Owner may switch it manually per §4.3.1. | All Workspace artifacts carry over per §34.5.1. No re-import, re-score, re-invite, or re-approval is required solely because of the upgrade. |
| Downgrade scheduled but not yet effective | Any active phase `1-13` | The Workspace remains fully functional until the §34.5.2 effective timestamp. | The §34.5.3 pre-downgrade validator lists affected Workspaces, object caps, and actions available before the billing boundary. | No data moves to preservation before the effective timestamp. |
| Downgrade effective, Workspace remains within new plan caps | `draft`, active phases `1-13`, `closed`, or `archived` | `pipeline_phase`, `pipeline_stage_id`, and phase locks are unchanged. The Workspace remains read-write and may advance per §10.16. | Future creation of plan-gated objects and capabilities uses the current post-downgrade plan tier. Historical artifacts remain readable and audit-valid. | No DowngradeExcessDataBucket is created for that Workspace. |
| Downgrade effective, Workspace exceeds new plan caps or is selected as excess | Any non-terminal active phase `1-12` | The Workspace enters §34.6 read-only preservation. Phase advancement, amendment writes, score writes, approval actions, Selection Report generation, and contract-closure mutations are blocked until restoration or re-upgrade. Reads, export, audit access, and billing-impact review remain available. | New plan-gated capability invocation is blocked while preserved read-only. Re-upgrade or under-cap resolution restores read-write per §34.6.2. | The Workspace and child artifacts remain preserved in DowngradeExcessDataBucket per §34.6 / §4.8.10; no data is hard-deleted by the plan-change action itself. |
| Downgrade effective after Phase 13 closure | `phase_13_contract_closure`, `closed`, or `archived` | The immutable Selection Record and contract metadata remain immutable. Later archive / retention transitions follow §10.13, Appendix E, and §40.2. | Future optional exports or premium post-evaluation capabilities use the current post-downgrade plan. | Closure artifacts remain governed by §40.2 retention and §34.6 only if the Workspace is bucketed as excess. |
| Console-scope change on a dual-console Org | Buyer Workspaces only | Buyer Workspaces never move across the dual-console firewall. Seller-side plan changes do not mutate Buyer `pipeline_phase`; Buyer-side plan changes do not mutate seller Bid Workspace state except through existing Console Bridge projections. | Console-specific entitlements resolve per §34.12.6 and §1.4. | Console-scoped entities remain in their original console scope; no cross-console data move is permitted. |

### 10.17.3 Fields and State That MUST NOT Auto-Recompute

Plan changes MUST NOT automatically mutate:

- `Workspace.pipeline_phase`
- `Workspace.pipeline_stage_id`
- `Workspace.status`
- `Workspace.evaluation_owner_mode`
- existing Requirements, Use Cases, vendor invitations, amendments, responses, scores, comments, Selection Report drafts, Approval Workflow rows, Defense View artifacts, or Selection Records
- phase-lock and score-immutability outcomes already established by §10.1, §10.10, §10.12, or §10.13

Any user-visible mode change after a plan transition MUST use the explicit §4.3.1 `evaluation_owner_mode` transition path and emit `workspace_evaluation_owner_mode_changed`. Any data preservation or read-only state caused by downgrade MUST be represented through §34.6 / §4.8.10, not by inventing a new Workspace status.

### 10.17.4 Notification and Impact Summary

The plan-change handler MUST attach a Workspace impact summary to the existing billing notification / webhook stream:

- `billing.plan.upgraded` includes affected Workspace count, newly-unlocked capability families, and a statement that in-flight evaluations continue without re-setup.
- `billing.plan.downgrade_scheduled` includes affected Workspace IDs visible to the recipient, over-cap classes, `scheduled_effective_at`, and available §34.5.3 actions.
- `billing.plan.downgraded` includes affected Workspace IDs visible to the recipient, any DowngradeExcessDataBucket IDs, read-only Workspace count, and restoration CTA per §34.6.2.

Recipients are governed by Appendix C Billing-Domain Events: Billing Admin, Org Owner, and affected Workspace Owners where the row already includes Workspace Owner digest delivery. The impact summary MUST respect the Workspace membership scope and the dual-console firewall; a Workspace Owner receives only Workspaces they can already access.

### 10.17.5 Acceptance Criteria

1. A plan upgrade MUST NOT mutate `pipeline_phase`, `pipeline_stage_id`, `Workspace.status`, or `evaluation_owner_mode` for any existing Workspace.
2. A plan downgrade scheduled for a future billing boundary MUST NOT place any Workspace into read-only preservation before `effective_at`.
3. At downgrade effective time, a Workspace that remains within the new plan caps MUST remain read-write and may advance through §10.16.
4. At downgrade effective time, a Workspace selected as excess or over cap MUST enter §34.6 read-only preservation; §10.16 phase advancement returns a read-only/preservation failure until the Workspace is restored or re-upgraded.
5. Existing phase artifacts MUST remain readable and exportable after any plan change, subject only to §34.6 read-only preservation, §40.2 retention, and §6.8 DSAR/legal-retention rules.
6. `evaluation_owner_mode` MUST remain unchanged on every plan transition unless the Workspace Owner performs the explicit §4.3.1 mode switch.
7. Plan-change notifications MUST include the §10.17.4 Workspace impact summary and MUST scope each recipient to Workspaces they can already access.
8. The §M.5 gate `plan_change_pipeline_phase_grandfather_completeness` MUST fail if §10.17, §32.8.15, §34.5, §34.6, or Appendix C Billing-Domain Events drift on plan-change impact handling.

## 10.18 Cold-Pipeline No-Vendor-Response Abort {#10.18-cold-pipeline-no-vendor-response-abort}

This section closes the cold-pipeline failure mode where a Workspace cannot advance because no vendor confirms intent to bid, no vendor submits a response, or no scoreable responses remain before scoring. It is not a soft-gate skip and not the §10.14 cancellation / soft-delete lifecycle.

### 10.18.1 Eligibility

The no-vendor-response abort is available only to a Workspace Owner, Workspace Admin, Use Case Lead, or Org Owner with Buyer-console write access when all of the following are true:

| Current phase | Required predicate | Failed advance gate |
|---|---|---|
| `phase_5_vendor_outreach` | Phase 5 deadline elapsed; ≥ 1 vendor was invited; zero vendors have confirmed intent to bid. | Phase 5 -> Phase 6 `gate_validation_failed` because `vendor_confirmed_intent_count = 0`. |
| `phase_6_vendor_bidding` | `bidding_close_at` elapsed; the §10.6 minimum bidding window was satisfied; zero Vendor Responses were submitted. | Phase 6 -> Phase 7 `gate_validation_failed` because `vendor_response_submitted_count = 0`. |
| `phase_9_final_clarifications` | All remaining Vendor Responses are withdrawn, invalidated, or removed; zero scoreable responses remain. | Phase 9 -> Phase 10 `gate_validation_failed` because `scoreable_vendor_response_count = 0`. |

The abort is unavailable in Phases 1-4, Phases 7-8 when at least one submitted response remains under due diligence, Phases 10-13 after scoring begins, any `status != active`, or any Workspace in §34.6 read-only preservation.

### 10.18.2 Endpoint

```
POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/abort
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
Idempotency-Key: {client-generated UUID per §32.3 idempotency convention; required}
X-Sourcera-Console: buyer
```

**Auth scope (§32 / §6.6.3 canonical scope axis):** `write:workspaces`.

**Rate-limit class (§32.4.5):** `data_mutation` — 60 requests/minute per Org per Workspace.

**Cursor pagination:** n/a (single-resource mutation).

**Request body schema:**

```json
{
  "reason": "no_vendor_response",
  "reason_note": "string (≤500 chars; optional)",
  "reuse_intent": "copy_requirements_to_future_workspace"
}
```

- `reason` is required and MUST equal Appendix J `workspace_closure_reason` value `no_vendor_response` for this endpoint version.
- `reason_note` is optional, visible only to buyer Workspace members, and DSAR-redacted if it contains subject PII.
- `reuse_intent` is optional and may be `copy_requirements_to_future_workspace`, `archive_without_reuse`, or `undecided`. It is advisory metadata for the M4 prompt (§48.5.4), not a state transition.

**Response (success — 200 OK):**

```json
{
  "workspace_id": "ws_01H8...",
  "status": "closed",
  "closure_reason": "no_vendor_response",
  "pipeline_stage_id": 14,
  "closed_at": "2026-04-11T14:30:00Z",
  "closed_by_user_id": "usr_...",
  "preserved_artifacts": [
    "requirements",
    "use_cases",
    "vendor_discovery_artifacts",
    "invitation_audit",
    "marketplace_search_context"
  ],
  "selection_record_created": false,
  "notification_event": "workspace_no_vendor_response_aborted"
}
```

**Error codes (registered in Appendix I):**

| HTTP | Code | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | `unauthenticated` | Missing / invalid bearer token. |
| 403 | `workspace_role_insufficient_for_phase_advance` | Caller lacks Workspace-write authority. |
| 404 | `workspace_not_found` | `workspace_id` not visible to caller. |
| 409 | `workspace_abort_already_terminal` | Workspace is already `closed` or `archived`. |
| 422 | `workspace_abort_not_eligible_no_vendor_response` | Eligibility predicates in §10.18.1 are not satisfied. |
| 503 | `phase_advancement_dependency_unavailable` | Required pre-commit dependency unavailable; no state or side effects commit. |

### 10.18.3 State, Retention, and Reuse Effects

On success, the abort handler atomically:

1. Sets `Workspace.status = closed`, `Workspace.closure_reason = no_vendor_response`, and `pipeline_stage_id = 14`.
2. Preserves the last active `pipeline_phase` in the AuditEvent diff payload; no forward phase advancement is emitted.
3. Writes AuditEvent `workspace_no_vendor_response_aborted` with the eligibility predicate snapshot and `reuse_intent`.
4. Enqueues Appendix C event `workspace_no_vendor_response_aborted` and Appendix G event `workspace_no_vendor_response_aborted`.
5. Leaves Requirements, Use Cases, Target Accounts, Marketplace search context, invitation audit rows, Internal Comments, and Q&A artifacts retained with the Workspace under §40.2.
6. Skips Selection Report, Selection Record, Defense View, scoring snapshot, contract metadata, cancellation soft-delete, and recovery-window creation.

M4 Next Evaluation Kickoff Session (§48.5.4) may offer to seed a future Workspace from the preserved Requirements / Use Cases / discovery context. Reuse creates a new Workspace; it does not reopen the aborted Workspace.

### 10.18.4 Notification and Console Bridge

`workspace_no_vendor_response_aborted` is a buyer-workspace closure notification. Recipients are Workspace members and vendors that were invited or added to a Bid Workspace for this evaluation. Vendor-facing copy is neutral and carries only: procurement name, closure timestamp, and a statement that the buyer closed the evaluation because no responses were available. Buyer `reason_note`, internal comments, sourcing strategy, and Marketplace search context are never carried to sellers.

No new Console Bridge `event_kind` is required. The handler may enqueue the existing `workspace_canceled` bridge projection only when a seller-side Bid Workspace exists and the seller had visibility into the evaluation; payload redaction follows §4.7.1 and MUST set `canceled_reason_public = "no_vendor_response_abort"`. The event is not a §10.14 cancellation and does not create a recovery window.

### 10.18.5 Acceptance Criteria

1. Phase 5 -> Phase 6, Phase 6 -> Phase 7, and Phase 9 -> Phase 10 advancement MUST remain blocked with `gate_validation_failed` when the relevant zero-vendor predicate is true; Solo soft gates MUST NOT advance a Workspace into scoring with zero scoreable vendor responses.
2. `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/abort` with `reason=no_vendor_response` MUST be idempotent by `(Idempotency-Key, workspace_id, reason)` for 24 hours and MUST NOT duplicate audit, notification, webhook, Console Bridge, or PostHog side effects on replay.
3. Successful abort MUST set `Workspace.status=closed`, `closure_reason=no_vendor_response`, and `pipeline_stage_id=14`; it MUST NOT introduce a new `workspace_status` enum value.
4. Successful abort MUST NOT create a Selection Report, Selection Record, Defense View, score snapshot, contract metadata, Cancellation Request, cancellation grace window, or `workspace_canceled` Appendix C event.
5. Preserved artifacts MUST remain readable/exportable to authorized buyer Workspace members per §40.2 and §6.8; seller projections remain limited to the redacted notification / bridge payload in §10.18.4.
6. Appendix E, Appendix J, Appendix C, Appendix G, Appendix I, and §M.5 MUST all contain the no-vendor-response abort bindings authored in this section.
7. The §M.5 gate `cold_pipeline_no_vendor_response_abort_path` MUST fail if a future edit reintroduces a zero-vendor indefinite block, creates `aborted_no_vendor_response` as a Workspace status, or routes this path through §10.14 cancellation.

# 11\. Buyer Console — Navigation & Layout {#11.-buyer-console-—-navigation-&-layout}

## 11.1 Overview {#11.1-overview}

The Buyer Console is the primary interface for procurement teams to manage sourcing evaluations. It combines a persistent sidebar navigation with content areas that adapt based on the active Phase and user role. The layout is designed to support both rapid list-view interaction (matrix view) and deep-dive analysis (detail view).

## 11.2 Sidebar Navigation Structure {#11.2-sidebar-navigation-structure}

### 11.2.1 Layout & Dimensions

- **Expanded width:** 240px  
- **Collapsed width:** 48px  
- **Collapse/expand toggle:** Top-left corner, visible in both states  
- **Collapse state behavior:** Icons only, tooltips on hover, no section labels  
- **Position:** Fixed, left edge, full viewport height, z-index 100  
- **Background:** Workspace theme primary color (dark by default)  
- **Text color:** Workspace theme text-on-primary (white by default)

### 11.2.2 Navigation Sections

All sections appear in the following order. Phase-gated sections render as phase-unavailable items when conditions are not met.

**Logo & Workspace Selector**

- Sourcera logo (16x16px) at top when collapsed, logo \+ workspace name when expanded  
- Workspace name truncated at 20 characters with ellipsis  
- Click to open workspace switcher modal (non-blocking, dismissible)

**Primary Navigation (Always Available)**

1. **Dashboard** (icon: home)  
     
   - Route: `/workspace/:workspace_id/dashboard`  
   - Always available from Phase 1  
   - Shows Pulse Health Score, Inbox count, recent activity

   

2. **Sourcing** (icon: briefcase)  
     
   - Route: `/workspace/:workspace_id/sourcing`  
   - Always available from Phase 1  
   - Expands to sub-items: Active, Paused, Archived  
   - Active shows count of non-archived workspaces

   

3. **Intelligence** (icon: brain)  
     
   - Phase-gated: Available Phase 10+  
   - Route: `/workspace/:workspace_id/intelligence`  
   - If Phase \< 10: renders as disabled item with tooltip "Available in Phase 10 (Scoring)"  
   - Tooltip background: light gray, dark text, 8px padding, max-width 200px

   

4. **Marketplace** (icon: store)  
     
   - Phase-gated: Available Phase 6+  
   - Route: `/workspace/:workspace_id/marketplace`  
   - If Phase \< 6: renders as disabled item with tooltip "Available in Phase 6 (Vendor Participation)"  
   - Shows count of available vendors matching workspace scope

   

5. **Templates** (icon: template)  
     
   - Always available from Phase 1  
   - Route: `/workspace/:workspace_id/templates`  
   - Organization-scoped, not workspace-scoped

   

6. **Settings** (icon: gear)  
     
   - Always available  
   - Route: `/workspace/:workspace_id/settings`  
   - Expands to sub-items based on user role (see Section 8 — Organization Admin)

**Contextual Navigation (Workspace-Level)**

- Appears below Primary Navigation when a workspace is active  
- Current workspace name as a section header  
- Nested items (depth 2):  
  - **Use Cases** (icon: folder): Count of active use cases  
  - **Vendors** (icon: users): Count of invited vendors  
  - **Team** (icon: people): Count of team members in workspace  
  - **Activity** (icon: feed): Recent changes, SLA alerts, scoring activity

### 11.2.3 Phase Gating Rules

- **Phase unavailable items:** Render with 50% opacity, strikethrough text, disabled cursor  
- **Tooltip trigger:** Hover or focus on disabled item  
- **Tooltip content:** "Available in Phase N (Phase Name)"  
- **Tooltip appearance:** Appears to the right of the sidebar (or left if sidebar is collapsed), 100ms delay  
- **Click behavior on disabled item:** No-op, tooltip remains visible for 2 seconds

### 11.2.4 Responsive Behavior

- **Desktop (≥1024px):** Sidebar fully visible, expanded by default  
- **Tablet (768px–1023px):** Sidebar fully visible, collapsed by default (can be toggled expanded)  
- **Mobile (\<768px):** Sidebar hidden, replaced by bottom tab bar (Dashboard, Sourcing, Intelligence, Marketplace, Settings) with icons \+ labels (12px font)

## 11.3 Content Layout & Regions {#11.3-content-layout-&-regions}

### 11.3.1 Main Content Area

- **Left margin:** Adjusts based on sidebar state (240px expanded, 48px collapsed)  
- **Transition:** 200ms ease-in-out when toggling sidebar  
- **Header region:** Contains breadcrumbs, title, action buttons (height: 60px)  
- **Breadcrumb structure:** Workspace \> Section \> \[Subsection\] \> \[Item\]. Clickable, last item bold/non-clickable.  
- **Content region:** Scrollable, padding 24px, background: workspace theme background

### 11.3.2 Content View Types

**Matrix View (Default for Lists)**

- **Use:** Use Cases, Requirements, Scoring, Scenario comparison  
- **Structure:** Spreadsheet-like grid, rows \= items, columns \= attributes  
- **Row height:** 48px (text), 32px (compact mode toggle available)  
- **Columns:** Configurable visibility via settings icon in column header  
- **Sorting:** Click column header to sort A-Z or reverse; chevron indicates direction  
- **Filtering:** Filter bar above matrix (chip-based, removable filters)  
- **Selection:** Checkbox column (shift+click for range, cmd/ctrl+click for multi), "Select All" in header  
- **Inline edit:** Double-click cell to edit (single-cell edit, not row-level). Changes auto-save (optimistic mutation with rollback). Edited cell shows checkmark, returns to display mode on blur.  
- **Floating action bar:** Appears when ≥1 row selected. Contains: Bulk Actions (dropdown), Clear Selection button. Positioned 24px above matrix, horizontally centered, z-index 50\.  
- **Keyboard navigation:**  
  - **J/K:** Navigate down/up one row  
  - **H/L:** Scroll left/right in wide matrices  
  - **Space:** Toggle selection of current row  
  - **Enter:** Open detail view of current row  
  - **Escape:** Deselect all, close any open popovers  
- **Right-click context menu:** Copy, Edit, Duplicate, Delete (if permissions allow), Copy Link  
- **Pagination:** "Load more" button (lazy-load) or page controls (5/10/25/50 rows per page)

**Detail View**

- **Trigger:** Click row in matrix view, or navigate to detail route  
- **Layout:** Sidebar (30% width, sticky, scrollable) \+ main content (70% width, scrollable)  
- **Sidebar contents:** Quick info (name, status, phase), metadata fields, related items  
- **Main content:** Full form/rich text editor, comments thread, related items panel  
- **Navigation:** "Previous" and "Next" buttons at bottom (context-aware, disabled if at boundary)  
- **Close:** X button (top-right) or Escape key, returns to matrix view, maintains scroll position

**Report View (Phase 11+)**

- **Trigger:** "Export" or "View Report" action in sourcing context  
- **Format:** Printable single-column layout, high contrast, no sidebars  
- **Export options:** PDF (via browser print), CSV (via download), Email (via dialog)

### 11.3.3 Empty States

- **Messaging:** Headline (16px, bold) \+ description (14px) \+ primary action button  
- **Illustration:** Generic icon (48x48px) centered above text  
- **Examples:**  
  - No Use Cases: "Start your sourcing evaluation. Create your first Use Case to define what you're looking for."  
  - No Vendors: "Invite vendors to participate. Search the Marketplace or add custom vendors."  
  - No Scoring data (Phase \<10): "Scoring analytics will appear when scoring begins in Phase 10."

## 11.4 Persistent UI Elements {#11.4-persistent-ui-elements}

### 11.4.1 Top Bar (Global)

- **Height:** 48px  
- **Position:** Fixed, top, spanning full viewport width  
- **Contents (left to right):**  
  - Workspace name (bold, 14px)  
  - Phase indicator: "Phase 7 (Vendor Participation)" with progress bar (width \= phase\_number/12 \* 100%)  
  - Spacer  
  - User avatar (32x32px, clickable for user menu)  
  - Notifications bell icon (with unread count badge, red)  
- **Background:** Workspace theme secondary color  
- **Sticky beneath:** Top padding on content area \= 48px

### 11.4.2 Notifications Popover

- **Trigger:** Click bell icon  
- **Position:** Top-right, anchored to bell  
- **Contents:** List of unread notifications, "Mark All as Read" button, link to "Settings" for notification preferences  
- **Dismissible:** Click outside or press Escape  
- **Persistence:** Unread count persists across page reloads

### 11.4.3 User Menu

- **Trigger:** Click avatar  
- **Contents:**  
  - User name (bold, 12px)  
  - User email (gray, 12px)  
  - Divider  
  - "Workspace Settings" (links to `/workspace/:workspace_id/settings`)  
  - "Organization Settings" (links to `/organization/:org_id/settings`)  
  - "Help & Feedback" (links to help center)  
  - "Sign Out"  
- **Keyboard:** Escape to close  
- **Position:** Anchored to avatar, top-right

## 11.5 Acceptance Criteria {#11.5-acceptance-criteria}

### 11.5.1 Navigation

- [ ] Sidebar toggles between 240px (expanded) and 48px (collapsed) with 200ms transition  
- [ ] Phase-gated items appear disabled (50% opacity, strikethrough) when Phase \< gating threshold  
- [ ] Tooltip appears on hover of disabled item, disappears after 2s or on mouseout  
- [ ] Breadcrumb renders all ancestors and current item; last item is bold and non-clickable  
- [ ] Collapsing sidebar on desktop does not hide or lose focus from current page content  
- [ ] Mobile view (\<768px) replaces sidebar with bottom tab bar with 5 primary items  
- [ ] Sidebar collapse state persists in localStorage per workspace

### 11.5.2 Matrix View

- [ ] J/K keyboard navigation moves cursor up/down one row, visual highlight follows  
- [ ] Space toggles checkbox for current row; shift+Space toggles range  
- [ ] Cmd/Ctrl+A selects all visible rows (not paginated rows)  
- [ ] Double-click cell enters edit mode; blur or Enter saves; Escape reverts  
- [ ] Column sorting by header click; chevron indicates direction (ascending/descending)  
- [ ] Filter chips appear above matrix; click X to remove filter  
- [ ] Floating action bar appears when ≥1 row selected, positioned 24px above matrix  
- [ ] Right-click context menu appears with Copy, Edit, Duplicate, Delete, Copy Link  
- [ ] "Load More" or pagination controls display remaining row count

### 11.5.3 Detail View

- [ ] Clicking matrix row opens detail view; maintains scroll position in matrix on close  
- [ ] Detail view sidebar is sticky (does not scroll with main content)  
- [ ] "Previous" and "Next" buttons navigate to adjacent items; disabled at boundaries  
- [ ] Escape or X button closes detail view, returns to matrix  
- [ ] URL changes to `/workspace/:id/section/:item_id/detail`; back button returns to matrix view

### 11.5.4 Empty States

- [ ] Empty state appears when section has no items (0 use cases, 0 vendors, etc.)  
- [ ] Headline and description are clearly visible  
- [ ] Primary action button is styled and clickable  
- [ ] Empty state icon is centered and 48x48px

### 11.5.5 Responsive Layout

- [ ] On tablet (768px–1023px), sidebar is collapsed by default  
- [ ] On mobile (\<768px), sidebar is replaced with bottom tab bar  
- [ ] Content area adjusts margin based on sidebar state without overflow  
- [ ] Matrix view columns stack or scroll horizontally on narrow viewports

# 12\. Policy-Powered Requirement Generation {#12.-policy-powered-requirement-generation}

## 12.1 Overview {#12.1-overview}

Policy Ingestion is a multi-stage pipeline that converts compliance documents (PDFs, Word) into structured requirements via LLM-powered extraction, semantic deduplication, and traceability mapping. Ingested requirements enter the Amendment Protocol before publishing to the workspace.

## 12.2 Supported Document Types {#12.2-supported-document-types}

- **Formats:** PDF, DOCX  
- **Max file size:** 500 pages (per plan limits)  
- **Languages:** English (v6.0); other languages rejected with error message "Currently English language documents are supported. Please translate your document and resubmit."  
- **Accessibility:** Must be readable (scanned images rejected with error "Document could not be parsed. Please ensure it is not image-only and is readable.")

## 12.3 Framework Detection & Classification {#12.3-framework-detection-&-classification}

### 12.3.1 Detection Pipeline

1. **Parse & Tokenize:** Upload endpoint streams document to Claude Opus (streaming via API)  
2. **Framework Inference:** Opus analyzes first 30 pages to identify framework(s) and compliance standard  
3. **Confidence Scoring:** Opus outputs `framework_list` with confidence 0.0–1.0 per framework  
4. **Threshold Logic:**  
   - **≥0.80:** Framework accepted, proceeds to extraction  
   - **0.60–0.79:** "Low Confidence" badge appears, user prompted to confirm or correct via dropdown  
   - **\<0.60:** "Unknown Framework — Manual Review Recommended" message, dropdown lists common frameworks, user must select

### 12.3.2 Supported Frameworks

- **Compliance:** SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, PCI-DSS  
- **Industry-Specific:** FedRAMP, HITRUST, SSAE 18, CIS Critical Security Controls  
- **Custom:** "Custom Policy / Other" — user must manually assign use case category (Security, Compliance, Operations, Data Privacy)

The framework vocabulary above is registered as the `policy_framework_kind` enum in Appendix J (`v7.2.0-REM Phase 10` block; closed-set with `custom_other` as the only fallback); the Custom-path use-case categories are the `policy_custom_use_case_category` enum. The confidence thresholds in §12.3.1 map to `policy_framework_confidence_band` / `policy_framework_inference_outcome` (Appendix J). Do not restate these value lists elsewhere — cite Appendix J.

### 12.3.3 User Interaction

- **Confirmation Modal:** Appears immediately after upload, displays detected frameworks with confidence bars  
- **Actions:** Confirm & Continue, Edit Selection (opens dropdown), Cancel (discards upload)  
- **Dropdown:** Searchable, filtered by document context, displays framework \+ description (20 words max)

## 12.4 Control Extraction {#12.4-control-extraction}

### 12.4.1 Extraction Process

1. **Input:** Parsed document \+ confirmed framework(s)  
2. **Model:** Claude Opus (streaming)  
3. **Extraction:** Full document tokenized, Opus extracts discrete controls/requirements per framework structure  
4. **Output Schema:** Per control:  
   - `control_id` (string, framework-specific, e.g., "2.1.1" for ISO)  
   - `title` (string, ≤100 chars)  
   - `description` (string, ≤500 chars, Markdown supported)  
   - `framework_section` (string, e.g., "Access Control")  
   - `raw_text` (string, verbatim from document, used for traceability)  
   - `page_references` (array of ints, page numbers)

### 12.4.2 Failure Handling

- **Network error during extraction:** Retry up to 3x with exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s); if all fail, error toast: "Extraction failed. Please try again or contact support."  
- **Malformed PDF:** Error toast: "Document could not be processed. Please ensure it is a valid PDF or Word document."  
- **Token limit exceeded (\>100k tokens):** Partial results returned; toast warns "Document exceeded processing limit. Extracted 187 of 234 controls. Review extracted controls and re-upload remaining sections."  
- **Timeout (\>15 minutes):** Extraction cancelled, error toast: "Processing took too long. Please try again with a shorter document (under 300 pages)."

## 12.5 Deduplication {#12.5-deduplication}

### 12.5.1 Semantic Deduplication

1. **Trigger:** After extraction, if ≥2 controls exist  
2. **Model:** Claude Haiku (cost-optimized)  
3. **Process:**  
   - Compare all extracted controls pairwise  
   - Compute semantic similarity via embedding-based comparison  
   - Flag pairs with similarity ≥0.90 (90% threshold)  
4. **Output:** Dedup report with candidate groups, recommended merge action, retention score (which control to keep)  
5. **User Review:** Modal displays groups with toggle to accept/reject merge per pair  
6. **Failure:** If dedup fails (API error), issue toast "Deduplication failed. Review controls manually for duplicates." User can proceed without dedup or retry.

### 12.5.2 Dedup Modal Interaction

- **Layout:** List of detected duplicate pairs, each shows:  
  - Control A (title \+ framework \+ snippet)  
  - Control B (title \+ framework \+ snippet)  
  - Similarity score (0-100%)  
  - "Merge" checkbox (default checked if confidence \>95%)  
  - "Keep A" / "Keep B" radio buttons if merge is checked  
- **Actions:** "Accept All Recommendations", "Reject All", "Review Individually" (toggle each pair)  
- **Proceeding:** Deselected pairs are both retained; merged pairs discard non-selected control

## 12.6 Traceability Mapping {#12.6-traceability-mapping}

### 12.6.1 Mapping Process

1. **Trigger:** After dedup resolution  
2. **Model:** Claude Sonnet (balance of speed & accuracy)  
3. **Input:** Control set \+ original document text  
4. **Mapping:** For each control, identify:  
   - `source_section` (document section heading)  
   - `implementation_guidance` (extracted how-to or example from doc, ≤300 chars)  
   - `evidence_indicators` (what evidence would satisfy this control, ≤200 chars)  
5. **Output:** Enriched control objects with above fields added

### 12.6.2 Storage & Retrieval

- **Traceability data** stored in `control.traceability` object  
- Used in reports to show document source and evidence hints to vendors

## 12.7 Requirement Conversion & Amendment Protocol {#12.7-requirement-conversion-&-amendment-protocol}

### 12.7.1 Control-to-Requirement Mapping

After traceability, each control is converted to a requirement:

- **Source:** `control.control_id`, `control.title`, `control.description`, `control.framework_section`  
- **Requirement fields:**  
  - `title` (inherited from control title)  
  - `description` (inherited from control description)  
  - `category` (mapped from framework section, e.g., "Access Control" → Security)  
  - `type` (set to "Capability")  
  - `framework_reference` (control\_id \+ framework name, e.g., "ISO 27001 2.1.1")  
  - `use_case_id` (pre-selected based on framework context; user can override)  
  - `source` (set to "Policy Ingestion")  
  - `source_document_id` (traces back to uploaded PDF)

### 12.7.2 Amendment Protocol Entry

**Each generated requirement individually enters the Amendment Protocol (see Section 10.3):**

- **Initial state:** PENDING\_REVIEW (held in draft)  
- **Proposed by:** System (automation)  
- **Assigned to:** Workspace Owner (or Use Case Lead if framework matches known use case)  
- **Review deadline:** 7 days  
- **Notification:** Email sent to Workspace Owner with summary of all ingested requirements

### 12.7.3 Batch Amendment UI

**For workspaces with ≥5 proposed amendments:**

- **Batch Review Modal:** Workspace Owner can review all amendments in a single modal  
- **Layout:**  
  - Left panel: List of amendments (grouped by use case)  
  - Right panel: Detail view (title, description, framework ref, source doc)  
  - Action buttons: "Accept", "Request Changes", "Reject"  
- **Batch actions (top-level):** "Accept All", "Reject All", "Request Changes for All"  
- **Individual actions:** Per-amendment actions apply to that amendment only  
- **Partial approval:** User can accept 3, reject 2, request changes on 1 within the same batch  
- **Batch atomic contract:** Batch does NOT auto-close when all amendments are actioned. User must explicitly click "Close & Publish" to apply all changes. If user navigates away, batch state is persisted (not lost).  
- **Outcome:** Each amendment state transitions to APPROVED/REJECTED/PENDING\_REFINEMENT independently  
- **Publishing:** Approved amendments auto-transition to ACTIVE; rejected amendments are discarded; pending-refinement amendments remain in PENDING\_REVIEW until refined and re-submitted

## 12.8 Plan Limits & Costs {#12.8-plan-limits-&-costs}

### 12.8.1 Ingestion Limits

Plan tier set per §34.1.1 (Buyer). Policy Ingestion uses the Opus-tier capability `policy_parsing` and is wallet-charged per §34.3.4; the per-tier ingestion-count caps below are operational throughput limits to prevent runaway batches and live in the Authored Extension table at §34.1.1 footnote line "Policy Ingestion (Opus capability)" — those §34.1.1 cells govern wallet-charging and Free-tier allowance behavior, while the table below governs throughput caps.

| Plan tier (per §34.1.1) | Ingestions/Month | Max Pages/Upload | Total Pages/Month |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Free | Free Allowance + Wallet (per §34.1.1) | 100 | 300 |
| Starter | 3 | 100 | 300 |
| Growth | 10 | 250 | 2,500 |
| Scale | Unlimited (subject to wallet) | 500 | Unlimited |
| Enterprise | Committed (per §34.1.1) | 500 | Unlimited |

### 12.8.2 Cost Model

- **Framework Detection (Opus):** $15–30 per ingestion (varies by document length, batched for efficiency)  
- **Deduplication (Haiku):** \~$0.50 per ingestion (minimal token usage)  
- **Traceability Mapping (Sonnet):** $2–5 per ingestion  
- **Total per ingestion:** \~$17.50–35.50  
- **Passed to customer:** Bundled into per-ingestion cost (not per-page), displayed in pricing UI

## 12.9 Acceptance Criteria {#12.9-acceptance-criteria}

### 12.9.1 Framework Detection

- [ ] Confidence ≥0.80 → proceed without prompt  
- [ ] Confidence 0.60–0.79 → "Low Confidence" badge, confirmation modal shown  
- [ ] Confidence \<0.60 → "Unknown Framework" message, user selects framework from dropdown  
- [ ] User can edit framework selection before proceeding  
- [ ] Unsupported language detected → error message in toast, upload rejected  
- [ ] Scanned-image PDF → error message in toast, upload rejected

### 12.9.2 Control Extraction

- [ ] All controls extracted with control\_id, title, description, framework\_section, page\_references  
- [ ] Network error → retry 3x with exponential backoff; after 3 failures, error toast shown  
- [ ] Malformed PDF → error toast within 5 seconds  
- [ ] Token limit exceeded → partial results shown, warning toast indicates number of controls skipped  
- [ ] Timeout \>15min → user notified, extraction halted, user can retry

### 12.9.3 Deduplication

- [ ] Pairs with similarity ≥0.90 flagged for dedup  
- [ ] Modal displays both controls with similarity percentage  
- [ ] User can toggle "Merge" per pair; "Keep A"/"Keep B" radio buttons control retention  
- [ ] "Accept All Recommendations" button applies all default recommendations  
- [ ] API failure during dedup → error toast, user can proceed without dedup or retry

### 12.9.4 Traceability Mapping

- [ ] Each control enriched with source\_section, implementation\_guidance, evidence\_indicators  
- [ ] Data persists in control.traceability object  
- [ ] Traceability data displayed in reports

### 12.9.5 Amendment Protocol

- [ ] Each generated requirement enters PENDING\_REVIEW state in Amendment Protocol  
- [ ] Workspace Owner notified via email with summary of amendments  
- [ ] Batch Amendment modal displays when ≥5 amendments are PENDING\_REVIEW  
- [ ] User can accept/reject/request changes per amendment or in batch  
- [ ] Approved amendments transition to ACTIVE upon "Close & Publish"  
- [ ] Rejected amendments discarded; pending amendments remain in review  
- [ ] Batch state persists if user navigates away

### 12.9.6 Plan Limits

- [ ] Starter plan: max 3 ingestions/month, max 100 pages/upload (per §12.8.1)  
- [ ] Enterprise plan: unlimited ingestions, max 500 pages/upload  
- [ ] Over-limit attempts show error toast with upgrade prompt

# 13\. Scoring & Grading {#13.-scoring-&-grading}

## 13.1 Overview {#13.1-overview}

Scoring is the process by which evaluators grade vendor responses against requirements using a standardized rubric. Scores are aggregated into use case and vendor totals, which feed into scenario modeling and TCO blending. Scoring is available in Phases 10–11 and immutable at Phase 12 entry.

**Solo Mode surface compression (Phase 14.6).** Scoring engine semantics — rubric, weighting, exclusion, append-only history, override tracking, divergence detection, aggregation, auto-scoring, lifecycle, and Phase 12 lock — are invariant across `Workspace.evaluation_owner_mode` settings. Solo Mode renders the scoring work under the **Score** step of the four-step compressed progress bar (§3.14.1), which aggregates engine Phases 7 (Vendor Response Refinement), 8 (Buyer Due Diligence & Demos), 9 (Final Vendor Clarifications), and 10 (Team Evaluation & Scoring). Team Mode renders the full 13-phase chip ribbon (§3.3.1) unchanged and exposes the per-phase chips for Phases 7–10 individually. Divergence detection (§13.6.2) is engine-on / surface-suppressed in Solo Mode (single-scorer condition per §2.8.4); the underlying append-only `individual_grades[]` history (§13.5.1) is written identically in both modes. Score-modification audit trail, override tracking, EX exclusion approval queue, and auto-scoring rules (§13.4–§13.8) all run identically in both modes — the surface compression is purely a rendering decision keyed to `evaluation_owner_mode`. The Phase 12 score-lock banner ("Scores locked at Phase 12 — to change, return to Phase 11") renders in both modes and is unchanged by §3.14 compression.

## 13.2 Rubric Definition {#13.2-rubric-definition}

### 13.2.1 Grade Scale

| Grade | Code | Value | Definition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Fully Meets | FM | 1.0 | Vendor response fully satisfies the requirement |
| Partially Meets | PM | 0.1–0.9 (configurable) | Vendor response satisfies part of the requirement |
| Does Not Meet | DNM | 0.0 | Vendor does not address the requirement |
| Excluded | EX | — | Vendor-requirement pair is excluded from scoring |

### 13.2.2 Rubric Configuration

- **PM Default Value:** 0.6 (configurable per workspace, range 0.1–0.9)  
- **FM Value:** Locked at 1.0  
- **DNM Value:** Locked at 0.0  
- **EX Handling:** Per-vendor per-requirement. See Section 13.4.  
- **Grade assignment:** Via dropdown during scoring, always in view

**Persistence.** Rubric is Workspace configuration, not a standalone §4.3 entity in v7.1.1. The canonical data-model home is `Workspace.rubric_config_json` (§4.3.1), initialized from `EvalStarter.default_rubric` (§4.5.9) during §13.12 materialization and then mutable through Workspace Settings. Historical rubric changes write Audit Event rows; if future product behavior needs versioned rubric history or approval workflow, that versioned entity must be authored as an Authored Extension before implementation.

## 13.3 Requirement Weighting {#13.3-requirement-weighting}

### 13.3.1 Weight Definition

- **Range:** 0–20 (integer)  
- **Semantics:**  
  - 0 \= Informational (excluded from scoring denominator)  
  - 1–5 \= Low importance  
  - 6–10 \= Medium importance  
  - 11–15 \= High importance  
  - 16–20 \= Critical  
- **Enforced rule:** Informational requirements (weight 0\) cannot be manually changed to non-zero; they are locked at 0 and appear with "Informational" label  
- **Configuration:** Set at use case creation or edited via Workspace Settings \> Use Cases

### 13.3.2 Weight Validation

- **Scenario Modeling:** All weights in a scenario cannot simultaneously be 0 (would cause divide-by-zero). Validation rule enforced on save.  
- **Error message:** "At least one requirement must have a non-zero weight."

## 13.4 Exclusion Handling (EX Grade) {#13.4-exclusion-handling-(ex-grade)}

### 13.4.1 Per-Vendor Exclusion Logic

- **EX is per-vendor:** Vendor A can be excluded (EX) on Requirement 1, while Vendor B is graded (FM/PM/DNM) on the same requirement  
- **Denominator impact:**  
  - For Vendor A: Requirement 1 is NOT in the denominator (not counted toward total requirements)  
  - For Vendor B: Requirement 1 IS in the denominator (all non-zero-weight requirements included)  
- **Example:**  
  - Requirement 1 (weight 5), Requirement 2 (weight 3\)  
  - Vendor A: Req1=EX, Req2=FM → Total \= (0 × 5 \+ 1.0 × 3\) / 3 \= 1.0 (100%)  
  - Vendor B: Req1=FM, Req2=DNM → Total \= (1.0 × 5 \+ 0.0 × 3\) / 8 \= 0.625 (62.5%)

### 13.4.2 Exclusion Proposal & Approval

- **Who proposes:** Reviewer (scoring team member)  
- **How:** Dropdown shows "Exclude (EX)" option alongside FM/PM/DNM  
- **Additional field:** `exception_reason` (required; length per §39 `Score.exception_reason` row) explains why vendor is excluded  
  - Examples: "Vendor does not operate in target geography", "Vendor already contracted; this is reference only"  
- **Approval required:** Workspace Owner OR Use Case Lead (if assigned)  
- **Until approved:** EX grade is in PENDING state (visually distinct, maybe gray background)  
- **Approval action:** Reviewer sees pending EX grades in a queue; approver reviews reason and clicks "Approve" or "Reject"  
- **If rejected:** Grade reverts to blank, reviewer must re-submit with FM/PM/DNM or a different EX reason  
- **Audit trail:** All EX proposals (approved and rejected) logged with timestamp, proposer, approver, reason

## 13.5 Score Modification & Audit Trail {#13.5-score-modification-&-audit-trail}

### 13.5.1 Append-Only Grades

- **Data structure:** `individual_grades[]` is an array, never mutated. New grades always appended.  
- **Grade object schema:**  
    
  {  
    
    id: uuid,  
    
    user\_id: string,  
    
    grade: "FM" | "PM" | "DNM" | "EX",  
    
    value: number (0.0–1.0, or null if EX),  
    
    supersedes: uuid (reference to prior grade.id, if this is an override),  
    
    timestamp: ISO 8601,  
    
    note: string (optional, reviewer's justification for override)  
    
  }  
    
- **Latest grade:** Computed as the last entry in `individual_grades[]` where `supersedes` is null or does not reference the current entry  
- **Prior entry retention:** All prior entries remain in the array for audit; marked as "superseded" in UI

### 13.5.2 Override Tracking

- **Override definition:** A new grade submitted when a prior non-null grade already exists for the same user-req-vendor triplet  
- **Override rate calculation:** `(total overrides / total grades) × 100%`, displayed per-use-case and workspace-wide  
- **Override cap:** No limit on overrides during Phases 10–11. At Phase 12 entry, all grades locked immutable.  
- **UI indication:** Superseded grades shown with strikethrough; new grade highlighted in yellow for 5 seconds  
- **Justification:** Override note is optional but recommended. If not provided, system suggests "No justification provided."

## 13.6 Collaborative Scoring & Disagreement Resolution {#13.6-collaborative-scoring-&-disagreement-resolution}

### 13.6.1 Concurrent Editing (Collaborative Scoring — universal per §34.1)

- **Per-user grades:** Each reviewer writes to their own entry in `individual_grades[]`. No write conflicts.  
- **Aggregated score:** Computed reactively from all entries in the array  
- **Real-time updates:** Via Convex subscriptions, live presence indicators show who is currently scoring which requirement  
- **Score independently toggle:** Each reviewer can toggle "Score Independently" to hide all other reviewers' grades until they submit. After submit, other grades become visible.  
- **Optimistic mutations:** UI shows user's grade immediately; if phase locks or validation fails, grade reverts with error toast

### 13.6.2 Divergence Detection & Resolution

- **Divergence definition:** When 2+ reviewers have independently scored the same requirement-vendor pair, compare the grades  
- **Divergence threshold:**  
  - If divergence meets the §13.6.3 Card threshold, the Disagreement Insight Card appears  
  - If divergence meets the §13.6.3 Lead-escalation threshold, automatic escalation to Use Case Lead occurs  
- **Disagreement Card UI:**  
  - Shows both grades with reviewer names  
  - Displays divergence % (calculated as percentage distance between grades on 0.0–1.0 scale)  
  - "Review Disagreement" button opens modal  
  - Card appears in matrix view, expandable  
- **Use Case Lead Escalation Modal:**  
  - Shows both grades with reviewer justifications (if available)  
  - Display calculation of average grade  
  - Options for Lead:  
    1. **Accept Average:** Grade set to mean of the two grades (e.g., FM & DNM → 0.5), logged as Lead decision  
    2. **Override to specific grade:** Dropdown allows Lead to select FM/PM/DNM, enters override justification (required), appends new entry to grades array with `supersedes` referencing both prior grades  
    3. **Request Re-Evaluation:** Sends notification to both reviewers, returns to independent scoring, and locks in the §44.1 scoring-disagreement re-evaluation deadline  
  - **Final decision:** Lead's override is appended to grades array and is final (cannot be overridden again)  
  - **Audit:** All disagreement resolutions logged with Lead name, decision, timestamp, justification

### 13.6.3 Disagreement Thresholds {#13.6.3-disagreement-thresholds}

This table is the canonical scoring-disagreement threshold registry for §13.6.2. Consumers MUST reference the threshold key rather than restating numeric values inline.

| Threshold key | Value | Trigger | Surface effect | Audit event |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `disagreement_card_min_delta` | 0.300 | `max_grade - min_grade >= value` after 2+ reviewers independently score the same requirement-vendor pair | Disagreement Insight Card appears in matrix view | `score.disagreement_card_visible` with `divergence_delta` and reviewer IDs |
| `use_case_lead_escalation_min_delta` | 0.600 | `max_grade - min_grade >= value`; equivalent to two rubric-level spread for FM vs DNM | Use Case Lead escalation modal opens automatically | `score.disagreement_escalated` with `divergence_delta`, `requirement_id`, `vendor_id`, and `use_case_lead_user_id` |

## 13.7 Score Calculation & Aggregation {#13.7-score-calculation-&-aggregation}

### 13.7.1 Vendor-Requirement Score

- **Formula:**  
    
  score\_vr \= latest\_grade\_value (FM/PM/DNM/EX)  
    
- **If EX:** Excluded from denominator for this vendor

### 13.7.2 Vendor Total Score (Per Use Case)

- **Formula:**  
    
  vendor\_use\_case\_score \=   
    
    SUM(score\_vr × weight\_r for all requirements where weight\_r \> 0 and grade ≠ EX)  
    
    /  
    
    SUM(weight\_r for all requirements where weight\_r \> 0 and grade ≠ EX)  
    
- **Output:** 0.0–1.0, displayed as percentage (0–100%)  
- **Minimum requirements:** If only 1 requirement with weight \> 0, score \= score\_vr × weight\_r / weight\_r \= score\_vr

### 13.7.3 Vendor Blended Score (All Use Cases \+ TCO)

- **Precondition:** Requires scenario definition (Section 14\)  
- **Formula:**  
    
  blended\_score \=   
    
    (SUM(vendor\_use\_case\_score × use\_case\_weight) \+ (tco\_percentile × tco\_value\_weight))   
    
    /  
    
    (SUM(use\_case\_weight) \+ tco\_value\_weight)  
    
  - `vendor_use_case_score` \= vendor's score on this use case (0.0–1.0)  
  - `use_case_weight` \= multiplier for this use case (0.0–5.0, from scenario)  
  - `tco_percentile` \= vendor's percentile rank in TCO (0.0–1.0), see Section 15  
  - `tco_value_weight` \= weight given to TCO (0.0–1.0, from scenario)  
  - See Section 14 for scenario parameter details

## 13.8 Auto-Scoring Rules {#13.8-auto-scoring-rules}

### 13.8.1 Boolean Requirements

- **Definition:** Requirements with only 2 valid answers (Yes/No or Present/Not Present)  
- **Auto-grading:**  
  - Vendor response \= "Yes" → FM (1.0)  
  - Vendor response \= "No" → DNM (0.0)  
- **Manual override:** Reviewer can manually override auto-grade; new grade appended to array with supersedes reference  
- **UI:** Auto-graded requirements marked with "Auto" label; grade locked until override submitted

### 13.8.2 Pricing Requirements

- **Exclusion:** Pricing requirements are NOT scored via FM/PM/DNM rubric  
- **Instead:** Pricing data extracted into TCO model (Section 15); does not contribute to capability scoring  
- **Weight:** Pricing requirements have weight 0 (informational) and cannot be manually scored  
- **Label:** Marked "Pricing (TCO Only)" in matrix

### 13.8.3 Informational Requirements

- **Definition:** Requirements with weight \= 0  
- **Scoring:** Not scored; no grade assigned  
- **Calculation:** Excluded from numerator and denominator in vendor\_use\_case\_score  
- **UI:** Marked "Informational" label, no grade dropdown shown, grayed out in matrix

## 13.9 Scoring Phase Lifecycle {#13.9-scoring-phase-lifecycle}

### 13.9.1 Phase 10 (Scoring)

- Scoring unlocked; reviewers can grade vendor responses  
- Collaborative scoring enabled (universal capability per §34.1.1 cell **Collaborative Scoring** — Free / Starter / Growth / Scale / Enterprise)  
- Grades are mutable; changes tracked in append-only array  
- Override rate visible to reviewers

### 13.9.2 Phase 11 (Decision)

- Scoring continues; further overrides allowed  
- Scenario modeling and TCO adjustments finalized  
- Disagreement resolution must be completed before Phase 12 entry

### 13.9.3 Phase 12 Entry (Post-Decision)

- **Immutability enforcement:** All grades locked. `individual_grades[]` marked read-only.  
- **Timestamp:** Phase 12 entry timestamp recorded as `scoring_locked_at`  
- **Violation prevention:** Any attempt to grade or modify grades in Phase 12+ results in error: "Scoring is locked. Phase 12 (Post-Decision) has begun."  
- **Report finalization:** Grades used to generate final reports; reports cached (see Section 17\)

## 13.10 Acceptance Criteria {#13.10-acceptance-criteria}

### 13.10.1 Rubric & Grading

- [ ] FM, PM, DNM grades available; PM value configurable 0.1–0.9  
- [ ] EX grade available; requires exclusion reason  
- [ ] Weight range 0–20 enforced; informational (weight 0\) not manually changeable  
- [ ] Grade dropdown always visible in matrix view

### 13.10.2 Exclusion (EX)

- [ ] EX is per-vendor-per-requirement; does not affect other vendors  
- [ ] EX excludes requirement from denominator for that vendor only  
- [ ] Exception reason required (≤200 chars)  
- [ ] EX in PENDING state until approved by Workspace Owner/Use Case Lead  
- [ ] Approval queue visible in Workspace Owner dashboard  
- [ ] All EX proposals (approved/rejected) logged with metadata

### 13.10.3 Append-Only & Audit

- [ ] New grades appended to individual\_grades\[\] array; prior grades retained  
- [ ] Supersedes reference links override to prior grade  
- [ ] Override rate calculated and displayed per-use-case and workspace-wide  
- [ ] Superseded grades shown with strikethrough in audit view  
- [ ] No limit on overrides during Phases 10–11

### 13.10.4 Concurrent Editing

- [ ] Two reviewers can independently score same requirement-vendor pair without write conflict  
- [ ] Real-time presence indicators show active reviewers  
- [ ] "Score Independently" toggle hides other grades until submit  
- [ ] Optimistic mutations revert on validation failure or phase lock

### 13.10.5 Disagreement Resolution

- [ ] Divergence ≥0.3 → Disagreement Card appears  
- [ ] Divergence ≥0.6 → Automatic escalation to Use Case Lead  
- [ ] Use Case Lead can accept average, override to specific grade, or request re-eval  
- [ ] Re-eval deadline set to 48 hours; reviewers notified  
- [ ] All disagreement resolutions logged with metadata  
- [ ] Lead override is final; cannot be overridden again

### 13.10.6 Score Calculation

- [ ] Vendor-use-case score \= SUM(grade × weight) / SUM(weight) for non-EX, non-zero-weight  
- [ ] Blended score includes TCO percentile weighting per scenario  
- [ ] Auto-scoring for boolean requirements: Yes→FM, No→DNM  
- [ ] Pricing requirements excluded from capability scoring  
- [ ] Informational requirements not scored; excluded from denominator

### 13.10.7 Phase Immutability

- [ ] Grades mutable in Phases 10–11  
- [ ] At Phase 12 entry, individual\_grades\[\] marked immutable  
- [ ] Attempt to score in Phase 12+ → error toast  
- [ ] scoring\_locked\_at timestamp recorded
