## 13.11 Defense View {#13.11-defense-view}

**Authoring note (Phase 14.5 — 2026-04-26; amended 2026-06-21).** Defense View is authored under §13 (Scoring) rather than §17 (Workspace Analytics) because it is the post-scoring leadership-meeting surface that consumes the immutable Selection Record (§4.3.24, §10.13) produced by the scoring pipeline. The §3.13 / Appendix M forward-reference ("§13.x or §14.x, Phase 14.5") is hereby tightened to §13.11. Selection Record is created in §10.13.5 (Phase 13 closure) and the Selection Report from which it is composed is generated in §10.12.4 (Phase 12.4) as §4.3.23. The Defense View is a downstream read-only synthesis surface — it never mutates the underlying Selection Report or Selection Record.

### 13.11.1 Purpose {#13.11.1-purpose}

The Defense View is the single surface a buyer-side Workspace Owner opens five minutes before a leadership meeting to defend a vendor recommendation in plain English. It synthesizes the finalized Selection Record (§4.3.24) into four sections — **Recommendation**, **Why**, **Risks**, **Evidence** — and produces a one-page printable CFO summary. It is not a rehearsal tool, a multi-stakeholder briefing engine, or a slide generator; the scope is deliberately constrained to the moment immediately preceding leadership presentation.

The surface is generated server-side via an Anthropic Sonnet AIOperation on the operator's first open of the view per Workspace; cached thereafter and regenerated only when the underlying Selection Record's content hash mutates. Generation is metered as the customer-billed AIOperation `defense_view_generate` (§13.11.5) under the outcome-based pricing model in §34.3 with an OutcomeContract per §4.8.4.

### 13.11.2 Inputs & Source-of-Truth Binding {#13.11.2-inputs-and-source-of-truth-binding}

Defense View has exactly one input: the finalized Selection Record (§4.3.24 `SelectionRecord.selection_record_sha256` and the immutable bundle assembled in §10.13.5). The view is content-addressed via `selection_record_hash`, the SHA-256 hash recorded on the Selection Record at creation and copied to `SelectionReport.selection_record_sha256` (§4.3.23). Generation, regeneration, and cache invalidation are all gated on this hash: a hash mismatch between the stored DefenseView row and the source Selection Record forces regeneration on next open (§13.11.5 AC 3).

The view does not read scores, requirements, or responses directly; the Selection Record bundle is the single read surface. This isolation guarantees that Defense View output cannot drift from the immutable artifact under audit.

### 13.11.3 Surface {#13.11.3-surface}

The Defense View renders as a single-screen overlay opened from the §10.12 Selection & Recommendation surface (when Phase ≥ 12) and from the §10.13 Phase 13 closure surface. Layout is exactly four sections plus a header and one action:

1. **Header** — Workspace name, vendor name (recommended primary), deadline countdown to the next workspace-attached leadership-meeting calendar event (if available; otherwise no countdown), and a "regenerated due to source change" chip when applicable.
2. **Recommendation** — One sentence: the recommended vendor and the one-sentence reason. Plain English; no scoring jargon.
3. **Why** — The three highest-weighted reasons, ranked by `requirement.weight × score_contribution` from the Selection Record. Each reason carries an inline evidence link to the underlying Score row(s).
4. **Risks** — One or two material risks (drawn from `selection_report.risk_assessment` per §10.12.4) with the mitigation that was authored in the Selection Report.
5. **Evidence** — A flat list of evidence references (Score id, Response id, Requirement id) keyed back to the Selection Record. Click-through opens the §11.3 detail surface in a side peek; the Defense View itself does not navigate away.
6. **Action** — One button: "Print / Export PDF" (§13.11.6). Cmd+P invokes the same action.

The surface is full-screen on desktop and full-screen on mobile (read-only on mobile per §13.11.13 AC 9). No other actions are available; in particular, the operator cannot edit the Selection Report from this surface — to edit, return to §10.12.

### 13.11.4 Plan Gating {#13.11.4-plan-gating}

Defense View visibility and content depth are plan-gated. Plan tiers are authoritative in §34.1; visibility is registered in §5.11 Feature Access Matrix; the Appendix M row (Defense View, §13.11) carries the canonical surface-level tier contract.

| Tier | Surface | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Buyer Free | Watermarked preview: Recommendation + first reason in **Why** visible. **Risks**, remaining **Why**, and **Evidence** sections are gated. | Preview MUST display a "Solo unlocks the full view" upgrade CTA per §34.8.5. PDF export is disabled on Free; the print action surfaces an upgrade modal. |
| Buyer Solo | Full surface, unwatermarked, full PDF export. | Solo plan tier landed in Phase 14.9 (`buyer_solo` enum value registered in Appendix J `buyer_plan_tier`); the Phase-14.6 alias to Business Starter+ is retired. |
| Business Starter+ | Full surface, unwatermarked, full PDF export. | |
| Buyer Enterprise | Full surface; PDF footer additionally carries the §4.3.24 Selection Record SHA-256 audit-receipt verbiage per §32.7. | |

The seller console never sees Defense View. The §7.2 Dual-Console Firewall MUST reject any seller-console session attempting to read a `DefenseView` row with HTTP 404 (existence-leak prevention per §1.3); a 403 would teach the seller that the resource exists.

### 13.11.5 Generation: AIOperation `defense_view_generate` {#13.11.5-generation-aioperation-defense-view-generate}

Generation is a customer-billed AIOperation per §4.8.1 with `capability_id = defense_view_generate` and the OutcomeContract specified below. The capability is added to the Agent Capability Registry per §4.8.2 / §21.4.2 (registry-update follows the registry-extension protocol — no §21.4 spec edit required); the rate-card row is added to §34.3.4 by the cost-base recalculation job at first publish per §34.3.3.

**Capability registration (authoritative for the §13.11 feature; runtime registry rows authored in a follow-on registry update — flagged Authored Extension):**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| `capability_id` | `defense_view_generate` |
| Display Name | Defense View Generation |
| Console | `buyer` |
| `model_tier_default` | `sonnet` |
| `billing_mode` | `customer_billed` |
| `requires_managed_agent` | `false` (single-shot Sonnet invocation; no batch / multi-tool orchestration) |
| `plan_gate_min_tier` | `buyer_solo` per §34.1.1 / §34.1.3 (alias to `business_starter` retired in Phase 14.9; line corrected in Phase 14.9.1) |
| Free Allowance | 10 ops lifetime per Org per §4.8.7 / Summary C.80 default — applies to preview generation on Free tier |
| Confidence Threshold | Per §13.11.5.A `confidence_threshold_pct`; below threshold, surface renders an "AI couldn't synthesize a confident defense for this Selection Record — open the Selection Report for the underlying detail" inline note per §21.3 |
| Output Contract | `agent_output_envelope` per §32 with structured fields `recommendation_text`, `top_reasons[]` (length 3, each with `text` and `evidence_ref`), `material_risks[]` (length 1–2, each with `text`, `mitigation`, `evidence_ref`), `cfo_summary_md` |

#### 13.11.5.A Defense View Runtime Constants {#13.11.5.A-defense-view-runtime-constants}

This table is the canonical §13.11 home for `defense_view_generate` OutcomeContract timing and confidence constants. Runtime fields that carry seconds use seconds in the Value column; human-readable unit conversions are explanatory only and MUST NOT be copied into field values.

| Constant key | Runtime field / consumer | Value | Unit | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `confidence_threshold_pct` | `Confidence Threshold`; `DefenseView.confidence_score` low-confidence branch | 70 | percent | Below this threshold, the surface renders the §21.3 low-confidence inline note; threshold suppression is a UX filter, not a billing event. |
| `accepted_signal_window_days` | OutcomeContract accepted-signal observation window | 90 | days from `generated_at` | Operator open must occur before this window closes. |
| `regeneration_reject_window_seconds` | OutcomeContract rejected-signal observation window | 86400 | seconds | Equivalent to 24 hours; operator-initiated regeneration inside this window rejects the operation. |
| `auto_accept_after_seconds` | OutcomeContract.`auto_accept_after_seconds` | 2592000 | seconds | Equivalent to 30 days; non-regenerated, non-opened DefenseViews auto-resolve to `rejected` because §4.8.4 sets `default_on_timeout=rejected`. |
| `signal_evaluation_grace_seconds` | OutcomeContract.`signal_evaluation_grace_seconds` | 86400 | seconds | Equivalent to 24 hours; late opens inside this grace materialize a `ContestRecord` per §4.8.5. |
| `contest_window_days` | OutcomeContract.`contest_window_days` | 14 | days from settlement | Customer contest window for settled Defense View AIOperations. |

**OutcomeContract (registered in §21.4.5):**

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Accepted Signal | `DefenseView.opened_at IS NOT NULL` before the §13.11.5.A `accepted_signal_window_days` boundary AND `regenerated_count = 0` AND no operator regeneration inside the §13.11.5.A `regeneration_reject_window_seconds` boundary. The operator opening the view at least once before leadership presentation is the success signal — quality is observable through the absence of regeneration. |
| Rejected Signal | Operator-initiated regeneration inside the §13.11.5.A `regeneration_reject_window_seconds` boundary after first generation. Equivalent to `DefenseView.regenerated_count ≥ 1 AND first_regeneration_at - generated_at <= regeneration_reject_window_seconds`. |
| Window | Per §13.11.5.A `accepted_signal_window_days` from `generated_at` |
| `auto_accept_after_seconds` | Per §13.11.5.A `auto_accept_after_seconds`; non-regenerated, non-opened DefenseViews auto-resolve to `rejected` per `default_on_timeout=rejected` in §4.8.4 |
| `signal_evaluation_grace_seconds` | Per §13.11.5.A `signal_evaluation_grace_seconds`; late opens inside this grace materialize a `ContestRecord` per §4.8.5 |
| `requires_explicit_user_signal` | `false` (the open event is the signal) |
| `contest_window_days` | Per §13.11.5.A `contest_window_days` |

**Generation flow:**

1. Operator opens the Defense View surface (§13.11.3) for a Workspace where Phase ≥ 12 and a finalized `SelectionReport` row exists (§4.3.23). 
2. Server checks for an existing `DefenseView` row keyed on `(workspace_id, selection_record_id)`. If present and `selection_record_hash` matches the current `SelectionRecord.selection_record_sha256`, the cached row is returned and `opened_at` is stamped (idempotent — first open only).
3. If no row exists, or the hash does not match (a regeneration trigger), the AIOperation `defense_view_generate` is invoked. Sonnet receives the Selection Record bundle as context and emits the four-section structured output. The `DefenseView` row is written transactionally with the Selection Record hash bound at write time.
4. The AIOperation row is written with `state=pending` and the standard `(parent_aioperation_id, capability_id, value_price_cents, cost_price_cents, outcome_contract_id, contract_version)` fields per §4.8.1. Wallet draw, Free Allowance handling, and the burn priority rules in §34.10.1 apply unchanged.
5. The Outcome Resolver (§34.11) settles the operation per the OutcomeContract above at the closer of (window expiry, signal observation, §13.11.5.A `auto_accept_after_seconds`).

**Performance budget.** Generation MUST complete within the §44.1 Defense View generation p95 budget from operator click to first paint of the four sections. Beyond that p95 budget, a §3.7 loading state is shown; beyond the §44.1 Defense View generation hard-timeout budget, the operation is flagged as a §21.6 Agent failure with a single-tap "Try again" affordance (§13.11.12 failure mode 1).

**Caching invariant.** Within a Workspace, the `(selection_record_hash → DefenseView)` mapping is one-to-one. A hash mutation on the Selection Record is not permitted after §10.13.5; before Phase 13, approval-workflow `request_changes` / `rejected` can produce a superseding Selection Report and therefore a new future Selection Record hash while the Workspace remains in `phase_12_selection` per §10.12 and Appendix L.12. The system MUST NOT serve stale Defense View content under a mismatched Selection Record hash.

### 13.11.6 Print / Export PDF {#13.11.6-print-export-pdf}

The Print/Export PDF action produces a single-page PDF containing all four sections plus a footer bearing the Selection Record SHA-256 hash, the workspace name, the recommended vendor, the `generated_at` timestamp, and (Enterprise only) the §32.7 Selection Record audit-receipt verbiage. PDF generation MUST complete within 3 seconds at p95.

The PDF is rendered server-side from a deterministic template (no client-side print stylesheet); the rendering job is observability-tagged with `defense_view_pdf_render` for §6.7 audit and §44 performance dashboards. The `cfo_summary_md` field of the `DefenseView` row is the single source for the printable body content; layout is fixed and not operator-configurable.

Watermarked Free-tier previews — when an operator on Free tier triggers Print — surface the upgrade modal in lieu of generating a PDF (§13.11.4).

### 13.11.7 Data Model — `DefenseView` Entity {#13.11.7-data-model-defenseview-entity}

`DefenseView` is a Buyer-console-scoped, Workspace-scoped entity whose canonical field table lives in this §13.11.7 Defense View data-model block. This is an explicit §4.3 placement exception: Defense View is generated and cached by the §13.11 engine surface, and every cross-reference must cite §13.11.7 rather than claiming a §4.3 entity home. One-to-one with the `SelectionReport` / Selection Record bundle.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | required, PK | |
| `org_id` | UUID | required, FK → Organization | Org-scoped (§7.2 firewall) |
| `console` | enum | required = `buyer` | Per §1.3.2 — seller console MUST NOT read |
| `workspace_id` | UUID | required, FK → Workspace | Workspace-scoped |
| `selection_record_id` | UUID | required, FK → SelectionRecord.id (§4.3.24) | One-to-one (unique constraint with `workspace_id`) |
| `selection_record_hash` | text | required | SHA-256 of the source Selection Record at generation time; mismatch with current `SelectionRecord.selection_record_sha256` triggers regeneration |
| `recommendation_text` | text | required; length per §39 (DefenseView.recommendation_text row) | One sentence; plain English. Authoritative limit lives at §39; do not restate inline. |
| `top_reasons` | jsonb | required, length = 3; each element's `text` length per §39 (DefenseView.top_reasons[i].text row) | Array of `{ text, evidence_ref: { score_id: UUID, requirement_id: UUID, response_id: UUID } }`. |
| `material_risks` | jsonb | required, length 1–2; each element's `text` and `mitigation` length per §39 (DefenseView.material_risks[i].text and material_risks[i].mitigation rows) | Array of `{ text, mitigation, evidence_ref: { score_id: UUID, requirement_id: UUID, response_id: UUID } }`. |
| `cfo_summary_md` | text | required; length per §39 (DefenseView.cfo_summary_md row) | One-page printable Markdown body; rendered to PDF deterministically. |
| `confidence_score` | numeric(4,3) | required, 0.000–1.000 | From the Sonnet output envelope; below the §13.11.5.A `confidence_threshold_pct` value surfaces the §21.3 low-confidence note |
| `aioperation_id` | UUID | required, FK → AIOperation.id | The generating AIOperation row |
| `generated_at` | timestamp | required | At first generation; updated on regeneration |
| `opened_at` | timestamp | nullable | First operator open after most recent generation; idempotent (first-write-wins). Drives the OutcomeContract accepted signal. |
| `regenerated_count` | integer | required, default 0 | Increments on each regeneration. Drives the OutcomeContract rejected signal when paired with `first_regeneration_at` inside the §13.11.5.A `regeneration_reject_window_seconds` boundary. |
| `first_regeneration_at` | timestamp | nullable | Timestamp of the first regeneration after initial generation; null until first regeneration. |
| `created_at` | timestamp | required | |
| `updated_at` | timestamp | required | |
| `created_by` | UUID | required, FK → User | Operator who triggered first generation |
| `updated_by` | UUID | required, FK → User | Operator who triggered most recent regeneration / open |
| `deleted_at` | timestamp | nullable | Soft delete; cascades on Workspace archive (§10.13) |

**Indexes:**

- `idx_defense_view_workspace` ON `(workspace_id)` — partial WHERE `deleted_at IS NULL`
- `idx_defense_view_selection_record` ON `(selection_record_id)` UNIQUE — partial WHERE `deleted_at IS NULL` (one Defense View per Selection Record)
- `idx_defense_view_hash` ON `(selection_record_hash)` — supports cache lookup on hash
- `idx_defense_view_org_workspace_generated` ON `(org_id, workspace_id, generated_at DESC)` — supports listing recent Defense Views per Org for §17.5 export
- `idx_defense_view_aiop` ON `(aioperation_id)` — supports the §4.8.1 ledger join

**Scope isolation.** Org-scoped (`org_id`) and Workspace-scoped (`workspace_id`); Buyer-console-only (`console=buyer` invariant). Cross-console reads return HTTP 404 per §1.3. Cross-Org reads return HTTP 403 per §32 RBAC.

**Retention.** Tied to Workspace retention per §40.2: soft-deleted at Workspace archive (`Workspace.status=closed` triggers cascade per §10.13.6), purged with Workspace at the §40.2 plan-tier retention boundary measured from `Workspace.archived_at`. DSAR export per §6.8.1 includes the `DefenseView` row when the requesting user is in `created_by` OR `updated_by` OR is a Workspace member at request time. DSAR redaction (§6.8.2) anonymizes `created_by` and `updated_by` to NULL, retaining the AI-generated content (which is not user-authored PII).

**Data residency.** Bound to the Workspace's residency region per §1.6 / §40.4. EU-residency Workspaces MUST NOT route generation through US Anthropic endpoints; the `defense_view_generate` AIOperation respects the Org's `data_residency_region` per §1.6.

**GDPR anonymization path.** On `DefenseView.deleted_at` write (soft delete), `cfo_summary_md`, `recommendation_text`, `top_reasons`, and `material_risks` MAY contain references to vendor names; vendor name handling on hard-purge follows the §6.8.3 right-to-erasure cascade — vendor name strings are not redacted because vendors are not Sourcera users; the `created_by` / `updated_by` user references follow §6.8.2.

### 13.11.8 API Endpoints {#13.11.8-api-endpoints}

Endpoints registered under §32.5 (Workspaces). Authentication: session token or API token with scope `read:workspaces` (read) / `write:workspaces` (regenerate). Rate-limit class: `workspace_read` for GET, `ai_invocation` for POST regenerate (§32.4.5). Pagination: cursor-based, default 50, max 250 (not applicable to single-row endpoints).

#### `GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/defense-view`

Returns the cached `DefenseView` row, generating one on first call if absent.

**Behavior.** Idempotent for read (subsequent calls return the same row provided the Selection Record hash is unchanged). On hash mismatch, internally regenerates (per §13.11.5), writing a new AIOperation row and an updated `DefenseView` row. On first generation, stamps `opened_at` and writes the §13.11.10 `defense_view.generated` webhook.

**Request:** No body. Path param `workspace_id`.

**Response 200 (cached or freshly generated):**

```
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "workspace_id": "uuid",
  "selection_record_id": "uuid",
  "selection_record_hash": "sha256-hex",
  "recommendation_text": "string",
  "top_reasons": [{ "text": "string", "evidence_ref": { "score_id": "uuid", "requirement_id": "uuid", "response_id": "uuid" } }, ...],
  "material_risks": [{ "text": "string", "mitigation": "string", "evidence_ref": { "score_id": "uuid", "requirement_id": "uuid", "response_id": "uuid" } }, ...],
  "cfo_summary_md": "string",
  "confidence_score": 0.872,
  "generated_at": "ISO 8601",
  "opened_at": "ISO 8601 | null",
  "regenerated_count": 0,
  "regenerated_due_to_source_change": false,
  "watermarked_preview": false,
  "agent_output_envelope": { "label": "[AI-Generated]", "model": "sonnet", "capability_id": "defense_view_generate", "aioperation_id": "uuid" }
}
```

For Free-tier callers, the response sets `watermarked_preview: true` and redacts `material_risks`, `top_reasons[1..2]`, and `cfo_summary_md` to a single-line "Upgrade to Solo to view the full Defense View" placeholder. The `agent_output_envelope` block is preserved.

**Errors:**

- `404 workspace_not_found` (also returned for cross-console / cross-Org reads per §1.3)
- `409 selection_record_not_finalized` — Workspace Phase < 12 OR no `SelectionReport` exists for the Workspace
- `402 wallet_hard_capped` — wallet exhausted and generation would charge an overage; surface upgrade CTA per §34.10.4
- `429 rate_limited` — `ai_invocation` rate-limit class exceeded; standard `Retry-After` header
- `503 capability_disabled` — capability disabled at the platform level; standard fallback per §21.6

#### `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/defense-view/regenerate`

Forces a regeneration of the Defense View regardless of hash. Operator-initiated; charged as a fresh AIOperation. Idempotency key required (`Idempotency-Key` header per §32.2); duplicate keys within 24h return the same response.

**Request body:**

```
{
  "reason_code": "operator_initiated" | "source_changed_manual_refresh" | "low_confidence_retry",
  "reason_note": "string ≤ 200 chars (optional)"
}
```

**Response 200:** Same shape as `GET …/defense-view`.

**Errors:**

- `404 workspace_not_found`
- `409 selection_record_not_finalized`
- `402 wallet_hard_capped`
- `429 regeneration_throttle` — more than 1 regeneration per 5 minutes per Workspace (anti-spam guard); standard `Retry-After` header populated per Appendix I (rate-limit-class semantics)
- `403 plan_requires_upgrade` — Free tier callers cannot regenerate (preview is read-only); §34.8.5 upgrade CTA in error body
- `429 rate_limited`

The above two endpoints are registered in §32.5 under the **Workspaces** group; full request/response schemas, idempotency semantics, and error codes are catalogued in Appendix I (new entries: `selection_record_not_finalized`, `regeneration_throttle`, `defense_view_capability_disabled` — registered in this phase).

#### `GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/defense-view.pdf`

Returns a single-page PDF rendering of the Defense View. Server-side rendered; `Content-Type: application/pdf`; `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="DefenseView_{workspace_slug}_{generated_at}.pdf"`.

**Behavior.** Read-only; does not regenerate. Free-tier callers receive `403 plan_requires_upgrade`. Enterprise callers receive a footer with the §32.7 Selection Record audit-receipt verbiage.

### 13.11.9 State Machine {#13.11.9-state-machine}

`DefenseView` carries a small lifecycle state machine driven by `(opened_at, regenerated_count, deleted_at)` field combinations. Registered in Appendix L.

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (none) | `generated_unopened` | First `GET /defense-view` write | `opened_at IS NULL`, `regenerated_count = 0` | Initial generation |
| `generated_unopened` | `opened` | Operator opens view | `opened_at` stamped on first read | Drives `accepted` signal eligibility |
| `opened` | `regenerated_unopened` | Hash mismatch on subsequent open OR explicit regenerate POST | `regenerated_count` incremented; `opened_at` reset to NULL on regenerate (next open re-stamps) | "regenerated due to source change" chip surfaces if hash mismatch was the trigger |
| `regenerated_unopened` | `opened` | Operator opens view post-regeneration | `opened_at` stamped | |
| `opened` / `regenerated_unopened` / `generated_unopened` | `archived` | Workspace closure cascade per §10.13 | `deleted_at` stamped; `Workspace.status=closed` | Soft delete |
| `archived` | (purged) | Retention boundary per §40.2 | Plan-tier retention elapsed from `Workspace.archived_at` | Hard purge; PII anonymization rules per §6.8.2 |

### 13.11.10 Webhooks {#13.11.10-webhooks}

Two webhook events are registered in Appendix C (Notification Event Catalog) and the corresponding Appendix G PostHog rows:

- `defense_view.generated` — fires on first generation per Workspace. Payload includes `defense_view_id`, `workspace_id`, `selection_record_id`, `selection_record_hash`, `confidence_score`, `aioperation_id`, `generated_at`.
- `defense_view.regenerated` — fires on each regeneration. Payload includes the above plus `regenerated_count`, `first_regeneration_at`, and `regeneration_reason_code`.

Both events follow §31 transport (HMAC-SHA256 signing, idempotency via `event_id`, Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve, DLQ after 5 failures, payload ≤ 256 KB). Console scope: buyer console only — seller-console webhook subscriptions attempting to register for these event types receive HTTP 404 per the §31 subscription-registration guard. User-facing in-app or email notification is NOT emitted for either event (the operator triggered the action; surfacing a notification would be redundant).

### 13.11.11 Plan Gating, Feature Access, and Object Size {#13.11.11-plan-gating-feature-access-and-object-size}

- **Plan gate.** Authoritative entry registered in §5.11 Feature Access Matrix as row `defense_view` with the gate semantics defined in §13.11.4 (Free: watermarked preview only; Solo+: full surface; Enterprise: full surface plus PDF audit-receipt footer).
- **Plan tier definitions.** Authoritative in §34.1; this section MUST NOT restate plan-tier dollar amounts or capability ceilings.
- **Object size constraints.** Authoritative in §39 — new row registered: `defense_view.cfo_summary_md` (≤ 4000 chars), `defense_view.recommendation_text` (≤ 500 chars), `defense_view.top_reasons[i].text` (≤ 280 chars), `defense_view.material_risks[i].text` (≤ 280 chars), `defense_view.material_risks[i].mitigation` (≤ 280 chars). Inline references in this section cite §39, never restate the numbers.
- **AIWallet behavior.** Authoritative in §4.8.3 / §34.10. The `defense_view_generate` capability draws from the wallet per the §34.10.1 burn priority unchanged.
- **Free Allowance.** Per §4.8.7 and §34.8.4, seeded at the C.80 default of 10 ops lifetime. The Free-tier preview path does NOT consume the Free Allowance (preview generation is metered on the watermarked render path, not on the full-surface render path).

### 13.11.12 Failure Modes {#13.11.12-failure-modes}

1. **Sonnet generation fails or exceeds the §44.1 Defense View generation hard-timeout budget.** §21.6 Agent failure handling applies. The surface renders the §3.7 generation-error state with a single "Try again" affordance; the failed AIOperation is reversed per §34.11 (cost_price refunded; no `accepted`/`rejected` signal recorded). The operator may regenerate without throttle-pause when the prior attempt failed (§13.11.8 `regeneration_throttle` exempts failure-recovery retries).
2. **Selection Record hash mutates mid-render (Workspace bounced from Phase 13 → 12 per §10.12.5).** The cached `DefenseView` row is invalidated; next operator open triggers regeneration. The "regenerated due to source change" chip surfaces in the header. PostHog mirror event `defense_view_regenerated_due_to_source_change` fires (Appendix G); source webhook naming remains `defense_view.regenerated` where applicable.
3. **Operator on Free tier triggers Print.** PDF generation is suppressed; the upgrade modal renders with deep-link to the §34.8.5 upgrade CTA (Solo plan tier post-Phase-14.6; Business Starter+ until then).
4. **Concurrent operator regenerations within 5 minutes.** Second and subsequent calls within the 5-minute window return `429 regeneration_throttle` (§13.11.8; Appendix I — rate-limit-class semantics with `Retry-After` populated). The throttle protects against accidental double-tap; explicit Ops override is available per §34.10 wallet-Ops controls.
5. **Anthropic outage during generation.** §44.1 performance budgets are suspended; the surface renders a "Sourcera AI is temporarily unavailable" state per §3.7. The Selection Report (§4.3.21) remains available as the ground-truth fallback; the surface deep-links to it. PostHog event `defense_view.generation_failed_third_party_outage` fires.
6. **Confidence score below the §13.11.5.A `confidence_threshold_pct` value.** Surface renders the §21.3 low-confidence inline note alongside the four sections; the underlying generation is still cached and the operator MAY regenerate to attempt a higher-confidence draft. The `accepted` signal still fires on open per §13.11.5 (low confidence is a quality signal, not a billing signal).
7. **Workspace archived between generation and operator open (§10.13 cascade).** The `DefenseView` row is soft-deleted as part of the cascade; the surface returns `404 defense_view_archived_with_workspace`. The cached PDF (if any was downloaded prior) remains valid as a static artifact.
8. **DSAR redaction during in-flight generation.** Generation aborts; the AIOperation is reversed per §34.11; the surface renders a "Defense View unavailable for this Workspace pending data-privacy processing" inline note. Standard §6.8 cascade applies.
9. **Mobile operator opens the surface.** Mobile renders the four sections in a vertically-stacked, full-width layout (read-only). PDF export is supported via the share sheet; regeneration is not exposed on mobile (the small-form regenerate gesture is intentionally suppressed to prevent accidental wallet draws). Cmd+P / Esc shortcuts are not applicable on mobile; mobile equivalents are the share sheet and the back gesture.
10. **Cross-Workspace contamination attempt (operator pastes another Workspace's Defense View URL into a different Workspace's session).** Server validates `(session.workspace_id, path.workspace_id)` membership and returns 404 on mismatch per §1.3.

### 13.11.13 Acceptance Criteria {#13.11.13-acceptance-criteria}

#### 13.11.13.1 Generation & Caching

1. Given a Workspace with `Phase ≥ 12` and a finalized `SelectionReport` row, when the operator opens the Defense View for the first time, the system invokes `defense_view_generate` and renders the Recommendation, Why (3 reasons), Risks (1–2), and Evidence sections within the §44.1 Defense View generation p95 budget from click to first paint of all four sections.
2. Given a previously-generated `DefenseView` row whose `selection_record_hash` matches the current `SelectionRecord.selection_record_sha256`, when the operator reopens the view, the system serves the cached row without invoking the AIOperation, in less than 500 ms at p95.
3. Given a `DefenseView` row whose `selection_record_hash` does NOT match the current `SelectionRecord.selection_record_sha256`, when the operator opens the view, the system regenerates the four sections, increments `regenerated_count`, stamps `first_regeneration_at` (if previously NULL), and surfaces the "regenerated due to source change" chip in the header.
4. Given an operator on Buyer Free, when they open the Defense View, the system renders a watermarked preview containing only the Recommendation and the first reason in **Why**; **Risks**, the remaining **Why** entries, and **Evidence** are gated with the §34.8.5 Solo upgrade CTA. PDF export on Free returns the upgrade modal, not a PDF.
5. Given an operator on Solo+ (per §13.11.4), when they open the Defense View, the four sections render unwatermarked and the PDF export is enabled.

#### 13.11.13.2 OutcomeContract Resolution

6. Given a Solo-tier operator with no prior `DefenseView` row for a Workspace, when they trigger generation, the AIOperation `defense_view_generate` resolves to `accepted` if and only if `DefenseView.opened_at IS NOT NULL` before the §13.11.5.A `accepted_signal_window_days` boundary AND `regenerated_count = 0` AND no regeneration occurred inside the §13.11.5.A `regeneration_reject_window_seconds` boundary.
7. Given the same operator regenerates inside the §13.11.5.A `regeneration_reject_window_seconds` boundary after first generation, the AIOperation resolves to `rejected` per the OutcomeContract.
8. Given the OutcomeContract window expires with no operator open and no regeneration, the AIOperation auto-resolves to `rejected` per `default_on_timeout=rejected` (§4.8.4); a `ContestRecord` may be filed within the §13.11.5.A `contest_window_days` boundary.

#### 13.11.13.3 PDF Export

9. Given an unwatermarked Defense View, when the operator clicks "Print / Export PDF" (or invokes Cmd+P), the server emits a single-page PDF containing all four sections plus a footer with `selection_record_sha256` (full hex), workspace name, recommended vendor, and `generated_at`, in less than 3 seconds at p95.
10. Given the operator's Org is on Buyer Enterprise, the PDF footer additionally carries the §32.7 Selection Record audit-receipt verbiage.
11. Given the operator's Org is on Buyer Free, clicking Print returns the upgrade modal; no PDF is generated.

#### 13.11.13.4 Mobile

12. Given a mobile operator (viewport < 768px) opens the Defense View, the four sections render read-only in a vertically-stacked, full-width layout; regeneration is not exposed; the share sheet replaces the PDF download button.

#### 13.11.13.5 Firewall & RBAC

13. Given a seller-console session attempts `GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/defense-view`, the server returns HTTP 404 (existence-leak prevention per §1.3); no row is leaked.
14. Given a buyer-console session in a different Org attempts the same call, the server returns HTTP 404; cross-Org existence is not leaked.
15. Given a seller-console webhook subscription attempts to register for `defense_view.generated` or `defense_view.regenerated`, the §31 subscription-registration guard returns HTTP 404.

#### 13.11.13.6 Webhook & Event Coverage

16. Each first generation per Workspace emits exactly one `defense_view.generated` webhook to subscribed buyer-console endpoints, with HMAC-SHA256 signing, `event_id` idempotency, payload ≤ 256 KB, and Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve.
17. Each regeneration emits exactly one `defense_view.regenerated` webhook with the same transport semantics; payload includes `regenerated_count` and `regeneration_reason_code`.
18. Each generation also writes the corresponding Appendix G PostHog mirror event (`defense_view_generated`, `defense_view_regenerated`, `defense_view_regenerated_due_to_source_change` where applicable) with `org_id`, `workspace_id`, `confidence_score`, and `aioperation_id` properties; each mirror carries the dotted source webhook event type in `source_webhook_event_type` when paired to an Appendix C event.

#### 13.11.13.7 State, Retention, DSAR, Residency

19. On Workspace closure (`Workspace.status=closed`), the `DefenseView` row is soft-deleted via the §10.13.6 cascade; subsequent reads return HTTP 404 `defense_view_archived_with_workspace`.
20. Retention follows §40.2: `DefenseView` rows are purged at the plan-tier retention boundary measured from `Workspace.archived_at`.
21. DSAR export per §6.8.1 includes the `DefenseView` row when the requesting user satisfies the §13.11.7 DSAR membership rule; redaction per §6.8.2 nullifies `created_by` / `updated_by`.
22. Generation respects the Workspace's `data_residency_region`: an EU Workspace MUST NOT route generation through US Anthropic endpoints; the AIOperation row carries `residency_region=eu` and the Anthropic invocation is region-bound.

#### 13.11.13.8 Failure & Resilience

23. Given a generation failure (Sonnet error or breach of the §44.1 Defense View generation hard-timeout budget), the AIOperation is reversed per §34.11; the surface renders the §3.7 generation-error state; the operator MAY retry without invoking `regeneration_throttle`.
24. Given two regenerations within 5 minutes for the same Workspace, the second returns HTTP 429 `regeneration_throttle` (per Appendix I rate-limit-class semantics; `Retry-After` header populated); the throttle is bypassed for failure-recovery retries.
25. Given an Anthropic outage, the surface deep-links to the underlying §4.3.21 Selection Report as the ground-truth fallback; the operator is not blocked from defending the recommendation through the Selection Report directly.

## 13.12 "What Are You Evaluating?" Intake {#13.12-what-are-you-evaluating-intake}

**Authoring note (Phase 14.7 — 2026-04-27).** This section is authored under §13 Scoring & Grading because the intake materializes the foundation of the Scoring engine — the rubric (§13.2), the per-Requirement weights (§13.3), the auto-scoring rules (§13.8) — into a freshly-created Workspace. The intake is the upstream surface that feeds every subsequent §13 mechanic, and the §13.X numbering reflects that engine binding. The supersedes-and-tightens relationship to the legacy §35.1 Step 4 "What are you evaluating?" prompt is explicit: §13.12 is the canonical intake; §35.1 Step 4 is updated in this same change to a one-line cross-reference. Drift surfaced and resolved in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Phase 14.7`.

### 13.12.1 Purpose {#13.12.1-purpose}

The "What Are You Evaluating?" intake is the single screen, single question shown to a buyer at every Workspace creation moment — first-time onboarding (§35.1) and every subsequent Workspace they create. It collapses the cold-start cost of a procurement evaluation from "stare at a blank Use Case grid" to "edit a half-built Workspace authored by someone who has done this evaluation a hundred times." The user's only required action is selecting one of six default vertical tiles or supplying free-text under "Other"; selection materializes a Workspace pre-populated with vertical-specific Use Cases, Requirements, scoring rubric, recommended vendor longlist, and a default deadline. Nothing is locked — every seeded artifact is editable from the moment the operator lands.

The intake is gated by the §13.12.4 plan-tier truncation rules. The seed itself is platform-scoped data sourced from the §4.5.9 EvalStarter registry; per-Org or per-Workspace overrides are explicitly out of scope (custom templates remain the domain of §19 Template Library, which is buyer-authored and Workspace-scoped).

### 13.12.2 Surface {#13.12.2-surface}

The intake renders as a single full-screen surface with one question, no preamble, and no progress stepper above the fold. Layout:

1. **Header.** "What are you evaluating?" — display heading per `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §2.1 typography. No sub-header, no helper copy above the tiles.
2. **Tile grid.** Six default vertical tiles in a 3 × 2 grid on desktop (≥ 1024px), 2 × 3 on tablet, 1 × 6 stacked on mobile. Each tile carries the EvalStarter `display_name`, `short_description`, and `icon_token`.
3. **"Other" affordance.** A seventh tile labeled "Other" beneath the six defaults, visually de-emphasized. Selecting it expands an inline free-text input ("What are you evaluating?") with a 1–120-character single-line input and a "Continue" button. The free-text path materializes a Workspace using the `other` EvalStarter seed (a deliberately minimal seed: 3 generic Use Cases, 30 generic Requirements, balanced rubric, no longlist, 28-day deadline) plus the buyer's free-text string captured into `Workspace.intake_freetext_label` for downstream display and analytics.
4. **No "Skip" or "Start blank" affordance above the fold.** A muted text-link "I want to start with a blank Workspace" is rendered below the tile grid for power users; selection materializes a blank Workspace with no Use Cases, no Requirements, no longlist, and the platform-default 28-day deadline. Telemetry distinguishes this path per §13.12.7.

The six default verticals — registered in Appendix J `EvalVertical` and seeded as EvalStarter rows by Sourcera Ops — are:

| `vertical_slug` | Display name | Tile sub-label |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `crm` | CRM | Sales, marketing, and customer success platforms |
| `itsm` | ITSM | IT service management, ticketing, asset management |
| `edr` | EDR / Endpoint Security | Endpoint detection and response, antivirus, EPP |
| `observability` | Observability | APM, logs, metrics, tracing, monitoring platforms |
| `payroll_hris` | Payroll / HRIS | Payroll, HRIS, benefits, time tracking |
| `other` | Other | Tell us in your own words |

Tile copy and icon tokens are Ops-editable via the §4.5.9 EvalStarter row; the surface re-renders within 60 seconds of an Ops edit per §4.5.9 AC #3.

### 13.12.3 Plan Gating {#13.12.3-plan-gating}

The intake surface itself is unconditionally available on every Buyer plan tier — the surface is the on-ramp to the platform and the registration of the operator's first artifact. Per-tier behavior diverges only in the materialization step (§13.12.4 truncation). The Appendix M row (EvalStarter, §4.5.9) and the surface-bound row authored in Appendix M for §13.12 carry the canonical contract; the §5.11 Feature Access Matrix enforces no separate gate beyond the universal "create a Workspace" permission.

### 13.12.4 Materialization & Plan-Tier Truncation {#13.12.4-materialization-and-plan-tier-truncation}

On tile selection (or "Other" continuation), the intake materializer runs synchronously inside a single Convex transaction:

1. **Read EvalStarter snapshot.** The materializer reads the EvalStarter row pinned to the row's `version` at click time. If the row has transitioned to `deprecated` between click and read, the materializer follows `successor_vertical_slug` and stamps the resulting Workspace's audit trail with `seeded_from_deprecated_redirect_to=<successor_slug>` per §13.12.6.
2. **Create the Workspace.** A new Workspace (§4.3.1) is created with `name = display_name + " evaluation"` (operator-editable from the next screen), `evaluation_owner_mode` defaulted per the buyer Org's plan tier (Free + Solo default `solo`; Starter+ default `team` per §4.3.1), `intake_eval_starter_id = <EvalStarter.id>`, `intake_eval_starter_version = <EvalStarter.version>`, `intake_freetext_label = <freetext when vertical=other else null>`, `seeded_from_deprecated_redirect_to = <successor_slug when the read followed a deprecated EvalStarter else null>`, and `expected_phase_durations` totaling `default_deadline_days` calendar days distributed proportionally across the §10.15 phase-duration benchmarks.
3. **Apply plan-tier truncation to seed counts.** The materializer compares the seed's Use Case and Requirement counts against the buyer Org's plan-tier ceilings from §34.1.1:
   - If `seed.use_cases.length > plan.use_cases_per_workspace_cap`, the materializer ranks Use Cases by `recommended_weight DESC` and instantiates the top N where N = the cap; truncated Use Cases are discarded along with their referenced Requirements.
   - If `seed.requirements.length > plan.requirements_per_workspace_cap` after Use Case truncation, the materializer ranks remaining Requirements by `weight DESC` and instantiates the top M where M = the cap.
   - Free tier (3 Use Cases, 200 Requirements per Workspace) is the only tier where truncation is reachable for the six default verticals at v7.0.0; Starter+ envelopes (50 / 2,000) accommodate the 3–8 / 30–80 seed bounds with headroom.
   - When truncation occurs, the resulting Workspace's "What we filled in for you" callout (§13.12.7 surface) MUST display the inline copy "Trimmed to fit your Free plan — upgrade to Starter to keep the full {N} Use Cases and {M} Requirements" with a single-click upgrade affordance routed per §34.5.
4. **Materialize Use Cases.** Each surviving seed Use Case is created as a §4.3.3 Use Case row, scoped to the new Workspace, with `name`, `description`, and ordering preserved.
5. **Materialize Requirements.** Each surviving seed Requirement is created as a §4.3.4 Requirement row attached to its parent Use Case via the seed's `requirement_indices` map. Seed fields are mapped into the canonical §4.3.4 column names: `title -> statement`, `description -> acceptance_criteria`, `category_enum -> type`, `priority_enum -> granularity`, `weight -> weight`, `scoring_model_enum -> scoring_model`, `response_type_enum -> response_type`, `default_pm_value -> default_pm_value`, and seed order -> `display_order`. Requirement has no local `status`; draft/readiness state is governed by the parent Workspace lifecycle, pipeline phase, and Amendment Protocol state machines.
6. **Apply rubric defaults.** The Workspace's `rubric_config_json` (§4.3.1 / §13.2.2) is initialized from `EvalStarter.default_rubric`: `pm_default_value` is set per the seed; FM/DNM remain locked at platform defaults; `scoring_model_mix` is copied as guidance metadata; `rubric_notes` is copied into `rubric_config_json.rubric_notes` for in-context display.
7. **Materialize recommended longlist.** Each surviving (post-opt-out-filter) `recommended_longlist` entry is materialized as a §4.3.20 Target Account row in the new Workspace with `status=prospect`, `created_from_eval_starter=true`, and `eval_starter_rationale=<seed entry's rationale>` for surface display. If `recommended_longlist` is null or filters to empty, the Workspace lands with no Target Accounts and the §13.12.7 surface renders the "no recommendations seeded yet — search the Marketplace" affordance.
8. **Stamp audit event.** Audit Event (§4.6.1) `workspace_created_from_eval_starter` is written with payload `{ eval_starter_id, eval_starter_version, vertical_slug, freetext_label, truncation_applied (boolean), use_cases_truncated (count), requirements_truncated (count), longlist_filtered (count), seeded_from_deprecated_redirect_to (nullable) }`. Action registered under the §4.6.1 entity_type `workspace`.
9. **Land on the Workspace.** The buyer is navigated to the new Workspace's §11.3 detail surface with the §13.12.7 "What we filled in for you" callout panel rendered for the first 60 seconds (or until dismissed).

The transaction is all-or-nothing: any failure in steps 4–7 reverts the Workspace creation and surfaces the §3.7 generic-error state with a "Try again or start blank" affordance. Partial materialization is impossible.

**Synchronous budget.** The full materialization MUST complete within p95 ≤ 2.5s for a 3-Use-Case / 30-Requirement seed (Free tier post-truncation) and within p95 ≤ 4.5s for an 8-Use-Case / 80-Requirement seed (Starter+). These bounds extend the §44.1 Performance Targets table (Workspace Load < 2s; Server-Side API Call Timeout 30s hard ceiling) — Authored Extension flagged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Phase 14.7 → Authored Extensions`; sign-off required from Engineering for the §44.1 row addition. Seeds exceeding the 4.5s upper bound at any future expansion MUST be moved to an asynchronous materialization path with a §3.7 progress-storytelling screen authored as an Authored Extension at that time.

### 13.12.5 Behavior — Free-Text "Other" Path {#13.12.5-behavior-other-path}

Selecting "Other" expands an inline 1–120-character free-text input. On submit, the materializer instantiates the Workspace against the `other` EvalStarter seed (the deliberately minimal default registered in §4.5.9) and stamps `Workspace.intake_freetext_label` with the buyer's input verbatim. The free-text label appears in the §11.3 Workspace header sub-label, in the inbox / Pulse cards as the workspace identifier, and in the §13.12.7 "What we filled in for you" callout as "We've started a generic Workspace for '{label}'. The defaults below are intentionally light — edit them as you go." The free-text label is not used to retrieve or match any other EvalStarter row; it is a display string only.

PII / abuse handling: the free-text input is rate-limited per buyer Org to 25 Workspace creations per day per §45.2 anti-spam controls, sanitized for HTML / script injection at write per §32 input validation, and excluded from public Marketplace surfaces (the label never crosses the buyer/seller firewall per §7.2). The label is included in the Workspace's DSAR export per §6.8.1 as part of the Workspace's user-supplied content.

### 13.12.6 Behavior — Deep Link to a Deprecated Slug {#13.12.6-behavior-deep-link-to-a-deprecated-slug}

A deep link of the form `/intake?vertical=<slug>` resolving to an EvalStarter row in `state=deprecated` MUST silently re-route to the row's `successor_vertical_slug` and materialize against the successor. The resulting Workspace's audit trail records `seeded_from_deprecated_redirect_to=<successor_slug>`. The buyer perceives no error or warning; the surface renders the successor's tile content as if it had been the original click. This invariant honors Principle 9 (§3.13 — Surface Simplicity, Engine Complexity): the registry-version mechanic is engine, the buyer's intent ("I want to evaluate this category") is the surface; the operator's intent must survive an Ops mid-flight content edit without being interrupted. If the deprecated row has no `successor_vertical_slug` set (a state forbidden at write per §4.5.9 state machine but defended against at read), the materializer falls back to the `other` EvalStarter seed with `intake_freetext_label = "<deprecated_slug>"` and stamps the audit trail with `seeded_from_deprecated_no_successor=<deprecated_slug>`.

### 13.12.7 Surface — "What We Filled In For You" Callout {#13.12.7-surface-what-we-filled-in-for-you}

On landing in the materialized Workspace (step 9 of §13.12.4), a callout panel renders pinned to the top-right of the §11.3 detail surface for the first 60 seconds or until dismissed. Layout:

1. **Header.** "What we filled in for you — edit anything."
2. **Body.** A four-row summary:
   - **Vertical.** "{Vertical display name}" (with the EvalStarter version stamp on hover for support diagnostics).
   - **Use Cases.** "{N} use cases" + a "Show" link that scrolls to the Use Case grid.
   - **Requirements.** "{M} requirements with default weights" + a "Show" link that scrolls to the Requirements Matrix.
   - **Vendors.** Either "{K} recommended vendors" + "Show" link (when `recommended_longlist` materialized non-empty), OR "No recommendations seeded yet — search the Marketplace" link routed to §27 Marketplace search filtered to the vertical's `Marketplace Category` (where the Marketplace Category mapping is set per the EvalStarter `vertical_slug`, registered in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Phase 14.7 → Authored Extensions` until the §22 inventory model lands).
   - **Deadline.** "Default deadline: {date} (in {default_deadline_days} days)" + a "Change" link that opens the §36.3 Workspace Settings deadline editor.
3. **Truncation banner (Free tier only when truncation applied).** Inline copy "Trimmed to fit your Free plan — upgrade to Starter to keep the full {N} Use Cases and {M} Requirements" with a single-click upgrade affordance routed per §34.5.
4. **Dismiss.** A single "Got it" button collapses the callout into a quiet "What we filled in for you" link in the §11.4 persistent UI; the callout can be re-opened from that link for the life of the Workspace.

The callout is read-only; every "Show" / "Change" / "upgrade" affordance navigates to the canonical edit surface for that artifact. The callout itself never edits Workspace state.

Telemetry: the `workspace_intake_completed` PostHog event (Appendix G — flagged Authored Extension; registration in §51 follow-up) carries `{ workspace_id, vertical_slug, freetext_label, truncation_applied, use_cases_materialized, requirements_materialized, longlist_materialized, deadline_days, time_to_intake_complete_ms, started_blank (boolean), seeded_from_deprecated_redirect_to (nullable) }`.

### 13.12.8 Edge Cases {#13.12.8-edge-cases}

The intake MUST handle the following edge cases explicitly:

1. **First-time user (no prior Workspaces).** The intake renders inside the §35.1 onboarding flow as Step 4; on completion, control returns to the onboarding sequencer for Step 5+ per §35.1. The Workspace is fully materialized; the §13.12.7 callout appears on the landing screen.
2. **Returning user (subsequent Workspace creation).** The intake renders standalone, triggered by the §3.10 / §11.4 "New Evaluation" CTA. On completion, the user lands directly in the new Workspace; no onboarding sequencer involved.
3. **Empty registry.** If every EvalStarter row is in `state ∈ {draft, deprecated, internal_ops_only}` (a deploy / Ops-config defect), the surface MUST render the muted "I want to start with a blank Workspace" link as the only affordance, and an Ops alert MUST fire (`eval_starter.empty_active_registry`, authored as an Authored Extension webhook in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Phase 14.7`). The buyer is never blocked from creating a Workspace.
4. **Materializer failure mid-transaction.** Per §13.12.4, the transaction is all-or-nothing; partial Workspaces never persist. The buyer sees the §3.7 generic-error state with two affordances: "Try again" (re-runs the materializer with the same EvalStarter snapshot) and "Start with a blank Workspace" (skips the seed entirely).
5. **Concurrent Ops edit during materialization.** The materializer's read-snapshot pin (step 1 of §13.12.4) guarantees the seed seen at click time is the seed materialized; concurrent Ops edits between click and write apply only to subsequent intakes.
6. **Plan downgrade after Workspace materialization.** If a buyer later downgrades and the materialized Workspace exceeds the new plan's caps, the standard §34.5.3 / §34.6 downgrade flow applies: 14-day pre-effective banner, 90-day read-only `DowngradeExcessDataBucket` for excess Use Cases / Requirements. The intake itself is silent on this — downgrade is a §34 mechanic.
7. **Buyer navigates away mid-intake.** The intake state is fully transient until tile click; navigating away before click discards no state. After click, the Workspace is materialized regardless of where the buyer navigates next; the materialized Workspace appears in the buyer's evaluation list.
8. **Mobile.** Tile grid stacks 1-column; tap targets meet the §38.6.2 per-tier minimum via §37.1. The "What we filled in for you" callout renders as a full-width card pinned to the top of the §11.3 mobile layout, dismissible the same way.
9. **Guest invite path.** Guests (§5.4) cannot create Workspaces and never see the intake; the surface is gated by the §5.11 RBAC matrix's "create Workspace" permission. Attempting to deep-link a guest to the intake redirects to the inbox with the standard "You don't have permission to do that" §3.7 state.
10. **Buyer/Seller console firewall.** The intake is a Buyer-console-only surface. A seller-console session that hits any intake URL MUST receive HTTP 404 per §1.3 / §7.2 firewall existence-leak rules.
11. **Data residency.** The materialized Workspace inherits the buyer Org's `data_residency_region` per §1.6 / §4.2.1; the EvalStarter seed itself is not residency-scoped (it is platform content, not user data). The intake never crosses residency boundaries.
12. **`recommended_longlist` references a Marketplace Listing that has been delisted between Ops publish and intake.** Per §13.12.4 step 7, the materializer re-validates every entry against the §4.5.6 render contract; delisted entries are silently filtered. The audit event payload's `longlist_filtered` count records the drop.

### 13.12.9 Plan-Gating, Feature Access, and Object Size {#13.12.9-plan-gating-feature-access-object-size}

Plan-tier behavior is governed by §34.1.1 (caps per tier) and §39 (object size). The intake itself adds no new plan-gated feature; it is a surface around existing entitlements. The Appendix M row authored for §13.12 binds the surface-level tier contract to the Feature Access Matrix; the row authored for §4.5.9 EvalStarter binds the registry-level tier contract.

### 13.12.10 Acceptance Criteria {#13.12.10-acceptance-criteria}

#### 13.12.10.1 Surface

1. The intake renders a single full-screen surface with the question "What are you evaluating?" as the only above-the-fold heading. No progress stepper, sub-header, or helper copy renders above the tile grid.
2. The tile grid renders six default verticals (CRM, ITSM, EDR, Observability, Payroll/HRIS, Other) in a 3 × 2 grid on desktop, 2 × 3 on tablet, 1 × 6 on mobile. Tile content (`display_name`, `short_description`, `icon_token`) is sourced from the §4.5.9 EvalStarter row whose `vertical_slug` matches the tile.
3. Selecting "Other" expands a single-line free-text input bounded to 1–120 characters with a "Continue" affordance. Submission materializes a Workspace against the `other` EvalStarter seed with `intake_freetext_label` set to the buyer's input verbatim.
4. A muted "I want to start with a blank Workspace" affordance renders below the tile grid for power users; selection materializes a blank Workspace with no Use Cases, Requirements, or longlist and the platform-default 28-day deadline.
5. Mobile renders the tile grid 1-column with tap targets meeting the §38.6.2 per-tier minimum via §37.1.

#### 13.12.10.2 Materialization

6. Tile selection materializes a Workspace synchronously inside a single Convex transaction; partial materialization MUST be impossible. Failure surfaces the §3.7 generic-error state with "Try again" and "Start with a blank Workspace" affordances.
7. The materialized Workspace's audit trail records `intake_eval_starter_id`, `intake_eval_starter_version`, `vertical_slug`, and `intake_freetext_label` (the latter only on the "Other" path).
8. On Free tier, when the seed exceeds the §34.1.1 caps (3 Use Cases / 200 Requirements per Workspace), the materializer truncates per §13.12.4 step 3 and surfaces the "Trimmed to fit your Free plan" inline copy in the §13.12.7 callout.
9. The full materialization completes within p95 ≤ 2.5s for Free-tier post-truncation seeds (3 / 30) and p95 ≤ 4.5s for Starter+ seeds (up to 8 / 80) per §44 budgets.
10. Every materialized artifact MUST be editable from the moment the operator lands. No seeded Use Case, Requirement, weight, scoring model, longlist entry, or deadline is locked. The materialization MUST NOT introduce any read-only or "starter-content protected" state on any seeded entity.

#### 13.12.10.3 Deprecated-Slug Routing

11. A deep link `/intake?vertical=<slug>` whose EvalStarter is `state=deprecated` AND has `successor_vertical_slug` set MUST silently materialize against the successor; the audit trail records `seeded_from_deprecated_redirect_to=<successor_slug>`. The buyer perceives no error or warning.
12. A deprecated slug with no successor (a state forbidden at write per §4.5.9 but defended at read) MUST fall back to the `other` EvalStarter seed with `intake_freetext_label=<deprecated_slug>` and audit-stamp `seeded_from_deprecated_no_successor`.

#### 13.12.10.4 "What We Filled In For You" Callout

13. The callout renders pinned to the top-right of the materialized Workspace's §11.3 detail surface for 60 seconds or until dismissed; thereafter it collapses into a "What we filled in for you" link in the §11.4 persistent UI re-openable for the life of the Workspace.
14. The callout displays five rows: Vertical, Use Cases (count + "Show"), Requirements (count + "Show"), Vendors (count + "Show", or the no-recommendations affordance), Deadline (date + "Change").
15. The Vendors row renders "No recommendations seeded yet — search the Marketplace" with a routed link to §27 Marketplace search filtered to the vertical's `Marketplace Category` whenever `recommended_longlist` materialized empty (null seed, fully filtered by opt-outs, or all entries delisted).
16. The Free-tier truncation banner renders inline in the callout when truncation was applied; it carries a single-click upgrade affordance routed per §34.5.

#### 13.12.10.5 Edge Cases & Firewall Integrity

17. A guest-role user attempting to access any intake URL MUST receive the §3.7 "You don't have permission to do that" state per §5.4 / §5.11.
18. A seller-console session attempting to read any intake URL MUST receive HTTP 404 per §1.3 / §7.2 firewall integrity rules; no row, count, or shape information leaks to the seller console.
19. An empty active EvalStarter registry (every row in `draft`, `deprecated`, or `internal_ops_only`) MUST render only the muted "blank Workspace" affordance and fire the `eval_starter.empty_active_registry` Ops alert; the buyer is never blocked from creating a Workspace.
20. The intake is rate-limited per buyer Org to 25 Workspace creations per day per §45.2 anti-spam controls; breaches surface the §3.7 rate-limit state with a "Try again in {N} hours" affordance.

#### 13.12.10.6 Telemetry & Audit

21. The `workspace_intake_completed` PostHog event fires on every successful materialization with the payload defined in §13.12.7.
22. An Audit Event (§4.6.1) `workspace_created_from_eval_starter` is written for every successful materialization with the payload defined in §13.12.4 step 8.
23. DSAR export (§6.8.1) for any user who created a Workspace via the intake MUST include `intake_freetext_label` (when set) and the `workspace_intake_completed` PostHog event payload as part of that user's data.

# 14\. Scenario Modeling {#14.-scenario-modeling}

## 14.1 Overview {#14.1-overview}

Scenario Modeling allows evaluators to define alternative weighting schemes, exclusions, and threshold configurations to rank vendors under different business assumptions. Scenarios are independent; multiple scenarios can coexist. Each scenario produces a ranked vendor list and optional comparison view.

## 14.2 Scenario Definition {#14.2-scenario-definition}

### 14.2.1 Scenario Object Schema

**V4 (D-4.5-001 P0 closure).** The canonical Evaluation Scenario entity field table is authored at §4.3.8; the canonical `parameters` JSON schema is §4.3.8.1; the canonical `results` JSON schema is §4.3.8.2. §14.2.1 forwards to those anchors and does not re-author the schema inline. The pre-V4 inline schema (which carried name ≤100 chars, description ≤300 chars constraints that contradicted §4.3.8's 1–200 / 0–2000 forms) is retired; §4.3.8 is canonical.

Cross-references:

- **Entity fields, scope isolation, indexes, retention, DSAR, residency, plan-tier metering treatment:** §4.3.8.
- **`parameters` structured object** (`weight_overrides`, `excluded_vendors`, `excluded_use_cases`, `rubric_overrides{pm_value}`, `min_threshold`, `tco_value_weight`) **with full validation rules:** §4.3.8.1.
- **`results` structured object** (`ranked_vendors[]`, `computed_at`, `scenario_version_at_compute`) **with stale-results detection:** §4.3.8.2.

### 14.2.2 Parameter Defaults

| Sub-field | Default | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `weight_overrides` | Empty object `{}` | All Use Cases inherit `original_weight` per §14.4.1 |
| `excluded_vendors` | Empty array `[]` | All Vendors in the parent Workspace contribute to the ranking |
| `excluded_use_cases` | Empty array `[]` | All Use Cases in the parent Workspace contribute |
| `rubric_overrides.pm_value` | Workspace `pm_default_value` (0.6 default per §13.2.2) | Range constraint 0.1 ≤ value ≤ 0.9 per §4.3.8.1 |
| `min_threshold` | 0.0 | No minimum; vendors below 0.0 are impossible by construction |
| `tco_value_weight` | 0.5 | Equal contribution of TCO percentile vs capability score blended into §14.4.1 |

The defaults apply on both POST-create (when `parameters` is omitted) and on the implicit "Original Scoring" scenario reference (§14.6.1 — the Workspace's baseline ranking computed without any scenario overrides).

## 14.3 Scenario Validation {#14.3-scenario-validation}

### 14.3.1 Validation Rules

All rules enforced on save. Errors listed inline above scenario form.

| Rule | Condition | Error Message |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| No all-zero weights | `SUM(weight_override[*]) + SUM(original_weight[non-excluded]) > 0` | "At least one use case must have a non-zero weight." |
| Vendor not excluded entirely | `COUNT(vendors) - COUNT(excluded_vendors) ≥ 1` | "At least one vendor must remain. Cannot exclude all vendors." |
| PM override range | `0.1 ≤ pm_value ≤ 0.9` | "PM override must be between 0.1 and 0.9." |
| Weight multiplier range | `0.0 ≤ multiplier ≤ 5.0` | "Weight multiplier must be between 0.0 and 5.0." |
| Min threshold range | `0.0 ≤ min_threshold ≤ 1.0` | "Minimum threshold must be between 0.0 and 1.0." |
| TCO weight range | `0.0 ≤ tco_value_weight ≤ 1.0` | "TCO value weight must be between 0.0 and 1.0." |

### 14.3.2 Error Presentation

- Errors displayed in a collapsible alert above the form (red background, icon)  
- Error messages listed as bullet points  
- Each error linked to the offending field (on click, scroll to field and highlight)  
- Save button disabled until all errors resolved

## 14.4 Scenario Scoring & Ranking {#14.4-scenario-scoring-&-ranking}

### 14.4.1 Blended Score with Scenario Overrides

- **Formula (revised with scenario parameters):**  
    
  blended\_score \=   
    
    (SUM(vendor\_use\_case\_score × effective\_weight) \+ (tco\_percentile × tco\_value\_weight))   
    
    /  
    
    (SUM(effective\_weight) \+ tco\_value\_weight)  
    
  where:  
    
    effective\_weight \= weight\_override\[use\_case\_id\] OR original\_weight\[use\_case\_id\]  
    
    vendor\_use\_case\_score uses rubric\_overrides.pm\_value if provided  
    
    tco\_percentile \= vendor's percentile in TCO ranking (0.0–1.0)

### 14.4.2 Ranking & Threshold

- **Ranked by:** Blended score, descending (highest score \= rank 1\)  
- **Threshold filtering:** Vendors with blended\_score \< min\_threshold marked as "Below Threshold" (still ranked, but highlighted in gray)  
- **Output:** Ranked vendor list with scores per use case, blended score, TCO percentile, threshold pass/fail

### 14.4.3 Recalculation

- **Trigger:** User saves scenario parameters  
- **Latency:** \<2 seconds (cached scoring data)  
- **Persistence:** Results persisted in `scenario.results`; timestamp in `computed_at`  
- **Refresh:** User can manually refresh results via "Recalculate" button; updates `computed_at`

## 14.5 Scenario Comparison View {#14.5-scenario-comparison-view}

### 14.5.1 Comparison Limit

- **Max scenarios in comparison:** 5 simultaneous  
- **Exceeding limit:** If user has \>5 scenarios, comparison UI shows dropdown to select which 5 to compare  
- **UI:** Toggle "Compare Scenarios" in scenario list; checkboxes appear, user selects ≤5, "Compare" button enabled

### 14.5.2 Comparison Matrix

- **Layout:** Matrix view (Section 11.3.2) with:  
  - **Rows:** Vendors (sorted by top scenario rank)  
  - **Columns:** Scenario 1 rank, Scenario 1 score, Scenario 2 rank, Scenario 2 score, ... (repeating)  
  - **Cell contents:** Rank (1–N) and score (% format), color-coded per scenario  
  - **Difference column (optional):** Shows ±rank change and ±score change vs. Scenario 1 (primary scenario)  
- **Interactions:**  
  - Click vendor row → detail view showing full score breakdown across all scenarios  
  - Hover cell → tooltip with breakdown (e.g., "Security: 0.95, Compliance: 0.88, TCO: 72nd percentile")  
  - Export → CSV with all scores and ranks

### 14.5.3 Scenario Sensitivity Analysis

- **Trigger:** "View Sensitivity" button in comparison view  
- **Purpose:** Show which parameter changes had the largest impact on vendor ranking  
- **Output:** Interactive chart showing:  
  - X-axis: Parameter (weight override, TCO weight, PM override, threshold)  
  - Y-axis: Rank change (for \#1 ranked vendor)  
  - Visualization: Line chart showing sensitivity curve  
- **Interaction:** Hover point → tooltip shows parameter value and resulting rank change  
- **Export:** Sensitivity data available in CSV export

## 14.6 Scenario Lifecycle & Permissions {#14.6-scenario-lifecycle-&-permissions}

### 14.6.1 Creation & Ownership

- **Creator:** Workspace Owner or Use Case Lead  
- **Ownership:** Workspace-level; visible to all team members with Viewer+ role  
- **Default scenario:** Workspace has implicit "Original Scoring" scenario (immutable, uses all original weights and rubric)

### 14.6.2 Editing & Deletion

- **Edit:** Only creator or Workspace Owner can edit scenario parameters  
- **Delete:** Only Workspace Owner can delete scenario; cannot delete "Original Scoring"  
- **Audit trail:** All scenario edits (parameter changes) logged with user, timestamp, before/after values

### 14.6.3 Immutability After Phase 12

- **At Phase 12 entry:** All scenarios locked; parameters and results immutable  
- **Reporting:** Final scenario results used in phase post-decision reports

## 14.7 Simulation Mode {#14.7-simulation-mode}

### 14.7.1 Interactive Scenario Adjustment

- **Trigger:** Press `S` while in Scenario view  
- **Entry:** Orange banner appears at top: "Simulation Mode — unsaved changes"  
- **State:** All parameter fields become editable inline (no need to click "Edit")  
- **Real-time recalculation:** Ranking updates live as user adjusts sliders/inputs  
- **Controls:** Inline sliders for weight multiplier (0.0–5.0), PM override (0.1–0.9), TCO weight (0.0–1.0)  
- **Checkboxes:** Vendor/use case exclusions as inline checkboxes  
- **Save:** Press `Cmd+S` (or `Ctrl+S` on Windows) to save simulation as a new scenario  
- **Reset:** Press `R` to revert to last saved state; exit simulation mode  
- **Exit:** Press `S` again or click X button to exit without saving

### 14.7.2 Simulation Limitations

- **No persistence:** If user navigates away without saving, simulation state is lost  
- **Separate from existing scenarios:** Simulation is a volatile session state; not saved to database  
- **Single simulation:** Only one active simulation per user session

## 14.8 Plan Limits & Report Integration {#14.8-plan-limits-&-report-integration}

### 14.8.1 Scenario Limits

Scenario Modeling is a universal Sourcera Method capability per §34.1.1 cell **Scenario Modeling** (wallet-charged on Free/Starter/Growth/Scale; Committed on Enterprise). The per-tier scenario-count caps below are throughput limits, NOT wallet caps; wallet ceilings are authoritative in §34.1.

| Plan tier (per §34.1.1) | Max Scenarios | Report Integration |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Free | 5 scenarios | No report integration; in-app only |
| Starter | 10 scenarios | No report integration; in-app only |
| Growth | 25 scenarios | Full integration; scenarios may be included/excluded in reports |
| Scale | 50 scenarios | Full integration; scenarios may be included/excluded in reports |
| Enterprise | Unlimited | Full integration + custom report appendices per §40.1 |

### 14.8.2 Report Integration (Growth and above)

- **Feature:** When generating a report on Growth, Scale, or Enterprise tiers, user can select which scenarios to include  
- **Report output:** For each included scenario, report shows ranked vendor list with scores and threshold status  
- **Comparison section:** Report can include scenario comparison matrix (shows top 5 scenarios only)

## 14.9 Acceptance Criteria {#14.9-acceptance-criteria}

### 14.9.1 Scenario Definition & Validation

- [ ] Scenario object persists with all parameters: weight\_overrides, excluded\_vendors/use\_cases, rubric\_overrides, thresholds, TCO weight  
- [ ] Save validation enforces: ≥1 vendor remaining, ≥1 use case with weight \> 0, parameter ranges  
- [ ] Errors displayed inline, linked to offending fields, Save button disabled until resolved  
- [ ] All validation rules from Table 14.3.1 enforced

### 14.9.2 Ranking & Scoring

- [ ] Blended score calculated per vendor using effective\_weight (overrides or original)  
- [ ] Vendors ranked by blended score descending  
- [ ] Threshold filtering marks vendors below min\_threshold; still ranked but visually distinct  
- [ ] Recalculation triggered on save; latency \<2s  
- [ ] Results persisted with computed\_at timestamp

### 14.9.3 Comparison View

- [ ] Max 5 scenarios compared; user selects which 5 if \>5 exist  
- [ ] Matrix displays rank \+ score per scenario per vendor  
- [ ] Difference column shows ±rank and ±score vs. primary scenario  
- [ ] Vendor row click opens detail view with full score breakdown  
- [ ] Sensitivity analysis chart shows parameter impact on top vendor rank  
- [ ] Export available (CSV)

### 14.9.4 Simulation Mode

- [ ] `S` key enters Simulation Mode; orange banner shown  
- [ ] Parameters editable inline (no "Edit" button required)  
- [ ] Real-time ranking updates as user adjusts sliders  
- [ ] `Cmd+S` / `Ctrl+S` saves simulation as new scenario  
- [ ] `R` resets to last saved state  
- [ ] `S` again exits simulation without saving  
- [ ] Navigation away without save loses simulation state

### 14.9.5 Plan Limits

- [ ] Free: scenarios not available  
- [ ] Business: max 10 scenarios, no report integration  
- [ ] Enterprise: max 50 scenarios, report integration enabled
