# 20\. Inbox & Pulse {#20.-inbox-&-pulse}

## 20.1 Overview {#20.1-overview}

Inbox is a unified notification center for all workspace activity. Pulse is a weekly digest of sourcing health via the Pulse Health Score and AI-generated insights delivered via email and in-app.

## 20.2 Inbox Structure {#20.2-inbox-structure}

### 20.2.0 Engine Source Bindings {#20.2.0-engine-source-bindings}

The buyer Inbox surface is a projection over the canonical entities InboxItem (§4.3.22.1), Inbox Item Group (§4.3.22), and Unread Marker (§4.3.15). §20 owns the surface behavior, filters, copy, and acceptance criteria; §4 owns field tables, indexes, scope isolation, retention, DSAR, and residency. §20 MUST NOT introduce another notification-item JSON shape.

The same engine writes run in Team Mode and Single-Operator Mode. When `Workspace.evaluation_owner_mode = solo`, the grouped team Pulse Inbox surface is suppressed per §2.8.4 and Appendix M.1, but InboxItem / Inbox Item Group rows continue to persist for audit, dashboarding, and post-`solo -> team` exposure. The Solo surface renders the §20.2.6 "What to do this week" panel from the same underlying item set.

### 20.2.1 Unified Feed

- **Location:** Dashboard \> Inbox tab (also accessible via global bell icon in top bar)  
- **Content types (priority-ordered):** Values resolve to Appendix J `notification_item_type`; UI labels are title-case and never render enum literals.
  1. **Phase transitions** (e.g., "Phase 7 started: Vendor Participation")  
  2. **SLA alerts** (e.g., "5 requirements due tomorrow")  
  3. **Q\&A mention** (e.g., "@You was mentioned in 'SSO Integration'")  
  4. **Amendment notifications** (e.g., "3 requirements pending review")  
  5. **Disagreement escalations** (e.g., "Disagreement on 'Security' — Use Case Lead review needed")  
  6. **Workspace invites** (e.g., "You've been invited to workspace 'Cloud RFx'")  
  7. **Team assignments** (e.g., "You've been assigned as Security use case lead")  
  8. **Scoring activity** (e.g., "Alice completed Security scoring")  
  9. **Response activity** (e.g., "Acme Corp submitted responses")  
  10. **General updates** (e.g., "Workspace created, Phase 1 started")

### 20.2.2 Canonical Inbox Render Model {#20.2.2-canonical-inbox-render-model}

Canonical persistence is InboxItem (§4.3.22.1). The prior JSON example is retired and MUST NOT be used as an implementation schema. The render model for the feed is:

| Render field | Source | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Item identity | InboxItem.`id` | Stable key for optimistic updates |
| Group identity | InboxItem.`inbox_item_group_id` -> Inbox Item Group (§4.3.22) | Optional; grouped rows expand into child items |
| Recipient | InboxItem.`recipient_user_id` | Feed is user-targeted; Org Admins do not see another user's feed unless an Ops-support impersonation path explicitly authorizes it |
| Type / filter chip | InboxItem.`notification_item_type` | Appendix J `notification_item_type` |
| Priority sort | InboxItem.`priority` | Appendix J `inbox_item_priority` |
| Copy | InboxItem.`title` + `description` | Title <=100 chars, description <=200 chars per §4.3.22.1 |
| Action | InboxItem.`action_url` + `action_label` | Re-authorized on click |
| Read / dismissed / expired state | InboxItem.`delivery_state`, `read_at`, `dismissed_at`, `expires_at` | Boolean `read` / `dismissed` fields are retired |
| Badge count | Unread Marker (§4.3.15) + Inbox Item Group.`unread_count` | Derived; never recomputed by scanning all item rows on every render |

### 20.2.3 Inbox Interactions

- **Mark as read:** Click notification or "Mark as read" action (single icon)  
- **Dismiss:** "X" button dismisses notification (removed from inbox, logged as dismissed)  
- **Click notification:** Opens action\_url in same tab or modal  
- **Mark all as read:** "Mark All as Read" button (top of feed)  
- **Filter:** Dropdown to show all, unread, or by type (PHASE\_TRANSITION, SLA\_ALERT, etc.)  
- **Sorting:** By priority (auto), then by created\_at (newest first)  
- **Pagination:** "Load More" button at bottom, lazy-load 20 at a time

### 20.2.4 Badge Count & Indicators

- **Unread count:** Red badge on bell icon (top bar) showing unread notification count  
- **Unread visual:** Unread items in feed have left blue bar \+ bold text  
- **Read visual:** Read items have normal opacity, gray text  
- **Dismissed visual:** Dismissed items removed from view; can be restored via filter "Show Dismissed" (admin view)

### 20.2.5 Notification Expiry

- **Auto-expiry:** Some notifications auto-dismiss after their relevance window passes. The expiry class is stored on InboxItem.`expires_at` / Inbox Item Group.`expires_at`; TTL behavior cites §40.2 and `inbox_item_group_ttl_class_enum` rather than adding new inline windows.
- **Expired notifications:** Removed from the default inbox view; archived visibility follows §40.2.

### 20.2.6 "What to do this week" Solo-Mode Panel {#20.2.6-what-to-do-this-week-solo-mode-panel}

When `Workspace.evaluation_owner_mode = solo`, the full grouped Pulse Inbox is suppressed per §2.8.4 and Appendix M.1. The operator instead sees a three-item "What to do this week" panel.

| Rule | Contract |
| :---- | :---- |
| Source | Same InboxItem / Inbox Item Group / Unread Marker writes as Team Mode; no second engine path |
| Item count | Exactly 3 slots; if fewer than 3 actionable items exist, remaining slots render positive completion copy, not dummy tasks |
| Ranking | `priority` first, then `created_at DESC`, then phase-criticality from §10 current phase |
| Eligible item types | `sla_alert`, `amendment_notification`, `disagreement_escalation`, `qa_mention`, `workspace_invite`, `team_assignment`, `response_activity`, and `general_update` when an action URL exists |
| Hidden from Solo | Cohort-grouping labels, per-component Pulse Health breakdown, SLA pills, and team-role chips |
| Transition to Team Mode | Previously-suppressed InboxItem rows become visible immediately after `solo -> team` transition; no backfill job required |

## 20.3 Pulse Health Score {#20.3-pulse-health-score}

### 20.3.1 Health Score Calculation

Canonical persistence is WorkspacePulseHealth (§4.3.22.2). The compute uses four normalized terms:

| Term | Definition | Applicability |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `sla_compliance_pct` | `safe_pct(requirements_within_sla, total_requirements)` | All active phases |
| `scoring_progress_pct` | `safe_pct(requirement_vendor_pairs_graded, total_requirement_vendor_pairs)` | Phase 10-11 |
| `response_rate_pct` | `safe_pct(requirements_with_vendor_response, total_requirements)` | Phase 6-11 |
| `phase_velocity_pct` | `clamp_pct(200 - ((actual_days_in_current_phase / sourcera_method_recommended_days) * 100))` | All active phases |

`safe_pct(numerator, denominator)` returns `null` when `denominator = 0`; otherwise it returns `clamp_pct((numerator / denominator) * 100)`. `clamp_pct(value)` returns `MAX(0, MIN(100, value))`. A null term is excluded from the weighted sum and the remaining non-null weights are renormalized to sum to 1.0. If every term in the selected weight set is null, the compute writes `composite_score = 0`, `color_band = red`, and `raw_inputs_json.empty_reason = no_available_terms`.

The old `Phase_velocity_ratio` term is retired. Velocity is now directionally correct: on-time phase velocity = 100; faster-than-recommended saturates at 100; a phase running twice the recommended duration yields 0. The deploy-time property test `pulse_health_velocity_monotonic_in_lateness` (§M.5) asserts the monotonicity.

### 20.3.2 Health Score Phases

| Phase band | Weight set | Term weights before null renormalization | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Before Phase 6 | `pre_phase_6` | SLA 0.5; Velocity 0.5 | Scoring and response terms excluded |
| Phase 6-9 | `phase_6_to_9` | SLA 0.4; Response 0.4; Velocity 0.2 | Scoring excluded |
| Phase 10-11 | `phase_10_to_11` | SLA 0.3; Scoring 0.3; Response 0.2; Velocity 0.2 | Full score |
| Phase 12+ | `phase_12_locked` | Latest Phase 10-11 score frozen | No mutable recompute; audit annotations append only |

State-machine table:

| From Phase | To Phase | Trigger | Weight Set | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Any pre-6 phase | Phase 6 | Phase Advancement API (§10.16) succeeds | `phase_6_to_9` | Next compute includes response-rate term if denominator exists |
| Phase 6-9 | Phase 10 | Phase Advancement API succeeds | `phase_10_to_11` | Next compute includes scoring-progress term if denominator exists |
| Phase 10-11 | Phase 12 | Phase 12 entry lock succeeds | `phase_12_locked` | Latest score is frozen; `locked_at` stamped |
| Any active phase | Same phase | Daily scheduler or manual refresh | Current phase-derived set | Append / update current-day WorkspacePulseHealth row |
| Archived / deleted Workspace | (terminal) | Retention boundary reached | n/a | No compute; retention follows §40.2 |

### 20.3.3 Health Score Output & Thresholds

- **Range:** 0–100 (displayed as percentage with color indicator)  
- **Green (80–100):** Healthy, on track  
- **Yellow (50–79):** At-risk, warning  
- **Red (0–49):** Critical, urgent action needed  
- **Breakdown display:** Show contribution of each non-null signal (e.g., "SLA: 95%, Response: 72%, Scoring: 58%, Velocity: 86%" -> blended Health Score 80%). Null terms render as "Not available yet" and do not count as zero unless every selected term is null.

### 20.3.4 Health Score Trend

- **Daily recording:** Health Score calculated daily at 9am UTC and persisted to WorkspacePulseHealth (§4.3.22.2). On-demand refresh updates the current-day row rather than creating duplicate same-day rows.
- **Trend visualization:** 7-day line chart showing historical scores \+ current  
- **Color trend:** Green line (healthy trajectory), yellow (neutral), red (declining)  
- **Actionable insights:** "Health score declining. Focus on SLA compliance (currently 62% vs target 95%)."
- **Threshold events:** Color-band transitions into yellow or red emit `pulse.health_score_threshold_breached` per §31 when the event registration is present; WorkspacePulseHealth.`band_transition_event_id` stores the correlation pointer.

## 20.4 Pulse Digest Email {#20.4-pulse-digest-email}

### 20.4.1 Weekly Digest Schedule

- **Frequency:** Every Monday morning at 9am workspace owner's local timezone (configurable to Wednesday or Friday)  
- **Recipient:** Workspace Owner, plus any team members opted in (Notification Settings)  
- **Delivery:** Via Loops.so email service  
- **Content:** HTML email \+ plain text fallback

### 20.4.2 Email Content Structure

Subject: \[Workspace Name\] Weekly Pulse — Health Score: 78% (Yellow)

\---- Header \----

Workspace: \[Workspace Name\]

Week: \[Date Range\]

Current Phase: \[Phase N\] (\[Phase Name\])

Health Score: \[Score\]% \[Color\] | \[Summary: e.g., "At-risk: Response rate low"\]

\---- Section 1: Health Overview \----

Your sourcing evaluation is progressing at medium pace.

Health Score Breakdown:

  • SLA Compliance: 95% ✓ (on target)

  • Response Rate: 72% ⚠ (below 85% target)

  • Scoring Progress: \[if Phase 10+\] X% (Y pairs graded)

  • Phase Velocity: 110% (trending 1 day late)

\---- Section 2: AI Summary (Agent-Generated) \----

\[\~300 tokens, Sonnet-generated summary of key trends \+ recommendations\]

Example:

"Responses are coming in slower than expected. Only 6 of 8 vendors have submitted responses to the RFI. 

Consider sending a reminder to CloudSoft and DataSys. SLA deadlines are approaching for the 'Compliance' 

use case—prioritize scoring those requirements this week to stay on track. Team velocity is strong; 

Alice and Bob have graded 40+ requirements each."

\---- Section 3: Action Items \----

Ranked by priority:

  1\. \[SLA alert\] 5 requirements due Friday. \[Action: Review Requirement\]

  2\. \[Disagreement\] 2 scoring disagreements await resolution. \[Action: Resolve\]

  3\. \[Amendment\] 1 policy ingestion pending review. \[Action: Review Amendment\]

\---- Section 4: Key Metrics \----

Table:

  Metric | Current | Target | Status

  \-------|---------|--------|--------

  SLA Compliance | 95% | 95% | ✓

  Response Rate | 72% | 85% | ⚠

  Scoring Progress | 45% | 70% | ⚠ (Phase 10+)

  Avg Phase Duration | 4d | 5d | ✓

\---- Footer \----

View full analytics: \[Link to Workspace \> Analytics\]

Update notification preferences: \[Link to Notification Settings\]

Workspace: \[Workspace Name\] | Org: \[Org Name\]

### 20.4.3 Agent-Generated Summary (Sonnet)

- **Model:** Claude Sonnet  
- **Input:** Current Health Score, all 4 signals, recent activities (new responses, new scores, SLA alerts, phase changes from past week)  
- **Output:** \~300 tokens, conversational summary highlighting:  
  - What's trending well (e.g., high SLA compliance, strong team velocity)  
  - What needs attention (e.g., low response rate, scoring disagreements)  
  - Top recommendation (e.g., "Send reminder to slow vendors", "Prioritize scoring X use case")  
- **Tone:** Professional, actionable, specific (mentions vendors/use cases by name)

## 20.5 In-App Pulse Widget {#20.5-in-app-pulse-widget}

### 20.5.1 Dashboard Pulse Card

- **Location:** Dashboard main panel (above or below Inbox)  
- **Display:**  
  - Health Score (large, color-coded: green/yellow/red)  
  - Trend sparkline (7-day history)  
  - Breakdown bars (SLA, Response, Scoring, Velocity, each weighted)  
  - "View Details" link (opens Pulse full view)  
  - "Last updated: \[timestamp\]"  
- **Real-time updates:** Pulse card updates daily (calculated at 9am UTC) or on-demand when user clicks "Refresh"

### 20.5.2 Full Pulse View

- **Route:** `/workspace/:workspace_id/pulse`  
- **Layout:**  
  - Left panel: Health Score summary (large), 7-day trend chart, breakdown breakdown  
  - Right panel:  
    - "This Week's Summary" (Agent-generated, \~300 tokens)  
    - "Action Items" (ranked by priority, max 5 shown)  
    - "Key Metrics" (table from email)  
  - Bottom: "View Weekly Digests Archive" (past 12 weeks)

### 20.5.3 Digest Archive

- **Accessible via:** "View Weekly Digests Archive" link on Pulse page or in email footer  
- **Display:** List of past 12 weekly digests (most recent first)  
- **Per digest:**  
  - Date range  
  - Health Score (on that date)  
  - Summary snippet (first 100 chars)  
  - "View" link (opens full digest as read-only)  
- **Export:** Export past 12 weeks as CSV (health score history \+ weekly summaries)

## 20.6 Notification Preferences & Settings {#20.6-notification-preferences-&-settings}

### 20.6.1 Notification Settings

- **Location:** Workspace Settings \> Notifications or User Settings \> Notifications  
- **Controls:**  
  - **Inbox:** Enable/disable all notifications (toggle)  
  - **Email digest:** Enable/disable weekly email, select day (Monday/Wednesday/Friday)  
  - **Per-notification-type:** Toggles for each type (Phase Transition, SLA Alert, Q\&A Mention, etc.)  
  - **Quiet hours:** Set time range (e.g., 6pm–9am) when notifications not sent (batched for next delivery)  
  - **Do Not Disturb:** Global pause all notifications for 24h (extends on click)

### 20.6.2 Notification Channels

- **In-app:** Always (if enabled globally)  
- **Email:** Only if "Email Notifications" enabled in settings  
- **SMS (Enterprise only):** Critical alerts only (Phase transitions, high-priority SLA); requires opt-in \+ phone verification  
- **Slack (future):** Integration planned for v7.0

## 20.7 Acceptance Criteria {#20.7-acceptance-criteria}

### 20.7.1 Inbox Feed

- [ ] Unified feed displays all notification types (Phase transitions, SLA alerts, Q\&A mentions, amendments, etc.)  
- [ ] Notifications priority-ordered (1=high, 2=medium, 3=low)  
- [ ] Unread badge shown on bell icon (count)  
- [ ] Mark as read / Dismiss actions available per notification  
- [ ] "Mark All as Read" button functional  
- [ ] Filter by type (All, Unread, PHASE\_TRANSITION, SLA\_ALERT, etc.)  
- [ ] Lazy-load pagination (20 per load)  
- [ ] Auto-expiry for relevant notifications (SLA alerts, phase transitions, Q\&A mentions, scoring activity)

### 20.7.2 Health Score Calculation

- [ ] Formula: 0.3×SLA \+ 0.3×Scoring \+ 0.2×Response \+ 0.2×Velocity (Phase 10+)  
- [ ] Before Phase 6: 0.5×SLA \+ 0.5×Velocity  
- [ ] Phase 6–9: 0.4×SLA \+ 0.4×Response \+ 0.2×Velocity  
- [ ] Velocity uses `phase_velocity_pct`, not retired `Phase_velocity_ratio`; on-time > late > 2× slow for the same phase baseline  
- [ ] Every term clamps to [0, 100]; final score clamps to [0, 100] after null-term weight renormalization  
- [ ] Denominator-zero terms become `null`, never NaN / Infinity; current score remains in [0, 100] at t=0  
- [ ] Output: 0–100, color-coded (green 80–100, yellow 50–79, red 0–49)  
- [ ] Breakdown chart shows contribution of each signal  
- [ ] 7-day trend chart visualized with historical scores  
- [ ] Daily calculation at 9am UTC persists exactly one WorkspacePulseHealth row per workspace per UTC date  
- [ ] Health Score locked at Phase 12 entry

### 20.7.3 Pulse Digest Email

- [ ] Weekly digest sent Monday 9am (configurable day \+ time) recipient's timezone  
- [ ] Subject includes workspace name \+ current health score \+ color  
- [ ] Content sections: Health Overview, AI Summary, Action Items, Key Metrics  
- [ ] AI summary: \~300 tokens, Sonnet-generated, specific \+ actionable  
- [ ] Action items: ranked by priority, max 5, include links  
- [ ] Metrics table: current, target, status  
- [ ] Footer: links to workspace analytics \+ notification settings  
- [ ] HTML \+ plain text versions

### 20.7.4 In-App Pulse Widget

- [ ] Dashboard Pulse card shows: Health Score, 7-day trend, breakdown bars  
- [ ] "View Details" link opens full Pulse view  
- [ ] Full Pulse view: Health Score summary, trend chart, This Week's Summary (AI), Action Items, Key Metrics  
- [ ] Digest Archive: past 12 weeks viewable, exportable as CSV  
- [ ] Last updated timestamp shown

### 20.7.5 Notification Settings

- [ ] Enable/disable all notifications (global toggle)  
- [ ] Weekly digest: enable/disable, select day (Mon/Wed/Fri)  
- [ ] Per-type toggles (Phase Transition, SLA Alert, Q\&A Mention, Amendment, Disagreement, Workspace Invite, Team Assignment, Scoring Activity, Response Activity)  
- [ ] Quiet hours: time range when notifications batched  
- [ ] Do Not Disturb: global pause for 24h (extendable)  
- [ ] Settings persist per user \+ workspace

# 21\. The Sourcera Agent {#21.-the-sourcera-agent}

## 21.1 Purpose {#21.1-purpose}

The Sourcera Agent is an AI-driven infrastructure layer woven into every stage of the product. It operates autonomously based on pipeline phase and user-configured rules, within strict data boundaries. The Buyer Console Agent cannot access Seller Console data, and vice versa. All Agent outputs are labeled `[AI-Generated]` with confidence scores. The Agent never replaces human judgment—it augments and accelerates it.

## 21.2 Architecture {#21.2-architecture}

**Multi-model approach:**

| Model | Use Cases | Cost Profile |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Claude Opus** | Complex document parsing (Policy Ingestion), deep reasoning tasks (scenario analysis) | $15–30 per framework. Used sparingly, one-time tasks |
| **Claude Sonnet** | Narrative generation, insight cards, risk analysis, Pre-Scoring, briefings, TCO analysis | \~$0.15–0.30 per call. Used frequently |
| **Claude Haiku** | High-frequency tasks: semantic matching, KB suggestions, deduplication, label tagging, staleness detection | \~$0.02–0.05 per call. Used at scale |

**Data boundaries:** Console isolation enforced at the Agent invocation layer — the LLM context window never receives cross-console data.

## 21.3 Guardrails & Hallucination Protection {#21.3-guardrails-&-hallucination-protection}

**Confidence thresholds:** Agent suggestions include a confidence score (0.0–1.0). Results below the configured threshold per capability are suppressed.

| Capability | Default Threshold |
| :---- | :---- |
| KB suggestions | 70% |
| Policy deduplication | 90% |
| Evidence parsing | 60% |
| Pre-Scoring | 65% |
| Disagreement Insight Cards | 50% |

Users may adjust thresholds per capability in Settings → Agent.

**Output labeling:** All Agent-generated content displays `[AI-Generated]` label with confidence score inline:

- Pre-Scores: "\[AI-Generated\] 82% confidence — FM(1.0)"  
- Suggestions: "\[AI-Generated\] 75% confidence — KB Entry \#4521"  
- Narratives: "\[AI-Generated\] Agent generated this summary. Edit to verify accuracy before sharing."

**User feedback loop:** Every Agent output includes "Was this helpful?" (thumbs up/down). Feedback is recorded per org and used for model recalibration. Users can report hallucinations via "This is wrong" link that opens a support form.

**Prohibited hallucinations:** Agent outputs are filtered against:

- Factually incorrect pre-scores (validated via override tracking)  
- Vendor names or data not from source documents  
- Scoring recommendations (Agent generates context, not a specific grade)

Failed or risky outputs gracefully degrade — the feature works without Agent suggestion.

## 21.4 Agent Capability Registry {#21.4-agent-capability-registry}

**Authoring Intent.** §21.4 supersedes the historic v6.0.0 hardcoded "21 capabilities" enumeration. The Agent Capability Registry is the platform-scoped, Ops-Console-managed list of every capability the Sourcera Agent can invoke, expressed authoritatively as `CapabilityRegistryEntry` rows (§4.8.2). Every billable AI invocation produces an `AIOperation` (§4.8.1) bound to a `capability_id`; every customer-billed operation settles against an `OutcomeContract` (§4.8.4) and draws from the Org's `AIWallet` (§4.8.3) per the burn priority in §34.10.1. Per Summary C.76, deprecations are soft and the registry is append-only; new capabilities are added by writing a `CapabilityRegistryEntry` + `OutcomeContract` + (if customer-billed) a `CostBaseRecalculationLog` seed — no §21.4 edit required.

**Source-of-truth pointers.**

- **Schema:** §4.8.2 `CapabilityRegistryEntry` (fields, indexes, state machine, acceptance criteria).
- **Settlement:** §4.8.1 `AIOperation` + §4.8.4 `OutcomeContract` + §34.11 Outcome Resolver.
- **Wallet behavior:** §4.8.3 `AIWallet` + §34.10 AI Wallet Service.
- **Pricing formula (`value_price = MAX(min_value, cost_base × value_multiplier)`; `cost_price = MAX(min_cost, cost_base × cost_multiplier)`; defaults `value_multiplier=10.000`, `cost_multiplier=1.050`, margin floor 88% blended):** §34.3.1.
- **Rate card (illustrative subset):** §34.3.4. **Live rate card:** Public Pricing API at `GET /v1/pricing` (§4.8.9).
- **Free Allowance (per Summary C.80, default 10 ops per Org per customer-billed capability; lifetime by default; resets only when `free_allowance_resets_per_period=true`):** §4.8.7 `FreeAllowanceCounter` + §34.8.4.
- **Plan gating:** §4.8.2 `plan_gate_min_tier` + §5.11 Feature Access Matrix + §34.1 Plan Tier Definitions + §34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix.
- **Marketplace-content cost-center routing (`platform_marketing` vs. `customer_billed` vs. `sourcera_owned`):** §4.8.2 `billing_mode` + §34.3.5.
- **Confidence thresholds:** §21.3 (per-capability confidence floor below which results are suppressed; threshold is an Org-tunable property of the registry entry, surfaced in Settings → Agent).

**Discoverability contract.** The customer-visible registry is the union of (a) every `CapabilityRegistryEntry` with `billing_mode=customer_billed` and `state ∈ {active, deprecated-within-grace, beta-and-customer-on-rollout-list}`, and (b) the rate-card snapshot in the latest `PricingTableVersion.published_payload_json` (§4.8.9). The Spec subsections below catalog the **seed state of the registry at v7.0.0** and the **extension delta from v6 → v7**; they are not the registry itself.

**Console firewall reminder.** Per §7.2 Dual-Console Firewall, a `CapabilityRegistryEntry`'s `console_applicability` array is enforced at AIOperation write time. A Buyer-only capability invoked from a Seller-console session is rejected with HTTP 403 `capability_console_mismatch` (Appendix I) before any ledger write.

**`sla_escalation` registry note.** Although rule-based and not LLM-invoked, `sla_escalation` is registered in `CapabilityRegistryEntry` with `model_tier_default=rule_based` and `billing_mode=sourcera_owned` so that (a) rate-card consumers see a comprehensive Agent surface, (b) Summary Summary §6.36 / Appendix G analytics taxonomy can correlate SLA-escalation events with downstream AI capabilities, and (c) future migrations to an LLM-augmented escalation path require no schema change.

**`org_intelligence_briefing` tri-split cardinality (C-3 resolution).** Row 16 is the root AI capability producing an organizational-intelligence briefing. At runtime it materializes into one of three plan-gated depth variants registered as sibling `CapabilityRegistryEntry` rows sharing `capability_family='org_intelligence'`: `org_intelligence_vendor_history` (Business Starter; vendor-history-only summary), `org_intelligence_full` (Business Growth; full briefing with competitor signals), `org_intelligence_suggestions` (Buyer Enterprise; full briefing + proactive suggestions + dedicated CSM review). Each variant has its own rate-card row in §34.14.1.b (Authored Extension for buyer-side — paired to the `org_intelligence_*` capabilities), its own OutcomeContract row in §34.15.1.b, and its own Entitlement Matrix row in §34.8.5 gated by plan tier. The `org_intelligence_briefing` root is reserved as the billing-ledger rollup identifier — customer-facing Billing Ledger reads aggregate the three variants under the root for display clarity, while the ledger itself records the invoked variant. Deploy-time validator `org_intelligence_family_cardinality` asserts exactly one of the three variants is invoked per briefing operation and that the root identifier never appears on an AIOperation row directly. This closes the cardinality ambiguity flagged by PHASE2_VERIFY item C-3.

**`tco_analysis_narrative` vs `tco_modeling` classification lock (C-2 resolution).** Row 14 `tco_analysis_narrative` is the AI-generated narrative layer — Phase 12, Sonnet, customer_billed. The related non-AI capability `tco_modeling` is a deterministic TCO calculator (not listed in §21.4.1 because it is non-AI) and appears in §34.8.5 with `enforcement_mode=n/a (non-AI)` and `free_allowance_ops=n/a`. These are distinct capabilities: `tco_modeling` computes the numeric TCO; `tco_analysis_narrative` produces the AI-authored narrative explaining the TCO result. The Entitlement Matrix plan-gates them separately — `tco_modeling` is available at `buyer_free` (no AI spend); `tco_analysis_narrative` is plan-gated at `business_starter` because the AI draw is Sonnet. Runtime invariant `tco_narrative_requires_tco_modeling_result` asserts a `tco_analysis_narrative` AIOperation MUST cite an upstream `tco_modeling` result id — running the narrative without an underlying calculation is rejected with HTTP 422 `tco_narrative_missing_source_calculation` (new; Appendix I). This closes the classification ambiguity flagged by PHASE2_VERIFY item C-2.

**`qa_suggestion` family-rooted sibling split (v7.2.0-REM Phase 4 D-EM-001 resolution).** Row 9 `qa_suggestion_family` is the **rollup root** for the Q&A Suggestion capability surface. Per the v6 → v7 canonicalization the historic single-row `qa_suggestion` v6 identifier was preserved through the v7.0.0 stamp solely because the seller-side Q&A response surface (§24 Seller Console Q&A) was the only customer-billed code path in the v6 baseline. The Phase 14.10 / 14.10.1 Solo-tier surface treatment introduces independent `surface_throttling_class`, `solo_envelope_override_value_cents`, and `solo_envelope_no_block` semantics per console, and the v7.1.0 Buyer Maya program elevated the buyer-side Agent Q&A Suggestion surface (§18.4) to first-class customer-billed status. The two surfaces share neither plan-gate floor, free-allowance default, OutcomeContract signal contract, nor surface_throttling_class — they MUST be registered as **family-rooted siblings** under the same pattern used by `org_intelligence_briefing` (above) and `kb_suggestion_buyer` / `kb_suggestion_seller`. At runtime row 9 materializes into exactly one of two plan-gated console-keyed variants registered as sibling `CapabilityRegistryEntry` rows sharing `capability_family='qa_suggestion'`: **`qa_suggestion_buyer`** (Buyer Workspace; §18.4 Agent Q&A Suggestion — buyer-side; Sonnet; Phase 6+) and **`qa_suggestion_seller`** (Bid Workspace; §24 Seller Console Q&A — seller-side answer composition; Sonnet; Phase 7). Each sibling has its own §34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix row, its own §21.4.5 Outcome Signal row, and its own §34.3.4 / §34.14.1 rate-card line. The `qa_suggestion_family` root identifier is reserved as the **billing-ledger rollup display identifier** — customer-facing Billing Ledger reads (§4.8.1 read serializer; `GET /v1/billing/operations`) aggregate the two siblings under the root for display clarity, while the ledger itself records the invoked sibling. Deploy-time validator `qa_suggestion_family_cardinality` asserts (a) exactly one sibling is invoked per `qa_suggestion_*` AIOperation, (b) the `qa_suggestion_family` root identifier NEVER appears on an AIOperation row directly — direct invocation is rejected at the AI invocation handler with HTTP 422 `capability_rollup_root_not_invokable` (new; Appendix I), and (c) the two siblings carry distinct `console_applicability` arrays such that a cross-console invocation is rejected at the §7.2 firewall check with HTTP 403 `capability_console_mismatch` (existing). The cross-validator `qa_suggestion_family_outcome_contract_isolation` asserts the buyer-side OutcomeContract version is independently versioned from the seller-side OutcomeContract version — a contract revision on one side MUST NOT retroactively re-resolve in-flight operations on the other (mirrors §4.8.4 acceptance criterion #2). This closes D-EM-001 P0 and remediates the §34.8.5 canonical-form lock note that previously referenced `qa_suggestion_buyer` as a runtime-bindable capability without a registry row. Full §4.8.2 field-set authority for both siblings lives in §21.4.1.B.

#### 21.4.1.B Q&A Suggestion Family-Rooted Sibling Split (v7.2.0-REM Phase 4 — D-EM-001 closure) {#21.4.1.B-qa-suggestion-family-split}

This subsection is the §4.8.2-fidelity registry-row authority for the two `qa_suggestion_*` siblings introduced by the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4 closure of D-EM-001 P0. Both rows are seeded into `CapabilityRegistryEntry` at the v7.1.0a hot-patch stamp; both inherit the §21.4.1 family-root rollup identifier `qa_suggestion_family` per the cardinality contract above. Each row is registered with full §4.8.2 field-set fidelity (every column populated; no implicit defaults). The seller-side row supersedes the historic v6.0.0 single-row `qa_suggestion` entry in-place — `CapabilityRegistryEntry.aliases` carries the v6 string on the seller-side sibling, and any in-flight v6 AIOperation rows continue to resolve via alias-rewrite at read time per §4.8.1 alias-projection rules.

**Why a sibling split rather than a console flag on a single row.** The two surfaces are functionally distinct AI capabilities that share only a product-area name. The buyer-side surface (§18.4) is a drafting tool that produces a single ≤300-character question post in a Public Buyer Q&A Thread (Sonnet; per-evaluation cadence; OutcomeContract window 14d aligned to the §13.7 RFP-phase Q&A surface). The seller-side surface (§24 Seller Console Q&A) is a per-answer composition tool that drafts a response paragraph against an inbound Buyer Q&A post (Sonnet; per-bid cadence; OutcomeContract window 7d aligned to the §22.20 Seller Maya bid-response flow). They draw on different KB scopes (buyer surface restricted to buyer-side workspace context + buyer's Org KB; seller surface bound to the seller's Bid Workspace context + the seller's Org KB per the §22.8.5 Managed Agent permission-scope policy), they carry different free-allowance trajectories (both 10 ops lifetime per the §21.4.4 default but on independent counters per `FreeAllowanceCounter` `(org_id, capability_id)` uniqueness), and they bind to different Solo-tier surface-throttling semantics (both `active_workflow` per `surface_throttling_class` because both sit on their respective operator's primary path, but the seller-side sibling carries `solo_envelope_no_block=true` per the §22.20.5 Hero Moment integrity contract — mid-bid Q&A interruption corrupts the seller's submission flow). A single console-flagged row cannot carry both Solo-envelope semantics simultaneously, and cannot satisfy the §44.6.4.1 `surface_throttling_class` mutation guard (which is per-CapabilityRegistryEntry, not per-console). The family-rooted sibling pattern resolves both constraints.

**In-place supersession rule (Row 2 only).** Per the §4.8.2 acceptance criterion #1 (`capability_id` MUST be immutable once any AIOperation has referenced it) and acceptance criterion #5 (hard-delete blocked), the v6.0.0 `qa_suggestion` registry entry is NOT deleted. Instead it is renamed in-place to `qa_suggestion_seller` under the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4 stamp-batch authority (recorded in AE-V72REM-PH4-01 with Ops Finance + Engineering Lead dual-signoff per the §4.8.2 acceptance criterion #1 exception clause registered as part of this closure — see Counterfactual #3 below). The renaming carries (a) the original `id` UUID, (b) the original `created_at`, (c) the full `published_in_pricing_api_versions` array, and (d) the original `outcome_contract_id` FK (the OutcomeContract row is the same row that has settled v6.0.0–v7.1.0 seller-side `qa_suggestion` operations — see §21.4.5 row `qa_suggestion_seller` below). Existing AIOperation rows that reference the legacy `qa_suggestion` `capability_id` string resolve to `qa_suggestion_seller` via alias-rewrite at read time per the §4.8.1 alias-projection rule; no AIOperation row migration is required. The `qa_suggestion_family` rollup root identifier inherits a new `id` UUID (no AIOperation row will ever directly reference the root — the deploy-time validator `qa_suggestion_family_cardinality` enforces this).

**Indexes (inherited from §4.8.2).** Both siblings participate in the standard CapabilityRegistryEntry index set: `(capability_id)` unique, `(state, console_applicability)` for available-capability listings, `(billing_mode, state)` for rate-card publication, `(plan_gate_min_tier)` partial for plan-gate enforcement queries, `(successor_capability_id)` partial for migration-graph traversal. A new partial index `(capability_family)` is registered alongside this remediation to support `qa_suggestion_family` rollup queries from the §4.8.1 Billing Ledger read serializer; index registration deferred to the M02.3 schema migration that lands the runtime wiring per AE-V72REM-PH4-01.

**Acceptance Criterion cross-reference (extension to §4.8.2 Acceptance Criteria).** AC #1 (`capability_id` immutability post-AIOperation reference) is satisfied for both siblings: the buyer-side row is new (no prior AIOperation references); the seller-side row preserves the original `id` UUID via in-place supersession (the visible `capability_id` string changes from `qa_suggestion` → `qa_suggestion_seller` but the storage-layer identifier — the `id` UUID — is unchanged; the legacy string survives as a `CapabilityRegistryEntry.aliases` array element, satisfying the immutability contract under the `aliases`-preservation interpretation registered in AE-V72REM-PH4-01). AC #6 (concurrent Ops writes rejected with HTTP 409 `capability_registry_concurrent_modification`) applies unchanged to both rows. AC #8 (Solo-tier surface-treatment fields) is satisfied per the field tables above. The new acceptance criterion #9 introduced by this remediation pass (qa_suggestion family-rooted sibling integrity) is registered as §4.8.2 AC #9 in the same edit: *"Every `qa_suggestion_*` AIOperation MUST cite a `capability_id ∈ {qa_suggestion_buyer, qa_suggestion_seller}` (the sibling set, NEVER the family-root `qa_suggestion_family` identifier); direct invocation of the family-root identifier MUST be rejected at the AI invocation handler with HTTP 422 `capability_rollup_root_not_invokable` (new; Appendix I). Deploy-time validator `qa_suggestion_family_cardinality` (§M.5.14) asserts."*

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Direct invocation of `qa_suggestion_family` rollup root identifier.** Resolved: HTTP 422 `capability_rollup_root_not_invokable` at the AI invocation handler; deploy-time validator `qa_suggestion_family_cardinality` (§M.5.14) blocks any code path that constructs an AIOperation with `capability_id = qa_suggestion_family`.
2. **Cross-console invocation (buyer-console session attempts `qa_suggestion_seller`, or vice versa).** Resolved: HTTP 403 `capability_console_mismatch` at the §7.2 firewall check per the existing `console_applicability` enforcement (§4.8.2). Sibling rows carry mutually exclusive `console_applicability` arrays.
3. **Legacy v6 `qa_suggestion` reference in an in-flight client SDK call after v7.1.0a stamp.** Resolved: alias-rewrite at the AI invocation handler resolves the legacy string to `qa_suggestion_seller` per the `CapabilityRegistryEntry.aliases` registry; AIOperation row writes against the canonical sibling `capability_id`; a one-time deprecation banner surfaces on the legacy code path per the §4.8.2 acceptance criterion #5 customer-visible-banner rule.
4. **Plan-tier downgrade mid-period where the buyer-side row's `plan_gate_min_tier` differs from the seller-side row.** Resolved: §34.8.6 #1 covers `pending` operations under prior wallet rules; downgrade applies per-sibling per-console at the next session-metadata refresh per §34.8.7 #5.
5. **OutcomeContract version bump on one sibling that the other sibling MUST NOT inherit.** Resolved: `outcome_contract_id` FKs are independent per sibling; the cross-validator `qa_suggestion_family_outcome_contract_isolation` (§M.5.14) asserts contract-version isolation per §21.4.1 family-split contract.
6. **PostHog analytics aggregation that double-counts the family-root + sibling event names.** Resolved: PostHog event-name aliasing per the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4 Appendix G extension routes the legacy `agent.qa_suggestion.invoked` event to the seller-side sibling event name `agent.qa_suggestion_seller.invoked` at ingestion time; the family-root identifier never emits a PostHog event because direct invocation is blocked.

**Retention.** Life of platform (per §4.8.2 retention rule); preserved indefinitely for FK integrity per the in-place supersession contract above. DSAR: not applicable (Ops-authored metadata; no subject PII per §6.8 DSAR cascade). Data-residency: platform-scoped (no `org_id`); both siblings replicate to every residency region per the §4.8.2 platform-scope rule.

#### 21.4.1.C Buyer-Console Augmentations Already in Registry (v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.2 — D-EM-002 Closure) {#21.4.1.C-buyer-console-augmentations}

This subsection is the §4.8.2-fidelity registry-row authority for six Buyer-side `CapabilityRegistryEntry` rows that were referenced from v7.0.0 publish onward by §34.3.4 (illustrative rate card), §34.8.5 (Entitlement Matrix Buyer Core Evaluation block), §34.1.1 cell narratives (AI Budget / Scenario Modeling / Selection Report companions), and BPS v3 §3–§5 (the Buyer Pricing Strategy capability surface) but were never seeded into §21.4.1 (Initial Seed) or §21.4.2 (Extended Capabilities) at v7.0.0 publish. The result is the D-EM-002 P0 defect (PROD-CRIT-009 in `_audit/REMEDIATION_BACKLOG.md §2`): every §34.8.5 matrix row whose `capability_id` is one of the six fails to resolve to a `CapabilityRegistryEntry` at the §34.8.2 runtime path, breaking the Buyer Core Evaluation billing path end-to-end. This subsection authors the six rows at full §4.8.2 field-set fidelity, mirroring the §21.4.1.B pattern used to close D-EM-001 (qa_suggestion family-rooted sibling split). The corresponding `qa_suggestion_buyer`-style §21.4.5 buyer-side outcome-signal rows are authored in the same closure batch (one new §21.4.5 row per registry row). Pricing seeds (cost_base + value_price + cost_price per §34.3.1 formula) are derived from the §34.3.4 illustrative rate card and recorded as `CostBaseRecalculationLog` seed rows per §4.8.6 at v7.1.0a hot-patch stamp; per-row `value_multiplier` and `cost_multiplier` overrides are applied where the §34.3.4 published price diverges from the §4.8.2-default `(10.000, 1.050)` formula result (illustrative-rate-card drift carried in via Authored Extension AE-V72REM-PH4.2-01 — Pricing Owner + Engineering Lead dual-signoff at v7.1.0a stamp).

**Authoring intent — why not §21.4.1.A.** §21.4.1.A is explicitly scoped to "Seller-Console Augmentations Already in Registry (KB Engineering Spec / Pricing Strategy)" — its mini-table format and seller-only content are not the right home for buyer-side rows. §21.4.1.C is the buyer-console counterpart, deliberately structured at full §4.8.2 field-set fidelity (one field-table per row) rather than the compact mini-table format used by §21.4.1.A, because (a) the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4 D-EM-001 closure (§21.4.1.B) established full-fidelity per-row tables as the authoring standard for v7.2.0-REM-program registry additions, and (b) the Solo-tier surface-treatment fields (`surface_throttling_class`, `solo_envelope_override_value_cents`, `solo_envelope_no_block`) per §4.8.2 AC #8 are per-row and cannot be compressed into a 6-column mini-table without semantic loss. The companion §21.4.1.A mini-table format is preserved in-place (no edits to §21.4.1.A in this closure batch).

**Counterfactual coverage (Opus mandatory pass).** Three realistic failure modes the closure addresses, each tested against an authored row before save: (1) **plan-tier downgrade mid-pending operation** (e.g., `deep_comparison` invoked under Business Starter, billing tier downgraded to Free before settlement) — §34.8.6 #1 covers `pending` operations under prior wallet rules; the `business_starter` plan-gate floor applies only to operations created at or after the downgrade timestamp; the `deep_comparison` row's `plan_gate_min_tier=business_starter` is honored at AIOperation write time, not at settlement time; (2) **Solo envelope exhaustion mid-evaluation on a Buyer Solo Org invoking `requirement_extraction`** — §44.6.4 silent-throttling engine evaluates against `surface_throttling_class`; every row in this subsection carries `active_workflow` per the §44.6.4.1 v7.1 membership rule (none is in the `low_priority_background` set), so the engine MUST NOT silently throttle these capabilities regardless of envelope state; the §M.5 gate `solo_envelope_throttling_targets_low_priority_background_only` asserts; (3) **concurrent invocation race when `FreeAllowanceCounter` is at quota_remaining=1** — §4.8.7 atomic decrement-and-return resolves the race; the loser's operation transitions to wallet-billed per §4.8.1 Failure Mode #11; the `(org_id, capability_id)` uniqueness constraint holds; no double-spend.

**Indexes (inherited from §4.8.2).** All six rows participate in the standard CapabilityRegistryEntry index set per §4.8.2: `(capability_id)` unique, `(state, console_applicability)` for available-capability listings, `(billing_mode, state)` for rate-card publication, `(plan_gate_min_tier)` partial for plan-gate enforcement queries, `(successor_capability_id)` partial for migration-graph traversal. No new indexes are introduced by this subsection.

**Acceptance Criterion cross-reference (extension to §4.8.2 Acceptance Criteria).** AC #1 (`capability_id` immutability post-AIOperation reference) is satisfied: all six rows are new authored rows whose `capability_id` strings have never been bound to a §21.4 registry row prior to v7.1.0a hot-patch stamp; runtime AIOperations for these capabilities since v7.0.0 stamp have written `capability_id` strings without a registry FK (per the D-EM-002 evidence — runtime path returns null on registry lookup), so there is no pre-existing immutable binding to preserve. Post-v7.1.0a stamp, the `capability_id` strings are bound to the newly-created `id` UUIDs and become immutable per AC #1. AC #2 (customer_billed → non-null `outcome_contract_id` before `state=active`) is satisfied per each row's `outcome_contract_id` field and the paired §21.4.5 outcome-signal row authored in the same closure batch. AC #6 (concurrent Ops writes rejected with HTTP 409 `capability_registry_concurrent_modification`) applies unchanged to all six rows. AC #8 (Solo-tier surface-treatment fields) is satisfied per the field tables above.

**Failure Modes Addressed (subsection-level).**

1. **Buyer-side billing path end-to-end resolution post-remediation.** Per the Self-Challenge pass logged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → v7.2.0-REM Program → Phase 4.2`: every §34.8.5 Buyer Core Evaluation row that lists one of the six `capability_id` strings now resolves at the §34.8.2 runtime path to a §21.4.1.C row with `state=active` and a non-null `outcome_contract_id`; entitlement evaluation passes; Free Allowance decrement proceeds atomically per §4.8.7; wallet draw proceeds per §34.10.1 burn priority; AIOperation row writes with full `capability_id` FK integrity.
2. **Concurrent invocation of `kb_suggestion_buyer` / `kb_suggestion_seller` from the same Org (cross-console parent context).** Resolved per §21.4.1.D below — the family-rooted sibling split routes invocations to per-console siblings; the `qa_suggestion_family_cardinality`-style validator extension `kb_suggestion_family_cardinality` (registered in §M.5.14 by the same v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.2 closure batch) asserts no direct invocation of the `kb_suggestion_family` rollup root.
3. **In-flight AIOperation rows pre-v7.1.0a stamp that reference one of the six `capability_id` strings without a registry FK.** Resolved: per §4.8.1 read-time alias-projection rule, pre-stamp AIOperation rows that wrote `capability_id` as a plain string (no FK) are upgraded at first read post-stamp to bind to the newly-created §21.4.1.C row's `id` UUID via the `capability_id` lookup; no data migration is required (the upgrade is read-time projection, not a destructive rewrite); historical billing-ledger reads preserve their original semantics.
4. **`scenario_modeling` rate-card publication absence at v7.1.0a stamp.** Resolved: the row is `state=active` and is published in the v7.1.0a PricingTableVersion per `published_in_pricing_api_versions`, but the §34.3.4 illustrative-rate-card snapshot does NOT yet carry a `scenario_modeling` row at v7.1.0a stamp (the §34.3.4 rate-card subsection is the v7.0.0 baseline, which omits scenario_modeling). Public Pricing API consumers MAY observe the capability in `GET /v1/pricing` (the live registry surface) but NOT in the §34.3.4 prose narrative until D-EM-013 P1 closure lands the §34.3.4 row addition at v7.1.1 stamp. Customer-facing pricing surfaces SHOULD treat the live API as authoritative per §4.8.9 v7.0.0 contract.
5. **`deep_comparison` soft-gate Free-Allowance-then-upgrade flow.** Resolved: per §34.8.5 line 29772 the row is `enforcement_mode=soft` at the Free plan tier (Free customers can use their 10-op Free Allowance, then hit a soft-gate upgrade CTA on the 11th invocation; `plan_gate_min_tier=business_starter` blocks wallet-billed invocations on Free); the §34.8.2 runtime path honors the soft-gate semantics per §34.8.5 acceptance criterion #2 (returns HTTP 200 with `upgrade_cta` + `blocked_reason` in the result envelope, not HTTP 403).
6. **Buyer Solo Org's six rows all engine-absorbed.** Resolved: per §44.6.3, every `customer_billed` capability invoked on a Buyer Solo Org is paid out of the engine-side margin envelope; the §44.6.4 silent-throttling engine evaluates against `surface_throttling_class`; all six rows carry `active_workflow` and are NEVER throttled; the Solo operator sees no wallet UI, no overage prompt, no billing surface — the §44 surface contract holds.

**Retention.** Life of platform (per §4.8.2 retention rule); preserved indefinitely for FK integrity. DSAR: not applicable (Ops-authored metadata; no subject PII per §6.8 DSAR cascade). Data-residency: platform-scoped (no `org_id`); all six rows replicate to every residency region per the §4.8.2 platform-scope rule.

#### 21.4.1.D KB Suggestion Family-Rooted Sibling Split (v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.2 — Extension to D-EM-002 Closure) {#21.4.1.D-kb-suggestion-family-split}

This subsection registers the **`kb_suggestion_family` rollup root** + two siblings — **`kb_suggestion_buyer`** and **`kb_suggestion_seller`** — at full §4.8.2 field-set fidelity, mirroring the §21.4.1.B pattern used to close D-EM-001 (qa_suggestion family-rooted sibling split). Authoring scope is an **Authored Extension to D-EM-002**: the prompt's named scope is the seven buyer-side `capability_id` rows enumerated in §34.8.5 lines 29178–29199, of which `kb_suggestion_buyer` is one. The counterfactual pass (Convention #16 of the v7.2.0-REM Program) revealed that authoring `kb_suggestion_buyer` as a standalone capability without authoring its `kb_suggestion_seller` sibling — which is already cited in the §34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix at line 29817 — would leave the matrix row orphaned and would fail the new `entitlement_matrix_registry_binding_completeness` CI gate (v7.2.0-REM Phase 4 D-EM-001 closure; §M.5.14) on first deploy-validator run post-wiring. The §34.8.5 canonical-form lock at line 29863 explicitly registers the dual-split contract: "(a) `kb_suggestion_family` → `kb_suggestion_buyer` / `kb_suggestion_seller`". Authoring the full three-row family in this same closure batch closes the gap atomically and prevents a cascading defect.

**Why a sibling split rather than a console flag on a single row.** The two surfaces are functionally distinct AI capabilities. The buyer-side surface (`kb_suggestion_buyer`) is a Phase 2/3 KB-mining suggestion tool that draws from the buyer's Org KB to suggest reusable Use Cases, Requirements, and Vendor records during evaluation onboarding (per §13.2 / §16.4 narrative; Haiku-tier, per-evaluation cadence). The seller-side surface (`kb_suggestion_seller`) is a Bid Workspace KB-mining suggestion tool that draws from the seller's Org KB to suggest reusable response paragraphs and capability declarations during bid drafting (per §22.13 / §24 narrative; Haiku-tier, per-bid cadence). They draw on different KB scopes (buyer surface restricted to buyer-Org KB; seller surface bound to seller-Org KB per §22.8.5 Managed Agent permission-scope policy), they carry different free-allowance trajectories (both 10 ops lifetime per §21.4.4 default but on independent counters per `FreeAllowanceCounter` `(org_id, capability_id)` uniqueness), and they bind to different Solo-tier surface-throttling semantics (both `active_workflow` because both sit on their respective operator's primary path, but per the §22.20 Hero Moment integrity contract the seller-side sibling could carry `solo_envelope_no_block=true` if Solo seller KB mining becomes a Hero Moment dependency — flag held at `false` at v7.1.0a stamp pending Hero Moment scope-amendment per AE-V11-01). A single console-flagged row cannot carry both Solo-envelope semantics simultaneously, and cannot satisfy the §44.6.4.1 `surface_throttling_class` mutation guard (which is per-CapabilityRegistryEntry, not per-console). The family-rooted sibling pattern resolves both constraints — identically to the §21.4.1.B `qa_suggestion_*` family-split.

**Authoring intent — relationship to §34.3.4 illustrative rate card.** §34.3.4 line 29467 currently publishes a single `kb_suggestion` (Cross-console, Haiku) rate-card row at value_price `$0.03` / cost_price `$0.004`. This is the **cardinality drift** flagged by D-EM-013 P1: the matrix splits into two siblings (lines 29767 `kb_suggestion_buyer` + 29817 `kb_suggestion_seller`) but the rate-card row is single. This subsection closes the registry side of the drift (authoring three §21.4.1.D rows); the §34.3.4 rate-card row split (single `kb_suggestion` → `kb_suggestion_buyer` + `kb_suggestion_seller`) is **deferred to D-EM-013 P1 closure at v7.1.1 stamp**, per the v7.2.0-REM Program scope discipline. Post-Phase-4.2 closure: the live `GET /v1/pricing` API surface (per §4.8.9) MUST publish the two siblings as separate rate-card lines (sourced from the new §21.4.1.D rows); the §34.3.4 illustrative prose narrative continues to show the single `kb_suggestion` row until D-EM-013 closure lands. This is the only inconsistency window introduced by the Phase 4.2 closure scope, and it is the minimum-blast-radius option given the prompt's "7 buyer-side capability_ids" scope.

**§21.4.1.D Footnote A — Console-disambiguated alias-rewrite for legacy `kb_suggestion` string.** Both buyer-side and seller-side siblings carry `[kb_suggestion]` in their `aliases` arrays. The AI invocation handler's alias-rewrite resolver is **console-disambiguated**: when a legacy `capability_id = kb_suggestion` invocation arrives, the resolver inspects the session's `console` context per §7.2 Dual-Console Firewall and routes to `kb_suggestion_buyer` for buyer-console sessions and `kb_suggestion_seller` for seller-console sessions. A session with no clear console context (theoretically impossible per §7.2 firewall enforcement, but covered for defensive completeness) is rejected with HTTP 422 `capability_alias_console_indeterminate` (new; Appendix I v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.2 extension). This is a **deliberate divergence from the §21.4.1.B `qa_suggestion_*` alias contract**, where the legacy `qa_suggestion` string aliases only to the seller-side sibling (because the v6.0.0 baseline was seller-only and the buyer-side surface is new in v7.1.0a). The kb_suggestion case differs: the legacy `kb_suggestion` string has cross-console rate-card history (§34.3.4 line 29467 explicitly publishes it as Cross-console) and both consoles have invoked it from v7.0.0 stamp onward via the matrix lines 29767 / 29817. A single-sibling alias-target would silently break one console's historical invocation chain. The console-disambiguated alias-rewrite is the narrowest possible extension to the §4.8.1 alias-projection rule that preserves historical AIOperation row resolution on both sides. The cross-validator `kb_suggestion_alias_console_resolution_integrity` (§M.5.14 v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.2 extension) asserts the disambiguation routes deterministically and that no AIOperation row writes against the family-root `kb_suggestion_family` identifier (which would bypass the console-disambiguation path entirely).

**Indexes (inherited from §4.8.2).** All three rows participate in the standard CapabilityRegistryEntry index set, plus the `(capability_family)` partial index registered by the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4 D-EM-001 closure (which the M02.3 schema migration lands at v7.1.0a stamp) — this same index supports `kb_suggestion_family` rollup queries from the §4.8.1 Billing Ledger read serializer.

**Acceptance Criterion cross-reference (extension to §4.8.2 Acceptance Criteria).** §4.8.2 AC #9 (qa_suggestion family-rooted sibling integrity per the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4 D-EM-001 closure) is **generalized** to all family-rooted sibling splits — including the new `kb_suggestion_*` family — under AC #9 amendment text: *"Every family-rooted sibling-split AIOperation MUST cite a `capability_id` from the sibling set of its `capability_family` (NEVER the family-root identifier); direct invocation of any family-root identifier (`qa_suggestion_family`, `kb_suggestion_family`, `org_intelligence_family`) MUST be rejected at the AI invocation handler with HTTP 422 `capability_rollup_root_not_invokable` per Appendix I. Deploy-time validators `{family}_family_cardinality` per §M.5.14 assert per-family."* The amendment is landed as part of this v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.2 closure (not a separate edit). The new validator `kb_suggestion_family_cardinality` is registered in §M.5.14 alongside `qa_suggestion_family_cardinality`.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Direct invocation of `kb_suggestion_family` rollup root identifier.** Resolved: HTTP 422 `capability_rollup_root_not_invokable` at the AI invocation handler; deploy-time validator `kb_suggestion_family_cardinality` (§M.5.14) blocks any code path that constructs an AIOperation with `capability_id = kb_suggestion_family`.
2. **Cross-console invocation (buyer-console session attempts `kb_suggestion_seller`, or vice versa).** Resolved: HTTP 403 `capability_console_mismatch` at the §7.2 firewall check per the existing `console_applicability` enforcement (§4.8.2). Sibling rows carry mutually exclusive `console_applicability` arrays.
3. **Legacy v6 / pre-Phase-4.2 `kb_suggestion` reference in an in-flight client SDK call after v7.1.0a stamp.** Resolved: console-disambiguated alias-rewrite per Footnote A above; AIOperation row writes against the canonical sibling `capability_id`; a one-time deprecation banner surfaces on the legacy code path per the §4.8.2 acceptance criterion #5 customer-visible-banner rule.
4. **Plan-tier downgrade mid-period where the buyer-side row's `plan_gate_min_tier=buyer_free` and the seller-side row's `plan_gate_min_tier=seller_free` apply to two different consoles of the same Org.** Resolved: §34.8.6 #1 covers `pending` operations under prior wallet rules; downgrade applies per-sibling per-console at the next session-metadata refresh per §34.8.7 #5. Cross-console pooled wallet behavior per §34.10.3 is unaffected — the wallet is Org-scoped and pooled; the plan-gate is per-console-per-sibling.
5. **OutcomeContract version bump on one sibling that the other sibling MUST NOT inherit.** Resolved: `outcome_contract_id` FKs are independent per sibling; the cross-validator `kb_suggestion_family_outcome_contract_isolation` (§M.5.14) asserts contract-version isolation per §21.4.1 family-split contract.
6. **PostHog analytics aggregation that double-counts the family-root + sibling event names.** Resolved: PostHog event-name aliasing per the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.2 Appendix G extension routes any legacy `agent.kb_suggestion.invoked` event to the appropriate console-disambiguated sibling event name (`agent.kb_suggestion_buyer.invoked` or `agent.kb_suggestion_seller.invoked`) at ingestion time based on the event's `console` property; the family-root identifier never emits a PostHog event because direct invocation is blocked. Historical pre-stamp analytics series preserve continuity via the same console-disambiguated alias-rewrite at the PostHog ingestion layer.

**Retention.** Life of platform (per §4.8.2 retention rule); preserved indefinitely for FK integrity. DSAR: not applicable. Data-residency: platform-scoped; all three rows replicate to every residency region per the §4.8.2 platform-scope rule.

#### 21.4.1.E First-Pass RFP Draft Per-Requirement Registry Row (v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.3 — D-EM-003 Closure) {#21.4.1.E-first-pass-rfp-draft-registry-row}

This subsection is the §4.8.2-fidelity registry-row authority for the single Seller-side capability **`first_pass_rfp_draft`** — the per-requirement, Seller-Free-on-ramp customer-billed capability cited as the runtime `capability_id` by §34.8.5 (Entitlement Matrix row, "Seller — Core AI (MS §2.8 baseline — §34.14.1 rows 1–12)" block), §34.14.1 row 1 (Rate Card MS §2.8 Baseline), §34.15.1 row 1 (Outcome Contract MS §2.9 Baseline), and §44.6.3 (Margin Envelope Defaults — First-Pass RFP Generator exemption). At v7.1.0a stamp the four §34/§44 surfaces co-reference a `capability_id = first_pass_rfp_draft` for which **no §21.4 registry row exists**, producing the D-EM-003 P0 defect: the §34.8.5 → §21.4 reverse-binding assertion `entitlement_matrix_registry_binding_completeness` (§M.5.14; introduced at v7.2.0-REM Phase 4 D-EM-001 closure and generalized at Phase 4.2 D-EM-002 closure) fails closed for this row on first deploy-validator run, and the §34.14.1 row 1 / §34.15.1 row 1 surfaces have no §21.4-resident `CapabilityRegistryEntry` to settle against, breaking the Seller-Free Hero Moment billing path end-to-end. This subsection authors the row at full §4.8.2 field-set fidelity, mirroring the §21.4.1.B / §21.4.1.C / §21.4.1.D pattern used to close D-EM-001 and D-EM-002 (sibling-split and standalone-row closures).

**Why a new §21.4.1.E subsection rather than appending to §21.4.1.A (Seller-Console Augmentations mini-table) or §21.4.2 (Extended Capabilities mini-table).** Per the §21.4.1.C "Authoring intent — why not §21.4.1.A" precedent established in the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.2 D-EM-002 closure, full §4.8.2 field-set fidelity (one field-table per row) is the authoring standard for v7.2.0-REM-program registry additions — not the compact mini-table format used by §21.4.1.A or §21.4.2. The Solo-tier surface-treatment fields (`surface_throttling_class`, `solo_envelope_override_value_cents`, `solo_envelope_no_block` per §4.8.2 AC #8) are per-row and load-bearing for the §44.6.3 First-Pass RFP exemption (`solo_envelope_no_block=true` is the engine-side guard); a 6-column mini-table cannot carry the flag without semantic loss. The §21.4.1.A and §21.4.2 mini-tables remain unedited in this closure batch.

**Naming-alias conflict surfaced and resolved (Convention #15 — surface before resolve).** Three distinct strings co-exist in the v7.1.0 corpus for the same conceptual capability and MUST be reconciled in this closure:

1. **`first_pass_rfp_draft`** — used as the `capability_id` by §34.8.5 line 30239, §34.14.1 row 1 (L30841), §34.15.1 row 1 (L30934), and §34.11.1 row 9 (signal name). This is also registered in §22.10.1.A row 1 as the **OutcomeContract signal name** (column 3) of the `first_pass_responses` batch capability. The §34/§44 surfaces treat the string as a `capability_id`; the §22.10.1.A table treats it as a signal-name. The §34 evidence is authoritative for the runtime `capability_id` per the Source-of-Truth Hierarchy (Master Spec §34 > §22 cross-reference table).
2. **`first_pass_responses`** — the Managed Agent batch capability registered in §21.4.2 row 3 (100-requirement batch; Sonnet; `seller_starter` plan-gate; `requires_managed_agent=true`). Per §22.10.1.A row 1 this is the canonical capability_id for the BATCH operation. NOT the same capability as the per-requirement `first_pass_rfp_draft`: different unit (1 requirement vs. 100-requirement batch), different plan-gate floor (`seller_free` vs. `seller_starter`), different Managed Agent requirement (`false` vs. `true`), different free-allowance default (10 vs. 10 batches; semantically distinct lifetime counters per §4.8.7 `(org_id, capability_id)` uniqueness). The two capabilities share the OutcomeContract **signal name** `first_pass_rfp_draft` (the artifact class is identical — RFP draft text) but settle against **independent OutcomeContract rows** with independent `outcome_contract_id` FKs, satisfying §4.8.4 acceptance criterion #1 ("Every OutcomeContract row MUST be referenced by exactly one CapabilityRegistryEntry row"). The shared-signal-name with independent-contracts pattern is permissible because the SellerOutcomeSignalConfig (§4.8.13) is indexed by `capability_id`, not by signal name.
3. **`first_pass_rfp_response_generator`** — referenced in §44.6.3 ("the First-Pass RFP Response Generator capability (`first_pass_rfp_response_generator` per §4.8.2 / §22.10) MUST NOT bid-wall a Solo seller mid-response"), §4.8.2 AC #8 ("notably `first_pass_rfp_response_generator` per §22.20.5"), and §44.6.5 narrative copy ("e.g., First-Pass RFP Response Generator"). The string is NOT registered as a `capability_id` anywhere in §21.4 and violates §22.10.1.A Hygiene Rule #3 (the `capability_id_canonicalization_lint` rule). This is a **non-canonical alias** that drifted into §44 and §4.8.2 AC #8 during the v7.1.0a Phase 14.10 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment program and was not reconciled at stamp time. The string is captured as an alias on the new row's `aliases` array.

**Resolution under the Source-of-Truth Hierarchy.** §34.14.1 / §34.15.1 / §34.8.5 — the runtime billing surfaces — are treated as authoritative for the `capability_id` literal at v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.3 closure: **`first_pass_rfp_draft` is the canonical `capability_id` for the per-requirement, Seller-Free customer-billed capability**, registered as a new row in this subsection. The §22.10.1.A row 1 alias-table entry is amended in this same closure to add a second row for `first_pass_rfp_draft` as a first-class canonical `capability_id` (independent of the batch capability's signal-name column-3 reference); see the §22.10.1.A patch block below. The §44.6.3 / §4.8.2 AC #8 / §44.6.5 references to `first_pass_rfp_response_generator` are reconciled in two parts: (a) the new row's `aliases` array carries `first_pass_rfp_response_generator` so alias-rewrite at the AI invocation handler resolves the string to `first_pass_rfp_draft`; (b) the §44.6.3 / §4.8.2 AC #8 / §44.6.5 prose hygiene rewrite to use the canonical form is deferred to a follow-on D-NOM-016 P2 cosmetic closure (registered in `_audit/REMEDIATION_BACKLOG.md → v7.1.1 Mechanical Hygiene` per scope discipline; the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.3 closure scope is the registry-row authoring + §34 binding, not corpus-wide prose hygiene). The §49.1.3 line 39781 reference to `first_pass_response` (singular) is also captured in the `aliases` array for completeness.

**Authoring intent — relationship to §34.14.1 row 1's published price.** §34.14.1 row 1 publishes `value_price = $0.15`, `cost_price = $0.02`, `cost_base = $0.019` for `first_pass_rfp_draft`. The §34.3.1 default formula `value_price = MAX(min_value, cost_base × 10)` evaluates to `MAX($0.05, $0.019 × 10 = $0.19) = $0.19`, which exceeds the published `$0.15`. This is a published-price-below-formula situation that does NOT match the §34.14.1 line 30856 narrative ("A recalc that would push `cost_base × 10` below the current `value_price` does NOT auto-reprice — it triggers a `cost_base_below_price_drift` alert") — that narrative covers the **opposite** drift direction (formula-below-published). The §34.14.1 row 1 published price is the MS §2.8 row 1 baseline lock per §34.14.1 line 30837, which §34.14.2 invariant #1 asserts at deploy: `value_price_cents = MAX(min_value_price_cents, ROUND(cost_base_cents × 10))`. To honor the published $0.15 without violating the invariant, the registry row applies a per-row `value_multiplier` override of `7.895` (i.e., `0.019 × 7.895 = 0.150`, rounded to integer cents) — mirroring the §21.4.1.C Row 1 / Row 2 / Row 3 precedent of using per-row multiplier overrides to align the formula with the §34.14.1 published rate. The deviation is logged in AE-V72REM-PH4.3-01 (Pricing Owner + Engineering Lead dual-signoff at v7.1.0a stamp). An alternative resolution — restating `cost_base` as `$0.015` so the default `× 10` multiplier yields `$0.15` exactly — is rejected because the §34.14.1 row 1 cost_base value `$0.019` is the published telemetry-derived cost-base from §34.3.2 nightly recalc and changing it would be a §34.3.3 BC-change requiring 30-day customer notification. The multiplier-override path preserves the §34.14.1 published surface unchanged.

**Free Allowance citation conflict surfaced (Convention #15) and resolved.** Three §34 surfaces disagree on the Free-tier lifetime allowance:

| Source | Claim | Citation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| §34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix L30239 | `free_allowance_ops = 10` | "Wallet-exhaustion CTA + concurrent-bids upgrade copy" |
| §34.14.1 row 1 plan-gating column L30841 | "All seller plans; Free = 25 lifetime (§34.1.2)" | MS §2.8 row 1; SPS §9 row 1 |
| §34.1.2 row "First-Pass RFP Response Generator" L29670 | "Wallet (Free $5 hard cap)" — does NOT state any per-capability lifetime free count | (the §34.14.1 cite is a forward-reference that drifted; §34.1.2 does not state 25) |

**Resolution.** The §34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix is the runtime contract per the §34.8.5 narrative "This matrix is the runtime contract for every plan-gated capability"; the runtime entitlement cache loads from §34.8.5 at deploy per §34.8.5 line 30297 "Matrix maintenance" rule. The registry row is authored with `free_allowance_quantity_default = 10` to align with §34.8.5 + Summary C.80 default + §4.8.2 default. The §34.14.1 / §34.1.2 "25 lifetime" drift is the **D-EM-009 P1 defect** registered in `_audit/REMEDIATION_BACKLOG.md → v7.1.1 Mechanical Hygiene` as a separate follow-on closure (not in v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.3 scope). The §34.14.1 row 1 plan-gating column SHALL be reconciled in D-PXC-007 closure either by (a) amending §34.1.2 to add the explicit "25 lifetime" cell value (if the MS §2.8 baseline is preserved) or (b) amending §34.14.1 row 1's plan-gating column to "Free = 10 lifetime (§34.8.5)" (if the §34.8.5 runtime contract is preserved). The Pricing Owner adjudicates the resolution at v7.1.1 stamp; engineering uses §34.8.5's value (10) in the interim.

**Counterfactual coverage (Opus mandatory pass — three realistic failure modes the closure addresses).**

1. **Seller Free Org invokes `first_pass_rfp_draft` mid-Hero-Moment after wallet exhaustion.** Per §44.6.3 First-Pass RFP exemption and §44.6.8 AC #6 (`solo_envelope_first_pass_rfp_no_block`), the capability MUST NOT bid-wall the operator mid-response. The new row carries `solo_envelope_no_block = true`. AIOperation handler honors the flag: the operation invokes successfully, AIOperation row is written with `effective_charge_cents = 0` and `solo_envelope_blocked = false` (the operation is NOT blocked — the flag tracks block-disposition, not actual blocking); the §44.6.5 `solo.capability.envelope_no_block_invoked` event fires to Ops Finance. Seller Free wallet at $0 still allows invocation; the cost is absorbed by the platform per §34.3.5; the seller surface continues to operate per §22.20.5 silent-AI rule (the seller never sees a wallet-exhaustion banner mid-bid).
2. **Seller Solo + Seller Free combination on the same Org invokes `first_pass_rfp_draft` while the Seller Solo per-bid envelope is exhausted.** Per §34.10.3 Solo-co-resident rule, the Seller Solo envelope is per-console engine-absorbed; per §44.6.7 #1, the envelope counter is per-console. The new row's `solo_envelope_no_block = true` honors the §44.6.3 contract for both Seller Solo (per-bid envelope exhaustion) and Seller Free (wallet exhaustion); the engine continues to serve the capability. `solo.capability.envelope_no_block_invoked` fires to Ops Finance for the Solo envelope exhaustion case (not for the Free wallet case — the Free wallet is a different exhaustion class per §34.10).
3. **Seller Free Org concurrent-invocation race when `FreeAllowanceCounter.quota_remaining = 1`.** Per §4.8.7 atomic decrement-and-return, the race resolves with one winner consuming the last free allowance; the loser's operation transitions to wallet-billed per §4.8.1 Failure Mode #11. Both operations cite the new `first_pass_rfp_draft` row's `outcome_contract_id` FK; both settle independently against the §34.15.1 row 1 signal contract; no double-spend. The §44.6.4 silent-throttling engine does NOT engage for `first_pass_rfp_draft` because `surface_throttling_class = active_workflow` per §44.6.4.1 v7.1 membership rule.

**Acceptance Criterion cross-reference (extension to §4.8.2 Acceptance Criteria).** §4.8.2 AC #1 (`capability_id` immutability post-AIOperation reference) is satisfied: the row is new — no AIOperation row has referenced `first_pass_rfp_draft` as a registry-resident `capability_id` prior to v7.1.0a stamp (the §34.14.1 / §34.15.1 / §34.8.5 / §44.6.3 references were unbound dangling references — the D-EM-003 defect itself). Existing AIOperation rows that carry `capability_id = first_pass_rfp_draft` written between v7.0.0 stamp and v7.1.0a stamp (the v7.0.0 → v7.1.0 production window during which the §34 surfaces were active but the §21.4 row was missing) are resolved at read time via the §4.8.1 alias-projection rule against this new row's canonical identifier; no AIOperation row migration is required. §4.8.2 AC #2 (customer_billed capability MUST have non-null `outcome_contract_id`) is satisfied per the field table. §4.8.2 AC #4 (Public Pricing API publication contract) is satisfied: the row is `state=active`, `billing_mode=customer_billed` and SHALL be included in the next published `PricingTableVersion` per §34.14.5 Lifecycle (`draft → under_review → approved → scheduled → published` flow). §4.8.2 AC #6 (concurrent Ops writes rejected with HTTP 409 `capability_registry_concurrent_modification`) applies unchanged. §4.8.2 AC #8 (Solo-tier surface-treatment fields) is satisfied per the field table; the `surface_throttling_class=active_workflow`, `solo_envelope_override_value_cents=NULL`, and `solo_envelope_no_block=true` values pass the §44.6.8 `solo_capability_registry_field_registration` validator. §4.8.2 AC #9 (family-rooted sibling-split integrity) does NOT apply (the row is standalone with `capability_family=NULL`; no family-root validator is registered for this capability).

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **AIOperation row written against `capability_id = first_pass_rfp_draft` between v7.0.0 stamp and v7.1.0a stamp resolves to NULL at the §4.8.1 read serializer.** Resolved: alias-projection at read time resolves the literal `first_pass_rfp_draft` against the new §21.4.1.E row's canonical identifier; the read serializer returns the new row's `display_name` / `unit_label` / `capability_id` consistently. The `effective_at = v7.0.0_stamp` carried in the §4.8.6 CostBaseRecalculationLog seed preserves billing-history continuity for these rows.
2. **Legacy `first_pass_rfp_response_generator` reference in an in-flight client SDK call OR engine-side §44.6.3 code path after v7.1.0a stamp.** Resolved: alias-rewrite at the AI invocation handler resolves the string to `first_pass_rfp_draft` per the new row's `aliases` array; AIOperation row writes against the canonical sibling `capability_id`; a one-time deprecation banner surfaces on the legacy code path per the §4.8.2 acceptance criterion #5 customer-visible-banner rule (banner suppressed on Solo / Free per §22.20.5 silent-AI surface).
3. **Direct invocation of `first_pass_responses` (batch sibling) by a Seller Free Org without an active Managed Agent.** Resolved: `first_pass_responses` carries `plan_gate_min_tier = seller_starter` (§21.4.2 row 3) and `requires_managed_agent = true`. The Seller Free Org hits HTTP 402 / 403 at the §34.8.5 entitlement-matrix path with the `first_pass_responses` upgrade-CTA copy "Batch First-Pass Responses (Managed Agent) unlocks at Seller Starter; Free tier uses `first_pass_rfp_draft` per requirement." Per the matrix copy, the customer is steered to the per-requirement `first_pass_rfp_draft` row authored here — closing the user-facing fallback path.
4. **Cross-console invocation (buyer-console session attempts `first_pass_rfp_draft`).** Resolved: HTTP 403 `capability_console_mismatch` at the §7.2 firewall check per `console_applicability=[seller]`. The buyer-console has no equivalent per-requirement capability (the buyer-side Response Drafting capability is `response_drafting` per §21.4.1.C Row 4).
5. **OutcomeContract version bump on `first_pass_responses` (batch) that this row's contract MUST NOT inherit.** Resolved: independent `outcome_contract_id` FKs per the field table; cross-validator `first_pass_rfp_draft_outcome_contract_isolation` (§M.5.16 v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.3 catalog block — sub-section landed at Phase 4.5 loose-ends closure 2026-05-19) asserts contract-version isolation per §4.8.4 AC #1. The §22.10.1.A patch row preserves the shared-signal-name semantic — the contract revision applies to the row's contract only, not to the sibling's contract.
6. **Seller Free wallet at $0 invokes `first_pass_rfp_draft` after Free Allowance exhaustion.** Per `solo_envelope_no_block=true` AND the §44.6.3 First-Pass RFP exemption AND the Seller Free $5 hard-cap rule per §34.10.4: the capability invokes successfully; the cost is absorbed by the platform per §34.3.5; `solo.capability.envelope_no_block_invoked` fires to Ops Finance for capacity-planning telemetry. The §22.20.5 silent-AI surface suppresses any wallet-exhaustion banner; the seller sees no UI change. **This is the critical Hero Moment integrity contract** — without `solo_envelope_no_block=true`, the §48.8.3 Hero Moment Stage 3 First-Pass Draft would block on Seller Free wallet exhaustion, breaking the §48.8.3 "Your bid is already drafted" workflow guarantee.

**Retention.** Life of platform (per §4.8.2 retention rule); preserved indefinitely for FK integrity. DSAR: not applicable (Ops-authored metadata; no subject PII per §6.8 DSAR cascade). Data-residency: platform-scoped (no `org_id`); the row replicates to every residency region per the §4.8.2 platform-scope rule.

**Authored Extension flag.** This entire §21.4.1.E subsection is **AE-V72REM-PH4.3-01** — registered in `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md → v7.2.0-REM Program → Phase 4.3 (D-EM-003 closure)`. Ratification requires Pricing Owner + Engineering Lead + Ops Lead triple-signoff before v7.1.1 stamp per the v7.2.0-REM Program scope discipline; the dual-signoff floor is elevated to triple-signoff because the row touches the §44.6.3 Solo-envelope contract (Ops Finance authority), the §34.14.1 rate-card (Pricing Owner authority), and the §22.10 Managed Agent surface (Engineering Lead authority).
