**Field-by-field interpretation.**

- **`Typical Tokens`** mirrors `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §13.2` for KB-side capabilities and is authored extension for buyer-side and platform-marketing capabilities (flagged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions` for Sales/Finance review).
- **Cost Base, Value Price, Cost Price** are seed values; nightly `CostBaseRecalculationLog` (§4.8.6) re-derives `cost_base` from actual Anthropic billing + Convex compute allocation per §34.3.3. Drift severity bands (`low ≥ 5%`, `medium ≥ 10%`, `high ≥ 25%`, `critical=margin-floor breach`) gate auto-publish per §34.11.3.
- **OutcomeContract Ref** points at the per-capability signal contract; full signal definitions are in §21.4.5 (this section). The contract's `default_on_timeout=rejected` rule per §4.8.4 acceptance criterion #5 applies to all 11 entries.
- **Default Confidence Threshold** is the per-capability floor below which the Agent suppresses the result per §21.3. Threshold is Org-tunable in Settings → Agent.
- **`plan_gate_min_tier`** uses the Plan Tier enum (Appendix J; values include `buyer_free`, `buyer_starter`, `buyer_growth`, `buyer_scale`, `buyer_enterprise`, `seller_free`, `seller_starter`, `seller_growth`, `seller_scale`, `seller_enterprise`). A capability marked `buyer_free` is available on every Buyer plan; `buyer_starter` requires Business Starter or higher; etc.
- **Free Allowance** specifies the seed value of `free_allowance_quantity_default` and `free_allowance_resets_per_period` in the registry entry; per Summary C.80, the platform default is **10 ops lifetime** unless explicitly overridden. `kb_bootstrap` and `ghost_rfp_ingestion` carry a **1-lifetime-free** override per Summary C.73 and SPS §9 (M15, KB §6.7).
- **`billing_mode`** drives whether the capability debits `AIWallet` or is recorded as COGS only. `platform_marketing` capabilities NEVER charge a customer Org regardless of which surface invoked them, even if the surface is customer-facing (e.g., a buyer reading a `category_faq_generation`-produced FAQ on a Marketplace Category Page).

**Output contract references.** The output contract per capability — i.e., the JSON schema returned by the Agent invocation handler — is enforced at the §32 API layer; per `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §13.4` and Master Spec §32, every Agent capability returns a structured response with `agent_output_envelope` (label `[AI-Generated]`, `confidence_score`, per-field provenance hash). Per-capability output contracts are versioned alongside the OutcomeContract; contract version skew between handler and OutcomeContract is rejected with HTTP 422 `agent_output_contract_version_mismatch` (Appendix I).

#### 21.4.2.A Failure Modes Addressed (Extended Capabilities)

1. **Customer attempts a Managed-Agent capability via direct invocation.** Resolved: `requires_managed_agent=true` on `first_pass_responses` (§22.10.2), `kb_bootstrap` (§22.10.3), and `ghost_rfp_ingestion` (§22.10.6) causes the AI invocation handler to reject direct `POST /v1/agent/invoke` calls with HTTP 422 `capability_requires_managed_agent` (new; Appendix I). Customers MUST invoke via the C.55 Managed Agent path, which (a) enforces the §22.8.5 permission-scope policy on KB MCP tool calls, (b) enforces the per-parent-AIOperation write caps on `kb_entry_draft_create` (§22.8.4.8) for bootstrap and ingestion workflows, and (c) rewrites parent/child `AIOperation` chaining per §4.8.1. The handler's refusal path logs `capability_requires_managed_agent_denied` to the §6.7 audit ledger (Appendix J extension — registered in this prompt) with `actor_user_id`, `capability_id`, `invocation_surface`.
2. **Platform-marketing capability invoked from a customer-tagged session.** Resolved: `billing_mode=platform_marketing` short-circuits wallet checks regardless of session tag; the AIOperation row is written with `cost_center=platform_marketing` per §34.3.5 and excluded from customer Billing Ledger reads.
3. **Lifetime-free capability concurrently invoked twice from same Org.** Resolved: §4.8.7 `FreeAllowanceCounter` uses an atomic decrement-and-return; the loser's operation transitions to wallet-billed with a single retry path per §4.8.1 Failure Mode #11.
4. **Confidence threshold tightened by Org during in-flight operation.** Resolved: confidence threshold is evaluated at result-render time (post-settlement), not at invocation time; the Outcome Resolver settles independently of threshold changes. A user-suppressed result still bills as an `AIOperation` per its OutcomeContract — threshold suppression is a UX filter, not a billing event.
5. **`market_intelligence_report` k-anonymity violation detected post-generation.** Resolved: editorial dual sign-off (Marketing + Finance) per §4.4.15 acceptance criteria gates publication; pre-publication failure transitions the AIOperation to `rejected` via §34.11.1 timeout (no signal received), and the operation is reversed via the Outcome Resolver per §34.11 (cost_price applies to the platform_marketing cost center per §34.3.5; no customer impact).

**Cost-center accounting rule.** Every `platform_marketing` and `sourcera_owned` `AIOperation` is written to the ledger with `cost_center` set to the registry default (per §4.8.2 `cost_center_default`). Reads of customer-facing Billing Ledger surfaces (§4.8.1 read serializer; §32 API `GET /v1/billing/operations`) MUST exclude these rows; QA test `aiop_platform_marketing_excluded_from_customer_ledger` asserts. Internal Sourcera dashboards (Summary Summary §6.36) include them under the appropriate cost-center filter.

**Anti-spam and quality controls.** All `platform_marketing` capabilities operate behind the §3.5 (Master Summary) anti-spam controls and the editorial workflows in §4.4.12–§4.4.16. A capability that produces content failing pre-publish content validation has its AIOperation reversed per §34.11 — the cost_price still applies to the Platform Marketing cost center, and a Signal Integrity Monitor (Summary C.100) alert raises if reversal rate exceeds the per-capability threshold (default 5% over 7 days).

### 21.4.4 Free-Plan Access Rules {#21.4.4-free-plan-access-rules}

This subsection is the §21.4 customer-facing summary; entitlement enforcement details live at §34.8 (Entitlement Enforcement) and the FreeAllowance machinery at §4.8.7 + §34.8.4. A capability is invokable from a Free plan if and only if **all four** of the following are true at AIOperation write time:

1. The capability's `plan_gate_min_tier` is `buyer_free` (or, for cross-console capabilities, the lower of `buyer_free` / `seller_free`); AND
2. The capability's `billing_mode = customer_billed` (Sourcera-owned and Platform-Marketing capabilities are never end-user-invokable from the customer console regardless of plan); AND
3. Either the Org's `FreeAllowanceCounter` for the capability has remaining units, OR the wallet has sufficient `budget_value_dollars` (Free plan: $5/mo unified pool; see §34.10.3 Pooled Budget Across Consoles, including the Free + Free pool-collapse rule) to cover `value_price_cents`; AND
4. The wallet is in `state ∈ {active, soft_warned_50, soft_warned_80}` — a `hard_capped_100` Free wallet rejects all customer-billed AIOperations with HTTP 402 `wallet_hard_capped` per §34.10.4.

**Per-capability free allowance defaults (seed at v7.0.0).** Per Summary C.80, every `customer_billed` capability seeds with `free_allowance_quantity_default = 10` and `free_allowance_resets_per_period = false` (lifetime). Two overrides at v7.0.0 seed:

| `capability_id` | `free_allowance_quantity_default` | `free_allowance_resets_per_period` | Override Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `kb_bootstrap` | 1 | false | SPS §9 (KB §6.7); Summary §6.13.2 |
| `ghost_rfp_ingestion` | 1 | false | SPS §9; Summary C.73 |

All other customer-billed seed entries (Initial Registry Seed §21.4.1, KB-Spec augmentations §21.4.1.A, and Extended capabilities §21.4.2) use the C.80 default (10 ops lifetime).

**Free-plan wallet caps (cross-reference).** Per BPS §3 / SPS §3 / §34.10.3, a Free Buyer + Free Seller Org sees a single $5/mo unified wallet pool (the Free + Free pool collapse rule, Authored Extension flagged in §34.10.3). Wallet overage is **disabled** on Free; an admin attempting to enable wallet overage on a Free wallet is rejected with HTTP 422 `wallet_overage_requires_paid_plan` (Appendix I).

**Plan-gated capability behavior on Free.** A capability whose `plan_gate_min_tier` exceeds Free is treated as `entitlement_mode=hard` per §34.8.5 — the capability is hidden from the in-product Agent surface and the AI invocation handler rejects direct invocation with HTTP 402 `capability_requires_plan_upgrade` (Appendix I), surfacing an upgrade CTA per §34.8.5 acceptance criteria. Examples in the v7 seed: `seller_page_enrichment` (`seller_starter`), `next_evaluation_suggestion` (`buyer_starter`).

### 21.4.5 Outcome Signals {#21.4.5-outcome-signals}

The OutcomeContract (§4.8.4) for every customer-billed `CapabilityRegistryEntry` defines the **accepted signal**, **rejected signal**, **window**, **`auto_accept_after_seconds`**, **`signal_evaluation_grace_seconds`**, **`requires_explicit_user_signal`**, and **`contest_window_days`** (default 14, ≤ 90). The full live registry is the OutcomeContract table; §21.4.5 below catalogs the **concrete accepted/rejected signal definitions** for the v7 seed. The `accepted` signal is what a product surface MUST emit through the event-bus interface to the Outcome Resolver (§34.11) to resolve a `pending` operation as `accepted`; the `rejected` signal is the user action (or absence of action through `auto_accept_after_seconds`) that resolves it as `rejected`.

**Versioning and customer notice.** Per §4.8.4 acceptance criterion #2, the OutcomeContract version active at AIOperation `created_at` is the version the Resolver uses; switching contract versions does NOT retroactively re-resolve in-flight operations. Per §34.11.1, a contract revision is a minor-version bump; per §34.3.3 + §4.8.9, customer-visible commercial impact (e.g., a window contraction that materially raises rejection probability) triggers the 30-day-advance notification gate and grandfathers annual contracts for the contract remainder.

**Per-capability `auto_accept_after_seconds` and `signal_evaluation_grace_seconds` defaults** are seeded per the table above (the "Auto-Accept After" column corresponds to `auto_accept_after_seconds`; `signal_evaluation_grace_seconds` defaults to 24h beyond the auto-accept timer to absorb late `rejected` signals — late rejected signals after auto-accept materialize a ContestRecord per §4.8.5).

**`requires_explicit_user_signal=true` overrides.** Two capabilities require an explicit user signal and do NOT auto-accept on timer alone: `kb_bootstrap` (because the value of bootstrap is gated on ≥ 60% acceptance, which is a deliberate seller action) and `ghost_rfp_ingestion` (because the value is gated on a future-bid citation, which is observable only retrospectively). For these, `auto_accept_after_seconds` is a soft surface trigger that prompts the seller for confirmation; a true `accepted` resolution requires the signal listed in the Accepted column.

#### 21.4.5.A Counterfactual Failure Modes (Outcome Signals)

1. **Signal-source service outage during the resolver window.** Resolved: per §34.11.4 acceptance criterion #1, every AIOperation MUST receive a settlement decision within `auto_accept_after_seconds + signal_evaluation_grace_seconds`. If the signal-emitting service is degraded, the operation auto-resolves per `default_on_timeout=rejected` (§4.8.4); customers may file a ContestRecord per §34.11.2 within the 14-day contest window for refund.
2. **Adversarial signal spoofing (e.g., automated "use" clicks to inflate `accepted` rate).** Resolved: every Outcome Resolver signal carries an `actor_id` and is anti-spam-screened via Signal Integrity Monitor (Summary C.100); anomalous signal velocity per Org per capability triggers a Signal Integrity alert and may pause auto-accept on the suspected capability for that Org pending Ops review.
3. **Signal-emitting surface ambiguity (e.g., user clicks "Use" then immediately reverts).** Resolved: legacy `kb_to_response_suggestion` invocations are alias-rewritten to `kb_suggestion_seller`; the `kb_suggestion_seller` signal contract requires the suggested content to appear in the **submitted** response artifact with retained paragraph/capability-declaration evidence, not merely the click event. The Resolver evaluates the persistence condition at the closer of (window expiry, surface-publish event, `auto_accept_after_seconds`). Click-and-revert within `signal_evaluation_grace_seconds` does not register as accepted.
4. **Capability with `requires_explicit_user_signal=true` accumulates indefinite `pending` rows.** Resolved: even with explicit-signal contracts, the operation is forced to `rejected` at window expiry per §4.8.4; an Ops-Finance dashboard surfaces capabilities with sustained pending-row growth as a quality signal (not a billing signal).

### 21.4.6 Solo Throttling Membership (v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.4 — D-EM-004 Closure) {#21.4.6-solo-throttling-membership}

This subsection is the §4.8.2-fidelity registry-row authority for the three `CapabilityRegistryEntry` rows whose `surface_throttling_class = low_priority_background` and which therefore constitute the v7.1 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment throttling-membership set per §44.6.4.1. The three rows were enumerated at v7.1.0 stamp in two forward-reference sites (§4.8.2 `surface_throttling_class` field Notes line and §44.6.4.1 membership block) without §21.4 registry rows — the result is the D-EM-004 P0 defect (PROD-CRIT-009 cluster in `_audit/REMEDIATION_BACKLOG.md §2`): the §44.6.4 silent-throttling engine cannot resolve the three `capability_id` strings to `CapabilityRegistryEntry` rows at the §34.8.2 runtime path, breaking the §44.6.8 #5 acceptance criterion (`solo_envelope_throttling_targets_low_priority_background_only`) and the §44.6.8 #17 schema-validation test (`solo_capability_registry_field_registration`). This subsection authors the three rows at full §4.8.2 field-set fidelity, mirroring the §21.4.1.B / §21.4.1.C / §21.4.1.D / §21.4.1.E pattern used to close D-EM-001 / D-EM-002 / D-EM-003 P0 sibling defects in the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4 program. The paired §21.4.5 outcome-signal rows (for the two `customer_billed` members), §34.8.5 entitlement-matrix rows, Appendix G PostHog event-name registrations, and `CostBaseRecalculationLog` seeds are authored in the same closure batch. AE-14.10-07 (v7.1 `low_priority_background` capability membership) is the binding ratification gate — sign-off lands at this closure per the AE Ledger transition recorded jointly with this Master Spec edit.

**Authoring intent — why §21.4.6 (new sub-section) rather than §21.4.2 or §21.4.3.** §21.4.2 is the Extended Capabilities (v7 Registry Additions) block — scoped to the 11 v7.0.0-stamp additions per Summary §6.12.2 and Appendix C.76 and not the appropriate home for a v7.1.0 retroactive seed pass. §21.4.3 is Platform-Owned Capabilities — the right home for the sole `sourcera_owned` member of this set (`vendor_page_enrichment_polling`) but not for the two `customer_billed` members. A new dedicated sub-section is the cleanest pattern because (a) the three rows share a single binding contract (the §44.6.4 Solo throttling-membership closed set, mutation-guarded by §44.6.4.1's Ops Finance + Founder dual-signoff rule), (b) the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.X precedent registers per-closure-batch sub-sections (§21.4.1.B / §21.4.1.C / §21.4.1.D / §21.4.1.E) at full §4.8.2 field-set fidelity, and (c) the closed-set integrity is a first-class invariant under the §44.6.4.1 mutation guard — separating the closed set into a single named sub-section makes the integrity-asserting deploy-time validator (`low_priority_background_solo_throttling_membership_canonical`) trivially bindable to the §21.4.6 table contents. Companion §21.4.3 entry for `vendor_page_enrichment_polling` is preserved cross-referentially — the row's storage-of-record is §21.4.6 (canonical authority) and §21.4.3 carries a single-line cross-reference annotation to avoid duplication while preserving the existing platform-owned-capability roster's completeness.

**Closed-set integrity invariant.** The v7.1 `low_priority_background` membership is exactly the three rows below. Any future addition or removal from this set is an Ops Finance + Founder dual-signoff action per §44.6.4.1, triggers a §4.8.9 PricingTableVersion publish (rate-card unchanged; registry version bumped for partner-integration freshness), AND requires extending the §M.5 catalog meta-gate `low_priority_background_solo_throttling_membership_canonical` (Authored Extension AE-V72REM-PH4.4-02 — Engineering Lead sign-off pending M02.3 runtime wiring; see CI-gate registration paragraph at the end of this subsection). Adding a fourth member without updating both the §21.4.6 table AND the meta-gate enumeration is a `closed_set_integrity_violation` and a P0 defect.

**Counterfactual coverage (Opus-mandatory pass).** Three realistic failure modes the closure addresses, each tested against an authored row before save: (1) **Solo Buyer Org with envelope at `throttling_threshold=80%` invokes `proactive_cmd_k_marketplace_surfacing` via the §3.2 Command Palette during active vendor evaluation** — §44.6.4 silent-throttling engine resolves `surface_throttling_class=low_priority_background` from the §21.4.6 Row 1; suppresses the invocation for the remainder of the envelope window; writes AIOperation row with `effective_charge_cents=0` and `solo_envelope_blocked=true` (§4.8.1 AE-14.10-04 flag); emits the single §44.6.4 #3 toast; does NOT engage on the operator's active workflow (e.g., a concurrently-invoked `pre_scoring` AIOperation continues normally per §44.6.4 #4); §44.6.8 #5 gate asserts the bounded-suppression semantics; (2) **non-Solo plan tier (e.g., `business_starter` Buyer) invokes the same `proactive_cmd_k_marketplace_surfacing` capability** — the §44.6.4 throttling engine evaluates against the Buyer Org's plan tier first per §44.6.4 ("When a **Solo** Org's actual consumption..."); non-Solo plans do NOT carry an engine-side margin envelope; the capability invokes normally regardless of `surface_throttling_class`; AIWallet draws `value_price_cents` per §34.8.4 / §34.10.1; §44.6.8 #5 gate asserts the Solo-only scope; (3) **concurrent invocation race** when two `proactive_cmd_k_marketplace_surfacing` AIOperations arrive for the same Solo Org within the same envelope-window second (e.g., two Cmd+K open events fired in quick succession at the threshold-crossing edge) — §44.6.7 #15 optimistic-locking pattern on `(org_id, console, envelope_window_id)` serializes the suppress decision; only one writer transitions the envelope to `throttled`; the second writer reads the resulting suppressed-write state and emits no second toast (per §44.6.4 #3 single-emission rule per envelope window); both AIOperation rows are written with `solo_envelope_blocked=true` and `effective_charge_cents=0`; §44.6.8 #7 gate `solo_throttling_toast_single_emission` asserts.

**Self-challenge pass (Opus-mandatory adversarial re-read).** Three hostile-staff-engineer findings on draft of this subsection, each revised in place before save: (a) earlier draft set `vendor_page_enrichment_polling` to `customer_billed` with a derived sub-cent `value_price` — flagged as overspecification of a passive polling job that has no clear customer-visible value and would saddle the seller with unexpected wallet draws on a Sourcera-initiated polling action; revised to `sourcera_owned` per the §44.6.4.1 mixed-cost-center membership pattern + the explicit D-EM-004 resolution prescription ("`sourcera_owned` for the polling job — Ops Finance + Founder dual-signoff per §44.6.4.1"); (b) earlier draft omitted §21.4.5 outcome-signal rows for the two `customer_billed` members on the (incorrect) assumption that silently-throttled capabilities don't need OutcomeContracts; revised — §4.8.2 AC #2 requires `outcome_contract_id` on every `customer_billed` row regardless of throttling-class membership, because the throttling layer is engine-side suppression (§44.6.4) but the surviving non-Solo invocations still settle through the §34.11 Outcome Resolver; the two §21.4.5 rows are authored below; (c) earlier draft listed `proactive_cmd_k_marketplace_surfacing` with `console_applicability=[buyer, seller]` on the (incorrect) assumption that Cmd+K Marketplace surfacing exists on both consoles — verified against §3.2 Command Palette + §27 Marketplace narratives: only the Buyer Cmd+K surfaces proactive Marketplace cards (the Seller Cmd+K is bid-workspace-scoped per §22.20.4); revised to `console_applicability=[buyer]`. All three findings are pre-emptive remediations of defects that would otherwise have surfaced at the first deploy-validator run post-wiring.

## 21.5 Agent AI Budgets (Value-Dollars and Wallet Behavior) {#21.5-agent-ai-budgets-(value-dollars)}

The §21.5 surface is the customer-facing summary of how Agent capabilities consume budget. Authoritative entity mechanics live at **§4.8.3 `AIWallet`** (schema, indexes, state machine, acceptance criteria) and operational policy at **§34.10 AI Wallet Service** (counters, configuration, pooled-budget-across-consoles rule, Stripe metering, downgrade behavior, failure modes). §21.5 references the wallet rather than re-stating its rules.

**Value-dollar denomination.** AI budgets are denominated in **value-dollars**, not Anthropic tokens. Value-dollars are stable across cost-base recalculation: per §34.3.1, `value_price_cents = MAX(min_value, cost_base × value_multiplier)` with `value_multiplier=10.000` held invariant across the platform; if Anthropic pricing moves, the multiplier holds and `cost_base` is re-derived nightly per §34.3.3 / §4.8.6. Customers see a single, stable value-dollar number; cost-base movement is internal to Sourcera's COGS.

**Authoritative references.** Per-plan AI included-budget figures are authoritative in §34.1.1 (Buyer Plan Tiers) and §34.1.2 (Seller Plan Tiers). Wallet overage configuration, auto-topup semantics, exhaustion behavior, and the wallet state machine are authoritative in §34.10 (AI Wallet Service). Pooled-across-consoles math, the Free-side collapse rule, and the `(Buyer + Seller)` unified-wallet invariant are authoritative in §34.10.3. Per-capability Free Allowance behavior is authoritative in §34.8.4 and `FreeAllowanceCounter` (§4.8.7). Wallet visibility surfaces — Settings → AI Usage, Public Pricing API parity, per-capability breakdown, per-model breakdown, burn-rate forecast, committed-remaining — are authoritative in §4.8.3 (AIWallet) acceptance criteria and §4.8.7 (FreeAllowanceCounter) acceptance criteria. Burn priority (`commit_burn_remaining → budget_value_dollars → overage_cap_value_dollars`, with Free Allowance bypassing all three) is authoritative in §34.10.1. Error codes for exhaustion (`ai_wallet_exhausted`, `wallet_hard_capped`) are authoritative in Appendix I.

The value-dollar denomination and the cost-base recalculation rule are described in this section's preamble (above); everything else is referenced. Per Authoring Convention #10 ("every dollar figure has one authoritative home"), §21.5 MUST NOT restate per-plan budget figures, wallet state transitions, or visibility surface bullets.

**Acceptance criteria.** §21.5 carries no independent acceptance criteria; the effective acceptance set is the union of §4.8.3 AIWallet ACs, §4.8.7 FreeAllowanceCounter ACs, §34.10 AI Wallet Service ACs, and §34.20 consolidated ACs. Specifically:

1. Settings → AI Usage ↔ `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/wallet` parity — §4.8.3 AC + §32.8.2.
2. Wallet hold placement precedes AIOperation write — §4.8.1 AC #7 + §4.8.3 AC.
3. Free Allowance distinct from wallet consumption in the UI — §4.8.7 AC + §34.8.4.
4. Unified single value-dollar number for pooled Orgs — §4.8.3 AC + §34.10.3.

## 21.6 Agent Failure Handling {#21.6-agent-failure-handling}

| Failure Type | Behavior | User Impact |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Model error / timeout | Retry once with exponential backoff (1s, then 2s). If retry fails, graceful degradation | Feature works without Agent output. Toast: "\[Feature Name\] suggestion unavailable. You can proceed manually." |
| AI Wallet exhausted | Reject call with `ai_wallet_exhausted` (cross-ref §34.10.4 wallet state machine: `hard_capped_100` blocks further AIOperation invocation; soft-capped states honor overage policy per §4.8.3) | User prompted to top up the AI Wallet, enable auto-topup, upgrade plan tier, or wait for the next billing period reset. Failed calls that retry consume value-dollars only on the settling attempt; failed calls that degrade gracefully consume the `cost_price` per §4.8.1. |
| Context window exceeded | Truncate input to fit window (with priority: most recent requirements first). Return partial results with warning | Toast: "Large request — Agent processed first 500 requirements. Remaining items skipped." |
| Prompt injection detected | Reject call and log security event | Toast: "Request blocked for security. Contact support if you believe this is an error." |

**Graceful degradation examples:**

- If Pre-Scoring fails, Scoring phase opens with empty suggested grades. Evaluators proceed with manual scoring.  
- If Evidence Parsing fails, vendor can still submit the file; it appears in responses without Agent summary.  
- If KB suggestion fails, Bid Workspace shows response form without suggestions.  
- If Policy Ingestion fails, user is prompted to retry or contact support.

**Cost:** Failed calls that retry consume value-dollars only on the settling attempt per §4.8.1 `effective_charge_cents` semantics (the wallet hold placed for the failed attempt is released when the retry settles). Failed calls that degrade gracefully — i.e., the user receives a partial or manual-fallback surface rather than a retry — consume the `cost_price` per §4.8.1 (the AIOperation resolves with `outcome_resolution=rejected` and `effective_charge_cents = cost_price_cents`), consistent with the outcome resolver (§34.11).

## 21.7 Agent Bias & Limitations {#21.7-agent-bias-&-limitations}

1. **Semantic matching** (Haiku) works well for exact-domain matches but may fail on novel jargon or industry-specific terminology. Confidence \< threshold is filtered out.  
2. **Policy parsing** (Opus) works reliably for NIST CSF, ISO 27001, SOC 2\. Non-standard or non-English documents produce lower quality. Scanned PDFs and image-only documents are rejected.  
3. **Narratives** (Sonnet) are generated from structured data and may lack nuanced domain expertise. All narratives are labeled `[AI-Generated]` and should be reviewed by domain experts before final use.  
4. **Pre-Scoring** assumes vendor response quality and clarity. Ambiguous or vague responses may receive lower confidence scores. The Agent never recommends a specific grade—it provides context via Insight Cards, not direction.  
5. **Evidence parsing** relies on document metadata and OCR quality. Handwritten notes, images, or non-standard file formats are not supported.

## 21.8 Custom Agent Instructions {#21.8-custom-agent-instructions}

**Purpose:** Allow Team Owners to define domain-specific rules that apply globally across all active Workspaces within their team.

**Example instructions:**

- "Flag any vendor response mentioning 'OpenAI' as High Risk — InfoSec concern."  
- "Auto-tag Requirements with 'GDPR' if the description contains 'data residency' or 'EU user data'."  
- "Boost KB suggestion confidence by \+10% for entries reviewed in the past 30 days."

**Storage & Security:**

- Instructions stored per Team in `team.agent_instructions` (array, max 50 instructions)  
- Each instruction is sandboxed against prompt injection via strict parameter filtering  
- All instruction changes are versioned in the audit trail with user attribution and timestamp  
- Instructions are applied within 60 seconds of save via a Convex scheduled function

**Constraints:**

- Max 5,000 characters per instruction  
- No access to cross-console data  
- Cannot modify RBAC or phase transitions  
- Cannot delete or modify vendor data

**User Interface:** Section 8 (Organization & Admin) covers the settings page. Instructions are edited in Team Settings → Agent Rules.

## 21.9 Acceptance Criteria {#21.9-acceptance-criteria}

- All Agent calls complete within specified timeouts (30–60s for Sonnet, 10–20s for Haiku, 3–10 min for Opus).  
- Agent failures gracefully degrade without blocking user workflows.  
- Monthly value-dollar consumption is accurately metered against the AIWallet (§34.10) and displayed per §4.8.3 / §4.8.7 visibility surfaces; `FreeAllowanceCounter` draw precedes wallet draw per §34.8.4; pooled-across-consoles math per §34.10.3.  
- Console isolation is enforced — no cross-console data in Agent context windows.  
- All Agent outputs labeled `[AI-Generated]` with confidence score.  
- Confidence threshold filtering removes results below configured threshold per org.  
- Custom Agent Instructions applied within 60 seconds of save.  
- User feedback loop captures helpfulness votes and hallucination reports.

# 22\. Seller Console — Knowledge Base {#22.-seller-console-—-knowledge-base}

**Authoring intent (v7.0.0).** §22 was rewritten in the v7.0.0 integration to absorb `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §0–§3` in full as the authoritative engineering substrate of the Seller KB. Prior to v7.0.0 (v6.0.0), §22 was a thin product-level description of the KB. The v7.0.0 rewrite preserves the v6.0.0 product surface (now reorganized as §22.1, §22.3, §22.5, §22.6, §22.7) and inserts the engineering surface (§22.2, §22.4, §22.8) verbatim from the KB Engineering Spec, with cross-links to the Capability Registry (§21.4), AIOperation settlement (§4.8.1, §34.11), and the Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2). All KB-Spec content is normalized to Master Spec authoring conventions: every entity gets a field table; every state machine renders as From/To/Trigger; every API tool gets a request/response schema; every new term lands in Appendix K (the canonical Glossary per Phase 12.3 amendment; Appendix B is the Keyboard Shortcut Reference); every new enum lands in Appendix J. CI gate `appendix_k_glossary_canonicality` asserts the appendix routing.

**Source-of-truth precedence inside §22.** Where this section reproduces content from `KB_Engineering_Spec.md`, the KB Spec is the upstream authority for retrieval, indexing, and MCP-server behavior; this Master Spec section is the authoritative rendering for the build. Conflicts between the KB Spec and the Master Spec are resolved in favor of the KB Spec for engineering questions and in favor of the Master Spec for billing, plan-gating, console-firewall, retention/residency, and acceptance-criteria questions. Any divergence is logged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md`.

## 22.1 Purpose & Scope {#22.1-purpose-&-scope}

The Knowledge Base is the seller's strategic asset — an AI-indexed library that grows smarter with every evaluation. It serves two functions: (1) a private response library used by sellers to build faster, more consistent answers across bids, and (2) a source of capability evidence that sellers can publish to their Seller Profile (and downstream Marketplace Pages, §4.4.10–§4.4.16) to increase discoverability.

The KB is **always Seller-Console-scoped**. No buyer-console session — interactive or agent-driven — may read a seller KB; no buyer-side Agent capability ever calls the KB MCP server (§7.2 Dual-Console Firewall, §22.8.5 Permission Policy). Cross-Org leakage between sellers is similarly impossible: every retrieval call carries a vault-issued JWT (§22.8.3) bearing the `seller_org_id` and `allowed_namespace_ids[]`; the MCP server rejects any call whose `namespace_preference` resolves outside that allow-list.

**Audience note — Seller Maya (canonical surface persona).** Every Seller-Console surface authored or referenced in §22, §22.18, §22.19, §22.20, §23, §24, §27, §35.2, and §48.8 is designed for **Seller Maya** — the title-agnostic operator who arrives via a buyer's magic-link invitation and is expected to make the bid response work without prior Sourcera training. Maya is not a single role; the persona resolves to **Account Executive**, **Solutions Engineer**, or **Bid Manager / Proposal Manager** at a 50–500-person B2B SaaS vendor. None of these titles assume prior Sourcera experience, prior RFP-tooling experience, or familiarity with capability declarations, retrieval engineering, AIOperation metering, or match-scoring math. The Seller-Console onboarding surface (the magic-link landing, the Hero Moment, the Bid Workspace populator, the Stake-Reveal Screen — `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §4.4.2) is authored against Maya's first-30-seconds comprehension test (§3.13). The §22.20 Seller Maya Surface Abstraction sub-section is the canonical home for the engine-vs-surface compression rules that bind §22 surfaces to this persona; every §22 surface element MUST satisfy the §3.13 acid test ("Would a panicked first-timer understand this surface element in the first 30 seconds with no training?") before authoring is considered complete. The persona is engine-side identifier-free — no `persona_kind`, no `seller_role` enum, no surface render uses the literal string "Maya"; the persona is an authoring constraint, not a runtime concept.

In scope for §22:

1. The KB data model (entries, namespaces, document library, Firecrawl sources) and ingestion channels (§22.3).
2. The KB Entry Lifecycle and indexing pipeline (§22.4) — re-vectorization, BM25 reindex, namespace migration, embedding-version bumps, and failed-vectorization handling.
3. The KB Health Model (§22.5) — confidence decay, staleness states, decay-curve mathematics, and Agent suppression behavior.
4. Firecrawl ingestion configuration (§22.6) and Document Library behavior (§22.7).
5. The Sourcera KB MCP Server (§22.8) — the single authoritative retrieval surface exposed to Claude Managed Agents, including all tool contracts, vault auth, permission policy, and implementation requirements.

Out of scope for §22 (cross-referenced):

- Retrieval engineering internals (BM25 + dense + re-rank fusion) — see `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §4`.
- Managed Agent definitions (system prompts, model selection, tool-set enablement) — see `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §6` and Master Spec §21.4.
- Per-capability AIOperation settlement (cost base, value/cost price, OutcomeContract) — see Master Spec §4.8.1, §4.8.4, §21.4.5, §34.3.4, §34.11.
- KB plan gating and quantitative limits — see §34.1 Plan Tier Definitions (canonical numerical authority for the **KB Entries** / **KB Document Library** / **KB Bootstrap (Opus)** / **Firecrawl Sources** cells) and §39 Object Size Constraints (per-tier mirror rows). §5.11 Feature Access Matrix is role-keyed and is NOT a KB-quantity authority — it carries `kb_*` operation rows for RBAC only.

## 22.2 Architectural Overview {#22.2-architectural-overview}

This subsection establishes the layered architecture in which the Seller KB operates, the Anthropic Managed Agents harness that drives every KB-grounded capability, and the version-pinning discipline that keeps Sourcera's integration stable across Anthropic API revisions. The content here is reproduced from `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §2` and normalized to Master Spec heading and citation conventions; cross-links to §21.4 Capability Registry and §4.8.1 AIOperation are added throughout.

### 22.2.1 Layered Model {#22.2.1-layered-model}

The KB sits at the bottom of a four-layer stack: the Sourcera application (Next.js + Convex + Postgres + Workers) at the top, the Sourcera Agent Orchestrator in the middle, the Anthropic Managed Agents harness and the Sourcera KB MCP Server side-by-side as parallel runtime surfaces, and the underlying retrieval stores (BM25, vector, metadata) at the bottom. The orchestrator owns AIOperation ledger writes (§4.8.1) and submission gates (§22.8.5); the Managed Agents harness owns prompt caching, container execution, and event streaming; the KB MCP Server is the only path through which the agent harness reads or writes seller KB state.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Sourcera Application (Next.js + Convex + Postgres + Workers)    │
│                                                                  │
│  ┌────────────┐   ┌────────────────┐   ┌────────────────────┐    │
│  │ Seller UI  │   │  KB Authoring  │   │  Bid Workspace     │    │

│  │  - consumes SSE event stream                     │            │
│  │  - handles user.custom_tool_result               │            │
│  │  - writes AIOperation ledger entries (§4.8.1)    │            │
│  │  - enforces submission gates (§22.8.5)           │            │
```

**Key mappings (Master Spec ↔ KB Engineering Spec).** The following table establishes the canonical correspondence between Master Spec concepts and their KB-Spec engineering realization. Where a Master Spec term and a KB-Spec term refer to the same thing, the Master Spec term is the authoritative external surface and the KB-Spec term is the authoritative engineering surface.

| Master Spec concept | Engineering realization (KB Spec) |
| :---- | :---- |
| `AIOperation` (§4.8.1) | One `session` in Claude Managed Agents, captured by `session.id`. Sub-operations map to `agent.tool_use` / `agent.custom_tool_use` events tracked via `parent_operation_id`. |
| Managed Agent (§21.4.2 `requires_managed_agent`) | A Claude Managed Agents session (`POST /v1/sessions`) using a versioned `agent` definition (`agent_sourcera_{capability}_v{N}`). |
| KB Namespace (§22.3.4) | A `namespace_id` field on every `KBEntry`; supplied as a filter on every retrieval tool call. Two namespace kinds: `software` (per `SellerSoftware` per §4.4.9) and `org` (per Seller Org). |
| Hybrid retrieval (§22.4 cross-ref) | Implemented inside `kb_retrieve` (§22.8.4.1) on the MCP server. Claude does not see BM25 vs vector; it sees a ranked list. |
| `parent_operation_id` (§4.8.1) | Maps to Managed Agents `session.id`. The session log is the authoritative parent record. |
| First-Pass Responder (§21.4.2 `first_pass_responses`) | Agent definition `agent_sourcera_first_pass_responder_v{N}` bound to the KB MCP server, the Sourcera document skills, and the built-in `agent_toolset_20260401` restricted to read-only ops. |
| Capability Registry (§21.4, §4.8.2) | Each KB-driven capability is one `CapabilityRegistryEntry` row; the `requires_managed_agent` boolean and the `outcome_contract_ref` link the registry row to the agent definition and the §4.8.4 OutcomeContract. |
| AIWallet debit (§4.8.3) | Every `AIOperation` settlement against a customer-billed capability debits the seller's `AIWallet`; KB-MCP read-only tools (§22.8.5) do not themselves debit, but the parent capability does. |

### 22.2.2 Why Managed Agents, Not Agent SDK {#22.2.2-why-managed-agents-not-agent-sdk}

Per Anthropic's product comparison (`/docs/en/managed-agents/overview`), the Messages API supports "custom agent loops and fine-grained control," and Claude Managed Agents provides a "pre-built, configurable agent harness that runs in managed infrastructure" suited to "long-running tasks and asynchronous work."

Every Sourcera KB-driven capability falls into the Managed Agents profile:

| Capability | Why Managed Agents |
| :---- | :---- |
| `first_pass_responses` (§21.4.2) | Long-running, async — runs for minutes across 50–200 requirements per batch. |
| `kb_bootstrap` (§21.4.2) | Long-running, async — may crawl 500 pages and extract hundreds of entries in one operation. |
| `ghost_rfp_ingestion` (§21.4.2) | Multi-stage, stateful — chains ingestion, bootstrap, and first-pass passes. |
| `qa_suggestion` (§21.4.1 #9) | Interactive but tool-heavy (retrieve → synthesize → cite); benefits from prompt caching across requirement turns. |
| `kb_to_capability_suggestion` (§21.4.1 #18) | Bulk, async, nightly batch over the entire KB. |
| `kb_to_response_suggestion` (§21.4.1 #7) | Tool-heavy interactive; benefits from agent-side prompt-caching of system prompt + tool definitions. |
| `kb_staleness_classifier` (§21.4.1 #17) | Bulk, async, nightly batch — runs across the seller's entire active KB. |

The Claude Agent SDK is the wrong primitive because it would require Sourcera to operate the agent loop, tool-execution runtime, container sandbox, and session log — all of which Managed Agents provides with better TTFT (per Anthropic Engineering "Scaling Managed Agents": p50 −60%, p95 −90% vs. self-hosted) and built-in prompt caching.

Managed Agents features Sourcera relies on (each linked to its consumer in the KB-driven capability set):

| Managed Agents feature | Sourcera consumer |
| :---- | :---- |
| Hosted harness with built-in prompt caching and compaction | Reduces per-AIOperation cost base (§4.8.6 nightly recalc) for `first_pass_responses` by ~80% on prompt-cache hits per §21.4.2 typical-tokens column. |
| Custom tools (client-executed) | KB MCP tools (§22.8.4) are exposed via MCP, not as inline JSON-schema tools, so they re-use across agent definitions without per-agent duplication. |
| MCP servers registered at agent level with auth supplied at session creation via vaults | Supports the firewall boundary (§22.8.3): agent definition is reusable across sellers; per-session vault binds JWT to a specific `seller_org_id` and `bid_workspace_id`. |
| Skills with progressive disclosure | Domain-specific workflow knowledge (cite-before-state, compliance-framework handling, attachments) lives in Skills (`KB_Engineering_Spec.md §8`) rather than the system prompt; Sonnet/Opus only loads the Skill body when relevant. |
| Session persistence | Events persist server-side; Sourcera's orchestrator can resume after a worker crash without re-driving the agent. |
| Event streaming via SSE with span events | Token accounting (§4.8.6 cost base) reads from `agent.usage` span events; tool-use spans link to `AIOperation.parent_operation_id` for sub-operation accounting. |

### 22.2.3 Beta Header & Version Pinning {#22.2.3-beta-header-&-version-pinning}

Every request Sourcera sends to Anthropic Managed Agents carries the following two headers:

```
anthropic-version: 2023-06-01
anthropic-beta: managed-agents-2026-04-01
```

Per Anthropic docs, "the SDK sets the beta header automatically." Sourcera uses the official Anthropic Python SDK (`client.beta.*`) server-side; raw `curl` is reserved for debugging. The beta header version is pinned centrally in `packages/sourcera-agents-client` and rotated **only via a deliberate canary rollout**:

1. New beta version is added to the client package as a build-time constant and shipped behind a feature flag (`anthropic_beta_version_v2`).
2. Canary cohort (5% of seller orgs, weighted toward internal test orgs) runs for ≥ 7 days.
3. KB evaluation harness (§22.8.6 Observability) compares retrieval-recall, citation-validity, and AIOperation acceptance rates between cohorts; canary must be within 2 percentage points across all three metrics.
4. On pass, flag is rolled to 100%; on fail, flag is reverted and a Linear ticket is filed against the agent definition.
5. The prior beta version remains supported in the client for ≥ 30 days post-rollout to allow in-flight long-running sessions to complete.

A version mismatch between the client's expected `anthropic-beta` and the Anthropic-side advertised support causes the client to return HTTP 503 `anthropic_beta_version_unsupported` (new; Appendix I) and emit `agent_beta_version_mismatch` to PostHog (Appendix G). The orchestrator quarantines the affected agent definition until the operator unblocks via the Ops Console.

## 22.3 Ingestion Channels {#22.3-ingestion-channels}

**Inherited content (v6.0.0, refined v7.0.0).** The three v6 ingestion channels are preserved and refined; a fourth (Ghost-Bid Importer) is registered as an explicit channel given §21.4.2 `ghost_rfp_ingestion` and §4.4.14 GhostBidImport.

1. **Manual authoring.** Seller creates KB entries directly via the KB Editor. No Agent invocation; no AIOperation. Subject to §39 Object Size Constraints (entry body ≤ 50,000 chars; title ≤ 200 chars). Always enters at `draft`.
2. **Bid response import.** After a Workspace closes (Phase 13 per §13), responses are offered to the seller KB with bulk save or auto-save on withdrawal (per `seller_bid_import_preference` setting, default `prompt_per_workspace`). Bulk imports run as a single Managed Agents session under the `kb_to_capability_suggestion` capability per §21.4.1 #18.
3. **Automated web crawling (Firecrawl).** Sellers configure crawl sources (help centers, API docs, trust centers) with crawl depth, frequency, and content scope per §22.6. Each crawl invocation is one `AIOperation` against the `firecrawl_crawl_dedupe` capability per §21.4.1.A.
4. **Ghost-Bid Importer.** A historical-bid import flow (§4.4.14 GhostBidImport, M15) that ingests a vendor's prior RFP responses into KB entries. Each ingestion is one `AIOperation` against the `ghost_rfp_ingestion` capability per §21.4.2 (1 lifetime free per Org per Summary C.73; opus-tier; 90-day OutcomeContract window).

All entries enter at `draft` (§22.4.1) regardless of channel and pass through the Lifecycle state machine before becoming `active` and eligible for retrieval. The only exception is Firecrawl re-crawls of previously approved entries, which transition `active` → `flagged_stale` (or `review_due`) on detected source change rather than re-entering at `draft`; a new `draft` sibling is created and linked via `derived_from_kb_entry_id` so the seller can compare deltas.

| `created_at` | Timestamp | | |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | | Triggers re-vectorize per §22.4.3. |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | FK → User; nullable for system-created (Firecrawl) | |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | FK → User; nullable for system-updated | |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp, nullable | Soft delete | Excluded from retrieval; surfaced in "Trash" with 30-day reversible window. |

**Scope.** Org-scoped, Seller-Console-scoped (`console = 'seller'`); never readable from a buyer-console session. Cross-Org reads are rejected at the MCP server (§22.8.3 vault JWT enforcement).

**Required indexes.** `(org_id, namespace_id, status, deleted_at)`, `(org_id, status, last_reviewed_at)` for staleness scans, `(org_id, status, last_used_at DESC)` for activity feeds, GIN on `topic_tags` and `compliance_framework`. Vector indexes: `embedding HNSW` and `embedding_v2 HNSW` (when present); BM25 index in OpenSearch keyed by `id` with `org_id` and `namespace_id` as filters.

**Retention.** Lives for the life of the Org. Soft-deleted entries are hard-deleted 30 days after `deleted_at` per §40.2 `kb_entry_soft_deleted` row. Account-holder DSAR right-to-erasure (§6.8) is satisfied by hard delete plus vector and BM25 index purge in the same Convex transaction when the entry itself is deleted or when the subject owns the entry and the Org has no §6.8.5 retention basis. Third-party named-person mentions inside `body_markdown` follow §22.3.1.1; the Org-owned KBEntry row remains structurally intact while the subject span is redacted and indexes are refreshed.

#### 22.3.1.1 KB Entry Body Third-Party DSAR Cascade — Authored Extension AE-V72REM-PH35-DSAR-01 {#22.3.1.1-kb-entry-body-third-party-dsar-cascade}

**Scope.** This cascade applies when the verified DSAR subject is named inside a KBEntry body, document excerpt, or imported historical response but is not the owner of the Org-owned KBEntry row. It covers both non-account-holder subjects under §6.8.6.1 and Sourcera account holders who appear in another Org's KB body text.

**Redaction workflow.**

1. The DSAR cascade worker scans `body_markdown` with the §48.4.4 PII detector and NER pass for the verified subject's name, email, role snapshot, and identity-proof aliases.
2. Each verified subject span is replaced in-place with `[REDACTED_DSAR_THIRD_PARTY]`; non-subject content remains unchanged unless §6.8.5 legal-hold handling requires Ops review.
3. The row stamps `dsar_body_redaction_state = redacted`, `dsar_body_redacted_at`, `dsar_body_redacted_under_request_id`, and `dsar_body_redaction_match_count`.
4. An AuditEvent `dsar.kb_entry.third_party_body_redacted` records `kb_entry_id`, `org_id`, `namespace_id`, `dsar_request_id`, actor, match count, residency region, and re-index job ID. The event body excludes the redacted text.
5. Re-vectorization is forced under the active embedding schema. `embedding_v` / `embedding_v2` version markers are preserved or incremented according to §22.4.5 migration state; the stale vector is not queryable after redaction begins.
6. BM25 / lexical index updates are transactionally coupled to the redacted body write. If OpenSearch is unavailable, the KBEntry enters `dsar_body_redaction_state = reindex_pending`.
7. While re-vectorization or BM25 update is pending, `kb_retrieve` (§22.8.4.1) MUST exclude the entry from retrieval results, parallel to review-state exclusion. Once both indexes confirm the redacted body, the entry returns to its prior lifecycle status.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Third-party DSAR on a KB body MUST redact verified subject spans without hard-deleting Org-owned KBEntry rows unless the row is otherwise deleted by the Org. QA test `kb_third_party_dsar_redaction_cascade` asserts.
2. Vector and BM25 indexes MUST be refreshed within the §6.8.6 fulfillment SLA; stale pre-redaction vectors or lexical tokens MUST NOT be queryable after `dsar_body_redaction_state = redaction_started`. CI gate `kb_third_party_dsar_index_refresh_sla` asserts.
3. `kb_retrieve` MUST exclude entries with `dsar_body_redaction_state IN ('redaction_started', 'reindex_pending')`. Property test `kb_retrieve_excludes_pending_dsar_redactions` asserts.
4. The AuditEvent `dsar.kb_entry.third_party_body_redacted` MUST be emitted once per KBEntry / DSARRequest pair and MUST NOT include raw redacted text.
5. Re-running the same DSARRequest MUST be idempotent on `dsar_body_redacted_under_request_id`; duplicate runs cannot double-redact or increment unrelated review counters.

**Residency.** Region-pinned per §22.8.6 (US or EU per Org's `data_residency_region`); the MCP server routes per region.

### 22.3.3 KB Firecrawl Source Entity {#22.3.3-kb-firecrawl-source-entity}

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |

| `id` | UUID | Primary key | |

| `console` | Enum | Always `seller` | |
| `namespace_id` | UUID (FK) | Required; FK → KBNamespace | Crawled entries land in this namespace. |
| `root_url` | String | ≤ 500 chars; HTTPS only; valid URI | Domain ownership verified via §4.4.10 SellerOrgPage domain-verification or seller-uploaded TXT record per §22.6. |
| `crawl_depth` | Integer | 1 ≤ x ≤ 5 | |
| `frequency` | Enum | See Appendix J `kb_firecrawl_frequency`: `manual`, `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly` | Plan-gated per §22.6 limits table. |
| `content_scope` | Text | ≤ 2,000 chars | Free-text instruction passed to Firecrawl extraction prompt. |
| `auto_approval_threshold` | Float | 0.0 ≤ x ≤ 1.0; default 0.0 | Similarity threshold above which a re-crawl auto-publishes; 0.0 = always queue as draft. |
| `last_crawled_at` | Timestamp, nullable | | |
| `next_crawl_at` | Timestamp | | Computed by scheduler from `frequency` + jitter. |
| `last_crawl_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `kb_firecrawl_crawl_status`: `pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed_partial`, `failed_total`, `quota_exceeded`, `domain_unverified`, `cancelled` | Failed-partial = some pages succeeded; reported in seller dashboard. |
| `last_crawl_pages` | Integer | ≥ 0 | |
| `last_crawl_error` | String, nullable | ≤ 500 chars | Surfaced on dashboard. |
| `is_paused` | Boolean | Default false | Sellers may pause without losing config; re-enable resumes scheduler. |
| `created_at` / `updated_at` / `created_by` / `updated_by` / `deleted_at` | Standard | | |

**Scope.** Org-scoped, Seller-Console-scoped. **Index.** `(org_id, next_crawl_at, is_paused)`. **Retention.** Lives for the life of the Org; soft-deleted sources retained 30 days for restore. Crawl-history rows (separate `KBFirecrawlCrawlEvent` table; not detailed here, see Linear ticket SOU-2210) retained 90 days hot, 365 days cold per §40.2.

### 22.3.4 KB Namespace Entity {#22.3.4-kb-namespace-entity}

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Cited as `namespace_id` in MCP tool I/O (§22.8.4). |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | Required | |
| `console` | Enum | Always `seller` | |
| `kind` | Enum | See Appendix J `kb_namespace_kind`: `software`, `org` | One `org` namespace per Seller Org; one `software` namespace per `SellerSoftware` (§4.4.9). |
| `seller_software_id` | UUID (FK), nullable | FK → SellerSoftware | Required when `kind=software`; null when `kind=org`. |
| `display_name` | String | ≤ 100 chars | Denormalized from SellerSoftware.display_name when `kind=software`. |
| `is_archived` | Boolean | Default false | Set when SellerSoftware is deleted; downstream effects per §22.4.4. |
| `created_at` / `updated_at` / `created_by` / `updated_by` / `deleted_at` | Standard | | |

**Scope.** Org-scoped, Seller-Console-scoped. **Uniqueness.** `(org_id, kind=org)` ⇒ exactly one row; `(org_id, kind=software, seller_software_id)` ⇒ exactly one row.

## 22.4 KB Entry Lifecycle & Indexing Pipeline {#22.4-kb-entry-lifecycle-&-indexing-pipeline}

This subsection consolidates the v6.0.0 KB Entry Lifecycle (the seven-state staleness machine) with the v7.0.0 KB Engineering Spec §5 Indexing Pipeline (vectorization, BM25 index, namespace migration, embedding-version bumps). The lifecycle states drive both retrieval inclusion (the `exclude_review_states` filter on `kb_retrieve`, §22.8.4.1) and decay math (§22.5).

### 22.4.1 Entry Lifecycle {#22.4.1-entry-lifecycle}

The KB Entry lifecycle is a state machine; status transitions are enumerated in the table below and rendered as a state machine in Appendix L (`kb_entry_state_machine`). Status enum values are registered in Appendix J `kb_entry_status`.

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (none) | `draft` | Entry created via any ingestion channel (§22.3) | Always; default initial state | §22.4.1.A moderation preflight runs before vector / BM25 index writes. Entries with `content_moderation_state ∈ {blocked, ops_escalated}` are not indexed. |
| `draft` | `under_review` | Seller initiates "Review for publication" | None | UI surfaces a side panel with citation source and proposed body. |
| `draft` | `archived` | Seller discards | None | Soft-delete via `deleted_at`; reversible 30 days. |
| `under_review` | `active` | Seller publishes | All required fields non-null; `content_moderation_state=passed`; vector + BM25 index green per §22.4.2 | Sets `last_reviewed_at = now()`. |
| `under_review` | `draft` | Seller cancels review | None | |
| `active` | `review_due` | `now() − last_reviewed_at ≥ review_cadence_days` | Daily Convex scheduled job | Still surfaced in retrieval but with `freshness=review_due` (§22.8.4.1). |
| `active` | `flagged_stale` | Seller manually flags | None | Removes from suggestions immediately. |
| `review_due` | `active` | Seller re-confirms (no body change) OR edits and republishes | Sets `last_reviewed_at = now()` | If body edits, retriggers §22.4.3 re-index. |
| `review_due` | `review_overdue` | `now() − last_reviewed_at ≥ 2 × review_cadence_days` | Daily Convex scheduled job | Confidence further deprioritized in retrieval. |
| `review_overdue` | `active` | Seller re-confirms or edits and republishes | Same as review_due → active | |
| `review_overdue` | `flagged_stale` | `now() − last_reviewed_at ≥ 3 × review_cadence_days` OR seller manual flag | Daily Convex scheduled job | Removed from `kb_retrieve` results entirely (default `exclude_review_states` includes `flagged_stale`). |
| `flagged_stale` | `active` | Seller re-confirms or edits and republishes | Same as above | |
| `flagged_stale` | `archived` | Seller archives | None | Searchable only with `include_archived=true`. |
| any | `archived` | Seller manual archive | None | Excluded from retrieval; reversible. |
| `archived` | `active` | Seller un-archives and re-confirms | Sets `last_reviewed_at = now()` | Triggers re-index. |
| any | (hard delete) | `deleted_at + 30d` reached | Background reaper | Vector + BM25 entries purged in same Convex transaction. |

**Defaults.** `review_cadence_days = 90` per `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §0` and v6.0.0 §22.3. Sellers may set per-entry cadence (1–730 days) — ISO certificates may be 365 days; product FAQs may be 30 days.

**`last_used_at` semantics.** `last_used_at` is updated whenever an entry appears in a `kb_retrieve` `top_k` payload (§22.8.4.1), regardless of whether the agent actually cites it. Manual KB Editor "Use" actions also set `last_used_at`. Used in §22.5 decay (`usage_boost`) and in seller analytics dashboards.

**Agent-originated drafts (Reviewer-Inbox routing).** KBEntry rows created by the KB-bootstrap Managed Agent (§22.10.3) and the Ghost-RFP-ingestion Managed Agent (§22.10.6) via the `kb_entry_draft_create` MCP tool (§22.8.4.8) land in the `draft` state stamped with `created_by=<agent_id>` and `created_via ∈ {kb_bootstrap, ghost_rfp_ingestion}`. These drafts are surfaced in the Seller-console Reviewer Inbox via the Appendix C `kb_entry_pending_review` notification event — the KB-entry sibling of the §22.8.4.6 `capability_declaration_pending_review` routing used by `capability_declare_draft` for capability drafts. A seller MUST walk every agent-originated draft through `draft` → `under_review` → `active` before it becomes retrievable via `kb_retrieve` — agent-originated drafts never auto-promote, regardless of confidence score, and the retrieval pipeline (§22.9.1 Stage 2 Metadata Pre-Filter) excludes `lifecycle_state='draft'` by default. Reviewer-Inbox ordering is ascending by `confidence` so low-confidence drafts surface first. Corresponding notifications, PostHog events, and audit-ledger rows are registered in Appendix C, Appendix G, and §22.10.3 / §22.10.6 respectively.

#### 22.4.1.A KB Content Moderation Pipeline — Authored Extension AE-V72REM-PH45-KB-CONTENT-MODERATION-01 {#22.4.1.a-kb-content-moderation-pipeline}

**Scope.** Every KBEntry `title` and `body_markdown` created through manual authoring, bid-response import, Firecrawl ingestion, Ghost-Bid Importer, or Managed-Agent draft creation MUST pass content moderation before vectorization, BM25 indexing, retrieval, citation, or transition to `active`. This pipeline adapts the §48.4.4 validator set to seller-private KB content and adds KB-specific brand-impersonation / illegal-content review. It does not expose private seller KB content to Marketplace readers; it prevents unsafe or unlawful content from becoming retrievable by Managed Agents.

**Pipeline stages.**

| Stage | Applies to | Gate | Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1. Syntax and render safety | `title`, `body_markdown`, imported chunks | §48.4.4 XSS sanitizer, structured-data injection guard, Markdown sanitizer | Hard failure returns HTTP 422 `kb_entry_content_moderation_blocked`; entry remains `draft`, non-indexed. |
| 2. Privacy and prompt-injection scan | KBEntry body, Firecrawl chunks, Ghost-Bid chunks | §48.4.4 PII detector in write-time mode plus prompt-injection scanner before any LLM context assembly | `needs_review` for remediable sensitive-content / injection risk; `blocked` for malicious or unrecoverable content. |
| 3. Editorial abuse scan | Customer-authored and imported prose | Profanity / hate-speech, off-topic spam, competitive disparagement, trademark / brand impersonation, illegal-content classifier | `passed`, `needs_review`, or `blocked` with Appendix J failure reasons. |
| 4. Critical escalation | Any high-confidence illegal-content, CSAM / exploitative-content, court-order subject, or trademark cease-and-desist match | Ops content / legal queue; §27.8.13 legal-process intake when legal process is implicated | `ops_escalated`; no vector / BM25 writes; AuditEvent emitted with raw content excluded. |

**Moderation-state transitions.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `not_checked` | `passed` | Automated validator completes | All required validators pass | Entry may vectorize / BM25-index and may later publish if lifecycle conditions pass. |
| `not_checked` | `needs_review` | Automated validator soft-flags content | Remediable privacy, prompt-injection, profanity, off-topic, or brand-risk signal | Seller may edit and resubmit; Ops may review when queue policy requires. |
| `not_checked` | `blocked` | Automated validator hard-blocks content | Illegal-content, exploitative-content, severe hate / harassment, malicious prompt-injection, or unresolved impersonation | Write / publish returns `kb_entry_content_moderation_blocked`; entry is non-retrievable. |
| `not_checked`, `needs_review`, `blocked` | `ops_escalated` | Critical classifier or legal-process match fires | CSAM / exploitative-content, court-order, DMCA, trademark cease-and-desist, or regulator-order subject | Escalation follows §27.8.13 when legal process is implicated; private-KB-only cases route to Ops content queue. |
| `needs_review`, `blocked`, `ops_escalated` | `not_checked` | Seller edits moderated fields | `title` or `body_markdown` changed | Re-runs the full pipeline on the edited content. |
| `needs_review` | `passed` | Ops or authorized seller reviewer approves after remediation | AuditEvent carries reviewer and reason; no critical blocker remains | Indexing resumes after approval. |
| `ops_escalated` | `blocked` | Ops / Legal concludes content cannot be used | Legal or Trust & Safety decision recorded | Terminal until seller edits and restarts at `not_checked`. |

**Retrieval and indexing invariant.** `kb_retrieve`, `kb_get_entry`, `cite_verify`, Firecrawl auto-publish, and Managed-Agent composition MUST exclude entries unless `content_moderation_state=passed`. This invariant is stronger than the `exclude_review_states` override: `kb_staleness_classifier` may include stale entries, but no capability may retrieve `needs_review`, `blocked`, `ops_escalated`, or `not_checked` moderation states.

**Failure modes.**

1. **Moderation provider outage.** New or edited KB entries remain `not_checked`, do not vectorize, and cannot publish; a retry worker resumes when the provider recovers. Existing `passed` entries remain retrievable unless re-edited.
2. **Firecrawl chunk soft-flagged.** The chunk is inserted as `draft` with `content_moderation_state=needs_review`, excluded from auto-publish, vector, BM25, and retrieval until the seller edits or approves through the review path.
3. **Critical legal-content match on private KB content.** The entry moves to `ops_escalated`, writes an AuditEvent without raw content, and routes to Ops content / legal review. If the content is tied to a Marketplace subject or legal process, §27.8.13 owns the legal-process flow.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. KBEntry create, update, publish, Firecrawl chunk insertion, Ghost-Bid import, and `kb_entry_draft_create` MUST run the moderation pipeline before vector or BM25 writes. QA test `kb_content_moderation_pre_vectorization_gate` asserts.
2. `kb_retrieve`, `kb_get_entry`, and `cite_verify` MUST exclude every entry whose `content_moderation_state != passed`; no `exclude_review_states` override may bypass this. Property test `kb_retrieve_content_moderation_state_exclusion` asserts.
3. Publish attempts on `needs_review`, `blocked`, `ops_escalated`, or `not_checked` entries MUST fail with HTTP 422 `kb_entry_content_moderation_blocked` and include the registered failure reasons in `details.failure_reasons[]`.
4. Firecrawl auto-publish MUST require `content_moderation_state=passed` in addition to the §22.6 `auto_approval_threshold` conditions. QA test `firecrawl_auto_publish_requires_content_moderation_passed` asserts.
5. Critical moderation escalations MUST emit exactly one AuditEvent per `(kb_entry_id, content_moderation_model_version, content_hash)` and MUST NOT include raw body text. QA test `kb_moderation_escalation_audit_redacts_body` asserts.

### 22.4.2 Failed Vectorization {#22.4.2-failed-vectorization}

**Authoritative engineering content (`KB_Engineering_Spec.md §5.2`).** Per `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §5.2`: "Entry with no embeddings (failed vectorization): falls back to BM25 only; a repair job re-vectorizes nightly."

Engineering implementation:

1. Create record in `kb_entries` with `embedding IS NULL`, `embedding_failed_at = now()`, `embedding_retry_count = 0`.
2. BM25 index write proceeds **regardless** in the same Convex transaction; entry is searchable via lexical matching even with no vector.
3. `kb_retrieve` (§22.8.4.1) includes `embedding IS NULL` entries in the BM25 path only; the dense path skips them. The retrieval-metadata response field `dense_candidates` reflects only entries with embeddings.
4. Nightly repair worker re-attempts Voyage embedding with exponential backoff (delays: 1m, 5m, 30m, 4h, 24h between attempts within the same nightly window). After 5 failures (`embedding_retry_count ≥ 5`), the worker:
   - Emits PostHog event `kb_vectorization_failure_persistent` (Appendix G).
   - Notifies the seller Team Lead via the §6 Notification system (`kb_vectorization_failed` notification kind; new; Appendix C).
   - Pages on-call Sourcera engineering if the failure spans ≥ 1% of an Org's KB entries within 24 hours.

**Failure modes addressed (counterfactual pass).**

1. **Voyage API outage during create.** Resolved: BM25 index write commits regardless; entry is retrieval-eligible (lexically) the same second it is created. Repair worker recovers vector path on next Voyage availability.
2. **Vector index write succeeds but Postgres `embedding` column write fails.** Resolved: All three writes (Postgres, BM25, vector) run inside one Convex transaction; partial failure rolls all three back. The entry is then placed into `embedding IS NULL` state via the same atomic transaction's catch path; it is NEVER left in a half-indexed state.
3. **Persistent vectorization failure for entries with corrupted body content (e.g., binary blob slipped past the 50K-char text validator).** Resolved: After 5 retries, the entry is auto-transitioned to `flagged_stale` with reason `vectorization_unrecoverable` (new enum value in Appendix J `kb_entry_flag_reason`); seller is prompted to re-author. Authored extension — flagged.

### 22.4.3 Re-Indexing on Entry Edit {#22.4.3-re-indexing-on-entry-edit}

Any edit to an entry's `title`, `body_markdown`, `topic_tags`, `compliance_framework`, `customer_segment`, or `region` triggers:

1. Re-vectorize via Voyage (async; typically < 500 ms p50, ≤ 2 s p99). Old embedding remains live in the dense index until the new embedding is written, so retrieval continuity is preserved.
2. BM25 re-index via OpenSearch `_update` (typically < 100 ms p50, ≤ 500 ms p99).
3. Invalidate any **live Managed Agent sessions** with pending retrievals against this entry. Mechanism: the orchestrator maintains a per-session map of `kb_entry_id` → outstanding tool-call IDs; on edit, it emits `session.error` with `retry_status: retriable` per `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §11`. The agent's harness will re-issue `kb_retrieve` on its next turn; the response then reflects the new content.

**Idempotency.** Re-index requests are keyed by `(kb_entry_id, updated_at)`; duplicate triggers within the same transaction are coalesced. A repeated edit within 5 seconds debounces to a single re-index after the burst settles.

**Failure modes addressed.**

1. **Edit during in-flight `cite_verify` call.** The §22.8.4.7 `cite_verify` tool returns `valid=false, reason="excerpt_mismatch"` per Appendix J `cite_verify_reason`; agent must re-retrieve. The orchestrator records the event in PostHog as `kb_cite_verify_post_edit_invalidation`.
2. **Vector update succeeds, BM25 update fails.** Same atomic Convex transaction as §22.4.2; partial-failure rollback applies. If transaction commits but the BM25 mirror is later detected (within 60 s) to be out-of-date, a reconciliation worker forces an OpenSearch `_reindex` for that entry; PostHog event `kb_bm25_drift_detected`.
3. **Edit lands on entry that just transitioned to `flagged_stale` via §22.4.1 daily job.** Resolved: Edit transitions the entry back to `active` per §22.4.1 (`flagged_stale` → `active`), with `last_reviewed_at = now()`.

### 22.4.4 Namespace Migration {#22.4.4-namespace-migration}

**Trigger.** A `SellerSoftware` (§4.4.9) is deleted; its associated `software` KB namespace must be reassigned so the Org does not lose authored knowledge. Per `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §5.4` and `Sourcera_Master_Summary.md Summary §6.13.4`.

**Procedure (executed in one Convex transaction with `kb_namespace_migration` background job for long-running re-vectorization):**

1. Mark the source namespace `is_archived = true`.
2. Rewrite `namespace_id` on every affected `KBEntry` to the Org's `org` namespace (`kind=org`).
3. Set `former_software_id` on each migrated entry to the deleted `SellerSoftware.id` for provenance.
4. Apply rank penalty: multiply `confidence_modifier × 0.7` (clamped to ≥ 0.1) on every migrated entry. The penalty persists until a Seller Team Lead re-approves the entry via the KB Editor; on re-approval, the penalty is removed and `last_reviewed_at = now()`.
5. Emit audit event `kb_namespace_migration` (new; Appendix J `audit_event_action_type` extension) capturing source namespace, target namespace, entry count, and actor.
6. Emit webhook `kb.namespace.migrated` (§31, Appendix C) to the Seller Org's configured endpoints.
7. Notify the Seller Team Lead via `kb_namespace_migration_required_review` notification (new; Appendix C).
8. Re-vectorize affected entries asynchronously if their existing embedding pool is namespace-conditioned (currently Sourcera vectors are not namespace-conditioned, so re-vectorize is a no-op; reserved for future embedding versions per §22.4.5).

**Failure modes addressed.**

1. **SellerSoftware deletion races a live retrieval.** Resolved: deletion is a soft-delete on SellerSoftware that immediately marks the namespace `is_archived=true` so retrievals filter it out, before the migration commits. In-flight retrievals see no migrated entries; post-migration retrievals see them in the Org namespace.
2. **Concurrent SellerSoftware deletions on the same Org.** Resolved: per-Org pessimistic lock on `kb_namespace_migration_lock_{org_id}` for the migration job duration; serial execution.
3. **Migration crashes mid-batch.** Resolved: per-entry idempotent updates keyed by `(kb_entry_id, target_namespace_id)`; resume worker re-runs the migration from the last committed checkpoint stored in `KBNamespaceMigrationProgress` (operational table; not detailed here).

### 22.4.5 Embedding Version Bumps {#22.4.5-embedding-version-bumps}

**Trigger.** Sourcera upgrades the embedding model (e.g., voyage-3-large → voyage-4) for retrieval-quality reasons. Per `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §5.5`. Cadence: ≤ 1× per quarter; rollout never overlaps with another active embedding bump.

**Procedure.**

1. Stand up parallel vector column `embedding_v2` (Postgres column add, online). Existing `embedding` is unchanged.
2. Backfill in a worker over 72 hours, rate-limited to ≤ 50% of Voyage API quota to avoid customer-impact on live retrievals.
3. `kb_retrieve` (§22.8.4.1) runs dense against `embedding_v2` for Orgs where `embedding_v2_coverage ≥ 99%`; otherwise falls back to `embedding`. Coverage is measured per Org per (`SELECT COUNT(*) WHERE org_id=? AND status='active' AND embedding_v2 IS NOT NULL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) WHERE org_id=? AND status='active'`).
4. Once **all** Orgs reach ≥ 99% coverage AND the eval harness (§22.8.6) confirms parity (recall@10 within 1 percentage point) for ≥ 7 days, drop the v1 column with a 30-day retention window in case of rollback.
5. Roll back to `embedding` if the eval harness detects regression: column drop is canceled; `kb_retrieve` reverts to v1 dense path globally within 5 minutes via the orchestrator feature flag `embedding_path_v2`.

**Failure modes addressed.**

1. **Voyage v2 returns vectors of different dimensionality than v1.** Resolved: `embedding_v2` schema is declared with the new dimensionality at column add; v1 retains its dimensionality; HNSW indices are independent.
2. **Backfill exhausts Voyage quota mid-rollout.** Resolved: rate-limit holds the backfill below 50% of quota; live retrievals on entries with `embedding_v2 IS NULL` fall back to v1 path automatically. Backfill resumes the next minute.
3. **Org tips below 99% coverage mid-day** (e.g., a 10K-entry KB import lands while in the 99%-tier band). Resolved: coverage is recomputed every 60 seconds per Org; the dense-path selector reads it via per-Org cached flag with 60s TTL. Single dropped retrievals tolerate the 60s lag.

No agent downtime; no customer-visible change; AIOperation cost-base impact (potential `low` drift severity per §4.8.6) is recalculated nightly.

## 22.5 KB Health Model {#22.5-kb-health-model}

Every KB entry carries a stored `confidence_score` (acceptance-rate scalar, 0.0–1.0), a stored `win_rate_weight` (closed-bid outcome scalar, 0.0–1.0), and a derived `confidence_modifier` (retrieval multiplier, 0.1–1.5 after clamping). The decay job runs daily as a Convex scheduled function (`kb_confidence_decay_daily`) at 04:00 UTC per Org region (US: 04:00 UTC; EU: 04:00 CET). The decay output drives both the `freshness` field returned by `kb_retrieve` (§22.8.4.1) and the per-entry sort order in retrieval re-ranking (`KB_Engineering_Spec.md §4`).

### 22.5.1 Decay Curve {#22.5.1-decay-curve}

```
confidence_modifier = clamp(
    confidence_score
    × (1 − (days_since_review / (review_cadence_days × 2)))
    × usage_boost
    × win_rate_modifier,
    min = 0.1,
    max = 1.5
)

where
  days_since_review     = (now − last_reviewed_at).days
  usage_boost           = clamp(1.0 + 0.1 × recent_usage_count, max = 1.5)
  recent_usage_count    = count of kb_retrieve hits over last 30 days
  win_rate_modifier     = clamp(0.5 + 0.5 × win_rate_weight, min = 0.5, max = 1.0)
```

**Boundary behavior.**

- `days_since_review = 0` → linear factor `1.0` → modifier = `confidence_score × usage_boost × win_rate_modifier` (capped at 1.5).
- `days_since_review = review_cadence_days` (entry just transitioned to `review_due`) → linear factor `0.5` → modifier halved.
- `days_since_review = 2 × review_cadence_days` (entry just transitioned to `review_overdue`) → linear factor `0.0` → modifier = max(0.1, raw).
- `days_since_review > 2 × review_cadence_days` → linear factor clamped to 0; modifier sticks at 0.1 minimum.
- `usage_boost` caps at 1.5 to prevent runaway boosting on highly trafficked entries.
- `win_rate_weight` defaults to 0.5 until the entry has ≥ 5 closed-bid citations; below that floor, `win_rate_modifier` defaults to 0.75 rather than overfitting on small samples. Once the floor is met, `win_rate_weight` updates only from closed-bid outcomes per §22.18.3.3.

### 22.5.2 Agent Behavior on Staleness {#22.5.2-agent-behavior-on-staleness}

- `kb_retrieve` (§22.8.4.1) defaults `exclude_review_states = ["review_overdue", "flagged_stale"]`. Agents may pass `exclude_review_states=[]` to override (only `kb_staleness_classifier` capability does this in seed) — but the override is logged in the orchestrator's audit ledger as `agent_kb_stale_override`.
- Entries returned with `freshness=review_due` carry a 0.5–1.0 confidence band and are rendered with a "Stale — review by [date]" badge in any UI surface that displays the citation.
- Entries with `win_rate_weight < 0.40` after the ≥ 5 closed-bid-citation floor are penalized through the canonical `win_rate_modifier`; they remain retrievable but de-ranked.
- Entries aged > 365 days without review trigger an in-Editor warning: "This entry hasn't been reviewed in [N] days. Consider updating before using." The warning is informational and does not block retrieval.
- The `kb_staleness_classifier` capability (§21.4.1 #17) runs nightly across the Seller Org's KB and writes proposed actions (re-verify, archive, version-bump) to a Seller Team Lead inbox; per §21.4.5 the OutcomeContract accepts on action within 14d and rejects on no-action within 30d.

### 22.5.3 Health Dashboard Contract {#22.5.3-health-dashboard-contract}

The KB Health Dashboard groups entries by status and surfaces:

- Count of entries in each status (`active`, `review_due`, `review_overdue`, `flagged_stale`, `archived`).
- Top 10 entries by `recent_usage_count` (high-leverage entries — staleness here is high-cost).
- Top 10 entries by lowest `win_rate_weight` after the ≥ 5 closed-bid-citation floor (poor performers — candidate for rewrite or archive).
- Distribution of `confidence_modifier` across the active set (histogram with 10 bins).
- Last decay-job run timestamp; alert if > 26 hours stale.

Plan-gated per §5.11: Free plan sees status counts only; paid tiers see usage and dismiss rankings; Enterprise sees the histogram and Team Lead inbox routing.

## 22.6 Firecrawl Integration {#22.6-firecrawl-integration}

Sellers configure Firecrawl sources (up to plan limits) per §22.3.3 with the fields detailed in that subsection. Crawled pages flow through:

1. **Domain ownership verification.** Crawl source is rejected at registration unless the seller's Org has verified ownership of `root_url`'s eTLD+1 via either (a) a verified `SellerOrgPage` (§4.4.10) on the same domain, or (b) a TXT record `_sourcera-firecrawl-verify=<token>` on the same domain. Unverified sources never crawl; status `domain_unverified` is surfaced on the dashboard.
2. **Chunking.** Pages are chunked into KB-entry-sized segments (≤ 2,000 chars per chunk), prioritizing semantic boundaries (paragraph and heading splits) before falling back to character splits.
3. **Deduplication.** Each chunk is compared against existing KB entries in the same `namespace_id` using semantic similarity (Haiku-tier classification per §21.4.1.A `firecrawl_crawl_dedupe`); ≥ 85% match flags as a likely duplicate. Duplicates either (a) skip ingestion entirely, (b) replace the existing entry as a new draft sibling linked via `derived_from_kb_entry_id`, or (c) merge per seller preference (`firecrawl_dedupe_action`, default `skip`).
4. **Draft queue.** Surviving chunks are inserted as `draft` entries via the standard ingestion path (§22.3.1) and the §22.4.1.A moderation preflight. Chunks may auto-publish with `last_reviewed_at = now()` if (and only if) the seller has set `auto_approval_threshold > 0`, the chunk's similarity to an already-active entry is ≥ threshold, and `content_moderation_state=passed`. Soft-flagged or blocked chunks remain non-indexed drafts until remediated.
5. **Re-crawl change detection.** On a subsequent crawl, the agent compares the freshly chunked content against the previously crawled chunks; changed chunks flag the affected `active` KB entries with status `flagged_stale` and reason `source_content_changed` (Appendix J `kb_entry_flag_reason`). A new `draft` is created and linked via `derived_from_kb_entry_id`.

**Plan limits.** Firecrawl source counts and re-crawl cadence are authoritative in §34.1.2 cell **Firecrawl Sources** (Seller plan tiers); per-crawl page caps are operational throughput controls and live in this subsection. Source-count and cadence values MUST be sourced from §34.1.2 — never restated.

| Plan tier (per §34.1.2) | Crawl Sources | Re-crawl Cadence | Max Pages Per Crawl |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
