| Free | 0 (per §34.1.2) | n/a | n/a |
| Starter | 2 (weekly per §34.1.2) | Weekly | 100 |
| Growth | 10 (daily per §34.1.2) | Daily | 1,000 |
| Scale | Unlimited (real-time, fair-use ≤ 50 domains per §34.1.2) | Real-time | 10,000 |
| Enterprise | Unlimited (per §34.1.2) | Real-time | 10,000 |

**AIOperation accounting.** Each crawl invocation produces one `AIOperation` row against `firecrawl_crawl_dedupe` per §21.4.1.A. The `accepted` signal per §21.4.5 is "new KB entry approved OR correct dedupe (no duplicate emitted)"; the `rejected` signal is "false-positive dedupe (user authors duplicate within 7d)". Window 7d, auto-accept after 24h.

**Failure modes addressed.**

1. **Crawl source goes offline mid-crawl.** `last_crawl_status = failed_partial`; partial chunks are inserted as `draft`; seller is notified with the page count succeeded vs. attempted.
2. **Domain becomes unverified post-registration** (e.g., seller deletes verifying TXT record). Resolved: nightly verifier job revalidates each source's domain; on failure, `is_paused = true`; dashboard surfaces `domain_unverified`; no crawls until re-verified.
3. **Crawl produces > plan max-pages.** Resolved: crawl is truncated at the plan limit; remaining pages flagged for the next crawl; seller dashboard surfaces "X pages skipped due to plan limit"; upgrade CTA.

## 22.7 Document Library {#22.7-document-library}

A centralized repository for compliance and corporate documents that apply across many bids. Document fields are defined in §22.3.2; behavior:

- Documents carry expiration dates and version chains (`prior_version_doc_id`, `superseded_by_doc_id`). When a new version is uploaded:
  - Its `prior_version_doc_id` points at the predecessor; the predecessor's `superseded_by_doc_id` is set; the predecessor transitions to `superseded`.
  - Every active bid referencing the old version is flagged for update; the Bid Owner receives a `document_version_superseded` notification (Appendix C).
- The Agent (via `document_library_find` and `doc_attach`, §22.8.4.3 / §22.8.4.4) auto-resolves matching documents and proposes attachment to bid responses. The seller may configure `auto_attach_policy` per Bid Workspace (`always`, `propose`, `never`; default `propose`).
- Expired documents (`status=expired`, computed daily from `expires_at`) render with a red "Expired" badge and are excluded from `document_library_find` results unless `require_unexpired=false` is explicitly passed.

**Plan limits.** KB Document Library document counts are authoritative in §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 cell **KB Document Library**. This subsection does NOT restate the per-tier values; consumers MUST reference §34.1 for the canonical Free / Starter / Growth / Scale / Enterprise document caps.

**Failure modes addressed.**

1. **Doc uploaded with `expires_at` in the past.** Resolved: registration accepts the upload but immediately transitions to `expired`; seller is warned in the upload UX.
2. **Bid owner receives `document_version_superseded` after the bid was already submitted.** Resolved: the notification's CTA is "Notify buyer of doc update" rather than "Re-attach"; submission is immutable per §23.3 (a new submission would be a separate bid revision).
3. **Active bid references a doc whose `attach_ref` was rotated due to file replacement.** Resolved: `attach_ref` rotation generates a new value; in-flight `doc_attach` calls in agent sessions present a stale `attach_ref` and receive `{"error":{"type":"stale_attach_ref",...}}` from the MCP server; the agent re-resolves via `document_library_find`.

## 22.8 The Sourcera KB MCP Server {#22.8-the-sourcera-kb-mcp-server}

The KB is a first-class Sourcera service exposed to Claude Managed Agents over MCP (Model Context Protocol). This is the **single authoritative entry point** for every agent-driven KB interaction. The content of §22.8 is reproduced from `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §3` in full and normalized to Master Spec authoring conventions.

### 22.8.1 Why MCP {#22.8.1-why-mcp}

Per Anthropic's MCP connector docs (`/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector`):

> "Claude Managed Agents connects to remote MCP servers that expose an HTTP endpoint. The server must support the MCP protocol's streamable HTTP transport."
>
> "MCP configuration is split across two steps: Agent creation declares which MCP servers the agent connects to, by name and URL. Session creation supplies auth for those servers by referencing a pre-registered vault. This separation keeps secrets out of reusable agent definitions while letting each session authenticate with its own credentials."

This is a fit for Sourcera because:

1. **Credential isolation.** Each bid workspace session gets a scoped vault credential (`bid_workspace_token`) that the MCP server validates. Tokens are per-session, short-lived (1 hour TTL), and never seen by the agent harness — Anthropic's MCP proxy fetches from the vault and forwards only on tool calls. See §22.8.3 and the new entity §22.8.3.1 MCPSessionTokenRecord.
2. **Firewall enforcement at the retrieval boundary.** Every MCP tool call carries a signed bearer token identifying the `seller_org_id`, `bid_workspace_id`, and `namespace_scope` (allowed namespaces: Software-level + Org-level for **this seller only**). The MCP server rejects any call that tries to cross the firewall (HTTP 403 `firewall_violation`; new error code, Appendix I).
3. **Reuse across agent types.** First-Pass, Ghost-Bid, KB-to-Capability Suggestion, and Q&A Suggestion all use the same MCP server with different tool subsets enabled via `mcp_toolset` configuration.
4. **Stable contract, swappable implementation.** The KB store can be switched from pgvector → Turbopuffer → Pinecone → OpenSearch-only without changing agent definitions.

### 22.8.2 Registration on the Agent {#22.8.2-registration-on-the-agent}

The KB MCP server is registered at agent definition time per the JSON shape below. Agent definitions live in `packages/sourcera-agent-definitions/`; deployment to Anthropic is via `client.beta.agents.create` / `.update` per `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §6.1`.

```json
{
  "mcp_servers": [
    {
      "type": "url",
      "name": "sourcera_kb",
      "url": "https://mcp.sourcera.com/kb/v1"
    }
  ],
  "tools": [
    { "type": "agent_toolset_20260401",
      "default_config": { "enabled": false },
      "configs": [
        { "name": "read", "enabled": true },
        { "name": "grep", "enabled": true },
        { "name": "glob", "enabled": true }
      ]
    },
    { "type": "mcp_toolset", "mcp_server_name": "sourcera_kb" }
  ]
}
```

**Rationale.** The First-Pass Responder needs `read`, `grep`, and `glob` for reading the scratch filesystem (where the agent serializes its in-progress outputs), but no `bash`, `edit`, `write`, `web_fetch`, or `web_search`. Minimal tool surface minimizes drift. Per-capability tool subsets are enumerated in `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §6.2–§6.10`.

**Versioning.** The MCP server URL embeds a `/v1` path segment. New tool contracts that break backward compatibility ship as `/v2` while `/v1` remains live for ≥ 90 days. Agent definitions are pinned to a specific URL version, and an Agent Definition update is required to migrate. Cross-version migrations follow the canary procedure in §22.2.3.

### 22.8.3 Vault Auth at Session Creation {#22.8.3-vault-auth-at-session-creation}

```
POST /v1/sessions
{
  "agent": "agent_sourcera_first_pass_responder_v17",
  "environment_id": "env_sourcera_kb_runner_v3",
  "vault_ids": ["vault_bid_ws_01HXYZ..."]
}
```

The vault holds a one-time-use JWT signed by Sourcera's identity service. The JWT encodes:

- `seller_org_id`
- `bid_workspace_id` (nullable for org-scope-only operations)
- `allowed_namespace_ids[]` (Software-level KBs the bid may read, plus the Org-level KB)
- `capability_scope[]` (e.g., `["kb_retrieve", "kb_get_entry", "document_library_find"]`)
- `data_residency_region` (e.g., `us`, `eu`)
- `parent_capability_id` (the §4.8.2 CapabilityRegistryEntry that drove the session creation; used by the MCP server to record per-tool spans against the parent AIOperation)
- `parent_aioperation_id` (the §4.8.1 AIOperation that owns this session; used for cross-tool sub-operation accounting)
- `iat`, `exp` (1 hour from issue), `jti` (one-time-use enforcement key; persisted by the MCP server in the §22.8.3.1 token record store).

The MCP server validates this JWT on every call via Sourcera's JWKS published at `mcp.sourcera.com/.well-known/jwks.json`. Per Anthropic's docs, "If the authorization credentials supplied in the vault are invalid, session creation will succeed and interaction is still possible. A `session.error` event is emitted describing the MCP auth failure." Sourcera's orchestrator handles `session.error` per `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §11`: the session is force-closed, an `AIOperation` is written with `settlement_state = rejected` and `failure_reason = mcp_auth_failure`, and the seller is notified with `kb_mcp_auth_failure` (new; Appendix C).

#### 22.8.3.1 MCPSessionTokenRecord (Org-Scoped, Seller-Only, Append-Only) {#22.8.3.1-mcpsessiontokenrecord}

**Authoring intent.** The MCP server must enforce one-time-use semantics on JWTs (`jti`) to prevent token replay even within the JWT's 1h `exp` window, must persist the per-session `parent_aioperation_id` linkage so per-tool spans roll up correctly into the parent §4.8.1 AIOperation, and must support fast revocation in incident-response scenarios (e.g., a compromised vault). Authored extension — flagged in RECONCILIATION.md.

**Scope.** Org-scoped (seller); Seller-Console-scoped (`console = 'seller'`); append-only (no field updates after `revoked_at` is stamped). Soft-delete forbidden; record is a security audit artifact and persists per the retention rule below.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | Required; FK → Org | Seller Org. |
| `console` | Enum | Always `seller` | See Appendix J `kb_console`. |
| `jti` | String | 32 chars; unique within `(org_id, jti)`; enforced via unique index | One-time-use enforcement key; populated from the JWT `jti` claim. |
| `bid_workspace_id` | UUID (FK), nullable | FK → BidWorkspace (§23.1) | Null for org-scope-only sessions (e.g., `kb_to_capability_suggestion` nightly batch). |
| `parent_capability_id` | String | See Appendix J `capability_id` (registry-defined values per §21.4) | The capability that drove the session. |
| `parent_aioperation_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → AIOperation (§4.8.1) | The owning AIOperation row; per-tool spans roll up here. |
| `allowed_namespace_ids` | Array\[UUID\] | FK → KBNamespace (§22.3.4) | Snapshot of the JWT's `allowed_namespace_ids[]`. |
| `capability_scope` | Array\[Enum\] | See Appendix J `mcp_tool_name` | Tools this session may invoke. |
| `data_residency_region` | Enum | See Appendix J `data_residency_region` | Snapshot of JWT claim. |
| `issued_at` | Timestamp | | JWT `iat`. |
| `expires_at` | Timestamp | | JWT `exp`. |
| `first_used_at` | Timestamp, nullable | | Stamped on first MCP call; subsequent calls succeed because `jti` is now associated with this session, not because it remains "unused". One-time-use means "may be redeemed by exactly one MCP-server-bound session." |
| `revoked_at` | Timestamp, nullable | | Set when the orchestrator force-revokes (e.g., session crashed, vault compromise). Subsequent calls return `{"error":{"type":"stale_token",...}}` per §22.8.6. |
| `revoked_reason` | Enum, nullable | See Appendix J `mcp_session_revocation_reason`: `expired`, `org_revoked`, `vault_compromised`, `bid_workspace_closed`, `firewall_violation`, `agent_session_crashed` | Drives downstream auditing. |
| `tool_call_count` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Updated atomically on each MCP call. |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | | Equal to `issued_at` at creation; immutable. |

**Required indexes.** Unique `(org_id, jti)`; `(org_id, parent_aioperation_id)` for sub-operation rollup; `(org_id, expires_at, revoked_at)` for expiry sweeps.

**Retention.** 13 months hot, then archive to cold storage for SOC-2 audit; hard-deleted at 7 years per §40.2 (new row: `mcp_session_token_record`). DSAR right-to-erasure (§6.8): `seller_org_id` and `bid_workspace_id` PII linkage redacted on erasure; the security-audit fields (`jti`, `parent_aioperation_id`, `revoked_reason`) are retained for SOC-2 compliance.

**Residency.** Region-pinned per `data_residency_region`; the MCP server in each region operates on its region-local token store; cross-region tokens are not permitted (a US-issued token presented to the EU MCP server returns HTTP 403 `wrong_region`).

### 22.8.4 Tools Exposed by the MCP Server {#22.8.4-tools-exposed-by-the-mcp-server}

Each tool is versioned via the URL path (`/kb/v1/*`, `/kb/v2/*`) so contracts can evolve without breaking deployed agent versions. All nine tools are registered in Appendix J `mcp_tool_name`. Every tool call:

- Authenticates via the JWT bearer (§22.8.3); rejects on missing or invalid token with HTTP 401 `mcp_auth_required` or HTTP 403 `mcp_auth_invalid` (Appendix I).
- Records a per-tool span linked to the session's `parent_aioperation_id` (§22.8.3.1); span fields include tool name, input hash, output size, latency, and confidence scores where applicable.
- Counts toward the per-tool rate limit (§22.8.6).
- Does **not** itself debit the AIWallet — the parent AIOperation does. MCP-tool sub-operation accounting is for cost-base (§4.8.6) recalculation only.

The cross-link between MCP tools and AIOperation settlement is summarized in the table below; see §21.4.5 for full OutcomeContract definitions.

| MCP tool | Parent capability(ies) | AIOperation settlement linkage |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `kb_retrieve` | `first_pass_responses`, `qa_suggestion`, `kb_to_response_suggestion`, `kb_bootstrap`, `ghost_rfp_ingestion`, `kb_to_capability_suggestion`, `kb_staleness_classifier` | Sub-operation; aggregated into parent AIOperation cost base via per-tool spans. Parent settlement signal is the parent capability's per §21.4.5 OutcomeContract. |
| `kb_get_entry` | Same as `kb_retrieve` | Sub-operation; same accounting. |
| `document_library_find` | `first_pass_responses`, `qa_suggestion`, `document_attach_suggest` | Sub-operation; `document_attach_suggest` settles per §21.4.5 (`accepted=document attached from suggestion`, `rejected=suggestion dismissed`, window 24h, auto-accept 1h). |
| `doc_attach` | `document_attach_suggest`, `first_pass_responses` (when applicable) | Side-effectful; success is a precursor signal contributing to the parent capability's `accepted` signal per §21.4.5. |
| `capability_find` | `kb_to_capability_suggestion`, `capability_declaration_suggest` | Sub-operation; `capability_declaration_suggest` settles per §21.4.5 (`accepted=Capability Declaration published from suggestion`, window 7d). |
| `capability_declare_draft` | `kb_to_capability_suggestion`, `capability_declaration_suggest` | Side-effectful (writes a draft Capability Declaration in `pending_review` state). The drafted Capability Declaration's transition to `published` constitutes the `accepted` signal per §21.4.5. |
| `kb_entry_draft_create` | `kb_bootstrap`, `ghost_rfp_ingestion` | Side-effectful; writes a KBEntry row in `draft` state (§22.4.1 initial state) stamped with `created_via ∈ {kb_bootstrap, ghost_rfp_ingestion}`. The seller-walked transition `draft` → `under_review` → `active` is the `accepted` signal per §21.4.5 for the parent bootstrap/ingestion capability. |
| `kb_dedupe_check` | `kb_bootstrap`, `ghost_rfp_ingestion` | Sub-operation; read-only similarity probe used by bootstrap/ingestion agents before calling `kb_entry_draft_create`. Aggregated into parent AIOperation cost base via per-tool spans; never settles independently. |
| `cite_verify` | All RAG-grounded capabilities (every capability that emits seller-facing text) | Sub-operation; gating — server-side verification per §22.8.5 also runs as a settlement gate. |

#### 22.8.4.1 `kb_retrieve` {#22.8.4.1-kb_retrieve}

Primary hybrid retrieval entry point. Used by First-Pass, Q&A Suggestion, KB-to-Response Suggestion, and the Ingestion family.

**Input schema:**

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "query": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The requirement text or sub-question to retrieve evidence for. Should be the rewritten, expanded query, not the original raw requirement. Length bounds are canonical in §39 row mcp_kb_retrieve_query.",
      "minLength": 1,
      "maxLength": 2000
    },
    "namespace_preference": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": { "type": "string" },
      "description": "Ordered list of namespace IDs. First is highest priority. Typically [software_kb_id, org_kb_id]. The server clamps to the allowed_namespace_ids from the vault JWT. Length bounds are canonical in §39 row mcp_kb_retrieve_namespace_preference_length.",
      "minItems": 1,
      "maxItems": 10
    },
    "filters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "compliance_framework": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string", "enum": ["soc2", "iso27001", "hipaa", "gdpr", "pci"] } },
        "region": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } },
        "kind": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string", "enum": ["qa", "fact", "policy", "evidence", "boilerplate"] } },
        "customer_segment": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string", "enum": ["smb", "midmarket", "enterprise"] } },
        "language": { "type": "string" },
        "exclude_review_states": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": { "type": "string", "enum": ["review_overdue", "flagged_stale"] },
          "default": ["review_overdue", "flagged_stale"]
        }
      }
    },
    "top_k": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 10, "default": 5 },
    "max_excerpt_chars": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 200, "maximum": 1000, "default": 400 }
  },
  "required": ["query", "namespace_preference"]
}
```

**Description** (what Claude sees — enforces the Anthropic tool-design principle of "aim for at least 3-4 sentences"):

> "Search the seller's Knowledge Base for entries relevant to a specific requirement or question. Call this whenever you need evidence to support a draft response or capability claim; call it once per distinct sub-question rather than combining unrelated questions into one query. The query field should be the rewritten, expanded version of the requirement — include synonyms, domain terms, and compliance frameworks when relevant. Always pass the Software-specific namespace first in `namespace_preference` so product-specific entries outrank org-level entries. Results are returned ranked by relevance; each carries a `kb_entry_id` you must cite verbatim in your response. Do NOT paraphrase excerpts into claims that go beyond what the excerpt supports."

**Output schema:**

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "hits": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "kb_entry_id": { "type": "string" },
          "namespace_id": { "type": "string" },
          "namespace_kind": { "type": "string", "enum": ["software", "org"] },
          "kind": { "type": "string" },
          "title": { "type": "string" },
          "excerpt": { "type": "string", "description": "Up to max_excerpt_chars of the entry text, with the most relevant passage highlighted." },
          "excerpt_offsets": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "integer" }, "description": "[start, end] character offsets of excerpt within the entry body, for downstream cite_verify." },
          "confidence": { "type": "number", "description": "0.0–1.0 retrieval + re-rank fused confidence." },
          "freshness": { "type": "string", "enum": ["fresh", "review_due"], "description": "review_overdue and flagged_stale are excluded from results unless exclude_review_states is overridden." },
          "win_rate": { "type": "number", "description": "Historical acceptance rate of this entry when previously surfaced." },
          "evidence_refs": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" }, "description": "Linked Document Library entry IDs (e.g., SOC2 report). Call document_library_find to retrieve metadata." }
        }
      }
    },
    "total_matches": { "type": "integer" },
    "retrieval_metadata": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "bm25_candidates": { "type": "integer" },
        "dense_candidates": { "type": "integer" },
        "reranker_used": { "type": "string" },
        "elapsed_ms": { "type": "integer" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**Concrete example (request).**

```json
POST https://mcp.sourcera.com/kb/v1/tools/kb_retrieve
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs...
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "query": "How does the platform encrypt data at rest, including key management and rotation cadence (AES-256 expected, FIPS 140-2)?",
  "namespace_preference": ["ns_software_acme_widget", "ns_org_acme"],
  "filters": {
    "compliance_framework": ["soc2", "iso27001"],
    "kind": ["fact", "policy", "evidence"]
  },
  "top_k": 3,
  "max_excerpt_chars": 500
}
```

**Concrete example (response).**

```json
{
  "hits": [
    {
      "kb_entry_id": "kbe_01HXY2ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVW",
      "namespace_id": "ns_software_acme_widget",
      "namespace_kind": "software",
      "kind": "policy",
      "title": "Data Encryption — At Rest",
      "excerpt": "All customer data is encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM. Master keys are managed in AWS KMS with FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSMs and rotated annually...",
      "excerpt_offsets": [0, 487],
      "confidence": 0.93,
      "freshness": "fresh",
      "win_rate": 0.78,
      "evidence_refs": ["doc_01HXSOC2REPORT2026..."]
    }
  ],
  "total_matches": 4,
  "retrieval_metadata": {
    "bm25_candidates": 12,
    "dense_candidates": 18,
    "reranker_used": "voyage-rerank-2",
    "elapsed_ms": 187
  }
}
```

**Response-shaping discipline** (per Anthropic "Design tool responses to return only high-signal information"):

- Full entry body is **never** returned from `kb_retrieve`. Only excerpts. If the agent needs the full body, it calls `kb_get_entry` (§22.8.4.2).
- No internal database IDs beyond the stable `kb_entry_id`.
- No author, reviewer, or timestamp fields (not relevant to drafting; available via `kb_get_entry` if needed).
- `retrieval_metadata` is for server-side telemetry; Claude does not reason on it.

**Error envelope** (per §22.8.6):

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limit_exceeded | invalid_namespace | stale_token | not_found | firewall_violation | wrong_region",
    "message": "Human-readable description.",
    "retry_after_ms": 0
  }
}
```

**Per-tool rate limit:** 60 rps per session.

#### 22.8.4.2 `kb_get_entry` {#22.8.4.2-kb_get_entry}

Fetch full text for a specific entry when the excerpt returned by `kb_retrieve` is insufficient.

**Input schema:**

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "kb_entry_id": { "type": "string" }
  },
  "required": ["kb_entry_id"]
}
```

**Description (what Claude sees):**

> "Retrieve the full body of a Knowledge Base entry by ID. Use this sparingly — prefer the excerpts returned by kb_retrieve. Call this only when the excerpt is truncated at a critical point or when the entry is referenced across multiple requirements and you need the full context. Returns the entry body, metadata, and any Document Library evidence attached."

**Output schema:**

```json
{
  "kb_entry_id": "...",
  "body_markdown": "...",
  "metadata": {
    "topic_tags": ["..."],
    "compliance_framework": ["..."],
    "customer_segment": ["..."],
    "language": "en"
  },
  "references": [
    { "doc_id": "...", "title": "...", "expiration": "2026-12-31" }
  ],
  "review_state": "fresh",
  "last_reviewed_at": "2026-03-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

**Concrete example (request/response).**

```json
POST /kb/v1/tools/kb_get_entry
{ "kb_entry_id": "kbe_01HXY2ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVW" }

200 OK
{
  "kb_entry_id": "kbe_01HXY2ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVW",
  "body_markdown": "## Data Encryption — At Rest\n\nAll customer data is encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM...",
  "metadata": {
    "topic_tags": ["encryption", "data-at-rest", "kms"],
    "compliance_framework": ["soc2", "iso27001"],
    "customer_segment": ["midmarket", "enterprise"],
    "language": "en"
  },
  "references": [
    { "doc_id": "doc_01HXSOC2REPORT2026", "title": "SOC 2 Type II Report — 2026", "expiration": "2027-01-15" }
  ],
  "review_state": "fresh",
  "last_reviewed_at": "2026-03-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

**Errors.** `not_found` if `kb_entry_id` does not exist or is in a namespace outside `allowed_namespace_ids[]`; `firewall_violation` if cross-Org access attempted (defense-in-depth — should already be caught at JWT validation).

**Per-tool rate limit:** 30 rps per session.

#### 22.8.4.3 `document_library_find` {#22.8.4.3-document_library_find}

Resolve Document Library evidence — compliance docs, certificates, DPAs.

**Input schema:**

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "query": { "type": "string", "description": "A phrase describing the evidence needed, e.g., 'latest SOC 2 Type II report'.", "maxLength": 500 },
    "compliance_framework": { "type": "string", "enum": ["soc2", "iso27001", "hipaa", "gdpr", "pci"] },
    "require_unexpired": { "type": "boolean", "default": true }
  },
  "required": ["query"]
}
```

**Description:**

> "Find the seller's Document Library entries (compliance certificates, DPAs, penetration test reports) matching a request. Pass a clear query like 'latest SOC 2 Type II'. The matching entry's file URL is intentionally never returned to you — instead, you receive an `attach_ref` token that you may pass to `doc_attach` to attach the document to a specific bid response slot. Set `require_unexpired=false` only if you specifically need to see expired evidence."

**Output schema:**

```json
{
  "matches": [
    {
      "doc_id": "...",
      "title": "SOC 2 Type II Report — 2026",
      "framework": "soc2",
      "issued_at": "2026-01-15",
      "expires_at": "2027-01-15",
      "file_url": null,
      "attach_ref": "doc_ref_01HXYZ..."
    }
  ]
}
```

**Note:** `file_url` is intentionally **null** in tool output to the agent. The `attach_ref` is a server-minted, time-limited (30-minute TTL) handle the agent passes back to `doc_attach` — the file itself is attached to the response by Sourcera's application, not by the agent writing URLs into response text. This prevents URL leakage and enables seller-side audit of every attach.

**Per-tool rate limit:** 10 rps per session.

#### 22.8.4.4 `doc_attach` {#22.8.4.4-doc_attach}

Attach a Document Library entry to a specific bid response slot.

**Input schema:**

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "response_slot_id": { "type": "string", "description": "Bid response slot identifier the agent received in its initial context." },
    "attach_ref": { "type": "string", "description": "Token returned by document_library_find. 30-minute TTL." }
  },
  "required": ["response_slot_id", "attach_ref"]
}
```

**Output schema:**

```json
{
  "status": "attached",
  "attachment_id": "att_01HX..."
}
```

**Side effects.** This tool has side effects in Sourcera's seller and (downstream) Buyer Console: the buyer ultimately sees the attached doc once the bid is submitted (§23.3 governs submission). The MCP server validates via the vault JWT that:

1. The session is authorized to act on this `bid_workspace_id` (per JWT claim).
2. The `response_slot_id` belongs to a bid workspace whose `seller_org_id` matches the JWT.
3. The `attach_ref` is unexpired (30-minute TTL) and was minted for this session's `seller_org_id` and the same `doc_id` is still `active` (not `expired` or `superseded`).

On success, the MCP server emits `kb.document.attached` (new webhook event; §31, Appendix C, Appendix G) with HMAC-SHA256 signing, idempotency via `event_id`, exponential backoff retry, DLQ after 5 failures, payload ≤ 256KB.

**Errors.** `stale_attach_ref` (attach_ref expired); `wrong_response_slot` (slot not in this seller's workspace); `doc_no_longer_active` (doc transitioned to `expired` or `superseded` between find and attach); `firewall_violation`.

**Per-tool rate limit:** 10 rps per session.

#### 22.8.4.5 `capability_find` {#22.8.4.5-capability_find}

Search the seller's existing Capability Declarations for relevance to a requirement.

**Input schema:**

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "query": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 500 },
    "namespace_preference": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" }, "minItems": 1, "maxItems": 10 },
    "top_k": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 10, "default": 5 }
  },
  "required": ["query", "namespace_preference"]
}
```

**Description:**

> "Search the seller's existing Capability Declarations (the seller's structured product capability claims) for entries matching a buyer requirement. Use this before drafting a new Capability Declaration to avoid duplicates."

**Output schema:**

```json
{
  "hits": [
    {
      "capability_declaration_id": "cd_...",
      "title": "AES-256-GCM at-rest encryption",
      "category": "security_compliance",
      "kind": "out_of_box",
      "evidence_kb_entry_ids": ["kbe_..."],
      "confidence": 0.91
    }
  ]
}
```

**Per-tool rate limit:** 10 rps per session.

#### 22.8.4.6 `capability_declare_draft` {#22.8.4.6-capability_declare_draft}

Create a draft Capability Declaration inferred from KB evidence. Powers `kb_to_capability_suggestion` (§21.4.1 #18) and `capability_declaration_suggest` (§21.4.1.A).

**Input schema:**

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "title": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 200 },
    "category": { "type": "string", "enum": ["security_compliance", "integration_technical", "operational_maturity", "company_profile"] },
    "kind": { "type": "string", "enum": ["out_of_box", "configurable", "roadmap", "not_supported"] },
    "evidence_kb_entry_ids": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" }, "minItems": 1 },
    "summary_markdown": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 5000 }
  },
  "required": ["title", "category", "kind", "evidence_kb_entry_ids", "summary_markdown"]
}
```

**Description:**

> "Create a draft Capability Declaration in pending_review state from KB evidence. Always include 1+ kb_entry_id in evidence_kb_entry_ids — the draft is rejected by the server if no evidence is provided. Drafts NEVER auto-publish; a Seller Team Lead must review."

**Output schema:**

```json
{
  "capability_declaration_id": "cd_...",
  "status": "pending_review"
}
```

**Side effect.** Writes a `CapabilityDeclaration` row in `pending_review` state per §22.x (existing entity in v6 spec). Triggers a Team Lead notification (`capability_declaration_pending_review`) per Appendix C. The entry NEVER auto-publishes regardless of confidence.

**Per-tool rate limit:** 10 rps per session.

#### 22.8.4.7 `cite_verify` {#22.8.4.7-cite_verify}

Validates that a citation is still live and that the claimed excerpt appears at the claimed offsets. The agent **must** call this immediately before emitting a final response. Server-side this is also run as a gate per §22.8.5 (a draft that contains an unverified citation is rejected at the orchestrator submission gate, not just at the agent).

**Input schema:**

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "kb_entry_id": { "type": "string" },
    "excerpt": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 2000 },
    "claimed_offsets": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "integer" }, "minItems": 2, "maxItems": 2 }
  },
  "required": ["kb_entry_id", "excerpt", "claimed_offsets"]
}
```

**Output schema:**

```json
{
  "valid": true,
  "reason": "ok"
}
```

or

```json
{
  "valid": false,
  "reason": "entry_not_found | offsets_out_of_bounds | excerpt_mismatch | stale | entry_archived | unauthorized_namespace"
}
```

`reason` is always a value from Appendix J `cite_verify_reason`; success returns `ok`.

**Description:**

> "Verify that a citation you produced is still live: the entry exists, is active, and the excerpt at the claimed offsets matches what you cited. Call this on EVERY citation immediately before emitting your final draft. If any citation returns valid=false, re-retrieve and re-author that sentence — do not emit unverified citations."

**Per-tool rate limit:** 60 rps per session (matched to `kb_retrieve` because every retrieval implies one verify per cited excerpt).

#### 22.8.4.8 `kb_entry_draft_create` {#22.8.4.8-kb_entry_draft_create}

Creates a KBEntry row in `draft` state (the §22.4.1 initial state for any ingestion channel) with `created_via ∈ {kb_bootstrap, ghost_rfp_ingestion}` stamped on the row. This is the engineering-surface **write** path used by the KB-bootstrap and Ghost-RFP-ingestion agents (§22.10.3, §22.10.6) after they have extracted candidate entries from authoritative source documents. The row is reviewer-gated: the §22.4.1 state machine does not permit `draft` → `active` directly — a seller MUST walk the entry through `draft` → `under_review` → `active`. Agent-originated `draft` entries never auto-promote regardless of confidence score (parity with `capability_declare_draft` §22.8.4.6).

**Auth.** Vault-issued JWT bearer (§22.8.3); rejected on missing/invalid token with HTTP 401 `mcp_auth_required` or HTTP 403 `mcp_auth_invalid` (Appendix I).

**Input schema:**

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "namespace_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "The target namespace_id for the draft entry. MUST be present in the session JWT's allowed_namespace_ids; otherwise HTTP 403 firewall_violation."
    },
    "kind": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["qa", "fact", "policy", "evidence", "boilerplate"],
      "description": "KBEntry kind (Appendix J kb_entry_kind)."
    },
    "title": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 240,
      "description": "Human-readable title for reviewer triage."
    },
    "body": {
      "type": "string",
      "maxLength": 20000,
      "description": "Entry body. Must carry at least one source_ref; plain fabricated prose is rejected."
    },
    "source_refs": {
      "type": "array",
      "minItems": 1,
      "maxItems": 10,
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "source_kind": { "type": "string", "enum": ["url", "document_library_id", "uploaded_file_hash"] },
          "source_value": { "type": "string" },
          "offsets": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "integer" }, "minItems": 2, "maxItems": 2 }
        },
        "required": ["source_kind", "source_value"]
      },
      "description": "Required provenance pointer(s). Bootstrap runs MUST cite Firecrawl-crawled URLs; ghost-ingestion runs MUST cite the uploaded file hash and in-document offsets. Absent source_refs → HTTP 422 missing_source_ref."
    },
    "metadata": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "compliance_framework": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string", "enum": ["soc2", "iso27001", "hipaa", "gdpr", "pci"] } },
        "region": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } },
        "customer_segment": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string", "enum": ["smb", "midmarket", "enterprise"] } },
        "language": { "type": "string" }
      }
    },
    "dedupe_verdict": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "checked": { "type": "boolean" },
        "nearest_entry_id": { "type": "string" },
        "nearest_similarity": { "type": "number" }
      },
      "required": ["checked"],
      "description": "Outcome of the immediately preceding kb_dedupe_check call (§22.8.4.9). If checked=false OR nearest_similarity ≥ 0.92 and the agent did not explicitly mark the draft as a deliberate duplicate, the server rejects with HTTP 422 dedupe_gate_failed."
    },
    "confidence": {
      "type": "number",
      "minimum": 0.0,
      "maximum": 1.0,
      "description": "Agent self-reported extraction confidence. Reviewer inbox sorts by this ascending so low-confidence drafts get human attention first."
    }
  },
  "required": ["namespace_id", "kind", "title", "body", "source_refs", "dedupe_verdict", "confidence"]
}
```

**Description** (what Claude sees):

> "Create a draft Knowledge Base entry in `draft` state (the §22.4.1 initial state) stamped with `created_via` naming the parent capability. Call this only from the KB-bootstrap or Ghost-RFP-ingestion workflows after you have (a) extracted the claim from an authoritative source document and (b) called `kb_dedupe_check` to verify the claim is not already covered. Every draft MUST carry at least one `source_refs` entry; do not fabricate the body. Agent-originated drafts NEVER auto-publish — a human reviewer walks the entry through `draft` → `under_review` → `active` per §22.4.1. If `kb_dedupe_check` returned a nearest-neighbor similarity ≥ 0.92, either skip the draft or set a deliberate-duplicate flag in your orchestration log and proceed — the server will reject the write otherwise."

**Output schema:**

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "kb_entry_id": { "type": "string", "description": "UUID of the created draft entry." },
    "lifecycle_state": { "type": "string", "enum": ["draft"], "description": "Always `draft` per §22.4.1 (the lifecycle initial state for any ingestion channel)." },
    "created_via": { "type": "string", "enum": ["kb_bootstrap", "ghost_rfp_ingestion"], "description": "Stamped from the parent capability_id on the session JWT; drives Reviewer-Inbox filtering per Appendix C `kb_entry_pending_review` notification." },
    "reviewer_inbox_url": { "type": "string", "description": "Deep-link into the Seller-console reviewer inbox filtered on `lifecycle_state=draft` AND `created_via IN {kb_bootstrap, ghost_rfp_ingestion}`; sibling to the §22.8.4.6 / Appendix C `capability_declaration_pending_review` reviewer-inbox flow." }
  },
  "required": ["kb_entry_id", "lifecycle_state", "created_via"]
}
```

**Example request:**

```json
{
  "namespace_id": "ns_software_acmeco_product",
  "kind": "policy",
  "title": "AES-256 encryption at rest (data-store and backups)",
  "body": "AcmeCo encrypts all customer data at rest using AES-256. This applies to primary datastores (Postgres, S3) and to daily encrypted backups retained for 35 days.",
  "source_refs": [
    { "source_kind": "url", "source_value": "https://acmeco.com/trust/security", "offsets": [1240, 1480] }
  ],
  "metadata": { "compliance_framework": ["soc2"], "language": "en" },
  "dedupe_verdict": { "checked": true, "nearest_entry_id": null, "nearest_similarity": 0.61 },
  "confidence": 0.88
}
```

**Example response:**

```json
{
  "kb_entry_id": "kb_01J9P4QM5...",
  "lifecycle_state": "draft",
  "created_via": "kb_bootstrap",
  "reviewer_inbox_url": "https://app.sourcera.com/seller/kb/review?filter=draft&created_via=kb_bootstrap&highlight=kb_01J9P4QM5"
}
```

**Error envelope.** Structured per §22.8.6 (Error envelope row). Tool-specific codes (Appendix I):

- HTTP 401 `mcp_auth_required` / HTTP 403 `mcp_auth_invalid` — token missing or invalid.
- HTTP 403 `firewall_violation` — `namespace_id` outside the session's `allowed_namespace_ids[]`.
- HTTP 403 `wrong_region` — JWT `data_residency_region` disagrees with target namespace residency.
- HTTP 422 `missing_source_ref` — `source_refs` empty or omitted.
- HTTP 422 `dedupe_gate_failed` — `dedupe_verdict.checked=false` OR `nearest_similarity ≥ 0.92` without an explicit duplicate-override flag.
- HTTP 422 `kb_entry_content_moderation_blocked` — §22.4.1.A moderation holds, blocks, or escalates the draft; entry remains non-retrievable until edited or reviewed.
- HTTP 422 `body_too_long` — `body` exceeds 20,000 chars (matches §39 Object Size Constraints KB entry body cap).
- HTTP 429 `rate_limit_exceeded` — carries `retry_after_ms`.
- HTTP 503 `write_unavailable` — retrieval store write unreachable; agent backs off per `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §17`.

**Side effect.** Writes a `KBEntry` row with `lifecycle_state=draft` per §22.4.1, `created_by=<agent_id>`, `created_via={kb_bootstrap | ghost_rfp_ingestion}` (inferred from parent capability in the JWT claims). Triggers a Reviewer-Inbox notification per Appendix C (`kb_entry_pending_review`; new — registered in this prompt). The entry is **not** retrievable by `kb_retrieve` until a seller walks it through `draft` → `under_review` → `active` per §22.4.1 — the retrieval pipeline §22.9.1 Stage 2 Metadata Pre-Filter requires `lifecycle_state='active'` (with optional inclusion of `review_due` / `review_overdue` / `flagged_stale` per `exclude_review_states` policy).

**Permission scope.** `scoped_allow_with_quota` per §22.8.5 (side-effectful batch write). Per-session quota: 500 successful `kb_entry_draft_create` calls per parent `kb_bootstrap` AIOperation; 200 per `ghost_rfp_ingestion` AIOperation. Exceeding the quota returns HTTP 429 `rate_limit_exceeded` with `reason=session_quota_exhausted`.

**Per-tool rate limit:** 10 rps per session (matched to `capability_declare_draft` §22.8.4.6 because both are side-effectful persistent writes gated by human review).

#### 22.8.4.9 `kb_dedupe_check` {#22.8.4.9-kb_dedupe_check}

Similarity probe used by the KB-bootstrap and Ghost-RFP-ingestion agents before calling `kb_entry_draft_create`. Given a candidate entry's `title` + `body` + optional `kind` hint, returns the nearest existing entries in the target namespace so the agent can avoid writing a near-duplicate. Read-only: no writes, no audit-ledger side-effects beyond the normal per-tool span (§22.8.6).

**Auth.** Vault-issued JWT bearer (§22.8.3); rejected on missing/invalid token with HTTP 401 `mcp_auth_required` or HTTP 403 `mcp_auth_invalid` (Appendix I).

**Input schema:**

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "namespace_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Target namespace_id to dedupe against. MUST be present in the session JWT's allowed_namespace_ids."
    },
    "candidate": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "title": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 240 },
        "body": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 20000 },
        "kind": { "type": "string", "enum": ["qa", "fact", "policy", "evidence", "boilerplate"] }
      },
      "required": ["title", "body"]
    },
    "top_k": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 5, "default": 3 }
  },
  "required": ["namespace_id", "candidate"]
}
```

**Description** (what Claude sees):

> "Before creating a draft KB entry via `kb_entry_draft_create`, call this to check whether a near-duplicate entry already exists. Pass the proposed title and body; the server returns up to 3 nearest entries with cosine similarity scores. If `nearest_similarity ≥ 0.92`, you SHOULD skip `kb_entry_draft_create` and instead update or reference the existing entry. If `0.75 ≤ similarity < 0.92`, you MAY proceed but mark the draft with a note for the human reviewer. The result of this call MUST be passed as the `dedupe_verdict` field on the subsequent `kb_entry_draft_create` call — the server rejects writes that were not preceded by a dedupe check."

**Output schema:**

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "nearest_entries": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "kb_entry_id": { "type": "string" },
          "title": { "type": "string" },
          "kind": { "type": "string" },
          "lifecycle_state": { "type": "string", "enum": ["draft", "under_review", "active", "review_due", "review_overdue", "flagged_stale", "archived"], "description": "Canonical §22.4.1 KBEntry lifecycle state of the nearest entry. Agents SHOULD prefer returning `active` matches; `draft` and `under_review` matches are surfaced so the agent can avoid creating near-duplicates of already-pending drafts authored by a sibling agent run." },
          "similarity": { "type": "number", "description": "0.0–1.0 cosine similarity against the candidate's dense embedding; ties broken by BM25 score." },
          "excerpt": { "type": "string", "description": "Up to 400 chars of the nearest-matching passage." }
        }
      }
    },
    "nearest_similarity": { "type": "number", "description": "Convenience field: similarity of the top match, or 0.0 if the namespace is empty." },
    "probe_metadata": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "embedding_model_version": { "type": "string" },
        "candidates_scanned": { "type": "integer" }
      }
    }
  },
  "required": ["nearest_entries", "nearest_similarity"]
}
```

**Example request:**

```json
{
  "namespace_id": "ns_software_acmeco_product",
  "candidate": {
    "title": "AES-256 encryption at rest",
    "body": "AcmeCo encrypts all customer data at rest using AES-256...",
    "kind": "policy"
  },
  "top_k": 3
}
```

**Example response (no near-match):**

```json
{
  "nearest_entries": [
    { "kb_entry_id": "kb_01J9H21...", "title": "TLS 1.3 in transit", "kind": "policy", "lifecycle_state": "active", "similarity": 0.61, "excerpt": "AcmeCo enforces TLS 1.3..." }
  ],
  "nearest_similarity": 0.61,
  "probe_metadata": { "embedding_model_version": "voyage-3-large-2025-q3", "candidates_scanned": 1247 }
}
```

**Error envelope.** Structured per §22.8.6. Tool-specific codes (Appendix I):

- HTTP 401 `mcp_auth_required` / HTTP 403 `mcp_auth_invalid` — token missing or invalid.
- HTTP 403 `firewall_violation` — `namespace_id` outside the session's `allowed_namespace_ids[]`.
- HTTP 403 `wrong_region` — JWT `data_residency_region` disagrees with target namespace residency.
- HTTP 422 `candidate_body_too_long` — candidate `body` exceeds 20,000 chars.
- HTTP 429 `rate_limit_exceeded` — carries `retry_after_ms`.
- HTTP 503 `retrieval_unavailable` — dense or BM25 backends unreachable; same degraded-mode semantics as `kb_retrieve` (§22.8.6 Failure handling row).

**Side effect.** None beyond the normal per-tool span and the PostHog `mcp_kb_tool_invoked` event (Appendix G).

**Permission scope.** `always_allow` per §22.8.5 (read-only retrieval; same class as `kb_retrieve`, `kb_get_entry`, `capability_find`).

**Per-tool rate limit:** 30 rps per session (matched to `kb_get_entry` §22.8.4.2 — both are pointwise read paths cheaper than full `kb_retrieve`).

### 22.8.5 MCP Server Permission Policy {#22.8.5-mcp-server-permission-policy}

Per Anthropic MCP docs: "The MCP toolset defaults to a permission policy of `always_ask`, which requires user approval before each tool call."

Sourcera overrides to `always_allow` for read-only tools (`kb_retrieve`, `kb_get_entry`, `kb_dedupe_check`, `document_library_find`, `capability_find`, `cite_verify`) because:

1. These tools are read-only and respect firewall boundaries enforced by the MCP server (§22.8.3).
2. A first-pass generation may fire 100+ retrievals; `always_ask` is unworkable for batch/async sessions.
3. Billing and audit are handled separately via Sourcera's event consumer and the AIOperation ledger (§4.8.1).

Sourcera retains `always_ask` for side-effectful tools (`doc_attach`, `capability_declare_draft`) in **interactive** sessions; **batch** sessions (including Managed-Agent bootstrap/ingestion runs) use `scoped_allow_with_quota` with the orchestrator enforcing guardrails (per-session quotas on `doc_attach` to prevent runaway attachments; pre-publish review gate on `capability_declare_draft`; per-parent-AIOperation write caps on `kb_entry_draft_create` per §22.8.4.8).

**Permission scope enum.** Registered in Appendix J `mcp_permission_scope`: `always_allow`, `always_ask`, `scoped_allow_with_quota`, `denied`.

**Submission gate.** Independently of the agent's behavior, the orchestrator enforces:

- **Citation completeness gate.** Every sentence in a final emitted response must carry a `[[cite:kb_entry_id=...,offsets=[s,e]]]` marker per `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §6.2`. Drafts failing the gate are rejected with `agent_output_uncited_sentence` (new orchestrator-level error code; HTTP 422; Appendix I); the AIOperation transitions to `rejected` per §4.8.1.
- **Citation validity gate.** Every cited `kb_entry_id` is re-verified via `cite_verify` server-side at submission time even if the agent already verified; failure rejects with `agent_output_invalid_citation` (new; Appendix I).
- **Firewall gate.** Every cited `kb_entry_id` must be in the session's `allowed_namespace_ids[]`; otherwise the AIOperation is rejected and a Trust & Safety alert fires.

### 22.8.6 MCP Server Implementation Requirements {#22.8.6-mcp-server-implementation-requirements}

| Concern | Requirement | Cross-link |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP per MCP spec; Cloudflare-backed Global Accelerator front door with regional failover. | `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §3.6` |
| Auth | JWT bearer (from vault) validated via JWKS published at `mcp.sourcera.com/.well-known/jwks.json`. Token lifetime 1h. Key rotation every 90 days with JWKS overlap window. | §22.8.3 |
| One-time-use enforcement | Per §22.8.3.1 MCPSessionTokenRecord; `jti` unique within `(org_id)`. | §22.8.3.1 |
| Per-tool rate limits | `kb_retrieve` 60 rps per session; `kb_get_entry` 30 rps; `kb_dedupe_check` 30 rps; `cite_verify` 60 rps; `document_library_find`, `doc_attach`, `capability_find`, `capability_declare_draft`, `kb_entry_draft_create` 10 rps. Overruns return structured `rate_limit_exceeded` errors with `retry_after_ms`. | §22.8.4 |
| Latency budget (p95) | `kb_retrieve` ≤ 500 ms; `kb_get_entry` ≤ 200 ms; `kb_dedupe_check` ≤ 250 ms; `cite_verify` ≤ 150 ms; `document_library_find` ≤ 300 ms; `doc_attach` ≤ 300 ms; `capability_find` ≤ 300 ms; `capability_declare_draft` ≤ 500 ms; `kb_entry_draft_create` ≤ 500 ms. | `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §3.6` |
| Observability | Every MCP call emits an OpenTelemetry span linked to the Managed Agents `session.id` and `agent.tool_use.id`; PostHog event per call (`mcp_kb_tool_invoked`; Appendix G); cost-base recalc (§4.8.6) consumes the spans nightly. | §15 (Observability) |
| Residency | MCP server deployed per-region (US, EU). Vault JWT carries `data_residency_region`; server routes to region-local retrieval store. Cross-region tokens rejected with HTTP 403 `wrong_region`. | §22.3.1, §40.2 |
| Error envelope | Structured: `{"error": {"type": "rate_limit_exceeded \| invalid_namespace \| stale_token \| not_found \| firewall_violation \| wrong_region \| stale_attach_ref \| wrong_response_slot \| doc_no_longer_active \| entry_archived \| entry_flagged_stale", "message": "...", "retry_after_ms": N}}`. Anthropic's tool-use docs recommend "semantic, stable identifiers" for errors. | Appendix I |
| Webhook emission | `kb.document.attached`, `kb.namespace.migrated`, `kb.entry.flagged_stale`, `kb.entry.published`, `kb.entry.archived`. HMAC-SHA256 signing; idempotent via `event_id`; 5-failure DLQ; payload ≤ 256KB. | §31, Appendix C, Appendix G |
| Audit | Every tool call writes a row to the Sourcera Tool Audit Ledger (operational store; not detailed here) keyed by `(org_id, session_id, tool_call_id)` with input hash, output size, latency, and outcome. 13-month retention. | §40.2 |
| Failure handling | On Voyage outage: dense path returns empty; retrieval falls back to BM25-only with a degraded-mode flag in `retrieval_metadata.degraded_mode=true`. On OpenSearch outage: BM25 path returns empty; dense-only with same flag. On both: `kb_retrieve` returns HTTP 503 `retrieval_unavailable`; the agent backs off per `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §17`. | §17 (KB Spec) |

**Failure modes addressed (counterfactual pass).**

1. **Vault JWT expires mid-session** (long-running agent runs > 1h). Resolved: orchestrator monitors `expires_at − now < 5min`; refreshes the vault token (re-mints JWT, updates the Anthropic vault entry) before expiry. The MCP server accepts the new JWT seamlessly because the rotation issues a new `jti` and immediately revokes the old via `revoked_at` in MCPSessionTokenRecord with `revoked_reason=expired`.
2. **Two MCP tool calls race a namespace migration (§22.4.4).** Resolved: migration sets `is_archived=true` on the source namespace **before** rewriting entries; `kb_retrieve` filters `is_archived=true` namespaces from results; in-flight calls see no migrated entries; post-migration calls see them in the Org namespace.
3. **Anthropic MCP proxy outage.** Resolved: `kb_retrieve` and friends become unreachable from the agent; the agent harness emits `session.error` per `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §11`; orchestrator retries the parent capability with backoff (5s, 30s, 5m, 30m); after 4 failures, AIOperation transitions to `rejected` with `failure_reason=mcp_proxy_unavailable`. PagerDuty alert if the rate exceeds 1% over 15 minutes.

## 22.9 Retrieval Engineering {#22.9-retrieval-engineering}

This section specifies the implementation behind the `kb_retrieve` MCP tool (§22.8.4.1). Claude never sees these details — the agent observes only a ranked candidate list with excerpts. The content here is reproduced from `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §4` and normalized to Master Spec authoring conventions; cross-references to §21.4 Capability Registry, §22.3 entities, §22.5 KB Health Model, and §34.11 OutcomeContract are added throughout.

### 22.9.1 Retrieval Pipeline {#22.9.1-retrieval-pipeline}

For every `kb_retrieve` call (`query`, `namespace_preference`, `filters`, `exclude_review_states`, `top_k`), the MCP server executes the following deterministic eight-stage pipeline. Stages are numbered for traceability — every span emitted by the MCP server (§22.8.6 `OpenTelemetry`) is tagged with `pipeline_stage` so latency regressions can be localized to a single stage.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. Query Normalization & Expansion                          │
│    - lowercase, strip punctuation (BM25 tokenization)       │
│    - detect compliance frameworks, product areas, locales   │
│    - synonym expansion via static thesaurus (SOC2 ↔ soc2)   │
└──────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 2. Metadata Pre-Filter (hard filter, zero recall cost)      │
│    - namespace_id IN allowed_namespace_ids                  │
│    - review_state NOT IN exclude_review_states              │
│    - content_moderation_state = passed                      │
│    - language / region / framework match                    │
└──────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 3. Parallel Retrieval                                       │
│    ┌──────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────────┐   │
│    │ BM25 (OpenSearch)    │  │ Dense (pgvector, cosine) │   │
│    │ → top 50 candidates  │  │ → top 50 candidates      │   │
│    └──────────┬───────────┘  └────────────┬─────────────┘   │
└───────────────┼───────────────────────────┼─────────────────┘
                └────────────┬──────────────┘
                             ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 4. Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)                             │
│    score(d) = Σ 1 / (k + rank_i(d))   where k = 60          │
│    → top 20 fused candidates                                │
└──────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 5. Namespace Preference Boost                               │
│    score *= 1.0 if first-pref namespace, 0.85 if second     │
└──────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 6. Freshness & Quality Weighting                            │
│    score *= confidence_modifier × (0.5 + 0.5 * win_rate)    │
└──────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 7. Re-rank (Voyage rerank-2 by default)                     │
│    → top top_k (default 5)                                  │
│    + Claude Haiku secondary re-rank for high-stakes flows   │
└──────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 8. Excerpt Extraction                                       │
│    - locate best passage via BM25 on sentence-tokenized body│
│    - return [start, end] offsets + 400-char window          │
└──────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       ▼
      [return to Claude]
```

**Stage-level invariants.**

| Stage | Invariant | Rejection / Fallback |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1. Normalization & Expansion | `query` length binds to §39 row `mcp_kb_retrieve_query`; `namespace_preference[]` length binds to §39 row `mcp_kb_retrieve_namespace_preference_length`; each filter value is a registered Appendix J enum value. | HTTP 422 `bad_request` with `details.invalid_field` populated. |
| 2. Metadata Pre-Filter | `allowed_namespace_ids[]` derived from JWT (§22.8.3) intersected with schema-non-empty `namespace_preference[]`; an empty intersection means no authorized namespace overlaps the requested set and returns `top_k = []` with `retrieval_metadata.no_authorized_namespace=true`. | Never falls back to a wider scope; the firewall is unconditional. |
| 3. Parallel Retrieval | BM25 and dense execute concurrently with a per-leg deadline of 250 ms; the `Promise.allSettled` wrapper records partial-failure spans. | Either leg returning empty → `retrieval_metadata.degraded_mode=true`; both legs returning empty → HTTP 503 `retrieval_unavailable`. |
| 4. RRF | `k = 60` constant; reproducible across deployments. | None — RRF cannot fail given non-empty inputs. |
| 5. Namespace Preference Boost | First-preference multiplier 1.0; second-preference 0.85; entries outside the preference list are not considered (already excluded at Stage 2). | None. |
| 6. Freshness & Quality Weighting | `confidence_modifier ∈ [0.1, 1.5]` (clamped per §22.3.1); `win_rate_weight ∈ [0.0, 1.0]` is the canonical closed-bid outcome field; multiplier `(0.5 + 0.5 × win_rate_weight)` is clamped to `[0.5, 1.0]` per §22.5. | None. |
| 7. Re-rank | Per §22.9.6 model selection; Voyage `rerank-2` p95 ≤ 30 ms; Claude Haiku secondary p95 ≤ 400 ms; per-call timeout 800 ms. | Re-rank API outage → fall back to RRF-fused order with `retrieval_metadata.rerank_skipped=true` and Ops alert. |
| 8. Excerpt Extraction | `[start, end]` offsets are character indices into `body_markdown` AFTER Markdown unescape; window default 400 chars; window expansion to 800 chars allowed for high-stakes flows. | Body shorter than the window → return the full body (no padding). |

### 22.9.2 Indexing Substrate {#22.9.2-indexing-substrate}

The retrieval substrate is a five-component stack. Each component is independently versionable; component versions are pinned per Org via the §22.4.5 embedding-bump and a parallel `bm25_substrate_version` pointer.

| Component | Technology | Rationale |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Lexical (BM25) | OpenSearch (AWS-managed) | Best-in-class BM25 tuning, multi-tenant namespace sharding, mature faceted filtering. Alternatives considered: Tantivy (embedded, faster but harder to operate at multi-tenant scale). |
| Dense embeddings | Voyage-3-large via Voyage AI API | Anthropic-recommended embedding model for RAG; 1024-dim, superior retrieval benchmarks vs OpenAI text-embedding-3-large on MTEB. `voyage-3` (512-dim) for cost-sensitive sellers on the seller_free tier per §5.11 / §39. |
| Vector store | pgvector in Convex/Postgres | Co-located with the §22.3.1 KBEntry table; transactional consistency between entry and embedding; `HNSW` index, `ef_construction=200`, `m=16`. For Orgs > 10M entries, shard by `namespace_id`. |
| Re-ranker (primary) | Voyage `rerank-2` | ~30 ms for top-20 → top-5, trained against retrieval-then-rerank objectives. |
| Re-ranker (secondary, optional) | Claude Haiku via Messages API | ~400 ms; model-grade re-rank for the First-Pass Responder's top-tier flows. Called from the MCP server, not from the agent, to avoid context pollution. Cost charged to Sourcera's internal cost base, not customer-billed (§21.4.2 cost base column for `first_pass_responses` already absorbs this). |

**Substrate version pinning.** Each Org's substrate state is captured in a `KBSubstrateVersion` denormalized record (engineered alongside §22.3.1 entity tables; not introduced as a new entity in this prompt) keyed by `(org_id, namespace_id)` containing the active `bm25_index_version`, `embedding_model`, `embedding_column`, and `reranker_version`. Substrate-version skew between an in-flight session and the active pointer is handled per §22.4.5 (rollback) and §22.4.3 (re-index on edit) — sessions captured at the older version continue to read from the older substrate until completion.

### 22.9.3 Chunking Strategy {#22.9.3-chunking-strategy}

KB entries are typically already short (Q&A pairs, policy paragraphs). Chunking applies at ingestion for long source documents (bootstrapped pages per §22.10.3, ghost-bid RFPs per §22.10.5).

- **Primary unit:** `KBEntry` = one coherent Q&A, fact, policy statement, or evidence reference. Mean length 400–1,200 chars; hard cap 50,000 chars per §39.
- **Long-doc chunking for bootstrap (§22.10.3):** hierarchical semantic chunking with 400–600 char target, 15% overlap, hard break on H1/H2 Markdown boundaries. Parent pointer retained via `derived_from_kb_entry_id` (§22.3.1) for context expansion if an excerpt truncates mid-thought.
- **Embedding scope:** one embedding per `KBEntry`. Title and body concatenated in canonical form `f"[{kind.upper()}] {title}\n\n{body}"`. Metadata is **not** embedded — metadata is a Stage-2 pre-filter only (§22.9.1).

### 22.9.4 Why Not Just Dense Retrieval {#22.9.4-why-not-just-dense-retrieval}

Pure dense retrieval on RFP-style content underperforms because:

1. **Rare terms matter** — vendor-specific product names, compliance codes, API identifiers. BM25 nails these; dense blurs them.
2. **Acronyms and code mentions** (ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, GDPR Art. 33). Exact match is high-signal.
3. **Query length asymmetry.** Buyer requirements are 1–3 sentences; KB entries may be paragraphs. Dense alone over-rewards entries that match the style, not the content.

Hybrid BM25 + dense + RRF + re-rank is the current best-practice recipe (references: Pinecone hybrid benchmarks, Voyage `rerank-2` paper, Anthropic "agentic search first" guidance). The §22.16.3 evaluation harness gates against a **dense-only** ablation baseline on every release; if hybrid loses to dense-only on Recall@5 by ≥ 1 percentage point, the release is blocked.

### 22.9.5 Query Expansion {#22.9.5-query-expansion}

The MCP server performs automatic, deterministic query expansion BEFORE BM25 (server-side, not agent-side):

- **Synonym table** (`packages/sourcera-kb-thesaurus/synonyms.yaml`): `SOC2 ↔ SOC 2`, `GDPR ↔ EU data protection`, etc.
- **Acronym expansion** (`packages/sourcera-kb-thesaurus/acronyms.yaml`): `DPA ↔ Data Processing Agreement`, `BAA ↔ Business Associate Agreement`.
- **Product-term normalization** (`packages/sourcera-kb-thesaurus/product_terms.yaml`): normalize CamelCase product references such as `SalesforceServiceCloud` → `Salesforce Service Cloud`.

**Why server-side, not agent-side.** Agent-side query rewriting tempts the model to "improve" the query, burning tokens and introducing drift across sessions for the same input. The server expansion is deterministic, audited (`retrieval_metadata.expansion_applied=[...]`), and improves cache hit rates on the §22.16.2 prompt-cache layer. Agents are explicitly instructed in their system prompts (§22.10) NOT to rewrite the query before calling `kb_retrieve`.

**Thesaurus governance.** The three YAML files are versioned in `packages/sourcera-kb-thesaurus/` and rolled forward via the Ops Console; CI requires every PR touching the thesaurus to include a regression-test case in `tests/retrieval/thesaurus_regression.json`.

### 22.9.6 Re-Rank Model Selection {#22.9.6-re-rank-model-selection}

Re-rank model is selected per `operation_class` (a server-side classification of the calling capability, derived from the JWT's `capability_id` claim):

```
if operation_class in {"first_pass_high_stakes", "q_and_a_suggestion"}:
    rerank = voyage("rerank-2") → claude_haiku_rerank_top_8 → top 5
elif operation_class in {"kb_to_capability_suggestion", "capability_find"}:
    rerank = voyage("rerank-2-lite") → top 3
else:
    rerank = voyage("rerank-2") → top 5
```

Claude Haiku secondary re-rank adds ~$0.0004 per retrieval but lifts acceptance rate measurably on the §22.16.3 calibration set (target: ≥ 90% relevant top-5 on the 1,000-pair benchmark per §22.16.3). The cost is absorbed into the parent capability's `cost_base` per §21.4.2 (e.g., `first_pass_responses` cost base ~$1.50 includes the secondary re-rank for high-stakes flows).

**`first_pass_high_stakes` classification.** A `first_pass_responses` invocation is classified `high_stakes` when ANY of the following hold: (a) the parent bid workspace's `bid_value_estimate_usd ≥ $250,000`, (b) the seller has opted in via Settings → Agent → "Use Opus for critical bids" (Open Item §22.16.6 — pending sign-off), or (c) the workspace contains ≥ 1 requirement tagged `compliance_critical` (§22.3.1 `topic_tags` includes any of `soc2`, `iso27001`, `hipaa`, `gdpr`, `pci`).

### 22.9.7 Metadata Pre-Filter — Why Pre-Filter {#22.9.7-metadata-pre-filter}

Filters run **before** retrieval (Stage 2 of §22.9.1), not after. Three reasons:

1. **Recall preservation.** Post-filtering from top-50 may leave top-5 empty if the filter is aggressive (e.g., language=fr on an English-dominant KB).
2. **Cost.** BM25 and dense shards are pre-partitioned by `namespace_id` and `language`; pre-filtering narrows the search space and reduces both index-scan cost and Voyage embedding-similarity cost.
3. **Security.** `allowed_namespace_ids` enforcement MUST be unconditional — filters run as a pre-condition, not a ranking influence. Post-filtering would mean the dense-similarity computation has already touched cross-tenant vectors, which is unacceptable for the §22.8.3 firewall guarantee.

### 22.9.8 Stale Entry Handling {#22.9.8-stale-entry-handling}

- Entries with `review_state ∈ {review_overdue, flagged_stale}` are **excluded** from `kb_retrieve` by default. The excerpt is still visible to the Seller Team Lead via direct entry view, but is not used for AI generation.
- Entries with `review_state = review_due` are included but multiplied by **0.85 confidence modifier** at Stage 6 of §22.9.1.
- The agent **cannot** cite a stale entry — `cite_verify` (§22.8.4.7) returns `{valid: false, reason: "stale"}`, which the agent handles by re-retrieving and selecting an alternate candidate.
- Override capability `kb_staleness_classifier` (§21.4.1 #17) is the **only** caller permitted to pass `exclude_review_states=[]` — the override is logged at the orchestrator's audit ledger as `agent_kb_stale_override` (Appendix J `Audit Event Action Type — KB additions`). All other capabilities passing the override receive HTTP 403 `firewall_violation`.

### 22.9.9 Failure Modes Addressed (Counterfactual Pass) {#22.9.9-failure-modes-retrieval}

1. **Voyage embedding API outage.** Resolved per §22.9.1 Stage 3: dense leg returns empty, retrieval falls back to BM25-only with `retrieval_metadata.degraded_mode=true`. Parent capability continues with reduced confidence; downstream `cite_verify` enforces correctness regardless of retrieval mode.
2. **OpenSearch index corruption mid-query.** Resolved per §22.9.1 Stage 3: BM25 leg returns empty; dense-only with same flag; if both legs return empty, HTTP 503 `retrieval_unavailable` returns and the agent backs off per §22.16.6 retry curve.
3. **Re-rank API rate limit.** Resolved per §22.9.1 Stage 7: rate-limit error from Voyage triggers fallback to RRF-fused order; `retrieval_metadata.rerank_skipped=true`; PagerDuty alert fires if the fallback rate exceeds 1% of calls over 15 minutes.

## 22.10 Managed Agent Definitions {#22.10-managed-agent-definitions}

Every Sourcera Seller-side AI capability backed by `requires_managed_agent=true` (§4.8.2; §21.4.2.A) is realized as a versioned Claude Managed Agents `agent` definition checked into `packages/sourcera-agent-definitions/` as JSON, version-controlled, and deployed via CI via `client.beta.agents.create` / `client.beta.agents.update`. The content here is reproduced from `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §6` and normalized to Master Spec authoring conventions; cross-references to §21.4 Capability Registry, §22.12 Skills, §22.13 Environments, and §34.11 OutcomeContract are added.

### 22.10.1 Agent Definition Conventions {#22.10.1-agent-definition-conventions}

- **Naming.** `agent_sourcera_{capability}_v{N}` — e.g., `agent_sourcera_first_pass_responder_v17`. The `capability` slug MUST match a `capability_id` registered in §21.4 (Capability Registry); the agent definition pointer is the foreign key from the §21.4.2 row's `requires_managed_agent` flag to the deployed agent.
- **Versioning.** Every prompt or tool-set change increments `N`. Anthropic also versions internally (each `update` creates a new Anthropic version); Sourcera pins both for full traceability via `packages/sourcera-agent-definitions/POINTERS.json` (`{capability_slug: {sourcera_version: N, anthropic_version_id: ...}}`).
- **System prompt discipline.** Max 8K chars per agent version. Anything longer is moved into a Skill (§22.12). The system prompt establishes identity, non-negotiables (citation discipline, firewall), and lists the capability's core workflow.
- **Model selection.** Per the §21.4 registry's `model_tier_default` column. Sonnet is default for generation; Haiku for classification and ranking; Opus for deep extraction (ingestion, policy parsing, ghost-bid).
- **Archival.** Deprecated agent versions are archived (read-only) so in-flight sessions continue running; new sessions cannot reference an archived version. Per Anthropic docs: "Archiving makes the agent read-only. Existing sessions continue to run, but new sessions cannot reference it."
- **Definition table format.** Every agent below is documented with the complete **Agent Definition Table** schema: `id`, `purpose`, `model`, `tool allowlist`, `skills`, `environment`, `version`, `update workflow ref`, plus the capability cross-link and OutcomeContract cross-link.

#### 22.10.1.A Capability-ID / KB-Spec / Signal-Contract Alias Table {#22.10.1.a-capability-alias-table}

The v7.0.0 corpus inherited three overlapping naming conventions for the same set of AI operations: (a) the **canonical `capability_id`** registered in §21.4.1 / §21.4.2 (Capability Registry), which is the primary key used by §4.8.2, §4.8.4 (OutcomeContract), §4.8.7 (FreeAllowanceCounter), the §34.3.4 public pricing API, the §34.8 entitlement engine, and every audit-ledger event; (b) the **KB-Spec alias** used informally in `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §6/§13` and carried into §22.10 cross-links; and (c) the **OutcomeContract signal name** registered in §34.11.1, which names the signal (the thing the user surface emits) rather than the capability (the thing that gets billed). These three namespaces diverged during the integration program and MUST be treated as authoritative in that order — the §21.4.1.A reconciliation note already records the primacy of the §21.4 Capability Registry.

This table is authoritative for resolving any ambiguity downstream. Any future reference in the corpus that uses a non-canonical alias MUST be rewritten to the canonical `capability_id`; the signal-contract column remains the authoritative name for §34.11.1 / §21.4.5 contract lookups.

| `kb_to_capability_suggestion` | `kb_to_capability_draft`, `capability_from_kb` | `kb_to_capability_suggestion` | `agent_sourcera_kb_to_capability_v4` (§22.10.5) | Nightly batch; writes `CapabilityDeclaration` rows in `pending_review`. |

| `kb_staleness_classifier` | `kb_staleness_scan`, `kb_staleness_review` | `kb_staleness_classifier` | (no standalone agent v7.0.0 seed — classifier runs as an Ops-side background job against the §22.5 KB Health Model) | Authorized sole holder of the `exclude_review_states=[]` override per §22.17 AC #49. |

**Hygiene rules.**

1. **Canonical-ID primacy.** Every new §22 authoring pass MUST use the Canonical `capability_id` column as the reference in prose. The agent-definition handle MAY be used inside §22.10 table rows and inside `packages/sourcera-agent-definitions/POINTERS.json`; it MUST NOT appear in §21.4, §34.3.4, §34.8, §34.11, §40.2, or Appendix C/G/I/J.
2. **Signal-contract reference.** OutcomeContract lookups MUST cite the signal name (column 3) qualified by section reference — e.g., `§34.11.1 \`first_pass_rfp_draft\`` — not the `capability_id`, because §34.11.1 is indexed by signal.
3. **CI enforcement.** A markdown-lint rule (`capability_id_canonicalization_lint`) flags any §21.4 / §34 / Appendix J occurrence of a non-canonical alias from column 2; CI blocks the PR. QA test `capability_alias_registry_cross_ref` asserts every row's canonical `capability_id` exists in §21.4 with `status=active`.
4. **Extension rule.** Any future capability introduced into §21.4 that imports a non-canonical alias from §22 or `KB_Engineering_Spec.md` MUST be registered in this table in the same PR; the integration-program reconciliation log requires it before phase sign-off.

| Field | Value |

| `model` | `claude-sonnet-4-6` (default); `claude-opus-4-6` for `first_pass_high_stakes` (§22.9.6) when seller-opt-in is honored. |
| `tool allowlist` | (a) `agent_toolset_20260401` — `read`, `grep`, `glob` enabled; `bash`, `edit`, `write`, `web_search`, `web_fetch` disabled. (b) `mcp_toolset` `sourcera_kb` — `kb_retrieve`, `kb_get_entry`, `document_library_find`, `doc_attach`, `cite_verify`. (c) Custom tools — `emit_structured_draft`, `request_seller_clarification`. |
| `skills` | `skill_sourcera_rfp_drafting` (latest), `skill_sourcera_compliance_citations` (latest), `skill_sourcera_confidence_thresholds` (latest). |
| `environment` | `env_sourcera_kb_runner_v3` (§22.13.1). |
| `version` | Sourcera `v17`; Anthropic version pinned in `POINTERS.json`. |
| `update workflow ref` | §22.10.7. |
| Capability cross-link | §21.4.2 `first_pass_responses` (Managed Agent batch). |
| OutcomeContract cross-link | §34.11.1 `first_pass_rfp_draft` (signal: ≥ 50% of generated draft retained in submitted bid; window 14d or on bid submission). |

**System prompt (excerpt; full version in `packages/sourcera-agent-definitions/first_pass_responder/system_prompt.md`).**

> You are Sourcera's First-Pass Response drafting assistant. Your job is to propose draft responses to buyer RFP requirements using ONLY evidence retrieved from the seller's Knowledge Base via the `sourcera_kb` tools.
>
> # Inviolable rules
> 1. **RAG-only.** Every sentence of every draft must be supported by a `kb_entry_id` retrieved via `kb_retrieve` or `kb_get_entry`. If no KB entry matches a requirement with confidence ≥ 0.6, return the draft as the literal string `__NO_KB_MATCH__` for that requirement. Do not guess.
> 2. **Inline citations are structural, not narrative.** Each sentence ends with a machine-parseable citation: `[[cite:kb_entry_id=...,offsets=[start,end]]]`. Omit trailing prose like "as noted above."
> 3. **No fabrication of claims not in retrieved excerpts.** If an excerpt says "we support AES-256 encryption at rest," you may not write "we also support TLS 1.3 in transit" unless a separate retrieval yields an entry supporting that claim.
> 4. **Firewall.** Do not reference any seller, org, or workspace other than the one whose KB is exposed via the `sourcera_kb` tools. Do not emit speculation about competitors.
> 5. **Before emitting any final response, call `cite_verify` on every citation you produced in that response.** Server will reject the draft if any citation fails verification.
>
> # Workflow (per requirement)
> 1. Read the requirement text provided in the user message.
> 2. Call `kb_retrieve` with an expanded query. Prefer the Software namespace first.
> 3. If no hit ≥ 0.6 confidence: emit `__NO_KB_MATCH__` and move on.
> 4. Select the top 1–3 relevant entries. If excerpts are insufficient, call `kb_get_entry` for the full body.
> 5. For requirements citing a compliance framework, call `document_library_find` and `doc_attach` to attach the matching evidence doc.
> 6. Draft the response, one sentence per claim, with an inline citation per sentence.
> 7. Call `cite_verify` on every citation.
> 8. Emit the draft as a structured block via `emit_structured_draft`.
>
> # Output format
> For each requirement, emit:
> ```
> <requirement id="REQ-...">
>   <draft>
>     <sentence cite="kb_entry_id=...,offsets=[s,e]">...</sentence>
>     ...
>   </draft>
>   <attachments>
>     <attachment doc_id="..."/>
>   </attachments>
>   <confidence>0.87</confidence>
> </requirement>
> ```

**Tools (JSON).**

```json
[
  { "type": "agent_toolset_20260401",
    "default_config": { "enabled": false },
    "configs": [
      { "name": "read", "enabled": true },
      { "name": "grep", "enabled": true },
      { "name": "glob", "enabled": true }
    ]
  },
  { "type": "mcp_toolset", "mcp_server_name": "sourcera_kb" }
]
```

**Rationale for restricting `agent_toolset_20260401`.** The First-Pass Responder operates over retrieved evidence and writes structured output. It has no legitimate need to `bash`, `edit`, `write` arbitrary files, `web_search` (we don't want the agent pulling in non-KB content), or `web_fetch`. Restricting the surface minimizes failure modes and aligns with the §22.16.7 prompt-injection-defense layering.

**MCP servers.**

```json
[
  { "type": "url", "name": "sourcera_kb", "url": "https://mcp.sourcera.com/kb/v1" }
]
```

**Skills.**

```json
[
  { "type": "custom", "skill_id": "skill_sourcera_rfp_drafting", "version": "latest" },
  { "type": "custom", "skill_id": "skill_sourcera_compliance_citations", "version": "latest" },
  { "type": "custom", "skill_id": "skill_sourcera_confidence_thresholds", "version": "latest" }
]
```

**Metadata.**

```json
{ "sourcera_capability_id": "first_pass_responses", "sourcera_internal_version": "v17" }
```
