The Master Spec has no §50 surface; the spec's analytics responsibilities are distributed across §17 (Workspace Analytics — Buyer), §24.5 (Seller Analytics — Seller Console), §42 (Observability), and §48.8.8 (Telemetry Registry). §22.18 routes its analytics cross-links to the actual Master Spec homes and flags the substitution in RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions. The substitution is additive, not destructive; §50 is not authored as a new top-level surface in this pass.

### 22.18.1 Design Principle — "Honest Portability; On-Platform Compounding" {#22.18.1-design-principle-honest-portability-on-platform-compounding}

The §22.18 design principle is stated, verbatim, as *"Honest Portability; On-Platform Compounding."* The principle expands as two concurrent, non-negotiable product contracts:

1. **Honest Portability.** The seller can, at any time, on any plan tier (including Free), export the full KB — entry bodies, entry metadata, provenance, attachments, and schema — in a format Sourcera documents publicly and commits to maintaining. The export is one-click, rate-limited only for abuse, never paywalled, and produces an artifact the seller can load into any other system (or no system) and continue operating from. No "export penalty" state is ever introduced; no feature, plan-gate, or retention rule is ever changed as a consequence of a seller exporting. The exported artifact is sufficient to reconstruct the seller's KB bodies externally; it is NOT a pitch deck for Sourcera's paid features — it is a complete copy of what the seller wrote.

2. **On-Platform Compounding.** The KB becomes materially more valuable inside Sourcera than anywhere else because Sourcera-side features (confidence scores from acceptance rates, staleness from the §22.5 Health Model, win-rate weighting from closed-bid outcomes, cross-bid citation graph, KB-to-Capability auto-declarations) are computed and maintained against the live corpus of Sourcera bids. These features travel out of Sourcera as **text** (the exported manifest records confidence scores and win-rate weights as snapshots) but do **not** continue to update outside the platform. The compounding stays behind. Stake is built because staying on Sourcera keeps the compounding live; leaving does not destroy the seller's work but does freeze it.

**Operationalization.** The two contracts are enforced in the product surface and the codebase by four invariants (each is a §22.18.7 acceptance criterion):

- **Invariant P1 (No-Paywall Export).** No plan-gate, entitlement check, `FeatureAccessMatrix` row, or `PlanTier` condition may block `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/kb/export` (§32.9) for any seller Org on any plan tier, including Free. An abuse-scope rate limit (§22.18.2) is permitted; a revenue-gated restriction is not.
- **Invariant P2 (Feature-Coupled Compounding).** Every on-platform compounding feature (§22.18.3) computes exclusively against live Sourcera state — the `KBEntry.confidence_score` pipeline (§22.4.1), the `kb.entry.flagged_stale` health transitions (§22.5), the closed-bid outcome join (§13.1 / §13.3 of Seller Pricing Strategy), the `KBCitationGraph` materialization (§22.18.3.4), and the KB-to-Capability auto-declaration pipeline (§22.18.3.5). None of these features operate on exported snapshots; none can be subscribed to via external API.
- **Invariant P3 (Export Does Not Degrade).** No code path may mutate `KBEntry`, `KBNamespace`, `KBDocument`, `confidence_score`, `KBCitationGraph`, or any §22 / §22.18 entity as a side effect of an export. Export is a read. A `§40 PostHog audit` of the seller's KB state one minute before and one minute after an export MUST be byte-identical; a `kb_export_mutation_firewall` deploy-time validator asserts.
- **Invariant P4 (Carry-Over Surfaces Honesty).** Every upgrade and downgrade confirmation surface cites the Carry-Over Guarantee (§34.19 and §22.18.5) with plain-language copy that enumerates what is preserved and — on downgrade — what goes read-only and for how long. Marketing copy that softens the downgrade ("Everything will be fine!") is explicitly banned by §34.19.4 and §22.18.5; a UX fixture test asserts.

**Platform-principle registration (see §50 for platform-level principle registration).** The "Honest Portability; On-Platform Compounding" principle is not a §22-local rule — it is a platform-level product principle. The principle statement, its two contracts, Invariants P1–P4, and the list of on-platform compounding features that enforce it are registered in the §50 Platform Principles Registry as principle `principle_honest_portability_on_platform_compounding` with authoritative body living here at §22.18.1 and cross-referenced by every platform surface that touches export, entitlement-on-downgrade, or compounding-feature exposure. Any platform-level change that would conflict with the principle (a new plan gate on export, a new paid API that exposes a compounding feature, a UX pattern that implies leaving the platform will destroy the seller's work) MUST be surfaced as a §50 principle-conflict review before merge; the `platform_principle_conflict_review` CI gate (§50) asserts pre-merge. §50 defines the registration schema, the conflict-review process, the `principle_id → authoritative_section` index, and the quarterly principle-audit cadence; §22.18.1 defines the principle itself and is treated as authoritative for all four invariants.

**What §22.18 is NOT.** §22.18 is not a pricing surface; §22.18 does not modify plan-tier definitions (§34.1), entitlement mappings (§5.11), or AIOperation pricing (§34.8). §22.18 is not a new cross-console surface; every entity and endpoint introduced is Seller-console-scoped. §22.18 does not supersede §34.19's thirteen Protected Asset Classes — it references them by pointer. §22.18 does not introduce new retention rules; the KB retention schedule in §40.2 (`kb_entry_soft_deleted`) and the §6.8 DSAR path apply unchanged.

### 22.18.2 Honest Portability — Full Export Specification {#22.18.2-honest-portability-export-specification}

Honest Portability is implemented as a single async export endpoint (`GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/kb/export`, §32.9), an export-job entity (`KBExportJob`, canonical field table at §4.4.30), a downloadable archive artifact (`KBExportArchive`, §22.18.2.2), a provenance log (`KBExportProvenanceLog`, §22.18.2.3), and a webhook (`kb.export.ready`, Appendix C). This subsection specifies each component, the archive's on-disk layout, the rate-limit envelope, and the §6.8 DSAR / Right-to-Erasure interaction.

#### 22.18.2.1 KBExportJob Entity {#22.18.2.1-kb-export-job-entity}

**Canonical data-model home.** The field table, scope isolation, required indexes, retention, residency, and core acceptance criteria for `KBExportJob` are canonical at §4.4.30. The table below is retained as the §22 export-endpoint projection and MUST NOT contradict §4.4.30; schema changes land in §4.4.30 first.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Stable; externally referenced as `export_id` in endpoint I/O. |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization; NOT NULL | Seller Org scope; cross-Org reads return HTTP 404 `kb_export_job_not_found` per non-leak convention. |
| `console` | Enum | `console = 'seller'` ONLY | `'buyer'` writes return HTTP 422 `kb_export_console_forbidden`. Buyer consoles have no KB surface (§8 buyer-side scope). |
| `namespace_filter` | Enum | `all` \| `org_only` \| `software_only` \| `per_namespace_id` | Default `all`. `per_namespace_id` requires `namespace_ids[]`. |
| `namespace_ids` | Array\[UUID\] | ≤ 50 namespace_ids | FK → KBNamespace rows owned by `org_id`. Rejected if any id is cross-Org (HTTP 422 `kb_export_namespace_cross_org`). |
| `include_archived` | Boolean | Default `false` | When `true`, exported archive includes entries with `lifecycle_state='archived'` (preserves forensic reconstruction). |
| `include_drafts` | Boolean | Default `false` | When `true`, `lifecycle_state='draft'` / `under_review` entries included; relevant for seller who wishes to export in-flight review backlog. |
| `format` | Enum | `markdown_zip_v1` \| `jsonl_zip_v1` \| `markdown_and_jsonl_zip_v1`; default `markdown_and_jsonl_zip_v1` | Appendix J `kb_export_format_kind_enum`. Seller-console UX defaults to `markdown_and_jsonl_zip_v1` to cover both human-readable and machine-readable consumers. |
| `status` | Enum | `queued` \| `running` \| `ready` \| `expired` \| `failed` | State machine in §22.18.2.5. |
| `requested_by` | UUID (FK) | FK → User; NOT NULL | Seller user who initiated the export; MUST belong to `org_id`. |
| `requested_at` | Timestamp | NOT NULL | Server clock at API receipt. |
| `started_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Populated on `queued → running`. |
| `completed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Populated on `running → ready` or `running → failed`. |
| `ready_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Alias of `completed_at` when terminal state is `ready`; convenience for reporting. |
| `expires_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set on `ready`; `ready_at + 72h`. On reach, status transitions to `expired` and the presigned URL is revoked. |
| `archive_size_bytes` | Integer | Nullable | Populated on `ready`; bytes of the produced archive. |
| `archive_entry_count` | Integer | Nullable | Populated on `ready`; count of exported `KBEntry` rows. |
| `archive_document_count` | Integer | Nullable | Populated on `ready`; count of exported `KBDocument` rows. |
| `archive_attachment_bytes` | Integer | Nullable | Populated on `ready`; bytes under `/attachments/` inside the archive. |
| `archive_sha256` | String (64) | Nullable | Populated on `ready`; hex-encoded SHA-256 of the archive file. Rendered to the seller for integrity verification. |
| `download_url` | String | Nullable | Presigned URL (S3 path-style, 15-minute TTL, single-IP-bound per §33.9); re-mintable up to three times before `expires_at`. |
| `residency_region` | Enum | Appendix J `data_residency_region`: `us` \| `eu` \| `apac` \| `custom` | Derived from the seller Org's `data_residency_region` at `requested_at`; the archive is produced and stored in the same region. Cross-region mint attempts return HTTP 409 `kb_export_residency_mismatch`. |
| `failure_code` | Enum (Appendix J `kb_export_failure_code_enum` — new) | Nullable | Populated on `running → failed`; values: `timeout`, `archive_size_exceeded`, `vector_source_unreadable`, `provenance_source_unreadable`, `residency_evacuation`, `org_suspended`, `internal_error`. |
| `failure_detail` | String (≤ 2048) | Nullable | Human-readable failure context; surfaced to the seller. |
| `dsar_hold_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Populated when a concurrent §6.8 DSAR enters `in_progress`; job pauses pending DSAR completion per §22.18.2.6. |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | NOT NULL | Row creation time; alias of `requested_at`. |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | NOT NULL | Last write time. |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | FK → User | Alias of `requested_by`. |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | FK → User \| System | System updates write `updated_by = system_agent_kb_exporter` (an internal service identity, Appendix J `system_agent_id_enum` extension — flagged as Authored Extension). |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft-delete timestamp; rows are retained for §40.2 `kb_export_job` retention tier (authored extension — 90-day retention for completed / failed / expired jobs, 13-month retention for ready jobs whose audit trail is referenced in a contest or DSAR). |

**Scope isolation.** Org-scoped; per-row read/write gated on `requested_by.org_id = org_id`. Cross-Org reads return HTTP 404. Cross-console writes (i.e., buyer-console attempt) return HTTP 422.

**Required indexes.**

- `(org_id, created_at DESC)` — seller-console job list rendering.
- `(org_id, status)` — in-progress job guard (§22.18.2.4 rate-limit enforcement).
- `(status, expires_at)` — nightly expiry sweeper.
- `(dsar_hold_at)` partial — DSAR-paused job sweep.

**Retention.** 90 days for jobs with `status ∈ {failed, expired}`; 13 months for jobs with `status = ready` (aligns with §40.2 billing-audit retention tier so the artifact can be referenced in an Ops contest). Registered as `kb_export_job` in §40.2 Retention Schedule — Authored Extension; flagged in RECONCILIATION.md.

**DSAR interaction.** A seller-originated §6.8 DSAR Right-to-Erasure request on the seller's own Org triggers a sweep: every `status IN {queued, running}` KBExportJob for that Org has `dsar_hold_at` stamped; jobs in terminal state (`ready`, `expired`, `failed`) are left untouched but the Org's `KBExportJob.rows.deleted_at` is populated and the archive file itself is deleted atomically with the KB purge. Reason: the export archive is a derivative of the KB corpus; it inherits the erasure fate of the corpus. Cross-Org DSARs (for buyer users referenced in KB attachments) follow §6.8's partial-redaction path — the archive's provenance log is regenerated without the erased buyer's identifiers. See §22.18.2.6 for the DSAR state diagram.

**Residency.** Archives are produced in the seller Org's `data_residency_region` and stored in the region-local S3 partition. A seller Org mid-residency-evacuation (residency change) pauses in-flight KB exports and resumes them in the new region once evacuation completes; the job `status` stays in `running` while `residency_region` is rewritten atomically with the KB corpus migration.

#### 22.18.2.2 KBExportArchive Layout {#22.18.2.2-kb-export-archive-layout}

The archive is a ZIP file (DEFLATE compression) with the following deterministic layout. The layout is versioned; the `format` enum (§22.18.2.1) binds the version. Versions are never breaking-changed in place; a new enum value is introduced (e.g., `markdown_zip_v2`) for any layout change.

```
kb_export_<org_id>_<export_id>_<format>_<ready_at_iso8601_basic>.zip
├── manifest.json                      // Top-level index (see §22.18.2.2.1)
├── schema/
│   ├── kb_entry.schema.json           // JSON Schema (draft-07) for KBEntry export shape
│   ├── kb_document.schema.json
│   ├── kb_namespace.schema.json
│   └── export_metadata.schema.json    // Schema for manifest.json itself
├── entries/
│   ├── <namespace_slug>/
│   │   └── <kb_entry_id>.md           // Markdown body; YAML front-matter carries metadata
│   └── _metadata.jsonl                // One line per entry: full KBEntry JSON per schema/kb_entry.schema.json
├── documents/
│   ├── <kb_document_id>/
│   │   ├── original.<ext>             // Binary; original uploaded file preserved
│   │   └── manifest.json              // Parsed metadata, extracted text, attachment list
│   └── _index.jsonl                   // One line per document
├── namespaces/
│   └── _index.jsonl                   // One line per namespace (id, kind, slug, former_kb_namespace_ids[])
├── attachments/
│   └── <attachment_id>_<original_filename>  // Preserved filenames, de-duped by (kb_entry_id, attachment_sha256)
├── provenance/
│   └── provenance.jsonl               // Per-entry provenance log (see §22.18.2.3)
└── README.md                          // Plain-language instructions for reading the archive outside Sourcera
```

**manifest.json contract (top-level envelope).**

```json
{
  "export_format_version": "markdown_and_jsonl_zip_v1",
  "export_id": "kbx_7f2a1c3d",
  "org_id": "org_c2b9fe11",
  "org_display_name": "Acme Analytics, Inc.",
  "requested_by_user_id": "usr_0f3a22b0",
  "requested_at": "2026-04-20T17:12:00Z",
  "ready_at": "2026-04-20T17:14:38Z",
  "residency_region": "us",
  "namespace_filter": "all",
  "namespace_ids": [],
  "include_archived": false,
  "include_drafts": false,
  "archive_sha256": "b8e4…",
  "counts": {
    "namespaces": 4,
    "kb_entries": 147,
    "kb_documents": 31,
    "attachments": 54,
    "provenance_rows": 147
  },
  "schema_versions": {
    "kb_entry": "1.0",
    "kb_document": "1.0",
    "kb_namespace": "1.0",
    "export_metadata": "1.0"
  },
  "documentation_url": "https://docs.sourcera.com/kb/export/v1"
}
```

**Design notes (archive).**

- **Markdown is the primary body format.** Markdown is human-editable and git-friendly and carries YAML front-matter for metadata. The `_metadata.jsonl` shadow file preserves machine-readable metadata without polluting the body.
- **JSON Schema is exported in-archive.** The schema files are the canonical machine contract; they are documented publicly at `https://docs.sourcera.com/kb/export/v1` and are semver-stable within a major version.
- **Attachments preserve original filenames.** De-duplication uses `(kb_entry_id, attachment_sha256)` so the same PDF cited from two entries appears once physically but is referenced twice in manifest rows.
- **Provenance is a first-class sub-archive.** Every KBEntry ingested via Firecrawl (§22.6) or a first-party upload (§22.7) contributes a row to `provenance/provenance.jsonl` with source URL, crawl timestamp, agent version, and edit history (§22.4). This is the artifact the seller cites externally when they need to prove how an entry came to be.
- **README.md is plain language.** Written for a seller reading the archive outside Sourcera: what each folder contains, how to cross-reference, and how to re-import into another system.

#### 22.18.2.3 KBExportProvenanceLog (intra-archive file) {#22.18.2.3-kb-export-provenance-log}

Per-entry provenance is written as NDJSON (one row per line) inside `provenance/provenance.jsonl`. Each row carries:

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `kb_entry_id` | UUID | FK to entry. |
| `namespace_id` | UUID | FK to namespace. |
| `created_via` | Enum | `firecrawl` \| `manual_upload` \| `kb_bootstrap` \| `ghost_rfp_ingestion` \| `bid_close_offer` \| `custom_import` |
| `origin_url` | String (nullable) | Populated for `firecrawl` and `custom_import` sources. |
| `first_crawl_at` | Timestamp (nullable) | For Firecrawl sources; ISO 8601 UTC. |
| `last_crawl_at` | Timestamp (nullable) | For Firecrawl sources; last refresh. |
| `source_agent_id` | String (nullable) | For agent-originated drafts; e.g., `agent_sourcera_kb_bootstrap`. |
| `source_agent_version` | String (nullable) | Model version / capability version pair. |
| `edit_history_summary` | String (≤ 2048) | Concise summary of edit events — "created by bootstrap, 3 seller edits, 1 re-crawl refresh, currently active." |
| `edit_event_count` | Integer | Count of edit events since creation. |
| `confidence_score_snapshot` | Number (0.0–1.0) | Snapshot of `KBEntry.confidence_score` at export. Authoritative only as-of `export_id.ready_at`. |
| `win_rate_weight_snapshot` | Number (nullable) | Snapshot of §22.18.3.3 weighting at export. |
| `citation_count_snapshot` | Integer | Snapshot of per-entry citations across closed bids (§22.18.3.4). |
| `staleness_state_snapshot` | Enum | Snapshot of §22.5 Health Model state. |
| `attachment_ids` | Array\[UUID\] | References into `/attachments/` sub-folder. |

**Design note.** Provenance rows are **snapshots**, not live feeds. The seller can read them outside Sourcera to understand where an entry came from; the seller cannot update them outside Sourcera (on-platform compounding invariant — §22.18.1 P2).

#### 22.18.2.4 Rate-Limit Envelope {#22.18.2.4-rate-limit-envelope}

Honest Portability is never paywalled, but it IS rate-limited to prevent abuse (bot scraping, cost-amplification attacks, and inadvertent self-DDoS via scripted re-exports). The envelope is:

| Rate-limit class | Seller Org limit | Burst | Token-bucket refill |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `kb_export_request` | 10 export initiations / hour / Org | 15 | 10/hour steady-state |
| `kb_export_download` | 30 download-URL mints / hour / Org | 50 | 30/hour steady-state |
| `kb_export_concurrency` | 2 concurrent `status ∈ {queued, running}` jobs / Org | n/a | n/a |

**Enforcement.** Per Appendix I, `kb_export_rate_limit_exceeded` (HTTP 429) with `Retry-After` set to the earliest expiring token. `kb_export_concurrency_exceeded` (HTTP 409) when the second concurrent job would exceed the cap; the seller is told which job is in-flight. The limits are configured in §44.4 rate-limit policy and are globally override-able by `ops_growth_admin` for a specific Org in a dispute (requires an `OpsActionRecord` audit row).

**Why this is not a paywall.** The envelope is permissive enough for daily operational use (a seller may export ≤ 240 times per day per Org); it is tight enough that a scripted adversary cannot exhaust a region's S3 bandwidth in under a minute. No plan-tier gates the envelope (Free, Starter, Growth, Scale, Enterprise are all identical at this rate). An `ops_growth_admin` override is the only path to a higher limit, and every override is audit-logged and flagged in the daily Ops dashboard.

#### 22.18.2.5 KBExportJob State Machine {#22.18.2.5-kb-export-job-state-machine}

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (none) | `queued` | `POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/kb/export` request accepted | Rate-limit not exhausted; concurrency ≤ cap | Job row written; `requested_at` stamped. |
| `queued` | `running` | Worker pulls job from queue | Capacity available in region | `started_at` stamped. |
| `queued` | `failed` | Org suspended / evacuated / DSAR enters erase | `failure_code = org_suspended \| residency_evacuation` | Terminal; `failure_detail` populated. |
| `running` | `ready` | Archive produced, SHA-256 computed, S3 upload complete | No residency / integrity errors | `completed_at = ready_at` stamped; `download_url` minted; `expires_at = ready_at + 72h`. Webhook `kb.export.ready` emitted. |
| `running` | `failed` | Any archive-production error | `failure_code` populated | `completed_at` stamped. |
| `running` | `queued` | DSAR `in_progress` intersects the job's namespace set | `dsar_hold_at` stamped | Pause; job resumes after DSAR completes per §22.18.2.6. |
| `ready` | `expired` | Wall-clock reaches `expires_at` | — | Presigned URL revoked; archive file remains in S3 until §40.2 retention expiry (13 months for audit continuity). |
| `expired` | (terminal) | — | — | Seller may initiate a new export; no automatic re-mint path. |
| `failed` | (terminal) | — | — | Seller may retry; retry is a fresh job (new `export_id`). |

**Invariant.** A `ready` job's `download_url` may be re-minted by the seller up to three times before `expires_at` (the presigned URL TTL is 15 minutes per §33.9; re-minting re-creates the signed URL without re-producing the archive). A fourth re-mint attempt returns HTTP 429 `kb_export_download_remints_exhausted`. The three-mint ceiling is a §22.18.7 acceptance criterion.

#### 22.18.2.6 DSAR / Right-to-Erasure Interaction {#22.18.2.6-dsar-interaction}

**Seller-originated DSAR (seller's own Org).** When a seller Org's own users file a §6.8 Right-to-Erasure request targeting the Org, every in-flight KBExportJob (`status IN {queued, running}`) has `dsar_hold_at` stamped and the job pauses. After DSAR completion (the KB corpus is purged per §6.8), the paused jobs are re-evaluated; if any target `KBEntry` rows are erased, the job transitions to `failed` with `failure_code = residency_evacuation` (reused for DSAR-driven archive invalidation) and the seller is notified via `kb.session.terminated` semantics (Appendix C) extended with `failure_reason = 'dsar_erasure_invalidated_export'`. The seller may initiate a new export post-DSAR.

**Cross-Org DSAR (buyer user's erasure affects seller's KB).** When a buyer-side user files a §6.8 Right-to-Erasure request for their personal data referenced in a seller's KB (e.g., a buyer's name appears in a KB entry citing a prior RFP), §6.8 performs a partial redaction pass on the affected entries. Existing `ready` and `expired` KBExportArchives are **not** retroactively rewritten (archives are snapshots); however, the archive's `provenance/provenance.jsonl` file is marked as **superseded** by a post-DSAR re-export. A nightly Ops dashboard surfaces archives whose corpus has been post-export-redacted so Ops can proactively notify affected sellers. The seller is not required to re-export; the artifact carries a snapshot timestamp that predates the redaction, which §6.8 treats as acceptable (snapshots are not ongoing processing).

**Design rule (invariant).** An export archive's residency, retention, DSAR, and residency-pinning rules follow the seller Org's master §40.2 retention tier; no export-specific override is introduced. §22.18 does not create new data classes with new retention rules; it reuses the existing KB retention and DSAR infrastructure.

### 22.18.3 On-Platform Compounding — Five Features {#22.18.3-on-platform-compounding-five-features}

The five on-platform compounding features are the engineered reason the KB is more valuable inside Sourcera than outside. Each feature is registered here with its data source, its computation cadence, its observable surface, and its export semantics (what traveling out of Sourcera as a snapshot looks like).

#### 22.18.3.1 Confidence Score from Acceptance Rates {#22.18.3.1-confidence-score-feature}

**Feature.** Every `KBEntry` carries a `confidence_score` (0.00 – 1.00) reflecting how often seller reviewers accept (vs. edit / reject) first-pass drafts that cite the entry, plus an initial prior from `kb_bootstrap` / `ghost_rfp_ingestion` confidence (§22.10.3 / §22.10.6).

**Data source.** `KBEntry.confidence_score` field (§22.3.1). `base_confidence` is the seed prior set at ingestion; `confidence_score` is the live compounding scalar; `confidence_modifier` is the derived retrieval multiplier and MUST NOT be used as the stored acceptance-rate source.

**Update rule.** On every first-pass response acceptance (`response.accepted_at` set; `response.cited_kb_entry_ids[] != null`), each cited entry's `confidence_score` is nudged up per a standard EMA (α = 0.05 for acceptance; α = -0.10 for rejection). An entry's confidence floor is 0.10 (never trends to zero while active); an entry's confidence ceiling is 0.99 (leaves headroom for evidence demotion). The EMA update rule is an Authored Extension; the canonical field is now declared in §22.3.1.

**Cadence.** Online at every acceptance / rejection event (sub-second). Reconciliation job nightly at 03:30 UTC recomputes from the `AIOperation` ledger as a consistency check.

**Observable surface.**

- Seller Console KB entry detail page renders the score prominently (§22.18.4 KB Value Meter panel also surfaces aggregate confidence).
- `kb_retrieve` (§22.8.4.1) returns `confidence_score` in every retrieved entry envelope so consuming agents can weight.
- Buyer-facing surfaces NEVER render per-entry confidence (KB privacy per §8); only the aggregate §34.19.2 buyer-facing scalar surfaces to buyers.

**Export semantics.** `confidence_score_snapshot` per §22.18.2.3 (ISO 8601 point-in-time). Snapshot does not update outside Sourcera.

**Cross-links.** §22.3.1 (KBEntry field table); §22.4 (Lifecycle); §22.8.4.1 (kb_retrieve tool); §22.18.4 (Seller Panel surface); §34.19.2 (buyer-facing scalar computation).

#### 22.18.3.2 Staleness State from the KB Health Model {#22.18.3.2-staleness-feature}

**Feature.** Every `KBEntry` carries a staleness state (`fresh` \| `review_due` \| `review_overdue` \| `flagged_stale`) driven by the §22.5 KB Health Model. The state gates retrieval (stale entries are excluded from `kb_retrieve` by default — §22.17 AC #26).

**Data source.** `KBEntry.status` (§22.3.1), surfaced in API payloads as `review_state` / `lifecycle_state` projection aliases for backward compatibility.

**Compounding mechanic.** The Health Model's transition triggers (time-since-last-publish, source-URL re-crawl deltas, acceptance-trend degradation) compute against the live seller corpus. An exported snapshot freezes the state at export time; it does not continue to update. A seller who exports and operates externally will find that week-old "fresh" snapshots progressively lose relevance to buyers who receive stale drafts — but the seller cannot see this degradation on the external artifact; they see only the frozen `fresh` label.

**Observable surface.** Per-entry staleness badge in Seller Console; aggregate Health % in §22.18.4 Seller Panel; health dashboards in §22.5.

**Export semantics.** `staleness_state_snapshot` per §22.18.2.3. Snapshot at export.

**Cross-links.** §22.5 (Health Model entity + transitions); §22.17 AC #26 (retrieval exclusion default); §22.18.4 (Seller Panel aggregate Health %).

#### 22.18.3.3 Win-Rate Weighting from Closed-Bid Outcomes {#22.18.3.3-win-rate-weight-feature}

**Feature.** Every `KBEntry` carries a `win_rate_weight` (0.0 – 1.0, centered at 0.5) learned from closed-bid outcomes: entries cited in won bids drift toward 1.0, entries cited in lost bids drift toward 0.0, entries never cited in closed bids remain at 0.5. The weight is a force multiplier on `confidence_score` at retrieval time (weighted scoring in §22.9 retrieval engineering).

**Data source.** `KBEntry.win_rate_weight` field (§22.3.1). The field is the canonical closed-bid outcome scalar consumed by §22.5 and §22.9.1 Stage 6.

**Update rule.** Join `AIOperation.child_operations[]` (first-pass response operations) to `Bid.outcome` (won / lost / no-decision) at bid close. For each cited KBEntry (`response.cited_kb_entry_ids[]`), nudge `win_rate_weight` toward the outcome with α = 0.08. Bids closing as `no-decision` or `cancelled` do not update the weight.

**Cadence.** Event-driven at bid close; reconciliation nightly at 04:00 UTC.

**Observable surface.** Seller Console KB entry detail page renders "Win-rate lift: +X%" when weight > 0.6 or < 0.4 and the entry has ≥ 5 citations (k-anonymity floor on the signal — prevents small-n whiplash). §22.18.4 Seller Panel surfaces aggregate "entries with win-rate lift" count.

**Export semantics.** `win_rate_weight_snapshot` per §22.18.2.3. Snapshot at export.

**Cross-links.** §22.9 (Retrieval Engineering); §13.1 / §13.3 of Seller Pricing Strategy (outcome signal model); §22.18.4 (Seller Panel rendering rules); §48.1.7 (CM3 "47 buyers" parallel — does not share the cardinality floor).

#### 22.18.3.4 Cross-Bid Citation Graph {#22.18.3.4-citation-graph-feature}

**Feature.** The `KBCitationGraph` is a materialized view where nodes are KBEntries and edges are citation events from first-pass response operations, weighted by citing bid's status and time. Load-bearing entries (high in-degree, cited across many bids) emerge as graph hubs; orphan entries (zero in-degree) are candidates for archival. The graph drives several Seller Console surfaces (entry detail "cited in N bids," Seller Panel "N cited in closed bids," the §22.18.6 outcome-debrief stake-reveal).

**Data source.** `KBCitationGraphEdge` canonical entity (§4.4.31). The table below restates the §22 feature projection for readability; schema changes land in §4.4.31 first.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK | |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | NOT NULL | Org scope. |
| `console` | Enum | `seller` | Seller-only. |
| `from_kb_entry_id` | UUID (FK) | NOT NULL | Cited entry (the entry providing evidence). |
| `to_bid_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | NOT NULL | Bid Workspace the citation lands in; canonical field name at §4.4.31. |
| `response_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable | FK to `BidResponse` (§4.4.2) or bridged `Response` (§4.3.5), depending on citation origin. |
| `response_id_fallback` | UUID (FK) | Nullable | FK to `Response` rows when denormalization is inapplicable (pre-bid seed citations). |
| `citation_kind` | Enum | `response_grounding` \| `evidence_attribution` \| `capability_extraction` | Drives weight assignment. |
| `bid_outcome` | Enum | `open` \| `won` \| `lost` \| `no_decision` \| `cancelled` | Snapshot at edge creation; updated at bid close. |
| `edge_weight` | Number (0.0–1.0) | Computed | `response_grounding=1.0`, `evidence_attribution=0.8`, `capability_extraction=0.6`. |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | NOT NULL | Citation event time. |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | NOT NULL | Last write. |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User, managed-agent, or system identity | Usually the AIOperation actor that created the citation. |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User, managed-agent, or system identity | Outcome sync worker on bid close; system actor allowed. |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete mirrors the underlying `Response` soft delete. |

**Scope isolation.** Org-scoped; never surfaced to buyer-console. Required indexes: `(org_id, from_kb_entry_id)`, `(org_id, to_bid_workspace_id)`, `(org_id, bid_outcome, updated_at)`.

**Retention.** Mirrors `Response` retention (§40.2); edges are hard-deleted when both endpoints are hard-deleted.

**Compounding mechanic.** The graph is computed exclusively from live Sourcera responses and bid outcomes. Export produces a snapshot (`citation_count_snapshot` and, in the `jsonl` format, a per-entry adjacency list projection); the adjacency list is read-only external to Sourcera.

**Observable surface.** Seller Console KB entry detail page ("Cited in 12 bids · 4 won, 6 lost, 2 open"), Seller Panel aggregate ("6 cited in closed bids"), and the §22.18.6 outcome-debrief overlay ("Cited entries in this bid: 8 · wins ↑ 2").

**Cross-links.** §22.9 (Retrieval, which reads the graph for ranking); §22.18.3.3 (win-rate-weight is derived from the graph × bid outcome join); §22.18.6.2 (outcome-debrief surface).

#### 22.18.3.5 KB-to-Capability Auto-Declarations {#22.18.3.5-kb-to-capability-auto-declarations-feature}

**Solo / Free override (Phase 14.8 — see §22.20.2).** The review-and-claim path described below is the authoritative behavior for `plan_tier ∉ {seller_free, seller_solo}`. On Solo and Free seller plans, the §22.20.2 auto-publish-and-render-as-chips contract supersedes review-and-claim: the §4.4.4 state machine row 7a `(none) → published` direct transition fires under `pending_review_reason = solo_free_auto_publish` when the four §22.20.2 / §4.4.4 preconditions hold, and the resulting `CapabilityDeclaration` rows render as the discoverable-categories chip list described in §22.20.2 (with add / remove / rename affordances) rather than as a "Suggested Capability Claims" review queue. Engineers and QA implementing against this section MUST treat §22.20.2 as the binding contract for Solo / Free renders; the prose below describes paid-tier behavior. CI gate `seller_maya_chip_list_auto_publish_state_machine` (§M.5) asserts.

**Feature.** Clusters of KBEntries with overlapping `topic_tags` and high confidence trigger the suggestion of a `CapabilityDeclaration` (§4.4.4). The seller is prompted to promote the cluster to a claimed capability; the proposed declaration is pre-filled with evidence citations pulling from the cluster's KBEntries. Auto-declarations accelerate marketplace discoverability without human authoring.

**Data source.** `KBEntry.topic_tags[]` (§22.3.1) and a materialized clustering pipeline (nightly).

**Compounding mechanic.** The clustering pipeline reads every Org's KB corpus, computes cluster centroids, matches against the Capability Registry (§21.4), and emits `CapabilityDeclarationSuggestion` rows (canonical entity at §4.4.32; Authored Extension ratified by AE-V72REM-PH5P53-DM-01). The seller reviews and claims; the promoted declaration writes through §4.4.4 with `capability_type = taxonomy_declaration` and carries `evidence_kb_entry_ids[]` of at least three KBEntries per §22.14.3.

**Cadence.** Nightly at 02:30 UTC.

**Observable surface.** Seller Console "Suggested Capability Claims" tab in the Capability workspace; Seller Panel "Capability coverage: 5 claimed · 3 suggested" surface.

**Export semantics.** The raw topic_tags are exported (they are seller-authored); the clustering pipeline's suggestions are NOT exported (they are on-platform derivative output; the seller can inspect suggestions while in Sourcera but cannot run the clusterer externally).

**Cross-links.** §4.4.4 (CapabilityDeclaration entity); §22.14.3 (evidence-overlap rule); §21.4 (Capability Registry); §48.3.5 S7 loop (inventory growth).

### 22.18.4 KB Value Meter — Seller Panel {#22.18.4-kb-value-meter-seller-panel}

**Purpose.** A persistent panel on the Seller Console KB landing screen that expresses the KB's accrued value in plain English. The panel is the seller's running receipt of stake accrual — it renders the outputs of the §22.18.3 compounding features as numbers and short narrative copy, with click-through explanations and source-entry drill-downs.

**Note on naming.** This panel is *the* KB Value Meter referenced in Summary §6.13.7. It is distinct from the `0.00–1.00` buyer-facing scalar defined in §34.19.2 (also named "KB Value Meter" in that subsection). To avoid terminology drift, this section refers to **"KB Value Meter — Seller Panel."** The scalar is an input to the Panel (it renders as one of several numbers); the Panel is NOT a rename of the scalar.

#### 22.18.4.1 Panel Rendering Contract {#22.18.4.1-panel-rendering-contract}

The panel renders on the KB landing screen above the entries list. It is visible on **every plan tier, including Free**. The panel renders five values in a fixed layout, with plain-language labels and click-through affordances:

| Position | Label | Value Shape | Source | Click-Through |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | "Entries" | Integer | `COUNT(KBEntry WHERE org_id = … AND lifecycle_state = 'active')` | Filter KB list to active entries. |
| 2 | "Cited in closed bids" | Integer | `COUNT(DISTINCT from_kb_entry_id) FROM KBCitationGraphEdge WHERE org_id = … AND bid_outcome IN {won, lost}` | Filter KB list to entries with ≥ 1 closed-bid citation. |
| 3 | "With win-rate lift" | Integer | `COUNT(KBEntry WHERE org_id = … AND win_rate_weight > 0.6 AND citation_count ≥ 5)` | Filter KB list to win-rate-lift entries; drill-down to per-entry trend chart. |
| 4 | "Estimated value" | Currency-display string (e.g., "$1,275/yr saved response time") | Plain-English formula: `entries × blended_draft_time_saved_min/entry × blended_seller_hourly_rate_cents / 6000` (annualized); `blended_draft_time_saved_min_per_entry` default 18, `blended_seller_hourly_rate_cents` default 8500 (= $85/hr), both configurable by the seller under Settings → KB Economics | Drill to "How this is calculated" explainer surface. |
| 5 | "Health" | Percent string (e.g., "94%") | `COUNT(KBEntry WHERE status = 'active') / COUNT(KBEntry WHERE deleted_at IS NULL)` with API projection aliases allowed for `review_state` / `lifecycle_state` | Drill to KB Health dashboard (§22.5.3). |

**Example render (inline on the KB landing screen).**

> *"Your KB: 47 entries · 6 cited in closed bids · 2 with win-rate lift · Estimated value: $1,275/yr saved response time · Health: 94%."*

**Cadence.** Nightly recompute at 03:30 UTC (same window as §34.19.2 buyer-facing scalar so the two numbers are temporally aligned). A "Last updated: {time_ago}" caption renders beneath the panel.

**Plan-tier visibility.** **Identical across all tiers**, including Free. The panel is deliberately not upsell-gated. However, **two plan-aware chips** render next to positions 2 and 4 for Free-tier sellers only:

- *"Upgrade Carry-Over applies"* chip on position 2 (the cited-in-closed-bids count). Click opens the Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee summary (§22.18.5).
- *"See how citations compound on Starter"* link on position 4 (the estimated-value number). Click opens a non-modal explainer card (NOT an upgrade modal — strict AP2 compliance per §48.8.7). The explainer describes how the estimated-value number increases as citations accrue.

**First-run empty state.** When `COUNT(KBEntry) = 0` (a brand-new Seller Org with no bootstrap), the panel renders:

> *"Your KB is empty. Import a few entries or run KB Bootstrap (§22.10.3 / C.46) to start building stake."*

with a CTA to `/seller/kb/bootstrap`. The panel does NOT disappear for empty KBs; the seller should see the surface from day one.

**Anti-pattern prevention.** The panel MUST NOT render an upgrade CTA for the Pro plan, Starter, Growth, or Scale. A UX fixture snapshot test asserts. Attempting to render such a CTA fails CI per §48.8.7 AP1.

#### 22.18.4.2 Click-Through Explainers {#22.18.4.2-click-through-explainers}

Every number on the panel is clickable; clicks open a non-modal drawer with the source-entry breakdown. The drawer lists the entries driving the number, with direct links to each entry's detail page. The drawer is read-only; the seller can navigate into entries to edit. The drawer for **position 4 (Estimated value)** shows the two configurable variables (`blended_draft_time_saved_min_per_entry` and `blended_seller_hourly_rate_cents`) and allows inline edits that re-run the estimate live — this is the plain-English "receipt" promised by the Summary.

#### 22.18.4.3 PostHog Telemetry {#22.18.4.3-panel-telemetry}

Two events are emitted:

- `kb_value_meter_viewed {seller_org_id, plan_tier, panel_position_count=5, entries_rendered, cited_in_closed_bids_rendered, with_win_rate_lift_rendered, estimated_value_display, health_percent_rendered, viewer_user_id, viewer_role}` — fires once per seller session on the KB landing screen render.
- `kb_value_meter_click_through {seller_org_id, position ∈ {entries, cited_in_closed_bids, with_win_rate_lift, estimated_value, health}, drawer_rendered=true, drill_down_target}` — fires on any panel number click.

Both are registered in Appendix G.

### 22.18.5 Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee — §22 Side of the Surface {#22.18.5-upgrade-carry-over-guarantee-kb-side}

**Cross-link authority.** §34.19 is the authoritative plan-tier carry-over guarantee spec (thirteen Protected Asset Classes, transition-specific behaviors, honest-portability microcopy, export/DSAR interaction, failure modes, acceptance criteria). §22.18.5 is the KB-side surface — the specific guarantees, confirmation copy, and UX surfaces the seller sees when the carry-over applies to their KB. §34.19 and §22.18.5 are consistent; conflicts are resolved in favor of §34.19.

**What §22.18.5 adds.** §22.18.5 enumerates the KB-specific assets that carry over (a subset of §34.19.1's thirteen classes), the seller-facing confirmation copy rendered at the upgrade moment, the downgrade surface rendered at the downgrade moment, and the cross-link to the upgrade surfaces that embed this guarantee (§48.1.7 / §48.8.6 conversion-moment modals).

#### 22.18.5.1 KB Assets Carried Over on Upgrade {#22.18.5.1-kb-assets-carried-over}

Per §34.19.1 / §34.19.1.A, the following subset relates to KB assets and is preserved on any upgrade transition. §22.18.5 calls them out for the KB workspace surface; the class/sub-class column cites §34.19.1.A and does not create an independent mapping.

| Asset | §34.19.1.A class / sub-class | Carry-over behavior | KB workspace observable |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| KBEntry rows (all fields) | Class 1 / 1a | 100% retained, read-write | Entry count and contents are unchanged before / after upgrade. |
| KBNamespace rows | Class 1 / 1b | 100% retained | Namespaces visible in unchanged order. |
| KBDocument rows & attachments | Class 1 / 1c | 100% retained | Document library unchanged. |
| `KBEntry.confidence_score` | Class 2 / 2b | 100% retained | Confidence scores unchanged across upgrade. |
| `KBEntry.status` (staleness / review-state projection) | Class 2 / 2c | 100% retained | Staleness badges unchanged; API aliases `review_state` / `lifecycle_state` project from the same column. |
| `KBEntry.win_rate_weight` | Class 2 / 2d | 100% retained | Win-rate-lift indicators unchanged. |
| KBCitationGraphEdge rows | Class 6 / 6b | 100% retained | Cross-bid citation counts unchanged. |
| CapabilityDeclarationSuggestion rows | Class 3 / 3b | 100% retained | Suggested-claim queue unchanged. |
| `KB_Value_Meter` scalar (§34.19.2) | Class 2 / 2a | 100% retained, recomputed per §34.19.2 | §22.18.4 Seller Panel number unchanged (recomputed ≤ 15 min post-upgrade). |
| KBExportJob rows | KB export audit proof row; not a separate §34.19.1 class | 100% retained per §22.18.2 / §40.2 unless DSAR invalidates the archive | Export history unchanged. |

#### 22.18.5.2 Upgrade Confirmation Copy {#22.18.5.2-upgrade-confirmation-copy}

When a Seller Org upgrades, the Seller Console confirmation surface renders a KB-scoped honest-portability block. The block is rendered BELOW the §34.19.4 generic carry-over summary (to preserve a single source of truth for the global summary at §34.19) and is scoped to the KB:

> *"Your KB moves with you. **47 entries** · **2 years of citation history** · **current confidence scores** · **win-rate weights** · **suggested capability claims** — all retained exactly. No re-bootstrap. No re-indexing. No fidelity loss."*

Variable substitutions (`47 entries`, `2 years`) bind to `COUNT(KBEntry)` and `DATE_DIFF(NOW, MIN(KBCitationGraphEdge.created_at), 'years')` at render time. If the Org's KB is empty (new signups), the block renders a fallback:

> *"When you build your KB, every entry — confidence scores, citations, staleness state, win-rate weights — moves with you on every future upgrade. You will never need to re-bootstrap."*

The generic carry-over CTA (from §34.19.4) links to the full §34.19.1 Protected-Asset table. The KB-scoped block renders no CTA (it is a statement, not an action).

#### 22.18.5.3 Downgrade Behavior {#22.18.5.3-downgrade-behavior}

Per §34.19.3, downgrades preserve KB data read-only for a preservation window. Two windows apply depending on the transition:

- **Starter → Free, Growth → Starter, Scale → Growth, etc.**: **90-day read-only** per §34.19.1 / §34.6. During the window, KB entries that exceed the new plan's entry-count cap (e.g., 50 entries on Free) go read-only but remain queryable (`kb_retrieve` returns them with a `readonly_mode = true` flag); the seller may archive or delete them to return to write-capable state. After 90 days, entries exceeding the cap transition to `preservation_status = hard_archived` per §34.6 DowngradeExcessDataBucket semantics (and per §34.19.6 Failure Mode #2, no Class-1 asset enters `hard_archived` unless the seller has signed a §34.6 acknowledgement).
- **Free-tier preservation of entries exceeding 50 cap**: Mirrors the 90-day read-only pattern; the Summary §6.13.7 narrative mentions "12 months" — the authoritative figure is **90 days** per §34.19 / §34.6. The 12-month figure in the Summary is superseded by the 90-day figure in the Master Spec and flagged as a conflict in RECONCILIATION.md under Known Conflicts; the seller-facing copy authoritatively cites 90 days.

**Downgrade confirmation copy.** The Seller Console downgrade confirmation surface renders a KB-scoped honest-portability block below §34.19.4's generic downgrade summary:

> *"Your KB stays. Entries over the new plan's cap go read-only for 90 days — still searchable, still exportable, just not editable until you archive some or re-upgrade. After 90 days, overflow entries are archived per our data retention schedule (§34.6)."*

### 22.18.6 Stake-Reveal Moments — Three Deliberate Surfaces {#22.18.6-stake-reveal-moments-three-surfaces}

Stake-reveal is a product pattern: at three deliberate moments, the seller is shown the compounding value they have accrued in the KB. No other moments are stake-reveals; the pattern is deliberately scarce so it reads as informative, not promotional. This subsection binds the three moments to the surfaces that render them.

The three stake-reveal moments (per Summary §6.13.7):

| # | Moment | Surface | Binding Section |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Free-tier KB landing Value Meter | §22.18.4 Seller Panel on the KB landing screen | §22.18.6.1 |
| 2 | Post-close outcome debrief overlay | Post-bid-close overlay within the Bid Workspace | §22.18.6.2 (new; Authored Extension) |
| 3 | Four-conversion-threshold upgrade previews | §48.1.7 CM1 / CM2 / CM3 / CM4 modals + §48.8.6 modal bodies | §22.18.6.3 |

Each moment emits the canonical `stake_reveal_rendered` event (Appendix G) with a new property `reveal_moment ∈ {free_tier_kb_landing, outcome_debrief, conversion_threshold}` — see §22.18.6.4.

#### 22.18.6.1 Moment 1 — Free-Tier KB Landing Value Meter {#22.18.6.1-moment-1-free-kb-landing}

**Surface.** §22.18.4 Seller Panel.

**Free-tier specificity.** The Seller Panel renders identically across plan tiers (per §22.18.4.1), but on the Free tier the `reveal_moment = free_tier_kb_landing` property is attached to the `stake_reveal_rendered` event; on paid tiers, the same panel fires `kb_value_meter_viewed` without the `stake_reveal_rendered` binding. The distinction is analytics-only (tier-specific cohort funnels) and does not change the UX rendering.

**Telemetry.** `stake_reveal_rendered {seller_org_id, session_id (nullable if not mid-session), reveal_moment = free_tier_kb_landing, kb_entry_count_on_reveal, cited_in_closed_bids_rendered, with_win_rate_lift_rendered, estimated_value_display, health_percent_rendered, plan_tier = 'seller_free', upgrade_cta_visible = false}`.

**Cross-link.** §22.18.4.3 (panel telemetry); §48.8.8 (telemetry registry).

#### 22.18.6.2 Moment 2 — Post-Close Outcome Debrief Overlay {#22.18.6.2-moment-2-outcome-debrief}

**Surface.** New Seller Console overlay rendered within the Bid Workspace when a bid transitions to `Bid.status IN {won, lost, no_decision}` AND the seller's user opens the Bid Workspace subsequently. The overlay renders once per bid-close per seller user (i.e., each teammate sees it once; subsequent renders are suppressed per user-Org pair with `BidWorkspace.outcome_debrief_seen_by_user_ids[]` tracking).

**Content.** The overlay shows:

- Outcome label ("You won this bid." / "You lost this bid.")
- Bid details (buyer Org display name, bid value if populated, close date).
- Cited KBEntries in responses for this bid — displayed as a list with per-entry badges: a green "↑" if the entry's win-rate weight nudged up as a result of this close, a red "↓" if it nudged down.
- Aggregate "KB Value delta from this bid: +{N} citations, +{M} win-rate-weight units" plain-language summary.
- A secondary "View your KB Value Meter" link that scrolls to the Seller Panel on the KB landing screen.
- **Zero upgrade CTAs.** The overlay is an informational stake reminder, NOT an upgrade surface. An upgrade modal opening on this surface is an §48.8.7 AP-2 anti-pattern violation; a UX fixture test asserts.

**Free-tier ceiling warning (inline).** If the seller is on Free and `COUNT(KBEntry) ≥ 45` (CM4 Free threshold approaching), a non-modal inline banner within the overlay reads: *"Your KB is 45 of 50 entries. Upgrade Carry-Over applies on every future upgrade."* with a quiet "Learn more" link (opens the Carry-Over explainer surface, NOT an upgrade modal). This is Not a Conversion Moment fire — CM4 fires from the KB workspace on a KB-write, not from the outcome-debrief overlay. The overlay's banner is purely informational and is frequency-capped to once per bid-close-per-seller-user.

**Data source.** `BidWorkspace` row; the overlay reads `KBCitationGraphEdge` rows where `to_bid_workspace_id = bid_workspace_id` AND joins to `KBEntry` for rendering.

**State-machine interaction.** Overlay rendering is idempotent per (bid_id, seller_user_id) pair via the `BidWorkspace.outcome_debrief_seen_by_user_ids[]` array; attempts to re-render after first render for the same user are suppressed.

**Telemetry.** `stake_reveal_rendered {seller_org_id, session_id (nullable), bid_workspace_id, reveal_moment = outcome_debrief, bid_outcome ∈ {won, lost, no_decision}, cited_entries_count, nudged_up_count, nudged_down_count, free_ceiling_warning_rendered ∈ {true, false}, upgrade_cta_visible = false}`.

**Cross-link.** Summary §6.16.4 (Summary outcome-debrief origin); §13.2 of Seller Pricing Strategy (outcome-debrief narrative); §48.8.6 (Four Seller Conversion Moments UX — the overlay is NOT a Conversion Moment surface and MUST NOT route to one).

#### 22.18.6.3 Moment 3 — Three Conversion-Threshold Upgrade Previews {#22.18.6.3-moment-3-conversion-thresholds}

**Surface.** The §48.1.7 CM1 / CM2 / CM3 / CM4 modals and the §48.8.6 modal body specifications.

**Stake-reveal responsibility.** Each of the four conversion-moment modals ALREADY renders the Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee summary per §48.1.7 and §48.8.6. §22.18.6.3 adds a §22-side requirement: the CM1, CM2, CM3, and CM4 modals MUST render a KB-scoped carry-over preview block beneath the generic summary, sourced from the §22.18.5 upgrade-confirmation-copy template and rendered with the seller's **current** KB statistics (entry count, citation count, win-rate-weight count). The block is identical in shape to §22.18.5.2 upgrade-confirmation copy; it is effectively a preview of what the seller will see after upgrade, rendered before upgrade as an anticipation moment.

**Implementation contract.** The §48.8.6 CM1 / CM2 / CM3 / CM4 modal body tables are EXTENDED to include a "KB Carry-Over Preview" row between the benefit list and the price display. The row renders the §22.18.5.2 block with live data. This is a **Master Spec internal coordination** — §48.8.6 is the authoritative surface for the CM1/CM2/CM3/CM4 modal body; §22.18.6.3 is the authoritative surface for the KB Carry-Over Preview row *within* those modal bodies. Conflicts are resolved in favor of §48.8.6 for modal shape and §22.18.6.3 for the KB content within the preview row.

**Telemetry.** Each of the four CM modals fires `stake_reveal_rendered {seller_org_id, session_id, reveal_moment = conversion_threshold, conversion_moment_kind ∈ {cm1_mid_bid_ai_budget_wall, cm2_second_concurrent_bid, cm3_first_eoi, cm4_kb_ceiling}, kb_entry_count_on_reveal, cited_in_closed_bids_rendered, with_win_rate_lift_rendered, upgrade_cta_visible = true}` at modal render. (Note: `upgrade_cta_visible = true` on CM modals — these modals ARE upgrade surfaces, per §48.1.7; the CM modal's stake-reveal role is preview-of-preservation, not stake-for-its-own-sake.)

**Cross-link.** §48.1.7 (Four Seller Conversion Moments Master Spec Binding); §48.8.6 (Four Seller Conversion Moments UX Surface Specification); §22.18.5.2 (upgrade-confirmation-copy template).

#### 22.18.6.4 Telemetry: the `reveal_moment` property {#22.18.6.4-reveal-moment-property}

The canonical event `stake_reveal_rendered` (Appendix G) is **extended** with a new property `reveal_moment ∈ {free_tier_kb_landing, outcome_debrief, conversion_threshold}` (Appendix J `kb_stake_reveal_moment_enum` — new). The extension is **additive and backward-compatible** — existing `stake_reveal_rendered` emitters continue to emit the event unchanged; new §22.18 emitters populate `reveal_moment`. Consumers without property awareness see the existing Phase-4 Post-Submission Reveal event shape (§48.8.5); consumers with property awareness can partition analytics by moment.

The legacy `stake_reveal_displayed` event (dual-emit per §48 Appendix G) is **also** extended with `reveal_moment` during the v7.0.x dual-emit window; at v7.1.0 the legacy alias retires and only `stake_reveal_rendered` carries `reveal_moment`.

A new event `kb_export_initiated {seller_org_id, export_id, format ∈ {markdown_zip_v1, jsonl_zip_v1, markdown_and_jsonl_zip_v1}, namespace_filter, include_archived, include_drafts, rate_limit_tokens_remaining}` is registered in Appendix G to observe export usage patterns (bot-scraping detection, rate-limit calibration, `honest_portability` adoption tracking).

**Audit event.** The companion audit ledger row `org.kb_exported` is written to the §6.7 audit ledger for every `kb.export.ready` webhook emission, registering `{export_id, requested_by_user_id, format, entry_count, bytes}`. Audit action enum registered in Appendix J.

#### 22.18.6.5 Bid Disqualification Cascade — Stake-Reveal & Outcome-Debrief Invalidation {#22.18.6.5-bid-disqualification-cascade}

**Authored Extension v7.1.0 → v7.1.1 — V5 D-5V-005 remediation 2026-05-06.** Closes the silent edge case surfaced by V5 adversarial seller-journey walk: when a buyer disqualifies a vendor mid-Stake-Reveal (Stage 6) or post-Win-Debrief render (Stage 7), §49.1.6 / §49.1.7 / §22.18.6 were previously silent on how `stake_reveal_rendered_at`, `outcome_debrief_seen_by_user_ids[]`, and the Activation-Metric write invalidate.

**Trigger.** Buyer-side disqualification cascade per §10.7 (Phase-9 buyer clarifications) or §25.3 (cross-console disqualification cascade) emits the `bid.disqualified` webhook (Appendix C) with payload `{bid_id, buyer_org_id, seller_org_id, disqualified_at, disqualification_reason ∈ disqualification_reason_enum, disqualifying_user_role, disqualified_phase ∈ pipeline_phase}`. The Cross-Console Bridge (§4.7) carries the event to the seller-side Convex deployment.

**Tech-stack realization (Convex Cross-Console Bridge consumer).** The seller-side bridge consumer (a Convex action subscribed to the `bid.disqualified` topic) updates the seller's `BidWorkspace` row inside a single transaction:

```ts
// inside Convex action handler for bid.disqualified
await ctx.runMutation(internal.bidWorkspace.applyDisqualification, {
  bidId: payload.bidId,
  disqualifiedAt: payload.disqualifiedAt,
  disqualificationReason: payload.disqualificationReason,
  disqualifyingUserRole: payload.disqualifyingUserRole,
  disqualifiedPhase: payload.disqualifiedPhase,
});
// mutation: stamp BidWorkspace.disqualified_at, .disqualification_reason,
// preserve outcome_debrief_seen_by_user_ids[] for analytics integrity,
// emit `seller_bid_disqualified` PostHog event.
```

**Cascade contract — Path B (canonical).** V5 §10.3 self-challenge selected **Path B** (overlay renders with disqualification annotation; Activation-Metric write preserved with disqualification flag) over **Path A** (suppress overlay; invalidate Activation-Metric write) for analytics integrity: sellers who completed the funnel deserve metric attribution even if the buyer disqualified them downstream. The cascade contract:

1. **`stake_reveal_rendered_at` is preserved.** The timestamp captures *that the seller saw the Stake-Reveal Screen*, which is independent of bid outcome. No invalidation.
2. **`outcome_debrief_seen_by_user_ids[]` is preserved.** Sellers who already opened the Win/Loss Debrief overlay (§22.18.6.2) before disqualification keep their entry; the overlay is not re-rendered.
3. **`Activation-Metric` write is preserved with annotation.** A new field `BidWorkspace.activation_metric_disqualification_annotated_at` (Timestamp; nullable) is stamped at cascade-apply time. Activation-Metric dashboards (§42 Seller Activation Dashboard) render disqualified-cohort retention with a visual annotation but do NOT exclude the cohort from p50/p90 SLO assertions.
4. **`BidWorkspace.disqualified_at` and `.disqualification_reason`** stamped. The entity's `bid_lifecycle_state` enum transitions to `disqualified` (Appendix L kb_bid_state_machine row 7a — new).
5. **Outcome-debrief overlay rendering on subsequent opens** — if a seller user opens the BidWorkspace AFTER the disqualification cascade applies (i.e., the user is in the suppressed-cohort `outcome_debrief_seen_by_user_ids[]` from a previous render OR has never seen it), the overlay renders the disqualified state directly. Overlay copy: *"This bid was disqualified by the buyer on {disqualified_at}. Reason: {disqualification_reason_display_label}. Your KB-citation contributions to this bid are preserved in the KB Citation Graph."* Zero upgrade CTAs (per §22.18.6.2 invariant + §48.8.7 AP-2 compliance).
6. **`KBCitationGraphEdge` rows are PRESERVED.** Citations from the seller's KB to the disqualified bid's responses are NOT deleted. The Citation Graph is the seller's stake; preserving it on disqualification is the honest-portability invariant of §22.18.1.
7. **`win_rate_weight` updates are SUPPRESSED for the disqualified bid.** The OutcomeContract `first_pass_rfp_draft` (§34.15.1 row 1) does NOT settle `accepted` or `rejected` — it settles to a new state `disqualified_no_signal` (§34.15.1 OutcomeContract status enum extension; AE flagged for Phase 13 ratification). No nudge up or down on the seller's KB win-rate-weight metrics from this bid.
8. **PostHog event** `seller_bid_disqualified {seller_org_id, bid_workspace_id, disqualification_reason, disqualifying_user_role, disqualified_phase, seconds_since_stake_reveal_rendered, outcome_debrief_overlay_was_already_rendered ∈ {true, false}}` emitted at cascade-apply time. Family `bid_lifecycle_core` per §51.1.1 envelope.

**Idempotency.** `bid.disqualified` webhook is idempotent on `(bid_id)` — a duplicate delivery from the bridge DLQ MUST NOT re-stamp `disqualified_at` or duplicate the PostHog event. Convex serializable transaction semantics + check on `BidWorkspace.disqualified_at IS NOT NULL` provide the idempotency guard.

**Concurrency — buyer disqualification mid-seller-edit.** If a seller is actively editing the BidWorkspace (e.g., authoring a Q&A Thread reply, attaching a document, or scoring an evaluation) at the moment the disqualification cascade applies, Convex's serializable transaction model serializes the two writes: the disqualification cascade transaction commits first; the seller's mutation observes `disqualified_at IS NOT NULL` on the next read and returns HTTP 410 `bid_workspace_disqualified` (Appendix I new). The Seller Console surfaces a non-blocking banner: *"This bid was disqualified by the buyer while you were editing. Your changes were not saved."* with a one-tap "View debrief" CTA opening the disqualified-state overlay.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

68. The `bid.disqualified` webhook MUST be registered in Appendix C with HMAC-SHA256 signing, idempotency on `(event_id)`, Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve, DLQ after 5 failures, payload ≤ 256 KB. (V5 D-5V-005 remediation; v7.2.0-REM D-8.2-005 normalizes the retired critical-business retry label to the binary webhook taxonomy.)
69. Cascade-applied BidWorkspace rows MUST stamp `disqualified_at`, `disqualification_reason`, and `activation_metric_disqualification_annotated_at` atomically inside one Convex transaction; partial-state failure MUST roll back. Property test asserts under 1,000 synthetic injection trials.
70. The Citation Graph (`KBCitationGraphEdge` rows where `to_bid_workspace_id = bid_workspace_id`) MUST be preserved on disqualification — no delete, no soft-delete cascade. QA test `bid_disqualification_citation_graph_preserved` asserts.
71. The OutcomeContract for the disqualified bid's `first_pass_rfp_draft` AIOperation (and any other in-flight per-capability OutcomeContracts on the bid) MUST settle to `disqualified_no_signal` (new state per §34.15.1 enum extension), NOT `accepted` or `rejected`. The `win_rate_weight` decay job MUST exclude this bid from its compute window. (Authored Extension AE-V5-005 ratifies before v7.1.1 stamp.)
72. The §42 Seller Activation Dashboard MUST render disqualified-cohort retention with a visual annotation (e.g., a "⚠ disqualified" badge on the cohort row) but MUST NOT exclude the cohort from §48.8.10 ACs #30 / #31 p50/p90 SLO assertions. Dashboard fixture snapshot test asserts.
73. A seller who attempts to mutate a disqualified BidWorkspace (Q&A reply, document attach, scoring) MUST receive HTTP 410 `bid_workspace_disqualified` (Appendix I new) on the mutation; the response payload MUST include a `view_debrief_url` field deep-linking to the disqualified-state overlay.
74. CI gate `bid_disqualification_cascade_active` (Appendix M.5; v7.1.1 stamp gate) asserts the cascade consumer is wired in the Cross-Console Bridge runtime AND that the disqualification annotation field is written on every cascade.

**Cross-references.** §4.7 Cross-Console Bridge Entities; §10.7 Phase-9 disqualification trigger; §25.3 disqualification cascade; §22.18.6.2 outcome-debrief overlay (rendering surface); §22.18.4 KB Value Meter (Citation Graph preservation invariant); §34.11.1 / §34.15.1 OutcomeContract `disqualified_no_signal` state extension (AE); §42 Seller Activation Dashboard (annotation rendering); §48.8.10 ACs #30 / #31 (SLO preservation); Appendix C `bid.disqualified` webhook (new); Appendix I `bid_workspace_disqualified` HTTP 410 (new); Appendix L kb_bid_state_machine row 7a (new); Appendix M.5 `bid_disqualification_cascade_active` CI gate (new).

### 22.18.7 Acceptance Criteria {#22.18.7-acceptance-criteria}

50. **No-Paywall Export invariant.** `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/kb/export` (§32.9) MUST succeed for every Seller Org on every plan tier (Free, Starter, Growth, Scale, Enterprise) subject only to the §22.18.2.4 abuse rate-limit envelope. A plan-tier-based rejection (other than rate-limit or concurrency) MUST return no code at all — the endpoint MUST NOT even have a plan-tier guard in its handler. QA test `kb_export_no_plan_gate` asserts across all five tiers via integration harness.
51. **Feature-Coupled Compounding invariant (P2).** Every on-platform compounding feature (§22.18.3.1–§22.18.3.5) MUST compute exclusively from live Sourcera state. A deploy-time validator (`compounding_feature_source_firewall`) asserts that none of the five compounding features read from a `KBExportArchive` (any suspected cross-consumption fails CI).
52. **Export Does Not Degrade invariant (P3).** Between one minute before and one minute after an export's `ready` transition, the following invariants MUST hold on the seller's KB corpus: `COUNT(KBEntry)`, SUM of `confidence_score`, SUM of `win_rate_weight`, `COUNT(KBCitationGraphEdge)`, `KBEntry.status` distributions. Any drift > 0.01% (outside normal nightly-job volatility) fires a P1 alert. QA test `kb_export_mutation_firewall` asserts under 1,000 synthetic export cycles.
53. **Export envelope rate-limit.** A Seller Org that exceeds 10 export initiations / hour / Org MUST receive HTTP 429 `kb_export_rate_limit_exceeded`; a Seller Org that attempts a third concurrent `status IN {queued, running}` job MUST receive HTTP 409 `kb_export_concurrency_exceeded`. QA tests `kb_export_request_rate_limit` and `kb_export_concurrency_cap` assert.
54. **Download re-mint cap.** A seller MAY re-mint the `download_url` on a `ready` job up to three times before `expires_at`; a fourth attempt MUST return HTTP 429 `kb_export_download_remints_exhausted`. QA test `kb_export_download_remint_cap` asserts.
55. **Archive integrity.** Every archive produced MUST pass the `archive_sha256` integrity check; a mismatch at download time MUST return HTTP 410 `kb_export_archive_integrity_failed` and the archive MUST NOT be re-served from the bad object. The customer must initiate a fresh export after the corrupted object is quarantined per §32.9.2 / Appendix I. QA test `kb_export_archive_sha256_integrity` asserts.
56. **Archive shape contract.** Every `markdown_and_jsonl_zip_v1` archive MUST contain the directory layout specified in §22.18.2.2; every `kb_entry_id.md` file MUST be valid YAML-front-matter-plus-Markdown; every `_metadata.jsonl` line MUST validate against `schema/kb_entry.schema.json`. A post-production validator `kb_export_archive_shape_validator` asserts before the job transitions to `ready`.
57. **DSAR compatibility.** A §6.8 Right-to-Erasure request on the seller's own Org MUST cause every in-flight KBExportJob (`status IN {queued, running}`) to pause (`dsar_hold_at` stamped) and transition to `failed` if the DSAR invalidates the corpus. QA test `kb_export_dsar_pause_and_invalidate` asserts under a synthetic DSAR harness.
58. **Residency pinning.** Every archive MUST be produced and stored in the Seller Org's `data_residency_region` at `requested_at`; a Seller Org mid-residency-evacuation MUST have the job paused and resumed atomically with the KB corpus migration. QA test `kb_export_residency_pinning` asserts across `us`, `eu`, and `apac`.
59. **KB Value Meter — Seller Panel plan-tier parity.** The §22.18.4 panel MUST render identically across Free, Starter, Growth, Scale, and Enterprise plans. A UX fixture snapshot test asserts pixel-equivalence of the panel header, number labels, and value positions across all five plans.
60. **KB Value Meter — Seller Panel no-upgrade-CTA invariant.** The §22.18.4 panel MUST NOT render an upgrade CTA under any plan tier. A UX fixture test asserts that no CTA-tagged element renders in the panel. The Free-tier "Upgrade Carry-Over applies" chip and "See how citations compound on Starter" explainer link are NOT upgrade CTAs (they route to explainer surfaces, not to Stripe Checkout); this distinction is asserted by a navigation-observer test.
61. **KB Value Meter — Seller Panel telemetry.** Every render of the Seller Panel MUST emit `kb_value_meter_viewed` (Appendix G) with the five required properties; every panel-number click MUST emit `kb_value_meter_click_through`. QA tests `kb_value_meter_viewed_emit_on_every_render` and `kb_value_meter_click_through_emit_on_every_click` assert.
62. **Empty-state rendering.** A Seller Org with zero KBEntries MUST render the §22.18.4.1 empty-state copy and the bootstrap CTA (NOT an upgrade CTA). UX fixture test asserts.
63. **Upgrade confirmation copy — KB-scoped block.** Every upgrade confirmation surface MUST render the §22.18.5.2 KB-scoped honest-portability block beneath the §34.19.4 generic summary. The block MUST substitute `entries` and `years_of_citation_history` with live values. UX fixture snapshot test asserts.
64. **Downgrade confirmation copy — KB-scoped block.** Every downgrade confirmation surface MUST render the §22.18.5.3 KB-scoped downgrade block beneath the §34.19.4 generic downgrade summary. The block MUST cite the authoritative 90-day read-only window (NOT the superseded Summary-narrative 12-month figure). UX fixture snapshot test asserts.
65. **Stake-Reveal — Moment 1 telemetry.** On every render of the Seller Panel for a `plan_tier = 'seller_free'` Seller Org, `stake_reveal_rendered {reveal_moment = free_tier_kb_landing, upgrade_cta_visible = false}` MUST emit within 2 seconds of render completion. QA test `stake_reveal_moment_1_emit` asserts.
66. **Stake-Reveal — Moment 2 rendering.** On every first view of a closed Bid Workspace by a seller user, the outcome-debrief overlay (§22.18.6.2) MUST render once. A subsequent view by the same user MUST NOT re-render the overlay (idempotency per `(bid_id, user_id)`). QA test `outcome_debrief_overlay_idempotent` asserts across 100-user × 100-bid synthetic matrix.
67. **Stake-Reveal — Moment 2 no-upgrade-CTA invariant.** The outcome-debrief overlay MUST NOT render an upgrade modal. The 45-entry inline ceiling banner on Free tier is informational-only; clicking "Learn more" MUST route to the Carry-Over explainer, NOT to Stripe Checkout. A navigation-observer test asserts (§48.8.7 AP-2 compliance).
68. **Stake-Reveal — Conversion-Moment KB Carry-Over Preview row.** The §48.8.6 CM1 / CM2 / CM3 / CM4 modal bodies MUST each render the §22.18.6.3 KB Carry-Over Preview row between the benefit list and the price display. UX fixture snapshot test asserts for all four CMs; copy drift fails CI.
69. **`reveal_moment` property — additive extension.** Every emission of `stake_reveal_rendered` (canonical) and `stake_reveal_displayed` (legacy, during v7.0.x dual-emit window) MUST carry a non-null `reveal_moment` value drawn from `kb_stake_reveal_moment_enum` (Appendix J). Consumers without property awareness MUST continue to receive the event's existing shape; property-aware consumers can partition by moment. QA test `stake_reveal_reveal_moment_property_populated` asserts ≥ 99.5% population on trailing 7-day event volume.
70. **Webhook emission on `ready`.** Every transition to `status = ready` MUST emit `kb.export.ready` (Appendix C KB-Domain Events) to the seller Org's registered webhook endpoints under §31 contract (HMAC-SHA256, idempotency via `event_id`, exponential backoff, DLQ after 5 failures, payload ≤ 256 KB). QA test `kb_export_ready_webhook_emission` asserts per-endpoint delivery within 30 seconds of `ready_at`.
71. **PostHog `kb_export_initiated` emission.** Every `POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/kb/export` request accepted into `status = queued` MUST emit `kb_export_initiated` (Appendix G) within 1 second. QA test asserts.
72. **Audit ledger write on `ready`.** Every transition to `status = ready` MUST write `org.kb_exported` to the §6.7 audit ledger within 2 seconds. QA test `kb_export_audit_ledger_write` asserts.
73. **Export console isolation.** `POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/kb/export` MUST reject any Buyer-console principal with HTTP 404 (subkind `firewall_non_leak`) and code `kb_export_console_forbidden` per the §7.2 dual-console firewall non-leak invariant; a Seller-console principal attempting to export a Buyer Org likewise receives HTTP 404 (cross-Org non-leak). The response shape is structurally indistinguishable from a true 404 to preserve entity-existence non-leak. **Phase V8.4 status correction (D-V8.4-018):** pre-V8.4 emissions used HTTP 422 for the buyer-console case and HTTP 403 in the Appendix I row; both are migrated to HTTP 404 with the same code; aliasing handler sets `Sourcera-Error-Code-Alias` for caller-side telemetry continuity. QA test `kb_export_console_isolation` asserts HTTP 404 for both buyer-console and cross-Org seller-console probes; CI gate `kb_export_console_firewall_status_consistency` (§M.5) asserts.
74. **Compounding-feature preservation across upgrade.** An upgrade from any tier to any higher tier MUST preserve `KBEntry.confidence_score`, `KBEntry.status`, `KBEntry.win_rate_weight`, `KBCitationGraphEdge` rows, and `CapabilityDeclarationSuggestion` rows byte-for-byte per §34.19.1.A sub-classes 2b, 2c, 2d, 6b, and 3b. QA test `compounding_feature_upgrade_preservation` asserts on a synthetic upgrade-matrix harness and MUST share the §34.19.1.A fixture factory with `plan_upgrade_13_asset_preservation`.
75. **Downgrade preservation window — authoritative citation.** Any seller-facing surface that states the downgrade KB read-only window MUST cite **90 days** per §34.19 / §34.6 (NOT the Summary §6.13.7 narrative figure of 12 months). A copy-linter CI rule `summary_narrative_12_month_reference_blocked` asserts on seller-facing copy strings.
76. **Stake-Reveal moment enumeration.** The set of stake-reveal moments is exactly three: `free_tier_kb_landing`, `outcome_debrief`, `conversion_threshold`. Additions require an Integration_Prompts phase; `kb_stake_reveal_moment_enum` is closed. A deploy-time validator `kb_stake_reveal_moment_enum_closed` asserts that no emitter uses a value outside the enum.
77. **KB Value Meter — Seller Panel and §34.19.2 scalar are not confused.** A copy-linter CI rule asserts that seller-facing surfaces use the phrase "KB Value Meter" (bare) consistently with the §22.18.4 Seller Panel semantics; buyer-facing surfaces use the phrase with the §34.19.2 scalar semantics. Cross-console mixing is a CI failure.
78. **KB Value Meter — Seller Panel and §34.19.2 scalar — recompute-barrier invariant.** The two surfaces read from overlapping inputs (`KBEntry.confidence_score`, `KBEntry.win_rate_weight`, `KBCitationGraphEdge` counts, the per-entry acceptance-rate rollup) but surface different downstream scalars to different consoles. To prevent inter-console drift, the nightly recompute jobs that produce (a) the Seller Panel's six numeric inputs (§22.18.4) and (b) the §34.19.2 buyer-facing KB Value scalar MUST execute within a single orchestrator transaction OR behind a shared stage-wait barrier on the same input snapshot. Drift between the two surfaces' materialized values (normalized to a per-Org, per-entry comparable basis) MUST NOT exceed 60 seconds, measured from the earliest job's commit to the latest job's commit. A drift > 60 seconds MUST fire the `kb_value_dual_surface_drift_exceeded` P2 alert (Appendix F, new) and MUST pause rendering of BOTH surfaces (display a "Refreshing…" skeleton with `last_successful_recompute_at` caption) until the barrier recovers. QA tests: `kb_value_dual_surface_single_snapshot` asserts the two recomputes read from the same `snapshot_id` under the orchestrator transaction; `kb_value_dual_surface_stage_wait_barrier` asserts stage-wait completion within 60 s on a synthetic 10,000-entry Org; `kb_value_dual_surface_drift_alarm` asserts the P2 alert fires within 30 s of a synthetic drift breach. The orchestrator is registered in §42 as `kb_value_dual_surface_orchestrator`; the barrier semantics, snapshot identifier, and failure-mode recovery path are authored as Authored Extension pending Phase 13 consolidation. Cross-reference: §22.18.4 Seller Panel authoritative; §34.19.2 scalar authoritative; §42 orchestrator registry.

**Failure Modes Addressed (Counterfactual Pass — three per feature cluster).**

- **Honest Portability (§22.18.2) failure modes:** (1) Abusive bot scraper exhausts S3 bandwidth — mitigated by `kb_export_request` rate limit (§22.18.2.4) + origin-shield at S3 layer (§33.9). (2) Seller exports, then a concurrent DSAR erases the corpus — mitigated by `dsar_hold_at` pause semantics (§22.18.2.6) + post-DSAR re-evaluation and `residency_evacuation` failure transition. (3) Archive becomes corrupt mid-transfer — mitigated by `archive_sha256` integrity check (AC #55) + re-production on mismatch.
- **On-Platform Compounding (§22.18.3) failure modes:** (1) Compounding feature accidentally reads from a stale snapshot — prevented by P2 invariant (AC #51) + `compounding_feature_source_firewall` validator. (2) Nightly win-rate recompute corrupts all weights due to a bid-outcome join bug — mitigated by nightly reconciliation snapshot (`win_rate_weight_history_snapshot` audit row — Authored Extension) + point-in-time restore. (3) Citation graph orphan entries are indefinitely retained, bloating retrieval — mitigated by nightly archival-candidate sweep surfaced to the seller in KB Health Dashboard (§22.5.3).
- **KB Value Meter Seller Panel (§22.18.4) failure modes:** (1) Estimated-value computation produces a wildly inflated number for a Seller Org with a small KB and aggressive per-entry time-saved configuration — mitigated by the seller-configurable defaults being conservative (18 min / entry, $85/hr) + a per-computation ceiling alerting Ops above $1M/yr estimated-value for a single Org. (2) Panel renders stale data > 24h old because nightly job failed — mitigated by "Last updated" caption + §42 alarm if recompute lag > 2h. (3) Seller Panel leaks to buyer console via a caching bug — prevented by strict `console = 'seller'` scope isolation on every computation + a caching-layer firewall validator.
- **Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee (§22.18.5) failure modes:** (1) Upgrade transaction fails mid-flight and some KB entries enter partial state — mitigated by §34.19.6 FM #1 transactional orchestration + rollback. (2) Downgrade DowngradeExcessDataBucket violates Protected Asset guarantees — mitigated by §34.19.6 FM #2 `protected_asset_downgrade_firewall`. (3) Seller disputes that win-rate weights degraded post-upgrade — mitigated by §34.19.6 FM #7 component-breakdown trend surface (reuses the same breakdown for the §22.18.4 panel).
- **Stake-Reveal Moments (§22.18.6) failure modes:** (1) Outcome-debrief overlay renders twice for the same user — prevented by `outcome_debrief_seen_by_user_ids[]` idempotency (AC #66). (2) CM4 KB-ceiling banner inside the outcome-debrief overlay is misread as a Conversion Moment fire — prevented by surface classification: CM4 fires from KB workspace on KB-write (§48.1.7); the overlay banner is informational-only (AC #67). (3) `stake_reveal_rendered` event is dropped due to a PostHog outbox overflow — mitigated by §31 outbox retry per Appendix F.1 `standard` plus a reconciliation job `stake_reveal_emission_coverage` asserting ≥ 99.5% coverage on trailing 7-day cohort.

**Authored Extensions (registered; require human sign-off).**
