1. `KBExportJob` entity (§4.4.30 / §22.18.2.1) — new entity; field table, retention tier, residency pinning. Ratified into §4 by AE-V72REM-PH5P53-DM-01.
2. `KBCitationGraphEdge` entity (§4.4.31 / §22.18.3.4) — new entity; field table, scope-isolation, retention. Ratified into §4 by AE-V72REM-PH5P53-DM-01.
3. `KBEntry.win_rate_weight` field (§22.3.1 / §22.18.3.3) — new field on the existing `KBEntry` entity; default 0.5, range [0.0, 1.0]. Ratified into §22.3.1 by AE-V72REM-PH5P53-DM-01.
4. `CapabilityDeclarationSuggestion` entity (§4.4.32 / §22.18.3.5) — new entity; field table, state machine, scope, indexes, and retention. The seed pipeline under Summary §6.13 C.46 is the conceptual parent. Ratified by AE-V72REM-PH5P53-DM-01.
5. `kb_stake_reveal_moment_enum` (Appendix J) — new enum with three closed values; §22.18.6.4 uses.
6. `kb_export_format_kind_enum`, `kb_export_failure_code_enum` (Appendix J) — new enums; §22.18.2.1 uses.
7. `org.kb_exported` audit action (Appendix J BillingAdminAuditAction / §6.7 audit ledger) — new action.
8. `kb_value_meter_viewed`, `kb_value_meter_click_through`, `kb_export_initiated` (Appendix G) — new PostHog events.
9. `reveal_moment` property extension on `stake_reveal_rendered` and `stake_reveal_displayed` (Appendix G) — additive, backward-compatible.
10. `kb.export.ready` webhook (Appendix C) — new webhook.
11. §32.9 `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/kb/export` endpoint — new top-level §32 subsection (not a §32.8 extension, since it is KB-scoped, not billing-scoped).
12. §22.18.4 KB Value Meter — Seller Panel — new seller-facing surface on the KB landing screen; §26.x (public seller pages) are NOT affected.
13. §22.18.6.2 outcome-debrief overlay — new seller-facing surface within the Bid Workspace. Seller Signals interaction (Summary §6.17) with this overlay is deferred to a later integration phase.
14. §22.18.5.3 citation of authoritative 90-day downgrade window (vs. Summary §6.13.7 narrative 12-month) — conflict resolution in favor of Master Spec §34.19 / §34.6.
15. Blended-draft-time-saved and blended-seller-hourly-rate defaults for §22.18.4 Estimated Value: 18 min / entry and $85 / hr. Seller-configurable under Settings → KB Economics. Calibration recommended post-launch.
16. `kb_value_dual_surface_orchestrator` (§42) — new orchestrator registering the single-transaction / stage-wait-barrier contract between §22.18.4 (Seller Panel) and §34.19.2 (buyer-facing scalar) nightly recomputes; 60-second drift tolerance; `kb_value_dual_surface_drift_exceeded` P2 alert (Appendix F). Phase 13 consolidation will finalize the orchestrator name, the `snapshot_id` contract, and the stage-wait-barrier timeout policy.

All Authored Extensions above are flagged in `/Sourcera/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions → §22.18 KB Value Capture & Stake-Building (2026-04-20)`.

## 22.19 Seller Compressed Surface Mapping {#22.19-seller-compressed-surface-mapping}

**Authoring intent (Phase 14.6 — 2026-04-26).** This section is the Seller-console mirror of §2.8.2 (Buyer Solo step-to-phase mapping). It documents the four-step compressed surface (**Receive → Draft → Review → Submit**) that renders on the Seller console and binds each step to the engine phases of the bound buyer Workspace per §3.14.2. The Seller console is always in the compressed surface — there is no `evaluation_owner_mode` on the seller side, and the Bid Workspace surface compresses by default per §2.8.6 and the §3.14.4 invariant `pipeline_surface_compression_seller_always_compressed`.

The seller side does not have a separately-numbered 13-phase engine pipeline. Each Bid Workspace (§4.4.1) is bound to a buyer Workspace and reads the buyer's `pipeline_stage_id` via the Console Bridge (§4.7.1, §25), subject to the firewall-bound projection rules (§7.2): the seller sees `pipeline_stage_id` (and its derived four-step compressed step) but never the buyer's `evaluation_owner_mode`, internal Comments, Selection Report internals, or any cohort-bound metadata. The "Phase N" labels below refer to the bound buyer Workspace's `pipeline_stage_id` value, with the seller's interpretation of each phase rendered inline.

### 22.19.1 Seller Compressed Step-to-Phase Mapping {#22.19.1-seller-compressed-step-to-phase-mapping}

The mapping is canonical for the Seller console and mirrors §3.14.2 verbatim per the §3.14.4 invariant `pipeline_surface_compression_step_to_phase_canonical`.

| Seller Solo step | Engine phases (§10) | What the seller sees | Bid Workspace status precondition | Step-to-phase first sub-phase (click target) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Receive** | Phase 1 (Bid invitation received — corresponds to buyer-side Phase 4–5 Vendor Outreach as observed from the seller; Bid Workspace `status=draft` per Appendix E), Phase 2 (Hero Moment bootstrap per §35.2 / §48.8 — first-time KB warmup, Capability Declaration check, Bid Workspace `status` advances to `active`) | "A buyer wants you to bid" — invitation card, the buyer's RFP summary as exposed by the firewall-bound projection, and the Hero Moment that activates the KB-driven first-pass response capability for first-time sellers. | `status ∈ {draft, active}` | Phase 1 |
| **Draft** | Phase 3 (First-pass response generation kicked off — `first_pass_responses` capability per §21.4.2 and §22.10), Phase 4 (KB-grounded drafting per §22.8 / §22.9 retrieval), Phase 5 (Capability evidence assembly), Phase 6 (Buyer Bidding window open per §10.6 — seller-side draft active), Phase 7 (Seller refinement per §10.7) | "Draft your responses" — the AI-drafted first-pass populates each requirement; the seller refines KB-grounded answers; the bidding-window deadline countdown is rendered inline. | `status=active` | Phase 3 |
| **Review** | Phase 8 (Operator review during buyer Due Diligence per §10.8 — seller responding to buyer follow-ups), Phase 9 (Final clarifications Q&A per §10.9 — Seller Q&A surface per §24.1), Phase 10 (Operator edits, KB-gap creation per §22.5 staleness classifier feedback loop) | "Review and finalize" — operator review, edits to drafted answers, last-mile clarifications via Seller Q&A, and KB-gap creation when the seller marks an entry stale or missing. | `status=active` | Phase 8 |
| **Submit** | Phase 11 (Submission per §23.3 Response Submission), Phase 12 (Post-bid debrief — buyer-side Selection & Recommendation; seller-side `bid.status` resolves to `won` or `lost`), Phase 13 (KB compounding — won-bid responses are offered to KB per §22.3 channel #2; debrief surfaces in Seller Pulse per §24.4) | "Submit and learn" — single Submit CTA at Phase 11; post-bid debrief overlay at Phase 12 (won / lost / no-decision); KB compounding offer at Phase 13 ("Add this bid's responses to your KB?" per §22.3 channel #2). | `status ∈ {active, submitted, won, lost}` | Phase 11 |

The Submit step is terminal in the surface sense: once the bid is submitted (`status=submitted`), the Submit step renders the post-bid debrief and KB compounding affordances rather than the Submit CTA. The four-step bar continues to render in its compressed form throughout — the seller console never renders the 13-phase chip ribbon under any plan tier or any Bid Workspace state per the §3.14.4 invariant `pipeline_surface_compression_seller_always_compressed`.

### 22.19.2 Engine vs. Surface Behavior — Seller Side {#22.19.2-engine-vs-surface-behavior-seller-side}

The seller-side compressed surface is governed by the same engine-on / surface-compressed discipline as the Buyer Solo surface (§2.8). The seller engine continues to:

1. Read the bound buyer Workspace's `pipeline_stage_id` via the Console Bridge (§4.7.1, §25) on every Bid Workspace tick. The compressed step is computed from this read; the four-step bar is a pure projection.
2. Persist Bid Workspace state transitions (Appendix E) on every operator action and on every buyer-driven trigger (e.g., Phase 6 bidding open → seller Bid Workspace `status=active`).
3. Compute and persist Seller Pulse (§24.4) and any seller-side analytics (§24.5) per Bid Workspace tick regardless of the rendered surface.
4. Emit identical webhooks (§31, Appendix C) on Bid Workspace state transitions and on bid outcome resolution. The compressed surface does not gate any webhook.
5. Settle every AIOperation (§4.8.1) — first-pass drafting, KB-grounded retrieval, capability evidence assembly, KB compounding suggestions — against the seller's AIWallet (§4.8.3) per the §34.11 Outcome Resolver, irrespective of which compressed step is currently rendered.

The compression is purely a rendering decision; the underlying bid-lifecycle engine — Bid Workspace state machine (Appendix E), Bid Response state (§25.5 materialization), KB indexing pipeline (§22.4), Managed Agents harness (§22.10) — is unchanged.

### 22.19.3 Soft Phase Gates — Seller Side {#22.19.3-soft-phase-gates-seller-side}

The seller-side compressed surface uses **soft phase gates** by default for any seller-controlled transition (e.g., advancing from Draft → Review by marking all drafted answers reviewed; submitting from Review → Submit). Soft-gate behavior is the same as the Buyer Solo behavior in §2.8.3: the same gate-validation logic runs; the same remediation list is computed; the API call is not blocked. Instead, the seller sees a skip-with-warning toast — "You haven't reviewed {N} drafted answers. Submit anyway?" — with two affordances: "Review them first" (returns to the open items) and "Submit anyway" (proceeds with the action and logs a `bid_workspace_advanced_with_unmet_gates` audit event with the unmet-gate enum list serialized into `metadata`).

Buyer-driven transitions (e.g., Phase 6 → Phase 7 when the buyer closes the Bidding window; Phase 9 → Phase 10 when the buyer locks Q&A; Phase 12 entry when the buyer locks scoring) are not subject to seller-side gating — the seller observes these transitions through the Console Bridge projection and the compressed step indicator advances accordingly. No seller-side toast is rendered for buyer-driven transitions; instead, the relevant inbound notification (§24.3 Seller Inbox) carries the engine-event copy.

### 22.19.4 Acceptance Criteria {#22.19.4-acceptance-criteria}

1. The Seller console four-step progress bar MUST render for every Bid Workspace regardless of plan tier (sF, sSt, sGr, sSc, sEnt) and regardless of `Bid Workspace.status`. The 13-phase chip ribbon MUST NOT render on the Seller console under any code path. CI gate `pipeline_surface_compression_seller_always_compressed` (§3.14.4) asserts.
2. The seller-side compressed step MUST be computed from the bound buyer Workspace's `pipeline_stage_id` via the Console Bridge (§4.7.1) per the mapping in §22.19.1. The mapping is canonical; any deviation from §3.14.2 is a defect against §3.14.4 `pipeline_surface_compression_step_to_phase_canonical`.
3. No engine code path may introduce a seller-specific phase counter distinct from the bound buyer Workspace's `pipeline_stage_id`. CI gate `pipeline_surface_compression_no_separate_seller_phase_counter` (§3.14.4) asserts.
4. Soft phase gates MUST render skip-with-warning toasts on seller-controlled transitions per §22.19.3. Buyer-driven transitions MUST NOT render a seller-side toast; instead, the §24.3 Seller Inbox MUST surface the engine-event notification.
5. Click navigation on a step MUST jump the seller's view to the engine phase corresponding to that step's first sub-phase per the "Step-to-phase first sub-phase (click target)" column in §22.19.1; the navigation MUST NOT advance or rewind the engine.
6. The Submit step MUST render the post-bid debrief overlay (§22.18.6.2) when `bid.status ∈ {won, lost, no_decision}` and `pipeline_stage_id ≥ 12`. The KB compounding offer ("Add this bid's responses to your KB?") MUST render when `bid.status ∈ {won, lost}` and `pipeline_stage_id = 13`.
7. The four-step bar MUST suppress all engine phase names from the primary surface; phase names appear only in the desktop tooltip (per §3.14.3 #4). Mobile (`<768px`) MUST NOT render the tooltip; the bottom-sheet detail per §3.14.3 #5 is the mobile-equivalent disclosure surface.
8. The compressed surface MUST NOT change any §22 KB engine semantics (entry lifecycle, indexing pipeline, MCP retrieval contracts, Managed Agent definitions, AIOperation settlement). CI gate `pipeline_surface_compression_engine_unchanged` (§3.14.4) asserts.

### 22.19.5 Cross-References {#22.19.5-cross-references}

- §2.8 (Single-Operator Mode), §2.8.2 (Buyer Solo step-to-phase mapping), §2.8.6 (cross-console behavior — seller-side always compressed): the Buyer-side analog and the cross-console firewall constraint.
- §3.14 (Pipeline Surface Compression), §3.14.2 (Compression Contract — Seller Console), §3.14.4 (Engine-vs.-Surface Invariants): the canonical surface contract.
- §4.4.1 (Bid Workspace), Appendix E (Bid Workspace status state machine): the seller-side state engine.
- §4.7.1 (Console Bridge Event), §7.2 (Dual-Console Firewall), §25 (Cross-Console Mechanics), §25.5 (Materialization Protocol): how the seller surface receives `pipeline_stage_id` projections from the bound buyer Workspace.
- §10 (13-Phase Evaluation Pipeline): the engine.
- §22.3 (KB Ingestion Channels — bid response import as channel #2): Submit-step Phase 13 KB compounding.
- §22.18.6.2 (outcome-debrief overlay): Submit-step Phase 12 post-bid debrief surface.
- §23.3 (Response Submission): Submit-step CTA at Phase 11.
- §24.1 (Seller Q&A): Review-step Phase 9 content.
- §24.3 (Seller Inbox): buyer-driven transition surfacing path.
- §24.4 (Seller Pulse): post-bid debrief surface.
- §35.2 / §48.8 (Seller Hero Moment): Receive-step Phase 2 content.
- Appendix M (Surface/Engine Mapping): authoritative row authored in this phase under "Pipeline Surface Compression."

## 22.20 Seller Maya Surface Abstraction {#22.20-seller-maya-surface-abstraction}

**Authoring intent (Phase 14.8 — 2026-04-27).** §22.20 is the canonical engine-vs-surface compression contract for the Seller Console as it applies to **Seller Maya** (per the §22.1 Audience Note). The pre-Phase-14.8 §22 corpus already contained surfaces authored against Maya — the §48.8 Hero Moment, the §22.18 KB Value Meter — Seller Panel, the §22.19 four-step compressed pipeline. What §22.20 adds is a single, durable home for the surface-abstraction rules that bind those surfaces to Maya's first-30-seconds comprehension test (§3.13 Principle 9): which engine concepts may render to Maya, which engine concepts must stay silent on her plan tier (Solo / Free), and which engine concepts surface only after a deliberate operator action. The rules below supersede any inline surface guidance elsewhere in §22 that conflicts; conflicts that surface during implementation are resolved in favor of §22.20 and logged to `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Phase 14.8`.

**Source authority.** §3.13 (Principle 9 — Surface Simplicity, Engine Complexity); §22.1 (Purpose & Scope, Audience Note — Seller Maya); §22.18 (KB Value Capture & Stake-Building); §22.19 (Seller Compressed Surface Mapping); §27.4 (Marketplace Match Score); §44 (Performance Budgets — Solo-Tier Surface Treatment authored in Phase 14.10); §48.8 (Seller Hero Moment & Onboarding Anti-Patterns); §48.8.7 (Six Banned Anti-Patterns — AP10: Capability Declarations are auto-suggested, not manually authored on the onboarding path); Appendix M (Surface/Engine Mapping); `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §4.4.2 (Seller Onboarding) and §4.4.2 Phase 14.8 polish (Seller Magic-Link Hero Moment Landing).

**Plan-tier scope.** §22.20 binds the **Solo / Free seller surface** — `plan_tier ∈ {seller_free, seller_solo}` per the §34.1.3 inclusive-of-Solo rule (line 27689). Phase 14.9 registered `seller_solo` as a discrete billable plan tier alongside `seller_free`; both are covered by Seller Maya's surface-compression contract because the canonical Maya destination per §34.1.2 narrative is the personal-card on-ramp (Solo) and Solo's §34.1 cell values are non-`—` for every row §22.20 compresses. Wherever the body and ACs below name `plan_tier = seller_free` literally, the binding semantically expands to `plan_tier ∈ {seller_free, seller_solo}` per the inclusive-of-Solo rule; the CI gate `seller_maya_surface_abstraction_engine_unchanged` (Phase 14.18) and the AC validators enforce on the union. The compression rules also apply to any seller-side workspace context where the operator's effective experience is single-operator and pre-Hero-Moment (e.g., a buyer-funded Pro Trial Seat per §34.13 / §4.3.17 surfaces the compressed Solo-equivalent rendering during the trial). Paid seller tiers (sSt, sGr, sSc, sEnt) retain the existing surface set per §22.18.4.1, §27.4, §22.5, and §48.8 unchanged; per-tier exceptions are called out inline in each compression rule below.

**What §22.20 is NOT.** §22.20 is not a new entity catalog, a new RBAC scope, a new billing semantic, a new state machine, or a new API endpoint. It introduces no new fields on `KBEntry`, `CapabilityDeclaration`, `SellerOnboardingSession`, `MarketplaceMatchScoreSnapshot`, `KBHealthRollup`, or `AIOperation`; the engine those entities encode is preserved byte-for-byte. §22.20 is a rendering-layer contract — what surfaces, what stays silent, when a silent engine emits a surface notification, and how a numeric score becomes a three-label compression on the Solo / Free surface. Engine-side data writes, audit-event emissions, AIOperation settlements, and webhook delivery are unchanged in every compression rule. CI gate `seller_maya_surface_abstraction_engine_unchanged` (Phase 14.18) asserts at deploy time.

### 22.20.1 Persona Anchor {#22.20.1-persona-anchor}

**Persona resolution.** Seller Maya is title-agnostic; the persona resolves to one of three real-world roles at a 50–500-person B2B SaaS vendor:

1. **Account Executive (AE).** Owns the customer relationship and reports against pipeline. Encounters Sourcera through a buyer's magic-link invitation when a deal in flight requires an RFP response; Sourcera is a tactical workflow on a deal she expects to close. Has zero prior Sourcera experience and zero patience for tools that require setup before producing output. Will abandon the surface within 30 seconds if the first interaction is a form.
2. **Solutions Engineer (SE).** Owns the technical answer set and, in companies without a dedicated Bid Manager, drafts the response. Encounters Sourcera through the same magic-link path — typically forwarded by an AE — and treats it as one more inbox item. Comfortable with technical terms but does not know that "Capability Declaration" or "Marketplace Match Score" are Sourcera nouns; will read them as jargon and disengage.
3. **Bid Manager / Proposal Manager.** Owns the response process at vendors mature enough to staff the role. Has experience with Loopio, Responsive (formerly RFPIO), or QorusDocs. Recognizes the bid-response workflow but assumes Sourcera's primitives map to the existing tools' primitives until proven otherwise. Will compare the surface to Loopio's "answer library" and Responsive's "knowledge base" and quietly judge any engine concept that does not map.

**Implications for surface authoring.** Across all three roles the surface must (a) require zero pre-bid configuration, (b) put the work in front of Maya before any pricing conversation, (c) surface only domain-native nouns ("response," "knowledge base," "categories," "buyer match"), and (d) hide any engine concept whose name is Sourcera-specific (Capability Declaration, Match Score numeric, AIOperation, KBHealthRollup, staleness classifier, deduplication threshold, retrieval-fusion ranking). The §22.20 compression rules below operationalize each "hide" rule with an engine-side preservation contract and a surface-side translation contract.

**Engine-side identifier-freedom.** No `persona_kind` enum is introduced. No `seller_persona` field is added to `User`, `Org`, `SellerOnboardingSession`, or `Bid Workspace`. The persona resolves at authoring time, not at runtime; the surface for `plan_tier = seller_free` is the Maya surface by construction. Future personas (e.g., a `seller_pro_evaluator` persona for the agency-side bid responder) will land their own §22.x sub-section if and when authored; the v7.0.0 Seller Console surface is single-persona at the Solo / Free tier.

### 22.20.2 Compression Rule 1 — Capability Declarations {#22.20.2-compression-rule-1-capability-declarations}

**Rule.** On Solo / Free, Seller Maya never authors a Capability Declaration. The §22.18.3.5 KB-to-Capability auto-declaration pipeline (and the §21.4.1 #18 `kb_to_capability_suggestion` capability per §22.10.5 `agent_sourcera_kb_to_capability_v4`) runs against her bootstrapped KB and emits `CapabilityDeclaration` rows that **auto-publish silently** without entering the §4.4.4 `pending_review` queue. The only Maya-visible surface is a **discoverable-categories chip list** rendered on the Bid Workspace populator and the published Seller Profile: *"Your profile is now discoverable for: CRM, Sales Engagement, Lead Scoring."* Maya can edit the displayed list (add a chip, remove a chip, rename a chip's display label); the underlying `CapabilityDeclaration` entities are managed silently by the engine.

**Engine preservation contract.** Every Capability Declaration emitted on Solo / Free remains a fully-formed §4.4.4 entity with all required fields populated: `capability_type = taxonomy_declaration` (the auto-publish path is taxonomy-bound only; `narrative_only` is never auto-emitted), `canonical_capability_id` (FK to §4.8.2 Capability Registry — resolved by the §22.10.5 agent during the Hero Moment Stage 5 `page_enrichment` window), `evidence_kb_entry_ids[]` (≥ 3 KB entries per §22.14.3 evidence-overlap rule), `state = 'published'` (terminal at write — see state-machine note below), `published_at = now()`, `created_via = 'kb_to_capability_suggestion_solo_free_auto_publish'` (Authored Extension to the §4.4.4 `created_via` provenance enum — flagged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Phase 14.8`). The §22.14.3 nightly KB-to-Capability batch continues to run; the existing buyer-side §27.4 Match-Score eligibility computation reads the auto-published rows the same way it reads seller-authored rows. Buyer-side discoverability and Match Score participation are unaffected by the surface compression.

**State-machine extension (Authored Extension — requires human sign-off).** The §4.4.4 Capability Declaration state machine is extended with a new transition: `(none) → published` directly via `pending_review_reason = 'solo_free_auto_publish'` when (a) the originating capability is `kb_to_capability_suggestion`, (b) the seller Org's `plan_tier = seller_free` at write time, (c) `evidence_kb_entry_ids[]` passes the §22.14.3 topic-overlap rule, AND (d) the resolved `canonical_capability_id` does not currently appear on the §48.4 Signal Integrity Monitor's quarantine list for the seller Org. If any precondition fails, the engine falls through to the existing `(none) → pending_review → published` path with `pending_review_reason = 'kb_to_capability_suggestion'` and the auto-publish surface is not rendered for that declaration. The new transition is registered in Appendix L `capability_declaration_state_machine` as row 7a; the existing rows 1–7 are unchanged. The §4.4.4 `pending_review_reason` enum is extended with `solo_free_auto_publish`; Appendix J `capability_declaration_pending_review_reason` registry updated.

**Surface compression — chip list.** The discoverable-categories chip list renders in two places per §22.18.4 / §22.19.1:

1. **Bid Workspace populator (Hero Moment Stage 5 onward).** Below the Stake-Reveal Screen primary copy, render: *"Your profile is now discoverable for: [chip] [chip] [chip]"* where each chip is the `display_label` of one of the auto-published Capability Declarations (sourced from `CapabilityRegistryEntry.display_name` per `canonical_capability_id`). Maximum 6 chips visible inline; a "+N more" affordance expands to a non-modal drawer listing all chips with edit / remove affordances. The chip set updates within 24 h of the §22.18.3.5 nightly batch (cadence preserved — no per-Org compute change).

2. **Seller Profile public page (per §4.4.10 SellerOrgPage).** "Discoverable for" section renders the same chip set in a bordered card. Public-page rendering inherits the chip set from the auto-published Capability Declarations; the buyer-side directory and Marketplace Tagger continue to read the underlying `CapabilityDeclaration` rows for §27.4 Match Score participation.

**Maya-side affordances.** The chip list is Maya-editable inline. Three operations are surfaced:

- **Add a chip.** Click "+ Add" → typeahead picker against `CapabilityRegistryEntry` (the same picker §4.4.4 Capability Declaration authoring uses, per `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §4.3.7). On select, a new auto-published Capability Declaration row is written with `created_via = 'maya_added_chip'` (Authored Extension `created_via` enum value), `evidence_kb_entry_ids[]` populated by the engine via a synchronous `kb_retrieve` against the chosen category's seed query (returning ≥ 3 entries per §22.14.3, or fewer if the seller's KB is too small — see edge case #2 below). The chip appears immediately. No "Pending review" or "Submitted for approval" copy appears anywhere on Maya's surface.
- **Remove a chip.** Click the chip's `×` icon → the underlying `CapabilityDeclaration` row transitions to `state = 'deprecated'` per the existing §4.4.4 state machine. Audit event `capability_declaration_deprecated` fires per §6.7 with `actor_user_id = maya_user_id`, `reason = 'maya_removed_chip'` (Authored Extension `reason` enum value). The chip disappears immediately. Buyer-side Match Score participation drops within 24 h per the existing §27.4 freshness window. Maya sees a 1-line confirmation: *"Removed. You won't appear in {Display Label} searches."*
- **Rename a chip's display label.** Click the chip's pencil icon → inline text input (1–50 chars). On save, the `display_label_override` field is written to the `CapabilityDeclaration` row (Authored Extension field — `display_label_override String, nullable, ≤ 50 chars`; populated when Maya edits the chip; empty falls back to `CapabilityRegistryEntry.display_name`). The buyer-side directory continues to display the canonical `display_name` (the override is seller-page-only — Maya is renaming her marketing label, not the canonical category); a quiet inline note on the chip-edit drawer reads *"This name shows on your profile only. Buyers searching the directory see the standard category name."* No engine semantics change.

**Edge cases.**

1. **First-time seller with empty KB.** During the Hero Moment, the §22.18.3.5 nightly batch has not yet run; the chip list renders empty with the placeholder copy *"We'll figure out your categories from the responses you draft and the website we just scanned. Check back in a day."* The Marketplace Tagger pre-arrival inference (§48.8.2 Workflow #2) can pre-seed up to 5 candidate `category_id` tags during pre-arrival preparation; if pre-seeded, the chip list renders those candidates with a quiet *"Suggested from your website — confirm these are right"* annotation. Maya can confirm or remove individually.
2. **Maya adds a chip but her KB has < 3 evidence entries.** The synchronous `kb_retrieve` returns < 3 entries; the engine writes the `CapabilityDeclaration` row in `state = 'pending_review'` (the existing §4.4.4 state) with `pending_review_reason = 'evidence_insufficient_solo_free_added_chip'` (Authored Extension reason value) and the chip appears with a quiet *"We're confirming this — give us a day"* annotation. The §22.18.3.5 nightly batch re-runs the evidence-overlap rule the next night; on pass, the row transitions to `published` and the annotation drops. On fail (still < 3 entries), the chip remains pending until Maya's KB grows or she removes the chip. No `pending_review` queue surfaces to Maya beyond the per-chip annotation.
3. **Auto-published declaration is later quarantined by the §48.4 Signal Integrity Monitor.** The existing §4.4.4 `state = 'quarantined_*'` transition fires; the chip disappears from Maya's profile and from the discoverable-categories chip list. Maya sees the chip's quiet "Removed" annotation reused with a different remediation copy: *"We removed {Display Label} because something looked off. {Plain-English remediation per §22.18 quarantine_reason_enum mapping}."* No `quarantine_reason_enum` value surfaces; the plain-English copy is computed from the existing `quarantine_reason_enum` per the §4.4.4 surface-compression rule already in Appendix M ("All 7 enum values resolve to plain-English copy").
4. **Maya upgrades to sSt during the Hero Moment.** The auto-publish path is preserved on upgrade — auto-published declarations remain `state = 'published'` and continue to participate in Match Score the same way. The §4.4.4 manual-authoring surface (per `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §4.3.7) becomes available and Maya can switch to authoring full declarations explicitly; the chip-list surface continues to render alongside the manual-authoring surface (the two are not mutually exclusive). The `created_via` provenance is preserved for audit.
5. **Maya downgrades from sSt to sF (rare; not the canonical Maya path).** Per §34.19.3, downgrades preserve KB and Capability state read-only for 90 days. Existing `state = 'pending_review'` rows complete their existing review path under the upgraded entitlement; new declarations created during the read-only window inherit the auto-publish path if the §22.14.3 evidence rule passes. No data loss; the surface compresses to chip-list-only.

**PostHog telemetry.** Two new events register in Appendix G:

- `capability_declaration_solo_free_auto_published {seller_org_id, capability_declaration_id, canonical_capability_id, evidence_kb_entry_ids_count, source_capability ∈ {kb_to_capability_suggestion, maya_added_chip}, created_via}` — fires on every `(none) → published` direct transition per the new state-machine row 7a.
- `capability_declaration_chip_edited {seller_org_id, capability_declaration_id, edit_kind ∈ {add, remove, rename_display_label}, prior_display_label, new_display_label}` — fires on every Maya-side chip-list edit.

**Cross-references.** §3.13 Principle 9; §4.4.4 Capability Declaration entity & state machine; §4.8.2 CapabilityRegistryEntry; §21.4.1 #18 `kb_to_capability_suggestion`; §22.10.5 `agent_sourcera_kb_to_capability_v4`; §22.14.3 evidence-overlap rule; §22.18.3.5 KB-to-Capability auto-declaration pipeline; §22.18.4 KB Value Meter Seller Panel; §27.4 Match Score eligibility; §48.4 Signal Integrity Monitor; §48.8.7 AP10 (Capability Declarations auto-suggested, not manually authored on onboarding path); Appendix J `capability_declaration_pending_review_reason` registry; Appendix L `capability_declaration_state_machine` row 7a; Appendix M Capability Declaration row (existing) plus the new Phase 14.8 row authored in this phase.

### 22.20.3 Compression Rule 2 — KB Governance {#22.20.3-compression-rule-2-kb-governance}

**Rule.** On Solo / Free, the §22.5 KB Health Model, the §22.4 Lifecycle staleness transitions, the §22.4.4 namespace migrations, the §22.5 confidence-decay computation, the §21.4.1 #17 `kb_staleness_classifier` nightly batch, and the §22.4 semantic-deduplication prompt run **silently** in the engine. Per-entry "Needs review" badges, per-entry staleness pills, per-entry confidence-decay indicators, dedupe-merge prompts, and namespace-migration notifications are **not rendered** to Seller Maya. The only governance surface visible to Maya is a single weekly notification: *"We refreshed your knowledge base from your website — N new entries proposed."* (or, when the refresh produces no new entries, *"We checked your knowledge base this week — everything is up to date."*).

**Engine preservation contract.** Every staleness transition (§22.4 `kb_entry_state_machine` `active → review_due → review_overdue → flagged_stale`), every confidence-modifier recompute (§22.5 nightly job), every Firecrawl re-crawl delta (§22.3 channel #3 transitions), every semantic-deduplication candidate (§22.4 dedupe pipeline), every namespace migration (§22.4.4), and every audit-ledger row (`kb_entry.flagged_stale`, `kb_entry.review_due`, `kb_entry.dedupe_proposed`, etc., per §6.7) continues to fire identically to the paid-tier engine. The §22.5.3 KB Health dashboard continues to materialize per Org. The §22.18.4 Seller Panel "Health" position #5 continues to render (the panel is the per-§22.18.4.1 deliberate stake-reveal surface and is exempt from this compression — see "Exemption" note below). The `kb.entry.flagged_stale` webhook (§31, Appendix C) continues to fire for any seller with a registered webhook endpoint; webhook firing is engine-side and not affected by surface compression.

**The weekly notification surface.**

- **Cadence.** Once per ISO calendar week, scheduled at the seller Org's `notification_window_local_time` (default Wednesday 09:00 in the Org's `data_residency_region` business-hours window per §29.3 Notification Preferences). Configurable in Notification Settings (§29.3) as a single per-seller-Org toggle: *"Weekly KB summary"* (default on for sF; default off for sSt+ where the per-event surfaces continue to render). The setting is a single toggle — no per-event sub-controls on Solo / Free.
- **Content.** A single in-app inbox card and (subject to the seller's email opt-in per §41.4) a single email. Body: *"We refreshed your knowledge base from your website. **{N}** new entries are ready for you to review. **{M}** existing entries had their citations refreshed. Open your KB →"* where N is the count of `KBEntry` rows with `created_at` inside the trailing 7-day window and `created_via ∈ {firecrawl, kb_bootstrap_recrawl}`; M is the count of rows with `updated_at` inside the trailing 7-day window and `lifecycle_state = 'active'` (excludes Maya's manual edits). When N = 0 and M = 0 the card body compresses to *"We checked your knowledge base this week — everything is up to date. Open your KB →"*.
- **Per-entry detail surfacing.** The "Open your KB →" link routes to the §22.18.4 KB landing screen (the existing surface). On that screen, Solo / Free renders **a single aggregated "What changed this week" banner** at the top of the entry list with a count of (a) new entries, (b) refreshed entries, and (c) entries the engine flagged as needing Maya's input (the count of `flagged_stale` and `review_overdue` entries combined). Clicking the banner expands an inline sub-list of those entries with a one-tap "Mark reviewed" affordance per entry. No per-entry staleness badge appears in the main entry list on Solo / Free; the sub-list under the banner is the only surface where flagged entries are visually distinguished.
- **Empty state on first week.** A new Seller Org's first weekly notification fires the Wednesday following the Hero Moment regardless of whether the §22.10.3 `kb_bootstrap` has produced any new entries since the Hero Moment finished. The first week's body reads *"Your knowledge base is set up and ready. We'll let you know if anything changes."* with no count substitution.

**What stays silent on Solo / Free.**

- Per-entry "Needs review" badges in the entry list (the §22.5 transitions still fire, but the badge is not rendered).
- The §22.5.3 "KB health: 92%" composite-score widget on the Seller Dashboard. The §22.18.4 Seller Panel position #5 ("Health: 94%") continues to render — see the Exemption note below.
- The §22.4 dedupe prompt ("Possible duplicate of {entry name} — merge?"). On Solo / Free, the engine performs the dedup-similarity check and either auto-merges (when similarity ≥ 0.95 per the existing engine threshold and the source entries share `namespace_id`) or auto-archives the lower-confidence duplicate (when similarity ∈ [0.80, 0.95)) without any Maya prompt. The resulting merge / archive event writes to the audit ledger as `kb_entry.auto_merged` or `kb_entry.auto_archived` (Authored Extension audit-event actions) for forensic traceability. On the next weekly notification, the merged / archived counts roll into the "What changed" banner.
- The §22.4.4 namespace migration notifications. Migrations fire engine-side; Maya is not notified per-migration. The migrated entries continue to participate in retrieval; the namespace change is audit-logged.
- The §22.5 confidence-decay indicators per entry. Decay still computes; the score still feeds the §22.18.4 Seller Panel position #1–#5 aggregates and the §22.10.2 retrieval ranking.

**Exemption — the §22.18.4 KB Value Meter Seller Panel.** The §22.18.4 panel is a **deliberate stake-reveal surface** (§22.18.6.1, the first of three Stake-Reveal Moments). Per §22.18.4.1, the panel renders identically across all plan tiers including Free. §22.20.3 does NOT compress the panel; the "Health: 94%" position #5 continues to render on the panel for Solo / Free and the panel's §22.18.4.3 telemetry continues to fire. The compression in §22.20.3 applies to the per-entry, per-event governance surfaces — the badges, pills, prompts, and notifications enumerated above — not to the panel's intentional aggregate view of KB health as a stake-building surface. The two surfaces are reconcilable: the panel's Health % is an aggregate "your KB is healthy" stake signal; the per-entry badges are operational governance surfaces that overload Maya's first-30-seconds capacity.

**Edge cases.**

1. **Seller has registered a `kb.entry.flagged_stale` webhook endpoint.** The webhook continues to fire engine-side per §31. The notification suppression on Maya's UI does not affect webhook delivery. Sellers using webhooks for downstream automation (rare on Solo / Free; common on sGr+) get the engine-event stream; Maya's UI gets the weekly aggregate.
2. **Critical-staleness entry referenced in an active Bid Workspace draft.** When the §22.10.2 `agent_sourcera_first_pass_responder` cites a `flagged_stale` entry in a draft for a still-open Bid Workspace, the inline citation card (per `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §4.3.6 Citation chip behavior, polished in §22.20.6 below) renders a quiet *"This is from older content — review and update?"* affordance on hover. This is not a per-entry staleness badge in the entry list; it is a contextual surface that fires only when a stale entry is in active use during the Hero Moment / Stage 4 review. The compression suppresses the entry-list badge; it does NOT suppress the contextual hover annotation, because the contextual annotation is the surface where Maya needs the information to make a decision about the in-flight draft.
3. **Weekly notification fires on a holiday in the Org's residency region.** The notification scheduler observes the Org's `data_residency_region` business-hours window per §29.3; if the scheduled hour falls on a regional public holiday, the notification defers to the next business day in the same week. Notifications are not skipped — the compression depends on Maya seeing the weekly aggregate; missing a week would degrade to per-event surfacing the following week.
4. **N + M = 0 for four consecutive weeks (KB has no activity).** The notification continues to fire weekly with the "everything is up to date" copy. The cadence does not adapt down to keep the cardinality of Maya's inbox stable. After 12 consecutive zero-activity weeks, a quiet inline annotation on the weekly notification reads *"You haven't added to your knowledge base in a while. Want to schedule a quick refresh?"* with a CTA that re-runs Firecrawl from the seller's existing source URLs. No upsell.
5. **Seller has zero KB entries and zero Firecrawl sources (extreme empty state).** The weekly notification suppresses entirely until the seller has at least one Firecrawl source registered or one manual KB entry; the inline §22.18.4.1 empty-state copy on the KB landing screen is the only governance surface for an empty-KB seller.

**PostHog telemetry.** Three events register in Appendix G:

- `kb_governance_weekly_notification_rendered {seller_org_id, in_app_rendered=true, email_sent ∈ {true, false, suppressed_by_user}, new_entry_count, refreshed_entry_count, flagged_count, plan_tier}` — fires on every weekly notification dispatch (weekly cadence per Org).
- `kb_governance_what_changed_banner_clicked {seller_org_id, banner_kind ∈ {new, refreshed, flagged}, expanded_sub_list_count, viewer_user_id}` — fires on banner expand on the KB landing screen.
- `kb_governance_silent_engine_event_count_rollup {seller_org_id, period_start, period_end, kb_entry_flagged_stale_count, kb_entry_review_overdue_count, kb_entry_auto_merged_count, kb_entry_auto_archived_count, kb_namespace_migrated_count}` — internal diagnostic, fires nightly with the prior 24-hour rollup so Ops can monitor that engine activity is unchanged across the surface compression.

**Cross-references.** §3.13 Principle 9; §22.4 KB Entry Lifecycle; §22.5 KB Health Model; §22.4.4 Namespace Migrations; §22.18.4 KB Value Meter Seller Panel (exempt); §22.18.6.1 Stake-Reveal Moment 1; §21.4.1 #17 `kb_staleness_classifier`; §29.3 Notification Preferences; §31 Webhooks (engine-side firing preserved); §41.4 Email Opt-Out; §6.7 Audit Ledger; Appendix M KB Health Model row plus the new Phase 14.8 row authored in this phase.

### 22.20.4 Compression Rule 3 — Match Scoring Three-Label Compression {#22.20.4-compression-rule-3-match-scoring-three-label-compression}

**Rule.** On Solo / Free, the §27.4 Marketplace Match Score numeric value, the per-feature contribution panel, the SHAP-style provenance arrows, and the model-version-id audit receipt are **not rendered** to Seller Maya. The surface compresses to **three labels exactly**: **Strong match** / **Likely match** / **Weak match**. Insufficient-signal cases (where §27.4 today renders a fourth "Insufficient signal" label and §27.4.10 the residency-incompatible 0-score short-circuit banner) are handled per the special-case mapping below. The numeric score, the provenance panel, and the model audit fields continue to compute and persist engine-side; only the surface rendering compresses.

**Engine preservation contract.** Every `MarketplaceMatchScoreSnapshot` row (§27.4.9) is computed and stored identically to paid-tier behavior. The score's feature vector, model-version-id, residency-compatibility flag, abuse-suppression flag, and feedback row are all written to the snapshot. The §27.4.7 cache-invalidation webhooks continue to fire for sellers with registered endpoints. The §27.4.11 feedback CTA ("This match seems wrong — tell us") continues to render; the feedback row writes the engine-side numeric score regardless of which label Maya saw. Buyer-side surfaces continue to render their own per-tier rendering per §27.4 (Buyer Free / Starter sees the existing four-label set; Buyer Growth+ sees numeric + provenance) — buyer-side surfacing is independent of seller-side rendering.

**Three-label compression mapping.** The four engine buckets per §27.4 Surface Bucketing collapse to three Solo / Free labels per the table below. The bucket boundaries (`strong_match_lower`, `moderate_match_lower`, `weak_match_lower`, `insufficient_signal_threshold`) are unchanged engine-side; the rendering layer applies the compression. The §27.4 numeric ranges referenced below are the existing engine ranges (Phase 14.8 does not introduce new range thresholds; the compression is purely a label rename and a fourth-bucket merge).

| Engine bucket (§27.4) | Numeric range | Solo / Free surface label | Rationale |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `strong_match` | ≥ 0.75 | **Strong match** | One-to-one rename; no semantic change. |
| `moderate_match` | [0.50, 0.75) | **Likely match** | Renamed for plain-language clarity ("moderate" reads as a quantitative hedge to a non-Sourcera-trained operator; "likely" carries a clear directional meaning). The internal bucket name is preserved for retrieval / API consumers. |
| `weak_match` | [0.30, 0.50) | **Weak match** | One-to-one rename; no semantic change. |
| `insufficient_signal` | < 0.30 OR k-anonymity floor not met OR `null_sentinel_flag = true` for ≥ 2 features | **Weak match** + quiet inline annotation *"We don't have a confident read on this one yet."* | Merged into "Weak match" on Solo / Free to keep the surface to three labels exactly; the inline annotation differentiates from a true `weak_match` so Maya understands the signal is thin without exposing the engine's `insufficient_signal` bucket name. |
| `residency_incompatible` (§27.4.10 hard gate; final score = 0) | n/a (hard short-circuit) | (Surface suppressed entirely — the candidate does not appear in the directory render) | Per existing §27.4.10 surface contract: the §22.20.4 compression does not change this behavior; the candidate is not rendered, no label appears, the existing buyer-facing residency-incompatible banner per §27.4.4 is buyer-side and unaffected. |
| `abuse_report_pending_suppression` (§27.4.3 soft gate) | n/a | (Surface suppressed entirely on Solo / Free; the existing "Under review — score temporarily suppressed" provenance note is not rendered) | The provenance-note surface depends on the provenance panel that is itself suppressed on Solo / Free per §22.20.4; the candidate is filtered out of the seller's directory render. The score remains suppressed at the buyer-side surface per the existing §27.4.3 contract. |
| `vendor_opt_out_effective_flag = true` (§27.4.4) | n/a | (Already engine-only per Appendix M — no surface change) | Preserved. |

**Where the labels render.**

The three-label compression renders on every seller-side surface that today renders the §27.4 score:

1. **Buyer-Interest weekly digest (§24.5 Seller Analytics surface) and the Marketplace Listings (Seller) page (`UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §4.3.10).** Each Marketplace Listing card renders a *"Match: {label}"* chip below the buyer-org display name. No numeric score, no contribution arrows, no model-version receipt.
2. **The Bid Workspace populator's "Why this bid?" inline contextual panel (per `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §4.3.3).** When Maya opens a bid invitation, the populator renders a single-line annotation: *"This bid is a {label} for what you offer."* No provenance arrows; no per-feature breakdown; no AIOperation cost. The annotation links to the chip-list (§22.20.2) so Maya can adjust her categories if the match feels wrong.
3. **The §27.5 EOI Marketplace card preview.** When Maya browses an open Marketplace Listing (zero EOIs available on Solo / Free per §27.5; the surface is browse-only), each Listing card renders the *"Match: {label}"* chip. The browse-only state is preserved per §27.5; the chip is rendered alongside the existing browse-only affordances.

**Match Score Feedback CTA preservation.** The §27.4.11 *"This match seems wrong — tell us"* CTA renders on every label render per the existing §27.4 contract. Clicking the CTA opens the existing feedback surface; the feedback row writes the engine-side numeric score per the existing schema. The CTA copy is unchanged (the §27.4.11 contract renders one CTA copy across plan tiers; tier-specific copy variants would degrade the feedback signal's cross-tier comparability).

**Provenance suppression (Solo / Free).** The §27.4.6 provenance panel ("Why this match?" → SHAP-style positive / negative arrows + three-bucket magnitude) is **not rendered** on Solo / Free. The panel surfaces on sGr+ unchanged. On Solo / Free, the inline *"Match: {label}"* chip is non-clickable for provenance; clicking it opens the §22.20.2 chip-list edit drawer (so Maya can adjust her discoverable categories) rather than the provenance panel. This is a deliberate routing decision: on Solo / Free, the actionable "make this match better" path is "fix what categories you appear in," not "understand the model's feature attribution."

**Edge cases.**

1. **Maya upgrades to sSt during a session.** The label render persists for the current session render; on next page render the upgraded surface (numeric score + provenance panel per existing §27.4) becomes available. No score-snapshot recomputation is required because the engine score has been computed identically throughout.
2. **Match Score has not yet been computed for a fresh listing (cache miss).** The §27.4 cache-miss path renders the existing "Computing…" state; Solo / Free uses the same cache-miss state copy. On compute completion, the chip renders the appropriate label.
3. **Maya is browsing a category where her seller Org has zero `CapabilityDeclaration` rows that match.** The §27.4 score is computed against an empty category-overlap; the engine returns `< 0.30` and the surface renders **Weak match** with the *"We don't have a confident read on this one yet."* annotation. The annotation routes Maya to the §22.20.2 chip-list edit drawer with the missing category pre-filled as a "Suggested addition."
4. **Buyer side is on sScale and uses the Match Score numeric audit receipt.** Buyer-side rendering is unaffected by §22.20.4. The seller Org's plan tier governs only the seller-side surface; buyer-side rendering follows §27.4 buyer-tier gates.
5. **Existing `match_score_numeric` AIOperation invoked by a tier-eligible buyer.** The §21.4.2 `match_score_numeric` capability per §22.10 (capability-id namespace per §22.10.1.A) is buyer-side only. Solo / Free seller surfaces do not invoke or render numeric scores; the on-demand numeric pathway is buyer-billed and seller-side rendering is unchanged on Solo / Free.

**PostHog telemetry.** Two events register in Appendix G:

- `marketplace_match_label_rendered {seller_org_id, listing_id, surface ∈ {weekly_digest, marketplace_card, bid_populator_inline, eoi_card_preview}, label ∈ {strong_match, likely_match, weak_match}, insufficient_signal_annotation_rendered ∈ {true, false}, plan_tier}` — fires on every label render to a Solo / Free seller surface.
- `marketplace_match_label_chip_clicked {seller_org_id, listing_id, surface, label, click_routed_to ∈ {chip_list_edit_drawer, feedback_cta, expanded_card}}` — fires on every chip click on a Solo / Free seller surface.

The existing §27.4 numeric-score telemetry events (`marketplace_match_score_computed`, `marketplace_match_score_rendered_to_buyer`, etc.) continue to fire engine-side per the existing contract; no event is renamed or removed.

**Cross-references.** §3.13 Principle 9; §27.4 Marketplace Match Score (existing contract); §27.4.6 provenance panel; §27.4.10 residency incompatibility hard gate; §27.4.11 Match Score Feedback; §22.20.2 chip-list edit drawer (the routing target for chip clicks on Solo / Free); §27.5 EOI surface; §24.5 Seller Analytics; `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §4.3.3 Bid Workspace Detail / §4.3.10 Marketplace Listings (Seller); Appendix M Marketplace Match Score row plus the new Phase 14.8 row authored in this phase.

### 22.20.5 Compression Rule 4 — AIOp Consumption (Cross-Reference) {#22.20.5-compression-rule-4-aiop-consumption-cross-reference}

**Rule.** On Solo / Free, the §4.8.1 AIOperation ledger, the §34.10 AIWallet balance counter, the §34.6 settlement-state copy ("accepted," "auto-accepted," "rejected"), the per-capability cost-base, the value-price multiplier (`× 10`), and the cost-priced-rejected accounting line are **not rendered** to Seller Maya. Solo / Free presents AI as **always-included, never-counted**. Per Phase 14.10's authoritative §44 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment authoring, the Hero Moment AI consumption (kb_bootstrap, first-pass response generation, q_and_a_suggestion fallback, kb_to_capability auto-publish) is hidden behind a single per-Org AI envelope; the engine continues to settle each AIOperation per §34.6 / §34.11 OutcomeContract semantics; the surface compresses to silence.

**Authority.** This rule cross-references and does not duplicate Phase 14.10's §44 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment. §22.20.5 binds the §22 surfaces (KB Editor, KB landing screen, Bid Workspace populator, Hero Moment Stage 4 review surface, Stake-Reveal Screen, Seller Q&A draft surface) to the §44 compression contract; the §44 authoring is the engine-side cost-absorption and throttling contract. Conflicts between §22.20.5 and §44 are resolved in favor of §44 for engine semantics and in favor of §22.20.5 for the §22-surface rendering. The AIWallet balance counter that previously rendered on the §48.8.4 Hero Moment in-workspace value-proof surface (per the existing §48.8.4 UX Surface Specification "Live AIWallet budget counter") MUST NOT render on Solo / Free per the §22.20.5 / §44 compression; the surface compresses to a silent engine. The §48.8.4 surface specification is updated by §22.20.5 / §44 to suppress the counter on Solo / Free; the counter render contract is preserved on sSt+. The corresponding §48.8.4 acceptance criteria (AC #13 AIWallet counter freshness, AC #17 AIWallet exhaustion path) continue to apply on sSt+ and are silently bypassed on sF (the engine continues to preserve the cost-priced-rejected fallback per §34.10; the surface change is the suppression of the counter, not the suppression of the engine fallback).

**What stays silent on Solo / Free.**

- The "Live AIWallet budget counter" at top of the Bid Workspace per §48.8.4.
- Per-AIOperation cost lines on the Stake-Reveal Screen ("Sourcera tracked $Y.YY of value pricing for the AI work on this bid") per §48.8.5 Stage-5 Workflow #3. The Stake-Reveal Screen on Solo / Free renders the value summary in non-monetary terms — *"You just built a reusable knowledge base of N verified entries in X minutes."* — without the monetary accounting line. The remaining Stake-Reveal surface (entry count, time invested, stake-building copy) is preserved.
- The §34.10.4 lifetime-free allowance counter (`{N} of 10 free runs left` inline near AI buttons per Appendix M FreeAllowanceCounter row). On Solo / Free, the counter is suppressed; the underlying counter continues to track engine-side.
- The §32.8 billing API surfaces. Solo / Free sellers retain API access per §32 generic plan-tier gates; the billing endpoints remain accessible on the seller's API key but are not surfaced in the in-app Settings → Billing surface.
- The §34.11 OutcomeContract settlement-state copy ("Charge appears on your wallet within {N} days of completion") on AI-using surfaces. On Solo / Free, the inline note is suppressed entirely.

**What surfaces on Solo / Free.**

A single, plain-language affordance on the Settings → Plan & Billing surface: *"AI is included with your plan. We'll let you know if your usage gets close to a fair-use limit."* No counter, no $-figure, no rate-card link. The link to the public Pricing page (§4.8.9) remains in the footer for seller-initiated discovery; no in-app upsell is rendered per §48.8.7 AP6 (banned: pricing page shown before first bid).

**Edge cases.**

1. **Solo / Free seller hits the §44 fair-use throttle.** Per Phase 14.10 §44 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment, the throttle activates a degraded mode (longer first-pass response queue, reduced `kb_to_capability_suggestion` cadence) without surfacing a wallet exhaustion banner. The seller sees the existing §48.8.4 "AI drafts are temporarily unavailable — try again in a few minutes" copy from the existing capability-degradation path; the copy is unchanged from the paid-tier degradation copy. The throttle event is logged engine-side per §44.
2. **Solo / Free seller upgrades to sSt mid-Hero-Moment.** The AIWallet counter renders immediately on the upgraded surface; engine-side billing for the post-upgrade AIOperations continues normally. Pre-upgrade AIOperations remain Solo / Free-absorbed per the §44 contract; no retroactive billing.
3. **Solo / Free seller's `cost_priced_rejected_cents_accumulated` exceeds the §44 envelope.** Per §44, the engine fires `seller_aiwallet_solo_envelope_exhausted` (Phase 14.10 event) to Ops; the seller surface continues to render the silent-AI surface per §22.20.5 with the existing degradation behavior. Ops may proactively reach out to the seller; no automatic in-app upsell.

**PostHog telemetry.** §22.20.5 introduces no new events; the Phase 14.10 §44 telemetry registry is authoritative. The §22.20.5 contribution is to assert that the Solo / Free seller-surface rendering of `aiwallet_counter_freshness_breach` (§48.8.4) and `seller_aiwallet_budget_exhausted_during_onboarding` (§48.8.4) is suppressed; the events continue to fire engine-side as internal diagnostics.

**Cross-references.** §3.13 Principle 9; §44 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment (Phase 14.10 — authoritative); §4.8.1 AIOperation; §34.10 AIWallet; §34.11 OutcomeContract; §48.8.4 Hero Moment in-workspace value proof (counter suppressed on sF); §48.8.5 Post-Submission Reveal (monetary accounting line suppressed on sF); §48.8.7 AP6 (no pricing page before first bid); Appendix M AIWallet / Free Allowance / Outcome Resolver rows plus the new Phase 14.8 cross-reference row authored in this phase.

### 22.20.6 Magic-Link Hero Moment Surface Polish {#22.20.6-magic-link-hero-moment-surface-polish}

**Authoring intent.** §22.20.6 is the §22-side binding contract for the Phase 14.8 polish of the Seller Magic-Link Hero Moment Landing surface. The surface itself — including its DOM, motion, accessibility, mobile rendering, and copy — is authored in `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §4.4.2 Phase-14.8 Seller Magic-Link Hero Moment Landing Polish (authored in this same phase). §22.20.6 is the engine-binding companion: it specifies which engine reads the polish surface depends on, which compression rules from §22.20.2 / §22.20.3 / §22.20.4 / §22.20.5 the polish surface must enforce, and the acceptance criteria the surface must satisfy from the §22 perspective.

**Surface elements polished in Phase 14.8 (per `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §4.4.2 Phase-14.8 polish).**

1. **Domain bootstrap progress narrative.** The §48.8.3 progress storytelling ("Scanning yourcompany.com…", "Found your security documentation…", "Drafting responses for [Buyer Company]'s 82 requirements…", "Your bid is ready to review.") is preserved as authored. Phase 14.8 polish refines the second status-line copy when the Firecrawl crawl resolves a non-security source page first ("Found your help center…", "Found your product docs…", etc.) so the literal-truth invariant per §48.8.3 AC #8 is preserved across Firecrawl resolution variance. The status-line variant set is registered as `firecrawl_resolution_status_line_variant_enum` (Authored Extension, Appendix J — five values: `security_documentation`, `help_center`, `product_docs`, `api_docs`, `trust_center`) and the variant is selected at render time based on the first Firecrawl-resolved page's category tag. Engine-side: no change to the §48.8.2 pre-arrival preparation or §48.8.3 workflow.
2. **Hero Moment counters.** The §48.8.3 landing counter per Workflow #7 ("Your bid is ready. **{N}** AI drafts prepared. **{M}** cite evidence from your website. Review time: **~{X} min**.") is preserved. Phase 14.8 polish adds a fourth counter line, conditional on N ≥ 1 AND M ≥ 1: *"**{P}** answers ready to review with one click."* where P is the count of first-pass drafts that pass the §22.10.2 `cite_verify` validation AND have `confidence_score ≥ 0.85` (the "ready-to-accept-without-edit" subset). The counter is computed at first paint of the Bid Workspace from the same `SellerOnboardingSession.stage_3_*` fields per §48.8.3; no new field is required. When P = 0, the fourth line is suppressed.
3. **Inline citation hover behavior.** The §22.7 / §48.8.4 Citation Inline Card hover behavior is preserved. Phase 14.8 polish adds the §22.20.3 staleness-aware contextual annotation per §22.20.3 Edge Case #2: when the hovered citation references a `flagged_stale` or `review_overdue` entry, the card renders a quiet *"This is from older content — review and update?"* affordance below the existing citation source link. The affordance routes to the entry's edit page; the entry-list per-entry staleness badge remains suppressed on Solo / Free per §22.20.3.
4. **KB-gap detector empty state.** The §48.8.4 Workflow #5 KB-Gap Detector ("No KB content answered this. Write your answer below and we'll save it as a KB entry.") is preserved. Phase 14.8 polish adds an empty-state affordance for the case where Maya hits a Reject and the seller's KB is entirely empty (Hero Moment first-time-with-no-bootstrap path): below the textarea, render a quiet *"Tip: anything you write here teaches your knowledge base. Future bids reuse it automatically."* annotation. The annotation is hidden when the seller's KB has ≥ 5 entries (the threshold below which the educational copy is most useful). Engine-side: no change to the §22.4 KB Entry Lifecycle.
5. **Stake-reveal screen on submission.** The §48.8.5 Stake-Reveal Screen Workflow #2–#7 is preserved. Phase 14.8 polish: per §22.20.5, the §48.8.5 Workflow #3 monetary accounting line ("Sourcera tracked $Y.YY of value pricing…") is suppressed on Solo / Free, replaced with a non-monetary stake summary ("You captured **{Q}** answers worth saving. Your next bid starts here."), where Q is the count of session-created KBEntries with `lifecycle_state = 'active'` per §48.8.5 Workflow #2. The §22.18.6 Stake-Reveal Moment 1 telemetry continues to fire per existing §22.18.6.4.

**Engine-binding contracts.** The polish surface depends on the following engine reads, all of which are pre-existing and unchanged by Phase 14.8:

- `SellerOnboardingSession.stage_3_population_latency_ms`, `stage_3_kb_draft_entry_count`, `stage_3_first_pass_response_requirement_count`, `stage_3_first_pass_response_cited_count` (§4.4.22).
- `KBEntry.confidence_score` (§22.3.1) for the "ready-to-accept-without-edit" P counter.
- `KBEntry.status` (§22.3.1; projected as `review_state` in API payloads) for the inline citation staleness annotation.
- `Firecrawl.first_resolved_page_category` (§22.6) for the bootstrap progress narrative variant selection — Authored Extension field flagged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Phase 14.8` (the §22.6 entity does not currently expose this denormalization; engineering will materialize it during Phase 14.8 implementation).
- `CapabilityDeclaration.state` and `display_label_override` (§4.4.4 + §22.20.2 Authored Extension) for the chip-list rendering on Stake-Reveal Stage 5.

**Acceptance criteria are the §22.20.7 set (below); UX-side acceptance criteria are authored in `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` §4.4.2 Phase-14.8 polish.**

### 22.20.7 Acceptance Criteria {#22.20.7-acceptance-criteria}

The acceptance criteria below extend the §22 numeric series. Items 79–98 are authored in Phase 14.8.

79. **Capability Declaration auto-publish on Solo / Free.** Every Capability Declaration emitted by `kb_to_capability_suggestion` (§22.10.5) on a `plan_tier = seller_free` Org MUST transition `(none) → published` directly via `pending_review_reason = 'solo_free_auto_publish'` when the four preconditions (§22.20.2 state-machine extension) are met. QA test `capability_declaration_solo_free_auto_publish_state_transition` asserts under a synthetic 1,000-entry KB harness across 100 Solo / Free Orgs.
80. **Auto-publish preserves §22.14.3 evidence rule.** Every auto-published Capability Declaration MUST cite ≥ 3 KB entries sharing at least one overlapping `topic_tags` value. QA test `capability_declaration_auto_publish_evidence_overlap` asserts; rejection rate against the existing §22.14.3 validator MUST be 0% for auto-published rows (per the precondition).
81. **Chip-list rendering parity with auto-publish.** Every auto-published Capability Declaration with `state = 'published'` MUST render in the §22.20.2 chip-list within 60 seconds of the §22.18.3.5 nightly batch completion (cache TTL aligned to the §22.18.4 Seller Panel cadence). UX fixture test asserts the chip count on a synthetic Org matches the COUNT of `state = 'published'` rows.
82. **Chip-list editability — add.** The chip-list "+ Add" affordance MUST open a typeahead picker against `CapabilityRegistryEntry` with autocomplete latency p95 ≤ 300 ms. On selection, a new `CapabilityDeclaration` row MUST be written with `created_via = 'maya_added_chip'` and rendered as a chip within 1 second of save. QA test `chip_list_add_latency` asserts.
83. **Chip-list editability — remove.** Clicking the chip's `×` icon MUST transition the underlying `CapabilityDeclaration` row to `state = 'deprecated'` within 500 ms p95. Buyer-side Match Score participation MUST drop within the existing §27.4 freshness window (≤ 24 h). QA test `chip_list_remove_state_transition` asserts.
84. **Chip-list editability — rename display label.** The `display_label_override` write MUST persist within 500 ms p95 and the chip rendering MUST update on the seller's profile-public-page render within 60 seconds. The buyer-side directory MUST continue to render the canonical `CapabilityRegistryEntry.display_name` (the override is seller-side only); a property test asserts cross-console label divergence.
85. **No `pending_review` queue surfaces on Solo / Free.** A UX fixture test asserts that no element labeled "Pending review", "Submitted for approval", "Awaiting Ops review", or any equivalent copy renders on any Solo / Free Seller Console surface for an Org whose only Capability Declarations are auto-published. Copy-string lint rule asserts.
86. **Weekly KB governance notification cadence.** Every `plan_tier = seller_free` Org with at least one Firecrawl source registered OR at least one manual KBEntry MUST receive exactly one weekly KB governance notification per ISO calendar week, scheduled at the Org's `notification_window_local_time`. Holiday deferrals to the next business day are permitted within the same week. QA test `kb_governance_weekly_cadence_solo_free` asserts under a 90-day synthetic harness across 100 Orgs.
87. **Per-entry staleness badge suppression on Solo / Free.** A UX fixture test asserts that no per-entry staleness badge (`needs_review`, `flagged_stale`, `review_overdue`, `confidence_decay`) renders on the §22.18.4 KB landing screen entry list for a Solo / Free seller Org. The §22.18.4 Seller Panel position #5 ("Health: 94%") continues to render per the §22.20.3 exemption; a UX fixture test asserts the panel renders identically across all tiers per the existing §22.18.4.1 contract.
88. **What-changed banner aggregation.** The "What changed this week" banner on the §22.18.4 KB landing screen MUST render the correct count of new + refreshed + flagged entries for the trailing 7-day window within 5-second p95 freshness of the underlying engine writes. QA test `what_changed_banner_aggregation` asserts.
89. **Engine-side governance events fire identically across tiers.** The PostHog event `kb_governance_silent_engine_event_count_rollup` MUST report event counts for Solo / Free Orgs that are statistically indistinguishable (within 5% on a 90-day rolling window) from sSt+ Orgs of comparable KB size. QA test `kb_governance_engine_parity_solo_vs_paid` asserts.
90. **`kb.entry.flagged_stale` webhook firing preserved.** The `kb.entry.flagged_stale` webhook MUST fire for every flagged-stale transition per §31, regardless of the seller Org's plan tier. QA test `kb_flagged_stale_webhook_solo_free` asserts on a synthetic Solo / Free Org with a registered webhook endpoint.
91. **Match Score three-label compression.** Every Marketplace Listing card render on a Solo / Free seller surface MUST render exactly one of three labels (**Strong match**, **Likely match**, **Weak match**); no fourth label, no numeric score, no provenance arrows MUST appear. UX fixture test asserts across the four engine buckets per §22.20.4 mapping.
92. **Insufficient-signal annotation.** The *"We don't have a confident read on this one yet."* annotation MUST render exactly when the engine bucket is `insufficient_signal` AND the surface label is **Weak match**. QA test `insufficient_signal_annotation_render` asserts the conjunction.
93. **`MarketplaceMatchScoreSnapshot` engine writes preserved.** Every Marketplace card render on a Solo / Free seller surface MUST persist a `MarketplaceMatchScoreSnapshot` row with the same field-vector schema as paid-tier renders. QA test `match_score_snapshot_engine_parity_solo_vs_paid` asserts.
94. **Match Score Feedback CTA preserved.** The §27.4.11 *"This match seems wrong — tell us"* CTA MUST render on every label render to a Solo / Free seller surface. The feedback row MUST write the engine-side numeric score (not the compressed label). QA test `match_score_feedback_numeric_persistence_solo_free` asserts.
95. **AIWallet counter suppression on Solo / Free.** A UX fixture test asserts that no AIWallet balance counter, no `{X} of {Y}` value-dollar display, and no per-AIOperation cost line render on the §48.8.3 / §48.8.4 / §48.8.5 Hero Moment surfaces for a `plan_tier = seller_free` Org. The §48.8.5 Stake-Reveal Workflow #3 monetary accounting line MUST be replaced with the §22.20.6 non-monetary stake summary copy.
96. **§22.18.4 Seller Panel exempt from §22.20.5.** The §22.18.4 KB Value Meter Seller Panel position #4 ("Estimated value: $1,275/yr saved response time") MUST render identically across all plan tiers per §22.18.4.1; §22.20.5 does NOT compress the panel. UX fixture test asserts that the panel renders unchanged on Solo / Free vs. sSt+ Orgs of comparable KB size.
97. **Magic-Link Hero Moment polish — Stake-Reveal non-monetary copy.** The §48.8.5 Stake-Reveal Screen on a Solo / Free seller MUST render the non-monetary stake summary copy *"You captured **{Q}** answers worth saving. Your next bid starts here."* with Q populated from the engine-computed session-created KBEntry count. UX fixture snapshot test asserts; copy drift fails CI.
98. **Magic-Link Hero Moment polish — fourth counter line.** The §48.8.3 landing counter MUST render the fourth line *"**{P}** answers ready to review with one click."* exactly when P ≥ 1 (i.e., at least one first-pass draft passes `cite_verify` AND has `confidence_score ≥ 0.85`); when P = 0, the fourth line MUST NOT render. UX fixture test asserts both branches.

**Failure Modes Addressed (Counterfactual Pass — three per compression rule).**

- **Capability Declarations auto-publish (§22.20.2) failure modes:** (1) Auto-publish writes a row with `evidence_kb_entry_ids[]` count < 3 due to a §22.14.3 validator regression — prevented by AC #80 + the §4.4.4 invariant #4 retained at the (none) → published transition. (2) The §22.10.5 `agent_sourcera_kb_to_capability_v4` agent fails to resolve a `canonical_capability_id` for a viable cluster — engine falls through to the existing `pending_review` path; chip does not appear; weekly KB governance notification surfaces the missing-categories signal as an inline annotation on the next refresh. (3) An auto-published declaration is later quarantined by §48.4 SIM — chip disappears with the §22.20.2 Edge Case #3 plain-English remediation copy; no engine concept leaks.
- **KB Governance silent-engine (§22.20.3) failure modes:** (1) The weekly notification fails to dispatch due to a §29.5 webhook-channel outage — the in-app inbox card still renders (in-app and email are independent dispatch paths per §29.2); the email retry curve (§29.7) handles the email path. (2) A high-staleness entry referenced in an active draft is hidden by the entry-list compression — prevented by §22.20.3 Edge Case #2 (the inline citation card surfaces the contextual annotation when the entry is in active use). (3) Engine governance events fire at materially different rates on Solo / Free vs. paid tiers, signaling a hidden engine divergence — prevented by AC #89 telemetry parity and the `kb_governance_silent_engine_event_count_rollup` nightly diagnostic.
- **Match Score three-label compression (§22.20.4) failure modes:** (1) The four-label-to-three-label mapping leaks a numeric score in a tooltip or hover panel — prevented by AC #91 fixture test enumerating every DOM element on the Solo / Free seller-side surface. (2) The Match Score Feedback CTA writes the surface label instead of the engine numeric score, polluting the feedback signal's cross-tier comparability — prevented by AC #94 numeric persistence. (3) Maya disputes a "Weak match" that is actually an `insufficient_signal` and the routing to the chip-list edit drawer is wrong — addressed by §22.20.4 Edge Case #3 (the annotation routes to chip-list with the missing category pre-filled as a "Suggested addition").
- **AIOp consumption suppression (§22.20.5) failure modes:** (1) The §48.8.4 AIWallet counter is accidentally rendered on a Solo / Free Hero Moment surface due to a feature-flag misconfiguration — prevented by AC #95 fixture test. (2) The §44 fair-use throttle activates and Maya sees a wallet exhaustion banner — prevented by §22.20.5 Edge Case #1 (the existing §48.8.4 capability-degradation copy is reused; no wallet exhaustion banner). (3) The §32.8 billing API returns Solo / Free `cost_priced_rejected_cents_accumulated` data via a public seller-API call — addressed by Phase 14.10 §44 contract; §22.20.5 cross-references and does not duplicate.

**Authored Extensions (registered; require human sign-off).**

1. §4.4.4 `pending_review_reason` enum extension: `solo_free_auto_publish`. Phase 13 schema consolidation will confirm the enum registration in Appendix J `capability_declaration_pending_review_reason`.
2. §4.4.4 state-machine row 7a: `(none) → published` direct transition under `solo_free_auto_publish`. Appendix L `capability_declaration_state_machine` updated.
3. §4.4.4 `display_label_override` field (`String, nullable, ≤ 50 chars`). Phase 13 will extend the §4.4.4 entity field table.
4. §4.4.4 `created_via` enum extensions: `kb_to_capability_suggestion_solo_free_auto_publish`, `maya_added_chip`. Phase 13 will register in Appendix J.
5. §6.7 audit-event action extensions: `capability_declaration_chip_added`, `capability_declaration_chip_removed`, `capability_declaration_chip_renamed`, `kb_entry.auto_merged`, `kb_entry.auto_archived`. Appendix J `audit_event_action_type` (KB additions sub-section) extended; these actions MUST NOT be registered under the Billing Admin Audit Action namespace.
6. Appendix J `firecrawl_resolution_status_line_variant_enum` (5 values: `security_documentation`, `help_center`, `product_docs`, `api_docs`, `trust_center`). Used by §22.20.6 polish.
7. §22.6 Firecrawl entity denormalization: `first_resolved_page_category` field. Phase 13 will extend the §22.6 entity field table.
8. PostHog events (Appendix G): `capability_declaration_solo_free_auto_published`, `capability_declaration_chip_edited`, `kb_governance_weekly_notification_rendered`, `kb_governance_what_changed_banner_clicked`, `kb_governance_silent_engine_event_count_rollup`, `marketplace_match_label_rendered`, `marketplace_match_label_chip_clicked`.
9. CI gate: `seller_maya_surface_abstraction_engine_unchanged` — deploy-time validator asserts that no §4.4.4, §22.5, §27.4, or §44 engine field is mutated as a side effect of the §22.20 surface compression. Phase 14.18 implements.
10. Buyer-funded Pro Trial Seat (M17 / §34.13) inheritance: the §22.20 compression rules also apply during the trial window, since the trial surfaces the Solo / Free-equivalent rendering. Phase 13 will register the inheritance contract in §34.13.

- §44 (Performance Budgets — Solo-Tier Surface Treatment): authoritative for §22.20.5 AIOp consumption invisibility (Phase 14.10).
- §48.4 (Signal Integrity Monitor): preserved engine-side; §22.20.2 routes quarantines through chip-disappear plain-English copy.
