# 23\. Seller Console — Bid Workspace & Response Management {#23.-seller-console-—-bid-workspace-&-response-management}

## 23.1 Bid Workspace Overview {#23.1-bid-workspace-overview}

A Bid Workspace is created in the vendor's Seller Console for each buyer evaluation they participate in. It mirrors the buyer's evaluation structure (Use Cases → Requirements) but presents a vendor-specific response interface. The Bid Workspace is read-only for all requirements and Use Cases — the vendor cannot edit them. The vendor can only respond to Requirements via the Response form.

**Bid Workspace fields:**

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `bid_workspace_id` | UUID | Same as `workspace_id` with `console = seller` |
| `buyer_workspace_id` | UUID | FK to buyer's Workspace |
| `bid_owner_id` | UUID | FK User. Single owner. Required. |
| `status` | Enum | `invited`, `nda_pending`, `nda_signed`, `active`, `submitted`, `disqualified`, `withdrawn`, `canceled` |
| `submission_deadline` | Timestamp | Buyer-set deadline for vendor response submission. Read-only. |
| `phase` | Integer (1–13) | Mirrors buyer workspace phase. Determines visibility of requirements. |

## 23.2 Response Lock & Concurrency Control {#23.2-response-lock-&-concurrency-control}

**Problem:** Two users editing the same response simultaneously causes merge conflicts.

**Solution:** Advisory lock at response level.

**Lock behavior:**

- When Vendor User A opens a response form for edit, a lock is acquired: `response.lock = { user_id: A, acquired_at: T, expires_at: T + 600s }`.  
- If Vendor User B tries to open the same response for edit, they see: "Currently being edited by \[User A\]. Changes are read-only. Try again in 10 minutes or force unlock."  
- The lock auto-releases after 10 minutes (600 seconds).  
- At T \+ 540s (9 minutes), User A sees a warning toast: "Your edit lock expires in 60 seconds. Save or your changes will be unlocked."  
- User A can extend the lock by clicking "Keep Editing" (adds 300 seconds).  
- User A can force-release by clicking "Done" button.  
- Force-unlock by User B requires confirmation: "Are you sure you want to unlock \[User A\]'s edit session? Their unsaved work will be lost."

**Lock implementation:** Advisory lock enforced at Convex mutation level via atomic compare-and-swap on `response.lock` field. No database-level locks.

**First-write-wins semantics:** If both users hit save simultaneously, the first to commit wins. The second sees: "This response was updated by another user. Your changes are shown below. \[Accept their changes\] \[Discard and keep mine\] \[Merge manually\]."

## 23.3 Response Submission {#23.3-response-submission}

For each requirement, the vendor submits a response matching the requirement's `response_type`:

- **Boolean:** Yes/No toggle. Auto-submitted upon selection.  
- **Qualitative:** Rich text (Markdown, 0–50,000 chars). Agent suggests from KB. Pre-filled via "Use This" on KB entry.  
- **Evidence:** File upload (up to 10 files, 50MB each) \+ optional text description (0–5,000 chars). Agent cross-references against requirement and surfaces summary with page citations. Evidence is locked in Phase 9+ per response.  
- **Informational:** Free text (0–50,000 chars). Not scored.  
- **Pricing:** Structured form matching the requirement's `pricing_config`. See Section 14.4.

**Response lifecycle:** `pending` → `draft` → `ready_for_review` → `submitted` → (optionally `needs_reverification` if buyer amends) → `locked` (Phase 9+).

**Bulk submit behavior (Gap 23.2):**

- Vendor clicks "Submit All" to submit all `draft` and `ready_for_review` responses at once.  
- Server validates all responses in a transaction.  
- If all valid: all submit successfully, status \= `submitted`, Bid Workspace status \= `submitted`.  
- If any invalid: partial success — N responses submitted successfully, M responses fail with error details listed: "4 responses submitted. 2 responses failed: \[Requirement Title\] — Response must include at least one file. \[Other Requirement Title\] — File exceeds size limit."  
- Failed responses remain in `draft` status and can be re-submitted.  
- User sees: "4 of 6 responses submitted successfully. \[2 errors\] \[Retry Failed\]"

## 23.4 Vendor Voluntary Withdrawal {#23.4-vendor-voluntary-withdrawal}

**Trigger:** Vendor clicks "Withdraw from Evaluation" in Bid Workspace settings.

**Workflow:**

1. Confirmation modal: "Are you sure you want to withdraw? Your responses will be saved but marked as withdrawn. This cannot be undone."  
2. Option to provide withdrawal reason (optional): "What prompted this withdrawal?" (text field, max 500 chars).  
3. On confirm: Bid Workspace status → `withdrawn`. Vendor notification email sent to Bid Owner.  
4. Buyer notification: Workspace Owner sees "Vendor \[Name\] has withdrawn from this evaluation." in Activity feed.  
5. Withdrawn vendor's responses remain in the system (`status = submitted` or `draft` at withdrawal time) but are excluded from Scoring phase (marked as "Not Participating" in scoring matrix).  
6. Withdrawal is permanent and irreversible within the same Workspace. If buyer wants to re-engage the vendor, a new Workspace must be created.

**Data retention:** All withdrawn responses are archived but retained for audit trail. Seller can export withdrawn responses to KB if desired.

## 23.5 Acceptance Criteria {#23.5-acceptance-criteria}

- Bid Workspace syncs buyer requirements within 5 seconds of Phase 6 entry.  
- Response form renders correct input type based on `response_type`.  
- KB suggestions appear within 2 seconds of opening a response form.  
- Response submission updates buyer-side view within 5 seconds.  
- Lock contention shows "Currently being edited by X" message.  
- Bulk submit shows partial success (N submitted, M failed with error list).  
- Withdrawal confirmation modal prevents accidental withdrawal.  
- Withdrawn vendor excluded from Scoring phase.

---

# 24\. Seller Console — Q\&A, NDA, Inbox & Pulse {#24.-seller-console-—-q&a,-nda,-inbox-&-pulse}

## 24.1 Seller Q\&A {#24.1-seller-q&a}

Vendors participate in Q\&A threads during Phase 7 (Q\&A Open). Behavior mirrors the buyer Q\&A contract in §18, but from the vendor perspective. The canonical conversation schema is §18.3.1; the seller-visible projection and firewall fields are cataloged at §4.4.2.1.

**Vendor-side behavior:**

- Vendor can view buyer-posted questions only when the §24.1.1 visibility matrix returns `visible`.  
- Vendor can post responses/clarifications.  
- Vendor cannot post questions to themselves.  
- Q\&A threads are read-only once Phase 8 begins (Q\&A Closed).

### 24.1.1 Seller Q&A Visibility Matrix {#24.1.1-seller-q&a-visibility-matrix}

The seller Q&A surface is NDA-gated and vendor-scoped. "All buyer-posted questions" means all buyer-authored questions visible to the current seller under this table, not all questions in the buyer Workspace and never questions directed only to another vendor. The `nda_visibility_state` column is a computed authorization value on §4.4.2.1, not a replacement for §4.5.3 NDA Record. It maps §4.5.3 `nda_status` as follows: `draft`, `pending_buyer`, or `pending_seller` -> `nda_pending`; `executed` -> `nda_executed`; `expired` -> `nda_expired`; superseded-version blockers -> `nda_superseded`; buyer-approved exceptions -> `exception_granted`. Pending change requests do not grant Q&A access until the NDA Record returns to `executed` or an exception is granted.

| Vendor / NDA state | Thread audience | Thread visibility | Pipeline phase | Seller result | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| NDA required and `nda_pending` | Any | Any | Any | Suppressed | Seller sees only the NDA module; Q&A list and unread counts are hidden |
| NDA required and `nda_expired` | Any | Any | Any | Suppressed | Q&A read access is revoked on the next page load or reactive permission refresh; seller sees "NDA expired — contact the buyer to extend"; AuditEvent action `qa_thread.access_revoked` records reason `nda_expired_qa_revoked` |
| NDA required and `nda_superseded` | Any | Any | Any until re-signature | Suppressed | Prior Q&A posts remain stored but inaccessible until the updated NDA is accepted or exceptioned |
| NDA not required OR `nda_executed` OR `exception_granted` | `specific_vendor` | `PRIVATE` | 6-7 | Visible only to `addressed_seller_org_id` | Non-addressed sellers receive HTTP 404 and no unread-marker row |
| NDA not required OR `nda_executed` OR `exception_granted` | `all_invited_vendors` | `PUBLIC` | 6-7 | Visible to every active invited seller in the Workspace | Vendor identity masking follows §18.3.3 |
| NDA not required OR `nda_executed` OR `exception_granted` | `specific_vendor` | `PUBLIC` | 6-7 | Visible to the addressed seller and, if buyer explicitly publishes, all active invited sellers | Publishing requires buyer confirmation; private-to-public is allowed, public-to-private is not per §18.3.2 |
| NDA not required OR `nda_executed` OR `exception_granted` | Any visible row | Any | 8-12 | Read-only | Historical posts render; compose actions are hidden and server writes are rejected |
| Bid Workspace disqualified or canceled | Any | Any | Any | Read-only or suppressed per §25.3 | Disqualification cascade controls whether history remains visible |

**Server authorization predicate.** Seller Q&A read access requires `nda_visibility_state IN {not_required, nda_executed, exception_granted}` AND `pipeline_phase IN {6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12}` AND the vendor/thread visibility predicate above. Compose access is narrower: it requires the same NDA predicate plus `pipeline_phase IN {6, 7}` and `compose_state='compose_enabled'`. `nda_pending`, `nda_expired`, `nda_superseded`, pending change requests, and any Ops revocation-equivalent access removal suppress Q&A reads and unread-marker derivation immediately on the next permission refresh. Expiry or revocation emits AuditEvent action `qa_thread.access_revoked` with reason `nda_expired_qa_revoked` when the cause is §4.5.3 `nda_status=expired`.

**Firewall invariants.** Seller APIs MUST filter by `(org_id, bid_workspace_id)` before loading any Q&A projection. A seller MUST NOT be able to enumerate, infer count, or receive unread markers for another vendor's private thread. Attachments cross only through the §4.6.2 carve-out for `qa_thread_post` and the §4.7.1 carried-field allowlist. Internal Comment Thread ids, buyer-internal mentions, buyer scoring notes, Target Account notes, and non-promoted buyer comments are never carried.

## 24.2 NDA Module & Execution {#24.2-nda-module-&-execution}

During Phase 4, vendors see only the NDA module. NDA acceptance is tracked per-vendor. The canonical entity schema is NDA Record (§4.5.3); this section defines the seller-console execution flow and maps its fields to that entity rather than defining a second NDA object.

**NDA flow:**

1. Buyer uploads NDA document (PDF or DOCX) to the Workspace.  
2. Vendor receives notification: "NDA available for review. Please review and accept to proceed."  
3. Vendor reviews NDA and clicks "Accept" or "Request Changes."

**On accept:**

- Checkbox: "I have reviewed and accept the NDA."  
- Timestamp recorded: `nda_accepted_at` (UTC).  
- NDA version recorded: `nda_version_id` (FK to version).  
- Target Account status → `nda_signed`.  
- Bid Workspace status → `nda_signed` (Phase 5 can now be entered).  
- Buyer notification: "Vendor \[Name\] has signed the NDA."

**On "Request Changes":**

- Buyer is notified: "Vendor \[Name\] requested changes to the NDA."  
- Manual negotiation expected outside Sourcera.  
- NDA remains in `pending` status until accepted or escalated.

**Multiple NDA versions (Gap 24.2):**

- Buyer can upload revised NDA at any phase.  
- New version stored with `version_number` (auto-increment) and `created_at`.  
- Old versions persist in the system but are marked `superseded = true`.  
- Vendor who previously signed receives notification: "Updated NDA available for signature. Remaining vendors require updated NDA acceptance before proceeding."  
- Vendor must re-sign updated NDA to proceed. Re-signing overwrites `nda_signed_at` and `nda_version_id`.  
- If vendor refuses updated NDA, buyer can choose to disqualify or create an exception.

**NDA signature method (Gap 24.1):**

- At v7.1.0a, NDA signing is a checkbox acknowledgment (not a third-party e-signature service like DocuSign).  
- Stored on NDA Record (§4.5.3) as seller-side signature fields, including `nda_signed_by_seller` and `nda_seller_signed_at`; seller-console projections may render these as `nda_signed` and `nda_signed_at` aliases only.  
- Legal enforceability depends on the clause language in the NDA itself and applicable jurisdiction law.  
- E-signature integration (e.g., DocuSign) is a post-v7.1.0a roadmap item and MUST preserve the §4.5.3 NDA Record as the canonical entity.

## 24.3 Seller Inbox {#24.3-seller-inbox}

Unified feed of action items for the seller:

- New buyer requirements mapped to seller's teams (requirements posted to Bid Workspace).  
- Amendment re-verification requests (buyer changed a requirement after Phase 6, vendor must re-verify response).  
- Q\&A responses from buyers.  
- KB entries flagged for review (staleness, source content changes).  
- Document Library expiration warnings (documents expiring within 30 days).  
- NDA signature requests (Phase 4).  
- Phase transitions (workspace advances to next phase).

Inbox is sorted by priority (action required \> updates \> info) and date (newest first). Each item is clickable and navigates to the relevant section.

**Canonical data model.** Seller Inbox item persistence is canonical at §4.4.33 SellerInboxItem and grouping is canonical at §4.4.34 SellerInboxItemGroup. The seven bullets above map to Appendix J `seller_inbox_item_kind`; priority sort uses Appendix J `seller_inbox_priority`. §24.3 is the surface contract and MUST NOT introduce additional inline item kinds without registering the enum and §4.4 field-table update in the same change.

## 24.4 Seller Pulse {#24.4-seller-pulse}

Health dashboard for Bid Workspace Owners:

- **Response progress:** % of requirements with submitted responses (e.g., "45/100 requirements submitted, 45%").  
- **Pending re-verification count:** Requirements with amendments pending vendor re-verification.  
- **Upcoming deadlines:** Q\&A close date, submission deadline, phase transitions.  
- **KB health status:** Count of entries needing review (stale, review\_due, flagged\_stale).  
- **Phase progress:** Current phase, phases completed, phases remaining.  
- **Team status:** For multi-team orgs, response count by team (e.g., "InfoSec: 12/15, Legal: 8/8, Operations: 3/10").

Seller Pulse is the inverse of Buyer Pulse — it shows seller bottlenecks instead of buyer bottlenecks.

### 24.4.1 Seller Pulse Canonical Data Model {#24.4.1-seller-pulse-canonical-data-model}

Seller Pulse persistence is canonical at §4.4.37 SellerBidWorkspacePulseHealth. §24.4 is the surface and formula contract; it MUST NOT introduce a second seller Pulse snapshot row, a raw inline JSON schema, or a buyer-readable projection. Seller Pulse reads are always seller-console-scoped and Bid-Workspace-scoped.

### 24.4.2 Seller Pulse Health Score Calculation {#24.4.2-seller-pulse-health-score-calculation}

Seller Pulse Health Score uses bounded 0-100 component terms and the same `safe_pct` / `clamp_pct` semantics as §20.3.1: `safe_pct(numerator, denominator)` returns `null` when `denominator = 0`; otherwise it returns `clamp_pct((numerator / denominator) * 100)`. `clamp_pct(value)` returns `MAX(0, MIN(100, value))`. Null terms are excluded from the weighted sum and remaining non-null weights are renormalized to 1.0. If every term in the selected weight set is null, the compute writes `score_value = 0`, `color_band = red`, and `raw_inputs_json.empty_reason = no_available_terms`.

| Term | Definition | Applicability |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `response_completion_pct` | `safe_pct(submitted_response_item_count, materialized_response_item_count)` | Phase 6+ while Bid Workspace is active/submitted. |
| `on_time_submission_pct` | `safe_pct(on_time_submitted_response_item_count, submitted_response_item_count)` | Phase 6+ when at least one response has been submitted. |
| `amendment_reverification_turnaround_pct` | `safe_pct(amendment_reverification_cleared_within_target_count, amendment_reverification_required_count)` | Only after buyer amendments require seller re-verification per §25.5. |
| `kb_utilization_pct` | `safe_pct(submitted_response_items_with_verified_kb_citation_count, submitted_response_item_count)` | Phase 6+ when at least one response has been submitted. |
| `deadline_readiness_pct` | `safe_pct(non_overdue_seller_deadline_count, seller_deadline_count)` | Any active Bid Workspace phase with seller-owned deadlines. |

| Phase / state band | Weight set | Term weights before null renormalization | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Before buyer Phase 6 projection | `pre_bidding` | Deadline readiness 0.5; KB utilization 0.5 | Response terms excluded until seller response items are materialized. |
| Buyer Phase 6-10 projection | `active_response` | Response completion 0.4; on-time submission 0.25; amendment turnaround 0.2; KB utilization 0.15 | Core bid-preparation window. |
| Buyer Phase 11-13 projection or Bid Workspace submitted | `post_submission` | Response completion 0.3; on-time submission 0.2; amendment turnaround 0.2; KB utilization 0.3 | Preserves post-submit learning signal. |
| Terminal Bid Workspace state | `final_lock` | Latest non-terminal score frozen | No mutable recompute; append-only audit / retention metadata only. |

Color thresholds reuse §20.3.3: green 80-100, yellow 50-79, red 0-49. The displayed Seller Pulse widget may show the component labels in plain language, but the engine stores the canonical term keys above on SellerBidWorkspacePulseHealth (§4.4.37).

### 24.4.3 Cadence and Locking {#24.4.3-cadence-and-locking}

Seller Pulse has two compute cadences, both written to the same entity:

| Cadence | Trigger | Snapshot kind | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Bid Workspace tick | Response submit/edit, amendment re-verification state change, seller deadline change, KB-citation verification change, or projected phase transition | `tick` | This is the freshness path for the dashboard; it replaces the prior unmeasurable "real-time" wording. |
| Daily summary | 9am UTC summarizer | `daily_summary` | One row per Bid Workspace per UTC date; used for the trend chart. |
| Final lock | Bid Workspace terminal state or bound Workspace closure | `final_lock` | Freezes latest score for post-bid debrief / KB compounding evidence. |

### 24.4.4 Solo Seller Surface Treatment {#24.4.4-solo-seller-surface-treatment}

The Seller Console is always surface-compressed per §2.8.6 / §3.14.2: it never renders the buyer-side 13-phase chip ribbon, and it does not have a separate `evaluation_owner_mode`. Seller Pulse still computes and persists on SellerBidWorkspacePulseHealth for every plan tier. On Seller Solo / Free, the surface renders a compact "Bid health: {score}/100" pill plus the single most actionable bottleneck; the per-component breakdown, team-status widget, and trend chart are hidden unless the seller is on a tier that exposes those panels per §34.1.2 / §44.6. Engine writes, final-lock behavior, and retention are unchanged by surface compression.

### 24.4.5 Acceptance Criteria {#24.4.5-seller-pulse-acceptance-criteria}

1. A Bid Workspace tick MUST recompute SellerBidWorkspacePulseHealth when any input term changes and MUST NOT create duplicate `daily_summary` rows for the same `(bid_workspace_id, recorded_date_utc)`.
2. The score computation MUST use `safe_pct`, `clamp_pct`, null-term exclusion, and final-score clamp exactly as specified in §24.4.2.
3. A terminal Bid Workspace state MUST write or preserve exactly one `final_lock` snapshot and reject mutable recompute after `locked=true`.
4. Seller Solo / Free MUST hide the per-component breakdown, team-status widget, and trend chart while preserving the same engine-side SellerBidWorkspacePulseHealth writes.
5. Buyer-console principals MUST receive HTTP 404 for Seller Pulse snapshot reads; seller-console principals outside the owning Seller Org or Bid Workspace MUST receive the same non-leak response.

## 24.5 Seller Analytics {#24.5-seller-analytics}

Per-Bid-Workspace metrics accessible via Analytics tab:

- **Response completion rate:** % of requirements with submitted responses over time (trend chart).  
- **Average response time:** Median hours from requirement posted (Phase 6 entry) to response submitted.  
- **KB utilization rate:** % of responses using KB-suggested content vs. written from scratch.  
- **Amendment re-verification time:** Median hours from amendment posted to vendor re-verification complete.  
- **Team breakdown:** Response completion by team.

## 24.6 Acceptance Criteria {#24.6-acceptance-criteria}

- NDA accept flow stores boolean \+ timestamp correctly.  
- NDA version updates require vendor re-signature.  
- Inbox surfaces all action items within 2 seconds of trigger event.  
- Seller Pulse recomputes on the Bid Workspace tick and daily summary cadences in §24.4.3; the prior "real-time" wording is retired.  
- Analytics reflect accurate completion rates and timelines.

# 25\. Cross-Console Mechanics {#25.-cross-console-mechanics}

**Authoring Intent (v7.0.0).** §25 is the prose operator-manual for the Console Bridge. §4.7.1 defines the Console Bridge Event entity at data-model fidelity — per-field types, redaction-verification hashes, indexes, retention — and is the normative source of truth for implementers. §25 is the surface that product, design, support, Ops, and on-call reference: what the bridge carries, what it never carries, how its SLO is enforced, how failures surface to both consoles, how buyer Requirements materialize as seller Response Items without leaking scores or internal comments, and how the system is observed. When §25 and §4.7.1 differ on a field name or a state-machine transition, §4.7.1 wins and §25 is updated in the same pass. When §25 and the Summary's C.116–C.117 differ, the Summary's Appendix-C descriptions are advisory; §25 and §4.7.1 are authoritative. §25 extends in v7.0.0 with entity-level redaction rules (§25.1), a normative bounded-lag SLO and dual-surface failure-visibility model (§25.2), a new Materialization Protocol for buyer Requirement → seller Bid Response translation (§25.5), and a new Console Bridge Observability contract (§25.6).

## 25.1 Data Flow via Console Bridge {#25.1-data-flow-via-console-bridge}

When data crosses the console boundary (buyer → seller or seller → buyer), it passes through a **Console Bridge** — a server-side Convex mutation side-effect on source-entity writes that emits a Console Bridge Event row (§4.7.1) carrying a redacted, firewall-compliant payload. The bridge is the only mechanism that carries buyer-origin data into a seller's Bid Workspace without breaching the Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2); it is enforced by write-time redaction validation, a defense-in-depth seller-side serializer projection, and a `redaction_verification_hash` that is recomputed on every retry. Sellers cannot write to the bridge under any circumstance (HTTP 403; `console_bridge_event_seller_write_forbidden`). Buyers cannot write directly to the bridge endpoint (HTTP 403; `console_bridge_event_direct_write_forbidden`) — bridge emission is always a server-side consequence of a source-entity mutation.

### 25.1.1 Directional Surface Inventory

**Buyer → Seller surfaces (Phase 4+, gated by Bid Workspace state and §7.2 NDA).**

- Requirement titles, descriptions, response types, weights, priorities, order, status, Use Case structure (all read-only in Bid Workspace).
- Q&A thread posts from buyer team that the author explicitly marked vendor-visible.
- Amendment diffs (semantic diff summary and affected Requirement ids only).
- Revert notifications (target version + public reason snippet ≤200 chars).
- Phase advancement events (from-phase, to-phase, timestamp, acting role; user identity never carried).
- NDA documents (Phase 4+, vendor-signed copy).
- EOI acceptance propagation (seller-visible projection only; §4.5.8).
- Disqualification notifications (vendor-visible copy; rationale withheld).
- Workspace cancel / Ops reopen events (public reason ≤500 chars; acting role only).

**Seller → Buyer surfaces.**

- Bid Response submissions (text, files, pricing); atomic per-Requirement payload.
- Q&A questions initiated by vendor.
- EOI submissions and withdrawals.
- Seller-side Q&A responses to buyer-authored questions.
- Voluntary withdrawal notifications (§23.4).

### 25.1.2 Entity-Level Redaction Rules (Normative)

Every cross-console event is emitted with a kind-specific payload whitelist. The write-time validator (a) confirms that no forbidden field is present at any depth in `payload_json`, (b) confirms the `redaction_verification_hash` matches a recomputed canonical hash, and (c) rejects with `console_bridge_event_firewall_violation` (HTTP 422) on any mismatch. A defense-in-depth seller-side serializer applies the same whitelist at read time so that even a malformed event that slipped past write-time validation is still stripped at the boundary. The full per-event-kind CARRIED / NEVER CARRIED matrix lives in §4.7.1; §25.1.2 is the entity-level summary that product, design, and support reference.

**Every buyer-Workspace entity is either CARRIED (in whole, in projection, or in diff summary) or NEVER CARRIED.** The below matrix is complete: every entity defined in §4.3 (Buyer Console) and every field of those entities that could plausibly cross the bridge has been classified. Entities and fields not listed are NEVER CARRIED by default (allow-list, not block-list).

| Buyer-Workspace Entity | Bridge Treatment | Fields CARRIED | Fields NEVER CARRIED |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Workspace** (§4.3.1) | CARRIED (projection) | `workspace_id`, `title_public`, `workspace_phase`, `currency`, `residency_region` | Internal description, evaluation_lead_user_id (role-only surfaces), Scenarios, scoring weights internal to Scenarios, selection_report_draft, intelligence_brief_draft, internal-comment threads, canceled_reason_internal, reopen_reason_internal |
| **Use Case** (§4.3.2) | CARRIED (projection) | `use_case_id`, `title`, `description_public`, `lead_role_kind` (role enum only), `included_requirement_ids`, `order` | `lead_user_id` (identity), internal-comment threads, Scenario-weight overrides per use case, any buyer-only metadata |

**Seller → Buyer: mirror rules apply.** Seller-internal artifacts NEVER carry: KB entries, Document Library contents, Internal Comment Threads on Bid Workspaces, Custom Agent Instructions, Capability Declaration drafts (published Capability Declarations are visible in the Marketplace via a separate mechanism, not the bridge), Bid Task assignments internal to the seller team, Bid Schedule internal detail, Seller Signals internal queries, Seller Analytics filter state, internal KB Value Meter computation provenance. The seller-authored payload in a `response_submitted` event carries `response_id`, `requirement_id`, `vendor_org_id`, `submitted_at`, `version`, and `response_payload` (text / files / pricing per the Bid Response entity §4.4.2).

**Never-Carry Invariants (Testable).** The following invariants MUST be asserted by unit tests on every bridge mutation (per §25.4 AC-2) and re-asserted by the defense-in-depth seller projection (§4.7.1 QA tests `console_bridge_seller_projection_defense_in_depth` AND `console_bridge_seller_projection_no_cardinality_leak`):

1. No score of any kind (grade, rubric value, blended score, scenario score, what-would-flip delta) appears in any seller-bound payload.
2. No buyer Internal Comment body or mention expansion appears in any seller-bound payload.
3. No Target Account list membership, order, status, or count for any seller other than the target itself appears in the target's seller-bound payload.
4. No buyer user-identity PII appears in any seller-bound payload; only `role_snapshot` enums per Appendix J.
5. No buyer financial / billing / AIOperation / seat-snapshot field appears in any seller-bound payload.
6. No Scenario weights, rubric configurations, or Selection-Report draft content appears in any seller-bound payload.
7. **No buyer-internal collection cardinality (count, length, size, or binary "is-non-trivial" signal) appears in any seller-bound payload** (D-V6-001 / D-6.1-001 / D-V6-004 composite invariant, 2026-05-06). This includes — non-exhaustively — Target Account list cardinality (`broadcast_to_vendor_count` is forbidden), fan-out group cardinality (the §4.7.1 `fanout_group_id` row-level rule must be a per-recipient HMAC pseudonym, never a conditional null), supersede chain cardinality across non-self sellers, and the buyer-side total length of any collection that is not per-recipient-projected to the seller's own scope. Array fields returned to the seller MUST be either (a) fully buyer-side-only (CARRIED only on the buyer projection) OR (b) per-recipient projected (intersection with the seller's own scope, e.g., `affected_requirement_ids_visible_to_seller = intersect(amendment.affected_requirement_ids, this_bid_response.requirement_ids)`).

### 25.1.3 Allow-List Evolution

Adding a new entity, adding a new event kind, or adding a new field to an existing carried projection requires: (a) a §4.7.1 `event_kind` enum registration in Appendix J, (b) a new row in the §25.1.2 matrix and the §4.7.1 per-event-kind redaction table, (c) updated unit tests in the bridge mutation validator, and (d) updated defense-in-depth projection tests. Removing a field from a carried projection is always safe and requires only a schema-version bump on the affected event kind. Adding a field to the NEVER CARRIED side is a pure documentation tightening and carries no runtime change (the allow-list is inclusive; a field absent from the CARRIED side is already not carried).

## 25.2 Sync Behavior, Bounded-Lag SLO & Retry {#25.2-sync-behavior-&-retry}

### 25.2.1 Bounded-Lag SLO

**Normative SLO.** The cross-console sync SLO is a percentile-based objective, not a literal per-event bound. For Console Bridge Events that ultimately reach `synced`, the bounded-lag interval `synced_at - created_at` MUST be ≤ 30,000 ms (30 seconds) for ≥ 99% of events measured over a rolling 15-minute window, partitioned per event kind and per residency region. The p99 threshold is the authoritative SLO; the p100 (maximum) is a non-goal, permitting pathological tail cases (single-event delays caused by cold-start retries, residency-region network excursions, or Loops.so-style downstream-dependency spikes) without failing the Org's sync SLO. This is the normative cross-console sync SLO per Summary C.117 and §4.7.1. Events that terminate in `failed`, `dlq`, or `superseded` are excluded from SLO calculations and surface as separate anomalies in §25.6 dashboards. Alert thresholds (§25.2.1 Alerting, below) translate the p99 objective into an actionable breach-rate signal: a rolling 15-minute breach rate > 1% means the p99 has moved below the 30s target. A junior reader approaching the prior MUST-≤-30,000-ms phrasing literally should read that as the per-event *target*; the rolling-window percentile is the enforcement contract.

**Measurement.** The `slo_bounded_lag_ms` field is populated at the transition to `synced` as `synced_at - created_at` in milliseconds. The `slo_breach_flag` boolean is set true when `slo_bounded_lag_ms > 30000`. Breach rate is computed as `count(slo_breach_flag=true AND sync_status=synced) / count(sync_status=synced)` over a rolling 15-minute window, partitioned per event kind and per residency region.

**Alerting.** Breach rate > 1% over a rolling 15-minute window pages Ops per §25.6.2. Sustained breach rate > 5% over a rolling 60-minute window escalates to the Cross-Console on-call runbook (§25.6.4) with P1 severity.

### 25.2.2 Retry Curve

Bridge-apply failures follow a fixed exponential-backoff schedule — the non-webhook `bridge_apply_standard` apply curve (D-6.1-012; renamed from the former `console_bridge_standard` label, which is NOT a webhook retry class — Bridge-domain webhooks use the Appendix F.1 `standard` curve and are registered in Appendix C with that class). The `bridge_apply_standard` apply curve is documented here in §25.2.2 only and is registered in Appendix J `webhook_retry_class` as explicitly NOT a member (the F.1/F.2 webhook taxonomy is binary):

| Attempt | Delay From Previous | Cumulative Elapsed | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 (initial) | 0 | 0 | Emitted by scheduler within 5s of Event creation |
| 2 | +1s | ~1s | Retryable failure reasons only (see below) |
| 3 | +2s | ~3s | |
| 4 | +4s | ~7s | |
| 5 | +8s | ~15s | |
| (abort) | +16s | ~31s | 5 failed attempts → transition to `dlq` |

**Retryable failure reasons.** `downstream_timeout`, `other_transient`. All other `failure_reason` values terminate in `failed` (non-retryable; see §4.7.1 state machine). Retryable failures respect the 30-second bounded-lag SLO best-effort; the 5-attempt curve is designed to fit inside ~31s cumulative wall-clock, so a successful retry within the curve keeps the SLO intact in most cases.

**Per-attempt jitter.** The scheduler applies ±20% uniform jitter to each delay to prevent thundering-herd retries after a brief downstream outage. Jitter does not affect the 5-attempt cap.

**DLQ semantics.** On the 5th failed attempt, the event transitions to `dlq` with `retry_count=5`, `next_retry_at=null`, `failure_reason` populated, and `failure_note` carrying a diagnostic snippet that MUST NOT contain buyer-internal content (validated at write). The Appendix C `console_bridge.dlq_entered` webhook fires within 10 seconds. Automated re-drive from DLQ is PROHIBITED — Ops must approve every re-drive with a ≥20-char note per §4.7.1 AC-9. If a new source-side mutation arrives while the DLQ event is resting, the new event supersedes the DLQ event (DLQ event transitions to `superseded`, new event enters `pending`) — this prevents stale retries from clobbering newer state.

### 25.2.3 Dual-Surface Failure Visibility

**Buyer-Workspace "Bridge Health" panel.** Every Buyer Workspace surfaces a Bridge Health panel (accessible from the Workspace header overflow menu and from §17 Analytics) showing:

- Rolling 15-minute SLO breach rate (by kind).
- `pending` / `retrying` / `failed` / `dlq` / `superseded` counts for this Workspace.
- Per-event detail on every `failed` and `dlq` event: event kind, source entity reference, `failure_reason`, `failure_note` (buyer-internal-redacted), `last_attempt_at`, `retry_count`, a "View Source Entity" deep link, and (for Ops-redriveable DLQ events) an Ops-only re-drive button.
- For events in `pending > 24h` or `retrying > 24h` (stale), an in-panel Warning banner and an email to the Workspace Owner per §25.2.5.

**Seller-Bid-Workspace "Sync Health" panel.** Every Bid Workspace surfaces a Sync Health panel showing, with redaction applied:

- Rolling 15-minute SLO breach rate (for events targeting this Bid Workspace only).
- `pending` / `retrying` / `failed` / `dlq` counts for this Bid Workspace.
- Per-event detail on every `failed` and `dlq` event: event kind (vendor-visible kinds only), `failure_reason` (vendor-visible reasons only: `downstream_timeout`, `bid_workspace_readonly`, `target_bid_workspace_disqualified`, `other_permanent` generic; internal reasons like `persistent_firewall_violation_suspected` are hidden from the seller and remapped to `other_permanent`), `last_attempt_at`, a "Contact Support" CTA, and (where applicable) a "Request Re-Sync" action that emits an Ops ticket. `failure_note` is never shown to the seller.
- For events in `pending > 24h` or `retrying > 24h` (stale), an in-panel Warning banner and an email to the Bid Owner per §25.2.5.

Both panels update via Convex reactive queries with <2 s visible freshness per §44.1 dashboard SLO and are subject to §37 accessibility requirements (focus-visible, reduced-motion, screen-reader attribution on the synthetic "Sync failed" announcement).

**Ops Cross-Workspace Bridge Dashboard.** Ops sees the full cross-Workspace dashboard in the Ops Console (§50) with: per-kind SLO breach rate, DLQ depth time-series, firewall-violation count, retry-count distribution, per-residency-region breakdown, and one-click re-drive with mandatory Ops note. The Ops dashboard surfaces full `failure_note` content and full failure-reason fidelity (no remapping).

### 25.2.4 Daily Reconciliation Job

A platform-wide reconciliation job runs at 02:00 UTC daily and:

- Scans every Console Bridge Event with `sync_status ∈ {pending, retrying}` AND `created_at < now() - 24h`.
- For stale entries whose underlying target Bid Workspace is still valid (not disqualified, not withdrawn, not deleted), the job re-triggers apply with fresh state. Idempotency is guaranteed by `idempotency_key` uniqueness — a duplicate apply on an already-`synced` event is a no-op.
- For stale entries whose underlying target is no longer valid, the job transitions the event to `failed` with the appropriate `failure_reason` and emits the buyer-side "Bridge Health" update.
- Emits Appendix C `console_bridge.reconciliation_summary` webhook (per §31; HMAC-SHA256 signed, idempotent via `event_id`, exponential backoff, DLQ after 5) with per-Workspace stale counts.
- Emits Ops alert if the job itself fails to run or completes with >1000 stale entries resolved (anomaly signal).

A missed job run (detected by the 06:00 UTC heartbeat check) pages Ops with P1 severity per §25.6.2.

### 25.2.5 User Notification on Persistent Failure

If a Console Bridge Event remains in `pending`, `retrying`, or `dlq` for > 24 hours after `created_at`:

- **Buyer-side email** to the Workspace Owner and all `workspace_editor` role-holders: "Synchronization issue between your Workspace and one or more vendor Bid Workspaces. *{N}* updates may not be visible to *{M}* vendors. No action required from you — our team is investigating. View details: {Bridge Health deep link}." Triggers at most once per 24h per Workspace (dedupe by `workspace_id + day`).
- **Seller-side email** to the Bid Owner and all `bid_contributor` role-holders, per affected Bid Workspace: "A buyer update to '{Workspace Title}' has not synchronized to your Bid Workspace. Their update may not be visible yet. No action required from you — our team is investigating. View details: {Sync Health deep link}. Contact support if this persists." Triggers at most once per 24h per Bid Workspace.
- **Ops page** via the Ops Console: a DLQ depth > 100 or a stale-count > 1000 platform-wide both trigger immediate page to the Cross-Console on-call per §25.6.2.

### 25.2.6 Kill-Switch Notification Suppression {#25.2.6-kill-switch-notification-suppression}

The §25.6.4 kill-switch deliberately stalls events in `pending`/`retrying` for the duration of the pause. Without a suppression rule, a sustained kill-switch engagement would cross the §25.2.5 24-hour threshold for every stalled event simultaneously on release, generating a flood of "synchronization issue" emails to Workspace Owners and Bid Owners for what was intentional Ops action. The suppression rule:

1. **Email suppression during engagement.** While `ops.bridge.kill_switch_engaged` is active, the §25.2.5 buyer-side and seller-side emails MUST NOT fire. The per-Workspace / per-Bid-Workspace dedup counter continues to advance (so any event that independently crosses the 24h threshold before the kill-switch was engaged still respects the once-per-24h cap after release), but new email dispatches in the kill-switch window are suppressed at the Loops.so send layer with `suppression_reason = bridge_kill_switch_engaged`.
2. **Post-release grace window.** For the 6-hour window immediately after `ops.bridge.kill_switch_released`, §25.2.5 emails remain suppressed. The 6-hour window is chosen to give the retry scheduler enough time to drain the backlog — a successful drain retroactively removes the stall signal, and a failed drain is detected by the existing §25.6.2 RB-003/RB-004 DLQ-depth alerts which page Ops directly (bypassing the user-facing email path).
3. **Operator-authored restoration notice.** The Ops user releasing the kill-switch MUST author a restoration notice (30–500 chars) that is dispatched via Loops.so transactional template `bridge_service_resumed.hbs` (new; Authored Extension — v7.0.0) to every Workspace Owner and Bid Owner whose Workspace or Bid Workspace had at least one `pending`/`retrying`/`dlq` event at any point during the kill-switch window. The notice body is: `"Cross-Console sync was paused for {duration_human} ending at {released_at}. Your updates are fully synchronized and no action is required. — The Sourcera team."` The `{restoration_note}` string authored by Ops is appended if the body has room under the 5,000-char template limit. Template variables: `{workspace_title}`, `{duration_human}`, `{released_at}`, `{restoration_note}`. Delivery is deduped once per recipient per kill-switch-cycle. The notice is dispatched within 10 minutes of release; delivery failures follow the §41 Loops.so non-webhook `transactional_email` policy.
4. **Webhook pass-through is not suppressed.** `console_bridge.dlq_entered` and other §31 webhooks continue to fire during the kill-switch window because downstream integrations need the signal to drive their own dashboards. Suppression applies only to the end-user Loops.so email path.
5. **Audit log.** Every suppression event writes an `ops.bridge.notification_suppressed` audit row (Appendix J `audit_event_action_type` — Console-Bridge Ops additions sub-section, registered per D-1.5-005 remediation 2026-05-01) with `affected_workspace_count`, `affected_bid_workspace_count`, `suppressed_email_count`, and the `kill_switch_engagement_id`. The audit row is inside the buyer Org scope for Workspace-side suppression and inside the seller Org scope for Bid-Workspace-side suppression; Ops sees the cross-Org roll-up. `entity_type = console_bridge_event`.
6. **Acceptance criteria addition.** §25.4 AC #7 is extended by this pass to explicitly include kill-switch suppression: "When the kill-switch is engaged or within 6 hours of release, §25.2.5 user emails MUST be suppressed; a single restoration notice per affected Workspace / Bid Workspace MUST fire via `bridge_service_resumed.hbs` within 10 minutes of release. Integration test: engage kill-switch for 2h; assert no §25.2.5 email dispatches; release; assert restoration notice dispatches and is deduped per recipient."

Logged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` → Authored Extensions → §25.2.6 Kill-Switch Notification Suppression (2026-04-24).

## 25.3 Disqualification (Gap 25.2) {#25.3-disqualification-(gap-25.2)}

**Authoring Intent.** §25.3 is the end-to-end formal specification of the Vendor Disqualification workflow — the act by which a Buyer Workspace Owner removes a bidding vendor from an active evaluation. The data-model truth for a disqualification is the `VendorDisqualificationRecord` entity authored in §4.7.2; §25.3 is the *workflow* home — the state machines, the buyer and vendor experiences, the read-only freeze semantics on the Bid Workspace, the audit-trail integrity contract, the notification template, the REST endpoint, the webhook, the PostHog event surface, the failure-mode coverage, and the acceptance criteria. §4.7.2 and §25.3 are dual surfaces of the same concept: §4.7.2 is what the row looks like at rest; §25.3 is what happens when a row is written.

**Source authority.** This section materializes Summary C.118 (Vendor Disqualification Workflow), §4.7.2 (Vendor Disqualification Record), §4.3.20 (Target Account entity; `target_account_state_enum`), §4.3.20 `target_account_disqualification_enum`, Appendix D (Response Status State Machine), Appendix E (Bid Workspace Status State Machine — extended herein to include `disqualified` as a terminal state), §4.6.1 (Audit Event), §4.7.1 (Console Bridge Event), §4.4.2 (Bid Response), §5.2 RBAC (Workspace Owner, Workspace Admin, Use Case Lead), Summary §6.11 (Internal Comments), §29 (Notifications), §31 (Webhooks), §32 (API), §41 (Loops.so transactional email), §42 (Observability), §44 (PostHog Event Taxonomy). Where this section's requirements extend prior sources (Bid Workspace `disqualified` terminal state, disqualification-originated `submitted → locked` Response transition, audit hash-chain), the extension is flagged in `/Sourcera/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` → Authored Extensions → §25.3 Formalization (2026-04-24).

**Scope rule.** §25.3 covers the `severity=soft` (workspace-local) path in full; it cross-references §4.7.2 for the cascade shape of `severity ∈ {account_level, global_ban}`. Soft disqualification is the everyday workflow — a Workspace Owner unilaterally removing a vendor mid-evaluation. Account-level and global-ban lanes route through §4.7.2 Scope Isolation and Ops review and are out of §25.3's mainline authoring, except where the state-machine edges converge (e.g., a soft disqualification being superseded by a later global ban).

### 25.3.1 Overview {#25.3.1-overview}

**Trigger.** A user with `workspace_owner` or `workspace_admin` role on the Workspace (or, by delegation, a `use_case_lead` on a Use Case whose Target Account includes this vendor) selects "Disqualify" on a Target Account in the Vendor Curation surface (§6.4.x) OR on the Vendor row of a Bid Acceptance / RFP Live / Q&A / Submissions-Closed / Scoring phase surface. The action is available in Phases 3 through 11 inclusive; Phase 12+ disqualification requires the Emergency Ops path per §4.7.2 Failure Modes #2.

**Behavior (summary; formal contract in §25.3.3–§25.3.10).**

1. **Rationale.** Required. Minimum 10 characters, maximum 4,000 characters (§39 Object Size Constraints). Stored in `VendorDisqualificationRecord.rationale_internal` (§4.7.2). NEVER shared with the vendor.
2. **Target Account status →** `disqualified` (`target_account_state_enum`; §4.3.20, Appendix J); `disqualification_reason` stamped with one of `no_capability_match`, `compliance_fail`, `pricing_out_of_band`, `duplicate_of_other_account`, `buyer_discretion`, `seller_declined_bid` per §4.3.20 (`target_account_disqualification_enum`). `buyer_discretion` requires non-empty `disqualification_note`; all other values make `disqualification_note` optional.
3. **Bid Workspace status →** `disqualified` (`bid_workspace_status` enum, extended in Appendix J by this pass to add the terminal value). The Bid Workspace is frozen to read-only per §25.3.4.
4. **Vendor notification** dispatched via the `vendor_disqualified` Loops.so transactional template (§41; §25.3.6) within 60 seconds; default body is neutral ("Your participation in '{Workspace Title}' has ended. Thank you for your interest.") with no rationale disclosed. The Workspace Owner MAY override the body at disqualification time, bounded by the §39 limit and the `notification_style` enum (§4.7.2; neutral / rationale-shared / silent).
5. **All vendor responses →** `locked` (`response_status` enum; Appendix D). The transition source `disqualification_cascade` (new Appendix-D trigger authored herein) is distinct from the Phase-9 automatic lock so that QA and Ops dashboards can filter disqualification-originated locks from lifecycle-ordinary locks.
6. **Q&A threads** initiated by this vendor are orphaned: the vendor retains read access to the historical thread body, but the compose surface is disabled, `can_reply=false` is stamped on the seller-side projection, and any in-flight draft is discarded with `autosave_discard_reason=disqualified_mid_compose` (§25.3.8).
7. **Scoring exclusion.** The vendor is excluded from any Scoring computation that has not yet committed; the scoring matrix renders a red "Disqualified" badge in place of the vendor's score cell (§25.3.7 Buyer-Side UX).
8. **Bridge event** of kind `disqualification_issued` emitted via the Console Bridge (§4.7.1) with the firewall-safe projection `{notification_body_to_vendor, disqualified_at}`. The rationale, rationale author, and any internal-comment context are NEVER carried across the firewall.
9. **Seller Signal suppression** — the buyer-vendor pair is suppressed from Seller Signals to this Seller Org for 90 days from `disqualified_at` (§4.4.18; §4.7.2 Cascade Action 9).
10. **SLA timers** tied to this vendor in any open Team queue are cancelled; `sla_timer.status → cancelled_by_disqualification` (§21 SLA state machine).

**Permanence.** Disqualification is permanent within a Workspace with one narrow reversal window: the Workspace Owner MAY reverse within 72 hours of `disqualified_at` per §4.7.2 Reversal (reason `buyer_workspace_owner_reversal_within_72h`). Beyond 72 hours, reversal requires Ops Compliance with `ops_manual_reversal`. To re-evaluate the same vendor for the same opportunity after the reversal window has closed, the Workspace Owner MUST create a new Workspace. Prior disqualification surfaces in Organization Intelligence as part of vendor history (§15 Org Intelligence; §4.7.2 Scope Isolation: buyer's own history visible to Workspace Owner and Org Admin in full; other buyer-Org users see the redacted projection; seller NEVER sees the rationale).

### 25.3.2 Authoritative Entity Pointer {#25.3.2-authoritative-entity-pointer}

The canonical row for any disqualification event is `VendorDisqualificationRecord` (§4.7.2). §25.3 does NOT duplicate that entity's field table, indexes, scope isolation, or cascade shape. Readers authoring engineering tickets against §25.3 MUST cross-read §4.7.2 for:

- Full field list including `severity`, `rationale_internal`, `rationale_author_user_id`, `rationale_author_role_snapshot`, `notification_style`, `cascade_status`, `cascade_actions_json`, `appeal_*`, `reversed_at`, `reversal_reason`, `console_bridge_event_id`, `related_abuse_report_id`.
- Indexes (`(seller_org_id, created_at DESC)`; `(buyer_workspace_id, seller_org_id)` unique partial where `severity='soft'`; and others).
- Scope isolation contract (buyer Org visibility, seller-visible projection, Org Intelligence surface, cross-Workspace reads for `account_level` / `global_ban`).
- Appeal workflow (soft = `not_offered`; account_level = 14-day window; global_ban = 30-day window; dual sign-off rules).
- Retention (`active` and `reversed` for Workspace life + 7 years) and Residency (buyer residency for soft; platform-global for global bans).

§25.3 carries the *workflow* detail that §4.7.2 delegates to it:
- State-machine table with `disqualification_cascade` as a distinct Appendix-D trigger (§25.3.3).
- Read-only freeze semantics on the Bid Workspace (§25.3.4).
- Audit-trail hash-chain (§25.3.5).
- Vendor notification template copy and substitution rules (§25.3.6).
- Buyer-side and vendor-side UX (§25.3.7, §25.3.8).
- REST API (§25.3.9).
- Webhook (§25.3.10).
- PostHog event surface (§25.3.11).

When these two sections appear to diverge on a detail, the *scope* of the divergence decides which wins: an entity-level field rule (field type, constraint, retention, residency) is §4.7.2-authoritative; a workflow-level semantics rule (state transition trigger name, UI text, API error code, webhook payload shape) is §25.3-authoritative. Any runtime conflict MUST be surfaced in RECONCILIATION.md → Conflicts Resolved within the same pass.

### 25.3.3 State Machine {#25.3.3-state-machine}

Disqualification spans four state-machine domains: Target Account (§4.3.20), Bid Workspace (Appendix E), Response (Appendix D), and Q&A Thread (§21 / §23). The authoritative transitions — all triggered by the `disqualification_cascade` logical trigger that fires on `VendorDisqualificationRecord` creation per §4.7.2 — are:

**Target Account (`target_account_state_enum`).**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Actor | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `solicited` | `disqualified` | `disqualification_cascade` | `VendorDisqualificationRecord.cascade_status ∈ {in_progress, complete}`; `severity=soft`; phase ∈ [3, 11] | Workspace Owner / Admin / Use Case Lead | `disqualification_reason` stamped; `bid_workspace_id` may be null (pre-NDA) |
| `bidding` | `disqualified` | `disqualification_cascade` | Same, with `bid_workspace_id` required | Same | Cascades into Bid Workspace and Response state machines |
| `shortlisted` | `disqualified` | `disqualification_cascade` | Same | Same | Shortlist exclusion recomputed atomically |
| `prospect` / `qualified` | `disqualified` | `disqualification_cascade` | Same | Same | Uncommon pre-EOI path; bridge event suppressed (no `bid_workspace_id` to emit to) |
| `disqualified` | `solicited` / `bidding` / `shortlisted` (prior state) | `disqualification_reversed` | Reversal within 72h (owner) OR Ops reversal | Workspace Owner / Ops Compliance | Target Account restored to pre-disqualification state; `disqualification_reason` cleared; audit row written |
| `disqualified` | `disqualified` (idempotent) | Duplicate write attempt | Same `(buyer_workspace_id, seller_org_id, severity='soft')` | Any | Rejected at `VendorDisqualificationRecord` uniqueness constraint with HTTP 409 `vendor_already_disqualified` (§25.3.9 error table) |
| `finalist` / `superseded` | — | N/A | Terminal states per §4.3.20; disqualification from these is out-of-band and routes to Emergency Ops per §4.7.2 FM #2 | — | — |

**Bid Workspace (`bid_workspace_status`, Appendix E — extended herein).**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Actor | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `draft` | `disqualified` | `disqualification_cascade` | Disqualification before Phase 5 activation; `bid_workspace_id` exists (vendor accepted NDA but Bid Workspace not yet active) | Workspace Owner / Admin | Rare — vendor disqualified while Bid Workspace still in draft. Freeze applies; vendor never sees an "active" Bid Workspace. |
| `active` | `disqualified` | `disqualification_cascade` | Disqualification during Phases 5–11 | Workspace Owner / Admin / Use Case Lead | Mainline path. Freeze per §25.3.4; cascades into Response state transitions. |
| `submitted` | `disqualified` | `disqualification_cascade` | Disqualification after Phase 9 (Submissions Closed) but before Phase 12 | Same | Responses already `locked` from Phase 9; disqualification adds scoring-exclusion and banner surfaces. |
| `disqualified` | `active` / `submitted` / prior state | `disqualification_reversed` | Reversal within 72h (owner) OR Ops reversal | Workspace Owner / Ops Compliance | Bid Workspace restored to pre-disqualification state; freeze lifted; vendor banner replaced by reversal banner per §25.3.8. |
| `disqualified` | — | Terminal | `disqualified` is terminal absent reversal | — | Phase 13 (Closed) on the parent Workspace does NOT transition a `disqualified` Bid Workspace to `closed`; the Bid Workspace remains `disqualified` for archive integrity. |
| `closed` | — | N/A | `closed` is terminal; Emergency Ops post-Phase-12 disqualification writes a `VendorDisqualificationRecord` WITHOUT mutating `bid_workspace.status` | — | Preserves Phase-12 report immutability per §4.7.2 AC #12. |

**Appendix E insertion (authored by this pass).** The Bid Workspace Status row set in Appendix E is extended to include the `disqualified` terminal state — see §25.3.15 Appendix Updates.

**Response (`response_status`, Appendix D — extended herein).**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Actor | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `pending` / `draft` / `submitted` / `needs_reverification` | `locked` | `disqualification_cascade` | `VendorDisqualificationRecord.cascade_status = in_progress` on the owning Bid Workspace | System (cascade worker) | Distinct from the Phase-9 `submitted → locked` transition; tagged `lock_reason = disqualification_cascade` on the row (new optional Response field; §4.4.2) so dashboards and QA can differentiate. |
| `locked` (disqualification-originated) | `submitted` / `draft` (prior) | `disqualification_reversed` | Reversal within 72h OR Ops reversal; row's `lock_reason = disqualification_cascade` | System (reversal worker) | Responses restored to pre-disqualification status; Phase-9 `locked` responses remain `locked` post-reversal (phase semantics supersede). |

**Appendix D insertion (authored by this pass).** The Response Status State Machine is extended with the `*→locked via disqualification_cascade` transition — see §25.3.15 Appendix Updates.

**Q&A Thread (`qa_thread_compose_state`, §21 / §23).**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Actor | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `compose_enabled` | `compose_disabled_orphaned` | `disqualification_cascade` | Vendor is the thread initiator OR the thread's compose window is scoped to this vendor | System (cascade worker) | Vendor retains READ on historical thread; compose surface disabled; `can_reply=false` on seller projection. |
| `compose_disabled_orphaned` | `compose_enabled` | `disqualification_reversed` | Reversal within 72h (owner) OR Ops reversal | System (reversal worker) | Compose restored to pre-disqualification state |

### 25.3.4 Bid Workspace Read-Only Freeze {#25.3.4-bid-workspace-readonly-freeze}

On transition to `bid_workspace.status = disqualified`, the Bid Workspace becomes read-only for the vendor. "Read-only" is enforced at four layers for defense-in-depth:

**Layer 1: Write-guard on every seller-side mutation.** Every Convex mutation that writes to a row whose `bid_workspace_id` has `status = disqualified` returns HTTP 423 `bid_workspace_readonly_disqualified` (new; Appendix I) regardless of the user's seller-role. The guard runs *before* schema validation to avoid leaking internal validation state. Exceptions: DSAR redaction writes by the §6.8 DSAR worker, Ops forensics reads by `ops_compliance_admin`, and reversal writes by the reversal worker itself.

**Layer 2: UI write-surface disable.** Seller-side surfaces (Bid Workspace home, Requirement detail, Q&A thread composer, Document Library attach, First-Pass Responder trigger, KB save-to-KB CTA, export request) render in a disabled visual state with a "Bid Workspace closed — no further edits" tooltip and an inline banner per §25.3.8. The banner is client-verified and server-verified; the client never writes without the server's concurrence.

**Layer 3: Bridge event suppression.** No further Console Bridge Events of a write kind (`requirement_amended`, `requirement_locked`, etc.) target a disqualified Bid Workspace; the bridge apply handler rejects with `failure_reason = target_bid_workspace_disqualified` per §4.7.1. Exception: reversal events (severity-neutral `disqualification_issued` with `reversed=true`) are permitted.

**Layer 4: Managed Agent suppression.** First-Pass Responder, QA Suggester, and KB-Bootstrap agents halt all active sessions targeting this Bid Workspace. Sessions in `running` state transition to `terminated` with `termination_reason = bid_workspace_disqualified` (new enum value for `managed_agent_session_termination_reason` — see §25.3.15). Queued sessions are deleted from the Agent Work Queue without execution; the seller-side Agent Inbox marks them "Cancelled: Bid Workspace closed."

**Idempotency.** A second disqualification cascade against an already-frozen Bid Workspace is a no-op. A second "freeze" write attempt is idempotent by row uniqueness on `VendorDisqualificationRecord(buyer_workspace_id, seller_org_id)` partial where `severity='soft'`.

**Reversal.** Reversal cascade reverses the freeze layers in order: (4) managed-agent re-enablement on operator request; (3) bridge event stream resumes; (2) UI re-enables; (1) write-guard lifts. Revert ordering is deliberately the reverse of application ordering so the vendor never sees a partial-reversal state (e.g., UI clickable while server still rejects).

**Observability.** A gauge `bid_workspace.readonly_freeze_active_count` tagged by `buyer_org_id`, `seller_org_id`, `residency_region` powers the Ops §50 Cross-Workspace Bridge Dashboard; a breach of expected behavior (freeze active with no corresponding disqualification record) raises `bid_workspace_freeze_orphan` Ops alert.

### 25.3.5 Audit Trail Record {#25.3.5-audit-trail-record}

Every disqualification action — including reversal, appeal submission, appeal decision, and cascade completion — writes a row to the Audit Event table (§4.6.1) AND populates the `VendorDisqualificationRecord` cascade-action log (§4.7.2 `cascade_actions_json`). The Audit Event row is the cross-workspace, cross-Org authoritative surface; the cascade-action log is the in-entity forensics surface.

**Audit Event row (written by this pass).** One row per action against the disqualification record:

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization; required | The buyer Org for `severity=soft`; ops-org for `ops_*` actions |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer` for soft disqualifications; `ops` for Ops-originated actions | Appendix J `audit_event_console` |
| `entity_type` | Enum | Fixed `vendor_disqualification_record` | Registered in Appendix J |
| `entity_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → `VendorDisqualificationRecord` | |
| `action` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_disqualification_audit_action` (new; this pass): `disqualified`, `disqualification_reversed`, `disqualification_appeal_submitted`, `disqualification_appeal_decided_upheld`, `disqualification_appeal_decided_overturned`, `disqualification_cascade_completed`, `disqualification_cascade_partial_failure`, `disqualification_notification_sent`, `disqualification_notification_failed`, `disqualification_body_edited_before_dispatch`, `disqualification_notification_style_overridden` | |
| `actor_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → User OR Ops user | |
| `actor_role_snapshot` | Enum | `workspace_roles` OR `ops_roles` | Frozen at write |
| `rationale_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex | `SHA-256(rationale_internal)` at disqualification time; allows QA to assert rationale identity without exposing content |
| `prior_state` | Enum | Source state of the affected primary entity (`target_account.state` OR `bid_workspace.status`) | Context |
| `new_state` | Enum | Destination state | Context |
| `related_audit_chain_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex | Hash chain pointer — see hash-chain section below |
| `timestamp` | Timestamp | UTC; immutable | |
| `ip_address_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex; nullable | Per §6.8 PII salt |
| `user_agent_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex; nullable | Per §6.8 PII salt |
| `workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Workspace; required for soft severity | |
| `bid_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Bid Workspace; required for soft severity | |
| `seller_org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization; required | |
| `target_account_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Target Account; required for soft severity | |
| `notes` | String | ≤ 2,000 chars; nullable | Ops notes on `ops_*` actions |
| `data_residency_region` | Enum | `us`, `eu`, `custom` | Inherits Workspace residency |

**Hash-chain integrity.** Each new Audit Event row for a given `VendorDisqualificationRecord` computes `related_audit_chain_hash = SHA-256(prior_row.related_audit_chain_hash || current_row_canonical_json)` where `current_row_canonical_json` excludes `related_audit_chain_hash` itself (to avoid self-reference). The first row's `related_audit_chain_hash = SHA-256(current_row_canonical_json)`. A nightly integrity job (§42.6 audit-integrity scan) re-computes the chain for every disqualification record active in the last 90 days and raises `audit_chain_break_detected` Ops alert on any mismatch. Rationale: disqualification is a high-impact mutation; an untouched audit chain is operationally and legally load-bearing.

**Retention.** Audit Event rows for `vendor_disqualification_record` entities follow §40.2 Audit Event retention (10 years minimum; legal-hold extends). DSAR field-level redaction applies to `actor_id` and `rationale_hash` per §6.8; the row is never deleted.

**Residency.** Rows inherit residency from the parent `VendorDisqualificationRecord` (§4.7.2 Residency).

**Query surface.** Exposed via `GET /v1/audit-events` (§32.5 Audit Events block) with filter `?entity_type=vendor_disqualification_record&entity_id=<id>` returning the chronological row list. Workspace Owner, Workspace Admin, and Org Admin see full rows; other buyer users see the redacted projection (without `rationale_hash`, `notes`, `ip_address_hash`, `user_agent_hash`). Sellers NEVER see disqualification Audit Event rows — attempts return HTTP 404 `audit_event_cross_console_access` per §7.2 Dual-Console Firewall non-leak rule.

### 25.3.6 Vendor Notification Template {#25.3.6-vendor-notification-template}

**Template id.** `vendor_disqualified.hbs` (already registered in §29.1 / Appendix C Transactional Events; authored herein with the complete copy and substitution contract).

**Dispatch path.** Loops.so transactional send via the §41 email integration; for customers with Slack enabled, an additional Slack DM via the §29.4 Slack integration to the bid-workspace-owner seller identity (Slack DM is opt-in per Seller Org; default off).

**Delivery window.** Within 60 seconds of `VendorDisqualificationRecord.created_at` (§4.7.2 AC #3 and §25.3.13 AC #7). Dispatch failure retries per the §41 Loops.so non-webhook `transactional_email` policy; DLQ after 5 failures with Ops alert and `disqualification.notification_failed` webhook fired.

**Sender.** `noreply@sourcera.io` (transactional). SPF/DKIM/DMARC-aligned per §41.

**Subject line (default).** `Your participation in "{workspace_title}" has ended`.

**Template variables and substitution.**

| Variable | Source | Default / Fallback | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `{vendor_org_name}` | `seller_org.display_name` | `"Vendor"` on NULL | Rendered in greeting |
| `{bid_workspace_owner_first_name}` | `user.first_name` on the Bid Workspace Owner | `"there"` on NULL | Rendered in greeting |
| `{workspace_title}` | `workspace.title` (buyer Workspace) | NO fallback — dispatch rejected with `disqualification_notification_template_variable_missing` (new; Appendix I) if null | Rendered in subject and body |
| `{disqualified_at}` | `VendorDisqualificationRecord.disqualified_at` | Locale-formatted per §37; fallback to ISO 8601 on locale resolution failure | Rendered in body |
| `{notification_body}` | `VendorDisqualificationRecord.notification_body_to_vendor` | Default per `notification_style` (see below) | Body of the email |
| `{buyer_org_display_name}` | `buyer_org.marketplace_display_name` if set, else `buyer_org.display_name` | `"The buyer"` on NULL | Rendered in footer; honors §27.10 Vendor Opt-Out masking if the buyer has opted out of seller-visible branding for this disqualification (edge case; opt-in) |
| `{appeal_cta}` | Rendered only when `appeal_status = eligible` AND `severity ∈ {account_level, global_ban}`; otherwise empty | — | CTA link to `/appeal/{disqualification_id}` magic-link |
| `{support_email}` | `support@sourcera.io` | Fixed | Footer |

**Default body copy by `notification_style`.**

- `neutral_no_rationale` (default): `"Hello {vendor_org_name} team, Your participation in the evaluation \"{workspace_title}\" has ended as of {disqualified_at}. Thank you for your interest and for the time you invested. We wish you the best in future opportunities. — Sourcera, on behalf of {buyer_org_display_name}"`.
- `rationale_shared_with_vendor` (requires buyer explicit opt-in AND Ops approval per §4.7.2): `"Hello {vendor_org_name} team, Your participation in the evaluation \"{workspace_title}\" has ended as of {disqualified_at}. The buyer has elected to share the following context: {notification_body}. Thank you for your interest. — Sourcera, on behalf of {buyer_org_display_name}"`. Note: `{notification_body}` IS the rationale-derived content the buyer has chosen to expose; `rationale_internal` remains firewall-isolated.
- `silent_no_vendor_notification` (global ban, Ops-only): no email sent. Audit row `disqualification_notification_sent` is NOT written; instead `disqualification_notification_suppressed_silent` is written (new enum value in `vendor_disqualification_audit_action`; see §25.3.15).

**Copy constraints.**
- Body length: 50–5,000 chars post-substitution (enforced at substitution time; longer payload → dispatch-time clip with `...` and audit flag `notification_body_truncated`).
- No rationale detail in `neutral_no_rationale`: substitution MUST NOT include `{rationale_internal}` in any form (template linter fails build if the variable appears).
- Forbidden-phrase list: a per-locale blocklist of legally sensitive phrases (e.g., "you are banned", "compliance violation", "security concern" in `neutral_no_rationale` mode) — reviewed by Legal quarterly per §40.2.
- Locale: English default; translations land per §37 internationalization roadmap; untranslated locales fall back to English.
- Accessibility: HTML-safe copy with alt text on any embedded logo; WCAG AA contrast on CTA buttons per §37.

**In-app notification (parallel channel).** Delivered to every seller Bid-Workspace Owner, Bid Contributor, and Seller Team Lead subscribed to `vendor_disqualified` (default: in-app ON, email ON; opt-out disabled — this is a transactional event per §29.1). In-app copy: `"Your Bid Workspace for \"{workspace_title}\" has been closed by the buyer. No further edits are possible. Read the buyer's note."`. Tap → Bid Workspace home with §25.3.8 banner in focus.

**Webhook side-effect.** §25.3.10 `vendor.disqualified` webhook fires on dispatch. `notification_sent_at` is stamped on `VendorDisqualificationRecord` after Loops.so accepts the send; failure sets `notification_sent_at = NULL` and triggers the retry curve.

### 25.3.7 Buyer-Side UX — Disqualified Lane {#25.3.7-buyer-side-ux-disqualified-lane}

Disqualified vendors are grouped into a dedicated "Disqualified" lane in every buyer-side vendor-list surface, so they remain auditable without polluting active-vendor views.

**Surfaces affected.**

1. **Vendor Curation (§6.4 Phase 3).** Three-lane column layout: "Shortlist" (default), "Under Consideration", "Disqualified". Disqualified lane is collapsed by default (summary chip with count); expand reveals full vendor cards with a red "Disqualified" badge, disqualification date, disqualification reason (rendered as the human-readable label from `target_account_disqualification_enum`), and a `…` overflow containing "View disqualification record" and "Reverse (within 72h)" actions. The Reverse action is gated to the 72h window and the user's role per §4.7.2 Reversal; outside the window the action is hidden. Tapping "View disqualification record" opens the §25.3 detail drawer with the full rationale (visible to Workspace Owner / Admin / Use Case Lead; redacted to "Rationale restricted to Workspace Owner" for other buyer users).
2. **Bid Tracker (§6.6).** A "Disqualified" tab adjacent to "Active", "Submitted", "Closed". Tab label includes the count badge. Tab content renders Bid-Workspace rows with `status=disqualified` showing: vendor name, disqualification date, disqualified-by (actor display name), disqualification reason label, "View" and (when in 72h window) "Reverse" actions.
3. **Scoring Matrix (§12).** Every matrix cell corresponding to a disqualified vendor renders the red `Disqualified` badge in place of the numeric score; hover reveals a tooltip with disqualification date and reason label. Sorts treat disqualified vendors as last regardless of score.
4. **Selection Report Draft (§43).** Disqualified vendors appear in a dedicated "Disqualified Vendors" subsection at the end of the vendor-analysis section with a standardized sentence: `"{vendor_org_name} was disqualified on {disqualified_at} ({disqualification_reason_label})."` The vendor's prior scores and notes remain in the report — Phase-12 immutability per §4.7.2 AC #12 prevents rewriting.
5. **Organization Intelligence Vendor History (§15).** Every past disqualification of this vendor by this buyer Org is listed chronologically with `disqualified_at`, `workspace_title`, `disqualification_reason`, and `rationale_internal` (visible to Org Admin and the original Workspace Owner only; other viewers see "Rationale restricted"). A count badge at the top of the Vendor History panel renders "N disqualifications across M workspaces" when N ≥ 2.
6. **Workspace Timeline (Summary §6.27 activity feed).** Every disqualification and reversal emits a timeline row with actor avatar, action ("disqualified X", "reversed disqualification of X"), timestamp, and deep link. The row is visible to all Workspace members; rationale is NOT rendered inline.
7. **Internal Comment inline reference (Summary §6.11).** When a Workspace member @-references a disqualified vendor in a comment, the vendor chip renders with a small strikethrough treatment and a "Disqualified {timeago}" footnote tooltip.

**Plan gating.** None — Disqualified Lane rendering is not plan-gated per §5.11 Feature Access Matrix. Disqualification itself is a core workflow available on every plan tier (Free, Growth, Scale, Enterprise). §5.11 is updated in this pass to explicitly list Disqualification under "Core Workflows — All Tiers" to close the gap.

**Empty state.** When no vendors are disqualified, the "Disqualified" lane renders a single-line empty chip: `"No disqualified vendors."` — no illustration, no pitch. Disqualification is negative-outcome functionality; the empty state MUST NOT feel celebratory per §3.9 UX voice rules.

**Loading state.** Skeleton cards mirror the Active-lane treatment; delay before skeleton render ≥ 300 ms to avoid flash per §3.6.

**Error state.** If the disqualification-record list query fails, render a single-line "Couldn't load disqualified vendors — Retry" banner with a retry button and an error code chip (`request_id` for support). Never block the rest of the page.

**Concurrency — Workspace Owner disqualifies while another Workspace Admin is editing a scoring cell for that vendor.** The scoring-cell submit is rejected on server with HTTP 409 `scoring_cell_vendor_disqualified_concurrent`; client shows an inline warning "This vendor was just disqualified — your score will not be saved" with a "View disqualification" CTA. The scoring draft is preserved locally for 24 hours (per §12 local draft retention) in case of reversal.

**Mobile parity.** Phase 3 Disqualified lane renders parity-collapsed on mobile per §38 Feature Parity Matrix; Bid Tracker Disqualified tab available; Scoring Matrix renders disqualified badges in compact form. "Reverse within 72h" is desktop + mobile (six-tap maximum per the §38.8 destructive-action exception).

### 25.3.8 Vendor-Side UX — Banner + Email {#25.3.8-vendor-side-ux-banner-email}

On disqualification, every vendor-side surface that could otherwise render an editable Bid Workspace control is replaced with a non-dismissible banner and a read-only rendering of prior content.

**Banner copy (seller Bid Workspace home).**

```
Headline: "This Bid Workspace is closed."
Body: "The buyer has ended your participation in '{workspace_title}' as of {disqualified_at}. Your prior responses remain visible but cannot be edited. {buyer_note_cta}"
buyer_note_cta (rendered only when VendorDisqualificationRecord.notification_body_to_vendor exists): "Read the buyer's note →"
CTA (primary): "Contact support" → https://support.sourcera.io/submit?topic=bid_workspace_closed&ref={bid_workspace_id}
```

**Banner visual.** Full-width; neutral-gray background (not red — per §3.9 UX voice rules, disqualification is not a negative-alarm signal to the vendor, it is a neutral closure); bold headline; body in secondary text; primary CTA right-aligned. Non-dismissible (the banner is persistent context, not an interruption). On reversal, the banner replaces its copy with: `"This Bid Workspace is open again. The buyer has reversed the earlier closure on {reversed_at}. You can resume your work."`.

**Q&A thread behavior.** Thread pages render historical posts read-only; the compose surface is hidden; a thread-level one-line notice renders above the compose area: `"You can no longer post here. This Bid Workspace is closed."`. In-flight drafts are preserved locally for 24 hours per Summary §6.11 local draft retention but server submission is blocked.

**Document Library behavior.** Upload surfaces are disabled with tooltip "Bid Workspace closed"; previously-uploaded attachments remain visible and downloadable by the vendor for the full Bid Workspace retention window per §40.2.

**First-Pass Responder, QA Suggester, KB Bootstrap agents.** Any running session transitions to `terminated` per §25.3.4 Layer 4; the Agent Inbox surfaces a "Cancelled: Bid Workspace closed" row with the termination timestamp. No AIOperation is billed for the terminated portion per §4.8.1 state-machine; a partial settlement for any completed sub-call up to the termination boundary is billed per the capability's Outcome Contract (§4.8.4).

**Email notification.** Per §25.3.6. Subject and body as specified. No rationale disclosed unless `notification_style = rationale_shared_with_vendor`.

**Slack DM.** Opt-in per Seller Org; default off. Body is a single-line: `"Bid Workspace '{workspace_title}' has been closed by the buyer. No further edits. [View]"` with a deep-link to the Bid Workspace home.

**Push notification (mobile).** Fires if the seller has push-notification opt-in and is in `vendor_disqualified` subscription (default on). Body: `"Bid Workspace '{workspace_title}' has been closed."`. Tap → Bid Workspace home.

**Cross-vendor firewall.** The banner on Vendor A's Bid Workspace MUST NOT leak Vendor B's disqualification state. The disqualification surface is strictly scoped to the disqualified vendor's Bid Workspace; other bidding vendors see no change and receive no notification.

**Appeal affordance (conditional).** When `severity=soft`, no appeal is offered (per §4.7.2 Appeal Workflow); banner omits appeal affordance entirely. When `severity=account_level` (Seller Org Admin recipient) or `severity=global_ban` (Seller Org Admin recipient), a secondary-CTA "Request review" is rendered, linking to the magic-link appeal form per §4.7.2 and subject to the `appeal_window_at` deadline rendered inline.

**Empty state (pre-disqualification, vendor-side Bid Workspace home).** Unchanged — the vendor sees the normal Bid Workspace home until disqualification fires.

**Accessibility.** Banner is `role="region" aria-labelledby="bid-workspace-closed-heading"`; headline is `aria-level="2"`; CTAs have `aria-describedby` pointing to the banner body for screen-reader context. High-contrast palette; no color-only signal (icon + text). Full keyboard navigation per §37.

### 25.3.9 API — `POST /v1/workspaces/:workspace_id/vendors/:vendor_id/disqualify` {#25.3.9-api-endpoint}

**Method & Path.** `POST https://api.sourcera.io/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/vendors/{target_account_id}/disqualify`. `vendor_id` in the path alias resolves to `target_account_id` on the backing entity (§4.3.20); `vendor_id` is preserved as the path parameter name for API ergonomics continuity with existing vendor-scoped endpoints (§32.5 Vendors / Target Accounts block).

**Auth.** `Authorization: Bearer srck_{org_prefix}_{token_string}` per §32.2. Token scope: `write:workspaces` OR `admin:workspaces`.
