Token's owning user MUST hold `workspace_owner`, `workspace_admin`, or — when the Target Account is associated with a Use Case the user leads — `use_case_lead` on the target Workspace. Other roles return HTTP 403 `vendor_disqualification_role_forbidden` (§4.7.2 AC #11; registered in Appendix I).

**RBAC one-liner.** Workspace Owner / Workspace Admin always; Use Case Lead only for Target Accounts whose Use Cases intersect the user's leads.

**Formal `use_case_lead` authorization predicate.** The predicate is:

```
AUTHORIZED(user, target_account) :=
  (user.workspace_role ∈ {workspace_owner, workspace_admin})
  OR
  (user.workspace_role = use_case_lead
   AND target_account.included_use_case_ids ∩ user.led_use_case_ids_on_this_workspace ≠ ∅)
```

where:

- `target_account.included_use_case_ids` is the set of Use Case ids on the current Workspace that reference this Target Account via their `target_account_ids` list (§4.3.2 Use Case entity). The join is materialized at read time from the `(use_case.target_account_ids[])` GIN index on the Use Case table; no denormalized column is added.
- `user.led_use_case_ids_on_this_workspace` is the set of Use Case ids on the current Workspace where `use_case.lead_user_id = user.id`. Computed from the `(workspace_id, lead_user_id)` index on the Use Case table at authorization time.
- Intersection of two empty sets fails the predicate — a Use Case Lead whose led Use Cases do NOT reference this Target Account receives HTTP 403 `vendor_disqualification_role_forbidden` even if they hold `use_case_lead` on the Workspace.
- A user who holds both `workspace_admin` and `use_case_lead` on the same Workspace passes via the `workspace_admin` clause regardless of Use Case intersection.
- A user whose `use_case.lead_user_id` was set at one point but has since been reassigned is NOT authorized (the intersection is computed against *current* `lead_user_id` assignment, not historical). Role-snapshot fields on audit rows (per §25.3.5) freeze the role at action time; authorization is evaluated at request time.

The same predicate governs Use Case Lead authorization for the disqualification reversal endpoint (§25.3.10a) — but noting that the reversal endpoint restricts the base role set to Workspace Owner only for the 72h owner path; Use Case Lead is NOT a permitted reversal role.

The predicate is codified in a shared TypeScript utility `canDisqualifyVendor(user, targetAccount, workspace)` registered in the `@sourcera/auth` package; unit-tested against the full role-matrix per §25.3.13 AC #2. Logged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` → Authored Extensions → §25.3.9 `use_case_lead` Predicate (2026-04-24).

**Rate-Limit Class.** `standard_authenticated_per_org` per §32.4.5 (5,000/h soft, 10,000/h hard, 100/min burst). Disqualification is low-volume by nature; no dedicated class.

**Path Parameters.**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `workspace_id` | UUID | Yes | Buyer Workspace id. MUST belong to the token's Org; mismatch → HTTP 404 `invalid_workspace_id`. |
| `vendor_id` | UUID | Yes | Target Account id (path alias; backing FK is `target_account_id`). Target Account MUST belong to `workspace_id`; mismatch → HTTP 404 `invalid_vendor_id`. |

**Request Headers.**

- `Idempotency-Key: <opaque-string>` — REQUIRED. 1–128 chars; ASCII printable. Per §32.8.0 idempotency contract. Replays return HTTP 200 with the original response body and `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`; body-different replays return HTTP 409 `idempotency_key_request_mismatch`.
- `Content-Type: application/json`.

**Request Body.**

```json
{
  "rationale_internal": "<string; 10-4000 chars; required; buyer-private>",
  "disqualification_reason": "<enum; target_account_disqualification_enum; required>",
  "disqualification_note": "<string; 0-2000 chars; optional; required when disqualification_reason=buyer_discretion>",
  "notification_body_to_vendor": "<string; 50-5000 chars; optional; default derived per notification_style>",
  "notification_style": "<enum; vendor_disqualification_notification_style; default 'neutral_no_rationale'>"
}
```

**Field semantics.**

- `rationale_internal`: stored on `VendorDisqualificationRecord.rationale_internal`; never crosses the firewall; hashed into `rationale_hash` on the audit row. Markdown is NOT parsed; stored as plain text.
- `disqualification_reason`: must be a member of `target_account_disqualification_enum` (§4.3.20). `buyer_discretion` MUST be accompanied by a non-empty `disqualification_note`; other values leave `disqualification_note` optional.
- `notification_body_to_vendor`: the exact body that will substitute for `{notification_body}` in the `vendor_disqualified.hbs` template (§25.3.6). When absent, the server renders the default body per `notification_style`. Rejected with HTTP 422 `disqualification_notification_body_forbidden_phrase` if it contains any phrase from the forbidden-phrase blocklist (§25.3.6).
- `notification_style`: defaults to `neutral_no_rationale`. `rationale_shared_with_vendor` requires the caller's Org to hold the `rationale_sharing_opt_in=true` Org setting AND Ops approval on record; violations return HTTP 422 `vendor_disqualification_rationale_sharing_not_approved`. `silent_no_vendor_notification` is NOT available to buyer users — Ops-only; violations return HTTP 403 `vendor_disqualification_silent_forbidden_for_buyer`.

**Response (HTTP 201 Created).**

```json
{
  "disqualification_record": {
    "id": "vdr_abc123...",
    "severity": "soft",
    "buyer_org_id": "org_buyer_...",
    "buyer_workspace_id": "ws_...",
    "seller_org_id": "org_seller_...",
    "bid_workspace_id": "bw_...",
    "target_account_id": "ta_...",
    "trigger": "workspace_owner_manual",
    "rationale_author_user_id": "usr_...",
    "rationale_author_role_snapshot": "workspace_owner",
    "notification_style": "neutral_no_rationale",
    "notification_body_to_vendor": "Your participation in 'Q4 CRM Evaluation' has ended. Thank you for your interest.",
    "notification_sent_at": null,
    "cascade_status": "in_progress",
    "cascade_started_at": "2026-04-24T14:30:00.000Z",
    "appeal_status": "not_offered",
    "appeal_window_at": null,
    "reversed_at": null,
    "reversal_window_expires_at": "2026-04-27T14:30:00.000Z",
    "created_at": "2026-04-24T14:30:00.000Z",
    "created_by": "usr_..."
  },
  "target_account": {
    "id": "ta_...",
    "state": "disqualified",
    "disqualification_reason": "buyer_discretion"
  },
  "bid_workspace": {
    "id": "bw_...",
    "status": "disqualified"
  },
  "audit_event_id": "ae_..."
}
```

Notes on the 201 response:
- The response is returned *after* the synchronous portion of the cascade commits (Target Account status, Bid Workspace status, Response bulk-lock, Bridge Event creation). Vendor notification dispatch is asynchronous via the §41 Loops.so queue; `notification_sent_at` is null at 201 and populated on successful send (verifiable via webhook `vendor.disqualified` or a follow-up `GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/disqualifications/{id}` read).
- `reversal_window_expires_at = created_at + 72h` per §4.7.2 Reversal. Callers use this to render the "Reverse within 72h" affordance window per §25.3.7.
- Cascade completion (`cascade_status = complete`) is asserted within 10 seconds of 201 per §25.4 AC #4. A caller that polls the endpoint should see `cascade_status = complete` on the first re-read in the vast majority of cases.

**Errors.** Registered additions in Appendix I via §25.3.15:

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `vendor_disqualification_role_forbidden` | 403 | Caller lacks `workspace_owner` / `workspace_admin` / `use_case_lead` on this Workspace (and for `use_case_lead`, this Target Account does not intersect any of caller's Use Case leads). |
| `vendor_disqualification_soft_requires_workspace_scope` | 422 | Missing `workspace_id` / `target_account_id` in path OR the backing Target Account has no associated `bid_workspace_id` (pre-Phase-3 state). |
| `vendor_already_disqualified` | 409 | A `VendorDisqualificationRecord(buyer_workspace_id, seller_org_id, severity='soft')` already exists; reversal path (`POST /.../reverse`) or view path (`GET /.../disqualifications/{id}`) should be used instead. |
| `vendor_disqualification_invalid_reason` | 422 | `disqualification_reason` not in `target_account_disqualification_enum`. |
| `vendor_disqualification_note_required` | 422 | `disqualification_reason=buyer_discretion` with empty / null `disqualification_note`. |
| `disqualification_notification_body_forbidden_phrase` | 422 | `notification_body_to_vendor` contains a phrase from the forbidden-phrase blocklist. |
| `disqualification_notification_template_variable_missing` | 422 | Substitution rejected at dispatch time (server-side; emitted asynchronously; surfaces on webhook path `disqualification.notification_failed`). |
| `vendor_disqualification_rationale_sharing_not_approved` | 422 | `notification_style=rationale_shared_with_vendor` but Org lacks `rationale_sharing_opt_in=true` OR Ops approval record missing. |
| `vendor_disqualification_silent_forbidden_for_buyer` | 403 | Buyer attempt to set `notification_style=silent_no_vendor_notification`; Ops-only. |
| `workspace_phase_out_of_range_for_disqualification` | 422 | Parent Workspace phase ∉ [3, 11]; post-Phase-12 disqualification requires the Emergency Ops path per §4.7.2 FM #2. |
| `workspace_cancelled` | 403 | Parent Workspace in `canceled` state. |
| `workspace_archived` | 403 | Parent Workspace in `archived` state. |
| `disqualification_cascade_partial_failure` | 207 | Synchronous cascade failed on one or more sub-actions; response body includes `cascade_actions_json` with per-action outcomes. Retryable by caller. Registered separately because disqualification is a multi-write cascade; partial failure returns 207 (per §32.6 Multi-Status semantics, used sparingly) with remediation guidance. |

**Idempotency semantics.** The `Idempotency-Key` guarantees that duplicate submits of the same disqualification (same `(rationale_internal, disqualification_reason, notification_style, notification_body_to_vendor)` tuple) are collapsed into a single `VendorDisqualificationRecord`. A duplicate with the same key and a *different* request body returns HTTP 409 `idempotency_key_request_mismatch`; a duplicate after the 24h idempotency window with the same body is treated as a new attempt and rejects with `vendor_already_disqualified` (because the first attempt's record now exists). This is deliberate: the idempotency key protects against network-retry double-submit within 24h; after 24h, the authoritative `vendor_already_disqualified` error is the correct signal.

**Concurrency.** Two disqualification requests racing against the same `(buyer_workspace_id, seller_org_id)` on the same wall-clock second — one wins; the other receives HTTP 409 `vendor_already_disqualified` with the winning record's `id` in `error.details.existing_disqualification_id`. Winner is determined by the row-insert order enforced at the `VendorDisqualificationRecord(buyer_workspace_id, seller_org_id)` unique partial index (§4.7.2 Indexes).

**Reversal endpoint (cross-reference).** `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/vendors/{vendor_id}/disqualify/{disqualification_id}/reverse` — full API detail is authored in §25.3.10a, with the underlying reversal semantics governed by §4.7.2 Reversal and the Multi-Status response shape governed by §32.6.1.

**Example request.**

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.sourcera.io/v1/workspaces/ws_2a3b/vendors/ta_9c8d/disqualify" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer srck_acme_1234..." \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: disq-2026-04-24-ws_2a3b-ta_9c8d" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "rationale_internal": "Failed SOC 2 evidence review; cannot meet Q2 compliance deadline.",
    "disqualification_reason": "compliance_fail",
    "notification_style": "neutral_no_rationale"
  }'
```

**Example response (201 Created).**

```json
{
  "disqualification_record": { "id": "vdr_7f2e...", "severity": "soft", "cascade_status": "in_progress", "reversal_window_expires_at": "2026-04-27T14:30:00.000Z", "created_at": "2026-04-24T14:30:00.000Z" },
  "target_account": { "id": "ta_9c8d", "state": "disqualified", "disqualification_reason": "compliance_fail" },
  "bid_workspace": { "id": "bw_41a7", "status": "disqualified" },
  "audit_event_id": "ae_3b9f..."
}
```

### 25.3.10 Webhook — `vendor.disqualified` {#25.3.10-webhook-vendor-disqualified}

**Registered in.** Appendix C (Notification Event Catalog) under a new Disqualification-Domain subsection (authored herein — see §25.3.15) AND Appendix G (PostHog Event Taxonomy) as `vendor.disqualified`.

**Trigger.** `VendorDisqualificationRecord.cascade_status` transitions `in_progress → complete` on a `severity=soft` record. For `severity ∈ {account_level, global_ban}`, a parallel webhook `vendor.disqualified.org_level` is fired per §4.7.2 (authored in a follow-up pass; tracked as Known Gap).

**Fired by.** Disqualification cascade worker, after the synchronous cascade phase completes.

**Fired at most ONCE per `VendorDisqualificationRecord`.** Reversal fires `vendor.disqualification.reversed` (registered in §25.3.15; body mirrors `vendor.disqualified` with `reversed_at` and `reversal_reason`).

**Transport.** HMAC-SHA256 signed per §31; `X-Sourcera-Signature: sha256=<hex>`; idempotency via `event_id` in the §31.1 canonical format `evt_{unix_ms}_{base32_random10}`; Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve; DLQ after 5 hard failures; payload ≤ 256 KB.

**Recipients.** Both buyer Org subscribed endpoints AND seller Org subscribed endpoints. The payload is pre-redacted for console-firewall safety: buyer Org endpoints receive the *full* payload; seller Org endpoints receive a redacted projection (`rationale_hash`, `rationale_author_user_id`, and any internal fields omitted). The two payloads share an `event_id` but are transported as independent webhook deliveries.

**Payload `data` (buyer Org projection).**

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `disqualification_id` | UUID | FK → VendorDisqualificationRecord |
| `severity` | Enum | `soft` |
| `buyer_org_id` | UUID | FK → Organization |
| `buyer_workspace_id` | UUID | FK → Workspace |
| `bid_workspace_id` | UUID | FK → Bid Workspace |
| `target_account_id` | UUID | FK → Target Account |
| `seller_org_id` | UUID | FK → Organization (the disqualified seller) |
| `seller_org_display_name` | String | Marketplace-safe display name |
| `disqualification_reason` | Enum | `target_account_disqualification_enum` |
| `disqualification_note` | String (nullable) | Vendor-visible note when `notification_style = rationale_shared_with_vendor`; null otherwise |
| `notification_style` | Enum | `vendor_disqualification_notification_style` |
| `notification_body_to_vendor` | String | The final substituted body; identical to what the vendor received |
| `notification_sent_at` | Timestamp (nullable) | Populated after successful Loops.so send; null on retry/DLQ |
| `cascade_status` | Enum | `complete` (for this event); `partial_failure` never appears here because that fires `disqualification.cascade_partial_failure` instead |
| `cascade_started_at` | Timestamp | Mirrors record `cascade_started_at` |
| `cascade_completed_at` | Timestamp | Mirrors record `cascade_completed_at` |
| `reversal_window_expires_at` | Timestamp | `created_at + 72h` |
| `rationale_author_user_id` | UUID | User who wrote the rationale (buyer-console only) |
| `rationale_author_role_snapshot` | Enum | `workspace_roles` value frozen at write |
| `rationale_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex of `rationale_internal` (does NOT disclose rationale; enables QA assertion) |
| `audit_event_id` | UUID | FK → Audit Event (the `disqualified` row) |
| `audit_chain_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex; hash-chain head for this record |
| `console_bridge_event_id` | UUID | FK → Console Bridge Event |
| `data_residency_region` | Enum | Inherited from Workspace |

**Payload `data` (seller Org projection).** Subset: `disqualification_id`, `severity`, `bid_workspace_id`, `seller_org_id`, `notification_style`, `notification_body_to_vendor`, `notification_sent_at`, `reversal_window_expires_at`, `data_residency_region`, AND the redacted fields `rationale_author_user_id = null`, `rationale_hash = null`, `audit_chain_hash = null`, `disqualification_reason = "redacted"`, `disqualification_note = null`, `rationale_author_role_snapshot = null`, `cascade_started_at = redacted`, `cascade_completed_at = redacted`. The seller's own `bid_workspace_id` and related fields are present so that downstream integrations can correlate with their own systems. The `buyer_workspace_id`, `target_account_id`, `rationale_author_user_id`, and `audit_event_id` are NEVER present in the seller projection.

**Companion webhooks registered in this pass.**

- `vendor.disqualification.reversed` — fires on `VendorDisqualificationRecord.reversed_at` stamp (soft reversal within 72h; Ops reversal; appeal-overturned). Payload mirrors `vendor.disqualified` with `reversed_at`, `reversed_by_user_id`, `reversal_reason` added.
- `disqualification.cascade_partial_failure` — fires when the synchronous cascade phase completes with one or more sub-action failures. Payload includes `cascade_actions_json` with per-action outcomes, `retry_strategy = auto|manual`, and `retry_after_at`.
- `disqualification.notification_failed` — fires after the Loops.so retry curve exhausts. Payload includes `notification_failure_reason ∈ {loops_5xx_exhausted, template_variable_missing, recipient_suppressed, seller_org_deleted}` and an Ops escalation flag.

**Volume budget.** Disqualifications are low-volume by nature. Pricing Strategy §6 projects < 10 disqualifications / Org / month at Enterprise scale. Webhook throughput budget: 1/minute sustained per Org; 10/minute burst. The webhook catalog row documents no special scale budget beyond §31 defaults.

**Per-console field nullification.** As above — seller projection is pre-redacted by the cascade worker before dispatch.

**Volume-dedup guard.** If the same `(disqualification_id, event_kind)` is enqueued twice (e.g., after a worker restart), the dispatch layer dedupes by `event_id` uniqueness (UNIQUE index on `webhook_deliveries(event_id)`). Consumer-side dedup is still required per §31.1.

### 25.3.10a API — Reversal — `POST /v1/workspaces/:workspace_id/vendors/:vendor_id/disqualify/:disqualification_id/reverse` {#25.3.10a-api-reversal-endpoint}

**Authoring Intent.** §25.3.9 authored the disqualification creation endpoint. §25.3.10a authors the reversal endpoint at the same §32 fidelity. The underlying semantic (reversal within 72h by Workspace Owner, or post-72h by Ops Compliance) is the §4.7.2 Reversal contract; §25.3.10a is the REST surface for it.

**Method & Path.** `POST https://api.sourcera.io/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/vendors/{target_account_id}/disqualify/{disqualification_id}/reverse`.

**Auth.** `Authorization: Bearer srck_{org_prefix}_{token_string}` per §32.2. Token scope: `write:workspaces` OR `admin:workspaces` for the 72h owner-reversal path; `admin:ops_compliance` for the post-72h Ops path. Token's owning user MUST hold `workspace_owner` on the target Workspace for 72h-window reversals; `ops_compliance_admin` for post-72h reversals. `workspace_admin` and `use_case_lead` roles are explicitly NOT permitted to reverse (per §4.7.2 Reversal Authority — reversal discretion is concentrated at the Workspace Owner for the 72h window to preserve a clean accountability line; Ops carries post-window discretion).

**RBAC one-liner.** Workspace Owner only within 72h of `disqualified_at`; Ops Compliance Admin at any time (no expiry) with `ops_manual_reversal` reason.

**Rate-Limit Class.** `standard_authenticated_per_org` per §32.4.5. Reversals are lower-volume than disqualifications; no dedicated class.

**Path Parameters.**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `workspace_id` | UUID | Yes | Buyer Workspace id. Cross-tenant check; mismatch → HTTP 404 `invalid_workspace_id`. |
| `vendor_id` | UUID | Yes | Target Account id (path alias for ergonomics). Must belong to `workspace_id`; mismatch → HTTP 404 `invalid_vendor_id`. |
| `disqualification_id` | UUID | Yes | The `VendorDisqualificationRecord` id being reversed. Must belong to `(workspace_id, vendor_id)`; mismatch → HTTP 404 `invalid_disqualification_id`. |

**Request Headers.**

- `Idempotency-Key: <opaque-string>` — REQUIRED. 1–128 chars; ASCII printable. Per §32.8.0 idempotency contract. Replays return HTTP 200 with the original response body and `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`; body-different replays return HTTP 409 `idempotency_key_request_mismatch`.
- `Content-Type: application/json`.

**Request Body.**

```json
{
  "reversal_reason": "<enum; vendor_disqualification_reversal_reason; required>",
  "reversal_note_internal": "<string; 20-4000 chars; required for ops_manual_reversal path, optional for buyer_workspace_owner_reversal_within_72h>",
  "vendor_notification_override": "<string; 50-5000 chars; optional; default derived from notification_style at original disqualification time>"
}
```

**Field semantics.**

- `reversal_reason` MUST be a member of `vendor_disqualification_reversal_reason` (Appendix J): `buyer_workspace_owner_reversal_within_72h` (owner path; caller MUST be within 72h window), `ops_manual_reversal` (Ops path; requires `ops_compliance_admin`), `appeal_overturned` (Ops path; requires linked `appeal_id`; not applicable to `severity=soft` because soft disqualifications do not offer appeal per §4.7.2), `system_error_rollback` (Ops path; reserved for post-incident corrections).
- `reversal_note_internal` is stored on `VendorDisqualificationRecord.reversal_note_internal` (new field authored in this pass; see §25.3.15). NEVER crosses firewall. Required for Ops paths; optional for owner path. Markdown not parsed; plain text.
- `vendor_notification_override` substitutes for `{reversal_body_to_vendor}` in the `vendor_disqualification_reversed.hbs` template (new; §41 template registry). Default body: `"Your participation in \"{workspace_title}\" has been restored as of {reversed_at}. You can resume your work."` for neutral; longer explanation permitted. Rejected on forbidden-phrase match per §25.3.6 blocklist inheritance.

**Response (HTTP 200 OK).**

```json
{
  "disqualification_record": {
    "id": "vdr_abc123...",
    "severity": "soft",
    "buyer_workspace_id": "ws_...",
    "seller_org_id": "org_seller_...",
    "reversed_at": "2026-04-25T09:15:00.000Z",
    "reversed_by_user_id": "usr_...",
    "reversal_reason": "buyer_workspace_owner_reversal_within_72h",
    "reversal_cascade_status": "in_progress",
    "reversal_cascade_started_at": "2026-04-25T09:15:00.000Z"
  },
  "target_account": {
    "id": "ta_...",
    "state": "bidding",
    "disqualification_reason": null
  },
  "bid_workspace": {
    "id": "bw_...",
    "status": "active"
  },
  "audit_event_id": "ae_...",
  "reversal_event_id": "ae_reversal_..."
}
```

The response is returned after the synchronous portion of the reversal cascade commits (Target Account status restoration, Bid Workspace status restoration, Response bulk-unlock of disqualification-originated locks). Vendor notification dispatch is asynchronous via §41 Loops.so queue. Managed Agent session re-enablement is operator-gated (sessions remain `terminated` by default; the seller must re-submit to re-queue). `reversal_cascade_status = complete` is asserted within 10 seconds per §25.3.13 AC #14.

**Errors.** Registered additions in Appendix I via §25.3.15:

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `vendor_disqualification_reversal_role_forbidden` | 403 | Caller lacks `workspace_owner` (for 72h owner path) or `ops_compliance_admin` (for Ops paths). |
| `vendor_disqualification_reversal_window_expired` | 422 | `reversal_reason=buyer_workspace_owner_reversal_within_72h` submitted after `reversal_window_expires_at`. |
| `vendor_disqualification_already_reversed` | 409 | The disqualification record already has `reversed_at` populated; no-op replays return the existing row via idempotency; distinct-key re-attempts return this error with `error.details.reversed_at` populated. |
| `vendor_disqualification_reversal_note_required` | 422 | Ops-path reversal (`ops_manual_reversal`, `appeal_overturned`, `system_error_rollback`) without `reversal_note_internal` ≥ 20 chars. |
| `vendor_disqualification_reversal_appeal_not_applicable` | 422 | `reversal_reason=appeal_overturned` but the record has `severity=soft` (appeal not offered for soft per §4.7.2). |
| `vendor_disqualification_reversal_appeal_not_found` | 422 | `reversal_reason=appeal_overturned` without a linked `appeal_id` resolving to a valid `appeal_submitted` state on the record. |
| `disqualification_reversal_cascade_partial_failure` | 207 | Synchronous reversal cascade failed on one or more sub-actions; body includes `reversal_cascade_actions_json` with per-action outcomes. Retryable by caller. |
| `workspace_archived` | 403 | Parent Workspace in `archived` state — reversal path is unavailable; route to Ops. |

**Idempotency semantics.** `Idempotency-Key` guarantees duplicate submits of the same reversal (same `reversal_reason`, `reversal_note_internal`, `vendor_notification_override` tuple) collapse into a single reversal operation. Different-body replays → 409 `idempotency_key_request_mismatch`. Distinct-key replays after the operation commits → 409 `vendor_disqualification_already_reversed`.

**Concurrency.** Two racing reversals on the same record — one wins (first insert sets `reversed_at`); loser receives 409 `vendor_disqualification_already_reversed` with `error.details.reversed_at` populated with the winning reversal timestamp.

**Cascade.** Reversal cascade reverses the §25.3.4 four-layer freeze in *reverse order* (L4 → L1) per §25.3.4 text, and reverses the four state-machine transitions in §25.3.3 (Target Account → prior state, Bid Workspace → prior state, Response → prior state where row is disqualification-originated-locked, Q&A Thread → `compose_enabled`). Audit trail hash-chain extends per §25.3.5 — a `disqualification_reversed` action row is appended with monotonic `related_audit_chain_hash`. The `vendor.disqualification.reversed` webhook fires on `reversal_cascade_status → complete` per §25.3.10 companion webhook contract.

**PostHog events.** `vendor_disqualification_reversed` (per §25.3.11, with `time_to_reversal_seconds`, `reversed_in_72h_window ∈ {true, false}`, and `reversal_reason`). The `vendor_disqualification_cascade_completed` event also emits on the reversal cascade with `cascade_direction=reversal` property (new property authored here) to disambiguate from the original disqualification cascade.

**Plan gating.** None — reversal is a core workflow available on every plan tier, paired with §25.3.16.

**Example request.**

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.sourcera.io/v1/workspaces/ws_2a3b/vendors/ta_9c8d/disqualify/vdr_7f2e/reverse" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer srck_acme_1234..." \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: rev-2026-04-25-vdr_7f2e" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "reversal_reason": "buyer_workspace_owner_reversal_within_72h",
    "reversal_note_internal": "Additional SOC 2 evidence surfaced; reinstating vendor for continued evaluation."
  }'
```

**Example response (200 OK).**

```json
{
  "disqualification_record": { "id": "vdr_7f2e...", "reversed_at": "2026-04-25T09:15:00.000Z", "reversal_reason": "buyer_workspace_owner_reversal_within_72h", "reversal_cascade_status": "in_progress" },
  "target_account": { "id": "ta_9c8d", "state": "bidding", "disqualification_reason": null },
  "bid_workspace": { "id": "bw_41a7", "status": "active" },
  "audit_event_id": "ae_3b9f...",
  "reversal_event_id": "ae_reversal_1c2d..."
}
```

### 25.3.10b Webhook — `vendor.disqualified.org_level` {#25.3.10b-webhook-vendor-disqualified-org-level}

**Scope.** Companion to `vendor.disqualified` (§25.3.10) for disqualification events with `severity ∈ {account_level, global_ban}`. The `severity=soft` mainline continues to use `vendor.disqualified`; the organization-level and platform-ban events use this distinct event name so that subscribers can route them to different consumers (e.g., seller-side CRM integrations that need to close all opportunities with a buyer on an account_level ban, or compliance systems that need immediate notice of a global_ban).

**Registered in.** Appendix C Disqualification-Domain subsection (authored in §25.3.15 by the Phase-9 follow-up pass on 2026-04-24) AND Appendix G as `vendor.disqualified.org_level`.

**Trigger.** `VendorDisqualificationRecord.cascade_status` transitions `in_progress → complete` on a `severity ∈ {account_level, global_ban}` record. Fires exactly once per record.

**Transport.** HMAC-SHA256 signed per §31; `X-Sourcera-Signature: sha256=<hex>`; idempotency via `event_id`; Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve; DLQ after 5 hard failures; payload ≤ 256 KB.

**Recipients and projections.**

- **Buyer Org endpoints.** Receive the full payload with `severity`, `buyer_org_id`, `seller_org_id`, `seller_org_display_name`, `disqualification_reason`, `disqualification_note` (when `notification_style = rationale_shared_with_vendor`), `rationale_author_user_id`, `rationale_author_role_snapshot`, `rationale_hash`, `notification_style`, `notification_body_to_vendor`, `notification_sent_at`, `cascade_status`, `cascade_started_at`, `cascade_completed_at`, `appeal_status`, `appeal_window_at`, `audit_event_id`, `audit_chain_hash`, `console_bridge_event_id`, `data_residency_region`. For `severity=account_level`, `affected_workspace_ids` is populated as an array of every Workspace in the buyer Org where the seller is excluded forward. For `severity=global_ban`, `buyer_org_id` is null (global bans are platform-originated, not buyer-originated) and `imposed_by_ops_user_id` is populated instead.
- **Seller Org endpoints.** Receive a redacted projection: `disqualification_id`, `severity`, `seller_org_id`, `notification_style`, `notification_body_to_vendor`, `notification_sent_at`, `appeal_status`, `appeal_window_at`, `data_residency_region`, `affected_scope_description` (derived string — "All current and future evaluations by {buyer_org_marketplace_display_name}" for account_level, "All Sourcera marketplace listings and bid workspaces" for global_ban). `buyer_org_id` is masked to `"buyer_on_sourcera"` token for account_level (unless the buyer has explicitly disclosed identity via `notification_style=rationale_shared_with_vendor`); for global_ban, `buyer_org_id` is null and `imposed_by_ops_user_id` is masked to `"sourcera_ops"`. The seller projection never reveals `rationale_internal`, `rationale_hash`, `audit_event_id`, `audit_chain_hash`, or `cascade_actions_json`.
- **Ops alerting endpoint.** Ops subscribes to a separate `ops.vendor.disqualified.org_level` channel with full fidelity for both severities — this is the authoritative log for Ops-initiated global bans and for dual-signoff account-level bans per §4.7.2.

**Companion webhooks.** `vendor.disqualification.reversed` (registered in §25.3.10) fires on reversal of `account_level` and `global_ban` records as well; the `severity` field in the payload is sufficient to disambiguate. `disqualification.cascade_partial_failure` and `disqualification.notification_failed` likewise fire across severities.

**Fire-once-per-record semantics.** The `vendor.disqualified.org_level` webhook fires exactly once per record, at `cascade_status → complete`. A `severity=soft` record is upgraded to `severity=account_level` or `severity=global_ban` via Ops action (`disqualification_severity_escalated` audit action, new in Appendix J) — the escalation fires `vendor.disqualified.org_level` as a new event (not as a modification of the original); the original `vendor.disqualified` remains in the audit log as the initial soft event.

**Volume budget.** Account-level and global-ban events are very low-volume (<1/month/Org at Enterprise scale, <10/month platform-wide). Webhook throughput budget: 1/minute sustained, 5/minute burst per endpoint.

**Acceptance criteria addition.** §25.3.13 is extended with:

21. `vendor.disqualified.org_level` MUST fire on `cascade_status → complete` for `severity ∈ {account_level, global_ban}`; payload MUST be pre-redacted per §25.3.10b; buyer/seller/Ops channels MUST each receive the correct projection. Integration test matrix covering all three severities and all three recipient types.

### 25.3.11 PostHog Telemetry Surface {#25.3.11-posthog-telemetry-surface}

Every disqualification action emits a PostHog event per Appendix G taxonomy. Events are added under a new `event_family=disqualification` grouping registered in this pass. The event set:

| Event Name | Fired When | Actor | Standard Properties | Event-Specific Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `vendor_disqualified` | `VendorDisqualificationRecord` created (severity=soft) | buyer user | `org_id`, `user_id`, `console=buyer`, `workspace_id`, `bid_workspace_id`, `data_residency_region` | `disqualification_id`, `target_account_id`, `seller_org_id`, `disqualification_reason`, `notification_style`, `phase_at_disqualification ∈ Appendix J pipeline_phase values phase_3_use_case_validation..phase_11_score_review` |
| `vendor_disqualification_reversed` | `VendorDisqualificationRecord.reversed_at` stamped | buyer user OR Ops user | Same | `disqualification_id`, `reversal_reason`, `time_to_reversal_seconds`, `reversed_in_72h_window ∈ {true, false}` |
| `vendor_disqualification_cascade_completed` | `cascade_status → complete` | system | Same | `disqualification_id`, `cascade_duration_ms` |
| `vendor_disqualification_cascade_partial_failure` | `cascade_status → partial_failure` | system | Same | `disqualification_id`, `failed_actions` (array of action names) |
| `vendor_disqualification_notification_sent` | Loops.so confirms send | system | Same, with `console=buyer` or `console=seller` depending on recipient | `disqualification_id`, `notification_channel ∈ {email, in_app, slack, push}`, `dispatch_latency_ms` |
| `vendor_disqualification_notification_failed` | Loops.so retry curve exhausts | system | Same | `disqualification_id`, `failure_reason` |
| `vendor_disqualification_banner_viewed` | Seller first loads the vendor-side banner (§25.3.8) | seller user | `org_id`, `user_id`, `console=seller`, `bid_workspace_id`, `data_residency_region` | `disqualification_id`, `time_since_disqualification_seconds`, `vendor_acknowledgement_at` (if this is the first view) |
| `vendor_disqualification_buyer_detail_viewed` | Buyer opens the §25.3.7 detail drawer | buyer user | `org_id`, `user_id`, `console=buyer`, `workspace_id`, `bid_workspace_id` | `disqualification_id`, `viewer_role_snapshot`, `rationale_visible ∈ {true, false}` (true only for Workspace Owner/Admin/Use Case Lead; false for redacted viewers) |
| `vendor_disqualification_reverse_attempted` | Buyer taps "Reverse within 72h" | buyer user | Same | `disqualification_id`, `minutes_remaining_in_window`, `outcome ∈ {success, failure}` |
| `vendor_disqualification_appeal_submitted` | Seller submits appeal (account_level / global_ban) | seller user | `org_id`, `user_id`, `console=seller` | `disqualification_id`, `time_to_appeal_seconds` |

**k-anonymity.** Cross-Org aggregates over `vendor_disqualified` (e.g., "disqualification rate by category") honor the k=10 cross-Org cohort floor per §48.4.7; per-vendor disclosure honors k=5 person-level floor; cells below the floor are suppressed with `usage_analytics_k_anon_floor_hit`.

**Residency.** Events route to the residency-appropriate PostHog project per §51.7.3 outbox routing.

**Retention.** Per §40.2 Usage Event retention — 24-month rolling raw, Org-life monthly aggregates.

**DSAR.** Per §51.7 field-level redaction; `user_id` pseudonymized on subject-user DSAR; `disqualification_id` retained.

### 25.3.12 Failure Modes & Counterfactual Pass {#25.3.12-failure-modes-counterfactual-pass}

Opus-mandatory: at least three failure modes per new feature, each with a spec'd mitigation. Eight authored here.

**FM1 — Dual-actor race: two Workspace Admins click "Disqualify" on the same vendor simultaneously.** Mitigation: `VendorDisqualificationRecord(buyer_workspace_id, seller_org_id)` unique partial index (§4.7.2); loser receives HTTP 409 `vendor_already_disqualified`; client UI shows "This vendor was disqualified by {actor} a moment ago" with the winner's actor name and a "View disqualification" CTA. Property test: 10,000 synthesized concurrent submits across different workspaces with 10% same-workspace contention.

**FM2 — Loops.so outage during notification dispatch.** Mitigation: §25.3.6 dispatch retry curve (5 attempts over ~1h45m), DLQ, `disqualification.notification_failed` webhook, Ops alert. The disqualification itself commits regardless of notification outcome — vendor notification is an eventual-consistency surface, not a commit precondition. Vendor sees the banner on their next login even if the email never arrives. Audit Event row `disqualification_notification_failed` written with `failure_reason`. Regression test: injected Loops.so 500 for 2h; assert disqualification record state unchanged, DLQ row present, banner visible to vendor.

**FM3 — Bridge event dispatch fails (bridge apply worker dead or bridge schema drift).** Mitigation: §4.7.1 Console Bridge Event retry curve + DLQ; `console_bridge_event_firewall_violation` or `other_transient` labeling; Ops alert. The Bid Workspace status transition on the seller side is consequently delayed until the bridge catches up. Seller-side banner renders as soon as the bridge event applies; until then, the seller sees their Bid Workspace as `active` with stale status. Mitigation: a 10-second SLO on bridge apply per §25.4 AC #4 and §25.2.1 bounded-lag SLO; breach emits `console_bridge_event_slo_breached`. Worst-case: seller can submit a response to an effectively-closed Bid Workspace for up to 30 seconds; server-side write still accepts the response (bridge is eventually consistent), but the response is immediately locked on apply. No firewall leak; no semantic corruption. Regression test: bridge apply paused for 60s, disqualification fired, seller submits response in the paused window; assert response ultimately `locked` with `lock_reason = disqualification_cascade`.

**FM4 — Audit-chain break (row inserted out-of-order due to clock skew between Convex replicas).** Mitigation: audit-chain integrity job runs nightly (§25.3.5); mismatch → `audit_chain_break_detected` Ops alert; Ops forensics tool reconstructs from Convex-native write timestamps. No mutation is blocked by the chain check — the chain is a detection surface, not a commit gate. Regression test: synthesized clock skew of 5 minutes; assert all rows land with monotonically increasing `related_audit_chain_hash` via Convex's coordinator-assigned timestamp.

**FM5 — Workspace Owner disqualifies the same vendor via two different Workspaces of the same Org seconds apart.** Mitigation: `VendorDisqualificationRecord(buyer_workspace_id, seller_org_id)` unique is scoped per-workspace, so both writes succeed independently with different record ids. This is correct behavior — a vendor can be disqualified from multiple simultaneous evaluations of the same Org. Both rows fire `vendor.disqualified` webhooks with distinct `disqualification_id`. No semantic error. Regression test: two disqualifications within 1 second across workspaces; assert two records, two webhooks, two audit trails.

**FM6 — Vendor's Bid Workspace is in `submitted` state and the buyer disqualifies post-Phase-9.** Mitigation: response-lock cascade is a no-op (rows already `locked` from Phase 9); scoring-exclusion cascade proceeds; banner and notification fire normally. Phase-12 disqualification is forbidden at API level by the `workspace_phase_out_of_range_for_disqualification` check; post-Phase-12 requires the Emergency Ops path per §4.7.2 FM #2. Regression test: disqualification at Phase 10; assert cascade succeeds, scoring excludes vendor, Selection Report draft annotates vendor as disqualified.

**FM7 — Seller Org deleted mid-disqualification (Org hard-delete in flight at disqualification time).** Mitigation: `VendorDisqualificationRecord` record is still written (audit integrity); vendor notification Loops.so send returns `recipient_suppressed`; `notification_sent_at` remains null; `disqualification.notification_failed` webhook fires with `failure_reason = seller_org_deleted`; banner is never viewable by the vendor because the Org no longer has active sessions. Appeal workflow is disabled (`appeal_status = not_offered` due to seller_org_deleted per §4.7.2 FM #4). Regression test: Org deletion in progress, disqualification submitted; assert record written, webhook fires, no banner leakage, audit trail complete.

**FM8 — Rationale contains sensitive buyer-internal content (e.g., includes a verbatim excerpt of an Internal Comment disparaging the vendor).** Mitigation: `rationale_internal` is buyer-private; firewall-isolated from all seller-facing surfaces; `redaction_verification_hash` on the Console Bridge Event (§4.7.1) ensures `rationale_internal` never crosses. Secondary mitigation: a `rationale_content_linter` runs at POST-time and flags rationales that quote Internal Comments verbatim (fuzzy match against live Internal Comment index); soft warning only (non-blocking) — "Your rationale appears to quote an internal comment; are you sure you want to store this verbatim?" — UX nudge, not a rejection, to preserve Workspace Owner discretion. Regression test: verbatim quote detected; nudge rendered; submission proceeds on user confirmation.

### 25.3.13 Acceptance Criteria {#25.3.13-acceptance-criteria}

1. `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/vendors/{vendor_id}/disqualify` invoked with a valid body by a `workspace_owner` / `workspace_admin` / `use_case_lead` MUST succeed in ≤ 500 ms p95 for the synchronous cascade phase (§42.1 API latency SLO band `auth_standard_mutation`). The 10-second full-cascade completion SLO (§25.4 AC #4) applies to `cascade_status = complete`.
2. The endpoint MUST enforce role-scope per §25.3.9 RBAC. A `reviewer`-only user MUST receive HTTP 403 `vendor_disqualification_role_forbidden`; a `use_case_lead` whose led Use Cases do NOT intersect the target Target Account MUST receive the same. Integration test matrix over all workspace-role × target-account combinations.
3. Duplicate-submit protection MUST be enforced via `Idempotency-Key` and the `VendorDisqualificationRecord(buyer_workspace_id, seller_org_id)` unique partial index. Re-POST with the same key and body MUST return HTTP 200 + `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`. Re-POST with the same key and different body MUST return HTTP 409 `idempotency_key_request_mismatch`. A DIFFERENT key against an already-disqualified vendor MUST return HTTP 409 `vendor_already_disqualified` with `error.details.existing_disqualification_id` populated. Property test.
4. Target Account status transitions MUST be atomic with Bid Workspace status transitions and Audit Event write — single Convex mutation or transactionally-equivalent path. A power-loss at the Convex leader during the cascade MUST NOT leave the system in a partially-committed state (Target Account `disqualified` but Bid Workspace `active`, or vice versa). Property test with injected crash at 10 different points in the cascade.
5. Response bulk-lock MUST complete within the 10-second cascade SLO (§25.4 AC #4); rows lock with `lock_reason = disqualification_cascade` (distinct from the Phase-9 lock reason). Integration test with 500-response Bid Workspace.
6. Console Bridge Event of kind `disqualification_issued` MUST be emitted within the 30-second bridge SLO (§25.4 AC #5); MUST NOT carry `rationale_internal`, `rationale_author_user_id`, or `audit_chain_hash`. QA test `vendor_disqualification_bridge_firewall` asserts redaction verification hash integrity.
7. Vendor notification dispatch MUST complete within 60 seconds of disqualification commit per §4.7.2 AC #3. Dispatch failure retries per the §41 Loops.so non-webhook `transactional_email` policy; DLQ after 5 failures with `disqualification.notification_failed` webhook and Ops alert. Synthetic trip test of Loops.so 500 for 2h; assert retry behavior, webhook, Ops alert.
8. Vendor-side banner MUST render on first Bid Workspace page load after disqualification, within 2s of first-byte per §3.6 render SLO. The banner content MUST match §25.3.8 copy verbatim for the `neutral_no_rationale` path. Integration test + visual regression test.
9. Buyer-side Disqualified lane MUST render in Vendor Curation, Bid Tracker, and Scoring Matrix surfaces per §25.3.7. Integration test matrix covering empty state, single-vendor, 20-vendor cases.
10. `vendor.disqualified` webhook MUST fire on `cascade_status → complete` with the buyer-Org projection; a parallel seller-Org projection MUST be pre-redacted per §25.3.10. HMAC-SHA256 signing MUST verify per §31. Dedup on `event_id` MUST hold across the §31.6 retry curve. Integration test with buyer and seller Org endpoints.
11. Disqualified Bid Workspace MUST return HTTP 423 `bid_workspace_readonly_disqualified` on any mutating seller-side API call. QA test matrix covering every mutating seller-side endpoint.
12. Managed Agent sessions targeting a disqualified Bid Workspace MUST transition to `terminated` with `termination_reason = bid_workspace_disqualified` within 30 seconds of disqualification. Sub-call billing per §4.8.1 partial-settlement rules. Integration test with in-flight First-Pass session.
13. Audit Event hash-chain MUST be monotonic per disqualification record; integrity scan job MUST run nightly and raise `audit_chain_break_detected` on any mismatch. Property test with synthesized out-of-order inserts.
14. Reversal within 72 hours MUST fully reverse the cascade within 10 seconds (§4.7.2 AC #7) and MUST emit `vendor.disqualification.reversed` webhook with `reversed_at` and `reversal_reason`. The reversal cascade MUST restore Target Account, Bid Workspace, and Response states to their pre-disqualification values (responses locked from Phase 9 independent of disqualification remain locked). Integration test.
15. PostHog events MUST emit per §25.3.11 with the specified properties; CI gate `posthog_disqualification_event_coverage` asserts all ten events register in Appendix G.
16. Plan gating: disqualification is available on every plan tier (Free, Growth, Scale, Enterprise). §5.11 Feature Access Matrix MUST explicitly list Disqualification under "Core Workflows — All Tiers" in this pass. No AIOperation is billed for the disqualification workflow (no AI is invoked in the cascade).
17. Residency: all writes honor the parent Workspace's `data_residency_region`. Bridge events, audit events, webhook payloads route through the residency-appropriate PostHog project and S3 region per §51.7.3. Cross-residency leakage MUST be impossible; deploy-time integration test.
18. DSAR compatibility: `rationale_internal`, `disqualification_note`, and `actor_id` are field-level redactable per §6.8. The disqualification record itself is retained for the §4.7.2 Retention window (Workspace life + 7 years) for audit integrity. DSAR deliverable MUST include the subject user's disqualification actions (as disqualifier OR as disqualified-party contact) with `rationale_internal` pseudonymized.
19. Workspace phase constraints: disqualification is accepted in phases 3 through 11 inclusive; phases 1, 2, 12, 13 return HTTP 422 `workspace_phase_out_of_range_for_disqualification`. Post-Phase-12 disqualification routes to the Emergency Ops path per §4.7.2 FM #2.
20. Webhook registration: `vendor.disqualified`, `vendor.disqualification.reversed`, `disqualification.cascade_partial_failure`, and `disqualification.notification_failed` MUST all be registered in Appendix C (Notification Event Catalog — disqualification-domain subsection) and Appendix G (PostHog Event Taxonomy) in this pass. CI gate `disqualification_webhook_registration_completeness` asserts.

### 25.3.14 Self-Challenge Pass {#25.3.14-self-challenge-pass}

Re-read as a hostile staff engineer attempting to break the spec.

- **Production code review.** The POST endpoint, the state-machine transitions, the cascade ordering, the idempotency contract, and the audit-chain are all unambiguous. The multi-write cascade is defined at the transaction granularity (Convex mutation); a junior engineer can implement. Engineering sign-off: pass.
- **QA acceptance.** Every AC in §25.3.13 is observable, measurable, and has a specified test kind (integration test, property test, regression test, CI gate, visual regression test). The test matrix for role-scope (#2) and mutating-endpoint write-guards (#11) is large but tractable. QA sign-off: pass.
- **Junior engineer buildability.** The data-model truth lives in §4.7.2, referenced explicitly. The API contract is fully spec'd (headers, body, response, errors, idempotency). State-machine transitions are in tabular form. UX copy is verbatim. A junior backend engineer can build the POST handler, the cascade worker, the reversal worker, and the webhook dispatch without ambiguity. A junior frontend engineer can build the banner, the disqualified lane, the scoring-matrix badge, and the 72h-reverse affordance. Engineering mentor sign-off: pass.
- **Security review.** Firewall isolation is explicit at four layers (bridge event redaction, seller-projection webhook payload, rationale never in any seller-visible surface, audit-chain redacted on cross-console reads); RBAC is enforced at the endpoint and in Convex; DSAR is field-level; HMAC-SHA256 on webhooks; idempotency protects against replay. Security sign-off: pass.
- **Privacy review.** `rationale_internal` never crosses firewall; `rationale_hash` is an opaque integrity signal; vendor notification style is buyer-elected with Ops gating on rationale sharing; DSAR honored; residency-locked dispatch. Privacy sign-off: pass.
- **Legal review.** Disqualification is a buyer's contractual right (evaluation is by invitation); vendor is not legally entitled to a reason in the neutral path. The `rationale_shared_with_vendor` style requires Ops approval to protect against defamation exposure. Forbidden-phrase blocklist (reviewed quarterly) is a belt-and-suspenders control. Legal sign-off: pass, contingent on Counsel confirmation that "closed" is the correct phrasing (not "terminated" — the vendor-Sourcera contract is unaffected).
- **Ops review.** Cascade failures, notification failures, bridge failures, and audit-chain breaks all have Ops alert paths. Ops has a reversal override beyond the 72h buyer window. Ops has access to the Vendor Disqualification Record's full field set. §50 Cross-Workspace Bridge Dashboard renders the freeze gauge and DLQ state. Ops sign-off: pass.
- **Product review.** The UX is neutral — disqualification is a workflow event, not a punitive one. The vendor experience preserves their content (read-only) and never discloses rationale unless the buyer explicitly opts in. The buyer experience consolidates disqualification context in a dedicated lane rather than bleeding into active views. The 72h reversal window balances correction-of-mistakes against finality-of-commitment. Product sign-off: pass.

**Known weakness caught in self-challenge — the scoring-matrix inclusion edge case.** §25.3.1 step 7 states "Vendor excluded from Scoring phase" — but the scoring phase may already be in flight with cell-level drafts. Resolution: §25.3.7 concurrency handling (HTTP 409 `scoring_cell_vendor_disqualified_concurrent`) addresses in-flight draft submission; committed scoring cells remain in the historical record for audit and Selection Report integrity (per §4.7.2 AC #12 the historical report is not rewritten). The scoring matrix visually marks the vendor with the red "Disqualified" badge, and sort/filter treats the vendor as excluded. No change required; the semantics are authored.

**Known weakness caught in self-challenge — the vendor seeing "Bid Workspace closed" without any context when the `notification_body_to_vendor` is blank.** Resolution: the banner copy (§25.3.8) renders `buyer_note_cta` conditionally; when the body is the default neutral copy, the CTA text reads "Read the buyer's note →" but the pop-open renders the standard closure sentence — no blank state. For `silent_no_vendor_notification`, the vendor sees no email; the banner still renders (a Bid Workspace that is `disqualified` is structurally closed regardless of notification style) — this is a design choice: the vendor MUST know the Bid Workspace is closed, even when Ops has suppressed the narrative notification. Documented as Authored Extension — the silent path still renders a banner, because not doing so would present a stale, clickable but non-functional UI to the seller.

**Known weakness caught in self-challenge — the 72h reversal creating a "flicker" experience for the vendor who was briefly disqualified and then restored.** Resolution: §25.3.8 reversal banner copy ("This Bid Workspace is open again. The buyer has reversed the earlier closure on {reversed_at}. You can resume your work.") explicitly acknowledges the reversal and frames it as a positive restoration. PostHog emits `vendor_disqualified` AND `vendor_disqualification_reversed` both; analysts can reconstruct the full flicker. No content loss (seller's in-flight drafts are preserved 24h per Summary §6.11). Product sign-off: accept the flicker; it is a legitimate workflow.
