## 25.4 Acceptance Criteria {#25.4-acceptance-criteria}

1. Cross-console sync latency MUST respect the bounded-lag SLO: `synced_at - created_at ≤ 30,000 ms` for ≥ 99% of Events that terminate in `synced`, measured over a rolling 15-minute window per event kind. Breach rate > 1% MUST page Ops per §25.6.2.
2. No buyer-internal data (scores, internal comments, rubrics, scenarios, selection-report drafts, intelligence briefs, Target Account list membership beyond the target seller itself, user-identity PII) crosses the bridge — enforced by unit tests on every bridge mutation AND by the defense-in-depth seller-side projection (`console_bridge_seller_projection_defense_in_depth` per §4.7.1).
3. Every event kind has a per-kind CARRIED / NEVER CARRIED entry in §4.7.1 and a matching row in §25.1.2. Adding a new event kind without updating both tables MUST fail CI (`bridge_redaction_table_completeness` check).
4. Disqualification cascade (status update, response lock, vendor notification, scoring exclusion) MUST complete within the severity-tiered SLO published in §4.7.2 AC #4 (`severity=soft` ≤ 10 seconds; `severity ∈ {account_level, global_ban}` ≤ 60 seconds — fan-out across N workspaces in account-level / global-ban cases requires the larger budget). Completion observable via `disqualification_cascade_status=complete`. (D-6.1-018 remediation 2026-05-06: AC reconciled with §4.7.2 AC #4 severity-tiered SLO; the prior flat 10-second cap was unmeetable for account_level fan-out.)
5. Amendment diff MUST be computed, redacted, and displayed in the seller's Bid Workspace within the 30-second SLO.
6. The daily reconciliation job MUST detect and re-sync failed entries with > 95% accuracy, MUST emit Appendix C `console_bridge.reconciliation_summary` per run, and a missed run MUST page Ops within 2 hours (06:00 UTC heartbeat check).
7. Persistent sync failures (> 24h) MUST trigger buyer-side and seller-side email notifications per §25.2.5, each deduped to at most one email per 24h per Workspace / Bid Workspace.
8. The Buyer "Bridge Health" panel MUST render `pending`, `retrying`, `failed`, `dlq`, `superseded` counts and per-event detail within 2 seconds of panel open, and MUST update reactively within 2 seconds of any relevant `sync_status` change (§44.1 dashboard SLO).
9. The Seller "Sync Health" panel MUST render redacted failure detail only (`failure_note` hidden; internal failure reasons remapped to `other_permanent`) and MUST update reactively within 2 seconds.
10. Ops Cross-Workspace Bridge Dashboard MUST render full fidelity (un-redacted `failure_note`, full failure-reason values, DLQ depth time-series, per-kind breach rate, per-residency breakdown).
11. Ops manual re-drive of a DLQ event MUST require an Ops note ≥ 20 chars (per §4.7.1 AC-9), MUST log `console_bridge_event_redriven` audit action with Ops user id, timestamp, and note body, and MUST reject with `console_bridge_event_cannot_redrive_disqualified` (HTTP 409) if the target is a disqualified Bid Workspace.
12. The Materialization Protocol (§25.5) MUST produce a Bid Response row for every new `requirement_created` event targeting a Bid Workspace in `accepted` state within the 30-second SLO, and MUST update the Bid Response row atomically on every `requirement_amended`, `requirement_reverted`, or `requirement_locked` event.
13. Observability metrics (§25.6) MUST be emitted as OTel spans and mirrored to PostHog per Appendix G; missing metrics MUST fail `console_bridge_observability_completeness` CI gate.
14. Client-cache DSAR flush for Console Bridge Event payloads MUST complete within the §40.2 72-hour target per §4.7.1 Phase 1.5 authored extension.

## 25.5 Materialization Protocol (Buyer Requirement → Seller Bid Response) {#25.5-materialization-protocol}

**Authoring Intent.** §25.5 names the adapter layer that translates buyer-side Requirement lifecycle events into seller-side Bid Response state changes without leaking scores, internal comments, or vendor-list membership. Today the bridge emits firewall-compliant events (§4.7.1) and the seller Bid Workspace renders them (§9 / §23) — but the materialization itself (create / update / lock / revert the Bid Response row keyed on `requirement_id`) was implicit. §25.5 makes it explicit, versioned, and testable.

### 25.5.1 Protocol Scope

Materialization is the server-side, idempotent transformation that applies a Console Bridge Event of kind `requirement_created`, `requirement_amended`, `requirement_reverted`, `requirement_locked`, or `use_case_structure_changed` to the target Bid Workspace as a create/update/lock of the corresponding Bid Response row (§4.4.2) and any dependent seller-side rows. Materialization runs in the apply-handler of the Console Bridge Event state machine — the same handler that transitions the Event from `pending` → `synced`. Materialization failure is a bridge failure: it increments `retry_count`, sets `failure_reason`, and triggers the retry curve per §25.2.2.

### 25.5.2 Target State Per Event Kind

| Event Kind | Seller-Side Target | Behavior on First Application | Behavior on Re-Application (Retry / Supersede) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `requirement_created` | Create Bid Response row | INSERT: `bid_workspace_id`, `requirement_id`, `question_text = requirement.title || requirement.description` (per §4.4.2 mapping), `answer_text = ""`, `answer_type` derived from `response_type` per §25.5.3, `status = draft`, `display_order = requirement.order`, `created_by = system_actor_id`. Emit `seller.bid_response.materialized` event (Appendix G). | Idempotent via `(bid_workspace_id, requirement_id)` unique constraint — return existing row. |
| `requirement_amended` | UPDATE Bid Response row | UPDATE: `question_text`, `display_order`, `answer_type` (if `response_type` changed). Preserve `answer_text`, `attachment_ids`, `status` IF `status = draft`. If `status = submitted`, mark `needs_reverification = true` (new field; see §25.5.4) and emit `seller.bid_response.amendment_needs_reverification` (Appendix C). Emit `seller.bid_response.amendment_applied`. | Idempotent via `(bid_workspace_id, requirement_id, source_entity_version)` — apply only if stored version < incoming version; otherwise no-op. |
| `requirement_reverted` | UPDATE Bid Response row | UPDATE: `question_text`, `display_order`, `answer_type` to the revert-target version. If the seller's submitted response was against a version between the revert-target and current, mark `needs_reverification = true`. Emit `seller.bid_response.reverted`. | Idempotent by target-version check. |
| `requirement_locked` | UPDATE Bid Response row | UPDATE: set `response_lock = true` with `lock_reason_public` populated from event payload. No further seller edits allowed (handled by §9 / §23 write-guard). Emit `seller.bid_response.locked`. | Idempotent — second application is a no-op. |
| `use_case_structure_changed` | UPDATE affected Bid Response rows | UPDATE: `display_order` for every Bid Response whose `requirement_id ∈ affected_requirement_ids`. Use Case grouping in the seller UI (§9) rerenders from the new `included_requirement_ids` list. | Idempotent — uses incoming `source_entity_version` to detect already-applied state. |
| `workspace_canceled` | No Bid Response row change; Bid Workspace state transitions | Propagate through §10.14 cancellation lifecycle on the seller side (Bid Workspace `status = withdrawn_by_buyer`). | Idempotent. |

**Mapping `response_type` → `answer_type`.** The buyer-side Requirement `response_type` enum maps to the seller-side Bid Response `answer_type` enum per the following table (codified in a shared TypeScript `mapResponseTypeToAnswerType` utility; registered in Appendix J under `requirement_response_type_to_bid_answer_type_map`):

| Buyer `response_type` | Seller `answer_type` | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `yes_no` | `text` | Seller renders as yes/no radio; stored as text "yes" / "no" |
| `short_text` | `text` | |
| `long_text` | `text` | Seller UI applies character-cap hint from Requirement |
| `numeric` | `text` | Seller UI applies numeric validation; stored as normalized text |
| `currency` | `text` | Stored with currency code; normalization per §15.2 |
| `date` | `text` | ISO-8601; validated |
| `file_upload` | `document` | Attachment ids captured in `attachment_ids` |
| `video_link` | `video_url` | URL validation per §39 |
| `demo_link` | `demo_link` | URL validation per §39 |
| `multi_select` | `text` | Stored as JSON-encoded array of selected option ids |
| `single_select` | `text` | Stored as option id |

### 25.5.3 Firewall Invariants in Materialization

The materialization handler MUST NOT read any buyer-side entity beyond the Console Bridge Event payload — it is strictly a function of `(existing Bid Response state, Console Bridge Event payload)`. Specifically:

1. The handler MUST NOT query buyer Scorecards, Rubrics, Scenarios, Selection Reports, Intelligence Briefs, Internal Comments, or Workspace Analytics — even for a "consistency check." Any such query is a firewall breach.
2. The handler MUST NOT query Target Account membership or any field that could reveal vendor-list composition. The handler knows only the one target Bid Workspace it is writing to.
3. The handler MUST NOT emit any seller-bound telemetry that embeds buyer-internal content. Emitted events in this section are pre-redacted by design.
4. The handler MUST NOT write to any buyer-side entity. Materialization is one-way (buyer → seller); any buyer-side state change on failure is carried by the Console Bridge Event row itself (via `sync_status` / `failure_reason`).
5. The handler's logging MUST redact `question_text` bodies beyond 256 chars in production logs to avoid inadvertent leakage via log aggregation pipelines (buyer-internal content is already excluded by §4.7.1 redaction; this is defense-in-depth).

### 25.5.4 New Bid Response Field — `needs_reverification`

The Materialization Protocol introduces a new boolean field on Bid Response:

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `needs_reverification` | Boolean | Default `false` | Set `true` by materialization when an amendment or revert changes a Requirement after the seller has `submitted` a response against the prior version. The seller UI surfaces a "Buyer changed this requirement — review and resubmit" CTA per §9 / §23. Cleared to `false` when the seller re-submits. |
| `reverification_reason` | Enum | Nullable; `requirement_amended`, `requirement_reverted` | Populated when `needs_reverification = true`. |
| `reverification_source_version` | Integer | Nullable; ≥ 1 | The Requirement version that triggered the reverification flag. |

Added to §4.4.2 in this same pass. Size constraints registered in §39. Retention follows the Bid Response row retention policy (Workspace life + 7 years per §40.2). Residency follows the Bid Workspace residency region.

### 25.5.5 Conflict Handling During Materialization

**Rapid successive amendments on the same Requirement.** The Console Bridge Event state machine's `superseded` transition (§4.7.1) ensures that only the newest event is applied. Materialization compares the Event's `source_entity_version` to the Bid Response's stored `reverification_source_version` (and a new `last_applied_source_version` tracking field — authored here, registered in §4.4.2) and applies only if the incoming version is strictly greater. Older events still in `pending`/`retrying` transition to `superseded` with `superseded_by_event_id` set.

**Revert to a version earlier than the seller's submission.** If the Requirement reverts to version V and the seller submitted a response against version V+N (N≥1), the Bid Response is marked `needs_reverification = true` with `reverification_reason = requirement_reverted` and `reverification_source_version = V`. The seller's prior submitted content is preserved and editable.

**Amendment on a locked Requirement.** Cannot happen — buyer cannot amend a locked Requirement (§4.3.3 state machine). A `requirement_amended` event targeting a locked Requirement is rejected with `console_bridge_event_invalid_transition` (HTTP 409) at write time.

**Use Case structure change after seller submission.** `display_order` updates only; seller's submitted responses remain; `needs_reverification` is NOT set (structural reordering is non-semantic). Emit `seller.bid_response.use_case_structure_changed` purely as a UX hint.

### 25.5.6 Failure Modes Addressed

1. **Bid Workspace in `disqualified` state at materialization time.** Apply handler rejects with `failure_reason=target_bid_workspace_disqualified`; Console Bridge Event transitions to `failed`.
2. **Requirement payload exceeds 256 KB.** Rejected at bridge emit time (§4.7.1 Failure Mode #3); never reaches materialization.
3. **Seller-side DB write conflict (Convex optimistic-concurrency retry exhausted).** `failure_reason=other_transient`; retry curve applies.
4. **Seller's Bid Response row already has `response_lock=true` from a prior `requirement_locked` event AND a `requirement_amended` arrives.** Invalid buyer-side transition; the event should not exist. If received, apply handler rejects with `failure_reason=schema_mismatch`; fires SIM alert (Signal Integrity Monitor per §50.17).
5. **`requirement_created` arrives but the Bid Workspace does not yet exist** (race between Target Account acceptance and bridge emission). Apply handler defers with `failure_reason=other_transient`; the retry curve's next attempt will find the Bid Workspace present (it should be created within single-digit seconds of acceptance).
6. **Partial Use Case structure change (incoming `included_requirement_ids` does not include a Requirement that IS in the current seller view).** Handler computes the diff and soft-deletes the orphaned Bid Response rows (move to `status=archived_by_buyer_remove`, new enum value; see §25.5.8). Seller retains read-access for audit per §9.
7. **Residency mismatch between buyer region and seller Bid Workspace region.** Bridge emission respects residency (§4.7.1 Residency block); materialization is a no-op for any Event routed to a wrong-region Bid Workspace (should be impossible post-§4.7.1 but defensive). Alerts SIM.
8. **Materialization succeeds but emits no `seller.bid_response.materialized` event.** CI-gated: every materialization code path MUST emit the corresponding PostHog event. This check is a named sub-check of the `console_bridge_observability_completeness` CI gate (§25.6.5 #4) — the single gate is the canonical enforcement point, and the per-check label surfaces in CI output as `console_bridge_observability_completeness → materialization_event_emission`. A missing emission fails the consolidated gate with the sub-check label populated for debugging. There is no standalone `materialization_event_completeness` gate; the per-check label is retained for log-grep convenience only. (Earlier drafts referenced both names — the consolidated single-gate shape is the authoritative v7.0.0 resolution per RECONCILIATION.md → §25.5.6/§25.6.5 CI Gate Consolidation.)

### 25.5.7 Observability Surface for Materialization

Materialization emits the following OTel spans (consumed by §25.6):

- `bridge.materialize.apply` — one span per Event apply attempt. Attributes: `event_id`, `event_kind`, `bid_workspace_id`, `requirement_id`, `source_entity_version`, `last_applied_source_version`, `outcome ∈ {applied, noop_superseded, noop_already_applied, failed}`.
- `bridge.materialize.bid_response_write` — child span per DB write. Attributes: `bid_response_id`, `operation ∈ {insert, update, lock}`, `needs_reverification_set ∈ {true, false}`.

PostHog events emitted: `seller.bid_response.materialized`, `seller.bid_response.amendment_applied`, `seller.bid_response.amendment_needs_reverification`, `seller.bid_response.reverted`, `seller.bid_response.locked`, `seller.bid_response.use_case_structure_changed`, `seller.bid_response.archived_by_buyer_remove`. All events carry standardized properties per Appendix G preamble (`org_id`, `console=seller`, `bid_workspace_id`, `bid_response_id`, `requirement_id`, `event_kind`, `source_entity_version`).

### 25.5.8 Enum & Error-Code Additions

- Appendix J `bid_response_status` — add `archived_by_buyer_remove` (new) alongside existing `draft`, `submitted`, `acknowledged`.
- Appendix J `bid_response_reverification_reason` — new enum: `requirement_amended`, `requirement_reverted`.
- Appendix I — add `console_bridge_event_invalid_transition` (HTTP 409), `console_bridge_materialization_schema_mismatch` (HTTP 422), `console_bridge_materialization_residency_mismatch` (HTTP 422; SIM-escalated).

### 25.5.9 Authoring Hand-Offs

§9 (Seller Bid Workspace) references §25.5 for the "Buyer changed this requirement" surface and the `needs_reverification` CTA copy.
§23 (First-Pass Responder) must re-trigger on `needs_reverification=true` if the seller opts to re-draft.
§4.4.2 Bid Response entity is updated in this same pass to add `needs_reverification`, `reverification_reason`, `reverification_source_version`, `last_applied_source_version`, `response_lock`, `lock_reason_public`.
§39 Object Size Constraints gains four rows for the new Bid Response fields.
Appendix C gains `seller.bid_response.amendment_needs_reverification` webhook event.
Appendix G gains the seven PostHog events enumerated in §25.5.7.

### 25.5.10 Acceptance Criteria {#25.5.10-materialization-protocol-acceptance-criteria}

#### 25.5.10.1 Idempotency & Versioning

- [ ] Re-applying a Console Bridge Event with `source_entity_version ≤ bid_response.last_applied_source_version` is a no-op; the apply handler returns `outcome = noop_already_applied` and emits no duplicate side effects.
- [ ] Re-applying a `superseded` event MUST NOT mutate the Bid Response row; outcome `noop_superseded` is recorded.
- [ ] Replaying a successful materialization 10× over a 60-second window MUST produce byte-identical Bid Response state at each replay (CI gate `materialization_idempotency_replay`).
- [ ] The `(bid_workspace_id, requirement_id)` unique constraint prevents duplicate Bid Response row creation under concurrent `requirement_created` deliveries.

#### 25.5.10.2 Firewall Invariants

- [ ] CI gate `materialization_firewall` asserts the apply handler's read set is restricted to `{ConsoleBridgeEvent, BidResponse, BidWorkspace}`; any read of buyer-side Scorecard, Rubric, Scenario, Selection Report, Internal Comment, or Workspace Analytics tables fails the gate.
- [ ] CI gate `materialization_firewall` asserts the apply handler's write set is restricted to `{BidResponse, ConsoleBridgeEvent (sync_status only)}`; writes to any buyer-side entity fail the gate.
- [ ] PostHog events emitted by materialization MUST NOT carry buyer-internal payload fields (`buyer_internal_comment_*`, `buyer_score_*`, `buyer_rubric_*`); a deploy-time `event_payload_firewall_lint` validator asserts.
- [ ] Production logs MUST redact `question_text` bodies beyond 256 chars; CI gate `materialization_log_redaction_lint` asserts on the log-emit code paths.

#### 25.5.10.3 Re-Verification Field

- [ ] On `requirement_amended` event for a Bid Response with `status = submitted`, materialization MUST set `needs_reverification = true`, `reverification_reason = requirement_amended`, `reverification_source_version = incoming_event.source_entity_version`.
- [ ] `needs_reverification` clears to `false` only on a fresh seller submission against the new Requirement version.
- [ ] Seller UI MUST surface a "Buyer changed this requirement — review and resubmit" CTA when `needs_reverification = true`; CTA absence on a flagged response is a §38 conformance failure.

#### 25.5.10.4 Conflict & Failure Handling

- [ ] Bid Workspace in `disqualified` state at materialization time MUST cause the bridge event to transition to `failed` with `failure_reason = target_bid_workspace_disqualified`; no Bid Response state change occurs.
- [ ] Materialization writes that fail Convex optimistic-concurrency retry exhaustion MUST set `failure_reason = other_transient` and follow the §25.2 retry curve.
- [ ] `requirement_amended` event arriving for a Bid Response with `response_lock = true` returns `failure_reason = schema_mismatch` and triggers a Signal Integrity Monitor alert (§50.17) within 60 seconds.
- [ ] `use_case_structure_changed` events that orphan Bid Response rows MUST soft-delete via `status = archived_by_buyer_remove`; orphaned rows remain queryable in audit views.

#### 25.5.10.5 Enums, Errors, and Catalog Registration

- [ ] Appendix J registers `bid_response_status.archived_by_buyer_remove` and the `bid_response_reverification_reason` enum; CI gate `appendix_j_enum_completeness` asserts.
- [ ] Appendix I registers `console_bridge_event_invalid_transition` (HTTP 409), `console_bridge_materialization_schema_mismatch` (HTTP 422), and `console_bridge_materialization_residency_mismatch` (HTTP 422).
- [ ] Appendix C catalog entry for `seller.bid_response.amendment_needs_reverification` is present with HMAC signing, idempotency via `event_id`, exponential backoff, and DLQ-after-5-failures semantics per §31.
- [ ] Appendix G PostHog taxonomy registers the seven events from §25.5.7 with complete property schemas; CI gate `posthog_taxonomy_completeness` asserts.

#### 25.5.10.6 Observability Coupling

- [ ] Every materialization apply attempt MUST emit a `bridge.materialize.apply` OTel span with attributes per §25.5.7.
- [ ] Every successful Bid Response write MUST emit a `bridge.materialize.bid_response_write` child span; missing spans fail the consolidated `console_bridge_observability_completeness` CI gate (§25.6.5 #4) with sub-check label `materialization_event_emission`.

## 25.6 Console Bridge Observability {#25.6-console-bridge-observability}

**Authoring Intent.** §25.6 makes the operational picture of the Console Bridge concrete: what metrics are emitted, what the alert thresholds are, who pages, and where the on-call runbook lives. Product, design, support, and Ops read §25.6. Engineering implements against §25.6.1 (metrics) and §25.6.2 (alerts). §25.6 composes with §42 Observability, §50 Ops Console, and §51 Product Usage Analytics — it is the Bridge-specific subset.

### 25.6.1 Metrics Catalog

Every metric below is emitted from the bridge emit handler, the bridge apply handler, and the daily reconciliation job. Metrics are OTel-instrumented; counter metrics mirror to PostHog per Appendix G; gauge metrics surface in the Ops Cross-Workspace Bridge Dashboard (§50).

| Metric | Type | Labels | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `bridge.event.emitted.count` | Counter | `event_kind`, `direction`, `buyer_org_id`, `seller_org_id`, `residency_region` | Count of Console Bridge Events written (post-redaction-validation). |
| `bridge.event.applied.count` | Counter | `event_kind`, `outcome ∈ {synced, failed, dlq}`, `residency_region` | Count of apply outcomes. |
| `bridge.event.retry.count` | Counter | `event_kind`, `attempt ∈ {2,3,4,5}`, `failure_reason` | Per-attempt retry distribution. |
| `bridge.event.bounded_lag_ms` | Histogram | `event_kind`, `residency_region` | Distribution of `synced_at - created_at` in ms. p50, p95, p99 surfaced. |
| `bridge.event.slo_breach_rate` | Gauge | `event_kind`, `residency_region`, `window=15m` | Rolling 15-min breach rate (0.0–1.0). |
| `bridge.event.dlq_depth` | Gauge | `residency_region` | Current count of `sync_status = dlq` rows platform-wide. |
| `bridge.event.firewall_violation.count` | Counter | `event_kind`, `buyer_org_id` (hashed for SIM) | Count of `console_bridge_event_firewall_violation` rejections. |
| `bridge.event.redaction_verification_fail.count` | Counter | `event_kind` | Count of `redaction_verification_hash` mismatches at write. |
| `bridge.event.superseded.count` | Counter | `event_kind` | Count of transitions to `superseded`. |
| `bridge.event.materialize.apply.count` | Counter | `event_kind`, `outcome ∈ {applied, noop_superseded, noop_already_applied, failed}` | Per §25.5.7. |
| `bridge.reconciliation.stale_count` | Gauge | `job_run_id` | Per-run stale-count emitted by the 02:00 UTC job. |
| `bridge.reconciliation.job_heartbeat` | Gauge | `job_run_id`, `ran_at` | Heartbeat for 06:00 UTC missed-run check. |
| `bridge.dashboard.render_latency_ms` | Histogram | `console ∈ {buyer, seller, ops}`, `panel` | Panel render latency; surfaces §44.1 violations. |

### 25.6.2 Alert Thresholds & On-Call Routing

| Alert | Threshold | Severity | Routing | Runbook Anchor |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| SLO breach — rolling 15m | `bridge.event.slo_breach_rate > 0.01` (>1%) on any event kind | P2 | Cross-Console on-call | §25.6.4 RB-001 |
| SLO breach — sustained 60m | `bridge.event.slo_breach_rate > 0.05` (>5%) on any event kind sustained 60m | P1 | Cross-Console on-call + Platform on-call | §25.6.4 RB-002 |
| DLQ depth | `bridge.event.dlq_depth > 100` platform-wide | P2 | Cross-Console on-call | §25.6.4 RB-003 |
| DLQ depth — sustained | `bridge.event.dlq_depth > 500` sustained 30m | P1 | Cross-Console on-call + Platform Lead | §25.6.4 RB-004 |
| Firewall violation | `bridge.event.firewall_violation.count > 0` over 5m | P1 | Cross-Console on-call + Security on-call + SIM | §25.6.4 RB-005 |
| Redaction hash mismatch | `bridge.event.redaction_verification_fail.count > 0` over 5m | P1 | Cross-Console on-call + Security on-call | §25.6.4 RB-006 |
| Reconciliation missed run | `bridge.reconciliation.job_heartbeat` absent from the 02:00 UTC run by 06:00 UTC | P1 | Cross-Console on-call | §25.6.4 RB-007 |
| Reconciliation anomaly | `bridge.reconciliation.stale_count > 1000` on a single run | P2 | Cross-Console on-call | §25.6.4 RB-008 |
| Materialization apply failure | `bridge.event.materialize.apply.count{outcome=failed}` > 10 over 5m on any event kind | P2 | Cross-Console on-call | §25.6.4 RB-009 |
| Dashboard render-latency regression | `bridge.dashboard.render_latency_ms{p95} > 2000` on any panel over 15m | P3 | Frontend Platform on-call | §25.6.4 RB-010 |

Alerts page via PagerDuty per §42.3; escalation policy follows the platform default (primary 5m → secondary 10m → manager 15m) with explicit Cross-Console on-call rotation.

### 25.6.3 Dashboards

- **Buyer Workspace Bridge Health panel** — per §25.2.3. Rendered at `/workspace/{id}/health`.
- **Seller Bid Workspace Sync Health panel** — per §25.2.3. Rendered at `/bid-workspace/{id}/health`.
- **Ops Cross-Workspace Bridge Dashboard** — per §50 (Sourcera Ops Console). Rendered at `/ops/bridge`. Surfaces every metric in §25.6.1 with 15m / 1h / 24h / 7d windows, per-kind / per-residency breakdowns, and one-click re-drive on DLQ rows (with mandatory Ops note).
- **Grafana `sourcera-bridge` board** — SRE-facing mirror of Ops Dashboard; linked from the runbook.

### 25.6.4 On-Call Runbook (Cross-Console Bridge)

**Runbook URL.** `https://runbooks.sourcera.com/cross-console-bridge` (governed by §42.5 Runbook Inventory). The runbook is versioned; every change logged with author + date per §42.5.

**Runbook anchors.** Each alert in §25.6.2 references a runbook anchor (RB-001 … RB-010). Each anchor contains: alert definition, likely root causes (3–5), initial diagnostic queries (Grafana + Convex), remediation steps, escalation criteria, post-incident follow-up template. Runbook anchors are authored and maintained by the Cross-Console on-call; initial authoring is a §25.6 deliverable.

**Kill-switch.** The Ops Console exposes a bridge-emit pause switch (§50.17) for the Cross-Console on-call. Activating the kill-switch:

- Halts new Console Bridge Event emission platform-wide (buyer-side mutations still commit locally but do not emit bridge events; emission resumes when kill-switch released).
- Pauses the retry scheduler for `pending` / `retrying` events (they stall in place; no transitions to `dlq` during pause).
- Surfaces a red banner in every Buyer Workspace and Bid Workspace: "Cross-Console sync is temporarily paused. Your updates are saved locally and will propagate once sync resumes."
- Requires an Ops note ≥ 50 chars on activation AND on release.
- Emits `ops.bridge.kill_switch_engaged` / `ops.bridge.kill_switch_released` audit actions (Appendix J).

Kill-switch use is last-resort — SIM auto-remediation, per-kind deny-lists, and DLQ drain strategies should be preferred. Sustained kill-switch engagement > 1h is an incident per §42.3 with a mandatory post-mortem per §42.8.

### 25.6.5 Completeness CI Gate

A CI gate `console_bridge_observability_completeness` asserts at build time that:

1. Every `event_kind` in the `console_bridge_event_kind` enum has a corresponding `bridge.event.emitted.count` label coverage and a `bridge.event.applied.count` label coverage.
2. Every metric in §25.6.1 is instrumented in the bridge emit handler, apply handler, or reconciliation job.
3. Every alert in §25.6.2 has a matching Grafana alert rule in `sourcera-bridge` and a runbook anchor in `https://runbooks.sourcera.com/cross-console-bridge`.
4. Every PostHog event referenced in §25.5.7 is registered in Appendix G with a complete property schema. This sub-check is the canonical enforcement point for the materialization-event-emission invariant named in §25.5.6 #8; the per-check label `materialization_event_emission` appears in CI output when the sub-check fails.
5. Every metric in §25.6.1 that is mirrored to PostHog per Appendix G has a registered Appendix-G event family with matching property schema.
6. The `bridge_service_resumed.hbs` Loops.so transactional template (§25.2.6) is registered in §41 template registry and passes the forbidden-phrase linter.

Gate failures block the PR. Gate owner: Cross-Console Platform Lead. The gate is the **only** build-time completeness check for Bridge observability — prior drafts referenced a separate `materialization_event_completeness` gate; that name is retired per RECONCILIATION.md → §25.5.6/§25.6.5 CI Gate Consolidation (2026-04-24).

### 25.6.6 Acceptance Criteria {#25.6.6-console-bridge-observability-acceptance-criteria}

#### 25.6.6.1 Metrics Coverage

- [ ] Every metric enumerated in §25.6.1 is instrumented at its named emission point (emit handler, apply handler, or reconciliation job); the `console_bridge_observability_completeness` CI gate (§25.6.5 #2) asserts at build time.
- [ ] Every `event_kind` registered in `console_bridge_event_kind` enum (Appendix J) MUST have non-zero coverage in `bridge.event.emitted.count` and `bridge.event.applied.count` over a synthetic-event load run; coverage validated by the `bridge_metrics_synthetic_load` CI test.
- [ ] Counter metrics mirroring to PostHog MUST appear in Appendix G with matching label sets; mismatches fail `console_bridge_observability_completeness` #5.

#### 25.6.6.2 Alert Routing

- [ ] Each alert in §25.6.2 has a registered Grafana alert rule under the `sourcera-bridge` board with severity, threshold, and routing matching this spec; `grafana_alert_parity` CI gate asserts.
- [ ] Alert routing to PagerDuty respects the §42.3 escalation policy (primary 5m → secondary 10m → manager 15m); a synthetic alert injection at deploy time validates routing within ≤ 30 s.
- [ ] P1 alerts (`bridge.event.firewall_violation.count > 0`, redaction hash mismatch, sustained SLO breach 60m, sustained DLQ depth) MUST page the Cross-Console on-call AND the Security on-call (firewall + redaction) within 1 minute.
- [ ] Reconciliation missed-run alert (`bridge.reconciliation.job_heartbeat` absent by 06:00 UTC) MUST page Cross-Console on-call exactly once per missed run; idempotency keyed on `(job_run_id, missed_at)`.

#### 25.6.6.3 Dashboard Behavior

- [ ] Buyer Workspace Bridge Health panel renders within p95 ≤ 2 s; missing data states fall back to the §3.7 empty-state pattern.
- [ ] Seller Bid Workspace Sync Health panel mirrors only seller-permitted projections; cross-Org data MUST NOT render even if the underlying metric carries cross-Org labels (CI gate `bridge_dashboard_firewall` asserts).
- [ ] Ops Cross-Workspace Bridge Dashboard renders 15m / 1h / 24h / 7d windows with per-kind / per-residency breakdowns; one-click DLQ re-drive MUST require an Ops note ≥ 50 chars and emit `ops.bridge.dlq_redrive` audit row.
- [ ] Grafana `sourcera-bridge` board mirrors the Ops Dashboard with read-only access for SRE; access is governed by §50.3 Ops role matrix.

#### 25.6.6.4 Runbook Anchors

- [ ] Every alert (RB-001 through RB-010) MUST resolve to a runbook anchor at `https://runbooks.sourcera.com/cross-console-bridge`; anchors MUST contain alert definition, 3–5 likely root causes, initial diagnostic queries, remediation steps, escalation criteria, and a post-incident follow-up template.
- [ ] Anchor authorship and revisions are governed by §42.5 (Runbook Inventory); each anchor edit emits a versioned audit log with `editor_id` and `change_summary`.
- [ ] CI gate `console_bridge_observability_completeness` #3 asserts every alert has a corresponding runbook anchor.

#### 25.6.6.5 Kill-Switch

- [ ] Kill-switch engagement MUST require an Ops note ≥ 50 chars on activation AND on release; releases without notes return HTTP 422 `ops_kill_switch_release_note_missing`.
- [ ] On engagement, every Buyer Workspace and Bid Workspace MUST render the red banner ("Cross-Console sync is temporarily paused...") within p95 ≤ 5 s of switch activation (Convex reactive push).
- [ ] During engagement, new Console Bridge Events MUST NOT emit (buyer-side mutations commit locally without bridge fanout); retry scheduler is paused; transitions to `dlq` MUST NOT occur.
- [ ] Engagement and release emit `ops.bridge.kill_switch_engaged` / `ops.bridge.kill_switch_released` audit actions (Appendix J ops audit catalog) with `actor_id`, `note`, and `engaged_at` / `released_at` timestamps.
- [ ] Sustained kill-switch engagement > 1 hour MUST escalate to incident-response per §42.3 with a mandatory post-mortem per §42.8.

#### 25.6.6.6 Completeness Gate Singularity

- [ ] `console_bridge_observability_completeness` is the SINGLE build-time completeness gate for Bridge observability; the deprecated `materialization_event_completeness` gate name MUST NOT be present in CI configuration (deploy-time validator `deprecated_gate_name_lint` asserts).
- [ ] Sub-check labels (e.g., `materialization_event_emission`) appear in CI output for failure debugging but do NOT register as standalone gates.

## 25.7 Internal Comments {#25.7-internal-comments}

**Purpose (Summary C.119).** §25.7 is the feature-level specification for Internal Comments — the buyer-side private collaboration surface attached to a Workspace, Use Case, Requirement, Response, Scenario, or Selection Report draft. Internal Comments are **strictly buyer-internal**: no Internal Comment Thread, Post, Mention, or attachment is ever carried across the Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2), rendered to a seller-console session, or surfaced in a vendor-visible projection via any API, webhook, export, or UI. §25.7 closes the contract: §4.3.11–§4.3.13 define the entities; §25.1.2 declares the NEVER-CARRIED bridge treatment; §25.7 specifies the surfaces, plan gating, firewall enforcement, API, webhook, DSAR, and acceptance criteria.

§25.7 is authored in §25 (Cross-Console Mechanics) rather than in a standalone feature section because the firewall integrity of Internal Comments is the primary contract the feature embodies. The buyer-facing UX chrome (thread list, composer, resolve / re-open) is rendered against components in §38 and interaction patterns in §3; §25.7 is the engineering contract that §38 and §3 implement against.

### 25.7.1 Entity Model (Cross-Reference) {#25.7.1-internal-comments-entity-model}

| Entity | Section | Role |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Internal Comment Thread | §4.3.11 | Container. Polymorphically anchored to Workspace / Use Case / Requirement / Response / Scenario / Selection Report draft via `(attached_to_type, attached_to_id)`. Carries `status`, `visibility_scope`, `subscribed_user_ids[]`, `post_count`, `last_post_at`, `plan_quota_counted`. |
| Internal Comment Post | §4.3.12 | Individual Markdown post within a thread. Carries `author_id`, `author_role_snapshot`, `body` (≤ 5,000 chars, Markdown), `attachment_ids[]`, `parent_post_id` (threaded replies), `edit_locked_at` (15-min author edit window), `deleted_placeholder`, `moderated_by`. |
| Internal Comment Mention | §4.3.13 | Normalized @-mention record (one row per mentioned user per post). Drives notification fan-out (§29) and the `has_unread_mention` flag on Unread Marker (§4.3.15). Supports `user`, `team`, `role` mention kinds with team/role expansion frozen at write time. |

Scope isolation is declared at the entity level: all three entities are workspace-scoped, buyer-console only, and enforce cross-console non-leakage via HTTP 404 (non-leak) on any seller-console read (`internal_comment_cross_console_access`, Appendix I; existing).

### 25.7.2 Attachment Surfaces {#25.7.2-internal-comments-attachment-surfaces}

An Internal Comment Thread can be anchored to any of the following entities. The attachment surface governs where buyers create and consume threads; the anchor does not change content semantics.

| Anchor | `attached_to_type` | Section | UX Surface |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Workspace | `workspace` | §4.3.1 | "Workspace Discussion" tab in the Workspace Peek / Workspace Dashboard sidebar. |
| Use Case | `use_case` | §4.3.3 | Use Case Detail header "Discussion" pill; Side Peek §3.8 inline tab. |
| Requirement | `requirement` | §4.3.4 | Requirement Matrix row inline comment chip; Requirement Detail "Discussion" tab. |
| Response | `response` | §4.3.5 | Response Detail "Internal Notes" tab (buyer-only; Response is otherwise vendor-facing data). Never leaks to vendor via §25.1.2. |
| Scenario | `scenario` | §14 | Scenario Detail "Deliberation" tab. |
| Selection Report draft | `selection_report_draft` | §10.13 | Selection Report editor "Redlines" pane. |

**Anchor validation.** Server-side write-time validation asserts `attached_to_id` resolves to an entity in the same Workspace (or in the case of Selection Report draft, to a draft whose parent Workspace matches the thread's `workspace_id`). An anchor pointing to an entity in a different Workspace rejects with HTTP 422 `internal_comment_thread_anchor_mismatch` (Appendix I, new in this pass).

**Anchor-entity archive.** When the anchor entity is archived (Workspace archive, Requirement soft-delete, Selection Report finalize), all threads attached to it cascade to `archived` per Appendix L.1. See §4.3.11 Retention and §40.2.

### 25.7.3 Thread Creation and Visibility Scope {#25.7.3-internal-comments-thread-creation-visibility}

**Create.** A Workspace Member (any role per §5.2 except a `guest_contributor` whose `assigned_use_case_ids` does not admit the anchor entity) MAY create a thread via `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/internal-comment-threads`. Required body fields: `attached_to_type`, `attached_to_id`, first `post.body` (≥ 1 char, ≤ 5,000 chars, Markdown). Optional: `title` (0–100 chars; auto-derived from first 80 chars of first post if blank), `visibility_scope` (default `buyer_workspace_members`).

**Visibility Scope Enum (`internal_comment_thread_visibility_scope`, Appendix J, new in this pass).**

| Value | Who Can Read | Who Can Write |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `buyer_workspace_members` | All Workspace Members (subject to guest `assigned_use_case_ids` scoping) | All Workspace Members per above |
| `buyer_team_leads` | `workspace_owner`, `workspace_admin`, `use_case_lead` only | Same readers |
| `private_to_author_plus_mentioned` | Author + users with an active Mention row targeting them | Same readers |

Visibility scope is **mutable** by the thread author, Workspace Owner, or Workspace Admin. Tightening the scope triggers:

- Unread Marker cleanup for now-excluded viewers (§3.12.5) with `suppressed_reason = visibility_tightened`.
- Convex reactive-subscription invalidation.
- An audit event `internal_comment_thread_visibility_tightened` per §4.6.

Loosening the scope triggers:

- Unread Marker seeding for newly-included viewers (markers start at `unread_count = <posts created before user was included>` capped at the §3.12.6 per-user marker cap; if the cap is exceeded, the surface falls back to the "99+" display semantics).
- An audit event `internal_comment_thread_visibility_loosened`.

Guest users with `assigned_use_case_ids` scoping see only threads whose `attached_to_id` resolves within their assigned Use Cases, regardless of `visibility_scope`.

### 25.7.4 Posts, Markdown, Mentions, Attachments {#25.7.4-internal-comments-posts-markdown-mentions-attachments}

**Posts.**

- Body ≤ 5,000 chars (Markdown) per §39 Internal Comment Post row.
- Rendered via the buyer-side sanitizing Markdown renderer (supports GFM tables, fenced code blocks, `@mentions`, inline task lists; strips raw HTML, `<script>`, `<iframe>`, and external image URLs from non-allowlisted domains).
- Threaded replies via `parent_post_id` — one level deep; replies-to-replies collapse to siblings (flat thread tree with a parent pointer).
- 15-minute author edit window per §4.3.12; edits record `edited_at`. Post-window edits rejected with `internal_comment_post_edit_window_expired` (Appendix I; existing).
- Author soft-delete within the edit window sets `deleted_placeholder = true`; the body renders as "Deleted by author" for readers. Hard-delete only by Workspace Owner / Admin via the moderation path; logs `moderated_by` and `moderated_reason`.

**Mentions (§4.3.13).**

- `@username`, `@TeamName`, or `@RoleName` syntax in the post body.
- On post write, the server parses mentions, expands `team` → member list and `role` → users-with-that-role snapshot, and writes one Internal Comment Mention row per resolved user.
- Mention expansion is frozen at write time; subsequent team-roster or role-grant changes do NOT retroactively notify new members (§4.3.13 author-intent-preservation rule).
- A single post carries at most 50 mentions (authored limit — new row added to §39 Object Size Constraints in this pass). Excess mentions rejected with `internal_comment_post_mention_limit_exceeded` (Appendix I, new in this pass).
- Mentions targeting guests without access to the anchor entity are skipped silently (no notification, no Mention row). Audit event `internal_comment_mention_skipped_no_access` per §4.6.

**Attachments.**

- Up to 10 files, 50 MB each, 500 MB total per post, per §39.
- Upload flow per §18.5.2: presigned S3 URL, virus scan, MIME allowlist (images, PDF, docx, xlsx, pptx, csv, txt, zip ≤ 50 MB).
- Attachments are workspace-scoped; the Attachment entity (§4.6) carries `owner_entity_type = internal_comment_post` and `org_id`; cross-console read returns HTTP 404.
- Attachment total-bytes overflow rejects with HTTP 413 `internal_comment_post_attachment_total_bytes_exceeded` (Appendix I, new in this pass).

### 25.7.5 State Machine and Resolve Semantics {#25.7.5-internal-comments-state-machine-resolve-semantics}

The Internal Comment Thread lifecycle is authoritative in **Appendix L.1**; this subsection is a pointer with feature-level context.

- **Open (initial).** New threads start `open`. Emits `internal_comment_thread.created` webhook (Appendix C — registered in this pass).
- **Resolved.** Workspace Owner, Workspace Admin, Use Case Lead (on use-case-scoped threads), or the thread author may click "Resolve". Sets `resolved_at`, `resolved_by`, `resolution_note` (optional ≤ 500 chars). Posts remain frozen except for in-edit-window author actions. Emits `internal_comment_thread.resolved`.
- **Re-opened.** Workspace Owner, Admin, or thread author may re-open a resolved thread. Clears `resolved_at`, `resolved_by`. Emits `internal_comment_thread.reopened`.
- **Archived.** Manual archive by Workspace Owner OR cascade from anchor-entity archive. Terminal absent backup restore. Emits `internal_comment_thread.archived`.

Invalid transitions return HTTP 409 `internal_comment_thread_invalid_state_transition` (Appendix I; existing).

### 25.7.6 Plan Gating and Per-Workspace Cap {#25.7.6-internal-comments-plan-gating}

| Plan Tier | Active Threads per Workspace | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Buyer Free | 25 | §34.1.1 (Authored Extension — Summary C.119 is silent on Free; 25 is chosen to enable trial usage without replicating paid-tier value) |
| Buyer Business Starter | 500 | §34.1.1 (Summary C.119) |
| Buyer Business Growth | 500 | §34.1.1 (Summary C.119) |
| Buyer Business Scale | 500 | §34.1.1 (Summary C.119) |
| Buyer Enterprise | Unlimited | §34.1.1 (Summary C.119) |

The authoritative cell is §34.1.1 (Buyer Plan Tiers) — this section cites, does not duplicate. A new row "Internal Comment Threads per Workspace" is added to §34.1.1 in this pass.

**Cap semantics.** The cap counts Internal Comment Threads with `plan_quota_counted = true` (§4.3.11). System-generated threads (for example, Ops-authored moderation notes — not yet implemented, reserved for future use) carry `plan_quota_counted = false` and are exempt. Archived threads do NOT count against the cap; only `open` + `resolved` threads count.

**Cap enforcement.**

1. Create-time: the server evaluates `COUNT(threads WHERE workspace_id = X AND plan_quota_counted = true AND status IN ('open','resolved') AND deleted_at IS NULL)` against the Org's plan tier.
2. At cap, create rejects with HTTP 402 `internal_comment_thread_workspace_cap_reached` (Appendix I, new in this pass) and surfaces the §5.11 upgrade CTA.
3. Bulk-archive of existing resolved threads is a documented self-serve mitigation; archive is free and unlimited.
4. Plan downgrade that drops a workspace below compliance (for example, Starter → Free with 200 active threads, exceeding the §34.1.1 Free-tier cap) invokes the §34.20 downgrade-excess-data pathway: the Org retains read access to all threads; new thread creation is blocked until the active count ≤ §34.1.1 cap; no threads are deleted. Surfaced via §5.11 and §34.20 grace-period semantics.

**Per-Workspace Mention Cap.** New size row in §39: a Workspace MAY accumulate at most 100,000 Internal Comment Mention rows (across all threads) before `mention_fanout_degraded` mode activates, which batches notifications into the digest cadence to protect downstream Loops.so throughput. Authored Extension — flagged in RECONCILIATION.md.

### 25.7.7 Firewall Enforcement (Cross-Console, Seller Console, Export) {#25.7.7-internal-comments-firewall-enforcement}

The Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2) is enforced at **four** layers; a single breach constitutes a P0 defect.

1. **Entity-level scope isolation.** §4.3.11–§4.3.13 carry `console = buyer` (fixed). Seller-console sessions cannot read.
2. **API authorization.** Every read endpoint (`GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/internal-comment-threads`, `GET /v1/internal-comment-threads/{id}`, `GET /v1/internal-comment-posts/{id}`, `GET /v1/internal-comment-mentions/{id}`) asserts the session's `console = buyer`; seller-console reads return HTTP 404 (non-leak) via `internal_comment_cross_console_access` (Appendix I; existing).
3. **Bridge NEVER-CARRIED.** §25.1.2 declares Internal Comment Thread / Post / Mention NEVER CARRIED across the Console Bridge. The bridge emit handler MUST NOT read these entities; a static-analysis CI gate `console_bridge_no_internal_comment_imports` asserts no bridge-handler code path imports the Internal Comment Convex modules.
4. **Export and DSAR pipelines.** Workspace JSON export includes Internal Comment Thread / Post / Mention rows only when the export initiator's session `console = buyer`. Seller-side export never includes them (the seller cannot export buyer-internal data, by construction). DSAR export of a buyer user includes the user's authored and mentioned posts; DSAR of a seller user (unrelated to buyer-internal data) does not.

**Promotion of an Internal Comment to a Vendor-Visible Q&A Post.** The ONLY legal path for internal-comment content to reach a vendor is via the `buyer_comment_visible_to_vendor` promotion event (§25.1.2 Q&A row), which creates a NEW Q&A Thread Post with buyer-authored, explicitly-redacted content; the underlying Internal Comment Post is **not copied**, **not referenced**, and **not linked** in the resulting Q&A Post. The Q&A Post carries only the promoted body text entered by the author at promotion time. A `promoted_from_internal_comment_post_id` field is intentionally NOT introduced — carrying such a field would create a leakable back-pointer. The buyer-side UX presents the promotion action as "Create Vendor Q&A Post from this comment" and renders a one-way promotion; no bidirectional link is stored.

**Mobile-domain leakage surfaces.** Mobile web and app clients honor the same console-scoped API boundaries. Copy-paste of an Internal Comment Post into a seller-visible surface is a buyer-user action, not a platform leakage; the platform is not responsible for user-initiated copy-paste but surfaces a pre-copy confirmation "Copy internal comment to external paste target?" dialog per §3.7.12 (External-Target Clipboard Confirmation Pattern) when the clipboard target is a known external app (heuristic: user pastes into a browser window whose URL matches a seller-console or public Marketplace route, or any non-`*.sourcera.com` URL). The dialog is a user-awareness affordance, not a DLP control — the platform does not modify or watermark copied content. Audit event `firewall_protected_clipboard_copy_confirmed` (Appendix G) emits on Copy-anyway with `surface = internal_comment_post`. Authored Extension — flagged in RECONCILIATION.md.

**Audit Coverage.** Every read, write, moderation, visibility-change, and cross-console-read attempt on Internal Comment Thread / Post / Mention writes an §4.6 AuditEvent row. Cross-console read attempts are additionally logged to the Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100) as `sim_firewall_probe` signals for anomaly detection.

### 25.7.8 Retention, DSAR, Residency {#25.7.8-internal-comments-retention-dsar-residency}

Authoritative retention is in **§40.2** and the Retention blocks of **§4.3.11–§4.3.13**; this subsection is a feature-level pointer.

1. **Retention.** Thread / Post / Mention retained for the life of the parent anchor entity. On soft-delete, cascading soft-delete; on hard-delete of the parent, cascading hard-delete within 30 days. On Org hard-delete, 90-day purge. On Workspace Member departure, the departing user's authored posts and mentions remain; the user's identity fields are pseudonymized only on full DSAR right-to-erasure.
2. **DSAR.** §6.8.5 applies. `created_by`, `updated_by`, `moderated_by`, `resolved_by`, `author_id`, `mentioned_user_id`, `expanded_from_team_id` subject fields pseudonymized within 30 days. `body` and `resolution_note` redacted to `[REDACTED_DSAR]` when subject PII is detected. Rows are retained for thread-integrity and audit per §6.8.5.
3. **Residency.** Threads, Posts, Mentions, and their Attachments are stored in the Organization's `data_residency_region`. Cross-region reads are blocked at the storage layer per §40.4. A guest from a different-region Org accessing a host Workspace reads host-region data via a residency-aware read path; no cross-region replication of Internal Comment data occurs.
4. **Right-to-Erasure compatibility.** Full. Any subject-author may request erasure; the Mention and Post rows remain but with pseudonymized identity fields, preserving thread-integrity for non-subject participants.

### 25.7.9 API Surface {#25.7.9-internal-comments-api-surface}

All endpoints follow §32 patterns: auth header, rate-limit class, cursor pagination (default 50, max 250), idempotency via `Idempotency-Key` header for POST, standardized error codes from Appendix I.

**Auth scope.** Every endpoint rejects seller-console session tokens with HTTP 404. Every endpoint rejects callers without Workspace Membership on the target workspace with HTTP 404. Every endpoint evaluates `visibility_scope` and guest `assigned_use_case_ids` against the caller before returning any row.

**Rate-limit class.** `internal_comment_api` (§32.4.5) — 120 requests/min per session for reads; 30 requests/min per session for writes.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Response |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `GET` | `/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/internal-comment-threads` | List threads in a workspace | Paginated; filters on `attached_to_type`, `attached_to_id`, `status`, `visibility_scope`. |
| `POST` | `/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/internal-comment-threads` | Create a new thread with its first post | Creates Thread + first Post + Mentions atomically; emits `internal_comment_thread.created`. |
| `GET` | `/v1/internal-comment-threads/{thread_id}` | Fetch thread + recent posts | Includes `posts_preview` (10 most recent). |
| `PATCH` | `/v1/internal-comment-threads/{thread_id}` | Mutate `title`, `status`, `visibility_scope`, `subscribed_user_ids` | Emits `internal_comment_thread.updated` or domain-specific events. |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/internal-comment-threads/{thread_id}` | Archive thread | Sets `deleted_at`; emits `internal_comment_thread.archived`. |
| `GET` | `/v1/internal-comment-threads/{thread_id}/posts` | List posts in thread | Paginated. |
| `POST` | `/v1/internal-comment-threads/{thread_id}/posts` | Append a post | Creates Post + Mentions atomically; updates thread `post_count`, `last_post_at`; emits `internal_comment_thread.post_appended` and per-Mention `internal_comment_thread.mention_sent` webhooks; triggers Unread Marker fanout (§3.12.4). |
| `PATCH` | `/v1/internal-comment-posts/{post_id}` | Edit post (15-min window) or moderate | Rejects post-window edits with `internal_comment_post_edit_window_expired`. Moderation requires Workspace Owner / Admin. |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/internal-comment-posts/{post_id}` | Author soft-delete (window) or Admin hard-delete | Sets `deleted_placeholder = true` (window) or `deleted_at` (admin). |
| `POST` | `/v1/internal-comment-threads/{thread_id}/read-receipt` | Mark as read (advances caller's Unread Marker) | Idempotent; returns `updated_marker`. |
| `GET` | `/v1/internal-comment-mentions?user_id=me&unread=true` | Current user's unread mentions across threads | Returns Mention rows with `read_at IS NULL`, scoped to caller. |

**Request / Response Example — `POST /v1/workspaces/{id}/internal-comment-threads`.**

Request:

```json
{
  "attached_to_type": "requirement",
  "attached_to_id": "req_01HXYZ...",
  "title": "Open question on SSO scope",
  "visibility_scope": "buyer_workspace_members",
  "subscribed_user_ids": ["usr_...", "usr_..."],
  "post": {
    "body": "Do we require SAML 2.0 or OIDC for this requirement? @alex @Security-Team",
    "attachment_ids": []
  }
}
```

Response (`201 Created`):

```json
{
  "thread": {
    "id": "ict_01HABC...",
    "workspace_id": "ws_01HDEF...",
    "attached_to_type": "requirement",
    "attached_to_id": "req_01HXYZ...",
    "title": "Open question on SSO scope",
    "status": "open",
    "visibility_scope": "buyer_workspace_members",
    "subscribed_user_ids": ["usr_...", "usr_..."],
    "post_count": 1,
    "last_post_at": "2026-04-24T12:34:56Z",
    "created_at": "2026-04-24T12:34:56Z",
    "created_by": "usr_01HGHI..."
  },
  "first_post": {
    "id": "icp_01HJKL...",
    "thread_id": "ict_01HABC...",
    "author_id": "usr_01HGHI...",
    "author_role_snapshot": "use_case_lead",
    "body": "Do we require SAML 2.0 or OIDC for this requirement? @alex @Security-Team",
    "mention_count": 5,
    "edit_locked_at": "2026-04-24T12:49:56Z",
    "created_at": "2026-04-24T12:34:56Z"
  },
  "mentions": [
    {
      "id": "icm_...",
      "mentioned_user_id": "usr_alex...",
      "mention_kind": "user"
    },
    {
      "id": "icm_...",
      "mentioned_user_id": "usr_member_of_security_team_...",
      "mention_kind": "team",
      "expanded_from_team_id": "team_security..."
    }
  ]
}
```

**Error responses.**

- `402 internal_comment_thread_workspace_cap_reached` — Plan cap hit.
- `404 internal_comment_cross_console_access` — Seller-console session OR non-Workspace-Member OR visibility scope excludes caller.
- `404 internal_comment_thread_not_found` — Thread does not exist (existing).
- `409 internal_comment_thread_invalid_state_transition` — Bad PATCH status transition (existing).
- `409 internal_comment_post_moderated_by_admin` — Author edit lost to concurrent admin moderation (new in this pass).
- `413 internal_comment_post_attachment_total_bytes_exceeded` — Sum of attachment sizes > 500 MB (new in this pass).
- `422 internal_comment_thread_anchor_mismatch` — Anchor target not in the thread's workspace (new in this pass).
- `422 internal_comment_post_mention_limit_exceeded` — More than 50 mentions in one post (new in this pass).
- `403 internal_comment_post_edit_window_expired` — Edit after 15-minute lock (existing).
- `429 rate_limit_exceeded` — Per §32 rate-limiting.

### 25.7.10 Webhook Events {#25.7.10-internal-comments-webhook-events}

All webhooks follow §31.1 transport: HMAC-SHA256 signing, `event_id` idempotency, Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve, payload ≤ 256 KB, event class `internal_comment_domain` (new; registered in Appendix J `webhook_event_class` extension in this pass).

| Event | Trigger | Recipient (webhook + notification) | Notification In-App | Notification Email | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `internal_comment_thread.created` | New thread created | Buyer Org webhook subscribers; subscribed users (in-app only by default) | No (default) | No | Opt-in via per-user notification preferences. |
| `internal_comment_thread.post_appended` | New post added | Buyer Org webhook subscribers; thread `subscribed_user_ids[]` | Yes | Yes (digest default) | Respects mute-until, DND, quiet hours per §29.3. |
| `internal_comment_thread.mention_sent` | New Mention row (one per mentioned user) | Mentioned user | Yes | Yes (immediate default) | The `comment_mention` row is already in the §29.1 notification catalog; this webhook extends with `thread_id`, `post_id`, `mention_id`. |
| `internal_comment_thread.resolved` | Status transitions `open → resolved` | Buyer Org webhook subscribers; thread `subscribed_user_ids[]` | Yes | Yes (digest) | Includes `resolved_by`, `resolution_note`. |
| `internal_comment_thread.reopened` | Status transitions `resolved → open` | Buyer Org webhook subscribers; thread `subscribed_user_ids[]` | Yes | No | |
| `internal_comment_thread.archived` | Status transitions to `archived` (manual or cascade) | Buyer Org webhook subscribers | No | No | Logged to audit only. |
| `internal_comment_thread.visibility_changed` | `visibility_scope` mutated | Buyer Org webhook subscribers; newly-included viewers receive "You now have access to thread X" | Yes (newly-included) | No | Newly-excluded viewers receive no notification (silent drop — per firewall rule). |
| `internal_comment_post.moderated` | Admin hard-delete with `moderated_reason` | Buyer Org webhook subscribers (audit); post author (notification) | Yes (author) | Yes (author) | Author-facing notification per §4.3.12 moderation semantics. |

All events carry a standardized payload: `event_id`, `event_type`, `org_id`, `workspace_id`, `thread_id`, `post_id` (where applicable), `actor_user_id`, `timestamp` (UTC), `delivery_id`. **Payload NEVER includes the Post `body` or `attachment_ids[]` verbatim** — subscribers receive metadata; body/attachment fetch requires an authenticated read via the API. This keeps webhook payloads below 256 KB and avoids accidental body leakage via webhook-endpoint logs. A CI gate `webhook_payload_no_internal_comment_body` asserts the generated webhook payload schema excludes `body` and `attachment_ids` fields.

**Appendix-C registration.** Events added to the Appendix-C Notification Event Catalog under a new Internal-Comment-Domain Events subsection in this pass.

**Appendix-G registration.** PostHog taxonomy rows added for the eight webhook events plus UI-surface events `ui_internal_comment_thread_composer_opened`, `ui_internal_comment_post_submitted`, `ui_internal_comment_post_edited`, `ui_internal_comment_thread_resolved`, `ui_internal_comment_thread_reopened`, `ui_internal_comment_thread_cap_hit_upgrade_prompt_shown`, `ui_internal_comment_thread_visibility_tightened`, `ui_internal_comment_post_moderated`.

### 25.7.11 Failure Modes (Counterfactual Pass) {#25.7.11-internal-comments-failure-modes}

| Failure Mode | Authored Handling |
| :---- | :---- |
| Seller-console session attempts to read an Internal Comment Thread | HTTP 404 via `internal_comment_cross_console_access`. Audit row written. SIM `sim_firewall_probe` signal emitted. |
| Mention target is a guest outside the thread's visibility | Mention row is NOT created; notification is suppressed; audit event `internal_comment_mention_skipped_no_access`. |
| Plan cap reached mid-authoring (user typing in composer) | The create API returns `internal_comment_thread_workspace_cap_reached` with an upgrade-CTA payload; the composer surfaces an inline error card per §3.7.4 and offers bulk-archive of resolved threads via a one-click action. |
| Anchor entity soft-deleted while a thread is being authored | Create rejects with `internal_comment_thread_anchor_mismatch` (or the equivalent `anchor_archived` variant if the anchor was soft-deleted); the composer surfaces "This [Requirement] was archived. Select a different anchor." |
| Mention expansion exceeds 50 per post | Post creation rejects with `internal_comment_post_mention_limit_exceeded`; the composer highlights overflow mentions and prompts the user to split the post or target a narrower team. |
| Attachment scan fails (virus or MIME violation) | Attachment upload returns 422; the composer shows a per-file error; post submission proceeds with the remaining attachments. |
| Visibility scope tightened while a Mention notification is in-flight | Notification dispatch re-checks current visibility at send time; if the target is no longer in scope, the notification is dropped and the Mention row's `notified_at` is left NULL. Audit event `internal_comment_mention_suppressed_visibility_tightened`. |
| Bridge handler accidentally imports the Internal Comment Convex module | CI gate `console_bridge_no_internal_comment_imports` fails the PR. |
| Export pipeline (JSON) attempts to include Internal Comment rows for a seller-initiated export | Export builder asserts `initiator_console = buyer` before materializing Internal Comment rows; seller-initiated exports carry `[]` for these collections. Test `export_seller_initiator_no_internal_comments`. |
| Convex query returns a row the caller should not see (permission drift) | The server-side `visibility_scope` evaluator runs in a middleware layer; any row emission where the evaluator returns `forbidden` is dropped and surfaces as an assertion failure in the `internal_comment_visibility_drift_test` suite. |
| User's DSAR erasure triggers cascade redaction of 50,000+ Mentions | The redaction batch is throttled at 5,000 rows/min; completes within the §6.8 72-hour DSAR target. `mentioned_user_id` is replaced with the `ANONYMIZED_USER` sentinel; `body` is redacted to `[REDACTED_DSAR]` only where subject PII is substring-matched by the PII detector. |
| Webhook endpoint receives the post body in payload (violating the no-body rule) | CI gate `webhook_payload_no_internal_comment_body` asserts the generated webhook payload schema excludes `body` and `attachment_ids`; the PR fails if violated. |
| Workspace Owner moderation (hard-delete) races with an author's edit | Moderation wins (Workspace Owner has priority); the author's in-flight edit returns `internal_comment_post_moderated_by_admin` (Appendix I, new) with HTTP 409; the author's UI surfaces "This post was moderated while you were editing." |
| Attachment upload exceeds 500 MB total per post | Upload API rejects with HTTP 413 `internal_comment_post_attachment_total_bytes_exceeded` (Appendix I, new); the composer surfaces per-file size totals and prompts the user to remove files. |

### 25.7.12 Observability & Operational Metrics {#25.7.12-internal-comments-observability}

**OTel spans.**

- `internal_comment.thread.create` — per create call.
- `internal_comment.post.append` — per post append; child span `internal_comment.mention.fanout`.
- `internal_comment.post.moderate` — per moderation.
- `internal_comment.thread.visibility_change` — per visibility mutation.
- `internal_comment.cross_console_read_blocked` — per blocked seller-console attempt.

**Gauge metrics.**

- `internal_comment.threads_per_workspace` — labeled by `workspace_id`; surfaces cap utilization.
- `internal_comment.posts_per_thread.p95` — distribution.
- `internal_comment.mentions_per_post.p95` — distribution.
- `internal_comment.firewall_violation.count` — counter; any non-zero value pages Security on-call per §25.6.2 (new alert row added in this pass).

**Alerts.**

| Alert | Threshold | Severity | Routing | Runbook |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Firewall violation on Internal Comment read | `internal_comment.firewall_violation.count > 0` over 5 m | P1 | Cross-Console on-call + Security on-call | `https://runbooks.sourcera.com/internal-comment-firewall-breach` |
| Mention fanout SLO breach | p95 fanout latency > 500 ms on 200-member workspace, sustained 15 m | P2 | Platform on-call | `https://runbooks.sourcera.com/unread-fanout` |
| Cap-reached spike | > 100 `internal_comment_thread_workspace_cap_reached` events in 15 m across the platform | P3 | Platform Product + Support on-call | Investigate for product gap / upsell signal. |

### 25.7.13 Acceptance Criteria {#25.7.13-internal-comments-acceptance-criteria}

1. Cross-console read from a seller-console session returns HTTP 404 via `internal_comment_cross_console_access`; Playwright `internal_comment_cross_console_firewall` passes on every PR.
2. Bridge NEVER-CARRIED invariant: unit test `console_bridge_no_internal_comment_event_kinds` asserts no `event_kind` in the bridge enum names an Internal Comment Thread / Post / Mention; CI blocks the PR if violated.
3. Plan cap enforced: a Buyer Starter / Growth / Scale workspace blocks the (cap + 1)-th thread creation with HTTP 402 per §34.1.1 cell **Internal Comment Threads per Workspace**; Playwright `internal_comment_cap_enforcement` passes for every paid Buyer tier.
4. Free-tier cap at 25 threads enforced; Enterprise uncapped; end-to-end tests for both tiers.
5. Mention fanout creates one Mention row per targeted user; team/role expansions are frozen at write time; later roster changes do NOT retroactively notify new members; test `mention_expansion_frozen`.
6. Mention cap per post: the 51st mention rejected with `internal_comment_post_mention_limit_exceeded`.
7. 15-minute author edit window enforced; test `post_edit_window_expires_at_15min`.
8. Visibility-scope tightening clears Unread Markers for now-excluded viewers within 30 s; Playwright `visibility_tighten_marker_cleanup` passes.
9. Visibility-scope loosening seeds Unread Markers for newly-included viewers with the correct initial `unread_count`; test `visibility_loosen_marker_seed`.
10. Webhook payload excludes `body` and `attachment_ids`; CI gate `webhook_payload_no_internal_comment_body` passes.
11. `buyer_comment_visible_to_vendor` promotion creates a Q&A Post without storing a back-pointer to the Internal Comment Post; test `no_back_pointer_after_promotion`.
12. A seller-initiated workspace export returns `[]` for Internal Comment collections; test `export_seller_initiator_no_internal_comments`.
13. DSAR hard-delete of a user with 50,000+ mentions completes within the §6.8 72-hour target; batch throttle holds.
14. Attachment virus-scan on Internal Comment Post upload blocks an infected file; Attachment entity `scan_status = infected`; post rejects with 422.
15. Audit events written for every state transition and every cross-console read attempt; §4.6 coverage test passes.
16. Residency: an EU-region Org's Internal Comment data is stored in the EU region only; cross-region query path returns `residency_storage_mismatch` (Appendix I; existing) on misconfiguration.
17. Anchor validation: the anchor `attached_to_id` must resolve to an entity in the same workspace; mismatched anchor rejects with `internal_comment_thread_anchor_mismatch`.
18. Anchor-entity archive cascades: archiving a Use Case moves its threads to `archived`; Appendix L.1 cascade test passes.
19. Guest scoping: a guest with `assigned_use_case_ids = [UC1]` has read access to threads anchored in UC1 only; test `guest_scope_internal_comment_visibility`.
20. Moderation race: Workspace Owner moderation wins over a concurrent author edit; the author's UI surfaces "moderated while editing" per §25.7.11.

### 25.7.14 Authoring Hand-Offs {#25.7.14-internal-comments-authoring-hand-offs}

- **§4.3.11–§4.3.13** already carry the entity definitions; no data-model changes in this pass.
- **§3.12** renders Unread and Presence surfaces for Internal Comments.
- **§5.11 Feature Access Matrix** — the Comments & Collaboration group already covers comment add/edit/delete; §5.11 is updated in this pass to add one row group "Internal Comment Thread Management" noting that `visibility_scope` mutation is restricted to thread author, Workspace Owner, Workspace Admin, and that "Resolve / Re-open" is restricted to thread author, Workspace Owner, Workspace Admin, Use Case Lead (on use-case-scoped threads).
- **§34.1.1** — row added in this pass for "Internal Comment Threads per Workspace" cell.
- **§39** — rows added: per-post mention cap (50); per-workspace mention cap (100,000).
- **Appendix C** — Internal-Comment-Domain Events subsection added (8 events).
- **Appendix G** — Internal-Comment-Domain PostHog taxonomy rows added.
- **Appendix I** — 6 error codes added: `internal_comment_thread_workspace_cap_reached`, `internal_comment_thread_anchor_mismatch`, `internal_comment_post_mention_limit_exceeded`, `internal_comment_post_moderated_by_admin`, `internal_comment_post_attachment_total_bytes_exceeded`, `unread_marker_cross_console_access`.
- **Appendix J** — `internal_comment_thread_visibility_scope`, `internal_comment_thread_attached_to_type`, `internal_comment_mention_kind`, `internal_comment_mention_skip_reason`, `webhook_event_class` extension, `unread_marker_suppressed_reason` registered.
- **Appendix L.1** — unchanged (existing Internal Comment Thread state machine remains authoritative).
- **§25.6.2** — new alert row added for `internal_comment.firewall_violation.count > 0`.
- **§29.1 Notification Event Catalog** — `internal_comment_thread.post_appended`, `internal_comment_thread.mention_sent` integrated (existing `comment_mention` row refined).
