# 26\. Seller Profiles, Verification & Capability Declarations {#26.-seller-profiles,-verification-&-capability-declarations}

## 26.1 Seller Profile {#26.1-seller-profile}

Each selling Organization maintains a Seller Profile, visible in the Marketplace when `marketplace_opted_in = true`.

**Profile fields:**

- Organization name  
- Organization logo (max 2MB, PNG/JPG)  
- Company description (0–1000 chars, Markdown)  
- Website URL  
- Location / HQ region  
- Founded year  
- Number of employees (range: 1-10, 11-50, 51-200, 201-1000, 1000+)  
- Industries served (multi-select from controlled vocabulary)  
- Certification badges (SOC2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, etc.)  
- Verification tier (Basic, Verified, Certified)  
- Public contact email

## 26.2 Verification Tiers {#26.2-verification-tiers}

| Tier | Criteria | Badge Display | Approval Workflow |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Basic** | Email verified \+ account created | Gray checkmark icon | Automatic upon signup |
| **Verified** | Email verified \+ legal entity confirmed via business registration lookup (OpenCorporates or similar) | Blue "Verified" badge \+ checkmark | Semi-automatic, \<1 hour processing |
| **Certified** | All Verified criteria \+ manual review by Sourcera team (compliance docs reviewed) | Gold "Certified" badge \+ checkmark | Manual review, \~5–10 business days |

Buyers can filter Marketplace by verification tier. Certified vendors have higher visibility in match scoring.

## 26.3 Capability Declarations {#26.3-capability-declarations}

Sellers declare capabilities across four categories: Security & Compliance, Integration & Technical, Operational Maturity, Company Profile.

**Declaration schema:**

- Capability name (string, ≤100 chars, e.g., "SOC2 Type II")  
- Category (enum: Security & Compliance, Integration & Technical, Operational Maturity, Company Profile)  
- Declaration text (0–3000 chars, Markdown)  
- Evidence files (max 10 files, 50MB each)  
- Verification status (enum: `pending`, `evidence_provided`, `verified`)  
- Published (boolean, controls visibility in Marketplace)

**Verification (Gap 26.1):**

- When seller uploads evidence (e.g., SOC2 report PDF), evidence is stored and status auto-advances to `evidence_provided`.  
- Badge displays as "Evidence Provided" (accurate, transparent).  
- Manual moderation (e.g., Sourcera staff verifying the evidence is legitimate) is deferred to Phase 2 roadmap and not implemented in v6.0.

## 26.4 KB-to-Capability Auto-Suggestion {#26.4-kb-to-capability-auto-suggestion}

When a seller is editing Capability Declarations, the Agent (Haiku) suggests capabilities from the seller's KB entries.

**Trigger:** Seller opens Capability Declarations editor. Agent scans KB entries for structured content (e.g., "SOC2 certification" in title or body). For each detected capability, Agent displays:

- Suggested capability name  
- Associated KB entry title  
- Confidence score (0-100%)  
- "Create From KB" button

**Behavior:** Clicking "Create From KB" pre-fills the Capability Declaration form with:

- Capability name from KB title or Agent-extracted term  
- Declaration text from KB entry (first 500 chars)  
- Flag to link evidence files from KB entry (if any)

Seller can edit before publishing.

## 26.5 UX Implementation {#26.5-ux-implementation}

- **Inline Edit:** Capability names and declaration text editable in place (double-click to edit).  
- **Drag-and-Drop:** Evidence files uploaded via drag-and-drop or file picker.  
- **Progressive Disclosure:** Collapsed card shows name \+ badge \+ category. Expanded shows full declaration \+ evidence list.  
- **Batch Actions:** Multi-select capabilities for bulk publish to Marketplace or bulk archive.  
- **Mobile:** Single-column card grid. Native file picker (no drag-and-drop on touch).  
- **Keyboard Shortcuts:** `Cmd+N` to create new capability. `Cmd+Shift+P` to publish all.

## 26.6 Acceptance Criteria {#26.6-acceptance-criteria}

- Seller can declare 5–10 capabilities in \<30 minutes.  
- Evidence files are securely stored in Convex Storage with access logs.  
- Capability badges render correctly in Marketplace listings.  
- "Evidence Provided" badge text is accurate and not misleading (does not claim "Verified" without manual review).  
- KB-to-Capability suggestions appear within 3 seconds of editor load.

## 26.7 Seller Organization Pages {#26.7-seller-organization-pages}

**Source:** Summary §6.15.4; entity definition at §4.4.10 (SellerOrgPage).

Seller Organization Pages are rich, public-facing pages at `sourcera.com/sellers/:slug` — the Sourcera-native storefront for each Seller Org. They serve as the primary SEO and organic-discovery moat for the Marketplace (§27), surfacing company detail, product portfolio, certifications, and case studies in a search-engine-optimized format. Every Seller Org with `marketplace_opted_in = true` may create at most one SellerOrgPage (one-to-one with Seller Profile).

### 26.7.1 Page Content & Structure {#26.7.1-page-content-and-structure}

A SellerOrgPage comprises the following content regions, rendered in order:

1. **Hero Section.** `hero_copy_markdown` (0–3000 chars, Markdown). Above-the-fold seller pitch. May include logo, tagline, and a "Contact Vendor" CTA that resolves to the public contact email from §26.1 Seller Profile.
2. **Body Sections.** `body_sections_json` (≤ 50 000 chars). An ordered array of typed sections, each containing a heading, body (Markdown), and optional asset references (images hosted in Convex Storage). Supported section types: `overview`, `products`, `certifications`, `case_studies`, `integrations`, `custom`. Section-type enum registered in Appendix J (`seller_org_page_section_type`).
3. **Capability Summary.** Auto-populated from the Seller Org's published Capability Declarations (§26.3). Read-only on the page; editable only via the Capability Declarations editor. Renders as badge grid with category grouping.
4. **Product Portfolio.** Auto-populated from published SellerSoftware rows (§4.4.9) where `page_status = page_published`. Each product renders as a card (logo, name, tagline, category badge) linking to the corresponding SoftwarePage at `/software/:slug` (§26.8).
5. **Verification Badge.** Inherited from §26.2. Badge tier (Basic / Verified / Certified) rendered prominently in the hero section. Gold "Certified" badge has tooltip explaining criteria.
6. **Structured Data Block.** Invisible to users; rendered as `<script type="application/ld+json">` containing the `schema_org_payload_json` cache (§26.9.1).

**Empty-State Handling.** If `body_sections_json` is empty, the page renders the hero section plus the auto-populated Capability Summary and Product Portfolio only; a "Complete your page" prompt is shown to seller-console users in the Seller Profile editor. If the Seller Org has zero published Capability Declarations and zero published SellerSoftware rows, the page MUST NOT be publishable — the `published` transition is gated by `(count(published_capabilities) + count(published_seller_software)) >= 1`.

### 26.7.2 Page Enrichment via `page_enrichment` Capability {#26.7.2-page-enrichment}

Enrichment is the AI-powered content-generation workflow that differentiates Sourcera pages from static profiles. The `seller_page_enrichment` capability (canonical Appendix J `capability_id` per §21.4.2 row 1; Opus-tier; `customer_billed`; $8.00 value-priced / $1.10 cost-priced; `seller_starter` minimum plan-gate per §29102 / §29616 / §34.1.2; legacy alias `page_enrichment` accepted at API boundary and rewritten to canonical at write time per §21.4.1.A) crawls the seller's public surfaces — corporate website, product documentation, press releases, G2/Capterra reviews, LinkedIn company page — and drafts page content for the seller's review.

**Enrichment Workflow (8-step).**

1. Seller creates a SellerOrgPage or clicks "Re-enrich" on an existing page. SellerOrgPage transitions to `pending_enrichment` (§4.4.10 state machine).
2. System queues a `seller_page_enrichment` AIOperation (§4.8.1; canonical capability_id per §21.4.2 row 1). Cost center is resolved at AIOperation creation by reading `CapabilityRegistryEntry.cost_center_default` for the canonical capability (§4.8.2) — at v7.1.0, `seller_page_enrichment` resolves to `customer_billed`, and the AIOperation debits the Seller Org's `AIWallet` per §4.8.3 / §34.10. Plan-tier free quotas are authoritative only in §34.1.2 cell **Seller Page Enrichment (Opus)**; §34.14.1 row 8 cites that cell and MUST NOT restate the per-tier quota inline. Free Allowance counter (§4.8.7) decrements before AIWallet debit. Resolved cost center is denormalized to `SellerOrgPage.enrichment_cost_center_resolved` (§4.4.10) at AIOperation creation for billing-ledger audit. Hard plan-gate enforcement per §29102 — `seller_free` Orgs receive HTTP 402 `capability_requires_plan_upgrade` (Appendix I) on direct invocation; `seller_starter` and above invoke through the wallet path. Deploy-time validator `enrichment_cost_center_single_source` asserts no inline cost-center hardcoding outside the registry-resolution path (CI gate `enrichment_cost_center_single_source`, Appendix M.5).
3. The enrichment worker resolves the seller's `website_url` from §26.1 Seller Profile and any linked SellerSoftware product URLs.
4. Firecrawl (§22.6) crawls up to 50 pages across the resolved domains. Rate limit: 5 req/s per target domain. Respect `robots.txt` — if the seller's site disallows crawling, enrichment fails gracefully with a user-visible notice ("We couldn't access your website. Please allowlist our crawler or author the page manually.").
5. Opus agent summarizes the crawled content, extracting: company overview, product list, certifications, integration partners, notable customers (public only — never from confidential bid data), and founding/growth narrative.
6. Agent drafts `hero_copy_markdown`, `body_sections_json`, and `meta_title` / `meta_description` into `pending_enrichment_draft_json`. Draft includes confidence annotations per section (high / medium / low).
7. SellerOrgPage transitions to `pending_review`. Seller receives an in-app notification and email (§35 Notification Templates) with a preview link.
8. Seller reviews the draft in a split-pane editor (left: current page, right: enrichment draft). Three actions available per section: **Accept** (merge into body), **Edit** (merge with modifications), **Reject** (discard section). On final approval, the page transitions to `published` (subject to domain verification gate).

**Enrichment Failure Modes.**

| Failure | Behavior | User-Visible |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Firecrawl timeout (target site unresponsive > 30s) | Enrichment fails; SellerOrgPage reverts to `draft`; AIOperation outcome: `rejected` | "Your website didn't respond. Try again later or author manually." |
| Content validator rejects AI output (anti-spam, PII detected) | Draft discarded; AIOperation outcome: `rejected`; Ops alerted | "Enrichment couldn't be completed. Our team has been notified." |
| Seller's `robots.txt` blocks Firecrawl | No crawl attempted; enrichment fails gracefully | "Your website blocks our crawler. Please allowlist `bot.sourcera.com`." |
| Opus API outage (Anthropic dependency) | Queue retries 3× with exponential backoff (1m, 5m, 15m); then fails | "Enrichment is temporarily unavailable. We'll retry automatically." |

**Re-Enrichment Rules.** Sellers may re-enrich at most once per 7 calendar days to prevent abuse. Rate limit enforced by comparing `last_enrichment_at` with current timestamp. Ops may override via the Ops Console.

### 26.7.3 Domain Verification Gate {#26.7.3-domain-verification-gate}

Publication of a SellerOrgPage requires `domain_ownership_verified_at IS NOT NULL` on the SellerOrgPage entity (§4.4.10). Domain ownership is established through the Seller Profile claim flow, which supports four verification methods (§4.4.9 `claim_verified_by_method` enum):

- **DNS TXT record.** Seller adds a `TXT` record `sourcera-verification={org_id}` to their domain's DNS. System polls every 5 minutes for up to 72 hours.
- **Email verification.** Seller confirms ownership of an email address at the claimed domain (e.g., `admin@vendorcorp.com`).
- **SSO domain match.** Seller's WorkOS SSO connection domain matches the Seller Profile website URL domain.
- **Ops manual verification.** For edge cases (e.g., acquired domains, vanity domains), Ops verifies manually and stamps `domain_ownership_verified_at`.

**Verification Loss.** If the domain is later re-verified to a different Org (concurrent claim dispute), or if the seller's SSO domain changes, the system MUST cascade `domain_ownership_verified_at = null` on the SellerOrgPage, which triggers automatic transition to `suppressed_by_opt_out` with a synthetic opt-out record (`reason_code = ops_imposed`) per §4.4.10 failure mode #1.

### 26.7.4 Write Access & Roles {#26.7.4-write-access-and-roles}

Write access to SellerOrgPage content is restricted to Seller Org members holding one of:

- `seller_org_admin` — full CRUD on all SellerOrgPage fields.
- `seller_marketing_editor` (new role; Appendix J) — CRUD on content fields (`hero_copy_markdown`, `body_sections_json`, `meta_title`, `meta_description`, `og_image_url`). Cannot change `publication_status` transitions to/from `published` (only `seller_org_admin` may publish or archive).

All write operations emit an audit event (`seller_org_page.updated`, `seller_org_page.published`, `seller_org_page.archived`) per Appendix G.

### 26.7.5 Marketplace Integration {#26.7.5-marketplace-integration}

Published SellerOrgPages surface in the Marketplace (§27) in three ways:

1. **Search results.** §27.3 Marketplace Search indexes SellerOrgPage `meta_title`, `meta_description`, and `hero_copy_markdown` in the full-text search corpus. Pages with `publication_status != published` are excluded from the index.
2. **Vendor profile link.** The "View Profile" button in §27.3 listing display resolves to `/sellers/:slug` for Seller Orgs that have a published SellerOrgPage. For Orgs without one, the button links to the basic Seller Profile card (§26.1 fields only).
3. **Category Pages.** §4.4.12 CategoryPage references published SellerOrgPages for vendor listings within each category.

### 26.7.6 Edge Caching, Cache Invalidation & Anti-Scraping {#26.7.6-edge-caching-cache-invalidation-and-anti-scraping}

Public Marketplace pages are read-heavy and latency-sensitive. To preserve Core Web Vitals (§26.9.10) and absorb traffic spikes (e.g., a SellerOrgPage shared on LinkedIn), all SellerOrgPage and SoftwarePage HTML responses are cached at the CDN edge. This subsection codifies the cache-key contract, the invalidation pipeline driven by state-machine transitions, and the bot/scraper rate-limit contract that protects the origin.

**Edge Cache Contract.**

| Surface | Cache Layer | TTL | Cache-Key Components | Vary On |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `/sellers/:slug` HTML | CDN (Cloudflare or equivalent per §42.3) | 600s (10 min) hot, 86 400s (24h) stale-while-revalidate | host, path, accepted content-encoding, viewport class (`mobile` vs `desktop`) | `Accept-Encoding`, `User-Agent` (UA-class only — `bot` vs `human` per §42.7 WAF rules) |
| `/software/:slug` HTML | CDN | Same as above | Same | Same |
| `/sellers/:slug/og-image.png` | CDN | 7 days | host, path, `og_image_url` content hash | None |
| Sitemap XML (§26.9.3) | CDN | 3 600s (1h) | host, path | None |
| `robots.txt` (§26.9.4) | CDN | 86 400s (24h) | host | None |
| Schema.org JSON-LD (inline, no separate URL) | Inline in HTML; inherits HTML cache | n/a | n/a | n/a |

**Cache Invalidation Triggers.** Every state-machine transition on a SellerOrgPage or SoftwarePage that changes the public projection MUST emit a `page_cache_purge` event consumed by the CDN purge worker. Triggers and the URLs they purge:

| Transition | URLs Purged | Async SLO |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `* → published` | `/sellers/:slug`, `/sellers/:slug/og-image.png`, `sitemap-index.xml`, `sitemaps/sellers.xml` (or `software.xml`), affected `CategoryPage` URLs | < 60s p95, < 300s p99 |
| `published → suppressed_by_opt_out` | Same as above | < 60s p95, < 300s p99 (per §4.4.10 AC #2 / §4.4.11) |
| `published → archived` | Same as above; and the URL is rewritten to return HTTP 410 (§26.9.5) | < 60s p95 |
| Page content edit while `published` (no enrichment re-run) | `/sellers/:slug`, `/sellers/:slug/og-image.png` only | < 60s p95 |
| `og_image_url` change while `published` | `/sellers/:slug/og-image.png` only; HTML page re-cached on next refresh | < 60s p95 |
| Vendor opt-out cascaded suppression of a referenced product | `/sellers/:slug` (parent), `/software/:slug` (product), affected `CategoryPage` URLs | < 60s p95 |

**Purge Failure Handling.** The CDN purge worker retries failed purges with exponential backoff (1s, 5s, 30s, 5m, 30m). After 5 failures, the purge enters a Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) and pages the Ops on-call. While in DLQ, the affected page returns the stale projection — Ops MUST manually purge from the CDN console within 30 minutes to maintain the §26.9.5 opt-out honoring SLA. The `page_cache_purge_event_kind` enum (Appendix J) tracks the trigger; `page_cache_purge_status` (Appendix J) tracks `pending`, `purged`, `failed_retrying`, `dlq`, `manually_purged`.

**Origin Shield.** A second-tier origin shield cache MUST be enabled in front of the application server to absorb purge stampedes (e.g., a homepage feature event triggers thousands of simultaneous SellerOrgPage requests). Origin-shield TTL: 60s. Origin-shield cache-key omits the `User-Agent` Vary dimension to maximize hit rate; UA classification is performed at the edge layer above the shield.

**Anti-Scraping Rate Limits.** The Marketplace surfaces are valuable to data aggregators and competitive intelligence firms. To prevent wholesale exfiltration of the SellerOrgPage / SoftwarePage corpus, the following per-IP rate limits apply at the WAF (§42.7) tier:

| Path Pattern | Anonymous Limit | Authenticated Limit | Burst | Action on Excess |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `/sellers/:slug`, `/software/:slug` | 60 req/min | 120 req/min | 30 | HTTP 429 with `Retry-After: 60` |
| `/sellers/`, `/software/` (listing-style scrapes) | 10 req/min | 30 req/min | 5 | HTTP 429 |
| `/sitemap-index.xml`, `/sitemaps/*.xml` | 30 req/hour | n/a | 10 | HTTP 429 |
| `/sellers/*/og-image.png` | 120 req/min | 240 req/min | 60 | HTTP 429 |

**Bot Allowlist.** Verified search-engine bots (Googlebot, Bingbot, DuckDuckBot, Yandex, Baidu) MUST be allowlisted via reverse-DNS verification (forward-confirmed reverse DNS, FCrDNS) and exempt from the per-IP limits above. Spoofed bot User-Agents that fail FCrDNS MUST be subject to the standard anonymous limits and logged to the abuse signal table (§3.5).

**Page-Level Preview Mode.** Sellers may share an unpublished SellerOrgPage with internal stakeholders (legal, marketing, exec) before publication using a signed preview token:

- **Token format.** JWT signed with the seller-console session key; payload `{seller_org_page_id, preview_user_id, expires_at}`. TTL: 7 days; non-renewable (re-issuance creates a new token; old token continues to work until expiry).
- **Token issuance.** A `seller_org_admin` or `seller_marketing_editor` clicks "Share Preview Link" in the Seller Console editor. System mints a token and returns a URL of the form `https://sourcera.com/sellers/:slug?preview=<jwt>`.
- **Token validation.** Edge worker validates JWT signature and expiry before serving. Invalid or expired tokens return HTTP 410 with the `seller_org_page_preview_token_expired` error (Appendix I). Valid tokens bypass the publish gate but MUST emit `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` to prevent search engines from indexing preview content.
- **Audit.** Preview-token issuance and access events are logged to the audit trail (`seller_org_page.preview_token_issued`, `seller_org_page.preview_accessed`).
- **Token revocation.** A `seller_org_admin` may revoke all outstanding preview tokens for a page (e.g., if a sensitive draft was leaked). Revocation flushes the JWT key version, invalidating all prior tokens.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **CDN purge stampede.** Origin shield absorbs simultaneous purges; Convex query layer rate-limits at 1 000 QPS per page entity to prevent database overload.
2. **Stale opt-out content served from CDN.** Purge SLO is < 60s p95; the §26.9.5 SLA is 24h, providing margin. Manual Ops purge available via DLQ alert.
3. **Aggressive scraper exhausts origin.** Per-IP rate limits + WAF + bot detection prevent corpus exfiltration; origin protected by edge cache hit-rate > 95% target.
4. **Preview token leak.** Tokens are bound to a `preview_user_id` for audit; revocation by token version flush; never indexed (`X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`).

## 26.8 SellerSoftware & Software Pages {#26.8-sellersoftware-and-software-pages}

**Source:** Summary §6.15.5; entity definitions at §4.4.9 (SellerSoftware) and §4.4.11 (SoftwarePage).

SellerSoftware entities represent individual software products owned by a Seller Org — distinct from the Org itself. Each SellerSoftware may have at most one SoftwarePage, the public-facing product page at `sourcera.com/software/:slug`. Together, they enable multi-product vendors to be discovered, compared, and evaluated at the product level rather than the vendor level. Published SellerSoftware entities populate the Marketplace (§27) search index, power product-level filtering in §27.3, and feed downstream Sourcera-owned content surfaces: CategoryPages (§4.4.12), GuidePages (§4.4.13), ComparisonPages (§4.4.14), and MarketIntelligenceReports (§4.4.15).

### 26.8.1 SellerSoftware Lifecycle {#26.8.1-sellersoftware-lifecycle}

**Creation.** A Seller Org member with `seller_org_admin` or `seller_marketing_editor` role creates a SellerSoftware row from the Seller Console's "Products" tab. Required at creation: `name`, `category_id`, `slug`. A KB namespace is auto-created and linked via `kb_namespace_id` (§22.3.4). Plan-tier limits on the number of SellerSoftware entities are authoritative in §34.1.2 cell **SellerSoftware Entities** (Free / Seller Starter / Seller Growth / Seller Scale / Seller Enterprise); §26.8.1 does NOT restate the per-tier values.

Attempting to create beyond the §34.1.2 plan-tier ceiling returns `entitlement_exceeded` (Appendix I; HTTP 402) with an upgrade CTA surface.

**Auto-Created (Unclaimed) Products.** Sourcera's enrichment workers may auto-create SellerSoftware rows with `claim_status = unclaimed` from public data sources (Summary §6.15.4 enrichment, ghost-bid imports per §4.4.17). These rows have a minimal profile (name, slug, category) and render a "Claim this listing" CTA on the public SoftwarePage. The claiming Org need not be the same as the Org that originally created the enriched row.

**Editing.** Content fields (`name`, `tagline`, `description`, `pricing_model`, `pricing_summary`, `category_id`, `secondary_category_ids`, `logo_url`, `hero_image_url`) are editable by `seller_org_admin` or `seller_marketing_editor` when `claim_status = claim_verified`. Capability Declarations are managed via the §26.3 editor and linked by reference in `capability_declaration_ids`. The `slug` is editable only when `page_status IN (no_page, page_drafting)`; once a SoftwarePage is published, the slug becomes immutable (slug renames create a 301 redirect alias per §4.4.9 Slug Collision Rule).

**Deletion (Soft Delete).** Soft-deleting a SellerSoftware triggers:
1. SoftwarePage (if any) transitions to `archived`; URL returns HTTP 410.
2. KB namespace migrates to the Org namespace per KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4 (`kb_namespace_migration` audit event emitted within 5 minutes).
3. Comparison Pages (§4.4.14) referencing this product re-evaluate their min-count rule.
4. `capability_declaration_ids` are preserved on the soft-deleted row for audit; declarations themselves are NOT deleted.

### 26.8.2 Claim Verification Flow {#26.8.2-claim-verification-flow}

Claim verification ensures that only the true owner of a software product can author its page and manage its KB namespace. The claim state machine is defined at §4.4.9 (`claim_status`).

**User-Facing Flow (5-step).**

1. Seller navigates to the unclaimed SoftwarePage (or searches Marketplace and finds an unclaimed listing).
2. Seller clicks "Claim this listing." System presents verification options based on the product's known domain:
   - **DNS TXT** — seller adds a `TXT` record `sourcera-verify-software={seller_software_id}` to the product's domain.
   - **Email verification** — seller confirms ownership of an email at the product's domain.
   - **SSO domain match** — automatic if the seller's WorkOS SSO domain matches.
   - **Ops manual** — fallback for edge cases (e.g., product hosted on a third-party platform).
3. `claim_status` transitions to `claim_pending`. A 14-day TTL starts.
4. System polls DNS (every 5 min), waits for email confirmation (72h expiry), or checks SSO match (immediate).
5. On success: `claim_status = claim_verified`; seller granted edit rights. On failure/expiry: `claim_status` reverts to `unclaimed`; logged in audit.

**Concurrent Claims (Dispute Resolution).**

When a second Org attempts to claim a product already in `claim_pending`, both claims transition to `claim_disputed`. Neither Org may edit the row. Resolution requires Ops intervention (`ops_taxonomy_admin` role):

- Ops reviews evidence from both parties (domain registrar records, product website, customer references).
- Ops resolves in favor of one party; the losing party is notified and blocked from re-claim for 30 days.
- Dispute resolution is logged in the audit trail with `ops_resolution_note`.

**Re-Verification.** Sourcera does not continuously re-verify domain ownership post-claim. However, if Ops receives a legitimate challenge (e.g., acquisition, domain transfer), Ops may revoke the claim (`claim_status = claim_revoked`), which suppresses the SoftwarePage and reverts the row to `unclaimed`.

### 26.8.3 Capability Declarations per Product {#26.8.3-capability-declarations-per-product}

Each SellerSoftware references up to 500 Capability Declarations (§26.3) via `capability_declaration_ids`. These declarations MUST belong to the same `org_id` as the SellerSoftware (cross-Org references rejected per §4.4.9 Scope Isolation). Declarations are shared across the Org; a single declaration (e.g., "SOC 2 Type II") may be referenced by multiple SellerSoftware rows if applicable.

**Product-Level Filtering.** In the Marketplace (§27.3), buyers may filter by capability at the product level — e.g., "show me HRMS products with SAML SSO support." This filter queries the `capability_declaration_ids` on SellerSoftware, not the Org-level declarations directly.

**KB-to-Capability Auto-Suggestion (§26.4) per Product.** When the seller edits capabilities for a specific SellerSoftware, the Haiku agent scans only the KB namespace associated with that product (`kb_namespace_id`), not the Org-level namespace. This ensures suggestions are product-relevant.

### 26.8.4 KB Namespace Isolation per Product {#26.8.4-kb-namespace-isolation}

Each SellerSoftware entity owns exactly one KB namespace (§22.3.4). This provides:

- **Retrieval isolation.** When a buyer asks a question about a specific product during an evaluation, the `first_pass_responder` agent (§22 / KB_Engineering_Spec §6.2) prioritizes the product's namespace before falling back to the Org namespace. This prevents cross-contamination between products (e.g., security docs for Product A polluting answers about Product B).
- **Ingestion isolation.** KB entries uploaded via the Seller Console are tagged to a specific namespace. The seller chooses which product (or Org-level) namespace to target at ingestion time.
- **Migration on deletion.** When a SellerSoftware is soft-deleted, its KB entries migrate to the Org namespace with a `confidence_modifier × 0.7` rank penalty until a Team Lead re-approves (KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4). `former_kb_namespace_ids` preserves provenance for audit.

### 26.8.5 Software Pages {#26.8.5-software-pages}

SoftwarePage (§4.4.11) is the public-facing page at `sourcera.com/software/:slug`, one-to-one with SellerSoftware. It mirrors the SellerOrgPage content model (§26.7) with the following product-specific additions:

- **Feature Highlights.** `feature_highlights` (0–10 entries, ≤ 200 chars each) — bullet-point feature summaries surfaced in Comparison Pages (§4.4.14) and Marketplace search snippets.
- **Pricing Summary.** `pricing_summary_markdown` (0–2000 chars) — human-readable pricing detail, rendered below the hero section.
- **Schema.org `Product` Type.** The structured data payload emits `Product` (not `Organization`), with `Offer` and `AggregateRating` sub-types where applicable (§26.9.1).

**Publication Gate.** SoftwarePage publication requires ALL of:
1. Parent SellerSoftware `claim_status = claim_verified`.
2. Parent SellerSoftware's Seller Org has `domain_ownership_verified_at IS NOT NULL` on the associated SellerOrgPage (or Seller Profile claim).
3. `meta_title` and `meta_description` populated within length constraints.
4. No active matching Vendor Opt-Out Record (§4.4.8).

Failure to meet any condition returns the applicable error code from Appendix I (HTTP 409).

**Enrichment.** SoftwarePages use the same `page_enrichment` capability and workflow as SellerOrgPages (§26.7.2). The enrichment worker additionally crawls product-specific URLs (documentation site, changelog, pricing page) identified from the SellerSoftware `logo_url` / `hero_image_url` domains and any KB entries with URL sources.

### 26.8.6 Comparison Page Participation {#26.8.6-comparison-page-participation}

Published SellerSoftware entities participate in Comparison Pages (§4.4.14) subject to the following rules:

1. **Minimum Participant Count.** A Comparison Page requires ≥ 2 published SellerSoftware rows in the same `category_id` with `claim_status = claim_verified`. If the count drops below 2 (e.g., claim revocation, opt-out), the Comparison Page transitions to `archived` per §4.4.14 archive-on-min-count rule.
2. **Vendor Opt-Out Redaction.** If a SellerSoftware's Seller Org has an active Vendor Opt-Out Record with `scope_kind = software` or `scope_kind = global` matching this product, the product's column is redacted per §4.5.6 Marketplace-Domain Read/Render Contract. The comparison remains visible but the opted-out product shows a placeholder ("Vendor data not available").
3. **Feature Highlights as Comparison Columns.** `feature_highlights` from each participating SellerSoftware are normalized and aligned as comparison rows. Alignment is best-effort (fuzzy match on highlight text); unmatched highlights render in an "Other Features" section.
4. **Category Reassignment.** If a SellerSoftware's `category_id` changes, the product is removed from the old category's Comparison Page and added to the new category's Comparison Page (subject to min-count). The transition triggers re-validation on both pages.

### 26.8.7 Product Transfer, Bulk Operations & Preview {#26.8.7-product-transfer-bulk-operations-and-preview}

This subsection codifies three operational lifecycle workflows that the Phase 5 base specification flagged as Authored Extensions: (1) inter-Org transfer of a SellerSoftware row when one Seller Org acquires another (M&A), (2) bulk product creation for multi-product vendors onboarding programmatically, and (3) preview tokens for unpublished SoftwarePages.

**Product Transfer (M&A Workflow).** When Seller Org A acquires the rights to a SellerSoftware row owned by Seller Org B (corporate acquisition, product spin-off, divestiture), the row MUST be transferable without losing slug continuity, KB history, claim verification, or SEO equity. The transfer flow is Ops-mediated to prevent fraudulent product theft.

| Step | Actor | Action | State Effect |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Acquiring Org (`seller_org_admin`) | Submits Transfer Request via Seller Console: target SellerSoftware ID, justification text (≥ 100 chars), supporting evidence (≤ 10 docs, ≤ 50 MB each — e.g., acquisition press release, registrar transfer record) | New `SellerSoftwareTransferRequest` row created with `transfer_status=requested` |
| 2 | Source Org (`seller_org_admin`) | Receives in-app + email notification; has 14 days to confirm or contest | `transfer_status=awaiting_source_consent` |
| 3a | Source Org confirms | Provides confirmation; transfer continues | `transfer_status=ops_review` |
| 3b | Source Org contests | Both Orgs frozen from edit; `transfer_status=disputed` | Manual Ops resolution required |
| 3c | Source Org silent for 14 days | Auto-escalates to Ops review | `transfer_status=ops_review` (with `silent_consent_inferred=true` flag) |
| 4 | Ops (`ops_taxonomy_admin`) | Reviews evidence; either approves or rejects | `transfer_status=approved` OR `transfer_status=rejected` |
| 5 | System (on `approved`) | Mutates SellerSoftware: `org_id` updated, `seller_profile_id` updated to acquiring Org's profile, KB namespace migrated to acquiring Org's namespace tree, `claim_status` reset to `claim_pending` (acquiring Org MUST re-verify), historical `former_org_ids` array appended | Transfer complete; SoftwarePage transitions to `pending_review` until acquiring Org re-verifies claim |

**Slug Continuity.** The SellerSoftware `slug` and the SoftwarePage `slug` are PRESERVED through transfer to maintain SEO equity. The canonical URL `sourcera.com/software/:slug` does not change. Transfer events emit a `seller_software.transferred` audit record (Appendix G PostHog event taxonomy and Appendix C webhook catalog).

**KB Namespace Migration on Transfer.** KB entries follow the product. The KB namespace `kb_namespace_id` is moved to the acquiring Org's namespace tree per KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4.1 (cross-Org migration variant — Authored Extension; KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4 currently covers intra-Org migration only). The migration MUST preserve `confidence_modifier` ranks; no rank penalty applies because the transfer is a legitimate ownership change, not an orphaning event. `former_kb_namespace_ids` is appended with the source-Org namespace ID for audit.

**Capability Declaration Handling on Transfer.** Capability Declarations referenced via `capability_declaration_ids` are NOT auto-transferred (they belong to the source Org and may not be assignable). Transfer wizard prompts the acquiring Org to either (a) clone-and-claim the declarations into their own Org-scoped declaration pool, or (b) drop the references (declarations show as "Pending re-declaration"). Choice is logged in audit.

**Reversal Window.** Transfers may be reversed within 30 days by Ops if the acquiring Org cannot verify domain ownership (`claim_status` remains `claim_pending` past TTL) or if the Source Org files a post-hoc dispute with new evidence. After 30 days, transfers are permanent and may only be reversed by a fresh Transfer Request in the opposite direction.

**Bulk SellerSoftware Creation API.** Multi-product vendors (e.g., a Seller Org with 25+ products on the Scale plan) MAY use the Bulk Create endpoint to provision SellerSoftware rows programmatically. Endpoint specification:

- **Method:** `POST`
- **Path:** `/api/v1/seller/software/bulk`
- **Auth:** Seller-console session token; caller MUST hold `seller_org_admin` (not `seller_marketing_editor`).
- **Rate limit class:** `bulk_write` (per §32.2 — 10 req/min, 100/hour).
- **Idempotency:** Required `Idempotency-Key` header (UUID, 24h replay window). Replays return the original response.
- **Request body schema:**

```json
{
  "products": [
    {
      "client_request_id": "string (caller-supplied; required for partial-failure mapping)",
      "name": "string (1-200)",
      "slug": "string (3-80, ^[a-z0-9-]+$)",
      "category_id": "uuid (FK Marketplace Category)",
      "tagline": "string (0-200, optional)",
      "description": "string (0-5000 markdown, optional)",
      "pricing_model": "enum (seller_software_pricing_model, optional)",
      "logo_url": "string (https url, optional)"
    }
  ]
}
```

- **Constraints:** Maximum 50 products per request (per §39 Object Size Constraints — added in this section). Partial-failure semantics: each product in the array is validated independently; the response returns a per-product status array indicating success/failure with the same `client_request_id` echoed.
- **Response 200 schema:**

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "client_request_id": "string",
      "status": "created | validation_failed | entitlement_exceeded | slug_conflict",
      "seller_software_id": "uuid (when status=created)",
      "error": {
        "code": "appendix-i error code",
        "message": "string",
        "details": {}
      }
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "total": 50,
    "created": 47,
    "failed": 3
  }
}
```

- **Failure modes:** If a single product would push the Org past plan-tier limits (§34.1), only the products fitting under the limit are created; the rest return `entitlement_exceeded`. The endpoint NEVER returns 4xx for the entire request when at least one product was created — partial success is the contract. If ALL products fail validation, the endpoint returns HTTP 422 with `seller_software_bulk_create_total_failure`.
- **KB namespace creation.** Each successfully created SellerSoftware row triggers synchronous KB namespace creation (§26.8.1). If namespace creation fails for any product, the SellerSoftware row is rolled back and that product is reported as `status=validation_failed` with `code=kb_namespace_provisioning_failed`.

**SoftwarePage Preview Tokens.** Identical contract to SellerOrgPage preview tokens (§26.7.6) with these adaptations:

- Preview URL: `https://sourcera.com/software/:slug?preview=<jwt>`.
- Token grants temporary access to the unpublished SoftwarePage AND the parent SellerOrgPage (transitively, so previewers can navigate the full vendor experience).
- Bulk preview: A `seller_org_admin` may issue a single bundled preview token covering all SoftwarePages owned by their Org for a multi-product launch (token TTL still 7 days; revocable per page or in bulk).

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Adversarial product theft.** Resolved by requiring source Org consent or 14-day silent-consent window plus Ops review.
2. **Acquired Org abandons before transfer completes.** 14-day TTL auto-escalates to Ops; Ops may infer consent from acquisition evidence even with no source-Org confirmation.
3. **Bulk-create exhausts plan limit mid-batch.** Partial-success semantics ensure successful rows persist; `entitlement_exceeded` returned for the overflow with an upgrade CTA in the response.
4. **KB namespace provisioning failure during bulk create.** Per-product rollback prevents orphaned SellerSoftware rows.
5. **SoftwarePage preview token shared publicly (e.g., Twitter).** `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` prevents indexing; `seller_org_admin` may revoke immediately.

## 26.9 SEO Requirements {#26.9-seo-requirements}

**Source:** Summary §6.15.4 (structured data, SEO moat); cross-references §4.4.10, §4.4.11, §4.4.12–§4.4.15.

SEO is a first-class architectural concern for all public Marketplace pages. Every page type (SellerOrgPage, SoftwarePage, CategoryPage, GuidePage, ComparisonPage, MarketIntelligenceReport) follows a unified SEO contract to maximize organic discoverability and maintain search-engine trust.

### 26.9.1 Schema.org Structured Data {#26.9.1-schema-org-structured-data}

Every public page emits a `<script type="application/ld+json">` block containing Schema.org structured data. The payload is cached in the entity's `schema_org_payload_json` field (≤ 20 000 chars) and regenerated on each publish event and by the nightly reconciliation worker (drift check: `updated_at > schema_org_payload_refreshed_at + 24h`).

| Page Type | Root Schema.org Type | Sub-Types Included | Source Fields |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| SellerOrgPage | `Organization` | `Offer` (if products listed), `AggregateRating` (if reviews available), `ContactPoint` | `hero_copy_markdown`, Seller Profile fields, published SellerSoftware list |
| SoftwarePage | `Product` | `Offer` (from `pricing_summary_markdown`), `AggregateRating`, `Brand` (parent Org) | `feature_highlights`, `pricing_summary_markdown`, SellerSoftware fields |
| CategoryPage | `CollectionPage` | `ItemList` (of `Product` entries) | Published SellerSoftware in category |
| ComparisonPage | `WebPage` | `ItemList` (of `Product` entries), `Table` | Feature highlights from participating products |
| GuidePage | `Article` | `Author` (Sourcera), `DatePublished`, `DateModified` | Guide body, publication timestamps |
| MarketIntelligenceReport | `Report` | `Author` (Sourcera), `DatePublished` | Report body, publication timestamps |

**Validation.** On publish, the `schema_org_payload_json` is validated against Google's Rich Results Test API (or equivalent offline validator). Validation failures block publish and return `schema_org_validation_failed` (Appendix I; HTTP 422) with a structured error listing the failing fields. Validation is non-blocking in staging environments.

### 26.9.2 Canonical URLs {#26.9.2-canonical-urls}

Every public page emits a `<link rel="canonical" href="...">` tag. Canonical URL rules:

- **SellerOrgPage:** `https://sourcera.com/sellers/{slug}`
- **SoftwarePage:** `https://sourcera.com/software/{slug}`
- **CategoryPage:** `https://sourcera.com/categories/{slug}`
- **ComparisonPage:** `https://sourcera.com/compare/{slug}`
- **GuidePage:** `https://sourcera.com/guides/{slug}`
- **MarketIntelligenceReport:** `https://sourcera.com/reports/{slug}`

Slug renames (pre-publication only, per §4.4.9 Slug Collision Rule) MUST update the canonical URL atomically with the slug change. Post-publication slug immutability means canonical URLs are stable for the life of the published page.

**301 Redirect Aliases.** When a page's slug is changed before publication and a previous slug was publicly crawled (detected via `seo_last_crawled_at IS NOT NULL`), a 301 redirect from the old slug to the new slug MUST be created. Redirect chains MUST NOT exceed depth 3 (per §4.5.4 Taxonomy Node redirect-chain constraint).

### 26.9.3 Sitemap Generation {#26.9.3-sitemap-generation}

Sourcera generates XML sitemaps per the Sitemaps Protocol (sitemaps.org). Sitemaps are regenerated daily and on-demand when a page publication event fires.

**Sitemap Structure.**

- `sourcera.com/sitemap-index.xml` — master index referencing per-type sitemaps.
- `sourcera.com/sitemaps/sellers.xml` — all published SellerOrgPages.
- `sourcera.com/sitemaps/software.xml` — all published SoftwarePages.
- `sourcera.com/sitemaps/categories.xml` — all published CategoryPages.
- `sourcera.com/sitemaps/comparisons.xml` — all published ComparisonPages.
- `sourcera.com/sitemaps/guides.xml` — all published GuidePages.
- `sourcera.com/sitemaps/reports.xml` — all published MarketIntelligenceReports.

Each sitemap entry includes `<loc>`, `<lastmod>` (from `last_published_at`), `<changefreq>` (weekly for seller/software pages, monthly for reports), and `<priority>` (0.8 for seller/software, 0.6 for categories/guides, 0.5 for comparisons/reports).

**Suppressed Pages.** Pages with `publication_status = suppressed_by_opt_out` are EXCLUDED from sitemaps. Pages with `publication_status = archived` are EXCLUDED from sitemaps and return HTTP 410 (see §26.9.5).

**Size Limits.** Per Sitemaps Protocol: max 50 000 URLs per sitemap file, max 50 MB uncompressed. If a type exceeds 50 000 entries, the sitemap is split into numbered files (`software-1.xml`, `software-2.xml`, etc.) and all are referenced from the sitemap index.

### 26.9.4 Robots.txt {#26.9.4-robots-txt}

`sourcera.com/robots.txt` content:

```
User-agent: *
Allow: /sellers/
Allow: /software/
Allow: /categories/
Allow: /compare/
Allow: /guides/
Allow: /reports/
Disallow: /app/
Disallow: /api/
Disallow: /admin/
Sitemap: https://sourcera.com/sitemap-index.xml
```

**Console Routes.** All buyer-console (`/app/buyer/`), seller-console (`/app/seller/`), and ops-console (`/admin/`) routes are disallowed. Only public Marketplace routes are crawlable.

**Crawl-Delay.** No `Crawl-delay` directive is set; rate limiting is handled at the CDN/WAF layer (§42 Infrastructure).

### 26.9.5 Vendor Opt-Out Honoring in SEO {#26.9.5-vendor-opt-out-honoring}

When a Vendor Opt-Out Record (§4.4.8) activates for a seller or product:

1. **Page suppression.** The affected SellerOrgPage or SoftwarePage transitions to `suppressed_by_opt_out` (§4.4.10 / §4.4.11 state machine). The public URL returns HTTP 200 with a placeholder body and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` header (NOT HTTP 404, to avoid recrawl thrash).
2. **Sitemap removal.** Suppressed pages are excluded from sitemaps on the next regeneration cycle (within 24h, or immediately on the on-demand trigger).
3. **Schema.org removal.** `schema_org_payload_json` is cleared on suppression; the nightly reconciliation worker confirms absence.
4. **Google Search Console deindex request.** For pages with `seo_indexed = true`, the system submits a URL removal request via the Search Console API within 24h of suppression. Authored Extension — requires human sign-off on whether Sourcera will have Search Console API access at launch.
5. **Comparison Page impact.** Opted-out products are redacted from Comparison Pages per §26.8.6 rule #2. If the opt-out causes the comparison to drop below 2 participants, the Comparison Page archives.

**Opt-Out Revocation.** When an opt-out is revoked, the page transitions back to `published`, is re-added to sitemaps, and `schema_org_payload_json` is regenerated. The `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` header is removed. Re-indexing is organic (no proactive submission; search engines recrawl based on sitemap `<lastmod>`).

### 26.9.6 SEO Status Tracking {#26.9.6-seo-status-tracking}

Each SellerSoftware row carries an `seo_status` field (§4.4.9) tracking the indexing lifecycle:

| Status | Meaning | Transition Trigger |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `not_indexed` | Page never indexed | Initial state |
| `indexing_pending` | Page published, awaiting first crawl | Publish event fires; sitemap updated |
| `indexed` | Page observed in Google Search Console index | Daily Search Console API poll confirms coverage |
| `deindexed_by_opt_out` | Page removed from index due to vendor opt-out | Opt-out activates; URL removal request submitted |
| `deindexed_manual` | Page manually deindexed by Ops | Ops action (e.g., content policy violation) |

`seo_last_crawled_at` is updated daily from Search Console API data. A page that has `seo_status = indexed` but `seo_last_crawled_at` is older than 30 days triggers a low-priority Ops alert (possible index coverage issue).

### 26.9.7 Open Graph & Social Card Meta Tags {#26.9.7-open-graph-and-social-card-meta-tags}

Schema.org structured data (§26.9.1) covers search-engine indexing. Open Graph (Facebook, LinkedIn) and Twitter Card meta tags cover social-share rendering — the rich preview cards that appear when a SellerOrgPage or SoftwarePage URL is pasted into LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Slack, Microsoft Teams, or iMessage. These cards are critical to the seller's organic-share virality loop (Summary §6.15.4 SEO moat) and MUST emit on every public page.

**Open Graph Tags (Required).**

| Tag | SellerOrgPage Source | SoftwarePage Source | Constraints |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `og:type` | `website` | `product` | Fixed per page type |
| `og:title` | `meta_title` (10–60 chars) | `meta_title` | Inherits `<title>` |
| `og:description` | `meta_description` (50–160 chars) | `meta_description` | Inherits meta description |
| `og:url` | Canonical URL (§26.9.2) | Canonical URL | HTTPS required |
| `og:image` | `og_image_url` if non-null; else generated default (`/sellers/:slug/og-image.png`) | Same | 1200×630 px recommended; 600×315 px minimum; ≤ 8 MB |
| `og:image:width` | 1200 | 1200 | Static |
| `og:image:height` | 630 | 630 | Static |
| `og:image:alt` | Generated from `meta_title` | Generated from `meta_title` | ≤ 200 chars; required for a11y |
| `og:site_name` | "Sourcera" | "Sourcera" | Static |
| `og:locale` | `en_US` (v1) | `en_US` (v1) | i18n deferred (§26.9.9) |

**Twitter Card Tags (Required).**

| Tag | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| `twitter:card` | `summary_large_image` |
| `twitter:site` | `@sourcera` |
| `twitter:creator` | `@sourcera` for Sourcera-owned content (CategoryPage, GuidePage, etc.); seller-supplied `twitter_handle` field on SellerOrgPage if provided (Authored Extension — adds optional `twitter_handle` String field to SellerOrgPage and SoftwarePage entities, ≤ 16 chars matching `^@[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,15}$`; flagged for human sign-off) |
| `twitter:title` | `meta_title` |
| `twitter:description` | `meta_description` |
| `twitter:image` | Same image as `og:image` |
| `twitter:image:alt` | Same alt text as `og:image:alt` |

**Default OG Image Generation.** When a seller does not supply `og_image_url`, the system MUST generate a default OG image at `/sellers/:slug/og-image.png` containing:

- Seller logo (centered, max 400px height)
- Seller name (sans-serif, 56px, brand-neutral)
- Verification badge (Basic / Verified / Certified)
- Sourcera wordmark in lower-right corner (16px, low-contrast)

For SoftwarePages, the generated image substitutes the product logo, product name, and parent vendor name. Generation is deferred to a `cf_workers/og_image_generator` edge function (Authored Extension — depends on the Vercel `@vercel/og` library or equivalent satori-based renderer). Images are cached at the CDN for 7 days per §26.7.6 cache contract.

**Validation.** OG / Twitter Card tags MUST validate against the Open Graph Object Debugger and Twitter Card Validator before publish. Validation is performed by an offline validator (`@sourcera/social-card-linter` — Authored Extension; flagged) on publish. Failures block publish with `social_card_validation_failed` (Appendix I; HTTP 422). Validation is non-blocking in staging.

**Format Enum.** `social_card_format` registered in Appendix J: `og_facebook`, `twitter_summary`, `twitter_summary_large_image`, `linkedin` (LinkedIn shares the OG protocol; included for analytics granularity).

### 26.9.8 Breadcrumb Structured Data {#26.9.8-breadcrumb-structured-data}

Every public page deeper than the homepage MUST emit a Schema.org `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD payload alongside the primary structured data block (§26.9.1). Breadcrumbs improve Google Search Console rich-result eligibility and click-through rates.

**Breadcrumb Trails.**

| Page Type | Breadcrumb Trail |
| :---- | :---- |
| SellerOrgPage | Home → Sellers → {Seller Name} |
| SoftwarePage | Home → Software → {Category Name} → {Product Name} |
| CategoryPage | Home → Categories → {Category Name} |
| ComparisonPage | Home → Compare → {Comparison Name} |
| GuidePage | Home → Guides → {Guide Title} |
| MarketIntelligenceReport | Home → Reports → {Report Title} |

**Visual Rendering.** Breadcrumbs MUST also render visually above the page hero (text links separated by `›`) for human navigation. Visual breadcrumbs MUST share the same source data as the JSON-LD payload (single source of truth, no drift).

**Cache Behavior.** Breadcrumb JSON-LD is included in the same `<script type="application/ld+json">` block as the primary structured data (a JSON-LD `@graph` array). It inherits the cache key and refresh cadence of the primary payload (§26.9.1).

### 26.9.9 Internationalization & Localization (Deferred Scope) {#26.9.9-internationalization-and-localization-deferred-scope}

**v7.0.0 scope:** All public Marketplace pages render in `en-US` only. The `og:locale` tag is fixed at `en_US`; `<html lang="en">` is hardcoded; no `hreflang` tags are emitted.

**Forward Compatibility.** Entity definitions for SellerOrgPage (§4.4.10), SoftwarePage (§4.4.11), CategoryPage (§4.4.12), GuidePage (§4.4.13), and ComparisonPage (§4.4.14) reserve a future `locale` Enum field (default `en-US`) and a future `localized_variants_json` JSON field for translated content. These fields are NOT created in v7.0.0 — Authored Extension flagged for v7.x i18n RFC.

**Deferred Items (Tracked in Roadmap, NOT Implemented in v7.0.0).**

1. `hreflang` link tag emission for multi-locale pages.
2. Locale-specific canonical URLs (`/sellers/:slug?locale=de-DE` or `/de/sellers/:slug` — URL pattern TBD).
3. Locale-specific OG / Twitter Card images (translated overlays).
4. Currency localization in `pricing_summary_markdown` (currently USD-only).
5. Schema.org `inLanguage` field emission on Article / Report types.
6. RTL (right-to-left) layout support.

**Migration Contract.** When i18n ships, existing v7.0.0 pages will be migrated by setting `locale = 'en-US'` on all rows and treating the existing content as the "primary" variant. No content loss; no SEO equity loss (canonical URLs unchanged in the en-US variant).

### 26.9.10 Page Accessibility & Core Web Vitals {#26.9.10-page-accessibility-and-core-web-vitals}

Public Marketplace pages MUST meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards and Google's Core Web Vitals (CWV) thresholds. Accessibility is both a legal compliance requirement (§44 Compliance) and an SEO ranking factor.

**WCAG 2.1 AA Requirements (Public Pages).**

| Criterion | Requirement | Verification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Color contrast | Body text ≥ 4.5:1 contrast against background; large text (18pt+) ≥ 3:1 | Automated via axe-core in CI; manual review on publish |
| Image alt text | Every `<img>` MUST have `alt` attribute; decorative images use `alt=""` | `body_sections_json` validator rejects images without alt; default OG images use generated alt |
| Heading hierarchy | One `<h1>` per page; no skipped levels (no `<h2>` directly inside `<h4>`) | Markdown renderer validates structure; serializer test in QA suite |
| Keyboard navigation | All interactive elements (CTAs, navigation, breadcrumbs) reachable via Tab; visible focus indicator | Manual audit per page type at v7.0.0 launch; automated via Playwright a11y tests |
| ARIA landmarks | `<header>`, `<main>`, `<footer>`, `<nav>` regions semantically marked | HTML template enforced |
| Language attribute | `<html lang="en">` set | Static (until i18n; §26.9.9) |
| Skip-to-content link | Visible-on-focus skip link at top of every page | HTML template includes |
| Form labels | All form fields (e.g., contact form) have associated `<label>` | Component-library enforced |

**Core Web Vitals Thresholds (75th Percentile, Mobile).**

| Metric | Target | Hard Failure | Measurement |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) | ≤ 2.5s | > 4.0s | RUM via Vercel Speed Insights or equivalent (§42.4); per-page-type aggregation |
| First Input Delay (FID) / Interaction to Next Paint (INP) | ≤ 200ms (INP) | > 500ms | RUM |
| Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) | ≤ 0.1 | > 0.25 | RUM |
| First Contentful Paint (FCP) | ≤ 1.8s | > 3.0s | RUM |
| Time to First Byte (TTFB) | ≤ 600ms (cached); ≤ 1 200ms (uncached) | > 1 800ms | Edge logs |

**Hard-Failure Action.** If 14 consecutive days of RUM data show > 25% of sessions for a given page type exceed any "Hard Failure" threshold, an Ops alert fires. Sustained CWV degradation (90 days) triggers a Performance Incident (§38) and pages the on-call engineer.

**Performance Budgets (Enforced at Build Time).**

| Asset Type | Budget |
| :---- | :---- |
| Initial HTML payload | ≤ 50 KB (gzipped) |
| Initial JS bundle (above-the-fold critical) | ≤ 80 KB (gzipped) |
| Inline CSS (critical path) | ≤ 14 KB (uncompressed; one TCP packet) |
| Hero image (`og_image_url` rendered above-the-fold) | ≤ 200 KB; AVIF or WebP preferred; JPEG/PNG fallback |
| Total page weight (above-the-fold) | ≤ 500 KB |
| Total page weight (full page, including below-the-fold lazy assets) | ≤ 2 MB |

Build-time budget enforcement: a CI check using `bundlesize` or equivalent fails the build if a budget is exceeded by > 5%. Ops may grant a temporary waiver via a feature-flag override.

**Image Optimization.** All images served from `sourcera.com/sellers/*` and `sourcera.com/software/*` MUST be:

1. Served via the Vercel Image Optimization API (or equivalent) at the edge.
2. Returned in AVIF format if the client supports it; WebP if AVIF not supported; JPEG/PNG otherwise.
3. Responsive: served at viewport-appropriate sizes via `<img srcset>` and `<picture>` elements.
4. Lazy-loaded (`loading="lazy"`) for below-the-fold images.
5. Eager-loaded (`loading="eager"` + `fetchpriority="high"`) for above-the-fold hero / OG imagery.

**Accessibility Audit Cadence.** A full WCAG 2.1 AA audit MUST be performed:

- Once at v7.0.0 launch (manual + automated).
- Quarterly via Lighthouse CI on a sampled subset (≥ 50 pages per page type).
- Ad-hoc on any page-template change (e.g., new hero section variant).

Audit findings are tracked in the Ops Console under a `page_a11y_finding` table (Authored Extension — entity definition deferred to a v7.1 spec increment; flagged).

## 26.10 Acceptance Criteria (Extended) {#26.10-acceptance-criteria-extended}

The following acceptance criteria extend §26.6 to cover §26.7–§26.9. Each criterion is numbered, testable, and scope-bound.

**Seller Organization Pages (§26.7).**

1. A SellerOrgPage MUST NOT be publishable if the Seller Org has zero published Capability Declarations AND zero published SellerSoftware entities. Attempting to publish returns `seller_org_page_requires_content` (Appendix I; HTTP 409).
2. Page enrichment via `page_enrichment` MUST complete within 5 minutes for target sites with ≤ 50 crawlable pages; AIOperation outcome is `accepted` on success or `rejected` on any failure mode in §26.7.2.
3. The split-pane enrichment review editor MUST render the current page alongside the enrichment draft with per-section Accept / Edit / Reject controls.
4. Re-enrichment MUST be rate-limited to once per 7 calendar days per SellerOrgPage; attempts within the window return `seller_org_page_enrichment_rate_limited` (Appendix I; HTTP 429).
5. Domain verification loss MUST cascade to page suppression within 15 minutes (measured via the `vendor_opt_out.applied` webhook chain per §4.4.10 AC #2).
6. `seller_marketing_editor` role MUST be able to edit content fields but MUST NOT be able to publish or archive the page (publish/archive transitions restricted to `seller_org_admin`).
7. Published SellerOrgPages MUST appear in §27.3 Marketplace Search full-text index within 60 seconds of publication.

**SellerSoftware & Software Pages (§26.8).**

8. Creating a SellerSoftware beyond the plan-tier limit (§34.1) MUST return `entitlement_exceeded` (Appendix I; HTTP 402) with an upgrade CTA.
9. Claim verification via DNS TXT MUST resolve within 72 hours of the seller adding the record; polling interval ≤ 5 minutes.
10. Two concurrent claims for the same SellerSoftware from different Orgs MUST both transition to `claim_disputed` (per §4.4.9 state machine); neither Org may edit until Ops resolves.
11. Publishing a SoftwarePage whose parent SellerSoftware has `claim_status != claim_verified` MUST be rejected with `seller_software_page_requires_verified_claim` (Appendix I; HTTP 409).
12. SoftwarePage publication MUST additionally require a published SellerOrgPage (or verified Seller Profile claim) for the parent Org's domain ownership verification.
13. KB namespace auto-creation on SellerSoftware creation MUST complete synchronously (visible in the response payload).
14. KB namespace migration on SellerSoftware soft-delete MUST complete within 5 minutes (observable via `kb_namespace_migration` audit event).
15. `feature_highlights` on SoftwarePages MUST render in Comparison Page columns; unmatched highlights MUST appear in an "Other Features" section.
16. Reducing the participant count of a Comparison Page below 2 (via claim revocation, opt-out, or soft-delete) MUST archive the Comparison Page within 60 seconds.

**SEO (§26.9).**

17. Every published page (SellerOrgPage, SoftwarePage, CategoryPage, GuidePage, ComparisonPage, MarketIntelligenceReport) MUST emit valid Schema.org structured data in `<script type="application/ld+json">`. Validation against Google Rich Results Test API (or offline equivalent) MUST pass; failures block publish with `schema_org_validation_failed` (Appendix I; HTTP 422).
18. Every published page MUST emit a `<link rel="canonical">` tag matching the canonical URL pattern in §26.9.2.
19. Sitemaps MUST be regenerated within 24 hours of any page publication event; each sitemap MUST conform to the Sitemaps Protocol (max 50 000 URLs, max 50 MB uncompressed).
20. `robots.txt` MUST disallow `/app/`, `/api/`, `/admin/` and MUST allow `/sellers/`, `/software/`, `/categories/`, `/compare/`, `/guides/`, `/reports/`.
21. Suppressed pages (`publication_status = suppressed_by_opt_out`) MUST return HTTP 200 with `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` (NOT HTTP 404); MUST be excluded from sitemaps; MUST have `schema_org_payload_json` cleared.
22. Archived pages (`publication_status = archived`) MUST return HTTP 410; MUST be excluded from sitemaps.
23. 301 redirect aliases for pre-publication slug changes MUST be created when the old slug was previously crawled (`seo_last_crawled_at IS NOT NULL`); redirect chain depth MUST NOT exceed 3.
24. Pages with `seo_status = indexed` and `seo_last_crawled_at` older than 30 days MUST trigger a low-priority Ops alert.
25. Vendor opt-out activation MUST trigger sitemap exclusion within 24 hours and Google Search Console URL removal request within 24 hours (for pages with `seo_indexed = true`).

**Edge Caching, Anti-Scraping & Preview (§26.7.6).**

26. Every state-machine transition that mutates the public projection of a SellerOrgPage or SoftwarePage MUST emit a `page_cache_purge` event consumed by the CDN purge worker; affected URLs MUST be purged from the CDN within 60 seconds at p95 (300 seconds at p99).
27. After 5 retry failures, a `page_cache_purge` event MUST land in the DLQ and trigger an Ops on-call page; manual Ops purge MUST occur within 30 minutes to maintain the §26.9.5 opt-out honoring SLA.
28. Per-IP rate limits on `/sellers/:slug` and `/software/:slug` MUST cap anonymous requests at 60 req/min (burst 30); exceeding requests return HTTP 429 with `Retry-After: 60`.
29. Verified Googlebot, Bingbot, DuckDuckBot, Yandex, and Baidu (FCrDNS-confirmed) MUST be exempt from per-IP scrape rate limits; spoofed bot User-Agents that fail FCrDNS MUST be subject to standard anonymous limits and logged to the §3.5 abuse signal table.
30. SellerOrgPage preview tokens MUST expire after 7 days; expired tokens MUST return HTTP 410 with `seller_org_page_preview_token_expired`; preview-mode renders MUST emit `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`.
31. A `seller_org_admin` MUST be able to revoke all outstanding preview tokens for a SellerOrgPage by flushing the JWT key version; revocation MUST take effect within 60 seconds at the edge.

**Product Transfer, Bulk Operations & Preview (§26.8.7).**

32. A SellerSoftware Transfer Request MUST require either explicit consent from the source Seller Org's `seller_org_admin` OR Ops review after a 14-day silent-consent window; transfers MUST NOT proceed without one of these conditions.
33. On approved transfer, the SellerSoftware `slug` and SoftwarePage `slug` MUST be preserved (no canonical URL change); KB namespace MUST migrate to the acquiring Org's namespace tree per KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4 within 5 minutes; `claim_status` MUST reset to `claim_pending` requiring re-verification.
34. Capability Declarations on a transferred SellerSoftware MUST NOT auto-transfer; the transfer wizard MUST prompt the acquiring Org to clone-and-claim or drop references; the choice MUST be logged in audit.
35. Transfers MAY be reversed by Ops within 30 days for failed claim re-verification or post-hoc dispute with new evidence; after 30 days, transfers MUST require a fresh Transfer Request in the opposite direction.
36. The `POST /api/v1/seller/software/bulk` endpoint MUST accept up to 50 products per request, MUST require an `Idempotency-Key` header (24h replay window), and MUST require `seller_org_admin` (NOT `seller_marketing_editor`).
37. Bulk-create MUST follow partial-success semantics: when at least one product is created, the response is HTTP 200 with per-product status; when all products fail validation, HTTP 422 with `seller_software_bulk_create_total_failure`.
38. KB namespace provisioning failure on any product within a bulk-create batch MUST roll back that SellerSoftware row (per-product transactionality) and report `code=kb_namespace_provisioning_failed`; sibling products MUST proceed independently.

**Open Graph, Social Cards & Breadcrumbs (§26.9.7, §26.9.8).**

39. Every published SellerOrgPage and SoftwarePage MUST emit the full set of Required Open Graph tags (§26.9.7 Open Graph Tags table) and Required Twitter Card tags (Twitter Card Tags table); validation against `@sourcera/social-card-linter` MUST pass; failures block publish with `social_card_validation_failed` (Appendix I; HTTP 422).
40. When a seller does not supply `og_image_url`, the system MUST generate a default OG image at `/sellers/:slug/og-image.png` (1200×630 px, ≤ 200 KB) containing the seller logo, name, and verification badge; the generated image MUST be cached at the CDN for 7 days.
41. Every public page deeper than the homepage MUST emit Schema.org `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD inline within the primary `<script type="application/ld+json">` block AND render visual breadcrumbs above the page hero; visual and JSON-LD breadcrumbs MUST share the same source data.

**Internationalization Deferral (§26.9.9).**

42. v7.0.0 MUST emit `<html lang="en">` and `og:locale=en_US` on all public pages; `hreflang` tags MUST NOT be emitted; locale-specific URL variants MUST NOT be exposed.

**Page Accessibility & Core Web Vitals (§26.9.10).**

43. Every published SellerOrgPage and SoftwarePage MUST meet WCAG 2.1 AA: every `<img>` MUST have an `alt` attribute, color contrast MUST be ≥ 4.5:1 for body text, heading hierarchy MUST not skip levels, all interactive elements MUST be keyboard-reachable with visible focus, and the page MUST include a skip-to-content link.
44. RUM data (75th percentile, mobile) for each page type MUST meet Core Web Vitals targets: LCP ≤ 2.5s, INP ≤ 200ms, CLS ≤ 0.1, FCP ≤ 1.8s, TTFB ≤ 600ms cached / 1 200ms uncached.
45. Build-time performance budgets MUST be enforced via CI: initial HTML ≤ 50 KB gzipped, initial JS ≤ 80 KB gzipped, hero image ≤ 200 KB AVIF/WebP preferred, total above-the-fold weight ≤ 500 KB; budgets exceeded by > 5% MUST fail the build.

**Sitemap Build Atomicity (§26.9.3).**

46. **Sitemap atomicity — no partial artifact is ever crawler-visible.** The sitemap generation job MUST write the full sitemap (and every referenced sitemap-index child) to an immutable staging prefix (`sitemap-builds/{build_id}/…`), validate the artifact end-to-end (URL count ≤ 50 000, file size ≤ 50 MB uncompressed, XML schema-validates against the Sitemaps Protocol, every URL MUST resolve to a `publication_status=published` row at build-time evaluation, no opted-out URL is present), and then atomically swap the `sitemap.xml` and `sitemap_index.xml` public pointers to the new build ONLY on successful validation. A build that fails any validation gate MUST leave the prior sitemap in place and emit `sitemap_build_validation_failed` (Appendix G PostHog event) with the failing gate and URL-count delta. Partially written artifacts MUST NOT be servable from the public sitemap endpoint; the public endpoint's ETag / `Last-Modified` headers MUST update only on atomic swap. CI test `sitemap_atomic_swap_integrity` asserts that under simulated mid-build process termination, the public sitemap endpoint serves the prior-build artifact unchanged (no 5xx, no half-written XML, no opted-out URLs). Operational observability: the `sitemap_build_duration_ms`, `sitemap_build_validation_outcome`, and `sitemap_atomic_swap_at` PostHog events are emitted per build; a rolling alert fires if two consecutive builds fail validation.

# 27\. Vendor Discovery & RFP Marketplace {#27.-vendor-discovery-&-rfp-marketplace}

## 27.1 Purpose {#27.1-purpose}

The Marketplace is a curated directory where buyers discover vendors and vendors discover evaluation opportunities. It is physically separate from both the Buyer and Seller Consoles — a neutral domain with its own access control rules.

## 27.2 Availability {#27.2-availability}

Marketplace plan-tier gating is authoritative in §34.1.1 cell **Marketplace Buyer Access** (Buyer side) and §34.1.2 cell **Proactive Marketplace EOIs** (Seller side). This subsection summarizes the resulting capability surface:

| Plan tier (per §34.1) | Buyer Access | Seller Access |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Free | Browse only (per §34.1.1) | Profile + Capability Declarations visible (per §34.1.2 Published Seller Profile) |
| Starter | Search + capability filter (per §34.1.1) | Proactive EOIs: 10/month (per §34.1.2) |
| Growth | Full + match scoring (per §34.1.1) | Proactive EOIs: Unlimited (per §34.1.2) |
| Scale | Full + match scoring (per §34.1.1) | Proactive EOIs: Unlimited (per §34.1.2) |
| Enterprise | Full + batch match API (per §34.1.1) | Proactive EOIs: Unlimited + API (per §34.1.2) |

## 27.3 Marketplace Search & Filtering {#27.3-marketplace-search-&-filtering}

**Filters:**

- Vendor name (text search, fuzzy match)  
- Industry (multi-select from controlled vocabulary)  
- Location / region (multi-select)  
- Certification (multi-select: SOC2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR, etc.)  
- **Capability:** Filter by declared capabilities (e.g., "SAML SSO", "Kubernetes Support"). Shows vendor count per capability.  
- Verification tier (checkbox: Basic, Verified, Certified)

**Listing display:**

- Vendor logo (48x48px)  
- Vendor name (bold, 16px)  
- Company description (2 lines, truncated)  
- Key certifications (badges)  
- Capability tags (max 5 visible, expandable)  
- Verification tier badge  
- "View Profile" button

**Sort order:** Relevance (default), Verification Tier (Certified first), Recently Active, Alphabetical.

## 27.4 Marketplace Match Score {#27.4-marketplace-match-score}

When a buyer publishes a Marketplace Listing (or opens a buyer-console surface that presents candidate vendors — the EOI queue, the palette L7 suggestion stream, the Marketplace search result list, the EOI acceptance confirmation dialog, the Command Palette Marketplace suggestion slice), the Marketplace computes and renders a **Match Score** for each candidate Seller Org / SellerSoftware pair relative to the buyer's authored Workspace and Listing. The score is a ranking instrument — not a scoring-math output, not a vendor grade — and is distinct from the Sourcera Method's `grade × weight` math (§10) which operates on vendor responses, not vendor candidacy.

### 27.4.1 Model Summary and Authority

Per **Summary C.61**, the Match Score is produced by a learned ranking model whose input features span Capability Declaration overlap, Seller verification tier, KB freshness, historical response quality, and category fit, with the feature list maintained in a versioned registry and weights refit on a rolling retraining window. The v6.0.0 keyword-intersection formula (old §27.4) is **superseded** at v7.0.0 and preserved only in §27.4.8 as the Legacy Baseline reference implementation (used as the v1 cold-start model and as a denominator for model-lift evaluation). This overwrite is logged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` → Summary-Overrides-Spec Log.

Authority precedence for this subsection:
- **Feature registry, retraining cadence, and free/paid rendering rules:** Summary C.61 → this subsection → `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §13.2` (for KB-freshness feature computation).
- **Billing and entitlement for numeric score exposure:** §21.4.2 `match_score_numeric` + §5.11 Feature Access Matrix + §34.1 Plan Tier Definitions + BPS §3 / SPS §9.
- **Teaser loop and label rendering:** §48.2.11 L10 Marketplace Match-Score Teaser.
- **Abuse / dispute path for score complaints:** §27.8 Marketplace Abuse & Takedown → §4.5.7 Marketplace Abuse Report.

### 27.4.2 Computation Surfaces and Triggers

A Match Score is materialized under exactly three trigger classes; no other code path may mint a score:

| Trigger Class | Trigger Event | Scoring Unit | Caching TTL | Cache Invalidators |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Listing-Publish** | Buyer publishes Marketplace Listing (§4.5.1 `state → active`) | `(marketplace_listing_id, seller_software_id)` pair, for all SellerSoftware rows whose `marketplace_category_id` ∈ the Listing's target categories | 24 hours from compute; refreshed on any `taxonomy.*`, `vendor_opt_out.applied`, `capability_declaration.updated`, or `marketplace_listing.updated` webhook | Any listed webhook; Listing edit; Seller Profile edit; Capability Declaration publish/deprecation |
| **EOI-Review** | Seller submits EOI (§4.5.2); buyer opens EOI queue | `(eoi_record_id)`, single-pair | 1 hour from compute | EOI revision; Listing edit; Capability Declaration edit |
| **On-Demand** | Buyer invokes `match_score_numeric` Agent capability (§21.4.2) with explicit `(workspace_id, seller_software_id)` | `(workspace_id, seller_software_id)` single-pair | No cache (always fresh; one AIOperation per invocation) | N/A (fresh compute) |

Each materialized score writes to a `MarketplaceMatchScoreSnapshot` row (authored in §27.4.9) with full feature-vector provenance so the render-time surface can cite the underlying features without recomputing.

### 27.4.3 Feature Registry — v7.0.0 Seed

The feature set is an Ops-managed registry (`MarketplaceMatchFeatureRegistry`, a new platform-scoped entity authored under §4.5.9 in the follow-on integration phase; the seed content lives here). Every feature row carries the fields listed in the table below; the registry is versioned and a new model-version invocation carries a frozen snapshot of the feature list it was trained on, so feature-set drift is observable end-to-end.

| `feature_id` | Name | Type | Source Entity | Freshness Requirement | Weight Mode | Null Handling |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `capability_declaration_overlap_ratio` | Capability Declaration Overlap Ratio | continuous (0.0–1.0) | Capability Declaration (§26.3) ↔ Workspace Requirement titles + descriptions ↔ Listing category target | ≤ 24h since the most recent Capability Declaration update on the seller; recompute on `capability_declaration.updated` | learned | Null only when seller has zero published Capability Declarations; treated as 0.0 with `null_sentinel_flag=true`; feature importance dampened by 50% in ensemble |
| `capability_declaration_recency_days` | Days Since Last Capability Declaration Update | continuous (0–∞, clipped at 730) | Capability Declaration `updated_at` (max over the seller's active declarations) | Live (recomputed per invocation) | learned | Null only on fresh seller (zero declarations); imputed with 730 (worst-case) + `null_sentinel_flag=true` |
| `verification_tier_ordinal` | Seller Verification Tier (Ordinal) | ordinal (1=basic, 2=verified, 3=certified) | Seller Profile `verification_tier` (§26.1; Appendix J `seller_verification_tiers`) | Live (verification state is strongly consistent) | static prior (see §27.4.4) then learned residual | Never null; default = 1 (`basic`) for newly provisioned sellers |
| `kb_freshness_score` | KB Freshness Score | continuous (0.0–1.0) | Seller KB (KB Spec §13.2): fraction of KB entries cited in the last 12 months whose `verified_at` is within their staleness window per the §21.4.2 `kb_staleness_classifier` | ≤ 24h from classifier last-run; nightly recompute | learned | Null when seller has < 10 KB entries; imputed at population-median 0.45 + `null_sentinel_flag=true` |
| `historical_response_quality_score` | Historical Response Quality Score | continuous (0.0–1.0) | Derived from completed Bid Workspaces (§4.4 bid_workspace): weighted blend of (a) buyer-reported `vendor_response_quality_rating` (§19.4), (b) grade-outcome lift over category cohort mean, (c) grade-append-only revision delta (stability) | ≤ 7d from last completed bid in the seller's cohort; weekly recompute | learned | Null when seller has zero completed bids platform-wide; imputed at platform-median 0.50 + `null_sentinel_flag=true`; dampened 60% in ensemble for cold-start sellers |
| `category_fit_score` | Category Fit Score | continuous (0.0–1.0) | Marketplace Category (§4.4.7) set intersection: (Listing's target categories) ∩ (SellerSoftware's primary + secondary categories), normalized by union size; includes parent-category transitive fit at 0.6 weight | Live (recomputed per invocation; Category FKs are strongly consistent) | learned | Never null; 0.0 when no category intersection exists (including through parent chain); a 0.0 floor result in 27.4.6 still emits the score but the surface MAY filter at threshold 0.05 |
| `industry_match_score` | Industry Match Score | continuous (0.0–1.0) | Seller Profile `industries[]` ↔ Workspace `industry` (when buyer authored one); alias-aware via Taxonomy Node `aliases` (§4.5.4) | ≤ 24h on Seller Profile edits | learned | Null when buyer Workspace has no `industry` set; imputed at 0.5 (neutral) + `null_sentinel_flag=true`; feature-importance dampened 40% |
| `certification_match_score` | Certification Match Score | continuous (0.0–1.0) | Intersection of Seller Profile `certifications[]` and Listing's declared `certification_requirements[]` (or Workspace-authored required certifications if Listing omits); normalized by count of required | ≤ 24h on Seller Profile edits | learned | Null when no certifications are required; imputed at 1.0 (non-blocking) + `null_sentinel_flag=true` |
| `region_match_score` | Region Match Score | continuous (0.0–1.0) | Seller Profile `locations[]` ↔ Listing `target_regions[]`; data residency compatibility is gated separately (see `residency_compatible_flag` below) | ≤ 24h on Seller Profile edits | learned | Null when Listing does not specify `target_regions`; imputed at 1.0 (non-blocking) + `null_sentinel_flag=true` |
| `residency_compatible_flag` | Data Residency Compatibility | binary (0/1) | Seller Org's `data_residency_region` ↔ Listing buyer Org's `data_residency_region` per §40.1; non-compatible pair → 0 | Live (residency assignment is strongly consistent) | **static hard gate**: 0 multiplies the final score by 0 (entire score = 0) and emits `residency_incompatible=true` in provenance | Never null; defaults to 1 when both sides have matching `data_residency_region`; when Listing is `residency_scope=global`, flag always = 1 |
| `seller_active_load_factor` | Seller Active Load Factor | continuous (0.0–1.0) | Count of the seller's in-flight Bid Workspaces (`status ∈ {draft, active, submitted}`) as a percentile within the seller's plan tier cohort; 1.0 = p95 saturated, 0.0 = idle | ≤ 24h recompute | learned (with negative coefficient expected: higher load ≈ lower responsiveness) | Never null; 0.0 for a seller with zero in-flight bids |
| `eoi_response_velocity_days` | EOI Response Velocity (Days, p50) | continuous (0–∞, clipped at 30) | Seller's median time-to-first-response on accepted EOIs over the rolling 180-day window | ≤ 24h recompute | learned (negative coefficient: slower = worse) | Null on cold-start sellers (< 3 historical EOIs); imputed at platform-median 2.5 days + `null_sentinel_flag=true`; dampened 50% |
