| `bid_submission_conversion_rate` | Bid Submission Conversion Rate | continuous (0.0–1.0) | Over the rolling 180-day window: fraction of accepted EOIs that led to a `bid_workspace.status=submitted` (i.e., the seller showed up) | ≤ 24h recompute | learned | Null on cold-start sellers (< 3 historical acceptances); imputed at platform-median 0.72 + `null_sentinel_flag=true`; dampened 50% |
| `kb_to_capability_linkage_ratio` | KB-to-Capability Linkage Ratio | continuous (0.0–1.0) | Fraction of the seller's active Capability Declarations that cite ≥ 1 KB entry as evidence (per §26.3) | ≤ 24h recompute on KB / Capability Declaration edits | learned (positive coefficient: declarations backed by evidence score higher) | Null when seller has zero Capability Declarations; imputed at 0.0 + `null_sentinel_flag=true` |
| `listing_category_priors_score` | Listing-Category Prior Score | continuous (0.0–1.0) | Category-level prior: for the Listing's primary category, the historical median Match Score of accepted EOIs for this seller (self-lift signal); computed from `MarketplaceMatchScoreSnapshot` + `EOIAcceptanceRecord` joins | Weekly recompute | learned | Null when the seller has never been accepted from this category; imputed at population-median 0.50 + `null_sentinel_flag=true` |
| `vendor_opt_out_effective_flag` | Vendor Opt-Out Effective Flag | binary (0/1) | §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Record scope-resolution outcome for the Seller Org at Listing-publish time or EOI-review time | **static hard gate**: 1 → final score suppressed AND the candidate row is removed from render per §4.5.6 render contract | n/a (hard gate) | Never null; 0 when no effective opt-out; 1 when any effective opt-out covers the rendering surface |
| `abuse_report_pending_suppression` | Abuse-Report Pending Suppression | binary (0/1) | 1 when an active Marketplace Abuse Report (§4.5.7) against this Seller Org or SellerSoftware has severity ∈ {`high`, `critical`} AND `ops_status ∈ {pending_review, awaiting_seller_response, escalated}` | **static soft gate**: 1 → render the candidate with a provenance note `under_review`; numeric scoring suppressed on buyer-facing surfaces (qualitative label falls back to `insufficient_signal`) | n/a (soft gate) | Never null; default 0 |
| `ghost_bid_coverage_ratio` | Ghost-Bid Coverage Ratio | continuous (0.0–1.0) | Fraction of the Listing's target category terms that the seller's Ghost-Bid Importer (§4.4.17) corpus covers | Weekly recompute | learned | Null when seller has not used Ghost-Bid Importer; imputed 0.3 + `null_sentinel_flag=true` |

**Feature-registry invariants.** (i) A feature may be added only via an Ops Console write authored by `ops_taxonomy_admin` (new Marketplace-Match-Registry scope attached — authored extension). (ii) A feature's `weight_mode` transitioning from `learned` → `static` is blocked mid-model-version — requires a new model-version publication. (iii) All continuous features are winsorized at the 1%/99% quantile at training time and linearly scaled to `[0,1]` at inference; provenance carries the raw and scaled values. (iv) Null-imputed values MUST carry a `null_sentinel_flag` in the feature vector (model trained with the flag as an additional column so it can learn to discount imputations).

### 27.4.4 Weightings, Hard Gates, and Fallbacks

Per Summary C.61, the ranking model is a **learned ensemble** — per-feature weights are not hand-tuned at v7.0.0 steady state. The model type is a gradient-boosted decision tree (GBDT) with logistic output in `[0,1]`, trained against the target `ensemble_target` defined in §27.4.5. Two categories of non-learned logic remain:

1. **Hard gates (static).** `residency_compatible_flag=0` and `vendor_opt_out_effective_flag=1` short-circuit the score to 0 regardless of all other feature values. No model weight can override. The surface's render contract honors these gates even if a stale cached score pre-dates the gate flip (see §27.4.7 cache invalidation).
2. **Cold-start fallback (v1 baseline).** When the ensemble model version is marked `cold_start` (i.e., insufficient training data for a new model epoch), the Legacy Baseline (§27.4.8) is used as the score source. The Legacy Baseline uses the v6 keyword-intersection formula as a static prior over `capability_declaration_overlap_ratio` and `category_fit_score`, weighted 0.6 and 0.4 respectively, with all other features ignored. Cold-start duration ≤ 90 days from platform launch in any new data-residency region.

Learned weights are **not published to any customer surface**. The provenance panel (§27.4.6) exposes feature values and a contribution indicator (SHAP-style local attribution: positive/negative arrow, three-bucket magnitude) but NEVER the underlying weight magnitudes — weight leakage would expose adversarial-gaming surface. QA test `match_score_weight_non_exposure` asserts that no surface (HTML, JSON API, Schema.org payload, PostHog event property, error response) exposes the weight vector.

### 27.4.5 Retraining Cadence and Model Versioning

| Retraining Dimension | Cadence | Trigger Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Full model refit** (all weights re-learned from scratch) | Quarterly (90 days, aligned to calendar quarters) | Drift alert AND ≥ 10,000 new labeled examples since last full refit; OR explicit Ops publish | Requires Marketing + Applied-ML dual sign-off for publish |
| **Incremental epoch** (warm-start refit on rolling training window) | Every 14 days (biweekly) | Rolling window of the last 180 days of `EOIAcceptanceRecord` outcomes, `vendor_response_quality_rating` signals, and explicit feedback reports | Auto-published if offline-eval metrics within the per-metric guardrails below |
| **Feature-registry bump** (new or removed feature) | On-demand | Ops Console edit to `MarketplaceMatchFeatureRegistry` | Requires a full model refit at the next cadence; interim retains prior feature set |
| **Emergency patch** (hot fix) | On-demand | P1 drift alert OR P1 abuse-gaming alert from SIM (Summary C.100) | Ops can push a patched model version outside cadence with dual sign-off; auto-rollback if post-deploy eval metrics regress |

**Target label.** The ensemble target `ensemble_target ∈ {0, 1}` is a composite success label:
- **1** (positive) IFF within 60 days of the score materialization, the candidate pair produced: (a) buyer accepted the EOI (`EOIAcceptanceRecord` row written), OR (b) buyer invited the seller to the Workspace via Marketplace, AND (c) the resulting bid was not withdrawn within 14 days of acceptance, AND (d) no dispute / takedown / opt-out reversal occurred against that pairing.
- **0** (negative) IFF the candidate pair was rendered but no acceptance / invitation occurred within the 60-day window, OR the pair was invited but the resulting bid was withdrawn / the EOI was reversed within 14 days.
- **censored** (excluded from training) IFF the candidate was filtered at render time by a hard gate (residency or opt-out) OR an abuse-report suppression was active during the window.

**Training data residency.** Training runs only on labels whose buyer Org and seller Org both fall inside a model-version's declared residency scope (per Seller Signal residency rules §4.4.18 reused; cross-residency training blocked). A distinct model version is trained per residency scope (`us`, `eu`, `apac`) to comply with GDPR-style region-locking.

**Offline eval guardrails.** Auto-publish of an incremental epoch requires: (a) AUC-ROC ≥ `baseline AUC − 0.01`; (b) Precision@10 ≥ `baseline P@10 − 0.015`; (c) per-category parity metric within ± 5% of baseline; (d) zero regression on the fairness audit suite (k-anonymity floor, small-seller parity, long-tail-category parity). Guardrail breach routes to manual Applied-ML review; the prior model version remains live.

**Model version artifact.** Every trained model version persists as a `MarketplaceMatchScoreModelVersion` entity (new; authored under §4.5.10 in the follow-on integration phase) with fields: `id`, `version_label`, `residency_scope`, `trained_at`, `feature_registry_version`, `training_window_start`, `training_window_end`, `auc_roc`, `p_at_10`, `is_published`, `published_at`, `deprecated_at`, `retired_at`, `rollback_of_version_id`, `created_by`, `approved_by`. The published version is the unique row with `is_published=true` AND `deprecated_at=null` per residency scope.

### 27.4.6 Buyer-Facing Rendering — Numeric vs Qualitative

Per Summary C.61 and the §48.2.11 L10 teaser loop, the score surfaces differently by plan:

| Buyer Plan Tier (§34.1) | Rendering | Label Shown | Numeric Shown? | Provenance Panel | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `buyer_free` | Qualitative label | `strong_match`, `moderate_match`, `weak_match`, `insufficient_signal` (per §48.2.11 bucketing) | No | Feature-count headline only ("Scored against 17 features"; individual values hidden) | Upgrade CTA rendered |
| `buyer_starter` | Qualitative label | Same as Free | No | Same as Free | Upgrade CTA rendered |
| `buyer_growth` | Numeric + label | Label + 0–100 integer | Yes | Feature-value + local-contribution (SHAP direction) for top 5 features | Powered by §21.4.2 `match_score_numeric` billing for per-view ops beyond the free allowance; `match_score_numeric` billing gate is Seller-side in the capability registry, but the Buyer-side numeric view is entitled via the §5.11 `Match Scoring (numeric)` row — the buyer does NOT pay per view; the Seller-side `match_score_numeric` AIOperation is billed to the Seller when the Seller views the score teaser against their own inbound (see §21.4.2 dual-console semantics) |
| `buyer_scale` | Numeric + label + batch | Numeric + batch API access (up to 500 pairs/call) | Yes | Full feature vector (all 18 features at v7.0.0 seed) + per-feature local contribution | Batch API rate-limited per §32.4 `batch_match_score` class |
| `buyer_enterprise` | Numeric + label + batch + audit | Numeric + batch + signed score receipt | Yes | Full feature vector + model version + training window + signed audit receipt | Signed receipt is HMAC-SHA256 over `(snapshot_id, score, model_version_id, feature_vector_hash)` |

**Label bucketing function.** Deterministic one-way map (matches §48.2.11 exactly):
- `numeric ∈ [80, 100]` → `strong_match`
- `numeric ∈ [50, 80)` → `moderate_match`
- `numeric ∈ [20, 50)` → `weak_match`
- `numeric ∈ [0, 20)` → `insufficient_signal`

**Label-only rendering invariants.** (i) The numeric score MUST NOT be serialized to the client on Free/Starter surfaces — no HTML data attribute, no hidden field, no JSON key. (ii) The label MUST be derived from the numeric server-side via the one-way bucketing function; client-side rebucketing is prohibited. (iii) QA test `match_score_label_no_numeric_leakage` (shared with §48.2.11) runs on every PR touching any Marketplace render path.

**Seller-facing rendering.** Sellers viewing their own inbound EOI queue see the score rendered under the same plan-tier rules as Buyers, keyed against the Seller plan tier (`seller_free`, `seller_starter` → labels only; `seller_growth` and above → numeric + provenance). The Seller-side numeric view is billed per the `match_score_numeric` capability (§21.4.2) with the free allowance (10 ops lifetime per C.80).

**Qualitative label floor.** Per §48.2.11 anti-spam control #1, a Marketplace Category with < 5 active SellerSoftware rows in the rolling 30-day window renders `insufficient_signal` on all labels regardless of the computed numeric — the cohort is too thin for label disclosure. This floor MUST apply before the bucketing function.

**Provenance panel — free-plan degradation.** On Free / Starter, the provenance panel renders only: "Scored against {N} features · Model version {hash_prefix}". Individual feature values, labels, and contribution arrows are hidden. QA test `match_score_provenance_free_plan_minimal` asserts no feature name or value leaks in the DOM / JSON on those plans.

### 27.4.7 Caching, Invalidation, and Staleness

Match Score snapshots are cached per the trigger-class table in §27.4.2 and invalidated on any of: (a) `taxonomy.category.updated` / `taxonomy.category_deprecated` / `taxonomy.category_retired` / `taxonomy.node.updated` webhooks for any category referenced by the Listing OR any category in the scored seller's SoftwarePage; (b) `vendor_opt_out.applied` / `vendor_opt_out.revoked` webhooks for the scored seller; (c) `capability_declaration.updated` / `capability_declaration.deprecated` webhooks for the scored seller; (d) `marketplace_listing.updated` webhook for the Listing; (e) `abuse_report.created` / `abuse_report.closed` against the scored seller where the closure disposition affected listing visibility; (f) `match_score.model_deployed` webhook (see §27.4.8) — triggers a wholesale cache sweep per residency scope; (g) nightly scheduled revalidation for snapshots older than the TTL.

**Staleness SLO.** The render path MUST NOT surface a snapshot older than 60 seconds since the most recent invalidation signal. A stale-snapshot render emits `match_score.render.stale` (PostHog) and re-fetches; a re-fetch failure renders the qualitative label with `insufficient_signal` fallback to avoid surfacing stale scores.

### 27.4.8 Model Deprecation Policy

Model versions transition through a four-state lifecycle:

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Actor | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `candidate` | Training job completes | Offline-eval metrics within guardrails | Applied ML | Not yet customer-facing |
| `candidate` | `shadow` | Ops promotes for shadow deploy | Dual sign-off (Applied ML + Marketing) | Ops | Score computed but NOT served to customers; diffed against published version for 7 days minimum |
| `shadow` | `published` | Ops publishes | Shadow metrics ≥ guardrails; no P1 alerts in shadow window | Ops | Exactly one published version per residency scope; the prior published version → `deprecated` |
| `published` | `deprecated` | New version published OR manual | `deprecated_at` set; snapshots written under this version remain valid for render for the grace window | Ops | Snapshots re-scored under the new version on next invalidation |
| `deprecated` | `retired` | Grace window expires | 30 days post-deprecation (Buyer/Seller Growth+); 90 days for Enterprise audit snapshots | System | `retired_at` set; snapshots referencing a retired version MUST be re-scored on next render or fall back to label-only |
| `published` | `rolled_back` | P1 drift / abuse alert OR guardrail regression detected post-deploy | `rollback_of_version_id` populated to point to the version being rolled back to | Ops (Applied-ML on-call + Ops leadership dual sign-off for production rollback) | Prior version reinstated as `published`; rollback model version retains its history for audit |

**Deprecation notifications.** (i) Published-version deprecation emits `marketplace.match_score.model_deprecated` webhook (§31 catalog, authored in §27.4.9 webhook list) to all Enterprise subscribers with audit-receipt consumption so they can rotate receipt validators. (ii) Retirement emits `marketplace.match_score.model_retired` webhook with the `retired_at`. (iii) Rollback emits `marketplace.match_score.model_rolled_back` webhook with the `rollback_of_version_id`.

**Retention of historical model versions.** Model versions are retained for life of platform (audit). Shadow and rolled-back versions are retained for 7 years for post-hoc dispute analysis. Feature-vector snapshots (`MarketplaceMatchScoreSnapshot`) are retained for the lifetime of the originating Workspace + 7 years aligned with §40.2 Workspace retention.

**Legacy Baseline v1 — preserved reference implementation.** The v6.0.0 keyword-intersection formula is preserved in the model registry as `model_version_label=v1_legacy_baseline` and remains invokable as the cold-start fallback described in §27.4.4 and as a non-published diff target for model-lift evaluation. Its computation is exactly: `Match Score = matched_requirement_count / total_scored_requirement_count × 100`, where `matched_requirement_count` is the number of requirements (excluding `response_type=informational`) for which ≥ 1 vendor Capability Declaration name OR declaration text contains ≥ 1 keyword extracted from the requirement title/description at ≥ 60% confidence. This is the original §27.4 algorithm; it is retained for denominator purposes and NEVER published as the primary v7.0.0 score source except as cold-start fallback.

### 27.4.9 Webhook Events (Added to Appendix C Notification Event Catalog and Appendix G PostHog Event Taxonomy)

| Webhook Event | Trigger | Payload Fields (core) | Retry Curve | Consumers |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `marketplace.match_score.model_deployed` | A `MarketplaceMatchScoreModelVersion` transitions to `published` (from `shadow`) | `event_id`, `timestamp`, `residency_scope`, `model_version_id`, `model_version_label`, `feature_registry_version`, `prior_model_version_id` (nullable), `auc_roc`, `p_at_10` | §31 standard | Enterprise buyers with audit-receipt consumption; Ops dashboards; MLOps pipelines |
| `marketplace.match_score.model_deprecated` | `published → deprecated` | `event_id`, `timestamp`, `residency_scope`, `model_version_id`, `deprecated_at`, `successor_version_id`, `grace_window_days` | §31 standard | Same as above |
| `marketplace.match_score.model_retired` | `deprecated → retired` | `event_id`, `timestamp`, `residency_scope`, `model_version_id`, `retired_at` | §31 standard | Same as above |
| `marketplace.match_score.model_rolled_back` | `published → rolled_back` | `event_id`, `timestamp`, `residency_scope`, `model_version_id`, `rollback_of_version_id`, `reason` (free-text, ≤ 500 chars) | §31 standard | Same as above; P0 status-page notice fires in parallel |
| `marketplace.match_score.computed` | A `MarketplaceMatchScoreSnapshot` row is written | `event_id`, `timestamp`, `snapshot_id`, `trigger_class`, `model_version_id`, `marketplace_listing_id` (nullable), `eoi_record_id` (nullable), `seller_org_id`, `seller_software_id` | §31 standard | Optional subscription (Enterprise buyers opting in for full score audit stream); rate-limited to Enterprise plans |
| `marketplace.match_score.cache_invalidated` | Cache invalidator fires (any of the §27.4.7 invalidation triggers) | `event_id`, `timestamp`, `invalidation_cause`, `affected_snapshot_ids` (up to 500 per event; overflow fan-out) | §31 standard | Ops dashboards; optional Enterprise subscription |

All webhooks follow §31.2 (HMAC-SHA256, `event_id` idempotency, exponential backoff per Appendix F, DLQ at 5 failures, payload ≤ 256KB). All are added to Appendix C Notification Event Catalog and Appendix G PostHog Event Taxonomy in the same v7.0.0 integration (see `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md`).

### 27.4.10 Acceptance Criteria (Match Score Internals)

1. Match Score computation at the three trigger classes (Listing-Publish, EOI-Review, On-Demand) MUST materialize exactly one `MarketplaceMatchScoreSnapshot` row per `(trigger_class, listing_or_eoi_or_workspace, seller_software_id, model_version_id)` tuple within the event handler's transaction; partial writes MUST be impossible.
2. `residency_compatible_flag=0` OR `vendor_opt_out_effective_flag=1` MUST force the final score to 0 AND set the provenance `hard_gate_triggered` to the gate name; QA test `match_score_hard_gate_short_circuit` asserts across both gates.
3. Model version publication (`candidate → shadow → published`) MUST require dual sign-off (Applied ML + Marketing); single-signoff publish MUST be rejected with `match_score_model_publish_requires_dual_signoff` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403).
4. Incremental-epoch auto-publish MUST be blocked if any offline-eval guardrail is breached; breach emits `match_score.epoch_auto_publish_blocked` PostHog event; prior model remains live.
5. A Free/Starter buyer or seller surface MUST NOT expose the numeric score in HTML, JSON, computed CSS, PostHog properties, or error response bodies; QA test `match_score_label_no_numeric_leakage` asserts across all four surfaces.
6. The full feature vector in the provenance panel MUST be gated on plan tier per §27.4.6; a Growth-plan request for Scale-plan-tier provenance (full 18 features) MUST be rejected with `match_score_provenance_plan_insufficient` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403).
7. Deprecating a published model version MUST emit `marketplace.match_score.model_deprecated` within 60 seconds and schedule re-scoring of all snapshots under that version on next invalidation; re-scoring is observable via `match_score.cache_invalidated` stream.
8. A cold-start residency scope (no prior model published) MUST use the Legacy Baseline v1 formula per §27.4.8; the provenance panel MUST explicitly label the cold-start mode.
9. Model-version rollback (`published → rolled_back`) MUST complete within 5 minutes of dual sign-off and emit `marketplace.match_score.model_rolled_back`; Enterprise subscribers receive the webhook within 60 seconds of rollback commit.
10. A numeric score change of ≥ 15 points on a cached snapshot across a cache invalidation (e.g., due to an opt-out flip or model redeployment) MUST emit a provenance note `score_delta_significant=true` on the next render so buyers understand why their view changed.
11. QA test `match_score_weight_non_exposure` MUST assert no weight magnitudes leak on any surface (HTML / JSON / PostHog / error responses); test runs on every PR touching any Match-Score render path.
12. The `eoi_record_id` snapshot MUST persist `match_score_at_acceptance` per §4.5.8 acceptance criteria #7 at the exact numeric computed at the EOI-Review trigger; if an On-Demand score existed within the last 60 seconds on the same `(workspace_id, seller_software_id)`, it MUST NOT be re-used — the snapshot stamp uses the fresh EOI-Review computation only.
13. A seller filing a `qualitative_label_dispute` (§48.2.11 failure mode #3) against their own rendered label MUST route to §4.5.7 Marketplace Abuse Report with `reason=misleading_claims` and `subject_kind=software_page` or `seller_org_page` depending on dispute surface; Ops retains the snapshot provenance panel for review.
14. Every PostHog event for match-score render MUST carry `model_version_id` and `feature_registry_version` as super-properties; audits trace every surfaced score to the exact model and feature configuration that produced it.
15. A Listing whose `target_regions` omits the seller's region and whose `data_residency_region` differs from the seller's Org residency MUST surface the candidate with a provenance banner "Data residency incompatible — cannot transact via Sourcera" and MUST suppress the Match Score numeric regardless of plan tier (the hard gate's 0 score is the rendered value).
16. On-Demand scoring via `match_score_numeric` billing MUST consume exactly one AIOperation per `(workspace_id, seller_software_id)` invocation; duplicate invocations within 60 seconds MUST be idempotency-keyed to the same AIOperation and return the cached snapshot (no double-billing).

### 27.4.11 Quality Monitoring, Fairness Audit, and Score-Feedback Loop {#27.4.11-quality-monitoring-fairness-audit-and-score-feedback-loop}

The §27.4.5 retraining pipeline depends on continuous quality and fairness signal. §27.4.11 authors the monitoring surfaces, the fairness-audit suite contract, and the closed-loop feedback entity that lets buyers and sellers flag a score they believe is wrong. All three feed Applied-ML's epoch decision-making and are the only authorized inputs to model rollback (§27.4.8 `published → rolled_back`).

**Scope discipline.** §27.4.11 introduces:
- One new entity: `MarketplaceMatchScoreFeedback` (platform-scoped, append-only).
- One new monitoring surface: the Score-Drift & Fairness Dashboard inside Ops Console (consumes existing PostHog and snapshot data; no new entity for the dashboard itself).
- Five new alert classes (registered to Appendix F): drift-AUC, drift-distribution, fairness-parity, fairness-k-anonymity, feedback-anomaly.
- Two new webhook events (Ops-only): `marketplace.match_score.drift_alert`, `marketplace.match_score.fairness_breach`.
- One new error code (Appendix I): `match_score_feedback_rate_limit_exceeded`.

**Entity — `MarketplaceMatchScoreFeedback` (platform-scoped; append-only after `submitted`).**

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK; ULID-encoded for sort-by-time | |
| `org_id` | UUID FK | NOT NULL; references the reporting Org (buyer or seller) | Scope-isolation: feedback is platform-scoped for analytics but `org_id` retained for rate-limiting, attribution, and DSAR. |
| `console` | enum (`buyer`, `seller`) | NOT NULL | Tracks which console the feedback was filed from. |
| `snapshot_id` | UUID FK → `MarketplaceMatchScoreSnapshot.id` | NOT NULL | The exact snapshot the user is contesting. Snapshot's frozen feature vector + model_version are the unit of dispute. |
| `model_version_id` | UUID FK | NOT NULL; denormalized from snapshot at write time | Snapshot may later be re-scored under a new model; `model_version_id` here is immutable so feedback ties to the exact version that produced the disputed score. |
| `feedback_kind` | enum `match_score_feedback_kind` (Appendix J — new) | NOT NULL; values: `score_too_high`, `score_too_low`, `feature_value_incorrect`, `wrong_seller_for_listing`, `should_have_been_filtered_out`, `other` | |
| `freeform_note` | text | ≤ 1000 chars; XSS-sanitized | Required for `feedback_kind ∈ {feature_value_incorrect, other}`; optional otherwise. |
| `cited_feature_id` | string FK → `MarketplaceMatchFeatureRegistry.feature_id` | nullable; required iff `feedback_kind=feature_value_incorrect` | Identifies which feature the user disputes. |
| `cited_feature_value_observed` | string | ≤ 200 chars; nullable | The value the user believes is correct. Free-form (not validated against feature schema; Ops review interprets). |
| `eoi_outcome_at_feedback` | enum (`pre_eoi`, `eoi_accepted`, `eoi_declined`, `bid_won`, `bid_lost`) | nullable | Captured if known at feedback time; helps Applied-ML correlate feedback to outcomes. |
| `applied_ml_review_status` | enum `match_score_feedback_review_status` (Appendix J — new): `submitted`, `triaged`, `accepted_for_training`, `rejected_invalid`, `rejected_duplicate`, `escalated_to_model_rollback` | NOT NULL; default `submitted` | State machine in the failure-modes block below. |
| `applied_ml_reviewer_user_id` | UUID FK → `users.id` | nullable | Stamped at `submitted → triaged`. |
| `applied_ml_decision_note` | text | ≤ 2000 chars; nullable | Internal Ops note; never surfaced to reporter. |
| `created_at` | timestamptz | NOT NULL; default now() | |
| `updated_at` | timestamptz | NOT NULL | Bumped on each Ops review action. |
| `created_by` | UUID FK → `users.id` | NOT NULL | Reporter. |
| `updated_by` | UUID FK → `users.id` | NOT NULL | Reporter on initial write; Ops on subsequent reviews. |
| `deleted_at` | timestamptz | nullable | Soft-delete reserved for DSAR-driven anonymization; row is otherwise immutable. |

**Indexes:** `(snapshot_id)`, `(org_id, created_at)`, `(applied_ml_review_status, created_at)`, `(model_version_id, created_at)`.
**Retention:** life of platform for aggregate analytics; per-feedback PII redacted on reporter DSAR per §40.2 (reporter `created_by` and `freeform_note` re-anonymized; row preserved for model training continuity).
**Rate limits:** 20 feedback rows per Org per rolling 24 hours per `(buyer, seller)` console. Excess returns HTTP 429 with `match_score_feedback_rate_limit_exceeded` (Appendix I — new).

**Feedback state machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Actor | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `submitted` | Reporter `POST /api/v1/marketplace/match-scores/:snapshot_id/feedback` | Rate-limit check passes; snapshot resolvable; `feedback_kind` valid for required-field set | Buyer or Seller user | Confirmation rendered; Applied-ML notified via SIM signal. |
| `submitted` | `triaged` | Applied-ML reviewer claims | Within 5 business days SLO | Applied-ML | If breached, emits `marketplace.match_score.feedback_review_slo_breach`. |
| `triaged` | `accepted_for_training` | Reviewer marks feedback as a usable label-correction signal | Reviewer note recorded | Applied-ML | Feedback row added to next epoch's training-label correction set. |
| `triaged` | `rejected_invalid` | Reviewer determines feedback misuses the channel (e.g., off-topic, abusive) | Reviewer note recorded | Applied-ML | Reporter notified with neutral message; no model impact. |
| `triaged` | `rejected_duplicate` | Reviewer matches feedback to a prior feedback already triaged for the same `(snapshot_id, feedback_kind)` | Duplicate snapshot ID present | Applied-ML | Reporter notified: "linked to prior feedback." |
| `triaged` | `escalated_to_model_rollback` | Reviewer believes feedback indicates a P1 model defect | Dual sign-off (Applied-ML + Marketing) at escalation, distinct from rollback dual-signoff at §27.4.8 | Applied-ML | Triggers an Ops-side incident; rollback flow per §27.4.8 begins. |

**Drift Detection Suite.** The Score-Drift & Fairness Dashboard runs continuously and emits an Ops-side alert when any of:

| Metric | Window | Alert Threshold | Alert Class | Severity |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| AUC-ROC delta vs. published model baseline | Rolling 14 days against next-180d hold-out target labels | > 0.02 absolute drop | `match_score_drift_auc` | P2 |
| Score-distribution KL divergence vs. trailing 90-day reference | Daily | > 0.15 | `match_score_drift_distribution` | P3 |
| Per-category fairness parity (ratio of mean score for top-decile-volume categories vs. bottom-decile) | Weekly | < 0.85 OR > 1.15 | `match_score_fairness_parity` | P2 |
| Per-residency-scope fairness parity (us / eu / apac) | Weekly | Pairwise mean-score Δ > 5 pts after controlling for cohort mix | `match_score_fairness_parity` | P2 |
| k-anonymity floor in fairness reporting (cohort-cell count) | Daily | Any reported cell < 5 | `match_score_fairness_k_anonymity` | P2 |
| Small-seller parity (sellers with `historical_response_quality_score=null` vs. cohort) | Weekly | Mean score Δ > 10 pts after controlling for verification tier | `match_score_fairness_parity` | P3 |
| Long-tail-category parity (categories with < 20 active sellers) | Weekly | Coverage rate of `strong_match` labels < 50% of cohort baseline | `match_score_fairness_parity` | P3 |
| Feedback-anomaly: `score_too_high` rate per model_version | Rolling 7 days | > 2σ above the trailing 30-day mean rate | `match_score_feedback_anomaly` | P2 |

P2 fires `marketplace.match_score.drift_alert` or `.fairness_breach` (Ops-only webhook); P3 surfaces in dashboard and emails Applied-ML on-call. Two consecutive P2 alerts on the same metric in 14 days auto-escalate to P1 and route to the §27.4.8 rollback dual-signoff queue.

**Webhook payload — `marketplace.match_score.drift_alert` (Ops-only).**

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_01HZX...",
  "event_type": "marketplace.match_score.drift_alert",
  "event_class": "marketplace_match_score_ops_domain",
  "emitted_at": "2026-04-20T18:03:11.204Z",
  "drift": {
    "metric": "match_score_drift_auc",
    "model_version_id": "mmsmv_01ABC...",
    "residency_scope": "us",
    "window_start": "2026-04-06T00:00:00Z",
    "window_end": "2026-04-20T00:00:00Z",
    "observed_value": 0.71,
    "baseline_value": 0.74,
    "threshold_breached": 0.02,
    "consecutive_breach_count": 1,
    "auto_escalation_triggered_at_2_consecutive": true
  }
}
```

**Schema for `.fairness_breach`** mirrors `.drift_alert` with `metric ∈ {match_score_fairness_parity, match_score_fairness_k_anonymity, match_score_feedback_anomaly}` and additional `cohort_descriptor` field describing which slice (e.g., `category_id`, `residency_scope`, `verification_tier=basic`).

**Acceptance Criteria (Quality Monitoring, Fairness, Feedback).**

1. A reporter MUST be able to file `MarketplaceMatchScoreFeedback` from a Match-Score render surface (Marketplace, EOI queue, Command Palette suggestion); the form SHALL pre-populate `snapshot_id` and `model_version_id`; QA test `match_score_feedback_render_pre_population` asserts.
2. Feedback rate-limit MUST be enforced per Org per console at 20/24h; HTTP 429 with `match_score_feedback_rate_limit_exceeded` MUST include Retry-After.
3. Applied-ML triage SLO is 5 business days; breach emits `marketplace.match_score.feedback_review_slo_breach`; QA test `match_score_feedback_review_slo` asserts via clock-skip.
4. `escalated_to_model_rollback` transition MUST require dual sign-off (Applied-ML + Marketing) and MUST link to the `MarketplaceMatchScoreModelVersion.rollback_of_version_id` field once the rollback completes.
5. Drift suite MUST run nightly for AUC-ROC and KL divergence and weekly for fairness parity; missed runs page Applied-ML on-call within 60 minutes.
6. Two consecutive P2 alerts on the same metric within 14 days MUST auto-escalate to P1 and queue the §27.4.8 rollback dual-signoff dialog with the alerting metric and current published model_version_id pre-populated.
7. Fairness reporting MUST honor a k=5 cohort-cell floor; any cell < 5 MUST be redacted in the dashboard with `redacted_for_k_anonymity=true`; QA test `match_score_fairness_k_floor` asserts.
8. Score-feedback rows MUST never expose reporter identity (`created_by`, `org_id`) on any non-Ops surface; QA test `match_score_feedback_reporter_redaction` asserts on dashboard, API, and webhook payloads.
9. A reporter DSAR MUST anonymize `created_by`, `org_id`, and `freeform_note` on every feedback row owned by the user within 30 days of DSAR commit while preserving the row for training continuity (per §40.2).
10. A feedback row MUST become immutable after `triaged` except for the Ops `applied_ml_review_status`, `applied_ml_decision_note`, and `applied_ml_reviewer_user_id` columns.
11. Drift- and fairness-alert webhooks MUST conform to §31 (HMAC-SHA256, idempotent, retry curve, DLQ); Ops-only audience enforced via subscription `delivery_audience_scope=ops` (per §27.8.9 model).
12. The Score-Drift & Fairness Dashboard MUST link from the published `MarketplaceMatchScoreModelVersion` row in Ops Console; access requires the `ops_applied_ml_admin` role (existing or new — registered in Appendix J `ops_role_kind` if missing).

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Brigading: a competitor seller files dozens of `score_too_high` reports against a rival seller's snapshots.** Resolved: rate-limit (20/Org/24h); SIM (C.100) clusters reporter-org patterns; Applied-ML reviewer flags `feedback_anomaly` cluster; the affected feedback rows triage to `rejected_invalid` if brigading confirmed; reporter-cluster Org receives a `competitor_sabotage_risk_factor=true` flag visible to Ops only.
2. **A snapshot the feedback references has been re-scored under a new model version.** Resolved: feedback's `model_version_id` is denormalized at write time and immutable; Applied-ML triage interprets the feedback against the historical version; if the new version already addresses the dispute, reviewer marks `rejected_invalid` with note "addressed by mvX".
3. **Reporter abuses `freeform_note` to harass Applied-ML reviewer or include PII about a third party.** Resolved: XSS sanitization at write; manual reviewer can redact-or-escalate via `applied_ml_decision_note`; abuse → SIM → §27.8 abuse report against the reporter.
4. **Drift suite false-positives on a holiday week (low traffic distorts KL divergence).** Resolved: trailing-30-day reference baseline updates daily; suite carries a `low_traffic_suppression` flag suppressing alerts when daily render volume < 5% of the trailing-30-day mean; Applied-ML reviews every suppressed alert in the next morning queue.
5. **Fairness parity alert recurs because a long-tail category genuinely has fewer qualified sellers.** Resolved: dashboard lets Applied-ML annotate a category with `parity_acknowledged_long_tail=true` for ≤ 90 days; alerts on that cohort are suppressed during the acknowledgment window with a re-evaluation reminder at expiry.
6. **Rollback escalation pre-empts an in-progress incremental epoch publish.** Resolved: rollback transition takes precedence; in-flight epoch's auto-publish blocked at the first guardrail check after rollback commits; epoch is re-trained on the next cadence using the rolled-back version as the new baseline.

### 27.4.12 Programmatic Access — APIs, Audit Receipts, and Schema.org Surfacing {#27.4.12-programmatic-access-apis-audit-receipts-and-schemaorg-surfacing}

Match Score consumers — Enterprise audit pipelines, third-party integrators, and SoftwarePage structured-data renderers — need API access to snapshots, audit-receipt verification, and schema surfacing rules. §27.4.12 authors the API contract; the §32 endpoint catalog references this subsection as the per-endpoint authoritative source for Marketplace Match-Score paths.

**Endpoint set.** All paths are under `/api/v1/marketplace/match-scores`. Authentication uses bearer tokens issued by §32 `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with org-scope. Rate-limit classes `marketplace_match_score_read` and `marketplace_match_score_batch` are registered in §32.4.5: 600/min per Org for single read, 60/min per Org for batch, 30/hr per Org for audit-receipt verification.

**`GET /api/v1/marketplace/match-scores/:snapshot_id`** — Retrieve a single snapshot.

- Auth: any valid bearer; the requesting Org MUST be either the buyer Org of the originating Listing/EOI/Workspace OR the seller Org of the scored SellerSoftware.
- Plan-tier gating: the rendering rules in §27.4.6 apply per plan; Free/Starter buyer plans receive label-only payload (numeric and feature vector elided).
- Response example (Growth plan; numeric exposed; top-5 feature provenance):

```json
{
  "snapshot_id": "mmss_01ABC...",
  "trigger_class": "listing_publish",
  "marketplace_listing_id": "mlst_01DEF...",
  "eoi_record_id": null,
  "workspace_id": "wks_01XYZ...",
  "seller_org_id": "org_01SUB...",
  "seller_software_id": "swsw_01SOF...",
  "model_version_id": "mmsmv_01MOD...",
  "model_version_label": "v7.2.4",
  "residency_scope": "us",
  "score": 78,
  "qualitative_label": "moderate_match",
  "hard_gate_triggered": null,
  "computed_at": "2026-04-20T18:00:00.000Z",
  "feature_provenance_top_5": [
    { "feature_id": "capability_declaration_overlap_ratio", "value": 0.84, "scaled_value": 0.84, "local_contribution_direction": "+", "local_contribution_magnitude_bucket": "high" },
    { "feature_id": "verification_tier_ordinal", "value": 3, "scaled_value": 1.0, "local_contribution_direction": "+", "local_contribution_magnitude_bucket": "medium" },
    { "feature_id": "kb_freshness_score", "value": 0.71, "scaled_value": 0.71, "local_contribution_direction": "+", "local_contribution_magnitude_bucket": "medium" },
    { "feature_id": "category_fit_score", "value": 1.0, "scaled_value": 1.0, "local_contribution_direction": "+", "local_contribution_magnitude_bucket": "high" },
    { "feature_id": "seller_active_load_factor", "value": 0.92, "scaled_value": 0.92, "local_contribution_direction": "-", "local_contribution_magnitude_bucket": "medium" }
  ]
}
```

- Errors: `match_score_snapshot_not_found` (HTTP 404), `match_score_provenance_plan_insufficient` (HTTP 403; existing), `match_score_cross_org_read_forbidden` (Appendix I — new; HTTP 403).

**`POST /api/v1/marketplace/match-scores/batch`** — Batch read for Scale+ plans (up to 500 `snapshot_ids` per call). Same auth and plan-tier rules; response is an array of the single-snapshot payload. Rate-limit class `marketplace_match_score_batch` (§32.4.5).

**`POST /api/v1/marketplace/match-scores/on-demand`** — On-Demand scoring (Buyer Growth+ or Seller Growth+ for self-inbound).

- Body: `{ "workspace_id": "wks_...", "seller_software_id": "swsw_..." }` OR `{ "listing_id": "mlst_...", "seller_software_id": "swsw_..." }`.
- Idempotency: 60-second window per `(workspace_id|listing_id, seller_software_id, requesting_org_id)`; duplicate calls return the cached snapshot and do NOT re-bill.
- Billing: consumes one `match_score_numeric` AIOperation per fresh call (§21.4.2).
- Response: same payload as `GET`.
- Errors: `match_score_on_demand_billing_required` (HTTP 402; Appendix I — new) when wallet balance insufficient.

**`POST /api/v1/marketplace/match-scores/:snapshot_id/feedback`** — File a `MarketplaceMatchScoreFeedback` row (§27.4.11).

- Body: `{ "feedback_kind": "...", "freeform_note": "...", "cited_feature_id": "...", "cited_feature_value_observed": "..." }`.
- Errors: `match_score_feedback_rate_limit_exceeded` (HTTP 429), `match_score_feedback_snapshot_unauthorized` (HTTP 403; reporter Org neither buyer nor seller in the snapshot pair).

**`POST /api/v1/marketplace/match-scores/:snapshot_id/audit-receipt/verify`** — Enterprise-only audit-receipt verification.

- Body: `{ "receipt_signature_b64": "..." }`.
- Validates the HMAC-SHA256 signature against `(snapshot_id, score, model_version_id, feature_vector_hash)` with the Enterprise customer's published verification key.
- Response: `{ "verified": true, "model_version_id": "...", "feature_vector_hash": "...", "signed_at": "..." }` or HTTP 422 `match_score_receipt_invalid` (Appendix I — new).
- Plan-tier gate: `buyer_enterprise` only; HTTP 403 `match_score_audit_receipt_plan_required` (Appendix I — new) for lower tiers.

**`GET /api/v1/marketplace/match-scores/model-versions`** — List published and deprecated model versions visible to the Org.

- Returns list of `{ model_version_id, version_label, residency_scope, is_published, deprecated_at, retired_at, auc_roc, p_at_10, training_window_start, training_window_end, feature_registry_version }`.
- Free/Starter plans receive `version_label` only (no metrics).
- Used by Enterprise pipelines to know when audit-receipt verification keys must rotate.

**Schema.org surfacing rules.** Match-Score snapshots referenced by SoftwarePage structured data (§4.4.11) MUST emit `schema.org/AggregateRating` ONLY when the snapshot's `qualitative_label ∈ {strong_match, moderate_match}` AND the SoftwarePage's parent SellerSoftware is in `verification_tier ∈ {verified, certified}`. Free/Starter buyer renderings of a SoftwarePage MUST suppress the `schema.org/AggregateRating` payload (numeric leakage avoidance carries through structured data). The Schema.org renderer is governed by §22.x (SoftwarePage structured-data pipeline); §27.4.12 only specifies the Match-Score-specific gating; QA test `softwarepage_match_score_schemaorg_gate` asserts.

**Webhook subscription extension.** Enterprise customers subscribing to `marketplace.match_score.computed` (existing, §27.4.9) MAY filter by `seller_org_id` (own-Org) OR `workspace_id` (own-Org). Filter rejection of cross-Org events is enforced server-side; QA test `match_score_webhook_org_scope_enforcement` asserts via cross-Org synthetic events.

**Acceptance Criteria (Programmatic Access).**

1. `GET /api/v1/marketplace/match-scores/:snapshot_id` MUST return only snapshots where the requesting Org is the buyer or seller party; cross-Org reads MUST return HTTP 403 `match_score_cross_org_read_forbidden`.
2. Batch read MUST cap at 500 snapshot_ids; oversize requests rejected with HTTP 422 `marketplace_batch_size_exceeded` (existing).
3. On-Demand idempotency MUST hold for 60 seconds per `(workspace|listing, seller_software, requesting_org)`; duplicate calls within the window MUST return the cached snapshot and MUST NOT consume an additional AIOperation.
4. Feedback POST MUST require buyer-or-seller party Org match against the snapshot pair; non-party reporters rejected with HTTP 403 `match_score_feedback_snapshot_unauthorized`.
5. Audit-receipt verification MUST be `buyer_enterprise` only; lower tiers MUST return HTTP 403 `match_score_audit_receipt_plan_required`.
6. Audit-receipt verification SHALL accept signatures generated within the model version's lifetime (including `published`, `deprecated`, and `rolled_back` states); `retired` versions return HTTP 410 `match_score_model_retired` (Appendix I — new).
7. Model-version list endpoint MUST return only versions for residency scopes the requesting Org is provisioned in; cross-residency leakage rejected.
8. Schema.org surfacing on a SoftwarePage MUST gate on `qualitative_label ∈ {strong_match, moderate_match}` AND `verification_tier ∈ {verified, certified}`; Free/Starter buyer renderings MUST omit the AggregateRating payload entirely.
9. Webhook subscription server-side filtering on `seller_org_id` / `workspace_id` MUST reject cross-Org events; QA test `match_score_webhook_org_scope_enforcement` asserts.
10. All `/api/v1/marketplace/match-scores/**` endpoints MUST honor the `marketplace_match_score_read` / `_batch` rate-limit classes; breach returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Enterprise audit pipeline pulls a snapshot whose model version was rolled back.** Resolved: `GET` returns the snapshot with `model_version_id` pointing to the rolled-back version; audit-receipt verification still validates against that signature; the response includes `model_version_state=rolled_back` so the pipeline can choose to re-fetch a fresh score.
2. **Batch read includes a snapshot whose subject seller has been opted-out post-snapshot-write.** Resolved: opt-out cascade invalidates the cached snapshot per §27.4.7; the batch endpoint refuses to return rows whose snapshot has been invalidated since `computed_at`; affected rows return `match_score_snapshot_invalidated` (Appendix I — new) per-row in the batch response, allowing partial success.
3. **A receipt signature is intercepted and replayed by an unauthorized verifier.** Resolved: verification MUST be over `(snapshot_id, score, model_version_id, feature_vector_hash)` AND the requesting Org's bearer-token Org-id MUST be a party to the snapshot; non-party verification calls return HTTP 403 even with a valid signature.
4. **Schema.org renderer races with a fresh hard-gate flip on the seller (e.g., new opt-out).** Resolved: SoftwarePage edge cache is invalidated within 60s of any `vendor_opt_out.applied` per §27.4.7; an in-flight render that completes within the propagation window MAY surface the stale `AggregateRating`; the next render purges. QA test `softwarepage_aggregate_rating_propagation_window` asserts ≤ 5 minutes worst-case.

## 27.5 Expression of Interest (EOI) {#27.5-expression-of-interest-(eoi)}

Buyers can send an EOI to Marketplace vendors to invite participation.

**EOI content:**

- Buyer's workspace title (public summary, not full requirement matrix)  
- Buyer's evaluation summary (1–500 chars, Markdown)  
- Capability checklist: Buyer selects which vendor capabilities are critical (multi-select from vendor's declared capabilities)  
- Timeline: Expected submission deadline, expected decision date  
- Evaluation scope: Number of requirements, number of evaluation weeks  
- Contact person: Buyer rep name \+ email

**Vendor EOI response:**

- Accept: Vendor enters evaluation pipeline. Bid Workspace is created. Vendor status → `active`.  
- Decline: Vendor notifies buyer. EOI status → `declined`. Vendor not added to evaluation.  
- Request More Info: Vendor asks clarifying questions. Buyer notified. EOI in `awaiting_info` status until buyer responds.

**EOI post-listing-close behavior (Gap 27.1):**

- When Marketplace Listing is closed (workspace advances past Phase 3 Vendor Curation), pending EOIs are auto-rejected.  
- Vendor receives notification: "The evaluation '\[Workspace Name\]' is no longer accepting new vendors. Thank you for your interest."  
- EOI status → `rejected` (with reason \= "Listing closed").  
- No manual buyer action required.

## 27.6 Marketplace Tags & Controlled Vocabulary (Gap 27.2) {#27.6-marketplace-tags-&-controlled-vocabulary-(gap-27.2)}

**Authoring Intent.** Per Summary C.60 (Marketplace Tags & Controlled Vocabulary) and C.95 (Taxonomy CMS), every taxonomy value surfaced in the Marketplace — Marketplace Category, Capability Category, Industry, Certification, Integration Vendor, Language, Region, Employee Size Band, and the seller-referenceable Controlled-Vocabulary Tag entries under each dimension — is Ops-authored, versioned, deprecation-aware, and migration-safe. Sellers MUST NOT mint freeform taxonomy strings on any consumer surface; freeform entry is rejected at the write layer with a suggestion of the closest approved term. This section consolidates the Marketplace-domain authoring flow, deprecation-with-cascade rules, freeform-tag prohibition enforcement, and migration tooling into one reference. It deliberately does not re-author entity field tables already in §4.5.4 (Taxonomy Node) and §4.5.5 (Controlled-Vocabulary Tag); those remain authoritative for schemas, state machines, and scope-isolation rules.

### 27.6.1 Source of Truth & Cross-References {#27.6.1-source-of-truth-&-cross-references}

The registry is the union of two tables, each with its own §4 entry:

| Layer | Entity | Section | Responsibility |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Dimension (taxonomy node) | Taxonomy Node | §4.5.4 | Registers each taxonomy *dimension* and each parent/child node within a dimension (e.g., dimension `capability_category`, node `security_compliance`). For `kind=marketplace_category`, the `§4.4.7 Marketplace Category` row is the specialized projection and carries category-specific fields. |
| Tag value under a dimension | Controlled-Vocabulary Tag | §4.5.5 | Registers each published *value* under a dimension (e.g., under `capability_category → security_compliance`, the tag "SAML SSO"). Seller-proposable, Ops-moderated. |

All consumer entities — Capability Declaration (§26.3), Marketplace Listing filters (§4.5.1, §27.3), Seller Profile industries and certifications (§26.1), SoftwarePage structured data (§4.4.11), HeatMapCell region facets (§4.4.16), Market Intelligence Report cohort slicers (§4.4.15), and any `/capabilities/:slug`, `/integrations/:slug`, `/certifications/:slug` derived page — reference the registry by FK, never by string.

### 27.6.2 Ops Console Authoring Flow (Taxonomy CMS per C.95) {#27.6.2-ops-console-authoring-flow}

The Taxonomy CMS surface lives in the Ops Console under `Taxonomy → {Categories | Capabilities | Industries | Certifications | Integrations | Regions | Languages | Size Bands}`. Write access is gated by the Ops roles defined in Appendix J: `ops_taxonomy_admin` (all dimensions and all state transitions) and `ops_marketing_editor` (restricted to Controlled-Vocabulary Tag moderation for `kind ∈ {capability_category, integration_vendor}` and to editorial-copy edits on `active` nodes — `description`, `long_description`, `seo_metadata_json`, `aliases` — with no state-transition authority). A buyer-console or seller-console write attempt against any Taxonomy CMS endpoint MUST receive HTTP 403 with `taxonomy_node_write_forbidden` (existing; §4.5.4) or `vocab_tag_buyer_access_forbidden` (existing; §4.5.5).

**Taxonomy Node lifecycle (Ops-authored).**

| Phase | Initiator | Precondition | Action | Outcome |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Create | `ops_taxonomy_admin` | Dimension `kind` chosen; proposed `slug` passes `^[a-z0-9-]+$` and is unique within `(kind, slug)`; `name`, `short_name`, `visibility` populated; if `kind=marketplace_category`, paired §4.4.7 Marketplace Category row created in the same transaction | POST `/ops/taxonomy/nodes` | Row persisted with `state=draft`; not resolvable on public paths; no webhook emitted |
| Publish (Activate) | `ops_taxonomy_admin` | Row in `state=draft`; all required fields populated; if `kind=marketplace_category`, paired §4.4.7 row in `state=active` | PATCH `/ops/taxonomy/nodes/:id` with `state=active` | Transition `draft → active`; `version=1`; `taxonomy.category_added` webhook emitted (§27.6.7); downstream caches invalidated within 60 s per §4.5.4 AC 7 |
| Editorial edit | `ops_taxonomy_admin` or `ops_marketing_editor` | Row in `state ∈ {active, deprecated}`; edit limited to non-structural fields on `deprecated` rows | PATCH `/ops/taxonomy/nodes/:id` | `version++`; `taxonomy.node.updated` webhook emitted (existing); downstream caches invalidated |
| Deprecate | `ops_taxonomy_admin` | Row in `state=active`; `deprecation_action ∈ {redirect_to_successor, redirect_to_parent, hard_retire}` supplied; if `redirect_to_successor`, `successor_id` in `state=active` and same `kind` supplied | PATCH `/ops/taxonomy/nodes/:id` with `state=deprecated` | Transition `active → deprecated`; `taxonomy.category_deprecated` webhook emitted; consumer migration scheduled per §27.6.3 |
| Merge | `ops_taxonomy_admin` | Row in `state=active`; `successor_id` in `state=active` same `kind`; merge preview shows ≤ 50 000 referencing rows (hard limit — larger merges require Ops-ops runbook) | POST `/ops/taxonomy/nodes/:id/merge` | Merge worker begins FK rewrite; source transitions `active → merged` when worker completes; `taxonomy.category_retired` webhook emitted on completion |
| Retire (Hard) | `ops_taxonomy_admin` | Row in `state=deprecated` for ≥ 90 days; zero active referencing rows | PATCH `/ops/taxonomy/nodes/:id` with `state=deprecated, deprecation_action=hard_retire` and retire-flag set | `taxonomy.category_retired` webhook emitted; node becomes fully unreferenceable; 410 Gone on resolution |
| Reactivate | `ops_taxonomy_admin` | Row in `state=deprecated`; within 30 days of deprecation; successor not yet used for FK migration | PATCH `/ops/taxonomy/nodes/:id` with `state=active` | Reverses deprecation; `taxonomy.node.updated` emitted; downstream caches invalidated |
| Soft-delete | `ops_taxonomy_admin` | Row in `state=draft` only; zero referencing rows | DELETE `/ops/taxonomy/nodes/:id` | `deleted_at` set; purged after 30 days |

**Controlled-Vocabulary Tag lifecycle (Ops moderation of seller proposals).** Full authoring and state machine in §4.5.5. Summary surface:

| Action | Actor | Ops Endpoint |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Seller proposes tag | Seller with ≥ 1 published Capability Declaration | POST `/marketplace/vocab/tags/proposals` |
| Ops picks up (auto-assigned or manual) | `ops_marketing_editor` | POST `/ops/vocab/tags/proposals/:id/claim` |
| Approve / Reject / Merge into existing / Request canonicalization | `ops_marketing_editor` | PATCH `/ops/vocab/tags/proposals/:id` |
| Deprecate approved tag | `ops_marketing_editor` with successor OR `ops_taxonomy_admin` for hard retire | PATCH `/ops/vocab/tags/:id` |

Review SLA: 5 business days from `submitted` to terminal state (per §4.5.5). Breach emits `vocab_tag.review_slo_breach` and pages editorial on-call.

**Editorial vs structural edit matrix (Taxonomy Node, per field).** The "Editorial edit" phase in the lifecycle table above permits in-place edits to non-structural fields on `active` and `deprecated` rows without routing through Create→Publish. Edits classified as **structural** MUST instead be published through Create→Publish: Ops clones the current `active` row into a new `draft`, edits the draft, validates, then publishes the draft to `active` — which deprecates the prior row with `redirect_to_successor`. Classification is per-field and authoritative:

| Field | Classification | In-place on `state=active` | In-place on `state=deprecated` | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `slug` | Structural | Forbidden | Forbidden | Slug changes break SEO, break consumer FKs keyed on `(kind, slug)` resolution, and break M9/M11 permalinks. Requires Create→Publish (clone → new slug → deprecate old with `redirect_to_successor`). |
| `kind` | Structural | Forbidden | Forbidden | Dimension migration invalidates every consumer FK. Requires Create→Publish plus a cross-kind migration plan with dual sign-off. |
| `parent_id` | Structural | Forbidden | Forbidden | Re-parenting changes descendant cascade semantics and alters `successor_chain` depth. Requires Create→Publish under the new parent with redirect-to-successor on the prior position. |
| `visibility` | Structural | Forbidden | Forbidden | Visibility downgrades (e.g., `public → internal_ops_only`) invalidate the public read projection and require pre-flight scope report; upgrades require editorial-copy review for all `visibility=public` mandatory fields. |
| `residency_scope` | Structural | Forbidden | Forbidden | Residency changes alter which residency-bounded worker runs the cascade and which residency-scoped consumer caches flush. Requires Create→Publish with residency-migration runbook. |
| `name` | Editorial | Permitted | Forbidden | Display-name edits refresh CategoryPage title; `taxonomy.node.updated` cascades to edge caches within 60 s per §4.5.4 AC 7. Forbidden on `deprecated` rows to preserve deprecation-state display. |
| `short_name` | Editorial | Permitted | Forbidden | Same rationale as `name`. |
| `description`, `long_description` | Editorial | Permitted | Permitted | Copy corrections may be applied to deprecated rows for historical accuracy (e.g., explaining why deprecated). |
| `seo_metadata_json` | Editorial | Permitted | Permitted | SEO copy may be updated on deprecated rows to improve the 301-redirect funnel. |
| `aliases[]` | Editorial | Permitted | Permitted | Additions permitted freely; removals on `active` require a 30-day advance notice emitted as `taxonomy.node.updated` with an `aliases_removed` delta payload for integrator SDKs relying on alias resolution (§27.6.10 `/aliases/resolve`). |
| `sort_order` | Editorial | Permitted | N/A | Deprecated rows are excluded from sort ordering. |
| `icon_token` | Editorial | Permitted | Permitted | Visual-only; no FK impact. |
| `deprecation_action` | Structural, terminal on deprecation | N/A | Forbidden post-transition | Chosen at the `active → deprecated` transition and immutable thereafter; altering the action would re-shape a cascade already executed. To change disposition, Ops MUST reactivate per lifecycle row 7 (within 30 days) and re-deprecate. |
| `successor_id` | Structural, terminal on deprecation | N/A | Forbidden post-transition | Immutable post-deprecation; altering successor would re-route cascade FK rewrites already committed. |
| `authored_by_ops_user_id` | Immutable | Forbidden | Forbidden | Authorship is append-only; corrections go via audit-row annotation, never in-place edit. |
| `version` | System-managed | N/A | N/A | Bumped by the write path on every persisted edit; never directly writeable. |

Either role (`ops_taxonomy_admin` or `ops_marketing_editor`) MAY perform an **Editorial** edit subject to the dimension scoping defined above. Only `ops_taxonomy_admin` MAY route a **Structural** edit through Create→Publish; an `ops_marketing_editor` attempt to clone a row for structural change MUST be rejected with `taxonomy_structural_edit_role_insufficient` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403). An API payload that attempts to set a structural field on a `PATCH` against an `active` or `deprecated` row MUST be rejected with `taxonomy_field_edit_classification_violated` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422) *before* any write occurs; the error payload enumerates the offending field and its classification. The per-field classification above is registered in Appendix J as `taxonomy_node_field_edit_classification` for CI-test cross-reference.

**Controlled-Vocabulary Tag edit classification.** The same classification applies to Tag fields: `slug`, `taxonomy_node_id`, `origin` are **Structural** (editable only via new-draft-then-approve flow); `display_name`, `aliases[]`, `description` are **Editorial** on `approved` rows. A `PATCH /ops/vocab/tags/:id` that violates this rule receives the same `taxonomy_field_edit_classification_violated` error.

**Dual sign-off.** A publication or deprecation that touches a dimension used as a residency slicer (`kind ∈ {region, language, employee_size_band}`) OR retires a tag referenced by ≥ 10 000 consumer rows OR retires a `kind=marketplace_category` node that anchors a `CategoryPage` with ≥ 90 days of SEO history requires dual sign-off (two distinct Ops users with the relevant role). Single-signoff attempts MUST be rejected with `taxonomy_action_requires_dual_signoff` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403), payload enumerating the specific condition that triggered the requirement.

**Identity of sign-off actors (no service accounts).** The `ops_taxonomy_admin` and `ops_marketing_editor` roles MUST be held by identified human accounts only. Service accounts, machine tokens, OAuth client-credentials grants, and bot identities are forbidden from holding either role. Every publish, deprecation, merge, retire, reactivate, editorial edit, proposal moderation, or dual-signoff recorded in the audit trail MUST resolve to an `actor_user_id` corresponding to a user with `account_type=human` and active MFA enrolment per §6.5; any attempt to grant either role to an `account_type=service` user MUST be rejected at the WorkOS role-assignment layer with `ops_role_requires_human_account` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403). The audit emit for each Taxonomy CMS action MUST include `actor_account_type=human` and `actor_mfa_verified_at` (within the current session TTL per §6.5). For dual-signoff actions, *both* signers MUST independently satisfy the human+MFA constraint; a mixed dual-signoff where one signer resolves to a service account MUST be rejected with `ops_role_requires_human_account` before either signature is persisted. Post-hoc audit review that surfaces any Taxonomy CMS action attributed to a non-human actor pages the security on-call and triggers an immediate role-audit sweep across all Ops roles.

**Audit trail.** Every Ops Taxonomy CMS action writes an Audit Event (§4.6.1) with `action_type=ops_taxonomy_cms_*` (new Audit action types registered in Appendix J `audit_event_action_type` — see reconciliation log). The audit row includes `actor_user_id`, `actor_account_type`, `actor_mfa_verified_at`, `diff` (before/after field-level snapshot), `edit_classification` (editorial | structural | system-managed | immutable), `affected_consumer_row_counts_by_entity` (at decision time), and the paired webhook `event_id` emitted downstream. Ops retains taxonomy CMS audit rows for life of platform.

### 27.6.3 Deprecation with Cascade Rules {#27.6.3-deprecation-with-cascade-rules}

Taxonomy changes cascade to every consumer that references the retiring node or tag. Cascade is governed by the `deprecation_action` on the deprecating row and the specific consumer binding.

**Cascade disposition enum.** A new enum `taxonomy_cascade_disposition` (Appendix J) defines the per-consumer-row outcome of a taxonomy deprecation:

| Disposition | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| `rewrite_to_successor` | FK on referencing consumer row is rewritten to the successor node/tag id. Applies when `deprecation_action=redirect_to_successor` and `successor_id` is set. |
| `rewrite_to_parent` | FK rewritten to the deprecating node's `parent_id`. Applies when `deprecation_action=redirect_to_parent`; valid only for nodes with non-null `parent_id`. |
| `drop_reference` | FK cleared on the consumer row. Applies when `deprecation_action=hard_retire` and the consumer field is nullable. The consumer's own state machine MAY require re-authoring (e.g., a Capability Declaration with `≥ 1 primary capability category` invariant transitions to `needs_seller_review`). |
| `archive_consumer` | Consumer row is archived (state machine-specific). Applies when `hard_retire` AND the consumer field is non-nullable AND the consumer's own contract forbids `drop_reference`. |
| `preserve_historical` | Consumer row retains the stale FK for audit/historical reporting; reads on live surfaces honor the node's 301 redirect chain. Applies to immutable snapshot fields (e.g., `EOI Acceptance Record.match_score_at_acceptance_features` capturing historical feature values). |

**Consumer-specific cascade map.**

| Consumer Entity | Field | Deprecation action | Cascade Disposition | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Capability Declaration (§26.3) | `primary_category_id`, `subcategories[]` | `redirect_to_successor` | `rewrite_to_successor` | Audit row includes pre/post FK; seller notified via `capability_declaration.migrated` |
| Capability Declaration (§26.3) | `primary_category_id` | `hard_retire` | `archive_consumer` | Declaration transitions to `needs_seller_review`; seller notified with 14-day re-authoring SLA |
| Seller Profile industries (§26.1) | `industries[]` | any | matching above | `seller_profile.taxonomy_migrated` event fires |
| Seller Profile certifications (§26.1) | `certifications[]` | `hard_retire` | `drop_reference` | Certification lists are nullable-array fields |
| Marketplace Listing (§4.5.1) filters | `category_ids[]`, `capability_ids[]` | any | matching above | Active listings auto-updated; `marketplace_listing.updated` webhook fires per-listing |
| SoftwarePage (§4.4.11) | `structured_category_ids[]`, `structured_capability_ids[]` | any | matching above | Edge cache re-rendered; `softwarepage.taxonomy_migrated` |
| HeatMapCell (§4.4.16) | `category_id`, `region_id` | `redirect_to_successor` | `rewrite_to_successor` | Nightly recomputation validates k-anonymity floor post-rewrite |
| Market Intelligence Report (§4.4.15) | `category_id`, `region_id` cohort slicers | any | `preserve_historical` for published reports; `rewrite_to_successor` for drafts | Published reports are snapshots; drafts re-resolved on publish |
| CategoryPage (§4.4.12) | `category_id` | `redirect_to_successor` | Page archives with 301 redirect to successor CategoryPage | SEO preserved via redirect chain depth ≤ 3 |
| GuidePage (§4.4.13), ComparisonPage (§4.4.14) | `category_id` | `redirect_to_successor` | Page re-rendered under successor category | URL updated; old URL 301-redirects |
| Controlled-Vocabulary Tag (§4.5.5) | `taxonomy_node_id` | `hard_retire` on parent dimension | `archive_consumer` | Tags under a retired dimension archive; proposing sellers notified |
| EOI Acceptance Record (§4.5.8) `referenced_capability_declaration_ids`, `match_score_at_acceptance_features` | (historical snapshot) | any | `preserve_historical` | Immutable post-write per §4.5.8 |
| Match Score computation (§27.4) | Category Fit, Industry Match features | any | `rewrite_to_successor` for active scoring; `preserve_historical` in snapshot caches | Cache invalidated via existing §27.4.5 rules |

**Migration worker SLOs.**

| Scope | SLO |
| :---- | :---- |
| `redirect_to_successor` migration — Capability Declaration, Seller Profile, Marketplace Listing filters, SoftwarePage, HeatMapCell | 10 minutes to full FK rewrite |
| `rewrite_to_parent` migration | 10 minutes |
| `archive_consumer` migration | 10 minutes to archive; seller notification within 30 minutes |
| Page re-render (CategoryPage, GuidePage, ComparisonPage) | 15 minutes |
| Published Market Intelligence Report `preserve_historical` verification (nightly reconciliation) | 24 hours |
| Dual-signoff-gated retirement cascade (≥ 10 000 rows) | 60 minutes |

Breach emits `taxonomy.migration.slo_breach` alert (existing Appendix F class `taxonomy_merge`; reused). Worker progress is observable via the Ops Taxonomy CMS dashboard with per-batch sequence indicator.

**Redirect-chain depth constraint.** Existing §4.5.4 AC 6 caps redirect chain depth at 3. When a deprecation would create a 4-hop chain, the Ops Console pre-flight check refuses the transition with `taxonomy_redirect_chain_depth_exceeded` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409); Ops MUST first consolidate the existing chain (merge intermediates into the terminal successor) before deprecating.

**Cross-residency behavior.** For nodes with `residency_scope ∈ {us, eu, apac}`, cascade migration runs per-residency via residency-bounded workers; a global node cascades once globally. Residency-partitioned consumers (Match Score features, MarketIntelligenceReport slicers) MUST update their residency-scoped caches within the residency worker's SLO.

### 27.6.4 Seller Tag Proposal Workflow {#27.6.4-seller-tag-proposal-workflow}

Sellers MAY propose new Controlled-Vocabulary Tag values to fill gaps in approved vocabulary. The proposal flow is the only non-Ops write path into the registry; state machine in §4.5.5.

1. **Eligibility gate.** Sellers MUST have ≥ 1 Capability Declaration in `state=published` to propose. Non-published sellers receive `vocab_tag_proposer_ineligible` (existing; Appendix I; HTTP 403).
2. **Entry surface.** Capability Declarations editor → "Propose new tag" CTA; also available in Seller Profile industry/certification pickers. Entry captures `proposed_name` (≤ 100 chars), `taxonomy_dimension` (enum; see §4.5.5), `proposal_rationale` (≤ 1000 chars), optional `suggested_aliases` (≤ 10).
3. **Server-side pre-checks (pre-persist).**
   - Canonicalization: lowercase, strip punctuation, collapse whitespace.
   - Exact-match duplicate against `state=approved AND visibility=public` tags in the same dimension: auto-rejected with `vocab_tag_duplicate_of_existing` (existing; HTTP 409), payload carries the approved tag id/slug.
   - Near-match (Levenshtein ≤ 2 OR embedding cosine ≥ 0.92) against `approved` tags: persisted in `state=submitted` with an `auto_surfaced_near_matches` field populated for Ops review; Ops may one-click-merge.
4. **Persistence.** Row written to Controlled-Vocabulary Tag with `state=submitted`, `origin=seller_proposed`, `proposing_org_id`, `proposing_user_id`, `visibility=internal_ops_only`.
5. **Ops review.** Ops `ops_marketing_editor` claims the row (`state=submitted → in_review`); decisions: `approved`, `rejected` (with enumerated reason), `merged_into_existing`.
6. **Notification.** On approval, the proposing seller receives `vocab_tag.approved` in-app + email; on rejection, receives `vocab_tag.rejected` with reason and, if similarity ≥ 0.85, suggested alternative.
7. **Availability.** Approved tags become immediately referenceable by all sellers; `origin=seller_proposed` and `proposing_org_id` are retained for attribution in the Ops dashboard and in `reference_count_cache`.

SLA: 5 business days from `submitted → in_review → terminal`. Ops dashboard shows per-reviewer queue depth; SLO breach pages the editorial on-call.

### 27.6.5 Freeform-Tag Prohibition Enforcement {#27.6.5-freeform-tag-prohibition-enforcement}

**Rule.** No consumer entity may persist a taxonomy value that is not present in the registry in `state=approved AND visibility=public` at write time.

**Enforcement layer: the write path.** Enforcement is performed at the server-side write layer for every consumer entity, not in the client UI. Direct API clients receive the same rejection as UI-driven writes. A write attempt containing an unknown tag string or a FK to a non-approved tag MUST be rejected with `consumer_requires_approved_tag` (existing; §4.5.5; HTTP 422). The error payload includes:

```json
{
  "error": "consumer_requires_approved_tag",
  "rejected_value": "SAML-SSO",
  "dimension": "capability_category",
  "suggestions": [
    { "tag_id": "cvt_01HXY...", "slug": "saml-sso", "display_name": "SAML SSO", "similarity": 0.94 }
  ],
  "propose_new_tag_url": "/seller/capabilities/propose-tag?dimension=capability_category&name=SAML-SSO"
}
```

Suggestions are generated via Levenshtein ≤ 2 OR embedding cosine ≥ 0.85 against `approved` tags in the same dimension; cap 5 suggestions.

**Consumer write paths covered (non-exhaustive; every consumer documented in §27.6.1 MUST implement).**

| Consumer | Endpoint | Validation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Capability Declaration | `POST/PATCH /seller/capabilities/:id` | FK to Taxonomy Node + FK to Controlled-Vocabulary Tag, both must be `state=active`/`state=approved AND visibility=public` |
| Marketplace Listing filter | `POST/PATCH /seller/marketplace/listings/:id/filters` | Same |
| Seller Profile | `PATCH /seller/profile` | `industries[]` and `certifications[]` FK validation |
| SoftwarePage structured data | `POST /seller/marketplace/software-pages/:id` | Same |
| Public API (partners, integrators) | `POST /api/v1/seller/**` | Same; no separate grace path |
| Bulk import (CSV seller tools) | `POST /seller/tools/import` | Per-row rejection with aggregated report; import rolls back if any row fails in strict mode, accepts partial in lenient mode (seller-selectable at import time) |

**Bypass attempts.** Any attempt to bypass validation — e.g., submitting a tag string via a typo-ed URL parameter, embedding an unapproved tag in a markdown field rendered on a SoftwarePage, or attempting to upload a document whose extracted metadata contains unapproved category references — is detected and rejected at the indexer or render layer with `consumer_requires_approved_tag` and a provenance link to the offending field. Repeated bypass attempts from the same Org (≥ 5 in 1 hour) emit `vocab_tag.freeform_bypass_detected` to the Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100) and trigger Ops review.

**Grandfathering on deprecation.** When an `approved` tag transitions to `deprecated`, consumer writes that reference the deprecated tag MUST be rejected with `consumer_requires_approved_tag` (not grandfathered), unless the reference is being replaced by the successor (which is the merge worker's job). Read-side surfaces continue to 301-redirect to the successor for existing consumer rows until the cascade worker migrates them per §27.6.3.

### 27.6.6 Migration Tooling (Tag Retirement) {#27.6.6-migration-tooling-tag-retirement}

Retiring an `approved` tag or an `active` taxonomy node triggers the migration toolchain. The toolchain is a combination of (a) the §4.5.4 merge worker, (b) a new per-consumer migration worker, and (c) Ops Console pre-flight tooling that reports migration scope before the Ops user commits the transition.

**Pre-flight scope report (Ops Console).** Before an Ops user confirms a deprecation, the Ops Console surfaces a scope report:

```
Deprecating: taxonomy_node_id=tn_01ABC (kind=capability_category, slug=legacy-integrations)
Planned action: redirect_to_successor → tn_01DEF (slug=integrations)

Consumer impact:
  - Capability Declarations: 1,247 rows (847 active, 400 archived)
  - Marketplace Listings: 423 rows
  - SoftwarePages: 312 rows
  - Seller Profiles (subcategory ref): 28 rows
  - Controlled-Vocabulary Tags (parent node): 34 tags (rewrite to new parent)
  - Market Intelligence Reports (published, snapshot): 12 (preserve_historical)
  - CategoryPages: 1 (archives with 301 redirect; depth after action: 2)

Estimated migration duration (95th-percentile batch workers): 4 minutes

Dual sign-off required? NO (thresholds: ≥ 10,000 rows or residency slicer or 90-day SEO history CategoryPage)

Webhooks that will fire (in order):
  1. taxonomy.category_deprecated (at transition)
  2. taxonomy.node.updated (version bump)
  3. Per consumer batch: capability_declaration.migrated, marketplace_listing.updated, ...
  4. taxonomy.migration.completed (at migration worker finish)

[Cancel]  [Confirm and Deprecate]
```

**Per-consumer migration worker (Convex background job).**

- Runs per residency partition.
- Batches of 500 rows per iteration; idempotent per `(source_node_id | source_tag_id, successor_id | null, consumer_kind, batch_sequence)` key.
- Writes an Audit Event (§4.6.1) per batch with `action_type=taxonomy_consumer_migration`.
- On per-row write conflict (e.g., consumer row concurrently edited), retries with jitter up to 5 attempts; rows exceeding retry budget route to `taxonomy_migration_dlq` and page Ops.
- On batch completion, emits a per-consumer progress ping via PostHog (`taxonomy_migration_progress`, Appendix G — see reconciliation).
- On all-batches-completed, emits `taxonomy.migration.completed` webhook with totals per consumer entity.

**Rollback.** Rollback is supported up to the source node's transition to `merged` or `retired` (hard retire past the 90-day window is irreversible). Rollback reverses per-consumer FK rewrites in the same order; rollback emits `taxonomy.migration.rolled_back` (reuses `retry-curve class=taxonomy_merge`).

**Orphan sweep.** A nightly reconciliation worker scans every consumer entity for FKs pointing to a taxonomy node in `state=deprecated AND deprecation_action=hard_retire` (a hard-retired node that the cascade should have cleared). Any discovered orphan emits `taxonomy.orphan_reference_detected` alert and is auto-queued for next-cycle cleanup per the node's `drop_reference` or `archive_consumer` disposition.

**Error recovery surfaces.** Failed migration rows appear in an Ops Console "Taxonomy Migration Issues" tab with per-row error, consumer id, and "Retry | Archive | Escalate" actions. Ops runbook `ops/taxonomy-migration.md` (referenced; authored in Phase 6) documents recovery.

### 27.6.7 Webhook Events for Taxonomy Changes {#27.6.7-webhook-events-for-taxonomy-changes}

Every taxonomy state transition with customer-visible or integrator-visible impact emits a §31-conformant webhook event. All events use HMAC-SHA256 signing (header `X-Sourcera-Signature`), idempotency via `event_id` in the §31.1 canonical format `evt_{unix_ms}_{base32_random10}`, Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve, payload ≤ 256 KB, and are registered in Appendix C (Notification Event Catalog) and Appendix G (PostHog Event Taxonomy).

**Events introduced by §27.6.**

| Event | Trigger | Delivery |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `taxonomy.category_added` | Taxonomy Node transitions `draft → active` OR Controlled-Vocabulary Tag transitions `submitted|in_review → approved` | Webhook to all subscribed Org endpoints; PostHog event `taxonomy_category_added` |
| `taxonomy.category_deprecated` | Taxonomy Node `active → deprecated` OR Controlled-Vocabulary Tag `approved → deprecated` | Webhook + PostHog `taxonomy_category_deprecated` |
| `taxonomy.category_retired` | Taxonomy Node `deprecated → merged` (merge completion) OR `deprecated` with `deprecation_action=hard_retire` after 90-day window OR Controlled-Vocabulary Tag `deprecated → merged_into_existing` | Webhook + PostHog `taxonomy_category_retired` |
| `taxonomy.node.updated` (existing; §4.5.4) | Editorial edit to an `active` node (description, aliases, seo_metadata_json, sort_order, icon_token) | Cache-invalidation event; webhook + PostHog `taxonomy_node_updated` |
| `taxonomy.migration.completed` | Migration worker finishes cascade for a deprecation | Webhook only (ops-oriented; not customer-notification) |
| `taxonomy.migration.rolled_back` | Ops rollback of an in-progress migration | Webhook only |
| `taxonomy.migration.slo_breach` | 10-minute SLO breach on the migration worker | Internal Ops alert (Appendix F alert class); no customer webhook |
| `taxonomy.orphan_reference_detected` | Nightly reconciliation detects orphaned FK | Internal Ops alert; no customer webhook |

**Event payload schema — `taxonomy.category_added`.**

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_01HXY7Q...",
  "event_type": "taxonomy.category_added",
  "event_class": "taxonomy_domain",
  "emitted_at": "2026-04-16T18:03:11.204Z",
  "residency_scope": "global",
  "node": {
    "taxonomy_node_id": "tn_01ABC...",
    "kind": "capability_category",
    "slug": "saml-sso",
    "name": "SAML SSO",
    "short_name": "SAML SSO",
    "parent_id": "tn_01DEF...",
    "parent_slug": "security-compliance",
    "visibility": "public",
    "version": 1,
    "aliases": ["saml", "saml2", "saml-2-0"]
  },
  "tag": null,
  "authored_by_role": "ops_taxonomy_admin",
  "authored_by_actor_pseudonym": "h_01HZBR8C9TKQ3F7..."
}
```

When the event represents a Controlled-Vocabulary Tag approval, `node` contains the tag's parent Taxonomy Node and `tag` is populated with `{ tag_id, taxonomy_dimension, slug, display_name, origin, proposing_org_id (nullable) }`.
