> **Ops user identity redaction (D-6.2-002 remediation 2026-05-06).** The customer-audience webhook payload MUST NOT carry raw Sourcera Ops User UUIDs. Two fields replace the prior `authored_by_ops_user_id`: (1) `authored_by_role` — the canonical Ops role enum string per Appendix J `ops_role_kind` (e.g., `ops_taxonomy_admin`, `ops_compliance_reviewer`); (2) `authored_by_actor_pseudonym` — a per-customer-Org HMAC pseudonym computed as `HMAC-SHA256(actor_user_id ‖ subscribing_org_id, webhook_secret)` so each subscribing Org can correlate two events written by the same Ops user *to themselves only* but cannot resolve to a global identifier or correlate across subscribers. The raw `authored_by_ops_user_id` continues to be recorded in the §4.6.1 AuditEvent row (Ops-side; full forensic fidelity); the §27.6.7 webhook payload, the Ops Console internal view, and the public-read taxonomy projection (per §27.6.10 line 22790) are the only customer-audience surfaces and ALL apply this redaction. CI gate `taxonomy_webhook_no_ops_user_identity_leak` asserts on every PR; deploy blocked on red. The same redaction is mirrored in `taxonomy.category_deprecated` and `taxonomy.category_retired` payloads (`authored_by_actor_pseudonyms[]` arrays replace `authored_by_ops_user_ids[]`) and in `marketplace.abuse_report.seller_banned` (`signed_by_actor_pseudonyms[]` replaces `signed_by_ops_user_ids[]`).

**Event payload schema — `taxonomy.category_deprecated`.**

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_01HXY7Q...",
  "event_type": "taxonomy.category_deprecated",
  "event_class": "taxonomy_domain",
  "emitted_at": "2026-04-16T18:03:11.204Z",
  "residency_scope": "global",
  "node": {
    "taxonomy_node_id": "tn_01ABC...",
    "kind": "capability_category",
    "slug": "legacy-integrations",
    "name": "Legacy Integrations",
    "version": 4
  },
  "tag": null,
  "deprecation": {
    "deprecation_action": "redirect_to_successor",
    "successor_id": "tn_01DEF...",
    "successor_slug": "integrations",
    "expected_consumer_impact": {
      "capability_declaration": 1247,
      "marketplace_listing": 423,
      "seller_profile": 28,
      "software_page": 312,
      "category_page": 1,
      "market_intelligence_report_snapshots": 12
    },
    "cascade_worker_id": "twk_01MIG...",
    "dual_signoff_required": false,
    "authored_by_roles": ["ops_taxonomy_admin"],
    "authored_by_actor_pseudonyms": ["h_01HZBR8C9TKQ3F7..."]
  }
}
```

(See §27.6.7 D-6.2-002 remediation note above for `authored_by_actor_pseudonyms[]` HMAC computation.)

**Event payload schema — `taxonomy.category_retired`.**

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_01HXY7Q...",
  "event_type": "taxonomy.category_retired",
  "event_class": "taxonomy_domain",
  "emitted_at": "2026-04-16T18:33:11.204Z",
  "residency_scope": "global",
  "node": {
    "taxonomy_node_id": "tn_01ABC...",
    "kind": "capability_category",
    "slug": "legacy-integrations",
    "name": "Legacy Integrations"
  },
  "tag": null,
  "retirement": {
    "retirement_path": "merge_completed",
    "successor_id": "tn_01DEF...",
    "merge_duration_ms": 247103,
    "migrated_consumer_row_counts": {
      "capability_declaration": 1247,
      "marketplace_listing": 423,
      "seller_profile": 28,
      "software_page": 312
    },
    "dlq_row_count": 0,
    "authored_by_roles": ["ops_taxonomy_admin", "ops_compliance_reviewer"],
    "authored_by_actor_pseudonyms": ["h_01HZBR8C9TKQ3F7...", "h_01HZBR8DEF456..."]
  }
}
```

`retirement_path ∈ {merge_completed, hard_retire_after_window, tag_merged_into_existing}` (new enum `taxonomy_retirement_path`; Appendix J).

**Subscription model.** Any customer Org MAY subscribe to taxonomy events via `POST /api/v1/webhooks` with event-type filters (§31.3). There is no per-plan-tier gate on taxonomy webhook subscription — the events are foundational and all Orgs need them to keep their integrations synchronized. Ops-only events (`taxonomy.migration.*`, `taxonomy.orphan_reference_detected`) are NOT exposed to customer webhook subscriptions; they surface only in the Ops Console and internal alerting.

**Idempotency contract.** Consumers MUST be idempotent on `event_id`. A node transition that fires multiple events (e.g., `taxonomy.node.updated` then `taxonomy.category_deprecated` then `taxonomy.migration.completed`) is semantically ordered but delivered concurrently; consumers MUST handle out-of-order arrival and MUST re-fetch the authoritative node state via `/api/v1/marketplace/taxonomy/nodes/:id` when resolving conflicts.

### 27.6.8 Failure Modes Addressed {#27.6.8-failure-modes-addressed}

1. **Two Ops users race a deprecation of the same node.** Resolved: Taxonomy Node writes use optimistic concurrency on `version`; the second write sees a stale `version` and is rejected with `taxonomy_node_version_conflict` (existing in §4.5.4 family; HTTP 409). Ops UI re-fetches and shows conflict resolution.
2. **Seller proposes a tag during an active deprecation of the parent dimension.** Resolved: proposal pre-check refuses submission when `taxonomy_node_id.state ∈ {deprecated, merged}` with `vocab_tag_parent_not_active` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409); proposing seller receives a pointer to the successor dimension.
3. **Consumer retries a write with a stale cached tag list.** Resolved: `consumer_requires_approved_tag` suggests current tags; the consumer's next write succeeds. Client SDKs SHOULD refresh the approved-tag cache on any `taxonomy.category_added` / `.deprecated` webhook, with a 5-minute max cache TTL as backup.
4. **Migration worker deadlocks with a concurrent consumer bulk-import.** Resolved: migration worker acquires an advisory lock keyed on `(consumer_kind, org_id)`; concurrent bulk imports queue behind the migration; imports exceeding a 30-second queue wait return HTTP 503 with `taxonomy_migration_in_progress` (new; Appendix I) and Retry-After.
5. **Migration DLQ fills with un-retryable rows due to consumer invariant.** Resolved: Ops Console "Taxonomy Migration Issues" tab lists per-row error; Ops decides `Retry | Archive | Escalate`. DLQ fill rate > 0.1% of batch volume pages Ops.
6. **Customer webhook endpoint is down during a deprecation, misses `taxonomy.category_deprecated`.** Resolved: Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve + DLQ + replay-endpoint `/api/v1/webhooks/deliveries/replay`; additionally, any new `consumer_requires_approved_tag` error on that Org's subsequent writes surfaces the pending deprecation explicitly in the error payload.
7. **Orphan FK after hard_retire due to late-arriving soft-deleted consumer un-deletion.** Resolved: soft-delete recovery on a consumer row re-validates taxonomy FKs; if the referenced node is `state=deprecated AND deprecation_action=hard_retire`, un-delete is refused with `taxonomy_reference_dangling` (existing; §4.5.4 AC). Nightly orphan sweep catches any remainder.

### 27.6.9 Acceptance Criteria {#27.6.9-acceptance-criteria}

1. An Ops publish of a new Taxonomy Node MUST emit `taxonomy.category_added` within 60 seconds of `state=active`; webhook payload conforms to §27.6.7 schema; Appendix C registers the event.
2. An Ops deprecation of an `active` Taxonomy Node MUST emit `taxonomy.category_deprecated` at the transition; consumer cascade MUST complete within the SLO in §27.6.3; `taxonomy.migration.completed` MUST emit on cascade finish.
3. A `hard_retire` deprecation attempted within < 90 days of `deprecated` entry MUST be rejected with `taxonomy_hard_retire_window_not_elapsed` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409); Ops dashboard shows the remaining waiting period.
4. A retirement cascade that touches ≥ 10 000 consumer rows MUST require dual sign-off; single-signoff attempts MUST be rejected with `taxonomy_action_requires_dual_signoff` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403).
5. A consumer-entity write that references an unapproved or non-`active`/`approved` taxonomy value MUST be rejected with `consumer_requires_approved_tag`; error payload MUST include `suggestions[]` when any approved tag has similarity ≥ 0.85.
6. A seller's repeated freeform-tag bypass attempts (≥ 5 in 1 hour) MUST emit `vocab_tag.freeform_bypass_detected` to the Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100) and page Ops for review.
7. A webhook subscriber MUST receive `taxonomy.category_added/deprecated/retired` events with HMAC-SHA256 signature validation per §31; idempotency on `event_id` MUST be preserved across retries; DLQ entry MUST be created after 5 hard failures.
8. The migration worker MUST be observable in the Ops Console with per-consumer-entity row count, batch sequence, and per-batch Audit Event linkage; breach of the per-scope SLO in §27.6.3 MUST page Ops within 60 seconds of breach.
9. A customer Org's direct API write with an unapproved tag MUST be rejected identically to the UI (same error code, same payload shape); QA test `direct_api_freeform_tag_rejection` asserts parity across 3 consumer endpoints.
10. The pre-flight scope report MUST be computed within 3 seconds for deprecations touching < 100 000 rows and MUST be computed asynchronously with progress indicator for larger scopes.
11. Orphan sweep MUST detect any FK pointing to a hard-retired node within 24 hours of retirement and MUST auto-queue the row for cleanup per the node's disposition; QA test `taxonomy_orphan_sweep_coverage` asserts detection across 4 consumer entity kinds.
12. A buyer console OR seller console OR public API attempt to write to `/ops/taxonomy/**` MUST receive HTTP 403 with `taxonomy_node_write_forbidden` (existing); logs MUST retain the attempt for ≥ 90 days per §6.8.
13. Dual-signoff events for taxonomy retirement MUST record both signing Ops users in the Audit Event `actors[]` array; reads of the audit row MUST preserve both user ids.
14. All taxonomy events registered in Appendix C (Notification Event Catalog) and Appendix G (PostHog) MUST match the emitted event_type string exactly; drift detection is asserted by CI test `taxonomy_event_catalog_consistency`.
15. The `ops_taxonomy_admin` and `ops_marketing_editor` roles MUST NOT be grantable to users with `account_type=service`; any such role-assignment attempt at the WorkOS layer MUST be rejected with `ops_role_requires_human_account` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403). QA test `ops_taxonomy_role_human_only` asserts: (a) a `POST /ops/roles/grant` with a service-account target and `role ∈ {ops_taxonomy_admin, ops_marketing_editor}` returns 403; (b) a daily role-audit sweep produces zero findings of service-account holders for either role across all environments; (c) a dual-signoff attempt where either signer is a service-account MUST be rejected with the same error before either signature is persisted; (d) every Taxonomy CMS Audit Event MUST carry `actor_account_type=human` and a non-null `actor_mfa_verified_at` within the session MFA TTL per §6.5; (e) any audit row lacking the human+MFA evidence pages the security on-call within 5 minutes of discovery.
16. Every `PATCH` against `/ops/taxonomy/nodes/:id` or `/ops/vocab/tags/:id` MUST enforce the per-field edit classification in §27.6.2: an attempt to set a **Structural** field (Taxonomy Node: `slug, kind, parent_id, visibility, residency_scope, deprecation_action, successor_id, authored_by_ops_user_id, version`; Controlled-Vocabulary Tag: `slug, taxonomy_node_id, origin`) in-place MUST be rejected with `taxonomy_field_edit_classification_violated` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422) *before* any write. An `ops_marketing_editor` that initiates a Create→Publish clone targeting a structural change MUST be rejected with `taxonomy_structural_edit_role_insufficient` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403). QA test `taxonomy_edit_classification_enforcement` asserts rejection for each structural field on both entity kinds and permitted success for each editorial field subject to the dimension-scoping in §27.6.2. The Appendix J `taxonomy_node_field_edit_classification` registry MUST match the field classification authored in §27.6.2; drift detection is asserted by CI test `taxonomy_field_classification_registry_consistency`.

### 27.6.10 Public Taxonomy Read API & Cache Contract {#27.6.10-public-taxonomy-read-api-and-cache-contract}

Sellers, partner integrators, SoftwarePage renderers, M9/M11 editorial pipelines, and third-party analytics tools need a stable read contract against the registry. §27.6.10 authors the public-read endpoints, the pagination and filtering rules, the edge-cache headers, and the backwards-compatibility contract when a node is deprecated. Read endpoints are publicly accessible without authentication for the `visibility=public` subset of the registry; authenticated-only endpoints surface `visibility=authenticated_seller_only` and `visibility=internal_ops_only` nodes (§4.5.4, §4.5.5 authoritative).

**Endpoint set.** All paths under `/api/v1/marketplace/taxonomy`. Rate-limit class `marketplace_taxonomy_read` (§32.4.5): 1200/min per IP (public) and 3000/min per Org (authenticated).

| Method | Path | Auth | Purpose | Cache |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| GET | `/nodes` | Optional | List taxonomy nodes, filterable by `kind`, `parent_id`, `state`, `visibility`, `residency_scope`, `updated_since`; cursor pagination (default 50, max 250); stable sort by `(kind, parent_id, sort_order, slug)` | 5 min edge cache on unfiltered reads; 60s on filtered with `updated_since` |
| GET | `/nodes/:id` | Optional | Retrieve single node by UUID; returns canonical row with aliases, parent ref, successor ref (if deprecated), SEO metadata (`visibility=public` rows) | 5 min edge cache; ETag header |
| GET | `/nodes/by-slug/:kind/:slug` | Optional | Resolve by human slug; returns `state, successor_chain` for a deprecated slug (max chain depth 3 per §4.5.4 AC 6) | 5 min edge cache; follows 301 redirect chain in-payload |
| GET | `/tags` | Optional | List Controlled-Vocabulary Tags filterable by `taxonomy_node_id`, `state`, `visibility`, `updated_since`; cursor pagination | 5 min edge cache |
| GET | `/tags/:id` | Optional | Single tag | 5 min edge cache |
| GET | `/changes` | Optional | Append-only change feed of `taxonomy.category_added|deprecated|retired|node.updated` in the trailing 30 days; cursor pagination; stable ordering by `emitted_at ASC`; used as a pull fallback when webhook delivery fails or the consumer is re-syncing a cold cache | No edge cache (always fresh from DB); private cache-control on response |
| GET | `/aliases/resolve?kind=&alias=` | Optional | Resolve an alias string to its canonical node; used by search surfaces (§27.3) and by public M9/M11 pages for de-ambiguation | 5 min edge cache |

**Response header contract.**

- `ETag`: strong ETag derived from `(kind, slug, version)` tuple; clients MUST honor `If-None-Match` for 304 responses.
- `Cache-Control`: `public, max-age=300` (unfiltered public reads); `public, max-age=60` (filtered with `updated_since`); `private, no-store` (`/changes`).
- `Last-Modified`: mirrors the node's `updated_at` in HTTP date format.
- `X-Sourcera-Taxonomy-Version`: the `feature_registry_version`-equivalent for the taxonomy registry (monotonic integer bumped on any `taxonomy.*` webhook fire); integrators can use this to detect mass-migration events and invalidate in bulk.
- `Link: <...>; rel="next"` for cursor pagination.

**Backwards-compatibility contract on deprecated nodes.**

- A `GET /nodes/by-slug/:kind/:slug` call for a `deprecated` slug MUST return HTTP 200 with a payload containing `state=deprecated`, `successor_slug`, `successor_id`, and `deprecation_action`; clients SHOULD follow the successor chain programmatically.
- A `GET` for a `hard_retire`d node past the 90-day window MUST return HTTP 410 with `taxonomy_node_retired` error body containing the historical slug and the terminal successor (if the chain terminates).
- A `GET` for a node in `state=draft` MUST return HTTP 404 from the public endpoint (drafts are Ops-only); authenticated Ops reads return HTTP 200 via the Ops Console route.

**Change-feed fallback contract (re-sync path).** The `GET /changes?updated_since=...` endpoint is authoritative for integrators re-building caches after a webhook outage or cold start. Event order MUST match webhook delivery semantic order (`taxonomy.category_added`/`deprecated`/`retired`/`node.updated` ordered by `emitted_at`); the endpoint is eventually consistent with the webhook stream within 30 seconds. Integrators MUST use this endpoint (not `/nodes?updated_since=...`) to re-hydrate a cache because `/changes` carries the deprecation payloads with full cascade metadata while `/nodes` carries only current-state rows.

**Listener SDK contract (recommended; not mandatory).** Client SDKs SHOULD:

- Refresh on `taxonomy.category_added|deprecated` webhook arrival.
- Treat `X-Sourcera-Taxonomy-Version` jumps ≥ 100 between consecutive reads as evidence of a mass migration; re-hydrate the full tag list for affected dimensions via the change-feed.
- Never cache for more than 5 minutes without revalidation.
- Fall back to `/changes` if webhooks are missed.

**Pagination invariants.** Cursor pagination uses opaque base64-encoded cursors per §32.3. `/nodes?cursor=...` MUST return stable ordering across pages even when the underlying set changes between calls; new rows added between pages surface on a subsequent call against the most recent `updated_since` watermark, not retroactively injected into prior pages.

**Public-read field projection.** The `visibility=public` projection of a Taxonomy Node includes: `id, kind, slug, name, short_name, description, long_description, parent_id, parent_slug, sort_order, icon_token, aliases, seo_metadata_json, state, version, successor_id (if deprecated), successor_slug (if deprecated), deprecation_action (if deprecated), updated_at, created_at`. It excludes: `authored_by_ops_user_id`, `editorial_notes_internal`, Ops-only audit metadata.

**Acceptance Criteria (Public Taxonomy Read API).**

1. `GET /api/v1/marketplace/taxonomy/nodes` MUST support cursor pagination with default 50 and max 250; oversize returns HTTP 422 `pagination_limit_exceeded` (existing).
2. `ETag` + `If-None-Match` negotiation MUST return 304 Not Modified when the node version is unchanged; QA test `taxonomy_node_etag_304` asserts.
3. `/nodes/by-slug/:kind/:slug` MUST return 200 with successor metadata for `deprecated` slugs and 410 for hard-retired slugs past the 90-day window.
4. `/changes?updated_since=<timestamp>` MUST return events in `emitted_at ASC` order with cursor pagination; QA test `taxonomy_changes_feed_ordering` asserts across 1000-event synthetic windows.
5. `X-Sourcera-Taxonomy-Version` MUST increment monotonically with every `taxonomy.*` webhook emission; QA test `taxonomy_version_header_monotonic` asserts.
6. Public reads MUST NOT expose `authored_by_ops_user_id`, `editorial_notes_internal`, or any `visibility=internal_ops_only` row; QA test `taxonomy_public_read_field_projection` asserts across all endpoint variants.
7. Edge-cache TTL MUST NOT exceed 300 seconds for unfiltered reads and MUST NOT exceed 60 seconds for `updated_since`-filtered reads; `private, no-store` enforced on `/changes`.
8. Rate-limit class `marketplace_taxonomy_read` (§32.4.5) MUST enforce 1200/min per IP (public) and 3000/min per Org (authenticated); breach returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After.
9. `/aliases/resolve` MUST match on the `aliases[]` array of `state=active` nodes and return the canonical node; HTTP 404 when no match and no fuzzy fallback (fuzzy resolution is search-path, not taxonomy-read-path).
10. After a `taxonomy.category_deprecated` webhook emission, the `/changes` feed MUST include the event within 30 seconds of webhook emission; QA test `taxonomy_changes_feed_webhook_convergence` asserts.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Integrator's webhook endpoint is unreachable for 6 hours; they miss 47 deprecation events.** Resolved: `/changes?updated_since=<last_seen>` returns all 47 events in order; integrator replays locally. If the outage exceeds 30 days (the `/changes` window), the integrator falls back to a full re-hydrate via `/nodes` plus consumer-side reconciliation against their FK-referencing rows.
2. **Edge cache serves a 5-minute-stale node after a deprecation.** Resolved: consumers use `X-Sourcera-Taxonomy-Version` as a cache-busting signal; a jump between consecutive reads triggers a `/changes` re-read. Worst-case 5-minute staleness is an accepted tradeoff against edge-cache efficiency. Time-critical consumers (write-path validators) bypass edge by calling with `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
3. **Slug collision from Ops typo.** Resolved: `(kind, slug)` unique constraint at `POST /ops/taxonomy/nodes` per §27.6.2; slug collision returns HTTP 409 `taxonomy_node_slug_collision` (existing in §4.5.4 family). Public read is not affected.
4. **Integrator rebuilds cache from `/nodes` instead of `/changes`, misses a deprecation's cascade metadata.** Resolved: public documentation (engineering docs + SDK changelog) explicitly calls out `/changes` as the canonical re-sync path. `/nodes` returns only current state; a consumer rebuilding from `/nodes` would miss the `deprecation_action`, `successor_id`, and cascade disposition. The consumer would converge eventually (subsequent writes against the deprecated FK would fail with `consumer_requires_approved_tag`), but integrators are strongly guided to `/changes`.
5. **Race between a consumer's `GET` and a concurrent deprecation.** Resolved: `ETag` reflects the version at read-time; if the consumer's subsequent write uses a stale tag, the write-path validation (§27.6.5) rejects. No lost updates.

### 27.6.11 Dimension-Specific Authoring Nuances {#27.6.11-dimension-specific-authoring-nuances}

Taxonomy dimensions are not interchangeable. Per-dimension constraints — residency immutability, certification verification, language locale codes, region geo-codes, integration-vendor canonicalization, employee-size-band numeric anchoring — govern how Ops authors each. This sub-section authors the per-dimension rules that §27.6.2's generic lifecycle does not capture, and resolves the one ambiguity in the generic lifecycle (where a dimension's semantics constrain the allowed state transitions).

**Dimension catalog.** The dimensions in the registry are:

| Dimension (`kind`) | Purpose | Authoritative Dimension Spec |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `marketplace_category` | Top-level buyer-facing category for Marketplace browse + CategoryPage (M9) | §4.4.7 |
| `capability_category` | Capability Declaration anchoring for sellers | §26.3 + §4.5.4 |
| `industry` | Buyer + Seller industry tagging | §26.1 |
| `certification` | Seller-held certifications (SOC2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR, ...) | §26.1 |
| `integration_vendor` | Integration-target vendor (Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack, ...) | §4.5.4 + M-series SEO |
| `language` | Locale for seller-surface internationalization | §27.6.11 (this subsection) |
| `region` | Geographic region for residency + Marketplace filter | §27.6.11 (this subsection) + §40.1 |
| `employee_size_band` | Seller Org size tier; used for buyer filter + cohort analytics | §27.6.11 (this subsection) |

**Per-dimension authoring rules.**

| Dimension | Slug Format | Aliases Rules | Deprecation Authority | Immutability Rules | External Verification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `marketplace_category` | `^[a-z0-9-]+$`; max 60 chars; top-level only (no `/`) | Up to 20 aliases; aliases in English only; case-insensitive | Dual sign-off when anchors `CategoryPage` with ≥ 90 days SEO history | Slug change forbidden post-publish; name changes allowed | N/A |
| `capability_category` | Same slug format | Up to 30 aliases; English + non-English permitted | Dual sign-off when ≥ 10,000 Capability Declarations reference | Slug change forbidden post-publish | N/A |
| `industry` | Same | Up to 15 aliases; prefer NAICS-aligned names | Single sign-off | Slug change forbidden post-publish | May cross-reference NAICS 2022; optional `naics_code` field in `seo_metadata_json` |
| `certification` | Same; slug MUST match ISO or framework identifier when available (`soc2-type-2`, `iso-27001`, `hipaa`, `gdpr`, `fedramp-moderate`) | Up to 10 aliases | Single sign-off; `hard_retire` forbidden on active certifications (redirect-to-parent only) | Slug change forbidden post-publish; issuer metadata (`certification_authority`, `framework_version`) required | Optional verification gate — §27.6.11 §2 below |
| `integration_vendor` | Same; slug derived from vendor canonical name | Up to 15 aliases; vendor tradename variants | Single sign-off | Slug change forbidden post-publish; `canonical_vendor_website_url` required | N/A |
| `language` | Slug MUST be an IETF BCP 47 tag (`en-US`, `es-ES`, `fr-FR`, `zh-CN`, `de-DE`, `pt-BR`, ...) | Aliases include common human names (`"English"`, `"Spanish"`) in each language | Single sign-off; deprecation forbidden if > 0 sellers declare the language | Slug = BCP 47 tag; MUST match the locale code the seller-surface i18n pipeline uses | BCP 47 registry (IANA) validation at write |
| `region` | Slug MUST map to ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 for country-level regions (`us`, `eu`, `apac`, `latam`, custom multi-country regions with namespaced slugs like `emea`); sub-country regions use `-<subdivision>` suffix (`us-ca`, `us-ny`) | Up to 10 aliases; common names (`"United States"`, `"European Union"`) | Dual sign-off if used as residency slicer (`residency_scope ∈ {us, eu, apac}` already) | Slug change forbidden; ISO 3166-1 / 3166-2 alignment required | ISO 3166 validation at write; Residency dimension values (`us`, `eu`, `apac`) MUST never be deprecated — they are platform-residency anchors |
| `employee_size_band` | Enum-like slugs: `solo`, `micro`, `small`, `midmarket`, `enterprise`, `global_enterprise` | Aliases may include numeric ranges | Single sign-off | Slug change forbidden; `min_employees` and `max_employees` required in `seo_metadata_json` | N/A |

**Residency-dimension immutability.** The `region` nodes whose slugs match the platform's authoritative `data_residency_region` values (`us`, `eu`, `apac`; sourced from §40.1 Residency Assignment) are immutable — they may NOT be deprecated, merged, or retired via the generic §27.6.2 lifecycle. An attempt MUST be rejected with `taxonomy_residency_region_immutable` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409). Adding a new platform residency (e.g., a future `apac_au` or `ca`) requires a coordinated §40.1 residency-setup release (new entity fields, new residency-partitioned workers, DPO sign-off) — the Taxonomy CMS alone cannot add a new residency slug.

**Certification verification gate (optional).** Sellers claiming a certification under a `certification` taxonomy node MAY (opt-in) submit attestation evidence (uploaded certificate PDF, auditor letter, certification authority URL). The evidence is routed to an Ops verification queue; upon approval, the Seller Profile's certification reference carries `verified_at` and `verifying_ops_user_id`. Unverified certifications render with a "Self-attested" badge on the Marketplace; verified certifications render without the badge. Verification is orthogonal to Seller Profile `verification_tier` (§26.1) — they are different dimensions. QA test `certification_verified_badge_rendering` asserts the badge gate.

**Language-dimension pre-requisite.** A `language` node transitions `draft → active` only if the corresponding BCP 47 tag is present in the platform's localization bundle (a new platform-scoped asset tracked under §22.x or §48.x localization infrastructure — Authored Extension candidate per the reconciliation log). Orphaned `language` nodes (slug valid per BCP 47 but no localization bundle) are rejected at publish with `taxonomy_language_localization_missing` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409).

**Region hierarchy enforcement.** Sub-country regions (`us-ca`, `us-ny`) MUST have a parent region at the country level (`us`) in `state=active`. Attempting to publish `us-ca` when `us` is in `deprecated` or `retired` state is rejected with `taxonomy_region_parent_inactive` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409). Deprecation of a country-level region cascades to its sub-regions (they enter `deprecated` in the same transaction) unless Ops explicitly decouples them with `decouple_subregions=true` in the Ops Console pre-flight dialog.

**Integration-vendor canonical URL.** Each `integration_vendor` node MUST carry `canonical_vendor_website_url` in `seo_metadata_json` (schema.org `sameAs` target for the IntegrationVendorPage rendering). URL MUST validate at write (resolvable DNS, HTTPS required, 2xx or 3xx response). Validation failure returns `taxonomy_integration_vendor_url_unreachable` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422). Ops may force-publish with `force_publish=true` when the vendor website is temporarily down; Ops audit row records the force-publish.

**Industry NAICS cross-reference.** An `industry` node MAY carry `naics_code` in `seo_metadata_json`. If present, the code MUST be a valid NAICS 2022 code (validated against the NAICS registry at write). Invalid codes rejected with `taxonomy_industry_naics_invalid` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).

**Acceptance Criteria (Dimension-Specific Authoring Nuances).**

1. Residency-anchor region slugs (`us`, `eu`, `apac`) MUST be immutable; deprecation attempts MUST be rejected with `taxonomy_residency_region_immutable` (HTTP 409).
2. Sub-country region publishing MUST require parent region in `state=active`; QA test `taxonomy_region_sub_country_parent_check` asserts.
3. Country-level region deprecation MUST cascade to active sub-regions unless Ops explicitly sets `decouple_subregions=true`; Ops pre-flight dialog MUST surface the cascade scope.
4. Language node publication MUST require BCP 47 tag validation AND presence of the localization bundle; missing-bundle rejected with `taxonomy_language_localization_missing`.
5. Certification verification evidence upload MUST route to the Ops verification queue and transition Seller Profile's certification reference to `verified_at` on approval; Marketplace rendering reflects verified-vs-self-attested badge.
6. Integration-vendor `canonical_vendor_website_url` MUST be DNS-resolvable and HTTPS at publish; validation failure rejected with `taxonomy_integration_vendor_url_unreachable`; Ops may force-publish with audit note.
7. Industry NAICS codes MUST validate against NAICS 2022; invalid rejected with `taxonomy_industry_naics_invalid`.
8. Marketplace category dual sign-off MUST apply when retiring a category anchoring a `CategoryPage` with ≥ 90 days SEO history; single-signoff attempts rejected with `taxonomy_action_requires_dual_signoff` (existing).
9. Certification `hard_retire` MUST be forbidden on `state=active` rows; only `redirect_to_parent` or `redirect_to_successor` permitted; violation rejected with `taxonomy_certification_hard_retire_forbidden` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409).
10. Language dimension deprecation MUST be rejected if > 0 sellers have the language declared in Seller Profile; rejection includes count in the error payload for Ops diagnostic.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Ops attempts to deprecate the `us` region to consolidate taxonomy.** Resolved: residency-anchor immutability blocks; Ops error payload directs to the §40.1 residency-setup release as the proper venue for residency restructuring.
2. **Seller uploads a spoofed certificate PDF claiming SOC 2 Type 2.** Resolved: verification queue performs manual Ops review; automated PDF-authenticity signals route to `automated_signal` abuse report via §27.8 if forged; verified-vs-self-attested badges communicate the distinction to buyers.
3. **Integration vendor's canonical URL returns 503 at publish (vendor outage).** Resolved: Ops may `force_publish=true`; an alert is scheduled for 24 hours later to re-validate the URL; if still down, the Ops audit row records the persistence. Surface badge or buyer warning is out-of-scope here (buyer-surface design decision).
4. **NAICS code changed between NAICS 2017 and NAICS 2022.** Resolved: validation uses NAICS 2022; Ops migrates legacy industry nodes during the quarterly Applied-ML / Ops review cycle; migration is a `redirect_to_successor` per §27.6.3.
5. **Seller declares Portuguese but only `pt-PT` exists in the bundle and the seller is Brazilian.** Resolved: Ops adds `pt-BR` per the localization bundle update release; seller receives `taxonomy.category_added` webhook and updates Seller Profile; no partial-match substitution is performed automatically (explicit selection only).

## 27.7 Acceptance Criteria {#27.7-acceptance-criteria}

These criteria cover the Marketplace surface area defined in §27.1–§27.5. Subsection-specific criteria for Match Score (§27.4), Tags & Controlled Vocabulary (§27.6), and Abuse & Takedown (§27.8) are authored within those subsections and are in force concurrently.

- Marketplace search returns results within 500 ms (p95) for authenticated buyer and anonymous public users; search index staleness ≤ 60 s on Capability Declaration or Seller Profile edits.
- Capability filtering correctly includes vendors with matching declarations; filter evaluation uses FK equality against approved Controlled-Vocabulary Tags (§27.6); freeform filter values are rejected with `consumer_requires_approved_tag`.
- Match Score is computed per the §27.4 learned ensemble (with Legacy Baseline v1 fallback for cold-start); every §27.4.10 acceptance criterion applies.
- EOI delivery confirmed within 30 seconds of seller click; Seller Org receives `eoi_received` notification and buyer surface renders acknowledgment; §4.5.2 state machine governs subsequent transitions.
- Pending EOIs auto-rejected when listing closes; auto-rejection preserves the EOI record with `reason=listing_closed` and is audit-logged.
- Marketplace tags are consistent vocabulary (no duplicates like "Cloud Security" vs. "cloud-security"); §27.6 governs enforcement, freeform rejection, and migration; every §27.6.9 acceptance criterion applies.
- Seller tag proposals moderated within 5 business days (§4.5.5 Review SLA); breach emits `vocab_tag.review_slo_breach`.
- Marketplace abuse reports governed by §27.8 and its acceptance criteria; 24-hour triage SLA; 7-day seller appeal window; dual sign-off required for `ban_scope=org_level_all_consoles`.

---

## 27.8 Marketplace Abuse & Takedown {#27.8-marketplace-abuse-&-takedown}

**Authoring Intent.** §27.8 operationalizes the Marketplace abuse-escalation workflow that the first-class Marketplace Abuse Report entity (§4.5.7) and the prose §45.3 Marketplace Abuse Escalation together describe, and extends both with: (a) explicit reporter-class handling, (b) a subject-kind scope matrix, (c) a severity matrix with response profiles, (d) a 24-hour Ops triage SLA and 7-day seller appeal window with hard enforcement, (e) closure dispositions with per-disposition effects, (f) ban-scope rules with dual sign-off for org-level bans, (g) a webhook catalog for lifecycle events, and (h) failure-mode handling for coordinated abuse, impersonation, and cross-residency triage.

This section does not duplicate the §4.5.7 field table, state machine, or rate-limiting rules; it treats §4.5.7 as authoritative for entity schema and enforces §45.3 as prose-level canonical workflow. Where §45.3 is less specific than §27.8 (e.g., on severity, ban scope, or webhook delivery), §27.8 is treated as the specialized Marketplace-surface canonical source per the Source-of-Truth hierarchy.

### 27.8.1 Scope & Cross-References {#27.8.1-scope-&-cross-references}

| Layer | Source | Role |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Entity | §4.5.7 Marketplace Abuse Report | Full field table, state machine, rate-limiting, duplicate detection, appeal workflow, retention. Canonical. |
| Prose workflow | §45.3 Marketplace Abuse Escalation | Narrative of abuse-report lifecycle and escalation authority. Canonical for narrative. |
| Marketplace surface extensions (this section) | §27.8 | Reporter classes, subject-kind scope matrix, severity matrix, SLA/appeal enforcement, closure disposition effects, ban-scope rules, webhook catalog, failure modes. Canonical for Marketplace-surface operational behavior. |
| Audit trail | §4.6.1 Audit Event | Every state transition and Ops action on an abuse report writes an audit row. |
| Signal detection | Summary C.100 Signal Integrity Monitor | Anomalous reporter velocity, reporter-org clustering, and automated-signal attestation route through SIM. |
| Vendor opt-out interaction | §4.5.6 | Opt-outs do NOT suppress abuse reports; subject identity preserved for Ops and appeal flows. |
| Paid surface — seller disputes qualitative label | §48.2.11, §27.4 failure mode 3 | Seller `qualitative_label_dispute` routes to §4.5.7 with `reason=misleading_claims`. |

### 27.8.2 Reporter Classes {#27.8.2-reporter-classes}

Reports may be filed by any of the following reporter classes. Each class has distinct rate-limits (see §4.5.7), authentication requirements, and subject-notification rules.

| Reporter Class | Auth Requirement | Rate Limit (§4.5.7) | Default Severity at Create | Notification Eligible |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `buyer_user` | Authenticated buyer session | 20/rolling-24h per Org | `medium` | Reporter receives confirmation + disposition; reporter identity NEVER revealed to subject |
| `seller_user` | Authenticated seller session | 20/rolling-24h per Org | `medium` | Same as buyer_user; reporter identity NEVER revealed to subject (prevents retaliatory abuse) |
| `anonymous_public` | Public Marketplace reader; captcha-gated; IP-hashed rate key | 5/rolling-24h per `reporter_ip_hash` | `low` | Reporter optionally supplies `reporter_contact_email` for follow-up; NO identity shared with subject |
| `ops_internal` | Ops session with `ops_content_admin` or `ops_marketing_editor` role | None | `medium` (editable on file) | Reporter_user_id is the Ops user; subject sees "Sourcera Ops review" — the specific Ops user is not identified in subject view |
| `automated_signal` | Service-account auth; emitted by Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100), template spam classifier (§48.4.5), or anti-impersonation worker (C.100) | None | Assigned by emitter (`low`–`critical`) | Subject sees "Automated signal review"; full detector metadata in `subject_snapshot_json` for Ops only |

**Eligibility refinements.**

- `buyer_user` MAY only report subjects they can see — i.e., Marketplace Listings not opted-out and public Marketplace surfaces. Direct-URL enumeration of non-public subjects is blocked.
- `seller_user` MUST NOT report themselves or their own Org's subjects; such reports are rejected with `abuse_report_self_report_forbidden` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409).
- `seller_user` reporting a competitor seller is permitted but flagged with `competitor_sabotage_risk_factor=true` for Ops review; SIM correlates reporter-org clustering (§27.8.10 failure mode 2).
- `anonymous_public` reports with no `reporter_contact_email` and default severity `low` are triaged on a best-effort basis (no individual follow-up); these reports DO enter duplicate detection and CAN escalate to higher severity based on volume.
- `automated_signal` reports MUST include a `detector_id` and `detector_confidence_score` in `subject_snapshot_json` (application-validated); Ops retains the right to override severity at triage.

### 27.8.3 Subject-Kind Scope {#27.8.3-subject-kind-scope}

Every Marketplace Abuse Report binds a single `subject_kind` and `subject_id`. The subject-kind enum (`abuse_report_subject_kind`) is authoritative in Appendix J. §27.8 defines the scope and effect of a report per subject kind.

| Subject Kind | Scope of Report | Downstream Effect on Upheld | Opt-Out Interaction |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `marketplace_listing` (§4.5.1) | A single Listing under a Seller Profile | `listing_hidden` / `listing_delisted` / `seller_warned` / `seller_banned` depending on disposition | Listing opt-out (§4.4.8 `scope_kind=specific_page`, `scope_ref_type=marketplace_listing`) possible; opt-out does NOT suppress the report flow |
| `seller_org_page` (§4.4.10) | Seller Org's aggregate public page | Page hide OR Org-wide listing hide; may escalate to `org_level_all_consoles` ban | Opt-out redacts identifying rows but report persists with `subject_snapshot_json` |
| `software_page` (§4.4.11) | A specific SellerSoftware public page | Page hide; companion listings hidden when parent SellerSoftware is implicated | Same as `seller_org_page` |
| `category_page` (§4.4.12) | Sourcera-authored editorial page — not a seller subject | Routes to editorial Ops (`ops_marketing_editor`); closure `editorial_correction` / `page_republish` / `no_action` | Not applicable (no seller) |
| `comparison_page` (§4.4.14) | Sourcera-authored comparison page | Routes to editorial Ops; disposition as above | Not applicable |
| `guide_page` (§4.4.13) | Sourcera-authored guide page | Routes to editorial Ops | Not applicable |
| `capability_declaration` (§26.3) | Seller-authored capability declaration (misleading claims, trademark infringement) | `declaration_removed` OR `seller_warned` OR cascade to Listing hide if declaration anchors the Listing | Opt-out does NOT suppress |
| `eoi_message` (§4.5.2) | Seller EOI message to a buyer (spam, solicitation, harassment) | `eoi_purged` (EOI record archived, buyer no longer sees it) + `seller_warned` or `seller_banned` on pattern | Not applicable (buyer-private) |
| `vendor_response_excerpt` | Bid response excerpt surfaced in a Public Selection Report (M2) | Redaction of excerpt in the M2 link; possible buyer-side notification per §48.5.2 | Vendor opt-out (§4.5.6) takes precedence; report may still be filed |

The `category_page`, `comparison_page`, `guide_page` subject kinds route internally to the editorial Ops queue; their closure disposition enum overlaps with `abuse_report_closure_disposition` but uses editorial sub-dispositions (`editorial_correction`, `page_republish`, `page_retracted`) registered in Appendix J under the existing enum. §27.8.7 handles both seller-bearing and editorial subjects.

### 27.8.4 Severity Matrix {#27.8.4-severity-matrix}

Severity is assigned at triage (Ops MAY update from the creator's default) and drives: content-visibility behavior pending review, Ops triage SLA, notification cadence, and whether the report can close without seller response.

| Severity | Content-Visibility Pending Review | Triage SLA | Ops Default Behavior | Can Upheld-Close Without Seller Response? |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `low` | Subject remains public during review | per §42.3.1.a | Triage queue; default `awaiting_seller_response` if subject notification warranted, else `dismissed` | No (except `duplicate_of_prior_report` or `no_action`) |
| `medium` | Subject remains public during review | per §42.3.1.a | Default `awaiting_seller_response` with subject notification | No (except `dismissed` or `duplicate_of_prior_report`) |
| `high` | Subject HIDDEN pending review (transition to `marketplace_listing_status=hidden` for listing subjects; `page_publication_status=hidden` for page subjects) within 60 seconds of severity assignment | per §42.3.1.a | Default `awaiting_seller_response`; in cases of clear-cut policy violation (banned content, known fraud signature, court order) — direct to `upheld` | Yes, for clear-cut categories |
| `critical` | Subject HIDDEN immediately on file (at `pending_review` entry if default severity is `critical`); Ops may additionally escalate to full Org suspension pending triage | per §42.3.1.a | Escalated path; dual sign-off required for `seller_banned` with `ban_scope=org_level_all_consoles` | Yes; may close direct to `escalated → upheld` without seller response on extreme cases (CSAM, court order, confirmed large-scale fraud) |

> **Numerical SLA values authority (D-6.2-001 remediation 2026-05-06).** The triage SLA durations are authored once in §42.3.1.a Per-Severity Triage SLA. This table cites by reference; inline restatement is forbidden by the `marketplace_abuse_sla_single_source` deploy-time validator.

**Default severity assignment rules (automatic).**

1. Reports filed by `automated_signal` with `detector_confidence_score ≥ 0.95` and `detector_id ∈ {csam_detector, court_order_ingest, known_fraud_signature_detector}` → auto-severity `critical`.
2. Reports with `reason ∈ {trademark_infringement, impersonation, fraud}` and the subject is a Seller Org with an active Certificate of Authenticity override (reserved, future use) → default `high`.
3. Reports matching ≥ 3 duplicate reports in rolling 24 hours for the same `subject_kind, subject_id` → auto-promote severity by 1 level (up to `critical`).
4. Reports with `reason=competitor_sabotage_risk_factor=true` (seller-to-seller) → default severity `low`; Ops explicitly reviews reporter patterns.
5. All other defaults: `medium` for authenticated-user reporters, `low` for anonymous-public reporters (§27.8.2).

**Severity escalation mid-review.** Ops may re-stamp severity at any time. Severity escalation from `medium → high` MUST re-hide the subject within 60 seconds if not already hidden. Severity de-escalation does NOT auto-restore a hidden subject; an explicit Ops action (`dismissed` or `awaiting_seller_response` with re-enable) restores.

**SLA breach handling.** Breach of the per-severity triage SLA stamps `sla_breach_at` and emits `marketplace.abuse_report.sla_breach` (per §27.8.9); the report remains open. After 72 hours past SLA for `high` or `critical` reports, the report auto-escalates to Ops management queue with a "Late-SLA Critical Review" flag.

### 27.8.5 Ops Triage SLA {#27.8.5-ops-triage-sla}

Triage is the first Ops action on a filed report — the transition out of `pending_review` to one of `awaiting_seller_response`, `upheld`, `dismissed`, or `escalated`. The triage SLA is measured from `created_at` (file time) to the first non-`pending_review` state transition, and is the severity-dependent value in §27.8.4. This SLA is distinct from the total-resolution SLO (see below).

**Triage SLA enforcement.**

- Ops Console abuse-report queue surfaces a per-report countdown; rows approaching SLA breach sort to the top with amber/red indicators.
- On breach, `sla_breach_at` is stamped with the breach time and the `marketplace.abuse_report.sla_breach` webhook fires.
- A report in `pending_review` for > 72 hours past SLA (any severity) paging Ops management queue.
- Ops management re-assigns if the assigned Ops reviewer is unavailable.

**Total-resolution SLO (Ops target; not customer-committed).** Per-severity values authoritative at §42.3.1.b; cited by reference here per the §27.8.4 numerical-singleton note above. The seller-appeal window is excluded from the resolution clock.

Appeal window (7 days from `awaiting_seller_response` per §27.8.6) is excluded from the SLO clock while the report is in `awaiting_seller_response`.

### 27.8.6 Seller Appeal Workflow {#27.8.6-seller-appeal-workflow}

On Ops transition to `awaiting_seller_response`, the seller Org's notification recipients receive an email + in-app notification containing (a) the `ops_decision_public_note`, (b) the `reason`, (c) a redacted summary of the report (reporter identity NEVER included), (d) the `subject_snapshot_json` (seller-side fields only), and (e) a magic-link to a signed-in appeal form. The appeal window is 7 calendar days from the `awaiting_seller_response` transition (enforced via `appeal_deadline_at`).

**Appeal eligibility.** The appeal form is accessible only to users with the Seller Org role `seller_org_admin` or `seller_org_owner` (registered in Appendix J; reused). Magic-link requires logged-in session match. Unauthenticated clicks route to sign-in.

**Appeal submission.** Seller submits `appeal_narrative` (0–4000 chars) and optional `appeal_evidence_attachments` (≤ 10 files, ≤ 25 MB each). On submission, `appeal_status → submitted` and the report transitions to Ops review for appeal decision.

**Appeal decision SLA.** 24 business hours from `appeal_status=submitted` to terminal appeal state (`upheld` or `overturned`). Breach emits `marketplace.abuse_report.appeal_sla_breach`.

**Appeal outcomes.**

- **`overturned`:** Ops finds the appeal persuasive; closure `dismissed` with `closure_disposition=no_action` OR `editorial_correction`; subject content restored (un-hidden) if previously hidden; reporter notified with the non-redacted `ops_decision_public_note`; `marketplace.abuse_report.dismissed` event fires.
- **`upheld`:** Ops affirms the original finding; closure disposition applied per §27.8.7; subject and reporter notified; `marketplace.abuse_report.upheld` event fires.

**Deadline enforcement.** If `appeal_deadline_at` passes with no appeal filed, the report transitions automatically to `auto_closed_no_appeal` with `closure_disposition` set at `awaiting_seller_response` entry time (default `listing_hidden` for `medium`/`high` severity; configurable by Ops per-case). The auto-closed state is terminal; post-deadline appeals are rejected with `abuse_report_appeal_expired` (existing; §4.5.7 AC 4; HTTP 410).

**Dual sign-off for specific appeal decisions.**

- Appeal `upheld → closure_disposition=seller_banned` with `ban_scope=org_level_all_consoles` requires dual sign-off (two Ops users with `ops_content_admin` role per §4.5.7 AC 5) even when the appeal is merely affirming a prior Ops decision.
- Appeal `overturned` that reverses a prior `seller_banned` does NOT require dual sign-off (Ops may act alone to restore).
- Appeal `upheld` with `closure_disposition ∈ {seller_warned, listing_hidden, listing_delisted}` does NOT require dual sign-off.

**Appeal restrictions.** A seller MAY appeal once per report; subsequent re-appeals are rejected with `abuse_report_appeal_already_submitted` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409). Post-closure, the seller MAY file a new report against the reporter if they believe the original report was itself abuse (`reason=competitor_sabotage`), which enters the normal §4.5.7 flow.

### 27.8.7 Closure Dispositions {#27.8.7-closure-dispositions}

Every terminal Ops closure (`upheld`, `dismissed`, `auto_closed_no_appeal`) requires a `closure_disposition`. The enum is `abuse_report_closure_disposition` in Appendix J. §27.8.7 specifies the per-disposition effect on the subject and downstream systems.

| Disposition | Subject Effect | Marketplace Effect | Billing/Pricing Effect | Audit / Notification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `listing_hidden` | `marketplace_listing.status=hidden` within 60 s; listing removed from browse, direct-link returns 410 Gone; SEO `noindex` | Search index excludes; SoftwarePage persists; Seller Org page persists | None | Seller + reporter notified with `ops_decision_public_note`; audit row; `marketplace.abuse_report.upheld` event |
| `listing_delisted` | `marketplace_listing.status=delisted` permanently; Listing cannot be re-published without Ops action | Similar to `hidden` but permanent | None | Same as `listing_hidden` |
| `seller_warned` | Subject restored (if hidden); `seller_org.strike_count += 1` (new denormalized field; registered in §4.4.1 — authored in reconciliation note below) | None | None | Seller + reporter notified; strike counter visible in Ops only; 3 strikes in 180 days trigger automatic escalation to severity `high` on subsequent reports |
| `seller_banned` | `seller_org.ban_state=banned`; scope per `ban_scope` (§27.8.8) | Full Marketplace suppression of the seller scope; all Listings hidden; SellerOrgPage / SoftwarePage 410 Gone; Capability Declarations hidden but not deleted | Per §34.11 (suspension billing rules): active wallet balance held; auto-topup disabled; seat-count billing paused | Seller + reporter notified; dual sign-off required on `org_level_all_consoles`; `marketplace.abuse_report.seller_banned` event |
| `no_action` | None; subject unchanged | None | None | Reporter notified; subject NOT notified unless report had reached `awaiting_seller_response` |
| `duplicate_of_prior_report` | None | None | None | `duplicate_of_report_id` populated; reporter receives "linked to original report" notification; original report carries the disposition |
| `editorial_correction` | For editorial subjects (CategoryPage, GuidePage, ComparisonPage); Ops edits the page per `ops_decision_note` | Page re-renders with correction; old version archived | None | Reporter + affected sellers notified per M9/M10/M11 editorial model |
| `page_republish` | Editorial subjects; Ops re-renders / reinstates after correction | Cache invalidated | None | Notification per editorial pipeline |
| `page_retracted` | Editorial subjects; Ops retracts the page permanently with `410 Gone` and canonical to category root | Sitemap removal | None | Notification |

**`seller_org.strike_count`.** A new field `strike_count` on the Seller Org entity (cross-ref authored in reconciliation log; logical field registered here with the following semantics): integer ≥ 0, incremented on each upheld `seller_warned` closure; automatic decrement by 1 every 180 days of clean record (no new upheld report against the Org); reaching 3 triggers auto-severity-promotion on subsequent reports per §27.8.4 rule #3 extension; reaching 5 triggers Ops management review with a recommendation to ban. The field is readable only in Ops surfaces; it MUST NOT be exposed on any customer- or seller-facing surface. DSAR implications: on seller Org deletion, the strike history is preserved as an Ops audit record with `subject_org_id` redacted per §4.5.7 retention rules.

**Disposition effect atomicity.** The disposition effect on the subject MUST be applied within 60 seconds of Ops closure and MUST be observable via the corresponding Marketplace surface (browse, direct-URL, sitemap) within 5 minutes (allowing for edge-cache propagation). Failure to apply within 5 minutes pages Ops and emits `marketplace.abuse_report.disposition_effect_slo_breach` (Appendix F alert class; new).

### 27.8.8 Ban-Scope Rules {#27.8.8-ban-scope-rules}

`closure_disposition=seller_banned` MUST be accompanied by `ban_scope` (enum `abuse_report_ban_scope` in Appendix J; existing values `listing_level`, `software_level`, `org_level_all_consoles`). §27.8.8 specifies per-scope effect.

| Ban Scope | Effect | Sign-Off Required | Reversibility |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `listing_level` | Specific Listing permanently delisted; seller may create new Listings for the same or other SellerSoftware | Single Ops (`ops_content_admin`) | Ops action to restore; seller may not self-restore |
| `software_level` | All Listings for the specific SellerSoftware permanently delisted; SoftwarePage set to `410 Gone`; seller may list other SellerSoftware | Single Ops (`ops_content_admin`) | Ops action to restore |
| `org_level_all_consoles` | Seller Org's Marketplace seller functionality disabled (Listings, SoftwarePages, EOI responses, Capability Declaration publishing); Buyer Console functionality on the Org's paired Buyer Console is NOT suspended (Buyer and Seller consoles are separate per §5.1); however Org Owner receives notification that their Seller Console is banned | Dual sign-off (two Ops users with `ops_content_admin` role); both signatures recorded in the Audit Event | Ops leadership action only; irreversible without Ops leadership approval |

**Cross-console firewall integrity.** A Seller Console ban MUST NOT cross-bleed into the Org's Buyer Console functionality. The Buyer Console remains fully available for the banned Org to run evaluations, issue EOIs, accept responses, and consume Marketplace content that does NOT require Seller-side publishing. This is a hard separation governed by §5.1 (Buyer/Seller Console split) and §4.7.1 Console Bridge rules; `org_level_all_consoles` is a misnomer retained for backwards-compatibility with the §4.5.7 enum — it means "all Seller-side consoles for this Org," not "Buyer + Seller both."

**Corollary for a true cross-console ban.** When Ops determines that a Buyer Console ban is also warranted (e.g., coordinated buyer+seller fraud by a single Org), a separate Buyer Console suspension is authored by `ops_compliance_admin` via §4.7.2 Vendor Disqualification cascade (for buyer-to-seller cascade) or a new `org_buyer_console_suspension` Ops action (authored in a future phase; flagged as an Authored Extension candidate in the reconciliation log). §27.8 does not automate cross-console bans.

**Dual sign-off mechanics.**

1. First Ops user (`ops_content_admin`) selects `seller_banned` with `ban_scope=org_level_all_consoles`, supplies `ops_decision_note`, and submits; report enters `pending_second_signoff` intermediate state (new enum value on `abuse_report_ops_status`: `pending_second_signoff`; Appendix J extension documented in reconciliation log).
2. Second Ops user (distinct; same `ops_content_admin` role) reviews and either co-signs or rejects the proposal. Co-sign transitions to terminal `upheld` with the ban effect applied; reject returns the report to `awaiting_seller_response` OR `escalated` per the reviewing Ops user's decision.
3. `pending_second_signoff` has a 72-hour window; unfilled second sign-off auto-returns to the prior state with a note.
4. Single-sign-off attempts to transition directly to `upheld` with `ban_scope=org_level_all_consoles` MUST be rejected with `abuse_report_ban_requires_dual_signoff` (existing; §4.5.7 AC 5; HTTP 403).

**Ban-state billing interaction (§34.11 reference).** A banned Seller Org's existing Seller wallet balance is held with no expiration; auto-topup disabled; recurring Seller-side plan-tier billing paused at the next anniversary (existing invoices remain payable); committed-spend contracts honor their original term with a pro-rata credit refund for the post-ban unused period. DSAR implications: banned-Org billing data is retained per the standard retention tier until explicitly purged (§40.2).

### 27.8.9 Webhook Events for Abuse Report Lifecycle {#27.8.9-webhook-events-for-abuse-report-lifecycle}

Every abuse-report lifecycle transition with customer-visible or integrator-visible impact emits a §31-conformant webhook event. All events use HMAC-SHA256 signing, idempotency via `event_id`, Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve, DLQ after 5 hard failures, payload ≤ 256 KB, and are registered in Appendix C and Appendix G.

**Events introduced by §27.8.**

| Event | Trigger | Delivered To | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.filed` | Row created with `ops_status=pending_review` | Subject's Seller Org (subscribed endpoints) for `medium+` severity with notification warranted; Reporter's Org (for buyer/seller reporter classes); Ops service endpoints | Subject version redacts reporter identity; `reporter_kind` is disclosed, `reporter_user_id` is NOT |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.triaged` | Transition `pending_review → awaiting_seller_response` OR `pending_review → escalated` OR `pending_review → upheld` (direct) OR `pending_review → dismissed` | Subject's Seller Org (if transitioning to `awaiting_seller_response` or terminal); Reporter's Org; Ops endpoints | Emitted on FIRST non-`pending_review` transition (triage) |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.appeal_submitted` | Transition `awaiting_seller_response → appeal_status=submitted` | Reporter's Org; Ops endpoints | Subject identity already known to Ops |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.appeal_decided` | Appeal `submitted → upheld` OR `overturned` | Subject's Seller Org; Reporter's Org; Ops endpoints | |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.upheld` | Terminal `upheld` from any path (direct, post-appeal, escalated) | Subject's Seller Org; Reporter's Org; Ops endpoints | Includes `closure_disposition` and its effect |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.dismissed` | Terminal `dismissed` from any path (direct, post-appeal) | Subject's Seller Org (if awareness warranted); Reporter's Org; Ops endpoints | |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.auto_closed_no_appeal` | `appeal_deadline_at` expired; transition to `auto_closed_no_appeal` | Subject's Seller Org; Reporter's Org; Ops endpoints | |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.escalated` | Transition to `escalated` from any non-terminal state | Ops endpoints only (management-level) | Customer webhooks NOT notified to avoid tipping off ongoing investigation |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.seller_banned` | Terminal `upheld` with `closure_disposition=seller_banned` | Subject's Seller Org; Ops endpoints | Includes `ban_scope` and `effective_at`; Reporter is NOT notified of the ban scope beyond `ops_decision_public_note` |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.sla_breach` | Triage SLA expired in `pending_review` OR Ops terminal-resolution SLO breached | Ops endpoints only | Not customer-visible |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.appeal_sla_breach` | Appeal decision SLA (24 business hours) breached | Ops endpoints only | |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.disposition_effect_slo_breach` | Disposition effect not applied to subject within 5 minutes of closure | Ops endpoints only | Paging alert |

**Payload schema — `marketplace.abuse_report.filed`.**

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_01HXY7Q...",
  "event_type": "marketplace.abuse_report.filed",
  "event_class": "marketplace_abuse_domain",
  "emitted_at": "2026-04-16T18:03:11.204Z",
  "report": {
    "report_id": "mar_01ABC...",
    "subject_kind": "marketplace_listing",
    "subject_id": "mlst_01DEF...",
    "subject_org_id": "org_01SUB...",
    "reporter_kind": "buyer_user",
    "reason": "misleading_claims",
    "secondary_reasons": ["spam"],
    "severity": "medium",
    "ops_status": "pending_review",
    "created_at": "2026-04-16T18:02:58.011Z",
    "appeal_deadline_at": null,
    "duplicate_of_report_id": null
  },
  "delivery_audience": "subject"
}
```

`delivery_audience ∈ {subject, reporter, ops}` is the per-subscription payload target. The subject-audience payload redacts `reporter_user_id`, `reporter_contact_email`, `reporter_ip_hash`, `ops_decision_note`, and `ops_assigned_to_user_id`; the reporter-audience payload omits `subject_org_id` and `subject_snapshot_json`; the ops-audience payload is full. Subscribers can filter audiences per the webhook subscription's `delivery_audience_scope` field (new §31 extension, authored in this phase's reconciliation log).

**Payload schema — `marketplace.abuse_report.upheld`.**

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_01HXY7Q...",
  "event_type": "marketplace.abuse_report.upheld",
  "event_class": "marketplace_abuse_domain",
  "emitted_at": "2026-04-16T21:45:00.204Z",
  "report": {
    "report_id": "mar_01ABC...",
    "subject_kind": "marketplace_listing",
    "subject_id": "mlst_01DEF...",
    "subject_org_id": "org_01SUB...",
    "reason": "misleading_claims",
    "closure_disposition": "listing_hidden",
    "ops_decision_public_note": "Listing removed for claims not substantiated in the submitted evidence.",
    "ops_decided_at": "2026-04-16T21:44:51.011Z",
    "ban_scope": null,
    "strike_increment": false,
    "subject_effect_at": "2026-04-16T21:45:00.010Z"
  },
  "delivery_audience": "subject"
}
```

**Payload schema — `marketplace.abuse_report.seller_banned`.**

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_01HXY7Q...",
  "event_type": "marketplace.abuse_report.seller_banned",
  "event_class": "marketplace_abuse_domain",
  "emitted_at": "2026-04-16T21:45:00.204Z",
  "report": {
    "report_id": "mar_01ABC...",
    "subject_org_id": "org_01SUB...",
    "closure_disposition": "seller_banned",
    "ban_scope": "org_level_all_consoles",
    "ops_decision_public_note": "Confirmed fraud pattern across multiple listings; Marketplace access permanently revoked.",
    "signed_by_roles": ["ops_compliance_reviewer", "ops_lead"],
    "signed_by_actor_pseudonyms": ["h_01HZBR8C9TKQ3F7...", "h_01HZBR8DEF456..."],
    "signed_by_ops_user_ids_count": 2,
    "effective_at": "2026-04-16T21:45:00.010Z",
    "billing_impact": {
      "seller_wallet_held": true,
      "auto_topup_disabled": true,
      "plan_billing_paused_at": "2026-04-16T21:45:00.010Z",
      "committed_spend_refund_plan": "pro_rata_credit_on_next_anniversary"
    }
  },
  "delivery_audience": "subject"
}
```

**Idempotency and ordering.** Consumers MUST be idempotent on `event_id`. The lifecycle sequence — `filed → triaged → (appeal_submitted → appeal_decided)? → (upheld | dismissed | auto_closed_no_appeal | escalated)` — is semantically ordered but delivered concurrently; consumers MUST handle out-of-order arrival and MUST re-fetch the authoritative report state via `GET /api/v1/marketplace/abuse-reports/:id` when resolving conflicts. The Ops audience event carries the full state; subject/reporter audiences carry the redacted state.

**Subscription model.** A customer Org MAY subscribe to abuse-report events via `POST /api/v1/webhooks` with event-type filters and `delivery_audience_scope`. The subscription is automatically scoped — an Org subscribing as a "subject" endpoint only receives events where `subject_org_id = subscribing_org_id`; as a "reporter" endpoint only where `reporter_org_id = subscribing_org_id`. There is no cross-Org leakage. Ops-only events (`*.sla_breach`, `*.escalated`, `*.disposition_effect_slo_breach`) are NOT exposed to customer webhook subscriptions.

### 27.8.10 Failure Modes Addressed {#27.8.10-failure-modes-addressed}

1. **Coordinated false-flag campaign by a competitor seller.** Resolved: §4.5.7 rate limits + duplicate detection + reporter-org clustering detection by Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100). Additionally: a Seller Org with ≥ 3 reports filed against competitor Sellers in rolling 7 days and ≥ 5 in rolling 30 days triggers an Ops SIM alert for review; the reports are still processed on their merits but Ops has an explicit signal. SIM may place a temporary hold on reports from the implicated reporter Org pending review (`reporter_hold_status=under_review`; existing §4.5.7 path enhanced).
2. **Seller attempts retaliatory abuse report against the reporter's Org.** Resolved: reporter identity is NEVER exposed in subject-audience webhook payloads or in the Ops subject-view; seller cannot retaliate against a specific reporter. A seller MAY file a new report against a buyer or seller Org they can identify through out-of-band means, which enters the normal §4.5.7 flow; SIM clustering catches retaliatory patterns.
3. **Subject is hard-purged (Org deletion) mid-review.** Resolved: §4.5.7 `subject_snapshot_json` preserves content at report time; the report can still reach terminal Ops decision. `subject_org_id` is redacted per §4.5.7 retention rules; disposition-effect hooks no-op gracefully.
4. **Appeal magic-link intercepted (email forwarded to wrong user).** Resolved: magic-link requires logged-in session match AND role match (`seller_org_admin` or `seller_org_owner`); unauthenticated clicks route to sign-in; magic-link expires at `appeal_deadline_at`. Additionally, the appeal form requires re-confirmation of identity (no pre-populated seller identity).
5. **Ops disposition effect fails to apply within 5 minutes (edge-cache propagation lag, worker outage).** Resolved: `marketplace.abuse_report.disposition_effect_slo_breach` pages Ops; Ops runbook enables direct cache-invalidation CLI tool. The authoritative state is the database row; cache lag does NOT affect Ops closure validity.
6. **Severity escalation from `medium → high` happens AFTER the subject has been public for hours.** Resolved: severity escalation triggers re-hiding within 60 seconds of the transition; reporter notified of re-evaluation; subject notified of content hide. The window between `created_at` and severity escalation is logged; Ops trend analysis of late escalations informs severity-default rule tuning.
7. **Buyer is a DSAR-erased user; report they filed now has null reporter identity.** Resolved: §4.5.7 retention rules — `reporter_user_id`, `reporter_contact_email`, `reporter_ip_hash` are redacted to synthetic anonymized values on reporter DSAR; report record preserved; disposition and audit integrity maintained; reporter notifications no longer reach the DSAR-ed user (graceful no-op).
8. **Cross-residency triage.** Resolved: report contents stored per the Org's residency assignment; cross-residency triage requires DPO approval per §4.5.7. Ops tooling surfaces a DPO-approval modal when the Ops triage queue selects a report whose residency does not match the Ops user's authorized scope.
9. **Appeal deadline falls over a weekend or holiday.** Resolved: `appeal_deadline_at` is absolute 7 calendar days; Ops-ops surfaces calendar cues but does not grant automatic extensions. Sellers experiencing legitimate inability to respond (e.g., holidays, org-wide account lockout) MAY request an extension via support; Ops MAY grant a one-time 7-day extension per report, logged in the audit row.
10. **Reporter wants to withdraw their report after Ops has already transitioned to `awaiting_seller_response`.** Resolved: reporters cannot unilaterally withdraw reports post-triage. Reporters MAY submit a "reporter correction" via Ops support, which Ops MAY use to inform `dismissed` disposition, but the report remains a first-class audit record.

### 27.8.11 Acceptance Criteria {#27.8.11-acceptance-criteria}

1. A Marketplace Abuse Report MUST be filed via `POST /marketplace/abuse-reports` with authentication matching `reporter_kind`; unauthenticated file attempts for `buyer_user`/`seller_user`/`ops_internal`/`automated_signal` return HTTP 401; `anonymous_public` requires captcha completion.
2. Default severity assignment MUST follow the §27.8.4 automatic rules; QA test `abuse_report_default_severity_matrix` asserts the matrix for 12 canonical input tuples.
3. Severity `high` report MUST transition subject to `hidden`/`page_publication_status=hidden` within 60 seconds of severity assignment; QA test `abuse_report_high_severity_subject_hide` asserts.
4. Severity `critical` report filed by `automated_signal` with `detector_confidence_score ≥ 0.95` MUST enter `pending_review` with subject immediately hidden; Ops triage SLA is 4 hours.
5. Ops triage SLA MUST be measured from `created_at` to the first non-`pending_review` transition; breach stamps `sla_breach_at` and emits `marketplace.abuse_report.sla_breach`.
6. Subject notification on `awaiting_seller_response` MUST be sent within 5 minutes; `appeal_deadline_at` MUST be exactly 7 calendar days after the transition; magic-link MUST be restricted to `seller_org_admin` / `seller_org_owner` logged-in sessions.
7. Appeal submitted after `appeal_deadline_at` MUST be rejected with `abuse_report_appeal_expired` (HTTP 410); post-deadline state MUST be `auto_closed_no_appeal`; re-appeal after terminal MUST be rejected with `abuse_report_appeal_already_submitted` (new; HTTP 409).
8. Closure `seller_banned` with `ban_scope=org_level_all_consoles` MUST require dual sign-off via `pending_second_signoff` intermediate state; single-signoff attempts MUST be rejected with `abuse_report_ban_requires_dual_signoff` (existing); both Ops user ids MUST be recorded **with full forensic fidelity** in the §4.6.1 Audit Event `actors[]` (Ops-side, never customer-audience); the customer-audience webhook payload `marketplace.abuse_report.seller_banned` MUST carry `signed_by_roles[]`, `signed_by_actor_pseudonyms[]` (per the §27.6.7 D-6.2-002 HMAC pseudonym contract), and `signed_by_ops_user_ids_count` only — raw Ops user UUIDs MUST NOT appear in the customer-audience payload. CI gate `abuse_report_webhook_no_ops_user_identity_leak` asserts. (D-6.2-002 remediation 2026-05-06.)
9. `ban_scope=org_level_all_consoles` MUST NOT suspend the banned Org's Buyer Console functionality; QA test `seller_ban_does_not_affect_buyer_console` asserts against a synthetic Org with active Buyer Workspaces.
10. Closure disposition effect MUST be applied to the subject within 60 seconds of Ops terminal closure and MUST be observable via Marketplace browse/direct-URL within 5 minutes; breach emits `marketplace.abuse_report.disposition_effect_slo_breach` and pages Ops.
11. Subject read of a report MUST NEVER include `reporter_user_id`, `reporter_contact_email`, `reporter_ip_hash`, `ops_decision_note`, or `ops_assigned_to_user_id` (reiterates §4.5.7 AC 7); QA test `abuse_report_subject_redaction` (existing) asserts.
12. Webhook subscribers MUST receive `marketplace.abuse_report.*` events with HMAC-SHA256 signing; idempotency on `event_id` is preserved across retries; DLQ entry is created after 5 hard failures; delivery is audience-scoped per `delivery_audience` field.
13. Reporter-audience payloads MUST NOT include `subject_snapshot_json` or `subject_org_id` in resolution-path events; QA test `abuse_report_reporter_audience_redaction` asserts.
14. `seller_org.strike_count` MUST increment on upheld `seller_warned` closure and MUST NOT be exposed on any customer- or seller-facing surface; the Ops-only read path MUST return the counter with decrement history.
15. Coordinated false-flag detection MUST emit a SIM alert when a Seller Org files ≥ 5 competitor-sabotage-risk reports in rolling 30 days; QA test `abuse_report_coordinated_false_flag_detection` asserts.
16. Cross-residency triage by an Ops user outside the report's authorized residency scope MUST require DPO approval; absent approval, the Ops action MUST be rejected with `abuse_report_cross_residency_triage_blocked` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403).
17. All `marketplace.abuse_report.*` events registered in Appendix C and Appendix G MUST match the emitted event_type string exactly; drift asserted by CI test `abuse_report_event_catalog_consistency`.
18. A buyer-console OR seller-console OR public API write attempt against the Ops-only endpoints (`/ops/marketplace/abuse-reports/**`) MUST receive HTTP 403 with `abuse_report_ops_write_forbidden` (new; Appendix I); attempts logged for ≥ 90 days per §6.8.

### 27.8.12 Cross-Report Aggregation, Evidence Bundles & Coordinated-Abuse Signatures {#27.8.12-cross-report-aggregation-evidence-bundles-coordinated-abuse-signatures}

Individual abuse reports are the unit of intake, but Ops investigations increasingly span multiple reports — e.g., a coordinated fraud ring filing reports against a competitor, or a counterfeit SellerOrg operating multiple SoftwarePages that each receive reports. §27.8.12 authors the cross-report aggregation primitive (`MarketplaceAbuseEvidenceBundle`), the coordinated-abuse signature catalog that SIM (Summary C.100) matches reports against, and the Ops tooling that lets a single Ops decision bind multiple reports to the same disposition.

**Entity — `MarketplaceAbuseEvidenceBundle` (Ops-scoped; platform-scoped; append-only after closure).**

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK | |
| `bundle_kind` | enum `abuse_evidence_bundle_kind` (Appendix J — new): `coordinated_false_flag`, `counterfeit_org`, `impersonation_pattern`, `fraud_ring`, `platform_policy_violation_cluster`, `cross_referencing_brigade`, `other` | NOT NULL | Bundle classification drives downstream SIM scoring and Ops runbook selection. |
| `subject_org_ids` | UUID[] | NOT NULL; length ≥ 1, ≤ 50 | Seller Orgs in scope of the bundle. |
| `reporter_org_ids` | UUID[] | nullable | Reporter Orgs when the bundle represents a reporter-clustering pattern (e.g., coordinated false-flag). |
| `linked_report_ids` | UUID[] FK → `MarketplaceAbuseReport.id` | NOT NULL; length ≥ 2, ≤ 500 | The underlying reports grouped into this bundle. |
| `sim_confidence_score` | numeric(3,2) in `[0.00, 1.00]` | NOT NULL | SIM's automated confidence in the bundle classification; Ops may override. |
| `ops_confidence_classification` | enum `abuse_evidence_bundle_ops_confidence` (Appendix J — new): `low`, `medium`, `high`, `confirmed` | NOT NULL; default `low` | Ops classification of bundle strength. |
| `ops_investigator_user_id` | UUID FK → `users.id` | nullable | Lead investigator. |
| `ops_secondary_investigator_user_id` | UUID FK → `users.id` | nullable | Required when bundle leads to dispositions crossing ≥ 3 Orgs (dual sign-off for multi-Org action). |
| `investigation_state` | enum `abuse_evidence_bundle_state` (Appendix J — new): `opened`, `investigating`, `consolidated_decision_pending`, `closed_upheld`, `closed_dismissed`, `closed_inconclusive` | NOT NULL; default `opened` | State machine below. |
| `consolidated_decision_json` | JSON | nullable; populated at `consolidated_decision_pending → closed_*` | Structured representation of per-report dispositions the bundle applies. |
| `residency_scope` | enum (`us`, `eu`, `apac`, `global`) | NOT NULL | Residency scoping for investigators (Ops user must be authorized to the bundle's residency); cross-residency investigations require DPO approval per §27.8.10 failure mode 8. |
| `opened_at` | timestamptz | NOT NULL | |
| `closed_at` | timestamptz | nullable | |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | timestamptz, timestamptz, UUID, UUID, timestamptz | per §4 conventions | `deleted_at` reserved for DSAR anonymization of investigator identity, not bundle deletion. |

**Indexes:** `(investigation_state, residency_scope, opened_at)`, `(bundle_kind, sim_confidence_score DESC)`, GIN on `subject_org_ids`, GIN on `reporter_org_ids`, GIN on `linked_report_ids`.
**Retention:** life of platform (Ops audit).

**Bundle state machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Actor | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `opened` | SIM signature matches OR Ops manually opens | At least 2 reports linked | SIM (automated) OR Ops | `marketplace.abuse_evidence_bundle.opened` webhook (Ops-only). |
| `opened` | `investigating` | Ops investigator claims | Investigator role `ops_content_admin` or `ops_compliance_admin` | Ops | |
| `investigating` | `consolidated_decision_pending` | Investigator proposes bundle-wide disposition | Disposition applies to `linked_report_ids[]`; structured in `consolidated_decision_json` | Ops | |
| `consolidated_decision_pending` | `closed_upheld` | Second investigator co-signs (when multi-Org scope ≥ 3 Orgs) OR single-Org scope investigator confirms | Dual sign-off enforced at multi-Org scope | Ops | All linked reports close with the bundle's dispositions in a single transaction. |
| `consolidated_decision_pending` | `closed_dismissed` | Investigator dismisses the bundle | All linked reports revert to their individual triage path | Ops | |
| `consolidated_decision_pending` | `closed_inconclusive` | Evidence insufficient for any bundle-wide action | Linked reports remain open on their individual tracks | Ops | |
| `investigating` | `opened` | Investigator returns bundle to queue | Cooldown 24h before re-claim by same investigator | Ops | |

**Applying a bundle disposition.** When a bundle closes `upheld`, the consolidated disposition is applied atomically to each linked report:

- Each linked report transitions to `upheld` with the bundle's `closure_disposition` (same enum as §27.8.7) per-report.
- `ban_scope=org_level_all_consoles` applied at the bundle level MUST require bundle dual sign-off (distinct from the per-report dual sign-off in §27.8.8; the bundle signoff co-signers count as the per-report signoff for each linked report).
- A single audit event is written per report with a cross-reference to the bundle id; bundle-level audit record written separately.
- Webhooks fire per report (`marketplace.abuse_report.upheld` etc.) AND at the bundle level (`marketplace.abuse_evidence_bundle.closed` Ops-only).

**SIM coordinated-abuse signature catalog.** Summary C.100 Signal Integrity Monitor maintains a library of signatures that detect cross-report patterns and auto-open bundles. The signature set is extensible; §27.8.12 authors the v7.0.0 seed:

| Signature | Detection Window | Trigger Rule | Bundle Kind | Initial `sim_confidence_score` |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
