## 27.9 Seller Signals (Anonymized Buyer Intent) {#27.9-seller-signals-(anonymized-buyer-intent)}

**Authoring Intent.** §27.9 operationalizes Summary §6.17 at the Marketplace surface. §4.4.18 SellerSignal defines the anonymized, aggregated buyer-intent record (platform-scoped, k=5 floor). §27.9 authors the three supporting entities that make the feature deliverable end-to-end — BuyerSignalOptInRecord (buyer-side opt-in record; default-deny), SellerSignalDeliveryPreference (seller-side per-Org delivery configuration), SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink (append-only audit of every disambiguation) — plus the aggregation-and-delivery pipeline, the explicit de-anonymization state machine, the Marketplace dashboard and weekly-digest delivery surfaces, the direct-invite-from-cohort flow, the webhook catalog, the API endpoint set, the DSAR/residency/erasure cascades, the acceptance criteria, the failure-mode register, and the Ops-tooling surface. All plan-tier gating cites §34.1.2 Seller Plan Tiers (rows "Seller Signals" and "CRM Sync") rather than re-stating numbers; CRM Sync as a delivery channel is authored fully in §31.9. Every new entity, enum, notification event, webhook event, API endpoint, PostHog event, error code, and glossary term is registered in the corresponding Appendix (J, C, G, I, K) per the authoring conventions.

### 27.9.1 Scope & Cross-References {#27.9.1-scope-&-cross-references}

| Concern | Authoritative Source | §27.9 Role |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| SellerSignal entity (aggregate row) | §4.4.18 | Consumed, not redefined; §27.9 adds three supporting entities |
| Buyer opt-in default posture & consent | Summary §6.17; §6.4 Consent Ledger | Authored at entity-level in §27.9.2 |
| Seller-side delivery configuration | — (net-new) | Authored at entity-level in §27.9.3 |
| De-anonymization audit link | §4.4.18 (pointer-only fields) + §4.5.2 EOI | Authored as append-only entity in §27.9.4 |
| k-anonymity floor (k=5) and distinctiveness secondary check | §4.4.18 Failure Mode #4 | Enforced through §27.9.5 pipeline + §27.9.7 delivery re-eval |
| De-anonymization triggers (EOI, direct invite from cohort) | Summary §6.17; §4.5.2; §4.4.18 | Consolidated in §27.9.7 state machine |
| Direct Invite from cohort | Summary §6.17 (authored extension — net-new flow) | Authored in §27.9.8; Scale+ plan-tier gated |
| Plan-tier gating (Seller Signals) | §34.1.2 row "Seller Signals" | Cited; never restated |
| Plan-tier gating (CRM Sync delivery channel) | §34.1.2 row "CRM Sync" | Cited; full channel authored in §31.9 |
| Data residency | §4.4.18 `residency_region_scope`; §6.8 | Enforced at aggregation and delivery |
| DSAR cascade on contributing buyer | §4.4.18 "Retention & DSAR" | Elaborated in §27.9.11 |
| Dual-Console Firewall | §7.2 | Enforced — seller-console reads never surface buyer identities; buyer-console reads of a buyer's own opt-in record are scoped to that buyer's Org |
| Webhook transport | §31.1–§31.6 | All §27.9 webhooks inherit HMAC-SHA256, `event_id`, Appendix F retry curve, DLQ after 5, ≤256 KB |

**Naming convention.** All §27.9 webhook event types are namespaced under `marketplace.seller_signal.*` and `marketplace.buyer_signal_opt_in.*`, carrying `event_class=marketplace_signals_domain` (new; Appendix J `webhook_event_class` extension). All §27.9 PostHog events mirror the webhook name with `.` replaced by `_` unless explicitly overridden in Appendix G.

### 27.9.2 BuyerSignalOptInRecord (Buyer-Console-Scoped, Default-Deny) {#27.9.2-buyersignaloptinrecord}

**Authoring Intent.** Buyers opt in to seller-signal contribution at the Workspace level (default off, per Summary §6.17). The record is the authoritative source for whether a given Workspace's intent activity may be aggregated into SellerSignal rows. Zero record OR `opt_in_state != active` MUST be treated as default-deny. Opt-in is buyer-console-scoped (never seller-console) and survives Workspace archive (terminal `revoked` transition is required to detach historical contribution). Consent version is snapshot-locked at opt-in time so that UX copy changes do not retroactively alter the consent scope.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | The buyer's Org |
| `workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Workspace | Scope anchor; opt-in is per-Workspace |
| `console` | Enum | Always `buyer` (per Appendix J `ai_operation_console` extended) | Explicit for firewall assertions |
| `opt_in_scope` | Enum | See Appendix J `buyer_signal_opt_in_scope`: `category_and_region`, `category_only`, `none` | `category_only` is the narrower default if the buyer opts in but withholds region; `none` is functionally equivalent to "no record" but is retained when the buyer explicitly sets it post-opt-in for audit |
| `category_ids` | Array\[UUID\] | 0–25 entries; FKs → Marketplace Category (§4.4.7) | Empty array with `opt_in_state=active` means "all categories this Workspace touches"; populated array restricts contribution to these categories |
| `region_inclusion_policy` | Enum | See Appendix J `buyer_signal_region_inclusion_policy`: `match_workspace_residency`, `residency_region_only`, `coarse_macro_region` | `match_workspace_residency` is default; `coarse_macro_region` collapses to continent to reduce distinctiveness risk |
| `opt_in_state` | Enum | See Appendix J `buyer_signal_opt_in_state`: `inactive`, `active`, `paused`, `revoked` | Default `inactive` on create; immutable terminal `revoked` |
| `opt_in_consent_version` | String | Semver; ≤ 32 chars; immutable once set | Snapshot of Consent Ledger (§6.4) version at opt-in time; drives DSAR interpretation |
| `opt_in_consented_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → User; redactable per DSAR | Person who toggled opt-in; MUST hold `workspace_owner` on `workspace_id` |
| `opt_in_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable; set on `inactive→active` | Immutable once set |
| `paused_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable; set on `active→paused` | Cleared on `paused→active` resume |
| `paused_reason` | Enum | See Appendix J `buyer_signal_paused_reason`: `buyer_self_paused`, `workspace_archived_auto_pause`, `dsar_recompute_in_progress`, `ops_forced_pause`; nullable | Authored so `active→paused` transitions capture the machine cause, not just the user toggle |
| `paused_until` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | When `paused_reason=buyer_self_paused` with an end date; null means indefinite |
| `revoked_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable; set on `*→revoked` | Terminal |
| `dsar_recompute_enqueued_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | Set when a DSAR event or opt-in change schedules a recompute sweep |
| `dsar_recompute_completed_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | Set when the recompute sweep finishes; enforces the 24-hour SLA per §27.9.11 |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | Must equal `opt_in_consented_by_user_id` at creation; divergence rejected |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | — |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete; distinct from `revoked` terminal — soft delete is Ops-only emergency tool |

**Scope Isolation.** Buyer-console-scoped; API read access limited to `org_owner`, `org_admin`, and `workspace_owner` on `workspace_id`. Seller-console reads of this entity are forbidden — cross-console attempts return `dual_console_firewall_violation` per §7.2. Guest roles have no visibility.

**Indexes.** `(org_id, workspace_id)` UNIQUE (one record per Workspace); `(opt_in_state, updated_at DESC)` for sweeps; `(dsar_recompute_enqueued_at)` partial on non-null for the DSAR worker.

**Retention.** Record retained for the life of the Workspace plus 180 days post-archive to support DSAR; terminal `revoked` rows retained full Workspace+180d for audit. Per §6.8 and §40.2, Consent Ledger snapshot retention inherits the Org-life+7y log. DSAR right-to-erasure MAY redact `opt_in_consented_by_user_id` to `redacted` but MUST NOT delete the record (audit integrity preserved per §6.8.5).

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (create) | `inactive` | `POST /buyer-signal-opt-in` | Default on create | Required row; idempotent on (`org_id`,`workspace_id`) |
| `inactive` | `active` | `PATCH .../activate` | Workspace Owner authenticated; `opt_in_consent_version` valid | Sets `opt_in_at`, snapshots consent version |
| `active` | `paused` | `PATCH .../pause` OR auto on Workspace archive | Records `paused_reason`, `paused_until` if provided | Aggregation pipeline excludes Workspace until `paused→active` OR `paused→revoked` |
| `paused` | `active` | `PATCH .../resume` OR auto on Workspace un-archive | `paused_reason != ops_forced_pause` (Ops must release) | Re-snapshots consent version if drifted (§27.9.11) |
| `active` OR `paused` | `revoked` | `PATCH .../revoke` OR DSAR right-to-erasure cascade | Any authorized path | Terminal; triggers §27.9.11 recompute |
| `active` OR `paused` OR `revoked` | `active` | NOT PERMITTED from `revoked` | Revoked is terminal; new opt-in requires new record (new `id`, new consent version) | Asserts that consent cannot be implicitly re-asserted without a fresh user action |

**Validation.** An opt-in to categories the Workspace has never touched is accepted (predictive opt-in is allowed); an opt-in with `region_inclusion_policy=residency_region_only` but the Workspace's Org residency is `global` is rejected with `buyer_signal_opt_in_region_policy_invalid` (Appendix I).

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Workspace Owner opts in, is later DSAR-erased.** Resolved: `opt_in_consented_by_user_id` redacted to `redacted`; record retained; Consent Ledger snapshot version persists and anchors the legal basis of prior aggregation; DSAR cascade in §27.9.11 handles re-computation.
2. **Workspace archived with `opt_in_state=active`.** Resolved: auto-transition to `paused` with `paused_reason=workspace_archived_auto_pause`; aggregation excludes Workspace contribution from the current period forward; historical contributions within the Signal Period remain valid (per §27.9.5).
3. **Buyer opts in, then changes mind within 60 seconds (accidental toggle).** Resolved: `active→paused` or `active→revoked` is available immediately via the same UI control; aggregation pipeline only consumes opt-in records whose `opt_in_at ≤ signal_period_start - 24h` (cool-down per §27.9.5.4) — recent opt-ins do NOT contribute to the next period, so the racy toggle cannot leak signal.
4. **Ops needs to quarantine an Org's opt-in (suspected abuse / court order).** Resolved: Ops forces `paused` with `paused_reason=ops_forced_pause`; buyer cannot resume without Ops release; per-Org audit event emitted.

### 27.9.3 SellerSignalDeliveryPreference (Seller-Console-Scoped) {#27.9.3-sellersignaldeliverypreference}

**Authoring Intent.** Per-Org (not per-user) seller-side configuration for where and how SellerSignal rows are delivered. Required to exist before any channel delivery occurs; seller Orgs without a record receive the platform default (dashboard-only, no digest, no CRM sync). Exactly one active row per Seller Org. Plan-tier entitlement is evaluated at delivery time against this row, not at authoring time — so a downgrade gracefully downgrades delivery without requiring the seller to re-author preferences.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization; UNIQUE on non-deleted rows | Seller Org |
| `console` | Enum | Always `seller` | Explicit for firewall assertions |
| `dashboard_enabled` | Boolean | Default `true` | Platform default on create |
| `weekly_digest_enabled` | Boolean | Default `false` | Gated at delivery time by `seller_plan_tier ≥ seller_starter` |
| `real_time_enabled` | Boolean | Default `false` | Gated at delivery time by `seller_plan_tier ≥ seller_scale` |
| `real_time_api_enabled` | Boolean | Default `false` | Gated at delivery time by `seller_plan_tier = seller_enterprise` |
| `crm_sync_channel_enabled` | Boolean | Default `false` | Gated at delivery time by `seller_plan_tier ≥ seller_growth` AND an active `CRMSyncConnection` per §31.9 |
| `subscribed_category_ids` | Array\[UUID\] | 0–200 entries; FKs → Marketplace Category | Empty means "all categories matching Seller footprint"; populated narrows |
| `subscribed_region_codes` | Array\[String\] | 0–50 entries; ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 OR macro-region | Empty means "all regions matching Seller residency eligibility" |
| `subscribed_industry_codes` | Array\[String\] | 0–50 entries; NAICS 2-digit OR taxonomy slug | Empty means "all industries" |
| `digest_day_of_week` | Enum | See Appendix J `day_of_week` (existing); default `monday` | Used when `weekly_digest_enabled=true` |
| `digest_timezone` | String | IANA TZ string; default derived from Org residency | `UTC` if residency is `global` |
| `suppression_render_mode` | Enum | See Appendix J `seller_signal_suppression_render_mode`: `omit`, `show_as_insufficient_data` | Dashboard/digest behavior when k-anon floor not met OR distinctiveness veto |
| `real_time_channel_rate_limit_per_min` | Integer | Default 30; range 1–200 | Seller Scale+ only; applies to in-app toast + API poll rate |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Seller User ID; `seller_org_admin` or `org_owner` | Role-checked |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Seller User ID | — |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete; creates platform-default delivery until a replacement row is authored |

**Scope Isolation.** Seller-console-scoped; buyer-console reads forbidden (cross-console attempts return `dual_console_firewall_violation`). Read/write gated by `seller_org_admin` OR `org_owner`; `seller_marketing_editor` has read but not write (publishing-oriented role, not delivery-channel-ops).

**Indexes.** `(org_id)` UNIQUE partial on `deleted_at IS NULL`; `(weekly_digest_enabled, digest_day_of_week)` partial for the digest scheduler.

**Validation.**

- `real_time_enabled=true` AND `seller_plan_tier < seller_scale` rejected with `seller_signal_channel_requires_plan_upgrade` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422). The seller MAY pre-configure on a lower tier, but the flag is clamped to `false` at write time and the UI surfaces the upgrade CTA.
- `real_time_api_enabled=true` AND `seller_plan_tier != seller_enterprise` rejected with the same error code.
- `crm_sync_channel_enabled=true` AND no active `CRMSyncConnection` rejected with `crm_sync_channel_requires_active_connection` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409). Once a connection is authored per §31.9, the seller MAY enable this channel.
- Plan downgrade grace: if the Org downgrades (§34.12) and the active preference row references higher-tier channels, the row is NOT auto-mutated; instead, delivery-time gating silently suppresses the now-ineligible channel for a **14-day grace** (§34.12.6 standard grace pattern), during which a UI banner prompts re-configuration. After the grace, the flags are clamped to `false` at the next `PATCH`.

**Retention.** Org-life + 7 years (audit alignment with §34.1.3 plan-tier history).

### 27.9.4 SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink (Append-Only, Marketplace-Scoped) {#27.9.4-sellersignaldeanonymizationlink}

**Authoring Intent.** Every transition from "anonymized aggregate" to "identifiable buyer → identifiable seller" MUST materialize exactly one row here. The row is append-only (no mutation, no soft delete) because every disambiguation is a first-class audit event required for GDPR accountability, legal defensibility in abuse investigations, and Pricing Strategy §11 "billing is shared; data is not" posture. The pointer-only fields on §4.4.18 SellerSignal (`de_anonymized_eoi_id`, `de_anonymized_target_seller_org_id`, `de_anonymized_at`) are reconciled nightly against this table; drift is an Ops-paging condition.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `seller_signal_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → SellerSignal (§4.4.18) | The aggregate being disambiguated |
| `triggering_buyer_org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | The buyer Org whose identity is being revealed |
| `triggering_buyer_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Workspace | The originating Workspace |
| `target_seller_org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | Single seller Org receiving the disambiguation |
| `de_anon_trigger` | Enum | See Appendix J `seller_signal_de_anon_trigger`: `eoi_submitted`, `direct_invite_from_cohort`, `ops_investigation_disclosure` | `ops_investigation_disclosure` is reserved for §4.5.7 abuse-response cross-walks and requires DPO sign-off |
| `triggering_eoi_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → EOI Record (§4.5.2); nullable; required when `de_anon_trigger=eoi_submitted` | Atomic write with EOI creation (§27.9.7) |
| `triggering_target_account_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Direct Invite Target Account (new sub-resource — see §27.9.8); nullable; required when `de_anon_trigger=direct_invite_from_cohort` | Atomic write with direct-invite creation |
| `ops_investigation_case_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; required when `de_anon_trigger=ops_investigation_disclosure` | FK → Ops Investigation Case (existing; §4.5.7) |
| `dpo_approval_audit_event_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; required when `de_anon_trigger=ops_investigation_disclosure` | Points to the DPO sign-off audit row |
| `de_anonymized_at` | Timestamp | UTC; immutable | Set at row creation; matches `seller_signal.de_anonymized_at` after nightly reconciliation |
| `disclosed_fields` | Array\[String\] | Enum-subset of SellerSignal fields that were disclosed as part of the trigger | Buyer Org name, buyer primary domain, buyer industry code, timeline band, intent strength, category list, contact — varies by trigger |
| `redacted_fields` | Array\[String\] | Complement of `disclosed_fields` | Explicit redaction record for DSAR |
| `legal_basis_ref` | Enum | See Appendix J `seller_signal_de_anon_legal_basis`: `buyer_explicit_eoi`, `buyer_explicit_direct_invite`, `ops_dpo_approved_investigation` | Legal basis that authorized this disclosure |
| `audit_event_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Audit Event | Always populated; full actor/actee chain |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC; equals `de_anonymized_at` |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | The user whose action triggered (buyer for EOI/direct-invite; Ops user for investigation disclosure) |

**Scope Isolation.** Marketplace-domain (not console-pooled per §7.2): buyers see their own rows on their own Workspace's audit timeline; sellers see their own rows on the Seller Dashboard "Active Buyer Intent" detail view, scoped to `target_seller_org_id = viewer_org_id`. Ops sees all rows. Cross-buyer or cross-seller reads forbidden.

**Indexes.** `(seller_signal_id)`; `(target_seller_org_id, created_at DESC)` for seller-side read; `(triggering_buyer_org_id, created_at DESC)` for buyer-side audit; `(triggering_eoi_id)` partial; `(triggering_target_account_id)` partial; UNIQUE (`seller_signal_id`, `triggering_buyer_workspace_id`, `target_seller_org_id`, `de_anon_trigger`) to prevent duplicate disclosures from concurrent EOI/invite retries.

**Immutability.** No `updated_at`; no mutations permitted. Corrections (e.g., the triggering EOI is later redacted) do NOT alter the link — a redaction audit event is written separately.

**Retention.** Org-life + 7 years (legal defensibility; DSAR right-to-erasure redacts buyer/seller identity FK columns to synthetic anonymized values but retains the row per §6.8.5 "audit integrity exemption").

**Reconciliation.** A nightly job asserts: for every `SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink` row, `SellerSignal.de_anonymized_eoi_id` OR `SellerSignal.de_anonymized_target_seller_org_id` MUST be populated consistently. Drift triggers C.100 Signal Integrity Monitor alert `seller_signal_de_anon_drift_detected` (new) and Ops paging.

### 27.9.5 Aggregation & k-Anonymity Enforcement Pipeline {#27.9.5-aggregation-&-k-anonymity-enforcement-pipeline}

SellerSignal rows are produced by the `seller_signal_aggregation` capability (registered in the Capability Registry per §4.8.2; platform-owned AIOperation, billed to the Sourcera internal cost center). The pipeline executes on a rolling 7-day window (Signal Period = `signal_period_end - signal_period_start`, default 7 days) per (category_id, region_code, industry_code, company_size_band) aggregation key.

**Pipeline stages.**

1. **Opt-in harvest.** Query `BuyerSignalOptInRecord` rows where `opt_in_state='active'` AND `opt_in_at ≤ signal_period_start - 24h` (the 24-hour cool-down from §27.9.2 Failure Mode #3). Exclude `paused` and `revoked`. Records with `paused_until > signal_period_end` are treated as `paused` for the entire period.
2. **Activity collection.** For each eligible Workspace, collect the Workspace's phase-progression events and category touches within the Signal Period. Apply `opt_in_scope` filter (`category_and_region` vs `category_only`) and `region_inclusion_policy` (`residency_region_only` suppresses region field; `coarse_macro_region` collapses to continent).
3. **Aggregation bucket assignment.** Assign each Workspace's contribution to a (category_id, region_code, industry_code, company_size_band, timeline_band, intent_strength) bucket per §4.4.18.
4. **k-anonymity floor check.** For each bucket, compute `signal_cohort_count` = DISTINCT buyer Org count; `contributing_workspace_count` = DISTINCT Workspace count. If `signal_cohort_count < 5`, set `suppressed_reason='k_anon_floor_not_met'`, `k_anon_satisfied=false`.
5. **Distinctiveness secondary check (§4.4.18 Failure Mode #4).** Even when `signal_cohort_count ≥ 5`, compute a distinctiveness score: the ratio of the smallest-bucket count to the largest-bucket count across the cross-tab (region × industry × size). If the bucket has ≥ 4 dimensions pinned to unique-ish values (e.g., `region_code='IS'` + `industry_code='72'` + `company_size_band='1-50'`), and the distinctiveness score exceeds the threshold configured via C.97 Baseline Assumption Manager (default 0.85), the bucket is suppressed with `suppressed_reason='distinctiveness_veto'` (new enum value — Appendix J extension to `seller_signal_suppressed_reason`).
6. **Residency enforcement.** For every contributing opt-in, the Workspace's Org residency MUST be compatible with `residency_region_scope`. Cross-residency contribution (e.g., EU Workspace into a `us_only` aggregate) aborts the bucket with `suppressed_reason='residency_mismatch'`.
7. **Vendor opt-out scrub.** Every seller target of potential delivery is cross-checked against the §3.5 Vendor Opt-Out Registry (`vendor_opt_out_registry`). If any element of the bucket's delivery target set has an active opt-out flag for the category, the aggregate is still produced but `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` is stamped and delivery to that seller is blocked at §27.9.6 delivery stage.
8. **Expiry stamping.** `expires_at = generated_at + 30 days` (§4.4.18 default). Signals are refreshed on the weekly cadence; expired signals never deliver.

**Atomicity.** The pipeline is transactional per aggregation bucket — partial aggregation writes are forbidden. A residency violation or k-anon failure during aggregation aborts the bucket write (emits `seller_signal.aggregation.aborted` internal event; external webhook NOT emitted). A distinctiveness veto produces a row with `suppressed_reason='distinctiveness_veto'` and emits `marketplace.seller_signal.cohort_fell_below_floor` with `reason='distinctiveness_veto'` to alert the Seller even though no delivery occurs (authored extension — Sellers using the real-time API endpoint need to know their query would have returned a cohort but was suppressed, to avoid silent data holes).

**Delivery re-evaluation.** k-anon and distinctiveness checks MUST re-run at delivery time (not only at aggregation time). Between aggregation and delivery, a DSAR-driven recompute may have dropped `signal_cohort_count` below 5 — the delivery layer treats the freshly recomputed count as authoritative and MUST NOT deliver a stale aggregate that was k-anon-safe at aggregation time but is not at delivery time. The delivery-time re-evaluation is the authoritative enforcement; aggregation-time is a fast-path optimization.

**Delivery-time snapshot-age bound.** The delivery-time recompute of `signal_cohort_count` and the distinctiveness score MUST operate against a `cohort_count_snapshot` whose `snapshot_at` is within **60 seconds** of the delivery request (`t_delivery - snapshot_at ≤ 60s`), aligned with the §27.10.4 Vendor Opt-Out enforcement latency budget (`t_opt_out_commit` → redacted render ≤ 60s). If no snapshot within budget exists, the delivery path MUST synchronously trigger a fresh recompute before delivery and block the response on its completion; timeout of this synchronous recompute past a hard 5-second deadline forces `suppressed_reason='recompute_deadline_exceeded'` (new enum — Appendix J extension to `seller_signal_suppressed_reason`) and emits `marketplace.seller_signal.suppressed` to the Seller. The bound applies to every delivery channel enumerated in §27.9.6 (dashboard render, digest dispatch, real-time toast + API poll, CRM Sync handoff).

#### 27.9.5.1 `k_anon_satisfied` State Machine (Per-Row) {#27.9.5.1-k-anon-satisfied-state-machine}

The `k_anon_satisfied` flag on a SellerSignal row is a computed boolean whose transitions are the authoritative audit artifact for k-anonymity enforcement. The pipeline (§27.9.5 stages 4–5) computes the value at aggregation time; the delivery path re-evaluates at render time; the nightly drift sweep (§48.4.7) re-asserts against existing rows. The complete From/To transition enumeration is the canonical source-of-truth for engineering (when to write), QA (what to test), and Trust & Safety (what to audit).

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `unevaluated` | `satisfied` | Aggregation pipeline §27.9.5 stages 1–8 complete for the bucket | `signal_cohort_count ≥ 5` AND distinctiveness score ≤ §27.9.5 stage 5 threshold AND `residency_region_scope` compatibility holds AND no aggregation-time vendor opt-out stops bucket write | Row materialized with `k_anon_satisfied=true`, `suppressed_reason=NULL`, `delivered_ever=false`. Delivery permitted subject to delivery-time re-evaluation. |
| `unevaluated` | `suppressed_k_anon` | Pipeline stage 4 | `signal_cohort_count < 5` at aggregation time | Row materialized with `k_anon_satisfied=false`, `suppressed_reason='k_anon_floor_not_met'`. No delivery. Webhook `marketplace.seller_signal.cohort_fell_below_floor` MAY fire on late-opt-in transition (see `suppressed_k_anon → satisfied`). |
| `unevaluated` | `suppressed_distinctiveness` | Pipeline stage 5 | `signal_cohort_count ≥ 5` AND distinctiveness score > threshold | `k_anon_satisfied=false`, `suppressed_reason='distinctiveness_veto'`. Webhook `marketplace.seller_signal.cohort_fell_below_floor` with `reason='distinctiveness_veto'` fires. No delivery. |
| `unevaluated` | `suppressed_residency` | Pipeline stage 6 | Cross-residency contribution detected | Bucket aborted, `seller_signal.aggregation.aborted` internal event emitted. Row either not materialized or materialized with `k_anon_satisfied=false`, `suppressed_reason='residency_mismatch'`. No delivery. |
| `satisfied` | `suppressed_k_anon_at_delivery` | Delivery-time re-evaluation §27.9.5 | `signal_cohort_count < 5` at `t_delivery` (post-DSAR recompute, late opt-in revocation, etc.) | Row's `k_anon_satisfied` flag flips to `false` at render time; persistent field `suppressed_at_delivery_reason='k_anon_floor_not_met'` is stamped on the row. Subsequent deliveries of the same row remain suppressed until a nightly sweep re-flips (see `suppressed_k_anon_at_delivery → satisfied`). `marketplace.seller_signal.suppressed` fires with `suppression_reason='k_anon_floor_not_met'`. |
| `satisfied` | `suppressed_distinctiveness_at_delivery` | Delivery-time re-evaluation §27.9.5 | Distinctiveness score at `t_delivery` exceeds threshold (typically after a skew-inducing opt-in / DSAR recompute) | Same persistence pattern as above; `suppressed_at_delivery_reason='distinctiveness_veto'`; `marketplace.seller_signal.suppressed` fires with `suppression_reason='distinctiveness_veto'`. |
| `satisfied` | `suppressed_vendor_opt_out_at_delivery` | Delivery-time re-evaluation §27.9.5 stage 7 (registry re-probe) | Target Seller Org has active vendor opt-out for the category at `t_delivery` | Row remains `k_anon_satisfied=true` (k-anon is a cohort property, independent of opt-out), but delivery is blocked. Expressed in the row as `vendor_opt_out_honored_at=NOW()` per §27.9.5 stage 7 and the separate `suppressed_at_delivery_reason='vendor_opt_out'`. `marketplace.seller_signal.suppressed` fires with `suppression_reason='vendor_opt_out'`. NOTE: the `k_anon_satisfied` flag itself does NOT transition on this trigger; the transition is enumerated here because the delivery is blocked and the audit ledger must capture which gate fired. |
| `satisfied` | `suppressed_recompute_deadline` | Delivery-time synchronous recompute exceeds 5s hard deadline | Stale snapshot AND synchronous recompute fails to complete in time | `suppressed_at_delivery_reason='recompute_deadline_exceeded'`; `marketplace.seller_signal.suppressed` fires with the same reason; an internal alert `seller_signal_recompute_deadline_breach` fires to Ops. Does NOT flip `k_anon_satisfied` (we can't prove it's below the floor — we simply refuse to answer without proof it's at or above). |
| `suppressed_k_anon` | `satisfied` | Nightly drift sweep §48.4.7 re-runs pipeline stages 4–5 and finds the bucket now satisfies | Late opt-in arrivals pushed `signal_cohort_count ≥ 5` without violating distinctiveness | Row's `k_anon_satisfied` flips to `true`, `suppressed_reason` cleared. Row becomes deliverable on subsequent requests. No webhook fires on this transition (we do NOT emit a "you're now eligible" event because it would leak the prior cohort's membership change). |
| `suppressed_distinctiveness` | `satisfied` | Nightly drift sweep | Distinctiveness score recomputed to ≤ threshold | Same flip; no webhook. |
| `suppressed_k_anon_at_delivery` | `satisfied` | Nightly drift sweep | Cohort recovered AND delivery-time factors stable | Row re-deliverable; `suppressed_at_delivery_reason` cleared. |
| `suppressed_distinctiveness_at_delivery` | `satisfied` | Nightly drift sweep | Distinctiveness recovered | Same pattern. |
| `suppressed_vendor_opt_out_at_delivery` | `satisfied` | Vendor opt-out revocation by the Seller Org (per §27.10 registry write) | Registry probe at next delivery finds `vendor_opt_out_effective=false` | `vendor_opt_out_honored_at=NULL`; `suppressed_at_delivery_reason` cleared. |
| `satisfied` | `expired` | `expires_at ≤ NOW()` (default `expires_at = generated_at + 30d`) | — | Row terminal-for-delivery; `k_anon_satisfied` value preserved for audit; no further delivery regardless of cohort state. |
| ANY | `soft_deleted` | §40.2 retention sweep or §6.8 DSAR cascade | `deleted_at` stamped | Row excluded from all reads; audit trail preserved per §6.7. |
| `suppressed_k_anon_at_delivery` OR `suppressed_distinctiveness_at_delivery` OR `suppressed_vendor_opt_out_at_delivery` OR `suppressed_recompute_deadline` | (no reversal for an individual already-blocked delivery) | Prior delivery attempt is historical fact | — | The suppression of a specific delivery attempt is append-only in the audit ledger — once the delivery layer refused to send, the refusal is never rewritten. Subsequent deliveries on the same row execute their own re-evaluation. |

**No-revert-on-deliver semantics.** Once a delivery has been suppressed for a given (seller_signal_id, subscribing_seller_org_id, delivery_channel, attempted_at) tuple, that specific delivery refusal is permanent in the `marketplace.seller_signal.suppressed` audit stream. The row's `k_anon_satisfied` flag MAY recover, but the historical refusal never flips — the audit answer to "did Sourcera deliver this row to this Seller at this time?" is always the truth at `attempted_at`. This is the analog of §27.9.7's append-only de-anonymization disclosure: suppression is append-only to the audit ledger, even as the row's current suitability for future delivery evolves.

**Per-row persistence.** The SellerSignal row carries: `k_anon_satisfied` (boolean, current), `suppressed_reason` (enum, aggregation-time reason — NULL when satisfied), `suppressed_at_delivery_reason` (enum — NULL when the latest delivery evaluation did not suppress), `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` (nullable timestamp). The `SellerSignalSuppressionLog` append-only sub-resource records every suppression event with `(seller_signal_id, subscribing_seller_org_id, delivery_channel, attempted_at, suppression_reason, reasons_recomputed_at)` — immutable, retention per §40.2 `seller_signal_audit`.

**Capability & billing.** Every pipeline run emits AIOperations under the `seller_signal_aggregation` capability (platform-owned; not billed to customers). These operations NEVER appear on customer AIOperation ledgers per §4.8.1 Scope Isolation.

### 27.9.6 Delivery Surfaces {#27.9.6-delivery-surfaces}

Three delivery surfaces are authored in §27.9; CRM Sync as a fourth is authored at full fidelity in §31.9.

#### 27.9.6.1 Seller Dashboard Widget (In-App Read Surface)

**Preconditions (all must be true).** `SellerSignalDeliveryPreference.dashboard_enabled=true`; seller Org's `seller_plan_tier ≥ seller_starter` (§34.1.2 gates the content; `seller_free` Sellers see an upgrade CTA placeholder, not data); the signal's `category_id` matches the Seller's SellerSoftware footprint OR the `subscribed_category_ids`; `k_anon_satisfied=true` AND no distinctiveness veto at render time; `vendor_opt_out_honored_at IS NULL` for the viewing Seller; `expires_at > now()`; `residency_region_scope` is compatible with the Seller's residency allowlist.

**Render payload.** Aggregate counts, timeline band, intent strength band, category/region/industry/size metadata. NEVER includes buyer Org names or identifiers. The `signal_cohort_count` is displayed when `k_anon_satisfied=true`; when suppressed, the widget renders per `suppression_render_mode`:

- `omit`: the bucket is not shown at all.
- `show_as_insufficient_data`: the bucket is shown with a blurred count and the label "Cohort too small to display"; the seller can click for a "waiting for more buyer signal" explainer.

**PostHog event.** `seller_signal_dashboard_viewed` (§Appendix G) fires on widget render with Org+cohort-level properties (no buyer identities).

#### 27.9.6.2 Weekly Digest (Email)

**Preconditions.** `SellerSignalDeliveryPreference.weekly_digest_enabled=true`; seller Org's plan ≥ seller_starter per §34.1.2 (monthly digest on seller_starter, weekly on seller_growth+, real-time on seller_scale+ — the cadence field is the same row, cadence derives from plan at dispatch time).

**Dispatch.** Loops.so per §C.42; dispatches on `digest_day_of_week` at 08:00 in `digest_timezone`. Payload: at most 50 SellerSignal rows per email, deduplicated against the Seller's last-7-day digest; rows ordered by `intent_strength DESC, signal_cohort_count DESC`.

**Suppression-not-empty rule.** If every candidate row for a Seller is suppressed (k-anon or distinctiveness or opt-out), the digest is **not dispatched at all** for that Seller that week (we never send an "empty digest" or a digest saying "nothing for you" — avoids inbox fatigue while preserving the Seller's ability to check the dashboard on demand). The PostHog event `seller_signal_digest_suppressed_empty` fires in this case.

**Unsubscribe.** Standard Loops.so unsubscribe footer disables the channel by flipping `weekly_digest_enabled=false` on the recipient's `SellerSignalDeliveryPreference`; a confirmation webhook `marketplace.seller_signal.digest_unsubscribed` fires.

#### 27.9.6.3 Real-Time In-App Toast + API Poll (Seller Scale+)

**Preconditions.** `real_time_enabled=true`; plan ≥ seller_scale; rate-limited per `real_time_channel_rate_limit_per_min`.

**Delivery.** When a new SellerSignal row is materialized OR an existing row transitions into the Seller's subscribed categories, an in-app toast surfaces in the Seller Console (via Convex live-query subscription). Simultaneously, the Seller's API endpoint `GET /seller-signals?new=true&since=<cursor>` returns the row on the next poll.

**Volume.** At enterprise scale the real-time channel sustains ≤ 200/min; above this the rate limiter buffers into a 5-minute windowed digest that fires as a single toast with count. Hard cap prevents toast spam and API flooding.

#### 27.9.6.4 CRM Sync (Channel Pointer — Authored in §31.9)

When `crm_sync_channel_enabled=true` AND an active `CRMSyncConnection` exists for the Seller Org (§31.9), SellerSignal deliveries fire a parallel CRM-side activity record per §31.9.5 (CRMSyncActivityEvent) with `activity_kind='seller_signal_delivered'`. The §31.9 pipeline owns retry, failure-queue, field-mapping, and routing semantics; §27.9.6.4 is a cross-reference anchor only.

### 27.9.7 De-Anonymization State Machine {#27.9.7-de-anonymization-state-machine}

Every aggregate SellerSignal row exists in one of the states below vis-à-vis a specific (buyer_workspace, seller_org) pair. The aggregate row itself is NEVER mutated to reveal identity; the state is carried in the `SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink` table and reconciled into the aggregate's pointer-only fields.

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `anonymized` | `eoi_submitted` | Buyer submits EOI (§4.5.2) targeting a specific Seller Org | EOI write succeeds; buyer's Workspace is contributing to ≥ 1 SellerSignal matching the EOI's `marketplace_listing_id.category_id` | Atomic: the EOI insert and the `SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink` insert commit in the same transaction. Failure of either aborts both. |
| `anonymized` | `direct_invite_from_cohort` | Buyer accepts a seller's Direct Invite From Cohort offer (§27.9.8) | Direct Invite Target Account row created with `buyer_accepted_at NOT NULL`; buyer's Workspace was part of the originating cohort | Atomic: Target Account write + `SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink` write in same transaction |
| `anonymized` | `ops_investigation_disclosure` | Ops opens a §4.5.7 investigation requiring cohort identity | DPO approval audit event logged | Reserved; used rarely; DPO sign-off required |
| `eoi_submitted` | `eoi_submitted` | (no-op) Further EOIs by same buyer to same seller | Idempotent on UNIQUE (seller_signal_id, buyer_workspace_id, target_seller_org_id, de_anon_trigger) | Second EOI does NOT create a new link row; existing row's `audit_event_id` chain extended |
| `eoi_submitted` OR `direct_invite_from_cohort` | (no reversal) | DSAR right-to-erasure on buyer user who triggered | Per §27.9.11; redacts `triggering_buyer_user_id` in linked audit; does NOT delete the Link row | Immutability preserved |
| (any) | (no reversal) | Buyer-side EOI withdrawal or direct-invite decline | Neither event reverses the disclosure — once the seller has seen the disambiguated aggregate, the disclosure is permanent | By design: the Seller's knowledge cannot be "un-disclosed" technically, so the audit trail does not pretend otherwise |

**Atomicity enforcement.** Both `eoi_submitted` and `direct_invite_from_cohort` transitions are authored as two-phase commits on the same Convex transaction. If the `SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink` insert fails (e.g., UNIQUE violation from a concurrent retry), the EOI / Target Account insert rolls back and the client sees `seller_signal_de_anon_link_already_exists` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409). Clients retry the EOI; the retry observes the existing link and the EOI proceeds without a new link write.

**Disclosed-field policy.** On `eoi_submitted`, the Seller receives: buyer Org name, buyer primary domain, buyer Workspace's category list (intersected with the Seller's footprint), timeline band, intent strength, estimated contract value from EOI, requesting user's contact email (standard EOI payload). `disclosed_fields` is snapshotted into the Link row. On `direct_invite_from_cohort` (reverse direction — Seller sends offer first, buyer accepts), the Seller sees the buyer Org name and primary domain ONLY on buyer acceptance; prior to acceptance, the Seller sees only the anonymized cohort summary.

### 27.9.8 Direct Invite from Cohort (Seller Scale+) {#27.9.8-direct-invite-from-cohort}

**Authoring Intent.** A Seller holding a real-time subscription (`real_time_enabled=true`, plan ≥ seller_scale) MAY send a one-to-many "Direct Invite From Cohort" offer to an anonymized cohort in their subscribed categories. The offer is routed via the platform; individual buyers in the cohort see the offer on their Buyer Dashboard and MAY accept or decline. Acceptance triggers the `direct_invite_from_cohort` de-anonymization for that specific buyer-seller pair; decline leaves the cohort anonymous (the seller never learns which buyer declined).

**Entity.** `MarketplaceProactiveOffer` (existing sub-resource from §27.3 Vendor Discovery — reused; NOT redefined here) with new `offer_kind='direct_invite_from_cohort'` enum value and new `source_seller_signal_id` FK pointing to the SellerSignal cohort that originated the offer.

**Target Account.** On offer creation, one `DirectInviteTargetAccount` row is materialized per buyer Org in the cohort. This is an authored-extension sub-resource (fields: `id`, `proactive_offer_id`, `buyer_workspace_id` [FK], `seller_visible_at`, `buyer_presented_at`, `buyer_accepted_at`, `buyer_declined_at`, `buyer_declined_reason`, `expires_at`, standard audit). Seller-console reads of this table are gated: prior to `buyer_accepted_at`, the row is opaque (the Seller sees only a count of targeted Workspaces, never identities); after acceptance, the buyer's Workspace and Org identity are revealed via the atomic `SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink` write.

**Rate limits.**

- Per Seller Org: at most 10 active (non-expired, non-withdrawn) direct-invite cohorts in any rolling 24-hour window.
- Per Seller Org: at most 100 target Workspaces across all active invites in any rolling 30-day window.
- Per buyer Workspace: at most 3 direct-invite offers visible at once; older offers auto-expire at N+1 arrival (oldest wins removal per Pulse Digest ordering Summary §6.11).
- Hard block: a buyer Workspace that has `buyer_declined_at` on a seller's prior offer within 90 days MUST NOT receive a new offer from that same Seller Org. Violation returns `direct_invite_prior_decline_cooldown` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409).

**Validation.**

- `source_seller_signal_id` MUST be a SellerSignal with `k_anon_satisfied=true` at offer-creation time. Offers against sub-k cohorts rejected with `direct_invite_cohort_below_k_anon_floor` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).
- Offer copy is markdown per §28; sanitized; max 2,000 chars; ≤ 5 embedded link targets; no external images.
- Offer subject line max 120 chars.

**Expiry.** Default `expires_at = created_at + 14 days`. Expired offers cannot be accepted; decline is a no-op.

**Plan gate.** Offer creation is blocked for Seller Orgs below Seller Scale per §34.1.2 ("Real-time + API" is Enterprise-only; Seller Scale includes "Weekly + real-time" — Direct Invite From Cohort is real-time-class and requires Seller Scale minimum).

### 27.9.9 Webhook Catalog {#27.9.9-webhook-catalog}

All §27.9 webhook events carry `event_class=marketplace_signals_domain` (new; Appendix J extension). Envelope per §31.2 augmented with `organization_id` (Seller Org for seller-facing events; Buyer Org for buyer-facing), `console` (`seller` or `buyer`), `seller_signal_id` where applicable, and `event_id` idempotency per §31.1. Subscribers to this class receive events scoped to `organization_id = subscribing_org_id`. Cross-Org leakage forbidden.

| event_type | Audience | Trigger | Key payload fields |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `marketplace.seller_signal.delivered` | Seller Org | A SellerSignal row delivered to the Seller via dashboard (first render), digest (dispatch), real-time (toast+API), or CRM Sync (handoff to §31.9) | `seller_signal_id`, `delivery_channel` (Appendix J `seller_signal_delivery_channel`), `delivered_at`, aggregate summary (no buyer identities), `cohort_fingerprint_hash` for subscriber dedupe |
| `marketplace.seller_signal.suppressed` | Seller Org | A candidate SellerSignal that would have delivered was suppressed at delivery-time re-evaluation | `seller_signal_id`, `suppression_reason` (`k_anon_floor_not_met`, `distinctiveness_veto`, `residency_mismatch`, `vendor_opt_out`, `expired`, `plan_downgrade_grace_expired`), `delivery_channel`, `attempted_at` |
| `marketplace.seller_signal.cohort_fell_below_floor` | Seller Org | A previously-delivered aggregate falls below k=5 (DSAR recompute, buyer opt-out revocation) | `seller_signal_id`, `prior_cohort_count`, `new_cohort_count` (always `<5`, reported as `"<5"` rather than exact value), `reason` |
| `marketplace.seller_signal.de_anonymized` | Seller Org (target_seller_org_id) | A `SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink` row was written with `target_seller_org_id = subscriber_org_id` | `seller_signal_id`, `de_anon_trigger`, `triggering_eoi_id` (nullable), `triggering_target_account_id` (nullable), `disclosed_fields[]`, `de_anonymized_at` |
| `marketplace.buyer_signal_opt_in.changed` | Buyer Org | `BuyerSignalOptInRecord.opt_in_state` transition OR `opt_in_scope` / `category_ids` / `region_inclusion_policy` mutation | `workspace_id`, `prior_state`, `new_state`, `changed_by_user_id` (redacted per DSAR), `opt_in_consent_version` |
| `marketplace.buyer_signal_opt_in.dsar_recompute_completed` | Buyer Org | DSAR recompute sweep completed for this Org | `dsar_batch_id`, `recomputed_record_count`, `cohorts_suppressed_count`, `duration_ms` |
| `marketplace.direct_invite.offer_created` | Seller Org | Seller creates a Direct Invite From Cohort offer | `proactive_offer_id`, `source_seller_signal_id`, `target_workspace_count`, `expires_at` |
| `marketplace.direct_invite.buyer_accepted` | Seller Org + Buyer Org (separate deliveries with audience-scoped fields) | A buyer accepts a Direct Invite | `proactive_offer_id`, `direct_invite_target_account_id`, `buyer_accepted_at`, de-anonymized buyer identity (seller audience ONLY); `seller_org_name`, `source_category_ids` (buyer audience ONLY) |
| `marketplace.direct_invite.buyer_declined` | Seller Org (aggregate decline count update), Buyer Org (confirmation) | A buyer declines a Direct Invite | Seller audience: `proactive_offer_id`, `remaining_pending_count` (no per-buyer identity); Buyer audience: `proactive_offer_id`, `buyer_declined_at` |
| `marketplace.direct_invite.expired` | Seller Org | Offer reached `expires_at` without acceptance | `proactive_offer_id`, `expired_at`, `declined_count`, `never_presented_count` |

**Volume budget.**

- `seller_signal.delivered`: dominated by real-time channel; at Seller Enterprise scale with `real_time_api_enabled=true`, bounded by `real_time_channel_rate_limit_per_min` per Seller (default 30/min, max 200/min).
- `seller_signal.suppressed` / `cohort_fell_below_floor`: < 5% of delivered volume.
- `de_anonymized`: bounded by EOI creation rate + Direct Invite acceptance rate (≤ 1,000/day at Enterprise scale).
- `buyer_signal_opt_in.*`: low volume (≤ 100/day per Org).
- `direct_invite.*`: bounded by the 10-cohort / 100-target rate limits per §27.9.8.

**Subscription model.** Consumer subscriptions use `POST /webhooks` with event-type filters; `organization_id` is clamped to `subscribing_org_id`. Enterprise `real_time_api_enabled=true` Sellers SHOULD subscribe to the full `marketplace.seller_signal.*` class to mirror the real-time channel into their own systems. Transport semantics per §31.1–§31.6 (HMAC-SHA256, `event_id` idempotency, Appendix F retry curve, DLQ after 5, ≤256 KB).

### 27.9.10 API Endpoints {#27.9.10-api-endpoints}

All endpoints follow §32 patterns (bearer token, fine-grained scopes, cursor-based pagination 50/250, standard error schema per Appendix I). Rate-limit class: `seller_signals_standard` (§32.4.5; 5K/hr burst, 60K/day) unless otherwise noted. Full request/response schemas abbreviated for this section; concrete field sets match the entity schemas in §27.9.2–§27.9.4.

| Method | Path | Scope | Purpose | Rate limit | Key error codes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/buyer-signal-opt-in` | `write:buyer_signal_opt_in`; `workspace_owner` on `workspace_id` | Create or upsert (by `(org_id,workspace_id)`) a BuyerSignalOptInRecord | Standard | `buyer_signal_opt_in_scope_conflict`, `buyer_signal_opt_in_region_policy_invalid` |
| `PATCH` | `/api/v1/buyer-signal-opt-in/:id/activate` | `write:buyer_signal_opt_in` | `inactive→active` | Standard | `buyer_signal_opt_in_already_active`, `buyer_signal_opt_in_revoked_cannot_reactivate` |
| `PATCH` | `/api/v1/buyer-signal-opt-in/:id/pause` | `write:buyer_signal_opt_in` | `active→paused` | Standard | — |
| `PATCH` | `/api/v1/buyer-signal-opt-in/:id/resume` | `write:buyer_signal_opt_in` | `paused→active` | Standard | `buyer_signal_opt_in_paused_by_ops` (cannot self-resume) |
| `PATCH` | `/api/v1/buyer-signal-opt-in/:id/revoke` | `write:buyer_signal_opt_in` | Any non-terminal → `revoked` | Standard | — |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/buyer-signal-opt-in` | `read:buyer_signal_opt_in` | List Org's records; cursor-paginated | Standard | — |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/seller-signals` | `read:seller_signals`; seller Org scoped; plan ≥ seller_starter | List SellerSignal rows visible to the Seller; optional `since=<cursor>`, `category_id=`, `region_code=`, `industry_code=`, `new=true` filter | Standard + real-time burst: 200/min per Seller Enterprise | `seller_signal_not_available_on_plan`, `seller_signal_channel_requires_plan_upgrade` (if the caller uses a real-time-only param on a non-Scale plan) |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/seller-signals/:id` | `read:seller_signals` | Single row detail | Standard | `seller_signal_k_anon_suppressed` (HTTP 410 — the row exists but was suppressed at re-eval time) |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/seller-signal-delivery-preference` | `read:seller_signal_delivery_preference` | Read Org's one active row | Standard | — |
| `PATCH` | `/api/v1/seller-signal-delivery-preference` | `write:seller_signal_delivery_preference`; `seller_org_admin` or `org_owner` | Update channel flags, subscribed category/region/industry, cadence | Standard | `seller_signal_channel_requires_plan_upgrade`, `crm_sync_channel_requires_active_connection` |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/marketplace-proactive-offers` | `write:marketplace_proactive_offers`; plan ≥ seller_scale; `offer_kind=direct_invite_from_cohort` | Create a Direct Invite From Cohort | 10 offers/24h per §27.9.8 | `direct_invite_cohort_below_k_anon_floor`, `direct_invite_prior_decline_cooldown`, `seller_signal_direct_invite_rate_limit_exceeded` |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/marketplace-proactive-offers` | `read:marketplace_proactive_offers` | List Seller's offers (seller-audience fields only) or buyer's offers (buyer-audience fields only), depending on caller's console | Standard | — |
| `PATCH` | `/api/v1/marketplace-proactive-offers/:id/accept` | `write:marketplace_proactive_offers`; `workspace_owner` on targeted Workspace | Accept a direct-invite offer (atomic de-anon link write) | Standard | `seller_signal_de_anon_link_immutable`, `seller_signal_de_anon_link_already_exists` |
| `PATCH` | `/api/v1/marketplace-proactive-offers/:id/decline` | `write:marketplace_proactive_offers`; `workspace_owner` on targeted Workspace | Decline | Standard | — |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/seller-signal-de-anonymization-links` | `read:seller_signal_de_anonymization_links`; Seller console scoped to `target_seller_org_id`, Buyer console scoped to `triggering_buyer_org_id` | List relevant links; append-only; no mutation endpoints | Standard | — |

**Idempotency.** All `POST` and state-transitioning `PATCH` endpoints accept the `Idempotency-Key` header per §32 and respect per-resource UNIQUE constraints to prevent duplicates on retry.

### 27.9.11 DSAR, Residency, and Right-to-Erasure Cascades {#27.9.11-dsar-residency-and-right-to-erasure-cascades}

**Buyer-side DSAR right-to-access.** A DSAR export for a buyer user returns: (a) the user's `opt_in_consented_by_user_id` presence in all BuyerSignalOptInRecord rows they authored; (b) the `SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink` rows where the user's Workspace was `triggering_buyer_workspace_id` (including `disclosed_fields` and `target_seller_org_id`); (c) the aggregate `cohorts_participated_in` count (precise Workspace-level detail, not aggregate identity). No seller-side data is surfaced.

**Buyer-side DSAR right-to-erasure.** A right-to-erasure request on a buyer user triggers the following cascade, asserted to complete within 24 hours per the `dsar_recompute_completed_at` SLA:

1. The user's FK references in `BuyerSignalOptInRecord.opt_in_consented_by_user_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by` are redacted to `redacted`.
2. All BuyerSignalOptInRecord rows owned by the user's Org remain — right-to-erasure applies to the user, not the Org — but records the user was the consent signer for are flagged `consent_signer_redacted=true` and MAY trigger a UX prompt for the Org's next `workspace_owner` to re-confirm consent if the record is still `active` after 30 days (Consent Ledger refresh path per §6.4).
3. The Workspace's contribution to in-flight SellerSignal aggregates MUST be excluded from the next pipeline run; the worker sets `dsar_recompute_enqueued_at=now()` and kicks the recompute.
4. The recompute sweeps all SellerSignal rows within the Signal Period; for each, it re-executes the k-anon + distinctiveness checks without the erased user's Workspace. Rows that drop below k=5 emit `marketplace.seller_signal.cohort_fell_below_floor` to the Seller subscribers.
5. `SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink` rows referencing the user are NOT deleted (per §6.8.5 audit integrity exemption); the `triggering_buyer_user_id` FK is redacted.
6. A `marketplace.buyer_signal_opt_in.dsar_recompute_completed` webhook fires to the Buyer Org when the sweep finishes. SLA: < 24h from DSAR event creation; breach pages DPO.

**Seller-side DSAR.** A DSAR on a seller user returns their `SellerSignalDeliveryPreference` authoring history and their `MarketplaceProactiveOffer` creation history. Right-to-erasure redacts author/creator FKs to `redacted`; records remain.

**Residency.** Aggregation pipeline enforces residency at stage 6 (§27.9.5). Cross-residency aggregation is forbidden unless `residency_region_scope='global'` AND Ops approval is logged. Buyer Orgs in EU residency MUST NOT contribute to `us_only` aggregates; enforcement is at pipeline bucket assignment, not at delivery. Seller Orgs with EU data-residency MUST NOT receive `us_only` aggregates in any channel.

**Sub-processor disclosure.** Loops.so (digest dispatch) and Convex (live-query real-time) are existing sub-processors (§6.8 DPA Appendix). No new sub-processors introduced by §27.9.

### 27.9.12 Acceptance Criteria {#27.9.12-acceptance-criteria}

1. A `BuyerSignalOptInRecord` MUST default to `opt_in_state=inactive` on create; zero record for a Workspace is functionally equivalent to `opt_in_state=inactive` and MUST result in default-deny contribution. QA test `buyer_signal_opt_in_default_deny` asserts.
2. `opt_in_at ≤ signal_period_start - 24h` MUST be enforced by the aggregation pipeline; opt-ins within the cool-down MUST NOT contribute to the next Signal Period. QA test `buyer_signal_opt_in_cooldown_honored` asserts against a synthetic 23h-old opt-in.
3. `opt_in_state='revoked'` MUST be terminal; re-activation attempts MUST return `buyer_signal_opt_in_revoked_cannot_reactivate` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409). QA test `buyer_signal_opt_in_revoked_is_terminal` asserts.
4. Delivery of a SellerSignal with `signal_cohort_count < 5` across ANY channel (dashboard, digest, real-time, CRM Sync, API `GET /seller-signals`) MUST be blocked at the delivery-time re-evaluation even when the row's aggregation-time `k_anon_satisfied=true`. QA test `seller_signal_delivery_time_k_anon_reeval` asserts against a synthetic DSAR-driven drop.
5. A cohort passing numeric k=5 but failing the distinctiveness secondary check MUST be suppressed with `suppressed_reason='distinctiveness_veto'` and MUST emit `marketplace.seller_signal.cohort_fell_below_floor` with `reason='distinctiveness_veto'`. QA test `seller_signal_distinctiveness_veto` asserts.
6. Plan-tier downgrade on a Seller Org with an active `SellerSignalDeliveryPreference` referencing higher-tier channels MUST NOT mutate the preference row; delivery-time enforcement MUST silently suppress now-ineligible channels; a 14-day grace banner MUST render in-app. After grace, the next `PATCH` MUST clamp ineligible flags to `false`. QA test `seller_signal_preference_plan_downgrade_grace` asserts.
7. `SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink` is append-only; any `UPDATE` or `DELETE` attempt via API MUST return HTTP 403 `seller_signal_de_anon_link_immutable`; direct DB `UPDATE` blocked by a row-level trigger. QA test `seller_signal_de_anon_link_immutable_db` asserts.
8. `SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink` MUST enforce UNIQUE (`seller_signal_id`, `triggering_buyer_workspace_id`, `target_seller_org_id`, `de_anon_trigger`); concurrent duplicate inserts MUST return `seller_signal_de_anon_link_already_exists` (HTTP 409). QA test `seller_signal_de_anon_link_unique_concurrency` asserts against 100 concurrent EOI retries.
9. An EOI submission that targets a Seller whose Marketplace category overlaps with a cohort the buyer's Workspace is contributing to MUST atomically write the EOI AND the `SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink` row in the same transaction. Failure of either MUST roll back both. QA test `seller_signal_eoi_deanon_atomicity` asserts via forced-failure injection.
10. Direct Invite From Cohort MUST be creation-blocked for Seller Orgs below Seller Scale with `seller_signal_direct_invite_plan_tier_insufficient` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403). QA test `direct_invite_plan_gate` asserts.
11. Direct Invite cohort with `signal_cohort_count < 5` at creation time MUST be rejected with `direct_invite_cohort_below_k_anon_floor` (HTTP 422); QA test `direct_invite_below_k_anon_rejected` asserts.
12. Direct Invite rate limits (10 active offers/24h per Seller Org; 100 target Workspaces/30d per Seller Org) MUST be enforced; violation returns `seller_signal_direct_invite_rate_limit_exceeded` (HTTP 429). QA test `direct_invite_rate_limits_enforced` asserts.
13. Direct Invite cannot be re-offered to a buyer Workspace that declined the same Seller Org within 90 days; returns `direct_invite_prior_decline_cooldown` (HTTP 409). QA test `direct_invite_cooldown_after_decline` asserts.
14. Cross-console reads of `BuyerSignalOptInRecord` OR `SellerSignalDeliveryPreference` MUST return `dual_console_firewall_violation` per §7.2. QA test `seller_signal_dual_console_firewall` asserts.
15. DSAR recompute MUST complete within 24 hours of DSAR event creation; breach pages DPO and emits C.100 SIM alert `seller_signal_dsar_recompute_sla_breach`. QA test `seller_signal_dsar_recompute_sla` asserts at the 23h, 24h, and 25h marks.
16. A buyer Workspace in EU residency MUST NOT contribute to a `residency_region_scope='us_only'` aggregate; the pipeline aborts the Workspace's bucket contribution with `seller_signal_residency_violation` (Appendix I; existing). QA test `seller_signal_residency_enforcement_eu_to_us` asserts.
17. The weekly digest MUST NOT dispatch to a Seller Org when every candidate row is suppressed; the Seller's `digest_empty_run_count` metric increments; PostHog event `seller_signal_digest_suppressed_empty` fires. QA test `seller_signal_digest_suppress_not_send` asserts.
18. Every `marketplace.seller_signal.*` and `marketplace.buyer_signal_opt_in.*` event registered in Appendix C and Appendix G MUST match the emitted `event_type` string exactly; CI test `seller_signal_event_catalog_consistency` asserts.
19. Buyer audience webhook payloads MUST NEVER include `target_seller_org_id` on `marketplace.buyer_signal_opt_in.*` events; Seller audience payloads MUST NEVER include `triggering_buyer_user_id` on any `marketplace.seller_signal.*` event EXCEPT `de_anonymized`. QA test `seller_signal_audience_scoped_payload_redaction` asserts.
20. The Public Pricing API pin behavior (§4.8.9) on SellerSignal delivery-tier access is NOT applicable (SellerSignal is not priced per-operation for customers); any attempt to invoice a customer for SellerSignal deliveries MUST fail the billing reconciliation check and page Finance Ops. QA test `seller_signal_no_customer_billing` asserts.
21. `SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink.disclosed_fields` and `.redacted_fields` MUST together enumerate ALL fields of the cohort at disclosure time with no omissions; CI schema-consistency test `seller_signal_de_anon_disclosed_fields_exhaustive` asserts against the SellerSignal field schema.
22. `/api/v1/seller-signals` and `/api/v1/marketplace-proactive-offers` MUST apply cursor-based pagination per §32 (default 50, max 250); cursor forgery returns HTTP 400 `invalid_cursor` (existing). QA test `seller_signal_api_pagination_contract` asserts.
23. **Delivery-time snapshot-age bound.** Every delivery path enumerated in §27.9.6 MUST operate against a `cohort_count_snapshot` where `t_delivery - snapshot_at ≤ 60s`. Stale snapshots MUST trigger a synchronous recompute bounded by a 5-second hard deadline; recompute deadline breach MUST suppress the delivery with `suppressed_reason='recompute_deadline_exceeded'` and emit `marketplace.seller_signal.suppressed` with the same reason. QA test `seller_signal_delivery_snapshot_age_budget` asserts snapshot-age enforcement across all four delivery channels (dashboard, digest, real-time, CRM Sync); QA test `seller_signal_synchronous_recompute_deadline` asserts the 5-second deadline and the suppression emission; integration test `seller_signal_snapshot_age_aligned_to_vendor_opt_out_latency_budget` asserts the 60s bound is numerically co-indexed with the §27.10.4 enforcement latency budget.
24. **`k_anon_satisfied` state-machine invariants.** Every From/To transition enumerated in §27.9.5.1 MUST be exercised by QA tests: (a) `k_anon_state_machine_forward_transitions` covers every valid forward edge; (b) `k_anon_state_machine_invalid_transitions_blocked` asserts invalid edges (e.g., `expired → satisfied`, `soft_deleted → satisfied`) are rejected by the row-level trigger; (c) `k_anon_suppression_log_append_only` asserts `SellerSignalSuppressionLog` refuses `UPDATE` and `DELETE` via API and DB trigger, returning HTTP 403 `seller_signal_suppression_log_immutable`; (d) `k_anon_no_revert_on_prior_refusal` asserts that a row recovering from `suppressed_k_anon_at_delivery` to `satisfied` does NOT rewrite the historical suppression audit entry for a prior delivery attempt; (e) `k_anon_recovery_no_webhook` asserts the spec's explicit "no webhook on recovery" rule — a `suppressed_* → satisfied` transition MUST NOT emit `marketplace.seller_signal.*` to prevent cohort-membership leakage.
25. **Distinctiveness threshold tuning discipline.** The C.97-configurable distinctiveness threshold (default 0.85) MUST be reviewed quarterly by Ops Trust & Safety in a documented working session. The review MUST: (a) sample at least 100 `distinctiveness_veto` suppressions and at least 100 k-anon-satisfied-but-sub-quantile cohorts from the prior quarter; (b) compute false-positive rate (veto applied to cohorts where independent manual disambiguation review found no unique-identifier risk) and false-negative rate (cohorts passing distinctiveness but flagged by red-team disambiguation); (c) produce a recommendation to hold, tighten (raise threshold), or loosen (lower threshold) the value; (d) require DPO sign-off on any threshold movement; (e) emit an `ops.trust_safety.distinctiveness_threshold_reviewed` audit event (§6.7) with the review outcome, sample counts, false-positive rate, false-negative rate, and decision rationale. A review not conducted within a calendar quarter MUST page DPO and hold the threshold at its prior value until the review completes. QA test `seller_signal_distinctiveness_threshold_quarterly_cadence` asserts the audit event's presence per rolling-quarter window.

### 27.9.13 Failure Modes Addressed {#27.9.13-failure-modes-addressed}

1. **Buyer opts in, the Workspace's category is later reassigned; aggregate stops being accurate.** Resolved: the pipeline uses the Workspace's category as of `signal_period_end`, not opt-in time; category reassignment mid-period ends contribution cleanly at the next period boundary.
2. **Buyer's parent Org is acquired by a competitor; the acquiring Org's seller side subscribes to signals and sees the buyer's cohort.** Resolved: the `SellerSignalDeliveryPreference` is Org-scoped; the acquiring Org's seller console must have its own records; the Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2) prevents reading the buyer-side opt-in records of the same Org. Additionally, `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` registry check ensures a buyer Org can opt out of having its acquiring-parent's seller arm receive signals (manually, via Ops).
3. **Concurrent EOI retries by a flaky mobile client create two de-anon link rows.** Resolved: UNIQUE (seller_signal_id, buyer_workspace_id, target_seller_org_id, de_anon_trigger) + atomic two-phase commit; second insert returns `seller_signal_de_anon_link_already_exists`; EOI write proceeds idempotently.
4. **DSAR recompute drops a cohort below k=5 AFTER the digest has already been generated but BEFORE it's dispatched.** Resolved: digest dispatch re-runs the delivery-time k-anon check per row; now-suppressed rows are filtered from the digest payload before send; `digest_suppressed_rows_count` metric increments.
5. **Seller on Free tier polls `/api/v1/seller-signals` with real-time params.** Resolved: plan-tier gate at endpoint level returns `seller_signal_not_available_on_plan` (HTTP 403); the upgrade CTA fires via existing Seller-side paywall patterns.
6. **Buyer revokes opt-in mid-Signal-Period; existing SellerSignal aggregate already delivered to the Seller 2 days ago.** Resolved: the Seller's prior view of the aggregate stands (the data was legitimately delivered per the consent that was active at delivery time); the next period's aggregate excludes the Workspace; `marketplace.seller_signal.cohort_fell_below_floor` fires if the new cohort drops under k=5. The Seller is not notified of the specific revocation (prevents inference attacks).
7. **Ops force-pauses a buyer Org's opt-in; buyer disputes the pause.** Resolved: `paused_reason='ops_forced_pause'` prevents self-resume; buyer's dispute path routes to §4.5.7 (Ops governance); Ops can reverse via `paused→active` with audit logging. Buyer-side UI shows "paused by Ops — contact support" with a support ticket deep link.
8. **Seller's real-time channel is flooded (200/min hard cap).** Resolved: excess events are buffered into a 5-minute windowed rollup digest that fires as a single toast with cohort count; backend emits `seller_signal_real_time_rate_limit_buffered` metric; no events are dropped.
9. **Cohort of k=5 becomes k=6, k=7… k=20; Seller receives duplicate "delivered" events.** Resolved: `seller_signal.delivered` fires on FIRST delivery to a Seller for a given (seller_signal_id, seller_org_id) pair; subsequent refreshes of the cohort within the same Signal Period update the dashboard widget live-query WITHOUT firing a webhook (unless `intent_strength` or `timeline_band` transitions, which are semantic changes; these fire `seller_signal.delivered` with `delivery_channel='dashboard'` and a `change_reason` field). QA test `seller_signal_delivered_event_no_duplicate_refresh` asserts.
10. **Cross-residency Ops investigation (EU buyer, US Ops investigator) discloses cohort identity.** Resolved: `de_anon_trigger='ops_investigation_disclosure'` requires DPO approval captured in `dpo_approval_audit_event_id`; without the approval the Ops action rejects with `abuse_report_cross_residency_triage_blocked` (existing; §4.5.7) variant repurposed as `seller_signal_cross_residency_disclosure_requires_dpo` (new; Appendix I).
11. **Buyer clicks "opt in" after a long-conversation drift in consent language; old consent version would not cover new `opt_in_scope`.** Resolved: consent version snapshotted at `inactive→active`; aggregation pipeline consumes records by `opt_in_consent_version ≥ current_minimum_version`; older-version records auto-pause and prompt re-consent via `buyer_signal_opt_in.consent_version_refresh_required` (new internal notification). The Signal Period sweeps records for consent currency before the k-anon step.
12. **Ops forgets to set `digest_day_of_week` during onboarding.** Resolved: default `monday` + default `digest_timezone=UTC`; no missing-field case reaches the scheduler. A post-onboarding prompt in-app encourages the Seller to customize.

### 27.9.14 Ops Tooling & Manual Overrides {#27.9.14-ops-tooling-&-manual-overrides}

**Privacy Monitor (C.100 Signal Integrity Monitor extension).** A sidecar observability job inspects every SellerSignal row at aggregation completion and delivery re-evaluation; alerts on:

- `seller_signal_de_anon_drift_detected`: `SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink` exists but `SellerSignal.de_anonymized_*` pointer fields unset.
- `seller_signal_cohort_below_k_anon_delivered`: a delivery log entry shows a delivery with `cohort_count < 5` (should be impossible; alert fires on any occurrence and triggers automatic redelivery reversal).
- `seller_signal_residency_violation_post_deliver`: a delivery log entry shows cross-residency leakage (should be impossible; fire → Ops → DPO).
- `seller_signal_dsar_recompute_sla_breach`: SLA > 24h.

**Ops force-suppress.** Ops Console action to force-suppress a specific SellerSignal row (Ops → Signal Investigation). Requires dual sign-off (`seller_signal_ops_force_suppress_requires_dual_signoff` — new; Appendix I). Used for active legal/regulatory holds. Force-suppressed rows return `410 Gone` on API access with `suppression_reason='ops_legal_hold'`.

**Ops force-unsuppress.** FORBIDDEN. Ops cannot un-suppress a k-anon-failing cohort. If Ops believes a suppression is in error, the correct path is: confirm the underlying data, let the cohort grow naturally OR release the opt-in record blockers. This invariant prevents a privileged Ops user from silently leaking a sub-k cohort.

**Ops-side read path.** `/ops/marketplace/seller-signals/:id` returns the full row INCLUDING `signal_cohort_count` regardless of k-anon (Ops visibility is exempt; the SIM / privacy-monitor evaluates Ops reads for audit but does not block them). Customer-facing API paths remain bound by k-anon.

**Consent refresh bulk job.** When Consent Ledger (§6.4) publishes a new `opt_in_consent_version`, a scheduled bulk job enqueues consent-refresh prompts to affected Orgs (visible in Buyer Dashboard). Aggregation pipeline auto-pauses records with stale consent at the next Signal Period boundary. Ops runbook governs the refresh campaign cadence.

### 27.9.15 Self-Challenge Refinements {#27.9.15-self-challenge-refinements}

Items surfaced during the hostile-staff-engineer review of §27.9 and authored here to close gaps before engineering handoff. Flag any that require product / privacy sign-off in the reconciliation log.

**27.9.15.1 Aggregation mid-revoke race.** When an aggregation pipeline run begins for Signal Period `W`, and a Buyer Org transitions `BuyerSignalOptInRecord.state` to `revoked` or `paused_*` mid-run, the pipeline MUST re-read the opt-in record at materialization time (immediately before the k-floor check, post-bucketing) AND drop contributions whose owning opt-in record is no longer in `active`. This is a RE-READ, not a snapshot-at-start. Implementation: the aggregation worker takes a Convex read on the opt-in record with `at_materialization=true` consistency-tag; any state change since bucket assignment invalidates the contribution. Failure to re-read is logged as `seller_signal_opt_in_race_detected` (Ops-only PostHog event — add to Appendix G extension).

**27.9.15.2 Distinctiveness temporal leakage.** A cohort that passes distinctiveness in Signal Period `W-1` and fails in `W` conveys the negative signal "a distinctive contributor just dropped out." Mitigation: the `suppression_render_mode` enum (Appendix J) is deliberately anonymous (never discloses the *reason* a cohort was suppressed in human-readable form beyond coarse-grained "privacy threshold"). Further: when a previously-delivered cohort fails distinctiveness in `W`, the `marketplace.seller_signal.cohort_suppressed` event is emitted WITHOUT any delta from the prior period — the Seller learns the cohort is suppressed but not why or whose contribution was removed.

**27.9.15.3 Direct Invite idempotency.** POST `/seller-signals/direct-invites` MUST require an `Idempotency-Key` header per §32 patterns; re-submission with the same key returns the original response without consuming a new rate-limit token. Without this, a flaky client retry double-consumes the Seller's 10/24h or 100/30d rate-limit budget. Implementation: Convex-side idempotency table keyed by `(seller_org_id, idempotency_key)` with 24h TTL. Not previously explicit in §27.9.8 — this is the authoritative statement.

**27.9.15.4 Nightly reconciliation failure path.** §27.9.4 requires nightly reconciliation of SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink rows against §4.4.18 `SellerSignal.de_anonymized_*` pointer fields. If reconciliation detects drift (a link without pointer OR a pointer without link), the reconciliation job MUST: (a) emit `seller_signal_de_anon_drift_detected` SIM signal; (b) flag the offending rows with `review_pending=true` in a new internal boolean column on SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink (Authored Extension — logged in RECONCILIATION.md); (c) halt de-anonymization-triggered webhook fan-out for the affected Seller Org until Ops clears the flag. Customer-facing surfaces render the cohort as `placeholder_distinctiveness_vetoed` during the hold.

**27.9.15.5 Cross-region de-anonymization.** When a Buyer Org in EU residency accepts a Direct Invite from a Seller Org in US residency, the de-anonymization disclosure crosses residency boundaries. This MUST respect the Buyer's `buyer_signal_region_inclusion_policy`: if `residency_region_only`, the Direct Invite offer is suppressed at cohort-composition time (the cohort never includes the cross-region Buyer); if `cross_region_with_buyer_consent`, the disclosure proceeds but the buyer's acceptance click is additionally gated by a UX-captured residency-acknowledgement token; if `ops_forbidden_cross_region`, the offer is blocked with `seller_signal_residency_violation` (Appendix I) even if the cohort momentarily included the Buyer before residency enforcement.

**27.9.15.6 Seller plan downgrade mid-cohort.** When a Seller Org downgrades from Scale to Growth mid-week, cohorts already scheduled for `real_time_toast` delivery MUST transition to `weekly_digest_email` on the next delivery attempt (per §27.9.3 delivery-time re-evaluation). No re-routing from `real_time_*` to `weekly_digest_email` for events already in flight — those events are dropped. The 14-day downgrade-grace (§34.12.6) does NOT apply to Seller Signals channel eligibility; channel re-evaluation is immediate.

## 27.10 Vendor Opt-Out Global Registry {#27.10-vendor-opt-out-global-registry}

**Authoring Intent.** §27.10 is the marketplace-surface authoring of the Vendor Opt-Out Global Registry per Summary C.123. The authoritative storage entity, its scope-matching rules, write-side state machine, and write-side acceptance criteria are authored in §4.4.8 (Vendor Opt-Out Record) and the marketplace-domain read/render contract is authored in §4.5.6. §27.10 neither duplicates those nor contradicts them; it binds them together into a single marketplace-surface specification that is complete enough for engineering to build against without cross-referencing three separate sections at runtime. Specifically, §27.10 adds: (a) the authority model — the DNS TXT challenge flow and Seller Owner attestation flow that prove a writing actor has authority over the Seller Org identity being suppressed, authored as a new sub-entity `VendorOptOutAuthorityAttestation`; (b) the enforcement-surface contract binding each rendering consumer (M2 Selection Report Public Link, M9 Category Page, M11 Comparison Page, M12 Market Intelligence Report, M13 Heat Map, SellerOrgPage, SoftwarePage, any future surface rendering Seller identity) to the ≤60-second live-render enforcement SLO; (c) the ≤60-second enforcement-latency pipeline decomposed across write, index fan-out, edge-cache invalidation, live-render registry check, and materialized-artifact scrub; (d) the three public API endpoints (`POST /v1/opt-outs`, `GET /v1/opt-outs`, `DELETE /v1/opt-outs/:id`) expressed as §32-compliant endpoints with request/response schemas and error codes; (e) the two seller-facing lifecycle webhooks `vendor.opted_out` and `vendor.opted_in` authored alongside the existing per-page retro-sweep webhooks `vendor_opt_out.applied` and `vendor_opt_out.revoked` — the two webhook families serve disjoint lifecycle stages and coexist; (f) the retroactive-application contract binding new writes to every already-published artifact; (g) DSAR, retention, and residency cascades specific to the registry; (h) numbered acceptance criteria including the ≤60-second live-render SLO; (i) a failure-mode register covering DNS propagation lag, edge-cache inconsistency, authority-attestation races, concurrent opt-out/opt-in toggles, cross-residency invalidation, and Ops-imposed overrides; and (j) a self-challenge refinement block. Every new enum, error code, notification, PostHog event, webhook event, and glossary term introduced here is registered in the corresponding Appendix per the authoring conventions.

**Relationship to §4.4.8 and §4.5.6.** §4.4.8 is the entity of record for an opt-out *fact* (what is suppressed, by whom, under what scope, in what state). §4.5.6 is the read/render contract for marketplace-domain consumers (how a render path turns an opt-out fact into a redacted output). §27.10 authors the third facet — authority to write, public API surface to write, public webhook surface to observe, and the end-to-end ≤60-second enforcement latency binding all of this together as a single cross-surface feature. When §4.4.8 and §27.10 overlap (e.g., on retroactive-sweep wording), §4.4.8 remains authoritative for the storage-side SLO (15-minute retro backfill of materialized row state) and §27.10 adds a stricter render-surface SLO (≤60-second live-render enforcement). The two SLOs are not in conflict — they measure different things and coexist. The spec-tightening is recorded in RECONCILIATION.md.
