**Naming convention.** §27.10 webhook event types for the opt-out lifecycle are namespaced under `vendor.*` per this prompt's explicit requirement (`vendor.opted_out`, `vendor.opted_in`); they carry `event_class=vendor_opt_out_registry_lifecycle` (new — Appendix J extension). The per-page retro-sweep events `vendor_opt_out.applied` and `vendor_opt_out.revoked` (existing from §4.5.6) retain `event_class=vendor_opt_out_page_sweep` (net-new class to name the existing events; Appendix J extension). PostHog events mirror webhook names with `.` replaced by `_` unless overridden. This dual-class arrangement is deliberate — subscribers interested in the seller-Org-level fact subscribe to `vendor_opt_out_registry_lifecycle`; subscribers interested in per-page invalidation fan-out subscribe to `vendor_opt_out_page_sweep`. No subscriber is required to take both.

### 27.10.2 Authority Model — DNS TXT & Seller Owner Attestation {#27.10.2-authority-model}

**Authoring Intent.** Per this prompt, "DNS TXT or Seller Owner attestation proves authority." Opt-outs affect public-facing platform content; an unauthorized actor toggling an opt-out can either (a) silently strip a competitor's marketing footprint by suppressing their name at a key category page, or (b) silently restore a seller's footprint against the seller's will by revoking a legitimate opt-out. Both are abuse vectors the authority model must close. §4.4.8 already gates writes to `seller_billing_admin` and `seller_org_admin` roles, which is RBAC-layer authority — sufficient for normal operations. §27.10 adds a stricter *domain-level* authority proof required for two specific cases: (1) initial registry activation for a Seller Org (the first opt-out a Seller Org ever writes); (2) any opt-out with `scope_kind=global` (the most disruptive scope). Ops may also bypass the authority check with `ops_imposed_attestation` requiring `ops_opt_out_admin` + DPO co-sign, captured in the same entity for audit.

Authority attestation is materialized as a first-class entity `VendorOptOutAuthorityAttestation`. Every Vendor Opt-Out Record with `scope_kind=global` MUST have at least one `verified`-state row in this table referencing its `org_id` at write time; lesser scope kinds MAY rely on an existing verified attestation from the same Org (attestation is Org-scoped, not per-opt-out). If the Org has never submitted an attestation, the first opt-out write MUST be preceded by an attestation write regardless of scope.

#### 27.10.2.1 VendorOptOutAuthorityAttestation (Org-Scoped, Seller-Origin) {#27.10.2.1-vendoroptoutauthorityattestation}

**Scope:** Org-scoped (`org_id` = Seller Org). Console-scoped writes (seller console only). Read: Seller Org's own rows via seller console + Ops Console full read. Buyer-console reads return HTTP 404 per §4.4.8 firewall rule.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | Seller's organization |
| `console` | Enum | `seller` (fixed) | Explicit for firewall assertions |
| `method` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_opt_out_authority_method`: `dns_txt`, `seller_owner_attestation`, `ops_imposed_attestation` | Attestation path taken |
| `domain` | String | 3–253 chars; IDN-normalized; lowercase; ASCII-only after punycode; nullable when `method != dns_txt` | Apex domain the TXT record MUST be placed on; MUST match `Organization.verified_primary_domain` per §4.4 ± explicit alternate-domain override |
| `dns_challenge_token` | String | 32-char URL-safe base32; nullable when `method != dns_txt` | Single-use; generated at write; verified by DNS resolver against `_sourcera-opt-out-challenge.<domain>` TXT value |
| `dns_challenge_issued_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable when `method != dns_txt` | When the token was issued |
| `dns_challenge_expires_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable when `method != dns_txt` | `dns_challenge_issued_at + 24h`; pending attestations past this transition to `expired` |
| `dns_last_probe_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | Last DNS lookup attempt; updated on every retry |
| `dns_last_probe_result` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_opt_out_authority_dns_probe_result`: `success`, `nxdomain`, `servfail`, `timeout`, `record_not_found`, `record_mismatch` | Latest probe status |
| `dns_probe_attempt_count` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Total probe attempts in this attestation's lifetime; capped at 50, then `verification_state=failed` with reason `dns_probe_retry_exhausted` |
| `dns_verifying_resolver_set` | Array\[String\] | 0–10 entries | IANA-blessed resolver endpoints used (Google 8.8.8.8, Cloudflare 1.1.1.1, Quad9 9.9.9.9) — MUST verify consistently across ≥ 2 resolvers to reject split-horizon DNS attacks |
| `attestation_signer_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → User; required when `method=seller_owner_attestation` | Person who signed the in-app attestation; MUST hold `seller_org_owner` at signature time |
| `attestation_signed_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | When the signer completed the MFA step-up and submitted the attestation |
| `attestation_mfa_factor_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → MFA Factor (§6.7); required when `method=seller_owner_attestation` | Specific factor used for step-up; WebAuthn passkey strongly preferred over TOTP |
| `attestation_text_snapshot` | String | 0–4000 chars; immutable once populated | Exact legal attestation language displayed to and signed by the user; versioned from Consent Ledger §6.4 |
| `attestation_text_version` | String | Semver; ≤ 32 chars; immutable | Consent Ledger version identifier |
| `ops_imposed_justification` | String | 0–2000 chars; required when `method=ops_imposed_attestation` | Free-text reason (court order ref, DPO decision ref) |
| `ops_imposed_dpo_approver_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → User; required when `method=ops_imposed_attestation` | DPO sign-off is mandatory for Ops-imposed path |
| `ops_imposed_case_ref_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → Ops Investigation Case (§4.5.7) | Optional case binding |
| `verification_state` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_opt_out_authority_verification_state`: `pending_proof`, `proof_submitted`, `verified`, `expired`, `revoked`, `failed` | Authoritative attestation lifecycle |
| `verification_failure_reason` | Enum | See Appendix J `vendor_opt_out_authority_failure_reason`: `dns_lookup_failed`, `dns_record_not_found`, `dns_record_mismatch`, `dns_probe_retry_exhausted`, `dns_split_horizon_detected`, `seller_owner_role_missing_at_signature`, `mfa_step_up_declined`, `mfa_factor_revoked`, `ops_imposed_missing_dpo`, `attestation_text_version_stale`; nullable | Populated on `*→failed` |
| `verified_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable; set on transition to `verified` | Immutable once set |
| `expires_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | Verified attestations expire 90 days after `verified_at`; an expired attestation suspends the Seller Org's opt-out write capability (existing opt-outs remain honored; new writes blocked until re-attestation) |
| `revoked_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable; set on `*→revoked` | Triggered by Ops, seller self-revocation, or DSAR right-to-erasure on the signer |
| `audit_event_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Audit Event; always populated | Full actor chain |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Seller User ID OR Ops User ID | MUST hold `seller_org_admin`, `seller_billing_admin`, or `seller_org_owner` when `method ∈ {dns_txt, seller_owner_attestation}`; MUST hold `ops_opt_out_admin` when `method=ops_imposed_attestation` |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | User ID | — |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete; equivalent to `revoked` when used |

**Scope Isolation.** Seller-console writes only (role-gated above). Buyer-console reads/writes return HTTP 404 `vendor_opt_out_cross_console_access`. Ops Console has full read and may create rows with `method=ops_imposed_attestation`. `seller_org_owner` is a prerequisite for `method=seller_owner_attestation`; `seller_billing_admin` and `seller_org_admin` CANNOT self-promote to this path (authored extension — tightens §4.4.8 role-gate for the authority-attestation step).

**Indexes.** `(org_id, verification_state)` composite for fast authority lookup on write; `(org_id) WHERE verification_state='verified' AND deleted_at IS NULL` partial for the authority-check cache; `(verification_state, expires_at)` partial on non-null for the expiration sweep; `(verification_state, dns_challenge_expires_at)` partial for the DNS-probe worker; `(created_by)` for Ops review.

**State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (create) | `pending_proof` | `POST /v1/opt-outs/authority-attestations` with `method=dns_txt` | Seller submits domain; platform issues `dns_challenge_token` | TTL 24h per `dns_challenge_expires_at` |
| (create) | `proof_submitted` | `POST /v1/opt-outs/authority-attestations` with `method=seller_owner_attestation` | `seller_org_owner` role + MFA step-up + attestation text signed | Skips `pending_proof`; DNS TXT path only uses `pending_proof` |
| `pending_proof` | `proof_submitted` | Seller signals "I've added the record" via `PATCH .../probe` OR the scheduled prober auto-detects the record | DNS probe returns `success` across ≥ 2 resolvers | Probe counter increments |
| `pending_proof` | `expired` | Scheduler past `dns_challenge_expires_at` | TTL exceeded | Attestation is dead; seller MUST create a new row |
| `pending_proof` OR `proof_submitted` | `verified` | Verification worker confirms DNS record OR attestation-signer validation passes | DNS: record matches token across ≥ 2 resolvers + no split-horizon; Attestation: signer held role at signing time + MFA factor valid + text version current | Sets `verified_at`; emits `vendor_opt_out.authority_verified` notification (new; Appendix C) |
| `pending_proof` OR `proof_submitted` | `failed` | Any terminal verification failure | `verification_failure_reason` populated | Seller MUST start a new row |
| `verified` | `expired` | Scheduler past `expires_at` | 90d post-verification | Blocks new opt-out writes; existing honored opt-outs remain in force |
| `verified` OR `expired` | `revoked` | Seller revocation OR Ops revocation OR DSAR erasure cascade on signer | Any authorized path | Existing opt-outs whose write-time authority was this attestation are NOT auto-revoked; they remain until independently revoked |
| (create) | `verified` | `POST /v1/opt-outs/authority-attestations` with `method=ops_imposed_attestation` + DPO sign-off recorded | `ops_opt_out_admin` + `ops_imposed_dpo_approver_user_id` populated + `ops_imposed_case_ref_id` optional | Bypasses probe; for court-order / GDPR-mandated suppressions |

**Validation.**

- `POST` with `method=dns_txt` and `domain` not matching `Organization.verified_primary_domain` OR any member of `Organization.alternate_domains_verified` is rejected with `vendor_opt_out_authority_domain_not_owned` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422). Sellers MUST first verify the domain via the existing domain-verification flow (§4.4.10 / §26).
- `POST` with `method=seller_owner_attestation` and caller lacking `seller_org_owner` is rejected with `vendor_opt_out_authority_owner_role_required` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403).
- `POST` with `method=seller_owner_attestation` and MFA step-up not completed within the same session is rejected with `vendor_opt_out_authority_mfa_required` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 401).
- `PATCH .../probe` called with `verification_state != pending_proof` returns `vendor_opt_out_authority_probe_invalid_state` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409).
- DNS probe detecting split-horizon (one resolver returns `success`, another returns `record_not_found`) transitions to `failed` with `dns_split_horizon_detected`. The seller MUST ensure public and authoritative DNS views agree before retrying.
- Attempting to write a Vendor Opt-Out Record with `scope_kind=global` when the Org has no `verified` attestation MUST be rejected with `vendor_opt_out_authority_not_verified` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403). Lesser-scope writes when no attestation exists anywhere on the Org are rejected with the same error code — the *first* opt-out of any kind requires an attestation.

**Retention.** `verified` and `failed` rows retained Org-life + 7y (audit). `pending_proof` rows that `expire` without verification are retained 30 days then hard-deleted. `revoked` rows retained Org-life + 7y. `ops_imposed_attestation` rows retained Org-life + 10y per legal-hold default.

**Residency.** Row stored in originating Seller Org's data region. DNS probes executed from the same region's egress to avoid cross-residency egress logs. Ops-imposed attestations stored in the Ops region with a replicated read index scoped to the Seller's region for audit-query purposes.

**DSAR & Right-to-Erasure.** DSAR on an `attestation_signer_user_id` redacts the FK to `redacted` and preserves the row's attestation validity; the attestation remains `verified` because the domain-level authority is not tied to the specific human. DSAR on an `ops_imposed_dpo_approver_user_id` similarly redacts but retains validity. If the Seller Org is hard-purged (§45.4 terminal Org deletion), all attestation rows cascade-delete after the 30-day soft-delete window.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **DNS propagation lag.** A seller publishes the TXT record at their authoritative DNS but the public DNS has not propagated. Resolved: the probe worker retries on an exponential-backoff curve (Appendix F class `dns_attestation_probe`) for up to 24 hours; `dns_probe_attempt_count` increments; when the TTL expires without success, the row transitions to `failed` with reason `dns_probe_retry_exhausted`. The seller can re-create a new attestation with a fresh token.
2. **Split-horizon DNS attack.** Attacker runs a local resolver that injects the correct TXT record for the platform's egress IP but not for the public. Resolved: the probe worker mandates consistent `success` across at least 2 independent resolvers (Google + Cloudflare baseline); disagreement forces `failed` with reason `dns_split_horizon_detected`. The seller is directed to fix their public DNS.
3. **MFA factor revoked between attestation signing and verification.** Resolved: the verification step re-checks factor validity at the commit moment; a revoked factor forces `failed` with reason `mfa_factor_revoked`. The seller must re-attest with a valid factor.
4. **Signer loses `seller_org_owner` role mid-attestation.** Resolved: the verification step asserts role at `attestation_signed_at`, not at verification time — consistent with other §5 role-gated audit events. Role loss after signing does NOT invalidate an already-verified attestation.
5. **Seller's apex domain is a shared-use service (`github.io`, `vercel.app`, etc.).** Resolved: the initial `POST` validates `domain` against a maintained shared-use deny-list (sourced from Mozilla PSL — Public Suffix List); matches are rejected with `vendor_opt_out_authority_domain_is_shared_suffix` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422). Sellers using shared-use infra MUST use `seller_owner_attestation` instead.
6. **DNS TXT record accidentally contains a trailing space / Unicode normalization issue.** Resolved: the probe worker normalizes the TXT record via NFKC + trim before comparison; normalization drift is logged but does not fail the probe.

### 27.10.3 Enforcement Surfaces {#27.10.3-enforcement-surfaces}

Opt-outs MUST be enforced on every rendering surface that can emit a Seller Org's identity (name, logo, domain, canonical slug, descriptive copy) or a SellerSoftware's identity (product name, product slug, logo, category-pinned metadata). The enforcement surfaces are enumerated below. This table is the canonical allowlist; any new surface rendering Seller identity MUST be added here AND to §4.5.6's consumer-specific redaction rules in the same edit.

| # | Surface | Spec Section | Render Kind | Opt-Out Evaluation Point | Redaction Behavior on Opt-Out Match |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | M2 Selection Report Public Link | §43 | On-demand render with edge-cached HTML (60s TTL) | On every cache MISS + edge-serialization | Redact vendor name to "Vendor Opted Out"; buyer notified at render time; edge cache purged on opt-out write |
| 2 | M9 Category Page | §4.4.12 | Materialized row + edge-cached HTML (60s TTL) | On render-path serialization via `referenced_vendor_opt_out_map_json` + live registry probe | Opted-out vendor's row hidden; Schema.org `Product`/`Organization` nodes omitted from JSON-LD; category still renders |

> ¹ **k-floor disambiguation (M12 and M13).** Two distinct k-floors govern these surfaces and MUST NOT be conflated. (a) **Publication k-floor** — the floor that gates whether the surface publishes at all (M12: `k=20` per §48.6.4; M13: cell-level `k=10` per §48.6.4). These are product-integrity floors authored against the surface's aggregate-disclosure contract. (b) **Opt-out-driven cell-suppression k-floor** — applied AFTER a vendor opt-out scrub removes an opted-out vendor from a cell's cohort. For M12 (row 4): the opt-out floor is `k=5`, enforced directly at refresh + render against the §4.4.8 registry. For M13 (row 5; post-D-2.2-042 v7.2.0-REM Phase 1 remediation): no separate opt-out-driven floor — opt-out propagation reaches HeatMapCell only via §4.4.18 SellerSignal upstream cohort-exclusion, and cohort shrinkage is evaluated against the same publication floor `k=10`. M13 therefore has a single floor (the publication floor); the prior pre-remediation wording that referred to "the opt-out floor is k=10 for M13" was an artifact of the retired sentinel-stamp model and is superseded. Rows 4–5 enforce the opt-out-effect: for M12, the dedicated opt-out floor; for M13, propagated cohort shrinkage against the publication floor. A cell's cohort MUST satisfy the applicable floor(s); failure suppresses the cell, and (for M12) failure of the publication floor additionally suppresses the page. The two M12 floors are numerically distinct for good reason: the publication floor is stricter because an undisclosed page-level cohort is easier to re-identify than an undisclosed single-cell cohort inside an already-disclosed page. Do not rewrite any floor without cross-pass review of §48.6.4, §27.10.3 row 4 (M12) and row 5 (M13), and the §4.4.16 *Vendor-Identity-Free Aggregate Invariant* (M13).

**Surface allowlist invariant.** The §27.10.9 acceptance criteria include a CI test (`vendor_opt_out_surface_allowlist_invariant`) that inspects the production render graph and asserts every rendering surface emitting Seller identity is present in the table above. Introducing a new surface without updating this table is a build-blocking CI failure. This closes the "silent new surface leaks opt-out" risk.

**Consumers NOT in the enforcement surfaces table.** EOI, NDA, EOI Acceptance, Marketplace Abuse Report, buyer-console private Intelligence Briefs, Selection Report (private, not public), and any internal Ops view are explicitly OUT of scope for §27.10 enforcement. These are private or investigative surfaces; the business rationale is that a seller's opt-out is a public-visibility preference, not a platform-wide muzzle. This is consistent with §4.5.6 "Consumer-Specific Redaction Rules" rows.

### 27.10.4 Enforcement Pipeline & ≤60-Second Latency Budget {#27.10.4-enforcement-pipeline-&-60-second-latency-budget}

**Authoring Intent.** Per this prompt, "enforcement latency ≤60 seconds across all rendering surfaces." The latency is defined as: `observed_latency = t_first_surface_emits_redaction − t_opt_out_commit`. Where `t_opt_out_commit` is the transactional commit of a new Vendor Opt-Out Record (create with `auto_honored` state effective-from ≤ now) and `t_first_surface_emits_redaction` is the server-side timestamp of the first page render for any Surface #1–#17 (§27.10.3) that requests the opted-out entity AFTER the commit. The SLO is observed per rendering surface per request, not across all possible rendering surfaces simultaneously — the invariant is "no surface rendering after t_commit + 60s emits the un-redacted identity."

**Latency Budget Decomposition.** The 60-second budget is decomposed across five serial stages, each with a maximum allowance:

| Stage | Work | Budget | Enforcement |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| S1: Registry commit | `POST /v1/opt-outs` transactional write to §4.4.8 storage | ≤ 2s | Convex-backed write; synchronous index write to the hot-registry index in the same transaction |
| S2: Hot-registry fan-out | The hot-registry index (global read-replica, region-partitioned) propagates the new row to every region's read replica | ≤ 10s | Global replication; metered via `vendor_opt_out_registry_replication_lag` metric |
| S3: Edge-cache invalidation | CDN tag-based purge fan-out for every cached key associated with the Seller Org or SellerSoftware | ≤ 20s | Cloudflare tag-purge API with parallel fan-out; metered per-POP via `vendor_opt_out_edge_purge_lag` |
| S4: Search-index sync | Search index snapshot is rebuilt or delta-applied for the affected entities | ≤ 15s | Incremental index update; non-blocking to other stages |
| S5: Live-render registry check | The first render after t_commit that reaches any Surface #1–#17 acquires a hot-registry snapshot ≤ 60s old; if the snapshot is older than 60s, the render MUST re-fetch | ≤ 10s (slack budget) | §4.5.6 snapshot TTL; the re-fetch path blocks the render until a fresh snapshot is acquired |
|  | **Total** | **≤ 57s + 3s engineering slack = ≤ 60s** | End-to-end observed via the `vendor_opt_out_enforcement_latency_measured` PostHog event |

**Implementation Requirements.**

1. **Hot-registry index.** A second storage layer (distinct from the authoritative §4.4.8 table) materializes the active opt-out set per `(seller_org_id, scope_kind, scope_ref_type, scope_ref_id, page_type_filter)` into a key-value structure replicated to every region with ≤ 10-second replication lag. This layer is the one every render path queries; queries never hit the §4.4.8 table directly in hot paths. The hot-registry MUST expose a per-query timestamp indicating the snapshot age; render paths reject snapshots > 60s old and re-fetch.
2. **Edge cache purge.** Every cached key that could serve Seller-Org-identifying content MUST carry a surrogate cache key tag of the form `seller_org:{id}` AND (for SellerSoftware-specific pages) `seller_software:{id}`. On opt-out commit, the purge fan-out issues a tag-purge for the Seller Org's tag AND every affected SellerSoftware's tag, in parallel, across all CDN POPs. Purge completion is acknowledged per POP; the fan-out completes when the slowest POP acks within the 20s budget. Un-acked POPs after 20s emit `vendor_opt_out_edge_purge_slow_pop` (new; Appendix G PostHog event) and trigger a secondary retry; the render path defense-in-depth relies on S5 live-render checks to catch un-purged content.
3. **Search index sync.** The search index (powering Marketplace Search / Browse #8) MUST support atomic per-entity suppression via a "soft-suppressed" flag. On opt-out commit, the suppression bit is set atomically; the full re-indexing sweep is scheduled but not required to hit the 60s budget — only the suppression bit set matters for the SLO. Query time filters `soft_suppressed=false` by default.
4. **Live-render registry check.** Every Surface #1–#17 render path MUST call `vendor_opt_out_registry.is_suppressed(seller_org_id, surface_context)` before emitting identifying content. Implementations MUST NOT rely on any materialized page state (including `publication_status=suppressed_by_opt_out` from §4.4.10) as the sole gate — the live registry check is authoritative. A missing or stale registry response MUST fail closed (render as if suppressed, emit `vendor_opt_out_registry_unavailable_fail_closed` PostHog event; alert Ops).
5. **Retroactive materialized-artifact scrub.** The §4.4.8 `retro_backfill_*` sweep continues to update per-row materialized state within the 15-minute SLO — this is a row-state correction process (transitioning pages to `suppressed_by_opt_out`), not an enforcement mechanism. The live registry check is the enforcement mechanism; the retro sweep is bookkeeping that ensures the database is self-consistent with what the render path is already doing.
6. **Fail-closed everywhere.** On any failure in S1–S5 (registry unavailable, replication lag > 10s, edge-purge ack timeout, search index sync failure, snapshot fetch timeout), the render path MUST default to the most conservative behavior: suppress the identifying content. This protects the seller from accidental leak at the cost of occasional over-redaction during infra incidents.
7. **Observability.** Every `vendor_opt_out.opted_out` webhook carries a `registry_commit_at` timestamp. Every render emitting redacted content on a recently-opted-out entity emits `vendor_opt_out_enforcement_latency_measured` with `latency_ms = now - registry_commit_at`. A rolling P99 alert on this metric fires when the daily P99 exceeds 50s (giving 10s of SLO headroom) via Signal Integrity Monitor (§27.9 C.100 extension).

**Opt-in (revocation) symmetric budget.** The same 60s budget applies to `DELETE /v1/opt-outs/:id` — un-suppressing a previously redacted entity MUST NOT take longer than 60s end-to-end. Edge cache is purged; the hot-registry drops the row; live renders stop suppressing. The `vendor.opted_in` webhook carries `registry_revoke_at` for symmetric latency measurement.

### 27.10.5 Retroactive Application Across All Orgs {#27.10.5-retroactive-application-across-all-orgs}

Opt-out is retroactive and applies across all Orgs per this prompt. This means: a Seller Org creating an opt-out today MUST see the suppression applied to every already-published rendering artifact that references the Seller, regardless of which Buyer Org generated the artifact or viewed it. The key cases are:

1. **Buyer-facing private artifacts referencing the Seller.** The opt-out does NOT suppress buyer-private Selection Reports, Intelligence Briefs, or internal comments — those are private to the buyer. It DOES suppress the M2 Public Link projection of a Selection Report (Surface #1). This is consistent with "public-facing mechanics" scope in Summary C.123.
2. **Public Selection Report links already in the wild.** Every Buyer Org who previously generated an M2 Public Link for any Selection Report that references the opted-out Seller MUST have the public projection of that link updated within 60s of the opt-out write. The M2 Public Link render path (§43) checks the registry on every GET; the buyer's share URL remains valid but serves the redacted projection. A buyer-visible banner in the buyer's Selection Report UI alerts them that the public projection now contains redactions and offers a one-click regenerate-link option.
3. **Cross-Org references in Ops-authored pages (M9/M10/M11/M12/M13).** These are Sourcera-owned public pages rendering comparative content across many Sellers. The opt-out retroactively redacts the Seller's column/row/node across every such page; render contract + materialized `referenced_vendor_opt_out_map_json` per §4.5.6. The full retro sweep completes within 15 minutes for ≤ 10K pages; ≤ 60 min for ≤ 100K; ≤ 4h for > 100K (per §4.5.6 AC #4). Live render paths are already enforcing within 60s via live registry probe, so the retro sweep is for database self-consistency, not enforcement.
4. **Seller Signals that already identified the Seller to a Buyer.** Seller Signals are seller-side deliveries about buyer cohort intent; they do not surface the Seller's identity to buyers. They do deliver to the Seller themselves. An opt-out does NOT suspend Seller Signal delivery to the Seller itself — the Seller can still receive anonymized buyer cohort signals. What it suspends is the reverse direction: Sourcera-initiated broadcasts that name the Seller publicly. CRM Sync outbound to the opted-out Seller's CRM is also NOT suppressed — the Seller's own CRM sync is private to the Seller.
5. **Previously issued M2 Public Link URLs that the Buyer has already shared externally (e.g., in emails to their team).** Resolved: the URL remains valid; hitting it after opt-out commit returns the redacted projection per Surface #1. The URL is not revoked (that would be a second, separate operation).

**Cross-Org scope invariant.** No Buyer Org can "override" a Seller's opt-out. No per-Buyer-Org exception exists. The registry is a global suppression authoritative for every public-facing render path regardless of which Buyer Org is the requesting context.

**Acceptance test.** The §27.10.9 AC #9 "cross-Org retroactive scope" test creates a synthetic fixture: 3 Buyer Orgs, each with an M2 Public Link referencing the target Seller; the Seller then opts out; within 60s, all 3 M2 Public Links MUST serve the redacted projection when GET from an outside network. Failure is a P1 data-integrity bug.

### 27.10.6 API Endpoints {#27.10.6-api-endpoints}

All endpoints follow §32 patterns: bearer token auth per §32.2, fine-grained scopes per §32.3, cursor-based pagination 50/250 per §32.4, standard envelope per §32.5, idempotency via `Idempotency-Key` header per §32.6, rate-limit headers per §32.7, standard error schema per Appendix I. Rate-limit class: `vendor_opt_out_standard` (§32.4.5; 200/hr burst, 5K/day) unless otherwise noted.

**Path convention.** The endpoints are authored under the spec's canonical `/v1/` prefix per §32. Historical opt-out path-prefix aliases are superseded by the `/v1/opt-outs` paths in this table and the §32.5 Vendor Opt-Outs catalog. This is a path-prefix normalization only; it does not change auth, rate-limit, idempotency, webhook, or serializer behavior.

| Method | Path | Scope | Purpose | Rate limit | Key error codes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `POST` | `/v1/opt-outs` | `write:vendor_opt_outs`; seller-console; role ∈ {`seller_billing_admin`, `seller_org_admin`, `seller_org_owner`} | Create an opt-out record | `vendor_opt_out_standard` | `vendor_opt_out_authority_not_verified`, `vendor_opt_out_authority_expired`, `vendor_opt_out_reason_note_required`, `vendor_opt_out_scope_ref_invalid`, `vendor_opt_out_cross_console_access`, `vendor_opt_out_duplicate_active_scope` |
| `GET` | `/v1/opt-outs` | `read:vendor_opt_outs`; seller-console (Seller Org sees its own rows); Ops-console (all rows) | List opt-out records | `vendor_opt_out_standard` | `vendor_opt_out_cross_console_access` |
| `GET` | `/v1/opt-outs/:id` | `read:vendor_opt_outs`; Seller sees its own; Ops sees all | Retrieve a single opt-out record | `vendor_opt_out_standard` | `vendor_opt_out_not_found`, `vendor_opt_out_cross_console_access` |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/opt-outs/:id` | `write:vendor_opt_outs`; role as above; `ops_imposed` rows may be DELETEd only by `ops_opt_out_admin` | Revoke an opt-out (transition `ops_review_status→revoked`) | `vendor_opt_out_standard` | `vendor_opt_out_not_found`, `vendor_opt_out_cross_console_access`, `vendor_opt_out_ops_imposed_seller_cannot_revoke`, `vendor_opt_out_already_revoked` |
| `POST` | `/v1/opt-outs/authority-attestations` | `write:vendor_opt_out_authority`; role as above | Create a VendorOptOutAuthorityAttestation row | `vendor_opt_out_standard` | `vendor_opt_out_authority_domain_not_owned`, `vendor_opt_out_authority_owner_role_required`, `vendor_opt_out_authority_mfa_required`, `vendor_opt_out_authority_domain_is_shared_suffix` |
| `GET` | `/v1/opt-outs/authority-attestations` | `read:vendor_opt_out_authority` | List Org's attestations | `vendor_opt_out_standard` | — |
