| `PATCH` | `/v1/opt-outs/authority-attestations/:id/probe` | `write:vendor_opt_out_authority` | Request an immediate DNS probe (normally auto-scheduled) | 6/hr/Org | `vendor_opt_out_authority_probe_invalid_state`, `vendor_opt_out_authority_probe_rate_limited` |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/opt-outs/authority-attestations/:id` | `write:vendor_opt_out_authority`; Ops may DELETE `ops_imposed_attestation` rows | Revoke an attestation | `vendor_opt_out_standard` | `vendor_opt_out_authority_attestation_not_found`, `vendor_opt_out_authority_already_revoked` |

#### 27.10.6.1 POST /v1/opt-outs {#27.10.6.1-post-opt-outs}

**Purpose.** Create a new Vendor Opt-Out Record (§4.4.8) with authority verification enforced at write time. Transitions the record to `auto_honored` synchronously; enqueues the retro-backfill sweep; fires the `vendor.opted_out` webhook.

**Authentication.** Bearer token; seller-console scope; caller MUST hold one of the permitted seller roles (see table above).

**Headers.**

- `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (required)
- `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` (optional but strongly recommended; per §32.6; same key within 24h returns the original response without creating a duplicate row)
- `X-Console: seller` (required per §7.2 firewall; incorrect value rejected with `dual_console_firewall_violation`)

**Request body (JSON).**

```json
{
  "scope_kind": "global",
  "scope_ref_type": null,
  "scope_ref_id": null,
  "page_type_filter": null,
  "effective_from": "2026-04-17T14:00:00Z",
  "effective_until": null,
  "reason_code": "competitive",
  "reason_note": "Strategic communications hold during acquisition close",
  "authority_attestation_id": "attestation_01HZ..."
}
```

Field semantics per §4.4.8 field table. `authority_attestation_id` MUST reference a `verified`-state `VendorOptOutAuthorityAttestation` row belonging to the caller's Org; missing / wrong-state / foreign-Org references are rejected with `vendor_opt_out_authority_not_verified` (HTTP 403).

**Response body (JSON, HTTP 201).**

```json
{
  "id": "opt_01HZ...",
  "org_id": "org_01H...",
  "scope_kind": "global",
  "scope_ref_type": null,
  "scope_ref_id": null,
  "page_type_filter": null,
  "effective_from": "2026-04-17T14:00:00Z",
  "effective_until": null,
  "reason_code": "competitive",
  "reason_note": "Strategic communications hold during acquisition close",
  "ops_review_status": "auto_honored",
  "retro_backfill_status": "pending",
  "authority_attestation_id": "attestation_01HZ...",
  "created_at": "2026-04-17T14:00:01.234Z",
  "created_by": "user_01H...",
  "registry_commit_at": "2026-04-17T14:00:01.234Z"
}
```

**Error responses.**

| HTTP | Code | Condition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 400 | `vendor_opt_out_scope_ref_invalid` | `scope_kind` + `scope_ref_type` + `scope_ref_id` incoherent per §4.4.8 scope rules |
| 401 | `auth_token_invalid` | Standard |
| 403 | `vendor_opt_out_authority_not_verified` | Org has no `verified` attestation OR the referenced attestation is not `verified` |
| 403 | `vendor_opt_out_authority_expired` | Referenced attestation is `expired` |
| 403 | `seller_console_role_insufficient` | Caller role not in permitted set |
| 404 | `vendor_opt_out_cross_console_access` | Buyer-console token |
| 409 | `vendor_opt_out_duplicate_active_scope` | Active opt-out with same `(scope_kind, scope_ref_type, scope_ref_id, page_type_filter)` already exists |
| 422 | `vendor_opt_out_reason_note_required` | `reason_code=other` without `reason_note` |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | `vendor_opt_out_standard` exceeded |

**Idempotency.** Same `Idempotency-Key` + same request body returns the original response with HTTP 201 again (per §32.6). Same key + different body returns HTTP 409 `idempotency_key_request_mismatch`.

**Side effects.**

- Transactional write to §4.4.8 table.
- Synchronous write to hot-registry index.
- Enqueue of §4.4.8 retro backfill sweep.
- Emission of `vendor.opted_out` webhook (see §27.10.7).
- Per-page `vendor_opt_out.applied` webhooks emitted during retro sweep fan-out.
- PostHog `vendor_opt_out_registry_lifecycle_opted_out` event.
- Audit Event row with `actor_user_id = created_by`, `actee_entity_id = opt_out_id`, `action = vendor_opt_out_create`.

#### 27.10.6.2 GET /v1/opt-outs {#27.10.6.2-get-opt-outs}

**Purpose.** List Vendor Opt-Out Records visible to the caller. Seller-console sessions see only their own Org's rows; Ops-console sees all rows.

**Query parameters.**

- `scope_kind` (optional; filter): `global`, `category`, `software`, `page_type`, `specific_page`
- `ops_review_status` (optional; filter): `auto_honored`, `pending_ops_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, `revoked`
- `active_at` (optional; ISO 8601 timestamp): returns rows with `effective_from ≤ active_at` AND (`effective_until IS NULL` OR `effective_until > active_at`)
- `cursor` (optional; base64 cursor per §32.4)
- `limit` (optional; default 50, max 250)

**Response body (JSON, HTTP 200).**

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "opt_01HZ...",
      "org_id": "org_01H...",
      "scope_kind": "global",
      "scope_ref_type": null,
      "scope_ref_id": null,
      "ops_review_status": "auto_honored",
      "effective_from": "2026-04-17T14:00:00Z",
      "effective_until": null,
      "retro_backfill_status": "complete",
      "created_at": "2026-04-17T14:00:01.234Z"
    }
  ],
  "pagination": { "next_cursor": "eyJpZCI6Im9wdF8wMUh..." }
}
```

**Error responses.**

| HTTP | Code | Condition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 404 | `vendor_opt_out_cross_console_access` | Buyer-console token |
| 400 | `invalid_cursor` | Cursor forgery or stale cursor |

#### 27.10.6.3 GET /v1/opt-outs/:id {#27.10.6.3-get-opt-out-detail}

**Purpose.** Retrieve a single opt-out record. Returns the full §4.4.8 field set (including `ops_reviewed_by`, `ops_review_status`, `retro_backfill_affected_page_count`). Ops sees all; Seller sees its own.

**Response body (JSON, HTTP 200).** Full §4.4.8 record serialization; `created_by` is redacted to `redacted` for DSAR-processed callers per §6.8.

**Error responses.**

| HTTP | Code | Condition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 404 | `vendor_opt_out_not_found` | Row does not exist OR exists in another Org and caller is not Ops |
| 404 | `vendor_opt_out_cross_console_access` | Buyer-console token |

#### 27.10.6.4 DELETE /v1/opt-outs/:id {#27.10.6.4-delete-opt-out}

**Purpose.** Revoke an active opt-out. Transitions `ops_review_status` to `revoked`; kicks a reverse retro-backfill sweep that re-publishes previously suppressed artifacts; fires the `vendor.opted_in` webhook.

**Authentication.** Seller role (own Org) or Ops role (`ops_opt_out_admin` for `ops_imposed` rows).

**Headers.**

- `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (required)
- `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` (optional; same semantics as POST)
- `X-Console: seller` or `ops` (required)

**Request body.** Empty (DELETE semantics). Optional JSON body may carry `{"revocation_note": "...", "revocation_reason_code": "<enum>"}` where `revocation_reason_code` ∈ `seller_change_of_position`, `ops_override`, `legal_dispute_resolved`, `gdpr_withdrawal`, `attestation_reinstated`, `other` (new Appendix J enum `vendor_opt_out_revocation_reason_code`). `other` requires `revocation_note`.

**Response body (JSON, HTTP 200).**

```json
{
  "id": "opt_01HZ...",
  "ops_review_status": "revoked",
  "revoked_at": "2026-05-01T09:00:00Z",
  "revocation_reason_code": "seller_change_of_position",
  "revocation_note": null,
  "retro_backfill_status": "pending",
  "registry_revoke_at": "2026-05-01T09:00:00.123Z"
}
```

**Error responses.**

| HTTP | Code | Condition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 404 | `vendor_opt_out_not_found` | — |
| 404 | `vendor_opt_out_cross_console_access` | Buyer-console token |
| 403 | `vendor_opt_out_ops_imposed_seller_cannot_revoke` | `reason_code=ops_imposed` and caller is not Ops |
| 409 | `vendor_opt_out_already_revoked` | Already in `revoked` state |

**Side effects.**

- Transactional update to §4.4.8 row (`ops_review_status=revoked`, `retro_backfill_status=pending`).
- Drop from hot-registry index.
- Edge-cache purge fan-out (same tag-purge paths as opt-out create).
- Reverse retro-backfill sweep enumerates previously suppressed pages and re-publishes them.
- Emission of `vendor.opted_in` webhook.
- Per-page `vendor_opt_out.revoked` webhooks emitted during retro sweep fan-out.
- PostHog `vendor_opt_out_registry_lifecycle_opted_in` event.
- Audit Event row.

**Note on "DELETE as revoke".** DELETE is semantically revoke-not-purge. The row is NOT hard-deleted; it is transitioned to `revoked` per §4.4.8 state machine. Hard delete is Ops-only and reserved for DSAR Org-level erasure per §45.4. This aligns with §4.4.8 soft-delete semantics and preserves audit integrity.

### 27.10.7 Webhook Catalog {#27.10.7-webhook-catalog}

All §27.10 webhook events use transport per §31.1–§31.6 (HMAC-SHA256 signing, `event_id` idempotency, Appendix F retry curve, DLQ after 5 consecutive failures, payload ≤ 256 KB). Envelope per §31.2.

**Two webhook families.** §27.10 introduces `vendor.opted_out` and `vendor.opted_in` as the lifecycle events a subscriber uses to track the Seller-Org-level opt-out decision. The existing §4.5.6 per-page sweep events `vendor_opt_out.applied` and `vendor_opt_out.revoked` are retained as the per-artifact invalidation events. The two families are disjoint:

- **Lifecycle (`vendor.opted_out` / `vendor.opted_in`):** fires ONCE per opt-out commit / revocation commit; consumed by seller's own integrations to mirror opt-out state into downstream systems.
- **Page-sweep (`vendor_opt_out.applied` / `vendor_opt_out.revoked`):** fires PER-PAGE during the retro backfill sweep; consumed by Ops observability, cache-bust infrastructure, and any external system that mirrors specific pages. High-volume during sweeps.

| event_type | event_class | Audience | Trigger | Key payload fields |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `vendor.opted_out` | `vendor_opt_out_registry_lifecycle` | Seller Org (emitter); Ops Org (observer) | `POST /v1/opt-outs` commits successfully | `vendor_opt_out_id`, `org_id` (Seller), `scope_kind`, `scope_ref_type`, `scope_ref_id`, `page_type_filter`, `effective_from`, `effective_until`, `reason_code`, `reason_note` (redactable), `authority_attestation_id`, `authority_method`, `registry_commit_at`, `retro_backfill_enqueued_at`, `expected_retro_backfill_complete_by` (= registry_commit_at + §4.5.6 AC #4 SLO based on page count estimate) |
| `vendor.opted_in` | `vendor_opt_out_registry_lifecycle` | Seller Org; Ops Org | `DELETE /v1/opt-outs/:id` commits successfully | `vendor_opt_out_id`, `org_id`, `revoked_at`, `revocation_reason_code`, `revocation_note` (redactable), `registry_revoke_at`, `retro_backfill_reverse_enqueued_at`, `reinstatement_scope` (derived summary of what becomes visible again) |
| `vendor_opt_out.applied` (existing; retained from §4.5.6 Cache-Bust on Write) | `vendor_opt_out_page_sweep` | Ops Org; subscribing external cache systems | Retro-backfill sweep applies opt-out to a specific page artifact | `vendor_opt_out_id`, `page_entity_type` (enum), `page_entity_id`, `applied_at`, `prior_page_status`, `new_page_status` |
| `vendor_opt_out.revoked` (existing; retained from §4.5.6) | `vendor_opt_out_page_sweep` | Ops Org; subscribing external cache systems | Reverse retro-backfill sweep restores a specific page artifact | `vendor_opt_out_id`, `page_entity_type`, `page_entity_id`, `restored_at`, `prior_page_status`, `new_page_status` |

**Envelope example (`vendor.opted_out`).**

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_01HZABCD...",
  "event_type": "vendor.opted_out",
  "event_class": "vendor_opt_out_registry_lifecycle",
  "event_timestamp": "2026-04-17T14:00:01.234Z",
  "organization_id": "org_01H...",
  "console": "seller",
  "api_version": "2026-04-01",
  "payload": {
    "vendor_opt_out_id": "opt_01HZ...",
    "org_id": "org_01H...",
    "scope_kind": "global",
    "scope_ref_type": null,
    "scope_ref_id": null,
    "page_type_filter": null,
    "effective_from": "2026-04-17T14:00:00Z",
    "effective_until": null,
    "reason_code": "competitive",
    "reason_note": "redacted",
    "authority_attestation_id": "attestation_01HZ...",
    "authority_method": "dns_txt",
    "registry_commit_at": "2026-04-17T14:00:01.234Z",
    "retro_backfill_enqueued_at": "2026-04-17T14:00:01.250Z",
    "expected_retro_backfill_complete_by": "2026-04-17T14:15:01.250Z"
  },
  "signature": "sha256=<hex>"
}
```

**Idempotency.** `event_id` is globally unique per event; subscribers MUST treat repeated deliveries of the same `event_id` as no-ops.

**Retry curve.** Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve.

**Volume budget.**

- `vendor.opted_out` / `vendor.opted_in`: low volume (≤ 100/day per Seller Org at steady state; bursts during competitive M&A events).
- `vendor_opt_out.applied` / `vendor_opt_out.revoked`: bounded by page count; can burst to ~1,000 events per retro sweep for a `global` scope on a Seller with many referenced pages. Batching not applied — each page event is a first-class row for cache-bust clarity.

**Subscription gating.** `vendor_opt_out_registry_lifecycle` events are delivered to subscribers with `organization_id = subscribing_org_id`; cross-Org delivery forbidden. `vendor_opt_out_page_sweep` events are delivered to Ops-subscribed endpoints and to any Seller-subscribed endpoint where `organization_id = seller_org_id` of the opt-out.

**PostHog mirrors.** Registered per Appendix G extension: `vendor_opt_out_registry_lifecycle_opted_out`, `vendor_opt_out_registry_lifecycle_opted_in`, `vendor_opt_out_page_sweep_applied`, `vendor_opt_out_page_sweep_revoked`, plus the latency/observability events: `vendor_opt_out_enforcement_latency_measured`, `vendor_opt_out_registry_unavailable_fail_closed`, `vendor_opt_out_edge_purge_slow_pop`, `vendor_opt_out_authority_submitted`, `vendor_opt_out_authority_verified`, `vendor_opt_out_authority_failed`.

### 27.10.8 DSAR, Retention, and Residency {#27.10.8-dsar-retention-and-residency}

**Retention.**

- Vendor Opt-Out Record: Org-life + 7y per §4.4.8 (unchanged).
- VendorOptOutAuthorityAttestation: `verified`/`failed`/`revoked` rows Org-life + 7y; `pending_proof` that expires without verification retained 30d then hard-deleted; `ops_imposed_attestation` rows Org-life + 10y (legal hold default per §45.2).

**Residency.**

- Vendor Opt-Out Record stored in originating Seller Org's data region; queried via globally-replicated read index per §4.4.8.
- VendorOptOutAuthorityAttestation stored in originating region; DNS probes executed from the same region's egress.
- Hot-registry index is globally-replicated read-only with per-region replicas; writes propagate bidirectionally with ≤ 10s lag (stage S2 of §27.10.4 budget).
- Edge CDN caches are region-partitioned; tag-purge fan-out crosses all regions in parallel.

**DSAR.**

*Right-to-access.* A DSAR on a Seller user returns: (a) the user's `created_by` / `updated_by` / `attestation_signer_user_id` appearances across Vendor Opt-Out Record rows in the Org; (b) any `ops_imposed_dpo_approver_user_id` appearances if the user is Ops/DPO; (c) the `dns_challenge_token` and probe history where the user was the creator. No buyer data is surfaced.

*Right-to-erasure on a Seller user.* Cascade:

1. Redact `created_by`, `updated_by`, `attestation_signer_user_id`, `ops_imposed_dpo_approver_user_id` FK references to `redacted`.
2. Do NOT delete Vendor Opt-Out Records or VendorOptOutAuthorityAttestation rows — audit integrity exemption per §6.8.5. The opt-out remains effective; the attestation remains valid.
3. If the erased user was the sole `seller_org_owner` who signed a `seller_owner_attestation`, the attestation does NOT invalidate automatically — the authority was domain-level at signature time (per 27.10.2 Failure Mode #4). However, a Consent Ledger check runs at next attestation expiration (90d): if the Org has no remaining `seller_org_owner` to re-attest, the attestation expires to `expired` state and new opt-out writes are blocked until a new owner is appointed.
4. If the erased user was the sole DPO approver on an `ops_imposed_attestation`, the attestation remains valid (DPO authority was exercised once; subsequent users do not need to re-exercise it); the redacted FK is preserved in the audit trail.

*Right-to-erasure on a Buyer user.* Not applicable — the Vendor Opt-Out Registry does not store buyer data.

**Cross-residency enforcement.** An EU-resident Seller Org's opt-out MUST be enforced across US-resident render paths (e.g., a US Buyer hitting a Schema.org-embedded M9 page that mentions the EU Seller). The hot-registry index is global (read-only replicas in every region) precisely to enable this cross-residency enforcement without round-tripping to the Seller's origin region. The write propagation path respects EU→US replication latency bounds (≤ 10s per S2).

**Sub-processor disclosure.** Cloudflare (edge CDN, tag-purge) and Convex (registry storage + global replication) are existing sub-processors (§6.8 DPA Appendix). No new sub-processors introduced by §27.10.

### 27.10.9 Acceptance Criteria {#27.10.9-acceptance-criteria}

1. A `POST /v1/opt-outs` with `scope_kind=global` and a valid `authority_attestation_id` pointing at a `verified` attestation MUST transition the Vendor Opt-Out Record to `ops_review_status=auto_honored` synchronously and return HTTP 201 within 2 seconds P95 at steady-state load. QA test `vendor_opt_out_create_global_auto_honored` asserts.
2. A `POST /v1/opt-outs` without a `verified` attestation on the Org MUST be rejected with HTTP 403 `vendor_opt_out_authority_not_verified`. QA test `vendor_opt_out_authority_gate_enforced` asserts.
3. A buyer-console bearer token calling ANY of `POST`, `GET`, `DELETE /v1/opt-outs*` MUST receive HTTP 404 with `vendor_opt_out_cross_console_access`. QA test `vendor_opt_out_cross_console_firewall` asserts across the full endpoint set.
4. The end-to-end live-render enforcement latency SLO is `P99 ≤ 60 seconds` across all Surface #1–#17 over any rolling 24-hour window. Measured via `vendor_opt_out_enforcement_latency_measured` PostHog events where `latency_ms = t_first_surface_emits_redaction - registry_commit_at`. Daily P99 > 50s fires SIM alert; daily P99 > 60s is a P1 incident. QA test `vendor_opt_out_latency_slo` asserts via a synthetic load generator hitting M2, M9, M11, M12, M13, SellerOrgPage, SoftwarePage, and `/api/public/*` endpoints within 55 seconds of opt-out commit.
5. A Vendor Opt-Out Record write MUST propagate to all region replicas of the hot-registry index within 10 seconds P99 (§27.10.4 S2). QA test `vendor_opt_out_registry_replication_lag` asserts under multi-region load.
6. Edge CDN cache tag-purge fan-out MUST ack from ALL POPs within 20 seconds P99 of opt-out commit (§27.10.4 S3). Un-acked POPs after 20s emit `vendor_opt_out_edge_purge_slow_pop` and trigger secondary retry; the SLO remains on the live-render registry check as the enforcement authority. QA test `vendor_opt_out_edge_purge_fan_out` asserts.
7. Every render path on Surface #1–#17 MUST call the live registry check before emitting identifying content; a missing or stale (> 60s) registry response MUST fail closed (suppress the identity) and emit `vendor_opt_out_registry_unavailable_fail_closed`. QA test `vendor_opt_out_fail_closed_on_registry_unavailable` asserts via forced dependency outage.
8. The Schema.org JSON-LD serializer on Surface #2, #3, #6, #7 MUST omit opted-out `Product` and `Organization` nodes entirely (not emit blanked stubs). CI test `schema_org_opt_out_omission` asserts (reused from §4.5.6 AC #2).
9. Cross-Org retroactive scope: given 3 Buyer Orgs each with an M2 Public Link referencing a target Seller, a subsequent `POST /v1/opt-outs` with `scope_kind=global` by the target Seller MUST cause all 3 M2 Public Links to serve the redacted projection within 60 seconds of commit when retrieved via anonymous HTTP GET from outside the VPN. E2E test `vendor_opt_out_m2_cross_org_retroactive` asserts.
10. A `DELETE /v1/opt-outs/:id` MUST transition `ops_review_status` to `revoked`, emit `vendor.opted_in`, and cause previously suppressed Surface #1–#17 artifacts to re-emit the Seller's identity within 60 seconds of DELETE commit (symmetric SLO). QA test `vendor_opt_out_revocation_symmetric_slo` asserts.
11. A `DELETE /v1/opt-outs/:id` on an `ops_imposed` row by a non-Ops caller MUST return HTTP 403 `vendor_opt_out_ops_imposed_seller_cannot_revoke`. QA test `vendor_opt_out_ops_imposed_seller_cannot_revoke_enforced` asserts.
12. The `vendor.opted_out` webhook MUST fire within 5 seconds of POST commit (P99) with `registry_commit_at` populated. The `vendor.opted_in` webhook MUST fire within 5 seconds of DELETE commit (P99) with `registry_revoke_at` populated. QA test `vendor_opt_out_lifecycle_webhook_timeliness` asserts.
13. Per-page `vendor_opt_out.applied` / `vendor_opt_out.revoked` webhooks MUST fire during retro backfill for each affected page with `page_entity_type` matching the canonical Appendix J enum and `page_entity_id` the canonical row id. CI test `vendor_opt_out_page_sweep_webhook_coverage` asserts every page entity type in the enum is covered by at least one regression fixture.
14. The enforcement-surface allowlist invariant test `vendor_opt_out_surface_allowlist_invariant` MUST inspect the production render graph and fail the CI build if any surface emitting Seller identity is missing from the §27.10.3 table. This closes the "silent new surface leaks opt-out" risk.
15. A DNS TXT attestation probe MUST succeed across at least 2 independent resolvers (Google 8.8.8.8 + Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 minimum) before transitioning to `verified`. Disagreement between resolvers forces `failed` with `dns_split_horizon_detected`. QA test `vendor_opt_out_authority_dns_multi_resolver` asserts.
16. A `seller_owner_attestation` MUST be gated by MFA step-up within the current session; absence returns HTTP 401 `vendor_opt_out_authority_mfa_required`. QA test `vendor_opt_out_authority_mfa_required_enforced` asserts.
17. A `seller_owner_attestation` creator MUST hold `seller_org_owner` at `attestation_signed_at`; role loss between signature and verification does NOT invalidate an already-verified attestation (per §27.10.2 Failure Mode #4). QA test `vendor_opt_out_authority_role_check_at_signature` asserts.
18. A `VendorOptOutAuthorityAttestation` with `method=dns_txt` and `domain` matching the Public Suffix List deny-list MUST be rejected with `vendor_opt_out_authority_domain_is_shared_suffix`. CI test `vendor_opt_out_authority_psl_denylist_enforced` asserts.
19. A `verified` attestation MUST expire 90 days after `verified_at`; thereafter new opt-out writes return `vendor_opt_out_authority_expired`. Existing opt-outs remain honored. QA test `vendor_opt_out_authority_expiration_90d` asserts.
20. `retro_backfill_status` MUST transition `pending → in_progress → complete` for every `auto_honored` row; timeouts roll to `failed` and Ops is paged. QA test `vendor_opt_out_retro_backfill_status_machine` asserts.
21. The Seller Signals pipeline (§27.9.5 stage 7) MUST consume the hot-registry index at aggregation time; opt-out writes that land within the Signal Period MUST cause the target Seller to stop receiving deliveries for all affected cohorts, with `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` stamped on every affected `SellerSignal` row. QA test `vendor_opt_out_seller_signals_pipeline_integration` asserts.
22. The CRM Sync outbound (§31.9) MUST drop outbound events destined for an opted-out Seller at source; `crm_sync_outbound_suppressed_by_opt_out` PostHog event fires. QA test `vendor_opt_out_crm_sync_outbound_dropped` asserts.
23. A `PATCH .../probe` call on an attestation already in `verified`, `failed`, `expired`, or `revoked` state MUST return HTTP 409 `vendor_opt_out_authority_probe_invalid_state`. QA test `vendor_opt_out_authority_probe_terminal_state_guard` asserts.
24. A `POST /v1/opt-outs/authority-attestations/:id/probe` MUST be rate-limited to 6 per hour per Org; the 7th returns HTTP 429 `vendor_opt_out_authority_probe_rate_limited`. QA test `vendor_opt_out_authority_probe_rate_limit` asserts.
25. Every `POST /v1/opt-outs` MUST be idempotent via the `Idempotency-Key` header per §32.6; same key + same body returns the same response; same key + different body returns HTTP 409 `idempotency_key_request_mismatch`. QA test `vendor_opt_out_create_idempotent` asserts.
26. A new rendering surface added to the product that emits Seller identity WITHOUT being added to §27.10.3 MUST fail the CI test `vendor_opt_out_surface_allowlist_invariant` before merge. QA test `vendor_opt_out_surface_allowlist_regression` asserts via a fixture that introduces a synthetic new surface.
27. The `vendor_opt_out_registry_lifecycle` and `vendor_opt_out_page_sweep` event classes MUST be independently subscribable; subscribing to one MUST NOT imply subscribing to the other. QA test `vendor_opt_out_webhook_class_independence` asserts against the webhook registration API.
28. A DSAR right-to-erasure on a single `seller_org_owner` who signed an attestation MUST NOT invalidate the attestation; subsequent behavior is governed by the 90-day expiration SLO. QA test `vendor_opt_out_authority_dsar_signer_erasure` asserts.
29. The `authority_attestation_id` referenced at `POST /v1/opt-outs` time MUST be preserved on the Vendor Opt-Out Record in field `authority_attestation_id_ref` (authored into §4.4.8 in the same edit that landed §27.10; see §4.4.8 AC #6–7); a subsequent revocation of the attestation MUST NOT auto-revoke the opt-out (the opt-out remains `auto_honored`; the authority was satisfied at write time). QA test `vendor_opt_out_authority_post_hoc_revocation` asserts.

### 27.10.10 Failure Modes Addressed {#27.10.10-failure-modes-addressed}

1. **Hot-registry index replication lag exceeds 10s.** A US writer commits; an EU reader on a cached M9 page emits the un-redacted identity before EU replica catches up. Resolved: live-render check requires a snapshot ≤ 60s old AND the CDN cache for the EU region was tag-purged in parallel (S3 completes within 20s regardless of S2 lag). If S2 lag and S3 purge both fail, S5 fails closed via `vendor_opt_out_registry_unavailable_fail_closed`. The 10s S2 budget is an optimization, not the invariant; the fail-closed default is the invariant.
2. **Cloudflare tag-purge partial failure.** One POP acks, another times out. Resolved: slow-POP PostHog event + secondary retry + defense-in-depth via S5 live-render check means un-purged edge caches still serve the correct (redacted) content because origin re-rendering hits the fresh registry. Cache eventually expires at TTL (60s edge TTL per §4.5.6); SLO honored.
3. **Concurrent opt-out and opt-in race (seller toggles twice in < 5 seconds).** Resolved: idempotency-key per-request prevents double-create; DELETE checks state is not already `revoked` and returns HTTP 409. Both writes are serialized at the §4.4.8 transactional layer; the final state reflects the last write. Webhooks fire in commit order; subscribers idempotently handle via `event_id`.
4. **Seller submits `POST /v1/opt-outs` with `scope_kind=global` but forgot to verify DNS TXT; writes succeed due to a cached stale authority check.** Resolved: authority check hits the attestation table directly (transactional read, no cache), returning the current state; cached stale reads are forbidden by the endpoint's `@Uncached` decorator. QA test asserts against a race where an attestation is revoked mid-request.
5. **DNS TXT probe flaky due to transient DNS outage; attestation stuck in `pending_proof` for 24h then expires.** Resolved: Appendix F retry curve for DNS probes with exponential backoff; manual `PATCH .../probe` allows the seller to force an immediate re-check (6/hr rate limit). If the 24h TTL expires, a new attestation row can be created with a fresh token.
6. **Seller removes their DNS TXT record after verification, then tries to write a new opt-out.** Resolved: attestation `verified_at` ages out at 90d; interim DNS record removal does NOT automatically invalidate the attestation (the domain authority was demonstrated at verification time). This is a deliberate design choice to avoid DNS jitter causing spurious authority failures; the 90d expiration re-checks periodically.
7. **Ops issues an `ops_imposed_attestation` without DPO sign-off (human error).** Resolved: validation rejects at write with `vendor_opt_out_authority_ops_imposed_missing_dpo` (new; Appendix I). The Ops Console UI blocks submission until the DPO approver is named.
8. **Seller Org downgrades from paid plan to free while having active opt-outs.** Resolved: opt-outs are NOT plan-gated (privacy/legal invariant is not a paid feature). Downgrade preserves all active opt-outs; the `VendorOptOutAuthorityAttestation` rows remain valid. New writes remain available on free tier. This is a deliberate deviation from typical §34 plan-gating; authored extension flagged in RECONCILIATION.md.
9. **Seller Org is acquired by a competitor; the acquiring Org wants to revoke opt-outs.** Resolved: opt-outs are Org-scoped. The acquiring Org inherits the Seller Org's `ops_review_status` rows per standard M&A data inheritance path (§45.5). An acquiring-Org Seller Owner can `DELETE /v1/opt-outs/:id` to revoke. Ops is notified via the M&A audit channel.
10. **Ops force-suppresses a Seller via `ops_imposed` opt-out; Seller disputes it in court and wins.** Resolved: Ops DELETEs the `ops_imposed` row per §27.10.6.4; the reverse retro-backfill sweep restores Seller's public presence within 60 seconds of commit; `vendor.opted_in` webhook notifies the Seller. The DELETE `revocation_reason_code=ops_override` with `revocation_note` referencing the court decision provides an audit trail.
11. **Search index sync fails but hot-registry and edge-purge succeed.** Resolved: search queries hit the `soft_suppressed` bit on the index; if the bit is not set due to sync failure, the query re-validates against the hot-registry at serialization time before emitting the result. Enforcement holds; search results may be momentarily stale but never leak the identity.
12. **Authority attestation MFA factor is passkey; user loses their hardware key.** Resolved: attestation remains valid for 90d regardless of subsequent factor state; user follows standard §6.7 MFA recovery flow to appoint a new factor; new attestations can be signed with the new factor.
13. **A new rendering surface is introduced in a future release that emits Seller identity but was not added to §27.10.3.** Resolved: CI test `vendor_opt_out_surface_allowlist_invariant` (AC #14, #26) inspects the render graph and fails the build. The feature cannot ship without updating §27.10.3.
14. **An opt-out expires (`effective_until`) at t, but a page rendered at t+5s still shows the Seller as suppressed because the edge cache is stale.** Resolved: the same 60s live-render re-check applies to `effective_until` expirations. The hot-registry index indexes active rows based on `effective_from ≤ now < (effective_until OR +∞)`; expirations trigger tag-purge fan-out symmetric to create/revoke.
15. **A Seller writes opt-out then revokes it, then writes opt-out again with the same scope; the idempotency window is 24h — do the two opt-outs collide?** Resolved: each opt-out is a new row per §4.4.8 append-only discipline. `vendor_opt_out_duplicate_active_scope` would fire ONLY if both were simultaneously in `auto_honored`; since the first was revoked before the second was created, no collision. Idempotency-Key scopes per-request, not per-content.

### 27.10.11 Self-Challenge Refinements {#27.10.11-self-challenge-refinements}

Items surfaced during the hostile-staff-engineer review of §27.10 and authored here to close gaps before engineering handoff. Flag any requiring product / privacy / legal sign-off in the reconciliation log.

**27.10.11.1 Authority-less "first ever" write deadlock.** A brand-new Seller Org has no attestation and wants to opt out immediately after sign-up. The `POST /v1/opt-outs` would reject because no `verified` attestation exists. Mitigation: the Seller Console flow forces the authority-attestation wizard before exposing the opt-out UI; the wizard captures `seller_owner_attestation` in-line during sign-up for a new Seller Org (DNS TXT is offered as an upgrade for sellers without `seller_org_owner` available). An Ops-bypass path using `ops_imposed_attestation` exists for extraordinary cases (court orders served on a Seller Org that has not yet had a `seller_org_owner` log in). Authored extension — flagged.

**27.10.11.2 Hot-registry "thundering herd" on mass opt-out event.** A compliance incident (e.g., category-wide GDPR complaint) causes 500 Sellers to opt out in a 5-minute window. Each write triggers a full edge-cache tag-purge fan-out, potentially DDoSing the CDN. Mitigation: the edge-purge fan-out uses batched tag-purges with a 1-second debounce window per Seller Org; multiple writes for the same Seller within the debounce coalesce into a single purge event. Bursts > 500 writes/min fall back to a global cache-TTL expiration (wait out the 60s TTL rather than purge) — SLO preserved because the 60s TTL equals the SLO. Authored extension — flagged.

**27.10.11.3 DNS challenge token information leak.** The `dns_challenge_token` appears in the seller's authoritative DNS, which is publicly queryable. If the token is guessable, an attacker could pre-seed a TXT record before the seller completes verification. Mitigation: tokens are 32-char URL-safe base32 (160 bits of entropy), single-use, and the probe expires after 24h. Additionally, the probe worker verifies the token was issued within the last 24h per the `dns_challenge_issued_at` field; an attacker would need both (a) to guess a 160-bit token AND (b) to do so within a 24h window AND (c) to pre-seed the seller's DNS. Computationally infeasible.

**27.10.11.4 Cache-key cardinality explosion on `scope_kind=category` with 500 Marketplace Categories.** If 500 Sellers each opt out of 10 different categories, the edge cache has ~5,000 distinct tag combinations to track. Mitigation: the surrogate tag schema uses `seller_org:{id}` primarily; category-scoped opt-outs also carry `seller_org:{id}+category:{category_id}` as a secondary tag. Purges target the primary tag (which covers all category-scoped opt-outs for that Seller Org); the secondary tag is for observability. Acceptable cardinality: O(Sellers) not O(Sellers × Categories).

**27.10.11.5 `ops_imposed` attestation revocation should NOT auto-revoke the underlying opt-out.** If Ops creates `ops_imposed_attestation` → writes opt-out → later revokes the attestation, does the opt-out remain? Per AC #29, the opt-out remains `auto_honored` (authority was satisfied at write time). Ops can independently revoke the opt-out via `DELETE /v1/opt-outs/:id` if that is the intent. This decoupling is deliberate — the attestation is proof-of-authority, not an ongoing permission. Authored extension — flagged for Legal / DPO sign-off.

**27.10.11.6 Authority path for a Seller Org with a privacy-protected WHOIS and no `seller_org_owner`.** A shell company sub-entity with a privacy-protected registration may have no `seller_org_owner` user on record (initial setup pending) AND cannot prove DNS TXT (if they don't control DNS directly — e.g., using a white-label reseller). Mitigation: Ops path via `ops_imposed_attestation` with justification + DPO sign-off + optional case-ref. Authored extension — confirm with Legal that this path is defensible.

**27.10.11.7 Reverse retro-backfill on `opted_in` MUST restore the same set of pages that were suppressed.** If the retro sweep applied to 1,000 pages, the reverse sweep MUST target exactly those 1,000 pages (not 999, not 1,001). Mitigation: the retro sweep persists an idempotent "sweep manifest" row capturing `(opt_out_id, swept_page_ids[])`; the reverse sweep consumes the manifest. Manifest integrity is asserted by the §27.10.9 AC #10 test. Authored extension — add sweep manifest as a sub-entity in a subsequent phase.

**27.10.11.8 Fail-closed default over-redaction.** If the hot-registry is unavailable, §27.10.4 requires fail-closed (suppress identity). For a 1-hour outage, this means every public page emits redactions. Mitigation: the fail-closed behavior is deliberate and is always preferable to leak; observability (`vendor_opt_out_registry_unavailable_fail_closed` rate) triggers P1 incident response within minutes. Sellers receive an Ops-status-page banner during the outage. Authored extension — Legal + Comms buy-in on user-facing Ops-status-page copy.

**27.10.11.9 Anti-circumvention — a Seller writes an opt-out, then creates a new SellerSoftware under the same Seller Org to re-emerge.** The new SellerSoftware MUST be covered by the existing `scope_kind=global` opt-out. Mitigation: `scope_kind=global` matches at `seller_org_id` level; the new SellerSoftware inherits the suppression because its `org_id` matches. Confirmed by §27.10.3 Surface #7 behavior. Re-emergence as a new `SellerSoftware` does not escape a `global` opt-out.

**27.10.11.10 Anti-circumvention — a Seller writes an opt-out, then transfers ownership to a different Org.** The new Org is a new `org_id`; the opt-out does NOT follow. Mitigation: the SellerSoftware transfer flow (§4.4.9) requires an Ops-validated transfer; Ops reviews active opt-outs on the source Org and either (a) propagates them to the destination Org (authoring new `ops_imposed` rows) or (b) confirms with the original Seller that the opt-out was intended to lapse at transfer. Authored extension — add to §4.4.9 transfer-flow authoring in a subsequent phase.

## 27.11 Marketplace Discovery Pricing (Non-AI Monetization Layer) {#27.11-marketplace-discovery-pricing-non-ai-monetization-layer}

### 27.11.1 Overview {#27.11.1-overview}

§27.11 is the **product-behavior layer** for Sourcera's non-AI monetization. It governs how the three marketplace-discovery surfaces — **Promoted Listings**, **Verification Tiers**, and **Featured Placements** — are rendered, gated, audited, and exposed across the Buyer Console, Seller Console, Ops Console, and public marketplace render paths. It does NOT define billing, invoicing, accounting, or tax semantics; those are exhaustively defined in §34.16 (Marketplace Discovery Pricing — Non-AI Layer) and in the append-only ledger entity §4.8.12 MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord. §27.11 implements against them; it does not supersede them.

**Source authority.** This section integrates and reconciles the following upstream sources (recorded in `/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → §27.11`):

| Source | Authority | Integrated Content |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Summary §2.10 | Authoritative product framing | Verification free-when-earned; Featured editorial-only; Promoted paid, second-price, k=5 |
| Summary §6.15.2 | Authoritative on Verification tier earn criteria | Basic / Verified / Certified; cadence; anti-gaming |
| Summary §6.16.6 | Upstream (conflicts on Verification and Featured paid framing) | Superseded by Summary §2.10 / C.131 / SPS §12 / §34.16 in the current release; paid modes reserved behind feature flags |
| Summary C.131 | Authoritative controlled-vocabulary entry | Free-when-earned verification; editorial-only featured |
| Seller Pricing Strategy §12 | Authoritative on Seller-facing pricing disclosure | Aligns with Summary §2.10 / §34.16 |
| Master Spec §34.16 | **Authoritative for billing, invoicing, ledger** | All dollar figures, auction-mechanic settlements, billing webhooks, revenue ledger |
| Master Spec §4.4.19 | **Authoritative for PromotedListing entity** | Field table, state machine, eligibility gate, auction mechanics |
| Master Spec §4.4.20 | **Authoritative for FeaturedPlacement entity** | Editorial-only default, paid_commitment mode feature-flag gated |
| Master Spec §4.4.21 | **Authoritative for VerificationReviewRecord entity** | Tier model, SLA, separation of duties, residency-locked reviewers |
| Master Spec §4.8.12 | **Authoritative for MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord ledger** | Append-only, cost-center=rev_marketplace_discovery, FX locking, legal-entity partitioning |
| Master Spec §7.2 | **Authoritative for Dual-Console Firewall** | Cross-console access returns HTTP 404; no leakage |
| Master Spec §31 | **Authoritative for webhook transport** | HMAC-SHA256; `event_id` canonical string format `evt_{unix_ms}_{base32_random10}`; Appendix F retry curve; DLQ after 5 |
| Master Spec §32 | **Authoritative for API patterns** | Cursor pagination; Idempotency-Key; rate-limit classes; error codes |

**Design principles** (each principle below is testable by the acceptance criteria in §27.11.8):

1. **Cost-center firewall.** Every dollar flowing through a marketplace-discovery surface is bound to `cost_center = rev_marketplace_discovery` (§4.8.3 Billing Ledger; §4.8.12 MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord). Zero revenue attribution to `rev_ai_wallet` or `rev_subscription` is tolerated.
2. **Buyer trust comes first.** Every paid surface is labeled per FTC 16 CFR Part 255.5; the label is non-suppressible; buyer opt-out is session-scoped to preserve Sourcera's disclosure obligation; bid amounts do not feed organic ranking.
3. **Dual-Console Firewall.** Buyer Console reads of Seller-owned records return scrubbed projections only (§4.4.19 *Cross-Console Projection Rule*, §4.4.20 *Buyer-Console Projection*); raw reads are rejected HTTP 404 per §7.2.
4. **k=5 anonymization on all aggregated auction / bidder metrics.** Categories with fewer than 5 distinct bidders in a window do NOT surface auction digests or clearing-price statistics to sellers or the public.
5. **Quality floor precedes commerce.** No paid surface renders for a seller who does not meet the applicable marketplace-discovery quality floor. For Promoted Listings, the source of truth is the full §4.4.19 Eligibility Gate plus the anti-spam checks in §27.11.6; §34.16.4 cites that gate instead of redefining it.
6. **Platform-integrity verification is never a revenue SKU.** Verification tiers are earned, not purchased. Charging sellers for verification destroys the signal (§34.16.2, Summary §2.10).
7. **Editorial Featured is the default.** Paid Featured placements are reserved behind `featured_placement_paid_mode_enabled=false` per-Org feature flag; enablement requires VP Marketing + VP Finance + VP Legal sign-off and an ethical-review gate (§34.16.3).
8. **No cross-marketplace-domain leakage.** Marketplace-domain rows (§43) never spill across domains; a Seller Org's Promoted Listing in the `us-defense-contractor` marketplace domain MUST NOT render in the `us-civilian-enterprise` marketplace domain even when category IDs collide.
9. **Residency inheritance.** Every marketplace-discovery entity inherits `data_residency_region` from its Origin Org (§4.4.19, §4.4.20, §4.4.21). No cross-region data motion is permitted.
10. **DSAR compatibility.** Pseudonymization of `created_by` / `updated_by` / `published_by_user_id` / `reviewer_user_id` on request, subject to the §45.1 platform-integrity financial-record retention exemption for revenue rows.

**What §27.11 does NOT cover:**

- **Billing mechanics** (auction settlement math, FX conversion, invoice line items, Stripe flows) — see §34.16.
- **Ledger schema** (MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord fields, state machine, CHECK constraints) — see §4.8.12.
- **Entity field tables** (PromotedListing, FeaturedPlacement, VerificationReviewRecord) — see §4.4.19, §4.4.20, §4.4.21.
- **Plan-tier entitlements** (which plans can bid, which can request Certified) — see §5.11 Feature Access Matrix and §34.1 Plan Tier Definitions.
- **Vendor Opt-Out cascade semantics** — see §27.10, which precedes §27.11 in authority for suppression and whose cascade clamps every surface in §27.11.

### 27.11.2 Promoted Listings {#27.11.2-promoted-listings}

**Buyer surface.** On every `CategoryPage` (§4.4.12) render and every EOI-eligible Buyer Workspace search result pane (§4.1), Sourcera may render up to **3 Promoted slots** per category, positioned above organic results and below any active Featured Placement for that category (display order: Featured > Promoted > Organic). Each Promoted slot renders the scrubbed PromotedListing projection (`{seller_software_id, category_id, ftc_disclosure_label: "Promoted", placement_surfaces[], active: true}`) plus the underlying SoftwarePage hero card (§4.4.11). The "Promoted" label is rendered in 14px / `--color-ui-emphasis-subtle` token per UX §tokens; it is non-suppressible, non-collapsible, and is rendered server-side to prevent client-side removal.

**Seller surface.** Seller Console → Marketplace Discovery → Promoted Listings (role: `seller_billing_admin` OR `seller_marketing_editor`; §4.4.10, Appendix J). The dashboard shows:

1. Active listings with live metrics: impression count (k=5-floored), qualified EOI acceptance count, spend-to-date, daily-cap headroom, frequency-cap headroom.
2. Historical listings with final-period metrics and clearing-price disclosures.
3. Category availability (remaining slots in each category for the current auction window).
4. Weekly bid submission modal (Sunday 12:00:00.000 UTC inclusive – Monday 00:00:00.000 UTC exclusive bid window per §34.16.1 #1; one bid per seller per category per window per §34.16.1 #2).
5. Monthly-allotment tracker (1/mo Seller Scale, 3/mo Seller Enterprise included; up to 4 additional purchased top-ups per month hard-capped).
6. Pause / Resume / Cancel controls.
7. Eligibility-gate status with actionable remediation links (e.g., "KB Health Score = 52.14, floor = 60.00; 9 SellerPage updates would raise your score — see checklist").

**Ops surface.** Ops Console → Marketplace → Promoted Listings (role: `ops_marketplace_editor` OR `ops_compliance_reviewer`). Ops can pause, terminate, adjust daily caps, or flag listings for anti-spam review. Every Ops action on a PromotedListing row writes an entry to the `SellerPlatformActionLog` (§4.4.22) with `action_category = promoted_listing_admin_action` and a mandatory justification string ≥ 40 characters.

**Lifecycle state machine.** PromotedListing status transitions (From / To / Trigger / Conditions / Notes). Enum values are registered in Appendix J `promoted_listing_status` (see §4.4.19; no new enum values required).

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| — | `draft` | POST `/v1/seller/marketplace/promoted-listings` | Seller holds `seller_billing_admin` OR `seller_marketing_editor` role; plan ≥ `seller_scale` | Emits `promoted_listing.created` webhook |
| `draft` | `pending_eligibility_check` | POST `/v1/seller/marketplace/promoted-listings/:id/submit` | All `draft`-required fields populated; idempotent on duplicate submit | No webhook emission (internal) |
| `pending_eligibility_check` | `active` | Eligibility-gate passes (§4.4.19 *Eligibility Gate*) | All 10 gate conditions hold transactionally | Emits `promoted_listing.auction_opened` at next Sunday 12:00 UTC window |
| `pending_eligibility_check` | `terminated_eligibility_lost` | Eligibility-gate fails | `eligibility_check_failed_reason` populated | Ops-visible; seller notified via `tpl_promoted_eligibility_failed` |
| `active` | `paused_by_seller` | POST `/v1/seller/marketplace/promoted-listings/:id/pause` | Seller-initiated | Emits `promoted_listing.paused` webhook with `paused_by = seller` |
| `active` | `paused_by_ops` | POST `/v1/ops/marketplace/promoted-listings/:id/pause` | Ops-initiated; justification required | Emits `promoted_listing.paused` webhook with `paused_by = ops` |
| `paused_by_seller` | `active` | POST `/v1/seller/marketplace/promoted-listings/:id/resume` | Only if remaining in billing cycle and eligibility still holds | Emits `promoted_listing.resumed` (existing internal event; no customer webhook) |
| `paused_by_ops` | `active` | POST `/v1/ops/marketplace/promoted-listings/:id/resume` | Ops-initiated; anti-spam flag cleared | Ops-only |
| `active` | `daily_cap_exhausted` | Impression / EOI charge pushes `spend_to_date_cents` past `daily_cap_cents` | UTC-day boundary re-evaluates to active at 00:00 UTC | Transient; auto-recovers |
| `active` | `frequency_cap_exhausted` | All qualifying buyers within category are at `frequency_cap_config.max_impressions_per_buyer_per_category_per_rolling_window` | Rolling 7-day window | Transient; auto-recovers as the window rolls |
| `active` | `monthly_allotment_exhausted` | Billing-cycle month exceeded included + purchased top-up allotment | Billing cycle boundary | Transient to next billing anniversary |
| `active` | `category_cap_exhausted` | Category reached 3 concurrent active listings after a race-condition loss | Should be prevented by `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` in eligibility gate | Defensive state |
| `active` | `exhausted` | `active_until` reached OR full budget depleted with no renewal | Terminal | **Emits `promoted_listing.exhausted` webhook**; `ended_at` stamped |
| `active` | `expired` | `active_until` reached with remaining budget (no exhaustion) | Terminal | `ended_at` stamped |
| `paused_by_seller` | `cancelled` | POST `/v1/seller/marketplace/promoted-listings/:id/cancel` | Seller-initiated; pro-rata refund per §34.2 | Terminal; emits `promoted_listing.cancelled` (existing §34.16.7) |
| `active` | `terminated_eligibility_lost` | Runtime re-check (KB Health Score drop, vendor opt-out cascade, claim revocation) | Triggered by `vendor_opt_out_ref_id` population, `eligibility_kb_health_score_snapshot` runtime re-evaluation daily at 02:00 UTC, or `seller_software_id.claim_status` regression | Terminal; emits `promoted_listing.terminated` (existing internal event) |

**Quality floor enforcement.** The quality floor is checked at three points:
1. **Eligibility gate** at `draft → active` transition (§4.4.19 Eligibility Gate conditions 1–10).
2. **Daily runtime re-check** at 02:00 UTC (all `status = active` rows re-evaluated; failing rows transition to `terminated_eligibility_lost`).
3. **Bid-submission time** (per-auction check; failing sellers receive HTTP 403 `promoted_listing_quality_floor_failed`).

A seller whose Verification Tier regresses from `verified` → `basic` at runtime has their active Promoted Listings re-evaluated per the quality-floor runtime re-check within 30 minutes of the tier regression.

**k=5 anonymization surfaces.**

| Surface | k=5 Rule | Behavior Below Threshold |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Seller `PromotedListingAuctionDigest` (weekly) | ≥5 distinct bidders in category-week | Digest not emitted; PostHog event `promoted_listing_digest_anonymization_threshold_breach`; Ops-only webhook `marketplace_discovery.anonymization_threshold_breach` |
| Seller impression attribution | ≥5 distinct buyer Orgs in the cohort at attribution time | Impression recorded in `k_anon_failed_attribution_count`; not in `impression_count` |
| Public category-insight page (buyer-visible) | ≥5 distinct active Promoted Listings in category | Surface hidden; fall through to organic rendering |
| Ops-facing metric panels | No k=5 applied (Ops is authorized) | N/A — Ops sees raw metrics |

**Buyer opt-out (Hide Sponsored).** Buyer Console → Settings → Display Preferences → "Hide Sponsored" toggle. Semantics:

1. **Scope:** session-only by default; persisted toggle requires a buyer-console dialog acknowledging Sourcera's FTC disclosure obligation ("By hiding sponsored content across sessions, you acknowledge that you will not see paid placements. Sourcera will still label sponsored content in API responses and in any third-party integration you control"). Buyer may opt to persist via `BuyerDisplayPreferences.hide_sponsored_persistent = true`.
2. **Effect on ranking:** Promoted slots are suppressed from rendering but the underlying organic ranking is unchanged; promoted sellers are not boosted into organic on opt-out.
3. **Effect on search:** the `promoted` query parameter on buyer search endpoints is ignored when the buyer has opted out; server returns `X-Promoted-Suppressed: true` response header for observability.
4. **Effect on billing:** suppressed impressions are NOT billed to the seller (no `impression_count` increment, no `cleared_cpm_cents` charge).

**Failure modes (registered with §34.16.5 and extended here).**

1. **Seller creates a draft PromotedListing, then deletes the underlying SellerSoftware before activation.** Resolved: the `seller_software_id` FK is `ON DELETE RESTRICT`; deletion of SellerSoftware with any non-terminal PromotedListing row is blocked with `seller_software_delete_blocked_promoted_listing_active` (Appendix I, HTTP 409). Seller must cancel the draft first.
2. **Race: two sellers hit the 3-slot category cap simultaneously.** Resolved: eligibility gate uses `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the `(category_id, status)` partial index; the later transaction observes the cap full and transitions to `category_cap_exhausted` with `waitlist_position = 4`.
3. **Vendor opt-out cascade mid-flight.** Resolved: opt-out registry sweep (§27.10) evaluates every 15 minutes against active PromotedListings; a matching opt-out cascades `status → terminated_eligibility_lost` with `vendor_opt_out_ref_id` populated; pro-rata refund per §34.2; `promoted_listing.terminated` webhook fires.
4. **Frequency-cap bypass attempt (buyer uses multiple browser sessions).** Resolved: frequency cap keys on `buyer_org_id` (not `buyer_user_id`), which stable across sessions; cross-Org attempts (shell Orgs) are downstream Ops anti-fraud concern and surfaced via `marketplace_discovery.frequency_cap_bypass_suspected` (Ops-only webhook, Appendix C extension).
5. **Buyer opts out of sponsored mid-click-through.** Resolved: the impression was already attributed at render time; the subsequent opt-out does NOT retroactively reverse the impression charge. Opt-out is forward-looking only.
6. **Seller pauses, then marketplace domain admin reassigns the seller to a different marketplace domain.** Resolved: domain reassignment is governed by §43 and writes a `MarketplaceDomainTransferRecord` that cancels all active PromotedListings with pro-rata refund before the transfer commits; the seller must re-create listings in the new domain.
7. **Eligibility gate passes at submit, fails 3 hours later due to KB Health Score regression.** Resolved: the 02:00 UTC daily runtime re-check catches this; seller receives `tpl_promoted_eligibility_regression` notification with remediation checklist; listing status → `terminated_eligibility_lost`. No pro-rata refund for the window before termination (seller benefited from the impressions).

### 27.11.3 Verification Tiers {#27.11.3-verification-tiers}

**Product surface (buyer-facing).** Every SoftwarePage (§4.4.11), CategoryPage card (§4.4.12), EOI-eligible search result, and Bid Workspace seller reference renders the seller's **Verification Badge** in the upper-right of the seller-identity card. Badge states:

| Badge | Rendering | Semantics |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **None** (unverified) | No badge | Seller has not completed Basic verification |
| **Basic** | Grey shield icon; tooltip "Basic — Identity verified" | KYB + email verification passed |
| **Verified** | Blue shield icon with check; tooltip "Verified — Domain + business registration" | Domain ownership + business registration + ≥90d uptime history |
| **Certified** | Gold shield icon with medal; tooltip "Certified — Compliance audit passed" + sub-tag for audit class (SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / HIPAA / PCI) | Full compliance audit with named auditor; sub-tag identifies which audit(s) were validated |

The badge tooltip renders the effective `verification_tier.effective_at` and `expires_at` dates in the buyer's locale. Expired tiers display the last-known tier grayed out with a "Renewal in progress" flag for 30 days post-expiry; after 30 days the badge reverts to the next-lower tier (or None).

**Product surface (seller-facing).** Seller Console → Profile → Verification (role: `seller_org_owner` OR `seller_compliance_officer`). Shows:

1. Current tier with effective / expiry dates.
2. History log of past tiers (audit trail).
3. "Request higher tier" button (disabled if seller already at highest feasible tier OR anti-spam flag active).
4. Required-documents checklist for the requested tier (dynamically generated per tier — see below).
5. SLA clock showing "Sourcera will respond within N business days" (SLA = 3 business days Basic, 5 business days Verified, 15 business days Certified; §4.4.21).
6. Active review record status (`requested` → `in_review` → `additional_documents_requested` → `approved` / `denied`).

**Ops surface.** Ops Console → Marketplace → Verification Review Queue (role: `ops_verification_reviewer` OR `ops_compliance_reviewer`). Shows:

1. Review queue sorted by `submitted_at` ASC with SLA-breach highlighting (≤24h remaining = amber, ≤0h = red).
2. Per-record document viewer with audit-trail of reviewer comments.
3. Two-reviewer flow for `Certified` tier (separation of duties per §4.4.21).
4. Approve / Deny / Request-Additional-Documents action buttons.
5. Residency enforcement: reviewers are assigned only to records whose `data_residency_region` matches the reviewer's authorized-region roster (residency-locked reviewers, §4.4.21).

**Tier progression rules.**

| From | To | Trigger | Criteria (§4.4.21 detail) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| None | Basic | Seller requests; Ops auto-verifies via KYB + email OTP | Business tax ID present; email OTP confirmed |
| Basic | Verified | Seller requests; Ops reviews | Domain TXT record proof; business registration document ≤12 months old; ≥90d uptime history evidence |
| Verified | Certified | Seller requests; Ops reviews; **two-reviewer sign-off** | Signed audit report from named auditor (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA BAA, or PCI DSS Level 1/2); audit report ≤18 months old; no material exceptions |
| Any | Lower | Post-hoc audit revocation OR auto-downgrade at expiry | Audit finding, anti-spam flag, or `expires_at` passed without renewal |

**Recertification cadence.**

| Tier | Cadence | Pre-Notification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Basic | 12 months | 30d pre-expiry via `verification.recertification_due` webhook and in-app banner |
| Verified | 12 months | 30d pre-expiry same as Basic |
| Certified | Annual audit recertification required | 60d pre-expiry (longer because audits take time to schedule) |

Sellers who do not renew within the cadence window auto-downgrade; downgrade fires `verification.tier_revoked` with `revocation_reason_enum = expired_not_renewed`.

**Anti-gaming.** A seller who presents a Sourcera Verified badge on their own website and the audit evidence does not support the claim is flagged per §3.5 (anti-spam) and is downgraded to Basic or None with a `verification.tier_revoked` webhook with `revocation_reason_enum = false_badge_use`. Buyers who have viewed the affected seller in the prior 90 days are notified via `buyer_verification_revocation_alert` (Appendix C; user-visible; severity = `critical` per §31.5).

**Verification review outcome.** The VerificationReviewRecord reaches a terminal state on any of the following, each an Appendix J `verification_review_outcome` value (enum already exists; see §4.4.21 — no new values required for this release):

| Outcome | Semantics | Webhook Emitted |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `approved` | Review passed; tier elevated | `verification.review_approved` + `verification.review_completed` |
| `denied` | Review failed; tier not elevated | `verification.review_denied` + `verification.review_completed` |
| `withdrawn` | Seller cancelled the request before terminal | `verification.review_withdrawn` + `verification.review_completed` |
| `expired_unreviewed` | SLA breached and auto-expired (rare; Ops incident) | `verification.review_expired` + `verification.review_completed` |

The `verification.review_completed` event is a **terminal aggregate wrapper** — it fires alongside the specific outcome event with the same `event_id_correlation` field, for integrators that prefer a single-subscription terminal state. See §27.11.7 for schema.

**Cost to seller.** `$0`, always. See §34.16.2 for the policy rationale. The seller never sees a line item, invoice, or billing event tied to a VerificationReviewRecord.

**Ledger behavior.** VerificationReviewRecord lifecycle generates **zero** MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord rows (no `amount_cents = 0` persistence). The Sourcera cost of performing reviews (reviewer labor + `verification_fetch` operations) is captured on the platform P&L under COGS, not as a seller-facing revenue line. See §34.16.2 *Ledger* note.

### 27.11.4 Featured Placements {#27.11.4-featured-placements}

**Buyer surface.** Marketplace home, each CategoryPage, and the Buyer Workspace Phase-3 Vendor Curation surface render **at most one active Featured Placement per surface** at any time. The Featured card renders prominently (top-of-page; hero-sized card) with:

1. SellerSoftware hero image and name.
2. Editorial rationale — a 40–280 character human-written blurb authored by the Sourcera Marketing + Editorial team.
3. The "Featured" label (14px, `--color-ui-accent` token; non-suppressible).
4. A CTA link to the SoftwarePage.
5. In `paid_commitment` mode (feature-flag-gated — see below): the "Sponsored" label per FTC 16 CFR Part 255.5 replaces "Featured", and the editorial rationale is suffixed with "(paid placement)".

**Seller surface.** Sellers do NOT request Featured Placements; they are editorially selected. Seller Console → Marketplace Discovery → Featured Placements (read-only) shows:

1. Historical featured placements (if any).
2. Upcoming scheduled placement (if any).
3. Selection criteria (documented, not applications): Verification Tier ≥ Certified (preferred), KB Value Meter (§34.19) tier, buyer feedback signals, outcome-metric percentile, launch recency.
4. In `paid_commitment` mode: a "Request Paid Feature" option appears only if the seller's Org has `featured_placement_paid_mode_enabled = true`.

**Ops surface.** Ops Console → Marketplace → Featured Placements (role: `ops_marketplace_editor` + secondary sign-off from `ops_marketing_lead` for publication). The Editorial workflow:

1. Editor drafts a FeaturedPlacement row with `status = draft`; `mode = editorial` by default.
2. Editor populates `seller_org_id`, `category_id` (or `null` for home-page global), `start_at`, `end_at`, `editorial_rationale_text`, `editorial_rationale_links[]`.
3. Editor submits for sign-off; `ops_marketing_lead` reviews and either approves (→ `scheduled`) or rejects back to `draft`.
4. At `scheduled → activated` transition (T-48h pre-start), Ops has a final commit window to review; activation locks the card content.
5. At `activated → live` transition (cron at `start_at`), the card renders; `featured_placement.published` webhook fires.
6. At `live → ended` transition (cron at `end_at`), the card unrenders; `featured_placement.expired` webhook fires.
7. Cancellation at any pre-terminal state fires `featured_placement.cancelled` with `cancellation_reason_enum`.

**Lifecycle state machine.** FeaturedPlacement status transitions (enum `featured_placement_status` registered in Appendix J per §4.4.20 — no new values required).

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| — | `draft` | POST `/v1/ops/marketplace/featured-placements` | Ops `ops_marketplace_editor` role | No webhook |
| `draft` | `scheduled` | POST `/v1/ops/marketplace/featured-placements/:id/schedule` | Two-role sign-off (`ops_marketplace_editor` + `ops_marketing_lead`); seller `verification_tier ≥ basic`; seller not anti-spam flagged | Emits `featured_placement.scheduled` (existing §34.16.7) |
| `scheduled` | `activated` | Cron T-48h pre-`start_at` | Still valid; seller still eligible | **Emits `featured_placement.activated` webhook (new in §27.11)** |
| `activated` | `live` | Cron at `start_at` | Seller quality floor still passes | Emits `featured_placement.published` (existing §34.16.7) |
| `live` | `ended` | Cron at `end_at` | Natural terminus | Emits `featured_placement.ended` (existing §34.16.7) AND **`featured_placement.expired` (new in §27.11)** — both are emitted for backward compatibility; see §27.11.7 alias note |
| `live` | `cancelled` | POST `/v1/ops/marketplace/featured-placements/:id/cancel` | Editorial pull (seller regression, policy violation, editorial change of direction); justification ≥ 40 chars | Emits `featured_placement.cancelled` (existing §34.16.7) |
| `scheduled` | `cancelled` | Same as above | Same | Same |
| `activated` | `cancelled` | Same as above | Same | Same |
| `ended` | `archived` | Cron T+90d post-`end_at` | Terminal retention transition | Internal; no webhook |

**Editorial selection criteria** (non-binding guidance; documented for transparency to sellers).

1. **Verification Tier ≥ Certified** (preferred; `verified` acceptable for smaller categories with no Certified candidates).
2. **KB Value Meter tier ≥ tier-2** per §34.19 (seller has actively contributed to marketplace KB quality signals).
3. **Outcome metrics above category median** (e.g., Workspace-acceptance rate, NPS signal).
4. **Buyer feedback signal non-negative** (≥4.2 average across recent Bid Workspace ratings).
5. **Launch recency bonus** (a seller who launched a significant new capability within the last 60 days is prioritized for home-page Featured to surface novelty).
6. **Cadence constraint.** A single seller MAY hold **at most 2 Featured Placements per 12-month rolling window** across all surfaces, to prevent over-saturation.

**Paid commitment mode (feature-flag-gated; reserved).**

Per §34.16.3, `FeaturedPlacement.mode = paid_commitment` is reserved behind `featured_placement_paid_mode_enabled = false` per-Org feature flag. Enablement requires VP Marketing + VP Finance + VP Legal sign-off AND an ethical-review gate. Until enablement:

- POST requests with `mode = paid_commitment` and the flag disabled are rejected with `featured_placement_paid_mode_not_enabled` (Appendix I, HTTP 403; existing).
- No Seller Console UI surfaces paid-commitment options (the "Request Paid Feature" control is flag-gated off).
- No MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord row is created (the flag gate precedes revenue attribution).

When (and only when) paid mode is enabled for an Org:

1. The seller may submit a paid-commitment request via POST `/v1/seller/marketplace/featured-placements/requests` (new endpoint; §27.11.7).
2. Ops reviews the request editorially; approval writes a FeaturedPlacement row with `mode = paid_commitment` and triggers invoicing per §34.16.3.
3. The buyer-facing card renders "Sponsored" instead of "Featured" per FTC 16 CFR Part 255.5.
4. A hard cap of **1 paid commitment per category per month** applies.
5. The paid placement does NOT bias Sourcera's outcome-data surfaces (KB Value Meter, Workspace acceptance metrics); the ethical-review gate at flag enablement asserts this.

**Authored Extension — Deferred.** Paid-commitment mode enablement workflow, the VP sign-off modal, and the ethical-review gate form are tracked in `/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions → §27.11.4 FeaturedPlacement.paid_commitment enablement workflow`.

### 27.11.5 Accounting Isolation {#27.11.5-accounting-isolation}

**Authority.** §4.8.12 MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord is the append-only ledger of record for all marketplace-discovery revenue. §34.16 is authoritative for billing semantics. §4.8.3 Billing Ledger is the unified cross-stream ledger carrying `revenue_stream_class`. §27.11 does not introduce new ledger semantics; it restates and enforces the isolation boundary.

**Cost-center isolation invariants.** All MUST hold; breach is a deploy-time validator failure.

1. Every MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord row has `cost_center = rev_marketplace_discovery`. Enforced by DB CHECK `marketplace_discovery_revenue_record_cost_center_check` (see §4.8.12).
2. No AIOperation (§4.5 family) writes a MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord row. Enforced by the DB trigger `ai_operation_to_marketplace_discovery_revenue_record_rejected`.
3. No subscription invoice line item is attributed to `rev_marketplace_discovery`. Enforced by the Stripe webhook ingest validator `stripe_invoice_line_item_revenue_stream_classifier`.
4. The MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord append-only constraint prohibits updates post-invoice; corrections are made via new compensating rows with `reversal_of_record_id`.
5. Deploy-time validator `revenue_stream_firewall` (§34.16.8 AC #1) re-asserts the three-stream separation every release.

**Non-revenue events.**

| Event | Revenue Recorded? | Rationale |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| PromotedListing `draft`, `paused`, `terminated_eligibility_lost`, `expired` (no charge) | **No** | No clearing price cleared |
| VerificationReviewRecord any state | **No** | $0 to seller per policy |
| FeaturedPlacement `mode = editorial` any state | **No** | Editorial placement; no revenue |
| FeaturedPlacement `mode = paid_commitment` in `scheduled` / `activated` (pre-invoicing) | **No** | Revenue recorded at invoice-issue time per §34.16.3 |
| MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord `pending` with k<5 awaiting cohort saturation | **Deferred** | Row exists; invoice issuance deferred until k=5 floor met or `pending_timeout_at` elapses per §4.8.12 |

**k=5 revenue deferral semantics.** Promoted Listing clearing prices in a category-week with <5 distinct bidders are held in `MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord.state = pending` with `pending_reason = anonymization_threshold_not_met`. If k=5 is reached by `pending_timeout_at` (default 30 days per §4.8.12), the row advances to `invoiced`. Otherwise the row is `voided` with `voided_reason = anonymization_threshold_timeout_elapsed` and the seller is NOT billed; impressions attributed to that listing remain but do not contribute revenue. This is intentional — preserving bidder anonymity is worth the revenue loss.

**DSAR compatibility.** On a DSAR right-to-erasure request, the MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord rows tied to the requester are **NOT deleted** under the §6.8.5 row #4 cost-center / FTC retained-row class. The `published_by_user_id` / `created_by` / `updated_by` fields are pseudonymized (replaced with a stable pseudonym `dsar_pseudonym_<hash>` matching §6.8 policy). The financial body of the record — amounts, cost center, auction clearing prices — is retained for the full 7-year §40.2 retention window. This is disclosed in the DSAR response artifact.

**Residency.** Every MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord row inherits `data_residency_region` from the Origin Seller Org. Cross-region movement is prohibited. Ledger queries spanning regions return region-partitioned results only; no single query result contains rows from multiple regions.

**Legal-entity partitioning.** Per §4.8.12, MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord rows are partitioned by the Seller Org's `legal_entity_id` (EU-residency sellers are partitioned into the EU legal entity; US into the US legal entity; etc.). The month-end close job runs partitioned and emits partitioned financial summaries for audit.

### 27.11.6 Buyer Experience Guardrails {#27.11.6-buyer-experience-guardrails}

Buyer trust is the binding constraint on all marketplace-discovery monetization. The following guardrails are mandatory; violations are platform-critical bugs.

**G1. FTC 16 CFR Part 255.5 disclosure.** Every paid surface (Promoted, paid Featured) renders a disclosure label visible to the naked eye on desktop and mobile at default zoom. Label text is tokenized (not hard-coded) and stored in the DB (`ftc_disclosure_label` on PromotedListing and `paid_mode_label` on FeaturedPlacement). Tokens: `"Promoted"` for Promoted Listings, `"Sponsored"` for paid Featured Placements. Label is rendered server-side to resist client-side removal via ad-blockers (which would then defeat FTC compliance). Accessibility: `aria-label="Paid placement disclosure"` and readable by screen readers.

**G2. Ranking integrity.** The organic ranking algorithm does NOT consume PromotedListing bid amounts, clearing prices, or spend totals. The `promoted_listing_features` source in the ranking model is explicitly empty. A model-card invariant `ranking_model_no_promoted_features` is asserted on every model deploy; violation blocks the deploy.

**G3. Paid-from-organic visual separation.** Promoted slots render with a 1px divider below the Promoted group. Featured placements render in a distinct hero card above the fold. Buyer clicks on Promoted vs. Organic are tagged distinctly in PostHog (`marketplace_promoted_clicked` vs. `marketplace_organic_clicked`) for buyer-side post-hoc attribution.

**G4. Buyer opt-out persistence rules.** Per §27.11.2, "Hide Sponsored" is session-only by default to preserve Sourcera's ongoing disclosure obligation. Persistent opt-out requires an explicit ack dialog; persisted opt-outs are surfaced in the buyer's Account Settings for easy reversal.

**G5. k=5 anonymization enforcement.** Every aggregated metric surfaced to sellers passes the §27.11.2 k=5 table. Ops surfaces are exempt (Ops is authorized). Public surfaces are NEVER exempt.

**G6. No third-party ad-network sharing.** Sourcera does not sell, share, or syndicate buyer click-stream or EOI-acceptance data to third-party ad networks. The data is `sourcera_owned` (§4.7.1 data-classification) for platform analytics only. A deploy-time lint `data_exfiltration_to_third_party_ad_network` scans for any outbound data flow to external ad-network domains and blocks the deploy.

**G7. Quality floor precedes visibility.** No paid surface renders for a seller who fails the applicable marketplace-discovery quality floor. For Promoted Listings, the canonical floor is the full §4.4.19 Eligibility Gate (plan-tier eligibility, claim verification, published/pending SoftwarePage, KB Health floor, closed-bid snapshot, active category, category cap, monthly allotment/top-up limits, and Vendor Opt-Out coverage) plus the anti-spam checks in this section. Failing Promoted attempts are rejected with `promoted_listing_quality_floor_failed` (existing; HTTP 403); for Featured, the editorial selection process self-excludes ineligible sellers.

**G8. No dark patterns.** Cancellation flows for Promoted Listings, Featured Placements, and Verification Review requests do NOT employ dark patterns (hidden cancel buttons, misleading retention offers, confusion pricing). Every cancel action is a single-click primary CTA with one confirmation modal. UX review gates this per the UX tokens and patterns corpus.

**G9. Residency-locked rendering.** A Buyer in the EU residency region renders only marketplace-discovery content from EU-region-authorized sellers. Cross-region rendering is blocked at the CategoryPage composition step. A deploy-time integration test `residency_cross_render_blocked` asserts.

**G10. Marketplace-domain firewall.** A Buyer in marketplace-domain `us-civilian-enterprise` renders only Promoted / Featured content from sellers authorized in that marketplace-domain. A Seller Org's Promoted Listing in `us-defense-contractor` is invisible to civilian buyers even on identical category IDs. A §43 cross-domain leakage test asserts.

### 27.11.7 API Endpoints {#27.11.7-api-endpoints}

All endpoints follow §32 conventions: cursor-based pagination (default 50, max 250); `Idempotency-Key` header required on all POST endpoints; HTTP 401 on missing/invalid auth; HTTP 403 on authorized-but-forbidden; HTTP 404 on cross-console access attempts per §7.2 Dual-Console Firewall (never HTTP 403 — 403 would leak existence). Rate-limit classes per §32.4.5: `marketplace_read = 300/min/Org`, `marketplace_write = 60/min/Org`, `ops_marketplace_admin = 120/min/Ops-user`.

**Authorization matrix.**

| Endpoint Family | Seller Console | Buyer Console | Ops Console |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `/v1/seller/marketplace/promoted-listings/*` | Yes (`seller_billing_admin` OR `seller_marketing_editor`) | 404 | Read-only |
| `/v1/seller/marketplace/verification/*` | Yes (`seller_org_owner` OR `seller_compliance_officer`) | 404 | Read-only |
| `/v1/seller/marketplace/featured-placements/requests` (paid mode only) | Yes (`seller_billing_admin`) when flag on | 404 | Read-only |
| `/v1/buyer/marketplace/*` | 404 | Yes (any authenticated buyer) | Read-only |
| `/v1/ops/marketplace/*` | 404 | 404 | Yes (role-gated per subpath) |

| `promoted_listing.paused` | Transition to `paused_by_seller` OR `paused_by_ops` | `{event_id, event_type, occurred_at, promoted_listing_id, org_id, paused_by: "seller"\|"ops", paused_at, pause_reason_enum, pause_reason_text, auto_resume_at}` | Yes (seller Org); Ops-visible on `ops` origin | New |
| `promoted_listing.exhausted` | Transition to `exhausted` (any exhaustion cause) | `{event_id, event_type, occurred_at, promoted_listing_id, org_id, exhaustion_cause_enum: "daily_cap" \| "monthly_allotment" \| "frequency_cap" \| "budget_depleted", exhausted_at, ended_at, final_spend_cents, final_impression_count, final_eoi_count}` | Yes (seller Org) | New |
| `verification.review_completed` | Transition to any terminal state (`approved`, `denied`, `withdrawn`, `expired_unreviewed`) | `{event_id, event_type, occurred_at, verification_review_record_id, org_id, tier_requested, outcome_enum, outcome_detail_text, correlated_event_id}` | Yes (requester Org) | New terminal aggregate wrapper; fires **alongside** the specific outcome event (`.review_approved`, `.review_denied`, `.review_withdrawn`, `.review_expired`) with `correlated_event_id` linking to the specific-outcome event's `event_id` for integrators who want a single subscription for terminal state |
| `featured_placement.activated` | Transition `scheduled → activated` at T-48h pre-start | `{event_id, event_type, occurred_at, featured_placement_id, seller_org_id, category_id, start_at, end_at, mode, activated_at}` | Yes (featured seller) | New — distinct from `.scheduled` (editorial intent) and `.published` (live render); activation is the T-48h lock-in confirming the placement will go live |
| `featured_placement.expired` | Transition `live → ended` at `end_at` cron | `{event_id, event_type, occurred_at, featured_placement_id, seller_org_id, category_id, expired_at, impressions_count, clicks_count}` | Yes (featured seller) | New; fires **alongside** existing `featured_placement.ended` with identical `event_id_correlation`. `.expired` is the §27.11.7 canonical name; `.ended` is retained for backward compatibility. Subscribers SHOULD migrate to `.expired` by v8; `.ended` will be deprecated in v8 and removed in v9 per `/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Deprecations → §34.16.7 featured_placement.ended` |

**Error-code additions for §27.11 endpoints** (registered in Appendix I per `/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Error Code Additions`).
