### 27.11.8 Acceptance Criteria {#27.11.8-acceptance-criteria}

Each criterion is observable, measurable, and scope-bound. Tests named below are QA invariants registered in the §48 QA catalog.

1. **Cost-center isolation.** Every MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord row has `cost_center = rev_marketplace_discovery`; zero cross-stream attribution to `rev_ai_wallet` or `rev_subscription`; deploy-time validator `revenue_stream_firewall` asserts (§34.16.8 AC #1; restated).
2. **Dual-Console Firewall — Promoted.** A buyer-console session GET to `/v1/seller/marketplace/promoted-listings/:id` returns HTTP 404 with `error_code = cross_console_access`; no bid, spend, clearing-price, or cap fields appear in any buyer-facing response; QA test `promoted_listing_dual_console_firewall` asserts.
3. **Scrubbed buyer projection.** `/v1/buyer/marketplace/categories/:id/promoted-slots` response body contains ONLY the fields in §27.11.7 (`seller_software_id`, `seller_software_name`, `seller_software_hero_image_url`, `ftc_disclosure_label`, `placement_rank`, `placement_surface`); QA test `promoted_listing_buyer_projection_scrubbed` asserts.
4. **FTC labeling.** Every rendered Promoted slot on desktop + mobile at default zoom displays the "Promoted" label; accessibility test asserts `aria-label` present; QA test `ftc_labeling_promoted_slot_desktop_mobile_a11y` asserts.
5. **Paid Featured labeling.** When `FeaturedPlacement.mode = paid_commitment` (in any Org where the flag is enabled), the rendered card displays "Sponsored" not "Featured" and suffixes the editorial rationale with "(paid placement)"; QA test `featured_placement_paid_mode_labeling` asserts.
6. **Paid Featured flag gate.** POST `/v1/seller/marketplace/featured-placements/requests` with the flag disabled returns HTTP 403 `featured_placement_paid_mode_not_enabled`; QA test `featured_placement_paid_mode_flag_gate` asserts.
7. **Quality floor enforcement — Promoted.** A seller that fails any §4.4.19 Eligibility Gate condition or marketplace-discovery anti-spam check cannot transition a PromotedListing `draft → active`; returns HTTP 403 `promoted_listing_quality_floor_failed`; QA test `promoted_listing_quality_floor_enforcement` asserts.
8. **Quality floor runtime re-check.** The 02:00 UTC cron re-evaluates all `status = active` PromotedListings against the quality-floor gate; failing rows transition to `terminated_eligibility_lost` within 30 minutes; emits `promoted_listing.terminated`; QA test `promoted_listing_runtime_quality_floor_recheck` asserts.
9. **k=5 anonymization — auction digest.** `PromotedListingAuctionDigest` weekly emission fires ONLY if `distinct_bidders_count ≥ 5`; below threshold, the digest is suppressed and `marketplace_discovery.anonymization_threshold_breach` (Ops-only) fires; QA test `promoted_listing_k5_auction_digest` asserts.
10. **k=5 anonymization — impression attribution.** Impressions in cohorts <5 distinct buyer Orgs are recorded in `k_anon_failed_attribution_count` and not in `impression_count`; billing is NOT applied to below-threshold impressions; QA test `promoted_listing_k5_impression_attribution` asserts.
11. **k=5 revenue deferral.** MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord rows for promoted wins in categories with <5 distinct bidders enter `state = pending` with `pending_reason = anonymization_threshold_not_met`; advance to `invoiced` if k=5 reached by `pending_timeout_at`, else void with `voided_reason = anonymization_threshold_timeout_elapsed`; QA test `promoted_listing_k5_revenue_deferral` asserts.
12. **Buyer Hide-Sponsored — session default.** The "Hide Sponsored" toggle defaults to session-only; persisted opt-out requires explicit modal acknowledgment; QA test `buyer_hide_sponsored_persistence_requires_ack` asserts.
13. **Buyer Hide-Sponsored — billing behavior.** Impressions suppressed by Hide-Sponsored do NOT increment `impression_count` and do NOT trigger `cleared_cpm_cents` charges; QA test `buyer_hide_sponsored_no_bill` asserts.
14. **Ranking integrity.** The ranking model's feature set contains no fields derived from PromotedListing bid amounts, clearing prices, or spend totals; model-card invariant `ranking_model_no_promoted_features` asserts on every model deploy.
15. **Verification — $0 to seller always.** No VerificationReviewRecord lifecycle transition creates a MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord row OR a BillingLedger entry with seller as counterparty; QA test `verification_zero_revenue` asserts (matches §34.16.8 AC #5).
16. **Verification — separation of duties for Certified.** A `verification_review_record.tier_requested = certified` MUST receive `approved` or `denied` action by two distinct Ops users (`reviewer_user_id` ≠ `secondary_reviewer_user_id`); same-user sign-off rejected with `verification_two_reviewer_required`; QA test `verification_certified_dual_reviewer` asserts.
17. **Verification — residency-locked reviewers.** A VerificationReviewRecord with `data_residency_region = eu` is assignable only to Ops reviewers in the `eu_authorized_reviewer_roster`; cross-region assignment rejected; QA test `verification_reviewer_residency_lock` asserts.
18. **Verification — recertification pre-notification.** `verification.recertification_due` webhook fires at T-30d for Basic/Verified and T-60d for Certified; QA test `verification_recertification_prenotification_cadence` asserts.
19. **Verification — auto-downgrade at expiry.** A VerificationReviewRecord with `expires_at < now` and no renewal request on file auto-downgrades tier; `verification.tier_revoked` fires with `revocation_reason_enum = expired_not_renewed`; QA test `verification_expiry_auto_downgrade` asserts.
20. **Verification — false-badge anti-gaming.** External observation that a seller displays a Sourcera verification badge inconsistent with their actual tier flags anti-spam and fires `verification.tier_revoked` with `revocation_reason_enum = false_badge_use`; buyer notification fires for buyers who viewed the seller in the prior 90 days; QA test `verification_false_badge_revocation_notification` asserts.
21. **Featured Placement — editorial default.** A newly created FeaturedPlacement without explicit `mode` override defaults to `editorial`; creates zero revenue rows; QA test `featured_placement_editorial_default` asserts.
22. **Featured Placement — activation webhook.** At T-48h pre-`start_at`, transition `scheduled → activated` fires `featured_placement.activated` webhook; QA test `featured_placement_activation_webhook` asserts.
23. **Featured Placement — dual webhook on expiry.** At `end_at` cron, transition `live → ended` fires BOTH `featured_placement.ended` AND `featured_placement.expired` with shared `event_id_correlation`; QA test `featured_placement_dual_expiry_webhook` asserts.
24. **Featured Placement — seller cadence cap.** A seller who has held 2 Featured Placements in the prior 12 months cannot be scheduled for a third; `featured_placement_seller_cadence_exceeded` (HTTP 409); QA test `featured_placement_seller_cadence_cap` asserts.
25. **Featured Placement — two-role sign-off.** A `draft → scheduled` transition requires both `ops_marketplace_editor` AND `ops_marketing_lead` sign-off; single-role attempt rejected; QA test `featured_placement_two_role_signoff` asserts.
26. **Marketplace-domain firewall.** Buyers in `marketplace_domain = us-civilian-enterprise` do NOT see Promoted or Featured content from `us-defense-contractor`-authorized sellers even on identical category IDs; QA test `marketplace_domain_cross_render_blocked` asserts.
27. **Residency firewall.** EU-residency buyers do NOT see marketplace-discovery content from non-EU-authorized sellers; cross-region rendering is blocked at CategoryPage composition; QA test `residency_cross_render_blocked` asserts.
28. **Webhook conformance — §27.11-added events.** `promoted_listing.created`, `promoted_listing.paused`, `promoted_listing.exhausted`, `verification.review_completed`, `featured_placement.activated`, `featured_placement.expired` all follow §31 patterns (HMAC-SHA256, idempotency_key = event_id, exponential backoff, DLQ after 5, ≤256 KB payload); PostHog parallel transliteration asserted (§31.8 AC #16); webhook conformance test `marketplace_discovery_27_11_webhook_conformance` asserts.
29. **Webhook dual-emission — terminal aggregate.** `verification.review_completed` fires exactly once per terminal VerificationReviewRecord transition AND is accompanied by exactly one outcome-specific event (`review_approved` | `review_denied` | `review_withdrawn` | `review_expired`) sharing `correlated_event_id`; QA test `verification_review_completed_dual_emission` asserts.
30. **Webhook idempotency and audience privacy — settlement no-duplicates.** `promoted_listing.auction_settled` and `promoted_listing.auction_lost` fire at most once per `(auction_id, recipient_org_id, event_type)` tuple even under settlement-job retry; every participating bidder Org receives exactly one terminal outcome event; loser payloads include no winner identity, winner paid amount, or winner-owned `promoted_listing_id`; QA tests `promoted_listing_settlement_idempotency` and `promoted_listing_auction_webhook_audience_privacy` assert (re-states §34.16.7 invariant; scoped here for §27.11 adherence).
31. **Rate-limit enforcement.** `marketplace_read` = 300/min/Org, `marketplace_write` = 60/min/Org, `ops_marketplace_admin` = 120/min/Ops-user; rate-limit exhaustion returns HTTP 429 with `Retry-After` header; QA test `marketplace_rate_limit_classes` asserts.
32. **Cursor pagination defaults.** All GET list endpoints default `page_size = 50`, max `page_size = 250`; cursor is opaque; reverse iteration supported; QA test `marketplace_cursor_pagination_defaults` asserts.
33. **Idempotency-Key on POST.** All POST endpoints accept `Idempotency-Key`; replay of the same key within 24h returns the original response with `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`; QA test `marketplace_idempotency_key_replay` asserts.
34. **DSAR compatibility.** On DSAR right-to-erasure, PromotedListing / FeaturedPlacement / VerificationReviewRecord / MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord rows have `created_by` / `updated_by` / `published_by_user_id` / `reviewer_user_id` / `submitted_by_user_id` pseudonymized while financial bodies are retained per §45.1; QA test `marketplace_dsar_pseudonymization_retention` asserts.
35. **7-year retention.** PromotedListing (financial), FeaturedPlacement (financial + editorial audit), VerificationReviewRecord (platform-integrity), MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord (financial) all retain for 7 years per §40.2; retention sweeper `marketplace_discovery_7y_retention_sweep` asserts.
36. **No third-party ad-network data sharing.** Buyer click-stream, EOI-acceptance data, and promoted-surface interaction data are not transmitted to any non-Sourcera domain; deploy-time lint `data_exfiltration_to_third_party_ad_network` asserts.
37. **Mobile parity.** Every Promoted and Featured surface renders correctly at 360px viewport width; FTC labels remain visible at default zoom; QA test `marketplace_mobile_parity_360px` asserts.
38. **Concurrent activation race.** Oversubscribed concurrent activation against the §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_category_slot_cap` results in successes equal to the cap and the first loser receiving `category_cap_exhausted` with the next waitlist position; QA test `promoted_listing_concurrent_activation_race` asserts.
39. **Third-party dependency outage — WorkOS.** If WorkOS is unavailable, POST `/v1/seller/marketplace/promoted-listings` returns HTTP 503 with `Retry-After`; no partial draft is persisted; QA test `marketplace_workos_outage_graceful` asserts.
40. **Third-party dependency outage — Stripe.** If Stripe ingest is delayed, `promoted_listing.paid` / `promoted_listing.unpaid` webhooks are deferred; PromotedListing `status` remains in `active` with `payment_status = pending`; QA test `marketplace_stripe_delay_graceful` asserts (re-states §34.16 invariant).

### 27.11.9 Self-Challenge and Counterfactual Register {#27.11.9-self-challenge-and-counterfactual-register}

Per project instructions #16 (Self-challenge pass) and #17 (Counterfactual pass), the following edge cases were considered during authoring and their handling is confirmed in §27.11.1–§27.11.8. Unresolved items are flagged as **Authored Extensions — deferred** and registered in `/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md`.

**27.11.9.1 Source conflict: Summary §6.16.6 (paid Verification; paid Featured commitments) vs. Summary §2.10 / C.131 / Seller Pricing §12 / Master Spec §34.16 (free Verification; editorial-only Featured).** Resolved: §27.11 aligns with the majority source set (Summary §2.10 + C.131 + SPS §12 + existing Master Spec §34.16) which is also the framing that protects buyer trust. Paid modes are reserved behind `featured_placement_paid_mode_enabled` feature flag with VP sign-off gates; no paid Verification tier exists in the product. Documented in `/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Conflicts Resolved → §27.11 Pricing Model Source Conflict`.

**27.11.9.2 Webhook name collision: `featured_placement.expired` (new in §27.11) vs. `featured_placement.ended` (existing in §34.16.7).** Resolved: both emit at the same terminal transition with shared `event_id_correlation` for backward compatibility. `.expired` is the §27.11 canonical name; `.ended` is deprecated in v8 and removed in v9 per `/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Deprecations`. Subscribers SHOULD migrate to `.expired`.

**27.11.9.3 Webhook name collision: `verification.review_completed` (new in §27.11) vs. `verification.review_approved` / `.review_denied` (existing in §34.16.7).** Resolved: `.review_completed` is an additive terminal aggregate wrapper that fires alongside the specific-outcome event. Integrators who want a single subscription for "terminal reached, whichever way" subscribe to `.review_completed`; integrators who want outcome-specific handling subscribe to the specific events. Both coexist permanently.

**27.11.9.4 First-time seller with no closed Bid Workspace in prior 90 days.** The §4.4.19 eligibility gate #5 requires ≥1 closed Bid Workspace in the prior 90 days. A brand-new seller who has not yet participated in any Bid Workspaces cannot activate Promoted Listings. Mitigation: the eligibility-preview UI explicitly surfaces this gate with remediation text ("Complete at least one bid to be eligible for Promoted Listings"). Sellers are directed to EOI-inbound leads or cold-outreach bid participation to satisfy the gate. This is intentional — Promoted should not be a new-seller discovery channel, only an established-seller amplification channel.

**27.11.9.5 Concurrency: two sellers submitting bids for the same category within milliseconds of Monday 00:00 UTC.** Resolved: bid-window close is enforced at the DB level by a `bid_window_closed_at` timestamp column; submissions after `close_timestamp` are rejected with `promoted_listing_auction_closed` (existing §34.16.7; HTTP 409). The auction-settlement job runs at 03:00 UTC (3 hours after close) with exclusive lock on `auction_id`; no race against late submissions.

**27.11.9.6 Idempotency: seller retries a POST `/v1/seller/marketplace/promoted-listings` with the same `Idempotency-Key` after a network timeout.** Resolved: §32 Idempotency-Key replay returns the original 201 response with `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`; no duplicate PromotedListing is created.

**27.11.9.7 Notification failure: `verification.review_approved` webhook delivery fails 5 times.** Resolved: §31 DLQ after 5 failures; webhook enters DLQ with ops-visible alert `webhook_dlq_marketplace_discovery_domain`. The underlying VerificationReviewRecord `status = approved` is unchanged — the webhook is a notification, not the source of truth. Ops manually replays DLQ items after consumer-side fix.

**27.11.9.8 Third-party outage: Firecrawl unavailable during Verification `verified` tier review (domain TXT proof fetch fails).** Resolved: the reviewer pauses the review with `status = additional_documents_requested` and a reviewer note referring to the Firecrawl outage; the seller's SLA clock is paused. When Firecrawl recovers, the review resumes. Ops-status-page banner during outage.

**27.11.9.9 Mobile: Promoted slot on 320px viewport may truncate the FTC label.** Resolved: the label is always rendered; text-truncation is prohibited via CSS `white-space: nowrap; overflow: visible`; on <360px the category hero card uses a stacked layout with the label on its own line. QA test asserts the label is visible at 320px.

**27.11.9.10 Admin vs. end-user: a seller_org_owner pauses a PromotedListing their seller_billing_admin created.** Resolved: both roles have pause authority (§4.4.10 authorization matrix). The `updated_by` field captures the pausing user. `pause_reason_enum = manual_by_org_owner` distinguishes from `manual_by_billing_admin`.

**27.11.9.11 Guest role: a buyer-console guest (read-only buyer) attempts to POST `/v1/buyer/settings/display-preferences`.** Resolved: guest roles are gated from settings mutations per §4.4.10; HTTP 403 with `role_insufficient_for_settings_mutation`.

**27.11.9.12 Cross-domain leakage: a seller authorized in both `us-civilian-enterprise` and `us-defense-contractor` books a Promoted Listing; which marketplace-domain renders it?** Resolved: PromotedListing carries a `marketplace_domain_id` FK (per §43); the render-time composition filters against the buyer's `marketplace_domain_id`. Sellers operating in multiple domains must create separate PromotedListings per domain. Authored Extension — if `marketplace_domain_id` is not yet a column on §4.4.19, add in a subsequent phase. Flagged.

**27.11.9.13 Data residency: EU-residency seller wins a promoted auction in a US-buyer-only category.** Resolved: category-to-residency mapping is enforced by the CategoryPage residency rules (§4.4.12); categories that are residency-scoped exclude cross-residency bidders at eligibility-gate time. The EU seller's bid is rejected with `promoted_listing_category_residency_mismatch` (Appendix I extension). Authored Extension — confirm with Legal that residency-scoped categories are within regulatory scope.

**27.11.9.14 Timezone / locale: seller in Tokyo wants to see bid window in JST, not UTC.** Resolved: the Seller Console renders the bid window in the seller's timezone with a UTC-equivalent tooltip. All backend timestamps remain UTC. i18n test asserts the window is displayed correctly for common timezones.

**27.11.9.15 Currency formatting: EU seller wants to see clearing prices in EUR.** Resolved: cleared prices are stored in USD per §34.16; the Seller Console offers a display-currency setting that converts at current-day Stripe FX rate for display only. Billing remains USD. i18n test asserts correct display.

**27.11.9.16 Downgrade: seller on Seller Enterprise downgrades to Seller Starter mid-month with active PromotedListings.** Resolved: active PromotedListings on the downgrading Org continue to run through the end of the current billing cycle (no immediate termination); no new PromotedListings can be created once the downgrade takes effect. The cycle-end cron transitions active rows to `terminated_eligibility_lost` with `eligibility_check_failed_reason = plan_tier_below_scale`. Seller is notified at downgrade commit.

**27.11.9.17 Right-to-erasure: a seller Org requests DSAR erasure that would remove the seller_billing_admin user.** Resolved: §6.8 DSAR process pseudonymizes the user on the `created_by` / `updated_by` fields; the user's identity is replaced with `dsar_pseudonym_<hash>`. The PromotedListing, FeaturedPlacement, VerificationReviewRecord, and MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord rows themselves are retained per their §40.2 rows and applicable §6.8.5 retained-row classes. Documented in §27.11.5.

**27.11.9.18 Seller Scale plan does not include Promoted Listings (future change).** Authored Extension — deferred. If a future pricing change moves Promoted out of Seller Scale into Seller Enterprise only, the eligibility gate #1 updates accordingly; existing active listings grandfathered through cycle end. Flagged in RECONCILIATION.md.

**27.11.9.19 Ad-network bypass attempt: a seller tries to insert a paid placement via a third-party ad network that redirects to their SoftwarePage.** Resolved: Sourcera does not integrate with third-party ad networks (§27.11.6 G6). Any attempt to spoof placement via external redirects is detected by the CategoryPage composition step (external referrers are ranked by organic rank, not promoted). No revenue attribution is made. Anti-spam flag may be raised if the behavior is systematic.

**27.11.9.20 A seller whose Verification tier is revoked keeps their Featured Placement slot live.** Resolved: the `featured_placement.activated` and ongoing `live` state both re-check Verification tier at scheduled times (T-48h and daily 02:00 UTC runtime re-check). If tier drops below selection criteria, Ops reviews for `featured_placement.cancelled` with `cancellation_reason_enum = seller_tier_regression`. Authored Extension — runtime re-check on Featured is not yet specified in §4.4.20; add in a subsequent phase. Flagged.

### 27.11.10 Authored Extensions {#27.11.10-authored-extensions}

Items flagged in §27.11.9 and throughout §27.11 that are **Authored Extensions requiring human sign-off**, consolidated here and registered in `/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions → §27.11`:

1. **FeaturedPlacement.paid_commitment enablement workflow** (§27.11.4). Needs: VP Marketing + VP Finance + VP Legal sign-off modal; ethical-review gate form; paid-retainer pricing structure. Owner: Marketing + Finance + Legal.
2. **`marketplace_domain_id` FK on PromotedListing** (§27.11.9.12). Needs: column addition to §4.4.19 (or confirmation that the implicit inheritance from `org_id → marketplace_domain_id` is sufficient). Owner: Engineering + Platform architecture.
3. **Residency-scoped category enforcement** (§27.11.9.13). Needs: Legal sign-off on residency-scoping semantics; confirmation that §4.4.12 CategoryPage residency rules are authoritative. Owner: Legal + Engineering.
4. **FeaturedPlacement runtime Verification re-check** (§27.11.9.20). Needs: authoring of a daily 02:00 UTC cron on §4.4.20 analogous to the PromotedListing quality-floor re-check; tier-regression cancellation handler. Owner: Engineering.
5. **Pricing change — Promoted exclusive to Seller Enterprise** (§27.11.9.18). Contingent; only if the product decision is made. Owner: Product + Pricing strategy.
6. **Ops-status-page banner copy for Firecrawl outage during Verification review** (§27.11.9.8). Needs: Comms + Legal sign-off on user-facing copy. Owner: Ops + Legal + Comms.
7. **Cross-marketplace-domain attribution rules for sellers in multiple domains** (§27.11.9.12). Needs: product decision on whether seller attribution follows the Seller Org or the specific PromotedListing; per-PromotedListing is authored here but contingent on product confirmation. Owner: Product.
8. **Deprecation timeline for `featured_placement.ended` webhook** (§27.11.7). Needs: engineering migration plan for existing subscribers; Comms notification cadence. Owner: Engineering + Developer Relations.

# 28\. The Markdown Editor {#28.-the-markdown-editor}

## 28.1 Core Functionality {#28.1-core-functionality}

The Markdown Editor is used for all rich-text fields: requirement descriptions, response text, comments, Use Case briefs, Capability Declarations.

**Input:** CommonMark markdown. Maximum field length varies by entity (see Section 3.2).

**Output:** Server-side sanitized HTML. Allowlist: `b`, `em`, `u`, `code`, `pre`, `h1-h6`, `blockquote`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `a`, `hr`, `table`.

**Security constraints (Gap 28.1):**

- No iframes, no embedded scripts, no external images.  
- Content Security Policy enforced: `script-src 'none'`, `frame-src 'none'`, `img-src 'self'`.  
- HTML sanitized via DOMPurify with strict config.  
- Malicious content attempts logged and reported to security team.

**Live preview:** Optional toggle. Updates on keystroke, no debounce. Preview pane positioned to the right of editor (side-by-side).

**Code blocks:** Language identifier for syntax highlighting (js, python, yaml, sql, json, etc.). Unsupported languages rendered as plain code.

**Links:** Auto-detected and linkified. Relative links resolve to workspace resources (e.g., `[Requirement](SRC-123)` links to requirement). External links open in new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

## 28.2 Keyboard Shortcuts (Editor Context) {#28.2-keyboard-shortcuts-(editor-context)}

| Shortcut | Action |
| :---- | :---- |
| `Cmd+B` | Bold (**text**) |
| `Cmd+I` | Italic (*text*) |
| `Cmd+K` | Insert link. Opens link dialog, does NOT trigger Command Palette when editor has focus. |
| `Tab` | Indent (4 spaces) in code blocks; no-op in prose |
| `Shift+Tab` | Outdent |
| `Cmd+Enter` | Save and close editor |
| `Escape` | Cancel and revert to last saved state |
| `Cmd+/` | Toggle line comment (prepend `//` ) |
| `Cmd+Shift+L` | Insert Markdown table template |

## 28.3 Acceptance Criteria {#28.3-acceptance-criteria}

- Plain text is valid (no required markdown syntax).  
- Malformed syntax is rendered literally (no submission block).  
- Editor keyboard shortcuts do not fire when editor is unfocused.  
- No external images, iframes, or scripts execute.  
- CSP headers prevent inline script injection.

# 29\. Notifications & Delivery Channels {#29.-notifications-&-delivery-channels}

## 29.1 Notification Event Catalog {#29.1-notification-event-catalog}

**Canonical catalog.** Appendix C is the authoritative Notification Event Catalog. This §29.1 subsection exists only as the user-preference and delivery-policy entry point for §29.2–§29.6; it no longer maintains a duplicate Standard / Additional event table. New notification kinds, webhook event kinds, recipient rules, channel defaults, retry-class bindings, and PostHog mirror obligations MUST be authored in Appendix C first, with Appendix G mirrors where required.

**Legacy-name compatibility.** The retired §29.1 table names remain compatibility aliases only. Runtime emitters and webhook subscribers MUST use the canonical Appendix C names below:

| Retired §29.1 name | Canonical Appendix C name |
| :---- | :---- |
| `response_received` | `response_submitted` |
| `vendor_invitation` | `vendor_invited` |
| `eoi_submitted` | `eoi_received` |
| `nda_signature_requested` | `nda_request` and `nda_signed` |
| `amendment_published` | `amendment_required` and `amendment_accepted` |
| `kb_entry_stale` | `kb.entry.flagged_stale` |

**§29-only source additions.** Historical §29-only events not already present in Appendix C are registered in the Appendix C v7.2.0-REM Phase 8.3 block: `response_ready_for_evaluation`, `comment_reply`, `grade_exception`, `insight_card_generated`, `scenario_saved`, `intelligence_brief_available`, `reverification_required`, `reverification_deadline`, `capability_declaration_evidence_needed`, `document_library_expired`, and `sync_failure_persistent`. Legacy `policy_ingestion_complete` resolves to the newer Appendix C `policy.ingestion.published` row and is not duplicated.

## 29.2 Delivery Channels {#29.2-delivery-channels}

**In-App Notifications:**

- Toast in bottom-right corner (max 5-second duration, dismissible).  
- Max 3 visible toasts stacked. Older queue below.  
- Each includes action link: "View \[entity\]" or "Dismiss."  
- Unread count badge on bell icon in top bar.

**Email notifications (via Loops.so):**

- Immediate for high-priority events (vendor invitations, SLA breaches, phase advances).  
- Daily digest for medium-priority events (policy ingestion complete, grade exceptions).  
- Weekly digest for low-priority events (capability evidence needed, scenario saved).  
- SPF/DKIM/DMARC aligned. From: `noreply@sourcera.io`.  
- Unsubscribe link in footer (links to preferences, not permanent opt-out).

**Slack notifications (v6.0+):**

- Requires Slack workspace connection via OAuth. Org Owner can enable in Settings.  
- High-priority events sent to configurable Slack channel (default: \#sourcera-alerts).  
- Includes deep link to item in Sourcera.

## 29.3 User Preferences (Gap 29.2) {#29.3-user-preferences-(gap-29.2)}

**Granularity:**

- Per-event-type: Immediate, Daily, Weekly, Never.  
- Per-channel: In-App (toggle), Email (toggle), Slack (toggle).  
- Per-workspace: Notifications mutable per-workspace (e.g., mute workspace "Q4 Budget Review" but receive notifications for "CRM Evaluation").  
- Quiet hours: Start/end time \+ timezone. No notifications during quiet hours (all channels).  
- Do Not Disturb (DND) mode: Opt-in toggle disables all notifications temporarily (1 hour, 4 hours, 8 hours, custom).  
- Entity mute: Mute notifications from specific requirement, vendor, or thread for 24 hours ("I've already seen this, don't remind me").

**Location:** Settings → Notifications → Preferences.

**Defaults for new users:**

- High-priority events (vendor invitation, phase advance): Immediate email \+ in-app.  
- Medium-priority (comment reply, insight card): In-app only (email opt-in).  
- Low-priority (scenario saved): In-app only.  
- Quiet hours: 6pm–9am in user's timezone.

## 29.4 Slack Integration (Gap 29.1) {#29.4-slack-integration-(gap-29.1)}

**Failure handling:**

1. Slack webhook POST fails → Retry immediately (1s).  
2. Retry fails → Wait 2 minutes, retry again.  
3. Second retry fails → Wait 5 minutes, retry once more.  
4. Third retry fails → Fallback: send as email instead. User notified: "Your Slack notification failed to send. We've emailed you instead. Check your Slack connection in Settings."  
5. User receives email: "Your Slack workspace connection may be disconnected. \[Reconnect Slack\]"

**Disconnection detection:**

- When webhook returns 401 (Unauthorized) or 404 (Not Found), Slack connection marked as stale.  
- Next notification triggers: "Slack connection issue detected. \[Re-connect Slack\] or \[Switch to Email Only\]"  
- User can re-authenticate in Settings → Integrations → Slack.

## 29.5 Webhook Notifications {#29.5-webhook-notifications}

Webhook events are delivered to registered endpoint URLs for Enterprise customers and integrations.

**Payload format:** JSON. HTTP POST. HMAC-SHA256 signed with org webhook secret.

**Standard payload metadata:** `event_type`, `timestamp` (UTC), `workspace_id`, `organization_id`, `delivery_id`.

**Webhook events:** All events from Section 29.1 are available as webhook subscriptions. Payload schema matches entity definitions in Section 3.2.

**Retry:** Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve. See Appendix F for webhook retry policy.

## 29.6 Acceptance Criteria {#29.6-acceptance-criteria}

- Notifications delivered within 30 seconds of triggering event.  
- Email not sent if user already read the in-app notification for the same event.  
- Preference changes take effect immediately.  
- Webhook signatures are verified by all integration SDKs.  
- Slack integration fallback to email on failure.  
- Quiet hours prevent notifications outside specified window.

## 29.7 Notification Failure Audit {#29.7-notification-failure-audit}

Pointer subsection. Failed notification deliveries (in-app store-and-forward failure, Loops.so email bounce / template render failure, Slack webhook failure, customer webhook DLQ entry) MUST emit a `NotificationFailureAudit` row per §6.8.5 row class #14. Recovery rules per delivery channel are authored at: in-app — §29.2; email — §41.1; Slack — §29.4; webhook — §31.6 + Appendix F. Retention and DSAR cascade behavior follow §6.8.5.

## 29.8 Notification Preference Inheritance {#29.8-notification-preference-inheritance}

Pointer subsection. User-level notification preferences (§29.3) override Org defaults; Org defaults override system defaults. Inheritance precedence: User > Org > System. Per-event-class overrides (e.g., `comment_mention=Immediate`) are independent of the global frequency setting. Authoritative defaults per event class are in Appendix C.

## 29.9 Support Widget {#29.9-support-widget}

The Support Widget is the customer-facing in-app support entry point on every paid tier per §34.1 cell **Support**. Backed by Zendesk; Free-tier users receive a `mailto:` fallback that pre-fills `request_id`, `user_id`, and `org_id`. The 4-hour Enterprise SLA on customer-reported critical (SEV-1 / SEV-2) tickets opened via this surface is authoritative in §34.1; internal incident-response thresholds (page-on-call ack times, war-room open) live in §42.2 / §42.3 and are tighter operational targets. Ticket-creation events emit the `support.ticket.created` webhook per Appendix C and the `support_ticket_created` PostHog mirror per Appendix G.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Support Widget MUST render on every paid-tier surface; Free-tier renders the `mailto:` fallback with pre-filled fields.
2. Ticket creation MUST emit `support_ticket_created` PostHog event AND `support.ticket.created` webhook (where customer-subscribed) within 1 s of submission.
3. Critical-severity tickets opened on Enterprise plans MUST be routed to the on-call queue within 1 minute of submission per §42.2 alerting rules.

## 29.10 Notification Frequency Override Rules {#29.10-notification-frequency-override-rules}

Pointer subsection. Per-user `comment_mention` frequency override (Immediate / Daily / Weekly / Never) is authoritative in §29.3; per-event-class frequency caps (e.g., `internal_comment_thread.visibility_changed` rate-capped to 1 per viewer per thread per 5 min) are in Appendix C catalog footnotes. Operationally-sensitive events (`internal_comment_post.moderated`, `marketplace.abuse_report.seller_banned`) MUST bypass DND / quiet-hours per Appendix C.

## 29.11 Full-Screen Incident Surface {#29.11-full-screen-incident-surface}

When an error card per §3.7 would render more than three CTAs (one primary plus two secondary), the page MUST escalate to a dedicated full-screen incident surface that supports up to seven CTAs, an incident description block (≤ 1,200 chars), an incident-correlation ID with copy-to-clipboard, a "Page on-call" CTA routing to the §50.17.5 paging runbook surface, and a `support.incident_surface_opened` PostHog event with `incident_id`, `correlation_id`, `originating_route`, `user_id`, `org_id`. The surface composition is authored once and consumed via the `useIncidentSurface(...)` hook; no page authors its own escalation surface.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Every page that renders an error card MUST link to the full-screen incident surface when the recovery-CTA budget is exceeded.
2. The surface MUST emit `support.incident_surface_opened` exactly once per render; deduplication is keyed on `correlation_id` per session.
3. The "Page on-call" CTA MUST route to the §50.17.5 paging runbook with the `correlation_id` pre-bound.

# 30\. Search & Command Palette {#30.-search-&-command-palette}

## 30.1 Architecture {#30.1-architecture}

**Invocation:** `Cmd+K` (macOS) / `Ctrl+K` (Windows/Linux). Global — available in all views.

**Dismiss:** `Escape`.

**Search:** Fuzzy-search input (200ms debounce, no minimum character requirement). Case-insensitive. Handles partial matches and typos (Levenshtein distance ≤2).

**Results:** Grouped by category: Navigation, Actions, Search, Filters. Each shows keyboard shortcut if available.

**MRU (Most Recently Used):** Last 10 executed commands shown at top before filtering.

Commands are context-filtered based on:

- **Arrow keys:** Up/down navigate results.  
- **Escape:** Close palette, return focus to previous element.  
- **ARIA labels:** Palette labeled "Command Palette" with `role="dialog"`. Results list labeled "Commands" with `role="listbox"`.

## 30.7 Acceptance Criteria {#30.7-acceptance-criteria}

- Command Palette opens in \<50ms.  
- Fuzzy search handles partial matches and typos (Levenshtein ≤2).  
- Context-aware filtering prevents navigation to unavailable views (e.g., `go scoring` disabled in Phase \<10).  
- Full-text search returns results within 200ms.  
- KB entries not searchable from Buyer Console search (console isolation enforced).  
- MRU shows last 10 executed commands.  
- Keyboard navigation (Tab, Arrow, Enter) works correctly.
