# 31\. Integrations & Webhooks {#31.-integrations-&-webhooks}

## 31.1 Webhook Event Types & Idempotency {#31.1-webhook-event-types-&-idempotency}

All events from Section 29.1 are available as webhook subscriptions. Each webhook delivery includes a unique `event_id` that persists across retries. Webhook consumers **must** implement idempotency by deduplicating based on `event_id`. Duplicate deliveries (same `event_id`) must produce no additional side effects.

**Event ID Format:** `evt_{unix_ms}_{base32_random10}` (e.g., `evt_1712761200000_mfrggzdfmn`). This is the sole canonical webhook event identifier format: a string, not UUID / UUIDv7, sortable by Unix-millisecond prefix and opaque beyond consumer idempotency. Immutable per event.

## 31.2 Webhook Payload Structure {#31.2-webhook-payload-structure}

Every webhook event, regardless of domain, uses the root envelope below. Domain-specific sections MAY add constraints to `data`, but MUST NOT remove or rename root fields.

{

  "event\_id": "evt\_1712761200000\_mfrggzdfmn",

  "event\_type": "response\_received",

  "event\_class": "product\_domain",

  "event\_version": "1.0",

  "schema\_version": "1.0",

  "delivery\_id": "del\_xyz789",

  "delivery\_attempt": 1,

  "timestamp": "2026-04-10T14:30:00Z",

  "organization\_id": "org\_abc",

  "workspace\_id": "ws\_def",

  "console": "buyer",

  "data": { ... }

}

**Envelope field contract.**

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `event_id` | String | Immutable across retries; MUST match §31.1 canonical format `evt_{unix_ms}_{base32_random10}` | Idempotency key per §31.1. |
| `event_type` | String | Registered event name | Must resolve to Appendix C when customer-visible or to an explicitly internal webhook catalog row. |
| `event_class` | Enum | Appendix J `webhook_event_class`; required | Enables class-level subscription filtering for every event family, not only billing-domain events. |
| `event_version` | Semver string | Required; current default `1.0` | Version of the event-type payload contract. Backward-compatible field additions increment minor; removals, type changes, or semantic reinterpretations increment major. |
| `schema_version` | Semver string | Required; current root envelope `1.0` | Version of the root envelope contract. Any root-field addition, type change, nullability change, or required-header change increments this value. |
| `delivery_id` | String | Unique per delivery attempt | Changes on retry; `event_id` does not. |
| `delivery_attempt` | Integer | 1–5 | Mirrors Appendix F attempt count. |
| `timestamp` | Timestamp | ISO 8601 UTC | Source mutation commit time, not delivery-send time. |
| `organization_id` | UUID | Required for Org-scoped customer events; nullable only for platform-internal webhooks | Subscriber scoping anchor. |
| `workspace_id` | UUID | Nullable | Present for workspace-scoped events. |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer`, `seller`, `cross_console`, `ops`, or `platform`; nullable only for public unauthenticated events | Firewall and routing hint; does not replace authorization checks. |
| `data` | Object | Event-specific schema | The event-type payload. |

Signed with HMAC-SHA256 using the Org webhook secret. Signature included in `X-Sourcera-Signature` header. The delivery headers in §31.5 repeat the class, version, attempt, and secret-version metadata so consumers can route or reject before parsing the body.

## 31.3 Integration Phase Export Mapping {#31.3-integration-phase-export-mapping}

At Phase 13 (Closed), Workspace Owners may export winning vendor action items and requirements to integrated tools. Export mappings:

| Sourcera Entity | Target System | Mapping |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Use Case | Jira Epic / Linear Project | title, description, labels |
| Requirement | Jira Issue / Linear Issue | title, description, priority (via weight), custom fields (status, response\_type) |
| Winning Vendor Response | Issue Description / Comment | vendor\_name, response\_text, confidence\_score |
| TCO Data | Spreadsheet Link | projected\_cost, cost\_per\_point, cost\_rank |

**Scope:** Only requirements marked "won" and the selected vendor's responses are exported. Internal scores, comments, and non-winning vendors are excluded.

**Supported Integrations:**

- Jira Cloud  
- Linear  
- Asana  
- Azure DevOps

Setup via Settings → Integrations → Configure Export Mapping.

## 31.4 Partner Integrations {#31.4-partner-integrations}

- **Salesforce:** Bidirectional vendor account sync. New vendors from Marketplace EOIs auto-create Salesforce Accounts.  
- **Slack / Microsoft Teams:** Channel-scoped notifications per workspace. Admin sets channel and notification types.  
- **Zapier / Make:** No native integration; use Webhook API (Section 32\) for custom automation.

Setup: Settings → Integrations → Partner Tools. Self-service configuration with OAuth flows.

## 31.5 Webhook Configuration & Limits {#31.5-webhook-configuration-&-limits}

Per-plan webhook-endpoint counts are authoritative in §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 cell **Webhook Endpoints** (Free / Starter / Growth / Scale / Enterprise). Retry semantics and payload size are uniform across all tiers and live here:

| Property | Value | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Endpoints per Org | Per §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 cell **Webhook Endpoints** | §34.1 (authoritative); Free 1 / Starter 5 / Growth 25 / Scale 50 / Enterprise 100 |
| Retry attempts | 5 (Appendix F retry curve) | §31.1; Appendix F |
| Payload size limit | 256 KB | §31.1; CI-enforced gate `webhook_payload_max_256kb` |
| Signature | HMAC-SHA256 | §31.2 |
| Idempotency | `event_id` in §31.1 canonical string format `evt_{unix_ms}_{base32_random10}` | §31.1; §31.6 |

**Standard delivery headers.** Every webhook delivery carries the following headers:

| Header | Value | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `X-Sourcera-Event-Type` | `event_type` | Registered dotted event name. |
| `X-Sourcera-Event-Class` | `event_class` | Required for class-level filters across every domain. |
| `X-Sourcera-Event-Version` | `event_version` | Lets consumers reject unsupported event payload versions before body processing. |
| `X-Sourcera-Schema-Version` | `schema_version` | Root envelope version. |
| `X-Sourcera-Delivery-Attempt` | `delivery_attempt` | Integer 1–5. |
| `X-Sourcera-Webhook-Secret-Version` | Integer ≥ 1 | Secret version used to sign the delivery; rotation contract in §31.10. |
| `X-Sourcera-Signature` | `sha256=<hex>` | HMAC-SHA256 over raw request body. |

## 31.6 Webhook Consumer Requirements {#31.6-webhook-consumer-requirements}

**Success Criteria:** HTTP 2xx response within 10 seconds.

**Failure Handling:** HTTP status handling is explicit and uniform across all event classes:

| Consumer result | Sourcera delivery behavior | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 2xx within 10s | Mark delivery succeeded; no retry | Consumer owns idempotent processing. |
| 3xx | Follow one redirect when the redirect target matches the subscription's registered hostname or an explicitly allow-listed replacement hostname; otherwise treat as failure | Prevents open-redirect exfiltration. A redirect loop is failure. |
| 4xx | Terminal failure for this delivery; no automatic retry | Treat as consumer configuration or payload-contract rejection. Mark the delivery `failed_terminal_4xx`, notify the Org Admin / configured webhook owner, and expose manual replay after the customer fixes the endpoint. |
| 5xx | Retry per Appendix F | Transient consumer-side failure. |
| Timeout >10s or network failure | Retry per Appendix F | Delivery attempt counted; retry follows the event's F.1 / F.2 class. |

**Idempotency Contract:** Consumer must handle duplicate `event_id` values gracefully (log warning, return success without re-processing).

**HMAC Verification:** Consumer must verify signature before processing:

signature \= HMAC-SHA256(webhook\_secret, raw\_request\_body)

X-Sourcera-Signature \= "sha256=" \+ hex(signature)

**Dead Letter Queue:** After 5 failed deliveries, webhook marked `failed`. Admin receives email notification. Failed webhooks available for manual retry from Settings → Integrations → Failed Webhooks (30-day retention).

**4xx terminal rule.** Consumer 4xx responses do NOT consume the 5-attempt retry budget. The failure is terminal until a manual replay or endpoint reactivation occurs. This rule aligns §31.6 with Appendix F.1 and §31.8.9 AC #13.

### 31.6.1 Payload Body-Exclusion Gates (Firewall-Sensitive Domains) {#31.6.1-payload-body-exclusion-gates}

Certain event domains carry firewall-sensitive content that MUST NOT appear in webhook payloads. Subscribers receive metadata only (entity IDs, actor, timestamps, classification flags); the consuming application MUST issue an authenticated API read against §32 endpoints to fetch the body or attachment data, applying the calling session's authorization at read time. This rule prevents leakage via webhook-endpoint logs, third-party logging proxies, or unencrypted-at-rest message buses, all of which are realistic exfiltration vectors that signed transport (HMAC-SHA256) does not address.

The exclusion gates below are CI-enforced — every PR that mutates the webhook payload schema runs the named gate and fails the build on violation.

| Domain | Authoritative Section | Excluded Fields | CI Gate Name | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Internal Comment | §25.7.10 | `body`, `attachment_ids[]` | `webhook_payload_no_internal_comment_body` | Subscribers receive `event_id`, `event_type`, `org_id`, `workspace_id`, `thread_id`, `post_id`, `actor_user_id`, `timestamp`, `delivery_id` only. Body and attachment fetch require authenticated buyer-console API read. |
| Selection Report draft | §10.13 webhook block | `narrative_markdown`, redline diff payloads | `webhook_payload_no_selection_report_narrative` | Same-pattern exclusion. Authored hand-off — Phase 11 to confirm gate registration in §10.13. |
| KB Entry (privacy_class ∈ {confidential_internal, restricted_audit}) | §22 KB webhook block | `body`, `attachment_ids[]` for privacy_class non-public | `webhook_payload_no_kb_restricted_body` | Public-class KB entries MAY include body in payload subject to size cap. |

**Cross-reference.** §25.7.10 is the canonical authoring site for the Internal Comment exclusion rule and the named CI gate `webhook_payload_no_internal_comment_body`. §31.6.1 records the cross-cutting pattern so that future firewall-sensitive domains (Selection Report, restricted-class KB entries) can declare their exclusion gate in one place. Adding a new domain to the table requires (a) authoring the exclusion in the domain's webhook subsection (mirroring the §25.7.10 pattern), (b) registering the named CI gate, and (c) appending the row here.

**Operational invariant.** The 256 KB payload ceiling at §31.5 is a transport limit; the body-exclusion gates are an authorization-and-leakage limit. Both are enforced independently — a payload that is below 256 KB but contains body for a firewall-sensitive domain MUST still fail the body-exclusion gate.

## 31.7 Acceptance Criteria {#31.7-acceptance-criteria}

- Every webhook delivery includes unique, immutable `event_id`.  
- Every webhook delivery includes required `event_class`, `event_version`, `schema_version`, and `delivery_attempt` fields in the body and the corresponding standard headers in §31.5.
- Webhook retry schedule follows Appendix F exactly.  
- Consumer 4xx responses never trigger automatic retry; 5xx and timeouts retry per Appendix F; 3xx follows the §31.6 one-redirect rule.
- Signature verification required; unsigned payloads rejected.  
- Webhook secret rotation follows §31.10 for every event class; billing-domain rotation is not a special case.
- Failed webhook notifications sent within 1 hour of final failure.  
- Webhook payload size enforced at API gateway level (256 KB hard limit).  
- Duplicate deliveries (same `event_id`) do not cause duplicate mutations in consumer system (idempotency requirement documented).

## 31.8 Billing-Domain Webhook Catalog {#31.8-billing-domain-webhook-catalog}

**Authoring Intent.** §31.8 authors the webhook surface for the §4.8 Billing & AI Accounting entities (`AIOperation`, `AIWallet`, `OutcomeContract`, `ContestRecord`, `CommittedSpendContract`, `FreeAllowanceCounter`) and the per-Org plan-tier lifecycle authored in §34. The Phase 4 / Phase 4c integrations explicitly deferred webhook authoring to this phase (`_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` → Webhook Additions; §32.8 Acceptance #21 names the four interim events `billing.wallet.overage_cap_changed`, `billing.wallet.auto_topup_config_changed`, `billing.contest.filed`, `billing.contest.decision_received` as a known-incomplete subset). This section catalogues the 13 net-new billing-domain events required by the integration program billing-webhook prompt, fixes their canonical event-type identifiers, declares per-event payload schemas, fixes signing/idempotency/retry semantics, and registers each event in Appendix C (where user-facing) and Appendix G (PostHog mirrors). All events authored here inherit §31.1–§31.6 transport semantics (HMAC-SHA256, `event_id`, Appendix F retry curve, DLQ after 5 failures, ≤256 KB payload).

**Source authority.** Summary §2 + Appendix C C.75–C.87 (entity foundation); `Sourcera_Buyer_Pricing_Strategy.md` §6 / §7 / §11 + `Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy.md` §6 / §7 / §11 (wallet, overage, committed-spend, plan upgrade/downgrade); §4.8.1–§4.8.11 (entity definitions); §32.8 (API surface coupling); §34 (plan-tier operational policy). Where the source documents are silent on a specific payload field, retry override, or alert routing, the authored value is flagged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` → Authored Extensions for human reviewer sign-off.

### 31.8.1 Naming Convention & Console Pooling

All billing-domain event-type identifiers are namespaced under the `billing.` prefix to match the existing `billing.wallet.*` / `billing.contest.*` events emitted by §32.8 mutating endpoints. The shorthand names used in the integration prompt (`ai_operation.settled`, `wallet.cap_warning_80`, etc.) MAP to the canonical prefixed identifiers below; consumer subscriptions MUST use the canonical prefixed form. The `billing.` namespace is reserved: any future non-billing event MUST NOT collide with this prefix.

Per §4.8.3 (AIWallet Org-pooling) and §32.8 (cross-console scope rule), billing-domain webhook deliveries are **Org-scoped, not console-scoped**. A single webhook subscription per Org receives events from both buyer-console and seller-console activity; the `console` field in the payload distinguishes the originating side. This preserves the Pricing Strategy §11 "billing is shared; data is not" rule: subscribers SHOULD NOT use the webhook surface to reconstruct cross-console workspace state — only the wallet/operation-level financial fields are shared. The Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2) is preserved by the payload field set: per-event payload field tables below explicitly enumerate which fields are populated per `console` value.

### 31.8.2 Common Billing-Webhook Payload Envelope

Every billing-domain webhook event delivery uses the §31.2 root envelope. Billing events fill the root envelope as follows and add billing-specific fields only where noted. Inherited root fields repeated in this table, including `event_class`, `event_version`, `schema_version`, `delivery_id`, and `delivery_attempt`, do not create billing-only overrides; §31.2 remains canonical for every event class.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `event_id` | String | `evt_{unix_ms}_{base32_random10}`; immutable across retries | Per §31.1; persists across all 5 retry attempts |
| `event_type` | String | One of the canonical names in §31.8.3–§31.8.7 plus the v7.1.1 completeness additions in §31.8.11; lowercase dotted | Subscriber filters on this field |
| `event_class` | Enum | Required root field; value `billing_domain` | Distinguishes billing events from product / marketplace / CRM events; permits class-level subscription filtering. |
| `event_version` | Semver string | Required root field; current `1.0` unless an event-specific subsection declares a higher version | Version of the billing event-type payload contract. |
| `schema_version` | Semver string | Required root field; current root envelope `1.0` | Version of the root envelope contract. |
| `delivery_id` | String | `del_{unix_ms}_{base32_random10}` | Unique per delivery attempt; differs across retries |
| `delivery_attempt` | Integer | 1–5 | Per Appendix F retry curve; populated to aid consumer dedupe + observability |
| `timestamp` | Timestamp | ISO 8601 UTC, millisecond precision | The moment the source mutation committed (NOT the moment the delivery attempt was sent) |
| `organization_id` | UUID | FK → Organization | The Org whose billing surface the event pertains to |
| `console` | Enum | Per Appendix J `ai_operation_console`: `buyer`, `seller`, `cross_console` (Org-pooled events that are not console-attributable, e.g., `billing.plan.*` when both consoles upgrade in one transaction) | Drives subscriber routing |
| `legal_entity` | Enum | Per Appendix J `legal_entity` | Mirrors AIWallet.`legal_entity`; subscribers performing accounting reconciliation MUST partition on this field |
| `billing_currency` | Enum | Per Appendix J `billing_currency` | Mirrors AIWallet.`billing_currency`; all monetary fields in `data` use both `..._cents` (USD) and `..._display` per §32.8.0 |
| `data` | Object | Per-event-type schema, §31.8.3–§31.8.7 and §31.8.11 | The event-specific payload |
| `signature_algorithm` | String | Billing-specific data-plane assertion; always `hmac_sha256_v1` | Future-proofs algorithm rotation; duplicates the header-level signing scheme for accounting consumers. |
| `webhook_secret_version` | Integer | ≥ 1 | Mirrors `X-Sourcera-Webhook-Secret-Version`; rotation increments this per §31.10. |

**Header set per delivery.** Standard headers per §31.2 plus:

- `X-Sourcera-Event-Type: billing.<...>`
- `X-Sourcera-Event-Class: billing_domain`
- `X-Sourcera-Event-Version: <semver>`
- `X-Sourcera-Schema-Version: <semver>`
- `X-Sourcera-Delivery-Attempt: 1..5`
- `X-Sourcera-Webhook-Secret-Version: <integer>`
- `X-Sourcera-Signature: sha256=<hex>` per §31.6

### 31.8.3 AIOperation Settlement Events

The three AIOperation lifecycle events fire on every settlement-state transition that has financial effect on the wallet, the commit pool, the free allowance, OR the customer's contest position. They MUST be subscribed to by any external system performing usage forecasting, accounting reconciliation, or contest-window monitoring.

#### `billing.ai_operation.settled`

**Trigger.** AIOperation transitions from `pending` to `accepted`, `auto_accepted`, or `rejected` per §4.8.1 state machine. Fired EXACTLY ONCE per AIOperation per terminal-pending transition; the late-signal handler (§4.8.1 Failure Mode #2) does NOT re-fire this event when a late `accepted` signal is silently ignored after `auto_accepted`.

**Fired by.** Outcome Resolver settlement worker.

**Payload `data`.**

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `ai_operation_id` | UUID | FK → AIOperation |
| `capability_id` | String | FK → CapabilityRegistryEntry |
| `workspace_id` | UUID (nullable) | Polymorphic FK; null for Org-level operations |
| `workspace_kind` | Enum (nullable) | Per AIOperation.`workspace_kind` |
| `actor_id` | UUID | Polymorphic; redacted to `redacted` if `redacted_at IS NOT NULL` |
| `actor_type` | Enum | Per AIOperation.`actor_type` |
| `model_tier` | Enum | Per AIOperation.`model_tier` |
| `settlement_state` | Enum | One of `accepted`, `auto_accepted`, `rejected` (NEVER `pending`, `contested`, `reversed` for this event) |
| `settlement_at` | Timestamp | UTC; mirrors AIOperation.`settlement_at` |
| `auto_accept_after_seconds` | Integer | Snapshot from OutcomeContract; aids consumer interpretation of `auto_accepted` |
| `effective_charge_cents` | Integer | Final wallet impact; equals `value_price_cents` for `accepted`/`auto_accepted`, equals `cost_price_cents` for `rejected` |
| `effective_charge_display` | Object | `{"amount", "currency", "fx_rate_locked"}` per §32.8.0 |
| `value_price_cents` | Integer | Reference: what would have been charged on `accepted` |
| `cost_price_cents` | Integer | Reference: what would have been charged on `rejected` |
| `cost_base_cents` | Integer | Locked at AIOperation write |
| `cost_base_version_id` | UUID | FK → CostBaseRecalculationLog |
| `wallet_id` | UUID | FK → AIWallet |
| `wallet_balance_after_cents` | Integer | Wallet's `budget_value_dollars_cents - consumed_value_dollars_cents` AFTER this charge applied; aids consumer-side wallet projection |
| `billed_against_free_allowance` | Boolean | True when the operation drew §4.8.7 FreeAllowanceCounter, not the wallet |
| `billed_against_committed_spend_id` | UUID (nullable) | FK → CommittedSpendContract |
| `provenance_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex; consumers performing reconciliation MAY use this to assert AIOperation identity |
| `contest_window_at` | Timestamp | UTC; equals `settlement_at + 14 days`; consumers building contest UI must surface this deadline |
| `parent_operation_id` | UUID (nullable) | For Managed Agent sub-call rollup |

**Volume budget.** Up to 1 event per AIOperation row. At enterprise scale (Pricing Strategy projection: ~50K customer-billed AIOperations/Org/month for Buyer Scale + Seller Growth combined), this is the highest-volume billing-domain event. Subscribers MUST handle ≥ 100/min sustained per-Org throughput; the §31.5 payload-size limit (256 KB) is sufficient with margin.

**Per-console field nullification.** When `console=platform_marketing` or `cost_center ∈ {sourcera_owned, platform_marketing}`, the event is NOT delivered to customer subscribers (per §4.8.1 Scope Isolation: these rows never appear on customer surfaces). Ops Console subscribers receive a parallel internal event class outside the scope of this catalog.

#### `billing.ai_operation.contested`

**Trigger.** AIOperation transitions from `accepted` / `auto_accepted` to `contested` per §4.8.1 state machine. ContestRecord materialized; soft credit posted to AIWallet. Fired ALSO when the late-signal handler (§4.8.1 Failure Mode #2) automatically materializes a contest with reason `auto_filed_late_signal`.

**Fired by.** §32.8.7 contest-file endpoint (customer-initiated path) OR Outcome Resolver late-signal handler (system-initiated path); the same event_type covers both paths, distinguished by `contest_origin`.

**Payload `data`.**

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `ai_operation_id` | UUID | FK → AIOperation |
| `contest_record_id` | UUID | FK → ContestRecord; mirrors AIOperation.`contest_record_id` |
| `contest_origin` | Enum | `customer_billing_admin` (per §32.8.7) OR `system_late_signal` (per §4.8.1 Failure Mode #2) |
| `prior_settlement_state` | Enum | `accepted` or `auto_accepted` (the state before contest) |
| `requested_credit_amount_cents` | Integer | Per ContestRecord; equals or less than original `effective_charge_cents` |
| `requested_credit_amount_display` | Object | `{"amount", "currency", "fx_rate_locked"}` |
| `soft_credit_applied_cents` | Integer | The amount actually credited to the wallet on contest filing (matches `requested_credit_amount_cents` per §32.8.7) |
| `wallet_id` | UUID | FK → AIWallet |
| `wallet_balance_after_soft_credit_cents` | Integer | Wallet's available balance AFTER the soft credit posted |
| `contest_window_at` | Timestamp | UTC; for late-signal contests, equals filing time + 14 days; for customer-filed contests, mirrors original AIOperation.`contest_window_at` |
| `filed_by_user_id` | UUID (nullable) | Per ContestRecord; null when `contest_origin=system_late_signal`; redacted to `redacted` if user later DSAR-erased |
| `filed_at` | Timestamp | UTC |
| `reason_category` | Enum | Per ContestRecord; e.g., `bad_output`, `wrong_capability`, `duplicate_charge`, `auto_filed_late_signal` |
| `capability_id` | String | FK → CapabilityRegistryEntry |
| `provenance_hash` | String | 64-char sha256 hex; identical to original AIOperation.`provenance_hash` |

**Volume budget.** Per Pricing Strategy §6, the realistic per-Org contest rate is < 0.5% of customer-billed operations (≤ 250 contests/Org/month at Enterprise scale). Late-signal-originated contests are bounded by Outcome Resolver bug-rate (target < 0.05%).

#### `billing.ai_operation.reversed`

**Trigger.** AIOperation transitions to `reversed` per §4.8.1 state machine. Three pathways fire this event:

1. ContestRecord approved by Ops Finance (`contested → reversed`).
2. Ops Finance emergency manual reversal post-contest-window (`accepted/auto_accepted → reversed`, the Ops emergency path per §4.8.1 state machine).
3. CostBaseRecalculationLog correction reversal (rare; system-initiated when a faulty cost-base seed is rolled back).

**Fired by.** Ops Finance contest-decision worker OR Ops Finance manual reversal endpoint OR CostBase correction worker. Distinguished by `reversal_origin`.

**Payload `data`.**

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `ai_operation_id` | UUID | FK → AIOperation |
| `contest_record_id` | UUID (nullable) | Populated when `reversal_origin=contest_approved`; null otherwise |
| `reversal_origin` | Enum | `contest_approved`, `ops_emergency`, `cost_base_correction` |
| `prior_settlement_state` | Enum | The state immediately before reversal: `accepted`, `auto_accepted`, `contested`, OR `rejected` |
| `original_effective_charge_cents` | Integer | The charge that was applied; this amount is being credited |
| `original_effective_charge_display` | Object | `{"amount", "currency", "fx_rate_locked"}`; FX rate matches the original charge per §4.8.1 FX-Locking Semantics |
| `credit_destination` | Enum | `wallet` (most common), `commit_pool` (when original drew from CommittedSpendContract), `free_allowance` (rare; when original consumed a free unit) |
| `wallet_id` | UUID | FK → AIWallet |
| `wallet_balance_after_credit_cents` | Integer | Wallet's available balance AFTER the credit posted |
| `committed_spend_contract_id` | UUID (nullable) | Populated when `credit_destination=commit_pool` |
| `free_allowance_counter_id` | UUID (nullable) | Populated when `credit_destination=free_allowance` |
| `reversed_at` | Timestamp | UTC; the moment the reversal credit posted |
| `reversed_by_user_id` | UUID (nullable) | Ops Finance reviewer; null when `reversal_origin=cost_base_correction` (system-initiated) |
| `decision_note` | String | ≤ 2000 chars; Ops Finance free-text reason; redacted to `redacted` if subsequently DSAR-erased |
| `audit_severity` | Enum | `standard` (contest_approved) or `elevated` (ops_emergency, cost_base_correction); per §4.8.1 emergency-reversal audit rule |

**Volume budget.** Per Pricing Strategy §6, expected reversal rate is < 0.3% of customer-billed operations (subset of contest rate). `ops_emergency` and `cost_base_correction` reversals are exception paths and SHOULD trigger Ops alerting at any non-zero rate.

### 31.8.4 Wallet Threshold and Auto-Topup Events

The five wallet events fire on threshold-crossing of `consumed_value_dollars / budget_value_dollars` ratio AND on auto-topup execution outcomes. They MUST be subscribed to by any external system that gates customer behavior on remaining wallet runway (e.g., procurement-side approval workflows that pause work when budget exhausts).

#### `billing.wallet.cap_warning_50`

**Trigger.** AIWallet `consumed_value_dollars_cents / budget_value_dollars_cents` first crosses ≥ 0.50 within the current billing period AND `wallet_state ∈ {active, soft_warned_50}`. Fires AT MOST ONCE per (`wallet_id`, billing_period). Re-arms on billing-period rollover OR on a manual top-up that drops utilization back below 0.50 (re-firing requires a NEW threshold crossing).

**Fired by.** Wallet utilization recalculation worker (event-driven, runs on every wallet-impacting AIOperation settlement).

**Payload `data`.** Identical structure to `cap_warning_80`, with `utilization_pct ≥ 50.00`, `remaining_value_dollars_cents` intentionally not negative, and `new_wallet_state=soft_warned_50`.

#### `billing.wallet.cap_warning_80`

**Trigger.** AIWallet `consumed_value_dollars_cents / budget_value_dollars_cents` first crosses ≥ 0.80 within the current billing period AND `wallet_state ∈ {active, soft_capped_80}`. Fires AT MOST ONCE per (`wallet_id`, billing_period). Re-arms on billing-period rollover OR on a manual top-up that drops utilization back below 0.80 (re-firing requires a NEW threshold crossing).

**Fired by.** Wallet utilization recalculation worker (event-driven, runs on every wallet-impacting AIOperation settlement).

**Payload `data`.**

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `wallet_id` | UUID | FK → AIWallet |
| `billing_period_start` | Date | UTC; AIWallet.`current_billing_period_start` |
| `billing_period_end` | Date | UTC |
| `budget_value_dollars_cents` | Integer | The wallet's included monthly budget |
| `consumed_value_dollars_cents` | Integer | Spend at the moment of crossing |
| `utilization_pct` | Decimal(5,2) | `consumed / budget`; will be ≥ 80.00 at first delivery |
| `remaining_value_dollars_cents` | Integer | `budget - consumed`; intentionally not negative for `cap_warning_80` |
| `overage_cap_value_dollars_cents` | Integer (nullable) | If overage enabled, the additional ceiling beyond `budget`; null when overage disabled |
| `auto_topup_enabled` | Boolean | Subscribers can correlate with auto-topup state |
| `auto_topup_trigger_utilization_pct` | Decimal(5,2) (nullable) | When subscriber sees this approaching `cap_warning_80`, an auto-topup may follow |
| `prior_wallet_state` | Enum | Per AIWallet state machine; typically `active` |
| `new_wallet_state` | Enum | Typically `soft_capped_80` |
| `crossing_at` | Timestamp | UTC |
| `triggering_ai_operation_id` | UUID | The operation whose settlement crossed the threshold |

#### `billing.wallet.cap_warning_100`

**Trigger.** AIWallet utilization first crosses ≥ 1.00 (i.e., included budget exhausted) within the current billing period. Fires AT MOST ONCE per (`wallet_id`, billing_period). Re-arms identically to `cap_warning_80`.

**Fired by.** Wallet utilization recalculation worker.

**Payload `data`.** Identical structure to `cap_warning_80` plus:

| Additional Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `overage_consumed_value_dollars_cents` | Integer | Spend in excess of `budget`; ≥ 0 |
| `overage_remaining_value_dollars_cents` | Integer | `overage_cap_value_dollars_cents - overage_consumed_value_dollars_cents`; for hard-cap detection |
| `hard_cap_imminent` | Boolean | True when `overage_remaining_value_dollars_cents ≤ 5% of overage_cap_value_dollars_cents`; flags consumers that a hard cap (operations rejected) is approaching |
| `new_wallet_state` | Enum | One of `soft_capped_100`, `hard_capped_100` (when overage disabled or already at overage ceiling) |

**Hard-cap relationship.** Crossing `utilization_pct ≥ 1.00` is NOT the same as `hard_capped_100` — the wallet may still serve operations from `overage_consumed_value_dollars` until the overage cap is hit. Subscribers MUST distinguish these conditions via `new_wallet_state` and `hard_cap_imminent`.

#### `billing.wallet.auto_topup_executed`

**Trigger.** AIWallet auto-topup fires successfully: a Stripe charge for `auto_topup_increment_value_dollars_cents` succeeds, AND the wallet's `budget_value_dollars_cents` is incremented atomically. Per §4.8.3 Failure Mode #4, mid-charge config disable does not affect this event — completion of a Stripe charge that was already in flight still fires this event.

**Fired by.** Auto-topup worker after Stripe charge confirmation.

**Payload `data`.**

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `wallet_id` | UUID | FK → AIWallet |
| `topup_amount_cents` | Integer | The increment applied |
| `topup_amount_display` | Object | `{"amount", "currency", "fx_rate_locked"}` |
| `stripe_payment_intent_id` | String | ≤ 200 chars; Stripe identifier for receipt linkage |
| `stripe_charge_id` | String | ≤ 200 chars |
| `payment_method_id` | String | Stripe PM id; redacted to `pm_redacted` if subsequently DSAR-erased |
| `payment_method_summary` | Object | `{"brand": "visa", "last4": "4242"}` per Stripe convention; SAFE to expose to Ops + customer |
| `triggering_utilization_pct` | Decimal(5,2) | Wallet utilization that triggered the top-up |
| `wallet_balance_after_topup_cents` | Integer | New available balance |
| `monthly_topup_total_after_cents` | Integer | Cumulative auto-topup spend in current billing period; subscribers can compare against `auto_topup_max_monthly_value_dollars_cents` to predict near-future failure |
| `max_monthly_value_dollars_cents` | Integer | Per AIWallet config |
| `executed_at` | Timestamp | UTC |
| `prior_wallet_state` | Enum | Typically `soft_capped_80` or `soft_capped_100` |
| `new_wallet_state` | Enum | Typically `active` (if balance > 80% threshold) or `soft_capped_80` (if still > 80%) |

#### `billing.wallet.auto_topup_failed`

**Trigger.** Stripe charge for auto-topup fails (declined card, insufficient funds, network error, etc.) OR auto-topup attempt blocked by configuration (would exceed `max_monthly_value_dollars_cents`). Fires after the Stripe-side retry budget per Appendix H is exhausted.

**Fired by.** Auto-topup worker.

**Payload `data`.**

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `wallet_id` | UUID | FK → AIWallet |
| `attempted_topup_amount_cents` | Integer | What the system tried to charge |
| `attempted_topup_amount_display` | Object | `{"amount", "currency", "fx_rate_locked"}` |
| `failure_category` | Enum | `stripe_card_declined`, `stripe_insufficient_funds`, `stripe_network_error`, `stripe_authentication_required` (3DS), `monthly_cap_would_be_exceeded`, `payment_method_removed`, `payment_method_expired`, `auto_topup_disabled_mid_attempt` |
| `stripe_decline_code` | String (nullable) | ≤ 80 chars; Stripe decline_code when applicable (e.g., `insufficient_funds`); null for non-Stripe failure categories |
| `stripe_payment_intent_id` | String (nullable) | Set when Stripe was contacted (even on decline) |
| `payment_method_id` | String (nullable) | Stripe PM id; null if no PM was attempted |
| `payment_method_summary` | Object (nullable) | `{"brand", "last4"}` |
| `triggering_utilization_pct` | Decimal(5,2) | Wallet utilization at attempt time |
| `wallet_balance_at_attempt_cents` | Integer | Pre-attempt balance |
| `wallet_state_at_attempt` | Enum | The wallet state when the attempt began |
| `next_retry_at` | Timestamp (nullable) | UTC; populated when the failure category permits another retry within the current billing period (e.g., `stripe_network_error`); null for terminal categories (`payment_method_removed`, `monthly_cap_would_be_exceeded`) |
| `failure_at` | Timestamp | UTC |
| `customer_action_required` | Boolean | True when subscriber-side workflow MUST surface a "Update payment method" or "Increase auto-topup ceiling" CTA to the customer; computed from `failure_category` |

**Audit elevation.** Two consecutive `auto_topup_failed` events for the same wallet within a billing period elevate the wallet's audit severity tag to `payment_method_at_risk`; downstream `cap_warning_100` / hard-cap events MAY arrive imminently.

### 31.8.5 Plan-Tier Lifecycle Events

The three plan events fire on every committed plan-tier change (§34 plan upgrade/downgrade flow). They MUST be subscribed to by any external system that gates feature access on the customer's tier (e.g., partner integrations that require Enterprise) or that surfaces tier in account dashboards.

#### `billing.plan.upgraded`

**Trigger.** Organization's `buyer_plan_tier` OR `seller_plan_tier` (per §4.2.1 plan-tier split) is updated to a higher-tier value via §32.8 plan-change endpoint OR via Sales-Ops manual provisioning. Fires once per console per upgrade transaction. When an Org upgrades both consoles in a single transaction, two events fire (one per console) sharing a `transaction_correlation_id`.

**Fired by.** Plan-change endpoint handler (customer-initiated path) OR Sales-Ops provisioning worker (Enterprise-tier path).

**Payload `data`.**

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `console_affected` | Enum | `buyer` or `seller` (NEVER `cross_console` for this event; cross-console pooled events use the parent envelope `console=cross_console` only when the change is genuinely indistinguishable per console) |
| `prior_plan_tier` | Enum | Per Appendix J Plan Tiers (split per §34.1.3) |
| `new_plan_tier` | Enum | Higher than `prior_plan_tier` per the per-console plan ladder |
| `change_origin` | Enum | `customer_self_serve` (via §32.8 plan-change), `sales_ops_provisioned`, `automated_trial_conversion`, `commit_signing_provisioned` (when Enterprise commit signing auto-promotes the tier per §4.8.8) |
| `effective_at` | Timestamp | UTC; for self-serve upgrades, equals commit time (immediate effect per §34.5.1); for Sales-Ops with delayed activation, equals the contractually agreed activation time |
| `transaction_correlation_id` | UUID | Shared across companion events when both consoles upgraded in one transaction; null when only one console changed |
| `actor_user_id` | UUID (nullable) | The Billing Admin or Org Owner who initiated; null for `automated_trial_conversion` |
| `wallet_changes` | Object | `{"prior_budget_value_dollars_cents", "new_budget_value_dollars_cents", "prior_overage_cap_default_cents", "new_overage_cap_default_cents", "free_allowance_resets_triggered": Boolean}` |
| `feature_access_diff` | Object | `{"capabilities_unlocked": [capability_id, ...], "limits_increased": [{"limit_name", "prior_value", "new_value"}, ...], "plan_gates_removed": [feature_name, ...]}` — bounded summary of what the customer just gained; useful for activation messaging |
| `prorated_invoice_id` | String (nullable) | ≤ 200 chars; Stripe invoice id for any prorated charge issued at upgrade time per Appendix H |
| `commit_contract_id` | UUID (nullable) | Set when `change_origin=commit_signing_provisioned`; FK → CommittedSpendContract |

**Cross-console correlation.** Subscribers performing per-Org tier reasoning MUST handle the case where two `billing.plan.upgraded` events arrive within the same `transaction_correlation_id` — these represent ONE customer action affecting both consoles, not two independent upgrades.

#### `billing.plan.downgraded`

**Trigger.** Organization's `buyer_plan_tier` OR `seller_plan_tier` is updated to a lower-tier value at the **effective** moment (NOT at scheduling — see `billing.plan.downgrade_scheduled` for that). Fires when the previously scheduled downgrade transitions to active state per §34.5.2 (e.g., at next billing anniversary).

**Fired by.** Downgrade execution worker (scheduled job that runs at billing anniversaries).

**Payload `data`.**

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `console_affected` | Enum | `buyer` or `seller` |
| `prior_plan_tier` | Enum | Per Appendix J Plan Tiers |
| `new_plan_tier` | Enum | Lower than `prior_plan_tier` |
| `effective_at` | Timestamp | UTC; the moment the downgrade took effect |
| `originally_scheduled_at` | Timestamp | UTC; the moment the customer scheduled the downgrade (per `downgrade_scheduled` event); equal to or later than `scheduled_event_timestamp` |
| `actor_user_id` | UUID (nullable) | The Billing Admin who scheduled; null for system-initiated downgrades (e.g., payment-failure-triggered automatic downgrade per Appendix H) |
| `wallet_changes` | Object | `{"prior_budget_value_dollars_cents", "new_budget_value_dollars_cents", "prior_overage_cap_default_cents", "new_overage_cap_default_cents"}` |
| `feature_access_diff` | Object | `{"capabilities_locked": [capability_id, ...], "limits_decreased": [{"limit_name", "prior_value", "new_value"}, ...], "plan_gates_added": [feature_name, ...]}` |
| `excess_data_bucket_id` | UUID (nullable) | FK → DowngradeExcessDataBucket; populated when downgrade triggered the §4.8.10 90-day preservation rule |
| `excess_data_bucket_summary` | Object (nullable) | `{"workspace_count_preserved", "kb_entry_count_preserved", "vendor_count_preserved", "preservation_window_until"}` |
| `transaction_correlation_id` | UUID | Shared across companion events when both consoles downgraded in one transaction |
| `change_origin` | Enum | `customer_self_serve_scheduled`, `payment_failure_automatic`, `sales_ops_decommitted` |

#### `billing.plan.downgrade_scheduled`

**Trigger.** Customer (or Sales-Ops) schedules a future downgrade per §34.5.2 (effective at next billing anniversary). Fires AT THE MOMENT OF SCHEDULING, NOT at execution. The companion `billing.plan.downgraded` event fires when the scheduled downgrade later executes.

**Fired by.** §32.8 plan-change endpoint when the change is a downgrade (which, per §34.5.2, schedules rather than immediately effects).

**Payload `data`.**

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `console_affected` | Enum | `buyer` or `seller` |
| `prior_plan_tier` | Enum | The current plan at scheduling time |
| `scheduled_new_plan_tier` | Enum | The tier that will take effect on `scheduled_effective_at` |
| `scheduled_effective_at` | Timestamp | UTC; per §34.5.2, typically `current_billing_period_end + 1 second` |
| `scheduled_at` | Timestamp | UTC; the moment the customer scheduled the change |
| `actor_user_id` | UUID | Billing Admin who scheduled |
| `pre_downgrade_validation_summary` | Object | Per §34.5.3: `{"warnings_acknowledged": [warning_code, ...], "data_above_new_tier_limits": {"workspace_count_excess", "kb_entry_count_excess", "vendor_count_excess", "storage_excess_gb"}, "feature_access_will_be_lost": [capability_id, ...]}` — surfaces what the customer will lose so subscribers can build retention workflows |
| `cancellation_window_until` | Timestamp | UTC; per §34.5.2 customers may cancel a scheduled downgrade until `scheduled_effective_at - 24h` |
| `transaction_correlation_id` | UUID | Shared across companion scheduled events |

**Cancellation handling.** If the customer later cancels the scheduled downgrade (per §34.5.2), no separate webhook event fires; instead, the companion `billing.plan.downgraded` event simply never arrives. Subscribers building retention dashboards SHOULD treat absence of the downgrade event after `scheduled_effective_at + 1h` as evidence of cancellation. (A future enhancement may add a `billing.plan.downgrade_canceled` event; flagged as Authored Extension future work in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md`.)

### 31.8.6 Committed-Spend Contract Events

The two committed-spend events fire on Enterprise CommittedSpendContract lifecycle transitions per §4.8.8.

#### `billing.committed_spend.contract_activated`

**Trigger.** CommittedSpendContract transitions to `active` state per §4.8.8 state machine (Sales-Ops countersignature recorded; commit pool funded; AIWallet linked).

**Fired by.** Sales-Ops commit-activation worker.

**Payload `data`.**

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `committed_spend_contract_id` | UUID | FK → CommittedSpendContract |
| `commit_amount_cents` | Integer | The annual commit total |
| `commit_amount_display` | Object | `{"amount", "currency", "fx_rate_locked"}` |
| `discount_band` | Enum | Per §4.8.8: `band_10pct` ($25K commit), `band_15pct` ($50K), `band_20pct` ($100K), `band_25pct` ($250K+) |
| `discount_pct_applied` | Decimal(5,2) | E.g., 10.00, 15.00, 20.00, 25.00 |
| `effective_value_pricing_basis_pct` | Decimal(5,2) | Effective per-operation `value_price` after discount; e.g., at `band_15pct`, value-price is 85% of standard |
| `commit_period_start` | Timestamp | UTC; contract activation moment |
| `commit_period_end` | Timestamp | UTC; activation + 1 year |
| `linked_wallet_id` | UUID | FK → AIWallet |
| `linked_legal_entity` | Enum | Per AIWallet.`legal_entity` |
| `auto_renewal_opt_out` | Boolean | Per §4.8.8 |
| `signed_by_user_id` | UUID | Customer signatory; redacted to `redacted` if subsequently DSAR-erased |
| `sales_ops_signed_by_user_id` | UUID | Sales-Ops countersignatory |
| `signed_at` | Timestamp | UTC; both signatures complete |
| `master_agreement_reference` | String (nullable) | ≤ 200 chars; customer's MSA reference number if applicable |

**Plan-tier coupling.** A `billing.committed_spend.contract_activated` event MAY arrive coupled with a `billing.plan.upgraded` event when commit signing auto-promotes the customer to Enterprise per §4.8.8 (`change_origin=commit_signing_provisioned`). When coupled, the two events share a `transaction_correlation_id`.

#### `billing.committed_spend.renewal_due_60`

**Trigger.** CommittedSpendContract is 60 days from `commit_period_end` AND `auto_renewal_opt_out=false` (i.e., the contract is on track to auto-renew unless the customer opts out per §4.8.8). Fires AT MOST ONCE per contract per renewal cycle.

**Fired by.** Daily commit-renewal scan worker.

**Payload `data`.**

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `committed_spend_contract_id` | UUID | FK → CommittedSpendContract |
| `current_commit_amount_cents` | Integer | The contract's current commit total |
| `current_discount_band` | Enum | Per §4.8.8 |
| `commit_period_end` | Timestamp | UTC; the upcoming renewal date |
| `auto_renewal_opt_out` | Boolean | Always `false` at this event (the event would not fire otherwise); restated for subscriber convenience |
| `opt_out_window_until` | Timestamp | UTC; per §4.8.8, the customer may opt out of auto-renewal until `commit_period_end - 60 days` (this event fires AT that boundary) — i.e., this event marks the LAST day to opt out without manual escalation to Sales-Ops |
| `prior_period_consumption_cents` | Integer | The Org's commit consumption in the current period; aids customer-side renewal-decision evidence |
| `prior_period_consumption_pct` | Decimal(5,2) | `consumption / commit` |
| `renewal_proposal` | Object | `{"proposed_commit_amount_cents", "proposed_discount_band", "proposed_discount_pct", "consumption_velocity_recommended_band"}` — Sales-Ops upsell payload; `consumption_velocity_recommended_band` recommends moving to a higher discount band when prior-period consumption suggests the next band would still be utilized |
| `committed_spend_contract_signed_at` | Timestamp | UTC; original signing for context |

**Renewal / expiry events.** `billing.committed_spend.renewed`, `billing.committed_spend.expired`, `billing.committed_spend.renewal_opted_out`, and `billing.committed_spend.decommitted` are authored in §31.8.11 with Appendix C / Appendix G registrations and Appendix F.2 financial-impact retry bindings where applicable.

### 31.8.7 Free Allowance Exhaustion Event

#### `billing.free_allowance.exhausted`

**Trigger.** §4.8.7 FreeAllowanceCounter `quantity_remaining` decremented to 0 for a given (`org_id`, `capability_id`) pair. Fires AT MOST ONCE per (`org_id`, `capability_id`, exhaustion_event); re-arms only if `free_allowance_resets_per_period=true` for the capability AND the billing period rolls over.

**Fired by.** FreeAllowanceCounter atomic-decrement worker (per §4.8.1 Failure Mode #11).

**Payload `data`.**

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `free_allowance_counter_id` | UUID | FK → FreeAllowanceCounter |
| `capability_id` | String | FK → CapabilityRegistryEntry |
| `capability_display_name` | String | Per CapabilityRegistryEntry; aids subscriber-side messaging |
| `quantity_initial` | Integer | The starting allowance per CapabilityRegistryEntry.`free_allowance_quantity_default` (or per-Org override) |
| `quantity_consumed` | Integer | Equals `quantity_initial` at exhaustion |
| `exhausted_at` | Timestamp | UTC |
| `triggering_ai_operation_id` | UUID | The operation that consumed the final unit |
| `next_invocation_will_bill_against` | Enum | `wallet`, `commit_pool`, `wallet_overage`, `hard_cap_reject` (when wallet is hard-capped already at exhaustion time) |
| `resets_per_period` | Boolean | Per CapabilityRegistryEntry.`free_allowance_resets_per_period` |
| `next_reset_at` | Timestamp (nullable) | UTC; populated when `resets_per_period=true`; null when allowance is lifetime per Org |
| `wallet_id` | UUID | FK → AIWallet; aids subscriber correlation with subsequent `billing.ai_operation.settled` events |
| `wallet_balance_cents` | Integer | Wallet balance at exhaustion moment; subscribers building upgrade prompts MAY surface this |
| `console_attribution` | Enum | The console of the triggering operation; useful when the capability is cross-console (`console_applicability=[buyer,seller]`) |

**Upgrade-prompt coupling.** Per §34 PLG flow, exhaustion of a Free Allowance is the canonical upgrade-trigger moment. Subscribers building partner-side upgrade UX SHOULD pair this event with the `upgrade_cta_viewed` PostHog event (§Appendix G; per Appendix G §31.8 update below).

### 31.8.8 Signing, Idempotency, Retry, DLQ

All §31.8 billing-domain events inherit §31 transport semantics with the following clarifications:

- **HMAC signing.** `X-Sourcera-Signature: sha256=<hex>` per §31.6, computed as `HMAC-SHA256(webhook_secret, raw_request_body)`. Per-Org webhook secret with rotation (versioned via `X-Sourcera-Webhook-Secret-Version`); the previous version remains valid for 30 days post-rotation to allow consumer migration.
- **Idempotency.** `event_id` per §31.1, format `evt_{unix_ms}_{base32_random10}`. Persists across retries. Consumers MUST deduplicate by `event_id` (NOT by the `data.*_id` payload identifiers — multiple events MAY legitimately reference the same AIOperation, e.g., `billing.ai_operation.settled` followed by `billing.ai_operation.contested`).
- **Retry curve.** Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve. Billing-domain events have NO override of the curve at the §31.8 level except the explicit Appendix F.2 financial-impact membership; financial-impact events DO get tightened first-attempt SLA, see Appendix F §F.2 below.
- **Dead Letter Queue.** Per §31.6: after 5 failed deliveries, the webhook is marked `failed`; Org Admin (and Billing Admin per §5.2) receive email notification within 1 hour; manual retry available from Settings → Integrations → Failed Webhooks; 30-day DLQ retention.
- **Payload size.** ≤ 256 KB per §31.5. Every authored event payload above is well within budget; the largest authored event (`billing.plan.upgraded` with full `feature_access_diff`) is bounded at ~32 KB even with maximum capability-list cardinality (estimated ~800 capabilities × 80-char id + structural overhead).
- **Delivery ordering.** §31 does not guarantee strict per-Org delivery ordering; the `timestamp` field is the source-of-truth ordering signal. Consumers MUST tolerate out-of-order delivery (e.g., `billing.ai_operation.contested` arriving before its prior `billing.ai_operation.settled` due to retry fan-out). The `event_id` includes `unix_ms` to aid out-of-order reconstruction.
- **Cross-console pooling.** Per §31.8.1: a single Org webhook subscription receives both buyer and seller billing events. Subscribers MAY filter on the envelope `console` field; subscribers MUST NOT assume per-console webhook isolation.

### 31.8.9 Acceptance Criteria

1. Every billing-domain webhook event MUST carry `event_class=billing_domain` in the envelope; consumers filtering on `X-Sourcera-Event-Class: billing_domain` MUST receive every event in §31.8.3–§31.8.7, §31.8.11, and §31.8.12 and no events outside this catalog.
2. `billing.ai_operation.settled` MUST fire EXACTLY ONCE per AIOperation per `pending → {accepted | auto_accepted | rejected}` transition; the late-signal path of §4.8.1 Failure Mode #2 MUST NOT cause a duplicate `settled` event for the same `ai_operation_id`. QA test `webhook_aiop_settled_no_duplicate_on_late_signal` asserts this.
3. `billing.ai_operation.contested` MUST distinguish customer-filed (`contest_origin=customer_billing_admin`) from system-filed (`contest_origin=system_late_signal`) contests; subscribers filtering on `contest_origin` MUST be able to triage the two paths separately. QA test `webhook_aiop_contested_origin_partition` asserts this.
4. `billing.ai_operation.reversed` MUST populate `prior_settlement_state` accurately; subscribers performing balance reconstruction depend on this field. The state MUST be one of `accepted`, `auto_accepted`, `contested`, OR `rejected` (the last only for `reversal_origin=cost_base_correction`). QA test `webhook_aiop_reversed_prior_state_correct` asserts this against every reversal pathway.
5. `billing.wallet.cap_warning_50`, `billing.wallet.cap_warning_80`, and `billing.wallet.cap_warning_100` MUST fire AT MOST ONCE per (`wallet_id`, billing_period); re-arming on billing-period rollover MUST be deterministic (the next period's first crossing fires the next event, not the prior period's residual). QA test `webhook_wallet_cap_warning_at_most_once_per_period` asserts this.
6. `billing.wallet.auto_topup_executed` MUST fire AFTER the wallet balance increment is committed (NOT before); a subscriber querying the §32.8 wallet endpoint immediately after receiving this event MUST observe the updated `budget_value_dollars_cents`. QA test `webhook_autotopup_executed_after_commit` asserts this.
7. `billing.wallet.auto_topup_failed` MUST fire ONLY after the Stripe-side retry budget is exhausted per Appendix H; transient first-attempt failures that subsequently succeed MUST NOT fire this event. QA test `webhook_autotopup_failed_only_terminal` asserts this.
8. `billing.plan.upgraded` and `billing.plan.downgraded` MUST share a `transaction_correlation_id` when both consoles change in one customer transaction; subscribers MUST be able to GROUP-BY this id. **Correlation window.** All events sharing a `transaction_correlation_id` MUST be EMITTED by the producer within 60 seconds of each other (typically milliseconds — the atomicity of the underlying Convex mutation; 60s is the ceiling for post-commit async fan-out). Subscribers MUST be able to close their correlation window at 10 minutes after receiving the first event in a `transaction_correlation_id` group — any event arriving later in that group is treated as an anomaly and logged for investigation (consumer-side guidance; not an enforcement check on Sourcera's side since network / retry can legitimately extend delivery time, but producer-side emission window is the hard guarantee). QA test `webhook_plan_change_dual_console_correlation` asserts same-id arrival in the producer's emit phase; `webhook_correlation_emit_window_60s` asserts the 60-second producer-emit ceiling.
9. `billing.plan.downgrade_scheduled` MUST fire at scheduling time, NOT at execution time; the companion `billing.plan.downgraded` event MUST fire at execution time. A scheduled downgrade that is later canceled MUST result in a scheduled event with no execution event. QA test `webhook_plan_downgrade_lifecycle_two_phase` asserts the two-phase delivery.
10. `billing.committed_spend.contract_activated` MUST share a `transaction_correlation_id` with any coupled `billing.plan.upgraded` event when commit signing auto-promotes the tier. QA test `webhook_commit_activated_plan_upgrade_correlated` asserts this.
11. `billing.committed_spend.renewal_due_60` MUST fire ONLY when `auto_renewal_opt_out=false`; opted-out contracts MUST NOT receive this event. QA test `webhook_renewal_due_60_skips_opted_out` asserts this.
12. `billing.free_allowance.exhausted` MUST fire AT MOST ONCE per exhaustion event per (`org_id`, `capability_id`); the §4.8.1 Failure Mode #11 race condition resolution MUST NOT cause duplicate exhaustion events even when two concurrent operations both attempt to consume the last unit. QA test `webhook_free_allowance_exhausted_no_race_dup` asserts this against a 1000-attempt concurrent stress test.
13. Every billing-domain event MUST be HMAC-SHA256 signed with the per-Org webhook secret per §31.6; signature verification failures at the consumer MUST NOT trigger Sourcera-side retry (the signature is correct on the wire; consumer rejection is a consumer config issue). Consumer 4xx responses (per Appendix F) cause NO retry.
14. Every billing-domain event MUST follow the Appendix F retry curve EXCEPT events listed in Appendix F §F.2 `financial_impact`, which MUST follow the tightened curve defined there. Section body text and Appendix C rows cite the retry class rather than restating timing values.
15. Every billing-domain event MUST be registered in Appendix C (Notification Event Catalog) with its user-facing notification mapping; events with no user-facing notification (e.g., `billing.ai_operation.settled` is too high-volume for direct user notification) are explicitly registered as "Webhook-only; no in-app/email notification" per §31.8.10 Appendix C update below.
16. Every billing-domain event MUST emit a parallel PostHog event per Appendix G; the PostHog event-name field MUST equal the webhook `event_type` field with `.` replaced by `_` (e.g., `billing.ai_operation.settled` → PostHog `billing_ai_operation_settled`) UNLESS the prompt-specified PostHog event names (§31.8.10 Appendix G update) override.
17. Every billing-domain event MUST be deliverable across the full §34.1 plan-tier set (Free / Starter / Growth / Scale / Enterprise per §34.1.1 cell **Webhook Endpoints**) per §31.5; no plan-tier gating applies to the billing event class itself (a Free customer subscribing to `billing.ai_operation.settled` MUST receive deliveries).
18. The §31.8 catalog MUST exhaustively account for every entity-level state-change in §4.8 that has financial impact on the customer; QA review checklist item `billing_webhook_coverage_audit` runs at every §4.8 entity revision and adds new events to §31.8 if a new financial-impact transition is introduced.

### 31.8.10 Appendix Updates Required (Cross-Reference)

- **Appendix C (Notification Event Catalog) — Lifecycle Events extension.** Eight of the 13 §31.8 events are user-facing AND emit in-app + email notifications via Loops.so; five are webhook-only (high volume or system-domain). See Appendix C update at line catalogued in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md`.
- **Appendix F (Webhook Retry & Recovery) — Tightened curve for financial-impact events.** §F.2 authored to override the standard 1-minute first-retry delay with a 5-second first-retry delay for `billing.ai_operation.reversed`, `billing.wallet.auto_topup_executed`, and `billing.wallet.auto_topup_failed` (rationale: consumer accounting reconciliation latency).
- **Appendix G (PostHog Event Taxonomy) — Advanced Feature Events extension.** Five billing-webhook-paralleled PostHog event names: `billing_wallet_viewed`, `billing_contest_submitted`, `billing_contest_approved`, `billing_contest_rejected`, `billing_auto_topup_executed` (each parallel to its §31.8 webhook per Acceptance #16). Plus two product-domain PostHog events with NO webhook parallel — `upgrade_cta_viewed` and `upgrade_completed` — which are product-domain analytics events owned by Appendix G alone (NOT §31.8 webhooks; they fire on client-side UI events, not entity state changes). Appendix G is the single authoritative home for the latter pair; §31.8 MUST NOT register `upgrade_cta_viewed` or `upgrade_completed` as webhook events. See Appendix G update.
- **Appendix J (Controlled Vocabulary Registry).** New enum block `webhook_event_class` (values: `billing_domain`, `product_domain` — extends the implicit single-class taxonomy). New enum block `upgrade_completed_trigger` (values: `evaluation_limit`, `vendor_limit`, `ai_budget_exhaustion`, `opus_gated_capability`; later extended with `solo_envelope_pressure` by §34.5.4 and `m8_value_curve_evidence` by §48.5.8). New enum value extension to `failure_category` enum (auto_topup_failed): see §31.8.4 above.

### 31.8.11 v7.1.1 Billing Webhook Completeness Pack {#31.8.11-v7.1.1-billing-webhook-completeness-pack}

**Authoring Intent.** This pack closes the billing-domain webhook coverage gaps left after the Phase-4d catalog: every §32.8 mutating endpoint emission, every revenue-affecting BuyerReferral / ProTrialSeatGrant / AIWallet / CommittedSpendContract / ContestRecord transition, and every already-referenced billing-domain interim event now resolves to a §31.8 payload family, Appendix C catalog row, Appendix G mirror, and Appendix F retry-class binding. These rows are additive to §31.8.3–§31.8.7; they do not retire the earlier event names.

**Shared payload contract.** Every event in this subsection uses the §31.2 root envelope and §31.8.2 billing envelope with `event_class=billing_domain`, HMAC-SHA256 signing, `event_id` idempotency, payload size ≤ 256 KB, DLQ after 5 failures, and the retry class named in the table. Event-specific payloads MUST include every field in the relevant `Required data fields` cell and MAY add non-PII diagnostic fields only when registered in Appendix G in the same change. Fields containing seller / buyer counterpart identity MUST use the dual-projection rule from the owning entity section.

| Event | Trigger | Required data fields | Retry class | Appendix C / G binding |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |

| `billing.wallet.auto_topup_config_changed` | §32.8 auto-topup configuration commits | `wallet_id`, `auto_topup_enabled`, `trigger_utilization_pct`, `increment_value_dollars_cents`, `max_monthly_value_dollars_cents`, `changed_by_user_id`, `audit_event_id` | `standard` | Appendix C row; PostHog `billing_wallet_auto_topup_config_changed` |
| `billing.wallet.topup_requested` | Manual top-up request accepted before Stripe confirmation | `wallet_id`, `topup_request_id`, `requested_amount_cents`, `payment_method_id_hash`, `requested_by_user_id`, `stripe_payment_intent_id_hash` | `standard` | Appendix C row; PostHog `billing_wallet_topup_requested` |
| `billing.wallet.topup_settled` | Stripe confirms manual top-up and wallet balance is incremented | `wallet_id`, `topup_request_id`, `settled_amount_cents`, `wallet_balance_after_cents`, `stripe_receipt_url`, `settled_at` | `financial_impact` | Appendix C row; PostHog `billing_wallet_topup_settled`; Appendix F.2 |

| `billing.wallet.closed` | AIWallet transitions into `closed` | `wallet_id`, `prior_wallet_state`, `closure_origin`, `closed_at`, `downgrade_bucket_id`, `final_balance_cents` | `financial_impact` | Appendix C row; PostHog `billing_wallet_closed`; Appendix F.2 |
| `billing.contest.filed` | ContestRecord is created and soft credit posts | `contest_record_id`, `ai_operation_id`, `wallet_id`, `requested_credit_amount_cents`, `soft_credit_applied_cents`, `filed_by_user_id`, `reason_category` | `standard` | Appendix C row; PostHog `billing_contest_filed` |
| `billing.contest.decision_received` | Ops Finance approves or rejects a contest | `contest_record_id`, `ai_operation_id`, `decision`, `approved_credit_amount_cents`, `decision_actor_id`, `decision_at`, `audit_event_id` | `standard` | Appendix C row; PostHog `billing_contest_decision_received` |

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Every event named in §32.8.23 AC #21 MUST resolve to exactly one row in §31.8.11 or §31.8.3–§31.8.7; QA test `billing_webhook_catalog_completeness` fails if a §32.8 mutating endpoint emits an unregistered event.
2. Every BuyerReferral transition in Appendix L.2 that affects credit eligibility or Stripe Credit Note state MUST emit the matching `billing.referral.*` event above exactly once per transition; retries preserve the same `event_id`.
3. Every ProTrialSeatGrant transition in Appendix L.3 that changes buyer pool accounting, vendor trial status, or conversion state MUST emit the matching `billing.pro_trial_seat.*` event above; buyer and seller projections MUST redact counterparty-only fields per §4.3.17.
4. `billing.wallet.suspended` and `billing.wallet.closed` MUST fire after the AIWallet state mutation commits and before any customer-facing billing dashboard refresh is marked complete.
5. Committed-spend renewal / expiry / decommit events MUST use Appendix F.2 `financial_impact` only when the successful webhook processing is required for accounting-period close or active balance display, per §F.2 class-membership rule.
6. No event in this pack may expose full payment method identifiers, raw email addresses, unredacted fraud heuristics, or internal Ops notes; hashes and customer-safe status values are required where the source entity contains sensitive fraud or payment data.
7. Appendix C, Appendix G, and Appendix F.2 MUST be amended in the same change as this pack; CI gates `appendix_c_webhook_catalog_completeness`, `appendix_c_to_appendix_g_coverage`, and `appendix_c_to_appendix_f_retry_class_coverage` enforce the binding.

### 31.8.12 Contest SLA and Pricing Table Lifecycle Webhook Completeness Pack {#31.8.12-contest-sla-and-pricing-table-lifecycle-webhook-completeness-pack}

**Authoring Intent.** This pack closes the remaining Phase 1.7 P1 billing-governance webhook gaps for ContestRecord SLA / abandonment outcomes and PricingTableVersion schedule / publish / rollback transitions. The canonical event namespace is `billing.*`; legacy references (`contest.sla_breach`, `contest.abandoned`, `pricing_table_scheduled`, `pricing_table_published`, `pricing_table_rolled_back`) are superseded aliases for historical reconciliation only and MUST NOT be emitted by new runtime paths.

**Shared payload contract.** Every event in this subsection uses the §31.2 root envelope and §31.8.2 billing envelope with `event_class=billing_domain`, HMAC-SHA256 signing, `event_id` idempotency, payload size ≤ 256 KB, DLQ after 5 failures, and the retry class named in the table. Contest payloads MUST identify the ContestRecord and AIOperation without exposing raw customer narrative text. PricingTableVersion payloads MUST expose the published payload hash and version linkage needed by downstream cache invalidators without exposing internal margin notes.

| Event | Trigger | Required data fields | Retry class | Appendix C / G binding |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `billing.contest.sla_breach` | ContestRecord pickup or decision SLA breach per §4.8.5 | `contest_record_id`, `ai_operation_id`, `wallet_id`, `org_id`, `breach_type`, `sla_target_at`, `breach_at`, `ops_reviewer_user_id`, `escalation_target`, `soft_credit_applied_cents`, `correlation_id` | `standard` | Appendix C Billing Governance row; PostHog `billing_contest_sla_breach` |
| `billing.contest.abandoned` | ContestRecord `open|in_review -> abandoned`; soft credit becomes permanent | `contest_record_id`, `ai_operation_id`, `wallet_id`, `abandonment_path`, `credit_amount_cents`, `credit_posted_at`, `resolution_reason`, `abandoned_at`, `audit_event_id`, `correlation_id` | `financial_impact` | Appendix C row; PostHog `billing_contest_abandoned`; Appendix F.2 |
| `billing.pricing_table.scheduled` | PricingTableVersion transition to `scheduled` with future `effective_at` | `pricing_table_version_id`, `version_label`, `effective_at`, `breaking_change_flag`, `customer_notification_sent_at`, `published_payload_hash`, `prior_version_id`, `scheduled_by_user_id` | `standard` | Appendix C row; PostHog `billing_pricing_table_scheduled` |
| `billing.pricing_table.published` | PricingTableVersion transition to `published`; Public Pricing API refresh begins | `pricing_table_version_id`, `version_label`, `effective_at`, `published_at`, `published_payload_hash`, `included_capability_count`, `breaking_change_flag`, `prior_version_id`, `public_pricing_api_cache_busted_at` | `standard` | Appendix C row; PostHog `billing_pricing_table_published` |
| `billing.pricing_table.rolled_back` | Ops Finance invokes emergency rollback for a published PricingTableVersion | `pricing_table_version_id`, `rolled_back_to_version_id`, `rollback_reason`, `rolled_back_at`, `ledger_reversal_batch_id`, `affected_ai_operation_count`, `estimated_reversal_cents`, `ops_finance_actor_id`, `correlation_id` | `financial_impact` | Appendix C row; PostHog `billing_pricing_table_rolled_back`; Appendix F.2 |

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Every ContestRecord SLA breach in §4.8.5, §34.11.2, §34.11.4, and §34.20.4 MUST resolve to `billing.contest.sla_breach`; no live spec section may emit the legacy alias `contest.sla_breach`.
2. Every ContestRecord abandonment transition in §4.8.5 MUST resolve to `billing.contest.abandoned`; successful processing follows Appendix F.2 because the event confirms a customer-facing credit finalization.
3. Every PricingTableVersion `scheduled`, `published`, or `rolled_back` transition in §34.14.5 MUST resolve to the matching `billing.pricing_table.*` event in this pack; cache invalidation, customer notice, and ledger reversal consumers MUST NOT depend on unregistered legacy names.
4. `billing.contest.sla_breach` uses the standard Appendix F retry curve unless and until the event itself becomes required for accounting-period close or active customer-facing balance display under §F.2 class-membership rules.
5. Appendix C, Appendix G, and Appendix F.2 MUST remain synchronized with this pack; CI gates `appendix_c_webhook_catalog_completeness`, `appendix_c_to_appendix_g_coverage`, and `appendix_c_to_appendix_f_retry_class_coverage` enforce the binding.

## 31.9 CRM Sync (Salesforce, HubSpot, Dynamics, Pipedrive) {#31.9-crm-sync-(salesforce,-hubspot,-dynamics,-pipedrive)}

**Authoring Intent.** §31.9 operationalizes Summary §6.18 as the authoritative Seller-Console CRM-sync surface: bidirectional handoff between Sourcera Marketplace activity and the Seller's CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Pipedrive). Replaces the loose "vendor bidirectional sync" bullet in Summary §6.19 for all CRM-provider flows; Summary §6.19 retains responsibility for non-CRM integrations (Jira, Linear, Asana, Azure DevOps, Slack/Teams). Plan-tier gating follows §34.1.2 row "CRM Sync" (Growth+ Included; Scale adds field-map customization; Enterprise adds custom RevOps). All webhook events authored here inherit §31.1–§31.6 transport semantics (HMAC-SHA256, `event_id`, Appendix F retry curve, DLQ after 5 failures, ≤256 KB payload). This section is the single authoritative home for CRM Sync connection entities, field-mapping semantics, routing rules, account-matching algorithm, activity-payload catalog, failure queue, OAuth-setup UX, and customer-facing API surface.

**Source authority.** `Sourcera_Master_Summary.md` Summary §6.18 (feature scope), Summary §6.19 (existing Salesforce bidirectional footprint — superseded for all CRM flows by §31.9), `Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy.md` §6/§7/§8 (plan-tier gating), §4.5.2 (EOI as trigger source), §27.9 (SellerSignal as trigger source), §4.4.17 GhostBidImport, §7 Bid Workspace (bid-closed as trigger source). Conflict log: §31.8 (Billing-Domain Webhook Catalog) occupies numbering slot `§31.8`; the integration-program task named "§31.8 CRM Sync" is numbered **§31.9** in the spec to avoid the conflict; documented in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Numbering Conflicts`.

### 31.9.1 Scope & Cross-References {#31.9.1-scope-&-cross-references}

| Concern | Authoritative Source | §31.9 Role |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Supported CRM providers | §31.9.3 `crm_provider` enum (Appendix J) | Authored; limited to Salesforce, HubSpot, Dynamics 365, Pipedrive in v7.0.0 |
| Plan-tier gating (Included vs field-map customization vs custom RevOps) | §34.1.2 row "CRM Sync" | Cited; never restated |
| OAuth credentials storage | §6.8 (secrets management); §6.5 (per-Org encryption) | Cited; §31.9.11 walks through per-provider OAuth setup |
| Activity triggering events | §4.5.2 EOI, §27.9 SellerSignal, §7 Bid Workspace lifecycle, §16 Q&A, §4.4.17 GhostBidImport | Consumed; §31.9.8 catalogues activity kinds |
| Webhook transport | §31.1–§31.6 | Inherited; events carry `event_class=crm_sync_domain` (new; Appendix J extension) |
| Vendor bidirectional Salesforce sync from Summary §6.19 | Summary §6.19 (loose) | Superseded by §31.9 for CRM-provider flows; non-CRM exports (Jira, Linear, Asana, Azure DevOps, Slack/Teams) retain their Summary §6.19 treatment |
| Dual-Console Firewall | §7.2 | CRM Sync is Seller-Console-scoped; buyer-console CRM connections forbidden |
| Data residency | §6.8; §40.2 | OAuth tokens stored per Org residency; cross-residency CRM push requires explicit policy flag |
| DSAR right-to-erasure | §6.8.5; §27.9.11 | A buyer user erased upstream cascades to CRM Activity redaction per §31.9.9 |
| Billing | §34.1.2; §4.8 | CRM Sync is plan-feature-included (not per-operation billed); aggregation operations run under `crm_sync_aggregation` capability (platform-owned, cross-Org-free) |

### 31.9.2 CRMSyncConnection (Seller-Console-Scoped) {#31.9.2-crmsyncconnection}

**Authoring Intent.** The single authoritative record of an active OAuth connection between a Seller Org and one external CRM provider. One Seller Org MAY hold at most one active connection per `crm_provider`; re-auth rotates the token in place (`token_rotated_at`), it does NOT create a new row. Connection lifecycle is explicit state-machine-driven.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Organization | Seller Org |
| `console` | Enum | Always `seller` | Firewall assertion |
| `crm_provider` | Enum | See Appendix J `crm_provider`: `salesforce`, `hubspot`, `dynamics_365`, `pipedrive` | — |
| `crm_instance_domain` | String | 3–255 chars; validated per-provider (e.g., `*.my.salesforce.com`, `*.pipedrive.com`, `<portal>.hubspot.com`, `*.crm.dynamics.com` region-prefixed) | For Salesforce sandboxes, matches `*.my.sandbox.salesforce.com`; the `is_sandbox` flag is set accordingly |
| `is_sandbox` | Boolean | Default `false` | Sandboxes supported but rate-limited lower; activity-write behavior differs per provider (see §31.9.11) |
| `connection_state` | Enum | See Appendix J `crm_sync_connection_state`: `oauth_pending`, `active`, `paused_token_expired`, `paused_api_rate_limit`, `paused_schema_mismatch`, `paused_manual`, `revoked`, `disconnected` | Default `oauth_pending` on create; lifecycle in §31.9.3 |
| `oauth_access_token_ciphertext` | String | ≤ 8 KB ciphertext; AES-256-GCM per §6.8 | Rotated on refresh; NEVER exposed in API responses |
| `oauth_refresh_token_ciphertext` | String | ≤ 8 KB ciphertext; AES-256-GCM | Rotated on refresh |
| `oauth_token_expires_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | Expected expiry; refresh worker wakes up at `expires_at - 10 min` |
| `oauth_scope_granted` | Array\[String\] | Per-provider scope strings | Snapshotted at OAuth complete; re-prompt required if scope drifts |
| `oauth_scope_required` | Array\[String\] | Per-provider required-scope list | The §31.9.11 minimum scope set; missing scopes trigger `paused_manual` with `pause_reason='oauth_scope_insufficient'` |
| `token_rotated_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | Stamped on every successful refresh |
| `api_user_identity` | String | 3–255 chars | The CRM user or integration-user identity the OAuth token represents; stamped at connection create; required for audit in the Seller Console |
| `residency_region` | Enum | Per Appendix J `market_intel_residency_scope` reused | The residency region of the connected CRM instance (affects where activity records may be pushed — cross-residency pushes require policy acknowledgment) |
| `pause_reason` | Enum | See Appendix J `crm_sync_pause_reason`: `oauth_token_expired`, `oauth_refresh_failed`, `oauth_scope_insufficient`, `api_rate_limit_sustained`, `schema_mismatch`, `residency_policy_conflict`, `ops_forced_pause`, `seller_manual_pause`; nullable | Required when `connection_state LIKE 'paused_%'` |
| `pause_since_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | Pause-SLA tracking |
| `last_successful_activity_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | Monitoring indicator |
| `last_failed_activity_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | Monitoring indicator |
| `connection_health_score` | Decimal | 0.0–1.0 | Rolling 24h: `successful_activities / (successful + failed)`; surfaced in Seller Console "CRM Health" widget |
| `total_activities_pushed_7d` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Observability counter |
| `total_activities_failed_7d` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Observability counter |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Seller User ID; `seller_org_admin` or `org_owner` | Role-checked at create |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Seller User ID | — |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete; `connection_state` MUST be `disconnected` before soft delete |

**Scope Isolation.** Seller-console only. Cross-console read attempts return `dual_console_firewall_violation`. Reads gated by `seller_org_admin`, `org_owner`, OR the Integrations Admin role (authored extension per §31.9.11 — role registered in Appendix J as `seller_integrations_admin`).

**Indexes.** `(org_id, crm_provider)` UNIQUE partial on `deleted_at IS NULL AND connection_state != 'revoked'`; `(connection_state, updated_at DESC)` for health sweeps; `(oauth_token_expires_at)` partial on `connection_state='active'` for the refresh worker.

**Retention.** Org-life + 7 years (audit alignment). `oauth_access_token_ciphertext` and `oauth_refresh_token_ciphertext` are zeroed on `connection_state=revoked` (tokens destroyed; row retained for audit with ciphertext fields set to explicit `"DESTROYED_ON_REVOKE"` sentinel).

### 31.9.3 CRMSyncConnection State Machine {#31.9.3-crmsyncconnection-state-machine}

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (create) | `oauth_pending` | `POST /crm-sync-connections` | OAuth redirect URL issued | Row exists but tokens null; 30-minute timeout |
| `oauth_pending` | `active` | OAuth callback success | Token exchange succeeded; required scopes granted | Sets `oauth_*`, `api_user_identity` |
| `oauth_pending` | `revoked` | OAuth callback failure OR timeout | User declined OR 30-min elapsed | Terminal from `oauth_pending`; new connection requires new row |
| `active` | `paused_token_expired` | Refresh worker detects `oauth_token_expires_at < now()` AND refresh call fails | Auto-transition; `pause_reason='oauth_token_expired'` or `oauth_refresh_failed` | Seller notified via in-app banner + email |
| `active` | `paused_api_rate_limit` | ≥ 5 consecutive `crm_provider_rate_limited` errors in 15 minutes | Rate-limit backoff triggered per provider | Auto-resume via backoff timer OR seller manual override |
| `active` | `paused_schema_mismatch` | CRM schema introspection shows a required mapped field is missing OR has incompatible type | Per-provider schema check runs hourly + on every write | `pause_reason='schema_mismatch'`; seller re-maps in UI |
| `active` | `paused_manual` | Seller `PATCH .../pause` | Seller-initiated | `pause_reason='seller_manual_pause'` |
| `active` | `paused_manual` | Ops `POST /ops/crm-sync-connections/:id/force-pause` | Ops force pause | `pause_reason='ops_forced_pause'`; dual sign-off for Enterprise customer |
| `paused_*` | `active` | Seller `PATCH .../resume` OR refresh worker re-auth success OR rate-limit backoff expiry | Only the machine that entered the pause may auto-resume; `paused_manual` with `pause_reason='ops_forced_pause'` requires Ops release | — |
| `active` OR `paused_*` | `revoked` | Seller `PATCH .../disconnect` OR Ops force-revoke OR token-revoked-externally detection | Zeros ciphertext fields; emits `seller.crm_sync.connection_revoked` | Terminal |
| `revoked` | (no path) | — | Terminal | Reconnection requires new row |
| `revoked` | `disconnected` | Soft-delete worker | Only after 30-day `revoked` quarantine | Formalizes deletion for Org audit exports |
