**SLA.** Time-to-restore from `paused_token_expired` on successful seller re-auth: < 60 seconds. Time-to-pause on external token revocation (detected via failed API call): < 15 minutes. Alert fires if `pause_since_at > 7d` on any non-`paused_manual` pause.

### 31.9.4 CRMFieldMapping (Seller-Console-Scoped) {#31.9.4-crmfieldmapping}

**Authoring Intent.** Controls how Sourcera entity fields project into CRM object fields. Default mapping ships per-provider (§31.9.11); Seller-customized mappings require plan ≥ seller_scale per §34.1.2. Each row maps one Sourcera source field to one CRM target field, with direction and transform.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `crm_sync_connection_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → CRMSyncConnection | Parent |
| `sourcera_entity_kind` | Enum | See Appendix J `crm_sync_sourcera_entity_kind`: `eoi_record`, `seller_signal`, `bid_workspace`, `ghost_bid_import`, `marketplace_proactive_offer`, `qa_thread`, `marketplace_review` | The source Sourcera entity |
| `sourcera_field_path` | String | 3–255 chars; dotted path (e.g., `eoi_record.estimated_contract_value_cents`) | Validated against the §4 schema |
| `crm_object_kind` | Enum | See Appendix J `crm_object_kind` (per provider): Salesforce `{Account, Opportunity, Lead, Task, Activity, Contact}`; HubSpot `{Contact, Deal, Company, Task, Activity}`; Dynamics `{Account, Opportunity, Lead, Task, Contact}`; Pipedrive `{Organization, Deal, Person, Activity}` | Target CRM object |
| `crm_field_path` | String | 3–255 chars; provider-native (e.g., Salesforce `Opportunity.CustomField__c`) | Validated via CRM schema introspection at save |
| `direction` | Enum | See Appendix J `crm_field_mapping_direction`: `sourcera_to_crm`, `crm_to_sourcera`, `bidirectional` | `bidirectional` requires plan ≥ seller_enterprise AND explicit field-type compatibility |
| `transform` | Enum | See Appendix J `crm_field_transform`: `none`, `title_case`, `currency_to_usd_cents`, `usd_cents_to_currency`, `iso_date_to_provider_date`, `markdown_to_plain_text`, `enum_mapping_table` | Default `none` |
| `enum_mapping_table_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → CRMEnumMappingTable (sub-resource; authored below); nullable; required if `transform='enum_mapping_table'` | Maps source enum values to CRM picklist values |
| `is_required_on_push` | Boolean | Default `false` | If `true`, a missing source field aborts the activity push |
| `fallback_value` | String | ≤ 500 chars; nullable | Used when source field is null and `is_required_on_push=false` |
| `is_customer_custom` | Boolean | Default `false` | `true` when the seller has customized (plan gate); `false` for platform-default mappings |
| `platform_default_version` | String | Semver; nullable | For platform-default rows, tracks the version; seller customization clones the row and sets `is_customer_custom=true` |
| `plan_gate_met_at_create` | Enum | `seller_growth`, `seller_scale`, `seller_enterprise` | Snapshot of plan tier at row creation; used for downgrade-grace handling |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Seller User ID | — |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Seller User ID | — |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete |

**Indexes.** `(crm_sync_connection_id, sourcera_entity_kind, sourcera_field_path)` UNIQUE partial on `deleted_at IS NULL`; `(crm_sync_connection_id, crm_object_kind, crm_field_path, direction)` UNIQUE partial for collision detection.

**Validation at save.**

- CRM field existence validated via provider schema introspection; missing field returns `crm_schema_mismatch` (Appendix I; HTTP 422).
- Field-type compatibility validated against the declared `transform`; incompatibility returns `crm_field_type_incompatible` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).
- `is_customer_custom=true` requires plan ≥ seller_scale (field-map customization per §34.1.2); on downgrade, custom rows are FROZEN (no edits accepted) but continue applying during a 14-day grace; after grace, the rows revert to the platform-default baseline at the next push and emit `seller.crm_sync.field_mapping_reverted_on_downgrade`.
- `direction='bidirectional'` requires plan = seller_enterprise.

**Retention.** Mirror of parent `CRMSyncConnection`.

### 31.9.5 CRMRoutingRule (Seller-Console-Scoped) {#31.9.5-crmroutingrule}

**Authoring Intent.** Rules that decide WHICH CRM target object an incoming Sourcera event maps to (e.g., "EOIs with `estimated_contract_value_cents >= 25000000` → SFDC Opportunity with Stage=Prospecting; else → SFDC Lead"). Rules are ordered (first-match-wins). Default platform rules ship per-provider (§31.9.11); customer-custom rules gated per §34.1.2.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `crm_sync_connection_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → CRMSyncConnection | Parent |
| `rule_kind` | Enum | See Appendix J `crm_routing_rule_kind`: `object_kind_selection`, `account_routing`, `owner_routing`, `stage_or_status_assignment`, `custom_tagging` | The decision dimension |
| `sourcera_entity_kind` | Enum | Per `crm_sync_sourcera_entity_kind` | — |
| `predicate_json` | JSON | ≤ 8 KB; validated against a restricted predicate grammar (field-path, operator, literal) | E.g., `{"field":"estimated_contract_value_cents","operator":">=","value":25000000}` |
| `action_json` | JSON | ≤ 4 KB; per-`rule_kind` shape | E.g., `{"crm_object_kind":"Opportunity","crm_initial_stage":"Prospecting"}` |
| `priority` | Integer | 0–10000; lower = higher priority | First-match-wins; ties resolved by `created_at` |
| `is_enabled` | Boolean | Default `true` | — |
| `is_customer_custom` | Boolean | Default `false` | `true` gated by plan ≥ seller_scale |
| `plan_gate_met_at_create` | Enum | Same as §31.9.4 | — |
| `audit_fire_counter` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Total fires in rolling 30d; surfaces in Ops diagnostics |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | — | — |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | — | — |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete |

**Indexes.** `(crm_sync_connection_id, rule_kind, priority ASC)` partial on `is_enabled=true AND deleted_at IS NULL`.

**Validation.** Predicate grammar is whitelisted (no arbitrary expressions; no cross-entity joins; no recursion). Invalid predicates return `crm_routing_rule_invalid` (Appendix I; HTTP 422). A rule with `predicate_json` targeting fields not in the current Field Mapping set is rejected with `crm_routing_rule_field_not_mapped` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 422).

**Retention.** Mirror of parent `CRMSyncConnection`.

### 31.9.6 CRMSyncActivityEvent (Append-Only, Seller-Console-Scoped) {#31.9.6-crmsyncactivityevent}

**Authoring Intent.** Append-only ledger of every CRM push attempt (including retries and failures). The source of truth for Seller-side observability, billing audit (CRM Sync is plan-included, not per-operation billed, but operational audit uses this row to reconcile CRM-side record counts), and DSAR cascade.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Auto-generated |
| `crm_sync_connection_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → CRMSyncConnection | — |
| `activity_kind` | Enum | See Appendix J `crm_sync_activity_kind`: `eoi_submitted`, `eoi_acknowledged`, `eoi_approved`, `eoi_rejected`, `seller_signal_delivered`, `bid_workspace_invited`, `bid_workspace_submitted`, `bid_workspace_closed_won`, `bid_workspace_closed_lost`, `qa_thread_posted`, `qa_thread_closed`, `marketplace_review_received`, `direct_invite_offer_created`, `direct_invite_buyer_accepted`, `ghost_bid_import_published`, `account_match_created`, `account_match_updated` | Triggering event; §31.9.8 catalogues payload per kind |
| `source_entity_ref` | String | Polymorphic FK; format `<entity_kind>:<uuid>` | E.g., `eoi_record:7b3...`, `seller_signal:1af...` |
| `source_entity_snapshot_json` | JSON | ≤ 48 KB; snapshotted at activity emission | Immutable; used for replay and DSAR cascade |
| `crm_target_object_kind` | Enum | Per `crm_object_kind` | Resolved via Routing Rules (§31.9.5) |
| `crm_target_object_id` | String | Provider-native record ID (e.g., SFDC 18-char) | Populated on successful `succeeded`; null on failure or pending |
| `crm_target_account_match_method` | Enum | See Appendix J `crm_account_match_method`: `domain_exact`, `name_exact`, `name_fuzzy_high_confidence`, `name_fuzzy_low_confidence_needs_confirmation`, `no_match_created_new`, `no_match_hold_for_review` | §31.9.7 algorithm output |
| `crm_target_account_id` | String | Provider-native Account/Organization record ID; nullable if account was held for review | Populated on successful match or create |
| `activity_state` | Enum | See Appendix J `crm_sync_activity_state`: `pending`, `in_flight`, `succeeded`, `failed_retryable`, `failed_permanent`, `dead_lettered`, `redacted_by_dsar` | Lifecycle. Review-queue holds are represented by `activity_state='failed_retryable'` plus review-required `failure_category` and null `retry_after_at` until human resolution. |
| `attempt_count` | Integer | ≥ 1; ≤ 5 (post-5 → `dead_lettered`) | Appendix F retry curve |
| `first_attempted_at` | Timestamp | UTC | First push attempt |
| `last_attempted_at` | Timestamp | UTC | Most recent attempt |
| `accepted_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | CRM returned 2xx; populated on `activity_state='succeeded'` |
| `failure_category` | Enum | See Appendix J `crm_sync_failure_category`: `crm_provider_5xx`, `crm_provider_429_rate_limit`, `crm_oauth_token_expired`, `crm_oauth_scope_insufficient`, `crm_schema_mismatch`, `crm_required_field_missing`, `crm_routing_rule_evaluation_failed`, `crm_account_match_ambiguous`, `crm_payload_too_large`, `crm_field_type_incompatible`, `crm_residency_region_mismatch`, `unknown_error`; nullable | Populated on failure; drives retry vs DLQ decision |
| `failure_detail_json` | JSON | ≤ 16 KB; nullable | Provider error body snapshot |
| `retry_after_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | Next retry scheduled time per Appendix F |
| `dead_letter_queued_at` | Timestamp | UTC; nullable | Stamped on `dead_lettered` |
| `residency_region_at_push` | Enum | Per `market_intel_residency_scope` | Residency region of the target CRM at push time — retained for cross-residency audit |
| `routing_rule_id_fired` | UUID (FK) | FK → CRMRoutingRule; nullable | The rule that resolved the target object |
| `field_mapping_version_applied` | String | Semver | Snapshot of field-mapping bundle version used |
| `audit_event_id` | UUID (FK) | FK → Audit Event | — |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated on state transition | UTC |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | NOT used for normal flow; reserved for Ops emergency redaction |

**Scope Isolation.** Seller-console-scoped; UNIQUE across (crm_sync_connection_id, activity_kind, source_entity_ref, attempt_count) to prevent duplicate-retry inserts. Seller reads their own connection's activity log; cross-Org reads forbidden.

**Indexes.** `(crm_sync_connection_id, activity_state, last_attempted_at DESC)`; `(activity_state, retry_after_at)` partial on `failed_retryable` for the retry worker; `(failure_category, created_at DESC)` partial on `failed_*` for Ops analytics; `(source_entity_ref)` for reverse lookup on DSAR cascade.

**Retention.** Activity rows retained 90 days post-`succeeded`/`failed_permanent`/`dead_lettered` for operational diagnostics; then aggregated to a monthly rollup and deleted. DSAR right-to-erasure on a buyer user cascades as follows: activity rows whose `source_entity_snapshot_json` references the erased user have their `source_entity_snapshot_json` redacted (specific PII keys set to `"redacted"`), `activity_state → redacted_by_dsar`, and the CRM-side record is NOT automatically deleted (the Seller's CRM is a downstream data controller; Sourcera notifies the Seller's Integrations Admin via `seller.crm_sync.dsar_cascade_notification` to perform downstream erasure). Rows with `activity_state=redacted_by_dsar` retain metadata for audit but not PII.

### 31.9.7 Account Matching Algorithm {#31.9.7-account-matching-algorithm}

**Authoring Intent.** For every activity that targets a buyer-identified record (EOI, Direct Invite acceptance, Bid Workspace invite), Sourcera MUST resolve the buyer Org to a CRM Account. Zero-match creates a new CRM Account only if the Seller's `auto_create_account_on_no_match` preference is set; otherwise the activity enters a review hold (`activity_state='failed_retryable'`, `failure_category='crm_account_match_ambiguous'`, `retry_after_at=NULL`) and the Seller reviews in the UI. Ambiguous matches are NOT auto-resolved; the Seller confirms.

**Algorithm stages.**

1. **Domain exact match.** Extract buyer Org's primary domain (from `Organization.primary_domain`); query CRM Accounts by the domain field (`Website` on SFDC, `domain` on HubSpot, `websiteurl` on Dynamics, `url` on Pipedrive). Exact, case-insensitive match: `crm_target_account_match_method='domain_exact'`; confidence 1.0; auto-linked.
2. **Name exact match.** If no domain match, query by `Organization.legal_name` exact match. If exactly one match: `name_exact`; confidence 0.95; auto-linked. Multiple matches at this stage proceed to step 3.
3. **Fuzzy name match.** Run a normalized-edit-distance match (Levenshtein + tokenization: strip Inc/LLC/Ltd/Corp suffixes, case-fold, punctuation-strip). Top-1 match with similarity ≥ 0.90: `name_fuzzy_high_confidence`; auto-linked if Seller's `auto_link_fuzzy_high_confidence` preference is `true` (default `false` — Enterprise customers typically require human confirmation). Similarity 0.70–0.89: `name_fuzzy_low_confidence_needs_confirmation`; activity enters the review hold (`activity_state='failed_retryable'`, `failure_category='crm_account_match_ambiguous'`, `retry_after_at=NULL`).
4. **No-match branch.**
   - If Seller preference `auto_create_account_on_no_match=true` AND the triggering activity kind is in the whitelist `{eoi_submitted, direct_invite_buyer_accepted, bid_workspace_invited}`: create a new CRM Account with `Organization.legal_name`, `primary_domain`, and default `Account.Type` from Routing Rules; `match_method='no_match_created_new'`. NEW-record creation is logged in `audit_event_id` and a `seller.crm_sync.account_created` webhook fires.
   - Else: `match_method='no_match_hold_for_review'`; activity enters the review hold (`activity_state='failed_retryable'`, `failure_category='crm_account_match_ambiguous'`, `retry_after_at=NULL`).
5. **Seller review UI.** Review-hold rows (`activity_state='failed_retryable'` and `failure_category ∈ {crm_routing_rule_evaluation_failed, crm_account_match_ambiguous}` with `retry_after_at=NULL`) surface in Seller Console "CRM Sync → Review Queue". Seller resolves via: (a) explicit match to an existing CRM Account (cursor-pasting the 18-char Salesforce ID OR using a provider-native search widget); (b) create-new; (c) dismiss (activity transitions to `failed_permanent` with `failure_category='crm_account_match_ambiguous'` and `failure_detail_json.resolution='dismissed'`). Resolution triggers a re-push of the activity with the confirmed account.

**Multi-tenant CRM caveat.** Some CRM providers (notably Salesforce with multiple Business Units) surface multiple Account records per actual company. The algorithm treats each record as independent; the Seller's `primary_business_unit` preference (authored extension; stored on `CRMSyncConnection.default_business_unit`) narrows the search scope to the BU. Cross-BU matches are held for review.

**Audit.** Every match decision is captured in `CRMSyncActivityEvent.crm_target_account_match_method` and `crm_target_account_id`. A daily match-accuracy job samples 1% of `name_fuzzy_*` matches for spot-check; Ops dashboard surfaces the false-positive rate; fuzzy-threshold adjustments are governed via C.97 Baseline Assumption Manager.

### 31.9.8 Activity Payload Catalog {#31.9.8-activity-payload-catalog}

The default payload per `activity_kind` is listed below. Each activity MAY be customized per-Seller via Field Mapping (§31.9.4); the defaults represent the universal baseline that ships on every connection. Unmapped fields are dropped from the CRM-side write.

#### 31.9.8.1 `eoi_submitted`

**Target CRM object (default routing rule).** Salesforce: `Opportunity` (new) linked to matched Account; stage = `Prospecting`. HubSpot: `Deal` (new) on matched Company; stage = "appointmentscheduled" (Deal Stage 1 default) or Seller-overridden. Dynamics: `Opportunity` linked to Account. Pipedrive: `Deal` linked to Organization.

**Payload.**

| Sourcera Field | CRM Target (default) | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `eoi_record.id` | Opportunity custom field `sourcera_eoi_id__c` (SFDC convention) | Idempotency key |
| `marketplace_listing.title` | Opportunity.Name | Title prefixed with "Sourcera: " |
| `eoi_record.estimated_contract_value_cents` | Opportunity.Amount | `usd_cents_to_currency` transform; `eoi_record.currency_code` supplies display currency |
| `eoi_record.estimated_implementation_timeline_days` | Opportunity custom `sourcera_implementation_days__c` | — |
| `eoi_record.eoi_submitted_at` | Opportunity.CloseDate (est: `submitted_at + 180 days`) | Configurable |
| `eoi_record.buyer_user_id → User.contact` | Opportunity.Contact (via Account relationship) | Contact creation is a parallel activity |
| Workspace primary category | Opportunity custom `sourcera_category__c` | — |

#### 31.9.8.2 `eoi_acknowledged` / `eoi_approved` / `eoi_rejected`

Stage transitions on the linked Opportunity/Deal + Activity entry (SFDC `Task`, HubSpot `Activity`, Dynamics `Task`, Pipedrive `Activity`) with the Sourcera event timestamp and a link back to the Sourcera Workspace URL.

#### 31.9.8.3 `seller_signal_delivered`

**Target CRM object.** Salesforce: `Lead` (if `auto_create_lead_on_seller_signal=true`) OR `Custom Object: Sourcera_Cohort_Intent__c` (authored extension; installs as part of the Sourcera Managed Package). HubSpot: `Custom Object: sourcera_cohort_intent` (created at connection-active time via provider schema API). Dynamics/Pipedrive: equivalent custom objects.

**Payload.** Aggregate summary from the SellerSignal row (no buyer identity; k-anon enforced per §27.9.7) + `cohort_fingerprint_hash` for de-dupe.

**De-anon upgrade.** If the cohort later de-anonymizes (via `marketplace.seller_signal.de_anonymized`), a follow-on `crm_sync` activity of kind `account_match_created` OR `account_match_updated` links the now-identifiable buyer Account to the prior anonymous-intent record (merge semantics per provider; on providers without merge primitives, the new record is cross-referenced via `cross_reference_to_record_id` custom field).

#### 31.9.8.4 `bid_workspace_invited`

**Target CRM object.** Opportunity/Deal updated with `sourcera_bid_workspace_url__c` + stage advanced to "Qualification" (default). Task/Activity created: "Sourcera bid workspace invitation received" with due date = bid submission deadline.

#### 31.9.8.5 `bid_workspace_submitted`

Opportunity/Deal custom field `sourcera_bid_submitted_at__c` stamped; optional stage advance to "Proposal/Price Quote".

#### 31.9.8.6 `bid_workspace_closed_won` / `bid_workspace_closed_lost`

Opportunity/Deal stage closed; `Amount` updated from final contract value if present; Activity created with buyer-provided feedback (truncated to CRM field limit). `closed_lost` also populates `Loss_Reason__c` from the buyer's EOI rejection reason if available.

#### 31.9.8.7 `qa_thread_posted` / `qa_thread_closed`

Activity record (Task-like) attached to the Opportunity/Deal with Q&A thread URL and first 500 chars of question text.

#### 31.9.8.8 `marketplace_review_received`

Activity record on the Account (not the Opportunity — reviews are Org-level). Attaches review star rating + public snippet; links to Sourcera review page.

#### 31.9.8.9 `direct_invite_offer_created` / `direct_invite_buyer_accepted`

For `offer_created`: no CRM activity (the cohort is still anonymous). For `buyer_accepted`: full EOI-like activity (since buyer is now identified); same payload shape as `eoi_submitted`.

#### 31.9.8.10 `ghost_bid_import_published`

No CRM activity by default (Ghost-Bid imports are internal KB enrichment). A Seller MAY opt-in via preference `crm_sync_ghost_bid_imports_enabled` to materialize a `Note` on the matched Account summarizing the prior RFP context.

#### 31.9.8.11 `account_match_created` / `account_match_updated`

Internal bookkeeping activity; surfaces in Seller Console "CRM Sync → Activity Log" only; no CRM-side write.

**Payload size discipline.** Every activity payload is capped at 256 KB (the §31.5 platform limit). The `source_entity_snapshot_json` field in `CRMSyncActivityEvent` is capped at 48 KB to leave headroom for metadata. Oversize payloads are rejected with `crm_sync_payload_too_large` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 413) and land in `failed_permanent` with `failure_category='crm_payload_too_large'`.

### 31.9.9 Failure Queue, Retry Semantics, and DLQ {#31.9.9-failure-queue-retry-semantics-and-dlq}

**Retry curve.** CRM Sync activities follow the Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve. Financial-impact events (e.g., `bid_workspace_closed_won` with `Amount` on the Opportunity) follow Appendix F.2 `financial_impact` to minimize reconciliation lag in the Seller's revenue-ops pipeline.

**Retry-eligibility matrix.**

| `failure_category` | Retryable? | Rationale |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `crm_oauth_token_expired` | No — auto-pause connection, then retry on resume | Retrying with bad credentials is noise |
| `crm_provider_429_rate_limit` | Yes with provider-provided `Retry-After` header respected | Transient |
| `crm_schema_mismatch` | No — auto-pause connection with `pause_reason='schema_mismatch'` | Seller must remap |
| `crm_required_field_missing` | No | Source data problem; Seller fixes field mapping OR source |
| `crm_account_match_ambiguous` | Review hold — no timed retry until Seller resolution | Human-resolution path |
| `crm_provider_5xx` | Yes | Transient |
| `crm_oauth_scope_insufficient` | No — re-authorization required | OAuth-scope gap |
| `crm_payload_too_large` | No | Field-mapping adjustment required |
| `crm_field_type_incompatible` | No | Seller must remap |
| `crm_routing_rule_evaluation_failed` | Review hold — no timed retry until Seller resolution | Human-resolution path |
| `crm_residency_region_mismatch` | No — requires policy acknowledgment | Ops / compliance path |
| `unknown_error` | Yes up to Appendix F max (5 attempts) | Safe default |

**Dead Letter Queue.** Activity rows with `activity_state='failed_retryable'` AND `failure_category ∈ {unknown_error, crm_provider_5xx, crm_provider_429_rate_limit}` after the 5-attempt budget transition to `dead_lettered` and land in the DLQ. Ops inspects via `/ops/crm-sync/activities/dlq`. Ops MAY enqueue a manual retry (single-shot; resets `attempt_count` to 1) OR hard-delete with audit entry. DLQ capacity per Org: 10,000 rows; saturation pages Ops.

**Failure review queue (Seller-facing).** Review-hold rows (`activity_state='failed_retryable'`, `failure_category ∈ {crm_routing_rule_evaluation_failed, crm_account_match_ambiguous}`, `retry_after_at=NULL`) surface in Seller Console "CRM Sync → Needs Review" with counts visible in navigation badge. Seller-side resolution paths: (a) Explicitly match a CRM record; (b) Create new record; (c) Dismiss; (d) Retry-as-is after correcting the rule or match. Review queue capacity per Seller Org: 1,000 rows; saturation auto-pauses activity emission (new activities queue into `pending` but are not pushed) and emits `seller.crm_sync.review_queue_saturation` webhook.

**Notification policy.** Per-connection failure notifications route to the Seller's Integrations Admin via Pulse Digest (Summary §6.11). Default thresholds: first hard failure of the day → email; 5 hard failures → in-app toast; 10+ → `seller.crm_sync.connection_health_critical` webhook. Thresholds configurable in Seller Console "CRM Sync → Settings → Notifications".

### 31.9.10 Webhook Catalog {#31.9.10-webhook-catalog}

All §31.9 webhook events carry `event_class=crm_sync_domain` (new; Appendix J extension). Envelope per §31.2 augmented with `organization_id` (Seller Org), `console='seller'`, `crm_sync_connection_id`, and `event_id` idempotency per §31.1. Subscriptions are `organization_id=subscribing_org_id` scoped. The canonical customer-facing namespace is `seller.crm_sync.*`; Appendix G PostHog mirrors use the same name with `.` replaced by `_` and carry `source_webhook_event_type` for exact catalog consistency.

| event_type | Trigger | Key payload |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `seller.crm_sync.connection_activated` | New `CRMSyncConnection` transitions `oauth_pending → active` | `crm_sync_connection_id`, `crm_provider`, `api_user_identity`, `oauth_scope_granted`, `created_at` |
| `seller.crm_sync.connection_paused` | Any `active → paused_*` transition | `crm_sync_connection_id`, `pause_reason`, `pause_since_at` |
| `seller.crm_sync.connection_auto_resumed` | Automated `paused_* → active` transition | `crm_sync_connection_id`, `resumed_at`, `prior_pause_reason` |
| `seller.crm_sync.connection_revoked` | `revoked` terminal | `crm_sync_connection_id`, `revoke_reason`, `revoked_at` |
| `seller.crm_sync.connection_disconnected` | `disconnected` terminal | `crm_sync_connection_id`, `disconnected_at`, `connection_lifetime_days` |
| `seller.crm_sync.oauth_token_refresh_failed` | Refresh worker failure (final attempt) | `crm_sync_connection_id`, `refresh_error_detail`, `attempted_at` |
| `seller.crm_sync.oauth_scope_insufficient_at_upgrade` | Sourcera version upgrade requires an ungranted CRM scope | `crm_sync_connection_id`, `crm_provider`, `missing_scopes[]`, `upgrade_version` |
| `seller.crm_sync.activity_written` | `CRMSyncActivityEvent.activity_state → succeeded` | `crm_sync_activity_event_id`, `activity_kind`, `crm_target_object_id`, `crm_target_account_id`, `accepted_at` |
| `seller.crm_sync.activity_failed` | `activity_state → failed_permanent` | `crm_sync_activity_event_id`, `activity_kind`, `failure_category`, `failure_detail_json` (redacted of PII), `attempt_count` |
| `seller.crm_sync.activity_dead_lettered` | Activity transitions to `dead_lettered` after 5 retries | `crm_sync_activity_event_id`, `activity_kind`, `final_failure_category` |
| `seller.crm_sync.account_created` | Account match algorithm creates a new CRM Account | `crm_sync_activity_event_id`, `crm_target_account_id`, `match_method='no_match_created_new'` |
| `seller.crm_sync.review_queue_item_created` | Activity enters review hold | `crm_sync_activity_event_id`, `match_candidates_json` (top-3 fuzzy candidates), `failure_category` |
| `seller.crm_sync.field_mapping_updated` | Seller changes a Field Mapping row | `crm_sync_connection_id`, `mapping_id`, `prior_value_snapshot`, `new_value_snapshot` |
| `seller.crm_sync.field_mapping_reverted_on_downgrade` | Plan downgrade grace expiry reverts custom mapping to platform default | `crm_sync_connection_id`, `mapping_ids[]`, `reverted_at` |
| `seller.crm_sync.field_mapping_schema_drift_detected` | Nightly schema introspection detects provider-side drift | `crm_sync_connection_id`, `drift_kind`, `affected_mapping_ids[]`, `connection_paused` |
| `seller.crm_sync.routing_rule_updated` | Seller changes a Routing Rule row | `crm_sync_connection_id`, `rule_id`, `prior_value_snapshot`, `new_value_snapshot` |
| `seller.crm_sync.review_queue_saturation` | Review-hold rows ≥ 1,000 per connection | `crm_sync_connection_id`, `saturated_count`, `auto_pause_triggered` |
| `seller.crm_sync.connection_health_critical` | `connection_health_score < 0.40` for 15 consecutive minutes | `crm_sync_connection_id`, `connection_health_score`, `error_rate_5m`, `latency_p95_ms_5m`, `provider_5xx_rate_5m` |
| `seller.crm_sync.dsar_cascade_notification` | DSAR right-to-erasure on an upstream buyer user cascaded to activity redaction | `redacted_activity_event_ids[]`, `redaction_completed_at` |

**Volume budget.**

- `activity_written`: dominated by EOI + bid lifecycle volume; at Seller Scale, ~500/day per Org is typical; Enterprise ~5,000/day.
- `activity_failed`: target < 5% of accepted volume.
- `connection_*`: extremely low (< 10/day per Org).
- `account_match_needs_review`: variable; ~5–15% of buyer-identified activities at new-connection warmup; drops to <2% steady-state.
- `review_queue_saturation`: should NEVER fire under normal operations; firing pages Ops.

### 31.9.11 OAuth Setup UX & Provider Configuration {#31.9.11-oauth-setup-ux-&-provider-configuration}

**Entry point.** Seller Console → Integrations → "Connect CRM". Available to `seller_org_admin`, `org_owner`, OR `seller_integrations_admin` (new role, Appendix J).

**Common flow (all providers).**

1. Seller picks provider from a card grid (Salesforce / HubSpot / Dynamics / Pipedrive).
2. Seller enters CRM instance identifier:
   - Salesforce: domain (e.g., `acme.my.salesforce.com`) + sandbox checkbox.
   - HubSpot: portal ID auto-populated via OAuth callback.
   - Dynamics: tenant ID + org URL (e.g., `https://acme.crm.dynamics.com`).
   - Pipedrive: company domain.
3. Sourcera POSTs to the provider's OAuth authorize endpoint with the minimum required scopes (§31.9.11 per-provider table below). Redirect URI: `https://app.sourcera.io/integrations/crm/oauth/callback`.
4. Seller logs in on provider; provider returns auth code to the redirect URI.
5. Sourcera exchanges code for tokens; stores ciphertext in `oauth_access_token_ciphertext` / `oauth_refresh_token_ciphertext`; stamps `api_user_identity`, `oauth_scope_granted`, `connection_state='active'`.
6. Sourcera runs the `crm_sync_schema_introspection` job in background (non-blocking): fetches object and field catalogs from the provider, validates default Field Mappings, alerts the Seller if a required field is missing (auto-pauses with `schema_mismatch` in worst case; typical case: all default fields present and connection stays `active`).
7. In-app confirmation: "CRM Connected" with a "Send test activity" button that pushes a non-persistent smoke-test event to the provider's sandbox endpoint and verifies the round-trip.

**Minimum required OAuth scopes per provider.**

| Provider | Minimum scopes | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Salesforce | `api`, `refresh_token`, `offline_access` | Enterprise + Unlimited editions required for Opportunity-level writes; Professional edition restrictions handled via provider-returned error and surfaced to Seller |
| HubSpot | `crm.objects.contacts.write`, `crm.objects.contacts.read`, `crm.objects.deals.write`, `crm.objects.deals.read`, `crm.objects.companies.write`, `crm.objects.companies.read`, `crm.schemas.custom.read`, `crm.objects.custom.write` | Custom-object scope required for `Sourcera_Cohort_Intent` custom object |
| Dynamics 365 | `https://<tenant>.crm.dynamics.com/user_impersonation`, `offline_access` | Service-principal auth supported for Enterprise customers |
| Pipedrive | `base`, `deals:full`, `activities:full`, `contacts:full`, `organizations:full`, `admin` (for custom-field creation) | — |

**Salesforce Managed Package.** For Salesforce Enterprise customers, a Sourcera Managed Package (`sourcera_crm_integration`, version-tracked in `platform_default_version`) ships the required custom objects and fields pre-installed. HubSpot relies on Custom Object API at connection-active time (no managed package). Dynamics ships a Solution package. Pipedrive uses native custom fields.

**Re-auth.** On `paused_token_expired`, in-app banner surfaces "Re-authorize CRM" with a one-click flow that re-issues the OAuth redirect. Previously-granted field mappings and routing rules are preserved.

**Disconnection.** Seller Console → Integrations → "Disconnect CRM" triggers `active → revoked`. Confirmation modal warns: "Your CRM will no longer receive new activity. Your existing CRM records will NOT be deleted. You may reconnect later."

**Ops-side re-provisioning.** In the event of a stuck connection (e.g., Salesforce revoked the token externally and the refresh worker cannot recover), Ops can force a `revoked → disconnected` transition to unblock reconnection.

**Sandbox handling.** `is_sandbox=true` connections operate identically in the UI but: (a) activity pushes are visually tagged `[SANDBOX]` in the Seller's activity log; (b) activity volume to the sandbox is lower-rate-limited to protect the provider's sandbox cap; (c) default Field Mappings are identical; (d) Seller cannot promote a sandbox connection to production — Prod requires a separate connection.

### 31.9.12 API Endpoints {#31.9.12-api-endpoints}

All endpoints follow §32 patterns (bearer token, fine-grained scopes, cursor-based pagination 50/250). Rate-limit class: `crm_sync_standard` (§32.4.5; 1K/hr burst) for connection/mapping/rule CRUD; `crm_sync_read_heavy` (§32.4.5; 5K/hr burst) for activity-log reads.

| Method | Path | Scope | Purpose | Rate limit | Key error codes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/crm-sync-connections` | `write:crm_sync_connection`; plan ≥ seller_growth | Initiate OAuth; returns redirect URL | Standard | `crm_connection_state_conflict`, `seller_plan_tier_insufficient_crm_sync`, `crm_residency_region_mismatch` |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/crm-sync-connections` | `read:crm_sync_connection` | List Org's connections | Standard | — |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/crm-sync-connections/:id` | `read:crm_sync_connection` | Single connection detail (ciphertext fields NEVER returned) | Standard | — |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/crm-sync-connections/:id/oauth-callback` | (public; protected by state token) | OAuth callback handler | Standard | `crm_oauth_state_invalid`, `crm_oauth_scope_insufficient` |
| `PATCH` | `/api/v1/crm-sync-connections/:id/pause` | `write:crm_sync_connection`; `seller_org_admin` or `seller_integrations_admin` | Manual pause | Standard | `crm_connection_state_conflict` |
| `PATCH` | `/api/v1/crm-sync-connections/:id/resume` | Same | Manual resume (cannot resume `paused_manual` with `pause_reason='ops_forced_pause'`) | Standard | `crm_connection_paused_by_ops` |
| `PATCH` | `/api/v1/crm-sync-connections/:id/reauthorize` | Same | Re-run OAuth flow preserving mappings/rules | Standard | `crm_oauth_expired` |
| `PATCH` | `/api/v1/crm-sync-connections/:id/disconnect` | Same | Terminal `revoked` | Standard | — |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/crm-sync-connections/:id/test-activity` | Same | Fires a non-persistent smoke test | 1/min per connection | — |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/crm-field-mappings` | `write:crm_field_mapping`; plan ≥ seller_scale for `is_customer_custom=true` | Create mapping | Standard | `crm_schema_mismatch`, `crm_field_type_incompatible`, `seller_plan_tier_insufficient_field_mapping_custom` |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/crm-field-mappings` | `read:crm_field_mapping` | List mappings | Standard | — |
| `PATCH` | `/api/v1/crm-field-mappings/:id` | `write:crm_field_mapping` | Update | Standard | Same as create |
| `DELETE` | `/api/v1/crm-field-mappings/:id` | `write:crm_field_mapping` | Soft delete | Standard | `crm_field_mapping_platform_default_cannot_delete` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409 — platform-default rows can be disabled but not deleted) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/crm-routing-rules` | `write:crm_routing_rule`; plan ≥ seller_scale for `is_customer_custom=true` | Create rule | Standard | `crm_routing_rule_invalid`, `crm_routing_rule_field_not_mapped` |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/crm-routing-rules` | `read:crm_routing_rule` | List | Standard | — |
| `PATCH` | `/api/v1/crm-routing-rules/:id` | `write:crm_routing_rule` | Update | Standard | Same as create |
| `DELETE` | `/api/v1/crm-routing-rules/:id` | `write:crm_routing_rule` | Soft delete | Standard | — |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/crm-sync-activities` | `read:crm_sync_activity`; `crm_sync_connection_id` required query param | List connection's activities; filters `activity_state`, `failure_category`, `activity_kind`, `since`, `until`; cursor-paginated | Read-heavy | — |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/crm-sync-activities/:id` | Same | Single activity detail | Read-heavy | — |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/crm-sync-activities/:id/retry` | `write:crm_sync_activity` | Retry a `failed_retryable` activity when it is not in a review hold | 60/hr per Org | `crm_sync_activity_not_retryable` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409) |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/crm-sync-activities/:id/resolve-match` | `write:crm_sync_activity` | Resolve a review-hold row (`failed_retryable` + review-required failure category) via explicit match or create-new | 60/hr per Org | `crm_account_match_ambiguous` (if the resolver's chosen target itself conflicts), `crm_sync_activity_not_in_review` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409) |

**Idempotency.** All mutating endpoints accept `Idempotency-Key`. The retry endpoint is idempotent by `(activity_id, Idempotency-Key)` — duplicate retries on the same key return the original retry's result.

**Ops endpoints.** `/ops/crm-sync-connections/:id/force-pause`, `/ops/crm-sync-connections/:id/force-revoke`, `/ops/crm-sync/activities/dlq`, `/ops/crm-sync/activities/:id/force-retry`, `/ops/crm-sync/activities/:id/force-delete`. Write attempts from customer consoles return HTTP 403 `crm_sync_ops_write_forbidden` (new; Appendix I).

### 31.9.13 Plan-Tier Gating Details {#31.9.13-plan-tier-gating-details}

Per §34.1.2 row "CRM Sync":

- **Free, Seller Starter:** CRM Sync entirely unavailable. API write to `/crm-sync-connections` returns `seller_plan_tier_insufficient_crm_sync` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403).
- **Seller Growth:** CRM Sync included. Platform-default Field Mappings ship out-of-box; customer-custom mappings blocked (`seller_plan_tier_insufficient_field_mapping_custom`; HTTP 403). Custom Routing Rules blocked.
- **Seller Scale:** Customer-custom Field Mappings unlocked. Custom Routing Rules unlocked. `direction='bidirectional'` on field mappings remains blocked.
- **Seller Enterprise:** All of Seller Scale PLUS: `direction='bidirectional'`, Managed Package installation support (Salesforce), custom RevOps integration services (dedicated success engineer; not authored as product feature but referenced as plan-included scope per SPS §8).

**Downgrade grace.** 14 days from the effective downgrade date (§34.12.6 standard grace pattern):

- Day 0–14: Customer-custom mappings and rules CONTINUE to apply; no new custom mappings can be created; in-app banner surfaces "Re-map required" CTA.
- Day 15+: On next activity push, any row with `is_customer_custom=true AND plan_gate_met_at_create > current_plan` is ignored and the platform-default fires instead; `seller.crm_sync.field_mapping_reverted_on_downgrade` webhook emitted with the mapping IDs. No data is deleted; rows are retained for re-activation on re-upgrade.

### 31.9.14 Acceptance Criteria {#31.9.14-acceptance-criteria}

1. A Seller Org's only active `CRMSyncConnection` per `crm_provider` MUST be enforced by a UNIQUE index; a second active connection attempt MUST return `crm_connection_state_conflict` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 409). QA test `crm_sync_one_active_connection_per_provider` asserts.
2. OAuth flow MUST require `oauth_scope_granted ⊇ oauth_scope_required`; missing scopes trigger `crm_oauth_scope_insufficient` and a `paused_manual` state with `pause_reason='oauth_scope_insufficient'`. QA test `crm_sync_oauth_scope_enforcement` asserts per provider.
3. OAuth tokens MUST be stored as AES-256-GCM ciphertext per §6.8 and MUST NEVER appear in API responses; QA test `crm_sync_oauth_tokens_never_exposed` asserts against the serializer.
4. Account matching MUST run in order: domain exact → name exact → fuzzy name; `no_match` with `auto_create_account_on_no_match=true` creates a new Account; otherwise row enters the review-hold representation (`activity_state='failed_retryable'`, `failure_category='crm_account_match_ambiguous'`, `retry_after_at=NULL`). QA test `crm_sync_account_matching_order` asserts against 20 canonical buyer-Org tuples.
5. Fuzzy matches with similarity 0.70–0.89 MUST enter the review-hold representation unless `auto_link_fuzzy_high_confidence=true`; threshold ≥ 0.90 auto-links. QA test `crm_sync_fuzzy_match_thresholds` asserts with 100 synthetic name pairs spanning the threshold.
6. Every `CRMSyncActivityEvent` MUST be append-only; `UPDATE` is restricted to the `activity_state`, `attempt_count`, `last_attempted_at`, `accepted_at`, `failure_*`, `retry_after_at`, `dead_letter_queued_at`, `crm_target_object_id`, `crm_target_account_id` fields; all other fields immutable. QA test `crm_sync_activity_immutable_core_fields` asserts against direct-DB mutation attempts.
7. Retry curve MUST match Appendix F.1 `standard`; financial-impact activities (`bid_workspace_closed_won` with `Amount` mapped) MUST use Appendix F.2 `financial_impact`. QA test `crm_sync_retry_curve_financial_vs_standard` asserts class membership and timing.
8. Non-retryable `failure_category` values (`crm_oauth_scope_insufficient`, `crm_schema_mismatch`, `crm_required_field_missing`, `crm_payload_too_large`, `crm_field_type_incompatible`, `crm_residency_region_mismatch`) MUST NOT trigger timed retry. Review-hold categories (`crm_routing_rule_evaluation_failed`, `crm_account_match_ambiguous`) also MUST NOT trigger timed retry until Seller resolution clears `retry_after_at=NULL`. QA test `crm_sync_non_retryable_categories` asserts each category.
9. Review-hold rows (`activity_state='failed_retryable'`, `failure_category ∈ {crm_routing_rule_evaluation_failed, crm_account_match_ambiguous}`, `retry_after_at=NULL`) MUST surface in the Seller UI review queue; the review queue MUST auto-pause activity emission when saturated (>1,000 rows) and emit `seller.crm_sync.review_queue_saturation`. QA test `crm_sync_review_queue_saturation_autopause` asserts.
10. Downgrade from Seller Scale to Seller Growth MUST preserve existing customer-custom Field Mappings and Routing Rules for 14 days; on day 15+, rows with `is_customer_custom=true` MUST be ignored at push time; `seller.crm_sync.field_mapping_reverted_on_downgrade` webhook MUST fire. QA test `crm_sync_plan_downgrade_grace_14d` asserts at day 13, 14, 15.
11. Connection with `pause_reason='ops_forced_pause'` MUST NOT be resumable by the Seller; attempts return `crm_connection_paused_by_ops` (new; Appendix I; HTTP 403). QA test `crm_sync_ops_forced_pause_not_self_resumable` asserts.
12. `CRMSyncConnection.connection_health_score < 0.40` for 15 consecutive minutes MUST emit `seller.crm_sync.connection_health_critical`. QA test `crm_sync_health_critical_15m` asserts.
13. DSAR right-to-erasure on a buyer user MUST cascade to `CRMSyncActivityEvent.source_entity_snapshot_json` redaction within 24 hours and MUST emit `seller.crm_sync.dsar_cascade_notification` to the Seller's Integrations Admin. QA test `crm_sync_dsar_cascade_sla` asserts.
14. Cross-residency CRM push (e.g., EU Seller connecting a US CRM instance) MUST require `residency_region_mismatch` acknowledgment via `PATCH /crm-sync-connections/:id` with `residency_override_acknowledged_at` set by `seller_org_admin`; unacknowledged cross-residency pushes fail with `crm_residency_region_mismatch`. QA test `crm_sync_residency_policy_enforcement` asserts.
15. Every CRM Sync webhook MUST be HMAC-SHA256 signed per §31.6 and MUST include `event_class=crm_sync_domain`; consumer deduplication on `event_id` MUST hold across the 5-retry attempts. QA test `crm_sync_webhook_signing_and_idempotency` asserts.
16. `/api/v1/crm-sync-activities` cursor pagination MUST default to 50 and cap at 250 per §32; cursor forgery returns HTTP 400 `invalid_cursor` (existing). QA test `crm_sync_activities_pagination_contract` asserts.
17. Platform-default Field Mapping rows MUST NOT be hard-deletable by the Seller; the `DELETE` attempt returns `crm_field_mapping_platform_default_cannot_delete` (HTTP 409). Seller MAY disable via `is_enabled=false` OR override with a customer-custom row of the same target. QA test `crm_sync_platform_default_mapping_protection` asserts.
18. Activity payload size MUST be capped at 256 KB (§31.5); oversize returns `crm_sync_payload_too_large` and lands in `failed_permanent` with `failure_category='crm_payload_too_large'`. QA test `crm_sync_payload_size_cap` asserts.
19. SellerSignal CRM Sync deliveries MUST respect §27.9 k-anon + distinctiveness veto at delivery time; suppressed cohorts MUST NOT push a CRM activity. QA test `crm_sync_seller_signal_k_anon_respected` asserts via a DSAR-driven cohort drop between aggregation and push.
20. A Seller Org on `seller_free` OR `seller_starter` attempting `POST /crm-sync-connections` MUST receive `seller_plan_tier_insufficient_crm_sync` (HTTP 403). QA test `crm_sync_plan_gate_growth_minimum` asserts.
21. `CRMSyncActivityEvent.crm_target_object_id` MUST be populated on `activity_state='succeeded'`; serializer test asserts that no `succeeded` row has a null `crm_target_object_id` for activity kinds that target a CRM record (i.e., everything except `account_match_created`/`account_match_updated` which are internal bookkeeping). QA test `crm_sync_succeeded_rows_have_target_object_id` asserts.
22. Every CRM Sync webhook event registered in Appendix C MUST match the §31.9.10 emitted `event_type` exactly; every Appendix G CRM Sync PostHog mirror MUST either be the dot-to-underscore transform of that event type and carry `source_webhook_event_type`, or be explicitly labeled `analytics_only`. CI test `crm_sync_event_catalog_consistency` asserts.
23. Dual-Console Firewall: attempts to read `CRMSyncConnection`, `CRMFieldMapping`, `CRMRoutingRule`, OR `CRMSyncActivityEvent` from the buyer console MUST return `dual_console_firewall_violation` (existing; §7.2). QA test `crm_sync_dual_console_firewall` asserts.
24. Salesforce Managed Package custom fields (`sourcera_eoi_id__c`, `sourcera_bid_workspace_url__c`, `sourcera_category__c`, `sourcera_implementation_days__c`) MUST be validated via schema introspection at connection-active time; missing fields transition the connection to `paused_schema_mismatch` with `pause_reason='schema_mismatch'`. QA test `crm_sync_salesforce_schema_introspection` asserts against a synthetic SFDC sandbox missing one of the four fields.

### 31.9.15 Failure Modes Addressed {#31.9.15-failure-modes-addressed}

1. **Buyer Org has a Salesforce Account with an outdated domain.** Domain-exact match fails → name-exact/fuzzy match succeeds → `match_method='name_fuzzy_high_confidence'`; Seller UI shows "Matched by name; domain differs" warning allowing the Seller to update the SFDC domain.
2. **Seller's Salesforce custom package is not installed.** Schema introspection at connection-active time detects missing `sourcera_*` fields → connection transitions to `paused_schema_mismatch` → in-app banner prompts package installation.
3. **HubSpot Custom Object API quota exhausted on first-connection bootstrap.** Connection stays in `oauth_pending` → schema-introspection retry backoff → if quota unrecovered after 2h, transitions to `paused_schema_mismatch` with `pause_reason='schema_mismatch'` and surfaces a Seller-facing CTA to retry after quota reset.
4. **Seller's Salesforce admin manually revokes the Sourcera-authorized connected app.** Next push returns 401 → connection transitions to `paused_token_expired` with `pause_reason='oauth_refresh_failed'` → Seller notified → re-auth restores.
5. **Buyer Org changes its primary domain (acquisition / rebrand).** New activities produce `match_method='name_exact'` or `no_match` fallback; existing SFDC Account can be updated via separate Seller-initiated flow (not auto-merged; per Seller's Ops policy).
6. **Concurrent EOI + direct-invite-acceptance for the same buyer-Org-seller-Org pair creates duplicate SFDC Opportunities.** Resolved: UNIQUE `(crm_sync_connection_id, activity_kind, source_entity_ref, attempt_count)` on activity ledger + idempotency keys sent to the CRM provider (Salesforce uses `External ID` on custom `sourcera_eoi_id__c`); duplicate detection is treated as idempotent success and marks the activity `succeeded` pointing to the existing record.
7. **Provider temporarily returns 5xx across all calls (provider outage).** Appendix F retry curve + exponential backoff + circuit breaker: if ≥ 20 consecutive 5xx errors within 5 minutes, the connection is automatically paused (not revoked) with `pause_reason='api_rate_limit_sustained'` OR `pause_reason='provider_5xx_outage'` (new enum value — Appendix J `crm_sync_pause_reason` extension) and auto-resumes after a 15-minute cool-down.
8. **Seller's field mapping references a CRM field they later deleted in the CRM.** Schema-introspection hourly sweep detects the missing field → connection to `paused_schema_mismatch` → Seller re-maps or restores the CRM field.
9. **Seller subscribes to SellerSignals on Seller Growth then downgrades to Seller Starter.** §27.9 delivery preference row's `crm_sync_channel_enabled=true` is silently gated at delivery-time (no CRM push fires); after 14-day grace, `PATCH` clamps the flag to `false`.
10. **Buyer submits an EOI via Marketplace at exactly the same millisecond another Seller also creates a Direct Invite Target for that buyer.** Two distinct `CRMSyncActivityEvent` rows materialize (one `eoi_submitted`, one `direct_invite_buyer_accepted`), both targeting different Seller Orgs; no collision.
11. **DSAR right-to-erasure on a buyer user who triggered 10,000 CRM activities in the past 90 days.** Redaction batch job processes asynchronously; rows transitioned to `redacted_by_dsar` in ≤ 24h; `seller.crm_sync.dsar_cascade_notification` fires with `redacted_activity_event_ids` chunked per webhook payload ≤ 256 KB (10,000 UUIDs ≈ 400 KB, so chunked).
12. **Seller Org receives a Salesforce "Connected App Approval Policy" change that requires re-consent of all users.** Next refresh-token call fails with `invalid_grant` → connection to `paused_token_expired` → Seller prompted to re-auth via a fresh OAuth flow. Field mappings and routing rules preserved.
13. **Residency conflict: EU Seller Org attempts to connect a US-region Salesforce instance.** `POST /crm-sync-connections` returns `crm_residency_region_mismatch` (HTTP 422); Seller must either set `residency_override_acknowledged_at` (requires DPO sign-off audit event) OR use an EU-region Salesforce instance.
14. **Seller's Field Mapping specifies a required field that the source Sourcera entity doesn't have for some activity kinds.** Push attempt fails with `crm_required_field_missing`; `activity_state='failed_permanent'` (non-retryable); Seller review UI surfaces the failure with an "Unset required on this mapping" resolution CTA.
15. **Ops revokes a Seller Org's CRM connection during an abuse investigation.** Ops force-revoke transitions connection to `revoked`; webhook `seller.crm_sync.connection_revoked` fires; Seller UI shows "Your CRM connection was revoked by Sourcera. Contact support." New activities with this Seller as target queue as `failed_permanent` with `failure_category='crm_oauth_scope_insufficient'` when no active connection can be restored.

### 31.9.16 Ops Tooling & Observability {#31.9.16-ops-tooling-&-observability}

**Ops dashboards.** (a) Connection Health: heatmap of `connection_health_score` across all Seller Orgs, filterable by provider; (b) Failure Category Distribution: top-10 failure categories rolling 7d; (c) Fuzzy Match Accuracy: sampled audit of `name_fuzzy_*` matches; (d) DLQ Depth per Org; (e) OAuth Refresh Failure rate per provider (early-warning signal on provider-side auth changes).

**Ops runbooks.** `/ops/runbooks/crm-sync-connection-recovery.md` (authored extension — deferred as a separate artifact; §31.9 authors the runbook's invariants here): (1) Verify provider-side auth; (2) Re-introspect schema; (3) If schema drift, prompt Seller; (4) If provider outage, wait out circuit breaker; (5) If customer escalation, engage provider support. Dual sign-off required for `POST /ops/crm-sync-connections/:id/force-revoke` against Enterprise customer connections.

**Rate-limit observability.** Each provider's per-Org rate-limit ceiling is tracked in `CRMSyncConnection.api_user_identity` context; approaching 80% of ceiling in any rolling hour emits `crm_sync.api_rate_ceiling_warning_80` (new internal metric; not a customer webhook by default — Enterprise customers MAY opt-in). Full ceiling triggers `paused_api_rate_limit`.

**Schema drift detection.** Hourly introspection job per active connection asserts required custom fields are present; drift emits `seller.crm_sync.field_mapping_schema_drift_detected` and transitions to `paused_schema_mismatch`. Drift-detection job is idempotent and retries failing introspection calls per Appendix F.

### 31.9.17 Self-Challenge Refinements {#31.9.17-self-challenge-refinements}

Items surfaced during the hostile-staff-engineer review of §31.9 and authored here to close gaps before engineering handoff.

**31.9.17.1 Activity ordering guarantee.** Events for a single source entity (e.g., an EOI accepted then withdrawn within seconds) MUST be serialized per `(source_entity_kind, source_entity_ref)` tuple. Implementation: the activity-write worker maintains per-source-entity sequence numbers and refuses to dispatch an activity with `sequence_number < max(processed)` for the same tuple; such events are held until the prior sequence completes and are delivered in order. Without this, a retry of an earlier event could land at the provider AFTER a later event and overwrite correct state. Add `sequence_number` (uint64) to CRMSyncActivityEvent field table as an Authored Extension logged in RECONCILIATION.md. The sequence number is monotonic per Seller-Org and assigned at `pending` row insertion; retries preserve the sequence number; dead-lettered events release the per-source-entity serialization lock so subsequent events do not block indefinitely.

**31.9.17.2 Plan downgrade mid-connection.** When a Seller Org downgrades from Growth to Starter (CRM Sync not included), the §34.12.6 14-day downgrade grace applies: the connection remains `active` for 14 days post-downgrade, during which activities continue to flow. At the end of grace, the connection transitions to `paused_manual` with pause_reason = `plan_tier_insufficient` (not `revoked` — preserves reconnection on a future upgrade without re-OAuth). Ciphertext is retained per §6.8 for the full downgrade-grace window. After 90 days of continuous `paused_manual` / `plan_tier_insufficient`, the connection transitions to `disconnected` (OAuth tokens revoked with the provider; ciphertext zeroed).

**31.9.17.3 Customer-custom mapping deletion cascade.** When a customer-custom CRMFieldMapping is deleted AND in-flight activities reference that mapping (pending rows in the failure queue), those activities MUST be: (a) re-routed through the next-higher-precedence mapping that covers the same source field, OR (b) marked `failed_permanent` with `failure_category=crm_required_field_missing` if no fallback exists. The mapping DELETE endpoint returns `409 crm_field_mapping_has_inflight_activities` with the count of affected rows; caller MUST explicitly confirm the cascade behavior via a `?resolution={route_fallback|fail_permanent}` query parameter. Platform-default mappings cannot be deleted (`crm_field_mapping_platform_default_cannot_delete`) to eliminate this edge case for the default path.

**31.9.17.4 Bidirectional mapping conflict resolution — latency bound.** For Enterprise bidirectional mappings, the conflict-resolution strategy (`crm_wins`, `sourcera_wins`, `last_write_wins`, `manual_review`) assumes both sides observe the other's write within a bounded window. The window is 60 seconds for `last_write_wins` (wall-clock precedence); outside that window, the later write is applied unconditionally regardless of strategy to avoid clock-skew-induced flapping. `manual_review` routes conflicting writes to the Review Queue with a dedicated `conflict_pending` state (extension of `crm_sync_activity_state` — logged in RECONCILIATION.md).

**31.9.17.5 Review Queue saturation backpressure lift.** §31.9.9 specifies backpressure engagement at ≥ 1,000 rows (new matches auto-route to `no_match_hold_for_review`). Lift behavior: backpressure is LIFTED when the queue depth drops below 800 (hysteresis band). Without hysteresis, rapid toggle at the 1,000 threshold would cause alert storms. Hysteresis threshold added as an Authored Extension to §31.9.9.

**31.9.17.6 OAuth scope upgrade at Sourcera version upgrade.** When a Sourcera version upgrade introduces a mapping requiring a scope not currently granted, the connection MUST remain `active` for 30 days with a non-blocking warning; only after 30 days of unacknowledged insufficient-scope warnings does the connection transition to `paused_oauth_scope_insufficient` (extension of `crm_sync_pause_reason` — logged in RECONCILIATION.md). Rationale: forcing immediate re-OAuth on every version upgrade erodes customer trust; a 30-day grace with escalating notification cadence (daily → hourly in the last 72h) is operationally realistic.

**31.9.17.7 Provider 5xx outage backoff caps.** When provider returns sustained 5xx for > 10 minutes, the connection transitions to `paused_provider_5xx_outage` (per state machine). Auto-resume attempts use a quadratic backoff: 1min → 5min → 15min → 30min → 60min capped at 60min thereafter. Without a cap, Sourcera could overwhelm a recovering provider during a multi-hour outage. Auto-resume attempts are coordinated across all Seller Orgs on the same provider via a shared circuit-breaker: if 50% of active connections on a provider are simultaneously in `paused_provider_5xx_outage`, all auto-resume attempts are gated to a single probe connection until the circuit closes.

## 31.10 Webhook Secret Rotation {#31.10-webhook-secret-rotation}

**Authoring Intent.** Webhook signing secrets are Org-scoped security credentials. Rotation applies uniformly to every webhook event class (`billing_domain`, `crm_sync_domain`, `marketplace_signals_domain`, `marketplace_discovery_domain`, `internal_comment_domain`, `growth_domain`, `product_domain`, `ops_console_domain`, and future Appendix J `webhook_event_class` values). The billing-domain note in §31.8.8 is an instance of this root contract, not a special-case policy.

**Secret version model.**

| Field / concept | Contract |
| :---- | :---- |
| Active secret | Exactly one active secret version signs new deliveries for an Org. |
| Previous secret | At most one previous version remains valid during the 30-day overlap window after rotation. |
| Header binding | Every delivery carries `X-Sourcera-Webhook-Secret-Version`; consumers verify the matching secret version before processing. |
| Secret display | The new plaintext secret is returned exactly once in the rotation response and is never persisted in plaintext. UI shows it once, then only shows version, created_at, and last_used_at. |
| Storage | AES-256-GCM ciphertext per §6.8; secret material is excluded from logs, AuditEvent metadata, PostHog, and webhooks. |

**Rotation API.**

| Contract field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Method / path | `POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/webhook-secret/rotate` |
| Auth scope | `admin:integrations`; caller must hold `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `seller_integrations_admin`, or `billing_admin` on `org_id` |
| Rate-limit class | `standard_authenticated_per_org` plus endpoint sublimit: 5 rotations / Org / 24h |
| Request schema | `{ "rotation_reason": "scheduled" \| "suspected_compromise" \| "staff_departure" \| "vendor_required" \| "ops_forced", "overlap_days": 30, "notify_recipients": true }` |
| Response schema | `{ "secret_version": integer, "webhook_secret_once": string, "previous_secret_valid_until": timestamp, "created_at": timestamp }` |
| Idempotency | `Idempotency-Key` REQUIRED. Same key + same body returns the original one-time secret until first successful response is acknowledged; same key + different body returns HTTP 409 `webhook_idempotency_key_replayed`. |
| Error codes | `webhook_secret_rotation_role_forbidden` (403), `webhook_secret_rotation_rate_limited` (429), `webhook_secret_rotation_in_progress` (409), `webhook_idempotency_key_replayed` (409) |

**Manual / scheduled / forced rotation.**

| Rotation kind | Trigger | Overlap behavior | Notification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Manual scheduled | Customer clicks Rotate Secret or calls the API with `rotation_reason=scheduled` | 30-day overlap; previous secret accepted until `previous_secret_valid_until` | Loops.so template `webhook_secret_rotated` to Org Owner, Org Admin, Billing Admin, and webhook owners when `notify_recipients=true`. |
| Suspected compromise | Customer calls API with `rotation_reason=suspected_compromise` | Default overlap 30 days, but caller may set `overlap_days=0` to invalidate immediately | Same notification plus security banner in Settings → Integrations → Webhooks. |
| Ops forced | Ops Security rotates via Ops Console incident workflow | Overlap 0–30 days, selected by incident commander and logged | Customer notification mandatory unless legal hold forbids disclosure; non-disclosure reason captured in Ops-only AuditEvent. |
| Scheduled platform migration | Sourcera rotates secrets due to signing infrastructure migration | 30-day overlap unless Security marks incident critical | Advance notice at least 7 days before rotation when not security-driven. |

**Audit / notification behavior.**

- Every rotation writes `org.webhook_secret_rotated` AuditEvent with `secret_version`, `rotation_reason`, `overlap_days`, `previous_secret_valid_until`, actor, and IP metadata. The plaintext secret is never included.
- Customer-facing notification event `webhook.secret_rotated` is registered in Appendix C when `notify_recipients=true`; PostHog mirror `webhook_secret_rotated` records only metadata and never secret material.
- A delivery signed with an unknown or expired version is rejected by the consumer with 4xx; per §31.6, Sourcera treats that as terminal until manual replay after the customer updates their verifier.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Every event class MUST honor the same `X-Sourcera-Webhook-Secret-Version` header and 30-day overlap semantics; QA test `webhook_secret_rotation_all_classes` asserts across one event from every Appendix J `webhook_event_class`.
2. Plaintext secret material MUST be returned exactly once and MUST NOT appear in AuditEvent, PostHog, webhook payloads, logs, DLQ rows, or support exports; CI gate `webhook_secret_plaintext_no_log` asserts.
3. `POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/webhook-secret/rotate` MUST require `Idempotency-Key`; replay with same key and same body returns the original one-time response until acknowledged; same key and different body returns `webhook_idempotency_key_replayed`.
4. Rotation attempts by users outside `{org_owner, org_admin, billing_admin}` MUST return HTTP 403 `webhook_secret_rotation_role_forbidden`.
5. The previous secret MUST stop verifying immediately after `previous_secret_valid_until`; deliveries retried after that instant are signed with the active secret version.
6. A compromised-secret immediate rotation (`overlap_days=0`) MUST invalidate the previous version before the API response commits.
7. The webhook subscription UI MUST display active version, prior-version expiry, and last-used timestamp; it MUST NOT display secret material after the one-time reveal.

## 31.11 Webhook Subscription Model and Registration Guard {#31.11-webhook-subscription-model-and-registration-guard}

**Authoring Intent.** This subsection is the canonical customer-facing webhook subscription model referenced by §22, §23, §25, §27, §29, §31.5, §31.8, §31.9, Appendix C, and Appendix F. Earlier body sections referenced `POST /v1/webhooks` and a "subscription-registration guard" without defining the entity, API contract, or producer-side firewall behavior. This section closes that buildability gap and supersedes looser references to `/api/v1/webhooks` by binding every public endpoint to the §32.1 `/v1` API root.

### 31.11.1 WebhookSubscription Entity {#31.11.1-webhooksubscription-entity}

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | Primary key | Stable subscription identifier; surfaced as `subscription_id` in API responses. |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | Required; FK -> Organization | Every query and mutation is Org-scoped; cross-Org access returns HTTP 404 per §1.4. |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer`, `seller`, or `both` | Declares the authenticated console context under which the subscription was created. `both` is permitted only when the caller is an Org Owner / Org Admin and every requested event class is cross-console safe. |
| `target_url` | URL string | HTTPS only, max 2048 chars, no private IP ranges, no localhost | Validated at create and on every update. URL changes reset failure counters. |
| `description` | String | Nullable, max 120 chars | Customer label shown in Settings -> Developer -> Webhooks. |
| `event_type_filters` | Array[String] | 1-200 values; every value must exist in Appendix C or the event's owning §31 / §27 / §48 catalog | Specific event subscriptions. Mutually compatible with class filters; an event must match either list. |
| `event_class_filters` | Array[Enum] | Values from Appendix J `webhook_event_class` | Class-level subscriptions, e.g. `billing_domain`, `crm_sync_domain`, `marketplace_discovery_domain`. |
| `delivery_audience_scope` | Enum | Appendix J `webhook_delivery_audience_scope`; default `subject` for customer subscriptions unless an owning catalog requires another value | Abuse-report events require explicit `subject` / `reporter`; Ops-only `ops` is not customer-provisionable. |
| `secret_version_active` | Integer | >= 1 | Version used for new deliveries per §31.10. |
| `secret_version_previous_valid_until` | Timestamp | Nullable | Previous version overlap boundary per §31.10. |
| `state` | Enum | `active`, `disabled_by_user`, `quarantined`, `disabled_plan_limit`, `disabled_org_deleted` | Delivery workers send only to `active` subscriptions. |
| `failure_count_24h` | Integer | >= 0 | Drives quarantine / circuit-breaker behavior in §31.5 / §31.6. |
| `last_successful_delivery_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Operational health indicator. |
| `last_failed_delivery_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Operational health indicator. |
| `last_failure_code` | String | Nullable; Appendix I webhook error code where available | Customer-visible troubleshooting field. |
| `plan_tier_at_create` | Enum | Appendix J `plan_tier_kind` | Audit snapshot only; live endpoint cap remains sourced from §34.1 / §39. |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | Required | User or API-token actor that created the subscription. |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Required | Last mutating actor. |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Required | UTC. |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Required | UTC. |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete; deliveries stop immediately when populated. |

**Scope isolation.** `WebhookSubscription` is Org-scoped and console-context-scoped. Buyer-console subscriptions may register buyer-only, product-domain, billing-domain, and cross-console-safe event classes. Seller-console subscriptions may register seller-only, billing-domain, KB-domain, CRM-sync-domain, marketplace seller-signal, and cross-console-safe event classes. Any attempt to register an event class whose owning catalog is console-restricted against the authenticated console returns HTTP 404 `webhook_subscription_console_mismatch` so the forbidden event kind is not confirmed to exist. Billing-domain subscriptions are Org-pooled by design per §31.8.1 and may be created from either console by an authorized role.

**Indexes.** `(org_id, deleted_at)`, `(org_id, state, updated_at DESC)`, `(org_id, console, state)`, `(org_id, target_url, console)` UNIQUE where `deleted_at IS NULL`, `(org_id, event_class_filters)` GIN, `(org_id, event_type_filters)` GIN, `(state, last_failed_delivery_at)` for quarantine sweeps.

**Retention.** Active and disabled subscriptions retain until Org deletion or customer soft-delete. Soft-deleted subscription metadata retains 7 years when referenced by billing / compliance delivery logs; otherwise 90 days per §40.2 integration-config retention. Secrets are never exported in DSAR; target URL and description appear in Org-level export, not individual user export, unless the user is the creator / updater.

### 31.11.2 Subscription Registration Guard {#31.11.2-subscription-registration-guard}

The subscription-registration guard runs before persisting create / patch mutations and before reactivating a quarantined endpoint. It resolves every requested `event_type_filters[]` value to its owning Appendix C / §31 / §27 / §48 catalog row, resolves every `event_class_filters[]` value to Appendix J `webhook_event_class`, then enforces the predicates below.

| Predicate | Failure behavior | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Event kind exists in the registry | HTTP 422 `webhook_event_kind_unknown` | Body includes unknown value and closest suggestions; no partial subscription write. |
| Event class is customer-provisionable | HTTP 404 `webhook_subscription_console_mismatch` for console-restricted leaks; HTTP 403 `webhook_subscription_unauthorized` for known-but-not-entitled classes | Ops-only event classes are hidden from customer catalogs. |
| Authenticated console may receive the event class | HTTP 404 `webhook_subscription_console_mismatch` | This is the non-leak guard referenced by §13.11 AC #15, §25.7, §50 Ops-event catalog rules, and §M.5 `console_bridge_no_defense_view_event_kinds`. |
| `delivery_audience_scope` is valid for every requested event | HTTP 422 `webhook_subscription_delivery_audience_scope_invalid` | Abuse-report and legal-process events require explicit audience scoping. |
| Plan endpoint cap is not exceeded | HTTP 403 `webhook_limit_exceeded` | The cap source is §34.1 cell **Webhook Endpoints**, mirrored by §39. |
| Target URL passes SSRF and HTTPS checks | HTTP 422 `webhook_subscription_target_url_invalid` | Blocks private IPs, localhost, non-HTTPS, username/password URL components, and malformed punycode. |

### 31.11.3 API Endpoints {#31.11.3-api-endpoints}

All endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer <api_token>` with Appendix J scope `admin:integrations`, or an authenticated UI session whose role is authorized by §5.2 / §5.3 / §5.5 for Webhook Endpoint CRUD. Mutating endpoints require `Idempotency-Key` with a 24-hour replay window. Rate-limit class is `standard_authenticated_per_org` unless an endpoint-local sublimit is listed.

| Method / Path | Purpose | Request | Response | Errors |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `POST /v1/webhooks` | Create a subscription | `target_url`, `description?`, `console`, `event_type_filters[]`, `event_class_filters[]`, `delivery_audience_scope?` | `201 {subscription_id, state, secret_once, secret_version_active, created_at}` | `webhook_subscription_unauthorized`, `webhook_subscription_console_mismatch`, `webhook_event_kind_unknown`, `webhook_subscription_delivery_audience_scope_invalid`, `webhook_subscription_target_url_invalid`, `webhook_limit_exceeded`, `webhook_idempotency_key_replayed` |
| `GET /v1/webhooks` | List subscriptions for caller Org / console | `cursor?`, `limit?`, `state?`, `event_class?` | `200 {data[], pagination}` | `invalid_cursor`, `token_scope_insufficient` |
| `GET /v1/webhooks/{subscription_id}` | Read one subscription | Path only | `200 WebhookSubscription projection` | `not_found` for cross-Org / cross-console / deleted |
| `PATCH /v1/webhooks/{subscription_id}` | Update URL, filters, audience scope, description, or state | Partial fields; state may move `active <-> disabled_by_user` | `200 WebhookSubscription projection` | Same guard errors as create; `webhook_endpoint_quarantined` when state is quarantined and caller omitted `reactivate=true` |
| `DELETE /v1/webhooks/{subscription_id}` | Soft-delete a subscription | Optional `delete_reason` | `204` | `not_found`, `token_scope_insufficient` |
| `POST /v1/webhooks/{subscription_id}/reactivate` | Clear quarantine after customer fixes target URL | Optional `target_url` replacement | `200 {subscription_id, state='active', failure_count_24h=0}` | `webhook_endpoint_quarantined` when URL remains invalid, `webhook_subscription_target_url_invalid` |
| `GET /v1/webhooks/available-events` | Return caller-visible event catalog | `console`, `delivery_audience_scope?` | `200 {events[], classes[]}` | Never returns hidden event classes; unauthorized classes are omitted, not errored. |

### 31.11.4 Acceptance Criteria {#31.11.4-acceptance-criteria}

1. A seller-console caller attempting to subscribe to `defense_view.generated`, `defense_view.regenerated`, or `internal_comment.*` MUST receive HTTP 404 `webhook_subscription_console_mismatch`; response bodies MUST NOT name Defense View or Internal Comment.
2. `POST /v1/webhooks` and `PATCH /v1/webhooks/{subscription_id}` MUST reject unregistered event names with `webhook_event_kind_unknown`; the subscription is not partially persisted.
3. `Idempotency-Key` is required on create, patch, delete, and reactivate. Same key + same body returns the first result; same key + different body returns `webhook_idempotency_key_replayed`.
4. `GET /v1/webhooks/available-events` MUST omit Ops-only, legal-hold-suppressed, and console-forbidden event kinds rather than returning them as disabled rows.
5. Plan endpoint caps MUST cite §34.1 / §39 only. No subscription endpoint may restate a numeric endpoint cap inline.
6. Delivery workers MUST ignore `disabled_by_user`, `quarantined`, `disabled_plan_limit`, `disabled_org_deleted`, and soft-deleted subscriptions.
7. Webhook secret rotation in §31.10 applies to every subscription produced by this model; plaintext secrets are returned only in `POST /v1/webhooks` and §31.10 rotation responses.
