**Authoring Intent.** This pack closes the KB-document and verification-tier lifecycle events that were referenced by §22 / §27 but not fully catalogued as webhook contracts. These events are not billing-domain events; they use the event classes named below and inherit §31.1–§31.6 transport semantics.

| Event | Event class | Trigger | Required data fields | Retry class | Appendix C / G binding |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `kb.document.expired` | `kb_domain` | KBDocument `active -> expired` by expiry sweep | `kb_document_id`, `seller_org_id`, `software_id`, `document_kind`, `expired_at`, `verification_review_record_id`, `replacement_required_by` | `standard` | Appendix C KB Completeness row; PostHog `kb_document_expired` |
| `kb.document.superseded` | `kb_domain` | KBDocument `active|expired -> superseded` | `kb_document_id`, `superseded_by_document_id`, `seller_org_id`, `document_kind`, `superseded_at`, `superseded_by_user_id` | `standard` | Appendix C row; PostHog `kb_document_superseded` |
| `kb.document.archived` | `kb_domain` | KBDocument `* -> archived` | `kb_document_id`, `seller_org_id`, `document_kind`, `archive_reason`, `archived_at`, `archived_by_user_id` | `standard` | Appendix C row; PostHog `kb_document_archived` |
| `verification.tier_downgraded` | `marketplace_discovery_domain` | Verification tier downgrade commits and cascades to seller marketplace projections | `verification_review_record_id`, `seller_org_id`, `prior_tier`, `new_tier`, `downgrade_reason_code`, `affected_surface_counts`, `downgraded_at` | `standard` | Appendix C Verification row; PostHog `verification_tier_downgraded` |
| `kb.export.failed` | `kb_domain` | KBExportJob `queued|running -> failed` | `export_id`, `seller_org_id`, `requested_by_user_id`, `failure_code`, `retryable`, `failed_at`, `residency_region` | `standard` | Existing Appendix C KB row; PostHog mirror `kb_export_failed` explicitly registered by this pack |

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. KBDocument `expired`, `superseded`, and `archived` transitions in Appendix L.5 MUST emit their matching event exactly once per transition.
2. A document-expiry-driven verification downgrade MUST emit both the KB document event and `verification.tier_downgraded`; the two events share `correlation_id` but have separate `event_id` values.
3. `verification.tier_downgraded` payloads MUST NOT expose buyer workspace identities, buyer evaluation state, or marketplace competitor data; `affected_surface_counts` is aggregate-only.
4. `kb.export.failed` MUST carry the Appendix J `kb_export_failure_code_enum` value and the `retryable` Boolean so integrators can distinguish structural failures from transient worker failures without polling §32.9.
5. Appendix C and Appendix G rows for all five events MUST be present in the same change as this section.

## 31.13 Marketplace Discovery Lifecycle Webhook Completeness Pack {#31.13-marketplace-discovery-lifecycle-webhook-completeness-pack}

**Authoring Intent.** This pack closes the Marketplace Discovery lifecycle/cascade events referenced by §4.4.19 PromotedListing and §4.4.20 FeaturedPlacement but previously left as flagged authored extensions without §31 contracts. These events are not the §34.16.7 18-event pricing catalog; they are seller-facing lifecycle fan-out events for eligibility loss, vendor-opt-out pause, and placement revocation. All inherit §31.1-§31.6 transport semantics: HMAC-SHA256 signing, immutable `event_id`, class/version headers, Appendix F retry behavior, DLQ after 5 failures, consumer 4xx terminal handling, and payload <= 256 KB.

| Event | Event class | Trigger | Required data fields | Retry class | Appendix C / G binding |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `promoted_listing.eligibility_lost` | `marketplace_discovery_domain` | PromotedListing `active -> terminated_eligibility_lost` after nightly or synchronous eligibility re-check fails | `promoted_listing_id`, `seller_org_id`, `seller_software_id`, `category_id`, `prior_status`, `new_status`, `eligibility_failure_reason`, `expected_resume_condition`, `unspent_daily_cap_cents`, `transitioned_at`, `correlation_id` | `standard` | Appendix C Marketplace Discovery lifecycle row; PostHog `promoted_listing_eligibility_lost` |
| `promoted_listing.paused_by_opt_out` | `marketplace_discovery_domain` | VendorOptOutRecord cascade causes an active PromotedListing to move to `paused_by_ops`; the event name preserves the opt-out cause even though the entity status remains the canonical §4.4.19 state | `promoted_listing_id`, `seller_org_id`, `seller_software_id`, `category_id`, `prior_status`, `new_status='paused_by_ops'`, `pause_reason='vendor_opt_out_active_for_category'`, `vendor_opt_out_record_id`, `buyer_org_id_hash`, `cache_bust_latency_ms`, `paused_at`, `correlation_id` | `standard` | Appendix C Marketplace Discovery lifecycle row; PostHog `promoted_listing_paused_by_opt_out` |
| `featured_placement.revoked` | `marketplace_discovery_domain` | FeaturedPlacement transitions from `scheduled` or `active` to `revoked`, `revoked_by_opt_out`, `revoked_by_verification_downgrade`, or `revoked_by_abuse_finding` | `featured_placement_id`, `seller_org_id`, `target_entity_type`, `target_entity_id`, `placement_mode`, `prior_status`, `new_status`, `revocation_reason_code`, `vendor_opt_out_record_id`, `partial_refund_cents`, `marketplace_discovery_revenue_record_id`, `surface_rerender_requested_at`, `revoked_at`, `correlation_id` | `financial_impact` | Appendix C Marketplace Discovery lifecycle row; PostHog `featured_placement_revoked`; Appendix F.2 |

**Audience and privacy constraints.**

- `promoted_listing.eligibility_lost` and `promoted_listing.paused_by_opt_out` are delivered only to the owning Seller Org's subscribed webhook endpoints and user notifications. Payloads MUST NOT include buyer workspace IDs, buyer Org IDs, raw buyer names, competing seller identities, auction runner-up values, or any buyer query text. `buyer_org_id_hash` on `promoted_listing.paused_by_opt_out` is one-way hashed with the same opt-out-cascade salt used by §4.4.8.
- `featured_placement.revoked` is delivered to the featured seller's Org and to Ops Marketplace dashboards. Buyer-console and public marketplace subscribers do not receive the raw revocation event; public render paths observe only the removed/updated placement state.
- `featured_placement.revoked` uses Appendix F.2 `financial_impact` because a future `paid_commitment` placement may carry pro-rated refund accounting via `partial_refund_cents` and `marketplace_discovery_revenue_record_id`. `promoted_listing.paused_by_opt_out` uses Appendix F.1 `standard` under the current Appendix F.2 membership rule: opt-out cascade timeliness is a compliance SLO, but successful webhook processing is not required for accounting-period close or active balance display.
- All three events MUST include `source_webhook_event_type` in their Appendix G mirror rows and MUST pass `webhook_payload_k_anonymity_floor` because Marketplace Discovery payloads can otherwise leak competitor or buyer-market intelligence.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Every PromotedListing `active -> terminated_eligibility_lost` transition MUST emit exactly one `promoted_listing.eligibility_lost` event with §31.1 `event_id` idempotency; replays of the same transition MUST NOT duplicate seller notifications, webhook deliveries, or PostHog rows.
2. Every VendorOptOutRecord cascade that pauses an active PromotedListing MUST emit `promoted_listing.paused_by_opt_out` within the §4.4.19 AC #7 cascade window and MUST populate `cache_bust_latency_ms`.
3. Every FeaturedPlacement revocation transition named in the §4.4.20 state machine MUST emit `featured_placement.revoked`; paid-mode revocations MUST include `partial_refund_cents` and `marketplace_discovery_revenue_record_id` when a refund or reversal is created.
4. Appendix C, Appendix G, and Appendix F.2 rows for the three events MUST remain in the same change set as this §31.13 pack; CI gates `appendix_c_webhook_catalog_completeness`, `appendix_c_to_appendix_g_coverage`, `appendix_c_to_appendix_f_retry_class_coverage`, and `webhook_payload_k_anonymity_floor` enforce.
5. Customer-visible payload fixtures MUST prove no buyer workspace identity, raw buyer Org identifier, competitor identity, auction price, or non-recipient seller row appears in any of the three event payloads.

# 32\. The Sourcera API {#32.-the-sourcera-api}

## 32.1 Overview {#32.1-overview}

REST API. Current version: `v1`. Base URL: `https://api.sourcera.io/v1`.

All responses are JSON. All timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC.

## 32.2 Authentication & Rate Limit Headers {#32.2-authentication-&-rate-limit-headers}

Authorization: `Bearer srck_{org_prefix}_{token_string}`

Token permissions: Fine-grained scopes (e.g., `read:requirements`, `write:responses`, `read:scores`).

**Rate limit headers returned on all responses:**

X-RateLimit-Limit: 5000

X-RateLimit-Remaining: 4999

X-RateLimit-Reset: 1712765400

X-RateLimit-RetryAfter: 60

**Definitions:**

- `X-RateLimit-Limit`: Burst limit (requests per hour)  
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: Requests remaining in current hour  
- `X-RateLimit-Reset`: Unix timestamp when limit resets  
- `X-RateLimit-RetryAfter`: Seconds to wait before retry (429 responses only)

### 32.2.1 Console-Scope Disambiguation Header {#32.2.1-console-scope-disambiguation-header}

`X-Sourcera-Console` is the canonical request header for endpoints whose execution console cannot be inferred unambiguously from the token alone.

| Header | Direction | Values | Required when | Failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `X-Sourcera-Console` | Request | `buyer`, `seller` | REQUIRED when the bearer token's §4.2.6 ApiToken.`console_scope` is `both`; OPTIONAL for tokens scoped to exactly one console unless an endpoint-local contract requires it. | HTTP 403 `console_isolation_violation` when the value is absent for a `both` token, not one of the two registered values, or mismatches the endpoint console. |

The header does not grant access by itself. The server first resolves the bearer token and `console_scope` per §6.6.3, then applies endpoint scope/RBAC, then consumes the per-request rate-limit bucket per §6.6.6 / §32.4.5. Buyer-only endpoints such as §10.16.1 `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/advance` MUST declare `X-Sourcera-Console: buyer` in their canonical request shape; seller-only endpoints use `seller`. Tokens with `console_scope = buyer` or `seller` may omit the header only when the endpoint console matches the token's single-console scope; a contradictory header still returns `console_isolation_violation`.

## 32.3 Pagination Model {#32.3-pagination-model}

All list endpoints use cursor-based pagination (not offset).

**Request:**

GET /v1/workspaces?cursor=abc123\&limit=50

**Response:**

{

  "data": \[ ... \],

  "pagination": {

    "has\_more": false,

    "next\_cursor": "def456",

    "limit": 50

  }

}

**Cursor Behavior:** Opaque token. Encode the next set of results. Safe for clients to store and share. Cursors invalidate after 24 hours; clients must restart pagination if cursor expires.

**Default & Max Page Size:** Default 50, max 250\.

## 32.4 Rate Limit Enforcement {#32.4-rate-limit-enforcement}

**Per-Organization Burst Limits (all plans):**

- Soft limit: 5,000 requests/hour. Warning response with `X-RateLimit-Remaining=0`, request succeeds.  
- Hard limit: 10,000 requests/hour. 429 Too Many Requests response.  
- Burst: 100 requests/minute (cannot exceed).

**Per-Plan Monthly API-Call Quotas.** API call counts (non-AI plane) are NOT customer-billed (per §34.4 invariant — API requests are rate-limited, never per-call billed) and use plan-tier ceilings only for abuse-prevention. Plan tiers per §34.1; ceilings below are operational throughput controls and live in this subsection.

| Plan tier (per §34.1) | Monthly API Calls | Monthly Policy Ingestion API Calls |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Free | 1,000 | Wallet-charged via §34.3.4 `policy_parsing` (subject to Free Allowance per §34.1) |
| Starter | 10,000 | 3,000 |
| Growth | 50,000 | 10,000 |
| Scale | 250,000 | Unlimited (subject to wallet) |
| Enterprise | Unlimited | Committed (per §34.1.1) |

Both burst (above) and monthly quotas enforced simultaneously. 429 returned when either is exceeded. AI calls follow §34.3 outcome-based billing and are independent of these non-AI plane caps.

**Per-User Concurrency:** Max 10 concurrent requests per user. 11th request queued. Queue timeout: 60 seconds.

**Rate Limit Enforcement Scope:** Default authenticated scope is per-organization (not per-API-key, not per-user). All API keys under the same organization share the same default quota unless a registered rate-limit class in §32.4.5 declares a narrower scope (for example per-IP, per-session, per-Ops-user, or per-Org-per-Workspace).

**Public Pricing API Rate Limit Class (`public_pricing_unauth`).** The single unauthenticated endpoint `GET /v1/pricing` (§32.8.1) is governed by an independent rate-limit class that does NOT consume per-Org quota and is NOT counted against any plan-tier monthly cap. Limits are per source IP address (X-Forwarded-For honored when the request arrives via the global edge cache):

- Soft limit: 600 requests/hour per IP. Warning header emitted; request succeeds.  
- Hard limit: 1,200 requests/hour per IP. HTTP 429 with `X-RateLimit-RetryAfter` populated.  
- Burst: 60 requests/minute per IP.  
- Edge cache: 60-second public TTL keyed on `(version_label OR "current", If-None-Match)`. Per §4.8.9 acceptance criterion #4, the response `ETag` equals `PricingTableVersion.published_payload_hash`; clients sending `If-None-Match` matching the current hash receive HTTP 304 Not Modified with empty body and the cache-hit does NOT count against the per-IP limit.

The `public_pricing_unauth` class shares no counters with the authenticated rate-limit class. Authenticated billing endpoints (§32.5 Billing list, excluding `GET /v1/pricing`) consume the standard per-Org burst and monthly limits documented above.

**Public Marketplace API Rate Limit Class (`marketplace_public_unauth`) — Authored Extension AE-V72REM-PH45-PUBLIC-MARKETPLACE-RATE-LIMIT-01.** Unauthenticated public Marketplace browse/search and public SellerOrgPage, SoftwarePage, CategoryPage, GuidePage, ComparisonPage, MarketIntelligenceReport, and MarketDemandHeatMapCell reads use the §32.4.5 `marketplace_public_unauth` class. The class is per source IP, does not consume Org quota, does not grant EOI submission, and does not grant Match Score reads. Edge-cache hits with matching `If-None-Match` are not counted. Saturation emits the same rate-limit headers as every §32.4.5 class plus HTTP 429 `marketplace_public_unauth_rate_limited`.

### 32.4.5 Rate-Limit Class Registry {#32.4.5-rate-limit-class-registry}

**Purpose.** This subsection is the canonical API rate-limit-class registry. Every endpoint-level `Rate-Limit Class` cell or prose reference in §27, §31, §32, §48, §50, §51, and future API sections MUST resolve to exactly one row below and one Appendix J `api_rate_limit_class` value. Section-local prose MAY add endpoint-specific sublimits, but it MUST NOT introduce an unregistered class name.

**Headers.** All classes emit `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-RetryAfter` on warn / deny responses. HTTP 429 responses MUST include `Retry-After` and the standard Appendix I error envelope. If the row names "endpoint-specific", the endpoint's error table supplies the concrete 429 code; otherwise the default code is `rate_limit_exceeded`.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Every endpoint-level rate-limit-class reference in §27, §31, §32, §48, §50, §51, and future API sections MUST match one `Class ID` in the table above and one Appendix J `api_rate_limit_class` value.
2. No endpoint table may use a marketplace, billing, analytics, Ops, or KB-export class name as an Auth Scope; rate-limit class and API-token scope are distinct vocabularies.
3. A class row's `Scope`, `Soft Limit`, `Hard Limit`, `Burst / Concurrency`, and `429 Error` cells are required. If an endpoint supplies a stricter sublimit, the endpoint MUST cite the base class and name the stricter error code locally.
4. HTTP 429 responses for every class MUST include `Retry-After`, `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-RetryAfter`; missing headers fail `api_rate_limit_class_registry_consistency`.
5. Adding, renaming, or retiring a class requires amending §32.4.5, Appendix J `api_rate_limit_class`, and the endpoint consumers in the same change.

## 32.6 Error Handling {#32.6-error-handling}

All errors return the standard envelope below. The Phase V8.4 spec-side remediation pass (D-V8.4-012, D-V8.4-013, D-V8.4-017) bound (a) a valid JSON example, (b) a `localization_key` field, (c) a `Sourcera-Error-Subkind` response header convention, and (d) a `Sourcera-Error-Code-Alias` response header convention.

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "gate_validation_failed",
    "message": "Cannot advance to Phase 2: 3 requirements are still in draft status.",
    "localization_key": "error.workflow.gate_validation_failed",
    "details": {
      "failing_rules": ["all_requirements_active"],
      "blocking_requirement_ids": ["req_abc", "req_def"]
    },
    "request_id": "req_789xyz",
    "retry_after_seconds": null
  }
}
```

### 32.6.2 Response Headers and Deprecation Aliases {#32.6.2-response-headers-and-deprecation-aliases}

Authored Phase V8.4 (D-V8.4-012, D-V8.4-014).

| Header | When | Source | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `X-Request-ID` | Every response | Request-ID injection middleware | Mirrors `error.request_id` for support escalation. |
| `Retry-After` | When the row's `retryable=transient` (HTTP 429 / 503 / 504, plus row-overrides) | §32.4 / Appendix F retry-curve binding | Seconds until next eligible retry. |
| `Sourcera-Error-Subkind` | When the canonical HTTP status admits more than one subkind (e.g., 402, 409, 423) | Appendix J `error_subkind` enum | Deterministic subkind for client-side routing. |
| `Sourcera-Error-Code-Alias` | When the canonical code was emitted by a deprecated-alias path | Appendix J `error_code_alias` enum | Original alias name; the deprecation window per the v7.x deprecation pattern (Master Spec line 206). Currently bound aliases: `ai_wallet_exhausted` → `wallet_hard_capped` (D-V8.4-003); `stale_token` → `mcp_token_revoked` / `mcp_token_expired` (D-V8.4-014); `kb_export_console_forbidden_403_legacy` → `kb_export_console_forbidden` (D-V8.4-018); `m6_claim_reclaim_cooldown_active_409_legacy` → `m6_claim_reclaim_cooldown_active` (D-V8.4-020). All aliases removed at v8.0.0. |

Complete error code catalog in Appendix I; controlled vocabularies in Appendix J.

### 32.6.1 Multi-Status (HTTP 207) Pattern {#32.6.1-multi-status-pattern}

**Scope.** Multi-Status is used only for endpoints that perform a multi-write cascade across distinct entities where partial failure is a real (but not nominal) outcome AND the caller needs actionable per-action remediation. As of v7.0.0, the canonical uses are:

- `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/vendors/{vendor_id}/disqualify` — disqualification cascade across Target Account, Bid Workspace, Response bulk-lock, and Console Bridge Event emission (§25.3.9 error `disqualification_cascade_partial_failure`).
- `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/vendors/{vendor_id}/disqualify/{disqualification_id}/reverse` — reversal cascade across the same four domains in inverse order, with request / response / error / idempotency detail and the endpoint-local 200 / 207 schema authored in §25.3.10a (§25.3.10a error `disqualification_reversal_cascade_partial_failure`).
- Any future endpoint whose documentation explicitly opts in to Multi-Status via this section.

Multi-Status is **not** the default error surface. Most endpoints return 2xx on success or 4xx/5xx on failure. Multi-Status exists to avoid two degenerate alternatives: (a) rolling back a mostly-successful cascade on a single non-critical sub-action failure, or (b) returning 200 with a buried `partial_failure` flag that callers may miss.

**Shape.** The Multi-Status response uses the standard error envelope with a top-level `error.code` of the endpoint's documented partial-failure code (e.g., `disqualification_cascade_partial_failure`) and a `cascade_actions` array populated with per-action outcomes:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "disqualification_cascade_partial_failure",
    "message": "Disqualification committed; 1 of 4 cascade sub-actions failed. The caller should retry the failed sub-action via the supplied retry hint.",
    "details": {
      "disqualification_id": "vdr_7f2e...",
      "cascade_actions": [
        { "action": "target_account_status_transition", "status": "succeeded", "duration_ms": 18 },
        { "action": "bid_workspace_status_transition", "status": "succeeded", "duration_ms": 22 },
        { "action": "response_bulk_lock", "status": "succeeded", "duration_ms": 412 },
        { "action": "console_bridge_event_emission", "status": "failed", "failure_reason": "downstream_timeout", "duration_ms": 5000, "retry_hint": { "strategy": "auto", "next_retry_at": "2026-04-24T14:30:05.000Z" } }
      ]
    },
    "request_id": "req_abc123"
  }
}
```

**Per-action fields.** Each element of `cascade_actions` MUST include:

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `action` | String | Stable machine-readable action name registered in Appendix J per endpoint (e.g., `vendor_disqualification_cascade_action` for §25.3). |
| `status` | Enum | `succeeded` \| `failed` \| `skipped` \| `deferred`. `deferred` applies when the sub-action is intentionally async (e.g., vendor notification dispatch). |
| `duration_ms` | Integer | Wall-clock duration of the sub-action. |
| `failure_reason` | String (nullable) | Machine-readable reason on `status=failed`. |
| `retry_hint.strategy` | Enum | `auto` (the system retries automatically via the §25.2.2 bridge retry curve or the §31 webhook retry curve — caller no-op), `manual` (caller SHOULD retry the whole endpoint with the same `Idempotency-Key`), `none` (the failure is terminal; caller cannot usefully retry). |
| `retry_hint.next_retry_at` | Timestamp (nullable) | Populated on `retry_hint.strategy=auto`; absent otherwise. |

**Commit semantics.** A Multi-Status 207 response means the canonical primary write has committed — the endpoint's authoritative row (`VendorDisqualificationRecord` for disqualification, reversal timestamp for reversal) is persisted — and a subset of cascade sub-actions have failed. The caller MUST NOT retry the endpoint expecting to "re-commit" the primary; retry is for the sub-actions only. Idempotency-Key on retry returns the original 207 body with `X-Idempotent-Replay: true` until the auto-retry curve resolves the sub-actions (at which point a fresh `GET` on the entity shows `cascade_status=complete` and the sub-action fields resolved).

**Distinction from 200 / 201 / 4xx.** 200/201 on cascade endpoints means the *synchronous* phase succeeded fully; async sub-actions (e.g., notification dispatch) may still be pending but are NOT in error. 207 means the synchronous phase committed the primary but one or more sub-actions are in a failed state at response time. 4xx/5xx on cascade endpoints means the primary did NOT commit and the cascade did NOT run.

**OpenAPI annotation.** Endpoints that emit 207 MUST declare it in their OpenAPI `responses` block with the full `cascade_actions` schema. A CI gate `api_multistatus_schema_registration` (new; Authored Extension — v7.0.0) asserts every endpoint returning 207 has a registered schema.

**Observability.** Every 207 emission fires a PostHog event `api_multistatus_emitted` with `endpoint`, `primary_commit_id`, `failed_action_count`, `deferred_action_count`, `retry_strategy_histogram` properties. Ops dashboards surface 207 rates per endpoint per 15m window. A 207 rate > 1% on any endpoint over a rolling 60m window pages the endpoint's owning on-call (Cross-Console on-call for §25.3 endpoints).

Logged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` → Authored Extensions → §32.6.1 Multi-Status Pattern (2026-04-24).

## 32.7 Acceptance Criteria {#32.7-acceptance-criteria}

- All endpoints documented with curl examples in API reference.  
- Pagination cursor-based, consistent across all list endpoints.  
- Rate limit headers present on every response.  
- 429 returned when limits exceeded; includes `X-RateLimit-RetryAfter`.  
- API test coverage ≥ 95%.  
- Rate limits enforced per Appendix I error codes.
- Billing endpoints (§32.8) MUST satisfy the per-endpoint acceptance criteria in §32.8.23 in addition to the global criteria above.

## 32.8 Billing Endpoint Detail {#32.8-billing-endpoint-detail}

**Authoring Intent.** §32.8 authors the request/response/error/idempotency/pagination contracts for the Billing endpoints enumerated in §32.5. The endpoints are the public REST surface for the §4.8 Billing & AI Accounting entities (AIWallet, AIOperation, FreeAllowanceCounter, ContestRecord, CommittedSpendContract, PricingTableVersion) and they back the §5.2.1 Billing Admin permission list, the customer-facing Billing Ledger UI (Summary C.82), the Public Pricing API (Summary C.83), and partner integrations that programmatically read consumption.

**Source authority.** This section materializes Summary C.83 (Public Pricing API), Pricing Strategy §6 / §7 / §11 (wallet, overage, committed-spend), §4.8 entity definitions (authoritative for response field semantics), §5.2.1.1 Permission List (authoritative for RBAC checks). Where §5.2.1.1 references implicit-Org aliases (`/v1/billing/...`) and §32.8 authors explicit-Org canonical paths (`/v1/orgs/{org_id}/...`), the explicit-Org form is authoritative; aliases resolve identically per the §32.5 Billing block reconciliation note. Logged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` → Authored Extensions and Conflicts Resolved.

**Cross-console scope rule.** Billing endpoints inherit the `AIOperation` cross-console firewall (§4.8.1 Scope Isolation). Buyer-console API tokens see only `console=buyer` AIOperations; seller-console tokens see only `console=seller`. The Billing Ledger union view (`?console=all`) is permitted ONLY for tokens whose owning user holds `org_owner` OR `billing_admin` per §4.8.1 Scope Isolation legitimate-exception rule; the cross-console union read is audit-logged with action `billing_ledger_cross_console_read` per §4.8.1.

### 32.8.0 Common Conventions for Billing Endpoints {#32.8.0-common-conventions-for-billing-endpoints}

The following conventions apply to every endpoint in §32.8 unless an endpoint explicitly overrides:

- **Path parameter `{org_id}`.** Authoritative explicit-Org canonical form. The token's owning Org MUST equal `{org_id}` unless the token holds the Ops-only `ops_finance_admin` role (which permits cross-Org read; mutating endpoints under §32.8 still reject Ops cross-Org writes — Ops mutations route through the Ops Console, not the public API). Mismatch returns HTTP 404 with `wallet_cross_org_access`, `ai_operation_cross_org_access`, `contest_cross_org_access`, `free_allowance_cross_org_access`, `committed_spend_cross_org_access`, or `billing_admin_cross_org_access` — selected by endpoint family per Appendix I — to avoid leaking Org existence (404 not 403, per §4.8 Scope Isolation rules).
- **Authorization.** `Authorization: Bearer srck_{org_prefix}_{token_string}` per §32.2. Tokens MUST hold the scope listed in each endpoint's "Auth Scope" row. Scopes are additive; `admin:billing` implies `write:billing`, which implies `read:billing`. Implication is enforced server-side (a token explicitly granted only `admin:billing` MAY perform any read or write in §32.8).
- **Token Scope Inheritance Rule.** A token created BEFORE the v7.0.0 introduction of the `*:billing` scopes is back-filled at the first authentication after v7.0.0 deploy as follows: tokens whose owning user holds `org_owner` OR `billing_admin` receive `read:billing` only (preserving least-privilege; explicit re-issuance with `write:billing` or `admin:billing` is required for mutation). Tokens of other users receive no billing scopes. Back-fill is one-shot, audit-logged with action `org.api_token_billing_scope_backfilled` (new; Appendix J Billing Admin Audit Action Types is extended additively).
- **Rate-limit class.** `standard_authenticated_per_org` per §32.4.5 unless explicitly overridden (the public `GET /v1/pricing` uses the `public_pricing_unauth` class).
- **Pagination.** All list endpoints follow §32.3: cursor-based, opaque `next_cursor`, default `limit=50`, max `limit=250`, cursor expires 24h. The pagination envelope is `{"data": [...], "pagination": {"has_more": ..., "next_cursor": ..., "limit": ...}}`.
- **Idempotency for POST mutations.** Every state-mutating POST endpoint in §32.8 requires an `Idempotency-Key` request header (1–128 chars, ASCII printable) unless that endpoint's local **Idempotency** block explicitly declares `N/A`. The (header value, `org_id`, endpoint path, token id) tuple uniquely identifies a logical request for 24 hours. Replays return HTTP 200/201/202 with the original response body and a header `X-Idempotent-Replay: true`; replays with the same key but a different request body return HTTP 409 `idempotency_key_request_mismatch` (Appendix I). Endpoint sub-sections MUST state REQUIRED / N/A locally so implementers do not need to infer the contract from this common block.
- **Currency presentation.** Monetary fields in responses appear in two forms per object: `..._cents` (integer USD cents per §4.8 entity definitions; canonical, never lossy) and `..._display` (object: `{"amount": "<decimal>", "currency": "<billing_currency>", "fx_rate_locked": "<decimal>"}` — derived at response time using the Org's `billing_currency` from the wallet (§4.8.3) and the FX rate locked at the source row write time per §4.8.1 `fx_rate_locked`). Clients integrating for accounting MUST consume `..._cents`; clients displaying to users MAY consume `..._display`. Locale formatting is the client's responsibility.
- **Timestamps.** All timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with millisecond precision and a trailing `Z` (e.g., `2026-04-15T14:30:00.000Z`).
- **Error envelope.** Per §32.6 / Appendix I. Every error includes `request_id` for support escalation. Errors specific to billing endpoints include the offending entity id (`wallet_id`, `ai_operation_id`, `contest_id`, etc.) in `error.details` to aid client-side diagnosis without requiring an additional roundtrip.
- **Webhook coupling.** State changes performed by mutating endpoints emit corresponding webhook events per §31 / Appendix C: `billing.wallet.overage_cap_changed`, `billing.wallet.auto_topup_config_changed`, `billing.contest.filed`, `billing.contest.decision_received`. Webhook delivery follows §31.1 idempotency rules (the API mutation and the webhook share an `event_id` for downstream correlation).
- **Canonical `capability_id` form (lock).** All billing endpoints in §32.8 — including `GET /v1/pricing`, `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/ai-operations`, `POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/ai-operations/{op_id}/contest`, and every webhook payload in §31.8 that carries `capability_id` — MUST emit the **canonical** `capability_id` form: the identifier as registered in Appendix J (Controlled Vocabulary Registry) and CapabilityRegistryEntry (§4.8.2). Canonical form strictly PROHIBITS leading `buyer_` or `seller_` prefixes. Console applicability is conveyed via the dedicated `console_applicability` field on the Public Pricing API response and the `originating_console` field on webhook payloads — never by mutating the `capability_id` itself. Side-disambiguating suffixes (e.g., `qa_suggestion_seller`, `qa_suggestion_buyer`) are permitted when both sides have independent rate-card rows per §34.14.1 / §34.14.1 Appendix reference; prefixes are not. Deploy-time validator `canonical_capability_id_lock` asserts (a) no Public Pricing API response contains a `capability_id` value beginning with `buyer_` or `seller_`; (b) CapabilityRegistryEntry.canonical_id never begins with those prefixes; (c) every webhook catalog entry's payload schema enforces the same. See §34.17.3 invariant 7 and §34.17.4 AC #7. Violations at runtime fail the request with HTTP 500 `capability_id_prefix_leak` (new; Appendix I) rather than serving non-canonical data.

### 32.8.1 GET /v1/pricing — Public Pricing API {#32.8.1-get-pricing}

**Method & Path.** `GET https://api.sourcera.io/v1/pricing`

**Auth Scope.** None. The endpoint is unauthenticated. Sending an `Authorization` header is permitted but ignored; the response does NOT vary by token. (Per Summary C.83 the rate card is intentionally public so customers can forecast spend programmatically without provisioning credentials.)

**RBAC.** N/A (no authentication).

**Rate-Limit Class.** `public_pricing_unauth` (§32.4.5). Per source IP: 600/h soft, 1,200/h hard, 60/min burst. Edge-cached 60s on `(version_label, If-None-Match)` per §4.8.9 acceptance #4.

**Query Parameters.**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `version` | String (semver-like, e.g., `2026.04.15.001`) | No | Pin to a specific PricingTableVersion. Must reference a `status ∈ {published, superseded}` row. Returns HTTP 404 `pricing_table_version_not_found` if no match. Default = the row with the most recent `effective_at ≤ now` AND `status=published`. Pinning is for forecasting reproducibility per §4.8.9 Failure Mode #2; AIOperation pricing always uses the current `published` row regardless of pin. |
| `currency` | Enum: `usd`, `eur`, `gbp`, `cad`, `aud` | No | Returns prices converted to the requested currency using the version's per-currency conversion table (per §4.8.9 `included_currencies`). Default = `usd`. Returns HTTP 400 `pricing_table_currency_not_published` if the requested currency is not in `included_currencies`. |
| `capability_id` | String | No | Filter to a single capability. Returns HTTP 200 with a single-element `capabilities` array; HTTP 404 `pricing_table_capability_not_published` if the capability is not `customer_billed` or not in the version. |
| `include_deprecated` | Boolean | No | Default `false`. When `true`, includes capabilities in `state=deprecated` (within `deprecation_grace_until`) for migration-aware clients. |

**Request Headers.**

- `If-None-Match: <hash>` — When the `<hash>` equals the current `PricingTableVersion.published_payload_hash`, the endpoint returns HTTP 304 Not Modified with empty body. Cache-hits do NOT count against the per-IP limit.
- `Accept-Language` — Locale hint for `display_name` localization. Default: `en-US`. Falls back to `en-US` if the requested locale is not maintained.

**Response Headers.**

- `ETag: "<published_payload_hash>"` — sha256 hex of the rate-card payload per §4.8.9 acceptance #4.
- `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` — 60-second public TTL; the edge cache and downstream HTTP caches MAY honor.
- `X-Sourcera-Pricing-Version: <version_label>` — Echoes the version_label served (the resolved version after `?version=` and the default-resolution rule).
- `X-Sourcera-Pricing-Effective-At: <iso8601>` — Echoes the version's `effective_at`.

**Response Body (HTTP 200).**

```json
{
  "version": {
    "id": "ptv_b5e8f2c1...",
    "version_label": "2026.04.15.001",
    "status": "published",
    "effective_at": "2026-04-15T00:00:00.000Z",
    "published_payload_hash": "9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08",
    "breaking_change_flag": false,
    "currency": "usd",
    "included_currencies": ["usd", "eur", "gbp", "cad", "aud"],
    "triggering_change_summary": "Cost-base recalc 2026-04-14; no customer-visible price change."
  },
  "plan_tiers": [
    {
```

| 503 | `service_unavailable` | Edge cache miss + origin down |

**Pagination.** None — the endpoint returns the full rate card in one response. Per §4.8.9 the `published_payload_json` is bounded at ≤ 1 MB; the response remains within HTTP-acceptable size and within client-side fetch budgets.

**Idempotency.** N/A (read endpoint).

### 32.8.3 POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/wallet/cap — Set Wallet Overage Cap {#32.8.3-post-wallet-cap}

**Method & Path.** `POST https://api.sourcera.io/v1/orgs/{org_id}/wallet/cap`

**Authoring Note.** §5.2.1.1 Operation #5 references this surface as `PATCH /v1/billing/wallet/overage`. Per the path-convention reconciliation logged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md`, the canonical method is POST and the canonical path is `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/wallet/cap`. The verb change from PATCH to POST is intentional: the endpoint accepts an `Idempotency-Key` and atomically materializes a state-machine transition (overage_disabled → overage_enabled / cap_changed / overage_disabled), which is more naturally modeled as a POST-mutation than a PATCH-update of a sparse field set. The implicit-Org alias `/v1/billing/wallet/cap` (POST) is also exposed and routes identically.

**Auth Scope.** `write:billing`.

**RBAC.** `role ∈ {org_owner, billing_admin}` per §5.2.1.1 Operation #5. `org_admin` and other roles return HTTP 403 `wallet_role_forbidden`.

**Rate-Limit Class.** `standard_authenticated_per_org` per §32.4.5.

**Request Body (JSON).**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `enabled` | Boolean | Yes | — | `true` enables overage; `false` disables it. When `false`, `cap_value_dollars_cents` is forced to `0` and the prior cap is recorded in audit only. |
| `cap_value_dollars_cents` | Integer | Conditional | ≥ 0 when `enabled=true`; = 0 when `enabled=false`. Upper bound: cite §4.8.3 `auto_topup_max_monthly_value_dollars` constraint (the absolute ceiling defined there is the canonical home; per Authoring Convention #10, this row MUST NOT restate the literal value — schema validation reads the constraint from §4.8.3). Free-tier orgs are additionally capped per Pricing Strategy §4 / §7 (bill-shock-free Free path). | The new monthly overage cap in USD cents. Inline `50000000` literal removed 2026-05-13 per V14 remediation pass D-V14-006 (numerical_singleton; refines D-DEC-008 multi-surface coordination scope). See §4.8.3 for the canonical ceiling and the (pending) Ops-override path per `_integration/Decisions.md → F-2`. |
| `confirm_acknowledgement_token` | String | Yes for `enabled=true` AND prior `enabled=false` | sha256 hex; 64-char | Returned by the prerequisite `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/wallet/overage-confirmation` (out of §32.8 scope; documented separately in the §34 Wallet Overage chapter). Confirms the Billing Admin saw the customer-warning copy. |
| `note_internal` | String | No | ≤ 500 chars | Audit-record-only note (e.g., "Q2 budget approved via FP-1428"). |

**Response Body (HTTP 200) — wallet object identical to §32.8.2 GET response, with the new `overage` block reflecting the change.** Plus a top-level `change_summary`:

```json
{
  "change_summary": {
    "transition": "overage_cap_changed",
    "prior": {"enabled": true, "cap_value_dollars_cents": 25000},
    "new": {"enabled": true, "cap_value_dollars_cents": 50000},
    "audit_event_id": "evt_1714153207_a8b3c2",
    "applied_at": "2026-04-15T14:30:07.000Z"
  },
  "wallet": { ... full wallet object per §32.8.2 ... }
}
```

**Error Codes.**

| HTTP | Code | Trigger |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 400 | `bad_request` | Missing required field; malformed JSON |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | Missing or invalid token |
| 403 | `wallet_role_forbidden` | Token's user role not in `{org_owner, billing_admin}` |
| 404 | `wallet_cross_org_access` | `{org_id}` ≠ token's owning Org |
| 404 | `wallet_not_found` | Wallet not provisioned |
| 409 | `idempotency_key_request_mismatch` | `Idempotency-Key` reused with a different request body |
| 422 | `wallet_overage_cap_out_of_range` (new; Appendix I) | `cap_value_dollars_cents` exceeds plan-tier ceiling |
| 422 | `wallet_overage_confirmation_required` (new; Appendix I) | First-time enable without `confirm_acknowledgement_token` |
| 422 | `wallet_overage_confirmation_token_invalid_or_expired` (new; Appendix I) | Token forged, mismatched, or > 15 minutes old |
| 422 | `wallet_state_conflict` (new; Appendix I) | Attempted to change overage while wallet is in `closed` or `suspended`; surface customer to update payment method first |

**Pagination.** N/A.

**Idempotency.** REQUIRED in production. `Idempotency-Key` header per §32.8.0; replay returns `X-Idempotent-Replay: true` with the original response. The audit row is written exactly once even on replay.

**State-Machine Effect.** Wallet `overage_cap_value_dollars` field updated atomically; if `enabled=true ∧ prior_enabled=false`, audit action `org.wallet_overage_enabled` (else `org.wallet_overage_cap_changed` or `org.wallet_overage_disabled` per Appendix J Billing Admin Audit Action Types). Webhook `billing.wallet.overage_cap_changed` emitted per §31. If the new cap is LOWER than current `overage_consumed_value_dollars`, the wallet immediately transitions to `hard_capped_100` for the remainder of the period; in-flight `pending` AIOperations honor their original holds per §4.8.3 Failure Mode #5.

**Concrete Example.**

```
curl -i -X POST 'https://api.sourcera.io/v1/orgs/org_b7d4f1a9/wallet/cap' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer srck_b7d4f1a9_8c7e9d2c5b...' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: 4e8f2c1d-7a93-4b21-9c5e-d3b1a8f76e2c' \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true,
    "cap_value_dollars_cents": 50000,
    "confirm_acknowledgement_token": "9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08",
    "note_internal": "Q2 budget approved via FP-1428"
  }'

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-RateLimit-Limit: 5000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 4911
Content-Type: application/json
{...}
```

### 32.8.4 POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/wallet/auto-topup — Configure Auto Top-Up {#32.8.4-post-wallet-auto-topup}

**Method & Path.** `POST https://api.sourcera.io/v1/orgs/{org_id}/wallet/auto-topup`

**Authoring Note.** §5.2.1.1 Operations #2 and #3 reference `PATCH /v1/billing/wallet/auto-topup`. Per the same path-convention reconciliation as §32.8.3, the canonical surface is POST against the explicit-Org path. The implicit-Org alias `/v1/billing/wallet/auto-topup` (POST) routes identically.

**Auth Scope.** `write:billing`.

**RBAC.** `role ∈ {org_owner, billing_admin}` per §5.2.1.1 Operations #2 and #3.

**Rate-Limit Class.** `standard_authenticated_per_org` per §32.4.5.

**Request Body (JSON).**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `enabled` | Boolean | Yes | — | `true` enables auto-topup. Per §4.8.3 acceptance #4, the operation MUST require explicit-confirmation copy: a first-time `enabled=true` flip without `confirm_acknowledgement_token` is rejected with `wallet_autotopup_confirmation_required`. |
| `trigger_utilization_pct` | Integer | Conditional | 50–95; required when `enabled=true` | When `(consumed + overage_consumed) / (budget + overage_cap) ≥ this %`, attempt top-up. Default 90 if omitted on first enable. |
| `increment_value_dollars_cents` | Integer | Conditional | 5000–1000000 ($50–$10,000) per §4.8.3 acceptance #5; required when `enabled=true` | Per-charge top-up. Out-of-range returns HTTP 422 `wallet_topup_increment_out_of_range`. |
| `max_monthly_value_dollars_cents` | Integer | Conditional | Lower bound and upper bound per §4.8.3 `auto_topup_max_monthly_value_dollars` constraint (canonical home; per Authoring Convention #10, this row MUST NOT restate the literal range — schema validation reads the bounds from §4.8.3). Required when `enabled=true`. | Total top-up ceiling per billing period. Inline `$50–$500,000` literals removed 2026-05-13 per V14 remediation pass D-V14-006 (numerical_singleton; refines D-DEC-008 multi-surface coordination scope). See §4.8.3 for the canonical bounds and the (pending) Ops-override path per `_integration/Decisions.md → F-2`. |
| `payment_method_id` | String | Conditional | ≤ 200 chars; required on first enable | Stripe PaymentMethod id; MUST belong to the Org's `stripe_customer_id` per §4.8.3. Mismatch returns HTTP 422 `wallet_autotopup_payment_method_not_owned`. |
| `confirm_acknowledgement_token` | String | Yes for first enable per period | sha256 hex; 64-char | Returned by the prerequisite `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/wallet/auto-topup-confirmation` (warning copy: "Auto top-up will charge your card without further prompts up to your monthly cap"). 15-minute TTL. |
| `note_internal` | String | No | ≤ 500 chars | Audit note. |

**Response Body (HTTP 200) — wallet object per §32.8.2 with `auto_topup` block reflecting the change, plus `change_summary`:**

```json
{
  "change_summary": {
    "transition": "autotopup_config_changed",
    "prior": {
      "enabled": false, "trigger_utilization_pct": null,
      "increment_value_dollars_cents": null, "max_monthly_value_dollars_cents": null
    },
    "new": {
      "enabled": true, "trigger_utilization_pct": 90,
      "increment_value_dollars_cents": 10000, "max_monthly_value_dollars_cents": 100000
    },
    "audit_event_id": "evt_1714153422_d2c8f1",
    "applied_at": "2026-04-15T14:33:42.000Z"
  },
  "wallet": { ... }
}
```

**Error Codes.**

| HTTP | Code | Trigger |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 400 | `bad_request` | Missing required field; malformed JSON |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | Missing or invalid token |
| 403 | `wallet_role_forbidden` | Role not in `{org_owner, billing_admin}` |
| 404 | `wallet_cross_org_access` | Cross-Org access attempted |
| 404 | `wallet_not_found` | Wallet not provisioned |
| 409 | `idempotency_key_request_mismatch` | Replay with different body |
| 422 | `wallet_topup_increment_out_of_range` | Increment outside [$50, $10,000] |
| 422 | `wallet_autotopup_max_monthly_out_of_range` (new; Appendix I) | Max monthly outside [$50, $500,000] |
| 422 | `wallet_autotopup_trigger_pct_out_of_range` (new; Appendix I) | Trigger pct outside [50, 95] |
| 422 | `wallet_autotopup_payment_method_not_owned` (new; Appendix I) | PaymentMethod not in Org's Stripe customer |
| 422 | `wallet_autotopup_confirmation_required` (new; Appendix I) | First-time enable without ack token |
| 422 | `wallet_autotopup_confirmation_token_invalid_or_expired` (new; Appendix I) | Token forged or > 15 minutes old |
| 422 | `wallet_state_conflict` | Wallet in `closed` or `suspended` |

**Idempotency.** REQUIRED. `Idempotency-Key` per §32.8.0. A replay during the 24h window returns the prior result without initiating a duplicate Stripe verification charge.

**State-Machine Effect.** Updates `auto_topup_enabled`, `auto_topup_trigger_utilization_pct`, `auto_topup_increment_value_dollars`, `auto_topup_max_monthly_value_dollars`, `last_topup_payment_method_id` atomically. Audit action `org.wallet_autotopup_enabled` / `org.wallet_autotopup_disabled` / `org.wallet_autotopup_config_changed` per Appendix J. Webhook `billing.wallet.auto_topup_config_changed` emitted. Disabling auto-topup mid-charge per §4.8.3 Failure Mode #4: in-flight Stripe charges complete; the disable applies to future trigger evaluations.

**Concrete Example.**

```
curl -i -X POST 'https://api.sourcera.io/v1/orgs/org_b7d4f1a9/wallet/auto-topup' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer srck_b7d4f1a9_8c7e9d2c5b...' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: 7b2e9d4c-3a18-4b62-9c1f-d5b8a3e6f9c4' \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true,
    "trigger_utilization_pct": 90,
    "increment_value_dollars_cents": 10000,
    "max_monthly_value_dollars_cents": 100000,
    "payment_method_id": "pm_1NQ8x9C7e...",
    "confirm_acknowledgement_token": "8d2c4f9e1b3a5c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d"
  }'

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Idempotent-Replay: false
{...}
```

### 32.8.5 GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/ai-operations — Billing Ledger (List) {#32.8.5-get-ai-operations-list}

**Method & Path.** `GET https://api.sourcera.io/v1/orgs/{org_id}/ai-operations`

**Auth Scope.** `read:billing`.

**RBAC.** `role ∈ {org_owner, org_admin (read-only), billing_admin}` per §5.2.1.1 Operation #7. Cross-console union (`?console=all`) requires `role ∈ {org_owner, billing_admin}` per §4.8.1 legitimate-exception rule; `org_admin` requesting `?console=all` returns HTTP 403 `billing_ledger_cross_console_role_insufficient` (new; Appendix I).

**Rate-Limit Class.** `standard_authenticated_per_org` per §32.4.5.

**Query Parameters.**

| Name | Type | Required | Constraints | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `cursor` | String | No | Opaque | §32.3 cursor; expires 24h |
| `limit` | Integer | No | 1–250; default 50 | Per §32.3 |
| `console` | Enum: `buyer`, `seller`, `all` | No | Default = the token's console scope | `all` requires elevated role per RBAC above |
| `capability_id` | String | No | — | Filter by capability |
| `settlement_state` | Enum or array | No | Subset of AIOperation.`settlement_state` | Multi-value: `?settlement_state=accepted&settlement_state=auto_accepted` |
| `cost_center` | Enum or array | No | Subset; defaults exclude `sourcera_owned`, `platform_marketing` per §4.8.1 acceptance #9 | Customer-facing read MUST NEVER return `sourcera_owned`/`platform_marketing` rows even if explicitly requested; the parameter is silently sanitized; QA test `aiop_sourcera_owned_isolation` asserts |
| `created_after` | Timestamp (ISO 8601) | No | — | Inclusive lower bound on `created_at` |
| `created_before` | Timestamp (ISO 8601) | No | — | Exclusive upper bound on `created_at` |
| `workspace_id` | UUID | No | — | Filter to operations originating in a specific workspace; cross-workspace requires `org_owner` / `billing_admin` |
| `actor_id` | UUID | No | — | Filter to operations by a specific user/agent |
| `billed_against_free_allowance` | Boolean | No | — | True returns only free-allowance-consumed rows |
| `committed_spend_burn_only` | Boolean | No | — | True returns only rows that burned the commit pool |
| `min_charge_cents` | Integer | No | ≥ 0 | Filter to rows with `effective_charge_cents ≥ value` |
| `include_redacted` | Boolean | No | Default `false` | When `true`, includes DSAR-redacted rows with redaction sentinels populated |
| `include_summary` | Boolean | No | Default `true` | When `true`, response includes `summary` block (totals for the filtered window) |

**Response Body (HTTP 200).**

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
```

**Error Codes.**

| HTTP | Code | Trigger |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 400 | `bad_request` | Malformed query parameter |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | Missing or invalid token |
| 403 | `billing_ledger_cross_console_role_insufficient` | `?console=all` without `{org_owner, billing_admin}` |
| 404 | `ai_operation_cross_org_access` | `{org_id}` cross-Org |
| 422 | `pagination_cursor_expired` (existing; Appendix I) | Cursor older than 24h |
| 429 | `rate_limit_exceeded` | Per-Org limit |

**Pagination.** §32.3 cursor-based, default 50, max 250. Order: `created_at DESC, id ASC` per §4.8.1 acceptance #8. The `summary` block is computed over the filter window, NOT the page — clients reconstructing totals from page sums will see a different number; documented in API reference.

**Aggregation currency caveat.** All `summary.*` fields and their `..._cents` counterparts are canonical integer-cents sums. The endpoint does NOT emit `..._display` objects on aggregated summary fields because FX-rate locking (§4.8.1) is a per-row property — aggregating rows with different `fx_rate_locked` values would produce a mixed-rate sum that cannot be faithfully re-expressed in a single locked `..._display` envelope. Clients rendering localized totals MUST perform their own FX conversion using the wallet's current `billing_currency` and a client-chosen FX rate snapshot; Sourcera deliberately refuses to emit a synthetic `summary.*_display` object to prevent silent FX-rate misattribution. QA test `aiop_summary_no_display_envelope` asserts the summary block contains only `*_cents` keys. Clients requiring per-currency aggregation MUST filter the list query by `billing_currency` first (currently all Orgs are single-currency per wallet, so this is a no-op in v7.0.0; documented for multi-currency-wallet future extension).

**Idempotency.** N/A.

**Performance Note.** Filter combinations that fall outside the indexed key prefixes (e.g., `actor_id` without `console` and without time bound) MAY return HTTP 422 `query_unsupported_filter_combination` (new; Appendix I) requesting the client narrow the filter. The supported index-aligned prefix combinations are: `(console)`, `(console, capability_id)`, `(console, settlement_state)`, `(console, created_after, created_before)`, `(console, workspace_id, created_after)`. Clients MAY explore arbitrary filters via the export endpoint (§5.2.1.1 Operation #8 — out of §32.8 explicit scope; documented separately in §34).

**Concrete Example.**

```
curl -i 'https://api.sourcera.io/v1/orgs/org_b7d4f1a9/ai-operations?console=buyer&created_after=2026-04-01T00:00:00Z&limit=50' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer srck_b7d4f1a9_8c7e9d2c5b...'

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-RateLimit-Limit: 5000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 4998
{...}
```

### 32.8.6 GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/ai-operations/{op_id} — Single AIOperation {#32.8.6-get-ai-operation-single}

**Method & Path.** `GET https://api.sourcera.io/v1/orgs/{org_id}/ai-operations/{op_id}`

**Auth Scope.** `read:billing`.

**RBAC.** `role ∈ {org_owner, org_admin (read-only), billing_admin}` per §5.2.1.1 Operation #7. The cross-console firewall (§4.8.1) applies: a `console=seller` operation requested via a buyer-console token returns HTTP 404 `ai_operation_cross_console_access` (404 not 403 to avoid leaking existence per §4.8.1 Scope Isolation).

**Rate-Limit Class.** `standard_authenticated_per_org` per §32.4.5.

**Path Parameters.**

| Name | Type | Constraints |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `org_id` | UUID | Token's owning Org |
| `op_id` | UUID | AIOperation id |

**Query Parameters.**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `include_subtree` | Boolean | No | Default `false`. When `true`, includes the Managed Agent sub-call subtree per `parent_operation_id` traversal (max depth 6 per §4.8.1 acceptance #13). |
| `include_outcome_signal_history` | Boolean | No | Default `false`. When `true`, includes the chronological list of outcome signals received against the operation (resolver-fired and user-fired). |

**Response Body (HTTP 200).** Same row shape as a single `data[]` element of §32.8.5, plus optional `subtree[]` and `outcome_signal_history[]` arrays:

```json
{
  "id": "aiop_5c8d3f2a...",
  "...": "...",
  "subtree": [
    {"id": "aiop_8e1a4f7c...", "parent_operation_id": "aiop_5c8d3f2a...", "capability_id": "pre_scoring_subcall_extract", "settlement_state": "accepted", "effective_charge_cents": 0, "cost_center": "sourcera_owned"}
  ],
  "outcome_signal_history": [
    {"signal_type": "user_accepted_score", "received_at": "2026-04-15T11:42:08.000Z", "source": "user", "actor_id": "usr_4f7e..."}
  ]
}
```

**Error Codes.**

| HTTP | Code | Trigger |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | Missing or invalid token |
| 404 | `ai_operation_cross_org_access` | Cross-Org id |
| 404 | `ai_operation_cross_console_access` | Console mismatch |
| 404 | `ai_operation_not_found` (new; Appendix I) | `op_id` does not exist within the Org and console scope |
| 422 | `ai_operation_managed_agent_depth_exceeded` | Subtree depth > 6 (defensive; capped on insert per §4.8.1) |

**Idempotency.** N/A.

**Concrete Example.**

```
curl -i 'https://api.sourcera.io/v1/orgs/org_b7d4f1a9/ai-operations/aiop_5c8d3f2a?include_subtree=true' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer srck_b7d4f1a9_8c7e9d2c5b...'
```

### 32.8.7 POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/ai-operations/{op_id}/contest — File Contest {#32.8.7-post-ai-operation-contest}

**Method & Path.** `POST https://api.sourcera.io/v1/orgs/{org_id}/ai-operations/{op_id}/contest`

**Auth Scope.** `admin:billing` (mutation that obligates Ops review and posts a soft credit; held to the highest-privilege scope).

**RBAC.** `role = billing_admin` ONLY per §5.2.1.1 Operation #9. `org_owner` MUST first hold or be granted `billing_admin` to file. The non-inheritance rule is enforced server-side; an `org_owner` without `billing_admin` receives HTTP 403 `contest_role_must_be_billing_admin` (new; Appendix I).

**Rate-Limit Class.** `standard_authenticated_per_org` per §32.4.5. PLUS a per-Org per-AIOperation contest write-ceiling: at most 5 contest filings per Org per minute (anti-abuse; bursts above this return HTTP 429 `contest_filing_rate_limit_exceeded` (new; Appendix I)).

**Path Parameters.** `{org_id}`, `{op_id}` per §32.8.6.

**Request Body (JSON).**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `reason_code` | Enum | Yes | See Appendix J `contest_reason_code` (excluding `auto_filed_late_signal` which is system-only) | Categorical reason |
| `reason_narrative` | String | Yes | 50–4000 chars | Customer's explanation; required for non-`auto_filed_late_signal` per §4.8.5 |
| `provenance_hash_at_file` | String | Yes | 64-char sha256 hex | MUST equal AIOperation.`provenance_hash`; mismatch returns HTTP 422 `contest_provenance_hash_mismatch` per §4.8.5 Failure Mode #4 |
| `requested_credit_amount_cents` | Integer | No | 0 ≤ value ≤ AIOperation.`effective_charge_cents` | Default = `effective_charge_cents` (full credit); partial-credit requests permitted but Ops may approve a different amount |
| `contact_email` | String | No | Valid email; ≤ 255 chars | Override default contact (defaults to filer's user email); used by Ops Finance for follow-up |

**Response Body (HTTP 201 Created).**

```json
{
  "id": "ctr_9d4f8c2a...",
  "ai_operation_id": "aiop_5c8d3f2a...",
  "org_id": "org_b7d4f1a9...",
  "console": "buyer",
  "filed_by_user_id": "usr_2a8c4f7e...",
  "filed_by_role_snapshot": "billing_admin",
  "reason_code": "outcome_resolver_bug_suspected",
  "reason_narrative": "The Pre-Scoring response for requirement REQ-184 returned 'partially meets' but our team had marked it 'fully meets' in the workspace 4 minutes prior. The auto-accept appears to have fired before our manual signal was processed.",
  "original_settlement_state": "auto_accepted",
  "original_charge_cents": 35,
  "provenance_hash_at_file": "a3f7c1d8b2e9...",
  "requested_credit_amount_cents": 35,
  "status": "open",
  "ops_reviewer_user_id": null,
  "sla_first_review_at_estimated": "2026-04-22T11:42:08.000Z",
  "sla_decision_at_estimated": "2026-04-29T11:42:08.000Z",
  "ai_operation_post_state": {
    "id": "aiop_5c8d3f2a...",
    "settlement_state": "contested",
    "contest_record_id": "ctr_9d4f8c2a...",
    "soft_credit_value_dollars_cents": 35
  },
  "wallet_post_state": {
    "id": "wal_3a8d12c4...",
    "consumed_value_dollars_cents": 21715,
    "remaining_value_dollars_cents": 3285
  },
  "audit_event_id": "evt_1714153807_e7d4c1",
  "webhook_event_id": "evt_1714153807_e7d4c1",
  "filed_at": "2026-04-15T14:43:27.000Z"
}
```

**Error Codes.**

| HTTP | Code | Trigger |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 400 | `bad_request` | Malformed body; reason_narrative outside 50–4000 chars |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | Missing or invalid token |
| 403 | `contest_role_must_be_billing_admin` | Filer lacks `billing_admin` |
| 404 | `ai_operation_cross_org_access` | Cross-Org |
| 404 | `ai_operation_cross_console_access` | Console mismatch |
| 404 | `ai_operation_not_found` | `op_id` not found |
| 409 | `contest_already_filed` | Prior ContestRecord exists for this AIOperation |
| 409 | `idempotency_key_request_mismatch` | Replay with different body |
| 410 | `ai_operation_contest_window_expired` | `now > AIOperation.contest_window_at` per §4.8.5 Failure Mode #1 |
| 422 | `contest_provenance_hash_mismatch` | `provenance_hash_at_file` ≠ AIOperation.`provenance_hash` |
| 422 | `contest_invalid_settlement_state` (new; Appendix I) | AIOperation.`settlement_state ∉ {accepted, auto_accepted}` (e.g., contesting a `rejected` row is invalid since the customer was already credited the difference) |
| 422 | `contest_requested_credit_exceeds_charge` (new; Appendix I) | `requested_credit_amount_cents > AIOperation.effective_charge_cents` |
| 423 | `contest_locked_for_dsar` | DSAR redaction pending on the AIOperation per §4.8.5 Failure Mode #5 |
| 429 | `contest_filing_rate_limit_exceeded` | > 5 contests/minute by the Org |

**Idempotency.** REQUIRED. Two filings with the same `Idempotency-Key` return the original ContestRecord (`X-Idempotent-Replay: true`). Two filings with different `Idempotency-Key` against the same AIOperation: the second returns HTTP 409 `contest_already_filed` (only one ContestRecord per AIOperation per §4.8.5 Scope).

**State-Machine Effect.** Atomically: (1) creates ContestRecord with `status=open`; (2) transitions AIOperation to `settlement_state=contested`, sets `contest_record_id`; (3) places soft credit on the AIWallet equal to `requested_credit_amount_cents` (NOT the full `effective_charge_cents` if partial-credit requested — the soft credit matches the request; Ops finalizes); (4) writes audit row `org.contest_filed`; (5) emits webhook `billing.contest.filed`. The 14-day window check uses the database transaction commit time per §4.8.5 acceptance #6 to prevent off-by-one-second exploits.

**Window Edge Behavior — 14-day Boundary.** A contest filed at `contest_window_at - 1 second` is accepted; at `contest_window_at` is REJECTED with HTTP 410 (the comparison is strict `now < contest_window_at`). When the OutcomeContract overrides `contest_window_days`, the effective window per AIOperation is what was locked at write time (NOT the current contract). The endpoint surfaces the effective window in the AIOperation response (`contest_window_at` field) for client-side proactive UI ("12 days remaining to file").

**Concrete Example.**

```
curl -i -X POST 'https://api.sourcera.io/v1/orgs/org_b7d4f1a9/ai-operations/aiop_5c8d3f2a/contest' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer srck_b7d4f1a9_8c7e9d2c5b...' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: c8b3e5d9-7a14-4b2f-9c6d-e8a4b1f7d3c2' \
  -d '{
    "reason_code": "outcome_resolver_bug_suspected",
    "reason_narrative": "The Pre-Scoring response for requirement REQ-184 returned partially meets but our team had marked it fully meets in the workspace 4 minutes prior. The auto-accept appears to have fired before our manual signal was processed.",
    "provenance_hash_at_file": "a3f7c1d8b2e9...",
    "requested_credit_amount_cents": 35
  }'

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Location: /v1/orgs/org_b7d4f1a9/contests/ctr_9d4f8c2a
{...}
```
