# 34\. Plan Tiers, Billing & Entitlements {#34.-plan-tiers,-billing-&-entitlements}

**Authoring Intent.** §34 is the operational and policy surface that sits on top of the §4.8 billing entity foundation (`AIOperation`, `CapabilityRegistryEntry`, `AIWallet`, `OutcomeContract`, `ContestRecord`, `CostBaseRecalculationLog`, `FreeAllowanceCounter`, `CommittedSpendContract`, `PricingTableVersion`, `DowngradeExcessDataBucket`, `BillingSeatSnapshot`). §4.8 holds the schema, state machines, and entity-level acceptance criteria; §34 holds the plan-tier definitions, the entitlement matrix, the wallet operational policy, the outcome-resolver policy, the cross-side billing rules, and the customer-visible commercial terms. Every monetary figure, character limit, and quota in this section is sourced from `Sourcera_Buyer_Pricing_Strategy.md` (v2, 2026-04-13) and `Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy.md` (v2, 2026-04-14); citations appear inline. Where a number is not in the source documents and is required for buildability, the value is flagged as an Authored Extension in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` for human sign-off.

**Cross-section dependencies.** §34 references but does not duplicate: §4.8.1–§4.8.11 (entity schemas and state machines), §5.2 (Org-Level Roles, including the new `billing_admin` role), §5.11 (Feature Access Matrix), §6.8 (DSAR / right-to-erasure), §7.2 (Dual-Console Firewall), §31 (Webhooks), §32 (API), §39 (Object Size Constraints), §40.2 (Data Retention), §44 (Performance), Appendix C (Notification Event Catalog), Appendix G (PostHog Event Taxonomy), Appendix I (API Error Code Catalog), and Appendix J (Controlled Vocabulary Registry). Every enum value used here is registered in Appendix J under a section ending in `(§4.8.x)`.

**Source-of-truth precedence within §34.** When a value can be read from multiple authorities, the precedence is: (1) the §4.8 entity tables (immutable schema-level truth), (2) the Buyer/Seller Pricing Strategy v2 documents (commercial intent), (3) Master Summary §2 and Appendix C.75–C.87 (architectural intent). §34 never invents a number that contradicts (1)–(3); discrepancies are resolved in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` and surface as Breaking Changes when the resolution overwrites the v6.0.0 §34 surface.

## 34.1 Plan Tier Definitions (Authoritative) {#34.1-plan-tier-definitions-(authoritative)}

This is the single authoritative plan-tier table for the platform. Every other section that references plan capabilities (§5.11, §6.2, §6.4, §10.7, §13, §14, §17, §20, §28, §29, §30, §39) MUST link back to §34.1 rather than restating cell values. Pricing is split across two parallel tracks — Buyer and Seller — that share one AI wallet mechanic at the Organization level (§4.8.3 AIWallet). Full narrative context lives in `Sourcera_Buyer_Pricing_Strategy.md` and `Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy.md`.

**Citation key.** Every cell value is sourced from one of the following: **BPS** = `Sourcera_Buyer_Pricing_Strategy.md` (v2, 2026-04-13); **SPS** = `Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy.md` (v2, 2026-04-14); **MS** = `Sourcera_Master_Summary.md §2`; **AE** = Authored Extension (logged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions`).

### 34.1.1 Buyer Plan Tiers

The Buyer Solo column is the v3 Personal-Card On-Ramp tier (BPS v3 §5; Phase 14.9). All Solo numerics live here authoritatively; BPS v3 narrative MUST cite §34.1.1 and never restate. The Solo surface contract — engine-absorbed AI envelope, hidden wallet/rate-card, unwatermarked Selection Report, full Defense View, Solo-Mode pipeline compression, $199 per-evaluation alternative — is governed by §44 (Solo-Tier Surface Treatment, Phase 14.10), §13.11 (Defense View, Phase 14.5), §3.14 / §2.8 (Pipeline Compression / Single-Operator Mode, Phase 14.4 / 14.6), §22.20 (Surface Compression, Phase 14.8), and Appendix M (Surface/Engine Mapping).

The `buyer_solo` and `seller_solo` values were authored as forward-references in Phases 14.4–14.6 (with operational aliasing to Business Starter / Seller Starter pending Phase 14.9 landing) and are made authoritative in this phase. The Solo column tier abbreviations registered for §39 / Appendix M / §5.11 inline tier lists are **Bs** (Buyer Solo) and **sSo** (Seller Solo); existing abbreviations (F, St, Gr, Sc, Ent on the Buyer side; sF, sSt, sGr, sSc, sEnt on the Seller side) are preserved.
- **Feature Access Matrix** (§5.11) is updated to (a) gate billing-admin actions to the `billing_admin` role, (b) gate per-capability access to plan tiers per the Entitlement Matrix in §34.8, (c) include rows for the §34.13 Pro Trial Seat issuance flow, and (d) recognize Solo as the surface destination for the §4.3.1 `evaluation_owner_mode=solo` default on the Buyer side (Solo and Free both default to `solo`; Solo's surface is the personal-card on-ramp variant of the same single-operator surface). ### 34.2.3 Universal Commercial Rules

1. **Trial.** A 14-day Business Starter trial is auto-applied to every Buyer signup (no credit card; §34.9). Seller Free is the seller-side on-ramp (no trial; SPS §15) — the Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat (M17, §34.13) is a separate, buyer-issued 30-day Seller Starter grant.
2. **Per-organization billing.** Unlimited seats on every paid tier (Buyer + Seller). Seat count is not a billing dimension; §34.7 is informational only.
3. **Vendor response to an invited evaluation is always free.** A vendor invited to a specific buyer's evaluation can always respond in full, end-to-end, on Seller Free. This is the supply-side growth promise (SPS §1) and is enforced by the Entitlement Matrix in §34.8 (capability `bid_workspace_respond` is unconditionally enabled on every Seller plan including Free).
4. **Published Seller Profile is free from day one** (SPS §2.7) and is unconditionally enabled on Seller Free. Publication eligibility requires only domain verification per Basic verification (§12.2 SPS).
5. **Buyer Scale and Buyer Enterprise include monthly Vendor Pro Trial Seat allowances** (§34.13).
6. **Enterprise contracts are annual.** Both Buyer Enterprise and Seller Enterprise require an annual `CommittedSpendContract` (§4.8.8) with a minimum **$12,000/year committed AI value spend** and a minimum **$3,000/month subscription floor**. Volume discount bands on overage are authored canonically in §34.2.4 (single source — never restated inline per the `volume_discount_band_single_source` validator). Bands are derived deterministically per `committed_spend_discount_band` (Appendix J).
7. **Pricing changes for the published Public Pricing API** (§4.8.9) are subject to a 30-day customer notification before `effective_at`; annual contract customers are grandfathered for the remainder of their contract term per §11 BPS / §11 SPS / §4.8.9 acceptance criteria.
8. **Currency, FX, and residency-locked invoicing** follow §4.8.1 (`fx_rate_locked`) and §4.8.3 (`legal_entity`, `residency_locked_entity`). Invoices issue in the Org's `billing_currency`; FX rate is locked at AIOperation settlement time. Data-residency region constrains which legal entity invoices (Sourcera US vs. EU) per MS C.84.
9. **Migration grandfathering.** Existing v6.0.0 Business customers ($499/mo, token-denominated budget) grandfather into Business Growth at the current $499 price for 12 months from the v7.0.0 §34 ship date; re-plan at renewal (BPS §13). Existing Free / Enterprise customers transition under separate runbooks coordinated by Sales Ops; details in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Breaking Changes`.

### 34.2.4 Volume Discount Bands (Enterprise Committed Spend — Authoritative) {#34.2.4-volume-discount-bands}

Authoritative home for the Enterprise `CommittedSpendContract` (§4.8.8) overage-volume discount ladder. Promoted from prose in §34.2.3 #6 in Phase 12.5 (R-06 closure). Bands are derived deterministically from `committed_spend_discount_band` (Appendix J).

| Band | Annual Committed AI Value Spend Threshold | Discount on Overage | Source of Authority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Band 0 (no discount) | \< $25,000 / year | 0% | n/a (below first band) |
| Band 1 | ≥ $25,000 / year | **10%** | BPS §6; SPS §8; MS §2 |
| Band 2 | ≥ $50,000 / year | **15%** | BPS §6; SPS §8; MS §2 |
| Band 3 | ≥ $100,000 / year | **20%** | BPS §6; SPS §8; MS §2 |
| Band 4 | ≥ $250,000 / year | **25%** | BPS §6; SPS §8; MS §2 |

**Authoring rules.**

1. The bands above are the **single authoritative source** for Enterprise volume-discount values. Any §34, §43, BPS, SPS, marketing-collateral, or sales-quote citation MUST reference this table — no inline restatement.
2. Band assignment is computed at `CommittedSpendContract` activation and recomputed on contract renewal; mid-contract band-shift is not supported (§4.8.8 invariant).
3. Adding, removing, or modifying a band is an Ops Finance + Founder dual-signoff action and triggers `pricing_table_breaking_change_requires_30d_notice` per §4.8.9.
4. The bands above are unaffected by §34.3 outcome-based pricing — the discount applies only to overage above the committed pool, never to the committed pool itself.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Deploy-time validator `volume_discount_band_single_source` asserts no other Master Spec section restates band thresholds or discount percentages; new inline restatements fail CI.
2. The Public Pricing API (§4.8.9) `GET /v1/pricing` response SHOULD echo this table verbatim under `enterprise.volume_discount_bands[]` for partner-integration parity.
3. The §34.18.3 plan-mix model uses Band 1 as the median Enterprise Year-1 contract assumption; deviations require AE-12.4-02 founder + GTM-lead sign-off (deferred to release-gating sign-off cycle per AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md).

### 34.2.5 Solo-Tier Per-Evaluation / Per-Bid Charge Orchestration (Authoritative) {#34.2.5-solo-tier-per-evaluation-per-bid-charge-orchestration}

Authoritative home for the **$199 per-evaluation** (Buyer Solo) and **$199 per-bid** (Seller Solo) one-time charge mechanics. Phase 14.9 — landed under v7.1 integration program.

**Buyer Solo per-evaluation charge.**

| Aspect | Value | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Charge amount | $199 USD per completed evaluation | BPS §5.1 |
| Charge trigger | Operator clicks "Export Selection Report PDF" with a finalized Selection Record (`SelectionReport.status = finalized` AND `evaluation_owner_mode = solo`) | BPS §5.4 |
| Charge timing | Stripe charge captured **before** PDF generation; PDF returned only on successful capture | BPS §5.4 |
| Stripe meter event | `sourcera_solo_buyer_per_eval_charge` (new; registered in §34.10.5) | Phase 14.9 (AE) |
| Refund window | 7 calendar days from charge time | BPS §5.4 |
| Refund eligibility check | Selection Report PDF MUST have been opened < 3 times (i.e., no more than 2 recipient downloads OR no more than 2 distinct viewer sessions on the share link) | BPS §5.4 |
| At 3+ opens | Refund is operator-judgment (Sourcera Support discretion) — automated path unavailable | BPS §5.4 |
| Read-only retention post-charge | 90 days from charge timestamp (Workspace + Selection Report + Defense View readable; mutations rejected with `solo_per_eval_retention_window_expired` after 90 days) | BPS §5.4 |
| Mid-eval subscription conversion | If operator converts to subscription mid-evaluation after charge, $199 credits against first month of subscription (no refund) | BPS §5.4 |
| Failure-mode (Stripe charge fails) | PDF generation rejected with HTTP 402 `solo_per_eval_charge_failed`; Workspace remains in `solo_per_eval_charge_pending` state for ≤ 24h with retry CTA; expires to `solo_per_eval_charge_abandoned` if not retried (Workspace remains accessible at Free tier with watermarked Selection Report) | Phase 14.9 (AE) |
| `BillingEvent.charge_kind` enum value | `solo_per_eval` (new in Appendix J `billing_event_charge_kind`) | Phase 14.9 (AE) |

**Seller Solo per-bid charge.**

| Aspect | Value | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Charge amount | $199 USD per submitted bid | SPS §5.1 |
| Charge trigger | Seller clicks "Submit Bid" on a finalized response (`BidResponse.status = ready_to_submit` → `submitted` transition) | SPS §5.4 |
| Charge timing | Stripe charge captured **before** submission delivery to buyer; submission delivered only on successful capture | SPS §5.4 |
| Stripe meter event | `sourcera_solo_seller_per_bid_charge` (new; registered in §34.10.5) | Phase 14.9 (AE) |
| Refund window | 7 calendar days from charge time | SPS §5.4 |
| Refund eligibility check | Buyer MUST NOT have opened the submission (`SubmittedBidResponse.first_buyer_open_at IS NULL`) | SPS §5.4 |
| Buyer-opened beyond refund window | Refund is operator-judgment (Sourcera Support discretion) | SPS §5.4 |
| KB persistence post-charge | KB entries above the Free 50-entry cap persist at the 250-entry Solo ceiling for 90 days from bid submission; after 90 days, entries beyond 50 enter read-only state (preserved, not deleted) per §34.6 downgrade-safe rule | SPS §5.4 |
| Mid-bid subscription conversion | If seller converts to subscription mid-bid after charge, $199 credits against first month of subscription (no refund) | SPS §5.4 |
| Failure-mode (Stripe charge fails) | Submission rejected with HTTP 402 `solo_per_bid_charge_failed`; Bid Workspace remains in `solo_per_bid_charge_pending` state for ≤ 24h with retry CTA; expires to `solo_per_bid_charge_abandoned` if not retried (Bid Workspace remains accessible at Free tier subject to $5 hard cap) | Phase 14.9 (AE) |
| `BillingEvent.charge_kind` enum value | `solo_per_bid` (new in Appendix J `billing_event_charge_kind`) | Phase 14.9 (AE) |

**Cross-cutting orchestration rules.**

1. **Subscription → per-eval / per-bid downgrade is NOT supported mid-cycle.** A Solo subscriber cancelling mid-cycle remains on subscription until renewal. At renewal, the seller / buyer may elect per-evaluation / per-bid pricing (no entitlement gap).
2. **Per-eval / per-bid → subscription conversion is supported mid-eval / mid-bid** with the credit rule above (no refund of the $199; credit applies on first month).
3. **Stripe charge orchestration uses idempotency keys** keyed on `(workspace_id | bid_workspace_id, charge_kind, charge_attempt_seq)` to prevent double-charge on retry. Required by §4.8.1 BillingEvent acceptance criteria.
4. **Refund processing** dispatches `org.solo_per_eval_charge_refunded` / `org.solo_per_bid_charge_refunded` audit events; refunds emit Stripe meter event `sourcera_solo_charge_refunded` with the original `charge_kind` carried in `metadata.original_charge_kind`.
5. **Plan-tier behavior at Workspace / Bid Workspace creation under Solo per-eval / per-bid:**
   - Workspace creation is GATED until charge captures (Buyer Solo per-eval flow charges on Selection Report export, NOT on Workspace creation — so a Workspace can be authored, edited, and finalized BEFORE the $199 charge fires; Free-tier ceilings apply during the work). The charge effectively converts the Free-tier Workspace's outputs (Selection Report + Defense View) to Solo-tier outputs at export time.
   - Bid Workspace creation is NOT gated (a Free-tier seller can author a draft response without paying). The $199 charge fires on Submit; pre-submit the Bid Workspace operates under Free entitlements (with $5 hard cap and watermarked outputs). On charge capture, retroactive Solo benefits apply to the post-submit retention window only — Free's $5 hard cap and Free-tier KB ceiling DURING drafting are NOT reversed.
6. **Solo per-eval / per-bid charge does NOT pool with the Org-level AIWallet.** The Solo absorbed envelope is engine-side per §44 and does not contribute to overage_balance, included_budget_remaining, or any other §34.10.1 wallet counter visible to the customer. Stripe meter events for Solo charges are reported under their own meter family.
7. **Subscription-based Solo activations charge monthly via the standard Stripe subscription mechanism** ($49 annual / $59 monthly billed in 1-month or 12-month invoicing terms per §34.2.3 #2). No per-eval / per-bid orchestration applies to subscription Solo accounts.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. The Solo per-eval charge MUST fire on Selection Report PDF export for Buyer Solo accounts on per-eval billing; QA test `solo_buyer_per_eval_charge_on_pdf_export` asserts.
2. The Solo per-bid charge MUST fire on bid submission for Seller Solo accounts on per-bid billing; QA test `solo_seller_per_bid_charge_on_submit` asserts.
3. The 7-day refund window with < 3-open automated check (Buyer) or buyer-not-opened check (Seller) MUST be evaluated automatically at refund-request time; QA tests `solo_buyer_per_eval_refund_open_threshold` and `solo_seller_per_bid_refund_buyer_opened_threshold` assert.
4. Mid-eval / mid-bid subscription conversion MUST credit the $199 against the first month of subscription (no refund); QA test `solo_per_charge_mid_cycle_conversion_credit` asserts.
5. Stripe charge failure MUST hold the Workspace / Bid Workspace in the `*_charge_pending` state for ≤ 24h with retry CTA; QA test `solo_per_charge_failure_retry_window` asserts.
6. The `BillingEvent.charge_kind` enum extension (`solo_per_eval`, `solo_per_bid`) MUST be registered in Appendix J `billing_event_charge_kind`; deploy-time validator `solo_charge_kind_registered` asserts.
7. The deploy-time validator `solo_tier_numeric_single_source` (per §34.1.3) MUST flag any inline restatement of the $199 figure outside §34.1, §34.2.1, §34.2.2, or §34.2.5; CI fails on drift.

## 34.3 Outcome-Based AI Operation Pricing {#34.3-outcome-based-ai-operation-pricing-(overage-rate-card)}

All customer-billed AI Operations (§4.8.1 AIOperation) are priced on an outcome basis. Each operation resolves as `accepted`, `auto_accepted`, or `rejected` per the OutcomeContract (§4.8.4) bound to its `capability_id`, with the value posted to the Org's AIWallet (§4.8.3) per the priority rules in §34.10.

### 34.3.1 Pricing Formula (Authoritative)

For every customer-billed CapabilityRegistryEntry (§4.8.2), the per-operation prices are derived deterministically:

```
value_price_cents[capability] = MAX(min_value_price_cents[capability], cost_base_cents[capability] × 10)
cost_price_cents[capability]  = MAX(min_cost_price_cents[capability],  cost_base_cents[capability] × 1.05)
```

- `cost_base_cents` is re-derived nightly from actual Anthropic billing + Convex compute allocation per §34.3.3 and §4.8.6 CostBaseRecalculationLog.
- `min_value_price_cents` and `min_cost_price_cents` are floor values configured per CapabilityRegistryEntry (§4.8.2). Floors prevent micro-priced capabilities from rounding to $0 and protect against pathological cost-base collapses (e.g., model price drops to ~0).
- Multiplier `× 10` (accepted) and `× 1.05` (rejected) is a **margin-floor invariant** held constant across the platform. Changing the multiplier is an Ops-Finance dual-signoff action and produces a `pricing_table_breaking_change_requires_30d_notice` enforcement gate per §4.8.9.
- Floor enforcement is performed at price-update time inside the cost-base recalculation job (§34.3.3); a cost-base recalc that would drop blended margin below the **88% margin floor** (per BPS §2.4 / SPS §2.2) triggers `cost_base_recalc.margin_floor_breach` (§34.11.3) and **does not auto-publish** — Ops Finance must explicitly approve.

### 34.3.2 Customer-Visible Surfaces

Pricing surfaces to customers in three modes only:

| Surface | When | What the customer sees | Per-op price visible? |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Included Budget** | Default for every plan | Single number: "AI budget used this month: $X of $Y in value-dollars" | No |
| **Wallet Overage** | When admin has explicitly enabled wallet overage and operations exceed the included budget | Per-capability rate card (§34.3.4); per-op charge appears in the Billing Ledger (§4.8.1 / API §32 — endpoint pending per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Endpoint Additions`); soft 80% notification + hard cap at configured ceiling | Yes |
| **Committed Spend (Enterprise)** | When `CommittedSpendContract.status=active` (§4.8.8) | Burn-down view: "Committed: $W of $Z value-dollars consumed YTD"; volume discount band displayed | No (per-op aggregated) |

### 34.3.3 Cost-Base Recalculation (Operational Policy Layer)

Entity-level mechanics live in §4.8.6 CostBaseRecalculationLog. The §34 policy layer fixes the operational rules:

| Rule | Value | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Recalc cadence | Nightly at 03:00 UTC | §4.8.6 AC #1 (authoritative); BPS §11 / SPS §9 narrative reconciled to §4.8.6 |
| Per-capability drift threshold (no notification, audit only — `normal`) | `\|drift\| ≤ 5%` | §4.8.6 `cost_base_recalc_drift_severity` enum |
| Per-capability drift threshold (Finance-aware, auto-publish — `warning_5_10`) | `5% < \|drift\| ≤ 10%` | §4.8.6 enum |
| Per-capability drift threshold (Finance-approval gate — `alert_10_25`) | `10% < \|drift\| ≤ 25%` | §4.8.6 AC #2 (authoritative); supersedes any prior §34.3.3 25%-auto-publish-block reading. Phase 7 V7 D-CONS-001 remediation 2026-05-07. |
| Per-capability drift threshold (Finance-approval gate, elevated severity — `critical_gt_25`) | `\|drift\| > 25%` OR margin-floor breach | §4.8.6 AC #2 + AC #3 |
| Margin-floor invariant (blended) | ≥ 88% | BPS §2.6; SPS §2.2 |
| Customer notification window for breaking-change publishes | ≥ 30 days before `effective_at` | §4.8.9; BPS §11 |
| Annual-contract grandfathering | Contract remainder, then re-plan at renewal | BPS §13 |
| Recalc inputs (sample window) | Prior 30-day rolling window of Anthropic invoice events + Convex compute allocation per `posthog_event_name` mapping | §4.8.2; §4.8.6 (Phase 7 V7 D-CONS-005 remediation — 30-day window supersedes prior 24h reading for statistical adequacy on low-volume capabilities) |

**Authoritative publish-gating rule (Phase 7 V7 D-CONS-001 remediation, 2026-05-07).** A cost-base recalc that produces `drift_severity ∈ {normal, warning_5_10}` AND `margin_floor_breach=false` **auto-publishes** a new `PricingTableVersion` (§4.8.9) within 60 seconds of recalc completion (per §4.8.6 AC #5). A recalc that produces `drift_severity ∈ {alert_10_25, critical_gt_25}` OR `margin_floor_breach=true` **does NOT auto-publish**; the recalc enters `pending_finance_approval` (§4.8.6 state machine) and an Ops Finance approver must explicitly approve, override (e.g., deprecate the capability), or roll back per §4.8.6 state machine. Concretely: a 12% drift on `policy_parsing` enters `pending_finance_approval` and blocks auto-publish until Ops Finance approves. The §4.8.6 AC #2 wording is canonical; the prior §34.3.3 row reading "≥ 25% auto-publish block" is **retired** and any code referencing the 25% threshold MUST migrate to the §4.8.6 enum membership check. Deploy-time validator `cost_base_publish_gate_threshold_single_source` (Appendix M.5) asserts the gate is evaluated against the §4.8.6 enum — never against an inline 25% threshold.

### 34.3.3.A Notice-Window Margin-Trajectory Enforcement (Phase 7 V7 D-V7-001 Remediation)

The §34.3.3 publish-gating decision happens at recalc time. The published price's `effective_at` is bounded to ≥ 30 days after publish for breaking-change publishes (§4.8.9 AC #3); for the 30-day notice window, *new* AIOperations continue to bill at the *old* `value_price_cents` (locked per §4.8.1 AC #4 + §4.8.4 AC #2) against the *new* `cost_base_cents`. This produces a **margin-trajectory window** during which blended margin compresses without the customer-facing price having risen. The §34.20.2 AC #7 88% margin floor must be enforced not only at recalc-publish time but also against the projected blended-margin trajectory over the notice window.

The Outcome Resolver and the cost-base recalc job collectively enforce the following decision tree at recalc time, after publish-gating but before commit:

| Projected blended margin over notice window | Operator action | Audit / event |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| ≥ 88% throughout the 30-day window (no trajectory breach) | Auto-publish or Finance-approve per the publish-gating rule. No additional action. | §4.8.6 `auto_applied` or `approved`; standard `pricing_table_version.published` webhook fires |
| ≥ 88% at recalc time but < 88% projected at any point in the 30-day window (trajectory breach) | **Block recalc publish** at the §4.8.6 state machine until one of: (a) Ops Finance approves a margin-absorption decision per §34.3.5 (overage routes to `Sourcera Cost Center: Operations`); OR (b) Ops Finance approves a customer-comm notice that pulls the published price within the notice window for non-grandfathered customers (annual-contract customers grandfathered to original notice per §34.5.1); OR (c) the offending capability transitions to `deprecated` per §4.8.2 with a `successor_capability_id`. | `cost_base_recalc.notice_window_trajectory_breach` (Appendix C; HMAC-SHA256 signed; recipient: `ops_finance_admin`); `pricing_table_version` row remains in `draft` until Finance acts. Customer notification suppressed until path (a) / (b) / (c) decided. |
| < 88% at recalc time (immediate margin-floor breach) | `margin_floor_breach=true` per §4.8.6 — already routes to `pending_finance_approval`. No auto-publish path. | `cost_base_recalc.margin_floor_breach` (Appendix C; existing) |

**Projected-blended-margin trajectory computation.** The cost-base recalc job computes the projected margin trajectory using:

```
projected_blended_margin_at_day_d = 1 - (
  SUM(forecast_aiop_volume[capability] × new_cost_base_cents[capability] for capability in customer_billed_active)
  /
  SUM(forecast_aiop_volume[capability] × old_value_price_cents[capability] for capability in customer_billed_active)
)
```

Forecast AIOperation volume is the prior 30-day rolling average per capability per `posthog_event_name`. The projection horizon is 30 days from `recalc_run_at`; any day on which the projected margin is < 88% triggers the trajectory-breach gate.

**Annual-contract grandfathering interaction.** Annual-contract customers are grandfathered through any breaking-change publish for the remainder of their contract term (§4.8.9 + BPS §13). The trajectory breach calculation uses the *blended* margin across the full active customer population including grandfathered customers. Path (b) — pulling the published price within the notice window — applies only to the non-grandfathered subset; grandfathered customers continue at their pre-publish price until renewal. Path (a) — margin absorption — covers the grandfathered remainder.

**Deploy-time validator.** `cost_base_recalc_notice_window_trajectory_gate` (Appendix M.5) asserts: every `auto_applied` or `approved` `CostBaseRecalculationLog` row whose new prices increase any `value_price_cents` MUST have a recorded projected-blended-margin trajectory ≥ 88% throughout the 30-day notice window OR a paired `margin_absorption_decision` audit row OR a `customer_comm_pull_published_price` audit row OR a paired capability `deprecated` transition. Missing trajectory metadata fails the deploy gate.

**Convex / Stripe / Anthropic stack alignment.** Anthropic invoice events arrive via the daily Anthropic Usage API ingestion job (Convex scheduled function); Convex compute allocation is read from internal Convex telemetry via `posthog_event_name` join keys. Stripe Treasury daily snapshot is the FX-rate source for cross-currency margin projections (§4.8.1 line 8170). The trajectory-breach gate is implemented as a Convex scheduled function fork that, on breach, writes the `cost_base_recalc.notice_window_trajectory_breach` event to the §31 webhook outbox and the audit log; the publish path remains held until Finance acts via the Ops Console (§50).

### 34.3.5 Sourcera-Owned and Platform-Marketing Capabilities

Per `capability_registry_billing_mode` (§4.8.2; Appendix J), capabilities are partitioned into three billing modes:

| Mode | Wallet behavior | Customer billing | Cost center | Examples |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `customer_billed` | Draws AIWallet (or FreeAllowance, or commit pool) | Yes | Customer Org | Pre-Scoring, KB Bootstrap, First-Pass RFP Draft |
| `sourcera_owned` | Never draws AIWallet | No | `Sourcera Cost Center: Operations` | Internal Ops triage, Convex query optimization helpers, Trust & Safety classifiers |
| `platform_marketing` | Never draws AIWallet | No | `Sourcera Cost Center: Platform Marketing` | M9 Category Page FAQ generation, M10 How-to-Evaluate Guides, M11 Comparison Pages, M12 Market Intelligence Reports, M13 Heat Map cell summaries |

Customer wallets are never charged for `sourcera_owned` or `platform_marketing` capabilities even if invoked from a customer surface; the Billing Ledger excludes these rows from customer-visible reports per §4.8.1 read serializer and §4.8.2 `cost_center_default`.

## 34.4 No Per-Unit Metering on Structural Resources {#34.4-no-per-unit-metering-on-structural-resources}

The following structural resources are **never priced per unit** under any plan, including Enterprise. They are tier ceilings only (§34.1) and are subject to the §34.6 downgrade-excess preservation policy when downgraded. This rule is invariant — pricing-strategy changes that would introduce per-unit metering on any resource in this list MUST require Founder + Sales-Ops dual-signoff and a Breaking Change entry.

| Resource | Why never per-unit | Tier-ceiling reference |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Storage (GB)** | Cheap; metering punishes upload of supporting evidence | §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 |
| **Workspaces / Bid Workspaces** | Active count is a usage signal, not a cost driver | §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 |
| **Requirements per Workspace** | Granularity of the Sourcera Method; metering corrupts evaluation quality | §34.1.1 |
| **Use Cases per Workspace** | Decomposition primitive of the Method | §34.1.1 |
| **KB Entries** | KB density is the seller's moat; metering suppresses the very investment the platform wants | §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 |
| **Vendors tracked / Capability Declarations / SellerSoftware Entities** | Marketplace-inventory contributors; metering dampens supply-side growth | §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 |
| **Seats / Members** | Procurement and vendor response are cross-functional; seat tax suppresses the exact collaboration the platform requires | §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 (§34.7) |
| **Guest invitations** | Stakeholder breadth is a Method primitive (M1 Stakeholder Read-Only Invite) | §5.4 |
| **Q&A threads, Comments, Internal Comments, Selection Reports** | Output artifacts; metering output destroys workflow velocity | AE (preserved) |
| **Audit log entries** | Compliance requirement; metering creates incentives to suppress audit | §40.2 |
| **Webhook deliveries** | Integration density; metering suppresses adoption | §31.5 |
| **API requests (non-AI)** | Plane is rate-limited (§32.4) but never per-call billed; AI calls follow §34.3 | §32.4 |

The single metered surface is **AI value-dollars** consumed via §34.3 outcome-accounted AIOperations. All other limits in §34.1 are soft tier ceilings enforced via `Entitlement Matrix` (§34.8) and `DowngradeExcessDataBucket` (§4.8.10) when exceeded.

## 34.5 Plan Upgrade / Downgrade {#34.5-plan-upgrade-/-downgrade}

### 34.5.1 Upgrade

| Aspect | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Effective time | Immediately on Stripe subscription change webhook receipt |
| Proration | Prorated charge for the remainder of the current billing cycle, calculated as `(new_plan_price − old_plan_price) × (days_remaining / days_in_period)` |
| Carry-over | All KB entries, in-flight evaluations / bids, Capability Declarations, Firecrawl source configs, Workspace state, RBAC assignments, audit log, Internal Comments, Pro Trial Seat balances, and DowngradeExcessDataBucket restorations are preserved; no data loss |
| Wallet behavior | `included_budget_remaining` (§4.8.3) is increased to the new plan's monthly budget at the next billing cycle (no in-period budget catch-up); overage cap and auto-topup configuration carry over unchanged |
| Audit | `org.plan_changed` audit event with prior + new plan tier and actor user_id |
| Notification | `plan_upgrade_complete` (Appendix C — to be added per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Webhook Additions`) emailed to Org Owner and `billing_admin` with the upgrade summary and carry-over confirmation |
| Free Allowance | Pre-existing FreeAllowanceCounter rows (§4.8.7) are unaffected by upgrade; they continue to decrement as designed |
| CTA copy requirement | Upgrade CTAs MUST explicitly state carry-over: "Your N KB entries, M in-flight evaluations, and your wallet configuration carry over automatically." |
| Solo throttling-pressure CTA | Solo throttling-pressure upgrade CTAs are governed only by §44.6.5.A. Buyer Solo routes to `business_starter`; Seller Solo routes to `seller_starter`. The `upgrade_completed.trigger` value is `solo_envelope_pressure`. The throttling toast itself MUST NOT include the CTA; the CTA renders only in the §44.6.2 single-card upgrade rail or the §34.5 plan-change surface. |

### 34.5.2 Downgrade

| Aspect | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Effective time | At the next billing cycle (`current_period_ends_at` per §4.8.3) |
| Pre-effective warning | If current usage exceeds the new plan's cap on any resource, customer is warned **14 days before the effective downgrade** with a specific overage list and confirmation gate; the `plan_downgrade_warning` notification (Appendix C, existing) carries the overage line items |
| Excess-data preservation | All preserved entities enter the §34.6 90-day read-only preservation flow via `DowngradeExcessDataBucket` (§4.8.10) on the effective downgrade timestamp |
| Wallet behavior | `included_budget_remaining` resets to the new plan's monthly budget at the next billing anniversary; `overage_balance` retains any deposited funds (refundable on request); `committed_remaining` (Enterprise → non-Enterprise) follows §4.8.8 `shortfall_policy` (default `forfeit`, alternates require explicit signature) |
| Audit | `org.plan_changed` audit event with prior + new plan tier and actor user_id |
| Pro Trial Seat balance (Buyer Scale → lower) | Unused Pro Trial Seats (§34.13) for the current cycle are forfeited at the downgrade boundary; new monthly allowances at the new plan tier apply from the next cycle |
| Notification | `plan_downgrade_complete` (Appendix C, existing) emailed to Org Owner and `billing_admin` |
| Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seats already issued | Trials in flight continue under their original 30-day window regardless of buyer downgrade; the buyer's audit trail retains the issuance record |

### 34.5.3 Pre-Downgrade Validation (Performed at Customer Confirmation Click)

Before allowing a downgrade to proceed, the platform MUST compute the diff between current usage and the new plan caps and surface it in the confirmation UI:

| Resource | Cap diff surfaced | Action available to customer in 14-day window |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Active Workspaces / Bid Workspaces | Show count over cap | Archive selected workspaces (soft delete; recoverable) |
| Requirements over cap | Per-workspace count | Archive use cases / requirements; export |
| KB entries over cap | Total count | Archive selected entries; export |
| Vendors tracked over cap | Total count | Archive vendors; export |
| API Keys / Webhook endpoints over cap | Count over cap | Revoke selected; export configurations |
| Storage over cap | GB over | Delete selected files; export |
| Capability Declarations / SellerSoftware over cap | Count over | Archive selected; export |
| Firecrawl sources over cap | Count over | Disable selected sources |
| Active in-flight bids over concurrency cap (Seller) | Count over | Submit or close bids; can also choose which ones go read-only |

If at the effective downgrade timestamp the customer has not resolved overages, §34.6 auto-archive applies.

### 34.5.4 Solo Throttling-Pressure Upgrade CTA

**Purpose.** This subsection binds the Buyer Pricing v3 §5.3 / §11 and Seller Pricing v3 §5.3 / §15.3 Solo expansion promise to a buildable plan-upgrade trigger. It does not alter the §44.6.4 throttling toast. The toast remains an operational surface with no upsell copy; this trigger controls a separate plan-change CTA after sustained or per-unit envelope pressure.

| Console / Solo billing mode | Trigger source | Threshold | Target plan | CTA copy source | Analytics |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Buyer Solo subscription | `solo.envelope.throttling_engaged` | ≥ 3 events in a rolling 30-day window per `(org_id, console=buyer)` | `business_starter` | "Starter unlocks the visible AI budget defined in §34.1.1 and lifts background-suggestion limits." | `upgrade_cta_viewed.triggering_event = billing.solo_upgrade_cta.triggered`; `upgrade_completed.trigger = solo_envelope_pressure` |
| Buyer Solo per-evaluation | `solo.envelope.exhausted` inside the charged evaluation envelope window | First event in that evaluation | `business_starter` | Same as Buyer Solo subscription | Same as above, with `solo_upgrade_cta_trigger_mode = per_eval_envelope_hit` |
| Seller Solo subscription | `solo.envelope.throttling_engaged` | ≥ 3 events in a rolling 30-day window per `(org_id, console=seller)` | `seller_starter` | "Starter unlocks the visible AI budget defined in §34.1.2 and lifts background-suggestion limits." | Same as above, with `console=seller` |
| Seller Solo per-bid | `solo.envelope.exhausted` inside the charged bid envelope window | First event in that bid | `seller_starter` | Same as Seller Solo subscription | Same as above, with `solo_upgrade_cta_trigger_mode = per_bid_envelope_hit` |

**Event contract.** A qualifying threshold writes `billing.solo_upgrade_cta.triggered` (Appendix C) and PostHog `solo_upgrade_cta_triggered` (Appendix G). The payload MUST include `org_id`, `console`, `plan_from`, `plan_to`, `solo_upgrade_cta_trigger_mode`, `source_event_id`, `envelope_window_id`, `rolling_window_started_at` (nullable for per-evaluation / per-bid), and `cta_surface`. It MUST NOT include `consumed_value_cents`, `envelope_value_cents`, raw prompt content, vendor identity, buyer identity, or any per-capability spend breakdown.

**Idempotency.** Subscription-mode triggers are idempotent for 30 days per `(org_id, console, solo_upgrade_cta_trigger_mode)`. Per-evaluation triggers are idempotent per `(org_id, console, evaluation_workspace_id, solo_upgrade_cta_trigger_mode)`. Per-bid triggers are idempotent per `(org_id, console, bid_workspace_id, solo_upgrade_cta_trigger_mode)`.

**Surface placement.** The CTA MAY render on the §44.6.2 single-card billing surface and on the §34.5 plan-change surface. It MUST NOT render inside the §44.6.4 throttling toast, the §29 notification-preferences UI, raw AIOperation rows, or the AIWallet widget (which is hidden on Solo).

## 34.6 Downgrade Excess Data Handling {#34.6-downgrade-excess-data-handling}

§34.6 is the operational policy layer on top of §4.8.10 DowngradeExcessDataBucket. Schema, indexes, and the state machine live in §4.8.10; the rules below are the customer-facing contract.

### 34.6.1 Preservation Window

When a downgrade results in overages on any §34.4 structural resource, the affected entities transition to **read-only preservation** for the §40.2 downgrade-preservation window (`preservation_until = downgrade_at + 90 days`; window value authoritative in §40.2 / §4.8.10). Bucket creation occurs within 5 minutes of downgrade per §4.8.10 acceptance criterion #1; SLO-violating creation triggers Ops alert.

### 34.6.2 Customer Actions During the 90-Day Window

| Action | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Resolve and resume** | Archive selected entities to free quota (soft-deleted, recoverable within the 90-day grace via Ops Console); active count drops below cap; bucket transitions to `restored` partial if applicable |
| **Re-upgrade** | Customer upgrades back to a tier that re-covers all preserved entities; bucket transitions to `restored`; preserved entities transition back to active read-write atomically (§4.8.10 acceptance criterion #4) |
| **Re-upgrade to insufficient tier** | If the upgraded tier covers only a subset, `restoration_partial=true`; the subset restores (customer chooses; UI surfaces the full set with active/keep-bucketed checkboxes); the remainder stays in the bucket; UI surfaces an upgrade-to-cover-all CTA |
| **Export** | Full export available at any time in all supported formats (§40.1); export does NOT remove entities from the bucket (export is non-destructive) |
| **Hard-delete preserved entity** | Customer can choose to permanently delete a preserved entity inside the bucket; this is irreversible and audit-logged with `org.preserved_entity_purged` |

### 34.6.3 Post-Preservation-Window Behavior

At `preservation_until`:

1. The pre-cliff customer notices (60-day and 80-day, fields `notice_d60_sent_at` / `notice_d80_sent_at` per §4.8.10; cadence per §40.2 retention table) have already been sent (one-shot, idempotent).
2. The hard-archive cron picks up the bucket within 1 hour of `preservation_until` (§4.8.10 acceptance criterion #3); SLO breach alerts Ops.
3. Entities are hard-archived to cold storage (S3 Glacier or equivalent) **with the §34.6.3.A Class-1 Protected-Asset Carve-Out applied**; `archive_storage_ref` set; entities hard-deleted from hot storage; metadata preserved for audit.
4. **Cold-storage retention** is authoritative in §4.8.10 (`archive_storage_ref` field definition + acceptance criterion #5: 7-year financial-record-aligned horizon; aligns with §40.2 `extended_financial` retention tier). §34.6 does NOT restate the cold-storage duration; consumers MUST reference §4.8.10. **Phase 7 V7 D-V7-009 remediation**: Class-1 Protected Assets per §34.19.1 carry an extended retention window of 10 years (vs the standard 7-year financial horizon) with extended customer-initiated restoration; see §34.6.3.A.
5. **Restoration window from cold storage** is authoritative in §4.8.10 state machine (`archived → restored` transition: 90 days post-archive Ops-assisted, 24-hour SLA; beyond 180 days post-archive, customer-initiated restoration is no longer supported and the data is legal-retention only). §34.6 does NOT restate the restoration windows; consumers MUST reference §4.8.10. Class-1 Protected Assets carve-out per §34.6.3.A extends the customer-initiated restoration window to 5 years.

### 34.6.3.A Class-1 Protected-Asset Carve-Out (Phase 7 V7 D-V7-009 Remediation, 2026-05-07)

The §34.19.1 13-asset Protected Asset list and the §34.19.6 #2 protected-asset-downgrade firewall previously read as forbidding hard-archive of Class-1 assets entirely. The §34.6.3 hard-archive cron contract reads as mandating hard-archive at `preservation_until`. Phase 7 V7 D-V7-009 reconciles the two contracts by introducing the **Class-1 Protected-Asset Carve-Out**: Class-1 assets DO hard-archive (cron contract preserved) but with an **extended cold-storage retention window** and **extended customer-initiated restoration** that materially exceeds the standard 90-day post-archive Ops-assisted window. The carve-out preserves both the operational cron contract and the §34.19.1 "100% retained, read-write" commitment by guaranteeing customer-initiated restoration without Ops intervention for the 5-year window.

| Aspect | Standard (non-Class-1) | Class-1 Protected Assets |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Cold-storage retention | 7 years (§4.8.10 AC #5) | 10 years |
| Customer-initiated restoration window | 0 days post-archive (Ops-assisted only) | 5 years post-archive (self-service via Settings → Billing → "Restore preserved data") |
| Ops-assisted restoration window | 90 days post-archive (24h SLA) | 5 years post-archive (24h SLA at any point in window) |
| Hard-archive forbidden? | No | **No (revised; previously read as forbidden)** — but preserves Class-1 commitment via 5-year self-service restoration |
| Customer-cost transparency | None (standard preservation) | Surface in Settings → Billing: "N Class-1 assets in cold storage; restore at any time within 5 years (free)" |
| `preservation_status` | `archived` (§4.8.10 enum value) | `archived_class_1_protected` (Phase 7 V7 D-V7-009 — new value added to §4.8.10 `status` enum + Appendix J `downgrade_excess_data_bucket_status`) |

The `protected_asset_downgrade_firewall` deploy-time validator (§34.20.16 AC #80) is updated to assert that Class-1 assets enter `status=archived_class_1_protected` (NOT `status=archived`) and that the cold-storage retention metadata (`archive_retention_horizon_years`) is set to 10 (NOT 7). The `preservation_status=hard_archived` field name referenced in the prior §34.19.6 #2 wording is retired; the validator now asserts against the canonical §4.8.10 `status` enum membership.

**Customer-facing rendering.** Solo→Free downgrade (Seller Solo with 240 KB → Seller Free 50 KB cap) produces a 190-entry Class-1 KB DowngradeExcessDataBucket. The customer sees, at any point in the 5-year window, a "Restore my preserved KB entries" CTA in Settings → Billing. Restoration is self-service, atomic (per §34.6.2 row "Re-upgrade"), and 24h-SLO bounded. The Public Pricing API and §40.2 retention table are updated to reference the §34.6.3.A carve-out.

**Stack alignment.** Cold-storage entities are stored in S3 Glacier (10-year retention); restoration triggers a Convex action that invokes the S3 Glacier `RestoreObject` API and writes the entity rows back into the Convex database with `restored_at` stamped. PostHog tracks `class_1_protected_asset_restored` with `(org_id, asset_class, entity_count)` for product-quality dashboards. Loops.so handles the customer notification on restoration completion. Ops Finance dashboards in Convex track aggregate Class-1 cold-storage volume and 5-year-cohort restoration rates for storage-cost forecasting.

### 34.6.4 Entities Subject to Downgrade Enforcement

Per §4.8.10 `downgrade_excess_data_class` enum (Appendix J): `workspaces`, `requirements_over_cap`, `kb_entries_over_cap`, `vendors_over_cap`, `capability_declarations_over_cap`, `seller_software_over_cap`, `firecrawl_sources_over_cap`, `concurrent_bids_over_cap`, `seller_signals_over_cap`, `evaluations_over_cap`. Additional resources are added by appending to this enum and to the §34.5.3 validation table in the same edit.

### 34.6.5 Entities NEVER Subject to Downgrade Enforcement

| Resource | Why preserved |
| :---- | :---- |
| Seats / Members | Per §34.7, seats are unlimited on every paid tier and never billed |
| Published Seller Profile + SellerOrgPage / SoftwarePage | Marketplace-inventory contributors; SPS §17.1 honest portability commitment |
| Audit log entries | Compliance requirement; retention is plan-tier-controlled per §40.2 |
| Billing history / AIOperation rows / AIWallet financial state | Financial records; retention is 7 years (§40.2) regardless of plan |
| ContestRecord / CommittedSpendContract / PricingTableVersion / DowngradeExcessDataBucket itself | Financial / Ops audit records (§40.2) |
| BillingSeatSnapshot | Reporting record (§40.2) |
| KB Documents that have been cited in any submitted bid (Seller side) | SPS §17.1 portability commitment — citations are seller IP and survive downgrade in read-only state |

### 34.6.6 DSAR / Right-to-Erasure Interaction

Per §6.8 and §40.2, DSAR right-to-erasure for an Org with `archived` data MUST purge cold-storage rows in addition to hot-storage. The legal-retention exception preserves financial records (AIOperation, ContestRecord, CommittedSpendContract, etc.) under `data_retention_tier=extended_financial`; non-financial preserved entities (KB entries, Workspaces, etc.) are purged on DSAR within 30 days regardless of preservation state.

### 34.6.7 Notifications

| Trigger | Notification | Recipient | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Bucket created on downgrade | `downgrade_bucket.created` | Org Owner, `billing_admin` | Pending — `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Webhook Additions` |
| 60-day notice (30 days remaining) | `downgrade_bucket.notice_d60` (existing `plan_downgrade_warning` superseded for bucket-specific case) | Org Owner, `billing_admin` | §4.8.10 |
| 80-day notice (10 days remaining) | `downgrade_bucket.notice_d80` | Org Owner, `billing_admin` | §4.8.10 |
| Hard archive | `downgrade_bucket.archived` | Org Owner, `billing_admin` | §4.8.10 |
| Restoration on upgrade | `downgrade_bucket.restored` (with partial-restoration flag) | Org Owner, `billing_admin` | §4.8.10 |

## 34.7 Billing Seat Count {#34.7-billing-seat-count}

Per MS C.86 and §4.8.11 BillingSeatSnapshot, Sourcera does **NOT bill per seat** under any plan. Seats are unlimited on every paid tier (BPS §3 / SPS §3 / MS §2). §34.7 documents the policy rules that govern the periodic seat counter used for reporting and plan-gate enforcement only.

### 34.7.1 What Counts as a Seat

| Identity kind | Counted as seat? | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Organization member with `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `member`, or `billing_admin` role | Yes | §5.2 |
| Workspace member (Workspace Owner, Workspace Admin, Use Case Lead, Reviewer) | Yes | §5.3 |
| Guest invited to a workspace via Guest Permission Profile (`read_only`, `contributor`, `scorer`, `full_participant`) | **No** — explicitly excluded | MS C.86; §4.8.11 |
| API-only identity (token-only user, no human session) | **No** — explicitly excluded | MS C.86; §4.8.11 |
| Deprovisioned member (`deleted_at IS NOT NULL`) | **No** — excluded; reassigned ownership preserved per §40.2 | §40.2 |
| Members deleted in trailing 30 days | Excluded from `active_seats_count`; reported separately as `deleted_count_30d` | §4.8.11 |

### 34.7.2 Snapshot Cadence and Triggers

| Trigger | Snapshot taken |
| :---- | :---- |
| Monthly cron | 1st of each month at 02:00 UTC for every active Org (§4.8.11 acceptance criterion #1) |
| Plan change | Within 60 seconds of any plan-tier change on either console (§4.8.11 acceptance criterion #2) |
| Stripe invoice generation | At invoice creation, linked via `linked_stripe_invoice_id` |
| Manual audit (Ops) | On-demand via Ops Console; `trigger=manual_audit` |
| DSAR request | Snapshot taken at DSAR start to preserve seat-state context |
| Ops capacity review | Quarterly, for cohort planning |

### 34.7.3 Plan-Gate Enforcement (Soft)

The v6.0.0 §39 / §34.1 had `max_members` caps per plan tier. Under v2 the plan tiers **do not enforce a seat cap as a billing dimension**. The `plan_max_members_at_snapshot` field on BillingSeatSnapshot is preserved for legacy compatibility and is informational only:

- `plan_gate_breach_flag=true` (when `active_seats_count > plan_max_members_at_snapshot`) is **informational only**; Sourcera does NOT block invoicing or feature access on seat count.
- The breach surfaces as an upgrade prompt to `org_owner` and `billing_admin` ("You have N members; consider plan X for additional governance features"), per §4.8.11 acceptance criterion #4.
- The Public Pricing API MUST NOT expose per-seat pricing under any plan; QA test `pricing_api_no_per_seat_pricing` asserts (§4.8.11 acceptance criterion #6).

### 34.7.4 Deprovisioning Behavior

- A deprovisioned user (via SCIM or manual deletion) remains in the audit trail with full attribution.
- Owned entities (Workspaces, Use Cases, KB entries, etc.) are reassigned per §5.3 ownership-reassignment rules within 24 hours of deprovisioning per §40.2.
- The deprovisioned user's identifiable PII is purged on DSAR per §6.8; financial-attribution fields (e.g., `actor_id` on AIOperation) are pseudonymized but the row is preserved.
- Seat count drops at the next snapshot.

## 34.8 Entitlement Enforcement {#34.8-entitlement-enforcement}

Entitlement enforcement is the runtime layer that blocks, gates, or surfaces upgrade CTAs for capabilities, features, and AIOperations based on the Org's plan tier(s) and the AIWallet state. Entity-level entitlement state lives in §4.8 (CapabilityRegistryEntry plan-gate fields, AIWallet wallet_state, FreeAllowanceCounter quota_remaining); §34.8 fixes the runtime policy.

### 34.8.1 Enforcement Modes

Per MS C.87, every gated capability has one of two enforcement modes:

| Mode | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Soft** | Feature is **visible** in the UI; attempting to use it surfaces an inline upgrade CTA with the capability's value proposition and a one-click upgrade flow. The capability is NEVER invoked at the API layer; no AIOperation is written. |
| **Hard** | Feature is **hidden** from the UI for users on plans that do not include it. API calls to the capability return HTTP 403 `feature_not_available_on_plan` (Appendix I) with the upgrade path in the error body. |

A capability cannot be both soft and hard for the same plan tier. Mode selection is per `(capability_id, plan_tier_minimum)` and is configured in the CapabilityRegistryEntry plan-gating sub-record.

### 34.8.2 Runtime Enforcement Path

```
const wallet = await ctx.db.aiWalletState(orgId);                // §4.8.3 cached at session metadata level
const buyerEntitlement = PLAN_ENTITLEMENTS[org.buyer_plan_tier]; // §34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix
const sellerEntitlement = PLAN_ENTITLEMENTS[org.seller_plan_tier];
const cap = await ctx.db.capabilityRegistryEntry(capabilityId);  // §4.8.2

// Plan-gate check (hard mode → 403; soft mode → upgrade CTA in result envelope)
if (cap.plan_tier_minimum && org[consoleOf(cap)].plan_tier < cap.plan_tier_minimum) {
  if (cap.enforcement_mode === "hard") {
    throw new ConvexError({ code: "feature_not_available_on_plan", upgrade_cta: cap.plan_tier_minimum });
  }
  return { result: null, upgrade_cta: cap.plan_tier_minimum, blocked_reason: "plan_gate_soft" };
}

// Free Allowance check (per §4.8.7; atomic decrement-and-return)
const freeAllowance = await ctx.db.freeAllowanceCounterAtomicDecrement(orgId, capabilityId);
if (freeAllowance.consumed) {
  // Free op — write AIOperation with billed_against_free_allowance=true; effective_charge_cents=0
  return invokeCapability({ /* ... */, billed_against_free_allowance: true });
}

// Wallet capacity check (commit pool first, then included budget, then overage)
const cost = estimatedCostCents(capabilityId);
if (!walletHasCapacity(wallet, cost)) {
  if (wallet.wallet_state === "hard_capped_100") {
    throw new ConvexError({ code: "wallet_hard_capped", upgrade_cta: walletUpgradePath(org) });
  }
  if (cap.enforcement_mode === "hard") {
    throw new ConvexError({ code: "ai_operation_wallet_insufficient", upgrade_cta: walletUpgradePath(org) });
  }
  return { result: null, upgrade_cta: walletUpgradePath(org), blocked_reason: "wallet_insufficient_soft" };
}

return invokeCapability({ /* ... */ });
```

Entitlement check MUST be O(1) at the cache layer — plan-tier and wallet state are pre-computed into session metadata at session start (§6.3) and refreshed on plan-change webhook receipt or wallet-state transition. Plan-tier lookups are NOT permitted to issue a database round trip per request.

### 34.8.3 Cross-Console Enforcement Isolation

Entitlements are evaluated **independently per console**. The Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2) applies to entitlement checks as it does to data:

- A Buyer console session evaluates buyer-side entitlements only; seller-side capability lookups are forbidden at the API layer (HTTP 403 `console_isolation_violation`).
- Cross-console capabilities (e.g., `kb_suggestion` with `console=cross_console`) are gated by **whichever side initiated the invocation** but draw against the unified Org-pooled AIWallet (§34.10.3).
- The `billing_admin` role is the one exception: a `billing_admin` may read wallet state, contest records, and the cross-console Billing Ledger from either console session (§4.8.3, §4.8.5). Read-only — no data mutations cross the firewall via this role.

### 34.8.4 Free Allowance Interaction

Per §4.8.7 FreeAllowanceCounter and MS C.80, every customer-billed capability grants 10 free operations on first invocation by an Org (default; overridable per CapabilityRegistryEntry). Free Allowance precedence:

1. On first invocation, if no FreeAllowanceCounter row exists for `(org_id, capability_id)`, atomically create one with `quota_total = CapabilityRegistryEntry.free_allowance_quantity_default` (10 by default) and decrement.
2. On subsequent invocations, atomically decrement. If `quota_remaining > 0` after decrement, the AIOperation is written with `billed_against_free_allowance=true` and `effective_charge_cents=0`. Wallet counters are not touched.
3. On exhaustion, stamp `exhaustion_cta_surfaced_at` and `roi_value_dollars_at_exhaustion` (one-shot); subsequent invocations follow standard wallet-draw semantics.
4. The exhaustion-CTA surface MUST display the ROI of the consumed free operations (sum of `value_price_cents` × consumed) to motivate upgrade.

### 34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix (Authoritative)

This matrix is the runtime contract for every plan-gated capability. Format: `capability_id | enforcement_mode | free_allowance_ops | gated_at_plan_minimum (per console) | upgrade_surface`. The matrix is evaluated against the requesting session's console plan tier; capabilities with `console=cross_console` apply to whichever console initiates.

**Matrix maintenance.** New customer-billed capabilities MUST be added to the Entitlement Matrix in the same edit that adds the CapabilityRegistryEntry row (§4.8.2), the rate-card row (§34.14.1 or §34.14.1.b if AE), and the OutcomeContract row (§34.15.1 or §34.15.1.b if AE). Plan-tier minimum changes are Breaking Changes and trigger the 30-day customer notification path per §34.3.3. The matrix is the single source of truth for runtime entitlement evaluation; the runtime cache loads from this table at deploy time.

**Canonical-form lock (post-v7.2.0-REM Phase 4).** Per §32.8.0, `capability_id` values in this matrix MUST NOT carry `buyer_` or `seller_` prefixes. Console applicability is conveyed by the paired Buyer-plan-minimum / Seller-plan-minimum columns. **Side-disambiguation via explicit suffixes is permitted exclusively under the §21.4.1 family-rooted sibling-split pattern**, where both consoles independently register the capability as sibling rows under a shared `capability_family` key with their own §4.8.2 field-set, OutcomeContract, surface_throttling_class, solo_envelope_no_block, and free-allowance defaults. The v7.1.0a registered family splits are: (a) **`kb_suggestion_family` → `kb_suggestion_buyer` / `kb_suggestion_seller`** — registered by the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.2 D-EM-002 closure per §21.4.1.D with full §4.8.2 field-set fidelity for both siblings plus the rollup root, including the console-disambiguated alias-rewrite contract (§21.4.1.D Footnote A) and the `kb_suggestion_family_cardinality` / `kb_suggestion_family_outcome_contract_isolation` / `kb_suggestion_alias_console_resolution_integrity` deploy-time validators; (b) `org_intelligence_family` → `org_intelligence_vendor_history` / `org_intelligence_full` / `org_intelligence_suggestions` (tri-split per §21.4.1 row 16); (c) **`qa_suggestion_family` → `qa_suggestion_buyer` (§18.4) / `qa_suggestion_seller` (§24)** — registered by the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4 D-EM-001 closure per §21.4.1.B with full §4.8.2 field-set fidelity for both siblings. Family-root identifiers (`*_family`) are reserved as billing-ledger rollup display identifiers; direct invocation of a family-root identifier as an AIOperation `capability_id` is rejected at the AI invocation handler with HTTP 422 `capability_rollup_root_not_invokable` (Appendix I), enforced by the `qa_suggestion_family_cardinality` / `org_intelligence_family_cardinality` / `kb_suggestion_family_cardinality` deploy-time validators. Grandfathered `seller_page_enrichment` and `seller_signals_*` identifiers are noun-scoped (the noun being enriched / emitted is the seller Marketplace page / seller signals object) and are whitelisted by the `canonical_capability_id_lock` deploy-time validator. Every `capability_id` cell in the matrix MUST resolve to a `CapabilityRegistryEntry` row in §21.4 (or to a registered exemption class per §34.8.5 line 29755 Platform-internal aggregation classification + the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4 `entitlement_matrix_registry_binding_completeness` CI gate at §M.5.14); reverse-pass enforcement is per §34.8.7 AC #6 hardened by the same gate.

**AE activation lock.** Rows in the "Authored Extensions" block above MUST have an active `AuthoredExtensionSignoff` row for the current `pricing_table_version_id` before the matrix entry is honored at runtime. Until sign-off lands, any entitlement check against an AE `capability_id` returns `capability_not_signed_off` (HTTP 422) per Appendix I. Staging activation is permitted under `rate_card_ae_signoff_bypass_dev_only=true` (§34.14.1.b).

**Platform-internal aggregation classification (Phase 13 inline fix F-3.1.A — 2026-04-26).** The two `*_aggregation` rows in the Platform-owned block (`market_intel_aggregation`, `seller_signal_aggregation`) are platform-internal aggregation pipeline jobs, NOT Agent capabilities, and therefore have NO `CapabilityRegistryEntry` row in §21.4 by design. They are listed in §34.8.5 strictly to make the entitlement-check contract complete (any session that attempts to trigger them at runtime through a customer surface MUST resolve to `n/a (sourcera_owned)` and skip wallet / free-allowance / plan-gate checks). The pipeline-execution surfaces are §51.5 (Seller Usage Parity rollups) for `seller_signal_aggregation` and §4.4.15 / §50.14 (MarketIntelligenceReport editorial pipeline) for `market_intel_aggregation`. The deploy-time validator `entitlement_matrix_to_capability_registry` (Phase 13 follow-on; §6 of `_integration/PHASE13_ENG_REVIEW.md`) honors this classification: rows whose `enforcement_mode = n/a (sourcera_owned)` AND whose name ends in `_aggregation` are exempt from the §21.4 cross-reference assertion.

### 34.8.6 Failure Modes Addressed

1. **Plan downgrade mid-pending AIOperation.** A `pending` AIOperation initiated under the prior plan settles under the prior wallet rules; the new plan's gating applies only to operations created at or after the downgrade effective timestamp. (§4.8.1 acceptance criterion #11; §4.8.10).
2. **Wallet hard-cap reached during an in-flight Managed Agent sub-call tree.** Sub-calls follow §4.8.1 Failure Mode #4: the parent operation marks `rejected` with reason `sub_call_wallet_exhausted`; the partial tree is valid; no orphaned wallet hold remains.
3. **A capability is deprecated mid-period but still invokable within deprecation grace.** Entitlement Matrix continues to honor the prior plan-tier minimum; CapabilityRegistryEntry `state=deprecated` does NOT bypass the gate (§4.8.2 acceptance criterion #4).
4. **Org changes plan tier between session start and capability invocation.** Session metadata refreshes on plan-change webhook receipt within 30 seconds (§4.8.11 acceptance criterion #2). A pre-refresh invocation may evaluate against the old tier; the Outcome Resolver settles the AIOperation under the entitlement state at write time, not at settlement time.

### 34.8.7 Acceptance Criteria

1. Entitlement check MUST be O(1) on the cache layer; database round trips for plan-tier or wallet-state lookups during entitlement evaluation are forbidden.
2. Soft-gated capabilities MUST surface upgrade CTAs in the result envelope (`upgrade_cta`, `blocked_reason`); hard-gated capabilities MUST return HTTP 403 with the same fields in the error body.
3. Free Allowance MUST be exhausted before any wallet draw for `customer_billed` capabilities; verified by §4.8.7 acceptance criterion #2.
4. Cross-console plan-tier evaluations MUST NOT leak across consoles; QA test `entitlement_dual_console_isolation` asserts.
5. Plan-change webhook MUST refresh session metadata within 30 seconds; QA test `entitlement_plan_change_propagation` asserts.
6. Every customer-billed capability in CapabilityRegistryEntry with `state=active` MUST have a row in the §34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix; **AND** every `capability_id` cell in the §34.8.5 matrix MUST resolve to a `CapabilityRegistryEntry` row in §21.4 (any state ∈ {`alpha`, `beta`, `active`, `deprecated`} during the deprecation grace window) **OR** to a registered exemption class. The reverse-direction binding is enforced by the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4 `entitlement_matrix_registry_binding_completeness` CI gate (§M.5.14), which fails closed on any matrix-row `capability_id` that does not resolve to a §21.4 row. Registered exemption classes (closed set; addition requires Pricing Owner + Engineering Lead dual-signoff per §M.5.14 `not_permitted_<rule>` override class): (a) platform-internal aggregation pipeline rows whose `capability_id` ends in `_aggregation` and whose `enforcement_mode = n/a (sourcera_owned)` per §34.8.5 line 29755 inline fix F-3.1.A; (b) non-AI Security/Admin rows (`mfa_enrollment`, `mfa_org_enforcement`, `saml_sso`, `scim_provisioning`, `ip_allowlist_residency`, `custom_branding`, `api_add_on`, `vendor_pro_trial_seat_grant`) whose enforcement is RBAC + plan-tier only, never AI invocation; (c) non-AI Free-Forever Seller surfaces (`bid_workspace_respond`, `seller_profile_publish`) whose enforcement is RBAC + plan-tier only; (d) non-AI Marketplace UI/API surfaces (`marketplace_search_filter`, `marketplace_match_score_view`, `marketplace_batch_match_api`) per §27 Marketplace Discovery surface-class registry; (e) the non-AI Buyer `tco_modeling` row per §21.4.1 row 14 classification-lock paragraph; (f) AE rows in the §34.8.5 "Authored Extensions" block until their `AuthoredExtensionSignoff` row activates (per the existing AE activation lock). Deploy-time validator `entitlement_matrix_registry_binding_completeness` asserts in both directions; per-direction failure-mode codes registered in Appendix I (`entitlement_matrix_unbound_capability_id`, `capability_registry_active_capability_missing_matrix_row`).

## 34.9 Onboarding and Trial Carry-Over {#34.9-onboarding-and-trial-carry-over}

### 34.9.1 Buyer Onboarding (14-Day Business Starter Trial)

| Aspect | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Trigger | New Org signup via Buyer Console (Google/Microsoft SSO; no credit card) |
| Effective plan | `business_starter` for 14 days |
| Wallet | $50 included budget (Business Starter monthly cap, prorated to the trial period); overage off by default; auto-topup off by default |
| Free Allowance | All `customer_billed` capabilities receive their default 10-op allowance per §4.8.7 |
| End-of-trial behavior (day 15, no payment method) | Auto-downgrade to `buyer_free`; `included_budget_remaining` decrements to $5/mo (Free); excess data flow per §34.6 (DowngradeExcessDataBucket) |
| End-of-trial behavior (day 15, payment method on file) | Conversion to chosen plan tier; carry-over per §34.5.1 |
| Trial-expiry notifications | Day 11: `trial_expiring` (Appendix C, existing). Day 14: `trial_expiring_today` (Appendix C — to be added per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Webhook Additions`). Day 15 on auto-downgrade: `plan_downgrade_complete` (existing) + bucket-creation notice if overages |
| Audit | `org.trial_started` and `org.trial_ended` events with actor, plan tier, wallet state |

### 34.9.2 Seller Onboarding (No Trial; Free Is the On-Ramp)

| Aspect | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Trigger | Buyer-invite magic-link click (M1, M5, M15) OR direct seller signup |
| Effective plan | `seller_free` |
| Hero moment | The full SPS §15 "Your first bid is already drafted" flow runs synchronously inside the SSO redirect; KB Bootstrap (Opus, lifetime free) + First-Pass RFP Draft + Published Seller Profile all materialize before the vendor reaches the workspace |
| Wallet | $5 included budget (Seller Free monthly cap); overage off by default; hard cap at $5 (no bill-shock path on Free per BPS §4) |
| Free Allowance | All `customer_billed` seller capabilities receive their default 10-op allowance |
| Anti-pattern controls | Per SPS §16.3 — no credit-card prompt before first upgrade intent click; no pricing page until first bid submitted; no "try Pro free for 14 days" modal on first login |

### 34.9.3 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat Carry-Over (M17)

When a vendor receives a Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat (§34.13), the 30-day Seller Starter trial supersedes the standard Seller Free onboarding. Vendors who arrive via M17 NEVER see Seller Free ceilings during the trial period; on day 31, the trial completes per §34.13.4 with explicit conversion paths:

| Outcome | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Convert | Plan persists at Seller Starter (or upgraded by vendor); included budget resets on new billing cycle; carry-over per §34.5.1 |
| Auto-downgrade | Plan transitions to Seller Free; entities exceeding Free caps enter §34.6 90-day read-only preservation; vendor is NOT subject to a second auto-downgrade if the vendor declines Free preservation by hard-deleting overages |
| Explicit decline | Same as auto-downgrade |

### 34.9.4 Carry-Over Invariants

- **No data loss on any upgrade or downgrade path.** KB entries, in-flight bids/evaluations, Capability Declarations, Firecrawl source configs, Wallet configuration, Pro Trial Seat balance, and bucket state all persist through plan transitions.
- **Wallet counters do NOT carry over across billing periods.** `included_budget_remaining` resets at each billing anniversary (§4.8.3); unused budget is not banked.
- **`overage_balance` deposits DO carry over across periods** until consumed or refunded.
- **Free Allowance is per-Org per-capability lifetime** (default; configurable per-CapabilityRegistryEntry); plan changes do not reset or replenish.

### 34.9.5 90-Day Solo Trial (v2-Cohort Migration)

**Source and scope.** BPS v3 §14 and SPS v3 §21 commit a no-credit-card 90-day Solo trial offer for existing v2-cohort Free customers at the v3 cutover. This section is the authoritative build contract. The trial is a migration mechanic only; it is NOT a standing new-signup trial and MUST NOT appear on first-login Seller Free onboarding (§34.9.2) or the standard Buyer Business Starter trial (§34.9.1).

| Console | Eligible cohort | Trigger | Effective plan during trial | Explicitly unaffected |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Buyer | Existing v2-cohort Org with `buyer_plan_tier = buyer_free` and no prior Buyer Solo migration trial for `(org_id, console=buyer, legal_entity)` | Org Owner or Billing Admin accepts the in-app Solo trial offer surfaced by the v3 migration announcement | `buyer_solo` subscription mode for 90 days; per-evaluation charge mode is disabled during the active trial | Existing Business Starter / Growth / Scale / Enterprise customers; existing Selection Reports generated under v2 keep their grandfathered watermark status per D-14.1-007 |
| Seller | Existing v2-cohort Org with `seller_plan_tier = seller_free` and no prior Seller Solo migration trial for `(org_id, console=seller, legal_entity)` | Seller Org Owner or Billing Admin accepts the in-app Seller Solo trial offer surfaced by the v3 migration announcement | `seller_solo` subscription mode for 90 days; per-bid charge mode is disabled during the active trial | Existing Seller Starter / Growth / Scale / Enterprise customers; v2-cohort KB cap grandfathering remains governed by the pending D-14.2-009 pass |

**TrialState extension.** The existing `Organization.trial_state_ref` forward-reference (§4.2.1) is extended for this migration mechanic. `TrialState.trial_kind` MUST be one of Appendix J `trial_state_kind`: `business_starter_14d`, `buyer_solo_migration_90d`, `seller_solo_migration_90d`. For Solo migration trials, `trial_state` is one of Appendix J `solo_trial_state`: `offer_presented`, `active`, `converted`, `auto_downgraded`, `canceled`, `expired_unaccepted`. `trial_outcome` is one of Appendix J `solo_trial_outcome`: `converted_to_solo_subscription`, `converted_to_higher_paid_plan`, `auto_downgraded_to_free`, `canceled_by_customer`, `expired_unaccepted`, `blocked_already_redeemed`.

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `offer_presented` | `active` | Eligible Org accepts the v3 migration offer | No prior accepted Solo migration trial for `(org_id, console, legal_entity)` | Stamps `trial_started_at = now`, `trial_expires_at = now + 90 days`, `trial_kind`, `console`, and `legal_entity`; emits `billing.solo_trial.started` and audit action `org.solo_trial_started`. |
| `offer_presented` | `expired_unaccepted` | Migration-offer window closes without acceptance | Offer row exists and `accepted_at IS NULL` | No plan change; emits no customer-visible downgrade. |
| `active` | `converted` | Customer adds payment method and explicitly confirms Solo subscription or higher paid plan before day 91 | Stripe payment method verified; selected plan is paid and valid for the active console | Emits `billing.plan.upgraded` with `change_origin = automated_trial_conversion`, `billing.solo_trial.ended`, and audit action `org.solo_trial_ended`. |
| `active` | `auto_downgraded` | Day 91 scheduled job runs with no confirmed paid conversion | `now >= trial_expires_at`; no active paid conversion | Plan returns to `buyer_free` or `seller_free`; excess data follows §34.6. Seller KB grandfathered rows, once authored by D-14.2-009, override only the affected pre-cutover KB rows. Emits `billing.plan.downgraded` with `change_origin = solo_migration_trial_auto_downgrade`, `billing.solo_trial.ended`, and audit action `org.solo_trial_ended`. |
| `active` | `canceled` | Org Owner or Billing Admin cancels the trial before day 91 | Caller confirms immediate return to Free | Same data-preservation behavior as auto-downgrade; emits `billing.solo_trial.ended` with `trial_outcome = canceled_by_customer`. |
| `converted`, `auto_downgraded`, `canceled`, `expired_unaccepted` | (terminal) | — | — | Retention follows §40.2 financial / billing-transition records. |

**Notification and audit cadence.**

| Event | Trigger | Recipient | Channels | Required payload |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `billing.solo_trial.started` | Trial enters `active` | Org Owner + Billing Admin | Webhook, in-app, email | `trial_state_id`, `trial_kind`, `console`, `plan_from`, `plan_trial`, `trial_started_at`, `trial_expires_at`, `legal_entity`, `source_migration_version` |
| `billing.solo_trial.expiry_notice_sent` | Day 80 and day 89 pre-expiry notices | Org Owner + Billing Admin | In-app, email; webhook for subscribed billing endpoints | Same as started plus `days_remaining`, `notice_kind ∈ {day_80, day_89}` |
| `billing.solo_trial.ended` | Trial converts, auto-downgrades, cancels, or expires unaccepted | Org Owner + Billing Admin | Webhook, in-app, email | Same as started plus `trial_outcome`, `plan_to`, `downgrade_bucket_summary` when applicable |

**Abuse controls.**

- Solo migration trial acceptance is lifetime-limited by `(org_id, console, legal_entity, trial_kind)`. A second acceptance attempt returns HTTP 409 `solo_trial_already_redeemed` and emits no plan change.
- A non-eligible Org attempting to accept the migration offer returns HTTP 403 `solo_trial_not_eligible`; the response MUST NOT reveal whether another Org in the same legal entity already redeemed a trial.
- Illegal state transitions return HTTP 409 `solo_trial_invalid_state_transition`.
- Ops may not grant a second migration trial by direct row mutation. Any extension or exceptional conversion MUST use §50.20 TrialAuthorization / PlanTierOverrideProposal and produce an Ops audit chain.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Eligible Buyer Free v2-cohort Orgs that accept the offer MUST enter `buyer_solo` subscription mode for 90 days with no credit card required; per-evaluation charges MUST NOT fire while the trial is active.
2. Eligible Seller Free v2-cohort Orgs that accept the offer MUST enter `seller_solo` subscription mode for 90 days with no credit card required; per-bid charges MUST NOT fire while the trial is active.
3. Day-80 and day-89 notices MUST dispatch idempotently; duplicate scheduled-job attempts MUST coalesce on `(trial_state_id, notice_kind)`.
4. Day-91 auto-downgrade MUST be idempotent and MUST write `billing.plan.downgraded`, `billing.solo_trial.ended`, and `org.solo_trial_ended` in the same transaction as the plan-tier change.
5. Paid conversion before day 91 MUST write `billing.plan.upgraded`, `billing.solo_trial.ended`, and `org.solo_trial_ended` in the same transaction as the plan-tier change.
6. One-trial-per-Org-per-console-per-legal-entity enforcement MUST be covered by deploy-time validator `solo_trial_one_per_org_lifetime`; attempts to bypass by legal-entity rebinding, console switch, or repeat offer acceptance fail closed.
7. The TrialState PostHog mirror MUST use Appendix G events `solo_trial_started`, `solo_trial_expiry_notice_sent`, and `solo_trial_ended` with the same `trial_state_id` as the webhook `event_id` correlation payload.
8. The Seller-side auto-downgrade path MUST explicitly call §34.6 preservation; the pending D-14.2-009 v2 KB grandfathering pass may narrow the preservation behavior for pre-cutover KB rows only and MUST NOT change the trial lifecycle.

## 34.10 AI Wallet Service {#34.10-ai-wallet-service}

The AIWallet (§4.8.3) is the org-scoped, console-pooled value-dollar account that every customer-billed AIOperation draws against. Schema, indexes, and wallet/top-up state machines live in §4.8.3 and §4.8.3.A; the §34.10 section fixes the operational policy.

### 34.10.1 Wallet Counters

| Counter | Field on AIWallet | Purpose | Replenishment |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Included Budget | `budget_value_dollars`, less `consumed_value_dollars` | Plan-included monthly allowance in value-dollars | Reset to plan-tier amount at each `current_period_ends_at` (billing anniversary) |
| Overage Balance | `overage_cap_value_dollars`, less `overage_consumed_value_dollars` | Customer-deposited wallet funds drawn after included budget exhausted | On admin-initiated top-up or auto-topup (per §4.8.3.A) |
| Committed Spend Pool (Enterprise) | `commit_burn_remaining_value_dollars` (denormalized from `CommittedSpendContract.commit_burn_remaining_value_dollars`) | Annual prepaid commit pool | At contract signature; auto-renewal per §4.8.8 |

**Burn priority** (per §4.8.3 Committed Spend Interaction): `commit_burn_remaining → budget_value_dollars (included) → overage_cap_value_dollars (wallet)`. Free Allowance bypasses all three (§4.8.3 Free Allowance Interaction).

All counters are stored in **integer USD cents** (denominated in value-dollars per BPS §11). Presentation in the customer's `billing_currency` is via `fx_rate_locked` at presentation time only; the stored value is never persisted in non-USD.

### 34.10.2 Wallet Configuration

| Setting | Default | Constraint | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Wallet overage enabled | `false` (off) | A `billing_admin` must explicitly enable; admin action audited as `org.wallet_overage_enabled` | BPS §7; §4.8.3 acceptance criterion #4 |
| Overage cap | 0 | When enabled, `billing_admin` sets a positive integer cap | BPS §7 |
| Daily / Weekly / Monthly caps | Unset | Each cap is independent; lowest cap binds | BPS §7 |
| Auto-topup enabled | `false` (off) | A `billing_admin` must explicitly enable | BPS §7; MS C.79; §4.8.3 |
| Auto-topup increment | $50–$10,000 single charge | Out-of-range values rejected with HTTP 422 `wallet_topup_increment_out_of_range` | MS C.79; §4.8.3 acceptance criterion #5 |
| Auto-topup max monthly | $50–$500,000 absolute ceiling | Authored ceiling; flagged for Sales/Finance review per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Phase 4 Known Gaps` | AE; §4.8.3 |
| Notification thresholds | 50%, 80%, 100% of `(budget + overage_cap)`; one-shot per period | Idempotency stamps prevent duplicates | §4.8.3 acceptance criterion #6 |

### 34.10.3 Pooled Budget Across Consoles (Authoritative Rule)
