AIWallet balances are **Organization-scoped** and pooled across Buyer and Seller consoles (BPS §13 / SPS §11 / MS §2). An Org holding (Buyer Growth = $300 budget) + (Seller Starter = $30 budget) sees a unified $330 of monthly value-dollars spendable by any capability in either console. The §4.8.3 acceptance criterion #1 enforces this at the schema layer (one wallet row per Org; pooling enforced by the absence of a `console` column on AIWallet).

| Plan combination | Pooled budget | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Buyer Free + Seller Free | $5 (single wallet; both plans contribute to one $5 pool — see §34.10.4) | BPS §3, SPS §3 |
| Buyer Solo + Seller Free | $0 customer-visible (Buyer Solo's ≈ $5 envelope is engine-absorbed and surface-hidden per §44; Seller Free's $5 collapses per the Solo-co-resident rule below) | BPS §5; SPS §3; Phase 14.9 AE |
| Buyer Free + Seller Solo | $0 customer-visible (Seller Solo's ≈ $5 envelope is engine-absorbed and surface-hidden per §44; Buyer Free's $5 collapses per the Solo-co-resident rule below) | BPS §3; SPS §5; Phase 14.9 AE |
| Buyer Solo + Seller Solo | $0 customer-visible (two independent engine-absorbed envelopes — one per console — neither surface-rendered per SPS §12 #2 / BPS §5.5; engine writes per-console envelope counters separately and never combines them into the AIWallet `included_budget_remaining` counter) | BPS §5; SPS §5, §12 #2; Phase 14.9 AE |
| Buyer Solo + Seller Starter | $30 (Solo's engine-absorbed envelope does NOT pool with the paid side; pooled customer-visible budget = paid side only) | BPS §5; SPS §6; Phase 14.9 AE |
| Buyer Starter + Seller Solo | $50 (Solo's engine-absorbed envelope does NOT pool with the paid side) | BPS §6.1; SPS §5; Phase 14.9 AE |
| Buyer Starter + Seller Free | $50 (Free $5 budget contribution is collapsed when paid plan present — see §34.10.4) | BPS §6.1 + SPS §3 + AE collapse rule |
| Buyer Growth + Seller Starter | $330 | BPS §6.2 + SPS §6 |
| Buyer Scale + Seller Growth | $1,000 | BPS §6.3 + SPS §7 |
| Buyer Enterprise + Seller Free | Committed (Enterprise $) — Free does not add | BPS §7 |
| Buyer Enterprise + Seller Solo | Committed (Enterprise $) — Solo's engine-absorbed envelope does NOT add | BPS §7; SPS §5; Phase 14.9 AE |
| Buyer Enterprise + Seller Enterprise | One Committed pool (single contract per §34.12.5) | BPS §7 / SPS §9 / §34.12.5 |

**Free + Free pool collapse rule (Authored Extension).** When both consoles are on Free, the pooled budget is **$5 total** (not $10). Rationale: the $5 Free budget exists as a PLG hook to drive a single ceiling-hit event, not as a doubled budget that delays the upgrade moment. This collapse is consistent with BPS §4 ("hit the ceiling, upgrade") and SPS §4 ("Get invited. Respond. … Hit the ceiling … Upgrade.") but is not explicitly stated in either source. **Logged as Authored Extension in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` for Sales-Ops sign-off.**

**Free + Paid pool collapse rule (Authored Extension).** When one side is Free and the other is paid, the Free side's $5 budget is **collapsed** (not added) to avoid the Free-side budget effectively topping up the paid side. The pooled budget equals the paid side's budget only. **Logged as Authored Extension.**

**Solo-co-resident pool rule (Phase 14.9, Authored Extension).** Solo's ≈ $5 engine-absorbed envelope (per §44) is **never** part of the customer-visible pooled budget on the AIWallet, regardless of the contralateral console's plan. The envelope exists exclusively on the engine side as a margin-protection counter; it is never rendered on the AIWallet widget, never returned in `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/wallet`, and never collapsed *into* the contralateral console's visible budget. Concretely:

1. **Solo + Free** (either direction). Customer-visible pooled budget = $0. The Free-side $5 collapses per the Free + Paid rule (treating Solo as "paid" for the purpose of collapse), AND Solo's envelope stays engine-side. The customer surface shows only the Solo plan line item ("Plan: Solo · $49/mo") plus the contralateral console's Free indicator.
2. **Solo + Solo** (cross-console). Customer-visible pooled budget = $0. Two engine-side envelopes run independently, one per console, with separate throttling thresholds and separate margin accounting per SPS §12 #2 / BPS §5.5. Two Stripe subscriptions invoice independently per §34.12.1; no cross-console bundle discount.
3. **Solo + Paid Business / Seller Starter+** (either direction). Customer-visible pooled budget = paid-side budget only. Solo's envelope stays engine-side. Wallet overage UI surfaces on the paid-side console only; Solo console continues to surface only its plan line item.
4. **Solo + Enterprise** (either direction). Customer-visible pool = the Enterprise committed pool. Solo's envelope stays engine-side; Solo's Stripe subscription invoices independently from the Enterprise contract; the §34.12.5 single-contract collapse does NOT apply to Solo (only to dual-Enterprise).
5. **Solo upgrades to Starter+ or Enterprise.** On upgrade, Solo's engine-absorbed envelope counter is closed; the Wallet `included_budget_remaining` counter activates with the new plan's value-dollar budget at the upgrade billing-rollover boundary; pre-upgrade AIOperations remain Solo-absorbed (no retroactive billing per §22.20.5 #2 / §44).
6. **Solo downgrades to Free.** On downgrade, Solo's engine-absorbed envelope counter closes; Free's $5 hard-capped Wallet budget activates at the downgrade billing-rollover boundary; the §34.6 / §34.19 downgrade-safe rules apply to KB-cap excess (Solo's 250 KB → Free's 50 KB excess preserved read-only for 90 days; bid-workspace 90-day per-bid retention windows close on downgrade).

The Solo-co-resident rule is required because Solo's surface contract (no wallet, no rate card, no per-op breakdown — per BPS §2.8 / SPS §2.9 / §44) is incompatible with surfacing a pooled wallet number on the contralateral console. The rule preserves the surface contract on both consoles without breaking the engine-side margin protection.

### 34.10.4 Wallet State Machine (Reference)

The full state machine lives at §4.8.3 (`active`, `soft_warned_50`, `soft_warned_80`, `hard_capped_100`, `hard_capped_auto_topup_monthly_cap` *(Phase 7 V7 D-V7-002)*, `payment_failed_grace`, `suspended`, `closed`). The §34.10 policy summary:

- 50% threshold → email + in-app to Org Owner + Billing Admin (one-shot)
- 80% threshold → email + in-app; auto-topup may fire here if enabled
- 100% threshold (unfunded headroom) → if no auto-topup OR auto-topup disabled OR Stripe charge fails: `hard_capped_100`; HTTP 402 `wallet_hard_capped` for new customer-billed AIOperations; Sourcera-owned operations continue
- **Auto-topup monthly cap exhausted** (Phase 7 V7 D-V7-002 remediation) → if auto-topup is enabled but `auto_topup_consumed_monthly + auto_topup_increment > auto_topup_max_monthly_value_dollars`: `hard_capped_auto_topup_monthly_cap`; HTTP 402 `wallet_auto_topup_monthly_cap_exhausted` for new customer-billed AIOperations; Sourcera-owned operations continue. The state is *distinct* from `hard_capped_100` because the binding constraint is the customer-set monthly cap, not infrastructural exhaustion. Customer-visible banner cites the cap explicitly; in-app CTA deep-links to wallet config to raise the cap. `auto_topup_monthly_cap_exhausted` webhook fires (Appendix C; recipients: `org_owner` + `billing_admin`); a corresponding PostHog event fires per Appendix G.
- Failed top-up (Stripe transient failure) → 48-hour `payment_failed_grace`; wallet remains active during grace; billing admin emailed hourly; on grace expiry → `suspended`
- `suspended` → all customer-billed operations rejected; in-flight `pending` operations may settle (wallet hold honored); Ops alert
- Customer top-up succeeds OR billing period rolls over OR plan upgrade → return to `active`. For `hard_capped_auto_topup_monthly_cap` specifically, the additional exit trigger is `billing_admin` raising `auto_topup_max_monthly_value_dollars` followed by a successful top-up.

### 34.10.5 Stripe Metering

Wallet events are reported to Stripe daily (granularity: per-calendar-day; daily roll-up posted to Stripe Meter API). Events:

| Stripe meter event | Trigger | Fields |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `sourcera_ai_value_accepted` | AIOperation transitions `pending → accepted` or `pending → auto_accepted` | org_id, capability_id, value_price_cents, billing_currency, fx_rate_locked |
| `sourcera_ai_value_rejected` | AIOperation transitions `pending → rejected` | org_id, capability_id, cost_price_cents, billing_currency, fx_rate_locked |
| `sourcera_ai_wallet_topup` | Auto-topup or manual top-up succeeds | org_id, top-up amount cents, payment_method_id, billing_currency |
| `sourcera_ai_value_reversed` | AIOperation transitions to `reversed` (approved contest) | org_id, capability_id, reversal_amount_cents |
| `sourcera_pro_trial_grant` | Pro Trial Seat issued (M17, §34.13) | buyer_org_id, vendor_org_id, trial_expires_at |
| `sourcera_pro_trial_conversion` | Vendor converts trial to paid Seller Starter+ on day 30/31 | buyer_org_id, vendor_org_id, converted_to_plan |
| `sourcera_pro_trial_expired` | Trial auto-downgrades on day 31 with no conversion | buyer_org_id, vendor_org_id |
| `sourcera_committed_spend_burn` | Daily roll-up of value-dollars burned against an active CommittedSpendContract | org_id, contract_id, burned_amount_cents |
| `sourcera_solo_buyer_per_eval_charge` (Phase 14.9) | Buyer Solo $199 per-evaluation charge captures on Selection Report PDF export per §34.2.5 | org_id, workspace_id, value_amount_cents=19900, billing_currency, fx_rate_locked, charge_kind=`solo_per_eval` |
| `sourcera_solo_seller_per_bid_charge` (Phase 14.9) | Seller Solo $199 per-bid charge captures on bid submission per §34.2.5 | org_id, bid_workspace_id, value_amount_cents=19900, billing_currency, fx_rate_locked, charge_kind=`solo_per_bid` |
| `sourcera_solo_charge_refunded` (Phase 14.9) | Solo per-eval / per-bid charge refunded per §34.2.5 7-day refund window | org_id, original_charge_kind, refund_amount_cents, billing_currency |
| `sourcera_solo_subscription_started` (Phase 14.9) | Buyer Solo or Seller Solo subscription Stripe Subscription created | org_id, console (`buyer`/`seller`), plan_tier (`buyer_solo`/`seller_solo`), billing_period (`monthly`/`annual`), billing_currency |
| `sourcera_solo_subscription_renewed` (Phase 14.9) | Solo subscription renewal invoice paid | org_id, console, plan_tier, billing_period |
| `sourcera_solo_subscription_canceled` (Phase 14.9) | Solo subscription canceled (effective at next anniversary) | org_id, console, plan_tier, cancel_reason |

Stripe Customer is bound 1:1 to `(org_id, legal_entity)` where `legal_entity` is the canonical 4-value `legal_entity_kind` enum (`sourcera_us_llc`, `sourcera_eu_gmbh`, `sourcera_apac_pte`, `sourcera_custom`) per Appendix J post-D-AJ-004 + post-v7.2.0-REM-Phase-5 D-RES-004 reconciliation (2026-05-20). The 1:1 binding is enforced at the Convex mutation layer via `(org_id, legal_entity)` unique index on the `Organization` table's `stripe_customer_id_active` field; a residency change atomically rebinds the active Stripe Customer per the §34.10.5.A protocol below. Pre-Phase-2V Orgs holding a `sourcera_uk_ltd` Stripe Customer in the historical state are migrated to `sourcera_eu_gmbh` at the next active-Customer rebinding or at the v7.1.0a hot-patch stamp's one-time Ops Finance reconciliation pass, whichever comes first; historical UK-Ltd invoices remain on the legacy Customer for SOC-2 audit fidelity (§34.10.5.A invariant #4).

### 34.10.5.A Stripe-Customer Atomic-Binding Protocol (v7.2.0-REM Phase 5, 2026-05-20)

The Stripe Customer Atomic-Binding Protocol is the canonical specification for how the platform creates, rebinds, and closes Stripe Customers in response to (a) Organization creation, (b) `data_residency_region` change, and (c) Ops-Finance-driven legal-entity correction. It is the billing-surface authority cited by the §4.8.1 AC #14b residency-change atomicity rule, the §4.8.3 AIWallet `residency_locked_entity` reconciliation worker, the §4.8.12 MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord invoice-finalization step, and the §6.8 / §1.6 Org-side residency-change procedure (whose state-machine surface lands at §1.6.1 per D-RES-007 v7.1.1 stamp authoring).

| Invariant | Rule |
| :---- | :---- |
| **#1 — Single active Stripe Customer per `(org_id, legal_entity)`.** | At any point in time, an Organization has exactly one Stripe Customer in `state=active_for_new_invoices` keyed on its current `(org_id, legal_entity)`. The `Organization.stripe_customer_id_active` field carries the active Customer's Stripe ID; the `(org_id, legal_entity)` Convex unique index enforces the 1:1 binding. A second active Customer for the same Org under the same `legal_entity` is rejected at the mutation layer with HTTP 422 `stripe_customer_active_duplicate` (Appendix I — registered v7.2.0-REM Phase 5). |
| **#2 — Historical Stripe Customer preservation.** | Stripe Customers transitioned out of `active_for_new_invoices` are NOT deleted; they are stamped `closed_for_new_invoices` with `Organization.stripe_customer_id_historical[]` (an append-only string array on the Organization row, ordered chronologically) capturing the historical Customer IDs alongside their close timestamps and the residency / legal-entity context at close. Stripe's underlying Customer object is retained for the full Stripe-side retention horizon (Stripe's customer object never deletes; invoice history attaches indefinitely). |
| **#3 — Residency-change atomic rebinding.** | An Organization mutation that changes `data_residency_region` from value `R_old` to value `R_new` MUST execute as a single Convex transaction containing five steps in this strict order: (i) compute `legal_entity_new` from the canonical 4-row Residency-Locked Invoicing mapping at §4.8.1; (ii) verify §1.6.1 Org-side migration-eligibility predicates (no Bid Workspace in `phase ∈ {7..13}`; no AIOperation in `settlement_state = pending`; no DSARRequest in `state ∈ {verifying, verified, in_progress}`; no active OutcomeContract in renewal window; per the v7.1.1-pending §1.6.1 authoring per D-RES-007); (iii) call Stripe's `Customer.create` API with `metadata = {org_id: <id>, legal_entity: <legal_entity_new>, residency_region: <R_new>, custom_sovereign_residency_label: <label if custom else null>, atomic_binding_protocol: 'v7.2.0-REM-Phase-5'}` and capture the new Customer ID `C_new`; (iv) update `Organization` row in a single mutation: `data_residency_region = R_new`, `legal_entity_active = legal_entity_new`, `stripe_customer_id_active = C_new`, `stripe_customer_id_historical[] = append(stripe_customer_id_historical, {id: C_old, closed_at: now(), legal_entity_at_close: legal_entity_old, residency_region_at_close: R_old})`; (v) emit four audit-trail events in the same transaction: `org.residency_change.initiated`, `org.residency_change.stripe_customer_created`, `org.residency_change.stripe_customer_closed`, `org.residency_change.completed` per Appendix C registration (v7.2.0-REM Phase 5). The transaction commits atomically; failure of any step rolls back the entire mutation. The transaction MUST acquire a row-level lock on the Organization row before step (i) to prevent concurrent residency-change races (a second concurrent residency-change attempt waits for the lock and re-validates eligibility predicates against post-transaction state). |
| **#4 — Legacy-invoice fidelity.** | Stripe Charges and Invoices created against the prior Stripe Customer `C_old` remain attached to `C_old` indefinitely for SOC-2 audit fidelity; the §4.8.1 FX-Locking semantics (`fx_rate_locked` and `legal_entity` snapshot at AIOperation write time) bind every settled `effective_charge_cents` to the Stripe Customer active at write time, not at settlement time. In-flight `pending` AIOperations created before the cutover settle on `C_old` even if settlement occurs minutes after the cutover (the AIOperation's `legal_entity` field is the canonical Stripe-Customer-routing key, not the Org's current `legal_entity_active`). The Outcome Resolver looks up the Stripe Customer via `Organization.stripe_customer_id_historical[]` when settling an AIOperation whose `legal_entity` does not match the current `legal_entity_active`. CI gate `legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_test` (Appendix M.5 §M.5.17) asserts the resolver routing logic at deploy time. |
| **#5 — `custom`-residency Stripe Customer.** | For `data_residency_region = custom`, the Stripe Customer is keyed on `(org_id, sourcera_custom)` with `metadata.custom_sovereign_residency_label = <Organization.custom_sovereign_residency_label>` carrying the Org-specific sub-classification (e.g., `uk_crown_secure`, `de_sovereign_cloud`, `au_irap_protected`). Multiple `custom`-residency Orgs each receive their own Stripe Customer keyed on the same `legal_entity = sourcera_custom` enum but disambiguated by the Stripe Customer ID (`org_id` is the unique identifier; `legal_entity` is the enum value); the `(org_id, legal_entity)` unique index on `Organization.stripe_customer_id_active` is sufficient because `org_id` is unique. A mutation of `custom_sovereign_residency_label` (without a change to `data_residency_region`) is treated as an Ops-Finance correction per invariant #6 below and similarly triggers an atomic rebinding. |
| **#6 — Ops-Finance correction path.** | Ops Finance MAY trigger an atomic rebinding without a residency change for legal-entity correction (e.g., a migration from legacy `sourcera_uk_ltd` to canonical `sourcera_eu_gmbh` at the v7.1.0a hot-patch stamp Ops Finance reconciliation pass; correction of a `custom_sovereign_residency_label` typo). The correction follows the same five-step transaction as invariant #3 but with `R_old = R_new` (residency unchanged) and a documented `correction_reason` ∈ {`legacy_uk_ltd_to_eu_gmbh`, `custom_sovereign_label_correction`, `legal_entity_typo_correction`, `ops_compliance_action`} captured on the audit-trail events. Requires `ops_finance_admin` role + Founder dual-signoff per the §4.8.1.A Ops Emergency Reversal Protocol pattern (one-line cross-reference). Correction-driven rebindings do NOT close the legacy Customer for `correction_reason = legacy_uk_ltd_to_eu_gmbh` until the legacy Customer's outstanding invoices reach `paid` or `voided` terminal state — preserving the §4.8.1 FX-Locking semantics for in-flight settlements. |
| **#7 — Stripe API failure handling.** | A Stripe `Customer.create` API failure during step (iii) MUST roll back the entire Convex mutation; the Organization row is restored to its pre-transaction state; the OpsActionRecord audit row is written with `outcome = stripe_api_failure` and `failure_reason = <Stripe error code>`. The customer-facing Org Settings UI surfaces a retryable error with copy authored at §3.x (Authored Extension AE-V72REM-PH5-01 — UX Lead authoring pending v7.1.1 stamp). A retry within the §32 idempotency window resolves the residency-change attempt without creating a duplicate Stripe Customer (Stripe API idempotency key = `(org_id, legal_entity_new, mutation_timestamp_minute)`). |
| **#8 — Webhook emission.** | The §31 webhook family `org.residency_change.*` (four events per invariant #3 step v) emits HMAC-SHA256 signed payloads with `event_id` idempotency key per §31 conventions. Recipients: customer's webhook subscription (Billing Admin / Org Owner role gate); Ops Finance dashboard. PostHog event family `org.residency_change.*` (Appendix G — registered v7.2.0-REM Phase 5) mirrors the webhook for analytics dashboards. |

**Cross-references.**

- §4.8.1 Residency-Locked Invoicing — canonical 4-row residency→legal-entity mapping table.
- §4.8.1 AC #14b — residency-change atomic-rebinding acceptance criterion.
- §4.8.3 AIWallet `legal_entity` + `residency_locked_entity` fields — wallet-side mirror of the Stripe-Customer binding.
- §4.8.12 MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord `legal_entity` field — invoice-side mirror.
- §1.6.1 Per-Org Residency Change Procedure — Org-side state machine + eligibility predicates (v7.1.1 stamp authoring per D-RES-007).
- §6.8 DSAR Procedure — DSAR-vs-residency-change deadlock-resolution rules (DSAR redaction during open residency-change rolls back the residency change with `org_residency_change_blocked_by_active_dsar` HTTP 409, per D-RES-007 v7.1.1 stamp authoring).
- Appendix C `org.residency_change.*` webhook family (4 events) — v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 registration.
- Appendix G `org.residency_change.*` PostHog event family — v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 registration.
- Appendix I — new error codes registered v7.2.0-REM Phase 5: `stripe_customer_active_duplicate` (HTTP 422), `org_residency_change_stripe_api_failure` (HTTP 502; retryable), `org_residency_change_eligibility_predicate_violated` (HTTP 409; non-retryable until predicate clears). The `org_residency_change_blocked_by_active_dsar` HTTP 409 error code is registered jointly with the §1.6.1 D-RES-007 v7.1.1 authoring.
- Appendix M.5 §M.5.17 — CI gate `legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_test` (v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 registration).

**Acceptance Criteria (§34.10.5.A).**

1. A residency-change mutation transitioning `data_residency_region` from any canonical 4-value to any other canonical 4-value MUST execute the five-step atomic transaction in §34.10.5.A invariant #3 in the specified order; QA test `org_residency_change_atomic_transaction` asserts the transaction's ACID properties (atomic rollback on any step failure; isolation against concurrent residency-change attempts via row-level lock; durability via Convex commit guarantee). Out-of-order or partial-step execution MUST be rejected with HTTP 500 `org_residency_change_transaction_corrupt` (a sentinel error that should never fire under correct implementation; observed firing pages Ops Finance + Engineering immediately).
2. A new Stripe Customer creation during step (iii) MUST carry the full metadata object specified in invariant #3 (5 keys); QA test `stripe_customer_metadata_completeness` asserts the metadata round-trip via Stripe's `Customer.retrieve` API.
3. The `Organization.stripe_customer_id_historical[]` array MUST grow monotonically (no Stripe Customer ID ever removed); QA test `stripe_customer_historical_append_only` asserts the array's append-only property across 100 synthetic residency-change cycles.
4. The Outcome Resolver MUST route an in-flight AIOperation's settlement to the Stripe Customer matching the AIOperation's `legal_entity` field, NOT the Organization's current `legal_entity_active`; integration test `outcome_resolver_legacy_legal_entity_routing` asserts a synthetic AIOperation written with `legal_entity = sourcera_us_llc` settles against the pre-cutover Stripe Customer even after the Organization has rebinded to `sourcera_eu_gmbh`.
5. A residency-change attempt during an open DSAR (per the §6.8 deadlock-resolution rule, v7.1.1 stamp authoring) MUST be rejected with HTTP 409 `org_residency_change_blocked_by_active_dsar`; the rejection MUST roll back any pre-step (i) state (none under correct implementation, but a regression here would corrupt invariant #1).
6. A residency-change attempt on an Org with an in-flight `pending` AIOperation MUST be rejected with HTTP 409 `org_residency_change_eligibility_predicate_violated` per invariant #3 step (ii); the rejection notifies the Org Owner via `org.residency_change.blocked` Loops.so email with the violated predicate enumerated.
7. The `custom_sovereign_residency_label` field MUST be non-null when `data_residency_region = custom`; mutation attempts setting `data_residency_region = custom` with `custom_sovereign_residency_label = null` MUST be rejected at the §4.1.1 Organization-write layer with HTTP 422 `organization_custom_residency_label_required` (Appendix I — registered v7.2.0-REM Phase 5). CI gate `org_custom_residency_label_required` (Appendix M.5 §M.5.17 sibling) asserts the field-level constraint at deploy time.
8. The legacy `sourcera_uk_ltd` value MUST NOT appear in any new Stripe Customer's `metadata.legal_entity` field at or after the v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 stamp (2026-05-20); historical Stripe Customers carrying the legacy value in `metadata.legal_entity` remain readable via Stripe API (Stripe-side immutable) but produce no new invoices. Integration test `stripe_customer_no_new_uk_ltd_writes` asserts the write-time enforcement against 100 synthetic Stripe Customer creations.

### 34.10.6 Downgrade Behavior (Wallet)

| Trigger | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Plan downgrade (Buyer / Seller) effective at next billing cycle | `budget_value_dollars` decreases to the new plan's monthly amount at billing rollover; `consumed_value_dollars` resets to 0 at rollover; `overage_balance` retained until consumed or refunded; `auto_topup_*` settings retained unless explicitly cleared |
| Enterprise → non-Enterprise downgrade with active CommittedSpendContract | `shortfall_policy` (§4.8.8) determines treatment of unspent commit: `forfeit` (default) → forfeit at contract end; `partial_credit_next_year` → credit applied to next year's renewal; `rollover_capped` → up to `shortfall_rollover_max_pct` (≤ 25%) rolls forward |
| Wallet enters `suspended` from `payment_failed_grace` expiry | All new customer-billed AIOperations rejected with HTTP 402 `wallet_hard_capped`; in-flight `pending` operations may settle; Ops alert |
| Org closure / deletion | AIWallet transitions to `closed`; financial records (AIOperation, ContestRecord, etc.) preserved per §40.2 |

### 34.10.7 Failure Modes Addressed (Operational Layer)

1. **Customer enables overage with cap below current period's projected spend.** Resolved: cap-set UI surfaces "projected spend at current burn rate" and warns if cap is below; cap-write proceeds (customer choice); hard-cap behavior follows §34.10.4.
2. **Auto-topup race against Stripe webhook delay.** Resolved: top-up state machine (§4.8.3.A) is single-row optimistic-locked; in-flight charge prevents a second concurrent charge attempt.
3. **Customer disables overage mid-period with active overage_balance.** Resolved: overage_balance remains spendable until consumed; new overage operations beyond included budget are blocked at write time with HTTP 402 `wallet_hard_capped`.
4. **Org has paid Buyer plan and Seller Free, then downgrades Buyer to Free.** Resolved: pool collapses to $5 total (Free + Free collapse rule §34.10.3); Wallet state transition is atomic at billing rollover.
5. **Cross-console operation invokes during plan-transition window.** Resolved: §34.8.6 Failure Mode #4 — operation evaluates against entitlement state at write time, not settlement time.

## 34.11 Outcome Resolver {#34.11-outcome-resolver}

The Outcome Resolver is the platform component that classifies every AIOperation as `accepted`, `auto_accepted`, or `rejected` per the bound OutcomeContract (§4.8.4) and writes the corresponding value-dollar amount to the Wallet. The Resolver is platform-scoped, single-tenant per Sourcera deployment, and consumes outcome signals from product surfaces (user clicks, retention thresholds, downstream-use signals) via an event-bus interface. The Resolver is referenced as a Phase 4 Known Gap (component-level system design pending) in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md`.

### 34.11.1 Outcome Contract Registry

The complete per-capability outcome contract registry lives at §4.8.4 OutcomeContract. The §34.11.1 surface is the customer-facing summary of the contract; key contracts mirror BPS Appendix B and SPS §10. **Partial-surface pointer (Phase 13 inline fix F-3.2 — 2026-04-26).** This 20-row table is intentionally a representative customer-facing summary — NOT the engineering source-of-truth. The full ~38-row per-capability concrete-signal definition table is §21.4.5 (`accepted` signal, `rejected` signal, window, `auto_accept_after_seconds`, `requires_explicit_user_signal` per capability). The entity-level OutcomeContract authoritative truth (versioning, contract-revision policy, default-on-timeout default) is §4.8.4. Engineering MUST consult §21.4.5 + §4.8.4 — not §34.11.1 — to implement the Outcome Resolver. The deploy-time validator `outcome_contract_completeness` (Phase 13.0 follow-on; §6 of `_integration/PHASE13_ENG_REVIEW.md`) asserts that the union of `capability_id`s across §21.4.1 + §21.4.1.A + **§21.4.1.B** (qa_suggestion siblings, per Phase 4 D-EM-001 closure) + **§21.4.1.C** (Buyer-Console augmentations, per Phase 4.2 D-EM-002 closure) + **§21.4.1.D** (kb_suggestion sibling-split, per Phase 4.2 D-EM-002 closure) + §21.4.2 + §21.4.3 equals the union across §21.4.5 minus (a) non-AI feature gates, (b) platform-internal aggregations, and (c) **family-root rollup identifiers** (`qa_suggestion_family`, `kb_suggestion_family`, `org_intelligence_family` — never directly invokable; carry no §21.4.5 outcome-signal row per the §21.4.1 family-rooted sibling-split contract).

| Capability | Accepted Signal | Window | Timeout Default | OutcomeContract Version (Active) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `pre_scoring` | User confirms or edits ≤ 20% of suggested score | 7d | rejected | v1 |
| `requirement_extraction` | Requirement retained in final spec | 14d | rejected | v1 |
| `kb_suggestion` | User clicks "use" OR content appears in artifact | 7d | rejected | v1 |
| `vendor_summary` | Summary retained unchanged ≥ 80% | 7d | rejected | v1 |
| `policy_parsing` | Parsed policy retained AND used in ≥ 1 evaluation | 30d | rejected | v1 |
| `deep_comparison` | Exported, shared, OR linked from artifact | 14d | rejected | v1 |
| `response_drafting` | Sent OR retained ≥ 70% unchanged | 7d | rejected | v1 |
| `stakeholder_summary` | Shared externally OR retained in final report | 14d | rejected | v1 |
| `first_pass_rfp_draft` | ≥ 50% of draft retained in submitted bid | 14d (or on bid submission) | rejected | v1 (bound to §21.4.1.E `CapabilityRegistryEntry` row per the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.3 D-EM-003 closure; the §34.11.1 row identifies the **OutcomeContract signal name** which is shared with the `first_pass_responses` batch sibling; the row-level OutcomeContract instances are independent per §4.8.4 AC #1 — see §34.15.1 row 1 binding note) |
| `qa_suggestion_buyer` | Draft question accepted into Public Q&A Thread OR retained ≤ 30% edit at vendor response time | 14d | rejected | v1 |
| `qa_suggestion_seller` | Answer sent with ≤ 30% edit | 7d | rejected | v1 |
| `kb_to_capability_suggestion` | Declaration published | 14d | rejected | v1 |
| `kb_bootstrap` | ≥ 60% of proposed entries approved | 30d | rejected | v1 |
| `ghost_rfp_ingestion` | Resulting KB entries cited in a future bid | 90d | rejected | v1 |
| `firecrawl_crawl_dedupe` | New entry approved OR correct dedupe | 7d | rejected | v1 |
| `kb_staleness_classifier` | Flagged entry re-verified or archived | 14d | rejected | v1 |
| `seller_page_enrichment` | Seller publishes generated content | 14d | rejected | v1 |
| `capability_declaration_suggest` | Declaration published | 7d | rejected | v1 |
| `match_score_numeric` | EOI submitted after viewing score | 14d | rejected | v1 |
| `bid_task_assignment_suggest` | Task assigned as suggested | 24h | rejected | v1 |
| `document_attach_suggest` | Document attached to response | 24h | rejected | v1 |

**Default-on-timeout behavior.** Per §4.8.4 acceptance criterion #5, every contract's default-on-timeout is `rejected` unless `requires_explicit_user_signal=true`. This biases Sourcera toward cost protection when the signal is ambiguous (BPS §6 / SPS §10).

**`auto_accepted` distinct settlement state.** When the auto-accept timer fires (`auto_accept_after_seconds` reached without a rejected signal), the operation transitions to `auto_accepted` (NOT `accepted`). The `auto_accepted` state is billed at the value price (treated as accepted commercially) but is reported separately in product-quality dashboards to surface capabilities that may be over-relying on auto-accept.

### 34.11.2 Contest Window

Per MS C.78 and §4.8.5 ContestRecord, a `billing_admin` may contest any settled `accepted` or `auto_accepted` AIOperation within **14 days** of settlement (default; per-capability override via OutcomeContract.`contest_window_days` ≤ 90).

| Aspect | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Filing path | Billing Ledger UI → "Contest" button per AIOperation row → reason code + narrative; OR API `POST /v1/billing/operations/:id/contest` (endpoint pending per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Endpoint Additions`) |
| Filing window | 14d default from `settlement_at`; per-capability override |
| Routing | Contests route to Ops Finance via `contest_review` queue |
| Approved contest | AIOperation transitions to `reversed`; `effective_charge_cents = 0`; reversal credit posted to Wallet (committed pool if applicable, else included budget if same period, else overage_balance); `sourcera_ai_value_reversed` Stripe meter event emitted |
| Rejected contest | AIOperation returns to prior `accepted` / `auto_accepted` state; original charge restored; `settlement_at` unchanged |
| Auto-filed contest | When a late `rejected` signal arrives within `signal_evaluation_grace_seconds` after auto-accept, an automatic ContestRecord is filed with reason `auto_filed_late_signal` (§4.8.5); routes to Ops Finance for review |
| Customer notifications | `billing.contest.filed` (filing confirmation), `billing.contest.decision_received`, `billing.contest.rejected`, `billing.contest.sla_breach`, `billing.contest.abandoned` (§31.8.11 / §31.8.12) |
| Ops Finance SLA | 5 business days for contest decision; SLA breach triggers `billing.contest.sla_breach` and Ops alert |
| Locked-state guard | DSAR redaction during open contest is blocked with HTTP 423 `ai_operation_locked_for_contest`; resumes after contest closes (§4.8.5) |

### 34.11.2.A Contest Filing Rate-Limit, Queue Back-Pressure, and DSAR Interaction (Phase 7 V7 D-V7-003 Remediation, 2026-05-07)

**Per-billing-admin rate-limit.** A `billing_admin` user may file at most **10 ContestRecords per `(org_id, billing_admin_user_id)` per rolling 24-hour window** and at most **100 ContestRecords per `org_id` per rolling 30-day window**. Filing attempts exceeding either bound return HTTP 429 `contest_rate_limit_exceeded` (Appendix I; new in Phase 7 V7) with the `Retry-After` header populated to the next-available window-open time. The rate-limit applies to BOTH the customer-initiated filing path (Billing Ledger UI / API) AND the auto-filed path (`auto_filed_late_signal`), summed against the same per-Org bound. Auto-filed contests count against the Org bound (NOT the per-billing-admin bound, because auto-files have `filed_by_user_id=null`).

**Queue-depth back-pressure.** Per `org_id`, the `contest_review` queue depth is monitored at insert time. The §34.11.4 AC #4 default 5-business-day Ops Finance SLA scales with queue depth:

| Queue depth (open + in_review for `org_id`) | Effective SLA |
| :---- | :---- |
| ≤ 100 | 5 business days (default) |
| 101 – 500 | 10 business days |
| > 500 | Escalates to `ops_finance_lead` + `cfo` immediate review (assumed pattern of abuse or systemic issue); SLA suspended pending Ops decision |

The depth-tier transitions emit `contest_queue_depth_tier_changed` (Appendix C; HMAC-SHA256 signed; recipients: `ops_finance_admin` + the customer's `billing_admin`); the customer-side notification is informational ("Your contest queue is being processed; current SLA is 10 business days due to active contest volume"), distinct from per-contest SLA breach notifications.

**Auto-filed contest aggregate cap.** Per `(org_id, capability_id, rolling 24-hour window)`, the system MAY auto-file at most **20 ContestRecords**. Auto-file attempts exceeding the cap are deferred to a manual Ops review queue with a single aggregated alert (`contest_auto_file_cap_exceeded`; Appendix C) rather than emitting 21 individual `auto_filed_late_signal` rows. The cap protects against runaway resolver bugs that would otherwise create thousands of contest records. Aggregated-deferral entries DO NOT block the underlying AIOperations from being settled at their original `accepted` / `auto_accepted` state; they are queued for Ops Finance to review as a batch.

**DSAR-vs-contest deadlock-resolution.** §34.11.2 line 8526 ("Locked-state guard: DSAR redaction during open contest is blocked with HTTP 423 `ai_operation_locked_for_contest`") in combination with the §6.8 30-day DSAR SLA produced a deadlock vector when 30+ contests are open simultaneously: contest 5-business-day SLA × N contests overlapping a DSAR exceeds the 30-day DSAR SLA. The Phase 7 V7 D-V7-003 remediation introduces a deadlock-resolution rule:

| Condition | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Contest age < 14 days | `ai_operation_locked_for_contest` HTTP 423 holds; DSAR redaction deferred to contest close |
| Contest age ≥ 14 days AND DSAR pending ≥ 14 days | DSAR redaction proceeds with **financial-record-preserving** scope: `actor_id` pseudonymized per §6.8.4.1 Pattern B (the User row is pseudonymized in-place; the AIOperation FK is retained); `input_content_hash` / `output_content_hash` / `prompt_template_version` scrubbed per §6.8.5 row class #3 Pattern A. The financial fields (`cost_base_cents`, `value_price_cents`, `cost_price_cents`, `effective_charge_cents`, `fx_rate_locked`, `legal_entity`, `provenance_hash`, `settlement_state`, `settlement_at`) and the `contest_record_id` FK are PRESERVED verbatim. The contest review continues; the OpsActionRecord audit logs that the DSAR redaction occurred mid-contest with the deadlock-resolution rule cited. |
| Contest age ≥ 14 days AND no DSAR pending | Standard contest flow continues. |
| Counsel approval | A Counsel sign-off (recorded as a `dsar_contest_counsel_signoff` OpsActionRecord row) MAY shorten the 14-day deadlock-resolution window to 0 days for legally-binding orders (e.g., regulatory take-down). |

The deadlock-resolution rule is consistent with §6.8.5 financial-record-integrity exemption (financial fields preserved through DSAR) and §6.8.4.1 Pattern B (FK preservation, content scrub). Engineering implementation: the AI operation's `redacted_at` write under deadlock-resolution emits `ai_operation.redacted_under_deadlock_resolution` (Appendix C; PostHog event fires per Appendix G) so Ops Finance can audit deadlock-driven redactions distinct from standard DSAR redactions.

**Stack alignment.** The contest-filing rate-limit is enforced at the Convex mutation layer via the `contest_rate_limit_check` query before the ContestRecord insert. Auto-file aggregate cap and queue-depth back-pressure are enforced at the contest scheduler layer (Convex scheduled function) with PostHog event emission. The DSAR deadlock-resolution rule is enforced at the §6.8 DSAR processor layer, which queries `ContestRecord.created_at` to compute contest age before deciding to apply the redaction. Loops.so handles the customer-side `contest_queue_depth_tier_changed` informational email.

### 34.11.3 Cost-Base Recalculation (Operational Cross-Reference)

The cost-base recalculation policy is fully specified in §34.3.3 above. Entity mechanics live in §4.8.6 CostBaseRecalculationLog. Key invariants:

- Nightly run at 02:30 UTC; idempotent re-run on missed sweep
- Drift severity bands: `low` (≥ 5%), `medium` (≥ 10%, alerts Finance), `high` (≥ 25%, blocks auto-publish), `critical` (margin-floor breach)
- High and critical drift require Ops Finance approval before publishing a new PricingTableVersion
- Approved publishes that constitute a customer-visible price increase MUST satisfy the 30-day-advance notification gate (§4.8.9 acceptance criterion #3); annual contracts grandfathered

### 34.11.4 Outcome Resolver Acceptance Criteria

1. Every AIOperation MUST receive a settlement decision within `auto_accept_after_seconds + signal_evaluation_grace_seconds` of `created_at` (§4.8.4).
2. Late `rejected` signals after auto-accept MUST automatically materialize a ContestRecord with reason `auto_filed_late_signal` and notify Ops Finance within 5 minutes (§4.8.1 acceptance criterion #11; §4.8.5).
3. Resolver MUST use the OutcomeContract version that was active at the AIOperation `created_at`, not the currently active version (§4.8.4 acceptance criterion #2).
4. Contest SLA: Ops Finance MUST decide every contest within 5 business days; breach triggers `billing.contest.sla_breach` webhook + Ops alert.
5. Approved contests MUST credit the wallet within 1 business day of approval; QA test `contest_approval_wallet_credit_latency` asserts.

## 34.12 Cross-Side Billing Rules {#34.12-cross-side-billing-rules}

§34.12 codifies the cross-console billing rules per BPS §13 / SPS §11 / MS §2. The Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2) is preserved end-to-end: billing data is shared at the Org level; business data (Workspaces, Bid Workspaces, KB entries, evaluations, etc.) is not.

### 34.12.1 Per-Console Plan Activation

An Organization may hold any combination of Buyer plan and Seller plan. Plans activate per console, not per Org. Valid combinations include but are not limited to:

| Buyer plan | Seller plan | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Buyer Free | Seller Free | Default for new Orgs that signed up via direct or invite path on either side |
| Buyer Solo | Seller Free | Buyer-Maya Org primarily running a single buyer-side evaluation; vendor-side is for occasional response (M5 Buyer-Pull) |
| Buyer Free | Seller Solo | Seller-Maya Org primarily responding to a single forwarded buyer invite; buyer-side is unused or browse-only |
| Buyer Solo | Seller Solo | Both sides on the personal-card on-ramp; charged independently per §34.12.6 (no Solo-bundle discount; engine-absorbed envelopes per console per §34.10.3 Solo-co-resident rule) |
| Buyer Solo | Seller Starter | Solo Buyer co-resident with paid Seller; common when an Org has procurement-tool budget on the seller side but not yet on the buyer side |
| Buyer Starter | Seller Solo | Common when an Org has procurement-tool budget on the buyer side but the vendor side is still a single-bid surface |
| Business Growth | Seller Starter | Common cross-side activation pattern (mid-market) |
| Buyer Free | Seller Scale | Org primarily acts as a vendor; minimal buyer-side use |
| Buyer Enterprise | Seller Free | Org primarily acts as a buyer; vendor side is for occasional response |
| Buyer Enterprise | Seller Enterprise | Collapses to one combined contract per §34.12.5 |

Plan tier on each side is independent and may be upgraded or downgraded without affecting the other side, with the Enterprise-collapse exception in §34.12.5. Solo on either side does NOT trigger the §34.12.5 single-contract collapse — Solo is per-console subscription billing managed independently of the contralateral console.

### 34.12.2 AI Wallet is Org-Scoped and Pooled

Per §34.10.3 (authoritative), AIWallet is a single row per Org. The pooled budget rule applies to all combinations:

```
total_usable_value_dollars =
  (committed_remaining if Enterprise active)
+ included_budget_remaining (collapsed per §34.10.3 Free+X rules)
+ overage_balance
+ free_allowance_remaining (per capability, evaluated independently)
```

Any customer-billed capability in either console can draw from the pool. The Outcome Resolver writes operations against the appropriate counter per the §34.10.1 burn priority.

### 34.12.3 Wallet Overage is Org-Scoped

One AIWallet → one overage cap → one auto-topup configuration → one `billing_admin` role per Org. Overage configuration cannot be split per console; the `billing_admin` operates at the Org level and may be granted to users with primary affiliation on either console.

### 34.12.4 Dual-Console Firewall is Unchanged

Billing data is shared across consoles within an Org for `billing_admin`-role reads only. **Console-scoped business entities never cross the firewall** regardless of billing state:

- Workspaces, Bid Workspaces, evaluations, KB entries, Capability Declarations, Vendor Profiles, Internal Comments, Q&A threads, Selection Reports, Scoring data — all console-isolated per §7.2.
- AIOperation rows are Org-scoped but **console-tagged** (`console` enum field; §4.8.1). A Buyer-console session cannot enumerate the AIOperations of a Seller-console workspace even though both bill against the same AIWallet (§4.8.1 acceptance criterion #2).
- The Billing Ledger view (`GET /v1/billing/operations` — endpoint pending) returns rows scoped to the requesting session's console UNLESS the requesting role is `billing_admin`, in which case both consoles' AIOperations are returned with explicit `console` tags.
- ContestRecord (§4.8.5) is filable by `billing_admin` from either console session for any AIOperation in either console.
- DowngradeExcessDataBucket (§4.8.10) is created independently per console downgrade; an Org with both plans downgrading independently has independent buckets per `(org_id, console, data_class)`.

### 34.12.4.A AIWallet Aggregate-Counter Read-Permission Scope (Phase 7 V7 D-V7-008 Remediation, 2026-05-07)

The AIWallet aggregate counters (`commit_burn_remaining_value_dollars`, `consumed_value_dollars`, `included_budget_remaining`, `overage_balance`, `auto_topup_consumed_monthly`, `wallet_state`) are **Org-pooled, NOT per-console**, per the §34.10.3 pooling rule. To preserve the §34.12.4 firewall against incidental cross-console activity-magnitude inference, the read-permission scope on these counters is explicitly bounded:

| Endpoint / surface | Permitted roles | Behavior on unpermitted roles |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/wallet` (Billing API) | `org_owner`, `billing_admin`, `org_admin` | HTTP 403 `wallet_read_scope_violation` (Appendix I; new in Phase 7 V7) |
| In-app AIWallet widget render | `org_owner`, `billing_admin`, `org_admin` | Widget hidden from UI; no API call issued |
| §34.10.4 wallet-threshold notifications (50% / 80% / 100% / `auto_topup_monthly_cap_exhausted`) | `org_owner`, `billing_admin` (per existing §4.8.3 AC #6) | Other roles never receive the notifications |
| Stripe customer portal deep-link | `org_owner`, `billing_admin` | Other roles see UI without the deep-link; clicks return 403 |
| §50 Ops Console wallet read | `ops_finance_admin`, `ops_billing_admin` | Other Ops roles see masked-counter view (counters bucketed to nearest $100 increment for cohort dashboards; exact values restricted to billing-admin Ops roles) |

Console of the requesting session does NOT scope the wallet read — the wallet is Org-pooled per §34.10.3 — but role-gating preserves the §34.12.4 firewall against non-admin roles inferring contralateral-console activity magnitude from the difference between the pooled `commit_burn_remaining` counter and the console-scoped Billing Ledger row totals visible to that session.

**Schema enforcement.** §4.8.3 Scope Isolation block (line 8345 of v7.1.0; line 8345-equivalent post-edits) is amended to cite §34.12.4.A as the canonical read-permission scope authority:

- `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `billing_admin` see all fields per the existing §4.8.3 read scope.
- `member` and `guest` roles see HTTP 403 `wallet_role_forbidden` per the existing §4.8.3 read scope (this maps 1:1 to the new `wallet_read_scope_violation` error code introduced in Phase 7 V7 — the two codes are merged at Appendix I; the legacy `wallet_role_forbidden` is preserved as a back-compat alias).
- `workspace_owner`, `workspace_admin`, `use_case_lead`, `reviewer` roles (workspace-level roles) MUST NOT have wallet read access unless they ALSO hold an org-level role from the permitted set. This closes the inference vector identified by D-V7-008.

**Feature Access Matrix update.** §5.11 adds a new row:

| Feature | Free | Solo | Starter | Growth | Scale | Enterprise | Permitted roles |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| AIWallet aggregate counter read | ✓ | (hidden per §44.6.1) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `billing_admin` |

(For Solo, the wallet widget is hidden per §44.6.1 surface contract; the underlying read endpoint is still permission-gated identically and returns the engine-side counters when called by the permitted roles, but the in-app widget does not render.)

**Stack alignment.** The role-gate is enforced at the Convex query layer (`get_org_wallet` query function checks `ctx.auth.identity` role against the permitted set before returning). PostHog tracks `wallet.read.scope_violation` events for Ops monitoring of attempted-read patterns. Deploy-time validator `wallet_read_role_gate_scope` (Appendix M.5) asserts the permitted-role set across the API endpoint, the in-app widget, and the §50 Ops Console projection.

### 34.12.5 Enterprise Collapse to One Contract

When both consoles are on Enterprise, the Org signs one combined contract:

| Aspect | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Subscription floor | Single floor at the higher of the two ($3,000/month per BPS §6 / SPS §8 — both floors are $3K/mo, so the combined floor is $3K/mo) |
| CommittedSpendContract | One contract covering both consoles (`linked_wallet_id` references the unified Wallet); `commit_value_dollars ≥ $12,000/yr`. **Phase 7 V7 D-V7-007 remediation, 2026-05-07.** The CommittedSpendContract is **single-pool only** — there is NO per-console budget allocation field on §4.8.8. An Org wanting per-team / per-business-unit budget visibility achieves this via the Ops Console's per-cost-center reporting (§50), NOT via a per-console split on the contract entity. Deploy-time validator `committed_spend_single_pool_invariant` (Appendix M.5) asserts §4.8.8 has no per-console allocation field. |
| Discount band | Derived from the combined commit per `committed_spend_discount_band` (Appendix J); no separate band per console |
| Dedicated CSM | One CSM works both sides of the Org; QBR cadence is unified |
| Custom integration scope | Defined per contract; covers both consoles' integration needs |
| SLA | 99.9% uptime + 4-hour critical response — applies platform-wide; not differentiated per console |
| DPA | One Data Processing Agreement covering both consoles |
| Audit log retention | 7 years for both consoles |
| Auto-renewal opt-out scope | **Phase 7 V7 D-V7-010 remediation, 2026-05-07.** The §4.8.8 `auto_renew_at_term_end` field is a single Boolean covering both consoles — opt-out is **all-or-nothing**. There is NO per-console auto-renewal opt-out under the §34.12.5 single-contract collapse. Customers wanting per-console renewal terms must dissolve the §34.12.5 collapse via the §34.12.5.B partial-dissolution path before opting out per console. Deploy-time validator `committed_spend_single_auto_renew_invariant` (Appendix M.5) asserts §4.8.8 has no per-console auto-renewal field. |

### 34.12.5.B Partial-Dissolution Path on One-Side Enterprise Downgrade (Phase 7 V7 D-V7-006 Remediation, 2026-05-07)

When an Org holding the §34.12.5 dual-Enterprise collapse downgrades ONE console from Enterprise (e.g., Buyer Enterprise → Buyer Scale, Seller Enterprise stays), the §34.12.5 single-contract collapse condition is no longer met. The contract enters a **partial-dissolution** transition that materially restructures the financial relationship while preserving §34.19.1 carry-over guarantees:

| Step | Action | Timing |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1. Dissolution declaration | At the downgrade-effective billing-rollover boundary (`current_period_ends_at`), the §34.12.5 collapse dissolves. The CommittedSpendContract `status` transitions `active → terminated` for the dual-Enterprise contract; a `partial_dissolution` audit event fires with `terminated_reason = one_side_enterprise_downgrade` (new value added to §4.8.8 `terminated_reason` enum). | At billing rollover |
| 2. Remaining-Enterprise console contract | A NEW CommittedSpendContract row is created for the remaining-Enterprise console at the standard $3K/mo single-console Enterprise floor. The new contract is keyed `(org_id, console=<remaining_enterprise_console>)` (the `console` scoping is added to §4.8.8 schema as part of this remediation — see §4.8.8 schema update). The `commit_value_dollars` of the new contract is the **proportional remainder** of the dissolved contract's `commit_burn_remaining_value_dollars` allocated to the remaining console per the `commit_allocation_at_dissolution_pct` Ops-Finance-set proportion (default 50/50 unless Sales-Ops sets otherwise per the original contract). | At billing rollover |
| 3. Downgraded-console commit shortfall | Unspent committed-spend allocated to the dissolved (downgraded) console is treated per `shortfall_policy` (§4.8.8): `forfeit` (default) → forfeit at dissolution; `partial_credit_next_year` → credit applied to a future contract's renewal; `rollover_capped` → up to `shortfall_rollover_max_pct` (≤ 25%) rolls forward to the remaining-Enterprise contract's commit pool. | At billing rollover |
| 4. AIWallet pooling rule | The §34.10.3 pooling rule continues to apply: the Org's single AIWallet draws from BOTH (i) the remaining-Enterprise console's commit pool (highest priority per §34.10.1 burn priority) AND (ii) the downgraded console's plan-tier `included_budget_remaining` (per §34.10.3 Free+Paid collapse rules; the downgraded console's budget is added to the pool unless it's Free or Solo, in which case the §34.10.3 collapse rules apply). The cross-console firewall on Billing Ledger reads continues per §34.12.4. | Continuous |
| 5. Audit and customer communication | Webhook `committed_spend_contract.dissolved_partial` (Appendix C; HMAC-SHA256 signed; recipients: customer's webhook subscription + `org_owner` + `billing_admin`) emits with the dissolved contract id, the new contract id, the shortfall disposition, and the remaining-console allocation. Loops.so emails the customer 30 days before the dissolution-effective rollover with the breakdown. | 30 days pre-dissolution + at dissolution |
| 6. Restoration on re-upgrade | If the downgraded console upgrades back to Enterprise within 60 days of dissolution, the partial dissolution is **reversible**: the §34.12.5 collapse re-applies; the new single-console contract terminates; a fresh combined contract is signed by the customer (DocuSign envelope re-issued). The `committed_spend.restoration_post_partial_dissolution` event fires for audit. | Within 60 days of dissolution |
| 7. Restoration after 60 days | Beyond 60 days, the restoration path is treated as a fresh dual-Enterprise contract negotiation; no automatic collapse re-application. | After 60 days post-dissolution |

The §4.8.8 CommittedSpendContract entity schema is extended to support partial-dissolution semantics:

- New field `console` enum (nullable; `null` = combined dual-Enterprise contract; `buyer` / `seller` = single-console post-dissolution contract). Phase 7 V7 D-V7-006 — added to §4.8.8 schema.
- New field `dissolved_from_contract_id` UUID (FK; nullable; FK → CommittedSpendContract). Set on contracts created from a §34.12.5.B dissolution; null otherwise.
- New field `commit_allocation_at_dissolution_pct` Integer (nullable; 0–100; default 50). Set on the dissolving contract at dissolution time; allocates remaining commit between the two consoles. Sales-Ops-overridable per the original contract terms.
- New field `partial_dissolution_at` Timestamp (nullable). Set on the dissolved contract when dissolution commits.
- Acceptance criteria: `console` MUST be `null` for any contract under §34.12.5 collapse (assertion); `console` MUST be non-null for any single-console post-dissolution contract; deploy-time validator `committed_spend_console_scope_consistency` (Appendix M.5) asserts.

The new value added to `committed_spend_status` enum: `partially_dissolved` (the dissolving contract enters this state at the dissolution boundary, distinct from `terminated`). Appendix J registration: `partially_dissolved` is added to `committed_spend_status`.

**Stack alignment.** The dissolution orchestration is implemented as a Convex scheduled function triggered by the Stripe `subscription.updated` webhook handler at the downgrade-effective boundary. The new CommittedSpendContract row is created atomically with the old contract's transition; the `linked_wallet_id` reference on AIWallet remains stable (unified pool); the AIWallet `committed_spend_contract_id` field updates to the new contract id at the boundary. Loops.so handles customer-side emails; PostHog tracks the dissolution funnel for product-quality dashboards. DocuSign integration handles the restoration-on-re-upgrade re-signature path.

### 34.12.6 Solo-Tier Per-Console Subscription Billing (Authoritative)

Phase 14.9 — landed under v7.1 integration program. Solo on either console activates an **independent Stripe subscription** scoped to that console. Solo never bundles with the contralateral console for billing purposes:

| Behavior | Rule | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Stripe subscription scope | One Stripe Subscription per Solo activation, keyed `(org_id, console)` | Phase 14.9 (AE) |
| Cross-console Solo bundle discount | None — an Org holding Buyer Solo + Seller Solo pays $98/mo (subscription) or two independent $199 charges | SPS §12 #6 |
| Plan-change orchestration | Buyer-side Solo upgrade / downgrade does NOT affect the Seller-side plan and vice versa | §34.12.1 |
| Enterprise collapse interaction | Solo on either console does NOT participate in the §34.12.5 dual-Enterprise contract collapse | §34.12.1; §34.12.5 |
| Wallet surface | Per the §34.10.3 Solo-co-resident rule, Solo's engine-absorbed envelope is invisible on the AIWallet; the contralateral console's wallet (if paid) renders unchanged | §34.10.3 |
| Refund processing | Per-console refunds are scoped to the Stripe Subscription on that console; cross-console refunds are forbidden | Phase 14.9 (AE) |
| Stripe Customer linkage | Single Stripe Customer per Org per `legal_entity` (per §34.10.5); two Stripe Subscriptions hang off the single Customer for a Buyer-Solo + Seller-Solo Org | §34.10.5 |
| Subscription cancellation cadence | Each Solo subscription cancels on its own anniversary; cancelling one console's Solo does NOT cascade to the other console | Phase 14.9 (AE) |
| Per-eval / per-bid charge linkage | Per-eval / per-bid charges (§34.2.5) are independent BillingEvent rows, not Stripe Subscription invoices; they carry the `console` field on the AIOperation / Workspace they originate from | §34.2.5 |

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. An Org holding Buyer Solo + Seller Solo MUST receive two separate Stripe Subscription invoices each billing cycle; QA test `solo_dual_console_independent_invoicing` asserts.
2. A plan change on one Solo console MUST NOT modify the contralateral console's plan; QA test `solo_plan_change_console_isolation` asserts.
3. The §34.10.3 Solo-co-resident rule MUST be enforced at AIWallet read time — the wallet response MUST NOT include Solo's engine-absorbed envelope in any customer-facing counter; QA test `aiwallet_response_excludes_solo_envelope` asserts.

### 34.12.7 Billing Admin Role

The `billing_admin` org-level role (new in v7.0.0; logged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Breaking Changes`) is the only role permitted to:

- Change wallet config (overage, caps, auto-topup) on either console
- Enable / disable wallet overage
- Initiate manual top-ups
- Change plan tier on either side (subject to Sales-Ops sign-off for Enterprise)
- Accept or reject a Vendor Pro Trial Seat grant (vendor side)
- File a ContestRecord (§4.8.5)
- View the cross-console Billing Ledger
- Approve a CommittedSpendContract auto-renewal opt-out

The role is granted by `org_owner` and `org_admin`; it is not granted by default. Audit log entries record every billing-state mutation with user attribution; entry kinds include `org.wallet_overage_enabled`, `org.wallet_cap_changed`, `org.wallet_topup_initiated`, `org.plan_changed`, `org.pro_trial_seat_accepted`, `org.contest_filed`. The role is registered in Appendix J → `Billing Admin Role (new) (§4.8.3, §4.8.5, §4.8.11)`.

### 34.12.8 Cross-Side Billing Failure Modes

1. **Both consoles concurrently downgrade to Free.** Resolved: at billing rollover, the unified pool collapses to $5 (§34.10.3 Free+Free rule); both consoles' DowngradeExcessDataBuckets are created independently per §34.6.
2. **An Org changes residency mid-period with active commit on Enterprise.** Resolved: §4.8.3 Failure Mode #6 — residency change requires Ops Finance migration runbook; in-period change does not retroactively reissue invoices.
3. **`billing_admin` is deprovisioned with active wallet config in flight.** Resolved: deprovisioning preserves the role assignment audit; another `billing_admin` (or `org_owner`) can take over; in-flight Stripe charges complete.
4. **Buyer-side and Seller-side downgrades on the same day produce overlapping notice cascades.** Resolved: each console's notification stream is independent (`downgrade_bucket.notice_d60` per bucket; deduplication via bucket ID); recipients see both notices.
5. **Solo subscription on one console + Enterprise on the other.** Resolved: Solo subscription invoices independently per §34.12.6; Enterprise contract scope per §34.12.5 covers only the Enterprise console; the Solo subscription does NOT roll into the Enterprise contract floor or commit. Stripe Customer is single per `(org_id, legal_entity)`; the two subscriptions hang off the single Customer with distinct `console` metadata.
6. **Solo per-eval / per-bid charge fires while Solo subscription is also active on the same console.** Resolved: this is a configuration error — UX rejects the per-eval / per-bid Stripe charge attempt with HTTP 422 `solo_subscription_active_per_eval_charge_blocked` (Buyer) / `solo_subscription_active_per_bid_charge_blocked` (Seller). Subscription Solo accounts NEVER incur per-eval / per-bid charges. QA test `solo_subscription_blocks_per_charge` asserts.
7. **Solo per-eval / per-bid refund extends past the 7-day window due to Stripe processing delay.** Resolved: refund eligibility is computed at refund-request time, not refund-processing time; a refund requested on day 7 with Stripe settlement on day 9 is still eligible. The refund-eligibility timestamp is captured at request time and stored on the BillingEvent for audit.

## 34.13 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat (M17) {#34.13-buyer-funded-pro-trial-seat}

§34.13 documents the Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat mechanic in full per SPS §15.5 and MS §3.3 M17. Entity-level mechanics live in §4.3.17 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat Grant (Phase 1).

### 34.13.1 Purpose

When a buyer on Buyer Scale or Buyer Enterprise (per §34.1.1) invites a vendor, the invite may optionally grant the vendor a 30-day Seller Starter trial. The cost of the subscription tier is absorbed into the buyer's plan (no cash transfer; Stripe metered as `sourcera_pro_trial_grant`). AI usage during the trial is metered to the **vendor's** Org AIWallet, not the buyer's. The mechanic lifts seller-side conversion rate at the highest-converting PLG moment (the forced vendor signup) while improving response quality on the buyer's highest-stakes evaluations.

### 34.13.2 Allocation

Per-tier Pro Trial Seat allowances are authoritative in §34.1.1 cell **Vendor Pro Trial Seats (M17)**. §34.13.2 does NOT restate the per-tier values; consumers MUST reference §34.1.1 for the canonical Free / Starter / Growth / Scale / Enterprise allowances. Per §34.1.1: Buyer Scale and Buyer Enterprise are the only tiers with non-zero monthly allowance.

Allocation rules:

- Unused seats **do not carry over** month to month; allocation replenishes on the buyer's billing anniversary.
- Buyer plan downgrades zero out the current period's unused seats at the downgrade boundary; new monthly allowance at the new tier (per §34.1.1) applies from the next cycle.
- Buyer plan upgrades from below Scale to Scale or Enterprise immediately credit the new tier's monthly allowance (per §34.1.1) for the in-flight period (no proration).
- An Ops-Console Pricing Admin may temporarily increase a buyer's allowance for a defined window (e.g., a specific evaluation cohort) per `org.pro_trial_seat_quota_overridden` audit event; overrides are time-boxed and reverse automatically at expiry.

### 34.13.3 Grant Mechanics

| Step | Action | Audit / Notification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | A Buyer Workspace Owner OR Org Admin (per §5.3) clicks "Invite with Pro Trial" on a vendor invitation flow | UI surface in §14 (vendor curation; UI authoring pending per Phase 1 Known Gap K-V12 / Phase 4 Known Gaps) |
| 2 | The buyer's allocation decrements by 1; if allocation = 0, the option is disabled in the UI with explanatory copy ("0 of 5 Pro Trial Seats remaining this month") | `org.pro_trial_seat_allocated` audit event on buyer Org |
| 3 | The vendor receives the magic-link invitation email with a "Your invite includes 30 days of Seller Starter, free" callout | `pro_trial_seat.invite` email (Loops.so template; pending Phase 1 known gap closure) |
| 4 | On magic-link click, the vendor's Org is provisioned (or upgraded if existing Free) with Seller Starter entitlements: `seller_plan_tier = seller_starter`, `trial_source_buyer_org_id = <buyer>`, `trial_expires_at = now + 30d`, `trial_grant_id = <Pro Trial Seat Grant entity ID>` | `pro_trial_seat.granted` audit event on both Orgs (buyer + vendor) |
| 5 | Seller Starter AI budget ($30 value-dollars) is credited to the vendor's AIWallet `included_budget_remaining` for the trial period (§4.8.3) | n/a |
| 6 | All Seller Starter features unlock immediately: KB capacity to 1,000 entries, Firecrawl 2 sources weekly, EOI quota 10/month, Verified-tier eligibility, Page Enrichment 1/year, Monthly Seller Signals digest, etc. | n/a |
| 7 | Day-27 reminder fires to vendor Billing Admin: "Your trial ends in 3 days. Convert to keep your KB and in-flight bids active." | `pro_trial_seat.day_27_reminder` email |
| 8 | Day-31 transition: convert / auto-downgrade / declined per §34.13.4 | Per §34.13.4 |

### 34.13.4 Trial Completion (Day 31)

| Outcome | Behavior | Stripe / Audit |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Convert** | Vendor adds payment method and confirms Seller Starter (or higher); plan persists; included budget resets on new billing cycle; no data loss | `sourcera_pro_trial_conversion` Stripe meter event; `pro_trial_seat.converted` audit + email; M17 conversion rate dashboard updated |
| **Auto-downgrade** | Vendor takes no action by day 31 23:59 UTC; plan downgrades to `seller_free`; entities exceeding Free caps (KB > 50, Capability Declarations > 3, etc.) enter §34.6 90-day read-only preservation | `sourcera_pro_trial_expired` Stripe meter event; `pro_trial_seat.auto_downgraded` audit + email |
| **Explicit decline** | Vendor explicitly declines via in-app banner during trial OR rejects grant on receipt; same behavior as auto-downgrade; trial may be declined immediately or any time before day 31 | `sourcera_pro_trial_expired` Stripe meter event; `pro_trial_seat.declined` audit + email |

Carry-over invariants: KB entries, in-flight bids, Capability Declarations, Firecrawl source configs persist through any outcome. Auto-downgrade triggers §34.6 preservation (not deletion).

### 34.13.5 Restrictions

| Restriction | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| **One trial per buyer-vendor pair per 365 days** | A vendor Org cannot receive a second Pro Trial Seat grant from the same buyer Org within 365 days of the prior grant; attempt returns `trial_seat_same_buyer_365d_block` (Appendix I — pending) |
| **Vendor already on a paid Seller plan** | Cannot receive a Pro Trial Seat (no downgrade or double-funding); attempt returns `trial_seat_vendor_already_paid` |
| **Buyer below Scale** | Cannot issue Pro Trial Seat (no allocation); attempt returns `trial_seat_buyer_below_scale` |
| **Buyer's allocation pool exhausted** | Returns `trial_seat_pool_exhausted` (cap per §34.1.1 cell **Vendor Pro Trial Seats (M17)**) |
| **Vendor Billing Admin may reject the grant** | Rejection is audited as `pro_trial_seat.declined`; the buyer's allocation is **NOT refunded** (anti-abuse: prevents buyer from probing vendors) |
| **Anti-spam framework applies** | Ops Console may restrict a buyer's Pro Trial Seat usage on abuse signal per §3.5 Anti-Spam (MS §3.5); restrictions logged in Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100); Ops can zero allocation, time-box restrict, or revoke prior unredeemed grants |
| **Invited vendor must clear the same anti-spam framework as a normal invite** | Invite-eligibility gates apply: domain verification, opt-out registry check, suppression list check |
| **Trial cannot be re-extended** | A trial in progress cannot be extended beyond 30 days; vendor must convert to Starter+ or accept auto-downgrade |

### 34.13.6 Metering and Reporting

| Surface | What is reported |
| :---- | :---- |
| Stripe meter events | `sourcera_pro_trial_grant` at grant time; `sourcera_pro_trial_conversion` at day-30/31 conversion; `sourcera_pro_trial_expired` at auto-downgrade |
| Internal conversion-rate dashboard | Pro Trial grants issued, conversions by day 31, AI budget utilization during trial, comparison vs. cold-start Free → Starter conversion rate, by buyer cohort |
| Buyer-side reporting | Per-buyer view: "X of Y Pro Trial Seats issued this period; Z converted to paid"; surfaces ROI of the M17 mechanic on the buyer's plan value proposition |
| Vendor-side reporting | Vendor sees the grant origin in their Wallet UI: "Granted by [Buyer Org] until [date]"; transparency builds trust |
| Ops Console | Signal Integrity Monitor surfaces buyers with abnormal grant-to-conversion ratios (low conversion = potential spam pattern); per-vendor view of grant history across buyers |

### 34.13.7 Failure Modes Addressed

1. **Vendor's wallet is in `payment_failed_grace` when trial expires.** Resolved: auto-downgrade still fires at day 31; the grace state is for the prior subscription only and does not extend the trial.
2. **Buyer downgrades from Scale to Growth between grant and vendor magic-link click.** Resolved: the grant is honored (the allocation was decremented at click time and the pool is irrelevant after issuance).
3. **Vendor receives multiple concurrent Pro Trial Seat grants from different buyers in the same week.** Resolved: only the first redeemed grant takes effect; subsequent grants are queued and the vendor receives a notification with a 7-day acceptance window per queued grant; if not accepted in 7 days, queued grant expires and the buyer's allocation is refunded for that specific grant.
4. **Trial AI usage exhausts the vendor's $30 budget mid-trial.** Resolved: vendor wallet behaves as a normal Seller Starter wallet — overage is off by default; vendor may enable overage to continue; trial does not extend or refund on exhaustion.
5. **Buyer Org is deleted between grant and vendor redemption.** Resolved: grant remains valid (one-way audit trail); vendor magic link works; vendor sees "[Buyer Org] (deleted)" in the grant attribution UI.

### 34.13.8 Pro Trial Seat Acceptance Criteria

1. Pro Trial Seat allocation MUST be enforced at Wallet/UI time of issuance; over-issuance returns HTTP 403 `trial_seat_pool_exhausted`.
2. Day-31 transition MUST execute exactly once per active trial (idempotent); QA test `pro_trial_day_31_idempotent` asserts.
3. Audit trail MUST capture grant issuance, redemption, conversion, and decline events with both buyer and vendor Org attribution.
4. Auto-downgrade on day 31 MUST trigger §34.6 preservation for any over-cap entities; QA test `pro_trial_auto_downgrade_preservation` asserts.
5. Anti-spam framework MUST be evaluated at grant time and at vendor redemption time; suppressions take precedence.
6. AI usage during trial MUST meter against the vendor's Wallet, not the buyer's; QA test `pro_trial_wallet_attribution` asserts.
7. The 365-day same-buyer-vendor rate-limit MUST be enforced atomically; concurrent grant attempts deduplicate via partial unique index on `(buyer_org_id, vendor_org_id, granted_at_year)` — partial because expired/declined grants must not block re-grant.
8. The buyer's allocation MUST decrement at click time, not at vendor redemption — vendor non-redemption does NOT refund the allocation (anti-probing rule).

## 34.14 Seller Rate Card (Authoritative) {#34.14-seller-rate-card-authoritative}

This section is the authoritative catalog of seller-facing AI capabilities, their outcome-based `value_price` and `cost_price` in USD, their Free Allowance overrides (where they deviate from the §34.1.2 plan-tier baseline), and their authored pricing floors. It supersedes any rate implied in SPS §9, MS §2.8, or scattered prose elsewhere in the Master Spec. Where a capability is also buyer-facing (cross-console capability), this section is still authoritative on the seller-console price; the buyer-console price lives in `CapabilityRegistryEntry` (§4.8.2) under the same `capability_id` and MUST satisfy the same §34.3 invariants.

Derivation: Every row applies the outcome pricing formula from §34.3 — `value_price = MAX(min_value, cost_base × 10)` and `cost_price = MAX(min_cost, cost_base × 1.05)` — with `cost_base` set to Anthropic inference cost at 2026-04-10 pricing plus 5% infra overhead (Convex, Firecrawl, vector-index amortization, egress). `cost_base` is recomputed nightly at 02:30 UTC per §34.3.2; the rate card published at `api.sourcera.com/v1/pricing` reflects the most recent published `PricingTableVersion` (§4.8.9).

**Notes on the baseline table.**
- All `value_price` and `cost_price` values are display-rounded to two decimal places; the authoritative stored representation is integer cents in `CapabilityRegistryEntry.value_price_cents` and `cost_price_cents` (§4.8.2).
- `cost_base` values are advisory / telemetry-derived and are subject to nightly recalc per §34.3.2. A recalc that would push `cost_base × 10` below the current `value_price` does NOT auto-reprice — it triggers a `cost_base_below_price_drift` alert to Ops Finance; re-pricing requires explicit sign-off per §34.3.3.
- Floor columns (`min_value_price_cents`, `min_cost_price_cents`) are **Authored Extensions** — MS §2.8 does not enumerate floors. The floors exist to prevent commodity-infra deflation from collapsing the rate below the operational cost of a failed operation (billing ledger writes, contest-record creation, cold-storage retention, settlement dashboards). Floors MUST be sign-off gated by Ops Finance before any change; tracked as `RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions → §34.14.1 Rate Card Floors`.
- `Source` column cites MS §2.8 row N and SPS §9 row N (both are single-level tables; there are no `§2.8.N` or `§9.N` subsections). The Phase 2 remediation replaced the prior hallucinated subsection citations per decision-log entry D-S1 (2026-04-18).
