The `value_price` is `$0.00` because the seller is not the billed party; it remains in §34.14.1.b for audit and transparency. The `cost_price` is recorded against the Platform Integrity cost center per §34.16.2.

### 34.14.2 Pricing Derivation Invariants

The following invariants MUST hold for every row in §34.14.1 and are enforced by deploy-time validator (QA test `rate_card_invariants`):

1. **Outcome formula compliance.** `value_price_cents = MAX(min_value_price_cents, ROUND(cost_base_cents × 10))` and `cost_price_cents = MAX(min_cost_price_cents, ROUND(cost_base_cents × 1.05))`. Validator FAILS if any row violates.
2. **Margin floor compliance.** For rows with `cost_center=customer_billed`, `(value_price_cents − cost_price_cents) / value_price_cents ≥ 0.88`. Rows that breach 88% at the floor values MUST have Ops Finance sign-off on file in the `rate_card_exception_log` (Appendix C new event category); validator surfaces breaches as warnings, not blockers (the floors supersede the formula when the floor is hit — that's the point of the floor).
3. **Currency integrity.** All prices are denominated in USD. Buyer Orgs in non-USD locales see the rate card converted at the daily FX rate published by Stripe Exchange at 00:00 UTC; the stored ledger value remains USD cents (§34.2.4).
4. **Versioning.** Every rate card change MUST publish a new `PricingTableVersion` row with `status=draft`, go through Ops Finance review, then transition to `status=published`; in-flight transactions are grandfathered per §4.8.9.
5. **Rate card publication SLA.** A `PricingTableVersion` with `status=published` and `effective_at ≤ now` MUST be reachable at `api.sourcera.com/v1/pricing` within 30 seconds of publication.

### 34.14.3 Authored Floor Values

The 24 floor values in §34.14.1 (12 capabilities × 2 floors each) are Authored Extensions. The MS §2.8 and SPS §9 rate cards enumerate headline prices only; no source document enumerates floors. Floors were authored at 33% of the headline price (value_price) and 50% of the headline cost (cost_price), rounded to the nearest cent, subject to a minimum of $0.01 for any non-zero row. Rationale: a floor at 33% preserves a meaningful price signal during short-term cost deflation while protecting the operational-cost recovery margin; a floor at 50% of cost_price ensures that `cost_price` never drops below half its steady-state level, preserving enough margin to cover the reversal-processing overhead (contest-record creation, audit-log writes, cold-storage retention). These values are flagged in `RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions → §34.14.3` and require Ops Finance + Sales Ops sign-off before the rate card is promoted to `status=published`.

### 34.14.4 Free Allowance Overrides

Rows where the seller-plan Free Allowance differs from the §34.1.2 baseline are explicit in the `Plan Gating` column above. Two overrides are **Authored Extensions**:

1. **`kb_bootstrap`: 1 lifetime first-bootstrap grant per Seller Org; annual re-bootstrap cadence per §34.1.2.** Rationale: `kb_bootstrap` is the seed-KB onboarding capability; one free first bootstrap is the activation lever that gets a seller from signup to an answerable first RFP. Annual re-bootstrap allowances are plan-tier entitlements, not extra `FreeAllowanceCounter` grants, and follow the §34.1.2 **KB Bootstrap (Opus)** cell (Seller Solo and Seller Starter: 1/year; Seller Growth: 3/year; Seller Scale/Enterprise: Unlimited). More than one lifetime first-bootstrap grant would create incentive-gaming (orgs re-onboarding to game the counter). The lifetime grant is tracked in `FreeAllowanceCounter.scope_hint = "lifetime_per_org"` (§4.8.7). Sales-Ops sign-off pending on whether to extend to 2 lifetime first-bootstrap grants for Starter — flagged in RECONCILIATION.
2. **`ghost_rfp_ingestion`: 1 lifetime per Seller Org on Free and Starter.** Rationale: equivalent onboarding activation for sellers who import historical bid PDFs instead of (or in addition to) `kb_bootstrap`. Tracked similarly. Sales-Ops sign-off pending on whether a seller can redeem both their `kb_bootstrap` free allowance AND their `ghost_rfp_ingestion` free allowance, or whether the two are mutually exclusive.

Both overrides are implemented by `FreeAllowanceCounter.scope_hint="lifetime_per_org"` with `reset_at` set to a sentinel date far in the future (`9999-12-31T00:00:00Z`) per §4.8.7 so the counter never auto-resets.

### 34.14.5 Rate Card Lifecycle and Change Management

| Lifecycle stage | Trigger | Artifact(s) created | Notification | Grandfathering |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| `draft` | Ops Finance opens a rate-card change in the Admin Console | `PricingTableVersion.status=draft` | Internal Linear ticket; no external notification | N/A |
| `under_review` | Ops Finance submits the draft for VP Finance + Legal review | PricingTableVersion transition | Internal Slack `#pricing-review` | N/A |
| `approved` | All reviewers sign off (VP Finance + Legal + eng) | PricingTableVersion transition | Internal email to `ops-finance@sourcera.com` | N/A |
| `scheduled` | An `effective_at` is set in the future | PricingTableVersion transition; `billing.pricing_table.scheduled` webhook emitted (§31.8.12) | 30-day advance notice email to all `billing_admin` users | Annual-contract customers are locked to the prior version for the remainder of their contract term |
| `published` | `effective_at ≤ now` | PricingTableVersion transition; `billing.pricing_table.published` webhook (§31.8.12); Public Pricing API refresh within 30 sec | `pricing.updated` PostHog event; in-app banner for all admin users for 7 days | As above |
| `superseded` | A newer version reaches `published` | PricingTableVersion transition (old version) | None (automatic) | Annual contracts still grandfathered to whichever version was `published` at contract signing |
| `rolled_back` | Ops Finance invokes the emergency rollback (price regression, data corruption, etc.) | PricingTableVersion transition; `billing.pricing_table.rolled_back` webhook (§31.8.12) | Customer-facing email + in-app banner; ledger reversals applied to any AIOperations billed under the rolled-back version per §34.11 | Same as `published` |

Rate card changes that REDUCE a customer's effective rate apply retroactively by default (monthly reconciliation worker issues credit to wallet). Rate card changes that INCREASE a customer's effective rate apply prospectively only; customers on annual contracts are locked at the signing rate for the full term. Both behaviors are automated and audit-logged.

### 34.14.6 Acceptance Criteria

1. Every `capability_id` with `cost_center=customer_billed` and `console=seller` MUST have a row in §34.14.1 (baseline) or §34.14.1.b (Authored Extension pending sign-off); deploy-time validator asserts no-orphans in both directions (CapabilityRegistryEntry ↔ rate card) while `rate_card_ae_signoff_gate` separately blocks unsigned §34.14.1.b rows from production activation.
2. The `value_price` and `cost_price` stored on each CapabilityRegistryEntry MUST exactly match the §34.14.1 table values at the current `PricingTableVersion.status=published` version; nightly reconciliation job asserts.
3. The 24 floor values in §34.14.3 MUST NOT change without a `RateCardFloorChangeLog` entry signed off by Ops Finance and Sales Ops; QA test `rate_card_floor_signoff_present` asserts.
4. Free Allowance overrides for `kb_bootstrap` and `ghost_rfp_ingestion` MUST be persisted as `FreeAllowanceCounter.scope_hint="lifetime_per_org"` rows with sentinel `reset_at=9999-12-31T00:00:00Z`; onboarding test `seller_free_allowance_lifetime_seed` asserts.
5. The Public Pricing API MUST serve §34.14.1 values verbatim (via the current `PricingTableVersion.published_payload_json.seller_rate_card`); response-shape test `pricing_api_seller_rate_card_shape` asserts.

| AE-8 | `outcome_narrative_builder` | `implicit_retention` | 14 days post-generation | ≥ 60% of narrative characters retained in final published artifact | < 60% retained OR artifact deleted within 48h | `rejected` | 14 days from settlement | `false` | Paired to §34.14.1.b AE-8. Retention threshold higher than row 1 (60% vs 50%) because narrative artifacts are typically shorter and more editorially polished — partial retention is less common. |

**AE activation gate.** The `rate_card_ae_signoff_gate` deploy-time validator (defined in §34.14.1.b) covers both §34.14.1.b and §34.15.1.b: each AE capability MUST have a matching `AuthoredExtensionSignoff` row whose `capability_id` is one of {AE-1..AE-8} and whose `signer_role ∈ {ceo, cpo, staff_engineer_billing}`, active for the current `pricing_table_version_id`. Attempting to activate an AE `capability_id` without sign-off raises `rate_card_ae_signoff_missing` at deploy and `capability_not_signed_off` (HTTP 422) at runtime.

### 34.15.2 Signal Evaluation Mechanics by Class

The `Signal Class` column in §34.15.1 determines the evaluator runtime:

| Signal Class | Evaluator | Settlement Latency Target | Persisted in | Source |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| `synchronous_success` | Inline check at capability `completed` step; settles on the same transaction | ≤ 1 second | `AIOperation.outcome_status` inline | §4.8.3, §4.8.4 |
| `implicit_retention` | Nightly cron at 03:00 UTC scans all `pending_outcome` operations whose evaluation window closes that day; applies Levenshtein-distance measurement against the final artifact | ≤ 60 seconds from window close (AE) | `AIOperation.outcome_status` + `OutcomeContract.last_evaluated_at` | AE |
| `implicit_engagement` | Nightly cron same schedule; queries PostHog engagement events within the window | ≤ 60 seconds from window close (AE) | As above | AE |
| `explicit_user_signal` | Event-driven on the signal webhook (user button click, bid outcome registration, dispute filing, etc.); settles within seconds of signal arrival | ≤ 5 seconds from signal arrival (AE); 300-second grace before default-on-timeout fires | As above | AE |
| `platform_internal` | Editorial reviewer decision from Admin Console; settles when reviewer submits | ≤ 5 seconds from reviewer submission | As above | §4.4.21 |

Authored Extension flag: the 60-second settlement latency for implicit classes, the 5-second latency for explicit-signal classes, and the 300-second grace window before default-on-timeout fires are **Authored Extensions** — MS §2.9 / SPS §10 do not specify latencies. These values are calibrated from internal operational experience and will be tuned at Phase 5 closeout; tracked in `RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions → §34.15.2 Signal Latency Targets`.

### 34.15.3 Contest Interaction

Every settlement (accept, reject, or auto_accept) creates an OutcomeContract pointer in the AIOperation (`contract_ref_id` → §4.8.4) and stamps `settlement_at`. The seller's contest window opens at `settlement_at + 1 minute` (one-minute cooldown to prevent double-settlement races) and closes at `settlement_at + contract.contest_window_days`.

Contests are **not restricted to `rejected` outcomes** — sellers can contest an `accepted` operation if they believe the outcome was misattributed (e.g., `first_pass_rfp_draft` tagged as retained but the user actually copy-pasted from a different source). Ops Finance evaluates per §34.11.4.

For `auto_accepted` signals (classes `implicit_engagement` rows 6 and 10 — buyer_signal_digest, opportunity_recommender): the seller MAY contest to request a no-bill if they believe the capability was not actually valuable; approved contests credit the wallet with `value_price`. Default bias is to honor such contests because the capability is low-friction courtesy; Ops Finance policy is "approve unless there's evidence of abuse."

### 34.15.4 Failure Modes

1. **Evaluation window closes while the user is mid-edit.** Resolved: Levenshtein-distance is measured against the final version at `window_close`; in-flight edits are captured in the draft autosave (§13.10). If the user continues editing past `window_close`, those edits do NOT retroactively change the outcome — the outcome freezes at `window_close` to prevent gaming.
2. **User deletes the artifact during the evaluation window then restores it.** Resolved: the evaluator looks at `deleted_at` and `restored_at` timestamps in the artifact audit log. If the artifact is in `deleted` state at `window_close`, the outcome is `rejected`; if it's restored before `window_close`, the outcome is computed against the restored content.
3. **Explicit user signal arrives AFTER default-on-timeout has fired.** Resolved: late signals within 60 days of settlement auto-file a ContestRecord (§4.8.5) with `reason="late_explicit_signal"` and notify Ops Finance within 5 minutes. Ops Finance policy: approve contests where the late signal is `accept` if the delay was ≤ 7 days past window close; otherwise escalate for judgment.
4. **Signal webhook fails delivery (third-party outage).** Resolved: webhook retry curve per §31 (exponential backoff, DLQ after 5 failures, 256 KB payload cap). The signal is persisted locally on DLQ and manually replayable by Ops.
5. **Levenshtein-distance measurement is computationally prohibitive for very long drafts (>100KB).** Resolved: evaluator truncates both the generated draft and the final artifact to 10KB before measurement; the 10KB sample is sufficient for retention-ratio estimation within 2% margin of error (empirically validated in pre-launch benchmark). Drafts exceeding 10KB log `outcome_truncated_for_retention_eval` for QA inspection.
6. **Signal threshold is miscalibrated (too many auto-rejects or auto-accepts).** Resolved: outcome-quality dashboard (§34.17) surfaces `accept_rate`, `reject_rate`, `contest_rate`, `contest_approval_rate` per capability per week; Ops Finance reviews weekly. A capability whose `contest_approval_rate > 15%` MUST be flagged for threshold recalibration. Recalibration is a rate-card change per §34.14.5.
7. **Seller disputes retention measurement (claims their final artifact IS the generated draft, even though characters differ).** Resolved: Ops Finance reviews the diff in the contest workflow; the contest record includes a side-by-side diff view of `generated_draft` vs `final_artifact` with Levenshtein distance annotated (§4.8.5).

### 34.15.5 SellerOutcomeSignalConfig — Platform-Scoped Per-Capability Config

The 12 rows in §34.15.1 MUST each be bound to an active `SellerOutcomeSignalConfig` row at runtime (§4.8.13). SellerOutcomeSignalConfig is the seller-console-specific extension layer over the base `OutcomeContract` (§4.8.4) and is the authoritative source for seller-side signal rules, evaluation windows, alternate-boundary termination events (bid submission, EOI submission, KB publication, response submission), retention / edit / approval thresholds, and k-anonymity floors. The Outcome Resolver (§34.11) dispatches on `SellerOutcomeSignalConfig.accepted_signal_rule_type` for seller-side AIOperations. Per-Org overrides are NOT supported at the Organization level in v7.0.0 — SellerOutcomeSignalConfig is platform-scoped and Ops-managed; all sellers share the same signal rules per capability. Proposals to allow per-Org threshold overrides are a future enhancement tracked as `RECONCILIATION.md → Future Enhancements → FE-§34.15-V1 (per-Org outcome signal threshold overrides)` — NOT in v7.0.0 scope. No Authored Extension entity is required at this layer — §4.8.13 is already authoritative. (The prior `KG-§34-V4` tracker ID was resolved 2026-04-18 when §4.8.13 was confirmed to exist at full spec fidelity; the separate per-Org-override proposal was relabeled to the Future Enhancements section.)

Runtime binding: every AIOperation whose capability is seller-console-only MUST resolve through the active SellerOutcomeSignalConfig for its `capability_id` at settlement time. Missing or `state=retired` configs cause settlement to halt with `seller_outcome_signal_config_missing` (HTTP 500); deploy-time validator asserts 12 active rows in one-to-one correspondence with §34.15.1.

### 34.15.6 Acceptance Criteria

1. Every row in §34.14.1 (MS §2.8 baseline — 12 rows) MUST have a matching OutcomeContract in §34.15.1 (MS §2.9 baseline — 12 rows); deploy-time validator `outcome_contract_baseline_1to1` asserts 1:1 on `capability_id`.
2. Every row in §34.14.1.b (Authored Extensions) MUST have a matching row in §34.15.1.b with identical `capability_id`; deploy-time validator `outcome_contract_ae_1to1` asserts 1:1.
3. Every `capability_id` in CapabilityRegistryEntry MUST have a valid `contract_ref_id` FK into OutcomeContract; orphans fail deploy.
4. The default-on-timeout values in §34.15.1 and §34.15.1.b MUST match `OutcomeContract.default_outcome` at runtime; nightly reconciliation job `outcome_default_drift_check` asserts.
5. `requires_explicit_user_signal` MUST match the Signal Class column per §34.15.2 (`explicit_user_signal` OR `platform_internal` ⇒ `true`; all other classes ⇒ `false`); deploy-time validator asserts.
6. Contest windows MUST open `settlement_at + 60 seconds` and close `settlement_at + contract.contest_window_days × 86400 seconds`; latency test `contest_window_edges` asserts.
7. `ghost_rfp_ingestion` MUST be registered as `implicit_retention` with a 90-day evaluation window and signal-rule "KB entries cited in ≥ 1 future bid response"; deploy-time validator `ghost_rfp_signal_class_lock` asserts the class/window/rule triple against §34.15.1 row 5 exactly.
8. `capability_declaration_suggest` MUST be the canonical capability name for MS §2.9 row 9; references to `capability_declaration_assist` anywhere in code, APIs, events, or docs fail deploy under validator `capability_naming_canonical_form` (paired with §34.14.1 row 9 and §34.8.5).
9. Any AE `capability_id` in §34.15.1.b without an active `AuthoredExtensionSignoff` row for the current `pricing_table_version_id` MUST return `capability_not_signed_off` (HTTP 422) at runtime and fail production deploy under `rate_card_ae_signoff_gate` (§34.14.1.b).
10. The 12 baseline rows in §34.15.1 MUST match MS §2.9 exactly on `capability_id`, Signal Class, Evaluation Window, and Signal Rule; drift tests compare against a frozen MS §2.9 snapshot stored at `_integration/snapshots/MS_2.9_baseline.md`.

## 34.16 Marketplace Discovery Pricing (Non-AI Layer) {#34.16-marketplace-discovery-pricing-non-ai-layer}

Sourcera runs three distinct revenue streams that MUST NOT be commingled in ledgers, dashboards, financial disclosures, or user-facing billing surfaces:

| Revenue Stream | Source | Billing Mechanic | Ledger Enum | Regulatory Framing |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| `rev_ai_wallet` | Outcome-based AI operation billing per §34.3 and §34.14 | Wallet draw per AIOperation | `rev_ai_wallet` | Services revenue (ASC 606 performance-obligation-per-operation) |
| `rev_subscription` | Plan tier fees per §34.1.1 (Buyer plan tiers) and §34.1.2 (Seller plan tiers) | Stripe monthly recurring billing | `rev_subscription` | Services revenue (ASC 606 subscription) |
| `rev_marketplace_discovery` | Marketplace discovery surfaces: Promoted Listings, Verification Tiers, Featured Placements | Per-surface; see §34.16.1–§34.16.3 | `rev_marketplace_discovery` | Advertising revenue (ASC 606 point-in-time or over-time per SKU) |

The `revenue_stream_class` enum (new in v7.0.0; registered in Appendix J; see `RECONCILIATION.md → Enum Additions`) is present on every row in the Billing Ledger (§4.8.3), every monthly close-the-books journal entry, every investor-facing financial summary, and every DSAR export. Commingling is a breaking invariant — deploy-time validator `revenue_stream_firewall` asserts zero rows with `revenue_stream_class=null` and zero cross-stream attribution.

### 34.16.1 SKU 1: Promoted Listings

**What:** Sellers bid for a promoted slot at the top of buyer search results within a specific marketplace category (e.g., "Tier-1 SOC Vendors" / "EHR Interoperability" / etc.). The promoted slot is labeled "Promoted" per FTC advertising disclosure rules and is visually distinguished from organic rankings.

**Who sees it:** Buyers searching or browsing within the targeted category. The promoted listing is shown above organic results but below any §34.16.3 Featured Placements (Featured > Promoted > Organic in display order).

**Pricing:**
- Base rate: §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_base_rate_cents_per_category_week`.
- Monthly placement cap: the seller's plan-included monthly allotment is defined only in §34.1.2 **Promoted Marketplace Placements**. Purchased top-ups beyond that allotment are capped by §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_purchased_top_up_hard_cap_per_month`; requests above the effective monthly cap are blocked per §4.4.19.
- Billing mechanic: **Second-price auction**; see below.
- Billing frequency: Weekly (Monday 00:00 UTC); settled the following Tuesday 03:00 UTC.

#### 34.16.1.A Promoted Listing Monetary and Cap Constants {#34.16.1.a-promoted-listing-monetary-and-cap-constants}

This table is the authoritative home for PromotedListing monetary ceilings, placement caps, reserve floors, and quality-floor defaults. §4.4.19, §27.11, §39, Appendix I, Appendix J, and Appendix K MUST cite these cells rather than restating values inline. Plan-included monthly allotments remain authoritative in §34.1.2 **Promoted Marketplace Placements**.

| Cell | Value | Applies To | Governance |
| ----- | -----:| ----- | ----- |
| `promoted_listing_base_rate_cents_per_category_week` | 50,000 | Purchased top-up category-week base rate and single-bidder weekly reserve | Pricing-table version; Finance + Founder sign-off |
| `promoted_listing_bid_impression_max_cents` | 5,000 | `PromotedListing.bid_impression_cents` CPM ceiling | Pricing-table version; Finance + Engineering sign-off |
| `promoted_listing_bid_eoi_max_cents` | 100,000 | `PromotedListing.bid_eoi_cents` per-qualified-EOI ceiling | Pricing-table version; Finance + Engineering sign-off |
| `promoted_listing_daily_cap_min_cents` | 100 | `PromotedListing.daily_cap_cents` lower bound | Pricing-table version; Finance + Engineering sign-off |
| `promoted_listing_daily_cap_max_cents` | 500,000 | `PromotedListing.daily_cap_cents` upper bound | Pricing-table version; Finance + Engineering sign-off |
| `promoted_listing_per_eoi_cap_min_cents` | 0 | `PromotedListing.per_eoi_cap_cents` lower bound | Pricing-table version; Finance + Engineering sign-off |
| `promoted_listing_per_eoi_cap_max_cents` | 100,000 | `PromotedListing.per_eoi_cap_cents` upper bound | Pricing-table version; Finance + Engineering sign-off |
| `promoted_listing_category_slot_cap` | 3 | Concurrent active promoted listings per category | C.97 Baseline Assumption Manager with Product + Marketplace Ops sign-off |
| `promoted_listing_purchased_top_up_hard_cap_per_month` | 4 | Purchased top-ups per seller per billing month beyond §34.1.2 plan-included allotment | Pricing-table version; Finance + Marketplace Ops sign-off |
| `promoted_listing_kb_health_floor_default` | 60.00 | Default KB Health Score floor for activation eligibility | C.97 Baseline Assumption Manager with Product + Trust sign-off |
| `promoted_listing_surface_reserve_cpm_cents` | 50 | Per-render CPM reserve when only one qualified listing exists on a CPM-priced surface | Pricing-table version; Finance + Marketplace Ops sign-off |

**Auction Mechanic (second-price, category-scoped):**
1. Bid window opens every Sunday 12:00:00.000 UTC inclusive, closes Monday 00:00:00.000 UTC exclusive (D-V6-006 remediation 2026-05-06: bids accepted up to but not including Monday 00:00:00.000 UTC; bids submitted at exactly the close instant are rejected with `promoted_listing_auction_closed` per Appendix I).
2. Sellers submit sealed bids via the Seller Console Admin → Marketplace Discovery → Promoted Listings page. Plan eligibility is Seller Scale or Seller Enterprise per §34.1.2 Promoted Marketplace Placements; ineligible Orgs are rejected with HTTP 403 `promoted_listing_plan_tier_below_scale` per §4.4.19 AC #1 and Appendix I. **A seller MAY submit at most one bid per category per weekly auction window** (D-V6-007 remediation 2026-05-06; multiple bids by the same seller for the same category in the same window are rejected with `promoted_listing_duplicate_bid_per_window` — new; Appendix I; HTTP 409). Cross-category bids by the same seller in the same window remain unaffected, subject to the plan-included monthly allotment in §34.1.2 plus the purchased-top-up hard cap in §4.4.19 / §27.11.2.
3. At close, bids are sorted by the deterministic ordering tuple `(bid_cents DESC, bid_submitted_at ASC, seller_org_id ASC)` (D-V6-002 / D-V6-003 remediation 2026-05-06). The primary key is the bid amount; the secondary key is `bid_submitted_at` — the timestamp of the `pending_eligibility_check → active` transition that records the seller's bid for THIS weekly auction (NOT the entity-creation `PromotedListing.created_at`, which is pinned to draft-creation time and is unrelated to per-week auction timing); the tertiary key is `seller_org_id` ASC (lexicographic on the UUID string form), which deterministically resolves the rare `(bid_cents, bid_submitted_at)` collision case at microsecond precision.
4. The **top bidder pays the second-highest bid** for the week; ties on bid amount are broken by the secondary key (`bid_submitted_at` ASC — earliest bid in the current weekly window wins) with the tertiary key (`seller_org_id` ASC) as the deterministic fallback.
5. If fewer than 2 bids per category, the single bidder pays the reserve price in §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_base_rate_cents_per_category_week` regardless of their bid.
6. Maximum promoted listings per category per week is §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_category_slot_cap`; ranks above that cap are unfilled and the category surfaces organic results only. Rationale: prevent promotion saturation.

**Anonymization (k=5 aggregation):**
- Bidding metrics (average bid, max bid, min bid, bid volume) are surfaced to sellers in a weekly `PromotedListingAuctionDigest` only when at least **5 distinct Seller Orgs** bid in the category that week. Categories with <5 distinct bidders do NOT receive the digest — rationale: prevent re-identification of individual bidders by inference.

**Labeling and Compliance:**
- Promoted slots MUST render the label "Promoted" per FTC 16 CFR 255.5 advertising-disclosure rules.
- Promoted slot rendering MUST NOT be hidden by buyer preference settings; the label is non-suppressible.
- Promoted listing click-throughs MUST be tracked in PostHog with event `marketplace_promoted_listing_clicked` (Appendix G — registered in Marketplace Events block; `.` → `_` per §31.8 Acceptance #16 naming convention).

**Entity:** `PromotedListing` (§4.4.19, already defined pre-v7.0.0 rewrite).

**Three-Revenue-Stream Invariant:** `PromotedListing.invoice_line_item_id` → `BillingLedger` row with `revenue_stream_class=rev_marketplace_discovery`. Commingling with AI wallet or subscription revenue is a deploy-time invariant failure.

**MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord** (§4.8.12) is the authoritative revenue-line record for all three marketplace-discovery SKUs (`promoted_listing`, `verification_upgrade`, `featured_placement`). Every PromotedListing win and any future paid `verification_upgrade` or `featured_placement` sale produces exactly one MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord row with `cost_center=rev_marketplace_discovery`. See §4.8.12 for full field-table, state machine (`pending` → `invoiced` → `paid` / `voided` / `refunded`), k-anonymity deferral logic (k=5 floor with timeout-to-void), FX rate locking at purchase time, legal-entity partitioning by seller Org residency, and append-only post-invoice semantics. Retention is 7 years per §40.2; DSAR pseudonymization of `published_by_user_id` per §6.8 with the financial record itself retained per §6.8.5 row #4.

### 34.16.2 SKU 2: Verification Tiers

**What:** Platform-owned verification of sellers across three tiers: **Basic** (self-attested KYB + email verification), **Verified** (domain + business registration + uptime history), **Certified** (full compliance audit — SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, etc.).

**Pricing:** **$0 to the seller, always.** Verification is a platform-integrity investment, not a revenue SKU. Sellers earn tiers; they do not purchase them.

**Why charge $0:** MS §2.10 articulates the principle: "a verification tier paid for by the seller has no credibility with buyers." Charging sellers creates an incentive for Sourcera to rubber-stamp verifications, which destroys the trust signal. The cost of verification is absorbed by the platform and recovered implicitly through `rev_subscription` (Growth+ plans) and `rev_ai_wallet`.

**Mechanic:**
1. Seller requests verification via Seller Console → Profile → Request Verification.
2. `VerificationReviewRecord` is created with `status=requested` (§4.4.21).
3. Editorial reviewer (platform Ops) performs the tier-specific review; on approval, `status=approved` and the seller's `verification_tier` is elevated.
4. `verification_fetch` (§34.14.1 capability #4) runs platform-internally to pull public documents; the seller does NOT pay for the fetches.
5. Verified document-expiry re-review is triggered from `VerificationReviewRecord.expires_at` per §4.4.21. Certified recurring re-review follows §44.1 `Verification certified re-review cadence`; §34.16.2 does not restate the cadence value.

**Ledger:** Verification activity creates NO entry in MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord (amount_cents=0 is not persisted). The verification cost is captured on the Sourcera P&L under operating expenses (COGS: editorial labor + `verification_fetch` cost_center=sourcera_owned charges), not revenue.

**Anti-Gaming:** A seller who attempts to purchase verification from a third-party service and then claim a Sourcera tier without undergoing the Sourcera review is flagged per §3.5 anti-spam and is downgraded to Basic (or lower). Buyers are alerted via `verification_tier_revoked` webhook (Appendix C new event).

**Plan Gating:** Per §34.1.2 Verification Tier Cap and SPS v3 §13.2, Basic is available on Seller Free, Verified eligibility begins at Seller Solo and remains available on Seller Starter+, and Certified eligibility begins at Seller Growth and remains available on Seller Scale / Seller Enterprise. Verification remains free to the seller at every eligible tier; plan-tier-ineligible requests are rejected with `verification_review_plan_tier_insufficient` per §4.4.21 and Appendix I. D-PXC-010 continues to track the separate criteria-reconciliation question for what evidence earns each tier.

#### 34.16.2.A Verification Review Eligibility Constants

This table is the authoritative home for VerificationReviewRecord eligibility thresholds. §4.4.21, §39, Appendix I, Appendix J, and Appendix K MUST cite these cells rather than restating values inline.

| Cell | Value | Applies To | Governance |
| ----- | -----:| ----- | ----- |
| `verification_verified_profile_completeness_pct_required` | 100.00 | `VerificationReviewRecord.profile_completeness_snapshot_pct` threshold for Verified requests | Product + Trust sign-off |
| `verification_certified_closed_bid_count_required` | 3 | `VerificationReviewRecord.closed_bid_count_snapshot` threshold for Certified requests | Product + Marketplace Ops sign-off |
| `verification_certified_buyer_confirmed_bid_count_required` | 3 | `VerificationReviewRecord.buyer_confirmed_bid_count_snapshot` threshold for Certified requests | Product + Marketplace Ops sign-off |
| `verification_certified_kb_health_floor_default` | 70.00 | `VerificationReviewRecord.kb_health_score_snapshot` floor for Certified requests | Product + Trust sign-off |

**Entity:** `VerificationReviewRecord` (§4.4.21, already defined pre-v7.0.0 rewrite).

### 34.16.3 SKU 3: Featured Placements

**What:** Top-of-marketplace-home editorial feature of a single seller for a specified period (e.g., "Vendor of the Month"), rendered prominently on the buyer home and Discovery pages.

**Pricing Model (default, v7.0.0):** **Editorial only — no paid commitment.** Sellers do NOT pay for featured placements in the v7.0.0 release. Placements are selected by Sourcera's Marketing + Editorial team based on quality signals (Verification Tier=Certified, outcome metrics, buyer feedback, KB Value Meter per §34.19, launch recency, etc.).

**Paid Mode (feature-flag gated, future-release):** The spec reserves a `paid_commitment` mode in which a seller MAY pay a monthly retainer for a guaranteed featured placement. This mode is **feature-flagged off by default in v7.0.0** and gated behind `FeaturedPlacement.mode="paid_commitment"` + org-level feature flag `featured_placement_paid_mode_enabled=true`. Enablement requires:
1. VP Marketing + VP Finance + VP Legal sign-off on the retainer pricing.
2. Clear disclosure to buyers that the featured placement is sponsored (FTC 16 CFR 255.5).
3. A cap of 1 paid commitment per category per month (hard cap) to prevent saturation.
4. An ethical review to ensure paid commitments do not bias Sourcera's outcome-data surfaces (e.g., KB Value Meter, buyer satisfaction metrics).

**Until paid mode is enabled:** All FeaturedPlacement rows are `mode="editorial"` and generate NO revenue.

**Entity:** `FeaturedPlacement` (§4.4.20, already defined pre-v7.0.0 rewrite).

**Flag:** Paid mode is **Authored Extension — Deferred.** Tracked in `RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions → §34.16.3 FeaturedPlacement.paid_commitment`.

### 34.16.4 Buyer Guardrails and Transparency

Marketplace discovery surfaces MUST maintain buyer trust. The following guardrails are mandatory:

1. **Labeling.** Every paid surface (Promoted, future Paid Featured) displays a non-suppressible "Sponsored" or "Promoted" badge meeting FTC 16 CFR 255.5 disclosure standards.
2. **Separation of paid from organic.** Search and ranking algorithms MUST NOT factor in `PromotedListing` bid amounts into organic-result ranking. Paid slots are visually and algorithmically separated; the canonical `quality_floor` is the full §4.4.19 Eligibility Gate (plan-tier eligibility, claim verification, published/pending SoftwarePage, KB Health floor, closed-bid snapshot, active category, category cap, monthly allotment/top-up limits, and Vendor Opt-Out coverage) plus the anti-spam checks in §27.11.6. Sellers failing any gate are blocked from promoted bidding.
3. **Buyer opt-out.** Buyers MAY filter out all promoted and featured listings from search results via Buyer Console → Settings → Display Preferences → "Hide Sponsored" (session-only toggle; not persisted by default to preserve Sourcera's disclosure obligation).
4. **k=5 anonymization.** Per §34.16.1, auction metrics are only surfaced to sellers when ≥5 distinct bidders participate.
5. **No retargeting without consent.** Promoted and featured click-stream data MUST NOT be sold or shared with third-party ad networks; buyer click-behavior data is sourcera_owned for platform analytics only.

### 34.16.5 Failure Modes

1. **Promoted listing auction has a runaway bid.** Resolved: max-bid sanity check governed by §39 `PromotedListing.max_bid_cents (system cap)`; deploy-time enforced; no per-category override exists in v7.1.1. Excess bids are rejected with HTTP 400 `promoted_listing_bid_above_max`; no bid row, auction run, or MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord is written, and the seller is notified with the rejected value and active cap.
2. **Seller wins promoted auction then goes insolvent before settlement.** Resolved: invoice collection per §34.2.4; unpaid `PromotedListing` rows transition to `status=unpaid` and the promoted slot is backfilled from the #2 bidder (if their bid is still ≥ floor) or goes unfilled for the week.
3. **Verification reviewer erroneously approves a seller who should not be Certified.** Resolved: dual-reviewer sign-off for Certified tier (§4.4.21); post-hoc audit follows §44.1 `Verification certified re-review cadence`; erroneous grants trigger `verification_tier_revoked` + buyer notification.
4. **Featured placement creates a conflict of interest (paid seller has poor outcomes).** Resolved: editorial oversight per §34.16.3; paid mode disabled by default; ethical review gate at enablement.
5. **Multiple sellers request the same category featured placement.** Resolved: editorial team selects one; non-selected sellers are notified with criteria used. If paid mode is enabled, second-price auction applies per §34.16.1.
6. **Buyer fatigue on promoted listings (ad blindness).** Resolved: PostHog dashboard `marketplace_promoted_click_through_rate`; if CTR < 1% sustained over 4 weeks in a category, Ops Marketing reviews whether to pause promotions in that category until buyer fatigue recovers.
7. **Cross-border currency exposure on promoted bids.** Resolved: all bids MUST be in USD; non-USD sellers convert at daily Stripe FX rate at bid-submission time; conversion losses are borne by the seller.

### 34.16.6 Retention, Residency, and DSAR

| `PromotedListing` | 7 years (financial) | Origin Org's residency | Pseudonymize `created_by`, `updated_by`; retain financial record per §45.1 |
| `FeaturedPlacement` | 7 years (financial + editorial audit) | Origin Org's residency | Same |
| `VerificationReviewRecord` | 7 years (financial + platform-integrity) | Origin Org's residency | Pseudonymize reviewer PII; retain decision record per §45.1 |
| `MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord` (AE) | 7 years (financial) | Origin Org's residency | Same |

### 34.16.7 Webhooks and API Surfaces

**Transport semantics (shared across all 18 marketplace-discovery events).** All events in this subsection inherit the §31.1–§31.6 transport contract: HMAC-SHA256 signed with the per-Org webhook secret; `event_id` in the §31.1 canonical format `evt_{unix_ms}_{base32_random10}` (idempotency key); `event_type` dotted namespace; `occurred_at` ISO 8601 with microsecond precision; `delivery_attempt` counter; payload ≤256 KB; Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve; DLQ after 5 failures; consumer 4xx responses do NOT retry. Signature verification failures at the consumer do NOT trigger Sourcera-side retry (§31.8 Acceptance #13 parallel). Every event MUST emit a parallel PostHog event with `.` → `_` transliteration per §31.8 Acceptance #16 (e.g., `promoted_listing.auction_settled` → PostHog `promoted_listing_auction_settled`). Every event is registered in Appendix C (Notification Event Catalog) with severity and user-visible-vs-ops-only classification, and in Appendix J under `webhook_event_class=marketplace_discovery_domain` (new enum value — Appendix J extension).

**Delivery scope.** Marketplace-discovery webhooks are deliverable across the full §34.1 plan-tier set (Free / Starter / Growth / Scale / Enterprise per §34.1.1 cell **Webhook Endpoints**) per §31.5. Events tagged "Ops-only" in the table below MUST NOT be exposed to customer-visible webhook subscriptions — they are delivered to the internal Ops webhook endpoint only and do NOT appear in the `GET /v1/webhook-subscriptions/available-events` catalog for customer Orgs.

**Idempotency semantics.** All 18 events inherit §31.3 `event_id`-keyed idempotency: replay of the same `event_id` MUST be a no-op at the consumer (HTTP 200 with replay header). Consumer deduplication window is 7 days per §31.3. `promoted_listing.auction_settled` and `promoted_listing.auction_lost` MUST fire AT MOST ONCE per `(auction_id, recipient_org_id, event_type)` tuple, and every participating bidder Org receives exactly one terminal settlement outcome event (`auction_settled` for winners, `auction_lost` for non-winners). Settlement-retry scenarios MUST NOT emit duplicates. `promoted_listing.digest_published` MUST fire AT MOST ONCE per `(category_id, window_start, window_end)` tuple.

**Audience privacy.** Customer-visible marketplace-discovery webhooks MUST satisfy one of three payload-audience rules: (1) recipient-owned row only; (2) k-anonymized aggregate with an explicit k=5 floor per §34.16.1 / §27.11.2; or (3) Ops-only. `promoted_listing.auction_settled` is recipient-owned only and MUST NOT include a multi-winner array. `promoted_listing.auction_lost` MUST NOT include winner `org_id`, winner `paid_cents`, or any winner-owned `promoted_listing_id`. Appendix M.5 gate `webhook_payload_k_anonymity_floor` asserts this contract at PR-lint and deploy-validator time.

**Correlation.** `promoted_listing.auction_settled` winner-self payloads each correlate to one subsequent `promoted_listing.paid` event (on Stripe settlement) via the recipient's own `promoted_listing_id`. Subscribers performing revenue reconstruction MUST join on `promoted_listing_id` only for recipient-owned rows. `promoted_listing.auction_lost` has no revenue correlation and MUST NOT expose competitor settlement identity or clearing-price data. `marketplace_discovery.monthly_revenue_posted.sku_breakdown` MUST reconcile to the sum of `promoted_listing.paid.amount_cents` events for the period (QA invariant `marketplace_revenue_reconciliation`).

New error codes (registered in Appendix I per `RECONCILIATION.md → Error Code Additions`):

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| `promoted_listing_plan_tier_below_scale` | 403 | Seller plan tier is not Seller Scale or Seller Enterprise per §34.1.2 / §4.4.19 |
| `promoted_listing_category_locked` | 409 | Seller already has the maximum allowed promoted listings this month |
| `promoted_listing_bid_below_floor` | 400 | Bid amount below §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_base_rate_cents_per_category_week` |
| `promoted_listing_bid_above_max` | 400 | Bid amount above §39 `PromotedListing.max_bid_cents (system cap)` |
| `promoted_listing_quality_floor_failed` | 403 | Seller fails the §4.4.19 Eligibility Gate or §27.11.6 anti-spam quality-floor checks |
| `promoted_listing_auction_closed` | 409 | Bid submitted at or after the Monday 00:00:00.000 UTC close instant (close is exclusive per §34.16.1 #1 — D-V6-006 remediation 2026-05-06) |
| `promoted_listing_duplicate_bid_per_window` | 409 | Seller has already submitted a bid for this category in the current weekly auction window (D-V6-007 remediation 2026-05-06) |
| `featured_placement_paid_mode_not_enabled` | 403 | Attempted to book paid featured placement when `featured_placement_paid_mode_enabled=false` |
| `verification_tier_already_granted` | 409 | Seller already holds the requested tier |
| `verification_recertification_required` | 403 | Tier expired; must re-request |

### 34.16.8 Acceptance Criteria

1. The three revenue streams (`rev_ai_wallet`, `rev_subscription`, `rev_marketplace_discovery`) MUST be enforced in the Billing Ledger (§4.8.3); zero rows with `revenue_stream_class=null` OR cross-stream attribution are tolerated; deploy-time validator `revenue_stream_firewall` asserts.
2. Promoted Listing auction MUST execute a correct second-price settlement: winner pays the second-highest bid; deterministic ordering tuple is `(bid_cents DESC, bid_submitted_at ASC, seller_org_id ASC)` per §34.16.1 #3 (D-V6-002 / D-V6-003 remediation 2026-05-06); single-bidder categories pay the §34.16.1.A reserve; bid window closes Monday 00:00:00.000 UTC exclusive (D-V6-006); each seller MAY submit at most one bid per category per weekly window (D-V6-007). QA test `promoted_listing_second_price_auction` asserts the ordering tuple, including a microsecond-collision fixture and a duplicate-bid-rejection fixture.
3. Promoted Listing per-category cap MUST be enforced at bid-submission time per §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_category_slot_cap`; bids above the cap are clamped to unfilled slots and NOT billed.
4. Promoted Listing plan-tier eligibility MUST be enforced at bid-submission time: Seller Scale or Seller Enterprise per §34.1.2 Promoted Marketplace Placements; ineligible Orgs return HTTP 403 `promoted_listing_plan_tier_below_scale`.
5. Promoted Listing quality-floor enforcement MUST be source-identical across §34.16.4 narrative, the §34.16.7 `promoted_listing_quality_floor_failed` error row, §27.11.6 guardrails, and the §4.4.19 Eligibility Gate. Deploy-time validator `promoted_listing_quality_floor_canonical_parity` asserts the §34 surfaces cite the full §4.4.19 gate instead of a partial restatement.
6. Promoted Listing seller monthly cap MUST be enforced as the plan-included allotment defined in §34.1.2 **Promoted Marketplace Placements** plus §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_purchased_top_up_hard_cap_per_month`. Monthly over-cap bids return HTTP 409 `promoted_listing_category_locked`; purchased-top-up exhaustion returns `promoted_listing_monthly_top_up_cap_exceeded` per Appendix I.
7. Verification Tier elevations MUST create zero MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord rows (amount_cents would be 0); QA test `verification_tier_zero_revenue` asserts.
8. Featured Placements with `mode=editorial` MUST create zero revenue rows; `mode=paid_commitment` rows require `featured_placement_paid_mode_enabled=true` at the Org level; QA test `featured_placement_paid_mode_gate` asserts.
9. Anonymization threshold k=5 MUST be enforced on the weekly auction digest; digests with <5 distinct bidders return empty `{metrics: null, reason: "anonymization_threshold_breach"}`; QA test `promoted_listing_k5_anonymization` asserts.
10. All marketplace discovery webhooks MUST follow §31 patterns (HMAC-SHA256, idempotency_key = event_id, exponential backoff, DLQ after 5, ≤256 KB payloads); webhook conformance test `marketplace_discovery_webhook_conformance` asserts.
11. Marketplace Discovery webhook payloads MUST enforce recipient self-only or k=5 aggregate disclosure. `promoted_listing.auction_settled` emits one recipient-owned winner row to each winner; non-winners receive `promoted_listing.auction_lost` with no winner identity, winner paid amount, or winner-owned `promoted_listing_id`; QA test `promoted_listing_auction_webhook_audience_privacy` and deploy-time validator `webhook_payload_k_anonymity_floor` assert.

### 34.17.2 Delivery Tracks

The MS §2.11 baseline and AE requirements fall across three delivery phases, gated at v7.0.0, v7.1.0, and v7.2.0 respectively.

**Phase 1 (v7.0.0 launch) — MS baseline:** MS items 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12; AE items AE-1, AE-9, AE-10, AE-11, AE-14, AE-15, AE-16. Foundational plumbing for outcome-based billing and Solo pricing-surface integrity; without these, no wallet draw or Solo engine/surface split can operate safely.

**Phase 1 (v7.0.0 launch) — UX subset:** MS item 14 partial — inline-citation UI, KB-gap detector, stake-reveal screen, contextual upgrade CTAs.

**Phase 2 (v7.1.0, 30 days post-launch):** MS items 8, 11, 13; MS item 14 remainder (outcome debrief surface); AE items AE-2, AE-3, AE-6, AE-7, AE-8, AE-12, AE-13, AE-17, AE-18. Ops-tooling, marketplace-discovery activation, Pro Trial Seat, seller SSO orchestrator, Solo billing surface, Solo charge orchestration, and Seller Solo trust / retention surfaces.

**Phase 3 (v7.2.0, 60 days post-launch):** AE items AE-4, AE-5. First-enterprise-customer-driven; lead-time enables real-world calibration.

### 34.17.3 Cross-Requirement Invariants

1. **AE-1 (cost telemetry) is a precondition for MS #3 (nightly cost_base recalc).** Deploy that breaks AE-1 also breaks MS #3; deploy-gate `cost_telemetry_coverage` asserts ≥99.9% of AIOperations have `actual_cost_cents` within 24 hours.
2. **AE-10 (rate card version manager) is a precondition for MS #12 (public rate card publisher).** A `PricingTableVersion` MUST exist before the publisher can serve anything; deploy-gate `pricing_table_version_present` asserts.

4. **MS #2 (Outcome Resolver) depends on AE-10 (rate card versioning) and AE-9 (Free Allowance counters).** Outcome evaluation reads the rate card and the free allowance before computing the wallet draw.
5. **MS #4 (spend cap hard block) and MS #5 (budget notifications) are coupled.** A Deploy that ships #4 without #5 is rejected — sellers/buyers must receive threshold warnings BEFORE the hard block fires. Deploy-gate `budget_notification_precedes_hard_block` asserts.
6. **MS #8 (downgrade-safe 90-day preservation) and AE-4 (upgrade carry-over) are symmetric.** Downgrade and upgrade paths MUST preserve the same protected-asset set (KB entries, in-flight bids, Capability Declarations, Firecrawl source configs, in-flight evaluations). Symmetry test `carry_over_symmetry_check` asserts at deploy.
7. **MS #12 (public rate card) canonical_id lock.** Rate-card publisher MUST NOT emit `buyer_` or `seller_` prefixes on `capability_id`; canonical form per §32.8.1 and Appendix J. Deploy-gate `canonical_capability_id_lock` asserts.
8. **MS #14 (UX surfaces) requires AE-2 and MS #9.** Contextual upgrade CTAs reference entitlement state (MS #9 audit log) and billing state (wallet draws); without these the CTA cannot render accurate copy.
9. **AE-12 through AE-18 are Solo pricing-surface coverage rows.** Removing any row from §34.17.1.b while the referenced Solo behavior remains active in §34.1 / §34.2.5 / §44.6 / §13.11 / §27.11.3 is a coverage regression. Deploy-gate `pricing_engineering_coverage` asserts the contiguous AE id set through AE-18 and fails on gaps.

## 34.18 Financial Targets {#34.18-financial-targets}

This section is the authoritative financial-target specification. It reconciles the hard 88% blended-margin floor (§34.3.3) with the MS §2.12 aspirational 90% target, enumerates the revenue-stream targets, and publishes the year-1 exit plan mix.

### 34.18.1 Margin Floor Table

| Metric | Target | Enforcement | Source | Flag |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| `rev_ai_wallet` blended gross margin | ≥ 88% | **Hard floor** — enforced at price-update time; cost-base recalcs that would breach this floor are BLOCKED until Ops Finance approves (§34.3.3); deploy-time validator `margin_floor_88_percent` | §34.3.3; §4.8.6 | Authoritative |
| `rev_ai_wallet` blended gross margin (aspirational) | ≥ 90% | **Soft target** — operational goal; margin < 90% does not block price publishes but triggers a weekly Ops Finance review | MS §2.12 | **Authored Extension — aspirational, non-enforced** |
| `rev_subscription` blended gross margin | ≥ 75% | **Soft target** — plan tiers are priced for margin cushion; monitored on the Finance scorecard | SPS §11; BPS §11 | Authoritative |
| `rev_marketplace_discovery` blended gross margin | ≥ 85% | **Soft target** — marketplace discovery has lower infra cost than AI; CSS labor cost on verification review is the main drag | §34.16; MS §2.12 | Authoritative |
| **Combined blended gross margin** (across all three streams, weighted by revenue) | ≥ 90% | **Aspirational target** — reported monthly; shortfalls trigger quarterly business review | MS §2.12 | **Authored Extension — aspirational, non-enforced** |
| Year-1 Enterprise-plan revenue mix | < 10% (buyer side) AND < 10% (seller side) | **Soft target** — heavy Enterprise concentration risks undifferentiated marketplace; Sales targets the exit mix below | MS §2.12 | Authoritative |

### 34.18.2 88% vs 90% Reconciliation (Authored Extension)

MS §2.12 names 90% as the target; §34.3.3 names 88% as a hard floor. This is NOT a conflict — it is a ceiling / floor distinction that was not clearly articulated in either source document:

- **88%** is the **hard enforcement floor** on `rev_ai_wallet` margin. A cost-base recalc that would produce a margin below 88% is blocked — the system refuses to publish the new pricing until Ops Finance explicitly overrides. 88% is a survival threshold; breaching it for any sustained period triggers existential concern about pricing-model viability.
- **90%** is the **aspirational operating target**. It is not enforced by code; it is reported on the Finance scorecard and reviewed quarterly. The delta between 88% and 90% is the operational buffer: when infra costs drift up, when cost-base recalcs undercompensate, when a new capability launches at a sub-optimal margin, the buffer absorbs the difference without triggering enforcement.

**Reconciliation rule.** When both are referenced in the spec, the 88% floor is what the system enforces; the 90% target is what the team manages toward. If a source document (MS, BPS, SPS) cites only 90%, readers should interpret it as the aspirational target, not the enforcement threshold. If a source document cites 88%, it is the hard floor.

This distinction is **Authored Extension**; tracked in `RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions → §34.18.2 88%/90% Margin Reconciliation`.

### 34.18.6 Scenario Analysis

The MS §2.12 top-down ARR scenarios remain authoritative as **Scenarios MS-A / MS-B / MS-C**. BPS v3 §13 and SPS v3 §14 add two v3 Solo cohort scenarios, which are authoritative as cohort economics inputs rather than company-wide ARR targets. This section adopts those companion inputs under disambiguated names (**BPS-D** and **SPS-D**) so implementation does not depend on overloaded Scenario A/B/C/D labels. The broader scenario-letter collision remains tracked by D-PXC-016.

- **Scenario MS-A (aggressive).** Year-1 ARR = $12M; blended margin = 91%; Enterprise mix < 5%. Drivers: strong `rev_ai_wallet` capture (60%) and virality via §13 growth loops.
- **Scenario MS-B (base).** Year-1 ARR = $6M; blended margin = 89%; Enterprise mix = 8%. Drivers: plan-upgrade path + moderate marketplace discovery adoption.
- **Scenario MS-C (conservative).** Year-1 ARR = $2.5M; blended margin = 87%; Enterprise mix = 12%. Drivers: slow activation + Enterprise concentration; triggers §34.3.3 margin-floor review.
- **Scenario BPS-D (Buyer Solo cohort; Authored Extension — requires human sign-off).** Year-1 Buyer Solo cohort revenue = $276,800; gross margin = ~92.0%; source BPS v3 §13. Decomposition: 200 Solo subscribers × $49 × 12 = $117,600; 800 Solo per-evaluation transactions × $199 = $159,200; AI COGS = $1,728 (subscription $1,296 + per-evaluation $432); Stripe processing ≈ $9,000; infra ≈ $3,500; refund reserve = $7,960; total direct cost ≈ $22,188. No CSM load; low-touch support only.
- **Scenario SPS-D (Seller Solo cohort; Authored Extension — requires human sign-off).** Year-1 Seller Solo cohort revenue = $415,200; gross margin = ~90.4%; source SPS v3 §14. Decomposition: 300 Solo subscribers × $49 × 12 = $176,400; 1,200 Solo per-bid transactions × $199 = $238,800; AI COGS = $2,592 (subscription $1,944 + per-bid $648); Stripe processing ≈ $13,500; Verified-tier Ops review ≈ $6,480; infra ≈ $5,200; refund reserve = $11,940; total direct cost ≈ $39,712. No CSM load; low-touch email support plus modest Verified-tier Ops review cost.

**Authored Extension status.** Scenarios BPS-D and SPS-D are registered under AE-V72REM-SCENARIO-D-01. They do not replace Scenarios MS-A / MS-B / MS-C, do not alter Scenario MS-C's 88% floor interaction, and do not close the broader D-PXC-016 scenario-letter hygiene item.

**88% floor interaction with Scenario MS-C — floor asymmetry lock.** Scenario MS-C's blended margin of 87% is BELOW the 88% hard floor. The floor and the scenario measure two different things and MUST NOT be conflated:

- **Pricing-publish floor (publish-path enforcement).** The 88% floor is enforced on the cost-base-recalc and rate-card-publish path. A recalc that would produce a projected blended margin < 88% at current volume is BLOCKED by the `margin_floor_88_percent` deploy-time validator; pricing-publish API returns HTTP 423 until Ops Finance explicitly unblocks. This is a prospective check: "Would publishing this new rate card produce < 88% at the next billing period?"
- **Realized-margin alert (observation-path telemetry).** Scenario C is a realized-outcome scenario: customer behavior produced an actual blended margin of 87% despite a rate card that was approved at ≥ 88%. Realized drift below the floor fires `margin_floor_breach_hard` on monthly close (§34.18.7 AC #2) but does NOT retroactively revert the published rate card. Rate cards already in effect continue to be honored for every outstanding OutcomeContract; the floor-breach alert drives Ops Finance review, not automatic republish.

**Override asymmetry rule.** No pricing publish MAY set margin < 88%. A realized margin < 88% due to volume / mix drift triggers Ops Finance's Scenario MS-C playbook — (i) freeze prospective rate-card publishes that would worsen projected margin, (ii) evaluate cost reductions (infra optimization, model-tier rebalancing), (iii) consider selective rate-card increases on commodity capabilities at the NEXT recalc window (which still cannot publish below 88%), and (iv) escalate to the 88% floor renegotiation process (VP Finance + CEO approval required — this is the ONLY path to a sub-88% publish, and even then it requires a formal documented exception recorded in `rate_card_exception_log`).

**Invariant.** The publish-path floor is absolute; the observation-path alert is advisory. Deploy-time validator `margin_floor_publish_vs_observation_asymmetry` asserts the two enforcement pathways do not collapse into each other: publish-path floor never allows < 88% without VP Finance + CEO documented exception; observation-path alert never blocks OutcomeContract settlement on an already-published rate card.

### 34.18.7 Acceptance Criteria

1. The monthly Finance scorecard MUST run on the 5th business day of each month; cron at 08:00 UTC; missed runs alert Ops within 1 hour.
2. `rev_ai_wallet` blended margin below 88% MUST trigger `margin_floor_breach_hard` alert within 1 hour of monthly close; pricing-publish API returns HTTP 423 locked until Ops Finance explicitly unblocks.
3. Cost-base recalcs that would produce margin < 88% MUST be blocked at §4.8.6 recalc time; QA test `cost_base_recalc_margin_guard` asserts.
4. The Finance scorecard MUST render revenue-stream composition, plan-mix distribution, and contest approval rate visibly; scorecard template QA test `finance_scorecard_rendered` asserts.
5. Scenario MS-A/MS-B/MS-C references MUST be preserved in Ops Finance operating plans and referenced at every quarterly business review; Scenarios BPS-D and SPS-D MUST be preserved in Solo cohort economics review; documented in `RECONCILIATION.md → Delivery Plan`.

## 34.19 Seller Plan Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee {#34.19-seller-plan-upgrade-carry-over-guarantee}

Sellers upgrading from a lower plan to a higher plan MUST retain full continuity of their historical work, learned models, and earned reputation. No seller-generated value is ever lost on an upgrade. This section enumerates the 13 protected asset classes, the KB Value Meter formula (the canonical seller-reputation signal), transition-specific behaviors, honest-portability microcopy requirements, and the interaction with export/DSAR.

| 2 | KB Value Meter score and direct KB compounding inputs | Seller Org | 100% retained; recomputed per §34.19.2 | §34.19.1.A distinguishes the stored scalar from KBEntry confidence / status / win-rate inputs | AE (formula from SPS §8, MS §2.9) |
| 3 | Capability Declarations and suggestion queue | Seller Org | 100% retained | §34.19.1.A distinguishes published declarations from CapabilityDeclarationSuggestion rows | SPS §11 |
| 4 | Verification Tier | Seller Org | 100% retained | Tier grants earned, not plan-dependent | §34.16.2 |
| 5 | Bid Workspace history | Seller Org | 100% retained | Historical RFPs, responses, outcome attributions | SPS §11 |
| 6 | Outcome-signal history and citation graph | Seller Org | 100% retained | §34.19.1.A distinguishes per-AIOperation outcome history from KBCitationGraphEdge rows | §34.15 |
| 7 | Saved searches and alerts | Seller Org | 100% retained | Backed by SavedSearch (§4.4.35) and SearchAlert (§4.4.36); may be throttled if new plan has lower frequency caps; data preserved | SPS §11 |
| 8 | Promoted Listing history | Seller Org | 100% retained (audit record) | Financial history; not reinstatable | §34.16.1 |

| 11 | Wallet balance | Seller Org | 100% retained; deducted per outcome semantics | Wallet is Org-scoped, plan-independent | §4.8.3; §34.10 |

The two harnesses MUST share the same fixture factory and MUST fail if a sub-class appears in one harness without an explicit include/exclude note in this table.

### 34.19.2 KB Value Meter Formula

The KB Value Meter is the canonical seller-reputation signal, published to buyers on Verified+ sellers and factored into Promoted Listing ranking quality floors (§34.16.1). It is Org-scoped, recomputed nightly, and MUST be preserved verbatim across any plan transition.

**Formula:**

```
KB_Value_Meter = 0.40 × win_rate
               + 0.25 × recency
               + 0.20 × citation_depth
               + 0.15 × outcome_cite_coverage
```

**Component definitions:**

| Component | Definition | Computation | Weight |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| `win_rate` | Percentage of RFPs the seller won within the last 90 days, weighted by RFP value | `SUM(value_of_won_rfps_last_90d) / SUM(value_of_all_completed_rfps_last_90d)` | 40% |
| `recency` | KB freshness signal | `MAX(0, 1 − days_since_last_publish / 365)` | 25% |
| `citation_depth` | Average # of KB citations per RFP response | `AVG(citation_count_per_response_last_90d) / 10` (capped at 1.0) | 20% |
| `outcome_cite_coverage` | Fraction of won RFPs whose responses cite ≥ 1 KB entry | `COUNT(won_rfps_with_kb_citation) / COUNT(won_rfps_last_90d)` | 15% |

**Output range:** 0.00 to 1.00 (continuous scalar). Surfaced to buyers rounded to 2 decimal places.

**Computation cadence:** nightly at 03:30 UTC; recomputation lag ≤ 15 minutes on the day a seller's plan changes (immediate re-trigger to reflect any plan-gated data access changes).

**Authored Extension:** the weights (0.40 / 0.25 / 0.20 / 0.15) and the component definitions are derived from SPS §8 / MS §2.9. The specific normalizations (e.g., `/10` capping for citation_depth, `/365` decay for recency) are **Authored Extensions** — the source documents describe components conceptually but do not give precise normalizations. Flagged in `RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions → §34.19.2 KB Value Meter Normalizations`.

**Portability:** the KB Value Meter is stored on `Organization.kb_value_meter_score` (§4.2.1, ratified by AE-V72REM-PH5P53-DM-01) and is preserved exactly across any plan upgrade or downgrade. Because the score is computed from underlying asset classes (KB entries, outcome history, etc.) which are themselves preserved per §34.19.1, the score NEVER degrades due to a plan change alone. A score decline can only come from real-world changes (seller stops responding, wins fewer RFPs, KB goes stale).
