### 34.19.3.A Per-Eval / Per-Bid Mid-Flight Handling at Plan-Transition Boundary (Phase 7 V7 D-V7-004 Remediation, 2026-05-07)

Solo on Buyer Console operates in subscription ($49/mo) OR per-evaluation ($199 per Selection Report PDF export) mode per §34.2.5. Solo on Seller Console operates in subscription ($49/mo) OR per-bid ($199 per submitted bid) mode. When a Solo Org with an in-flight per-eval Workspace or per-bid Bid Workspace transitions plan tier (any of the above transitions), the in-flight charge resolution follows this rule:

| Edge case | Resolution |
| :---- | :---- |
| Solo per-eval Workspace created at `T - 6h` before plan-rollover boundary; Selection Report PDF export attempted at `T + 6h` (post-rollover) | The Stripe per-eval charge gating uses the **plan-tier captured at Workspace creation time** (NOT at PDF export time), with a **24-hour grace window** beyond the rollover boundary. If `now < (workspace.created_at + 24h grace)` AND PDF export trigger fires within grace, the Solo per-eval $199 charge captures normally; the captured plan-tier on the Workspace row governs. Beyond the 24h grace, the Workspace transitions to the new plan-tier's behavior (no per-eval charge for Free; subscription Wallet for Starter+). |
| Solo per-bid Bid Workspace created at `T - 12h`; bid submission triggered at `T + 12h` (post-rollover) | Same rule as above. The plan-tier captured at Bid Workspace creation governs the per-bid $199 charge for 24h post-rollover; beyond that, the new plan-tier's behavior applies. |
| Customer abandons mid-eval (Workspace `solo_per_eval_charge_pending`) and downgrades to Free before retry | Workspace transitions to read-only preservation per §34.6.3.A Class-1 carve-out (Workspaces are Class-5 per §34.19.1, not Class-1, so standard §34.6 90-day preservation applies; KB entries within the Workspace remain Class-1 protected). The pending $199 charge is voided; no charge captures. |
| Customer abandons mid-bid (Bid Workspace `solo_per_bid_charge_pending`) and upgrades to Starter+ | The pending $199 per-bid charge is voided; on Bid submission post-upgrade, no per-bid charge captures (subscription mode active). The customer's Wallet (Starter+) absorbs the AIOperations per §34.10. |
| Solo subscription cancellation in-cycle | Subscription remains active through `current_period_ends_at`; per-eval / per-bid mode does NOT activate during the active-subscription window. Cancellation orchestration treats the cancellation as effective at the billing-rollover boundary. |

The `solo_per_eval_charge_pending` and `solo_per_bid_charge_pending` Workspace / Bid Workspace states (introduced in §44.6.7 #7 / #8) are extended in §34.19.3.A to carry a `plan_tier_captured_at_creation` field (Authored Extension — Phase 7 V7 D-V7-004) that drives the gating decision above. Stripe charge attempts query this field via the §4.8.1 AIOperation `org_id.plan_tier` resolution path; the Stripe Subscription customer-id remains stable throughout the transition. Loops.so emits a customer notification confirming the per-eval / per-bid behavior at the plan transition.

**Updated §34.19.7 AC #1.** The `plan_upgrade_13_asset_preservation` deploy-time test runs the **full Solo-inclusive matrix** of upgrade and downgrade transitions (24+ transitions including all Solo↔X paths) and asserts data integrity. The matrix is Solo-row inclusive per Phase 7 V7 D-V7-004.

### 34.19.4 Honest-Portability Microcopy

When a seller upgrades, the confirmation UI MUST render microcopy that clearly states what is preserved, what is newly unlocked, and (where applicable) what remains restricted. Generic "Upgraded!" success copy is prohibited. Required elements:

1. Explicit list of newly unlocked capabilities and features (e.g., "You can now bid on promoted listings").
2. Explicit statement that all prior work is preserved ("Your KB, Bid Workspaces, and KB Value Meter stay with you").
3. Explicit reference to any plan-capped areas that remain (e.g., "Your wallet overage ceiling is now $5,000 — raise this anytime in Settings").
4. Link to the plan comparison page (§5.11) for full detail.

**Downgrade microcopy** MUST be equally honest: "Your data is preserved for 90 days; caps that exceed the new plan go read-only per §34.6. You can re-upgrade any time to restore mutation access." Vague or reassuring-only ("Everything will be fine!") copy is prohibited.

### 34.19.4.A Solo-Bordering Transition Microcopy (Phase 7 V7 D-V7-005 Remediation, 2026-05-07)

When the plan transition crosses the Solo boundary in either direction (Free → Solo, Solo → X, X → Solo for any X ∈ {Free, Starter, Growth, Scale, Enterprise}), the microcopy MUST additionally include the following Solo-specific elements (extending the §34.19.4 baseline 4-element list to 7):

5. **Surface-onset acknowledgement.** When transitioning into Solo (X → Solo), the microcopy MUST state explicitly that the AIWallet widget, the per-capability rate-card link, the per-AIOperation Billing Ledger row breakdown, and the FreeAllowanceCounter inline counter will be **hidden** post-transition (per the §44.6.1 surface hide list). Example: "On Solo, you'll see a single billing line item — no per-AI-operation breakdown, no rate-card calculator, no wallet widget. Your AI engine continues to power your work; only the surface simplifies." When transitioning out of Solo (Solo → X), the microcopy MUST state explicitly that those surfaces will become **visible** post-transition. Example: "Your AI Wallet will appear post-upgrade — see your monthly budget, per-operation billing ledger, and rate-card details that were previously hidden on Solo." This element is required because the §44.6 surface contract is materially different from the standard plan-tier surface contract; surface-onset surprise erodes customer trust in the carry-over guarantee.

6. **Envelope-vs-wallet semantic difference.** When transitioning into Solo (X → Solo), the microcopy MUST state explicitly that the Solo "envelope" is engine-absorbed and customer-invisible per §44.6.3, NOT a customer-facing wallet balance. Example: "Solo doesn't have a customer-facing AI budget — the AI is absorbed into your Solo subscription. You'll never see an overage charge or a wallet running low." When transitioning out of Solo (Solo → X), the microcopy MUST state that the new plan exposes a customer-facing Wallet with monthly budget, overage configuration, and auto-topup options. Example: "Starter includes a monthly $50 AI budget you can see and configure — including optional overage and auto-topup, which were not available on Solo."

7. **Per-eval / per-bid charge-mode change acknowledgement** (when applicable). If the Solo Org is on per-evaluation or per-bid mode (§34.2.5) and the transition changes that mode (e.g., Solo per-eval → Free, where per-eval mode is unavailable), the microcopy MUST state explicitly: "Per-evaluation billing mode is not available on Free — your future evaluations will not incur the $199-per-Selection-Report charge. In-flight evaluations within 24 hours of the transition complete under their captured plan-tier per §34.19.3.A." If the per-eval / per-bid mode is preserved or activated, microcopy MUST cite the captured-plan-tier rule and the 24-hour grace window.

The §34.19.7 AC #4 content-QA test `plan_transition_microcopy_present` is tightened to assert all 7 elements are present on Solo-bordering transitions (Free ↔ Solo, Solo → Starter+, Starter+ → Solo). For non-Solo-bordering transitions, the original 4-element baseline applies. Loops.so email templates and in-app confirmation modals BOTH render the 7-element microcopy verbatim; an automated content-diff CI gate `solo_microcopy_template_parity` (Appendix M.5) asserts no drift between the email and in-app copy.

### 34.19.5 Export and DSAR Interaction

Upgrade carry-over is a plan-level preservation guarantee; it does NOT override DSAR (§6.8) or export (§40.4) rights. If a seller exercises a right-to-erasure request mid-upgrade:

1. The upgrade transaction completes atomically (no partial state).
2. The erasure request is processed after the upgrade completes.
3. The KB Value Meter is recomputed post-erasure; the seller's score MAY drop as a result of erased historical data.
4. The seller is notified that the Meter was recomputed and the before/after values.

Export (§40.4) returns the seller's full historical record including KB Value Meter component-breakdown JSON; portable across plans and exportable at any plan tier (including Free).

### 34.19.6 Failure Modes

1. **Upgrade transaction fails mid-flight.** Resolved: transactional orchestration per §34.5.1; on failure, full rollback + `plan_upgrade_failed` webhook + email to `billing_admin`.
2. **Downgrade creates DowngradeExcessDataBucket that violates Protected Asset guarantees.** Resolved by the **§34.6.3.A Class-1 Protected-Asset Carve-Out** (Phase 7 V7 D-V7-009 remediation, 2026-05-07). Class-1 assets DO hard-archive at `preservation_until` (preserves §34.6.3 cron contract) but enter `status=archived_class_1_protected` per §4.8.10, NOT `status=archived`; cold-storage retention is 10 years (vs 7-year standard); customer-initiated self-service restoration is available throughout a 5-year window (vs 0 days for non-Class-1). The §34.19.1 "100% retained, read-write" commitment is honored via the long self-service restoration window. Deploy-time validator `protected_asset_downgrade_firewall` asserts that every Class-1 asset in any DowngradeExcessDataBucket carries `status=archived_class_1_protected` (not `status=archived`) AND `archive_retention_horizon_years=10` (not 7). The prior wording "no asset in the 13-class list enters `preservation_status=hard_archived`" referenced a phantom field/value combination not present in §4.8.10's `status` enum; that wording is retired in favor of the canonical §4.8.10 enum membership check.
3. **KB Value Meter drops spuriously post-upgrade due to recomputation timing.** Resolved: recomputation is deterministic; if a seller sees a Meter drop within 15 minutes of upgrade, Ops Finance reviews the computation trace. A ≥5% unexplained delta triggers a `kb_value_meter_drift_alert`.
4. **Seller upgrades specifically to gain access to a promoted listings category but finds it already locked (3-per-category cap hit).** Resolved: UX messaging at upgrade confirmation states "Promoted Listings are subject to category-level availability — upgrade does NOT guarantee a slot." Sellers retain bid rights; they may need to wait for the next auction window.
5. **KB citation counts inflate unnaturally (seller spams their own KB to boost KB Value Meter).** Resolved: anti-spam framework per §3.5 monitors citation density; abusive patterns flag the Org for review; KB Value Meter contribution from flagged KB entries is suppressed.
6. **Historical Outcome Contract entries reference a prior plan tier (rate card) that no longer exists post-upgrade.** Resolved: historical AIOperations preserve their `pricing_table_version_id` (§4.8.9); billing reversal on contest uses the historical rate, not the current rate. QA test `outcome_reversal_uses_historical_rate` asserts.
7. **Seller disputes that their KB Value Meter was degraded post-upgrade.** Resolved: component-breakdown surface (in Seller Console → Profile → KB Value Meter) shows the four components, their values, their weights, and a 90-day trend. The trend line persists through upgrades so the seller can visually verify no plan-induced drop.

### 34.19.7 Acceptance Criteria

1. Every row in §34.19.1 and every sub-class in §34.19.1.A MUST be preserved on any upgrade transition; QA test `plan_upgrade_13_asset_preservation` runs a full matrix of upgrade transitions and asserts data integrity.
2. KB Value Meter computation MUST follow the §34.19.2 formula with the documented weights and normalizations; deploy-time unit test `kb_value_meter_formula` asserts.
3. KB Value Meter MUST recompute within 15 minutes of any plan transition; latency test `kb_value_meter_post_upgrade_latency` asserts.
4. Honest-portability microcopy MUST be present on every upgrade and downgrade confirmation UI per §34.19.4; content-QA test `plan_transition_microcopy_present` asserts.
5. Protected-asset downgrade firewall MUST block any of the 13 asset classes from entering hard-archive in a DowngradeExcessDataBucket; deploy-time validator asserts.
6. Export (§40.4) payload MUST include `kb_value_meter` object with component-breakdown at the time of export; export-QA test `export_includes_kb_value_meter` asserts.

## 34.20 Acceptance Criteria {#34.20-acceptance-criteria}

The criteria below are §34-scope (plan / pricing / wallet / entitlement / outcome / cross-side / Pro Trial Seat / Seller Rate Card / Seller Outcome Signals / Marketplace Discovery / Pricing Engineering / Financial Targets / Seller Upgrade Carry-Over). Entity-level acceptance criteria for AIOperation, CapabilityRegistryEntry, AIWallet, OutcomeContract, ContestRecord, CostBaseRecalculationLog, FreeAllowanceCounter, CommittedSpendContract, PricingTableVersion, DowngradeExcessDataBucket, BillingSeatSnapshot, PromotedListing, FeaturedPlacement, VerificationReviewRecord, and MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord live at §4.8.1–§4.8.11 and §4.4.19–§4.4.21 and are NOT restated here.

### 34.20.1 Plan-Tier Definitions and Pricing

1. The §34.1 plan-tier tables MUST be the single source of truth for plan capabilities; §5.11 Feature Access Matrix and §39 Object Size Constraints reference §34.1 cells with `Source: §34.1.x` annotations and never restate values.
2. Every cell in §34.1.1 and §34.1.2 MUST have a `Source` citation back to BPS, SPS, MS, or AE; deploy-time validator asserts no orphan cells.
3. Plan-tier prices in §34.2 MUST match `PricingTableVersion.published_payload_json.plan_tiers` (§4.8.9) at all times; nightly reconciliation job asserts; mismatch triggers `pricing_table_drift_alert` to Ops Finance.
4. The Public Pricing API (`api.sourcera.com/v1/pricing`) MUST publish the latest `PricingTableVersion` with `status=published` and `effective_at ≤ now` (§4.8.9 acceptance criterion #1).
5. Annual contract customers MUST be grandfathered through any breaking-change publish for the remainder of their contract term (§4.8.9; BPS §11; SPS §11).

### 34.20.2 Outcome-Based Pricing

6. The pricing formula `value_price = MAX(min_value, cost_base × 10)` and `cost_price = MAX(min_cost, cost_base × 1.05)` MUST be applied uniformly across all customer-billed capabilities; deploy-time validator asserts.
7. The 88% blended-margin floor MUST be enforced at price-update time; cost-base recalcs that would breach the floor are blocked until Ops Finance approves (§34.3.3; §4.8.6).
8. Cost-base recalculations MUST run nightly at 02:30 UTC; missed run alerts Ops within 1 hour.

### 34.20.3 Wallet and Entitlements

9. Entitlement check MUST be O(1) on the cached session metadata; database round trips for plan-tier or wallet-state lookup during entitlement evaluation are forbidden (§34.8.2).
10. AIWallet MUST be Org-scoped, console-pooled, and never partition pooling by console — except for the §34.10.3 Free+Free and Free+Paid collapse rules (Authored Extensions; Sales-Ops sign-off pending).
11. Wallet overage MUST default to OFF on every plan; admin opt-in is mandatory and audited (§4.8.3 acceptance criterion #4).
12. Auto-topup MUST default to OFF; admin opt-in is mandatory; auto-topup increment is constrained to $50–$10,000 per charge (§4.8.3 acceptance criterion #5).
13. Wallet 50% / 80% / 100% notifications MUST be one-shot per period (idempotency stamps prevent duplicates; §4.8.3 acceptance criterion #6).
14. Free Allowance MUST be exhausted before any wallet draw for `customer_billed` capabilities (§4.8.7 acceptance criterion #2).
15. Soft-gated capabilities MUST surface upgrade CTAs in the result envelope; hard-gated capabilities MUST return HTTP 403 with the upgrade path in the error body (§34.8.1, §34.8.7).
16. Every customer-billed capability with `state=active` in CapabilityRegistryEntry MUST have a row in the §34.8.5 Entitlement Matrix; deploy-time validator asserts.

### 34.20.4 Outcome Resolver and Contests

17. Default-on-timeout MUST be `rejected` for every OutcomeContract unless `requires_explicit_user_signal=true` (§4.8.4 acceptance criterion #5).
18. `auto_accepted` MUST be a distinct settlement state, billed at value price but reported separately for product-quality dashboards.
19. Customers MUST be able to file ContestRecords within 14 days (or per-capability override) of settlement; auto-filing on late `rejected` signals MUST notify Ops Finance within 5 minutes (§4.8.5).
20. Ops Finance contest decisions MUST occur within 5 business days; SLA breach triggers `billing.contest.sla_breach` webhook + Ops alert.
21. Approved contests MUST credit the wallet within 1 business day of approval.

### 34.20.5 Plan Upgrade / Downgrade and Preservation

22. Upgrades MUST be effective immediately (Stripe webhook receipt → entitlement refresh ≤ 30 seconds); proration applied per §34.5.1.
23. Downgrades MUST surface a 14-day warning when current usage exceeds new caps; warning enumerates specific overages with action options per §34.5.3.
24. DowngradeExcessDataBucket creation MUST occur within 5 minutes of effective downgrade (§4.8.10 acceptance criterion #1).
25. Preserved entities MUST remain readable but not mutable for 90 days; restoration on upgrade is atomic per §34.6.2; partial restoration requires explicit user confirmation (§4.8.10 acceptance criterion #4).
26. Cold-storage hard-archive MUST occur within 1 hour of `preservation_until`; cold-storage retention is 7 years; restoration window is 90 days post-archive (§34.6.3; §4.8.10 acceptance criterion #5).

### 34.20.6 Seat Counting (Informational Only)

27. Sourcera MUST NOT charge per seat on any plan; the Public Pricing API MUST NOT expose per-seat pricing (§4.8.11 acceptance criterion #6).
28. `BillingSeatSnapshot.plan_gate_breach_flag` MUST be informational only — no invoicing or feature-access gate on seat count (§4.8.11 acceptance criterion #4).
29. Guests and API-only identities MUST be excluded from `active_seats_count` (§4.8.11 acceptance criterion #3).
30. Monthly snapshots MUST run at 02:00 UTC on the 1st of each month for every active Org (§4.8.11 acceptance criterion #1).

### 34.20.7 Cross-Side Billing

31. AIWallet MUST be Org-scoped (one row per Org); the Dual-Console Firewall MUST NOT partition the wallet (§4.8.3 acceptance criterion #1).
32. Console-scoped business entities (Workspaces, Bid Workspaces, KB entries, Capability Declarations, etc.) MUST NOT cross the firewall regardless of billing state (§7.2; §34.12.4).
33. The `billing_admin` role MUST be the only role permitted to mutate wallet config, file contests, change plan tier, or accept Pro Trial Seat grants on the vendor side; mutations are audit-logged with user attribution.
34. Enterprise + Enterprise Org MUST collapse into one combined contract with one committed spend minimum at the higher floor ($3K/mo) and one dedicated CSM (§34.12.5).

### 34.20.8 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat (M17)

35. Pro Trial Seat allocation (5/mo Scale; 15/mo Enterprise) MUST be enforced at issuance time; over-issuance returns HTTP 403 `trial_seat_pool_exhausted`.
36. Day-31 transition (convert / auto-downgrade / decline) MUST execute exactly once per active trial and trigger §34.6 preservation for over-cap entities on auto-downgrade.
37. AI usage during trial MUST meter against the vendor's Wallet, not the buyer's (§34.13.6).
38. The 365-day same-buyer-vendor rate-limit MUST be enforced atomically.
39. Vendor non-redemption MUST NOT refund the buyer's allocation (anti-probing rule §34.13.5).
40. Anti-spam framework (§3.5) MUST gate Pro Trial Seat issuance and redemption.

### 34.20.9 Webhooks, Events, and API Surfaces

41. Webhook events for §34 (wallet thresholds, contest lifecycle, cost-base recalc, committed-spend lifecycle, pricing-table publish, downgrade-bucket lifecycle, seat-snapshot triggers, Pro Trial Seat lifecycle) MUST be added to Appendix C (Notification Event Catalog) and Appendix G (PostHog Event Taxonomy) per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Webhook Additions`. Each event MUST follow §31 patterns: HMAC-SHA256 signing, idempotency via `event_id`, exponential backoff retry curve, DLQ after 5 failures, payload ≤ 256 KB.
42. API endpoints for §34 (Billing Ledger, Public Pricing API, Wallet read/configure, Contest file/list, Capability Registry public read, CommittedSpend admin, DowngradeExcessDataBucket read + Ops restore, BillingSeatSnapshot list) MUST follow §32 patterns: authentication, rate-limit headers, cursor pagination (default 50, max 250), error codes from Appendix I per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Endpoint Additions`.
43. Every error code referenced in §34 MUST be added to Appendix I per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Phase 4 Known Gaps` (catalog extension still pending).

### 34.20.10 Glossary and Enum Discipline

44. Every multi-section term introduced or used in §34 MUST have a glossary entry under "Terms Introduced in §34 (v7.0.0 Pricing Rewrite)" in Appendix K (Glossary) — to be added per the Pricing Rewrite Track Phase reconciliation.

### 34.20.11 Seller Rate Card

47. Every customer-billed seller capability in CapabilityRegistryEntry MUST have a matching row in §34.14.1; deploy-time validator `rate_card_coverage` asserts bijection.
48. `value_price_cents` and `cost_price_cents` on each CapabilityRegistryEntry MUST match the published PricingTableVersion (§4.8.9) byte-for-byte; nightly reconciliation asserts.

51. The Public Pricing API `api.sourcera.com/v1/pricing` MUST serve the §34.14.1 seller rate card verbatim; response-shape test `pricing_api_seller_rate_card_shape` asserts.

### 34.20.12 Seller Outcome Signals

52. Every row in §34.14.1 (except `verification_fetch`) MUST have a 1:1 matching OutcomeContract in §34.15.1 with the documented default-on-timeout and contest window; deploy-time validator asserts.
53. Outcome signal evaluation latencies MUST meet: synchronous_success ≤ 1s; implicit_retention / implicit_engagement ≤ 60s from window close; explicit_user_signal ≤ 5s from signal arrival + 300s grace before default-on-timeout fires; platform_internal ≤ 5s from reviewer submission; latency tests assert.

### 34.20.13 Marketplace Discovery

57. The three revenue streams (`rev_ai_wallet`, `rev_subscription`, `rev_marketplace_discovery`) MUST be enforced by Billing Ledger `revenue_stream_class` column; zero rows with `revenue_stream_class=null` OR cross-stream attribution; deploy-time validator `revenue_stream_firewall` asserts.

76. All 13 protected asset classes in §34.19.1 and every sub-class in §34.19.1.A MUST be preserved on every upgrade transition; QA test `plan_upgrade_13_asset_preservation` runs the full matrix and asserts data integrity, including SavedSearch (§4.4.35) and SearchAlert (§4.4.36) rows for Class 7.

# 35\. User Onboarding Experience {#35.-user-onboarding-experience}

## 35.1 Buyer Onboarding Flow {#35.1-buyer-onboarding-flow}

### Step 1: Sign Up

Email \+ password (or SSO for Enterprise). Auto-creates Organization and first Workspace.

### Step 2: Organization Setup

Organization name, logo (optional). Plan selection (Free, or auto-applied 14-day Business Starter trial per §34.2.3 rule #1).

### Step 3: Team Setup

Invite team members by email (bulk paste or single). Assign workspace roles: Workspace Admin, Use Case Lead, Reviewer. Skip option available.

### Step 4: First Use Case

Prompt: "What are you evaluating?" — rendered as the canonical §13.12 "What Are You Evaluating?" Intake. Six default vertical tiles (CRM, ITSM, EDR, Observability, Payroll/HRIS, Other) plus a free-text "Other" path and a muted "blank Workspace" affordance per §13.12.2. Selection materializes a Workspace pre-populated with vertical-specific Use Cases, Requirements, scoring rubric, recommended longlist, and default deadline per §13.12.4. The legacy "Custom SaaS Evaluation / Security-First Evaluation / Compliance Evaluation" Template Gallery affordances are superseded by the §13.12 intake; pre-built templates remain available from the §19 Template Library accessible from inside the materialized Workspace. (Phase 14.7 — 2026-04-27: this Step 4 is a thin wrapper around §13.12; the canonical surface, materialization, and edge-case behavior live in §13.12.)

### Step 5: First Requirement

"Create your first requirement" with guided field completion (title, description, response type, weight). Inline help for each field. Or "Import from policy document" (links to Policy Ingestion).

### Step 6: Optional — TCO Setup

If applicable: "Do you want to compare vendor costs?" Links to TCO Use Case creation.

### Step 7: Dashboard Tour

Highlight tour: Sidebar navigation, Command Palette (`Cmd+K`), Keyboard shortcuts, Pulse dashboard. Tour is dismissible and can be replayed from Settings → Help.

## 35.2 Seller Onboarding Flow {#35.2-seller-onboarding-flow}

The Seller Onboarding Flow exploits the single highest-converting moment in Sourcera's GTM: the forced vendor signup triggered by an incoming buyer invite. The vendor arrives at peak pain (incoming RFP, deadline, blank response, no chosen tool) with an immediate business reason to engage. The onboarding is engineered to collapse the new-vendor cold-start wall from ~2 days (status quo: manual triage, KB hunt, draft from scratch) to under 60 minutes end-to-end.

Narrative context and conversion rationale live in `Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy.md §14–§17`. This section is the implementation spec.

### 35.2.1 Seven-Stage Flow

| Stage | Duration | State | Product Surface |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Magic-link arrival | 0–30s | Buyer invite email, magic-link |
| 2 | Signup + synchronous bootstrap | 30s–3m | Progress storytelling screen |
| 3 | Ready-workspace landing | 3–5m | Bid Workspace with drafts staged |
| 4 | Review and submit | 5–60m | Inline drafts + KB-gap detector |
| 5 | Post-submit stake reveal | Day 0 | Stake-reveal screen |
| 6 | Outcome debrief | Day 3–30 | Win/loss debrief surface |
| 7 | Upgrade touch | Day 1–90 | Contextual upgrade CTAs |

### 35.2.2 Step 1 — Magic-Link Arrival

Vendor receives email: *"You've been invited to participate in '{Workspace Name}' evaluation."* Magic-link opens Sourcera. No credit card prompt. No company profile form gate. Domain + invite identity is sufficient.

**Pre-arrival preparation (hidden from vendor):**
- Domain enrichment against public records (company name, industry, HQ region)
- Marketplace Tagger assigns probable category tags based on domain + buyer-side evaluation context
- Bootstrap queue is pre-warmed; crawl URLs resolved and rate-limited against Firecrawl

The bootstrap starts within the SSO redirect latency window — before the vendor sees a workspace.

### 35.2.3 Step 2 — Signup + Synchronous Bootstrap

Three operations run in parallel while the vendor watches a progress storytelling screen:

1. **Domain Bootstrap** (Capability S1, Opus, lifetime-free on Free). Crawls homepage, help center, docs, trust center. 30–90 seconds.
2. **KB Propose.** 40–200 draft KB entries staged with confidence scores and provenance URLs.
3. **First-Pass Draft** (Capability S2, Sonnet). Drafts responses for every requirement in the buyer's evaluation, citing newly bootstrapped KB entries.

**Progress storytelling screen.** Narrates true status lines:
- *"Scanning yourcompany.com..."* (0–15s)
- *"Found your security documentation..."* (15–30s)
- *"Drafting responses for {Buyer Company}'s 82 requirements..."* (30–90s)
- *"Your bid is ready to review."*

Status lines must reflect real operations — never fabricate steps.

**Account linking (for existing users):** If invitee already has a Sourcera account in a different Organization, present choice:
- *"Join the new organization with your existing account"* → Account linked to new org. Console switcher in sidebar shows all memberships.
- *"Create a new account with different email"* → Separate account created.

**Published Seller Profile** is auto-created on first signup (Basic verification tier, domain-verified). Profile appears in the public Marketplace immediately — no publication gate.

### 35.2.4 Step 3 — Ready-Workspace Landing

Vendor lands on the Bid Workspace with this headline:

> *Your bid for {Buyer Company} is ready. **47** of **82** requirements have AI drafts. **31** cite evidence from your website. Review time: **~35 min**.*

Three clear next steps surfaced inline (not in a modal):
- Review drafts
- Add or edit KB
- Invite teammates

No pricing page. No demo walkthrough. No "try Pro free for 14 days" modal. The hero moment is the pitch.

### 35.2.5 Step 4 — Review and Submit

**Inline citations.** Every First-Pass draft shows its KB citation in the response row: *"from: yourcompany.com/trust/soc2"* with hover expansion to the exact quoted sentence.

**Accept / Edit / Reject per requirement.** Three buttons. Every click is an outcome signal written to the Outcome Resolver (§34.11) for Capability S2.

**Live budget counter.** Top of workspace shows *"AI budget used: $X.XX of $5.00 · N drafts accepted, M rejected."* — visible to the user, sized so a complete first bid end-to-end fits within the $5 Free budget.

**KB-gap detector.** Rejected-response empty state is not a dead end:
> *"No KB content answered this. Write your answer below and we'll save it as a KB entry."*
> `[inline text field with 1-click save]`

One-click creates a KB entry from the vendor's inline answer. Every rejection grows the KB.

**"AI got this right" confirmation.** Accepting a draft with no edits records the strongest acceptance signal and surfaces a confirmation chip (*"added to your KB as verified response"*).

**NDA Review.** If the evaluation requires an NDA (Marketplace §27, NDA Record §4.5.3), the NDA module is surfaced as a blocking step before final submission. NDA review does not delay the hero moment — drafts are still prepared and reviewable during NDA negotiation.

### 35.2.6 Step 5 — Post-Submit Stake Reveal

On submission, the closing screen reads:

> *You just built a reusable KB of **N** verified entries in **Y** minutes.*
> *Your next bid will reuse them automatically.*
> *Sourcera tracked **$X.XX** of value pricing for the AI work on this bid (covered by your Free plan).*

This is a **stake-reveal screen**, not an upgrade CTA. It reminds the vendor what they have built, what it is worth, and how it compounds. Upgrade conversations come later at natural ceilings (Step 7).

### 35.2.7 Step 6 — Outcome Debrief

Triggered by buyer-side bid close event. Agent generates a debrief surface for the vendor:

**Win debrief:**
> *You won. **N** KB entries cited on winning responses. Those entries are now higher-weighted in your KB — Sourcera learned what answers close deals for you. Keep your KB alive — upgrade to Starter to unlock weekly crawls of your site and auto-staleness checks.*

**Loss debrief (with buyer's published reasoning where available):**
> *You lost this one. Gap analysis identified **N** requirements where your KB had no strong answer. Those gaps are flagged in your KB. Upgrade to Starter to let Sourcera crawl your product docs weekly and fill gaps automatically.*

### 35.2.8 Step 7 — Upgrade Touch

Three planned conversion moments, each with a distinct buying reason:

| # | Trigger | Buying reason | CTA |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Second concurrent invited bid | Urgency — "my deal is at risk" | *"Starter unlocks 3 concurrent bids and shares your KB across all of them."* |
| 2 | First proactive EOI attempt | Ambition — "I want to find more deals" | *"Outbound EOIs start at Starter. Your first 10/month are included."* |
| 3 | KB approaches 50-entry cap | Investment — "don't lose what I've built" | *"Your KB is about to hit the Free ceiling. Starter raises it to 1,000 entries."* |

Every upgrade CTA must carry over KB, in-flight bids, Capability Declarations, and Firecrawl configs without re-setup (§34.5). CTAs state the carry-over explicitly.

### 35.2.9 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat Acceptance

If the invite was issued with a Pro Trial Seat (§34.13), Step 2 provisions Seller Starter entitlements instead of Seller Free. The Billing Admin role on the vendor's Org receives a notification and may reject the grant; rejection is audited. On day 31, the vendor is prompted to convert, explicitly decline, or auto-downgrade to Seller Free (all data preserved per §34.6).

### 35.2.10 Activation Metric

**"Minutes from magic-link click to first submitted requirement response"** — targets are sourced from §44.1 `Seller Activation Metric p50 target` and §44.1 `Seller Activation Metric p90 target`. This is a top-level product metric and must be surfaced in the founder dashboard and Ops Console.

### 35.2.11 Onboarding Anti-Patterns (Explicitly Banned)

The onboarding surface must not:
- Ask for a credit card at any point before the first upgrade intent click
- Require the vendor to describe their company or industry before bootstrap runs
- Gate any feature behind a "try Pro free for 14 days" modal on first login
- Show a pricing page until the vendor has submitted their first bid
- Use dark patterns on upgrade CTAs (roach motels, hard-to-find downgrade, fake urgency)
- Present upgrade offers during active bid work — only at natural completion points or ceiling events

These bans exist because the supply-side flywheel depends on vendor trust. Any onboarding friction that reads as sales-ey kills that trust.

### 35.2.12 Required Platform Capabilities

Shipped as dependencies for the Seller Onboarding Flow to go live:

1. Magic-link SSO orchestrator that starts bootstrap inside the SSO redirect latency
2. Progress storytelling UI that renders bootstrap and first-pass status honestly
3. Inline-citation UI on every First-Pass draft response row
4. Budget counter persistent at top of Bid Workspace on Free and Starter
5. KB-gap detector in rejected-response empty states with 1-click KB-entry creation
6. Stake-reveal screen on first bid submission
7. Outcome debrief surface triggered by buyer-side bid close
8. Contextual upgrade CTAs that carry over KB, bids, and in-flight state
9. Pro Trial Seat plumbing (pool allocation, 30-day trial state, auto-downgrade on day 31)
10. Free-ceiling-approaching notifications (40/48 KB entries, 80% budget utilization, first EOI attempt)

## 35.3 Skipped Steps Recoverability {#35.3-skipped-steps-recoverability}

A persistent "Setup Checklist" widget appears in the sidebar during onboarding. Steps completed are checked off. Uncompleted steps remain visible.

**Behavior:**

- Checklist remains until all steps completed or explicitly dismissed  
- Dismissed checklist can be re-opened from Settings → Onboarding → Resume Setup  
- Clicking a step in checklist navigates to that onboarding screen  
- Checklist can be dismissed per-step (click X on individual step) or entirely (Dismiss All)

**Dismissal State:**

- Individual step dismissals: per-step flag stored in onboarding state  
- Full dismissal: `setup_checklist_dismissed` flag set on org record, but steps remain recoverable via Settings

## 35.4 Acceptance Criteria {#35.4-acceptance-criteria}

- Buyer onboarding complete in < 10 minutes.
- **Seller onboarding — time from magic-link click to first submitted requirement response satisfies §44.1 `Seller Activation Metric p50 target` and §44.1 `Seller Activation Metric p90 target`.**
- Seller Profile published publicly in the Marketplace by end of Step 2 (signup + bootstrap).
- KB Bootstrap completes within 90 seconds on p90 for domains under 500 pages.
- First-Pass Draft Generator produces drafts for ≥40% of requirements on p50 for invited bids with ≥40 requirements.
- All tooltips dismissible with single click or `Escape`.
- Onboarding never shows a pricing page before first bid submission.
- Onboarding never prompts for credit card before first upgrade intent click.
- Multi-org users can join additional organizations without account conflict.
- Setup Checklist persists until completed or dismissed, and is recoverable from Settings.
- Pro Trial Seat grants provision Seller Starter entitlements at signup; auto-downgrade on day 31 preserves all data for 90 days per §34.6.
- Activation metric (magic-link → first submitted response) surfaced in founder dashboard and Ops Console in real time.

## 35.5 Buyer Hero Moment {#35.5-buyer-hero-moment}

*(V13 D-HM-002 remediation 2026-05-12. Authored Extension AE-V13-003 — Analytics + Engineering Director + Design Director sign-off pending v7.1.1 ratification. Parallels §48.8 Seller Hero Moment surface specification.)*

**Authoring intent.** The Master Spec at v7.1.0 carried a fully-instrumented Seller Hero Moment (§48.8 + §49.1 + §4.4.22 + §22.20.6 + §44.6) and an explicit out-of-scope buyer-side counterpart (§48.8.1 line 38362: *"Buyer-side invite-creation UX (covered in §48.2.2 L1 and §48.5 M1 / M5 / M15)"*). The §13.12 Buyer Maya intake materialization is structurally a Hero Moment in everything but name — entry condition (Workspace creation from Evaluation Starter), moment-of-value (the materialized Workspace landing + §13.12.7 "What we filled in for you" callout), exit condition (first Requirement edit) — but is not framed or instrumented as a Hero Moment. §35.5 closes the asymmetry: a buyer-side Hero Moment surface specification + activation metric + abandonment recovery, authored at engineering-build fidelity in parallel to §48.8.

**Source authority.** §13.12 Buyer Maya intake materialization; §35.1 Buyer Onboarding Flow (steps 1–7); §13.12.7 "What we filled in for you" callout; §13.12.10 Buyer Maya acceptance criteria; §4.3.1 Workspace entity (the persistence layer); §44.6 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment (Solo-plan render compression parity with seller side); §48.1.5 Phase mapping framework (mirrored on the buyer side for cross-symmetry).

### 35.5.1 Buyer Hero Moment Framework — Five-Phase {#35.5.1-buyer-hero-moment-framework-five-phase}

The buyer-side Hero Moment is structurally five phases (not four — the buyer pipeline has a pre-intake "describe your evaluation" surface that has no seller-side analog). Each phase binds to (a) the SellerOnboardingSession-analog field on §4.3.1 Workspace (V13-extended; see §4.3.1 V13 block), (b) the §13.12 Buyer Maya intake workflow, (c) the §22 Maya capability that funds the AI work (`workspace_intake_materializer` capability — Authored Extension AE-V13-004), and (d) the §34.10 AIWallet ledger entry that records the free-budget consumption during buyer onboarding (lifetime-free `workspace_intake_materializer` allowance per Buyer Org).

| Phase | Window | What Happens (Surface) | Workspace Field(s) | Capability Reference | AIWallet Entry |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Pre-Arrival / Sign-up** | Hidden from buyer; runs from SSO completion through landing on Evaluation Starter | Org provisioning via WorkOS SSO; Workspace pre-allocation; Buyer Maya capability warm-up | `org_id`, `created_by`, `created_at` | §13.12 Buyer Maya readiness probe | None (no AI inference yet) |
| **2. Evaluation Starter Intake (Minutes 0–2)** | `eval_starter_intake_started_at` → `eval_starter_intake_submitted_at` | Zero-form unauthenticated-feel landing surface: *"What are you evaluating?"* free-text + optional "Use cases I care about" multi-select; submit. No team selection, no template picker, no plan-tier gate. | `eval_starter_intake_started_at`, `eval_starter_intake_submitted_at`, `eval_starter_intake_text`, `eval_starter_use_case_count` *(all V13-extension fields on §4.3.1 Workspace — see §4.3.1 V13 block)* | §13.12 Buyer Maya capability `workspace_intake_materializer` (Opus 4.6) | Lifetime-free `workspace_intake_materializer` allowance per Buyer Org (1 per Org per lifetime; subsequent intakes are value-priced under §34.X buyer pricing) |
| **3. Phase 5 (Post-Intake Reveal) is a POST-HERO-MOMENT surface.

### 35.5.2 Buyer Activation Metric & Leading Indicators {#35.5.2-buyer-activation-metric-leading-indicators}

**Buyer Activation Metric** = `activation_metric_elapsed_seconds = buyer_first_requirement_edit_at - eval_starter_intake_started_at`. Cohort: every Buyer Org workspace with `eval_starter_intake_started_at IS NOT NULL`.

**Targets.**

- p50 ≤ 6 minutes (paid tiers Starter+).
- p90 ≤ 25 minutes.
- Solo / Free relaxed bands (per §44.6 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment throttling): p50 ≤ 8 minutes; p90 ≤ 35 minutes.

**Leading indicators** (parallels §48.1.6 seller-side):

1. **Intake submission rate.** Of all `eval_starter_intake_started_at` writes, % that reach `eval_starter_intake_submitted_at`. Target ≥ 75%.
2. **Materialization success rate.** Of all submitted intakes, % that reach `workspace_intake_completed_at`. Target ≥ 95%.
3. **First-edit rate.** Of all completed materializations, % that record `buyer_first_requirement_edit_at` within 24 hours. Target ≥ 80%.
4. **Stake-Reveal dwell.** Median `buyer_stake_reveal_dwell_seconds`. Target ≥ 15 seconds.
5. **24-hour return-edit rate.** Of all completed materializations, % that record a second `requirement_edit` event within 24 hours. Target ≥ 60%.
6. **Solo-tier parity.** Solo / Free Buyer Org activation metric MUST be within 1.5× of paid-tier (a guardrail against §44.6 throttling silently degrading the buyer Hero Moment).

### 35.5.4 Abandonment Recovery (parity with §48.8.12) {#35.5.4-buyer-hero-moment-abandonment-recovery}

The §48.8.12 three-stage Loops.so cadence (24h re-engagement; 7d pre-sweep; 14d re-issue) MUST apply to Buyer Org workspaces at parity. Trigger: `eval_starter_intake_started_at IS NOT NULL AND buyer_first_requirement_edit_at IS NULL`. Email types: `buyer_hero_moment_abandonment_24h`, `buyer_hero_moment_abandonment_pre_sweep`, `buyer_hero_moment_abandonment_re_issue` (Appendix C — new); subject-line catalog at §41.2 V13 block. The Convex cron `buyer_hero_moment_abandonment_sweeper` runs at 15-minute cadence with idempotency parity to §48.8.12.

### 35.5.5 Acceptance Criteria {#35.5.5-buyer-hero-moment-acceptance-criteria}

1. The `buyer_hero_moment_completed_at` field on §4.3.1 Workspace MUST be written by the Workspace render path at first paint IFF (i) all four landing surfaces (Use Cases pre-populated count ≥ 1, Requirements pre-populated count ≥ 1, suggested Vendors count ≥ 0 — `0` allowed, the surface itself is present, callout rendered) are present AND (ii) `workspace_intake_materialization_latency_ms ≤ 60,000` (pause-adjusted for provider-outage windows per the §48.8.3 FM #6 pattern applied to Maya / Anthropic Opus 4.6).
2. The buyer activation metric `activation_metric_elapsed_seconds = buyer_first_requirement_edit_at - eval_starter_intake_started_at` MUST be computed transactionally inside the §4.3.1 Workspace edit path; concurrent edits MUST resolve via the first-edit wins rule.
3. Buyer Hero Moment p50 / p90 SLOs per §35.5.2 MUST be assertable across the `plan_tier × referrer_surface` cohort cross-product; regression > 10% on any cohort raises a §42 P2 to `ops_growth_admin`.
4. Solo / Free Buyer Org cohort SLO relaxation MUST be registered at §44.6.4.X "Throttled-Tier Buyer Hero Moment SLO" (parity with §48.8.10 AC #42 V13 amendment); deploy-time validator `solo_tier_buyer_hero_moment_slo_single_source` (§M.5 — new) asserts.
5. The §35.5.4 Loops.so abandonment cadence MUST honor §6.8 DSAR pseudonymization; CI gate `dsar_erased_buyer_excluded_from_recovery_cadence` (§M.5 — new) asserts.
6. Console-firewall enforcement: Seller Console GET on any Workspace row returns HTTP 404 per §7.2; `buyer_hero_moment_*` events emit with `console="buyer"` and do not leak to Seller Console analytics.
7. CI gate `buyer_activation_metric_canonical_consumer` (§M.5 — new; pack assignment M21.3 — Buyer Maya intake) asserts that the activation metric formula is single-sourced at §35.5.2 and every §51 / §42 / §50.14 dashboard tile queries it via the canonical formula.
8. *(Authored Extension AE-V13-007 — Privacy Officer sign-off pending v7.1.1 ratification; buyer parity with §48.8.12 AC #8.)* The §35.5.4 buyer abandonment cadence MUST apply the same enqueue→send in-flight DSAR fail-closed re-check as §48.8.12 AC #8: the `buyer_hero_moment_abandonment_sweeper` dispatch MUST re-evaluate the §6.8 pseudonymization predicate at Loops.so send/retry time; a §6.8 right-to-erasure landing after enqueue (including during the §48.8.12-AC-#4-parity Tier-2 retry curve) drops the dispatch, leaves the Workspace recovery state unchanged, and emits a PII-minimized skip §4.6.1 AuditEvent (`{org_id, workspace_id, recovery_stage, skip_reason='dsar_pseudonymized'}` per the Appendix J `recovery_cadence_skip_reason` enum — registered under AE-V13-007 — never the erased subject email). The §M.5.12 CI gate `dsar_erased_buyer_excluded_from_recovery_cadence` assertion is extended to cover the send-time re-check. # 37\. Accessibility & Internationalization {#37.-accessibility-&-internationalization}

## 37.1 Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA) {#37.1-accessibility-(wcag-2.1-aa)}

- **Color and contrast.** Text, non-text contrast, focus indicators, and High Contrast mode inherit the §3.11.3 / §3.11.8 token contracts; color is never the sole information conveyor (WCAG 1.4.1 / 1.4.3 / 1.4.11).
- **Keyboard navigation.** All interactive elements are reachable by keyboard, focus order follows DOM reading order, focus returns to the opener after modal / dropdown / Side Peek close, and focus ring geometry is sourced from §3.6.2 plus the §3.11.8 High Contrast delta. No §37 row may restate focus-ring numeric values.
- **Screen reader semantics.** Interactive elements carry accessible names; forms bind labels via `<label for>` or `aria-labelledby`; landmarks (`<main>`, `<nav>`, `<aside>`) are present; status messages use rate-limited `aria-live` regions; custom controls expose state through ARIA only when native HTML cannot express the state.
- **Motor and target size.** Touch-target minimums are sourced only from §38.6.2. §37 interprets those tier values against WCAG 2.5.5 / 2.5.8 and never authors an independent target-size number.
- **Reflow and zoom.** Authenticated and public routes MUST reflow at 320 CSS px wide by 256 CSS px tall and at 400% desktop zoom without two-dimensional scrolling. Matrix, table, and chart surfaces satisfy this by rendering the mobile card-list / data-table alternative declared in §38.6.2, not by adding horizontal and vertical scroll to the same viewport.
- **Bypass blocks.** Every authenticated page and public Marketplace page renders a "Skip to main content" link as the first tab stop, visually hidden until focused, moving focus to the `<main>` landmark.
- **Focus management contracts.** Modals move focus to the first meaningful control and return to the opener on close; Side Peek focus-traps per §3.8.7; toast creation never steals focus; dropdowns / comboboxes focus the selected or first option and return to trigger on close; Command Palette autofocuses the input and returns focus to the opener; session-expiry mid-modal moves focus to the login form while preserving `return_to`.
- **Timing and motion.** Session-expiry warnings, auto-running animations, and reduced-motion handling inherit §6, §38.10, and §3.9. Motions longer than 5 seconds require pause / stop / hide controls unless the surface is a one-shot transition under the §38.10 reduced-motion contract.

**Per-Surface Conformance Binding (Authored Extension — v7.1.0 / Phase 10V remediation; amended by v7.2.0-REM Phase 37 P1 remediation; ratification queued under AE-37-01 and AE-V72REM-PH37-A11Y-01).** Every UI surface MUST carry a WCAG conformance posture binding. The binding takes one of two forms:

1. **Catalog-row binding.** Surfaces enumerated in the §3.7.6 per-surface state catalog (Dashboard / Matrix / Detail / Settings / Ops Console / Knowledge Base) inherit conformance posture from this §37.1 universal contract via their `page_surface_kind`. The catalog row need not restate the WCAG Success Criterion list; the per-surface row inherits.
2. **§-anchor binding.** Surfaces with a primary §-anchor in §11–§27 / §50 / §51 (e.g., Defense View §13.11, Buyer Maya intake §13.12, Seller Maya Polish §22.20, Pipeline Surface Compression bar §3.14, AIWallet widget §4.8.3) MUST carry an Appendix M.1 row whose Notes cell includes `Conformance posture: inherits_§37.1` for surfaces meeting the §37 universal posture. Deviations (e.g., embedded third-party iframes like Stripe Checkout, Adobe Sign, Zendesk Support Widget — see §3.7.6.6 NDA Execution row in §38.8.2) declare the deviation rationale + mitigations inline.

Appendix M conformance posture is enforced by `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` (§M.4) and the §M.5 gate `appendix_m_conformance_posture_completeness`. The gate fails any diff that adds a surface §-anchor without an Appendix M.1 conformance-posture note, OR that adds an Appendix M.1 row with an empty / malformed posture note.

**Success Criterion set.** The §37.6 acceptance criteria are the binding test surface for WCAG 2.1 AA Success Criteria 1.1.1, 1.3.1, 1.3.2, 1.3.3, 1.3.4, 1.3.5, 1.4.1, 1.4.3, 1.4.4, 1.4.5, 1.4.10, 1.4.11, 1.4.12, 1.4.13, 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.1.4, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.4.1, 2.4.3, 2.4.4, 2.4.5, 2.4.6, 2.4.7, 2.5.1, 2.5.2, 2.5.3, 2.5.4, 2.5.5, 3.1.1, 3.1.2, 3.2.1, 3.2.2, 3.2.3, 3.2.4, 3.3.1, 3.3.2, 3.3.3, 3.3.4, 4.1.2, 4.1.3 plus WCAG 2.2 AA Success Criteria 2.4.11, 2.5.7, 2.5.8, 3.2.6, 3.3.7, and 3.3.8.

## 37.2 Internationalization (i18n) {#37.2-internationalization-(i18n)}

**English-only through v7.1.x.** The codebase is i18n-ready:

- All UI strings externalized via `next-intl` library.  
- No hardcoded strings in components.  
- Locale-aware formatting is supported:  
  - Dates: Per browser locale (en-US: MM/DD/YYYY, en-GB: DD/MM/YYYY, etc.)  
  - Numbers: Thousands separator and decimal per locale.  
  - Currency: Configurable per Organization (default USD).  
  - Timezone: User-configurable (default browser timezone).

**Locale Resolution Engine.** Authenticated routes resolve locale in this order: explicit URL `?lang=` preview parameter when present and valid BCP-47; User.`locale`; `Accept-Language`; `en-US` fallback. Public Marketplace routes resolve URL locale prefix first, then `Accept-Language`, then `en-US`. Every rendered document sets `<html lang="{resolved_locale}">`; user-generated content whose language differs from the page locale carries `lang` on the containing element when known.

**Pluralization and formatting.** Translation strings use ICU MessageFormat through `next-intl`, including CLDR plural categories. Dates, times, percentages, negative numbers, compact numbers, and currency values must render through locale-aware formatters rather than string concatenation. Billing currency remains governed by §34 / AIWallet; §37 controls display formatting only.

**Roadmap:** Spanish, French, German, and Japanese UI translations are deferred to v8.x. User-generated content (requirements, responses, comments, KB entries) remains in original language unless a future translation feature is explicitly authored.

## 37.3 Right-to-Left (RTL) Support {#37.3-right-to-left-(rtl)-support}

**Layout mirroring is implemented; translations are deferred.** RTL layout behavior is implemented through the `useDirectionality()` hook and the §38.11 Right-to-Left & Locale Mirror Behavior contract. Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu, and other RTL UI translations are deferred to the v8.x localization rollout; the layout engine must nevertheless render mixed LTR / RTL content correctly before those translations ship.

**CSS architecture.** Layouts use CSS Logical Properties (`inline-start`, `inline-end`, `block-start`, `block-end`) instead of directional properties (`left`, `right`) except in audited allow-list cases where the physical direction is semantically required (e.g., a canvas coordinate grid). Directional icons mirror only when the icon conveys direction; non-directional icons do not mirror per §38.11.

**Mixed-direction text.** Buyer requirements, seller responses, KB snippets, and Marketplace copy may contain mixed LTR / RTL content. Renderers must use Unicode bidi isolation (`dir="auto"` or `<bdi>`) around user-generated inline fragments and must not rely on punctuation position as a semantic signal.

## 37.4 Accessibility Settings & User Preferences {#37.4-accessibility-settings-user-preferences}

Settings -> Accessibility is a first-class User Settings panel (§36.1) backed by §4.2.14 UserAccessibilityPreference.

| Preference | Source field | Default | Surface effect |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Show teammate cursors | UserAccessibilityPreference.`show_teammate_cursors` | true | Hides live cursor rendering from §3.9 without disabling presence avatars or typing indicators. |
| Mention announcement priority | UserAccessibilityPreference.`mention_announcement_priority` | `assertive` | Maps mention live regions to `assertive` or `polite` per §3.12.9. |
| High Contrast | UserAccessibilityPreference.`high_contrast_mode` | `auto` | Applies §3.11.8 High Contrast mode by explicit user choice or OS contrast preference. |
| Assistive-tech shortcut remaps | UserAccessibilityPreference.`assistive_tech_keymap_overrides_json` | null | Stores user remaps for Appendix B shortcut conflicts with NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, switch control, or enterprise assistive technology. |

**Behavior.** The panel lazy-creates the preference row on first save; unsaved changes warn before navigation; every save writes `accessibility.preference_updated` AuditEvent with changed field names only. Admins may see that a custom keymap exists but not its raw JSON. The panel is available in buyer and seller consoles and resolves to the same Org-scoped row.

## 37.5 Testing & Audit Pipeline {#37.5-testing-and-audit-pipeline}

- **Automated gate.** CI gate `accessibility_audit_v7_1_aa_full` runs `axe-core@4.10.x` (or latest patch within 4.10) on every UI-affecting PR and nightly full sweep. The gate blocks merge on any `critical` or `serious` violation and on any `moderate` / `minor` violation tagged to the §37.1 Success Criterion set unless the row carries an approved Appendix M.5 override.
- **Route scope.** The route set is the union of §3.7 `page_surface_kind` routes, public Marketplace routes, §38.6.5 `responsive_conformance_suite` routes, and §46.1.2 critical-path E2E flows. Each route renders in light, dark, and High Contrast modes across the five §38.6.1 tiers plus the 320 CSS px reflow fixture and 400% desktop zoom fixture.
- **Screen reader matrix.** Critical workflows run monthly and pre-release against NVDA (Windows), JAWS (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS), VoiceOver (iOS), and VoiceOver (iPadOS). The flow set mirrors §46.1.2 and includes login/MFA, Workspace creation, Requirements Matrix edit, Side Peek edit, Seller bid response, Settings -> Accessibility update, billing plan change, and public Marketplace search.
- **Keyboard and focus.** The keyboard suite asserts skip-link presence, modal / dropdown / Side Peek focus behavior, Command Palette focus return, no keyboard traps, and no assistive-tech default shortcut shadowing per Appendix B §B.10.
- **RTL and i18n.** `responsive_conformance_suite` includes LTR and RTL render passes through `useDirectionality()` (§38.11); `no_hardcoded_directional_css` fails any new physical `left` / `right` CSS outside the allow-list. Locale formatting tests assert BCP-47 resolution, `<html lang>`, ICU pluralization, and language-of-parts behavior.
- **Annual external audit.** A third-party WCAG audit is required annually +/- 60 days and before any Enterprise customer contract that names WCAG conformance as a pre-signature requirement. Findings map to the platform severity ladder: P0/P1/P2/P3 remediation targets follow §42.3.0 unless Legal sets a shorter customer commitment.

## 37.6 Acceptance Criteria {#37.6-acceptance-criteria}

1. Every PR touching `app/styles/**`, design tokens, `components/**/*.tsx`, route shells, public Marketplace pages, or Settings -> Accessibility MUST run `accessibility_audit_v7_1_aa_full`; the run MUST record `axe-core@4.10.x` version, route id, viewport tier, theme mode, resolved locale, and directionality.
2. Every route in the §37.5 route scope MUST return zero unapproved axe violations in light, dark, and High Contrast modes across all §38.6.1 tiers, the 320 CSS px reflow fixture, and the 400% desktop zoom fixture.
3. Every Success Criterion listed in §37.1 MUST have at least one named fixture or documented manual-test procedure in the accessibility audit manifest; missing fixture coverage blocks v7.1.1 stamp through Appendix M.5 `accessibility_success_criterion_fixture_coverage`.
4. Touch target assertions MUST read the per-tier source of truth from §38.6.2. Any new inline touch-target number outside §38.6.2 fails `touch_target_per_tier_single_source`.
5. Every page MUST render a skip-link as the first tab stop and MUST move focus to `<main>` when activated; missing skip-link or focus target is a blocking accessibility regression.
6. Modal, dropdown, Side Peek, toast, and Command Palette focus behavior MUST satisfy the §37.1 focus-management contracts in automated keyboard tests; any keyboard trap blocks merge.
7. Settings -> Accessibility MUST persist all §37.4 preferences to UserAccessibilityPreference, apply them without reload, emit the redacted AuditEvent, and include the row in DSAR export.
8. Screen-reader tests MUST pass for NVDA, JAWS, macOS VoiceOver, iOS VoiceOver, and iPadOS VoiceOver on the §37.5 critical workflow set; default shortcut conflicts must be remappable through §37.4.
9. RTL test fixtures MUST prove `useDirectionality()` applies `dir`, icon mirroring, number alignment, and CSS logical properties per §38.11; translation availability is not required for v7.1.x.
10. Locale fixtures MUST prove BCP-47 resolution, `<html lang>`, language-of-parts, ICU pluralization, date/time/number/currency formatting, and `en-US` fallback.
11. Annual third-party audit findings MUST be logged as defects, mapped to severity, assigned an owner, and tracked to closure; unresolved P0/P1 findings block any release claiming WCAG conformance.
12. Appendix M.1 MUST contain rows for Accessibility Compliance Posture, Settings -> Accessibility, Axe-core CI gate, Annual WCAG Audit Pipeline, `useDirectionality()` RTL hook, and Locale Resolution Engine; Appendix M.5 MUST contain the corresponding gate rows.
