# 38\. Responsive Design & Platform Support {#38.-responsive-design-&-platform-support}

## 38.1 Breakpoints {#38.1-breakpoints}

| Breakpoint | Width | Layout |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Mobile | \< 640px | Single-column. Sidebar collapsed to hamburger menu. Bottom navigation bar. |
| Tablet | 640-1024px | Two-column (sidebar \+ main). Touch targets follow §38.6.2. Top navigation. |
| Desktop | \> 1024px | Three-column (sidebar \+ main \+ detail pane). Keyboard shortcuts enabled. Sidebar pinned. |

## 38.2 Browser Support {#38.2-browser-support}

**Desktop:** Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge (latest 2 versions each). Minimum 1024x768px. **Mobile:** iOS Safari, Chrome Android (latest 2 versions). Samsung Internet (latest). Minimum 375x667px. **Unsupported:** Internet Explorer (all versions).

## 38.3 JavaScript Requirement {#38.3-javascript-requirement}

Sourcera requires JavaScript. The platform is built on Convex (real-time reactive subscriptions) which requires the Convex SDK (JavaScript). There is no server-side rendering fallback for JavaScript-disabled browsers. If JavaScript is disabled, the app displays a static banner: "Sourcera requires JavaScript to function. Please enable JavaScript in your browser settings."

## 38.4 Mobile Feature Parity {#38.4-mobile-feature-parity}

Mobile experience is read \+ limited write. Full workflows (scoring, complex editing) require desktop.

**Mobile Read Access:**

- View requirements, responses, scores, comments  
- View workspace status and phase  
- View Pulse health metrics  
- View Intelligence briefings (read-only)

**Mobile Limited Write Access:**

- Comment on requirements (threaded comments)  
- Submit boolean responses (Seller Console)  
- View and acknowledge notifications

**Mobile Not Supported:**

- Collaborative scoring (requires Tablet+ due to multi-pane layout)  
- Policy Ingestion (file upload, complex extraction review)  
- TCO configuration (complex parameterization)  
- Scenario modeling (matrix-intensive)  
- Command Palette (replaced by Search Bar on mobile)  
- Full requirement editing (Markdown editor requires larger viewport)

**Mobile Search Bar:** On mobile, `Cmd+K` is not available. Instead, top navigation includes "Search" icon (magnifying glass) that opens mobile search. Searches: requirements, vendors, use cases, comments.

## 38.5 Acceptance Criteria {#38.5-acceptance-criteria}

- Mobile experience displays correctly on 375px width.  
- Touch targets follow the §38.6.2 per-tier minimum.  
- Read workflows fully functional on mobile.  
- Limited write workflows (comments, boolean responses) fully functional on mobile.  
- Mobile search bar responsive and discoverable.  
- Tablet layout properly reflows when rotated (landscape ↔ portrait).

## 38.6 Breakpoints — Authoritative Taxonomy & Per-Breakpoint Layout Rules {#38.6-breakpoints-authoritative-taxonomy}

**Purpose (C.114).** §38.1 captures a coarse three-tier breakpoint story (mobile / tablet / desktop) suitable for narrative chapters; §38.6 is the engineering-authoritative five-tier taxonomy that every `@media` rule, responsive hook, and layout component MUST key off. The taxonomy aligns with the Summary C.114 specification of `640 / 768 / 1024 / 1280 px` and is the binding surface for Tailwind breakpoint configuration, Convex reactive query viewport-aware diffing, and per-surface layout token selection. Where §38.1 and §38.6 disagree, §38.6 is authoritative; §38.1 must be interpreted as a rounded narrative view of the §38.6 taxonomy.

**Enum.** `responsive_breakpoint_tier` (Appendix J): `mobile_xs`, `mobile_sm`, `tablet`, `desktop`, `desktop_xl`. Exactly one tier is active per viewport; transitions fire on `window.resize` debounced at 150ms. Tier-transition telemetry emits `ui_responsive_breakpoint_crossed` (Appendix G) with `from_tier`, `to_tier`, `width_px`, `reason ∈ {resize, rotation, dev_tools_open, split_view_change}`.

### 38.6.1 Breakpoint Definitions {#38.6.1-breakpoint-definitions}

| Tier | Viewport Width | Canonical Devices | Tailwind Alias |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `mobile_xs` | `< 640px` | iPhone SE (375×667), iPhone 15 (390×844), Pixel 7a (412×915), portrait Android midrange | *(default, unprefixed)* |
| `mobile_sm` | `640px ≤ w < 768px` | Large-screen phones in portrait (Pixel 8 Pro 412→ scaled web zoom), phablets landscape, small foldables folded | `sm:` |
| `tablet` | `768px ≤ w < 1024px` | iPad portrait (768×1024), iPad Mini portrait, Galaxy Tab portrait, Surface Duo unfolded | `md:` |
| `desktop` | `1024px ≤ w < 1280px` | iPad landscape (1024×768), Surface Pro landscape, small laptop (13″ @ 1366×768 scaled), split-view 50% on 24″ monitor | `lg:` |
| `desktop_xl` | `≥ 1280px` | Standard laptop ≥14″, external monitors, 4K displays at ≤1.5× OS scaling | `xl:` *(and above)* |

**Rounding & edge rules.** A viewport at exactly `640px` belongs to `mobile_sm`, exactly `768px` to `tablet`, exactly `1024px` to `desktop`, exactly `1280px` to `desktop_xl`. CSS `@media (min-width: 640px)` semantics govern; our resize debouncer MUST NOT introduce off-by-one drift. Fractional widths (e.g., `767.5px` on high-DPI displays) resolve per CSS spec: `mobile_sm` at `767.5px`, `tablet` at `768px`. Tier computation MUST use `window.innerWidth` for authenticated sessions and `document.documentElement.clientWidth` as fallback for kiosk-mode readers (no scrollbar reservation). Zooming via `Cmd+Plus`/pinch-zoom alters tier (zoomed-in narrow effective width); orientation change alters tier (portrait→landscape for tablets/foldables). Split-view (iPadOS, ChromeOS) alters tier at the split boundary.

### 38.6.2 Per-Breakpoint Layout Rules {#38.6.2-per-breakpoint-layout-rules}

The following table binds each tier to a canonical layout contract. Every page surface (§3.7 `page_surface_kind`) MUST conform. Component-level divergences are documented per §38.8.

| Dimension | `mobile_xs` | `mobile_sm` | `tablet` | `desktop` | `desktop_xl` |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Column layout | Single column | Single column, wider gutters | Two-column (sidebar + main) | Three-column (sidebar + main + optional Peek) | Three-column with expanded Peek max-width |
| Sidebar (§3.1) | Hidden; hamburger menu + bottom nav | Hidden; hamburger menu + bottom nav | Icon-rail (56px); expandable on tap | Pinned, 240px full | Pinned, 240px full |
| Side Peek (§3.8) | Full-screen modal takeover | Full-screen modal takeover | Full-width overlay above main (72% viewport width) | 480px default, 360–640px user-resizable | 480px default, 360–720px user-resizable |
| Command Palette (§3.2) | Not rendered; `Cmd+K` inert; mobile Search Bar replaces | Not rendered; Search Bar | Rendered; opens as centered modal at 640px width | Rendered; opens as centered modal at 720px width | Rendered; centered modal at 840px width |
| Primary navigation | Bottom nav bar (5 items max: Dashboard, Requirements, Vendors, Inbox, More) | Bottom nav bar | Top nav bar + icon-rail sidebar | Sidebar navigation | Sidebar navigation |
| Secondary nav / breadcrumbs | Collapsed to back-chevron + current page title | Collapsed to back-chevron + current page title | Breadcrumb with middle-segment truncation | Full breadcrumb | Full breadcrumb |
| Tab bars within pages | Horizontal scroll with fade-edge affordance | Horizontal scroll | Full-width tabs | Full-width tabs | Full-width tabs |
| Matrix/Table rendering | Card-list (no table) | Card-list (no table) | Horizontal-scroll table with sticky ID column | Full table, fit-to-width | Full table with expanded column widths; priority columns wider |
| DataTable column density | N/A (card-list) | N/A (card-list) | Priority columns only (§9.7 UX doc rules) | Standard column set | Extended column set (all non-hidden columns) |
| Side Peek trigger | Tap row → full-screen peek | Tap row → full-screen peek | Tap row → 72% overlay peek | `Enter`/row-click → 480px peek | `Enter`/row-click → 480px peek |
| Cursor Presence (§3.9) | Static avatar strip only; no live cursors | Static avatar strip only | Live cursors enabled with reduced opacity (60% cap to save paint) | Full live cursors (up to 8 palette) | Full live cursors |
| Bulk Action Toolbar (§3.10) | Hidden; bulk actions via long-press → action sheet | Hidden; long-press action sheet | Top-of-table toolbar, simplified action set (assign, delete, status) | Full toolbar, all 14 action surfaces | Full toolbar |
| Keyboard shortcuts active | Only `Escape` (for closing overlays) | Only `Escape` | Full keyboard shortcuts if external keyboard detected, otherwise `Escape` only | All keyboard shortcuts active | All keyboard shortcuts active |
| Hover interactions | Absent (`@media (hover: none)`) | Absent | Present if external mouse detected; otherwise absent | Present | Present |
| Touch-target minimum | 48 × 48 CSS px | 48 × 48 CSS px | 44 × 44 CSS px | 32 × 32 CSS px | 32 × 32 CSS px |
| Typography base | 16px body; 32px display | 16px body; 36px display | 15px body; 36px display | 14px body; 40px display | 14px body; 44px display |
| Line-length cap | 65ch | 65ch | 72ch | 80ch | 90ch |
| Page-level padding (gutters) | `16px` | `20px` | `24px` | `32px` | `48px` |
| Modal dimensions | Full-screen takeover | Full-screen takeover | 80% viewport, centered | Fixed width (480–720px depending on content) | Fixed width (480–840px) |
| Bottom sheet | Slides from bottom to 85% viewport height | Slides from bottom to 85% viewport height | Slides from bottom to 60% viewport height (tablet-optimized) | N/A (replaced by side peek or modal) | N/A |
| `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` participation | Full (§3.11) | Full | Full | Full | Full |
| `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)` participation | Instant transitions, no animation | Instant transitions | Instant transitions | Reduced-motion respected | Reduced-motion respected |
| Seller Console Bid Composer rendering | Simplified card list (no split-pane) | Simplified card list | Two-pane split (requirements + response) | Three-pane split (requirements + response + KB suggestions) | Three-pane with expanded KB suggestion rail |
| Ops Console (§50) default rendering | Blocked; redirects to `/ops/mobile-unsupported` informational page | Blocked; redirects to `/ops/mobile-unsupported` | Read-only surfaces permitted; writes blocked with redirect banner | Full Ops Console | Full Ops Console |

**Convex query viewport-aware diffing.** Reactive subscriptions running in a `mobile_xs` or `mobile_sm` session MAY request a smaller row fanout (e.g., the Requirements Matrix subscription defaults to `limit=20` on mobile vs `limit=50` on desktop) to reduce bandwidth on cellular links. The tier is passed as a subscription parameter; server-side reducers MUST accept it and MUST NOT leak rows outside the requested fanout window. Cached results are keyed by `(org_id, console, surface, breakpoint_tier, filter_hash)` to prevent desktop-cached rows bleeding into mobile renders.

### 38.6.3 Breakpoint-Aware Entity Fields {#38.6.3-breakpoint-aware-entity-fields}

Two entities store per-breakpoint user preferences; both are User-scoped and cross-console-shared.

| Entity | Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `UserUIPreference` | `id` | UUID | PK | |
| `UserUIPreference` | `user_id` | UUID (FK → User) | Not null | Owning user |
| `UserUIPreference` | `last_observed_breakpoint_tier` | Enum (`responsive_breakpoint_tier`) | Nullable | Updated on `ui_responsive_breakpoint_crossed` |
| `UserUIPreference` | `sidebar_collapsed_per_tier_json` | JSON | Key set = Appendix J `responsive_breakpoint_tier`; value ∈ `{true, false}` | Per-tier sidebar collapse state |
| `UserUIPreference` | `side_peek_width_px_per_tier_json` | JSON | Key set = `responsive_breakpoint_tier`; value ∈ `[360, 720]` | Per-tier user-resized peek width |
| `UserUIPreference` | `datatable_columns_hidden_per_tier_json` | JSON | Per-tier array of hidden column IDs | Overrides automatic column hiding |
| `UserUIPreference` | `created_at` | Timestamp | Not null | |
| `UserUIPreference` | `updated_at` | Timestamp | Not null | |
| `UserUIPreference` | `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable (soft delete) | Default null |

**Scope.** User-scoped, cross-console-shared (a single User has one `UserUIPreference` record regardless of active console). Cross-org: preferences do NOT persist across Org boundaries for the same email — a User represented by `user_id` in two Orgs has two distinct `UserUIPreference` rows. DSAR: exported under the User's identity package per §6.8; anonymized on right-to-erasure per §40.2.

**Indexes.** `(user_id)` unique. **Retention.** Follows User lifecycle (§40.2 User row); no independent retention. **Residency.** Replicates User's residency (US vs EU vs custom per §40.4).

### 38.6.4 Tier-Transition Edge Cases {#38.6.4-tier-transition-edge-cases}

| Condition | Behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Window resize crosses tier boundary mid-interaction (e.g., user drags between `tablet` and `desktop`) | Layout reflows on next debounced frame (150ms). Active modals, peeks, and bottom sheets rerender at the new tier's component form via §38.8.1 transition contract. Unsaved form state MUST be preserved across reflow (controlled via React state, not layout). |
| Orientation change (portrait ↔ landscape) on tablet mid-Side-Peek | Peek animates from 72%-overlay (portrait) to 60%-overlay (landscape) per §38.8.1; scroll position preserved; focus preserved. |
| iPadOS split-view resize drags viewport below `tablet` threshold | Peek collapses to full-screen modal takeover; sidebar collapses to hamburger; preserve focus and scroll; emit `ui_responsive_breakpoint_crossed` with `reason=split_view_change`. |
| External monitor unplugged (laptop lid-close) | Viewport drops to primary display dimensions; layout reflows. If the user was in an Ops Console surface on an external monitor and the laptop's primary display resolves to `tablet` tier, Ops Console gracefully degrades to read-only view with banner "Ops Console writes paused — primary display is below minimum resolution. Reconnect an external monitor to resume." |
| Zoom > 200% on `desktop_xl` causes effective width to fall into `tablet` | Tier recomputed against effective width; layout reflows to `tablet`. User zoom is honored; this is accessibility-positive. |
| User rotates phone with `Command Palette` open on `mobile_sm` (unreachable state per §38.6.2, but defensive) | Command Palette is server-side-rendered-absent on `mobile_sm`; a hydration pass that detects it present emits `ui_command_palette_mobile_leak_detected` and closes it. |
| Developer-tools opening in side-panel mode crosses the tier | Treated identically to viewport resize; layout reflows. Analytics event `reason=dev_tools_open`. |
| Print stylesheet (`@media print`) | Tier forced to `desktop` for layout purposes; sidebar/navigation hidden; side peek expanded inline; see §38.9 future extension. |

### 38.6.5 Responsive Tier Conformance Tests {#38.6.5-responsive-tier-conformance-tests}

Every top-level route (§3.7 `page_surface_kind` × route) MUST pass an automated `responsive_conformance_suite` test that renders the route at each of the five canonical widths (`375px`, `720px`, `820px`, `1200px`, `1440px`) plus the §37.1 WCAG reflow fixtures (`320px × 256px` and 400% desktop zoom) and asserts: (a) no horizontal overflow except for surfaces that render the §38.6.2 mobile card-list / data-table alternative, (b) touch targets meet the tier's minimum, (c) required panels visible, (d) forbidden components absent (e.g., Command Palette not rendered on `mobile_sm`). Failures block merge. Conformance results are aggregated into the `responsive_tier_conformance` dashboard (§50.14.3).

### 38.6.6 Acceptance Criteria {#38.6.6-acceptance-criteria}

1. The `responsive_breakpoint_tier` enum MUST resolve deterministically from `window.innerWidth` per the §38.6.1 table, including exact-value tie-breaks (640 → `mobile_sm`, 768 → `tablet`, 1024 → `desktop`, 1280 → `desktop_xl`).
2. Tier transitions MUST debounce at 150ms ±20ms and emit `ui_responsive_breakpoint_crossed` with `from_tier`, `to_tier`, `width_px`, `reason` on every crossing.
3. Every page surface MUST pass `responsive_conformance_suite` at all five canonical widths plus the §37.1 reflow fixtures; zero horizontal overflow except for the explicitly authored §38.6.2 mobile card-list / data-table alternative; touch targets meet the §38.6.2 tier minimum.
4. Sidebar, Side Peek, Command Palette, and Bottom Nav MUST render exactly per §38.6.2 with no cross-tier component leakage (e.g., Command Palette hydrated on `mobile_xs` is a CI failure).
5. `UserUIPreference.last_observed_breakpoint_tier` MUST be updated within 500ms of a tier transition (network permitting; offline queues the update).
6. Side Peek width resolves from `UserUIPreference.side_peek_width_px_per_tier_json` if set, else from the §38.6.2 default; out-of-range values are clamped and re-persisted.
7. Unsaved form state MUST be preserved across any tier transition, orientation change, or split-view resize; no data loss on reflow is detectable by the `reflow_form_state_preservation` E2E test.
8. Print stylesheet resolves to `desktop` tier; sidebar and navigation hidden; peek contents inlined; verified by `print_preview_regression` visual test.
9. Tier-transition telemetry MUST NOT cross the Dual-Console Firewall (§7); events emit to the active console's PostHog project only.
10. Ops Console (§50) MUST return HTTP 302 redirect to `/ops/mobile-unsupported` for any `mobile_xs` or `mobile_sm` request against a write route; read routes permitted on `tablet` read-only; full access on `desktop` and `desktop_xl`.

**Failure Modes (counterfactual coverage).**

- *Tier thrash on resize:* A user slowly dragging a browser window between 639 and 641 px can cause rapid tier oscillation. Mitigation: 150ms debounce + hysteresis (20px buffer around each boundary before re-crossing).
- *iOS Safari URL bar toggle fires resize events:* The 48px URL bar show/hide mutates `window.innerHeight` but not `innerWidth`; breakpoint computation MUST key on `innerWidth` alone. The hide/show MUST NOT emit a tier-transition event.
- *Dev-tools split consumes viewport:* Dev-tools opening on the side reduces effective `innerWidth`; tier must recompute. Documented as `reason=dev_tools_open`.
- *Accessibility zoom combined with small laptop screen:* User at 200% zoom on a 1280px laptop → effective 640px; MUST reflow to `mobile_sm` layout. Accessibility over precision.
- *Foldable devices (Galaxy Fold):* Folded → `mobile_xs`; unfolded → `tablet`; transition via Samsung Internet fires resize twice (mid-fold and settled). Second (settled) event is authoritative.
- *External-monitor hot-plug unplug mid-session:* Laptop lid-close or cable yank fires `ui_responsive_breakpoint_crossed` with `reason=resize`; session state preserved; writes in progress complete; banner shown on Ops surfaces.

## 38.7 Gesture Equivalents — Keyboard-to-Gesture Translation Contract {#38.7-gesture-equivalents}

**Purpose (C.114).** The Linear Constraint (§3.1) is keyboard-first on desktop. On mobile (`mobile_xs` and `mobile_sm` per §38.6.1), every keyboard pattern translates to a gesture-first equivalent that preserves the constraint's "linear flow" principle while enforcing the 5-tap ceiling defined in §3.4.1. §38.7 supersedes §3.4 as the authoritative gesture-translation contract for all Sourcera surfaces; §3.4's table is a narrative recap.

**Enum.** `mobile_gesture_kind` (Appendix J): `tap`, `double_tap`, `long_press`, `two_finger_tap`, `swipe_up`, `swipe_down`, `swipe_left`, `swipe_right`, `pull_to_refresh`, `pinch_zoom`, `bottom_sheet_drag_down`, `back_gesture_ios_edge_swipe`, `back_gesture_android_hardware_back`, `keyboard_dismiss_swipe_down`. Exactly one gesture per interaction unit.

**Enum.** `mobile_keyboard_shortcut_target` (Appendix J): `row_next`, `row_prev`, `open_peek`, `close_overlay`, `open_command_palette`, `open_search`, `submit_form`, `inline_edit`, `range_select`, `select_all`, `delete_selection`, `advance_phase`, `switch_console`, `show_shortcut_overlay`. Every §3.7 keyboard shortcut MUST map to exactly one target in this enum.

### 38.7.1 Keyboard-to-Gesture Translation Table {#38.7.1-keyboard-to-gesture-translation-table}

This is the authoritative binding. Every §3.7 keyboard shortcut MUST have a row below; shortcuts with no sensible mobile analogue route to "Command Equivalent" (long-press surface-level action menu).

| Desktop Keyboard | Target | Mobile Gesture (`mobile_xs`, `mobile_sm`) | Tablet w/o Keyboard | Tablet w/ External Keyboard | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `J` | `row_next` | `swipe_up` within scrollable list | `swipe_up` OR `J` key | `J` key | Swipe velocity MUST exceed 300 px/s to trigger row advance; slower swipe = scroll. |
| `K` | `row_prev` | `swipe_down` within scrollable list | `swipe_down` OR `K` key | `K` key | Mirror of `J`. Focus ring moves one row at a time regardless of swipe distance. |
| `Enter` (on focused row) | `open_peek` | `tap` row | `tap` row or `Enter` | `Enter` | Tap triggers full-screen peek on mobile; 72%-overlay on tablet; 480px peek on desktop. |
| `Escape` | `close_overlay` | `bottom_sheet_drag_down` OR `back_gesture_android_hardware_back` OR tap backdrop | Same as mobile, or `Escape` | `Escape` | On iOS, `back_gesture_ios_edge_swipe` is reserved by the OS for WebView history navigation and MUST NOT be reassigned; use swipe-down-on-drag-handle instead. |
| `Cmd+K` | `open_command_palette` | **Bottom-sheet palette**: tap Search Bar icon (magnifying glass) in top nav → bottom sheet with search input + results list | Tap Search Bar icon → bottom-sheet palette | `Cmd+K` | On mobile the palette is a bottom sheet (not a centered modal), 85% viewport height, with keyboard auto-focused. Close via swipe-down on drag handle or `Escape` (tablet w/ external keyboard). |
| `Cmd+/` or `?` | `show_shortcut_overlay` | Long-press any nav item → action sheet with "Show gestures" | Long-press nav item or `?` | `?` | The gesture overlay on mobile shows gesture cheatsheet (not keyboard cheatsheet). |
| `Cmd+\` | *toggle sidebar* | N/A (sidebar is always-hamburger on mobile) | Tap hamburger or `Cmd+\` | `Cmd+\` | Sidebar hamburger on mobile replaces toggle; no gesture equivalent. |
| `L` | `inline_edit` | `long_press` on cell (≥500ms) | `long_press` or `L` key | `L` | Long-press opens inline editor; haptic feedback on press-and-hold threshold. |
| `Shift+Click` | `range_select` | `long_press` first row → tap last row (visual anchor shown) | Same or `Shift+Tap` w/ keyboard | `Shift+Tap` | Long-press-to-anchor pattern; subsequent taps extend range. See §3.10.3. |
| `Cmd+A` | `select_all` | Long-press any row → action sheet → "Select all matching filter" | Same or `Cmd+A` | `Cmd+A` | Respects the §3.10.4 10,000-row cap. |
| `D` (delete) | `delete_selection` | `swipe_left` on row → Delete action button revealed | `swipe_left` or `D` | `D` | Swipe threshold 50% viewport width to reveal; further swipe auto-triggers with haptic warning. |
| `Cmd+Enter` | `submit_form` | Tap the pinned "Submit" / "Send" button (always visible above virtual keyboard) | Tap or `Cmd+Enter` | `Cmd+Enter` | Button MUST remain pinned above the virtual keyboard via `position: sticky; bottom: env(keyboard-inset-height)`. |

| `Cmd+.` | `advance_phase` | Top-right "Advance" button in workspace header (only when gate conditions met) | Tap or `Cmd+.` | `Cmd+.` | Button disabled with tooltip/sheet when gate conditions unmet. |
| Console switch | `switch_console` | Tap console-switch button in top nav | Tap or `Cmd+K` → "Switch to Seller/Buyer Console" | Same | Cross-console firewall still enforced (§7). |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | *Form field nav* | Virtual-keyboard "Next" / "Previous" chevron buttons | Same or `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` | `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` | iOS exposes `inputAccessoryView`; Android exposes `imeOptions=actionNext`. |
| `Cmd+[` / `Cmd+]` (peek prev/next) | `side_peek_navigation_direction` | In full-screen peek: `swipe_right` (prev) / `swipe_left` (next) with 100px edge-drag threshold | Same or `Cmd+[`/`Cmd+]` | `Cmd+[`/`Cmd+]` | Edge-drag must originate ≥24px inside the viewport to avoid collision with iOS back-gesture. |

### 38.7.2 5-Tap Ceiling — Normative Definition & Enforcement {#38.7.2-5-tap-ceiling}

**Definition.** A "tap" is a discrete touch-down-to-release interaction on an interactive target that transitions the user forward in a workflow. The following interactions are counted AS taps: tapping a button, link, row, cell, pill, chip, icon, or action-sheet item. The following interactions are NOT counted: scrolling, pinch-zoom, keyboard entry (virtual or physical), gesture dismissals (swipe-down to close, back-gesture), focus transitions (Tab, virtual-keyboard Next/Prev chevron), and long-press-to-reveal (the long-press itself is not a tap; the subsequent action-sheet selection IS a tap). `pull_to_refresh` is a gesture and NOT a tap.

**5-Tap Ceiling.** Every major workflow (enumerated in §38.8.4) MUST complete in ≤5 taps on `mobile_xs` and `mobile_sm`, starting from a pre-authenticated entry point (Dashboard or Inbox). Text entry within the workflow does not count against the ceiling but MUST NOT exceed the content-appropriate field (e.g., comment body is free, boolean response toggle is one tap).

**Destructive-action exception.** Workflows whose final step is destructive (delete requirement, withdraw EOI, disqualify vendor) MAY exceed the ceiling by one tap for the confirmation dialog, capping at 6 taps. Destructive workflows MUST be tracked separately in the Feature Parity Matrix (§38.8) with a `destructive_exception=true` annotation.

**Ceiling-breach handling.** The `tap_count_probe` CI job (see §38.7.4) simulates each top-20 workflow and fails the build on any breach. A runtime telemetry probe (`ui_mobile_tap_count_probe_exceeded`, Appendix G) also fires on observed production sessions where the instrumented workflow exceeds the ceiling, with `workflow_kind`, `observed_taps`, `ceiling`, `user_agent_class` — used to catch regressions from component refactors that escaped the CI gate.

### 38.7.3 Gesture Safety, Conflicts & Edge Cases {#38.7.3-gesture-safety}

| Condition | Gesture Rule |
| :---- | :---- |
| iOS edge-swipe back-gesture conflict | Swipe-right gestures used for peek-prev MUST originate ≥24px inside viewport left edge. Targets within the 24px safe-area absorb only WebKit's native back-gesture. Enforced by touch-start origin filter. |
| Android hardware/gesture back | Maps to `Escape`/`close_overlay`. On stacked overlays (peek within modal within bottom-sheet), closes one at a time, top-down. System default. |
| Accidental swipe during scroll | Swipe velocity thresholds: < 300 px/s → scroll only; ≥ 300 px/s on horizontal swipe → swipe-action candidate; ≥ 50% viewport horizontal distance → commit. Below commit threshold, snaps back. |
| Long-press on interactive elements | 500ms hold + haptic feedback at threshold + 60% opacity dim on target. Cancellation: release before 500ms or finger drift > 10px cancels. |
| Pull-to-refresh on non-refreshable surfaces | Only enabled on surfaces whose data model supports refresh (Dashboard, Inbox, Workspace Overview, Bid Workspace). Otherwise `pull_to_refresh` gesture is consumed by natural bounce without action. |
| Two-finger-tap on Scoring Matrix | Reserved to show cell popover details instead of committing a score (per UX Summary §9.7); prevents accidental score changes on pinch-misfire. |
| `pinch_zoom` on Scoring Matrix | Disabled via `touch-action: manipulation` CSS per UX Summary §9.7 to prevent accidental grid-zoom during collaborative scoring. |
| Virtual keyboard obscures Submit button | `position: sticky; bottom: env(keyboard-inset-height)` or iOS `interactive-widget=resizes-content` viewport meta. Submit MUST remain visible. |
| Gesture within a full-screen peek | Prev/next gestures consume horizontal swipe; vertical swipe remains scroll. Close via drag-down on header drag-handle (40×6px bar at top of peek); drag threshold 30% viewport height. |
| Rapid back-to-back taps (double-tap) | Default: treated as two distinct taps (e.g., double-confirm a button). Exception: score pills implement debounce (250ms) to prevent double-submit. |
| Keyboard-driven devices (iPad with Magic Keyboard, Surface) on `tablet` tier | Keyboard shortcuts activated; gesture equivalents still present; either path leads to the same target. Detection via `matchMedia('(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)')` + keyboard-event listener. |
| `prefers-reduced-motion` | Transitions that would normally animate (peek open/close, bottom-sheet slide) render instantly; gestures still trigger the transition, only visual motion suppressed. |
| Accessibility assistive-touch / Voice Control | Long-press and gesture primitives MUST have tap-only fallbacks exposed via explicit buttons (e.g., a visible "⋯" overflow button beside swipe-action targets). |
| Cursor Presence gestures | Not user-gestures; presence renders passively per §3.9. Mobile shows static avatar strip, no live cursor animations. |

### 38.7.4 Tap-Count Probe Test Harness {#38.7.4-tap-count-probe-test-harness}

**Tooling.** Playwright + Appium + `@sourcera/tap-probe` in-house test library. The harness boots a clean signed-in session, navigates to a defined entry point, and executes the workflow via simulated taps, asserting the tap count against the ceiling. Each workflow has a fixture file declaring: `entry_point`, `expected_taps_max`, `destructive_exception_boolean`, `step_sequence[]` (each step: gesture, selector, expected state change).

**Execution cadence.**

- **Pre-merge** on every PR touching files under `/src/mobile`, `/src/ui/components/**/*Mobile*`, `/src/ui/hooks/useBreakpoint.ts`, or `/src/ui/layout/**`. Blocks merge on failure.
- **Nightly full-sweep** against top-20 workflows on all three device classes (iOS Safari, Chrome Android, Samsung Internet), two tiers (`mobile_xs` @ 375×667, `mobile_sm` @ 720×1280), two orientations.
- **Release gate** immediately before a production cut; full matrix plus tablet tier.

**Artifacts.** On failure, the harness saves: full video recording of the run, tap-by-tap screenshot series, DOM snapshot per step, observed vs. expected tap count, and a JSON diff of step deviation. Uploaded to the `responsive_tier_conformance` dashboard (§50.14.3).

**Runtime companion.** Production sessions emit `ui_mobile_workflow_tap_sequence` events for the top-20 workflows, tagged with `workflow_kind` (enum `tap_count_probe_workflow_kind`), `tap_count`, `completed ∈ {true, false}`, `device_class`. Aggregated daily into a p50 / p95 / p99 tap-count time series; alert fires if p95 > ceiling for 3 consecutive days.

### 38.7.5 Error Codes {#38.7.5-gesture-error-codes}

The following error codes are registered in Appendix I (§38.7 additions) to harden the contract:

- `gesture_out_of_safe_area` (HTTP 422) — touch-start origin within iOS back-gesture safe area; gesture absorbed; no user-visible error, telemetry only.
- `mobile_command_palette_hydration_forbidden` (HTTP 500) — Command Palette rendered on `mobile_xs`/`mobile_sm`; SSR defect; Sentry alert + auto-close.
- `tap_count_probe_ceiling_breach` (CI only, exit code 42) — tap-count probe exceeded ceiling.
- `mobile_ops_console_write_attempted` (HTTP 403) — write against Ops Console from `mobile_xs`/`mobile_sm` session; redirects to `/ops/mobile-unsupported`.

### 38.7.6 Acceptance Criteria {#38.7.6-gesture-acceptance-criteria}

1. Every §3.7 keyboard shortcut MUST have a row in the §38.7.1 translation table and MUST map to exactly one `mobile_keyboard_shortcut_target` enum value.
2. `J`/`K` keyboard navigation MUST translate to `swipe_up`/`swipe_down` with the 300 px/s velocity threshold; low-velocity swipes MUST remain scroll and not advance focus.
3. `Cmd+K` MUST render as a bottom-sheet palette on `mobile_xs`/`mobile_sm`, 85% viewport height, with the search input auto-focused and the virtual keyboard auto-shown.
4. Side Peek MUST render as a full-screen modal on `mobile_xs`/`mobile_sm` and as a 72%-overlay on `tablet`; dismiss via drag-down on header handle (30% viewport-height threshold) or Android hardware back.
5. The 5-tap ceiling MUST be enforced in CI via `tap_count_probe` job against the top-20 workflows in §38.8.4 on every qualifying PR; ceiling breach blocks merge.
6. Production runtime probe MUST emit `ui_mobile_workflow_tap_sequence` for each top-20 workflow completion; p95 alert fires if ceiling exceeded for 3 consecutive days.
7. iOS back-gesture safe-area (24px left edge) MUST NOT register custom swipe-right gestures; all peek-prev handlers MUST filter touch-start origin.
8. Gesture equivalents MUST coexist with external-keyboard shortcuts on `tablet` tier; either input path leads to the same `mobile_keyboard_shortcut_target` action and the same analytics event.
9. Destructive-action workflows MUST NOT exceed 6 taps on mobile (ceiling + 1 for confirmation); `destructive_exception=true` flag MUST be set in the workflow fixture.
10. Virtual keyboard MUST NOT obscure the Submit/Send CTA; sticky-positioning or `interactive-widget=resizes-content` MUST preserve CTA visibility on iOS 16.4+ and Android 13+.
11. `prefers-reduced-motion` MUST suppress gesture animation while preserving gesture recognition; transitions render instantly.
12. Assistive Touch / Voice Control users MUST have a non-gesture fallback (explicit visible button) for every swipe-action or long-press-action surface.

**Failure Modes (counterfactual coverage).**

- *iOS WebKit edge-swipe back hijacks peek-prev gesture:* Safe-area filter MUST be tested on iOS 16, 17, and 18 WebKit; regression suite includes a fixture that triggers both the safe-area-absorbed swipe and the safe-area-clear swipe.
- *Low-velocity swipe accidentally advances row:* 300 px/s threshold empirically validated; tested with iOS scroll-physics momentum to ensure no false positives from inertial scroll.
- *Bottom-sheet palette obscures row detail on mobile landscape:* 85% viewport height leaves 15% (~80px) of background visible even on shortest landscape device; verified on iPhone SE landscape (375×667 rotated → 667×375).
- *Double-tap interpreted as gesture vs. two separate taps:* System debounce on score pills (250ms) prevents double-submit; other buttons treat as two discrete taps per spec.
- *Accessibility user cannot long-press (no motor-control for sustained press):* Explicit "⋯" overflow buttons exposed on every swipe-action / long-press-action surface provide full tap-only access.
- *Virtual-keyboard-inset-height unsupported on old Android WebView:* Fallback uses `resize` event + bottom offset of `max(0, keyboard_height_via_ime_callback)`; graceful degradation.
- *External Bluetooth keyboard paired mid-session on `mobile_sm`:* Keyboard-event listener upgrades the session to accept shortcuts; gesture equivalents remain active; tested via hotplug simulation in Appium.
- *Prefers-reduced-motion user experiences broken gesture feedback:* Haptic feedback MAY continue when motion is suppressed; visual dimming on long-press still renders (static, no fade); gesture completion communicates via haptic + instant state change.

## 38.8 Mobile Feature Parity Matrix {#38.8-mobile-feature-parity-matrix}

**Purpose (C.114).** §38.4 ("Mobile Feature Parity") is a prose summary of which features work on mobile. §38.8 is the structured, enum-bound, per-feature authoritative matrix that governs engineering acceptance, QA test plans, release gates, and user-facing capability messaging. Every feature in the Sourcera product surface MUST have a row in this matrix. Any feature without a row is presumed `not_supported` on mobile and MUST NOT leak a code path on mobile devices.

**Enum.** `mobile_feature_parity_status` (Appendix J): `parity`, `supported`, `simplified`, `not_supported`.

**Status Definitions.**

- `parity` — Feature behaves identically to desktop at the interaction and capability level. Tier-appropriate touch-target sizing and layout reflow per §38.6 are expected and do not demote the status.
- `supported` — Feature available with mobile-specific UX patterns (e.g., Command Palette replaced by bottom-sheet palette). Functional capability is equivalent; the UX is different.
- `simplified` — Reduced capability surface. Some sub-features or modes are unavailable on mobile; the user can still complete a meaningful portion of the workflow. Simplification MUST be enumerated in the row's Notes column.
- `not_supported` — Feature unavailable on mobile. User attempting access receives an informational surface ("[Feature] is best experienced on desktop. Continue on your computer or dismiss.") with a `dismiss` option where the fallback workflow makes sense, or a hard redirect where it does not.

### 38.8.1 Cross-Tier Transition Contract {#38.8.1-cross-tier-transition-contract}

When a feature's rendering component crosses a breakpoint tier mid-interaction (e.g., user drags browser from `desktop` to `tablet` while a peek is open), the component MUST:

1. Preserve all form state (React state or equivalent).
2. Reflow to the new tier's layout per §38.6.2 within one animation frame.
3. Preserve scroll position within the content panel.
4. Preserve keyboard/screen-reader focus.
5. Emit `ui_responsive_tier_component_reflowed` with `component_id`, `from_tier`, `to_tier`, `preserved_state_bytes`.

Any component that fails to preserve state across a tier transition is a Priority-1 regression.

### 38.8.3 Simplification Disclosure Contract {#38.8.3-simplification-disclosure-contract}

Features in `simplified` or `not_supported` state MUST disclose the limitation to the user at the point of interaction, not hide it silently. The disclosure surface MUST be one of:

| Status | Disclosure Pattern |
| :---- | :---- |
| `simplified` | **Informational chip** at the top of the mobile feature surface: "Some features are simplified on mobile. Open on desktop to access: [list]." Dismissible per session. |
| `not_supported` (redirect permitted) | **Redirect banner** with continue/dismiss: "[Feature] is best experienced on desktop. [Continue on Desktop] [Dismiss]" — see §38.4 existing pattern. |
| `not_supported` (hard block) | **Hard redirect** to the `/:console/mobile-unsupported` informational page with deep-link preservation; Ops Console surfaces use this. |

### 38.8.4 Top-20 Workflows for Tap-Count Probe {#38.8.4-top-20-workflows-for-tap-count-probe}

The `tap_count_probe` CI job (§38.7.4) MUST run against these 20 workflows. Each workflow's ceiling is declared here; breaches block merge.

| # | `tap_count_probe_workflow_kind` | Workflow | Entry Point | Ceiling | Destructive Exception | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | `buyer_open_workspace_from_dashboard` | Open a specific Workspace from the Dashboard | Buyer Dashboard | 2 | no | 1 tap Workspace card → 1 tap confirm (auto-navigate). |

### 38.8.5 Release-Gate Rule {#38.8.5-release-gate-rule}

No Sourcera production release MAY ship if any of the following is true:

1. `tap_count_probe` CI job failing against ≥1 of the 20 workflows at `mobile_xs` or `mobile_sm` tier.
2. `feature_parity_matrix_completeness` CI job failing (a new feature was added without a matrix row).
3. Runtime p95 tap-count for any top-20 workflow has exceeded its ceiling for 3 consecutive days on the production canary cohort.
4. `responsive_conformance_suite` failing at any of the 5 canonical widths (375, 720, 820, 1200, 1440 px).
5. Any route in `/ops/*` serving HTTP 200 to a `mobile_xs` or `mobile_sm` write request (Ops Console must return 302 redirect).

Release-gate failures block merge to `release/*` branches until resolved.

### 38.8.6 Acceptance Criteria {#38.8.6-mobile-parity-matrix-acceptance-criteria}

1. Every feature in §11–§51 (including all §48 growth mechanics) MUST have exactly one row in the §38.8.2 matrix with a valid `mobile_feature_parity_status` value.
2. `feature_parity_matrix_completeness` CI job MUST scan the spec for feature-introducing sections and fail if any is missing a row.
3. Every row with status `simplified` MUST have a Notes column explaining what is simplified; empty Notes on `simplified` rows is a CI failure.
4. Every row with status `not_supported` MUST either redirect to desktop via the §38.8.3 banner pattern or hard-redirect per §38.8.3; silent no-op on tap is a bug.
5. Cross-tier component transitions (tier boundary crossed mid-interaction) MUST preserve form state, scroll position, and focus per §38.8.1 — verified by `cross_tier_preservation` E2E test.
6. The tap-count probe MUST run against every one of the 20 workflows in §38.8.4 on every qualifying PR and on nightly full-sweep; ceiling breach blocks merge.
7. The runtime probe (`ui_mobile_workflow_tap_sequence`) MUST fire at 100% sample rate for the top-20 workflows on mobile sessions; non-top-20 workflows MAY sample at 10%.
8. Destructive-exception workflows MUST NOT exceed 6 taps; `destructive_exception=true` MUST be set in fixtures and the runtime-probe event.
9. Simplification disclosure chip (§38.8.3) MUST render on first entry to any `simplified` feature per session; dismiss persists for session only.
10. Release gate (§38.8.5) MUST block merges to `release/*` branches on any of the five failure conditions; Ops gate override requires `ops_platform_admin` role + documented justification in the audit log.

**Failure Modes (counterfactual coverage).**

- *New feature merges without a matrix row:* `feature_parity_matrix_completeness` CI job scans for `## N.` feature-introducing headings and cross-checks against matrix rows; absence blocks merge.
- *`simplified` row misses Notes column:* Lint rule in `spec_matrix_lint` (a separate §38.8.2-specific lint suite from `feature_parity_matrix_completeness`; the completeness job asserts every feature has a row, the `spec_matrix_lint` suite asserts per-row invariants including Notes-non-empty on `simplified`, `destructive_exception` boolean presence on top-20 destructive entries, and enum-value validity per §38.8 `mobile_feature_parity_status`) enforces non-empty Notes when status = `simplified`. Both jobs run in the same CI stage and both block merge independently.
- *User reaches a `not_supported` surface via deep link and sees blank page:* Every `not_supported` surface MUST register a mobile-fallback route that renders the §38.8.3 banner or redirect; `mobile_unsupported_surface_test` E2E verifies no 404 leakage.
- *Tap-count probe false-positive from flaky selector:* Probe runs 3× retries with element-ready waits; failure reported only on 3× consecutive breach.
- *Runtime p95 alert fires in the middle of a campaign that legitimately drove new users to hit a complex workflow:* Alert has `cohort_context` annotation support; Ops can acknowledge with rationale without suppressing the alert class.
- *Tier-transition component reflow loses unsaved comment:* React state preservation verified by `cross_tier_preservation` E2E; reflow that loses bytes is a P1 regression per §38.8.1.
- *Mobile release ships with one of the release-gate conditions bypassed accidentally:* The gate is enforced at the CI layer via the `release_gate_assert` job; manual bypass requires `ops_platform_admin` + audit-log-documented justification (not bypassable by developer role).
- *Matrix row says `parity` but component has hover-only tooltip that fails silently on mobile:* Acceptance Criteria #5 + the `responsive_conformance_suite` catch this; rows claiming `parity` must pass conformance at all 5 widths.

## 38.9 Print Stylesheet Behavior {#38.9-print-stylesheet-behavior}

Pointer subsection. The `@media print` stylesheet forces every console surface to the `desktop` responsive tier (per §38.6.1) for layout purposes regardless of the rendering viewport: sidebar and navigation are hidden, side peek panels expand inline, all content reflows to a single linear column, page breaks are inserted between top-level cards (`break-inside: avoid` on cards, `break-after: page` on H1 headings), and color is preserved with `-webkit-print-color-adjust: exact`. Body citations of "§38.9" point at this contract. Tier-rules-by-tier behavior is otherwise authored at §38.6.

## 38.10 Reduced-Motion & Accessibility Tier Overrides {#38.10-reduced-motion-and-accessibility-tier-overrides}

Pointer subsection. The `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` media query suppresses the §3.9 motion catalog (transitions ≤ 80 ms or none); the `prefers-contrast: more` query swaps neutral-surface tokens for higher-contrast variants per §3.11.2. The §50.17.4 token-drift CI gate verifies that every responsive token has a high-contrast equivalent. No body section MAY author its own reduced-motion override; the §38.10 contract is universal.

## 38.11 Right-to-Left & Locale Mirror Behavior {#38.11-right-to-left-and-locale-mirror-behavior}

Pointer subsection. RTL locale rendering inverts: layout direction (`dir="rtl"`), icon orientation for directional icons (chevrons, breadcrumb separators, drag handles), and number alignment (right-aligned in tables for LTR, left-aligned for RTL). Non-directional icons (gear, search, plus) are NOT mirrored. Implementation lives in the `useDirectionality()` hook; tier-by-tier RTL conformance tests run inside `responsive_conformance_suite` (§38.8.5).

## 38.12 Presence Avatar Stack Component {#38.12-presence-avatar-stack-component}

The `PresenceAvatarStack` component renders the Convex Presence subsystem's collaborator-avatars (§3.9 cursor primitives + Convex Presence) as a horizontally-stacked, depth-overlapped avatar list with collision remediation. Up to 4 visible avatars; beyond 4, the stack collapses to a "+N more" affordance; hovering the affordance opens a dropdown enumerating the additional collaborators. Collision behavior on narrow viewports (§38.6.1 `mobile_xs`, `mobile_sm`) reduces the visible count to 2 and renders the "+N more" affordance more aggressively.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Stack MUST render at most 4 avatars on `desktop` / `tablet`, at most 2 on `mobile_*` per §38.6.1.
2. Beyond the visible count, the "+N more" affordance MUST surface; the dropdown lists every additional collaborator with avatar + name + last-seen timestamp.
3. Avatar rendering MUST satisfy the §3.11 contrast tokens (token drift checked by `ux_token_drift_check` per §50.17.4).
4. Presence updates MUST satisfy the §44.1 reactive-query latency budget (p95 ≤ 500 ms commit-to-render).

# 40\. Data Export & Import {#40.-data-export-&-import}

## 40.1 Export Formats {#40.1-export-formats}

| Format | Contents | Availability |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **CSV** | Requirements, responses, scoring matrix, plan tier breakdown | All plans |
| **PDF** | Selection Report (executive summary \+ full scorecard) | All plans |
| **Excel** | Multi-sheet workbook (Requirements, Vendors, Scores, Comments, Traceability Matrix if applicable). Includes formulas for score aggregation | All paid tiers (Starter / Growth / Scale / Enterprise per §34.1.1 cell **Export Formats**) |
| **JSON** | Complete workspace snapshot (all entities, relationships, audit metadata) | All paid tiers via read-only API; full export on Enterprise (per §34.1.1 cell **Export Formats**) |

### Additional Export Types

- **Traceability Matrix:** Standalone CSV/Excel of requirement ↔ framework control mappings (Policy Ingestion only).  
- **Scenario Export:** Scenario name, parameters, summary, and optional score snapshot. JSON or Excel.  
- **Intelligence Briefing:** JSON (raw) or PDF (formatted). Via Settings → Data & Privacy or API.  
- **Audit Export:** All audit events for a workspace (CSV/JSON). Enterprise only.

## 40.2 Data Retention & Deletion {#40.2-data-retention-&-deletion}

**Authoring note (V9 remediation, 2026-05-09 — closes D-9.1R-001 / D-9.1R-002 / D-9.1R-003 / D-9.1R-007 / D-9.1R-014 / D-9.1R-016 / D-9.1R-020 / D-9.1R-021 / D-9.1R-024 P0/P1; ASCII-renaming amendment 2026-05-11 — closes D-11.3-009).** §40.2 is the canonical authoritative home for entity retention TTLs (per Authoring Convention #10). Entity field tables in §4 cite §40.2 by reference; inline numerical retention literals outside §40.2 / §6.8 / §34 fail CI gate `retention_singleton_section_40_2_canonical` (Appendix M.5 — V9 row; renamed in V11 from `retention_singleton_§40.2_canonical` per ASCII-identifier convention per D-11.3-009; runtime status `spec_binding_pending_pack_m02_3` per §M.5.5). New §4 entity table additions trigger `entity_retention_coverage_on_diff` (Appendix M.5 — V9 row) which asserts a corresponding §40.2 row exists for every new or renamed entity.

| Condition | Retention |
| :---- | :---- |
| Deleted workspace (soft delete) | **30 days, then permanent purge — with explicit cascade matrix (V9 remediation, closes D-9.1R-020).** Child entities purged with the workspace: Use Case (§4.3.3), Requirement (§4.3.4), Response (§4.3.5), Score (§4.3.6) when not cited in finalized Selection Report, Intelligence Cache Entry (§4.3.7), Evaluation Scenario (§4.3.8), Pulse Event (§4.3.10) past 90-day pulse-history dashboard window, Internal Comment Thread / Post / Mention (§4.3.11–§4.3.13) per parent-cascade row, Presence Record (§4.3.14) ephemeral, Unread Marker (§4.3.15), Target Account (§4.3.20), Selection Report Draft (§4.3.21) when not finalized, Inbox Item Group (§4.3.22), InboxItem (§4.3.22.1), WorkspacePulseHealth (§4.3.22.2), TCO Model (§4.3.28) when not cited in finalized Selection Report / Selection Record evidence. Child entities **retained beyond workspace purge** by their own §40.2 row: Console Bridge Event (financial / operational classes both outlive parent workspace per row below), AIOperation (7y financial), AuditEvent (7y financial), Score and Selection Report when finalized (Workspace-life + 7y per row 6 / Selection-Report-finalized row), Buyer Referral / Pro Trial Seat Grant financial fields, Usage Event aggregates, Time-Saved Credit aggregates, OutcomeContract (life-of-platform). `Workspace.archived_at` is the anchor for archive-retention math after a Workspace enters `status=archived`; `deleted_at` remains the soft-delete processing anchor. |
| Workspace cancellation grace + processing window (§10.14) | **14-day undo grace + 30-day processing/recovery window = 44 days from cancellation initiation.** During Days 0-14, the Workspace remains recoverable by the Workspace Owner. During Days 14-44, deletion processing and retained-entity partitioning execute per §10.14.4. After Day 44, the Workspace row is permanently deleted unless a retention exemption row in this §40.2 table applies to the child entity. §10.13 does not define a separate 30-day-from-closure purge window. |
| Response (§4.3.5) | Life of workspace; Workspace-life + 7y if cited in a finalized Selection Report (procurement-defensibility evidence). DSAR per §6.8 with body-field redaction sweep per §6.8.4.5 if response body contains subject-attributable free text. Residency: Workspace's `data_residency_region`. |
| Internal Comment Thread / Post / Mention (V9 split from former row 2 — closes D-9.1R-024) | Life of parent entity (Workspace / Use Case / Requirement / Response / Scenario / Selection Report draft). On parent soft-delete, cascade soft-delete + 30-day purge. **§6.8.5 row 6 exception:** Threads / Posts / Mentions linked to a finalized Selection Report or active legal hold retained Workspace-life + 7 years; cascade DSAR Pattern B per §6.8.4.1 + body sweep per §6.8.4.5. |
| Canceled subscription | **90 days for the workspace and customer-data scope, then purge — except for entities with a financial-class or audit-integrity-class retention exemption per §6.8.5 (notably AIOperation, AIWallet, ContestRecord, CommittedSpendContract, OutcomeContract, OpsActionRecord, AuditEvent, DSARRequest, NDA Record, MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord, BillingSeatSnapshot, BidSuccessShare, VerificationReviewRecord, Buyer Referral financial fields, Pro Trial Seat Grant financial fields, PromotedListing financial fields, FeaturedPlacement paid-commitment fields).** Exempt entities follow their own §40.2 row below; the 90-day workspace purge does not apply to them. V9 remediation closes D-9.1R-021 (overbroad pre-V9 row). |
| GDPR DSAR processing SLA (V9 reword — closes D-9.1R-016 entity-vs-processing-time misuse) | **Processing-time SLA only:** verified DSAR fulfillment follows the §6.8.6 fulfillment window from `verified_at`; cascade pause accounting follows §6.8.4.6; verification timing follows §6.8.6.1. **NOT entity retention** — DSARRequest entity retention is governed by the dedicated DSARRequest row below (7y per §6.8.5 audit-integrity exemption). |
| Deprovisioned user (SCIM) | Owned entities reassigned within 24 hours. User record retained but marked `deprovisioned`. |
| Internal Comment Thread / Post / Mention | Life of parent entity (Workspace / Use Case / Requirement / Response / Scenario / Selection Report draft). On parent soft-delete, cascade soft-delete + 30-day purge. |
| Q&A Thread / Post / Mention (§18.3.1) | Life of parent Workspace. On Workspace soft-delete, cascade soft-delete to Q&A Thread, Q&A Post, and Q&A Mention rows and purge after the 30-day processing window unless linked to finalized Selection Report / legal-hold evidence. On Workspace cancellation, follows §10.14 cancellation grace + processing window. DSAR Pattern B pseudonymizes `author_user_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `moderated_by`, and `mentioned_user_id`; body fields are swept per §6.8.4.5. Residency: inherited from Workspace `data_residency_region`; seller projections inherit Bid Workspace residency and carry only the §4.7.1 allowed field set. |
| Q&A Attachment (§18.5.2 / §4.6.2 owner_entity_type `qa_thread_post`) | Linked attachments inherit parent Q&A Post retention and purge with the parent post after the 30-day cascade window. Presigned orphan uploads purge after 24 hours per §4.6.2. Malware-positive binaries purge immediately while metadata follows §4.6.2 forensic-retention rules. DSAR binary detach follows §4.6.2 Attachment within 72 hours, with Q&A Post body links redacted in the same DSAR cascade. |
| Presence Record | Ephemeral (Convex session). Evicted 60s after last heartbeat or on explicit disconnect. Never written to cold storage. Not subject to DSAR export. Excluded from round-trip fidelity per §40.4. |
| Unread Marker | Purged 30 days after parent thread hard-delete **or** 30 days after user loses Workspace Membership, whichever fires first. Org-delete cascade per 90-day rule above. |
| InboxItem (§4.3.22.1) | Visible / read items retained for the life of the recipient's active Org membership unless an earlier `expires_at` applies. Dismissed, expired, or archived items purge after the grouped-inbox retention boundary that applies to their `expires_at` class, unless linked to an audit-retained source event. On Workspace hard-delete, Workspace-linked InboxItems purge with the Workspace after the 30-day soft-delete window; Org-level items follow Org membership. DSAR Pattern B pseudonymizes actor and recipient FKs; title / description body sweep per §6.8.4.5. |
| WorkspacePulseHealth (§4.3.22.2) | Daily raw rows retained 12 weeks for dashboard trend and digest archive. At 12 weeks, raw `raw_inputs_json` is purged and weekly aggregate score / color-band summaries are retained for Workspace life; finalized Phase-12 locked rows retained Workspace-life + 7 years when cited by Selection Report / Selection Record evidence. DSAR Pattern B on actor FKs; raw input counts carry no subject text by construction. |

## 40.3 Data Import {#40.3-data-import}

Enterprise customers receive assisted data import from existing procurement tools. Supported source formats: CSV, Excel, JSON.

**Process:**

1. Customer provides source data export.  
2. Import consultant maps source schema to Sourcera schema.  
3. Test import run. Customer reviews mappings and reconciles conflicts.  
4. Production import. Verification run. Audit log generated.

Typically 2-4 weeks. Sourcera does not modify source data; mapping is customer responsibility.

## 40.4 Import Round-Trip Fidelity {#40.4-import-round-trip-fidelity}

**Tested Guarantee:** A workspace exported to JSON and re-imported produces equivalent entities. Equivalence defined as:

- All requirement fields match exactly.  
- All vendor/target account mappings preserved.  
- All response text preserved (formatting may normalize).  
- Audit trail fields retained (timestamps, user IDs).  
- Internal relationships (Use Case ↔ Requirement, Requirement ↔ Response) preserved.

**Lost in Round-Trip:**

- Real-time presence indicators (last login, active sessions).  
- Transient Agent task states (in-progress Pre-Scoring operations).  
- WebSocket subscription state.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- Round-trip test suite (sample workspaces exported → re-imported → validated).  
- Passes as part of regular QA for each release.  
- JSON import format documented for Enterprise customers.

## 40.5 Acceptance Criteria {#40.5-acceptance-criteria}

- All export formats complete within 30 seconds for workspaces with ≤ 10,000 requirements.  
- JSON export includes complete audit metadata.  
- Traceability Matrix export includes framework control mapping.  
- Import process preserves all entity relationships and timestamps.  
- Round-trip fidelity tested quarterly.

| **Feature Announcement** | feature\_announcement.hbs | New feature: \[Feature Name\] | [marketing@sourcera.io](mailto:marketing@sourcera.io) | Marketing | New feature released. Sent to opted-in users. Unsubscribe in footer. |
| **Webinar Invitation** | webinar\_invitation.hbs | Join us: \[Webinar Title\] on \[Date\] | [marketing@sourcera.io](mailto:marketing@sourcera.io) | Marketing | Webinar scheduled. Sent to opted-in users. |
| **Weekly Digest** | weekly\_digest.hbs | Your Sourcera Pulse digest | [noreply@sourcera.io](mailto:noreply@sourcera.io) | Lifecycle | Weekly. Configurable frequency. Includes workspace status, SLAs, scores. |

## 41.3 Email Compliance {#41.3-email-compliance}

- **CAN-SPAM:** Unsubscribe link \+ physical address (sourcera.io footer) in all emails.  
- **GDPR:** Transactional emails not subject to marketing consent. Marketing requires explicit opt-in. Transactional email address (`noreply@sourcera.io`) not used for marketing.  
- **CASL:** Same as GDPR (implied consent for transactional, explicit for marketing).  
- **Bounce Rate Target:** \< 2%.  
- **Complaint Rate Target:** \< 0.5%.  
- **Deliverability Monitoring:** Sent emails \> 100/day. Spam trap monitoring. List hygiene (bounce management, complaint handling).

## 41.4 Opt-Out Classification {#41.4-opt-out-classification}

| Email Type | Opt-Out Classification | Enforcement |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Vendor Invitation, NDA, Q\&A, Response notifications, Phase advancement, SLA alerts, Comment mentions, Selection Report, Disqualification, EOI received, Workspace invitation, GDPR notifications | **Transactional (No opt-out)** | Sent regardless of preference. Cannot unsubscribe. |
| Trial expiring, plan downgrade warning | **Transactional-Critical** | Sent regardless of preference for account/billing changes. |
| Weekly Digest, feature announcements, webinar invitations | **Marketing/Lifecycle (Opt-in)** | Require explicit opt-in. Unsubscribe link in footer. User preference honored. |

## 41.5 Acceptance Criteria {#41.5-acceptance-criteria}

- All email templates have preview URL for QA review.  
- All transactional emails delivered within 60 seconds of trigger.  
- All marketing emails respect user opt-out preference.  
- Weekly digest emails include unsubscribe link in header and footer.  
- Bounce and complaint rates monitored weekly via Loops.so dashboard.  
- No transactional emails sent from marketing sender address.

# 42\. Observability, Reliability & Disaster Recovery {#42.-observability,-reliability-&-disaster-recovery}

## 42.1 SLA Commitments {#42.1-sla-commitments}

Customer-contract SLAs are gated per §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 cell **SLA**. This subsection restates the operational measurement approach; per-tier SLA values are sourced from §34.1 — NO numeric value is inline-duplicated (Phase V12 closure: D-42-018).

| Plan tier (per §34.1) | Uptime SLA source | Response Time SLA source | Severities Covered |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Free | §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 cell **SLA** | None (best effort) | N/A |
| Solo (`buyer_solo` / `seller_solo`) | §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 cell **SLA** | Best effort; per-evaluation refund window per §34.2.5 | N/A (operational only) |
| Starter | §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 cell **SLA** | Best effort | N/A |
| Growth | §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 cell **SLA** | Best effort | N/A |
| Scale | §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 cell **SLA** | Best effort | N/A |
| Enterprise | §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 cell **SLA** (Authoritative) | §34.1 cell **SLA** (BPS §6; SPS §8) | All severities (SEV-1 / SEV-2 / SEV-3) |

The customer-reported critical response SLA on Enterprise applies to tickets opened via the §29.9 Support Widget or the dedicated CSM channel. Internal incident-response thresholds (page-on-call, war-room open, ack-time targets) live in §42.2 (alerting) and §42.3 (severity ladder); those are operational targets, NOT customer SLAs, and are tighter than the customer SLA by design. CI gate `plan_tier_sla_single_source` (Appendix M.5) asserts that no §42.1 cell inline-states a numeric SLA value outside §34.1.

**SLA Measurement.** Uptime is measured via synthetic monitoring (Datadog endpoint checks) every 60 seconds from 3+ geographies; aggregation window is calendar-monthly per §34.18.5 finance scorecard cadence. Per-endpoint latency targets are authoritative in §44.1 (FCP, TTI, API p95 / p99, real-time subscription, search index, PDF export, workspace load). §42.1 does NOT restate §44.1 latency thresholds.

**SLA breach customer notification.** Per §31 webhook contract: a new `sla.platform.uptime_breach` webhook event (Appendix C — V12 addition) fires to Enterprise customer subscribers when monthly uptime in the customer's residency partition falls below the §34.1 cell **SLA**. HMAC-SHA256 signed; idempotent via `event_id`; exponential backoff per Appendix F; DLQ after 5 failures; payload ≤ 256 KB.

## 42.3 Incident Response {#42.3-incident-response}

V12 remediation (2026-05-11; closes D-12V-001, D-12V-002, D-12V-003, D-12V-007, D-12V-008). §42.3 now carries the canonical Severity Ladder + Customer-Reported Incident Ingest + numbered Process with explicit actors + unified Postmortem Timeline.

### 42.3.0 Canonical Severity Ladder {#42.3.0-severity-ladder}

The canonical platform severity ladder. **All §42 / §43 / §50 references to incident severity MUST cite this table by anchor.** No alternate severity namespace is authoritative. CI gate `severity_ladder_single_source` (Appendix M.5 — V12 addition) greps the spec for non-canonical severity tokens (`SEV-N`, `Sev0`, `P0/P1` incident references) outside the cited authoritative anchors.

| Severity | Impact (customer-observable) | Detection-window trigger (per §42.6.0) | Response Time | Update Frequency | Customer Comms |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **P0 (Critical)** | Customer-visible primary surfaces blocked (Stripe degraded > 24h blocking auto-topups for > 50 Orgs; Convex unavailable; revenue-meter-event submission failing > 30 min); data loss | Immediate on customer-block detection OR persistent P1 > 4h | Page on-call < 5 min | Statuspage + Customer-Owner Inbox + every 30 min | Statuspage SEV-1 + per-Enterprise webhook |
| **P1 (Major)** | Service degraded for a single residency partition; revenue-affecting alarm fired; SLA breach imminent | Persistent P2 > 4h OR direct-fired by revenue alarm or DSAR cascade SLO breach | Page on-call < 15 min | Statuspage + every 60 min | Statuspage SEV-2 + per-Enterprise webhook |
| **P2 (Minor)** | Single service degraded with mitigation in place; perf-budget breach without customer-blocking effect | Persistent P3 > 30 min OR direct-fired by perf-budget alarm | Page on-call < 1 h | Internal-only #incident channel; every 4 h | In-app degraded banner per §42.4.3 (Service Degraded — non-residency variant); no Statuspage by default |
| **P3 (Investigative)** | Provider degraded with no customer impact; first-detection state for any provider-degraded detector | First-detection signal | Page on-call < 4 h | Internal-only #incident channel; daily | No customer comms; in-app banner only if customer-facing surface inherits the latency |

**Severity-namespace reconciliation.** The legacy `SEV-1 / SEV-2 / SEV-3` terminology used by some on-call language maps to `P1 / P2 / P3` respectively (no `SEV-0`; the criticality previously named `SEV-1 (Critical)` now maps to `P0` when customer-blocking and `P1` when single-region degraded). The retired §43.5.4 `Sev0 / Sev1 / Sev2 / Sev3` is deprecated; the §50.6.4 "P0/P1 incident" terminology aligns with this canonical ladder.

**Severity transitions.** Severity assignment may upgrade over time (per the §42.6.0 timer-based escalation: P3 → P2 at 30 min → P1 at 4h → P0 on customer-visible block) but never downgrades within a single incident lifetime; mitigation closes the incident, not downgrades.

### 42.3.0.A Customer-Reported Incident Ingest {#42.3.0-customer-reported-ingest}

Latency-only and other detector-blind failure modes (e.g., Anthropic MCP proxy returning 200s with elevated latency, no 5xx) are invisible to §42.6.0 detectors. Customer-reported escalation is the load-bearing detection route for these modes. V12 closure: D-12V-003.

**Ingest path.**

1. **Customer files a Zendesk ticket** via the §29.9 Support Widget OR the dedicated CSM channel. The ticket carries a customer-supplied severity tag from the `customer_reported_severity` enum (Appendix J — V12 addition): `critical`, `major`, `minor`, `cosmetic`.
2. **Zendesk Trigger** routes `critical`-tagged tickets to the Sourcera `incident_intake@sourcera.com` shared inbox AND fires a webhook to the §42.9 IncidentRecord API (`POST /api/v1/ops/incidents/intake`) with `intake_source = 'customer_reported'`, `customer_reported_severity = 'critical'`, `linked_zendesk_ticket_id`, `affected_org_id` (resolved from ticket-domain mapping).
3. **Auto-page** to the on-call PagerDuty queue fires within 5 min p95 of ticket creation when `customer_reported_severity = 'critical'`. Detector: `customer_reported_critical_intake`. PagerDuty incident severity is set to P1 (provisional); on-call primary may upgrade to P0 after triage.
4. **Major tag** routes to the on-call queue at PagerDuty P2 with a 15-min ack SLA. **Minor / cosmetic tags** route to support-rotation Slack channel only; no PagerDuty page.
5. **Manual escalation surface.** The Ops Console support widget renders a "Promote to Incident" button on every Zendesk ticket per §50.27 ACs; promotion creates an IncidentRecord (§42.9) with `intake_source = 'support_promoted'`.
6. **SLO.** `customer_reported_incident_ingest_latency_p95` < 5 min for `critical`-tag tickets; < 15 min for `major`-tag tickets. Datadog SLO object `customer_reported_critical_ingest_5m`. Breach raises P2 alarm.

**Acceptance criteria (§42.3.0.A).**

1. Every customer-filed Zendesk ticket with `customer_reported_severity ∈ {critical, major}` creates an IncidentRecord row within the SLO above. QA test: `customer_reported_intake_sla`.
2. `critical`-tag tickets auto-page on-call PagerDuty primary; no manual triage required. QA test: `customer_reported_critical_auto_page`.
3. Promotion-to-incident from Ops Console writes an `OpsActionRecord` with `action_kind = 'customer_report_promoted_to_incident'` (Appendix J — V12 addition). QA test: `customer_reported_promotion_ops_action_record`.
4. Ingest path is residency-partitioned: EU subject PII in the customer ticket body stays in EU Zendesk + EU IncidentRecord partition. QA test: `customer_reported_intake_residency_isolation`.
