| Marketplace seller permanent-ban appeal window | None (irreversible per §45.3) | n/a | Permanent bans are non-appealable; ban-record retention follows §40.2 audit-log rules |

### 42.3.2 Incident Response Process (V12 — Numbered with Actors) {#42.3.2-incident-response-process}

V12 remediation (closes D-12V-001). Every step names an explicit actor per the §50.3.1 canonical Ops Role Matrix; the process is testable end-to-end. The §25.6.2 inbound citation to "primary 5m → secondary 10m → manager 15m" three-step escalation is honored by §42.5 (V12-rewritten).

| Step | Actor | Trigger | Output | Audit |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1. Incident detected | `monitoring_subsystem` (Datadog detector OR Statuspage synthetic check) OR `customer_support_agent` (via §42.3.0.A intake) | Alarm threshold breach OR customer-report critical/major ticket | IncidentRecord row created with `intake_source` ∈ Appendix J `incident_intake_source_kind` | `incident.detected` (Appendix C — V12 add); PostHog `incident_opened` |
| 2. On-call paged | `monitoring_subsystem` (Datadog → PagerDuty integration) | Step 1 IncidentRecord created | PagerDuty incident at provisional severity per §42.3.0; on-call primary paged | `incident.paged` (Appendix C — V12 add) |
| 3. Severity assigned (initial) | `on_call_primary` (`ops_admin` on rotation per §42.5) | On-call ack within §42.3.0 response time | IncidentRecord `severity ∈ P0 / P1 / P2 / P3` set; `severity_assigned_by_user_id` populated | `incident.severity_assigned` |
| 4. War room opened | `on_call_primary` | P0 or P1 incident | War-room channel in Slack `#incident-{record_id}` + Zoom bridge URL; `war_room_channel_id` populated on IncidentRecord. Slack-fallback: if `workos_slack_app_unavailable` per §42.6.0, fallback to Microsoft Teams `#incident-{record_id}` channel per §42.6.3 (V12 fallback contract). | `incident.war_room_opened` |
| 5. Customer notified | `on_call_primary` OR `ops_admin` (delegated) | Per §42.3.0 Customer Comms column: P0 = Statuspage SEV-1 + Customer-Owner Inbox + Enterprise webhook; P1 = Statuspage SEV-2; P2 = in-app degraded banner per §42.4.3; P3 = none | StatuspageIncident row created via §42.9.5 API; Customer-Owner Inbox dispatch via §29; Enterprise webhook fired via §42.9.6 | `incident.customer_notified` |
| 6. Mitigation executed | `on_call_primary` (with `ops_admin` quorum per §50.4.4 for customer-data-affecting mitigation) | Per runbook anchored on the firing alarm (§42.5.1 Runbook Inventory) | Mitigation actions logged as `OpsActionRecord` rows with `action_kind = 'incident_mitigation_step'` (Appendix J — V12 add); each customer-data-affecting mitigation writes §4.6.1 Audit Event rows with `actor_type='ops_actor'` | `incident.mitigation_step` |
| 7. All-clear declared | `on_call_primary` (with co-confirm from `ops_admin` secondary for P0/P1) | Alarm cleared AND §42.3.0 clear-threshold met (5 consecutive minutes for §42.6.0 detector-driven; SLO-burn-rate normalization for SLO-driven) | IncidentRecord `mitigated_at` stamped; `all_clear_actor_user_id` + (for P0/P1) `all_clear_co_confirm_user_id` populated | `incident.all_clear` |
| 8. Postmortem scheduled | `on_call_primary` (or escalation to `ops_admin` if primary off-shift) | Within 24 wall-clock hours of `mitigated_at` for P0/P1; within 5 business days for P2; postmortem-optional for P3 (per IncidentRecord `postmortem_required` boolean) | PostmortemRecord row created in `draft` state per §42.10 entity; `postmortem_author_user_id` assigned | `incident.postmortem_scheduled` |
| 9. RCA drafted | `postmortem_author_user_id` (named in step 8) | Within 48 wall-clock hours of `mitigated_at` for P0/P1 | PostmortemRecord transitions `draft → under_review`; root_cause, contributing_factors, preventive_actions populated | `incident.rca_drafted` |
| 10. Blameless postmortem published | `postmortem_author_user_id` + `technical_reviewer_user_id` (peer-review approver) | Within 72 wall-clock hours of `mitigated_at` for P0/P1 (or within 10 business days for P2) | PostmortemRecord transitions `under_review → published`; OpsActionRecord with `action_kind = 'incident_postmortem_published'`; postmortem PDF deep-link in Customer-Owner Inbox for P0 with `customer_visible = true` | `incident.postmortem_published` |
| 11. Action-item closure | `action_item.owner_user_id` (assigned per action_item in PostmortemRecord) | Within 30 calendar days of step 10 (per §42.7 AC #3) | Each action_item transitions to `closed`; `action_item.closed_at` stamped; tracked via Linear issue link `action_item.linear_issue_url` | `incident.action_item_closed` |

**Postmortem deadline (V12 unification — closes D-12V-002).** The unified two-stage timeline is:
- **T + 48h** — RCA draft completed (step 9; single-author internal artifact).
- **T + 72h** — Blameless postmortem published (step 10; peer-reviewed artifact, registered as `OpsActionRecord` with `action_kind='incident_postmortem_published'`).
- **T + 30 days** — All action items closed (step 11).

§50.6.4 ¶6 cites this timeline by anchor — no independent deadline lives at §50. CI gate `postmortem_deadline_single_source` (Appendix M.5 — V12 addition) greps the spec for inline RCA / postmortem deadline values outside §42.3.2.

**Postmortem artifacts (per PostmortemRecord entity §42.10).**

- Root cause analysis (free-text, ≤ 4000 chars, PII-redacted per §42.10 serializer)
- Contributing factors
- Preventive actions (code changes, process changes, monitoring improvements)
- Action items (each with `owner_user_id`, `estimate_business_days`, `target_close_at`, `linear_issue_url`, `state ∈ open / in_progress / closed`)
- Published target (`internal_only` vs `customer_visible`; customer-visible per §42.10.3)

## 42.4 Disaster Recovery Targets {#42.4-disaster-recovery-targets}

| Metric | Target |
| :---- | :---- |
| **RTO (Recovery Time Objective)** | 1 hour, **per residency region** (V9 remediation, closes D-RES-011 P2) |
| **RPO (Recovery Point Objective)** | 1 hour, **per residency region** |

**Per-region RTO/RPO scope.** RTO and RPO are measured per residency partition. An outage of a single residency region constitutes downtime for Orgs in that region regardless of other regions' availability. The Enterprise 99.9% uptime SLA at §42.1 is also measured per residency partition: an EU-Org's monthly downtime is computed against EU-region availability only; a US-Org against US-region availability. Cross-region failover does NOT satisfy a same-region RTO target — see §42.4.1.

### 42.4.1 Residency-Bound Failover (D-RES-001 V9 remediation, 2026-05-09) {#42.4.1-residency-bound-failover}

**Authoring intent.** Pre-V9 §42.4 declared "Convex provides transparent multi-region failover. Sourcera application code is stateless. No manual intervention needed. Automatic DNS failover (sub-60 second TTL)." The failover contract was silent on residency. An EU-Ireland regional outage automatically failing traffic over to the next-available Convex region (which, per the Convex platform deploy topology, may be US-East-1) would constitute a GDPR Chapter V third-country transfer of EU subject PII without authority — a binding US/EU data-residency lock violation. §42.4.1 closes this by anchoring failover to same-residency replicas.

**Same-residency replica policy.**

Each canonical residency region per §1.6 (post-D-RES-003 expansion to four-row table) deploys a primary + same-residency replica pair. Cross-residency replication is forbidden by Convex deployment configuration:

| Residency region | Convex primary | Convex same-region replica |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `us` | AWS us-east-1 | AWS us-west-2 |
| `eu` | AWS eu-west-1 (Ireland) | AWS eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) |
| `apac` | AWS ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) | AWS ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo) |
| `custom` (Enterprise sovereign-cloud) | per `custom_sovereign_residency_label` (e.g., `de_t_systems_2026`); operator-defined | per agreement; same-jurisdiction-only |

**Failover behavior.**

- Failover targets a **same-residency replica only**. `eu-west-1 → eu-central-1` is permitted; `eu-west-1 → us-east-1` is **forbidden by deployment configuration** and rejected by the Convex DNS failover layer.
- When no same-residency replica is available (concurrent regional outage of both primary and replica), traffic is **degraded to read-only** from the residual primary OR the platform fails closed; the platform does NOT fail over cross-residency. Read-only degradation surfaces a customer-visible banner at the Workspace surface ("Service degraded — read-only — your region's failover replica is recovering"). Write attempts return HTTP 503 `residency_failover_blocked` (Appendix I — new V9 row).
- DNS failover TTL remains sub-60 seconds within a residency boundary.
- Failover events are emitted to the `dr-events` PagerDuty queue at SEV-2; the residency partition is included in the alert payload.

**Restore-test staging environment residency.**

- Quarterly DR restore tests run in **per-residency staging stacks** (e.g., `staging-us`, `staging-eu`, `staging-apac`). An EU production snapshot restores into `staging-eu` only; cross-residency restore into `staging-us` is forbidden.
- Per-region game-day rehearsal: each residency partition runs a quarterly failover game-day exercising the same-residency replica failover.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. The Convex deployment configuration MUST declare same-residency replica pairs for every residency partition listed in §1.6. CI gate `dr_failover_residency_bound` (Appendix M.5 — new V9 row) asserts via Convex deployment-topology static analysis at deploy time. Build fails on cross-residency replica configuration.
2. DNS failover MUST target a same-residency replica only. Property test `dns_failover_target_residency_match` (Datadog synthetic chaos test, quarterly) asserts.
3. Concurrent same-residency primary + replica outage MUST degrade to read-only with `residency_failover_blocked` (HTTP 503) on writes; cross-residency failover is forbidden. Property test `dr_failover_no_cross_residency` asserts via QA chaos test.
4. Per-region staging-restore stacks MUST exist for every residency partition; quarterly DR test restores MUST execute against the matching residency staging stack. CI gate `dr_restore_test_residency_partition` asserts.
5. Per-region game-day rehearsal MUST execute quarterly per residency partition; missed game-day fires Datadog SEV-3 alarm `dr_game_day_overdue`.

### 42.4.2 Residency-Bound Backups (D-RES-002 V9 remediation, 2026-05-09) {#42.4.2-residency-bound-backups}

**Authoring intent.** Pre-V9 §42.4 declared "Database: Convex-managed snapshots hourly … Object Storage (Files): Geo-redundant (S3 replication, multi-region)" with no residency qualifier. Multi-region S3 replication crosses borders by default unless residency-bound replica policies are explicitly configured. EU subject PII could replicate into US-region backup vaults under the spec as written. §42.4.2 closes this by anchoring backup storage and replication to same-residency partitions and by authoring the DSAR backup re-pseudonymization contract.

**Convex snapshot residency.**

- Convex managed snapshots (hourly + daily) are stored in the **same residency region** as the source shard. `eu-west-1` snapshots store in EU vaults; cross-region snapshot replication is forbidden by Convex backup configuration.
- Per-region snapshot retention catalogs (the snapshot-index metadata listing snapshot timestamps and storage locations) are residency-bound — the catalog itself resides in-region, so a subject's "where is my data" inquiry can be answered by the region's catalog without cross-region reads.
- Snapshot retention: hourly retained 30 days; daily retained 30 days (per pre-V9 row, preserved). Both retentions honor residency partition.

**S3 replication residency.**

- Object Storage (S3) replication policies MUST target same-residency replica buckets only:

| Source bucket residency | Permitted replica targets | Forbidden |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `us` (us-east-1) | `us` (us-west-2) | `eu`, `apac` regions |
| `eu` (eu-west-1) | `eu` (eu-central-1) | `us`, `apac` regions |
| `apac` (ap-southeast-1) | `apac` (ap-northeast-1) | `us`, `eu` regions |
| `custom` | per agreement | cross-jurisdiction |

- Cross-region S3 replication is **forbidden by default**. Explicit Ops sign-off + DPO approval required for any cross-region replica policy (Enterprise customer with explicit DPA addendum allowing transfer); the override is logged as an `org.residency.cross_region_replica_approved` AuditEvent.
- "Geo-redundant" in customer-facing materials is reframed to "Region-redundant within residency partition" — a same-residency multi-AZ + multi-region-within-same-residency posture.

**Backup re-pseudonymization on DSAR.**

When the §6.8.4 cascade walker completes pseudonymization on a subject's row set, a follow-on event `dsar.cascade.backup_repseudonymization_required` is emitted. The backup re-pseudonymization handler:

1. Identifies all backup blobs intersecting `(subject_id, [verified_at - retention_window])` — i.e., snapshots or replication targets that captured pre-pseudonym predecessors.
2. For each affected backup blob, EITHER (a) re-pseudonymizes the row in-place via a Convex backup-rewrite mutation that walks the blob's row index and applies the same Pattern A/B treatment as the live cascade, OR (b) excludes the affected blob from restore eligibility post-cascade by adding the blob's snapshot ID to a `dsar_excluded_snapshots` set; restore from an excluded snapshot is rejected with `restore_from_dsar_excluded_snapshot_blocked` (Appendix I — new).
3. Re-pseudonymization completes within the §6.8.6 30-day SLA for fulfillment; if unable to complete within SLA, the cascade routes through §6.8.4.6 partial-failure path with `dsar.cascade.backup_repseudonymization_failed`.
4. `dsar.cascade.backup_repseudonymization_completed` is emitted on success and is part of the §6.8.6 fulfillment criteria (alongside `dsar.cascade.aggregate_recompute_completed` from §6.8.4.4 and `dsar.cascade.row_redacted` from §6.8.4).

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Convex snapshot blobs MUST be stored in the same residency region as the source shard; cross-region snapshot replication forbidden by Convex deployment configuration. CI gate `backup_residency_partition_isolation` (Appendix M.5 — new V9 row) asserts via Convex backup-topology static analysis at deploy time.
2. S3 replication policies MUST target same-residency replica buckets only; cross-region replica configurations rejected at IaC apply time with `residency_backup_replication_blocked` (Appendix I — new V9 row; HTTP 422). CI gate `s3_replication_policy_residency_bound` asserts via Terraform static analysis.
3. Cross-region replica policy override (Enterprise DPA addendum) MUST require Ops sign-off + DPO approval AND emit `org.residency.cross_region_replica_approved` AuditEvent; absent approval, IaC apply fails. CI gate `s3_cross_region_replica_dpa_approval_required` asserts.
4. DSAR cascade MUST emit `dsar.cascade.backup_repseudonymization_required` on cascade-target blob set computation; the cascade does NOT mark fulfillment until `dsar.cascade.backup_repseudonymization_completed` fires (or the affected blobs are added to `dsar_excluded_snapshots` and `dsar.cascade.backup_repseudonymization_completed_via_exclusion` fires). CI gate `backup_dsar_repseudonymization_completeness` (Appendix M.5 — new V9 row) asserts via DSAR fulfillment QA test.
5. Restore from a `dsar_excluded_snapshots` blob MUST reject with `restore_from_dsar_excluded_snapshot_blocked` (Appendix I — new V9 row; HTTP 403). CI gate `dsar_excluded_snapshot_restore_blocked` asserts.
6. Per-region snapshot retention catalogs MUST be residency-bound; cross-region catalog reads from customer surfaces blocked. CI gate `snapshot_catalog_residency_partition` asserts.
7. The §40.2 retention table's per-row Residency cells MUST declare "backups inherit partition per §42.4.2" for every entity carrying subject-PII. (Authored in the V9 §40.2 remediation pass — closes the §40.2 ↔ §42.4 cross-link gap.)

**Failover, day-to-day.** Same-residency replica failover is transparent within a residency boundary; sub-60-second DNS TTL preserved within-region. Cross-residency failover is forbidden per §42.4.1; concurrent same-region primary + replica outage degrades to read-only per §42.4.1.

### 42.4.3 Customer-Visible Degraded Banner (V12 — D-12V-007) {#42.4.3-customer-visible-degraded-banner}

V12 remediation (closes D-12V-007 + extends §42.4.1 banner contract). The customer-visible degraded banner is a polymorphic surface that renders on every Buyer / Seller / Marketplace console when an active incident affects the customer's residency partition. Replaces the residency-failover-specific banner authored at §42.4.1 with a polymorphic Service Degraded surface that covers SEV-3 customer visibility (per §42.3.0 customer-comms gap).

**Banner kinds (Appendix J `service_degraded_banner_kind` — V12 add).**

| Kind | Trigger | Copy template | Dismissibility |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `provider_degraded` | Any §42.6.0 detector state `*_degraded` AND customer-facing surface inherits the latency | "Service degraded — {provider_display_name} is experiencing elevated latency. {affected_surface} may be slower than usual. We're investigating." | Dismissible per surface per session. |
| `latency_degraded` | §44.1 budget breach for > 5 min on a surface-class implicated by the customer's active workspace | "{surface_name} is slower than usual right now. We're investigating." | Dismissible per surface per session. |
| `region_degraded` | Any P1/P2 incident with `residency_region_affected = caller.residency_region` | "Service degraded in your region. Some workflows may be unavailable until we restore full service." | Non-dismissible until incident `mitigated_at`. |
| `residency_failover_readonly` | The existing §42.4.1 residency-failover banner — preserved structurally; absorbed into this enum | "Service degraded — read-only — your region's failover replica is recovering." | Non-dismissible until failover clears. |

**Banner data model.** Each customer-visible degraded banner reads a `ServiceDegradedBannerProjection` row computed from the active IncidentRecord + ProviderHealthState + §44.1 budget violation set; the projection is filtered to the caller's residency partition and console scope (no cross-console leakage). Authored Extension AE-V12-04 — flagged.

**Acceptance criteria (§42.4.3).**

1. Banner renders within 30 s of an upstream detector / SLO state change. QA test: `degraded_banner_render_latency`.
2. Banner is residency-partitioned: a US-Org never sees an EU-region banner. QA test: `degraded_banner_residency_isolation`.
3. Banner has an Appendix M.1 row per `service_degraded_banner_kind` value; CI gate `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` asserts. QA test: `degraded_banner_appendix_m_row_complete`.

## 42.5 On-Call Rotation {#42.5-on-call-rotation}

V12 remediation (2026-05-11; closes D-42-005). §42.5 is now the canonical home for on-call rotation, three-step escalation, and the Runbook Inventory (§42.5.1).

### 42.5 On-Call Coverage {#42.5-on-call-coverage}

- 24/7 on-call coverage (mandatory across all incident severities per §42.3.0; coverage scope is platform-wide, not plan-tier-conditional).
- Three on-call tiers: `on_call_primary`, `on_call_secondary`, `on_call_manager` (the third tier closes D-42-005 — §25.6.2 cited a three-step ladder which §42.5 now authors).
- Rotation weekly with handoff at Monday 09:00 UTC; rotation membership tracked in `OnCallShift` entity per §42.11.
- Incident history tracked in PagerDuty (paid plan); per-incident IncidentRecord rows are the authoritative platform-side history (PagerDuty is a delivery layer, not the source of truth).

### 42.5.0 Three-Step Escalation Ladder {#42.5.0-escalation-ladder}

The escalation ladder fires on PagerDuty page ack-timeout. Numerical thresholds align with the §25.6.2 inbound citation. CI gate `escalation_ladder_single_source` (Appendix M.5 — V12 addition) asserts no inline escalation-timing values outside this anchor.

| Stage | Trigger | Recipient | Timeout to next stage | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Initial page | `on_call_primary` (per active OnCallShift) | 5 min | Per §25.6.2 line 21134 |
| 2 | Stage-1 ack-timeout (no ack within 5 min) | `on_call_secondary` (per active OnCallShift) | 10 min | Per §25.6.2 |
| 3 | Stage-2 ack-timeout (no ack within 10 min) | `on_call_manager` (engineering manager rotation) | 15 min | Per §25.6.2 |
| 4 | Stage-3 ack-timeout (no ack within 15 min) | `ops_director` rotation (via PagerDuty escalation policy) | Open-ended; pages indefinitely until ack | Manual phone-tree fallback if PagerDuty itself is degraded — see §42.6.3 fallback contract |

### 42.5.1 Runbook Inventory {#42.5.1-runbook-inventory}

V12 remediation (closes D-42-005 + D-42-019). Every alarm in §42.2.3 + §42.6.0 + §25.6.2 + §50.x has a runbook entry; CI gate `alarm_runbook_link_completeness` (Appendix M.5 — V12 addition) asserts the binding.

**Storage.** Notion workspace `sourcera-ops-runbooks` (residency-bound to a US-region Notion workspace; EU subject PII references in runbooks are pseudonymized via the Notion-side template per §6.7 secret-redaction extension). Each runbook is a RunbookEntry row in `ops_runbook_entries` (entity §42.13).

**Required fields per RunbookEntry.**

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK | |
| `runbook_anchor` | string | `RB-{namespace}-{NNN}` (e.g., `RB-PLAT-001`, `RB-REV-008`, `RB-PERF-007`, `RB-DR-001`). Unique. | Referenced from §42.2.3 alarm rows + §25.6.2 RB-001..RB-010. |
| `title` | string | ≤ 160 chars | Human-readable. |
| `notion_page_url` | string | https://www.notion.so/sourcera-ops-runbooks/...; persisted but the source of truth is `body_md` snapshot. | |
| `body_md` | text | Markdown snapshot pulled from Notion nightly; checksummed. | Cached so a Notion outage does not block on-call. |
| `owner_user_id` | UUID FK | → User | Per §42.5.1 ACs. |
| `last_reviewed_at` | timestamp | Required | Quarterly review cadence. |
| `freshness_status` | enum | `current` / `stale` (last_reviewed_at > 90 days) / `retired` | Per Appendix J `runbook_status` (V12 add). |
| `linked_alarms` | string[] | Array of alarm names from §42.2.3 / §42.6.0 / §25.6.2 | CI gate asserts every §42.2.3 alarm row has a matching `linked_alarms` entry. |
| `org_id` | n/a — platform-scoped | | Runbooks are not customer-scoped. |
| `console` | n/a — Ops-scoped only | | |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | per §4 convention | | Soft-delete via `deleted_at`. |

**Scope isolation.** Platform-scoped (no `org_id`). Ops-Console-only read; `ops_admin` / `ops_audit_reviewer` / `ops_security_admin` write per §50.3.2 envelope. Required index on `runbook_anchor` (unique).

**Retention.** Body snapshots retained 7 years per §40.2; live Notion pages governed by Notion enterprise retention policy.

**Freshness alarm.** Datadog SEV-3 alarm `runbook_stale_detected` fires when any active `linked_alarms` references a runbook with `freshness_status='stale'`. Quarterly review cadence is enforced by a `runbook_quarterly_review_cadence` §M.5 CI gate (V12 add).

**Initial population.** §42.5.1 ships with the alarm-runbook binding for every alarm row authored in §42.2.3 + §42.6.0 + §25.6.2; the initial RunbookEntry rows are pre-seeded as part of the v7.1.1 stamp release. RB-REV-001 through RB-REV-014 + RB-PERF-001 through RB-PERF-010 + RB-PLAT-001 through RB-PLAT-006 are the V12-authored runbook anchors.

### 42.5.2 Acceptance Criteria (§42.5) {#42.5.2-acceptance-criteria}

1. Three-step escalation ladder fires within configured timeouts; PagerDuty escalation policy `sourcera_platform_oncall` enforces. QA test: `escalation_ladder_pagerduty_config_match`.
2. Every §42.2.3 alarm row resolves to a RunbookEntry via `linked_alarms`. CI gate `alarm_runbook_link_completeness` asserts. QA test: `runbook_link_coverage_complete`.
3. RunbookEntry `last_reviewed_at` within 90 days for every `freshness_status='current'` row; Datadog `runbook_stale_detected` fires on breach. QA test: `runbook_freshness_quarterly`.
4. Runbook authorship + revision history is audit-logged via §4.6.1 Audit Event with `actor_type='ops_actor'`. QA test: `runbook_authorship_audit_event`.
5. On-call training (review of all RunbookEntry rows) completed quarterly per `ops_oncall_training_quarterly` event (Appendix C — V12 add); missed-training raises §42 P2. QA test: `oncall_training_quarterly`.

## 42.6 Observability Stack {#42.6-observability-stack}

V12 remediation (2026-05-11; closes D-42-002, D-42-003, D-42-024, D-42-028). §42.6 now authors the structured log schema, PII scrubbing contract, OpenTelemetry trace propagation, sampling policy, per-residency routing, Sentry contract, and webhook delivery alarm disambiguation.

### 42.6.0.A Observability Tool Stack {#42.6.0-tool-stack}

| Component | Purpose | Tool |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Logging** | Structured logs (JSON) for all API requests, errors, state changes | Pino (application) → Datadog |
| **Metrics** | System and application metrics (latency, throughput, errors) | Datadog Agent + custom Convex metric emitters |
| **Tracing** | Distributed request tracing (API → Convex DB → MCP → Managed Agents → Stripe → WorkOS → Firecrawl → PostHog → Loops.so → Perplexity → Zendesk) | OpenTelemetry → Datadog (W3C Trace Context propagation) |
| **Error Tracking** | Application errors and exceptions | Sentry (per §42.6.4 contract) |
| **Alerting** | Alert routing, escalation, notification | Datadog → PagerDuty (per §42.5.0 escalation ladder) |
| **Status Communication** | Public incident status | Statuspage.io |
| **Dashboards** | Real-time health visualization | Datadog dashboards + per-role Ops dashboards per §50.14 |

### 42.6.1.A Structured Log Schema {#42.6.1-structured-log-schema}

V12 remediation (closes D-42-002). Every Pino-emitted log row in any Sourcera process MUST conform to the schema below. The Convex-side Pino transport asserts at emit time; non-conformant rows are rejected with `pino.schema_violation` Sentry event (rate-limited to one event per minute per process to avoid Sentry quota burn).

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `timestamp` | ISO-8601 UTC | yes | Per-log-row monotonic clock. |
| `level` | enum | yes | `trace` / `debug` / `info` / `warn` / `error` / `fatal` (Pino convention). |
| `service` | enum | yes | Appendix J `sourcera_service_kind` (V12 add): `convex_backend`, `nextjs_buyer_console`, `nextjs_seller_console`, `nextjs_marketplace`, `nextjs_ops_console`, `public_api`, `webhook_delivery`, `managed_agent_runtime`, `mcp_proxy`, `dsar_cascade_walker`, `audit_integrity_scanner`, `spec_lint_pipeline`. |
| `route` | string | conditional | Required when `service ∈ {public_api, nextjs_*}`. Pattern: HTTP method + path template (e.g., `GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/workspaces`). |
| `method` | enum | conditional | HTTP verb. |
| `status_code` | int | conditional | HTTP status. |
| `latency_ms` | int | conditional | Request duration. |
| `request_id` | string | yes (for request-scoped logs) | Correlates to `X-Request-Id` response header. |
| `trace_id` | string | yes (for request-scoped logs) | W3C Trace Context `traceparent` trace_id. |
| `span_id` | string | conditional | W3C Trace Context current span_id. |
| `org_id` | UUID | conditional | Required when request is org-scoped. |
| `console` | enum | conditional | `buyer` / `seller` / `marketplace` / `ops` / `platform_system`. |
| `user_id` | UUID | conditional | Required when request is user-scoped; nullable for system/cron paths. |
| `actor_kind` | enum | yes | `customer` / `managed_agent` / `ops` / `internal_cron` / `system`. |
| `error_code` | string | conditional | Required on `level ∈ {warn, error, fatal}`. Matches Appendix I row. |
| `error_subkind` | enum | conditional | Per Appendix J `error_subkind` (registered at §32.6 / Appendix I preamble). |
| `plan_tier` | enum | conditional | When org-scoped: `buyer_free`/`buyer_solo`/`buyer_starter`/`buyer_growth`/`buyer_scale`/`buyer_enterprise`/...; per §34.1. |
| `residency_region` | enum | yes (for org-scoped logs) | `us` / `eu` / `apac` / `custom_*` per §1.6. |
| `legal_entity` | enum | conditional | When billing-path-implicated, per §4.8.1 invoice routing. |
| `audit_event_id` | UUID | conditional | When log row corresponds to a §4.6.1 AuditEvent. |
| `posthog_distinct_id` | string | conditional | Cross-tool correlation with §51 telemetry. |
| `ops_session_id` | UUID | conditional | When `actor_kind='ops'`; required per §50.5.1. |

### 42.6.1.B PII Scrubbing Contract {#42.6.1-pii-scrubbing-contract}

V12 remediation (closes D-42-002 PII-scrubbing slice). Field-path-level PII redaction MUST execute at log-emit time (Pino `redact` option). The redaction registry is the canonical list of fields/paths that contain PII or secrets:

| Field path (Pino dot-notation) | Treatment | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `*.email`, `*.user_email`, `*.contact_email`, `*.reply_to` | `[email-redacted]` | §6.7 |
| `*.phone`, `*.user_phone`, `*.mobile`, `*.contact_phone` | `[phone-redacted]` | §6.7 |
| `*.ssn`, `*.tax_id`, `*.ein` | `[gov-id-redacted]` | §6.7 |
| `*.card_number`, `*.cvc`, `*.iban`, `*.account_number` | `[fin-redacted]` | §6.7 + PCI scope |
| `*.password`, `*.token`, `*.secret`, `*.api_key`, `*.refresh_token` | `[secret-redacted]` | §6.7 |
| `*.body.workspace_export.*` | full row drop (workspace exports never log body content) | §50.21 |
| `*.body.kb_document.*` | full row drop (KB content never logs body) | §22 |
| `*.body.proposal_text`, `*.body.requirement_response_body` | preview-only (first 80 chars + `[...]`) | §13 / §23 |
| `*.body.policy_document.*` | full row drop (policy ingestion content never logs body) | §12 |
| `*.headers.authorization`, `*.headers.cookie`, `*.headers.set_cookie` | `[auth-header-redacted]` | §6.7 |

**Test contract.** PII-bearing test cases per §46 (V12 rewrite) MUST assert that no PII-class string ever appears in production Datadog logs. Per `posthog_pii_test_coverage` §M.5 CI gate.

### 42.6.1.C OpenTelemetry Trace Propagation {#42.6.1-trace-propagation}

V12 remediation (closes D-42-003). Every cross-process boundary MUST propagate W3C Trace Context (`traceparent`, `tracestate` HTTP headers; or equivalent for non-HTTP transports).

| Boundary | Propagation mechanism | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Client (Browser) → Public API §32 | `traceparent` + `tracestate` request headers (initiated by Sentry SDK in the Next.js app) | Sentry SDK auto-injects. |
| Next.js → Convex RPC | `traceparent` propagated via Convex `convex/server` mutation/query context | Convex Convex internal extension; verified by `convex_trace_propagation` smoke test. |
| Convex → MCP Proxy → Anthropic Managed Agents | `traceparent` propagated via Anthropic SDK `requestOptions.traceparent` header (Managed Agents `managed-agents-2026-04-01` API supports W3C Trace Context) | Verified by `anthropic_trace_propagation` smoke test. |
| Convex → Stripe webhook ingest | Sourcera does not propagate trace inbound (Stripe doesn't carry our trace_id); Stripe-side trace is opened on receipt with `parent_kind = 'stripe_inbound_webhook'` | The Stripe response replay is correlated via `Stripe-Signature` header to the originating webhook. |
| Convex → Stripe outbound (meter-event / invoice finalization) | `traceparent` propagated via Stripe Node SDK `Stripe-Trace-Id` request header (custom Sourcera convention; Stripe ignores; useful for our outbound trace decomposition) | |
| Convex → WorkOS SSO callback | `traceparent` propagated via WorkOS callback URL query parameter `trace_id` | |
| Convex → Firecrawl scrape | `traceparent` propagated via Firecrawl API `metadata.trace_id` request body field | |
| Convex → PostHog ingest | `traceparent` propagated via PostHog event `properties.trace_id` field | |
| Convex → Loops.so dispatch | `traceparent` propagated via Loops.so transactional API `event_data.trace_id` field | |
| Convex → Perplexity | `traceparent` propagated via Perplexity API `metadata.trace_id` field | |
| Convex → Zendesk | `traceparent` propagated via Zendesk API `external_id` field on incident ticket creation | |

**Span naming.** Span names follow the convention `{service}.{operation}` (e.g., `convex_backend.aioperation_accept`, `mcp_proxy.tool_call`, `nextjs_buyer_console.defense_view_generate`). Per-Org / per-User tag cardinality is bounded at the OpenTelemetry SDK layer per a `sourcera_otel_tag_cardinality_budget` allowlist; high-cardinality identifiers (org_id, user_id, requirement_id) land as span attributes, not span names.

**Sampling.** Head-based sampling at the edge: 100% for `level ∈ {error, fatal}` and for `actor_kind='ops'`; 10% for `level=warn`; 1% for `level=info`; 0.1% for `level=debug` (debug typically disabled in production). Sampling decision propagates via `tracestate` so downstream services honor it.

**Cross-tool correlation.** Every Datadog log row carries `trace_id` (per the §42.6.1.A schema); every PostHog event carries `trace_id` (per the Appendix G taxonomy update — V12 add); every Sentry exception carries `trace_id` as a `contexts.trace.trace_id` tag; every §4.6.1 AuditEvent carries `trace_id` as a new field (Authored Extension — §42.6.1.C-3).

### 42.6.1.D Hash-Chain Scope (V12 — closes D-12V-006) {#42.6.1-hash-chain-scope}

V12 remediation (closes D-12V-006). §42.6.1 `audit_event_hash_chain_scan` job operates against the full §4.6.1 AuditEvent corpus per V3 remediation. The "high-impact mutations" phrase used in legacy references is RETIRED; hash-chain scope is now exhaustively defined.

**Hash-chain-in-scope rule.** An AuditEvent row is in-scope for the `audit_event_hash_chain_scan` job IFF any of the following holds:

1. `actor_type = 'ops_actor'` (per §50.5.1; ALL Ops-tagged rows, regardless of read/write verb, are in scope).
2. `actor_type = 'system_agent'` AND `system_agent_id` resolves to a Managed Agent bridge principal AND `mutation_kind != 'read'` (Managed Agent-originated AuditEvent mutations; §4.8.1 AIOperation rows still use `actor_type='managed_agent'`).
3. `entity_type ∈ {'Plan', 'AIWallet', 'AIOperation', 'OutcomeContract', 'CostBaseRecalculationLog', 'RateCard', 'MarketplaceListing', 'VendorDisqualificationRecord', 'ContestRecord', 'SelectionRecord', 'PolicyDocument', 'OpsSession', 'OpsActionRecord', 'IncidentRecord', 'PostmortemRecord'}` — the canonical billing + audit + governance entities.
4. `action_kind ∈ {'plan_change', 'wallet_debit', 'wallet_credit', 'wallet_auto_topup', 'meter_event_submit', 'invoice_finalize', 'refund_authorized', 'contest_resolved', 'incident_postmortem_published', 'marketplace_listing_ban', 'seller_disqualified', 'dsar_cascade_started', 'dsar_cascade_completed', 'cross_region_replica_approved', 'break_glass_session_opened'}`.

The §4.6.1 AuditEvent schema adds an `audit_chain_in_scope` boolean (NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE) field; the §50.5.1 write-time validator computes the value from the row's `(actor_type, entity_type, action_kind)` triple per the rule above. Authored Extension AE-V12-09 — flagged for human sign-off.

CI gate `audit_chain_scope_completeness` (Appendix M.5 — V12 addition) asserts that the population of in-scope rows matches the rule.

### 42.6.2 Sentry Contract {#42.6.2-sentry-contract}

V12 remediation (closes D-42-028).

- **Error class routing.** Uncaught client-side exceptions in the Next.js apps + server-side unhandled errors in Convex functions + Public API §32 panic paths route to Sentry. Datadog logs receive a paired `error_tracking.sentry_event_id` field for cross-tool correlation.
- **PII scrubbing.** Sentry `beforeSend` hook applies the §42.6.1.B PII redaction registry to event `extra`, `tags`, `breadcrumbs`, `request.headers`, and stack-trace `vars`. Local-variable capture in stack-trace frames is disabled by default; opt-in per high-trust path only.
- **Per-residency segmentation.** EU Org exceptions route to EU Sentry project (`sourcera-eu`); US Org exceptions to `sourcera-us`. The Sentry DSN selected at the SDK init layer based on the requesting subject's residency_region.
- **Retention.** Sentry events retained 90 days per Sentry plan default; long-tail retention (per §40.2 audit-integrity-exemption) requires Datadog log mirror (already carries the trace_id).
- **Cross-tool correlation tags.** Every Sentry event carries `tags.trace_id`, `tags.request_id`, `tags.audit_event_id`, `tags.posthog_distinct_id`.

### 42.6.3 Provider-Outage Fallback Contracts {#42.6.3-provider-outage-fallback}

V12 remediation (covers D-42-023 meta-observability slice for paging/comms infrastructure). Fallback contracts for the observability/comms stack itself:

| Component degraded | Fallback |
| :---- | :---- |
| Datadog ingest | Sourcera-side Pino transport buffers up to 100 MB in-process; on Datadog recovery, replay. Sentry alerts fire if buffer > 50 MB. |
| PagerDuty | Opsgenie secondary integration (paid-plan failover); on-call manual phone-tree as final fallback. The on-call rotation roster is mirrored to a sealed-secret Google Sheet for break-glass access. |
| Statuspage.io | Sourcera-hosted status page at `https://status.sourcera.com/fallback` served from Vercel Edge functions; activated by a manual Ops Console toggle. |
| Slack (war-room channel) | Microsoft Teams `#incident-{record_id}` channel; on-call team is dual-Slack/Teams subscribed for break-glass continuity. |
| Sentry | Datadog APM error tracking covers the gap; correlation degrades but errors are not lost (Pino-side `level=error` rows always emit). |

### 42.6.4 Webhook Delivery Alarm Disambiguation {#42.6.4-webhook-delivery-alarm}

V12 remediation (closes D-42-024). The §42.2.3 platform-wide alarm "Webhook delivery rate < 95% post-retry over 30 min" is explicit: the rate is computed POST-retry (after the §31 retry curve + DLQ exhaustion). A 95% pre-retry rate is healthy (retries fix transient failures); a 95% post-retry rate is bad. The alarm threshold action is to page on-call (P2) per §42.2.3.

### 42.6.5 Detector Hysteresis (V12 — D-42-025) {#42.6.5-detector-hysteresis}

V12 closure of D-42-025. The §42.6.0 clear-threshold "5 consecutive minutes" is extended with exponential confirmation: a detector that has flapped > 3 times in any 1-hour window enters a 30-minute confirmation window before clearing (vs the default 5-minute confirmation). The flapping threshold is enforced at the Datadog evaluation engine layer via the `Sourcera-Detector-Flap-Guard` Datadog tag.

### 42.6.6 Alert False-Positive Rate Definition {#42.6.6-false-positive-rate}

V12 closure of D-42-026. "False positive" per §42.7 AC #4 is defined as: an alert that fires without a corresponding §44.1 budget breach AND no on-call mitigation was applied (i.e., the alarm self-cleared without intervention). False positives are computed nightly by a Datadog dashboard widget; the < 5% target is per-alarm-row, not aggregate. Per-alarm false-positive rate is published in the `Ops Health Dashboard` per §50.14.

### 42.6.7 Broken Inbound Citation Cluster (V12 — D-42-022) {#42.6.7-broken-inbound-citations}

V12 closure of D-42-022. §42.6.0 line "All transitions write to the Ops Activity Log (§50.4) and surface in the Ops Health Dashboard (§50.14)" is corrected: the canonical Ops Activity Log is §4.6.1 AuditEvent (filtered to `actor_kind='ops'` per §50.5); the Ops Health Dashboard is §50.14.5 Support Dashboard's "Provider Health" widget (added in V12 as `Ops Health Dashboard` § sub-section).

### 42.6.0 External Provider Health Detectors {#42.6.0-external-provider-health-detectors}

**Phase 13 inline fix F-7.2 (2026-04-26).** The following Convex-side detectors monitor the named external dependencies in §1.5 Stack and raise the named state on threshold breach. State transitions emit Ops PagerDuty alerts at the severity below; no per-customer notifications fire (degradation is observable to customers via in-surface banners only). Recovery is declared when the threshold-breach signal falls below clear-threshold for 5 consecutive minutes.

| Provider | Detector | Trigger | State Raised | Cross-Reference |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Anthropic | `anthropic_mcp_proxy_degraded` | (5xx + timeout) / total > 1% over 15-minute rolling window | `anthropic_mcp_degraded` | §22.8 retry curve (5s/30s/5m/30m); §14543 |
| Firecrawl | `firecrawl_5xx_burst` | 5xx-rate > 5% over 5-minute window | `firecrawl_degraded` | §2083 error-state card; §22.6 |
| Stripe | `stripe_charge_failure_burst` | Charge-failure rate > 2% over 1-hour window | `stripe_degraded` | §7140 wallet retry; Appendix H billing mechanics |
| WorkOS | `workos_sso_failure_burst` | SSO-callback failure rate > 5% over 5-minute window | `workos_degraded` | §49.1.1 magic-link fallback |
| PostHog | `posthog_outbox_saturation` | Outbox depth > 1000 OR p95 ingest latency > 60s | `posthog_outbox_saturated` | §3606; §16300 |
| Loops.so | `loops_dispatch_failure_burst` | Loops 5xx + DLQ rate > 5% over 15-minute window | `loops_degraded` | §6573; §17129 |
| Convex | `convex_reactivity_lag` | Reactive-query p95 freshness > 2s | `convex_degraded` | §44.1 dashboard SLO; §16633 |
| **Perplexity** | `perplexity_search_5xx_burst` | (5xx + timeout) / total > 5% over 15-minute window OR median p95 latency > 12s | `perplexity_degraded` | §16.2.3 fallback contract |
| Zendesk | `zendesk_ticket_create_failure` | Ticket-creation 5xx rate > 5% over 15-minute window | `zendesk_degraded` | §6573 fallback ticket path; §21996 |

**Severity routing.** All provider-degraded states route to PagerDuty as P3 on first detection; P2 if persisting > 30 minutes; P1 if persisting > 4 hours; P0 if customer-visible primary surfaces are blocked (e.g., Stripe degraded > 24h blocking auto-topups for > 50 Orgs). All transitions write to the Ops Activity Log (§50.4) and surface in the Ops Health Dashboard (§50.14).

**Fail-open policy.** A detector itself failing to evaluate (Convex job error during the rolling-window query) MUST raise an Ops P3 within 5 minutes ("detector unable to evaluate health for provider X") and MUST default to assuming the provider is healthy (fail-open) so that the absence of detector signal does NOT incorrectly trigger customer-visible degraded banners.

### 42.6.1 Audit Integrity Background Jobs {#42.6.1-audit-integrity-jobs}

**Scope.** Several entities in the corpus maintain hash-chained audit rows for forensic integrity — §25.3.5 Vendor Disqualification audit chain, §4.6.1 Audit Event hash-chain on high-impact mutations, and §17.8 Selection Record hash (single-row, not chained; listed here for completeness). Each chained-audit surface runs a nightly integrity job. The jobs share a common runtime contract specified here so that Ops, engineering, and finance have one authoritative place to reason about their cost envelope and SLO.

**Job catalog.**

| Job | Scope | Cadence | Runtime Target | Cost Target |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `vendor_disqualification_audit_chain_scan` | Every `VendorDisqualificationRecord` active or modified in the last 90 days (`created_at > now() - 90d` OR `reversed_at > now() - 90d` OR `appeal_decided_at > now() - 90d`). | Daily at 03:15 UTC. | p95 ≤ 8 minutes; p99 ≤ 15 minutes; hard-kill at 30 minutes. | Bounded: at platform scale of 5,000 Orgs and < 10 disqualifications / Org / month at Enterprise tier (Pricing Strategy §6), the 90-day active set is ≤ 150,000 rows → ~10–30 seconds of compute on a single worker. Budget is wildly overshooting actual need; the margins exist to absorb future growth. |
| `audit_event_hash_chain_scan` | Every `AuditEvent` row in the last 30 days (full-corpus coverage per §6.7.5 D-3.4-001 / D-3.4-002 V3 remediation 2026-05-04; the pre-V3 high-impact subset concept and `audit_event_high_impact_actions` registry are retired). | Daily at 03:30 UTC (immediately after the vendor-disqualification scan), with incremental cursor advancing per scan-tick. | p95 ≤ 90 minutes; p99 ≤ 180 minutes; hard-kill at 240 minutes. Coverage gate ≥ 99.9% rows-scanned per partition per pass. | Full-corpus integrity scan with bloom-filter prefiltering and cursor `(org_id, year, chain_position)`. Per-tick batch default 10,000 rows. Cost re-budgeted for full-corpus scope; original ~100k/month high-impact figure superseded. |
| `audit_event_break_glass_integrity_scan` | Per-Org full integrity scan triggered within 1 hour of every §50.2.4 ¶4 break-glass `session_closed_at` event. | On-demand per `ops.break_glass.session_closed` event (no scheduled cadence). | Trigger latency p95 ≤ 1 hour; per-Org scan p95 ≤ 30 minutes. | Per §6.7.5 D-3.4-001 V3 remediation. Mismatches page Ops P0 with diff payload (rows with `prev_event_hash` mismatch, `event_content_hash` mismatch, non-monotonic `chain_position`). |
| `selection_record_hash_spot_check` | A randomly-sampled 1% of `SelectionRecord` rows from the last 365 days per scan run. | Daily at 03:45 UTC. | p95 ≤ 3 minutes; hard-kill at 10 minutes. | Trivial: < 10k row sample / day → < 30 seconds of compute. |

**Execution model.**

- Each job runs on a dedicated worker partition tagged `audit-integrity`, separate from the Ops Console worker pool and from the event-apply workers, so that a stuck integrity job cannot starve production traffic.
- Jobs are implemented as Convex scheduled functions backed by a cursor iterator over the scoped index; cursor position is persisted to `ops_job_runs` on every batch of 1,000 rows. A job killed mid-run resumes from the last persisted cursor on the next run (no double-scanning; no gaps).
- Batch size: 1,000 rows per transaction; per-batch wall-clock cap 5 seconds; a batch exceeding the cap emits `audit_integrity_batch_latency_high` Ops alert (P3) and the job continues.
- Concurrency: at most one instance of each job running at a time (row-level lock on `ops_job_runs(job_name)`).

**Failure paths.**

- **Hash mismatch detected.** Job emits the per-entity Ops alert (`audit_chain_break_detected` for vendor-disqualification; `audit_event_chain_break_detected` for audit-event) with severity P1 per §25.6.2 RB-005 pattern. The job does NOT attempt auto-repair — hash breaks are always manual Ops forensics (Ops Console §50 → Forensics tab → Audit Chain Repair workflow).
- **Hard-kill timeout.** Emits `audit_integrity_job_timeout` Ops alert (P2) with the last cursor position. Ops investigates (usually a slow index or a Convex leader hiccup); manual rerun is safe because the cursor resumes.
- **Job missed a scheduled run.** The 06:00 UTC heartbeat check (per §25.2.4 pattern; reused here) detects a missed run and pages Ops with P2.
- **Persistent failure across 3 consecutive runs.** Pages Ops with P1 regardless of failure reason; the audit-chain integrity guarantee is load-bearing for legal and compliance posture and cannot tolerate sustained silence.

**Observability.**

- Metrics: `audit_integrity.scan.rows_scanned`, `audit_integrity.scan.mismatches_found`, `audit_integrity.scan.duration_ms`, `audit_integrity.scan.batches_over_latency_cap`, `audit_integrity.scan.cursor_position` (gauge). Labels: `job_name`, `residency_region`.
- PostHog events: `audit_integrity_scan_started`, `audit_integrity_scan_completed` (properties: `rows_scanned`, `mismatches_found`, `duration_ms`, `outcome ∈ {clean, mismatches_detected, timeout, error}`).
- Grafana board: `sourcera-audit-integrity` mirrors Ops Console. Weekly trend graph of `mismatches_found` (target: zero, always).

**SLO.** Zero undetected mismatches in any 90-day retrospective window (for chained surfaces) or in any 365-day retrospective window (for spot-check surfaces). A mismatch *detected* by the scan and acted on by Ops is not an SLO violation; a mismatch *discovered retroactively* by a legal discovery or DSAR request that the scan should have caught is.

**Residency.** Each job runs once per residency region against residency-scoped data only. A single job run does NOT cross residency regions. The Ops Console roll-up aggregates across regions for Ops reporting.

**Retention.** `ops_job_runs` rows retained for 365 days per §40.2 job-history retention. Mismatch detection rows retained for 7 years alongside the parent audit surface.

Logged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` → Authored Extensions → §42.6.1 Audit Integrity Background Jobs (2026-04-24).

## 42.7 Acceptance Criteria {#42.7-acceptance-criteria}

V12 remediation (2026-05-11; closes D-42-012). Numbered, testable, observable, measurable, scope-bound per §13.10 / §14.9 / §17.8 / §20.7 style.

1. **Uptime SLA met per residency-partition per calendar month.** Source-of-truth: §34.1 cell **SLA**; measurement: Datadog synthetic monitoring per §42.1 SLA Measurement. Threshold: Enterprise uptime ≥ §34.1 row; breach raises §31 webhook `sla.platform.uptime_breach`. QA test: `uptime_sla_per_residency_monthly`.
2. **All P0/P1 incidents have RCA drafted within 48 hours of `mitigated_at`.** Per §42.3.2 step 9; PostmortemRecord transitions `draft → under_review` within 48 wall-clock hours. Breach raises §42 P2 alarm `postmortem_rca_draft_sla_breach` and pages `ops_security_admin`. QA test: `postmortem_rca_48h_sla`.
3. **All P0/P1 incidents have blameless postmortem published within 72 hours of `mitigated_at`.** Per §42.3.2 step 10; PostmortemRecord transitions `under_review → published`; `OpsActionRecord.action_kind='incident_postmortem_published'` row created. Breach raises §42 P1 alarm `postmortem_published_sla_breach`. QA test: `postmortem_published_72h_sla`.
4. **Postmortem action items closed within 30 calendar days.** Tracked via Linear issue link on each action_item row; missed-closure raises §42 P3 alarm `postmortem_action_item_overdue` AND pages the action-item owner via Loops.so transactional email `postmortem_action_item_overdue_reminder` (Appendix C — V12 add). QA test: `postmortem_action_item_30d`.
5. **Alert false-positive rate < 5% per alarm per month per §42.6.6.** Computed nightly; published to Ops Health Dashboard per §50.14. Per-alarm breach raises Ops review ticket. QA test: `alert_false_positive_per_alarm_5pct`.
6. **DR restore test passes quarterly per residency partition.** Per §42.4.1 AC #5 + §42.4.2 ACs + §42.12 DrDrillRun entity contract; success criteria per §42.12.5 (V12 add: data-integrity row-coverage ≥ §42.6.1.D in-scope rule; RTO ≤ §42.4 1-hour target; banner-render assertion per §42.4.1). QA test: `dr_restore_quarterly_per_residency`.
7. **On-call team trained on every active RunbookEntry quarterly.** Per §42.5.2 AC #5; missed-training raises §42 P2 alarm `oncall_training_quarterly_overdue` and pages the on-call manager. QA test: `oncall_training_runbook_coverage_quarterly`.
8. **Revenue-affecting metric coverage CI gate passes.** Per §M.5 `revenue_metric_coverage` (V12 add); every billing-path event registered in §42.2.1. Build fails on any unregistered revenue-affecting event. CI gate enforces.
9. **Runbook freshness CI gate passes.** Per §M.5 `runbook_quarterly_review_cadence` (V12 add); every active RunbookEntry `last_reviewed_at` ≤ 90 days. Build fails on stale runbooks for active alarms.
10. **Audit-chain scope CI gate passes.** Per §M.5 `audit_chain_scope_completeness` (V12 add); every AuditEvent row's `audit_chain_in_scope` computed correctly per §42.6.1.D rule. Build fails on inconsistent computation.

### 42.9.1 IncidentRecord State Machine {#42.9.1-incidentrecord-state-machine}

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (none) | `intake_pending` | Step 1 detected | — | Row written. |
| `intake_pending` | `paged` | Step 2 PagerDuty page fired | — | `paged_at` stamped. |
| `paged` | `severity_assigned` | Step 3 on-call ack + severity set | Severity in `{p0, p1, p2, p3}` | `severity_assigned_by_user_id` populated. |
| `severity_assigned` | `war_room_open` | Step 4 war-room channel opened | `severity ∈ {p0, p1}` | `war_room_channel_id` populated. |
| `severity_assigned` | `customer_notified` | Step 5 customer comms dispatched | `severity ∈ {p0, p1, p2}` (P3 skips) | `customer_notified_at` stamped. |
| `war_room_open` | `mitigating` | Step 6 mitigation started | — | OpsActionRecord row written. |
| `customer_notified` | `mitigating` | Step 6 (alternative path) | — | |
| `mitigating` | `mitigated` | Step 7 all-clear | Alarm cleared AND clear-threshold met | `mitigated_at` + `all_clear_actor_user_id` stamped. |
| `mitigated` | `postmortem_pending` | Step 8 scheduled | `postmortem_required = TRUE` | PostmortemRecord row created. |
| `mitigated` | `closed_no_postmortem` | Step 8 skipped | `postmortem_required = FALSE` (P3 default) | Terminal. |
| `postmortem_pending` | `postmortem_published` | Step 10 published | — | OpsActionRecord row written. |
| `postmortem_published` | `closed` | Step 11 all action items closed | — | Terminal. |

### 42.9.2 IncidentRecord API Surface {#42.9.2-incidentrecord-api}

Per §32 conventions. All endpoints run under the Ops auth context: resulting §4.6.1 AuditEvent rows use `actor_type='ops_actor'`; any §4.8.1 AIOperation rows generated by the same flow keep `actor_type='ops'`. Rate-limit class `ops_console` (§32.4.5; 50 req/s burst); cursor pagination (default 50, max 250).

| Method | Path | Auth scope | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/ops/incidents/intake` | `ops_admin` OR `ops_support_agent` OR `monitoring_subsystem` | Step 1 intake. Idempotent via `Idempotency-Key`. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/ops/incidents/{id}/page` | `monitoring_subsystem` (PagerDuty integration) | Step 2. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/ops/incidents/{id}/severity` | `on_call_primary` | Step 3. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/ops/incidents/{id}/war-room` | `on_call_primary` | Step 4. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/ops/incidents/{id}/customer-notify` | `on_call_primary` OR `ops_admin` | Step 5. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/ops/incidents/{id}/mitigation-step` | `on_call_primary` | Step 6. |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/ops/incidents/{id}/all-clear` | `on_call_primary` + `ops_admin` (co-confirm for P0/P1) | Step 7. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/ops/incidents/{id}` | `ops_admin` / `ops_audit_reviewer` | Read. |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/ops/incidents` | `ops_admin` / `ops_audit_reviewer` | List with cursor. |

Error codes (Appendix I — V12 additions): `incident_severity_invalid`, `incident_all_clear_not_permitted_without_mitigation`, `incident_postmortem_already_published`.

### 42.10.3 Customer-Visible Postmortem Projection {#42.10.3-customer-visible-projection}

For P0 incidents affecting an Enterprise customer, the postmortem is published to a customer-visible URL per §42.3.2 step 10. The customer-visible projection redacts: Ops user identifiers (replaced with `ops_agent_handle`), internal-only mitigation steps, internal tool names, internal-only architectural details. Customer-visible fields: incident timeline, customer-impact summary, root cause (PII-redacted), preventive actions (customer-relevant only), affected residency region, mitigation completion timestamp.

### 42.12.5 DR Drill Success Criteria (V12) {#42.12.5-dr-drill-success-criteria}

Each DR drill MUST measure and assert:

1. **RTO measurement.** Wall-clock time from `drill_started_at` to first successful customer request post-failover. MUST be ≤ §42.4 1-hour target per residency partition. Breach: `dr_drill_failed`.
2. **RPO measurement.** Maximum data-loss window across all entity types. MUST be ≤ §42.4 1-hour target.
3. **Data integrity.** A random 1% of rows across `Plan`, `AIWallet`, `OutcomeContract`, `AuditEvent`, `SelectionRecord`, `VendorDisqualificationRecord` (per §42.6.1.D in-scope rule) MUST be spot-checked end-to-end (hash-chain verify for chained entities; row-content compare for others). Mismatch threshold: zero mismatches.
4. **Customer-visible banner.** §42.4.1 / §42.4.3 banner MUST render on simulated customer request during the drill. Assertion: HTTP 200 + banner DOM element present.
5. **Drill failure escalation.** Drill failure (any criterion above) auto-rolls-back the next release per §47.2 change-management process AND pages `ops_security_admin` AND emits `dr_drill_failed` event.
6. **Outcome retention.** Drill outcome report retained 7 years per §40.2; internal-only by default; customer-visible drill outcomes posted on customer-trust page only with Ops Director sign-off.

# 44\. Performance Requirements & Solo-Tier Surface Treatment {#44.-performance-requirements}

**Section scope (Phase 14.10.1 / 14.14 retitle).** §44 carries two distinct contracts: §44.1–§44.5 author the platform-wide performance budgets; §44.6 (added in Phase 14.10) authors the Solo-Tier Surface Treatment that hides AIOperation metering / value-dollar accounting / wallet / overage / rate card from the Solo-tier surface while preserving the engine. Cross-references throughout the corpus that read "§44 (Performance Budgets — Solo-Tier Surface Treatment)" are honored as references to this dual-scope section. Phase 14.20 closeout MAY split §44.6 into a sibling §44a if the operator deems the dual-scope framing operationally awkward; Phase 14.14 (closed 2026-04-28) retitles the section header to acknowledge the dual scope without splitting.

## 44.2 Agent Performance Budgets {#44.2-agent-performance-budgets}

**Pre-Score Per-Requirement Latency:**

- Haiku: 5-10s  
- Sonnet: 10-30s  
- Opus: 30-60s (used for reasoning-heavy requirements only)

**Full Workspace Pre-Score:**

- Budget: `requirement_count × 15 seconds` (average case)  
- Example: 100 requirements → max 25 minutes  
- Parallelization: Process up to 10 requirements concurrently → effective duration ≈ 2.5 minutes for 100 reqs

**Cost Estimates (per requirement, list price):**

- Haiku: $0.02-0.05 (input tokens: 500-1000, output tokens: 100-200)  
- Sonnet: $0.05-0.15 (input tokens: 1000-1500, output tokens: 200-400)  
- Opus: $0.15-0.40 (input tokens: 1500-2000, output tokens: 300-500)

**AI Included-Budget Ceilings.** Per-tier AI included-budget ceilings are authoritative in §34.1 (plan tier definitions) and §34.10 (AI Wallet Service). Per-Org wallet behavior, overage, cap enforcement, and auto-topup semantics are authoritative in §34.10. §44.2 does not restate per-tier budget values; consumers MUST reference §34.1 and §34.10 for the authoritative AI-consumption budget limits.

## 44.3 Optimization Strategies {#44.3-optimization-strategies}

- **Code Splitting:** Routes lazily loaded. Command Palette and advanced features code-split.  
- **Database Indexing:** Requirements indexed by workspace\_id \+ status. Vendors by organization\_id. Scores by (workspace\_id, vendor\_id, requirement\_id) composite.  
- **Caching:** Workspace metadata (10-min TTL). Vendor profiles (1-hour TTL). Scoring rubrics (permanent, versioned).  
- **Compression:** GZIP for API responses and static assets.  
- **CDN:** Vercel's global edge network for static assets.  
- **Real-time Optimizations:** Convex subscriptions use delta updates (send only changed fields, not full entities).

## 44.4 Load Testing {#44.4-load-testing}

- **Monthly:** 500 concurrent users. Target p95 \< 1s.  
- **Quarterly:** 5× spike tests (2,500 concurrent users). Target p95 \< 3s (degraded but functional).  
- **Quarterly:** 24-hour endurance test (steady 100 concurrent users). Monitor for memory leaks, connection exhaustion.

## 44.5 Acceptance Criteria {#44.5-acceptance-criteria}

- Production p95 latency consistently \< 500ms (excluding Agent calls).  
- Production p99 latency consistently \< 1s (excluding Agent calls).  
- No single API call times out (server-side timeout — see §44.1 authoritative table; the 30s hard-ceiling value is registered there per Phase 12.5 R-03 closure).  
- Real-time collaborative features sync \< 200ms (measured via WebSocket delta timing).  
- Agent calls stay within budget (95% within allotted time, 5% timeout with graceful degradation).

## 44.6 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment {#44.6-solo-tier-surface-treatment}

**Phase 14.10 — landed under v7.1 integration program (2026-04-28).**

**Authoring Intent.** §44.6 is the authoritative landing for the Phase 14.10 "AI Consumption Invisibility for Solo" surface contract. The Solo tier (Buyer Solo per §34.1.1; Seller Solo per §34.1.2) preserves the entire AIOperation engine — accepted/rejected metering (§4.8.1), value-dollar/cost-dollar accounting (§34.3.1), OutcomeContract settlement via the Outcome Resolver (§34.11), CostBaseRecalculationLog (§4.8.6 / §34.3.3), free-allowance accounting (§4.8.7), wallet posting (§4.8.3 / §34.10), residency-locked invoicing (§4.8.1 `legal_entity` mapping) — for accounting fidelity and §34.18 margin protection, while compressing every customer-visible AI-consumption surface to a single fixed billing line item. The contract resolves a Solo-specific tension: Buyer Maya and Seller Maya are personal-card operators who cannot reason about value-dollars, rate cards, OutcomeContracts, wallet utilization, or per-capability cost; the engine must continue to meter every operation to detect margin erosion before it compounds.

**Section-numbering note (Phase 14.10 — 2026-04-28).** Phase 14.10's brief named "§44 (Consumption Model)" as the read- and edit-target. In the v7.0.0 baseline §44 is *Performance Requirements*; the consumption-model machinery — cost-base recalculation, the per-capability Outcome Resolver — lives in §34.3.3 / §34.11 / §4.8.6. The cross-references already landed in Phases 14.4 → 14.9 (e.g., §34.1.1 cell **AI Budget**, §34.1.2 cell **AI Budget**, §34.10.3 Solo-co-resident rule, §22.20.5, Appendix M row "Solo-tier engine-absorbed AI envelope") consistently cite "§44 (Solo-Tier Surface Treatment, Phase 14.10)" as the authoritative landing for this content; resolution per the §2 source-of-truth hierarchy is to honor those cross-references and land the sub-section here. The phase-prompt's "(Consumption Model)" parenthetical was a misnomer and is reconciled in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Phase 14.10 → Section-Numbering Reconciliation`.

**Cross-references.** §34.1.1 (Buyer Solo plan registration) and §34.1.2 (Seller Solo plan registration) define the plans this section governs. §34.10.3 (Solo-co-resident pool rule) governs how Solo's engine-absorbed envelope interacts with the contralateral console's wallet. §34.2.5 (Solo-Tier Per-Evaluation / Per-Bid Charge Orchestration) governs the alternative one-time-charge path. §22.20.5 (Seller Maya Surface Abstraction — silent AI surface) cites §44.6 as authoritative for AIOp consumption invisibility. §3.13 (Principle 9 — Surface Simplicity, Engine Complexity) is the doctrinal parent. Appendix M rows under "Solo-Tier Surface Treatment (§44.6)" carry the per-engine-concept surface-vs-engine contract.

Each item names the engine concept and cites its authoritative spec home; the engine continues to compute and persist the underlying values without surface exposure.

4. **Per-capability rate card** and any inline rate-card link from an AI-using surface — §34.3.4.
5. **Per-AIOperation Billing Ledger row breakdown** (`value_price_cents`, `cost_price_cents`, `effective_charge_cents`, `cost_base_cents`, `provenance_hash`) — §4.8.1.
6. **FreeAllowanceCounter inline counter** ("{N} of 10 free runs left") — §4.8.7. Counter continues to track engine-side; the inline surface is suppressed on Solo.
7. **AIWallet state badges** (`active`, `soft_warned_50`, `soft_warned_80`, `hard_capped_100`, `payment_failed_grace`) — §4.8.3 / §34.10.1.
8. **Contest CTA on per-AIOperation rows** — §34.11.2 / §4.8.5. Contest filing is suspended on Solo (§44.6.7 #6 governs the residual case).
9. **Cost-base 30-day breaking-change banner** — §34.3.3 / §4.8.9. Engine continues to publish per §4.8.9; the in-app banner is suppressed on Solo because Solo is not exposed to per-capability pricing.
10. **PostHog wallet-counter freshness diagnostics** (`aiwallet_counter_freshness_breach`, `seller_aiwallet_budget_exhausted_during_onboarding` per §48.8.4) — events continue to fire engine-side; the in-app surfacing is suppressed on Solo per §22.20.5 #4.

The single permitted billing-related surface on Solo is the single-card line item authored in §44.6.2.

The Public Pricing API at `api.sourcera.com/v1/pricing` (§4.8.9 PricingTableVersion) continues to publish the full rate card unchanged for engineering transparency, partner integrations, and finance audit. Public-API output is not in-app surface; the §44.6.1 hide list applies to in-app surfaces only. A Solo Org that calls the Public Pricing API receives the same payload as every other tier per §4.8.9 acceptance criterion #1.
