### 44.6.3 Margin Envelope Defaults {#44.6.3-margin-envelope-defaults}

The Solo margin envelope is the engine-absorbed value-dollar ceiling against which Solo AI consumption is measured for throttling and margin-protection purposes. The envelope is per-console and per-billing-mode; it is never customer-visible.

| Plan tier | Billing mode | Margin envelope (default) | Cited cell |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `buyer_solo` | Subscription | $5 absorbed value-dollars / month | §34.1.1 cell **AI Budget** (Buyer Solo column); BPS §5.2 |
| `buyer_solo` | Per-evaluation | $5 absorbed value-dollars / completed evaluation | §34.1.1 cell **AI Budget**; §34.2.5; BPS §5.2 |
| `seller_solo` | Subscription | $5 absorbed value-dollars / month | §34.1.2 cell **AI Budget** (Seller Solo column); SPS §5.2 |
| `seller_solo` | Per-bid | $5 absorbed value-dollars / submitted bid | §34.1.2 cell **AI Budget**; §34.2.5; SPS §5.2 |

Per Authoring Convention #10, §44.6.3 cites §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 / §34.2.5 for the value-dollar ceilings and never restates them. Any future change to the Solo absorbed envelope amount MUST land in §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 / §34.2.5 first; §44.6.3 follows. Deploy-time validator `solo_envelope_value_single_source` (§44.6.8 #13) asserts.

**Per-capability override.** The envelope is per-capability configurable. Ops Finance (`ops_finance_admin`) MAY override the default envelope contribution on a per-capability basis via the §4.8.2 CapabilityRegistryEntry `solo_envelope_override_value_cents` field (Authored Extension — Phase 14.10; flagged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Phase 14.10 → Authored Extensions`). When set, the override governs that capability's contribution to the Solo envelope budget independent of the standard `value_price_cents` and `cost_price_cents` per §34.3.1. The override is a margin-protection lever, not a customer-facing rate adjustment; Public Pricing API continues to publish the standard value/cost rate.

**First-Pass RFP Generator exemption (Seller Solo).** The First-Pass RFP Draft capability (`first_pass_rfp_draft` per §21.4.1.E / §22.10; canonical capability_id registered at §21.4.1.E per the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.3 D-EM-003 closure — the prior non-canonical alias `first_pass_rfp_response_generator` was rewritten to canonical form at the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.5 loose-ends closure 2026-05-19 per D-NOM-016 P2; legacy alias preserved as an `aliases` array entry on the §21.4.1.E row for SDK back-compat) MUST NOT bid-wall a Solo seller mid-response per the SPS §5 contract and the §34.1.2 cell **First-Pass RFP Response Generator** annotation ("no mid-bid budget wall"). The capability is exempt from envelope-exhaustion blocking on Solo: the engine continues to meter, and once envelope exhaustion is detected, the capability falls back to the §44.6.3 fallback policy (continue to serve at engine cost; Ops alert per §44.6.5 `solo.envelope.exhausted`). This exemption is registered as a §4.8.2 capability flag `solo_envelope_no_block=true` on the §21.4.1.E row.

### 44.6.4 Throttling Behavior {#44.6.4-throttling-behavior}

When a Solo Org's actual consumption against its margin envelope reaches `throttling_threshold` (default 80%, configured per Capability Registry per §4.8.2; range 50–95), the engine SHALL silently throttle the subset of capabilities whose `surface_throttling_class = low_priority_background` (registered in §44.6.4.1). Capabilities outside that class — i.e., the operator's active workflow — are NEVER throttled.

The throttling action SHALL:

1. Suppress new invocations of `low_priority_background` capabilities for the remainder of the envelope window. The window closes at: subscription billing-cycle rollover (subscription mode); successful new $199 charge (per-evaluation or per-bid mode); explicit Ops manual clear via OpsActionRecord.
2. NOT cancel or interrupt any in-flight AIOperation. In-flight operations settle normally per §34.11 (Outcome Resolver `pending → accepted | auto_accepted | rejected | reversed`).
3. Emit a single in-app toast per Org per throttling-state transition: **"Some background suggestions paused — your active workflow is unaffected."** The toast respects §29.3 user preferences (quiet hours), but is NEVER suppressed by DND because the suppressed capability set may otherwise surface as an unexplained absence.
4. NOT surface a per-capability detail pane, a value-dollar consumption number, an envelope-percentage indicator, or an upgrade CTA inline. The throttling toast is the ONLY customer-visible surface.
5. Continue to write engine-side metering rows. AIOperation writes for suppressed invocations are written with `effective_charge_cents = 0` and `solo_envelope_blocked = true` (Authored Extension flag on §4.8.1; Phase 14.10) for audit and the §44.6.5 telemetry stream.
6. Auto-clear when the underlying envelope counter resets at the boundary above; the surface emits no recovery toast (the operator never knew it happened).

The throttling state is per-console: a Buyer Solo Org with concurrent Seller Free has independent envelope counters and independent throttling states (per §34.10.3 Solo-co-resident rule).

#### 44.6.4.1 `surface_throttling_class` (Capability-Registry Field & Enum)

Field added to §4.8.2 CapabilityRegistryEntry (Authored Extension — Phase 14.10; previously forward-referenced from Appendix M Solo-tier engine-absorbed AI envelope row, now formally registered).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `surface_throttling_class` | Enum | See Appendix J `surface_throttling_class` (new — Phase 14.10): `active_workflow`, `low_priority_background`, `never_throttle` | Default `active_workflow`. Drives §44.6.4 throttling behavior on Solo Orgs. Capabilities with `surface_throttling_class = never_throttle` are exempt from envelope-exhaustion suppression in all cases (e.g., critical billing capabilities). The First-Pass RFP Response Generator carries `surface_throttling_class = active_workflow` AND the `solo_envelope_no_block=true` flag per §44.6.3. |
| `solo_envelope_override_value_cents` | Integer | Nullable; ≥ 0 | Per §44.6.3 per-capability override. Null = use standard `value_price_cents`. |
| `solo_envelope_no_block` | Boolean | Default false | Per §44.6.3 First-Pass RFP exemption. When true, the capability invokes successfully even when the Solo envelope is exhausted; the cost is absorbed by the platform per §34.3.5; an Ops alert fires per §44.6.5. |

Appendix J registration: `surface_throttling_class` enum values are `active_workflow`, `low_priority_background`, `never_throttle`. Source authority: §44.6.4.1.

The v7.1 Solo-throttling membership of `low_priority_background` is exactly the following capability ids, registered as §4.8.2-fidelity `CapabilityRegistryEntry` rows at **§21.4.6 Solo Throttling Membership** (v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.4 D-EM-004 closure, 2026-05-19):

- `proactive_cmd_k_marketplace_surfacing` (proactive Cmd+K Marketplace suggestions; §21.4.6 Row 1; `billing_mode=customer_billed`; `console=[buyer]`)
- `weekly_kb_refresh_suggestions` (weekly KB refresh cadence per §22.20.3; §21.4.6 Row 2; `billing_mode=customer_billed`; `console=[seller]`)
- `vendor_page_enrichment_polling` (passive vendor-page enrichment poller; §21.4.6 Row 3; `billing_mode=sourcera_owned`; `console=[seller]`)

§21.4.6 is the canonical §4.8.2-shape authority; this enumeration is the readable customer/spec-reader summary preserved in-place. The runtime path `ctx.db.capabilityRegistryEntry(capabilityId)` resolves each of the three identifiers to the corresponding §21.4.6 row at the §34.8.2 entitlement-enforcement layer; the §44.6.4 silent-throttling engine reads `cap.surface_throttling_class === 'low_priority_background'` directly from the registry. The closed-set integrity invariant is asserted by the §M.5 meta-gate `low_priority_background_solo_throttling_membership_canonical` per §21.4.6 — adding a fourth member without updating both the §21.4.6 table AND the §M.5 meta-gate enumeration is a `closed_set_integrity_violation` P0 defect.

Adding or removing a capability from `low_priority_background` is an Ops Finance + Founder dual-signoff action per the §4.8.2 capability-registry edit governance, triggers a §4.8.9 PricingTableVersion publish (the rate card itself does not change, but the registry version does, for partner-integration freshness), AND requires extending the §M.5 catalog meta-gate enumeration per §21.4.6.

### 44.6.5 Engine Telemetry, Webhook Catalog, and Ops Routing {#44.6.5-engine-telemetry-and-ops-routing}

Phase 14.10 introduces the following engine telemetry. None of these events surface to the Solo customer; all route to Ops, the Billing Admin (cross-console only when operating both consoles in pooled-wallet mode — N/A on pure Solo + Solo per §34.10.3), and the §44.6 internal margin-protection dashboards.

| Event | Trigger | Recipient | Webhook? | In-App? | Email? | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `solo.envelope.throttling_engaged` | Solo Org consumption first crosses `throttling_threshold` in the current envelope window | Ops Finance dashboard | Yes | No | No | Includes `console`, `plan_tier`, `envelope_window_id`, `consumed_value_cents`, `envelope_value_cents`. Engine-side only; the customer-facing surface is the §44.6.4 toast. |
| `solo.envelope.throttling_cleared` | Envelope counter resets at billing-cycle rollover (subscription) or new $199 charge (per-evaluation / per-bid) or Ops manual clear | Ops Finance dashboard | Yes | No | No | Includes `clear_reason ∈ {subscription_rollover, per_eval_charge, per_bid_charge, manual_ops_clear}`. |
| `solo.envelope.exhausted` | Solo Org actual cost exceeds 100% of envelope (margin-protection breach) | Ops Finance + Sales Ops alert (proactive outreach trigger) | Yes | Yes (Ops only) | Yes (Ops only) | Generalizes the §22.20.5 #3 reference event `seller_aiwallet_solo_envelope_exhausted` to both consoles. No automatic in-app upsell; Ops decides on outreach. |
| `solo.capability.envelope_no_block_invoked` | A capability with `solo_envelope_no_block=true` (e.g., `first_pass_rfp_draft` per §21.4.1.E — the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.3 / 4.5 canonical capability_id; prior narrative alias "First-Pass RFP Response Generator" rewritten to canonical-citation form at Phase 4.5 D-NOM-016 P2 closure 2026-05-19) is invoked while the envelope is exhausted | Ops Finance dashboard (capacity planning) | Yes | No | No | Counts the volume of margin-absorbed protected-workflow invocations to detect Solo unit-economics drift. |

These events are registered in **Appendix C → Billing-Domain Events** under "Solo-Tier Surface Treatment (§44.6)" and in **Appendix G → PostHog Event Taxonomy** with property schemas (Authored Extension — Phase 14.10; Appendix C / Appendix G additions flagged). Event delivery follows §31 (HMAC-SHA256, idempotency via `event_id`, Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve, DLQ after 5 failures, payload ≤ 256 KB).

The customer-facing notification suppression is intentional and enforced. A Solo Org MUST NEVER receive an in-app or email notification originating from the four events above; the §29.3 notification-preferences UI on Solo MUST NOT expose these event types as user-toggleable. Receipt of any of these events on a Solo customer's webhook subscription, in-app inbox, or email is a P0 surface defect (per Appendix M Process Gate #6 — Tier visibility integrity).

#### 44.6.5.A Sustained Throttling Upgrade-CTA Aggregation

**Authoritative trigger.** §34.5.4 is the plan-upgrade behavior contract. This subsection defines the engine aggregation that feeds it. The raw §44.6.5 events remain Ops-only; the only customer-visible output is the redacted `billing.solo_upgrade_cta.triggered` event plus the corresponding `upgrade_cta_viewed` UI analytics event.

| Mode | Input event(s) | Aggregation rule | Trigger mode | Output |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Subscription (`buyer_solo`, `seller_solo`) | `solo.envelope.throttling_engaged` | First time the Org reaches ≥ 3 events in a rolling 30-day window for the same console | `subscription_throttling_3_in_30d` | Write `billing.solo_upgrade_cta.triggered`; render CTA on §44.6.2 / §34.5 surfaces only |
| Buyer per-evaluation (`buyer_solo` one-time charge) | `solo.envelope.exhausted` | First event inside the charged evaluation envelope window | `per_eval_envelope_hit` | Same output; target plan `business_starter` |
| Seller per-bid (`seller_solo` one-time charge) | `solo.envelope.exhausted` | First event inside the charged bid envelope window | `per_bid_envelope_hit` | Same output; target plan `seller_starter` |

**Payload redaction.** `billing.solo_upgrade_cta.triggered` MUST carry the minimum fields needed to render and attribute the CTA: `org_id`, `console`, `plan_from`, `plan_to`, `solo_upgrade_cta_trigger_mode`, `source_event_id`, `envelope_window_id`, `rolling_window_started_at` (nullable for per-evaluation / per-bid), `cta_surface`, and `cta_copy_variant`. It MUST NOT carry value-dollar envelope amounts, Anthropic cost values, per-capability spend, raw prompt/response content, vendor identity, buyer identity, or source-document snippets.

**State handling.** The aggregation worker writes a single trigger row under the §4.8.1 AIOperation transaction boundary that produced the qualifying source event. If the output write fails, the source event remains Ops-visible and the aggregation worker retries with the idempotency keys in §34.5.4. If the Org upgrades before the retry succeeds, the worker suppresses the CTA and writes an Ops-only audit note instead of rendering a stale prompt.

**No-toast upsell invariant.** The §44.6.4 throttling toast remains copy-stable: "Some background suggestions paused — your active workflow is unaffected." The toast does not link to §34.5, does not include the target plan, and does not expose envelope-pressure counts. The upgrade CTA is a separate plan-change affordance and is tested by `solo_upgrade_cta_threshold_3_events_30d_subscription_immediate_per_eval_bid` (§M.5.22).

### 44.6.6 Public Pricing API Behavior on Solo {#44.6.6-public-pricing-api-behavior-on-solo}

The Public Pricing API at `api.sourcera.com/v1/pricing` (§4.8.9 PricingTableVersion) continues to emit the full rate card unchanged for any caller — including a Solo Org calling with its own API token (post-upgrade scenarios) or any unauthenticated caller. This is the engineering-transparency contract: rate-card publication is decoupled from in-app surface treatment.

A Solo Org that pins a PricingTableVersion via §4.8.9 receives the same pinning semantics as any other tier. The pin is engine-side; it is not surfaced in-app on Solo. Solo Orgs do not have access to the API add-on at the in-app level (per §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 cell **API Add-On**; Solo is excluded), but the public unauthenticated `GET /v1/pricing` endpoint is accessible to any caller per §4.8.9 acceptance criterion #1.

### 44.6.7 Edge Cases & Failure Modes {#44.6.7-edge-cases-and-failure-modes}

1. **Solo Org operates both consoles (Buyer Solo + Seller Solo).** Two independent engine-side envelope counters per §34.10.3; two independent throttling states per §44.6.4. The single billing card per §44.6.2 renders twice (once per console); no consolidated "Solo Bundle" card exists. Per §34.12.6, no Solo-bundle discount is applied.
2. **Solo Org upgrades to Starter+ mid-period.** Per §34.5 / §34.10.3 Solo-co-resident rule item 5, the engine-absorbed envelope counter closes at the upgrade billing-rollover boundary; the AIWallet widget activates with the new plan's value-dollar budget; pre-upgrade AIOperations remain Solo-absorbed and never retroactively bill. The single billing card per §44.6.2 is replaced with the Starter+ wallet widget at the same boundary.
3. **Solo Org downgrades to Free.** Per §34.6 / §34.19 / §34.10.3 Solo-co-resident rule item 6, the envelope counter closes; Free's $5 hard-capped Wallet activates at the downgrade billing-rollover boundary; the wallet widget renders for Free per existing §34.10 / Appendix M row "AIWallet" (line 45808 baseline). Excess data per §34.6 / §4.8.10 is preserved 90-day read-only.
4. **Solo Org's actual cost approaches `throttling_threshold` mid-active-workflow.** Throttling does NOT engage on `active_workflow` capabilities per §44.6.4. The active workflow continues; only `low_priority_background` capabilities are suppressed for the remainder of the envelope window. The operator perceives a single toast and proceeds without interruption.
5. **Solo Org's actual cost crosses 100% of envelope (margin-protection breach).** The `solo.envelope.exhausted` event fires (§44.6.5); Ops Finance is alerted; no customer-facing notification fires. The operator continues to operate at engine cost (the engine absorbs the overage); Ops decides on proactive outreach. This is a deliberate trade — the alternative (surfacing the overage) would defeat the §44.6.1 surface contract.
6. **Customer-filed contest of an absorbed AIOperation.** Suppressed on Solo per §44.6.1 #8: the §34.11.2 Contest CTA does not render. Engine-side, an absorbed AIOperation is `effective_charge_cents = 0`; there is nothing to contest from the customer's perspective. Ops-side contest filing remains available via the Ops Console.
7. **Per-evaluation Buyer Solo abandons mid-eval before charge captures.** Per §34.2.5 Buyer Solo failure-mode, the Workspace remains in `solo_per_eval_charge_pending` state for ≤ 24h with retry CTA; the engine envelope counter for that pending evaluation is engaged; throttling on `low_priority_background` capabilities applies; on retry success, the per-evaluation $5 envelope ceiling activates.
8. **Per-bid Seller Solo abandons mid-bid before charge captures.** Per §34.2.5 Seller Solo failure-mode; same envelope/throttling semantics as #7 with `solo_per_bid_charge_pending` state.
9. **Anthropic price spike during a Solo billing cycle.** Solo's value/cost prices are locked at AIOperation write time per §4.8.1 / §34.11; CostBaseRecalculationLog runs nightly per §34.3.3. A price spike does NOT retroactively adjust Solo's envelope spend; the new cost_base applies only to operations created after the recalc's effective time. If the spike pushes blended Solo unit economics below the 88% margin floor (§34.3.3), the `cost_base_recalc.margin_floor_breach` event fires per §34.11.3 to Ops Finance; Solo customers are unaffected at the surface level until the next billing cycle.
10. **Throttled `low_priority_background` capability becomes critical mid-period.** Reclassifying a capability from `low_priority_background` to `active_workflow` requires Ops Finance + Founder dual-signoff per §44.6.4.1. Existing in-progress envelope windows continue with the old classification through the current period; the new classification takes effect at the next envelope rollover to avoid mid-window throttling churn (§44.6.8 #12).
11. **Solo Org creates an API token (post-upgrade) and queries `/v1/billing/operations`.** Per §4.8.1, the Org-scoped billing-operations endpoint returns AIOperation rows. On a former-Solo Org, historical rows include the absorbed-envelope operations with `solo_envelope_blocked=true` and `effective_charge_cents = 0`; the field-set is preserved for forensic and DSAR purposes. The endpoint is NOT in-app surface; this is an engineering-transparency channel parallel to the Public Pricing API.
12. **DSAR by a Solo operator under §6.8.1.** Engine-side AIOperation rows with `effective_charge_cents = 0` are returned with the same field-redaction policy as paid-tier rows per §4.8.1 AC #12. The `solo_envelope_blocked` flag is operational metadata (not subject PII) and is NOT redacted.
13. **Webhook subscription on a Solo Org.** Solo Orgs MAY have one webhook endpoint per §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 cell **Webhook Endpoints** (1 endpoint, mirroring Free). Per §44.6.5, the four §44.6 events MUST NOT route to a Solo Org's webhook endpoint. CI gate `solo_telemetry_no_customer_routing` (§44.6.8 #8) asserts.
14. **Third-party AI provider outage during Solo session.** The §22.10 / §44.1 third-party-outage protocol applies unchanged. AIOperations attempted during the degraded window settle to `rejected` with `failure_reason=external_provider_outage` per §22.10; the cost-base routing per §34.3.5 applies; no customer-facing wall renders on Solo (the outage manifests as the active-workflow capability returning a degraded result with the standard "Sourcera AI is temporarily unavailable" copy per §3.7).
15. **Concurrent envelope-window writes (e.g., burst of low-priority invocations within the same second).** Per the §4.8.1 optimistic-locking pattern, simultaneous suppress decisions are serialized on the `(org_id, console, envelope_window_id)` key; only one writer transitions to `throttled`; the rest receive the resulting suppressed-write state without double-toast.

### 44.6.8 Acceptance Criteria {#44.6.8-acceptance-criteria}

1. **`solo_surface_hides_wallet`.** A reactive read of any in-app surface on a Solo Org (`buyer_solo` or `seller_solo`) MUST NOT include the AIWallet widget, the wallet-overage configuration UI, the auto-topup configuration UI, or any per-capability rate-card affordance per §44.6.1. QA test asserts every UX surface authored in `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` and rendered on Solo passes a DOM snapshot check excluding the suppressed selector set.
2. **`solo_billing_single_card_invariant`.** The single permitted billing-related surface on Solo is the §44.6.2 single-card line item. A second billing surface (wallet widget, rate-card link, per-AIOperation breakdown) rendering on a Solo Org's UI is a P0 defect.
3. **`solo_engine_metering_parity`.** Every AIOperation written by a Solo Org MUST be metered with `value_price_cents` and `cost_price_cents` per §34.3.1, MUST settle through the §34.11 Outcome Resolver, and MUST appear in the §4.8.6 CostBaseRecalculationLog as a contributor to the cost-base computation. The engine path is identical to paid-tier Orgs; only the surface differs.
4. **`solo_envelope_throttling_threshold_default`.** The default `throttling_threshold` is 80% of envelope. Per-capability override is admitted via §4.8.2; an override outside the 50–95 range is rejected with HTTP 422 `solo_envelope_throttling_threshold_out_of_range` (new; Appendix I).
5. **`solo_envelope_throttling_targets_low_priority_background_only`.** Capabilities with `surface_throttling_class ∈ {active_workflow, never_throttle}` MUST NEVER be suppressed by Solo envelope throttling. QA test asserts that every capability member of the §44.6.4.1 v7.1 `low_priority_background` set is suppressed at threshold breach AND every capability outside the set continues to invoke normally.
6. **`solo_envelope_first_pass_rfp_no_block`.** The First-Pass RFP Response Generator capability MUST NOT block on envelope exhaustion for a Solo Org per §44.6.3 (`solo_envelope_no_block=true` flag). QA test `seller_solo_first_pass_rfp_envelope_exhaustion_no_block` asserts the capability invokes successfully when envelope is at 100%.
7. **`solo_throttling_toast_single_emission`.** The throttling toast per §44.6.4 #3 fires AT MOST ONCE per Org per envelope window. Subsequent suppressed invocations within the same window are silent.
8. **`solo_telemetry_no_customer_routing`.** The four events at §44.6.5 (`solo.envelope.throttling_engaged`, `solo.envelope.throttling_cleared`, `solo.envelope.exhausted`, `solo.capability.envelope_no_block_invoked`) MUST route to Ops Finance and MUST NOT be delivered to the Solo Org's webhook subscription, in-app inbox, or email channels per §29.3. CI gate asserts.
9. **`solo_public_pricing_api_unchanged`.** A `GET /v1/pricing` request from a Solo Org's caller context MUST return the full PricingTableVersion payload identical to any other tier per §4.8.9 AC #1. The Public Pricing API does not gate on plan tier.
10. **`solo_envelope_clears_at_boundary`.** The throttling state MUST auto-clear at: (a) subscription billing-cycle rollover for `buyer_solo` or `seller_solo` subscription mode; (b) successful new $199 charge for per-evaluation or per-bid mode; (c) explicit Ops manual clear via OpsActionRecord. No customer-facing recovery toast fires.
11. **`solo_envelope_no_in_app_upsell`.** The throttling toast MUST NOT include an upgrade CTA, a "buy more budget" button, or a link to the §34.5 plan-change surface. Sustained envelope pressure MAY produce the separate §34.5.4 / §44.6.5.A upgrade CTA, but the toast itself remains a non-upsell operational notice.
12. **`solo_throttling_class_change_takes_effect_at_next_envelope_rollover`.** Updates to a CapabilityRegistryEntry's `surface_throttling_class` MUST NOT take effect mid-envelope-window for any Solo Org currently in that window; the new classification applies at the next envelope rollover per §44.6.7 #10.
13. **`solo_envelope_value_single_source`.** The Solo envelope default ($5 absorbed value-dollars per §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 / §34.2.5) is cited from §34, never restated inline at §44.6 except as a non-authoritative illustration in §44.6.3. Deploy-time validator asserts no other section restates the envelope value.
14. **`solo_billing_card_price_single_source`.** The §44.6.2 single-card content MUST source prices from §34.2.1 / §34.2.2 / §34.2.5 verbatim at presentation time. Static prices in component code are forbidden. CI gate asserts.
15. **`solo_envelope_exhausted_no_workflow_break`.** The `solo.envelope.exhausted` event firing (§44.6.5) MUST NOT block, slow, or interrupt any active-workflow capability invocation. The engine continues to absorb the overage; the surface continues to operate normally.
16. **`solo_envelope_per_console_isolation`.** A Buyer Solo + Seller Solo Org operating both consoles MUST have two independent envelope counters and two independent throttling states per §34.10.3 / §44.6.4. QA test asserts that throttling on one console does not affect the other.
17. **`solo_capability_registry_field_registration`.** The §4.8.2 CapabilityRegistryEntry MUST carry `surface_throttling_class`, `solo_envelope_override_value_cents`, and `solo_envelope_no_block` as defined in §44.6.4.1. Schema-validation test on the CapabilityRegistryEntry table asserts.
18. **`solo_aiwallet_solo_envelope_exhausted_event_alias`.** The historical reference `seller_aiwallet_solo_envelope_exhausted` (per §22.20.5 #3 / §17.8 line 17818 baseline) maps 1:1 to `solo.envelope.exhausted` (§44.6.5) with `console=seller`, `plan_tier=seller_solo`. Webhook subscribers receive the canonical `solo.envelope.exhausted` event; the alias is preserved as a back-compat citation only.
19. **`solo_upgrade_cta_threshold_3_events_30d_subscription_immediate_per_eval_bid`.** The §44.6.5.A aggregation worker MUST emit `billing.solo_upgrade_cta.triggered` only when: (a) subscription-mode Solo has ≥ 3 `solo.envelope.throttling_engaged` source events in a rolling 30-day window for the same `(org_id, console)`; (b) Buyer Solo per-evaluation receives the first `solo.envelope.exhausted` event in the charged evaluation; OR (c) Seller Solo per-bid receives the first `solo.envelope.exhausted` event in the charged bid. QA asserts target-plan correctness (`business_starter` for Buyer, `seller_starter` for Seller), CTA placement outside the throttling toast, and redacted payload shape.

## 44.7 FTC Native-Ad Compliance Observation {#44.7-ftc-native-ad-compliance-observation}

**Scope.** §44.7 is the runtime observation contract for buyer-visible native-ad disclosure labels on Marketplace Discovery surfaces. In v7.1.1 it binds FeaturedPlacement (§4.4.20); PromotedListing's click/impression funnel remains governed by §34.16.7 and Appendix G. The goal is compliance evidence, not customer notification: every successful FeaturedPlacement render that includes the FTC label + tooltip creates a §4.3.18 Usage Event row and an Appendix G PostHog mirror, but no Appendix C webhook or §29 notification is emitted.

**Observation event.** `featured_placement_ftc_disclosure_rendered` fires from the server-side public-render compositor after the render payload includes `ftc_disclosure_label`, the accessible tooltip affordance, and the WCAG contrast assertion. Client-side hydration MAY emit diagnostics, but it MUST NOT be the source of compliance truth because client-side blockers can suppress scripts. The server-side observation is idempotent per `render_observation_id` and joins to `FeaturedPlacement.id`.

**Latency and persistence.** The p99 enqueue budget is §44.1 `FeaturedPlacement FTC disclosure observation latency`. The first successful observation stamps `FeaturedPlacement.ftc_disclosure_first_observed_render_at` when null; each successful observation updates `ftc_disclosure_last_observed_render_at`. The per-render proof remains the §4.3.18 Usage Event row keyed by Appendix G `render_observation_id`.

**Required event properties.**

| Property | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| `featured_placement_id` | UUID; required; joins to §4.4.20 |
| `seller_org_id` | UUID; required; featured seller |
| `seller_software_id` | UUID; nullable; populated for software-level placement |
| `target_entity_type` | Appendix J `featured_placement_target_entity_type` |
| `target_entity_id` | UUID; required |
| `placement_surface` | Appendix J `featured_placement_surface` |
| `slot_kind` | Appendix J `featured_placement_slot_kind` |
| `slot_position` | Integer 0-19 |
| `placement_mode` | Appendix J `featured_placement_mode` |
| `viewer_org_id` | UUID; nullable for anonymous marketplace reads |
| `viewer_session_id_hash` | SHA-256 12-hex truncation; required for anonymous-session dedup |
| `render_observation_id` | UUID; required idempotency join key |
| `render_observed_at` | Timestamp; UTC |
| `ftc_disclosure_label` | String; MUST equal the rendered label from §4.4.20 |
| `tooltip_present` | Boolean; MUST be true for successful observation |
| `wcag_contrast_passed` | Boolean; MUST be true for successful observation |
| `observation_latency_ms` | Integer; measured from render composition to Usage Event enqueue |

**Failure handling.**

1. If the server-side compositor cannot prove the label + tooltip are present, it MUST NOT emit the success event; it emits a §42 P1 marketplace-compliance alert with the `featured_placement_id`.
2. If §4.3.18 Usage Event persistence succeeds but PostHog delivery fails, the Usage Event row remains the compliance record and the PostHog outbox follows §4.3.18 retry / DLQ.
3. If an active FeaturedPlacement has no successful observation within 60 seconds of `active_from`, Marketplace Ops is paged, paid-mode activation is blocked for that row, and editorial-mode rendering carries an Ops-visible warning until the next successful observation.
4. If `wcag_contrast_passed=false`, the render is treated as a compliance failure even if the label text exists; the surface follows §3.11 contrast remediation and §42 incident triage.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Every active FeaturedPlacement render on CategoryPage, ComparisonPage, and HeatMapCell MUST emit `featured_placement_ftc_disclosure_rendered` within §44.1 `FeaturedPlacement FTC disclosure observation latency`.
2. The first successful observation MUST stamp `ftc_disclosure_first_observed_render_at`; subsequent observations MUST keep the first timestamp immutable and update `ftc_disclosure_last_observed_render_at`.
3. The event MUST carry no buyer requirement text, search-query text, scores, or buyer-internal metadata; payload review enforces the same marketplace-domain firewall posture as §4.4.20.
4. A synthetic fixture with disabled client-side JavaScript MUST still produce a server-side observation event, proving that client telemetry is not the compliance source of truth.
5. A stale-observation sweep MUST detect active placements whose last observation is older than the configured public-render freshness window and page Marketplace Ops.

# 45\. Privacy & Abuse Prevention {#45.-privacy-&-abuse-prevention}

## 45.1 Data Privacy {#45.1-data-privacy}

- **Data Ownership:** All customer data owned by the Organization. Sourcera is Data Processor.  
- **Model Training:** No customer data used for model training. Claude calls do not train models.  
- **Analytics:** Aggregated anonymized metrics sent to PostHog for product analytics (feature adoption, user behavior). No PII in analytics events.  
- **Error Logs:** May include non-sensitive metadata (user ID, feature name, error code) but never requirement text, response data, or customer-specific scores.  
- **Data Processor Agreement (DPA):** Available for all plans. Sourcera signs DPA for GDPR compliance.  
- **Subprocessor List:** Published at sourcera.io/compliance/subprocessors. Updated quarterly.
- **Vendor Opt-Out Global Registry:** Seller-side public Marketplace identity suppression is authoritative at §27.10, backed by the §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Record and §4.5.6 Marketplace-Domain Read/Render Contract. §27.10 owns authority attestation, enforcement surfaces, latency SLOs, webhooks, DSAR / retention / residency behavior, and CI guardrails; §45.1 routes to that contract and does not restate its numerical controls.
- **Right-to-Erasure Retained-Row Authority:** §45.1 does not define financial-record or platform-integrity exemptions. The canonical retained-row classes are §6.8.5, with retention windows in §40.2. Privacy / security text that needs an erasure exception MUST cite the specific §6.8.5 row and the applicable §40.2 row rather than a generic §45.1 exemption.

## 45.2 Abuse Prevention {#45.2-abuse-prevention}

- **Rate Limiting:** §32.4.5 is the canonical rate-limit-class registry. Abuse-prevention readers MUST resolve public pricing to `public_pricing_unauth`, public Marketplace reads to `marketplace_public_unauth`, authenticated Marketplace reads / writes to `marketplace_read` / `marketplace_write`, taxonomy reads to `marketplace_taxonomy_read`, EOI submission caps to §48.4.12 / §4.4.26, abuse-report create caps to §4.5.7, vendor opt-out authority-probe caps to §27.10.9, and Promoted Listing auction / frequency controls to §27.11.2. §45 does not restate class limits.  
- **Login Throttling:** Exponential backoff after 5 failed attempts (WorkOS-managed). Account locked per the §33.6 authoritative lockout row (15 minutes; cited from §33.6 per Phase 12.5 R-04 closure — do not duplicate the value here).  
- **API Token Rotation:** Recommended 90 days. Enforced for Enterprise (token expires after 90 days).  
- **Response Validation and KB Moderation:** Rendered responses use sandboxed rendering and strict Markdown sanitization. Seller KB content additionally runs the §22.4.1.A write-time content moderation pipeline before vectorization, BM25 indexing, retrieval, citation, or Managed-Agent composition. §48.4.4 owns the shared validator family; §22.4.1.A owns KB-specific application and failure handling.
- **Marketplace Abuse Reporting:** Buyers, sellers, Ops, automated signals, and rate-limited anonymous public reporters can report Marketplace subjects as spam, fraud, harmful, competitor sabotage, impersonation, legal-process concern, or otherwise policy-violating. Entity schema, state machine, rate limiting, idempotency, retention, and reporter classes are authoritative at §4.5.7. Operational behavior — severity matrix, triage SLA, appeal workflow, closure dispositions, ban-scope rules, webhook catalog, coordinated-abuse signatures, court-order / DMCA / trademark intake, and transparency reporting — is authoritative at §27.8. SLA timings cite §42.3.1 and are never restated in §45.

## 45.3 Marketplace Abuse Escalation {#45.3-marketplace-abuse-escalation}

**Authoritative-source note (Phase 12.5 R-05 closure).** The numerical SLA values for this workflow live in the §42.3.1 *Marketplace Abuse Operational SLA* table. The narrative below describes the state-transition workflow only; SLA durations cite §42.3.1 and MUST NOT duplicate values inline.

**Canonical routing.** §45.3 is the narrative companion for the abuse-report lifecycle. Operational behavior — severity matrix, triage SLA, appeal workflow, closure dispositions, ban-scope rules, webhook catalog, coordinated-abuse signatures, legal-process ingestion, and transparency reporting — is authoritative at §27.8. Entity schema, fields, state machine, idempotency, rate limiting, and retention are authoritative at §4.5.7. Every transition and Ops action writes an AuditEvent per §4.6.1 and §27.8.1.

**Narrative state machine:**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (none) | `pending_review` | Report filed through eligible report path | Reporter class, subject kind, rate limit, duplicate-detection, and idempotency checks pass per §4.5.7 | Report enters Ops triage queue with severity derived by §27.8.4. |
| `pending_review` | `dismissed` | Ops initial review dismisses report | Evidence insufficient, duplicate, spam report, or not policy-violating per §27.8.7 closure dispositions | Subject remains visible unless another active report / legal hold applies. |
| `pending_review` | `awaiting_seller_response` | Ops confirms a report with appeal-eligible remediation | Subject is hidden, de-ranked, or otherwise actioned per §27.8.6; seller appeal is permitted | Seller receives redacted report summary; reporter identity remains firewalled per §27.8.6 / §4.5.7 serializers. |
| `pending_review` | `upheld` | Ops confirms a report where no seller response is required | Severity / legal / platform-integrity policy permits immediate disposition | Closure consequences and ban scope are governed by §27.8.7 and §27.8.9. |
| `pending_review` | `escalated` | Severity, coordinated-abuse, legal-process, or dual-signoff predicate fires | §27.8.4 severity matrix, §27.8.12 evidence bundle, §27.8.13 legal-process intake, or §27.8.9 ban-scope rules require escalation | Ops management / legal queue owns next decision. |
| `awaiting_seller_response` | `awaiting_seller_response` | Seller submits appeal | Appeal payload accepted within the §42.3.1 appeal window; `appeal_status` changes to `submitted` per §4.5.7 | Report status remains awaiting seller response while appeal review runs. |
| `awaiting_seller_response` | `auto_closed_no_appeal` | Appeal window expires without valid appeal | No timely seller response | Terminal unless Ops re-opens under §27.8.8 self-challenge rules. |
| `awaiting_seller_response` | `dismissed` | Ops overturns after appeal review | Appeal evidence clears the violation under §27.8.8 | Subject restoration / unhide behavior follows §27.8.7. |
| `awaiting_seller_response` | `upheld` | Ops upholds after appeal review | Appeal does not clear the violation | Subject remains actioned; seller receives final disposition. |
| `escalated` | `dismissed` | Ops management / legal resolves in subject's favor | Escalated evidence or legal process does not require enforcement | Disposition, notifications, and transparency-report aggregation follow §27.8. |
| `escalated` | `upheld` | Ops management / legal confirms enforcement | Dual-signoff / legal-process conditions satisfied where required | Ban-scope and irreversible actions follow §27.8.9 and §42.3.1 permanent-ban caveat. |

## 45.4 Acceptance Criteria {#45.4-acceptance-criteria}

1. Every §4 entity that retains customer, marketplace, billing, audit, or operational data MUST resolve to a §40.2 retention row or a named retained-row class in §6.8.5. QA test `privacy_retention_source_table_coverage` asserts §45 references do not create standalone retention rules.
2. DPA availability, DSAR handling, right-to-erasure exceptions, and retained-row behavior MUST cite §6.8 / §6.8.5 / §40.2 rather than a generic §45 privacy exemption. QA test `privacy_dpa_dsar_retained_row_cross_reference` asserts.
3. Every Marketplace Abuse Report MUST transition out of `pending_review` within the §42.3.1 severity-routed triage SLA cited by §27.8.5; §45 MUST NOT restate the SLA value. QA test `marketplace_abuse_triage_sla_compliance` asserts.
4. Every rate-limit reference in §45.2 MUST resolve to either §32.4.5 or the section-specific cap owner named in §45.2. QA test `privacy_abuse_rate_limit_reference_coverage` asserts `marketplace_public_unauth`, abuse-report create caps, EOI caps, opt-out authority-probe caps, and Promoted Listing controls are reachable.
5. Error-log and analytics emission MUST exclude requirement text, response body text, score rationale, seller private KB body text, and other customer-authored confidential content unless a referenced Appendix G event explicitly permits a redacted / hashed value. QA test `privacy_event_payload_pii_allowlist` asserts.
6. KBEntry create, update, publish, Firecrawl chunk insertion, Ghost-Bid import, and `kb_entry_draft_create` MUST run §22.4.1.A content moderation before vectorization, BM25 indexing, retrieval, citation, or Managed-Agent composition. QA test `kb_content_moderation_pre_vectorization_gate` asserts.
7. Vendor Opt-Out suppression and public Marketplace privacy controls referenced from §45.1 MUST remain source-routed to §27.10 / §4.4.8 / §4.5.6; edits that restate §27.10 numerical SLOs in §45 fail `vendor_opt_out_privacy_single_source_reference`.

# 46\. Test Strategy & QA Framework {#46.-test-strategy-&-qa-framework}

V12 remediation (2026-05-11; closes D-46-001 through D-46-022). Comprehensive rewrite from v6.0.0-era test strategy to v7.1.0 per-service pyramid + v7.x feature coverage + AIOperation evaluation + console firewall + DSAR/GDPR + performance regression + accessibility + mobile + feature flag + §M.4/§M.5 self-test + AIWallet/OutcomeContract/Cost-Base + canary + chaos + schema migration + entitlement + i18n + fixtures + security + nomenclature.

## 46.1 Test Pyramid (Per-Service) {#46.1-test-pyramid}

V12 remediation (closes D-46-001). The pyramid is per-service, not platform-flat. Coverage methodology is line-coverage primarily, branch-coverage on conditional-heavy modules (Outcome Resolver, DSAR Cascade Walker, §M.4 spec-lint pipeline). Critical-path E2E flows enumerated in §46.1.2.

### 46.1.1 Per-Service Coverage Targets {#46.1.1-per-service-coverage}

| Service | Unit (line %) | Integration (line %) | E2E / Other | Tools |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Convex backend functions** | ≥ 85% line; ≥ 75% branch | ≥ 75% line (`convex-test` against real preview deploy per CLAUDE.md global feedback: NO DB mocking) | property-based via `fast-check` on Outcome Resolver + AIWallet state machine | Vitest + `convex-test` npm package |
| **Next.js Buyer Console** | ≥ 80% component | ≥ 70% page-flow | ≥ 50% critical E2E (per §46.1.2) + visual-regression on every Pipeline / Defense View / Buyer Maya / Pulse surface | Vitest + React Testing Library + Playwright + Chromatic |
| **Next.js Seller Console** | ≥ 80% component | ≥ 70% page-flow | ≥ 50% critical E2E (Bid Workspace, KB Editor, Marketplace Listing, Seller Maya) + visual-regression | Vitest + RTL + Playwright + Chromatic |
| **Next.js Marketplace** | ≥ 80% component | ≥ 70% page-flow | ≥ 50% critical E2E (Vendor Discovery, EOI, NDA Execution iframe deviation) | Vitest + RTL + Playwright |
| **Next.js Ops Console** | ≥ 80% component | ≥ 70% page-flow | ≥ 70% critical E2E (impersonation, plan-tier-override, refund, kill-switch, DR drill) | Vitest + RTL + Playwright |
| **Public API §32** | ≥ 90% line | ≥ 100% endpoint × method × rate-limit-class contract against OpenAPI + Appendix I error-code set | external API smoke via Postman/Newman | Vitest + contract-test framework |
| **Webhook delivery §31** | ≥ 90% line | idempotency replay + DLQ + HMAC-SHA256 forgery rejection (Sourcera-side and consumer-side) | per-event smoke against mock consumer endpoint | Vitest + custom webhook harness |
| **AI Agent runtime §22** | n/a (production behavior; see §46.4) | tool-use replay + skill registry coverage | per-capability eval suite (§46.4) | Anthropic evals API + Braintrust |
| **AIOperation metering / AIWallet engine** | ≥ 95% line; ≥ 90% branch | property-based via `fast-check` on accept/reject + Outcome Resolver settlement | Stripe meter-event replay test | Vitest + fast-check |
| **OutcomeContract / Outcome Resolver** | ≥ 95% line | settlement transitions full-walk; contest flow per §34.11.2 | E2E pending → accepted / rejected / reversed scenarios | Vitest + Playwright |
| **Cost-Base Recalculation §4.8.6** | ≥ 95% line | 30-day breaking-change window simulation; CostBaseRecalculationLog write parity | E2E rate-card change → recalc → public-API freshness | Vitest |

**Methodology.** Coverage is line-coverage primarily; modules with high conditional density (Outcome Resolver, DSAR Cascade Walker, §M.4 spec-lint pipeline, AIWallet state machine) MUST additionally meet branch-coverage targets. Coverage tool: `c8` for Node-side Vitest; Playwright code-coverage extension for E2E coverage attribution.

**Test type breadth.** Contract testing (consumer-driven contracts between Convex backend and Next.js frontend + Public API ↔ external integrators), property-based testing (`fast-check` for AIWallet / Outcome Resolver / Cost-Base recalculation), snapshot testing (component output stability), visual regression (Chromatic on every Pipeline / Defense View / Buyer Maya / Pulse / Solo single-card surface), mutation testing (Stryker on AIWallet + Outcome Resolver engines), load testing (per §44.4 cadence).

### 46.1.3 Test Infrastructure (D-46-019 closure) {#46.1.3-test-infrastructure}

- **Fixture strategy.** Per-feature seed fixtures under `tests/fixtures/`. Synthetic PII per §46.6.3. Multi-tenant scaffolding (Buyer Org × Seller Org × Marketplace × Ops Console) seeded in `tests/fixtures/multi-tenant/`.
- **Mocking strategy.** Integration tests run against a real Convex preview deploy (CLAUDE.md global feedback: NO DB mocking). Unit tests may stub Stripe / Anthropic / Firecrawl / PostHog / Loops.so / Perplexity / Zendesk via per-provider mock adapters in `tests/mocks/{provider}/`.
- **Test-environment matrix.** local-dev → per-PR ephemeral preview (Convex preview deploy + Vercel preview deploy) → staging → canary → prod. Each environment allows specific test categories (unit + integration in local; integration + E2E in preview; E2E + load in staging; canary smoke in canary; prod synthetic only).
- **Flaky-test management.** 3-retry budget; quarantine after 3 consecutive cycles; flake-rate budget ≤ 1% per service tracked via Datadog `ci.flaky_test_rate` metric.
- **Test-artifact retention.** Reports / screenshots / traces retained 30 days in GitHub Actions artifacts; archived to S3 (per-residency partition) for 365 days.
- **Test-failure escalation routing.** CI red on `main` branch pages `on_call_primary` per §42.5.0 escalation ladder.
- **Test execution parallelism.** Test sharding via Vitest `--shard`; max wall-clock 20 min for full unit + integration; max 45 min for E2E.

## 46.3 QA Process (V12 Rewrite) {#46.3-qa-process}

V12 remediation (closes D-46-007 perf-regression slice + D-46-014 stability/canary/rollback + D-46-015 chaos + D-46-021 nomenclature + D-46-022 Datadog 1%).

**Pre-Release.**

- All tests pass per §46.1.1 per-service coverage targets.
- Axe DevTools accessibility audit passes (zero unapproved violations) per §37.5 contract (V12 closure of D-46-008 anchor cite, amended by Phase 37 P1 remediation). Screen-reader testing (NVDA / JAWS / VoiceOver) per §37.5 on the §46.1.2 critical-path E2E flow set.
- Manual regression on the §46.1.2 critical-path E2E flow set (v7.x surfaces explicit).
- Load test per §44.4 cadence (monthly 500-user / quarterly 2,500-user spike / quarterly 24h endurance) with performance-regression CI gate `performance_budget_regression` (Appendix M.5 — V12 add).
- Datadog dashboard green: error-rate < §44.1 row `error_rate_budget` (V12 add — < 1% over 5-minute window per surface class, single-sourced); latency within §44.1 authoritative budgets per surface class.
- Lighthouse CI hook for in-app Core Web Vitals (LCP / INP / CLS / TTFB) per §44.1 row table.
- Build-time bundle-size CI hook for in-app surfaces (parallel to §26.9.10 public-page `bundlesize` hook).

**Canary Release.**

- Feature flag rollout to 10% (canary) via PostHog.
- **Stability criterion (V12 add — D-46-014).** Error-rate < §44.1 budget per surface class; p95 latency within §44.1 budget; CSAT delta ≤ 5 percentage points from 30-day baseline; zero Sev0 incidents in 24h window.
- **Cohort selection (V12 add).** Default canary cohort: random N% of trialing Free-tier users. Opt-in Enterprise canary fleet. Never canary on paying Solo / Starter / Growth / Scale by default.
- **Rollback trigger (V12 add).** Auto-rollback on stability-criterion breach: error-rate or p95 latency 2× §44.1 budget over 15-min window. Manual rollback by `on_call_primary` per §42.5.0 ladder. PagerDuty incident opens automatically on rollback trigger.
- Monitor 24 hours.
- If stable, 100% rollout.
- Post-release monitoring 48 hours.

## 46.4 AIOperation Testing Strategy (V12 — D-46-004) {#46.4-aiop-testing-strategy}

V12 remediation (closes D-46-004). The §4.8.1 AIOperation engine and §22 Managed Agent runtime are billable, accounted, margin-protected surfaces. AI-quality regression has direct margin and customer-trust consequences.

### 46.4.1 Golden Datasets Per Capability {#46.4.1-golden-datasets}

Per-capability golden dataset stored at `tests/fixtures/aiop-eval/{capability_key}/` with curated inputs, expected outputs, pass/fail thresholds. Capabilities covered (matching §4.8.2 CapabilityRegistry):

- `policy_ingestion`
- `first_pass_rfp_response_generator`
- `scenario_modeling`
- `ai_vendor_research` (Perplexity-backed)
- `match_score_numeric`
- `buyer_maya_intake`
- `seller_maya_intake`
- `defense_view_generator`
- `evaluation_pulse_health_score`
- `kb_managed_agent_*` (per skill in §22 skill registry)
- `solo_envelope_throttling_classifier`

### 46.4.2 Regression Thresholds {#46.4.2-regression-thresholds}

Per-capability regression thresholds (illustrative; capability-specific tuning per §34.3.4 cost-base data):

- Buyer Maya intake: completion-rate ≥ 90%; factuality ≥ 95%; latency p95 ≤ §44.2 budget.
- First-Pass RFP Response Generator: factuality ≥ 95%; relevance score ≥ 85%; latency p95 ≤ §44.2 budget.
- Defense View generator: completeness ≥ 95%; latency p95 ≤ §44.1 budget (8s).
- Scenario Modeling: numerical-accuracy ≥ 99%; latency p95 ≤ §44.2 budget.

### 46.4.3 Eval Harness {#46.4.3-eval-harness}

**Primary:** Anthropic evals API (model-snapshot-pinning regression across `claude-opus-4-6`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`).

**Secondary:** Braintrust for trace-aware eval + dataset versioning + cost tracking.

Eval cadence: per-PR for changed capability prompts; nightly for stable capability prompts; pre-release full-corpus sweep.

### 46.4.4 Model-Snapshot Regression {#46.4.4-model-snapshot-regression}

Anthropic deprecates model snapshots; production cannot silently fall back. Snapshot-version pinning is enforced via `anthropic_model_snapshot_pin` runtime config; deviation pages `on_call_primary` with P2 severity per `RB-PERF-009`.

### 46.4.5 Cost-Base Drift Detection {#46.4.5-cost-base-drift-detection}

Bound to §34.3.3 30-day breaking-change window. The §4.8.6 CostBaseRecalculationLog write event triggers an alert when blended margin shifts > 5%. V12 add: CI gate `cost_base_regression_eval` re-runs the golden dataset against the new cost-base.

CI gate: `aiop_eval_coverage_per_capability` (Appendix M.5 — V12 add) asserts every CapabilityRegistry entry has a golden dataset.

## 46.5 Console Firewall Test Scenarios (V12 — D-46-005) {#46.5-console-firewall-tests}

V12 remediation (closes D-46-005).

1. **Per-entity org-scope leakage matrix.** Every console-scoped entity in §1.3.2 (17 entities) × Buyer / Seller / Marketplace caller × negative test (cross-console call MUST return zero rows OR HTTP 404 per §7.2 non-leak). Integration test fixture `multi_org_multi_console_firewall_fixture`.
2. **Cross-Console Bridge field-redaction round-trip.** §4.7 carried-vs-redacted enumeration test: every Bridge entity round-trips through Buyer + Seller views and the redacted-field set matches the §4.7 declaration.

4. **Marketplace-domain neutral-zone test.** §27.10 firewall enforcement: a Buyer query NEVER receives Seller-only fields from a Marketplace-resident entity.
5. **Webhook event-class firewall.** Event_kinds tagged `console=buyer_only` cannot deliver to a Seller-only webhook subscriber (test the §31 subscription routing).

CI gate: `console_firewall_negative_test_coverage` (Appendix M.5 — V12 add).

**Flag-AND-entitlement precedence.** A feature MUST pass both the flag check AND the §34.8 entitlement check. Precedence order: entitlement first (returns HTTP 403 `feature_not_entitled` per Appendix I if denied); flag second (returns HTTP 503 `feature_flag_disabled` per Appendix I — V12 add, if flag is killed). UX surface: a 403 renders the "Upgrade" upsell modal; a 503 renders the "Feature temporarily unavailable" toast.

Test scenario per feature flag: positive (flag on + entitlement on); negative (flag off + entitlement on → 503); negative (flag on + entitlement off → 403); negative (both off → 403 wins).

# 47\. Governance & Future Roadmap {#47.-governance-&-future-roadmap}

## 47.1 Specification Versioning {#47.1-specification-versioning}

This specification is versioned using semantic versioning: Major.Minor.Patch.

- **Major:** Breaking API changes, fundamental architecture shifts.  
- **Minor:** New features, non-breaking schema changes, behavioral enhancements.  
- **Patch:** Bug fixes, clarifications, documentation updates.

Current version: **6.0.0** (released 2026-04-11).

## 47.2 Change Management Process {#47.2-change-management-process}

**Minor/Patch Changes:**

1. Change proposed (feature request, bug report, clarification).  
2. Reviewed by Product and Engineering leads.  
3. Specification section(s) updated. Version incremented (Minor or Patch).  
4. Changelog generated (Section 1.4 will maintain a change log of all versions).  
5. Deployed to staging. QA validates.  
6. Rolled out to production via feature flag (canary → 100%).

**Major Changes:**

1. Change proposed (RFC document).  
2. All-hands review. Feedback collected.  
3. Specification rewritten (new major version).  
4. Deprecated features marked with sunset date (minimum 6 months notice).  
5. Migration guide published.  
6. Old version kept in read-only archive.

## 47.3 Known Limitations & Future Work (Phase 2+) {#47.3-known-limitations-&-future-work-(phase-2+)}

| Item | Current | Phase 2 Target |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| RTL Support | CSS-ready; UI deferred | Full RTL (Arabic, Hebrew) |
| i18n Languages | English only | Spanish, French, German, Japanese |
| Customer-Managed Encryption Keys | — | Available for Enterprise |
| Field-Level PII Encryption | — | Automatic for sensitive fields |
| Custom Scoring Rubrics | Fixed rubrics per response type | Custom rubrics per requirement |
| Requirement Hierarchies | Flat (no dependencies) | Dependency trees (with blockers) |
| Custom Pipeline Phases | Fixed 13 phases | Customizable phase structure (Enterprise) |
| Two-Sided Marketplace Ratings | Not supported (by design) | Alternative: objective performance metrics |
| Agent Fine-Tuning | Public Claude models only | Custom fine-tuned models (Enterprise, Phase 3\) |
| Video Demos | Not supported | Native video upload \+ AI summarization |
| Mobile Full Parity | Read \+ limited write | Full write (scoring, editing) |

## 47.4 Data Residency & Compliance Expansion {#47.4-data-residency-&-compliance-expansion}

**Current:**

- Data residency region selectable (data\_residency\_region on Organization).  
- GDPR DPA signed.  
- SOC 2 Type II targeted.

**Phase 2:**

- HIPAA BAA available.

## 47.5 Acceptance Criteria {#47.5-acceptance-criteria}

- Specification version tracked in Git (semantic versioning).  
- All breaking changes communicated 6+ months in advance.  
- Changelog maintained for each version.  
- Feature flags allow incremental rollout of new features.

# 48\. PLG, Growth Mechanics & Network Effects {#48.-plg-growth-mechanics-and-network-effects}

**Source authority.** This section integrates `Sourcera_Master_Summary.md` §3 (PLG Motion, Growth, and Network Effects) into the Master Spec at engineering fidelity. Where the Summary names a loop or mechanic by short prose, this section defines the entity shape, telemetry events, anti-spam controls, kill-switch wiring, and acceptance criteria required to build, instrument, and operate it. Every field, event, and enum referenced here is canonically defined in §4 (Global Data Model), Appendix G (PostHog Event Taxonomy), Appendix C (Notification Event Catalog), or Appendix J (Controlled Vocabulary Registry).

**Scope.** §48 governs three concerns: (a) the customer-funnel path from signup to enterprise (§48.1); (b) the ten in-product growth loops that compound supply, demand, and content (§48.2); and (c) the global anti-spam, anti-abuse, and content-integrity controls that gate every loop's outbound surface (§48.4). It does NOT redefine the M1–M17 expanded growth mechanics — those are catalogued in the existing entity sections (§4.3.16 Buyer Referral / M16, §4.3.17 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat / M17, §4.4.12 CategoryPage / M9, §4.4.13 GuidePage / M10, §4.4.14 ComparisonPage / M11, §4.4.15 MarketIntelligenceReport / M12, §4.4.16 HeatMapCell / M13, §4.4.17 GhostBidImport / M15) and in §34.13 (M17 procedural mechanics). §48 cross-links to those sections; it does not duplicate them.

**Cross-section invariants.** Every loop and every anti-spam control authored in §48 (a) emits at least one PostHog event registered in Appendix G; (b) is gated by at least one Signal Integrity Monitor (SIM, Summary C.100) signal class registered in Appendix J; (c) is subject to the §41 Email Deliverability & Compliance controls when it produces email; (d) honors the §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Record, §4.5.6 Vendor Opt-Out marketplace-domain render contract, and §41.4 Opt-Out Classification when it produces public or vendor-targeted artifacts; (e) is killable from the Ops Console via a feature-flag publish path with a 60-second worst-case orchestrator-cache invalidation latency (per §22.16.5 kill-switch publish path). Any §48 mechanic that violates any of (a)–(e) is non-shippable.

## 48.1 PLG Framework Overview {#48.1-plg-framework-overview}

**Authoring intent.** §48.1 fixes the canonical PLG funnel that the rest of the spec instruments and bills against. The funnel is parallel across the Buyer Console paid path (§48.1.1) and the Seller Console paid path (§48.1.2). Both paths are authored at full fidelity as independent-but-reconciled funnels because (a) the Seller Console has a structurally different acquisition surface — Forced-Vendor-Signup from buyer invites is the dominant origination channel per Summary C.136, not self-service discovery — and (b) the Seller Hero Moment (Summary §3.6 / C.132) is a product surface that has no Buyer analogue, warranting its own framework (§48.1.5), activation metric (§48.1.6), and Conversion Moments binding (§48.1.7). §48.1.5–§48.1.7 extend but do not replace §48.1.2; every seller funnel claim in §48.1.2 is unchanged, and the new subsections operationalize the Hero Moment mechanics, the Seller Activation Metric (C.135), and the four Seller Conversion Moments (SPS v3 §15.3; C.133 pre-Solo baseline) as Master-Spec-fidelity building blocks. Sources: Summary Summary §3.1, Summary §3.1b, §3.6, C.132–C.138, C.141; full Seller Onboarding seven-stage funnel at Summary §6.28.2; entity schema at §4.4.22 SellerOnboardingSession.

### 48.1.1 Buyer Console Paid Path (Five Stages) {#48.1.1-buyer-console-paid-path}

| Stage | Name | Plan State | Defining Event | Telemetry Marker (Appendix G) | Median-Target Time From Stage Entry |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Signup | Free | Google/Microsoft SSO completes; no credit card; Buyer Console provisioned | `signup_completed` (existing) + `funnel_stage_entered {stage="signup"}` | n/a (entry stage) |
| 2 | Aha Moment | Free | First Pre-Scoring AIOperation across ≥ 3 vendors completes with `settlement_state=accepted` OR `auto_accepted` | `funnel_stage_entered {stage="aha_moment"}`; correlation key = first `pre_scoring` AIOperation `id` | ≤ 60 minutes from signup (median target) |
| 3 | Ceiling Hit | Free → Starter (upgrade-pressure event) | First of: workspace-count cap breach, vendor-count cap breach, AI budget exhaustion (`free_allowance_exhausted` OR wallet `available_balance_cents=0`), Opus-gated capability invocation | `funnel_stage_entered {stage="ceiling_hit"}`; carries `upgrade_pressure_trigger` per Appendix J `upgrade_completed_trigger` | ≤ 14 days from aha (median target) |
| 4 | Expansion | Starter → Growth → Scale | Wallet utilization ≥ 80% in two consecutive billing months OR active-evaluation-count exceeds tier ceiling OR CRM Sync request OR numeric Match Score request (Buyer-side: workspace-count proxy) | `funnel_stage_entered {stage="expansion"}`; carries `expansion_trigger ∈ {wallet_utilization_consecutive, evaluation_ceiling, opus_capability_request}` (Appendix J `expansion_trigger` — new) | n/a (chronic) |
| 5 | Enterprise Trigger | Scale → Enterprise | First of: SSO/SAML request, signed DPA request, ≥ $12K annual AI commit interest, custom integration scoping request | `funnel_stage_entered {stage="enterprise_trigger"}`; carries `enterprise_trigger ∈ {sso_request, dpa_request, committed_spend_interest, custom_integration_request}` (Appendix J `enterprise_trigger` — new); routes the Org to founder-led Sales | n/a (qualified-lead handoff) |

**Stage-entry semantics.** A `funnel_stage_entered` event is emitted **at most once per Org per stage** (not per user). Re-entry into a prior stage (e.g., a downgrade from Starter back to Free) does NOT re-emit a prior `funnel_stage_entered` event; instead, a `funnel_stage_regressed {from_stage, to_stage, reason}` event is emitted. The funnel-progression view in PostHog uses the union of `funnel_stage_entered ∪ funnel_stage_regressed` keyed by `org_id`. Stage attribution is monotonic-forward by default; regression is observable but does not roll back the "highest stage reached" property persisted on the Org.

**Persisted Org-level properties.** Two Org-level PostHog properties are written on every stage-transition event and replicated as columns on the §4.2.1 Organization entity for Spec-readability and downstream billing/CRM joins: `plg_funnel_stage_max_reached ∈ {signup, aha_moment, ceiling_hit, expansion, enterprise_trigger}` (monotonic-forward) and `plg_funnel_stage_current ∈ {signup, aha_moment, ceiling_hit, expansion, enterprise_trigger, regressed}` (current). Both are sourced from the Usage Event ledger (§4.3.18) so that re-derivation from the source-of-truth is always possible.

### 48.1.2 Seller Console Paid Path {#48.1.2-seller-console-paid-path}

The Seller Console funnel mirrors the Buyer Console funnel with stage-specific definitions consistent with `Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy.md` and Summary §2.1.4:

| Stage | Defining Event (Seller-Side) | Telemetry Marker |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Signup | Vendor magic-link click from a buyer invite (M1, M5, M15, M17) OR direct Seller Console signup; Seller Console provisioned | `signup_completed {console="seller", origin ∈ {vendor_invite, direct_signup, m17_grant}}` |
| Aha Moment | First First-Pass RFP Response batch (`first_pass_responses`) settles with `settlement_state=accepted` OR `auto_accepted` (≥ 50% of draft retained in submitted bid per §34.11.1 contract) OR Seller Profile published (`seller.profile.published` event, existing) | `funnel_stage_entered {stage="aha_moment", console="seller"}` |
| Ceiling Hit | Second concurrent invited bid OR first proactive EOI OR KB 50-entry ceiling reached OR first Firecrawl request | `funnel_stage_entered {stage="ceiling_hit", console="seller", upgrade_pressure_trigger ∈ {concurrent_bid_limit, proactive_eoi_request, kb_entry_ceiling, firecrawl_request}}` |
| Expansion | Active-bid ceiling breach, AI budget utilization ≥ 80% for two consecutive months, CRM Sync request, OR numeric Match Score request | `funnel_stage_entered {stage="expansion", console="seller"}` |
| Enterprise Trigger | SSO/SAML, DPA, ≥ $12K annual AI commit, custom integration, OR multi-region data residency | `funnel_stage_entered {stage="enterprise_trigger", console="seller"}` |

**Five-row-vs-seven-stage reconciliation.** The five-row Seller Paid Path table above is the **billing-and-telemetry-aligned PLG funnel view** (Signup → Aha Moment → Ceiling Hit → Expansion → Enterprise Trigger) that mirrors §48.1.1's Buyer Console funnel structure and feeds the §48.3.3 PLG Funnel Dashboard and §34 plan-billing analytics. Summary Summary §3.1b and Summary §6.28.2 separately enumerate a **seven-stage Seller Onboarding Experience** (Stage 1 Arrival → Stage 2 SSO + Bootstrap → Stage 3 Bid Workspace Loaded → Stage 4 First Requirement Response + First Bid Submitted → Stage 5 Stake Reveal → Stage 6 Outcome Debrief → Stage 7 Conversion Moment + Upgrade) that is the **operational onboarding taxonomy** tracked at per-session granularity on §4.4.22 SellerOnboardingSession (`stage_1_arrival_at` through `stage_7_upgrade_completed_at` plus the `activation_metric_elapsed_seconds` computation rule). The two views are deliberately different in grain: the seven-stage taxonomy records the Hero Moment product surfaces (§48.1.5) and the Four Seller Conversion Moments (§48.1.7); the five-row funnel collapses Stages 1–4 of the operational taxonomy into "Signup" + "Aha Moment" (since Stage 3 Bid Workspace Loaded and Stage 4 First Requirement Response are the observable sub-signals that constitute the Aha-Moment emission per §48.1.4 AC 2), treats Stages 5 and 6 (Stake Reveal + Outcome Debrief) as intra-Aha-Moment / intra-Ceiling-Hit affordances, and locates Stage 7 (Win/Loss Debrief as upgrade trigger) within the §48.7.6 Win/Loss Debrief Mechanic. The five-row funnel is the canonical view for investor metrics, dashboard cohort splits, and plan-progression analytics; the seven-stage taxonomy is the canonical view for onboarding-quality QA, activation-latency diagnostics, and §48.1.6 leading-indicator reporting. Both are reconciled from the §4.4.22 SellerOnboardingSession row — the seven-stage fields are the source-of-truth, and the five-row `funnel_stage_entered` events are derived from them.

**Dual-funnel reconciliation.** An Org with active plans on both consoles holds two funnel histories — one keyed `(org_id, console="buyer")` and one keyed `(org_id, console="seller")`. The `enterprise_trigger` stage is collapsed at the Org level for handoff to founder-led Sales: hitting Enterprise on either console is sufficient. The `plg_funnel_stage_max_reached` Org-level property is the **maximum across both consoles**.

### 48.1.3 PLG Funnel Configurability {#48.1.3-funnel-configurability}

Each stage's defining event MAY be tuned by Ops via a per-environment configuration row (`plg_funnel_definition`, Ops-Console-managed; not customer-facing). Tuning a stage emits a `plg_funnel_definition_changed {stage, prior_definition_hash, new_definition_hash, ops_actor_user_id, effective_at}` audit event (Appendix G); funnel analytics dashboards (§48.3.3) display the configuration version active at the point of each transition. Tuning never retroactively recomputes prior `funnel_stage_entered` events; a §48.3.3 dashboard "definition cohort" filter lets Ops scope analyses to a single configuration version.

### 48.1.4 Acceptance Criteria {#48.1.4-acceptance-criteria}

1. Every Org provisioned through SSO emits exactly one `signup_completed` event AND exactly one `funnel_stage_entered {stage="signup"}` event within 5 seconds of provisioning.
2. The `funnel_stage_entered` event for `aha_moment` MUST be emitted within 30 seconds of the qualifying AIOperation reaching `settlement_state=accepted` OR `auto_accepted`; longer latencies fail QA.
3. The `funnel_stage_entered` event for `ceiling_hit` MUST be emitted within 5 seconds of the underlying upgrade-pressure event (cap breach OR `free_allowance_exhausted` OR Opus-gated capability invocation); event MUST carry the `upgrade_pressure_trigger` enum value matching the upstream trigger.
4. The `funnel_stage_entered` event for `enterprise_trigger` MUST automatically open a CRM lead record routed to founder-led Sales within 60 seconds (CRM integration: §31.6); failure to create the CRM record raises a §42 P1 alert.
5. `plg_funnel_stage_max_reached` is monotonic-forward; any decrease detected by the nightly audit job emits an `analytics_invariant_violation` PagerDuty alert and freezes the Org's funnel-analytics view pending Ops review.
6. Funnel-regression detection: any Org transitioning from `expansion` back to `ceiling_hit` (or earlier) within 30 days of the upgrade emits a `funnel_stage_regressed` event AND opens a Customer Success follow-up ticket via the Zendesk integration (§31.6).
7. Per-Org PostHog Insights → Funnels analysis from `signup` → `enterprise_trigger` MUST resolve in ≤ 30 seconds at p95 across the full Org population.
8. Every stage-definition change emits a `plg_funnel_definition_changed` audit event AND requires `ops_finance_admin` OR `ops_growth_admin` (new role; Appendix J `ops_growth_admin` — new) approval; non-approved drafts are inert.

### 48.1.5 Seller Hero Moment Framework — Cross-Reference {#48.1.5-seller-hero-moment-framework-cross-reference}

**Authoring intent.** §48.1.5 fixes the canonical four-phase Hero Moment surface and binds each phase to (a) the §4.4.22 SellerOnboardingSession field that records its observed completion, (b) the §22 KB Bootstrap workflow that produces the underlying state, (c) the §21.4 Capability Registry capability that funds the AI work (`kb_bootstrap`, `first_pass_response`, `q_and_a_suggestion`, `page_enrichment`), and (d) the §34.10 AIWallet ledger entry that records the free-budget consumption during onboarding (lifetime-free `kb_bootstrap` allowance per Seller Org per C.140). The full UX-and-mechanics spec lives at §48.8 (newly authored in this edit); §48.1.5 is the funnel-level view that anchors the §48.1.6 Activation Metric and §48.1.7 Conversion Moments tables.

**Source authority.** Summary §3.6 (Hero Moment Mechanics), Summary C.132 (Hero Moment Mechanics — appendix), Summary §6.28.2 (Seven-Stage Seller Onboarding Experience), Summary C.136 (Forced-Vendor-Signup Playbook), Summary C.140 (Seller Onboarding Required Capabilities), Summary C.141 (Onboarding Anti-Patterns). For per-phase product-surface acceptance criteria, see §48.8. For the SellerOnboardingSession entity that records the observable completion timestamps, see §4.4.22.

**Four-Phase Hero Moment Framework.**

| Phase | Window | What Happens (Surface) | Authoritative Source | SellerOnboardingSession Field(s) | KB / Capability Reference | AIWallet Entry |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1. Pre-Arrival Preparation** | Hidden from vendor; runs from invite-send through magic-link click | Email-domain enrichment (company name, industry, HQ region); Marketplace Tagger assigns probable category tags from `seller_domain_hint` + buyer-side evaluation context; Firecrawl rate-limit pre-warm; `kb_bootstrap` Managed Agent queue pre-resolution (URLs resolved, robots.txt cached, crawl-depth and per-host budget allocated) | Summary §3.6 ¶1; C.132 ¶1; C.136 magic-link structure | `invite_source`, `invite_magic_link_id`, `seller_domain_hint`, `bid_id`, `recipient_email_hash` (all populated pre-arrival when invite is created) | §22.4 KB Bootstrap pre-resolution; §22.16.5 Orchestrator cache pre-warm | None (no AI inference yet; pre-warm is queue-only) |
| **2. Onboarding Surface (Minutes 0–3)** | `stage_1_arrival_at` → `stage_3_bid_workspace_loaded_at` | Zero-form unauthenticated landing page; SSO/magic-link only; no credit card, no role selection, no company description; progress storytelling narrates literal work in flight (*"Scanning yourcompany.com…"* → *"Found your security documentation…"* → *"Drafting responses for [Buyer Company]'s 82 requirements…"* → *"Your bid is ready to review."*); landing counter on completion (*"Your bid is ready. **47** AI drafts prepared. **31** cite evidence from your website. Review time: **~35 min**."*) | Summary §3.6 ¶2; C.132 in-SSO-redirect execution; Summary §6.28.2 Stage 1 + Stage 2 + Stage 3 | `stage_1_arrival_at`, `stage_1_reached_cta`, `stage_1_cta_rendered_at`, `stage_2_sso_initiated_at`, `stage_2_sso_completed_at`, `stage_2_bootstrap_started_at`, `stage_3_bid_workspace_loaded_at`, `stage_3_population_latency_ms`, `stage_3_population_complete`, `stage_3_kb_draft_entry_count`, `stage_3_first_pass_response_requirement_count`, `stage_3_first_pass_response_cited_count`, `hero_moment_completed_at` | §22.4 KB Bootstrap (Opus); §22.5 First-Pass RFP Draft (Sonnet); §21.4 capabilities `kb_bootstrap`, `first_pass_response` | Lifetime-free `kb_bootstrap` allowance per Seller Org (one entry per Org per lifetime per C.140); `first_pass_response` runs draw from $5 free Seller Wallet credit (§34.10.4) until exhausted, then accrue as cost-priced settlement-state-rejected entries with no charge to the seller until acceptance |
| **3. In-Workspace Value Proof (Minutes 3–45)** | `stage_3_bid_workspace_loaded_at` → `first_requirement_response_at` (and onward to `first_bid_submitted_at`) | Inline citation chip on every draft (*"from: yourcompany.com/trust/soc2"*, hover-expand exact quoted sentence per §22.7 Citation Inline Card pattern); Accept / Edit / Reject three-button affordance per requirement, every click a settlement-resolution signal (§34.6); live AIWallet budget counter top-of-workspace (refresh ≤ 2 s lag); KB-gap detector on rejected drafts (empty state → 1-click KB-entry creation; *"No KB content answered this. Write your answer below and we'll save it as a KB entry."*); subtle confirmation chip on no-edit acceptances (*"added to your KB as verified response"*) | Summary §3.6 ¶3; C.132 ¶2; §22.7 Citation Inline Card; §34.6 Outcome Resolver | `stage_3_first_edit_at`, `stage_4_first_kb_accept_at`, `stage_4_first_kb_reject_at`, `stage_4_first_q_and_a_suggestion_at`, `first_requirement_response_at`, `stage_2_bootstrap_accepted_entry_count`, `first_bid_submitted_at` | §22.6 KB-Gap Detector; §22.7 Citation Inline Card; §21.4 capabilities `q_and_a_suggestion` (on-demand for rejected/empty requirements) | Per-edit AIOperation settlement (§34.6); accepted edits → value-priced settlement (`cost_base × 10`); rejected edits → cost-priced settlement (`cost_base × 1.05`); on-demand `q_and_a_suggestion` invocations charged the same way |
| **4. Post-Submission Reveal (Hour 1+)** | `first_bid_submitted_at` → `stage_5_stake_reveal_rendered_at` (and `stage_5_dwell_seconds`) | Stake-Reveal Screen on Submit (*"You just built a reusable KB of 47 verified entries in 35 minutes. Your next bid will reuse them automatically. Sourcera tracked $1.47 of value pricing for the AI work on this bid (covered by your Free plan)."*); deliberately NOT an upgrade CTA — a stake reminder; published Seller Profile URL surfaced (*"View your published profile: sourcera.com/sellers/[your-org-slug]"*); opt-in to Seller Signals (Summary §6.17) presented as a checkbox-default-off | Summary §3.6 ¶4; C.132 stake-reveal; Summary §6.28.2 Stage 5 | `stage_5_stake_reveal_rendered_at`, `stage_5_dwell_seconds`, `stage_5_seller_signals_opt_in`, `stage_5_seller_signals_opt_in_at`, `stage_5_profile_url_rendered` | Summary §6.17 Seller Signals; Summary §6.28.2 Stage 5 stake-reveal copy | Total-AIWallet-spend-on-this-bid surfaced as a freeze-frame ledger summary; no further AI work funded post-submission until the seller takes a new action |

**Phase-to-Capability Cost Anchor.** The free-budget consumption during onboarding has one canonical accounting home: §34.10.4 (Seller Wallet — Lifetime-Free Bootstrap Allowance). The Hero Moment never silently exceeds the free budget; if `kb_bootstrap` is consumed and `first_pass_response` would exceed remaining wallet balance, the system MUST proceed to draft the cheapest-cost-base requirements first and surface a *"Some requirements need more budget"* inline message at the top of the Bid Workspace per §34.10.4 — never a hard block, never a paywall on the Hero Moment.

**Phase-to-Onboarding-Stage Mapping.** Phase 1 maps to Summary §6.28.2 Stage 0 (Pre-Arrival, hidden) — not a numbered onboarding stage but tracked in §4.4.22 as the row's pre-existing fields. Phase 2 maps to Stages 1, 2, and 3. Phase 3 maps to Stages 4. Phase 4 maps to Stage 5. Stages 6 (Outcome Debrief) and 7 (Conversion Moment) are post-Hero-Moment events and are addressed in §48.1.7 (Conversion Moments) and §48.8.5 (Stake-Reveal extension).

**Terminal-state predicate — canonical contract. (V13 D-HM-001 remediation 2026-05-12.)** Across the prior §4.4.22 / §48.1.5 / §48.8.5 authoring, the Hero Moment was assigned three non-equivalent terminal predicates (Stage-3 `hero_moment_completed_at` write; §48.1.5 Phase-4 reveal; §48.8.5 Stake-Reveal Screen as moment-of-value-perception). For all engineering, analytics, alerting, and acceptance-criteria purposes, the SINGLE canonical Hero Moment terminal predicate is the §4.4.22 `hero_moment_completed_at` write: a non-null timestamp set by the Bid Workspace render path at first paint IFF (i) all three Stage 3 surfaces (KB Draft + first-pass response + progress strip) are present AND (ii) `stage_3_population_latency_ms` satisfies §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold` (pause-adjusted per §48.8.3 Failure Mode #6(c) when Firecrawl-outage pause applies). §48.1.5 Phase 4 (Post-Submission Reveal) and §48.8.5 Stake-Reveal Screen are POST-HERO-MOMENT surfaces — they fire AFTER `hero_moment_completed_at` writes and serve to reinforce stake-perception; they do NOT redefine the Hero Moment's terminal predicate. The §48.8.10 ACs #30 / #31 activation-metric measurement window (`activation_metric_elapsed_seconds = first_requirement_response_at - stage_1_arrival_at`) measures end-to-end-to-first-value, NOT end-to-end-to-Stake-Reveal. CI gate `hero_moment_terminal_state_single_source` (§M.5 — new; pack assignment M02.3) asserts that the three sections cite the same predicate exclusively at `hero_moment_completed_at`. The §48.1.5 Phase 4 row above is hereby re-framed as "Post-Hero-Moment Stake-Reveal" with cross-reference to §48.8.5; the §48.8.5 Stake-Reveal Screen is the canonical `reveal_moment = post_submission_reveal` surface per the §22.18.6 enum extension (D-HM-005 remediation; see §22.18.6 V13 block).

**Cross-Console Firewall Note.** Hero Moment surfaces are Seller-Console-only. Buyer Console GET on any SellerOnboardingSession row returns HTTP 404 per §7.2. Hero-moment-completion telemetry events emit with `console="seller"` and the dual-console audit firewall (Appendix I `seller_onboarding_cross_console_access`) prevents leakage into Buyer Console analytics surfaces.

**Authoring intent.** §48.1.6 fixes the singular Seller Activation Metric (Summary Summary §3.1b ¶ "single most-important seller-side activation metric" + C.135) and the eight leading-indicator metrics from Summary Summary §3.1b. Each indicator is bound to the PostHog event(s) that emit it, the §4.4.22 SellerOnboardingSession field(s) that record it, the §43.x dashboard tile that surfaces it, the alert/threshold band that pages Ops on regression, and the cohort dimensions over which it is computable. This section is the single authoritative cross-reference; downstream documents (Engineering Spec, Seller Pricing Strategy) point here.
