| Q2 | **Blended seller-side margin per plan** | (Σ AIWallet revenue accrued per plan per month − Σ Anthropic cost incurred per plan per month) ÷ Σ revenue per plan per month | n/a — Snowflake reverse-ETL nightly | §34.10 AIWallet ledger + §43.x Cost Ledger | Per Seller Pricing Strategy §11 — Authored Extension | Finance-internal; Anthropic cost is the canonical denominator |

**Indicator-to-Dashboard Map.** Indicators 1, 4, 6, Q1 surface on the **Seller Activation Dashboard** (Ops-internal). Indicators 2, 3 surface on **Forced-Signup Funnel Dashboard** (Ops-internal). Indicators 5, 7, 8 surface on the **Seller Plan Progression Dashboard**. Q2 surfaces only on the **Seller Margin Dashboard** (`ops_finance_admin` only). All five dashboards are sub-surfaces of the §43 Admin Dashboard with `ops_growth_admin` write-access for cohort filters.

**Computation cadence and freshness.** Real-time tiles (activation latency, second-invitation arrivals) refresh every 60 seconds via PostHog Live Insights; daily tiles (free-to-Starter conversion, KB-bootstrap acceptance, days-to-first-bid) refresh once per 24 hours via the Snowflake reverse-ETL pipeline; monthly tiles (Starter-to-Growth expansion, EOI submission rate, blended margin) refresh on the first business day of each month. Each tile shows source and timestamp.

**Reconciliation invariant.** The Seller Activation dashboard's p50 / p90 rolling metric MUST be reconcilable to the Usage Event ledger (§4.3.18) within 1% drift on a daily comparison job; drift > 1% pages `ops_growth_admin` and pauses the dashboard write per §4.4.22 AC 3.

### 48.1.7 Four Seller Conversion Moments — Master Spec Binding {#48.1.7-three-conversion-moments-master-spec-binding}

**Authoring intent.** §48.1.7 binds the four Seller Conversion Moments (SPS v3 §15.3) to (a) the trigger event that fires them, (b) the canonical upgrade CTA copy that renders, (c) the PostHog telemetry event emitted at trigger and at click, (d) the plan-from / plan-to mapping that the upgrade flow effects, and (e) the SellerOnboardingSession field that records the moment for funnel reporting. The product MUST catch all four; the pricing model deliberately does not optimize a single one. This subsection is the implementation contract; product and engineering build against it; QA tests against it; PLG dashboards report against it.

**Source authority.** SPS v3 §15.3 (four Seller conversion moments; mid-bid AI budget wall added as the primary Free -> Solo trigger), Summary Summary §3.1b ¶4 / C.133 (pre-Solo three-moment baseline), and C.134 (Seller Paid-Path Progression). For UX surface specification, see §48.8.6. For SellerOnboardingSession field schema, see §4.4.22 (`stage_7_*` fields).

**Four Seller Conversion Moments — Definitive Binding.**

| # | Moment | Trigger Event (Source) | Trigger PostHog Event | Upgrade CTA Copy (Authoritative) | Click PostHog Event | Plan-From → Plan-To | SellerOnboardingSession Field Set | Acceptance Window |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1** | **Mid-bid AI budget wall** | `seller_aiwallet_budget_exhausted_during_onboarding` fires for a Seller Free Org while an active Bid Workspace for that seller is in `status IN {'populating', 'drafting', 'reviewing', 'editing', 'draft_pending_review', 'in_review'}` and the attempted customer-billed AIOperation would otherwise return HTTP 402 `wallet_hard_capped` | `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_fired {seller_org_id, kind='mid_bid_ai_budget_wall', triggering_bid_id, wallet_balance_cents, plan_tier='seller_free'}` | *"**Your bid response is paused — Sourcera Free's AI budget is exhausted.** Solo unlocks the engine-absorbed envelope (no hard cap, no mid-bid walls) for $49/mo or $199/bid."* | `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_clicked {seller_org_id, kind='mid_bid_ai_budget_wall', upgrade_target_plan='seller_solo'}` | `seller_free` → `seller_solo` | `stage_7_conversion_moment_triggered_at`, `stage_7_conversion_moment_kind='mid_bid_ai_budget_wall'`, `stage_7_upgrade_prompt_rendered_at`, `stage_7_upgrade_cta_clicked_at`, `stage_7_upgrade_completed_at`, `stage_7_upgrade_target_plan='seller_solo'` | Trigger event MUST emit within 2 s of the wallet-exhaustion decision; the bid draft state MUST be preserved; click → upgrade complete MUST flow through Stripe checkout in ≤ 3 user-facing screens and resume the paused bid response without requiring re-entry |
| **2** | **Second concurrent bid** | A new buyer invite arrives (Bid Workspace creation event, §4.4.1 `bid_workspace.invited`) for a Seller Org that has `≥ 1` open Bid Workspace where `Bid.status NOT IN {'closed', 'archived'}` AND the Seller Org's current `plan_tier = 'seller_free'` | `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_fired {seller_org_id, kind='second_concurrent_bid', triggering_bid_id, concurrent_open_bid_count, plan_tier='seller_free'}` | *"**Don't let your second deal slip.** Starter unlocks 3 concurrent bids and keeps your KB shared across all of them. Your in-flight bid stays exactly as it is — no re-bootstrap, no lost work."* | `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_clicked {seller_org_id, kind='second_concurrent_bid', upgrade_target_plan='seller_starter'}` | `seller_free` → `seller_starter` | `stage_7_conversion_moment_triggered_at`, `stage_7_conversion_moment_kind='second_concurrent_bid'`, `stage_7_upgrade_prompt_rendered_at`, `stage_7_upgrade_cta_clicked_at`, `stage_7_upgrade_completed_at`, `stage_7_upgrade_target_plan='seller_starter'` | Trigger event MUST emit within 5 s of bid arrival; upgrade prompt MUST render at next foreground render of the Bid Workspace inbox; click → upgrade complete MUST flow through Stripe checkout in ≤ 3 user-facing screens |
| **3** | **First EOI attempt** | Seller clicks "Submit EOI" (§4.5.x EOI entity creation attempt) on a Marketplace listing AND the Seller Org's current `plan_tier = 'seller_free'` AND no prior EOI exists for the Seller Org (`COUNT(EOI WHERE seller_org_id = … AND status NOT IN {'draft', 'cancelled'}) = 0`) | `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_fired {seller_org_id, kind='first_eoi_attempt', triggering_listing_id, triggering_listing_category, plan_tier='seller_free'}` | *"**Outbound EOIs start at Starter.** Your first **10 EOIs / month** are included. Marketplace listings showed your profile to **47 buyers** this week — Starter lets you reach back."* (the "47 buyers" figure is computed from `seller_profile.view_count` for the Seller Org's published profile in the prior 7 days; if no profile exists, fallback copy: *"Marketplace listings put your profile in front of **buyers searching your category**."*) | `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_clicked {seller_org_id, kind='first_eoi_attempt', upgrade_target_plan='seller_starter'}` | `seller_free` → `seller_starter` | `stage_7_conversion_moment_triggered_at`, `stage_7_conversion_moment_kind='first_eoi_attempt'`, `stage_7_upgrade_prompt_rendered_at`, `stage_7_upgrade_cta_clicked_at`, `stage_7_upgrade_completed_at`, `stage_7_upgrade_target_plan='seller_starter'` | Trigger event MUST emit within 1 s of EOI-submit click; upgrade prompt is in-line modal (NOT a pricing-page redirect — that violates Summary §3.6 anti-pattern, see §48.8.7); click → upgrade complete in ≤ 3 user-facing screens |
| **4** | **KB ceiling approach** | The Seller Org's KB entry count (`COUNT(KBEntry WHERE seller_org_id = … AND status NOT IN {'archived', 'rejected'})`) reaches a plan-relative threshold during a KB-write operation: `plan_tier='seller_free' AND count ≥ 45` OR `plan_tier='seller_solo' AND count ≥ 225` | `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_fired {seller_org_id, kind='kb_ceiling_approach', current_kb_entry_count, plan_tier ∈ {'seller_free','seller_solo'}, triggering_entry_id}` | Free copy: *"**Your KB is about to hit the Free ceiling (50 entries).** Solo raises it to **250 entries** and keeps your existing work."* Solo copy: *"**Your KB is about to hit the Solo ceiling (250 entries).** Starter raises it to **1,000 entries** and keeps your existing work."* Both variants include the Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee bind per C.139. | `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_clicked {seller_org_id, kind='kb_ceiling_approach', upgrade_target_plan ∈ {'seller_solo','seller_starter'}}` | `seller_free` → `seller_solo`; `seller_solo` → `seller_starter` | `stage_7_conversion_moment_triggered_at`, `stage_7_conversion_moment_kind='kb_ceiling_approach'`, `stage_7_upgrade_prompt_rendered_at`, `stage_7_upgrade_cta_clicked_at`, `stage_7_upgrade_completed_at`, `stage_7_upgrade_target_plan='seller_solo' OR 'seller_starter'` | Trigger event MUST emit within 5 s of the plan-relative threshold crossing; upgrade prompt is an in-line banner; SUBJECT TO THE HARD CONSTRAINT that the prompt MUST NOT block the seller from completing the in-flight KB-write or any other in-flight bid work (§48.8.7 anti-pattern enforcement) |

**Mutual exclusivity.** A Seller Org records ONE `stage_7_conversion_moment_kind` per SellerOnboardingSession row per plan-tier stage — the **first** Conversion Moment to fire at that plan tier wins the attribution. If a Seller Free Org hits Moment 3 (first EOI) and then Moment 2 (second concurrent bid) before clicking either upgrade prompt, the row carries `stage_7_conversion_moment_kind = 'first_eoi_attempt'` (whichever fired first) and a `metadata_json.subsequent_conversion_moments_fired[]` array logs all later fires for funnel-overlap analysis (Appendix J `seller_onboarding_subsequent_moment_metadata`). A later paid-plan-stage moment after a successful Free -> Solo upgrade MAY record as a new plan-stage observation without overwriting the original Free-stage attribution.

**Frequency cap (anti-spam).** Each Conversion Moment can fire AT MOST ONCE PER `(seller_org_id, moment_kind, plan_tier)` over the row's lifetime. A second qualifying trigger for the same tuple MUST NOT re-fire the prompt; instead it emits `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_re_eligible {seller_org_id, kind, plan_tier, days_since_first_fire}` (Appendix G) for diagnostic-only Ops review, and the seller continues unprompted unless they hit a different Conversion Moment or a new plan-tier stage. This tuple granularity is load-bearing: a Seller Free Org can hit Moment 1 and upgrade to Solo, then later hit Moment 4 as Seller Solo and route to Starter without violating the anti-spam rule.

**Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee (C.139) binding.** Every Conversion Moment upgrade flow MUST surface the Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee summary on the upgrade screen: *"Everything you've built — KB, in-flight bids, Capability Declarations, Firecrawl source configs — moves with you. No re-bootstrap. No re-indexing. No fidelity loss."* (Verbatim copy per C.139.) Failure to surface this is a §48.8.7 anti-pattern violation and a P3 QA defect.

**Conversion-Moment Dashboard.** Per-Seller-Org Conversion-Moment funnel (trigger → prompt-rendered → click → upgrade complete) tile on the Seller Activation Dashboard (§48.1.6). Per-moment-kind aggregate trailing-90-day conversion rate tile (target ≥ 18% per SPS v3 §15.3 / C.133) on the Forced-Signup Funnel Dashboard. Moment 1 (mid-bid AI budget wall) MUST be segmented separately from the three pre-Solo baseline moments so Free -> Solo conversion is measurable.

**Cross-references.** §4.4.22 SellerOnboardingSession (`stage_7_*` fields); §48.8.6 (full UX surface spec); §34.13 Subscription Tier Change (the upgrade fulfillment surface); §15 (Stripe Checkout flow); SPS v3 §15.3; C.133 (pre-Solo conversion-moment baseline); C.139 (Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee — appendix); §22.x KBEntry (KB ceiling source field); §34.10.4 / Appendix C `billing.wallet.cap_warning_100` and Appendix G `seller_aiwallet_budget_exhausted_during_onboarding` (mid-bid wall source signals).

### 48.1.8 Acceptance Criteria (Extended) {#48.1.8-acceptance-criteria-extended}

(Extends §48.1.4. The criteria below are additive to §48.1.4 and apply to the §48.1.5–§48.1.7 extensions.)

9. Every Forced-Vendor-Signup arrival (`invite_source ∈ {buyer_invite, ghost_bid_conversion, pro_trial_seat_m17}`) MUST traverse all four Hero Moment phases (§48.1.5) when the dependency stack (Bootstrap, First-Pass Responder, Bid Workspace populator) is healthy; phase-skipping MUST NOT silently degrade — it MUST emit `hero_moment_phase_skipped {seller_org_id, phase, reason ∈ {capability_unavailable, latency_breach, dependency_outage, anti_pattern_blocked}}` (Appendix G — new) per skip event AND set `SellerOnboardingSession.capability_degradation_triggered = true` if the skip is due to capability failure.
10. The Seller Activation Metric (§48.1.6) p50 and p90 dashboard tiles MUST refresh within 60 seconds of `first_requirement_response_at` writes; staleness > 60 seconds raises a §42 P3 alert; staleness > 5 minutes raises a P2.
11. The KB-Bootstrap acceptance-rate leading indicator (§48.1.6 #3) MUST be denominated by **activated** sessions only (sessions where `activation_achieved = true`); abandoned or errored sessions are excluded from the denominator. A daily reconciliation job confirms denominator integrity; drift > 1% pages `ops_growth_admin`.
12. Each of the four Seller Conversion Moments (§48.1.7) MUST emit its named trigger PostHog event within the windows specified in the §48.1.7 acceptance-window column; CI gates merge if any trigger-event integration test is missing or skipped.
13. Each Conversion Moment upgrade flow MUST surface the Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee verbatim copy per §48.1.7; a UX-fixture-snapshot test guards the copy; copy drift fails CI.
14. The mutual-exclusivity invariant (§48.1.7) MUST be enforced at the SellerOnboardingSession write path per `(seller_org_id, moment_kind, plan_tier)`: duplicate writes for the same tuple return HTTP 409 `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_already_recorded` (Appendix I) AND the offending event is appended to `metadata_json.subsequent_conversion_moments_fired[]`; distinct plan-stage observations after a successful Free -> Solo upgrade are allowed. A property test asserts 100% invariant retention across 10,000 simulated dual-trigger sequences.
15. The Conversion Moment trailing-90-day conversion rate (§48.1.7) MUST be queryable per moment kind (including `mid_bid_ai_budget_wall`), per `invite_source`, per `data_residency_region`, per calendar week of `stage_1_arrival_at`, AND per `bid_id`-derived buyer-Org cohort; query latency p95 ≤ 30 seconds at full population.
16. The Hero Moment four-phase framework (§48.1.5) MUST be enforced as a state-machine on the SellerOnboardingSession write path; out-of-order phase advancement attempts (e.g., setting `stage_5_stake_reveal_rendered_at` before `first_requirement_response_at`) are permitted ONLY when documented in §48.1.5 phase-to-stage mapping (e.g., Stage 6 Outcome Debrief firing after Stage 7 Conversion Moment is allowed because Stage 6 fires asynchronously at bid close); other out-of-order writes return HTTP 422 `seller_onboarding_phase_invariant_violation` (Appendix I — new).
17. The forty-second-Anthropic-cost-cap on Hero Moment AI work MUST hold: total AIWallet debits across all Hero-Moment-phase capabilities (`kb_bootstrap` + `first_pass_response` + `q_and_a_suggestion` + `page_enrichment`) per session MUST NOT exceed `$5.00` (the Free Seller Wallet allowance per §34.10.4). Sessions that would exceed the cap MUST proceed in cost-priced-rejected mode (no charge to the seller) AND surface the *"Some requirements need more budget"* inline message per §48.1.5 phase 3 narrative; events `hero_moment_wallet_cap_breached {seller_org_id, capability_id, attempted_debit_cents, remaining_balance_cents}` (Appendix G — new) emit per overflow.
18. Buyer Console attempts to read SellerOnboardingSession-derived analytics (e.g., a buyer admin trying to query "how long did our invited vendors take to activate?") MUST return HTTP 404 with audit-log entry `firewall_violation_scope = seller_activation_analytics_cross_console_access` (Appendix I `seller_onboarding_cross_console_access` — existing). Aggregate funnel rollups MAY be exposed to buyer-side dashboards ONLY at the per-`bid_id` level AND ONLY when k-anonymity floor k=5 is satisfied (`COUNT(DISTINCT seller_org_id) ≥ 5`).

## 48.2 The 10 Core Growth Loops {#48.2-the-10-core-growth-loops}

**Authoring intent.** §48.2 enumerates the 10 numbered loops named in Summary §3.2 — including the two retired entries (annotated in place per the prompt's "retired, replaced by MX" requirement) — and gives each a full spec block: id, mechanism, trigger event, acting entity, targeted entity, telemetry events (PostHog), anti-spam controls, and acceptance criteria. The numbering 1–10 is preserved verbatim from the Summary so the cross-document mapping is unambiguous; retired loops retain their slot rather than being deleted. Two new growth-domain entities are introduced in §48.2.12 to make per-loop execution observable and auditable: GrowthLoopExecution and GrowthLoopKillSwitch.

### 48.2.2 Loop L1: Vendor-Invite-Creates-Account {#48.2.2-l1-vendor-invite-creates-account}

**Mechanism.** Every vendor invited to a buyer's evaluation receives a magic-link signup email. On signup, the vendor's first bid response triggers `kb_bootstrap` (§21.4.2; 1 lifetime free per Seller Org per Summary C.73) which seeds their KB with 50–500 extracted entries. Each buyer evaluation seeds an estimated 3–10 new Seller Orgs.

**Trigger event.** Buyer creates a §4.3.x Target Account whose `email_domain` is not associated with an existing Seller Org with `account_status ∈ {active, pending_approval}`. The trigger fires at Target Account write, not at email send — so the signup-attribution window opens before the first email touch.

**Acting entity.** Buyer Org (specifically, the user with `workspace_admin` OR `use_case_lead` role; §5.2 RBAC).

**Targeted entity.** The vendor named on the Target Account (a not-yet-provisioned Seller Org).

**Loop instrumentation entity.** GrowthLoopExecution (§48.2.12) row with `loop_id=vendor_invite_creates_account`; one row per Target Account created. Lifecycle states per §48.2.12 state machine. The row's `target_seller_org_id` is null at creation and populated when the vendor signs up (within the 60-day attribution window).

**Telemetry events (Appendix G — new).**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `growth_loop_l1_invite_emitted` | Target Account written; email queued to Loops.so | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `buyer_org_id`, `vendor_email_domain_hash` (SHA-256, 12 hex), `invitation_kind ∈ {direct_invite, m5_buyer_pull, m17_pro_trial}` |
| `growth_loop_l1_invite_clicked` | Magic-link click recorded | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `buyer_org_id`, `time_to_click_seconds`, `user_agent_class` |
| `growth_loop_l1_signup_attributed` | Vendor signs up within 60-day attribution window | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `buyer_org_id`, `vendor_org_id`, `time_to_signup_seconds`, `m17_grant_id` (nullable) |
| `growth_loop_l1_first_bid_completed` | First bid submitted by the attributed Seller Org | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `vendor_org_id`, `bid_workspace_id`, `kb_bootstrap_initiated` (Boolean) |
| `growth_loop_l1_kb_seeded` | `kb_bootstrap` AIOperation reaches `settlement_state=accepted` (≥ 60% of proposed entries approved) | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `vendor_org_id`, `kb_entries_seeded_count`, `bootstrap_ai_operation_id` |
| `growth_loop_l1_attribution_expired` | 60-day attribution window closes without signup | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `buyer_org_id`, `vendor_email_domain_hash` |

**Anti-spam controls.**

1. Per-user invite throttle: 20 invites/user/30 days at Buyer Free, 50/Buyer Starter, 100/Buyer Growth, 200/Buyer Scale, unlimited at Enterprise (caller-side throttle; rejected with `growth_loop_l1_throttle_exhausted` HTTP 429 — Appendix I — new).
2. Per-target-domain throttle: 5 distinct buyer Orgs/30 days per `vendor_email_domain` (target-side throttle to prevent collusive over-targeting of a single vendor). Excess invites are accepted but emit `growth_loop_l1_target_throttled {vendor_email_domain_hash}` (Appendix G — new) and route the email to a deferred-send queue.
3. Shared-use-domain exclusion: `vendor_email_domain` matched against the §48.4.3 shared-use-domain registry (e.g., gmail.com, outlook.com); excluded domains are rejected at Target Account write with `growth_loop_l1_invite_shared_use_domain_rejected` (HTTP 422; Appendix I — new).
4. DMARC/SPF preflight: §48.4.2 reputation check on `buyer_org.org_email_domain` runs before the email send — a domain with `dmarc_alignment_pass_rate < 0.85` (rolling 7d) defers all L1 invites to a manual-review queue and emits `growth_loop_l1_dmarc_preflight_failed {buyer_org_id}` (Appendix G — new).
5. Vendor Opt-Out check: `vendor_email_domain` matched against Vendor Opt-Out Records (§4.4.8) AND the global Vendor Opt-Out Registry (§4.4.8 + §48.4.9) — opted-out vendors are NEVER emailed; the Target Account is created with `vendor_opt_out_ref_id` populated and the Email send is suppressed with audit row `email_suppressed_by_vendor_opt_out`.
6. Signal Integrity Monitor (Summary C.100) cross-reference: per-Org rolling 30-day signup-attribution rate is monitored; an Org whose attribution rate drops > 3σ below cohort baseline is flagged for SIM review (low rate may indicate spam invitations to non-existent vendors). Conversely, an Org whose invite velocity exceeds 4× cohort 95th-percentile triggers a `growth_loop_velocity_anomaly_detected` SIM event (Appendix G — new) and an Ops kill-switch eligibility flag.

**Notification cross-references.** `vendor_invited` notification (Appendix C, existing) is the email; no new notification kinds are introduced for L1.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Every Target Account write whose `email_domain` is not associated with an existing Seller Org MUST create exactly one GrowthLoopExecution row with `loop_id=vendor_invite_creates_account` within 5 seconds.
2. `growth_loop_l1_invite_emitted` MUST be emitted before the email enters the Loops.so send queue; failure to emit blocks the send.
3. Throttle breaches (per-user, per-target-domain) MUST return HTTP 429 from the Target Account create endpoint; the response MUST include `Retry-After` seconds AND a JSON body with `throttle_kind ∈ {per_user, per_target_domain}` and `next_allowed_at`.
4. Shared-use-domain rejections MUST return HTTP 422 with `error_code=growth_loop_l1_invite_shared_use_domain_rejected` and a human-readable error message naming the rejected domain.
5. The 60-day attribution window MUST be evaluated against `growth_loop_execution.created_at`; signups beyond the window emit `growth_loop_l1_attribution_expired` and do NOT credit the original buyer.
6. The funnel `growth_loop_l1_invite_emitted → invite_clicked → signup_attributed → first_bid_completed → kb_seeded` MUST be queryable in PostHog Insights → Funnels with `growth_loop_execution_id` as the funnel key; the full funnel resolves at p95 ≤ 30 seconds across the full execution-row population.
7. SIM velocity anomaly detection MUST raise an `Ops Growth Console` alert (new surface; §48.3.3) within 5 minutes of the anomalous window crossing.
8. `kb_bootstrap` outcome correlation: every `growth_loop_l1_kb_seeded` event MUST carry the `bootstrap_ai_operation_id` linkable to the §4.8.1 AIOperation row with matching `id`; orphan events are flagged in the nightly audit job.

**Failure modes addressed.**

1. **Buyer Org with poor email reputation tries to abuse L1 to mass-invite vendors.** Resolved by §48.4.2 DMARC preflight (control #4) + §48.4.9 vendor opt-out + per-user throttle.
2. **Magic-link expiration (vendor signs up 91 days after invite).** Resolved by `growth_loop_l1_attribution_expired` semantics — signups outside the window are not credited but DO still create a Seller Org (no data loss); the event is logged for forensic review.
3. **Vendor signs up via direct path while invite is in-flight (race).** Resolved by signup-time matching on `vendor_email_domain`: the GrowthLoopExecution row is reconciled within the 60-day window via nightly job; ambiguous matches (multiple in-flight invites from different buyers) credit the earliest invite, emit `growth_loop_l1_attribution_ambiguous_resolved {chosen_buyer_org_id, contender_buyer_org_ids[]}`, and notify all contenders for visibility.

### 48.2.3 Loop L2: Template-Clone-Attribution {#48.2.3-l2-template-clone-attribution}

**Mechanism.** Every cloned template carries a badge linking back to the originating Seller — clicks deep-link into the §4.4.10 SellerOrgPage and §4.4.11 SoftwarePage. Template adoption compounds seller visibility into Marketplace traffic.

**Trigger event.** Buyer user clones a published seller-authored Template (Template visibility = `marketplace_published`) into a new Workspace OR appends template content to an existing Workspace.

**Acting entity.** Buyer Org (workspace creator OR admin with template-clone permission).

**Targeted entity.** The Seller Org that authored and published the cloned template.

**Loop instrumentation entity.** GrowthLoopExecution row with `loop_id=template_clone_attribution`. The row records `template_id`, `template_version`, `originating_seller_org_id`, `cloning_buyer_org_id`, `clone_workspace_id`, and a denormalized `template_clone_lineage_depth` (depth of fork-chain from the original Sourcera-authored or seller-authored root).

**Telemetry events (Appendix G — new).**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `growth_loop_l2_template_cloned` | Workspace created from template OR template appended | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `template_id`, `template_version`, `originating_seller_org_id`, `cloning_buyer_org_id`, `clone_kind ∈ {new_workspace, append_to_existing}`, `template_clone_lineage_depth` |
| `growth_loop_l2_attribution_badge_rendered` | Workspace UI renders the "Cloned from {SellerOrgName}" badge | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `surface ∈ {workspace_header, requirements_index, use_case_modal}`, `viewing_user_id`, `viewing_org_id` |
| `growth_loop_l2_attribution_badge_clicked` | Buyer user clicks the attribution badge | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `target_page_kind ∈ {seller_org_page, software_page}`, `target_page_id` |
| `growth_loop_l2_attribution_eoi_emitted` | EOI submitted from the cloning Workspace within 30 days, citing the cloned template's seller in the EOI rationale | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `eoi_id`, `seller_org_id`, `time_from_clone_to_eoi_seconds` |

**Anti-spam controls.**

1. **Template anti-spam classifier** (§48.4.5) gates publication, not cloning — a published template has already passed the classifier, so the loop trusts the publication state.
2. **Vendor Opt-Out:** if the originating seller activates a Vendor Opt-Out (§4.4.8) with scope covering the template's content (e.g., `scope_kind=software` matching the template's referenced SellerSoftware), the attribution badge is rendered as "Originating vendor opted out of attribution" and the deep-link target is suppressed (rendered as a non-clickable label). The clone itself is preserved (the buyer's Workspace content is unchanged); only the public attribution surface respects the opt-out.
3. **Lineage depth cap:** templates with `template_clone_lineage_depth > 5` (i.e., a clone of a clone of a clone of a clone of a clone) drop the seller attribution badge entirely, since the originating-seller signal is too diluted to be meaningful. Cap is configurable per-environment.
4. **Self-clone exclusion:** a Seller Org cloning its own template into its own Buyer-Console Workspace (dual-console Org) does NOT emit L2 events — this would inflate the loop's apparent performance.

**Notification cross-references.** None — L2 is silent to the seller until the EOI cross-link surfaces the path in the seller's own EOI inspector.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Every clone of a `marketplace_published` template MUST emit `growth_loop_l2_template_cloned` within 5 seconds AND create a GrowthLoopExecution row.
2. The attribution badge MUST render in the cloning Workspace's header, requirement index header, AND use-case modal header within 1 second p95 of the Workspace load.
3. Clicks on the badge MUST navigate to the seller's primary public surface — `software_page` if the template's `template_referenced_seller_software_id` is non-null AND the SoftwarePage is `published`; otherwise `seller_org_page`.
4. EOI cross-attribution MUST be observable via PostHog funnel `growth_loop_l2_template_cloned → growth_loop_l2_attribution_eoi_emitted` keyed by `(buyer_org_id, originating_seller_org_id)` within the 30-day attribution window.
5. Vendor Opt-Out applied AFTER a clone has occurred MUST update the attribution badge state on next render (within the §4.4.8 60-second snapshot freshness floor) — the historical clone event is not retroactively redacted.
6. Lineage depth > 5 MUST suppress the attribution badge AND emit `growth_loop_l2_attribution_badge_lineage_capped {growth_loop_execution_id, lineage_depth}` (Appendix G — new) on the would-have-rendered surface.
7. Self-clones (same Org on both sides) MUST NOT create GrowthLoopExecution rows; a nightly audit job rejects any row whose `cloning_buyer_org_id == originating_seller_org_id` and emits `analytics_invariant_violation` for forensic review.

**Failure modes addressed.**

1. **Seller spams the template library to acquire attribution.** Resolved by §48.4.5 ML classifier at publication, §48.4.8 suppression list, and Ops template review (§19 + Summary C.96).
2. **Buyer clones template, then renames the Workspace to obscure attribution.** Resolved: attribution is a structural property of the clone lineage, not of the Workspace name; the badge is always rendered regardless of rename.
3. **Originating Seller Org is deleted while clones remain in market.** Resolved: the badge falls back to a static "Originating vendor no longer on Sourcera" label with no deep-link; the GrowthLoopExecution row preserves the historical `originating_seller_org_id` for audit.

### 48.2.4 Loop L3: (Retired — Legacy Selection Report Sharing) {#48.2.4-l3-retired-selection-report-share}

**Status: retired, replaced by M2 (Selection Report Public Link, watermarked).** Legacy direct-share-by-link mechanic is superseded by the M2 watermarked-public-link surface (Summary §3.3 M2, Appendix C extension entry). The retired loop's identifier `selection_report_share_legacy` is reserved (Appendix J `growth_loop_id`); no telemetry, no anti-spam controls, no acceptance criteria. Migration: any data referencing the retired loop slug from pre-v7 instrumentation is preserved in the §4.3.18 Usage Event ledger but excluded from §48.3 dashboards. Replacement surface authored at §4.4.x (M2 Public Selection Report entity — registered placeholder pending full M2 entity authoring; see Known Gaps in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md`).

### 48.2.5 Loop L4: Seller-Profile SEO {#48.2.5-l4-seller-profile-seo}

**Mechanism.** Public §4.4.10 SellerOrgPage and §4.4.11 SoftwarePage emit Schema.org structured data; organic search traffic compounds into Marketplace sessions. M9 Category Pages, M10 Guide Pages, M11 Comparison Pages, M12 Market Intelligence Reports, and M13 Heat Map pages amplify the seller's discoverability surface area.

**Trigger event.** Seller Org transitions a SellerOrgPage OR SoftwarePage to `page_status=published` (§4.4.10 / §4.4.11).

**Acting entity.** Seller Org (authoring user with `workspace_admin` role on the Seller Console).

**Targeted entity.** Search engines (indirect); ultimately, prospective buyer Orgs reaching the page via organic search.

**Loop instrumentation entity.** GrowthLoopExecution row with `loop_id=seller_profile_seo`. One row per published page (`(seller_org_id, page_kind ∈ {seller_org_page, software_page}, page_id)`).

**Telemetry events (Appendix G — new).**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `growth_loop_l4_page_published` | Page transitions to `published` | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `page_kind`, `page_id`, `seller_org_id`, `schema_org_payload_kind ∈ {organization, product, faq_page, item_list}`, `vendor_opt_out_ref_id` (nullable) |
| `growth_loop_l4_organic_session_started` | Public-page session whose `referrer_kind=search_engine` (per §41 + Marketplace edge attribution) | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `page_kind`, `page_id`, `seller_org_id`, `search_engine ∈ {google, bing, duckduckgo, brave, other}`, `query_intent_class` (truncated; see §48.4.7 k-anonymity floor) |
| `growth_loop_l4_organic_to_eoi` | EOI submitted within session whose first touch was a `growth_loop_l4_organic_session_started` | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `eoi_id`, `seller_org_id`, `time_from_session_to_eoi_seconds`, `pages_visited_count` |
| `growth_loop_l4_organic_to_signup` | New buyer Org signup whose attribution session was a `growth_loop_l4_organic_session_started` | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `attributed_seller_org_id`, `new_buyer_org_id`, `time_from_session_to_signup_seconds` |

**Anti-spam controls.**

1. Schema.org payload validator at publish-time (§4.4.10, §4.4.11) — malformed payloads block publish.
2. §48.4.4 content validators on `seller_org_description` and `software_description` — adversarial content (cross-site scripting, structured-data injection, off-topic promotional spam) blocks publish AND emits `growth_loop_l4_page_publish_content_rejected` (Appendix G — new).
3. Vendor Opt-Out (§4.4.8) honored: opted-out pages return `410 Gone` and are excluded from sitemap.xml; the Schema.org payload is omitted entirely (not blanked).
4. SEO-quality floor: pages with `seller_org_description.length < 200 chars` OR `software_description.length < 300 chars` are publishable but emit `growth_loop_l4_page_seo_quality_warning` (Appendix G — new) and are deprioritized in `/sitemap.xml` (rendered with `<priority>0.3</priority>` instead of the default `<priority>0.7</priority>`).
5. Search-query intent classification (`query_intent_class` property) is bucketed via §48.4.7 k=5 floor — buckets with cohort < 5 in the rolling 30-day window collapse into `query_intent_class=other` to prevent k-anonymity collisions.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. `growth_loop_l4_page_published` MUST be emitted within 5 seconds of page publication AND MUST carry the resolved Schema.org payload kind.
2. The page's Schema.org payload MUST validate against the Google Rich Results test corpus (CI-gated; failure blocks publish).
3. Organic-session attribution MUST be honored across the §4.5 marketplace domain edge — the `referrer_kind` and `search_engine` properties are populated via the §41 referrer-parsing pipeline; failures default to `referrer_kind=unknown` and DO NOT inflate `growth_loop_l4_organic_session_started`.
4. EOI-to-organic correlation MUST link via session-cookie carrying the `growth_loop_execution_id` of the first L4 organic session within the 90-day session-cookie TTL.
5. Vendor Opt-Out applied to a previously-published page MUST update sitemap.xml within 60 minutes AND deindex the page via Google Search Console API within 24 hours; failure raises a §42 P2 alert.
6. The L4 funnel `page_published → organic_session_started → organic_to_eoi` MUST be queryable per `seller_org_id` AND aggregable to the platform level for §48.3.3 SEO ROI dashboards.
7. The L4 funnel `page_published → organic_session_started → organic_to_signup` MUST attribute new Buyer Org signups to the `attributed_seller_org_id` for the Marketplace-side Sales referral analytics.

**Failure modes addressed.**

1. **Schema.org schema changes break the seller payload (e.g., Google deprecates `AggregateRating` for Organization).** Resolved: nightly Schema.org validator re-runs; deprecations emit `growth_loop_l4_schema_org_validator_deprecation_warning` (Appendix G — new) and trigger Ops-managed payload-template updates per §4.4.10 schema_org_payload_template_version.
2. **Seller publishes adversarial content to game ranking (e.g., keyword stuffing).** Resolved by §48.4.4 content validator + §48.4.5 ML spam classifier (cross-applied to seller-authored Marketplace content) + Ops periodic audit per §43 admin tooling.
3. **Search engine indexes a page that has since been opt-out-redacted.** Resolved by sitemap.xml regeneration within 60 min + Google Search Console deindexing within 24 h + the §4.5.6 render contract returning `410 Gone` so search-engine crawlers naturally drop the URL.

### 48.2.6 Loop L5: Free-AI-Teaser-to-Paid {#48.2.6-l5-free-ai-teaser-to-paid}

**Mechanism.** Per Summary C.80 and §4.8.7 FreeAllowanceCounter, every customer-billed capability grants 10 free operations on signup as a PLG lever. Exhaustion surfaces an inline upgrade CTA with the ROI of the operations already run. The 10-free-per-capability allowance is the primary PLG lever.

**Trigger event.** AIOperation against a `customer_billed` capability decrements `FreeAllowanceCounter.quantity_remaining`; on the operation that takes the counter to 0, the upgrade CTA is rendered.

**Acting entity.** Sourcera platform (the loop is platform-orchestrated, not user-initiated); the actor user is the operator who triggers the final consumption.

**Targeted entity.** The Org being decremented (Buyer or Seller, console-scoped per FreeAllowanceCounter).

**Loop instrumentation entity.** GrowthLoopExecution row with `loop_id=free_ai_teaser_to_paid`. One row per `(org_id, capability_id)` pair, created at first AIOperation invocation against the capability, closed when one of (a) the counter reaches 0, (b) Org upgrades to a tier that removes the free-allowance ceiling, OR (c) the row's TTL of 365 days is reached without exhaustion (cold-loop closure).

**Telemetry events (Appendix G — new).**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `growth_loop_l5_first_use` | First AIOperation against the capability for the Org | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `org_id`, `capability_id`, `console`, `quantity_remaining_after` |
| `growth_loop_l5_threshold_warning` | `quantity_remaining` crosses ≤ 3 (configurable per environment) | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `org_id`, `capability_id`, `quantity_remaining` |
| `growth_loop_l5_exhaustion` | `quantity_remaining` reaches 0 | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `org_id`, `capability_id`, `total_value_received_usd` (sum of `value_price` across consumed ops), `console`, `actor_user_id` |
| `growth_loop_l5_upgrade_cta_rendered` | Inline upgrade CTA rendered post-exhaustion | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `cta_surface ∈ {ui_free_allowance_exhausted_modal, ui_capability_paywall, ui_workspace_inline_banner, command_palette}`, `cta_copy_variant`, `triggering_event=growth_loop_l5_exhaustion` |
| `growth_loop_l5_upgrade_completed` | Org upgrades plan within 30-day attribution window with `upgrade_completed.trigger=ai_budget_exhaustion` per §34.5.1 + Appendix G `upgrade_completed_trigger` enum | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `org_id`, `plan_from`, `plan_to`, `time_from_exhaustion_to_upgrade_seconds`, `cta_views_before_upgrade` |

**Anti-spam controls.**

1. **Per-capability-per-Org single-counter invariant** (§4.8.7) — only one FreeAllowanceCounter per `(org_id, capability_id)`; cannot be reset to extend the teaser.
2. **Anti-fatigue quiet rules** (`Sourcera_Buyer_Pricing_Strategy.md` §6 + §29.3 user preferences): in-app `growth_loop_l5_upgrade_cta_rendered` is at most once per surface per session AND `growth_loop_l5_upgrade_cta_rendered.cta_surface=ui_free_allowance_exhausted_modal` is at most once per Org per capability per 7-day window.
3. **Cross-Org abuse:** a user attempting to create multiple Orgs under the same payment-card hash to harvest Free Allowances is detected by §48.4.6 referral fraud controls (`same_payment_method` signal) and SIM `cross_org_free_allowance_harvest_detected` (Appendix G — new); offending Orgs lose the Free Allowance via `FreeAllowanceCounter.suppressed_by_fraud=true` (new field on §4.8.7; flagged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` → Authored Extensions).
4. **Capability-level kill-switch (Ops Console):** Ops MAY disable the L5 mechanic for a specific capability if that capability is being abused; disabling sets `FreeAllowanceCounter.disabled=true` for new counters AND emits `growth_loop_l5_capability_disabled {capability_id, ops_actor_user_id, reason}` (Appendix G — new). Existing counters are NOT retroactively zeroed; they continue to function until exhausted.

**Notification cross-references.** `billing.free_allowance.exhausted` (Appendix C, existing) is the customer notification of the underlying `FreeAllowanceCounter` exhaustion; `growth_loop_l5_exhaustion` is the analytics-side dual.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Every first invocation of a `customer_billed` capability for a given `(org_id, capability_id)` MUST emit `growth_loop_l5_first_use` AND create a GrowthLoopExecution row within 5 seconds.
2. The exhaustion CTA MUST render within 1 second p95 of the AIOperation completion that took `quantity_remaining` to 0; render failure raises a §42 P2 alert.
3. The CTA copy MUST contain both (a) the ROI of operations already run (`total_value_received_usd` displayed in the customer's `billing_currency`) and (b) the upgrade target plan (`plan_to`).
4. The L5 funnel `growth_loop_l5_first_use → growth_loop_l5_threshold_warning → growth_loop_l5_exhaustion → growth_loop_l5_upgrade_cta_rendered → growth_loop_l5_upgrade_completed` MUST be PostHog-queryable per `(org_id, capability_id)`.
5. Cross-Org Free-Allowance-harvest detection MUST suppress the Free Allowance for offending Orgs within 60 seconds of SIM detection AND emit a §29 notification to the offending Org's Billing Admin (notification kind `free_allowance_suppressed_by_fraud` — Appendix C extension below).
6. Capability-level kill-switch MUST take effect within 60 seconds of Ops Console publish AND MUST NOT zero existing FreeAllowanceCounter rows.

**Failure modes addressed.**

1. **Customer hits exhaustion at end of business day, never sees CTA, churns silently.** Resolved by `billing.free_allowance.exhausted` email notification (Appendix C, existing) + `growth_loop_l5_threshold_warning` email at `quantity_remaining ≤ 3` (new email subscription, default off but recommended at signup; see Appendix C extension below).
2. **AIOperation that exhausts the counter is later contested and reversed.** Resolved: contest reversal restores `quantity_remaining` per §34.11 Outcome Resolver semantics; the `growth_loop_l5_exhaustion` event is NOT retroactively rolled back (it remains a forensic record), but a `growth_loop_l5_exhaustion_reversed {growth_loop_execution_id, contest_record_id}` event (Appendix G — new) is emitted for analytics integrity.
3. **Capability-level kill-switch rolled forward by Ops mistakenly.** Resolved: kill-switch is publish-path with optimistic concurrency check (§22.16.5) and an audit row; rollback is single-click and takes effect within 60 seconds.

### 48.2.7 Loop L6: (Retired — Legacy Domain-Match Auto-Suggest) {#48.2.7-l6-retired-domain-match-auto-suggest}

**Status: retired, replaced by M7 (Suggested Team Discovery).** Legacy domain-match team-suggestion mechanic is superseded by the M7 surface authored against the §21.4.2 `team_suggestion` capability and the Summary C.65 entry. Reserved slug: `domain_match_auto_suggest_legacy`. No telemetry, no anti-spam controls, no acceptance criteria. Replacement surface authored at §21.4.2 (capability) + Summary C.65 (M7 mechanic narrative). The k-anonymity floor for M7 cohort displays is k=5 per §48.4.7.

### 48.2.8 Loop L7: Cmd+K Suggestion Loop {#48.2.8-l7-cmd-k-suggestion-loop}

**Mechanism.** Per Summary §3.2 #7 + Summary §6.16 (M9 §6.16.5), the §30 Command Palette (Cmd+K) surfaces relevant Marketplace content based on current page context. Examples: viewing a data-privacy requirement surfaces matching SoftwarePages (§4.4.11) and CategoryPages (§4.4.12); viewing a Use Case surfaces matching ComparisonPages (§4.4.14); viewing a TCO Use Case surfaces matching MarketIntelligenceReports (§4.4.15) for pricing-band signals.

**Trigger event.** User opens Cmd+K (`command_palette_opened`, existing in Appendix G) AND the open-context resolves to a Marketplace-eligible context type (`requirement`, `use_case`, `tco_use_case`, `vendor_disqualification`, OR `bid_workspace`).

**Acting entity.** The user opening the palette (any role on either console).

**Targeted entity.** Marketplace pages (CategoryPage, GuidePage, ComparisonPage, MarketIntelligenceReport, SoftwarePage, SellerOrgPage) AND, indirectly, the Seller Orgs they reference.

**Loop instrumentation entity.** GrowthLoopExecution row with `loop_id=cmd_k_suggestion`. One row per `command_palette_opened` event whose context is Marketplace-eligible. The row records the originating user, Org, console, palette context, and the suggestions surfaced.

**Telemetry events (Appendix G — new).**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `growth_loop_l7_palette_marketplace_eligible` | `command_palette_opened` whose context is Marketplace-eligible | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `org_id`, `console`, `palette_context_kind ∈ {requirement, use_case, tco_use_case, vendor_disqualification, bid_workspace}`, `palette_context_id`, `suggestion_engine_version` |
| `growth_loop_l7_suggestions_returned` | Suggestion engine returns ≥ 1 result | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `result_count`, `result_kinds[] ⊆ {category_page, guide_page, comparison_page, market_intelligence_report, software_page, seller_org_page}`, `latency_ms` |
| `growth_loop_l7_suggestion_clicked` | User clicks a Marketplace suggestion | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `result_kind`, `result_id`, `result_position` (1-indexed), `time_to_click_ms` |
| `growth_loop_l7_suggestion_to_eoi` | EOI submitted within 30-day attribution window for the seller named on the clicked suggestion | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `eoi_id`, `seller_org_id`, `clicked_result_kind`, `clicked_result_id` |

**Anti-spam controls.**

1. **Vendor Opt-Out applied** (§4.4.8): suggestions whose `seller_org_id` has an active Vendor Opt-Out are filtered out at the suggestion-engine retrieval layer; opted-out suggestions never appear in the palette.
2. **k-Anonymity floor for context-driven suggestions**: cohort size for the `palette_context_kind` × `palette_context_id` cohort MUST be ≥ 5 buyer Orgs in the rolling 30-day window before context-personalized ranking is applied; below the floor, the palette returns generic-category suggestions only and emits `growth_loop_l7_k_anon_floor_hit` (Appendix G — new).
3. **Marketplace abuse signal** (§4.5.7 Marketplace Abuse Report): a Seller Org with ≥ 3 active Marketplace Abuse Reports of `kind=spam_listing` OR `kind=misrepresentation` in the rolling 90-day window is excluded from L7 suggestions until the reports are resolved; emits `growth_loop_l7_seller_excluded_by_abuse_state` (Appendix G — new).
4. **Click-fraud detection**: clicks whose `time_to_click_ms < 50` (super-fast clicks indicating automation) are flagged as suspect AND excluded from EOI-attribution credit; SIM accumulates and reviews.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. `growth_loop_l7_palette_marketplace_eligible` MUST be emitted within the same request as the underlying `command_palette_opened` event (synchronous); orphan opens fail QA.
2. Suggestion engine latency MUST satisfy p95 ≤ 250 ms from `growth_loop_l7_palette_marketplace_eligible` to `growth_loop_l7_suggestions_returned`; breaches trigger a §42 P2 alert per §44 performance budget.
3. Vendor-opt-out filtering MUST be enforced at the engine layer, NOT the UI layer; UI-only filtering is rejected in code review.
4. The full L7 funnel `palette_marketplace_eligible → suggestions_returned → suggestion_clicked → suggestion_to_eoi` MUST be PostHog-queryable per `seller_org_id` AND per `palette_context_kind`.
5. k-anonymity floor enforcement MUST be unit-tested with synthetic cohort sizes of {0, 4, 5, 6} — only the {5, 6} cases proceed with personalized ranking.
6. Marketplace-abuse-state exclusion MUST be reflected within 60 seconds of the third report being filed (Marketplace Abuse Report write); exclusion is removed within 60 seconds of report resolution.

**Failure modes addressed.**

1. **Suggestion engine returns stale results after a vendor opt-out is filed.** Resolved by §4.5.6 60-second snapshot freshness floor on the opt-out cache that the suggestion engine reads.
2. **Suggestion engine timeout due to upstream Marketplace search service degradation.** Resolved: the palette degrades to non-Marketplace results (existing palette commands) and emits `growth_loop_l7_suggestion_engine_degraded` (Appendix G — new); the underlying §44 SLO measures the percentage of palette opens that get Marketplace suggestions.
3. **A buyer's context contains PII (e.g., a requirement description with a stakeholder's name) that the suggestion engine accidentally embeds in a query to upstream MarketIntelligence.** Resolved: §48.4.4 content validators run on the palette query before forwarding; PII is stripped via the §6.8 PII redaction pipeline before the engine sees the query.

### 48.2.9 Loop L8: Bid-Close-Offers-KB-Sync {#48.2.9-l8-bid-close-offers-kb-sync}

**Mechanism.** On bid close (BidWorkspace transitions to `closed` per §23 / Appendix E), the seller is offered a one-click "save this response to KB" CTA per Summary §3.2 #8. Adoption of the CTA grows the seller's KB with high-quality, real-bid-validated content, which improves future First-Pass response quality and makes the seller stickier on Sourcera.

**Trigger event.** BidWorkspace transitions to `closed` per Appendix E.

**Acting entity.** Seller Org user with `bid_workspace_owner` OR `team_lead` role on the closed BidWorkspace.

**Targeted entity.** The Seller Org's KB (KBEntry namespace per §22.4).

**Loop instrumentation entity.** GrowthLoopExecution row with `loop_id=bid_close_kb_sync_offer`. One row per BidWorkspace close.

**Telemetry events (Appendix G — new).**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `growth_loop_l8_bid_close_cta_rendered` | BidWorkspace `closed`; CTA shown to bid-workspace-owner on next session OR via `kb.bid_close_offer_pending` notification (Appendix C extension below) | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `bid_workspace_id`, `seller_org_id`, `eligible_response_count` (number of `bid_response` rows whose grade is `submitted` AND not already in KB), `estimated_kb_seed_value_usd` (sum of `value_price` for projected `kb_entry_draft_create` ops) |
| `growth_loop_l8_bid_close_cta_clicked` | Seller user clicks the CTA | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `actor_user_id`, `time_from_render_to_click_seconds` |
| `growth_loop_l8_kb_sync_initiated` | KB sync AIOperation kicks off through the canonical `kb_suggestion_seller` path (legacy `kb_to_response_suggestion` strings alias-rewrite before write; see §21.4.1.A / §22.10) | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `parent_ai_operation_id`, `proposed_entry_count` |
| `growth_loop_l8_kb_sync_completed` | Sync AIOperation reaches `settlement_state=accepted` | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `parent_ai_operation_id`, `accepted_entry_count`, `rejected_entry_count`, `acceptance_rate` |
| `growth_loop_l8_kb_sync_dismissed` | Seller user dismisses the CTA without converting | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `dismissal_reason ∈ {not_interested, low_value, time_constraint, other}` (UI-collected; nullable) |

**Anti-spam controls.**

1. **Per-bid-workspace single-CTA invariant**: at most one `growth_loop_l8_bid_close_cta_rendered` per BidWorkspace; re-rendering the CTA after a dismissal is allowed only after a 30-day cooling period.
2. **Quality floor**: BidWorkspaces with `eligible_response_count < 5` do NOT render the CTA (the loop's value is too thin to justify the offer); such workspaces emit `growth_loop_l8_quality_floor_below_threshold {growth_loop_execution_id, eligible_response_count}` (Appendix G — new) at close.
3. **Vendor-disqualified-bid exclusion**: if the BidWorkspace ended in vendor disqualification (per §4.7.2 Vendor Disqualification Record), the CTA is suppressed — the bid response is not a clean signal for KB seeding.
4. **§22.16.7 KB injection scanner** runs on every entry seeded via L8, identical to manual KB ingestion; entries flagged as injection attempts are held for review.

**Notification cross-references.** New notification kind `kb.bid_close_offer_pending` (Appendix C extension below) — sent to bid-workspace-owner on bid close.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. BidWorkspace close MUST emit `growth_loop_l8_bid_close_cta_rendered` within 60 seconds AND create the GrowthLoopExecution row.
2. The CTA MUST surface in (a) the in-app inbox of the bid-workspace-owner and (b) the BidWorkspace post-close summary view; both surfaces share the `growth_loop_execution_id` for click-attribution.
3. CTA click MUST trigger the §22.10 seller KB-suggestion AIOperation using canonical `capability_id=kb_suggestion_seller` (legacy `kb_to_response_suggestion` input strings are alias-rewritten before write) OR an explicit `bid_close_kb_sync` capability (Appendix J `capability_id` — new placeholder; full capability authored in a follow-up KB-spec extension prompt) within 5 seconds.
4. Dismissal MUST persist a `dismissal_reason` to the GrowthLoopExecution row (Org-scoped audit visible to Seller Team Lead).
5. The full L8 funnel `cta_rendered → cta_clicked → kb_sync_initiated → kb_sync_completed` MUST be PostHog-queryable per `seller_org_id`; conversion-rate dashboards (§48.3.3) drive Sales-Ops messaging.
6. The KB-injection scanner pass MUST run within the AIOperation's existing settlement window; entries flagged as injection attempts MUST be held in `review_pending` state and surfaced to Seller Team Lead via existing `kb.entry.flagged_stale` semantics.

**Failure modes addressed.**

1. **Bid closes but the seller never returns to Sourcera.** Resolved: `kb.bid_close_offer_pending` notification (Appendix C extension; daily-digest aggregable) keeps the offer warm for 30 days; CTA expires after that window with a `growth_loop_l8_cta_expired` event (Appendix G — new).
2. **Seller clicks CTA but the KB sync AIOperation fails (e.g., MCP auth failure).** Resolved: failure emits `growth_loop_l8_kb_sync_failed {failure_reason}` (Appendix G — new) AND surfaces a retry CTA via `kb.session.mcp_auth_failed` semantics (Appendix C, existing).
3. **Seller game the loop by deliberately closing low-quality bids to seed KB with junk.** Resolved by §22.16.7 KB injection scanner + §48.4.5 content validators on synthesized KB entries + Ops periodic audit per §43.

### 48.2.10 Loop L9: Template Publish Incentive {#48.2.10-l9-template-publish-incentive}

**Mechanism.** Per Summary §3.2 #9, sellers earn visibility credits (featured placements in the §19 Template Library buyer-facing browse surface) for publishing templates that are widely cloned. The incentive amplifies L2 — a seller publishing a high-quality template gets featured placement, drives more clones, drives more attribution badges, drives more EOIs.

**Trigger event.** A seller-authored template's `clone_count_30d` (denormalized counter on the Template entity) crosses one of the configured incentive thresholds (default: 10 clones / 30d → "Trending"; 50 clones / 30d → "Featured"; 200 clones / 30d → "Top Pick").

**Acting entity.** Sourcera platform (the loop is platform-orchestrated; the Seller is the beneficiary).

**Targeted entity.** The Seller Org that authored the templated.

**Loop instrumentation entity.** GrowthLoopExecution row with `loop_id=template_publish_incentive`. One row per `(template_id, threshold_tier ∈ {trending, featured, top_pick})` pair; the row is reopened if the template oscillates above/below the threshold.

**Telemetry events (Appendix G — new).**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `growth_loop_l9_template_published` | Seller publishes a template to Marketplace | `growth_loop_execution_id` (placeholder; full row created on first threshold cross), `template_id`, `seller_org_id`, `template_clone_lineage_root` (the original template `id` from which this is forked, if any) |
| `growth_loop_l9_threshold_crossed` | `clone_count_30d` crosses a threshold from below | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `template_id`, `seller_org_id`, `threshold_tier ∈ {trending, featured, top_pick}`, `clone_count_30d_at_cross` |
| `growth_loop_l9_featured_placement_shown` | Buyer browses Template Library and sees the template in a featured slot | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `template_id`, `viewing_buyer_org_id`, `slot_kind ∈ {hero_carousel, trending_strip, top_pick_card}`, `slot_position` |
| `growth_loop_l9_threshold_decayed` | `clone_count_30d` drops below the active threshold | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `template_id`, `prior_threshold_tier`, `clone_count_30d_at_decay` |
| `growth_loop_l9_template_demoted_by_quality_signal` | Template demoted due to anti-spam OR quality signal (e.g., abuse reports OR low post-clone retention) | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `template_id`, `demotion_reason ∈ {abuse_reports, low_clone_retention, content_validator, ml_classifier_revision, ops_action}` |

**Anti-spam controls.**

1. **§48.4.5 Template Spam ML Classifier** runs at publish AND nightly across already-published templates; classifier-flagged templates are demoted from any incentive tier AND emit `growth_loop_l9_template_demoted_by_quality_signal {demotion_reason=ml_classifier_revision}`.
2. **Clone retention floor**: a template whose 30-day post-clone Workspace-deletion rate exceeds 50% (i.e., > 50% of cloning Workspaces are deleted within 30 days of clone) is demoted from the incentive tier — high deletion rate signals low value or spam-triggered cloning.
3. **Self-clone exclusion** (per L2): self-clones do NOT contribute to `clone_count_30d`.
4. **Cross-buyer-org diversity floor**: `clone_count_30d` must come from ≥ 5 distinct buyer Orgs to qualify for any threshold tier (k-anonymity-like floor preventing a single buyer Org from gaming the loop).
5. **Marketplace Abuse Report cross-reference** (§4.5.7): templates referenced in ≥ 3 active abuse reports are demoted regardless of clone count.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. `clone_count_30d` MUST be recomputed nightly by an audit job AND incrementally on each L2 clone event (race-resolution: nightly job is authoritative).
2. Threshold crossings MUST emit `growth_loop_l9_threshold_crossed` within 60 seconds of the cross.
3. Featured placements in the Template Library MUST honor the active threshold tier within 60 seconds of the cross AND MUST stop honoring it within 60 seconds of decay.
4. Cross-buyer-org diversity floor (≥ 5 distinct buyer Orgs) MUST be enforced; failures emit `growth_loop_l9_diversity_floor_below_threshold` (Appendix G — new) AND prevent the threshold cross.
5. Template Library buyer-browse surface (§19) MUST surface trending/featured/top-pick slots in dedicated UI containers per the §19 design tokens.
6. Demotion events MUST emit `growth_loop_l9_template_demoted_by_quality_signal` with the appropriate `demotion_reason` enum value AND notify the Seller Team Lead via `marketplace.listing.flagged` (Appendix C — Marketplace-Listing-Domain; cross-applies to template demotion).
7. Sellers MUST have a Seller-Console-visible "Template Performance" surface showing current threshold tier, clone count, decay risk (clone count trending down), and demotion history.

**Failure modes addressed.**

1. **Clone-count race condition between nightly job and incremental updates.** Resolved by nightly job authority semantics: incremental updates are advisory; the nightly job authoritatively recomputes from the GrowthLoopExecution L2 ledger.
2. **Sudden viral clone spike (e.g., a popular template gets shared on LinkedIn) crosses Top Pick threshold faster than featured-slot pipeline can render.** Resolved: featured-slot pipeline polls every 60 seconds; the Sales-Ops dashboard surfaces a `growth_loop_l9_threshold_crossed_pending_render` warning if the cross-to-render latency exceeds 5 minutes.
3. **Adversarial seller forks a popular template to siphon clones.** Resolved: clone attribution (L2) flows to the originating-seller-org_id (lineage-root), not the fork; forking does NOT yield L9 incentive credit unless the fork has its own independent clone_count_30d ≥ threshold from ≥ 5 distinct buyer Orgs.

### 48.2.11 Loop L10: Marketplace Match-Score Teaser {#48.2.11-l10-marketplace-match-score-teaser}

**Mechanism.** Per Summary §3.2 #10, free viewers see qualitative match score labels ("Strong match", "Moderate match", "Weak match") on Marketplace search results and EOI candidate lists; numeric match scores live behind the §21.4.2 `match_score_numeric` paid AI capability (Seller Growth and above per §15 plan gating; cf. §15.3, §15.4). The teaser surfaces enough signal to drive curiosity without giving away the paid value.

**Trigger event.** Buyer user views a Marketplace listing OR an EOI candidate list whose computed Match Score exists per §27.4.

**Acting entity.** Buyer Org user (any role).

**Targeted entity.** The viewer's own Org (the loop drives the viewer's upgrade to a tier that exposes numeric scores) AND, indirectly, the Seller Orgs whose match scores are partially revealed (the teaser markets their relevance).

**Loop instrumentation entity.** GrowthLoopExecution row with `loop_id=marketplace_match_score_teaser`. One row per `(viewing_user_id, palette_or_listing_context_id)` pair per session.

**Telemetry events (Appendix G — new).**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `growth_loop_l10_qualitative_label_rendered` | Marketplace listing OR EOI candidate row renders the qualitative match-score label to a viewer whose plan does not include numeric scores | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `viewing_user_id`, `viewing_org_id`, `viewing_org_plan_tier`, `seller_org_id`, `qualitative_label ∈ {strong_match, moderate_match, weak_match, insufficient_signal}`, `surface ∈ {marketplace_listing_page, eoi_candidate_list, command_palette}` |
| `growth_loop_l10_upgrade_cta_clicked` | Buyer user clicks the "See numeric score" CTA | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `viewing_user_id`, `target_plan_tier ∈ {business_growth, business_scale, business_enterprise}` |
| `growth_loop_l10_upgrade_completed` | Org upgrades to a tier that exposes numeric scores within 30-day attribution window | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `org_id`, `plan_from`, `plan_to`, `time_from_first_label_render_to_upgrade_seconds` |
| `growth_loop_l10_paid_view_after_upgrade` | Same viewing user views the numeric score within 30 days of upgrade | `growth_loop_execution_id`, `viewing_user_id`, `time_from_upgrade_to_paid_view_seconds` |

**Anti-spam controls.**

1. **k-anonymity floor on qualitative labels**: a Marketplace category with < 5 active SellerSoftware rows in the rolling 30-day window does NOT render any qualitative label (the label cohort is too thin to be meaningful AND risks over-disclosing per-seller match-score signal); the surface renders `qualitative_label=insufficient_signal` instead.
2. **Vendor Opt-Out**: if a referenced seller has an active opt-out covering the surface, the row is suppressed entirely (no label rendered); the loop's surface area degrades gracefully.
3. **No-numeric-leakage invariant**: the rendered label MUST be derived from the numeric score via a one-way bucketing function — the numeric value MUST NEVER be exposed in HTML data attributes, JSON properties, or computed CSS; QA test `match_score_label_no_numeric_leakage` asserts this on every render path.
4. **Per-seller-per-viewer label render cap**: at most 50 distinct seller labels per viewer per session — exceeding the cap collapses the surface to a "Showing top 50; upgrade for full visibility" CTA.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Every render of a qualitative label MUST emit `growth_loop_l10_qualitative_label_rendered` within the same render cycle.
2. The label-derivation bucketing function MUST be a stable, deterministic, one-way map: `numeric ∈ [80, 100]` → `strong_match`; `[50, 80)` → `moderate_match`; `[20, 50)` → `weak_match`; `[0, 20)` → `insufficient_signal`. Boundaries are configurable per environment but stable across renders within a deployment.
3. The "See numeric score" CTA MUST render in the same row as the qualitative label AND link to the §34.5 plan upgrade flow with `upgrade_completed.trigger=opus_gated_capability` (since `match_score_numeric` is a Sonnet capability gated to Seller Growth+; for the buyer-side CTA, the upgrade target is Buyer Business Growth+ which exposes the buyer-side numeric Match Score view per §27.4).
4. The full L10 funnel `qualitative_label_rendered → upgrade_cta_clicked → upgrade_completed → paid_view_after_upgrade` MUST be PostHog-queryable per `viewing_org_id` AND aggregable to platform-level conversion-rate dashboards.
5. No-numeric-leakage QA MUST run on every PR touching the Marketplace match-score render path; failure blocks merge.
6. k-anonymity floor enforcement MUST be unit-tested and integration-tested with synthetic category cohorts.

**Failure modes addressed.**

1. **Buyer with browser DevTools opens the page and inspects the DOM for the numeric score.** Resolved by no-numeric-leakage invariant (control #3) — the numeric score is NEVER serialized to the client.
2. **Bucket-boundary instability across deployments causes a seller to see their label oscillate between "Strong" and "Moderate" without a real change in match score.** Resolved by per-environment stable bucketing function + PostHog `qualitative_label_bucket_version` property on every render event for forensic review.
3. **A Seller Org disputes the qualitative label as misleading.** Resolved: §4.5.7 Marketplace Abuse Report kind extension `qualitative_label_dispute` (new enum value; Appendix J `marketplace_abuse_report_kind` — new) lets a seller file a dispute; Ops review per §43.

### 48.2.12 GrowthLoopExecution Entity (Org-Scoped, Cross-Console, Append-Only Audit Unit) {#48.2.12-growthloopexecution-entity}

**Authoring intent.** GrowthLoopExecution is the per-loop-instance audit row that makes every loop fire observable, attributable, queryable, and killable. Without this entity, a junior engineer cannot distinguish "the loop fired and converted" from "the loop fired and decayed" from "the loop never fired because the kill-switch was active." The entity is append-only at the row level (no field deletes; field updates allowed via the explicit lifecycle state machine in §48.2.12.2). Scope: Org-scoped on the acting Org (`acting_org_id`) for primary RBAC; cross-console for surface attribution.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK, immutable | Standard pattern. |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | → Organization (§4.2.1); the **acting Org**; required | Primary RBAC scope; matches `acting_org_id` per Summary §1.4 query-scoping invariant. |
| `console` | Enum | One of `buyer`, `seller`, `cross_console`; required | The console that initiated the loop fire. `cross_console` for L1 (buyer initiates, seller signs up). |
| `loop_id` | Enum | Appendix J `growth_loop_id` (`vendor_invite_creates_account`, `template_clone_attribution`, `selection_report_share_legacy`, `seller_profile_seo`, `free_ai_teaser_to_paid`, `domain_match_auto_suggest_legacy`, `cmd_k_suggestion`, `bid_close_kb_sync_offer`, `template_publish_incentive`, `marketplace_match_score_teaser`); required | Loop identifier; matches §48.2.1 inventory. |
| `acting_user_id` | UUID (FK) | → User (§4.2.3); nullable for platform-orchestrated loops (L5, L9) | The user who initiated the loop fire, if attributable. |
| `target_org_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → Organization (§4.2.1) | The Org targeted by the loop (e.g., the vendor Org for L1 once attributed; the seller Org for L2 attribution). Null for platform-orchestrated loops. |
| `target_entity_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `growth_loop_target_entity_kind` (new: `target_account`, `template`, `seller_org_page`, `software_page`, `category_page`, `comparison_page`, `guide_page`, `market_intelligence_report`, `kb_entry_set`, `marketplace_listing`, `eoi`, `bid_workspace`, `command_palette_context`); required | The entity-kind on which the loop acts. |
| `target_entity_id` | UUID | Nullable | The id of the targeted entity, if applicable. |
| `lifecycle_state` | Enum | Appendix J `growth_loop_execution_lifecycle_state` (new: `initiated`, `in_progress`, `converted`, `decayed`, `killed`, `expired`); required | State machine §48.2.12.2. |
| `lifecycle_state_reason` | Enum | Appendix J `growth_loop_execution_lifecycle_state_reason` (new — full list in Appendix J update below); nullable | Populated on each state transition. |
| `attribution_window_expires_at` | Timestamp | Required for loops with attribution windows (L1, L2, L4, L7, L10); null for loops without | Computed from `created_at` + per-loop window (L1: 60d, L2: 30d, L4: 90d, L7: 30d, L10: 30d). |
| `loop_outcome_value_usd` | Decimal | ≥ 0; null until conversion | The realized value of the loop fire — varies per loop semantics: L1 = `kb_entries_seeded × per-entry value`; L2 = EOI conversion value (TBD via §27 Match-Score-derived weight); L4 = organic-session-to-EOI conversion value; L5 = upgrade plan value (annualized); L7 = EOI conversion value; L9 = featured-placement count × placement weight; L10 = upgrade plan value (annualized). |
| `metadata_json` | JSON | ≤ 8,000 chars per row; loop-specific structure per §48.2.12.3 | Per-loop denormalized fields (e.g., L1: `{vendor_email_domain_hash, kb_bootstrap_ai_operation_id}`; L9: `{template_id, threshold_tier, clone_count_30d_at_cross}`). |
| `kill_switch_ref_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → GrowthLoopKillSwitch (§48.2.12.4) | Set if `lifecycle_state=killed` by an Ops kill-switch; null otherwise. |
| `signal_integrity_flags` | Array[Enum] | Appendix J `growth_loop_signal_integrity_flag` (new: `velocity_anomaly`, `attribution_ambiguity`, `cross_org_harvest`, `low_quality_outcome`, `vendor_opt_out_overlap`, `dmarc_failure_correlation`, `manual_ops_review_pending`); empty array default | Populated by SIM (Summary C.100); multiple flags allowed. |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Required | Standard pattern. |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Required | Standard pattern. |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | → User (§4.2.3); nullable for platform-orchestrated loops | Standard pattern; null for `acting_user_id=null` rows. |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | → User (§4.2.3); nullable | Standard pattern; null for system writes. |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable; soft delete | Standard pattern. |

**Scope isolation.** Org-scoped on `org_id`. Cross-console reads gated by §1.4 query-scoping invariant — a seller-console caller MAY read GrowthLoopExecution rows where `target_org_id = self.org_id` (L1 attribution-target view) AND where `console=seller`; a buyer-console caller MAY read rows where `org_id = self.org_id` AND `console ∈ {buyer, cross_console}`. The `loop_outcome_value_usd` field is Org-readable to `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `billing_admin`, AND `ops_growth_admin` (new role; Appendix J — new); never readable to `member`, `guest`, OR cross-console viewers.

**Required indexes.** `(org_id, loop_id, lifecycle_state)`, `(loop_id, created_at)`, `(target_org_id, loop_id)` (sparse; null `target_org_id` excluded), `(attribution_window_expires_at)` (sparse; null excluded — for nightly attribution-expiry job), `(kill_switch_ref_id)` (sparse).

**Retention.** Org-life + 7 years per platform-integrity + financial-audit policy (rows underlie loop-conversion attribution and inform pricing/discount decisions for Sales). Not subject to right-to-erasure under the applicable §6.8.5 retained-row classes; identity fields (`acting_user_id`, `created_by`) pseudonymized on DSAR within the §6.8.6 fulfillment window.

**Authoring extensions flagged.** GrowthLoopExecution is a wholly new entity — flagged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` → Authored Extensions. The loop-specific metadata structure in `metadata_json` is per-loop and schema-validated server-side per §48.2.12.3 catalogue.

#### 48.2.12.1 Per-Loop GrowthLoopExecution Row Lifecycle

| Loop | Created When | Initiated → In_Progress | In_Progress → Converted | In_Progress → Decayed | In_Progress → Expired |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| L1 | Target Account write | Magic-link click recorded | Vendor signs up + first bid + `kb_bootstrap` accepted | Signup occurs > 60d after invite (no longer credited) | 60d window passes without signup |
| L2 | Template clone | Attribution badge first rendered | EOI emitted to originating seller within 30d | `lineage_depth > 5` cap hit OR Vendor Opt-Out applied | 30d EOI-attribution window passes |
| L3 | n/a (retired) | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| L4 | Page publish | First organic session attributed | EOI OR signup attributed within 90d | `growth_loop_l4_page_seo_quality_warning` AND no traffic for 90d | 90d session-attribution window passes |
| L5 | First AIOperation per `(org_id, capability_id)` | `quantity_remaining ≤ 3` (threshold warning) | Upgrade with `upgrade_completed.trigger=ai_budget_exhaustion` within 30d of exhaustion | Counter exhausted, no upgrade in 30d, Org churns | 365d cold-loop closure |
| L6 | n/a (retired) | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| L7 | Marketplace-eligible palette open | Suggestions returned | EOI to suggested seller within 30d | All suggestions dismissed in-session | 30d EOI-attribution window passes |
| L8 | BidWorkspace close | CTA rendered | KB sync AIOperation completes (`acceptance_rate ≥ 0.6`) | CTA dismissed OR sync fails | 30d CTA-render TTL passes |
| L9 | Template `clone_count_30d` ≥ trending threshold | Featured placement first rendered | Sustained ≥ trending tier for 30d | `clone_count_30d` decays below trending OR demoted by quality signal | n/a (no fixed expiry; tracked indefinitely until decay) |
| L10 | First qualitative label render in session | Upgrade CTA clicked | Upgrade completed within 30d AND paid view of numeric score within 30d post-upgrade | Upgrade CTA dismissed in-session | 30d CTA-attribution window passes |

#### 48.2.12.2 GrowthLoopExecution Lifecycle State Machine

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `initiated` | `in_progress` | Loop's per-loop "initiated→in_progress" event (§48.2.12.1) | Targeting validated; SIM not actively flagged | Standard happy-path advance. |
| `initiated` | `killed` | Ops Console kill-switch publish for `loop_id` | `kill_switch_ref_id` set; `lifecycle_state_reason=ops_kill_switch_active` | Ops can preemptively kill new fires of a loop. |
| `in_progress` | `converted` | Loop's per-loop "in_progress→converted" event (§48.2.12.1) | Conversion event arrives within attribution window; SIM does not flag | `loop_outcome_value_usd` populated from per-loop value model. |
| `in_progress` | `decayed` | Loop's per-loop "in_progress→decayed" event (§48.2.12.1) | Conversion does not arrive within attribution window OR loop-specific decay condition | `lifecycle_state_reason ∈ {window_expired, target_opted_out, lineage_capped, quality_floor_failed, dismissed_by_target}` |
| `in_progress` | `killed` | Ops Console kill-switch publish OR SIM auto-kill | SIM flag with severity `critical` OR Ops manual action | `kill_switch_ref_id` set; `lifecycle_state_reason=ops_kill_switch_active` OR `sim_auto_kill_critical` |
| `in_progress` | `expired` | `attribution_window_expires_at` reached | Conversion did not arrive AND decay did not trigger | Distinct from `decayed` to support Sales-Ops triage of "stale loops" vs "actively-decayed loops." |
| `converted` | (terminal) | n/a | n/a | Append-only post-conversion. |
| `decayed` | (terminal) | n/a | n/a | Append-only post-decay. |
| `killed` | (terminal) | n/a | n/a | Append-only post-kill. |
| `expired` | (terminal) | n/a | n/a | Append-only post-expiry. |

**Invariants.**

1. No state may transition to `initiated` from any other state — `initiated` is the entry state.
2. Terminal states (`converted`, `decayed`, `killed`, `expired`) MAY NOT transition further; subsequent loop fires create new GrowthLoopExecution rows.
3. `kill_switch_ref_id` MUST be non-null IFF `lifecycle_state=killed`.
4. `loop_outcome_value_usd` MUST be non-null IFF `lifecycle_state=converted`.
