#### 48.2.12.4 GrowthLoopKillSwitch Entity (Platform-Scoped, Ops-Managed)

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK, immutable | Standard. |
| `loop_id` | Enum | Appendix J `growth_loop_id`; required | One kill-switch row per `loop_id`; partial-uniqueness enforced via `(loop_id) WHERE active=true`. |
| `active` | Boolean | Required | True = loop is currently disabled platform-wide. |
| `scope` | Enum | Appendix J `growth_loop_kill_switch_scope` (new: `platform`, `org`, `capability`, `region`); required | Granularity. |
| `scope_ref_type` | Enum | Appendix J `growth_loop_kill_switch_scope_ref_type` (new: `null`, `org`, `capability_registry_entry`, `data_residency_region`); required | Type of `scope_ref_id`. |
| `scope_ref_id` | UUID | Nullable when `scope=platform`; required otherwise | The id of the scoped target. |
| `reason_code` | Enum | Appendix J `growth_loop_kill_switch_reason_code` (new: `sim_auto_kill_critical`, `sim_auto_kill_warning`, `ops_manual_action`, `legal_request`, `compliance_review`, `dependency_outage`, `experiment_rollback`); required | Why the kill-switch was activated. |
| `reason_note` | Text | ≤ 2,000 chars; required | Free-text Ops note. |
| `activated_at` | Timestamp | Required | When activated. |
| `deactivated_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When the kill-switch was lifted; null while active. |
| `activated_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | → User (§4.2.3); required | Must hold `ops_growth_admin` OR `ops_security_admin` role. |
| `deactivated_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | → User (§4.2.3); nullable | Must hold same roles as activated_by. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | Standard | Standard | Standard pattern. |

**Scope isolation.** Platform-scoped; Ops-managed; not customer-readable. Audit log entry written on every state transition per §4.6.1 Audit Event.

**Publish-path semantics.** Kill-switch state changes propagate via the existing §22.16.5 feature-flag publish path; worst-case orchestrator-cache invalidation latency is 60 seconds. New loop fires after activation are killed at `lifecycle_state=initiated → killed`; in-progress loop fires are killed at the next state-transition checkpoint per loop semantics.

**Dependency-outage automated activation (Authored Extension #39; §50 Phase 6 Verification Remediation 2026-04-21).** When a named upstream dependency provider reports unhealthy status for ≥ 90 seconds (defined as 3 consecutive 30-s health-check failures emitted by the §42.6 Dependency Health Probe subsystem), a kill-switch MAY auto-activate against the affected loops with `reason_code='dependency_outage'`. Automated-activation contract:

1. **Provider catalog.** The `reason_dependency_name` field (new, nullable, FK Appendix J enum `growth_loop_kill_switch_dependency_provider` — new: `loops_so`, `firecrawl`, `anthropic`, `perplexity`, `stripe`, `workos`, `convex`, `posthog`, `zendesk`) identifies the outage source. If a pre-existing `third_party_dependency_provider` enum covers these values, `growth_loop_kill_switch_dependency_provider` is a reference-only registration (no duplicate enum). The `reason_started_at` field (new, nullable timestamp) captures the first unhealthy probe observation.
2. **Hysteresis.** Activation requires 3 consecutive unhealthy 30-s probes (90 s total); deactivation requires 10 consecutive healthy 30-s probes (300 s total) to prevent flap-driven oscillation. Property-test `growth_loop_kill_switch_dependency_hysteresis_property` asserts across 5,000 simulated health signal streams.
3. **Auto-emitted events.** Activation emits webhook event `growth_loop_kill_switch.dependency_auto_activated` (Appendix C — new) and PostHog event `growth_loop_kill_switch_dependency_auto_activated` (Appendix G — new); deactivation emits `growth_loop_kill_switch.dependency_auto_deactivated` and `growth_loop_kill_switch_dependency_auto_deactivated`. Both events carry `reason_dependency_name`, `reason_started_at`, `activated_by_user_id = SYSTEM_AUTO` (Ops-role reserved system actor).
4. **Operator override-to-keep-enabled.** Operator override of an auto-activated kill-switch is prohibited unless the operator holds `ops_admin` role (NOT specialized sub-roles without `ops_admin` inheritance per §50.3.2; non-inheriting roles including `ops_fraud_analyst`, `ops_pricing_admin`, `ops_template_reviewer`, `ops_support_agent`, `ops_finance`, `ops_taxonomy_admin` are REJECTED with HTTP 403 `growth_loop_kill_switch_dependency_override_requires_ops_admin` (Appendix I — new)). Override requires the operator to populate `override_justification_category` (new, nullable, FK Appendix J enum `growth_loop_kill_switch_override_justification_category` — new: `dependency_degraded_but_usable`, `partial_failover_active`) plus a free-text `override_note` (≤ 2,000 chars). Override carries a 4-hour max-duration ceiling — on expiry, the kill-switch auto-re-activates and the operator must re-consent to continue the override.
5. **Override escalation.** Three or more consecutive overrides by any `ops_admin` on the same `reason_dependency_name` within a 24-hour window escalates the override to quorum-gated (two distinct `ops_admin` signers required). Property-test `growth_loop_kill_switch_override_escalation_property` asserts. Escalations emit `growth_loop_kill_switch.dependency_override_escalated` webhook and page `ops_security_admin`.
6. **Every override emits** PostHog event `growth_loop_kill_switch_dependency_override` and pages `ops_security_admin` within 60 s via PagerDuty.
7. **Field additions (Authored Extension #39).** Five new fields on `GrowthLoopKillSwitch`: `reason_dependency_name` (nullable, FK enum), `reason_started_at` (nullable timestamp), `override_justification_category` (nullable, FK enum), `override_applied_at` (nullable timestamp), `override_applied_by_ops_session_id` (nullable FK §4.6.3 OpsSession). Data-team schema + Security + Engineering sign-off per Authored Extension #39. Migration path: legacy rows default all five fields to NULL; CI gate `growth_loop_kill_switch_dependency_outage_field_population_post_cutover` asserts any row with `reason_code='dependency_outage'` created after 2026-04-21 carries populated `reason_dependency_name` + `reason_started_at`.

### 48.2.13 Cross-Loop Acceptance Criteria {#48.2.13-cross-loop-acceptance-criteria}

These criteria apply to all 8 active loops collectively (L3 and L6 retired):

1. Every loop fire MUST create exactly one GrowthLoopExecution row within 5 seconds of the loop's trigger event.
2. Every loop's lifecycle MUST conform to §48.2.12.2 state machine; invalid transitions raise an `analytics_invariant_violation` PagerDuty alert.
3. Every loop's telemetry events MUST carry the `growth_loop_execution_id` property; orphan events (no matching row) flag the row's nightly audit job.
4. Every loop MUST be killable via the §48.2.12.4 GrowthLoopKillSwitch within 60 seconds of Ops Console publish.
5. Every loop's funnel MUST be PostHog-Insights-Funnels queryable end-to-end keyed by `growth_loop_execution_id`, and the full funnel MUST resolve at p95 ≤ 30 seconds across the full execution-row population.
6. Every loop MUST have at least one §48.3.3 dashboard surface in the Ops Growth Console.
7. Cross-loop attribution overlap (e.g., a Buyer Org reached via L4 organic SEO who also clones a template via L2 in the same session) MUST be resolved deterministically by first-touch attribution (the loop whose `growth_loop_execution_id` was created first wins primary attribution; secondary attributions are recorded in `metadata_json.cross_loop_attribution[]` array; see §48.2.12.3 implicit extension).
8. Retired loops (L3, L6) MUST NOT create GrowthLoopExecution rows; any attempt is rejected at the API layer with HTTP 410 `growth_loop_retired` (Appendix I — new).
9. Every loop's anti-spam controls MUST be unit-testable; CI gates merge if any control's unit test is missing or skipped.
10. Every loop's per-loop metadata_json MUST validate against the §48.2.12.3 schema; violations return HTTP 422 from the row-write endpoint AND emit `growth_loop_execution_metadata_schema_violation` (Appendix G — new) for forensic review.

## 48.3 Network Effects {#48.3-network-effects}

**Authoring intent.** Network effects are the qualitative claim that Sourcera's value compounds with usage. §48.3 makes this claim measurable: §48.3.1 frames the qualitative claim per-effect; §48.3.2 names the specific quantitative signal that proves (or disproves) each effect; §48.3.3 specifies the dashboard surfaces that operationalize the signals for Sales-Ops, Growth, and Finance.

### 48.3.1 Qualitative Framing {#48.3.1-qualitative-framing}

Per Summary §3.4, Sourcera asserts six compounding effects:

1. **Sellers compound sellers.** More sellers → more templates (L9, L2) → faster buyer setup → more bids → more KB content (L8) → sellers stay (lower churn).
2. **Buyers compound buyers.** More buyers → more aggregate signals (M12, M13) → stronger Marketplace value for sellers → more seller investment in Sourcera presence → more Marketplace content (L4) for buyers.
3. **Data compounds both sides.** More evaluations → richer Org Intelligence (M8) → stronger MarketIntelligenceReport (M12) → more accurate HeatMapCell (M13) → better CategoryPage (M9, L4 amplifier).
4. **SEO compounds everything.** M9 + M10 + M11 + M12 + M13 build a defensible organic-search moat per category (L4 amplifier). First-mover advantage in each category is disproportionate.
5. **Certificates and shares compound trust.** M3 (Evaluation Certificate Badge) + M14 (Seller Bid Success Share) + M2 (Selection Report Public Link) operate as distributed, zero-marginal-cost marketing artifacts.
6. **Referrals compound quality.** M16 (Buyer Referral Credit) skews acquisition toward high-intent channels; peer-vouched signups activate faster.

**Signal integrity.** Every signal computation includes a `signal_freshness_seconds_max`, a `data_completeness_pct`, and a `k_anonymity_floor_satisfied` Boolean. Dashboards refuse to render any signal whose `k_anonymity_floor_satisfied=false` AND emit `growth_signal_k_anonymity_floor_violation` (Appendix G — new) for SIM review.

### 48.3.3 Dashboards {#48.3.3-dashboards}

Three dashboard surfaces in the Ops Growth Console (new sub-surface of the §43 Admin Dashboard):

1. **Growth Loop Operations Dashboard** — per-loop lifecycle funnel, kill-switch state, SIM flag rate, conversion-rate trends, attribution-window-expiry alert. Read access: `ops_growth_admin` (new), `ops_finance_admin`, `ops_security_admin`.
2. **Network Effects Dashboard** — six-effect signal trend lines per §48.3.2, with per-category drill-down for effects #1, #2, #3, #4. Read access: `ops_growth_admin`, `ops_finance_admin` *(V13 D-48.3-008 remediation 2026-05-12 — added because §48.3.5 S2 KB → EOI → Revenue and S6 Pro-Trial → Paid are revenue-leading indicators; Marketing / Finance roll-ups depend on this dashboard; the prior asymmetry against the Growth Loop Operations Dashboard (which already granted `ops_finance_admin`) was unjustified)*, `ops_security_admin` *(read-only, audit purposes)*, founder leadership.
3. **Anti-Spam & SIM Dashboard** — per-control fire rate, kill-switch eligibility flags, SIM anomaly stream, false-positive feedback loop. Read access: `ops_security_admin`, `ops_growth_admin`.

**Dashboard data freshness.** Real-time tiles (loop fire rates, SIM flag stream) refresh every 60 seconds via PostHog Live Insights; nightly tiles (network-effect signal curves, retention curves) refresh once per 24h via Snowflake; hourly tiles (per-loop conversion rates) refresh every 60 minutes. Each tile shows its source and timestamp.

### 48.3.4 Acceptance Criteria {#48.3.4-acceptance-criteria}

1. All twelve §48.3.2 signals MUST be computed nightly AND surfaced in the §48.3.3 Network Effects Dashboard within 25 hours of source-data write.
2. Each signal computation MUST refuse to render below k-anonymity floor AND emit `growth_signal_k_anonymity_floor_violation`.
3. Per-loop conversion-rate dashboards MUST be queryable per loop, per Org, per category, AND per cohort (signup month).
4. Founders MUST have a "Sourcera Network-Effects Health" exec-roll-up surface combining six top-line signals (`m9_category_page_session_growth_30d`, `m12_signal_density_per_category_per_quarter`, `m16_referral_org_retention_rate_90d`, `seller_template_clone_velocity_30d`, total `growth_loop_l5_upgrade_completed_30d`, total `growth_loop_l4_organic_to_signup_30d`); refresh hourly.
5. SIM flag rate MUST be sub-1-minute-fresh on the Anti-Spam Dashboard.
6. Dashboard access MUST be RBAC-gated per §48.3.3 role list; non-permitted access returns 403 AND audit-logs the attempted access per §4.6.1.

### 48.3.5 Seller-Side Compounding Network Effects (Inventory & Instrumentation) {#48.3.5-seller-side-compounding-network-effects}

**Authoring intent.** §48.3.5 inventories the seven seller-side compounding loops named in Summary §3.4 ("Seller-Side Network Effects (Compounding Loops)") and C.138 (Seller-Side Network Effects Inventory). Every loop operates regardless of plan tier — Free sellers contribute to every loop and pricing gates sit downstream — so the section's primary instrumentation purpose is to (a) make the per-loop contribution measurable across paid and free cohorts and (b) make the cross-loop reinforcement cycle ("Buyer invite → Forced vendor signup → Hero moment → Bid submitted → KB compounds → Marketplace inventory grows → SEO compounds → Inbound buyer demand grows → More buyer invites") observable as a single end-to-end funnel. Each loop receives mechanism, primary §4 entity refs, primary telemetry events, the measurable signal that proves (or disproves) its contribution, the dashboard tile, and the k-anonymity floor.

**Source authority.** Summary §3.4 (Network Effects + Seller-Side Compounding Loops); C.138 (Seller-Side Network Effects Inventory — appendix); the existing §48.3.1–§48.3.4 framing (six platform-level effects). The seven seller-side loops EXTEND §48.3.1's six effects; they do not replace them. §48.3.1 frames effects at the platform level (sellers compound sellers, buyers compound buyers, etc.); §48.3.5 is the seller-side decomposition of the "sellers compound sellers" and "data compounds both sides" effects into the actual seven loops that produce the compounding.

**Cross-Reference to Existing Six Platform Effects (§48.3.1).** The seven seller-side loops below MAP into the six platform effects as follows: Loops S1, S2, S5, S6 → Platform Effect #1 (sellers compound sellers); Loop S4 → Platform Effect #4 (SEO compounds everything); Loops S2, S3 → Platform Effect #3 (data compounds both sides); Loop S7 → Platform Effects #1 + #4 (sellers compound sellers + SEO). The platform-level signals at §48.3.2 are the rolled-up versions; the loop-level signals here are the disaggregated versions.

**S4 Gartner / G2 Baseline Refresh Cadence (Authored Extension — Ops Growth Workflow).** The S4 "per-category SEO moat tile shows organic-traffic share vs. Gartner / G2 baseline (manual-input baseline)" table cell above creates a staleness risk: a stale baseline silently degrades the moat-vs-competition comparison into a nostalgic view. To prevent silent decay, the Gartner and G2 baseline inputs are refreshed on a **mandatory quarterly cadence** (every 90 calendar days from the last refresh timestamp). Cadence enforcement: (a) each baseline row carries a `baseline_last_refreshed_at` timestamp; (b) a nightly invariant check pages `ops_growth_admin` with P3 alert `s4_baseline_staleness_warning` at 75-day staleness, P2 alert `s4_baseline_staleness_breach` at 90-day staleness, and freezes the S4 moat tile rendering with a *"Baseline refreshed more than 90 days ago"* visual banner at 105-day staleness; (c) refresh requires manual entry from Ops Growth, sourced from the latest Gartner category share-of-voice report and the latest G2 Grid position per category, with a §47 Governance sign-off noted on each entry (`ops_growth_admin` actor + date + source-report URL / G2 grid snapshot URL); (d) all prior baseline values retain their entry rows for trend visualization — baselines are append-only, never overwritten. Events: `s4_baseline_refreshed {category_id, source_kind ∈ {gartner, g2}, refreshed_by, prior_value, new_value, source_document_hash}` (Appendix G — new); `s4_baseline_staleness_warning`; `s4_baseline_staleness_breach`. Acceptance: the Ops Growth Dashboard MUST render a per-category baseline-staleness tile showing days-since-last-refresh for every tracked category with color-coded bands (green < 75d, amber 75–90d, red > 90d). Cadence failure is a Product-VP-escalation per §47 Governance.

**Reinforcing-Loop Closure (Summary §3.4 diagram).** The seven loops compose into the canonical reinforcement cycle: `Buyer invite → Forced vendor signup (M1/M5/M15/M17) → Hero moment (S1 Inventory) → Bid submitted (S3 Calibration) → KB compounds (S2 KB→Match→EOI) → Marketplace inventory grows (S1 + S7 Templates) → SEO compounds (S4 Profile SEO) → Inbound buyer demand grows → More buyer invites`. Each step has a measurable signal in §48.3.5; the closed loop is observable end-to-end as a multi-month cohort journey on the Network Effects Dashboard (Cycle-Time-Per-Loop tile, refreshed weekly).

**Reinforcement-Cycle Time Signal.** `seller_side_reinforcement_cycle_p50_days` = median elapsed time from a Buyer Org sending its first vendor invite to that buyer Org receiving an inbound EOI from a different invited vendor (Authored Extension — operational measurement design). Target: ≤ 90 days at steady state. Pages `ops_growth_admin` if degraded > 25% MoM. Used to detect "is the flywheel actually spinning?" at the platform level.

**Free-Tier Contribution Audit.** A per-loop column above ("Free-Tier Contribution?") asserts that **every loop except S6 (Pro Trial)** receives Free-tier contribution. The "Pricing gives sellers access to outbound tools; Marketplace integrity defines the acceptable use floor" thesis (Summary §3.5) is operationalized here: Free sellers are first-class participants in S1, S2, S3, S4, S5 (first import), S7. Any future product-policy proposal that would suppress Free-tier contribution to any of these loops MUST go through Ops Council review per the §47 Governance gate, with explicit network-effect-impact analysis.

**Acceptance Criteria (§48.3.5 specific; complement §48.3.4).**

7. Each of the seven seller-side loops MUST surface its primary signal as a §48.3.3 Network Effects Dashboard tile within 24 hours of the source-data write.
8. Each loop's primary telemetry event MUST be PostHog-Insights-Funnels queryable end-to-end keyed by `seller_org_id`; the full funnel for each loop MUST resolve at p95 ≤ 30 seconds across the full active-Seller-Org population.
9. Free-tier contribution metrics for loops S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S7 MUST be computable separately from paid-tier contribution metrics; per-tier contribution percentages are surfaced on each loop's dashboard tile (e.g., "S2 KB → Match → EOI: Free 47% / Starter 32% / Growth 15% / Scale 6%").
10. The closed reinforcement-cycle metric (`seller_side_reinforcement_cycle_p50_days`) MUST be computed weekly AND surfaced on the founders' "Sourcera Network-Effects Health" exec roll-up (per §48.3.4 AC 4), AND degradation > 25% MoM MUST raise a §42 P2 to `ops_growth_admin`.
11. Pro Trial Seat conversion (Loop S6) MUST be benchmarked side-by-side against cold-start Free → Starter conversion (Indicator #1 in §48.1.6) on a single dashboard tile; the side-by-side comparison is the validation of the M17 loop's existence.
12. k-anonymity floors per loop MUST be enforced at the dashboard render path; below-floor signals MUST refuse to render AND emit `growth_signal_k_anonymity_floor_violation` per §48.4.7.

### 48.3.8 Third-Party-Outage Render Behavior {#48.3.8-third-party-outage-render-behavior}

*(V13 D-48.3-009 remediation 2026-05-12.)*

Network-effect dashboards depend on three third-party pipelines: PostHog (Live Insights / real-time queries), Snowflake (nightly reverse-ETL for rollups), Datadog (per-tile metric rendering). Each carries an authored render-during-outage contract.

| Pipeline | Outage Behavior | UI Render |
|---|---|---|
| **PostHog Live Insights outage** (real-time tile freshness > 60s) | Tile renders the last-known value with a "Stale (last refreshed Nh ago)" banner; emits `growth_signal_freshness_breach {pipeline=posthog, tile_id, last_refresh_at, staleness_seconds}` (Appendix G — new); pages `ops_growth_admin` if staleness > 5 minutes | Last-known value + yellow "Stale" banner |
| **Snowflake reverse-ETL outage** (> 24h since last snapshot) | Daily rollup tiles render the last-known value; "Stale (rollup pending)" banner; emits `growth_signal_freshness_breach {pipeline=snowflake, ...}`; pages on-call if > 48h | Last-known value + yellow banner |
| **Datadog metrics outage** (per-tile metric query 5xx) | Tile renders empty state: "Data pipeline temporarily unavailable — refresh"; auto-retry every 30 seconds; pages if > 15 minutes | Empty-state placeholder with retry CTA |
| **All three simultaneous** | Full dashboard renders gray-out + banner "Dashboard temporarily unavailable — Ops investigating"; emits `growth_signal_freshness_breach {pipeline=composite, ...}`; pages SEV-2 | Gray-out + SEV-2 banner |

CI gate `network_effects_dashboard_outage_render_contract` (§M.5 — new) asserts all four render paths are wired.

### 48.3.9 Residency Partitioning {#48.3.9-residency-partitioning}

*(V13 D-48.3-010 remediation 2026-05-12.)*

Network-effect signal aggregation respects §41 / §42.4.1 / §42.4.2 data-residency boundaries. PostHog routes events per Seller / Buyer Org `residency_region`; Snowflake reverse-ETL partitions by residency; cross-region rollups are computed inside the regional partition and aggregated to a global view ONLY at the Sourcera-internal Ops dashboard layer (never customer-facing). EU-residency Orgs' signal contributions are not rendered on a US-residency Ops-admin's dashboard except via the §6.8.4.4 Marketplace-Aggregate Cascade Trigger contract (k-anon-floor-protected; subject-erasure-cascaded). CI gate `network_effects_residency_partition_canonical_consumer` (§M.5 — new) asserts the partition contract is implemented at the PostHog routing layer + Snowflake partition layer + dashboard render layer; pack assignment M21.3.

## 48.4 Anti-Spam & Abuse Controls (Global) {#48.4-anti-spam-and-abuse-controls-global}

**Authoring intent.** §48.4 catalogues every cross-loop, cross-mechanic anti-spam control. Each control has (a) a clear scope, (b) a fire-rate budget, (c) a kill-switch eligibility, (d) an Appendix G PostHog event, and (e) acceptance criteria. The Signal Integrity Monitor (§48.4.10, Summary C.100) is the cross-cutting Ops surface that aggregates control fires and triggers escalations; it is documented in summary form here and elsewhere (Summary C.100, §43, §4.3.16, §4.3.17).

### 48.4.1 Email Throttling {#48.4.1-email-throttling}

**Scope.** Every loop and mechanic that emits email — primarily L1 (vendor invites), M1 (stakeholder invites), M5 (buyer-pull vendor invites), M16 (referral invites), M17 (Pro Trial Seat invites), and the §41.2 Email Type Catalog at large.

**Controls.**

1. Per-Org outbound email-rate cap: 1,000 emails/Org/24h (Free tier), 5,000/24h (Starter), 10,000/24h (Growth), 25,000/24h (Scale), 100,000/24h (Enterprise) — enforced at the Loops.so adapter layer (§41.1).
2. Per-recipient inbound dedup: at most 1 email per `(sending_org_id, recipient_email_address, email_kind)` per 24h; duplicates are coalesced into the existing send (no separate emission).
3. Per-Loops.so account total cap: 50K emails/24h aggregate across all Orgs (Loops.so plan ceiling); breaching the cap fails open with email queueing AND emits `email_loops_so_account_cap_breach_imminent` (Appendix G — new) at 80%.

**Kill-switch.** Ops MAY suspend all outbound email for a specific Org via §48.2.12.4 GrowthLoopKillSwitch with `scope=org` AND `loop_id=vendor_invite_creates_account` (which the email-emitter respects as a global Org-level signal); broader email kill is via Loops.so-account-level pause.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Per-Org email-rate caps MUST be enforced at the Loops.so adapter; breaches return HTTP 429 to the calling code AND queue the email with a `Retry-After`.
2. Per-recipient dedup MUST coalesce duplicates within the 24h window; exact-duplicate body is detected via `email_payload_hash`.
3. The Loops.so account-level cap MUST emit a §42 P2 alert at 80% utilization AND a P1 at 95%.

### 48.4.2 DMARC/SPF Reputation {#48.4.2-dmarc-spf-reputation}

**Scope.** Every Org whose `org_email_domain` is used as a `From:` address on outbound L1 / M5 / M16 / M17 invitations (i.e., when Sourcera sends "on behalf of" the Org per §41.3 Email Compliance).

**Controls.**

1. Nightly DMARC alignment scan against the rolling 7-day Loops.so-reported delivery telemetry; an Org whose `dmarc_alignment_pass_rate < 0.85` is flagged AND its outbound L1 / M5 / M16 / M17 invitations are routed to a deferred-send queue pending Ops review.
2. SPF record validation at Org email-domain registration (one-time at signup; re-checked monthly); invalid SPF blocks "send-on-behalf-of" until remediated.
3. DKIM signing via Sourcera's signing keys for all outbound (always); DKIM signing failures emit `email_dkim_signing_failed` (Appendix G — new) and quarantine the message.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. DMARC alignment rate computation MUST be a documented function with seed inputs from Loops.so delivery telemetry; QA-tested with synthetic delivery records.
2. Deferred-send queue MUST surface in the Ops Growth Dashboard (§48.3.3) with a queue-depth metric AND a per-Org breakdown.
3. SPF and DKIM remediation flows MUST surface in the Org Settings → Domain Verification surface (§36.2) with clear remediation guidance and Loops.so dashboard link.

### 48.4.3 Shared-Use Domain Detection {#48.4.3-shared-use-domain-detection}

**Scope.** Every L1, M5, M16, M17 target email — the `vendor_email_domain` (or `recipient_email_domain` for M16) is matched against the shared-use-domain registry.

**Controls.**

1. Maintained shared-use-domain registry (Ops-managed; covers `gmail.com`, `outlook.com`, `yahoo.com`, `hotmail.com`, `aol.com`, `proton.me`, `icloud.com`, `qq.com`, `163.com`, `inbox.com`, `mail.com`, `gmx.com`, `tutanota.com`, etc.; ~250 entries at v7.0.0 seed; expandable per §43 Ops tooling).
2. Domains in the registry are rejected at L1 / M5 Target Account write with HTTP 422 `growth_loop_l1_invite_shared_use_domain_rejected` (Appendix I — new); for M16 referrals, the referee email is allowed (since referrals are personal, not vendor) but emits `growth_loop_referral_shared_use_domain_warn` (Appendix G — new) for SIM correlation.
3. New shared-use-domain candidates are auto-detected by Ops-Console daemon: any domain with > 100 Sourcera Orgs claiming it as `org_email_domain` is flagged for Ops review.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Registry MUST be queryable as a sub-100-ms hash lookup at L1 / M5 / M16 / M17 trigger time.
2. Auto-detection of new shared-use-domain candidates MUST run nightly AND surface candidates in the Ops Growth Dashboard.
3. Adding a new shared-use-domain MUST require `ops_security_admin` approval AND emit `shared_use_domain_registry_updated` (Appendix G — new).

### 48.4.4 Content Validators {#48.4.4-content-validators}

**Scope.** Every customer-authored content surface that flows to a public Marketplace surface OR an outbound email body — including SellerOrgPage descriptions (§4.4.10), SoftwarePage descriptions (§4.4.11), CategoryPage editorial content (§4.4.12), GuidePage (§4.4.13), ComparisonPage (§4.4.14), Template descriptions (§19), L1 / M5 invitation custom messages, M16 referral custom messages.

**Controls.**

1. **XSS sanitizer**: stripped of `<script>`, `<iframe>`, `<object>`, `<embed>`, on-event-attribute handlers; passed through DOMPurify-equivalent server-side.
2. **Structured-data injection guard**: fields that emit Schema.org payloads validate that no embedded JSON-LD can hijack the rendered structured data.
3. **PII detector**: §6.8 PII redaction pipeline runs in dry-run mode on Marketplace-bound content; PII detected blocks publish with `content_validator_pii_detected` (Appendix G — new) AND surfaces a remediation banner.
4. **Profanity / hate-speech classifier**: lightweight Haiku-tier classifier (per §21.4.1) on customer-authored Marketplace surfaces; flagged content blocks publish.
5. **Prompt-injection scanner** (§22.16.7 KB injection scanner extension): customer-authored content destined for downstream LLM consumption (e.g., Template descriptions cloned into KBEntry context) is scanned; flagged content is held for review.
6. **Off-topic spam classifier**: a content-classifier (Sonnet-tier) checks that customer-authored Marketplace content is on-topic relative to the surface (e.g., a SoftwarePage description must describe the software, not a different product) — off-topic content blocks publish.

**Kill-switch.** Ops MAY disable any individual validator via Ops Console; disabling logs and emits `content_validator_disabled {validator_name, reason, ops_actor}` (Appendix G — new).

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Every public-bound customer-authored content write MUST pass all six validators before publish; failure surfaces a per-validator remediation message.
2. Validators MUST run with p95 latency ≤ 1 second per write; slower validators (e.g., Sonnet off-topic classifier) run async with a `pending_validation` state.
3. Validator-flagged content MUST surface in the Ops Anti-Spam Dashboard (§48.3.3) with per-validator drill-down.

### 48.4.5 Template Spam ML Classifier {#48.4.5-template-spam-ml-classifier}

**Scope.** Every seller-authored template at publish-time AND nightly across already-published templates per L9 (§48.2.10).

**Controls.**

1. Sonnet-tier classifier trained on labeled spam/non-spam template corpus (per Summary C.96 Seller Template Review Rubric); outputs `spam_probability ∈ [0, 1]` AND a labeled rationale.
2. Templates with `spam_probability ≥ 0.85` are blocked at publish AND moved to `template_review_status=spam_blocked` (new enum value; Appendix J — new) with a Seller-visible remediation surface.
3. Templates with `spam_probability ∈ [0.65, 0.85)` are held for human review by a `template_reviewer` (§5.2 Ops role; existing).
4. Templates with `spam_probability < 0.65` are auto-published per §19 publish flow.
5. Nightly re-classification: as the classifier model is retrained, already-published templates are re-scored; templates whose new score crosses ≥ 0.85 are demoted via L9 mechanism AND emit `template_demoted_by_classifier_revision` (Appendix G — new).

**Kill-switch.** Ops MAY disable the classifier (e.g., for false-positive remediation rolling out) via Ops Console.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Classifier inference MUST complete with p95 latency ≤ 5 seconds per template at publish.
2. Classifier MUST emit `template_spam_classifier_decision {template_id, spam_probability, decision, model_version}` (Appendix G — new) on every inference.
3. Sellers blocked at `spam_blocked` MUST receive a remediation notification (`template_spam_blocked` — Appendix C extension below) with a clear path to dispute via §43 Ops support tooling.
4. Classifier model version MUST be versioned in Appendix J `template_spam_classifier_model_version` (new) with retraining cadence (target: monthly).

### 48.4.6 Referral Fraud Controls {#48.4.6-referral-fraud-controls}

**Scope.** §4.3.16 Buyer Referral entity AND §4.3.17 Pro Trial Seat Grant entity (M16, M17). Cross-applies to L5 cross-Org Free-Allowance harvest detection (§48.2.6 control #3).

**Controls.**

1. **Same-domain detection**: referrer Org and referee Org share the same `org_email_domain` (excluding shared-use-domains) → flag `same_domain` per Appendix J `referral_fraud_signal` (existing).
2. **Same-payment-method detection**: referrer and referee Orgs add identical Stripe payment method (same `payment_method_fingerprint`) → flag `same_payment_method` (existing).
3. **Same-IP-range detection**: ≥ 80% of session IPs for both Orgs in the past 30 days fall within the same `/24` subnet → flag `same_ip_range` (existing).
4. **Bootstrapping pattern detection**: referrer Org's referee Orgs share a graph structure consistent with single-actor Org creation (e.g., common admin user across Orgs OR common SSO upstream identity) → flag `bootstrapping_pattern` (existing).
5. **Velocity spike detection**: referrer Org issues > 5 successful referrals in any 24-hour window → flag `velocity_spike` (existing).
6. **Activity-threshold gating**: referee Org must reach a minimum-activity threshold (e.g., create 1 Workspace AND complete first AIOperation OR submit first bid) before the referral converts from `signed_up` to `activated` (§4.3.16 state machine, existing).
7. **Cross-Org Free-Allowance harvest detection** (§48.2.6 #3 dual): orgs detected via #1, #2, #3 above are additionally flagged with `cross_org_free_allowance_harvest_detected` (Appendix G — new) to suppress L5 Free Allowances per §48.2.6 control #3.

**Kill-switch.** Ops MAY block all M16 referral credits for a specific Org via Ops Console.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. All seven signals MUST be computed nightly AND populated to §4.3.16 `fraud_signal_flags[]` per Appendix J `referral_fraud_signal`.
2. Same-day signals (velocity_spike, same_payment_method) MUST also fire in real-time via PostHog Live Insights.
3. Cross-Org harvest detection MUST suppress L5 Free Allowance for the offending Orgs within 60 seconds of detection.
4. Fraud-flag accumulation MUST surface in the Ops Anti-Spam Dashboard (§48.3.3); SIM auto-kill-switch eligibility is computed from accumulated flag count (≥ 3 distinct flags = auto-kill-switch eligible).

### 48.4.7 k-Anonymity Floors {#48.4.7-k-anonymity-floors}

**Authoring intent.** k-anonymity is the cross-cutting privacy and signal-integrity invariant per Summary §3.5: every aggregated metric, signal, market-intelligence cell, search bucket, suggestion cohort, and referral cohort MUST satisfy a minimum-cohort-size floor before being rendered, exported, or piped into downstream consumers. The three-tier floor structure is canonical:

| Tier | Floor (k) | Surfaces (non-exhaustive) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Signal | k=5 | Per-Org seller signals (§4.4.18 SellerSignal); CategoryPage (§4.4.12) per-metric aggregates; M2 Public Selection Report aggregates; M14 Bid Success Share aggregates; M16 Referral cohort aggregates (`m16_referral_signup_to_activation_time_p50`, `m16_referral_org_retention_rate_90d`); §48.3.2 signals annotated `k=5`; L7 Cmd+K context-personalization cohort; L9 cross-buyer-org diversity floor. |
| Aggregate | k=10 | HeatMapCell (§4.4.16); per-category aggregate metrics across surfaces; §48.3.2 signals annotated `k=10`; M9 CategoryPage cross-category aggregates; M13 Heat Map demand cells; L10 Marketplace category cohort floor. |
| Market Intelligence | k=20 | MarketIntelligenceReport (§4.4.15); quarterly aggregate publications; cross-Org pricing-band signals; §48.3.2 signals annotated `k=20` (`m12_signal_density_per_category_per_quarter`). |

**Enforcement.** Every render path that emits an aggregated metric MUST execute the k-anonymity check against the underlying-cohort-size at render time; checks below the floor MUST replace the rendered metric with `Insufficient data` AND emit `growth_signal_k_anonymity_floor_violation` per §48.3.2. Publication of a page containing aggregate-derived metrics is blocked if `k_anon_satisfied=false`; pure-editorial pages with no aggregate-derived metrics MAY be published with `k_anon_satisfied=false`.

**Cohort definition.** Cohort size is computed across the *minimum* applicable axis — for a HeatMapCell `(category, region, industry, company_size_band, period)`, the cohort is the count of distinct Orgs contributing data to that exact 5-tuple, NOT the cohort across any single axis.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Every aggregate-emitting render path MUST have a unit test asserting cohort-size enforcement at the appropriate floor.
2. Every aggregate-emitting render path MUST emit `growth_signal_k_anonymity_floor_violation` on floor breaches AND fail the render with `Insufficient data` placeholder.
3. The cohort-size computation MUST be deterministic and reproducible from the §4.3.18 Usage Event ledger; QA-tested via synthetic cohort-replay.
4. Floor values (5, 10, 20) MUST be Ops-configurable per surface but seeded at the canonical values; non-canonical floor values require `ops_security_admin` approval AND emit `k_anonymity_floor_changed` (Appendix G — new).

**Post-Launch Empirical Backtest (Phase 5+ Authored Extension — Policy Validation).** The canonical floor values (5, 10, 20) are policy choices adopted at v7.0.0 in the absence of production cohort-distribution data. Once v7.0.0 has accumulated ≥ 90 days of live Marketplace traffic, a **mandatory empirical backtest** MUST run to validate that the chosen floors (a) suppress a tolerably-small fraction of surfaces (target: < 10% of cohort-render attempts) and (b) still prevent the worst-case re-identification attacks the floors are designed to defeat. Backtest scope: (i) per-surface cohort-size distribution histograms (CategoryPage, HeatMapCell, SellerSignal, MarketIntelligenceReport) computed nightly across the first 90 days; (ii) simulated re-identification attacks — per Summary §3.5 privacy thesis — run against synthesized adversarial cohorts at the k=5, k=10, k=20 floors to measure residual leak probability; (iii) calibration check: if p95 of per-surface cohort size is < 2× the floor for > 30% of surfaces, raise a §42 P2 re-evaluation alert to `ops_security_admin` AND `ops_growth_admin` (the floor may be set too high — is suppressing excessive content); if any adversarial simulation reconstructs > 1 Org identity out of 100 adversarial runs, raise a §42 P0 to `ops_security_admin` (the floor is set too low — structural privacy failure). Backtest outputs MUST be archived to `k_anonymity_floor_validation_reports` (Authored Extension — Ops Security artifact bucket; retention 7 years) and reviewed by the Ops Security Council at least annually thereafter. Event: `k_anonymity_floor_backtest_completed {floor_under_test, report_artifact_id, suppression_rate_observed, adversarial_reidentification_success_rate, recommendation ∈ {retain, lower, raise, subdivide_per_surface}}` (Appendix G — new). Floor changes recommended by the backtest follow the §48.4.7 AC 4 approval path; recommendation `subdivide_per_surface` unlocks surface-specific floor tuning with a documented rationale.

### 48.4.8 Suppression List {#48.4.8-suppression-list}

**Authoring intent.** The Ops-maintained suppression list is the global denylist for both inbound and outbound flows: addresses, domains, IPs, payment-method fingerprints, and SSO upstream identifiers that have been flagged as fraud, spam, OR legal-takedown subjects. Entries on the suppression list are universally honored across L1, L2, L4, L5, L7, L8, L9, L10, M1–M17, and the §41 Email Catalog.

**Entity stub.** SuppressionListEntry (Platform-Scoped, Ops-Managed); minimal field set:

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK | Standard. |
| `subject_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `suppression_list_subject_kind` (new: `email_address`, `email_domain`, `ip_address`, `ip_subnet_cidr`, `payment_method_fingerprint`, `sso_upstream_identity`, `org_id`, `user_id`); required | What is being suppressed. |
| `subject_value_hash` | String | SHA-256 hash, 64 chars; required | One-way hash for privacy-respectful storage of PII subjects. |
| `subject_value_plain` | String | Nullable; populated only for non-PII subjects (e.g., `email_domain`, `ip_subnet_cidr`); ≤ 256 chars | For Ops review. |
| `reason_code` | Enum | Appendix J `suppression_list_reason_code` (new: `legal_takedown`, `fraud_confirmed`, `spam_confirmed`, `compliance_request`, `gdpr_request`, `ops_decision`); required | Why suppressed. |
| `reason_note` | Text | ≤ 2,000 chars; required | Free-text Ops note. |
| `effective_at` | Timestamp | Required | Suppression effective time. |
| `expires_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Optional auto-expiry. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | Standard | Standard | `created_by` MUST hold `ops_security_admin` role. |

**Lookup contract.** Sub-100-ms hash lookup; cached at the edge. Every L1 / M5 / M16 / M17 trigger AND every L4 / L9 publish AND every email send checks the suppression list before proceeding.

**Acceptance criteria.**

1. Suppression list lookup MUST be sub-100-ms p95.
2. Adding a suppression list entry MUST require `ops_security_admin` approval AND emit `suppression_list_entry_added` (Appendix G — new).
3. Suppressed entities MUST be silently rejected at the trigger time (HTTP 422 with a generic error code; no leak of suppression state to the suppressed subject).

### 48.4.10 Signal Integrity Monitor (SIM) Cross-Reference {#48.4.10-sim-cross-reference}

**Authoring intent.** The Signal Integrity Monitor (SIM, Summary C.100) is the cross-cutting Ops surface that aggregates anti-spam control fires, kill-switch eligibility flags, anomaly detections, and false-positive feedback. It is referenced from §48.2.x loop sections and §48.4.1–§48.4.8 controls; the canonical SIM surface is documented at §4.3.16, §4.3.17, and §43 Ops Tooling. §48.4.10 enumerates the SIM signal classes that §48.4 controls produce and feeds, completing the cross-reference graph:

| SIM Signal Class | Origin (§48 controls) | Severity Default | Auto-Kill-Switch Eligible |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `velocity_anomaly` | §48.2.2 (L1), §48.2.3 (L2), §48.4.6 (referrals), §48.4.1 (email) | warning | No (warning only) |
| `cross_org_free_allowance_harvest` | §48.2.6 (L5), §48.4.6 (referrals) | critical | Yes |
| `dmarc_failure_correlation` | §48.4.2 | warning | No |
| `template_classifier_revision_demotion` | §48.4.5 | informational | No |
| `content_validator_repeat_offender` | §48.4.4 | warning | Yes (after ≥ 3 distinct flags within 30 days) |
| `vendor_opt_out_overlap` | §48.4.9 (cross-loop) | informational | No |
| `low_quality_outcome` | §48.2.9 (L8 KB-injection scanner), §48.2.10 (L9 demotion), §48.4.5 | warning | No |
| `referral_fraud_pattern_accumulation` | §48.4.6 | critical | Yes (after ≥ 3 distinct flags) |
| `k_anonymity_floor_violation` | §48.4.7 | warning | No |
| `suppression_list_lookup_anomaly` | §48.4.8 | warning | No |
| `manual_ops_review_pending` | Any control flagging Ops review | informational | No |

**SIM emits a `sim_signal_emitted` PostHog event** (Appendix G — new) on every fire, with `signal_class`, `severity`, `target_org_id` (nullable), `auto_kill_switch_eligible`, `triggering_event_ids[]`. Aggregated SIM dashboard surfaces in the Anti-Spam Dashboard (§48.3.3).

### 48.4.11 Acceptance Criteria {#48.4.11-acceptance-criteria}

1. Every §48.4 control MUST be unit-testable; CI gates merge if any control's unit test is missing.
2. Every §48.4 control fire MUST emit its named PostHog event within 5 seconds of the underlying trigger.
3. Every §48.4 control MUST be killable via Ops Console with a 60-second worst-case propagation latency.
4. The SIM signal-class catalog (§48.4.10) MUST be exhaustive — every signal-emitting §48.4 control maps to exactly one SIM signal class.
5. SIM auto-kill-switch eligibility MUST be deterministic given the source signals; QA-tested via synthetic-signal replay.
6. False-positive feedback loop: every Ops Anti-Spam Dashboard signal review action (uphold, dismiss, escalate) MUST be persisted AND fed back into classifier-retraining pipelines (per §48.4.5 monthly cadence).
7. Cross-control interactions MUST be documented: e.g., a referral-fraud-flagged Org auto-suppresses L5 Free Allowance (§48.4.6 + §48.2.6); the documentation cross-link MUST be present in both sections.

### 48.4.12 Seller Pricing Acceptable-Use Floor (Cross-Plan-Tier Constraints) {#48.4.12-seller-pricing-acceptable-use-floor}

**Authoring intent.** §48.4.12 codifies the seven seller-pricing-specific anti-abuse constraints from Summary §3.5 ("Seller-side pricing levers add specific constraints that pricing ceilings do not override"). The thesis of the section is verbatim: *"Pricing gives sellers access to outbound tools; Marketplace integrity defines the acceptable use floor. A paid tier is not an unlimited license to pollute."* Every paid-tier ceiling above (concurrent bid count, EOI quota, KB entry count, Firecrawl frequency) is a NORMATIVE upper bound on what a seller MAY do; §48.4.12 is the EFFECTIVE upper bound — the bound that actually constrains all sellers regardless of plan. Where a §48.4.12 limit and a plan-tier limit conflict, §48.4.12 wins.

**Source authority.** Summary §3.5 ¶ "Seller-side pricing levers add specific constraints" (the 7 enumerated items); Summary §3.4 ¶ Loop S1–S7 (Free-tier-contribution thesis); Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy.md §11 (Pricing-vs-Acceptable-Use); Summary §6.16.6 Marketplace Discovery (taxonomy gating); §4.4.8 CapabilityDeclaration (taxonomy enforcement); §4.4.22 SellerOnboardingSession (zombie-inventory denominator).

**The Seven Constraints — Effective-Upper-Bound Normative Spec.**

| # | Constraint | Scope | Numeric Limit / Rule | Enforcement Path | Telemetry Event (Appendix G) | Ops Override Authority | Plan-Tier Interaction |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1** | **EOI rate limit (per-seller)** | Per Seller Org per rolling 24h window | EOIs / Seller Org / 24h ≤ floor of (plan_tier `marketplace_eoi_monthly_quota / 30`, `30`) — i.e., even if the plan ceiling normalizes to > 30/day, the per-day floor caps at 30 to suppress burstiness | At EOI write path: SERIALIZABLE check against `(seller_org_id, created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours')` count; reject with HTTP 429 `marketplace_eoi_per_seller_24h_rate_limit_exceeded` (Appendix I — new) | `marketplace_eoi_rate_limit_fired {seller_org_id, scope ∈ {per_seller_24h, per_category_7d, per_buyer_30d}, current_count, limit_value, plan_tier}` (Appendix G — new) | `ops_security_admin` MAY raise the per-Org limit by writing an EOIRateLimitOverride (§4.4.x — Authored Extension flagged) with rationale; override audit-logged | Plan tier sets the *normative* monthly quota; §48.4.12 #1 sets the *effective* per-day burst-suppressor that is independent of plan |
| **2** | **EOI rate limit (per-category)** | Per Seller Org per category per rolling 7d window | EOIs / Seller Org / category / 7d ≤ `5` regardless of plan tier; further reduced to `3` for Seller Orgs in Marketplace verification tier `basic` (i.e., domain-verified only, no Verified or Certified badge) | Same write-path SERIALIZABLE check, scoped to `(seller_org_id, listing_category_id)` | Same event with `scope='per_category_7d'` | `ops_security_admin` override with rationale; Verified-tier sellers can request the limit be raised to `7`/category/7d by the Verification process (`ops_verification_admin`) | Independent of plan tier; verification tier provides the lift, NOT the plan tier — this is deliberate per Summary §3.5 ¶ "EOI submission is rate-limited per seller, per category, per buyer — independent of plan ceiling" |
| **3** | **EOI rate limit (per-buyer)** | Per Seller Org per Buyer Org (across all listings) per rolling 30d window | EOIs from a single Seller Org targeting a single Buyer Org across all that buyer's listings ≤ `3` per 30d. After the third, all subsequent EOIs are demoted to `pending_buyer_review_required` AND the buyer is notified once per 30d window (anti-stalking control; protects buyer mailbox) | Write-path check joining EOI → Listing → BuyerOrg | Same event with `scope='per_buyer_30d'`; AND `marketplace_eoi_buyer_relationship_demoted {seller_org_id, buyer_org_id, prior_eoi_count}` (Appendix G — new) when demotion fires | None for sellers; buyer MAY explicitly opt-out of further EOIs from a specific Seller Org via §4.4.8 vendor opt-out registry (existing) | Independent of plan tier; this is a hard buyer-mailbox-protection floor |
| **4** | **Capability Declarations validated against controlled taxonomy** | All CapabilityDeclarations (§4.4.8) at write | Every CapabilityDeclaration MUST be validated against the Marketplace Taxonomy registry (Summary §6.16.6); fabricated declarations (declarations whose `category_id` and `subcategory_id` do not resolve to active Taxonomy entries) MUST be suppressed at write — return HTTP 422 `capability_declaration_taxonomy_violation` (Appendix I — new). Free-text "additional capability" declarations are PERMITTED only at the *narrative* level (a description field); they MUST NOT generate Match Score signal | Pre-write Convex validator function `validateCapabilityDeclaration(declaration, taxonomy)` returning hard reject on taxonomy mismatch | `capability_declaration_taxonomy_violation_fired {seller_org_id, attempted_category_id, attempted_subcategory_id, taxonomy_version}` (Appendix G — new) | `ops_taxonomy_admin` (new role; Appendix J — new) MAY add new taxonomy entries in response to legitimate feedback; Sellers cannot bypass taxonomy validation at any plan tier | Independent of plan tier — Free, Starter, Growth, Scale, Enterprise all face identical taxonomy validation. Per Summary §3.5: *"Capability Declarations are validated against the controlled taxonomy; fabricated declarations are suppressed."* |
| **5** | **Anomalous-velocity detection (Signal Integrity Monitor)** | All Seller Orgs across plan tiers | SIM (§48.4.10) computes per-Seller-Org anomaly score across three dimensions: (a) EOI submission velocity ≥ 95th percentile of plan-cohort over rolling 7d; (b) Match Score → EOI conversion rate < 5th percentile of plan-cohort over rolling 30d; (c) Buyer-reported noise rate ("not a fit" / "not relevant" buyer feedback ÷ EOIs received) > 50% over rolling 30d. Any seller with `≥ 2 of 3` anomaly flags is auto-flagged for `ops_security_admin` review within 24h | SIM nightly sweep + on-write incremental computation; emits SIM signal class `seller_anomalous_velocity` (Appendix J — extension to existing SIM signal class enum) | `sim_signal_emitted {signal_class='seller_anomalous_velocity', seller_org_id, severity, anomaly_dimensions[], auto_kill_switch_eligible=false}` (existing event, new value) | `ops_security_admin` reviews and MAY (a) dismiss as false positive, (b) issue warning via Loops.so, (c) throttle (reduce per-day EOI cap by 50% for 30d), (d) suspend outbound tools, (e) suspend Marketplace listing — see Constraint 6 below | Independent of plan tier; paid sellers face identical SIM scrutiny |
| **6** | **Ops downgrade / throttle / suspend authority** | All Seller Orgs across plan tiers | `ops_security_admin` (with `ops_finance_admin` co-sign for any action with billing impact) MAY (a) throttle outbound tools (EOI rate cap to floor of plan limit and 25% of normal), (b) suspend outbound tools (no EOIs accepted), (c) demote Marketplace ranking (delisted from Featured, deprioritized in CategoryPage), (d) suspend Seller Profile (returns 410 Gone with re-list pathway in seller dashboard), (e) downgrade plan with no refund (last-resort for severe abuse). All actions are reversible via `ops_security_admin`; permanent termination requires Ops Council review per §47 Governance | OpsActionRecord (§4.6.x — Authored Extension flagged for the seller-action variants) | `ops_seller_action_taken {ops_actor_user_id, target_seller_org_id, action ∈ {throttle, suspend, demote, profile_suspend, plan_downgrade_no_refund}, rationale, sim_signal_class_triggers[], reversible_by ∈ {ops_security_admin, ops_council}, effective_at, scheduled_review_at}` (Appendix G — new) | `ops_security_admin` per the rules above; `ops_council` for permanent termination | Independent of plan tier; the action vocabulary is identical for Free and Enterprise sellers. Per Summary §3.5: *"Sellers can be downgraded, throttled, or suspended by Ops Console for outbound-tool abuse regardless of plan."* |
| **7** | **180-day zombie-inventory demotion** | Free Seller Orgs with `Subscription.plan_tier = 'seller_free'` (paid sellers exempt) | Free Sellers who (a) published a Seller Profile (`seller_profile.status = 'published'`) AND (b) have not (i) responded to a buyer invite, (ii) submitted a bid, (iii) submitted an EOI, (iv) accepted a KB entry, OR (v) edited their profile within rolling 180 days are demoted: Marketplace ranking score multiplier set to `0.25`, removed from CategoryPage default rotation, no longer eligible for organic Featured Placement. Demotion is reversible by ANY of (i)–(v) within 30 days of demotion (re-promotion); after 30 days, profile is hidden from Marketplace search (still resolvable by direct URL for backlink integrity); after 365 days of total inactivity, profile is archived per §4.4.6 retention rules | Nightly sweep; computed via `(seller_org_id, last_activity_at)` index on a denormalized SellerActivityWatermark column updated on each of (i)–(v) actions | `seller_org_zombie_inventory_demoted {seller_org_id, last_activity_at, days_since_last_activity}` (Appendix G — new); on re-promotion: `seller_org_zombie_inventory_promoted {seller_org_id, re-activation_action, days_in_demoted_state}` (Appendix G — new); on archival: `seller_org_zombie_inventory_archived {seller_org_id, last_activity_at}` (Appendix G — new) | `ops_growth_admin` MAY exempt specific Seller Orgs (e.g., during a documented onboarding-blocker incident) by writing a SellerInventoryDemotionExemption (§4.4.x — Authored Extension flagged) with expiry date | Free sellers only — paid sellers are exempt by design (paid sellers signal commitment by paying; the zombie-inventory pollution risk is limited to Free) |

**Cross-Constraint Interaction Rules.**

- A seller flagged by Constraint 5 (SIM anomalous velocity) AND simultaneously demoted under Constraint 7 (180-day zombie) MUST be reviewed by `ops_security_admin` BEFORE any re-promotion. Re-promotion is blocked until the SIM dismissal is recorded.
- A seller throttled under Constraint 6 (Ops throttle) is exempt from Constraint 7's zombie-inventory demotion sweep for the duration of the throttle (because the seller can't submit anyway, so inactivity is artificial).
- Constraints 1, 2, 3 (EOI rate limits) are independent of each other; a seller hit by ANY of them is rejected at the write path; the rejection is for the FIRST limit hit (not all).
- Constraint 4 (taxonomy validation) is a hard pre-write check; no plan-tier or Ops override permits taxonomy bypass at the seller-write path. Ops can ADD new taxonomy entries; Ops cannot bypass validation against the existing taxonomy.

**Effective-Upper-Bound vs. Plan-Ceiling Reconciliation.** §5.11 Feature Access Matrix lists the *normative plan-tier ceilings* (e.g., Seller Starter `marketplace_eoi_monthly_quota = 10`); §48.4.12 lists the *effective acceptable-use floor* (per-day, per-category, per-buyer caps). When a seller approaches the lower of the two, the lower wins. The §5.11 matrix MUST cross-reference §48.4.12 in the EOI quota row(s) per the §5.11 cross-reference convention (added in this section's appendix-update block).

**Failure Modes Addressed (Counterfactual Pass).**

1. **Seller Org under SIM dismissal pending hits a Conversion Moment trigger.** The Conversion Moment trigger (§48.1.7) fires unchanged AND emits its event; the upgrade prompt rendering MUST defer until the SIM dismissal completes; if SIM rules `throttle` or `suspend`, the upgrade prompt is suppressed and the seller sees a *"We need to review your account before upgrading. Our security team will reach out within 1 business day."* placeholder.
2. **Buyer with adversarial intent uses M5 Buyer-Pull Vendor Invite to flood a single Seller Org with EOI-eligible listings.** Constraint 3 (per-buyer EOI cap) caps the seller's outbound responses to 3/30d to the buyer's listings; further attempts demote silently; the buyer is notified once per 30d window of the demotion to maintain transparency.
3. **Taxonomy registry update inadvertently invalidates 100,000 existing Capability Declarations.** The taxonomy update path MUST include a "validate-against-existing-declarations" pre-flight check; if > 5% of existing declarations would be invalidated, the update requires Ops Council review per §47 Governance. Mid-flight invalidation: existing declarations are GRANDFATHERED (continue to render, continue to feed Match Score) for 90 days; re-validation prompts surface in the seller dashboard with 90 days to remediate.
4. **Free seller hitting Constraint 7 demotion notification race condition.** Demotion notification (Loops.so email) MUST fire BEFORE the demotion takes effect (24h grace); if Loops.so fails delivery (DLQ), demotion is deferred to next nightly sweep AND a §42 P3 alert raised.

**Acceptance Criteria (§48.4.12 specific).**

8. Every of the seven §48.4.12 constraints MUST be unit-testable AND integration-testable against synthetic fixtures; CI gates merge if any constraint's test is missing.
9. Constraint 1, 2, 3 (EOI rate limits) MUST be enforced at the EOI write path with sub-100ms p95 latency overhead; load-tested at 10,000 concurrent seller EOI submissions.
10. Constraint 4 (taxonomy validation) MUST be enforced at the CapabilityDeclaration write path; bypass attempts via direct API or via SDK MUST return HTTP 422 with `capability_declaration_taxonomy_violation`; integration test asserts 100% rejection across 1,000 fabricated-category attempts.
11. Constraint 5 (SIM anomalous velocity) MUST compute per-Seller-Org anomaly scores nightly AND incrementally on EOI write; nightly sweep MUST complete in ≤ 60 minutes at full active-Seller-Org population.
12. Constraint 6 (Ops authority actions) MUST emit the `ops_seller_action_taken` event within 5 seconds of action; the action MUST be reflected in the seller dashboard within 60 seconds; the audit trail (immutable; §4.6 audit log) MUST capture full rationale and Ops actor identity.
13. Constraint 7 (180-day zombie demotion) MUST honor the 24h pre-demotion notification grace; nightly sweep MUST process all candidate Seller Orgs in ≤ 30 minutes at steady-state population (projected 500K+ Free Seller Orgs).
14. The Acceptable-Use Floor MUST be queryable by Ops via a single dashboard tile per Seller Org showing all 7 constraints' current state (in-bounds, near-limit, throttled, suspended, demoted) — refresh ≤ 60 seconds.
15. Cross-constraint-interaction rules above MUST be encoded in the OpsActionRecord state machine (§4.6.x) AND cross-checked at every Ops action write; violations return HTTP 409 `ops_seller_action_constraint_interaction_violation` (Appendix I — new).

## 48.5 M1–M8 Growth Mechanics {#48.5-m1-m8-growth-mechanics}

**Authoring intent.** §48.5 authors the first eight numbered Expanded Growth Mechanics from Summary §3.3 (M1–M8) at full Master Spec fidelity. The remaining nine mechanics (M9–M17) are catalogued in their existing entity sections per §48-overview source-mapping note: M9 → §4.4.12 CategoryPage; M10 → §4.4.13 GuidePage; M11 → §4.4.14 ComparisonPage; M12 → §4.4.15 MarketIntelligenceReport; M13 → §4.4.16 HeatMapCell; M14 → §4.4.x Bid Success Share entity (Known Gap, see RECONCILIATION.md); M15 → §4.4.17 GhostBidImport; M16 → §4.3.16 Buyer Referral; M17 → §4.3.17 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat Grant + §34.13 procedural mechanics. §48.5 does NOT duplicate those sections; it cross-links.

**Per-mechanic structure.** Every M1–M8 subsection follows the same thirteen-block layout: (1) Purpose; (2) Trigger; (3) Actor & Entity Schema (referencing or authoring §4 entities); (4) Workflow (step-by-step including phase-gating); (5) UX Surfaces (referencing §3.3 pattern mapping); (6) Data Collected / Retained; (7) Anti-Abuse Controls (specific rules cross-linked to §48.4); (8) Plan Gating & Entitlement; (9) Telemetry Events; (10) Notifications Fired; (11) Webhooks Fired; (12) API Endpoints (with auth scope); (13) Acceptance Criteria. Each mechanic also closes with a **Failure Modes Addressed** subsection enumerating ≥ 3 realistic failure modes per the §48 counterfactual-pass requirement.

**Cross-mechanic invariants.** Every M1–M8 mechanic (a) emits at least one PostHog event registered in Appendix G (additions in this section's appendix-update block); (b) is gated by at least one §48.4 anti-spam control; (c) honors §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Records and §4.5.6 Marketplace-Domain Render Contract where it produces public or vendor-targeted artifacts; (d) is killable from the Ops Console via either the §48.2.12.4 GrowthLoopKillSwitch (when M-mechanic-aligned to a Loop) OR a feature-flag publish path with 60-second worst-case orchestrator-cache invalidation latency (§22.16.5); (e) honors §41 Email Deliverability & Compliance for any email-emitting flow; (f) is RBAC-gated per §5.11 Feature Access Matrix updates registered in this section's appendix-update block.

**Mechanic-to-Loop linkage.** M1 anchors L1's buyer-side analogue; M2 supersedes retired L3; M3, M4, M8 are platform-amplifier mechanics with no direct Loop assignment; M5 is the principal driver of L1 via buyer-pull invitations; M6 supersedes retired L6 (with M7); M7 is the active replacement for retired L6 (cross-team discovery surface). Every mechanic registered in §48.5 inherits the §48.2.12 GrowthLoopExecution audit-row contract when its activity is loop-attributable, OR persists a dedicated mechanic entity authored in this section when its activity stands outside the loop catalog (M1 StakeholderInvite, M2 PublicSelectionReport, M3 EvaluationCertificate, M4 NextEvaluationKickoffSession, M5 BuyerPullVendorInvite, M6 DomainAutoJoinClaim, M7 SuggestedTeamMemberCard, M8 OrgIntelligenceValueCurveCheckpoint).

**Source authority.** Summary §3.3 (M1–M17 inventory table); Summary C.63 (M5 anti-abuse), C.64 (M6 shared-use exclusion), C.65 (M7 k-anonymity + opt-out), C.66 (M8 value curve); §4.3 / §4.4 / §4.5 entities; §10.12–§10.13 Phase 12/13 procedural text (M2, M3, M4 trigger context); §16 Organizational Intelligence (M8 anchor); §6.4 Domain Governance + §6.5 Guest Users (M1, M6 SSO/auth context); §48.2.2 L1 (M5 amplifier coupling); §48.4 Anti-Spam framework (every mechanic).
