New error codes (Appendix I update): `m2_selection_report_not_approved` (HTTP 422), `m2_org_active_link_ceiling_exceeded` (HTTP 422), `m2_redaction_profile_unknown_key` (HTTP 422), `m2_redaction_profile_invalid_value_type` (HTTP 422), `m2_redaction_profile_internal_comments_must_be_false` (HTTP 422), `m2_watermark_opacity_out_of_range` (HTTP 422), `m2_watermark_disable_unauthorized` (HTTP 403), `m2_link_password_required` (HTTP 401, public render), `m2_link_password_invalid` (HTTP 401, public render), `m2_link_allowlist_domain_mismatch` (HTTP 403, public render), `m2_link_revoked` (HTTP 410, public render), `m2_link_expired` (HTTP 410, public render), `m2_password_brute_force_throttled` (HTTP 429, public render).

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. M2 publication MUST be hard-gated to `workspace.phase ≥ 12 AND selection_report.status='approved'`; pre-approval attempts MUST return HTTP 422 `m2_selection_report_not_approved`.
2. The per-Org active-link ceiling (100) MUST be enforced atomically; over-ceiling returns HTTP 422.
3. The `internal_comments_visible` redaction key MUST be hard-locked to `false`; the API MUST reject any publish payload with `internal_comments_visible=true`. QA test `m2_internal_comments_never_leak` asserts on every PR touching the M2 publish path.
4. The watermark MUST render on every page of the PDF AND every web view. The footer Sourcera badge MUST be present unless `co_marketing_authorized=true` Ops flag is set on the row.
5. The watermark MUST include a verifiable provenance hash (first 8 chars of `selection_report_snapshot_payload_hash`) on PDF pages by default; disabling requires `co_marketing_authorized=true`.
6. Vendor Opt-Out filed AFTER publish MUST be applied to the rendered output within 60 minutes (nightly resweep semantics) AND emit `m2_link_vendor_opt_out_resweep_applied`. The `m2.link.vendor_opt_out_applied` notification MUST fire to the Workspace Owner.
7. Edge cache TTL MUST be ≤ 600s; default 60s; tunability is server-config-only, not customer-config.
8. Password-protected links MUST rate-limit to 5 attempts / 10 min per IP-hash; 6th attempt MUST return HTTP 429 `m2_password_brute_force_throttled` for 10 minutes.
9. Email-allowlist links MUST require §6.1 SSO completion; resolved-email-domain mismatch MUST return HTTP 403 `m2_link_allowlist_domain_mismatch`.
10. `share_slug` MUST be 14 chars URL-safe Base32 (≥ 70 bits entropy); enumeration via incremental slug-guessing is computationally infeasible.
11. The provenance verify endpoint `GET /v1/public-reports/{share_slug}/verify` MUST return the snapshot hash, publish timestamp, republish count, revocation status, and current redacted-vendor count without authentication; this endpoint is deliberately unauthenticated to support recipient verification.
12. Republishing MUST preserve `share_slug` (link-stability) AND increment `republished_count`; the `selection_report_snapshot_payload_hash` MUST update to the current snapshot hash.
13. Revocation MUST bust the edge cache within 60 seconds AND replace the public render with a friendly "This link has been revoked" 410 page.
14. The full M2 funnel `m2_link_published → m2_link_view_recorded → m2_pdf_downloaded` MUST be PostHog-Insights-Funnels queryable per `org_id`, per `workspace_id`, AND per `link_visibility`.

#### Failure Modes Addressed

1. **Vendor files an opt-out the day after the buyer publishes a public M2 link with their name.** Resolved: nightly resweep applies the opt-out within 60 minutes via the §4.4.8 retroactive scan + §48.5.2 resweep job; the rendered surface replaces the vendor name with "Vendor Opted Out"; the buyer is notified via `m2.link.vendor_opt_out_applied`. Edge cache busted automatically.
2. **An attacker brute-forces a password-protected M2 link's password.** Resolved: per-IP rate limit (5 / 10 min) returns HTTP 429 with progressive backoff; SIM observes the attempt count and emits `velocity_anomaly` if a single IP attempts ≥ 50 distinct M2 slugs in 24h; suppression list addition is Ops-discretionary.
3. **Buyer's Selection Report is later corrected (Ops emergency override per §10.12 Step 6) while a public M2 link is live.** Resolved: corrections to `SelectionReport` do NOT auto-update the M2 link (snapshot is frozen at publish per `selection_report_snapshot_id`); the inviter is notified `m2.link.snapshot_drift_detected` (Appendix C extension below) and prompted to either republish (refresh snapshot) OR revoke. The drift-detection nightly job ensures the inviter sees the discrepancy within 25h.
4. **Buyer mistakenly publishes with `evaluator_names_visible=true` and only realizes after the link has been viewed.** Resolved: republish allows zero-friction redaction-profile mutation (preserves `share_slug`); the prior render is invalidated within the cache TTL (default 60s); the prior PDF download by readers in possession of it is not retractable but the verification endpoint will surface `republished_count > 1` as a flag for any recipient who cross-checks. The inviter receives a `m2.link.republished` confirmation.
5. **The §10.12 SelectionReport entity has not been formally authored in the Master Spec (Known Gap).** Resolved: M2 references `selection_report_snapshot_id` as a placeholder FK pending §10.12 entity formalization; the snapshot semantics (frozen JSON payload + payload_hash) are defined in §48.5.2 and survive the underlying entity's eventual formalization. RECONCILIATION.md carries this Known Gap forward.

### 48.5.3 M3 Evaluation Certificate Badge {#48.5.3-m3-evaluation-certificate-badge}

#### Purpose

M3 issues a verifiable "Selected via Sourcera" certificate to BOTH the buyer Org AND the winning vendor Org at Phase 13 closure. The certificate is a cryptographically signed, hash-anchored artifact containing the evaluation outcome (winning vendor name, evaluation date, requirement count, vendor-count evaluated, anonymized buyer org-name OR full buyer org-name per buyer toggle) that either party MAY embed externally — winning-vendor case-study microsites, buyer procurement-team LinkedIn posts, vendor RFP-response collateral. The mechanic exists because procurement-decision proof is high-trust currency in B2B sales — a third-party-verifiable claim of "we won this competitive selection" is far more credible than a vendor's self-reported case study. M3 turns Sourcera into the issuing authority and embeds Sourcera's brand into both sides' downstream marketing artifacts.

#### Trigger

Workspace transitions to `phase=13_closed` (Appendix E Workspace state machine) AND Selection Report `status='approved'` (per §10.12 Step 5). Certificate issuance is automatic on the phase transition: ONE certificate per (workspace, winning_vendor_org) pair is auto-generated within 60 seconds of the transition, in `status='draft_pending_buyer_review'`. The Workspace Owner MUST review + publish the certificate before it becomes public; pre-publish, only the buyer Org can see it.

#### Actor & Entity Schema

**Acting entity.** The Sourcera platform issues the certificate (system-orchestrated); the Workspace Owner OR Org Owner reviews + publishes. Vendor-side acceptance is implicit: the winning vendor Org receives an in-app + email notification with the option to embed the certificate; vendor declines are logged but do not block buyer-side publication.

**Targeted entity.** The (buyer Org, winning vendor Org, Workspace) triple — exactly one EvaluationCertificate per Workspace.

**New entity: EvaluationCertificate (Workspace-Originated, Cross-Console-Visible, Public).**

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK, immutable | Standard. |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | → Organization (§4.2.1); buyer Org; required | Buyer Org owns the cert; vendor Org has read access via cross-console projection. |
| `console` | Enum | `cross_console` (fixed) | Both consoles see the cert under their own scoping. |
| `workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | → Workspace (§4.3.1); required; UNIQUE one cert per workspace | Source workspace. |
| `winning_vendor_org_id` | UUID (FK) | → Organization (§4.2.1); required | Vendor Org being certified. |
| `winning_vendor_software_id` | UUID (FK) | → SellerSoftware (§4.4.9); nullable | Specific software product if the win was product-specific; null if the win was Org-level. |
| `certificate_serial_number` | String | 18 chars; format `SRC-{YYYY}-{NNNNNNNNNNNN}` (12 base32 chars after `SRC-{4-digit-year}-`); UNIQUE platform-wide | Human-displayable serial. |
| `certificate_uuid` | String | UUID v4 (separate from `id`); required; embedded in QR code | Public-facing identifier; surfaces in the embed widget. |
| `payload_canonical_json` | JSON | Canonicalized, ≤ 8,000 chars; required | The signed payload. Schema: see §48.5.3.x below. |
| `payload_canonical_json_hash` | String | SHA-256, 64 chars; required | Hash of `payload_canonical_json`; used in Ed25519 signature. |
| `signature_ed25519` | String | Base64; 88 chars (64-byte signature); required | Ed25519 signature of `payload_canonical_json_hash` using Sourcera's certificate-issuing key. |
| `signing_key_id` | String | Max 64 chars; required | Identifies which Sourcera signing key was used; supports key rotation (current key + N prior keys remain verifiable). |
| `issued_at` | Timestamp | Required | Issuance moment. |
| `published_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when buyer publishes. |
| `revoked_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set on revocation. |
| `revoked_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → User (§4.2.3) | Buyer Owner / Vendor Owner / Ops. |
| `revoked_reason` | Enum | Appendix J `m3_revoked_reason` (new): `buyer_request`, `vendor_request`, `disputed_outcome`, `legal_takedown`, `ops_security_action`, `data_correction`, `other` | Required when `revoked_at` non-null. |
| `vendor_acceptance_status` | Enum | Appendix J `m3_vendor_acceptance_status` (new): `pending_review`, `accepted`, `declined`, `embed_disabled_by_vendor` | Vendor's posture; default `pending_review`. |
| `vendor_responded_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When vendor reviewed. |
| `buyer_anonymity_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `m3_buyer_anonymity_kind` (new): `full_name`, `anonymized_industry_size_band`, `anonymized_industry_only`, `anonymized_size_band_only`, `fully_anonymous` | Buyer's choice for how their identity is represented in the public certificate. Default: `full_name`. |
| `buyer_anonymity_industry` | Enum | Appendix J `m3_industry` (new): `saas`, `fintech`, `healthcare`, `manufacturing`, `retail`, `government`, `education`, `media`, `nonprofit`, `other` | Populated when `buyer_anonymity_kind` is `anonymized_industry_*` OR `fully_anonymous`. |
| `buyer_anonymity_size_band` | Enum | Appendix J `m3_company_size_band` (new): `1_50`, `51_250`, `251_1000`, `1001_5000`, `5001_25000`, `25000_plus` | Populated when `buyer_anonymity_kind` is `anonymized_*size_band*` OR `fully_anonymous`. |
| `embed_widget_html_snapshot_url` | String | URL; max 2,000 chars | Stable URL to the embed widget HTML, served from Sourcera's verification-domain edge. |
| `verification_url` | String | URL; max 2,000 chars | Public verification page: `https://verify.sourcera.io/certs/{certificate_serial_number}`. |
| `view_count` | Integer | ≥ 0; default 0 | Aggregate views across all embed surfaces (debounced 1/min/IP). |
| `embed_count` | Integer | ≥ 0; default 0 | Distinct domains hosting the embed widget (resolved via Referer header + SHA-256 domain hash). |
| `signal_integrity_flags` | Array[Enum] | Per §48.2.12 enum; empty default | SIM-populated. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | Standard | Standard pattern | `created_by` is the system orchestrator (a synthetic User with `system` role); `updated_by` is the buyer or vendor user on review actions. |

**Scope isolation.** The buyer Org has full read + publish + revoke; the vendor Org has read + accept/decline + own-side-revoke (vendor-side revoke sets `vendor_acceptance_status=embed_disabled_by_vendor` AND prevents the vendor from embedding the certificate but does NOT remove the buyer-side public certificate). Ops has full lifecycle access. Cross-Org enumeration is impossible: the certificate URL is the only access point and is gated by serial number.

**Required indexes.** `(workspace_id)` UNIQUE, `(org_id, published_at DESC)`, `(winning_vendor_org_id, published_at DESC)`, `(certificate_serial_number)` UNIQUE, `(certificate_uuid)` UNIQUE, `(vendor_acceptance_status)` (sparse for vendor-side review queue).

**Retention.** Workspace-life + 7 years; certificate is immutable post-revocation per audit semantics. Identity fields pseudonymized on DSAR.

##### EvaluationCertificate Lifecycle State Machine

The `lifecycle_state` is derived from `published_at`, `vendor_acceptance_status`, and `revoked_at` per the table below.

| From (Computed State) | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `draft_pending_buyer_review` | Auto-issuance on Phase-13 closure + Selection Report approval | `published_at IS NULL`, `vendor_acceptance_status='pending_review'`, `revoked_at IS NULL` | `payload_canonical_json` + signature populated; cert NOT publicly accessible. |
| `draft_pending_buyer_review` | `published_pending_vendor_review` | Buyer PATCH publish | Buyer sets `published_at`; chooses `buyer_anonymity_kind` | Vendor receives `m3.certificate.published_for_vendor`; public verification page now live. |
| `published_pending_vendor_review` | `published_vendor_accepted` | Vendor POST respond with `accepted` | `vendor_acceptance_status → accepted` | Vendor MAY embed; counterparty notified. |
| `published_pending_vendor_review` | `published_vendor_declined` | Vendor POST respond with `declined` | `vendor_acceptance_status → declined` | Vendor MAY NOT embed; buyer cert remains live. |
| `published_pending_vendor_review` | `published_embed_disabled_by_vendor` | Vendor POST respond with `embed_disabled_by_vendor` | `vendor_acceptance_status → embed_disabled_by_vendor` | Vendor MAY NOT embed; buyer cert remains live. |
| `published_*` | `revoked_by_buyer` | Buyer / Org Owner DELETE | Caller holds eligible buyer-side role | `revoked_at`, `revoked_by_user_id`, `revoked_reason` populated; vendor notified via `m3.certificate.revoked`. |
| `published_*` | `revoked_by_vendor` | Vendor / Vendor Org Owner DELETE | Caller holds eligible vendor-side role | Same as buyer revocation but with vendor as initiator; buyer notified. |
| `published_*` | `revoked_by_ops` | Ops DELETE | `ops_security_admin` | Counterparty notified; `revoked_reason ∈ {legal_takedown, ops_security_action}`. |
| `published_*` (vendor named) | `published_*` (vendor name redacted) | Nightly Vendor-Opt-Out retro scan | New §4.4.8 opt-out filed for `winning_vendor_org_id` | Verification page replaces vendor name with "Vendor Opted Out"; embed badge mirrors; `m3.certificate.vendor_opt_out_applied` notification fires. |
| `revoked_*` | (terminal) | n/a | Append-only | New cert requires new EvaluationCertificate row (in practice impossible per UNIQUE `workspace_id` constraint; revoked certs are forever). |

**Invariants.** (a) `payload_canonical_json` is immutable post-issuance; the signature would no longer verify if mutated. (b) The cryptographic signature MUST verify against the JWKS-served public key on every public render. (c) Workspace UNIQUE constraint prevents duplicate-issuance even on phase-regression-then-re-close paths.

#### Certificate Payload Schema (Signed `payload_canonical_json`)

The signed payload is a canonicalized JSON document — fields sorted alphabetically by key, no whitespace, UTF-8 — to ensure stable hashing. Schema:

```json
{
  "buyer_org_display": "BoardCo Inc." OR "SaaS company, 1001-5000 employees" OR ...,
  "buyer_anonymity_kind": "full_name",
  "buyer_industry": "saas" OR null,
  "buyer_size_band": "1001_5000" OR null,
  "certificate_serial_number": "SRC-2026-K7Q4XPRMNB42",
  "certificate_uuid": "01HXYZ-...-...-...-...",
  "evaluation_close_date": "2026-04-15",
  "issuance_date": "2026-04-15",
  "issuer": "Sourcera Inc.",
  "issuer_url": "https://sourcera.io",
  "requirement_count": 142,
  "signing_key_id": "src-cert-key-2026-q1",
  "vendor_count_evaluated": 7,
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "winning_software_name": "Acme Cloud Platform" OR null,
  "winning_vendor_name": "Acme Corp",
  "workspace_name_hash": "sha256:5e8f..." (12 hex chars; raw name not exposed to preserve workspace privacy)
}
```

**Signature scheme.** Ed25519 over the SHA-256 hash of `payload_canonical_json`. Sourcera maintains a key-rotation log; current and prior 5 keys remain verifiable. Public keys served at `https://verify.sourcera.io/.well-known/sourcera-cert-keys.json` (JWKS-style).

**Embed format.** The embed widget is a single-line HTML snippet:

```html
<a href="https://verify.sourcera.io/certs/SRC-2026-K7Q4XPRMNB42" target="_blank" rel="noopener" data-sourcera-cert="01HXYZ-...">
  <img src="https://verify.sourcera.io/badges/SRC-2026-K7Q4XPRMNB42.svg" alt="Selected via Sourcera — SRC-2026-K7Q4XPRMNB42" width="200" height="60" />
</a>
```

The badge SVG is dynamically generated server-side; the image content is cached at the edge with a 5-minute TTL. The badge contains the Sourcera wordmark + the serial-number footer + a small QR code linking to the verification URL.

**Verification page.** `https://verify.sourcera.io/certs/{serial}` renders an unauthenticated page showing: Sourcera's claim ("Sourcera certifies that {Vendor} was selected by {Buyer or anonymized identity} on {Date} after evaluating {N} vendors against {M} requirements"), the issuance date, signature verification status (live-verified against the JWKS), revocation status, and a "Verify the signature yourself" code snippet showing how to verify the Ed25519 signature against the public key. The page is search-engine indexable to amplify SEO value (L4 amplifier).

#### Workflow

1. **Auto-issuance.** On Workspace `phase=13_closed` + Selection Report `status='approved'` transition, the orchestrator: (a) computes the `payload_canonical_json` from the §10.12 outcome data, the §10.13 closure metadata, and the §13 vendor / requirement counts; (b) hashes it; (c) signs it with the current Sourcera certificate-issuing key; (d) writes the EvaluationCertificate row in `vendor_acceptance_status=pending_review` AND `published_at IS NULL` (draft state). Issuance latency target: ≤ 60 seconds from phase transition. Issuance failures alert §42 P1.
2. **Buyer review.** The Workspace Owner sees a Pulse card "Your Evaluation Certificate is ready" and an inline draft preview in the Workspace > Closure tab. Buyer chooses `buyer_anonymity_kind` (default `full_name`); buyer MAY edit the certificate's display fields ONLY in the bounded ways specified by `buyer_anonymity_kind` (the underlying outcome data is immutable). Buyer publishes via "Publish Certificate" button.
3. **Vendor notification + review.** On buyer publish, the vendor Org's Bid Owner + Org Owner receive `m3.certificate.published_for_vendor` notification with a CTA to review + accept the certificate. Vendor sees the rendered certificate + embed widget; vendor MAY accept (default behavior — embed enabled) OR decline (sets `vendor_acceptance_status=declined`; vendor cannot embed; buyer's public cert remains live) OR disable embed only (sets `embed_disabled_by_vendor`; buyer cert remains live but the public verification page suppresses the vendor-name reference if vendor opt-out is also present).
4. **Public verification page.** Anonymous viewers hit the verification URL; rendered server-side with live signature verification.
5. **Embed in external sites.** Buyer / vendor copies the embed snippet from their respective Workspace / Bid Workspace closure tab and embeds in their own marketing collateral. The embed widget loads from Sourcera's verification domain; revocation OR disablement is reflected within the badge SVG cache TTL (5 min).
6. **Revocation.** Buyer, Vendor, OR Ops MAY revoke. Revocation: (a) sets `revoked_at` + `revoked_by_user_id` + `revoked_reason`; (b) the verification URL renders "This certificate has been revoked on {date} for the following reason: {reason public-display}"; (c) the embed badge SVG renders an inline "Revoked" stripe; (d) edge cache busted within 60s.
7. **Vendor Opt-Out interaction.** If the winning vendor files a §4.4.8 `global` Vendor Opt-Out, the M3 certificate's verification page replaces the vendor name with "Vendor Opted Out" AND the embed badge replaces the vendor name with the same; the buyer is notified `m3.certificate.vendor_opt_out_applied`.

| Buyer Certificate Draft Preview (Workspace > Closure > Certificate) | `Detail Panel + Inline Editing` per §3.3 | Live preview of badge SVG + verification page; toggle anonymity choices. |
| Buyer Publish Modal | `Modal + Confirmation` per §3.3 | "Publish certificate as-is — recipients can verify it forever" with terms checkbox. |
| Vendor "Certificate Available" notification (in-app + email) | `In-App Inbox` per §20 | CTA "Review your win certificate." |
| Vendor Certificate Review (Bid Workspace > Closure > Certificate) | `Detail Panel + Action Bar` per §3.3 | Accept / Decline / Disable Embed / Copy Embed Snippet. |
| Public verification page | Custom marketing-domain template | SEO-optimized; semantic HTML; social meta tags for OpenGraph + Twitter Card. |
| Embed snippet copy widget | `Inline Code Block + Copy Button` per §3.3 | Snippet auto-selects on click. |
| Mobile parity | Per §3.4 | Cert preview is responsive. |

#### Data Collected / Retained

Per the EvaluationCertificate field table. The signed payload is immutable after issuance. View counts and embed counts are aggregable signals for §48.3 dashboards. DSAR pseudonymization applies to identity fields; the payload itself is not redactable post-issuance (the signature would no longer verify) but the public render IS subject to the §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out registry.

#### Anti-Abuse Controls

1. **One-cert-per-workspace invariant.** UNIQUE constraint on `(workspace_id)`; system orchestrator prevents duplicate issuance even on retry.
2. **Buyer-only edit scope.** The buyer can only edit the bounded anonymity fields (`buyer_anonymity_kind`, `buyer_anonymity_industry`, `buyer_anonymity_size_band`); attempts to edit the underlying outcome data (vendor name, count, dates) return HTTP 403 `m3_outcome_data_immutable`.
3. **Vendor-side revoke does not affect buyer-side cert.** Asymmetric revoke prevents vendor weaponization (e.g., a losing vendor cannot stop a buyer from publishing a cert; the certified vendor IS the winner, who may decline-only).
4. **Signature verification on every render.** The verification page re-verifies the Ed25519 signature against the JWKS-served public key; a failed verification (key rotation gone wrong) renders an error page AND raises §42 P1.
5. **Edge cache bounded to 5 min.** Badge SVG and verification page cached with short TTL; revocation propagates within the TTL.
6. **§4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out applied at render** — verification page suppresses vendor name on opt-out.
7. **§48.4.4 content validators** — applied to any free-text fields (none in the canonical payload, but applies to buyer-edited anonymity fields if Other-style values are added in future versions).
8. **SIM cross-cert enumeration detection.** If a single IP requests ≥ 100 distinct certificate verification URLs in 24h, SIM emits `velocity_anomaly`; the IP is rate-limited to 10 verification requests per hour for the next 24h. Prevents enumeration scraping.

#### Plan Gating & Entitlement

M3 is included on every Buyer plan tier (Free → Enterprise) AND every Seller plan tier — the certificate is the canonical artifact of evaluation closure, gated only by the workspace reaching `phase=13_closed`. Vendor-side embed is included on every Seller plan including Free.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. EvaluationCertificate auto-issuance MUST complete within 60 seconds of `phase=13_closed AND selection_report.status='approved'`; failure raises §42 P1.
2. Exactly one EvaluationCertificate per Workspace; UNIQUE constraint enforced atomically; duplicate-issuance attempts (e.g., on phase regression + re-advance) MUST detect the existing row AND skip.
3. The Ed25519 signature MUST verify against the published JWKS at `https://verify.sourcera.io/.well-known/sourcera-cert-keys.json`; signature mismatch on render MUST raise §42 P1 AND render a friendly error page (not the cert).
4. Public verification page MUST be search-engine indexable (no `noindex`), MUST include OpenGraph + Twitter Card meta tags for social-share preview, AND MUST live-verify the signature on every load.
5. Buyer anonymity choice MUST be enforced at render: if `fully_anonymous`, the verification page MUST NOT contain the buyer Org name OR any direct identifier in HTML, JSON, OR meta tags.
6. Vendor-side decline MUST NOT remove the buyer-side public certificate; vendor-side embed-disable MUST prevent the vendor from embedding without affecting buyer embed.
7. Vendor Opt-Out filed AFTER cert publish MUST suppress the vendor name on the verification page within 60 minutes (retroactive scan) AND emit `m3_certificate_vendor_opt_out_applied`.
8. Embed badge SVG MUST cache at the edge with TTL ≤ 5 min; revocation propagates within the TTL.
9. SIM enumeration detection (≥ 100 distinct serial verification requests from one IP in 24h) MUST trigger per-IP rate-limit (10 verifications/h for the next 24h).
10. The full M3 funnel `m3_certificate_issued → m3_certificate_published → m3_certificate_verification_viewed → m3_certificate_embed_loaded` MUST be PostHog-Insights-Funnels queryable per `winning_vendor_org_id` (vendor-attribution analysis) and per `org_id` (buyer-attribution analysis).
11. The certificate serial number format MUST be `SRC-{YYYY}-{12-char-base32}`; collisions MUST be impossible (12 chars × 5 bits = 60 bits entropy, 2⁶⁰ ≈ 10¹⁸ ≫ certificate volume).

#### Failure Modes Addressed

1. **Sourcera's signing key is compromised and rotated mid-deployment.** Resolved: `signing_key_id` is per-cert; the JWKS retains the prior 5 keys for verification continuity. Any new cert uses the current key. Compromised-key revocation is an Ops emergency procedure that flags all certs signed with the compromised key for re-signing under a new key + re-publication; the verification page surfaces a "This cert was re-signed under a new key on {date} due to a key-rotation event" banner.
2. **Vendor disputes the win attribution post-publish (claims they were not actually selected).** Resolved: vendor-side `decline` flag sets `vendor_acceptance_status=declined`; vendor MAY also file §4.5.7 Marketplace Abuse Report `kind=qualitative_label_dispute` extension OR a new `m3_outcome_dispute` enum value (Appendix J extension below). Ops review per §43; resolution paths include cert revocation OR confirmation-with-buyer-rationale.
3. **Buyer publishes cert then their org is acquired and the new entity wants the cert removed.** Resolved: revocation by org-owner of acquiring entity (post-§7 acquisition, the new org-owner inherits §5.2 Org Owner role) is a single-click revoke operation; the cert revocation propagates within the 5-minute edge cache TTL.
4. **Verification URL is mass-scraped by a competitor for competitive intelligence.** Resolved: per-IP rate limit (per AC #9) + SIM detection + the verification page deliberately reveals only the certificate-payload metadata (no per-vendor performance data, no per-requirement scoring detail). The cert's information disclosure is bounded by the canonical payload schema.
5. **Vendor's Org is deleted between cert publish and a future verification access.** Resolved: the cert payload is immutable AND the verification page renders the historical vendor name (with a footer note "This vendor is no longer active on Sourcera"); the cert remains valid until explicitly revoked.

### 48.5.4 M4 "Kick Off Next Evaluation" on Close {#48.5.4-m4-kick-off-next-evaluation-on-close}

#### Purpose

M4 surfaces a one-click "Start your next evaluation" prompt at the moment of peak procurement-success momentum: immediately after Phase 13 closure. The mechanic exists because the highest-conversion moment for a Workspace Owner to commit to using Sourcera for their NEXT evaluation is the moment they have just experienced a clean, successful close. M4 carries forward team membership, evaluation methodology preferences, common requirement templates, vendor-pool history, and Org Intelligence context (M8) into a pre-populated new Workspace draft so the friction to start the next evaluation drops from "schedule a kickoff meeting + create a Workspace from scratch" to "click one button + name the Workspace."

#### Trigger

Workspace transitions to `phase=13_closed` (Appendix E) AND Selection Report `status='approved'`. M4 surface is rendered: (a) inline in the Workspace > Closure tab; (b) as a Pulse card to the Workspace Owner; (c) as a one-time toast on next dashboard load post-closure.

#### Actor & Entity Schema

**Acting entity.** Workspace Owner OR Org Owner of the closed Workspace.

**Targeted entity.** A new Workspace draft (not yet committed to Phase 1 — sits in `phase=0_draft` per Appendix E extension below if not already present).

**New entity: NextEvaluationKickoffSession (Workspace-Originated, Buyer-Only).** Tracks the prompt → click → new-Workspace flow for attribution.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK, immutable | Standard. |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | → Organization (§4.2.1); buyer Org; required | RBAC scope. |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer` (fixed) | M4 is buyer-only. |
| `source_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | → Workspace (§4.3.1); required | The closed workspace whose closure triggered the M4 prompt. |
| `prompted_user_id` | UUID (FK) | → User (§4.2.3); required | The user who saw the M4 prompt (Workspace Owner). |
| `prompt_surface` | Enum | Appendix J `m4_prompt_surface` (new): `closure_tab_inline`, `pulse_card`, `dashboard_toast` | Where the prompt fired. |
| `prompt_rendered_at` | Timestamp | Required | When prompt rendered. |
| `clicked_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When user clicked the CTA. |
| `dismissed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When user explicitly dismissed (X button) without converting. |
| `dismissal_reason` | Enum | Appendix J `m4_dismissal_reason` (new): `not_planning_another_evaluation_now`, `will_start_later`, `team_decides`, `using_different_tool_next`, `other` | Optional UI-collected; nullable. |
| `target_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → Workspace (§4.3.1) | Set when the user clicks-through and a new Workspace draft is created. |
| `prefill_strategy` | Enum | Appendix J `m4_prefill_strategy` (new): `full_carry_over`, `team_only`, `template_only`, `vendor_pool_only`, `methodology_only`, `none` | The selected prefill strategy. Default: `full_carry_over`. |
| `prefill_artifact_count` | JSON | `{team_members: N, requirements: N, vendors: N, use_cases: N, scoring_rubric_carried: Boolean, m8_value_curve_imported: Boolean}` | Telemetry of what was actually carried. |
| `attribution_window_expires_at` | Timestamp | Required; computed: `prompt_rendered_at + 30 days` | After 30d, the M4 row is closed (decayed) for attribution purposes. |
| `outcome` | Enum | Appendix J `m4_outcome` (new): `pending`, `converted_workspace_created`, `converted_workspace_advanced_to_phase_2`, `dismissed`, `expired_30d` | Lifecycle terminal states. |
| `outcome_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set on terminal transition. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | Standard | Standard pattern | Created by the system orchestrator on prompt fire. |

**Scope isolation.** Org-scoped on `org_id` AND Workspace-scoped on `source_workspace_id`. Read access: `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `workspace_owner` of source.

**Required indexes.** `(org_id, prompted_user_id, prompt_rendered_at DESC)`, `(source_workspace_id)`, `(target_workspace_id)` (sparse; populated post-conversion), `(outcome, outcome_at DESC)`, `(attribution_window_expires_at) WHERE outcome='pending'` (nightly expiry sweep).

**Retention.** Org-life + 7 years for analytics + audit. DSAR pseudonymization on `prompted_user_id`.

#### Workflow

1. **Auto-prompt.** On Workspace `phase=13_closed` + Selection Report `status='approved'`, the orchestrator creates a NextEvaluationKickoffSession row in `outcome=pending` AND renders the M4 surfaces (inline closure tab, Pulse card, dashboard toast on next load).
2. **Prompt copy.** "You closed {Workspace Name} successfully — congratulations. Want to start your next evaluation with the same team, methodology, and template?" Single-CTA "Start Next Evaluation" + secondary "Maybe later" + dismiss X.
3. **Click-through.** User clicks; modal opens with prefill-strategy chooser:
   - Team (carry over team members AND their roles)
   - Vendor pool (carry over vendors that were evaluated; useful for re-evaluation cycles)
   - Requirements (carry over requirements OR start from a Sourcera Template OR start from the Workspace's saved Template)
   - Methodology (scoring rubric, granularity profile, phase-gate preferences)
   - M8 Org Intelligence import (attach M8 Value Curve insights to the new Workspace)
   Default selection: full carry-over (team + methodology + scoring rubric + M8 curve; vendor pool and requirements OFF by default since most "next evaluations" are different categories).
4. **New Workspace creation.** On confirm, the orchestrator: (a) creates a new Workspace in `phase=1_draft` per §10.2 (NEW state per Appendix E extension below); (b) attaches the chosen prefill artifacts; (c) sets `target_workspace_id` on the M4 row; (d) transitions M4 outcome to `converted_workspace_created`; (e) navigates the user to the new Workspace's Phase 1 entry view.
5. **Phase-2 advancement attribution.** If the new Workspace advances from Phase 1 → Phase 2 within 30 days of the original prompt, the M4 outcome is upgraded to `converted_workspace_advanced_to_phase_2` (the higher-quality conversion signal).
6. **Dismissal.** User clicks X OR "Maybe later"; M4 row transitions to `outcome=dismissed` with optional `dismissal_reason`. Dismissed prompts do NOT re-render for the same source workspace.
7. **Expiry.** Nightly sweep at 02:30 UTC transitions `outcome=pending → expired_30d` after `attribution_window_expires_at`.

#### UX Surfaces

| Surface | §3.3 Pattern | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Closure-tab inline card | `Detail Panel + CTA` per §3.3 | Visible only post-Phase-13 closure. |
| Pulse card | `In-App Inbox` per §20 | "Closed an evaluation? Start your next one." |
| Dashboard toast | `Toast` per §3.3 | Appears once on next dashboard load post-closure; dismissible. |
| Prefill-strategy modal | `Modal + Multi-Select` per §3.3 | Checkbox tree of prefill artifact categories. |
| Mobile parity | Per §3.4 | Modal becomes full-screen sheet. |

#### Data Collected / Retained

Per the field table. Telemetry of conversion drives §48.3 dashboards.

#### Anti-Abuse Controls

1. **One M4 row per source workspace.** UNIQUE constraint on `(source_workspace_id)`; re-render attempts on phase regression + re-close detect the existing row AND do NOT create a duplicate.
2. **Dismissed prompts do not re-render.** Avoids prompt fatigue; aligns with §29.3 quiet-hours respect.
3. **30-day attribution window.** Conversion attribution is bounded to prevent stale-conversion inflation.
4. **No PII in prefill artifacts beyond what the source Workspace already exposes** — M4 carries internal Workspace state into a new Workspace within the same Org; no cross-Org leakage by definition.
5. **§48.4 cross-cutting controls inherit** — M4 prompts respect §48.4.1 email throttling (M4 fires no email by default; opt-in only) and §29.3 user preferences for in-app notifications.

#### Plan Gating & Entitlement

M4 is included on every Buyer plan tier. The new-Workspace creation is subject to the per-plan `Active Evaluations` cap (§34.1.1); attempting to convert when at the cap returns HTTP 422 `m4_active_evaluations_cap_exceeded` AND surfaces an upgrade CTA per §48.2.6 L5 conversion path. Free-tier buyers hit the cap at 1 active evaluation; the M4 conversion to a new evaluation requires either (a) closing/archiving the source evaluation already (which the user just did) OR (b) upgrading the plan.

#### Telemetry Events

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `m4_prompt_rendered` | Auto-prompt fires | `m4_session_id`, `source_workspace_id`, `prompted_user_id`, `prompt_surface` |
| `m4_prompt_clicked` | User clicks CTA | `m4_session_id`, `time_from_prompt_to_click_seconds` |
| `m4_prompt_dismissed` | User explicitly dismisses | `m4_session_id`, `dismissal_reason` |
| `m4_workspace_created` | New workspace created from M4 flow | `m4_session_id`, `target_workspace_id`, `prefill_strategy`, `prefill_artifact_count` |
| `m4_workspace_advanced_to_phase_2` | Target workspace advances Phase 1 → 2 within 30d | `m4_session_id`, `target_workspace_id`, `time_from_creation_to_phase_2_seconds` |
| `m4_session_expired` | Nightly expiry | `m4_session_id`, `time_from_prompt_to_expiry_seconds` |

#### Notifications Fired

| Notification | Recipient | Channels | Frequency | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `m4.next_evaluation_prompt` | Workspace Owner | In-App (Pulse + Toast) | Once per closed workspace | No email by default; in-app only. |

(M4 is intentionally low-touch; one in-app prompt + dashboard toast covers conversion without cluttering inbox.)

#### Webhooks Fired

| Webhook event_type | Trigger | Payload Highlights |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `growth.m4.workspace_created` | M4 conversion | `m4_session_id`, `source_workspace_id`, `target_workspace_id`, `prefill_strategy` |

#### API Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth Scope | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `GET` | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/workspaces/{workspace_id}/m4-sessions` | `read:workspaces` + role in {`org_owner`, `org_admin`, `workspace_owner`} | Fetch the M4 row (one per source workspace). |
| `POST` | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/workspaces/{workspace_id}/m4-sessions/convert` | `write:workspaces` + same roles | Body: `{prefill_strategy, target_workspace_name}`. Returns the new Workspace. |
| `POST` | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/workspaces/{workspace_id}/m4-sessions/dismiss` | `write:workspaces` + same roles | Body: `{dismissal_reason}` (optional). |

New error code: `m4_active_evaluations_cap_exceeded` (HTTP 422; upgrade CTA in error body per §32.6 + §48.2.6 L5 contract).

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. M4 prompt MUST auto-fire on `phase=13_closed AND selection_report.status='approved'` AND create exactly one NextEvaluationKickoffSession row per source workspace within 60 seconds.
2. Conversion MUST create a new Workspace AND link `target_workspace_id` atomically with the M4 outcome transition.
3. The `m4_workspace_advanced_to_phase_2` event MUST fire only if the target Workspace advances within 30 days of the original prompt; later advancements do NOT retroactively credit M4.
4. Hitting the per-plan Active Evaluations cap during M4 conversion MUST return HTTP 422 `m4_active_evaluations_cap_exceeded` with an upgrade CTA in the error body.
5. The full M4 funnel `m4_prompt_rendered → m4_prompt_clicked → m4_workspace_created → m4_workspace_advanced_to_phase_2` MUST be PostHog-Insights-Funnels queryable per `org_id`.
6. Dismissed M4 prompts MUST NOT re-render for the same source workspace; QA test `m4_dismiss_persistence` asserts.

#### Failure Modes Addressed

1. **User clicks M4 conversion but team membership has churned (members departed since source workspace).** Resolved: prefill-strategy confirmation modal warns "{N} of the source workspace's team members are no longer in your Org" with options to (a) carry over only active members, (b) carry over all members and re-invite the departed (auto-issuing M1 invites for ex-members who are still procurement-relevant), (c) skip team carry-over. Authoring extension; flagged.
2. **User dismisses M4 then later changes their mind.** Resolved: M4 prompt is one-shot per workspace (per AC #6). Workaround: user creates a new Workspace manually + uses the existing "Clone from Workspace" feature (§19 Templates) to achieve similar carry-over. Acceptable trade-off for prompt-fatigue avoidance.
3. **Source workspace was closed via `cancel` not `phase 13` — should M4 fire?** Resolved: M4 fires ONLY on `phase=13_closed AND selection_report.status='approved'`; cancelled workspaces (per §10.14) do NOT trigger M4. The cancellation is a different signal (negative procurement outcome) and prompting "start another" would be jarring.

### 48.5.5 M5 Buyer-Pull Vendor Invite {#48.5.5-m5-buyer-pull-vendor-invite}

#### Purpose

M5 lets a buyer add a vendor to an evaluation by name (or website / email) BEFORE that vendor exists on Sourcera, using an anonymized templated outreach that names the buyer's evaluation context (category + use case + close-by-date) without naming the buyer Org. The mechanic is the principal driver of L1 (Vendor-Invite-Creates-Account, §48.2.2): a single Phase 4 vendor-discovery exercise typically pulls 3–10 not-yet-on-Sourcera vendors into the platform per evaluation, each of whom may sign up as a Seller Org and bootstrap their KB. The "buyer-pull" name distinguishes M5 from the Marketplace's seller-push EOI flow (§4.5.2): in M5, the buyer initiates and the vendor responds; in EOI, the vendor initiates.

#### Trigger

A Workspace Owner, Evaluation Lead, OR Use Case Lead clicks "Add Vendor" on Phase 4 (Vendor Discovery) OR Phase 5 (Vendor Outreach) per §10.5; selects the "Invite a vendor not yet on Sourcera" option (vs the Marketplace-search option); fills the M5 modal. Trigger fires at Target Account creation per §48.2.2 L1 trigger semantics. M5 is gated to `workspace.phase ∈ {4_vendor_discovery, 5_vendor_outreach, 6_vendor_bidding_open}` per §10.5–§10.6 — Phase 4–6 inclusive (M5 invites in Phase 6 are uncommon but supported when an additional vendor is added late). Outside this window, the option is hidden in the UI and the API returns HTTP 422 `m5_invite_phase_out_of_window`.

#### Actor & Entity Schema

**Acting entity.** Buyer Org user with `workspace_owner`, `evaluation_lead`, OR `use_case_lead` role per §5.3.

**Targeted entity.** A not-yet-on-Sourcera vendor — identified by EITHER (a) email address (preferred), (b) corporate website (Sourcera attempts to discover the vendor's primary contact email via §22.6 Firecrawl OR public-WHOIS/contact-page heuristics), OR (c) free-form vendor name + manual buyer-supplied email.

**New entity: BuyerPullVendorInvite (Workspace-Scoped, Buyer-Origin).** Distinct from §4.3.x Target Account in that this entity tracks the M5-specific anonymized-outreach lifecycle including the throttle bookkeeping; the underlying Target Account is the §10.5 procurement-pipeline entity. One BuyerPullVendorInvite row per Target Account whose creation triggered an M5 send.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK, immutable | Standard. |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | → Organization (§4.2.1); buyer Org; required | RBAC scope. |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer` (fixed) | M5 is buyer-only origin. |
| `workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | → Workspace (§4.3.1); required | The evaluation context. |
| `target_account_id` | UUID (FK) | → Target Account (§10.5); required; UNIQUE one M5 row per Target Account | Pipeline-level entity reference. |
| `inviter_user_id` | UUID (FK) | → User (§4.2.3); required | Inviter; must hold §5.3-eligible role. |
| `vendor_name_supplied` | String | 1–200 chars | Buyer-supplied vendor name as displayed. |
| `vendor_website_supplied` | String | URL; max 2,000 chars; nullable | Buyer-supplied vendor website. |
| `vendor_email_supplied` | String | Valid email; max 320 chars; nullable | Buyer-supplied OR Firecrawl-discovered. |
| `vendor_email_resolved` | String | Valid email; max 320 chars; lowercased; required | The final email used for the send (after disambiguation). |
| `vendor_email_domain` | String | Max 253 chars; lowercased; required; denormalized | For §48.4.3 shared-use-domain check + §48.2.2 throttle bookkeeping. |
| `vendor_email_domain_hash` | String | SHA-256, 12 hex chars | Privacy-respectful denormalization for cross-Org SIM correlation. |
| `email_discovery_method` | Enum | Appendix J `m5_email_discovery_method` (new): `buyer_supplied`, `firecrawl_homepage`, `firecrawl_contact_page`, `whois_lookup`, `manual_ops_supplement` | Provenance of `vendor_email_resolved`. |
| `email_discovery_confidence_score` | Decimal | 0.0–1.0; nullable | Discovery confidence (1.0 = buyer_supplied; lower for heuristic discovery). |
| `outreach_template_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `m5_outreach_template_kind` (new): `default_anonymized`, `custom_buyer_message`, `category_specific`, `hybrid` | Template selection. |
| `category_id` | UUID (FK) | → Marketplace Category (§4.4.7); nullable | If `outreach_template_kind=category_specific`. |
| `custom_message_body` | String | 0–1,000 chars; nullable | If `outreach_template_kind=custom_buyer_message`; passes §48.4.4 content validators. |
| `evaluation_close_by_date` | Date | Required | Buyer-supplied close-by hint surfaced in the email. |
| `buyer_anonymity_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `m5_buyer_anonymity_kind` (new): `fully_anonymous`, `industry_size_band_only`, `named_buyer` | The buyer's anonymity posture in the outbound email. Default: `fully_anonymous`. |
| `email_send_status` | Enum | Appendix J `m1_email_send_status` (reused) | Mirrors §41 Loops.so telemetry. |
| `email_payload_hash` | String | SHA-256, 64 chars | Per §48.4.1 dedup. |
| `redemption_status` | Enum | Appendix J `m5_redemption_status` (new): `pending`, `clicked`, `signed_up_outside_window`, `signed_up_within_window`, `bid_response_submitted`, `expired_unredeemed`, `bounced_undeliverable`, `revoked_by_inviter`, `revoked_by_ops`, `suppressed_pre_send` | Lifecycle. |
| `attribution_window_expires_at` | Timestamp | Required; computed: `created_at + 60 days` | Aligned with L1 attribution window (§48.2.2). |
| `signed_up_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when the vendor signs up via the magic link OR is matched to an existing Seller Org via email-domain. |
| `signed_up_seller_org_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → Organization (§4.2.1) | Resolved Seller Org. |
| `bid_response_submitted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when the vendor submits any bid response to this evaluation. |
| `growth_loop_execution_id` | UUID (FK) | → GrowthLoopExecution (§48.2.12); required | Linked L1 GrowthLoopExecution row. |
| `signal_integrity_flags` | Array[Enum] | Per §48.2.12 enum; empty default | SIM-populated. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | Standard | Standard pattern | Standard. |

**Scope isolation.** Workspace-scoped on `workspace_id`; Org-scoped on `org_id`. The `vendor_email_resolved` and `vendor_name_supplied` are PII to the targeted vendor; the buyer Org has full read; cross-Org access is blocked at the API layer. The signed-up vendor's Seller Org gets a separate, opaque view (per §10.5 + §4.5 cross-console firewall): the vendor sees their bid invitation in their Seller Console (Bid Workspace) without seeing the M5 metadata directly.

**Required indexes.** `(workspace_id, redemption_status)`, `(inviter_user_id, created_at DESC)` (per-inviter throttle bookkeeping), `(vendor_email_domain, created_at DESC)` (per-target-domain throttle bookkeeping per §48.2.2 L1), `(target_account_id)` UNIQUE, `(growth_loop_execution_id)` (links to L1 ledger), `(attribution_window_expires_at) WHERE redemption_status='pending'` (nightly expiry sweep).

**Retention.** Workspace-life + 7 years per L1 attribution-audit semantics. PII pseudonymization on DSAR.

##### BuyerPullVendorInvite Lifecycle State Machine

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `pending` | M5 row written + email queued | All pre-issuance gates pass | Default initial state. |
| (init) | `suppressed_pre_send` | §48.4.8 SuppressionList OR §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out match | Suppression check fires | Forensic row; no email. |
| `pending` | `clicked` | Magic-link click recorded | Pre-signup interaction | L1 `growth_loop_l1_invite_clicked` fires. |
| `clicked` | `signed_up_within_window` | Vendor SSO completes within 60d attribution window | Per §48.2.2 L1 attribution semantics | `signed_up_at`, `signed_up_seller_org_id` populated; L1 GrowthLoopExecution → `in_progress`. |
| `pending` | `signed_up_within_window` | Vendor signs up directly (skipping click) within 60d | Per §48.2.2 L1 attribution-ambiguity-resolution | Race-resolved via nightly attribution job. |
| `signed_up_within_window` | `bid_response_submitted` | Vendor submits any bid response to this evaluation | Bid Workspace `phase ∈ {6, 7, 8, 9, 10}` | `bid_response_submitted_at` populated; L1 GrowthLoopExecution → `converted`. |
| `clicked` | `signed_up_outside_window` | SSO completes after 60d window | Late signup; not L1-credited | Per §48.2.2 — signup creates Seller Org but no buyer attribution. |
| `pending` | `bounced_undeliverable` | Loops.so reports bounce | Hard bounce | Inviter notified via `m5.invite.bounced`. |
| `pending`, `clicked` | `expired_unredeemed` | 60d attribution window closes | `now > attribution_window_expires_at` | L1 GrowthLoopExecution → `expired`. |
| `pending`, `clicked` | `revoked_by_inviter` | Inviter / Workspace Owner DELETE | Caller holds eligible role | Cascades to Target Account if vendor has not yet bid. |
| `pending`, `clicked` | `revoked_by_ops` | Ops DELETE | `ops_security_admin` OR §48.2.12.4 GrowthLoopKillSwitch fires | Cascades. |
| `signed_up_within_window`, `bid_response_submitted`, `signed_up_outside_window`, `expired_unredeemed`, `revoked_*`, `bounced_undeliverable`, `suppressed_pre_send` | (terminal) | n/a | Append-only | New invitations require new BuyerPullVendorInvite rows. |

**Invariants.** (a) The M5 row's `redemption_status` mirrors the linked L1 GrowthLoopExecution lifecycle per §48.2.2; divergence raises `analytics_invariant_violation`. (b) `growth_loop_execution_id` is non-null on every M5 row (the L1 row is created atomically with the M5 row per §48.5.5 Workflow step 5).

#### Workflow

1. **Pre-issuance gate.** UI verifies (a) inviter holds an eligible role; (b) `workspace.phase ∈ {4, 5, 6}`; (c) per-inviter throttle: 20 M5 invites/user/30 days per §48.2.2 L1 control #1 (HTTP 429 `growth_loop_l1_throttle_exhausted` on breach with `throttle_kind=per_user`); (d) per-target-domain throttle: 5 distinct buyer Orgs/30 days per `vendor_email_domain` per §48.2.2 L1 control #2 (HTTP 429 with `throttle_kind=per_target_domain` AND deferred-send queue for the 6th-onward); (e) §48.4.3 shared-use-domain check (HTTP 422 if rejected); (f) §48.4.8 SuppressionList lookup (HTTP 422 generic non-leak); (g) §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out registry check (silent suppress).
2. **Inviter fills M5 modal.** Fields: vendor name (required); vendor website OR vendor email (one required; if only website is supplied, Sourcera triggers a Firecrawl-based email discovery in step 3); category (dropdown referencing §4.4.7 Marketplace Category, optional); evaluation close-by date (required, ≥ 7 days from today per §10.6 minimum-bidding-window rule); outreach template kind selector with previews; buyer anonymity selector (default `fully_anonymous`); custom-message body if applicable.
3. **Email discovery (when only website supplied).** §22.6 Firecrawl crawls the vendor's homepage + `/contact`, `/about`, `/team` URLs looking for `mailto:` patterns AND inferring `vendor_email_resolved` per a deterministic heuristic ranking: (1) explicit `mailto:` on `/contact`; (2) explicit `mailto:` on homepage; (3) generic `info@`, `sales@`, `hello@`, `partnerships@`, `procurement@` at the vendor's domain. Sets `email_discovery_method` + `email_discovery_confidence_score`. Confidence < 0.5 surfaces a buyer-confirmation modal: "We're not certain this is the right contact — please confirm or supply manually."
4. **Server validation.** Re-runs all gates atomically (race-safe).
5. **Row write + Target Account create + L1 GrowthLoopExecution row create.** BuyerPullVendorInvite written; underlying Target Account written per §10.5; GrowthLoopExecution row written per §48.2.2 L1 with `loop_id=vendor_invite_creates_account` AND `metadata_json.invitation_kind=m5_buyer_pull`. The three writes are atomic per §32.8 transactional patterns.
6. **Email send.** Loops.so adapter (§41.1) sends with the resolved template + payload; the email body NEVER includes the buyer Org name unless `buyer_anonymity_kind=named_buyer`. The from-address is `noreply-m5@sourcera.io` + display name "Sourcera on behalf of a buyer evaluation"; reply-to is a Sourcera-managed inbox that routes responses to the buyer's Workspace Inbox per §20. The email DKIM-signs with Sourcera keys per §48.4.2.
7. **Outreach template — default anonymized body.** Subject: "{Category} evaluation — bidding closes {close_by_date}"; body summarizes: "A buyer in the {industry} space ({company size band, if `industry_size_band_only`}) is evaluating {category} solutions. They've added you to the shortlist. The evaluation closes on {close_by_date}. Click below to set up your free Sourcera account, see the requirements, and submit your response." CTA: magic link.
8. **Recipient receives + clicks magic link.** Standard L1 redemption flow per §48.2.2: the vendor signs up via Google/Microsoft SSO, lands in their Seller Console with the bid auto-attached, and may bootstrap their KB per §22 (1 lifetime free per Seller Org per Summary C.73).
9. **Attribution.** L1 GrowthLoopExecution lifecycle proceeds per §48.2.2; the M5 row's `redemption_status` mirrors the L1 lifecycle states.
10. **Reply handling.** If the vendor REPLIES to the email instead of clicking the magic link, the reply lands in the Sourcera-managed reply inbox; an Ops parser routes the reply text to the Workspace Inbox AND surfaces a Pulse card to the inviter. The vendor reply does NOT auto-create a Seller Org; the buyer-side Workspace Owner sees the reply and may either re-send the magic link OR re-route the conversation to the existing Marketplace EOI flow if appropriate.
11. **Expiry / Revocation.** Standard L1 semantics; M5-row state mirrors.

#### UX Surfaces

| Surface | §3.3 Pattern | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| "Add Vendor → Invite Vendor Not Yet on Sourcera" button (Phase 4/5/6 vendor-discovery surface) | `Sidebar Navigation + Modal` per §3.3 | Two paths: Marketplace search OR M5 invite. |
| M5 Invite Modal | `Modal + Multi-Step Wizard` per §3.3 | Step 1: vendor identity; Step 2: category + close-by; Step 3: outreach template + anonymity; Step 4: preview. |
| Email-discovery confirmation modal (when confidence < 0.5) | `Modal + Confirmation` per §3.3 | "We found {email}; is this correct?" with edit field. |
| Pulse card on vendor reply | `In-App Inbox` per §20 | "Vendor responded by email — view in Workspace Inbox." |
| Throttle exhaustion error toast | `Toast + Inline` per §3.3 | Surfaces the specific throttle (per-user vs per-target-domain) + Retry-After. |
| Mobile parity | Per §3.4 | Wizard becomes full-screen sequential pages. |

#### Data Collected / Retained

Per the field table; same DSAR + retention semantics as M1 with the addition of `growth_loop_execution_id` linkage to the §48.2.12 ledger.

#### Anti-Abuse Controls

1. **Per-inviter throttle: 20 invites/user/30 days.** §48.2.2 L1 control #1; HTTP 429 on breach with `Retry-After` AND JSON body `{throttle_kind: 'per_user', next_allowed_at}`.
2. **Per-target-domain throttle: 5 distinct buyer Orgs/30 days per `vendor_email_domain`.** §48.2.2 L1 control #2; the 6th buyer attempting to invite the same vendor domain in the rolling 30d window is accepted but routed to a deferred-send queue with `growth_loop_l1_target_throttled` event AND notification to Ops review queue. The buyer is informed: "This vendor is being invited by multiple buyers; your invite is queued pending Ops review (typically 24h)."
3. **§48.4.3 shared-use-domain rejection.** `vendor_email_domain` matched against the registry; gmail.com / outlook.com / etc. REJECTED at write with HTTP 422 `growth_loop_l1_invite_shared_use_domain_rejected` AND a friendly explanatory message: "Personal email domains aren't supported for vendor invitations. Please ask the vendor for their corporate email."
4. **DMARC preflight (§48.4.2).** A buyer Org with `dmarc_alignment_pass_rate < 0.85` (rolling 7d) routes M5 invites to the Sourcera neutral From: address (no send-on-behalf-of) AND emits `growth_loop_l1_dmarc_preflight_failed`.
5. **§4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out registry.** Opted-out vendors are silently suppressed; buyer sees the generic non-leak error.
6. **§48.4.8 SuppressionList lookup.** Hard reject with non-leak.
7. **§48.4.4 content validators on `custom_message_body`.** XSS, PII detector, profanity classifier, off-topic spam classifier.
8. **Custom-message-body length cap (1,000 chars).** Prevents abuse via message stuffing.
9. **Email-discovery confidence floor for automated send.** If `email_discovery_confidence_score < 0.3`, the system REFUSES auto-send AND requires buyer manual confirmation per §48.5.5 step 3 confirmation modal.
10. **SIM cross-loop velocity anomaly.** Per §48.2.2 L1 control #6 — buyer Orgs with > 4× cohort 95th-percentile invite velocity trigger `growth_loop_velocity_anomaly_detected` AND become Ops-kill-switch eligible.
11. **Reply-handler PII sanitization.** Vendor email replies are scrubbed for embedded malicious content (XSS, executable links) before insertion into the Workspace Inbox per §48.4.4.

#### Plan Gating & Entitlement

M5 is included on every Buyer plan tier with the per-user throttle (20/user/30d) being universal. The throttle is a §48.4 anti-abuse cap, NOT a plan-tier monetization lever — Sourcera explicitly does NOT charge for M5 invitations because the loop is the platform's primary supply-side viral coefficient. Free-tier buyers have the same throttle as Enterprise. The §5.11 Feature Access Matrix is updated to grant M5 to `workspace_owner`, `evaluation_lead`, `use_case_lead`.

#### Telemetry Events

Per §48.2.2 L1 telemetry events, plus M5-specific:

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `m5_invite_modal_opened` | M5 modal rendered | `workspace_id`, `phase`, `inviter_user_id` |
| `m5_email_discovery_attempted` | Firecrawl-based discovery initiated | `vendor_website_domain_hash`, `discovery_method`, `confidence_score` |
| `m5_email_discovery_confirmation_shown` | Confidence < 0.5 → modal | `discovery_confidence_score` |
| `m5_invite_sent` | M5 row written + Target Account created + L1 GrowthLoopExecution created + email queued | `m5_invite_id`, `target_account_id`, `growth_loop_execution_id`, `outreach_template_kind`, `buyer_anonymity_kind`, `email_discovery_method` |
| `m5_invite_throttle_exhausted_per_user` | Per-user 20/30d cap hit | `inviter_user_id`, `attempted_count`, `next_allowed_at` |
| `m5_invite_throttle_exhausted_per_target_domain` | Per-target-domain 5/30d cap hit | `vendor_email_domain_hash`, `attempted_buyer_org_count`, `deferred_send_eta` |
| `m5_invite_email_reply_routed` | Vendor replied to email, reply routed to Workspace Inbox | `m5_invite_id`, `reply_text_length`, `pii_redaction_applied` (Boolean) |

L1 events (`growth_loop_l1_invite_emitted`, `growth_loop_l1_invite_clicked`, `growth_loop_l1_signup_attributed`, etc.) ALSO fire per §48.2.2 with `metadata_json.invitation_kind=m5_buyer_pull` distinguishing M5 from direct invitations.

#### Notifications Fired

| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `m5.invite.sent` | Inviter | In-App | Immediate | "{Vendor Name} has been invited." |
| `m5.invite.bounced` | Inviter | In-App + Email | Immediate | Per L1 bounce semantics. |
| `m5.invite.signed_up` | Workspace Owner, inviter | In-App + Email | Immediate | "{Vendor} signed up and is reviewing the bid requirements." |
| `m5.invite.bid_response_submitted` | Workspace Owner, Use Case Lead | In-App + Email | Immediate | Inherits from `response_submitted` (Appendix C existing) but tagged with M5 attribution. |
| `m5.invite.email_reply_routed` | Inviter | In-App | Immediate | "Vendor replied by email; view in Workspace Inbox." |
| `m5.invite.deferred_pending_ops_review` | Inviter | In-App | Immediate | "Your invite to {vendor} is queued — multiple buyers are inviting them; we'll send within 24h." |

#### Webhooks Fired

Per §48.2.2 L1 webhook events with M5-tag.

| Webhook event_type | Trigger | Payload Highlights |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `growth.m5.invite.sent` | M5 row written | `m5_invite_id`, `workspace_id`, `growth_loop_execution_id`, `vendor_email_domain_hash` |
| `growth.m5.invite.signed_up` | Vendor signs up | `m5_invite_id`, `signed_up_seller_org_id`, `growth_loop_execution_id` |
