#### API Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth Scope | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `POST` | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/workspaces/{workspace_id}/m5-invites` | `write:workspaces` + role in {`workspace_owner`, `evaluation_lead`, `use_case_lead`} | Issue M5 invite. Idempotency-Key supported. |
| `GET` | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/workspaces/{workspace_id}/m5-invites` | `read:workspaces` + roles + `org_owner` | List per-Workspace invites. |
| `GET` | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/workspaces/{workspace_id}/m5-invites/{m5_invite_id}` | Same | Fetch one. |
| `POST` | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/workspaces/{workspace_id}/m5-invites/{m5_invite_id}/resend` | `write:workspaces` + same roles | Resend; respects throttles. |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/workspaces/{workspace_id}/m5-invites/{m5_invite_id}` | Same OR Ops | Revoke; cascades to Target Account if vendor has not yet bid. |
| `POST` | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/workspaces/{workspace_id}/m5-invites/email-discovery-preview` | `read:workspaces` + same roles | Preview email-discovery without committing — surfaces `email_discovery_method` + `confidence_score` for buyer confirmation. |

New error codes: `m5_invite_phase_out_of_window` (HTTP 422), `m5_invite_close_by_date_too_soon` (HTTP 422; ≥ 7-day rule per §10.6), `m5_invite_email_discovery_confidence_below_floor` (HTTP 422 — requires manual confirmation), `m5_invite_custom_message_content_validator_failed` (HTTP 422 — per-validator error sub-detail).

(All §48.2.2 L1 error codes also apply: `growth_loop_l1_throttle_exhausted` (HTTP 429), `growth_loop_l1_invite_shared_use_domain_rejected` (HTTP 422), `growth_loop_anti_spam_target_suppressed` (HTTP 422), `growth_loop_l1_dmarc_preflight_failed` (HTTP 422).)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. M5 issuance MUST be hard-gated to `workspace.phase ∈ {4, 5, 6}`; outside the window MUST return HTTP 422 `m5_invite_phase_out_of_window`.
2. The per-inviter throttle (20/user/30d) MUST be enforced atomically; HTTP 429 with `throttle_kind=per_user` AND `next_allowed_at` per §48.2.2 L1 contract.
3. The per-target-domain throttle (5 distinct buyer Orgs/30d per `vendor_email_domain`) MUST be enforced atomically; the 6th buyer's invite MUST be deferred-send-queued AND emit `growth_loop_l1_target_throttled`; the buyer MUST be notified via `m5.invite.deferred_pending_ops_review`.
4. Shared-use-domain emails MUST be rejected at write with HTTP 422; QA test `m5_shared_use_domain_rejection` asserts.
5. The email send MUST NEVER include the buyer Org name when `buyer_anonymity_kind ∈ {fully_anonymous, industry_size_band_only}`; QA test `m5_anonymity_no_leak` asserts on every PR touching the M5 send template.
6. The L1 GrowthLoopExecution row MUST be created atomically with the BuyerPullVendorInvite row AND the Target Account; failure of any of the three rolls back all three per §32.8 transactional contract.
7. Email-discovery confidence < 0.3 MUST require buyer manual confirmation; auto-send MUST be refused.
8. Custom-message content MUST pass §48.4.4 validators before send; failures return per-validator error sub-detail.
9. Vendor reply emails MUST be routed to the Workspace Inbox within 60 seconds of receipt at the Sourcera reply-inbox AND MUST pass through PII sanitization per §48.4.4.
10. The full M5 funnel `m5_invite_sent → growth_loop_l1_invite_clicked → growth_loop_l1_signup_attributed → growth_loop_l1_first_bid_completed` MUST be PostHog-Insights-Funnels queryable per `org_id`, per `inviter_user_id`, AND per `vendor_email_domain_hash` (cohort).
11. SIM velocity-anomaly detection (per §48.2.2 control #6) MUST flag M5-source velocity separately from direct-invite velocity for forensic clarity.
12. The Ops Console MUST be able to globally pause M5 sends for a specific Org within 60 seconds via §48.2.12.4 GrowthLoopKillSwitch with `scope=org` AND `loop_id=vendor_invite_creates_account` AND `reason_note` requiring justification.

#### Failure Modes Addressed

1. **Buyer-supplied vendor email is to a personal address (founder@gmail.com) for a small startup vendor.** Resolved: §48.4.3 shared-use-domain rejection at write; HTTP 422 with friendly explainer "Personal email domains aren't supported. Ask the vendor for their corporate email." The buyer can either (a) ask the vendor for a corporate address OR (b) use the website-only path which Firecrawl-discovers a corporate email.
2. **Multiple buyer Orgs simultaneously invite the same niche vendor (same `vendor_email_domain`) in the same week.** Resolved: per-target-domain throttle defers 6th-onward invite; the 6th buyer is informed transparently. After 30d window resets, subsequent invites flow normally. Authoring extension: the deferred queue auto-releases at 24h cooldown per Ops policy; sustained queue depth raises §48.4.10 SIM warning.
3. **Vendor's email address has a typo and bounces; buyer doesn't notice for 2 weeks.** Resolved: bounce notification fires immediately to inviter via `m5.invite.bounced`; the inviter sees a Pulse card; the bounced row is excluded from `phase_4_vendor_count_active` per §10.5; on Phase 6 entry (bidding open), all bounced M5 invites are surfaced in a Pulse digest "{N} of your invited vendors did not receive their invitation — please correct or remove."
4. **Custom message body contains a competitive slur or false claim against a rival vendor.** Resolved: §48.4.4 content validators (off-topic spam + profanity classifier) flag at write; the buyer is shown a remediation message AND the send is blocked. Repeat violations accumulate via §48.4.10 SIM `content_validator_repeat_offender` with auto-kill-switch eligibility.
5. **Vendor signs up via M5 magic link AND the same vendor is also invited via M17 Pro Trial Seat from the same buyer.** Resolved: per §48.2.2 attribution-ambiguity-resolution semantics, the FIRST GrowthLoopExecution row created (chronologically) wins primary attribution; the second is recorded as `metadata_json.cross_loop_attribution[]` per §48.2.13 AC #7. The vendor's experience is unchanged — they receive M17's Pro Trial entitlement IF the M17 invitation took precedence.

### 48.5.6 M6 Domain-Based Auto-Join {#48.5.6-m6-domain-based-auto-join}

#### Purpose

M6 reduces the friction of onboarding the Nth employee at a corporate buyer by allowing employees of a verified corporate domain to auto-join the Org as pending-approval members on signup. The mechanic exists because a typical enterprise procurement team has 10–40 people who might touch a Sourcera Workspace over the course of a year; forcing each to be individually invited creates friction AND fragmentation (employees create accidental personal Orgs with their work emails). M6 eliminates both: an employee signing up with `@buyer-co.com` is auto-attached as a pending-approval member of BuyerCo's verified Sourcera Org; an Org Owner / Org Admin approves or rejects via a queue; reversible within 30 days per Summary C.64. M6 is the active replacement for the retired L6 Loop (§48.2.7), together with M7 (§48.5.7).

**Source authority.** Summary C.64; §6.4 Domain Governance (pre-existing); Summary C.104 Domain Claiming & Verification.

#### Trigger

A new user signs up (Google / Microsoft SSO per §6.1) with an email whose domain matches a verified DomainAutoJoinClaim row (see entity schema below) belonging to a buyer Org that has `domain_auto_join_enabled=true`. The new user's SSO completion handler checks the registry BEFORE provisioning a fresh Org; if a match is found, the user is routed down the M6 auto-join path rather than the default `new_org_provisioned` path.

#### Actor & Entity Schema

**Acting entity.** The Sourcera platform (auto-join is system-orchestrated); the buyer Org's Org Owner / Org Admin approves or rejects pending-approval members downstream.

**Targeted entity.** The new user signing up AND the matched buyer Org.

**New entity: DomainAutoJoinClaim (Org-Scoped, Buyer-Only).** Represents a buyer Org's claim to a specific corporate domain for the purpose of M6 auto-join. The domain MUST have been verified per §6.4 / Summary C.104 (DNS TXT record) before the claim becomes active. One DomainAutoJoinClaim row per `(org_id, domain)`; an Org may claim multiple domains (e.g., `buyer-co.com` + `buyer-co.co.uk` + `buyer-co-subsidiary.com`).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK, immutable | Standard. |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | → Organization (§4.2.1); buyer Org; required | RBAC scope. |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer` (fixed) | M6 is buyer-only. |
| `domain` | String | 1–253 chars; lowercased; RFC-1035-compliant; required; UNIQUE platform-wide | The verified corporate domain. Wildcard subdomains NOT supported in v7.0.0 (authored extension; see Known Gaps). |
| `domain_verification_method` | Enum | Appendix J `m6_domain_verification_method` (new): `dns_txt_record`, `email_handshake_verified_at_domain`, `ops_imposed_with_evidence` | How the claim was verified. Summary C.104 specifies DNS TXT as canonical; email handshake is an authored extension for small-org cases. |
| `domain_verified_at` | Timestamp | Required | When verification completed. |
| `domain_verified_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | → User (§4.2.3); required | Verifier; must hold `org_owner` OR `org_admin` at verification time. |
| `auto_join_enabled` | Boolean | Default: true on claim creation | Can be toggled off without revoking the underlying domain verification. |
| `default_member_role` | Enum | Appendix J `m6_default_member_role` (new): `member_pending_approval`, `member_active` (Ops-override only) | Default: `member_pending_approval` (requires Org Admin to activate; SUM C.64 explicit). Ops MAY set `member_active` only for contractually-approved large-enterprise customers who request zero-friction auto-join. |
| `approval_queue_notification_recipients` | Array[Enum] | Appendix J: `org_owner`, `org_admin`, custom_user_id; ≤ 10 entries | Who gets notified of pending-approval joins. Default: `[org_owner, org_admin]` aggregated. |
| `shared_use_domain_exclusion_checked_at` | Timestamp | Required | Last time the claim was re-verified against the §48.4.3 Shared-Use-Domain Registry. |
| `sim_hold_reason` | Enum | Appendix J `m6_sim_hold_reason` (new): `none`, `shared_use_domain_detected`, `velocity_anomaly`, `ops_manual_hold`, `legal_dispute`, `duplicate_claim_detected` | Populated by §48.4.10 Signal Integrity Monitor. |
| `sim_held_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When SIM placed a hold. |
| `first_auto_join_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set on the first auto-join via this claim. |
| `total_auto_joins_count` | Integer | ≥ 0; default 0 | Lifetime auto-joins via this claim. |
| `auto_joins_last_30d` | Integer | ≥ 0; default 0 | Rolling counter; updated nightly. |
| `revocable_until` | Timestamp | Required; computed: `created_at + 30 days` | The 30-day Org Owner reversibility window per Summary C.64. |
| `revoked_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set on claim revocation. |
| `revoked_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → User (§4.2.3) | Org Owner / Org Admin / Ops. |
| `revoked_reason` | Enum | Appendix J `m6_revoked_reason` (new): `org_owner_reversal`, `shared_use_domain_detected`, `legal_request`, `ops_security_action`, `duplicate_claim_resolved`, `other` | Required when `revoked_at` non-null. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | Standard | Standard pattern | `created_by` MUST hold `org_owner` OR `org_admin` at claim time. |

**New entity: DomainAutoJoinEvent (Org-Scoped, Cross-Console-Visible, Append-Only Audit Row).** Every auto-join transaction produces one row for the Org's audit trail.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK, immutable | Standard. |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | → Organization (§4.2.1); required | The target Org. |
| `claim_id` | UUID (FK) | → DomainAutoJoinClaim (this section); required | Matched claim. |
| `joined_user_id` | UUID (FK) | → User (§4.2.3); required | The auto-joined user. |
| `joined_email_domain` | String | Max 253 chars; lowercased; denormalized | Stored for audit. |
| `initial_role` | Enum | `member_pending_approval` OR `member_active` | The role assigned at join. |
| `approved_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when Org Admin approves the pending member. |
| `approved_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → User (§4.2.3) | Approver. |
| `rejected_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set on rejection. |
| `rejected_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → User (§4.2.3) | Rejecter. |
| `rejected_reason` | Enum | Appendix J `m6_rejected_reason` (new): `not_a_real_employee`, `former_employee`, `incorrect_org`, `spam_attempt`, `other` | Required when `rejected_at` non-null. |
| `reverted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set if the Org Owner reverts the auto-join within `revocable_until`. |
| `reverted_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable | Reverter. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | Standard | Standard pattern | Standard. |

**Scope isolation.** DomainAutoJoinClaim is Org-scoped; DomainAutoJoinEvent is Org-scoped AND references the user identity. Cross-Org enumeration is blocked: one Org cannot see another Org's claims OR auto-join events. The `domain` field's UNIQUE constraint across all rows is the mechanism by which duplicate-claim conflicts are detected (see Duplicate Claim Resolution below).

**Required indexes.** `(domain)` UNIQUE, `(org_id, auto_join_enabled)`, `(sim_hold_reason)` (sparse), `(revocable_until) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL` (nightly window-expiry sweep), `(claim_id, created_at DESC)` on DomainAutoJoinEvent, `(joined_user_id)` on DomainAutoJoinEvent.

**Retention.** Org-life + 7 years. DSAR pseudonymization on `joined_user_id`, `created_by`, `revoked_by_user_id`, `approved_by_user_id`, `rejected_by_user_id`, `reverted_by_user_id`.

##### DomainAutoJoinClaim Lifecycle State Machine

The claim's effective state is computed from `domain_verified_at`, `auto_join_enabled`, `sim_hold_reason`, and `revoked_at`.

| From (Computed State) | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `pending_dns_verification` | POST claim | Pre-write gates pass (shared-use check, UNIQUE collision check, reclaim cooldown) | DNS TXT record displayed to inviter; 10-min poll begins. |
| `pending_dns_verification` | `verified_active` | DNS TXT poll succeeds | TXT record found at the buyer's domain | `domain_verified_at` populated; auto-join begins. |
| `pending_dns_verification` | `verification_failed` | DNS TXT poll fails after N retries | Retry count exceeded | Inviter notified; MAY retry verification OR delete the row. |
| `verified_active` | `verified_disabled` | PATCH `auto_join_enabled=false` | Caller holds eligible role | Auto-join paused; existing memberships unaffected; verification preserved. |
| `verified_disabled` | `verified_active` | PATCH `auto_join_enabled=true` | Caller holds eligible role | Auto-join resumes. |
| `verified_active`, `verified_disabled` | `sim_held` | §48.4.10 SIM emits `velocity_anomaly` OR nightly shared-use re-scan match OR Ops manual hold | `sim_hold_reason ∈ {velocity_anomaly, shared_use_domain_detected, ops_manual_hold, legal_dispute, duplicate_claim_detected}` | Auto-join paused; Org notified via `m6.claim.sim_hold`. |
| `sim_held` | `verified_active` | Ops clears hold | `sim_hold_reason → none`; `ops_growth_admin` action | Auto-join resumes. |
| `verified_active`, `verified_disabled`, `sim_held` | `revoked_by_org_owner` | DELETE within 30d window | Caller holds `org_owner` OR `org_admin`; `now ≤ revocable_until` | All `approved_at IS NULL` DomainAutoJoinEvent rows auto-revert. |
| `verified_active`, `verified_disabled`, `sim_held` | `revoked_by_ops` | Ops DELETE | `ops_security_admin` OR `ops_growth_admin` | Same revert semantics; reason logged. |
| `revoked_*`, `verification_failed` | (terminal) | n/a | Append-only | Re-claim by same Org subject to 90d cooldown; different Org may claim immediately. |
| `revoked_*` (Ops) | `verified_active` | Ops emergency un-revoke | Rare; `ops_security_admin` action with audit | NOT a customer path; Ops-only data-correction. |

##### DomainAutoJoinEvent Lifecycle State Machine

| From (Computed State) | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `pending_approval` | M6 auto-join provisioning fires | New User signup matched a claim with `member_pending_approval` default | User has read-only Org Directory access; no Workspace reads. |
| (init) | `active` | M6 auto-join provisioning fires | New User signup matched a claim with Ops-override `member_active` default | User has full Org default-seat-role access. |
| `pending_approval` | `approved` | Org Admin POST approve | Caller holds `org_owner` OR `org_admin` | User role transitions to default seat role per §5.2. |
| `pending_approval` | `rejected` | Org Admin POST reject | Caller holds same; `rejected_reason` required | User offered fresh single-user Org path. |
| `pending_approval`, `approved` | `reverted` | Org Owner POST revert within 30d window | `now ≤ DomainAutoJoinClaim.revocable_until` | User's Org membership removed; user offered fresh single-user Org. |
| `approved`, `rejected`, `reverted` | (terminal) | n/a | Append-only | Re-join requires new SSO signup OR direct Workspace invite. |

**Invariants.** (a) `approved_at` non-null IFF state ∈ {`approved`}; (b) `rejected_at` non-null IFF state ∈ {`rejected`}; (c) `reverted_at` non-null IFF state ∈ {`reverted`}; (d) The `reverted` state may follow `pending_approval` OR `approved` but NOT `rejected` (rejected is terminal-from-init).

#### Duplicate Claim Resolution

Because `DomainAutoJoinClaim.domain` is UNIQUE platform-wide, two buyer Orgs cannot both claim `buyer-co.com`. The resolution protocol:

| Scenario | Resolution |
| :---- | :---- |
| Both Orgs attempt to claim simultaneously | First-writer-wins at the UNIQUE index level; second returns HTTP 409 `m6_domain_already_claimed` with the claimant-org-id's public display name (if the losing claimant is a member of the winning claimant's Org, they are redirected to "Join the existing Org"). |
| Legitimate M&A scenario: BuyerCo acquires SubCo; SubCo's domain (`subco.com`) was previously claimed by SubCo's existing Org | Ops-mediated claim transfer per §43 Admin Tooling; transfer requires evidence (M&A filing public record OR Sourcera Sales-Ops sign-off per `ops_manual_domain_transfer_approved` audit event). |
| Bad-faith claim: a consulting firm verifies `big-client.com` via rogue DNS access | §48.4.10 SIM escalation path; if a claim's `auto_joins_last_30d` exhibits a pattern inconsistent with the claimant Org's `seats_count` (e.g., 200 auto-joins for a 3-seat org), the SIM emits `m6_velocity_anomaly` AND the claim is auto-held pending Ops review. Ops revocation of a bad-faith claim automatically reverts all auto-joins made under it within the prior 30 days. |

#### Workflow

1. **Claim creation.** Org Owner or Org Admin initiates a domain claim from Org Settings > Domain Governance (§6.4). UI presents three verification paths: (a) DNS TXT record (canonical); (b) Email handshake verification at the domain (user must receive + click a verification email sent to `admin@{domain}` OR `postmaster@{domain}`); (c) Ops-imposed for contractually-approved enterprise customers.
2. **Shared-use-domain check at claim write.** The `domain` is matched against §48.4.3 Shared-Use-Domain Registry. If match → HTTP 422 `m6_domain_shared_use_rejected` with explainer: "Shared-use domains (gmail.com, outlook.com, etc.) cannot be claimed for auto-join." SIM emits `m6_shared_use_domain_attempt` for forensic forensics.
3. **DNS TXT verification.** Sourcera generates a verification TXT record (e.g., `sourcera-verify-01HXYZ...`) that the Org Admin places in the domain's DNS. Sourcera checks every 10 minutes via standard DNS lookup; first successful resolution sets `domain_verified_at`.
4. **Claim activation.** On verification, the row is written with `auto_join_enabled=true` AND `default_member_role=member_pending_approval`. Ops-override for `member_active` requires `ops_growth_admin` sign-off per §48.4.10 SIM posture.
5. **30-day reversibility window.** `revocable_until = created_at + 30 days` per Summary C.64. During this window, the Org Owner MAY unilaterally revoke the claim AND auto-revert all DomainAutoJoinEvent rows whose `approved_at IS NULL` (pending-approval joins). Revocation outside the window requires the standard Ops path (rare).
6. **New user signup triggers M6 check.** The SSO completion handler: (a) extracts the email's domain; (b) queries DomainAutoJoinClaim for `WHERE domain=X AND auto_join_enabled=true AND revoked_at IS NULL AND sim_hold_reason='none'`; (c) if match → M6 auto-join path; else → default `new_org_provisioned` path.
7. **M6 auto-join provisioning.** Server: (a) creates the User row per §6.1; (b) attaches the User to the matched Org with role `default_member_role` (almost always `member_pending_approval`); (c) writes a DomainAutoJoinEvent row; (d) notifies the Org's `approval_queue_notification_recipients` via `m6.auto_join.pending_approval` notification (Appendix C extension below); (e) shows the user an interstitial: "Welcome! Your company's Sourcera Org is active. An Org Admin will approve your membership shortly — we'll notify you when you have full access. Meanwhile, here's a tour of the platform." The user has read-only access to the Org Directory (names + roles) AND public Marketplace content; they cannot read any Workspace data until approval.
8. **Pending-approval queue.** Org Admin views Settings > Members > Pending Approvals. Each row shows the joining user's name, email, SSO provider, signup timestamp, and optional context (if M7 Suggested Team Discovery signals indicate the user is a known colleague — see §48.5.7). Admin clicks Approve or Reject; rejection requires a reason code.
9. **Approval outcomes.** Approval: the User's role transitions to the Org's default seat role per §5.2 (usually `member`); Workspace access is granted per Org settings (default: no automatic Workspace access; Workspace Owners must add them). Rejection: the User is offered the default `new_org_provisioned` path (a fresh single-user Org) OR the option to abandon and sign out.
10. **30-day reversibility.** Within `revocable_until`, the Org Owner MAY undo any M6 auto-join even after approval. Reversal: (a) removes the User's Org membership; (b) re-routes the User to a fresh single-user Org; (c) logs `reverted_at` + `reverted_by_user_id` on the DomainAutoJoinEvent; (d) notifies the User via `m6.auto_join.reverted`. Post-30-day reversals require the standard user-removal path per §5.2.
11. **Shared-use-domain periodic re-check.** Nightly job at 02:30 UTC re-matches every active claim's `domain` against the Shared-Use-Domain Registry; new matches (if the registry was expanded) transition the claim to `sim_hold_reason=shared_use_domain_detected` AND notify the Org. SIM emits `m6_claim_shared_use_detection_post_hoc`.
12. **SIM velocity anomaly.** Per-claim nightly computation of `auto_joins_last_30d / seats_count` ratio. Anomalous ratios (e.g., > 10× cohort median) set `sim_hold_reason=velocity_anomaly` AND pause further auto-joins pending Ops review per §48.4.10. The Signal Integrity Monitor is the canonical surface for Ops to adjudicate M6 holds per Summary C.100.

#### UX Surfaces

| Surface | §3.3 Pattern | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Claim domain flow (Org Settings > Domain Governance) | `Sidebar Navigation + Multi-Step Form` per §3.3 | DNS TXT record display with copy button; poll-every-10-min verification progress indicator. |
| Pending-Approvals queue (Settings > Members > Pending Approvals) | `Inline Table + Action Bar` per §3.3 | Per-row Approve / Reject buttons; bulk approve / reject via checkbox selection. |
| Auto-joined user interstitial post-SSO | `Full-Page Splash + Single CTA` per §3.3 | Welcome message + "Your membership is pending" + platform tour CTA. |
| Org Owner "Recent auto-joins" Pulse digest | `In-App Inbox` per §20 | Daily digest opt-in for active claims with ≥ 5 auto-joins in 24h. |
| SIM hold banner on claim | `Inline Alert` per §3.3 | Surfaces hold reason + Ops-contact CTA. |
| Mobile parity | Per §3.4 | Queue becomes card-stack on mobile. |

#### Data Collected / Retained

Per the two entity tables. Aggregate `total_auto_joins_count` and `auto_joins_last_30d` drive §48.3 Network Effects signals (M6 is a signal of M8 Org-Intelligence compounding). DSAR pseudonymization applies.

**Residency.** DomainAutoJoinClaim lives in the Org's data region per §1.6. The global UNIQUE index on `domain` lives in a globally-replicated read-only index for first-writer-wins arbitration; writes are coordinated via the platform's global coordination service with monotonic sequence numbers.

#### Anti-Abuse Controls

1. **§48.4.3 Shared-Use-Domain Registry — hard reject at claim write.** Per Summary C.64 explicit requirement.
2. **Nightly shared-use re-scan.** Catches registry expansions applied post-claim.
3. **§48.4.10 Signal Integrity Monitor (SIM) velocity-anomaly detection.** Flags `auto_joins / seats_count` anomalies. Per the task requirement, M6 MUST reference SIM — this control is the canonical SIM integration.
4. **First-writer-wins UNIQUE domain index.** Prevents duplicate-claim race conditions.
5. **Ops-mediated claim transfer.** Only Ops can transfer a verified claim from one Org to another (e.g., for M&A scenarios); not a customer-self-serve operation.
6. **30-day reversibility window.** Bounds the risk of a bad-faith claim: within 30d, the Org Owner can undo every auto-join atomically.
7. **`member_pending_approval` default gate.** Auto-joined users cannot read any Workspace content until an Org Admin approves.
8. **DNS TXT verification as canonical.** Minimizes verification fraud vs email-handshake methods.
9. **Ops-override for `member_active` default requires `ops_growth_admin`.** Per-customer contractually-approved only; not self-serve.
10. **Per-domain re-claim cooldown.** A revoked claim cannot be re-claimed by the same Org for 90 days (prevents abuse via cycle-claim-revoke-claim bypass). A different Org can immediately claim a released domain subject to the standard verification flow.

#### Plan Gating & Entitlement

M6 is included on every Buyer plan tier (Free → Enterprise) AND every Seller plan tier (Seller Free → Seller Enterprise). The mechanic is critical infrastructure for team scalability and is deliberately not gated. However, Ops-override for `member_active` default (bypassing the pending-approval gate) is Enterprise-only and requires contractual sign-off per §34.13-adjacent enterprise-contract clauses.

New error codes: `m6_domain_already_claimed` (HTTP 409), `m6_domain_shared_use_rejected` (HTTP 422), `m6_claim_sim_hold_active` (HTTP 403; operations blocked), `m6_claim_reclaim_cooldown_active` (HTTP 409; 90-day same-Org cooldown), `m6_domain_verification_pending` (HTTP 409; verification not complete), `m6_domain_verification_failed` (HTTP 422; DNS TXT not found after N retries), `m6_claim_revocable_window_expired` (HTTP 403; outside 30d), `m6_ops_transfer_evidence_required` (HTTP 422).

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. Shared-use-domain claims MUST be hard-rejected at write with HTTP 422 `m6_domain_shared_use_rejected`.
2. Nightly shared-use re-scan MUST re-match all active claims against the §48.4.3 registry within 24h of registry updates; matches MUST set `sim_hold_reason=shared_use_domain_detected` AND notify the Org.
3. UNIQUE `domain` constraint MUST prevent duplicate claims atomically; second-writer returns HTTP 409 `m6_domain_already_claimed`.
4. DNS TXT verification MUST poll every 10 min; manual re-verify endpoint MUST be available on-demand.
5. Default `member_pending_approval` role MUST gate all Workspace reads; QA test `m6_pending_approval_workspace_read_blocked` asserts.
6. The 30-day `revocable_until` window MUST be enforced server-side; post-window revocations require Ops; QA test `m6_revocable_window_enforcement` asserts.
7. SIM velocity-anomaly detection (§48.4.10) MUST evaluate `auto_joins_last_30d / seats_count` nightly; ratio > 10× cohort median MUST emit `sim_signal_emitted {signal_class=velocity_anomaly, severity=warning}` AND set `sim_hold_reason=velocity_anomaly`.
8. Claim reversal MUST atomically revert ALL DomainAutoJoinEvent rows for that claim whose `approved_at IS NULL` AND within the 30-day window; approved joins MUST use the standard `revert` flow per API.
9. 90-day reclaim cooldown MUST be enforced at claim write for the SAME Org; different Orgs may claim immediately.
10. The full M6 funnel `m6_claim_created → m6_claim_verified → m6_auto_join_completed → m6_auto_join_approved` MUST be PostHog-Insights-Funnels queryable per `org_id`.
11. Ops-mediated claim transfer MUST log `ops_manual_domain_transfer_approved` audit event with evidence-category tag per §4.6.1; evidence attachments MUST be retained 7 years.
12. M6 auto-join MUST NEVER grant access to any Workspace directly; Workspace-level access requires separate Workspace invite per §5.3.

#### Failure Modes Addressed

1. **Consulting firm claims `big-client.com` via rogue DNS access they obtained during a consulting engagement.** Resolved: §48.4.10 SIM velocity-anomaly detection catches the unusual `auto_joins / seats_count` ratio; Ops can revoke the claim AND atomically revert all auto-joins within 30 days. Post-30-day reversal requires Ops per-user removal per §5.2. Summary C.100 SIM is the canonical surveillance surface.
2. **Sourcera adds `proton.me` to the shared-use-domain registry AFTER a buyer has already claimed it via `proton.me`.** Resolved: nightly re-scan job sets `sim_hold_reason=shared_use_domain_detected`; the claim is paused (no new auto-joins) AND the Org is notified; Ops review with evidence (e.g., the buyer legitimately operates a `proton.me` corporate domain via Proton's Business plan) may clear the hold; typical resolution: the claim is revoked AND existing auto-joined members are individually notified + offered fresh-Org path.
3. **BuyerCo acquires SubCo mid-evaluation; BuyerCo wants to migrate SubCo's `subco.com` claim to their own Org.** Resolved: Ops-mediated claim transfer with M&A public-record evidence OR Sales-Ops sign-off per `ops_manual_domain_transfer_approved` audit event. The transfer is atomic: all pending-approval DomainAutoJoinEvent rows migrate to the target Org; approved members retain their Workspace memberships at the source Org (which usually persists briefly during M&A integration).
4. **User signs up with `@buyer-co.com` but legitimately wants a personal Sourcera Org (e.g., personal procurement learning).** Resolved: the M6 auto-join interstitial offers a "Don't auto-join — create a personal Sourcera account" escape hatch. If the user declines auto-join, they are routed to the default `new_org_provisioned` path; the DomainAutoJoinEvent row is NOT written; the Org admin is NOT notified.
5. **Org Owner revokes a claim 31 days after creation and wants to reverse it.** Resolved: revocations within 30 days are single-click customer-self-serve; post-30 days revocation is Ops-mediated per §43 Admin Tooling. The per-member removal is NOT atomic post-window — the Org Owner must remove each member individually OR Ops performs a bulk-remove with `ops_manual_bulk_member_removal` audit event.

### 48.5.7 M7 Suggested Team Discovery {#48.5.7-m7-suggested-team-discovery}

#### Purpose

M7 surfaces "your colleagues are on Sourcera" discovery cards to help buyer-side procurement teams discover peers at their same Org who are already active on the platform. The mechanic exists because a typical procurement organization has 10–40 people who might touch Sourcera over time, and enterprise procurement is a cross-team function (IT, Finance, Security, Legal, Compliance, HR, department owners) — each team of 5–10 people discovering Sourcera in a silo leads to fragmented Workspaces and duplicated effort. M7 is the active replacement for the retired L6 Loop (§48.2.7), together with M6. Summary C.65 specifies k-anonymity floor, per-user opt-out, and cross-team invite flow preserving firewall + audit.

**Source authority.** Summary C.65; §48.4.7 k-Anonymity Floors (existing); §8 Teams (existing); §48.2.7 retired L6 replacement semantics.

#### Trigger

M7 surfaces fire in three UX contexts:

1. **Onboarding (§35.1).** After a new user completes SSO signup — whether via M6 auto-join OR standard signup — AND their Org has ≥ 5 active members (the k=5 k-anonymity floor per §48.4.7), the onboarding flow shows a "Your colleagues at {Org}" card featuring 3–5 colleagues with whom the user has NO existing Workspace overlap.
2. **Workspace creation (§10.2).** When a user creates a new Workspace, the Workspace team-selection step surfaces suggested teammates who have worked on similar Workspaces (same category OR similar requirement patterns) in the same Org.
3. **Dashboard nudge.** On the user's Dashboard, a "Teammates you haven't worked with" card appears intermittently (at most once per user per 7 days per §29.3 anti-fatigue rules).

M7 fires ONLY when the Org has ≥ 5 active members (k=5 floor); below the floor, the surface renders an empty state with no discovery suggestions.

#### Actor & Entity Schema

**Acting entity.** The Sourcera platform (M7 is platform-orchestrated; recommendations are computed in a nightly Convex job + surfaced via reactive queries).

**Targeted entity.** The user viewing the M7 card AND the suggested colleagues.

**New entity: SuggestedTeamMemberCard (Org-Scoped, Per-User, Ephemeral).** A per-user-per-session recommendation row. Rows are ephemeral (TTL 30 days) but written to the audit trail.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK, immutable | Standard. |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | → Organization (§4.2.1); required | RBAC scope. |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer` (fixed) | M7 is buyer-only in v7.0.0; seller-side peer discovery is a future Known Gap. |
| `viewing_user_id` | UUID (FK) | → User (§4.2.3); required | Card viewer. |
| `surface_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `m7_surface_kind` (new): `onboarding_card`, `workspace_creation_step`, `dashboard_nudge` | Where the card rendered. |
| `suggested_user_ids` | Array[UUID] | 3–5 entries; all in same Org | Recommended colleagues. |
| `suggestion_ranking_signal` | Enum | Appendix J `m7_ranking_signal` (new): `same_department`, `same_workspace_overlap`, `similar_requirement_authoring`, `similar_category_activity`, `recent_org_joiner_bonus`, `k_anonymity_fallback_random` | How suggestions were ranked. |
| `k_anonymity_satisfied` | Boolean | Default: true | Whether the k=5 floor was met; false = fallback to generic card. |
| `cohort_size_at_computation` | Integer | ≥ 0 | The actual Org-active-member count at the computation moment. |
| `viewer_opt_out_status` | Enum | Appendix J `m7_viewer_opt_out_status` (new): `opted_in`, `opted_out_discovery`, `opted_out_being_suggested`, `opted_out_both` | Viewer's preference; mirrored from User settings. |
| `rendered_at` | Timestamp | Required | Render moment. |
| `clicked_suggested_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → User (§4.2.3) | If the viewer clicked a specific suggestion. |
| `invite_sent` | Boolean | Default: false | True if the click resulted in a cross-team invite flow. |
| `invite_sent_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → Workspace (§4.3.1) | The target workspace of the cross-team invite. |
| `dismissed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Explicit dismissal. |
| `ttl_expires_at` | Timestamp | Required; computed: `rendered_at + 30 days` | Cleanup window. |
| `signal_integrity_flags` | Array[Enum] | Per §48.2.12 enum; empty default | SIM-populated. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | Standard | Standard pattern | Standard; TTL-aware cleanup job purges rows post-expiry. |

**Scope isolation.** Org-scoped on `org_id`; per-user on `viewing_user_id`. Cross-Org reads are blocked. The `suggested_user_ids` are User IDs within the SAME Org; the suggestion engine NEVER crosses Org boundaries (that would violate the Dual-Console Firewall + privacy invariants).

**Required indexes.** `(org_id, viewing_user_id, rendered_at DESC)`, `(ttl_expires_at)` (nightly cleanup), `(org_id, surface_kind)`.

**Retention.** 30-day rolling per TTL; aggregate usage signals persist indefinitely in §48.3 dashboards. DSAR pseudonymization on `viewing_user_id` AND `suggested_user_ids[]`.

#### Suggestion Ranking Algorithm

Computed nightly at 02:00 UTC in a Convex batch job:

1. **Candidate pool:** All active members of the viewer's Org who are NOT already in a shared Workspace with the viewer AND who have `m7_viewer_opt_out_status ∈ {opted_in, opted_out_discovery}` (the target has not opted out of being suggested).
2. **k-anonymity gate:** If `candidate_pool_size < 5`, M7 returns `k_anonymity_fallback_random` AND renders the empty-state card.
3. **Ranking signals (in order of weight):**
   - `same_department` (weight 3.0) — requires the §8 Team + Department metadata; if unavailable, signal contributes 0.
   - `same_workspace_overlap` (weight 2.0) — users who have worked on Workspaces in the same Marketplace Category as the viewer's most-recent Workspace.
   - `similar_requirement_authoring` (weight 1.5) — users whose recent-authored requirements have ≥ 0.3 cosine similarity to the viewer's recent-authored requirements (embedding-based; computed per §22.9 retrieval engineering patterns).
   - `similar_category_activity` (weight 1.2) — users whose Org Intelligence cache indicates activity in similar vendor categories.
   - `recent_org_joiner_bonus` (weight 1.0) — users who joined the Org in the last 14 days (to help newcomers find peers).
   - `k_anonymity_fallback_random` — only used when specific signals are insufficient AND the k-anonymity floor is met.
4. **Top-N selection:** Top 5 ranked candidates; if fewer than 5 candidates pass the ranking threshold, M7 renders what's available (down to 3) but still emits `k_anonymity_satisfied=true` if cohort size ≥ 5.
5. **Diversity rotation:** The suggestion algorithm enforces that the same candidate is NOT shown to the same viewer for 14 days after a dismissal (per `SuggestedTeamMemberCard.dismissed_at` lookback).

#### Workflow

1. **Nightly computation.** 02:00 UTC Convex job computes per-user suggestion sets for every active Org with ≥ 5 members. Results cached in a per-user recommendation slot (materialized view).
2. **Surface render.** When the viewer hits onboarding OR workspace-creation OR dashboard, the UI reactively reads the cached recommendation slot AND writes a SuggestedTeamMemberCard row with `rendered_at=now` + `surface_kind=...`.
3. **Per-user opt-out.** User Settings > Privacy > "Team Discovery" allows the user to toggle:
   - Discovery on/off (am I shown suggestions?): `opted_in` vs `opted_out_discovery`.
   - Being suggested on/off (can colleagues be suggested ME?): `opted_in` vs `opted_out_being_suggested`.
   - Both can be off: `opted_out_both`.
   Opt-outs are honored in real-time in the recommendation algorithm (cache is busted within 60s of opt-out toggle via the Convex reactive query).
4. **Click interaction.** Clicking a suggested colleague opens a modal with (a) their name + display role + public department label; (b) the Workspaces they have in common IF any (zero by definition of the candidate pool, but future Workspaces MAY overlap); (c) an "Invite to Workspace" CTA opening the standard §5.4 Workspace invite flow (preserving firewall per §7.2 + audit per §4.6.1).
5. **Cross-team invite flow.** Clicking "Invite to Workspace" from the M7 modal: (a) opens the viewer's current Workspace (if in workspace-creation context) OR a Workspace picker; (b) pre-fills the invite form with the suggested user; (c) the standard §5.4 Guest permission profile selector applies. The invite is logged both in the standard Workspace Invite audit + as an M7-attributed row (`invite_sent=true` on the SuggestedTeamMemberCard).
6. **Dismissal.** Viewer clicks dismiss; `dismissed_at` is set; future cards within 14 days do NOT re-suggest the same candidates (per diversity rotation).

#### UX Surfaces

| Surface | §3.3 Pattern | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Onboarding "Your colleagues at {Org}" card | `Card List + CTA` per §3.3 | Shows 3–5 avatar + name cards; single-click to open modal. |
| Workspace-creation team-selection step | `Modal + Multi-Select` per §3.3 | Suggested colleagues appear as suggestions alongside manual search. |
| Dashboard nudge card | `Inline Card + Dismissible` per §3.3 | Appears at most 1 per user per 7 days. |
| Suggested-user detail modal | `Modal + CTA` per §3.3 | Name, role, public department, "Invite to Workspace" CTA. |
| User Settings > Privacy > Team Discovery | `Toggle Switches` per §3.3 | Two toggles: discovery, being-suggested. |
| Empty state (k < 5) | `Empty State with Explainer` per §3.3 | "We'll show suggestions once your Org has 5+ members — your privacy is protected by a cohort floor." |
| Mobile parity | Per §3.4 | Card list stacks vertically. |

#### Data Collected / Retained

Per the SuggestedTeamMemberCard field table. Aggregate click-through rate, dismissal rate, and invite-conversion rate drive §48.3 M7 dashboards. DSAR pseudonymization applies; when a user opts out of being suggested, existing SuggestedTeamMemberCard rows that include them in `suggested_user_ids[]` are NOT retroactively mutated (the card was a historical render), but future cards will exclude them.

**Residency.** SuggestedTeamMemberCard lives in the Org's data region. Cross-Org suggestions are IMPOSSIBLE by construction — the algorithm only considers same-Org members.

#### Anti-Abuse Controls

1. **§48.4.7 k-Anonymity Floor k=5.** Summary C.65 explicit requirement. Below k=5 → empty-state card; NO per-user suggestions surfaced.
2. **Per-user opt-out (both directions).** Summary C.65 explicit requirement.
3. **§48.4.10 SIM velocity-anomaly.** If a single user triggers > 50 M7-attributed cross-team invites in 24h, SIM emits `velocity_anomaly` — M7 is NOT a bulk-invite vector. The threshold is below §5.3 Workspace-invite rate limits to catch M7 abuse specifically.
4. **No cross-Org suggestions.** Algorithm is strictly same-Org-scoped.
5. **Diversity rotation: dismissed candidates not re-suggested for 14 days.** Prevents nag-pattern abuse by the algorithm itself.
6. **Anti-fatigue: dashboard nudge at most 1 per user per 7 days.** Aligned with §29.3 quiet-hours semantics.
7. **Firewall preservation per §7.2.** Cross-team invites through M7 follow the standard §5.4 Guest permission profile flow; M7 itself grants no Workspace access.
8. **Audit trail per §4.6.1.** Every M7-attributed invite is logged AND distinguishable from direct invites via audit metadata.
9. **Users opted out of being-suggested are excluded from ALL M7 ranking computations** — not even shown in the candidate pool; the opted-out user's identity is NEVER exposed to other users via M7.

#### Plan Gating & Entitlement

M7 is included on every Buyer plan tier. Rationale: team discovery is a scale enabler; gating it would friction-out the supply-side of team growth.

| `growth.m7.invite.sent` | M7-attributed invite sent | `m7_card_id`, `workspace_id`, `viewing_user_id_hash`, `suggested_user_id_hash` |

#### API Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth Scope | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `GET` | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/users/{user_id}/suggested-team-members` | `read:org_settings` AND `user_id == self` OR role in {`org_owner`, `org_admin`} | Fetch current suggestions. |
| `POST` | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/users/{user_id}/suggested-team-members/{card_id}/dismiss` | Same as GET | Dismiss card. |
| `PATCH` | `/v1/users/{user_id}/settings/team-discovery` | `write:user_settings` AND `user_id == self` | Body: `{discovery_enabled: Boolean, being_suggested_enabled: Boolean}`. |

New error codes: `m7_k_anonymity_floor_unmet` (HTTP 200 with empty array; NOT an error per se — the client receives an empty list with `k_anonymity_satisfied=false` metadata), `m7_user_opted_out` (HTTP 404 when requesting suggestions for an opted-out user; non-leak).

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. M7 suggestions MUST require the Org's active-member count ≥ 5 (the k=5 floor per §48.4.7 Summary C.65); below the floor, the surface MUST render the empty state AND emit `m7_k_anon_floor_unmet`.
2. Per-user opt-out (both discovery AND being-suggested) MUST be honored in real-time; opt-out changes propagate within 60 seconds to the recommendation cache.
3. Suggestions MUST NEVER cross Org boundaries; QA test `m7_cross_org_suggestion_blocked` asserts.
4. Dismissed candidates MUST NOT be re-suggested to the same viewer for 14 days per diversity rotation.
5. Dashboard nudge MUST fire at most 1 per user per 7 days per §29.3 anti-fatigue; QA test `m7_nudge_frequency_cap` asserts.
6. M7-attributed cross-team invites MUST flow through the standard §5.4 Guest permission profile flow — M7 itself grants no Workspace access.
7. SIM velocity-anomaly detection (> 50 M7-attributed invites by one user in 24h) MUST fire `velocity_anomaly` AND route the user to Ops review per §48.4.10.
8. The full M7 funnel `m7_card_rendered → m7_suggestion_clicked → m7_invite_initiated → m7_invite_sent` MUST be PostHog-Insights-Funnels queryable per `org_id` AND per `surface_kind`.
9. Nightly computation MUST complete within 2 hours of the 02:00 UTC start for all Orgs below 10,000 active members; larger Orgs complete via partitioned jobs within 6 hours.
10. Users opted out of being-suggested MUST NOT appear in ANY other user's `suggested_user_ids[]`; QA test `m7_opt_out_exclusion` asserts over synthetic cohorts.

#### Failure Modes Addressed

1. **User opts out of being-suggested WHILE another user is viewing a card that includes them.** Resolved: the card was a historical render; it is NOT retroactively mutated (that would create race conditions AND leak state changes). Future renders exclude the opted-out user within 60 seconds per AC #2. The opted-out user's identity was exposed to the viewer during that card render, but no Workspace access was granted (M7 only surfaces names). The user's opt-out applies prospectively.
2. **Org grows from 4 to 5 members; the 5th member triggers k-anonymity satisfaction.** Resolved: the nightly computation at 02:00 UTC detects the new cohort size AND begins generating suggestions the following day. A user hitting M7 surfaces between the 4→5 transition and the nightly job still sees the empty state (since `k_anonymity_satisfied` is computed per-render from the current cohort size, not from the cached suggestions). Safe-default-closed semantics.
3. **Malicious actor tries to enumerate Org membership via repeated M7 card fetches.** Resolved: §48.4.10 SIM velocity-anomaly detection catches > 50 card-fetches per user per 24h; per-user rate-limiting at 20 card-fetches per hour applies at the API layer. Enumeration is computationally infeasible: the viewer can only see their own card slot, which contains 3–5 names per render.
4. **Suggestion engine crashes or times out.** Resolved: the UI degrades to the empty state (no suggestions surfaced) AND emits `m7_suggestion_engine_degraded` PostHog event; §42 P2 alert triggers Ops.
5. **Org Admin wants to disable M7 entirely for their Org for privacy-policy reasons.** Resolved: Org Settings > Privacy > "Disable Team Discovery for all members" toggle disables M7 at the Org level (all members default to `opted_out_both`; new members inherit the Org default). Logged as `org_m7_disabled` audit event. Authored extension; flagged in RECONCILIATION.md.

### 48.5.8 M8 Org Intelligence Value Curve {#48.5.8-m8-org-intelligence-value-curve}

#### Purpose

M8 surfaces an in-app curve showing the compounding analytical value an Org accrues with each additional evaluation — concrete time-saved estimates, vendor-pool-learning value, requirement-template reuse, discrepancy-analysis insight count, and predictive-suggestion accuracy improvement. The mechanic exists because the ROI story for Org Intelligence (§16) is non-obvious to customers until they have ≥ 3 completed evaluations; M8 makes the compounding-value claim concrete AND measurable, driving both expansion conversion (Starter → Growth → Scale) AND Enterprise retention. Summary C.66 explicitly specifies "visible in-app curve showing the compounding analytical value of each additional evaluation within an Org, with concrete time-saved estimates."

**Source authority.** Summary C.66; §16 Organizational Intelligence (existing); §4.3.19 Time-Saved Credit (existing); §48.3.1 qualitative framing effect #3 "Data compounds both sides."

#### Trigger

M8 surfaces fire in three UX contexts:

1. **Org Intelligence dashboard (§16).** Whenever an Org Owner / Org Admin visits the Org Intelligence dashboard, the M8 Value Curve appears as the first visual tile.
2. **Post-Phase-13 closure summary.** When a new evaluation closes (Phase 13), the M8 curve updates AND the closure summary includes a "Your compounding value has grown by {X%} with this evaluation" callout.
3. **Upgrade CTA context.** On plan-tier upgrade prompts (per §48.2.6 L5 flow), the M8 curve appears as "What you're unlocking" evidence.

M8 requires the Org to have ≥ 1 completed evaluation (Phase 13 closed); Orgs below the threshold see a "Your curve will appear after your first evaluation closes" placeholder.

#### Actor & Entity Schema

**Acting entity.** The Sourcera platform (M8 is platform-orchestrated; the curve is recomputed nightly + on each evaluation closure).

**Targeted entity.** The Org.

**New entity: OrgIntelligenceValueCurveCheckpoint (Org-Scoped, Append-Only Audit Row).** One checkpoint row per evaluation closure; an Org's curve is the time-series of its checkpoints.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK, immutable | Standard. |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | → Organization (§4.2.1); required | RBAC scope. |
| `console` | Enum | `buyer` (fixed) | M8 is buyer-only in v7.0.0; seller-side value curve is a future Known Gap. |
| `sequence_number` | Integer | ≥ 1; UNIQUE with `(org_id, sequence_number)` | Monotonic per-Org evaluation closure index. `sequence_number=N` is the Org's N-th closed evaluation. |
| `triggering_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | → Workspace (§4.3.1); required | The evaluation closure that produced this checkpoint. |
| `checkpoint_computed_at` | Timestamp | Required | Computation moment. |
| `total_closed_evaluations` | Integer | = `sequence_number` | Redundant-but-denormalized for query convenience. |
| `total_minutes_saved_cumulative` | Decimal(12,2) | ≥ 0 | Sum of all §4.3.19 Time-Saved Credit `minutes_saved` across the Org's history. |
| `total_value_saved_usd_cumulative` | Decimal(12,2) | ≥ 0 | Sum of all §4.3.19 `value_saved_usd` across history. |
| `delta_minutes_saved_this_evaluation` | Decimal(10,2) | ≥ 0 | Minutes-saved attributable to THIS evaluation (per §4.3.19). |
| `delta_value_saved_usd_this_evaluation` | Decimal(10,2) | ≥ 0 | Dollar value of the delta. |
| `vendor_pool_coverage_pct` | Decimal(5,2) | 0.00–100.00 | % of this evaluation's vendors that already existed in the Org's vendor-intelligence cache (reused-intelligence metric). |
| `requirement_template_reuse_pct` | Decimal(5,2) | 0.00–100.00 | % of this evaluation's requirements derived from the Org's template library (§19). |
| `discrepancy_insight_count` | Integer | ≥ 0 | Number of §16.5 Discrepancy Insight Cards generated for this evaluation. |
| `predictive_suggestion_accuracy_pct` | Decimal(5,2) | 0.00–100.00; nullable | Accuracy of §16.6 predictive top-candidate suggestions vs actual final ranking; null for Orgs on plans without Predictive Suggestions access per §16.9.1. |
| `compounding_factor` | Decimal(6,4) | ≥ 1.0 | The curve's multiplier: `total_value_saved_usd_cumulative / (sequence_number × baseline_value_per_evaluation_usd)`. A value > 1.0 indicates compounding; rising values indicate accelerating compounding. |
| `baseline_value_per_evaluation_usd` | Decimal(10,2) | > 0 | The Org's first-evaluation `delta_value_saved_usd_this_evaluation`, frozen at `sequence_number=1`; used as the compounding-factor denominator. For Orgs whose first-evaluation was pre-M8 (legacy data), a synthetic baseline is computed from the Org's earliest completed evaluation. |
| `narrative_text_rendered` | String | ≤ 1,000 chars | Human-readable copy rendered on the UI (e.g., "You've saved {N} hours across {K} evaluations — your per-evaluation time savings have grown by {X}% since your first."). Computed server-side for stable rendering; cached for 24h per checkpoint. |
| `m8_upgrade_cta_rendered_count` | Integer | ≥ 0; default 0 | Number of times this checkpoint's curve was shown alongside an upgrade CTA. |
| `m8_upgrade_cta_clicked_count` | Integer | ≥ 0; default 0 | Number of CTA clicks attributable to this checkpoint. |
| `signal_integrity_flags` | Array[Enum] | Per §48.2.12 enum; empty default | SIM-populated for data-integrity anomalies. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | Standard | Standard pattern | Append-only; never soft-deleted except via Ops for data-integrity reasons. |

**Scope isolation.** Org-scoped on `org_id`. Read access: `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `billing_admin` (for ROI reporting). Workspace-level users (`workspace_owner`, etc.) do NOT see the curve because it is an Org-aggregate metric; §16 RBAC precedent applies. Cross-Org access is blocked with HTTP 404 `m8_cross_org_access`.

**Required indexes.** `(org_id, sequence_number)` UNIQUE, `(org_id, checkpoint_computed_at DESC)`, `(triggering_workspace_id)` UNIQUE (one checkpoint per closed Workspace).

**Retention.** Org-life; not subject to right-to-erasure under the applicable §6.8.5 retained-row classes (the curve is an aggregate metric; individual PII is not exposed). Identity fields pseudonymized on DSAR.

#### Workflow

The M8 lifecycle is platform-orchestrated; the customer-facing surfaces consume the curve reactively. The end-to-end workflow:

1. **Trigger.** New evaluation closes (Phase 13). The Convex closure handler enqueues an M8-checkpoint job.
2. **Job execution.** Within 5 minutes of closure, the job:
   - Queries §4.3.19 Time-Saved Credit rows for the Org, computes `total_minutes_saved_cumulative` + `total_value_saved_usd_cumulative`.
   - Computes `delta_*` for the triggering workspace.
   - Computes `vendor_pool_coverage_pct` by comparing this evaluation's vendors to the Org's §16.2.1 Vendor Performance cache.
   - Computes `requirement_template_reuse_pct` by scanning Requirement rows for `source_template_id` references.
   - Counts §16.5 Discrepancy Insight Cards.
   - Computes `predictive_suggestion_accuracy_pct` by comparing §16.6 predictions vs actual rankings.
   - Computes `compounding_factor`.
   - Renders `narrative_text_rendered`.
3. **Write checkpoint.** Atomic write with `sequence_number = (last sequence_number for Org) + 1`.
4. **Publish to UI.** Convex reactive query updates the §16 dashboard AND Pulse within sub-second.
5. **Nightly re-computation.** 02:30 UTC nightly job re-computes the most-recent checkpoint's derived metrics (to capture late-arriving §4.3.19 reversals OR contest-adjusted Time-Saved Credits); prior checkpoints are immutable once written + aged ≥ 7 days.

#### UX Surfaces

| Surface | §3.3 Pattern | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Org Intelligence dashboard top tile | `Line Chart + Narrative Card` per §3.3 | X-axis: `sequence_number`; Y-axis: cumulative value-saved-USD; inflection-point annotations. |
| Phase-13 closure summary callout | `Inline Card` per §3.3 | "Your compounding value has grown by {X%} with this evaluation." |
| Upgrade CTA context panel | `Sidebar Panel` per §3.3 | Inline curve with "What you're unlocking" narrative. |
| Settings > Organization > Value Curve | `Full-Page Detail` per §3.3 | Interactive chart with per-checkpoint drill-down. |
| Export to PDF / CSV | Standard §40 export flow | For QBR slides + exec-committee reporting. |
| Mobile parity | Per §3.4 | Chart responsive; drill-down becomes stacked rows. |

#### Data Collected / Retained

Per the OrgIntelligenceValueCurveCheckpoint field table. Aggregate signals feed §48.3.2 Network Effects signal #3 "`org_intelligence_value_curve_slope`" (the slope of the curve is a canonical compounding-data signal). DSAR pseudonymization applies; the curve itself is Org-aggregate and not subject to right-to-erasure.

**Residency.** OrgIntelligenceValueCurveCheckpoint lives in the Org's data region per §1.6. Exports respect §40 format + §47.4 residency.

#### Anti-Abuse Controls

1. **Curve computation based on authoritative §4.3.19 Time-Saved Credit ledger.** No customer self-report; the curve is computed from immutable Usage Event data.
2. **Reversal-aware aggregation (§4.3.19.)** Reversed Time-Saved Credits flow through to curve recomputation within the 7-day immutability window.
3. **Per-Org UNIQUE `sequence_number`.** Prevents duplicate checkpoints on phase-regression-then-re-close edge cases.
4. **Plan-gated Predictive Suggestion Accuracy field.** Nullable when Org's plan lacks §16.9.1 access; prevents data exposure across plan tiers.
5. **§4.8.5 Contest integration.** If a Time-Saved Credit is reversed via a customer-filed contest within the 7-day window, the affected checkpoint is regenerated; the original checkpoint row is marked as `superseded_by_checkpoint_id` (authored extension; not a new field per se but a synthetic tombstone record) for audit.
6. **SIM integrity alert.** If the `compounding_factor` ever decreases between two consecutive checkpoints (violates the monotonicity-or-compounding invariant), SIM emits `m8_curve_monotonicity_violation` (possibly legitimate in edge cases like data corrections; Ops review).
7. **No direct customer write.** M8 is read-only for customers; only the platform orchestrator + Ops (via emergency-correction path per §43) may write.

#### Plan Gating & Entitlement

M8 is included on Buyer Growth, Buyer Scale, and Buyer Enterprise per §16.9.1 Intelligence Availability matrix (Free AND Starter lack Org Intelligence). Buyer Free AND Starter Orgs see a locked-state M8 tile with "Upgrade to Growth to see your compounding value curve" copy + an inline upgrade CTA — this is explicit: M8 is one of the canonical §48.2.6 L5 upgrade-pressure surfaces.

The §5.11 Feature Access Matrix is updated to add the row "View M8 Org Intelligence Value Curve": ✓ for `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `billing_admin` (on plans that include §16); ✗ for everyone else (see appendix-update block).

#### Telemetry Events

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `m8_checkpoint_computed` | Phase-13 closure triggers checkpoint computation | `checkpoint_id`, `org_id`, `sequence_number`, `triggering_workspace_id`, `compounding_factor`, `delta_value_saved_usd_this_evaluation`, `total_value_saved_usd_cumulative` |
| `m8_curve_viewed` | User views M8 tile | `checkpoint_id` (most-recent), `viewer_user_id`, `surface_kind ∈ {org_intelligence_dashboard, closure_summary, upgrade_cta_context, full_page_detail}`, `view_duration_seconds`, `current_compounding_factor` |
| `m8_curve_exported` | User exports to PDF / CSV | `org_id`, `export_format ∈ {pdf, csv}`, `checkpoint_count_exported` |
| `m8_upgrade_cta_rendered_with_curve` | Upgrade CTA rendered alongside M8 curve | `org_id`, `current_plan`, `target_plan`, `current_compounding_factor` |
| `m8_upgrade_cta_clicked_with_curve` | User clicks the CTA | `org_id`, `current_plan`, `target_plan`, `time_from_render_to_click_seconds` |
| `m8_curve_locked_view_attempted` | Free / Starter user views the locked-state tile | `org_id`, `current_plan`, `viewer_user_id` |

| `m8_checkpoint_regenerated_post_reversal` | Nightly re-compute picks up a §4.3.19 reversal | `checkpoint_id`, `reversal_count`, `compounding_factor_delta` |

#### Notifications Fired

| `m8.milestone_reached` | Org Owner, Org Admin, Billing Admin | In-App | Triggered on milestones: sequence_number ∈ {3, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100} | "You've closed {N} evaluations — your compounding value is now {X%} above baseline." Optional email opt-in. |
| `m8.curve_export_ready` | Exporter | In-App | Immediate | Standard export-ready semantics. |

| `growth.m8.checkpoint_computed` | Checkpoint write | `checkpoint_id`, `org_id`, `sequence_number`, `compounding_factor`, `total_value_saved_usd_cumulative` |
| `growth.m8.milestone_reached` | Milestone | `checkpoint_id`, `milestone_sequence_number`, `compounding_factor` |

#### API Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth Scope | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `GET` | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/value-curve` | `read:org_intelligence` + role in {`org_owner`, `org_admin`, `billing_admin`} | Returns the full curve (all checkpoints). Supports `?since_sequence_number=N` for incremental fetch. |
| `GET` | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/value-curve/checkpoints/{checkpoint_id}` | Same | Fetch single checkpoint. |
| `POST` | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/value-curve/export` | `read:org_intelligence` + same roles | Body: `{format ∈ {pdf, csv}}`. Async export; returns a job ID. |
| `POST` | `/v1/orgs/{org_id}/value-curve/recompute` | `admin:org_intelligence` + Ops | Ops-only force-recompute; rare; audit-logged. |

New error codes: `m8_cross_org_access` (HTTP 404), `m8_plan_gate_insufficient` (HTTP 402 with upgrade path in error body — consistent with §34.8.1 soft-gate semantics), `m8_no_checkpoints_available` (HTTP 200 with empty array; not an error; indicates Org has 0 closed evaluations), `m8_recompute_rate_limit_exceeded` (HTTP 429; Ops-force-recompute is rate-limited to 10/hour per Org).

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. M8 checkpoints MUST be auto-computed within 5 minutes of every Phase-13 closure; failure raises §42 P2 alert.
2. The `sequence_number` MUST be monotonically increasing per Org with no gaps; UNIQUE constraint enforced atomically.
3. The `compounding_factor` MUST be ≥ 1.0 by construction; monotonicity violations MUST emit `m8_curve_monotonicity_violation` AND trigger Ops review per §48.4.10.
4. Plan-gated fields (e.g., `predictive_suggestion_accuracy_pct`) MUST be null when the Org's plan lacks access per §16.9.1; QA test `m8_plan_gate_field_nullification` asserts.
5. Free / Starter Orgs MUST see the locked-state tile with upgrade CTA; attempting to fetch the curve via API returns HTTP 402 `m8_plan_gate_insufficient` with the upgrade path in the error body per §34.8.1.
6. Nightly re-computation MUST update the most-recent checkpoint's derived metrics within 7 days of its original computation; older checkpoints MUST be immutable.
7. Time-Saved Credit reversals (§4.3.19) MUST flow through to curve re-computation within the 7-day window; emits `m8_checkpoint_regenerated_post_reversal`.
8. Milestone notifications MUST fire exactly once per milestone sequence_number per Org; duplicate-fires raise `analytics_invariant_violation`.
9. The curve MUST be renderable at sub-second latency for Orgs with ≤ 100 checkpoints; larger curves (> 100 closed evaluations) MAY use pagination via `?since_sequence_number=N`.
10. Cross-Org access MUST be blocked with HTTP 404 (not 403) to preserve Org existence non-leak.
11. The `narrative_text_rendered` field MUST be localized per §37.2 i18n for the Org's `default_locale`; re-renders on locale change are nightly-scheduled.
12. The full M8 funnel `m8_curve_viewed → m8_upgrade_cta_rendered_with_curve → m8_upgrade_cta_clicked_with_curve → upgrade_completed` MUST be PostHog-Insights-Funnels queryable per `org_id` with M8 as the `trigger` per Appendix G `upgrade_completed_trigger` extension (new value `m8_value_curve_evidence` — see appendix-update block).

#### Failure Modes Addressed

1. **Org has a pre-M8 legacy evaluation as its first evaluation; no `baseline_value_per_evaluation_usd` can be computed directly.** Resolved: the computation algorithm falls back to a synthetic baseline derived from the Org's earliest Usage Event ledger entries + §4.3.19 Time-Saved Credit retroactive calculation; the synthetic baseline is flagged on the checkpoint via `narrative_text_rendered` ("your first evaluation predates our compounding-value tracking; baseline is estimated"). Authoring extension; flagged.
2. **Time-Saved Credit reversal arrives 8 days after the corresponding checkpoint is written.** Resolved: older-than-7-day checkpoints are immutable; the reversal is applied to the next checkpoint's cumulative fields as an "adjustment" AND narrative copy notes "includes retroactive adjustment of {X} from prior-period reversals." Data integrity preserved; user-facing monotonicity preserved (cumulative never decreases visually).
3. **Org churns (downgrades from Growth → Free) but retains historical M8 data.** Resolved: the curve remains computed + retained; customer loses view access until they re-upgrade. `m8_plan_gate_insufficient` error is returned on API attempts post-downgrade. If the customer returns on a paid plan, the full historical curve is restored immediately.
4. **Phase regression: a closed Workspace re-opens via Ops emergency path, then re-closes.** Resolved: the checkpoint for that Workspace is NOT regenerated (per UNIQUE `triggering_workspace_id`); if the re-closure produces materially different Time-Saved Credits, they flow into the NEXT checkpoint as adjustments. A forensic audit note is added to the original checkpoint's `signal_integrity_flags`.
5. **Ops force-recompute a checkpoint due to a data-correction incident.** Resolved: the Ops endpoint writes a new checkpoint row with `superseded_by_checkpoint_id` pointing at it on the original row; the original is NOT deleted (audit integrity); subsequent reads surface the new checkpoint + optionally a "data correction applied on {date}" banner. Rate-limited to 10/hour per Org.

### 48.5.9 Cross-Mechanic Acceptance Criteria (M1–M8) {#48.5.9-cross-mechanic-acceptance-criteria}

These criteria apply to all eight M1–M8 mechanics collectively:

1. Every M1–M8 mechanic MUST emit at least one PostHog event registered in Appendix G within 5 seconds of its trigger.
2. Every M1–M8 mechanic that emits email MUST honor §41 deliverability controls AND §48.4.1–§48.4.3 throttling + shared-use-domain exclusions.
3. Every M1–M8 mechanic that produces public or vendor-targeted artifacts MUST honor §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Records AND §4.5.6 Marketplace-Domain Render Contract.
4. Every M1–M8 mechanic MUST be killable via EITHER the §48.2.12.4 GrowthLoopKillSwitch (when loop-attributable — M5 primarily) OR a feature-flag publish path with 60-second worst-case orchestrator-cache invalidation latency (§22.16.5).
5. Every M1–M8 mechanic MUST be RBAC-gated per §5.11 Feature Access Matrix updates registered in the Appendix-update block below.
6. Every M1–M8 mechanic MUST have at least one §48.3.3 Ops Growth Console dashboard surface tracking conversion + adoption rates.
7. Every M1–M8 mechanic MUST log its lifecycle operations (issuance, redemption, revocation) to §4.6.1 Audit Event per §6.7 Audit Logging semantics.
8. M1–M8 cross-mechanic attribution overlap (e.g., a user auto-joins via M6 AND is then featured in an M7 card AND later publishes an M2 link) MUST be resolvable via `growth_loop_execution_id` cross-references OR mechanic-specific attribution rows per §48.2.13 AC #7 first-touch attribution.
9. Every M1–M8 mechanic MUST be unit-testable AND integration-testable; CI gates merge if any mechanic's unit-test suite is incomplete.
10. Every M1–M8 mechanic MUST have its per-loop metadata_json schema (where loop-attributable) validate against §48.2.12.3; violations return HTTP 422.
