## 48.6 M9–M13 Public Marketplace Content Mechanics {#48.6-m9-m13-public-marketplace-content-mechanics}

**Authoring intent.** §48.6 authors the operational, editorial, render-contract, and lifecycle behavior for the five Sourcera-owned, AI-generated, public-Marketplace content mechanics M9–M13 from Summary §3.3 (M9–M13 inventory) and Summary C.67–C.71. The persisted entity schemas for these mechanics already exist in §4.4.12 CategoryPage (M9), §4.4.13 GuidePage (M10), §4.4.14 ComparisonPage (M11), §4.4.15 MarketIntelligenceReport (M12), and §4.4.16 HeatMapCell (M13). §48.6 does NOT re-author those field tables; it authors the operational machinery that makes those entities ship: the AI capability invocation contract, the editorial review workflow + rubric, the refresh-orchestration cadence, the Schema.org structured-data render contract, the k-anonymity render gate, the Vendor Opt-Out honoring behavior, the takedown/appeal flow, the cost-center routing (Platform Marketing — never customer-billed), the per-mechanic anti-abuse controls, the telemetry events, the notifications, the webhooks, the API endpoints (Ops admin + anonymous public render), and the per-mechanic acceptance criteria.

**Per-mechanic structure.** Every M9–M13 subsection follows the thirteen-block layout established by §48.5: (1) Purpose; (2) Trigger; (3) Actor & Entity Schema (cross-link to the existing §4.4.x entity); (4) Generation + Editorial Workflow (step-by-step from capability invocation through publication, including refresh cadence and refresh-analysis capability); (5) UX Surfaces (referencing §3.3 patterns and the public Marketplace render path); (6) Data Collected / Retained (cross-link to entity); (7) Anti-Abuse Controls (specific to public-page mechanics; cross-linked to §48.4); (8) Plan Gating & Cost-Center Routing (Platform Marketing routing; never customer-billed); (9) Telemetry Events; (10) Notifications Fired; (11) Webhooks Fired; (12) API Endpoints (Ops admin endpoints + anonymous public render); (13) Acceptance Criteria — including the universal `MUST fail to render when k-anonymity floor is not met` criterion. Each mechanic also closes with a **Failure Modes Addressed** subsection enumerating ≥ 3 realistic failure modes per the §48 counterfactual-pass requirement.

**Cross-mechanic invariants.** Every M9–M13 mechanic (a) is exclusively powered by `platform_marketing` capabilities from the §21.4.3 Platform-Owned Capability Registry — no customer wallet is debited; (b) writes its `AIOperation` rows with `cost_center=platform_marketing` per §21.4.3 cost-center accounting rule; (c) emits at least one PostHog event registered in Appendix G (additions in §48.6.7 below); (d) is gated by at least one §48.4 anti-spam control; (e) honors §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Records and the §4.5.6 Marketplace-Domain Render Contract; (f) is killable from the Ops Console via a per-mechanic feature-flag publish path with 60-second worst-case orchestrator-cache invalidation latency (§22.16.5); (g) honors the Schema.org cross-mechanic render contract authored in §48.6.1 below; (h) honors the editorial review workflow + rubric authored in §48.6.2 below; (i) honors the takedown / appeal flow authored in §48.6.3 below; (j) is RBAC-gated per §5.11 Feature Access Matrix updates registered in the appendix-update block in §48.6.9.

**Mechanic-to-Loop linkage.** M9, M10, M11, M12, M13 are platform-amplifier mechanics; none directly own a §48.2 Loop, but all five compound L4 (Marketplace SEO Pull) and L10 (Category-Vertical Compounding) per Summary §3.4 ("Why these mechanics compound"). Telemetry from M9–M13 feeds the §48.3 Network Effects dashboard and the L4 / L10 attribution rows; the GrowthLoopExecution audit-row contract (§48.2.12) does NOT apply (these mechanics do not pivot on per-execution attribution), but the per-mechanic publish events ARE registered as inputs to the §48.3 Marketplace SEO compounding metric set.

**Source authority.** Summary §3.3 (M9–M13 inventory table); Summary §3.4 ("Why these mechanics compound" — the M9 + M10 + M11 + M12 + M13 SEO moat); Summary C.67 (M9 CategoryPage), C.68 (M10 GuidePage), C.69 (M11 ComparisonPage), C.70 (M12 MarketIntelligenceReport), C.71 (M13 Heat Map), C.123 (Vendor Opt-Out Registry); §4.4.12 CategoryPage entity, §4.4.13 GuidePage entity, §4.4.14 ComparisonPage entity, §4.4.15 MarketIntelligenceReport entity, §4.4.16 HeatMapCell entity; §4.4.7 Marketplace Category, §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Record; §4.5.6 Marketplace-Domain Render Contract; §21.4.3 Platform-Owned Capability Registry, §21.4.5 Outcome Signals (M9–M13 capability rows); §27 Vendor Discovery & RFP Marketplace; §48.4 Anti-Spam framework (every mechanic); §1.6 Deployment Regions (residency); §3.5 Master Summary k-anonymity floor structure (k=5 / k=10 / k=20).

### 48.6.1 Cross-Mechanic Schema.org Render Contract {#48.6.1-cross-mechanic-schema-org-render-contract}

**Authoring intent.** Every M9–M13 mechanic emits Schema.org JSON-LD on its public render. To prevent per-mechanic divergence, drift between rendered HTML and emitted structured data, or vendor-opt-out leakage via structured-data payloads, §48.6.1 fixes the cross-mechanic Schema.org contract that every public render path MUST honor. The contract is implemented as a single render-time function `render_schema_org_payload(entity, rendered_html_dom)` invoked from the public render path of every M9–M13 surface.

**Per-mechanic Schema.org type assignments (canonical).**

| Mechanic | Entity | Primary Schema.org type | Required additional types | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| M9 CategoryPage | §4.4.12 CategoryPage | `CollectionPage` | `FAQPage` (FAQ block); `ItemList` of `Product` (vendor shortlist); `BreadcrumbList` (Marketplace > Category) | The FAQ block's `mainEntity` array MUST exactly mirror the `faq_payload_json` rendered Q&A pairs. |
| M10 GuidePage | §4.4.13 GuidePage | `Article` | `BreadcrumbList`; `HowTo` (the evaluation steps section); `Person` for any quoted analyst (only when `person_quote_attribution_consented=true`; default false); `Organization` for Sourcera as `publisher` | `Article.author = Sourcera Editorial Team`; never a named individual. |
| M11 ComparisonPage | §4.4.14 ComparisonPage | `ItemList` of `Product` | `BreadcrumbList`; per-product `Review` (with `Rating` and `reviewBody` — limited to ≤ 200 chars per product, sourced from `narrative_markdown`); `Organization` for Sourcera as `publisher` | Opted-out products MUST be entirely omitted from `ItemList` (not blank-entry). |
| M12 MarketIntelligenceReport | §4.4.15 MarketIntelligenceReport | `Article` | `Dataset` (the report's underlying aggregated dataset; `Dataset.creator = Sourcera`; `Dataset.license = "Sourcera Marketplace Public License"`); `BreadcrumbList`; `Organization` for Sourcera as `publisher` | The `Dataset.distribution` MUST point to the cached PDF URL from `download_pdf_url`; if `download_pdf_url IS NULL`, the `Dataset` block is omitted entirely. |
| M13 Heat Map | §4.4.16 HeatMapCell (one cell per row); the Heat Map UI page is a derived view that aggregates cells | `DataCatalog` (the Heat Map landing page); per-cell `Dataset`; `Place` references for `region_code` (ISO 3166 + macro-region overlay); `BreadcrumbList` | Cells with `k_anon_satisfied=false` MUST be entirely omitted from the rendered DataCatalog (not represented as null). |

**Cross-mechanic Schema.org render rules (all five mechanics).**

1. **Vendor Opt-Out omission.** Any `Product` (M9 vendor shortlist; M11 compared products) OR `Organization` (any reference to a vendor's Org) corresponding to a §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Record with active scope MUST be entirely omitted from the JSON-LD payload — not emitted as a redacted-name placeholder. The QA test `schema_org_opt_out_omission` (existing per §4.4.8) MUST run on every M9–M13 publish gate AND every render path; the test fails the publish if any opted-out entity name appears anywhere in the JSON-LD payload OR the rendered HTML alt text.
2. **k-anonymity omission.** Any aggregate metric whose cohort fails the per-mechanic k-anonymity floor MUST be omitted from the JSON-LD payload AND the rendered HTML — never rendered as `null`, `0`, OR a placeholder count. The k-anonymity floor evaluation is the §48.6.4 Cross-Mechanic k-Anonymity Render Gate.
3. **Canonical URL invariants.** Every payload includes a top-level `@id` (the canonical URL of the rendered page) that exactly matches the `canonical_url` field on the entity row; mismatches fail the publish gate with HTTP 422 `marketplace_content_canonical_url_mismatch` (Appendix I — new).
4. **Publisher attribution.** Every payload includes `"publisher": {"@type": "Organization", "name": "Sourcera", "url": "https://sourcera.io"}`; this is non-overridable.
5. **`dateModified` freshness invariant.** Every payload's `dateModified` MUST equal the entity's `last_published_at`; the render-time validator asserts this at every render. A drift > 60 seconds emits `schema_org_date_modified_drift` (Appendix G — new) and fails-open with the corrected value used at render.
6. **Length budget.** Each mechanic's `schema_org_payload_json` field has a §39 ceiling (M9 / M10 / M12 = 20,000 chars; M11 = 20,000 chars per the existing §39 ComparisonPage entry; M13 derived per-cell at render with no persisted ceiling because cells are aggregated at the DataCatalog level). Payloads exceeding their ceiling fail the generation gate with HTTP 422 `marketplace_content_schema_org_payload_too_large` (Appendix I — new).
7. **Validator.** Every M9–M13 publish gate AND every nightly health sweep runs the rendered JSON-LD through the open-source Schema.org Validator (per `schema.org/validator` reference) AND a Sourcera-internal allowlist that asserts only the types listed in the per-mechanic table above appear. Validator errors fail the publish gate with HTTP 422 `marketplace_content_schema_org_invalid` (Appendix I — new).

**Schema.org payload caching.** Per the §4.4.12 / §4.4.13 / §4.4.14 / §4.4.15 entity `schema_org_payload_json` field: the JSON-LD is materialized at every publish AND at every refresh AND at every Vendor Opt-Out resweep; the rendered HTML embeds the cached payload at render. Cache TTL at the §31 edge: 60 seconds (matching the §4.4.8 opt-out 60-second snapshot freshness floor); the cache is busted within 60 seconds on any of (a) entity republish, (b) opt-out resweep, (c) takedown acceptance, (d) feature-flag mechanic-kill.

### 48.6.2 Cross-Mechanic Editorial Review Workflow & Rubric {#48.6.2-cross-mechanic-editorial-review-workflow-rubric}

**Authoring intent.** Every M9–M13 mechanic except M13 (auto-published per §4.4.16) routes its draft content through an editorial review workflow staffed by the Ops Marketing role pool (and, for M12, the Ops Finance role pool). §48.6.2 fixes the workflow, the rubric, the SLA, the queue routing, and the auto-escalation behavior so that the per-mechanic subsections below can cross-link rather than re-author.

**Editorial roles.** Three roles participate in the M9–M13 editorial workflow. All three are existing or near-existing Ops Console roles per §5.2 / §43:

| Role | New / Existing | Responsibility | Mechanic Coverage |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `ops_marketing_editor` | Existing per §4.4.12, §4.4.13, §27.6 | Per-page editorial review against the §48.6.2 rubric; queue triage; revision-request authorship; publish authorization | M9, M10, M11, M12 (Marketing leg) |
| `ops_marketing_finance_reviewer` | New (Authored Extension #20; Appendix J `ops_role` enum extension) | Finance-correctness review for M12 only (pricing-band correctness, signal-cohort sufficiency, residency invariants) | M12 (Finance leg) |
| `ops_legal_takedown_admin` | New (Authored Extension #21; Appendix J `ops_role` enum extension) | Takedown / appeal adjudication; legal-takedown authorization for content removal | All M9–M13 takedowns (§48.6.3) |

**Editorial Review Rubric (RUBRIC v1.0).** Every M9–M12 editorial review applies the RUBRIC v1.0 below. The rubric is versioned (Appendix J `editorial_rubric_version` — new; v7.0.0 seed: `1.0`) so future bumps are observable in the audit log. M13 cells skip the rubric (auto-published) but cell-aggregation surfaces (e.g., featured-cell promo strips on the Marketplace landing page) DO apply the rubric.

| Rubric Dimension | Pass Criterion | Fail Action |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **R1 Factual Accuracy** | Every claim about a vendor's capability, pricing band, or market position is sourced from a citable Sourcera-internal signal (KB entry, capability declaration, marketplace listing, Workspace evaluation, Org Intelligence aggregate) OR a clearly-attributed external source. | Reject; populate `editorial_rejection_reason` with the specific unsourced claim. |
| **R2 Vendor-Neutrality** | The page does not exhibit unfair preferential treatment of any single vendor. For M11, the comparison narrative MUST present each vendor's strengths AND weaknesses. For M9, the vendor shortlist MUST be drawn from the §4.4.7 marketplace-category-aware ranking algorithm (per §27 Match Score) AND not hand-selected by any reviewer. | Reject; require AI re-generation OR shortlist re-ranking. |
| **R3 k-Anonymity Compliance** | Every aggregate metric on the page passes its per-mechanic k-anonymity floor (k=5 / k=10 / k=20 per §48.4.7). | Reject; require either coarser aggregation OR metric suppression; re-run §48.6.4 render gate. |
| **R4 Vendor Opt-Out Compliance** | No opted-out vendor name appears anywhere on the page (HTML, alt text, JSON-LD, image filenames, redirect URLs). | Reject; force a re-render with §4.4.8 opt-out resweep applied. |
| **R5 Schema.org Compliance** | The rendered JSON-LD validates against §48.6.1 contract AND the open-source Schema.org Validator. | Reject; require regeneration with the specific validator error addressed. |
| **R6 Tone & Brand Voice** | The rendered prose adheres to the Sourcera Brand Voice Guide (Ops-managed; Appendix K Glossary entry `brand_voice_guide_v1` — the canonical Glossary per Phase 12.3 amendment); no profanity, hate speech, or off-topic content (per §48.4.4 content validators). | Reject; require regeneration. |
| **R7 SEO Hygiene** | `meta_title` 10–60 chars, `meta_description` 50–160 chars, `canonical_url` resolves, `slug` matches §4.4.7 Category slug conventions where applicable, `BreadcrumbList` present in Schema.org. | Reject; require regeneration. |
| **R8 Refresh-Diff Justification (refresh-only)** | For refresh runs (`guide_refresh_analysis` outputs OR M9 / M11 nightly refresh): the `refresh_diff_score` is justified by an explicit content-delta summary in the editorial review row. | Reject; require explicit justification OR cancel the refresh. |
| **R9 Residency Compliance (M12 only)** | The signal cohort underlying the report respects `residency_region_scope` per §4.4.15 residency enforcement. | Reject; abort the report for that region-period. |
| **R10 Pricing-Band Correctness (M12 Finance only)** | Every pricing band reported is reproducible from the §15 TCO + §27 Marketplace pricing-signal pipeline AND no individual vendor's contract terms are inferable. | Reject; require coarser aggregation. |

**Workflow steps (M9 / M10 / M11 / M12).**

1. **Generation queue.** A `platform_marketing` capability invocation (per §21.4.3) writes a draft entity row in `editorial_review_status=pending` AND `publication_status=pending_review`. The draft writes an `EditorialReviewTask` row (new entity authored below in §48.6.2.A) and enqueues it on the per-mechanic editorial queue.
2. **Triage.** An `ops_marketing_editor` claims the task within the SLA (5 business days for M9, M10, M11; 10 business days for M12 Marketing leg). Claim writes `editorial_review_task.claimed_by_user_id` AND `claimed_at` AND moves the task to `under_review`.
3. **Rubric application.** The reviewer applies RUBRIC v1.0 dimension-by-dimension. The reviewer UI surfaces a rubric checklist per §48.6.2 with each dimension annotated pass / fail; failures require a free-text `editorial_rejection_reason` (≥ 30 chars; ≤ 1,000 chars).
4. **Decision.** Three terminal decisions: (a) `approved` → entity row transitions to `editorial_review_status=approved` AND `publication_status=published`; (b) `revision_requested` → entity row transitions to `editorial_review_status=revision_requested`; the underlying capability is re-invoked (cost-charged again to Platform Marketing) and a new draft is queued; (c) `rejected` → entity row transitions to `editorial_review_status=rejected` AND `publication_status=archived`; the AIOperation is reversed via §34.11 Outcome Resolver (cost still applies to Platform Marketing per §21.4.3 anti-spam controls section). For M12, `approved` requires BOTH `editorial_marketing_reviewer_id` AND `editorial_marketing_reviewed_at` AND `editorial_finance_reviewer_id` AND `editorial_finance_reviewed_at` non-null per §4.4.15 dual-sign-off.
5. **Publish.** On approval, the publish handler (a) re-runs the §48.6.4 k-anonymity render gate, (b) re-runs the §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out resweep, (c) materializes `schema_org_payload_json` per §48.6.1, (d) writes `last_published_at`, (e) busts the §31 edge cache. Failure of any gate at this final step transitions the entity to `revision_requested` and notifies the reviewer.
6. **SLA monitoring.** A queue-depth alert fires per §48.4 (existing pattern) at >20 tasks pending >7 days; a per-task age alert fires at task age >SLA threshold. The Ops Marketing dashboard (§43.1) surfaces these.
7. **Auto-escalation.** A task in `under_review` with `claimed_at` >24h ago and no `last_reviewer_activity_at` within 24h auto-escalates to a queue-supervisor role (`ops_marketing_supervisor` — Authored Extension #22; Appendix J `ops_role` enum extension) AND emits `editorial_review_task_auto_escalated` (Appendix G — new).
8. **Bypass conditions.** Two bypass conditions apply: (a) M9 / M10 minor-update bypass when `refresh_diff_score < 0.10` per existing §4.4.12 / §4.4.13 acceptance criteria — the entity transitions straight from `pending_review` to `published` without a human reviewer, the `EditorialReviewTask` is closed with `decision=auto_approved_minor_update`, AND the `auto_approved_at` timestamp is recorded; (b) M11 emergency-removal bypass when a vendor opt-out reduces non-suppressed `compared_seller_software_ids` count below 2 — the entity transitions to `archived` without a human reviewer per §4.4.14 archive rule.

#### 48.6.2.A EditorialReviewTask (New Entity; Platform-Scoped) {#48.6.2.A-editorialreviewtask}

**Authoring intent.** EditorialReviewTask is the persisted task row for every M9–M12 editorial review. Authoring it as a first-class entity (rather than a transient queue message) makes the editorial workflow auditable, reportable, SLA-monitorable, and re-runnable. The entity is platform-scoped (no `org_id`); read access is restricted to the four Ops roles listed above.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK, immutable | Standard. |
| `mechanic_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `marketplace_content_mechanic_kind` (new): `m9_category_page`, `m10_guide_page`, `m11_comparison_page`, `m12_market_intelligence_report`, `m13_heat_map_aggregation_card` (rare; only for featured-cell promo strips); required | Routes the task to the appropriate queue + role. |
| `target_entity_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `marketplace_content_entity_kind` (new): `category_page`, `guide_page`, `comparison_page`, `market_intelligence_report`, `heat_map_aggregation_card`; required | Mirrors `mechanic_kind` 1:1 today; separated for forward-extensibility. |
| `target_entity_id` | UUID (FK) | → CategoryPage / GuidePage / ComparisonPage / MarketIntelligenceReport / HeatMapAggregationCard; required | The reviewed entity row. |
| `target_entity_content_version` | String | Semver; required | The content version of the draft being reviewed; ensures concurrent re-generation doesn't lose review state. |
| `triggering_capability_id` | String | FK → §21.4.3 `capability_registry_entry`; required | Which `platform_marketing` capability produced the draft. |
| `triggering_ai_operation_id` | UUID (FK) | → §4.8.3 AIOperation; required | The specific AIOperation that produced the draft; enables §34.11 Outcome Resolver reversal on rejection. |
| `task_status` | Enum | Appendix J `editorial_review_task_status` (new): `queued`, `under_review`, `approved`, `revision_requested`, `rejected`, `auto_approved_minor_update`, `auto_archived_below_min_count`, `superseded_by_takedown`, `cancelled_by_ops`; required | Lifecycle. |
| `assigned_queue` | Enum | Appendix J `editorial_review_queue` (new): `m9_marketing`, `m10_marketing`, `m11_marketing`, `m12_marketing`, `m12_finance`, `m13_marketing`; required | Queue routing per mechanic + role. |
| `claimed_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → Ops User; required when `task_status ∈ {under_review, approved, revision_requested, rejected}` | Reviewer. |
| `claimed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | First claim. |
| `last_reviewer_activity_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Last UI interaction by `claimed_by_user_id` on this task; updated debounced 1/min. |
| `decision_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set on terminal decision. |
| `decision_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `editorial_review_decision_kind` (new): `approved`, `revision_requested`, `rejected`, `auto_approved_minor_update`, `auto_archived_below_min_count`, `cancelled`; nullable | Mirrors terminal `task_status`. |
| `rubric_evaluations_json` | JSON | ≤ 5,000 chars | Per-dimension pass/fail + per-failure rejection notes; schema is the RUBRIC v1.0 dimension list. |
| `editorial_rejection_reason` | String | 0–1,000 chars; nullable | Required when `decision_kind=rejected`; concatenated rubric-failure summaries. |
| `editorial_revision_request_note` | String | 0–1,000 chars; nullable | Required when `decision_kind=revision_requested`. |
| `editorial_rubric_version` | String | Semver; required | RUBRIC version applied; v7.0.0 seed: `1.0`. |
| `sla_due_at` | Timestamp | Required | Computed at queue: `created_at + sla_seconds_per_mechanic`. |
| `sla_breached_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when nightly sweep observes `now > sla_due_at AND task_status ∈ {queued, under_review}`. |
| `auto_escalated_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set on §48.6.2 auto-escalation. |
| `auto_escalated_to_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → Ops User | The supervisor who received the escalation. |
| `superseded_by_takedown_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → §48.6.3 MarketplaceContentTakedownRequest | When a takedown supersedes an in-flight editorial review, the task transitions to `superseded_by_takedown` AND points back to the takedown row. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | Standard | Standard pattern | `created_by` is `system_content_worker` for AI-triggered drafts. |

**Scope isolation.** Platform-scoped (no `org_id`). Read access: the four Ops roles listed above plus Sourcera internal Ops dashboards (§43.1, Summary Summary §6.36). Customer-side read access: NONE (the editorial workflow is internal Ops). Cross-Org enumeration is structurally impossible (no `org_id`).

**Required indexes.** `(assigned_queue, task_status, sla_due_at)` (queue scan per role); `(target_entity_id, target_entity_content_version)` (per-entity audit); `(triggering_ai_operation_id)` UNIQUE (1:1 with AIOperation); `(sla_breached_at) WHERE sla_breached_at IS NOT NULL` (sparse; SLA-breach reporting); `(claimed_by_user_id, last_reviewer_activity_at DESC)` (per-reviewer activity).

**Retention.** 7 years (Ops audit + financial-reconciliation relevance for §21.4.3 cost-center routing + §34.11 Outcome Resolver settlement traceability). DSAR pseudonymization applies to `claimed_by_user_id`, `auto_escalated_to_user_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by` per §6.8 — but the rubric evaluations and decision-trail are preserved per platform-integrity exemption per §45.1.

**EditorialReviewTask Lifecycle State Machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `queued` | Draft entity row written by `platform_marketing` AIOperation | Capability invocation succeeds | `sla_due_at` computed. |
| `queued` | `under_review` | Reviewer clicks "Claim" | Reviewer holds appropriate role for `assigned_queue` | `claimed_by_user_id`, `claimed_at` populated. |
| `queued` | `auto_approved_minor_update` | Refresh-diff bypass condition met (M9 / M10 only) | `refresh_diff_score < 0.10` | Skip human review; entity transitions to `published`. |
| `queued` | `auto_archived_below_min_count` | M11 emergency removal | Non-suppressed comparison count drops below 2 | Skip human review; entity transitions to `archived`. |
| `queued` | `superseded_by_takedown` | A takedown referencing this entity is filed AND in `under_review` | Takedown precedence rule per §48.6.3 | Task closes; takedown adjudication takes precedence. |
| `queued`, `under_review` | `cancelled_by_ops` | Ops cancel | `ops_marketing_supervisor` OR higher | `decision_kind=cancelled`. |
| `under_review` | `approved` | Reviewer submits approval | All RUBRIC v1.0 dimensions pass; for M12, both Marketing AND Finance approvals required | Entity transitions to `published`; publish gates re-run per §48.6.2 step 5. |
| `under_review` | `revision_requested` | Reviewer submits revision request | At least one RUBRIC dimension fails AND reviewer chooses revision over rejection | Entity transitions to `revision_requested`; underlying capability re-invoked. |
| `under_review` | `rejected` | Reviewer submits rejection | At least one RUBRIC dimension fails AND reviewer chooses rejection | Entity transitions to `rejected`; AIOperation reversed via §34.11. |
| `under_review` | `superseded_by_takedown` | Takedown filed during review | Per §48.6.3 precedence rule | Same as queued→superseded. |
| `under_review` | (auto-escalation; same status) | `last_reviewer_activity_at + 24h < now` | Auto-escalation worker | `auto_escalated_at`, `auto_escalated_to_user_id` populated; `assigned_queue` unchanged. |
| `approved`, `revision_requested`, `rejected`, `auto_approved_minor_update`, `auto_archived_below_min_count`, `superseded_by_takedown`, `cancelled_by_ops` | (terminal) | n/a | Append-only post-terminal | Re-review of the same entity content version is forbidden; refresh produces a NEW EditorialReviewTask row with a new `target_entity_content_version`. |

**Invariants.** (a) `decision_at` is non-null IFF `task_status ∈ terminal`. (b) `claimed_by_user_id` is non-null whenever `task_status ∈ {under_review, approved, revision_requested, rejected}`. (c) `sla_breached_at` MAY be set independently of terminal status (a task may breach SLA and still complete; the breach is a permanent observation). (d) For M12 tasks, terminal `approved` requires the entity row's `editorial_marketing_reviewer_id` AND `editorial_finance_reviewer_id` AND timestamps both populated — the publish gate enforces.

#### 48.6.2.B SLA, Queue Routing, and Escalation Defaults {#48.6.2.B-editorial-sla-defaults}

| Mechanic | Queue | SLA (queued → terminal) | Auto-escalation if `under_review > N hours idle` | Reviewer rate-limit (per Ops user) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| M9 CategoryPage | `m9_marketing` | 5 business days | 24h | 8 approvals / 24h |
| M10 GuidePage | `m10_marketing` | 5 business days | 24h | 4 approvals / 24h (longer-form) |
| M11 ComparisonPage | `m11_marketing` | 5 business days | 24h | 6 approvals / 24h |
| M12 MarketIntelligenceReport (Marketing leg) | `m12_marketing` | 10 business days | 48h | 2 approvals / 24h |
| M12 MarketIntelligenceReport (Finance leg) | `m12_finance` | 10 business days | 48h | 2 approvals / 24h |
| M13 HeatMapAggregationCard | `m13_marketing` | 3 business days | 24h | 12 approvals / 24h |

Per-reviewer rate limits exist to discourage rubber-stamping; breaches emit `editorial_review_task_reviewer_rate_limit_hit` (Appendix G — new) and queue the additional reviews to a deferred-queue requiring supervisor pre-clearance.

### 48.6.3 Cross-Mechanic Takedown & Appeal Flow {#48.6.3-cross-mechanic-takedown-appeal-flow}

**Authoring intent.** Public Marketplace content (M9–M13) is occasionally subject to takedown requests from vendors, customers, or third parties on grounds of legal claim (DMCA, trademark, defamation), factual inaccuracy, GDPR data-subject claim, vendor opt-out breach, or competitive harm. §48.6.3 authors a single cross-mechanic takedown / appeal entity + workflow that applies to all M9–M13 publications. The flow is distinct from the §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Registry (which is a vendor-self-service global suppression flag) — takedowns are per-page, adjudicated, optionally appealable.

**New entity: MarketplaceContentTakedownRequest (Platform-Scoped, Public-Filable, Ops-Adjudicated).** Because takedown filers may be non-Sourcera users (a third-party legal counsel for a vendor not on the platform; a private individual filing GDPR data-subject claims), the entity supports anonymous filing via the public takedown endpoint with an email-verification round trip; it ALSO supports authenticated filing from any Sourcera user.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK, immutable | Standard. |
| `target_mechanic_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `marketplace_content_mechanic_kind` (per §48.6.2.A); required | Which mechanic is being targeted. |
| `target_entity_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `marketplace_content_entity_kind`; required | Mirrors `target_mechanic_kind` 1:1. |
| `target_entity_id` | UUID (FK) | → CategoryPage / GuidePage / ComparisonPage / MarketIntelligenceReport / HeatMapCell; required | The targeted page row. |
| `target_entity_content_version` | String | Semver; required | The content version observed by the filer at filing time. |
| `target_entity_canonical_url` | String | Valid HTTPS URL; ≤ 2,000 chars; required | The canonical URL the filer is targeting (denormalized for filer-friendliness). |
| `filer_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `takedown_filer_kind` (new): `anonymous_third_party`, `authenticated_sourcera_user`, `verified_vendor_legal_counsel`, `regulator`, `internal_ops`; required | Filer category. |
| `filer_email` | String | Valid email; ≤ 320 chars; required for `anonymous_third_party` and `verified_vendor_legal_counsel` filers; nullable for `internal_ops` | Verified via email round-trip. |
| `filer_email_verified_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set on email verification; required before adjudication for non-`internal_ops` filers. |
| `filer_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → User | Set for `authenticated_sourcera_user` filers. |
| `filer_org_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → Organization | Set for `authenticated_sourcera_user` filers. |
| `filer_display_name` | String | 1–120 chars; required | Filer name (used in adjudication audit). |
| `filer_legal_capacity_note` | String | 0–500 chars | Nullable for non-legal filers; required for `verified_vendor_legal_counsel` (e.g., "External counsel for Vendor X, retained 2026-01-15"). |
| `takedown_reason_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `takedown_reason_kind` (new): `legal_dmca`, `legal_trademark_infringement`, `legal_defamation_claim`, `factual_inaccuracy`, `gdpr_data_subject_request`, `vendor_opt_out_breach`, `competitive_harm_claim`, `outdated_information`, `other`; required | Why takedown is requested. |
| `takedown_reason_note` | String | 30–4,000 chars; required | Free-text justification; required even for enumerated reasons. |
| `supporting_evidence_attachments_json` | JSON | ≤ 10,000 chars (URL list to S3 attachments); ≤ 10 attachments per filing | Filer-uploaded supporting documents (legal letters, screenshots, etc.); attachments live in §6.7 audit-log-paired S3 bucket. |
| `requested_remedy_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `takedown_requested_remedy_kind` (new): `full_archive`, `targeted_redaction_of_specific_section`, `targeted_redaction_of_vendor_name`, `correction_publication`, `right_of_reply_addition`; required | Filer's requested remedy. |
| `requested_remedy_note` | String | 0–2,000 chars | Detail on requested remedy. |
| `takedown_status` | Enum | Appendix J `takedown_status` (new): `submitted_pending_email_verification`, `submitted_verified_pending_triage`, `under_review`, `accepted_redacted`, `accepted_archived`, `accepted_correction_published`, `accepted_right_of_reply_added`, `rejected_no_violation`, `rejected_insufficient_evidence`, `superseded_by_vendor_opt_out`, `appealed_pending_review`, `appeal_upheld`, `appeal_rejected`, `withdrawn_by_filer`; required | Lifecycle. |
| `triaged_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when an `ops_legal_takedown_admin` claims the task. |
| `triaged_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → Ops User | Triager. |
| `decision_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set on initial decision. |
| `decision_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → Ops User | Adjudicator. |
| `decision_rationale` | String | 30–4,000 chars; nullable | Required when `takedown_status ∈ accepted_*, rejected_*`. |
| `decision_remedy_applied_kind` | Enum | Same as `requested_remedy_kind`; nullable | What remedy was actually applied (may differ from requested). |
| `decision_remedy_applied_note` | String | 0–2,000 chars | Detail on applied remedy. |
| `appeal_filed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set when the filer (OR the affected vendor, if different) files an appeal. |
| `appeal_filed_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → User | Authenticated appeal filer. |
| `appeal_filed_by_email` | String | Valid email; nullable | Anonymous appeal filer email. |
| `appeal_rationale` | String | 30–4,000 chars; nullable | Required when `appeal_filed_at` is non-null. |
| `appeal_decision_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set on appeal decision. |
| `appeal_decision_by_user_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → Ops User | Appeal adjudicator (MUST be different from initial `decision_by_user_id` — separation of duties). |
| `appeal_decision_rationale` | String | 30–4,000 chars; nullable | Required when `appeal_decision_at` is non-null. |
| `affected_vendor_org_ids` | Array[UUID] | 0–10 entries; FKs → Organization | Vendor Orgs whose names appear on the targeted page; populated at triage. Relevant for opt-out collision detection AND vendor-side notification. |
| `is_legally_binding` | Boolean | Default false | True for `legal_dmca`, `legal_trademark_infringement`, `legal_defamation_claim`, `gdpr_data_subject_request`, `regulator` filings — these have shorter SLAs AND stricter adjudication standards. |
| `sla_due_at` | Timestamp | Required | Computed at filing: 5 business days for `is_legally_binding=true`, 10 business days otherwise. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | Standard | Standard pattern | `created_by` is the `system_takedown_intake_worker` for anonymous filings, OR the user for authenticated. |

**Scope isolation.** Platform-scoped. Read access: `ops_legal_takedown_admin`, `ops_marketing_editor`, `ops_marketing_supervisor`, plus Sourcera internal dashboards. Filer read access: only the filer's OWN row, surfaced via the public takedown-status endpoint authenticated by the original `filer_email_verification_token` per filing. Affected vendor Orgs receive notification AND limited read access (see Workflow below).

**Required indexes.** `(takedown_status, sla_due_at)`; `(target_entity_id, target_entity_content_version)`; `(filer_email_hash)` (sparse; anti-spam velocity); `(triaged_by_user_id, decision_at DESC)` (per-adjudicator caseload); `(is_legally_binding) WHERE takedown_status NOT IN (terminal)` (legal triage queue).

**Retention.** 10 years (legal-defensibility horizon). DSAR pseudonymization applies to filer identity fields per §6.8 — but adjudication-trail fields are preserved under the applicable §6.8.5 retained-row classes.

**Workflow.**

1. **Filing (anonymous).** Filer hits `https://reports.sourcera.io/takedowns/new` (a platform-scoped intake form; not Org-gated). Fills the form: target URL OR direct paste of the offending page URL, takedown reason, requested remedy, evidence attachments, contact email, contact name. Submission writes a row in `submitted_pending_email_verification` AND triggers an email-verification round trip (token in URL). Email-verification click transitions the row to `submitted_verified_pending_triage`.
2. **Filing (authenticated).** Authenticated Sourcera users may file directly from any M9–M13 public page via a "Report a Concern" link in the page footer; submission writes the row in `submitted_verified_pending_triage` (no email verification needed).
3. **Triage.** An `ops_legal_takedown_admin` claims the task within the SLA. Triage populates `affected_vendor_org_ids` from the targeted entity's referenced vendors. If `is_legally_binding=true`, the task is flagged for priority routing AND optionally routed to external counsel (Ops-managed; not modeled here).
4. **Adversarial-vendor notification.** On triage, every vendor in `affected_vendor_org_ids` receives a `takedown.affecting_your_vendor` notification (Appendix C extension below) with the takedown summary AND an opportunity to submit a response within 3 business days. The vendor's response is captured as a takedown comment row (a sub-resource not modeled in detail; ≤ 4,000 chars, ≤ 5 attachments).
5. **Adjudication.** The adjudicator weighs the takedown reason, evidence, vendor response (if any), and applicable RUBRIC v1.0 dimensions. Decisions:
   - `accepted_redacted` — targeted redaction of the specific section / vendor name in the targeted entity; the entity is republished with the new redaction map; the §4.4.8 opt-out registry MAY also be updated for the named vendor (with vendor consent OR per the adjudicator's authority — Ops policy).
   - `accepted_archived` — full archival of the targeted entity per the §4.4.x archive transition; the URL transitions to a friendly "Archived" landing page OR a 410-gone per per-mechanic policy.
   - `accepted_correction_published` — a Correction Notice is published as a sticky banner on the targeted entity AND a Correction History row is added to a per-entity correction log (sub-resource not modeled in detail).
   - `accepted_right_of_reply_added` — a Right-of-Reply section is added to the targeted entity OR a linked addendum page is published.
   - `rejected_no_violation` / `rejected_insufficient_evidence` — no remedy; filer notified; appeal eligible.
   - `superseded_by_vendor_opt_out` — if the vendor named in the takedown registers a Vendor Opt-Out before adjudication completes, the opt-out auto-supersedes the takedown; the takedown closes with this status; no further adjudication.
6. **Apply remedy.** On `accepted_*` decisions, the remedy is applied: entity row republished OR archived; Schema.org payload re-materialized; edge cache busted within 60 seconds; `EditorialReviewTask.task_status=superseded_by_takedown` if a review is in flight.
7. **Notify.** The filer receives a `takedown.decision` notification (Appendix C extension) with the decision rationale, applied remedy, AND appeal eligibility. Affected vendors receive `takedown.outcome.affecting_your_vendor` notification.
8. **Appeal.** Within 14 business days of `decision_at`, the filer (OR an affected vendor whose name was redacted/archived) MAY file an appeal. Appeal writes `appeal_filed_at`, `appeal_filed_by_user_id` / `appeal_filed_by_email`, `appeal_rationale`. Appeal triage routes to a DIFFERENT `ops_legal_takedown_admin` (separation of duties; the original adjudicator is excluded). Appeal decisions are terminal: `appeal_upheld` (the appeal succeeds; original remedy reversed AND a new remedy applied) OR `appeal_rejected` (original remedy stands).
9. **Withdrawal.** The filer MAY withdraw a takedown at any time before terminal decision; transitions to `withdrawn_by_filer`. Withdrawal does NOT entitle a refund (no payment is required for filing).

**Takedown precedence rule.** When a takedown is in `under_review` AND a §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out is filed by the same vendor named in the takedown, the opt-out auto-supersedes the takedown per §48.6.3 step 5 `superseded_by_vendor_opt_out`. When a takedown is in `under_review` AND an editorial review is concurrently in flight on the same `target_entity_id`, the takedown takes precedence: the EditorialReviewTask transitions to `superseded_by_takedown` AND the takedown adjudication runs first; if the takedown is rejected, a NEW EditorialReviewTask is queued for the entity's continued lifecycle.

**Anti-abuse.** The takedown intake endpoint has its own throttle (per §48.4.1 alignment): 5 takedowns per `filer_email_hash` per 24h; 50 per `filer_email_domain` per 24h; rate-limit breach returns HTTP 429 `marketplace_takedown_filer_rate_limit_exceeded` (Appendix I — new). The §48.4.4 content validators apply to `takedown_reason_note` AND `appeal_rationale` (XSS, profanity, prompt-injection). The §48.4.8 SuppressionList is checked at intake; suppressed `filer_email_hash` values are silently rejected per §48.4.8 confidentiality.

### 48.6.4 Cross-Mechanic k-Anonymity Render Gate {#48.6.4-cross-mechanic-k-anonymity-render-gate}

**Authoring intent.** §48.4.7 fixed the k=5 / k=10 / k=20 floor structure. §48.6.4 fixes the render-time function `render_with_k_anonymity_gate(entity, render_context) → (rendered_html, schema_org_payload, gate_evaluation_log)` that every M9–M13 render path MUST invoke. The gate exists because k-anonymity compliance is not just a publish-time check but a per-render check (a cohort that satisfied the floor at publish may shrink below it post-publish due to DSAR, opt-out cascade, or signal-decay).

**Gate algorithm.**

1. **Per-metric cohort enumeration.** For every aggregate metric on the entity's draft rendered output, compute the underlying cohort (distinct contributing Orgs, distinct contributing signals — whichever is the minimum applicable per Summary §3.5).
2. **Floor lookup.** Per the §48.4.7 tier table, look up the applicable floor: M9 = k=5; M10 = k=5 (per §4.4.13 `k_anon_floor`); M11 = k=5 (per §4.4.14 `k_anon_floor`); M12 = k=20 (per §4.4.15 `k_anon_floor`); M13 = k=10 (per §4.4.16 `k_anon_floor`).
3. **Per-metric gate evaluation.** Each metric is one of: (a) `pass` — cohort ≥ floor; rendered as-is; (b) `coarsen` — cohort < floor BUT a coarser-aggregation alternative is available (e.g., a per-industry metric where the per-industry cohort is below floor coarsens to per-macro-industry); rendered with the coarser bucket; (c) `suppress` — cohort < floor AND no coarser-aggregation alternative; rendered as `Insufficient data` placeholder; (d) `omit` — for Schema.org JSON-LD, the metric is omitted entirely (never rendered as `null`). The gate is per-metric, not per-page.
4. **Page-level fail-closed.** If after evaluation, ALL aggregate metrics on the page would render as `Insufficient data` (i.e., the entire page's aggregate-content is suppressed), the page MUST fail to render entirely AND return HTTP 410 `marketplace_content_k_anonymity_floor_breached_page_level` (Appendix I — new). This is the universal §48.6 acceptance criterion required by the prompt: a page fails to render if k-anonymity is not met at the page level. The render path returns a friendly "This page is temporarily unavailable due to insufficient data; please check back" surface for human visitors AND HTTP 410 + `noindex` for crawlers. Pure-editorial pages (no aggregate-derived metrics) pass the gate trivially per §4.4.12 / §4.4.13 acceptance criteria.
5. **Audit log.** Every gate evaluation writes a row to a per-entity `k_anon_render_gate_log` (sub-resource of the entity; ≤ 90-day retention; ≤ 100 most recent log rows per entity), capturing: `entity_id`, `entity_content_version`, `evaluated_at`, per-metric pass/coarsen/suppress/omit decisions, page-level pass/fail decision, `signal_freshness_max_seconds`. The log is never customer-readable.
6. **PostHog event.** Every gate evaluation emits `marketplace_content_k_anon_render_gate_evaluated` (Appendix G — new) with `entity_kind`, `entity_id`, `floor`, `metric_count_pass`, `metric_count_coarsen`, `metric_count_suppress`, `metric_count_omit`, `page_level_decision`. Page-level `fail` evaluations additionally emit `marketplace_content_k_anon_page_level_failure` (Appendix G — new) which is treated as an SIM signal class `k_anonymity_floor_violation` per §48.4.10.
7. **Notification on page-level fail.** When a page that was previously passing the gate transitions to page-level fail, the page's responsible Ops Marketing role pool receives a `marketplace_content.k_anon_page_level_failure` notification (Appendix C extension below) with the page URL, the failed metrics, and the next steps (republish with coarser aggregation, OR archive).

**Gate latency budget.** The gate MUST execute with p95 latency ≤ 50ms per render to avoid degrading the public-render performance budget per §44.1; cohort-size lookups are precomputed in a hot cache refreshed at each entity's `last_published_at` AND each §4.4.8 opt-out resweep AND each §6.8 DSAR completion.

### 48.6.5 M9 Per-Category Marketplace Landing Pages {#48.6.5-m9-per-category-marketplace-landing-pages}

#### Purpose

M9 publishes one Sourcera-owned, AI-generated, editorially-reviewed Marketplace landing page per active Marketplace Category — e.g., "Best HRMS for Mid-Market" — anchoring the long-tail SEO surface that drives L4 (Marketplace SEO Pull) per §48.2.5. The page combines (a) a hero narrative on the category's procurement landscape, (b) an FAQ block of 5–15 Q&A pairs powered by `category_faq_generation` (§21.4.3), (c) a vendor shortlist drawn from §27 Match Score top-N within the category, (d) a "How to evaluate" cross-link to the M10 GuidePage for the same category, (e) a "Compare top vendors" cross-link to the M11 ComparisonPage(s) anchored to the category, and (f) Schema.org structured data per §48.6.1 that signals the page's authority to search engines.

#### Trigger

M9 pages are generated under three conditions: (a) **Category bootstrap** — when an `ops_taxonomy_admin` activates a new Marketplace Category (per §4.4.7 state machine `inactive → active`), the bootstrap orchestrator queues a CategoryPage draft for the new category; (b) **Refresh cadence** — every 90 days (per §4.4.12 `refresh_cadence_days` default; range 14–365), the per-Category refresh worker runs `category_faq_generation` AND emits a refreshed draft for editorial review; (c) **Vendor-opt-out resweep** — when the §4.4.8 nightly resweep detects a new opt-out affecting an existing CategoryPage's `vendor_shortlist_seller_software_ids`, the resweep enqueues a re-render (NOT a re-generation; the FAQ + narrative content is preserved AND only the shortlist is mutated) AND a fast-path `EditorialReviewTask` with the M9 minor-update bypass condition (per §48.6.2 step 8a) when `refresh_diff_score < 0.10`.

#### Actor & Entity Schema

Cross-link to §4.4.12 CategoryPage entity (full field table). M9 mechanic does NOT introduce additional persisted fields beyond those in §4.4.12. The §48.6.2.A EditorialReviewTask row is created per draft per the editorial workflow.

**Acting entity.** `ops_marketing_editor` for editorial review; `ops_taxonomy_admin` for bootstrap-trigger; `system_content_worker` (a system identity, not a User) for AI-driven refresh-trigger writes; `ops_legal_takedown_admin` for takedown-driven mutations.

**Targeted entity.** §4.4.7 Marketplace Category (one CategoryPage per active Category, one-to-one on published rows per §4.4.12 indexes).

#### Generation + Editorial Workflow

1. **Trigger hits orchestrator.** Per the trigger conditions above, the M9 orchestrator enqueues a generation job. The job derives the input context: the Category record, the top-50 SellerSoftware rows in the Category by §27 Match Score (filtered to non-opted-out vendors per §4.4.8 active opt-out check), the §4.3 / §4.5 Workspace-aggregate signals for the Category (count of distinct buyer Orgs evaluating the Category, average evaluation duration, common requirement themes — per §4.4.12 k-anonymity floor).
2. **`category_faq_generation` invocation.** The capability (§21.4.3, `cost_center=platform_marketing`) is invoked with the input context. The AIOperation row is written to §4.8.3 with `cost_center=platform_marketing`; the wallet debit goes to the Sourcera Platform Marketing internal cost center (NOT a customer wallet). The capability output is the draft `body_sections_json`, `faq_payload_json`, `meta_title`, `meta_description`, `hero_copy_markdown`, `vendor_shortlist_seller_software_ids` (typically ≤ 10 of the top-50 input).
3. **k-anonymity pre-validation.** Per §48.6.4 gate, the orchestrator pre-validates that any aggregate metric in the draft passes k=5 floor; metrics that fail are coarsened OR suppressed before the draft is written.
4. **Draft entity write.** A CategoryPage row is written with `editorial_review_status=pending` AND `publication_status=pending_review`; `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` is stamped at draft-write; `referenced_vendor_opt_out_map_json` is materialized.
5. **EditorialReviewTask write.** A §48.6.2.A row is written for the draft, routed to `m9_marketing` queue; SLA = 5 business days.
6. **Editorial review.** An `ops_marketing_editor` claims the task, applies RUBRIC v1.0 (R1–R7 are mandatory; R8 is mandatory for refresh runs only), and decides. Approval transitions the entity to `published`.
7. **Refresh-only minor-update bypass.** Per §48.6.2 step 8a, refresh runs with `refresh_diff_score < 0.10` skip human review.
8. **Publish gate re-run.** On approval, the publish handler re-runs §48.6.4 k-anonymity gate, §4.4.8 opt-out resweep, §48.6.1 Schema.org materialization, and edge-cache bust per §31. Failure of any gate transitions the entity back to `revision_requested`.
9. **Render path.** Public anonymous viewers hit `https://marketplace.sourcera.io/categories/{slug}`. The render path re-runs §48.6.4 gate AND §4.4.8 opt-out resweep AND §48.6.1 Schema.org validation per render (cache-respecting per §31).

#### UX Surfaces

| Surface | §3.3 Pattern | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Public CategoryPage (anonymous) | Custom marketing-domain template; per §1.6 marketing domain | No buyer/seller-app chrome; SEO-optimized layout: hero + FAQ + vendor shortlist + cross-links to M10/M11/M12. |
| Ops Console > Marketplace Content > CategoryPages (Ops admin) | `Sidebar Navigation + Inline Table` per §3.3.1 | Per-row: category, slug, last_published_at, editorial_review_status, k_anon_satisfied, view_count_30d, takedown_count_30d, actions (approve, reject, force-refresh, archive). |
| Editorial Review Modal | `Modal + Split View` per §3.3.3 | Left: rendered preview iframe; Right: RUBRIC v1.0 checklist with per-dimension pass/fail toggles + per-failure rejection notes. |
| Takedown Submission Form (anonymous) | Single-CTA full-page route | Per §48.6.3 intake endpoint. |
| Mobile parity | Per §3.4 Mobile Translation | Public CategoryPage responsive; Ops admin surfaces are desktop-only per §3.4 (Ops Console is not mobile-supported). |

**Empty / error / loading states.** Pre-bootstrap (Category is `active` but no CategoryPage yet) renders a "Category page coming soon" placeholder for human visitors AND HTTP 503 + `noindex` for crawlers. Post-archive (Category deprecated) renders a 301 redirect to the successor Category's CategoryPage per §4.4.12 acceptance criterion #4. k-anonymity page-level failure (per §48.6.4 gate) renders the friendly "Temporarily unavailable" surface AND HTTP 410.

**Accessibility (§37.1).** Public CategoryPage MUST meet WCAG 2.1 AA: semantic HTML for FAQ accordion (`<details>` / `<summary>` OR `aria-expanded` on button); alt text on vendor logos; keyboard-navigable accordion; contrast-compliant; tab-order linear from top to bottom.

#### Data Collected / Retained

Cross-link to §4.4.12 entity field table for persisted fields. Anonymous viewer IP addresses are SHA-256-hashed before storage per §4.3.18; raw IPs never persist. View counts are debounced 1/min/IP-hash. Schema.org payload is re-materialized per publish AND per render (cache-respecting); never cached beyond 60 seconds at the §31 edge.

**Residency.** CategoryPage rows are platform-scoped (no `org_id`); content is rendered globally from a global edge cache. Underlying signal cohort is global by default but MAY be restricted to a region per a future §47.4 expansion (Known Gap noted in RECONCILIATION.md — full per-region M9 not in v7.0.0 scope; M9 v7 = global only).

#### Anti-Abuse Controls

1. **§48.4.4 content validators** — applied to all draft text fields at editorial review (XSS sanitizer, structured-data injection guard, PII detector, profanity / hate-speech classifier, prompt-injection scanner, off-topic spam classifier). Failures block the publish gate.
2. **§4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Registry** — pre-applied at draft generation; re-applied at publish; re-applied retroactively at every nightly resweep (per §4.4.12 failure mode #3); never overridable by an editor.
3. **§48.6.4 k-anonymity render gate** — every render evaluates per-metric AND page-level k=5 floor; page-level fail returns HTTP 410.
4. **§48.6.2 editorial reviewer rate-limit** — 8 approvals / 24h per `ops_marketing_editor`.
5. **§48.6.3 takedown intake throttle** — 5 takedowns / `filer_email_hash` / 24h.
6. **§48.4.7 k-anon cohort drift detection** — nightly job per §4.4.12 failure mode #2 sweeps existing CategoryPages for cohort drift; transitions to `pending_review` if drift breaks the floor.
7. **`category_faq_generation` reversal-rate alarm** — per §21.4.3 anti-spam controls, reversal rate > 5% over 7 days raises a §43 P2 alert.
8. **Schema.org payload validator** — per §48.6.1 contract; failures block the publish gate.

#### Plan Gating & Cost-Center Routing

M9 is a Sourcera-owned mechanic; no customer plan tier gates it AND no customer wallet is debited. Every `category_faq_generation` AIOperation is written to §4.8.3 with `cost_center=platform_marketing` per §21.4.3 cost-center accounting rule; the operation is excluded from customer-facing billing surfaces (§4.8.1 read serializer; `GET /v1/billing/operations`); the QA test `aiop_platform_marketing_excluded_from_customer_ledger` (§21.4.3) asserts. The cost is reported to the Sourcera Platform Marketing internal cost-center via Summary Summary §6.36 internal dashboards. The Outcome Resolver (§34.11) settles `category_faq_generation` per the §21.4.5 Outcome Signals row (accepted = FAQ block published after editorial review within 30d; rejected = editorial rejection OR no publish within 30d; auto-accept after 30d).

The §5.11 Feature Access Matrix is updated to include the rows: "Approve M9 CategoryPage draft" (✓ for `ops_marketing_editor`, `ops_marketing_supervisor`; ✗ for everyone else); "Force-refresh M9 CategoryPage" (✓ for `ops_marketing_editor`, `ops_taxonomy_admin`); "Archive M9 CategoryPage" (✓ for `ops_marketing_supervisor`, `ops_legal_takedown_admin`).

#### Telemetry Events

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `m9_category_page_draft_generated` | `category_faq_generation` AIOperation completes | `category_page_id`, `category_id`, `content_version`, `vendor_shortlist_count`, `faq_pair_count`, `underlying_signal_count`, `is_refresh ∈ {true, false}` |
| `m9_category_page_editorial_decision` | Editorial review terminal decision | `category_page_id`, `editorial_review_task_id`, `decision_kind`, `claimed_by_user_id`, `time_to_decision_seconds`, `rubric_dimensions_failed[]` |
| `m9_category_page_published` | Publish handler successfully writes `last_published_at` | `category_page_id`, `category_id`, `content_version`, `is_first_publish ∈ {true, false}`, `republish_due_to ∈ {refresh_cadence, opt_out_resweep, takedown_remedy, manual_force_refresh}` |
| `m9_category_page_view_recorded` | Anonymous render (debounced 1/min/IP-hash) | `category_page_id`, `referrer_kind ∈ {organic_search, direct, social, internal_link, other}`, `is_unique_30d` (Boolean) |
| `m9_category_page_vendor_opt_out_resweep_applied` | Nightly resweep changes the rendered shortlist | `category_page_id`, `prior_redacted_vendor_count`, `new_redacted_vendor_count`, `delta` |
| `m9_category_page_archived` | Archive (Category deprecated OR takedown) | `category_page_id`, `archive_reason ∈ {category_deprecated, takedown_accepted_archived, ops_force_archive}` |
| `m9_category_page_k_anon_render_gate_evaluated` | Per render | Per §48.6.4 emit shape |

#### Notifications Fired

New notification kinds are registered in Appendix C `v7.2.0-REM Phase 8.3 Notification Catalog P1 Additions`.

#### Webhooks Fired

Per §31.1 transport semantics. All M9–M13 webhooks use the `marketplace_content_domain` event class (Appendix J `webhook_event_class` extension below). These are PLATFORM-scoped (not Org-scoped) — they fire to a Sourcera-internal webhook endpoint by default; Ops MAY configure additional destinations via `marketplace_content_webhook_destination` rows (sub-resource not modeled in detail).
