#### Acceptance Criteria

1. M9 CategoryPage publication MUST require `editorial_review_status=approved` UNLESS the §48.6.2 step 8a minor-update bypass condition is met (`refresh_diff_score < 0.10`); attempts to publish without satisfying one of these MUST return HTTP 422 `m9_category_page_publish_requires_editorial_approval` (Appendix I — new).
2. M9 CategoryPage MUST fail to render at the public URL with HTTP 410 `marketplace_content_k_anonymity_floor_breached_page_level` if the §48.6.4 k-anonymity render gate evaluates page-level fail (i.e., all aggregate metrics on the page would suppress); the friendly "temporarily unavailable" surface MUST also include `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`.
3. Every `category_faq_generation` AIOperation MUST be tagged `cost_center=platform_marketing` in the §4.8.3 ledger; rows with `cost_center=customer_billed` for this capability MUST be flagged AND reversed via §34.11 (the QA test `aiop_platform_marketing_excluded_from_customer_ledger` from §21.4.3 covers).
4. A referenced SellerSoftware acquiring an active opt-out MUST cause the CategoryPage to redact the vendor row within 15 minutes (per §4.4.12 failure mode #3) AND emit `category_page.vendor_redacted` (existing per §4.4.12 acceptance criterion #3) AND `m9_category_page_vendor_opt_out_resweep_applied`.
5. Category deprecation MUST transition all CategoryPages for that Category to `archived` within 24 hours AND install a 301 redirect to the successor Category's CategoryPage (per §4.4.12 acceptance criterion #4).
6. Editorial review SLA breach (>5 business days in `queued ∪ under_review`) MUST surface in the Ops Marketing dashboard (§43.1) AND emit `editorial_review_task_sla_breached` (Appendix G — new) within 1 hour of breach.
7. Takedown remedy applied to an M9 page MUST bust the §31 edge cache within 60 seconds AND re-materialize the §48.6.1 Schema.org payload AND emit `marketplace_content.m9.category_page.takedown_remedy_applied` webhook.
8. `EditorialReviewTask` rows for M9 MUST be queryable per `(assigned_queue=m9_marketing, task_status=queued, sla_due_at)` with p95 latency ≤ 100ms.
9. Schema.org JSON-LD on every published M9 page MUST validate against §48.6.1 contract AND the open-source Schema.org Validator; QA gate runs on every publish.
10. The §48.6.2 per-reviewer rate limit (8 M9 approvals / 24h per `ops_marketing_editor`) MUST be enforced atomically; breaches return HTTP 429 `editorial_review_task_reviewer_rate_limit_exceeded` (Appendix I — new).

#### Failure Modes Addressed

1. **`category_faq_generation` produces content with a hallucinated vendor capability claim.** Resolved: RUBRIC v1.0 R1 (Factual Accuracy) requires every claim to be sourced from a citable Sourcera-internal signal OR a clearly-attributed external source; failure rejects the draft AND requires re-generation. The reviewer's rubric annotation captures the specific unsourced claim. The reversed AIOperation per §34.11 flags the capability quality issue; reversal rate >5% over 7 days raises a §43 P2 alert per §21.4.3.
2. **Vendor opt-out filed mid-editorial-review breaks the rendered shortlist.** Resolved: the opt-out resweep job (per §4.4.12 failure mode #3 + §48.6 cross-mechanic invariant (e)) re-applies the opt-out to the in-flight draft; the editorial review surface updates in real-time; the reviewer is notified via `m9.category_page.vendor_opt_out_resweep_applied`; the reviewer MAY proceed (the redaction is automatic) OR reject (force a re-generation with the post-opt-out vendor pool).
3. **k-anon cohort shrinks below floor post-publish (DSAR cascade).** Resolved: §48.6.4 page-level fail-closed returns HTTP 410 + `noindex`; the responsible Ops Marketing team is notified via `m9.category_page.k_anon_page_level_failure`; the page's underlying signal pool is re-evaluated; either the cohort recovers OR the page is archived OR the page is republished with all aggregates suppressed (pure-editorial subset).
4. **Editorial reviewer is unavailable for >24 hours mid-review.** Resolved: §48.6.2 step 7 auto-escalation transitions the task to `ops_marketing_supervisor` after 24h idle; SLA timer continues running; `editorial_review_task_auto_escalated` PostHog event is emitted for Ops dashboard surfacing.
5. **Takedown filed concurrently with an editorial review.** Resolved: §48.6.3 takedown precedence rule transitions the EditorialReviewTask to `superseded_by_takedown`; the takedown adjudication runs first; if takedown is accepted, the entity transitions per the remedy; if takedown is rejected, a NEW EditorialReviewTask is queued.

### 48.6.6 M10 "How to Evaluate [X]" Guides {#48.6.6-m10-how-to-evaluate-x-guides}

#### Purpose

M10 publishes one Sourcera-owned, AI-generated, editorially-reviewed long-form (2,000–80,000 chars) buying guide per active Marketplace Category — e.g., "How to Evaluate HRMS for Mid-Market." The mechanic exists to capture long-tail SEO traffic for buyer-intent queries that don't map to the M9 vendor-shortlist surface but DO map to the procurement-process surface (e.g., "what to look for in an HRMS," "HRMS evaluation checklist," "HRMS RFP template"). M10 cross-links to the M9 CategoryPage AND the M11 ComparisonPage(s) for the same category, completing the SEO compounding effect per Summary §3.4.

#### Trigger

M10 pages are generated under three conditions: (a) **Category bootstrap** — same as M9, but with a 2-week lag after M9 to avoid simultaneous review burden on `ops_marketing_editor` queue; (b) **Refresh cadence** — every 180 days (per §4.4.13 `refresh_cadence_days` default; range 30–730), the per-Category refresh worker runs `guide_refresh_analysis` to compute `refresh_diff_score`; if the score is ≥ 0.10, a full refresh draft is produced via `guide_draft_generation` AND queued for review; if < 0.10, the minor-update bypass per §48.6.2 step 8a auto-publishes; (c) **Manual force-refresh** — an `ops_marketing_editor` may force-refresh out of cadence (e.g., when category-relevant regulation changes) via the API endpoint registered in M9's API table (the same endpoint serves all M9–M12 mechanics).

#### Actor & Entity Schema

Cross-link to §4.4.13 GuidePage entity. M10 mechanic does NOT introduce additional persisted fields beyond §4.4.13. The §48.6.2.A EditorialReviewTask row is created per draft.

**Acting entity.** Same role pool as M9 (`ops_marketing_editor` for review; `ops_taxonomy_admin` for bootstrap; `system_content_worker` for refresh; `ops_legal_takedown_admin` for takedown remedies).

**Targeted entity.** §4.4.7 Marketplace Category (one GuidePage per active Category, one-to-one on published rows per §4.4.13 indexes).

#### Generation + Editorial Workflow

1. **Trigger hits orchestrator.** Per the trigger conditions, the M10 orchestrator enqueues a generation OR refresh-analysis job. Generation invokes `guide_draft_generation` (full draft); refresh invokes `guide_refresh_analysis` (which produces ONLY the `refresh_diff_score` AND a flagged-section list — NOT a full draft).
2. **`guide_refresh_analysis` invocation (refresh-only).** The capability is invoked with the existing GuidePage content + the latest §27 Match Score top-50 vendors + the latest §16 Org Intelligence aggregates. Output: `refresh_diff_score ∈ [0.0, 1.0]` AND a list of guide sections flagged for rewrite. If `refresh_diff_score < 0.10` AND the flagged section list is empty AND `editorial_review_status=not_required` is configured for this guide (Ops-toggleable), the minor-update bypass triggers per §48.6.2 step 8a; the entity's `last_refreshed_at` is updated; no new content is produced. If `refresh_diff_score ≥ 0.10`, `guide_draft_generation` is invoked next.
3. **`guide_draft_generation` invocation (full draft).** The capability is invoked with the input context (existing GuidePage, flagged sections, full vendor + signal pool). Output: a full new `body_markdown` (2,000–80,000 chars) + `toc_json` + `meta_title` + `meta_description`. The AIOperation rows for both `guide_refresh_analysis` AND `guide_draft_generation` are written with `cost_center=platform_marketing`.
4. **k-anonymity pre-validation.** Per §48.6.4 gate, any aggregate metric in the draft passes k=5 floor.
5. **Draft entity write.** GuidePage row is updated with the new draft content (or a new row is written for first-bootstrap); `editorial_review_status=pending`, `publication_status=pending_review`, `refresh_diff_score` populated.
6. **EditorialReviewTask write.** Routed to `m10_marketing` queue; SLA = 5 business days.
7. **Editorial review.** RUBRIC v1.0 R1–R7 mandatory; R8 (refresh-diff justification) mandatory for refresh runs.
8. **Publish gate re-run.** Same as M9 step 8.
9. **Render path.** Public viewers hit `https://marketplace.sourcera.io/guides/{slug}`. Same render-time gate execution as M9.

#### UX Surfaces

| Surface | §3.3 Pattern | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Public GuidePage (anonymous) | Custom marketing-domain template | Long-form article layout: `<article>` with table-of-contents sticky sidebar, anchor-link H2 sections, in-line vendor logos, FAQ block, cross-link to M9 + M11. |
| Ops Console > Marketplace Content > GuidePages | Same pattern as M9 | Per-row: category, slug, last_refreshed_at, refresh_diff_score, editorial_review_status, view_count_30d, takedown_count_30d. |
| Editorial Review Modal | Same pattern as M9 | Adds R8 dimension toggle for refresh runs. |
| Mobile parity | Per §3.4 | Long-form article is mobile-first; sticky TOC collapses to a hamburger overlay on mobile. |

**Empty / error / loading states.** Same as M9. Refresh-in-progress shows a per-page admin banner: "Refresh-analysis in progress (started {time} ago)."

**Accessibility (§37.1).** Long-form article MUST meet WCAG 2.1 AA: heading-level hierarchy preserved (H1 → H2 → H3 with no skipped levels); table-of-contents links MUST land on visible focus targets; in-line images MUST have alt text; reading-level target = grade 12 (Flesch-Kincaid grade 10–14 acceptable; >14 fails RUBRIC R6 and is rejected).

#### Data Collected / Retained

Cross-link to §4.4.13. Same residency posture as M9 (global only at v7.0.0).

#### Anti-Abuse Controls

Same as M9 (1)-(8), with one M10-specific addition:

9. **`guide_refresh_analysis` thrash detection** — per §4.4.13 failure mode #3, if the same GuidePage is rejected 3 times within 90 days, the refresh cadence is automatically extended by 30% AND the responsible Ops team is paged. The cadence-extension event emits `guide_refresh_cadence_auto_extended` (Appendix G — new).

#### Plan Gating & Cost-Center Routing

Same as M9. Both `guide_refresh_analysis` AND `guide_draft_generation` are `platform_marketing` per §21.4.3 and routed to the Sourcera Platform Marketing internal cost-center via §6.36. The §5.11 Feature Access Matrix is updated to include rows: "Approve M10 GuidePage draft" and "Force-refresh M10 GuidePage" (same role assignments as M9).

The §21.4.5 Outcome Signals row for `guide_draft_generation`: accepted = guide published after editorial review within 30d; rejected = editorial rejection OR no publish within 30d; auto-accept after 30d. For `guide_refresh_analysis`: accepted = refresh published OR explicit "no-action" confirmation within 14d; rejected = no editorial action within 14d; auto-accept after 14d.

#### Telemetry Events

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `m10_guide_page_refresh_analysis_run` | `guide_refresh_analysis` AIOperation completes | `guide_page_id`, `category_id`, `refresh_diff_score`, `flagged_section_count` |
| `m10_guide_page_draft_generated` | `guide_draft_generation` AIOperation completes | `guide_page_id`, `content_version`, `body_markdown_length_chars`, `is_first_publish` |
| `m10_guide_page_editorial_decision` | Editorial review terminal decision | `guide_page_id`, `editorial_review_task_id`, `decision_kind`, `time_to_decision_seconds`, `rubric_dimensions_failed[]` |
| `m10_guide_page_published` | Publish handler success | `guide_page_id`, `content_version`, `is_first_publish`, `republish_due_to` |
| `m10_guide_page_view_recorded` | Anonymous render (debounced 1/min/IP-hash) | `guide_page_id`, `referrer_kind`, `is_unique_30d`, `scroll_depth_pct_max` (for engagement) |
| `m10_guide_page_minor_update_bypass_triggered` | Refresh `refresh_diff_score < 0.10` triggers bypass | `guide_page_id`, `refresh_diff_score` |
| `guide_refresh_cadence_auto_extended` | Per §48.6.6 anti-abuse #9 | `guide_page_id`, `prior_cadence_days`, `new_cadence_days`, `consecutive_rejection_count` |

#### Notifications Fired

Same notification-kind structure as M9 (with `m10` prefix substitution). New notification kinds are registered in Appendix C `v7.2.0-REM Phase 8.3 Notification Catalog P1 Additions`.

#### Webhooks Fired

Same shape as M9 (with `m10.guide_page` substitution): `marketplace_content.m10.guide_page.published`, `.archived`, `.vendor_opt_out_applied`, `.takedown_remedy_applied`.

#### API Endpoints

The M9 endpoint table covers M10 by substitution: `/v1/ops/marketplace-content/guide-pages` replaces `/v1/ops/marketplace-content/category-pages`; the EditorialReviewTask endpoints are shared. The public render path is `https://marketplace.sourcera.io/guides/{slug}`.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. M10 GuidePage publication MUST require `editorial_review_status=approved` UNLESS the §48.6.2 step 8a minor-update bypass condition is met (`refresh_diff_score < 0.10` AND `editorial_review_status=not_required` configured); attempts to publish otherwise MUST return HTTP 422 `m10_guide_page_publish_requires_editorial_approval` (Appendix I — new).
2. M10 GuidePage MUST fail to render at the public URL with HTTP 410 if the §48.6.4 k-anonymity render gate evaluates page-level fail.
3. Publishing with `body_markdown` length <2,000 chars MUST be rejected with `guide_page_body_too_short` (existing per §4.4.13 acceptance criterion #1; HTTP 422 in Appendix I).
4. Minor-update bypass MUST be rejected when `refresh_diff_score ≥ 0.10` with `guide_page_editorial_required` (existing per §4.4.13 acceptance criterion #2; HTTP 409 in Appendix I).
5. Both `guide_draft_generation` AND `guide_refresh_analysis` AIOperations MUST be tagged `cost_center=platform_marketing` (per §4.4.13 acceptance criterion #3 + §21.4.3 routing).
6. `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` MUST be stamped at every publish AND every nightly opt-out resweep (per §4.4.13 acceptance criterion #4).
7. The §48.6.6 anti-abuse #9 cadence-extension MUST trigger after exactly 3 rejections within 90 days; QA test `m10_guide_refresh_cadence_thrash_detection` asserts.
8. Schema.org JSON-LD for M10 MUST include `Article` + `BreadcrumbList` + `HowTo` types per §48.6.1; QA gate validates per publish.
9. The `m10_guide_page_minor_update_bypass_triggered` event MUST be emitted within 5 seconds of bypass; the event drives the Ops Marketing dashboard's "auto-published refresh" tile.
10. `EditorialReviewTask` rate limit (4 M10 approvals / 24h per `ops_marketing_editor`) MUST be enforced atomically per §48.6.2.B.

#### Failure Modes Addressed

1. **`guide_draft_generation` produces content failing RUBRIC R6 reading-level (Flesch-Kincaid >14).** Resolved: RUBRIC R6 fail rejects the draft; reviewer requests revision; re-generation prompts the LLM with explicit reading-level constraint. Persistent reading-level failures (3 rejections within 30 days) extend the refresh cadence per anti-abuse #9 AND raise a §43 P2 alert for capability tuning.
2. **`guide_refresh_analysis` returns `refresh_diff_score=0.09` (just below bypass threshold) but a flagged section list is non-empty.** Resolved: the bypass condition requires BOTH `refresh_diff_score < 0.10` AND empty flagged section list per §48.6.6 step 2; this scenario does NOT bypass; `guide_draft_generation` is invoked next.
3. **External regulatory change makes the published guide materially out-of-date mid-cadence.** Resolved: an `ops_marketing_editor` triggers force-refresh via the API endpoint; force-refresh bypasses cadence AND invokes both refresh-analysis AND draft-generation; the new draft enters editorial review at the front of the queue (priority flag set on the EditorialReviewTask).
4. **Long-form draft exceeds 80,000-char §39 ceiling.** Resolved: the `guide_draft_generation` capability has an output-length post-processor that truncates to ≤ 80,000 chars at semantically-aware section boundaries; draft entity write rejects with HTTP 422 `guide_page_body_too_long` (new; Appendix I) if truncation produces an invalid TOC; reviewer notified to re-prompt.
5. **Takedown for factual inaccuracy in a single guide section.** Resolved: §48.6.3 step 5 `accepted_redacted` remedy targets the specific section; the GuidePage is republished with the section omitted OR replaced with a Correction Notice; the `referenced_vendor_opt_out_map_json` is unaffected (the takedown is not vendor-side).

### 48.6.7 M11 Software Comparison Pages {#48.6.7-m11-software-comparison-pages}

#### Purpose

M11 publishes one Sourcera-owned, AI-generated, editorially-reviewed side-by-side software comparison page per 2-to-5-product comparison pair — e.g., "Workday vs. ADP vs. Paylocity." The mechanic exists to capture high-intent SEO traffic (buyer-intent queries naming specific competing vendors) AND to harvest the §27 Match Score signal pool into a Marketplace surface that vendors can NOT directly author. Vendor opt-out is honored at the column level: an opted-out vendor's column is omitted entirely (NOT redacted to a "Vendor Opted Out" placeholder; per §4.4.14 + §48.6.1 cross-mechanic Schema.org rule #1). When the post-suppression non-opted-out vendor count drops below 2, the page archives per §4.4.14.

#### Trigger

M11 pages are generated under four conditions: (a) **Category bootstrap completion** — when the M9 + M10 pages for a Category are both published, the M11 orchestrator picks the top-N comparison pairs (default N=10 per Category) by a combination of search-volume signal (Ops-managed hot-comparison list) + §27 Match Score frequency, AND queues comparison drafts; (b) **Refresh cadence** — every 45 days (per §4.4.14 `refresh_cadence_days` default; range 14–180), the per-page refresh worker invokes `comparison_page_generation`; (c) **New vendor in category enters top-5** — when a SellerSoftware's §27 Match Score in a Category enters the top-5 AND no comparison page exists involving that vendor + a top-5 peer, the orchestrator queues a new comparison page; (d) **Manual force-refresh** — Ops-triggered.

#### Actor & Entity Schema

Cross-link to §4.4.14 ComparisonPage entity. M11 mechanic does NOT introduce additional persisted fields beyond §4.4.14.

**Acting entity.** Same role pool as M9 / M10. M11 introduces no new roles.

**Targeted entity.** A pair (or triple-to-5) of §4.4.9 SellerSoftware rows; comparison page is identified by a deterministic `slug` derived from the alphabetically-sorted SellerSoftware names.

**`comparison_page_generation` capability formalization.** Per §21.4.3, this capability is registered as a placeholder; M11 formalizes it: input = the 2-to-5 SellerSoftware rows + their §22 KB Capability Declarations + their §27 Match Score breakdowns; output = `comparison_matrix_json` (feature × product matrix, ≤ 80,000 chars) + `narrative_markdown` (intro + per-product pros/cons + recommendation, ≤ 20,000 chars) + `winner_by_use_case_json` (≤ 10,000 chars) + `meta_title` + `meta_description`. Sonnet-tier model recommended. Output validators enforce: every comparison-matrix cell carries an explicit source-reference; per-product pros/cons sections are balanced (≥ 1 pro AND ≥ 1 con per product, per RUBRIC R2 vendor-neutrality).

#### Generation + Editorial Workflow

1. **Trigger hits orchestrator.** Per the trigger conditions, the M11 orchestrator enqueues a generation job. The job derives the input context: the comparison-pair SellerSoftware rows; their §22.x KB Capability Declarations; their §27 Match Score breakdowns; the §16 Org Intelligence aggregates per Category; the §4.4.8 active opt-out check (any opted-out SellerSoftware in the input pair is excluded from generation; if exclusion drops the pair below 2 vendors, the job aborts AND emits `m11_comparison_page_generation_aborted_below_min_count`).
2. **`comparison_page_generation` invocation.** AIOperation written with `cost_center=platform_marketing`.
3. **k-anonymity pre-validation.** Per §48.6.4 gate, any aggregate metric (e.g., "X% of buyers in our Marketplace prefer Vendor A") passes k=5 floor.
4. **Output validation.** RUBRIC R2 vendor-neutrality is enforced at draft-write: the orchestrator counts pros AND cons per product; <1 pro OR <1 con per product fails the draft AND re-prompts the capability.
5. **Draft entity write.** ComparisonPage row written; `compared_seller_software_ids` populated; `suppressed_seller_software_ids` populated from the §4.4.8 opt-out check; `editorial_review_status=pending`.
6. **EditorialReviewTask write.** Routed to `m11_marketing` queue; SLA = 5 business days.
7. **Editorial review.** RUBRIC v1.0 R1–R7 mandatory; R8 mandatory for refresh runs. R2 (vendor-neutrality) is the most-critical dimension; any reviewer suspicion of imbalance MUST result in revision-request.
8. **Publish gate re-run.** Same as M9 step 8, plus the §4.4.14 archive-on-min-count check (non-suppressed count ≥ 2 required for publication).
9. **Render path.** Public viewers hit `https://marketplace.sourcera.io/compare/{slug}`. Same render-time gates as M9 + the §4.4.14 archive-on-min-count check at render-time (if a vendor opted out between cache TTL boundaries AND the count drops below 2, render returns HTTP 410 `comparison_page_archived_below_min_count` (new; Appendix I)).

#### UX Surfaces

| Surface | §3.3 Pattern | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Public ComparisonPage (anonymous) | Custom marketing-domain template | Side-by-side comparison layout: hero banner with product logos; comparison matrix as a sticky-header HTML table; per-product pros/cons as cards; per-use-case "Best for" recommendation cards; cross-link to M9 + M10. |
| Ops Console > Marketplace Content > ComparisonPages | Same pattern as M9 | Per-row: slug, compared products (with opt-out flag indicators), last_published_at, editorial_review_status, view_count_30d, takedown_count_30d. |
| Editorial Review Modal | Same pattern as M9 / M10 | Adds an explicit per-product pros/cons balance check UI. |
| Mobile parity | Per §3.4 | Comparison matrix transforms to a vertically-stacked per-product card list on mobile (matrix is unreadable on narrow screens). |

**Empty / error / loading states.** Below-min-count archived state renders a friendly "This comparison is no longer available; explore alternatives" surface with cross-links to M9 CategoryPages.

**Accessibility (§37.1).** Comparison matrix MUST be a properly-marked-up `<table>` with `<thead>` / `<tbody>` / `<th scope>`; all cells keyboard-navigable; alt text on product logos; WCAG 2.1 AA color contrast.

#### Data Collected / Retained

Cross-link to §4.4.14.

#### Anti-Abuse Controls

Same as M9 (1)-(8), with two M11-specific additions:

9. **Vendor-neutrality automated check** — at draft-write, the orchestrator counts pros AND cons per product; imbalanced drafts (any product with 0 pros OR 0 cons) are rejected pre-review AND re-prompt the capability. This is in addition to the human RUBRIC R2 check.
10. **Comparison-pair anti-collusion** — the orchestrator MAY NOT generate comparison pages that include only vendors from the same Org / parent-Org per §4.5.5 (a Sourcera-internal denylist mechanism prevents trivial "Vendor A vs Vendor A's reseller" pages); the denylist is Ops-managed.

#### Plan Gating & Cost-Center Routing

Same as M9. `comparison_page_generation` is `platform_marketing` per §21.4.3. The §21.4.5 Outcome Signals row: accepted = page published with ≥ 2 non-suppressed columns; rejected = insufficient non-opted-out vendors OR editorial rejection; auto-accept after 14d.

The §5.11 Feature Access Matrix is updated for: "Approve M11 ComparisonPage draft" and "Force-refresh M11 ComparisonPage" (same role assignments as M9 / M10).

#### Telemetry Events

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `m11_comparison_page_draft_generated` | `comparison_page_generation` AIOperation completes | `comparison_page_id`, `compared_seller_software_count`, `suppressed_seller_software_count_at_draft`, `is_refresh ∈ {true, false}` |
| `m11_comparison_page_generation_aborted_below_min_count` | Generation aborts at step 1 (post-opt-out exclusion) | `comparison_pair_attempted_seller_software_ids`, `surviving_count` |
| `m11_comparison_page_editorial_decision` | Editorial review terminal | Same shape as M9 |
| `m11_comparison_page_published` | Publish handler success | `comparison_page_id`, `non_suppressed_count_at_publish`, `is_first_publish`, `republish_due_to` |
| `m11_comparison_page_view_recorded` | Anonymous render | Same shape as M9 |
| `m11_comparison_page_archived_below_min_count` | Archive due to non-suppressed count <2 | `comparison_page_id`, `triggering_opt_out_seller_software_id` |
| `m11_comparison_page_vendor_neutrality_check_rejected` | Pre-review automated R2 check fails | `comparison_page_id`, `imbalanced_product_seller_software_id`, `pros_count`, `cons_count` |

#### Notifications Fired

Same notification-kind structure as M9 (with `m11` prefix). Adds:

- `m11.comparison_page.archived_below_min_count` — to `ops_marketing_editor` queue; in-app + email; immediate; explains which opt-out triggered the archive AND offers cross-link to M9 / M10 surfaces for the affected category.

#### Webhooks Fired

Same shape as M9 (with `m11.comparison_page` substitution). Adds `marketplace_content.m11.comparison_page.archived_below_min_count` per the failure mode above.

#### API Endpoints

Same endpoint shape as M9 with substitution: `/v1/ops/marketplace-content/comparison-pages`. Public render path: `https://marketplace.sourcera.io/compare/{slug}`.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. M11 ComparisonPage publication MUST require `editorial_review_status=approved`; attempts otherwise MUST return HTTP 422 `m11_comparison_page_publish_requires_editorial_approval` (Appendix I — new).
2. M11 ComparisonPage MUST fail to render at the public URL with HTTP 410 if the §48.6.4 k-anonymity render gate evaluates page-level fail.
3. Publication with `|compared_seller_software_ids| - |suppressed_seller_software_ids| < 2` MUST be rejected with `comparison_page_insufficient_vendors` (existing per §4.4.14 acceptance criterion #1; HTTP 409 in Appendix I).
4. `schema_org_payload_json` MUST never list an opted-out `Product`; the §4.4.14 + §48.6.1 cross-rule QA test asserts (per existing §4.4.14 acceptance criterion #2).
5. When a `suppressed_seller_software_ids` transition reduces non-suppressed count below 2, the page MUST archive + 410-gone within 15 minutes (per §4.4.14 acceptance criterion #3).
6. Editorial review MUST be completed before any publish (per §4.4.14 acceptance criterion #4).
7. Pre-review automated vendor-neutrality check MUST reject imbalanced drafts (any product with 0 pros OR 0 cons) AND emit `m11_comparison_page_vendor_neutrality_check_rejected`.
8. Comparison-pair anti-collusion check MUST reject pairs from the same Org / parent-Org per §48.6.7 anti-abuse #10; rejected pairs emit `m11_comparison_page_anti_collusion_check_rejected` (Appendix G — new).
9. Schema.org JSON-LD for M11 MUST include `ItemList` of `Product` with NO opted-out products AND per-product `Review` blocks per §48.6.1.
10. `comparison_page_generation` AIOperations MUST be tagged `cost_center=platform_marketing`.

#### Failure Modes Addressed

1. **All vendors in a comparison opt out simultaneously.** Resolved: the §4.4.14 archive-on-min-count transition fires; the page archives + 410-gones within 15 minutes; `m11_comparison_page_archived_below_min_count` notifies the Ops team. The `marketplace_content.m11.comparison_page.archived_below_min_count` webhook fires for downstream SEO-tooling consumers.
2. **`comparison_page_generation` produces a draft heavily favoring one vendor (RUBRIC R2 fail).** Resolved: the pre-review automated vendor-neutrality check (§48.6.7 anti-abuse #9) rejects imbalanced drafts; if the imbalance is subtle and passes automation, the human RUBRIC R2 check rejects in editorial review; persistent R2 failures (>5% of M11 drafts in 7 days) raise a §43 P2 alert for capability tuning.
3. **Vendor opt-out filed mid-render (between two render-cache TTLs) drops the non-suppressed count below 2.** Resolved: the render-time §4.4.14 archive-on-min-count check transitions the page to `archived` AND returns HTTP 410 immediately on the very next render after the resweep; the cache-TTL boundary is the §31 60-second edge cache. Vendors observing the archive transition receive `m11.comparison_page.archived_below_min_count` notification (if they are Sourcera Sellers) AND the page's incoming organic-search traffic gracefully degrades to a 410 + sitemap-removal cycle (per §27 SEO operations).
4. **A SellerSoftware referenced in a comparison is hard-purged via §4.4 lifecycle.** Resolved: per §4.4.14 failure mode #2, the element is removed from `compared_seller_software_ids`; the downstream min-count check fires; if the count drops below 2, the page archives.
5. **Editorial reviewer disagrees with AI-generated `winner_by_use_case_json`.** Resolved: per §4.4.14 failure mode #3, the editor MAY rewrite the field; the AIOperation cost is NOT reversed (the content is valid; human judgment diverges); the editor's rewrite is persisted via the EditorialReviewTask `editorial_revision_request_note`.

### 48.6.8 M12 Aggregate Market Intelligence Reports {#48.6.8-m12-aggregate-market-intelligence-reports}

#### Purpose

M12 publishes one Sourcera-owned, AI-generated, dual-Marketing-and-Finance-reviewed quarterly market-intelligence report per Marketplace Category — e.g., "HRMS Market Intelligence — Q2 2026." The mechanic exists to (a) capture high-authority SEO traffic for category-level analyst queries (e.g., "HRMS market trends 2026," "HRMS pricing benchmarks"), (b) provide a sales-collateral surface for Sourcera's own go-to-market motion, and (c) compound L4 + L10 by cross-Org aggregation that no single vendor can match. M12 enforces the strictest k-anonymity floor (k=20) AND a dual-sign-off editorial workflow (Marketing for tone + factual accuracy; Finance for pricing-band correctness + signal-cohort sufficiency).

#### Trigger

M12 reports are generated under one condition: **scheduled quarterly run.** A per-Category quarterly cron (`refresh_cadence_days=90`; per §4.4.15) invokes `market_intelligence_report` capability at the first-day-of-quarter UTC. Force-generation outside cadence is restricted to `ops_marketing_supervisor` AND requires a free-text rationale (logged to §6.7 audit log with `audit_action_type=m12_market_intel_force_generation`).

#### Actor & Entity Schema

Cross-link to §4.4.15 MarketIntelligenceReport entity. M12 mechanic does NOT introduce additional persisted fields.

**Acting entity.** `ops_marketing_editor` for the Marketing leg; `ops_marketing_finance_reviewer` (new role, Authored Extension #20) for the Finance leg; `system_content_worker` for refresh-trigger writes; `ops_marketing_supervisor` for force-generation OR cancel.

**Targeted entity.** §4.4.7 Marketplace Category (one report per Category per quarter, optionally per `residency_region_scope`).

#### Generation + Editorial Workflow

1. **Quarterly cron fires.** The M12 orchestrator enumerates active Categories AND their `residency_region_scope` (default `global`; OR per-region per Ops configuration). For each (Category, scope) tuple, it enqueues a generation job.
2. **Pre-generation k-anonymity gate.** Per §4.4.15 k-anonymity enforcement, the orchestrator computes the underlying signal cohort for the (Category, scope, quarter) tuple; if `signal_count < 20`, the generation job aborts AND emits `m12_market_intel_pre_generation_k_anon_floor_breach` (Appendix G — new); the report for that (Category, scope, quarter) is skipped entirely; the next quarter retries.
3. **`market_intelligence_report` invocation.** The capability is invoked with the input cohort. Output: `executive_summary_markdown` (500–5,000 chars), `content_sections_json` (≤ 200,000 chars covering demand trends, pricing bands, vendor performance, strategic themes), `per_metric_k_anon_audit_json` (per-metric signal counts for the publish-time AND render-time k-anonymity gate), `meta_title`, `meta_description`. AIOperation written with `cost_center=platform_marketing`.
4. **Per-metric k-anonymity validation.** Per §4.4.15 + §48.6.4, every metric in the draft is per-metric-validated; metrics below k=20 are coarsened OR suppressed at draft-write; the `per_metric_k_anon_audit_json` is materialized.
5. **Residency validation.** Per §4.4.15 residency enforcement, if `residency_region_scope != global`, the underlying cohort MUST be filtered to in-region signals only; cross-region leak aborts the generation AND emits `market_intel_residency_violation` (existing per §4.4.15; HTTP 422 in Appendix I).
6. **Draft entity write.** MarketIntelligenceReport row written; `editorial_review_status=pending`; `editorial_marketing_reviewer_id` / `editorial_finance_reviewer_id` are NULL until reviews complete.
7. **EditorialReviewTask writes (TWO).** Two EditorialReviewTask rows are created per draft: one routed to `m12_marketing` queue, one routed to `m12_finance` queue. Both must reach `approved` for the entity to publish. Marketing leg MUST complete first per §48.6.8 ordering (Finance leg is enabled ONLY after Marketing approves; this prevents Finance approving a draft that Marketing later rejects).
8. **Marketing review.** RUBRIC v1.0 R1–R7 mandatory; R9 (residency compliance) mandatory.
9. **Finance review.** RUBRIC v1.0 R3 (k-anonymity), R4 (vendor opt-out), R10 (pricing-band correctness) mandatory; R10 is the Finance-specific dimension that NO other mechanic exercises.
10. **Publish gate re-run.** Same as M9 step 8, plus the dual-sign-off check (`editorial_marketing_reviewed_at` AND `editorial_finance_reviewed_at` non-null required).
11. **PDF render.** On publish, a backend job renders the report as a downloadable PDF (using a §40 PDF rendering infrastructure shared with §10.12 Selection Report; `download_pdf_url` populated; `download_pdf_refreshed_at` updated). The PDF render failure does NOT block publication; the report is published HTML-only AND a `m12_market_intel_pdf_render_failed` (Appendix G — new) event raises a §43 P2 alert.
12. **Render path.** Public viewers hit `https://marketplace.sourcera.io/intelligence/{slug}`. Same render-time gates as M9; PDF download served from `download_pdf_url`.
13. **8-quarter archive sweep.** Per §4.4.15 acceptance criterion #4, reports older than 8 quarters auto-archive nightly; archived reports retain their URL with `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`; PDF download redirects to a "Report archived" landing page.

#### UX Surfaces

| Surface | §3.3 Pattern | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Public MarketIntelligenceReport (anonymous) | Custom marketing-domain template | Long-form report layout: cover banner with quarter label + region badge + Sourcera publisher attribution; executive summary; content sections with chart-rich layout; PDF download CTA; cross-link to M9 + M10 + M11 + M13 for the same Category. |
| Ops Console > Marketplace Content > MarketIntelligenceReports | Same pattern as M9 | Per-row: category, quarter, residency region, marketing review status, finance review status, last_published_at, view_count_30d, takedown_count_30d. |
| Editorial Review Modal (Marketing leg) | Same as M9 / M10 / M11 | RUBRIC R9 explicit toggle. |
| Editorial Review Modal (Finance leg) | Same shape | RUBRIC R10 explicit toggle; dimension-failure rejection requires a per-pricing-band rationale. |
| Mobile parity | Per §3.4 | Long-form report is mobile-first; charts collapse to vertically-stacked per-section views. |

**Empty / error / loading states.** Per-quarter generation skip (k-anon floor breach OR residency violation OR Marketing+Finance both rejected) shows a "Q3 2026 report skipped due to insufficient signal cohort" banner on the per-Category MarketIntelligenceReport index page. The 8-quarter archived state renders a "This report has been archived; the most recent report is at {URL}" surface with `noindex`.

**Accessibility (§37.1).** Long-form report MUST meet WCAG 2.1 AA; charts MUST have a textual data-table alternative (per §40 PDF tagging requirements, applied to HTML render too); PDF MUST be tagged-PDF per §37.1.

#### Data Collected / Retained

Cross-link to §4.4.15. Residency enforcement is the most-strict dimension: per-region reports' underlying cohorts MUST be region-filtered AND the §4.4.15 residency-region-scope is enforced at every render.

#### Anti-Abuse Controls

Same as M9 (1)-(8), with three M12-specific additions:

9. **Pre-generation k-anonymity gate** — per §48.6.8 step 2; aborts generation if cohort < 20.
10. **Residency leak detection** — per §4.4.15; aborts generation on cross-region leak.
11. **Dual-reviewer separation of duties** — `editorial_marketing_reviewer_id` MUST NOT equal `editorial_finance_reviewer_id`; the publish gate enforces.

#### Plan Gating & Cost-Center Routing

Same as M9. `market_intelligence_report` is `platform_marketing` per §21.4.3. The §21.4.5 Outcome Signals row: accepted = report published after Marketing + Finance dual sign-off within 60d; rejected = sign-off rejected OR no publish within 60d; auto-accept after 60d (the longest auto-accept window in the M9–M13 set, reflecting the dual-sign-off complexity).

The §5.11 Feature Access Matrix is updated for: "Approve M12 MarketIntelligenceReport draft (Marketing leg)" (✓ for `ops_marketing_editor`, `ops_marketing_supervisor`); "Approve M12 MarketIntelligenceReport draft (Finance leg)" (✓ for `ops_marketing_finance_reviewer`); "Force-generate M12 MarketIntelligenceReport out of cadence" (✓ for `ops_marketing_supervisor` only).

#### Telemetry Events

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `m12_market_intel_pre_generation_k_anon_floor_breach` | Pre-generation k-anon abort | `category_id`, `residency_region_scope`, `quarter`, `signal_count`, `floor=20` |
| `m12_market_intel_draft_generated` | `market_intelligence_report` AIOperation completes | `report_id`, `category_id`, `residency_region_scope`, `quarter`, `executive_summary_length_chars`, `content_section_count`, `metric_count_pass`, `metric_count_coarsen`, `metric_count_suppress` |
| `m12_market_intel_marketing_decision` | Marketing-leg editorial decision | Same shape as M9 + `leg=marketing` |
| `m12_market_intel_finance_decision` | Finance-leg editorial decision | Same shape + `leg=finance` |
| `m12_market_intel_published` | Publish handler success (both legs approved) | `report_id`, `category_id`, `residency_region_scope`, `quarter`, `time_from_draft_to_publish_seconds`, `pdf_render_succeeded ∈ {true, false}` |
| `m12_market_intel_pdf_render_failed` | PDF render fails | `report_id`, `error_class` |
| `m12_market_intel_archived_8_quarter_sweep` | Nightly archive sweep | `report_id`, `quarters_since_publish` |
| `m12_market_intel_view_recorded` | Anonymous render | Same shape as M9 + `download_pdf_clicked ∈ {true, false}` |
| `m12_market_intel_pdf_downloaded` | PDF download | `report_id` |
| `m12_market_intel_residency_violation_aborted` | Residency leak abort | `report_id`, `attempted_residency_region_scope`, `leak_source_region` |
| `m12_market_intel_separation_of_duties_violation` | Same user attempts both legs | `report_id`, `attempted_user_id`, `leg` |

#### Notifications Fired

Same notification-kind structure as M9 (with `m12` prefix). Adds:

- `m12.market_intel.marketing_leg_ready_for_review` — to `ops_marketing_editor` queue.
- `m12.market_intel.finance_leg_ready_for_review` — to `ops_marketing_finance_reviewer` queue (fires only after Marketing leg approves).
- `m12.market_intel.dual_signoff_complete_published` — to both reviewers + supervisor.
- `m12.market_intel.pre_generation_k_anon_breach` — to `ops_marketing_supervisor`; in-app + email; explains skip.
- `m12.market_intel.pdf_render_failed` — to `ops_marketing_editor` (claimer); in-app + email.

#### Webhooks Fired

Same shape as M9 (with `m12.market_intel` substitution). Adds `marketplace_content.m12.market_intel.k_anon_degradation` per existing §4.4.15 webhook reference (per §4.4.15 failure mode #2 nightly resweep).

#### API Endpoints

Same endpoint shape as M9 with substitution: `/v1/ops/marketplace-content/market-intelligence-reports`. Public render path: `https://marketplace.sourcera.io/intelligence/{slug}`. PDF download path: `https://marketplace.sourcera.io/intelligence/{slug}.pdf` (resolved via `download_pdf_url`).

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. M12 publication MUST require BOTH `editorial_marketing_reviewed_at` AND `editorial_finance_reviewed_at` non-null; attempts otherwise MUST return HTTP 409 `market_intel_dual_signoff_required` (existing per §4.4.15 acceptance criterion #1).
2. M12 MUST fail to render at the public URL with HTTP 410 if the §48.6.4 k-anonymity render gate evaluates page-level fail.
3. Any rendered metric with an audit row showing `count < 20` MUST fail the publish gate with `market_intel_k_anon_floor_not_met` (existing per §4.4.15 acceptance criterion #2).
4. Cross-region signal leak at generation MUST be detected AND aborted with `market_intel_residency_violation` (existing per §4.4.15 acceptance criterion #3).
5. Reports older than 8 quarters MUST auto-transition to `archived` via nightly sweep (existing per §4.4.15 acceptance criterion #4).
6. `editorial_marketing_reviewer_id` MUST NOT equal `editorial_finance_reviewer_id`; the publish gate enforces; violations return HTTP 409 `m12_market_intel_separation_of_duties_violation` (Appendix I — new) AND emit the matching event.
7. PDF render failure MUST NOT block HTML publication; the §43 P2 alert MUST fire AND PDF re-render MUST be retriable via API.
8. Schema.org JSON-LD for M12 MUST include `Article` + `Dataset` + `BreadcrumbList` per §48.6.1; `Dataset.distribution` MUST point to the cached PDF URL when available.
9. Force-generation MUST require `ops_marketing_supervisor` AND a free-text rationale logged to §6.7 audit log with `audit_action_type=m12_market_intel_force_generation`.
10. The §48.6.2.B per-reviewer rate limit (2 M12 approvals / 24h per reviewer per leg) MUST be enforced atomically.

#### Failure Modes Addressed

1. **Signal cohort below k=20 at generation.** Resolved: §48.6.8 step 2 pre-generation gate aborts; the report for that (Category, scope, quarter) is skipped; the next quarter retries; Ops alerted via `m12.market_intel.pre_generation_k_anon_breach`.
2. **DSAR reduces cohort post-publication, breaking k=20 floor.** Resolved: per §4.4.15 failure mode #2, `market_intel.k_anon_degradation` webhook fires AND a re-render with coarser aggregation OR suppression is triggered. If post-coarsening the page would render at the page level as fully suppressed, §48.6.4 page-level fail-closed returns HTTP 410.
3. **Marketing and Finance reviewers disagree on a single pricing-band figure.** Resolved: per §4.4.15 failure mode #3, the page is held in `revision_requested`; the disagreement note is captured in both EditorialReviewTask `editorial_revision_request_note` fields; the next-version draft addresses the dispute; both legs re-review.
4. **Residency leak at generation (e.g., a US-only report's cohort accidentally includes EU signals).** Resolved: per §4.4.15 failure mode #4, the residency check at generation aborts; Ops paged; no report published for that region-period.
5. **Same Ops user attempts both Marketing AND Finance legs.** Resolved: §48.6.8 anti-abuse #11 separation-of-duties check rejects with HTTP 409; `m12_market_intel_separation_of_duties_violation` event fires; Ops Marketing supervisor notified to assign different reviewers.

### 48.6.9 M13 Public Marketplace Heat Map {#48.6.9-m13-public-marketplace-heat-map}

#### Purpose

M13 publishes the Public Marketplace Heat Map — an interactive, anonymized, category-level demand visualization that surfaces which procurement Categories are seeing the most evaluation activity, segmented by `(category, region, industry, company_size_band, period)`. Each cell of the heat map is a §4.4.16 HeatMapCell row; the Heat Map landing page is a derived view that aggregates cells. The mechanic exists to (a) capture top-of-funnel SEO traffic for analyst-style queries (e.g., "what software categories are most-evaluated in 2026"), (b) signal Sourcera's data-density advantage to prospects, (c) cross-link to M9 / M10 / M11 / M12 for any high-demand Category. M13 enforces k=10 floor at the cell level AND is auto-published per §4.4.16 (cells skip the editorial workflow). The Heat Map landing page itself, however, includes Ops-curated featured-cell promo strips that DO route through the §48.6.2 editorial workflow (queue `m13_marketing`).

#### Trigger

M13 cells are generated under one condition: **scheduled cell refresh.** A per-(Category, region, industry, company_size_band) cron (`refresh_cadence_days=14`; per §4.4.16) invokes `heat_map_cell_summary` capability at the start of each refresh window. Refresh windows are aligned to UTC-week boundaries (every other Monday at 02:00 UTC).

The Heat Map landing page itself (the aggregated render) is NOT triggered separately; it is rendered live from cells at every public page request, with the §31 60-second edge cache.

#### Actor & Entity Schema

Cross-link to §4.4.16 HeatMapCell entity. M13 mechanic introduces ONE additional persisted entity for the Heat Map landing page's curated promo surface: `HeatMapAggregationCard`.

**New entity: HeatMapAggregationCard (Marketplace-Domain, Sourcera-Owned, Public).** Curated promo strips on the Heat Map landing page; e.g., "Hot This Quarter: HRMS in EU+Mid-Market" or "Trending: Cybersecurity in US+Enterprise." Each card aggregates a small set of HeatMapCell rows AND adds editorial narrative.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK, immutable | Standard. |
| `slot_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `heat_map_aggregation_card_slot_kind` (new): `hot_this_quarter`, `trending_up`, `trending_down`, `editor_pick`, `regional_spotlight`, `industry_spotlight`; required | Slot routing on the Heat Map landing page. |
| `slot_position` | Integer | 1–10; required | Ordering within slot kind. |
| `included_heat_map_cell_ids` | Array[UUID] | 1–20 entries; FKs → §4.4.16 HeatMapCell | Cells aggregated by this card; ALL referenced cells MUST satisfy `k_anon_satisfied=true` at publish time. |
| `card_title` | String | 10–80 chars; required | Display title. |
| `card_narrative_markdown` | String | 50–500 chars; required | Editorial narrative (one-paragraph). |
| `card_metric_summary_json` | JSON | ≤ 2,000 chars | Pre-computed aggregate (e.g., "75% YoY growth"); MUST satisfy k=10 per included cell. |
| `editorial_review_status` | Enum | `editorial_review_status` | Per §48.6.2. |
| `editorial_reviewed_by` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → Ops User | Marketing reviewer. |
| `editorial_reviewed_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | — |
| `editorial_rejection_reason` | String | 0–1,000 chars; nullable | — |
| `publication_status` | Enum | `page_publication_status` | — |
| `published_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | — |
| `last_published_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | — |
| `expires_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Optional auto-archive (e.g., quarterly cards expire at quarter-end). |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | Standard | Standard pattern | `created_by` is `ops_marketing_editor`. |

**Vendor-Identity-Free Aggregate Invariant (D-V72REM-PH1-001 sibling closure of D-2.2-042, v7.2.0-REM Phase 1, 2026-05-15; AE-V72REM-01).** HeatMapAggregationCard aggregates HeatMapCell rows (which are themselves vendor-identity-free per §4.4.16) plus editorial narrative authored by Ops Marketing reviewers; the card surface renders NO vendor names, NO Seller Org references, and NO SellerSoftware references at any depth. The prior v7.1.0 table row stamping `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` "per uniform source-of-truth linkage" was structurally defective for the same reasons enumerated in §4.4.16's D-2.2-042 remediation (the included cells carry no vendor identity, the card narrative is editorially constrained to non-vendor-identifying copy by the §M.5 CI gate `seller_maya_solo_free_copy_string_lint`-style content-validator extension at §M13 editorial review, and the Opt-Out Registry probe would have no target to honor). The field is removed; the entity inherits the §4.4.16 Vendor-Identity-Free Aggregate Invariant; the §4.5.6 Marketplace-Domain Read/Render Contract treats HeatMapAggregationCard as a vendor-identity-free surface and does not probe the Opt-Out Registry at render time. CI gate `enum_bound_no_inline_sentinel_admission` (§M.5 V72REM block) prohibits future re-introduction of inline sentinel admissions against the §4.4.8 closed enum across all aggregate entities, including this one.

**Scope isolation.** Marketplace-domain (no `org_id`); Sourcera-owned. Read access public for `publication_status=published`; write access `ops_marketing_editor` AND `ops_marketing_supervisor`.

**Required indexes.** `(slot_kind, slot_position) WHERE publication_status='published'`; `(editorial_review_status, updated_at)` for review queue; `(expires_at) WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL AND publication_status='published'` (nightly expiry sweep).

**Retention.** Published rows: platform-life unless expired or archived. Archived rows retained 180 days then purged.

**Acting entity.** `ops_marketing_editor` for Heat Map Aggregation Card review; `ops_taxonomy_admin` for taxonomy alignment; `system_content_worker` for cell refresh.

**Targeted entity.** §4.4.16 HeatMapCell (one cell per (Category, region, industry, company_size_band, period) tuple); HeatMapAggregationCard (one card per slot per slot_position).

#### Generation + Editorial Workflow

**Cell-level workflow (auto-published, no editorial):**

1. **Refresh cron fires.** The cell-refresh worker enumerates all (Category, region, industry, company_size_band) tuples whose `next_scheduled_refresh_at` is ≤ now.
2. **`heat_map_cell_summary` invocation.** AIOperation written with `cost_center=platform_marketing`. Output: `signal_count`, `demand_index`, `demand_trend`, `prior_period_signal_count`, `contributing_source_hash`.
3. **k-anonymity enforcement.** Per §4.4.16 + §48.6.4, `k_anon_satisfied` is computed (`signal_count ≥ 10`). If false, `demand_index=null` AND `demand_trend=insufficient_data`; the cell is still persisted but renders suppressed.
4. **Residency enforcement.** Per §4.4.16, the contributing signal cohort MUST respect `residency_region_scope`; cross-region leak aborts the refresh AND emits `heat_map_residency_violation` (existing per §4.4.16).
5. **Cell row write.** Cell row updated; `last_refreshed_at` populated; `publication_status=published` (per §4.4.16 cells auto-publish).
6. **Render path (Heat Map landing).** Public viewers hit `https://marketplace.sourcera.io/heat-map`. The render path enumerates all `k_anon_satisfied=true AND publication_status=published` cells; renders the heat map grid (HTML + Schema.org `DataCatalog`); overlays the `HeatMapAggregationCard` rows in their slot positions.

**HeatMapAggregationCard workflow (editorial-reviewed):**

1. **Card draft.** An `ops_marketing_editor` manually authors a card via the Ops Console, OR a periodic Ops cron (Authored Extension #23) suggests cards based on `demand_trend=up` cells.
2. **EditorialReviewTask write.** Routed to `m13_marketing` queue; SLA = 3 business days.
3. **Editorial review.** RUBRIC v1.0 R1 (factual accuracy of the metric summary), R3 (k-anonymity — every included cell MUST be `k_anon_satisfied=true`), R5 (Schema.org), R6 (tone), R7 (SEO). R2 (vendor neutrality) is NOT applicable because cards reference NO vendor names per §4.4.16.
4. **Publish gate re-run.** Same as M9 step 8 but tailored: every `included_heat_map_cell_ids` row MUST be `k_anon_satisfied=true` at publish time; if any cell has dropped below floor, the publish is rejected with HTTP 422 `heat_map_aggregation_card_included_cell_below_k_anon_floor` (Appendix I — new) AND the editor MUST re-author with different cells.

#### UX Surfaces

| Surface | §3.3 Pattern | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Public Heat Map landing page (anonymous) | Custom marketing-domain template | Interactive heat map: grid layout (rows = Categories, columns = (region, industry, company_size_band) tuples); each cell color-coded by `demand_index`; hover reveals tooltip with cell metrics; click drills into a per-cell view; Aggregation Card promo strips above the grid. |
| Per-cell drill-in view | Sub-route of Heat Map landing | Shows the cell's metrics over the past 24 months (limited by §4.4.16 retention); cross-link to M9 / M10 / M11 / M12 for the cell's Category. |
| Ops Console > Marketplace Content > Heat Map Cells | `Sidebar Navigation + Inline Table` | Per-row: cell tuple, signal_count, k_anon_satisfied, demand_index, last_refreshed_at; filters: `?k_anon_satisfied=`, `?demand_trend=`, `?residency_region_scope=`. Read-only (cells cannot be manually edited). |
| Ops Console > Marketplace Content > Heat Map Aggregation Cards | Same pattern | Per-row: slot_kind, slot_position, card_title, included_cell_count, editorial_review_status, view_count_30d. Standard editorial actions. |
| Editorial Review Modal (Aggregation Cards) | Same pattern as M9 / M10 | Tailored RUBRIC dimension list (R1, R3, R5, R6, R7 only). |
| Mobile parity | Per §3.4 | Heat map grid transforms to a vertically-scrolling per-Category list on mobile (the cross-axis density is unreadable on narrow screens); Aggregation Cards are mobile-first cards. |

**Empty / error / loading states.** A cell that fails k-anonymity renders as a grayed-out "Insufficient data" tile; the tile is keyboard-focusable and announces "Insufficient data" to screen readers per §37.1. Heat Map landing page-level fail (per §48.6.4: ALL cells are suppressed) returns HTTP 410 (extreme edge case; very unlikely given the cross-Category aggregation).

**Accessibility (§37.1).** Heat map grid MUST have a tabular alternative (`role="table"` with `<th>` for axes) that conveys the same data; keyboard-navigable via arrow keys; tooltips MUST be screen-reader-announced via `aria-describedby`; color-coding MUST NOT be the only conveyor of `demand_index` (use both color AND a numerical label per cell).

#### Data Collected / Retained

Cross-link to §4.4.16. HeatMapAggregationCard rows are platform-scoped + Sourcera-owned; same retention semantics as M9 / M10. Anonymous viewer IP addresses SHA-256-hashed before storage.

**Residency.** Cells are residency-scoped per `residency_region_scope`; the Heat Map landing page renders a global view by default but supports a per-region toggle that filters cells AND Aggregation Cards by residency region.

#### Anti-Abuse Controls

Same as M9 (1)-(8) for HeatMapAggregationCards. For HeatMapCells (which auto-publish), the relevant controls reduce to:

1. **§4.4.16 + §48.6.4 k-anonymity floor enforcement** at every refresh AND every render.
2. **§4.4.16 residency enforcement** at refresh (cross-region leak aborts).
3. **§4.4.16 stale-cell detection** at render (cells older than 2× refresh cadence are flagged `stale=true`; UI shows "data may be stale" banner per §4.4.16 failure mode #3).
4. **`heat_map_cell_summary` capability reversal-rate alarm** per §21.4.3 (>5% reversal rate over 7 days raises §43 P2 alert).

#### Plan Gating & Cost-Center Routing

Same as M9. `heat_map_cell_summary` is `platform_marketing` per §21.4.3. The §21.4.5 Outcome Signals row: accepted = cell summary published in Heat Map at next refresh; rejected = cell fails k-anonymity (k=10) gate; auto-accept after 7d.

The §5.11 Feature Access Matrix is updated for: "Approve M13 HeatMapAggregationCard" (✓ for `ops_marketing_editor`, `ops_marketing_supervisor`); "Force-refresh M13 HeatMapCell" (✓ for `ops_taxonomy_admin`, `ops_marketing_supervisor`); "Archive M13 HeatMapAggregationCard" (✓ for `ops_marketing_supervisor`, `ops_legal_takedown_admin`).

Public render paths: `https://marketplace.sourcera.io/heat-map` (landing); `https://marketplace.sourcera.io/heat-map/cells/{cell_id}` (drill-in).

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. M13 HeatMapCell with `signal_count < 10` MUST never expose `demand_index` via any public endpoint; serializer test enforces (existing per §4.4.16 acceptance criterion #1).
2. M13 Heat Map landing page MUST fail to render with HTTP 410 if §48.6.4 page-level fail-closed evaluates true (i.e., ALL cells render as suppressed); friendly "temporarily unavailable" surface AND `noindex`.
3. M13 HeatMapAggregationCard publish MUST require ALL `included_heat_map_cell_ids` rows to have `k_anon_satisfied=true` at publish time; attempts otherwise MUST return HTTP 422 `heat_map_aggregation_card_included_cell_below_k_anon_floor`.
4. Cross-region leakage in contributing signal set MUST be detected AND the refresh aborted with `heat_map_residency_violation` (existing per §4.4.16 acceptance criterion #2).
5. Cells older than 24 months MUST be purged; nightly sweep enforces (existing per §4.4.16 acceptance criterion #3).
6. `heat_map_cell_summary` AIOperations MUST be tagged `cost_center=platform_marketing`.
7. Schema.org JSON-LD for the Heat Map landing page MUST include `DataCatalog` with per-cell `Dataset` references AND `Place` references for `region_code`; cells with `k_anon_satisfied=false` MUST be entirely omitted (NOT rendered as `null`) per §48.6.1 cross-mechanic rule #2.
8. Per-cell stale detection MUST flag cells older than `2 × refresh_cadence_days`; the UI MUST show a "data may be stale" banner (existing per §4.4.16 failure mode #3).
9. HeatMapAggregationCard editorial review MUST apply the tailored RUBRIC subset (R1, R3, R5, R6, R7); R2 and R4 are skipped per §48.6.9 (no vendor names).
10. The Heat Map landing page MUST be globally renderable AND additionally renderable per-region via the `?region=` query parameter; per-region renders MUST filter cells AND Aggregation Cards to the matching residency scope.

#### Failure Modes Addressed

1. **Signal cohort shrinks below k=10 due to opt-out cascade or DSAR.** Resolved: the cell transitions to `k_anon_satisfied=false`; `demand_index` nulled; UI renders suppressed; if all cells in a row simultaneously breach floor, the row is rendered as fully grayed-out; the §48.6.4 page-level fail-closed only triggers if EVERY cell is suppressed (extremely rare cross-Category event).
2. **Residency leakage at cell refresh.** Resolved: per §4.4.16 failure mode #2, the residency check at refresh aborts AND emits `heat_map_residency_violation`; Ops paged; cell remains at the prior `last_refreshed_at` (stale) until the residency-correct cohort can be derived.
3. **Stale cells (refresh worker outage).** Resolved: per §4.4.16 failure mode #3, cells older than 2× cadence are flagged `stale=true`; UI shows banner; if the outage persists >7 days, a §43 P2 alert pages the responsible Ops team.
4. **HeatMapAggregationCard published with cells that subsequently breach floor.** Resolved: a nightly sweep re-evaluates every published Card's included cells; any Card with at least one cell dropped below floor transitions to `editorial_review_status=revision_requested` AND is unpublished from the Heat Map landing page within 60 seconds; `m13.heat_map_aggregation_card.included_cell_below_floor_at_publish` notification fires.
5. **Takedown of an Aggregation Card on competitive-harm grounds.** Resolved: per §48.6.3, takedowns of Cards are routed via the standard adjudication; `accepted_archived` removes the Card from the landing page; `accepted_correction_published` adds a Correction Notice to the Card surface; takedowns of underlying cells are NOT supported (cells contain no per-Org-attributable data per §4.4.16; takedown filers are redirected to the Aggregation Card OR the §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Registry).

### 48.6.10 Cross-Mechanic Acceptance Criteria (M9–M13) {#48.6.10-cross-mechanic-acceptance-criteria-m9-m13}

These criteria apply to all five M9–M13 mechanics collectively:

1. Every M9–M13 mechanic MUST emit at least one PostHog event registered in Appendix G within 5 seconds of its trigger.
2. Every M9–M13 mechanic that emits public-facing content MUST honor §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Records AND §4.5.6 Marketplace-Domain Render Contract AND the §48.6.1 cross-mechanic Schema.org render contract.
3. Every M9–M13 mechanic MUST be killable via a per-mechanic feature-flag publish path with 60-second worst-case orchestrator-cache invalidation latency (§22.16.5); kill suspends new generation/refresh AND new publication, but does NOT retroactively unpublish existing pages (use the §48.6.3 takedown flow OR the per-mechanic archive endpoint for that).
4. Every M9–M13 mechanic MUST be RBAC-gated per the §5.11 Feature Access Matrix updates registered in §48.6.11 below.
5. Every M9–M13 mechanic MUST have at least one §43.1 Ops Marketing Console dashboard surface tracking publication rate, editorial-decision rate, takedown rate, and view-count rolling 30d.
6. Every M9–M13 mechanic MUST log its lifecycle operations (generation, editorial decision, publication, archive, takedown remedy) to §4.6.1 Audit Event per §6.7 Audit Logging semantics.
7. Every M9–M13 capability AIOperation MUST be tagged `cost_center=platform_marketing` per §21.4.3; rows with `cost_center=customer_billed` for any of these capabilities MUST be flagged AND reversed via §34.11 Outcome Resolver; QA test `aiop_platform_marketing_excluded_from_customer_ledger` from §21.4.3 covers.
8. Every M9–M13 mechanic's public render path MUST execute the §48.6.4 k-anonymity render gate AND the §4.4.8 opt-out resweep (cache-respecting); page-level fail returns HTTP 410.
9. Every M9–M13 mechanic MUST be unit-testable AND integration-testable; CI gates merge if any mechanic's unit-test suite is incomplete.
10. The §48.6.2 EditorialReviewTask SLA MUST be enforced via nightly sweep AND `editorial_review_task_sla_breached` event; SLA breaches MUST surface in the Ops Marketing dashboard (§43.1) within 1 hour.
11. The §48.6.3 takedown / appeal flow MUST treat legally-binding takedowns (`is_legally_binding=true`) with the 5-business-day SLA AND non-legally-binding with the 10-business-day SLA; SLA breaches MUST raise §43 P2 alerts.
12. The §48.6.1 Schema.org cross-mechanic render contract MUST be QA-tested at every publish gate AND on a nightly sweep across all published M9–M13 entities; drift detections raise §43 P2 alerts.
13. Cost-center accounting MUST reconcile: the sum of `platform_marketing` AIOperation `cost_price_cents` per Sourcera Platform Marketing internal cost-center MUST match the Summary Summary §6.36 internal-finance dashboard within 1% per month; reconciliation drift raises a §43 P1 alert.
