## 48.7 M14–M17 Cross-Console & Seller Conversion Mechanics {#48.7-m14-m17-cross-console-seller-conversion-mechanics}

**Authoring intent.** §48.7 authors the final four numbered Expanded Growth Mechanics from Summary §3.3 (M14–M17) at full Master Spec fidelity. M14 (Seller Bid Success Share) and M15 (Ghost-Bid Importer) are seller-console-originating mechanics that compound the seller funnel. M16 (Buyer Referral Credit) is a buyer-console-originating mechanic with financial settlement implications. M17 (Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat) is a cross-console mechanic with the most complex billing reconciliation path in the M-mechanic catalog. Entity schemas for M15, M16, and M17 already exist in §4.4.17 GhostBidImport, §4.3.16 Buyer Referral, and §4.3.17 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat Grant respectively; §48.7 does NOT duplicate those field tables — it authors the operational workflow, anti-abuse controls, telemetry, notifications, webhooks, API endpoints, and acceptance criteria. M14 introduces a new entity (BidSuccessShare) authored inline below, closing the Known Gap registered in RECONCILIATION.md Phase 5.

**Per-mechanic structure.** Every M14–M17 subsection follows the thirteen-block layout established by §48.5: (1) Purpose; (2) Trigger; (3) Actor & Entity Schema (referencing or authoring §4 entities); (4) Workflow (step-by-step including gating); (5) UX Surfaces; (6) Data Collected / Retained; (7) Anti-Abuse Controls; (8) Plan Gating & Entitlement; (9) Telemetry Events; (10) Notifications Fired; (11) Webhooks Fired; (12) API Endpoints; (13) Acceptance Criteria. Each mechanic also closes with a **Failure Modes Addressed** subsection enumerating ≥ 3 realistic failure modes per the §48 counterfactual-pass requirement.

**Cross-mechanic invariants.** Every M14–M17 mechanic (a) emits at least one PostHog event registered in Appendix G (additions in §48.7.5 below); (b) is gated by at least one §48.4 anti-spam control; (c) honors §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Records where applicable (M14 seller-authored content; M15 seller-authored KB content); (d) is killable from the Ops Console via a per-mechanic feature-flag publish path with 60-second worst-case orchestrator-cache invalidation latency (§22.16.5); (e) honors §41 Email Deliverability & Compliance for any email-emitting flow; (f) is RBAC-gated per §5.11 Feature Access Matrix updates registered in §48.7.5.

**Mechanic-to-Loop linkage.** M14 compounds L1 (winning sellers share, drawing new buyers) and amplifies the §48.3.2 "Certificates and shares" network effect (#5). M15 feeds L8 (Bid-Close-Offers-KB-Sync) by pre-seeding KB content. M16 compounds the "Referrals compound quality" network effect (#6). M17 is the principal driver of seller conversion at the L1 forced-signup moment.

**Source authority.** Summary §3.3 (M14–M17 inventory table); Summary C.72 (M14), C.73 (M15), C.74 (M16); SPS §15.5 (M17); BPS §3 footer (M17 allocation); §4.3.16 (M16 entity), §4.3.17 (M17 entity), §4.4.17 (M15 entity); §34.13 (M17 procedural mechanics); §48.4.6 (Referral Fraud Controls); §48.3.2 signals #5 `m14_bid_success_share_rate_per_winning_bid` and #6 `m16_referral_signup_to_activation_time_p50`, `m16_referral_org_retention_rate_90d`.

### 48.7.1 M14 Seller Bid Success Share {#48.7.1-m14-seller-bid-success-share}

#### Purpose

M14 lets a winning seller publish a one-click social-media post celebrating a bid win on Sourcera. The post is pre-generated by the platform with the seller's authorship retained and the buyer's identity fully anonymized. The mechanic compounds trust (Summary §3.4, effect #5: "Certificates and shares compound trust") by creating zero-marginal-cost marketing artifacts that signal seller credibility on LinkedIn, X/Twitter, and other social surfaces without exposing the buyer's identity or evaluation details. M14 extends the M2 Public Selection Report / M3 Evaluation Certificate ecosystem by producing a seller-initiated share artifact (M2 and M3 are buyer-initiated or buyer-approved).

#### Trigger

The platform presents the "Share Your Win" CTA to the seller when ALL of the following conditions are met:

1. A Bid Workspace transitions to Phase 13 (Closure) per §10.13.
2. The seller's bid outcome is `awarded` (the seller won the evaluation).
3. The seller Org's current plan permits social share generation (see Plan Gating below).
4. The buyer has NOT opted out of seller win shares for this workspace via the `buyer_win_share_opt_out` workspace-level flag (see §48.7.1 Anti-Abuse Controls).
5. No prior BidSuccessShare row exists for this `(bid_workspace_id, seller_org_id)` pair in a non-terminal state (dedup guard).

The CTA surfaces on: (a) the seller's Bid Workspace closure summary (the Phase 13 panel); (b) a one-time in-app toast notification within 24 hours of closure; (c) a Loops.so `m14.bid_success_share.eligible` email sent 2 hours after closure (email-throttled per §48.4.1).

#### Actor & Entity Schema

**Acting entity.** Seller Org user with `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `seller_marketing_editor`, or `bid_workspace_member` role on the originating Bid Workspace. Any of these roles may trigger the share. The role check is evaluated at click time, not at closure time.

**New entity: BidSuccessShare (Console-Scoped, Seller).**

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK, immutable | Standard. |
| `org_id` | UUID (FK) | → Organization (§4.2.1); seller Org; required | Primary RBAC scope. |
| `console` | Enum | `seller` (fixed) | M14 is seller-only. |
| `bid_workspace_id` | UUID (FK) | → Bid Workspace; required | The workspace where the seller won. |
| `buyer_org_id` | UUID (FK) | → Organization; required | Buyer Org; stored for audit; NEVER exposed in the share artifact. |
| `initiator_user_id` | UUID (FK) | → User (§4.2.3); required | Seller user who clicked "Share Your Win." |
| `share_status` | Enum | See Appendix J `bid_success_share_status`: `draft`, `pending_anonymization_check`, `ready`, `published`, `expired`, `revoked_by_seller`, `revoked_by_ops`, `blocked_anonymization_fail` | Lifecycle state. |
| `generated_post_text` | String | 50–500 chars; required when `share_status ∈ {ready, published}` | Platform-generated social post copy. |
| `generated_post_text_hash` | String | SHA-256, 64 chars | Dedup + tamper detection on post text. |
| `anonymization_check_passed` | Boolean | Required; default false | Set to true by the anonymization validator (see Workflow step 3). |
| `anonymization_check_failed_reason` | String | 0–500 chars; nullable | Populated when check fails; contains the detected buyer-name fragment (Ops-only visible). |
| `anonymization_check_run_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; FK → AIOperation ledger | Links to the validation AI operation. |
| `seller_edited_post_text` | String | 50–500 chars; nullable | If the seller edits the generated text, the edited version; subject to re-anonymization-check. |
| `seller_edit_count` | Integer | ≥ 0; default 0 | Number of seller edits; capped at 5 per §39 addition. |
| `social_platform_targets` | Array[Enum] | See Appendix J `bid_success_share_social_platform`: `linkedin`, `x_twitter`, `facebook`, `copy_to_clipboard`; ≤ 4 | Selected share destinations. |
| `published_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | When the share was published to at least one platform. |
| `published_urls` | Array[String] | ≤ 4 URLs; max 2,000 chars each; nullable | URLs of the published social posts (captured via callback or manual paste). |
| `category_id` | UUID (FK) | Nullable; → Marketplace Category (§4.4.7) | The evaluation's primary category; used for aggregate analytics. |
| `anonymized_buyer_descriptor` | String | 10–120 chars; required when `share_status ∈ {ready, published}` | Platform-generated anonymized descriptor (e.g., "a Fortune 500 financial services company"). |
| `buyer_win_share_opt_out_checked` | Boolean | Required; default false | True after confirming buyer has NOT opted out. |
| `signal_integrity_flags` | Array[Enum] | Appendix J `growth_loop_signal_integrity_flag` (existing per §48.2.12); empty array default | SIM flags. |
| `expires_at` | Timestamp | Required; = `created_at + 90 days` | Share offer expires 90 days after closure. |
| `created_at` | Timestamp | Immutable | UTC. |
| `updated_at` | Timestamp | Auto-updated | UTC. |
| `created_by` | UUID (FK) | = `initiator_user_id` | Invariant. |
| `updated_by` | UUID (FK) | Last mutator. | — |
| `deleted_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Soft delete (Ops only). |

**Indexes.** `(org_id, share_status, created_at DESC)` — seller dashboard listing. `(bid_workspace_id, org_id)` UNIQUE partial WHERE `share_status NOT IN ('revoked_by_seller', 'revoked_by_ops', 'expired')` — dedup guard. `(buyer_org_id)` — Ops audit cross-reference (not seller-visible). `(expires_at) WHERE share_status='ready'` — nightly expiry sweep. `(category_id, published_at)` — aggregate analytics.

**Scope Isolation.** Console-scoped (Seller). Buyer-console MUST return 404 on any BidSuccessShare read. The `buyer_org_id` field is Ops-only; seller-side API projections exclude it. The `anonymization_check_failed_reason` field is Ops-only; seller sees only "Anonymization check failed — please contact support."

**Retention.** Published shares: retained Org-life + 2 years (marketing artifact). Draft/expired/revoked: purged 90 days after terminal state. DSAR: `initiator_user_id` pseudonymized; `buyer_org_id` pseudonymized; `generated_post_text` and `seller_edited_post_text` retained (they contain no PII by construction — the anonymization validator ensures this). Residency: stored in the seller Org's data region.

#### Workflow

| Step | Action | System Behavior | Audit / Notification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Seller clicks "Share Your Win" CTA | BidSuccessShare row created in `draft`; system checks `buyer_win_share_opt_out` flag on the buyer's workspace. If opt-out = true → row transitions to `blocked_anonymization_fail` with reason "Buyer has opted out of win shares for this evaluation"; seller sees "This buyer has chosen not to participate in win shares." | `m14.bid_success_share.initiated` audit event |
| 2 | Platform generates post text | An AI capability `bid_success_share_text_generation` (see §21.4.2 registration) generates `generated_post_text` and `anonymized_buyer_descriptor`. Inputs: seller Org name, seller software name, category name, anonymized buyer industry + size band (from §4.4.18 SellerSignal k=5 layer). The capability is `cost_center=platform_marketing` — no seller wallet charge. | `m14.bid_success_share.text_generated` PostHog event |
| 3 | **Anonymization validator** | A synchronous post-generation validation pass scans `generated_post_text` AND `anonymized_buyer_descriptor` for: (a) buyer Org `display_name` (exact and fuzzy, Levenshtein distance ≤ 2); (b) buyer Org `legal_entity_name`; (c) buyer Org `domain`; (d) names of all buyer-side Workspace members (first name, last name, full name); (e) buyer workspace `title`. If ANY match is detected → `anonymization_check_passed=false`, `anonymization_check_failed_reason` populated, row transitions to `blocked_anonymization_fail`. If no match → `anonymization_check_passed=true`, row transitions to `pending_anonymization_check → ready`. | `m14.bid_success_share.anonymization_passed` OR `m14.bid_success_share.anonymization_failed` PostHog event |
| 4 | Seller previews and optionally edits | Seller sees the generated post in a preview modal. Seller may edit the text (≤ 5 edits per §39). Each edit triggers a re-run of step 3 (anonymization validator on `seller_edited_post_text`). If re-check fails → row transitions back to `blocked_anonymization_fail`; seller must revise further or abandon. | `m14.bid_success_share.seller_edited` PostHog event (per edit) |
| 5 | Seller selects platforms and publishes | Seller selects ≥ 1 social platform target. For `linkedin` and `x_twitter`: the platform opens the respective social-share intent URL (pre-populated with the post text + a canonical Sourcera URL). For `copy_to_clipboard`: the post text is written to the clipboard. `share_status → published`; `published_at` stamped. | `m14.bid_success_share.published` audit + PostHog event; `m14.bid_success_share.published` notification to seller (confirmation) |
| 6 | Post-publish callback (optional) | If the seller pastes the published social post URL back into the Sourcera UI (prompted via in-app nudge 24h after publish), `published_urls` is populated. This is best-effort and not enforced. | `m14.bid_success_share.url_captured` PostHog event |

#### UX Surfaces

- **Seller Bid Workspace Phase 13 panel:** "Share Your Win" CTA card with preview of anonymized post. Card hidden if buyer opted out OR if share already published.
- **Seller Dashboard > Wins tab:** List of all BidSuccessShare rows with status badges. "Share" action available for `ready` rows; "View" for `published`.
- **In-app toast:** One-time toast 24h post-closure (per §48.4.1 email throttle alignment).
- **Email:** Loops.so `m14.bid_success_share.eligible` template (2h post-closure).

#### Data Collected / Retained

Cross-reference BidSuccessShare entity retention above. Additional: the anonymization validator's match results are retained for 90 days in the AIOperation audit trail (per §4.8.1 retention); after 90 days, only the Boolean `anonymization_check_passed` persists.

#### Anti-Abuse Controls

1. **Buyer opt-out:** Buyer Workspace Owner may set `buyer_win_share_opt_out=true` on the Workspace settings (§10 Phase settings extension). This flag is checked at step 1 and again at step 5 (race-condition guard). Opt-out is per-workspace, not per-Org (a buyer may allow shares on one evaluation but not another).
2. **Anonymization validator (step 3):** Blocks publication if buyer identity detected. False negatives are mitigated by the fuzzy-match layer (Levenshtein ≤ 2) and the buyer-member-name scan. False positives (seller's Org name partially overlaps with buyer's) are resolvable by seller editing the text and re-running the check.
3. **Velocity throttle:** *(V13 D-48-004 remediation 2026-05-12 — reconciled with §34.1.2 "Unlimited" Scale/Enterprise plan-tier semantic.)* Per-Seller-Org velocity throttle is plan-tier-bound per §34.1.2 cited cell (NOT a single inline 10/30d literal). Free / Starter / Growth tiers carry a per-30-day publish cap per §34.1.2 (Free = 0, Starter = 3/month per §34.1.2 buyer-pricing intent, Growth = 10/month); Scale / Enterprise tiers are throttled by an Ops-Console-configurable **anti-abuse safety net** at 100/30d (NOT a plan-tier ceiling — a sustained-abuse circuit-breaker that fires HTTP 429 `m14_bid_success_share_velocity_exceeded` with `Retry-After` and a notification to Ops Security). The 100/30d safety-net floor is registered in §34.1.2 V13-extension block "M14 Anti-Abuse Floors" and is overridable per-Org by `ops_security_admin`. The Scale/Enterprise "Unlimited" semantic remains intact at the plan-tier level — the 100/30d ceiling is anti-abuse, not a plan promise. CI gate `m14_velocity_cap_plan_tier_anti_abuse_distinction` (§M.5 — new) asserts the plan-tier cap and anti-abuse cap are sourced from different §34.1.2 cells.
4. **Content validator (§48.4.4):** `generated_post_text` and `seller_edited_post_text` are scanned by the §48.4.4 content validator for profanity, competitive disparagement, and trademark infringement signals. Flagged posts transition to `blocked_anonymization_fail` with the content-validator reason.
5. **SIM integration:** Abnormal publish-to-win ratios (e.g., seller publishes shares for workspaces where they were NOT actually awarded) are detectable via the `bid_workspace_id` → Phase 13 outcome cross-check; SIM flags such rows and Ops may revoke (`revoked_by_ops`).
6. **Third-party-vendor Opt-Out scan (NER-based, MANDATORY at publish).** In addition to the §48.4.4 content validator, `generated_post_text` and every `seller_edited_post_text` revision MUST be passed through a Named-Entity-Recognition (NER) extraction step that emits candidate `{organization_name}` and `{product_name}` entities. Each extracted entity is normalized (lowercase, strip legal suffixes per §48.4.8 normalization rules) and matched against the §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Registry's global-scope and software-scope rows at publish time (NOT at generation time — Opt-Out state may change between generation and publish). Match semantics: (a) exact normalized name match; (b) fuzzy match at Levenshtein distance ≤ 2 against `vendor_opt_out.normalized_name`; (c) domain-inferred match if a URL or domain token appears in the post body AND the domain is registered on any `vendor_opt_out.scope_kind='domain'` row. Any match transitions the row to `blocked_anonymization_fail` with `anonymization_check_failed_reason='third_party_vendor_opt_out'`, emits `m14_bid_success_share_third_party_opt_out_blocked {seller_org_id, bid_success_share_id, matched_vendor_opt_out_id, match_kind ∈ {exact, fuzzy, domain_inferred}}` (Appendix G — new), and surfaces to the seller: *"Your post mentions **{matched-vendor-display-name}**, who has opted out of being referenced in Sourcera public content. Please remove the reference to publish."* The NER scan is SYNCHRONOUS and blocks publication; p95 latency budget ≤ 300 ms per scan; latency breaches emit `m14_bid_success_share_ner_latency_breach` (Appendix G — new) but do NOT fail open — a scan that times out blocks publish with `error_code=m14_bid_success_share_ner_unavailable` (HTTP 503; Appendix I — new) and the seller is invited to retry. The Vendor Opt-Out Registry check is re-run at each seller edit (step 4) AND again as a final race-condition guard at step 5 publish (mirroring the buyer-identity re-check contract). Ops kill-switch: `m14_ner_scan_kill_switch` (Ops Console, §43) disables the scan globally in a detector outage; while disabled, M14 publishes are BLOCKED entirely (fail-closed) rather than proceed without Opt-Out protection. See §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Registry, §48.4.8 Entity Normalization Rules (new / Authored Extension), and Appendix I error codes.

#### Plan Gating & Entitlement

*(V13 D-48-004 remediation 2026-05-12 — numerical caps cite §34.1.2 cited cells exclusively; no inline integer duplication.)*

| Seller Plan | M14 Access | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Seller Free | ❌ Not available | §34.1.2 seller_free cell |
| Seller Solo *(V13 D-48-004 — Solo plan-tier row added; access decision per §44.6 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment)* | Per §34.1.2 seller_solo cell *(reference, not duplication)* | §34.1.2 seller_solo cell |
| Seller Starter | Per §34.1.2 seller_starter cell | §34.1.2 seller_starter cell |
| Seller Growth | Per §34.1.2 seller_growth cell | §34.1.2 seller_growth cell |
| Seller Scale | "Unlimited" plan-tier promise per §34.1.2 seller_scale cell, subject to the §48.7.1 anti-spam #3 safety-net at 100/30d (NOT a plan ceiling) | §34.1.2 seller_scale cell + §48.7.1 anti-spam #3 |
| Seller Enterprise | "Unlimited" plan-tier promise per §34.1.2 seller_enterprise cell, subject to the §48.7.1 anti-spam #3 safety-net at 100/30d | §34.1.2 seller_enterprise cell + §48.7.1 anti-spam #3 |

AI generation cost is `cost_center=platform_marketing` per §21.4.3 — no seller wallet charge. The `bid_success_share_text_generation` capability is registered in §21.4.2 with `cost_center=platform_marketing`, Opus-tier, estimated $0.15 value / $0.02 cost per invocation. *(V13 D-48-004 amendment: numerical values single-sourced at §34.1.2; §48.7.1 anti-abuse #3 + §48.4.X anti-abuse-vs-plan-tier-cap registry CI gate `m14_inline_plan_tier_numerical_singleton_purged` (§M.5 — new) asserts the §48.7.1 body carries no inline integer plan-tier caps.)*

#### API Endpoints

**`POST /v1/bid-success-shares`** — Create a new BidSuccessShare (triggers step 1–3). Auth: Seller console; `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `seller_marketing_editor`, or `bid_workspace_member` on the referenced workspace. Rate limit: `standard_write` (§32). Idempotency key: `(bid_workspace_id, org_id)`. Request body: `{ "bid_workspace_id": "<uuid>" }`. Response 201: full BidSuccessShare object (seller-projection). Errors: `m14_buyer_opted_out` (HTTP 403), `m14_already_exists` (HTTP 409), `m14_plan_not_eligible` (HTTP 403), `m14_bid_not_awarded` (HTTP 422), `m14_workspace_not_phase_13` (HTTP 422), `m14_bid_success_share_velocity_exceeded` (HTTP 429).

**`PATCH /v1/bid-success-shares/{id}`** — Edit post text (triggers step 4 re-anonymization). Auth: same as create; must be the `initiator_user_id` OR `org_owner`. Rate limit: `standard_write`. Request body: `{ "seller_edited_post_text": "<string>" }`. Response 200. Errors: `m14_edit_limit_exceeded` (HTTP 422), `m14_anonymization_failed` (HTTP 422), `m14_share_not_editable` (HTTP 422; share not in `ready` state).

**`POST /v1/bid-success-shares/{id}/publish`** — Publish to selected platforms (step 5). Auth: same. Rate limit: `standard_write`. Request body: `{ "social_platform_targets": ["linkedin", "copy_to_clipboard"] }`. Response 200. Errors: `m14_anonymization_not_passed` (HTTP 422), `m14_already_published` (HTTP 409).

**`DELETE /v1/bid-success-shares/{id}`** — Seller-initiated revocation. Auth: `initiator_user_id` OR `org_owner`. Response 200 (`share_status → revoked_by_seller`). Errors: `m14_share_already_terminal` (HTTP 422).

**`GET /v1/bid-success-shares`** — List shares for the seller Org. Auth: any Seller console member. Cursor-paginated (default 50, max 250 per §32). Filter params: `share_status`, `created_after`, `created_before`, `category_id`.

**Ops endpoints** (§43 Admin Console):

**`POST /v1/ops/bid-success-shares/{id}/revoke`** — Ops revocation. Auth: `ops_growth_admin` or `ops_security_admin`. Request body: `{ "reason": "<string>" }`. Fires `m14.bid_success_share.revoked_by_ops` notification.

**`GET /v1/ops/bid-success-shares`** — Ops listing across all Orgs. Cursor-paginated. Filter params: `org_id`, `buyer_org_id`, `share_status`, `anonymization_check_passed`, `signal_integrity_flags`.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The anonymization validator MUST block publication (`share_status = blocked_anonymization_fail`) if any of the following buyer-identifiable strings are detected in `generated_post_text` OR `seller_edited_post_text`: buyer Org `display_name`, `legal_entity_name`, `domain`, or the first name, last name, or full name of any buyer-side Workspace member; fuzzy matching (Levenshtein distance ≤ 2) MUST be applied. QA test: `m14_anonymization_validator_blocks_buyer_name`.
2. Seller edits MUST trigger a re-run of the anonymization validator; edits that introduce buyer-identifiable content MUST be blocked. QA test: `m14_seller_edit_triggers_recheck`.
3. The `buyer_org_id` field MUST be excluded from all seller-facing API responses and webhook payloads. QA test: `m14_buyer_org_id_not_in_seller_projection`.
4. Buyer opt-out (`buyer_win_share_opt_out=true`) MUST prevent share creation at step 1 AND must be re-checked at publish time (step 5). QA test: `m14_buyer_opt_out_blocks_share`.
5. AI generation cost MUST be routed to `cost_center=platform_marketing`; the seller's AI wallet MUST NOT be debited. QA test: `m14_cost_center_platform_marketing`.
6. The velocity throttle (≤ 10/30d per Org; configurable) MUST be enforced at create time; exceeding returns HTTP 429. QA test: `m14_velocity_throttle`.
7. BidSuccessShare rows MUST be unique per `(bid_workspace_id, org_id)` for non-terminal statuses; duplicate creation attempts MUST return HTTP 409. QA test: `m14_dedup_guard`.
8. Nightly expiry sweep MUST transition `ready` shares past `expires_at` to `expired`. QA test: `m14_expiry_sweep`.
9. Every M14 lifecycle event MUST emit the corresponding PostHog event from the Telemetry Events table within 5 seconds. QA test: `m14_telemetry_events`.
10. The content validator (§48.4.4) MUST scan seller-edited text; flagged content MUST block publication. QA test: `m14_content_validator_blocks_flagged`.

#### Failure Modes Addressed

1. **Anonymization validator false negative (buyer name leaks into published post).** Mitigated by: (a) fuzzy matching with Levenshtein ≤ 2; (b) scanning buyer workspace member names (not just Org name); (c) scanning buyer workspace title. Residual risk: buyer uses an extremely generic Org name (e.g., "Tech Solutions") that also appears in the generated post as a generic phrase. Residual risk is accepted because the generic phrase would not identify the buyer. Ops may retroactively revoke if a buyer reports a leak.
2. **Seller injects buyer name into `seller_edited_post_text`.** Resolved: every edit triggers re-anonymization (step 4); the validator blocks the edit.
3. **Buyer opts out AFTER seller creates a `ready` share but BEFORE publish.** Resolved: step 5 re-checks the `buyer_win_share_opt_out` flag. If opt-out is now true, publish fails with HTTP 403 `m14_buyer_opted_out`.
4. **AI text generation capability is unavailable (Anthropic outage).** Resolved: BidSuccessShare stays in `draft`; seller sees "Share generation is temporarily unavailable — please try again later." The 90-day expiry window provides ample retry time. No billing is incurred (generation is `platform_marketing` cost-center).
5. **Seller Org is downgraded below Starter between share creation and publish.** Resolved: publish endpoint re-checks plan eligibility; returns HTTP 403 `m14_plan_not_eligible`. The `ready` share remains accessible (read-only) until expiry.

### 48.7.2 M15 Ghost-Bid Importer {#48.7.2-m15-ghost-bid-importer}

#### Purpose

M15 lets sellers paste or upload historical RFP/response content to seed their Knowledge Base before any live bid arrives. The mechanic exists because the canonical seller cold-start problem — an empty KB that produces low-quality AI drafts on the first real bid — is the primary churn driver for newly-invited sellers. By ingesting prior RFP responses, the seller's KB is pre-populated with domain-specific Q&A pairs, which immediately lifts first-pass response quality and reduces seller time-to-value from days to minutes. The first import per Seller Org is free (§4.4.17 `is_first_import_free_for_org`), removing cost friction at the onboarding moment. The mechanic feeds L8 (Bid-Close-Offers-KB-Sync) by bootstrapping the KB content that L8 subsequently enriches.

#### Trigger

A seller user navigates to the KB section of their Seller Console and clicks "Import Historical RFP" (or equivalent CTA). The CTA is visible on: (a) the KB empty-state page (when `kb_entry_count = 0`); (b) the KB dashboard header (always visible); (c) the seller onboarding wizard (Phase 1 of seller activation). No phase-gating applies; M15 is available from the moment a Seller Org exists.

#### Actor & Entity Schema

**Acting entity.** Seller Org user with `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `seller_kb_editor`, or `seller_marketing_editor` role. The `seller_kb_editor` role is required for the review → publish transition (step 5 in the workflow below).

**Persisted entity: GhostBidImport (§4.4.17).** Full entity schema, state machine, indexes, retention, and acceptance criteria are authored in §4.4.17. This section does NOT duplicate the field table. Cross-reference: §4.4.17.

#### Workflow

| Step | Action | System Behavior | Audit / Notification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Seller creates import | Seller pastes text OR uploads a document (PDF, DOCX, TXT, ZIP of documents; max per §39 `GhostBidImport.source_file_byte_size`). GhostBidImport row created in `draft`. `import_type` set per input mode. If upload: `source_file_attachment_id` populated via standard attachment flow. | `m15.ghost_bid_import.created` audit + PostHog event |
| 2 | Seller submits for parse | Seller clicks "Parse." `import_status → parsing`. The `ghost_rfp_ingestion` capability (§21.4.2; Opus-tier; ~$25 value, ~$3.30 cost) is invoked. If `is_first_import_free_for_org = true`, no AIOperation billing record is created. Otherwise, an AIOperation is created against the seller's wallet. | `m15.ghost_bid_import.parse_started` PostHog event |
| 3 | Parse completes | On success: `parsed_qa_pairs_json` populated; `parsed_entry_count` set; `import_status → parsed → review_pending` (auto-advance). On failure: `import_status → failed`; `failure_reason` populated; billing reversed via §34.11 Outcome Resolver. | `m15.ghost_bid_import.parsed` OR `m15.ghost_bid_import.parse_failed` PostHog event |
| 4 | **Review queue** | The seller reviewer (must hold `seller_kb_editor`) sees the parsed Q&A pairs in a review UI. Each pair is displayed with: question text, answer text, confidence score, and a "merge target" suggestion (existing KB entry that overlaps). The reviewer may: (a) **Accept** individual pairs; (b) **Reject** individual pairs; (c) **Edit** a pair before accepting; (d) **Accept All** (bulk action); (e) **Reject All** and abandon the import. The review UI shows a progress bar: "X of Y pairs reviewed." | `m15.ghost_bid_import.pair_accepted` / `m15.ghost_bid_import.pair_rejected` PostHog events (per pair) |
| 5 | Reviewer approves (publish) | When the reviewer clicks "Publish Accepted Pairs," `import_status → publishing`. Accepted pairs are written atomically into the target KB namespace as standard KB entries (§22.3.1). If the write succeeds: `import_status → published`; `imported_at` stamped; billing entry created if not first-import-free. If write fails: `import_status → failed`; partial writes rolled back atomically. | `m15.ghost_bid_import.published` audit + PostHog event; `m15.ghost_bid_import.published` notification to seller |
| 6 | Reviewer rejects | If the reviewer clicks "Reject All" or "Reject Import," `import_status → rejected`; `rejected_by_role = seller_user`. No KB entries created; no billing. | `m15.ghost_bid_import.rejected` PostHog event |

**Content validator integration.** At any point during steps 2–5, the §48.4.4 content validator may flag the import for spam, adversarial content, or PII leakage. If flagged: `import_status → rejected` with `rejected_by_role = content_validator`; SIM credited with a flag on the Org.

**Dedup integration.** At step 2, a SHA-256 hash of the normalized `raw_text` is computed and compared against prior GhostBidImport rows for the same Org. If a match is found: `duplicate_of_import_id` is set; the import auto-rejects after 7 days if not superseded. Duplicates do not consume the first-import-free slot (§4.4.17 acceptance criterion #4).

#### UX Surfaces

- **KB Empty State:** Large "Import Historical RFP" CTA with explanation copy ("Seed your KB with your past RFP responses to get better AI drafts from day one.").
- **KB Dashboard Header:** Persistent "Import" button.
- **Seller Onboarding Wizard:** Step 2 of 4 ("Bring your knowledge").
- **Review Queue:** Full-screen review UI with pair-by-pair accept/reject, bulk actions, merge-target suggestions, and progress bar.
- **Import History:** Table of all GhostBidImport rows for the Org with status, entry count, and "Re-import" action for failed/rejected imports.

#### Data Collected / Retained

Cross-reference §4.4.17 Retention & DSAR. Summary: `raw_text` and `parsed_qa_pairs_json` retained 90 days after `published`, then purged; KB entries produced persist per KB retention policy (§22.3.1). Rejected/failed imports purged 30 days after terminal state. Residency: seller Org's data region.

#### Anti-Abuse Controls

1. **Content validator (§48.4.4):** Scans `raw_text` for spam, adversarial, and PII content; rejects on flag.
2. **File size cap (§39):** Per §39 `GhostBidImport.source_file_byte_size`; oversized uploads reject with `ghost_bid_import_file_too_large` (HTTP 413).
3. **Dedup (SHA-256):** Identical imports auto-flagged; duplicates do not consume the first-import-free slot.
4. **Velocity throttle:** ≤ 5 imports per Org per 24-hour rolling window (configurable in Ops Console). Exceeding returns HTTP 429 `m15_ghost_bid_import_velocity_exceeded` (Appendix I — new).
5. **First-import-free abuse prevention:** The first-free slot is computed as "first to reach `published` status" per §4.4.17; concurrent racing imports are retroactively billed via the post-publish reconciliation worker.
6. **SIM integration:** Orgs with > 3 failed or rejected imports in a 7-day window are flagged; Ops may restrict import access.

#### Plan Gating & Entitlement

| Seller Plan | M15 Access | First Import Free | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Seller Free | ✅ (first import only) | ✅ 1 lifetime per Org | §34.1.2, SPS §3 |
| Seller Starter | ✅ | ✅ 1 lifetime per Org (if not already used on Free) | §34.1.2 |
| Seller Growth | ✅ | ✅ 1 lifetime per Org | §34.1.2 |
| Seller Scale | ✅ | ✅ 1 lifetime per Org | §34.1.2 |
| Seller Enterprise | ✅ | ✅ 1 lifetime per Org | §34.1.2 |

Subsequent imports bill at the `ghost_rfp_ingestion` capability rate ($25 value, $3.30 cost per §21.4.2) against the seller's AIWallet. Seller Free users cannot run a second import (wallet balance = $0, overage disabled by default).

| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `m15.ghost_bid_import.created` | Step 1 | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |
| `m15.ghost_bid_import.parse_started` | Step 2 | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |

| `m15.ghost_bid_import.parse_failed` | Step 3 failure | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |
| `m15.ghost_bid_import.pair_accepted` | Step 4 pair accept | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |
| `m15.ghost_bid_import.pair_rejected` | Step 4 pair reject | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |
| `m15.ghost_bid_import.published` | Step 5 success | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |
| `m15.ghost_bid_import.rejected` | Step 6 or content validator | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |

| `m15.ghost_bid_import.velocity_exceeded` | Throttle hit | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |

| Kind | Channel | Recipient | Trigger |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `m15.ghost_bid_import.parse_complete` | In-app | Import creator | Step 3 success (parse complete, ready for review) |
| `m15.ghost_bid_import.parse_failed` | In-app + Email | Import creator | Step 3 failure |

| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `ghost_bid_import.published` | GhostBidImport (seller-projection; excludes `raw_text` for payload size) | Appendix F.1 `standard` | New |
| `ghost_bid_import.failed` | GhostBidImport (seller-projection; includes `failure_reason`) | Appendix F.1 `standard` | New |

HMAC-SHA256 signed per §31. `event_id` idempotency. Payload ≤ 256KB (enforced by excluding `raw_text` and `parsed_qa_pairs_json` from webhook payloads; consumers use the API to retrieve full content).

#### API Endpoints

**`POST /v1/ghost-bid-imports`** — Create a new import (step 1). Auth: Seller console; roles per Actor section. Rate limit: `standard_write`. Idempotency key: client-generated. Request body: `{ "target_seller_software_id": "<uuid|null>", "import_type": "paste|upload_document|upload_zip", "raw_text": "<string>" }` (for paste) OR multipart form upload (for document/zip). Response 201: GhostBidImport object. Errors: `ghost_bid_import_file_too_large` (HTTP 413), `m15_ghost_bid_import_velocity_exceeded` (HTTP 429), `ghost_bid_import_cross_org_namespace` (HTTP 422).

**`POST /v1/ghost-bid-imports/{id}/parse`** — Submit for parse (step 2). Auth: same. Response 202 (accepted; async processing). Errors: `m15_import_not_in_draft` (HTTP 422), `m15_wallet_insufficient` (HTTP 402; for non-first imports when wallet is empty/capped).

**`GET /v1/ghost-bid-imports/{id}/review`** — Retrieve parsed Q&A pairs for review (step 4). Auth: Seller console; `seller_kb_editor` required. Response 200: array of `{ pair_id, question, answer, confidence, merge_target_kb_entry_id }`. Cursor-paginated (default 50, max 250).

**`POST /v1/ghost-bid-imports/{id}/review`** — Submit review decisions (step 4). Auth: `seller_kb_editor`. Request body: `{ "decisions": [{ "pair_id": "<uuid>", "action": "accept|reject|edit", "edited_question": "<string|null>", "edited_answer": "<string|null>" }] }`. Response 200. Errors: `m15_import_not_in_review` (HTTP 422).

**`POST /v1/ghost-bid-imports/{id}/publish`** — Publish accepted pairs (step 5). Auth: `seller_kb_editor`. Response 200. Errors: `m15_import_not_in_review` (HTTP 422), `m15_no_accepted_pairs` (HTTP 422).

**`POST /v1/ghost-bid-imports/{id}/reject`** — Reject entire import (step 6). Auth: `seller_kb_editor` OR creator. Response 200. Errors: `m15_import_already_terminal` (HTTP 422).

**`GET /v1/ghost-bid-imports`** — List imports for the seller Org. Auth: any Seller console member. Cursor-paginated. Filter params: `import_status`, `created_after`, `created_before`, `target_seller_software_id`.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The first successful `published` import per Seller Org MUST NOT produce an AIOperation billing record; second and subsequent imports MUST bill at the `ghost_rfp_ingestion` capability rate. QA test: `m15_first_import_free`.
2. The ingestion → review-queue → accept/reject flow MUST be atomic: a reviewer MUST see all parsed pairs before publishing; partial publishes (where some pairs are still pending review) MUST NOT be allowed. QA test: `m15_review_completeness`.
3. File size rejection above §39 `GhostBidImport.source_file_byte_size` MUST return HTTP 413 `ghost_bid_import_file_too_large` at upload time, not after parse begins. QA test: `m15_file_size_rejection`.
4. KB namespace write failures MUST roll back ALL entries atomically; partial KB state is disallowed. QA test: `m15_atomic_kb_write`.
5. Content validator rejection MUST be logged in audit with the triggering validator rule. QA test: `m15_content_validator_audit`.
6. Duplicate dedup (SHA-256 of normalized `raw_text`) MUST be enforced server-side; duplicates MUST NOT consume the first-import-free slot. QA test: `m15_dedup_enforcement`.
7. The review UI MUST display each parsed pair with question, answer, confidence score, and merge-target suggestion. QA test: `m15_review_ui_completeness`.
8. Parse failure MUST trigger billing reversal via §34.11 Outcome Resolver for non-first imports. QA test: `m15_parse_failure_billing_reversal`.
9. Every M15 lifecycle event MUST emit the corresponding PostHog event within 5 seconds. QA test: `m15_telemetry_events`.
10. The velocity throttle (≤ 5 imports/24h per Org; configurable) MUST be enforced at creation time. QA test: `m15_velocity_throttle`.

#### Failure Modes Addressed

1. **Parse fails due to malformed document.** `import_status = failed`; `failure_reason` populated with structured error. Billing reversed via Outcome Resolver. Seller notified with remediation steps ("The uploaded document could not be parsed. Please ensure it is a valid PDF, DOCX, or TXT file.").
2. **Content validator flags spam or adversarial content mid-parse.** `import_status → rejected` with `rejected_by_role = content_validator`. SIM credited. Seller Org flagged if 3+ rejections in 7 days.
3. **Duplicate import (identical `raw_text` hash).** `duplicate_of_import_id` populated; import auto-rejects after 7 days. First-import-free slot preserved. Seller notified: "This content matches a previous import."
4. **Target KB namespace deleted between parse and publish.** Parse job checks namespace existence at step 5 publish time; if deleted, `import_status → failed` with `failure_reason = target_namespace_deleted`. Billing reversed.
5. **Concurrent racing imports for the first-free slot.** Both imports start with `is_first_import_free_for_org = true`. The first to reach `published` wins the free slot. The second import's post-publish reconciliation worker flips `is_first_import_free_for_org = false` and creates a billing AIOperation retroactively. Refund semantics follow §34.11 if the retroactive bill is disputed.
6. **Wallet insufficient for non-first import (Seller Free user, second import).** Resolved at step 2: parse endpoint returns HTTP 402 `m15_wallet_insufficient` before the AIOperation is created. Seller sees upgrade prompt.

### 48.7.3 M16 Buyer Referral Credit {#48.7.3-m16-buyer-referral-credit}

#### Purpose

M16 provides a structured referral program for buyer Orgs on Business Scale or Enterprise. A referrer invites another buyer Org to Sourcera via a tracked referral link. When the referee Org signs up, meets the minimum-activity threshold, and passes all fraud checks, the referrer receives an invoice credit ($100 for Scale, $200 for Enterprise per §4.3.16). The mechanic compounds the "Referrals compound quality" network effect (§48.3.2, effect #6) because peer-vouched signups activate faster and have higher 90-day retention than cold signups. M16 includes comprehensive fraud controls per §48.4.6 (same-domain self-referral block, payment-method overlap detection, IP-range overlap detection, velocity spike detection, bootstrapping pattern detection, and minimum-activity gating).

#### Trigger

A buyer user on Business Scale or Enterprise navigates to Settings > Referrals and clicks "Invite a Colleague." Alternatively, the referral link is available via: (a) the Buyer Dashboard referral card (persistent for Scale+); (b) the "Invite" menu in the global header; (c) a periodic Loops.so `m16.referral.reminder` email (monthly, per §48.4.1 throttle). The CTA generates a unique referral link containing the `referral_code` from §4.3.16.

#### Actor & Entity Schema

**Acting entity.** Buyer Org user with `org_owner`, `org_admin`, or `billing_admin` role. The role check is evaluated at referral creation time and persisted in `referrer_user_id`.

**Persisted entity: BuyerReferral (§4.3.16).** Full entity schema, indexes, scope isolation, retention, failure modes, and the Referee Exclusivity Rule are authored in §4.3.16. This section does NOT duplicate the field table. Cross-reference: §4.3.16.

#### Workflow

| Step | Action | System Behavior | Audit / Notification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Referrer creates referral | BuyerReferral row created in `pending`. `referral_code` generated (10-char Base32). `credit_value_usd` set per referrer's plan ($100 Scale, $200 Enterprise). `activity_threshold_policy_version` stamped. | `m16.referral.created` audit + PostHog event |
| 2 | Referrer shares link | Referrer copies the link (`https://app.sourcera.io/r/{referral_code}`) or shares via email/social. `invited_via_channel` recorded. | `m16.referral.link_shared` PostHog event (per channel) |
| 3 | Referee clicks link and signs up | Referee visits the link; Sourcera signup flow is pre-populated with the referral attribution. On Org provisioning: `referee_org_id` set; `status → signed_up`. | `m16.referral.referee_signed_up` audit + PostHog event |
| 4 | **Same-domain self-referral block** | **(V13 D-13V-004 remediation 2026-05-12 — canonical enforcement contract.)** Enforcement runs at TWO complementary points by design: (i) **CREATE-TIME hard block at step 1**: POST /v1/referrals validator rejects with HTTP 422 `m16_same_domain_blocked` IFF `referrer_email_domain = referee_email_domain` AND the domain is NOT in §48.4.3 shared-use registry AND the call site provided `referee_email` to the API; this is the primary enforcement point and prevents the row from being created. (ii) **SIGNUP-TIME safety net at step 4**: at the `pending → signed_up` transition (step 3 event), if the referee provisions a User whose actual SSO-resolved email-domain matches the referrer's Org domain (a case that escapes (i) — e.g., a referrer entered `john@personal-gmail.com` at create-time but the referee SSO'd under `john@same-corp.com`), `same_domain_suppressed = true`; `status → flagged_fraud` with `fraud_signal_flags += ['same_domain']`. Ops may override per §4.3.16 `ops_override_user_id`. Referee's account is still provisioned. The two points are non-overlapping (the create-time path rejects with 422 and never reaches signup-time; the signup-time path catches the SSO-domain-divergence case the create-time validator cannot see). CI gate `m16_same_domain_enforcement_dual_point_canonical` (§M.5 — new) asserts both points exist and the create-time validator runs IFF the referee_email was provided at create. | `m16.referral.same_domain_blocked` PostHog event (fired at either point with `enforcement_point ∈ {create_time, signup_time}`) |
| 5 | **Payment-method overlap detection** | On referee's first invoice (Stripe webhook `invoice.paid`): compare referee's PaymentMethod fingerprint against referrer's. If match: `payment_method_overlap_detected = true`; `fraud_signal_flags += ['same_payment_method']`; `status → flagged_fraud`. | `m16.referral.payment_overlap_detected` PostHog event |
| 6 | **Minimum-activity gating** | Referee Org must reach the activation threshold (default: completed ≥ 1 Workspace through Phase 9 AND has ≥ 3 paid seats; configurable by Ops). When threshold met: `min_activity_reached_at` stamped; `status → activated`. The activity threshold is versioned (`activity_threshold_policy_version`) to prevent retroactive disqualification when Ops adjusts the threshold. | `m16.referral.referee_activated` audit + PostHog event |
| 7 | **Fraud signal aggregation** | At the `activated` transition, a final fraud-signal sweep runs: IP-range overlap (§48.4.6 #3), bootstrapping pattern (§48.4.6 #4), and velocity spike (§48.4.6 #5) are computed. If ANY fraud signal is set AND auto-kill-switch eligibility is triggered (≥ 3 distinct flags per §48.4.6 AC #4): `status → flagged_fraud`. Otherwise: row remains in `activated` awaiting the nightly credit-issuance job (step 9). Fraud signals set at this step are evaluated AGAIN by the nightly job before issuance. | `m16.referral.fraud_sweep_completed` PostHog event |
| 8 | **Referee Exclusivity Rule check** *(fires at step 3's `pending → signed_up` transition — documented here as a dedicated step for clarity; in temporal order, it runs coincident with step 3)* | Per §4.3.16 + Appendix L.2, the exclusivity rule fires at the `pending → signed_up` transition, NOT at `activated → credit_issued`. When a referee provisions a new Buyer Org via magic-link, the system checks whether another BuyerReferral row has already bound this `referee_org_id`. The FIRST referral to bind wins; all other referrals for the same `referee_email` transition to `forfeited` with `credit_forfeited_reason = referee_exclusivity_claimed` (Appendix J — new enum value). The losing referral's API surface returns `referral_referee_already_bound` (HTTP 409) for any subsequent state-probe. First-to-signup binds. Losing referrals do NOT progress to steps 4–7; they terminate at `forfeited`. | `m16.referral.exclusivity_blocked` PostHog event (emitted per losing referral) |
| 9 | Credit issued (nightly job) | Credit issuance is authored ONLY by the nightly credit-issuance job (§4.3.16 Appendix L.2). The job runs at 03:00 UTC and evaluates every row in `activated` status against all SIM fraud signals. For each row passing all checks: `credit_issued_at` stamped; `credit_expires_at = credit_issued_at + 365 days`; Stripe Credit Note created and ID appended to `stripe_credit_note_ids`; credit applied to the referrer's next invoice. The `activated → credit_issued` transition is never inline at `activated` entry — attempts return `referral_credit_issuance_deferred` (Appendix I — new). | `m16.referral.credit_issued` audit + PostHog event; `m16.referral.credit_issued` email to referrer |
| 10 | Credit redemption (ongoing) | On each subsequent invoice: credit balance decremented; `credit_redeemed_usd` updated. When `credit_redeemed_usd = credit_value_usd`: `status → credit_redeemed`. If credit expires before full redemption: `status → credit_expired`; remaining balance forfeited. | `m16.referral.credit_applied` PostHog event (per invoice); `m16.referral.credit_fully_redeemed` OR `m16.referral.credit_expired` PostHog event |

#### UX Surfaces

- **Buyer Dashboard > Referral Card:** Shows referral link, copy button, share-via-email button, and a summary: "You've referred X colleagues. Y credits earned. Z credits remaining."
- **Settings > Referrals:** Full referral management UI: create referrals, view status of all referrals, see credit balances, and view fraud-flag status (user sees "Under review" for flagged referrals, not the specific fraud signals).
- **Billing > Credits:** Credit balance shown alongside plan invoices.
- **Referral Link Landing Page:** Custom Sourcera signup page with referral attribution, referrer Org name (anonymized to company size + industry if referrer opts for anonymous referral), and a CTA to sign up.

#### Data Collected / Retained

Cross-reference §4.3.16 Retention. Summary: retained for financial audit + Stripe Credit Note reconciliation per §40.2; `referee_email` pseudonymized on DSAR; core financial fields retained unaltered under the §6.8.5 row #3 financial-record retained-row class. Residency: referrer Org's data region.

#### Anti-Abuse Controls

All seven controls from §48.4.6 Referral Fraud Controls apply. Additionally:

1. **Same-domain self-referral block (§48.4.6 #1):** Referrer and referee on the same email domain (excluding shared-use per §48.4.3) → `same_domain_suppressed = true`, credit blocked.
2. **Payment-method overlap (§48.4.6 #2):** Same Stripe fingerprint → `payment_method_overlap_detected`, credit blocked.
3. **IP-range overlap (§48.4.6 #3):** ≥ 80% of session IPs in same /24 → `ip_range_overlap_detected`, credit flagged.
4. **Bootstrapping pattern (§48.4.6 #4):** Graph analysis → `bootstrapping_pattern`, credit flagged.
5. **Velocity spike (§48.4.6 #5):** > 5 referrals in 24h → `velocity_spike`, credit flagged.
6. **Minimum-activity gating (§48.4.6 #6):** Referee must reach activation threshold before credit issues.
7. **Cross-Org Free-Allowance harvest (§48.4.6 #7):** Detected referral-ring Orgs have L5 Free Allowances suppressed.
8. **Ops kill-switch (§48.4.6):** Ops may block all M16 credits for a specific Org.
9. **Referee Exclusivity Rule (§4.3.16):** Only first-to-activate referrer gets credit per referee email.

#### Plan Gating & Entitlement

| Buyer Plan | M16 Access | Credit Value | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Buyer Free | ❌ | — | §34.1.1 |
| Business Starter | ❌ | — | §34.1.1 |
| Business Growth | ❌ | — | §34.1.1 |
| Business Scale | ✅ | $100 per qualified referral | §34.1.1, §4.3.16 |
| Buyer Enterprise | ✅ | $200 per qualified referral | §34.1.1, §4.3.16 |

No cap on the number of referrals a Scale or Enterprise Org can issue. The velocity throttle (§48.4.6 #5) serves as the abuse brake.

#### API Endpoints

**`POST /v1/referrals`** — Create a new referral. Auth: Buyer console; `org_owner`, `org_admin`, or `billing_admin`. Rate limit: `standard_write`. Request body: `{ "referee_email": "<email>", "invited_via_channel": "in_app|email|link_copy|social" }`. Response 201: BuyerReferral object (referrer-projection). Multiple concurrent referrals for the same `referee_email` ARE permitted at create time; exclusivity is enforced at the `pending → signed_up` transition per §4.3.16 + Appendix L.2 (Referee Exclusivity Rule). Errors: `m16_plan_not_eligible` (HTTP 403), `m16_same_domain_blocked` (HTTP 422; when domain is not shared-use), `m16_velocity_exceeded` (HTTP 429), `m16_referrer_org_in_fraud_cooldown` (HTTP 403; referrer Org currently in `flagged_fraud` SIM cooldown).

**`GET /v1/referrals`** — List referrals for the buyer Org. Auth: Buyer console; `org_owner`, `org_admin`, or `billing_admin`. Cursor-paginated (default 50, max 250). Filter params: `status`, `created_after`, `created_before`.

**`GET /v1/referrals/{id}`** — Get a single referral. Auth: same. Response 200 (referrer-projection).

**`GET /v1/referrals/summary`** — Aggregate referral stats for the Org. Auth: same. Response 200: `{ "total_referrals": N, "credits_earned_usd": "X.XX", "credits_remaining_usd": "X.XX", "pending_referrals": N }`.

**Ops endpoints** (§43 Admin Console):

**`GET /v1/ops/referrals`** — Ops listing across all Orgs. Cursor-paginated. Filter params: `referrer_org_id`, `referee_org_id`, `status`, `fraud_signal_flags`, `same_domain_suppressed`, `payment_method_overlap_detected`.

**`POST /v1/ops/referrals/{id}/override`** — Override a fraud block. Auth: `ops_security_admin` or `ops_finance_admin`. Request body: `{ "override_note": "<string>" }`. Sets `ops_override_user_id` and `ops_override_note`; transitions `status` from `flagged_fraud` to `activated` (re-runs step 7–9).

**`POST /v1/ops/referrals/{id}/revoke`** — Revoke a referral credit. Auth: `ops_finance_admin`. Request body: `{ "reason": "<string>" }`. Transitions to `revoked`; Stripe Credit Note reversed.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. Same-domain self-referral (referrer Org domain = referee email domain, excluding §48.4.3 shared-use domains) MUST set `same_domain_suppressed = true` and block credit issuance. QA test: `m16_same_domain_block`.
2. Payment-method overlap MUST be detected on referee's first Stripe invoice and MUST set `payment_method_overlap_detected = true` and transition to `flagged_fraud`. QA test: `m16_payment_overlap`.
3. Minimum-activity gating MUST prevent credit issuance until the referee Org reaches the activation threshold. QA test: `m16_activity_gating`.
4. The Referee Exclusivity Rule (§4.3.16 + Appendix L.2) MUST be enforced at the `pending → signed_up` transition: the first referral to bind a given `referee_org_id` wins; losing referrals transition to `forfeited` with `credit_forfeited_reason = referee_exclusivity_claimed`; subsequent API state-probes of losing referrals return `referral_referee_already_bound` (HTTP 409). Multiple concurrent referrals in `pending` for the same `referee_email` MUST be permitted at create time. QA test: `m16_exclusivity_rule`.
5. Credit issuance MUST create a Stripe Credit Note and append its ID to `stripe_credit_note_ids`. QA test: `m16_stripe_credit_note`.
6. Credit expiry (365 days from issuance) MUST be enforced by nightly sweep; expired credits MUST NOT be applied to future invoices. QA test: `m16_credit_expiry_sweep`.
7. All seven §48.4.6 fraud signals MUST be computed nightly AND populated to `fraud_signal_flags[]`; same-day signals (velocity_spike, same_payment_method) MUST also fire in real-time. QA test: `m16_fraud_signals_computed`.
8. Fraud-flag accumulation (≥ 3 distinct flags) MUST trigger auto-kill-switch eligibility per §48.4.6 AC #4. QA test: `m16_auto_kill_switch`.
9. Every M16 lifecycle event MUST emit the corresponding PostHog event within 5 seconds. QA test: `m16_telemetry_events`.
10. Ops override MUST require `ops_security_admin` or `ops_finance_admin` role and MUST log `ops_override_user_id` + `ops_override_note` in audit. QA test: `m16_ops_override_audit`.

#### Failure Modes Addressed

1. **Double-credit on duplicate referrals for the same referee.** Resolved: Referee Exclusivity Rule (§4.3.16 + Appendix L.2) fires at `pending → signed_up`. Multiple referrals for the same `referee_email` coexist in `pending`; the first to bind `referee_org_id` at signup wins; losing referrals transition to `forfeited` with `credit_forfeited_reason = referee_exclusivity_claimed`. Only the winning referral reaches `credit_issued` via the nightly credit-issuance job. The `m16.referral.exclusivity_blocked` PostHog event is emitted once per losing referral for funnel diagnostics.
2. **Payment-method fraud (referrer and referee share a credit card).** Resolved: Stripe PaymentMethod fingerprint comparison on referee's first invoice; match triggers `flagged_fraud`. Credit is withheld; Ops must explicitly override to release.
3. **Sybil attack (single actor creating a referrer → referee chain).** Resolved: `same_ip_range` + `bootstrapping_pattern` co-occurrence detection via SIM. L5 Free Allowances suppressed for the offending Orgs per §48.4.6 #7.
4. **Referee Org reaches activation threshold but referrer Org has since been downgraded below Scale.** Resolved: `credit_value_usd` is frozen at referral creation time; the credit is still issued at the original value. Referrer Org's current plan does not retroactively disqualify. Authored extension — flagged.
5. **Stripe Credit Note creation fails (Stripe outage).** Resolved: the `activated → credit_issued` transition is retried with exponential backoff (1s/2s/4s/8s/16s; DLQ at 5). While in retry, `status` remains `activated` (not `credit_issued`). Once DLQ'd, an Ops alert fires (§43 P2); Ops manually reconciles via `POST /v1/ops/referrals/{id}/override`.
6. **Ops adjusts the minimum-activity threshold mid-flight.** Resolved: `activity_threshold_policy_version` is stamped at referral creation; the activation check uses the stamped version, not the current version. Retroactive threshold changes cannot disqualify existing referrals.

7. **Stripe chargeback post-credit-issuance. (V13 D-13V-025 remediation 2026-05-12.)** When Stripe issues a chargeback against an invoice that consumed an M16 credit (the referee's invoice voids while the referrer's credit was already applied), the Stripe webhook `credit_note.voided` fires. The §4.3.16 BuyerReferral state machine transitions `credit_redeemed → forfeited_post_redemption` (new state — §4.3.16 V13 extension); a reverse Stripe Credit Note is queued for the referrer; the audit event `m16.referral.credit_forfeited_post_redemption {referral_id, reason, voided_credit_note_id, reverse_credit_note_id}` writes; a Loops.so email `m16_referral_credit_forfeited_post_redemption` fires to the referrer's `billing_admin` + `org_owner`. The referee's account is unaffected. State-machine row authored at Appendix L.2 V13 block.

#### M16 Conversion Funnel (V13 D-13V-008 remediation 2026-05-12)

The canonical M16 buyer referral conversion funnel is registered at §51.0.3 as `buyer_referral_funnel`. Funnel stage definitions, anchor events, customer-visible dashboard surface, and §42 alert thresholds are single-sourced at §51.0.3 to prevent inline drift. §48.7.3 cites §51.0.3 and does not duplicate the funnel definition. The 13 telemetry events listed in §48.7.3 telemetry table compose the 7 funnel stages (`created → link_shared → referee_signed_up → referee_activated → credit_issued → credit_applied → credit_redeemed`) plus 6 non-funnel diagnostic events (`same_domain_blocked`, `payment_overlap_detected`, `fraud_sweep_completed`, `exclusivity_blocked`, `credit_expired`, `ops_override`) that surface on the §51.3 Org-Level Dashboard "Referral Funnel" panel as side-channel diagnostics. CI gate `m16_funnel_canonical_consumer` (§M.5 — new) asserts the §51.0.3 registry is the sole authoring home for the M16 funnel.

### 48.7.4 M17 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat {#48.7.4-m17-buyer-funded-pro-trial-seat}

#### Purpose

M17 allows buyers on Business Scale (5 seats/month) or Buyer Enterprise (15 seats/month) to grant invited vendors a 30-day Seller Starter trial, free to the vendor, with cost absorbed into the buyer's plan. The mechanic lifts seller-side conversion rate at the highest-converting PLG moment — the forced vendor signup during a live evaluation — by eliminating the Free-tier ceiling exactly when the vendor is most engaged. AI usage during the trial is metered to the vendor's Org AIWallet, not the buyer's. The trial auto-downgrades to Seller Free on day 31 unless the vendor converts.

**§34.13 is the authoritative procedural specification for M17.** This section does NOT duplicate §34.13 content. It provides the operational integration context (anti-abuse, telemetry, notifications, webhooks, API endpoints, and acceptance criteria) that §34.13 defers to §48.7.4 per the M-mechanic catalog structure. For grant mechanics, allocation rules, trial completion outcomes, restrictions, metering, and failure modes, see §34.13 verbatim.

**§4.3.17 is the authoritative entity specification for M17.** This section does NOT duplicate the field table. For the BuyerFundedProTrialSeatGrant entity, indexes, scope isolation, retention, and entity-level failure modes, see §4.3.17 verbatim.

#### Trigger

A buyer user clicks "Invite with Pro Trial" during the vendor invitation flow. The CTA surfaces in: (a) the Workspace > Vendor Curation panel (§14); (b) the Marketplace > EOI Acceptance flow (§4.5.8); (c) the "Invite Vendor" global action. The CTA is visible only when `buyer_plan_tier ∈ {scale, enterprise}` AND `buyer_pool_seats_remaining > 0` for the current billing cycle. If allocation = 0, the CTA is disabled with copy: "0 of {N} Pro Trial Seats remaining this month."

#### Actor & Entity Schema

**Acting entity.** Buyer Org user with `org_admin`, `workspace_owner`, or `billing_admin` role per §5.3. Role check at click time (§34.13.3 step 1).

**Persisted entity: BuyerFundedProTrialSeatGrant (§4.3.17).** Cross-reference only. See §4.3.17 for full entity.

#### Workflow

The eight-step grant workflow is defined in §34.13.3. The ten-step trial completion flow is defined in §34.13.4. The restrictions are defined in §34.13.5. This section adds the operational integration context:

**Cross-console billing reconciliation.** The trial grant creates a financial relationship that spans the Buyer and Seller consoles:

| Financial Event | Console | Entity | Billing Effect |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Grant issued | Buyer | BuyerFundedProTrialSeatGrant | Buyer's pool decremented (no Stripe charge; pool is plan-included) |
| Trial provisioned | Seller | Seller Org plan change | Seller Org plan set to `seller_starter` with `trial_source_buyer_org_id`; entitlements activated |
| AI usage during trial | Seller | AIOperation rows | Metered to **vendor's** AIWallet (§34.13.1); NOT the buyer's |
| Day-27 reminder | Seller | — | Notification to vendor Billing Admin |
| Day-31 conversion | Seller | Seller Org plan persists | `sourcera_pro_trial_conversion` Stripe meter event |
| Day-31 auto-downgrade | Seller | Seller Org → `seller_free` | `sourcera_pro_trial_expired` Stripe meter event; §34.6 preservation |
| Day-31 decline | Seller | Same as auto-downgrade | `sourcera_pro_trial_expired` Stripe meter event |

The **30-day auto-downgrade** is the default outcome. Per §34.13.4: vendor takes no action by day 31 23:59 UTC → plan downgrades to `seller_free` → entities exceeding Free caps enter §34.6 90-day read-only preservation. The downgrade executes as a scheduled job that runs at `trial_expires_at`; idempotent (QA test `pro_trial_day_31_idempotent` per §34.13.8 AC #2).

#### UX Surfaces

- **Buyer > Vendor Invitation Flow:** "Invite with Pro Trial" toggle/button with pool balance indicator.
- **Buyer > Settings > Pro Trial Seats:** Pool balance, history of issued grants, conversion rate summary.
- **Seller > Onboarding (post-magic-link):** "Your invite includes 30 days of Seller Starter, free" banner with feature highlights.
- **Seller > Billing:** "Granted by [Buyer Org] until [date]" in Wallet UI (per §34.13.6).
- **Seller > Day-27 Banner:** In-app + email conversion prompt.

#### Data Collected / Retained

Cross-reference §4.3.17 Retention. Summary: Org-life + 7 years for financial audit; DSAR pseudonymization on `vendor_email`, `issuer_user_id`, `vendor_email_domain`; aggregate conversion metrics retained.

#### Anti-Abuse Controls

1. **One trial per buyer-vendor pair per 365 days (§34.13.5).** Enforced via `same_buyer_365d_block_triggered`.
2. **Vendor already on paid plan (§34.13.5).** `already_paid_block_triggered = true`; grant reversed to buyer pool.
3. **Buyer below Scale (§34.13.5).** No allocation; CTA hidden.
4. **Pool exhaustion (§34.13.5).** Returns `trial_seat_pool_exhausted` (HTTP 403).
5. **Anti-spam framework (§34.13.5, §48.4.6).** Referral Fraud Controls §48.4.6 cross-apply to Pro Trial Seat grants. Signal Integrity Monitor may restrict a buyer's usage.
6. **Invite-eligibility gates (§34.13.5).** Domain verification, opt-out registry check, suppression list check.
7. **Anti-probing rule (§34.13.5, §34.13.8 AC #8).** Buyer's allocation decrements at click time, not at vendor redemption. Non-redemption does NOT refund. This prevents a buyer from repeatedly issuing grants to probe whether vendors will engage.

#### Plan Gating & Entitlement

Per §34.13.2 (authoritative):

| Buyer Plan | Pro Trial Seats per Month | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Buyer Free / Business Starter / Business Growth | 0 | BPS §3 |
| Business Scale | 5 | BPS §3, §3 footer |
| Buyer Enterprise | 15 | BPS §3, §3 footer |

AI usage during trial: metered to vendor's wallet at Seller Starter included budget ($30 value-dollars per §34.13.3 step 5). Cost-center: `customer_billed` (vendor's wallet), NOT `platform_marketing`.

#### Telemetry Events

| Event | Trigger | Appendix G Section |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `m17.pro_trial_seat.grant_issued` | §34.13.3 step 1–2 | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |
| `m17.pro_trial_seat.invite_sent` | §34.13.3 step 3 | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |
| `m17.pro_trial_seat.provisioned` | §34.13.3 step 4 | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |
| `m17.pro_trial_seat.day_27_reminder` | §34.13.3 step 7 | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |
| `m17.pro_trial_seat.converted` | §34.13.4 Convert | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |
| `m17.pro_trial_seat.auto_downgraded` | §34.13.4 Auto-downgrade | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |
| `m17.pro_trial_seat.declined` | §34.13.4 Decline | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |
| `m17.pro_trial_seat.buyer_revoked` | Buyer revocation pre-provisioning | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |
| `m17.pro_trial_seat.fraud_blocked` | Anti-spam hold | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |
| `m17.pro_trial_seat.expired_unaccepted` | 30-day invite TTL expiry | M14–M17 Mechanics Events |

#### Notifications Fired

| Kind | Channel | Recipient | Trigger |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `pro_trial_seat.invite` | Email (Loops.so) | Vendor email | §34.13.3 step 3 |
| `pro_trial_seat.granted` | In-app | Buyer issuer + Vendor (post-signup) | §34.13.3 step 4 |
| `pro_trial_seat.day_27_reminder` | Email + In-app | Vendor Billing Admin | §34.13.3 step 7 |
| `pro_trial_seat.converted` | Email + In-app | Both Orgs | §34.13.4 Convert |
| `pro_trial_seat.auto_downgraded` | Email + In-app | Vendor Billing Admin + Vendor Org Owner | §34.13.4 Auto-downgrade |
| `pro_trial_seat.declined` | In-app | Buyer issuer | §34.13.4 Decline |
| `pro_trial_seat.expired_unaccepted` | In-app | Buyer issuer | 30-day invite TTL |

#### Webhooks Fired

| Event Kind | Payload Entity | Retry Curve | Appendix C Registration |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `pro_trial_seat.granted` | BuyerFundedProTrialSeatGrant (buyer-projection) | Appendix F.1 `standard` | New |
| `pro_trial_seat.provisioned` | BuyerFundedProTrialSeatGrant (dual-projection per §4.3.17) | Appendix F.1 `standard` | New |
| `pro_trial_seat.converted` | BuyerFundedProTrialSeatGrant (dual-projection) | Appendix F.1 `standard` | New |
| `pro_trial_seat.auto_downgraded` | BuyerFundedProTrialSeatGrant (dual-projection) | Appendix F.1 `standard` | New |
| `pro_trial_seat.expired_unaccepted` | BuyerFundedProTrialSeatGrant (buyer-projection) | Appendix F.1 `standard` | New |

HMAC-SHA256 signed per §31. `event_id` idempotency. Payload ≤ 256KB. Dual-projection: buyer endpoint receives buyer-visible fields; vendor endpoint receives vendor-visible fields; per §4.3.17 Scope Isolation.

#### API Endpoints

**`POST /v1/pro-trial-seats`** — Issue a Pro Trial Seat grant. Auth: Buyer console; `org_admin`, `workspace_owner`, or `billing_admin`. Rate limit: `standard_write`. Idempotency key: `(buyer_org_id, vendor_email, buyer_billing_cycle_month)`. Request body: `{ "vendor_email": "<email>", "issuing_workspace_id": "<uuid|null>", "issuing_target_account_id": "<uuid|null>" }`. Response 201. Errors: `trial_seat_pool_exhausted` (HTTP 403), `trial_seat_buyer_below_scale` (HTTP 403), `trial_seat_vendor_already_paid` (HTTP 422), `trial_seat_same_buyer_365d_block` (HTTP 422).

**`GET /v1/pro-trial-seats`** — List grants for the requesting Org (buyer sees buyer-projection; vendor sees vendor-projection). Auth: any authenticated user. Cursor-paginated (default 50, max 250). Filter params: `status`, `outcome`, `created_after`, `created_before`.

**`GET /v1/pro-trial-seats/{id}`** — Single grant. Auth: buyer or vendor Org member per §4.3.17 dual-projection. Third-party Org → 404.

**`DELETE /v1/pro-trial-seats/{id}`** — Buyer revocation (pre-provisioning only). Auth: Buyer console; `org_admin` or `billing_admin`. Response 200 (`status → buyer_revoked`). Errors: `m17_grant_already_provisioned` (HTTP 422; cannot revoke a live trial).

**`GET /v1/pro-trial-seats/pool`** — Current pool balance for the buyer Org. Auth: Buyer console; `org_admin`, `workspace_owner`, or `billing_admin`. Response 200: `{ "plan_tier": "scale|enterprise", "monthly_allocation": 5|15, "used_this_cycle": N, "remaining_this_cycle": M, "cycle_start": "YYYY-MM-DD", "cycle_end": "YYYY-MM-DD" }`.

**Ops endpoints:**

**`GET /v1/ops/pro-trial-seats`** — Ops listing across all Orgs. Cursor-paginated. Filter params: `buyer_org_id`, `vendor_org_id`, `status`, `outcome`, `anti_spam_hold_reason`.

**`POST /v1/ops/pro-trial-seats/{id}/override-quota`** — Temporarily increase a buyer's allocation for a defined window (§34.13.2 Ops override path). Auth: `ops_pricing_admin`. Request body: `{ "additional_seats": N, "expires_at": "<timestamp>", "reason": "<string>" }`. Fires `org.pro_trial_seat_quota_overridden` audit event.

#### Acceptance Criteria

Per §34.13.8, eight acceptance criteria are defined for the Pro Trial Seat mechanic. This section adds operational integration criteria:

1. All eight §34.13.8 acceptance criteria MUST pass. This section extends, does not replace.
2. Day-31 auto-downgrade MUST trigger §34.6 preservation for over-cap entities; the downgrade job MUST execute exactly once per active trial (idempotent). QA test: `m17_day_31_preservation`.
3. Cross-console billing reconciliation: the buyer's pool decrement at grant time MUST be reflected in the buyer's billing dashboard within 60 seconds; the vendor's Seller Starter entitlements MUST activate within 5 minutes of magic-link redemption. QA test: `m17_cross_console_billing`.
4. Every M17 lifecycle event MUST emit the corresponding PostHog event within 5 seconds. QA test: `m17_telemetry_events`.
5. Webhook payloads MUST respect the dual-projection rule (§4.3.17 Scope Isolation): buyer endpoints receive buyer-visible fields only; vendor endpoints receive vendor-visible fields only. QA test: `m17_dual_projection_webhook`.
6. Pool balance endpoint MUST return real-time balance (within 2 seconds of the most recent grant issuance). QA test: `m17_pool_balance_realtime`.
7. Ops quota override MUST be time-boxed; overrides that pass `expires_at` MUST auto-reverse with `org.pro_trial_seat_quota_override_expired` audit event. QA test: `m17_ops_override_expiry`.

#### Failure Modes Addressed

The five failure modes in §34.13.7 and the six entity-level failure modes in §4.3.17 are authoritative. This section confirms operational coverage:

1. **Day-31 auto-downgrade concurrent with vendor conversion attempt.** Resolved: the conversion endpoint acquires a row-level lock on the BuyerFundedProTrialSeatGrant row; the auto-downgrade job checks `outcome IS NULL` before executing; if the vendor converts at 23:58 UTC, the conversion wins (last-write-wins with lock).
2. **Buyer Org deleted between grant issuance and vendor redemption (§4.3.17 failure mode #5).** The grant remains valid; vendor magic link works; vendor sees "[Buyer Org] (deleted)" in grant attribution UI. Pool accounting is moot (Org deleted).
3. **Multiple concurrent Pro Trial Seat grants from different buyers to the same vendor.** Per §34.13.7 failure mode #3: only the first redeemed grant activates; subsequent grants are queued with a 7-day acceptance window. If vendor does not accept within 7 days, queued grants expire and the issuing buyer's pool is refunded.
4. **Webhook delivery to buyer and vendor endpoints fails simultaneously (Stripe + notification outage).** Resolved: Appendix F.1 `standard` retry applies independently to buyer and vendor endpoints. DLQ'd events surface in Ops Console for manual reconciliation.

### 48.7.6 Cross-Mechanic Cross-Console Invariants (M14–M17) {#48.7.6-cross-mechanic-cross-console-invariants-m14-m17}

The four mechanics in §48.7 share a small set of cross-console invariants that are NOT restated in the per-mechanic subsections above and that MUST hold at all times. They are enumerated here so that CI, QA, and Ops have a single compact reference.

1. **Buyer-Seller console firewall integrity (M14, M17).** The buyer Org identifier MUST NEVER appear in any seller-facing M14 projection (API response, webhook payload, PostHog event property, email body). The only buyer-visible M14 surface is the `buyer_win_share_opt_out` workspace-level flag that the Buyer Workspace Owner can toggle. For M17, dual-projection webhooks per §4.3.17 are the sole allowed cross-console payload surface. Any violation raises `cross_console_firewall_violation` (Appendix I — existing) and pages `ops_security_admin`.
2. **Referrer attribution immutability (M16).** Once `BuyerReferral.created_at` is stamped, the `referrer_user_id`, `referrer_org_id`, `credit_value_usd`, and `activity_threshold_policy_version` fields are immutable for the lifetime of the row. Downgrade, role change, or policy update MUST NOT retroactively mutate these fields. Enforced at the Convex mutation layer; violation returns `entity_field_immutable` (Appendix I — existing).
3. **Signed_up transition is the exclusivity boundary (M16).** Per §4.3.16 + Appendix L.2, the Referee Exclusivity Rule fires at the `pending → signed_up` transition, not at referral creation and not at `activated → credit_issued`. Multiple referrals for the same `referee_email` MAY coexist in `pending`; the first to reach `signed_up` binds the referee Org; subsequent `signed_up` attempts for the same referee Org are rejected with `referral_referee_already_bound` (HTTP 409) and the losing referral transitions to `forfeited` with `credit_forfeited_reason = referee_exclusivity_claimed` (Appendix J extension — new).
4. **Nightly credit-issuance job is the sole credit writer (M16).** The `activated → credit_issued` transition is authored ONLY by the nightly credit-issuance job (§4.3.16 Appendix L.2 row), never inline at `activated` transition. Attempts to inline-issue credit MUST return `referral_credit_issuance_deferred` (Appendix I — new) with remediation pointing to the nightly job.
5. **Ghost-Bid first-free slot is lifetime-scoped (M15).** Per §4.4.17, the first-import-free slot is a lifetime allowance scoped to `seller_org_id`, not per billing cycle, plan tier, or M17 trial window. A seller Org that arrives via M17 and runs a Ghost-Bid Import during the trial consumes the lifetime-free slot. Post-trial downgrade to Seller Free does NOT refund the slot. This is an authored extension — flagged in RECONCILIATION.md.
6. **Review-queue staleness sweep (M15).** Any GhostBidImport row in `review_pending` for > 30 days MUST auto-transition to `rejected` with `rejected_by_role = staleness_sweep` and `failure_reason = review_pending_exceeded_30d_sla`. First-import-free slot is retained (the lifetime-free allowance is consumed only at `published` per §4.4.17 AC #1). The sweep is a Convex scheduled job that runs nightly at 02:00 UTC. QA test: `m15_review_queue_staleness_sweep`.
7. **Cross-mechanic attribution ambiguity (M14, M16, M17).** When a single seller Org is the target of multiple mechanics simultaneously — e.g., vendor was invited via M17 Pro Trial Seat, also received an M5 buyer-pull invite, and later publishes an M14 share — each mechanic's GrowthLoopExecution row records its own attribution independently; no mechanic "wins" another's attribution. Attribution compounding is tracked via `metadata_json.cross_mechanic_attribution[]` per §48.2.13 AC #7.
8. **Ops kill-switch feature-flag parity (M14–M17).** Each mechanic's per-mechanic Ops kill-switch (M14: `feature_flag_m14_bid_success_share_enabled`; M15: `feature_flag_m15_ghost_bid_import_enabled`; M16: `feature_flag_m16_buyer_referral_enabled`; M17: `feature_flag_m17_pro_trial_seat_enabled`) MUST propagate to orchestrator caches within 60 seconds worst-case per §22.16.5. When disabled, the corresponding API endpoints return `mechanic_disabled_by_ops` (Appendix I — new) with HTTP 503.
9. **Appendix J enum extension (M16 exclusivity).** The `referral_forfeit_reason` enum is extended to include `referee_exclusivity_claimed` in addition to the pre-existing values (`fraud_suspected`, `payment_overlap`, `same_domain_violation`, `insufficient_activity`, `referee_opt_out`). Registered in Appendix J under §29 Controlled Vocabulary Registry.

**Acceptance Criteria (Cross-Mechanic).**

1. A QA invariant test MUST assert that no seller-facing M14 API response, webhook payload, or PostHog event property contains the string value of any buyer Org `display_name`, `legal_entity_name`, `domain`, or `org_id`. QA test: `m14_cross_console_firewall_invariant`.
2. An immutability test MUST assert that updating `BuyerReferral.referrer_user_id`, `BuyerReferral.credit_value_usd`, or `BuyerReferral.activity_threshold_policy_version` after row creation returns `entity_field_immutable` (HTTP 422). QA test: `m16_immutability_invariant`.
3. A concurrency test MUST assert that concurrent `pending → signed_up` transitions for referrals with the same `referee_email` resolve deterministically: exactly one referral reaches `signed_up`; all others transition to `forfeited` with `credit_forfeited_reason = referee_exclusivity_claimed`. QA test: `m16_signed_up_exclusivity_concurrency`.
4. A staleness-sweep test MUST assert that a GhostBidImport created 30+ days ago in `review_pending` auto-transitions to `rejected` on the nightly sweep; the first-import-free slot remains available. QA test: `m15_review_queue_staleness_sweep`.
5. An Ops kill-switch test MUST assert that disabling any M14–M17 feature flag causes the corresponding API endpoint to return HTTP 503 `mechanic_disabled_by_ops` within 60 seconds. QA test: `m14_m17_ops_kill_switch_propagation`.
