## 48.8 Seller Hero Moment & Onboarding Anti-Patterns {#48.8-seller-hero-moment-and-onboarding-anti-patterns}

**Authoring intent.** §48.8 is the product-surface specification for the Seller Hero Moment — the coordinated UX surface that puts a pre-populated KB Draft, a first-pass response set, and a progress strip in front of the seller *before the seller touches anything* — and the hard ban-list of six onboarding anti-patterns. The content here is normative for engineering, product, design, and QA; the six anti-patterns are HARD QA-testable bans, not guidelines, and every banned behavior has an explicit detector, a failure mode, and an acceptance criterion that CI must enforce.

The Hero Moment is the single largest product bet in the Seller Console. It collapses the new-vendor cold-start wall from ~2 days (status quo: manual triage, KB hunt, draft from scratch) to ~30 seconds of latency hidden behind an honest onboarding progress bar. The vendor arrives with the work already started, their own content already in the tool, and the buyer's real requirements already answered — before any pricing conversation. If the Hero Moment degrades, the Seller Activation Metric degrades, the Forced-Vendor-Signup funnel collapses, and the network effects (S1, S2, S3, S4, S7 per §48.3.5) lose their Free-tier fuel. Treat this section as P0.

**Source authority.** Summary Summary §3.1b ¶ ¶1–2 ("Your first bid is already drafted"); Summary §3.6 (Seller-Side Hero Moment Mechanics, verbatim) — four paragraphs + six anti-patterns; C.132 (Seller Hero Moment Mechanics — appendix); SPS v3 §15.3 Four Seller Conversion Moments; C.133 (pre-Solo Three Conversion Moments baseline); C.135 (Seller Activation Metric); C.136 (Forced-Vendor-Signup Playbook); C.140 (Seller Onboarding Required Capabilities); C.141 (Seller Onboarding Anti-Patterns — banned); Summary §6.28.2 (Seven-Stage Seller Onboarding Experience). Entity schema at §4.4.22 SellerOnboardingSession. Four-phase framework cross-reference at §48.1.5. Four Seller Conversion Moments binding at §48.1.7.

### 48.8.1 Overview & Scope {#48.8.1-overview-and-scope}

**In scope.** The Seller Console onboarding UX from magic-link invitation through post-submission Stake-Reveal, comprising: (a) pre-arrival preparation, (b) onboarding surface (minutes 0–3), (c) in-workspace value proof (minutes 3–45), (d) post-submission reveal (hour 1+). Plus the four Seller Conversion Moments (mid-bid AI budget wall, second concurrent bid, first EOI, KB ceiling) and the six banned anti-patterns.

**Out of scope.** Buyer-side invite-creation UX (covered in §48.2.2 L1 and §48.5 M1 / M5 / M15); the Ops surface that manages Seller verification tiers (§4.4.21 VerificationReviewRecord); post-activation Conversion-Moment mechanics beyond the first moment (covered at §48.1.7 for definitional binding; §48.8.6 for UX surface). The Win/Loss Debrief (C.137) is covered in §48.7 Seller Conversion Mechanics and is NOT authored in §48.8.

**Per-surface structure.** Each onboarding phase subsection below (§48.8.2 through §48.8.5) follows the same eleven-block layout: (1) Purpose; (2) Authoritative Source; (3) Trigger / Entry Condition; (4) Workflow (step-by-step); (5) UX Surface Specification; (6) Data Read / Written (entity refs); (7) Capabilities Invoked (§21.4); (8) AIWallet Debits (§34.10); (9) Telemetry Events; (10) Failure Modes Addressed; (11) Acceptance Criteria. §48.8.6 (Four Seller Conversion Moments UX Surface) follows the same structure with moment-specific variations.

**Cross-references.** Four-phase summary framework: §48.1.5. Activation Metric targets and leading indicators: §48.1.6. Four Seller Conversion Moments definitive binding: §48.1.7. SellerOnboardingSession entity schema: §4.4.22. KB Bootstrap workflow: §22.4. First-Pass RFP Draft: §22.5. KB-Gap Detector: §22.6. Citation Inline Card: §22.7. Capability Registry: §21.4. AIWallet Lifetime-Free Bootstrap Allowance: §34.10.4. Marketplace Taxonomy: §6.16.6. Seven-Stage Seller Onboarding Experience: §6.28.2.

### 48.8.2 Pre-Arrival Preparation {#48.8.2-pre-arrival-preparation}

**Purpose.** Before the vendor clicks the magic-link, Sourcera resolves every deterministic piece of state needed to make the in-SSO-redirect execution of KB Bootstrap + First-Pass RFP Draft possible within §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold`. Pre-arrival preparation is invisible to the vendor and runs on invite-creation (§4.5.x MarketplaceInviteLink) not on invite-click.

**Authoritative Source.** Summary §3.6 ¶1; C.132 ¶1 "Pre-arrival preparation."

**Trigger / Entry Condition.** Creation of a MarketplaceInviteLink row (§4.5.x) with `invite_source ∈ {buyer_invite, ghost_bid_conversion, pro_trial_seat_m17}` (pre-arrival preparation does NOT run for `direct_signup` — direct signups have no pre-bound context to prepare against).

**Workflow.**

1. **Email-domain enrichment.** On MarketplaceInviteLink write, enqueue a `seller_domain_enrichment` job that queries public records (Clearbit / BuiltWith / Perplexity citations) to resolve `company_name`, `industry`, `hq_region`, and `estimated_employee_count` keyed by the email domain. Results persist on a SellerDomainEnrichmentRecord (§4.5.x — Authored Extension flagged). Cached for 30 days; re-enrichment occurs on cache miss.
2. **Marketplace Tagger category inference.** Feed `seller_domain_hint` + buyer-side bid category into the Marketplace Tagger (Summary §6.16.6 taxonomy service) to assign up to 5 candidate `category_id` tags (probability-weighted) that will seed Capability Declaration suggestions at Stage 3.
3. **Firecrawl rate-limit pre-warm.** For each candidate domain (`seller_domain_hint`), reserve Firecrawl quota (§31.x integration) for (a) homepage, (b) security / trust center subpages, (c) product / help / docs subpages per the Opus Bootstrap crawl contract. Reservation is cancellable if the magic-link is not clicked within 7 days; cancellation re-credits the quota.
4. **`kb_bootstrap` queue pre-resolution.** Enqueue a speculative `kb_bootstrap` job in the Managed Agent orchestrator (§22.16) with `execution_state = 'pre_resolved'` — the job is prepared (URLs resolved, robots.txt parsed, per-host budget allocated) but NOT executed. At magic-link click, the job transitions to `execution_state = 'executing'` without re-preparing.
5. **Bid-context pre-fetch.** If `bid_id` is set (Forced-Vendor-Signup), pre-fetch the buyer's bid requirements so that at magic-link click, the First-Pass RFP Draft can fire against the full requirements list without a synchronous DB join.

**UX Surface Specification.** None — pre-arrival is hidden. The only vendor-visible artifact is the email invitation itself (see §41.2 Email Type Catalog).

**Data Read / Written.** MarketplaceInviteLink (read); SellerDomainEnrichmentRecord (write); `kb_bootstrap` pre-resolved job (write — transient row in §4.3.18 Usage Event with `event_category = 'pre_resolved_job'` and `settlement_state = 'deferred'`); Firecrawl-reservation metadata (write to §31.x integration state).

**Capabilities Invoked.** None executed; `kb_bootstrap` pre-resolved.

**AIWallet Debits.** None (no AI inference runs during pre-arrival).

**Telemetry Events.**

- `seller_invite_pre_arrival_enrichment_started {invite_id, seller_domain_hint}` (Appendix G — new)
- `seller_invite_pre_arrival_enrichment_completed {invite_id, seller_domain_hint, enrichment_fields_resolved[], elapsed_seconds}` (Appendix G — new)
- `seller_invite_pre_arrival_enrichment_failed {invite_id, seller_domain_hint, failure_reason ∈ {domain_unresolvable, external_api_timeout, taxonomy_match_failure}}` (Appendix G — new)
- `seller_invite_pre_resolved_bootstrap_job_created {invite_id, bootstrap_job_id}` (Appendix G — new)

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Enrichment external API (Clearbit / BuiltWith) outage.** Enrichment is best-effort; on failure, `company_name`/`industry`/`hq_region` stay null; Stage 3 populator falls back to domain-only display (*"Drafting responses for [Buyer Company]'s 82 requirements…"* with no *"Scanning yourcompany.com…"* line). Pre-arrival does NOT block magic-link validity.
2. **Firecrawl per-host rate-limit exhaustion.** Reservation attempt fails; pre-arrival persists a `pre_arrival_firecrawl_reservation_failed` flag on the MarketplaceInviteLink row. Stage 3 populator detects the flag and enqueues a degraded bootstrap path (fewer URLs, lower depth) — no silent failure.
3. **Magic-link never clicked (expired pre-arrival prep).** Cleanup sweep (nightly) purges stale pre-resolved jobs older than 7 days; Firecrawl reservations re-credited; SellerDomainEnrichmentRecord retained 30 days (caching use).

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Every MarketplaceInviteLink with `invite_source ∈ {buyer_invite, ghost_bid_conversion, pro_trial_seat_m17}` MUST trigger pre-arrival preparation within **10 seconds** of creation; synthetic-load test asserts 99% compliance at 1,000 concurrent invite creations.
2. Pre-resolved `kb_bootstrap` jobs MUST transition to `execution_state = 'executing'` within **500 ms** of magic-link click (i.e., the pre-resolution work is NOT re-done at click time).
3. Firecrawl-reservation credit release on cancellation MUST execute within the nightly cleanup window AND be reconcilable to the Firecrawl integration ledger within 1% drift daily.
4. Pre-arrival failures (enrichment, Firecrawl, taxonomy) MUST NOT block magic-link validity; the fallback path MUST engage silently AND emit `seller_invite_pre_arrival_enrichment_failed` for Ops telemetry.

### 48.8.3 Onboarding Surface — Minutes 0–3 {#48.8.3-onboarding-surface-minutes-0-3}

**Purpose.** From magic-link click through Bid Workspace first paint, the seller sees (a) a zero-friction SSO / magic-link flow, (b) an honest progress-storytelling screen, and (c) the landing counter (*"Your bid is ready. **47** AI drafts prepared…"*). The window is bounded at 3 minutes by §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold` and by the Activation-Metric leading indicator that 80% of sellers make first edit within 3 minutes.

**Authoritative Source.** Summary §3.6 ¶2; Summary Summary §3.1b ¶2; C.132 ¶2 (in-SSO-redirect execution); Summary §6.28.2 Stages 1–3; C.141 anti-patterns (for what the surface MUST NOT contain).

**Trigger / Entry Condition.** Magic-link click → HTTP GET on the MarketplaceInviteLink landing URL.

**Workflow.**

1. **T=0: Landing page load.** Unauthenticated Marketplace landing renders an RFP summary preview + single primary CTA (*"Accept this bid and draft your response in 3 minutes"*). Zero form fields. No credit card. No role selection. No company description. No industry dropdown. No team size. Just: "Accept and draft".
2. **T=0–15 s: Primary CTA click → SSO initiate.** Seller clicks CTA → `stage_2_sso_initiated_at` written. SSO flow begins (Google / Microsoft). Magic-link fallback offered if SSO unavailable.
3. **T=15–30 s: SSO redirect + parallel Bootstrap start.** At the SSO OAuth redirect, the pre-resolved `kb_bootstrap` job transitions to `execution_state = 'executing'`. `stage_2_bootstrap_started_at` written. The Bootstrap is drawing from the lifetime-free allowance per C.140.
4. **T=30–60 s: SSO completion + Seller Org provisioning.** SSO callback → Seller Org created (if new) or resolved (existing); User created (if new); `stage_2_sso_completed_at` written. `org_id` backfilled on SellerOnboardingSession row.
5. **T=30–90 s: Progress storytelling.** Progress screen renders with **literal** status lines sequenced against the actual work:
    - *"Scanning yourcompany.com…"* (displays while Firecrawl crawl is in flight — 0–15 s after Bootstrap start)
    - *"Found your security documentation…"* (displays when first security-category page is resolved — typically 15–30 s)
    - *"Drafting responses for [Buyer Company]'s 82 requirements…"* (displays when First-Pass Draft invocation begins — 30–90 s)
    - *"Your bid is ready to review."* (displays when Bid Workspace populator is ready to render — done)
   Each status line MUST be literally true; faking progress is an anti-pattern (§48.8.7 #7 — banned).
6. **T=60–90 s: First-Pass RFP Draft execution.** `first_pass_response` capability fires per requirement; per-requirement drafts are streamed to the Bid Workspace populator. Per §22.7, every draft MUST cite before stating.
7. **T=90 s: Bid Workspace loaded.** `stage_3_bid_workspace_loaded_at` written. `stage_3_population_latency_ms` computed. `hero_moment_completed_at` written if all three Stage 3 surfaces are present (KB Draft + first-pass response + progress strip) AND `stage_3_population_latency_ms` satisfies §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold`. Landing counter renders: *"Your bid is ready. **[N]** AI drafts prepared. **[M]** cite evidence from your website. Review time: **~[X] min**."* (N = drafted-requirement count, M = drafts with KB-backed citations, X = median review-time estimate from analogous cohort).
8. **T=90 s–3 min: First edit signal.** Seller begins reviewing; first click on any Accept / Edit / Reject button writes `stage_3_first_edit_at`. Summary §6.28.2 Stage 3 success criterion: ≥ 80% of sessions record `stage_3_first_edit_at` within 3 minutes of `stage_3_bid_workspace_loaded_at`.

**UX Surface Specification.**

- **Landing page (pre-SSO).** Single centered column; 64 px vertical spacing; brand logo + bid-title H1 + one-sentence buyer-company summary + primary CTA button (56 px, primary-dark token). No footer links beyond "Privacy" and "Terms" (required for legal compliance). No upgrade callouts. No pricing page link. No "Learn more about Sourcera" secondary CTA. NO modal dialogs of any kind. NO cookie banner that blocks interaction (use a non-blocking bottom-right banner per §45.x cookie-consent pattern).
- **Progress screen (post-SSO, pre-Bid-Workspace-load).** Full-viewport dark-mode-respecting progress UI with four status lines, scrolling into view as each completes. Per-line animation duration matches the median elapsed-time for that step (i.e., the line does NOT rush ahead of the actual work — that would be anti-pattern-adjacent to faked-progress). A small elapsed-seconds counter top-right builds trust.
- **Landing counter.** Rendered at first paint of the Bid Workspace, position top-right of the primary workspace canvas. Three-number composition: `{N}` AI drafts, `{M}` citations, `{X}` min estimated review. No call-to-action. No upgrade prompt. No "Try Pro free for 14 days" modal.

**Data Read / Written.** MarketplaceInviteLink (read); SellerOnboardingSession (create at T=0; update at each timestamp); Seller Org (create at T=30–60 s if new); User (create at T=30–60 s if new); KBEntry (writes during Bootstrap); AIOperation + Usage Event (writes during Bootstrap + First-Pass); Bid Workspace (populator writes).

**Capabilities Invoked.** `kb_bootstrap` (Opus; lifetime-free); `first_pass_response` (Sonnet/Opus; cost-priced-rejected unless accepted). Secondary: `page_enrichment` may fire to enrich the Seller Profile at publication (triggers at Stage 5 per Summary §6.28.2).

**AIWallet Debits.** `kb_bootstrap` draws lifetime-free allowance (no wallet debit). `first_pass_response` runs draw from the $5 free Seller Wallet allowance (§34.10.4); if wallet is exhausted mid-Hero-Moment, remaining drafts are cost-priced-rejected with zero charge to the seller. NEVER hard-block mid-Hero-Moment.

**Telemetry Events.**

- `seller_onboarding_stage_entered {seller_org_id (nullable pre-SSO), stage ∈ {1,2,3}, invite_source, elapsed_seconds_since_arrival, stage_outcome ∈ {completed, abandoned, errored}}` (Appendix G — new; replaces any ad-hoc `seller_onboarding_stage_*` events from prior drafts)
- `hero_moment_completed {seller_org_id, bid_id, stage_3_population_latency_ms, stage_3_kb_draft_entry_count, stage_3_first_pass_response_requirement_count, stage_3_first_pass_response_cited_count, capability_degradation_triggered=boolean}` (Appendix G — new)
- `hero_moment_latency_breached {seller_org_id, bid_id, stage_3_population_latency_ms, threshold_ms}` (Appendix G — new) — fires whenever §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold` is breached; `threshold_ms` is populated from the §44.1 source row
- `hero_moment_first_edit {seller_org_id, bid_id, elapsed_seconds_from_bid_workspace_loaded}` (Appendix G — new)
- `first_pass_response_capability_degradation_triggered {seller_org_id, bid_id, degradation_kind ∈ {capability_unavailable, partial_draft_coverage, timeout}}` (Appendix G — new)

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **SSO provider outage mid-flow.** Magic-link fallback is surfaced inline on SSO-redirect failure — NEVER a hard error page. Stage 2 stalls cleanly; seller retries via email link.
2. **First-Pass Responder capability unavailable.** Graceful degradation per C.140: Bootstrap still runs, KB entries are proposed, and the Bid Workspace loads with KB-Draft-only mode. A banner renders: *"Response drafting unavailable right now — your KB is ready and we'll notify you when drafts are available. Retry →"*. NEVER silent empty Bid Workspace.
3. **Stage 3 population latency threshold breach.** Session proceeds to Bid Workspace; `hero_moment_completed_at` NOT populated; `hero_moment_latency_breached` emits; on-call paged per §4.4.22 AC 4 and §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 latency breach page SLA`.
4. **Seller hits Back button mid-Stage-2.** Session remains `in_progress`; the back navigation does NOT create a new session row. If seller retries within 24h, same session row progresses; if retries post-24h, existing row abandons on sweep.
5. **Seller's email alias resolves to an existing Seller Org (Org-disambiguation).** Per §4.4.22 failure mode 10: disambiguation flow engaged; session transitions to `errored` with `error_code = 'seller_org_disambiguation_required'`.
6. **Firecrawl outage during Stage 2 / Stage 3 (`kb_bootstrap` URL crawl path).** *(V13 D-13V-022 remediation 2026-05-12.)* When the Firecrawl API returns HTTP 5xx, exceeds the per-request 30-second timeout, or its health-detector state (§42.6.0 ProviderHealthState `provider_kind = 'firecrawl'`) is `degraded` or `down`, the Hero Moment surface MUST follow the full degradation contract below:
   - **(a) Progress-storytelling substitution.** The literal `"Scanning yourcompany.com…"` line at minute 0–15 s (line 38427, §48.8.3 step 5) MUST NOT render. The §48.8.3 step 5 sequencer reads `provider_health_state(firecrawl)` at line-render time; if `state ∈ {degraded, down}`, the line is replaced with the substitute line `"Drafting from your KB while we connect to your website…"` (literal-truth invariant preserved: the Bootstrap is proceeding with the reduced URL set; no scan claim is made). The remaining three progress lines (Found / Drafting / Ready) sequence normally against the reduced corpus. The substitution itself emits a new PostHog event `firecrawl_outage_progress_line_substituted {seller_org_id, session_id, provider_health_state, substituted_at_stage}` (Appendix G — new).
   - **(b) User-facing degradation banner.** A non-blocking yellow-warning banner renders above the Bid Workspace canvas: *"We couldn't reach yourcompany.com just now — your bid is being drafted from what you've already taught us. We'll auto-refresh if your site comes back."* The banner is dismissible. It mirrors the §48.8.3 Failure Mode #2 capability-unavailability banner pattern (precedent for non-blocking degradation surfaces).
   - **(c) Stage-3 latency budget interaction.** Stage-3 latency budget per §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold` MUST be PAUSED for the duration of the Firecrawl-retry path when `provider_health_state(firecrawl) ∈ {degraded, down}`. The `stage_3_population_latency_ms` write at line 38433 records the wall-clock total but adds a sibling column `stage_3_firecrawl_outage_pause_ms` (§4.4.22 field-table extension — see §4.4.22 V13-remediation block) so the on-call alarm is recomputed against the pause-adjusted threshold predicate. The `hero_moment_latency_breached` event (per §48.8.3 Failure Mode #3) does NOT fire under provider-outage pause.
   - **(d) `hero_moment_completed_at` predicate behavior.** The §4.4.22 predicate "all three Stage 3 surfaces are present (KB Draft + first-pass response + progress strip)" SHALL hold under Firecrawl outage IFF the KB Draft surface renders with `kb_draft_entry_count ≥ 1` from cached, pre-existing, or fallback-corpus entries. If `kb_draft_entry_count = 0` (the seller has no prior corpus AND Firecrawl is unavailable from the magic-link click), `hero_moment_completed_at` is NOT written; the session remains in Stage 3 with `capability_degradation_triggered = true` and the seller is offered a "Try again in a moment — we're reconnecting" retry CTA. The retry CTA fires only against `provider_health_state(firecrawl)` recovery; a closed-loop polling check runs at 30-second cadence for up to 15 minutes.
   - **(e) Partial-success rendering.** When Firecrawl returns successfully for a subset of requested URLs (≥ 1 page; < the full requested set), partial success is treated as success: the KB Draft surface renders the partial corpus; a footer cite in the workspace reads *"Drafted from N of M pages on yourcompany.com"* with `N`, `M` as integers; no banner; no on-call page.
   - **(f) Provider-recovery callback.** When `provider_health_state(firecrawl)` transitions back to `healthy` within 7 days of a `capability_degradation_triggered = true` SellerOnboardingSession row, the §22.X `kb_bootstrap_recovery_re_run_scheduler` (Convex cron, runs at 5-minute cadence) MAY schedule a silent re-run of `kb_bootstrap` against the cached URL list (paid via the lifetime-free allowance only if §22.X.Y Bootstrap Allowance Compensation Contract has restored it per §48.8.X — see also §48.8.X.2 below). On re-run success, a Loops.so email `firecrawl_recovery_re_bootstrap_completed` fires to the seller (see §41.2 V13-remediation block).
   - **Telemetry events (Appendix G — new).** `firecrawl_outage_degraded_kb_bootstrap {seller_org_id, session_id, firecrawl_outage_kind ∈ {provider_5xx, provider_timeout, health_detector_degraded, health_detector_down}, kb_draft_entry_count_at_emit, partial_success_count_nullable}`; `firecrawl_outage_progress_line_substituted` (see (a)); `kb_bootstrap_recovery_re_run_scheduled {seller_org_id, session_id, prior_capability_degradation_at}`; `kb_bootstrap_recovery_re_run_completed {seller_org_id, session_id, new_kb_draft_entry_count}`.
   - **Error codes (Appendix I — new).** `kb_bootstrap_firecrawl_outage_degraded` (HTTP 503, retry_after_seconds = 30); `kb_bootstrap_zero_corpus_pending_provider_recovery` (HTTP 423 Locked — the seller has no prior corpus and Firecrawl is unavailable; surfaces the retry CTA in (d)).
   - **CI gate (§M.5 — new).** `firecrawl_outage_progress_line_substitution` asserts: (i) §48.8.3 step 5 sequencer reads `provider_health_state(firecrawl)` at line-render time; (ii) the substitute progress line never renders the literal substring `"Scanning"`; (iii) the §48.8.7 #7 banned-anti-pattern detector does not fire against the substitute line; (iv) Stage-3 latency pause is recorded as `stage_3_firecrawl_outage_pause_ms`; (v) the pause-adjusted predicate satisfies §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold`. Pack assignment: M02.3.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

5. The onboarding landing page MUST render in ≤ 500 ms p95 on a 3G-throttled mobile device; CI Lighthouse test asserts.
6. Zero form fields MUST appear on the landing page before SSO initiation; a UX-snapshot test asserts (any change that adds a form field fails CI).
7. SSO → Bid Workspace loaded p90 latency MUST satisfy §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold`; breach raises `hero_moment_latency_breached` event AND pages `ops_growth_admin`. *(V13 amendment 2026-05-12: the latency budget is computed against `stage_3_population_latency_ms - stage_3_firecrawl_outage_pause_ms` per §48.8.3 Failure Mode #6(c); the `hero_moment_latency_breached` event does NOT fire under provider-outage pause; the CI gate `firecrawl_outage_progress_line_substitution` asserts the predicate.)*
8. All four progress-storytelling status lines MUST correspond to actual work in flight; no line may display before the underlying work starts; a fuzz test with contrived latency profiles asserts (no line renders > 500 ms before its work begins). *(V13 amendment 2026-05-12: per §48.8.3 Failure Mode #6(a), the line-render sequencer reads `provider_health_state(firecrawl)` at line-render time and substitutes the line per the Firecrawl-outage contract; the fuzz test extends to assert that the substitute line is exercised when the provider state is forced `degraded` or `down`.)*
9. The landing counter MUST render at first paint of the Bid Workspace AND MUST show integer counts derived from the SellerOnboardingSession row's `stage_3_*` fields (no hardcoded or aspirational numbers).
10. Capability-degradation paths MUST surface the degradation banner within 1 s of the degradation trigger AND MUST NOT leave the workspace silently empty. *(V13 amendment 2026-05-12: the Firecrawl-outage path per §48.8.3 Failure Mode #6(b) MUST render the non-blocking yellow-warning banner with the canonical copy `"We couldn't reach yourcompany.com just now — your bid is being drafted from what you've already taught us. We'll auto-refresh if your site comes back."`)*
11. On-call rotation paging on Stage-3 population latency breach MUST satisfy §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 latency breach page SLA` via the §44.3 alerting pipeline. *(V13 amendment 2026-05-12: paging is suppressed when `provider_health_state(firecrawl) ∈ {degraded, down}` is the proximate cause and the pause-adjusted latency predicate holds; the provider-degraded state itself raises a separate §42.6.0 ProviderHealthState alarm.)*
12. **Firecrawl-outage zero-corpus retry CTA. (V13 D-13V-022 remediation 2026-05-12.)** When `kb_draft_entry_count = 0` AND `provider_health_state(firecrawl) ∈ {degraded, down}` at Stage-3 boundary, the session MUST present the retry CTA per §48.8.3 Failure Mode #6(d); the CTA closed-loop polls `provider_health_state(firecrawl)` at 30-second cadence for up to 15 minutes; on recovery, the workspace auto-advances to Stage 3 with the populated KB Draft surface. QA test `firecrawl_outage_zero_corpus_retry_cta` asserts.

### 48.8.4 In-Workspace Value Proof — Minutes 3–45 {#48.8.4-in-workspace-value-proof-minutes-3-45}

**Solo / Free override (Phase 14.8 / 14.10 — see §22.20.5 and §44.6).** This section describes the AIWallet-counter rendering for paid seller tiers (`seller_starter+`). On `plan_tier ∈ {seller_free, seller_solo}` the live AIWallet budget counter, the value-price accounting line, and the cost-priced rejection counter MUST be suppressed per §22.20.5 (counter compression) and §44.6 (Solo-Tier Surface Treatment). The engine continues to write `AIOperation` rows, the cost-priced-rejected fallback per §34.10 still fires, and the §34.6 Outcome Resolver settles every operation identically — only the rendering compresses. CI gates `seller_maya_solo_free_copy_string_lint`, `solo_engine_metering_parity`, and `solo_telemetry_no_customer_routing` (§M.5) assert that the suppressed strings ("AIWallet", "AIOperation", "value_price_cents", "cost-priced rejection") never reach Solo / Free seller surfaces.

**Purpose.** From first edit through first-bid-submit, the seller reviews each pre-drafted response, edits where needed, rejects with a KB-entry-creation flow where the KB gap is real, and submits. Every interaction is instrumented as a settlement-resolution signal (§34.6) so that by the time the seller hits Submit, their KB has accreted N verified entries and their AIWallet has resolved N value-priced acceptances and M cost-priced rejections.

**Authoritative Source.** Summary §3.6 ¶3; Summary Summary §3.1b ¶3; C.132; §22.7 Citation Inline Card; §22.6 KB-Gap Detector; §34.6 Outcome Resolver.

**Trigger / Entry Condition.** `stage_3_first_edit_at` is set (seller has begun reviewing).

**Workflow.**

1. **Per-requirement draft review.** Each requirement in the bid renders with its First-Pass draft, an inline citation chip (when the draft is grounded), and three action buttons: **Accept** / **Edit** / **Reject**.
2. **Citation inline expansion.** Hover on the citation chip (*"from: yourcompany.com/trust/soc2"*) expands a §22.7 Citation Inline Card showing the exact quoted sentence from the source, a link to the source URL (opens in new tab), and a *"This isn't from my company"* report flag (triggers a `kb_citation_provenance_disputed` event — Appendix G — new — and routes to Ops for review).
3. **Accept (no-edit).** Click Accept without editing → AIOperation settles `accepted` → value price (`cost_base × 10`) charged to AIWallet if wallet has sufficient balance; else cost-priced-rejected-settlement with no charge. KB entry is promoted to `status = 'active'`. Subtle confirmation chip renders (*"added to your KB as verified response"*). `stage_4_first_kb_accept_at` written if first accept.
4. **Edit.** Click Edit → inline text editor opens with the First-Pass draft pre-populated. Seller edits; on save, the edit diff is computed; if the diff is < 50% of the original draft, the AIOperation settles `accepted` (per §34.11.1 "≥50% retained" contract); else settles `rejected`. Either way, the edited response becomes the submitted response. KB entry gets a provenance tag `source = 'first_pass_edited'`.
5. **Reject.** Click Reject → the KB-Gap Detector renders: *"No KB content answered this. Write your answer below and we'll save it as a KB entry."* Seller types the answer in a multi-line textarea. On save, a new KBEntry row is created (`source = 'q_and_a_onboarding_rejection'`, `confidence_score = 0.5` initial). `stage_4_first_kb_reject_at` written if first reject. The new KBEntry is also attached to the bid response.
6. **On-demand Q&A for empty requirements.** If a requirement has no First-Pass draft (capability degraded OR First-Pass Responder chose to skip OR seller hit a requirement after the degradation banner), an inline *"Draft with AI"* button renders. Click → `q_and_a_suggestion` capability fires on-demand; a new draft is generated in the same requirement's slot. `stage_4_first_q_and_a_suggestion_at` written if first invocation.
7. **Live AIWallet budget counter.** Top of the workspace, refresh ≤ 2 s lag on any AIWallet debit. Format: *"Free budget remaining: $[X.XX] of $5.00"*. When the counter reaches $0.00, it flips to: *"Free budget used — remaining AI drafts won't count against your bill."* (This is the value-priced-vs-cost-priced reality: cost-priced-rejected settlements don't charge anything).
8. **First requirement response submitted.** First requirement acknowledged (Accept, Edit, or Reject) AND the per-requirement state transitions to `submitted_for_bid` → `first_requirement_response_at` written. Seller Activation Metric is computed inside the same transaction per §4.4.22 Computation Rules.
9. **Whole-bid submission.** Seller reviews summary, clicks Submit → `first_bid_submitted_at` written; Bid Workspace transitions to Stage 5 Stake-Reveal.

**UX Surface Specification.**

- **Per-requirement card.** Each card stacks requirement title, requirement description, inline citation chip (if present), First-Pass draft in a read-optimized type stack, three action buttons (Accept / Edit / Reject) with tooltip hints. No upgrade banners. No pricing mentions. No "Upgrade for better citations" CTA.
- **Citation chip.** 28 px height; primary-background token; right-arrow icon on hover; expand-on-hover (tap on mobile) behavior per §3.3 pattern library.
- **KB-gap rejection editor.** Textarea field (min 4 lines, autosize); placeholder text reproduces the requirement's prompt; "Save as KB entry" button primary-action; "Cancel" secondary.
- **AIWallet counter.** Top of the workspace, 56 px right-of-title; primary-background token; transitions smoothly on debit (opacity 0.7 → 1.0 with 200 ms crossfade). NEVER use red / warning color as a pressure tactic — cost-priced-rejected model means reaching $0 is NOT a wall.
- **Requirement progress pill.** Rendered at top of workspace: *"32 of 82 reviewed — 19 accepted, 7 edited, 6 rejected"*. Updates in real time.

**Data Read / Written.** Bid Workspace (read); KBEntry (write on accept/edit/reject); AIOperation + Usage Event (write per interaction); Settlement outcome (§34.6); SellerOnboardingSession (update all `stage_4_*` timestamps). Capability Declaration (inferred / suggested from accepted KB entries at Stage 5; not at Stage 4).

**Capabilities Invoked.** `first_pass_response` (per-requirement settlement finalization); `q_and_a_suggestion` (on-demand for empty requirements); `kb_to_capability_suggestion` (background, fires at Stage 5 on first-bid-submitted). `page_enrichment` NOT fired at Stage 4; it fires at Stage 5 when Seller Profile publishes.

**AIWallet Debits.** Per-interaction settlement per §34.6; accepted interactions value-priced; rejected interactions cost-priced-rejected (the cost price `cost_base × 1.05` is debited as a platform-cost accounting entry, NOT a seller-visible charge).

**Telemetry Events.**

- `seller_onboarding_stage_entered {stage=4, ...}` (per §48.8.3 event convention)
- `aioperation.settled {capability_id, settlement_state, bid_id, seller_org_id, requirement_id}` (existing)
- `kb_entry.accepted {seller_org_id, kb_entry_id, source, confidence_score_at_creation, bid_id}` (existing)
- `kb_entry.q_and_a_onboarding_created {seller_org_id, kb_entry_id, requirement_id, bid_id}` (Appendix G — new)
- `kb_citation_provenance_disputed {seller_org_id, kb_entry_id, citation_url, requirement_id}` (Appendix G — new)
- `seller_onboarding_first_requirement_response {seller_org_id, bid_id, requirement_id, elapsed_seconds_since_arrival, response_mode ∈ {accept, edit, reject_and_kb_entry}}` (Appendix G — new) — this is THE activation-metric event
- `seller_onboarding_first_bid_submitted {seller_org_id, bid_id, total_requirements, accept_count, edit_count, reject_count, activation_metric_elapsed_seconds}` (Appendix G — new)
- `seller_aiwallet_budget_exhausted_during_onboarding {seller_org_id, bid_id, requirements_remaining_for_draft, cost_priced_rejected_cents_accumulated}` (Appendix G — new) — fires once per session if wallet hits $0

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **AIWallet balance race: two concurrent `first_pass_response` invocations both debit against remaining balance.** Per §34.10 AIWallet SERIALIZABLE balance check; second invocation settles cost-priced-rejected transparently; no double-debit.
2. **Seller disputes a citation that is actually correct.** Disputed citation is routed to Ops for review via `kb_citation_provenance_disputed`; Ops MAY (a) mark the citation verified (no further action), (b) mark the citation hallucinated and deduct the KB entry's `confidence_score` by `0.3`. Seller sees the resolution in their KB dashboard.
3. **Seller rejects 40+ drafts and never accepts any (extreme-skeptic workflow).** Session proceeds; every rejection creates a new KBEntry with `q_and_a_onboarding_rejection` source — so the seller accretes a KB via rejection instead of acceptance. Activation still achieves.
4. **Citation inline expansion fails to load source URL (404 / source-removed).** Fallback: card shows *"Source no longer available — your KB still cites the quoted sentence"* with the quoted sentence preserved. `kb_citation_source_unavailable` event (Appendix G — new) emits.
5. **Seller leaves mid-Stage-4 and returns 3 days later.** Session remains `in_progress`; Bid Workspace state persists; seller resumes; `first_requirement_response_at` has likely already been set (if first edit happened in the prior session), so Activation Metric is preserved.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

12. Every Accept / Edit / Reject click MUST write an AIOperation settlement within **500 ms** at p95; CI integration test asserts.
13. The AIWallet counter MUST refresh within **2 seconds** of any debit at p95; a visible staleness > 5 seconds raises `aiwallet_counter_freshness_breach` (Appendix G — new; internal diagnostic).
14. The KB-Gap Detector MUST render on every Reject click WITHIN the same viewport (no modal redirect); and MUST create a new KBEntry on save within **1 second** at p95.
15. On capability unavailability for `q_and_a_suggestion`, the "Draft with AI" button MUST disable AND show tooltip *"AI drafts are temporarily unavailable — try again in a few minutes"*; NEVER silent failure.
16. The `first_requirement_response_at` write path MUST compute `activation_metric_elapsed_seconds` inside the same transaction; Property test asserts monotonicity (`first_requirement_response_at > stage_1_arrival_at`) across 10,000 randomized timelines.
17. The AIWallet exhaustion path MUST continue drafting in cost-priced-rejected mode AND MUST NEVER hard-block the seller mid-Hero-Moment; an integration test with a zeroed-balance Seller Wallet asserts that all remaining drafts render.
18. The requirement-progress pill MUST reflect the current SellerOnboardingSession state within **2 seconds** of any per-requirement interaction.

### 48.8.5 Post-Submission Reveal — Hour 1+ {#48.8.5-post-submission-reveal-hour-1}

**Solo / Free override (Phase 14.8 — see §22.20.5 and §22.20.6).** The Stake-Reveal Screen is rendered on Solo and Free with a non-monetary stake summary per §22.20.6 — copy reframed in qualitative ("KB entries verified", "responses pre-drafted") rather than monetary ("value-price acceptances", "cost-priced rejections", "AIWallet credit balance") terms. The engine-side `SellerOnboardingSession` writes (`stake_reveal_at`, `first_bid_submitted_at`) and the §34.6 Outcome Resolver settlement counters fire identically across all tiers; only the rendering compresses. CI gate `seller_maya_solo_free_copy_string_lint` (§M.5) asserts the monetary copy strings never reach Solo / Free seller surfaces.

**Purpose.** Immediately after first-bid-submission, the seller lands on the Stake-Reveal Screen — an explicit, non-upgrade-CTA reminder of what the seller just built, what it would have cost to do elsewhere, and how it compounds. This is the second-most-important product surface in the Seller Console (after the Hero Moment itself) because it is where the vendor first perceives Sourcera as an asset (their KB) rather than a workflow tool. Upgrade conversations do NOT happen here — they happen at the four Seller Conversion Moments (§48.1.7, §48.8.6).

**Authoritative Source.** Summary §3.6 ¶4; Summary Summary §3.1b ¶3 (stake-reveal copy); C.132 stake-reveal; §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stake-Reveal dwell target` carrying forward the C.135 dwell target; Summary §6.28.2 Stage 5.

**Trigger / Entry Condition.** `first_bid_submitted_at` is written on the SellerOnboardingSession row.

**Workflow.**

1. **Immediate Stake-Reveal render.** On bid-submit confirmation, the Bid Workspace transitions to the Stake-Reveal Screen. `stage_5_stake_reveal_rendered_at` written.
2. **Primary copy render.** *"You just built a reusable KB of **[N]** verified entries in **[X]** minutes. Your next bid will reuse them automatically."* Where N = count of KBEntries with `source IN {bootstrap_accepted, first_pass_edited, q_and_a_onboarding_rejection}` created during the session, X = `activation_metric_elapsed_seconds / 60`. Rendered at H1 size.
3. **Value-price accounting.** Secondary line: *"Sourcera tracked **$[Y.YY]** of value pricing for the AI work on this bid (covered by your Free plan)."* Where Y = sum of value-priced-accepted AIOperation settlement amounts in the session (cost_base × 10 per accept). This is NOT framed as *"you saved $Y"* or *"worth $Y elsewhere"*; it is an honest accounting line.
4. **Published Seller Profile link.** *"Your profile is live: **sourcera.com/sellers/[your-org-slug]**"* — `stage_5_profile_url_rendered` written. Click opens the published Seller Profile in a new tab.
5. **Seller Signals opt-in.** Below the primary copy: a checkbox *"Share anonymized win/loss signals to improve Match Scoring. You can change this anytime in Settings."* Default: unchecked (opt-in). On check: `stage_5_seller_signals_opt_in` = true, `stage_5_seller_signals_opt_in_at` written.
6. **Secondary content: KB freshness reminder.** Below the opt-in: *"Your KB will stay fresh automatically as long as you submit at least one bid per 90 days."* No upgrade CTA. No "Upgrade to Starter for auto-crawls" link. (Note: the Win/Loss Debrief at bid-close IS an upgrade trigger per C.137 — but the Stake-Reveal Screen is NOT.)
7. **Dwell measurement.** On navigate-away from the Stake-Reveal Screen: `stage_5_dwell_seconds` written (seconds elapsed from render to navigate-away). Target sourced from §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stake-Reveal dwell target`.

**UX Surface Specification.**

- **Page layout.** Single centered column (720 px max width on desktop); 96 px vertical rhythm. Primary copy at H1 display-lg token; accounting line at body-lg token; profile link at body-md with code-treated slug; opt-in at body-md with 16 × 16 checkbox.
- **No upgrade CTAs of any kind.** This is the hardest constraint on the screen. No *"Upgrade to Starter"* button, no *"See all features"* link, no pricing page crosslink, no *"Your KB can grow to 1,000 entries on Starter"* banner. A QA snapshot test asserts zero upgrade-tagged elements render on this screen; CI fails on any addition.
- **Single exit action.** Primary button: *"Back to your workspace"* or *"View your Seller Profile"* (depending on cohort). Secondary text link: *"Settings"* (minor visual weight). No other exits.

**Data Read / Written.** SellerOnboardingSession (`stage_5_*` fields write); Seller Profile (read for URL); KBEntry (read for count); AIOperation settlement aggregates (read for value-price total); Seller Signals consent (write on opt-in).

**Capabilities Invoked.** None at Stage 5 directly. `page_enrichment` may fire asynchronously (triggered at Seller Profile publication) if the profile was just enriched.

**AIWallet Debits.** None (Stage 5 is UX only).

**Telemetry Events.**

- `seller_onboarding_stage_entered {stage=5, ...}`
- `stake_reveal_rendered {seller_org_id, bid_id, kb_entry_count_on_reveal, value_price_total_cents, published_profile_url}` (Appendix G — new)
- `stake_reveal_navigated_away {seller_org_id, bid_id, dwell_seconds, exit_action ∈ {back_to_workspace, view_profile, settings, browser_close}}` (Appendix G — new)
- `seller_signals_opt_in {seller_org_id, opt_in_at, source_surface='stake_reveal'}` (Appendix G — new)

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Published Seller Profile URL not yet indexed.** Link still renders; the screen does not wait for indexing; the profile is viewable at the URL even pre-indexing.
2. **KBEntry count discrepancy (race between Stage-4 writes and Stage-5 render).** Render uses a read-at-transaction-boundary snapshot; if the snapshot miscount is > 1, a backfill event re-renders the count within 2 s.
3. **Seller immediately closes browser (dwell = 0 s).** Dwell event still emits with `dwell_seconds = 0`; the Stage-5 dwell leading indicator absorbs this datapoint.
4. **Seller opts into Seller Signals then immediately revokes.** Consent is retained with a `revoked_at` timestamp (Summary §6.17 Seller Signals consent lifecycle); funnel analytics reflect the net-out consent state.
5. **Seller navigates directly to Settings from Stake-Reveal without any other click.** Dwell captured; Settings audit-logs the referring surface for UX analysis.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

19. The Stake-Reveal Screen MUST render within **500 ms** of bid-submit confirmation at p95.
20. Zero upgrade CTAs of any form MUST appear on the Stake-Reveal Screen; a UX-fixture-snapshot test asserts (any CTA-tagged element added fails CI).
21. `stage_5_dwell_seconds` MUST satisfy §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stake-Reveal dwell target`.
22. Published Seller Profile URL MUST be included verbatim in the Stake-Reveal copy; URL shape matches `sourcera.com/sellers/[slug]` pattern exactly; slug matches the Seller Org's `seller_org_slug` field (§4.4.6).
23. Seller Signals opt-in MUST default to unchecked (opt-in, not opt-out); a UX-fixture test asserts.

### 48.8.6 Four Seller Conversion Moments — UX Surface Specification {#48.8.6-three-conversion-moments-ux-surface-specification}

**Purpose.** §48.1.7 fixes the four Seller Conversion Moments' triggers, CTAs, telemetry, and plan mappings definitively. §48.8.6 spells out the UX surface, timing, frequency controls, and anti-pattern prevention for each moment. The binding is: §48.1.7 is the what; §48.8.6 is the how.

**Authoritative Source.** SPS v3 §15.3 (four Seller conversion moments); Summary Summary §3.1b ¶4 / C.133 (pre-Solo baseline); §48.1.7 (Master Spec Binding). All four moments use the Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee (C.139) as the dominant message on the upgrade screen.

**Common UX Constraints (Apply to All Four Moments).**

- The upgrade prompt MUST be a single-modal inline surface (not a page redirect); the modal has a clear close affordance (X icon top-right AND ESC key) per §3.3.x modal pattern.
- Upon close, the seller returns to exactly where they were (no state loss, no auto-navigation to pricing page).
- The prompt MUST render the Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee verbatim copy per §48.1.7.
- No hidden costs, no fake urgency ("Only 3 days left!"), no dark-pattern countdown timers, no pre-filled credit card information, no auto-check "I agree to auto-renew" boxes.
- The Stripe Checkout flow launched from the upgrade CTA MUST complete in ≤ 3 user-facing screens per §15 Stripe Checkout.
- On upgrade success: the original triggering action completes (e.g., the second concurrent bid opens, the EOI submits, the KB entry saves) WITHOUT the seller having to re-do it.

**Conversion Moment #1 — Mid-bid AI Budget Wall.**

| Element | Specification |
| :---- | :---- |
| Trigger UX | The active Bid Workspace preserves the draft and renders an inline recovery rail at the top of the response composer when `seller_aiwallet_budget_exhausted_during_onboarding` fires for Seller Free during active bid work. The response is paused, not discarded. |
| Modal copy (verbatim) | *"**Your bid response is paused — Sourcera Free's AI budget is exhausted.** Solo unlocks the engine-absorbed envelope (no hard cap, no mid-bid walls) for $49/mo or $199/bid."* |
| Modal body | Three-line benefit list: *"No mid-bid AI budget wall"* / *"250-entry KB (up from 50)"* / *"Verified-tier eligibility"*. Followed by the Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee summary (verbatim per §48.1.7 / C.139). Price display resolves monthly, annual, and per-bid Seller Solo pricing from §34.2.2; static price literals outside the authoritative copy are forbidden. |
| Primary CTA | *"Upgrade to Solo and resume this bid →"* (opens Stripe Checkout) |
| Secondary action | *"Keep drafting manually"* (closes modal; AI-assisted response generation remains unavailable until wallet remediation or plan upgrade, but manually-entered draft text remains editable) |
| Frequency cap | Fires at most once per `(Seller Org, mid_bid_ai_budget_wall, seller_free)` tuple (§48.1.7 frequency cap) |
| Post-upgrade success | The paused response composer resumes; the draft text and requirement cursor are preserved; Seller Solo envelope semantics apply from the successful checkout forward |

**Conversion Moment #2 — Second Concurrent Bid.**

| Element | Specification |
| :---- | :---- |
| Trigger UX | Bid inbox renders the incoming second bid invitation card AS NORMAL (do NOT hide it behind the upgrade prompt — seller should always see what they'd be getting). An overlay banner appears at the top of the inbox: *"Your first bid is still in flight. Starter lets you work on both at once."* Click → upgrade modal. |
| Modal copy (verbatim) | *"**Don't let your second deal slip.** Starter unlocks 3 concurrent bids and keeps your KB shared across all of them. Your in-flight bid stays exactly as it is — no re-bootstrap, no lost work."* |
| Modal body | Three-line benefit list: *"3 concurrent bids"* / *"1,000-entry KB (up from 50)"* / *"10 outbound EOIs per month"*. Followed by the Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee summary (verbatim per §48.1.7 / C.139). Price display resolves monthly and annual Seller Starter pricing from §34.2.2; no inline price restatement is permitted in this modal copy. |
| Primary CTA | *"Upgrade to Starter →"* (opens Stripe Checkout) |
| Secondary action | *"Not now — work on one bid at a time"* (closes modal; seller continues) |
| Frequency cap | Fires at most once per `(Seller Org, second_concurrent_bid, seller_free)` tuple (§48.1.7 mutual-exclusivity + frequency cap) |
| Post-upgrade success | Both bids open; both use the same KB; both draw from the upgraded AIWallet allowance |

**Conversion Moment #3 — First EOI Attempt.**

| Element | Specification |
| :---- | :---- |
| Trigger UX | Seller clicks "Submit EOI" on a Marketplace listing. Instead of submitting immediately (since Free can't), the upgrade modal renders in-line. (Do NOT redirect to a pricing page — that violates §48.8.7 #4.) |
| Modal copy (verbatim) | *"**Outbound EOIs start at Starter.** Your first **10 EOIs / month** are included. Marketplace listings showed your profile to **[N]** buyers this week — Starter lets you reach back."* (N = `seller_profile.view_count` over prior 7 days; fallback *"buyers searching your category"* if N not available) |
| Modal body | Three-line benefit list (all Starter-eligible per §34.1.2): *"10 outbound EOIs / month"* / *"Shared KB across all bids"* / *"Monthly Seller Signals digest"*. Followed by Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee summary. |
| Primary CTA | *"Upgrade and submit this EOI →"* (opens Stripe Checkout; on success, EOI submits) |
| Secondary action | *"Save this EOI for later"* (EOI goes into a drafts queue for future submission if seller upgrades later; emits `eoi_saved_as_draft_for_future_upgrade`) |
| Frequency cap | Fires at most once per `(Seller Org, first_eoi_attempt, seller_free)` tuple |
| Post-upgrade success | EOI submitted; seller sees confirmation; remaining EOI quota displayed |

**Conversion Moment #4 — KB Ceiling Approach.**

| Element | Specification |
| :---- | :---- |
| Trigger UX | An inline banner renders at the top of the KB workspace when the seller crosses the plan-relative approach threshold: 45 of 50 entries on Seller Free or 225 of 250 entries on Seller Solo. The triggering KB-write completes normally (anti-pattern: do NOT block the write; that would violate §48.8.7 #2). |
| Modal copy (verbatim) | Free variant: *"**Your KB is about to hit the Free ceiling (50 entries).** Solo raises it to **250 entries** and keeps your existing work."* Solo variant: *"**Your KB is about to hit the Solo ceiling (250 entries).** Starter raises it to **1,000 entries** and keeps your existing work."* Both variants append the Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee summary. |
| Modal body | Free variant benefit list: *"250-entry KB"* / *"Weekly Firecrawl source"* / *"Verified-tier eligibility"*. Solo variant benefit list: *"1,000-entry KB"* / *"Weekly Firecrawl auto-refresh"* / *"3 concurrent bids"*. Plus the **Carry-Over Guarantee** heading at 1.5× body-lg size and verbatim paragraph per §48.1.7. |
| Primary CTA | Free variant: *"Upgrade to Solo →"*; Solo variant: *"Upgrade to Starter →"* |
| Secondary action | *"Not now — keep writing"* (closes modal; seller continues; if the seller crosses the plan-relative hard ceiling, a NEW banner asks them to archive an entry or upgrade rather than deleting existing work) |
| Frequency cap | Fires at most once per `(Seller Org, kb_ceiling_approach, plan_tier)` tuple. A second banner (no modal) renders at the hard ceiling crossing: 50 entries for Seller Free or 250 entries for Seller Solo. This hard-ceiling banner is explicitly a soft-block UX, NOT a second Conversion Moment fire; it does NOT re-emit `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_fired`, does NOT re-open the upgrade modal automatically, and does NOT consume a new `stage_7_conversion_moment_triggered_at` slot. The banner emits `seller_kb_ceiling_reached {seller_org_id, plan_tier, current_kb_entry_count, triggering_entry_id, prior_cm4_fired_at}` (Appendix G) for diagnostic tracking, and presents two affordances: (a) *"Archive an entry"* and (b) Free: *"Upgrade to Solo"* / Solo: *"Upgrade to Starter"*. |
| Post-upgrade success | KB ceiling raises to the target tier's limit; all existing entries remain intact with all metadata; the triggering KB-write is preserved |

**Telemetry Events.** Per §48.1.7 table (trigger and click events already specified there), plus:

- `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_modal_closed {seller_org_id, kind, close_action ∈ {x_icon, esc_key, secondary_cta, stripe_checkout_abandoned}}` (Appendix G — new)
- `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_upgrade_succeeded {seller_org_id, kind, stripe_checkout_session_id, elapsed_seconds_from_trigger_to_upgrade}` (Appendix G — new)
- `seller_kb_ceiling_reached {seller_org_id, plan_tier, current_kb_entry_count, triggering_entry_id, prior_cm4_fired_at}` (Appendix G) — CM4 hard-ceiling secondary banner; soft-block UX only, not a second Conversion Moment fire (see CM4 Frequency-cap row above)

**Acceptance Criteria.**

24. Each of the four Seller Conversion Moment upgrade modals MUST render the Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee verbatim; copy-drift fails the UX-fixture-snapshot CI test.
25. The modal MUST have both X-icon and ESC close affordances; keyboard-navigation test asserts.
26. Closing the modal MUST NOT navigate the seller away from their current workspace; state-preservation test asserts.
27. On Stripe-Checkout-success, the original triggering action (paused bid response / second-bid-open / EOI-submit / KB-write) MUST complete WITHOUT requiring the seller to retry; integration test asserts.
28. The Conversion Moment modal MUST NEVER redirect to an external pricing page; a navigation-observer test asserts.
29. Each Conversion Moment's fire-once-per-`(seller_org_id, moment_kind, plan_tier)` invariant MUST be enforced per §48.1.8 AC 14.
30. **CM3 profile-view-count cohort snapshot tests (two cohorts).** The CM3 First EOI modal dynamic copy — *"Marketplace listings showed your profile to **[N]** buyers this week"* (published profile) vs. *"Marketplace listings put your profile in front of **buyers searching your category**"* (unpublished profile) — MUST be covered by two UX-fixture snapshot tests: **Cohort A** (seller with `seller_profile.published = true` AND `seller_profile.view_count_7d ≥ 1`): asserts the modal renders the numeric N, renders the exact copy *"showed your profile to **N** buyers this week"*, and the numeric is the `view_count_7d` value at trigger time (not a cached older value, freshness ≤ 60s lag per §48.1.6). **Cohort B** (seller with `seller_profile.published = false` OR `view_count_7d = 0` OR `view_count_7d IS NULL`): asserts the modal renders the fallback copy verbatim *"put your profile in front of **buyers searching your category**"* with NO numeric substitution, NO "showed your profile" phrase, and no layout collapse from the missing figure. Both fixtures are independently asserted per PR; copy drift in either cohort fails CI. Edge case (CM3-Cohort-Boundary): a seller whose profile published less than 7 days ago falls into Cohort B — the 7-day window is the denominator, not the publication age.
31. **CM4 plan-relative hard-ceiling soft-block banner and event.** The hard-ceiling secondary banner (§48.8.6 CM4 Frequency-cap row) MUST render without re-firing `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_fired`, MUST emit `seller_kb_ceiling_reached` within 2 seconds of the plan-relative hard-ceiling KB-write (50th entry on Seller Free; 250th entry on Seller Solo), AND MUST present both "Archive an entry" and the plan-correct upgrade affordance ("Upgrade to Solo" for Free; "Upgrade to Starter" for Solo); a UX-fixture snapshot test asserts. Attempting to write the next over-ceiling entry MUST continue to follow §34.6 downgrade-safe / cap-preservation behavior without deleting existing entries; the banner remains persistently rendered until the seller archives, upgrades, or dismisses (dismissal is session-scoped; banner re-renders on next session per §22 KB workspace render contract).

### 48.8.7 Six Banned Anti-Patterns — Hard Requirements {#48.8.7-six-banned-anti-patterns-hard-requirements}

**Authoring intent.** §48.8.7 codifies the six onboarding anti-patterns named in Summary §3.6 ¶ "Onboarding anti-patterns (banned)" and the extended list from C.141. Each anti-pattern is a HARD requirement — a QA-testable ban with a detector, a failure consequence, and an acceptance criterion. CI gates merge if any detector's unit or integration test is missing or skipped. Deviation requires a written exception approved by the Ops Council per §47 Governance; the exception audit-logs to an `onboarding_anti_pattern_exception_grant` record (Appendix J `anti_pattern_violation_kind` — new).

**Source authority.** Summary §3.6 six anti-patterns (verbatim); C.141 extended list (onboarding-surface + UX anti-patterns); §47 Governance (Ops Council exception process).

**The Six Banned Anti-Patterns (Each Is a Hard Requirement).**

| # | Anti-Pattern (Banned Behavior) | Why Banned (Rationale) | Detector | Test Path | Failure Consequence on Detection | Enforcement Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **AP1** | **Credit card requested at any point before the first upgrade-intent click** | Gates the Hero Moment behind friction; poisons the *"zero cost, zero friction to try"* promise. Summary §3.6 ¶5a; C.141. | Detector: no HTTP endpoint that accepts credit card data (Stripe token, PAN, etc.) SHALL be callable from any onboarding surface (Stages 1–6). Detector implements as (a) a UX-fixture snapshot test asserting zero `cc-input` elements render on any Stages 1–6 surface, (b) an API-surface test asserting the Stripe Checkout endpoint is not reachable from any onboarding deep-link, (c) a full-cohort audit asserting zero Stripe `payment_method.created` events correlate to sessions where `stage_7_upgrade_cta_clicked_at IS NULL` | CI integration test (per-PR), weekly audit sweep | HTTP 400 `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation_ap1` (Appendix I — new); P1 PagerDuty to `ops_growth_admin` if detected in production | P0 |
| **AP2** | **Upgrade offer presented during active bid work** | Interrupts the Hero Moment; breaks trust. Summary §3.6 ¶5f; C.141. | Detector: upgrade-offer modals SHALL NOT render while the seller has any Bid Workspace in Stage-4 state (`bid_workspace.status IN {populating, drafting, reviewing, editing}`) unless the trigger matches one of the four explicit Conversion Moments per §48.8.6. Whitelisted exceptions: #1 mid-bid AI budget wall — fires only after the Seller Free wallet would otherwise hard-cap an active response and preserves draft state; #2 second concurrent bid — fires on NEW bid arrival; #3 first EOI — fires on explicit seller action outside active bid; #4 KB ceiling — fires on the seller's own KB-write action and is the active-work-during-KB-write whitelist. Detector: a middleware on the upgrade-modal-render path checks the active-bid-Stage-4 state AND rejects render unless the trigger matches one of the four whitelisted moments with the plan-correct trigger conditions. | CI middleware unit test; full-cohort audit weekly | HTTP 409 `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation_ap2` returned at render attempt; P2 alert | P0 |
| **AP3** | **Dark-pattern upgrade CTAs (roach motels, hard-to-find downgrade, fake urgency)** | Dark patterns violate trust and weaponize the Seller Pricing thesis into adversarial tactics. Summary §3.6 ¶5e; C.141. | Detector: (a) every Stripe subscription MUST have a *"Downgrade / Cancel"* action accessible from the Seller Console account settings within 2 clicks AND no modal (a UX-pathway test asserts); (b) no fake-urgency copy (*"Only 3 days left"*, *"Limited time offer"*, countdown timers) SHALL render on any upgrade surface — a lint rule on copy strings scans for the banned phrases and flags; (c) pre-checked auto-renew checkboxes are banned — a UX-fixture test asserts default-unchecked | Pre-commit copy lint + UX-fixture tests | Merge blocker on lint flag; HTTP 400 `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation_ap3` on runtime detection | P0 |
| **AP4** | **Upgrade-intent redirect to external pricing page during onboarding flow** | Breaks the in-context upgrade experience; seller loses state, trust, and the Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee context. Summary §3.6 ¶5d; C.141. | Detector: upgrade CTAs in Stages 1–7 SHALL render inline modals, NOT page redirects. A navigation-observer test asserts that clicking any upgrade CTA from Stages 1–7 does NOT invoke `window.location.assign` or `window.location.replace` or `<a href="/pricing">`. The modal MUST carry the upgrade copy + Stripe Checkout handoff within its own surface | CI navigation-observer test | Merge blocker if test fails; HTTP 400 `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation_ap4` on runtime detection | P0 |
| **AP5** | **Requiring vendor to describe company / industry / role before Bootstrap runs** | Adds friction before the Hero Moment; violates the zero-form onboarding commitment. Summary §3.6 ¶5b; C.141. | Detector: the Stage-1 landing page and Stage-2 SSO flow SHALL have zero form fields beyond SSO / magic-link. A UX-fixture snapshot test enumerates every DOM element matching `input`, `select`, `textarea` on Stages 1–2 surfaces; count MUST equal the SSO / magic-link set (provider email address at SSO provider side; 0 Sourcera-owned fields). Additionally, the first 3 minutes of post-SSO MUST not surface any "Tell us about your company" modals — a mid-session prompt test asserts | CI UX-fixture test + mid-session integration test | Merge blocker if form fields appear; P1 alert if runtime-detected | P0 |
| **AP6** | **Pricing page shown before the vendor submits their first bid** | Sales-forward posture kills the stake-building thesis; pricing conversations occur only at natural completion points or ceilings. Summary §3.6 ¶5c; C.141. | Detector: the in-app pricing page (the `/account/pricing` route AND any upgrade-intent deep-link) MUST be gated by a feature-flag-style check: `if (SellerOnboardingSession.first_bid_submitted_at IS NULL) { redirect to workspace }`. A full-cohort audit asserts zero pricing-page GET events correlate to sessions where `first_bid_submitted_at IS NULL`. Secondary CTA flows (e.g., a navigation sidebar link) MUST hide pricing page entries for sessions in this state | CI integration test + weekly cohort audit | HTTP 302 redirect to workspace on gated GET; P2 alert on cohort anomaly | P1 |

**Additional Banned Behaviors (Extended from C.141 — Non-Exhaustive).**

These are QA-testable bans that extend the six core anti-patterns; violations are P2 alerts (vs. P0/P1 for AP1–AP6).

| # | Banned Behavior | Detector |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| AP7 | Fake progress-storytelling (status line shows work that isn't happening) | Fuzz-test on progress-line render: no line may render > 500 ms before the corresponding backend job starts. Per §48.8.3 AC 8. |
| AP8 | Tour modal blocking the Bid Workspace | UX-fixture test: any modal with `data-tour` attribute on Stages 3–4 surfaces fails CI. |
| AP9 | Requiring workspace naming before first bid work | UX-fixture test: the Bid Workspace MUST render without a "Name your workspace" prompt on first load. |
| AP10 | Requiring manual Capability Declaration authoring on the onboarding path | Per C.140: Capability Declarations are auto-suggested by `kb_to_capability_suggestion`; manual authoring UI is post-Stage-5 only. |
| AP11 | Manual profile-publish confirmation requirement | Publication is default on domain verification (Summary C.141); a test asserts the profile publishes automatically at Stage 5 without a confirm-click. |

**AP6 Priority Re-Evaluation (Authored Extension — Ops Council Review Required).** AP6 is initially classified P1 while AP1–AP5 are P0. The rationale parity between AP6 (pricing-page-before-first-bid) and AP1–AP5 (zero-form, zero-CC, zero-redirect, zero-dark-pattern, zero-required-declaration) is strong: a pricing page shown prematurely is functionally equivalent to the AP4 redirect-to-pricing-page violation in its Hero-Moment-poisoning effect, and the `/account/pricing` GET is a far more discoverable leak surface than the in-flow modal paths that AP1–AP5 guard. Ops Council MUST review the AP6 P1 classification within the first 30 days of v7.0.0 production use and either (a) elevate AP6 to P0 (matching AP1–AP5, requiring runtime HTTP 302 + immediate PagerDuty, not a P2 cohort anomaly alert), or (b) author a written finding documenting why the weaker priority is defensible. Until the review completes, the weekly cohort audit detector remains authoritative. This re-evaluation is audit-logged to `onboarding_anti_pattern_priority_reevaluation` (Authored Extension — Ops Council workflow row; Appendix J `anti_pattern_priority_reevaluation_status ∈ {pending_review, elevated_to_p0, retained_at_p1, deferred}` — new).

**Exception Process.** Any deviation from AP1–AP6 OR AP7–AP11 requires a formal Ops Council exception per §47 Governance. Exception request: (a) Ops Council proposal with rationale, (b) engineering impact estimate, (c) PLG-impact estimate per §48.1.6 (activation metric regression), (d) written dissent log. Approved exceptions are time-bounded (max 90 days, enforced as a write-path invariant per §4.6.x `onboarding_anti_pattern_exception_grant` schema below) and audit-logged to `onboarding_anti_pattern_exception_grant` (Appendix J enum `anti_pattern_exception_status` — new).
