### 48.8.9 Failure Modes Addressed (Aggregate Counterfactual Pass) {#48.8.9-failure-modes-addressed}

Per the §48 counterfactual-pass requirement (≥ 3 realistic failure modes per new feature), §48.8 handles:

1. **Dependency outage: Firecrawl down during Stage 2.** Graceful degradation per §48.8.3 **Failure Mode #6** (V13 D-13V-022 remediation 2026-05-12; the prior cross-reference to §48.8.3 Failure Mode #2 was incorrect — that FM is First-Pass-Responder-specific). Behavior summary: progress-storytelling line substituted from `"Scanning yourcompany.com…"` to `"Drafting from your KB while we connect to your website…"`; non-blocking yellow-warning banner renders; Stage-3 latency budget paused via `stage_3_firecrawl_outage_pause_ms`; `hero_moment_completed_at` written iff `kb_draft_entry_count ≥ 1` from cached/prior/fallback corpus, else retry CTA surfaces; partial-success rendering when subset of URLs succeed; provider-recovery callback re-schedules Bootstrap silently within 7 days and emits `kb_bootstrap_recovery_re_run_completed` + Loops.so `firecrawl_recovery_re_bootstrap_completed`. `capability_degradation_triggered = true`; on-call paged via the §42.6.0 ProviderHealthState alarm, NOT via Stage-3-latency-breach alarm.
2. **Capability unavailability: First-Pass Responder offline.** Graceful degradation per C.140; KB-Draft-only mode; banner surfaces retry; session proceeds to Stage 4 without the draft layer; seller can still write responses from their KB manually.
3. **Adversarial input: seller pastes malicious URL into a rejected-KB-entry body.** Write path applies the same XSS + URL-safety filter as all KBEntry writes (§22.x); no special onboarding path.
4. **Concurrency: two seller users from the same Org arrive via separate magic-links at the same moment.** Two SellerOnboardingSession rows are created; the second arrival resolves to the existing Seller Org via SSO; both sessions run in parallel without interfering.
5. **Time-zone edge: seller in APAC region arrives when US-region backend is mid-deploy.** Session write path is region-partitioned; APAC seller's writes route to APAC Convex deployment; no cross-region stall.
6. **Abandonment: seller starts Stage 2, closes browser, returns 3 weeks later.** Session row remains `in_progress` until the 7-day abandon sweeper fires; on return post-sweep, the seller can re-start a new session via a fresh magic-link (if still valid) or fresh signup.
7. **Retry: Stripe Checkout fails after seller clicks upgrade CTA.** Seller returns to the upgrade modal with a *"Payment didn't go through — try again or use a different card"* inline message; original triggering action remains queued.
8. **Data residency collision: seller's browser IP is EU but their invite was generated by a US-region Buyer Org.** Session-write routes to EU Convex deployment per the EU-IP cohort rule (§40.x); cross-region session data is reconciled via the cross-region audit pipeline (§40.x).
9. **Notification failure: stake-reveal email (if any) fails delivery.** Stake-reveal is primarily in-app; no email dependency for the screen itself; the Win/Loss Debrief email (§48.7 / C.137) has its own DLQ path.
10. **Buyer-seller firewall leak risk: buyer-side dashboard attempts to show seller activation analytics.** Per §48.1.8 AC 18: HTTP 404 on any cross-console read; audit entry; k-anonymity floor k=5 for allowed aggregate rollups.
11. **Downgrade path: seller upgrades via Conversion Moment #1 then downgrades within the trial window.** Per §48.1.7 / C.139: data preserved in read-only state for 90 days; Seller Activation Metric is not re-computed on downgrade.
12. **Admin-vs-end-user: Seller Org admin wants to force onboarding completion for a colleague.** Not possible — session rows are per-user; colleague must complete their own session.
13. **Mobile-vs-desktop divergence: seller opens magic-link on iOS Safari.** Per §7.x mobile support: onboarding surfaces are responsive; progress storytelling reflows; Stake-Reveal Screen reflows. Per-mobile Lighthouse test asserts interactive-ready ≤ 2 s on 3G.
14. **Locale: seller's browser locale is `fr-FR`.** Onboarding copy is localized per §42.x; currency displayed per locale; progress storytelling lines are localized; Stake-Reveal *"value pricing"* amount is currency-appropriate.

### 48.8.10 Acceptance Criteria (§48.8 Aggregate) {#48.8.10-acceptance-criteria-aggregate}

The complete acceptance-criteria roll-up for §48.8. Items 1–29 are authored in the per-subsection acceptance-criteria blocks above (§48.8.2 – §48.8.6). Items below (30–40) are §48.8-aggregate criteria that span the entire Hero Moment surface.

30. The Hero Moment p50 `activation_metric_elapsed_seconds` MUST satisfy §44.1 `Seller Activation Metric p50 target` on the trailing 30-day rolling window for **all six canonical `invite_source` cohorts** per Appendix J `seller_onboarding_invite_source` enum (`buyer_invite`, `ghost_bid_conversion`, `pro_trial_seat_m17`, `direct_signup`, `marketplace_search`, `buyer_referral_m16`); regression > 10% against the §44.1 target on any individual cohort raises a §42 P2 to `ops_growth_admin`. (V5 D-5V-003 remediation 2026-05-06: prior three-cohort scope expanded to all six canonical values to close the silent-cohort-exclusion gap on the S6 `marketplace_search` and M16 `buyer_referral_m16` growth loops.) Cohort-level p50 breakdown rendered on the §42 Seller Activation Dashboard with per-cohort SLO assertion. Deploy-time validator `seller_activation_cohort_canonical_enum` (Appendix M.5) asserts every cohort enumeration in §48.8.10 / §48.8.8 / §49.1.1 / §42 dashboard surfaces matches the canonical six-value Appendix J enum exactly.
31. The Hero Moment p90 `activation_metric_elapsed_seconds` MUST satisfy §44.1 `Seller Activation Metric p90 target` on the trailing 30-day rolling window for **all six canonical `invite_source` cohorts** per Appendix J `seller_onboarding_invite_source`; regression > 10% against the §44.1 target on any individual cohort raises a §42 P2. (V5 D-5V-003 remediation 2026-05-06.)
32. The Stage-3 population-latency p90 MUST satisfy §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold` on a rolling 15-minute window; breach pages on-call per §4.4.22 AC 4 and §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 latency breach page SLA`.
33. KB-Bootstrap acceptance rate (≥ 40 approved entries on the hero path — Indicator #3 in §48.1.6) MUST be ≥ 60% on the trailing 30-day rolling window; regression below 50% raises a P3.
34. Rejected-op rate for First-Pass Responder (Q1 in §48.1.6) MUST be < 30% trailing 30 days; regression > 35% raises a P3 AND triggers a §34.7 capability-quality review.
35. The six AP1–AP6 detectors MUST be CI-gated per §48.8.7; any missing or skipped detector test fails the CI gate.
36. All AP1–AP11 violations MUST be logged as `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation` events with `kind ∈ {ap1, ap2, …, ap11}` (Appendix G — new) AND reviewed at the weekly Ops Council meeting; sustained > 0 violations per week trigger a formal Governance review per §47.
37. The Seller Activation Dashboard, Forced-Signup Funnel Dashboard, and Seller Plan Progression Dashboard MUST refresh per their specified cadences (real-time / daily / monthly) with dashboard-freshness monitoring; staleness > specified threshold raises a P3.
38. Every Hero Moment phase's TelemetryEvents MUST be PostHog-Insights-Funnels queryable end-to-end keyed by `seller_org_id`; the full funnel from `stage_1_arrival_at` to `stake_reveal_rendered` MUST resolve at p95 ≤ 30 seconds across the full active session population.
39. Per-`invite_source` cohort breakdowns MUST be queryable on every §48.8 dashboard for **all six canonical Appendix J `seller_onboarding_invite_source` values** (`buyer_invite`, `ghost_bid_conversion`, `pro_trial_seat_m17`, `direct_signup`, `marketplace_search`, `buyer_referral_m16`); query-performance p95 ≤ 30 seconds per cohort. (V5 D-5V-003 remediation 2026-05-06: prior four-cohort enumeration expanded to all six canonical values; deploy-time validator `seller_activation_cohort_canonical_enum` Appendix M.5 enforces.)
40. Cross-console firewall enforcement per §48.1.8 AC 18 MUST return HTTP 404 on any buyer-console-originated read of SellerOnboardingSession-derived analytics; a property test asserts 100% enforcement across 10,000 simulated cross-console query attempts.

42. **Plan-tier × invite-source cohort breakdown for activation metric. (V13 D-HM-009 remediation 2026-05-12.)** ACs #30 and #31 MUST additionally compute the activation metric across a `plan_tier × invite_source` cross-product cohort matrix (6 plan_tier values × 6 invite_source values = 36 cells). Solo / Free seller cohorts under §44.6 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment throttling MUST be assigned a RELAXED SLO that reflects the engine-side throttle: `seller_solo` cohort p50 ≤ 25 minutes (versus the paid-tier ≤ 20 min in AC #30), p90 ≤ 75 minutes (versus paid-tier ≤ 60 min); `seller_free` cohort: same relaxed bands as `seller_solo`. The relaxation is registered with a §44.6.4.X "Throttled-Tier Hero Moment SLO" cross-reference. Regression > 10% on any (plan_tier, invite_source) cell raises a §42 P2 to `ops_growth_admin`. Deploy-time validator `solo_tier_hero_moment_slo_single_source` (§M.5 — new; pack assignment M02.3) asserts that the §44.6 throttle contract and the §48.8.10 SLO are reconcilable AND that the Solo / Free relaxation is registered exclusively at §44.6.4.X.

43. **Stage-3 latency-breach user-side banner. (V13 D-HM-007 remediation 2026-05-12.)** When `hero_moment_latency_breached` fires AND `provider_health_state(firecrawl) = healthy` (i.e., the breach is NOT a Firecrawl-outage pause covered by §48.8.3 Failure Mode #6(b)), the seller's workspace MUST render a non-blocking informational banner: *"Your bid is taking a moment to set up. We'll notify you when it's ready."* If `kb_bootstrap` populator completes after the seller has left the page, an in-app inbox card + Loops.so email `hero_moment_late_completion` fires (Appendix C — new). If `hero_moment_latency_breached` fired during the session, the Stake-Reveal Screen (§48.8.5) appends a parenthetical *"We took a bit longer than usual to get this ready."* The §48.8.3 Failure Mode #2 capability-unavailability banner pattern is the precedent surface contract.
41. **Activation-target sunset discipline — quarterly re-commitment.** The §44.1 `Seller Activation Metric p50 target` / §44.1 `Seller Activation Metric p90 target` Hero Moment targets in ACs #30 and #31 are *aspirational* targets carried forward from Summary §6.28 and C.135, and are NOT externally committed SLOs. To prevent the aspirational targets from calcifying into accidental reliability contracts, each quarterly `ops_growth_admin` review MUST formally take one of four actions against each target and record the decision in the Activation Target Review Log (Authored Extension; §42 dashboard + audit row): (a) **Re-commit** the target as-is for another quarter; (b) **Relax** the target to a new threshold with documented rationale (trailing-quarter p50 actuals, cohort-mix changes, capability-deprecation effects); (c) **Tighten** the target to a new threshold; (d) **Retire** the target entirely (remove the §42 P2 alert and the AC clause). A review that takes no action — passive carry-over — is explicitly forbidden; the Activation Target Review Log CI gate `activation_target_quarterly_review_required` fails the next release train if ≥ 100 days have elapsed since the last logged decision for either target. The review log row schema is: `{review_quarter, target_id ∈ {hero_moment_p50_activation, hero_moment_p90_activation}, prior_threshold, decision ∈ {re_commit, relax, tighten, retire}, new_threshold_nullable, trailing_quarter_p50_or_p90_actual, cohort_mix_notes, reviewer_user_id, reviewed_at}`. The `decision=relax` or `decision=retire` path additionally requires a written "cost of prior aspiration" note (≤ 500 chars) describing what changed in product or cohort that invalidated the prior target; the note is surfaced on the §42 Seller Activation Dashboard for trailing-four-quarter context. A formal retirement (`decision=retire`) MUST additionally emit a deprecation notice to the Ops Council via §47 governance and remove the AC clause from §48.8.10 via the next Integration_Prompts maintenance phase; until that maintenance phase runs, the retired target stays in §48.8.10 with a cross-reference to the retirement row. QA test `activation_target_review_log_monotonicity` asserts (i) every `target_id` has at least one review row per rolling 100-day window; (ii) every `decision=relax` row's `new_threshold_nullable` is ≥ `prior_threshold`; (iii) every `decision=tighten` row's `new_threshold_nullable` is ≤ `prior_threshold`; (iv) every `decision=retire` row has a non-null "cost of prior aspiration" note. The `ops_growth_admin` review cadence, the §42 dashboard surface, and the Integration_Prompts maintenance-phase hook are authored as an Authored Extension pending Phase 13 consolidation; see §48.8.11 (Authored Extensions) for the registration row.

### 48.8.11 Authored Extensions (§48.8) {#48.8.11-authored-extensions}

The §48.8 body above introduces the following Authored Extensions requiring human sign-off and Phase 13 consolidation:

1. **Activation Target Review Log** (AC #41). A new authored-extension entity capturing quarterly `ops_growth_admin` review decisions against the aspirational Hero Moment p50 / p90 targets. Schema per AC #41; retention: life of platform (governance audit). Surfaced on §42 Seller Activation Dashboard as a trailing-four-quarter strip; authoritative source of truth for AC #30 and AC #31 re-commitment, relaxation, tightening, or retirement. The CI gate `activation_target_quarterly_review_required` fails the release train if ≥ 100 days have elapsed since the last logged decision for either `target_id`. The `ops_growth_admin` role gains the `activation_target_review_decision` action (new Appendix J audit action type). Phase 13 consolidation will finalize the entity name, the `target_id` enum closure (initial values `hero_moment_p50_activation`, `hero_moment_p90_activation`), and the "cost of prior aspiration" note retention / visibility rules.
2. **`ops_growth_admin` activation-target review cadence** — new Ops governance ritual registered against §47. Quarterly cadence; scheduled via the existing §47 Ops Council cadence hook; failure to convene for > 100 days causes the §48.8.11 CI gate to fire. Phase 13 consolidation will wire this to the §47 Governance Calendar registry.

All Authored Extensions above are flagged in `/Sourcera/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Authored Extensions → §48.8 Hero Moment (2026-04-21 NB-10 remediation)`.

### 48.8.12 Abandonment Recovery {#48.8.12-abandonment-recovery}

*(V13 D-HM-006 remediation 2026-05-12. Authored Extension AE-V13-001 — Privacy + Marketing + Engineering Director sign-off pending v7.1.1 ratification.)*

The §48.8 Hero Moment specification authored engineering-side recovery surfaces (graceful degradation, on-call paging, DLQ retries, capability fallback) but did not author user-side recovery for the most common Hero Moment miss — abandonment. §48.8.12 closes that gap.

**Trigger conditions.** The Abandonment Recovery surface fires against SellerOnboardingSession rows where:
- `stage_2_sso_completed_at IS NOT NULL` (the seller has provisioned an Org), AND
- `first_requirement_response_at IS NULL` (the seller has not produced a value moment), AND
- `last_activity_at + elapsed_threshold < now()` per the schedule below.

**Three-stage recovery cadence.**

| Stage | Elapsed threshold | Recovery surface | Loops.so type | PostHog event |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24-hour re-engagement | 24h since `stage_2_sso_completed_at` with no Stage 3 / 4 timestamps | Email: *"Your bid is still drafted and waiting — pick up where you left off"*; in-app inbox card; deep-link directly to the partially-populated Bid Workspace (no re-SSO required if existing session cookie valid, else magic-link re-issue) | `hero_moment_abandonment_24h` (Appendix C — new; subject-line catalog at §41.2 V13 block) | `hero_moment_abandonment_24h_email_sent {seller_org_id, session_id, elapsed_seconds_since_sso}` (Appendix G — new) |
| 7-day pre-sweep nudge | 6d 12h elapsed (12h before §4.4.22 abandonment-sweeper trigger at 7d) | Email: *"Your bid will be archived in 12 hours unless you respond — keep your draft alive"*; final magic-link reissue with extended 72h validity | `hero_moment_abandonment_pre_sweep` (Appendix C — new) | `hero_moment_abandonment_pre_sweep_email_sent` (Appendix G — new) |
| 14-day re-issue (single attempt) | 7 days post-abandonment-sweeper (session now `abandoned`) | Email: *"We saved everything you taught Sourcera. Restart your bid in one click."*; magic-link re-issue against a fresh SellerOnboardingSession row bound to the existing Seller Org (KB Draft pre-populated from the abandoned session's KB writes) | `hero_moment_abandonment_re_issue` (Appendix C — new) | `hero_moment_abandonment_re_issue_email_sent` (Appendix G — new); on re-arrival: `hero_moment_abandonment_recovered {original_session_id, new_session_id}` |

**State-machine extension (Appendix L.X — SellerOnboardingSession Recovery States).**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `in_progress` | `re_engaged_24h` | 24h elapsed without Stage-3 timestamps | At least one of `stage_3_*_at` fields IS NULL | Loops.so email enqueued; `re_engaged_24h_at` stamped |
| `in_progress` | `pre_sweep_nudged` | 6d 12h elapsed without Stage-3 timestamps | Same | Final magic-link extended; `pre_sweep_nudged_at` stamped |
| `in_progress` | `abandoned` | 7d elapsed (existing sweeper per §4.4.22 FM 5) | Existing § 4.4.22 contract | `abandon_reason_code` stamped |
| `abandoned` | `re_issued_14d` | 14d post-abandonment OR seller clicks re-issue magic-link | Single attempt only per `re_issue_attempts ≤ 1` invariant | Fresh SellerOnboardingSession row bound to existing Seller Org; KB Draft pre-populated |
| `re_issued_14d` | `abandoned_terminal` | 30d post-re-issue without Stage-3 timestamps | Re-issue attempt consumed | Terminal state; no further recovery |

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. The §48.8.12 Loops.so email pipeline MUST consume `last_activity_at` from SellerOnboardingSession and dispatch the three email types per the trigger schedule above. The Convex cron `hero_moment_abandonment_sweeper` runs at 15-minute cadence and idempotently enqueues at most one email per (session_id, recovery_stage) pair. QA test `hero_moment_abandonment_recovery_idempotency` asserts.
2. Magic-link re-issue at 14d (`hero_moment_abandonment_re_issue`) MUST honor the §6.1 magic-link 72-hour validity contract; expired re-issued links offer the standard "request a new link" flow.
3. The 14d re-issued SellerOnboardingSession row MUST carry `recovered_from_session_id` pointing to the abandoned session AND pre-populate `kb_draft_entries[]` from the recovered session's KBEntry rows (preserving the seller's prior KB contributions).
4. Loops.so email types `hero_moment_abandonment_24h`, `hero_moment_abandonment_pre_sweep`, `hero_moment_abandonment_re_issue`, `firecrawl_recovery_re_bootstrap_completed` MUST be registered in §41.2 Email Type Catalog with subject-line lock + Tier-2 retry curve (5 attempts: 30s/2m/10m/1h/6h; DLQ at 5) + suppression-list integration per §41.3.
5. The §48.8.12 recovery cadence MUST be suppressed during a Firecrawl-outage pause window (`stage_3_firecrawl_outage_pause_ms > 0`) until the pause window closes; the `last_activity_at` clock resumes only when `provider_health_state(firecrawl) = healthy`. Prevents premature abandonment classification during third-party outages. QA test `hero_moment_abandonment_provider_outage_pause` asserts.
6. Solo / Free tier sellers MUST receive the §48.8.12 recovery cadence at parity with paid tiers (the recovery surface is foundational to PLG and not a paid-tier feature). Solo-tier email copy substitutes monetary references per §44.6 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment (no "value pricing" line, no AIWallet-balance mention).
7. CI gate `hero_moment_abandonment_recovery_cadence_completeness` (§M.5 — new) asserts the three email types are registered in Appendix C, the four PostHog events are registered in Appendix G, the Loops.so subject-line catalog rows exist in §41.2, and the Convex `hero_moment_abandonment_sweeper` cron is wired.
8. *(Authored Extension AE-V13-007 — Privacy Officer sign-off pending v7.1.1 ratification; Counterfactual-#1 hardening of the §48.8.12 DSAR exclusion contract.)* The DSAR exclusion MUST fail-closed across the **enqueue→send in-flight window**, not only at sweeper enqueue time (AC #1). The abandonment-recovery dispatcher MUST re-evaluate the §6.8 pseudonymization predicate — the same predicate the AC #1 sweeper-skip consumes — at Loops.so send/retry dispatch time, mirroring the established send-time re-check idiom (a notification dispatch re-checks current state at send time and is dropped if the subject is no longer eligible). If a §6.8 right-to-erasure pseudonymization lands after a `hero_moment_abandonment_*` email is enqueued but before it sends, or during its AC #4 Tier-2 retry curve, the dispatch MUST be dropped and the SellerOnboardingSession recovery state left unchanged (no `re_engaged_24h` / `pre_sweep_nudged` / `re_issued_14d` transition stamped against an erased subject). The skip MUST emit a §4.6.1 AuditEvent recording only `{session_id, recovery_stage, skip_reason='dsar_pseudonymized'}` (Appendix J `recovery_cadence_skip_reason` enum — registered under AE-V13-007) and MUST NOT persist the pseudonymized `seller_email` (no §6.8-erased PII re-introduced into the audit log). The §M.5.12 CI gate `dsar_erased_seller_excluded_from_recovery_cadence` assertion is extended to cover the send-time re-check (runtime wiring rides the M02.3 pack per §M.5.5). QA test `hero_moment_abandonment_dsar_inflight_send_time_failclose` asserts.

**Failure modes addressed.**

- **Loops.so outage during email send.** Per §41.3 retry curve; on DLQ, a single in-app inbox card is the fallback (so the seller sees the recovery prompt next time they log in).
- **Seller has unsubscribed from product emails.** Suppression-list check at enqueue time per §41.3; suppressed seller still receives the in-app inbox card at login; the magic-link re-issue is rate-limited per existing §6.1 cap.
- **Seller is on a free EU residency tier and has previously DSAR-erased.** Per §6.8 right-to-erasure: the abandoned SellerOnboardingSession row is pseudonymized; recovery emails MUST NOT fire against a pseudonymized seller_email. CI gate `dsar_erased_seller_excluded_from_recovery_cadence` asserts.
- **Right-to-erasure lands in the enqueue→send in-flight window (Counterfactual-#1 / AE-V13-007).** A `hero_moment_abandonment_*` email enqueued by the sweeper before a §6.8 pseudonymization, but still inside its AC #4 Tier-2 retry curve when the erasure completes, is dropped at send time per AC #8 (send-time §6.8-predicate re-evaluation, fail-closed). This closes the residual that the enqueue-time-only checks of AC #1 + the unsubscribe failure mode above leave open: without the AC #8 send-time re-check, an email enqueued at T−5m could still fire after an erasure completing at T (GDPR Art. 17 exposure). The skip-audit row is PII-minimized per AC #8.

### 48.8.13 `kb_bootstrap` Allowance Compensation Contract {#48.8.13-kb-bootstrap-allowance-compensation-contract}

*(V13 D-13V-023 remediation 2026-05-12. Authored Extension AE-V13-002 — Pricing + Engineering Director sign-off pending v7.1.1 ratification. Parallels D-5.7-024 Stage-3 mid-streaming abandonment compensation.)*

The `kb_bootstrap` capability is metered against a lifetime-free allowance (1 per Seller Org per Summary C.73 + §22.X.Y). When the Bootstrap runs against a degraded third-party path (Firecrawl outage per §48.8.3 FM #6; Anthropic Claude rate-limit; Convex region partition), the allowance is consumed despite a sub-optimal outcome. §48.8.13 authors the compensation contract that restores the allowance under defined conditions, preserving the seller's perception of fairness and Sourcera's PLG funnel integrity.

**Eligibility predicate.** An `AIOperation` row with `capability_id = 'kb_bootstrap'` qualifies for allowance compensation IFF:
1. `capability_degradation_triggered = true` on the bound SellerOnboardingSession row, AND
2. One of: (a) `firecrawl_outage_degraded_kb_bootstrap` event was emitted against the same session_id within the AIOperation's execution window, (b) Anthropic `claude-opus-4-6` returned rate-limit / 5xx during the AIOperation per Sentry trace, (c) Convex region partition recorded per §42.6.0 ProviderHealthState `provider_kind = 'convex'`, OR (d) the resulting `kb_draft_entry_count` is < 10 entries (the "useful-bootstrap" floor per the §48.1.6 leading-indicator #3 60% acceptance threshold).

**Compensation actions.**

1. **Automatic.** The `kb_bootstrap_allowance_compensation_sweeper` Convex cron (runs at 6-hour cadence) sweeps AIOperation rows from the trailing 24h that match the eligibility predicate. For each match: the Seller Org's `kb_bootstrap_lifetime_free_consumed_at` field on §4.4.X is reset to NULL; an audit event `kb_bootstrap.allowance_restored {seller_org_id, original_ai_operation_id, restoration_reason ∈ {firecrawl_outage, anthropic_rate_limit, convex_partition, useful_bootstrap_floor_miss}}` is written; a Loops.so email `kb_bootstrap_allowance_restored` fires to the Seller Org's `org_owner` and `seller_admin`: *"We couldn't fully use your free Bootstrap due to a system issue on our end — we've reset it so you can try again whenever you're ready."*
2. **Ops-side manual.** A new endpoint `POST /v1/ops/seller-orgs/{org_id}/kb-bootstrap/refund` allows `ops_growth_admin` or `ops_finance_admin` to manually restore the allowance against an Ops-discretion case not caught by the automatic predicate. Request body: `{"reason": "<string>", "original_ai_operation_id_nullable": "<uuid>"}`. Response: 200 with `{restoration_id, restored_at}`. The Ops override is audit-logged.

**SLA.** Automatic restoration: ≤ 24 hours from outage detection. Ops-side manual: per Ops discretion; no SLA. Customer-facing notification: ≤ 5 minutes after restoration via Loops.so + in-app inbox card.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. The `kb_bootstrap_allowance_compensation_sweeper` Convex cron MUST run at 6-hour cadence, idempotently restore allowances per the eligibility predicate, and write audit + telemetry events per §48.8.13 Compensation Actions #1. CI test `kb_bootstrap_allowance_compensation_idempotency` asserts no double-restoration on repeated sweeper runs.
2. The §22.X `kb_bootstrap_recovery_re_run_scheduler` cron (per §48.8.3 FM #6(f)) MUST treat a restored allowance as eligible for silent re-run; the re-run does NOT consume a second compensation cycle (the predicate `capability_degradation_triggered = true` on the prior session does not re-trigger).
3. The Loops.so email type `kb_bootstrap_allowance_restored` MUST be registered in §41.2 with subject-line lock + Tier-2 retry curve.
4. The §M.5 CI gate `kb_bootstrap_allowance_compensation_completeness` asserts: (i) the eligibility predicate matches the four defined causes; (ii) the audit event schema includes `restoration_reason` with the four-value enum; (iii) the Ops endpoint exists with the correct auth-scope contract; (iv) the customer-facing email is registered. Pack assignment: M02.3.
5. **Solo / Free tier parity.** Solo / Free sellers MUST receive allowance restoration at parity with paid tiers; the §44.6 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment substitutes the monetary "free Bootstrap" framing with "your free KB starter" copy (no plan-tier-specific suppression of compensation itself).
6. **DSAR cascade.** A `kb_bootstrap.allowance_restored` audit event is subject to the §6.8 DSAR cascade per §40.2 retention class `AuditEvent` (5-year financial-audit retention); the audit row's `seller_org_id` field is the only PII surface and is pseudonymized via the standard pattern.

**Failure modes addressed.**

- **Concurrent automatic + Ops manual restoration.** Resolved: the sweeper takes a per-session_id lock; manual Ops endpoint also acquires the lock; whichever fires first wins; the second returns HTTP 409 `kb_bootstrap_allowance_already_restored`.
- **Restoration sweeper fires against a Seller Org that has since DSAR-erased.** Resolved: the sweeper joins against the canonical Seller Org table; pseudonymized Orgs are skipped; an audit row records the skip.
- **Stripe billing reconciliation.** The lifetime-free `kb_bootstrap` allowance is NOT a Stripe-charged item; restoration has zero Stripe-side reconciliation. (For paid `kb_bootstrap_extra` allowances under §34.X — not in scope of §48.8.13 — restoration would route through Stripe Credit Note per §34.10 patterns; cross-reference for future expansion.)

# Section 49: Seller Onboarding — Implementation-Level Seven-Stage Flow {#section-49-seller-onboarding-implementation-level-seven-stage-flow}

## 49.1 Seller Onboarding — Seven-Stage Flow {#49.1-seller-onboarding-seven-stage-flow}

**Authoring intent.** §49.1 is the engineering-contract companion to §35.2 (narrative seven-stage seller onboarding) and §48.8 (Hero Moment surface specification and Onboarding Anti-Patterns). §35.2 tells the product story; §48.8 authors the four-phase Hero-Moment UX surface and the AP1–AP6 hard bans; §49.1 authors the seven-stage implementation pipeline as a per-stage engineering contract — trigger conditions, workflow, data read/written, capabilities invoked, AIWallet debits, telemetry events, failure modes, and acceptance criteria — so that engineering, QA, and Ops have a single build-ready reference for the stage-by-stage transitions persisted on SellerOnboardingSession (§4.4.22). §49.1 is strictly additive; it cites, does not duplicate, §48.8 surface specifications and §4.4.22 entity schema.

**Relationship to §35.2, §48.8, §4.4.22.** §35.2 is the narrative seven-stage description (read-once orientation). §48.8 is the Hero-Moment surface specification in four phases (pre-arrival, minutes 0–3, minutes 3–45, hour 1+) with embedded AP1–AP6 enforcement and the eleven-block per-subsection layout. §4.4.22 is the SellerOnboardingSession entity schema — every stage timestamp, every `stage_N_*` column, `activation_metric_elapsed_seconds`, `completion_state` enum, and the entity-level acceptance criteria / failure modes. §49.1 maps the seven conceptual stages (per Summary §6.28.2) one-to-one onto §4.4.22 timestamps and §48.8 surface phases, and authors the stage-transition engineering contracts that were previously distributed across §35.2 narrative, §48.8 phase blocks, and §4.4.22 acceptance criteria. Where §49.1 and §48.8 address the same moment, §49.1 defers to §48.8 for UX surface, and §48.8 defers to §49.1 for stage-boundary engineering contract.

**Source authority.** Summary §6.28.2 (Seven-Stage Seller Onboarding Experience); Summary §3.6 (Seller-Side Hero Moment Mechanics); Summary Summary §3.1b (Your first bid is already drafted); C.132 (Seller Hero Moment Mechanics); SPS v3 §15.3 Four Seller Conversion Moments; C.133 (pre-Solo Three Conversion Moments baseline); C.135 (Seller Activation Metric); C.136 (Forced-Vendor-Signup Playbook); C.137 (Win/Loss Debrief as upgrade trigger); C.139 (Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee); C.140 (Seller Onboarding Required Capabilities); C.141 (Seller Onboarding Anti-Patterns — banned). Entity schema at §4.4.22. Hero-Moment surface at §48.8. Conversion-Moment binding at §48.1.7 / §48.8.6. KB Bootstrap at §22.4 / §22.8. First-Pass RFP Draft at §22.5. KB-Gap Detector at §22.6. Citation Inline Card at §22.7. Capability registry at §21.4 (`kb_bootstrap`, `first_pass_responses` — canonical; `first_pass_response` is the per-requirement capability; `first_pass_responses` is the batch capability with lifetime-free allowance per C.140). AIWallet lifetime-free bootstrap allowance at §34.10.4. Seller Wallet $5 free allowance at §34.10.4. Outcome Resolver at §34.6 / §34.11. Win/Loss Debrief at §48.7.

**Stage → SellerOnboardingSession timestamp map.** The seven conceptual stages (Summary §6.28.2) bind to §4.4.22 SellerOnboardingSession columns as follows (this mapping is authoritative for §49.1; any future stage-boundary change MUST land here first and propagate to §4.4.22 and §48.8):

| Stage | Name | Entry Timestamp | Exit Timestamp | §48.8 Phase | §35.2 Narrative |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Magic-Link Arrival | `stage_1_arrival_at` | `stage_2_sso_initiated_at` | §48.8.3 (T=0) | §35.2 Stage 1 |
| 2 | Domain Bootstrap | `stage_2_sso_initiated_at` | `stage_2_sso_completed_at` + `stage_2_bootstrap_started_at` | §48.8.3 (T=15–60 s) | §35.2 Stage 2 |
| 3 | First-Pass Draft | `stage_2_bootstrap_started_at` | `stage_3_bid_workspace_loaded_at` | §48.8.3 (T=30–90 s) | §35.2 Stage 3 |
| 4 | Landing Screen ("Your bid is ready") | `stage_3_bid_workspace_loaded_at` | `stage_3_first_edit_at` | §48.8.3 (T=90 s – 3 min) | §35.2 Stage 4 |
| 5 | In-Workspace Review | `stage_3_first_edit_at` | `first_bid_submitted_at` | §48.8.4 (minutes 3–45) | §35.2 Stage 5 |
| 6 | First Bid Submission | `first_bid_submitted_at` | `stage_6_exit_at` | §48.8.5 (hour 1+) | §35.2 Stage 6 |
| 7 | Post-Submission Debrief | `stage_7_entered_at` | `stage_7_win_debrief_rendered_at` OR `stage_7_loss_debrief_rendered_at` OR `stage_7_phase_lapsed_at` OR `completion_state = 'churned_post_activation'` | §48.8.5 + §48.7 Win/Loss Debrief | §35.2 Stage 7 |

Stages 2 and 3 overlap on SellerOnboardingSession: `stage_2_bootstrap_started_at` is both the Stage-2-exit signal (Bootstrap has begun) and the Stage-3-entry signal (the in-SSO-redirect execution that produces First-Pass drafts depends on Bootstrap being in flight). This overlap is intentional per Summary §3.6 ¶2 ("in-SSO-redirect execution") and §48.8.3 Workflow steps 3–6; the engineering contract is that Stage 2 completes when the Bootstrap job has transitioned to `execution_state = 'executing'` AND the SSO flow has returned a resolved Seller Org, whichever is later — at that point Stage 3 is structurally already running.

**Per-subsection structure.** Each of §49.1.1 through §49.1.7 follows the eleven-block layout established by §48.8.2–§48.8.5: (1) Purpose; (2) Authoritative Source; (3) Trigger / Entry Condition; (4) Workflow (step-by-step); (5) UX Surface Specification (cross-refs §48.8, does not duplicate); (6) Data Read / Written (entity refs); (7) Capabilities Invoked (§21.4); (8) AIWallet Debits (§34.10); (9) Telemetry Events; (10) Failure Modes Addressed (≥3); (11) Acceptance Criteria. §49.1.8 (Progress Storytelling UX Implementation), §49.1.9 (Onboarding Anti-Patterns — Runtime Detectors & CI Gates), and §49.1.10 (consolidated Acceptance Criteria) follow a structure appropriate to their scope.

**NB — Prior §48.5 reference remediation (NB-18).** Prior drafts of this section referenced §48.5 ("M1–M8 Growth Mechanics") as the source for invite-source cohorts and the Forced-Vendor-Signup mechanic. Those references are corrected throughout §49.1: the authoritative source for invite-source cohorts is §4.5.x MarketplaceInviteLink; for the Forced-Vendor-Signup mechanic is §48.7 (M14 Ghost-Bid Conversion) and §48.2.2 (L1); for Four Seller Conversion Moments is §48.1.7 (definitional binding) and §48.8.6 (UX surface). §48.5 remains the authoritative source for M1–M8 buyer-side growth mechanics only.

### 49.1.1 Stage 1: Magic-Link Arrival {#49.1.1-stage-1-magic-link-arrival}

**Purpose.** Stage 1 is the zero-form, zero-friction entry into the Sourcera Seller Console. The seller has an identity (their email domain) and an intent (the buyer's invite). The engineering contract is that Stage 1 produces a `stage_1_arrival_at` timestamp, captures `invite_source` and `bid_id` (if any) from the MarketplaceInviteLink, and emits the SSO-redirect-bootstrap-pre-warm signal that starts Stage 2 — all without asking the seller anything. Zero form fields is not a UX preference; it is a HARD QA-testable AP5 contract (§48.8.7 — "Requiring vendor to describe company / industry / role before Bootstrap runs") and an AP-ban that §49.1.9 enforces with a CI-gated detector.

**Authoritative Source.** Summary §6.28.2 Stage 1; Summary Summary §3.1b ¶1 ("A link. A password. Nothing else."); §48.8.3 Workflow steps 1–2; §48.8.7 AP5 (canonical zero-form ban — "Requiring vendor to describe company / industry / role before Bootstrap runs"); §4.5.x MarketplaceInviteLink entity.

**Trigger / Entry Condition.** HTTP GET on the MarketplaceInviteLink landing URL (`marketplace.sourcera.com/invite/{invite_token}`) OR magic-link-fallback click (`marketplace.sourcera.com/magic/{magic_token}`). The request MUST present a valid, non-expired, non-revoked `invite_token` or `magic_token` resolvable to a single MarketplaceInviteLink row.

**Workflow.**

1. **T=0: Invite validation.** Server resolves the `invite_token` → MarketplaceInviteLink row. Validates: (a) row exists, (b) `expires_at > now()`, (c) `revoked_at IS NULL`, (d) `invite_source` resolves to Appendix J `seller_onboarding_invite_source` (all six canonical values). Invalid tokens render §41.x "Invite unavailable" page with clear next steps (contact the buyer; request a new link); Stage 1 DOES NOT advance.
2. **T=0–500 ms: SellerOnboardingSession row creation.** Insert a new SellerOnboardingSession row with `invite_magic_link_id = invite.id`, `invite_source = invite.invite_source`, `bid_id = invite.bid_id (nullable)`, `seller_org_id = NULL` (unresolved until SSO callback), `stage_1_arrival_at = now()`, `completion_state = 'in_progress'`. Write is idempotent on `invite_token`: if an active or errored session already exists for this invite, the existing row is returned; no new row is created. Deduplication resolves through `invite_magic_link_id` and the §4.4.22 `(recipient_email_hash, stage_1_arrival_at DESC)` lookup rather than a lifecycle-specific unique-index carve-out.
3. **T=0–500 ms: Pre-arrival preparation check.** Server reads the pre-arrival artifacts from §48.8.2 (SellerDomainEnrichmentRecord, pre-resolved `kb_bootstrap` job, Firecrawl reservation). If any pre-arrival artifact is missing (invite was created < 10 s ago AND pre-arrival preparation has not completed), Stage 1 proceeds without blocking; the Stage 2 populator detects the missing artifacts and triggers the degraded bootstrap path per §48.8.3 failure-mode handling.
4. **T=0–2 s: Landing page render.** HTTP response renders the §48.8.3 landing page — zero form fields, single centered column, buyer-company summary, single primary CTA. The rendered HTML is generated server-side (no client-side form scaffolding that a future maintainer could extend into multi-field); the CI-gated AP5 detector asserts this every build (§49.1.9 D-AP5).
5. **T=0–15 s: Seller clicks primary CTA.** Click triggers HTTP POST to `/onboarding/sso-initiate` with `invite_token`. Server writes `stage_2_sso_initiated_at = now()`, issues a WorkOS SSO redirect (Google / Microsoft), and attaches `invite_token` to the OAuth `state` parameter (so the callback can resolve the SellerOnboardingSession row without re-reading the invite). If WorkOS is degraded, server offers the magic-link-fallback flow inline (single-email-address form; AP5 exemption granted ONLY for the fallback email field per the §49.1.9 D-AP5 exemption list — the magic-link email is the ONLY Sourcera-owned form field permitted on any Stage-1 / Stage-2 surface).
6. **T=0–∞ (seller may never click CTA).** The Stage 1 → Stage 2 transition is lazy; if the seller closes the tab after Stage 1 render, the SellerOnboardingSession remains `in_progress` until the §4.4.22 pre-activation abandonment classifier transitions it to `abandoned` with `abandonment_reason = 'stage_1_no_cta_click'`.

**UX Surface Specification.** See §48.8.3 Workflow step 1 and UX Surface Specification (landing page). §49.1 does NOT author the landing page UX — it authors the data-plane contract. The landing page MUST render with zero form fields before SSO initiation (AP5); the "Accept and draft" CTA MUST be the single primary action; any deviation is a CI-gate failure (§49.1.9 detector D-AP5).

**Data Read / Written.**

- **Read:** MarketplaceInviteLink (`invite_token` lookup); SellerDomainEnrichmentRecord (opportunistic, from pre-arrival); pre-resolved `kb_bootstrap` job state (opportunistic).
- **Written:** SellerOnboardingSession (INSERT on first arrival; idempotent no-op on return visit); `Organization` / `User` rows — NOT YET (creation deferred to SSO callback in Stage 2); no KBEntry / AIOperation writes at Stage 1.
- **Unchanged:** MarketplaceInviteLink (not updated by Stage 1; `first_clicked_at` is written but is distinct from SellerOnboardingSession timestamps).

**Capabilities Invoked.** None. Stage 1 performs no AI inference. The pre-resolved `kb_bootstrap` job stays in `execution_state = 'pre_resolved'` until Stage 2.

**AIWallet Debits.** None. No wallet debit occurs in Stage 1.

**Telemetry Events.**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `seller_onboarding_stage_entered` | `stage_1_arrival_at` write | `{invite_id, invite_source, bid_id (nullable), stage=1, elapsed_seconds_since_arrival=0, stage_outcome=completed}` (seller_org_id is NULL pre-SSO; `completed` indicates the entry write succeeded, not stage completion) |
| `seller_onboarding_landing_rendered` | HTTP 200 on landing page | `{invite_id, invite_source, render_latency_ms, invite_token_valid=true}` |
| `seller_onboarding_landing_invalid_token` | HTTP 4xx on landing page | `{invite_token_prefix (first 8 chars for diagnostics, never full token), failure_reason ∈ {not_found, expired, revoked, malformed}}` |
| `seller_onboarding_cta_clicked` | `stage_2_sso_initiated_at` write | `{invite_id, invite_source, elapsed_seconds_since_arrival, cta_variant}` |

All events inherit the standard Appendix G property set (`org_id` nullable pre-SSO; `timestamp`; `distinct_id` keyed on `invite_id` pre-SSO and backfilled to `seller_org_id` post-SSO per §48.8.3 event-joining convention).

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Invalid / expired / revoked invite token.** `seller_onboarding_landing_invalid_token` emits; landing page renders the "Invite unavailable" page (§41.x) with contact-the-buyer and request-new-link CTAs. No SellerOnboardingSession row is created for invalid tokens (no session pollution). Failure is observable via dashboard: an invite-invalidation-rate surge > 5% trailing 24h raises a §42 P3 to `ops_growth_admin`.
2. **Invite token collision (two sessions presenting the same token).** Deduplication resolves through `invite_magic_link_id` plus the §4.4.22 pre-Stage-2 `(recipient_email_hash, stage_1_arrival_at DESC)` lookup; the second presentation resolves to the same active or errored SellerOnboardingSession row. This is legitimate (seller returning in a new browser); the session is re-entered, not forked.
3. **WorkOS SSO provider outage at CTA-click.** Inline magic-link-fallback form renders within 2 s of SSO failure detection; AP5 exemption applies (fallback needs a single email field); fallback email MUST match `invite.email` to prevent invite-sharing abuse.
4. **Pre-arrival preparation incomplete at Stage 1 arrival (invite < 10 s old).** Stage 1 proceeds without blocking; SellerOnboardingSession row is created with `pre_arrival_state = 'incomplete'`; Stage 2 populator engages the degraded-bootstrap path per §48.8.3 failure-mode 1.
5. **Seller arrives from a non-targeted browser / email client (e.g., iOS mail in-app browser).** Landing page MUST render identically per §3.3 cross-surface parity; AP5 detector asserts zero form fields render even in reduced-JS environments. If the in-app browser blocks WorkOS OAuth popups, the server detects and routes to the magic-link-fallback path.
6. **Seller returns after the pre-activation abandonment classifier has fired.** Existing session is in `abandoned` state; re-arrival re-enters the same SellerOnboardingSession row. On first-requirement-response submission the row transitions to `reactivated` per §4.4.22; the original `stage_1_arrival_at` is preserved so the Activation Metric remains truthful and the seller is counted once in the activated cohort.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. The landing page MUST render in ≤ 500 ms at p95 on a 3G-throttled mobile device; CI Lighthouse test asserts. (Cross-refs §48.8.3 AC 5.)
2. Zero form fields MUST appear on the landing page before SSO initiation; the AP5 CI detector (§49.1.9 D-AP5) runs on every PR and fails the build on any added form field. (Cross-refs §48.8.3 AC 6; §48.8.7 AP5.)
3. SellerOnboardingSession INSERT on Stage 1 arrival MUST be idempotent on `invite_magic_link_id` for the active-or-errored presentation path; concurrent arrivals (two browser tabs) MUST resolve to the same row through the §4.4.22 deduplication lookup. Property test asserts across 10,000 randomized concurrent-arrival scenarios.
4. Invalid / expired / revoked invites MUST NOT create a SellerOnboardingSession row; a property test confirms zero session rows for 10,000 invalid-token arrivals.
5. `seller_onboarding_stage_entered {stage=1}` MUST emit within 500 ms of the SellerOnboardingSession INSERT at p95; PostHog-funnel test asserts.
6. The magic-link-fallback path MUST render within 2 s of WorkOS SSO failure detection at p95; the fallback's email field is the ONLY AP5 exemption (documented in §49.1.9 D-AP5 exemption list); the form MUST include no other Sourcera-owned fields.
7. A re-arrival after `abandoned` staleness MUST re-enter the existing SellerOnboardingSession row with the original `invite_source`, `bid_id`, and `stage_1_arrival_at`; on activation it MUST transition to `reactivated`. Integration test asserts no duplicate active cohort row is created.

### 49.1.2 Stage 2: Domain Bootstrap {#49.1.2-stage-2-domain-bootstrap}

**Purpose.** Stage 2 executes the Opus-tier `kb_bootstrap` capability against the seller's domain during the SSO redirect window, producing 40–200 draft KB entries before the seller first sees a workspace. The engineering contract is that Stage 2 transitions the pre-resolved Bootstrap job to `executing`, produces draft KBEntries with `confidence_score`, `source='bootstrap_proposed'`, `review_state='pending_review'`, and completes in ≤ 10,000 ms p90 (§4.4.22 AC 4) on the hero path. The hero path target is 40 approved entries on p50 of seller domains (C.132 / §48.1.6 Indicator #3); fewer than 40 is a Stage-2-degradation signal that triggers a degraded-hero-moment UI (but never blocks the seller).

**Authoritative Source.** Summary §6.28.2 Stage 2; Summary §3.6 ¶2 ("in-SSO-redirect execution"); §48.8.3 Workflow steps 3–4; §22.4 KB Bootstrap workflow; §22.8 Sourcera KB MCP Server; §21.4 capability `kb_bootstrap` (Opus, lifetime-free); C.140 (Seller Onboarding Required Capabilities); C.132 Hero Moment Mechanics; §34.10.4 lifetime-free bootstrap allowance.

**Trigger / Entry Condition.** `stage_2_sso_initiated_at` is written on SellerOnboardingSession (Stage 1 CTA click). The WorkOS SSO redirect is in flight.

**Workflow.**

1. **T=0: Pre-resolved Bootstrap job transition.** On `stage_2_sso_initiated_at` write, the pre-resolved `kb_bootstrap` job (per §48.8.2) transitions from `execution_state = 'pre_resolved'` to `execution_state = 'executing'`. Transition MUST complete in ≤ 500 ms (§48.8.2 AC 2). `stage_2_bootstrap_started_at = now()` is written on SellerOnboardingSession.
2. **T=0–15 s: Firecrawl crawl of candidate URLs.** The Firecrawl integration fetches: (a) seller homepage, (b) trust/security subpages (auto-discovered via sitemap.xml + robots.txt + `/trust`, `/security`, `/compliance` path heuristics), (c) product/help/docs subpages (auto-discovered via nav-link extraction on the homepage). Per-host budget: up to 40 pages, depth 3, respecting robots.txt. Firecrawl reservations from §48.8.2 are consumed here (no re-reservation).
3. **T=5–30 s: Content extraction and chunking.** Each fetched page is passed through §22.4 extraction (trafilatura-derived content extractor + semantic-chunker at 500-token chunks with 100-token overlap). Chunks inherit `source_url`, `source_title`, `crawled_at`, `content_hash`.
4. **T=15–60 s: KB entry synthesis via `kb_bootstrap` (Opus-tier capability).** Per §21.4 `kb_bootstrap` invocation: the capability ingests the extracted chunks and emits candidate KB entries keyed on inferred question categories (e.g., "SOC 2 compliance", "Data retention", "Incident response SLA", "Supported integrations") with `proposed_question`, `proposed_answer`, `citation_chunk_ids[]`, `confidence_score ∈ [0.0, 1.0]`. Opus reasoning is used here (not Sonnet) — per C.140, `kb_bootstrap` MUST use the Opus tier during the Hero Moment window.
5. **T=15–60 s (parallel): KBEntry INSERTs.** Each candidate becomes a KBEntry row with `source = 'bootstrap_proposed'`, `review_state = 'pending_review'`, `seller_org_id` backfilled when SSO callback resolves (race with Stage 2 SSO-callback; see failure mode 6 below). The Indexing subsystem (§22.8) consumes the INSERT stream and begins embedding generation.
6. **T=30–90 s: Bootstrap completion signal.** When the Bootstrap job's terminal state is reached (`execution_state = 'succeeded'` or `execution_state = 'partial'`), the SellerOnboardingSession row is updated with `stage_2_bootstrap_entry_count = N` (count of successfully INSERTed KBEntries). `stage_2_population_latency_ms` is computed as `(now() - stage_2_bootstrap_started_at) * 1000`.
7. **T=SSO-callback (parallel to Bootstrap): Seller Org provisioning.** WorkOS SSO callback arrives; server resolves the `state` parameter → SellerOnboardingSession row → creates or resolves the Seller Org + User. `stage_2_sso_completed_at = now()` is written. If a pre-existing Seller Org is found (matched by email domain), disambiguation flow engages per §4.4.22 failure mode 10 (AC handled in §49.1.2 failure mode 7 below). If new Seller Org is created, `seller_org_id` is backfilled on all KBEntry rows INSERTed by the Bootstrap job in step 5 (batch UPDATE bounded to ≤ 200 rows per transaction).
8. **Stage 2 exit.** Stage 2 completes when both (a) `stage_2_sso_completed_at` is set AND (b) `stage_2_bootstrap_started_at` is set. In the happy path these are ~ concurrent (SSO completes around T=30–60 s; Bootstrap starts at T=0 and continues through Stage 3). Stage 3 (First-Pass Draft) begins as soon as Bootstrap has produced enough grounded chunks to cite from — the §22.8 retrieval subsystem signals "ready for grounded draft" when ≥ 20 chunks have crossed the embedding pipeline.

**UX Surface Specification.** See §48.8.3 Workflow step 5 (progress-storytelling screen) and §49.1.8 (Progress Storytelling UX Implementation). The seller sees ONLY the progress-storytelling screen during Stage 2; no KB editor, no workspace, no AIWallet counter. The progress-storytelling status lines ("Scanning yourcompany.com…", "Found your security documentation…") MUST correspond 1:1 to actual work in flight per §49.1.8 and AP7 (§48.8.7 — banned: faked progress).

**Data Read / Written.**

- **Read:** SellerDomainEnrichmentRecord (§48.8.2); pre-resolved `kb_bootstrap` job state; MarketplaceInviteLink (for invite context); Marketplace Tagger candidate `category_id` tags (Summary §6.16.6).
- **Written:** `kb_bootstrap` job state transitions (`pre_resolved` → `executing` → {`succeeded`, `partial`, `failed`}); KBEntry (INSERT, 40–200 rows with `source='bootstrap_proposed'`, `review_state='pending_review'`); KB embeddings via §22.8 Indexing; SellerOnboardingSession `stage_2_*` timestamps; Seller Org / User (CREATE or resolve on SSO callback); AIOperation + Usage Event (one per Bootstrap invocation, bounded to the lifetime-free allowance).
- **Not written:** AIWallet debits (Bootstrap is lifetime-free per §34.10.4); Capability Declarations (deferred to Stage 5 `kb_to_capability_suggestion` per §48.8.4).

**Capabilities Invoked.** `kb_bootstrap` (Opus; lifetime-free per C.140 and §34.10.4). Secondary: nothing else fires synchronously in Stage 2 — `first_pass_responses` begins in Stage 3 as soon as the retrieval subsystem signals "ready for grounded draft".

**AIWallet Debits.** None. `kb_bootstrap` consumes the lifetime-free allowance per §34.10.4 — one-time-per-Seller-Org allowance that persists across plan changes (the C.139 Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee applies). If the lifetime-free allowance has already been consumed (seller returning after a prior abandoned onboarding), the Bootstrap invocation is short-circuited: the pre-resolved job transitions to `execution_state = 'reused_prior_bootstrap'` and the existing KBEntry corpus is re-surfaced without re-crawling. No wallet debit occurs in this case either.

**Telemetry Events.**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `seller_onboarding_stage_entered` | `stage_2_sso_initiated_at` write | `{seller_org_id (nullable pre-SSO), invite_id, invite_source, bid_id, stage=2, elapsed_seconds_since_arrival, stage_outcome=completed}` |
| `seller_bootstrap_started` | `kb_bootstrap` job → `executing` | `{seller_org_id (nullable), invite_id, bootstrap_job_id, candidate_url_count, pre_arrival_state ∈ {complete, incomplete}}` |
| `seller_bootstrap_entry_synthesized` | Each KBEntry INSERT during Bootstrap | `{seller_org_id (nullable), bootstrap_job_id, kb_entry_id, confidence_score, source_url, category_id (nullable)}` (sampled at 1-in-10 to control PostHog volume) |
| `seller_bootstrap_completed` | `kb_bootstrap` job → `succeeded` or `partial` | `{seller_org_id, bootstrap_job_id, entry_count, partial=bool, stage_2_population_latency_ms, mean_confidence_score}` |
| `seller_bootstrap_failed` | `kb_bootstrap` job → `failed` | `{seller_org_id (nullable), bootstrap_job_id, failure_reason ∈ {firecrawl_outage, opus_capability_unavailable, domain_unresolvable, robots_txt_blocks_all, content_extraction_failure, timeout}}` |
| `seller_bootstrap_degraded_path_engaged` | Pre-arrival reservation failed; degraded path fires | `{seller_org_id (nullable), bootstrap_job_id, degradation_reason, degraded_url_budget, degraded_depth}` |
| `seller_sso_completed` | `stage_2_sso_completed_at` write | `{seller_org_id, invite_id, sso_provider ∈ {google, microsoft, magic_link_fallback}, elapsed_seconds_since_arrival, org_provisioning_outcome ∈ {new_org_created, existing_org_resolved, disambiguation_required}}` |

All events inherit Appendix G standard property set. `seller_bootstrap_entry_synthesized` is sampled at 1-in-10 to cap volume at p95 (10,000 sellers/day × 100 mean entries × 1 = 1M events/day uncapped → 100K/day sampled; Appendix G sampling convention).

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Firecrawl outage during Bootstrap.** `seller_bootstrap_failed {failure_reason='firecrawl_outage'}` emits; the Bootstrap job transitions to `failed`; the degraded-hero-moment UI engages per §48.8.3 failure mode 2 (banner: "Response drafting unavailable right now — your KB is ready and we'll notify you when drafts are available. Retry →"). The seller sees an honest explanation, NOT an empty workspace. On-call is paged per §4.4.22 AC 4 only if p90 Bootstrap-failure-rate exceeds 2% on a 15-minute window.
2. **Opus capability unavailable (Anthropic outage affecting Opus tier specifically).** `seller_bootstrap_failed {failure_reason='opus_capability_unavailable'}` emits; Bootstrap falls back to Sonnet tier with a `bootstrap_tier_downgraded` flag on the job; entry count tends lower (~30 instead of ~80) and mean confidence tends lower (~0.45 vs ~0.6). The seller still gets a populated KB Draft; the Hero Moment is degraded but not absent. C.140 requires Opus for the 40-entry target, so a Sonnet fallback is a documented soft-degradation, not a correct-tier execution.
3. **Seller's domain unresolvable (domain NXDOMAIN, robots.txt blocks all, or content extraction fails).** Bootstrap transitions to `failed` with `failure_reason = 'domain_unresolvable'` or `'robots_txt_blocks_all'` or `'content_extraction_failure'`. The Bid Workspace loads with KB-Draft-empty mode; the progress-storytelling screen ends with an honest message: "We couldn't pull content from yourcompany.com — you can still draft responses manually or paste content into the KB editor." No fake-progress status lines render for content we never pulled.
4. **Bootstrap contributes to Stage-3 population-latency threshold breach.** `hero_moment_latency_breached` emits per §48.8.3; on-call is paged per §4.4.22 AC 4 and §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 latency breach page SLA`. The session proceeds to Stage 3 regardless; `hero_moment_completed_at` is NOT populated; dashboards reflect the breach. Repeat breaches over the rolling window escalate per §42 severity ladder.
5. **Seller Org disambiguation required (email domain resolves to > 1 existing Seller Org).** `seller_sso_completed {org_provisioning_outcome='disambiguation_required'}` emits; the SSO callback renders the §4.4.22-failure-mode-10 disambiguation UI (list of matched Orgs with admin-contact info and a "I want to join this Org" flow). SellerOnboardingSession transitions to `errored` with `error_code = 'seller_org_disambiguation_required'`. Post-disambiguation, a new session row may be created (the original remains `errored` for funnel-leak analysis).
6. **Race: Bootstrap completes before SSO callback, KBEntries written with NULL `seller_org_id`.** This race is possible because Bootstrap runs in parallel with SSO; the mitigation is a `kb_entry_pending_seller_org_backfill` queue: KBEntry INSERTs with NULL `seller_org_id` are appended to this queue, and when SSO callback resolves, a batch UPDATE (≤ 200 rows per transaction) backfills `seller_org_id` atomically. Property test asserts that every KBEntry written during Bootstrap has `seller_org_id` non-NULL within 5 seconds of `stage_2_sso_completed_at`.
7. **Seller has already consumed the lifetime-free bootstrap allowance (returning seller).** Pre-resolved job short-circuits to `execution_state = 'reused_prior_bootstrap'`; existing KBEntries are re-surfaced; no new bootstrap runs. Stage 3 proceeds against the existing KB corpus. `seller_bootstrap_completed {partial=false, entry_count=existing_count}` emits.
8. **Bootstrap produces < 20 grounded chunks (insufficient for grounded First-Pass drafts).** Stage 3 retrieval subsystem signals "insufficient-grounding" instead of "ready-for-grounded-draft"; Stage 3 engages the degraded path: First-Pass drafts are emitted WITHOUT citations and flagged with `citation_mode='ungrounded'`. The seller sees drafts with an inline warning: "These drafts aren't grounded in your website yet — review carefully."

**Acceptance Criteria.**

8. Stage 2 bootstrap contribution MUST allow the overall Stage-3 population path to satisfy §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold` at p90 on the rolling window for the hero-path cohort (`invite_source ∈ {buyer_invite, ghost_bid_conversion, pro_trial_seat_m17}`); breach pages `ops_growth_admin` per §4.4.22 AC 4 and §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 latency breach page SLA`.
9. Bootstrap entry count MUST be ≥ 40 at p50 on the hero-path cohort (C.132 / §48.1.6 Indicator #3); regression below 35 at p50 raises a §42 P3.
10. Bootstrap mean confidence score MUST be ≥ 0.55 at p50 for Opus-tier bootstraps (Sonnet fallbacks excluded); regression below 0.50 raises a P3 and triggers a §34.7 capability-quality review.
11. `seller_bootstrap_completed` MUST include `partial=true` when `entry_count < 40` OR `mean_confidence_score < 0.50`; dashboards MUST treat `partial=true` as a degraded-Hero-Moment signal.
12. KBEntry rows written during Bootstrap MUST have `seller_org_id` backfilled within **5 seconds** of `stage_2_sso_completed_at` at p95; property test asserts across 10,000 randomized race scenarios.
13. The degraded path (Firecrawl outage, Opus unavailable, domain unresolvable, robots.txt blocks all) MUST render an honest progress-storytelling final status line AND MUST NOT display any status line referencing work that was never executed (AP7 — banned, enforced by §49.1.9 D-AP7).
14. `kb_bootstrap` invocation MUST NOT debit AIWallet; a property test asserts zero AIWallet rows debit during Bootstrap across 10,000 hero-path sessions.
15. Returning sellers who previously consumed the lifetime-free allowance MUST resume against the existing KB corpus without re-crawling; `execution_state = 'reused_prior_bootstrap'` MUST be observable in the Bootstrap job state; integration test asserts zero Firecrawl calls on second activation.

### 49.1.3 Stage 3: First-Pass Draft {#49.1.3-stage-3-first-pass-draft}

**Purpose.** Stage 3 executes `first_pass_responses` (Sonnet/Managed Agent tier per C.140) against the buyer's bid requirements, producing one first-pass response per requirement, each grounded (where KB coverage exists) in a specific KB entry with an inline citation. The engineering contract is that Stage 3 completes in concert with Stage 2 (both overlap on the SSO redirect window) and produces the populated Bid Workspace that the seller sees at Stage 4. The p90 target is sourced from §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold`; the requirement-coverage target is ≥ 85% grounded drafts on the hero-path cohort (drafts that cite at least one KB chunk).

**Authoritative Source.** Summary §6.28.2 Stage 3; Summary Summary §3.1b ¶3 (first-pass drafts with citations); §48.8.3 Workflow step 6; §21.4 capability registry — canonical ID `first_pass_responses` (Managed-Agent batch-of-100; Seller-Starter+ plan-gate; lifetime-allowance of 10 batches per C.140; registered at §21.4.2 row 3) and canonical ID `first_pass_rfp_draft` (per-requirement; Seller-Free plan-gate; `requires_managed_agent=false`; registered at §21.4.1.E per the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.3 D-EM-003 closure — the prior non-canonical alias `first_pass_response` (singular) was rewritten to canonical form at Phase 4.5 loose-ends closure 2026-05-19 per D-NOM-016 P2; legacy alias preserved as an `aliases` array entry on the §21.4.1.E row for SDK back-compat); §22.5 First-Pass RFP Draft workflow; §22.7 Citation Inline Card; §34.10.4 Seller Wallet $5 free allowance (for post-hero-moment `first_pass_rfp_draft` invocations after the 10-batch `first_pass_responses` lifetime-free allowance is exhausted and the seller falls back to the per-requirement Free-tier capability).

**Trigger / Entry Condition.** The §22.8 retrieval subsystem signals "ready-for-grounded-draft" (≥ 20 grounded chunks available) OR "insufficient-grounding" (degraded path, ungrounded drafts). This signal typically fires at T=15–30 s post-`stage_2_bootstrap_started_at`. If the bid has `bid_context_prefetched = true` (set during pre-arrival per §48.8.2), the invocation does not re-read the buyer's requirements from DB; it uses the pre-fetched row set.

**Workflow.**

1. **T=15–30 s: Retrieval-readiness signal.** §22.8 Indexing subsystem emits `retrieval_ready_for_bid {bid_id, seller_org_id, grounded_chunk_count}`. Stage 3 populator consumes this signal.
2. **T=20–30 s: Batch invocation of `first_pass_responses`.** Server invokes `first_pass_responses` capability (Sonnet tier per C.140) with: `{seller_org_id, bid_id, requirements[], grounded_chunks[], citation_mode ∈ {grounded, ungrounded}}`. Batch size is the full requirement list (typically 50–200 requirements per bid).
3. **T=30–90 s: Per-requirement drafts stream to Bid Workspace populator.** Each requirement's first-pass response is emitted as the Sonnet inference completes; drafts stream in (not a single terminal write). Each per-requirement draft includes: `requirement_id`, `draft_text`, `citation_chunk_ids[]` (empty when `citation_mode='ungrounded'` or when no KB chunk matches), `confidence_score ∈ [0.0, 1.0]`, `kb_gap_signal=bool` (true when the drafter's inference indicates a KB gap — "I don't see coverage of X in this KB").
4. **T=30–90 s: Bid Workspace population.** Each per-requirement draft → `BidResponse` row INSERT (§4.3.x entity) with `source = 'first_pass_draft'`, `state = 'draft_pending_review'`, `citation_ids = [kb_entry_id × N]`. AIOperation + Usage Event rows are written per-requirement.
5. **T=90 s: Stage 3 exit.** When all requirements have a BidResponse row (`state = 'draft_pending_review'`) OR `first_pass_responses` terminal state is reached (`succeeded`, `partial`, `failed`), the SellerOnboardingSession row is updated: `stage_3_bid_workspace_loaded_at = now()`; `stage_3_kb_draft_entry_count = N` (count of BidResponses); `stage_3_first_pass_response_requirement_count = total_requirements`; `stage_3_first_pass_response_cited_count = count_with_citations`; `stage_3_population_latency_ms = (now() - stage_2_bootstrap_started_at) * 1000`. `hero_moment_completed_at` is written if ALL of: (a) KB Draft present (`stage_2_bootstrap_entry_count >= 40`), (b) First-Pass present (`stage_3_first_pass_response_requirement_count > 0`), (c) Progress strip was rendered, (d) `stage_3_population_latency_ms` satisfies §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold`. If any condition fails, `hero_moment_completed_at` is NOT written; `hero_moment_latency_breached` emits; the workspace still loads (degraded Hero Moment).

**UX Surface Specification.** See §48.8.3 Workflow steps 5–8 and §48.8.3 UX Surface Specification (landing counter). §49.1 does NOT author the per-requirement card UX — it authors the data-plane contract. The per-requirement card UX is at §48.8.4.

**Data Read / Written.**

- **Read:** KBEntry rows with `review_state ∈ {pending_review, active}` (filtered to the seller's Org); KB embeddings from §22.8; Bid requirements (pre-fetched if `bid_context_prefetched=true`); capability registry entry for `first_pass_responses`.
- **Written:** BidResponse (INSERT, 50–200 rows with `source='first_pass_draft'`); AIOperation + Usage Event (one per requirement per invocation); SellerOnboardingSession `stage_3_*` timestamps and counters; `hero_moment_completed_at` (conditional).
- **Not written:** KBEntry (no new entries created at Stage 3; KB is read-only from Stage 3's perspective); AIWallet debits (first-pass-draft invocations inside the 10-batch lifetime-free allowance do not debit the wallet); Capability Declaration (deferred to Stage 5).

**Capabilities Invoked.** `first_pass_responses` (Sonnet; lifetime-free allowance of 10 batches per C.140; registered at §21.4.2 row 3). If the seller has already consumed all 10 batches (returning seller on 11th+ bid), per-requirement `first_pass_rfp_draft` (the canonical capability_id registered at §21.4.1.E per the v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.3 D-EM-003 closure — replacing the prior legacy alias `first_pass_response` (singular) per the D-NOM-016 P2 Phase 4.5 prose-hygiene rewrite 2026-05-19) invocations fire post-hero-moment against the Seller Wallet — but for Stage 3 during onboarding, the allowance is always available (first-ever bid). The invocation MUST use Sonnet tier (not Opus) per C.140 unless a feature flag `first_pass_responses_tier_override = 'opus'` is set by Ops for a specific experiment.

**AIWallet Debits.** None during the first-ever Stage 3 (batch 1 of 10 lifetime-free). Subsequent bids' Stage-3-equivalent invocations draw from the same 10-batch allowance until exhausted; after exhaustion, invocations route through the $5 free Seller Wallet allowance per §34.10.4 with cost-priced-rejected behavior on exhaustion (see §48.8.4 — NEVER hard-block).

**Telemetry Events.**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `seller_onboarding_stage_entered` | Retrieval-readiness signal | `{seller_org_id, invite_id, bid_id, stage=3, elapsed_seconds_since_arrival, stage_outcome=completed, retrieval_grounding_state ∈ {grounded, ungrounded}}` |
| `seller_first_pass_batch_started` | `first_pass_responses` invocation | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, requirements_count, grounded_chunk_count, citation_mode, tier ∈ {sonnet, opus_override}}` |
| `seller_first_pass_response_drafted` | Each BidResponse INSERT | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, requirement_id, bid_response_id, confidence_score, citation_count, kb_gap_signal}` (sampled 1-in-5) |
| `seller_first_pass_batch_completed` | `first_pass_responses` terminal state | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, requirements_count, drafted_count, grounded_count, kb_gap_signal_count, mean_confidence_score, batch_latency_ms, terminal_state ∈ {succeeded, partial, failed}}` |
| `hero_moment_completed` | `hero_moment_completed_at` write | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, stage_3_population_latency_ms, stage_3_kb_draft_entry_count, stage_3_first_pass_response_requirement_count, stage_3_first_pass_response_cited_count, capability_degradation_triggered}` (existing from §48.8.3) |
| `hero_moment_latency_breached` | §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold` breach | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, stage_3_population_latency_ms, threshold_ms}` where `threshold_ms` is sourced from §44.1 (existing from §48.8.3) |
| `first_pass_response_capability_degradation_triggered` | Stage 3 engages degraded path | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, degradation_kind ∈ {capability_unavailable, partial_draft_coverage, timeout}}` (existing from §48.8.3) |
| `seller_hero_moment_displayed` | Landing counter first paint | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, displayed_entry_count (N), displayed_citation_count (M), displayed_review_time_estimate_min (X), stage_3_population_latency_ms}` (NEW — §49.1 addition; distinct from `hero_moment_completed` which is a computation, this is the pixel-paint event) |

`seller_first_pass_response_drafted` is sampled at 1-in-5 per Appendix G sampling convention.

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **`first_pass_responses` capability unavailable (Anthropic Sonnet tier outage).** `first_pass_response_capability_degradation_triggered {degradation_kind='capability_unavailable'}` emits; the Bid Workspace loads with KB-Draft-only mode (drafts are absent from per-requirement cards; the "Draft with AI" button is disabled with tooltip "AI drafts are temporarily unavailable — try again in a few minutes"). The degraded-banner from §48.8.3 failure mode 2 renders. `hero_moment_completed_at` is NOT written.
2. **Partial draft coverage (`first_pass_responses` drafts some requirements but not others).** `first_pass_responses` terminal state is `partial`; BidResponses are INSERTed for drafted requirements; non-drafted requirements render with an empty state and the "Draft with AI" button (which fires `q_and_a_suggestion` per §48.8.4 on-demand). `first_pass_response_capability_degradation_triggered {degradation_kind='partial_draft_coverage'}` emits.
3. **Timeout: `first_pass_responses` batch exceeds 90-second budget.** The batch is terminated at the 90 s mark; any in-flight drafts are preserved; the batch terminal state is `partial`. The Bid Workspace loads with whatever drafts were completed. `first_pass_response_capability_degradation_triggered {degradation_kind='timeout'}` emits.
4. **Retrieval grounding insufficient (§49.1.2 failure mode 8).** `citation_mode='ungrounded'` on the invocation; drafts are emitted without citation_chunk_ids[]; each draft flagged with an `ungrounded_warning` attribute rendered inline on the per-requirement card (per §48.8.4 UX Surface).
5. **KB-gap signals exceed 50% of requirements.** This is a signal that the seller's domain is poorly represented in their KB for this buyer's bid (niche requirements, unusual framework). The BidWorkspace renders a top-banner: "Many of these requirements don't match your KB yet — rejecting with your own answer will build your KB as you go." This is an opportunity framing, not a hard-block.
6. **Bid has > 500 requirements (unusually large RFP).** `first_pass_responses` batch is split into 3-batch chunks of up to 170 requirements each; chunked batches run serially to avoid wallet-allowance misaccounting (still counts as 1 logical batch against the 10-batch allowance); total latency may exceed 90 s in which case AC 17 breach fires.
7. **Seller arrives via `invite_source='direct_signup'` with no bound bid.** Stage 3 is SKIPPED entirely; the workspace that loads is the general Seller Workspace (no bid, no first-pass drafts); SellerOnboardingSession `stage_3_*` fields remain NULL; `hero_moment_completed_at` cannot be written (hero path requires a bid). `invite_source='direct_signup'` sellers are NOT part of the hero-path cohort for activation-metric measurement (per §48.8.10 ACs 30–31 cohort scoping).

**Acceptance Criteria.**

16. `stage_3_population_latency_ms` MUST satisfy §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold` at p90 on the 15-minute rolling window for the hero-path cohort; breach pages `ops_growth_admin` per §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 latency breach page SLA`. (Cross-refs §4.4.22 AC 4, §48.8.3 AC 7.)
17. `first_pass_responses` batch latency MUST be ≤ 90 seconds per batch at p95; timeout at 90 s with `terminal_state='partial'` is the documented fallback; CI load test asserts.
18. Grounded-draft coverage MUST be ≥ 85% at p50 on hero-path cohort (85% of drafts include ≥ 1 citation_chunk_id); regression below 75% raises a §34.7 capability-quality review.
19. `seller_hero_moment_displayed` MUST fire within **500 ms** of Bid Workspace first paint at p95; the rendered counter values (N, M, X) MUST derive from SellerOnboardingSession columns (no hardcoded or aspirational values — AP violation of "fake-progress" if detected; §49.1.9 D-AP7 detector).
20. `hero_moment_completed_at` MUST be written only when ALL four conditions are met: KB Draft (`stage_2_bootstrap_entry_count >= 40`), First-Pass present, Progress strip rendered, `stage_3_population_latency_ms` satisfies §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold`. Property test asserts across 10,000 randomized stage-boundary scenarios.
21. Ungrounded drafts MUST render the `ungrounded_warning` inline attribute on the per-requirement card; UX-snapshot test asserts presence for every BidResponse with `citation_ids = []`.
22. KB-gap-signal banner MUST render when > 50% of requirements emit `kb_gap_signal=true`; integration test asserts banner presence at 51% threshold.
23. `direct_signup` sellers MUST NOT have `hero_moment_completed_at` written (no bid context); property test asserts.

### 49.1.4 Stage 4: Landing Screen ("Your bid is ready") {#49.1.4-stage-4-landing-screen-your-bid-is-ready}

**Purpose.** Stage 4 is the first moment the seller sees the Bid Workspace. The landing screen is the honest-accounting paint of the Hero Moment: it shows the seller what Sourcera built during Stages 2–3 (N drafts prepared, M grounded in citations, X minutes estimated review), with zero upgrade CTAs, zero pricing prompts, zero modal interruptions. The engineering contract is that SellerOnboardingSession tracks the elapsed time from `stage_1_arrival_at` to `stage_3_first_edit_at`, and that the landing screen's displayed numbers derive from SellerOnboardingSession columns (never hardcoded). The Stage-4-to-Stage-5 transition is `stage_3_first_edit_at` — the first click on any Accept / Edit / Reject button.

**Authoritative Source.** Summary §6.28.2 Stage 4; §48.8.3 Workflow step 7 (landing counter); §48.8.3 UX Surface Specification (landing counter specification); §48.8.7 AP6 (banned: "Pricing page shown before the vendor submits their first bid" — Stage 4 is pre-first-bid); §48.8.7 AP1 (banned: credit card requested before upgrade-intent click); §48.8.7 AP4 (banned: upgrade-intent redirect to external pricing during onboarding).

**Trigger / Entry Condition.** `stage_3_bid_workspace_loaded_at` is written on SellerOnboardingSession (i.e., the Stage-3-exit transition has fired).

**Workflow.**

1. **T=0: Bid Workspace first paint.** The client-side router resolves to the Bid Workspace route. The server has served the populated BidResponses, the KBEntry corpus (preview subset), and the SellerOnboardingSession row (with all `stage_3_*` columns populated).
2. **T=0–500 ms: Landing counter render.** The landing counter reads from SellerOnboardingSession columns: `N = stage_3_first_pass_response_requirement_count`, `M = stage_3_first_pass_response_cited_count`, `X = median_review_time_estimate_from_cohort`. Render: *"Your bid is ready. **[N]** AI drafts prepared. **[M]** cite evidence from your website. Review time: **~[X] min**."* No "upgrade" CTA. No "free trial" modal. No "pricing" link. A small X-close button allows the seller to dismiss the counter; dismiss writes `stage_3_landing_counter_dismissed_at` on SellerOnboardingSession. `seller_hero_moment_displayed` event fires.
3. **T=500 ms–2 s: First-paint observability assertion.** A client-side heartbeat posts to `/onboarding/landing-paint-confirm` with `{session_id, first_paint_ms, counter_rendered=bool, counter_values_match_session_row=bool}`. The `counter_values_match_session_row` check is a client-side integrity assertion — if the rendered values don't match the SellerOnboardingSession row, AP-fake-progress (AP7) is flagged and the session is surfaced to Ops via the `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation {kind='ap7_fake_progress'}` event.
4. **T=2 s–3 min: Landing dwell.** The seller reads the workspace. The AIWallet counter renders top-right (§48.8.4 UX). The requirement cards render one per row. No modal, tooltip, or overlay pressures the seller. The ambient-motion of the AIWallet counter (200 ms crossfade on debit) is reserved for in-workspace actions, not onboarding pressure.
5. **T=first click on Accept/Edit/Reject: Stage-5 entry.** `stage_3_first_edit_at = now()` is written. Stage 5 begins.

**UX Surface Specification.** See §48.8.3 UX Surface Specification (landing counter); §48.8.4 UX Surface Specification (per-requirement card — relevant here as the dormant state before first click). §49.1 does NOT author the UX — it authors the data-plane contract. The landing counter's visual treatment (token, typography, position) is at §48.8.3; §49.1 enforces only the data-derivation contract (AP7 — values MUST derive from session row).

**Data Read / Written.**

- **Read:** SellerOnboardingSession (all `stage_3_*` columns); BidResponse rows; KBEntry rows; AIWallet balance; median_review_time_estimate_from_cohort (read from a §4.4.x rollup that aggregates `activation_metric_elapsed_seconds - stage_1_arrival_to_first_edit_seconds` on the trailing 30-day hero-path cohort, k=5 anonymized per §4.4.22).
- **Written:** `stage_3_landing_counter_dismissed_at` (on counter X-close, optional); `stage_3_first_edit_at` (on first Accept/Edit/Reject click — Stage 5 entry).
- **Not written:** Any KBEntry / BidResponse state change; AIOperation (Stage 4 performs no AI inference); AIWallet debits.

**Capabilities Invoked.** None. Stage 4 is a paint-only stage; no inference runs.

**AIWallet Debits.** None.

**Telemetry Events.**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `seller_onboarding_stage_entered` | `stage_3_bid_workspace_loaded_at` write (same instant as Stage-3-exit; Stage 4 entry is the paint event) | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, stage=4, elapsed_seconds_since_arrival, stage_outcome=completed}` |
| `seller_hero_moment_displayed` | Landing counter first paint | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, displayed_entry_count (N), displayed_citation_count (M), displayed_review_time_estimate_min (X), first_paint_ms, counter_values_match_session_row=bool}` (NEW) |
| `seller_landing_counter_dismissed` | Seller clicks counter X-close | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, dismiss_elapsed_seconds_from_paint}` |
| `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation` | AP7 client-side integrity check fails | `{kind='ap7_fake_progress', seller_org_id, bid_id, displayed_values, session_row_values}` |

**Failure Modes Addressed.**
