1. **Landing counter values mismatch SellerOnboardingSession row (AP7 — fake progress).** Client-side integrity check emits `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation {kind='ap7_fake_progress'}`; Ops dashboard surfaces within 60 s; §49.1.9 D-AP7 CI detector runs on every PR and fails the build on any client-side hardcoded or aspirational value.
2. **Seller dismisses counter immediately (< 2 s from paint).** Legitimate; `seller_landing_counter_dismissed` emits with `dismiss_elapsed_seconds_from_paint < 2`; no adverse effect. Ops dashboards surface an X% dismissal rate; a sudden spike (> 40% on 24h window) raises a P3 for UX review.
3. **Seller hits browser back button from landing screen.** SellerOnboardingSession remains `in_progress`; back navigation is benign (returns to the progress-storytelling screen or to the buyer's invite page depending on router history). On re-forward, the session resumes at Stage 4 without re-running Stages 2–3.
4. **Stage 4 paint exceeds 500 ms (P95 breach).** `seller_hero_moment_displayed {first_paint_ms > 500}` emits; tracked as UI-performance signal; regression > 15% on 24h raises a P3.
5. **Rollup `median_review_time_estimate_from_cohort` is unavailable (cold start, k < 5 cohort).** `X` falls back to a static default of 15 minutes (documented in a §4.4.x configuration row); display uses "~" prefix to signal estimation. No adverse effect on activation metric.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

24. Landing counter values (N, M, X) MUST derive from SellerOnboardingSession columns — NEVER hardcoded, NEVER aspirational; the AP7 client-side integrity check and CI detector D-AP7 assert this on every build.
25. Landing counter render MUST complete within **500 ms** of Bid Workspace first paint at p95.
26. Zero upgrade CTAs, zero pricing prompts, zero credit-card-collection surfaces, zero external pricing redirects, and zero modal interruptions MAY render during Stage 4 (AP1 / AP4 / AP6 enforcement — Stage 4 is dormant pre-first-bid and pre-upgrade-intent, so the canonical "upsell-during-active-bid-work" ban AP2 is not yet applicable at this stage); §49.1.9 D-AP1, D-AP4, and D-AP6 CI detectors assert on every build.
27. `stage_3_first_edit_at` MUST be written atomically on the first Accept/Edit/Reject click across the whole Bid Workspace; property test asserts across 10,000 randomized click orderings that only the FIRST click writes the timestamp (subsequent clicks are no-op on this column).

### 49.1.5 Stage 5: In-Workspace Review {#49.1.5-stage-5-in-workspace-review}

**Purpose.** Stage 5 is the per-requirement review flow — inline citations (§22.7), Accept / Edit / Reject actions per-requirement, a KB-gap detector (§22.6) that converts every Reject into a new KBEntry, and a live AIWallet counter that updates on every debit within 2 s. The engineering contract is that each interaction settles an AIOperation (§34.6), accretes KB (accepts and rejects both), and moves the seller toward the first-requirement-response signal — the THE activation-metric event. Stage 5 ends when the seller submits the whole bid (`first_bid_submitted_at`).

**Authoritative Source.** Summary §6.28.2 Stage 5; §48.8.4 (the primary authoring of this stage's surface — §49.1.5 is the engineering-contract companion, not a restatement); §22.6 KB-Gap Detector; §22.7 Citation Inline Card; §34.6 Outcome Resolver; §34.11 Value-price vs Cost-price settlement contract; C.135 (Seller Activation Metric).

**Trigger / Entry Condition.** `stage_3_first_edit_at` is written on SellerOnboardingSession.

**Workflow.**

The Stage 5 workflow is fully authored at §48.8.4 Workflow steps 1–9. §49.1.5 does NOT re-author the workflow; it adds the stage-boundary engineering contracts below.

1. **Stage 5 entry contract.** On `stage_3_first_edit_at` write, the SellerOnboardingSession row transitions logically from Stage 4 to Stage 5 (no state-machine column, just a timestamp chain). The AIWallet balance is snapshotted at this moment as `stage_5_entry_aiwallet_balance_cents`; the snapshot enables Stage 7 debrief math ("you used $X during this bid").
2. **First-requirement-response write.** The first Accept / Edit / Reject interaction that transitions a BidResponse to `submitted_for_bid` writes `first_requirement_response_at` on SellerOnboardingSession. Inside the same transaction, `activation_metric_elapsed_seconds` is computed as `(first_requirement_response_at - stage_1_arrival_at).total_seconds()`. Property test asserts monotonicity (`first_requirement_response_at > stage_1_arrival_at`) across 10,000 randomized timelines. (Cross-refs §48.8.4 AC 16.)
3. **Stage 5 exit contract.** When the seller clicks "Submit Bid" on the workspace summary, the server validates all BidResponses are in `submitted_for_bid` state (or exempt per the bid's rubric), transitions the Bid to `submitted`, and writes `first_bid_submitted_at` on SellerOnboardingSession. `completion_state = 'activated'` is written atomically inside the same transaction. Stage 6 entry is this timestamp.

**UX Surface Specification.** Fully authored at §48.8.4 UX Surface Specification. §49.1.5 adds: the AIWallet snapshot (`stage_5_entry_aiwallet_balance_cents`) is NOT rendered to the seller; it is a server-side column used for Stage 7 debrief math.

**Data Read / Written.**

- **Read:** BidResponse rows; KBEntry rows; AIWallet balance; `rubric_exemption_allowlist` (per-bid column controlling which requirements are optional).
- **Written:** BidResponse state transitions (`draft_pending_review` → `submitted_for_bid` OR `submitted_for_bid_after_edit` OR `rejected_and_kb_authored`); KBEntry state transitions on accept (`pending_review` → `active`); new KBEntry INSERTs on reject (source='q_and_a_onboarding_rejection'); AIOperation + Usage Event per interaction; SellerOnboardingSession `stage_5_entry_aiwallet_balance_cents` (write-once on Stage 5 entry), `first_requirement_response_at`, `activation_metric_elapsed_seconds`, `first_bid_submitted_at`, `completion_state='activated'`.

**Capabilities Invoked.** `first_pass_response` (per-requirement settlement finalization on Accept / Edit); `q_and_a_suggestion` (on-demand for empty requirements); `kb_to_capability_suggestion` (background, fires at first-bid-submitted — Stage 6 start signal); `page_enrichment` is NOT invoked at Stage 5 (it fires at Stage 5 exit / Stage 6 entry when Seller Profile publishes per §48.8.4).

**AIWallet Debits.** Per-interaction settlement per §34.6 — Accepted interactions settle value-priced (cost_base × 10); Edited interactions with ≥ 50% retained settle value-priced; Edited with < 50% retained settle cost-priced-rejected; Rejected interactions settle cost-priced-rejected. §48.8.4 AIWallet Debits block authors the exhaustive semantics; §49.1.5 defers to it.

**Telemetry Events.**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `seller_onboarding_stage_entered` | `stage_3_first_edit_at` write | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, stage=5, elapsed_seconds_since_arrival, stage_outcome=completed}` |
| `seller_first_requirement_response` | `first_requirement_response_at` write | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, requirement_id, activation_metric_elapsed_seconds, response_mode ∈ {accept, edit, reject_and_kb_entry}}` (NEW — canonical short form; semantically equivalent to §48.8.4 `seller_onboarding_first_requirement_response` which is aliased; see §49.1 reconciliation log) |
| `aioperation.settled` | Per-interaction settlement | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, requirement_id, capability_id, settlement_state ∈ {accepted, cost_priced_rejected}, amount_cents}` (existing) |
| `kb_entry.accepted` | KBEntry → active on Accept / Edit | `{seller_org_id, kb_entry_id, source, confidence_score_at_creation, bid_id}` (existing) |
| `kb_entry.q_and_a_onboarding_created` | KBEntry INSERT on Reject | `{seller_org_id, kb_entry_id, requirement_id, bid_id}` (existing from §48.8.4) |
| `seller_aiwallet_budget_exhausted_during_onboarding` | AIWallet hits $0 during Stage 5 | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, requirements_remaining_for_draft, cost_priced_rejected_cents_accumulated}` (existing from §48.8.4) |

**Failure Modes Addressed.** Authored at §48.8.4 Failure Modes. §49.1.5 adds:

7. **Stage 5 entry AIWallet snapshot write failure (DB error on snapshot column).** The `stage_5_entry_aiwallet_balance_cents` snapshot is a soft write — if it fails, Stage 5 proceeds; Stage 7 debrief falls back to computing `stage_5_entry_aiwallet_balance_cents = sum(aioperation.settled.amount_cents WHERE seller_org_id=X AND bid_id=Y)` at debrief time. Acceptable degradation.
8. **Seller completes all requirements but never clicks Submit.** Session remains `activated`; `first_bid_submitted_at` is NULL; `first_requirement_response_at` is set. The §4.4.22 post-activation churn classifier owns the inactivity window and transitions the session to `churned_post_activation` when it qualifies; this is distinct from pre-activation `abandoned`.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

28. `first_requirement_response_at` write MUST compute `activation_metric_elapsed_seconds` inside the same transaction; property test asserts monotonicity across 10,000 randomized timelines. (Cross-refs §48.8.4 AC 16.)
29. `stage_5_entry_aiwallet_balance_cents` snapshot MUST be written within the same transaction as `stage_3_first_edit_at`; a soft-failure on snapshot MUST NOT block Stage 5 entry (Stage 7 debrief will re-compute on demand).
30. Activation Metric p50 MUST be < 20 minutes on the 30-day rolling window for the hero-path cohort (C.135); regression > 10% (p50 > 22 min) raises §42 P2. (Cross-refs §48.8.10 AC 30.)
31. Activation Metric p90 MUST be < 60 minutes on the 30-day rolling window for the hero-path cohort (C.135); regression > 10% (p90 > 66 min) raises §42 P2. (Cross-refs §48.8.10 AC 31.)
32. Stage 5 exit (`first_bid_submitted_at` write) MUST write `completion_state='activated'` atomically inside the same transaction; property test asserts across 10,000 randomized submission scenarios that the two writes are never split.
33. `seller_first_requirement_response` event MUST be emittable under BOTH canonical short form (§49.1.5) AND legacy long form (`seller_onboarding_first_requirement_response` per §48.8.4); PostHog-funnel tests for both funnel definitions MUST resolve to the same underlying SellerOnboardingSession row. (See Appendix G alias registration.)

### 49.1.6 Stage 6: First Bid Submission {#49.1.6-stage-6-first-bid-submission}

**Purpose.** Stage 6 is the bid-submission transition AND the Stake-Reveal Screen render. The engineering contract is that Stage 6 publishes the Seller Profile (if not yet published), fires `kb_to_capability_suggestion` to propose Capability Declarations from the KB accreted during Stages 2–5, and renders the Stake-Reveal Screen with honest-accounting numbers derived from SellerOnboardingSession + AIOperation aggregates. The stake-reveal copy is prescribed by §48.8.5; §49.1.6 authors the data-plane contract.

**Authoritative Source.** Summary §6.28.2 Stage 6; §48.8.5 (the primary authoring of this stage's Stake-Reveal surface); Summary §3.6 ¶4; Summary Summary §3.1b ¶3 (stake-reveal copy); C.132 stake-reveal; §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stake-Reveal dwell target`.

**Trigger / Entry Condition.** `first_bid_submitted_at` is written on SellerOnboardingSession (Stage 5 exit).

**Workflow.**

1. **T=0: Stake-Reveal Screen render.** The Bid Workspace transitions to the Stake-Reveal Screen. `stage_5_stake_reveal_rendered_at = now()` is written on SellerOnboardingSession. (Note: the column is named `stage_5_*` for historical reasons — at column-naming time the stage-boundary mapping was coarser; §49.1.1 table authors the Stage 6 mapping; §4.4.22 column names are preserved for schema stability.)
2. **T=0–500 ms: Stake-Reveal values computation.** Server computes: `N_kb_entries_accreted = count(KBEntry WHERE seller_org_id=X AND created_at BETWEEN stage_1_arrival_at AND first_bid_submitted_at)`; `Y_value_priced_cents_accumulated = sum(AIOperation.amount_cents WHERE settlement_state='accepted' AND bid_id=Y)`; `X_activation_minutes = activation_metric_elapsed_seconds / 60`. These three values populate the stake-reveal copy per §48.8.5.
3. **T=0–2 s: `kb_to_capability_suggestion` background invocation.** Server enqueues a `kb_to_capability_suggestion` capability invocation with `{seller_org_id, kb_entry_ids[]}` — asynchronous, does NOT block the Stake-Reveal paint. The capability proposes up to 10 Capability Declarations with `inferred_capability_name`, `source_kb_entry_ids[]`, `confidence_score`. Proposals land in the Seller Profile Capability Declarations list as `review_state='pending_review'`.
4. **T=0–2 s: Seller Profile first-publication.** If the Seller Profile is not yet published (first-bid-ever flow), the server publishes it with: `published_at = now()`, `capability_declarations = []` (the pending-review proposals from step 3 do NOT auto-publish), `kb_size = N_kb_entries_accreted`. `page_enrichment` capability fires to enrich the public profile content (e.g., summary blurb, hero image).
5. **T=2 s–hour+: Stake-Reveal dwell.** The seller reads the Stake-Reveal Screen. No upgrade CTA. No pricing prompt. No modal. A single secondary CTA ("Return to my workspace") routes back to the Seller Workspace home; a second CTA ("View my Seller Profile") opens the published profile in a new tab.
6. **Stage 6 exit.** Stage 6 ends when the seller navigates away from the Stake-Reveal Screen (any route transition), sends the `beforeunload` heartbeat, or idles long enough for server-side recovery. The server writes `stage_6_exit_at = now()` and `stage_7_entered_at = now()` atomically, then emits `stake_reveal_dwell_completed`. If the tab closes before the heartbeat reaches the server, the idle-recovery worker backfills both timestamps on next session resume.

**UX Surface Specification.** Fully authored at §48.8.5 UX Surface Specification. §49.1.6 adds: the computed values (N, Y, X) MUST derive from DB aggregates — NEVER hardcoded, NEVER cached past the Stake-Reveal render. The AP7 (fake-progress) detector applies to the Stake-Reveal Screen just as to the Stage 4 landing counter.

**Data Read / Written.**

- **Read:** SellerOnboardingSession (`stage_1_arrival_at`, `activation_metric_elapsed_seconds`, `stage_5_entry_aiwallet_balance_cents`); KBEntry (count during session window); AIOperation (aggregate `amount_cents` WHERE `settlement_state='accepted'`); Seller Profile; Capability Declaration registry.
- **Written:** SellerOnboardingSession `stage_5_stake_reveal_rendered_at` (note preserved column naming), `stage_6_exit_at`, and `stage_7_entered_at`; Seller Profile `published_at` (first-bid-ever flow); Capability Declaration proposals (async, may land after Stake-Reveal first paint); AIOperation + Usage Event for `kb_to_capability_suggestion` and `page_enrichment` invocations.

**Capabilities Invoked.** `kb_to_capability_suggestion` (background, async after Stake-Reveal paint); `page_enrichment` (Seller Profile enrichment, async after Stake-Reveal paint).

**AIWallet Debits.** `kb_to_capability_suggestion` and `page_enrichment` invocations consume from the Seller Wallet's $5 free allowance (§34.10.4) if still available; on exhaustion, cost-priced-rejected settlement. Neither capability hard-blocks the Stake-Reveal paint.

**Telemetry Events.**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `seller_onboarding_stage_entered` | `first_bid_submitted_at` write (same instant as Stage 5 exit; Stage 6 entry is the submission event) | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, stage=6, elapsed_seconds_since_arrival, stage_outcome=completed}` |
| `seller_first_bid_submitted` | `first_bid_submitted_at` write | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, total_requirements, accept_count, edit_count, reject_count, activation_metric_elapsed_seconds}` (NEW — canonical short form; semantically equivalent to §48.8.4 `seller_onboarding_first_bid_submitted` which is aliased) |
| `stake_reveal_rendered` | `stage_5_stake_reveal_rendered_at` write | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, N_kb_entries_accreted, Y_value_priced_cents_accumulated, X_activation_minutes, first_paint_ms, counter_values_match_aggregates=bool}` (existing from §48.8.5) |
| `seller_profile_first_published` | Seller Profile publication (first-bid-ever flow) | `{seller_org_id, profile_id, kb_size_at_publish, capability_declaration_proposal_count (after kb_to_capability_suggestion completes)}` |
| `stake_reveal_dwell_completed` | After the atomic `stage_6_exit_at` / `stage_7_entered_at` transaction commits | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, stage_6_exit_at, stage_7_entered_at, dwell_seconds}` |

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **`kb_to_capability_suggestion` unavailable at Stage 6.** Capability invocation fails; Stake-Reveal paint proceeds unaffected. The Seller Profile publishes with `capability_declarations = []`. A retry job runs on a 6-hour schedule; proposals land asynchronously into the seller's Profile edit flow.
2. **`page_enrichment` fails at Stage 6.** Profile publishes with minimal content (name, kb_size, empty summary); a retry job runs. Graceful degradation.
3. **Seller closes tab before Stake-Reveal first paint.** `stage_5_stake_reveal_rendered_at` is NOT written; session remains with `completion_state='activated'` (activation was achieved at Stage 5 exit). Stake-Reveal dwell signal is absent but activation metric is intact.
4. **AIWallet cost-priced-rejected for `kb_to_capability_suggestion` (wallet exhausted).** Proposal generation still runs at cost-priced-rejected settlement (cost_base × 1.05 accounting entry, no seller charge); the proposals land with full fidelity; the seller is not aware of the cost-priced-rejected settlement (it's internal accounting).
5. **Stake-Reveal computed values fail integrity check (AP7 — computed value doesn't match DB aggregate).** `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation {kind='ap7_fake_progress', surface='stake_reveal'}` emits; Ops surfaced within 60 s.

**Acceptance Criteria.**

34. Stake-Reveal Screen values (N_kb_entries_accreted, Y_value_priced_cents_accumulated, X_activation_minutes) MUST derive from DB aggregates — NEVER hardcoded, NEVER cached past the paint; §49.1.9 D-AP7 detector asserts on every build.
35. Stake-Reveal first paint MUST complete within **1 second** of `first_bid_submitted_at` at p95.
36. `kb_to_capability_suggestion` MUST be enqueued within **500 ms** of Stake-Reveal paint; invocation failures MUST NOT block the Stake-Reveal paint.
37. Seller Profile first publication MUST complete within **2 seconds** of Stake-Reveal paint at p95 on the first-bid-ever flow; failures gracefully degrade to minimal-content profile.
38. Stake-Reveal dwell-time MUST satisfy §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stake-Reveal dwell target`.

### 49.1.7 Stage 7: Post-Submission Debrief {#49.1.7-stage-7-post-submission-debrief}

**Purpose.** Stage 7 begins the moment the seller leaves the Stake-Reveal Screen and extends through the eventual bid outcome (win / loss / phase-lapsed). The engineering contract is that Stage 7 is the transition from the onboarding loop into the steady-state Seller Console, AND — when the bid resolves — the surface for the Win/Loss Debrief that C.137 identifies as the first upgrade trigger. The debrief is NOT an upgrade wall; it is a consequence-narration moment that naturally surfaces "what you'd need to do differently next time" and, when appropriate, "this insight is gated on Pro."

**Authoritative Source.** Summary §6.28.2 Stage 7; C.137 (Win/Loss Debrief as upgrade trigger); §48.7 (M14 — Ghost-Bid Conversion / Win-Loss Debrief authoring); §48.1.7 (Four Seller Conversion Moments — definitional binding); §48.8.6 (Four Seller Conversion Moments UX Surface); C.139 (Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee — important to reference at any upgrade moment in Stage 7).

**Trigger / Entry Condition.** Seller navigates away from the Stake-Reveal Screen (Stage 6 exit). Stage 7 continues until one of the following terminal conditions: (a) bid resolves win → `stage_7_win_debrief_rendered_at`; (b) bid resolves loss → `stage_7_loss_debrief_rendered_at`; (c) bid phase-lapses without resolution → `stage_7_phase_lapsed_at`; (d) seller churns → `completion_state='churned_post_activation'` via the §4.4.22 post-activation churn classifier.

**Workflow.**

1. **T=0: Stake-Reveal exit.** Seller navigates away. Stage 7 begins. SellerOnboardingSession `stage_6_exit_at = now()` and `stage_7_entered_at = now()` are written in the same transaction.
2. **T=hours–days: KB compounding passive signals.** The seller's KB continues to accumulate passive signals: (a) accepted-but-unreviewed KBEntries are eligible for promotion after a 7-day soak; (b) Capability Declaration proposals from Stage 6 land in the Profile edit flow and await seller review; (c) the §48.7 Ghost-Bid mechanic may surface additional invites targeting the seller's new profile.
3. **T=bid-closes-for-all-vendors: Win/Loss Debrief render trigger.** When the buyer resolves the bid (selects a winner, rejects all, or phase-lapses), the Seller Console sends a notification (§41 email + in-app) to the seller. Notification includes a link to the Win/Loss Debrief screen.
4. **T=seller-clicks-debrief-link: Debrief render.** The Debrief screen renders at §48.7 authoring (M14). For WIN: confetti animation (subtle), "You won this bid" headline, next-steps prompt (legal handoff, onboarding-the-customer flow). For LOSS: honest narration, "You scored Y/10 on these requirements — here's where the winning vendor scored higher." This comparative insight is the C.137 upgrade hook: Free-tier sellers see up to 3 requirement-level insights; Pro-tier sellers see all. `stage_7_win_debrief_rendered_at` or `stage_7_loss_debrief_rendered_at` is written.
5. **T=debrief-upgrade-trigger: Conversion Moment (if applicable).** The loss-debrief can lead into one of the four Seller Conversion Moments (§48.1.7) when its trigger predicates are independently satisfied. If the seller meets Conversion-Moment conditions (e.g., first loss AND KB has grown past the plan-relative threshold), a discoverable upgrade link renders inline on the debrief — but NOT a modal, NOT a wall. §48.8.6 authors the UX surface; §49.1.7 authors only the trigger contract.
6. **T=days-weeks: Plan progression or churn.** The seller either (a) converts to a paid plan, (b) continues on Free tier drawing on the KB they accreted, or (c) churns. The §4.4.22 post-activation churn classifier owns the inactivity threshold and transitions the session to `churned_post_activation` when it qualifies.

**UX Surface Specification.** The Win/Loss Debrief screen is authored at §48.7 (M14). The Conversion-Moment link surface is authored at §48.8.6. §49.1.7 does NOT author UX; it authors the trigger and persistence contracts.

**Data Read / Written.**

- **Read:** SellerOnboardingSession (terminal state); Bid (for resolution outcome); Requirement-level scoring (for loss debrief); Capability Declaration proposals; Plan entitlements (for insight-gating).
- **Written:** SellerOnboardingSession `stage_6_exit_at`, `stage_7_entered_at`, `stage_7_win_debrief_rendered_at` or `stage_7_loss_debrief_rendered_at` or `stage_7_phase_lapsed_at`, `completion_state` terminal transition (from `activated` / `reactivated` → `churned_post_activation` via §4.4.22 post-activation churn classifier, OR `activated` remains stable for active sellers).

**Capabilities Invoked.** `win_loss_insight_synthesis` (Authored Extension — new capability at §21.4, flagged in reconciliation log); `page_enrichment` for passive Seller Profile updates; `kb_to_capability_suggestion` for ongoing KB → Capability inference as the KB grows.

**AIWallet Debits.** All Stage 7 invocations draw from the Seller Wallet per §34.10 normal-settlement rules (no lifetime-free allowance applies post-activation). `win_loss_insight_synthesis` is value-priced on acceptance (seller engages with the insight) and cost-priced-rejected otherwise.

**Telemetry Events.**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `seller_onboarding_stage_entered` | Stake-Reveal exit | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, stage=7, elapsed_seconds_since_arrival, stage_outcome=completed}` |
| `seller_onboarding_completed` | Stage 7 entry | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, completion_state='activated', activation_metric_elapsed_seconds, kb_size_at_completion, aiwallet_cents_consumed, capabilities_declared_count, stages_completed=[1,2,3,4,5,6,7]}` (NEW) |
| `seller_win_debrief_rendered` | `stage_7_win_debrief_rendered_at` write | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, days_from_submission_to_win, insight_count_shown, plan_tier_at_debrief}` |
| `seller_loss_debrief_rendered` | `stage_7_loss_debrief_rendered_at` write | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, days_from_submission_to_loss, insight_count_shown, insight_count_gated, plan_tier_at_debrief, conversion_moment_link_rendered}` |
| `seller_phase_lapsed_debrief_rendered` | `stage_7_phase_lapsed_at` write | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, days_from_submission_to_lapse, plan_tier_at_debrief}` |
| `conversion_moment_triggered` | Conversion-Moment link renders on loss debrief | `{seller_org_id, bid_id, moment_kind='loss_debrief_insight_gate', plan_tier_at_trigger, kb_size_at_trigger}` (§48.1.7 binding) |
| `seller_churned_post_activation` | §4.4.22 post-activation churn classifier fires | `{seller_org_id, last_activity_at, days_since_last_activity, final_completion_state='churned_post_activation'}` |

**Failure Modes Addressed.**

1. **Bid never resolves (buyer never closes the phase).** `stage_7_phase_lapsed_at` is written at the bid-workspace-phase-timeout sweep (§10.14 — Bid Workspace Cancellation Protocol) with `lapsed_reason='phase_timeout'`. A debrief renders with "The buyer didn't complete this bid — your KB still grew" framing. No upgrade pressure.
2. **Seller opts out of debrief emails.** Notification does not fire; Stage 7 debrief is still accessible via in-app inbox (per §41 opt-out respects email channel, not in-app). Seller engagement with debrief becomes opt-in via in-app only.
3. **`win_loss_insight_synthesis` capability unavailable at debrief-render time.** Debrief still renders with basic scoring summary (no synthesized insights); a banner indicates "Detailed insights are being generated — we'll notify you when ready." Retry job runs on 1-hour schedule.
4. **Seller converts to a paid plan during debrief (Conversion-Moment hit).** Plan upgrade flow runs per §34 Plans & Billing. Per C.139 Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee, the seller's KB and settings carry over intact; no data migration needed. `conversion_moment_converted {moment_kind='loss_debrief_insight_gate'}` emits (§48.7 M17 measurement).
5. **Loss debrief would show gated insights but seller is already on Pro-equivalent plan.** No Conversion-Moment link renders; all insights unlock; `conversion_moment_link_rendered=false` in the event properties. (Prevents AP8-adjacent behavior of showing upgrade pressure to already-upgraded sellers.)

**Acceptance Criteria.**

39. Stage 7 terminal states (`stage_7_win_debrief_rendered_at`, `stage_7_loss_debrief_rendered_at`, `stage_7_phase_lapsed_at`) MUST be mutually exclusive on a single SellerOnboardingSession row; DB constraint asserts at most one is non-NULL before terminal resolution and exactly one is non-NULL after a debrief terminal path fires.
40. `seller_onboarding_completed` event MUST fire exactly once per SellerOnboardingSession row with `completion_state='activated'`; idempotency key on `(seller_org_id, session_id)` asserts across 10,000 randomized re-emissions.
41. Loss Debrief MUST gate Pro-tier insights on plan entitlement (§5.11 Feature Access Matrix); a property test asserts that Free-tier sellers see exactly ≤ 3 insights AND that Pro-tier sellers see ALL insights; no skew in either direction.
42. Conversion-Moment link on loss debrief MUST NOT render for sellers already at Pro-tier-or-higher; integration test asserts.
43. Staleness-sweep transition to `churned_post_activation` MUST respect the canonical §4.4.22 post-activation churn classifier; property test asserts across 10,000 randomized activity timelines.
44. `win_loss_insight_synthesis` capability unavailability MUST NOT block debrief render; graceful degradation is authored above.

### 49.1.8 Progress Storytelling UX Implementation {#49.1.8-progress-storytelling-ux-implementation}

**Purpose.** §49.1.8 is the engineering contract for the progress-storytelling screen rendered during Stages 2–3 (minutes 0–3). The UX surface is authored at §48.8.3; §49.1.8 authors the data-plane contract — the mapping from progress-storytelling status lines to actual backend work, and the AP7 "every status line MUST be true" enforcement.

**Authoritative Source.** §48.8.3 Workflow step 5 (progress storytelling); §48.8.3 UX Surface Specification (progress screen); §48.8.7 AP7 (banned: "Faked progress — loaders or 'scanning' animations that don't correspond to real work").

**Status line → backend condition map.** The four literal status lines from §48.8.3 Workflow step 5 map to the following backend conditions. Each line MUST NOT render before its backend condition is true; AP7 detector D-AP7 asserts this on every build AND at runtime via the client-side integrity check described below.

| Status Line | Backend Condition for Render | Render Duration | AP7 Detector |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| *"Scanning yourcompany.com…"* | `kb_bootstrap.firecrawl_job.state = 'fetching' OR 'parsing'` (seller's domain) | Elapsed-time-match: renders until first `kb_bootstrap.chunk_extracted` event | D-AP7-line-1 (client asserts `kb_bootstrap` status is `fetching` or `parsing` at line-render-start) |
| *"Found your security documentation…"* | `kb_bootstrap.chunk_extracted` event with `category_id = 'security_compliance'` has emitted | Elapsed-time-match: renders until `kb_bootstrap.entry_synthesized` event count ≥ 10 | D-AP7-line-2 (client asserts `category_id='security_compliance'` chunk was extracted) |
| *"Drafting responses for [Buyer Company]'s 82 requirements…"* | `first_pass_responses.batch_started` event has emitted | Elapsed-time-match: renders until `first_pass_responses.batch_completed` event | D-AP7-line-3 (client asserts `first_pass_responses.batch_started` was emitted) |
| *"Your bid is ready to review."* | `stage_3_bid_workspace_loaded_at` has been written | Renders until Stage 4 landing screen paint (one state-transition away) | D-AP7-line-4 (client asserts `stage_3_bid_workspace_loaded_at` is non-NULL) |

**Degraded-path status line handling.** When a capability fails (e.g., Opus unavailable, Firecrawl outage), the fallback status lines MUST NOT fabricate work. The degraded-path status line map:

| Failure Mode | Fallback Status Line | Backend Condition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `kb_bootstrap` fails (Firecrawl outage) | *"We couldn't pull content from yourcompany.com — you can still draft responses manually."* | `kb_bootstrap.state='failed'` |
| `first_pass_responses` fails | *"AI drafts are temporarily unavailable — your KB is ready."* | `first_pass_responses.state='failed'` AND `kb_bootstrap.state='succeeded'` |
| Both fail | *"We ran into a hiccup — your bid workspace is ready but we'll need a moment to catch up."* | Both capabilities `failed` |

**Client-side integrity check.** On every status-line render, the client asserts the backend condition via a lightweight `/onboarding/progress-integrity-check` endpoint that returns the current Bootstrap and First-Pass job states. If the assertion fails, the client emits `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation {kind='ap7_fake_progress', surface='progress_storytelling', line_id, backend_state_actual, line_expected_state}` AND the status line is hidden immediately (replaced with a generic "Working…" line until the next legitimate status-line trigger).

**Telemetry Events.**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `seller_progress_storytelling_line_rendered` | Each status line render | `{seller_org_id (nullable pre-SSO), invite_id, line_id ∈ {1,2,3,4,degraded_1,degraded_2,degraded_3}, elapsed_seconds_since_arrival, backend_state_at_render}` |
| `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation` | AP7 client-integrity-check failure | `{kind='ap7_fake_progress', surface='progress_storytelling', line_id, seller_org_id, invite_id, backend_state_actual, line_expected_state}` (existing kind from §48.8.3) |

**Acceptance Criteria.**

45. No status line MAY render > **500 ms** before its backend condition is true; fuzz test with contrived latency profiles asserts. (Cross-refs §48.8.3 AC 8.)
46. Client-side integrity check MUST execute within **200 ms** of each status-line render at p95.
47. AP7 violations MUST fire `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation` AND hide the offending status line within **500 ms** of detection at p95.
48. Degraded-path status lines MUST be authored verbatim per the degraded-path table above; UX-snapshot test asserts exact-match string comparison on every PR.
49. CI-gated AP7 detector (D-AP7) MUST run on every PR and MUST fail the build on any new or modified status-line string that is not registered in the map above.

### 49.1.9 Onboarding Anti-Patterns — Runtime Detectors & CI Gates {#49.1.9-onboarding-anti-patterns-runtime-detectors-and-ci-gates}

**Purpose.** §49.1.9 authors the runtime-detector and CI-gate implementation contracts for the AP1–AP11 banned anti-patterns defined at §48.8.7. §48.8.7 is authoritative for the ban semantics, rationale, and enforcement priority (P0 / P1 / P2). §49.1.9 authors the engineering-level detector implementations that bind those bans to CI gates, runtime middleware, and the `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation` event emission path. Enum values are registered at Appendix J `onboarding_anti_pattern_kind_enum` — §49.1.9 does NOT extend or rename these; deviation requires an Ops Council exception per §48.8.7.

**Authoritative Source.** §48.8.7 (authoritative ban table: six core APs + AP7–AP11 extended bans); Summary §3.6 (six anti-patterns, verbatim); C.141 (extended bans); Appendix J `onboarding_anti_pattern_kind_enum` (canonical enum registrations); §47 Governance (Ops Council exception process).

**Enum-bound detector table.** The canonical enum values `ap1_upgrade_cta_in_phase_1_to_3`, `ap2_credit_card_collected_pre_value`, `ap3_seat_collected_in_hero_moment`, `ap4_workspace_creation_blocked_by_seat_assignment`, `ap5_first_pass_response_requires_paid_capability`, `ap6_eoi_required_at_first_session`, `ap7_kb_pre_population_obscured`, `ap8_first_pass_response_invisible_to_buyer`, `ap9_post_submission_reveal_replaced_with_upgrade_modal`, `ap10_capability_review_skip_button_hidden`, `ap11_telemetry_blocked_by_consent_modal_in_hero_moment` are authored by §48.8.7 Appendix J registration. The ban semantics below follow §48.8.7 §48.8.7's table verbatim for AP1–AP6; §49.1.9 authors the detector implementation.

| AP | Ban (per §48.8.7) | Runtime Detector (D-APn) | CI Gate |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| AP1 | Credit card requested at any point before the first upgrade-intent click. | D-AP1: HTTP-endpoint guard — no `/onboarding/*` or Stages 1–6 surface route SHALL invoke the Stripe Elements credit-card widget OR call the Stripe SetupIntent / PaymentMethod endpoints. Full-cohort audit: zero `payment_method.created` Stripe events correlate to sessions where `stage_7_upgrade_cta_clicked_at IS NULL`. | CI: Playwright snapshot test asserts zero `cc-input`, `[data-stripe-element]`, or `iframe[src*="js.stripe.com"]` elements render on Stages 1–6 surfaces. Integration test simulates full onboarding with a Free-tier Org and asserts zero Stripe SetupIntent API requests fire. Runs on every PR. |
| AP2 | Upgrade offer presented during active bid work (Bid Workspace in `{populating, drafting, reviewing, editing}`). | D-AP2: Middleware on the upgrade-modal render path — rejects render if `bid_workspace.status IN {populating, drafting, reviewing, editing}` UNLESS the trigger is one of the three whitelisted Conversion Moments per §48.1.7 / §48.8.6 (#1 second concurrent bid, #2 first EOI, #3 KB ceiling 45-entry). The D-AP2 middleware inspects the trigger's `moment_kind` and rejects with HTTP 409 `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation_ap2` if the trigger does not match whitelist. | CI: Middleware unit test — for each non-whitelisted trigger kind, asserts HTTP 409 response; for each whitelisted trigger kind, asserts HTTP 200 + modal render. Weekly full-cohort audit sweeps for `upgrade_cta_impression {surface=hero_moment_*}` events that lack a matching whitelist trigger. |
| AP3 | Dark-pattern upgrade CTAs (roach motels, hard-to-find downgrade, fake urgency, pre-checked auto-renew). | D-AP3: (a) UX-pathway test asserts the "Downgrade / Cancel" action is accessible from Seller Console account settings within ≤ 2 clicks AND no modal blocks the path; (b) pre-commit copy lint scans for banned phrases (`"Only \d+ days? left"`, `"Limited time offer"`, countdown-timer DOM patterns) and flags; (c) UX-fixture test asserts auto-renew checkboxes default-unchecked on every subscription confirmation surface. | CI: Pre-commit copy lint (fails the commit on any banned phrase in English copy strings); UX-fixture tests (fail the PR on any roach-motel-pathway regression OR any pre-checked auto-renew). Runtime detection emits HTTP 400 `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation_ap3`. |
| AP4 | Upgrade-intent redirect to external pricing page during onboarding flow. | D-AP4: Navigation-observer test asserts that clicking any upgrade CTA from Stages 1–7 surfaces does NOT invoke `window.location.assign`, `window.location.replace`, OR render an `<a href>` targeting `/pricing` or external pricing URLs. All upgrade CTAs MUST render an inline Stripe-Checkout-handoff modal that carries the full Upgrade-Carry-Over-Guarantee context. | CI: Playwright navigation-observer test on every upgrade CTA across Stages 1–7. Fails the build on any redirect. Runtime detection emits HTTP 400 `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation_ap4`. |
| AP5 | Requiring vendor to describe company / industry / role before Bootstrap runs (zero-form commitment). | D-AP5: DOM-traversal assertion — Stages 1–2 surfaces render zero Sourcera-owned form fields (the Sourcera-owned count of `<input>`, `<select>`, `<textarea>` elements is zero; the SSO provider's own fields at the provider's domain are out of scope). Additionally, a mid-session integration test asserts no "Tell us about your company" modal renders during the first 3 minutes post-SSO. Exemption: the magic-link-fallback email field (single field; whitelist-enforced via a `data-ap5-exempt="magic_link_fallback_email"` attribute required on the fallback input; the attribute is on an allowlist enforced by D-AP5; any other use of the attribute fails CI). | CI: Playwright UX-fixture snapshot test enumerates form elements on Stages 1–2 surfaces; count MUST equal zero (exemption attribute excluded). Mid-session test asserts no tell-us-about-your-company modal fires. Runs on every PR. |
| AP6 | Pricing page shown before the vendor submits their first bid. | D-AP6: Route-gate middleware on `/account/pricing` and any upgrade-intent deep-link — `if (SellerOnboardingSession.first_bid_submitted_at IS NULL) { HTTP 302 redirect to /workspace }`. 50. AP1–AP11 runtime detectors (D-AP1 through D-AP11) MUST be CI-gated on every PR; any skipped or missing detector test fails the build. (Cross-refs §48.8.10 AC 35.)
51. AP1–AP11 runtime violations MUST emit `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation {ap_kind=…}` within **1 second** of detection at p95; `ap_kind` MUST be enum-bounded by Appendix J `onboarding_anti_pattern_kind_enum` (no inline string values permitted).
52. CI-gated AP detector job (`ci_seller_onboarding_ap_detectors`) MUST complete in < 60 s at p95 to preserve PR-throughput SLA.
53. Weekly Ops Council review of `onboarding_anti_pattern_violation` events MUST be documented per §47 Governance; sustained > 0 violations for two consecutive weeks trigger a formal Governance review.
54. AP1–AP6 detectors MUST surface across BOTH `ci_gate` AND `runtime_guard` enforcement layers per §48.8.7 enforcement priority; a meta-test asserts the `enforcement_layer` property domain includes both values for every AP1–AP6 violation event in the trailing 30-day window.

### 49.1.10 Acceptance Criteria {#49.1.10-acceptance-criteria}

**Consolidated Stage-Level Acceptance Criteria.** §49.1.10 is the authoritative consolidated list of stage-boundary-crossing acceptance criteria. Per-stage ACs are distributed in §49.1.1 through §49.1.9; §49.1.10 collects the cross-stage / system-level assertions that do not fit neatly into a single stage.

1. **Activation Metric p50 target (C.135, cross-refs §48.8.10 AC 30).** Hero-path-cohort (`invite_source ∈ {buyer_invite, ghost_bid_conversion, pro_trial_seat_m17}`) activation metric MUST satisfy §44.1 `Seller Activation Metric p50 target` on the trailing 30-day rolling window; regression > 10% against the §44.1 target raises a §42 P2.
2. **Activation Metric p90 target (C.135, cross-refs §48.8.10 AC 31).** Same cohort activation metric MUST satisfy §44.1 `Seller Activation Metric p90 target` on the trailing 30-day rolling window; regression > 10% against the §44.1 target raises a §42 P2.
3. **Bootstrap entry-count target (C.132).** ≥ 40 approved bootstrap entries on p50 of hero-path sessions (Indicator #3 in §48.1.6); regression below 50% raises a P3.
4. **Zero AP1–AP7 violations in QA per build.** Every PR CI run MUST complete with zero AP1–AP7 runtime-detector violations AND zero CI-gate skips; any violation blocks merge.
5. **Stage-boundary monotonicity.** Every SellerOnboardingSession row MUST satisfy the monotonic invariant: `stage_1_arrival_at <= stage_2_sso_initiated_at <= stage_2_sso_completed_at <= stage_2_bootstrap_started_at <= stage_3_bid_workspace_loaded_at <= stage_3_first_edit_at <= first_requirement_response_at <= first_bid_submitted_at <= stage_5_stake_reveal_rendered_at <= stage_6_exit_at <= stage_7_entered_at`. A DB constraint or check trigger enforces; property test asserts across 10,000 randomized timelines.
6. **Stage transitions are atomic.** Stage-exit and Stage-entry writes that logically pair (e.g., `first_bid_submitted_at` and `completion_state='activated'`) MUST be written in the same DB transaction; property test asserts no split-write scenarios across 10,000 crash-injection tests.
7. **Hero-path cross-console firewall.** SellerOnboardingSession-derived analytics MUST be inaccessible from the Buyer Console; property test asserts HTTP 404 on 10,000 simulated buyer-console-originated queries. (Cross-refs §48.8.10 AC 40.)
8. **Seller Activation Dashboard freshness.** The Seller Activation Dashboard (real-time) MUST reflect every `completion_state='activated'` transition within **30 seconds** at p95.
9. **PostHog funnel queryability.** The full funnel from `seller_onboarding_stage_entered {stage=1}` through `seller_onboarding_completed` MUST be PostHog-Insights-Funnels queryable end-to-end keyed on `seller_org_id` (post-SSO) or `distinct_id = invite_id` (pre-SSO, backfilled); query-performance p95 ≤ 30 seconds. (Cross-refs §48.8.10 AC 38.)
10. **Invite-source cohort breakdowns queryable.** Per-`invite_source` cohort breakdowns MUST be queryable on every §49.1 dashboard (buyer_invite vs ghost_bid_conversion vs pro_trial_seat_m17 vs direct_signup); query-performance p95 ≤ 30 seconds. (Cross-refs §48.8.10 AC 39.)
11. **Completion-state event fires exactly once.** `seller_onboarding_completed` MUST fire exactly once per session with `completion_state='activated'`; an idempotency key on `(seller_org_id, session_id)` asserts across 10,000 randomized re-emissions.
12. **Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee preserved across plan changes.** KB, AIOperations, Capability Declarations, and SellerOnboardingSession history MUST carry over intact on plan upgrade per C.139; property test asserts across 10,000 upgrade simulations.
13. **Data residency compliance.** All SellerOnboardingSession rows AND derived analytics MUST be region-scoped per §1.6 (US / EU / custom); cross-region leakage raises an AP-adjacent Ops P1.
14. **DSAR compliance.** On DSAR right-to-erasure, SellerOnboardingSession rows MUST be anonymized (`seller_org_id` nulled, PostHog events reassigned to a pseudonymous distinct_id) per §6.8; integration test asserts.
15. **Mobile parity.** The onboarding landing page, progress-storytelling screen, and Stake-Reveal Screen MUST render correctly on a mobile viewport (min-width 360 px); UX-snapshot tests assert on every PR.

# Section 50: Sourcera Ops Console {#section-50-sourcera-ops-console}

**Authoring Note (Numbering Reconciliation).** The governing integration task called for this section as §49. §49 is already occupied by *Seller Onboarding — Implementation-Level Seven-Stage Flow* (authored 2026-04-20; 53 cross-references throughout the Spec). Per project convention #11 ("Do NOT delete existing Master Spec content unless the prompt explicitly says 'replace'"), the existing §49 is preserved; the Sourcera Ops Console is authored here as §50, positioned immediately after §49 and therefore still "after §48" as the task directive requires. The numbering deviation is logged in `/Sourcera/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Numbering Decisions → §50 Ops Console`.

**Authoring Intent.** §50 is the engineering-contract companion to Summary Summary §6.35 (Sourcera Ops Console) and Summary Appendix C.17 (Ops Console Depth). It replaces and supersedes the cursory §43 (Admin Dashboard) narrative for everything the Ops Console does against customer data; §43 remains the reference for Sourcera-internal developer tooling (Datadog, Sentry, Zendesk linkage) that is *not* part of the Ops Console mutation surface. §50 authors the five hard contracts that the Summary required: (1) the Ops Console is a *separate application* from the customer product with its own auth, deployed to its own origin, firewall-isolated from customer-facing infrastructure except at the customer-API boundary; (2) every Ops mutation against customer data traverses the *same customer APIs* that the customer's own users traverse, distinguished by Appendix J `audit_event_actor_type = 'ops_actor'` on §4.6.1 AuditEvent rows and by §4.8.1 `ai_operation_actor_type = 'ops'` only on AIOperation rows; (3) Ops impersonation is time-boxed, justified, quorum-gated above thresholds, and the customer Org Owner is notified at session open AND close; (4) every Ops role is scoped to a capability envelope per Summary C.94, and role-change writes are dual-signed; (5) every Ops-originated Audit Event appears in the customer's own audit log carrying the Ops role, session id, and justification pointer.

**Source Authority.** Summary Summary §6.35 (Sourcera Ops Console) is the high-level directive. Summary C.93 (Separation Architecture), C.94 (Ops Role Matrix), C.95 (Taxonomy CMS), C.96 (Seller Template Review Rubric), C.97 (Baseline Assumption Manager), C.98 (Impersonation Audit Requirements), C.99 (Internal Analytics Dashboards), C.100 (Signal Integrity Monitor) are the specific contract clauses. §50.2 (Separation Architecture) derives from C.93. §50.3 (Ops Role Matrix) derives from C.94. §50.4 (Impersonation Audit Requirements) derives from C.98. §50.5 (Ops-Tagged Audit Actor) derives from the composite of §4.6.1 Audit Event, §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord, and the §4.6.3 OpsSession entity authored above in this edit.

**Scope.** §50 authors the contract for the Ops Console's separation architecture, its six-role capability matrix, its impersonation-audit discipline, and its Ops-tagged audit-actor pattern. §50 does NOT author the full feature catalog of the Ops Console (taxonomy CMS in §27.6, template review in §48.2, anti-spam kill-switches in §48.4, SIM in Summary C.100, etc. each carry their own Ops surface specification). §50 is the cross-cutting contract those per-feature Ops surfaces MUST satisfy; where a per-feature section contradicts §50, §50 prevails and the contradiction is logged as a defect in RECONCILIATION.md.

**Relationship to §43 (Admin Dashboard).** §43.1–§43.5 is the narrative-era admin-tooling description from v6.0.0. §50 authors the engineering contract. Where §43 and §50 conflict — e.g., §43.3 permits an unstructured "Assume user session" button scoped to Enterprise support; §50 requires a structured OpsSession row with quorum and time-box — §50 prevails. A follow-up phase will retire the conflicting §43 prose; until then, §43.2 `is_staff` gate and §43.4 `admin_audit_log` are superseded by §50.2 Ops auth and §50.5 Ops-Tagged Audit Actor respectively; implementation MUST use the §50 contracts.

---

## 50.1 Purpose {#50.1-purpose}

The Sourcera Ops Console is the internal application that Sourcera employees use to run the business against customer data — pricing-table publishes, controlled-vocabulary maintenance, seller-template review, customer-support impersonation, fraud investigation, dispute adjudication, manual billing reconciliation, kill-switch operation, and the Signal Integrity Monitor (Summary C.100). It exists because Sourcera engineers MUST NOT have production database access for day-to-day operations; every discretionary action against a customer row MUST flow through the same APIs customers use, so that the audit trail, rate-limit semantics, webhook emission, residency routing, and invariant enforcement apply uniformly.

**Contractual goals.**
1. **No direct database access.** Ops users cannot query the customer database directly. Ops Console mutations are customer-API calls; Ops Console reads are customer-API reads; Ops Console analytics are read-through the §4.6.1 Audit Event + Appendix G PostHog surfaces.
2. **Separation of origin.** The Ops Console lives at a distinct origin (`ops.sourcera.com` authored-extension — finalized at §50.2.1), served from a distinct CloudFront distribution, CSP-isolated, WAF-protected, and reachable only from Sourcera corporate IP ranges + VPN (§50.2.1 AC #3).
3. **Ops actor attribution.** Every mutation Ops executes against a customer Org carries `actor_type = 'ops_actor'` in AuditEvent (§4.6.1) rows; AIOperation (§4.8.1) rows, where present, continue to carry `actor_type = 'ops'` per their separate enum. The customer's Billing Admin Audit View (§5.2.1.4) surfaces Ops-tagged rows with a distinct visual treatment; the Ops Cross-Reference view aggregates them.
4. **Time-boxed impersonation.** No Ops user may impersonate a customer user or Org session without opening a §4.6.3 OpsSession row; sessions are auto-closed at time-box expiry; the customer Org Owner is notified at open and close.
5. **Capability envelopes by role.** Each of the six Ops roles carries a statically-defined capability envelope (§50.3.2); Ops users cannot act outside their envelope; envelope changes require dual sign-off.

**Non-goals.** §50 does NOT author:
- Ops Console UI component library (inherits the customer design system with distinct theming; authored in `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` Ops Console Extension, pending Phase 13).
- Ops-internal tooling that does NOT touch customer data (Datadog, Sentry, PostHog admin, Grafana, Jira — those live under §43.3 Support Tools).
- Per-feature Ops surfaces — those are authored in the home section of the feature (e.g., §27.6 Taxonomy CMS, §48.2 Template Review, §48.4 Anti-Spam, Summary C.100 SIM).

**Precedence.** §50 is the cross-cutting contract every per-feature Ops surface MUST implement. Where a per-feature Ops surface is silent on (a) separation architecture, (b) auth, (c) role envelope, (d) impersonation binding, or (e) audit attribution, the §50 defaults apply. Where a per-feature Ops surface contradicts §50, the conflict MUST be resolved in favor of §50 and the per-feature section edited to conform in the next integration phase.

---

## 50.2 Separation Architecture {#50.2-separation-architecture}

**Source Authority.** Summary C.93 (Separation Architecture): "Ops Console is a separate app with its own auth and audit boundary; all mutations flow through the same APIs customers use, tagged with an Ops actor. No direct database access."

### 50.2.1 Deployment Isolation {#50.2.1-deployment-isolation}

The Ops Console is a separate Next.js application (shared monorepo packages, distinct `apps/ops-console` workspace per the Build Execution Strategy Summary §3.1) deployed to a distinct origin and CDN distribution from the customer product. The isolation contract:

| Isolation Dimension | Customer Product | Ops Console |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Origin | `app.sourcera.com`, `seller.sourcera.com`, `marketplace.sourcera.com` | `ops.sourcera.com` (authored extension — flagged) |
| CloudFront distribution | Customer distribution (public WAF rules; rate limits per §44) | Ops distribution (restrictive WAF rules; allowlist-origin; no public rate limits) |
| Network reachability | Public internet | Sourcera corporate IP ranges + Sourcera-issued VPN + approved contractor IP allowlist; no public internet reachability |
| CSP | `script-src` / `connect-src` tuned for customer web app | `script-src 'self'`; `connect-src` restricted to `api.sourcera.com/ops/*` + Convex + `auth.workos.com`; no third-party analytics except PostHog project `sourcera-ops` (distinct from the customer PostHog project) |
| WorkOS tenant | Customer WorkOS tenant | Ops WorkOS tenant (distinct tenant id per §50.2.2); no cross-tenant SSO |
| Database shard | Customer Convex production | Customer Convex production (NO separate Ops DB — see §50.2.3; the Ops Console is an API client, not a DB client) |
| Secret rotation | Standard §6.6 rotation | Hardened rotation: Ops Console signing keys rotate every 30 days; customer keys rotate every 90 days |

**Authored Extension:** The final origin string `ops.sourcera.com` and the WAF allowlist ruleset are authored here at Master Spec fidelity pending infrastructure sign-off; registered in RECONCILIATION.md.

### 50.2.2 Authentication Model {#50.2.2-authentication-model}

**Ops WorkOS tenant.** Ops users authenticate via a distinct WorkOS tenant from customer users; there is no cross-tenant session sharing. The Ops WorkOS tenant enforces:

1. **SSO only.** No password auth; no magic-link auth. Ops users sign in via the Sourcera Google Workspace SSO connection (IdP-initiated or SP-initiated) or, for on-call rotation members, via the Okta connection provisioned for Security-team-approved contractors.
2. **Hardware-key MFA mandatory.** Every Ops user MUST present a WebAuthn / Yubikey U2F factor at SSO completion; TOTP / SMS factors are explicitly disallowed. Authored in WorkOS tenant configuration `require_factor_kind = 'webauthn'`.
3. **Step-up re-auth for sensitive actions.** Opening an OpsSession (§4.6.3), publishing a pricing-table version (§4.8.9), writing a kill-switch scope (§48.2.12.4), or granting an AntiPattern exception (§4.4.23) each require a step-up re-auth within 5 minutes of the action. The step-up re-auth validates the hardware key *again*; `auth_factor_evidence_json.step_up_reauthed_at` is stamped at validation and must satisfy the 5-minute freshness rule (§4.6.3 AC #2; §50.4.1 AC #2).
4. **Session duration.** Ops WorkOS sessions default to 8 hours (vs. customer 24 hours); idle timeout 15 minutes (vs. customer 30 minutes); concurrent session cap 2 per Ops user (vs. customer 5) — reflects insider-threat hardening.
5. **Data-residency-access tier.** Every Ops user carries a `residency_access_tier` ∈ `us`, `eu`, `uk`, `apac`, `global` stored in their WorkOS user profile attributes. `global` is restricted to `ops_admin` role holders and tier grants ≤ 5 Ops users at any time (authored limit; enforced by a WorkOS tenant policy `ops_global_residency_tier_cap`). Sessions on Orgs outside the Ops user's tier are rejected per §4.6.3 Failure Mode #4.
6. **Device trust.** The Ops WorkOS tenant requires a device-trust posture check via the Sourcera MDM (authored extension — MDM vendor selection pending; authored here pending Phase 13): device posture MUST satisfy `disk_encryption = on`, `screen_lock_timeout ≤ 5m`, `os_patch_level = current`, `endpoint_agent_running = true`; posture failures block session creation with `ops_session_device_posture_failed` (Appendix I — new).

**Acceptance criteria (§50.2.2).**

1. An Ops user without a hardware-key WebAuthn / Yubikey factor cannot complete SSO and receives a WorkOS-side error surfaced as `ops_auth_mfa_factor_required`. QA test: `ops_auth_webauthn_required`.
2. A step-up re-auth older than 5 minutes blocks any sensitive action with HTTP 403 `ops_step_up_reauth_required` (Appendix I — new). QA test: `ops_step_up_freshness_5m`.
3. Ops session idle beyond 15 minutes auto-invalidates; the Ops user is forced to re-SSO. QA test: `ops_session_idle_15m_invalidates`.
4. `residency_access_tier = 'global'` assignments require an `ops_admin` + `ops_security_admin` dual sign-off written to OpsActionRecord (§4.4.27) with `action_kind = 'ops_residency_tier_granted'` (new enum value; Appendix J extension below). QA test: `ops_global_tier_dual_signoff`.
5. Device-posture failure blocks session creation with HTTP 403 `ops_session_device_posture_failed` (Appendix I — new); Ops user is directed to remediate posture via the Sourcera IT help desk. QA test: `ops_device_posture_enforced`.

### 50.2.3 Mutation Path: Customer-API Tagged with Ops Actor {#50.2.3-mutation-path}

**Core contract.** The Ops Console has NO direct database access. Every Ops mutation against customer data is a customer-API call carrying an Ops auth context. The mutation-path contract:

1. **Ops HTTP middleware.** The customer API's HTTP middleware (§32.1) accepts two bearer-token classes: (a) customer tokens (`srck_{org_prefix}_{token}` per §6.6), which produce §4.6.1 AuditEvent rows with `actor_type = 'customer_user'` for human-user calls or `actor_type = 'system_agent'` for managed-agent-originated audit writes while preserving §4.8.1 AIOperation `actor_type = 'user'` / `'managed_agent'` where AIOperation rows are created; (b) Ops tokens (`srop_{ops_env}_{token}` — authored extension; distinct prefix), which produce AuditEvent rows with `actor_type = 'ops_actor'` and AIOperation rows with `actor_type = 'ops'`. Token verification is identical (HMAC over payload); the difference is which claim asserts role, session binding, and residency-access tier.
2. **Ops-session binding.** Every Ops token is bound to an active OpsSession `id`; the middleware looks up the session row, verifies `session_state ∈ {'active'}`, verifies the token's `org_id_impersonated` matches the request's target `org_id`, verifies `ended_at IS NULL`, verifies `now() ≤ started_at + effective_time_box_minutes`, verifies residency tier coverage, and verifies the Ops role's capability envelope (§50.3.2) permits the requested endpoint. Any failure returns HTTP 403 `ops_session_required_for_ops_actor` with a structured error body.
3. **Request-id appended atomically.** On every successful authorization, the middleware appends the request's `request_id` to `OpsSession.api_request_ids`, increments `actions_taken_count` and `mutation_count` or `read_count`, and writes the §4.6.1 Audit Event row with `actor_type = 'ops_actor'`, `ops_session_id = session.id`, in the same Convex transaction as the mutation. §4.6.3 AC #8 asserts atomicity.
4. **No Ops-only endpoints for customer data.** The Ops Console MUST NOT ship private endpoints at `/api/v1/ops/orgs/{id}/...` that duplicate customer endpoints. The Ops Console calls the SAME `/api/v1/orgs/{id}/...` endpoints the customer calls. Ops-Console-specific endpoints exist ONLY for Ops-owned entities (OpsActionRecord read, OpsSession open/close, SIM read, taxonomy CMS — each under `/api/v1/ops/...` — and those endpoints reject Ops tokens whose role envelope does not permit them).
5. **Rate-limit class.** Ops tokens are rate-limited identically to customer Enterprise tokens (§44.1). The Ops Console does not bypass rate limits. If an Ops user must execute a bulk operation that would breach the rate limit, the Ops middleware surfaces `rate_limit_exceeded`; the Ops user must raise the breach to `ops_admin` who may use the `ops_rate_limit_override` action (new enum value; Appendix J) writing an OpsActionRecord with justification.
6. **Idempotency.** Ops mutations honor idempotency keys identically to customer mutations (§32.2). The Ops middleware does NOT synthesize idempotency keys; they MUST be supplied by the Ops Console client. Missing idempotency keys on mutating endpoints return HTTP 400 `idempotency_key_required` (Appendix I — existing).
7. **Residency routing.** Ops mutations route to the same residency-partitioned API surface as the target Org's customer users. An Ops user with `residency_access_tier = 'us'` invoking against an EU Org first authenticates against the EU residency partition via the Ops Console's residency-aware SDK; cross-partition Ops tokens are rejected with `ops_session_residency_access_denied` (Appendix I — new). Per §40.3, the residency-partitioned API surface is the SAME endpoints, merely hosted at EU-region infrastructure.

**Acceptance criteria (§50.2.3).**

1. Ops tokens without an active OpsSession reference are rejected with HTTP 403 `ops_session_required_for_ops_actor` (Appendix I — new). QA test: `ops_token_requires_active_session`.
2. Ops tokens whose bound OpsSession `org_id_impersonated` does NOT match the request's target `org_id` are rejected with HTTP 403 `ops_session_org_mismatch` (Appendix I — new). QA test: `ops_token_org_bind_enforced`.
3. Ops mutations MUST emit a §4.6.1 Audit Event row with `actor_type = 'ops_actor'`, `ops_session_id` populated, and `notes` containing `{ops_role, justification_category, linked_support_ticket_ref}`. QA test: `ops_mutation_audit_event_tagged`.
4. Ops mutations MUST NOT alter the customer's Audit Event `user_id` field semantics — `user_id` stays null for Ops-actor rows (the Ops user identity is NOT a customer User row); the `actor_type = 'ops_actor'` value unambiguously routes rendering to the Ops attribution surface per §50.5. QA test: `ops_audit_user_id_null_for_ops_actor`.
5. Customer-side API endpoints MUST NOT expose any new fields to Ops tokens that are hidden from customer tokens (no privilege escalation via actor type). The projection layer keys off `org_id` membership, NOT actor type. Ops tokens see the SAME projection a customer Org Owner would see. QA test: `ops_projection_parity_with_customer_owner`.
6. The middleware MUST fail closed on any unknown Ops role; an Ops token carrying a role not in Appendix J `ops_role_kind` is rejected with HTTP 403 `ops_role_unknown` (Appendix I — new). QA test: `ops_role_kind_closed_enum_enforced`.
7. Ops-only endpoints (`/api/v1/ops/...`) MUST reject customer tokens (`srck_*`) with HTTP 404 `endpoint_not_found` (do NOT leak Ops-endpoint existence to customer tokens). QA test: `ops_endpoints_404_to_customer_tokens`.

### 50.2.4 No-Direct-DB-Access Enforcement {#50.2.4-no-direct-db-access-enforcement}

**Contract.** Ops users (human or service) MUST NOT have credentials that permit direct Convex database reads or writes against customer-scoped tables. This is enforced at multiple layers:

1. **IAM.** The Ops WorkOS tenant's SAML assertions carry no Convex deploy-key claims. Convex deploy keys exist only in (a) the production-deploy pipeline (service account, auditable), (b) the Sourcera Security on-call break-glass key (vaulted in the Security-team HSM; break-glass use requires dual Ops Director + Security Director sign-off + incident-retrospective postmortem).
2. **Network.** The Convex production endpoint is reachable only from the customer-API service; direct connections from Ops Console servers or Ops user workstations are blocked at the VPC security-group layer.
3. **Audit.** Any Convex-admin-console access emits an internal `convex_admin_access_attempted` event to the Security team's SIEM; audits beyond the deploy pipeline and break-glass are investigated as insider-threat events.
4. **Break-glass path.** The only sanctioned path for direct DB access is the break-glass path, which requires: (a) active production incident declared via §50.6.4 incident-response, (b) dual Ops Director + Security Director sign-off, (c) a session via the vaulted break-glass key, (d) all queries logged to an immutable audit store, (e) a postmortem within 72 hours of break-glass use that enumerates every query executed. Break-glass use is expected to be ≤ 2 per calendar year; regression above this rate triggers a Security Council review.

**Acceptance criteria (§50.2.4).**

1. Convex deploy-key rotation MUST remove any expired keys within 1 hour of rotation; CI gate `convex_deploy_key_rotation_age_lt_1h` asserts.
2. Break-glass access MUST write an `OpsActionRecord` row with `action_kind = 'break_glass_db_access'` (new enum value; Appendix J extension below) AND an immutable SIEM entry; absence of either raises a P0 Security incident.
3. Ops Console server process MUST NOT have Convex deploy-key environment variables; startup config sanity-check fails the pod boot if any are detected.

## 50.3 Ops Role Matrix {#50.3-ops-role-matrix}

**Source Authority.** Summary C.94: "Six Ops roles: Ops Admin, Pricing Admin, Template Reviewer, Support Agent, Fraud Analyst, Finance. Each with scoped permissions; role changes are audit-logged and require Ops Admin approval."

### 50.3.1 Roles {#50.3.1-roles}

The six canonical Ops roles enumerated in Summary C.94 are registered as `ops_role_kind` enum values in Appendix J. Each is a distinct capability envelope; Ops users are assigned one or more roles via the Ops WorkOS tenant's group-to-role mapping, which propagates to the Ops token's claims.

| Role Key | Display Name | Summary | Primary Surfaces |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `ops_admin` | Ops Admin | Super-role. Role assignment (dual-sign required), kill-switch operation, quorum override, emergency incident response, global residency-tier grants. | §50.3.4 role assignment; §48.2.12.4 kill-switch; §50.4.4 quorum authority; §50.6.4 incident response. |
| `ops_pricing_admin` | Pricing Admin | Pricing-table versioning, capability registry, committed-spend contracts, cost-base recalculation review. | §4.8.2 Capability Registry; §4.8.9 PricingTableVersion; §4.8.6 Cost-Base Recalculation; §4.8.8 CommittedSpendContract. |
| `ops_template_reviewer` | Template Reviewer | Seller template review per C.96 rubric; template library curation; category fit checks. | §4.4.28 TemplateLibraryEntry curation; §48.2.10 Template Publish Incentive reviews. |
| `ops_support_agent` | Support Agent | Customer-support impersonation (with quorum at `console_scope = 'both'`), ticket-driven read access, buyer/seller-side diagnostic reads. | §4.6.3 OpsSession (support-class); §50.4 impersonation surface. |
| `ops_fraud_analyst` | Fraud Analyst | Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100), abuse-report adjudication, fraud-flag review, zombie-demotion proposal. | Summary C.100 SIM; §4.5.7 Abuse Report; §48.4.12 zombie-demotion. |
| `ops_finance` | Finance | Billing reconciliation, contest adjudication, wallet manual adjustment, refund authorization, revenue-recognition review. | §4.8.1 AIOperation (manual reversal); §4.8.5 ContestRecord adjudication; §4.8.3 AIWallet manual intervention. |

**Authoring note on role-name mapping.** Summary C.94 names the roles "Ops Admin, Pricing Admin, Template Reviewer, Support Agent, Fraud Analyst, Finance." The spec-level enum values add the `ops_` prefix for uniform namespacing with existing Ops roles (e.g., `ops_growth_admin`, `ops_security_admin`, `ops_taxonomy_admin`, `ops_finance_admin`, `ops_capability_admin`, `ops_audit_reviewer`, `ops_verification_reviewer`, `ops_marketplace_editor`, `ops_marketing_editor`, `ops_marketing_lead`, `ops_compliance_admin`, `ops_compliance_reviewer`, `ops_applied_ml_admin`, `ops_marketplace_curator`, `ops_platform_admin`, `ops_sim_admin`). The six Summary C.94 roles map to the `ops_*` namespace as above. The pre-existing Ops roles are NOT deleted; they remain valid enum values and their capability envelopes are preserved under §50.3.2 ¶ "Pre-existing specialized Ops roles" below.

### 50.3.2 Capability Envelope Matrix {#50.3.2-capability-envelope-matrix}

The capability envelope matrix enumerates which Ops roles permit which Ops-surface capabilities. A capability is the unit of Ops-Console action; capabilities are the endpoint targets of the §50.2.3 mutation path. The matrix is additive-by-role: an Ops user holding multiple roles has the UNION of those roles' capabilities. The absence of a capability in a role's column means that role MUST NOT permit that capability.

**Legend.** `✓` = permitted; `✓²` = permitted but requires quorum sign-off (second Ops user of the row's required-quorum role); `✓ᴱ` = permitted but requires step-up re-auth within 5 minutes; `·` = not permitted.

| Capability | `ops_admin` | `ops_pricing_admin` | `ops_template_reviewer` | `ops_support_agent` | `ops_fraud_analyst` | `ops_finance` |
| :---- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **Impersonation — core** | | | | | | |
| Open OpsSession, `console_scope = 'buyer'`, ≤ 30 min | ✓ᴱ | · | · | ✓ᴱ | ✓ᴱ | ✓ᴱ |
| Open OpsSession, `console_scope = 'seller'`, ≤ 30 min | ✓ᴱ | · | ✓ᴱ | ✓ᴱ | ✓ᴱ | ✓ᴱ |
| Open OpsSession, `console_scope = 'both'`, any duration | ✓²ᴱ | · | · | ✓²ᴱ (with `ops_admin` quorum) | ✓²ᴱ (with `ops_admin` quorum) | · |
| Open OpsSession, duration 61–240 min | ✓²ᴱ | · | · | ✓²ᴱ (with `ops_admin` quorum) | ✓²ᴱ (with `ops_admin` quorum) | ✓²ᴱ (with `ops_admin` quorum) |
| Open OpsSession, duration 241–480 min | ✓²ᴱ (with `ops_security_admin` quorum) | · | · | · | · | · |
| Force-close any OpsSession | ✓ | · | · | · | · | · |
| **Audit + reads** | | | | | | |
| Read any OpsSession row (all fields) | ✓ | · | · | ✓ (own only) | ✓ (own only) | ✓ (own only) |
| Read Billing Admin Audit View (§5.2.1.4) for any Org | ✓ | ✓ | · | · | · | ✓ |
| Read OpsActionRecord (§4.4.27) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | · | ✓ | ✓ |

| **Mutations — pricing + capability** | | | | | | |
| Publish PricingTableVersion (§4.8.9) | ✓²ᴱ (with `ops_finance` quorum) | ✓²ᴱ (with `ops_finance` quorum) | · | · | · | · |

| **Mutations — finance + billing** | | | | | | |
| Manually reverse AIOperation (§4.8.1) | · | · | · | · | · | ✓²ᴱ (with `ops_admin` quorum) |
| Adjudicate ContestRecord (§4.8.5) | · | · | · | · | · | ✓ |

| **Mutations — fraud + abuse** | | | | | | |

| Flag SellerSignal row for force-suppress (§4.4.8) | · | · | · | · | ✓²ᴱ (with `ops_compliance_reviewer` pre-existing role) | · |
| Open/close SIM signal investigation (C.100) | ✓ | · | · | · | ✓ | · |

**Matrix invariants.**

1. Every `✓²` cell MUST identify the quorum role explicitly (parenthetical in the cell). The middleware MUST reject actions with `quorum_signoff_user_ids` that do not carry the required role.
2. Every `✓ᴱ` cell MUST require step-up re-auth within 5 minutes of the action (§50.2.2 #3). Middleware enforces via `auth_factor_evidence_json.step_up_reauthed_at` freshness.
3. A `·` cell MUST reject with HTTP 403 `ops_capability_outside_envelope` (Appendix I — new); the error body includes the caller's Ops role, the required role, and the action key.
4. The matrix is closed: every Ops capability used anywhere in the Spec (existing or future) MUST register in this matrix OR in a §50.3.2-extension subsection authored in the same edit that adds the capability. Ops capabilities authored without matrix registration are a CI gate failure (`ops_capability_matrix_coverage_complete`).

**Pre-existing specialized Ops roles.** The pre-§50 roles (`ops_growth_admin`, `ops_security_admin`, `ops_taxonomy_admin`, `ops_finance_admin`, `ops_capability_admin`, `ops_audit_reviewer`, `ops_verification_reviewer`, `ops_verification_senior_reviewer`, `ops_marketplace_editor`, `ops_marketing_editor`, `ops_marketing_lead`, `ops_compliance_admin`, `ops_compliance_reviewer`, `ops_applied_ml_admin`, `ops_marketplace_curator`, `ops_platform_admin`, `ops_sim_admin`) continue to hold their existing capability envelopes as authored in their home sections. They are semantically sub-specialties of the six Summary C.94 roles and are mapped to the C.94 roles for matrix-classification purposes as follows:

| Pre-existing specialized role | Maps under Summary C.94 role |
| :---- | :---- |
| `ops_growth_admin` | `ops_admin` (growth-surface specialist) |
| `ops_security_admin` | `ops_admin` (security-surface specialist) |
| `ops_taxonomy_admin` | `ops_pricing_admin` (content taxonomy adjacency) + `ops_template_reviewer` (template taxonomy adjacency) |
| `ops_finance_admin` | `ops_finance` |
| `ops_capability_admin` | `ops_pricing_admin` |
| `ops_audit_reviewer` | `ops_admin` (read-only audit specialist) |
| `ops_verification_reviewer`, `ops_verification_senior_reviewer` | `ops_template_reviewer` (verification-review workflow) |
| `ops_marketplace_editor`, `ops_marketing_editor`, `ops_marketing_lead` | `ops_admin` (marketing-content specialist) |
| `ops_compliance_admin`, `ops_compliance_reviewer` | `ops_admin` (compliance-surface specialist) + `ops_fraud_analyst` adjacency |
| `ops_applied_ml_admin` | `ops_pricing_admin` (pricing-model adjacency) |
| `ops_marketplace_curator` | `ops_template_reviewer` |
