**State machine** (enum `template_review_assessment_state`):

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| — | `assigned` | Queue routing assigns reviewer | |
| `assigned` | `in_progress` | Reviewer opens assessment | |
| `in_progress` | `awaiting_calibration` | Reviewer hits low-confidence threshold OR flags for calibration | Triggers peer calibration |
| `awaiting_calibration` | `in_progress` | Calibrator submits | |
| `in_progress` | `submitted` | Reviewer publishes scored assessment | All dimensions scored; rationales meet length minima |
| `submitted` | `finalized` | 24 h grace window elapses without self-retraction | |
| `submitted` | `retracted` | Reviewer retracts within 24 h grace | |
| `retracted` | `in_progress` | Reviewer resumes | |
| `finalized` | `overturned_on_appeal` | §50.11.6 appeal upheld | Terminal for this assessment; successor assessment links |

`finalized`, `overturned_on_appeal`, `retracted→assigned→…` per standard flow; only `finalized` and `overturned_on_appeal` are permanently terminal.

**Required indexes:** `(template_library_entry_id, rubric_id)`, `(reviewer_ops_user_id, assessment_state)`, `(assessment_state, sla_due_at) WHERE assessment_state IN ('assigned','in_progress')`, `(org_id_of_seller, assessment_state)`.

### 50.11.5 Reviewer Workflow {#50.11.5-reviewer-workflow}

**Assignment.** A round-robin-with-load-balancing queue routes `submitted` TemplateLibraryEntry rows to `ops_template_reviewer` role-holders. Assignment respects residency (EU-residency templates route to EU-residency reviewers; APAC follows-the-sun policy applies). Caps per reviewer: 8 concurrent `assigned` or `in_progress` assessments; new assignments queue behind releases.

**SLA.** Default time-to-finalize: 72 h from `assigned_at`. Overrides per `template_kind` permitted (e.g., `mcp_template` 48 h). Breach behavior: `sla_breached=true`, reviewer escalation notification (in-app + email), work auto-reassigned if not opened within 6 h of breach, visible on §50.14.5 Support dashboard.

**Calibration.** Every reviewer takes a monthly calibration pack (§50.11.7) containing 10 re-scored historical templates; inter-rater agreement ≤ 0.6 Cohen's κ triggers a mandatory coaching pairing with a senior reviewer before further assignments. Calibration pack scoring does NOT affect seller-visible projection.

**Escalation.** Reviewer may transition to `escalate_to_senior` for any template: assessment hands to `ops_template_senior_reviewer` (new role, §50.3.1 extension) with the reviewer's draft dimension_scores preserved; senior reviewer's scored outcome is authoritative. Mandatory escalation triggers: any `hard_block_on_any_fail` fail on `schema_validity`; brand-impersonation flagged by automated check; seller disputes prior assessment within 90 days.

**Chat with seller.** Reviewer may open a clarifying-question thread with the seller through §42 Support-bridged Messaging under `thread_kind='template_review_clarification'`; threads are linked to the assessment and projected to the seller.

### 50.11.8 Customer-Visible Projection and DSAR Rules {#50.11.8-customer-visible-projection-and-dsar-rules}

Sellers see, for each of their templates:

- `outcome` (enum-mapped to human-friendly label).
- `outcome_rationale` (verbatim).
- Per-dimension score with rubric anchor labels; **no reviewer identity**.
- Appeal entry point if within 30-day window.
- Thread link to any §42 clarifying-question thread.

Sellers never see `internal_notes`, `calibrator_ops_user_id`, `reviewer_ops_user_id`, or `ops_session_id`. DSAR export for a seller org includes all assessments and appeals pertaining to the org, with reviewer identity replaced by a stable pseudonym (`reviewer_pseudonym_id`). Ops-side DSAR (reviewer requesting their own Ops history) is governed by §50.2.5 Ops Records and is not triggered by seller-DSAR.

### 50.11.10 Rubric Authoring Surface {#50.11.10-rubric-authoring-surface}

Ops screen at `/template-rubrics` lists existing rubrics per `template_kind` with state badges. `New rubric` CTA opens the authoring flow: dimension editor (add / remove dimensions, edit anchors, set weights, set gate behavior), automated-checks picker (bind dimension to named validator functions from §27 plugin surface), aggregation selector, publish threshold slider, calibration pack builder, preview mode (score a sandbox template live), submit-for-senior-approval CTA.

Senior approver screen at `/template-rubrics/:id/approve`: side-by-side with current published rubric; field-level diff; calibration κ chart; approve / request changes / reject CTAs.

### 50.11.11 Acceptance Criteria {#50.11.11-acceptance-criteria}

1. No TemplateLibraryEntry MUST transition from `submitted` to `published` (§4.4.28 state machine) without a `finalized` or `overturned_on_appeal` §50.11.4 assessment with `outcome ∈ {'approve', 'approve_with_changes'}`. Integration test asserts enforcement across all four `template_kind` values.
2. Every `submitted` assessment MUST have all rubric dimensions scored and each dimension rationale ≥ 60 chars; `outcome_rationale` ≥ 80 chars. Server returns HTTP 422 on violation.
3. An appeal adjudicator MUST NOT equal the original reviewer; server returns HTTP 403 with code `template_review_appeal_adjudicator_same_as_reviewer`. Property-test asserts across 10,000 simulated assignments.
4. Rubric publish MUST be blocked if calibration pack is not at `published` state (code `template_review_calibration_pack_required`, HTTP 412) or inter-rater κ < 0.7 (code `template_review_inter_rater_agreement_below_threshold`, HTTP 409).
5. Rubric versions MUST be immutable after publish; any write returns HTTP 409. Integration test.
6. Every §50.11 mutation MUST emit a §4.6.1 Audit Event with `actor_type='ops_actor'` and exactly one §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord with `linked_ops_session_id`. Audit-integrity property-test asserts 100% across 10,000 simulated mutations.
7. Seller-visible projection MUST NOT include reviewer identity fields (`reviewer_ops_user_id`, `calibrator_ops_user_id`, `ops_session_id`, `internal_notes`). Serializer-level test asserts zero leakage across 10,000 projected rows.
8. Reviewer capacity cap (8 concurrent open assessments) MUST be enforced at assignment; breach returns HTTP 409 and triggers queue rebalance.
9. DSAR export for a seller org MUST include every assessment and appeal record for the org with reviewer identity pseudonymized; pseudonym MUST be stable across exports for the same `reviewer_ops_user_id`.
10. Appeal SLA: an appeal in `under_adjudication` for > 10 business days without resolution MUST trigger a P1 Ops alert; appeals unresolved past 20 business days auto-escalate to `ops_admin`.
11. SLA breach rate for assessments (`sla_breached=true` at finalization) MUST stay ≤ 5% rolling 30-day; breach triggers §50.14.5 Support dashboard warning.
12. Residency isolation: EU-residency templates MUST be assessed by EU-residency reviewers; server rejects cross-residency assignments with HTTP 403.
13. Calibration κ MUST be computed automatically and surfaced on the rubric's state transition to `awaiting_approval`; low κ blocks publish per AC #4.

### 50.11.12 Counterfactual Failure-Mode Pass {#50.11.12-counterfactual-failure-mode-pass}

**Failure mode 1 — reviewer bias against specific seller orgs.** Mitigation: conflict-of-interest declaration required at reviewer onboarding; conflict table keyed on `ops_user_id × seller_org_id`; assignment skips conflicts; seller appeals with `grounds='bias_or_conflict'` auto-route to adjudicators in a different residency region and raise a mandatory senior-review flag.

**Failure mode 2 — rubric drift across template kinds.** Mitigation: `template_kind` is a required dimension of the rubric entity; one published rubric per kind at a time (uniqueness constraint `(template_kind, state) WHERE state='published'`); supersession is explicit; calibration packs per rubric version preserve historical gold-standard baselines.

**Failure mode 3 — appeal abuse (serial identical appeals).** Mitigation: a seller org may open at most 1 appeal per assessment; repeat appeals on the same assessment return HTTP 409 with code `template_review_appeal_already_resolved`. Sellers may escalate to §42 Support for override, but Support cannot open a new appeal — only `ops_admin` can authorize a second adjudication (audit-trailed).

**Failure mode 4 — reviewer SLA cascade failure.** Mitigation: §50.11.5 auto-reassign after 6 h post-breach; reviewer capacity cap plus auto-reassign ensures queue drains; §50.14.5 Support dashboard surfaces breach rate; breach > 5% rolling 30-day triggers §50.8 Ops capacity-planning ticket.

**Failure mode 5 — seller-submitted evidence contains PII of third parties.** Mitigation: evidence upload runs through §40.8 PII-redaction pre-scan; flagged uploads block submission with "Remove third-party PII" error; adjudicator cannot view unredacted evidence; upload retention per §40.2 asset-class policy.

## 50.12 Pricing Admin Surface {#50.12-pricing-admin-surface}

### 50.12.1 Purpose and Scope {#50.12.1-purpose-and-scope}

§50.12 authors the Ops Console surface for mutating the authoritative Sourcera pricing table, `cost_base` overrides, and free-allowance policies. Pricing structures are referenced across §34 Plan Tier Definitions, §4.8.1 AIOperation, §4.8.2 CapabilityRegistryEntry, §4.8.4 OutcomeContract, §4.8.9 PricingTableVersion, and §28 Public Pricing API. §50.12 is the authoritative source for how pricing mutations are authored, reviewed, quorum-gated, published, and propagated.

**Non-negotiable gates (per task brief):**

- Any rate-card change ≥ 5% (absolute or relative to last published) requires **two-Ops-approver** workflow (proposer + second approver, distinct OpsSessions, distinct devices per §50.3.3).
- Any `cost_base` override drift ≥ 10% relative to the prior published value requires the same two-approver workflow.
- Free-allowance changes that reduce an existing allowance require two-approver workflow regardless of magnitude (downgrade protection).

Plan gating: N/A — §50.12 is Ops-only. Surface is §50.3.2-gated to role `ops_pricing_admin` (proposer) and role `ops_finance` (second approver for ≥ 5% moves).

Retention: pricing change proposals retain 10 years (finance compliance window); published PricingTableVersion retains indefinitely (§4.8.9 invariant). DSAR: pricing is platform-scoped; no DSAR implication.

| `residency_region` | enum `residency_region` | NOT NULL | Residency of the pricing surface (global pricing changes author one proposal per region) |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | | | Standard |

**Scope isolation:** platform-scoped; residency isolation by region. **Required indexes:** `(state, residency_region)`, `(proposer_ops_user_id, state)`, `(approver_ops_user_id, state)`, `(two_approver_gate_triggered, state)`.

**State machine** (enum `pricing_admin_change_proposal_state`):

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| — | `drafting` | `POST /ops/pricing/change-proposals` | Proposer has `pricing.change.author` |
| `drafting` | `awaiting_simulation` | `POST /.../run-simulation` | `change_scope` valid |
| `awaiting_simulation` | `simulated` | Simulation job completes | Results attached |
| `simulated` | `awaiting_approval` | `POST /.../submit-for-approval` | `two_approver_gate_triggered` check made; if true, approver role required |
| `awaiting_approval` | `approved` | `POST /.../approve` | Approver distinct from proposer; `approver_role_required` capability held |
| `awaiting_approval` | `rejected` | `POST /.../reject` | Terminal |
| `approved` | `awaiting_comms_plan` | If customer comms required | |
| `awaiting_comms_plan` / `approved` | `awaiting_publish_window` | `POST /.../schedule-publish` | |
| `awaiting_publish_window` | `publishing` | Scheduler | |
| `publishing` | `published` | §4.8.9 PricingTableVersion publish completes + §28 Public Pricing API cache refreshed | |
| `publishing` | `publish_failed` | Failure | Roll back to `approved` or escalate |
| `approved` | `withdrawn` | `POST /.../withdraw` | Proposer or `ops_admin` |

`published`, `rejected`, `withdrawn` terminal. `publish_failed` requires explicit retry or withdraw.

### 50.12.3 `change_scope` JSONB Schema {#50.12.3-change-scope-jsonb-schema}

```
{
  "rate_card_changes": [
    {
      "ai_operation_id": "opk_mcp_call_v2",
      "prior_base_unit_cost_usd": 0.0025,
      "proposed_base_unit_cost_usd": 0.00275,
      "delta_pct_relative": 0.10
    }
  ],
  "cost_base_overrides": [
    {
      "capability_registry_entry_id": "cap_search_v4",
      "prior_cost_base_usd": 0.0014,
      "proposed_cost_base_usd": 0.0016,
      "delta_pct_relative": 0.142,
      "override_reason": "Anthropic price update effective 2026-05-01"
    }
  ],
  "free_allowance_changes": [
    {
      "allowance_key": "free_tier_monthly_buyer_ai_operations",
      "prior_amount": 200,
      "proposed_amount": 150,
      "delta_direction": "reduction",
      "effective_cohort_rule": "new_orgs_only"
    }
  ],
  "bundle_changes": [],
  "committed_spend_tier_changes": []
}
```

Required-field validation: every delta entry computes `delta_pct_relative`; server recomputes and rejects on mismatch to prevent client-side spoofing.

### 50.12.4 Gate Evaluation {#50.12.4-gate-evaluation}

At `submit-for-approval` time, server evaluates:

- **Rate-card gate:** `max(|delta_pct_relative|) over rate_card_changes ≥ 0.05` → `approver_role_required='second_pricing_admin'` (any second `ops_pricing_admin`) when 0.05–0.15, → `approver_role_required='ops_finance'` when ≥ 0.15, → `approver_role_required='senior_quorum'` when ≥ 0.25.
- **Cost-base gate:** `max(|delta_pct_relative|) over cost_base_overrides ≥ 0.10` → `approver_role_required='ops_finance'` (finance owns cost-of-goods integrity).
- **Allowance-reduction gate:** any `delta_direction='reduction'` on `free_allowance_changes` → `approver_role_required='ops_finance'` AND `customer_comms_plan_id` required before `published`.
- **Multiple triggers:** server resolves to the strictest required role.

`two_approver_gate_triggered=true` if any gate fires. Low-impact changes (all deltas < 5%, no reductions) can proceed with single-approver pattern (proposer is also the publisher) but STILL emit a §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord with `action_kind='pricing_admin_publish_single_approver'` and are subject to post-publish review by finance weekly.

### 50.12.5 Simulation {#50.12.5-simulation}

Every proposal MUST run a §50.12.5 simulation before `approved`. Simulation computes:

- Projected ARR impact over next 12 months (Monte Carlo, 10,000 samples, confidence interval 95%).
- Projected margin impact (gross margin delta vs. baseline).
- Affected customer count by plan tier and residency.
- Projected AIWallet top-up cadence shift (lagged demand proxy).
- Contest-rate projection if rate-card changes touch high-contest operations (§4.8.5 ContestRecord history).
- Downgrade risk: estimated count of orgs likely to downgrade plan tier based on historical elasticity.

Simulation entity `PricingSimulationRun` (authored in §50.12 extension appendix):

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID PK | |
| `proposal_id` | FK §50.12.2 | |
| `state` | enum `pricing_simulation_run_state` | `queued`, `running`, `completed`, `failed` |
| `arr_delta_usd_p50` | decimal | |
| `arr_delta_usd_p95_low` / `p95_high` | decimal | |
| `gross_margin_delta_pct` | float | |
| `affected_customer_count_by_plan` | JSONB | |
| `downgrade_risk_count_p50` | int | |
| `contest_rate_delta_pct_projected` | float | |
| `simulation_model_version` | semver | For reproducibility |
| `model_inputs_hash` | sha256 | |
| `run_at` | timestamp | |
| `inputs_snapshot_uri` | string | S3 URI with encryption; retention per §40.2 Ops audit |

Models and inputs are versioned; simulation reruns with newer inputs generate new rows (no overwrite).

### 50.12.7 Rate-Card Editor UX {#50.12.7-rate-card-editor-ux}

Ops screen at `/pricing/rate-card`. Table view: every AIOperation × Capability × plan tier, showing prior `base_unit_cost_usd`, proposed `base_unit_cost_usd`, `delta_pct_relative`, gate chip. Editor allows inline proposal-row creation; bulk import from CSV (schema-validated); revert-to-baseline CTA; diff preview CTA.

Per-row safety rails:

- Min: `cost_base × (1 + min_margin_floor_pct)` where `min_margin_floor_pct` is a §34 parameter (default 25%); below floor triggers a hard warning and requires `ops_finance` sign-off regardless of magnitude.
- Max: any per-row increase > 50% over prior surfaces a "Rate-card shock" warning and requires senior-quorum gate irrespective of gate thresholds.

### 50.12.8 `cost_base` Override Editor UX {#50.12.8-cost-base-override-editor-ux}

Ops screen at `/pricing/cost-base`. Table of §4.8.2 CapabilityRegistryEntry with fields: `provider` (Anthropic, Convex, Firecrawl, Perplexity, custom), `current_cost_base_usd`, `last_provider_price_change_at`, `proposed_cost_base_usd`, `drift_vs_prior_pct`, `rationale` (required textarea). Sources panel (right): link to provider price change documentation (stored as §40.8 asset), Anthropic webhook integrations surfaced if automated price-change signal available.

Override scope: global per capability (no per-customer cost_base). Per-residency override optional (EU vs US cost_base may differ; both fields editable when residency divergence expected).

### 50.12.9 Free-Allowance Editor UX {#50.12.9-free-allowance-editor-ux}

Ops screen at `/pricing/free-allowances`. Table: allowance key, scope (`buyer`/`seller`/`both`), current amount, proposed amount, scope cohort (all / new orgs / existing orgs only), reduction-safety flag. Reductions to existing-org allowances are disallowed by default; a senior-quorum override exists, scoped by cohort rule (e.g., "new signups 2026-Q3+"). Existing orgs on pre-change allowance amounts are grandfathered via `FreeAllowanceCounter` (§4.8.6) extension field `grandfathered_under_pricing_table_version_id`.

### 50.12.10 Publish Flow {#50.12.10-publish-flow}

`POST /ops/pricing/change-proposals/:id/publish`:

1. Validate state = `awaiting_publish_window` (or `approved` for immediate) AND `publish_window_start ≤ now ≤ publish_window_end` (or no window set).
2. Acquire pricing-publish advisory lock (only one publish per residency at a time; §4.8.9 invariant).
3. Snapshot `resulting_pricing_table_version_id` = new §4.8.9 PricingTableVersion with `snapshot_at=now()`, `supersedes_version_id`, `change_proposal_id`.
4. Write §4.8.9 row; emit `pricing.table.version_published` webhook; bump §28 Public Pricing API cache via dual-key cache invalidation.
5. Emit §4.6.1 Audit Event `actor_type='ops_actor'` + §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord `action_kind='pricing_admin_publish'` with `linked_ops_session_id=ops_session_id_proposer` AND `co_approver_ops_session_id=ops_session_id_approver` (new field on OpsActionRecord; §50.12 extension).
6. Invalidate in-memory rate-card caches across all Convex regions; assert cache miss-then-hit round-trip within 60 s.
7. Schedule customer comms delivery per `PricingAdminCustomerCommsPlan`.
8. Transition `published_at = now()`; emit PostHog `ops_pricing_proposal_published`.

Rollback: publishing is idempotent by `proposal_id`; failure mid-step triggers compensating transactions (§42.5 transactional retry). Catastrophic failure routes to `publish_failed` and opens a P0 incident (§50.6.4) with `kill_switch_bundle_template_id='pricing_publish_rollback'`.

### 50.12.13 Acceptance Criteria {#50.12.13-acceptance-criteria}

1. Every proposal with `two_approver_gate_triggered=true` MUST be rejected at publish time (HTTP 412, `pricing_admin_change_requires_quorum`) unless `approver_ops_user_id IS NOT NULL` AND `approver_ops_user_id ≠ proposer_ops_user_id` AND `ops_session_id_approver ≠ ops_session_id_proposer` AND approver device fingerprint differs from proposer. Property-test: 10,000 simulated gate permutations; zero quorum evasion.
2. Gate threshold evaluation MUST be server-side; client-submitted `delta_pct_relative` is recomputed against the baseline PricingTableVersion; mismatch returns HTTP 422. Regression test.
3. Simulation MUST complete and attach to the proposal before `approved`; a proposal whose simulation is older than 24 h at publish time MUST be re-simulated (HTTP 412, `pricing_admin_change_simulation_required`).
4. Rate-card moves breaching the `min_margin_floor_pct` (default 25%) MUST be blocked (HTTP 422, `pricing_admin_change_margin_floor_breach`); override requires senior-quorum + `ops_finance` dual sign-off.
5. Free-allowance reductions MUST require `ops_finance` approval and a `customer_comms_plan_id`; publish blocked if comms not sent OR lead-time not elapsed.
6. Publish MUST acquire a per-residency advisory lock; concurrent publishes return HTTP 423. Chaos test asserts across 1,000 simulated publish races.
7. Published PricingTableVersion MUST propagate to §28 Public Pricing API cache within 60 s (p95); breach surfaces on §50.14 Finance dashboard.
8. Every §50.12 mutation MUST emit §4.6.1 Audit Event + §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord; `OpsActionRecord.co_approver_ops_session_id` populated for gated actions. Audit-integrity property-test 100%.
9. `FreeAllowanceCounter` grandfathering MUST be atomic with publish; no org shifts below a reduced allowance until their subscription period rolls over.
10. Weekly finance post-publish review MUST surface every `pricing_admin_publish_single_approver` action for attestation; unattested actions older than 30 days trigger a finance-backoff alert.
11. Rollback of a failed publish (`publish_failed`) MUST revert to prior PricingTableVersion within 120 s; cache invalidation MUST re-propagate. Chaos test.
12. Weekly automated margin-floor sweep MUST fire a §50.14 Finance alert if any live rate × current `cost_base` produces a margin < `min_margin_floor_pct`, regardless of when the rate was published.
13. **Cumulative rate-card drift gate (Authored Extension #41; §50 Phase 6 Verification Remediation 2026-04-21).** The two-approver gate MUST auto-trigger on a true **90-day rolling window** of cumulative absolute percentage drift against a pre-window baseline ≥ 10%, even when each individual proposal's `delta_pct_relative` sits below the 5%-single-proposal threshold. "Cumulative drift" is evaluated as `Σ |ΔRate_i|` across every `published` and `awaiting_approval` PricingAdminChangeProposal whose target covers the same `(capability_id, console, residency_region)` scope AND whose `simulated → awaiting_approval` transition timestamp falls in the preceding 90 days; withdrawn proposals count toward the window (FM#7 counter-surveillance). The window is evaluated at the incoming proposal's `simulated → awaiting_approval` transition time — a true rolling 90-day window, not a fixed calendar quarter. Breach returns HTTP 409 `pricing_admin_cumulative_drift_gate_exceeded` (Appendix I — new); the proposer is forced to invoke two-approver quorum regardless of individual delta. Property-test `pricing_admin_cumulative_drift_gate_property_test` (1,000 simulated proposal streams) AND `pricing_admin_rolling_window_boundary_property` (10,000 simulated streams crossing window boundaries) assert correctness. Cross-scope enforcement: cumulative drift is evaluated across the UNION of rate-card + cost_base proposals on the same scope (so cost_base-override end-runs are absorbed; FM#7).
14. **Per-proposer + team-wide withdrawal rate-limit (Authored Extension #42; §50 Phase 6 Verification Remediation 2026-04-21).** A Pricing Admin proposer MAY NOT withdraw more than 10 `PricingAdminChangeProposal` rows within any rolling 24-hour window, and the Pricing Admin team as a whole MAY NOT exceed 40 withdrawals within the same window (multi-proposer round-robin coordination guard). Breach of the per-proposer cap returns HTTP 429 `pricing_admin_proposal_withdrawal_rate_limit_exceeded` (Appendix I — new); breach of the team cap emits the same error code AND pages `ops_security_admin` within 60 s via PagerDuty. Property-test `pricing_admin_withdrawal_rate_limit_property_test` (1,000 simulated withdrawal streams for both per-proposer and team-wide) asserts; rate-limit state is evaluated on a true rolling 24-h window, not a fixed calendar day. Emits PostHog event `pricing_admin_proposal_withdrawal_rate_limit_hit` and webhook `pricing_admin.proposal.withdrawal_rate_limit_hit` (Appendix C — new) on breach.

### 50.12.14 Counterfactual Failure-Mode Pass {#50.12.14-counterfactual-failure-mode-pass}

**Failure mode 1 — approver colludes with proposer.** Two approvers on the same shared-desk device split their sessions but share a laptop. Mitigation: device-fingerprint check at approval (§50.3.3 AC inherited); approver device MUST differ from proposer device across WorkOS-enforced device-trust posture + MDM-vendor attestation; breach returns `pricing_admin_change_approver_device_conflict`.

**Failure mode 2 — time-of-check / time-of-use on gate threshold.** Proposer authors with 4.9% delta, gate does not fire, sneak-merges a later amendment bumping delta to 5.1%. Mitigation: state transition `simulated → awaiting_approval` freezes `change_scope` as a hash-signed snapshot; subsequent mutations require state reset to `drafting`, re-running simulation and re-computing gates; publish verifies `change_scope_hash` matches.

**Failure mode 3 — Public Pricing API cache inconsistency across regions.** Convex region A reflects new pricing; region B serves stale for > 60 s. Mitigation: dual-key cache invalidation (global key + regional key); publish acknowledgment requires round-trip miss-then-hit assertion in every region before transitioning to `published`; breach triggers automatic rollback (`publish_failed`) and re-queues.

**Failure mode 4 — customer sees rate-card increase without comms.** Comms plan marked `sent` but email provider failed silently. Mitigation: `PricingAdminCustomerCommsPlan.sent_at` writes ONLY after confirmed per-channel delivery (Loops.so delivery webhook; in-app-dismissible flag reaches ≥ 80% of active users); publish gate checks `sent_at + lead_time_days ≤ now()` AND delivery telemetry meets threshold.

**Failure mode 5 — cost_base override lag vs. provider price change.** Anthropic raises model pricing on day N; Sourcera's `cost_base` stays stale, producing sub-floor margins until next manual review. Mitigation: nightly automated provider-price-diff job (§50.12.8 source panel) raises a P2 alert on divergence > 5%; daily §50.14 Finance dashboard chip shows cost_base staleness per capability; staleness > 14 days auto-opens a draft proposal pre-populated with provider deltas for review.

**Failure mode 6 — grandfathering race producing transient under-charge.** Publish transitions mid-billing-cycle; `FreeAllowanceCounter` grandfather flag set on some orgs before counter reset runs. Mitigation: publish runs in maintenance window OR performs billing-cycle-aware phased rollout: reductions apply only to orgs whose current counter period ends ≥ `lead_time_days` in the future; orgs mid-cycle honor prior allowance for the remainder of the cycle.

**Failure mode 7 — cumulative drift evasion via serial sub-threshold proposals (Authored Extension #41; §50 Phase 6 Verification Remediation 2026-04-21).** A proposer authors a sequence of individual proposals each sitting just below the 5%-single-proposal threshold (e.g., 4.9%, 4.8%, 4.9%, 4.7% across 90 days), each of which evades the single-proposal two-approver gate. Net effect: ≥ 19% cumulative rate-card drift against the pre-window baseline with single-approver sign-off throughout. Mitigation: AC #13 cumulative-drift gate evaluates `Σ |ΔRate_i|` on a rolling 90-day window per `(capability_id, console, residency_region)` scope and auto-triggers the two-approver quorum gate the moment cumulative drift reaches ≥ 10%. Window boundary exploitation (proposer times proposals to straddle fixed calendar boundaries) is defeated by the true-rolling-window semantics — `pricing_admin_rolling_window_boundary_property` asserts 10,000 simulated streams crossing boundaries. Cross-scope end-runs (proposer pivots to cost_base override proposals to accumulate drift via a different vector) are defeated by the UNION enforcement — cumulative drift is evaluated across the UNION of rate-card + cost_base proposals on the same scope. Withdrawn proposals remain in the cumulative-drift tally so withdraw-and-resubmit evasion is also defeated; the withdrawal-rate-limit in AC #14 prevents volumetric abuse of withdrawals as a separate signal.

**Failure mode 8 — withdrawal abuse for approver surveillance or fatigue (Authored Extension #42; §50 Phase 6 Verification Remediation 2026-04-21).** A malicious or misbehaving Pricing Admin proposer rapidly creates, simulates, and withdraws PricingAdminChangeProposal rows (20+ per day) to either (a) accumulate approver fatigue — approvers start rubber-stamping the next real proposal — or (b) surveil approver behavioral signals by watching which proposals get clicked-into vs. ignored. A coordinated multi-proposer ring could amortize the per-proposer cap by round-robin withdrawal. Mitigation: AC #14 rate-limit enforces per-proposer cap ≤ 10 withdrawals per rolling 24 h AND team-wide cap ≤ 40 withdrawals per rolling 24 h; the team-wide cap absorbs multi-proposer coordination. Every team-wide cap breach auto-pages `ops_security_admin` as a coordinated-abuse signal. Property-test `pricing_admin_withdrawal_rate_limit_property_test` asserts across 1,000 simulated streams for both per-proposer and team-wide caps including multi-proposer round-robin patterns. Legitimate approver-fatigue countermeasures (approver-requested proposer feedback; rotation of approvers per proposal batch) are out of scope for AC #14 and captured as Pending Follow-Through.

## 50.13 Baseline Assumption Manager {#50.13-baseline-assumption-manager}

### 50.13.1 Purpose and Scope {#50.13.1-purpose-and-scope}

§50.13 authors the Ops Console surface for editing the **baseline assumption library** — the conversion factors used by the §4.3.19 Time-Saved Credit computation, the Time-Saved Baseline Model referenced in Summary §6.35 Master Summary C.97, and any downstream heuristics (outcome-verification baselines, cost-benefit projections in §28 Public Pricing calculators, efficacy narratives in seller marketplace copy §27). Every assumption is versioned; no in-flight Time-Saved Credit is recomputed under a new version (see §4.3.19 `conversion_factor_version`), but new Time-Saved emissions use the currently-published version as of emission time.

Scope: platform-scoped; residency isolation by region (EU cohorts may diverge in baseline inputs).

Plan gating: N/A (platform). Surface: §50.3.2-gated to role `ops_baseline_admin` (new granular role; registered in §50.13.7 extension) and `ops_admin`.

Retention: baseline assumptions and versions retain 10 years (finance + product defensibility). DSAR: platform-scoped; no DSAR implication.

### 50.13.2 BaselineAssumption (Entity) {#50.13.2-baselineassumption}

Represents a single assumption concept (e.g., "Time saved per MCP-automated intake triage").

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK | |
| `key` | string | NOT NULL, UNIQUE, kebab-case, ≤ 96 chars | e.g., `time-saved-per-mcp-intake-triage-minutes` |
| `display_name` | string | NOT NULL, ≤ 120 chars | |
| `description` | text | NOT NULL, ≥ 200 chars | Narrative justifying the assumption's role in product computations |
| `unit_kind` | enum `baseline_assumption_unit_kind` | NOT NULL | Values: `minutes`, `hours`, `dollars`, `count`, `ratio`, `probability`, `index_score`, `custom` |
| `unit_custom_label` | string | Nullable | Required when `unit_kind='custom'` |
| `applicability_scope` | JSONB | NOT NULL | `{ consumers: string[], cohort_filters: JSONB }` — consumers like `time_saved_credit`, `outcome_verification_baseline`, etc. |
| `provenance_source` | enum `baseline_assumption_provenance_kind` | NOT NULL | Values: `customer_survey`, `internal_telemetry`, `public_research`, `expert_estimate`, `mixed` |
| `provenance_notes` | text | Nullable, ≤ 4,000 chars | References and methodology summary |
| `current_version_id` | FK §50.13.3 | Nullable | The active published version |
| `state` | enum `baseline_assumption_state` | NOT NULL | Values: `active`, `retired` |
| `residency_region_applicability` | enum `residency_region`[] | NOT NULL | Residency regions where this assumption applies |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | | | Standard |

Scope: platform-scoped. Required indexes: `(key)`, `(state, residency_region_applicability)`.

### 50.13.3 BaselineAssumptionVersion (Entity) {#50.13.3-baselineassumptionversion}

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |

Scope: platform-scoped. Indexes: `(assumption_id, state)`, `(state, published_at)`.

**State machine:**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| — | `drafting` | `POST /ops/baseline-assumptions/:id/versions` | |
| `drafting` | `piloting` | `POST /.../pilot` | Sandbox rollout against synthetic Time-Saved computations |
| `piloting` | `awaiting_approval` | `POST /.../submit-for-approval` | |
| `awaiting_approval` | `published` | `POST /.../publish` | Two-approver gate satisfied if fired; prior `current_version_id` superseded |
| `awaiting_approval` | `drafting` | `POST /.../request-revisions` | |
| `published` | `rolled_back` | `POST /.../rollback` | `rollback_successor_version_id` set to prior published |
| `published` | `superseded` | Next version publishes | |

`rolled_back`, `superseded` terminal relative to in-flight state.

### 50.13.4 Downstream Consumer Binding {#50.13.4-downstream-consumer-binding}

§4.3.19 Time-Saved Credit already carries `conversion_factor_version` (per the pre-existing data model). §50.13 extends the contract:

- Every Time-Saved Credit written after a new BaselineAssumptionVersion is published MUST bind its `conversion_factor_version` to the version id of the underlying BaselineAssumption-set at emission time.
- §4.3.19 `conversion_factor_minutes` MUST equal the `value_numeric` of the bound version at emission time; server validates at insert.
- Retroactive recomputation is explicitly NOT performed; §4.3.19 values are immutable post-emission. Downstream reporting surfaces (seller ROI dashboards, buyer procurement ROI views) present amounts under their emission-time factor with a footnote linking to the active version.
- A BaselineAssumption rollback creates a NEW `published` version (with `rollback_successor_version_id` pointing to the prior) rather than mutating existing credits.

Other consumers:

- §28 Public Pricing calculator embeds the current published version(s) at page render; calculator pages carry `baseline_assumption_version_set_hash` so caches invalidate on publish.
- §27 Marketplace seller copy may embed a baseline citation (e.g., "average 47 min saved per triage"); citations are server-rendered using currently-published version; SOC-2 audit trail includes the version referenced.
- Summary §6.35 Master Summary references are informational only; no programmatic binding required.

### 50.13.5 Pilot and Rollout Surface {#50.13.5-pilot-and-rollout-surface}

Before publish, a pilot run exercises the draft version against:

1. A 30-day backtest of Time-Saved emissions (replay synthetic emissions under new factor; surface projected distribution shift via KS statistic vs. current).
2. A sensitivity matrix: how proposed change affects headline metrics in seller ROI and buyer procurement-ROI dashboards (absolute and relative deltas).
3. A variance analysis: per-cohort (plan tier, residency, industry) spread vs. historical cohort values.

Pilot output entity `BaselineAssumptionPilotRun`:

| Field | Notes |
| :---- | :---- |
| `id` / `version_id` / `state` / `run_at` | Standard |
| `backtest_window_start` / `backtest_window_end` | |
| `ks_statistic` | |
| `cohort_variance_table` | JSONB |
| `sensitivity_matrix` | JSONB |
| `warnings` | JSONB array — e.g., `{ kind: 'high_variance', cohort: 'seller_pro_eu', magnitude: 0.32 }` |

### 50.13.6 Ops UX {#50.13.6-ops-ux}

Primary screen at `/baseline-assumptions`. Table view: assumption key, consumers, current version semver, last-published-at, drift-last-12-months chip (min/median/max absolute drift across historical versions), applicability-scope chips. Click-through opens the assumption detail page with:

- Version history timeline with drift labels per transition.
- Current-value card with p50 / p10 / p90 (for composite versions).
- "Propose new version" CTA → opens the BaselineAssumptionVersion authoring flow: value editor (scalar or composite), derivation-method picker with input snapshot uploader, justification textarea, pilot-run launcher, submit-for-approval CTA.
- "View consumers" panel: every downstream system bound to this assumption (§4.3.19, §28 calculator, marketplace listings citing it), with live count of emissions / renders / citations in the last 30 days.
- Rollback CTA: visible to `ops_admin`; requires a rollback justification and surfaces the projected customer-visible impact count.

Retention controls: every version row displays derivation input URI (opens signed S3 preview for authorized role); expired URIs (retention boundary reached) display an archival reference pointer.

### 50.13.8 Appendix Extensions (Authored) {#50.13.8-appendix-extensions}

**Appendix C — new events:** `baseline_assumption.version_published`, `baseline_assumption.version_rolled_back`, `baseline_assumption.retired`.

**Appendix G — new PostHog events:** `ops_baseline_version_created`, `ops_baseline_version_piloted`, `ops_baseline_version_published`, `ops_baseline_version_rolled_back`, `ops_baseline_consumer_queried`.

**Appendix J — new enum values:**

- `baseline_assumption_unit_kind`: `minutes`, `hours`, `dollars`, `count`, `ratio`, `probability`, `index_score`, `custom`.
- `baseline_assumption_provenance_kind`: `customer_survey`, `internal_telemetry`, `public_research`, `expert_estimate`, `mixed`.
- `baseline_assumption_state`: `active`, `retired`.
- `baseline_assumption_version_state`: `drafting`, `piloting`, `awaiting_approval`, `published`, `superseded`, `rolled_back`.
- `baseline_assumption_derivation_kind`: `static_ops_input`, `computed_from_telemetry`, `survey_weighted`, `meta_analysis`, `bayesian_update`.
- `ops_action_kind` — add: `baseline_assumption_version_publish`, `baseline_assumption_version_rollback`, `baseline_assumption_retire`.

### 50.13.9 Acceptance Criteria {#50.13.9-acceptance-criteria}

1. Every published BaselineAssumptionVersion MUST have a `piloted` run attached within the prior 30 days; publish without pilot returns HTTP 412.
2. Drift ≥ 15% relative to prior published value MUST require two-approver gate; unsatisfied gate returns HTTP 412 (`baseline_assumption_version_publish_forbidden`). Property-test: 10,000 simulated permutations.
3. Every §4.3.19 Time-Saved Credit MUST bind `conversion_factor_version` to the published version id in effect at emission time; retroactive updates are rejected (insert-time validation; mutation returns HTTP 409). Integration test.
4. Rollback MUST create a new published version (`rolled_back_at` + `rollback_successor_version_id`) rather than mutating any prior version; existing Time-Saved Credits retain their emission-time version. Property-test.
5. Every §50.13 mutation MUST emit §4.6.1 Audit Event + §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord with `linked_ops_session_id`. Audit-integrity property-test.
6. Customer-visible projection of a Time-Saved amount MUST render a "Methodology version vX.Y.Z" footnote linking to the §28 public baseline methodology page; the page renders the corresponding BaselineAssumptionVersion description and provenance.
7. Assumption retirement MUST be blocked if any `conversion_factor_version IS NULL` field is referenced by an open emission window of an active Outcome Contract (§4.8.4); server returns HTTP 409 (`baseline_assumption_consumer_binding_conflict`).
8. Proposed values outside `value_validity_bounds` MUST be rejected (HTTP 422).
9. Pilot runs MUST publish their KS statistic, cohort variance, and warnings; the approver page MUST surface any `high_variance` warnings with a mandatory "Acknowledge variance" checkbox before approval.
10. Consumer binding (§50.13.4) MUST be idempotent: replays of Time-Saved emissions under a rollback produce identical outputs (reproducibility property-test).

### 50.13.10 Counterfactual Failure-Mode Pass {#50.13.10-counterfactual-failure-mode-pass}

**Failure mode 1 — stealth factor edit changes customer ROI narratives silently.** Mitigation: versioning is append-only; published versions are immutable; the customer-visible methodology page displays version semver + publish timestamp; any §27 marketplace citation embeds the version hash at render; cache invalidation on publish ensures all surfaces align.

**Failure mode 2 — rollback corrupts prior emissions.** Mitigation: §4.3.19 emissions are immutable; rollback publishes a NEW version; downstream reporting surfaces display emission-time factors and allow users to view "If re-measured under latest version" comparison (read-only) without mutating records.

**Failure mode 3 — cohort-variance blindspot.** A global median baseline masks large variance in one residency. Mitigation: pilot run's cohort-variance matrix MUST be surfaced; `high_variance` warnings (threshold cohort σ / global σ > 1.5) block one-click approval; approver must type a variance-acknowledgment justification.

**Failure mode 4 — provenance drift (customer-survey staleness).** Survey-based assumption ages without refresh. Mitigation: each assumption carries a `provenance_freshness_horizon_days` (default 365); §50.14 Finance/Product dashboard surfaces overdue refreshes; overdue > 180 days opens a P2 Product ticket.

**Failure mode 5 — downstream consumer binding drift.** §27 marketplace listings carry stale baseline citations after publish. Mitigation: server-render citations against `current_version_id`; cache bust on publish event; fallback to last published version if current lookup fails; stale-citation alarm raised after 30 s propagation breach.

## 50.14 Internal Analytics Dashboards by Role {#50.14-internal-analytics-dashboards-by-role}

### 50.14.1 Purpose and Scope {#50.14.1-purpose-and-scope}

§50.14 authors the Ops Console's role-specific analytics dashboards, each scoped to the operational signals most relevant to a particular Ops function. All dashboards source their data via the **customer-API** and the **PostHog analytics pipeline** — never via direct DB access (see §50.14.2 invariant #1). Each dashboard refreshes on a cadence appropriate to its role (realtime, 15 min, hourly, daily) and carries its own §50.14 SLO.

Plan gating: N/A. Role gating: every dashboard is gated by its owning Ops role per §50.14 role-dashboard matrix.

Retention: dashboard configuration versioned (10 years); computed materialized views refresh per cadence (retention 90 days rolling per §40.2 analytics).

DSAR: dashboards may surface customer-identifiable aggregates; any per-org drill-through is an `ops_session`-gated action and emits a §4.6.1 Audit Event with the org id surfaced.

### 50.14.2 Cross-Dashboard Invariants {#50.14.2-cross-dashboard-invariants}

1. Data source discipline: every widget MUST source from either a §32 customer-API endpoint (with Ops auth scope) or the PostHog materialized-view service; direct DB reads are forbidden. CI gate `ops_dashboard_source_is_customer_api` asserts, inheriting from the pre-existing §50 AC.
2. Widget freshness: every widget MUST render its `last_refreshed_at` timestamp and a refresh-cadence chip.
3. Drill-through lineage: every widget that supports drill-through to per-org details MUST emit a §4.6.1 Audit Event (`actor_type='ops_actor'`, `ops_session_id`, `policy_key='dashboard_drill_through'`) for every drill.
4. Residency isolation: a US-residency Ops user MUST NOT see EU-residency per-org data; widgets MUST respect residency in their source query; aggregated global-KPI widgets MAY aggregate across residencies only when the user's role includes `analytics.global_aggregate.read`.
5. PII projection: dashboards MUST NOT project customer user PII (names, emails) unless the viewing Ops role has `pii.read`; widgets fallback to pseudonymous `org_id` + `workspace_id` otherwise.
6. Export gating: CSV / JSON export from any dashboard MUST require `analytics.export` capability, MUST emit a §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord, and MUST be watermarked with the exporting Ops user's pseudonym and a retention expiry of 7 days.
7. Dashboard config versioning: every dashboard has a semver config row; config changes follow a light two-approver flow (peer `ops_analyst` + `ops_admin`) when the change alters data sources or refresh cadence.

### 50.14.3 Growth PM Dashboard {#50.14.3-growth-pm-dashboard}

| Activation rate by acquisition channel | `/ops/analytics/activation-by-channel` | Channel performance | Any channel activation < 20% |
| Retention D1/D7/D30 | PostHog retention model | Cohort retention curves | D7 retention < 30% |
| Feature adoption Pareto | `/ops/analytics/feature-adoption` | Top 20 features by % orgs using | N/A |
| Experiments ledger | Convex feature-flag service via customer-API | Active A/B tests and effect sizes | Experiment running > 60 days without readout |

**Drill-through:** from funnel drop to per-org profile (requires `org.read.deep` capability; audit-logged).

| `dashboard_pii_projection_capability_denied` | 403 | PII projection requested without `pii.read` |

### 50.14.10 Appendix Extensions (Authored) {#50.14.10-appendix-extensions}

**Appendix G — new PostHog events:** `ops_dashboard_viewed`, `ops_dashboard_widget_drill_through`, `ops_dashboard_export_enqueued`, `ops_dashboard_export_completed`, `ops_dashboard_config_published`.

**Appendix J — new enum values:**

- `ops_analytics_dashboard_kind`: `growth_pm`, `gtm_lead`, `support`, `fraud_analyst`, `finance`.
- `ops_dashboard_pii_projection_mode`: `none`, `pseudonymous`, `full_on_capability`.
- `ops_action_kind` — add: `dashboard_drill_through`, `dashboard_export`, `dashboard_config_publish`.

**§50.3.1 new granular Ops roles:** `ops_growth_pm`, `ops_gtm_lead`, `ops_fraud_analyst`, `ops_finance`, `ops_analyst` (dashboard-config authoring).

### 50.14.11 Acceptance Criteria {#50.14.11-acceptance-criteria}

1. Every dashboard widget MUST source from a registered customer-API endpoint OR the PostHog materialized-view service; publish blocked otherwise (HTTP 403, `dashboard_source_not_customer_api`). CI gate asserts at every dashboard-config merge.
2. Every widget render MUST include a `last_refreshed_at` timestamp; missing timestamp fails render-time assertion (fatal to the widget, non-fatal to the dashboard).
3. Drill-through MUST emit a §4.6.1 Audit Event with `policy_key='dashboard_drill_through'` and `ops_session_id`; missing audit fails property-test.
4. Residency isolation: a US-residency Ops user's dashboard query MUST NOT return any EU-residency per-org row; widget engine filters residency server-side; breach returns HTTP 403. Property-test across 10,000 simulated queries.
5. PII projection without `pii.read` MUST return pseudonymous identifiers only; serializer-level assertion.
6. Export MUST be watermarked with the exporting Ops user's pseudonym, export timestamp, and retention expiry (7 days); subsequent access after expiry returns HTTP 410.
7. Dashboard config mutations altering `source` or `refresh_cadence` MUST require two-approver publish; peer-review-only patches to cosmetic fields allowed via single approver (audited).
8. Dashboard page first-load p95 ≤ 1.5 s; widget render p95 ≤ 2.0 s; breach triggers §50.8 Ops-performance SLO alert.
9. Breach-alert widgets (threshold-based) MUST emit a PostHog event `ops_dashboard_breach_detected` with widget id, threshold, observed value, residency — downstream alerting consumes.
10. Export job MUST fail gracefully for > 1M rows; surface export-size guidance; offer async-delivery-via-email alternative.
11. Every §50.14 mutation MUST emit §4.6.1 Audit Event + §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord. Audit-integrity property-test.
12. Breach of the `ops_dashboard_source_is_customer_api` CI gate MUST block merge to main; regression test asserts.

### 50.14.12 Counterfactual Failure-Mode Pass {#50.14.12-counterfactual-failure-mode-pass}

**Failure mode 1 — widget author adds a direct-DB source for convenience.** Mitigation: CI gate at merge-time rejects; runtime assertion at dashboard-load rejects any source not in registered customer-API allowlist (`dashboard_source_not_customer_api`, HTTP 403); config cannot reach `published` state without gate pass.

**Failure mode 2 — Ops user exports and exfiltrates PII.** Mitigation: exports are capability-gated (`analytics.export`), watermarked with user pseudonym, retention 7 days; downloads emit OpsActionRecord; anomalous export-volume per user triggers §50.14.6 Fraud dashboard alert; DLP policy on Ops-device egress (§50.2.2 MDM).

**Failure mode 3 — per-org drill-through leaks residency.** Mitigation: server-side residency filter on every drill-through query; breach returns HTTP 403 (`dashboard_residency_leakage_blocked`); property-test asserts across 10,000 residency-permutation queries.

**Failure mode 4 — breach-alert flooding from a single misconfigured widget.** Mitigation: per-widget alert rate-limit (max 1 alert per threshold breach per 15 min window); §50.14.2 invariant extends — alert config requires §50.14.8 two-approver publish for alert sensitivity changes; observability surfaces alert-volume anomalies to Ops Admin.

**Failure mode 5 — stale dashboard during an incident.** Support agent views a 15-min-stale "open tickets" widget during P0 outage, misdiagnoses. Mitigation: Support dashboard is realtime (≤ 30 s); widgets degrade to a prominent "Stale — last refresh > 2× cadence" banner when lag breaches 2× cadence; drill-through disabled while stale.

**Failure mode 6 — dashboard config drift across environments.** Prod dashboard config differs from staging after hotfix. Mitigation: config-version promotion flow binds staging config to a publish-candidate; publish-to-prod replays the signed config blob; checksum verification at each environment boundary.
