## 50.15 Signal Integrity Monitor — Detector, Review, and Kill-Switch Surface {#50.15-signal-integrity-monitor-detector-review-and-kill-switch-surface}

### 50.15.1 Purpose and Scope {#50.15.1-purpose-and-scope}

§50.15 authors the **Ops Console surface** for Sourcera's Signal Integrity Monitor (SIM, Summary C.100). §50.15 is the Ops-operational home of the SIM contract. It does not re-author the data model or cross-loop semantics that already live in §2.3.5 (narrative), §48.4 (anti-spam control cross-links), §48.4.10 (pre-existing SIM signal-class catalog — eleven classes), §48.4.12 (seller pricing acceptable-use floor), §48.2.12.4 (GrowthLoopKillSwitch entity and 60-second publish-path contract), §50.3.2 (capability envelope matrix rows for SIM signal review and kill-switch activation), §50.6.3 (Ops Console cross-cutting SIM contract), and §50.14.6 (Fraud Analyst Dashboard realtime widgets). §50.15 authors, in one place, the pieces that were previously distributed:

1. The **two new SIM entities** — `SIMSignal` (detector fire; append-only) and `SIMCase` (analyst-owned investigation). Pre-§50.15 the Spec referenced a "SIM signal" abstractly; §50.15 gives it schema.
2. The **four new detector categories** named verbatim in Summary C.100: anomalous query patterns, referral velocity spikes, suspicious uploads, email sender-reputation drift. These extend (do not replace) the pre-existing eleven §48.4.10 signal classes.
3. The **SIMCase lifecycle state machine** (`flagged → investigating → resolved → escalated`) and its transition gating.
4. The **one-click-per-growth-mechanic kill-switch wiring** — UX target, activation path, 60-second global propagation contract (reused from §48.2.12.4), Ops-Admin-only reversibility (tightened from §48.2.12.4 for SIM-initiated activations), and the mandatory Slack alert to the on-call engineering channel on every kill-switch state transition.
5. The **SIM-scoped API, webhook, PostHog, error-code, and Appendix J enum registrations** that make the surface buildable.

**Numbering reconciliation.** The authoring task brief referenced §49.11 / §49.12 / §49.13. Applied prior §49→§50 numbering decision (logged in the preceding §50 reconciliation entries at `/Sourcera/_integration/RECONCILIATION.md`): §49 remains Seller Onboarding (preserves the 53 existing §49 cross-references); the Ops Console is §50; new Ops-Console subsections continue the §50.10–§50.14 sequence. Therefore the task's §49.11 → §50.15, §49.12 → §50.16, §49.13 → §50.17. No prior content was displaced.

**Cross-link to §48.4 anti-spam controls (required by task brief).** SIM is the aggregation and human-review layer atop the §48.4.1–§48.4.9 anti-spam primitives. Every §48.4 control fire MAY produce a `SIMSignal` row in accordance with the §48.4.10 signal-class catalog. §50.15 adds four NEW detector categories native to the SIM surface (§50.15.4) that extend the §48.4.10 signal-class catalog (§50.15.5). The relationship is: §48.4 = the *detectors* (many, distributed, per-control); §48.4.10 = the *signal-class registry* (the controlled vocabulary all detectors use); §50.15 = the *human-review surface* (review queue, case lifecycle, Ops actions, kill-switch). A §48.4 control that fires without producing a SIMSignal row is a CI-gate failure (§50.15.11 AC #5).

**Plan gating.** SIM is platform-internal; not plan-gated. The surface is §50.3.2-gated to roles `ops_admin`, `ops_security_admin`, `ops_fraud_analyst`, and `ops_sim_admin` (pre-existing). Support agents and template reviewers have no SIM access (no read, no write).

**Retention and DSAR.** `SIMSignal` and `SIMCase` rows are Ops-audit-class artifacts. Retention 7 years per §40.2 Ops audit horizon. On DSAR right-to-erasure for a target user or Org, `target_user_id` / `target_org_id` fields are pseudonymized per §6.8; signal and case structure, detector metadata, and Ops reviewer pseudonyms are retained for aggregate fraud analytics. `raw_detector_evidence_json` with customer-PII payloads is truncated at 10 years (Ops retention exceeds customer retention for financial-fraud-defense reasons; §45.1 regulatory-defense exemption).

### 50.15.2 `SIMSignal` Entity (Platform-Scoped, Ops Audit, Append-Only) {#50.15.2-simsignal-entity}

**Authoring intent.** One row per detector fire. Immutable post-write. Materializes what §48.4.10 previously described only as a concept. `SIMSignal` is the atomic unit of SIM; `SIMCase` (§50.15.3) aggregates one or more signals under a single analyst review. Pre-existing PostHog event `sim_signal_emitted` (per §48.4.10) gains a 1:1 correspondence with `SIMSignal` rows (§50.15.10 registers the row-write as the emitter of the PostHog event).

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK, immutable | Standard. |
| `signal_class` | Enum | Appendix J `sim_signal_class` (existing eleven + four new from §50.15.5); required | The signal-class catalog entry. |
| `detector_id` | Enum | Appendix J `sim_detector_id` (new; registry of concrete detectors); required | The concrete detector instance (e.g., `referral_velocity_detector_v3`). Bound to `signal_class` via §50.15.4 detector catalog. |
| `detector_version` | String | Semver; ≤ 32 chars; required | For auditability across detector rollouts. |
| `severity` | Enum | Appendix J `sim_signal_severity` (existing: `informational`, `warning`, `critical`); required | Severity at emit time. Ops MAY re-stamp at `SIMCase` creation (§50.15.6 AC #3); the original `severity` persists immutably. |
| `auto_kill_switch_eligible` | Boolean | Required | Mirrors the §48.4.10 column; determined by `signal_class` + `detector_id`; NOT re-computable at row write (emitter supplies). |
| `target_scope_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `sim_signal_target_scope_kind` (new: `platform`, `org`, `user`, `capability`, `growth_loop`, `listing`, `marketplace_domain`, `email_sender_domain`); required | What the signal targets. |
| `target_org_id` | UUID (FK) | → Organization; nullable | Populated when `target_scope_kind ∈ {org, user, growth_loop, listing}` and the target has an owning Org. |
| `target_user_id` | UUID (FK) | → User; nullable | Populated when `target_scope_kind='user'`. |
| `target_ref_type` | Enum | Appendix J `sim_signal_target_ref_type` (new; polymorphic FK kind); nullable | Polymorphic ref kind when the target is an entity beyond Org/User. |
| `target_ref_id` | UUID | Nullable; polymorphic FK per `target_ref_type` | The specific target row. |
| `triggering_event_ids` | Array[UUID] | 0–50 entries; FK to PostHog event ids OR §48 detector-event ids; required (may be empty for platform-level signals) | The evidence the detector relied on. Cap 50 keeps payload ≤ 256 KB per §31.5. |
| `raw_detector_evidence_json` | JSON | ≤ 32,000 chars; required | Detector-local payload (feature values, anomaly score, threshold, cohort stats). Truncated at emit time if over budget; truncation recorded via `evidence_truncated_at_emit=true`. |
| `evidence_truncated_at_emit` | Boolean | Required; defaults `false` | Truncation flag. |
| `signal_state` | Enum | Appendix J `sim_signal_state` (new: `open`, `rolled_into_case`, `auto_dismissed`, `expired`); required | Lifecycle state of the signal. See §50.15.6 signal-to-case roll-up rules. |
| `rolled_into_case_id` | UUID (FK) | → `SIMCase`; nullable | Set when `signal_state='rolled_into_case'`. |
| `auto_dismissed_reason` | Enum | Appendix J `sim_signal_auto_dismiss_reason` (new: `below_severity_threshold`, `k_anonymity_floor_not_met`, `detector_false_positive_model_override`, `superseded_by_later_signal`); nullable | Populated when `signal_state='auto_dismissed'`. |
| `emitted_at` | Timestamp | Required; immutable | When the detector fired. |
| `ingested_at` | Timestamp | Required | When SIM wrote the row. `ingested_at - emitted_at ≤ 60 s p95` per §50.15.11 AC #2. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by` | Standard | `updated_*` writable only by SIM ingest pipeline on `signal_state` transitions; no `deleted_at` (append-only) | No soft delete. |

**Scope isolation.** Platform-scoped. Console enum not applicable (platform audit). Not customer-readable. Ops read access limited to roles listed in §50.15.1 plan-gating clause.

**Required indexes.** `(signal_class, emitted_at DESC)`; `(target_org_id, emitted_at DESC) WHERE target_org_id IS NOT NULL`; `(target_user_id, emitted_at DESC) WHERE target_user_id IS NOT NULL`; `(signal_state, severity, emitted_at DESC)` partial for `signal_state='open'`; `(rolled_into_case_id) WHERE rolled_into_case_id IS NOT NULL`; `(detector_id, detector_version, emitted_at DESC)` for detector-performance analytics.

**Atomicity requirement.** SIM ingest writes a `SIMSignal` row AND emits the parallel `sim_signal_emitted` PostHog event in a single Convex transaction. Partial write raises `sim_signal_atomic_write_violation` (Appendix I — new; HTTP 500) and pages `ops_security_admin`.

**Append-only invariant.** UPDATE is permitted only by the SIM ingest pipeline for the two transitions (`open → rolled_into_case`, `open → auto_dismissed`); DELETE is forbidden in all cases. UPDATE / DELETE attempts outside the ingest pipeline raise `sim_signal_append_only` (Appendix I — new; HTTP 405).

### 50.15.3 `SIMCase` Entity (Platform-Scoped, Ops Audit, Analyst-Owned) {#50.15.3-simcase-entity}

**Authoring intent.** An analyst-owned investigation aggregating one or more `SIMSignal` rows under a single case with a deterministic lifecycle. Every Fraud Analyst action surface in §50.16 operates in the context of a `SIMCase`.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `id` | UUID | PK, immutable | Standard. |
| `case_state` | Enum | Appendix J `sim_case_state` (new: `flagged`, `investigating`, `resolved`, `escalated`); required | State machine in §50.15.6. |
| `severity_at_open` | Enum | Appendix J `sim_signal_severity`; required | Max severity across aggregated `SIMSignal` rows at case creation. |
| `severity_current` | Enum | Appendix J `sim_signal_severity`; required | May be adjusted by analyst on `flagged → investigating`; §50.15.6 AC #3 permits adjustment UP or DOWN once. |
| `aggregated_signal_class_set` | Array[Enum] | Appendix J `sim_signal_class`; 1–20 entries; required | De-duplicated set of classes across aggregated signals. |
| `aggregated_signal_ids` | Array[UUID] | 1–500 entries; FKs → `SIMSignal.id`; required | All signals rolled into this case. Upper bound avoids unbounded case sprawl; exceeding raises `sim_case_signal_cardinality_exceeded` (Appendix I — new; HTTP 422), emits `sim_case_signal_overflow_rolled_to_new_case` (Appendix G — new), and opens a sibling case. |
| `target_scope_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `sim_signal_target_scope_kind`; required | Inherits from the dominant aggregated-signal target; see §50.15.6 AC #2 for "dominant" rule. |
| `target_org_id` | UUID (FK) | → Organization; nullable | Same rules as §50.15.2. |
| `target_user_id` | UUID (FK) | → User; nullable | Same. |
| `target_ref_type`, `target_ref_id` | Enum + UUID | Nullable | Same. |
| `assigned_ops_user_id` | UUID (FK) | → Ops User (must hold `ops_fraud_analyst` or `ops_sim_admin`); nullable | Null while `case_state='flagged'`; non-null from `investigating` onward. |
| `investigation_note` | Text | 0–10,000 chars; nullable | Analyst's running note. |
| `resolution_kind` | Enum | Appendix J `sim_case_resolution_kind` (new: `false_positive`, `upheld_action_taken`, `upheld_no_action`, `merged_into_case`, `expired_no_action`); nullable | Populated on transition to `resolved` or `escalated`; on `escalated` the populated value indicates the resolution INTENT prior to escalation. |
| `resolution_note` | Text | 50–4,000 chars; required when `resolution_kind != null` | Analyst rationale. |
| `escalated_to_role` | Enum | Appendix J `ops_role`; required when `case_state='escalated'` | `ops_admin`, `ops_security_admin`, `ops_compliance_admin`, or `ops_council`. |
| `escalation_reason` | Enum | Appendix J `sim_case_escalation_reason` (new: `cross_console_action_required`, `dual_sign_off_required`, `legal_review_required`, `pattern_exceeds_analyst_authority`, `repeat_offender_threshold_met`, `other_analyst_discretion`); required when `case_state='escalated'` | |
| `linked_kill_switch_action_ids` | Array[UUID] | FKs → §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord; 0–10 entries | OpsActionRecords produced by kill-switch activations referenced from this case. |
| `linked_fraud_action_ids` | Array[UUID] | FKs → §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord; 0–20 entries | OpsActionRecords produced by §50.16 Fraud Analyst actions (`fraud_org_suspend`, `fraud_user_suspend`, `fraud_referral_credit_reverse`, `fraud_opt_out_claim_revoke`). |
| `merged_into_case_id` | UUID (FK) | → `SIMCase`; nullable | When `resolution_kind='merged_into_case'`. Merge target inherits this case's `aggregated_signal_ids`. |
| `flagged_at`, `investigating_at`, `resolved_at`, `escalated_at` | Timestamp | Nullable; set on each state entry | State-entry stamps. |
| `case_deadline_at` | Timestamp | Required; immutable after first set | SLA deadline per §50.15.6 AC #5: `flagged_at + max_triage_sla_by_severity(severity_at_open)`. |
| `sla_breach_at` | Timestamp | Nullable | Set on breach of `case_deadline_at`; triggers `sim_case_sla_breach` (Appendix G — new). |
| `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at` | Standard | Soft-deletable by `ops_admin` with dual sign-off only; deletion is for data-error recovery, not business action | Standard. |

**Scope isolation.** Platform-scoped. Not customer-readable. Ops read access: `ops_admin`, `ops_security_admin`, `ops_fraud_analyst`, `ops_sim_admin`, `ops_compliance_admin`.

**Required indexes.** `(case_state, severity_current, flagged_at DESC)` partial for `case_state IN ('flagged', 'investigating')`; `(assigned_ops_user_id, case_state)`; `(target_org_id, flagged_at DESC) WHERE target_org_id IS NOT NULL`; `(case_deadline_at) WHERE case_state IN ('flagged', 'investigating')` for SLA sweeps; `(escalated_to_role, escalated_at DESC) WHERE case_state='escalated'`.

### 50.15.4 Detector Catalog — Four New Categories (Task Brief Verbatim) {#50.15.4-detector-catalog-four-new-categories}

§50.15.4 specifies the four detectors named in Summary C.100 and the authoring task brief. Each detector maps to a new `sim_signal_class` enum value registered in §50.15.5 and a `sim_detector_id` enum value. Pre-existing §48.4.10 detectors continue to operate unchanged; §50.15.4 is additive.

| Detector Category | `sim_detector_id` | Emits `sim_signal_class` | Primary Inputs | Computation Cadence | Threshold Logic (v1 seed) | Default Severity | Auto-Kill-Switch Eligible? |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Anomalous query patterns** | `anomalous_query_pattern_detector_v1` | `anomalous_query_pattern` | §16 Org Intelligence query logs; §16 RAG/Market-Intelligence retrieval logs; §22 KB retrieval logs; §27 Marketplace search logs | On-write incremental rolling-30-min window + nightly full-day sweep | Per-Org query-rate z-score > 3.5 across rolling 30 min OR per-user query-rate z-score > 4.0 OR rare-query-shape fingerprint (e.g., enumeration across capability ids, listing ids, org ids) ≥ k-anonymity-violating rate over rolling 24h | `warning` by default; `critical` when `rare_query_shape_fingerprint` triggers | No (analyst review required; bulk data-exfiltration risk can be latent) |
| **Referral velocity spikes** | `referral_velocity_detector_v2` | `referral_velocity_spike` | §4.3.16 Buyer Referral rows (existing); §48.2.12 GrowthLoopExecution L1/L6 rows | On-write incremental rolling-7-day window | Per-referrer-Org referral creation count > 10 in rolling 7d (matches §4.3.16 `velocity_flag`); per-referrer-Org referral creation count > 25 in rolling 7d triggers `critical` | `warning` at 10; `critical` at 25 | Yes at `critical` (auto-pauses M16 Buyer Referral credit issuance for the referrer Org pending analyst review — does NOT trip a platform-wide kill-switch, scope is `org`) |
| **Suspicious uploads** | `suspicious_upload_detector_v1` | `suspicious_upload` | §22 KB upload events; §10 bid response attachments; §27.8 abuse report evidence uploads; §4.5.7 subject-snapshot uploads | On-write synchronous + async deep scan | Sync: MIME-type vs. file-content mismatch; embedded executable / script payload; known-malware hash match against ClamAV signatures; PII-leak regex on file contents (SSN, credit card, JWT). Async: ML-based content-anomaly score > 0.85 on the upload | `critical` for sync hits (blocks the upload at write); `warning` for async hits (upload persists pending analyst review) | Yes at `critical` sync hits (the upload is blocked at write; `auto_kill_switch` here means the uploading user's future uploads are quarantined pending analyst review, not a growth-mechanic kill-switch) |
| **Email sender-reputation drift** | `email_sender_reputation_detector_v1` | `email_sender_reputation_drift` | Summary §6.28 Loops.so bounce + complaint + spam-report telemetry; DMARC/SPF/DKIM pass rate per sender domain; Google Postmaster Tools + Microsoft SNDS signals (polled hourly) | Hourly aggregate + daily rollup | Per-sender-domain bounce rate > 5% (24h rolling), OR complaint rate > 0.3% (24h rolling), OR DMARC pass rate < 95% over 7d, OR Google Postmaster reputation score drop > 2 deciles in 7d | `warning` at any single threshold breach; `critical` at any two thresholds breached concurrently | Yes at `critical` (auto-pauses the affected sender-domain's outbound email via §48.4.1 email throttling + rerouting to a lower-reputation sub-domain pending analyst review) |

**Detector-to-§48.4-control cross-reference.** Detectors 1, 3, 4 are NEW primary sources of SIM signals (no §48.4 control authored them previously). Detector 2 OVERLAPS with the pre-existing §48.4.10 `velocity_anomaly` signal class origin (§48.4.6 referrals); §50.15.4 authors a dedicated referral-specific signal class (`referral_velocity_spike`) because the task brief enumerates it verbatim. The §48.4.10 `velocity_anomaly` signal class continues to exist for non-referral velocity contexts (email, L1/L2 invite velocity). Both classes may fire for a referral event; the §50.15 SIM ingest de-duplicates via the `triggering_event_ids` overlap check and rolls both into a single `SIMCase` with `aggregated_signal_class_set=['velocity_anomaly', 'referral_velocity_spike']`.

**Threshold governance.** Every detector's thresholds are tunable via the §43 Admin Dashboard → SIM Detector Thresholds surface; mutations require `ops_sim_admin` role + `ops_security_admin` quorum + write an OpsActionRecord with `action_kind='sim_detector_threshold_adjust'` (Appendix J — new on `ops_action_kind`). Thresholds MUST NOT be adjusted by analysts mid-investigation (defends against collusion bias).

**Detector rollout discipline.** New detector versions ship behind the §22.16 feature-flag system in shadow mode (emit `sim_signal_emitted_shadow`, Appendix G — new) for ≥ 14 days before promoting to active signal emission. Promotion requires `ops_sim_admin` + `ops_security_admin` dual sign-off with an OpsActionRecord `action_kind='sim_detector_promote_to_active'`.

### 50.15.5 SIM Signal-Class Catalog Extensions {#50.15.5-sim-signal-class-catalog-extensions}

§50.15.5 extends the §48.4.10 SIM Signal-Class catalog with four new classes. The authoritative catalog is now the UNION of §48.4.10 (11 classes) + §50.15.5 (4 classes) = 15 classes. The canonical forward-reference is maintained at §48.4.10 (which now explicitly cross-references §50.15.5 — see Appendix J enum extension below for the full 15-value `sim_signal_class` enum).

| SIM Signal Class (new) | Origin (detector, §50.15.4) | Severity Default | Auto-Kill-Switch Eligible | Default Case-Aggregation Window |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `anomalous_query_pattern` | §50.15.4 detector 1 | warning (critical on fingerprint match) | No (analyst review required) | 30 minutes per `target_user_id` + `target_org_id` |
| `referral_velocity_spike` | §50.15.4 detector 2 | warning (critical at > 25/7d) | Yes (critical only; `scope='org'`) | 24 hours per `target_org_id` |
| `suspicious_upload` | §50.15.4 detector 3 | critical (sync) / warning (async) | Yes (critical sync; `scope='user'` quarantine) | 5 minutes per `target_user_id` (burst-aware) |
| `email_sender_reputation_drift` | §50.15.4 detector 4 | warning (1 threshold) / critical (2+ concurrent) | Yes (critical; `scope='email_sender_domain'`) | 24 hours per sender domain |

**Aggregation window.** When multiple `SIMSignal` rows of the same class fire for the same target within the window, SIM's case-aggregator rolls them into a SINGLE `SIMCase` (sets `rolled_into_case_id` on each signal; the `SIMCase.aggregated_signal_ids` array is appended to). This prevents analyst fatigue from exhaustive per-signal review. Cross-class aggregation (different classes, same target, within max window across the classes) also rolls into one case per §50.15.6 AC #2.

**k-Anonymity compatibility (§48.4.7).** `anomalous_query_pattern` and `email_sender_reputation_drift` may produce per-user and per-domain signals that implicate small cohorts. SIM refuses to emit a signal where the cohort size is below the k-anonymity floor (§48.4.7); the suppressed detection is instead routed to an aggregate-only analyst surface under §50.14.6 Fraud Analyst Dashboard, and `sim_signal_k_anonymity_floor_violation` (Appendix G — new; distinct from the existing `growth_signal_k_anonymity_floor_violation`) is emitted for detector-tuning review.

### 50.15.6 `SIMCase` State Machine {#50.15.6-simcase-state-machine}

SIMCase has four states plus one compound-transition (merge). Transitions are append-only to the audit trail — state stamps on the entity are the canonical record.

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (none) | `flagged` | SIM case-aggregator creates case from 1+ `SIMSignal` rows | At least one `SIMSignal` matches the aggregation rule (§50.15.5); `signal_state='open'` → `rolled_into_case`; `assigned_ops_user_id=null`; `case_deadline_at = flagged_at + max_triage_sla_by_severity(severity_at_open)` per AC #5 | Entry point. `case_deadline_at` immutable post-set. |
| `flagged` | `investigating` | Analyst claims the case via `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/cases/{id}/claim` | Caller holds `ops_fraud_analyst` OR `ops_sim_admin`; `assigned_ops_user_id` set to caller; analyst MAY re-stamp `severity_current` up or down once (invariant enforced; subsequent attempts rejected with `sim_case_severity_mutation_exceeded` — Appendix I — new; HTTP 409) | Start of analyst work. Writes OpsActionRecord with `action_kind='sim_case_claim'`. |
| `flagged` | `resolved` (with `resolution_kind='auto_dismissed_expired'`) | Nightly SLA sweep on breach of `case_deadline_at` for `severity_at_open='informational'` OR `severity_at_open='warning'` with no signals in the case escalating to `critical` | Case has remained in `flagged` past `case_deadline_at + 7 days`; no analyst action | Auto-expire path. Critical-severity cases are EXCLUDED from auto-expire; they escalate per the next row. |
| `flagged` | `escalated` | Nightly SLA sweep on breach of `case_deadline_at + 24h` for `severity_at_open='critical'` | No analyst claim within 24h past SLA for a critical case | Forced escalation. `escalated_to_role='ops_admin'`; `escalation_reason='pattern_exceeds_analyst_authority'` (interpreted here as "no one claimed it"). |
| `investigating` | `resolved` | Analyst resolves via `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/cases/{id}/resolve` | `resolution_kind ∈ {false_positive, upheld_action_taken, upheld_no_action, merged_into_case}`; `resolution_note` 50–4,000 chars; if `upheld_action_taken` then `linked_fraud_action_ids` MUST be non-empty OR `linked_kill_switch_action_ids` MUST be non-empty | Terminal state. If merged, `merged_into_case_id` set. |
| `investigating` | `escalated` | Analyst escalates via `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/cases/{id}/escalate` | `escalated_to_role ∈ {ops_admin, ops_security_admin, ops_compliance_admin, ops_council}`; `escalation_reason` required | Transfers case out of Fraud Analyst authority. Terminal for the Fraud Analyst; the receiving role opens a new lifecycle (not authored in §50.15; falls under §50.6.4 incident response or §47 governance). |
| `escalated` | `resolved` | Receiving role executes `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/cases/{id}/resolve_from_escalation` | Caller holds role matching `escalated_to_role` OR higher in §50.3.2 hierarchy; `resolution_kind` + `resolution_note` required | Receiving-role terminal. |
| `resolved` | (terminal) | — | — | Terminal. No outbound transitions. |

**State-machine invariants.**

1. Terminal states (`resolved`, `escalated` after resolution-from-escalation) have no outbound transitions.
2. Every transition writes a §4.6.1 Audit Event AND a §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord atomically; partial-write raises `sim_case_transition_atomic_write_violation` (Appendix I — new; HTTP 500). The audit row carries `ops_session_id` (§4.6.3) linkage.
3. A `SIMCase` in `flagged` without an `investigating` transition within `case_deadline_at` is an SLA breach (emits `sim_case_sla_breach`, Appendix G — new); `sla_breach_at` stamped.
4. `severity_current` mutation is once-per-case and only in `flagged → investigating`; subsequent mutation attempts rejected with `sim_case_severity_mutation_exceeded`.
5. `aggregated_signal_ids` MAY grow only in `case_state='flagged'`; once `investigating`, late-arriving signals for the same target open a NEW case rather than appending (prevents analyst context thrash). The new case sets `merged_into_case_id = (the prior case id)` at creation and emits `sim_case_sibling_created` (Appendix G — new).

**Case-aggregation deterministic rule (AC #2).** A new `SIMSignal` rolls into an existing `flagged` `SIMCase` when ALL of: (a) target fields match exactly (`target_scope_kind`, `target_org_id`, `target_user_id`, `target_ref_type`, `target_ref_id`); (b) `emitted_at` falls within the aggregation window of the existing case (per §50.15.5 table; cross-class cases use the MAX window across classes); (c) the case is still `flagged` and `aggregated_signal_ids` count < 500; (d) the signal's severity does not escalate the case above its current `severity_current` — if it does, the signal rolls in AND `severity_current` is updated to the new max (this is distinct from analyst-driven severity mutation and is NOT counted against AC #4's one-mutation limit). Otherwise, a new case is opened.

**Dominant target rule (for cross-class aggregation).** When signals of different `target_scope_kind` roll in (e.g., a user-scope signal and an org-scope signal for a user within that org), the CASE adopts the most-permissive scope (`org` > `user` > `listing` > `capability`; the exact ordering is Appendix J `sim_case_dominant_target_ordering`). Signals referencing unrelated targets DO NOT aggregate.

### 50.15.7 Kill-Switch Mechanics (One-Click per Growth Mechanic) {#50.15.7-kill-switch-mechanics}

The kill-switch UX is surfaced in-line on every SIM case card AND on every Growth-Loop Operations Dashboard row (§48.3.3 existing dashboard #1). One click per row activates a kill-switch targeting the specific growth mechanic under review. The activation path reuses §48.2.12.4 `GrowthLoopKillSwitch` with SIM-specific write-time semantics authored here.

**Activation path.**

1. Analyst clicks **"Kill switch: {loop_id}"** from a `SIMCase` card. UI surfaces a confirmation dialog showing: the `loop_id`, the `scope` (platform / org / capability / region), the `scope_ref_id` (if non-platform), the selected `reason_code` (pre-populated from the case class: `sim_auto_kill_critical` when case severity is critical; `sim_auto_kill_warning` otherwise; analyst may override within the enum), and a required `reason_note` 100–2,000 chars.
2. On confirm, the client calls `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/kill-switches` (§50.15.8). The middleware:
    - Verifies analyst holds `ops_fraud_analyst` (sufficient for `ops_admin` quorum co-sign flow per §50.3.2 matrix) OR `ops_growth_admin` OR `ops_security_admin` (direct-activation authority per §48.2.12.4).
    - For `ops_fraud_analyst`, requires `ops_admin` quorum sign-off per §50.3.2 row "Trigger kill-switch on growth mechanic" (`✓²ᴱ with ops_admin quorum`). Quorum is collected via the standard §50.3.2 quorum-resolver.
    - Writes the `GrowthLoopKillSwitch` row with `active=true`, `activated_by_user_id=caller`, `reason_code`, `reason_note` — per §48.2.12.4.
    - Writes a §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord with `action_kind='sim_kill_switch_activate'` (Appendix J — new on `ops_action_kind`); links to `SIMCase.linked_kill_switch_action_ids`.
    - Fires the §48.2.12.4 publish-path propagation: the feature-flag system publishes the kill-switch state across the Convex cluster + edge caches within **60 seconds p99** (existing SLA inherited from §48.2.12.4 and §22.16.5).
    - Emits `sim.kill_switch.activated` webhook (§50.15.9) AND PostHog event `sim_kill_switch_activated` (§50.15.10).
    - Triggers the Slack alert (see below).

**60-second propagation contract (required by task brief).** The contract is inherited without change from §48.2.12.4 ¶ "Publish-path semantics." §50.15.11 AC #1 asserts the 60-second ceiling as a §50.15 invariant via the `sim_kill_switch_propagation_sla` CI gate that replays the publish path under synthetic load.

**Ops-Admin-only reversibility (required by task brief — tightens §48.2.12.4).** Prior §48.2.12.4 ¶ field-table constraint allowed deactivation by `ops_growth_admin` OR `ops_security_admin`. §50.15.7 TIGHTENS this for SIM-initiated kill-switches (`reason_code ∈ {sim_auto_kill_critical, sim_auto_kill_warning}`): deactivation MUST be performed by `ops_admin` only. Attempts by `ops_fraud_analyst` return HTTP 403 `sim_kill_switch_deactivate_requires_ops_admin` (Appendix I — new). Attempts by `ops_growth_admin` or `ops_security_admin` return HTTP 403 `sim_kill_switch_deactivate_requires_ops_admin_scope_sim_origin` (Appendix I — new) UNLESS those roles ALSO hold `ops_admin` (recall §50.3.2: `ops_growth_admin`, `ops_security_admin` map UNDER `ops_admin` — see §50.3.2 "Pre-existing specialized Ops roles" mapping table; the specialized role SATISFIES `ops_admin` for matrix evaluation purposes). The tightening is recorded as Authored Extension §50.9 item #29 (below).

Non-SIM-initiated kill-switches (`reason_code ∈ {ops_manual_action, legal_request, compliance_review, dependency_outage, experiment_rollback}`) retain the pre-existing §48.2.12.4 dual-role deactivation contract.

**Deactivation path.**

1. `ops_admin` opens the kill-switch management surface (§43 Admin Dashboard → Growth Loop Kill-Switches).
2. For a SIM-origin kill-switch, the "Deactivate" button is gated per the tightening above.
3. On deactivate, middleware writes `GrowthLoopKillSwitch.active=false`, `deactivated_at`, `deactivated_by_user_id`; writes OpsActionRecord `action_kind='sim_kill_switch_deactivate'`; emits webhook `sim.kill_switch.deactivated` AND PostHog `sim_kill_switch_deactivated`.
4. Triggers the Slack alert for deactivation (see below).
5. Propagation is symmetric — 60 seconds p99.

**Slack alert to on-call engineering channel (required by task brief — every kill-switch event).** §50.15.7 requires a Slack alert on EVERY kill-switch state change (activation AND deactivation) for SIM-origin kill-switches. The alert is emitted via the Sourcera-operated PagerDuty → Slack bridge (existing integration; §42 Observability) routed to the `#eng-oncall` Slack channel. The alert carries: (a) the `GrowthLoopKillSwitch.id`, (b) the `loop_id` and `scope`, (c) the activator/deactivator Ops user pseudonym (never PII — the Ops display-name pseudonym per §50.4.8 Customer-Visible Projection rules; see below for the Ops-internal Slack exception), (d) the originating `SIMCase.id` and URL to the case surface at `ops.sourcera.com/sim/cases/{id}`, (e) the `reason_code` and `reason_note` (truncated to 500 chars), (f) the state transition (`activated` | `deactivated`). The alert is FIRE-AND-FORGET (no retry); the bridge itself has its own retry semantics (Appendix F `webhook_observability` class). Delivery failure is NOT a blocker on the kill-switch write (the write has already committed); the delivery failure is captured via `sim_kill_switch_slack_alert_delivery_failure` (Appendix G — new) and surfaces on §50.14.6 Fraud Analyst Dashboard as a widget.

**Ops-internal Slack exception to the §50.4.8 pseudonymization rule.** §50.4.8 Customer-Visible Projection requires Ops user identities be pseudonymized in any customer-visible surface. The Slack alert is EXPLICITLY internal (the `#eng-oncall` channel is the Sourcera-internal on-call channel; no customer access). Therefore the Slack alert payload MAY include the Ops user's display name / email as first-class fields for operational efficiency. This exception is codified as an Authored Extension (§50.9 item #31) requiring Ops Director sign-off. The alert SHALL NEVER be forwarded outside the on-call channel; the channel ACL is enforced at the Slack tenant configuration layer.

**Slack alert payload schema (for engineering reference).**

```json
{
  "alert_kind": "sim_kill_switch_state_change",
  "transition": "activated" | "deactivated",
  "kill_switch_id": "<UUID>",
  "loop_id": "<growth_loop_id enum>",
  "scope": "platform" | "org" | "capability" | "region",
  "scope_ref_type": "<sim_signal_target_scope_kind or null>",
  "scope_ref_id": "<UUID or null>",
  "reason_code": "<growth_loop_kill_switch_reason_code>",
  "reason_note_truncated": "<first 500 chars>",
  "ops_actor_display_name": "<Ops display name; see §50.4.8 exception>",
  "ops_actor_email": "<Ops email; see §50.4.8 exception>",
  "sim_case_id": "<UUID or null>",
  "sim_case_url": "https://ops.sourcera.com/sim/cases/<UUID>",
  "activated_at": "<ISO-8601>",
  "deactivated_at": "<ISO-8601 or null>",
  "severity_at_open": "<sim_signal_severity>",
  "correlation_id": "<UUID; used to pair activation + later deactivation in analytics>"
}
```

**Slack-alert acceptance test.** A kill-switch activate followed by a deactivate produces exactly two Slack messages within 5 seconds of each state change (§50.15.11 AC #7). CI integration test stubs the Slack bridge and asserts message content + delivery timing.

### 50.15.8 API Endpoints {#50.15.8-api-endpoints}

All endpoints follow §32 conventions: `/api/v1/ops/sim/*`, cursor-pagination (default 50, max 250), HMAC-SHA256 request-body hashing via `X-Sourcera-Ops-Signature` (existing §50.2.3 contract), middleware stamping that writes AuditEvent `actor_type='ops_actor'` plus `ops_session_id`, rate-limit class `ops_sim_mutation` (§32.4.5; default 300 rpm per Ops user).

#### 50.15.8.1 `GET /api/v1/ops/sim/signals`

**Auth scope.** `ops_fraud_analyst`, `ops_sim_admin`, `ops_security_admin`, `ops_admin`.

**Query params.** `signal_class`, `severity`, `signal_state`, `target_org_id`, `target_user_id`, `target_scope_kind`, `emitted_after`, `emitted_before`, `detector_id`, `limit`, `cursor`.

**Response (200).**

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "sim_sig_01HX2Y...",
      "signal_class": "referral_velocity_spike",
      "detector_id": "referral_velocity_detector_v2",
      "detector_version": "2.1.3",
      "severity": "critical",
      "auto_kill_switch_eligible": true,
      "target_scope_kind": "org",
      "target_org_id": "org_01HV9Q...",
      "target_user_id": null,
      "target_ref_type": null,
      "target_ref_id": null,
      "triggering_event_ids": ["evt_1750000000_abc123", "..."],
      "raw_detector_evidence_json": {"observed_count_7d": 32, "threshold": 25, "z_score": 4.7},
      "evidence_truncated_at_emit": false,
      "signal_state": "rolled_into_case",
      "rolled_into_case_id": "sim_case_01HX2Z...",
      "auto_dismissed_reason": null,
      "emitted_at": "2026-04-21T14:03:12.118Z",
      "ingested_at": "2026-04-21T14:03:15.412Z",
      "created_at": "2026-04-21T14:03:15.412Z"
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "c_..."
}
```

#### 50.15.8.2 `GET /api/v1/ops/sim/cases`

**Auth scope.** Same as §50.15.8.1.

**Query params.** `case_state`, `severity_current`, `assigned_ops_user_id`, `target_org_id`, `signal_class_member`, `aggregated_signal_id`, `flagged_after`, `flagged_before`, `limit`, `cursor`.

**Response shape.** Mirrors `SIMCase` field table; ACL filter redacts `raw_detector_evidence_json` from aggregated signal expansion if `pii.read` capability is not held.

#### 50.15.8.3 `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/cases/{id}/claim`

**Auth scope.** `ops_fraud_analyst` OR `ops_sim_admin`.

**Request body.** `{"severity_current_new": "<sim_signal_severity or null>"}` — optional severity re-stamp; null means no change.

**Response (200).** Updated `SIMCase` row with `case_state='investigating'`, `investigating_at` set, `assigned_ops_user_id=caller`.

**Errors.** HTTP 409 `sim_case_already_investigating` (another analyst claimed it); HTTP 403 `sim_case_claim_role_insufficient`; HTTP 409 `sim_case_severity_mutation_exceeded`.

#### 50.15.8.4 `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/cases/{id}/resolve`

**Auth scope.** `ops_fraud_analyst` OR `ops_sim_admin` (the case's `assigned_ops_user_id`).

**Request body.**

```json
{
  "resolution_kind": "upheld_action_taken",
  "resolution_note": "Upheld referral fraud pattern; reversed $1,200 M16 credit; suspended referrer Org outbound tools pending CS review.",
  "linked_fraud_action_ids": ["opar_01HX3A...", "opar_01HX3B..."],
  "linked_kill_switch_action_ids": [],
  "merged_into_case_id": null
}
```

**Response (200).** Updated `SIMCase` row with `case_state='resolved'`, `resolved_at`, `resolution_kind`, `resolution_note`, populated link arrays.

**Invariants.** `linked_fraud_action_ids` and `linked_kill_switch_action_ids` rows MUST reference OpsActionRecord rows with `linked_ops_session_id` matching the caller's active OpsSession (§4.6.3). Validation raises `sim_case_linked_action_session_mismatch` (Appendix I — new; HTTP 409). When `resolution_kind='upheld_action_taken'`, the link arrays MUST NOT both be empty (§50.15.6 AC row).

#### 50.15.8.5 `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/cases/{id}/escalate`

**Auth scope.** `ops_fraud_analyst` OR `ops_sim_admin`.

**Request body.**

```json
{
  "escalated_to_role": "ops_admin",
  "escalation_reason": "cross_console_action_required",
  "resolution_note": "Pattern requires cross-console ban (buyer + seller). Escalating to ops_admin per §27.8.8 cross-console firewall rule."
}
```

**Response (200).** Updated `SIMCase` row with `case_state='escalated'`, `escalated_at`, `escalated_to_role`, `escalation_reason`.

#### 50.15.8.6 `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/cases/{id}/resolve_from_escalation`

**Auth scope.** Caller MUST hold role matching `SIMCase.escalated_to_role` OR a higher role in the §50.3.2 hierarchy (`ops_council` > `ops_admin` > other).

**Request body.** Same as §50.15.8.4 plus `escalation_resolution_note` 50–4,000 chars.

**Response (200).** Updated `SIMCase` row with `case_state='resolved'`.

#### 50.15.8.7 `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/kill-switches`

**Auth scope.** `ops_fraud_analyst` (requires `ops_admin` quorum), `ops_growth_admin`, `ops_security_admin`, `ops_admin`.

**Request body.**

```json
{
  "sim_case_id": "sim_case_01HX2Z...",
  "loop_id": "vendor_invite_creates_account",
  "scope": "org",
  "scope_ref_type": "org",
  "scope_ref_id": "org_01HV9Q...",
  "reason_code": "sim_auto_kill_critical",
  "reason_note": "SIM case 01HX2Z critical-severity referral velocity spike; 32 invites/7d at z=4.7; suspected harvesting of M16 credit. Killing L1 for this Org pending investigation.",
  "quorum_signoff_user_ids": ["usr_ops_admin_01..."]
}
```

**Response (201).** Returns the new `GrowthLoopKillSwitch` row + the produced OpsActionRecord id. The corresponding webhook fires asynchronously within 1 s; the Slack alert fires within 5 s.

**Errors.** HTTP 403 `ops_capability_outside_envelope` (caller role insufficient); HTTP 403 `sim_kill_switch_quorum_required` (quorum missing); HTTP 409 `growth_loop_kill_switch_already_active` (existing partial-uniqueness constraint from §48.2.12.4); HTTP 422 `sim_kill_switch_reason_note_too_short` (<100 chars); HTTP 422 `sim_kill_switch_reason_code_invalid` (reason code not in enum).

#### 50.15.8.8 `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/kill-switches/{id}/deactivate`

**Auth scope.** `ops_admin` only (for SIM-origin kill-switches); §50.3.2 specialized-role mapping (`ops_growth_admin`, `ops_security_admin`) counts as `ops_admin` per §50.3.2.

**Request body.**

```json
{
  "deactivation_reason_note": "SIM case 01HX2Z resolved `upheld_no_action`; analyst determined signal was cohort-of-one outlier; kill-switch lifted with no action against Org."
}
```

**Response (200).** Updated `GrowthLoopKillSwitch` row with `active=false`, `deactivated_at`, `deactivated_by_user_id`.

**Errors.** HTTP 403 `sim_kill_switch_deactivate_requires_ops_admin`; HTTP 404 `growth_loop_kill_switch_not_found`; HTTP 409 `growth_loop_kill_switch_already_inactive`.

### 50.15.9 Webhook Events {#50.15.9-webhook-events}

All events conform to §31 transport: HMAC-SHA256 signing via `X-Sourcera-Signature`, `event_id` idempotency (format `evt_{unix_ms}_{base32_random10}`), standard 5-attempt exponential-backoff retry curve per Appendix F, DLQ after 5 hard failures, payload ≤ 256 KB, `event_class='ops_sim'` (new; Appendix J enum extension — see §50.15.10). Console pooling: SIM events are platform-scoped; the Ops webhook subscription (distinct from customer webhooks) receives them. Customer webhook subscriptions do NOT receive SIM events — SIM is internal.

| Event | Trigger | Payload (key fields) | Retention |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `sim.signal.emitted` | `SIMSignal` row written | `signal_id`, `signal_class`, `detector_id`, `severity`, `target_*`, `emitted_at` | 30-day delivery log per §31.6 |
| `sim.signal.rolled_into_case` | Signal state transitions to `rolled_into_case` | `signal_id`, `case_id`, `severity_current` | Same |
| `sim.signal.auto_dismissed` | Signal state transitions to `auto_dismissed` | `signal_id`, `auto_dismissed_reason` | Same |
| `sim.case.flagged` | `SIMCase` created | `case_id`, `case_state='flagged'`, `severity_at_open`, `aggregated_signal_class_set`, `target_*`, `case_deadline_at` | Same |
| `sim.case.investigating` | Analyst claims | `case_id`, `assigned_ops_user_id` (pseudonymized), `severity_current` | Same |
| `sim.case.resolved` | Resolution | `case_id`, `resolution_kind`, `resolved_at`, `linked_fraud_action_ids`, `linked_kill_switch_action_ids` | Same |
| `sim.case.escalated` | Escalation | `case_id`, `escalated_to_role`, `escalation_reason` | Same |
| `sim.case.sla_breach` | SLA breach | `case_id`, `case_deadline_at`, `sla_breach_at` | Same |
| `sim.kill_switch.activated` | Kill-switch activated | Full payload per §50.15.7; cross-signed with the §48.2.12.4 entity id | Same |
| `sim.kill_switch.deactivated` | Kill-switch deactivated | Full payload per §50.15.7 | Same |

**Example payload — `sim.kill_switch.activated`.**

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_1745243000000_b3k2m9pxq7",
  "event_type": "sim.kill_switch.activated",
  "event_class": "ops_sim",
  "delivery_id": "del_01HX2Z...",
  "timestamp": "2026-04-21T14:03:20.118Z",
  "producer_version": "v7.0.0",
  "data": {
    "kill_switch_id": "gls_01HX2Z...",
    "loop_id": "vendor_invite_creates_account",
    "scope": "org",
    "scope_ref_type": "org",
    "scope_ref_id": "org_01HV9Q...",
    "reason_code": "sim_auto_kill_critical",
    "reason_note_truncated": "SIM case 01HX2Z critical-severity referral velocity spike; 32 invites/7d at z=4.7; suspected harvesting of M16 credit. Killing L1 for this Org pending investigation.",
    "sim_case_id": "sim_case_01HX2Z...",
    "activated_by_user_pseudonym": "ops_user_pseudo_c7k3",
    "activated_at": "2026-04-21T14:03:15.412Z",
    "quorum_signoff_user_pseudonyms": ["ops_user_pseudo_a1b2"],
    "correlation_id": "ks_corr_01HX2Z..."
  }
}
```

**Example payload — `sim.case.sla_breach`.**

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_1745329600000_c9p3n4mxt2",
  "event_type": "sim.case.sla_breach",
  "event_class": "ops_sim",
  "delivery_id": "del_01HX3B...",
  "timestamp": "2026-04-22T14:00:00.000Z",
  "producer_version": "v7.0.0",
  "data": {
    "case_id": "sim_case_01HX2Y...",
    "case_state_at_breach": "flagged",
    "severity_at_open": "critical",
    "flagged_at": "2026-04-21T10:00:00.000Z",
    "case_deadline_at": "2026-04-22T10:00:00.000Z",
    "sla_breach_at": "2026-04-22T10:00:15.000Z",
    "minutes_past_deadline": 0,
    "auto_escalation_pending_at": "2026-04-23T10:00:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

**Signing, idempotency, retry, DLQ.** Per §31.6 / §31.8.8. `sim.kill_switch.*` events use the tightened 5-second first-retry curve per Appendix F §F.2 (financial/operational-impact class) — the analyst surface depends on timely deactivation-event delivery to update the UI; slow delivery creates analyst confusion.

**Consumer registration.** SIM webhooks are NOT customer-subscribable. Ops-internal consumers: the `#eng-oncall` Slack bridge (kill-switch events), the Sourcera data warehouse (all events for analytics), the Sourcera on-call status dashboard (SLA breach + escalation events), the PagerDuty integration (critical events only). Consumer registration lives in the Ops webhook-subscription catalog at `/ops/observability/subscriptions` (referenced; the catalog surface is an Authored Extension in §50.9 item #32).

### 50.15.10 Appendix Registrations {#50.15.10-appendix-registrations}

**Appendix J `sim_signal_class` enum — extension.** Add `anomalous_query_pattern`, `referral_velocity_spike`, `suspicious_upload`, `email_sender_reputation_drift` to the pre-existing eleven-value enum registered at §48.4.10. Total post-extension: 15 values.

**Appendix J — new enums (§50.15-originated).**

### 50.15.11 Acceptance Criteria {#50.15.11-acceptance-criteria}

1. **Kill-switch 60-second propagation SLO.** Every `sim.kill_switch.activated` or `sim.kill_switch.deactivated` event MUST take the kill-switch state observable cluster-wide within 60 seconds p99. CI gate `sim_kill_switch_propagation_sla` asserts against synthetic load; violations emit `sim_kill_switch_propagation_slo_breach` AND page `ops_security_admin`.
2. **Detector-to-ingest latency SLO.** `SIMSignal.ingested_at - SIMSignal.emitted_at ≤ 60 s p95`, `≤ 120 s p99`. Breach emits `sim_detector_ingest_lag_slo_breach` (Appendix G — new; added here as coverage).
3. **Ops-Admin-only SIM kill-switch deactivation.** Any deactivation attempt on a SIM-origin kill-switch (reason_code ∈ `{sim_auto_kill_critical, sim_auto_kill_warning}`) by a caller who does NOT hold `ops_admin` (directly or via specialized-role mapping per §50.3.2) MUST return HTTP 403 `sim_kill_switch_deactivate_requires_ops_admin`. QA property-test asserts 100% enforcement across 1,000 simulated deactivation attempts across the six C.94 parent roles.
4. **Slack alert on every SIM kill-switch state change.** Every activation and every deactivation of a SIM-origin kill-switch MUST produce exactly one Slack message to `#eng-oncall` within 5 seconds of the underlying state write (measured server-side via the bridge's ACK). Delivery failure MUST NOT block the state write and MUST emit `sim_kill_switch_slack_alert_delivery_failure`. QA integration test asserts exactly-once delivery across 100 simulated transitions.
5. **SIM signal coverage of §48.4 controls.** Every §48.4.1–§48.4.9 control fire that produces a signal MUST write a `SIMSignal` row matching a registered `signal_class` in the §48.4.10 + §50.15.5 union (15 classes). CI gate `sim_signal_coverage_of_anti_spam_controls` asserts at every §48.4 or §50.15 merge.
6. **Case aggregation deterministic.** The `SIMSignal → SIMCase` roll-up algorithm (§50.15.6 case-aggregation rule) MUST be deterministic given the same inputs. Property-test replays 10,000 signal streams and asserts byte-equal `SIMCase` outputs across replays.
7. **State-machine closure.** Every `SIMCase` transition MUST match one of the §50.15.6 table rows. Middleware-level property-test asserts 100% enforcement; violations raise `sim_case_transition_not_in_state_machine` (Appendix I — new on this criterion's enforcement).
8. **Audit + OpsActionRecord atomicity.** Every `SIMCase` transition that requires a §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord write MUST write the OpsActionRecord in the SAME Convex transaction as the entity mutation AND the §4.6.1 Audit Event; partial-write raises `sim_case_transition_atomic_write_violation`. QA property-test asserts across 5,000 simulated transitions.
9. **`ops_session_id` linkage.** Every §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord produced by §50.15.8 endpoints MUST carry `linked_ops_session_id` matching the caller's active OpsSession per §50 aggregate AC #2. Breach is a P0 audit-integrity defect.
10. **Fraud Analyst cannot deactivate kill-switch.** A `SIMCase` investigated by `ops_fraud_analyst` MAY reach `resolved` with `resolution_kind='upheld_no_action'` even when a SIM-origin kill-switch is still `active`; deactivation of the kill-switch is a separate `ops_admin` action. The `SIMCase` resolution does NOT implicitly deactivate any kill-switch. QA asserts via property-test that 1,000 simulated `upheld_no_action` resolutions leave any linked kill-switch in its prior `active` state.
11. **Append-only SIMSignal.** SIMSignal UPDATE/DELETE outside the ingest pipeline MUST return HTTP 405 `sim_signal_append_only`. QA test asserts.
12. **Detector threshold mutation audit.** Every `sim_detector_threshold_adjust` OpsActionRecord MUST carry both the pre-change and post-change threshold values in `pre_action_state_json` / `post_action_state_json` per §4.4.27 invariant. Missing snapshots raises `ops_action_record_state_snapshot_required` per existing §4.4.27.
13. **Cross-class aggregation determinism.** Cross-class aggregation (per §50.15.6 dominant-target rule) MUST produce a deterministic `target_scope_kind` on the aggregated case. Property-test with 10,000 mixed-class signal streams asserts.
14. **k-Anonymity floor enforcement.** No `SIMSignal` for `signal_class ∈ {anomalous_query_pattern, email_sender_reputation_drift}` MAY emit below the §48.4.7 k-anonymity floor for the relevant cohort; enforcement returns `sim_signal_k_anonymity_floor_violation` and routes to the aggregate-only surface.
15. **Ops `#eng-oncall` channel ACL.** The Slack tenant enforces `#eng-oncall` membership to Sourcera engineering + Ops roster only; a monthly audit verifies non-Sourcera members = 0. Any non-compliance pages Security.
16. **Shadow-mode rollout gate.** New detectors MUST emit `sim_signal_emitted_shadow` (NOT `sim_signal_emitted`) for ≥ 14 days before promotion to active emission; CI gate `sim_detector_shadow_rollout_discipline` asserts the 14-day minimum against the OpsActionRecord with `action_kind='sim_detector_promote_to_active'` timeline.
17. **Retention.** `SIMSignal` + `SIMCase` rows retained 7 years per §40.2 Ops audit horizon; `raw_detector_evidence_json` truncated at 10 years; QA verifies nightly retention sweep.

### 50.15.12 Counterfactual Failure-Mode Pass {#50.15.12-counterfactual-failure-mode-pass}

**Failure mode 1 — Fraud Analyst floods kill-switches to cause self-inflicted outage.** Mitigation: `ops_fraud_analyst` kill-switch activations REQUIRE `ops_admin` quorum per §50.3.2; solo analyst cannot trip a kill-switch. Rate-limit class `ops_sim_mutation` (§32.4.5) caps mutation rate at 300 rpm — insufficient for mass-activation. OpsActionRecord append-only audit trail captures every attempt including quorum-rejected ones (§4.4.27). `sim_kill_switch_burst_detection` (§50.14.6 Fraud Analyst Dashboard widget) alerts `ops_security_admin` if an analyst submits > 3 kill-switch requests in 15 minutes.

**Failure mode 2 — Kill-switch stuck inactive due to propagation-cache poisoning.** A malicious actor or bug poisons the §22.16.5 feature-flag cache such that the 60-second propagation completes but the observed state is stale. Mitigation: the §48.2.12.4 publish path is defense-in-depth — cluster-level Convex state, edge-cache invalidation via §22.16.5, AND runtime-check at every loop-fire point (`GrowthLoopKillSwitch.active` is read from Convex at row-write time, not from cache). AC #1 CI gate asserts against synthetic poisoning. `sim_kill_switch_propagation_slo_breach` pages on breach.

**Failure mode 3 — Slack `#eng-oncall` channel is down during kill-switch activation.** Mitigation: Slack delivery is fire-and-forget; delivery failure does NOT block the kill-switch write (which has already committed; propagation is in-flight). `sim_kill_switch_slack_alert_delivery_failure` emits. Backup: PagerDuty integration (via the same bridge, independent path) also receives kill-switch events for `critical` severity — an engineer is paged even if Slack is down. The `#eng-oncall` channel ACL + audit (AC #15) ensures no unauthorized delivery even in failure.

**Failure mode 4 — SIM signal flood from a malfunctioning detector swamps the case queue.** A detector bug emits 100,000 false-positive signals in an hour. Mitigation: (a) case-aggregation (§50.15.6) rolls signals into minimal cases per target-tuple + window; 100,000 signals for the same target become ONE case. (b) `ops_sim_admin` can flip the detector to shadow-mode via `sim_detector_promote_to_shadow` (inverse of the rollout action; registered as Authored Extension below) within 5 minutes. (c) 300-rpm rate limit on mutations prevents a cascade of analyst actions. (d) §50.14.6 Fraud Analyst Dashboard widget "detector-fire-rate-anomaly" alerts `ops_sim_admin` when any single detector exceeds 10× its rolling 7-day median fire rate.

**Failure mode 5 — Analyst resolves case `upheld_no_action` on a true-positive, missing subsequent escalation.** An analyst dismisses a real fraud signal as false-positive; the fraudulent behavior continues. Mitigation: (a) `resolution_note` (50–4,000 chars) required for all resolutions creates a reviewable artifact. (b) Nightly `sim_case_resolution_calibration_sweep` (Ops-internal; `ops_audit_reviewer`) samples 5% of `upheld_no_action` and `false_positive` resolutions against ground-truth (subsequent fraud confirmed within 30 days) and produces an analyst-calibration report. (c) `repeat_offender_threshold_met` escalation reason auto-fires when the same `target_org_id` appears in ≥ 3 prior `false_positive` resolutions within 90 days. (d) Escalation to `ops_security_admin` is always available; analysts are trained to escalate on uncertainty.

**Failure mode 6 — Same target, signals arrive before and after case closure; late signal is silently dropped.** Mitigation: §50.15.6 state-machine AC row "late-arriving signals for the same target open a NEW case"; `sim_case_sibling_created` emitted; sibling case carries `merged_into_case_id` pointer to the prior case for continuity. Late signals are NEVER silently dropped.

**Failure mode 7 — Detector false-positive model override is abused to silence real signals.** The `detector_false_positive_model_override` auto-dismiss reason could be weaponized by an insider to silence signals. Mitigation: (a) the `detector_false_positive_model_override` auto-dismiss reason is set ONLY by the detector-local ML classifier, NOT by any Ops action; classifier mutation is `ops_applied_ml_admin`-gated per §50.3.2 extension (§48.4.5 pre-existing). (b) Overrides are sampled for calibration (same nightly sweep as #5). (c) `sim_signal_override_rate_by_detector` dashboard surfaces anomalous override rates to `ops_security_admin`.

**Failure mode 8 — Referral fraud kill-switch scope 'org' accidentally affects a legitimate sibling Org (org tree / acquisition scenario).** `scope='org'` with `scope_ref_id` targets a specific Org. Mitigation: §48.2.12.4 `scope_ref_type='org'` resolves to the exact Org id; no cascade to parent/child orgs. The §4.2.1 Organization entity does not model Org trees (Sourcera is flat per §4.2.1); if a future org-tree model is added, §50.15.7 kill-switch scope rules MUST be revisited as a Pending Follow-Through item.

## 50.16 Fraud Analyst Surface {#50.16-fraud-analyst-surface}

### 50.16.1 Purpose and Scope {#50.16.1-purpose-and-scope}

§50.16 authors the Ops Console surface for the Fraud Analyst role (`ops_fraud_analyst`, registered as a new granular role in §50.9 item #16 — pre-existing specialization of `ops_admin` per §50.3.2 mapping). §50.16 complements §50.14.6 (Fraud Analyst Dashboard — monitoring widgets) with:

1. A **review queue UX** over open `SIMCase` rows (§50.15.3) filtered and prioritized for Fraud Analyst attention.
2. The **case action set** — suspend Org, suspend User, reverse referral credit, revoke opt-out claim — with per-action role gating, audit requirements, and reversibility semantics.
3. The **capability envelope extensions** to §50.3.2 registering each action.
4. The **per-action API, webhook, and OpsActionRecord registrations**.

**Numbering reconciliation.** See §50.15.1 numbering note. §49.12 (task brief) → §50.16 here.

**Plan gating.** Internal. Not plan-gated. Surface accessible to `ops_fraud_analyst`, `ops_sim_admin`, `ops_security_admin`, `ops_admin`.

**Retention and DSAR.** All Fraud Analyst actions write §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord rows retained 7 years. Per-action customer-visible effects (Org suspension, User suspension, referral-credit reversal, opt-out revocation) are recorded in the respective entity's audit trail (referenced, not duplicated).

### 50.16.2 Review Queue UX {#50.16.2-review-queue-ux}

**Target surface.** `ops.sourcera.com/sim/cases` — default landing page for Fraud Analysts on sign-in.

**Default filter.** `case_state ∈ {flagged, investigating}` AND (`assigned_ops_user_id = $caller` OR `assigned_ops_user_id IS NULL`); sorted by `severity_current DESC, case_deadline_at ASC` (most-urgent, most-at-risk of SLA breach first).

**Queue columns (left to right).**

| Column | Data Source | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Severity chip | `severity_current` | Red for `critical`, amber for `warning`, gray for `informational`. |
| Case ID (short) | `SIMCase.id` first 8 chars | Click → case detail. |
| Aggregated signal classes | `aggregated_signal_class_set` | Pill-stack; full list in tooltip. |
| Target | `target_*` | Org name (pseudonymized for `ops_fraud_analyst` unless step-up re-auth held; see §50.16.5), otherwise user / listing / domain display. |
| Flagged at / Age | `flagged_at` | Absolute + relative ("2h ago"). |
| SLA Remaining | `case_deadline_at - now()` | Amber at < 30% remaining; red at breach. |
| Assigned To | `assigned_ops_user_id` (pseudonym) | "— unclaimed —" or "@me". |
| Linked KS | count of `linked_kill_switch_action_ids` | Kill-switch badge if any active. |
| Linked Fraud Actions | count of `linked_fraud_action_ids` | Count badge. |

**Row actions (right-click / context menu).** Claim (if unclaimed) → `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/cases/{id}/claim`; Open → case-detail page; Bulk-resolve-false-positive → batch endpoint (see §50.16.4).

**Case detail page.** On click into a case, the page shows:

- **Case header.** Case id, state, severity, target, flagged_at, case_deadline_at, assigned_ops_user_id.
- **Aggregated signals panel.** Expandable list of `SIMSignal` rows with detector metadata, evidence (JSON viewer, truncation-aware), emit time, auto-kill-switch eligibility.
- **Target context panel.** Drill-through to the target Org / User / listing / domain — rendered via customer-API (not direct-DB) per §50.14.2 invariant #1. For Org context: last 30 days AIOperation volume, contest rate, EOI volume, referral activity, active wallet balance, marketplace listing count. For User context: last 30 days login history, mutations, recent support tickets.
- **Actions panel.** The four §50.16.3 case actions + escalate + resolve. Each action surfaces its own confirm dialog with required fields per §50.16.4.
- **Audit trail panel.** Chronological list of the §4.6.1 Audit Events AND §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord rows linked to this case.

**PII projection rules.** The target context panel renders PII (Org legal name, user email, user name) ONLY when the caller holds `pii.read` capability + has step-up re-authed within 5 min (§50.2.2). Without step-up, PII is replaced by pseudonyms (the `anonymized_display_name` pattern per §50.4.8 / §43.3 Customer-Visible Projection rules). The case-detail page header always shows pseudonyms; step-up re-auth unlocks a "Reveal PII" button that flips the target context panel to identified-mode for the duration of the session (capped at 30 min). Every PII-reveal action writes an OpsActionRecord with `action_kind='pii_reveal'` (Appendix J — new on `ops_action_kind`; tracked for audit review).

**Queue realtime refresh.** Queue refreshes every 30 seconds via PostHog Live Insights feed (§50.14.6 existing pattern). New flagged cases appear at the top with a momentary highlight.

**Queue-level analytics.** The queue page footer shows: open cases by severity, SLA-breach-imminent count, analyst workload by pseudonym, median time-to-claim, median time-to-resolve. These are aggregate metrics suitable for `ops_sim_admin` and Fraud Analyst-lead views.

### 50.16.3 Case Action Set (Verbatim from Task Brief) {#50.16.3-case-action-set}

The four case actions specified in the task brief, each with API, role gating, audit, and reversibility semantics.

| # | Action | API | Role Gating | OpsActionRecord `action_kind` | Reversibility |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Suspend Org | `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/cases/{id}/actions/suspend-org` | `ops_fraud_analyst` WITH `ops_admin` quorum (cross-console impact; §5.1 firewall is preserved — "suspend Org" means Seller-console suspension by default; buyer-console suspension requires additional quorum with `ops_compliance_admin`) | `fraud_org_suspend` | Reversible by `ops_admin` via `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/cases/{id}/actions/restore-org` — writes `fraud_org_restore` OpsActionRecord. Committed-spend contract treatment per §34.11. |
| 2 | Suspend User | `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/cases/{id}/actions/suspend-user` | `ops_fraud_analyst` solo (user-scope is narrower than org; no quorum required at suspend) | `fraud_user_suspend` | Reversible by `ops_fraud_analyst` solo OR `ops_admin` via `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/cases/{id}/actions/restore-user` — writes `fraud_user_restore`. |
| 3 | Reverse referral credit | `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/cases/{id}/actions/reverse-referral-credit` | `ops_fraud_analyst` WITH `ops_finance` quorum (financial impact; §4.3.16 credit reversal requires `ops_finance` per §50.3.2 `✓²ᴱ (with ops_admin quorum)` precedent extended here to `ops_finance` for referral credits — `ops_finance` is the correct approver because the reversal is a Stripe Credit Note mutation) | `fraud_referral_credit_reverse` | Reversible by `ops_admin` with `ops_finance` quorum via `POST .../restore-referral-credit` — writes `fraud_referral_credit_restore`. Reversal emits Stripe Credit Note reversal per §4.3.16 `stripe_credit_note_ids` append-only record. |
| 4 | Revoke opt-out claim | `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/cases/{id}/actions/revoke-opt-out-claim` | `ops_fraud_analyst` solo (opt-out revocation is narrow; restores seller presence on the marketplace — scope is typically "seller falsely claimed opt-out to suppress a competitor's page"); however the target entity must be a §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Record AND must carry the fraud-signal metadata from the associated `SIMCase.aggregated_signal_class_set` — cannot be used arbitrarily | `fraud_opt_out_claim_revoke` | Reversible by `ops_fraud_analyst` via `POST .../restore-opt-out-claim` — writes `fraud_opt_out_claim_restore`. |

**Shared request semantics (all four actions).**

```json
{
  "action_reason_note": "<50–4,000 chars; required>",
  "quorum_signoff_user_ids": ["<opsuser_uuid>", "..."],
  "dry_run": false
}
```

**Dry-run mode.** Each action endpoint supports `dry_run=true`. In dry-run, the action path validates role gating, quorum, and pre-action state; returns what the `pre_action_state_json` and `post_action_state_json` WOULD be; does NOT mutate. `dry_run` is the safe-surface for analyst prep. `dry_run` writes a §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord with `action_kind='fraud_action_dry_run'` (Appendix J — new on `ops_action_kind`) for audit completeness; dry-run records do NOT count against reversibility tracking.

**Shared response semantics.** On success (200), returns the updated target entity row (redacted per §50.4.8 customer-visible-projection rules) + the `OpsActionRecord.id` + the linked `SIMCase.id` with `linked_fraud_action_ids` appended.

### 50.16.4 Per-Action Detail {#50.16.4-per-action-detail}

#### 50.16.4.1 Suspend Org

**Target.** `target_org_id` of the `SIMCase`. If the case's `target_scope_kind != 'org'`, the endpoint returns 422 `sim_case_fraud_action_scope_mismatch` (Appendix I — new).

**Effect.**

- Writes §4.4.27 OpsActionRecord with `action_kind='fraud_org_suspend'`; `pre_action_state_json` captures current `organization.state` (enum `organization_state` existing); `post_action_state_json` captures post-state (`state='suspended_fraud'` — new enum value on `organization_state`; Appendix J extension).
- Updates `organization.state = 'suspended_fraud'`.
- Sets `organization.suspended_at` (new field — Authored Extension §50.9 item #33), `organization.suspended_reason_category='fraud'`, `organization.suspended_by_ops_session_id`.
- Fires existing §42 Customer Communication: Org Owner receives an in-app banner + email "Your organization has been suspended pending fraud review. Please contact Sourcera Support."
- §4.8.1 AIOperation writes are blocked at the write path (HTTP 403 `organization_suspended_for_fraud` — new; Appendix I); §5.x customer-console UI shows a suspended-state banner; wallet operations frozen per §34.11 suspension billing rules; committed-spend contracts honor original terms with pro-rata credit if the suspension persists past 30 days.
- Emits webhook `sim.fraud_action.org_suspended` (§50.16.6) AND PostHog `sim_fraud_action_org_suspended`.

**Cross-console preservation.** By default, suspension scope is SELLER console only — Org cannot publish listings, accept EOIs, or respond to bids. Buyer-console functionality remains. Additional scope expansion to BOTH consoles (`cross_console=true` in request body) requires `ops_compliance_admin` additional quorum (three signers total: caller + `ops_admin` + `ops_compliance_admin`) and writes an explicit OpsActionRecord with `action_kind='fraud_org_suspend_cross_console'`. Cross-console suspension fires `sim.fraud_action.org_suspended_cross_console` webhook.

**Restoration.** `POST /api/v1/ops/sim/cases/{id}/actions/restore-org` requires `ops_admin` solo. Restores `organization.state` to pre-suspension value per `pre_action_state_json`. Emits webhook `sim.fraud_action.org_restored`.

#### 50.16.4.2 Suspend User

**Target.** `target_user_id` of the `SIMCase`. If `target_scope_kind != 'user'`, returns 422 `sim_case_fraud_action_scope_mismatch`.

**Effect.**

- Writes OpsActionRecord `action_kind='fraud_user_suspend'`.
- Updates `user.state = 'suspended_fraud'` (new enum value on `user_state`; Appendix J extension).
- Sets `user.suspended_at`, `user.suspended_reason_category='fraud'`, `user.suspended_by_ops_session_id`.
- Active sessions for the user are revoked per §6.5 WorkOS session-revocation path (synchronous).
- Subsequent authenticator callbacks for the user return HTTP 403 `user_suspended_for_fraud` (Appendix I — new).
- User's Org is NOT suspended — other users of the same Org continue normal operation.
- User does NOT receive a proactive email (suspension is a potentially-hostile target; notification could alert an attacker); the user sees a generic "Your account is temporarily unavailable. Please contact Support." message on next login attempt.
- Emits webhook `sim.fraud_action.user_suspended` AND PostHog `sim_fraud_action_user_suspended`.

**Restoration.** `POST .../restore-user` — `ops_fraud_analyst` solo; restores `user.state`; re-enables login on next attempt (no forced re-auth of the now-revoked WorkOS sessions — user must sign in fresh). Webhook `sim.fraud_action.user_restored`.

#### 50.16.4.3 Reverse Referral Credit

**Target.** A `buyer_referral_id` referenced from one of the `SIMCase.aggregated_signal_ids` signals (specifically a signal with `signal_class='referral_velocity_spike'` OR an existing `velocity_anomaly` / `referral_fraud_pattern_accumulation` per §48.4.10). The endpoint requires an explicit `buyer_referral_id` in the request body.

**Request body addition.**

```json
{
  "buyer_referral_id": "buy_ref_01HX2P...",
  "reverse_amount_usd": 100.00,
  "forfeit_reason": "referral_fraud_velocity_spike",
  "action_reason_note": "...",
  "quorum_signoff_user_ids": ["<ops_finance_uuid>"]
}
```

**Effect.**

- Writes OpsActionRecord `action_kind='fraud_referral_credit_reverse'`.
- Updates §4.3.16 BuyerReferral:
  - If `credit_issued_at IS NOT NULL` AND `credit_redeemed_usd < credit_value_usd`: partial or full reversal — `credit_value_usd` reduced to `credit_redeemed_usd` (already-redeemed portion not clawed back to avoid recursive Stripe complexity) OR `forfeited` per analyst choice.
  - If `credit_issued_at IS NULL`: `status='forfeited'`, `credit_forfeited_reason=forfeit_reason`.
  - `ops_override_user_id=caller`, `ops_override_note=action_reason_note`, `fraud_signal_flags` appended with the class(es) from the linking SIMCase.
- Stripe Credit Note reversal: if `credit_issued_at` IS populated, call Stripe's Credit Note reversal API per §4.3.16 `stripe_credit_note_ids` lifecycle; append the reversal note id to the array; emits `billing.wallet.credit_note_reversed` (existing webhook pattern — see §31.8.4).
- §4.8.3 AIWallet balance adjusted correspondingly; emits `billing.wallet.balance_changed`.
- Emits webhook `sim.fraud_action.referral_credit_reversed` AND PostHog `sim_fraud_action_referral_credit_reversed`.

**Restoration.** `POST .../restore-referral-credit` — `ops_admin` WITH `ops_finance` quorum. Reverses the reversal: re-issues the credit via a new Stripe Credit Note. Webhook `sim.fraud_action.referral_credit_restored`.

**Race condition guard.** Concurrent `reverse-referral-credit` against the same `buyer_referral_id` is blocked via Convex serializable-transaction guard; second attempt returns HTTP 409 `buyer_referral_concurrent_reversal_in_progress` (Appendix I — new).

#### 50.16.4.4 Revoke Opt-Out Claim

**Target.** A `vendor_opt_out_record_id` referenced from one of the `SIMCase.aggregated_signal_ids` signals (specifically a signal with `signal_class='vendor_opt_out_overlap'` per §48.4.9 / §48.4.10 OR an `anomalous_query_pattern` signal targeting a marketplace domain). The endpoint requires an explicit `vendor_opt_out_record_id` in the request body.

**Request body addition.**

```json
{
  "vendor_opt_out_record_id": "vor_01HX2Q...",
  "revoke_reason": "opt_out_claim_filed_fraudulently_to_suppress_legitimate_listing",
  "action_reason_note": "...",
  "restore_seller_listings": true
}
```

**Effect.**

- Writes OpsActionRecord `action_kind='fraud_opt_out_claim_revoke'`.
- Updates §4.4.8 VendorOptOutRecord: `revoked_by_ops_at = now()`, `revoked_by_ops_session_id = caller's active session`, `revoke_reason = revoke_reason`; entity soft-deleted via existing `deleted_at` field.
- §4.5.6 Marketplace-domain render contract re-computes; listings previously hidden due to the opt-out are restored to public visibility within 5 minutes (leveraging existing §4.5.6 cache invalidation).
- If `restore_seller_listings=true` (default), the affected Seller Org's listings return to their prior `marketplace_listing.status`; if `false`, listings remain hidden pending further Ops review.
- The seller Org (now-restored) is NOT proactively notified; re-appearance of their listings on the Marketplace is self-evident on next browse.
- Emits webhook `sim.fraud_action.opt_out_claim_revoked` AND PostHog `sim_fraud_action_opt_out_claim_revoked`.

**Restoration.** `POST .../restore-opt-out-claim` — `ops_fraud_analyst` solo. Re-instates the opt-out record (un-soft-deletes); re-hides listings per §4.4.8. Webhook `sim.fraud_action.opt_out_claim_restored`.

**Guard against opt-out ping-pong.** A `buyer_referral_id` or `vendor_opt_out_record_id` that has been reversed/revoked AND subsequently restored MORE than 3 times within 180 days triggers `ops_admin` mandatory review (`ops_fraud_analyst` loses solo authority on the 4th transition); `sim_fraud_action_ping_pong_detected` (Appendix G — new) emits and pages `ops_security_admin`.
