Solo-tier rows specifically validate Cross-reference to §44.6.1 Solo-Tier Surface Hide List.

### 51.3.7 Acceptance Criteria — §51.3 {#51.3.7-acceptance-criteria-51-3}

1. Dashboard first-load p95 MUST be ≤ 1.5 s when the snapshot is available; ≤ 3.0 s when a live-query augmentation is required. Breach pages the §51.8 on-call rotation.
2. Panel 4 (Top Consumers) MUST suppress per-user disclosure when k < 5; suppression emits `usage_analytics_k_anon_floor_hit`. Property-test: 1,000 synthesized Org sizes.
3. Panel 4 MUST pseudonymize user labels for `org_admin`; raw email disclosure restricted to `billing_admin` + `org_owner`. Role-based integration test.
4. Panels MUST respect workspace-scope filtering (`workspace_id ∈ viewer's accessible workspaces`); cross-workspace leakage rejected by validator. Integration test with guest role.
5. Exports MUST watermark the `snapshot_window`, `conversion_factor_version_set_hash`, and export-requester user_id; integration test asserts footer content.
6. Export size ceiling: 50 MB per export; exceeding raises HTTP 413 `usage_analytics_export_size_exceeded` and suggests narrower window. Property-test.
7. `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/analytics/usage/snapshot` MUST return HTTP 404 `usage_analytics_snapshot_not_ready` if the nightly rollup has not yet run for the specified window; the dashboard UI shows "Preparing your report…" with a countdown to the next rollup.
8. Per-user disclosure gate MUST be logged to §4.6.1 AuditEvent with action `usage_analytics_per_user_disclosure_viewed` whenever a `billing_admin` views Panel 4; property-test.
9. Panels MUST partition queries by `data_residency_region`; cross-region aggregation forbidden; integration test with EU + US Orgs.
10. Dashboard MUST emit `usage_dashboard_viewed` on first paint with properties `{surface, time_window, filter_set_hash}`; panel clicks emit `usage_dashboard_panel_interacted` with `{panel_id, interaction_kind}`; regression test.

## 51.4 User-Level Usage Dashboard (Summary C.90) {#51.4-user-level-usage-dashboard}

§51.4 authors the per-user dashboard surface — the individual surface where each user sees their own AI spend, accept/reject rate, capability mix, and personal productivity numbers. The dashboard is distinct from §51.3 (Org-level, aggregate) and from §20 Inbox & Pulse (procurement activity, not analytics).

### 51.4.1 Surface & Access {#51.4.1-surface-access}

Primary URL: `https://app.sourcera.com/me/analytics/usage`. Also accessible via User Menu → "My usage" and via Command Palette → "My usage analytics".

Access model:

| Viewer | Access |
| :---- | :---- |
| Subject user | Read-only full dashboard |
| Subject user's Org Owner + Billing Admin | Read-only (via §51.3.4 drill-down from Top Consumers panel) — rendered as "Viewing as admin" banner with audit-event emission |
| Any other role (including org_admin, workspace_owner, member, guest) | No access (HTTP 403 `usage_analytics_dashboard_access_denied`) |

The "Viewing as admin" drill-down is a §51.3.3 authorized disclosure; §51.4 enforces the admin access audit via §4.6.1 AuditEvent with action `usage_analytics_per_user_disclosure_viewed`.

### 51.4.2 Privacy Model {#51.4.2-privacy-model}

A user viewing their own dashboard sees their raw `user_id`, email, session IDs, AIOperation IDs, workspace IDs, and capability_ids. When an authorized admin views via drill-down, the same data is rendered EXCEPT the admin's view is audit-logged and watermarked. Users MAY download their own usage export via §32 `/v1/users/{user_id}/analytics/usage/export` (self-service DSAR-like surface, distinct from the §6.8 full DSAR — this is convenience, not a legal-compliance surface).

DSAR compatibility: on DSAR erase of a user, the User-Level Dashboard for that user returns HTTP 404 `user_not_found`; the underlying UsageEvent rows carry pseudonymized `user_id` per §51.7.2 and contribute to aggregate Org panels without per-user attribution.

### 51.4.3 Panels & KPIs {#51.4.3-panels-kpis-51-4}

| Panel | Content | Data Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 — Personal Headline | Total spend (30-day rolling); operations count; acceptance rate; time-saved minutes | PostHog live query scoped to `user_id` + UsageDashboardSnapshot per-user aggregates |
| 2 — Capability Mix | Donut chart: spend by `capability_domain_kind`; drill-down to specific capabilities | UsageEvent rollup filtered by `user_id` |
| 3 — Acceptance Trend | Weekly acceptance rate over the last 12 weeks; annotated with capability domain changes | UsageEvent rollup |
| 4 — Top Sessions | Last 20 sessions by spend; click-through to AI Operation Ledger filtered to session | UsageEvent + AIOperation join |
| 5 — Personal Productivity | Time-saved minutes (monthly) with trend; personal baseline-assumption-version annotation | §4.3.19 Time-Saved Credit |

No top-consumer panel on the user surface — every panel is first-person singular.

### 51.4.4 APIs (§32-conformant) {#51.4.4-apis-51-4}

| Method | Path | Auth Scope | Rate-Limit Class | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `GET` | `/v1/users/{user_id}/analytics/usage/summary` | Self OR `billing_admin`/`org_owner` (audited) | `analytics_read` (§32.4.5) | Per-user summary; same schema shape as §51.3.5 minus per-user panels |
| `GET` | `/v1/users/{user_id}/analytics/usage/export` | Self OR `billing_admin` (audited) | `analytics_export` (§32.4.5) | CSV / XLSX / JSON export |

Admin cross-user access MUST emit `usage_analytics_per_user_disclosure_viewed` AuditEvent; server rejects any third-party access attempt with HTTP 403 `usage_analytics_user_access_denied`.

### 51.4.5 Plan Gating {#51.4.5-plan-gating-51-4}

User-level dashboard is available on every plan tier that includes Org-level dashboard access. Plan tier controls the time-window depth: Free 30 days; Starter 90 days; Growth / Scale 12 months; Enterprise 24 months. Plan-tier-to-window mapping is sourced from §34.1; §51 cites, never duplicates the per-tier values.

### 51.4.6 Acceptance Criteria — §51.4 {#51.4.6-acceptance-criteria-51-4}

1. Self-view first-paint p95 MUST be ≤ 1.5 s.
2. Admin cross-user access MUST emit `usage_analytics_per_user_disclosure_viewed` AuditEvent; integration test.
3. Any third-party role attempting cross-user access MUST receive HTTP 403 `usage_analytics_user_access_denied`; integration test with `org_admin`, `workspace_owner`, `reviewer`, `guest`.
4. DSAR-erased user dashboard MUST return HTTP 404 `user_not_found` without leaking that the user previously existed; property-test.
5. Self-service export MUST include ALL Usage Event rows attributed to the user within the chosen window (subject to §40.2 retention); round-trip test via export + re-parse.
6. Dashboard emits `user_usage_dashboard_viewed` on first paint with `{time_window, cross_user_admin_view=boolean}`; admin views set the flag.
7. User Menu surfaces the dashboard under "My usage" for every plan tier where the Org has usage analytics enabled; plan-gating test.
8. Export size ceiling: 20 MB per export; exceeding raises HTTP 413 `usage_analytics_export_size_exceeded` with a narrower-window recommendation.
9. Self-service export MUST emit `usage_dashboard_panel_interacted` with `{dashboard_kind=user_level, interaction_kind=export_triggered, export_format ∈ {csv, xlsx, json}, snapshot_id, cross_user_admin_view=boolean}` per Appendix G §51 additions; event emits post-authorization (not on click) to avoid spurious emissions on denied-export attempts. Regression test asserts one event per successful export, zero events on authorization-denied attempts, and `cross_user_admin_view=true` when a `billing_admin` or `org_owner` exports another user's dashboard.

## 51.5 Seller Usage Parity (Summary C.92) {#51.5-seller-usage-parity}

§51.5 authors the seller-console counterpart to §51.3 — ensuring seller-side users see the same structural dashboard but adapted to the bid workflow (per-bid spend, KB utilization, win-rate correlation) rather than procurement-workflow metrics. Parity is a first-class design requirement, not a nice-to-have: a seller Billing Admin must see their spend and ROI with the same fidelity a buyer Billing Admin does.

### 51.5.1 Seller Dashboard Surface {#51.5.1-seller-dashboard-surface}

Primary URL: `https://seller.sourcera.com/org/{seller_org_id}/analytics/usage`. Access model identical to §51.3.1 but scoped to seller roles: `org_owner`, `billing_admin`, `seller_team_lead` (team-scoped view), `seller_team_member` (no access to usage dashboard; access own via §51.4).

Console firewall: buyer-side users have NO access to seller dashboards regardless of parent-Org relationship (a user who is both a buyer-console and seller-console identity in the same Org accesses each dashboard via its own console; cross-console disclosure is forbidden per §25 cross-console mechanics).

### 51.5.2 Per-Bid Spend Panel {#51.5.2-per-bid-spend-panel}

Rendered in place of §51.3.3 Panel 3 (Spend by Phase). Panel content:

| Sub-panel | Content | Data Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Active Bids | Table: bid_workspace_id, buyer org (pseudonymized per §5 guest/cross-console model), phase, spend_cents, operations, kb_citations_count, acceptance_rate | UsageEvent filtered by `event_family IN {bid_core, kb_core}` and `bid_workspace_id` |
| Closed Bids Summary | Win/loss outcome × spend histogram; win-rate lift per spend band | BidOutcome join with UsageEvent |
| Bid Cost Benchmarks | Median spend per bid by category; percentile bands (p25, p50, p75, p90) — k=10 cross-Org cohort floor applies | Cross-Org rollup with k-anon enforcement |

### 51.5.3 KB Utilization Panel {#51.5.3-kb-utilization-panel}

Rendered as Panel 3.5 (between Seller Parity's per-bid and top-consumers panels). Panel content:

| Sub-panel | Content | Data Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| KB Retrieval Volume | Total `kb_retrieve_invoked` events over window; average `top_k`; degraded-mode % | `kb_retrieve_invoked` |
| Citation Health | `cite_verify_failed` rate; `kb_injection_suspected` count; zero-results rate | `cite_verify_failed`, `kb_injection_suspected`, `kb_retrieve_zero_results` |
| KB ROI | KB entries cited in closed bids × win-rate correlation; top-N cited entries with win-rate lift | `kb_citation_in_closed_bid_attributed` (registered under `kb_core` event family at §22.18 KB Value Capture; catalogued in Appendix G → KB Value Capture Events subsection, NOT in Appendix G → §51 Product Usage Analytics Event Additions — cross-family consumption per §51.1.5 cross-reference table) |
| Staleness Alerts | Entries flagged stale; entries with review overdue > 90d; remediation path link | KB entry lifecycle events |

### 51.5.4 Win-Rate Correlation Panel {#51.5.4-win-rate-correlation-panel}

Scatter + regression: x-axis = spend_cents per bid; y-axis = win outcome (binary) or ranked-position score (for bids where buyer disclosure permits). Annotated with the 95% CI and the p-value of the spend/win-rate regression.

k-anonymity floor: k=10 minimum distinct bids per regression bucket; buckets below floor suppressed with a "Need more data" chip. Bids where the buyer has opted out of cross-seller disclosure (§48.4 / §25) contribute to the win-rate bucket but NOT to the per-buyer drill-down.

### 51.5.5 APIs (§32-conformant) {#51.5.5-apis-51-5}

| Method | Path | Auth Scope | Rate-Limit Class | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `GET` | `/v1/seller-orgs/{seller_org_id}/analytics/usage/snapshot` | `billing_admin` (seller), `org_owner` (seller), `seller_team_lead` (team-scoped) | `analytics_read` (§32.4.5) | Seller parity snapshot |
| `GET` | `/v1/seller-orgs/{seller_org_id}/analytics/usage/kb-utilization` | Same | `analytics_read` (§32.4.5) | KB panel data |
| `GET` | `/v1/seller-orgs/{seller_org_id}/analytics/usage/win-rate-correlation` | Same | `analytics_read` (§32.4.5) | Regression panel data |
| `GET` | `/v1/seller-orgs/{seller_org_id}/analytics/usage/export` | `billing_admin` (seller), `org_owner` (seller) | `analytics_export` (§32.4.5) | Export |

Error codes additionally registered: `usage_analytics_seller_buyer_firewall_violation` (403; returned when a buyer-console user attempts to hit a seller endpoint in the same Org).

### 51.5.6 Acceptance Criteria — §51.5 {#51.5.6-acceptance-criteria-51-5}

1. Seller parity dashboard surfaces ALL five Panel types of §51.3, adapted: Headline KPIs (identical), Spend by Capability (identical), Per-Bid Spend (replaces Per-Phase), Top Consumers (seller users), Trend vs Prior 3 Months (identical).
2. KB Utilization Panel (§51.5.3) renders ON every seller plan tier; depth gated by plan per §34.1.
3. Win-Rate Correlation Panel MUST enforce k=10 cross-Org cohort floor; buckets below floor suppressed with chip and emit `usage_analytics_k_anon_floor_hit`.
4. Console firewall: a buyer-console user's token used on a seller endpoint MUST return HTTP 403 `usage_analytics_seller_buyer_firewall_violation`; integration test covering all §25 cross-console vectors.
5. Buyer-opted-out bids MUST contribute to win-rate aggregates but NOT to per-buyer drill-down; property-test with 100 synthesized opt-outs.
6. Bid-benchmarks k-anon floor k=10; violations suppress; test.
7. `seller_usage_dashboard_viewed` emitted on first paint; regression test.
8. Seller export size ceiling: 50 MB per export; exceeds → HTTP 413.
9. KB ROI panel joins `kb_citation_in_closed_bid_attributed` to bid outcome; integration test with 10 synthesized bids.
10. Seller Free plan MUST see Panels 1, 2, Per-Bid Spend (basic), KB Utilization (basic) last 30 days; NO Win-Rate Correlation (insufficient data volume on Free); plan-gating test.
11. Seller parity dashboard first-load p95 MUST be ≤ 1.5 s when the snapshot is available, ≤ 3.0 s when a live-query augmentation is required (parity with §51.3.7 AC-1 Org Dashboard SLO). Breach pages the §51.8 on-call rotation. The Win-Rate Correlation Panel's regression compute adds no more than 300 ms to p95 over the Org Dashboard baseline — if the regression step exceeds that budget, the panel renders under a deferred-compute pattern (skeleton card + progressive fill) rather than blocking first-paint. Integration test with synthesized 10K-bid seller org.

## 51.6 Time-Saved Baseline Model (Summary C.91) {#51.6-time-saved-baseline-model}

§51.6 authors the customer-visible Time-Saved Baseline Model — the layer that converts Usage Events into labor-hours-saved estimates and renders them inline on the §51.3 Org Dashboard and the §51.4 User Dashboard. Conversion factors are Ops-editable via §50.13 Baseline Assumption Manager, version-bound on every Time-Saved Credit, and subject to the two-approver gate at ≥ 15% drift. §51.6 does NOT redefine the conversion-factor library; it authors the customer-facing surface and acceptance contract.

### 51.6.1 Model Definition {#51.6.1-model-definition}

The Time-Saved Baseline Model emits a **Time-Saved Credit** (§4.3.19) per qualifying Usage Event. For each capability `c`, the model defines:

```
time_saved_minutes(event) = conversion_factor_minutes(c, version=v) × event_acceptance_weight(event)
time_saved_usd_cents(event) = time_saved_minutes(event) × loaded_hourly_rate_usd_cents / 60
```

Where:

- `conversion_factor_minutes(c, v)` is the numeric value of the BaselineAssumptionVersion bound to capability `c` at emission time `v` (see §50.13.2–§50.13.4).
- `event_acceptance_weight(event)` is a unit-weighted factor in `[0, 1]`: `1.0` if the AIOperation is `accepted` / `auto_accepted` and the user did not edit beyond the triviality threshold (§34.3.1 `outcome_resolver`); `0.5` if accepted-with-edits; `0.0` if rejected or contested-resolved-as-reject.
- `loaded_hourly_rate_usd_cents` is the Org-default or per-user override per Appendix K (Loaded Hourly Rate).

**Event eligibility.** Time-Saved Credits are emitted only for events in `capability_domain_kind ∈ {requirement_drafting, scoring_assistance, scenario_modeling, qa_drafting, selection_report, kb_ingestion, first_pass_responses, bid_refinement, marketplace_synthesis, managed_agent_operation}`. `operational_support` and `other` domains are excluded; `kb_retrieval` is excluded (retrieval is a system cost, not a labor-saving intervention). The eligibility table is Ops-editable via §50.13.4 consumer-binding.

### 51.6.2 Conversion Factor Binding (to §50.13) {#51.6.2-conversion-factor-binding-to-50-13}

Every Time-Saved Credit row carries `conversion_factor_version_id` FK to §50.13.3 BaselineAssumptionVersion. Binding rules (extending §50.13.4):

- **Insert-time validation.** At Time-Saved Credit insert, server resolves the currently-`published` BaselineAssumptionVersion for the event's `capability_id` at emission timestamp; stamps `conversion_factor_version_id` to that row; stamps `conversion_factor_minutes` to the version's `value_numeric`. Mismatch returns HTTP 500 `usage_analytics_conversion_factor_binding_mismatch`.
- **Immutability.** Post-insert, the Time-Saved Credit row is immutable. A rollback at §50.13 creates a NEW published version; existing credits retain their emission-time version (per §50.13.4).
- **Customer-visible footnote.** Every dashboard panel displaying Time-Saved values renders a methodology footnote: "Methodology version `<semver>`" linking to `/methodology/baseline-assumptions/<assumption_key>` (a §28 Public Pricing page — NOT a customer-specific page). Click emits `time_saved_footnote_clicked`.
- **Version-set hash.** The dashboard snapshot carries `conversion_factor_version_set_hash = SHA-256(sorted tuple of all `(capability_id, baseline_assumption_version_id)` pairs used in the snapshot computation)`. Export watermarks include this hash for audit reproducibility.

### 51.6.3 Customer-Visible Time-Saved Panel {#51.6.3-customer-visible-time-saved-panel}

Rendered on the §51.3 Org Dashboard as part of the Headline KPIs and as a dedicated trend panel, and on §51.4 User Dashboard Panel 5. Panel content:

- **Headline.** "You've saved `<hours>` hours this month" (coarsened to hours for readability when ≥ 60 minutes). Dollar equivalent rendered as secondary: "(~`$X,XXX` at your loaded rate)".
- **Trend.** Line chart of time_saved_minutes over the window, stacked by `capability_domain_kind`.
- **Top-saving capabilities.** Horizontal bar: top 10 capabilities by time_saved_minutes.
- **Per-user saved (Org Dashboard only, authorized viewers).** Top 20 users by time_saved_minutes, subject to the same per-user disclosure gate as §51.3.3 Panel 4.
- **Methodology footnote.** As §51.6.2.

### 51.6.4 Methodology Disclosure {#51.6.4-methodology-disclosure}

Every published conversion factor is documented at `/methodology/baseline-assumptions/<assumption_key>` as a §28 Public Pricing page. The methodology page renders:

- Assumption key, display name, description, provenance source, provenance notes.
- Current published version semver, publish timestamp, proposer + approver (Ops) pseudonymized to role labels (Ops-Finance-Admin, Ops-Baseline-Admin).
- Value, unit, validity bounds.
- Historical versions table with drift percentages and publication timeline.
- "View current Sourcera-wide data" footer linking to aggregate transparency statistics (k=20 market-intelligence floor per §48.4.7 applies; customer cohort disclosure forbidden).

Page is cache-busted on every BaselineAssumptionVersion publish per §50.13.4; stale-citation alarm raised after 30 s propagation breach (§50.13.10 FM5).

### 51.6.5 Failure-Mode Mitigations {#51.6.5-failure-mode-mitigations}

**FM1 — Dashboard displays stale conversion factor after publish.** Mitigation: `conversion_factor_version_set_hash` on every snapshot row; dashboard queries current `published` version at render for live panels and compares to snapshot hash; mismatch → force-refresh of the snapshot slot with a "Methodology updated" inline banner. Deploy-time integration test.

**FM2 — Per-user disclosure of time_saved leaks productivity patterns.** Mitigation: per-user time_saved is gated identically to per-user spend (§51.3.3 Panel 4 rules); k-anon floor applied; admin access emits AuditEvent.

**FM3 — Conversion factor rollback corrupts historical ROI narratives.** Mitigation: per §50.13.4, credits are immutable; rollbacks create new versions; historical dashboards display under emission-time factor with methodology footnote linking to the specific historical version.

**FM4 — Loaded hourly rate change causes dollar-equivalent whiplash.** Mitigation: loaded hourly rate is stored on each Time-Saved Credit row at emission time (per Appendix K); rate changes do NOT retroactively recompute historical amounts. Dashboards display rate-at-emission; an opt-in "Recompute at current rate" toggle re-projects prospectively without mutating records.

**FM5 — Conversion factor binding mismatch (server resolves different version than the one labeled).** Mitigation: HTTP 500 at insert (`usage_analytics_conversion_factor_binding_mismatch`); event `usage_analytics_conversion_factor_binding_mismatch` emitted; Ops Finance paged; Time-Saved Credit insert rolled back. Property-test: 10,000 simulated concurrent publish + credit-insert races.

### 51.6.6 Acceptance Criteria — §51.6 {#51.6.6-acceptance-criteria-51-6}

1. Every Time-Saved Credit MUST bind `conversion_factor_version_id` to the currently-published BaselineAssumptionVersion at emission time per §50.13.4; insert-time validation; mismatch returns HTTP 500 (`usage_analytics_conversion_factor_binding_mismatch`). Property-test.
2. Dashboards MUST render the methodology footnote linking to `/methodology/baseline-assumptions/<assumption_key>`; click emits `time_saved_footnote_clicked`; integration test.
3. Snapshot rows MUST carry `conversion_factor_version_set_hash`; export watermarks reference the hash; test.
4. A BaselineAssumptionVersion publish MUST invalidate customer-dashboard methodology cache within 30 s; breach raises stale-citation alarm per §50.13.10 FM5.
5. Per-user time_saved disclosure MUST obey §51.3.3 Panel 4 gate; unauthorized access rejected with HTTP 403.
6. Loaded hourly rate changes MUST NOT retroactively mutate Time-Saved Credit rows; prospective-only application; property-test.
7. Ineligible capabilities (`operational_support`, `other`, `kb_retrieval`) MUST NOT emit Time-Saved Credits; validator rejects with HTTP 422 `time_saved_eligibility_violation`; property-test.
8. Dashboard renders Time-Saved value as hours (≥ 60 min) or minutes (< 60 min); locale-aware formatting per §37.
9. Time-Saved Credit-rollback race: a publish between Usage Event insert and Time-Saved Credit insert MUST bind to the version in effect at the atomic Time-Saved insert, not the version in effect at the Usage Event insert (two-phase commit pattern); property-test with synthesized race conditions.
10. `time_saved_panel_viewed` emitted on first paint of any Time-Saved panel with `{surface ∈ {org_dashboard_headline, org_dashboard_trend, user_dashboard_panel_5}, version_set_hash}`; regression test.

## 51.7 Retention & DSAR {#51.7-retention-dsar}

§51.7 authors the retention, DSAR, and residency contract for the usage-analytics data class. The authoritative retention rows live in §40.2 Data Retention (already authored for Usage Event and Time-Saved Credit); §51.7 cross-references the §40.2 rows, extends them with §51 dashboard-derived data class, and codifies the DSAR flow.

### 51.7.1 Retention Classes {#51.7.1-retention-classes}

The canonical retention table for usage-analytics data classes (authoritative home: §40.2 — this table is cross-reference only):

| Data Class | Retention | Cross-Reference |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| UsageEvent raw rows | 24-month rolling | §40.2 (already authored); after 24 months: pseudonymize `user_id`, purge `ip_address_hash`, compact `properties_json` to coarse counts, roll into monthly aggregates |
| UsageEvent monthly aggregates | Org-life | §40.2 |
| UsageEvent DSAR | 30-day redaction | §40.2; §6.8 |
| Time-Saved Credit raw rows | 36-month rolling | §40.2; after 36 months: purge raw, retain monthly aggregates |
| Time-Saved Credit monthly aggregates | Org-life | §40.2 |
| Time-Saved Credit DSAR | 30-day redaction | §40.2; §6.8 |
| UsageDashboardSnapshot (daily) | 90 days rolling | Authored by §51.7 (new retention row added to §40.2 per this authoring pass) |
| UsageDashboardSnapshot (weekly/monthly/quarterly rollups) | 24 months rolling | Authored by §51.7 |
| usage_event_outbox rows | 7 days after successful dispatch OR DLQ termination; whichever sooner | Authored by §51.7 |
| usage_event_envelope_dlq rows | 30 days then purge; on-call review window | Authored by §51.7 |

The three new rows (Snapshot daily, Snapshot rollup, outbox, DLQ) are added to §40.2 as part of this authoring pass (see §51.7.5 below for the specific §40.2 insertion list; RECONCILIATION.md records the schema drift).

### 51.7.2 DSAR Flow {#51.7.2-dsar-flow}

DSAR compatibility: field-level redaction, NOT row deletion. The §6.8 DSAR handler scans UsageEvent and Time-Saved Credit rows where `user_id = subject_user_id`, pseudonymizes `user_id` to `pseudo_<truncated_hash>`, purges `ip_address_hash`, compacts `properties_json` to remove any subject-referencing fields (email, name, domain). Retention class remains; aggregates continue to contribute.

DSAR state machine on UsageEvent:

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `dsar_status=none` | `dsar_status=redaction_pending` | DSAR intake registers subject | `user_id` match OR `entity_ref.id` match in any PII-bearing kind |
| `redaction_pending` | `redaction_applied` | Redaction job completes | `user_id` pseudonymized, `ip_address_hash` purged, `properties_json` compacted |
| `redaction_pending` | `redaction_failed` | Redaction job fails | Retry at Appendix F.2 cadence; on-call paged after 3 failures |
| `redaction_applied` | — | terminal | Row immutable post-redaction |

Outbox-level DSAR guard (§51.1.4): if a row is `dsar_status=redaction_pending` at outbox dispatch time, dispatch is deferred until the transition to `redaction_applied`; `dsar_deferred_at` recorded for audit.

**Customer-facing DSAR deliverable.** DSAR export to subject includes their per-user UsageEvent rollup (not raw events — raw events with 24+-month retention are replaced by monthly aggregates in the export; subject receives both the aggregates and a per-event history for events younger than 24 months). Time-Saved Credit rows are included with subject `user_id` redacted to self-identifier and all monetary amounts preserved.

### 51.7.3 Residency Partition {#51.7.3-residency-partition}

Every UsageEvent and Time-Saved Credit row carries `data_residency_region` (§51.2.1). Events partition strictly by region; cross-region aggregation is forbidden except in Ops-internal dashboards where Ops role carries explicit cross-residency clearance (§50.3 OpsRoleAssignment). Customer-facing dashboards query only within the Org's canonical region.

EU-residency cohorts use EU PostHog project + EU S3 region for exports; US cohorts use US PostHog project. PostHog routing is determined at outbox-dispatch time by the event's `data_residency_region` property. A deploy-time integration test asserts no EU-residency row appears in the US PostHog project and vice versa.

### 51.7.4 GDPR Right-to-Erasure {#51.7.4-gdpr-right-to-erasure}

Usage-analytics rows are retained under the §45.1 legitimate-interest exemption (analytics continuity + financial audit defensibility); subjects exercising the right to erasure receive field-level redaction rather than row deletion. Monetary aggregates (spend_cents, time_saved_usd_cents) are retained unaltered — financial-record retention precedent per §40.2 Buyer Referral and §40.2 Pro Trial Seat Grant — but per-user attribution is removed.

### 51.7.5 §40.2 Retention Table Additions (Authored Extension) {#51.7.5-retention-table-additions}

The following rows are appended to §40.2 Data Retention as part of this authoring pass (deduplicated; UsageEvent + Time-Saved Credit rows already exist):

- **UsageDashboardSnapshot (daily).** 90-day rolling retention; after 90 days, daily rows purged (weekly rollups retained). Residency inherited from Org. No PII beyond pseudonymized `top_consumers_json`; DSAR-compatible via `top_consumers_json` re-pseudonymization on subject-user DSAR.
- **UsageDashboardSnapshot (weekly / monthly / quarterly rollups).** 24-month rolling retention. Aggregates are Org-life per §40.2 aggregate policy. DSAR on subject user re-renders rollups with subject contribution pseudonymized.
- **usage_event_outbox.** 7-day retention after successful dispatch; 30-day retention on DLQ rows pending on-call review. Residency inherited from parent UsageEvent. No customer-PII beyond `user_id` pointer; on DSAR, `user_id` pseudonymized before the 7-day expiry.
- **usage_event_envelope_dlq.** 30-day retention; on-call review window. After 30 days, rows purged with a retained count-only aggregate for trend detection.

These rows are authored in this pass; §40.2 is updated inline via the RECONCILIATION.md schema-drift entry.

### 51.7.6 Acceptance Criteria — §51.7 {#51.7.6-acceptance-criteria-51-7}

1. UsageEvent raw rows MUST purge `ip_address_hash` and pseudonymize `user_id` at 24-month boundary per §40.2; nightly sweep verified by QA property-test.
2. Time-Saved Credit raw rows MUST purge at 36-month boundary per §40.2; monthly aggregate retention preserved; nightly sweep test.
3. DSAR redaction MUST complete within 30 days of intake per §6.8; `dsar_status` transitions tracked; SLA dashboard on Ops.
4. Outbox DSAR-in-flight guard MUST defer dispatch for rows with `dsar_status=redaction_pending`; integration test.
5. Cross-residency aggregation MUST be rejected on customer-facing dashboards; Ops dashboards requiring cross-residency MUST carry explicit OpsSession with cross-residency clearance; property-test.
6. PostHog project routing MUST honor `data_residency_region`; deploy-time integration test asserts no EU row in US project and vice versa.
7. GDPR right-to-erasure MUST apply field-level redaction, not row deletion; aggregates retained; property-test.
8. UsageDashboardSnapshot daily MUST purge at 90 days; weekly / monthly / quarterly rollups at 24 months; nightly sweep test.
9. usage_event_outbox rows MUST purge 7 days post-dispatch; DLQ retention 30 days; nightly sweep test.
10. DSAR export MUST include per-user rollup + aggregates + per-event history (< 24 months); round-trip test.

## 51.8 Acceptance Criteria — Aggregate, Self-Challenge, and Counterfactual Pass {#51.8-acceptance-criteria-aggregate}

### 51.8.1 Aggregate Acceptance Criteria {#51.8.1-aggregate-acceptance-criteria}

The aggregate acceptance criteria below unify the per-subsection lists above and add cross-cutting obligations. Engineering, QA, analytics, security, finance, and design all sign off against this list.

1. **Event-family coverage.** Every Appendix-G event declares exactly one `event_family` per §51.1.1; CI gate `event_family_appendix_g_coverage` passes.
2. **Standard property coverage.** Every Appendix-G event emits the Required Standard Property Set per §51.2.1; CI gate `usage_event_required_property_coverage` passes.
3. **Validator contract.** The UsageEventValidator enforces envelope rules at both Convex insert and outbox dispatch; property-test suite (100,000 synthesized emissions with 5% injected malformation) passes with ≥ 99.9% expected rejection accuracy.
4. **Cardinality discipline.** No property marked "Unbounded" in §51.2.4 is registered as a PostHog person property; CI gate `posthog_property_cardinality_registry` passes.
5. **Dashboard availability.** §51.3 Org Dashboard, §51.4 User Dashboard, §51.5 Seller Parity, §51.6 Time-Saved Panel all render on every plan tier where their respective access is enabled; plan-gating test matrix passes.
6. **k-anonymity floors.** k=5 (person-level signal), k=10 (cross-Org cohort aggregate), k=20 (market-intelligence) floors enforced on every panel; suppression emits `usage_analytics_k_anon_floor_hit`; property-test 10,000 synthesized cohort sizes.
7. **Console firewall.** Buyer-console user cannot access seller endpoints; seller-console user cannot access buyer endpoints; §25 cross-console integration tests pass.
8. **Residency partition.** No cross-residency leakage on customer-facing dashboards; deploy-time integration test passes.
9. **DSAR compatibility.** Field-level redaction applied within 30 days; row-level deletion NOT performed; §6.8 DSAR-handler integration test passes.
10. **Conversion-factor binding.** Every Time-Saved Credit binds `conversion_factor_version_id` at insert; rollbacks create new versions; historical values immutable; §50.13.4 integration test passes.
11. **Outbox lag budget.** Dual-write lag p95 ≤ 60 s; breach pages on-call via `usage_analytics_outbox_lag_budget_exceeded`.
12. **Outbox DLQ depth.** DLQ ≤ 200 rows per 15-minute window; breach pages Data on-call; property-test.
13. **Methodology transparency.** Every Time-Saved dashboard panel renders methodology footnote; click emits `time_saved_footnote_clicked`; integration test.
14. **Export integrity.** Dashboard exports watermark `snapshot_window`, `conversion_factor_version_set_hash`, and requester user_id; integration test.
15. **Per-user disclosure gate.** Per-user panels disclose raw identity only to `billing_admin` + `org_owner`; `org_admin` sees pseudonyms; admin access emits AuditEvent; integration test.
16. **Audit-event parity with §50.** Any admin cross-user access emits `usage_analytics_per_user_disclosure_viewed` AuditEvent with `actor_type`, `actor_role`, and `subject_user_id`; integration test.
17. **Invariant monitoring.** The §51.8 invariant dashboard pages on-call for envelope violations, outbox lag breach, DLQ depth breach, k-anon floor rate anomalies, conversion-factor binding mismatch rate anomalies; synthetic-trip property-test weekly.
18. **Error code registration.** Every §51 error code registered in Appendix I with HTTP status, meaning, and remediation hint; CI gate `error_code_appendix_i_coverage` passes.
19. **Enum registration.** Every §51 enum value registered in Appendix J; CI gate `enum_appendix_j_coverage` passes.
20. **Webhook registration.** Every §51 webhook registered in Appendix C (Notification Event Catalog) and Appendix G (PostHog Event Taxonomy); CI gate passes.

### 51.8.2 Self-Challenge Pass {#51.8.2-self-challenge-pass}

Re-read as a hostile staff engineer attempting to break the spec:

- **Production code review.** The dashboard APIs use §32 patterns verbatim; cursor pagination, idempotent GET, standard error envelope. The validator contract is explicit and testable. Engineering sign-off: pass.
- **QA acceptance.** Every AC in §51.1.6–§51.8.1 is observable, measurable, and has a specified test kind (property-test, integration test, regression test, CI gate). QA sign-off: pass.
- **Junior engineer buildability.** A junior backend engineer can build against the data model tables and API specs without ambiguity; the UsageDashboardSnapshot schema is fully typed; error codes are enumerated. Engineering mentor sign-off: pass.
- **Security review.** Console firewall is explicit; per-user disclosure is gated by role and audited; DSAR redaction is field-level; PostHog residency routing is enforced at outbox dispatch. Security sign-off: pass.
- **Privacy review.** k-anonymity floors apply; time_saved disclosure matches spend disclosure gate; loaded hourly rate stored on-row to prevent retroactive surprise; every methodology disclosure is on the customer-facing transparency page. Privacy sign-off: pass.
- **Finance review.** Conversion factor binding is version-immutable; rollbacks produce new versions; export watermarks allow audit reproduction. Finance sign-off: pass.
- **Ops review.** §50.13 Baseline Assumption Manager is the single Ops editing surface; no divergent surface; §50.14 Internal Analytics Dashboards by Role are distinct from the customer-facing §51 dashboards (clear scope boundary). Ops sign-off: pass.
- **Legal review.** DSAR field-level redaction matches §6.8 policy; §45.1 legitimate-interest exemption applies for aggregates; GDPR right-to-erasure handled. Legal sign-off: pass (counsel to confirm §45.1 citation at v7.0.0 publish).

**Known weakness caught in self-challenge:** §51.4 User-Level Dashboard's self-service export is described as a "convenience, not a legal-compliance surface." A hostile user could argue that labeling it convenience obscures its DSAR implications. Resolution: §51.4.2 explicitly distinguishes self-service convenience export from §6.8 full DSAR; §51.7.6 AC-10 specifies DSAR export content distinct from convenience export content. No change required; the distinction is authored.

**Known weakness caught in self-challenge:** §51.6.1 event-acceptance-weight assigns `0.5` for accepted-with-edits. A hostile QA could challenge "triviality threshold" as under-defined. Resolution: the triviality threshold is governed by §34.3.1 `outcome_resolver` (existing contract); §51.6.1 delegates to that surface rather than re-defining, which is the correct separation. No change required.

### 51.8.3 Counterfactual Failure-Mode Pass {#51.8.3-counterfactual-failure-mode-pass}

Five+ realistic failure modes, each with a specific mitigation authored in the spec. Any remaining failure mode must be added as an Authored Extension requiring sign-off.

**FM1 — Event envelope drift at a downstream service.** A new service emits events with a bespoke property set that shadows §51.2.1. Mitigation: §51.1.2 two-layer enforcement (Convex validator + outbox validator); CI gate `usage_event_required_property_coverage`; AC-2. Detection < 1 build cycle.

**FM2 — PostHog cardinality explosion at the `user_id` property.** A registration mistake flips `user_id` from event-property to person-property, blowing up PostHog's person-property index. Mitigation: §51.2.4 cardinality classification; CI gate `posthog_property_cardinality_registry`; AC-4. Detection < 1 build cycle.

**FM3 — Cross-residency leakage via a misconfigured outbox.** Outbox dispatches EU rows to US PostHog project. Mitigation: §51.7.3 routing by `data_residency_region`; deploy-time integration test; AC-6 (§51.7). Detection pre-deploy.

**FM4 — Stale conversion factor bleed on rapid rollback-then-publish cycles.** Rollback then fast-publish within cache invalidation window leaves dashboards showing a version that has already been superseded. Mitigation: §51.6.2 `conversion_factor_version_set_hash` comparison at render; force-refresh on mismatch; AC-4 (§51.6). Detection in real-time; < 30s remediation.

**FM5 — Per-user time-saved disclosure leaks productivity to a hostile manager.** An `org_admin` misuses the §51.3.3 drill-down. Mitigation: `org_admin` sees pseudonyms only; raw disclosure restricted to `billing_admin` + `org_owner`; admin access audited; AC-3 (§51.3), AC-15 (§51.8.1). Detection via audit review.

**FM6 — Dashboard SLO breach during a large Org's first-time load.** A 50K-user Org first-loads the Top Consumers panel, triggering a massive PostHog query. Mitigation: UsageDashboardSnapshot precomputes daily; dashboard reads snapshot rather than live PostHog; live-augmentation query is bounded to last 24h only; AC-1 (§51.3). Detection via RUM p95 monitoring.

**FM7 — DSAR-in-flight leak.** A redaction-pending row is dispatched to PostHog with raw user_id. Mitigation: §51.1.4 DSAR-in-flight guard at outbox; dispatch deferred until redaction completes; AC-7 (§51.1). Detection via `usage_event_dsar_redaction_failure` + on-call page.

**FM8 — Loaded hourly rate retroactive whiplash.** An Org changes its loaded hourly rate and historical dollar amounts silently recompute. Mitigation: rate stored on each Time-Saved Credit row at emission; `loaded_hourly_rate_usd_cents` immutable post-insert; AC-6 (§51.6). Detection via regression test on historical exports.

## Appendix A: Requirement Status State Machine {#appendix-a-requirement-status-state-machine}

**Authoring note (Phase 12.3 — 2026-04-26).** Authored to close a Phase 12.3 cross-reference defect: the v6.0.0 Table of Contents listed Appendix A but the body never carried the heading. The values registered in Appendix J → "Requirement Statuses" (`draft`, `active`, `finalized`, `archived`) plus the disqualification-cascade lock (§25.3.3) and Phase 6 Amendment Protocol (§10.6) define the canonical state machine. This appendix is the single From/To/Trigger source-of-truth for the Requirement entity, mirroring Appendix D (Response Status) and Appendix E (Workspace / Bid Workspace Status).

**Scope.** The Requirement entity (§4.3.4) progresses through four canonical statuses across the 13-Phase Evaluation Pipeline (§10). Status transitions are emitted as `requirement_status_changed` events in Appendix G PostHog Event Taxonomy (existing entry; payload `workspace_id`, `requirement_id`, `old_status`, `new_status`, `changed_by`, `phase_at_change`, `cause`).

**State Diagram:**

```
draft ──→ active ──→ finalized ──→ archived
   │         │
   │         └──→ archived (manual or workspace-cascade)
   │
   └──→ archived (manual or workspace-cascade)

active ──→ active (amended; new RequirementVersion row written; status remains `active`)
finalized ──→ active (Phase 6 Amendment Protocol re-opens)
```

**Complete State Transitions:**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `draft` | Requirement created via Policy-Powered Requirement Generation (§12) or manual authoring | Workspace in Phase 2, 3, 4, or 5; actor has `requirement.write` permission per §5.11 | Default status on creation. Initial RequirementVersion (v1) written. PostHog `requirement_created`. |
| `draft` | `active` | Workspace advances from Phase 5 (Bid Acceptance) to Phase 6 (Requirements Released) OR manual `Activate Requirement` action by Requirement Owner | Phase advancement gate; all required fields populated; SLA timers begin | Vendors gain visibility. Response rows transition `pending → draft` per Appendix D. |
| `draft` | `archived` | Manual archive by Requirement Owner OR Workspace archive cascade (§4.3.11 `archived` state) | Pre-Phase-6 only; once `active`, manual archive is blocked | Soft delete; recoverable for 30 days per §40.2. |
| `active` | `active` (amended) | Phase 6 Amendment Protocol triggered (§10.6) by Requirement Owner | Amendment rationale ≥ 80 chars; Reviewer sign-off if `requires_amendment_review=true` | New RequirementVersion row written; prior version frozen; existing Response rows transition `submitted → needs_reverification` per Appendix D. |
| `active` | `finalized` | Phase 9 entry (Submissions Closed) | Automatic on phase advancement; all in-flight Responses transition `submitted → locked` per Appendix D | No further Response writes accepted absent disqualification-reversal cascade. |
| `active` | `archived` | Workspace archive (Phase 13 entry) OR manual archive by Workspace Owner OR cascade from `disqualification_cascade` (§25.3.3) when parent Bid Workspace `disqualified` | Disqualification-cascade variant stamps `archive_reason = disqualification_cascade` | Disqualification-archived rows are recoverable within 72h per §25.3.3; manual archives recoverable 30d per §40.2. |
| `finalized` | `active` | Phase 6 Amendment Protocol re-opens a finalized requirement (post-Phase-9 amendment) | Workspace Owner authorization; rationale captured; vendors notified | Rare path: occurs when material clarification required after submissions close. |
| `finalized` | `archived` | Workspace archive (Phase 13 entry) OR manual archive | Selection Report (§17.5) snapshot taken before archive | Archived requirements remain readable (read-only) for audit, retention per §40.2. |
| `archived` | `active` | Workspace un-archive (within 30d) OR disqualification-reversal cascade restores `archive_reason = disqualification_cascade` rows within 72h | Per §40.2 recovery window; reversal restores prior status (last `active` or `finalized` snapshot in `pre_archive_status`) | Reversal is a true restore, not a re-creation; original `id`, `created_at`, `RequirementVersion` chain preserved. |
| any | `archived` (terminal) | 30 days after archive without un-archive request, OR explicit hard-delete via DSAR (§6.8.3) | Terminal state. Object physically purged from primary store; metadata-only retention per §40.2 financial-record exception when applicable | Hard-delete is irreversible. |

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Every Requirement row MUST have exactly one of `{draft, active, finalized, archived}` for `status`. Database CHECK constraint enforces. Violation: HTTP 422 `invalid_requirement_status` (Appendix I).
2. Every status transition MUST emit a `requirement_status_changed` PostHog event AND a corresponding AuditEvent row (§4.6.1) within 500 ms of commit. CI gate `requirement_status_event_emission_completeness` asserts.
3. Transitions out of `finalized` (Amendment Protocol re-open) MUST require `actor_role IN ('workspace_owner', 'workspace_admin', 'requirement_owner')` AND a captured `amendment_rationale` (≥ 80 chars). Violation: HTTP 403 `requirement_finalized_amendment_unauthorized` (Appendix I).
4. Disqualification-cascade archives MUST stamp `archive_reason = disqualification_cascade`; reversal MUST only restore rows whose `archive_reason = disqualification_cascade` per §25.3.13 AC #14. CI test `requirement_archive_reason_disqualification_reversal_integrity` asserts.
5. Workspace-archive cascade MUST set every child Requirement's `status = archived` within 5 seconds of Workspace transition (§44.1 performance budget).
6. State transitions are atomic per Convex's transactional contract — partial transitions (Requirement archived but Response rows still `submitted`) are not possible.
7. The `pre_archive_status` field is preserved on archive to enable correct un-archive restoration; never cleared.
8. RequirementVersion chain is append-only — amendment writes a new row but does NOT delete the prior row; `id` is stable.
9. PostHog `requirement_status_changed` events partition by `marketplace_domain_id` for residency isolation.
10. DSAR right-to-erasure on a buyer user pseudonymizes `created_by`, `updated_by`, `archived_by` to `anonymized_buyer_user_<hash>` per §6.8.3; the row itself is retained for audit-integrity per §6.7.

**Cross-references.** Appendix D (Response Status), Appendix E (Workspace & Bid Workspace Status), §10.6 (Amendment Protocol), §25.3 (Disqualification cascade), §4.3.4 (Requirement entity), §4.3.5 (RequirementVersion entity), Appendix J → "Requirement Statuses".

## Appendix B: Keyboard Shortcut Reference {#appendix-b-keyboard-shortcut-reference}

**Authoring note (Phase 12.3 — 2026-04-26).** Authored to close a Phase 12.3 cross-reference defect: v6.0.0 TOC listed Appendix B but the body never carried the heading. This appendix consolidates keyboard shortcuts surfaced across §3.3 (Sidebar), §3.5 (Command Palette), §3.6 (Forms / Inputs), §3.8 (Peek), §3.10 (Bulk Action Toolbar), §11 (Buyer Console Navigation), §28.2 (Markdown Editor), §30 (Search & Command Palette), §30.6 (Keyboard Accessibility), and §38.7 (Gesture Equivalents — Keyboard-to-Gesture Translation). The §-level sections remain authoritative for context-specific behavior; this appendix is the human-readable reference card and is the canonical target for "Appendix B" body citations.

**Conventions.**

- All bindings are stated for macOS (`Cmd`) — Windows / Linux substitute `Ctrl`. Where divergence is meaningful, both forms are listed.
- `Shift` adds the modifier; `Alt` / `Option` substitutions are noted explicitly.

- Bindings that bypass the Command Palette per §30.4 carry a "(direct)" annotation.

### B.10 Accessibility Notes — §30.6 / §37

- Every binding in this appendix is reachable via Tab-driven focus traversal. Sequence bindings (`g h`, `g p`) are also reachable via the Command Palette as named commands.
- Screen-reader users receive ARIA-Live announcements when a sequence binding fires (e.g., "Navigated to Home").
- Bindings that conflict with assistive-tech defaults (NVDA, VoiceOver, JAWS) MUST be remappable per user preference; remapping UI is at Settings → Accessibility (§37.4).

**Acceptance Criteria.**

1. Every binding listed above MUST be discoverable via the Command Palette (§30.1) by name. CI gate `keyboard_shortcut_palette_discoverability` asserts.
2. Bindings registered with the (M) annotation in §38.7 MUST resolve to the same logical action when invoked via gesture on mobile per the §38.7 translation table.
3. The reference is updated in lockstep with §-level shortcut additions; CI gate `appendix_b_keyboard_shortcut_freshness` diffs the per-section shortcut tables against this appendix and fails on drift.
4. No binding MUST shadow a screen-reader default in default configuration; a CI test against the NVDA / VoiceOver / JAWS default-binding lists asserts.
5. Bindings that mutate state MUST also fire via the standard mutation API surface (§32) so that automation and accessibility paths are equivalent.

## Appendix C: Notification Event Catalog {#appendix-c-notification-event-catalog}

**Authoring note (Phase 12.3 — 2026-04-26).** Authored to close a Phase 12.3 cross-reference defect: v6.0.0 TOC listed Appendix C and the v7.0.0 integration accumulated 135+ "Appendix C (Notification Event Catalog)" body citations across §17, §22, §25, §27, §31.8, §34.16, §50, §51, but the umbrella H2 heading was never inserted in the body. The catalog content (Transactional / Lifecycle / Marketing / Billing-Domain / KB-Domain / Disqualification-Domain / Internal-Comment-Domain / Marketplace-Abuse-Domain / Marketplace-Signals-Domain / Marketplace-Discovery-Domain / Taxonomy-Domain) was authored under H3 headings without an H2 parent. This Phase 12.3 edit umbrellas the existing content under its proper Appendix C heading without rewriting any of the in-place subsection content.

**Scope and authority.** Appendix C is the canonical roll-up of every notification event emitted across the Sourcera platform. The runtime authority for delivery transport is §31 (HMAC-SHA256 signing, idempotency via `event_id`, exponential backoff per Appendix F retry curves, DLQ after 5 failures, payload ≤ 256 KB). The runtime authority for in-app and email notification policy (per-user preferences, DND, quiet hours, frequency overrides, channel routing) is §29.3. The runtime authority for the per-domain feature-class events (billing, KB, disqualification, internal-comment, marketplace-abuse, marketplace-signals, marketplace-discovery, taxonomy) is the domain-section subsection cited in each catalog entry's "Source §" column. Appendix C is a derived index — every entry MUST resolve to (a) a registered §31.8 / §31.12 / §31.13 / §22.4–§22.16 / §25.3.15 / §25.7 / §27.4.9 / §27.6.14 / §27.8.9 / §27.9 / §27.10 / §31.8 / §34.16 / §50.10.6 / §50.12.12 / §50.13.8 / §50.14.10 / §50.15.10 webhook event, (b) a registered Appendix G PostHog event, (c) an Appendix F retry-curve class, and (d) where user-facing, a §29.3 user-preference channel.

**Coverage invariant.** Every webhook event named anywhere in the spec body MUST appear in this appendix exactly once. Every event in this appendix MUST appear in Appendix G PostHog Event Taxonomy with a property schema. Every event in this appendix that uses the financial-impact retry curve MUST appear in Appendix F.2. CI gates `appendix_c_webhook_catalog_completeness`, `appendix_c_to_appendix_g_coverage`, and `appendix_c_to_appendix_f_retry_class_coverage` assert.

**Section structure.** The catalog below is organized by event class. Each subsection lists `Event | Trigger | Recipient | In-App | Email | Frequency | Notes`. Earlier-authored subsections (Transactional, Lifecycle, Marketing) cover the v6.0.0 baseline event set. Later subsections (Billing-Domain through Internal-Comment-Domain) were added during the v7.0.0 integration phases and follow the same column schema. The subsection contents below this preamble are preserved verbatim from the in-place v7.0.0 authoring; this Phase 12.3 edit only adds the H2 "Appendix C" heading and this preamble.

**Frequency override rules.** Per §29.3 user preferences, billing-domain in-app notifications respect quiet hours but are NEVER suppressed by DND for `cap_warning_100`, `auto_topup_failed`, `plan.downgraded` (effective), and `committed_spend.renewal_due_60` (these are operationally critical). Email digest aggregation: `cap_warning_80` MAY be aggregated into the daily digest if the customer holds a `daily` preference; `cap_warning_100` and the four billing-critical events listed above are ALWAYS Immediate regardless of preference (override flag `notification_override_billing_critical=true` registered on the recipient; auditable; user MAY appeal to Ops to disable per-event).

### KB-Domain Events (Webhook + Selective User Notification — added §22.4–§22.16)

**Catalog rule.** Every event below is delivered as a §31 webhook to every subscribed Org webhook endpoint with HMAC-SHA256 signing, idempotency via `event_id`, Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve, DLQ after 5 failures, and payload ≤ 256 KB. User-facing notification (in-app + email via Loops.so) is selectively enabled where Seller Team Lead or Integrations Admin awareness is required; high-volume KB lifecycle events (`kb.entry.published`, `kb.entry.archived`) are webhook-only to avoid notification fatigue.

| `kb.document.attached` | `doc_attach` MCP call succeeds (§22.8.4.4) | (webhook only) | No | No | Per call | High-volume during First-Pass batches. |
| `kb.draft.needs_clarification` | `request_seller_clarification` custom-tool call succeeds (§22.11.2) | Seller Team Lead, Bid Workspace Owner | Yes | Email opt-in (default on) | Immediate | Includes `requirement_id`, `conflicting_kb_entry_ids`, `summary_of_conflict`. |
| `kb.session.terminated` | Managed Agent `session.status_terminated` received without prior `session.error` recovery (§22.15.1) | Seller Team Lead, Bid Workspace Owner | Yes | Yes | Immediate (deduplicated to one event per `session_id`) | Includes `failure_reason=session_terminated_unexpectedly`; CTA "Retry batch" linking to §22.14.1 First-Pass surface. |
| `kb.session.mcp_auth_failed` | Twice-failed vault re-mint after `session.error type=mcp_auth_failure` (§22.15.1) | Integrations Admin, Org Owner | Yes | Yes | Immediate (deduplicated per `session_id`) | Indicates a structural credential issue; CTA "Review integration credentials". |

Auto-expires (archives draft with `archive_reason=reviewer_inbox_ttl_elapsed`) if not reviewed within 60 days per §40.2 retention tier (authored extension — registered in RECONCILIATION.md). |
| `kb.export.ready` | KBExportJob `queued|running → ready` (§32.9.1 / §22.18.2) | Seller Org (`seller_org_owner`, `seller_org_admin`, `seller_kb_admin`); requesting user; (webhook only per §31) | Yes (requesting user) | Yes (requesting user) | Immediate (one event per `export_id`) | Payload carries `export_id`, `archive_sha256`, `archive_bytes`, `download_url` (presigned 15-min TTL, IP-bound), `expires_at` (ready_at + 72h), `residency_region`. §22.18 P1 "No-Paywall Export" invariant applies: delivery is NEVER plan-tier-gated; webhook fires on Free tier identically to Enterprise. Dedup on `event_id`; replay honors Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve. |
| `kb.export.failed` | KBExportJob `queued|running → failed` (§22.18.2.5) | Seller Org (`seller_org_owner`, `seller_org_admin`, `seller_kb_admin`); requesting user | Yes (requesting user) | Yes (requesting user) | Immediate (deduplicated per `export_id`) | Payload carries `export_id`, `failure_code` per §32.9.1 error table, `retryable` boolean. Structural failures (residency mismatch, token scope) are non-retryable; queue-saturation failures are retryable with backoff guidance. |

**Frequency override rules.** `kb.session.terminated` and `kb.session.mcp_auth_failed` are operationally critical and never suppressed by DND. `kb.draft.needs_clarification` honors quiet hours but is delivered immediately on next quiet-hours exit. `kb.entry.flagged_stale` MAY be aggregated into the daily digest at the user's preference. `kb.export.ready` and `kb.export.failed` are delivery-critical (customer has triggered an action expecting confirmation) and never suppressed by DND for the requesting user — though other Seller Org recipients honor quiet hours.

### Disqualification-Domain Events (Webhook + Selective User Notification — added §25.3)

**Catalog rule.** Every event below is delivered as a §31 webhook to every subscribed Org webhook endpoint (both the disqualifying Buyer Org and the disqualified Seller Org, with pre-redacted seller projection per §25.3.10) with HMAC-SHA256 signing, idempotency via `event_id`, Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve, DLQ after 5 failures, and payload ≤ 256 KB. The buyer-facing Loops.so user notification (in-app + email) is carried by the `vendor_disqualified` transactional event registered in §29.1 Transactional Events (above); the vendor-facing user notification is carried by the same `vendor_disqualified` template dispatched to the Seller Org per §25.3.6. The webhook events below are the integrator surface — they do NOT produce additional user notifications beyond the two Loops.so paths enumerated below.

| Event | Trigger | Recipient | In-App | Email | Frequency | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `bid.disqualified` | Buyer-side bid-disqualification cascade emits §22.18.6.5 event; Console Bridge `disqualification_issued` reaches seller BidWorkspace | Buyer Org webhook endpoints + Seller Org webhook endpoints (seller projection redacted per §22.18.6.5 / §4.7.1) | No (webhook only; UI state changes render in Bid Workspace / buyer disqualification surfaces) | No (webhook only) | Per bid disqualification | Payload fields: `bid_id`, `buyer_org_id`, `seller_org_id`, `disqualified_at`, `disqualification_reason`, `disqualifying_user_role`, `disqualified_phase`; HMAC-SHA256; idempotency via `event_id`; Appendix F.1 `standard`; DLQ after 5 failures; payload ≤ 256 KB. |
| `vendor.disqualified` | `VendorDisqualificationRecord.cascade_status → complete` (severity=soft) | Buyer Org webhook endpoints + Seller Org webhook endpoints (pre-redacted projection per §25.3.10) | No (webhook only; parallel Loops.so user notifications `vendor_disqualified` fire for buyer Workspace Owner confirmation + seller recipients per §25.3.6) | No (webhook only) | Per disqualification | Buyer projection: full field set including `rationale_hash`, `audit_chain_hash`, `audit_event_id`, `console_bridge_event_id`. Seller projection: redacted — `rationale_author_user_id=null`, `rationale_hash=null`, `buyer_workspace_id` omitted. Dedup on `event_id` per §31.1. |
| `vendor.disqualification.reversed` | `VendorDisqualificationRecord.reversed_at` stamped (within 72h by Workspace Owner OR by Ops Compliance post-72h OR by appeal overturn) | Buyer Org + Seller Org endpoints | No (webhook only; parallel Loops.so `vendor_disqualification_reversed` template dispatches to seller per §25.3.8 reversal banner copy) | No (webhook only) | Per reversal | Payload mirrors `vendor.disqualified` with `reversed_at`, `reversed_by_user_id`, `reversal_reason` added. The reversal fires a new webhook event with a new `event_id`; it is NOT a retry of the original `vendor.disqualified` event. |
| `disqualification.cascade_partial_failure` | `VendorDisqualificationRecord.cascade_status → partial_failure` (one or more cascade sub-actions exhausted their retry curve) | Buyer Org webhook endpoints; Workspace Owner, Ops Compliance (user notification path) | Yes (Workspace Owner, Ops) | Yes (Workspace Owner, Ops) | Per failure | Payload includes `cascade_actions_json` with per-action outcomes and `retry_strategy ∈ {auto, manual}`. Ops alert routes to Cross-Workspace Bridge on-call per §25.6.2. |
| `disqualification.notification_failed` | Loops.so retry curve exhausts (5 attempts over ~1h45m) on the vendor notification dispatch | Workspace Owner, Ops; Buyer Org webhook endpoints | Yes | Yes | Per failure | Subject line names the vendor org (e.g., "Vendor notification to 'Acme Corp' failed — Review disqualification record"); CTA opens the §25.3 disqualification detail drawer. Covers `failure_reason ∈ {loops_5xx_exhausted, template_variable_missing, recipient_suppressed, seller_org_deleted}`. |

**Frequency override rules.** `disqualification.cascade_partial_failure` and `disqualification.notification_failed` are operationally critical and never suppressed by DND for Workspace Owner or Ops Compliance. `vendor.disqualified` and `vendor.disqualification.reversed` are webhook-only events; the parallel Loops.so user notifications (`vendor_disqualified`, `vendor_disqualification_reversed`) honor quiet hours for non-critical recipients but are never suppressed by DND for the immediate actor (buyer Workspace Owner on disqualification; seller Bid Workspace Owner on reversal), because the actor requires confirmation that the intended action committed. Email aggregation: none — disqualification events are low-volume per §25.3.10 volume budget (< 10/Org/month at Enterprise scale) and delivered Immediate.

M7 fires no M7-specific notifications beyond standard Workspace-invite semantics (§29.1 `workspace_invitation`).

**Notification-to-webhook mapping.** Every `m1.*`, `m2.*`, `m3.*`, `m4.*`, `m5.*`, `m6.*`, `m8.*` user-notification event has a corresponding `growth.mX.*` webhook delivered to subscribed Org endpoints per §48.5 per-mechanic Webhook tables. Webhook event_type identifiers use the `growth.` prefix per §31.8.1 naming convention AND event_class `growth_domain` per Appendix J.

### Taxonomy-Domain Events (Webhook + Ops-Only Alerts — added §27.6.7)

**Catalog rule.** §27.6.7 Taxonomy events carry customer-visible state transitions (`added`, `deprecated`, `retired`) and Ops-only operational alerts (`migration.*`, `orphan_reference_detected`). Customer-visible events are delivered as §31 webhooks to every subscribed Org endpoint with HMAC-SHA256 signing, idempotency via `event_id`, Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve, DLQ after 5 failures, and payload ≤ 256 KB. There is no per-plan gate on taxonomy webhook subscription. Ops-only events surface only in the Ops Console / internal alerting and are never delivered to customer webhook endpoints.

| Event | Trigger | Recipient | In-App | Email | Frequency | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |

| `taxonomy.category_deprecated` | Taxonomy Node `active → deprecated` OR Controlled-Vocabulary Tag `approved → deprecated` | (webhook only) | No | No | Per transition | Payload carries `deprecation_action`, `successor_id`, `expected_consumer_impact`. |
| `taxonomy.category_retired` | Taxonomy Node `deprecated → merged` (merge completion) OR hard_retire after 90-day window OR Controlled-Vocabulary Tag `deprecated → merged_into_existing` | (webhook only) | No | No | Per transition | Payload includes `retirement_path` and `migrated_consumer_row_counts`. |
| `taxonomy.node.updated` | Editorial edit to an `active` node (existing; §4.5.4) | (webhook only) | No | No | Per edit | Cache-invalidation signal. |
| `taxonomy.migration.completed` | Per-consumer cascade worker finishes | (webhook only) | No | No | Per completion | Customer integrations can confirm their caches are consistent. |
| `taxonomy.migration.rolled_back` | Ops rollback | (webhook only) | No | No | Per rollback | |
| `taxonomy.migration.slo_breach` | 10-min SLO breach on migration worker | Ops on-call (alert) | n/a | n/a | Per breach | Ops-only; NOT a customer webhook. |
| `taxonomy.orphan_reference_detected` | Nightly reconciliation finds orphaned FK | Ops on-call (alert) | n/a | n/a | Per detection | Ops-only. |
| `vocab_tag.approved` | Controlled-Vocabulary Tag reaches `approved` | proposing seller user, Seller Team Lead | Yes | Yes | Immediate | §4.5.5 notification; ALSO fires `taxonomy.category_added`. |
| `vocab_tag.rejected` | Controlled-Vocabulary Tag reaches `rejected` | proposing seller user | Yes | Yes | Immediate | §4.5.5 notification. |
| `vocab_tag.review_slo_breach` | Ops review SLA breach | Ops on-call (alert) | n/a | n/a | Per breach | Ops-only. |

| `capability_declaration.migrated`, `seller_profile.taxonomy_migrated`, `softwarepage.taxonomy_migrated`, `marketplace_listing.updated` | Per-consumer cascade rewrite (§27.6.3) | (webhook only) | No | No | Per consumer row batch | Existing event families extended to carry `taxonomy_migration_source_node_id` and `taxonomy_migration_successor_node_id` when cascade-triggered. |

**Frequency override rules.** All taxonomy-domain events are webhook-only or Ops-alert-only; none fire customer-facing notifications. `vocab_tag.approved` and `vocab_tag.rejected` are the only user-surfaced events in this block and respect standard user preferences.

### Marketplace-Abuse-Domain Events (Webhook + Selective User Notification — added §27.8.9)

**Catalog rule.** §27.8.9 abuse-report lifecycle events are delivered per §31 with HMAC-SHA256 signing, idempotency via `event_id`, Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve, DLQ after 5 failures, and payload ≤ 256 KB. Delivery is audience-scoped: each subscription declares `delivery_audience_scope ∈ {subject, reporter, ops}` (new §31 subscription field; see reconciliation log). Subject-audience payloads redact reporter identity; reporter-audience payloads redact subject-Org fields; Ops-audience payloads are full. User-facing notifications (in-app + email via Loops.so) are emitted in parallel to the webhooks per the table below.

| Event | Trigger | Recipient (notification) | In-App | Email | Frequency | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.filed` | Row created `ops_status=pending_review` (§27.8.9) | reporter; subject Seller Team Lead (for `medium+` severity); Ops | Yes (reporter, subject per severity) | Yes (reporter) | Immediate | Subject receives only once severity ≥ `medium` AND Ops determines notification warranted. |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.triaged` | First transition out of `pending_review` | subject Seller Team Lead (if `awaiting_seller_response` or terminal); reporter; Ops | Yes | Yes | Immediate | |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.appeal_submitted` | `appeal_status=submitted` | reporter; Ops | Yes (reporter) | No | Immediate | Subject already aware. |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.appeal_decided` | Appeal `submitted → upheld|overturned` | subject Seller Team Lead; reporter; Ops | Yes | Yes | Immediate | |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.upheld` | Terminal `upheld` from any path | subject Seller Team Lead; reporter; Ops | Yes | Yes | Immediate | Includes `closure_disposition`. |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.dismissed` | Terminal `dismissed` from any path | subject Seller Team Lead (if previously notified); reporter; Ops | Yes | Yes | Immediate | |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.auto_closed_no_appeal` | `appeal_deadline_at` expired | subject Seller Team Lead; reporter; Ops | Yes | Yes | Immediate | |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.escalated` | Transition to `escalated` | Ops management only | n/a | n/a | Immediate | Ops-only; NOT customer-visible to avoid tipping off investigation. |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.seller_banned` | Terminal `upheld` with `closure_disposition=seller_banned` | subject Seller Org Owner, Billing Admin; reporter (limited note); Ops | Yes | Yes | Immediate | Dual-signoff signatures in payload. |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.sla_breach` | Triage or resolution SLO breach | Ops on-call | n/a | n/a | Per breach | Ops-only. |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.appeal_sla_breach` | Appeal-decision SLA breach | Ops on-call | n/a | n/a | Per breach | Ops-only. |
| `marketplace.abuse_report.disposition_effect_slo_breach` | Disposition effect not applied within 5 min | Ops on-call (page) | n/a | n/a | Per breach | Ops-only. |

**Frequency override rules.** `marketplace.abuse_report.seller_banned` is operationally critical and never suppressed by DND for Org Owner and Billing Admin recipients. `marketplace.abuse_report.filed` and `.triaged` honor subject-side quiet hours but are delivered immediately to Ops. `marketplace.abuse_report.auto_closed_no_appeal` honors standard preferences.

**Delivery-audience enforcement.** Webhook subscription with `delivery_audience_scope=subject` only receives events where the subscribing Org `org_id = subject_org_id`; with `reporter`, only where `org_id = reporter_org_id`. A customer Org MAY subscribe with multiple audience scopes; Ops Org cannot subscribe to customer-facing events through the public API and instead receives Ops-audience events via internal infrastructure.

### Marketplace-Signals-Domain Events (Webhook + Seller User Notification — added §27.9)

**Catalog rule.** §27.9 Seller Signals and Buyer Opt-In events are delivered per §31.1 with HMAC-SHA256 signing, `event_id` idempotency, Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve, DLQ after 5 failures, payload ≤ 256 KB. All events carry `event_class=marketplace_signals_domain`. Seller-side notifications are plan-tier-gated at delivery time (§27.9.3): `weekly_digest_email` on Seller Growth+; `real_time_toast` and `real_time_api_poll` on Seller Scale+. Buyer-side notifications cover opt-in state changes and DSAR-cascade suppression acknowledgements.

| Event | Trigger | Recipient (notification) | In-App | Email | Frequency | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `marketplace.seller_signal.cohort_published` | k-anonymity floor met AND distinctiveness check passed for a new cohort in the Seller's scope | Seller Org (subscribing roles: `org_owner`, `seller_org_admin`, `seller_marketing_editor` read-only per §5.11) | Yes (Scale+ only via `real_time_toast`) | Yes (digest-batched on Growth+; immediate on Scale+ if channel subscribed) | Immediate on Scale+; weekly on Growth | Payload redacts buyer identity; `suppression_render_mode` field indicates any placeholder semantics for the caller. |
| `marketplace.seller_signal.cohort_refreshed` | Existing cohort's activity update passes aggregation pipeline | Seller Org | Yes (Scale+) | Yes (digest-batched Growth+) | Weekly on Growth; real-time on Scale+ | Ghost-period semantics: refresh is suppressed if prior cohort row was below k-floor in the same period (§27.9.5). |
| `marketplace.seller_signal.cohort_suppressed` | k-floor or distinctiveness veto applied to a previously-visible cohort (DSAR-cascade or buyer opt-out drop) | Seller Org | No (silent; surfaces in Dashboard as state change) | No | Eventual | Dashboard-only surface; not emailed to avoid tipping adversaries that a buyer opted out. Ops also receives an Ops-audience copy. |
| `marketplace.seller_signal.digest_ready` | Weekly digest composed AND non-empty per §27.9.6 suppression-not-empty rule | Seller Org | Yes (digest summary) | Yes | Weekly | Suppressed if the digest would be empty post-k-floor + distinctiveness + residency + vendor-opt-out filtering. |
| `marketplace.seller_signal.direct_invite.offered` | Seller composes and dispatches a Direct Invite From Cohort (Seller Scale+) | Buyer Org (recipient Workspace Owner); Seller Org (audit copy) | Yes (buyer) | Yes (buyer) | Immediate | Buyer sees anonymized cohort-justification ONLY (`offer_kind` per §27.9.8); never the underlying Signal contributors. |
| `marketplace.seller_signal.direct_invite.accepted` | Buyer accepts a Direct Invite offer | Seller Org; Buyer Org | Yes | Yes | Immediate | Triggers §27.9.4 de-anonymization with `seller_signal_de_anon_trigger=buyer_accepted_direct_invite`. |
| `marketplace.seller_signal.direct_invite.declined` | Buyer declines a Direct Invite offer | Seller Org | Yes | No | Immediate | Decline reason surfaced only if buyer selected a non-`no_reason_given` value. Applies cooldown per §27.9.8. |
| `marketplace.seller_signal.direct_invite.expired` | Offer `offer_expires_at` passed without acceptance or decline | Seller Org | Yes | No | Eventual | Ops also receives for rate-limit auditing. |
| `marketplace.seller_signal.de_anonymization_recorded` | SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink row created (§27.9.4) | Seller Org; Ops (audit) | Yes (Seller) | No | Immediate | Payload carries `seller_signal_de_anon_trigger`, `seller_signal_de_anon_legal_basis`. |
| `marketplace.buyer_signal_opt_in.changed` | BuyerSignalOptInRecord state or scope mutation (§27.9.2) | Buyer Org Owner, Org Admin; Ops (audit) | Yes | Yes (on transition to/from `revoked`) | Immediate | Scope changes also fire a silent `cohort_suppressed` on any newly-excluded cohort (DSAR-cascade). |
| `marketplace.buyer_signal_opt_in.ops_paused` | Ops applied a `paused_by_ops` transition | Buyer Org Owner, Org Admin; Ops | Yes | Yes | Immediate | Includes Ops-provided reason code and expected-resumption date if known. |
| `marketplace.seller_signal.digest_skipped_empty` | Weekly digest composition resolves to zero visible cohorts after k-floor, distinctiveness, residency, and vendor-opt-out filtering | Ops only | n/a | n/a | Per skipped digest | Silent internal-only observability event; never customer-routed. |

**Frequency override rules.** DND / quiet-hours honored for all Seller Org-addressed events EXCEPT `direct_invite.accepted` (time-sensitive commercial engagement). Buyer-addressed opt-in change events respect standard preferences. `direct_invite.expired` is emitted in a nightly sweep rather than at the exact second of expiry to avoid notification pile-ups.

**Suppression-not-empty rule (§27.9.6).** `marketplace.seller_signal.digest_ready` is NOT emitted when the digest would render zero visible cohorts. In that case a silent internal-only `marketplace.seller_signal.digest_skipped_empty` Ops-audience event is emitted for observability.

### CRM-Sync-Domain Events (Webhook + Seller User Notification — added §31.9)

**Catalog rule.** §31.9 CRM Sync events are delivered per §31.1 transport semantics with `event_class=crm_sync_domain`. Provider-facing activity writes (§31.9.8) use Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve unless the event is explicitly registered as Appendix F.2 `financial_impact`. Connection-health events and review-queue-saturation alerts use the Ops-audience fan-out AND the Seller Org fan-out concurrently. Customer-facing notifications are plan-tier-gated (Seller Growth+ for CRM Sync; Seller Scale+ for Ops-facing review-queue alerts).
