| `seller.crm_sync.field_mapping_updated` | Seller creates, updates, deletes, restores, or reorders a CRMFieldMapping | Seller Org (`seller_integrations_admin`) | Yes (batched) | No | Daily digest | High-volume configuration telemetry; immediate notification reserved for schema drift or downgrade reversal. |
| `seller.crm_sync.field_mapping_reverted_on_downgrade` | Downgrade grace expires and custom mappings revert to platform default | Seller Org (`org_owner`, `seller_org_admin`, `seller_integrations_admin`) | Yes | Yes | Immediate | Payload includes `mapping_ids[]` and the downgrade effective date. |
| `seller.crm_sync.field_mapping_schema_drift_detected` | Nightly schema-introspection job detects a provider-side field rename, type change, or deletion | Seller Org (`seller_integrations_admin`) | Yes | Yes | Daily | Connection enters `paused_schema_mismatch` if the drift affects a `required=true` mapping; otherwise informational only. |
| `seller.crm_sync.routing_rule_updated` | Seller creates, updates, deletes, restores, or reorders a CRMRoutingRule | Seller Org (`seller_integrations_admin`) | Yes (batched) | No | Daily digest | Payload carries rule id, operation, and redacted before/after snapshots. |
| `seller.crm_sync.dsar_cascade_notification` | DSAR redaction cascade completes for upstream buyer-user data in CRM activity rows | Seller Org (`org_owner`, `seller_org_admin`, `seller_integrations_admin`); Ops | Yes | Yes | Immediate | Payload chunked when affected activity ids exceed the 256 KB webhook payload budget. |

**Frequency override rules.** `seller.crm_sync.connection_revoked`, `connection_health_critical`, `review_queue_saturation`, and `activity_dead_lettered` are never suppressed by DND / quiet-hours for `org_owner` and `seller_org_admin` (operationally critical). Digest events (`activity_written`, `review_queue_item_created`) respect user-configured digest cadence. Single-event emails are rate-capped at 50/hour per Seller Org to prevent email flooding during sustained provider outages.

**Ops-audience events (no customer notification).** `seller.crm_sync.ops.compliance_hold_applied`, `seller.crm_sync.ops.compliance_hold_cleared`, `seller.crm_sync.ops.schema_drift_ops_review_required` (when drift exceeds automated-handling confidence). These are internal-only and route to the Ops dashboard per the Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100) sibling pattern.

### Ops-Console-Domain Events (Customer Notification — added §50)

**Catalog rule.** §50 Ops Console impersonation events are delivered per §31.1 with HMAC-SHA256 signing, `event_id` idempotency, Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve by default, DLQ after 5 failures, payload ≤ 256 KB, and `event_class=ops_console_domain`; events explicitly listed in the §50 outbox semantics as `financial_impact` use Appendix F.2. These events carry customer-visible surface because the Ops-to-customer trust model (§50.4.1) requires that the customer Org Owner is notified at both session open and session close — failure to deliver blocks or flags the session per §50.4.5. User-facing notifications (in-app + email via Loops.so) are emitted in parallel to the webhooks to every customer Org Owner and Billing Admin of the impersonated Org. Transactional; never opt-out-able (§50.4.1 requires customer visibility; opt-out would defeat the control).

| Event | Trigger | Recipient (notification) | In-App | Email | Frequency | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `ops_session_started` | OpsSession transitions `pending_justification|pending_quorum → active` (§50.4.3); customer notification dispatch succeeds OR enters degraded-notify mode per §50.4.5 | Customer Org Owner(s), Billing Admin(s) of `org_id_impersonated`; Ops (audit) | Yes (customer) | Yes (customer) | Immediate | Payload carries `ops_session_id`, `ops_role_at_session_open` (canonical six-role kind, §50.3.1), `justification_category`, `justification_note` (redacted to first 500 chars if longer), `requested_duration_minutes`, `effective_time_box_minutes`, `started_at`, `residency_region_at_open`. Customer-facing email subject: "Sourcera Support has started a support session on your account." Suppressed-for-DND is explicitly disabled for this event (§50.4.5). |
| `ops_session_ended` | OpsSession transitions `active → closed_by_ops|closed_by_time_box|closed_by_customer|closed_by_ops_admin` (§50.4.3) | Customer Org Owner(s), Billing Admin(s) of `org_id_impersonated`; Ops (audit) | Yes (customer) | Yes (customer) | Immediate | Payload carries `ops_session_id`, `close_reason`, `actions_taken_count`, `mutation_count`, `read_count`, `ended_at`, and a Customer-Visible Projection URL deep-linking into the customer-facing audit surface (§50.4.8). Customer-facing email subject: "Sourcera Support has ended the support session on your account." Fires even when `actions_taken_count = 0` (a zero-action session still represents access and must be disclosed). |
| `ops_session_customer_revoked` | Customer exercises the Revoke Support Access surface (§50.4.7) mid-session; OpsSession transitions `active → closed_by_customer` | Customer Org Owner, Billing Admin; Ops (paged) | Yes | Yes | Immediate | Payload carries `revoker_user_id`, `revoked_at`, `session_state_at_revocation`. Ops side receives an operational alert (never silent) because customer-initiated revocation may indicate dissatisfaction requiring Ops follow-up. |
| `ops_session_auto_closed_time_box_expired` | Time-box enforcement job closes OpsSession (§50.4.2) | Customer Org Owner, Billing Admin; Ops (audit) | Yes (customer) | Yes (customer) | Immediate | Distinct from `ops_session_ended` so customer disclosure surfaces can color-code "auto-closed" vs "ops-closed" events; payload is a superset of `ops_session_ended`. |
| `ops_session_quorum_required_requested` | OpsSession transitions `pending_justification → pending_quorum` (§50.4.4) because the intended action requires dual-control | Ops Admin quorum pool; the requesting Ops user | n/a (Ops-audience customer-facing: no) | n/a | Immediate | Ops-only; NOT customer-visible — customer is notified only when session becomes `active` per `ops_session_started`. Routes via internal Ops alert channel (PagerDuty or equivalent). |
| `ops_session_customer_notification_failed` | §50.4.5 customer-notification dispatch fails after retry exhaustion | Ops on-call (paged) | n/a | n/a | Immediate | Ops-only. Payload carries `ops_session_id`, `notification_failure_code`, and `degraded_notify_mode` state. Session behavior upon failure is governed by the policy: strict-mode (default) blocks the session from becoming `active`; degraded-notify mode permits activation with audit-flag and requires Ops Admin acknowledgement within 24h. |
| `ops_role_assignment_changed` | OpsRoleAssignment transitions `proposed → pending_quorum → active|rejected` OR `active → revoked` OR `active → expired` (§50.3.4) | Ops subject user; Ops Admin quorum pool; Ops (audit) | n/a (Ops-audience only) | n/a | Immediate | Ops-only. Customer is NEVER notified of Ops role-assignment changes (those are Sourcera-internal and do not affect the customer's Org). |

**Frequency override rules.** `ops_session_started`, `ops_session_ended`, `ops_session_customer_revoked`, and `ops_session_auto_closed_time_box_expired` are operationally critical and NEVER suppressed by DND / quiet-hours for any customer Org Owner or Billing Admin recipient. `ops_session_quorum_required_requested` and `ops_role_assignment_changed` route only to Ops audience and follow internal Ops alert preferences (PagerDuty, Ops Slack channel).

**Delivery guarantees for customer-visibility events.** Because §50.4.1 requires customer awareness at both open and close, the in-app + email fan-out for `ops_session_started` and `ops_session_ended` is subject to a stricter delivery guarantee than normal Loops.so transactional email: on email dispatch failure (bounce, template error, vendor outage), the notification subsystem writes an audit row `ops_session_customer_notification_failed` (as an internal notification-failure event tied to the OpsSession), and the OpsSession row's `customer_owner_notification_failure_code` field is set per §4.6.3 OpsSession. Customer-Org-Owner absence (zero active Org Owner users at the time of session open) escalates to Billing Admin, then to the sole Ops admin who holds Ops-Admin-escalation authority (§50.4.4); if no channel is available, the session is blocked in strict mode (default).

**No customer opt-out.** Per §50.4.1, customer recipients CANNOT disable these notifications via standard opt-out controls. Attempting to unsubscribe via a Loops.so unsubscribe link returns a confirmation page explaining the notification is transactional-critical and governed by the Sourcera Trust model; the user MAY escalate to Billing Admin / Org Owner to adjust recipient composition (changing which users are Org Owner) but MAY NOT mute the class entirely.

**Audit-copy forwarding.** Every customer-facing Ops Console event additionally writes an AuditEvent row with `actor_type=ops_actor`, `actor_role=<canonical_ops_role>`, `ops_session_id=<session id>`, and `action=<matching audit action>` per §50.5.1. These AuditEvent rows are queryable by the customer via the Billing Admin Audit View (§5.2.1.4 extended by §50.5.4) AND exported in the Customer-Visible Projection (§50.4.8), guaranteeing that customer-facing awareness of Ops activity survives even if in-app or email notification is transiently lost.

### Internal-Comment-Domain Events (Webhook + Buyer User Notification — added §25.7)

**Catalog rule.** §25.7 Internal Comment events are delivered per §31.1 transport with `event_class = internal_comment_domain` (Appendix J; added in this pass). HMAC-SHA256 signing, idempotency via `event_id`, Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve, DLQ after 5 failures, payload ≤ 256 KB. All events are strictly buyer-console-scoped: a seller-console webhook subscription MUST return HTTP 404 on attempted delivery registration for these event types (enforced via the §31 subscription-registration guard that cross-references `webhook_event_class` against the subscribing Org's console context). Payloads NEVER include the Internal Comment Post `body` or `attachment_ids[]` verbatim — subscribers receive metadata only (§25.7.10); post body must be fetched via an authenticated API call. CI gate `webhook_payload_no_internal_comment_body` asserts the generated webhook payload schema excludes `body` and `attachment_ids` fields.

| Event | Trigger | Recipient (webhook + notification) | In-App | Email | Frequency | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `internal_comment_thread.created` | POST `/v1/workspaces/{id}/internal-comment-threads` succeeds | Buyer Org webhook subscribers; thread `subscribed_user_ids[]` | No (default) | No | Immediate | Subscribers opt-in via per-user notification preferences per §29.3. Payload carries `thread_id`, `workspace_id`, `attached_to_type`, `attached_to_id`, `visibility_scope`, `created_by`. |
| `internal_comment_thread.post_appended` | POST `/v1/internal-comment-threads/{thread_id}/posts` succeeds | Buyer Org webhook subscribers; thread `subscribed_user_ids[]` | Yes | Yes (digest default) | Immediate | Respects mute-until, DND, quiet hours per §29.3. Payload carries `thread_id`, `post_id`, `author_id`, `author_role_snapshot`, `mention_count`, `attachment_count`, `post_created_at`. |
| `internal_comment_thread.mention_sent` | Internal Comment Mention row inserted (one event per mentioned user) | Mentioned user | Yes | Yes (immediate default) | Immediate | Replaces / refines the existing §29.1 `comment_mention` row for Internal Comment threads. Payload carries `thread_id`, `post_id`, `mention_id`, `mention_kind`, `expanded_from_team_id`, `expanded_from_role`. Silently suppressed at dispatch if visibility scope tightened mid-flight (§25.7.11). |
| `internal_comment_thread.resolved` | PATCH InternalCommentThread `status: resolved` succeeds | Buyer Org webhook subscribers; thread `subscribed_user_ids[]` | Yes | Yes (digest) | Immediate | Payload carries `thread_id`, `resolved_by`, `resolved_at`, `resolution_note` (truncated to 500 chars per §39). |
| `internal_comment_thread.reopened` | PATCH InternalCommentThread `status: open` (from `resolved`) succeeds | Buyer Org webhook subscribers; thread `subscribed_user_ids[]` | Yes | No | Immediate | Payload carries `thread_id`, `reopened_by`, `reopened_at`. |
| `internal_comment_thread.archived` | Manual archive OR cascade from anchor-entity archive (Appendix L.1) | Buyer Org webhook subscribers | No | No | Immediate | Logged to audit only; no end-user notification. Payload carries `thread_id`, `archive_cause ∈ {manual, anchor_entity_archived, workspace_archived}`. |
| `internal_comment_thread.visibility_changed` | PATCH InternalCommentThread `visibility_scope` mutation succeeds | Buyer Org webhook subscribers; newly-included viewers (notification) | Yes (newly-included viewers only) | No | Immediate | Newly-excluded viewers receive NO notification (silent drop per firewall rule § 25.7.10). Payload carries `thread_id`, `from_scope`, `to_scope`, `changed_by`, `included_user_ids[]`, `excluded_user_ids[]`. |
| `internal_comment_post.moderated` | Workspace Owner / Admin hard-delete with `moderated_reason` | Buyer Org webhook subscribers (audit); post author (user notification) | Yes (post author) | Yes (post author) | Immediate | Payload carries `thread_id`, `post_id`, `author_id`, `moderated_by`, `moderated_reason`, `moderated_at`. |

**Frequency override rules.** `internal_comment_thread.mention_sent` is high-salience and defaults to Immediate email for the mentioned user; respects per-user `comment_mention` frequency override (Immediate / Daily / Weekly / Never) per §29.3. `internal_comment_thread.archived` and `internal_comment_thread.visibility_changed` are audit-only for webhook; the newly-included-viewer notification path on `visibility_changed` is rate-capped at one notification per viewer per thread per 5 minutes to prevent notification storms from rapid scope oscillation. `internal_comment_post.moderated` is operationally sensitive (user's content was removed) and bypasses DND / quiet-hours for the post author.

**Webhook-to-notification mapping.** Every Internal-Comment-Domain webhook event has a corresponding user-notification policy per the table above; the notification subsystem consumes the webhook event_id as its idempotency key so that repeated deliveries do not produce repeated user notifications.

**Bridge firewall invariant.** Internal-Comment-Domain events MUST NOT be emitted from any Console Bridge Event apply handler (§25.1.2 NEVER-CARRIED). They originate exclusively from the Internal Comment Thread / Post / Mention mutation handlers in Convex. A CI gate `console_bridge_no_internal_comment_event_kinds` asserts no `event_kind` value in the Console Bridge Event enum names an Internal Comment domain event.

### Q&A-Thread-Domain Events (Webhook + User Notification — added §18)

**Catalog rule.** §18 Q&A Thread events are delivered per §31.1 transport with HMAC-SHA256 signing, `event_id` idempotency, Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve, exponential backoff, DLQ after 5 failures, and payload ≤ 256 KB. Buyer-source events are scoped to the Buyer Workspace; seller-visible delivery occurs only through §4.4.2.1 / §24.1.1 projections and re-checks NDA, phase, visibility, residency, and disqualification state at dispatch time. Webhook payloads carry metadata only; `body_markdown` and raw attachment URLs are fetched through authenticated APIs.

| `qa_thread.post_appended` | POST `/v1/qa-threads/{thread_id}/posts` succeeds | Buyer Org webhook subscribers; thread subscribers; seller projection recipients when visible | Yes | Yes (digest default) | Immediate | Payload carries `qa_thread_id`, `qa_post_id`, `author_console`, `author_role_snapshot`, `attachment_count`, `mention_count`, and `post_created_at`. | `qa_thread.attachment_quarantined` | Attachment scanner marks Q&A attachment malware-positive | Post author, Workspace Owner/Admin, Ops Security | Yes | Yes | Immediate | Operationally sensitive; bypasses quiet hours for Workspace Owner/Admin and Ops Security. |
| `qa_thread.visibility_changed` | PATCH Q&A Thread visibility succeeds | Buyer Org webhook subscribers; newly-included recipients only | Yes (newly-included only) | No | Immediate | Payload carries `qa_thread_id`, `from_visibility`, `to_visibility`, `changed_by`, `pre_flip_history_revealed`. **Frequency override rules.** Q&A mention and post notifications follow §29.3 per-user channel routing, DND, quiet hours, and frequency overrides. `qa_thread.attachment_quarantined` is operationally sensitive and bypasses quiet hours for the affected author and Workspace Owner/Admin. Empty daily digests are suppressed. Seller recipients whose NDA or visibility predicate fails at dispatch time are silently suppressed and AuditEvent `qa_thread.mention_suppressed` records the reason.

**Appendix G coverage.** Each event above has an underscore-form Appendix G row (`qa_thread_created`, `qa_thread_post_appended`, `qa_thread_mention_sent`, etc.) with the standard §51 property envelope plus event-specific ids. CI gate `appendix_c_to_appendix_g_coverage` asserts coverage.

### Defense-View-Domain Events (Webhook Only — added §13.11)

**Catalog rule.** §13.11 Defense View events are delivered as §31 webhooks to subscribed Buyer Org endpoints with HMAC-SHA256 signing, idempotency via `event_id`, Appendix F.1 `standard` retry curve, DLQ after 5 failures, and payload ≤ 256 KB. All events are strictly Buyer-Console-scoped: a Seller-Console webhook subscription attempting to register for these event types is rejected with HTTP 404 by the §31 subscription-registration guard (the Buyer-only nature of `DefenseView` is non-leak: the subscription guard returns 404, not 403). User-facing in-app and email notifications are NOT emitted — the operator triggered the action and surfacing a notification would be redundant. The webhook surface is for buyer-side integrators (e.g., procurement-ops automations) that wish to be notified when a Defense View has been generated or regenerated for a Workspace.

| Event | Trigger | Recipient | In-App | Email | Frequency | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `defense_view.generated` | First successful generation of a `DefenseView` row for a Workspace (state machine transition `(none) → generated_unopened` per Appendix L.7) | Buyer Org webhook subscribers | No | No | Immediate (one event per `DefenseView.id`) | Payload carries `defense_view_id`, `workspace_id`, `selection_record_id`, `selection_record_hash`, `confidence_score`, `aioperation_id`, `generated_at`. Dedup on `event_id` per §31.1. |
| `defense_view.regenerated` | Successful regeneration (state machine transitions `opened → regenerated_unopened`, `generated_unopened → regenerated_unopened`, or `regenerated_unopened → regenerated_unopened` self-loop per Appendix L.7) | Buyer Org webhook subscribers | No | No | Immediate (one event per regeneration) | Payload mirrors `defense_view.generated` plus `regenerated_count`, `first_regeneration_at`, `regeneration_reason_code` (canonical enum registered in Appendix J — values `operator_initiated`, `source_changed_manual_refresh`, `source_hash_mismatch_auto`, `low_confidence_retry`, `failure_recovery_retry`, `ops_force_regenerate`). The `source_hash_mismatch_auto` value is reserved for the auto-trigger path when `selection_record_hash` mutates between reads; `failure_recovery_retry` (§L.7 AC #8, `regeneration_throttle`-exempt) and `ops_force_regenerate` (Ops-forced path) may also appear on this event. |

**Frequency override rules.** Both events are webhook-only and follow standard subscriber DND / digest preferences for non-customer-facing webhook delivery (i.e., webhook is delivered immediately; subscribers MAY apply their own queueing). No event in this domain produces an in-app or email notification.

**Bridge firewall invariant.** Defense-View-Domain events MUST NOT be emitted from any Console Bridge Event apply handler (§25.1.2 NEVER-CARRIED — the `DefenseView` entity is registered as a NEVER-CARRIED row in §25.1.2). They originate exclusively from the Defense View generation / regeneration handler in the Buyer-console API layer (`GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/defense-view` and `POST …/defense-view/regenerate`). A CI gate `console_bridge_no_defense_view_event_kinds` asserts no `event_kind` value in the Console Bridge Event enum names a Defense-View-Domain event.

**Coverage invariant.** Both events are registered in Appendix G PostHog Event Taxonomy with property schemas matching the webhook payloads above as underscore-form mirrors (`defense_view_generated`, `defense_view_regenerated`); a third PostHog-only event `defense_view_regenerated_due_to_source_change` is registered to power the §13.11 surface chip without an additional webhook fan-out. CI gate `appendix_c_to_appendix_g_coverage` asserts.

### v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 Additions (2026-05-20) — Residency-Change Webhook Family {#appendix-c-v72rem-phase-5}

v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 remediation closure batch (D-RES-004 P0). All webhooks follow §31 conventions: HMAC-SHA256 signing, `event_id` idempotency, Appendix F.2 `financial_impact` retry curve, DLQ at 5, payload ≤ 256 KB. The four events are emitted as a sequenced family from a single §34.10.5.A invariant #3 5-step atomic transaction; ordering is guaranteed by the Convex transaction's commit log and the `event_seq` field on each payload (monotonically increasing within `(org_id, residency_change_id)`).

| Event Kind | Trigger | Recipient | Channel | Cadence | Payload | Retry Curve |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `org.residency_change.initiated` | §34.10.5.A invariant #3 step (ii) eligibility predicates PASS; the 5-step atomic transaction has begun | Org `org_owner` + `billing_admin`; Ops Finance dashboard; subscribed customer endpoints (Billing Admin / Org Owner role-gated subscription per §31.5) | Webhook + In-app inbox card | Idempotent on `(org_id, residency_change_id)`; emitted exactly once per residency-change attempt regardless of subsequent rollback | `{event_id, event_seq=1, org_id, residency_change_id, residency_region_old, residency_region_new, legal_entity_old, legal_entity_new, custom_sovereign_residency_label_old, custom_sovereign_residency_label_new, initiated_at, initiator_user_id, initiator_role ∈ {org_owner, enterprise_admin, ops_finance_admin}, correction_reason ∈ Appendix J residency_change_correction_reason_kind \| null}` | `financial_impact` (Appendix F.2) |
| `org.residency_change.stripe_customer_created` | §34.10.5.A invariant #3 step (iii) Stripe `Customer.create` API call returns success and the new Stripe Customer ID is captured | Org `billing_admin` + `org_owner`; Ops Finance dashboard; subscribed customer endpoints | Webhook only (no in-app; the customer-facing notification is consolidated in `org.residency_change.completed`) | Idempotent on `(org_id, residency_change_id, stripe_customer_id_new)`; emitted once per successful Stripe Customer creation | `{event_id, event_seq=2, org_id, residency_change_id, stripe_customer_id_new, legal_entity_new, residency_region_new, custom_sovereign_residency_label_new \| null, stripe_metadata: {atomic_binding_protocol: 'v7.2.0-REM-Phase-5', legal_entity, residency_region, custom_sovereign_residency_label}, created_at}` | `financial_impact` |
| `org.residency_change.stripe_customer_closed` | §34.10.5.A invariant #3 step (iv) Organization row is updated; the legacy Stripe Customer is transitioned to `closed_for_new_invoices` and appended to `stripe_customer_id_historical[]` | Org `billing_admin` + `org_owner`; Ops Finance dashboard; subscribed customer endpoints | Webhook only | Idempotent on `(org_id, residency_change_id, stripe_customer_id_closed)`; emitted once per legacy-Customer closure; NO-OP-emission with `payload.no_op=true` at Org-creation (no legacy Customer exists at first Org-creation) per §34.10.5.A invariant #3 step (v) emission contract | `{event_id, event_seq=3, org_id, residency_change_id, stripe_customer_id_closed, legal_entity_at_close, residency_region_at_close, closed_at, no_op (bool; true if Org-creation path)}` | `financial_impact` |
| `org.residency_change.completed` | §34.10.5.A invariant #3 step (v) all prior audit events have been emitted; the Convex transaction has committed atomically; the new Stripe Customer is the active billing target | Org `org_owner` + `billing_admin`; Ops Finance dashboard; subscribed customer endpoints | Webhook + Email (Loops.so `lo_org_residency_change_completed`) + In-app inbox card | Idempotent on `(org_id, residency_change_id)`; emitted exactly once at successful completion; NOT emitted on rollback (a rollback fires `org.residency_change.rollback` per Appendix F.2 financial-impact emission contract, registered as a Phase-V72REM-PH5 forward-track in §31 rollback semantics) | `{event_id, event_seq=4, org_id, residency_change_id, residency_region_new, legal_entity_new, stripe_customer_id_active, stripe_customer_id_historical_appended, completed_at, total_transaction_duration_ms, total_pending_aiops_settled_on_legacy_customer (int)}` | `financial_impact` |

**Sequencing and ordering guarantees.** The four events are emitted in `event_seq` order (1 → 2 → 3 → 4) from the same Convex transaction; consumers MAY rely on the `event_seq` ordering for state-machine reconciliation but SHOULD ALSO honor `event_id` idempotency in case of webhook delivery retries reordering arrival. The §34.10.5.A invariant #3 atomicity guarantee means no partial sequence (e.g., 1 + 2 without 3 + 4) is ever emitted on commit; a rollback at any step (i)–(iv) suppresses all four events and replaces them with a single `org.residency_change.rollback` event (forward-tracked at v7.1.0a stamp with the same retry curve).

**PostHog mirror.** Every Phase-5 webhook event above is registered in Appendix G PostHog Event Taxonomy `org.residency_change.*` family with property schemas matching the webhook payloads (Appendix C → Appendix G coverage gate `appendix_c_to_appendix_g_coverage` asserts at deploy time per Appendix C coverage invariant).

**Bridge firewall invariant.** Phase-V72REM-PH5 events do NOT cross the Console Bridge. Residency-change events are Org-scoped and emitted to the Org's `billing_admin` + `org_owner` regardless of console (Org-Settings is a platform-wide surface, not a console-scoped surface per §1.3); the events carry no per-Console payload and do not register a `console_bridge_event_kind` enum value. CI gate `console_bridge_no_residency_change_event_kinds` (§M.5 forward-track at v7.1.1 stamp per the §M.5.17 sibling-gate registration pattern) asserts.

**Loops.so transactional templates.** Two templates register with this Phase 5 closure:
- `lo_org_residency_change_blocked` — fires on HTTP 409 `org_residency_change_eligibility_predicate_violated` from §34.10.5.A invariant #3 step (ii). Variables: `{org_id, residency_region_attempted, violated_predicates[], remediation_steps[]}`. Recipient role-gate: Org Owner + Enterprise Admin (the initiator). Subject line authored under AE-V72REM-PH5-01 (UX Lead authoring pending v7.1.1 stamp; placeholder: "Action needed: Your data residency change is blocked").
- `lo_org_residency_change_completed` — fires from `org.residency_change.completed` webhook payload. Variables: `{org_id, residency_region_old, residency_region_new, legal_entity_new, completed_at, stripe_customer_id_active, customer_invoice_history_link}`. Recipient role-gate: Org Owner + Billing Admin. Subject line authored under AE-V72REM-PH5-01 (placeholder: "Your data residency change is complete").

Both templates are registered in the Loops.so transactional template registry (operational layer; not duplicated in this Master Spec body) and bound to §34.10.5.A invariants #3 and #6 via the Authority anchor `Phase 5 D-RES-004 closure → Appendix C v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 block`. Deploy-time presence-verification of both templates in the Loops.so account is the responsibility of the M11.3 implementation pack's Loops.so reconciliation worker (the existing Loops.so template-deploy step runs in CI per the v7.1.0a hot-patch stamp pipeline). A spec-side CI gate `loops_so_template_completeness` covering all spec-registered Loops.so transactional templates is forward-tracked for authoring at v7.1.1 stamp under the D-RES-007 / D-LSO-N1 cluster (the Loops.so registry has additional v7.1.0 + V12 + V13 templates that share the same completeness assertion pattern; consolidating gate authoring across the cluster avoids per-Phase gate duplication).

### v7.2.0-REM Phase 10 Additions (2026-06-14) — §12 Policy Ingestion Webhook Catalog-Completeness {#appendix-c-v72rem-phase-10}

v7.2.0-REM Phase 10 spec-wide catalog-completeness sweep — closes the Appendix C portion of the §12 Policy Ingestion cluster (catalog-class P1 defects **D-12-004**, **D-4.3-008**). §12 produced no webhook contract; Appendix C previously carried only the user-notification `policy_ingestion_complete` (not a customer webhook). Each event below conforms to §31: HMAC-SHA256 signing, `event_id` idempotency, Appendix F backoff, DLQ after 5 failures, payload ≤ 256 KB. Every event uses the **`standard`** webhook retry class (Appendix F.1) per the §F.1 default-coverage rule — none is financial-impact. `webhook_event_class = product_domain`. PostHog mirrors registered in Appendix G `v7.2.0-REM Phase 10` block (`appendix_c_to_appendix_g_coverage` asserts). **Console-firewall note:** every event below is **Buyer-Org-scoped** (Policy Ingestion is a buyer-console-only surface; §12 has no seller projection). No event crosses the Console Bridge; no `console_bridge_event_kind` value is registered; recipients are the uploading Buyer Org's webhook subscribers only — no marketplace-domain or seller-domain fan-out. **Cross-cohort naming reconciliation:** D-4.3-008 used a `policy.*` namespace with alternative leaf names (`policy.framework_detected`, `policy.extraction.completed`, `policy.amendment.proposed/approved/rejected`, `policy.published_to_workspace`); the canonical family below is `policy.ingestion.*` aligned to the Appendix L.9 job-status transitions, and the D-4.3-008 names are recorded as aliases in the Notes column so both defects close against one registered event set.

**Shared payload schema (all `policy.ingestion.*` events).** `{ event_id, occurred_at, org_id, workspace_id, policy_ingestion_job_id, policy_document_id, policy_framework_kind (nullable until detected), policy_framework_confidence (float, nullable), policy_framework_confidence_band (nullable), control_count (int, nullable), merged_count (int, nullable), discarded_count (int, nullable), error_code (Appendix I `policy_*` code, nullable) }`. Per-event key fields noted inline. Signed per §31; dedup on `event_id`.

| Event | Trigger (Appendix L.9 transition) | Recipients | In-app | Email | Retry curve | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `policy.ingestion.queued` | `(none) → parsing` | Buyer Org subscribers | No | No | `standard` (F.1) | Upload accepted; `policy_ingestion_job_id` minted. Alias: D-4.3-008 `policy.ingestion.queued`. |
| `policy.ingestion.framework_detected` | `parsing → framework_detected` | Buyer Org subscribers | Yes | No | `standard` (F.1) | Carries `policy_framework_kind`, `policy_framework_confidence`, `policy_framework_confidence_band = high`. Alias: D-4.3-008 `policy.framework_detected`. |
| `policy.ingestion.framework_pending_user` | `parsing → framework_detected` (low/unknown branch) | Buyer Org subscribers | Yes | No | `standard` (F.1) | Fired when `policy_framework_inference_outcome ∈ {low_confidence_pending_user, unknown_pending_user}`; surfaces §12.3.3 confirmation modal. |
| `policy.ingestion.extraction_completed` | `extracting → dedup_pending` | Buyer Org subscribers | No | No | `standard` (F.1) | Carries `control_count`. Alias: D-4.3-008 `policy.extraction.completed`. |
| `policy.ingestion.extraction_partial` | `extracting → dedup_pending` (token-limit condition) | Buyer Org subscribers | Yes | No | `standard` (F.1) | Token-limit partial result per §12.4.2; carries `control_count` + `error_code = policy_ingestion_extraction_token_limit_exceeded`. Full partial-resume engine semantics are D-12-007 (out of catalog scope). |
| `policy.ingestion.extraction_failed` | `extracting → failed` | Buyer Org subscribers | Yes | Yes | `standard` (F.1) | Carries `error_code`. Alias: D-4.3-008 `policy.ingestion.failed` (failure family). |
| `policy.ingestion.dedup_completed` | `dedup_pending → dedup_resolved` | Buyer Org subscribers | No | No | `standard` (F.1) | Carries `merged_count`, `discarded_count`. Alias: D-4.3-008 `policy.dedup_pending` (lifecycle). |
| `policy.ingestion.amendments_drafted` | `mapping → amendments_drafted` | Buyer Org subscribers | Yes | Yes | `standard` (F.1) | Email to Workspace Owner with amendment summary (§12.7.2). Alias: D-4.3-008 `policy.amendment.proposed`. |
| `policy.ingestion.published` | `amendments_drafted → completed` | Buyer Org subscribers | Yes | No | `standard` (F.1) | Fired on batch "Close & Publish"; carries published-requirement count. Alias: D-4.3-008 `policy.published_to_workspace`. |
| `policy.ingestion.discarded` | `* → failed` (user cancel / discard) | Buyer Org subscribers | No | No | `standard` (F.1) | User-cancelled or discarded upload. |
| `policy.ingestion.failed` | `* → failed` (terminal error) | Buyer Org subscribers | Yes | Yes | `standard` (F.1) | Terminal failure not covered by `extraction_failed`; carries `error_code`. |

**Per-amendment lifecycle events** (`policy.amendment.approved`, `policy.amendment.rejected` per D-4.3-008) are intentionally **PostHog-only** (Appendix G `v7.2.0-REM Phase 10` block) to avoid per-amendment webhook fan-out on large batches; the batch-level `policy.ingestion.published` carries the aggregate outcome. This mirrors the §6.1-sweep PostHog-only treatment for high-cardinality lifecycle events.

### v7.2.0-REM Phase 8.3 Notification Catalog P1 Additions (2026-06-21) {#appendix-c-v72rem-phase-8-3-notification-catalog-p1}

This block closes the residual P1 notification-catalog defects from the Phase 8.3 family. It is an Appendix C index only; source behavior remains in the owning sections named in each row. All webhook rows follow §31 transport: HMAC-SHA256 signing, `event_id` idempotency, Appendix F retry-class binding, DLQ after 5 failures, and payload <= 256 KB. Rows marked "notification only" use §29.3 preference routing and §41 email dispatch rather than Appendix F webhook retry.

## Appendix D: Response Status State Machine {#appendix-d-response-status-state-machine}

**State Diagram:**

pending ──→ draft ──→ submitted ──→ locked

                         │              ↑

                         └→ needs\_reverification ──→ submitted (re-verified) ──→ locked

**Complete State Transitions:**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| pending | draft | Vendor opens response form | Response form accessed; no data required | Initial state when requirement released to vendor. |
| draft | submitted | Vendor clicks "Submit" | All required fields populated per response type | Buyer notified. Response locked from further vendor edits (until amendment). |
| submitted | locked | Phase 9 entry (Submissions Closed) | Automatic on phase advancement | Vendor cannot edit response. |
| submitted | needs\_reverification | Requirement amended (Amendment Protocol, Phases 6-9) | Buyer amends requirement via Amendment Protocol | Vendor notified. Response status changes. Existing submission moved to archive. New empty response created (`pending`). |
| needs\_reverification | draft | Vendor re-opens response to amend | Vendor clicks "Edit" on amended requirement | Vendor must re-verify against amended requirement. |
| draft (amended) | submitted (amended) | Vendor re-submits amended response | All required fields populated per amended response type | New version created. Buyer notified. |
| submitted (amended) | locked | Phase 9 entry | Automatic | Vendor cannot edit. |
| pending \| draft \| submitted \| needs\_reverification | locked | `disqualification_cascade` (§25.3.3) | Parent Bid Workspace transitions to `disqualified` (§25.3.7 / §25.3.8); bulk-lock cascade worker writes `lock_reason = disqualification_cascade` on every affected row | Distinct from Phase-9 `submitted → locked`: the lock_reason differentiates the two paths so dashboards, QA tests, and `disqualification_reversed` cascade can filter. Reversal within 72h restores rows whose `lock_reason = disqualification_cascade` back to their pre-disqualification status; rows already Phase-9-locked remain `locked`. |

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- All response status transitions logged to audit trail.  
- Vendor cannot submit incomplete responses (validation prevents Submit button click).  
- Amendment-triggered re-verification clearly communicated to vendor (banner in response form).
- Disqualification-originated lock MUST stamp `lock_reason = disqualification_cascade` per the row added above; reversal MUST only unlock rows whose `lock_reason = disqualification_cascade` (§25.3.13 AC #14). CI test `response_lock_reason_disqualification_reversal_integrity` asserts.

## Appendix E: Workspace & Bid Workspace Status State Machine {#appendix-e-workspace-bid-workspace-status-state-machine}

### Workspace Status (Buyer Console)

**Enum.** Appendix J `workspace_status`: `draft`, `active`, `suspended`, `closed`, `archived`.

**State Diagram:**

draft ──→ active ──→ closed ──→ archived

active ──→ suspended ──→ active

active ───────────────→ archived

| Transition | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (none) → draft | Workspace shell created before first evaluation open | Caller can create Workspace per §5.11 | Draft is not an active pipeline phase; `pipeline_phase` is null until activation. |
| draft → active | Workspace Owner opens the first evaluation | Required Workspace fields complete; `pipeline_phase` initializes to `phase_1_stakeholder_alignment` | Enters the §10 pipeline. |
| active → suspended | Platform or Ops hold pauses the Workspace | Billing, security, legal, or abuse hold recorded in AuditEvent; no customer self-serve trigger | Pipeline timers pause; writes requiring phase advancement are blocked until resumed. |
| suspended → active | Hold cleared | Clearing actor has Ops authority or the blocking condition is resolved | Pipeline resumes at the same `pipeline_phase`; timers re-anchor per the hold-resolution audit row. |
| active → closed | Phase 13 closure confirmed | §10.13 Phase Gate Rules satisfied; immutable Selection Record created | Canonical Phase 13 Workspace lifecycle transition. Workspace remains read-only; vendors retain permitted read-only projections. |
| active → closed | Workspace Owner invokes §10.18 no-vendor-response abort | §10.18.1 eligibility predicate satisfied; `closure_reason=no_vendor_response`; no Selection Record exists | Non-destructive cold-pipeline closure. Requirements, Use Cases, vendor-discovery artifacts, and invitation audit remain retained for future M4 reuse; no §10.14 cancellation or recovery window is created. |
| active → archived | Workspace Owner manually archives before formal closure | Workspace Owner confirms archive; no pending destructive operation | Allowed for abandoned or duplicate evaluations; preserves audit trail and pipeline_phase snapshot; sets `Workspace.archived_at=now()` in the same transaction. |
| closed → archived | Workspace Owner archives after closure OR retention/archive policy runs after the closure dwell window | Workspace `status=closed`; Selection Record exists and is immutable | Archive hides the Workspace from default Buyer-console lists; read access follows §40.2 retention; sets `Workspace.archived_at=now()` if the field is null. |
| archived → active | Workspace Owner restores within archive recovery window | Recovery window open; no purge job executed | Restores pre-archive `pipeline_phase` and read/write affordances allowed by current phase gates; clears `Workspace.archived_at` in the same transaction. |
| archived → (terminal purge) | Retention purge job | §40.2 retention window elapsed OR §10.14 deletion process completed | Hard delete / cold-storage transition per retention policy. |

### Bid Workspace Status (Seller Console)

**State Diagram:**

draft ──→ active ──→ submitted ──→ closed

  │          │            │

  │          │            │

  ↓          ↓            ↓

disqualified (terminal absent reversal; reversal returns to prior state — see §25.3)

| Transition | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| draft | NDA accepted by vendor | Vendor accepts NDA in Phase 4 | Bid Workspace auto-created. Initial status `draft`. |
| draft → active | Phase 5 entry (Bid Acceptance) | Buyer marks vendor as accepted | Bid Workspace unlocks. Vendor can view all requirements and begin responding. |
| active → submitted | Phase 9 entry (Submissions Closed) | Automatic phase advancement | Vendor console hard-locked. No further edits. |
| submitted → closed | Phase 13 entry (Closed) | Automatic phase advancement | Bid Workspace archived. Read-only access. Responses available for KB import. |
| draft → disqualified | `disqualification_cascade` (§25.3.3) | Vendor disqualified pre-Phase-5 activation; `bid_workspace_id` exists (uncommon; disqualification in Phases 3–4 when Bid Workspace already materialized but not yet active) | §25.3.4 freeze applies; vendor never sees an `active` Bid Workspace. |
| active → disqualified | `disqualification_cascade` | Disqualification during Phases 5–11 | Mainline path. §25.3.4 four-layer freeze; Response bulk-lock per Appendix D; scoring exclusion; vendor banner + notification per §25.3.6 / §25.3.8. |
| submitted → disqualified | `disqualification_cascade` | Disqualification during Phases 9–11 | Responses already locked from Phase 9 (`lock_reason=phase_9_submissions_closed`); disqualification adds scoring-exclusion, banner, notification. |
| disqualified → active \| submitted \| draft (prior) | `disqualification_reversed` | Workspace Owner reverses within 72h OR Ops reversal beyond 72h | Restores to pre-disqualification state per §4.7.2 Reversal; §25.3.4 freeze lifted; bridge emits reversal event. |
| disqualified → (terminal) | — | `disqualified` is terminal absent reversal | Phase 13 (Closed) on the parent Workspace does NOT transition a `disqualified` Bid Workspace to `closed`; archive integrity preserved per §4.7.2 AC #12. |

### Target Account Status (Vendor Curation)

**State Diagram:**

invited ──→ nda\_pending ──→ active ──→ closed

                   │

                   └───────→ withdrawn

                   

active ──────────→ disqualified

| Transition | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| invited | Phase 3 entry (Vendor Curation) | Target Account created | NDA not yet sent. Vendor not yet invited. |
| invited → nda\_pending | NDA link sent to vendor | Buyer sends NDA | Waiting for vendor signature. |
| nda\_pending → active | Vendor signs NDA, Phase 5 entry | Phase 5 (Bid Acceptance) required for activation | Bid Workspace unlocked. Vendor can respond. |
| nda\_pending → withdrawn | Buyer retracts NDA (before vendor signs) | Buyer withdraws vendor from evaluation | Vendor notified. Bid Workspace not created. |
| active → disqualified | Buyer marks vendor as disqualified | Any phase after Phase 5 | Vendor notified. Bid Workspace marked read-only. Responses archived. |
| active → closed | Phase 13 entry (Closed) | Automatic | Target Account archived. |

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- All status transitions logged with timestamp and user attribution.  
- Status changes trigger appropriate email notifications.  
- Phase locks prevent invalid transitions (e.g., cannot mark as active before NDA).

## Appendix F: Webhook Retry & Recovery {#appendix-f-webhook-retry-recovery}

**Default coverage rule (Phase 13 inline fix F-4.1 — 2026-04-26; v7.2.0-REM D-8.2-005 reconciliation — 2026-06-21).** Every webhook event registered in Appendix C (Notification Event Catalog), §31.1 (general event types), §31.8 (billing-domain events), §31.9 (CRM Sync events), §22.18 (KB Export events — `kb.export.ready`, `kb.export.failed`), §27.x / §29.x / §50.x (Marketplace, notification dispatch, Ops events), OR any future webhook authored anywhere in this Spec is governed by the **standard retry curve in §F.1 below** UNLESS explicitly listed in §F.2 (Financial-Impact Curve). Authoring a new webhook event without an explicit retry-class assignment defaults to standard. The deploy-time validator `webhook_default_retry_class` (Phase 13 follow-on) asserts every catalog-registered webhook resolves to either F.1 (default) or F.2 (explicit override). New event-type proposals attempting to introduce a third webhook retry class MUST author it as a new §F.x subsection with rationale, MUST register the class membership in Appendix J `webhook_retry_class`, and MUST update §M.5 `webhook_default_retry_class` in the same change. At v7.2.0-REM D-8.2-005 close, the live webhook taxonomy is intentionally binary: `standard` and `financial_impact`.

**No inline timing rule.** §F.1 and §F.2 are the only normative homes for webhook retry timing. Body sections, Appendix C rows, and Appendix G rows cite the retry class (`standard` or `financial_impact`) instead of restating delays. Non-webhook retry schedules, such as §25.2.2 `bridge_apply_standard`, Loops.so email dispatch retries, Stripe charge retries, DNS probes, or provider reconnect backoff, MUST be labeled as non-webhook schedules and MUST NOT be added to Appendix J `webhook_retry_class`.

### F.1 Standard Retry Curve

**Retry Schedule:** 5 delivery attempts total over 2 hours 36 minutes. `delivery_attempt` includes the initial delivery (attempt 1) and is therefore bounded to 1-5 per §31.2 / §31.5. Historical five-delay variants such as `1m / 5m / 30m / 2h / 12h` are retired for webhook transport because they imply six deliveries when combined with the initial attempt.

| Attempt | Delay from Previous | Cumulative | Condition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Immediate | 0 min | Initial delivery |
| 2 | 1 minute | 1 min | If attempt 1 fails |
| 3 | 5 minutes | 6 min | If attempt 2 fails |
| 4 | 30 minutes | 36 min | If attempt 3 fails |
| 5 | 2 hours | 156 min (2.6 hrs) | If attempt 4 fails |

After 5 failures, the webhook is marked `failed`. Org Admin is notified via email. Failed webhooks available for manual retry from Settings → Integrations → Failed Webhooks (30-day retention).

**Success Criteria:** HTTP 2xx response within 10 seconds. HTTP 5xx responses and network / timeout failures trigger the next retry. HTTP 3xx follows the §31.6 one-redirect rule and then fails according to the resolved response class. HTTP 4xx is terminal and does not consume the retry budget per §31.6 / §31.7.

**Idempotency:** Each delivery includes unique `event_id`. Consumer must deduplicate. Same `event_id` delivered multiple times must produce idempotent result.

**Payload Signing:**

signature \= HMAC-SHA256(webhook\_secret, raw\_request\_body)

Header: X-Sourcera-Signature \= "sha256=" \+ hex(signature)

Consumer must verify signature before processing.

**Dead Letter Queue (DLQ):** Permanently failed deliveries (after 5 retries) stored in DLQ. Org can query DLQ via Settings → Integrations → Failed Webhooks. DLQ entries retained 30 days, then purged.

**Webhook Consumer Contract:**

- Accept HTTP POST request (JSON body).  
- Verify HMAC-SHA256 signature.  
- Deduplicate by `event_id`.  
- Process idempotently.  
- Return 2xx within 10 seconds.  
- If processing fails (internal error), return 5xx (will trigger retry).  
- If payload invalid (malformed), return 4xx (will NOT retry).

### F.2 Tightened Retry Curve for Financial-Impact Events (§31.8)

A subset of billing-domain and financially material marketplace-discovery events require accelerated first-retry latency because consumer accounting reconciliation depends on near-real-time confirmation of financial movements. The event-types below use the **financial-impact retry curve** in place of the standard curve above:

- `billing.ai_operation.reversed`
- `billing.wallet.auto_topup_executed`
- `billing.wallet.auto_topup_failed`
- `billing.wallet.topup_settled`
- `billing.wallet.suspended`
- `billing.wallet.closed`
- `billing.contest.abandoned`
- `billing.contest.rejected`
- `billing.contest.withdrawn`
- `billing.referral.credit_issued`
- `billing.referral.credit_redeemed`
- `billing.referral.forfeited`
- `billing.referral.revoked`
- `billing.pro_trial_seat.converted`
- `billing.committed_spend.renewed`
- `billing.committed_spend.expired`
- `billing.committed_spend.renewal_opted_out`
- `billing.committed_spend.decommitted`
- `billing.pricing_table.rolled_back`
- `featured_placement.revoked`

| Attempt | Delay from Previous (Standard) | Delay from Previous (Financial-Impact) | Cumulative (Financial-Impact) | Condition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Immediate | Immediate | 0 sec | Initial delivery |
| 2 | 1 minute | 5 seconds | 5 sec | If attempt 1 fails |
| 3 | 5 minutes | 1 minute | 65 sec | If attempt 2 fails |
| 4 | 30 minutes | 15 minutes | 16 min 5 sec | If attempt 3 fails |
| 5 | 2 hours | 1 hour | 1 hr 16 min 5 sec | If attempt 4 fails |

After 5 failures, DLQ behavior matches the standard curve (per §F.1 above): webhook marked `failed`, Org Admin + Billing Admin notified within 1 hour, manual retry available from Settings → Integrations → Failed Webhooks (30-day retention).

**Rationale.** Customer accounting systems integrating with the Billing Ledger MUST observe wallet credit/charge events within ≤ 2 minutes of the financial mutation to satisfy SOC-2 internal-control timing claims. The standard 1-minute → 5-minute retry curve produces a worst-case 6-minute delay across the first three attempts; the financial-impact curve produces a worst-case 65-second delay across the first three attempts (covering ~99.5% of transient consumer-side failures per Phase 2 reliability data). Consumers operating against the financial-impact curve MUST budget for the higher peak attempt rate (5 attempts within 1 hour 16 minutes vs. 2 hours 36 minutes).

**Class membership rule.** A new event is added to the financial-impact class IF AND ONLY IF its successful processing is required for accounting-period close OR for active customer-facing balance display. New event-type proposals MUST cite this rule in their authoring section. Class membership is registered in Appendix J `webhook_retry_class` enum.

**Backwards compatibility.** Consumers that observed events on the standard curve before the §31.8 catalog publication continue to receive standard-curve deliveries for `billing.wallet.overage_cap_changed`, `billing.wallet.auto_topup_config_changed`, `billing.contest.filed`, and `billing.contest.decision_received` (the four Phase 4c interim events). The financial-impact curve applies only to the event-types named above; this is non-breaking for existing subscribers.

## Appendix G: PostHog Event Taxonomy {#appendix-g-posthog-event-taxonomy}

### Required Standard Property Set (Appendix G Preamble) {#appendix-g-standard-property-set}

This preamble formalizes the property envelope every first-party PostHog event MUST carry regardless of family. It is the binding contract referenced by §51.2 (Standardized Event Properties), §50.2 (Ops Console analytics isolation), §31.8 (webhook-to-PostHog dual-emit), and the PostHog outbox validator. Events that cannot populate a required property MUST populate the nullability sentinel documented below or they will be rejected at the outbox validator with `usage_event_envelope_violation` (Appendix I).

**Required properties (every PostHog event).**

| Property | Type | Nullability | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `org_id` | UUID | Non-null for Org-scoped events; `null` ONLY for Sourcera-internal Ops events emitted to the Ops PostHog project (§50 Appendix G subsection) | Tenant identity. On dual-emitted Ops-to-customer events, `org_id` is the impersonated Org, not the Ops user's home Org. |
| `console` | enum `console_kind` (Appendix J) — `buyer`, `seller`, `ops`, `public_api`, `system_job` | Non-null | Canonicalizes the surface on which the event originated. Cross-console leakage is a console-firewall violation (§25) and is blocked at the validator. |
| `workspace_id` | UUID | Nullable when the event is Org-scoped rather than workspace-scoped | When populated, MUST resolve to a Workspace whose `org_id` matches the event's `org_id`. |
| `user_id` | UUID | Nullable for system-emitted events (cron, webhook replay, job runners); redacted on DSAR | When populated, MUST resolve to a User within the event's `org_id`. Redaction sentinel on DSAR is `redacted_user_<short_hash>` per §51.7.3. |
| `phase` | enum `workspace_phase_kind` (Appendix J) | Nullable when the event is not workspace-scoped | Resolves to the Workspace's current phase at event emission time. |
| `entity_ref` | JSON `{kind: entity_ref_kind, id: UUID}` (Appendix J) | Nullable when the event has no single anchoring entity | When populated, `kind ∈ entity_ref_kind` (§51.2.1) and `id` resolves to the canonical row; the dashboards use this for drill-through. |
| `capability_id` | UUID | Nullable for non-AI events; non-null for every AI-capability invocation event and every `usage_*` event tied to a CapabilityRegistryEntry | Cardinality-bounded by the CapabilityRegistryEntry registry (target ≤ 200). |
| `capability_domain` | enum `capability_domain_kind` (Appendix J; 13 values) | Nullable when `capability_id` is null | Canonical domain-tag used for grouping panels (discovery, drafting, analysis, review, ingestion, scoring, intelligence, reporting, compliance, authoring, retrieval, ops_surface, billing_surface). |
| `plan_tier_buyer` | enum `plan_tier_kind` (Appendix J) | Nullable when `console ∈ {seller, ops, public_api, system_job}` | The Org's buyer-plan tier at emission time. |
| `plan_tier_seller` | enum `plan_tier_kind` (Appendix J) | Nullable when `console ∈ {buyer, ops, public_api, system_job}` | The Org's seller-plan tier at emission time. |
| `residency_region` | enum `residency_region_kind` (Appendix J) | Non-null | `us`, `eu`, or `custom_*` per §40.4. Used for residency-partitioned storage and cross-residency firewall enforcement. |
| `legal_entity` | enum `legal_entity_kind` (Appendix J) | Non-null | The Sourcera legal entity handling the event; bound to `residency_region`. |
| `schema_version` | string (semver) | Non-null | Schema contract version for the event envelope; increments break the validator until dashboards are updated. |
| `sampling_rate` | decimal ∈ {1.0, 0.1, 0.01} | Non-null | Identifies whether the event was 1:1 emitted or sampled; dashboards apply inverse weighting. |
| `idempotency_key` | string | Non-null | `(event_name, entity_ref.id OR org_id + emitted_at, capability_id)` or equivalent SHA-256 hash when tuple is non-trivial; exactly-once delivery is enforced downstream by this key. |
| `emitted_at` | timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC) | Non-null | Server-clock timestamp at outbox enqueue; distinct from `received_at` which PostHog assigns. |

**Optional canonical property set (event-family-specific).** `seller_org_id`, `buyer_org_id`, `bid_id`, `knowledge_object_id`, `ai_operation_id`, `wallet_id`, `ops_session_id`, `time_saved_minutes`, `accept_reject_status`, `conversion_factor_version`, `cost_usd_cents`, `duration_ms`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `model_name`, `residency_partition_violation_code`. Every optional property has a single canonical type registered in Appendix J when enum-bounded.

**Cardinality discipline.** PostHog property cardinality limit is 1,000 distinct values per property. The following properties are deliberately bounded and protected by a CI-gate that fails the build if a new enum value is added without Appendix J registration: `console`, `capability_domain`, `plan_tier_buyer`, `plan_tier_seller`, `residency_region`, `legal_entity`, `phase`, `entity_ref.kind`, `model_name`, `accept_reject_status`, `console_kind`. The following properties are unbounded and MUST NOT be used for person-level property sync to avoid cardinality explosion: `org_id`, `workspace_id`, `user_id`, `capability_id`, `wallet_id`, `ai_operation_id`, `ops_session_id`, `knowledge_object_id`, `bid_id`, `idempotency_key`, `emitted_at`. These are event-level properties only.

**Validator contract.** The PostHog outbox validator (`UsageEventValidator`, §51.2.5) runs the following checks at emit time: (1) every required property present per this preamble; (2) every enum-bounded property matches an Appendix J value; (3) `residency_region` matches the Org's current residency binding or one of the Org's declared-residency values; (4) `org_id`/`workspace_id`/`user_id`/`capability_id` tuple resolves to a consistent tenancy graph (no cross-org leakage); (5) `console ∈ {buyer, seller}` events emit only into that console's PostHog project (console-firewall integrity); (6) `idempotency_key` is non-null and ≤ 512 characters. A validator failure emits `usage_analytics_envelope_violation` (with the failing property path) and drops the event into the envelope DLQ (§51.7.5). Validator enforcement is blocking for `mutation=true` events (billing-tied usage events, AI operations, time-saved credits) and non-blocking (warn-and-emit) for `mutation=false` reads during the first 30 days of any new event family's deployment window, after which the validator becomes blocking.

**Nullability sentinels.** When a required field cannot be populated because the row is unknown at emission time (e.g., an envelope-violation event has no anchoring `capability_id`), the validator accepts the well-known sentinel `__unresolved__` for string-typed fields and `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` for UUID-typed fields; dashboards treat these as "unresolved" and surface them to Ops observability (§51.2.5 CI-gate).

**DSAR redaction.** `user_id` is field-level redacted (not row-deleted) on DSAR per §51.7.3; the redaction sentinel is `redacted_user_<short_hash>` where `short_hash` is the first 8 characters of SHA-256(`user_id` + Org DSAR pepper). This preserves the cohort shape for the dashboards while erasing the identity. Retention periods are defined in §40.2 and §51.7.5 by event family, not per-row.

**Schema-version discipline.** Any change to this preamble (addition, type change, nullability change, enum extension) increments `schema_version` on every affected event family. Dashboards MUST declare their supported `schema_version` range; events outside the range render in the "Instrumentation Drift" observability surface and do not contaminate customer-facing dashboards.

PostHog event `name` is the canonical identifier; webhook `event_type` and PostHog `name` MAY differ where the prompt-specified PostHog name is shorter than the webhook canonical form. | `upgrade_completed` | Customer confirms a plan upgrade (companion to §31.8.5 `billing.plan.upgraded` webhook) | `plan_from`, `plan_to`, `console_affected`, `trigger` (per Appendix J `upgrade_completed_trigger`: `evaluation_limit`, `vendor_limit`, `ai_budget_exhaustion`, `opus_gated_capability`, `solo_envelope_pressure`), `time_from_first_cta_view_seconds` (correlates with prior `upgrade_cta_viewed` events), `cta_view_count_before_completion`, `prorated_amount_cents` |
| `solo_trial_started` | 90-day Solo migration trial enters `active` (mirror of Appendix C `billing.solo_trial.started`) | `trial_state_id`, `trial_kind`, `console`, `plan_from`, `plan_trial`, `trial_started_at`, `trial_expires_at`, `legal_entity`, `source_migration_version` |
| `solo_trial_expiry_notice_sent` | Day 80 or day 89 Solo migration trial expiry notice is dispatched (mirror of Appendix C `billing.solo_trial.expiry_notice_sent`) | `trial_state_id`, `trial_kind`, `console`, `plan_trial`, `trial_expires_at`, `notice_kind`, `days_remaining`, `legal_entity`, `source_migration_version` |
| `solo_trial_ended` | 90-day Solo migration trial converts, auto-downgrades, cancels, or expires unaccepted (mirror of Appendix C `billing.solo_trial.ended`) | `trial_state_id`, `trial_kind`, `console`, `plan_from`, `plan_trial`, `plan_to`, `trial_started_at`, `trial_expires_at`, `trial_outcome`, `downgrade_bucket_summary`, `legal_entity`, `source_migration_version` |
| `solo_upgrade_cta_triggered` | §44.6.5.A Solo throttling-pressure aggregation writes the redacted CTA trigger event (mirror of Appendix C `billing.solo_upgrade_cta.triggered`) | `solo_upgrade_cta_trigger_id`, `console`, `plan_from`, `plan_to`, `solo_upgrade_cta_trigger_mode`, `source_event_id`, `envelope_window_id`, `rolling_window_started_at` (nullable), `cta_surface`, `cta_copy_variant` |

**Property cardinality budget.** PostHog property cardinality limit is 1,000 distinct values per property. The high-cardinality properties above are `capability_id` (bounded by `CapabilityRegistryEntry` count, target ≤ 200), `wallet_id` (one per Org, currently target ≤ 50K total Orgs), and `ai_operation_id` (cardinality unbounded; PostHog stores these as event-level properties NOT person-level properties to avoid cardinality explosion). `payment_method_last4` is bucketed to "redacted" for all DSAR-erased rows.

**Trigger taxonomy.** The `upgrade_completed.trigger` enum is the canonical attribution for upgrade conversion analysis. It is set on the customer's confirmation click and carried through Sales-Ops dashboards. The allowed values map to the upgrade-pressure points in §34.5.1 + §34.5.4 + §34.8: hitting an `evaluation_limit` (workspace count cap), hitting a `vendor_limit` (per-workspace vendor count cap), hitting `ai_budget_exhaustion` (wallet hard-cap or overage-cap exhaustion), attempting an `opus_gated_capability` (Opus-tier-only capability invocation per CapabilityRegistryEntry.`plan_gate_min_tier=enterprise`), or upgrading from a Solo throttling-pressure trigger (`solo_envelope_pressure`). Multi-trigger upgrades record the most-proximate trigger (the one that produced the click); secondary triggers are surfaced via the `cta_view_count_before_completion` field.

**Correlation requirement.** Every `upgrade_completed` event MUST be correlatable to ≥ 1 prior `upgrade_cta_viewed` event for the same `org_id` within the prior 30 days. Conversion funnel analysis (PostHog Insights → Funnels) uses `upgrade_cta_viewed → upgrade_completed` with `org_id` as the funnel key. Orphan `upgrade_completed` events (no prior CTA view) are flagged in the analytics dashboard for investigation (typically Sales-Ops manual provisioning per `change_origin=sales_ops_provisioned`).

### KB / MCP / Managed-Agent Events (added §22.9–§22.16)

The events below mirror operational signals from the §22 Knowledge Base and the Sourcera KB MCP Server; they feed the §22.16.4 dashboards (Ops Console). Standard property set: `org_id`, `seller_org_id`, `bid_workspace_id` (nullable), `capability_id`, `session_id` (nullable), `agent_definition_version`, `console=seller`. DSAR-erased rows redact `bid_workspace_id` to `redacted`.

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `kb_retrieve_invoked` | `kb_retrieve` MCP tool call returns to the agent | `pipeline_stage_latency_ms` (object keyed by stage 1–8), `top_k`, `degraded_mode` (Boolean), `rerank_skipped` (Boolean), `dense_candidates_count`, `bm25_candidates_count` |
| `kb_retrieve_zero_results` | `kb_retrieve` returns `top_k=[]` | `query_normalized_hash`, `allowed_namespace_count`, `exclude_review_states[]`, `degraded_mode` |
| `cite_verify_failed` | `cite_verify` returns `valid=false` | `kb_entry_id`, `reason` (per Appendix J `cite_verify_reason`), `agent_self_check_round` (1=agent-side, 2=server-side post-emit) |
| `agent_emit_draft_repeated_rejection` | ≥ 3 `emit_structured_draft` rejections on the same `requirement_id` within a session (§22.11.1) | `requirement_id`, `rejection_reasons[]`, `final_action` (`escalated_to_manual_review`, `agent_self_recovered`) |
| `agent_query_pre_expanded` | `kb_retrieve` invoked with a query containing synonym-expanded tokens that the §22.9.5 server-side expansion would have produced (§22.17 AC #24) | `expanded_tokens_detected[]`, `agent_definition_version` |
| `agent_compaction_anomaly` | > 1 `agent.thread_context_compacted` events observed within a single First-Pass session (§22.16.2) | `compaction_count`, `session_id`, `requirements_in_batch_count` |
| `agent_max_turns_exhausted` | `session.status_idle` with `stop_reason=max_turns` (§22.15.1) | `requirements_processed`, `requirements_outstanding`, `parent_ai_operation_id` |
| `kb_injection_suspected` | `kb_injection_scanner` flags an entry on ingestion (§22.16.7) | `kb_entry_id`, `injection_pattern_matched[]`, `held_for_review` (Boolean) |
| `managed_agent_session_started` | `client.beta.sessions.create` returns 200 (§22.14, §22.15.2) | `agent_definition_version`, `environment_version`, `vault_id` (hashed), `parent_ai_operation_id` |
| `managed_agent_session_completed` | `session.status_idle stop_reason=end_turn` reaches the orchestrator | `duration_ms`, `tokens_input`, `tokens_output`, `cache_read_input_tokens`, `requirements_processed`, `compaction_count`, `mcp_tool_call_count` |
| `managed_agent_session_terminated_unexpectedly` | `session.status_terminated` without prior recovery (§22.15.5) | `failure_reason`, `requirements_outstanding`, `last_processed_event_id` |
| `kb_health_dashboard_viewed` | Seller user opens KB Health Dashboard (§22.5.3) | `surface=ui_kb_health_dashboard`, `view_duration_seconds`, `entries_in_active`, `entries_in_review_due`, `entries_in_flagged_stale` |

**Property cardinality budget.** `kb_entry_id` and `requirement_id` are unbounded; PostHog stores as event-level properties only. `query_normalized_hash` is a SHA-256 truncated to 12 hex chars to protect query confidentiality while retaining cardinality control. `agent_definition_version` is bounded by §22.10.7 update cadence (target ≤ 200 per agent across history).

**Correlation requirement.** Every `kb_retrieve_invoked` carries `parent_ai_operation_id` so dashboards can join to the §4.8.1 AIOperation ledger; every `cite_verify_failed` carries the same `parent_ai_operation_id` plus `agent_self_check_round` so the §22.16.1 layered-enforcement diagnosis is reconstructable end-to-end.

### KB Value Capture & Stake-Building Events (added §22.18)

Events below instrument the §22.18 KB Value Capture & Stake-Building surfaces (Seller Panel, Honest Portability export, Stake-Reveal Moments). Standard property set: `org_id`, `seller_org_id`, `user_id` (nullable; redacted on DSAR), `console=seller`, `plan_tier` at emit time, `bid_workspace_id` (nullable), `session_id` (nullable). All events carry `event_class=kb_value_capture_domain`. Events fire on every plan tier including Free (§22.18.1 P1 "No-Paywall Export" and P4 "Carry-Over Surfaces Honesty").

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `kb_value_meter_viewed` | KB Value Meter Seller Panel (§22.18.4) first becomes visible in the viewport on the Seller KB home surface, after-bid outcome debrief, or at-conversion-threshold review (frequency-capped at one emission per `(seller_org_id, user_id, view_surface, calendar_day)` tuple to bound cardinality) | `view_surface ∈ {seller_kb_home, outcome_debrief_overlay, conversion_threshold_review, upgrade_confirmation, downgrade_preview}`, `panel_position_states[]` (array of the 5 rendering positions per §22.18.4.1 — each entry is `{position_id, visible_value, visible_cta_kind}`), `kb_entry_count_at_view`, `cited_in_closed_bids_count_at_view`, `win_rate_lift_at_view_pct` (nullable if below k-anon floor), `estimated_value_display_usd_cents`, `health_percent_at_view`, `plan_tier_at_view`, `view_duration_seconds` (UI measurement; null for server-side synthetic view events), `triggering_referrer ∈ {direct_nav, command_palette, bid_outcome_debrief, conversion_moment_modal, upgrade_flow, downgrade_flow}` |
| `kb_value_meter_click_through` | User clicks a KB Value Meter explainer (§22.18.4 click-through explainers) OR a deep-link CTA on the panel | `view_surface`, `position_id` (1–5 per §22.18.4.1), `click_target ∈ {explainer_confidence, explainer_staleness, explainer_win_rate_weighting, explainer_citation_graph, explainer_capability_autodecl, deep_link_kb_health_dashboard, deep_link_kb_entry_list_cited_in_closed_bids, deep_link_kb_export}`, `time_on_panel_ms`, `target_entity_id` (nullable; populated when click resolves to a specific `kb_entry_id` or `capability_id`) |
| `kb_export_initiated` | `POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/kb/export` returns HTTP 202 (§32.9.1) | `export_id`, `format ∈ {markdown_zip_v1, jsonl_zip_v1, markdown_and_jsonl_zip_v1}` (Appendix J `kb_export_format_kind_enum`), `namespace_filter ∈ {all, selected}`, `namespace_ids_count`, `include_archived`, `include_drafts`, `include_attachments`, `include_citation_graph`, `include_confidence_history`, `plan_tier_at_initiation` (captured at emit for §22.18.1 P1 parity assertions — analytics MUST observe Free-tier initiations in the stream), `source ∈ {seller_console_ui, api_token, managed_agent_kb_exporter}`, `requested_by_user_id`, `entries_total_estimate`, `estimated_archive_bytes`, `residency_region`, `idempotent_replay=boolean` |
| `kb_export_completed` | KBExportJob `running → ready` state transition per §22.18.2.5 / §32.9.1 | `export_id`, `format`, `plan_tier_at_completion`, `archive_bytes`, `archive_sha256_prefix` (first 12 hex chars; SHA for forensic audit without leaking the full content hash into PostHog's unbounded string index), `entries_exported`, `documents_exported`, `attachments_exported`, `citation_edges_exported`, `generation_duration_seconds`, `residency_region` |
| `kb_export_failed` | KBExportJob `queued|running → failed` (§22.18.2.5) | `export_id`, `failure_code` (enum per §32.9.1 error table), `retryable=boolean`, `plan_tier_at_failure`, `failure_phase ∈ {dispatch, fetch, serialize, compress, upload, integrity_check}`, `elapsed_ms`, `residency_region` |
| `kb_export_download_url_minted` | GET §32.9.2 returns with a newly minted `download_url` (each mint is an emission; per-job rate-limited to 10 mints total) | `export_id`, `mint_sequence_number` (1-based), `download_url_expires_at`, `download_remaining_mints_after`, `residency_region` |
| `kb_export_archive_downloaded` | S3 edge reports successful download of the archive (edge access log stream routes to PostHog via the §33.9 presigned-URL-fetch observability pipeline) | `export_id`, `archive_bytes`, `download_duration_ms`, `download_ip_hash` (SHA-256 truncated 12 hex; IP retention policy per §40 PII redaction), `mint_sequence_number_at_download` |
| `stake_reveal_rendered_kb_value_capture` | Alias-emission adjunct — fires alongside `stake_reveal_rendered` whenever the renderer is operating in a KB Value Capture surface (§22.18.6 Moments 1–3) so §22.18 analytics can filter without forcing an `OR` over two canonical events | `reveal_moment ∈ {free_tier_kb_landing, outcome_debrief, conversion_threshold}`, `canonical_event_id` (foreign reference to the `stake_reveal_rendered` emission), `kb_entry_count_on_reveal`, `cited_in_closed_bids_rendered`, `free_ceiling_warning_rendered`, `upgrade_cta_visible=false` |

**`reveal_moment` property extension on canonical `stake_reveal_rendered` / `stake_reveal_displayed` events.** Per §22.18.6.4, the canonical `stake_reveal_rendered` event (and its legacy `stake_reveal_displayed` alias during the v7.0.x dual-emit window) carries an additive property `reveal_moment ∈ {free_tier_kb_landing, outcome_debrief, conversion_threshold}` (enum per Appendix J `kb_stake_reveal_moment_enum`). The extension is backward-compatible: consumers that do not observe `reveal_moment` continue to receive all prior-contract properties. At v7.1.0 the `stake_reveal_displayed` alias retires and only `stake_reveal_rendered` carries `reveal_moment`. A deploy-time validator (`kb_stake_reveal_moment_enum_closed`, §22.18.7 AC #76) asserts that no emitter writes a value outside the closed enum. Analytics dashboards using `reveal_moment` for segmentation MUST tolerate null values for pre-v7.0.0 historical rows.

**Property cardinality budget.** `export_id`, `target_entity_id`, `canonical_event_id`, `requested_by_user_id`, `download_ip_hash`, `archive_sha256_prefix` are unbounded; PostHog stores as event-level properties only. `reveal_moment` is bounded to 3 values (Appendix J `kb_stake_reveal_moment_enum`). `view_surface` is bounded to 5 values. `click_target` is bounded to ~10 values. `failure_code` is bounded to the §32.9.1 error-catalog cardinality. `format`, `namespace_filter`, `failure_phase`, `source`, `residency_region`, `plan_tier_*`, `triggering_referrer`, `position_id` are all enum-bounded. `cited_in_closed_bids_count_at_view`, `kb_entry_count_at_view`, `entries_exported`, `archive_bytes`, `generation_duration_seconds`, `download_duration_ms` are integers within conventional range.

**Correlation requirement.** Every `kb_value_meter_click_through` MUST carry `position_id` matching one of the 5 positions in the preceding `kb_value_meter_viewed` event's `panel_position_states` array (funnel key `seller_org_id + user_id + view_surface + calendar_day`). Every `kb_export_completed` and `kb_export_failed` MUST join back to a prior `kb_export_initiated` via `export_id`. Every `kb_export_archive_downloaded` MUST join back to a `kb_export_download_url_minted` via `(export_id, mint_sequence_number)`. Every `stake_reveal_rendered_kb_value_capture` MUST carry `canonical_event_id` pointing to the same-timestamp `stake_reveal_rendered` emission (enforced at the analytics-ETL layer).

**Plan-tier parity assertion.** Analytics dashboards include a daily invariant check `kb_export_free_tier_nonzero_when_population_nonzero`: if the population of Free-tier Seller Orgs is ≥ 50 in the 30-day window AND the observed count of `kb_export_initiated` events with `plan_tier_at_initiation=seller_free` is 0, the dashboard pages the Ops-on-call rotation because a §22.18.1 P1 regression is strongly suspected (the endpoint MUST succeed on Free, so nonzero usage is the healthy default). Population-floor prevents false positives in early Seller-Free adoption.

**Residency partition.** All KB Value Capture events partition by the Seller Org's `residency_region` at emit time. Cross-region events are not expected for KB Value Capture; Ops investigates any cross-region correlation as a potential data-residency breach.

**Correlation to §22.18 conversion analysis.** The KB Value Meter click-through funnel is `kb_value_meter_viewed → kb_value_meter_click_through → (optional) upgrade_cta_viewed → upgrade_completed` keyed by `seller_org_id`; PostHog Insights → Funnels queries the chain with a 30-day conversion window. The Stake-Reveal moment funnel is `stake_reveal_rendered{reveal_moment=X} → (optional) upgrade_completed{trigger=...}` keyed by `seller_org_id` and filtered by `reveal_moment`. The Honest-Portability usage funnel is `kb_export_initiated → kb_export_completed → kb_export_archive_downloaded` keyed by `export_id`; dashboards surface Free-vs-paid usage parity and median archive size distribution.

**`kb_citation_in_closed_bid_attributed` event registration.** *(V13 D-51-013 remediation 2026-05-12.)* Fires when a KBEntry is cited by a bid response that subsequently reaches a closed-bid outcome (won, lost, or withdrawn). Payload schema: `{seller_org_id, kb_entry_id, bid_workspace_id, cited_at, bid_closed_at, bid_outcome ∈ {won, lost, withdrawn}, response_id, citation_count_in_bid, kb_entry_confidence_at_citation, kb_entry_first_cited_in_closed_bid_at (nullable; populated only on first attribution per `kb_entry_id`)}`. Trigger contract: fires exactly once per `(kb_entry_id, bid_workspace_id)` pair at the bid-close transition (§13 Phase 13 → terminal). Idempotency key: `(kb_entry_id, bid_workspace_id)`. The event is referenced by §51.5.3 KB Utilization Panel + §51.5.6 AC-9 integration test (`kb_citation_in_closed_bid_attributed` join to bid outcome with 10 synthesized bids); the prior §51 cross-reference asserting this event was "registered under `kb_core` event family" was non-binding — V13 makes the registration canonical. Cardinality bound: `kb_entry_id` per-event-row only; PostHog stores as event-level property. DSAR cascade: pseudonymized via standard pattern. Residency: partition by Seller Org's `residency_region` at emit time. CI gate `kb_citation_in_closed_bid_attributed_registered` (§M.5 — new) asserts schema canonicity and idempotency-key uniqueness.

**Property cardinality budget.** `growth_loop_execution_id`, `template_id`, `bid_workspace_id`, `vendor_email_domain_hash` are unbounded; PostHog stores as event-level properties only. `loop_id` is bounded to 10 values (Appendix J `growth_loop_id`). `signal_class` is bounded to ~11 values (§48.4.10). `qualitative_label_bucket_version` is bounded to deployment-version count.

**Correlation requirement.** Every `growth_loop_l*_*` event MUST carry `growth_loop_execution_id` linkable to the §48.2.12 GrowthLoopExecution row. Every loop-conversion event (e.g., `growth_loop_l5_upgrade_completed`) MUST carry the upstream `triggering_event_id` for funnel analysis. SIM `sim_signal_emitted` events MUST carry `triggering_event_ids[]` so analysts can join from a SIM flag back to the source events that produced it.

The `cta_view_count_before_completion` property now includes M8-curve CTA renders, preserving §34.5.1 attribution semantics.

**Property cardinality budget.** `seller_org_id`, `buyer_org_id`, `cohort_id`, `offer_id`, `user_id`, `ops_user_id` are unbounded. `seller_plan_tier`, `suppression_render_mode`, `suppression_cause`, `seller_signal_de_anon_trigger`, `seller_signal_de_anon_legal_basis`, `offer_kind`, `decline_reason`, `buyer_signal_opt_in_state`, `buyer_signal_opt_in_scope`, `region_inclusion_policy`, `redaction_profile`, `reason`, `cohort_size_bucket` enums are bounded per Appendix J. `buyer_org_id_opaque_token` is bounded pre-acceptance (opaque UUID) and resolves to `buyer_org_id` in the `direct_invite_buyer_accepted` event only.

**Residency partition.** Seller-scoped events partition by Seller Org residency. Buyer-scoped events (`buyer_signal_opt_in_*`) partition by Buyer Org residency. `seller_signal_de_anonymized` partitions by Seller Org residency AND carries `buyer_residency` as a correlated property for cross-residency audit (Ops-only dashboards).

Activity events MUST be correlatable to their triggering Sourcera event (EOI, Signal cohort accept, bid-workspace transition) via a top-level `source_event_id` property.
