### §48.6 M9–M13 Marketplace Content Mechanics — Event Additions {#appendix-g-section-48-6-additions}

The events registered below are emitted by §48.6 (M9–M13 Public Marketplace Content Mechanics) AND the cross-mechanic editorial, takedown, and k-anonymity render-gate infrastructure shared across M9–M13. All events partition by principal entity residency region at emit time (§4.4.12–§4.4.16 `residency_region_scope` where applicable, otherwise `ops_platform_region`). All events follow §G governance (Appendix G Property Cardinality Budget; PII redaction; PostHog outbox 24-hour retry curve with permanently-failed terminal state).

**Emission intent.** Every M9–M13 lifecycle transition, editorial-review lifecycle transition, takedown lifecycle transition, and k-anonymity render-gate evaluation emits a PostHog event from the tables below. §48.6.11 mandates 47 M9–M13-domain events plus 6 cross-mechanic events (editorial + k-anon + schema.org); the complete enumeration is authored here. All event names are normalized to underscore form (per Appendix G naming convention); any inline dot-form occurrences in §48.6 per-mechanic telemetry tables (e.g., `m9.category_page.draft_ready_for_review`) name **notification** kinds, not PostHog events, and are registered in Appendix C — the Appendix G canonical names are underscore-separated.

**Property cardinality budget (§48.6 additions).** Enum-bounded properties: `target_mechanic_kind` (`m9_category_page`, `m10_guide_page`, `m11_comparison_page`, `m12_market_intelligence_report`, `m13_heat_map_cell`, `m13_heat_map_aggregation_card`), `assigned_queue` (`m9_marketing`, `m10_marketing`, `m11_marketing`, `m12_marketing`, `m12_finance`, `m13_marketing`), `decision_kind` (Appendix J `editorial_review_decision_kind`), `archive_reason` (union across mechanics), `referrer_kind` (`organic_search`, `direct`, `social`, `internal_link`, `other`), `republish_due_to` (`refresh_cadence`, `opt_out_resweep`, `takedown_remedy`, `manual_force_refresh`), `leg` (`marketing`, `finance`), `filer_kind` (Appendix J `takedown_filer_kind`), `takedown_reason_kind` (Appendix J `takedown_reason_kind`), `requested_remedy_kind` (Appendix J `takedown_requested_remedy_kind`), `takedown_status` (Appendix J `takedown_status`), `entity_kind` (union above), `page_level_decision` (`pass`, `fail`), `sim_signal_class` (`k_anonymity_floor_violation`; extends §48.4.10 registry), `notification_channel` (`in_app`, `email`), `constraint_kind` (`per_email_24h`, `per_domain_24h`). Unbounded identifiers: `editorial_review_task_id`, `target_entity_id`, `takedown_id`, `category_page_id`, `guide_page_id`, `comparison_page_id`, `report_id`, `cell_id`, `card_id`, `superseding_takedown_id`, `superseding_vendor_org_id`, `triggering_ai_operation_id`, `triggering_opt_out_seller_software_id`, `notified_vendor_org_id`. Hashed properties: `filer_email_hash` (SHA-256; satisfies §40 PII redaction for anonymous filer events). Integer-band properties (`*_count`, `*_seconds`, `*_days`, `*_pct`) follow standard cardinality discipline.

**Residency partition (§48.6 additions).** Per-mechanic events partition by the target entity's `residency_region_scope` (M9 CategoryPage, M10 GuidePage, M11 ComparisonPage, M13 HeatMapCell) OR `residency_region_scope` (M12 MarketIntelligenceReport). Takedown events partition by the target entity's residency. Editorial-review-task events partition by the target entity's residency via FK join. Cross-region leak events (`m12_market_intel_residency_violation_aborted`, `m13_heat_map_residency_violation_aborted`) carry BOTH `attempted_residency_region_scope` and `leak_source_region` for forensics; cross-region analytics are Ops-only. Anonymous public views (`*_view_recorded`) partition by the rendered entity's residency region, not the viewer's inferred geolocation.

**Correlation requirement (§48.6 additions).** Every M9–M13 mechanic event MUST carry both the per-mechanic entity identifier and (where the event has a content version) `content_version`. Every editorial-review-task event MUST carry `editorial_review_task_id` AND `target_entity_id` AND `target_mechanic_kind`. Every takedown event MUST carry `takedown_id` AND `target_entity_id` (once triaged). Every k-anonymity render-gate event MUST carry `entity_kind` AND `entity_id`. Cross-event correlation across the editorial pipeline (AIOperation → draft generated → review task → decision → publish) uses `triggering_ai_operation_id` as the initial join key and transitions to `editorial_review_task_id` at task creation; the Ops dashboards treat a published entity lacking any of (`*_draft_generated`, `editorial_review_task_created`, `editorial_review_task_*_decision`, `*_published`) as instrumentation-broken and pages `ops_marketing_supervisor`.

**Outbox & retry semantics (§48.6 additions).** All §48.6 events route through the standard PostHog outbox per §4.3.18 with Appendix F.1 `standard`. Two classes of events use the financial-impact retry curve (Appendix F.2) because they gate downstream Outcome Resolver settlement and cost-center audit: (a) `*_editorial_decision` events across M9–M13 (used by §34.11 Outcome Resolver for `platform_marketing` cost-center settlement); (b) `editorial_review_task_sla_breached` (used by §43 P2/P3 alerting and Summary Summary §6.36 Ops dashboards). All other §48.6 events use Appendix F.1 `standard`.

### §48.7 M14–M17 Cross-Console & Seller Conversion Mechanics — Event Additions {#appendix-g-section-48-7-additions}

The events registered below are emitted by §48.7 (M14 Seller Bid Success Share, M15 Ghost-Bid Importer, M16 Buyer Referral Credit, M17 Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat). All events partition by the emitting Org's `data_residency_region`; cross-console mechanics (M17) emit one event per console with dual-projection property redaction per §4.3.17. All events follow §G governance.

**Naming convention normalization (authored extension).** The §48.7 per-mechanic telemetry tables (lines §48.7.1–§48.7.4) enumerate event names in dot-separated form (e.g., `m14.bid_success_share.initiated`). The Appendix G canonical form is underscore-separated (e.g., `m14_bid_success_share_initiated`). Emitters MUST emit the underscore form; PostHog dashboards and outbox consumers MUST consume the underscore form. The dot form is reserved for **notification** kinds (Appendix C) and webhook event kinds (Appendix C). This normalization resolves the NB-12 naming drift; the per-mechanic §48.7 tables are to be read as abbreviated notation for the underscore-normalized canonical names registered here.

The two additional M14 NB-4 events (`m14_bid_success_share_third_party_opt_out_blocked`, `m14_bid_success_share_ner_latency_breach`) are authored extensions per the Phase 4 remediation pass and are registered in RECONCILIATION.md.

**Property cardinality budget (§48.7 additions).** Enum-bounded: `origination_surface` (M14; registered in Appendix J), `fail_reason` (M14 anonymization), `match_source` (M14), `match_kind` (M14 NER), `social_platform` / `social_platform_targets[]` (Appendix J `bid_success_share_social_platform`), `revoker_kind` (M14), `source_file_kind` (M15), `failure_reason` (M15 parse), `review_action` (Appendix J `ghost_bid_import_review_action`), `rejected_by_role` (M15), `constraint_kind` (M15 velocity; M16 nothing new), `referral_invite_channel` (existing), `share_surface` (M16), `overlap_kind` (M16), `fraud_flags[]` (M16 sweep), `forfeit_reason` (Appendix J `referral_forfeit_reason`), `override_kind` (M16), `grant_plan_tier_at_issue` (existing `plan_tier` enum), `converted_plan_tier` (existing), `auto_downgraded_to_plan` (existing), `decline_reason` (M17), `revoke_reason` (M17 buyer), `fraud_flag_kind` (M17). Unbounded identifiers: `bid_success_share_id`, `ghost_bid_import_id`, `buyer_referral_id`, `pro_trial_seat_grant_id`, `colliding_ghost_bid_import_id`, `invoice_item_id`, `invoice_id`, `capability_invocation_id`, `sweep_run_id`. Hashed properties: `vendor_email_hash`, `referrer_org_domain_hash`, `referee_email_domain_hash`, `matched_token_hash`, `matched_vendor_org_id_hashed` (SHA-256 where PII); satisfies §40.

**Residency partition (§48.7 additions).** M14, M15 events partition by `seller_org_id`'s residency. M16 events partition by `referrer_org_id`'s residency (the issuing Org's residency determines Stripe balance-transaction residency). M17 events emit once per console, partitioned by each console's residency (the buyer-projection event partitions by `buyer_org_id` residency; the seller-projection event partitions by `vendor_org_id` residency once provisioned). Cross-residency grants (US buyer → EU vendor) carry `counterpart_residency_region` for audit; Ops-only dashboards query across residency partitions with Summary Summary §6.36 restrictions.

**Correlation requirement (§48.7 additions).** Every M14 event MUST carry `bid_success_share_id` AND `seller_org_id`. Every M15 event MUST carry `ghost_bid_import_id` AND `seller_org_id`. Every M16 event MUST carry `buyer_referral_id`; post-`signed_up` events MUST additionally carry `referee_org_id`. Every M17 event MUST carry `pro_trial_seat_grant_id`; post-`provisioned` events MUST additionally carry `vendor_org_id`. Cross-mechanic attribution compounding (per §48.7.6 invariant #7) uses `GrowthLoopExecution.metadata_json.cross_mechanic_attribution[]` as the join key, NOT event properties.

**Outbox & retry semantics (§48.7 additions).** `m16_referral_credit_issued`, `m16_referral_credit_applied`, `m16_referral_credit_fully_redeemed`, `m16_referral_credit_expired`, `m17_pro_trial_seat_converted`, and `m17_pro_trial_seat_auto_downgraded` use the financial-impact retry curve (Appendix F.2) because they gate Stripe invoice adjustments. `m14_bid_success_share_third_party_opt_out_blocked` uses the financial-impact curve because it gates §4.4.8 audit completeness. All other §48.7 events use Appendix F.1 `standard`.

**Property cardinality budget (§48 additions).** The following property names introduced in this subsection are enum-bounded per Appendix J registrations: `origination_surface`, `phase`, `stage`, `skip_reason`, `degradation_path_taken`, `degradation_reason`, `dismissal_method`, `navigation_method`, `close_method`, `update_reason`, `cite_kind`, `failure_category` (pre-arrival), `final_state` (pre-arrival), `moment_kind`, `triggering_entity_kind`, `cta_variant`, `re_eligibility_trigger`, `outcome` (calibration), `import_source`, `redaction_reason`, `placement_kind`, `discovery_path`, `qualifying_activity_kinds_observed`, `demotion_severity`, `constraint_kind`, `demotion_reason`, `violation_kind` (taxonomy), `action_kind` (ops_seller_action_taken), `ap_kind`, `enforcement_layer`, `reevaluation_trigger`, `prior_priority`, `status` (reevaluation), `scope` (exception grant), `reason_category`, `bottleneck_phase`, `edit_kind`, `opt_in_scope`, `opt_in_source`, `reactivation_kind`, `first_activity_kind`, `dispute_kind`, `failure_kind` (citation source), `baseline_source`, `alert_severity`, `surface` (k-anon backtest), `adversarial_simulation_result`, `recommendation` (k-anon backtest), `calibration_alert_fired`. The properties `seller_org_id`, `buyer_org_id`, `vendor_org_id`, `session_id`, `kb_entry_id`, `citation_id`, `bid_workspace_id`, `template_id`, `eoi_draft_id`, `seat_grant_id`, `bootstrap_job_id`, `invite_id`, `ghost_bid_id`, `ghost_bid_import_id`, `pro_trial_seat_grant_id`, `ops_user_id`, `caller_user_id`, `triggering_entity_id`, `grant_id`, `ops_council_session_id`, `baseline_id`, `backtest_run_id`, `stripe_invoice_id`, `edit_target_entity_id`, `citing_bid_workspace_id` are unbounded. Boolean and integer-band properties (`*_count`, `*_ms`, `*_cents`, `*_band`, `*_seconds`, `*_days`) follow standard cardinality discipline. `target_seller_domain_hash`, `source_url_hash` are SHA-256 hashes to satisfy §40 PII redaction for events fired before any Seller Org exists OR for content-source URLs.

**Residency partition (§48 additions).** All events partition by the principal Org's `data_residency_region` at emit time. Cross-residency events (e.g., a US-buyer Forced-Vendor-Signup invite resolving to an EU-seller Org post-arrival) carry `target_residency_region` as a correlated property; cross-residency analytics dashboards are Ops-only. Anti-spam and Anti-pattern enforcement events partition by the enforcement-layer's residency.

**Correlation requirement (§48 additions).** Every Hero Moment lifecycle event MUST carry both `seller_org_id` and `session_id`. Every Conversion Moment event MUST carry `session_id`, `moment_kind`, and `triggering_entity_id`. Every Network Effect event MUST carry `loop_id` (matching the §48.3.5 S1–S7 catalog). Every Anti-Pattern violation event MUST carry `ap_kind` and `enforcement_layer`. Cross-event correlation across Hero Moment → Conversion Moment → Activation Metric chains uses `session_id` as the join key; the analytics dashboard treats a session lacking any of (`seller_onboarding_session_created`, ≥ 1 `seller_onboarding_stage_entered`, `seller_activation_metric_recorded`, `seller_onboarding_first_requirement_response`) as instrumentation-broken and pages the §48.1.6 Quality-Signal Q2 alarm. During the v7.0.x dual-emit window (see Naming reconciliation table above), a session satisfying the canonical event set OR the legacy event set is treated as healthy; at v7.1.0, only the canonical event set is recognized.

**Outbox & retry semantics (§48 additions).** All §48 events route through the standard PostHog outbox per §4.3.18 with Appendix F.1 `standard`. Events that use the financial-impact retry curve (Appendix F.2) because they gate downstream billing / audit operations: `seller_aiwallet_budget_exhausted_during_onboarding` (§34.10 wallet auto-degradation engine); `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_fired` and its legacy alias `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_recorded` for `moment_kind=cm4_kb_ceiling` (§34.1 Upgrade-Carry-Over reconciler); `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_upgrade_succeeded` (Stripe subscription reconciliation); `onboarding_anti_pattern_exception_grant_issued` (§4.6.x OpsActionRecord audit integrity); `s4_baseline_staleness_breach` (Summary Summary §6.36 Ops dashboard integrity); `k_anonymity_floor_backtest_completed` (§48.4.7 calibration gate). All other §48 events use Appendix F.1 `standard`.

### §49.1 Seller Onboarding Implementation-Level Event Additions {#appendix-g-section-49-1-additions}

The events registered below are emitted by §49.1 (Seller Onboarding — Implementation-Level Seven-Stage Flow) and complement the §48.8 / §48.8.8 canonical registry. All events partition by Seller Org residency (or `invite_id`-distinct pre-SSO) and follow §G governance.

**Naming clarification with §48.8.8 canonical registry.** §49.1 uses short forms for two activation-metric events (`seller_first_requirement_response`, `seller_first_bid_submitted`) in running text to match the Summary §6.28.2 / C.135 prose. These short forms are terminology clarifications, NOT new PostHog emitters: they refer to the existing canonical `seller_onboarding_first_requirement_response` and `seller_onboarding_first_bid_submitted` events registered above. No new alias is introduced; no dual-emit is required; no CI gate changes. §49.1 AC 33 authors the compatibility contract (PostHog-funnel tests MUST resolve to the same underlying SellerOnboardingSession row regardless of which short or long form appears in dashboard queries; the short form is a human-readable alias in documentation only).

**Stage enum extension for `seller_onboarding_stage_entered`.** The existing §48.8.3 registration of `seller_onboarding_stage_entered` authored the `stage` property with domain `{1, 2, 3}` (Hero Moment window only). §49.1 extends the property domain to `{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}` to cover the full seven-stage flow. Appendix J registration (§49.1 addition) updates `seller_onboarding_stage_enum` to include values 4–7. Backward compatibility: PostHog queries filtering on `stage ∈ {1, 2, 3}` continue to work unchanged; new queries filtering on stages 4–7 access the extended domain. Property `stage_outcome` enum (`{completed, abandoned, errored}`) is unchanged. New property added: `retrieval_grounding_state ∈ {grounded, ungrounded}` (optional, Stage 3 only) per §49.1.3.

**New events (truly additive).**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `seller_onboarding_landing_rendered` | HTTP 200 on landing page | `invite_id`, `invite_source`, `render_latency_ms`, `invite_token_valid=true` |
| `seller_onboarding_landing_invalid_token` | HTTP 4xx on landing page | `invite_token_prefix` (first 8 chars; never full token for PII hygiene), `failure_reason ∈ {not_found, expired, revoked, malformed}` |
| `seller_onboarding_cta_clicked` | `stage_2_sso_initiated_at` write | `invite_id`, `invite_source`, `elapsed_seconds_since_arrival`, `cta_variant` |
| `seller_bootstrap_started` | `kb_bootstrap` job transitions to `executing` | `seller_org_id` (nullable pre-SSO), `invite_id`, `bootstrap_job_id`, `candidate_url_count`, `pre_arrival_state ∈ {complete, incomplete}` |
| `seller_bootstrap_entry_synthesized` | Each KBEntry INSERT during Bootstrap (sampled 1-in-10) | `seller_org_id` (nullable), `bootstrap_job_id`, `kb_entry_id`, `confidence_score`, `source_url`, `category_id` (nullable) |
| `seller_bootstrap_completed` | `kb_bootstrap` → `succeeded` or `partial` | `seller_org_id`, `bootstrap_job_id`, `entry_count`, `partial=boolean`, `stage_2_population_latency_ms`, `mean_confidence_score` |
| `seller_bootstrap_failed` | `kb_bootstrap` → `failed` | `seller_org_id` (nullable), `bootstrap_job_id`, `failure_reason ∈ {firecrawl_outage, opus_capability_unavailable, domain_unresolvable, robots_txt_blocks_all, content_extraction_failure, timeout}` |
| `seller_bootstrap_degraded_path_engaged` | Pre-arrival reservation failed; degraded path fires | `seller_org_id` (nullable), `bootstrap_job_id`, `degradation_reason`, `degraded_url_budget`, `degraded_depth` |
| `seller_sso_completed` | `stage_2_sso_completed_at` write | `seller_org_id`, `invite_id`, `sso_provider ∈ {google, microsoft, magic_link_fallback}`, `elapsed_seconds_since_arrival`, `org_provisioning_outcome ∈ {new_org_created, existing_org_resolved, disambiguation_required}` |
| `seller_first_pass_batch_started` | `first_pass_responses` invocation | `seller_org_id`, `bid_id`, `requirements_count`, `grounded_chunk_count`, `citation_mode ∈ {grounded, ungrounded}`, `tier ∈ {sonnet, opus_override}` |
| `seller_first_pass_response_drafted` | Each BidResponse INSERT during Stage 3 (sampled 1-in-5) | `seller_org_id`, `bid_id`, `requirement_id`, `bid_response_id`, `confidence_score`, `citation_count`, `kb_gap_signal=boolean` |
| `seller_first_pass_batch_completed` | `first_pass_responses` terminal state | `seller_org_id`, `bid_id`, `requirements_count`, `drafted_count`, `grounded_count`, `kb_gap_signal_count`, `mean_confidence_score`, `batch_latency_ms`, `terminal_state ∈ {succeeded, partial, failed}` |
| `seller_hero_moment_displayed` | Landing counter first paint (Stage 4) | `seller_org_id`, `bid_id`, `displayed_entry_count` (N), `displayed_citation_count` (M), `displayed_review_time_estimate_min` (X), `first_paint_ms`, `counter_values_match_session_row=boolean` — distinct from the computation-milestone event `hero_moment_completed` (existing); this event fires on the pixel-paint of the landing counter and carries the displayed values for AP7 client-integrity assertion |
| `seller_landing_counter_dismissed` | Seller clicks landing-counter X-close | `seller_org_id`, `bid_id`, `dismiss_elapsed_seconds_from_paint` |
| `seller_profile_first_published` | Seller Profile publication (first-bid-ever flow, Stage 6) | `seller_org_id`, `profile_id`, `kb_size_at_publish`, `capability_declaration_proposal_count` (populated after `kb_to_capability_suggestion` completes; may be 0 at publish time and updated async) |
| `stake_reveal_dwell_completed` | Seller navigates away from Stake-Reveal Screen | `seller_org_id`, `bid_id`, `dwell_seconds` |
| `seller_win_debrief_rendered` | `stage_7_win_debrief_rendered_at` write | `seller_org_id`, `bid_id`, `days_from_submission_to_win`, `insight_count_shown`, `plan_tier_at_debrief` |
| `seller_loss_debrief_rendered` | `stage_7_loss_debrief_rendered_at` write | `seller_org_id`, `bid_id`, `days_from_submission_to_loss`, `insight_count_shown`, `insight_count_gated`, `plan_tier_at_debrief`, `conversion_moment_link_rendered=boolean` |
| `seller_phase_lapsed_debrief_rendered` | `stage_7_phase_lapsed_at` write | `seller_org_id`, `bid_id`, `days_from_submission_to_lapse`, `plan_tier_at_debrief` |
| `seller_churned_post_activation` | §4.4.22 post-activation churn classifier fires | `seller_org_id`, `last_activity_at`, `days_since_last_activity`, `final_completion_state='churned_post_activation'` |
| `seller_onboarding_completed` | `stage_7_entered_at` write (Stake-Reveal exit → Stage 7 entry; terminal onboarding event) | `seller_org_id`, `bid_id`, `completion_state='activated'`, `activation_metric_elapsed_seconds`, `kb_size_at_completion`, `aiwallet_cents_consumed`, `capabilities_declared_count`, `stages_completed=[1,2,3,4,5,6,7]` — exactly-once per SellerOnboardingSession row with idempotency key `(seller_org_id, session_id)` per §49.1 AC 11 / §49.1.7 AC 40 |
| `seller_progress_storytelling_line_rendered` | Each progress-storytelling status-line render (Stages 2–3) | `seller_org_id` (nullable pre-SSO), `invite_id`, `line_id ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, degraded_1, degraded_2, degraded_3}`, `elapsed_seconds_since_arrival`, `backend_state_at_render` |

**Property cardinality budget (§49.1 additions).** `invite_id`, `bootstrap_job_id`, `bid_response_id`, `profile_id`, `kb_entry_id` are unbounded. `invite_source`, `failure_reason`, `pre_arrival_state`, `sso_provider`, `org_provisioning_outcome`, `citation_mode`, `tier` (first_pass_responses), `terminal_state`, `line_id` (progress storytelling), `completion_state`, `degradation_reason`, `cta_variant`, `final_completion_state` are enum-bounded per Appendix J (new §49.1 enum additions). Integer properties (`*_count`, `*_ms`, `*_seconds`, `*_cents`) follow standard cardinality discipline. `invite_token_prefix` is exactly 8 chars (first 8 of the token, never the full token) for PII hygiene — the full `invite_token` is NEVER emitted to PostHog. `source_url`, `category_id` may be null; when non-null, `source_url` is the full URL (not hashed) per §49.1.2 sampling convention (1-in-10 sampling caps volume so full-URL retention is feasible). `displayed_entry_count`, `displayed_citation_count`, `displayed_review_time_estimate_min` are integer-bounded by SellerOnboardingSession column semantics.

**Residency partition (§49.1 additions).** All §49.1 events partition by the seller's `data_residency_region`. Pre-SSO events (`invite_id`-keyed) partition by the invite's creation-time residency (inherited from the issuing Buyer Org). Post-SSO events (`seller_org_id`-keyed) partition by the Seller Org's residency. Residency-transition events (pre-SSO → post-SSO same session) carry both residency keys for cross-residency audit dashboards (Ops-only).

**Correlation requirement (§49.1 additions).** Every §49.1 lifecycle event MUST carry a correlatable `session_id` (post-SSO) or `invite_id` (pre-SSO); pre-SSO and post-SSO events on the same session MUST be linkable via the SellerOnboardingSession row's `invite_id` foreign key. A session lacking the canonical event set `seller_onboarding_session_created` → `seller_onboarding_stage_entered {stage=1}` → … → `seller_onboarding_completed` is treated as instrumentation-broken per §48.1.6 Q2 alarm. The dual-emit window for the existing `seller_onboarding_first_requirement_response` / `seller_onboarding_first_bid_submitted` canonical events is unchanged by §49.1 (no new alias introduced per the naming-clarification above).

**Outbox & retry semantics (§49.1 additions).** `seller_onboarding_completed` uses the financial-impact retry curve (Appendix F.2) because it is the gating event for downstream plan-progression analytics, activation-metric dashboards, and the 30-day hero-path cohort rollups; at-least-once-with-idempotency is enforced via the `(seller_org_id, session_id)` idempotency key. `seller_hero_moment_displayed` uses Appendix F.1 `standard` but MUST emit before any subsequent Stage 5 interaction event on the same session — out-of-order delivery is tolerated but a missing `seller_hero_moment_displayed` event 5 minutes after the corresponding `seller_onboarding_stage_entered {stage=4}` triggers an instrumentation-broken flag. All other §49.1 events use Appendix F.1 `standard`.

**Sampling discipline (§49.1 additions).** `seller_bootstrap_entry_synthesized` is sampled at 1-in-10 (Bootstrap averages 80 entries × 10,000 hero-path sellers/day uncapped = 800K events/day → 80K/day sampled). `seller_first_pass_response_drafted` is sampled at 1-in-5 (mean 100 requirements × 10,000 hero-path sellers/day uncapped = 1M events/day → 200K/day sampled). Sampling decisions are recorded on the event row via the Appendix G `sampling_rate` property (`0.1` and `0.2` respectively) to enable accurate dashboard unbiased-estimation computations.

### §50 Ops Console Event Additions {#appendix-g-section-50-additions}

The events registered below are emitted by §50 (Sourcera Ops Console). All events partition by the Ops PostHog project (an infrastructure-level separation from the customer PostHog project per §50.2.1 Deployment Isolation) AND are replicated into the customer analytics project with a redacted property envelope that matches the Customer-Visible Projection (§50.4.8). Ops-only events are NEVER emitted to the customer PostHog project; only the Ops-Console customer-visibility events are dual-emitted with divergent property envelopes.

**Event domain prefix.** All §50 events use the `ops_` prefix to avoid collision with the customer-facing `seller_*` and `buyer_*` namespaces. The existing growth/seller-admin events `ops_seller_action_taken`, `ops_seat_grant_issued`, and related Ops-action-record events continue to use their established names and are not renamed; §50 extends but does not replace those.

**New events (truly additive).**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `ops_session_opened` | OpsSession row INSERT into `pending_justification` state (§50.4.3) | `ops_session_id`, `ops_user_id`, `ops_role_at_session_open`, `org_id_impersonated`, `console_scope ∈ {buyer, seller}`, `justification_category`, `requested_duration_minutes`, `residency_region_at_open`, `quorum_required=boolean`, `parent_ops_session_id` (nullable; set when the session was opened during an existing Ops-Admin-escalation chain) |
| `ops_session_activated` | OpsSession transitions `pending_justification|pending_quorum → active` (§50.4.3); dispatched after customer-notification success OR degraded-notify-mode activation | `ops_session_id`, `activation_latency_ms_from_open`, `effective_time_box_minutes`, `customer_owner_notified_open_at`, `customer_owner_notification_failure_code` (nullable), `degraded_notify_mode=boolean` |
| `ops_session_closed` | OpsSession transitions `active → closed_by_*` (§50.4.3) | `ops_session_id`, `close_reason ∈ ops_session_close_reason` (enum), `actions_taken_count`, `mutation_count`, `read_count`, `session_duration_seconds`, `force_close_actor_user_id` (nullable), `auto_close=boolean` |
| `ops_session_auto_closed_time_box_expired` | Time-box enforcement job closes OpsSession (§50.4.2) | `ops_session_id`, `effective_time_box_minutes`, `actions_taken_count`, `warning_rendered_at_90_percent=boolean` (observability for §50.4.2 warning-band behavior) |
| `ops_session_customer_revoked` | Customer exercises §50.4.7 revoke surface | `ops_session_id`, `revoker_user_id`, `revoker_role ∈ {org_owner, billing_admin}`, `session_state_at_revocation`, `actions_taken_count`, `revocation_latency_ms_from_activation` |
| `ops_session_policy_enforced` | Any §50 policy-gate denial (capability outside envelope, cross-console access denied, cross-Org access denied, time-box exceeded, step-up-reauth stale, quorum required, residency-partition denial, justification invalid) | `ops_session_id` (nullable if the denial occurred before session creation), `ops_user_id`, `policy_kind ∈ ops_policy_kind_enum` (enum: `capability_outside_envelope`, `cross_console_access_denied`, `cross_org_access_denied`, `time_box_exceeded`, `step_up_reauth_stale`, `quorum_required`, `residency_partition_denial`, `justification_invalid`, `device_posture_failed`, `per_user_concurrency_exceeded`), `denied_action_kind`, `ops_role_at_denial` |

| `ops_session_quorum_signoff_granted` | Second Ops Admin co-signs a `pending_quorum` OpsSession (§50.4.4) | `ops_session_id`, `quorum_signoff_user_id`, `signoff_latency_ms_from_request`, `signoff_method ∈ {console_button, slash_command, oncall_pager_ack}` |
| `ops_session_quorum_signoff_expired` | `pending_quorum` OpsSession times out before second signoff (§50.4.4) | `ops_session_id`, `quorum_signoff_window_seconds`, `quorum_timeout_reason` |
| `ops_role_assignment_changed` | OpsRoleAssignment state transition (§50.3.4) | `ops_role_assignment_id`, `subject_ops_user_id`, `role_kind ∈ ops_role_kind` (enum: six canonical roles), `from_state`, `to_state`, `transition_trigger ∈ {proposal, quorum_signoff, rejection, revocation, expiration, emergency_grant}`, `acting_ops_admin_user_id` (nullable), `role_assignment_duration_days` (populated on expiration/revocation) |
| `ops_role_emergency_grant_issued` | Emergency Ops-Admin grant issued via break-glass (§50.3.5) | `ops_role_assignment_id`, `subject_ops_user_id`, `granted_role_kind`, `incident_id`, `pre_grant_active_ops_admin_count`, `grant_actor_user_id`, `acknowledgement_required_by` |
| `ops_capability_invocation` | Every Ops action tied to an OpsSession (1-in-N sampled for high-volume reads; 1:1 for mutations) | `ops_session_id`, `ops_user_id`, `ops_role_at_invocation`, `capability_kind ∈ ops_capability_kind` (enum), `is_mutation=boolean`, `org_id_impersonated`, `console_scope`, `latency_ms`, `sampling_rate ∈ {1.0, 0.1}` |
| `ops_impersonation_linked_action_emitted` | A customer-surface AuditEvent row is emitted while an OpsSession is active (§50.5.1) | `ops_session_id`, `audit_event_id`, `actor_type='ops_actor'`, `audit_action_kind`, `customer_visible=boolean` |
| `ops_rate_limit_override_applied` | An Ops-role-authorized rate-limit override is issued (§50.3.2 envelope row) | `ops_session_id`, `override_kind ∈ {burst_rate, monthly_quota, concurrent_session}`, `subject_org_id`, `duration_minutes`, `requested_by_user_id` |
| `ops_break_glass_db_access_invoked` | Break-glass direct-DB access invoked (Ops Security Admin only; §50.2.4 enforcement deviation) | `ops_session_id`, `incident_id`, `ticket_ref`, `invocation_actor_user_id`, `co_approver_user_id`, `data_class_accessed ∈ {customer_row, audit_row, billing_row, secrets_vault}`, `justification_text_length` |
| `ops_incident_declared` | Ops Admin declares an internal incident via §50.6 SIM surface | `incident_id`, `declaring_ops_user_id`, `severity ∈ {sev0, sev1, sev2, sev3}`, `incident_category`, `related_ops_session_ids_json` |
| `ops_incident_postmortem_published` | Postmortem doc published for a declared incident | `incident_id`, `postmortem_url_hash` (SHA-256 of the canonical URL), `severity`, `days_from_declaration_to_publish`, `action_items_count` |

**Property cardinality budget (§50 additions).** `ops_session_id`, `ops_role_assignment_id`, `audit_event_id`, `incident_id`, `org_id_impersonated`, `subject_ops_user_id`, `ops_user_id`, `revoker_user_id`, `grant_actor_user_id`, `acting_ops_admin_user_id`, `quorum_signoff_user_id`, `requested_by_user_id`, `co_approver_user_id`, `invocation_actor_user_id`, `force_close_actor_user_id`, `parent_ops_session_id`, `ticket_ref` are unbounded. Enum-bounded per Appendix J (new §50 additions): `ops_role_kind`, `ops_session_close_reason`, `ops_session_notification_failure_code`, `ops_policy_kind_enum`, `ops_capability_kind`, `ops_session_console_scope`, `ops_session_justification_category`, `denied_action_kind`, `audit_action_kind`, `role_assignment_transition_trigger`, `signoff_method`, `override_kind`, `data_class_accessed`, `incident_category`, `severity` (SEV-band). `session_duration_seconds`, `latency_ms`, `effective_time_box_minutes`, `*_count`, `*_ms_from_*`, `role_assignment_duration_days`, `quorum_signoff_window_seconds`, `pre_grant_active_ops_admin_count`, `days_from_declaration_to_publish`, `justification_text_length` are integer-band discipline. `postmortem_url_hash` is SHA-256 (never a raw URL). `related_ops_session_ids_json` is a bounded JSON array (maximum 50 IDs; truncated with `truncated=true` flag if longer).

**Residency partition (§50 additions).** All Ops events partition by `residency_region_at_open` (on OpsSession events) OR by `org_id_impersonated`'s residency at emit time (for `ops_capability_invocation` and downstream events). Cross-residency denials (`ops_session_policy_enforced` with `policy_kind=residency_partition_denial`) carry both `attempted_residency_region` and `ops_user_cleared_residency_regions_json` for audit reconstruction. Ops-role-assignment events are residency-neutral (Ops user identity is Sourcera-internal, not customer-Org-scoped); however, the `role_kind` values that grant cross-residency clearance are recorded on the assignment row and surface on the event as `cross_residency_clearance_granted=boolean`.

**Correlation requirement (§50 additions).** Every `ops_session_*` event after `ops_session_opened` MUST carry `ops_session_id`. Every `ops_capability_invocation` and `ops_impersonation_linked_action_emitted` event MUST carry both `ops_session_id` and either `audit_event_id` (for customer-surface actions) or `ops_action_record_id` (for Sourcera-internal Ops actions). Every `ops_role_assignment_changed` event MUST carry `ops_role_assignment_id` AND `subject_ops_user_id`. The analytics dashboards treat an OpsSession lacking the canonical sequence `ops_session_opened` → (`ops_session_quorum_signoff_granted`? →) `ops_session_activated` → (zero or more `ops_capability_invocation`) → `ops_session_closed` as instrumentation-broken and pages the Ops observability on-call. Sessions closed via auto-close emit both `ops_session_auto_closed_time_box_expired` AND `ops_session_closed` (superset/subset pair; dashboards deduplicate on `ops_session_id`).

**Customer-visibility replication.** The following §50 events are dual-emitted to the customer PostHog project with a redacted property envelope matching §50.4.8 Customer-Visible Projection: `ops_session_activated`, `ops_session_closed`, `ops_session_auto_closed_time_box_expired`, `ops_session_customer_revoked`. The redacted envelope includes ONLY: `ops_session_id` (opaque UUID; non-enumerating), `ops_role_at_session_open` (canonical role kind; the customer sees role but not the individual Ops user), `justification_category` (enum only; never `justification_note` or `linked_support_ticket_ref`), `started_at`, `ended_at`, `close_reason`, `actions_taken_count`, `mutation_count`, `read_count`, `residency_region_at_open`, `customer_revoker_user_id` (for revoked sessions, always populated from the customer's own user pool — no leak). Everything else — `ops_user_id`, `justification_note`, `linked_support_ticket_ref`, `quorum_signoff_user_ids`, `ip_address_origin`, `user_agent_origin`, `auth_factor_evidence_json`, `api_request_ids`, `force_close_actor_user_id`, `parent_ops_session_id` — is NEVER replicated to the customer project. Redaction is enforced at the PostHog outbox stage via an allow-list property filter; a deploy-time test asserts the customer-project event schema contains no disallowed property.

**Outbox & retry semantics (§50 additions).** `ops_session_opened`, `ops_session_activated`, `ops_session_closed`, `ops_session_auto_closed_time_box_expired`, and `ops_session_customer_revoked` use the financial-impact retry curve (Appendix F.2) because they are the audit-integrity spine of the Ops-to-customer trust model (§50.4.1) and downstream legal, compliance, and customer-disclosure surfaces depend on their at-least-once-with-idempotency delivery. `ops_session_policy_enforced`, `ops_session_customer_notification_failed`, `ops_role_emergency_grant_issued`, `ops_break_glass_db_access_invoked`, and `ops_incident_declared` also use the financial-impact curve (regulatory-audit criticality). All other §50 events use Appendix F.1 `standard`. Idempotency key for every `ops_session_*` terminal event is `(ops_session_id, event_name)`; exactly-once downstream is enforced at the dashboard-computation layer via the idempotency key.

**Sampling discipline (§50 additions).** `ops_capability_invocation` is 1:1 for `is_mutation=true` invocations and 1-in-10 sampled for `is_mutation=false` reads to control volume; sampling decisions are recorded on the event row via `sampling_rate ∈ {1.0, 0.1}` to enable unbiased-estimation dashboards. All other §50 events are 1:1.

**Dashboard partitioning.** A Sourcera-Internal dashboard surfaces Ops-session metrics at the org-wide, role-wide, and per-user levels: sessions opened, sessions auto-closed, mean time-box utilization, justification-category distribution, customer-revocation rate, policy-enforcement denial rate, quorum-signoff expiration rate, emergency-grant rate, break-glass rate, incident declaration rate, postmortem publication latency. A Customer-Admin dashboard (rendered to Billing Admin per §50.5.4) surfaces ONLY the redacted-envelope events scoped to the customer's `org_id`, showing the customer's-own Ops-access timeline, last-90-day session count, median session duration, and per-role breakdown using only the canonical `ops_role_kind` enum values.

### §51 Product Usage Analytics Event Additions {#appendix-g-section-51-additions}

The events below are emitted by §51 (Product Usage Analytics & PLG Instrumentation). They form the `analytics_meta` event family registered in the 11-canonical-family registry (§51.1.4). Every event in this subsection carries the Required Standard Property Set (Appendix G preamble) PLUS the per-event properties below; any deviation triggers `usage_analytics_envelope_violation` (Appendix I) and routes the event into the envelope DLQ (§51.7.5).

**Event-family scope.** The `analytics_meta` family is reserved for events that describe the analytics surface itself (dashboard views, panel interactions, envelope-validator signals, outbox-observability signals, DSAR-redaction signals, k-anonymity-floor signals, conversion-factor-binding signals, family-registration signals, alias-retirement signals). The `analytics_meta` family MUST NOT be used as a catch-all; any capability-invocation event is registered in the domain-specific family (`ai_capability`, `billing`, `workspace`, etc.) per §51.1.4. The customer-facing Product Usage Analytics dashboards (§51.3, §51.4, §51.5) read from BOTH the `analytics_meta` family (for dashboard-view telemetry) AND all other families (for the spend/acceptance/mix panels).

**New events.**

| Event | Trigger | Key Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `usage_dashboard_viewed` | Buyer Org-Level Usage Dashboard is rendered (§51.3) OR an API consumer invokes `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/analytics/usage/snapshot` | `dashboard_kind ∈ {org_level, user_level, seller_parity}` (registered as `usage_dashboard_kind` enum, Appendix J), `window_start`, `window_end`, `snapshot_id` (UUID of the `UsageDashboardSnapshot` row rendered), `time_saved_enabled=boolean` (whether the Time-Saved panel was visible for this Org's plan tier), `comparison_window_kind ∈ {prior_3_months, prior_90_days, custom}`, `panels_loaded_count`, `render_duration_ms`, `viewer_role ∈ {org_owner, billing_admin, workspace_owner, reviewer, seller_admin, public_api_consumer}` (registered as `usage_dashboard_viewer_role_kind`), `surface ∈ {ui_settings_usage, ui_command_palette, ui_billing_ledger_cta, api_get_usage_dashboard}` |
| `usage_dashboard_panel_interacted` | Buyer interacts with a panel (filter change, drill-through, export, date-range pick, capability-domain pivot, top-N expand) within any Usage Dashboard | `dashboard_kind`, `panel_id ∈ usage_dashboard_panel_id` (Appendix J; see §51.3.2), `interaction_kind ∈ {filter_applied, date_range_changed, drill_through_opened, export_triggered, capability_domain_pivoted, top_n_expanded, sort_changed}`, `snapshot_id`, `export_format ∈ {csv, xlsx, json}` (nullable; populated only on export interactions), `drill_through_entity_kind ∈ entity_ref_kind` (nullable), `drill_through_entity_id` (nullable), `filter_cardinality_after` (integer; number of rows the panel displays after the filter applied), `interaction_latency_ms` |
| `time_saved_panel_viewed` | Time-Saved Baseline panel renders on any dashboard (§51.6) | `dashboard_kind`, `snapshot_id`, `conversion_factor_version_set_hash` (SHA-256 of the canonical conversion-factor version tuple used at render time per §51.6.2), `baseline_assumption_version_id`, `total_minutes_saved`, `comparison_window_kind`, `domain_breakdown_json` (bounded object, ≤ 13 keys per `capability_domain_kind`), `footnote_rendered=boolean` (whether the conversion-factor-disclosure footnote was rendered at render time per §51.6.4), `panel_state ∈ {normal, conversion_factor_mismatch_suppressed, baseline_not_ready, k_anonymity_floor_hit}` |
| `time_saved_footnote_clicked` | User expands or follows a link inside the Time-Saved footnote disclosing the conversion-factor source (§51.6.4) | `snapshot_id`, `baseline_assumption_version_id`, `conversion_factor_version_set_hash`, `destination_target ∈ {baseline_assumption_version_view, conversion_factor_methodology_doc, help_center_article, internal_ops_link}`, `destination_target_path_hash` (SHA-256 of the destination path; never a raw URL) |
| `user_usage_dashboard_viewed` | User-Level Usage Dashboard is rendered (§51.4) OR `GET /v1/users/{user_id}/analytics/usage/summary` is invoked | `subject_user_id` (person whose usage is being displayed), `viewing_user_id`, `viewer_role`, `self_view=boolean` (true when viewing_user_id == subject_user_id), `snapshot_id`, `window_start`, `window_end`, `time_saved_enabled=boolean`, `accept_reject_panel_visible=boolean`, `capability_mix_panel_visible=boolean`, `k_anonymity_floor_hit=boolean` (true when subject_user_id's cohort is below k=5 and panels were suppressed per §51.7.4), `surface` |
| `seller_usage_dashboard_viewed` | Seller Usage Parity dashboard is rendered (§51.5) OR `GET /v1/seller-orgs/{seller_org_id}/analytics/usage/snapshot` is invoked | `seller_org_id`, `viewer_user_id`, `viewer_role ∈ {seller_admin, seller_billing_admin, seller_workspace_owner, public_api_consumer}`, `snapshot_id`, `window_start`, `window_end`, `bid_spend_panel_visible=boolean`, `kb_utilization_panel_visible=boolean`, `win_rate_correlation_panel_visible=boolean`, `capability_mix_panel_visible=boolean`, `k_anonymity_floor_hit=boolean`, `surface ∈ {ui_seller_settings_usage, ui_seller_command_palette, api_get_seller_usage_dashboard}` |
| `usage_analytics_envelope_violation` | PostHog outbox validator rejects an event for missing/invalid required properties (Appendix G preamble) | `violating_event_name`, `violating_property_path` (dot-path), `violation_kind ∈ {missing_required, enum_violation, type_mismatch, tenancy_mismatch, residency_mismatch, cardinality_exceeded, cross_console_leak, schema_version_unsupported}` (registered as `usage_envelope_violation_kind`, Appendix J), `attempted_org_id` (nullable; `__unresolved__` if unparseable), `attempted_console` (nullable), `validator_version`, `mutation=boolean` (determines blocking vs warn-and-emit behavior per Appendix G preamble), `sample_payload_hash` (SHA-256 of canonicalized payload; never the raw payload — payload itself is parked in the envelope DLQ for Ops review) |
| `usage_analytics_outbox_lag_budget_exceeded` | PostHog outbox lag crosses the p95 budget for Appendix F.1 `standard` OR the financial-impact curve's 30-minute alerting threshold (Appendix F.2) | `outbox_kind ∈ {standard, financial_impact}` (registered as `usage_outbox_curve_kind`), `current_lag_seconds`, `budget_threshold_seconds`, `queue_depth`, `residency_region`, `pager_triggered=boolean`, `oldest_unacked_emitted_at` |
| `usage_analytics_dsar_redaction_applied` | A DSAR field-level redaction is applied to a historical `usage_event` row (§51.7.3) | `redaction_kind ∈ {user_id_redaction, entity_ref_redaction, capability_id_redaction}` (registered as `usage_dsar_redaction_kind`), `redacted_property_path`, `rows_affected_count`, `redaction_pepper_version`, `residency_region`, `dsar_request_id`, `dsar_actor_role ∈ {subject_user, org_dpo, ops_privacy_admin}`, `dsar_verification_method ∈ {email_proof, workos_sso, ops_override}`, `redaction_latency_seconds` |
| `usage_analytics_k_anon_floor_hit` | A dashboard panel is suppressed for hitting the k-anonymity floor (§51.7.4) | `dashboard_kind`, `panel_id`, `snapshot_id`, `k_floor_kind ∈ {k5_signal, k10_aggregate, k20_market_intel}` (registered as `usage_k_anon_floor_kind`), `cohort_size_observed`, `cohort_size_floor`, `suppression_reason_category ∈ {cross_user_drill, cross_capability_drill, cross_domain_drill, cross_org_market_intel}`, `fallback_rendered=boolean` (whether the panel rendered a "not enough activity" fallback per §51.4.4) |
| `usage_analytics_conversion_factor_binding_mismatch` | A Time-Saved rollup is computed with a conversion-factor version set that does not match the bound set recorded on the `TimeSavedCredit` rows per §51.6.2 | `snapshot_id`, `expected_conversion_factor_version_set_hash`, `actual_conversion_factor_version_set_hash`, `rows_affected_count`, `drift_direction ∈ {snapshot_newer, credit_newer, parallel_fork}` (registered as `usage_conversion_factor_drift_direction`), `ops_pager_triggered=boolean`, `rollup_is_suppressed=boolean` |
| `usage_analytics_event_family_registered` | A new event-family entry is registered or updated in the 11-canonical-family registry (§51.1.4) via the Ops Console surface | `family_kind ∈ event_family` (Appendix J), `registration_action ∈ {created, updated, retired, alias_added, alias_retired}` (registered as `usage_event_family_registration_action`), `event_name_added_json` (bounded JSON array ≤ 50 items), `actor_ops_user_id`, `quorum_required=boolean` |
| `usage_analytics_alias_retirement_overdue` | An event-name alias is still emitted past its published retirement date (§51.1.6 deprecation policy) | `retired_alias_name`, `canonical_event_name`, `retirement_effective_at`, `days_overdue`, `last_emission_at`, `last_emission_source_console`, `pager_tier ∈ {tier_0_warn, tier_1_oncall, tier_2_exec}` (registered as `usage_alias_retirement_pager_tier`) |

**Property cardinality budget (§51 additions).** Enum-bounded per Appendix J (new §51 additions): `usage_dashboard_kind`, `usage_dashboard_panel_id`, `usage_dashboard_viewer_role_kind`, `usage_envelope_violation_kind`, `usage_outbox_curve_kind`, `usage_dsar_redaction_kind`, `usage_k_anon_floor_kind`, `usage_conversion_factor_drift_direction`, `usage_event_family_registration_action`, `usage_alias_retirement_pager_tier`, `event_family`, `console_kind`, `entity_ref_kind`, `plan_tier_kind`, `residency_region_kind`, `capability_domain_kind`, `legal_entity_kind`, `workspace_phase_kind`, `panel_interaction_kind`. Integer-band: `render_duration_ms`, `interaction_latency_ms`, `panels_loaded_count`, `filter_cardinality_after`, `rows_affected_count`, `cohort_size_observed`, `cohort_size_floor`, `total_minutes_saved`, `current_lag_seconds`, `budget_threshold_seconds`, `queue_depth`, `redaction_latency_seconds`, `days_overdue`. Unbounded (event-level only, never person-sync): `snapshot_id`, `baseline_assumption_version_id`, `subject_user_id`, `viewing_user_id`, `seller_org_id`, `drill_through_entity_id`, `dsar_request_id`, `actor_ops_user_id`, `retired_alias_name`, `canonical_event_name`, `expected_conversion_factor_version_set_hash`, `actual_conversion_factor_version_set_hash`, `conversion_factor_version_set_hash`, `sample_payload_hash`, `destination_target_path_hash`. Hashes are SHA-256 (never raw URLs, never raw payloads). `domain_breakdown_json` and `event_name_added_json` are bounded arrays (≤ 13 keys for domain; ≤ 50 items for event-family registration) and are truncated with a `truncated=true` flag when the cap is exceeded.

**Residency partition (§51 additions).** All §51 events carry the canonical `residency_region` property from the Appendix G preamble and partition into residency-specific PostHog projects. `usage_analytics_dsar_redaction_applied` additionally carries `residency_region` as a required property (never `null`) because DSAR pepper-version tracking is residency-scoped. `usage_analytics_outbox_lag_budget_exceeded` is emitted per residency region — a lag-budget breach in EU does NOT page the US Ops on-call and vice-versa. Cross-residency dashboard views (e.g., a customer with `residency=eu` attempting to view a `residency=us`-partitioned dashboard for a cross-residency Org) are blocked at `UsageEventValidator` with `residency_mismatch` per Appendix G preamble; a blocked access attempt emits `usage_analytics_envelope_violation` with `violation_kind=residency_mismatch` and does NOT proceed to render.

**Correlation requirement (§51 additions).** Every `usage_dashboard_viewed`, `usage_dashboard_panel_interacted`, `time_saved_panel_viewed`, `time_saved_footnote_clicked`, `user_usage_dashboard_viewed`, and `seller_usage_dashboard_viewed` event MUST carry `snapshot_id`. The analytics read-model treats any dashboard-view event missing `snapshot_id` as instrumentation-broken and pages the analytics observability on-call. `time_saved_panel_viewed` and `time_saved_footnote_clicked` MUST carry `conversion_factor_version_set_hash` AND `baseline_assumption_version_id` — the footnote disclosure (§51.6.4) is legally tied to this binding. `usage_analytics_envelope_violation`, `usage_analytics_dsar_redaction_applied`, `usage_analytics_k_anon_floor_hit`, and `usage_analytics_conversion_factor_binding_mismatch` MUST carry `validator_version` (for envelope violations) or `snapshot_id` (for dashboard-side signals) to enable post-hoc reconstruction. `usage_analytics_alias_retirement_overdue` MUST carry BOTH `retired_alias_name` AND `canonical_event_name` — dashboards treat a missing pair as instrumentation-broken.

**Customer-visibility.** `usage_dashboard_viewed`, `usage_dashboard_panel_interacted`, `time_saved_panel_viewed`, `time_saved_footnote_clicked`, `user_usage_dashboard_viewed`, and `seller_usage_dashboard_viewed` are customer-visible events (dual-emitted to the customer's analytics project with identical property envelopes — no redaction because they carry no Sourcera-internal state). `usage_analytics_envelope_violation`, `usage_analytics_outbox_lag_budget_exceeded`, `usage_analytics_dsar_redaction_applied` (beyond customer-facing confirmation surface), `usage_analytics_k_anon_floor_hit`, `usage_analytics_conversion_factor_binding_mismatch`, `usage_analytics_event_family_registered`, and `usage_analytics_alias_retirement_overdue` are Sourcera-internal events (emitted ONLY to the Ops PostHog project per §50.2.1 Deployment Isolation). DSAR confirmation to the customer is surfaced via the DSAR receipt endpoint (§6.8), not via direct PostHog customer-project emission; the Sourcera-internal `usage_analytics_dsar_redaction_applied` is strictly for Ops observability.

**Outbox & retry semantics (§51 additions).** `usage_analytics_dsar_redaction_applied`, `usage_analytics_conversion_factor_binding_mismatch`, and `usage_analytics_envelope_violation` (for `mutation=true` violations) use the financial-impact retry curve (Appendix F.2) because they are audit/legal/integrity-critical: DSAR redactions have right-to-erasure legal exposure (§6.8), conversion-factor binding mismatches invalidate Time-Saved disclosures (§51.6.4), and envelope violations on mutation events break billing reconciliation (§4.8). All other §51 events use Appendix F.1 `standard`. Idempotency key for every `usage_*` dashboard-view event is `(event_name, snapshot_id, viewing_user_id, emitted_at_minute_bucket)` — a user hammering the refresh button produces one event per minute, not one per keystroke. Idempotency key for `usage_analytics_envelope_violation` is `(validator_version, sample_payload_hash)`. Idempotency key for `usage_analytics_outbox_lag_budget_exceeded` is `(outbox_kind, residency_region, 5_minute_bucket)` to avoid alert-storm behavior.

**Sampling discipline (§51 additions).** `usage_dashboard_viewed`, `user_usage_dashboard_viewed`, `seller_usage_dashboard_viewed`, and `time_saved_panel_viewed` are 1:1 (no sampling; they are the primary PLG-adoption signals). `usage_dashboard_panel_interacted` is 1:1 for `interaction_kind ∈ {export_triggered, drill_through_opened}` (conversion-signal-critical) and 1-in-10 sampled for all other interaction kinds to control volume; the `sampling_rate` property carries the decision. `time_saved_footnote_clicked` is 1:1 (legal-disclosure telemetry). All `usage_analytics_*` meta-events are 1:1.

**Dashboard partitioning (§51 additions).** The Customer-Facing Product Usage Analytics dashboard (§51.3-§51.5) reads from the customer's PostHog project and renders buyer-console views, seller-console-parity views, and user-level views, partitioned by `residency_region` and gated by the capability domain, plan-tier, and role-matrix of §51.3.5/§51.4.5/§51.5.5. The Sourcera-Internal Analytics Observability dashboard (distinct from §50.14 Internal Analytics Dashboards by Role, which covers Ops-facing business metrics) reads from the Ops PostHog project and surfaces: envelope-violation rate by `violation_kind`; outbox-lag-budget breach rate by `outbox_kind` and `residency_region`; DSAR-redaction volume by `residency_region`; k-anonymity-floor-hit rate by `dashboard_kind` and `panel_id`; conversion-factor-binding-mismatch rate (target: zero — any non-zero is a pager event); event-family registration activity; and alias-retirement-overdue open count.

### §3 UX Token & State Catalog — Event Additions {#appendix-g-section-3-ux-additions}

Registered in the §3.6–§3.11 Authoring Pass (2026-04-22). These events instrument the UX contract surfaces authored in §3.6 Form & Input Tokens, §3.7 Loading/Empty/Error Catalog, §3.8 Side Peek, §3.9 Cursor Presence, §3.10 Bulk Action Toolbar, and §3.11 Dark Mode Parity. All events belong to the `ops_surface` event family (per §51.1.4 canonical-family registry) with `surface_kind ∈ page_surface_kind` as a qualifying dimension; any UX event crossing a per-family cardinality budget is rejected by `UsageEventValidator` with `usage_envelope_violation`. Every event carries the Required Standard Property Set (Appendix G preamble).

**Scope note.** These events are Sourcera-internal (emitted only to the Ops PostHog project per §50.2.1 Deployment Isolation) unless otherwise noted. They drive UX health dashboards, the `ux_token_contrast_check` CI gate's runtime counterpart, and the Accessibility Compliance monitoring surface. They are NOT dual-emitted to the customer analytics project.

**New events.**

| `ui_cursor_presence_hue_wrap_collision_detected` | Hue assignment wraps because >8 concurrent sessions share a surface | `workspace_id`, `surface`, `active_session_count`, `colliding_hue_token`, `luminance_delta_applied_pct` (expected ≈ 8) |
| `ui_cursor_presence_viewport_indicator_shown` | An off-screen presence's viewport indicator is rendered | `workspace_id`, `surface`, `remote_user_count_off_screen`, `overflow_chip_rendered=boolean`, `edge ∈ {top, right, bottom, left}` |
| `ui_cursor_presence_cross_console_leak_blocked` | A presence render is blocked because the remote session's console differs from the viewing console (§7.2 firewall) | `workspace_id`, `viewing_console ∈ {buyer, seller, ops}`, `remote_console`, `block_point ∈ {subscribe, render}` |
| `ui_cursor_presence_mobile_degraded_render` | Mobile device renders static avatars instead of live cursors (mobile divergence path) | `workspace_id`, `device_class ∈ {mobile_web, ios_app, android_app}`, `concurrent_session_count`, `reason ∈ {device_policy, battery_saver, reduced_data}` |
| `ui_bulk_action_selection_started` | User selects the first row of a bulk selection | `surface`, `page_surface_kind`, `initial_selection_mode ∈ bulk_action_selection_mode`, `initial_selection_count` |
| `ui_bulk_action_selection_cleared` | Selection is cleared (via X button, Escape, sort/filter change with user confirmation, or surface unmount) | `surface`, `cleared_count`, `clear_reason ∈ {user_dismiss, escape_key, navigation_away, filter_changed_confirmed, selection_capped_rejected, surface_unmount}` |
| `ui_bulk_action_shift_range_expanded` | Shift+Click expands a range selection | `surface`, `anchor_row_id`, `target_row_id`, `range_rows_added`, `total_selected_after`, `selection_mode ∈ bulk_action_selection_mode` |
| `ui_bulk_action_all_in_filter_selected` | Cmd+A or equivalent expands selection to all rows matching the active filter | `surface`, `filter_definition_hash` (SHA-256 of canonicalized filter definition), `total_matching_row_count`, `capped_at_10000=boolean`, `current_page_row_count` |
| `ui_bulk_action_cap_breach_warned` | Selection breaches the 10,000-row `all_in_filter` cap | `surface`, `filter_definition_hash`, `attempted_selection_count`, `cap_value`, `fallback_offered ∈ {export_filter_process_offline, api_only_path, retry_with_narrower_filter}` |
| `ui_bulk_action_dispatched` | Bulk action is sent to the API | `surface`, `action_kind ∈ bulk_action_kind` (registered per §3.10; 14 values spanning the action catalog), `selection_mode`, `row_count`, `destructive=boolean`, `confirmation_shown=boolean`, `idempotency_key` |
| `ui_bulk_action_progress` | Bulk action reports progress (on-dispatch subscription update) | `surface`, `action_kind`, `completed_count`, `total_count`, `elapsed_ms`, `estimated_remaining_ms` |
| `ui_bulk_action_pagination_persistence_resolved` | Selection is re-resolved after pagination or sort change | `surface`, `selection_mode`, `rows_preserved_count`, `rows_invalidated_count` (only for `visible_only` when underlying rows deleted), `rows_newly_included_count` (only for `all_in_filter` when sort reveals new rows) |
| `ui_theme_mode_switched` | User or Org changes `theme_mode` | `from_mode ∈ theme_mode`, `to_mode ∈ theme_mode`, `source ∈ theme_override_source`, `system_preference_at_switch ∈ {light, dark, no_preference}` |
| `ui_theme_mode_system_preference_applied` | Session resolves `theme_mode=system` to a concrete rendering | `system_preference ∈ {light, dark, no_preference}`, `org_default ∈ theme_mode`, `user_override ∈ theme_mode_or_null`, `resolved_mode`, `resolution_source ∈ theme_override_source` |
| `ui_theme_mode_contrast_regression_detected` | Runtime token-pair contrast check fails WCAG 2.1 AA at render time (paired with CI gate `ux_token_contrast_check`) | `theme_mode`, `surface`, `token_pair` (e.g., `color_text_primary_on_surface_elevated`), `observed_ratio`, `required_ratio`, `token_drift_commit_hash` (nullable; populated when a token-file change can be blamed) |
| `ui_theme_mode_high_contrast_enabled` | Session activates the Authored-Extension `theme_mode=high_contrast` (§3.11.8) | `trigger ∈ {user_toggle, os_preference, org_enforced}`, `prior_mode ∈ theme_mode`, `section_508_compliance_mode_enabled=boolean` |
| `ui_theme_mode_high_contrast_disabled` | Session exits high-contrast mode | `to_mode ∈ theme_mode`, `reason ∈ {user_toggle, session_expired, org_revoked, os_preference}`, `dwell_seconds` |

**Property cardinality budget (§3 UX additions).** Enum-bounded per Appendix J: `input_validation_state`, `page_state_kind`, `page_surface_kind`, `empty_state_next_best_action_kind`, `error_recovery_kind`, `side_peek_navigation_direction`, `bulk_action_selection_mode`, `theme_mode`, `theme_override_source`, `entity_ref_kind` (reused), `presence_client_device_class` (reused), `hue_1..hue_8` (reused). Integer-band: `dwell_ms`, `open_latency_ms`, `fetch_latency_ms`, `interaction_latency_ms`, `row_count`, `rows_preserved_count`, `active_session_count`, `concurrent_session_count`, `width_px`, `observed_ratio` (rounded to two decimals). Unbounded (event-level only, never person-sync): `form_id`, `field_id`, `peek_id`, `peek_target_entity_id`, `workspace_id`, `filter_definition_hash`, `anchor_row_id`, `target_row_id`, `idempotency_key`, `token_drift_commit_hash`. Hashes are SHA-256.

**Residency partition (§3 UX additions).** All events carry the canonical `residency_region` property from the Appendix G preamble. Form-input events, theme events, and page-state events partition into the residency-scoped PostHog project of the acting user's Org. Cursor-presence events partition into the residency of the Workspace's owning Org. Cross-console leak-block events (`ui_cursor_presence_cross_console_leak_blocked`) emit to the ACTING user's residency project (the would-be remote viewer), and are dual-emitted to the Ops Security project for firewall-integrity auditing.

**Correlation requirement (§3 UX additions).** Every `ui_side_peek_*` event MUST carry `peek_target_entity_kind` AND `peek_target_entity_id`. Every `ui_bulk_action_*` event MUST carry `selection_mode` (even for clear/dispatch events where selection is about to be invalidated). Every `ui_cursor_presence_*` event MUST carry `workspace_id`. Every `ui_theme_mode_*` event MUST carry the `resolution_source` OR a paired `from/to` mode tuple. Instrumentation missing these properties is treated as broken and pages the frontend-observability on-call.

**Customer-visibility.** All `ui_*` UX events in this subsection are Sourcera-internal (Ops PostHog project only). They are NOT dual-emitted to the customer analytics project. Customer-facing usage analytics (§51.3, §51.4, §51.5) consume the `ops_surface` family in aggregate form (panel counts, state-entry counts) but do NOT surface individual field-level events; an Org's session-level debug telemetry is available only through Ops with proper authorization.

**Outbox & retry semantics (§3 UX additions).** All `ui_*` UX events use Appendix F.1 `standard`. None are financial-impact-tier. Idempotency key for UX events is typically `(event_name, session_id, 1_minute_bucket, surface)` to collapse rapid-fire emissions (e.g., a user Shift+Click selecting 500 rows produces at most one `ui_bulk_action_shift_range_expanded` per minute per session per surface).

**Sampling discipline (§3 UX additions).** `ui_form_input_focus_entered`, `ui_form_input_focus_exited`, and `ui_cursor_presence_session_idled` are 1-in-10 sampled by default to control volume; all other events are 1:1. `ui_theme_mode_contrast_regression_detected` is 1:1 AND pages frontend-observability regardless of sampling — any regression is a potential WCAG compliance breach. `ui_cursor_presence_cross_console_leak_blocked` is 1:1 AND pages security-on-call — any firewall-block event is a potential §7.2 violation under investigation.

**CI-gate pairing.** `ui_theme_mode_contrast_regression_detected` is the runtime counterpart of the CI gate `ux_token_contrast_check` (§3.11.10). Zero runtime emissions is the success criterion; any non-zero rate over a 24-hour window triggers an Ops alert and a mandatory design-token regression review.

**Event class.** All events in this subsection are Sourcera-internal (buyer-Org-scoped PostHog project) and carry the standardized property set from the Appendix G preamble: `org_id`, `user_id`, `session_id`, `console = buyer`, `workspace_id`, `residency_region`, `plan_tier`, `page_surface_kind`, `client_device_class`, `client_timezone`. Cross-console leak-block events (`unread_marker_cross_console_access_blocked`, `internal_comment_cross_console_read_blocked`) are 1:1-sampled AND paged to Security on-call per §7.2 firewall-integrity invariant.

**Firewall residency partitioning.** All Internal-Comment-Domain events partition into the buyer Org's residency PostHog project. Cross-console block events dual-emit to the Ops Security project for audit. NO event in this subsection is ever emitted to a seller-Org PostHog project.

Any non-zero production emission is an incident per §42.3.

**Customer-visibility.** All events in this subsection are Ops-internal (Sourcera PostHog project only). None are dual-emitted to the customer's PostHog project (customer self-serve analytics are governed by §51).

### v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 Additions (2026-05-20) — Residency-Change Event Family + Spec-Lint CI Gate Event {#appendix-g-v72rem-phase-5}

v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 remediation closure batch (D-RES-004 P0). Five new PostHog events are registered: four mirroring the Appendix C `org.residency_change.*` webhook family per the Appendix C → Appendix G coverage gate `appendix_c_to_appendix_g_coverage`; one mirroring the §M.5.17 CI gate runtime emissions per the §M.4.5.1 audit-event schema. All events carry the Appendix G standard property set (`org_id`, `user_id`, `session_id`, `console`, `workspace_id`, `residency_region`, `plan_tier`, `page_surface_kind`, `client_device_class`, `client_timezone`) plus the event-specific properties enumerated below.

**Firewall residency partitioning.** All `org.residency_change.*` events partition into the Org's CURRENT residency PostHog project at emission time. On the `org.residency_change.completed` event (which represents the cutover moment), the event is emitted to the NEW residency PostHog project per §34.10.5.A invariant #3 step (iv) (the Org's `data_residency_region` has transitioned to the new value at step iv before step v emits the audit events). Events emitted by the Convex transaction prior to step (iv) (`org.residency_change.initiated`, `org.residency_change.stripe_customer_created`, `org.residency_change.stripe_customer_closed`) emit to the OLD residency PostHog project. This partitioning is the GDPR-compliant emission rule and aligns with §51 envelope-facing analytics binding via `legal_entity_kind`.

| Event | Trigger | Properties |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `org.residency_change.initiated` | Appendix C `org.residency_change.initiated` webhook emission per §34.10.5.A invariant #3 step (v) | `residency_change_id`, `residency_region_old`, `residency_region_new`, `legal_entity_old`, `legal_entity_new`, `custom_sovereign_residency_label_old (nullable)`, `custom_sovereign_residency_label_new (nullable)`, `initiator_user_id`, `initiator_role ∈ {org_owner, enterprise_admin, ops_finance_admin}`, `correction_reason ∈ Appendix J residency_change_correction_reason_kind \| null` |
| `org.residency_change.stripe_customer_created` | Appendix C `org.residency_change.stripe_customer_created` webhook emission per §34.10.5.A invariant #3 step (v) | `residency_change_id`, `stripe_customer_id_new`, `legal_entity_new`, `residency_region_new`, `custom_sovereign_residency_label_new (nullable)`, `stripe_api_idempotency_key`, `created_at`, `stripe_api_round_trip_ms` |
| `org.residency_change.stripe_customer_closed` | Appendix C `org.residency_change.stripe_customer_closed` webhook emission per §34.10.5.A invariant #3 step (v) | `residency_change_id`, `stripe_customer_id_closed`, `legal_entity_at_close`, `residency_region_at_close`, `closed_at`, `no_op (bool; true if Org-creation path)`, `historical_invoice_count_at_close` |
| `org.residency_change.completed` | Appendix C `org.residency_change.completed` webhook emission per §34.10.5.A invariant #3 step (v) | `residency_change_id`, `residency_region_new`, `legal_entity_new`, `stripe_customer_id_active`, `stripe_customer_id_historical_appended`, `total_transaction_duration_ms`, `total_pending_aiops_settled_on_legacy_customer (int)`, `eligibility_predicate_set_evaluated (string[])` (the §1.6.1 predicate names the transaction step (ii) evaluated to PASS — for analytics on which predicates customers most often run into) |
| `spec_lint.legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak.gate_run` | §M.5.17 `legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_test` gate execution at PR-lint + deploy_validator + runtime_test + synthetic_monitor contexts per §M.4.5.1 audit-event schema | `gate_id = 'legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_test'`, `pr_number (nullable)`, `result_status ∈ {pass, fail}`, `failure_sub_assertion ∈ {a, b, c, d, e, f} \| null`, `execution_context ∈ {pr_lint, deploy_validator, runtime_test, synthetic_monitor}`, `synthetic_op_count (int)`, `runtime_ms (int)`, `commit_sha (nullable)`, `branch (nullable)` — DUAL-EMITTED to Ops `spec-ops` project for nightly digest aggregation per §M.4.6 |

**Correlation requirement.** Every `org.residency_change.*` event MUST carry `residency_change_id` (a UUID generated at the start of the §34.10.5.A invariant #3 transaction; preserved across the four event types of a single residency-change attempt). Every `spec_lint.legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak.gate_run` event MUST carry `gate_id` AND `execution_context` AND `result_status`; instrumentation missing these properties is treated as broken and pages the spec-ops on-call.

**Sampling discipline.** All `org.residency_change.*` events are 1:1-sampled (no sampling) — residency changes are low-volume, high-business-impact events and full fidelity is required for analytics. `spec_lint.legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak.gate_run` is 1:1-sampled at `result_status = fail` (every failure is dual-emitted to Ops `spec-ops` project and triggers PagerDuty SEV-3 via the `legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_monitor` Datadog monitor); 1-in-100 sampled at `result_status = pass` (the green-run signal is dominated by passing gate runs; 1% sampling is sufficient for trend analysis).

**Datadog monitor pairing.** `spec_lint.legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak.gate_run` with `result_status = fail` is the runtime counterpart of the Datadog monitor `legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_monitor` (5-minute polling interval; alerts to the `spec-ops-oncall-rotation` PagerDuty schedule per §M.5.17 closure paragraph). Any production emission triggers Phase 5 P0 regression-investigation per §42.3 incident-response runbook.

**CI-gate pairing.** `spec_lint.legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak.gate_run` is the runtime counterpart of the §M.5.17 CI gate `legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_test`; `org.residency_change.completed` is the runtime counterpart of the §M.5.17 CI gate `legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_test` sub-assertion (b) atomic-transaction success path (a successful production residency-change emits `org.residency_change.completed`; a failed transaction emits no `org.residency_change.completed` event but instead emits the forward-tracked `org.residency_change.rollback` event registered at v7.1.0a stamp).

**Customer-visibility.** The `org.residency_change.*` family events are dual-emitted to the customer's PostHog project per §51 envelope-facing analytics binding (the customer sees their own residency-change history in their analytics dashboards); the `spec_lint.*` event is Ops-internal only (Sourcera `spec-ops` project) and never dual-emitted to the customer.

v7.2.0-REM Phase 10 spec-wide catalog-completeness sweep — closes the Appendix G portion of the §12 Policy Ingestion cluster (catalog-class P1 defects **D-12-004**, **D-4.3-008**). Every webhook registered in the Appendix C `v7.2.0-REM Phase 10` block has its PostHog mirror here with the §31.8 AC #16 `.` → `_` transliteration; plus the two per-amendment observability-only events. The Appendix G preamble standard property set applies to every row (`org_id`, `user_id`, `session_id`, `console`, `workspace_id`, `plan_tier`, `page_surface_kind`, `client_device_class`, `client_timezone`); only the event-specific key properties are listed. `appendix_c_to_appendix_g_coverage` asserts.

**Webhook mirrors (one per Appendix C `v7.2.0-REM Phase 10` event):** `policy_ingestion_queued`, `policy_ingestion_framework_detected`, `policy_ingestion_framework_pending_user`, `policy_ingestion_extraction_completed`, `policy_ingestion_extraction_partial`, `policy_ingestion_extraction_failed`, `policy_ingestion_dedup_completed`, `policy_ingestion_amendments_drafted`, `policy_ingestion_published`, `policy_ingestion_discarded`, `policy_ingestion_failed`. Event-specific properties: `policy_ingestion_job_id`, `policy_document_id`, `policy_framework_kind`, `policy_framework_confidence`, `policy_framework_confidence_band`, `control_count`, `merged_count`, `discarded_count`, `error_code`.

> - **Metered SKUs and outcome-based billing:** §34.3.4 (rate card subset); §32.4 ("API calls are NOT customer-billed — rate-limited only"); §4.8.1 + §34.10 + §34.11 (outcome-resolver + AIWallet model).
> - **Wallet-charge retry curve:** §4.8.3 + §7140 `auto_topup_charge` retry-curve class (1s, 5s, 30s, 2m, 10m; DLQ at attempt 5). The "3 retries / 15 days" policy below applies to the **subscription-invoice-charge path** (Stripe-side dunning for the recurring plan-tier charge), not to wallet top-ups.
> - **Public Pricing API:** §32.8.1 + §4.8.9 PricingTableVersion (the canonical live rate card surface for customers).

### Subscription Products

| Product | Price | Billing | Renewal |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `sourcera-free` | $0/month | Tracking only (no payment method) | N/A |
| `sourcera-business` | $499/month (annual) or $599/month (monthly) | Recurring, auto-renew | Monthly or yearly |
| `sourcera-enterprise` | Custom | Annual contract | Annually |

### Metered SKUs

| SKU ID | Trigger | Pricing | Billing Granularity |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `sourcera_api_calls` | API call count | Free: $0.01/100 (beyond 1K). Business: $0.005/100 (beyond 10K). Enterprise: unlimited | Daily meter event |
| `sourcera_policy_ingestions` | Policy Ingestion count | Business: $25/ingestion (beyond 3/mo). Enterprise: unlimited | Per ingestion |
| `sourcera_ai_operation_overage_value_dollars_cents` | AIOperation settlement in excess of included AI wallet budget (per §34.10) | Settled at `value_price` or `cost_price` per §34.3.1 outcome resolver; billed in integer-USD-cents as `effective_charge_cents` per §4.8.1 | Per AIOperation settlement (real-time meter event via §31.8.3) |
| `sourcera_wallet_topup_value_dollars_cents` | Manual customer-initiated AI Wallet top-up (per §34.10.5) | At face value of top-up amount in USD cents; no markup; `stripe_charge_id` bound to the resulting `WalletTopupRecord` | Per top-up request |
| `sourcera_wallet_autotopup_value_dollars_cents` | Auto-topup execution triggered by wallet drop below `auto_topup_threshold_cents` (per §34.10.5) | At configured `auto_topup_amount_cents`; respects `monthly_autotopup_cap_cents` per §4.8.3 | Per auto-topup execution (§31.8.4 `billing.wallet.auto_topup_executed`) |
| `sourcera_committed_spend_annual` | Enterprise annual committed-spend contract (per §34.12) | At contracted `commit_value_cents`; invoiced per agreed cadence (upfront / quarterly / monthly-pro-rata); discount band per §34.12.2 | Per contract activation + renewal cycle |
| `sourcera_storage_overage` | Storage beyond plan limit (GB) | All plans: $0.10/GB/month | Daily meter event (1 GB units) |

### Billing Mechanics

- **Monthly Invoices:** Generated on subscription anniversary date.  
- **Line Items:** Subscription amount \+ metered overages \+ prorated changes.  
- **Auto-Charging:** Stripe auto-charges default payment method.  
- **Failed Charges:** 3 retries over 15 days. After final failure, subscription paused (access revoked until payment successful).  
- **Tax:** Stripe Billing handles Sales Tax/VAT/GST automatically (requires tax ID configuration).  
- **Meter Reporting:** Metered charges reported to Stripe daily. Events aggregated by date and SKU.  
- **Invoice Visibility:** Customer views invoices in Settings → Billing → Invoice History.

### Free-to-Paid Upgrade

- Free → Business: Immediate upgrade. Customer enters trial or paid subscription. Billing cycle starts on upgrade date (prorated for remainder of month if mid-cycle).  
- Paid-tier renewal (Starter / Growth / Scale / Enterprise): On anniversary date, Stripe charges the §34.2.1 / §34.2.2 plan price plus any metered AI wallet overage from the previous month per §34.10.

### Plan Downgrade

- Any paid tier → Free: Effective at next renewal date. If current usage exceeds the §34.1 Free-tier ceilings, customer enters the §34.6 DowngradeExcessDataBucket 90-day read-only preservation flow (per §40.2 retention).  
- Metered charges stop on downgrade date.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- Stripe webhooks synced (invoice.paid, customer.subscription.updated, etc.).  
- Metered charges reported daily, appear on next invoice.  
- Billing calculations audit trail (can trace any charge to source).  
- Failed payment retry logic honored (3 attempts over 15 days).
