## Appendix I: API Error Code Catalog {#appendix-i-api-error-code-catalog}

### Appendix I Preamble — Catalog Conventions {#appendix-i-preamble}

Authored in the Phase V8.4 spec-side remediation pass (2026-05-08; defects D-V8.4-005, D-V8.4-006, D-V8.4-012, D-V8.4-013, D-V8.4-016, D-V8.4-020). The preamble binds the catalog-wide column conventions, retryability mapping, HTTP-status-class discipline, and i18n contract. Every row in the catalog inherits these conventions; per-row deviations are explicit and documented inline.

**Canonical row schema.** Every Appendix I row carries five logical fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- |
| `code` | snake_case identifier; immutable once published. Renames go through deprecation aliasing per §32.6.2 (paired with the `Sourcera-Error-Code-Alias` response header). |
| `http` | Canonical HTTP status. The status-class discipline below binds default retryability. |
| `used_by` | Endpoint set that can return the code. May be a single endpoint, an endpoint family, or a generalization (`All authenticated endpoints` for codes like `unauthorized`). When older table rows omit the column, the v7.1.1 backfill (per §M.5 `appendix_i_endpoint_cross_reference_completeness`) populates it from the §32 reverse-pass. |
| `retryable` | One of `transient` (auto-retry safe with backoff), `permanent` (do not retry; remediation required), `conditional` (retry on caller-side disambiguation, often via `Sourcera-Error-Subkind`), `idempotent_retry_only` (safe to retry only when the caller carries an `Idempotency-Key`). When the row is silent, the HTTP-status-class default below applies. |
| `localization_key` | Stable translation key in the form `error.<scope>.<code>` (e.g., `error.billing.wallet_hard_capped`). Default English message stays inline; locale resolution and the `Accept-Language` request header drive translation lookup at response render time per §37.2. |

**HTTP-status-class default retryability mapping.** Used as the default when a row does not explicitly annotate `retryable`. Override discipline: a row may name its own `retryable` value to overcome this default; the deviation MUST be justified inline.

| HTTP class | Default retryable | Rationale |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `400` | `permanent` | Request is malformed; remediation required client-side. |
| `401` | `conditional` | Re-authenticate then retry; permanent if the credential is revoked. |
| `402` | `permanent` (plan-upgrade subkind) / `conditional` (payment-processor subkind) | See `Sourcera-Error-Subkind` discipline below. |
| `403` | `permanent` | Caller lacks the required scope, role, or context; remediation requires elevation, not retry. |
| `404` | `permanent` | Resource does not exist (or non-leak per §7.2). |
| `409` | `permanent` (state conflict) / `conditional` (idempotency replay) | The row names which subclass applies. |
| `410` | `permanent` | Resource gone; do not retry. |
| `413` | `permanent` | Payload exceeds limit; reduce and retry only after client-side remediation (treated as `permanent` from the catalog's perspective). |
| `422` | `permanent` | Validation rejected; remediation required client-side. |
| `423` | `permanent` (locked-for-policy) / `transient` (locked-for-contest, when window short) | The row names which subclass applies. |
| `429` | `transient` | Honor `Retry-After`; retry deterministically. |
| `500` | `conditional` | Retry idempotent reads; mutations require an `Idempotency-Key` to be safe. |
| `502` | `transient` | Upstream transient. |
| `503` | `transient` | Service unavailable; honor `Retry-After`. |
| `504` | `transient` | Gateway timeout; retry with backoff. |

**Sourcera-Error-Subkind response header.** Authored in Phase V8.4 (D-V8.4-012). HTTP 402 is overloaded across "plan upgrade required" and "Stripe charge failed at runtime" semantics. To allow deterministic client routing, the §32.6 error envelope MUST carry the response header `Sourcera-Error-Subkind` whenever the code's HTTP status admits more than one canonical subkind. Controlled vocabulary registered in Appendix J `error_subkind`:

| Subkind | Applies to | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `plan_upgrade_required` | 402 | Caller's current plan tier excludes the requested capability or feature. Permanent until plan tier upgraded. |
| `payment_processor_failure` | 402 | A Stripe charge attempted at request time was declined. Conditional retry: card-level decline is permanent until card replaced; processor-outage decline is transient. |
| `wallet_runtime_block` | 402 | Wallet hard-cap reached; AIOperation rejected. Permanent within billing period; resolved by top-up, auto-topup settling, plan upgrade, or period reset. |
| `state_conflict_strict` | 409 | Server-side state machine disallows the transition; remediation requires resolving the underlying state. |
| `idempotency_key_replay` | 409 | Replay of a request with the same `Idempotency-Key` whose body differs; safe to discard the second request. |
| `firewall_non_leak` | 404 | Resource exists in another scope; the response shape is structurally identical to a true 404 to preserve §7.2 non-leak. |
| `policy_lock` | 423 | Resource locked by a policy (e.g., DSAR hold, contest window, billing freeze). |

**Localization-key discipline.** Authored in Phase V8.4 (D-V8.4-013). Every Appendix I row carries an implicit `localization_key` of the form `error.<scope>.<code>`, where `<scope>` derives from the sub-section heading (e.g., `error.billing.wallet_hard_capped`, `error.kb_export.kb_export_archive_integrity_failed`). Rows authored after 2026-05-08 explicitly carry the key in a `localization_key` column where the sub-section adopts the v7.1.1 expanded row schema (§M.5 `error_code_localization_key_completeness` gates completeness). Rows authored before 2026-05-08 inherit the implicit key form; the v7.1.1 hygiene pass backfills explicit columns.

**Cooldown HTTP-status convention.** Authored in Phase V8.4 (D-V8.4-020). Time-bounded blockers with `Retry-After` semantics map to HTTP 429 (`transient`); permission-bounded blockers with no auto-resume map to HTTP 403 (`permanent`); state-conflict blockers requiring manual resolution map to HTTP 409 (`permanent` subkind `state_conflict_strict`). Rows that drift from this convention are progressively migrated; CI gate `cooldown_status_convention` (§M.5) blocks new drift.

**Console-firewall discipline (cross-reference §1.3 / §7.2).** Cross-console reads on data-bearing endpoints MUST return HTTP 404 with subkind `firewall_non_leak` to honor the non-leak invariant. The legacy code `console_isolation_violation` is now scoped to **management-plane denials only** (carve-out documented inline at the row); it MUST NOT be returned from any data-bearing endpoint. Defense-in-depth: every domain-scoped 404 row carries the suffix `_cross_console_access` per the convention.

**Internal events vs HTTP errors.** Appendix I catalogues HTTP error responses returned over `api.sourcera.io/v1`. Internal integrity events (e.g., audit-chain breaks raised by background jobs) and polling payload flags (e.g., `kb_export_download_remints_exhausted`) live in dedicated sub-sections (see "Internal Integrity Events" and "Polling Payload Flags" below) and are catalogued for completeness with explicit non-HTTP shape annotations.

**Authored Extension status.** The Phase V8.4 preamble itself is an Authored Extension; ratification queued under AE-V8.4-04 in `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md`. The four §M.5 gates the preamble registers (`appendix_i_billing_code_completeness`, `appendix_i_retryability_completeness`, `appendix_i_endpoint_cross_reference_completeness`, `error_code_localization_key_completeness`, `cooldown_status_convention`, `console_isolation_violation_no_data_path_use`, `vendor_opt_out_capability_layer_enforcement`, `kb_export_console_firewall_status_consistency`, `appendix_anchor_slug_no_colon`) carry runtime wiring in implementation pack M02.3.

NOT an HTTP response code. Cross-listed here for §25.3 authoring-pass readers; canonical contract lives in the Internal Integrity Events sub-section below. |

### KB / MCP Server Errors (§22)

The codes below are referenced from §22.4–§22.16 (Seller KB and Sourcera KB MCP Server). All inherit the standard error-response schema below; the `details` block is per-code.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `firewall_violation` | 403 | MCP tool call references a `namespace_id` outside the JWT's `allowed_namespace_ids[]`, or attempts a cross-Org read; also raised by `console_bridge_event_firewall_violation` validators (§4.7.1). Always SIM-alerted. |
| `wrong_region` | 403 | Vault JWT's `data_residency_region` does not match the MCP server's region; e.g., US-issued JWT presented to the EU MCP server (§22.8.6, §22.16.7). |
| `mcp_token_revoked` | 401 | JWT explicitly revoked: `MCPSessionTokenRecord.revoked_at IS NOT NULL`. Security-incident response — Ops alerts SHOULD page on emit. Retryable: `permanent` (no retry; require user re-authentication). Authored Phase V8.4 (D-V8.4-014; replaces the revoke-half of legacy `stale_token`). |
| `mcp_token_expired` | 401 | JWT expired beyond the §22.8.3.1 grace window. Retryable: `transient` (refresh JWT and retry). Authored Phase V8.4 (D-V8.4-014; replaces the expiry-half of legacy `stale_token`). |
| `stale_token` | 401 | **Deprecated alias** (Phase V8.4, D-V8.4-014). Retained through v7.x deprecation window. Aliasing handler returns the canonical `mcp_token_revoked` or `mcp_token_expired` body based on `MCPSessionTokenRecord.revoked_at` vs expiry timestamp; sets `Sourcera-Error-Code-Alias: stale_token`. Removed at v8.0.0. |
| `invalid_namespace` | 422 | `namespace_preference[]` contains a value that is not registered in Appendix J `kb_namespace_kind`, or references a deleted KBNamespace (§22.3.4). |
| `retrieval_unavailable` | 503 | Both BM25 and dense retrieval legs returned empty due to substrate outage (§22.9.1 Stage 3 fallback exhausted; §22.16.6). |
| `entry_archived` | 404 | `kb_get_entry` or `cite_verify` invoked on an entry whose `status=archived` (§22.4.1). |
| `entry_flagged_stale` | 409 | `cite_verify` invoked on an entry whose `review_state ∈ {review_overdue, flagged_stale}` (§22.9.8). |
| `kb_entry_invalid_state_transition` | 422 | Lifecycle state-machine transition outside the §22.4.1 allowed set (e.g., `archived` → `active` without namespace remap). |
| `stale_attach_ref` | 409 | `doc_attach` invoked with an `attach_ref` whose 5-minute TTL has elapsed (§22.8.4.4). |
| `wrong_response_slot` | 422 | `doc_attach` `response_slot_id` does not belong to the seller's bid_workspace from the JWT (§22.8.4.4). |
| `doc_no_longer_active` | 409 | KBDocument transitioned to `expired` or `superseded` between `document_library_find` and `doc_attach` (§22.7). |
| `mcp_jwt_missing_claim` | 422 | Vault JWT missing a required claim (e.g., `data_residency_region`) when presented to the MCP server (§22.8.3, Self-Challenge Log finding #7 from Phase 22-Rewrite). |
| `environment_archived` | 422 | Session-create attempted against a `Managed Agent environment` that has been archived (§22.13.3); orchestrator pre-checks env existence and blocks before the Anthropic-side `client.beta.sessions.create` call. |
| `agent_output_uncited_sentence` | 422 | Orchestrator second-pass validator detected a sentence in an `emit_structured_draft` payload without a structural citation (§22.16.1 Layer 5). |
| `agent_output_invalid_citation` | 422 | Orchestrator second-pass `cite_verify` returned `valid=false` on at least one citation in an `emit_structured_draft` payload (§22.16.1 Layer 5). |
| `missing_source_ref` | 422 | `kb_entry_draft_create` called with empty/omitted `source_refs[]` (§22.8.4.8). Bootstrap and ghost-ingestion workflows MUST cite provenance; fabricated-body drafts are rejected at the write path. |
| `dedupe_gate_failed` | 422 | `kb_entry_draft_create` called with `dedupe_verdict.checked=false` OR `dedupe_verdict.nearest_similarity ≥ 0.92` without a deliberate-duplicate override flag (§22.8.4.8). Enforces the pre-write dedupe contract against `kb_dedupe_check` (§22.8.4.9). |
| `body_too_long` | 422 | `kb_entry_draft_create` `body` exceeds 20,000 chars (§22.8.4.8, §39 KB entry body cap). |
| `candidate_body_too_long` | 422 | `kb_dedupe_check` `candidate.body` exceeds 20,000 chars (§22.8.4.9). |
| `write_unavailable` | 503 | Retrieval-store write path (pgvector index or draft-entry row write) unreachable; agent backs off per `KB_Engineering_Spec.md §17`. Applies to `kb_entry_draft_create` (§22.8.4.8). |

### KB Export Endpoint Errors (added §32.9 / §22.18)

The codes below are emitted exclusively from the §32.9 Seller KB Export endpoints. All inherit the standard error-response schema; the `details` block is per-code. None of these codes MAY be hoisted into a generic `feature_not_available_on_plan` 402 response: per §22.18.1 P1 "No-Paywall Export," the export endpoint is invariant on plan tier and MUST NEVER return 402.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `kb_export_archive_shape_invalid` | 400 | `format` unknown, `namespace_filter=selected` with empty `namespace_ids`, or `idempotency_ttl_hours` outside [1, 72]. Resolve by fixing the request body; archive shape constraints are documented in §32.9.1 and §22.18.2.2. |
| `kb_export_namespace_cross_org` | 400 | One or more entries in `namespace_ids` are not owned by the `org_id` path parameter. Enforces the §22.18.2.6 DSAR isolation rule: cross-Org namespace references MUST NOT be resolvable via the export surface. |
| `kb_export_role_insufficient` | 403 | Caller role is not in `{seller_org_owner, seller_org_admin, seller_kb_admin}`. Export is a privileged egress channel; `seller_kb_editor`, `seller_kb_viewer`, `seller_bid_captain`, `seller_bid_contributor`, and `seller_guest` are denied. |
| `kb_export_console_forbidden` | 404 | **Phase V8.4 status correction (D-V8.4-018):** API token was issued from a buyer-console scope. Cross-console access to Seller KB export resolves to HTTP 404 (subkind `firewall_non_leak`) per §7.2 to preserve entity-existence non-leak invariant. The error envelope is structurally indistinguishable from a true 404. Pre-V8.4 emissions used HTTP 403; aliasing handler returns the canonical 404 shape and sets `Sourcera-Error-Code-Alias: kb_export_console_forbidden_403_legacy` for caller-side telemetry continuity. CI gate `kb_export_console_firewall_status_consistency` (§M.5) asserts. |
| `kb_export_token_scope_insufficient` | 403 | Token does not carry the `export:kb` scope. Re-mint the token with the scope; issuance is plan-tier-invariant per §22.18.1 P1. |
| `kb_export_residency_mismatch` | 409 | Request was routed to a region other than the Org's pinned `residency_region`. Re-route the caller to the correct regional edge (`us`, `eu`, `apac`). Archive generation MUST NOT egress the region's S3 partition. |
| `kb_export_concurrency_exceeded` | 409 | Org already has 2 KBExportJobs in `queued|running` state. Wait for an in-flight job to reach `ready` or `failed`, OR cancel an in-flight job, then retry. |
| `kb_export_dsar_hold_active` | 422 | Org is under an active DSAR / right-to-erasure hold per §6.8. New exports are paused until the hold releases. In-flight jobs transition to `paused` (terminal-until-resume) per §22.18.2.6. |
| `kb_export_rate_limit_exceeded` | 429 | > 10 KB export initiations within the rolling 60-minute window for the Org. Response carries `Retry-After` per §32.4.5. |
| `kb_export_queue_saturated` | 503 | Ops-triggered circuit breaker (§44.4) during KB Export queue pressure. Retry with exponential backoff; SLO is 60 minutes or less under normal operation. |
| `kb_export_job_not_found` | 404 | `export_id` does not exist OR belongs to another Org. Cross-Org ID leaks are resolved to 404 per §32.6 existence-leak convention; the caller MUST NOT distinguish between "never existed" and "exists in another Org." |
| `kb_export_archive_integrity_failed` | 410 | On-demand integrity check failed — `sha256(archive_bytes)` does not match the recorded `archive_sha256`. Archive has been tampered with or corrupted in S3 and is no longer downloadable. Ops is paged automatically; affected Orgs SHOULD re-initiate export. |
| `kb_export_download_remints_exhausted` | (polling payload flag — see "Polling Payload Flags" sub-section) | **Phase V8.4 relocation (D-V8.4-011):** Polling payload flag, NOT an HTTP error response. Surfaces inside an HTTP 200 polling response body. Canonical contract lives in the Polling Payload Flags sub-section below. |

### API Detail Pack Errors (§32.10)

The codes below are emitted by the v7.1.1 API detail pack endpoints in §32.10. They inherit the standard error-response schema, response headers, and existence-leak rules from §32.6 / Appendix I. Data-bearing cross-console denials return 404 with `Sourcera-Error-Subkind: firewall_non_leak` unless the row is explicitly a management-plane denial.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `outcome_contract_not_found` | 404 | OutcomeContract ID does not exist, is outside the caller's Org-visible settlement scope, or cannot be exposed to the caller's role. |

| `eoi_not_found` | 404 | EOI ID does not exist, belongs to another Org, or is outside the caller's buyer/seller projection. |
| `eoi_acceptance_role_insufficient` | 403 | Caller lacks the buyer Workspace or seller projection role required for the requested EOI transition. |
| `eoi_acceptance_duplicate` | 409 | An active EOI Acceptance Record already exists for the EOI and replay does not match the original idempotency body. |
| `eoi_invalid_state_transition` | 422 | Requested EOI transition is not allowed from the current `eoi_status`. |
| `eoi_acceptance_eoi_not_submitted` | 422 | Buyer attempted to accept an EOI before the seller submitted it. |

| `kb_entry_not_found` | 404 | KBEntry ID does not exist, is archived when active-only reads are requested, belongs to another Org, or was requested from the buyer console. |
| `kb_document_not_found` | 404 | KBDocument ID does not exist, is archived / superseded when active-only reads are requested, belongs to another Org, or was requested from the buyer console. |
| `kb_namespace_not_found` | 404 | KBNamespace ID does not exist, is deleted, belongs to another Org, or was requested from the buyer console. |

### Error Response Schema {#appendix-i-error-response-schema}

Authored 2026-04-14; re-authored Phase V8.4 (D-V8.4-017) to remove markdown-escape leak and bind the v7.1.1 column-schema fields (`Sourcera-Error-Subkind`, `Sourcera-Error-Code-Alias`, `localization_key`).

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "gate_validation_failed",
    "message": "Cannot advance to Phase 2: 3 requirements are still in draft status.",
    "localization_key": "error.workflow.gate_validation_failed",
    "details": {
      "failing_rules": ["all_requirements_active"],
      "blocking_requirement_ids": ["req_abc", "req_def", "req_ghi"],
      "invalid_fields": ["title", "weight"]
    },
    "request_id": "req_789xyz",
    "retry_after_seconds": null
  }
}
```

**Required response headers.** Every error response carries:

| Header | When | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `X-Request-ID` | Always | Mirrors `error.request_id` for support escalation per §32.6. |
| `Retry-After` | Always when retryable is `transient` (HTTP 429 / 503 / 504) | Seconds until the next eligible retry. |
| `Sourcera-Error-Subkind` | When the row's HTTP status admits more than one subkind (see Appendix I Preamble) | Deterministic subkind from Appendix J `error_subkind` enum. |
| `Sourcera-Error-Code-Alias` | When the canonical code was emitted by a deprecated-alias path | Original alias name; deprecation window per §32.6.2. |

**All error responses include `request_id` for support escalation.**

### §4.3 Buyer Console Entity Errors (Internal Comments, Usage Events, Pro Trial Seat Grants, Referrals)

The codes below are referenced from §4.3.11–§4.3.19 (Internal Comments, Presence, Unread Markers, Buyer Referrals, Pro Trial Seat Grants, Usage Events, Time-Saved Credits) and their state machines in Appendix L. The §7.2 Dual-Console Firewall is enforced uniformly: cross-console read / write attempts return HTTP 404 (non-leak) rather than HTTP 403 to avoid disclosing entity existence to the opposite console.

| Code | HTTP | Used By | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |

- Cross-console read/write attempts (buyer ↔ seller firewall): `internal_comment_cross_console_access`, `presence_record_cross_console_access`, `usage_event_console_mismatch`.
- Double-booking and referral abuse: `referral_referee_already_bound`, `trial_seat_same_buyer_365d_block`, `trial_seat_vendor_already_paid`.
- Plan / pool entitlement violations: `trial_seat_buyer_below_scale`, `trial_seat_pool_exhausted`.
- Retroactive-safety invariant: `referral_activity_threshold_policy_drift_rejected`, `time_saved_credit_conversion_factor_version_missing`.
- Third-party delivery failures: `usage_event_posthog_delivery_exhausted`, `trial_seat_loops_dispatch_unrecoverable`, `referral_credit_reversal_failed`.
- State-machine illegal transitions: `internal_comment_thread_invalid_state_transition`, `trial_seat_invalid_state_transition`, plus the existing `kb_entry_invalid_state_transition` covering §22.4.1.

- Instrumentation / invariants: `seller_onboarding_activation_metric_missing`, `seller_onboarding_monotonicity_violation`.
- Disambiguation / Org contamination: `seller_org_disambiguation_required`.

### §50 Sourcera Ops Console Errors

The codes below are referenced from §50 (Sourcera Ops Console), §4.6.3 OpsSession, and the Ops-Tagged Audit Actor pattern (§50.5). All codes are emitted from the Sourcera Ops Console service layer OR from the shared Customer-API surface when an OpsSession context is attached to the request. Cross-console and cross-Org reads by an OpsSession that lacks the required clearance are non-leak 404s (`not_found`) per §7.2 dual-console firewall preservation; explicit Ops-policy denials (capability envelope, time-box, quorum, residency, step-up-reauth, posture) are HTTP 403 with a structured error body that names the policy kind.

| Code | HTTP | Used By | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `ops_session_required_for_ops_actor` | 403 | §50.5.1 audit-schema-extension enforcement | A Customer-API mutation arrived with `actor_type=ops_actor` but no active OpsSession. The audit subsystem refuses the write; the mutation is rolled back. Error body cites `ops_session_id` requirement and the canonical Ops flow (§50.4.1). |
| `ops_session_immutable_field_mutation` | 409 | §4.6.3 OpsSession immutability invariants | Attempted write to an append-only or initialization-only field on an existing OpsSession row (e.g., `ops_user_id`, `org_id_impersonated`, `console_scope`, `started_at`, `justification_category` post-activation). Error body names the field. |
| `ops_session_append_only` | 409 | §4.6.3 OpsSession insert-once, mutate-once semantics | Attempted hard delete or state regression on an existing OpsSession. OpsSession rows are append-only with a one-way state machine (§50.4.3); soft-delete via `closed_* + ended_at` is the only closure path. |
| `ops_session_auth_evidence_incomplete` | 403 | §50.3.3 / §50.4.1 authentication evidence requirement | OpsSession open attempted without hardware-key MFA / WebAuthn evidence recorded in `auth_factor_evidence_json`. Enforced at OpsSession insert time; the session cannot transition out of `pending_justification` without evidence. |
| `ops_session_justification_invalid` | 422 | §50.4.1 justification requirement | `justification_category` missing, uses a non-registered enum value, or `justification_note` is empty/below the §4.6.3 minimum character floor (20 chars). Error body names the field and the minimum length. |
| `ops_session_quorum_required` | 403 | §50.4.4 dual-control gate | Requested Ops action requires a quorum signoff but the OpsSession is still in `pending_justification` with no co-signing Ops Admin. Error body names the required signoff-role pool and the expected signoff SLA. |
| `ops_session_quorum_self_signoff_forbidden` | 403 | §50.4.4 separation-of-duties | Opener of an OpsSession attempted to self-sign the quorum. Forbidden; quorum signoff must come from a distinct active Ops Admin user. |
| `ops_session_cross_console_access_denied` | 403 | §50.3.2 capability envelope | OpsSession attempted to act on a console (`buyer` vs `seller`) for which the Ops role lacks clearance. Error body names the denied `console_scope` and the canonical six-role matrix row that governs access. |
| `ops_session_residency_access_denied` | 403 | §50.2.1 residency partitioning | OpsSession attempted to impersonate an Org in a residency region the Ops user is not cleared for. Error body names the attempted `residency_region` and the user's cleared set. Cross-residency clearance is a separate role-pool grant per §50.3. |
| `ops_session_step_up_reauth_required` | 403 | §50.4.1 / §50.4.6 step-up | Ops Admin attempted a high-sensitivity action (e.g., break-glass DB access, emergency role grant) whose policy demands a step-up re-auth within the last N minutes. Error body names the action kind and the step-up window. |
| `ops_session_step_up_reauth_stale` | 403 | §50.4.1 / §50.4.6 step-up | Step-up re-auth performed but the credential cache has expired. Retry with fresh WebAuthn evidence. |
| `ops_session_device_posture_failed` | 403 | §50.2.2 authentication model | Ops user's device failed posture check (managed device, compliant OS, jailbreak-free). Error body names the failed posture attribute; user must remediate. |
| `ops_session_org_mismatch` | 403 | §50.4.1 session-scope integrity | Customer-API mutation arrived on a path whose `org_id` does not match the OpsSession's `org_id_impersonated`. Server refuses the mutation to prevent cross-Org leakage. |
| `ops_session_closed_mid_request` | 410 | §50.4.2 time-box enforcement / §50.4.7 customer-revoked | In-flight Customer-API request observed the OpsSession transitioning to `closed_*` after the request began but before the mutation committed. Partial-state cleanup is invoked; the caller MUST re-open a fresh OpsSession to retry. |
| `ops_session_chain_depth_exceeded` | 409 | §50.3.5 bootstrap / escape-hatch chain bound | Opening a new OpsSession with a `parent_ops_session_id` chain that exceeds the allowable depth (default 2). Prevents infinite-escalation abuse. |
| `ops_session_overlap_conflict` | 409 | §50.4.6 session hard limits | Ops user already has an active OpsSession for the same `(org_id_impersonated, console_scope)` pair and no second-concurrent is permitted by policy. Close the prior session first or request a concurrency-override per §50.4.6. |
| `ops_session_per_user_concurrency_exceeded` | 429 | §50.4.6 session hard limits | Ops user exceeded the per-user concurrent OpsSession ceiling (default 3 across all Orgs). Close prior sessions to open a new one. |
| `ops_session_revoke_role_required` | 403 | §50.4.7 customer revocation surface | Customer-initiated revoke call arrived without an `org_owner` or `billing_admin` role on the invoking user. Error body cites §50.4.7 eligibility. |
| `ops_action_record_session_link_required` | 422 | §50.5.3 OpsActionRecord extension | An OpsActionRecord INSERT (§4.4.27) raised from an Ops surface arrived without `linked_ops_session_id` set. OpsActionRecords raised from an Ops surface MUST link to an OpsSession to preserve the audit chain. |
| `ai_operation_ops_actor_session_required` | 422 | §50.5.2 AIOperation extension | An AIOperation INSERT (§4.8.1) arrived with `actor_type=ops` (e.g., Ops-triggered re-run of a customer capability) but no `ops_session_id` set. AIOperations attributed to an Ops actor MUST carry the OpsSession linkage; otherwise billing attribution and the Ops-tagged audit chain are broken. |
| `audit_event_actor_type_consistency_violation` | 500 | §50.5.1 / Appendix J `audit_event_actor_type` enum | AuditEvent INSERT observed an `actor_type` value inconsistent with its required identity fields (e.g., `actor_type=ops_actor` with no Ops role assignment or missing `ops_session_id`; `actor_type=customer_user` with an Ops-only `ops_session_id`; `actor_type=external_integration` with no `external_integration_principal_id`). Server-side invariant violation; pages Ops observability on-call. |
| `ops_role_unknown` | 422 | §50.3.1 role registry enforcement | OpsRoleAssignment write referenced a `role_kind` not registered in Appendix J `ops_role_kind`. Only the six canonical roles (plus the two Ops-Admin variants: `ops_admin` and `ops_admin_escalated`) are valid. |
| `ops_role_assignment_self_signoff_forbidden` | 403 | §50.3.4 state-machine separation-of-duties | Ops Admin attempted to co-sign their own OpsRoleAssignment proposal. Forbidden; a distinct Ops Admin must co-sign. |
| `ops_role_assignment_quorum_required` | 403 | §50.3.4 quorum gate | OpsRoleAssignment transition to `active` requires quorum (second Ops Admin signoff) but none recorded. Error body names the required signoff pool. |
| `ops_role_assignment_quorum_expired` | 410 | §50.3.4 quorum window | OpsRoleAssignment quorum-signoff window expired without receiving a second signoff. Row transitions to `rejected` with reason `quorum_timeout`; a fresh proposal is required. |
| `ops_capability_outside_envelope` | 403 | §50.3.2 capability envelope matrix | Ops role attempted a capability outside its declared envelope (e.g., `support_agent` attempting `rate_card_mutation` — a `pricing_admin`-only capability). Error body names the requested capability, the user's role, and the allowed-role set. |
| `ops_rate_limit_override_unauthorized` | 403 | §50.3.2 rate-limit-override authority | Ops role without the `rate_limit_override_authority` capability row attempted to issue a rate-limit override. Restricted to `ops_admin` and `pricing_admin` per §50.3.2 envelope. |
| `ops_rate_limit_override_duration_exceeded` | 422 | §50.3.2 rate-limit-override authority | Requested override duration exceeds the maximum allowed per the Ops role (default: 24 hours for `pricing_admin`, 72 hours for `ops_admin`). |
| `ops_break_glass_db_access_unauthorized` | 403 | §50.2.4 no-direct-DB-access deviation | Ops user invoked break-glass DB access without the `ops_security_admin` role OR without a linked incident_id. Hardcoded to `ops_security_admin` only; error body cites the §50.2.4 policy. |
| `ops_break_glass_db_access_co_approver_required` | 403 | §50.2.4 two-person-rule | Break-glass DB access requires co-approval from a second `ops_security_admin` OR `ops_admin_escalated`. Error body names the co-approver pool. |
| `ops_incident_declaration_unauthorized` | 403 | §50.6 incident response | Ops user without incident-declaration authority attempted a declaration. Default: `ops_admin` and `ops_security_admin` only. |
| `ops_customer_notification_block_strict_mode` | 409 | §50.4.5 customer-notification enforcement (strict mode) | OpsSession open was attempted in strict-notify mode but the customer-notification dispatch failed (no active Org Owner / Billing Admin OR transport layer returned structural failure). Session blocked from activating; Ops user must remediate or escalate to Ops-Admin degraded-notify-mode override. |
| `ops_customer_notification_degraded_mode_acknowledgement_required` | 403 | §50.4.5 degraded-notify mode | OpsSession opened in degraded-notify mode (customer notification failed but Ops Admin override permitted activation); post-session acknowledgement from an additional Ops Admin is required within 24 hours of close. Absence of acknowledgement locks Ops Admin's ability to open further sessions for the same `org_id_impersonated` until acknowledged. |
| `ops_session_customer_revocation_cooldown` | 429 | §50.4.7 customer revocation cooldown | Customer Org has revoked ≥ 2 OpsSessions within the last 24 hours; Ops can no longer open new sessions for this customer without Ops-Admin approval. Error body names the cooldown window and the approval path. |
| `ops_session_export_projection_unauthorized` | 403 | §50.4.8 Customer-Visible Projection surface | Caller attempted to export the Customer-Visible Projection without `billing_admin` or `org_owner` role on the customer Org. |

**Counterfactual Coverage (§50 additions).** Each code above addresses at least one §50.7 failure mode:

- **Audit-chain integrity under Ops attribution:** `ops_session_required_for_ops_actor`, `ops_action_record_session_link_required`, `ai_operation_ops_actor_session_required`, `audit_event_actor_type_consistency_violation`.
- **OpsSession lifecycle immutability:** `ops_session_immutable_field_mutation`, `ops_session_append_only`, `ops_session_closed_mid_request`, `ops_session_chain_depth_exceeded`, `ops_session_overlap_conflict`, `ops_session_per_user_concurrency_exceeded`.
- **Authentication + step-up + posture:** `ops_session_auth_evidence_incomplete`, `ops_session_step_up_reauth_required`, `ops_session_step_up_reauth_stale`, `ops_session_device_posture_failed`.
- **Justification + quorum discipline:** `ops_session_justification_invalid`, `ops_session_quorum_required`, `ops_session_quorum_self_signoff_forbidden`, `ops_role_assignment_quorum_required`, `ops_role_assignment_self_signoff_forbidden`, `ops_role_assignment_quorum_expired`.
- **Envelope + residency + console-firewall enforcement:** `ops_capability_outside_envelope`, `ops_session_cross_console_access_denied`, `ops_session_residency_access_denied`, `ops_session_org_mismatch`, `ops_role_unknown`.
- **Rate-limit / privilege escalation control:** `ops_rate_limit_override_unauthorized`, `ops_rate_limit_override_duration_exceeded`, `ops_break_glass_db_access_unauthorized`, `ops_break_glass_db_access_co_approver_required`, `ops_incident_declaration_unauthorized`.
- **Customer-notification and customer-revocation integrity:** `ops_customer_notification_block_strict_mode`, `ops_customer_notification_degraded_mode_acknowledgement_required`, `ops_session_customer_revocation_cooldown`, `ops_session_revoke_role_required`, `ops_session_export_projection_unauthorized`.

### §51 Product Usage Analytics Errors {#appendix-i-section-51-additions}

The codes below are referenced from §51 (Product Usage Analytics & PLG Instrumentation), the Appendix G preamble (Required Standard Property Set), and the `UsageEventValidator` envelope-validator contract. All codes are emitted from (a) the PostHog outbox validator on event-emit paths, (b) the customer-facing analytics API endpoints registered in §51.3-§51.5, and (c) the DSAR/redaction subsystem paths in §51.7. Enum-bounded codes pair 1:1 with Appendix J `usage_envelope_violation_kind` per the §51.2.5 validator contract; deploy-time CI gate `usage_envelope_violation_kind_appendix_i_pairing` asserts the pairing.

| Code | HTTP | Used By | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `usage_analytics_dashboard_access_denied` | 403 | §51.3.5 / §51.4.5 / §51.5.5 dashboard role-matrix | Caller holds an Org-scoped role not listed in the applicable dashboard role-matrix (e.g., `member` attempting `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/analytics/usage/snapshot` when only `org_owner`, `billing_admin`, and `org_admin` are permitted for the Buyer Org-Level dashboard). Error body names the missing role and the matrix-row that governs the denial. |
| `usage_analytics_user_access_denied` | 403 | §51.4.5 User-Level Dashboard scoping | Caller attempted to view a User-Level Dashboard for a `subject_user_id` they are not authorized to view (self-view permitted for all; cross-user view restricted to `workspace_owner` within the workspace and `billing_admin`/`org_owner` at Org scope). Error body names the caller's role and the permitted-scope set. |
| `usage_analytics_seller_buyer_firewall_violation` | 403 | §51.5 seller-parity dashboard firewall | Caller attempted to read Seller Usage Parity data using a buyer-console token, OR attempted to read Buyer Org-Level Dashboard data using a seller-console token. Console firewall per §25 is hard-enforced. Error body names the `console` mismatch. |
| `usage_analytics_snapshot_not_ready` | 404 | §51.3.1 `UsageDashboardSnapshot` lifecycle | `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/analytics/usage/snapshot` called for a requested `console` / `snapshot_window` / `snapshot_kind` whose compute state is still `pending` or `computing`. Error body carries the current `snapshot_state` and the `estimated_ready_at` timestamp. Caller MUST retry after the estimated time or poll; retries within the estimated window do NOT bypass rate-limit class `analytics_read`. |
| `usage_analytics_snapshot_window_invalid` | 422 | §51.3.1 dashboard query contract | Request `window_start`/`window_end` parameters failed validation (window > 24 months, window_end < window_start, window crosses the DSAR deletion horizon, or window_start predates the Org's creation date). Error body names the failing constraint. |
| `usage_analytics_export_size_exceeded` | 413 | §51.3.2 panel export contract | Panel-export request would produce a payload > 50 MB uncompressed. Caller MUST narrow the window or filter the result set. Error body names the current estimated size and the 50 MB ceiling. |
| `usage_event_envelope_violation` | 422 | §51.2.5 `UsageEventValidator` (validator-side rejection on customer-emitted events routed through a customer-surface path) | A customer-surface event-emit path violated the Appendix G preamble required property set. Pairs with `usage_envelope_violation_kind=missing_required`. Error body names the failing property path and the required-property list. |
| `usage_event_envelope_unknown_property` | 422 | §51.2.5 `UsageEventValidator` | Event payload carried a property not registered in the Appendix G preamble's required-or-optional set. Pairs with `usage_envelope_violation_kind=enum_violation`. Error body names the unknown property and the canonical property registry location. |
| `usage_event_envelope_type_mismatch` | 422 | §51.2.5 `UsageEventValidator` | Event payload carried a property whose concrete type does not match the declared type (e.g., `capability_id` as integer rather than UUID). Pairs with `usage_envelope_violation_kind=type_mismatch`. Error body names the property, the declared type, and the observed type. |
| `usage_event_envelope_enum_violation` | 422 | §51.2.5 `UsageEventValidator` | Event payload carried an enum-bounded property with a value not registered in Appendix J. Pairs with `usage_envelope_violation_kind=enum_violation`. Error body names the property, the observed value, and the Appendix J registry anchor. |
| `usage_event_capability_unresolved` | 422 | §51.2.5 `UsageEventValidator` + §51.6.2 capability-resolution integrity | Event payload carried a `capability_id` that does not resolve to an active CapabilityRegistryEntry row. Pairs with `usage_envelope_violation_kind=capability_unresolved`. Error body names the unresolved `capability_id`. Blocking for `mutation=true` events; warn-and-emit for reads per Appendix G preamble validator contract. |
| `usage_event_residency_mismatch` | 422 | §51.2.5 `UsageEventValidator` + §40.4 residency partitioning | Event `residency_region` did not match the Org's residency binding or one of the Org's declared-residency values. Pairs with `usage_envelope_violation_kind=residency_mismatch` (violator stage) and `usage_envelope_violation_kind=residency_partition_denial` (cross-residency read attempt). Error body names the expected residency set and the observed value. |
| `usage_event_dsar_redaction_failure` | 500 | §51.7.3 DSAR field-level redaction pipeline | DSAR redaction job failed to apply a redaction sentinel to a historical `usage_event` row. Pairs with `usage_envelope_violation_kind=dsar_redaction_failure`. Pages Ops observability on-call; MUST be remediated within the §6.8 DSAR SLA window. | `usage_analytics_conversion_factor_binding_mismatch` | 500 | §51.6.2 Time-Saved binding integrity | Server-side invariant violation: a computed `UsageDashboardSnapshot` rollup was persisted with a `conversion_factor_version_set_hash` that does not match the bound hash on the contributing `TimeSavedCredit` rows. Error body names the `ai_operation_id` and the failing eligibility axis. |

**Counterfactual Coverage (§51 additions).** Each code above addresses at least one §51 failure mode documented in §51.8.3 Counterfactual Pass:

- **Dashboard role-matrix + firewall integrity:** `usage_analytics_dashboard_access_denied`, `usage_analytics_user_access_denied`, `usage_analytics_seller_buyer_firewall_violation`.
- **Snapshot compute lifecycle integrity:** `usage_analytics_snapshot_not_ready`, `usage_analytics_snapshot_window_invalid`, `usage_analytics_export_size_exceeded`.
- **Envelope validator integrity (8 paired rejection causes):** `usage_event_envelope_violation`, `usage_event_envelope_unknown_property`, `usage_event_envelope_type_mismatch`, `usage_event_envelope_enum_violation`, `usage_event_capability_unresolved`, `usage_event_residency_mismatch`, `usage_event_dsar_redaction_failure`.
- **Time-Saved binding integrity:** `usage_analytics_conversion_factor_binding_mismatch`, `time_saved_eligibility_violation`.

### v7.1.0 Surface-Abstraction Program Errors (Phase 14.5 / 14.7 / 14.9 / 14.10 / 14.14) {#appendix-i-v7-1-0-errors}

Authored in the v7.1.0 Surface-Abstraction & Dual-Maya Integration program. Phases 14.5 (Defense View), 14.7 (Per-Vertical Eval Starters), 14.9 (Solo plan tier), and 14.10 (Solo-Tier Surface Treatment) introduced these codes inline; Phase 14.14 error-code-catalog rollup (closed 2026-04-28) lands the canonical Appendix I rows. Each code MUST round-trip through the §32 API error envelope per the Standard HTTP Errors contract; CI gate `error_code_catalog_completeness` (§M.4) asserts presence in this catalog.

#### Defense View Errors (§13.11)

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `selection_record_not_finalized` | 409 | `GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/defense-view` or `POST .../defense-view/regenerate` invoked on a Workspace whose phase is `< 12` OR for which no finalized `SelectionReport` row exists. Per §13.11.2 (Inputs & Source-of-Truth Binding) the Defense View is a strictly downstream surface; its only input is the finalized Selection Record bundle. Resolve by completing Phase 12 (Selection Report finalization) per §10.13. Error body carries `workspace_id`, `current_phase`, and `selection_report_state`. |
| `regeneration_throttle` | 429 | `POST .../defense-view/regenerate` invoked within 5 minutes of the most recent regeneration on the same Workspace. Per §13.11.5 OutcomeContract throttle. Error body carries `last_regenerated_at` and `retry_after_seconds`. Standard `Retry-After` header populated. |
| `defense_view_capability_disabled` | 402 | The `defense_view_generate` capability is `state ∈ {alpha, deprecated→retired}` for the calling Org's plan tier (per §4.8.2 / §21.4.4 capability gating), OR the Org's AIWallet is `wallet_state ∈ {hard_capped_100, suspended, closed}` and the capability has `solo_envelope_no_block=false`. ### Spec-Lint CI Gate Internal Failure Modes (Non-HTTP) {#appendix-i-spec-lint-ci-gate-internal-failure-modes}

Authored in the v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 remediation pass (2026-05-15; closes D-11.2-004 P0 firewall-bypass + the §M.4.4.5 sibling-override Counterfactual #1 / #2 / #3 cluster). Catalogues codes returned by the `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` CI gate's override-rejection paths (§M.4.4.2.A through §M.4.4.2.G) and the §M.4.4.5 sibling-override-annotation grammar parser. These codes are **NOT** HTTP error responses — they are PR-check failure-mode identifiers that surface in (a) the inline review comment posted to the PR, (b) the §M.4.5 audit-trail JSON record (`gate_outcome` field), (c) the §M.4.6 nightly digest, (d) the Datadog log emitted by service `spec-lint` (log level `error` for rejection; `warn` for `override_applied`), and (e) the PostHog event `spec_lint.appendix_m_gate_run` property `gate_outcome`. CI gate `appendix_i_internal_event_no_http_status` (§M.5) asserts no row in this sub-section carries an HTTP status column.

The shape of every row is a **CI-gate emit-path** record:

- **Code** — snake_case immutable identifier; emitted in the `gate_outcome` field of the §M.4.5.1 record schema; surfaced to PR review comment and the §M.4.6 nightly digest.
- **Source gate** — the §M.5 catalog row identifier whose failure path emits the code (always `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` for §M.4.4.2.A–§M.4.4.2.G rejections; any catalog row for §M.4.4.5 sibling-override rejections — the row's `Gate ID` value is carried in the emitted record).
- **Trigger** — the falsifiable precondition that causes the code to be emitted.
- **Resolution path** — the author-facing remediation guidance surfaced in the inline review comment.
- **Authority anchor** — the Master Spec section that authorizes the code and the defect / AE row that the code remediates.

| Code | Source gate | Trigger | Resolution path | Authority anchor |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `override_target_not_flagged_by_detector` | `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` (§M.4.4.2.A) | The `{concept_name}` in a `@appendix-m-internal-only:` annotation does not exactly match any concept the §M.4.2 trigger detector flagged in the same PR diff (after applying §M.4.2.1 anchor-alias resolution symmetrically on both sides). The author submitted an override for a concept that does not appear in the diff. | (a) Fix the annotation's `{concept_name}` to exactly match one of the detected concepts surfaced in the rejection comment; (b) Author the §M.1 row directly without invoking the override path; (c) If the concept is genuinely internal-only AND the PR is a no-op for the trigger detector, the override path is unavailable — the §M.1 row must be authored directly with the `Internal-only, never surfaced` sentinel in the `Tier visibility` cell. | §M.4.4.2.A; D-11.2-004 (P0) v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 closure; AE-V72REM-09. |
| `override_target_customer_visible` | `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` (§M.4.4.2.B–§M.4.4.2.E) | The `{concept_name}` passes §M.4.4.2.A detector-flag cross-validation but evaluates `true` on at least one of the four v7.2.0-REM customer-surface-reachability predicates (console enum, RBAC, plan-tier, surface-class non-internal). | (a) Author an explicit §M.1 row with a surface metaphor + `Tier visibility` cell value listing the tiers that see the surface; (b) If the customer-surface reach is incidental, file a follow-up Authored Extension to amend the §M.4.4.2 predicate-sub-check set OR rename the concept to break the heuristic match; (c) If the concept genuinely should NOT be customer-reachable, fix the upstream spec-side cite at the evidence anchor surfaced in the rejection comment. | §M.4.4.2.B / §M.4.4.2.C / §M.4.4.2.D / §M.4.4.2.E; D-11.2-004 (P0) V11 closure + v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 hardening; AE-V11-06 + AE-V72REM-09. |
| `invalid_override_rationale` | `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` (§M.4.4.1) | A `@appendix-m-internal-only:` annotation is malformed: missing the required substring `internal-only construct, not surfaced`; missing the prefix colon or `—` em-dash separator; missing the `{concept_name}` token; or missing the required cross-class qualifier per §M.4.4.1 ¶4. | Repair the annotation per the §M.4.4.1 canonical form: `@appendix-m-internal-only: {concept_name} — {rationale}` where the rationale carries the substring, the ≥60-character floor, and the cross-class qualifier(s). The rejection comment names the specific grammar-rule violation. | §M.4.4.1; D-11.2-005 (P1) V11 closure; AE-V11-06. |
| `override_rationale_too_short` | Any §M.5 row whose `override_path` admits `@ci-gate-override:` or `@appendix-m-internal-only:` annotations (§M.4.4.1 ¶2 + §M.4.4.5 ¶1) | The rationale text (after stripping the `@<prefix>: {gate_id_or_concept_name} — ` prefix and trimming leading/trailing ASCII whitespace) is < 60 Unicode-NFC-normalized characters. | Expand the rationale to ≥ 60 characters with substantive justification (the 60-character floor exists to defeat the D-11.2-004 attack class where adversarial authors paste boilerplate). The rejection comment surfaces the measured character count. | §M.4.4.1 ¶2 + §M.4.4.5 ¶1; v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 Counterfactual #2 closure; AE-V72REM-09. |
| `override_unknown_gate` | Any `@ci-gate-override:` annotation (§M.4.4.5 ¶2) | The `{gate_id}` cited in a `@ci-gate-override:` annotation does not exactly match any `Gate ID` value in the §M.5 catalog row set (computed deterministically from §M.5.4 / §M.5.5 / §M.5.10 / §M.5.12 / §M.5.13 / §M.5.14 / §M.5.NN catalog blocks at gate boot). | Replace the cited `{gate_id}` with one of the closest-match suggestions surfaced in the rejection comment (Levenshtein distance < 5), OR add a §M.5 catalog row for the cited gate in the same PR if the gate is being introduced. | §M.4.4.5 ¶2; v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 Counterfactual #1 closure; AE-V72REM-09. |
| `ci_gate_override_not_permitted` | Any §M.5 row whose `override_path` column declares `not_permitted` or `not_permitted_<rule>` (§M.4.4.5 ¶3) | An `@ci-gate-override:` annotation is syntactically well-formed and cites a known `{gate_id}`, but the catalog row's `override_path` cell forbids override. The `<rule>` token in the `not_permitted_<rule>` form names the binding contract (e.g., `not_permitted_gdpr_art_17`, `not_permitted_console_firewall`, `not_permitted_residency_lock`, `not_permitted_hero_moment_integrity`, `not_permitted_solo_surface_integrity`, `not_permitted_billing_singleton`, `not_permitted_closed_enum_integrity`, `not_permitted_vendor_identity_free_aggregate_invariant`). | Fix the underlying invariant violation (the override path is unavailable by design). The rejection comment names the `<rule>` token and links to the spec section that authors the invariant. Appeal path: file a discussion with the spec-ops oncall — invariant relaxation requires a full Authored Extension ratification, not a per-PR override. | §M.4.4.5 ¶3; D-11.2-011 V11 closure; AE-V11-06. |
| `override_coupled_gate_unknown` | Any §M.5 row whose `override_path` cell declares `coupled_with:<other_gate_id>` (§M.4.4.5 ¶4) | The `<other_gate_id>` cited in the catalog row's `override_path` cell does not resolve to a §M.5 catalog row. Detected at gate boot (catalog-load time) AND at override-apply time as part of the `appendix_m5_self_consistency` meta-gate cluster. | Fix the catalog row's `override_path` cell to cite a `<other_gate_id>` that exists in the §M.5 catalog, OR author the missing coupled gate in the same PR. The §M.5 catalog self-consistency meta-gate enforces this invariant at every PR touching the catalog. | §M.4.4.5 ¶4; v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 Counterfactual #3 closure; AE-V72REM-09. |
| `override_requires_audit_event_kind_unknown` | Any §M.5 row whose `override_path` cell declares `requires_audit_event:<event_kind>` (§M.4.4.5 ¶5) | The `<event_kind>` cited in the catalog row's `override_path` cell is not a member of the Appendix J `audit_event_kind` enum. Detected at gate boot (catalog-load time). | Fix the catalog row's `override_path` cell to cite an `<event_kind>` registered in Appendix J `audit_event_kind`, OR register the new event kind in Appendix J and §31 / Appendix C catalogs in the same PR. | §M.4.4.5 ¶5; v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 hardening; AE-V72REM-09. |
| `orphan_inline_gate_reference` | `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` (§M.4.2 trigger #12) | An inline `` Appendix M.5 `<gate_id>` `` citation in the Master Spec body resolves to a `<gate_id>` absent from the §M.5 catalog row set. | Add a §M.5 catalog row for each cited gate in the same diff, OR remove the inline `Appendix M.5` placement claim. | §M.4.2 trigger #12; D-11.3-002 V11 closure; AE-V11-06. |
| `parse_error` | `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` (§M.4.2 / §M.4.3) | The post-edit Markdown parse tree cannot be constructed (malformed table; orphan anchor; broken frontmatter). | Fix the parse error surfaced in the rejection comment. The detector cites the offending line and character offset. | §M.4.3; AE-V11-06. |
| `comment_post_failed` | `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` (§M.4.3.1) | The GitHub API is degraded and the gate cannot post the inline review comment. The gate falls **closed** (fail-secure); the gate run is marked `comment_post_failed` and the PR is blocked from merge until either the comment post succeeds on retry (exponential backoff: 1s / 4s / 16s / 64s / 256s; max 5 retries) or the spec-ops oncall manually unblocks via `@ci-gate-comment-post-bypass:` annotation. | Wait for GitHub API recovery and let the retry sequence run, OR spec-ops oncall posts `@ci-gate-comment-post-bypass: {gate_run_id} — {rationale}` to unblock manually. | §M.4.3.1; AE-V11-06. |
| `comment_post_bypass_applied` | `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` (§M.4.3.1) | The spec-ops oncall has posted a `@ci-gate-comment-post-bypass:` annotation for a `comment_post_failed` run. The bypass is itself audit-logged. | n/a — informational only; routed to the §M.4.6 nightly digest under the "Bypasses applied" panel for human review. | §M.4.3.1; AE-V11-06. |

**Cross-references and CI gate pairings.**

- All eleven codes above are paired with `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` (§M.5 Phase V11 cluster, runtime_active at v7.1.0, hardened v7.2.0-REM Phase 2) OR with any §M.5 catalog row that admits an override annotation. **Counterfactual coverage (v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 additions).** Each code above addresses at least one realistic failure mode documented in the §M.4.4.2.A counterfactual analysis (orphan annotation, typo'd concept name, prefix-substring near-match) or in the §M.4.4.5 Counterfactual #1 / #2 / #3 cluster (unknown gate, rationale too short, coupled-gate unknown). Authored in the V9 Phase 9 Verification spec-side remediation pass to land §6.8.4.3 (Cascade Class Coverage Registry), §6.8.4.4 (Marketplace-Aggregate Cascade Trigger), §6.8.4.5 (Bridge-Event Body Text PII Sweep), §6.8.4.6 (Partial-Failure Procedure), §42.4.1 (Residency-Bound Failover), §42.4.2 (Residency-Bound Backups), and the §40.2 retention authoritative-home pack. Closes D-9.2-007 / D-9.2-009 / D-9.2-011 / D-9.1R-014 / D-RES-001 / D-RES-002 P0; closes D-9.2-001 / D-9.2-002 / D-9.2-005 / D-9.2-006 / D-9.1R-* P1 cluster. Each code MUST round-trip through the §32 API error envelope; CI gate `error_code_catalog_completeness` (§M.4) asserts presence in this catalog.

#### DSAR Cascade Completeness Errors (§6.8.4.3 / §6.8.4.4 / §6.8.4.5 / §6.8.4.6)

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `dsar_cascade_class_assignment_missing` | 422 | The §6.8.4 cascade-plan generator resolved a §4 cascade target to a §6.8.4.3 row that does not exist (entity not registered in the Cascade Class Coverage Registry). Per §6.8.4.3 AC #2, plans missing class or pattern assignment for any subject-touching entity MUST be rejected. Error body carries `entity_type`, `entity_id`, `expected_section_anchor`. Resolve by adding the entity to the §6.8.4.3 registry and re-running the cascade plan. |
| `dsar_cascade_aggregate_recompute_failed` | 503 | The §6.8.4.4 synchronous Marketplace-aggregate recompute failed for one or more cohort tuples (Convex serializable-transaction conflict exceeded retries; Anthropic outage on the cohort scoring capability; § 4.4.18 / §4.4.12 / §4.4.15 / §4.4.16 entity-level recompute mutation transient). Per §6.8.4.4 AC #4 the cascade does NOT advance to `dsar.cascade.row_redacted`; cascade routes to §6.8.4.6 partial-failure path. Standard `Retry-After` header populated. Error body carries `failed_cohort_tuples[]`, `dependency_state`, and the `dsar_request_id`. |
| `dsar_cascade_body_pii_sweep_failed` | 503 | The §6.8.4.5 Bridge-Event Body Text PII sweep failed because the §48.4.4 PII detector pipeline is unavailable (Anthropic outage per §22.8 `anthropic_mcp_degraded` state) OR the detector returned an unparseable response on > 5% of bridge-event rows in the cascade plan. Per §6.8.4.5 AC #4 the cascade does NOT advance to `dsar.cascade.row_redacted`; cascade routes to §6.8.4.6 partial-failure path. Standard `Retry-After` header populated. Error body carries `failed_bridge_event_count`, `total_bridge_event_count`, `dependency_state`, and the `dsar_request_id`. |
| `dsar_cascade_partial_failure_sla_breach` | 503 | The §6.8.4.6 24-hour Ops-review SLA on a `dsar.cascade.partial_failure` pause was breached. Datadog alarm fires SEV-1; PagerDuty pages on the `dsar-ops-escalation` queue (Privacy Officer + Engineering Director). Per §6.8.4.6 AC #2 the breach MUST trigger §6.8.6 +60-day extension auto-escalation if cumulative pause-duration breaches the 30-day window. Error body carries `pause_started_at`, `sla_deadline`, `dsar_request_id`. |
| `dsar_cascade_resume_missing_required_fields` | 422 | `dsar.cascade.resume` event payload missing one or more required fields (`actor_user_id`, `ops_session_id`, `rationale`, `remediation_action`, `audit_event_id`). Per §6.8.4.6 AC #3. Error body identifies the missing fields. |
| `dsar_cascade_resume_dual_signoff_required` | 403 | `dsar.cascade.resume` invoked with `remediation_action = skip_rows_with_documented_exemption` but the second signer is missing OR the second signer is the same actor as the original triage actor (separation-of-duties violation). Per §6.8.4.6 AC #4 + §6.8.6.2 manifestly-unfounded path precedent. Error body carries `triage_actor_user_id`, the proposed second-signer `user_id`, and the resolution path. |
| `restore_from_dsar_excluded_snapshot_blocked` | 403 | A backup-restore operation targets a snapshot ID that is in the `dsar_excluded_snapshots` set (per §42.4.2 — the snapshot captured pre-pseudonym predecessors and was excluded from restore eligibility post-DSAR cascade rather than re-pseudonymized). Per §42.4.2 AC #5. Error body carries `snapshot_id`, `excluded_at`, `dsar_request_id`, and the resolution path (use a non-excluded snapshot or initiate a re-pseudonymization request). |

#### Residency-Bound DR Errors (§42.4.1 / §42.4.2)

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `residency_failover_blocked` | 503 | A write request was issued during a `paused_partial_failure` failover state where both the same-residency primary and replica are unavailable. Per §42.4.1, cross-residency failover is forbidden by Convex deployment configuration; the platform degrades to read-only on writes rather than failing over cross-residency. Standard `Retry-After` header populated (typically with the same-residency replica recovery ETA). Error body carries `residency_region`, `primary_state`, `replica_state`, `expected_recovery_at`. The customer-visible Workspace banner reads "Service degraded — read-only — your region's failover replica is recovering." |
| `residency_backup_replication_blocked` | 422 | An IaC apply (Terraform / Convex deployment configuration) was rejected because an S3 replication policy or Convex backup-replication rule targets a cross-residency replica without explicit DPA-addendum + DPO approval per §42.4.2. Per §42.4.2 AC #2. Error body carries `source_bucket_residency`, `replica_target_residency`, `iac_resource_path`. Resolve by either correcting the replica target to same-residency OR obtaining DPA-addendum + DPO sign-off and emitting `org.residency.cross_region_replica_approved` AuditEvent prior to the IaC apply. |

### v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 Additions (2026-05-20) — P0 Residency & Legal-Entity Reconciliation + Stripe-Customer Atomic-Binding {#appendix-i-v72rem-phase-5}

v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 remediation closure batch (D-RES-004 P0 numerical_singleton; D-RES-015 P1 consistency_drift sibling; D-V14-007 P2 cross-flag — all closed in-place 2026-05-20). New error code registrations follow Appendix I preamble conventions; each row carries explicit `http`, `retryable`, `used_by`, `localization_key` per the V8.4 row schema. Authority anchors: §34.10.5.A Stripe-Customer Atomic-Binding Protocol (invariants #1, #3, #5, #7; ACs #1, #6, #7); §4.8.1 AC #14a / #14b (Residency-Locked Invoicing); §M.5.17 CI gates.

**Stripe-Customer Atomic-Binding family** (closes D-RES-004; binds §34.10.5.A invariants #1 + #7 + AC #1; §M.5.17 CI gate `legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_test` sub-assertion (c) + Datadog synthetic monitor `legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_monitor`):

- `stripe_customer_active_duplicate` — HTTP 422; `permanent`; non-retryable. The Convex `(org_id, legal_entity)` unique index on `Organization.stripe_customer_id_active` rejects any mutation that would result in two active Stripe Customers keyed on the same `(org_id, legal_entity)` pair per §34.10.5.A invariant #1. The error fires when (a) the Organization-write transaction at step (iv) of the §34.10.5.A invariant #3 5-step atomic protocol attempts to stamp `stripe_customer_id_active` on an Organization row already carrying a distinct active Customer ID under the same `legal_entity`, or (b) a faulty Ops-Finance correction-path invocation (invariant #6) attempts to mint a parallel active Customer without first transitioning the legacy Customer to `closed_for_new_invoices` via `stripe_customer_id_historical[]`. Remediation requires either (i) reaching out to Ops Finance for an atomic-rebinding via the §34.10.5.A invariant #6 correction path, or (ii) waiting for the in-flight residency-change transaction to complete (the row-level lock at invariant #3 step (i) serializes concurrent attempts). Used by: §32 `POST /v1/organizations/{org_id}/residency-migration-requests` (D-RES-007 forward-tracked); Convex Organization-write mutation layer; Ops Finance correction-path mutation. Localization key: `error.billing.stripe_customer_active_duplicate`. Authority anchor: §34.10.5.A invariant #1 + AC #1.

- `org_residency_change_stripe_api_failure` — HTTP 502; `transient`; retryable via Stripe API idempotency-key convention (`(org_id, legal_entity_new, mutation_timestamp_minute)` per §34.10.5.A invariant #7). The error fires when the Stripe `Customer.create` API call at step (iii) of the §34.10.5.A invariant #3 5-step atomic protocol returns a Stripe-side error (network timeout; Stripe outage; Stripe 5xx response). The entire Convex mutation is rolled back per invariant #3 atomic-rollback semantics; the Organization row is restored to its pre-transaction state. An OpsActionRecord audit row is written with `outcome = stripe_api_failure` and `failure_reason = <Stripe error code>` capturing the originating Stripe API error code. Customer-facing Org Settings UI surfaces a retryable error with copy authored under AE-V72REM-PH5-01 (UX Lead authoring pending v7.1.1 stamp; placeholder copy: "We couldn't update your data residency due to a temporary issue with our billing provider. Please try again in a few minutes."). Retry within the §32 idempotency-key window (default 24 hours per §32.5) resolves the residency-change attempt without creating a duplicate Stripe Customer per Stripe API idempotency semantics. Used by: §32 residency-change endpoint (forward); Convex Organization-write mutation layer step (iii); Ops Finance correction-path mutation. Localization key: `error.billing.org_residency_change_stripe_api_failure`. Authority anchor: §34.10.5.A invariant #7.

**Residency-Change Eligibility family** (closes D-RES-004 paired with D-RES-007 forward-track; binds §34.10.5.A invariant #3 step (ii); §M.5.17 CI gate `legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_test` sub-assertion (b)):

- `org_residency_change_eligibility_predicate_violated` — HTTP 409; `permanent` until predicate clears (Sourcera-Error-Subkind `state_conflict_strict`); the response envelope MUST carry the `Sourcera-Error-Detail` extension naming the violated predicate from the closed set: `bid_workspace_active_phase_7_through_13`, `ai_operation_pending_settlement`, `dsar_request_in_flight`, `outcome_contract_in_renewal_window`. The error fires when an Organization-write transaction attempting to change `data_residency_region` is rejected at step (ii) of the §34.10.5.A invariant #3 5-step atomic protocol because at least one eligibility predicate fails. The predicate set is the §1.6.1 closed set (v7.1.1 stamp authoring per D-RES-007); the Phase 5 closure registers the error code with cross-reference targets in place, with body-side §1.6.1 predicate enumeration owed at v7.1.1 stamp. The error notifies the Org Owner via Loops.so transactional template `lo_org_residency_change_blocked` (registered with this Phase 5 closure) enumerating the violated predicate(s) and the remediation path (close in-flight Bid Workspaces; wait for `pending` AIOperations to settle; close DSAR; etc.). Retry: not until the violated predicate clears (the operator must take a remediation action; auto-retry is not safe and will produce identical 409 responses). Used by: §32 residency-change endpoint (forward); Convex Organization-write mutation layer step (ii). Localization key: `error.residency.org_residency_change_eligibility_predicate_violated`. Authority anchor: §34.10.5.A invariant #3 step (ii) + AC #6; §1.6.1 (v7.1.1 stamp authoring).

**`custom`-Residency Sub-Classification family** (closes D-RES-004 `custom`-cohort fail-closed regression; binds §34.10.5.A AC #7 + invariant #5; §M.5.17 CI gate `org_custom_residency_label_required`):

- `organization_custom_residency_label_required` — HTTP 422; `permanent`; non-retryable until the caller provides a non-null `custom_sovereign_residency_label`. The §4.1.1 Organization-write validator rejects any POST or PATCH that sets `data_residency_region = custom` with `custom_sovereign_residency_label = null` (or missing from the request body). The `custom_sovereign_residency_label` field is the canonical sub-classification driver for the §34.10.5.A invariant #5 `custom`-residency Stripe Customer keying — without the label, the Stripe Customer cannot be metadata-disambiguated from other `custom`-residency Customers under the same `legal_entity = sourcera_custom` enum value. Remediation: re-submit the mutation with a non-null label from the §4.1.1 example set (`uk_crown_secure`, `de_sovereign_cloud`, `au_irap_protected`, etc.) or a contract-negotiated label per the Enterprise sovereign-cloud agreement. Used by: §4.1.1 Organization-write handler (Org-creation + residency-change paths); Ops Finance correction-path mutation. Localization key: `error.residency.organization_custom_residency_label_required`. Authority anchor: §34.10.5.A AC #7; §M.5.17 CI gate `org_custom_residency_label_required`.

**Forward-Tracked code (cross-reference target landed; body authoring owed at v7.1.1 stamp per D-RES-007).**

- `org_residency_change_blocked_by_active_dsar` — HTTP 409; `permanent` until DSAR closes (Sourcera-Error-Subkind `state_conflict_strict`). Registration anchor: §34.10.5.A AC #5 cross-reference. Body authoring is owed at v7.1.1 stamp jointly with the §1.6.1 D-RES-007 closure (the DSAR deadlock-resolution rule lands at §6.8 in the v7.1.1 stamp); the Phase 5 closure registers the code identifier and the cross-reference target so any downstream consumer (§32 endpoint, Convex validator, Loops.so template) can cite the code without waiting for the §1.6.1 body. Used by: §32 residency-change endpoint (forward); §6.8 DSAR cascade interaction (forward).

## Appendix J: Controlled Vocabulary Registry {#appendix-j-controlled-vocabulary-registry}

**All enum values used throughout the specification are canonically defined here. Section 3 schema definitions must reference these values exactly.**

### Response Types

`boolean`, `qualitative`, `evidence`, `informational`, `pricing`

### TCO Pricing Model

`perpetual`, `subscription`, `consumption`, `custom`

### Rubric Grade Categories

| Grade | Code | Value | Default PM (if PM mode) | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Fully Meets | FM | 1.0 | 100% | Vendor response meets requirement fully, out of box |
| Partially Meets | PM | 0.6 (configurable per workspace, default) | Configurable (0.1-0.9) | Vendor response meets requirement partially; requires customization or integration |
| Does Not Meet | DNM | 0.0 | 0% | Vendor response does not meet requirement |
| Exception | EX | Excluded | — | Requirement scored as exception (excluded from vendor comparison, flagged in report) |

### Global Organization Roles

`org_owner`, `org_admin`, `billing_admin`, `member`, `guest`

**Notes.**
- `billing_admin` (added v7.0.0; §5.2, §5.2.1, §4.8, §34.12.6) — org-scoped, console-pooled billing & AI-accounting authority; orthogonal to `org_admin` (a user MAY hold both, but neither implies the other). See §5.2.1 for the full operation-level permission list and the Replacement Pattern that lets `org_owner` retain de facto Billing Admin authority when the role pool is empty.
- `org_owner` retains de facto Billing Admin authority by fallback per §5.2.1.2 even when the Org has zero `billing_admin` users — this is enforced at the API layer, not at the enum level.
- `member` and `guest` are NEVER Billing-Admin-eligible by direct grant — granting `billing_admin` to a `guest` is rejected with HTTP 422 `billing_admin_grant_target_ineligible_role` (new; Appendix I) per §5.2.1.2 Assignment.

### Workspace Roles

`workspace_owner`, `workspace_admin`, `use_case_lead`, `reviewer`, `guest`

### Team Roles

`team_owner`, `team_lead`, `team_member`

### console_modes_active (§4.2.1 Organization)

`buyer_only`, `seller_only`, `both`

**Notes.** Org-level activation discriminator. Distinct from Appendix J `console`, which is the per-entity scope discriminator. `buyer_only` requires `buyer_plan_tier` non-null and `seller_plan_tier` null; `seller_only` requires the inverse; `both` requires both per-console plan fields and drives unified billing-statement assembly per §34.

### console (§4 per-entity scope discriminator)

`buyer`, `seller`

**Notes.** Per-entity scope discriminator used by console-scoped rows such as Team, Workspace, Bid Workspace, Audit Event projections, Capability Declaration, and Marketplace-adjacent seller entities. Distinct from `console_modes_active` (§4.2.1 Org-level activation) and `ops_session_console_scope` (§4.6.3 Ops-session targeting). New console-scoped entities MUST cite this enum rather than restating `buyer | seller` inline.

### kb_entry_dsar_body_redaction_state (§22.3.1 KBEntry)

`none`, `redaction_started`, `reindex_pending`, `redacted`, `redaction_failed`

**Notes.** Tracks third-party DSAR body-redaction lifecycle for KBEntry `body_markdown`. `redaction_started` and `reindex_pending` are retrieval-exclusion states; `redacted` means the body, vector index, and BM25 index have all been updated; `redaction_failed` pauses retrieval and routes to Ops under §6.8.4.6 partial-failure procedure.

### user_lifecycle_status (§4.2.3 User)

`active`, `deprovisioned`, `guest_pending_acceptance`, `deletion_pending`

**Notes.** `active` users may authenticate subject to §6.1–§6.3. `deprovisioned` users are audit tombstones with sessions revoked. `guest_pending_acceptance` is written by §6.5 invite creation before magic-link redemption. `deletion_pending` starts the §6.8.3 reflection window before pure-PII hard-delete / tombstone preservation.

### mfa_factor_kind (§4.2.8 MfaEnrollment)

`totp`, `webauthn`

### mfa_enrollment_state (§4.2.8 MfaEnrollment; §6.2.5)

`enrolling`, `enrolled_with_recovery_codes_unused`, `enrolled_with_recovery_codes_partially_consumed`, `disabled`

**Notes.** The generic phrase `enrolled` in §6.2 means either of the two enrolled states above. Recovery-code regeneration returns the row to `enrolled_with_recovery_codes_unused`; factor removal / reset / DSAR transitions to `disabled`.

### mfa_factor_revoked_reason (§4.2.8 MfaEnrollment)

`user_self_remove`, `admin_reset`, `ops_reset`, `dsar`, `account_closure`

### guest_invite_kind (§4.2.9 GuestInvite)

`org_guest`, `workspace_guest`, `bid_workspace_guest`

### guest_permission_profile (§4.2.9 GuestInvite)

`read_only`, `contributor`, `scorer`, `full_participant`

`pending`, `accepted`, `expired`, `revoked`

`saml`, `oidc`, `scim_only`, `email_password_only`

### workos_provisioning_state (§4.2.10 WorkOSConnection)

`pending`, `active`, `suspended`, `revoked`

Retained verbatim for Phase 4 back-compat documentation. MUST NOT be used for new writes on or after v7.0.0 deploy. ### Workspace Statuses

`draft`, `active`, `suspended`, `closed`, `archived`

**Notes.** Canonical Workspace lifecycle states are governed by Appendix E Workspace Status. Cancellation uses the §10.14 cancellation workflow and audit events; `canceled` / `cancelled` are not valid `workspace_status` values for new writes.

### `workspace_closure_reason` (§4.3.1 / §10.13 / §10.18)

`phase_13_completed`, `no_vendor_response`

**Notes.** Required when `Workspace.status=closed`. `phase_13_completed` is written only by §10.13 normal closure after Selection Record creation. `no_vendor_response` is written only by §10.18 and MUST NOT create a Selection Report, Selection Record, Defense View, or §10.14 cancellation lifecycle.

### `EvaluationOwnerMode` (§4.3.1 Workspace)

`solo`, `team`

**Notes.** Drives Workspace surface compression per Principle 9 (§3.13). `solo` = single-operator compressed surface (Phase 14.4 authoring); `team` = full multi-stakeholder surface as authored in §3.3 and §10. Plan-default behavior on Workspace create is defined in §4.3.1 (Free + Solo plan tiers default `solo`; Starter+ default `team`); never restated inline elsewhere. Transition rule (`solo → team` always allowed; `team → solo` blocked when stakeholders or guests are present) is authored in §4.3.1 and enforced by the Phase Advancement and Workspace Settings APIs. The literal enum strings MUST NOT surface in the UI — Appendix M row binds the surface metaphor. Audit-event action namespace: `workspace_evaluation_owner_mode_changed` is registered under §4.6.1 Audit Event action registry for `entity_type=workspace`.

### Bid Workspace Statuses

`draft`, `active`, `submitted`, `closed`, `disqualified`

**Notes.** `disqualified` added v7.0.0 per §25.3 Disqualification formalization. Terminal absent reversal per Appendix E Bid Workspace Status state machine. Reversal (within 72h by Workspace Owner OR by Ops Compliance post-72h) restores the Bid Workspace to its pre-disqualification status per §4.7.2 Reversal and §25.3.3 state machine. Phase 13 (Closed) on the parent Workspace does NOT transition a `disqualified` Bid Workspace to `closed` — archive integrity is preserved per §4.7.2 AC #12.

### `vendor_disqualification_audit_action` (§25.3.5)

`disqualified`, `disqualification_reversed`, `disqualification_appeal_submitted`, `disqualification_appeal_decided_upheld`, `disqualification_appeal_decided_overturned`, `disqualification_cascade_completed`, `disqualification_cascade_partial_failure`, `disqualification_notification_sent`, `disqualification_notification_failed`, `disqualification_notification_suppressed_silent`, `disqualification_body_edited_before_dispatch`, `disqualification_notification_style_overridden`

**Notes.** Audit Event `action` values valid only when `entity_type=vendor_disqualification_record`. Registered under the §4.6.1 Audit Event action registry per-entity-type namespace. Any new value requires a corresponding §25.3 behavior entry AND an update to the `audit_event_action_enum_union_validator` CI test surface.

### `vendor_disqualification_cascade_status` (§4.7.2)

`pending`, `in_progress`, `complete`, `partial_failure`

**Notes.** Value on `VendorDisqualificationRecord.cascade_status`. `pending` is the initial state between row insert and cascade worker pickup (typically < 200 ms); `in_progress` during the synchronous cascade; `complete` on successful completion of all cascade actions; `partial_failure` when at least one cascade action has exhausted its retry curve. `partial_failure` is recoverable via Ops manual re-drive; registered separately for Ops alerting.

### `response_lock_reason` (§25.3.3; Appendix D extension)

`phase_9_submissions_closed`, `disqualification_cascade`, `workspace_cancelled`, `ops_emergency_freeze`

**Notes.** Populated on Bid Response rows when `status=locked`. Distinguishes the five lock paths so the disqualification-reversal cascade (§25.3.4) only unlocks rows it itself locked. Backfill default: `phase_9_submissions_closed` (the dominant historical lock path). Reversal worker MUST filter on `lock_reason = disqualification_cascade` before unlocking; other lock_reasons MUST NOT be touched by disqualification reversal.

### Plan Tiers

The v6.0.0 single-console enum (`free`, `business`, `enterprise`) was split into two per-console enums in v7.0.0 per §34.1.3 (Phase 4 Pricing Rewrite Track), and the **Solo tier was added to both consoles in Phase 14.9** under the v7.1 integration program.

**Buyer plan tier** enum (`buyer_plan_tier`):

`buyer_free`, `buyer_solo`, `business_starter`, `business_growth`, `business_scale`, `buyer_enterprise`

**Seller plan tier** enum (`seller_plan_tier`):

`seller_free`, `seller_solo`, `seller_starter`, `seller_growth`, `seller_scale`, `seller_enterprise`

**Authoritative cell values** for each enum value live in §34.1.1 (Buyer) and §34.1.2 (Seller). The `buyer_solo` and `seller_solo` enum values were authored as forward-references in Phases 14.4 / 14.5 / 14.6 with operational aliasing to `business_starter` / `seller_starter` until Phase 14.9 landed. Phase 14.9 makes both values authoritative; the `business_starter` / `seller_starter` alias is retired and the inline §4.8.2 alias note ("aliases to `business_starter` until then") is removed.

**Backward compatibility.** A v6.0.0 `Organization.plan_tier` value of `free` migrates to `buyer_plan_tier=buyer_free` AND `seller_plan_tier=seller_free`; `business` migrates to `buyer_plan_tier=business_growth` AND `seller_plan_tier=seller_free` (with a 12-month annual-contract grandfather per §34.2.3 #9); `enterprise` migrates to `buyer_plan_tier=buyer_enterprise` AND `seller_plan_tier=seller_free` unless an active seller-side commit is present, in which case both sides migrate to Enterprise. The migration is a Breaking Change logged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Breaking Changes`. Solo did NOT exist in v6.0.0 and has no pre-image; v6 → v7 migrations never produce a Solo enum value automatically (Solo is opt-in on the buyer / seller console at upgrade time only).
