### API Token Scopes

**Canonical source (D-1.1-015 closure, 2026-06-21).** This section is the single authoritative `api_token_scope` value registry. §6.6.3 and endpoint tables MUST cite this registry; they MUST NOT publish divergent inline scope vocabularies.

`read:workspaces`, `write:workspaces`, `admin:workspaces`, `read:requirements`, `write:requirements`, `read:responses`, `write:responses`, `read:scores`, `write:scores`, `read:billing`, `write:billing`, `admin:billing`, `export:billing`, `export:kb`, `read:kb`, `write:kb`, `admin:integrations`, `read:vendor_opt_outs`, `write:vendor_opt_outs`, `read:vendor_opt_out_authority`, `write:vendor_opt_out_authority`, `export:audit_events`, `admin:ops_compliance`

**Legacy migration map.** Pre-V3 tokens with `bidding:write`, `evaluation:read`, `scoring:write`, `responses:read`, or `analytics:read` are migrated on first authentication and audit-logged with action `org.api_token_scope_migrated`. Mappings: `bidding:write -> write:workspaces`; `evaluation:read -> read:requirements`; `scoring:write -> write:scores`; `responses:read -> read:responses`; `analytics:read -> read:workspaces` unless the token's only consumer is billing analytics, in which case Org Owner re-issuance is required for `read:billing`.

**Workspace / seller authority scope semantics.**

| Scope | Grants | Required For |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `read:workspaces` | Buyer-workspace read APIs and read-only M1-M5 artifact listing | §32.5 / M1-M5 GET endpoints |
| `write:workspaces` | Workspace mutation APIs, invite issue/revoke, public-report publish/revoke, evaluation-certificate publish, M4/M5 conversion flows | §32.5 / M1-M5 POST/PATCH/DELETE endpoints |
| `admin:workspaces` | High-trust workspace actions where a Workspace Owner override or owner-reversal path is permitted | Vendor-disqualification and reversal paths that explicitly cite `admin:workspaces` |
| `read:vendor_opt_outs` | Vendor Opt-Out Record list and detail reads | §27.10.6 GET `/v1/opt-outs` endpoints |
| `write:vendor_opt_outs` | Vendor Opt-Out Record creation and revocation | §27.10.6 POST / DELETE `/v1/opt-outs` endpoints |
| `read:vendor_opt_out_authority` | VendorOptOutAuthorityAttestation list and detail reads | §27.10.6 GET authority-attestation endpoints |
| `write:vendor_opt_out_authority` | Seller authority-attestation creation, DNS probe request, and revocation | §27.10.6 authority-attestation mutation endpoints |
| `admin:ops_compliance` | Ops-compliance-only post-window reversal path | §4.7.2 post-72-hour reversal path; not issuable through customer self-serve token creation |
| `export:audit_events` | Audit-event export endpoint | §32 audit-event export endpoint |
| `export:kb` | KB export endpoint, plan-tier invariant | §22.18.1 / §32 KB export endpoints |
| `read:kb` / `write:kb` | KB read/write API families when exposed to API-token callers | §22 KB API surfaces |
| `admin:integrations` | Integration administration APIs | §31 / §32 integration administration surfaces |

### API Rate-Limit Classes

**Canonical source (D-V8.1-011 closure, 2026-06-21).** This section registers the closed Appendix J enum `api_rate_limit_class`. The binding contract and numerical cells live in §32.4.5 Rate-Limit Class Registry; this Appendix J block is the controlled-vocabulary mirror used by validators and endpoint-schema generation.

`standard_authenticated_per_org`, `public_pricing_unauth`, `marketplace_public_unauth`, `dsar_subject_request`, `data_mutation`, `workspace_read`, `ai_invocation`, `internal_comment_api`, `kb_export_request`, `kb_export_poll`, `marketplace_match_score_read`, `marketplace_match_score_batch`, `marketplace_taxonomy_read`, `seller_signals_standard`, `vendor_opt_out_standard`, `marketplace_read`, `marketplace_write`, `ops_marketplace_admin`, `crm_sync_standard`, `crm_sync_read_heavy`, `billing_read`, `billing_mutation`, `billing_export`, `audit_events_export`, `ops_console`, `growth_domain`, `marketplace_content_admin`, `ops_taxonomy`, `ops_analytics`, `ops_sim_mutation`, `analytics_read`, `analytics_export`

**Semantics.** Endpoint `Rate-Limit Class` cells MUST use one value from this enum and MUST cite §32.4.5 for the applied limits. API-token scopes remain governed by Appendix J `api_token_scope`; values such as `marketplace_read`, `marketplace_write`, and `marketplace_match_score_read` are rate-limit classes only and are invalid in Auth Scope columns.

**Billing Scope Semantics (§32.8 — added Phase 4c).**

| Scope | Grants | Required For (§32.8 endpoints) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `read:billing` | All read endpoints in §32.8 (current Org only; cross-Org reads remain Ops-only via `ops_finance_admin` outside the public API) | `GET /v1/pricing` (no auth required, but tokens that send the header are not rejected); `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/wallet`; `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/ai-operations`; `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/ai-operations/{op_id}`; `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/free-allowance`; `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/committed-spend` |
| `write:billing` | All `read:billing` rights PLUS wallet-configuration mutations | `POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/wallet/cap`; `POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/wallet/auto-topup` |
| `admin:billing` | All `write:billing` rights PLUS contest filing AND any future high-trust mutation (manual top-up initiation, plan-tier change, CommittedSpend opt-out — endpoint paths catalogued under §32.5 Billing implicit-Org aliases at §5.2.1.1; explicit-Org canonical paths to be authored in a follow-up integration phase per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` → Known Gaps) | `POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/ai-operations/{op_id}/contest` |

**Implication Rule.** `admin:billing` ⊃ `write:billing` ⊃ `read:billing`. A token granted only `admin:billing` MAY perform any §32.8 read or write operation. Implication is enforced server-side; the API does NOT require clients to enumerate all three scopes when granting `admin:billing`.

**Back-Fill Rule (one-shot at v7.0.0 deploy per §32.8.0).** API tokens issued before v7.0.0 deploy are back-filled at the first authentication after deploy: tokens whose owning user holds `org_owner` OR `billing_admin` receive `read:billing` only; other tokens receive no billing scopes. Explicit re-issuance is required for `write:billing` or `admin:billing` — preserving least-privilege at upgrade.

**RBAC Cross-Reference.** Holding a token with `read:billing` is necessary but NOT sufficient for the §5.2.1.1 RBAC checks: the token's owning user MUST also hold one of the role(s) listed in the endpoint's RBAC row. A `read:billing` token whose owning user is a `member` (no billing role) returns HTTP 403 `wallet_role_forbidden` on `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/wallet`; the user-role check runs after the scope check.

### Audit Event Action Types

**Bare-verb enum (non-billing entity audits).** The following verbs are the canonical `action` values for Audit Event rows whose `entity_type` is a non-billing entity (workspace, use case, requirement, response, score, selection report, bid workspace, bid response, KB entry, capability declaration, marketplace listing, EOI, NDA, seller signal, CRM sync row, taxonomy node, vocab tag proposal, abuse report, etc.):

`created`, `updated`, `deleted`, `archived`, `submitted`, `approved`, `rejected`, `advanced_phase`, `reverted`, `amended`, `signed`, `exported`

**Enum Extension — `billing_admin_action` Namespace (§5.2, §5.2.1, §5.2.1.4).** The bare-verb enum above is EXTENDED — not replaced — by the qualified-string `billing_admin_action` namespace registered in the next subsection (`Billing Admin Audit Action Types`). Qualified strings follow the form `org.<billing_subdomain>_<verb>` (e.g., `org.wallet_viewed`, `org.contest_filed`, `org.plan_changed`) and are the ONLY valid `action` values for Audit Event rows whose `entity_type` ∈ {`ai_wallet`, `contest_record`, `committed_spend_contract`, `pricing_table_version`, `pro_trial_seat_grant`, `trial_state`, `organization_plan`, `free_allowance_counter`, `billing_seat_snapshot`, `downgrade_excess_data_bucket`, `billing_admin_role_assignment`, `audit_event_view`}. The write-time validator at §4.6.1 MUST accept the union of both enums; implementations that whitelist only the bare-verb enum MUST be treated as a blocking deploy bug. QA test `audit_event_action_enum_union_validator` asserts that a write of `action = 'org.wallet_viewed'` against `entity_type = 'ai_wallet'` succeeds, that a write of `action = 'created'` against `entity_type = 'ai_wallet'` fails with HTTP 422 `audit_event_action_namespace_mismatch` (new; Appendix I), and that a write of `action = 'org.wallet_viewed'` against `entity_type = 'workspace'` also fails with the same error (the two namespaces are mutually exclusive per `entity_type`).

**Deploy-Time Validator Rules.** Per the §5.2.1.6 acceptance-criteria family, a deploy-time validator MUST assert: (1) every qualified action emitted by §5.2.1.1 Permission List Operations is present in the Billing Admin Audit Action Types registry; (2) every registry entry is emitted by at least one code path (audit-action-dead-code check); (3) the bare-verb enum does not contain any dotted string; (4) the qualified namespace does not contain any bare verb. The validator runs in CI against the production Convex schema and fails the build on drift.

**Cross-Reference.** The `billing_admin_action` namespace is used by the Billing Admin Audit View filter at §5.2.1.4 (regex `^org\.(wallet|contest|committed_spend|plan|solo_trial|pro_trial_seat|billing|downgrade_bucket|free_allowance|pricing|scim_billing|billing_admin)_*`), the PostHog event mirror in Appendix G, and the webhook event emission in §31.8 / Appendix C.

The `billing_admin_action` namespace registers the qualified action enum used for every Billing Admin Audit View row (§5.2.1.4). Action strings follow the dotted form `org.<billing_subdomain>_<verb>`. The full enum is partitioned by subdomain:

`org.pro_trial_seat_allocated`, `org.pro_trial_seat_granted`, `org.pro_trial_seat_accepted`, `org.pro_trial_seat_declined`, `org.pro_trial_seat_acceptance_rejected`, `org.pro_trial_seat_converted`, `org.pro_trial_seat_auto_downgraded`, `org.pro_trial_seat_quota_overridden`, `org.pro_trial_seat_revoked_by_buyer`

**Billing Admin Audit View Self-Reference (§5.2.1.4):**

`org.billing_audit_viewed`, `org.billing_audit_exported`

**Semantics:**

- Every action above is an Audit Event entity row (§4.6.1) with `action` = the qualified string above (the field's bare-verb enum is extended via this namespace; the bare-verb enum continues to govern non-billing entity audits unchanged).
- `status` ∈ `success`, `failure` per §4.6.1; on failure the action string is preserved and `failure_reason` populated.
- `entity_type` MUST be one of: `ai_wallet`, `contest_record`, `committed_spend_contract`, `pricing_table_version`, `pro_trial_seat_grant`, `trial_state`, `organization_plan`, `free_allowance_counter`, `billing_seat_snapshot`, `downgrade_excess_data_bucket`, `billing_admin_role_assignment`, `audit_event_view`. The `entity_type` enum in §4.6.1 is extended accordingly (Authored Extension; logged in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md`).
- `changes` JSON populated for state mutations (per §4.6.1); for read actions (`*_viewed`), `changes` is `{}` and `notes` carries the query-filter snapshot for forensic re-execution.
- Notification dispatches (§5.2.1.1 Operation #22) are NOT audit-logged at the recipient level; the underlying state-change event (e.g., `org.wallet_overage_enabled`) is the audit anchor.
- Retention: standard per §40.2 plan-tier defaults, with `org.contest_*` and `org.committed_spend_*` rows retained for 7 years on every plan (financial-record exception per §40.2 `extended_financial`).
- DSAR / right-to-erasure: per §6.8 the user attribution fields (`user_id`, `created_by`) anonymize on request; the action and `entity_id` survive (financial-record exception). For `billing_admin_role_assignment` audits, the deprovisioned user's `user_id` is replaced with the synthetic `anonymized_former_user_<hash>` token to preserve the role-change trail without exposing the deprovisioned identity.

### Referral Status

`pending`, `signed_up`, `activated`, `credit_issued`, `credit_redeemed`, `credit_expired`, `forfeited`, `flagged_fraud`, `revoked`

**Semantics:**

- `pending` — referral created, no signup yet.
- `signed_up` — referee Org provisioned, activation threshold not yet met.
- `activated` — referee met minimum-activity threshold; eligible for credit issuance on next nightly job.
- `credit_issued` — credit posted to referrer wallet; `credit_issued_at` populated.
- `credit_redeemed` — `credit_redeemed_usd = credit_value_usd` (fully used); Stripe Credit Notes captured.
- `credit_expired` — `credit_expires_at` passed with residual credit; residual forfeit.
- `forfeited` — credit withheld due to fraud or eligibility violation; `credit_forfeited_reason` populated.
- `flagged_fraud` — Signal Integrity Monitor flagged; Ops review pending; credit suspended.
- `revoked` — Ops manual revocation post-issuance (distinct from forfeited, which is pre-issuance block).

### Referral Fraud Signals

`same_domain`, `same_payment_method`, `same_ip_range`, `bootstrapping_pattern`, `velocity_spike`

### Referral Forfeit Reasons

`fraud_suspected`, `payment_overlap`, `same_domain_violation`, `insufficient_activity`, `referee_opt_out`, `referee_exclusivity_claimed`

`referee_exclusivity_claimed` is set on a losing BuyerReferral row when another referral has already bound the referee Org at the `pending → signed_up` transition per §4.3.16 + Appendix L.2 (Referee Exclusivity Rule). Added in §48.7 integration.

### Pro Trial Seat Status

`issued`, `invite_sent`, `provisioned`, `in_trial`, `converted`, `auto_downgraded`, `vendor_declined`, `expired_unaccepted`, `buyer_revoked`, `fraud_blocked`

**Semantics:**

- `issued` — grant created; grant_code minted; invite not yet sent.
- `invite_sent` — vendor invite email dispatched via Loops.so.
- `provisioned` — vendor signed up; Seller Starter entitlements active; `trial_starts_at` set.
- `in_trial` — within 30-day trial window.
- `converted` — vendor converted to Seller Starter+ with payment method; `converted_at` + `converted_to_plan` set.
- `auto_downgraded` — day 31 reached with no conversion action; vendor downgraded to Seller Free; 90-day read-only preservation triggered.
- `vendor_declined` — vendor Billing Admin explicitly declined the grant during trial.
- `expired_unaccepted` — invite sent but vendor never signed up before 30-day invite TTL.
- `buyer_revoked` — buyer revoked grant before provisioning.
- `fraud_blocked` — Signal Integrity Monitor blocked; `anti_spam_hold_reason` populated.

### Legal Entity (§4.8.1, §4.8.3)

**Canonical 4-value set (post-Phase-2V D-AJ-004 + post-v7.2.0-REM-Phase-5 D-RES-004 reconciliation, 2026-05-20):**

`sourcera_us_llc`, `sourcera_eu_gmbh`, `sourcera_apac_pte`, `sourcera_custom`

**Mapping (deterministic from `data_residency_region`; total + surjective; closed set):**

- `us` → `sourcera_us_llc`
- `eu` → `sourcera_eu_gmbh`
- `apac` → `sourcera_apac_pte`
- `custom` → `sourcera_custom`

**Retired value: `sourcera_uk_ltd`.** Phase 2V D-AJ-004 retired the value from the envelope-facing `legal_entity_kind` enum (line 49596 sibling registration). v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 D-RES-004 closure (2026-05-20) propagates the retirement to (a) this body-side enum, (b) the §4.8.1 mapping table, (c) the §4.8.3 AIWallet `legal_entity` citation, (d) the §4.8.12 MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord `legal_entity` citation, (e) the Appendix K Glossary "Residency-Locked Invoicing" entry. UK-resident Orgs are routed through `sourcera_eu_gmbh` per the v7.0.0 pre-Phase-2V "subset of `eu`" treatment (now canonical), OR through `sourcera_custom` keyed on a `custom_sovereign_residency_label` of `uk_crown_secure` per §4.1.1 for UK-sovereign-cloud Enterprise contracts. Historical AIOperation / AIWallet / AIWalletLedgerEntry / MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord rows with `legal_entity='sourcera_uk_ltd'` settled prior to the v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 stamp are preserved verbatim per §4.8.1 Settlement Freeze + §40.2 7-year SOC-2 retention; the historical Stripe Customer attached to those legacy invoices remains in place per §34.10.5.A invariant #4. New writes against `sourcera_uk_ltd` are rejected at the Convex schema-validation layer; CI gate `legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_test` (Appendix M.5 §M.5.17) asserts the canonical 4-value write-time enforcement AND the historical-row read-fidelity invariant.

**Companion: `legal_entity_kind` envelope enum (line 49596).** The §51 envelope-facing enum `legal_entity_kind` is the canonical Appendix-G-envelope registration with the same 4-value set. Finance reconciliation joins (Stripe invoice → §51 dashboard panel via `legal_entity_kind` → §4.8.1 / §4.8.3 / §4.8.12 `legal_entity`) now resolve cleanly across all four canonical values without alias drift. CI gate `legal_entity_enum_canonical_consistency` (Appendix M.5 §M.5.17 sibling, registered jointly with `legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_test` at v7.2.0-REM Phase 5 closure) asserts the two enums share the same 4-value membership at deploy time.

### Surface Throttling Class (§4.8.2, §44.6.4.1)

`active_workflow`, `low_priority_background`, `never_throttle`

**Authored in Phase 14.10; field registered on §4.8.2 in Phase 14.10.1.** Drives Solo-tier silent throttling per §44.6.4 — `active_workflow` capabilities are never suppressed on envelope exhaustion (operator's primary task is sacrosanct); `low_priority_background` capabilities are silently throttled at ≥ `throttling_threshold` of envelope (default 80% per §44.6.4); `never_throttle` is reserved for billing-cycle-critical capabilities that MUST run regardless of throttling state (e.g., outcome resolution, refund processing). Internal-only; never surfaced; the literal enum string MUST NOT appear in any customer-facing API response, in-app surface, webhook payload, or PostHog event property. v7.1 default-on `low_priority_background` membership: `proactive_cmd_k_marketplace_surfacing`, `weekly_kb_refresh_suggestions`, `vendor_page_enrichment_polling` (per §44.6.4.1 v7.1 set; full registry seeding lands in the Phase 14.10.1 capability-registry seed pass and is appended to this enum's authoritative source as additional `customer_billed` capabilities are registered). Default value on new entries is `active_workflow`.

### Committed Spend Discount Band (§4.8.8)

`none`, `band_25k_10pct`, `band_50k_15pct`, `band_100k_20pct`, `band_250k_25pct`

**Derivation rule (deterministic from `commit_value_dollars`):**

- `commit_value_dollars < 2,500,000 cents ($25K)` → `none`
- `2,500,000 ≤ commit_value_dollars < 5,000,000` → `band_25k_10pct` (10%)
- `5,000,000 ≤ commit_value_dollars < 10,000,000` → `band_50k_15pct` (15%)
- `10,000,000 ≤ commit_value_dollars < 25,000,000` → `band_100k_20pct` (20%)
- `commit_value_dollars ≥ 25,000,000` → `band_250k_25pct` (25%)

### AIWallet Auto-Topup Charge Retry Policy `auto_topup_charge` (§4.8.3; non-webhook)

Stripe charge retry policy referenced by AIWallet auto-topup charges: exponential backoff 1s, 5s, 30s, 2m, 10m with DLQ at attempt 5; on DLQ, wallet enters `payment_failed_grace`; subsequent retries are manual (Ops or customer). This governs the Stripe payment attempt itself, not customer webhook delivery, and is not a member of Appendix J `webhook_retry_class`.

### Public Pricing API Publish Fanout Policy `pricing_api_publish` (§4.8.9; non-webhook)

Public Pricing API publish fanout policy: exponential backoff 1s, 5s, 30s, 2m, 10m, 30m, 2h, 8h with DLQ at attempt 8 and Ops alert on DLQ entry. Larger retry curve due to public-cache eventual-consistency tolerance. This is a public-cache fanout policy, not a customer webhook retry class, and is not a member of Appendix J `webhook_retry_class`.

### Webhook Event Class (§31, §31.8, §27.9, §31.9) (canonical)

`product_domain`, `billing_domain`, `kb_domain`, `marketplace_content_domain`, `marketplace_discovery_domain`, `marketplace_abuse_domain`, `marketplace_signals_domain`, `internal_comment_domain`, `growth_domain`, `crm_sync_domain`, `ops_console_domain`, `ops_sim`.

**Notes.**

- `product_domain` — the implicit class for every §31.1 / Appendix C event NOT introduced under §31.8 / §27.9 / §31.9 / specialized domain (workspace, requirement, response, score, comment, vendor, marketplace core, capability declaration, NDA, KB, etc.). Subscribers MAY filter on this class via the `X-Sourcera-Event-Class` header.
- `billing_domain` — every §31.8.3–§31.8.7 event plus every v7.1.1 completeness-pack event in §31.8.11. Subscribers integrating accounting systems SHOULD subscribe by class to avoid missing future billing events added under this prefix.
- `kb_domain` — KB entry, KB document, KB export, Managed-Agent, and Seller KB governance events authored under §22 / §31.12.
- `marketplace_content_domain` — Summary §14.11 / Marketplace-authored content events.
- `marketplace_discovery_domain` — Promoted Listing, Featured Placement, Verification Review, marketplace-discovery monetization, and verification-tier lifecycle events authored under §27.11 / §31.12 / §34.16.
- `marketplace_abuse_domain` — §27.8 Marketplace Abuse Reporting events.
- `marketplace_signals_domain` (NEW per §27.9) — every `marketplace.seller_signal.*` and `marketplace.buyer_signal_opt_in.*` event.
- `internal_comment_domain` — buyer-console Internal Comment webhook events authored under §25.7.
- `growth_domain` — §31 growth / M9–M13 events.
- `crm_sync_domain` (NEW per §31.9) — every `seller.crm_sync.*` event.
- `ops_console_domain` — Ops Console events that are customer-visible only when an owning section explicitly declares a customer projection; otherwise Ops-only.
- `ops_sim` — Signal Integrity Monitor events authored under §50.15; customer webhook subscriptions do not receive this class.
- Future class additions (e.g., `compliance_domain`, `audit_domain`) require a new enum entry here AND a §31.N catalog subsection authored to Master Spec fidelity.

### Webhook Retry Class (§31, Appendix F) (canonical)

`standard`, `financial_impact`

**Notes.**

- `standard` — Appendix F.1. Default for every webhook event NOT explicitly classified otherwise.
- `financial_impact` — Appendix F.2. Applied only to events explicitly listed or registered under the Appendix F.2 membership rule.
- Non-webhook schedules such as `bridge_apply_standard`, `transactional_email`, `auto_topup_charge`, `pricing_api_publish`, and `retroactive_sweep` are operational retry policies outside `webhook_retry_class`. They MUST NOT appear in Appendix C `Retry Curve` cells for customer webhook delivery.

### Upgrade Completed Trigger (§Appendix G, §34.5.1, §34.8) (new)

`evaluation_limit`, `vendor_limit`, `ai_budget_exhaustion`, `opus_gated_capability`, `solo_envelope_pressure`

**Notes.**

- The canonical conversion-attribution enum on the `upgrade_completed` PostHog event. One value per upgrade transaction; multi-trigger upgrades record the most-proximate trigger (the one that produced the customer's confirmation click).
- `evaluation_limit` — the customer hit the per-plan workspace count cap (e.g., Buyer Free 1 workspace, Buyer Starter 3 workspaces).
- `vendor_limit` — the customer hit the per-workspace vendor count cap (e.g., Buyer Free 5 vendors per workspace).
- `ai_budget_exhaustion` — the customer's AIWallet hard-capped per §4.8.3 (overage cap exhausted) OR the customer received a `billing.wallet.cap_warning_100` and clicked the upgrade CTA from the in-app notification.
- `opus_gated_capability` — the customer attempted a `plan_gate_min_tier=enterprise` capability invocation per §4.8.2 and was redirected to the upgrade CTA.
- `solo_envelope_pressure` — the customer upgraded after a §34.5.4 / §44.6.5.A Solo throttling-pressure CTA. This value is deliberately distinct from `ai_budget_exhaustion` because Solo has no customer-visible AIWallet hard cap or overage UI.

### Solo Upgrade CTA Trigger Mode (§34.5.4, §44.6.5.A) (v7.2.0-REM Solo throttling P1 addition)

`subscription_throttling_3_in_30d`, `per_eval_envelope_hit`, `per_bid_envelope_hit`

**Notes.** Carried on `billing.solo_upgrade_cta.triggered` and `solo_upgrade_cta_triggered`. Values are mutually exclusive for a single trigger row. Subscription mode uses the rolling 30-day aggregation rule; per-evaluation / per-bid modes fire on the first `solo.envelope.exhausted` event inside the charged envelope window.

### Auto-Topup Failure Category (§31.8.4) (new)

`stripe_card_declined`, `stripe_insufficient_funds`, `stripe_network_error`, `stripe_authentication_required`, `monthly_cap_would_be_exceeded`, `payment_method_removed`, `payment_method_expired`, `auto_topup_disabled_mid_attempt`

**Notes.**

- Carried on `billing.wallet.auto_topup_failed` payload; subscribers route to remediation flows by category.
- `stripe_authentication_required` covers 3DS challenge cases (PSD2-mandated EU customer-present authentication that auto-topup cannot satisfy).
- `monthly_cap_would_be_exceeded` is a Sourcera-side rejection BEFORE Stripe is contacted (no charge attempt is made when the resulting top-up total would exceed `auto_topup_max_monthly_value_dollars_cents`).
- `auto_topup_disabled_mid_attempt` covers the Failure Mode #4 case from §4.8.3 where a Stripe charge was already in flight when the customer disabled auto-topup; the charge that completed before disable triggers `auto_topup_executed`, the next would-be charge is suppressed and reported as this category.

### AIOperation Settled-Event Settlement States (§31.8.3) (new)

`accepted`, `auto_accepted`, `rejected`

**Notes.**

- Subset of `ai_operation_settlement_state` (see §4.8.1) that the `billing.ai_operation.settled` event MAY carry. The full state enum (`pending`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `auto_accepted`, `contested`, `reversed`) is the AIOperation entity-level enum; this subset names the values valid in this specific webhook payload field.
- `pending` is invalid (no settlement has occurred); `contested` and `reversed` belong to separate webhook events (`billing.ai_operation.contested`, `billing.ai_operation.reversed`) per §31.8 catalog.

### AIOperation Reversed-Event Prior States (§31.8.3) (new)

`accepted`, `auto_accepted`, `contested`, `rejected`

**Notes.**

- Subset of `ai_operation_settlement_state` valid as the `prior_settlement_state` field in `billing.ai_operation.reversed` payload. `pending` is invalid (a reversal cannot precede settlement); `reversed` is invalid (cannot reverse a reversal).
- `rejected` appears ONLY when `reversal_origin=cost_base_correction` (rare: a faulty cost-base seed retroactively rolled back, refunding the previously-charged `cost_price_cents` to the wallet).

### Contest Origin (§31.8.3) (new)

`customer_billing_admin`, `system_late_signal`

**Notes.**

- Disambiguates the two pathways that materialize a ContestRecord per §4.8.5. `customer_billing_admin` corresponds to §32.8.7 endpoint invocation. `system_late_signal` corresponds to §4.8.1 Failure Mode #2 auto-materialized contest after a late `rejected` signal arrives post-`auto_accepted`.

### Reversal Origin (§31.8.3) (new)

`contest_approved`, `ops_emergency`, `cost_base_correction`

**Notes.**

- Disambiguates the three pathways that produce a `reversed` AIOperation per §4.8.1 state machine. `contest_approved` is the standard customer-initiated path; `ops_emergency` and `cost_base_correction` are the elevated-audit paths.

### Plan Change Origin (§31.8.5) (new)

`customer_self_serve`, `sales_ops_provisioned`, `automated_trial_conversion`, `commit_signing_provisioned`, `customer_self_serve_scheduled`, `payment_failure_automatic`, `sales_ops_decommitted`, `solo_migration_trial_auto_downgrade`

**Notes.**

- `billing.plan.upgraded.change_origin` accepts: `customer_self_serve`, `sales_ops_provisioned`, `automated_trial_conversion`, `commit_signing_provisioned`.
- `billing.plan.downgraded.change_origin` accepts: `customer_self_serve_scheduled`, `payment_failure_automatic`, `sales_ops_decommitted`, `solo_migration_trial_auto_downgrade`.
- `billing.plan.downgrade_scheduled` does NOT carry `change_origin` (always customer-initiated by definition; Sales-Ops decommit follows a separate flow that surfaces as `payment_failure_automatic` or `sales_ops_decommitted` only at the execution event).

- `expired` is computed daily from `expires_at`; `superseded` is set when a new version is uploaded and `prior_version_doc_id` is established.

`manual`, `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`

**Notes.**

- Plan-gated per §22.6 plan-limits table; Free plan is restricted to `weekly` and `manual`.

`pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed_partial`, `failed_total`, `quota_exceeded`, `domain_unverified`, `cancelled`

### MCP Tool Name (§22.8.4, §22.10.3) (extended)

`kb_retrieve`, `kb_get_entry`, `document_library_find`, `doc_attach`, `capability_find`, `capability_declare_draft`, `cite_verify`, `kb_entry_draft_create`, `kb_dedupe_check`

**Notes.**

- The first seven values (`kb_retrieve`, `kb_get_entry`, `document_library_find`, `doc_attach`, `capability_find`, `capability_declare_draft`, `cite_verify`) are the primary drafting surface exposed by the Sourcera KB MCP Server (§22.8.4.1–§22.8.4.7). Capability scope on the §22.8.3 JWT is expressed as a subset of these values.
- `kb_entry_draft_create` (§22.8.4.8) and `kb_dedupe_check` (§22.8.4.9) are the bootstrap/ingestion surface used exclusively by `agent_sourcera_kb_bootstrap` (§22.10.3) and `agent_sourcera_ghost_bid_ingestion` (§22.10.6). Per §22.8.5, `kb_dedupe_check` is read-only (`always_allow`) and `kb_entry_draft_create` is a side-effectful persistent write gated by `scoped_allow_with_quota` with per-parent-AIOperation write caps (500 per `kb_bootstrap`; 200 per `ghost_rfp_ingestion`) and a mandatory human review gate before promotion to `active`.
- Cross-link to upstream parent capability(ies) in §22.8.4 cross-link table; auditable via QA test `mcp_tool_capability_link_audit`.

### MCP Permission Scope (§22.8.5) (new)

`always_allow`, `always_ask`, `scoped_allow_with_quota`, `denied`

**Notes.**

- Read-only tools (`kb_retrieve`, `kb_get_entry`, `kb_dedupe_check`, `document_library_find`, `capability_find`, `cite_verify`) default to `always_allow`. Side-effectful tools (`doc_attach`, `capability_declare_draft`) default to `always_ask` in interactive sessions and `scoped_allow_with_quota` in batch sessions per §22.8.5. `kb_entry_draft_create` (§22.8.4.8) is always `scoped_allow_with_quota` because it is invoked exclusively in batch bootstrap/ingestion sessions and writes persistent KBEntry rows gated by human review.

### MCP Session Revocation Reason (§22.8.3.1) (new)

`expired`, `org_revoked`, `vault_compromised`, `bid_workspace_closed`, `firewall_violation`, `agent_session_crashed`

**Notes.**

- Populated on `MCPSessionTokenRecord.revoked_reason` when the orchestrator force-revokes a session token. Drives downstream auditing and incident-response runbooks.

### Cite Verify Reason (§22.8.4.7, §22.16.1) (new)

`ok`, `entry_not_found`, `offsets_out_of_bounds`, `excerpt_mismatch`, `stale`, `entry_archived`, `unauthorized_namespace`

**Notes.**

- Canonical reason vocabulary for every `cite_verify` result. §22.8.4.7, §22.16.1, Appendix G `cite_verify_failed`, and any tool-result or orchestrator-submission-gate payload MUST use these values verbatim.
- `ok` is returned only when `valid=true`. The remaining values are returned only when `valid=false`.
- `entry_archived` covers lifecycle state `archived`; `stale` covers `review_overdue` and `flagged_stale`.

**Notes.**

Without registration, the financial-class retention exemption in §4.6.1.1 AC #4 cannot bind, and the QA test `audit_event_financial_retention_exemption` would either fail or pass-on-vacuity. ### Growth-Mechanic Kill-Switch Alignment (§48.2.12.4, §48.5)

The existing `growth_loop_kill_switch_scope` enum (`platform`, `org`, `capability`, `region`) is reused for mechanic-level kill-switches. M1–M8 mechanics registered for kill-switch coverage:

| Mechanic | Kill-switch scope applicable | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| M1 | `platform`, `org` | Org-scope kill suspends per-Org M1 issuance. |
| M2 | `platform`, `org` | Org-scope kill suspends per-Org M2 publishing; existing links unaffected unless scope=platform. |
| M3 | `platform`, `org` | Kills auto-issuance at Phase 13; existing certs unaffected. |
| M4 | `platform`, `org` | Kills the Phase-13 prompt; no downstream artifact. |
| M5 | `platform`, `org` | Reuses §48.2.12.4 loop=vendor_invite_creates_account kill-switch. |
| M6 | `platform`, `org` | Org-scope kill suspends auto-join on a specific Org's claims without revoking them. |
| M7 | `platform`, `org` | Org-scope kill disables M7 per Org (mapped to `org_m7_disabled` audit event). |
| M8 | `platform`, `org` | Org-scope kill suspends curve computation; prior checkpoints preserved. |

### Taxonomy & Controlled-Vocabulary Enums — §27.6 additions

#### `taxonomy_cascade_disposition` (NEW)

Governs how live references to a deprecated or retired Taxonomy Node are transformed during the migration window defined in §27.6.5.

| Value | Semantics |
| :---- | :---- |
| `rewrite_to_successor` | Replace the reference with the nominated successor `taxonomy_node_id`. Requires `successor_node_id` to resolve to an `active` node within the same `kind`. |
| `rewrite_to_parent` | Collapse the reference to the deprecated node's immediate parent. Requires the parent to be `active`. Not permitted when parent is `root`. |
| `drop_reference` | Null the reference on the consumer row. Permitted only for optional FK slots (e.g., optional capability tags). Forbidden where a non-null constraint exists. |
| `archive_consumer` | Soft-archive the consuming row entirely. Permitted for low-criticality consumers (e.g., draft CategoryPages). Forbidden for Catalog Listings, RFP Instances, active Use Cases. |
| `preserve_historical` | Freeze the reference as-is; exempt the consumer from further cascade. Applies to historical audit-only surfaces (Selection Reports ≥ `finalized`, archived RFP transcripts). Never applies to live discovery surfaces. |

Scope: platform. Authoring authority: Ops Taxonomy Admin (§27.6.2). Each `cascade_policy` on a Taxonomy Node is a `{consumer_entity, disposition}` pair; registry lives in `taxonomy_node.cascade_policies` (see §4.5.4).

#### `taxonomy_retirement_path` (NEW)

Categorizes the terminal transition of a Taxonomy Node from `active` → `retired` per §27.6.5.

| Value | Semantics |
| :---- | :---- |
| `merge_completed` | Node retired after successor migration completed with zero residual live references. |
| `hard_retire_after_window` | Node retired by policy after the 90-day deprecation window elapsed; residual references were force-cascaded per node `cascade_policies`. |
| `tag_merged_into_existing` | Controlled-Vocabulary Tag was absorbed into a canonical Taxonomy Node; the tag's `status` moves to `retired` and all references rewrite to the absorbing node. |

Scope: platform. Emitted on the `taxonomy.category_retired` webhook payload and the audit event `ops_taxonomy_cms_node_retired`.

#### `audit_event_action_type` — §27.6 extensions

Extends the existing `audit_action_type` enum with: `ops_taxonomy_cms_node_drafted`, `ops_taxonomy_cms_node_activated`, `ops_taxonomy_cms_node_renamed`, `ops_taxonomy_cms_node_reparented`, `ops_taxonomy_cms_node_deprecated`, `ops_taxonomy_cms_node_retired`, `ops_taxonomy_cms_tag_promoted_to_node`, `ops_taxonomy_cms_tag_retired`, `ops_taxonomy_cms_migration_enqueued`, `ops_taxonomy_cms_migration_completed`, `ops_taxonomy_cms_migration_rolled_back`, `ops_taxonomy_cms_cascade_policy_updated`, `taxonomy_consumer_migration_applied`, `taxonomy_consumer_migration_rolled_back`, `vocab_tag_freeform_bypass_detected`.

Extends the enum registered on §4.5.7 with the intermediate state required for dual-signoff workflows (§27.8.8):

Expires in 72 hours (§27.8.8.5) and reverts to `triaging`. Audit trail records both signers and the elapsed interval. |

| `page_retracted` | Page was hidden and will not be republished. Used when editorial content must be removed without suspending an Org (e.g., Ops authored a flawed CategoryPage). |

#### `audit_event_action_type` — §27.8 extensions

### Webhook Delivery-Audience Scope (§31 subscription extension, §27.8.9) — NEW

#### `webhook_delivery_audience_scope` (NEW)

Authored Extension. Required on every subscription targeting Marketplace-Abuse-Domain events (§27.8.9). Governs who receives which slice of the event's lifecycle.

| Value | Semantics |
| :---- | :---- |
| `subject` | Events pertaining to the subject of the report (e.g., `abuse.report.action_applied` delivered to the sanctioned Org's subscription). Redacts reporter identity and Ops-only triage notes. |
| `reporter` | Events pertaining to the reporting party (e.g., `abuse.report.triage_complete`, `abuse.report.closed` with user-facing disposition). Redacts subject internals and Ops-only triage notes. |

### Seller-Org Field Extension — §27.8.7

Authored Extension. The `seller_org` entity (registered on §4.4.1 / platform Org record with `console=seller`) gains:

| Field | Type | Constraints | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `strike_count` | integer | ≥ 0, default 0 | Increments on every `abuse_report_closure_disposition in {vendor_suspended, vendor_banned, violation_confirmed}` where severity ∈ {medium, high, critical}. Decays −1 per 180 days of clean history (no new qualifying closures). Threshold 3 triggers `marketplace_abuse_strike_auto_promotion_triggered` (next qualifying sanction auto-promoted one severity tier). Threshold 5 triggers mandatory management review before any further sanction. Index: `(strike_count desc, org_id)` for Ops caseload triage. Retention: lifetime of Org record. ### Seller Signals & Buyer Opt-In Enums (§27.9) — NEW

#### `buyer_signal_opt_in_scope`

`none`, `all_active_workspaces`, `selected_use_case_categories`, `selected_vertical_codes`, `all_subject_to_redaction_policy`.

**Semantics:**

- `none` — the default-deny baseline (§27.9.2). No BuyerSignal contribution; any aggregation pipeline stage skips this Buyer Org.
- `all_active_workspaces` — contribute signal from every active Workspace (`workspace.status=active` AND `pipeline_phase ∈ {phase_1, …, phase_13_contract_closure}` per §5.10 V4 enum-membership rule; pre-V4 ordinal `pipeline_stage_id < 13` form retired per D-4.2-001 closure); future workspaces auto-included.
- `selected_use_case_categories` — contribute only from Workspaces whose `use_case.category_id` ∈ the opt-in record's `included_category_ids` array.
- `selected_vertical_codes` — contribute only from Workspaces whose buying Org's `vertical_code` ∈ the opt-in record's `included_vertical_codes` array (the Buyer Org's own `vertical_code`; this does NOT condition on vendor vertical).
- `all_subject_to_redaction_policy` — contribute from all active Workspaces subject to an explicit redaction policy (e.g., pricing-band masked, vendor-name masked unless EOI is filed). Governed by `buyer_signal_redaction_profile` (NEW; see below).

#### `buyer_signal_opt_in_state`

`inactive`, `active`, `paused_by_buyer`, `paused_by_ops`, `revoked`.

**State machine (§27.9.2):** `inactive → active` (on explicit opt-in); `active → paused_by_buyer` (workspace-scoped or org-scoped pause); `active → paused_by_ops` (Ops manual pause, e.g., DSAR processing in flight, privacy concern escalation); `paused_by_buyer → active` (buyer resumes); `paused_by_ops → active` (Ops resumes after review); `active | paused_* → revoked` (terminal; re-opting-in requires a new record with new `id`).

#### `buyer_signal_region_inclusion_policy`

`residency_region_only`, `cross_region_with_buyer_consent`, `ops_forbidden_cross_region`.

**Semantics:** Governs whether a Buyer Org's contribution may aggregate across data-residency regions per §27.9.5 residency enforcement stage. Default `residency_region_only`. `cross_region_with_buyer_consent` requires explicit UX-captured affirmation; `ops_forbidden_cross_region` blocks cross-region aggregation even if the buyer opted in (used for regulated industries flagged by Ops).

#### `buyer_signal_paused_reason`

`buyer_org_policy_change`, `buyer_workspace_sensitivity`, `dsar_in_flight`, `ops_privacy_investigation`, `residency_policy_tightened`, `other_buyer_specified`, `other_ops_specified`.

#### `buyer_signal_redaction_profile`

`default`, `pricing_masked`, `vendor_name_masked_unless_eoi`, `strict_k_floor_plus_distinctiveness`.

**Semantics:** Determines which fields survive into the aggregation pipeline. `default` suppresses pricing and vendor-name attribution pre-EOI; `pricing_masked` additionally suppresses any pricing-band contribution; `vendor_name_masked_unless_eoi` restricts vendor-attribution to cohorts where EOI is filed; `strict_k_floor_plus_distinctiveness` raises k from 5 to 10 and applies the §27.9.5 distinctiveness veto unconditionally.

#### `seller_signal_de_anon_trigger`

`buyer_eoi_submitted`, `buyer_accepted_direct_invite`, `ops_investigation_disclosure_with_dpo_approval`.

**Semantics:** Governs creation of a SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink per §27.9.4. These are the ONLY three permissible triggers — any other pathway is a privacy violation and blocked at the API layer.

#### `seller_signal_de_anon_legal_basis`

`contract_performance`, `legitimate_interest_disclosed_to_buyer`, `regulatory_investigation_with_dpo_approval`.

**Semantics:** GDPR Article 6 basis per disclosure event. `contract_performance` applies to EOI / direct-invite acceptance (buyer initiated a commercial engagement). `legitimate_interest_disclosed_to_buyer` applies to direct-invite offer acceptance flows where the buyer has been informed of the reveal. `regulatory_investigation_with_dpo_approval` is reserved for Ops-initiated disclosures with recorded DPO sign-off.

#### `seller_signal_suppression_render_mode`

`hidden`, `placeholder_below_k_floor`, `placeholder_distinctiveness_vetoed`, `placeholder_residency_excluded`, `placeholder_vendor_opt_out_scrubbed`.

**Semantics:** Determines how Seller Dashboard renders a cohort cell suppressed by §27.9.5. `hidden` omits the row entirely (used by default on weekly digest to avoid empty-digest noise per §27.9.6). Placeholder modes surface a non-disclosing cell ("Cohort suppressed — below privacy threshold") so the Seller can confirm coverage without seeing content. `placeholder_vendor_opt_out_scrubbed` is a rendering state for cohorts where the Seller's own opt-out scrubbed contributions.

#### `seller_signal_delivery_channel`

`dashboard_live`, `weekly_digest_email`, `real_time_toast` (NEW per §27.9.6), `real_time_api_poll` (NEW per §27.9.6), `crm_sync_activity` (NEW per §27.9.6 → §31.9 bridge).

**Plan-tier gating at delivery time (§27.9.3):** `dashboard_live` available on all Seller plans eligible for Seller Signals (Seller Growth+ per §34.1.2); `weekly_digest_email` on Growth+; `real_time_toast` + `real_time_api_poll` on Seller Scale+; `crm_sync_activity` requires active CRMSyncConnection (Seller Growth+ for CRM Sync itself per §34.1.2). Channel eligibility is re-evaluated at each delivery attempt per §27.9.3; cross-channel fallback is forbidden (a Scale+ → Growth downgrade disables `real_time_*` channels but does not re-route their events onto `weekly_digest_email`).

### Direct Invite Enums (§27.9.8) — NEW

#### `direct_invite_offer_kind`

`cohort_interest_signal`, `capability_match_hint`, `vertical_alignment`, `use_case_ready`.

**Semantics:** The cohort-justification class surfaced on the invite UX (Seller composes the invite around this rationale, but the actual signal underlying the cohort is never revealed). The enum extends `MarketplaceProactiveOffer.offer_kind` (Authored Extension per §27.9.8 — logged in RECONCILIATION.md).

#### `direct_invite_decline_reason`

`not_interested`, `wrong_timing`, `procurement_policy_prohibits`, `duplicate_vendor_outreach`, `no_reason_given`.

**Semantics:** Captured on buyer decline; `procurement_policy_prohibits` and `duplicate_vendor_outreach` trigger the 90-day cooldown per §27.9.8; other reasons trigger the standard 30-day cooldown.

### Webhook Event Class — §27.9 / §31.9 Extension

The existing `webhook_event_class` enum is extended with TWO new values:

- `marketplace_signals_domain` (NEW) — every `marketplace.seller_signal.*` and `marketplace.buyer_signal_opt_in.*` event carries this class. Sellers integrating Market Intelligence pipelines SHOULD subscribe by class.
- `crm_sync_domain` (NEW) — every `seller.crm_sync.*` event carries this class. Seller RevOps teams building custom CRM integrations on top of Sourcera's native CRM Sync MAY subscribe by class to receive full transport-layer telemetry.

The canonical enum is therefore: `product_domain`, `billing_domain`, `marketplace_content_domain`, `growth_domain`, `marketplace_abuse_domain`, `marketplace_signals_domain`, `crm_sync_domain`.

### CRM Sync Enums (§31.9) — NEW

#### `crm_provider`

`salesforce`, `hubspot`, `dynamics_365`, `pipedrive`.

**Semantics:** Provider identifier for CRMSyncConnection. Each provider row has its own OAuth minimum scope set (§31.9.11), object-kind mapping (§31.9.8), and rate-limit envelope (§31.9.9).

#### `crm_sync_connection_state`

`oauth_pending`, `active`, `paused_token_expired`, `paused_api_rate_limit`, `paused_schema_mismatch`, `paused_manual`, `paused_provider_5xx_outage` (NEW authored extension per §31.9.3), `revoked`, `disconnected`.

**State machine (§31.9.3):** `oauth_pending → active` (on successful token exchange); `active ↔ paused_*` (automated or manual pause with auto-resume per pause reason); `active | paused_* → revoked` (provider or Sourcera OAuth revoke — immediate hard stop); `revoked → disconnected` (terminal; re-connecting requires a fresh OAuth flow and a new `id`).

#### `crm_sync_pause_reason`

Same values as the `paused_*` subset of `crm_sync_connection_state` plus: `crm_connection_revoked` (terminal pause prior to `disconnected` sink), `ops_compliance_hold` (privacy / DPA investigation; only `ops_platform_admin` can set and clear).

#### `crm_sync_sourcera_entity_kind`

`eoi`, `seller_signal_cohort_accept`, `bid_workspace_invite`, `bid_workspace_response_submitted`, `bid_workspace_response_shortlisted`, `bid_workspace_response_selected`, `bid_workspace_response_declined`, `qa_thread_message`, `public_review_received`, `direct_invite_offer`, `direct_invite_accepted`, `direct_invite_declined`, `ghost_bid_received`.

**Semantics:** Canonical Sourcera-side source-entity kinds that the CRM Sync pipeline can propagate per §31.9.8. Each kind has a per-provider payload template.

#### `crm_object_kind` (per-provider partial)

- Salesforce: `opportunity`, `account`, `lead`, `contact`, `task`, `custom_object_sourcera_signal`.
- HubSpot: `deal`, `company`, `contact`, `engagement_note`, `engagement_task`, `custom_object_sourcera_signal`.
- Dynamics 365: `opportunity`, `account`, `lead`, `contact`, `task`, `custom_entity_sourcera_signal`.
- Pipedrive: `deal`, `organization`, `person`, `activity`.

**Semantics:** Target CRM object kind on the provider side. Each platform-default CRMFieldMapping row references one `crm_object_kind` at the provider namespace above. `custom_object_sourcera_signal` (Salesforce/HubSpot) and `custom_entity_sourcera_signal` (Dynamics) are the Sourcera-provided custom objects installed via Managed Package (Salesforce) / Custom Object API (HubSpot) / Dynamics Solution (Dynamics). Pipedrive does not support a Sourcera-specific custom entity at v7.0.0; Pipedrive integrations write to `deal` + `activity` only.

#### `crm_field_mapping_direction`

`sourcera_to_crm`, `crm_to_sourcera`, `bidirectional`.

**Semantics:** Governs data flow per §31.9.4. `sourcera_to_crm` is the default for all activity events. `crm_to_sourcera` is used for owner-sync (Salesforce Opportunity Owner → Sourcera recipient resolution) and for custom pullbacks (e.g., deal-stage → Sourcera dashboard filter). `bidirectional` is **Enterprise-plan-only** per §31.9.13 and requires conflict-resolution-strategy (`crm_wins`, `sourcera_wins`, `last_write_wins`, `manual_review`) defined per-mapping.

#### `crm_field_transform`

`identity`, `uppercase`, `lowercase`, `trim`, `truncate_n`, `prefix_literal`, `enum_map_table_ref`, `date_format_iso8601`, `currency_iso_code_enrich`, `url_domain_only`, `concat_template`.

**Semantics:** Server-side transforms applied at field-mapping time. Custom JS transforms are NOT permitted (security risk). `enum_map_table_ref` references a sub-resource `CRMEnumMappingTable` (Authored Extension — logged in RECONCILIATION.md) for customer-maintained enum-to-enum value maps (e.g., Sourcera `bid_workspace_status=selected` → Salesforce `Opportunity.StageName=Closed Won`).

#### `crm_routing_rule_kind`

`account_match_whitelist`, `account_match_blacklist`, `field_value_predicate`, `territory_mapping`, `default_fallback`.

**Semantics:** Ordered rules per §31.9.5, first-match-wins. Whitelisted predicate grammar only; see §31.9.5 for the whitelisted operator list (`equals`, `not_equals`, `in`, `not_in`, `matches_regex_safe`, `is_null`, `is_not_null`).

#### `crm_account_match_method`

`domain_exact`, `name_exact`, `name_fuzzy_high_confidence`, `name_fuzzy_low_confidence_needs_confirmation`, `no_match_created_new`, `no_match_hold_for_review`.

**Semantics:** The matching-algorithm outcome per §31.9.7. Confidence thresholds: `name_fuzzy_high_confidence` ≥ 0.90 (auto-accept); `name_fuzzy_low_confidence_needs_confirmation` 0.70–0.89 (routed to Review Queue); below 0.70 → `no_match_hold_for_review`. `no_match_created_new` is allowed only when the CRM mapping opts in to auto-create accounts (off by default).

#### `crm_sync_activity_kind`

Mirrors `crm_sync_sourcera_entity_kind` values with `.activity_write` suffix in payload; the enum itself uses the entity-kind stems for terseness.

#### `crm_sync_activity_state`

`pending`, `in_flight`, `succeeded`, `failed_retryable`, `failed_permanent`, `dead_lettered`, `redacted_by_dsar`.

**State machine (§31.9.6):** `pending → in_flight` (worker claim); `in_flight → succeeded | failed_retryable | failed_permanent` (terminal for `succeeded`/`failed_permanent`); `failed_retryable → pending` (retry eligibility per §31.9.9 retry curve); `failed_retryable → dead_lettered` (after attempt cap per §31.9.9); `succeeded | failed_permanent | dead_lettered → redacted_by_dsar` (terminal; payload bytes zeroed but row preserved for audit).

#### `crm_sync_failure_category`

`crm_provider_5xx`, `crm_provider_429_rate_limit`, `crm_oauth_token_expired`, `crm_oauth_scope_insufficient`, `crm_schema_mismatch`, `crm_required_field_missing`, `crm_routing_rule_evaluation_failed`, `crm_account_match_ambiguous`, `crm_payload_too_large`, `crm_field_type_incompatible`, `crm_residency_region_mismatch`, `unknown_error`.

**Retry-eligibility matrix (§31.9.9):** `crm_provider_5xx`, `crm_provider_429_rate_limit`, `crm_oauth_token_expired` (after silent refresh) → `failed_retryable`. `crm_oauth_scope_insufficient`, `crm_schema_mismatch`, `crm_required_field_missing`, `crm_payload_too_large`, `crm_field_type_incompatible` → `failed_permanent` (operator intervention required). `crm_routing_rule_evaluation_failed`, `crm_account_match_ambiguous` → `failed_retryable` with a hold on the Review Queue (does not consume retry attempts until Review resolves). `crm_residency_region_mismatch` → `failed_permanent` (privacy defect).

### Seller Console Role Extension — §5.11, §27.9, §31.9

#### `seller_console_role` (NEW authored extension — requires human sign-off if §5.2 does not yet define these)

`seller_org_admin`, `seller_marketing_editor`, `seller_integrations_admin`.

**Semantics:** Seller-console sub-roles granted additive to `org_owner`. Enforced at the API layer via the seller-console role resolver. See §5.11 Seller Console Role Overlay notes for per-role operation grants. `seller_integrations_admin` is the new role introduced by §31.9.11; its OAuth-initiation grants on CRM Sync and its exclusion from Scale+ customer-custom mapping mutations are canonical.

### CRM Sync Sub-Resource Registrations — §31.9

#### `CRMEnumMappingTable` sub-resource

Authored Extension (requires human sign-off). A sub-resource owned by the parent CRMFieldMapping row when `transform = enum_map_table_ref`. Fields: `id`, `field_mapping_id` (FK), `source_enum_value` (string), `target_crm_value` (string), `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at`. Retention: lifetime of parent field-mapping row; cascade-deleted when the field-mapping is deleted. Plan-gating: Scale+ (matches the parent `is_customer_custom=true` gate). Indexes: `(field_mapping_id, source_enum_value)` unique partial on `deleted_at IS NULL`.

#### `DirectInviteTargetAccount` sub-resource

Authored Extension (requires human sign-off). Links a MarketplaceProactiveOffer authored under §27.9.8 to the target Buyer Org without revealing the cohort composition to the Seller pre-acceptance. Fields: `id`, `proactive_offer_id` (FK), `buyer_org_id_opaque_token` (UUID; opaque until acceptance triggers §27.9.4 de-anonymization), `seller_signal_cohort_id` (FK; the cohort from which this offer was composed), `offer_expires_at` (timestamptz; 14 days default; enforces §27.9.8 rate cap windows), `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at`. Retention: 90 days post-expiry for accepted offers (supports §27.9.4 audit reconciliation); 30 days post-expiry for declined/expired offers. Indexes: `(proactive_offer_id)` unique; `(seller_signal_cohort_id, created_at desc)` for rate-limit enforcement.

### Marketplace Monetization & Seller Onboarding Enums — §4.4.19–§4.4.22 Additions

All enums in this subsection are closed; any new value requires a spec amendment. Each enum is referenced by at least one entity in §4.4.19–§4.4.22 and by at least one acceptance criterion therein.

#### `promoted_listing_placement_surface` (§4.4.19)

`category_page_top_slot`, `category_page_adjacent_rail`, `eoi_eligible_search_result`, `workspace_phase_4_vendor_discovery_surface`.

**Semantics:** The set of public / in-Workspace surfaces on which a PromotedListing may render. Each surface runs an independent second-price auction. `category_page_top_slot` renders the hero position on CategoryPage (§4.4.12); `category_page_adjacent_rail` renders in the rail adjacent to the organic match lane; `eoi_eligible_search_result` renders inline in EOI-eligible search results across marketplace browse; `workspace_phase_4_vendor_discovery_surface` renders inside a Buyer Workspace during Phase 4 Vendor Discovery (§10.5). The seller selects a subset at authoring time; an empty set rejects with `promoted_listing_no_surfaces_selected` (Appendix I).

#### `promoted_listing_placement_mode` (§4.4.19)

`included_allotment`, `purchased_top_up`.

**Semantics:** `included_allotment` consumes one of the Seller Org's plan-included monthly Promoted Listing slots per §34.1.2; no incremental charge. `purchased_top_up` is billed per §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_base_rate_cents_per_category_week` and counts against §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_purchased_top_up_hard_cap_per_month`.

#### `promoted_listing_status` (§4.4.19)

`draft`, `pending_eligibility_check`, `active`, `paused_by_seller`, `paused_by_ops`, `daily_cap_exhausted`, `monthly_allotment_exhausted`, `category_cap_exhausted`, `frequency_cap_exhausted`, `exhausted`, `expired`, `terminated_eligibility_lost`.

**State machine:** see §4.4.19 *State Machine*. Terminal states: `exhausted`, `expired`, `terminated_eligibility_lost`. Auto-reset states (rollover to `active`): `daily_cap_exhausted` (UTC midnight), `monthly_allotment_exhausted` (billing-cycle rollover). Ops-only transitions: `paused_by_ops` → `active`, `paused_by_ops` → `terminated_eligibility_lost`.

#### `promoted_listing_eligibility_failure_reason` (§4.4.19)

`kb_health_floor_not_met`, `no_closed_bids_prior_90d`, `plan_tier_below_scale`, `category_inactive`, `seller_software_not_claim_verified`, `software_page_not_published`, `vendor_opt_out_active_for_category`.

**Semantics:** Populated on `pending_eligibility_check → terminated_eligibility_lost` transitions per §4.4.19 *Eligibility Gate*. Each reason maps 1:1 to one of the ten eligibility rules (§4.4.19 rules 1–10); the subset omits the rules enforced by category-cap race resolution (`category_cap_exhausted`), monthly-allotment enforcement (`monthly_allotment_exhausted`), and top-up hard-cap (`promoted_listing_monthly_top_up_cap_exceeded` — surfaced as a write-time error, not a terminal eligibility reason).

#### `promoted_listing_auction_run_console_scope` (§4.4.19.1)

`platform_internal`.

**Semantics:** Fixed console marker for platform-internal auction-decision audit rows. Buyer and seller consoles never receive raw rows; seller reporting consumes only k-anonymity-safe aggregates.

#### `promoted_listing_auction_metric` (§4.4.19.1)

`cpm`, `eoi`.

**Semantics:** The bid metric used by the auction engine. `cpm` reads `bid_impression_cents`; `eoi` reads `bid_eoi_cents`.

#### `promoted_listing_auction_outcome` (§4.4.19.1)

`winner_selected`, `single_bidder_floor`, `no_eligible_listing`, `skipped_by_cap`, `rerun_after_cap_skip`, `shadow_recorded`.

**Semantics:** Outcome classification for a single auction decision. `shadow_recorded` is reserved for primary-write failure paths where the secondary incident queue accepted the decision payload and reconciliation later restores the canonical row.

#### `promoted_listing_auction_suppression_reason` (§4.4.19.1)

`daily_cap_exhausted`, `per_eoi_cap_exceeded`, `frequency_cap_exhausted`, `vendor_opt_out_active`, `category_inactive`, `no_keyword_match`, `below_k_anonymity_floor`.

**Semantics:** Optional reason when an auction does not produce a normal winner or reruns after a filtered winner. Values map to §4.4.19 eligibility, cap, k-anonymity, and opt-out predicates.

#### `promoted_listing_auction_run_write_status` (§4.4.19.1)

`recorded`, `shadow_queued`, `reconciled`, `rolled_up`.

**Semantics:** State machine values for the auction-decision audit log. See §4.4.19.1 *State Machine*.

#### `featured_placement_surface` (§4.4.20)

`category_page`, `comparison_page`, `heat_map`.

**Semantics:** Public marketplace surfaces that render FeaturedPlacement slots (§4.4.12 CategoryPage, §4.4.14 ComparisonPage, §4.4.16 HeatMapCell).

#### `featured_placement_target_entity_type` (§4.4.20)

`category_page`, `comparison_page`, `heat_map_cell`.

**Semantics:** Polymorphic target kind. `target_entity_id` (§4.4.20 field) is resolved per this enum to the corresponding entity row (§4.4.12 / §4.4.14 / §4.4.16). Writing `target_entity_id` against a mismatched `target_entity_type` rejects with `featured_placement_target_entity_type_mismatch` (Appendix I).

#### `featured_placement_slot_kind` (§4.4.20)

`hero_tile`, `carousel_rail`, `sidebar_strip`, `comparison_spotlight`, `heat_map_annotation_callout`.

**Semantics:** Visual treatment. `hero_tile` and `carousel_rail` are valid for `category_page`; `comparison_spotlight` is valid for `comparison_page`; `heat_map_annotation_callout` is valid for `heat_map_cell`; `sidebar_strip` is valid for `category_page` only. Mismatched `slot_kind` / `placement_surface` pair rejects with `featured_placement_slot_kind_surface_mismatch` (Appendix I).

#### `featured_placement_mode` (§4.4.20)

`editorial`, `paid_commitment`.

**Semantics:** `editorial` is the current authoritative mode (per Summary §2.10, C.131, Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy §12.3). `paid_commitment` is reserved under feature-flag `featured_placement_paid_mode_enabled` (default `false`); activation requires Ops Council + Finance + Legal sign-off per the Known Gap documented in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md`.

#### `featured_placement_commitment_period` (§4.4.20)

`monthly`, `quarterly`, `ops_discretion_variable`.

**Semantics:** Duration of the featuring window. Under `editorial` mode: `monthly` and `quarterly` map to Marketing's editorial calendar cadences; `ops_discretion_variable` is for event-driven featurings (e.g., a category spike following a MarketIntelligenceReport). Under `paid_commitment` mode (reserved): reflects the contract term.

#### `featured_placement_status` (§4.4.20)

`scheduled`, `active`, `paused_by_ops`, `expired`, `revoked`, `revoked_by_opt_out`, `revoked_by_verification_downgrade`, `revoked_by_abuse_finding`.

**State machine:** see §4.4.20 *State Machine*. Terminal: `expired`, `revoked`, `revoked_by_opt_out`, `revoked_by_verification_downgrade`, `revoked_by_abuse_finding`. Re-enter-able from terminal: none — the seller creates a new row to be re-featured.

#### `featured_placement_revocation_reason` (§4.4.20)

`vendor_opt_out`, `verification_tier_downgrade`, `abuse_report_upheld`, `kb_health_below_floor`, `seller_org_deleted`, `seller_software_unpublished`, `editorial_discretion`, `paid_commitment_cancelled_by_seller_with_proration`, `paid_commitment_cancelled_by_ops`.

**Semantics:** Populated on any `revoked*` status. Paid-mode-specific reasons are reserved and only fire when the paid-mode feature-flag is active.

#### `verification_review_request_kind` (§4.4.21)

`initial_upgrade`, `quarterly_rereview`, `ops_imposed_rereview`, `document_expiry_rereview`, `post_downgrade_reinstatement`.

**Semantics:** Drives SLA class and workflow routing. `quarterly_rereview` and `document_expiry_rereview` are system-created (auto-scheduled). `initial_upgrade` and `post_downgrade_reinstatement` are seller-submitted. `ops_imposed_rereview` is Ops-created with justification.

#### `verification_review_outcome` (§4.4.21)

`pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `revision_requested`, `escalated_to_legal`, `withdrawn_by_seller`, `auto_rejected_sla_breach`.

**State machine:** see §4.4.21 *State Machine*. `escalated_to_legal` is a substate of `pending` — Legal team drives resolution to `approved` / `rejected` / `withdrawn_by_seller`.

#### `verification_review_rejection_reason` (§4.4.21)

`document_illegible`, `document_expired`, `document_mismatched_org`, `soc_2_type_1_insufficient_for_certified`, `iso_27001_scope_excluded_target_services`, `hipaa_attestation_insufficient`, `pci_scope_excluded_target_services`, `closed_bid_count_below_threshold`, `buyer_confirmation_count_below_threshold`, `profile_completeness_below_threshold`, `kb_health_below_floor`, `seller_under_active_abuse_investigation`, `plan_tier_below_required`, `other`.

**Semantics:** Populated on `rejected` or `revision_requested`. The `other` bucket requires a non-empty `outcome_notes_markdown` (§4.4.21) and is audited weekly by Ops for new-reason candidates.

#### `verification_review_legal_escalation_reason` (§4.4.21)

`documentation_forgery_suspected`, `trademark_dispute`, `compliance_boundary_ambiguous`, `other`.

**Semantics:** Populated when `outcome = 'escalated_to_legal'`. Legal team receives an automated escalation notification; seller receives a neutral "under review" status message.

#### `verification_tier_downgrade_reason` (§4.4.21)

`document_expired_not_renewed`, `ops_imposed_abuse`, `plan_downgraded_below_required`, `seller_revoked_self`, `closed_bid_count_fell_below_threshold`, `quarterly_rereview_not_submitted`.

**Semantics:** Populated on records that cause a tier downgrade. Downgrade cascades to SellerSoftware / SellerOrgPage / PromotedListing / FeaturedPlacement within 15 minutes (§4.4.21 Acceptance Criterion 8).

#### `seller_onboarding_invite_source` (§4.4.22)

`buyer_invite`, `ghost_bid_conversion`, `direct_signup`, `marketplace_search`, `buyer_referral_m16`, `pro_trial_seat_m17`.

**Semantics:** Origination channel per Summary C.136 Forced-Vendor-Signup playbook and §48.5 growth-mechanic channels. `ghost_bid_conversion` is the GhostBidImport-driven path (§4.4.17). `buyer_referral_m16` and `pro_trial_seat_m17` are the growth-mechanic channels registered under §48.5.

#### `seller_onboarding_win_loss_disclosed` (§4.4.22)

`win`, `loss`, `undisclosed`, `not_applicable`.

**Semantics:** Populated from buyer-side disclosure at bid close. `not_applicable` is used when the session never reached Stage 6 (e.g., abandoned earlier, or Stage 6 debrief not yet delivered).

#### `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_kind` (§4.4.22)

`second_concurrent_bid`, `first_eoi_attempt`, `kb_ceiling_approach`, `none`.

**Semantics:** Per SPS v3 §15.3 / §48.1.7 Four Seller Conversion Moments. `none` is set when Stage 7 fires on a non-conversion-moment trigger (reserved future path). `mid_bid_ai_budget_wall` = Seller Free wallet exhaustion pauses AI-assisted response drafting during active bid work; `second_concurrent_bid` = a second active Bid Workspace concurrent with the first; `first_eoi_attempt` = seller attempts to send an EOI (§4.5.8) from a free-tier account; `kb_ceiling_approach` = KB size nears the plan-tier ceiling (§22.3.4 quotas) for Seller Free or Seller Solo.

#### `seller_onboarding_completion_state` (§4.4.22)

`in_progress`, `activated`, `activated_and_upgraded`, `abandoned`, `errored`, `reactivated`, `churned_post_activation`.

**State machine:** see §4.4.22 *State Machine*. Used as the primary funnel-segmentation axis on the Seller Activation dashboard.

#### `seller_onboarding_abandon_reason` (§4.4.22)

`no_sso_completion`, `no_bid_workspace_load`, `no_first_edit_within_3min`, `no_submission_within_7d`, `seller_explicit_rejection`, `firecrawl_rate_limit_block`, `capability_unavailable_graceful_degradation_triggered`, `seller_pointed_to_wrong_domain`, `other`.

**Semantics:** Populated on `in_progress → abandoned`. `seller_explicit_rejection` captures the "Not interested" CTA click (Summary §6.28.2 Stage 1 fallback). `firecrawl_rate_limit_block` is surfaced specifically because it is a measurable dependency failure (see §22.3.3 and the Firecrawl graceful-degradation path in KB_Engineering_Spec).

### Ops Role Extensions — §4.4.19–§4.4.22

#### `ops_verification_reviewer` (§4.4.21)

New Ops role (Authored Extension — requires §5.2 sign-off). Granted to Ops users approved to review Verified-tier and lower-risk Certified-tier requests. Residency-locked: EU-residency sellers' documents MUST route to reviewers with `residency_region = 'eu'`. Excluded from Verified/Certified separation-of-duties chain for the *same seller* (cannot approve both prerequisite Verified and dependent Certified for a single seller).

#### `ops_verification_senior_reviewer` (§4.4.21)

New Ops role (Authored Extension — requires §5.2 sign-off). Granted to Ops reviewers authorized to override the separation-of-duties rule with explicit, audited rationale. Acts as SLA-breach queue escalation recipient.

#### `paid_featured_write` (§4.4.20)

New Ops entitlement (not a role, a capability bit). Required (in addition to `ops_marketing_editor` role) to write a FeaturedPlacement with `placement_mode = 'paid_commitment'` once the feature-flag is activated. Absence of this entitlement rejects with `featured_placement_paid_mode_entitlement_missing` (Appendix I).

### Firewall Violation Scope Extension — §4.4.19, §4.4.21, §4.4.22

#### `firewall_violation_scope` additions (§7.2, §4.6)

`seller_promoted_listing`, `seller_verification_review`, `seller_onboarding_session`.

**Semantics:** Logged by §4.6 Audit entries when a cross-console read attempt hits one of the §4.4.19 / §4.4.21 / §4.4.22 entities. Paired with HTTP 404 response (not 403) per §7.2 Dual-Console Firewall non-leak rule.

### Phase 1.5 Enum Cluster — §4.3.20 / §4.3.21 / §4.3.22 / §4.6.2

**Authoring note — Phase 1.5 Completion Delta (Authored Extension — requires human sign-off).** The following enums register the controlled-vocabulary surface for the Phase 1.5 stubs authored to resolve dangling polymorphic FK targets (F-S-4, F-S-8). Each enum is the canonical reference for its home entity; any addition requires a cross-reference to the home-entity section and a migration entry in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md`.

#### `target_account_source_enum` (§4.3.20)

`ai_discovery`, `manual_entry`, `csv_import`, `marketplace_browse`, `referral`, `sourcera_curated`

**Notes.** Determines the FK target of `source_artifact_id`: `ai_discovery → Discovery Run`, `csv_import → CSV Import Batch`, `marketplace_browse → Marketplace Session`, `referral → Referral Invite`. `manual_entry` and `sourcera_curated` leave `source_artifact_id` null. Polymorphic FK integrity enforced at application layer (Convex) per §4.3.20 Failure Mode #2.

#### `target_account_state_enum` (§4.3.20)

`prospect`, `qualified`, `solicited`, `bidding`, `shortlisted`, `finalist`, `disqualified`, `superseded`

**Notes.** Authoritative state enum for the §4.3.20 Target Account entity. State-machine semantics defined in Appendix L.6. Terminal states: `finalist`, `disqualified`, `superseded`. **Supersedes the legacy "Target Account Status (Vendor Curation)" enum at §Appendix J earlier in this appendix (preserved verbatim for Phase 4 back-compat documentation); that legacy enum is deprecated at Phase 5 integration and MUST NOT be used for new writes on or after v7.0.0 deploy per `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md` → Phase 1.5 Completion Delta.** Migration mapping at Phase 5: `invited → prospect`, `nda_pending → solicited`, `active → bidding`, `disqualified → disqualified`, `withdrawn → superseded`.

#### `target_account_disqualification_enum` (§4.3.20)

`no_capability_match`, `compliance_fail`, `pricing_out_of_band`, `duplicate_of_other_account`, `buyer_discretion`, `seller_declined_bid`

**Notes.** Populated only when `state = disqualified`. Combination with `disqualification_note` is required for `buyer_discretion`; optional for other values. `seller_declined_bid` emitted automatically when a Bid Workspace transitions to `withdrawn` with `withdrawal_initiator = seller`.

#### `selection_report_draft_state_enum` (§4.3.21)

`initial`, `drafting`, `ai_generating`, `review`, `finalized`, `abandoned`

**Notes.** `finalized` is terminal (the draft crystallizes into a Selection Report). `abandoned` is reached when the workspace archives without a finalized draft; triggers the Phase 7 disposition sweep.

#### `selection_report_status` (§4.3.23)

`generated`, `signed`, `approval_pending`, `approved`, `superseded`, `archived`

**Notes.** Governs finalized Selection Report lifecycle. `generated` is the initial immutable-report row; `signed` means Workspace Owner signature is complete; `approval_pending` means Org approval workflow is active; `approved` is the Phase 12 gate-satisfying state; `superseded` means a newer report version replaced this row before Phase 13; `archived` follows Workspace closure / archive.

#### `vendor_selection_status` (§4.3.23, §10.12)

`primary`, `secondary`, `alternate`, `not_selected`

**Notes.** Canonical vendor outcome value written into `SelectionReport.selection_status_map_json` and referenced by §10.12 Finalist Selection. Exactly one evaluated vendor may be `primary`.

#### `approval_workflow_status` (§4.3.25, Appendix L.12)

`pending`, `approved`, `request_changes`, `rejected`

**Notes.** Sub-state of Phase 12 Selection & Recommendation. `request_changes` and `rejected` keep the Workspace in `phase_12_selection`; neither value unlocks scores or creates a backward pipeline transition.

#### `approval_workflow_required_role` (§4.3.25)

`cfo`, `legal`, `cro`, `procurement_owner`, `custom_policy_approver`

**Notes.** Role policy discriminator for Org-specific approval routing. Values map to users through §5.11 / Org policy configuration; they are not global RBAC roles by themselves.

#### `cancellation_request_status` (§4.3.26)

`initiated`, `undo_grace`, `processing`, `recovered`, `hard_deleted`

**Notes.** Mirrors §10.14 cancellation lifecycle on the first-class Cancellation Request row. Timing singletons derive from `cancelled_at` per §10.14 and §40.2.

#### `post_evaluation_feedback_sentiment` (§4.3.27)

`positive`, `neutral`, `negative`, `mixed`

**Notes.** Lightweight analytics classification for optional post-evaluation feedback. Does not affect vendor outcome, Selection Report, or Selection Record.

#### `inbox_item_group_type_enum` (§4.3.22)

`thread_collapse`, `digest_rollup`, `cross_console_bundle`, `notification_digest`, `marketplace_signal_cluster`

**Notes.** Determines the anchor-entity type for the group. `thread_collapse` anchors to a conversation thread (Q&A Thread, Internal Comment Thread); `digest_rollup` anchors to a daily/weekly digest window; `cross_console_bundle` anchors to a Console Bridge Event batch; `notification_digest` anchors to a user-preference-scoped delivery window; `marketplace_signal_cluster` anchors to a marketplace-signal cluster per §27.9.

#### `anchor_entity_type_enum` (§4.3.22, §4.3.15)

`qa_thread`, `internal_comment_thread`, `workspace`, `bid_workspace`, `requirement`, `response`, `selection_report_draft`, `console_bridge_event_batch`, `digest_window`, `marketplace_signal_cluster`

**Notes.** Polymorphic FK target enum used by Inbox Item Group (`anchor_entity_type`) and Unread Marker (`container_type`). FK resolution performed at application layer (Convex); database CHECK constraint validates enum membership only. Additions require a cross-reference to the home-entity section.

#### `attachment_owner_entity_type_enum` (§4.6.2)

`requirement`, `response`, `qa_thread_post`, `internal_comment_post`, `bid_workspace`, `workspace`, `selection_report_draft`, `capability_declaration`

**Notes.** Controls the application-layer polymorphic resolution of `owner_entity_id` in the §4.6.2 Attachment entity. Determines firewall isolation path: `qa_thread_post`, `capability_declaration` → seller-side storage (`{org_id}/seller/{marketplace_domain_id}/...`); all others → buyer-side storage (`{org_id}/buyer/...`). Cross-console reads blocked at the storage-signer layer per §7.2.

#### `attachment_scan_status_enum` (§4.6.2)

`pending`, `scanning`, `clean`, `infected`, `scan_failed`, `scan_timeout`

**Notes.** Anti-malware scan lifecycle. Transitions `pending → scanning → {clean, infected, scan_failed, scan_timeout}`. `infected` is terminal and triggers redaction to `infected_quarantined` state (below). `scan_failed` and `scan_timeout` enter a 3-retry backoff per §22.3.3; after final retry, the row is flagged for Ops manual review and the attachment download surface returns HTTP 423 `attachment_scan_pending`.

#### `attachment_redaction_state_enum` (§4.6.2)

`active`, `dsar_redacted`, `org_deleted_redacted`, `infected_quarantined`

**Notes.** Storage-level redaction state. `active` = object readable per normal permission checks. `dsar_redacted` = object body replaced with `[REDACTED_DSAR]` tombstone per §6.8.3 right-to-erasure. `org_deleted_redacted` = object physically purged on Org hard-delete sweep; row retained for audit integrity with body zeroed to `DESTROYED_ON_ORG_DELETE`. `infected_quarantined` = object moved to quarantine bucket, download blocked with HTTP 451 `attachment_quarantined`.

#### `attachment_redaction_reason_enum` (§4.6.2)

`dsar_subject_request`, `org_hard_delete`, `malware_detected`, `legal_hold_release`, `ops_discretion`

**Notes.** Populated when `redaction_state != active`. `legal_hold_release` covers the narrow case where a legal-hold placeholder is released and the underlying content was redacted during the hold. `ops_discretion` requires Ops Finance or Ops Capability Admin approval with audit trail.

#### `storage_backend_enum` (§4.6.2)

`s3_us_east_1`, `s3_eu_west_1`, `s3_custom_region`, `r2_global`, `gcs_custom`

**Notes.** Residency-bound storage backend selection. `s3_us_east_1` = default US-residency; `s3_eu_west_1` = EU-residency; `s3_custom_region` = enterprise data-residency plan (plan-gated per §34.1). `r2_global` and `gcs_custom` are reserved for future enterprise procurement; not yet provisioned. Storage region MUST match the Org's `data_residency_region` at write time per §40.2; mismatch rejects with HTTP 422 `residency_storage_mismatch`.

#### `inbox_item_group_ttl_class_enum` (§4.3.22)

`session_transient`, `daily`, `weekly`, `persistent_until_dismissed`

**Notes.** Governs the `expires_at` TTL sweep on Inbox Item Groups. `session_transient` = 24h; `daily` = 7d; `weekly` = 30d; `persistent_until_dismissed` = no automatic expiry (cleared on user dismissal or anchor-entity deletion).

#### `notification_item_type` (§4.3.22.1, §20.2.1)

`phase_transition`, `sla_alert`, `qa_mention`, `amendment_notification`, `disagreement_escalation`, `workspace_invite`, `team_assignment`, `scoring_activity`, `response_activity`, `general_update`

**Notes.** Buyer-console InboxItem family enum. Values map one-to-one to the §20.2.1 content-type rows and MUST be extended in Appendix J before §20 adds a new feed filter chip.

#### `inbox_item_priority` (§4.3.22.1)

`high`, `medium`, `low`

**Notes.** Sort band for buyer InboxItem. This replaces the pre-remediation integer priority example in §20.2.2.

#### `notification_delivery_state` (§4.3.22.1)

`visible`, `read`, `dismissed`, `expired`, `archived`

**Notes.** InboxItem lifecycle state for user-visible delivery. `read`, `dismissed`, and `expired` carry timestamp fields on InboxItem; `archived` is the retention-visible state for items still queryable by admin / support views.

#### `pulse_health_weight_set` (§4.3.22.2, §20.3.2)

`pre_phase_6`, `phase_6_to_9`, `phase_10_to_11`, `phase_12_locked`

**Notes.** Records the per-phase Pulse Health Score weight set selected by §20.3.2. Values are derived from Workspace pipeline phase and MUST NOT be user-editable.

#### `pulse_health_color_band` (§4.3.22.2, §20.3.3)

`green`, `yellow`, `red`

**Notes.** Render band for WorkspacePulseHealth. Color token mapping is a design-system concern; this enum only records the semantic band and drives threshold-transition detection for `pulse.health_score_threshold_breached`.

### Contest Status (§4.8.5) — Phase 1.5 Update

**Authored Extension — requires human sign-off.** The existing "Contest Status (§4.8.5)" enum earlier in this appendix is updated to include a terminal `abandoned` state per §4.8.5 dual-path abandonment (90-day Ops-side open-queue non-pickup; 120-day Ops-side in-review non-decision). The authoritative enum is:

`open`, `in_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, `withdrawn`, `escalated`, `abandoned`
