### §48 PLG, Growth Mechanics & Hero Moment — Enum & Role Additions

The enum and role values registered below are referenced by §48.1.5–§48.1.8, §48.2 (GrowthLoopExecution / GrowthLoopKillSwitch), §48.3.5 (S1–S7 network effects), §48.4.12 (Seller Pricing Acceptable-Use Floor), §48.8.2–§48.8.7 (Hero Moment surface + anti-pattern enforcement), and the Appendix G §48 event additions block. All values are governed by §48 authoring; future expansions require a Growth Admin + Product VP sign-off entry in RECONCILIATION.md.

#### `seller_onboarding_phase_enum` (§48.1.5, §48.8)

`pre_arrival`, `phase_1_sso`, `phase_2_capability_review`, `phase_3_first_pass_response`, `phase_4_post_submission_reveal`, `completed`, `errored`, `abandoned`

**Notes.** Monotonic forward progression only. `errored` is reachable from any phase; `abandoned` is reached when no phase progress observed for `phase_idle_ceiling_minutes` (default 90 min; configurable per residency cohort). `completed` requires Phase 4 reveal acknowledgement OR Phase 3 first-pass-response submission with Phase 4 dismissed. Hero Moment phase invariants per §48.1.5; violations emit `seller_onboarding_phase_invariant_violation` (Appendix I).

#### `seller_onboarding_origination_surface_enum` (§48.1.5)

`m1_target_account`, `m5_outreach`, `m15_eoi_invite`, `m17_capability_request`, `direct_signup_organic`, `direct_signup_paid_search`, `partner_referral`, `ops_provisioned`

**Notes.** First five values map directly to the §48.2 origination playbooks. `direct_signup_organic` is the public Capability-page / Featured-listing self-signup path (S2 / S3 loops). `direct_signup_paid_search` reserved for paid-acquisition reactivation (currently feature-flagged off). `partner_referral` reserved for the future affiliate replacement path (L9 was retired; replacement TBD). `ops_provisioned` is the Ops-side seed-tenant provisioning path; requires `ops_growth_admin` role.

#### `seller_onboarding_phase_skip_reason_enum` (§48.1.5)

`client_clock_skew`, `invariant_violation`, `deeplink_bypass`, `degraded_mode_phase_collapse`

**Notes.** `client_clock_skew` is auto-corrected via server `NOW()` substitution (no surfaced error). `invariant_violation` and `deeplink_bypass` page on-call. `degraded_mode_phase_collapse` covers the Sonnet single-pass fallback path that intentionally collapses Phase 2 + Phase 3 into a single rendering window per §48.8.4; not an error.

#### `seller_onboarding_degradation_path_enum` (§48.1.5, §48.8.4)

`sonnet_fallback`, `single_capability_only`, `manual_completion_required`, `blank_kb_manual_capability_entry`

**Notes.** Ordered by user-experience severity. `sonnet_fallback` preserves Phase 3 latency targets at reduced classification quality. `single_capability_only` reduces the first-pass response surface to a single highest-confidence capability. `manual_completion_required` removes auto-population entirely and requires the seller to draft from scratch. `blank_kb_manual_capability_entry` is reached when both pre-arrival Firecrawl and Opus classification fail unrecoverably; activation metric still tracked but expected to fall outside the p90 < 60-min target band.

#### `seller_onboarding_pre_arrival_failure_category_enum` (§48.8.2)

`firecrawl_404`, `firecrawl_5xx`, `firecrawl_rate_limited`, `firecrawl_robots_disallow`, `opus_classification_timeout`, `opus_classification_low_confidence`, `opus_classification_unavailable`, `residency_mismatch_holdback`

**Notes.** Drives the `seller_invite_pre_arrival_failed` event's `failure_category` property. `firecrawl_robots_disallow` is the only category that triggers permanent abandonment (no retry); all others retry on first arrival per `seller_onboarding_pre_arrival_final_state_enum`.

#### `seller_onboarding_pre_arrival_final_state_enum` (§48.8.2)

`fallback_blank_kb`, `retry_on_arrival`, `abandoned`, `partial_success_low_confidence`

**Notes.** `partial_success_low_confidence` is the case where Opus classification returned but with confidence below the `pre_arrival_classification_confidence_floor` (default 0.55); the partial KB is preserved as a hint for in-session Sonnet fallback rather than discarded.

#### `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_kind_enum` (§48.1.7)

`cm1_mid_bid_ai_budget_wall`, `cm2_second_concurrent_bid`, `cm3_first_eoi`, `cm4_kb_ceiling`

**Notes.** Mutually exclusive within `mutual_exclusivity_window_hours` (default 72h) per plan-tier stage. The earliest-emitted moment stands within the same `(seller_org_id, moment_kind, plan_tier)` tuple; later attempts emit `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_already_recorded` (Appendix I) and are suppressed from billing impact. Each moment has one or two canonical plan-from / plan-to mappings per §48.1.7 binding table.

#### `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_triggering_entity_kind_enum` (§48.1.7)

`aiwallet_budget_exhaustion`, `bid_workspace`, `eoi_record`, `kb_entry_count_observation`

**Notes.** Maps 1:1 to the conversion-moment-kind: `cm1_mid_bid_ai_budget_wall` → `aiwallet_budget_exhaustion`, `cm2_second_concurrent_bid` → `bid_workspace`, `cm3_first_eoi` → `eoi_record`, `cm4_kb_ceiling` → `kb_entry_count_observation`. Cross-mapping is rejected at write time as `seller_onboarding_conversion_moment_already_recorded` precondition violation.

`carry_over_token_redeemed`, `carry_over_token_expired`, `upgrade_path_self_service`, `upgrade_path_ops_assisted`, `eoi_draft_promoted_post_upgrade`, `kb_ceiling_observed_post_grace_window`

`creation`, `cite_reinforcement`, `ops_override`, `ai_recomputation`, `time_decay_floor`, `seller_dsar_redaction`

**Notes.** `time_decay_floor` is the nightly job that decays confidence on KB entries with no citations in the last 90 days, floored at the `kb_entry_confidence_floor` (default 0.20). `seller_dsar_redaction` overrides confidence to NULL and marks the entry `redacted_for_dsar`. Drives `kb_entry.confidence_updated` events.

**Notes.** `hero_moment_seed` is the in-session synthesis path during Phase 3 First-Pass Response generation; it carries elevated weight in the §48.3.5 S1 calibration loop because the citation is occurring against a freshly-generated KB entry and validates the entry's relevance immediately.

#### `kb_stake_reveal_moment_enum` (§22.18.6)

`free_tier_kb_landing`, `outcome_debrief`, `conversion_threshold`

**Notes.** Three canonically-registered stake-reveal surfaces introduced by §22.18.6 KB Value Capture & Stake-Building Stake-Reveal Moments. Closed enum — the three values are mutually exclusive per render and are the ONLY legal values for the `reveal_moment` property on `stake_reveal_rendered` / `stake_reveal_displayed` PostHog events (Appendix G) when the reveal was triggered by the §22.18 KB-value-capture surface family. Dual-emit window in effect from v7.0.0 through v7.1.0 per the Appendix G alias-retirement note; after v7.1.0 the legacy `stake_reveal_rendered_kb_value_capture` alias is retired and only the canonical event carrying `reveal_moment ∈ kb_stake_reveal_moment_enum` is emitted. The `conversion_threshold` value maps to the §48.1.7 CM1 / CM2 / CM3 / CM4 conversion-moment modals as a precursor stake-build; `free_tier_kb_landing` surfaces before KB-ceiling pressure, and `outcome_debrief` surfaces after a bid closes and can feed later conversion-moment eligibility. Extension requires Product VP sign-off and a new §22.18.6 sub-subsection.

`queued`, `running`, `ready`, `expired`, `failed`

**Notes.** Closed lifecycle enum for KBExportJob. Transitions are governed by §22.18.2.5; `ready`, `expired`, and `failed` are terminal for the job row, though a seller may initiate a new export.

#### `kb_export_format_kind_enum` (§22.18.2.1, §32.9.1)

`markdown_zip_v1`, `jsonl_zip_v1`, `markdown_and_jsonl_zip_v1`

**Notes.** Canonical format enum for the §32.9 Seller KB Export endpoint and the §22.18.2.1 `KBExportJob` entity `format` field. `markdown_zip_v1` produces a ZIP archive of per-entry `.md` files with YAML frontmatter carrying canonical metadata (entry_id, namespace_path, confidence, staleness, citation_count, last_cited_at, residency_region, export_version, generated_at_iso8601). `jsonl_zip_v1` produces a ZIP archive containing one or more JSONL shards of 10k-entry max shard size, with one JSON object per line mirroring the KBEntry schema plus the archive-shape envelope fields. `markdown_and_jsonl_zip_v1` is the default and combines both in a single archive with `/markdown/` and `/jsonl/` top-level directories and a root `manifest.json` enumerating both trees with SHA-256 per file. All three formats embed the identical archive-shape envelope defined in §22.18.2.1 — format affects only the per-entry serialization, never the envelope. Version suffix `_v1` reserves namespace for future incompatible revisions; a `_v2` format must be added as a new enum value and negotiated via explicit `format` request, never silently substituted for `_v1` requests (archive-shape invariance AC #85 §32.9.4). No format is plan-tier-gated — all three values are available on every plan per §22.18.1 P1 No-Paywall Export invariant.

#### `kb_export_failure_code_enum` (§22.18.2.1, §32.9.1)

`timeout`, `archive_size_exceeded`, `vector_source_unreadable`, `provenance_source_unreadable`, `residency_evacuation`, `org_suspended`, `internal_error`

**Notes.** Canonical failure-code enum for the §22.18.2.1 `KBExportJob.failure_code` field and the `kb.export.failed` webhook (Appendix C) / `kb_export_failed` PostHog event (Appendix G). This enum is distinct from the synchronous HTTP error codes in Appendix I "KB Export Endpoint Errors (added §32.9 / §22.18)" — HTTP errors are returned at request time when the job is rejected before queuing; `kb_export_failure_code_enum` values are returned inside the async `KBExportJob` row after queuing completed but generation failed. `timeout` fires when the worker exceeds `kb_export_generation_ceiling_minutes` (default 20 min); retryable. `archive_size_exceeded` fires when the generated archive would exceed `kb_export_archive_byte_ceiling` (default 2 GiB) — retryable only after the caller reduces scope via narrower `namespace_filter` or `include_attachments=false`; job is not retried automatically. `vector_source_unreadable` and `provenance_source_unreadable` are backend-side read failures against the Convex KB shard or provenance graph shard respectively; both retryable with exponential backoff. `residency_evacuation` fires when the Org's data-residency region is mid-evacuation per §6.8 / §40.4 and the KB shard is read-locked; retryable after evacuation completes. `org_suspended` is terminal — emitted when the Org enters `suspended` status mid-generation; not retryable, customer must contact Ops. `internal_error` is the catch-all unclassified failure; retryable once automatically, then surfaced. The enum is closed; a new failure mode requires a new enum value, a §22.18.2.1 table row, an Appendix G property-registration update, and CI gate `kb_export_failure_code_enum_exhaustive` (asserts every enum value is handled by the worker's switch with no fallthrough default).

#### `kb_citation_graph_edge_kind` (§4.4.31, §22.18.3.4)

`response_grounding`, `evidence_attribution`, `capability_extraction`

**Notes.** Closed discriminator for KBCitationGraphEdge weight assignment. The default edge weights are registered at §4.4.31 and §22.18.3.4; a new value requires an explicit edge-weight row and a win-rate recompute migration.

#### `kb_citation_graph_bid_outcome` (§4.4.31, §22.18.3.4)

`open`, `won`, `lost`, `no_decision`, `cancelled`

**Notes.** Snapshot enum of the seller Bid Workspace outcome as consumed by the citation graph. `no_decision` and `cancelled` preserve citation history but do not update `KBEntry.win_rate_weight`.

#### `capability_declaration_suggestion_state` (§4.4.32, §22.18.3.5)

`pending_review`, `published`, `dismissed`, `superseded`, `expired`

**Notes.** Closed lifecycle enum for CapabilityDeclarationSuggestion rows. Only `pending_review` can transition to a terminal state; terminal rows never reopen and a future clustering run emits a new suggestion if the source cluster changes.

#### `capability_declaration_suggestion_dismissed_reason` (§4.4.32)

`not_supported`, `duplicate`, `too_broad`, `too_narrow`, `bad_evidence`, `seller_not_ready`, `other`

**Notes.** Seller-facing dismissal reason for suggested capability claims. Used to suppress exact-repeat suggestions and to tune the clustering pipeline; free-text notes, if any, are stored outside the enum and follow §6.8 redaction.

#### `system_agent_id_enum` (§4.6.1, §14, §22.18.2.1 — Authored Extension)

`system_agent_ingest_pipeline`, `system_agent_classification_pipeline`, `system_agent_confidence_recomputation`, `system_agent_time_decay_sweeper`, `system_agent_kb_exporter`, `system_agent_webhook_dispatcher`, `system_agent_residency_evacuator`, `system_agent_dsar_redactor`, `system_agent_plan_downgrade_sweeper`, `system_agent_pricing_table_pinner`, `system_agent_billing_reconciler`, `system_agent_scim_sync`, `system_agent_audit_integrity_verifier`, `system_agent_retention_purger`, `system_agent_managed_agent_bridge`, `system_agent_spec_lint_pipeline`, `system_agent_deploy_validator`

**Notes.** Closed enum of internal service identities used as the `created_by` / `updated_by` FK value when an audit-logged entity mutation is initiated by a Sourcera system agent rather than a User row. Each identity is a stable, versionless string — the agent's underlying code version is tracked separately via the `system_agent_code_version` property on the owning audit-event row and is NOT encoded into the enum value, preserving cross-version referential stability for `BillingAdminAuditAction` / §4.6.1 Audit Event rows. Rendering surfaces MUST display the human-readable label (defined in the §22.18.2.1 and §14 adjacent tables — e.g., "Sourcera System · KB Exporter") and MUST NOT render the raw enum value. `system_agent_kb_exporter` is the identity used by the §32.9 worker for KBExportJob row mutations and for the provenance `export_archive_manifest.generated_by` field. All `system_agent_*` rows are treated as non-User FKs by the DSAR anonymizer (§6.8) — the enum value survives anonymization. Adding a new value requires: (1) an Authored-Extension reconciliation-log entry, (2) an Appendix G property-registration update if the agent emits PostHog events, (3) a CI gate `system_agent_id_enum_no_alias_collision` (asserts no value aliases any existing User UUID and no two values share a human-readable label). Authored Extension — requires human sign-off; flagged.

#### `kb_export_lifecycle_audit_subaction_enum` (§22.18.2.1, §32.9.1, extends `billing_admin_action` namespace)

`initiated`, `ready`, `expired`, `download_presigned_url_minted`

**Notes.** Sub-action discriminator for the `org.kb_exported` audit action (registered in the Billing Admin Audit Action Types subsection above via cross-reference). Each KBExportJob emits exactly one `initiated` audit-event row at POST /kb/export time (with `changes` carrying the request body's filter set and the minted `export_id`), zero-or-one `ready` rows at worker-success (with `changes` carrying `archive_bytes`, `archive_sha256`, `entries_exported`, `documents_exported`, `attachments_exported`, `citation_edges_exported`, `generation_duration_seconds`, `residency_region`), zero-or-one `expired` rows at the 72h TTL expiry (with `changes` carrying `expired_at`), and zero-to-N `download_presigned_url_minted` rows (one per GET poll that re-mints a presigned URL — capped at 10 mints per §32.9.2 re-mint semantics). All four sub-action rows carry `entity_type = 'kb_export_job'`, `entity_id = export_id`, and share the same `request_id` for forensic correlation. The audit-completeness AC #92 §32.9.4 asserts that every terminal KBExportJob state has exactly the expected audit-row count per sub-action. Retention: standard §40.2 plan-tier defaults — NOT the 7-year financial-record exception (KBExportJob is not a billing artifact; the `org.kb_exported` action exists in the billing-admin audit namespace solely because the action is authorized at `seller_kb_admin` / `seller_org_admin` RBAC rows that co-occur in the Billing Admin Audit View filter per §5.2.1.4).

**Billing Admin Audit Action Types — §22.18 / §32.9 Extension.** The subsection "Billing Admin Audit Action Types (§5.2.1, §4.8.3, §4.8.5, §4.8.7, §4.8.8, §4.8.9, §4.8.10, §4.8.11, §34.12.6, §34.13)" above is EXTENDED with the following partition:

**Seller KB Export (§22.18, §32.9):**

`org.kb_exported.initiated`, `org.kb_exported.ready`, `org.kb_exported.expired`, `org.kb_exported.download_presigned_url_minted`

The four qualified strings follow the form `org.kb_exported.<sub-action>` where `<sub-action>` ∈ `kb_export_lifecycle_audit_subaction_enum`. The `entity_type` enum in §4.6.1 is extended with `kb_export_job` to accommodate these actions. Per the §22.18.7 Deploy-Time Validator Rules, CI gate `audit_action_kb_export_lifecycle_registry_complete` asserts the four qualified strings are present in the audit-action registry AND emitted by the §32.9 worker's four lifecycle hooks with no dead-code path. Retention override: these rows follow standard §40.2 plan-tier retention (NOT the 7-year financial-record exception). DSAR: the user attribution field `user_id` anonymizes on §6.8 right-to-erasure request; `entity_id = export_id` and the qualified action string survive — the archive referenced by `export_id` is itself subject to §22.18.2.1 DSAR deletion rules which are independent of the audit-row retention.

### §50 Ops Console Controlled Vocabulary Additions {#appendix-j-section-50-additions}

The enums below are referenced from §50 (Sourcera Ops Console), §4.6.3 OpsSession, and §50.5 Ops-Tagged Audit Actor pattern. All values are canonical and registered only in Appendix J; §50 authoring MUST cite this appendix rather than re-declare values inline.

#### `ops_role_kind` (§50.3.1 canonical six-role matrix)

`ops_admin`, `pricing_admin`, `template_reviewer`, `support_agent`, `fraud_analyst`, `finance`

**Notes.** Canonical six-role set per Summary C.94. `ops_admin` is additionally the super-role for quorum signoff (§50.4.4), Ops-role-assignment authority (§50.3.3), emergency grant authority (§50.3.5), and time-box-override authority. Two Ops-internal variants extend the role registry for escalation-chain integrity but are enforced solely within the Ops-internal role subsystem and are NEVER surfaced to customers via the Customer-Visible Projection (§50.4.8): `ops_admin_escalated` (used for dual-control co-approval on break-glass DB access per §50.2.4), and the historical `ops_growth_admin`, `ops_taxonomy_admin`, `ops_capability_admin`, `ops_finance_admin`, `ops_security_admin`, `ops_verification_reviewer`, `ops_verification_senior_reviewer` (preserved for backward compatibility with §48.4.12, §4.4.21, and other pre-§50 registrations per the Ops-role-namespace-preservation convention). The canonical six-role matrix supersedes the granular pre-§50 roles for all §50 Ops Console surfaces; pre-§50 capabilities are subsumed as follows: `ops_growth_admin` ≡ `ops_admin` (the growth-admin role surface continues to function as an alias during the v7.0.x transition window and retires at v7.1.0 per the role-migration reconciliation entry), `ops_capability_admin` and `ops_taxonomy_admin` are subsumed under `pricing_admin` for rate-card / taxonomy-lock mutations and `template_reviewer` for template-library mutations, `ops_finance_admin` ≡ `finance`, `ops_security_admin` retains its distinct role for break-glass DB access (§50.2.4 requires this role or `ops_admin_escalated`), `ops_verification_reviewer` / `ops_verification_senior_reviewer` are subsumed under `support_agent` for §4.4.21 verification-review flows with the senior role expressed as an additional capability envelope row on the `support_agent` assignment rather than a distinct role kind. Customer-Visible Projection renders the canonical six-role kind ONLY — the pre-§50 granular roles are Sourcera-internal and never emitted to a customer surface. Deploy-time CI gate `ops_role_canonicalization_lock` asserts every OpsSession row, AuditEvent row, and PostHog event carries a canonical-six-role value in `ops_role_at_session_open` / `ops_role_at_invocation` / equivalent. Adding a new canonical role requires a §50.3.1 sub-subsection, dual Ops-Director sign-off, and an Authored-Extension reconciliation entry.

#### `ops_session_state` (§4.6.3, §50.4.3)

`pending_justification`, `pending_quorum`, `active`, `closed_by_ops`, `closed_by_time_box`, `closed_by_customer`, `closed_by_ops_admin`, `blocked_strict_notify`

**Notes.** Canonical state machine per §50.4.3. `pending_justification` is the insert-time state for every OpsSession; the row CANNOT bypass this state. `pending_quorum` is reached only when the intended action requires dual-control per §50.4.4 envelope policy; sessions that do not require quorum transition directly `pending_justification → active`. The four `closed_*` variants are mutually exclusive and terminal; a closed OpsSession CANNOT reopen. `blocked_strict_notify` is the terminal state for sessions that failed strict-mode customer-notification dispatch per §50.4.5; it is distinct from the closed states because it represents a never-activated session (actions_taken_count = 0 by construction). State-machine transitions are governed by Appendix L entry §50.1 (authored below). Adding a state requires §50.4.3 sub-subsection amendment and the CI gate `ops_session_state_machine_exhaustive`.

#### `ops_session_justification_category` (§4.6.3, §50.4.1)

`customer_support_ticket`, `incident_investigation`, `billing_correction`, `data_correction`, `abuse_investigation`, `security_investigation`, `legal_hold_assistance`, `dsar_fulfillment`, `ops_internal_audit`, `onboarding_assistance`, `post_incident_cleanup`, `other`

**Notes.** The `other` value is permitted only when `justification_note` is ≥ 120 characters (stricter floor than the general 20-character minimum) and writes an internal Ops review flag for monthly sampling. Each category has a default expected-duration band applied to the time-box defaults (e.g., `customer_support_ticket` defaults to 30 minutes; `incident_investigation` defaults to 60 minutes; `security_investigation` defaults to 30 minutes with step-up re-auth required; `dsar_fulfillment` defaults to 20 minutes with legal-hold cross-check). A `linked_support_ticket_ref` is required when the category is `customer_support_ticket` or `onboarding_assistance`. Adding a category requires §50.4.1 sub-subsection amendment.

#### `ops_session_close_reason` (§4.6.3, §50.4.3)

`ops_completed`, `ops_user_abandoned`, `time_box_expired`, `customer_revoked`, `ops_admin_force_closed`, `system_failure_rollback`, `escalation_handoff`, `policy_violation_detected`

**Notes.** Close-reason populated on every transition to a terminal `closed_*` state. `ops_completed` — normal completion; the Ops user explicitly closed the session after finishing the task. `ops_user_abandoned` — Ops user went idle for > 15 minutes without action (auto-detected). `time_box_expired` — time-box enforcement job triggered close per §50.4.2. `customer_revoked` — customer exercised §50.4.7 revoke surface. `ops_admin_force_closed` — Ops Admin force-closed the session mid-active (e.g., upon suspected fraud or policy drift). `system_failure_rollback` — transactional rollback due to a system-level failure during an in-flight mutation; the OpsSession row is terminated to preserve audit integrity. `escalation_handoff` — session closed to open a parent_ops_session-linked successor session (chain-depth bound per §50.3.5 escape-hatch). `policy_violation_detected` — automated policy drift detector observed an invariant breach during the session and force-closed. Adding a reason requires §50.4.3 sub-subsection amendment.

#### `ops_session_notification_failure_code` (§4.6.3, §50.4.5)

`no_active_org_owner`, `no_active_billing_admin_fallback`, `email_transport_failure`, `in_app_outbox_failure`, `loops_template_invalid`, `recipient_unsubscribe_attempted`, `residency_transport_unavailable`, `vendor_outage`, `rate_limit_transient`, `customer_notification_suppressed_by_tenant_policy`

**Notes.** The `customer_notification_suppressed_by_tenant_policy` value is reserved for a narrow exception: a regulated-tenant policy (e.g., certain defense / intelligence deployments) that requires Ops access to NOT emit customer-facing notifications for a named set of residency regions. This exception is hardcoded in the deployment-residency policy and is NEVER a runtime-configurable customer setting; it exists to accommodate specific regulated-deployment contracts. Any OpsSession using this suppression must carry a signed, cryptographically-witnessed deployment-policy attestation in `auth_factor_evidence_json.tenant_policy_attestation_sha256`. The `recipient_unsubscribe_attempted` value records an anomaly: the recipient's email address is flagged as unsubscribed in the transactional-email provider (Loops.so), which SHOULD be impossible per §50.4.5 no-customer-opt-out invariant — this code pages Ops observability as a potential data-pipeline breach. All other values route to standard retry / escalation flows.

#### `ops_session_console_scope` (§4.6.3)

`buyer`, `seller`

**Notes.** Binary console selector per §50.2.1 Deployment Isolation; an OpsSession MUST target exactly one console. Cross-console Ops operations that genuinely require both consoles (rare; typically cross-console-bridge audits) are implemented as two OpsSessions with `parent_ops_session_id` linkage. There is NO `cross_console` or `both` value — §7.2 Dual-Console Firewall integrity depends on this invariant. Adding a value would violate §50.2.1 and §7.2; any such attempt requires a fresh authoring round with Security-Architect sign-off.

#### `audit_event_actor_type` (§4.6.1 extension, §50.5.1)

`customer_user`, `system_agent`, `ops_actor`, `external_integration`

**Notes.** Extends the implicit `actor_type` field on AuditEvent rows to name the four legitimate actor kinds. `customer_user` is a human user of the customer Org (the common case). `system_agent` is one of the internal service identities registered in `system_agent_id_enum`, including managed-agent bridge, spec-lint, and deploy-validator service identities. `ops_actor` is a Sourcera Ops user operating under an active OpsSession per §50.5.1; AuditEvent rows with this value MUST carry a non-null `ops_session_id`. `external_integration` is an API call originating from a customer-configured integration (CRM Sync, custom webhook consumer, etc.) where the action is attributed to the integration principal rather than to the user who configured it — rare but required for certain §31.9 CRM-sync-initiated background mutations. Deploy-time CI gate `audit_event_actor_type_enum_exhaustive` asserts every AuditEvent insert code path sets `actor_type` and that `user_id`, `ops_session_id`, `system_agent_id`, and `external_integration_principal_id` are populated consistently per the enum value (governed by the `audit_event_actor_type_consistency_violation` error per Appendix I).

#### `ops_role_assignment_state` (§50.3.4)

`proposed`, `pending_quorum`, `active`, `rejected`, `revoked`, `expired`

**Notes.** Canonical state machine for OpsRoleAssignment rows per §50.3.4. `proposed` is the insert-time state. `pending_quorum` is reached when a second Ops Admin signoff is required. `active` is the operational state; the role is enforced at OpsSession open time by checking `ops_role_assignment_state = active AND role_assignment_expires_at > now()`. `rejected` is the terminal state for proposals that failed quorum (either by explicit rejection or by quorum timeout). `revoked` is the terminal state for active assignments explicitly revoked by an Ops Admin (not the subject user — self-revocation is forbidden). `expired` is the terminal state reached when `role_assignment_expires_at` elapses without renewal. Each transition writes an AuditEvent row with `entity_type=ops_role_assignment`. Adding a state requires §50.3.4 sub-subsection amendment.

#### `ops_capability_kind` (§50.3.2 envelope capability registry)

`session_open`, `session_close`, `customer_org_read`, `customer_org_mutation`, `billing_read`, `billing_mutation`, `audit_read`, `audit_export_projection`, `kb_read`, `kb_mutation`, `template_library_mutation`, `rate_card_mutation`, `outcome_contract_mutation`, `pricing_table_version_pin`, `taxonomy_lock_override`, `sim_signal_review`, `abuse_report_triage`, `abuse_report_resolution`, `seller_verification_decision`, `marketplace_listing_mutation`, `contest_record_decision`, `ai_operation_reversal`, `committed_spend_contract_mutation`, `free_allowance_quota_override`, `plan_downgrade_for_abuse`, `eoi_rate_limit_override`, `zombie_reactivation`, `promoted_listing_mutation`, `featured_placement_mutation`, `vendor_opt_out_mutation`, `break_glass_db_access`, `rate_limit_override_issue`, `incident_declare`, `incident_postmortem_publish`, `ops_role_assignment_propose`, `ops_role_assignment_signoff`, `ops_role_assignment_revoke`, `ops_session_force_close`, `support_ticket_cross_reference_read`

**Notes.** Canonical set of Ops capabilities referenced from the §50.3.2 Capability Envelope Matrix. Each value maps to zero-or-more canonical `ops_role_kind` values per the envelope matrix; the mapping is the ground truth for §50 access control and is tested by deploy-time CI gate `ops_capability_envelope_matrix_complete`. Adding a capability requires §50.3.2 sub-subsection amendment, an envelope-row mapping, and a corresponding AuditEvent action registration (below).

#### `ops_action_kind` (§4.4.27 extension, §50 additions)

The existing enum registered at §4.4.27 (`plan_downgrade_for_abuse`, `eoi_rate_limit_override`, `taxonomy_lock_override`, `zombie_reactivation`, `k_anon_floor_temporary_lower`, `signal_integrity_review_open`, `seller_pricing_fraud_clear`, `seller_pricing_fraud_uphold`) is EXTENDED with the following §50 values (truly additive):

`ops_residency_tier_granted`, `break_glass_db_access`, `ops_session_customer_revoked`, `incident_declared`, `incident_postmortem_published`, `ops_role_emergency_grant`, `ops_role_assignment_quorum_expired`, `ops_rate_limit_override`, `ops_session_force_closed`, `ops_session_blocked_strict_notify`, `ops_session_degraded_notify_mode_activated`, `ops_session_degraded_notify_mode_acknowledged`, `ops_session_quorum_signoff_granted`, `ops_session_quorum_signoff_expired`, `ops_role_assignment_proposed`, `ops_role_assignment_rejected`, `ops_role_assignment_revoked`, `ops_role_assignment_expired`, `ops_capability_invocation_denied`

The §4.4.27 value-count assertion in RECONCILIATION.md is updated in lockstep. Deploy-time CI gate `ops_action_kind_exhaustive` asserts every OpsActionRecord insert path uses a registered value (no free-form strings) and that every value is emitted by at least one code path (no dead-code entries). #### `ops_policy_kind_enum` (§50 policy denial taxonomy; drives PostHog `ops_session_policy_enforced.policy_kind`)

`capability_outside_envelope`, `cross_console_access_denied`, `cross_org_access_denied`, `time_box_exceeded`, `step_up_reauth_stale`, `step_up_reauth_required`, `quorum_required`, `quorum_self_signoff_forbidden`, `residency_partition_denial`, `justification_invalid`, `device_posture_failed`, `per_user_concurrency_exceeded`, `session_overlap_conflict`, `chain_depth_exceeded`, `auth_evidence_incomplete`, `customer_revocation_cooldown`, `rate_limit_override_duration_exceeded`, `rate_limit_override_unauthorized`, `break_glass_co_approver_required`, `break_glass_unauthorized`, `incident_declaration_unauthorized`, `export_projection_unauthorized`

Deploy-time CI gate `ops_policy_kind_enum_appendix_i_pairing` asserts every enum value has a paired Appendix I row and vice versa; drift fails the build. ### Ops-Tagged Audit Action Types (§50.5.1 extension to §4.6.1 Audit Event Action Registry)

The bare-verb enum at "Audit Event Action Types" above is extended to recognize a small set of Ops-specific qualified actions that MAY appear in AuditEvent rows with `actor_type=ops_actor`. These actions are emitted by Customer-API mutations that pass through the Ops-as-impersonator path (§50.2.3); the `action` values themselves are NOT new — they are the same bare verbs (`created`, `updated`, `deleted`, etc.) used for customer-user actions, BUT the `actor_type`, `ops_session_id`, and `actor_role` (canonical six-role kind per `ops_role_kind`) fields are populated to indicate Ops attribution. There is therefore no new action-verb namespace; the namespace extension is strictly in the actor-attribution fields.

**Ops-Internal Audit Event Action Registry (distinct from customer-visible AuditEvent).** A second audit row-type is emitted for Sourcera-internal actions that do not mutate a customer-visible entity (e.g., OpsSession lifecycle, OpsRoleAssignment transitions, break-glass DB access invocation). These write to the Ops-internal audit subsystem (`OpsActionRecord`, §4.4.27) and use the `ops_action_kind` enum canonicalized above. Ops-internal audit rows are NEVER emitted to a customer surface — they remain within the Sourcera Ops project and are accessible only to `ops_admin` and `support_agent` (read-only) roles.

**Deploy-time validator.** CI gate `ops_actor_audit_event_dual_path_integrity` asserts that every Customer-API mutation executed under an active OpsSession writes (a) exactly one customer-surface AuditEvent row with `actor_type=ops_actor`, and (b) exactly one Ops-internal OpsActionRecord row with the matching `ops_session_id` — the pair MUST commit in the same transaction or both roll back. The customer-surface AuditEvent row surfaces in the Billing Admin Audit View (§5.2.1.4 extended by §50.5.4) and drives the Customer-Visible Projection (§50.4.8).

### §51 Product Usage Analytics Enum Cluster {#appendix-j-section-51-additions}

The enums below are registered as part of §51 Product Usage Analytics & PLG Instrumentation. Each value is bound to an Appendix G event property, an Appendix I error code, or a §51 data-model field; deploy-time CI gates assert round-trip integrity per the per-enum notes.

#### `event_family` (§51.1.4 canonical family registry; drives PostHog outbox routing and dashboards)

`ai_capability`, `workspace`, `billing`, `vendor`, `seller_kb`, `bid`, `marketplace`, `identity`, `ops_surface`, `analytics_meta`, `system_job`

**Notes.** Exactly 11 canonical families. Every PostHog event MUST belong to exactly one family; cross-family emission is blocked at the validator. Adding a family requires a §51.1.4 amendment, an Appendix G subsection, a Sourcera-internal family-registration event (`usage_analytics_event_family_registered`), and a two-approver quorum signoff per §51.1.6. Deploy-time CI gate `event_family_exhaustive` asserts every PostHog event schema maps to exactly one registered family and no family is dead (every family has ≥ 1 registered event after 90 days).

#### `console_kind` (Appendix G preamble required property; §51.2.1 envelope contract)

`buyer`, `seller`, `ops`, `public_api`, `system_job`

**Notes.** Canonical closed enum for the `console` property on every PostHog event. `buyer` and `seller` are customer-surface consoles; `ops` is the Sourcera Ops Console (§50); `public_api` is customer-API-driven events not tied to a visible console; `system_job` is scheduler-driven or cron-driven events with no user-interactive surface. Cross-console leakage (e.g., an event with `console=buyer` emitted into the seller PostHog project) is blocked at the validator with `cross_console_leak` (see `usage_envelope_violation_kind`). Console-firewall integrity per §25 is enforced via this enum; any new console kind requires a §25 amendment.

#### `usage_dashboard_kind` (§51.3/§51.4/§51.5 dashboard surface registry)

`org_level`, `user_level`, `seller_parity`

**Notes.** Bounded to three canonical dashboards. `org_level` is the Buyer Org-Level Usage Dashboard (§51.3); `user_level` is the User-Level Usage Dashboard (§51.4); `seller_parity` is the Seller Usage Parity Dashboard (§51.5). Adding a dashboard kind requires a new §51.N subsection with 5+ numbered ACs and an Appendix G event-property amendment; `usage_dashboard_viewed.dashboard_kind` and `usage_dashboard_panel_interacted.dashboard_kind` enum-coverage is asserted at CI-gate `usage_dashboard_kind_exhaustive`.

#### `usage_dashboard_panel_id` (§51.3.2/§51.4.2/§51.5.2 panel registry)

`org_spend_by_capability`, `org_acceptance_rate`, `org_top_consumers`, `org_trend_vs_prior_3mo`, `org_time_saved`, `user_spend_by_capability`, `user_accept_reject`, `user_capability_mix`, `user_time_saved`, `user_activity_heatmap`, `seller_bid_spend`, `seller_kb_utilization`, `seller_win_rate_correlation`, `seller_capability_mix`, `seller_time_saved`

#### Rate-Limit Classes for §51 (§32.4.5 binding)

The §51 API endpoints consume the canonical §32.4.5 / Appendix J `api_rate_limit_class` values below:

- `analytics_read` — applied to `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/analytics/usage/snapshot`, `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/analytics/usage/live`, `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/analytics/usage/export/{export_id}`, `GET /v1/users/{user_id}/analytics/usage/summary`, `GET /v1/seller-orgs/{seller_org_id}/analytics/usage/snapshot`, `GET /v1/seller-orgs/{seller_org_id}/analytics/usage/kb-utilization`, and `GET /v1/seller-orgs/{seller_org_id}/analytics/usage/win-rate-correlation`. Default: 60 rpm per Org; Enterprise: 300 rpm.
- `analytics_export` — applied to panel export endpoints (`GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/analytics/usage/export`, `GET /v1/users/{user_id}/analytics/usage/export`, `GET /v1/seller-orgs/{seller_org_id}/analytics/usage/export`). Default: 5 rpm per User per Org; Enterprise: 20 rpm per User per Org. Backed by a signed, time-limited export URL per §32.13 export-URL contract.

**Notes.** Deploy-time CI gate `analytics_rate_limit_class_enforcement` asserts every §51 endpoint declares a rate-limit class and the class is enforced in the API gateway. The spec-wide gate `api_rate_limit_class_registry_consistency` rejects any §51 class not registered in §32.4.5 and Appendix J `api_rate_limit_class`. CI gate `appendix_j_rate_limit_class_path_resolves` (§M.5.35) asserts every Appendix J path listed above exactly matches a §51.3.5 / §51.4.4 / §51.5.5 endpoint row and forbids legacy `/usage/dashboard` aliases unless a dual-emit/deprecation row is authored.

### §3 UX Token & State Catalog Enum Cluster {#appendix-j-section-3-ux-additions}

Registered in the §3.6–§3.11 Authoring Pass (2026-04-22). Each enum is authoritative for its listed authoring home; all inline §3 uses of the enum names below dereference to this cluster.

#### `input_validation_state` (§3.6)

`default`, `focus`, `error`, `warning`, `success`, `disabled`, `read_only`

**Notes.** Per-field rendering state. Precedence from lowest to highest: `default` < `focus` < `success` < `warning` < `error` < `disabled`. `read_only` composes orthogonally with `default` or `success`. Exactly one active state per field at any time. Deploy-time CI gate `input_validation_state_coverage` asserts every component in the Input family registers a rendering for each of the seven values.

#### `page_state_kind` (§3.7)

`loading`, `empty`, `error`, `partial`, `ready`

**Notes.** Page-level state machine. `partial` is the intermediate state when one or more panels have resolved but at least one is still loading; content-shaped skeletons render in unloaded panels; primary chrome renders normally. The transition `partial → ready` is gated on all top-level panels resolving. Every state transition emits `ui_page_state_changed` (Appendix G) with `from_state`, `to_state`, `latency_ms`. Deploy-time CI gate `page_state_kind_coverage` asserts every registered `page_surface_kind` has treatments for all five values.

#### `page_surface_kind` (§3.7)

`dashboard`, `matrix`, `detail`, `settings`, `ops_console`, `knowledge_base`

**Notes.** Per-surface state-catalog key. Binds the state-treatment rules in §3.7.5 to the surface it applies to. Deploy-time CI gate `page_surface_kind_coverage` asserts every top-level route registers a surface kind.

#### `empty_state_next_best_action_kind` (§3.7)

`create`, `import`, `invite`, `browse`, `configure`, `contact_ops`, `none`

**Notes.** Empty-state primary-CTA taxonomy. Every empty state MUST map to exactly one value. `none` is reserved for terminal/plan-gated empty states where the recovery path is upgrade or out-of-product (routes through the §5.11 Feature Access Matrix upgrade flow). Deploy-time CI gate `empty_state_next_best_action_coverage` asserts every registered `page_surface_kind` × empty tuple declares a next-best-action value.

#### `error_recovery_kind` (§3.7)

`retry`, `reload`, `contact_support`, `change_input`, `wait`, `upgrade_plan`, `view_status`, `no_recovery`

**Notes.** Failure / Reason / Recovery recovery-path taxonomy. Every error state MUST offer at least one recovery option from this enum. `no_recovery` is reserved for terminal states (permanently deleted resource, revoked permission) and always pairs with a "Return to parent surface" fallback link. Retry actions honor §3.7.6 retry-storm suppression (exponential backoff 30s/60s/120s/300s ceiling).

#### `side_peek_navigation_direction` (§3.8)

`prev`, `next`

**Notes.** Navigation direction for Cmd+[ (prev) and Cmd+] (next) peek traversal. Drives `ui_side_peek_navigated.direction`. Reaching a pagination bound emits `reached_bound: true` and disables the direction's keyboard action without closing the peek.

#### `bulk_action_selection_mode` (§3.10)

`visible_only`, `all_in_filter`

**Notes.** Cmd+A disambiguation. `visible_only` selects the rows currently rendered; `all_in_filter` selects every row matching the active filter definition, capped at 10,000 rows per §3.10.4. `all_in_filter` preserves its filter definition across pagination, sort changes, and re-renders; row-set resolution is recomputed at dispatch time. `visible_only` preserves a row-ID set. Filter changes mid-selection re-evaluate `all_in_filter` but preserve `visible_only` selections per row ID.

#### `theme_mode` (§3.11)

`light`, `dark`, `system`

**Notes.** User-facing theme preference. `system` follows OS `prefers-color-scheme`; `light` and `dark` are explicit overrides that persist regardless of OS changes. Future value `high_contrast` is reserved by §3.11.8 as an Authored Extension pending human sign-off; implementations MUST tolerate the reserved value (forward-compatible serialization) but MUST NOT render it until the extension is signed off.

#### `theme_override_source` (§3.11)

`org_default`, `user_override`, `system_preference`

**Notes.** Resolution-order attribution. Resolution order: `user_override` wins if set; else `org_default`; else `system_preference`. Emitted on `ui_theme_mode_resolved.source` so downstream analytics can distinguish user-set vs system-inherited theme changes.

#### `accessibility_mention_announcement_priority` (§4.2.14, §37.4)

`assertive`, `polite`

**Notes.** Governs mention live-region priority for §3.12.9 and Settings -> Accessibility. `assertive` is the default because mentions are collaboration interrupts; `polite` is available for users who prefer lower-priority announcements.

#### `accessibility_high_contrast_mode` (§4.2.14, §37.4)

`auto`, `off`, `light`, `dark`

**Notes.** `auto` follows OS `forced-colors` / `prefers-contrast`; `off` suppresses explicit Sourcera High Contrast rendering while preserving browser / OS forced-colors behavior; `light` and `dark` select Sourcera-authored high-contrast token variants. This enum is separate from `theme_mode`; it does not make `high_contrast` an emitted theme_mode value before §3.11.8 sign-off.

#### `assistive_tech_family` (§4.2.14, §37.4)

`nvda`, `jaws`, `voiceover_macos`, `voiceover_ios`, `voiceover_ipados`, `switch_control`, `other`, `unknown`

**Notes.** Optional self-declared compatibility target for shortcut-remapping warnings. Sourcera MUST NOT infer this value through fingerprinting; it is user-entered or `unknown`.

#### `accessibility_audit_violation_severity` (§37.5)

`critical`, `serious`, `moderate`, `minor`

**Notes.** Mirrors `axe-core@4.10.x` impact buckets for §37.5 audit reporting. Severity mapping to Sourcera P0/P1/P2/P3 defects is done in §37.5 and §42.3.0, not in this enum.

#### `audit_event_action_type` — §37 accessibility preference extension

Extends the existing `audit_event_action_type` controlled vocabulary with: `accessibility.preference_updated`.

**Notes.** Valid when `entity_type = user_accessibility_preference`; emitted by Settings -> Accessibility saves per §37.4 and §4.2.14 AC #2. Payloads include changed field names only and MUST NOT include raw `assistive_tech_keymap_overrides_json`.

#### `audit_event_entity_type` — §37 accessibility preference extension

Extends the existing AuditEvent `entity_type` controlled vocabulary with: `user_accessibility_preference`.

**Notes.** Entity type for §4.2.14 UserAccessibilityPreference audit rows. The audit row's `entity_id` is the UserAccessibilityPreference.`id`; customer-visible audit projections redact raw assistive-tech shortcut payloads.

### §25.7 Internal Comments + §3.12 Presence & Unread Enum Cluster

**Authoring note (2026-04-24).** The enums below register the controlled vocabulary for the §25.7 Internal Comments feature and the §3.12 Presence & Unread Tracking surface contract. Every value is referenced by a §25.7 or §3.12 behavior and is the canonical reference for its home entity; additions require a cross-reference to the home-entity section and an entry in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md`.

#### `internal_comment_thread_visibility_scope` (§4.3.11, §25.7.3)

`buyer_workspace_members`, `buyer_team_leads`, `private_to_author_plus_mentioned`

**Notes.** Authoritative scope enum for Internal Comment Thread visibility. Mutable by thread author, Workspace Owner, or Workspace Admin. Tightening transitions (`buyer_workspace_members → buyer_team_leads → private_to_author_plus_mentioned`) cascade Unread Marker cleanup with `suppressed_reason = visibility_tightened` (§3.12.5). Loosening transitions seed markers for newly-included viewers per §25.7.3.

#### `internal_comment_thread_attached_to_type` (§4.3.11, §25.7.2)

`workspace`, `use_case`, `requirement`, `response`, `scenario`, `selection_report_draft`

**Notes.** Polymorphic anchor enum. FK resolution performed at application layer (Convex); `attached_to_id` must point to an entity in the same Workspace as the thread's `workspace_id`. Mismatch rejects with Appendix I `internal_comment_thread_anchor_mismatch` (HTTP 422). Archive of the anchor entity cascades the attached threads per Appendix L.1.

#### `internal_comment_mention_kind` (§4.3.13, §25.7.4)

`user`, `team`, `role`

**Notes.** Mention-target kind. `user` resolves directly to `mentioned_user_id`. `team` expands to each Team member at write time; `expanded_from_team_id` is populated. `role` expands to all users holding that Workspace Role at write time; `expanded_from_role` is populated. Expansion is frozen at write time per §4.3.13 author-intent-preservation rule.

#### `internal_comment_mention_skip_reason` (§25.7.4)

`no_access_to_anchor_entity`, `visibility_tightened_before_dispatch`, `user_deleted`, `user_left_workspace`

**Notes.** Populated on the `internal_comment_mention_skipped_no_access` audit event when a mention is silently dropped during expansion or in-flight notification dispatch. `no_access_to_anchor_entity` covers guests whose `assigned_use_case_ids` does not admit the thread's anchor. `visibility_tightened_before_dispatch` covers the race where the thread's `visibility_scope` is tightened between Mention-row write and notification dispatch; the Mention row's `notified_at` remains NULL and the dispatch is suppressed.

#### `webhook_event_class` (Appendix C extension — §25.7.10)

**Additions in this pass:** `internal_comment_domain`.

**Notes.** Subscribers may filter webhook streams by `event_class`. `internal_comment_domain` carries the eight events enumerated in §25.7.10 (`internal_comment_thread.created`, `.post_appended`, `.mention_sent`, `.resolved`, `.reopened`, `.archived`, `.visibility_changed`, `internal_comment_post.moderated`). Class values are additive; prior classes (billing, marketplace, growth, etc.) are preserved verbatim.

#### `unread_marker_suppressed_reason` (§4.3.15, §3.12.5)

`muted`, `left_workspace`, `archived_thread`, `visibility_tightened`, `ops_impersonation_suppressed`

**Notes.** Populated on Unread Marker rows when `unread_count` is not incrementing. `muted` corresponds to user-set `muted_until > now()`. `left_workspace` is set on membership revocation (soft-delete of the marker within 30 s; §3.12.5). `archived_thread` is set when the parent thread transitions to `archived`. `visibility_tightened` is set when a thread's `visibility_scope` tightens and the viewer is newly excluded. `ops_impersonation_suppressed` is set on impersonation-session marker writes that are silently dropped per §3.12.8 #4 — though in practice no marker is written at all during Ops impersonation, the reason value is reserved for forward-compatibility and for deployments that log suppressed-write attempts.

#### `presence_non_cursor_surface_kind` (§3.12.2)

`workspace_header_avatar_stack`, `bid_workspace_header_avatar_stack`, `thread_viewer_indicator`, `cell_row_viewer_indicator`, `typing_indicator`, `joined_thread_toast`, `off_screen_peer_indicator`, `last_here_badge`

#### Phase 12.1 — Newly Authored Enums (Body-Required, Previously Missing)

##### `content_refresh_status` (§4.4.12, §4.4.13, §4.4.14, §4.4.15, §4.4.16) — NEW

`scheduled`, `running`, `completed_no_op`, `completed_minor_auto_publish`, `completed_major_review_required`, `completed_published`, `failed_partial`, `failed_total`, `cancelled`, `superseded_by_subsequent_run`

**Scope.** Platform-scoped; applies to refresh-job rows for CategoryPage (§4.4.12 `category_faq_generation` cadence), GuidePage (§4.4.13 `guide_refresh_analysis`), ComparisonPage (§4.4.14 continuous refresh), MarketIntelligenceReport (§4.4.15 quarterly refresh), and HeatMapCell (§4.4.16 nightly aggregation). The enum governs the lifecycle of a *refresh run* — a discrete capability invocation that re-derives page content from upstream signals; it is orthogonal to `Page Publication Status` (which governs the page entity's publish state).

**Semantics.**

- `scheduled` — the next-refresh scheduler has registered the run; no work is in flight. `next_scheduled_refresh_at` on the parent page row is the canonical timestamp.
- `running` — the capability invocation is in flight; the parent page's publish state is not mutated until completion.
- `completed_no_op` — the refresh capability ran and emitted `refresh_diff_score < min_diff_threshold` (default `0.05`); no page mutation; the page's `last_refreshed_at` is bumped, `next_scheduled_refresh_at` is recomputed.
- `completed_minor_auto_publish` — the refresh emitted `refresh_diff_score ∈ [min_diff_threshold, minor_diff_ceiling]` (default `[0.05, 0.10)`) AND `editorial_review_status = not_required` on the parent; the page is auto-republished without human review per §4.4.13 minor-update bypass.
- `completed_major_review_required` — the refresh emitted `refresh_diff_score ∈ [minor_diff_ceiling, major_diff_floor)` (default `[0.10, 0.75)`) OR a discrete content class triggered editorial review (e.g., new factual claim, vendor name added/removed); the page transitions to `pending_review`.
- `completed_published` — terminal success state for either auto-publish (mirroring `completed_minor_auto_publish`) or post-review publish (mirroring `completed_major_review_required` after editorial approval); persisted to support a single canonical "completed and live" state for downstream telemetry.
- `failed_partial` — the capability invocation succeeded for some pages in a batch refresh but failed for others (relevant to ComparisonPage batch refresh and HeatMapCell nightly aggregation); requires the parent run row to enumerate the failed children. Retryable per §31 standard webhook retry curve; AI Operation reversal eligible per §4.8.5 if the failure occurred mid-billing.
- `failed_total` — the capability invocation failed unrecoverably; the parent page is unaffected (the prior published version remains live); paged to Ops if `consecutive_failed_total_count ≥ 3` per §C.100 SIM signal class.
- `cancelled` — Ops-initiated mid-run cancellation (typically driven by an emergency Vendor Opt-Out propagation that obsoletes the in-flight refresh content); the run row is preserved for audit, no page mutation.
- `superseded_by_subsequent_run` — a later refresh run completed before this one; the late-arriving completion is suppressed at the page-mutation layer to avoid stale-content overwrites. Common when manual `POST /v1/ops/marketplace/pages/{page_id}/refresh` is invoked while a scheduled run is mid-flight.

**State machine.** `scheduled → running` (worker claim); `running → {completed_no_op, completed_minor_auto_publish, completed_major_review_required, failed_partial, failed_total, cancelled, superseded_by_subsequent_run}` (terminal except `completed_minor_auto_publish` and `completed_major_review_required`, which transition to `completed_published` once the page is republished). Authored as Appendix L state-machine entry §27.6 (added in Phase 12.2 deferred work).

**Webhooks.** Each terminal transition emits `marketplace_content.refresh.{status}` per §31 catalog (registered as Phase 12.2 deferred work). Class: `marketplace_content_domain`. Retry curve: Appendix F.1 `standard`.

**Retention.** Refresh-run rows retained 365 days (operational telemetry); aggregated refresh metrics roll into the Marketplace Content Quality dashboard with §40.2 standard plan-tier retention.

**Acceptance criterion (§4.4.12 / §4.4.13 / §4.4.14 / §4.4.15 / §4.4.16 cross-cutting).** Every refresh-eligible page entity MUST emit exactly one `content_refresh_status` row per scheduled or manual refresh invocation; missing rows fail the QA test `content_refresh_status_emission_completeness` and block the build.

**Authored Extension — requires human sign-off.** Logged in RECONCILIATION.md.

##### `match_score_mode` (§27.4.6) — NEW

`qualitative_label_only`, `numeric_with_label`, `numeric_with_label_batch`, `numeric_with_label_batch_audit`, `cold_start_v1_fallback`, `hard_gated_zero`

**Scope.** Platform-scoped; the rendering-mode discriminator drawn from the §27.4.6 plan-tier rendering matrix. Carried on `MarketplaceMatchScoreSnapshot.render_mode_at_serialization` and on the `match_score.rendered` PostHog event.

**Semantics.**

- `qualitative_label_only` — Free / Starter (Buyer or Seller) tier; surfaces only the bucketed label (`strong_match` / `moderate_match` / `weak_match` / `insufficient_signal`); numeric MUST NOT serialize per §27.4.10 AC #5.
- `numeric_with_label` — Growth tier; numeric 0–100 + label + top-5 feature provenance.
- `numeric_with_label_batch` — Scale tier; adds batch API access (up to 500 pairs/call per §32.4 `batch_match_score`) and the full 18-feature provenance vector.
- `numeric_with_label_batch_audit` — Enterprise tier; adds the HMAC-SHA256 signed score receipt over `(snapshot_id, score, model_version_id, feature_vector_hash)`.
- `cold_start_v1_fallback` — emitted when no published `MarketplaceMatchScoreModelVersion` exists for the serving residency scope; the §27.4.4 Legacy Baseline v1 keyword-intersection formula is used. Provenance panel MUST explicitly label "Cold Start — Baseline v1." Renders even on Free/Starter under the qualitative-label rules.
- `hard_gated_zero` — emitted when `residency_compatible_flag=0` OR `vendor_opt_out_effective_flag=1`; the rendered numeric is fixed at 0 regardless of plan tier per §27.4.10 AC #2; the qualitative label is forced to `insufficient_signal`. Provenance panel reveals only the gate name (`residency` / `vendor_opt_out`).

**Plan-tier mapping.** Cross-referenced from §5.11 Feature Access Matrix row "Match Scoring (qualitative)" / "Match Scoring (numeric)" / "Match Scoring (audit-receipted)." A snapshot's `render_mode` is computed at serialization time from the requesting User's plan tier ∩ the snapshot's gate flags; mismatch is impossible by construction.

**Acceptance criterion.** QA test `match_score_mode_plan_tier_consistency` asserts every rendered Match Score's `render_mode` exactly matches the §27.4.6 row for the serializing User's plan tier (after gate-override application). Failure blocks the build.

**Authored Extension — requires human sign-off.** Logged in RECONCILIATION.md.

##### `match_score_model_version_state` (§27.4.8) — NEW

`candidate`, `shadow`, `published`, `deprecated`, `retired`, `rolled_back`

**Scope.** Platform-scoped; the canonical state enum for `MarketplaceMatchScoreModelVersion.state` per §27.4.8 lifecycle. Authored explicitly into Appendix J because §27.4.8 referenced the values in prose and in the §27.4.9 webhook payload tables but never registered them under a canonical enum heading.

**State machine.**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (init) | `candidate` | Training job completes | Offline-eval metrics within §27.4.5 guardrails | Not customer-facing |
| `candidate` | `shadow` | Ops promotes for shadow deploy | Dual sign-off (Applied ML + Marketing) | Shadow-served, not customer-rendered |
| `shadow` | `published` | Ops publishes | Shadow window ≥ 7 days; shadow metrics ≥ guardrails; no P1 alerts | Exactly one `published` per residency scope |
| `published` | `deprecated` | New version published OR manual deprecation | Successor version exists | Snapshots remain valid for grace window |
| `deprecated` | `retired` | Grace window expires | 30 days (Growth+) / 90 days (Enterprise audit) | Snapshots referencing retired version re-score on next render |
| `published` | `rolled_back` | P1 drift / abuse alert OR guardrail regression | Dual sign-off (Applied ML on-call + Ops leadership) | `rollback_of_version_id` populated; prior version reinstated |
| `rolled_back` | (terminal) | n/a | n/a | Retained for audit; never reinstated |
| `retired` | (terminal) | n/a | n/a | Audit-only retention per §27.4.8 |

**Webhooks.** `marketplace.match_score.model_deployed` (on `shadow → published`), `marketplace.match_score.model_deprecated`, `marketplace.match_score.model_retired`, `marketplace.match_score.model_rolled_back`. Class: `marketplace_signals_domain` (per §27.9 / §31.9 extension). Retry curve: Appendix F.1 `standard`.

**Acceptance criterion (§27.4.10 AC #3, AC #9 binding).** Every `MarketplaceMatchScoreModelVersion` insert MUST set `state ∈ {candidate}` (no skipping the candidate state); state mutations MUST follow the table above; QA test `match_score_model_version_state_machine_exhaustive` asserts no transition outside the table is permitted.

**Authored Extension — requires human sign-off.** Logged in RECONCILIATION.md.

##### `seller_signal_state` (§4.4.18, §27.9) — NEW

`aggregating`, `active`, `suppressed_below_k_floor`, `suppressed_distinctiveness_veto`, `suppressed_buyer_opt_out`, `suppressed_vendor_opt_out`, `suppressed_residency`, `partially_de_anonymized`, `expired`, `superseded_by_recompute`, `redacted_dsar`

**Scope.** Platform-scoped; the canonical state enum for the SellerSignal entity (§4.4.18). The pre-existing `seller_signal_suppressed_reason` enum (above) is retained for backward compatibility but is now a property of the suppressed-state cluster rather than the primary state axis. Phase 12.2 deferred work: migrate the §4.4.18 entity field `suppressed_reason` to a paired `state` + `state_reason` field set per the canonical pattern in §4.4.19 PromotedListing.

**Semantics.**

- `aggregating` — initial state during the windowed aggregation period; `signal_cohort_count` is incrementing; the row is never delivered while in this state.
- `active` — `k_anon_satisfied = true`, `expires_at > now()`, no opt-out or residency veto applied; row is eligible for delivery via `delivered_via` channels.
- `suppressed_below_k_floor` — `signal_cohort_count < k_anon_floor`; not delivered. Canonical replacement for `seller_signal_suppressed_reason = k_anon_floor_not_met`.
- `suppressed_distinctiveness_veto` — distinctiveness-secondary check triggered per §4.4.18 Failure Mode #4 (cohort = k but distinctness exceeds threshold). New state for an existing failure-mode behavior that previously lacked an explicit suppression value.
- `suppressed_buyer_opt_out` — at least one contributing Buyer Org revoked opt-in mid-window; recompute is in flight or complete and the row remains below k as a result.
- `suppressed_vendor_opt_out` — the Seller Org has an active `vendor_opt_out` for the rendering surface or category that scrubs this signal; the aggregate row exists but render is blocked.
- `suppressed_residency` — cross-region aggregate flagged for Ops review per §4.4.18 Failure Mode #2; not delivered until Ops approval. Distinct from `buyer_signal_region_inclusion_policy = ops_forbidden_cross_region` — that enum is the *configuration*; this state is the *runtime* outcome.
- `partially_de_anonymized` — `de_anonymized_eoi_id IS NOT NULL`; the cohort is partially de-anonymized for a single Seller Org per §4.4.18 De-Anonymization Flow. Other Sellers continue to see the anonymous aggregate; this state captures that the aggregate is no longer fully anonymous in absolute terms.
- `expired` — `expires_at ≤ now()`; the row is no longer eligible for delivery; persists until §4.4.18 Retention sweep at 180 days.
- `superseded_by_recompute` — a more recent recompute (e.g., post-DSAR) replaces this row; the old row is preserved for audit but never delivered.
- `redacted_dsar` — DSAR-driven recomputation excluded a contributor and the resulting cohort dropped below k; the row body is preserved with `signal_cohort_count` zeroed and `state_reason` populated.

**State machine.** `aggregating → {active, suppressed_below_k_floor, suppressed_distinctiveness_veto, suppressed_buyer_opt_out, suppressed_residency}` (initial classification at window-close). Active rows transition to `suppressed_*` reactively (opt-out applied, recompute drops below k, residency policy tightened). All `suppressed_*` and `active` states transition to `expired` at TTL. `active | partially_de_anonymized | suppressed_*` transition to `redacted_dsar` on DSAR-driven recomputation. `redacted_dsar | expired | superseded_by_recompute` are terminal (audit-only).

**Webhooks.** State transitions emit `marketplace.seller_signal.state_changed` per §27.9 catalog. Class: `marketplace_signals_domain`. Retry curve: Appendix F.1 `standard`.

**Acceptance criterion.** QA test `seller_signal_state_machine_exhaustive` asserts every SellerSignal mutation paths sets `state` to a registered value and that no row reaches delivery while in any `suppressed_*` or non-`active` non-`partially_de_anonymized` state.

**Authored Extension — requires human sign-off.** Logged in RECONCILIATION.md.

#### Phase 12.1 — Naming-Consistency Audit Findings

The following findings were surfaced by the Phase 12.1 audit pass. Each is logged with its disposition (Resolved / Deferred / Accepted-As-Is) and a cross-reference to the verification log.

1. **Heading-form drift between `*_enum`-suffixed and noun-phrase forms.** Approximately 60% of Phase 1.5 / §48 / §50 / §51 enum headings use the `*_enum` or `*_kind` suffix (e.g., `seller_onboarding_phase_enum`, `ops_role_kind`); approximately 40% use the bare noun-phrase form (e.g., "Pro Trial Seat Status," "Marketplace EOI Statuses"). **Disposition: Deferred to Phase 12.2** — Phase 12.1 records the inconsistency and authors aliases for the nine highest-traffic body-cited enums; full normalization is Phase 12.2 work. **Verification:** PHASE12_1_VERIFY.md → Section 3.1.

2. **Plural vs. singular heading inconsistency.** "Marketplace Listing Statuses," "Notification Frequencies," "Notification Channels," "Pricing Structures," "Plan Tiers," "Scoring Modes," "Capability Categories," "Referral Fraud Signals," "Referral Forfeit Reasons," "Referral Invite Channels," "Pro Trial Seat Outcomes," "Pro Trial Seat Converted-To Plans," "Usage Event Categories," "Usage Event Entity Ref Types," "Usage Event Outcomes," "Usage Event User Agent Classes," "Time-Saved Loaded Hourly Rate Sources," "Time-Saved Reversal Reasons," and several others use plural heading nouns (against the project convention "no plurals"). **Disposition: Accepted-As-Is for v7.0.0** — these are heading captions, not enum identifier names; the underlying value-set identifiers themselves are singular (`plan_tier_kind`, `referral_status`, `usage_event_category` etc.); rewriting the captions risks breaking link anchors and historical reference integrity. **Verification:** PHASE12_1_VERIFY.md → Section 3.2.

3. **Redundant enum coverage between body-section enums and Appendix J.** Several body sections (notably §4.3.20 `target_account_state_enum`, §4.4.18 `seller_signal_suppressed_reason`, §4.7.2 `vendor_disqualification_*` family) declare enum values inline AND in Appendix J. **Disposition: Resolved by precedence rule** — Appendix J is authoritative; body-section enum declarations are read as informational/redundant; conflicting values resolve to Appendix J per the §2 source-of-truth hierarchy. CI gate `appendix_j_body_redundancy_check` (Phase 12.2 deferred work) will assert no body-section enum declares values that diverge from Appendix J. **Verification:** PHASE12_1_VERIFY.md → Section 3.3.

4. **Mixed-case enum values flagged.** Zero mixed-case enum values found across Appendix J (all values strictly snake_case). **Disposition: Resolved (no action required).** **Verification:** PHASE12_1_VERIFY.md → Section 3.4 (full grep methodology recorded).

5. **Hyphenated enum values flagged.** Zero hyphenated enum values found. **Disposition: Resolved (no action required).** **Verification:** PHASE12_1_VERIFY.md → Section 3.5.

The plural form is documented and CI gate `enum_value_plural_audit` (Phase 12.2 deferred) will whitelist the seven approved plurals and reject any new plural without an explicit grandfather entry. **Verification:** PHASE12_1_VERIFY.md → Section 3.6.

The §25.7-canonical-form names (lines 44882 / 44894 / 44888) are canonical going forward; the original-form names are retired aliases preserved for back-compat. CI gate `appendix_j_phase_12_1_alias_coverage` is hereby extended to cover the Phase-14.x cluster — a future Phase 2V follow-on may collapse the duplicates entirely; no schema change required at v7.1.1.

**D-AJ-014 — `Unread Marker Suppressed Reasons` supersession.** The original 3-value registration at line 42791 is superseded by the §3.12 5-value cluster registration `unread_marker_suppressed_reason` at line 44912. **D-AJ-015 — `Scoring Modes` duplicate.** The bare 2-value registration at line 42589 and the descriptive 2-value registration at line 42735 are identical and refer to the same enum. Both forms are permitted; the descriptive registration (line 42735) is canonical going forward.

**D-AJ-016 — `Marketplace Abuse Report Kind` phantom-extension reference.** The line 43679 extension reference is a phantom — there is no enum literally named "Abuse Report Kind" in §4.5.7. The intended target is `Abuse Report Reason` (line 43090). The extension value `qualitative_label_dispute` is hereby registered as an extension to `Abuse Report Reason`; the phantom-name reference is corrected by this alias note.

The Phase-14.x extensions registered under §22 / §27 / §48 / §50 / §51 add namespace-qualified entity-typed audit actions (e.g., `kb_namespace_migration`, `marketplace_abuse_report_submitted`); these are NOT extensions of the bare-verb enum but are canonical entries in their own namespace. The pattern: bare-verbs apply to the 12-action audit class on §4 entities; namespace-qualified actions apply to surface / mechanic / ops events. The §13.5 / Appendix J post-Phase-1.5 canonicalization is hereby extended to assert this partition by audit class. **`dsar_cascade_remediation_action` enum (D-9.2-011 V9 remediation).** Carried in `dsar.cascade.resume.remediation_action`. Closed enum.

| Value | Sign-off requirement | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `retry_failed_rows` | Single-signoff (any `ops_dsar_admin` / `ops_dpo_admin` / `ops_dsar_escalation_admin`) | Resume the cascade; rows that previously failed are re-attempted on the standard retry curve. |
| `skip_rows_with_documented_exemption` | Dual-signoff (separation of duties; two distinct actors, second cannot be the original triage actor) | Resume the cascade with the documented-exemption row set excluded from redaction; exemption rationale stored as audit-trail artifact per §6.8.5 row 1. |
| `abort_to_extension_path` | `ops_dsar_escalation_admin` only | Cascade is paused beyond reasonable resume; subject is notified of §6.8.6 +60-day extension; cumulative-pause clock continues. |
| `escalate_to_supervisory_authority` | `ops_dsar_escalation_admin` + Privacy Officer dual-signoff | Cascade administratively closed; supervisory-authority notification path opened per §6.8.6.2. |

| :---- | :---- |

| `cross_residency_dpa_approved` | Replica target crosses residency; explicit DPA addendum + DPO approval logged via `org.residency.cross_region_replica_approved` AuditEvent. |

| `cross_residency_dpa_failover_active` | Enterprise DPA addendum permits cross-residency failover; explicit Ops + DPO sign-off logged. Reserved for sovereign-cloud / DPA-amended deployments. |

#### Phase 3V+ WorkOS April 2026 Integration Enums (2026-05-04)

**Authoring intent.** WorkOS released two RBAC-relevant capabilities in April 2026 (Groups API on 2026-04-22; FGA Custom Roles scoped to resource types on 2026-04-21) plus the new Predefined Attributes pipeline (with `raw_attributes` deprecated effective 2026-04-15). Sourcera consumes these per §5.13 + §4.2.3 V3+ + §4.2.5. Phase-3V+ enum registrations:

**`workos_predefined_attribute_kind` enum.** `display_name`, `employee_number`, `organization`, `phone_numbers`, `manager_name`, `manager_id`. The 6-value canonical set per the WorkOS April 2026 release. Consumed by §4.2.3 User entity V3+ extension and the SCIM webhook handler. Authoritative source: WorkOS predefined-attribute pipeline; Sourcera mirrors the values and SHALL NOT consume the deprecated `raw_attributes` field (CI gate `workos_raw_attributes_not_consumed`).

**`fga_custom_role_scope_type` enum.** `organization`, `workspace`, `bid_workspace`, `marketplace`, `platform`. Maps Sourcera RBAC role enum values onto WorkOS FGA Custom Role scope types per §5.13.1. Every Sourcera role enum value MUST declare exactly one `fga_custom_role_scope_type`; CI gate `fga_custom_role_scope_canonical_consumer` (§M.5 — new) asserts. Resource-type binding values:

- `organization` — Sourcera Org level (`org_owner`, `org_admin`, `member`, `billing_admin`, all `seller_*` roles except per-Bid-Workspace, `marketplace_publisher`, `marketplace_viewer`).
- `workspace` — per-Workspace Buyer Console role (`workspace_owner`, `workspace_admin`, `use_case_lead`, `reviewer`, `guest`).
- `bid_workspace` — per-Bid-Workspace Seller Console role (`seller_bid_captain`, `seller_bid_contributor`, `seller_kb_viewer` per Bid Workspace, `seller_guest`).
- `marketplace` — reserved for future marketplace-domain-scoped roles per Phase 3V+ extension; currently no consumers.
- `platform` — Sourcera Ops Console roles (`ops_*` per Phase 3V `ops_console_role` enum); not visible to customer Orgs.

**`workos_group_membership_role_assignment_priority` enum.** `directory_group_takes_precedence`, `sso_group_fallback`. Per the WorkOS April 2026 contract, directory-group role assignments take precedence over SSO group role assignments. Sourcera's §5.13.2 SCIM precedence rule consumes this enum at role-resolution time. CI gate `workos_directory_group_role_assignment_precedence` asserts.

**`auto_derivation_source` enum (Executive Sponsor V3+ extension).** `explicit`, `manager_chain`, `most_senior_org_owner`, `most_senior_org_admin_fallback`. Captured on every Pulse event row per §5.9 V3+ designation flow for forensic clarity. The auto-derivation precedence is enumerated in §5.9 V3+ remediation block.

**`workos_group_audit_event_action_type` extensions (Phase 3V+ Audit-System sub-section additions to Appendix J `audit_event_action_type` registry).** New action-type values registered to support the §4.2.5 Group entity lifecycle and §6.9.3 deprovisioning Groups cascade:

`org.group_created`, `org.group_updated`, `org.group_deleted`, `org.group_member_added`, `org.group_member_removed`, `org.group_assigned_role_slug_changed`, `org.role_revoked_via_group_deletion`, `org.scim_group_role_assigned`, `org.scim_group_role_revoked`, `org.executive_sponsor_org_owner_absent`, `org.workos_groups_api_outage`. Each binds to `entity_type ∈ {group, organization_membership}`. `org.scim_billing_admin_mapping_enabled` / `org.scim_billing_admin_mapping_disabled` retained for historical projections per §6.8.5 audit-integrity exemption (pre-V3+ events).

**Phase 3V+ Disambiguation Note — `User.organization_attribute` vs `OrgMembership.org_id`.** The new `User.organization_attribute` predefined attribute is the customer-Org-internal department / organizational-unit field supplied by the Directory provider (e.g., "Engineering", "Procurement", "Legal"). It is distinct from Sourcera's `OrgMembership.org_id` foreign key, which references the Sourcera Organization entity. The two are NOT synonyms; CI gate `user_organization_attribute_disambiguation` (§M.5 — new) asserts no spec-side prose conflates the two.
