### v7.2.0-REM Phase 5.5 Seller Q&A Projection Enum Registrations (2026-06-21) {#appendix-j-v72rem-phase-5-5-seller-qa-projection-enums}

**Authoring intent.** Lands the controlled vocabularies consumed by §4.4.2.1 and §24.1.1 while closing the D-5.5-001 / D-5.5-002 / D-5.5-003 seller Q&A visibility cluster. These registrations are straight canonicalization of body-side Q&A projection values; they do not introduce a new customer-facing surface beyond the Seller Q&A row already registered in Appendix M.

#### `qa_thread_question_audience` (§4.4.2.1, §24.1.1)

`specific_vendor`, `all_invited_vendors`

**Notes.** Distinguishes a thread addressed to one seller from a broadcast thread intended for every active invited seller in the buyer Workspace. This enum drives the cross-vendor visibility predicate in §24.1.1 and the seller projection uniqueness rules in §4.4.2.1.

#### `qa_thread_visibility` (§18.3.2, §4.4.2.1, §24.1.1)

`PUBLIC`, `PRIVATE`

**Notes.** Canonicalizes the existing §18.3.2 value set. `PUBLIC` means all NDA-cleared invited sellers may read; `PRIVATE` means only the addressed seller may read. Public-to-private transitions remain forbidden per §18.3.2.

#### `qa_thread_status` (§18.3.1, Appendix L.13)

`open`, `closed`, `archived`, `orphaned`

**Notes.** `open` accepts new posts in Phase 6-7 when visibility and NDA gates pass. `closed` is read-only, including Phase 8 auto-close. `archived` is the soft-delete / retention state. `orphaned` is set when the addressed seller is disqualified or otherwise loses compose authority while the buyer-side audit trail remains visible to authorized buyer users.

#### `qa_thread_mention_kind` (§18.3.1, §18.5.3)

`user`, `team`, `role`

**Notes.** Mentions expand at Q&A Post write time into one Q&A Mention row per target user. Team and role expansion is frozen at write time and does not retroactively notify later team members or role holders.

#### `qa_additional_slots_request_status` (§18.7.2, §18.9)

`requested`, `approved`, `denied`, `expired`, `canceled`

**Notes.** Tracks the Workspace Owner approval queue for vendor requests to exceed the base Q&A question limit. Denied and expired requests do not increase the vendor's slot cap; approved requests carry the granted slot count and approver AuditEvent.

#### `qa_thread_nda_visibility_state` (§4.4.2.1, §24.1.1)

`not_required`, `nda_pending`, `nda_executed`, `nda_expired`, `nda_superseded`, `exception_granted`

**Notes.** Computed from NDA Record (§4.5.3), Bid Workspace (§4.4.1), and any buyer-approved exception. The value is used only for read/write authorization and surface rendering; it does not replace the NDA Record lifecycle. Canonical mapping: §4.5.3 `nda_status ∈ {draft, pending_buyer, pending_seller}` -> `nda_pending`; `executed` -> `nda_executed`; `expired` -> `nda_expired`; superseded-version blockers -> `nda_superseded`; buyer-approved exception -> `exception_granted`; no NDA required -> `not_required`.

#### `qa_thread_compose_state` (§25.3.3, §4.4.2.1)

`compose_enabled`, `compose_disabled_orphaned`

**Notes.** Canonicalizes the §25.3.3 Q&A disqualification state machine. Phase read-only behavior and NDA blockers are computed guards layered before write authorization, not persisted compose states.

#### `seller_inbox_item_kind` (§4.4.33, §24.3)

`new_requirement_assigned`, `amendment_reverification_required`, `qa_response_received`, `kb_review_due`, `document_expiring_soon`, `nda_signature_requested`, `phase_transition`

**Notes.** Canonical item-family enum for SellerInboxItem. These seven values correspond exactly to the seven §24.3 surface bullets. Additions require a §24.3 surface update, a §4.4.33 field-table review, and notification/catalog review under D-24-008.

#### `seller_inbox_priority` (§4.4.33, §4.4.34, §24.3)

`action_required`, `update`, `info`

**Notes.** Sort band for SellerInboxItem and SellerInboxItemGroup. `action_required` rows require seller action before a deadline or phase gate; `update` rows are material changes that do not require immediate action; `info` rows are FYI only. This enum intentionally uses semantic labels instead of buyer-side numeric priority labels.

#### `seller_inbox_item_state` (§4.4.33)

`pending`, `read`, `dismissed`, `expired`

**Notes.** Lifecycle enum for SellerInboxItem. Terminal retention behavior is governed by §4.4.33 and the grouped-inbox retention pattern in §4.3.22 / §40.2.

#### `seller_inbox_anchor_entity_type` (§4.4.34)

`bid_workspace`, `requirement`, `response`, `qa_thread`, `nda_record`, `kb_entry`, `document`, `console_bridge_event`, `phase_transition`, `seller_org`

**Notes.** Polymorphic grouping anchor for SellerInboxItemGroup. FK resolution is application-layer because the anchor can point to seller-console rows, cross-console bridge events, or seller-visible notification concepts. Cross-console reads still apply the §4.4.33 / §4.4.34 seller Org and Bid Workspace authorization predicates before any anchor is resolved.

#### `seller_pulse_snapshot_kind` (§4.4.37)

`tick`, `daily_summary`, `final_lock`

**Notes.** Records the compute cadence for SellerBidWorkspacePulseHealth. `tick` rows update after seller-side input changes, `daily_summary` rows support the trend chart, and `final_lock` freezes post-bid evidence.

#### `seller_pulse_weight_set` (§4.4.37, §24.4.2)

`pre_bidding`, `active_response`, `post_submission`, `final_lock`

**Notes.** Records the phase-derived Seller Pulse weight set selected by §24.4.2. Values are derived from the bound buyer Workspace phase projection and Bid Workspace terminal state; they are not user-editable.

#### `seller_pulse_lock_reason` (§4.4.37)

`bid_won`, `bid_lost`, `submitted_and_not_awarded`, `withdrawn`, `disqualified`, `workspace_closed`

**Notes.** Explains why SellerBidWorkspacePulseHealth entered `snapshot_kind=final_lock`. The lock reason is audit metadata and MUST NOT expose buyer-internal selection rationale.

#### `seller_pulse_metric_id` (§24.4)

`response_completion`, `on_time_submission`, `amendment_reverification_turnaround`, `kb_utilization`, `deadline_readiness`

**Notes.** Canonical metric ids for the Seller Pulse component breakdown. These ids map to the persisted SellerBidWorkspacePulseHealth term fields in §4.4.37 and the formula terms in §24.4.2.

#### `saved_search_console` (§4.4.35, §4.4.36)

`buyer`, `seller`

**Notes.** Console scope for SavedSearch and SearchAlert. The enum intentionally mirrors the two customer consoles and excludes `ops`; Ops-curated collections are represented through `surface_kind`, not by giving Ops user-owned saved-search rows.

#### `saved_search_visibility` (§4.4.35)

`private`, `team`

**Notes.** Sharing scope for SavedSearch. `team` remains Org-local and console-local; cross-Org saved-search sharing is forbidden.

#### `saved_search_surface_kind` (§4.4.35)

`marketplace_discovery`, `buyer_workspace_vendor_search`, `seller_signal_market_scan`

**Notes.** Surface family that owns the query grammar. `marketplace_discovery` covers public Marketplace / Vendor Discovery searches; `buyer_workspace_vendor_search` covers Buyer Workspace-local vendor search; `seller_signal_market_scan` covers seller-side signal and category monitoring.

#### `search_alert_state` (§4.4.36)

`active`, `paused`, `delivery_suppressed`, `errored`, `deleted`

**Notes.** Lifecycle state for SearchAlert. `deleted` is terminal and always paired with `deleted_at`.

#### `search_alert_frequency` (§4.4.36)

`instant`, `daily`, `weekly`

**Notes.** Evaluation cadence. Destination-plan throttling may lower effective frequency but MUST NOT delete the SearchAlert row.

#### `search_alert_channel` (§4.4.36)

`in_app`, `email`, `weekly_digest`

**Notes.** Delivery channel preference for SearchAlert. Channel availability still respects notification preferences and §29 frequency rules.

**Audit Event Action Types — Seller Q&A / Seller Inbox extension.** The Appendix J `audit_event_action_type` controlled vocabulary is extended with:

`qa_thread.access_revoked`, `qa_thread.mention_suppressed`, `qa_thread.visibility_changed`, `qa_thread.archived`, `nda_expired_qa_revoked`, `seller_inbox_item_created`, `seller_inbox_item_read`, `seller_inbox_item_dismissed`, `seller_inbox_item_expired`, `saved_search.created`, `saved_search.updated`, `saved_search.deleted`, `search_alert.created`, `search_alert.updated`, `search_alert.paused`, `search_alert.resumed`, `search_alert.deleted`

**Notes.** `qa_thread.access_revoked` is emitted when a seller loses Q&A visibility after an NDA expiry, superseded NDA version, disqualification, or revocation-equivalent permission change. `qa_thread.mention_suppressed` records mention delivery drops caused by visibility, NDA, residency, deprovisioning, or digest-suppression rules; it is audit-only and does not notify the suppressed recipient. `qa_thread.visibility_changed` and `qa_thread.archived` mirror §18 / Appendix L.13 mutations. `nda_expired_qa_revoked` is the reason/action discriminator required by §24.1.1 when §4.5.3 `nda_status=expired` removes access. The seller-inbox actions are emitted by §4.4.33 state transitions and carry `entity_type ∈ {seller_inbox_item, seller_inbox_item_group}`. SavedSearch and SearchAlert actions are emitted by §4.4.35 / §4.4.36 create, update, pause/resume, and delete transitions.

**Audit Event Entity Type — Seller Inbox / Seller Pulse / Saved Search extension.** Appendix J `audit_event_entity_type` is extended with:

`seller_inbox_item`, `seller_inbox_item_group`, `seller_bid_workspace_pulse_health`, `saved_search`, `search_alert`

**Notes.** These values are used by §4.6.1 AuditEvent rows emitted from §4.4.33 / §4.4.34 lifecycle changes, §4.4.37 final-lock / retention / support-review events, and §4.4.35 / §4.4.36 saved-search lifecycle changes.

## Appendix K: Glossary {#appendix-k-glossary}

**Authoring note (Phase 12.3 — 2026-04-26).** The Sourcera project-level authoring conventions previously referenced "Appendix-B Glossary." This drift was resolved during Phase 12.3 of the v7.0.0 integration: Appendix B is the Keyboard Shortcut Reference (authored under Phase 12.3 as the canonical resolution of v6.0.0's TOC-only entry); Appendix K is — and remains — the canonical Glossary. The project-level CLAUDE.md and SWE_Project_Instructions.md were updated in lockstep to cite "Appendix-K Glossary" instead of "Appendix-B Glossary." Every Glossary entry MUST be added under this Appendix K. CI gate `appendix_k_glossary_canonicality` asserts that no spec-body authoring instruction directs glossary entries elsewhere. Resolved entry in `_integration/RECONCILIATION.md → Phase 12.3 — Cross-Reference Integrity → Appendix-Letter Drift Resolution`.

### Canonical Role Glossary Entries (Phase 3.1 P1 Remediation)

**Workspace Owner** (`workspace_owner`). Workspace-scoped Buyer Console role that owns workspace settings, team membership, phase advancement, final selection authority, disqualification reversal, Defense View regeneration, and workspace-scoped audit-log access. See §5.3, §5.3.1, §5.11, §13, §25.3, §32, and Appendix J `workspace_role_kind`.

**Workspace Admin** (`workspace_admin`). Workspace-scoped Buyer Console role that coordinates evaluation execution and can operate most workspace content and phase workflows, excluding owner-only actions such as workspace deletion, team management, score-lock overrides, Defense View regeneration, and audit-log viewing. Pre-V3 "Evaluation Lead" is retired in favor of this canonical enum. See §5.3, §5.3.1, §5.11, §13.10, §17.8, §20.7, and Appendix J `workspace_role_kind`.

**Use Case Lead** (`use_case_lead`). Workspace-scoped Buyer Console role authorized to author requirements, score, comment, and view responses within assigned Use Cases. Pre-V3 "Evaluator" is retired in favor of this canonical enum. See §5.3, §5.3.1, §5.11, §12, §17, §18, §20, §32, and Appendix J `workspace_role_kind`.

**Reviewer** (`reviewer`). Workspace-scoped Buyer Console role authorized to score vendor responses and provide rationale during the scoring phases, without requirement-edit authority. Pre-V3 "Scorer" is retired in favor of this canonical enum. See §5.3, §5.3.1, §5.7, §5.11, §17, §20, §32, and Appendix J `workspace_role_kind`.

**Workspace Guest** (`guest`). Workspace-specific Buyer Console role whose permissions are controlled by the Guest Permission Profile (`read_only`, `contributor`, `scorer`, or `full_participant`) selected at invitation time. Guest scope is bounded to the invited Workspace and, when assigned, specific Use Cases. See §5.3, §5.4, §5.11, §29, §32, and Appendix J `workspace_role_kind`.

**Evaluation Lead (retired alias).** Retired pre-V3 name for `workspace_admin`; new authoring MUST use `workspace_admin` / Workspace Admin. Historical references resolve through §5.3 Role canonicality and Appendix J `workspace_role_kind`.

**Evaluator (retired alias).** Retired pre-V3 name for `use_case_lead`; new authoring MUST use `use_case_lead` / Use Case Lead. Historical references resolve through §5.3 Role canonicality and Appendix J `workspace_role_kind`.

**Scorer (retired alias).** Retired pre-V3 name for `reviewer`; new authoring MUST use `reviewer` / Reviewer. Historical references resolve through §5.3 Role canonicality and Appendix J `workspace_role_kind`.

**Seller Org Owner** (`seller_org_owner`). Org-scoped Seller Console role with top-of-tree Seller Org authority across seller product operations, including Seller Org / Software page management, KB authority, verification requests, CRM Sync oversight, and seller billing fallback where §5.2.1 permits owner authority. See §5.5, §5.5.1, §5.11 Seller Console Role Overlay, §22, §27, §31.9, §34.12.6, and Appendix J `seller_workspace_role`.

**Seller Org Admin** (`seller_org_admin`). Org-scoped Seller Console role with broad seller product-operation authority, excluding seller billing mutation authority unless separately granted `seller_billing_admin`. See §5.5, §5.5.1, §5.11, §22, §27, §31.9, and Appendix J `seller_workspace_role`.

**Seller Billing Admin** (`seller_billing_admin`). Org-scoped Seller Console billing role that mirrors §5.2.1 Billing Admin authority in Seller Org context for seller-side billing surfaces, contests, wallet configuration, plan changes, and billing webhooks. See §5.2.1, §5.5, §5.5.1, §34.12.6, §31, and Appendix J `seller_workspace_role`.

**Seller Marketing Editor** (`seller_marketing_editor`). Org-scoped Seller Console role for Marketplace-facing profile and capability content, including SellerOrgPage / SoftwarePage edits, Seller Maya polish surfaces, Capability Declarations, and read-oriented Seller Signal usage where allowed. See §5.5, §5.5.1, §22.20, §27, §44.6, and Appendix J `seller_workspace_role`.

**Seller KB Admin** (`seller_kb_admin`). Org-scoped Seller Console role that administers KB namespaces, document library upload, KB Bootstrap, namespace migration, entry approval, and KB export authority. See §5.5, §5.5.1, §22, §32.9, and Appendix J `seller_workspace_role`.

**Seller KB Editor** (`seller_kb_editor`). Org-scoped Seller Console role that can create and edit KB entries within assigned namespaces but cannot approve own high-risk rows, trigger KB Bootstrap, or export the KB unless another role grants that authority. See §5.5, §5.5.1, §22, and Appendix J `seller_workspace_role`.

**Seller KB Viewer** (`seller_kb_viewer`). Org-scoped Seller Console read-only role for KB entries and Bid Response surfaces, subsuming the retired pre-V3 "Bid Viewer" surface plus KB-read-only access. See §5.5, §5.5.1, §22, §24, and Appendix J `seller_workspace_role`.

**Seller Bid Captain** (`seller_bid_captain`). Bid-Workspace-scoped Seller Console role that owns a seller Bid Workspace, manages assigned team members, tracks responses, transitions bid workflow state, and interfaces with the buyer through seller-safe projections. Pre-V3 "Bid Owner" is retired in favor of this canonical enum. See §5.5, §5.5.1, §24, §31, and Appendix J `seller_workspace_role`.

**Seller Bid Contributor** (`seller_bid_contributor`). Bid-Workspace-scoped Seller Console role that completes assigned bid-response sections and collaborates inside the seller Bid Workspace without owner-level team or lifecycle authority. See §5.5, §5.5.1, §24, §32, and Appendix J `seller_workspace_role`.

**Seller Compliance Officer** (`seller_compliance_officer`). Org-scoped Seller Console role responsible for verification-tier prerequisites, takedown responses, DPA/compliance tasks, and seller-side compliance evidence workflows. See §5.5, §5.5.1, §27.9.6, §27.10.4, §50 handoff surfaces, and Appendix J `seller_workspace_role`.

**Seller Integrations Admin** (`seller_integrations_admin`). Org-scoped Seller Console role for CRM Sync configuration, webhook endpoint CRUD, API-token issuance, and integration activity-queue operations, subject to dual-signoff where destructive OAuth revoke or custom routing requires owner/admin co-signature. See §5.5, §5.5.1, §31.5, §31.9, §31.10, and Appendix J `seller_workspace_role`.

**Seller Guest** (`seller_guest`). Bid-Workspace-scoped Seller Console role that receives a limited seller-safe projection for an explicitly invited Bid Workspace and no KB, CRM, Seller Signal, billing, Marketplace publishing, or Org settings authority. See §5.5, §5.5.1, §24, and Appendix J `seller_workspace_role`.

**Bid Owner (retired alias).** Retired pre-V3 name for `seller_bid_captain`; new authoring MUST use `seller_bid_captain` / Seller Bid Captain. Historical references resolve through §5.5 Role canonicality and Appendix J `seller_workspace_role`.

**Bid Contributor (retired alias).** Retired pre-V3 name for `seller_bid_contributor`; new authoring MUST use `seller_bid_contributor` / Seller Bid Contributor. Historical references resolve through §5.5 Role canonicality and Appendix J `seller_workspace_role`.

**Bid Viewer (retired alias).** Retired pre-V3 name for the read-only seller Bid surface now covered by `seller_kb_viewer`; new authoring MUST use `seller_kb_viewer` / Seller KB Viewer. Historical references resolve through §5.5 Role canonicality and Appendix J `seller_workspace_role`.

**Marketplace Publisher** (`marketplace_publisher`). Seller-Org-scoped Marketplace role that can create and edit Marketplace Listings, manage seller profile publication surfaces, publish Capability Declarations, and request verification workflows when the owning Seller Org and plan gates allow. Buyer Org grants are invalid. See §5.6, §5.11 Marketplace Role Overlay, §22, §27, §4.4.10, §4.4.11, §4.5.1, and Appendix J `marketplace_role`.

**Marketplace Viewer** (`marketplace_viewer`). Authenticated buyer-Org Marketplace role that can browse Marketplace listings and submit EOIs within plan-tier entitlement, subject to buyer Org context and §34.1.1 Marketplace Buyer Access gates. See §5.6, §5.11, §27.2, §27.5, §4.5.2, §34.1.1, and Appendix J `marketplace_role`.

**Marketplace Public Reader** (`marketplace_public_reader`). Synthetic unauthenticated Marketplace read role used for public browse surfaces. It can read public Marketplace pages under anonymous rate limits but cannot submit EOIs, read private Match Score details, or mutate any marketplace entity. See §5.6, §27.2, §32.4, and Appendix J `marketplace_role`.

### Terms Introduced in §4.3 (v7.0.0 Integration)

**Internal Comment.** A private buyer-side comment surface attached to a Workspace, Use Case, Requirement, Response, Scenario, or Selection Report draft. Never visible to vendors or seller-console users. Materialized as three entities: Internal Comment Thread (container), Internal Comment Post (content), and Internal Comment Mention (normalized @-mention record). See §4.3.11, §4.3.12, §4.3.13.

**Internal Comment Thread.** Container entity for Internal Comment Posts. Polymorphically anchored to a workspace-scoped entity via `attached_to_type` and `attached_to_id`. See §4.3.11.

**Internal Comment Post.** An individual post within an Internal Comment Thread. Editable by the author for 15 minutes after creation; overridable by Workspace Owner with audit. See §4.3.12.

**Internal Comment Mention.** A normalized @-mention record linking an Internal Comment Post to a targeted User. Drives notification fan-out and the `has_unread_mention` flag on Unread Markers. `mention_kind` supports `user`, `team`, and `role` targets, with team/role expansions frozen at mention time. See §4.3.13.

**Presence Record.** A Convex Presence-backed, session-scoped, ephemeral entity that tracks live-cursor and collaboration state for an active user session. Not persisted to cold storage; never subject to DSAR export; excluded from round-trip import/export fidelity. See §4.3.14 and §40.4.

**Unread Marker.** A per-user-per-thread unread-count tracker shared across Internal Comment Threads, Q&A Threads, and Inbox Item Groups. One row per (user, thread_type, thread_id) tuple; `thread_type` resolves polymorphically. Drives in-app badge counts and the Inbox unread experience. See §4.3.15.

**InboxItem.** Buyer-console action/update row backing the §20.2 unified Inbox feed. Each row belongs to a Buyer Org, may target a Workspace and recipient user, carries canonical notification type / priority / delivery-state enums, and groups under Inbox Item Group for feed compaction. Seller-console reads return HTTP 404. See §4.3.22.1 and §20.2.

**WorkspacePulseHealth.** Workspace-scoped daily persistence row for the §20.3 Pulse Health Score. It stores the bounded composite score, component percentages, selected weight set, raw input counts, color band, and threshold-transition event binding used by Pulse UI, digest email, webhooks, and Solo-mode engine-on / surface-off behavior. See §4.3.22.2 and §20.3.

**SellerBidWorkspacePulseHealth.** Seller-console Bid-Workspace-scoped Pulse snapshot row for §24.4. It stores the bounded seller-side health score, component percentages, selected seller weight set, tick / daily / final-lock cadence, raw aggregate inputs, color band, and final-lock metadata without exposing raw buyer Workspace identifiers or buyer-internal content. See §4.4.37 and §24.4.

**Selection Report.** The immutable, finalized Phase 12 recommendation artifact created from a Selection Report Draft. Carries vendor selection statuses, signed report content, approval linkage, evidence references, and the `selection_record_sha256` binding copied from the Selection Record. See §4.3.23 and §10.12.

**Selection Record.** The immutable Phase 13 closure bundle containing the finalized Selection Report plus snapshots of Requirements, Responses, Scores, comments/discussion manifests, and contract document references. It is the source bundle for Defense View and audit receipts. See §4.3.24 and §10.13.5.

**Approval Workflow.** The Phase 12 sub-state used when Org policy requires CFO / Legal / CRO / Procurement approval of a Selection Report. Request-changes and rejection states do not move the Workspace backward and do not unlock scores. See §4.3.25 and Appendix L.12.

**Cancellation Request.** The first-class buyer-side record for a Workspace cancellation lifecycle, carrying cancellation reason, grace-window deadlines, recovery state, and audit-event links. See §4.3.26 and §10.14.

**Post-Evaluation Feedback.** Optional buyer-side stakeholder feedback captured after Phase 13 closure. It supports future process improvement and never mutates the Selection Report, Selection Record, scores, rankings, or vendor notifications. See §4.3.27 and §10.13.3.

**TCO Model.** Workspace-scoped buyer entity that stores §15 pricing-only requirements, projection configuration, vendor pricing response snapshots, and computed TCO results without converting pricing rows into scorable Requirements. See §4.3.28 and §15.

**PricingRequirement (TCO).** The pricing-only JSON element inside `TCOModel.pricing_requirements_json`. It is not a standalone Requirement row and always carries `weight=0`, `type=pricing`, and a Pricing Structures enum value. See §4.3.28.1 and §15.2.2.

**TCOConfiguration.** The canonical JSON schema inside `TCOModel.projection_parameters_json` for projection years, initial seat count, seat-growth rate, currency, and assumption notes. Exactly one active configuration exists per live TCO Model. See §4.3.28.2 and §15.5.1.

**Vendor Pricing Response FX Snapshot.** The locked-currency and locked-FX representation of a vendor or buyer-estimator monetary response to a TCO pricing requirement. TCO aggregation uses the converted USD integer-cent fields from the snapshot, while rendering uses the locked FX rate rather than live rates. See §4.3.28.3 and §15.2.4.

**Buyer Referral.** M16 growth-mechanic entity tracking a structured referrer → referee relationship with credit issuance, fraud signals, activity gating, and Stripe Credit Note reconciliation. Cross-referenced by Summary C.74. See §4.3.16.

**Referral Code.** 10-character URL-safe Base32 string, unique per Buyer Referral, used in magic-link redemption.

**Minimum Activity Threshold.** Referee-side activity bar that must be reached before a Buyer Referral transitions to `activated` status and becomes credit-eligible. Default: referee Org has completed ≥1 workspace through Phase 9 with ≥3 paid users. Configurable by Ops via C.97; version-stamped on each Buyer Referral for retroactive-change safety.

**Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat Grant.** M17 entity that records the lifecycle of a single 30-day Seller Starter trial gifted from a buyer (Scale or Enterprise) to an invited vendor. Pool-accounted against the buyer's billing month. Complements §34.13 procedure with the persistent record. See §4.3.17.

**Grant Code.** 16-character URL-safe Base32 string, unique per Pro Trial Seat Grant, used in vendor signup URL.

**Dual-Projection Read.** API pattern applied to Pro Trial Seat Grants: a single endpoint returns different field projections depending on whether the requesting Org is the buyer (issuer) or the vendor (redeemer). Third-party Orgs receive HTTP 404. Authored in §4.3.17.

**Webhook Subscription.** Org-scoped integration configuration that binds a customer-owned HTTPS endpoint to one or more webhook event types or event classes. The canonical entity, API contract, console-scoped registration guard, retention rule, and secret-rotation binding are authored in §31.11. Subscription registration is fail-closed: forbidden cross-console event kinds return HTTP 404 so the event kind's existence is not leaked.

**Usage Event.** Canonical product-analytics ledger entity mirroring every buyer- and seller-side action. Dual-written to Convex (system of record for billing and DSAR) and PostHog (dashboards and long-tail analytics) via an outbox pattern. Standardized property schema per C.89. See §4.3.18.

**Outbox Pattern (PostHog).** Pattern for dual-writing Usage Events: Convex is the source of truth; PostHog delivery is tracked via `posthog_delivery_status` with idempotent retry keyed on `id`. Skipped when DSAR redaction is mid-process.

**Time-Saved Credit.** C.91 Time-Saved Baseline Model output. One credit per qualifying Usage Event. Version-stamped against the conversion-factor policy at credit time so Ops edits do not retroactively change dashboard totals. Supports reversal entities for retroactive AI-outcome undoes. See §4.3.19.

**Conversion Factor.** Capability-specific minutes-saved-per-event value used by the Time-Saved Baseline Model to convert Usage Events into labor-hours-saved estimates. Managed via C.97 Baseline Assumption Manager; version-stamped.

**Loaded Hourly Rate.** Labor rate used to monetize Time-Saved minutes into USD. Org-default with optional per-user override (Enterprise only) and Ops calibration override. Stored on each Time-Saved Credit row to preserve audit integrity across rate changes.

**Signal Integrity Monitor (SIM).** C.100 Ops surface that detects anomalous referral velocity, same-domain patterns, payment-method overlap, and suspicious grant issuance. Emits flags onto Buyer Referral `fraud_signal_flags` and Pro Trial Seat Grant `anti_spam_hold_reason`. Can trigger kill-switches on M16 and M17 mechanics.

**Pro Trial Seat Pool.** Buyer's monthly allocation of 5 (Scale) or 15 (Enterprise) Pro Trial Seats per §34.13.2. Replenishes on the buyer's billing anniversary. Unused seats do not carry over. Pool snapshots frozen on each grant via `buyer_pool_seats_remaining_at_grant`.

**Author Role Snapshot.** Enum field on Internal Comment Post that freezes the author's workspace role at post time, preserving context across later role changes.

**Edit Lock Window.** 15-minute window from Post creation during which the author may edit or soft-delete (placeholder) their own post without admin involvement. Enforced server-side via `edit_locked_at`.

### Terms Introduced in §4.4 (v7.0.0 Integration, Phase 2)

**Marketplace Category.** The Ops-maintained, single-global taxonomy node used as the canonical FK target for SellerSoftware, SoftwarePage, CategoryPage, GuidePage, ComparisonPage, MarketIntelligenceReport, HeatMapCell, and SellerSignal. Supports two-level hierarchy (parent + child) and deprecation-with-successor migrations. See §4.4.7. Maintained per Summary C.60.

**Vendor Opt-Out Record.** The append-only Opt-Out Registry entity per Summary C.123. A seller-authored suppression record that retroactively redacts the seller's name, pages, or product references from all public Sourcera-owned Marketplace content. Supports global, category-, software-, page-type-, and page-level scopes. Auto-honored on write; Ops post-hoc review governs approved/rejected/revoked state. See §4.4.8.

**SellerSoftware.** A distinct software product owned by a Seller Org (one-to-many). Carries its own slug, category, capability declaration refs, KB namespace, claim status, page status, and SEO status. See §4.4.9. Introduced per Summary §6.15.5.

**Claim Status (SellerSoftware).** The lifecycle state tracking whether a Seller Org has verified ownership of a SellerSoftware row. States: `unclaimed`, `claim_pending`, `claim_verified`, `claim_disputed`, `claim_revoked`. Verification methods include DNS TXT, verified email, Ops manual, and SSO domain match. See §4.4.9.

**KB Namespace (Software-Level).** A per-SellerSoftware KB namespace that isolates retrieval by product. Defined in KB_Engineering_Spec §5.4; referenced by SellerSoftware as `kb_namespace_id`. Migrated to the Org namespace on SellerSoftware soft-delete.

**SellerOrgPage.** The public, SEO-indexed page backing `/sellers/:slug` per Summary §6.15.4. Auto-enriched via the Opus-tier `page_enrichment` capability; seller-reviewed before publication. Enrichment billed to Platform Marketing. See §4.4.10.

**SoftwarePage.** The product-level equivalent of SellerOrgPage, backing `/software/:slug`. One-to-one with SellerSoftware. Publication requires `claim_status=claim_verified` on the parent. See §4.4.11.

**CategoryPage (M9).** AI-generated, editorially-reviewed per-category Marketplace landing page, powered by `category_faq_generation`. Sourcera-owned; Platform Marketing cost center; k-anonymity floor k=5. Summary C.67. See §4.4.12.

**GuidePage (M10).** Long-form "How to Evaluate [X]" SEO guide generated by `guide_draft_generation` and refreshed by `guide_refresh_analysis`. Sourcera-owned; Platform Marketing cost center; k-anonymity floor k=5. Summary C.68. See §4.4.13.

**ComparisonPage (M11).** AI-generated, continuously refreshed side-by-side software comparison page. Vendor opt-out honored globally via column suppression. Auto-archives when non-suppressed comparison count drops below 2. Summary C.69. See §4.4.14.

**MarketIntelligenceReport (M12).** Quarterly, k-anonymized (k=20) aggregate market intelligence publication produced by `market_intelligence_report`. Dual-sign-off (Marketing + Finance) required before publication. Summary C.70. See §4.4.15.

**HeatMapCell (M13).** Aggregated demand cell for the Public Marketplace Heat Map: one cell = one (category, region, industry, company_size_band, period). k-anonymity floor k=10. Summary C.71. See §4.4.16.

**GhostBidImport (M15).** A historical RFP ingestion record. Sellers paste or upload historical RFPs to seed their Software- or Org-level KB via `ghost_rfp_ingestion`. First import per Seller Org is free; subsequent imports bill as AI Operations. Summary C.73. See §4.4.17.

**SellerSignal.** Anonymized, aggregated buyer-intent record per Summary §6.17. Buyer opt-in; k-anonymity floor k=5. Delivered via in-app Dashboard, weekly digest, and CRM Sync. De-anonymization only on explicit buyer EOI or direct invite. See §4.4.18.

**SellerInboxItem.** Seller-console action/update row backing §24.3 Seller Inbox. Each item belongs to a Seller Org, may target a seller user or team, and carries a canonical `seller_inbox_item_kind`, priority, lifecycle state, source-event pointer, and seller-safe action URL. See §4.4.33 and §24.3.

**SellerInboxItemGroup.** Seller-console grouped feed row that compacts related SellerInboxItem rows by anchor entity and group type. It mirrors the buyer-side Inbox Item Group pattern while preserving seller Org, Bid Workspace, and residency scope. See §4.4.34.

**SavedSearch.** Org-scoped saved query definition for Marketplace Discovery, Buyer Workspace vendor search, or Seller Signal market-scan surfaces. Seller-console rows are Class 7 protected assets under §34.19.1 / §34.19.1.A and preserve across plan transitions. See §4.4.35.

**SearchAlert.** Scheduled notification contract attached to a SavedSearch. It stores cadence, channel, delivery state, dedupe fingerprint, and scheduler cursor separately from the saved query definition. Seller-console rows are Class 7 protected assets under §34.19.1 / §34.19.1.A. See §4.4.36.

**Opt-Out Registry Source-of-Truth Rule.** For every public-facing content entity that references a seller or product, the denormalized `vendor_opt_out_ref_id` field points at the active Vendor Opt-Out Record; `vendor_opt_out_honored_at` stamps the last registry evaluation. Nightly reconciliation enforces drift <1% between the denormalized pointer and the authoritative Registry. Introduced in §4.4.

**Sourcera-Owned Cost Center.** AI Operations performed by `category_faq_generation`, `guide_draft_generation`, `guide_refresh_analysis`, `comparison_page_generation`, `market_intelligence_report`, `page_enrichment`, and `seller_signal_aggregation` are billed to the internal Platform Marketing cost center, not to any customer Org. Summary §6.16.5.

**k-Anonymity Floor.** Minimum cohort size before any aggregate-derived fact is surfaced publicly. Floors per Summary §3.5: k=5 (SellerSignal, CategoryPage, GuidePage, ComparisonPage), k=10 (HeatMapCell), k=20 (MarketIntelligenceReport). Violations suppress or coarsen the rendered content.

**Claim Verification Method.** The mechanism by which a Seller Org proves ownership of a SellerSoftware row. One of: DNS TXT record, verified email at the seller's domain, Ops manual verification, or SSO domain match. See §4.4.9.

**Minor-Update Bypass (GuidePage).** A publish path for GuidePage that skips editorial re-review when `refresh_diff_score < 0.10`, allowing small cadence refreshes to land without reviewer involvement. Authored extension; flagged for human sign-off in RECONCILIATION.md.

**First-Import-Free Rule.** A Seller Org's first successful GhostBidImport transition to `published` does not create an AI Operation billing entry; second and subsequent imports do. Computed atomically at publish via a reconciliation worker that handles race conditions between concurrent imports.

**Distinctiveness Score (SellerSignal).** A secondary check on top of the raw k-anon floor that suppresses a signal when the combination of (region, industry, company_size_band) is narrow enough that identifying a single contributing buyer becomes feasible even at cohort ≥ k. Threshold governed via C.97 Baseline Assumption Manager.

### Terms Introduced in §4.4.19–§4.4.22 (Marketplace Monetization & Seller Onboarding)

**PromotedListing.** The keyword-targeted, category-scoped paid-placement record governed by §34.16.1 and §4.4.19. Purchased by eligible Seller Orgs per §34.1.2; priced under a second-price auction on dual metrics (impression + qualified EOI acceptance); category-slot cap, purchased-top-up cap, and monetary ceilings are authoritative in §34.16.1.A. Accounting-isolated under `rev_marketplace_discovery`. See §4.4.19.

**Second-Price Auction Clearing.** The auction mechanic used by PromotedListing: the highest bidder wins but pays the second-highest bid plus a 1-cent increment. When only one qualified listing exists, the cleared price equals the listing's declared floor (min of `bid_impression_cents` and the published surface reserve). Property-tested at §4.4.19 AC 5 against first-price clearing regressions.

**Frequency Cap Config (PromotedListing).** The JSON schema on `PromotedListing.frequency_cap_config` that bounds per-buyer repetition: default max **3 impressions per (buyer_org_id, category_id) per rolling 7-day window** per Summary §6.16.6. Overridable only by Ops. Schema keys: `max_impressions_per_buyer_per_category_per_rolling_window`, `rolling_window_days`, `max_eois_solicited_per_buyer_per_rolling_window`.

**Category Cap (PromotedListing).** The maximum number of concurrently-active PromotedListings per Marketplace Category. Value source: §34.16.1.A `promoted_listing_category_slot_cap`. Enforced transactionally via `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the `(category_id, status)` partial index under SERIALIZABLE isolation (§4.4.19 AC 2).

**Included Allotment vs. Purchased Top-Up.** The two `placement_mode` values on PromotedListing. `included_allotment` consumes one of the Seller Org's plan-included monthly slots per §34.1.2; `purchased_top_up` is billed and capped per §34.16.1.A.

**FeaturedPlacement.** The Ops-curated, editorially-selected placement record per Summary §2.10, C.131, and Sourcera_Seller_Pricing_Strategy §12.3. Rendered on CategoryPage (M9), ComparisonPage (M11), and HeatMapCell (M13). Strictly editorial at launch; paid-commitment variant is reserved under feature-flag `featured_placement_paid_mode_enabled` (default `false`) and requires Ops Council + Finance + Legal sign-off to activate. Labeled with persistent "Featured" FTC-compliant visual treatment on every render. See §4.4.20.

**Editorial Mode (FeaturedPlacement).** `placement_mode = 'editorial'`: the current authoritative FeaturedPlacement mode. Ops Marketing Editor authors a `selection_rationale` and `selection_signal_snapshot_json` capturing the frozen selection criteria (verification tier, category relevance, KB health, buyer engagement signals). No seller payment. Billing fields (`contracted_price_cents`, `billing_currency`, `invoice_ref_id`) MUST be null.

**Paid-Commitment Mode (FeaturedPlacement).** `placement_mode = 'paid_commitment'`: reserved future mode. Requires the `featured_placement_paid_mode_enabled` feature-flag and the `paid_featured_write` Ops entitlement. Represents a contractual commitment window; billing fields populated. Proration handled via Finance policy. See RECONCILIATION → Known Gaps for the editorial-vs-paid source-conflict resolution path.

**FTC Native-Advertising Disclosure (§4.4.19 / §4.4.20).** Per FTC 16 CFR Part 255, paid or sponsored content must be clearly and conspicuously disclosed. PromotedListing carries a fixed `ftc_disclosure_label = "Promoted"`; FeaturedPlacement carries a fixed `ftc_disclosure_label = "Featured"` plus an Ops-authored `ftc_tooltip_copy_markdown` explaining the editorial basis. DOM contract tests enforce render on every surface.

**VerificationReviewRecord.** The Ops-review ledger for Seller Org verification-tier upgrades governed by §34.16.2 eligibility / platform-integrity policy and §44.1 verification-review operational windows. Captures the request (Verified or Certified), the uploaded documentation refs, the reviewer assignment, the outcome, and the cadence of re-review. Verification tiers are **earned, not purchased** — no seller ever pays Sourcera for a tier badge. See §4.4.21.

**Verification Tier Prerequisites.** `verified` requires Seller Solo+ plan, the §34.16.2.A `verification_verified_profile_completeness_pct_required` threshold, and SOC 2 or ISO 27001 documentation. `certified` requires Seller Growth+, a valid Verified prerequisite record, §34.16.2.A `verification_certified_closed_bid_count_required` / `verification_certified_buyer_confirmed_bid_count_required` thresholds, the §34.16.2.A `verification_certified_kb_health_floor_default`, and all applicable compliance docs (SOC 2 always; ISO 27001 always; HIPAA or PCI per Marketplace Category configuration). See §4.4.21.

**Separation of Duties (VerificationReviewRecord).** The rule that the reviewer who approved a Seller Org's Verified prerequisite cannot be the sole reviewer for the dependent Certified upgrade. Enforced at write-time via `verification_review_separation_of_duties_violation` (Appendix I); override path requires a senior reviewer (`ops_verification_senior_reviewer` role) with explicit audited rationale.

**Quarterly Re-Review (Certified Tier).** The recurring cadence for Certified verification records is authoritative in §44.1 `Verification certified re-review cadence`. A nightly scheduler creates a new `quarterly_rereview` record at the §44.1 `Verification certified re-review pre-notification lead` before `next_review_due_at` for seller pre-notification. Failure to submit by the due date triggers downgrade (`quarterly_rereview_not_submitted`).

**SLA Breach Auto-Rejection (VerificationReviewRecord).** Review SLA targets are authoritative in §44.1 `Verification review terminal-decision SLA - Verified` and §44.1 `Verification review terminal-decision SLA - Certified`. Nightly sweeper transitions `pending` records past `sla_target_at` to `auto_rejected_sla_breach`; seller receives a zero-cost resubmit credit.

**SellerOnboardingSession.** The per-seller-user onboarding-funnel ledger per Summary §6.28.2 (seven-stage Seller Onboarding Experience) and C.132 / C.133 / C.135 / C.136 / C.140 / C.141. The system-of-record for the **Seller Activation Metric** (C.135). Every stage transition emits a PostHog event; every stage's success criterion is asserted against this row. See §4.4.22.

**Seller Activation Metric.** The canonical per-seller activation latency: `activation_metric_elapsed_seconds = EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM first_requirement_response_at - stage_1_arrival_at)`. Targets are authoritative in §44.1 `Seller Activation Metric p50 target` and §44.1 `Seller Activation Metric p90 target`, with C.135 carried forward as source material. Computed inside the same transaction as `first_requirement_response_at` write; a database trigger asserts monotonicity.

**Hero-Moment Completion.** `SellerOnboardingSession.hero_moment_completed_at IS NOT NULL` iff all three Stage 3 surfaces (KB Draft, first-pass response, progress strip) rendered pre-touch AND `stage_3_population_latency_ms` satisfies §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold`. Written by the Bid Workspace render path at first paint. Per Summary §6.28.2, Stage-3 population success is a P0 availability metric; on-call paging follows §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 latency breach page SLA`.

**Four Seller Conversion Moments.** The SPS v3 §15.3 set: (a) mid-bid AI budget wall, (b) second concurrent bid, (c) first EOI attempt, (d) KB ceiling approach. Recorded on `SellerOnboardingSession.stage_7_conversion_moment_kind`. Power the 18% trailing-90-day conversion target reporting and the CM1 Free -> Solo funnel segment.

**Forced-Vendor-Signup Playbook.** The Summary C.136 / Summary §6.28.2 playbook that automatically creates a SellerOnboardingSession on magic-link click from a Buyer-initiated invite, GhostBidImport, buyer referral, or Pro Trial Seat Grant. The Seller Org + User are created at Stage 2 SSO completion.

**Abandonment Classifier.** The nightly sweep that transitions `SellerOnboardingSession.completion_state = 'in_progress'` to `'abandoned'` when no stage advancement has occurred for 7 days AND `stage_reached < 4`. Sets `abandoned_at`, `abandon_stage`, and `abandon_reason_code`. Abandoned sessions that later resume on activation transition to `reactivated`, preserving the original `stage_1_arrival_at` for truthful latency reporting.

**Reactivation (SellerOnboardingSession).** The completion state for sessions that previously abandoned but subsequently achieve `first_requirement_response_at`. The original `abandoned_at` is retained for funnel histograms; the seller is counted once in the activated cohort but their activation latency is computed against the original `stage_1_arrival_at` (§4.4.22 AC 9).

**Capability Graceful Degradation (Onboarding).** Per C.140, if the `first_pass_response` capability fails at Stage 2/3, the Bid Workspace renders KB-Draft-only and `capability_degradation_triggered = true`; the session still progresses. The Stage-3 population-latency alert still fires when §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold` is breached.

**MarketplaceDiscoveryLedgerEntry (retired alias).** Pre-Phase-2.2 placeholder name for the PromotedListing marketplace-discovery billing row. The live canonical entity is `MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord` (§4.8.12), keyed for PromotedListing by `sku='promoted_listing'`, `source_entity_type='promoted_listing'`, and `source_entity_id = PromotedListing.id`. Do not author a separate `MarketplaceDiscoveryLedgerEntry` table; financial isolation is enforced by §4.8.12 `cost_center='rev_marketplace_discovery'`.

**PromotedListingAuctionRun.** The platform-internal append-only auction decision log row for PromotedListing second-price clearing. Captures `auction_run_id`, `eligible_listing_ids[]`, `winner_promoted_listing_id`, `cleared_price_cents`, and a per-auction-salted `buyer_org_id_hash`. Retained per the §40.2 PromotedListing auction-run raw-retention window, then rolled into quarterly auction-fairness aggregates. See §4.4.19.1.

### Terms Introduced in §4.5 (v7.0.0 Integration, Phase 3)

**Taxonomy Node.** The single platform-scoped registry behind every controlled-vocabulary dimension the Marketplace depends on beyond Marketplace Category. Multi-kind (one table, one state machine, `kind`-scoped namespacing), Ops-managed, versioned, deprecation-aware with successor-pointer migrations. Two-level hierarchy max (depth 0 or 1). For `kind=marketplace_category`, the paired §4.4.7 Marketplace Category row holds authority over category-specific fields; the Taxonomy Node row exists as a shared-registry projection. See §4.5.4. Summary C.60 and C.95.

**Taxonomy Projection (Marketplace Category).** The 1:1 pairing between a `kind=marketplace_category` Taxonomy Node row and a §4.4.7 Marketplace Category row. Reconciled nightly by `taxonomy_projection_drift` alert; mismatches raise an Ops alert.

**Taxonomy Merge.** The Ops operation that collapses a Taxonomy Node into its `successor_id`. Executes FK rewrites on all referencing entities in idempotent batches of 500 with a 10-minute bounded-lag SLO. Transitions source node to `merged`; irreversible post-completion.

**Taxonomy Redirect Chain.** The 301 redirect path generated by deprecated Taxonomy Nodes with `deprecation_action=redirect_to_successor`. Maximum chain depth is 3 hops; the 4th hop returns 410 with a canonical fallback to the root Marketplace index.

**Controlled-Vocabulary Tag.** The individual, seller-referenceable tag values attached to Capability Declarations, Marketplace Listings, Seller Profile industries and certifications, and SoftwarePage structured data. Finer-grained than Taxonomy Node (a Taxonomy Node represents a dimension; a Controlled-Vocabulary Tag represents an individual published value under a dimension). Sellers MAY propose new tags via the §27.6 proposal workflow; Ops approval gates publication. Append-only once approved; retirement via deprecation-with-successor. See §4.5.5.

**Sellers-Cannot-Create-Freeform-Tags Rule.** The write-layer enforcement that every tag value written to any consumer entity (Capability Declaration, Marketplace Listing filter, Seller Profile industries/certifications, SoftwarePage structured data) MUST exist in `(state=approved AND visibility=public)` at the time of write. Violations return `consumer_requires_approved_tag` (HTTP 422) with a Levenshtein-based "did you mean" suggestion. Summary C.60. See §4.5.5.

**Vocab Tag Review SLA.** 5 business days from `submitted` → `in_review` → terminal decision on a Controlled-Vocabulary Tag proposal. Breach emits `vocab_tag.review_slo_breach` and pages the `ops_marketing_editor` on-call. See §4.5.5.

**Marketplace-Domain Read/Render Contract.** The uniform precondition pipeline every marketplace-domain render path executes before emitting any row identifying a Seller Org or a SellerSoftware: acquire opt-out snapshot (≤ 60s), resolve scope matches, apply redaction decision, build Schema.org with suppressed-ids omitted, honor partial-opt-out page-type filters. Consolidated in §4.5.6 as a cross-reference to the §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Record entity.

**Retroactive Sweep (Vendor Opt-Out).** The worker that enumerates every already-published marketplace-domain page referencing a newly opted-out entity and re-renders each with the opt-out applied. Progress tracked in `retro_backfill_status`. SLO: ≤ 15 minutes for ≤ 10,000 pages; ≤ 60 minutes for ≤ 100,000; up to 4 hours for > 100,000 (with explicit Ops progress bar). Batching per `retroactive_sweep` retry-curve class in §31.

**Vendor Opt-Out Redaction Placeholder.** The deterministic, layout-preserving token emitted in place of an identifying row when the opt-out render contract suppresses a candidate (e.g., ComparisonPage emits an "Opted out" column rather than collapsing the column). See §4.5.6.

**Marketplace Abuse Report.** The first-class entity materializing the §45.3 abuse-escalation workflow. Supports buyer, seller, anonymous public, Ops-internal, and automated-signal reporters; polymorphic subject kinds; severity triage; seller appeal within a 7-day window; Ops 24-hour triage SLA; immutable `subject_snapshot_json` so closure survives subject hard-purge. See §4.5.7.

**Abuse Report Triage SLA.** 24 hours from `created_at` to the first transition out of `pending_review`. Breach stamps `sla_breach_at` and emits `abuse_report.sla_breach`.

**Appeal Magic Link.** The authenticated, deadline-gated link emailed to the subject Seller Org Admin when a Marketplace Abuse Report reaches `awaiting_seller_response`. Requires logged-in session match to the `subject_org_id` with `seller_org_admin` role; unauthenticated click routes to sign-in; link expires at `appeal_deadline_at`. See §4.5.7, §4.7.2 (reused for disqualification appeals).

**Subject Snapshot.** The immutable `subject_snapshot_json` captured on Marketplace Abuse Report creation. Preserves the subject content at report time so terminal Ops decision is possible even when the subject is subsequently hard-purged. See §4.5.7.

**EOI Acceptance Record.** The first-class, queryable, auditable record of the buyer-side one-click EOI acceptance decision referenced in Summary C.62 and §27.5. 1:1 with the §4.5.2 EOI Record; materializes a Target Account, emits a Console Bridge Event, dispatches seller and buyer-team notifications, and optionally materializes a Bid Workspace (immediately on `accept_and_skip_nda`, on NDA execution otherwise). Supports bulk acceptance (≤ 25 per batch) and reversal within 72 hours. See §4.5.8.

**One-Click Acceptance Flow.** The atomic, transactional sequence that fires on an EOI Acceptance Record write: Target Account creation, Console Bridge Event emission with firewall-redacted payload, seller notification via Loops.so, buyer-team notification fan-out per §18, EOI Record state transition to `approved`, optional Bid Workspace materialization, and Match Score snapshot stamping. See §4.5.8.

**Bulk Acceptance Batch.** A single API call that accepts up to 25 EOIs, producing one EOI Acceptance Record per EOI with a shared `bulk_accept_batch_id`. Per-record failures do not roll back the batch; successes remain. Rate-limited to 2 batches per 15 minutes per buyer user.

**Acceptance Reversal.** An append-only reversal record that points at the original EOI Acceptance Record (and vice-versa) and executes a reversal cascade: Target Account withdrawal, Bid Workspace cancellation, NDA revocation, Console Bridge Event emission of kind `eoi_acceptance_reversed`. Permitted by Workspace Owner/Admin within 72 hours of original acceptance; post-72h requires Ops. See §4.5.8.

**EOI Acceptance Seller-Visible Projection.** The fixed whitelist of EOI Acceptance Record fields carried across the firewall to the Seller Console: `{id, accepted_at, acceptance_action, acceptance_conditions, referenced_capability_declaration_ids, resulting_bid_workspace_id, nda_required, nda_record_id}`. All other fields (including `accepted_by_user_id`, `source_surface`, `bulk_accept_batch_id`, `match_score_*`, reversal internals) are NEVER returned to the seller. Enforced at the API serializer.

### Terms Introduced in §4.7 (v7.0.0 Integration, Phase 3)

**Console Bridge Event.** The authoritative per-change cross-console sync unit between a Buyer Workspace and its linked Seller Bid Workspace(s). One row per atomic source change (fan-out events produce N rows, one per Bid Workspace). Carries a firewall-compliant redacted payload, retry state, bounded-lag SLO metadata, conflict resolution disposition, and cross-Workspace correlation. Summary C.116 and C.117. See §4.7.1.

**Dual-Console Firewall — Bridge Enforcement.** The two-layer redaction-and-projection enforcement applied by Console Bridge Event: write-time validator ensures `payload_json` conforms to the kind's field-level redaction whitelist and rejects mismatches with `console_bridge_event_firewall_violation`; seller serializer applies a defense-in-depth secondary whitelist at read. Firewall violation patterns alert the Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100). The authoritative isolation contract is **§1.3 Dual-Console Data Isolation Model** + **§1.4 Query Scoping Requirements**; body citations of "(§7.2)" are anchor-shorthand resolving to §1.3 + §1.4 per the §7.2 disambiguation note (D-6.1-013 remediation, 2026-05-06). See §4.7.1 for the bridge-enforcement projection rules.

**Redaction Verification Hash.** The sha256 hash over a canonicalized serialization of `payload_json` with the kind's whitelist applied. Stored on every Console Bridge Event; re-verified at every retry. Mismatch triggers firewall-violation rejection and SIM alert.

**Seller-Visible Projection (Console Bridge Event).** The kind-specific whitelist applied by the seller-side serializer to every Console Bridge Event read. Defense-in-depth over write-time redaction. QA test `console_bridge_seller_projection_defense_in_depth` asserts compliance for each event kind. See §4.7.1.

**Bounded-Lag SLO (Console Bridge).** The 30-second SLO from `created_at` to `synced_at` per Summary C.117. Observable via `slo_bounded_lag_ms` and `slo_breach_flag`. Breach rate > 1% over a rolling 15-minute window pages Ops. Terminal `dlq` and `failed` states are excluded from the SLO accounting (surfaced separately as anomalies).

**Bridge Apply Schedule `bridge_apply_standard`.** The non-webhook exponential-backoff schedule applied to Console Bridge Event apply failures: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s — 5 attempts total. Post-5 transitions to `dlq` with Ops alert. Defined in §25.2.2 and Appendix J as outside `webhook_retry_class`; Bridge-domain webhooks use Appendix F.1 `standard`.

**Console Bridge DLQ.** The dead-letter queue state entered after 5 failed Console Bridge Event apply attempts. Visible in the buyer Workspace Bridge Health panel (full detail), the seller Bid Workspace Sync Health panel (redacted detail), and the Ops Console cross-Workspace bridge dashboard. Re-drive requires explicit Ops action (no automated re-drive) to prevent infinite loops on persistent failures. See §4.7.1.

**Idempotency Key (Console Bridge).** The unique `(buyer_workspace_id, bid_workspace_id, event_kind, source_entity_id, source_entity_version)` tuple enforced by a unique index on Console Bridge Event rows. Duplicate writes return the existing row's id (HTTP 200) rather than failing. Prevents duplicate apply across restarts and retries.

**Fan-Out Group.** The `fanout_group_id` correlation id that groups Console Bridge Events produced by a single source operation broadcast to N Bid Workspaces (e.g., Amendment broadcast, account-level Vendor Disqualification cascade). One row per target; shared `fanout_group_id` enables batch observability. See §4.7.1.

**Superseded Event.** A Console Bridge Event in the `superseded` state, set when a newer event for the same source entity arrives before the current event is applied. The `superseded_by_event_id` pointer carries the forwarding. Implements `last_write_wins` conflict resolution for rapid successive edits. See §4.7.1.

**Last-Write-Wins (Console Bridge).** The default conflict-resolution rule for concurrent buyer-side edits on the same source entity. Newer event supersedes older pending/retrying events. Alternatives per event kind: `buyer_origin_wins` (bidirectional conflicts), `operation_non_idempotent_dlq` (non-idempotent operations like `requirement_reverted` on amended versions), `merge_op` (Amendments are rebased against current state). See §4.7.1.

**Daily Bridge Reconciliation.** The 2am UTC job per §25.2 that scans for stale Console Bridge Events (`pending` or `retrying` > 24h) across all workspaces, escalates to DLQ or re-drives as appropriate, and emits `console_bridge.reconciliation_summary` with per-workspace counts.

**Vendor Disqualification Record.** The first-class entity materializing the §25.3 / Summary C.118 disqualification workflow. Supports three severities: `soft` (workspace-local), `account_level` (buyer Org's Workspaces, forward-looking 12 months), `global_ban` (Ops-imposed across the platform). Binds the buyer-private `rationale_internal` to the vendor-visible `notification_body_to_vendor` with explicit asymmetric-visibility fields; carries cascade status, appeal workflow, and reversal rules. See §4.7.2.

**Disqualification Cascade.** The set of downstream effects triggered by a Vendor Disqualification Record write: Target Account transition, Bid Workspace transition, response locking, Q&A orphaning, Scoring-matrix exclusion (where applicable), Console Bridge Event emission, Seller Signal suppression, EOI auto-rejection (account_level), Marketplace Listing hiding and page 410 (global_ban). Completion observable via `cascade_status`. Soft SLA: 10s. Account-level SLA: 60s (fan-out). See §4.7.2.

**Disqualification Reversal.** The reverse of the cascade, executed when a disqualification is overturned on appeal, reversed by the Workspace Owner within 72 hours (soft only), or reversed by Ops leadership (global_ban). Preserves historical Selection Reports (no rewrite); post-Phase-12 reversals annotate rather than re-open Scoring. See §4.7.2.

**Rationale Asymmetry.** The deliberate separation between buyer-private `rationale_internal` (NEVER carried across the firewall) and vendor-visible `notification_body_to_vendor` (always carried) on Vendor Disqualification Records. Enforced by the Console Bridge Event redaction validator for kind `disqualification_issued`. See §4.7.2.

**Notification Style (Disqualification).** The `notification_style` enum on Vendor Disqualification Records: `neutral_no_rationale` (default; no rationale shared), `rationale_shared_with_vendor` (buyer explicit opt-in + Ops approval; not permitted for global_ban), `silent_no_vendor_notification` (global_ban Ops-covert investigations). See §4.7.2.

**Disqualification Appeal Window.** The deadline for a Seller Org to appeal a Vendor Disqualification Record: `not_offered` for `soft`, 14 days for `account_level`, 30 days for `global_ban`. Global ban overturn requires Ops leadership dual sign-off. See §4.7.2.

**Ops Compliance Admin Role.** The Ops Console role empowered to reverse Vendor Disqualification Records beyond the 72-hour Workspace Owner window and to co-sign `global_ban` severity transitions with an Ops leadership user. Appendix J.

**Ops Content Admin Role.** The Ops Console role empowered to take `seller_banned` closure dispositions on Marketplace Abuse Reports. `org_level_all_consoles` bans require dual sign-off by two `ops_content_admin` users. Appendix J.

**Superseded by Global Ban.** The annotation applied to existing soft Vendor Disqualification Records when a global ban on the same seller takes effect. Existing records remain in place for audit integrity; `superseded_by_global_ban=true` flags them; surfaces reduce to Ops-only. See §4.7.2.

### Terms Introduced in §4.8 (v7.0.0 Integration, Phase 4)

**AIOperation.** The canonical, immutable, single-row record of one billable AI invocation. Org-scoped, console-tagged, append-only after settlement. Joins the four billing facts: what was billed (capability, model_tier, cost basis), who consumed it (actor + console + workspace), against which wallet, locked at which FX rate. Settlement state machine: `pending → accepted | rejected | auto_accepted → contested → reversed`. Per Summary C.75 the single billing unit across the platform. See §4.8.1.

**CapabilityRegistryEntry.** The Ops-Console-managed authoritative list of every capability that can produce an AIOperation. Supersedes the v6.0.0 hardcoded "21 capabilities" reference. State machine: `alpha → beta → active → deprecated → retired`. Per Summary C.76. See §4.8.2.

**AIWallet.** The Org-scoped, console-pooled value-dollar account that customer-billed AIOperations draw against. One row per Org. Pooled across both buyer and seller consoles per Pricing Strategy §11. State machine includes `active`, `soft_warned_50`, `soft_warned_80`, `hard_capped_100`, `payment_failed_grace`, `suspended`, `closed`. See §4.8.3.

**OutcomeContract.** The per-capability versioned, Ops-managed signal contract that drives AIOperation acceptance/rejection resolution. Versioned: contract changes do NOT retroactively reclassify settled operations; pending operations resolve under the contract version active at AIOperation write. Per Pricing Strategy §10. See §4.8.4.

**ContestRecord.** The per-AIOperation, customer-initiated dispute record. Filed by `billing_admin` within the 14-day contest window per Summary C.78. State machine: `open → in_review → approved | rejected | escalated`; `withdrawn` from `open`. Auto-filed by the system when a late outcome signal arrives after auto-accept. See §4.8.5.

**CostBaseRecalculationLog.** The per-run audit record of the nightly job that re-derives `cost_base_cents` from actual Anthropic billing, Convex compute attribution, and external-provider billing. Drift severity drives auto-applied vs Ops-Finance-approval routing per Summary C.77. Margin-floor breach (margin < 88%) requires explicit override. See §4.8.6.

**FreeAllowanceCounter.** The per-Org-per-capability counter implementing Summary C.80: 10 free operations per signup as a PLG lever. Default lifetime quota; per-period reset configurable per capability. Atomic decrement-and-return prevents double-spend. AIOperation rows consumed against this counter set `billed_against_free_allowance=true` and `effective_charge_cents=0`. See §4.8.7.

**CommittedSpendContract.** The Enterprise annual AI value-dollar commit per Summary C.81. Discount bands derived from `commit_value_dollars` are authored canonically in §34.2.4 (single source — never restated inline per the `volume_discount_band_single_source` validator). Floor: $12K/yr per Pricing Strategy §6. AIOperations preferentially burn down the commit pool before drawing the wallet's `budget_value_dollars`. See §4.8.8, §34.2.4.

**PricingTableVersion.** The publish-time snapshot that backs the Public Pricing API at `api.sourcera.com/v1/pricing` per Summary C.83. Immutable once published; customers can pin a version for forecasting reproducibility but AIOperation pricing always uses the current published version. `breaking_change_flag=true` requires 30-day-advance customer notification. See §4.8.9.

**DowngradeExcessDataBucket.** The per-Org-per-data-class record of entities preserved in read-only mode for 90 days after a plan downgrade per Summary C.85. State machine: `active_preservation → notice_sent_d60 → notice_sent_d80 → archive_pending → archived`; `restored` reachable from any prior state when customer upgrades back. Hard-archive at preservation_until; cold-storage retention 7 years. See §4.8.10.

**BillingSeatSnapshot.** The periodic point-in-time count of active seats per Org per console for analytics, plan-gate enforcement, and Stripe invoice line-item context per Summary C.86. Sourcera does NOT charge per seat; this snapshot is reporting-only. Guests and API-only identities excluded. Snapshots immutable post-creation. See §4.8.11.

**Value Price.** The customer-facing price of an AIOperation when the Outcome Resolver fires `accepted` or `auto_accepted`. Default formula: `cost_base_cents × value_multiplier` (default `value_multiplier = 10.000`); floor `min_value_price_cents` from CapabilityRegistryEntry. Locked at AIOperation write time.

**Cost Price.** The customer-facing price of an AIOperation when the Outcome Resolver fires `rejected`. Default formula: `cost_base_cents × cost_multiplier` (default `cost_multiplier = 1.050`); floor `min_cost_price_cents`. Bills at near-cost so rejected outputs are never profitable per Pricing Strategy §2.4 / §2.6. Margin-protection mechanism.

**Cost Base.** The per-capability per-model-tier underlying cost in integer USD cents, re-derived nightly by the cost_base recalc job from actual Anthropic billing + Convex compute + external-provider billing. The customer never sees `cost_base` directly; they see `value_price` and `cost_price` denominated in stable value-dollars per Pricing Strategy §11.

**FX-Locking.** The mechanism by which an AIOperation's billing-currency exchange rate is locked at write time to the daily Treasury rate for `(legal_entity, billing_currency)`. Preserved through `contested` and `reversed` so a reversal credit issues at the same FX rate as the original charge. Per Summary C.84.

**Residency-Locked Invoicing.** The mechanism by which the legal entity that issues the customer's invoice is determined deterministically from the Org's `data_residency_region` per the canonical 4-row mapping: `us → sourcera_us_llc`, `eu → sourcera_eu_gmbh`, `apac → sourcera_apac_pte`, `custom → sourcera_custom`. The mapping is total over the 4-value `residency_region_kind` enum (Appendix J post-D-AJ-005) and surjective onto the 4-value `legal_entity_kind` enum (Appendix J post-D-AJ-004 / post-v7.2.0-REM-Phase-5 D-RES-004 reconciliation, 2026-05-20); the pre-Phase-2V value `sourcera_uk_ltd` is retired (UK-resident Orgs route through `sourcera_eu_gmbh` per the pre-Phase-2V "subset of `eu`" treatment, now canonical, OR through `sourcera_custom` keyed on `custom_sovereign_residency_label = uk_crown_secure` for UK-sovereign-cloud Enterprise contracts). Locked on AIWallet at first creation; locked on AIOperation at write; preserved through `contested` and `reversed`. Atomically rebound on Org residency change per §34.10.5.A Stripe-Customer Atomic-Binding Protocol (v7.2.0-REM Phase 5, 2026-05-20): new Stripe Customer created keyed on the new `(org_id, legal_entity)` pair; prior Stripe Customer closed for new invoices; legacy invoices remain on the legacy Customer for SOC-2 audit fidelity; in-flight `pending` AIOperations settle on the prior Customer to honor the §4.8.1 FX-Locking semantics. Per Summary C.84. CI gate `legal_entity_residency_change_revenue_leak_test` (Appendix M.5 §M.5.17) asserts the canonical 4-value enforcement + the atomic-binding invariant + the historical-row read-fidelity for legacy `sourcera_uk_ltd` rows.

**Settlement Freeze.** The state of an AIOperation in which all writes other than DSAR redaction are rejected with `ai_operation_immutable_after_settlement` (HTTP 422). Reached when `settlement_state ∈ {accepted, rejected, auto_accepted, reversed}` AND `contest_window_at < now`. Preserves financial-record integrity.

**Contest Window.** The 14-day (default; capability-overridable per OutcomeContract.`contest_window_days`) period after `settlement_at` during which a customer's `billing_admin` may file a ContestRecord against an AIOperation. Per Summary C.78.

**Outcome Resolver.** The system component responsible for transitioning AIOperations from `pending` to `accepted` / `rejected` / `auto_accepted` based on the OutcomeContract for the operation's capability. Operates per AIOperation. Default-on-timeout is `rejected` per Pricing Strategy §6 unless `requires_explicit_user_signal=true`.

**Auto-Accept Timer.** The `auto_accept_after_seconds` countdown on a `pending` AIOperation; on expiry without an outcome signal, the operation transitions to `auto_accepted` and bills at value price. Distinct from `accepted` for product-quality dashboards (high `auto_accepted` rate is a quality signal).

**Wallet Hold.** The soft reservation of `value_price_cents` from the wallet at AIOperation write time, ensuring the funds are available for the eventual settlement charge. On settlement, the hold is converted to a charge (if accepted/auto_accepted) or partially released (if rejected, with `cost_price_cents` charged).

**Soft Credit.** The temporary wallet credit applied when a ContestRecord is filed against an `accepted` or `auto_accepted` AIOperation. Reversed if the contest is rejected; finalized as a permanent credit if approved.

**Drift Severity.** The categorical magnitude of the per-capability cost_base change observed by the nightly recalc job: `normal` (≤5%), `warning_5_10` (5–10%), `alert_10_25` (10–25%), `critical_gt_25` (>25%). Drives auto-apply vs explicit Ops Finance approval routing per Summary C.77.

**Margin Floor Breach.** A flag on a CostBaseRecalculationLog row indicating the proposed new value price would yield gross margin below 88% (per Pricing Strategy §2.6). Never auto-applied; requires explicit Ops Finance override or capability deprecation.

**Free Allowance.** The per-Org-per-capability default-10 free operations granted on signup as the primary PLG lever per Summary C.80 / Pricing Strategy §3 / Seller §14. Exhaustion surfaces an inline upgrade CTA with the ROI of the operations already run.

**Committed Spend Pool.** The Enterprise pre-paid commit balance that AIOperations preferentially burn down before drawing the wallet's `budget_value_dollars`. Tracked via `commit_burn_remaining_value_dollars` on AIWallet, reconciled nightly against CommittedSpendContract.

**Discount Band.** The categorical Enterprise commit-volume discount per Summary C.81: `none`, `band_25k_10pct`, `band_50k_15pct`, `band_100k_20pct`, `band_250k_25pct`. Derived deterministically from `commit_value_dollars` at signature; locked.

**Public Pricing API.** The publicly-readable rate-card endpoint at `api.sourcera.com/v1/pricing` per Summary C.83. Backed by PricingTableVersion. Customers can forecast spend programmatically; published payload includes capabilities, value/cost prices, currencies, plan tiers, free allowances, deprecation banners.

**Breaking Pricing Change.** A PricingTableVersion change involving a customer-visible price increase or capability removal. Requires 30-day-advance customer notification per Pricing Strategy §11; publish rejected with HTTP 422 if `customer_notification_sent_at < effective_at - 30 days`.

**Downgrade Excess Preservation.** The 90-day read-only preservation period per Summary C.85 during which entities exceeding the new plan's caps remain accessible (read-only) to the customer. After preservation, hard-archived to cold storage; restorable for up to 90 days post-archive.

**Restoration Partial.** The case in which a customer upgrades back from a downgrade but to a tier insufficient to re-cover all preserved entities. The bucket flags `restoration_partial=true`; the user explicitly selects which entities to restore; remaining entities stay in the bucket.

**Billing Admin Role.** A new Org-scoped role authored in Phase 4 (orthogonal to `org_admin`): permissions are confined to the billing surface — read AIWallet, file ContestRecord, view BillingSeatSnapshot, configure auto-topup, view Billing Ledger across both consoles. No data access to workspaces or marketplace surfaces. Authored as the role gate for the Pricing Strategy §6 / §7 admin actions.

**Ops Finance Admin Role.** The Ops Console role with full read/write across the §4.8 entities for financial review, contest decisions, cost-base approvals, commit-contract management, pricing-table publication, and downgrade restorations.

**Ops Capability Admin Role.** The Ops Console role with CRUD authority on CapabilityRegistryEntry and OutcomeContract — the only role that may add new capabilities to the platform's billable surface.

**Cost Center.** The accounting attribution on every AIOperation: `customer_billed` charges hit the wallet; `sourcera_owned` and `platform_marketing` are recorded for COGS without wallet impact. Drives the Marketplace-content (M9–M13) Sourcera-funded AI operations that produce public pages without customer billing.

**Provenance Hash.** The 64-char sha256 hex over `(capability_id, prompt_template_version, input_content_hash, model_id, cost_base_version_id, billing_currency, fx_rate_locked)` on AIOperation. Used by ContestRecord to assert a specific operation; immutable after AIOperation write.

**Effective Charge.** The final wallet charge for an AIOperation after settlement. Equals `value_price_cents` for `accepted`/`auto_accepted`, `cost_price_cents` for `rejected`, and `0` for `reversed`. Frozen at settlement.

**Auto-Filed Contest.** A ContestRecord automatically generated by the system (not by a user) when a late `rejected` outcome signal arrives after an AIOperation has already auto-accepted. Reason code `auto_filed_late_signal`; routes to Ops Finance for review. Customer-trust + margin-protection mechanism: catches outcome-resolver bugs without requiring the customer to notice.

**MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord.** The seller-Org-scoped, accounting-isolated line-item record for non-AI marketplace monetization (promoted listings, verification-tier reserve, featured-placement reserve) per Summary §2.10 / Summary §6.16.6 / C.131. `cost_center` MUST equal `rev_marketplace_discovery`; rows MUST NOT be aggregated with `rev_ai_wallet` or `rev_subscription` in any finance dashboard. Integer-cents monetary storage; FX-locked per C.84; `legal_entity` residency-derived at invoice finalization. Does NOT debit AIWallet and does NOT create or mutate AIOperation rows. Append-only post-invoice; refunds create companion negative rows. 7-year SOC-2 retention; hard-delete forbidden. See §4.8.12.

**Marketplace Discovery Cost Center.** The single-value cost-center constant `rev_marketplace_discovery` required on every MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord per Summary §6.16.6. Target gross margin ≈ 95%+. Finance dashboard queries MUST partition by this cost center and MUST NOT UNION with `rev_ai_wallet` (≈ 4.5%) or `rev_subscription` (≈ 85–90%).

**Marketplace Discovery SKU.** The three-value enum `{promoted_listing, verification_upgrade, featured_placement}` governing MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord classification. Currently only `promoted_listing` is priced; its pricing and cap constants are authoritative in §34.16.1.A and plan eligibility is authoritative in §34.1.2. `verification_upgrade` and `featured_placement` are reserved per Summary C.131 but unpriced per Seller Pricing §12.

**K-Anonymity Cohort (Promoted Listing).** The minimum concurrent-seller cohort size (3) in a category before a promoted listing renders. Captured on MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord at sale time in `k_anonymity_cohort_size_at_sale`; below-floor sales remain `pending` with `status_reason=k_anonymity_pending` until threshold met or 30-day timeout (then `voided` with `k_anonymity_timeout`). Preserves buyer-identity privacy in attribution.

**Refund Companion Row.** The append-only discipline for MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord refunds: the original `paid` row is retained unchanged; a companion negative-amount row is created with `refund_parent_id` pointing at the original. Preserves 7-year SOC-2 audit trail without mutating the financial record.

**SellerOutcomeSignalConfig.** The platform-scoped, seller-console-only, versioned binding from each of the 12 seller capabilities in Summary §2.9 / Seller Pricing §10 to its accepted-signal rule, evaluation window, alt-boundary event, and mandatory `timeout_default = rejected`. Extends OutcomeContract (§4.8.4) with the seller-specific cost-protection stance: silence ⇒ rejected. Exactly one active row per capability; prior versions superseded but retained for AIOperations pending under older rules. See §4.8.13.

**Seller Outcome Signal Capability Set.** The canonical 12-value `seller_outcome_signal_capability` enum: `seller_first_pass_rfp_draft`, `seller_qa_suggestion`, `seller_kb_to_capability_suggestion`, `seller_kb_bootstrap`, `seller_ghost_rfp_ingestion`, `seller_firecrawl_crawl_dedupe`, `seller_kb_staleness_classifier`, `seller_page_enrichment`, `seller_capability_declaration_suggest`, `seller_match_score_numeric`, `seller_bid_task_assignment_suggest`, `seller_document_attach_suggest`. Migration MUST seed exactly 12 SellerOutcomeSignalConfig rows, one per enum value.

**Alt-Boundary Event.** The downstream marketplace event that terminates a SellerOutcomeSignalConfig evaluation window before `window_seconds` elapses (whichever fires first). One of `bid_submission`, `eoi_submission`, `kb_publication`, `response_submission`, or `none`. Implements Seller Pricing §10 semantics such as "14d or on bid submission" for `seller_first_pass_rfp_draft`. On simultaneous time-and-event firings at `t = window_seconds`, tie-breaks to the event to preserve event-primary semantics.

**Timeout-Default-Rejected.** The Seller Pricing §10 / Summary §2.9 invariant that every seller outcome signal defaults to `rejected` on silence. Encoded on SellerOutcomeSignalConfig as `timeout_default = 'rejected'` (single-value enum, DB CHECK enforced). Biases Sourcera toward cost protection when signal is ambiguous.

**K-Anonymity Floor (Seller Outcome Signal).** The cohort-size threshold on a SellerOutcomeSignalConfig below which an accepted-signal fire is deferred to protect buyer identity in attribution-sensitive signals. `seller_match_score_numeric` requires `k_anonymity_floor ≥ 3` per Summary C.131; sub-floor cohorts defer signal firing and then time out to `rejected`.

**Late-Signal Grace (Seller).** Late `accepted` signals arriving after a SellerOutcomeSignalConfig window has expired and the AIOperation has settled as `rejected` (by timeout default) MUST auto-file a ContestRecord with reason `auto_filed_late_signal` per the parallel §4.8.4 OutcomeContract behavior. Protects the customer from resolver-latency bugs without requiring the customer to notice.

**Accounting Isolation.** The rule that MarketplaceDiscoveryRevenueRecord rows MUST NEVER be aggregated with AIWallet (`rev_ai_wallet`) or subscription (`rev_subscription`) revenue in any finance dashboard or report per Summary §6.16.6. Enforced by DB CHECK on `cost_center`, by partitioned indexes, and by QA test `finance_dashboard_cost_center_isolation` asserting dashboard queries never UNION across cost centers. Preserves margin-reporting integrity: discovery ≈ 95%+, AI wallet ≈ 4.5%, subscription ≈ 85–90%.

### Terms Introduced in §21.4 (v7.0.0 Capability Registry Rewrite)
