**Agent Capability Registry.** The platform-scoped, Ops-Console-managed list of every capability the Sourcera Agent can invoke. Authoritatively expressed as `CapabilityRegistryEntry` rows (§4.8.2). Supersedes the v6.0.0 hardcoded "21 capabilities" enumeration; capabilities are added by writing a registry entry, not by editing §21.4. See §21.4 and Summary C.76.

**Initial Registry Seed (v6 → v7).** The set of `CapabilityRegistryEntry` rows loaded at the v7.0.0 publish boundary, comprising (a) the 21 capabilities cataloged in Master Spec v6.0.0 / Summary §6.12.1 (catalogued in §21.4.1); (b) the five seller-console KB Engineering Spec / Pricing Strategy augmentations cataloged in §21.4.1.A (`firecrawl_crawl_dedupe`, `capability_declaration_suggest`, `match_score_numeric`, `bid_task_assignment_suggest`, `document_attach_suggest`); and (c) the 11 Extended Capabilities per Summary §6.12.2 / Appendix C.76 cataloged in §21.4.2 (including `seller_page_enrichment`, `kb_bootstrap`, and `ghost_rfp_ingestion`, which are defined in both KB Engineering Spec §13.2 and Summary §6.12.2 but housed in §21.4.2 per the classification notes in §21.4.1.A to avoid duplicate catalog rows). Total seed: 21 + 5 + 11 = 37 customer-facing registry rows, plus the Platform-Owned seed roster in §21.4.3 and the `org_intelligence_*` tri-split siblings in §21.4.1. See §21.4.1, §21.4.1.A, §21.4.2, and §21.4.3.

**Extended Capabilities.** The 11 v7 registry additions per Summary §6.12.2 / Appendix C.76: `seller_page_enrichment`, `kb_bootstrap`, `first_pass_responses`, `team_suggestion`, `next_evaluation_suggestion`, `external_vendor_lookup`, `guide_draft_generation`, `guide_refresh_analysis`, `category_faq_generation`, `market_intelligence_report`, `ghost_rfp_ingestion`. See §21.4.2.

**Platform-Owned Capability.** A `CapabilityRegistryEntry` with `billing_mode ∈ {sourcera_owned, platform_marketing}`. Never debits a customer's `AIWallet`; recorded as Sourcera COGS against the appropriate cost center (`Operations` or `Platform Marketing`). Powers the M9–M13 Marketplace content surfaces and Ops/Trust-and-Safety internal capabilities. See §21.4.3 and §34.3.5.

**Confidence Threshold (Per-Capability).** The Org-tunable floor (default per capability per §21.3) below which an Agent capability's output is suppressed from rendering. Threshold suppression is a UX filter, not a billing event — a suppressed result still settles as an AIOperation per its OutcomeContract. See §21.3 and §21.4.2.

**Output Contract (Agent).** The JSON schema returned by the Agent invocation handler for a given capability, comprising `agent_output_envelope` (`[AI-Generated]` label, `confidence_score`, per-field provenance hash) plus the per-capability payload. Versioned alongside the OutcomeContract; version skew between handler and OutcomeContract returns HTTP 422 `agent_output_contract_version_mismatch`. See §21.4.2 and KB Engineering Spec §13.4.

**Free Allowance Override.** A capability-specific override of the Summary C.80 default (10 ops per Org, lifetime). At v7.0.0 seed, two capabilities carry overrides: `kb_bootstrap` (1 lifetime free per Summary §6.13.2) and `ghost_rfp_ingestion` (1 lifetime free per Summary C.73). See §21.4.4.

### Terms Introduced in §22 (v7.0.0 KB Rewrite)

**Sourcera KB MCP Server.** The internally hosted, HTTPS-streamable MCP server that exposes the Seller KB to Anthropic Managed Agents at `https://mcp.sourcera.com/kb/v1`. The single authoritative entry point for every agent-driven KB interaction. See §22.8.

**KB Namespace.** The org-scoped retrieval scope on every KB Entry. Two kinds: `software` (1:1 with `SellerSoftware` per §4.4.9) and `org` (1:1 with Seller Org). Supplied as `namespace_preference[]` on every `kb_retrieve` call; clamped server-side against the JWT's `allowed_namespace_ids[]`. See §22.3.4.

**Vault JWT (KB).** The one-time-use JWT signed by Sourcera's identity service, held in an Anthropic vault, and validated by the KB MCP server on every tool call. Encodes `seller_org_id`, `bid_workspace_id`, `allowed_namespace_ids[]`, `capability_scope[]`, `data_residency_region`, `parent_capability_id`, `parent_aioperation_id`, `iat`, `exp` (1h), and `jti` (one-time-use enforcement key). See §22.8.3.

**MCPSessionTokenRecord.** The append-only, security-audit record persisted by the Sourcera KB MCP Server for every JWT issued. Enforces one-time-use semantics on `jti`, persists per-session `parent_aioperation_id` linkage for sub-operation accounting, and supports fast revocation. See §22.8.3.1. Authored extension — flagged.

**`kb_retrieve`.** The primary hybrid retrieval entry point on the KB MCP Server. Inputs: rewritten query, `namespace_preference[]`, optional filters, `top_k`, `max_excerpt_chars`. Outputs: ranked hits with `kb_entry_id`, excerpt, offsets, confidence, freshness, win_rate, evidence refs. Used by First-Pass, Q&A, KB-to-Response, KB Bootstrap, Ghost-RFP, KB-to-Capability, KB Staleness Classifier. See §22.8.4.1.

**`kb_get_entry`.** Tool that fetches the full body of a KB entry by ID. Called sparingly when a `kb_retrieve` excerpt is insufficient. See §22.8.4.2.

**`document_library_find`.** Tool that resolves Document Library evidence (compliance certs, DPAs, pen-test reports). Returns `attach_ref` tokens with 30-minute TTL; never returns `file_url`. See §22.8.4.3.

**`doc_attach`.** Side-effectful tool that attaches a Document Library entry to a bid response slot. Validated against the JWT's `bid_workspace_id` and `seller_org_id`. See §22.8.4.4.

**`capability_find`.** Tool that searches the seller's existing Capability Declarations for relevance to a requirement. See §22.8.4.5.

**`capability_declare_draft`.** Side-effectful tool that creates a draft Capability Declaration in `pending_review` state from KB evidence. Drafts NEVER auto-publish. See §22.8.4.6.

**`cite_verify`.** Tool that validates a citation is still live and that the claimed excerpt appears at the claimed offsets. Called by the agent before emitting a final response; also enforced server-side at the orchestrator submission gate. See §22.8.4.7.

**Citation Submission Gate.** Orchestrator-level enforcement at submission time that every sentence in a final emitted response carries a `[[cite:kb_entry_id=...,offsets=[s,e]]]` marker, every cited entry is re-verified via `cite_verify`, and every citation is in the session's `allowed_namespace_ids[]`. Failures reject the AIOperation with `agent_output_uncited_sentence`, `agent_output_invalid_citation`, or `firewall_violation`. See §22.8.5.

**Confidence Decay (KB).** The daily-recomputed `confidence_modifier` on every KB Entry, derived from `base_confidence`, `days_since_review`, `review_cadence_days`, `usage_boost`, and `win_rate_modifier`. Drives both retrieval re-ranking and Health Dashboard signaling. See §22.5.1.

**Embedding Version Bump.** The procedure for upgrading the embedding model (e.g., voyage-3-large → voyage-4) without agent downtime: parallel column, 72h backfill, 99%-coverage gate, eval parity within 1 percentage point, 5-minute feature-flag rollback. See §22.4.5.

**Namespace Migration (KB).** The procedure for migrating a Software namespace to the Org namespace when a `SellerSoftware` is deleted, applying a 0.7× rank penalty until a Team Lead re-approves. See §22.4.4.

**KB Content Moderation Pipeline.** The seller-KB write-time safety pipeline that runs before KBEntry vectorization, BM25 indexing, retrieval, citation, Firecrawl auto-publish, and Managed-Agent composition. It adapts the §48.4.4 validator family to private Seller KB content and records `content_moderation_state` plus failure reasons on KBEntry. Entries not in `passed` moderation state are non-retrievable regardless of lifecycle / staleness overrides. Authored Extension AE-V72REM-PH45-KB-CONTENT-MODERATION-01. See §22.4.1.A, §45.2, and Appendix J.

### Terms Introduced in §48 (PLG, Growth Mechanics & Network Effects)

**PLG Funnel.** The five-stage paid path (signup → aha moment → ceiling hit → expansion → enterprise trigger) defined per console in §48.1. Materialized as Org-level monotonic-forward `plg_funnel_stage_max_reached` and `plg_funnel_stage_current` properties. See §48.1.

**Growth Loop.** A repeating, instrumented mechanism that compounds supply, demand, content, or attention on Sourcera. Ten loops (L1–L10) catalogued in §48.2; two retired (L3, L6) with reserved identifiers; eight active. Every fire materializes a §48.2.12 GrowthLoopExecution row.

**GrowthLoopExecution.** Org-scoped, append-only audit row per loop fire that captures actor, target, lifecycle state, attribution window, telemetry, anti-spam flags, kill-switch reference, and realized outcome value. Drives §48.3 Network Effects dashboards. See §48.2.12.

**GrowthLoopKillSwitch.** Platform-scoped, Ops-managed kill-switch that disables a growth loop globally, per-Org, per-capability, OR per-region. Activated via §48.2.12.4 Ops Console publish path with 60-second propagation latency. Required for SIM-driven incident response.

**Loop Attribution Window.** The per-loop time bound during which a downstream event (signup, EOI, upgrade) is credited back to the originating loop fire. L1=60d; L2=30d; L4=90d; L7=30d; L10=30d. See §48.2.12.1.

**Signal Integrity Monitor (SIM).** Cross-cutting Ops surface (Summary C.100) that aggregates anti-spam control fires, anomaly detections, kill-switch eligibility flags, and false-positive feedback. Eleven signal classes catalogued in §48.4.10. Emits `sim_signal_emitted` PostHog event on every fire.

**k-Anonymity Floor.** The minimum-cohort-size invariant on every aggregated metric (k=5 signal, k=10 aggregate, k=20 market intelligence). Enforced at render; violations replace the metric with `Insufficient data` AND emit `growth_signal_k_anonymity_floor_violation`. See §48.4.7.

**Suppression List.** Ops-maintained global denylist of email addresses, domains, IPs, payment-method fingerprints, and SSO upstream identities flagged as fraud, spam, OR legal-takedown subjects. Universally honored across L1, L2, L4, L5, L7, L8, L9, L10, M1–M17, and §41 email flows. See §48.4.8.

**Shared-Use Domain Registry.** Ops-maintained registry of public-mail-service domains (gmail.com, outlook.com, etc.) that are blocked from L1 / M5 vendor invitations and warning-flagged on M16 referrals. Auto-detection daemon flags candidates for Ops review. See §48.4.3.

**Template Spam ML Classifier.** Sonnet-tier classifier that scores every seller-authored template at publish AND nightly across published templates, blocking `spam_probability ≥ 0.85` and surfacing `[0.65, 0.85)` for human review. Drives L9 demotion. See §48.4.5.

**Featured Placement.** L9 Template Library buyer-browse surface treatment for templates that cross the trending / featured / top-pick clone-count thresholds. Subject to cross-buyer-org diversity floor (k=5 distinct buyers). See §48.2.10.

**Qualitative Match-Score Label.** L10 publicly-rendered bucketed match-score label (`strong_match`, `moderate_match`, `weak_match`, `insufficient_signal`) derived via one-way bucketing from the underlying numeric Match Score. Numeric scores never exposed to free viewers; QA-tested by `match_score_label_no_numeric_leakage`. See §48.2.11.

**Org Growth Console.** Sub-surface of the §43 Admin Dashboard that hosts the three §48.3.3 Growth Loop Operations / Network Effects / Anti-Spam dashboards. RBAC-gated to `ops_growth_admin`, `ops_finance_admin`, `ops_security_admin`, founder leadership.

**Ops Growth Admin.** New Ops Console role (Appendix J) empowered to manage GrowthLoopKillSwitch rows, edit `plg_funnel_definition` rows, and read all Growth-Loop / Network-Effects dashboards. Distinct from `ops_finance_admin` and `ops_security_admin`.

### Terms Introduced in §48.5 (M1–M8 Growth Mechanics)

**StakeholderInvite (M1).** Workspace-scoped, buyer-only entity tracking the lifecycle of a single Phase-8+ read-only stakeholder magic-link invitation. Issued with `redemption_status=pending`; resolves to one of four `redemption_path_kind` values on click. 14-day expiry; per-Workspace ceiling 25; per-inviter throttle 10/24h. See §48.5.1.

**PublicSelectionReport (M2).** Marketplace-domain entity representing a watermarked, per-section-redactable, signed snapshot of a Phase-12-approved Selection Report. Rendered at `https://reports.sourcera.io/{share_slug}` with anonymous, password, OR email-allowlist visibility. Honors §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out via nightly resweep. Replaces retired L3 Loop. See §48.5.2.

**Redaction Profile (M2).** 12-key JSON schema (`m2_redaction_profile_v1`) controlling per-section visibility of a PublicSelectionReport. `internal_comments_visible` is hard-locked `false`. Republish updates the profile while preserving `share_slug`. See §48.5.2.

**Watermark Spec (M2).** Three-layer artifact applied to every PublicSelectionReport render: diagonal page-fill text ("Selected via Sourcera — {Buyer} — {Workspace} — {Date}"), Sourcera footer badge, page-corner provenance hash (first 8 chars of `selection_report_snapshot_payload_hash`). See §48.5.2.

**EvaluationCertificate (M3).** Cross-console, public, Ed25519-signed certificate of evaluation outcome auto-issued at Phase-13 closure. Carries serial number `SRC-{YYYY}-{12-base32}`, canonicalized JSON payload, JWKS-verifiable signature, embed widget HTML snippet, public verification page. Buyer + winning vendor each have read access; vendor MAY decline-only. Honors §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out at render. See §48.5.3.

**Sourcera Cert Issuing Key.** The Ed25519 key used to sign EvaluationCertificate `payload_canonical_json_hash`. Identified by `signing_key_id`; key-rotation log retains current + 5 prior keys via the JWKS-style endpoint at `https://verify.sourcera.io/.well-known/sourcera-cert-keys.json`. See §48.5.3.

**NextEvaluationKickoffSession (M4).** Workspace-originated, buyer-only entity tracking the M4 Phase-13-closure prompt → click → new-Workspace-creation flow with 30-day attribution window. Telemetry drives §48.3 dashboards. See §48.5.4.

**BuyerPullVendorInvite (M5).** Workspace-scoped, buyer-only entity tracking buyer-initiated invitations to vendors not yet on Sourcera. Linked to a §48.2.12 GrowthLoopExecution row (`loop_id=vendor_invite_creates_account`). Subject to 20/user/30d + 5/target-domain/30d throttles per Summary C.63. See §48.5.5.

**Anonymized Outreach Template (M5).** Default M5 email template that names the evaluation context (category + use case + close-by date) without naming the buyer Org. Buyer anonymity controlled via `m5_buyer_anonymity_kind` enum. See §48.5.5.

**DomainAutoJoinClaim (M6).** Org-scoped, buyer-only entity representing a verified corporate-domain claim that grants auto-join to new SSO signups whose email matches the domain. Subject to §48.4.3 shared-use-domain rejection, §48.4.10 SIM velocity-anomaly detection, 30-day customer-self-serve revocation per Summary C.64. See §48.5.6.

**DomainAutoJoinEvent (M6).** Org-scoped, append-only audit row written on every M6 auto-join transaction. Captures pending-approval, approved, rejected, OR reverted lifecycle. See §48.5.6.

**SuggestedTeamMemberCard (M7).** Org-scoped, per-user, ephemeral (30-day TTL) recommendation row materializing M7 cross-team discovery. Subject to k=5 anonymity floor per Summary C.65 + per-user opt-out (discovery AND being-suggested toggles). Cross-team invites flow through §5.4 Guest profile; M7 itself grants no Workspace access. See §48.5.7.

**OrgIntelligenceValueCurveCheckpoint (M8).** Org-scoped, append-only checkpoint row written per evaluation closure. Captures cumulative + delta time-saved value, vendor-pool-coverage %, requirement-template-reuse %, discrepancy-insight count, predictive-suggestion-accuracy %, and a `compounding_factor` ≥ 1.0 by construction. Drives the M8 Value Curve UI tile per Summary C.66. See §48.5.8.

**Compounding Factor (M8).** Per-checkpoint multiplier `total_value_saved_usd_cumulative / (sequence_number × baseline_value_per_evaluation_usd)`. A value > 1.0 indicates compounding; rising values indicate accelerating compounding. Monotonicity violations emit `m8_curve_monotonicity_violation` SIM signal. See §48.5.8.

**Buyer Anonymity (M2 / M3 / M5).** Three different anonymity-control schemas across mechanics: M2 anonymizes vendor-side names (`vendor_names_visible` toggle); M3 anonymizes buyer-side identity (`m3_buyer_anonymity_kind` enum, 5 values); M5 anonymizes buyer-side identity in outbound vendor invitations (`m5_buyer_anonymity_kind` enum, 3 values). Each schema is independent and purpose-fit. See §48.5.2 / §48.5.3 / §48.5.5.

**M-Mechanic Kill-Switch.** Reuse of the §48.2.12.4 GrowthLoopKillSwitch entity for M1–M8 mechanic-level disablement. Scope values (`platform`, `org`, `capability`, `region`) align with loop-level kill-switches. Per-mechanic kill-switch coverage table at §48.5.10. See §48.5.10.

### Terms Introduced in §27.9 (Seller Signals)

**Seller Signal.** An aggregated, k-anonymized surface exposing buyer-side procurement activity (active evaluations, capability matches, vertical composition) to the Seller who qualifies for the underlying cohort. Never reveals the identity of any individual buyer pre-EOI or pre-direct-invite-acceptance. Subject to the §27.9.5 aggregation pipeline including k=5 floor, distinctiveness secondary check, residency enforcement, and vendor-opt-out scrubbing. See §27.9.1, §4.4.18.

**Buyer Signal Opt-In.** The BuyerSignalOptInRecord entity capturing an explicit, default-deny, Org-scoped affirmation that a Buyer Org's activity MAY be aggregated into SellerSignal cohorts. Supports scope restriction (by category, vertical, residency policy, or redaction profile) and can be paused at workspace or org granularity. Revocation is terminal. See §27.9.2.

**Signal Cohort.** A Sourcera-authored, period-scoped aggregation bucket composed of ≥ k (default 5) opted-in Buyer Org contributions matching a Seller's capability / vertical / use-case / residency fingerprint. Each cohort corresponds to one SellerSignal row (§4.4.18) and is (re)evaluated nightly. See §27.9.5.

**Signal Period.** The ISO-week-aligned window over which a Signal Cohort's underlying activity is counted. A new Signal Period opens Monday 00:00 UTC; a cohort row carrying a prior period's `signal_period_iso_week` remains readable but is marked `stale=true` at next publication. See §27.9.5.

**Distinctiveness Check.** The §27.9.5 secondary aggregation-pipeline stage that vetoes a cohort whose vertical / capability / residency composition is sufficiently narrow that an adversary with outside knowledge could re-identify a Buyer Org even above the k-floor. Measured via a distinctiveness scalar ∈ [0, 1] computed from cohort-member attribute entropy; threshold `≥ 0.25` passes, `< 0.25` vetoes. Vetoed cohorts surface as `placeholder_distinctiveness_vetoed`. See §27.9.5.

**De-Anonymization Trigger.** One of three permissible events that allow a specific Buyer Org's identity to be revealed to the cohort's Seller: (a) the Buyer submits an EOI on the Seller's public profile; (b) the Buyer accepts a Direct Invite composed from the cohort; (c) Ops applies a regulatory-investigation disclosure with DPO approval. Any other pathway is a privacy violation and blocked at the API layer. Each trigger creates an append-only SellerSignalDeAnonymizationLink row. See §27.9.4, §27.9.7.

**Direct Invite From Cohort.** A Seller Scale+ feature (§27.9.8) that lets a Seller dispatch a MarketplaceProactiveOffer to one anonymized Buyer Org pulled from one Signal Cohort. The Seller never learns the target's identity pre-acceptance. Rate-limited to 10/24h / 100/30d per Seller Org, with per-Buyer-Org cooldown on decline (30d default, 90d for `procurement_policy_prohibits` or `duplicate_vendor_outreach`). Acceptance triggers §27.9.4 de-anonymization. See §27.9.8.

**Signal Delivery Preference.** The SellerSignalDeliveryPreference entity capturing a Seller Org's channel-eligibility, digest cadence, CRM-routing, and residency-filter configuration for receiving SellerSignal cohorts. One active row per Seller Org; plan-tier entitlement is evaluated at delivery time (not authoring time) so that plan changes take effect immediately without preference-row churn. See §27.9.3.

**Seller Signal Suppression Render Mode.** The enum (Appendix J) governing how a suppressed cohort row is rendered on the Seller Dashboard: `hidden` (default for the weekly digest), or one of four placeholder modes disclosing only the *reason* a cell is suppressed (k-floor, distinctiveness, residency, vendor-opt-out). Never leaks cohort content. See §27.9.5, §27.9.6.

### Terms Introduced in §31.9 (CRM Sync)

**CRM Sync Connection.** The CRMSyncConnection entity representing an authenticated, authorized, health-tracked integration between a Seller Org and one of four supported CRM providers (Salesforce, HubSpot, Dynamics 365, Pipedrive). One active connection per (Seller Org, provider) tuple. OAuth ciphertext stored AES-256-GCM per §6.8. Includes a computed `connection_health_score ∈ [0, 1]`. See §31.9.2.

**CRM Account Match Algorithm.** The 5-stage matching algorithm (§31.9.7) that resolves a Sourcera-side event's Buyer Org to a CRM provider's Account / Company / Organization record: (1) domain exact match; (2) name exact match; (3) name fuzzy high-confidence (≥ 0.90 similarity); (4) name fuzzy low-confidence (0.70–0.89) → Review Queue; (5) no match → either auto-create new account (opt-in) or hold in Review Queue (default). Handles multi-tenant CRMs (e.g., Salesforce Business Units) via the §31.9.7 caveat.

**Activity Payload.** The provider-specific payload written for each §31.9.8 activity kind (EOI submission, SellerSignal cohort acceptance, bid-workspace lifecycle events, Q&A messages, public reviews received, direct-invite offers, direct-invite acceptance/decline, ghost bids). Each payload references a canonical Sourcera entity via `source_entity_ref` for audit correlation. Payload ≤ 256 KB per §31.1 transport limit.

**Field Mapping.** The CRMFieldMapping entity mapping one Sourcera-side field to one CRM-provider-side field via a `direction` (default `sourcera_to_crm`) and a server-side `transform` (from the whitelist in Appendix J `crm_field_transform`). Custom JS transforms are not permitted. Platform defaults ship with every CRM connection; customer-custom mappings (`is_customer_custom=true`) are Seller Scale+. Bidirectional mappings are Enterprise-only and require a conflict-resolution strategy. See §31.9.4.

**Routing Rule.** The CRMRoutingRule entity governing per-activity routing decisions (target object kind, account-matching whitelist/blacklist, territory-mapping lookup). First-match-wins across an ordered list. Predicate grammar is restricted to a whitelisted operator set (`equals`, `not_equals`, `in`, `not_in`, `matches_regex_safe`, `is_null`, `is_not_null`) to prevent injection. See §31.9.5.

**Review Queue.** The per-Seller-Org surface where activity events with `account_match_method = name_fuzzy_low_confidence_needs_confirmation` or `no_match_hold_for_review` await human disposition. Saturation (≥ 1,000 rows) triggers backpressure: new low-confidence matches auto-route to `no_match_hold_for_review` and do not create new Review Queue rows until the queue drains. See §31.9.9.

**Connection Health Score.** A scalar ∈ [0, 1] computed from 5-minute windowed error rate, p95 latency, provider 5xx rate, and OAuth-scope-sufficiency flag. A sustained score < 0.40 for ≥ 15 minutes emits `seller.crm_sync.connection_health_critical`. Surfaced in the CRM Sync Dashboard. See §31.9.2, §31.9.16.

**Schema Drift.** A nightly schema-introspection job detects provider-side field renames, type changes, or deletions that affect one or more CRMFieldMapping rows. Affecting a `required=true` mapping transitions the connection to `paused_schema_mismatch`; informational drift emits a notification but does not pause. See §31.9.16.

**Managed Package (Salesforce) / Custom Object API (HubSpot) / Dynamics Solution.** Provider-specific installation artifacts that deploy the Sourcera custom object (`custom_object_sourcera_signal` / `custom_entity_sourcera_signal`) plus all platform-default field mappings. Available on Salesforce Enterprise plans; HubSpot Operations Hub Professional+; Dynamics 365 with Power Platform. See §31.9.11.

### Terms Introduced in §51 (Product Usage Analytics & PLG Instrumentation)

**Event Family.** One of exactly 11 canonical families (`ai_capability`, `workspace`, `billing`, `vendor`, `seller_kb`, `bid`, `marketplace`, `identity`, `ops_surface`, `analytics_meta`, `system_job`) under which every PostHog event is registered. Events are routed, cardinality-budgeted, retention-scoped, and dashboard-surfaced by family. Adding a family requires a §51.1.4 amendment and a two-approver quorum signoff per §51.1.6. See §51.1.4 and Appendix J `event_family`.

**Standardized Event Property Set.** The binding property envelope every first-party PostHog event MUST carry regardless of family, formalized in the Appendix G preamble and §51.2.1: `org_id`, `console`, `workspace_id`, `user_id`, `phase`, `entity_ref`, `capability_id`, `capability_domain`, `plan_tier_buyer`, `plan_tier_seller`, `residency_region`, `legal_entity`, `schema_version`, `sampling_rate`, `idempotency_key`, `emitted_at`. Envelope violations are rejected by `UsageEventValidator` with a paired Appendix I error code. See Appendix G → "Required Standard Property Set."

**Capability Domain.** One of 13 canonical tags (`discovery`, `drafting`, `analysis`, `review`, `ingestion`, `scoring`, `intelligence`, `reporting`, `compliance`, `authoring`, `retrieval`, `ops_surface`, `billing_surface`) bound to every CapabilityRegistryEntry. Used to pivot the Capability Mix panels on the Usage Dashboards (§51.3.2, §51.4.2, §51.5.2). Renaming a capability does not change its domain; changing a capability's domain requires a §51.2.3 amendment and emits a `usage_analytics_event_family_registered` event. See Appendix J `capability_domain_kind`.

**UsageDashboardSnapshot.** The rollup entity computed per (Org, dashboard_kind, window_start, window_end) tuple that feeds the customer-facing Org-Level, User-Level, and Seller-Parity dashboards. Snapshots are lifecycle-managed (`pending → computing → ready | failed`), conversion-factor-version-bound, residency-partitioned, and retained at two granularities: daily rollups for 90 days and monthly rollups for 24 months (§51.7.5, §40.2). Customer-facing reads resolve through `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/analytics/usage/snapshot` with `console`, `snapshot_window`, and `snapshot_kind` query parameters. See §51.3.1.

**Seller Usage Parity.** The §51.5 dashboard surface that mirrors the buyer Org-Level and User-Level dashboards for Seller Orgs, with seller-specific panels for `seller_bid_spend`, `seller_kb_utilization`, `seller_win_rate_correlation`, and `seller_capability_mix`. Parity ensures feature-equivalent analytics across the console firewall (§25) without cross-firewall data leakage — seller data never surfaces in buyer dashboards and vice-versa. See §51.5 and Appendix J `usage_dashboard_kind`.

**Conversion Factor Version Set Hash.** The SHA-256 hash of the canonical tuple of conversion-factor versions (one per `capability_domain`) used at Time-Saved snapshot compute time. The hash is recorded on every `UsageDashboardSnapshot` row AND on every contributing `TimeSavedCredit` row; a mismatch emits `usage_analytics_conversion_factor_binding_mismatch` and suppresses the affected rollup from rendering. The hash is surfaced to the user via the Time-Saved footnote (§51.6.4) for methodology disclosure. See §51.6.2 and §50.13 Baseline Assumption Manager.

**Time-Saved Baseline Model (customer-facing).** The customer-visible rendition of Time-Saved credits on the Usage Dashboards, comprising: (a) a `total_minutes_saved` scalar per dashboard window; (b) a per-capability-domain breakdown; (c) a trend-vs-prior-window comparison; (d) a required methodology footnote disclosing the `conversion_factor_version_set_hash` and the authoritative §50.13 Baseline Assumption version. Distinct from the Ops-facing §50.13 Baseline Assumption Manager (which governs conversion-factor authoring, versioning, and the two-approver gate at 15% drift). The customer-facing surface READS the Ops-facing library; customers cannot edit conversion factors. See §51.6.

**Console Firewall (§51 binding).** The §25-originating console-isolation invariant as it applies to Product Usage Analytics: (a) buyer events are emitted only to the buyer PostHog project and never to seller dashboards; (b) seller events are emitted only to the seller PostHog project and never to buyer dashboards; (c) cross-console read attempts via the §51 APIs are rejected with `usage_analytics_seller_buyer_firewall_violation`; (d) envelope violations crossing the firewall are tagged `cross_console_leak` in `usage_envelope_violation_kind`. The firewall is distinct from residency partitioning (§40.4), which is enforced independently. See §51.5 and §25.

### Terms Introduced in §3.6–§3.11 (UX Token & State Catalog, 2026-04-22)

**Side Peek.** A right-rail secondary-surface component (480px default; 360–640px user-resizable clamp) that renders an entity detail view without navigating away from the parent list or matrix surface. Triggered by Enter on a focused row, click on a row's "open" affordance, or deep-link with `peek_id` query parameter. Closed via Escape; dismissed-all via Shift+Escape (with per-peek confirmation on unsaved changes). Navigation within a peek via Cmd+[ (prev) and Cmd+] (next) per `side_peek_navigation_direction`. Auto-closes on console switch or list unmount. See §3.8.

**Cursor Presence.** The live-collaboration rendering contract for active sessions within a shared surface (workspace, matrix, detail page). Each active session is represented by a colored cursor with user initial, assigned a hue from the 8-value palette via `hash(user_id, session_id) mod 8` with secondary-entropy disambiguation on wrap. Cursors idle-fade per four thresholds: 3s → 60% opacity, 10s → 30% opacity, 30s → hidden from viewport, 60s → session evicted. Viewport indicators (max 3 + overflow chip) mark off-screen presences. Cross-console firewall enforced: buyer-console presences never render in seller-console; Ops presences render only to other Ops viewers. Mobile divergence: static presence avatars only (no live cursor). See §3.9 and §4.3.14.

**Bulk Action Toolbar.** The multi-row action surface that appears when one or more rows are selected in a list or matrix. Supports `visible_only` and `all_in_filter` selection modes per `bulk_action_selection_mode`; Shift+Click for range selection; Cmd+A for all-in-filter with 10,000-row soft cap. Persists across pagination and sort changes (row-ID preservation for visible_only; filter-expression preservation for all_in_filter). Action catalog spans 14 surfaces; destructive actions gated by type-to-confirm at ≥10 rows. See §3.10.

**Dark Mode Parity.** The contract that every buyer-console and seller-console surface renders equivalently at WCAG 2.1 AA compliance (≥4.5:1 contrast text, ≥3:1 UI components) under both `light` and `dark` values of `theme_mode`. Resolution order: `user_override` > `org_default` > `system_preference` (where `theme_mode=system`). Twenty token pairs are authoritatively mapped in §3.11.4; regressions are caught by the `ux_token_contrast_check` CI gate. Third-party embeds (Stripe, Firecrawl, Zendesk) are theme-aware via explicit attribute wiring. Ops Console defaults to dark regardless of org setting. See §3.11.

**Content-Shaped Skeleton.** A loading-state rendering pattern that reserves visual space matching the shape, approximate dimensions, and typographical rhythm of the content it will replace, rather than rendering a generic spinner or blank area. Reduces perceived latency and prevents CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) on resolve. Used across all six `page_surface_kind` values for the `loading` and `partial` states. See §3.7.3.

**Next-Best-Action.** The empty-state design pattern in which the primary CTA is labeled as a verb corresponding to the most likely user action given the surface context (`Create Workspace`, `Invite Teammates`, `Upload Document`, etc.). Every empty state maps to exactly one value of `empty_state_next_best_action_kind`. Plan-gated empty states (`none` action kind) route through the §5.11 Feature Access Matrix upgrade flow rather than rendering a generic "Try again" CTA. See §3.7.4.

**Failure / Reason / Recovery.** The three-part error-copy contract governing every user-facing error state: (1) Failure — what did not happen, stated in plain language from the user's perspective; (2) Reason — why it did not happen, at the correct level of technical detail for the surface audience; (3) Recovery — what the user can do now, drawn from `error_recovery_kind`. Errors MUST NOT render raw stack traces, database error codes, or technical identifiers without a human-readable Failure statement above them. See §3.7.5.

**Idle Fade.** The four-threshold opacity decay applied to live cursors as a user's session becomes inactive. Threshold ladder: 3 seconds idle → fade to 60% opacity; 10 seconds → 30% opacity; 30 seconds → hidden from viewport (name still visible in presence strip); 60 seconds → session evicted from Presence Record with `status=disconnected`. Honors `prefers-reduced-motion` by swapping to instant state change. See §3.9.4.

**Viewport Indicator.** The off-screen-presence cue rendered at the nearest viewport edge when a collaborator's cursor is outside the current scroll window. Max 3 distinct indicators + "+N more" overflow chip. Indicator color matches the remote cursor's hue; click or keyboard-Enter scrolls the viewport to center on the remote cursor. See §3.9.5.

**High Contrast Mode.** An Authored Extension (§3.11.8; pending human sign-off) reserving `theme_mode=high_contrast` as a forward-looking WCAG AAA / Section 508 compliance tier for public-sector Buyer orgs. Authored but not yet rendered; implementations MUST tolerate the reserved enum value as forward-compatible serialization but MUST NOT emit the rendering until the extension is signed off. See §3.11.8.

**Accessibility Settings.** The Settings -> Accessibility panel in §36.1 / §37.4 that lets a user configure live-cursor visibility, mention announcement priority, High Contrast preference, and assistive-tech shortcut remaps. Backed by §4.2.14 UserAccessibilityPreference. The surface is user-owned, Org-scoped, DSAR-exportable, and never exposes raw assistive-tech shortcut JSON to other customer users.

**UserAccessibilityPreference.** The Org-scoped user preference entity (§4.2.14) backing Accessibility Settings. Fields include `show_teammate_cursors`, `mention_announcement_priority`, `high_contrast_mode`, and `assistive_tech_keymap_overrides_json`. Retention follows the User lifecycle in §40.2; DSAR erasure hard-deletes raw assistive-tech keymap JSON.

**ARIA-Live.** The WAI-ARIA live-region mechanism used for status announcements, unread-marker changes, mention notifications, bulk-action progress, and async validation. §37.1 owns the cross-surface live-region posture; individual surfaces may set `assertive` only where the event interrupts active work, and user preference may demote mentions per §37.4.

**BCP-47.** The language-tag standard used by User.`locale`, locale-resolution in §37.2, and `<html lang>` rendering. Examples: `en-US`, `en-GB`, `fr-FR`, `ja-JP`, `ar-SA`.

**CSS Logical Properties.** The CSS layout property family (`inline-start`, `inline-end`, `block-start`, `block-end`, etc.) used to make LTR and RTL layouts share one source. Physical `left` / `right` CSS is allowed only through the §37.3 audited allow-list.

**WCAG 2.1 AA.** The accessibility conformance baseline for Sourcera customer and Ops surfaces. §37.1 enumerates the binding Success Criterion set; §37.5 and §37.6 define automated, manual, and external-audit verification.

**axe-core.** The automated accessibility rule engine used by CI gate `accessibility_audit_v7_1_aa_full`. §37.5 pins the rule-set version and severity handling; axe findings do not replace screen-reader, keyboard, reflow, RTL, or external-audit testing.

**Token Drift Check.** The CI gate `ux_token_contrast_check` that runs on every PR touching `design-tokens/*.json`, computing token-pair contrast across all 20 mapped pairs in §3.11.4 and failing the build if any pair regresses below WCAG 2.1 AA thresholds (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for UI components). Tied to §50.17.4 `token_audit_inputs` Ops Console drift check for runtime monitoring. See §3.11.10.

**10,000-Row Bulk Action Cap.** The soft upper bound on rows selectable via `bulk_action_selection_mode=all_in_filter`. Breaches emit `ui_bulk_action_cap_breach_warned` and route the user to the "export filter → process offline" fallback (API-backed batch processing). Destructive operations above 10,000 rows are gated to API-only (no UI path). See §3.10.4.

**8-Hue Palette Wrap.** The behavior of the cursor-presence hue assignment algorithm when a single shared surface has >8 concurrent active sessions. Base assignment is `hash(user_id, session_id) mod 8`; on collision, a secondary entropy bit produces a subtle ~8% luminance delta on the duplicated hue to preserve semantic distinguishability. Telemetry: `ui_cursor_presence_hue_wrap_collision_detected` emitted per collision. See §3.9.2.

### Terms Confirmed in Phase 12.2 Glossary Sweep (v7.0.0 Integration)

This subsection consolidates glossary entries for cross-section terms introduced or redefined across Phases 1–11 that previously had body-section definitions but no Appendix K registration. Every entry below is verified against its authoring section; where the term is also covered by a more specific entry above (e.g., `Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat Grant` for `Pro Trial Seat Grant`), the entry below acts as the canonical short-form alias and points at the long-form entry.

**Vendor Opt-Out Registry.** The platform-wide collection of all `VendorOptOutRecord` rows (§4.4.8) plus the §4.5.6 Marketplace-Domain Read/Render Contract that enforces them. The Registry is the authoritative source-of-truth for whether any seller-identifying row may be rendered on a public, Sourcera-owned Marketplace surface (CategoryPage, ComparisonPage, GuidePage, MarketIntelligenceReport, HeatMapCell, SellerOrgPage, SoftwarePage, PublicSelectionReport). Append-only; auto-honored on write; Ops post-hoc review governs `auto_honored → approved | rejected | revoked` transitions. Reads are platform-internal only — no buyer-console API surface (cross-console reads return HTTP 404 `vendor_opt_out_cross_console_access`). Cross-referenced by Summary C.123. See §4.4.8 (entity), §4.5.6 (render contract), §27.10 (authority attestation), and the related Appendix K entries `Vendor Opt-Out Record`, `Opt-Out Registry Source-of-Truth Rule`, and `Retroactive Sweep (Vendor Opt-Out)`.

**Pro Trial Seat Grant.** Canonical short-form for the §4.3.17 entity recorded in full as `Buyer-Funded Pro Trial Seat Grant` above. The 30-day Seller Starter trial gifted from a Scale or Enterprise buyer to an invited vendor; pool-accounted against the buyer's billing month per §34.13. M17 mechanic. Use the long-form term when distinguishing from any future seller-funded or platform-funded grant variants. See §4.3.17 and §34.13.

**Ops Session.** A single time-bounded authenticated session of an Ops Console user, scoped to a single `console = 'ops'` JWT and recorded in the §50.18 Ops Session Viewer for audit. Carries the Ops user's role assignments at session start (frozen for the lifetime of the session for audit-stability), MFA satisfaction state, IP-allowlist match result, and the cross-Org access trail emitted by every Ops mutation. Distinct from a Buyer or Seller session: the Ops Session NEVER carries an `org_id` claim and may read/write across Orgs subject to Ops-role gating. See §50.1 (Ops Console base), §50.3 (Ops Role Matrix), §50.18 (Ops Session Viewer), §6 (Auth + MFA invariants), §7.2 (firewall semantics for Ops cross-console access).

**Ops Role Matrix.** The §50.3 closed registry of every Ops Console role and the platform-scoped capability set each role grants. Closed in two senses: every Ops capability referenced anywhere in the spec MUST be registered in the matrix (CI gate `ops_capability_matrix_coverage_complete` asserts), and every role assignment MUST resolve to a matrix row at session-start. Roles include `ops_finance_admin`, `ops_capability_admin`, `ops_compliance_admin`, `ops_content_admin`, `ops_growth_admin`, `ops_marketing_editor`, `ops_security_admin`, `ops_verification_senior_reviewer`, and others enumerated in Appendix J `ops_console_role`. The matrix is authoritative; inline `ops_*` role references throughout the spec MUST resolve here. See §50.3.

**Match Score.** The Marketplace-domain ranking score produced by the §27.4 learned ranking model that estimates the fit between a candidate Seller Org / SellerSoftware pair and a buyer's authored Workspace and Listing. Materialized under three trigger classes — Listing-Publish, EOI-Review, On-Demand — and persisted as `MarketplaceMatchScoreSnapshot` rows with full feature-vector provenance (§27.4.9). Numeric exposure is plan-gated per §5.11 / BPS §3 / SPS §9; bucketed labels (`strong_match`, `moderate_match`, `weak_match`, `insufficient_signal`) are exposed at lower tiers via the §48.2.11 Qualitative Match-Score Label loop. Distinct from the Sourcera Method's `grade × weight` math (§10) which scores vendor *responses*, not vendor *candidacy*. See §27.4 (model), §27.4.8 (legacy v6 keyword baseline preserved as cold-start), §48.2.11 (label rendering), §21.4.2 `match_score_numeric` (capability), Summary C.61 (authoritative model summary).

**Managed Agent.** A Claude Managed Agents `agent` definition (per Anthropic's `managed-agents-2026-04-01` beta) deployed by Sourcera to back any §21.4 capability whose `requires_managed_agent=true` flag is set. Sourcera Managed Agents are versioned, JSON-defined, checked into `packages/sourcera-agent-definitions/`, deployed via CI through `client.beta.agents.create` / `client.beta.agents.update`, and pinned by the §22.10 Capability-ID / KB-Spec / Signal-Contract Alias Table. Each agent definition binds (a) a system prompt ≤ 8K chars, (b) a model selection (Sonnet, Haiku, or Opus) per the §21.4 registry's `model_tier_default`, (c) a tool allowlist comprising `agent_toolset_20260401` filters, MCP tool scopes, and Sourcera custom tools, (d) a Skill set (§22.12), (e) an Environment (§22.13). Managed Agent invocations may produce parent + child AIOperation rows linked via `parent_operation_id` (§4.8.1) up to depth 6. See §22.10 (definitions), §22.10.1.A (canonical-ID alias table), §22.10.7 (update workflow), KB Engineering Spec §6, Summary C.55.

**MCP Server.** A Model Context Protocol server registered with a Sourcera Managed Agent that exposes a tool surface to the agent at runtime. Sourcera operates a single first-party MCP server — the **Sourcera KB MCP Server** (`https://mcp.sourcera.com/kb/v1`, §22.8) — that proxies all Seller KB retrieval, citation verification, document attachment, and capability-declaration drafting. MCP Servers are referenced by `mcp_server_name` in Managed Agent definitions, gated by Vault JWTs (§22.8.3) issued per session, and authorized via per-session `allowed_namespace_ids[]` and `capability_scope[]` claims. Third-party MCP servers (Firecrawl, Anthropic-hosted skills) are subject to the §22.13 Environment `allowed_hosts` allowlist. Per Anthropic Managed Agents docs, MCP-tool-call rate limits are enforced per (server, Anthropic Org). See §22.8 (Sourcera KB MCP Server), §22.13.1 (Environment-side networking config), §22.10 (per-agent MCP scoping).

**Skill.** A Sourcera-authored Anthropic Skill registered under the Anthropic Skills API and referenced by name in one or more Managed Agent definitions. Skills encode Sourcera's domain expertise (RFP-drafting tone, compliance citation patterns, confidence thresholds, extraction rules) as markdown bodies ≤ 500 lines that load only when relevant to the agent's task — the progressive-disclosure pattern referenced in §22.2.2. Per Anthropic's Skills constraint, a session may carry ≤ 20 skills; Sourcera uses 3–5 per agent definition. Skills are version-controlled in `packages/sourcera-skills/`, uploaded via CI to the Skills API, and pinned by `skill_*` IDs in `POINTERS.json`. Skill updates are subject to the §22.16.5 canary rollout. See §22.12 (authoring), §22.12.9 (distribution), KB Engineering Spec §8 (source).

**Environment.** A Claude Managed Agents `environment` definition (per Anthropic's `managed-agents-2026-04-01` beta) specifying the cloud container configuration where a Sourcera Managed Agent runs: pip/apt package set, networking type (`limited` for production), `allowed_hosts[]` allowlist, `allow_mcp_servers` flag, and `allow_package_managers` flag (always `false` in production to mitigate supply-chain risk). Sourcera defines two Environments — `env_sourcera_kb_runner` (minimal, retrieval-driven) and `env_sourcera_bootstrap` (extended, ingestion-heavy) — each version-tracked in code (Anthropic does not version Environments) and recreated rather than mutated on changes. Old Environments archive after their last referencing session ends, then delete after 30 days. See §22.13 (definitions), §22.13.3 (lifecycle), KB Engineering Spec §9 (source).

**Beta Header.** The `anthropic-beta: managed-agents-2026-04-01` HTTP header pinned on every request Sourcera sends to the Anthropic Managed Agents API. Paired with `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`. Pinned centrally in `packages/sourcera-agents-client`; rotation requires the §22.2.3 canary rollout (5% canary, ≥ 7 days, ≤ 2-pp metric drift across retrieval recall, citation validity, and AIOperation acceptance, ≥ 30-day prior-version support window). A version mismatch between the client's expected header and Anthropic's advertised support returns HTTP 503 `anthropic_beta_version_unsupported` (Appendix I) and emits `agent_beta_version_mismatch` (Appendix G). See §22.2.3.

**KB Value Meter.** A name shared by two **deliberately distinct** objects whose disambiguation is enforced by §22.18 and Reconciliation Log entry "KB Value Meter name collision." (a) The **§34.19.2 buyer-facing scalar** — a `0.00–1.00` continuous reputation signal computed nightly per Seller Org as `0.40 × win_rate + 0.25 × recency + 0.20 × citation_depth + 0.15 × outcome_cite_coverage`, surfaced to buyers on Verified+ sellers and factored into Promoted Listing ranking quality floors (§34.16.1). (b) The **§22.18.4 KB Value Meter — Seller Panel** — a seller-facing plain-English panel on the KB landing screen rendering accrued KB value (entry count, citations in closed bids, win-rate-weight units, response-time saved, $/yr saved). The scalar is **one of several inputs** the Seller Panel renders; the Panel is NOT a rename of the scalar. Both are preserved across plan transitions per §34.19.1 / §22.18.5 (Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee). Use the qualifiers "(scalar)" or "(Seller Panel)" wherever ambiguity is possible. See §34.19.2, §22.18.4, RECONCILIATION.md → Known Conflicts → "KB Value Meter name collision."

**Hero Moment.** The §48.1.5 Seller-Console four-phase onboarding-to-stake-reveal arc that converts a buyer-issued vendor invitation into a fully-rendered Bid Workspace with KB drafts, cited first-pass responses, and a stake-reveal screen — all before the seller is asked to upgrade, enter a credit card, or assign seats. Phases: (1) Pre-Arrival Preparation; (2) Onboarding Surface (minutes 0–3); (3) In-Workspace Value Proof (minutes 3–45); (4) Post-Submission Reveal (hour 1+). The authoritative completion timestamp is `SellerOnboardingSession.hero_moment_completed_at` (§4.4.22), set iff all three Stage-3 surfaces (KB Draft, first-pass response, progress strip) render pre-touch AND `stage_3_population_latency_ms` satisfies §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold`. Stage-3 population is a P0 availability metric with on-call paging governed by §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 latency breach page SLA`. The seven Onboarding Anti-Patterns (Summary C.141; Appendix J `onboarding_anti_pattern_kind`) bind the Hero Moment to a non-negotiable no-paywall, no-credit-card, no-seat-assignment contract. Seller-Console-only; Buyer-Console reads on SellerOnboardingSession return HTTP 404 (§7.2). See §48.1.5 (framework), §48.8 (UX surface), §4.4.22 (entity), Summary §3.6 / C.132.

**Stake-Reveal Moment.** One of three deliberately scarce Seller-Console surfaces at which the seller is shown the compounding KB value they have accrued, per §22.18.6: (1) Free-tier KB landing Value Meter (Seller Panel render on the KB landing screen for `plan_tier='seller_free'`); (2) Post-close outcome debrief overlay (rendered once per seller user per closed bid in `Bid.status ∈ {won, lost, no_decision}`); (3) Conversion-threshold upgrade previews (CM1 / CM2 / CM3 / CM4 modals at §48.1.7 / §48.8.6). Every fire emits the canonical `stake_reveal_rendered` event with `reveal_moment ∈ {free_tier_kb_landing, outcome_debrief, conversion_threshold}` (Appendix J `kb_stake_reveal_moment_enum`; Appendix G). Moments 1 and 2 MUST NOT render an upgrade CTA (anti-pattern AP-2, §48.8.7). Moment 3 IS an upgrade surface; its stake-reveal role is preview-of-preservation. The pattern is deliberately scarce so it reads as informative, not promotional. See §22.18.6, §48.8.5, Summary §6.13.7.

**Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee.** The §34.19 plan-level guarantee that a Seller Org upgrading from any plan to a higher plan retains 100% of all 13 Protected Asset Classes — KB entries, KB Value Meter score and compounding inputs, Capability Declarations and suggestions, Verification Tier, Bid Workspace history, outcome-signal history and citation graph, SavedSearch / SearchAlert rows, Promoted Listing audit history, Pro Trial Seat grants received, buyer relationship history, wallet balance, committed-spend contract, and API keys + integrations. Asset preservation also applies to *downgrades*, with the §34.6 `DowngradeExcessDataBucket` 90-day read-only preservation window and the §22.18.5 KB-side honest-portability microcopy. The §34.19.1.A bridge maps each class to concrete rows / fields. The guarantee is enforced by the deploy-time validator `protected_asset_downgrade_firewall` (asserts no Protected Asset enters `preservation_status=hard_archived`). Honest-portability microcopy on every upgrade and downgrade confirmation is required (§34.19.4); reassuring-only marketing copy is prohibited. See §34.19 (plan-level surface), §22.18.5 (KB-side surface), Summary C.139.

**Honest Portability.** The §22.18 design contract that a seller may, at any time, on any plan tier (including Free), export the full Seller KB — entry bodies, entry metadata, provenance, attachments, and schema — in a format Sourcera documents publicly and commits to maintaining. The export is one-click, rate-limited only for abuse, never paywalled, and produces an artifact the seller can load into any other system and continue operating from. No "export penalty" state may ever be introduced; no feature, plan-gate, or retention rule may change as a consequence of exporting (Invariant P3, `kb_export_mutation_firewall`). Implementation: the §32.9 export endpoint, the §22.18.2.1 `KBExportJob` entity, the §22.18.2.2 `KBExportArchive` artifact, the §22.18.2.3 `KBExportProvenanceLog`, and the `kb.export.ready` webhook (Appendix C). Pair with `On-Platform Compounding`. See §22.18.1 (principle), §22.18.2 (full spec), §22.18.7 AC #50 (no-paywall invariant).

**On-Platform Compounding.** The §22.18 design contract that the Seller KB becomes materially more valuable inside Sourcera than anywhere else because Sourcera-side features — KBEntry confidence scores from acceptance rates (§22.4.1), staleness signals from the §22.5 KB Health Model, win-rate weighting from closed-bid outcomes, the cross-bid `KBCitationGraph` materialization, and KB-to-Capability auto-declarations — are computed and maintained against the live corpus of Sourcera bids. These features travel out of Sourcera as **text snapshots** in the export archive but do **not** continue to update outside the platform. The compounding stays behind. Stake is built because staying on Sourcera keeps the compounding live; leaving does not destroy the seller's work but does freeze it. Enforced by Invariant P2 (`compounding_feature_source_firewall` deploy-time validator). Pair with `Honest Portability`. See §22.18.1, §22.18.3 (the five compounding features), §22.18.7 AC #51, Summary §6.13.7.

**Marketplace Discovery Pricing.** The §34.16 non-AI revenue layer that monetizes paid placement and earned verification on the Marketplace, accounting-isolated under the `rev_marketplace_discovery` cost center per §4.8.12. Three SKUs: (a) **PromotedListing** — keyword-targeted, category-scoped second-price-auction-cleared paid placement whose monetary ceilings, purchased-top-up cap, category-slot cap, reserve floor, and KB-health floor default are authoritative in §34.16.1.A (§4.4.19 consumes those cells); (b) **VerificationReviewRecord** — earned-not-purchased Verified and Certified tier badges with §27.10 authority-attestation review cadence, separation-of-duties enforcement, and Certified re-review per §44.1 `Verification certified re-review cadence` (§34.16.2, §4.4.21); (c) **FeaturedPlacement** — Ops-curated editorial placements at launch with a feature-flagged `paid_commitment` mode reserved for future activation (§34.16.3, §4.4.20). Target gross margin ≈ 95%+. Finance dashboards MUST partition by `rev_marketplace_discovery` and MUST NOT UNION with `rev_ai_wallet` or `rev_subscription` per §4.8.12 / §34.16. FTC Native-Advertising Disclosure (16 CFR Part 255) labels are mandatory: PromotedListing renders "Promoted"; FeaturedPlacement renders "Featured" plus an Ops-authored editorial-rationale tooltip. See §34.16, §4.4.19–§4.4.22, §4.8.12, Seller Pricing Strategy §12.

**Time-Saved Baseline Model.** The §50.13 Ops-managed conversion-factor library that translates qualifying Usage Events (§4.3.18) into labor-hours-saved estimates, version-stamped per `capability_domain` and bound at compute time via the `Conversion Factor Version Set Hash` (§51.6.2). Customer-facing rendition (§51.6) reads the library and renders `total_minutes_saved`, per-capability-domain breakdowns, trend-vs-prior-window comparisons, and a methodology footnote disclosing the version-set-hash; customers cannot edit conversion factors. Ops-facing surface (§50.13 Baseline Assumption Manager) governs authoring, versioning, and the two-approver gate on factor drift > 15%. Distinct from individual `TimeSavedCredit` rows (§4.3.19), which are the per-Usage-Event credit records the model produces. See §50.13 (Ops surface), §51.6 (customer surface), §4.3.19 (per-event credit), Summary C.91.

### Terms Introduced in §13.11 (Phase 14.5 — Defense View)

**Defense View.** The buyer-side, single-screen leadership-meeting surface generated server-side from the finalized Selection Record (§4.3.24, §10.13.5) on the operator's first open per Workspace. Renders four sections — Recommendation (1 sentence), Why (3 highest-weighted reasons with linked evidence), Risks (1–2 material risks with mitigation), Evidence (links back to the Selection Record) — plus a one-page printable PDF for the CFO. Generated by the customer-billed Sonnet AIOperation `defense_view_generate` (§13.11.5) and cached against `selection_record_hash`; regenerated only when the Selection Record hash changes through a superseding pre-closure report/record path or the operator explicitly requests regeneration. Buyer-console-only; seller console returns HTTP 404 per §7.2 firewall. Plan-gated: Buyer Free renders a watermarked preview (Recommendation + first reason only); Buyer Solo+ renders the full surface unwatermarked; Buyer Enterprise additionally embeds the §32.7 Selection Record audit-receipt verbiage in the PDF footer. Mobile is read-only (regeneration not exposed). See §13.11.

**`defense_view_generate` (capability).** Customer-billed Sonnet AIOperation capability registered in the Agent Capability Registry (§4.8.2 / §21.4.2) and metered per the §34.3 outcome-based pricing model. Bound to an OutcomeContract (§4.8.4) whose accepted, rejected, timeout, grace, confidence, and contest constants are canonical in §13.11.5.A. Performance budgets are canonical in §44.1. See §13.11.5.

**Selection Record Hash Binding.** The cache invariant on `DefenseView`: the `selection_record_hash` field stamps the SHA-256 of the source `SelectionRecord.selection_record_sha256` (§4.3.24) at generation time; subsequent reads compare against the current Selection Record hash, and a mismatch forces regeneration with the "regenerated due to source change" surface chip. Guarantees the Defense View can never present stale content if a superseding Selection Report / Selection Record is produced before Phase 13 closure. See §13.11.2, §13.11.5.

**Watermarked Preview (Defense View).** The Buyer-Free-tier render path of the Defense View: Recommendation + the first **Why** reason render in full; **Risks**, the remaining **Why** reasons, and the **Evidence** list are gated behind a §34.8.5 "Solo unlocks the full view" upgrade CTA. PDF export on Free returns the upgrade modal in lieu of generating a PDF. Free Allowance counter consumption is bound to the watermarked render path, not the full-surface render path. See §13.11.4.

### Terms Introduced in Phase 2V Glossary Backfill (2026-05-03)

The following entries close the Phase-2.2 Appendix K coverage backlog (defects D-AK-004 through D-AK-027). Each entry satisfies the multi-section threshold (CLAUDE.md §12) and the §4 entity / surface / mechanic glossary parity rule (Authoring Convention #4).

**Buyer Maya.** The buyer-console conversational evaluation-intake agent (§13.12) that translates a buyer's free-text procurement goal into a scaffolded EvalStarter Workspace via a per-vertical seed schema (§4.5.9). Bound to the `buyer_maya_intake` capability registered in §21.4 and gated through the §13.12.4 materializer (Free p95 ≤ 2.5s; Solo / Starter+ p95 ≤ 4.5s per §44.1, AE-14.7-08). Plan-tier behavior: the intake surface is unconditionally available on every Buyer plan tier; per-tier divergence applies only at materialization (use-case / requirement truncation against §34.1.1 caps per §13.12.4 step 3). Engine-side AIOperations are full-fidelity on every tier; surface compression is engine-vs-surface separated per §3.13 Principle 9. See §13.12, §3.14, §4.5.9, F-264, F-898.

**Seller Maya.** The seller-console surface-abstraction agent (§22.20) that binds the Solo / Free seller surface to a first-30-seconds-comprehension contract via engine-vs-surface compression. Renders KB-to-Capability suggestions as auto-published chip lists (§22.20.2 — `pending_review_reason = 'solo_free_auto_publish'`), magic-link Hero Moment polish (§22.20.6), three-label Match Score compression (§22.20.4), and Solo-tier surface treatment (§44.6). Plan-tier scope is `plan_tier ∈ {seller_free, seller_solo}` per §34.1.3 inclusive-of-Solo rule. Engine-side AIOperations and outcome-resolution are unchanged on the Maya surface; the surface compression is enforced by §M.5 CI gate `seller_maya_surface_abstraction_engine_unchanged` (F-818). See §22.20, §3.13, §3.14, §44.6.

**Single-Operator Mode (Solo Mode).** The default UX posture for evaluation owners on the Solo plan tier (`buyer_solo` / `seller_solo`) running a structured evaluation or bid alone. Surfaces are compressed per §3.13 Principle 9 (Engine vs Surface) and §3.14 Pipeline Surface Compression; engine-side AIOperations and outcome-resolution remain at full fidelity per §44.6 Solo-Tier Surface Treatment. Plan-gated per §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 cell **Evaluation Owner Mode** and the `EvaluationOwnerMode` enum (Appendix J, registered as `solo` / `team`). The surface-compression contract is enforced by Solo-tier feature-access matrix rules (§5.11) and the §M.5 surface/engine CI gates. See §2.8, §3.13, §3.14, §44.6, §34.1.1, §34.1.2, F-023, F-841, F-853.

**Solo-Tier Surface Treatment.** The §44.6 contract that, on the Solo plan tier (`buyer_solo` / `seller_solo`), hides AI-consumption surfaces (AIWallet balance, per-capability rate card, per-AIOp ledger entries, contest-window banners, free-allowance counters) from the customer surface while the engine continues full metering, outcome resolution, AIOperation row writes, and FX-locking. The surface compression is the UX consequence of Single-Operator Mode (§2.8) and is enforced by feature-access matrix rules (§5.11), the wallet-pooling override (§34.10.3), and the §M.5 surface/engine CI gates (`solo_envelope_value_single_source`, `solo_tier_numeric_single_source`). See §44.6, §22.20.5, §3.13, §34.1.1, §34.1.2, §34.10.3, F-616.

**Capability Declaration.** A reusable, structured assertion of a Seller's capability to deliver a specific buyer requirement category, with evidence files, maturity rating (`capability_maturity_level` enum), geographic scope (`capability_geographic_scope` enum), and version-tracked reuse counter. Org-scoped on the seller side; published to the Marketplace per §27.4 Match Score model and §48.2.11 Qualitative Match-Score Label loop. Authored manually via §26.3 or auto-suggested by KB content via §22.8.4.6 (`capability_declare_draft` MCP tool). Solo / Free chip-list auto-publish flow at §22.20.2 (AE-14.8-01); pending-review state machine via `capability_declaration_state` (Appendix J). Reuse tracking per F-206. See §4.4.4, §26.3, §22.20, §27.4, §9.3, §9.3.2, F-417, F-205, F-206.

**Console Bridge.** The cross-console firewall-bounded sync substrate that projects atomic source-side changes from a Buyer Workspace to its linked Seller Bid Workspace(s) (and vice-versa for narrowly-defined seller-originated events) under a defense-in-depth redaction-and-projection contract. Materialized by the §4.7.1 Console Bridge Event entity (one row per atomic source change) and the §4.7.1.1 row-level seller projection allow-list. Enforced by the Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2; see also Console Firewall below); observed via the §25.6 Console Bridge Observability stack with bounded-lag SLO p99 < 30s (§25.2.1, F-398). See §4.7.1, §25.1–§25.6, §7.2, F-122, F-396.

**Console Firewall.** The platform security primitive (§7.2) enforcing strict isolation between the buyer console and the seller console: no field, query path, webhook event, dashboard panel, or audit-event surface may carry data across the firewall except via the §4.7.1 Console Bridge Event entity's whitelisted, redaction-validator-enforced, defense-in-depth-projected payload schema. Cross-console read attempts return HTTP 404 (§7.2). The firewall is enforced at write-time (§4.7.1 redaction validator), at read-time (§4.7.1 seller-side serializer defense-in-depth projection), in observability (§25.6, §51), and in Ops Console cross-Org access (§50.4). Specializations: `Dual-Console Firewall (§7.2) — Bridge Enforcement` (above) and `Console Firewall (§51 binding)` (above). See §1.3, §7.2, §4.7.1, §25, §51, §50.4.

**Workspace.** The buyer-side root container entity (§4.3.1) representing one structured procurement evaluation. Org-scoped; one Workspace per evaluation; lifecycle managed via the Sourcera Method's 13-phase pipeline (§10) and the Workspace Status state machine (Appendix E, F-776). `console = buyer (fixed)`. Houses all per-evaluation entities (Use Cases, Requirements, Responses, Scores, Scenarios, Selection Reports, Internal Comments). Cross-references the Seller-side Bid Workspace (below) via Console Bridge (above). `evaluation_owner_mode ∈ {solo, team}` per §4.3.1 (Appendix J `EvaluationOwnerMode`). See §4.3.1, §10, §11, Appendix E, F-083, F-776.

**Bid Workspace.** The seller-side root container entity (§4.4.1) bound to a buyer Workspace (above) via Console Bridge (above). One Bid Workspace per (Seller Org, Buyer Workspace) pair; lifecycle managed via the Bid Workspace Status state machine (Appendix E, F-776). Houses all seller-side per-bid entities (Bid Response, Seller Profile reference, Bid Tasks, Bid Schedule). Read-only on Requirements (mirrors buyer-side); editable only via Response form per §23.1. Hero-Moment-bound at first paint per §48.8 (F-685). See §4.4.1, §23.1, §22, §25, §35.2, §48.8, F-105, F-387, F-776.

**Marketplace Domain.** The public, SEO-indexed, Sourcera-owned content surface scope distinct from the org-scoped buyer console (Workspaces, Use Cases, Requirements) and the org-scoped seller console (Bid Workspaces, Bid Responses, KB). Carries CategoryPage (M9), GuidePage (M10), ComparisonPage (M11), MarketIntelligenceReport (M12), HeatMapCell (M13), SellerOrgPage, SoftwarePage (§4.4.10–§4.4.16), PromotedListing renders, FeaturedPlacement renders, PublicSelectionReport (M2), and EvaluationCertificate (M3). Renders are governed by the §4.5.6 Marketplace-Domain Read/Render Contract (above) and the §4.4.8 Vendor Opt-Out Registry. Consumer entities declare `scope = marketplace_domain` on the §4.x entity field tables. See §4.4.10–§4.4.16, §4.5.6, §27, §27.10, §34.16.

**EOI (Expression of Interest).** A buyer-initiated, structured opt-in signal that a Buyer Org wishes to engage with a specific Seller Org or SellerSoftware on the Marketplace. Materialized by the §4.5.2 EOI Record entity. Acceptance by the seller is materialized by the §4.5.8 EOI Acceptance Record (one-click flow) and triggers Target Account creation, Console Bridge Event emission (`eoi_acceptance_propagated`), optional Bid Workspace materialization (immediately on `accept_and_skip_nda`, on NDA execution otherwise), and §27.9.4 buyer de-anonymization for the cohort the seller previously saw via SellerSignal. Drafted in §4.4.24 EOIDraftQueue when wallet/cost gates apply; rate-limited per §4.4.26 EOIRateLimitOverride and §48.4.12 (per-seller-24h, per-category-7d, per-buyer-30d caps). CRM-sync activity payload per §31.9.6. See §4.5.2, §4.5.8, §4.4.24, §4.4.26, §27.5, §27.9.4, §31.9.6.

**Verification Tier.** The three-tier seller-trust badge framework (`basic`, `verified`, `certified` per Appendix J `Seller Verification Tiers`) earned (never purchased — §34.16.2 platform-integrity invariant) via the §4.4.21 VerificationReviewRecord workflow. Tier prerequisites per `Verification Tier Prerequisites` (above); review SLAs per `SLA Breach Auto-Rejection (VerificationReviewRecord)` (above); Certified tier subject to Quarterly Re-Review (above). Renders the trust badge on every public-facing seller surface (Marketplace Listing, SellerOrgPage, SoftwarePage, PromotedListing, FeaturedPlacement). Plan-tier-gated for upgrade eligibility per §34.16.2 (Verified eligibility begins at Seller Solo; Certified eligibility begins at Seller Growth). Distinct from FTC Native-Advertising Disclosure labels (above). See §4.4.21, §26.2, §27.11.3, §34.16.2, F-416.

**Capability Registry (also: Agent Capability Registry).** The Ops-Console-managed authoritative list of every capability that can produce an AIOperation, materialized as the §4.8.2 CapabilityRegistryEntry entity. Canonical short-form alias of `Agent Capability Registry` (above) — both forms permitted; "Capability Registry" is the bare-term form used in body-section narrative (§21.4 capability catalog, §22 cross-references). State machine: `alpha → beta → active → deprecated → retired`. See §4.8.2, §21.4.

**Console.** One of the three top-level UI surfaces of the Sourcera platform — the Buyer Console (org-scoped procurement-evaluation surface), the Seller Console (org-scoped vendor-response surface), or the Ops Console (platform-scoped Sourcera-internal-only surface). Strictly isolated by the §7.2 Console Firewall (above); cross-console data flow restricted to the §4.7.1 Console Bridge Event entity (above). The `console` field on every console-scoped entity is registered in Appendix J `console_enum` (`buyer | seller | ops`); the foundational conceptual term is canonical here. See §1.3, §7.2, §4 entity scope declarations.

**KB Value Capture.** The §22.18 design principle binding the Seller Knowledge Base to plan-upgrade economics via two paired contracts: `Honest Portability` (above — sellers may export the full KB at any time, on any plan tier, with no penalty) and `On-Platform Compounding` (above — KB-derived features compute and update only inside Sourcera; export is a snapshot, not a live feed). Materialized by the §22.18.2 KBExportJob entity, the §22.18.3 five compounding features, the §22.18.5 Honest-Portability microcopy, and the §34.19 Plan Upgrade Carry-Over Guarantee. The "value capture" framing is buyer-pricing-side narrative (Buyer Pricing companion §22 / F-850); the engineering contract is `Honest Portability` + `On-Platform Compounding`. See §22.18, §34.19, F-370, F-850.

**KB Hero Moment.** The Stage 3 sub-arc of the Seller Hero Moment (above) in which the KB Bootstrap output, the first-pass response output, and the bid-progress strip render pre-touch on the Bid Workspace landing. Bound to `SellerOnboardingSession.hero_moment_completed_at` iff `stage_3_population_latency_ms` satisfies §44.1 `Seller onboarding Stage-3 population-latency threshold`. The KB-specific framing distinguishes the Stage 3 sub-arc from the Stage 2 onboarding surface and the Stage 4 post-submission stake reveal. Distinct from `Stake-Reveal Moment` (above) which addresses post-submission and KB-landing-Value-Meter renders. See §22.18.6, §22.20.6, §35.2, §48.8.3, F-386, F-685.

**Forced-Vendor-Signup.** The platform-mechanic class that automatically materializes a SellerOnboardingSession (§4.4.22) on magic-link click from a Buyer-initiated invite, GhostBidImport, buyer referral, or Pro Trial Seat Grant — the Seller Org and User are created at Stage 2 SSO completion without prior seller intent. The lifecycle playbook is `Forced-Vendor-Signup Playbook` (above). See §35.2, §48.8, F-559.

**Vendor Disqualification.** The platform-mechanic by which a Buyer Workspace Owner / Admin (or Ops, for `global_ban` severity) excludes a Seller Org from a single Workspace, all of the buyer Org's Workspaces, or the entire platform. Materialized by the §4.7.2 Vendor Disqualification Record entity (above). Three severities: `soft` (workspace-local), `account_level` (12-month forward-looking buyer-Org-wide), `global_ban` (Ops-imposed cross-platform). Cascade per `Disqualification Cascade` (above); reversal per `Disqualification Reversal` (above); appeal windows per `Disqualification Appeal Window` (above). See §25.3, §4.7.2, F-403, F-404.

**Promoted Listing.** Bare-term alias of the §4.4.19 `PromotedListing` entity (above). Both forms permitted; "Promoted Listing" is the human-readable narrative form used in customer-facing copy and in body-section §27.11 / §34.16.1 narratives. See §4.4.19, §27.11, §34.16.1, F-458.

**brand_voice_guide_v1 (Authored Extension — requires Marketing + Founder sign-off).** The named identity of the canonical Sourcera Brand Voice Guide content artifact that the §34 / §48 R6 ("Tone & Brand Voice") acceptance criterion binds for tone / profanity / off-topic validation across rendered Marketplace-Domain prose (CategoryPage M9, GuidePage M10, ComparisonPage M11, MarketIntelligenceReport M12, HeatMapCell M13, PublicSelectionReport M2, EvaluationCertificate M3). This Glossary entry binds the artifact's **identity, schema, ownership, version axis, storage, and validator contract** — it does NOT inline-restate the guide's payload (tonal-axis values, per-surface tone-calibration values, brand-voice anchor copy). A Marketing-side rewrite of the guide's payload propagates to the R6 validator without amending this entry; the entry is amended only when the schema, ownership, version-axis, storage, or validator-contract identity changes (e.g., bump to `brand_voice_guide_v2` registered as a sibling entry, with `v1` retired per the Appendix K retirement convention). The non-inline-restatement invariant is enforced as Counterfactual #1 of the v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 Prompt 2.2 closure.

**Schema.** The artifact is a structured payload with five field slots, each defined by reference — not by value:
1. `tonal_axes` — Marketing-authored tonal-axis dimensions (voice attributes; pacing; reading-level target; persona).
2. `surface_tone_calibration` — per-Marketplace-Domain-surface tone-calibration table, keyed by the seven §4.4.10–§4.4.16 rendered surfaces (M2, M3, M9, M10, M11, M12, M13). Each row carries the Marketing-authored tone-calibration value for that surface; the row keys are stable.
3. `prohibited_term_registry_ref` — cross-reference pointer to the §48.4.4 prohibited-content registry (profanity / hate speech / political-partisan content / unverified competitive comparisons / off-platform contact information). Inline restatement of the registry is forbidden; updates to the §48.4.4 registry propagate automatically.
4. `brand_voice_anchors_ref` — cross-reference pointer to the UX motion / typography / tone tokens registered in `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` (§3.x token catalog).
5. `schema_version` — the schema-version axis (current canonical value `v1`).

The five-slot schema is the validator's contract; values within slots are Marketing-owned payload.

**Canonical storage.** Ops-Console-managed Marketing-content table (target entity `marketing_content_artifact`, scoped `platform`, slug `brand_voice_guide_v1`). Until the table is materialized (v7.1.x Marketing-Content backlog row), the interim storage location is `assets/brandguidelines/brand_voice_guide_v1.json` in the Sourcera project folder, owned by Marketing Lead via the standard editorial workflow (§48.6.2). Storage location may change without amending this entry provided the canonical-slug binding (`brand_voice_guide_v1`) remains stable.

**Schema-version axis.** Schema version `v1` is the canonical value at v7.1.0a hot-patch / v7.1.1 stamp. Future schema evolutions register as sibling entries (`brand_voice_guide_v2`, etc.) with the R6 acceptance criterion amended in lockstep. The `v1` entry is retired only when no in-flight Master Spec acceptance criterion binds to it; transitional periods may carry both versions concurrently per the standard Appendix K retirement convention.

**Validator binding.** The §48.4.4 content validator resolves this entry's `slug=brand_voice_guide_v1` against the canonical storage location, loads the five-slot payload, and applies the per-surface tone-calibration row to the rendered prose under evaluation. R6 rejects regeneration when the validator reports non-compliance (`editorial_rejection_reason` is populated with the specific dimension that failed; per §48.6.2 RUBRIC v1.0 Fail Action). The validator does NOT read this Appendix K entry directly — it reads the named artifact at the canonical storage location and uses this entry only for identity / schema / ownership resolution.

**Ownership.** Marketing Lead authors the payload; Ops (Marketing role pool, §48.6.2) publishes the artifact and curates version-axis transitions; Founder signs off on the Authored Extension flag governing this entry's existence and structural invariants. Payload edits follow the §48.6.2 RUBRIC v1.0 editorial workflow with the rubric checked against itself recursively (a payload edit cannot reduce R6 enforcement strictness without a separate Authored Extension amendment).

**Authored Extension provenance.** Original authoring 2026-05-03 under Phase 2V D-AK-004 closure (companion AE row `AE-V2-001` in `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md` Phase 2V — Audit Remediation Authored Extensions block). v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 Prompt 2.2 ratification 2026-05-18 — Counterfactual #1 hardening (this rewrite, removing inline payload restatement and adding the non-inline-restatement invariant) — registered under companion AE row `AE-V72REM-02` in the v7.2.0-REM Program Authored Extensions Registry. Both AE rows ratify before v7.1.0a hot-patch stamp per the v7.2.0-REM Program release-gate policy preamble.

**Counterfactual coverage (the non-inline-restatement invariant).** The following three Marketing-side rewrites of the guide payload MUST NOT require amending this Appendix K entry. The illustrative value strings in each scenario below are **purely synthetic — they are NOT current canonical values of the guide payload**, which lives at the canonical storage location (see "Canonical storage" above) and is not restated in this spec. The synthetic strings are present only to disambiguate "payload value" from "schema slot identifier"; they are placeholder transformations, not declarations of state.
1. **Tonal-axis rewrite.** Marketing changes the voice attributes (synthetic-illustration only: "value-A" → "value-A′" in the `tonal_axes` slot). Propagates via `tonal_axes` slot payload edit at the canonical storage location; this entry unchanged.
2. **Per-surface tone-calibration rewrite.** Marketing recalibrates one or more of the seven M2 / M3 / M9 / M10 / M11 / M12 / M13 surface rows (synthetic-illustration only: a row value "value-B" → "value-B′" in the `surface_tone_calibration` slot table). Propagates via `surface_tone_calibration` slot payload edit at the canonical storage location; this entry unchanged.
3. **Prohibited-term registry expansion.** Legal / Marketing add new prohibited-content classes to §48.4.4 (synthetic-illustration only: any number of new closed-set values registered per the §48.4.4 enum-registration discipline). Propagates via the §48.4.4 registry edit (a separate authoring pass with its own Authoring Convention #3 enum-registration discipline); the `prohibited_term_registry_ref` slot in the payload is a pointer and does not need to be re-authored; this entry unchanged.

A Marketing-side rewrite that DOES require amending this entry is necessarily a schema-, ownership-, version-axis-, storage-, or validator-contract-identity change — for instance, adding a sixth slot (`accessibility_voice_overlay`), or switching the prohibited-term-registry source from §48.4.4 to a new external service, or bumping to `v2`. Such amendments require a new Authored Extension ledger row; the body of this entry is not silently rewritten.

**Cross-references.** See §34 / §48 R6 (validator binding); §48.4.4 (prohibited-content registry); §48.6.2 (editorial RUBRIC v1.0); §4.4.10–§4.4.16 (rendered surfaces under R6 jurisdiction); §3.x (UX token catalog for `brand_voice_anchors_ref` resolution); Appendix K retirement convention (sibling version handling); `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md` AE-V2-001 + AE-V72REM-02 (provenance).

### Appendix K Cross-Reference and Disambiguation Notes (Phase 2V)

The following notes amend pre-existing entries to close defects D-AK-023 (Featured Placement collision), D-AK-024 / D-AK-025 / D-AK-026 (duplicate-entry alias), D-AK-027 (§4.3 sweep cross-reference pointers).

**Featured Placement disambiguation (D-AK-023).** Two pre-existing entries share the human-readable name "Featured Placement" with deliberately distinct meanings: (a) `FeaturedPlacement` (above, §4.4.20) — Marketplace-Discovery monetization entity rendered on M9 / M11 / M13; (b) `Featured Placement` (above, §48.2.10) — L9 Template Library buyer-browse surface treatment for templates that cross trending / featured / top-pick clone-count thresholds, subject to cross-buyer-org diversity floor (k=5 distinct buyers). The two concepts share the human-readable name; use the qualifiers `(Marketplace-Discovery entity, §4.4.20)` and `(Template Library surface, §48.2.10)` wherever ambiguity is possible.
