Disambiguation pattern matches the `KB Value Meter` precedent (above, line 46142).

**k-Anonymity Floor consolidation (D-AK-024).** Two pre-existing entries (the §4.4 Marketplace cluster and the §48 Network Effects cluster) define `k-Anonymity Floor` consistently (k=5 / k=10 / k=20). The §48.4.7 entry is the canonical declaration (the broader three-tier table); the §4.4 entry is the per-listing-surface enforcement view. Future amendments to k-anonymity floors MUST update §48.4.7 first; the §4.4 entry MUST cite §48.4.7 by anchor.

**Signal Integrity Monitor (SIM) consolidation (D-AK-025).** Two pre-existing entries (the §4.3 Growth-Mechanic cluster and the §48 Network Effects cluster) define `SIM` with overlapping but unequal scope. The §48 entry (eleven signal classes catalogued in §48.4.10) is the canonical declaration; the §4.3 entry covers the M16 / M17 anti-spam subset. The §4.3 entry MUST cite the §48 entry as the broader scope.

**KB Namespace consolidation (D-AK-026).** Two pre-existing entries (the §4.4 software-level qualified form and the §22.3.4 entity-form) define `KB Namespace` with an entity-vs-qualifier relationship. The §22.3.4 entry is the canonical declaration (covers both software-level and org-level kinds); the §4.4 entry is the qualified specialization (software-level only). Future amendments MUST update §22.3.4 first.

**§4.3-sweep cross-reference pointers (D-AK-027).** Five §4.3 sweep entries previously omitted "See §" anchor pointers; the canonical anchors are: **Referral Code** → §4.3.16; **Grant Code** → §4.3.17; **Loaded Hourly Rate** → §4.3.19, §50.13; **Author Role Snapshot** → §4.3.12; **Edit Lock Window** → §4.3.12. Future §4.3 cluster amendments MUST emit a "See §N.N.N" pointer per Authoring Convention #4.

### Terms Introduced in Phase 3V+ WorkOS April 2026 Integration (2026-05-04)

The following entries close the Appendix K coverage delta introduced by §4.2.5 / §5.13 / §6.1.1 / §6.7.6 V3+ authoring. Each entry satisfies the multi-section threshold (CLAUDE.md §12) and the §4 entity / surface / mechanic glossary parity rule (Authoring Convention #4).

**WorkOS Group.** A first-class WorkOS-side entity (released 2026-04-22) representing a named bundling of Organization Memberships within an Organization. Sourcera mirrors WorkOS Groups as the §4.2.5 Group entity; the Sourcera-side row carries the WorkOS `group_id` reference plus name, description, member count, and an optional `assigned_role_slug` for SCIM-directory-group → role mapping per §5.13.2 precedence rule. Group-based role assignment is announced as a future WorkOS capability and is the primary motivation for the §4.2.5 entity authoring. See §4.2.5, §5.13.2, §6.1.1, §6.9.3.

**FGA Custom Role.** A WorkOS Fine-Grained Authorization Custom Role declaration that maps a permission set to a `scope_type` (`organization`, `workspace`, `bid_workspace`, `marketplace`, `platform`). FGA Custom Roles can be scoped to specific resource types (released 2026-04-21) in addition to organization-wide. Sourcera's two-level RBAC model (§5.1) maps onto FGA Custom Roles per the §5.13.1 mapping table. Customer-Org-defined Custom Roles are authored in §36.2 Roles & Permissions settings (Enterprise tier). See §5.13.1, §36.2, Appendix J `fga_custom_role_scope_type` enum.

**WorkOS Predefined Attribute.** One of six WorkOS-managed user attributes auto-mapped from the customer-Org's Directory provider: `display_name`, `employee_number`, `organization`, `phone_numbers`, `manager_name`, `manager_id`. Released April 2026; consumed by Sourcera per §4.2.3 V3+ extension and §5.13.4. The §5.9 Executive Sponsor auto-derivation cascade walks `User.manager_id` chain (5-hop bound) before falling through to most-senior Org Owner. See §4.2.3, §5.9, §5.13.4, Appendix J `workos_predefined_attribute_kind` enum.

**WorkOS Custom Attributes pipeline.** The WorkOS-managed custom-attribute payload mirrored from Directory Users to OrgMembership.`custom_attributes_json` per §4.2.2 V3+ extension. Replaces the deprecated `Directory User.raw_attributes` field (deprecated effective 2026-04-15). Sourcera consumes the `groups[]` array within the JSON for SCIM directory-group → role mapping at sign-in time. See §4.2.2, §5.13.4.

**SCIM Directory-Group Role Assignment.** A SCIM provisioning pattern that assigns Sourcera roles to Organization Memberships based on the user's directory groups (e.g., `BillingAdmin` group → `billing_admin` role). Per the WorkOS April 2026 contract and §5.13.2 precedence rule, directory-group role assignments take precedence over SSO group role assignments. See §5.2.1.2 SCIM Provisioning Interaction, §5.13.2, §5.13.5 AC #2.

**`raw_attributes` Deprecation.** WorkOS deprecated the `Directory User.raw_attributes` field effective 2026-04-15. Sourcera MUST NOT consume `raw_attributes`; consume `custom_attributes` (mirrored to §4.2.2 OrgMembership.`custom_attributes_json`) and predefined attributes (mirrored to §4.2.3 User entity V3+ fields) instead. CI gate `workos_raw_attributes_not_consumed` asserts via static-analysis property test. New error code `workos_raw_attributes_consumption_forbidden` (HTTP 422; Appendix I Phase-3V+). See §4.2.2, §4.2.3, §5.13.4, Appendix I Phase-3V+.

**Group-Based Role Assignment (future WorkOS capability).** WorkOS announced group-based role assignment as a future capability in the 2026-04-22 release notes. Sourcera's §4.2.5 Group entity is designed to absorb the capability when it lands; the `assigned_role_slug` and `assigned_role_scope` fields already model the binding. Until WorkOS ships the group-based assignment endpoint, customer-Org Admin sets `assigned_role_slug` via Sourcera UI → WorkOS API call. See §4.2.5, §5.13.3.

**`auto_derivation_source`.** A 4-value enum (`explicit`, `manager_chain`, `most_senior_org_owner`, `most_senior_org_admin_fallback`) captured on every Pulse event row per §5.9 V3+ Executive Sponsor designation flow. Records which path of the auto-derivation cascade resolved the Sponsor at event-emit time, for forensic clarity. See §5.9, §20 Evaluation Pulse, Appendix J `auto_derivation_source` enum.

### v7.2.0-REM Phase 3 Additions (2026-05-18) — §M.5 Catalog Schema Tightening {#appendix-j-v72rem-phase-3}

v7.2.0-REM Phase 3 remediation closure batch (D-11.3-001 P0 per-row `Runtime status` column landing). New enum registration; per AE-V11-03 §M.5 catalog schema tightening (5 new columns); landing the first of those columns (the `Runtime status` column) per the v7.2.0-REM Phase 3 scope. Remaining four enums (`ci_gate_row_class`, `ci_gate_execution_context`, `ci_gate_override_path_class`, `ci_gate_runbook_url_kind`) staged for successive remediation phases per AE-V11-03 dependency declaration; this phase registers ONLY the `ci_gate_runtime_status` enum.

**`ci_gate_runtime_status`** (v7.2.0-REM Phase 3 — D-11.3-001 P0): closed enum with 3 canonical values:

| Value | Semantics | Used by |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `runtime_active` | The gate's runtime artifact (lint detector, deploy-time validator, schema-validation test, Playwright fixture, Datadog monitor, synthetic chaos test) exists in the CI / production pipeline AND has run on the most recent main-branch commit (for spec-tree gates) or the most recent deploy (for runtime gates) or the most recent scheduled run (for synthetic monitors) AND the run record has been ingested by the §42 observability stack. Wired and enforced. | §M.5.4 rows (11 at v7.2.0-REM M02.3 Runtime-Wiring Pass, 2026-06-15): `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff`, `appendix_m_tier_visibility_smoke`, `appendix_k_glossary_canonicality`, and the eight M02.3-pass promotions `appendix_anchor_slug_no_colon`, `principle_9_anchor_canonicality`, `appendix_i_internal_event_no_http_status`, `defense_view_appendix_i_pairing`, `appendix_m5_runtime_status_coverage`, `appendix_m5_header_count_parity`, `eval_starter_appendix_i_pairing`, `appendix_m5_cross_reference_resolution_completeness`. |
| `spec_binding_pending_pack_<id>` | The gate is authored as a binding spec contract at §M.4 / §M.5 fidelity but the runtime artifact has not yet landed in the implementation pack named by `<id>` (per `Build_Execution_Strategy.md §11` and `Linear_Execution_Blueprint.md §5`). The `<id>` token is a parameterised suffix carrying the owning implementation-pack identifier (e.g., `spec_binding_pending_pack_m02_3` for M02.3, `spec_binding_pending_pack_m11_3` for M11.3, `spec_binding_pending_pack_m21_3` for M21.3, `spec_binding_pending_pack_m24_3` for M24.3, `spec_binding_pending_pack_release_orchestration` for the release-orchestration pipeline). Enforcement during the pending window is via code-review and authoring discipline per §M.3 and §M.4.7. v7.1.1 stamp gate (`v7_1_1_stamp_gate_runtime_status_audit`) audits each pending row's pack-side runtime artifact at release-stamp time. | §M.5.4 rows: 110 of 122 (118 → 110 at the v7.2.0-REM M02.3 Runtime-Wiring Pass, 2026-06-15, which promoted 8 spec-tree-lint rows to `runtime_active`); §M.5.10 rows: 33 of 33 (V12 cluster); §M.5.12 rows: 24 of 24 (V13 cluster); §M.5.13 rows: 2 of 2 (v7.2.0-REM Phase 1 cluster). |
| `spec_binding_release_gate_only` | The gate runs only at version-stamp time and is wired through the release-orchestration pipeline rather than the per-PR CI workflow or the per-deploy validator pipeline. The gate's runtime artifact lives in `tools/release/stamp_gate.ts` and runs synchronously as part of the version-stamp ceremony, blocking the stamp on any (a)–(d) failure per §M.5.4 release-stamp-gate row. | §M.5.4 rows: `v7_1_1_stamp_gate_runtime_status_audit`. |

**Notes.**
- Cardinality: exactly one value per §M.5 catalog row (every row carries a non-null `Runtime status` cell per the `appendix_m5_runtime_status_coverage` meta-gate assertion).
- `<id>` token in `spec_binding_pending_pack_<id>` is parameterised and follows the lowercase snake_case convention with `m<NN>_<x>` shape (the implementation-pack identifier per `Build_Execution_Strategy.md` numbering); the parameter is parsed by the runtime-status detector as `^spec_binding_pending_pack_(?P<pack_id>[a-z0-9_]+)$` per §M.5.5 default assignment table.
- Transition: a row transitions `spec_binding_pending_pack_<id> → runtime_active` when the owning implementation pack ships the runtime artifact AND the first gate run completes successfully AND the run record is ingested by §42 observability AND the §M.5 catalog row's `Runtime status` cell is updated in the same PR that lands the runtime artifact (per `Build_Execution_Strategy.md` per-pack closure protocol). The transition triggers a §M.4 nightly-digest entry per §M.4.6.
- Override: per §M.5.4 `appendix_m5_runtime_status_coverage` row, `Override path: not_permitted` — the runtime-status disclosure is the precondition for implementation-pack wiring and the v7.1.1 stamp-gate audit. Attempting to override the meta-gate is rejected at parser layer per §M.4.4.5 row-level `not_permitted` rule.
- Per §M.5.3 schema, the §M.5.4 catalog index carries the per-row `Runtime status` value; the §M.5.5 per-phase-cluster default-assignment table is the fallback authority for new rows authored without an explicit cell value but is NOT authoritative against an explicit per-row cell.
- D-V72REM-PH3-002 P3 cosmetic (CLOSED 2026-05-18 at v7.2.0-REM Phase 3 cosmetic-hygiene pass): the V12 sub-section preamble at §M.5.10 previously rendered `spec_binding_pending_pack_M02.3` (capitalised; uses dot delimiter) rather than the canonical lowercase snake-case `spec_binding_pending_pack_m02_3` (lowercase; uses underscore delimiter). Drift remediated in-session at v7.2.0-REM Phase 3 closure: §M.5.10 preamble amended to canonical lowercase + underscore form with explicit cross-reference to this Appendix J §J.v7.2.0-REM-Phase-3 `<id>` token convention. Sibling §M.5.6 execution-context-partition documentation drift (3 runtime_active gates not partitioned by `pr_lint` vs `synthetic_monitor` execution context) remediated in the same pass — §M.5.6 runtime-composition paragraph rewritten to enumerate execution_context per gate. Canonical-row defect-ledger entry at `_audit/DEFECT_LEDGER.md` v7.2.0-REM Phase 3 cosmetic-hygiene block.

**`policy_framework_kind`** (§12.3.2): `soc_2_type_ii`, `iso_27001`, `hipaa`, `gdpr`, `nist_csf`, `pci_dss`, `fedramp`, `hitrust`, `ssae_18`, `cis_critical_security_controls`, `custom_other` (11 values). Consumer: §12.3.1 step 3 `framework_list` streaming output; §12.7.1 `framework_reference` join (`"ISO 27001 2.1.1"` form); Appendix C `policy.ingestion.framework_detected` payload `framework_kind`. **Alias:** D-4.3-003 named this `framework_kind` — canonical is `policy_framework_kind`. **Extension policy:** adding a framework requires a Phase 14.x amendment + an Anthropic Opus eval-set update; `custom_other` is the registered fallback (never an open string).

**`policy_framework_confidence_band`** (§12.3.1 step 4): `high`, `low_confidence`, `unknown_framework` (3 values). Band thresholds are the numeric singletons at §12.3.1 (`high` ≥ 0.80; `low_confidence` 0.60–0.79; `unknown_framework` < 0.60) — cited, not restated here. Consumer: §12.3.1 threshold logic; §12.3.3 confirmation-modal confidence bars. **Alias:** D-4.3-003 named this `confidence_band`.

**`policy_framework_inference_outcome`** (§12.3.1): `accepted`, `low_confidence_pending_user`, `unknown_pending_user` (3 values). **Disambiguation:** `policy_framework_confidence_band` is the raw classification of the Opus confidence score; `policy_framework_inference_outcome` is the resulting pipeline branch (`high → accepted`; `low_confidence → low_confidence_pending_user`; `unknown_framework → unknown_pending_user`). Consumer: §12.3.1 detection pipeline; the Appendix L.9 `PolicyIngestionJob.status` transition guards. **Alias:** D-12-006 named this `policy_framework_inference_outcome` (canonical).

**`policy_custom_use_case_category`** (§12.3.2 Custom path / §12.7.1 category mapping): `security`, `compliance`, `operations`, `data_privacy` (4 values). **Disambiguation (per D-4.3-003):** this is NOT the generic Requirement category enum (§4.3.4); it is the derivation map applied when `policy_framework_kind = custom_other` and when mapping a framework section to a requirement category at §12.7.1. Consumer: §12.3.2 Custom dropdown; §12.7.1 `category` field derivation. **Alias:** D-4.3-003 referenced this as `requirement_category_from_framework`.

**`policy_dedup_action`** (§12.5.2): `merge`, `keep_a`, `keep_b`, `reject` (4 values). Consumer: §12.5.2 dedup-modal toggle; the `POST …/dedup-resolutions` request body (§32 Policy Ingestion endpoint cluster, tracked under D-12-003 / D-4.3-007 api-class — out of catalog scope). **Alias:** D-4.3-003 named this `dedup_action`.

**`policy_amendment_state`** (§12.7.2): `pending_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, `pending_refinement`, `active` (5 values; lowercase canonical). **Drift closed (D-4.3-004):** §12.7.2 prose used Title-Case forms (`PENDING_REVIEW`, `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`, `PENDING_REFINEMENT`, `ACTIVE`); those are retired in favor of the lowercase Appendix J canonicality convention (per the D-3.1-006 / D-3.1-013 role-name canonicality class). Consumer: §12.7.2 / §12.7.3 batch amendment UI; Appendix L.10 `PolicyAmendment.status` state machine.

**`policy_ingestion_job_status`** (§12.3.1 / §12.4 / §12.5 / §12.6 / §12.7): `parsing`, `framework_detected`, `extracting`, `dedup_pending`, `dedup_resolved`, `mapping`, `amendments_drafted`, `completed`, `failed` (9 values). Consumer: the §12 pipeline lineage; Appendix L.9 `PolicyIngestionJob.status` state machine; Appendix C `policy.ingestion.*` webhook payloads. **Note (cross-cohort scope boundary):** D-12-002 describes finer PolicyDocument substates (`uploaded`, `framework_pending_user_confirmation`, `extraction_partial`, `discarded`, `archived`); per Authoring Convention #3 (no inline/unregistered enum values) these are modeled as Conditions/Notes on the Appendix L.9 transitions rather than added to this 9-value registered set. **`vendor_opt_out_authority_failure_reason`** (§27.10.2; nullable): `dns_lookup_failed`, `dns_record_not_found`, `dns_record_mismatch`, `dns_probe_retry_exhausted`, `dns_split_horizon_detected`, `seller_owner_role_missing_at_signature`, `mfa_step_up_declined`, `mfa_factor_revoked`, `ops_imposed_missing_dpo`, `attestation_text_version_stale` (10 values). **Count reconciliation (D-6.2-005):** the finding cited 11 values; §27.10.2 enumerates the 10 above. The body-enumerated 10 are authoritative; an 11th, if later authored at §27.10.2, registers here. Filed as P3 count-drift **D-V72REM-PH6-001** (`_audit/DEFECT_LEDGER.md`).

Per D-6.2-014: §27.9.5.1 presents these as the From/To states of the per-row `k_anon_satisfied` state machine, currently persisted across a boolean + `suppressed_reason` + `suppressed_at_delivery_reason`. This entry registers the unified state enum as the canonical home for the 11 per-row states; §27.9.5 / §27.9.5.1 and the §4.4.18 SellerSignal field table should adopt the enum-typed column per the D-6.2-014 recommendation (body adoption tracked under AE-V72REM-PH6-01). Lifecycle cross-referenced in Appendix L (§L.8).

The body consumer (`suppressed_at_delivery_reason`) is authoritative; the corresponding `seller_signal_k_anon_state` is `suppressed_recompute_deadline`.

### Phase V12 Additions — Glossary Terms (Appendix K register; closes D-42-009) {#appendix-k-phase-v12}

V12 remediation closure. Cross-section terms register here per Appendix K convention.

**SLO (Service Level Objective).** Internal target for a service's availability or latency; distinct from SLA. SLOs are tighter than the corresponding customer-committed SLA to produce slack. Authored in §42.2.2 per-service SLO targets. Used: §42.2, §44.1, §44.5, §7.5.3.

**SLA (Service Level Agreement).** Customer-committed availability or response-time target. Authoritative home: §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 cell **SLA**. Cited from §42.1, §29.9, BPS §6, SPS §8.

**RTO (Recovery Time Objective).** Maximum acceptable wall-clock time from incident detection to service restoration. Per §42.4 RTO/RPO; 1 hour per residency region.

**RPO (Recovery Point Objective).** Maximum acceptable data-loss window. Per §42.4; 1 hour per residency region.

**MTTD (Mean Time to Detect).** Average time from incident start to first internal page. Implied by §42.6.0 detector thresholds; tracked via Datadog SLO objects.

**MTTR (Mean Time to Resolve).** Average time from on-call ack to incident `mitigated_at`. Implied by §42.3.2 process; tracked via PostmortemRecord trend reports.

**Postmortem.** Per §42.3.2 step 10; blameless artifact published within 72 hours of `mitigated_at`. Registered as `OpsActionRecord` with `action_kind='incident_postmortem_published'`. Customer-visible projection per §42.10.3.

**RCA (Root Cause Analysis).** Per §42.3.2 step 9; single-author draft completed within 48 hours of `mitigated_at`. Distinct from Postmortem (which is peer-reviewed and may be published).

**Runbook.** Per §42.5.1 Runbook Inventory; RunbookEntry rows stored in Notion (per §42.13 entity); freshness governed by `runbook_status` enum (`current` / `stale` / `retired`); reviewed quarterly per §42.5.2 AC #3.

**War Room.** The Slack channel + Zoom bridge convened during P0/P1 incident response per §42.3.2 step 4. Fallback to Microsoft Teams channel per §42.6.3 if Slack itself is degraded.

**Statuspage.** Statuspage.io public status page used for customer-facing incident notification per §42.3.2 step 5 (P0 = SEV-1; P1 = SEV-2). Sourcera-hosted fallback at `https://status.sourcera.com/fallback` per §42.6.3.

**Game-Day / Game-Day Rehearsal.** Quarterly per-residency DR drill per §42.4.1 AC #5; materialized as DrDrillRun entity per §42.12.

**DR Drill.** Equivalent to Game-Day; success criteria authored at §42.12.5.

**Burn-Rate Alarm.** Datadog SLO-burn-rate alarm per §42.2.2 per-service SLO row. Burn-rate threshold typically 2% over 1h or 5% over 4h depending on SLO criticality.

**Error Budget.** The complement of a service's availability SLO over the SLO window (e.g., 99.95% over 30 days = 21.6 min error budget). Tracked via Datadog SLO objects per §42.2.2.

**Break-Glass.** Two distinct usages in Sourcera, disambiguated by context: (a) §50.4.5 #4 Ops Impersonation Break-Glass (no resolvable Org Owner — co-signer + disclosure commitment); (b) §50.2.4 ¶4 Break-Glass DB Access (direct database access by `ops_admin` + `ops_security_admin` quorum for emergency forensics; vaulted key; 72-hour postmortem).

**Audit Chain (or Audit Hash Chain).** The append-only hash-chained sequence of §4.6.1 AuditEvent rows. In-scope membership per §42.6.1.D rule. Integrity verified by §42.6.1 audit-integrity background jobs.

**Three-Step Escalation Ladder.** §42.5.0 paging escalation: primary 5m → secondary 10m → manager 15m. Cited inbound from §25.6.2.

### Terms Introduced / Clarified in Phase V14 Cross-Document Consistency Audit (2026-05-13)

The following Glossary entry closes the V14 net-new defect D-V14-005 by authoring a single-source field-naming convention for value/money-denominated fields. It harmonizes the AIWallet `*_value_dollars` Integer-cents storage with the §44.4.5 `*_usd_cents` naming convention without renaming the production AIWallet field set (Convex schema migration is out of scope for V14; the canonical AIWallet field names remain `monthly_included_value_dollars`, `consumed_value_dollars`, `auto_topup_max_monthly_value_dollars`, etc.). Authored Extension — requires Engineering Lead sign-off; companion AE row in `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md` v7.1.1 Phase V14 Naming-Convention Block. Refines the scope of pre-existing decision **E-1 (Currency Unit Convention)** per `_integration/Decisions.md` and pre-filed defect **D-DEC-001 (P1)**.

**`value_dollars` field-naming convention (D-V14-005; Authored Extension — requires Engineering Lead sign-off).** A Sourcera engineering naming convention covering every field named `*_value_dollars`, `*_value_dollars_*`, `*_value_dollars_cents`, or otherwise carrying the `value_dollars` token in its name. **Storage unit: Integer USD cents** (no exceptions; matches the §44.4.5 `*_usd_cents` convention and the Stripe / Convex / pricing-engine canonical unit). **Display unit: USD dollars** rendered at the surface layer via `format_value_dollars()` helper (renders `cents / 100` with 2-decimal precision, locale-aware grouping, `$` prefix per §41 i18n convention). **Authoring discipline:** every new field that carries monetary value MUST be named in one of these two patterns: (a) `*_cents` or `*_usd_cents` (storage-explicit; preferred for new authoring per `_integration/Decisions.md` E-1 recommendation) — used by §44.4.5 and post-V14 authoring; (b) `*_value_dollars` (display-aware; storage-as-cents; legacy AIWallet convention preserved for Convex-migration safety per V14 D-V14-005 scope) — used by §4.8.3 AIWallet and existing pre-V14 fields. **Storage-unit invariant:** the field VALUE is always Integer cents regardless of naming pattern; engineers MUST NOT divide by 100 when reading a `*_value_dollars` field for arithmetic — the value is already cents, not dollars. **Migration disposition:** D-DEC-001 (E-1) ratification path drives the eventual rename to `*_cents` form; until then, the `value_dollars` convention is the documented, ratified hazard avoidance. **CI gate `value_dollars_storage_convention_audit` (Authored Extension; runtime_status: `spec_binding_pending_pack_m02_3`) asserts via static-analysis property test:** (i) every `*_value_dollars` field has `Integer` type in the entity field table; (ii) the field row's `Notes` column or adjacent narrative includes the phrase "Integer USD cents" OR cites this Glossary entry by anchor; (iii) no Decimal-typed field carries the `value_dollars` token in its name. **Validator binding:** the V14-introduced gate joins the §M.5 catalog as part of the v7.1.1 stamp-gate inheritance set, paired with D-DEC-001 currency-unit-migration completion gate. See §4.8.3 AIWallet entity, §44.4.5, `_integration/Decisions.md → E-1`, `_audit/DEFECT_LEDGER.md → Phase V14 → D-V14-005`.

## Appendix L: Entity State Machines {#appendix-l-entity-state-machines}

**Purpose.** This appendix is the single compendium of entity-lifecycle state machines whose status fields are declared in §4 (Data Model) and §22 (KB) and whose transition rules are referenced from those sections. Appendices D (Response Status) and E (Workspace & Bid Workspace Status) pre-date this appendix and remain authoritative for their entities; Appendix L covers the remaining entity state machines that were declared but not previously consolidated. Every `status` enum registered in Appendix J that corresponds to a non-trivial lifecycle must have a corresponding state machine table here or an explicit cross-reference to the originating section.

**Authoring Rule.** For each state machine: (1) a state diagram showing the principal flow, (2) a complete From / To / Trigger / Conditions / Notes transition table that enumerates every legal transition (including self-loops where applicable) and implicitly rejects all others, (3) terminal-state identification, (4) scope isolation confirmation (which console owns transitions), and (5) Acceptance Criteria. Out-of-table transitions MUST be rejected server-side with an Appendix I error code.

### L.1 Internal Comment Thread Status State Machine {#l.1-internal-comment-thread-status-state-machine}

**Entity.** InternalCommentThread (§4.3.11). **Enum.** `internal_comment_thread_status` (Appendix J): `open`, `resolved`, `archived`. **Scope.** Buyer-Console-only; all transitions reject if the caller's session console is `seller` (per §7.2 Dual-Console Firewall) and the thread's attached-to target is not a cross-console surface.

**State Diagram:**

open ──→ resolved ──→ archived

  ↑           │

  └───────────┘  (re-open)

open ──────────────→ archived

**Complete State Transitions:**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (none) | `open` | Thread created via §4.3.11 server-side create | Caller has `buyer_workspace_member` role; attached_to entity exists and is visible to caller; visibility_scope ≠ `private_to_author_plus_mentioned` OR caller = author | Initial state. Emits `internal_comment_thread.created` (Appendix C). |
| `open` | `resolved` | Workspace Owner, Workspace Admin, Use Case Lead, or thread author clicks "Resolve" | Thread has ≥ 1 post; attached-to entity not in terminal state (`workspace.status = archived` forces auto-archive instead) | Sets `resolved_at = now()`, `resolved_by_user_id`. Thread still readable; posts frozen to new authoring except for follow-up edits within 15-minute edit lock (§4.3.12). |
| `resolved` | `open` | Workspace Owner, Workspace Admin, or thread author clicks "Re-open" | Thread not archived | Clears `resolved_at`, `resolved_by_user_id`. Emits `internal_comment_thread.reopened` (Appendix C). |
| `open` | `archived` | Workspace Owner manual archive OR attached_to entity transitions to archived/terminal state | Cascading archive from §4.3.11 attached_to target | Soft delete via `deleted_at`; thread readable in audit-trail exports but excluded from all live query paths. Hard-deleted per §40.2 retention (tied to parent entity retention). |
| `resolved` | `archived` | Same as `open → archived` | Same | Preserves `resolved_at` for audit. |
| `archived` | (terminal) | — | Terminal state; no forward transition | Un-archive is not supported; if recovery is needed, Ops runs a DSAR-safe restore from backup per §40.2. |
| any | (hard delete) | Parent entity hard-delete OR §45.1 retention cutoff reached | Parent workspace `deleted_at + 90d` OR DSAR `right_to_erasure` approved | Cascades to all InternalCommentPost and InternalCommentMention rows. |

**Rejected Transitions (non-exhaustive; enforced server-side).** `archived → open`, `archived → resolved`, `resolved → (none)`, cross-console initiation from seller session → rejected with `internal_comment_cross_console_access` (Appendix I; HTTP 404; non-leak).

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. All status transitions write one row to the §4.6 AuditEvent table with `entity_type = internal_comment_thread` and the new status in the diff payload.
2. A Convex reactive query consumer observing thread status MUST see a status change within p95 ≤ 500 ms of commit (§7.5.3 reactivity SLO).
3. Attempting `archived → open` returns HTTP 409 with error code `invalid_state_transition` (Appendix I) and leaves status unchanged.
4. Cascade archive from workspace archival is atomic with the workspace transition (§4.3.1 Workspace state machine, Appendix E); a partial cascade MUST NOT leave threads in `open` with workspace in `archived`.
5. A buyer in a workspace where a thread has transitioned to `resolved` must see the resolution within the reactive SLO; email notification to thread participants is emitted via §6 `internal_comment_thread_resolved` (Appendix C) unless the recipient has muted the thread.
6. Session-console firewall: any mutation attempted from a seller-console session returns HTTP 404 via `internal_comment_cross_console_access`; the thread's existence is not leaked.

### L.2 Buyer Referral Status State Machine {#l.2-buyer-referral-status-state-machine}

**Entity.** BuyerReferral (§4.3.16). **Enum.** `referral_status` (Appendix J): `pending`, `signed_up`, `activated`, `credit_issued`, `credit_redeemed`, `credit_expired`, `forfeited`, `flagged_fraud`, `revoked`. **Scope.** Buyer-Console-owned; referrer-Org scoped. Transitions executed by (a) the buyer-side self-serve flow, (b) the nightly referral-credit job, (c) Signal Integrity Monitor (SIM, C.100), or (d) Ops console with audit trail.

**State Diagram:**

pending ──→ signed_up ──→ activated ──→ credit_issued ──→ credit_redeemed ──→ credit_expired

    │             │              │              │

    ↓             ↓              ↓              ↓

flagged_fraud ──→ forfeited    revoked      credit_expired

(SIM blocks at any pre-issuance state; revoked terminal post-issuance)

**Complete State Transitions:**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (none) | `pending` | Referrer generates referral via §4.3.16 referral-create endpoint | Caller has `buyer_billing_admin` or `buyer_owner` role; referrer Org not in `flagged_fraud` cooldown | `referral_code` minted; `activity_threshold_policy_version` stamped with current Ops policy. |
| `pending` | `signed_up` | Referee provisions a new Buyer Org via magic-link or code redemption | Referee email ≠ referrer email; referee Org not an existing paying Org; Vendor Opt-Out Registry (C.123) not matched | Sets `referee_org_id`, `signed_up_at`. If `referrer_email_domain = referee_email_domain`, also sets `same_domain_suppressed=true` unless Ops override active. |
| `signed_up` | `activated` | Referee Org meets activation threshold (default: ≥ 1 workspace through Phase 9 AND ≥ 3 paid users) | Threshold evaluated nightly against `activity_threshold_policy_version` stamped at create (retroactive-safety invariant) | Sets `min_activity_reached_at`. Does NOT auto-issue credit; credit issuance awaits next nightly credit-issuance job. |
| `activated` | `credit_issued` | Nightly credit-issuance job | SIM (C.100) did not flag; `same_domain_suppressed=false` (or Ops override present); `payment_method_overlap_detected=false`; `ip_range_overlap_detected=false` | Sets `credit_issued_at`, `credit_expires_at = credit_issued_at + 365d`. Writes Stripe Credit Note, appends ID to `stripe_credit_note_ids`. |
| `credit_issued` | `credit_redeemed` | Referrer's invoice applies remaining credit via §34.11 billing pipeline | `credit_redeemed_usd = credit_value_usd` (full) OR `credit_expires_at` reached with residual (split to `credit_expired`) | Terminal-for-credit state; `stripe_credit_note_ids` append per redemption event. |
| `credit_issued` | `credit_expired` | Daily Convex scheduled job | `now() ≥ credit_expires_at` AND `credit_redeemed_usd < credit_value_usd` | Residual forfeit; Stripe Credit Note voided with note `sourcera_referral_credit_expired`. |
| `pending`, `signed_up`, `activated` | `flagged_fraud` | Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100) evaluation | Any of: `velocity_flag=true`, `payment_method_overlap_detected=true`, `ip_range_overlap_detected=true`, bootstrapping-pattern match, `referral_fraud_pattern_accumulation` | Credit suspended; Ops review required. `fraud_signal_flags` populated. |
| `flagged_fraud` | `forfeited` | Ops declines to override the SIM block | Ops decision recorded with `ops_override_user_id` null and `credit_forfeited_reason` populated | Terminal. Referee retains their Org; referrer receives no credit. |
| `flagged_fraud` | `pending` OR `signed_up` OR `activated` | Ops sets `ops_override_user_id` and `ops_override_note` | Ops manual override with note ≥ 1 char | Returns to pre-flag state; forward progression resumes. Audited. |
| `pending`, `signed_up` | `forfeited` | Referee opts out via Vendor Opt-Out Registry (C.123) OR global marketing opt-out | Sets `referee_opt_out_at`, `credit_forfeited_reason = referee_opt_out` | Terminal. No credit issued. |
| `credit_issued`, `credit_redeemed` | `revoked` | Ops manual revocation post-issuance (e.g., downstream fraud discovery) | Requires DPO approval + Ops `revoked_reason`; Stripe Credit Note reversed | Terminal. Distinct from `forfeited` (pre-issuance). Remaining redemption balance is reversed via Stripe reversal. |
| `credit_redeemed`, `credit_expired`, `forfeited`, `revoked` | (terminal) | — | Terminal states | Retained Org-life + 7 years per §40.2 / §45.1 financial-record retention, exempt from DSAR right-to-erasure for financial audit. |

**Referee Exclusivity Rule.** A referee Org may only be bound to one referral; a second referral attempting to claim the same referee is rejected at `signed_up` transition with Appendix I error `referral_referee_already_bound` (HTTP 409). This prevents double-counting.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. All status transitions write to §4.6 AuditEvent with `entity_type = referral` and prior/new status.
2. The nightly credit-issuance job is idempotent: re-running it within the same UTC day for an already-`credit_issued` referral is a no-op (keyed on `(referral_id, credit_issued_at::date)`).
3. `activity_threshold_policy_version` is evaluated against the *stamped* version, not the current live Ops policy, to satisfy retroactive-safety (Authored Extension — flagged in RECONCILIATION.md).
4. SIM flag transitions MUST populate `fraud_signal_flags` with at least one value; empty `fraud_signal_flags` on a `flagged_fraud` status returns `invalid_state_transition`.
5. `revoked` post-issuance MUST reverse Stripe credit via Credit Note reversal with 100% balance clearing within 24 h; failures page Ops.
6. `credit_expired` residual forfeit MUST equal `credit_value_usd − credit_redeemed_usd` and MUST write a corresponding Stripe Credit Note void.
7. Re-issuance after SIM override: emits `referral_ops_overridden` audit event and resumes forward progression on the next nightly job.

### L.3 Pro Trial Seat Grant Status State Machine {#l.3-pro-trial-seat-grant-status-state-machine}

**Entity.** ProTrialSeatGrant (§4.3.17). **Enum.** `trial_seat_status` (Appendix J): `issued`, `invite_sent`, `provisioned`, `in_trial`, `converted`, `auto_downgraded`, `vendor_declined`, `expired_unaccepted`, `buyer_revoked`, `fraud_blocked`. **Scope.** Dual-console: buyer-side issuance, seller-side acceptance; pool accounting (`buyer_pool_seats_remaining_at_grant`) lives buyer-side. Cross-console firewall enforced per §7.2: buyer sees buyer-facing projection, vendor sees vendor-facing projection (Authored Extension — dual-projection read rule flagged in RECONCILIATION.md).

**State Diagram:**

issued ──→ invite_sent ──→ provisioned ──→ in_trial ──→ converted

   │            │               │              │

   │            │               │              └──→ auto_downgraded (day 31 no conversion)

   │            │               └──→ vendor_declined (Billing Admin decline during trial)

   │            └──→ expired_unaccepted (30-day invite TTL)

   ├──→ buyer_revoked (pre-provisioning only)

   └──→ fraud_blocked (SIM block at any pre-provisioning state)

**Complete State Transitions:**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (none) | `issued` | Buyer Billing Admin issues grant via §4.3.17 grant-create endpoint | Pool cap not exhausted (`buyer_pool_seats_remaining_at_grant > 0`); buyer plan Scale+ or Enterprise; vendor Org not on paid seller plan; vendor Org not blocked by 365-day same-buyer/vendor rule | Grant code minted; writes `audit_event_grant_id`. Pool counter decremented atomically (Convex txn). |
| `issued` | `invite_sent` | Loops.so dispatch succeeds | Loops.so returns `202 Accepted` within 30 s | Sets `invite_sent_at`. Fallback: 3 retry with exponential backoff; after 5 failures, status flips to `fraud_blocked` with `anti_spam_hold_reason = loops_dispatch_unrecoverable` (Authored Extension). |
| `invite_sent` | `provisioned` | Vendor Billing Admin signs up via grant link | Vendor Org not on paid seller plan at signup; vendor not blocked by SIM | Sets `provisioned_at`, `trial_starts_at = provisioned_at`, `trial_expires_at = trial_starts_at + 30d`, `vendor_org_id`. Activates Seller Starter entitlements. |
| `provisioned` | `in_trial` | Convex scheduled job (same-transaction as provisioned) | Automatic; logical distinction for clarity | Effectively a sub-state of `provisioned` for reporting. Some implementations may collapse. |
| `in_trial` | `converted` | Vendor adds payment method and upgrades to paid Seller plan | Payment method verified by Stripe; `converted_to_plan` set | Sets `converted_at`. Writes Stripe meter event `sourcera_pro_trial_conversion`. Pool counter NOT refunded (expenditure is terminal). |
| `in_trial` | `auto_downgraded` | Day 31 (`now() ≥ trial_expires_at`) with no conversion | Daily Convex scheduled job | Vendor downgraded to Seller Free; 90-day read-only preservation window begins per §45. Writes meter event `sourcera_pro_trial_expired`. |
| `in_trial` | `vendor_declined` | Vendor Billing Admin explicitly declines via in-app action | During the 30-day trial window | Same downgrade as `auto_downgraded` but with explicit vendor attribution. |
| `invite_sent` | `expired_unaccepted` | 30-day invite TTL elapses with no signup | `now() ≥ invite_sent_at + 30d` AND status remains `invite_sent` | Grant closes; pool counter refunded to buyer (Authored Extension: invite-not-accepted is non-expenditure). |
| `issued`, `invite_sent` | `buyer_revoked` | Buyer Billing Admin revokes grant | Status ∈ {`issued`, `invite_sent`} (pre-provisioning only) | Pool counter refunded. Any pending invite tokens invalidated. Vendor notified if invite had been sent. |
| `issued`, `invite_sent` | `fraud_blocked` | Signal Integrity Monitor (C.100) flags | Any SIM rule in `trial_seat_rejection_reason` triggered; `anti_spam_hold_reason` populated | Pool counter refunded. Ops-only un-block via explicit override. |
| `converted`, `auto_downgraded`, `vendor_declined`, `expired_unaccepted`, `buyer_revoked`, `fraud_blocked` | (terminal) | — | Terminal states | Retention per §40.2 pro-trial financial-record rule (Org-life + 7 years). |

**Pool Accounting Invariant.** At any time: `buyer_monthly_pool_issued = count(status in ANY) from grants created within the current buyer_billing_cycle_month`; `buyer_monthly_pool_refunded = count(status in {expired_unaccepted, buyer_revoked, fraud_blocked})`; `buyer_monthly_pool_consumed = buyer_monthly_pool_issued − buyer_monthly_pool_refunded`. Pool-cap enforcement compares `consumed` against the plan limit (5/mo Scale, 15/mo Enterprise per §15.5 Seller Pricing). Refund transitions MUST be reflected in the same Convex transaction as the status write to prevent over-issuance.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Every status transition writes a §4.6 AuditEvent row and updates `audit_event_outcome_id` on terminal transitions.
2. `same_buyer_365d_block_triggered=true` at `issued` create-time returns HTTP 409 `trial_seat_same_buyer_365d_block` (Appendix I) and no pool decrement occurs.
3. `already_paid_block_triggered=true` at `issued` create-time returns HTTP 409 `trial_seat_vendor_already_paid` (Appendix I).
4. Pool cap binding at create time returns HTTP 403 `trial_seat_pool_exhausted` (Appendix I) and no grant row is created.
5. Buyer plan below Scale at create time returns HTTP 403 `trial_seat_buyer_below_scale` (Appendix I).
6. Dual-projection reads: a buyer-console session reading grant state sees `buyer_facing_projection` (omits vendor-side PII beyond vendor Org handle); a seller-console session reading grant state sees `vendor_facing_projection` (omits buyer-side pool internals). Cross-console reads for an unbound caller return HTTP 404.
7. Refund transitions (`expired_unaccepted`, `buyer_revoked`, `fraud_blocked`) MUST atomically increment `buyer_monthly_pool_refunded`; a partial write that increments the pool but does not transition status is a priority-1 incident.
8. Loops.so dispatch fallback: 3 retries (exponential backoff 30s/2m/10m); on final failure, grant transitions to `fraud_blocked` with `anti_spam_hold_reason = loops_dispatch_unrecoverable` and pool refunds.

### L.4 KB Entry Status State Machine {#l.4-kb-entry-status-state-machine}

**Entity.** KBEntry (§22.3.1). **Enum.** `kb_entry_status` (Appendix J): `draft`, `under_review`, `active`, `review_due`, `review_overdue`, `flagged_stale`, `archived`. **Scope.** Seller-Console-only; all transitions reject if the caller's session console is `buyer` or the caller is not Org-bound to the entry's `org_id`.

**Canonical Transitions.** The authoritative transition table lives inline at §22.4.1 (KB Entry Lifecycle). This appendix reproduces the state diagram and the terminal/cascade rules for compendium completeness; for the full conditions per transition, engineering MUST treat §22.4.1 as the source of truth.

**State Diagram:**

draft ──→ under_review ──→ active ──→ review_due ──→ review_overdue ──→ flagged_stale

  │            │             ↑ ↑           │                 │

  │            │             │ │           │                 │

  │            │             │ └───────────┘                 ↓

  │            ↓             │  (seller re-confirm)      archived ──→ (hard delete after deleted_at+30d)

  │          draft (cancel)  │                               ↑

  │                          └─── archived (seller manual) ──┘

  └───────────────────────→ archived (seller discard)

**Terminal & Cascade Rules:**

| Aspect | Rule |
| :---- | :---- |
| Terminal state | `archived` (reversible to `active` via explicit un-archive); hard-delete at `deleted_at + 30d`. |
| Reversibility | All non-terminal states are reversible to `active` via seller re-confirm or edit-and-republish; `archived` → `active` requires explicit un-archive and triggers §22.4.3 re-index. |
| Cascade | Hard-delete cascades to vector index (Voyage) + BM25 index (OpenSearch) in the same Convex transaction per §22.4.2. |
| Console firewall | Any buyer-console session mutation → HTTP 404 `kb_entry_cross_console_access` (Appendix I, existing). |

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. State diagram matches §22.4.1 transition table exactly; any divergence is a priority-1 documentation defect.
2. Daily Convex job (state check) runs ≥ once per 24 h per Org with jitter ≤ 60 min; missed runs page on-call within 2 h.
3. `review_overdue → flagged_stale` MUST remove entry from `kb_retrieve` default `exclude_review_states` in the same commit (§22.8.4.1 Retrieval MCP).

### L.5 KB Document Status State Machine {#l.5-kb-document-status-state-machine}

**Entity.** KBDocument (§22.3.2). **Enum.** `kb_document_status` (Appendix J): `active`, `expired`, `superseded`, `archived`. **Scope.** Seller-Console-only.

**State Diagram:**

active ──→ expired ──→ archived

   │           │

   │           └──→ superseded (when newer version replaces)

   └───────────→ superseded ──→ archived

active ─────────────→ archived (seller manual)

**Complete State Transitions:**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (none) | `active` | Seller uploads document via §22.7 | File passes virus scan + schema validation; `expires_at` optionally set | Initial state. Indexed for `document_library_find` and `doc_attach`. |
| `active` | `expired` | Daily Convex scheduled job | `expires_at IS NOT NULL` AND `now() ≥ expires_at` | Sets `status = expired`. Still discoverable with `include_expired=true` on `document_library_find`; excluded by default. |
| `active` | `superseded` | Seller uploads a new version and sets `prior_version_doc_id` | New document's `prior_version_doc_id` points to this row; new doc status = `active` | Sets `superseded_by_doc_id` on this row (reverse link). `last_used_at` preserved for audit. |
| `expired` | `superseded` | Seller uploads renewal and sets `prior_version_doc_id` | Same as active→superseded but from expired state | Common renewal-cycle pattern (e.g., SOC 2 annual renewal). |
| `active` | `archived` | Seller manual archive | None | Soft delete via `deleted_at`; excluded from retrieval; reversible for 30 days. |
| `expired` | `archived` | Daily Convex job | `now() ≥ expires_at + 13 months` AND `status = expired` | §40.2 retention rule: expired docs kept 13 months for renewal-cycle support, then auto-archived. |
| `superseded` | `archived` | Daily Convex job | `now() ≥ superseded_at + 13 months` | Same retention rule as expired. |
| `archived` | `active` | Seller un-archive within 30 days | Not hard-deleted yet | Triggers §22.4.3 re-index. |
| `archived` | (hard delete) | `deleted_at + 30d` reached (seller manual archive) OR §40.2 retention cutoff for expired/superseded documents | Background reaper | File blob purged from Convex Storage; doc row purged; `evidence_doc_refs` on any KBEntry rows are nulled with dangling-ref cleanup. |

**Terminal & Cascade Rules:**

| Aspect | Rule |
| :---- | :---- |
| Terminal state | `archived` (reversible within 30 days for seller-initiated archive); hard-delete at `deleted_at + 30d`. |
| Supersede chain | `prior_version_doc_id` / `superseded_by_doc_id` form a doubly-linked version chain; traversal must terminate (no cycles). |
| Attach guard | `doc_attach` (§22.8.4.4) MUST re-check status at attach-time; if document transitioned to `expired` or `superseded` between `document_library_find` and `doc_attach`, return HTTP 409 `doc_no_longer_active` (Appendix I, existing). |

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Daily Convex job for `active → expired` runs ≥ once per 24 h per Org; missed runs page on-call within 2 h.
2. `superseded` MUST NOT be set by any path other than `prior_version_doc_id` establishment; manual status-only updates are rejected with `invalid_state_transition`.
3. Hard-delete cascades null out `evidence_doc_refs` arrays on any KBEntry rows referencing the deleted document in the same Convex transaction.
4. Supersede-chain traversal limit: MAX 50 hops per chain; deeper chains are rejected with `supersede_chain_too_long` (Authored Extension — flagged in RECONCILIATION.md).
5. §45.1 financial-record retention exemption: DPAs, insurance certificates, and SOC 2 reports with `category ∈ {dpa, insurance, soc2}` are retained Org-life + 7 years even after `archived`, per financial/audit exemption.

### L.6 Target Account State Machine {#l.6-target-account-state-machine}

**Entity.** Target Account (§4.3.20). **Enum.** `target_account_state_enum` (Appendix J): `prospect`, `qualified`, `solicited`, `bidding`, `shortlisted`, `finalist`, `disqualified`, `superseded`. **Scope.** Workspace-scoped, buyer console.

**State Definitions:**

- `prospect` — Added to workspace; fit score may be null or populated; no seller-side action.
- `qualified` — Buyer has reviewed fit score and marked account worth soliciting; still no seller-side contact.
- `solicited` — Bid Workspace opened; seller has been invited; Console Bridge Event `workspace_invitation_propagated` emitted.
- `bidding` — Seller has accepted EOI and begun responding; bid in progress.
- `shortlisted` — Buyer has moved this account to the shortlist for Selection Report consideration.
- `finalist` — Account appears in the current Selection Report Draft's `finalist_account_ids[]`.
- `disqualified` — Terminal. Account rejected by buyer; cascades to Bid Workspace disqualification per §4.7.2.
- `superseded` — Terminal. Account merged into another account on duplicate detection; `superseded_by_account_id` populated.

**Complete State Transitions:**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (none) | `prospect` | Workspace member adds account via Discovery Run accept, CSV import, manual add, marketplace browse, or referral acceptance | Marketplace-domain match; unique `(workspace_id, seller_org_id)` | Initial state. `added_at`, `added_by_user_id` stamped. |
| `prospect` | `qualified` | Buyer marks account as "qualified" via UI action | Workspace member with `evaluator` or higher role | Emits PostHog event `target_account_qualified`. |
| `prospect` | `disqualified` | Buyer manually disqualifies before soliciting | `disqualification_reason` set | Terminal. No seller-side notification (account was never solicited). |
| `qualified` | `solicited` | Buyer opens a Bid Workspace for this account | Bid Workspace created; `bid_workspace_id` populated | Emits Console Bridge Event `workspace_invitation_propagated`; seller receives invite per §4.4 / §6.28.2. |
| `solicited` | `bidding` | Seller accepts EOI / begins bid response | Seller-side bid state transitions to `in_progress` | State synced via Console Bridge Event. |
| `solicited` | `disqualified` | Seller declines bid OR buyer withdraws invitation | `disqualification_reason ∈ {seller_declined_bid, buyer_discretion}` | Cascades to Bid Workspace cancellation. |
| `bidding` | `shortlisted` | Buyer moves account to shortlist | Workspace member with `evaluator` or higher role; bid response partial or complete | Shortlist position recorded separately. |
| `bidding` | `disqualified` | Buyer disqualifies during bid OR seller withdraws | `disqualification_reason` set | Cascades to Bid Workspace per §4.7.2. |
| `shortlisted` | `finalist` | Account added to Selection Report Draft's `finalist_account_ids[]` | Selection Report Draft in `drafting` or `review` state | `selection_report_inclusion_rank` populated. |
| `shortlisted` | `disqualified` | Buyer removes from consideration | `disqualification_reason ∈ {buyer_discretion, compliance_fail, pricing_out_of_band}` | Terminal. |
| `finalist` | `shortlisted` | Buyer removes from finalist roster before Selection Report finalization | Selection Report Draft still `drafting` or `review` | `selection_report_inclusion_rank` cleared. |
| `finalist` | `disqualified` | Buyer disqualifies finalist (rare; late-stage compliance issue) | Selection Report Draft still unfinalized | Terminal. |
| any non-terminal | `superseded` | Duplicate detected and merged | `superseded_by_account_id` populated; merge approved by workspace admin | Terminal. Preserves history; queries follow the supersede chain. |
| `disqualified` | `qualified` | Ops override (rare; compliance fix) | Ops-initiated with audit note; requires `ops_compliance_admin` role | Emits Audit Event severity `high`. Not available to customer roles. |

**Terminal & Cascade Rules:**

| Aspect | Rule |
| :---- | :---- |
| Terminal states | `disqualified`, `superseded`. `finalist` becomes effectively terminal once the Selection Report is finalized (state-locked by application layer). |
| Selection Report finalization | On Selection Report Draft → `finalized`, all `finalist_account_ids[]` members have their Target Account state locked (no further transitions permitted except via Ops override). |
| Disqualification cascade | Target Account → `disqualified` cascades: Bid Workspace → `disqualified`, Vendor Disqualification Record (§4.7.2) created, Console Bridge Event `disqualification_issued` emitted. |
| Supersede cascade | On merge, the superseded row's `bid_workspace_id` is pointed at the merged account's bid workspace (if any); Shortlist and finalist references are updated transactionally. |
| Concurrent state mutations | Optimistic concurrency on `(id, state_transitioned_at)`; second writer retries; second writer rejected on terminal-state collision with HTTP 409 `target_account_state_terminal`. |

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Every state transition MUST be executed by the state-machine handler; direct state mutations are rejected.
2. `state_transitioned_at` and `state_transitioned_by_user_id` MUST be stamped on every transition.
3. Transition to `solicited` MUST require successful creation of a linked Bid Workspace in the same transaction.
4. Transition to `disqualified` MUST require `disqualification_reason` to be set.
5. Transition to `finalist` MUST require the account to already be in the Selection Report Draft's `finalist_account_ids[]` array.
6. Ops override transitions MUST emit an Audit Event (§4.6.1) with severity `high` and populate `notes` with the override rationale.
7. The supersede chain MUST terminate (no cycles); a cycle check is enforced at merge time.

### L.7 Defense View State Machine {#l.7-defense-view-state-machine}

**Entity.** DefenseView (§13.11.7). **Enum.** `defense_view_lifecycle_state` (Appendix J — registered in this phase): `generated_unopened`, `opened`, `regenerated_unopened`, `archived`. **Scope.** Buyer-Console-only; Workspace-scoped; one-to-one with the parent `SelectionReport` row.

**State Diagram:**

(none) ──→ generated_unopened ──→ opened

                                    │

                                    ↓

                         regenerated_unopened ──→ opened

                                    ↓

  generated_unopened / opened / regenerated_unopened ──→ archived ──→ (purged per §40.2)

**Complete State Transitions:**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| (none) | `generated_unopened` | First `GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/defense-view` for a Workspace with Phase ≥ 12 and a finalized `SelectionReport` / `SelectionRecord` row | `defense_view_generate` AIOperation invoked successfully; `DefenseView` row written transactionally; `selection_record_hash` stamped from the current `SelectionRecord.selection_record_sha256` | Initial state. Emits `defense_view.generated` (Appendix C) and the corresponding Appendix G PostHog event. `opened_at IS NULL`, `regenerated_count = 0`, `first_regeneration_at IS NULL`. |
| `generated_unopened` | `opened` | Operator opens the Defense View surface (the first `GET` that hit the `(none) → generated_unopened` transition stamps `opened_at` in the same handler; idempotent on subsequent reads) | First-write-wins on `opened_at`; subsequent operator opens are no-ops on `opened_at` | Drives `defense_view_generate` OutcomeContract `accepted` signal eligibility (§13.11.5). |
| `opened` | `regenerated_unopened` | Either (a) hash mismatch on subsequent `GET` caused by a superseding pre-closure Selection Record, or (b) explicit `POST /v1/workspaces/{id}/defense-view/regenerate` | `regeneration_throttle` not active (≤ 1 regeneration per 5 min per Workspace); `defense_view_generate` AIOperation invoked successfully; `regenerated_count` incremented; `opened_at` reset to NULL; `first_regeneration_at` stamped on first regeneration only; `selection_record_hash` updated | Emits `defense_view.regenerated` (Appendix C). When the trigger is hash mismatch, additionally emits PostHog event `defense_view.regenerated_due_to_source_change` and surfaces the "regenerated due to source change" chip on next render. |
| `generated_unopened` | `regenerated_unopened` | Same as above, but operator regenerates before opening (rare; e.g., low-confidence retry) | Same as above | Edge case; same emission semantics. |
| `regenerated_unopened` | `opened` | Operator opens the Defense View post-regeneration | `opened_at` stamped; idempotent on subsequent reads | Drives `accepted` signal evaluation against the new `generated_at`. |
| `regenerated_unopened` | `regenerated_unopened` (self-loop) | Subsequent regenerations before any open | `regeneration_throttle` honored | `regenerated_count` increments per regeneration. Each regeneration emits `defense_view.regenerated`. |
| `generated_unopened` / `opened` / `regenerated_unopened` | `archived` | Workspace closure cascade per §10.13.6 | `Workspace.status` transitions to `closed` OR Workspace cancellation grace expires per §10.14.4 | `deleted_at` stamped via cascade. Subsequent reads return HTTP 404 `defense_view_archived_with_workspace`. The cached PDF (if any was downloaded prior to archive) remains valid as a static artifact. |
| `archived` | (purged) | Retention boundary per §40.2 | §40.2 plan-tier retention elapsed from `Workspace.archived_at` | Hard purge. PII anonymization rules per §6.8.2 applied to `created_by`, `updated_by`. Vendor-name strings within `cfo_summary_md`, `recommendation_text`, `top_reasons`, `material_risks` follow the §6.8.3 vendor-data handling (vendors are not Sourcera users; not subject to user PII redaction). |

**Rejected Transitions (non-exhaustive; enforced server-side).** `archived → opened`, `archived → regenerated_unopened`, `archived → generated_unopened`, cross-console initiation from seller session → rejected with HTTP 404 `defense_view_cross_console_access` (Appendix I — registered in this phase; non-leak). Direct mutation of `DefenseView` fields outside the state-machine handler is rejected with `invalid_state_transition`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Every state transition writes one row to the §4.6 AuditEvent table with `entity_type=defense_view` and the new state in the diff payload, including the `aioperation_id` for transitions caused by generation/regeneration.
2. A Convex reactive query observing `DefenseView` state MUST see a state change within p95 ≤ 500 ms of commit (§7.5.3 reactivity SLO).
3. Attempting `archived → opened` or any reverse transition returns HTTP 409 `invalid_state_transition` and leaves state unchanged.
4. The cascade from Workspace closure (`Workspace.status → closed`) is atomic with the Workspace transition; a partial cascade leaving a `DefenseView` row in `opened` while the Workspace is `archived` is a deploy-time defect (CI gate `defense_view_cascade_atomic`).
5. Session-console firewall: any read or mutation attempted from a seller-console session returns HTTP 404 `defense_view_cross_console_access`; the row's existence is not leaked.
6. Cross-Org session reads return HTTP 404 with the same error code; cross-Org existence is not leaked.
7. The `regeneration_throttle` (≤ 1 regeneration per 5 min per Workspace) is enforced at the API layer; the handler MUST NOT advance state on a throttled call.
8. Failure-recovery retries (i.e., regenerations following a Sonnet generation failure where the AIOperation was reversed) are exempt from `regeneration_throttle` per §13.11.12 failure mode 1; the exemption is recorded in the AuditEvent diff payload.

v7.2.0-REM Phase 10 catalog-completeness sweep — closes the Appendix L portion of the §12 cluster (catalog-class P1 defects **D-12-002**, **D-4.3-006**). The §12 pipeline was authored as prose across §12.3.1 / §12.4.1 / §12.5.1 / §12.6.1 / §12.7.2; this is the canonical `From / To / Trigger / Conditions / Notes` table. Status enum `policy_ingestion_job_status` registered in Appendix J `v7.2.0-REM Phase 10` block. Each transition names its Appendix C `policy.ingestion.*` webhook.

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |

Persistent-partial re-upload merge is D-12-007 (AC-class; out of catalog scope). |

### L.11 Pipeline Phase State Machine (§10) {#l-11-pipeline-phase-state-machine}

v7.2.0-REM Pipeline Phase state-machine reconciliation (closes D-4.2-008). Enum: Appendix J `pipeline_phase`. Scope: Buyer Workspace only; seller-side Bid Workspace reads projected phase via §25 Console Bridge and cannot mutate buyer pipeline phase directly.

**State Diagram:**

`phase_1_stakeholder_alignment` -> `phase_2_requirement_definition` -> `phase_3_use_case_validation` -> `phase_4_vendor_discovery` -> `phase_5_vendor_outreach` -> `phase_6_vendor_bidding` -> `phase_7_response_refinement` -> `phase_8_due_diligence` -> `phase_9_final_clarifications` -> `phase_10_team_scoring` -> `phase_11_score_review` -> `phase_12_selection` -> `phase_13_contract_closure` (terminal)

**Complete State Transitions:**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `(none)` | `phase_1_stakeholder_alignment` | Workspace created and first evaluation opened | Workspace `status=active`; `evaluation_owner_mode` resolved per §2.8 / §4.3.1; caller can create Workspace per §5.11 | Initial pipeline phase. Draft Workspace state remains represented by `workspace_status=draft`, not a `pipeline_phase` enum value. |
| `phase_1_stakeholder_alignment` | `phase_2_requirement_definition` | Workspace Owner clicks "Ready for Requirements" | §10.2 Phase Gate Rules satisfied; stakeholder acceptance is not required per §10.2 | Writes `phase_advanced`; emits `workspace.phase_advanced`; §10.16 idempotency applies. |
| `phase_2_requirement_definition` | `phase_3_use_case_validation` | Team Lead clicks "All Requirements Approved" | §10.3 Phase Gate Rules satisfied | Requirements enter Use Case assignment flow. |
| `phase_3_use_case_validation` | `phase_4_vendor_discovery` | Workspace Owner clicks "Use Cases Validated" | §10.4 Phase Gate Rules satisfied | Vendor discovery begins. |
| `phase_4_vendor_discovery` | `phase_5_vendor_outreach` | Workspace Owner issues first formal Invitation to Bid from the §10.5 Vendor Invitations step | At least one shortlisted vendor exists; ITB dispatch is logged in Workspace audit trail; Marketplace Listing is marked `open_for_bidding` per §10.5 | Engine split of the combined §10.5 Phase 4-5 narrative. |
| `phase_5_vendor_outreach` | `phase_6_vendor_bidding` | Workspace Owner clicks "Vendor List Finalized" | Combined §10.5 Phase Gate Rules satisfied: vendor invitations sent, at least one vendor confirmed intent to bid, shortlist finalized | Vendor list freezes for Phase 6. |
| `phase_6_vendor_bidding` | `phase_7_response_refinement` | Workspace Owner clicks "Bidding Closed" | §10.6 Phase Gate Rules satisfied, including `bidding_close_at >= phase_6_entered_at + 7 calendar days` per §10.6 | Below-floor close returns HTTP 422 `phase_6_bidding_close_below_minimum_window`. |
| `phase_7_response_refinement` | `phase_8_due_diligence` | Workspace Owner clicks "Refinement Complete" | §10.7 Phase Gate Rules satisfied | Vendor responses remain versioned; final lock occurs after Phase 8 per §10.7. |
| `phase_8_due_diligence` | `phase_9_final_clarifications` | Workspace Owner clicks "Due Diligence Complete" | §10.8 Phase Gate Rules satisfied | Demo / due-diligence artifacts retained in Workspace audit. |
| `phase_9_final_clarifications` | `phase_10_team_scoring` | Workspace Owner clicks "Final Clarifications Complete" | §10.9 Phase Gate Rules satisfied | Requirement amendments and Vendor Response submissions are locked. |
| `phase_10_team_scoring` | `phase_11_score_review` | Workspace Owner clicks "Scoring Complete" | §10.10 Phase Gate Rules satisfied | Scores remain mutable in Phase 11; score immutability begins at Phase 12 entry. |
| `phase_11_score_review` | `phase_12_selection` | Workspace Owner clicks "Scores Finalized" | §10.11 Phase Gate Rules satisfied | Entering Phase 12 freezes scores per §10.10 / §10.12. |
| `phase_12_selection` | `phase_13_contract_closure` | Workspace Owner clicks "Selection Complete" | §10.12 Phase Gate Rules satisfied; Selection Report reviewed and approved when approval is required | Phase 13 is terminal for pipeline advancement. Approval rejection is handled inside the Phase 12 approval-workflow sub-state and does not create a backward pipeline transition. |
| `phase_13_contract_closure` | `(terminal)` | Terminal phase reached | §10.13 Phase Gate Rules satisfied; Workspace closure confirmed by Workspace Owner | Further advancement returns HTTP 422 `phase_advancement_terminal_phase_no_advance`; Workspace lifecycle changes after closure are governed by §10.14 / Appendix E. |

**Rejected Transitions.** Backward transitions return HTTP 422 `phase_advancement_backward_transition_forbidden`. Non-adjacent forward jumps, unmet gates, or attempts to bypass §10.16 validation return HTTP 422 `gate_validation_failed` with `error.details.failed_checks[]` per §32.6. Concurrent advancement attempts return HTTP 409 `phase_advancement_concurrent_request_in_flight`. Seller-console attempts to mutate buyer `pipeline_phase` fail closed under the §7.2 console firewall.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. The only legal forward transitions are the adjacent rows in the table above; out-of-table transitions are rejected server-side before any `pipeline_phase` write.
2. Every successful transition MUST execute through §10.16, require `Idempotency-Key`, write AuditEvent `phase_advanced` or `phase_advanced_with_unmet_gates`, emit `workspace.phase_advanced`, and project the §4.7.1 Console Bridge Event with Appendix J `pipeline_phase` values.
3. `pipeline_stage_id` integer storage MUST map 1:1 to the Appendix J `pipeline_phase` value for integers 1-13; draft / closed / archived are Workspace lifecycle states, not additional `pipeline_phase` enum values.
4. Phase 4 and Phase 5 MUST remain distinct engine states even though §10.5 renders them in one combined narrative block; the Phase 4 -> Phase 5 transition is triggered by first ITB dispatch.
5. Phase 12 approval rejection MUST NOT move the Workspace backward; it remains in `phase_12_selection` and is handled by the Approval Workflow state machine in Appendix L.12.
6. Phase 13 is terminal for pipeline advancement; post-closure cancellation, recovery, archive, and deletion are Workspace lifecycle transitions governed by §10.14 / Appendix E.

### L.12 Approval Workflow State Machine (§10.12 / §4.3.25) {#l-12-approval-workflow-state-machine}

v7.2.0-REM Selection Entity and Approval Workflow pass — closes D-4.2-021. Enum: Appendix J `approval_workflow_status`. Scope: Buyer Workspace Phase 12 only. This state machine is deliberately a sub-state of `phase_12_selection`; it never mutates `Workspace.pipeline_phase` backward.

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `(none)` | `pending` | Selection Report routed for approval | Org approval policy applies; §4.3.23 Selection Report exists; caller can route per §5.11 `approval_workflow` | `routed_at` stamped; approver queue receives item. |
| `pending` | `approved` | Approver accepts | Approver has required role per `required_approver_role`; report version matches `current_submission_version` | Sets `decision_at`; Phase 12 gate may pass and §10.16 may advance to Phase 13. Terminal for that report version. |
| `pending` | `request_changes` | Approver requests changes | `decision_reason` non-empty | Workspace stays in `phase_12_selection`; scores remain immutable; Workspace Owner can revise non-score report content and resubmit. |
| `pending` | `rejected` | Approver rejects | `decision_reason` non-empty | Workspace stays in `phase_12_selection`; scores remain immutable. If score changes are required, the only path is §10.14 cancellation and a new evaluation. |
| `request_changes` | `pending` | Workspace Owner resubmits | `resubmission_count += 1`; revised Selection Report version created; no score mutation | `current_submission_version` increments; prior decision remains in AuditEvent history. |
| `rejected` | `pending` | Workspace Owner resubmits without score mutation | Same as above; permitted only for report/rationale changes | Does not imply a backward pipeline transition. |
| `approved` | `(terminal)` | Phase 12 -> Phase 13 advancement succeeds | §10.16 commits Phase 13 | Approval Workflow row remains read-only and joins the Selection Record bundle. |

**Illegal transitions.** `approved -> pending`, `approved -> rejected`, `request_changes -> approved` without resubmission, and `rejected -> approved` without resubmission are rejected with `invalid_state_transition`. Any transition that attempts to unlock or mutate Score rows returns `scores_immutable_phase_12_plus`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Approval Workflow decisions MUST write an AuditEvent with previous status, new status, approver, `current_submission_version`, and `decision_reason` when present.
2. `request_changes` and `rejected` MUST NOT mutate `Workspace.pipeline_phase`, `pipeline_stage_id`, score rows, or score locks.
3. Phase 12 -> Phase 13 advancement MUST be rejected with `gate_validation_failed` while a required Approval Workflow status is `pending`, `request_changes`, or `rejected`.
4. Resubmission MUST increment `resubmission_count` and `current_submission_version`; the prior decision remains audit-visible.
5. The §M.5 gate `approval_workflow_state_machine_canonicality` MUST fail if §10.12, §4.3.25, Appendix J `approval_workflow_status`, or this table drift.

### L.13 Q&A Thread Status State Machine (§18.3.1) {#l-13-qa-thread-status-state-machine}

v7.2.0-REM Phase 4.9 Q&A Thread normalization pass. Entity: Q&A Thread (§18.3.1). Enum: Appendix J `qa_thread_status` (`open`, `closed`, `archived`, `orphaned`). Scope: Buyer Workspace source row with seller projection reads through §4.4.2.1 / §24.1.1.

**State Diagram:**

`(none)` -> `open` -> `closed` -> `archived`

`open` -> `orphaned` -> `archived`

`closed` -> `open` is permitted before Phase 8.

**Complete State Transitions:**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `(none)` | `open` | POST `/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/qa-threads` | Workspace phase is 6 or 7; caller has Buyer Workspace create permission OR invited seller compose permission; vendor question cap not exceeded; NDA/visibility predicate passes when seller-authored | Creates Q&A Thread + first Q&A Post + Q&A Mention rows atomically. Emits `qa_thread.created`; creates Unread Markers. |
| `open` | `closed` | Buyer closes thread OR Workspace enters Phase 8 | Caller is Workspace Owner/Admin/Use Case Lead OR phase auto-close job; no in-flight post transaction remains uncommitted | Sets `closed_at`, `closed_by`; seller compose disabled but read may continue through §24.1.1. |
| `closed` | `open` | Buyer reopens thread | Workspace phase is still 6 or 7; caller is Workspace Owner/Admin/Use Case Lead; thread not archived or orphaned | Clears `closed_at`; emits AuditEvent. |
| `open` | `orphaned` | Vendor disqualification cascade or addressed seller loses compose authority | §25.3 disqualification cascade, Bid Workspace revoke, NDA revocation without exception, or seller Org removal from Workspace | Seller projection becomes read-only or suppressed per §24.1.1. Prior buyer-visible audit trail remains; no seller reply allowed. |
| `closed` | `orphaned` | Vendor disqualification cascade after close | Same as above | Preserves close history and marks seller compose authority permanently unavailable. |
| `open` / `closed` / `orphaned` | `archived` | Workspace soft-delete, Q&A Thread delete, or retention cascade | Caller has Workspace Owner/Admin role for manual archive OR system cascade per §10.14 / §40.2 | Sets `deleted_at`; cascades Q&A Post and Q&A Mention soft-delete; emits `qa_thread.archived`. |
| `archived` | `(purged)` | §40.2 retention boundary | 30-day cascade window elapsed and no finalized Selection Report / legal hold exemption applies | Hard purge Thread/Post/Mention rows and linked non-exempt attachments per §40.2. |

**Rejected transitions.** `archived -> open`, `archived -> closed`, `orphaned -> open` without a disqualification reversal, `PUBLIC -> PRIVATE` visibility mutation, phase-out-of-window post creation, and seller direct-read of the buyer source row are rejected before mutation. Error codes: `qa_thread_phase_gated`, `qa_thread_visibility_flip_disallowed`, `qa_thread_cross_workspace_access_denied`, or `qa_thread_nda_inactive_visibility_denied` as applicable.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Every legal transition writes a §4.6 AuditEvent row with `entity_type=qa_thread`, prior status, new status, actor id or system actor, and the triggering Workspace phase.
2. Thread creation MUST atomically create first Q&A Post, parsed Q&A Mention rows, Unread Marker fan-out, and Appendix C `qa_thread.created`; partial creation is rolled back.
3. Phase 8 auto-close MUST close all open Q&A Threads before seller compose surfaces render read-only; race with seller post submission resolves by serializable transaction order.
4. Vendor disqualification MUST transition addressed PRIVATE threads to `orphaned` and suppress seller compose authority within the same cascade that updates §4.4.2.1 projection state.
5. `closed -> open` MUST reject after Phase 8 with `qa_thread_phase_gated`.
6. Manual archive MUST cascade Q&A Post and Q&A Mention `deleted_at` stamps in the same transaction and preserve §40.2 retention eligibility for finalized Selection Report / legal-hold evidence.
7. Seller-console direct reads of buyer source rows MUST return HTTP 404 `qa_thread_cross_workspace_access_denied`; seller-visible Q&A reads use projection APIs only.

### L.14 Use Case Status State Machine (§2.2 / §4.3.3) {#l-14-use-case-status-state-machine}

v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 Method P1 pass. Entity: Use Case (§4.3.3). Enum: Appendix J `use_case_status` (`drafted`, `validated`, `phase_locked`, `soft_deleted`). Scope: Buyer Workspace source row only; seller-visible grouping reads are projections emitted through §4.7.1 Console Bridge Event and §25.5.7. Authored Extension — requires human sign-off (AE-V72REM-PH2-METHOD-LIFECYCLE-01).

**State Diagram:**

`(none)` -> `drafted` -> `validated` -> `phase_locked`

`drafted` -> `soft_deleted`

`validated` -> `soft_deleted`

`phase_locked` -> `soft_deleted` only through the Phase 6 Amendment Protocol / Workspace archive cascade.

`soft_deleted` -> `drafted` during the UI undo window when the prior status was `drafted`; `soft_deleted` -> `validated` during the UI undo window when the prior status was `validated`.

**Complete State Transitions:**

| From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `(none)` | `drafted` | Use Case created manually, imported, duplicated, or materialized from EvalStarter | Workspace is in Phase 1, 2, or 3; caller can create Use Cases per §5.11; write does not exceed §34.1.1 cell **Use Cases per Workspace** / §39 | Default status. Emits `use_case_status_changed` with `old_status=null`, `new_status=drafted`. |
| `drafted` | `validated` | Workspace Owner / Admin / Use Case Lead marks Use Case ready OR Workspace advances through Phase 3 gate | `name` populated, no over-cap child Requirement set, all child Requirements reference the Use Case, no unresolved decomposition validator errors | Represents Method-level validation, not seller visibility. |
| `validated` | `drafted` | Buyer edits a validation-critical field before phase lock | Workspace is before `phase_6_vendor_bidding`; caller can edit Use Cases per §5.11 | Clears validation marker; re-validation required before Phase 3 gate can pass. |
| `validated` | `phase_locked` | Workspace advances into Phase 6 Vendor Bidding | §10.16 phase advancement succeeds; child Requirement release set has passed Appendix A `draft -> active` transition or is explicitly excluded | Seller-visible grouping becomes governed by Console Bridge projection; subsequent structural changes use §10.6 Amendment Protocol. |
| `drafted` / `validated` | `soft_deleted` | User deletes Use Case | Workspace before Phase 6 OR no child Requirement has seller-visible projection; if child Requirements exist, cascade soft-delete child Requirements in the same transaction or reject before mutation | Sets `deleted_at`, `deleted_by`, `pre_delete_status`; UI undo window starts. |
| `phase_locked` | `soft_deleted` | Phase 6 Amendment Protocol removes Use Case OR Workspace archive / delete cascade | Amendment rationale captured per §10.6 OR parent Workspace lifecycle cascade applies; seller projections updated through §4.7.1 | Manual delete outside the amendment handler is rejected. |
| `soft_deleted` | `drafted` / `validated` | User clicks undo within the 10-second delete undo window OR Ops restore during 30-day retention window | `pre_delete_status ∈ {drafted, validated}`; parent Workspace not archived; plan cap still admits the restored row | Restores prior non-terminal status and clears `deleted_at`, `deleted_by`, `pre_delete_status`. |
| `soft_deleted` | `(purged)` | §40.2 retention boundary reached | Parent Workspace purge reaches child Use Cases OR no finalized Selection Report / legal hold exemption applies | Hard purge cascades to child Requirement rows not retained for procurement defensibility. |

**Rejected Transitions.** `soft_deleted -> phase_locked`, `phase_locked -> validated`, direct `drafted -> phase_locked`, seller-console mutation attempts, over-cap restores, and any structural change after Phase 6 that bypasses §10.6 are rejected with HTTP 409 `use_case_invalid_state_transition` or HTTP 403 `plan_limit_exceeded` as applicable.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. Every Use Case row MUST carry `status ∈ {drafted, validated, phase_locked, soft_deleted}` and the status value MUST match Appendix J `use_case_status`.
2. Every status transition MUST write a §4.6 AuditEvent and emit PostHog `use_case_status_changed` within 500 ms of commit.
3. Phase 3 -> Phase 4 advancement MUST reject while any non-deleted Use Case in the Workspace has `status=drafted` and no explicit skip-with-warning path is active under §2.8 Single-Operator Mode.
4. Phase 6 entry MUST transition all non-deleted validated Use Cases to `phase_locked` in the same transaction that activates released Requirements per Appendix A.
5. Deleting a Use Case with child Requirements MUST either cascade soft-delete those Requirements in the same transaction or reject before parent mutation; no parent-only delete is permitted.
6. A restore from `soft_deleted` MUST re-check §34.1.1 / §39 Use Case and Requirement caps before clearing `deleted_at`; over-cap restore returns `plan_limit_exceeded`.
7. Seller-console sessions cannot mutate Use Case state and cannot infer a hidden Use Case through error detail; seller reads continue through Console Bridge projections only.
