## Appendix M — Surface/Engine Mapping {#appendix-m-surface-engine-mapping}

Appendix M is the canonical contract enforcing Principle 9 (Master Spec §3.13 — Surface Simplicity, Engine Complexity). Every engine concept that exists anywhere in the corpus has a corresponding row here mapping it to a surface metaphor, **or** an explicit "internal-only, never surfaced" entry that documents why it stays inside the engine. Adding an engine concept to the spec — a new entity in §4, a new role in §5, a new capability in §21.4 / §22.10, a new feature flag, a new state in any state machine, a new plan-gated feature in §34, a new webhook in §31, a new API endpoint in §32 — without adding a row to Appendix M in the same change is a CI-gate failure (see Phase 14.18 enforcement). Every UX surface authored in `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` (and every future surface-authoring phase: Phase 14.4 Single-Operator Mode, Phase 14.5 Defense View, Phase 14.6 Solo pricing tier / Pipeline Surface Compression, Phase 14.7 Buyer Maya Onboarding & Per-Vertical Eval Starters, Phase 14.x Marketplace-as-RFP-Exchange — phase number to be reassigned) cross-references the relevant Appendix M row.

The contract is bidirectional: the row binds the surface to the engine concept (so engineering knows which entity / state / event the UI is reading), and it binds the engine concept to the surface (so the spec author cannot ship a feature that has no surface story or no documented reason for being internal-only).

#### M.1.1 Column legend (Phase V11 remediation) {#m-1-1-column-legend}

The fourth column is named **`Tier visibility`** per the Phase V11 remediation pass (D-11.1-010 column-semantics clarification). The pre-V11 column header `Hidden from tier(s)` carried a negative semantic (tiers listed = hidden from those tiers) that collided with the special value `All` (legend defined `All` as "visible on every paid and free plan on the relevant console" — positive semantic). The V11 amendment adopts a single positive semantic across all cells:

- **Tier list** (e.g., `Bs, sSo`) = surface is **visible to those tiers only**.
- **`All`** = surface is visible to **all** plan tiers on the relevant console (positive; the same meaning as pre-V11).
- **`All paid in Team Mode; surface-suppressed (engine-only) when Workspace.evaluation_owner_mode=solo per §2.8`** = explicit Solo-suppression annotation per §2.8.
- **`Internal-only, never surfaced`** = no customer-visible surface exists; engine-only construct. This is the canonical sentinel value emitted by `@appendix-m-internal-only:` override auto-row-generation per §M.4.4.3.
- **`—`** = not applicable (concept is console-scoped to the other side).

The §5.11 Feature Access Matrix governs *who can act* on a surface; this column governs *who sees the surface at all*. A tier that is NOT listed in a Tier-visibility cell renders no surface for that plan (the user does not see the affordance — not "sees a disabled state"). Tier abbreviations: **F** = Buyer Free, **Bs** = Buyer Solo (Phase 14.9), **St** = Business Starter, **Gr** = Business Growth, **Sc** = Business Scale, **Ent** = Buyer Enterprise; **sF** = Seller Free, **sSo** = Seller Solo (Phase 14.9), **sSt** = Seller Starter, **sGr** = Seller Growth, **sSc** = Seller Scale, **sEnt** = Seller Enterprise.

The pre-V11 column header `Hidden from tier(s)` is retired. Existing rows whose cells use the pre-V11 semantic (i.e., listing tiers to indicate hidden-from-those-tiers) are mechanically rewritten to the positive semantic in the Phase 11.5 backfill pass (AE-V11-04). Until that mechanical rewrite lands, the `appendix_m_tier_visibility_smoke` runtime gate (§M.5 Phase 14.2 cluster) tests the **canonical positive semantic** — any row whose authored cell deviates fails the smoke test. The reader-of-existing-rows interpretation rule: if a row's cell appears to enumerate `Bs, sSo` (Solo tiers only), the surface is **visible to those tiers**; if a row's cell appears to enumerate `Internal-only, never surfaced`, the surface is engine-only.

#### M.1.2 Companion-document anchor syntax (Phase V11 remediation) {#m-1-2-companion-doc-anchors}

Per the Phase V11 remediation pass (D-11.4-003 companion-doc anchor schema), the `Spec home` cell may cite a companion document anchor using the syntax:

```
Companion: <doc-filename>.md §<anchor>
```

Example:

```
Companion: UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md §5.2.19 PipelineSurface
```

The pre-V11 row at the original line 49301 (`UX Design §Patterns.Navigation`) is the singular existing companion-doc M.1 row; it is rewritten to canonical form `Companion: UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md §Patterns.Navigation` in the Phase 11.5 backfill pass. The `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` CI gate at §M.4.2 trigger #1 / #4 recognizes the `Companion: ` prefix as a valid `Spec home` cell binding for companion-doc engine concepts; the `appendix_m_no_orphan_engine_concept` (§M.5 Phase 14.2 cluster) gate resolves `Companion: <doc>.md §<anchor>` cells against the companion document's existing anchor set (parsed at CI time from the same spec repo).

Companion-document engine concepts that warrant M.1 rows are enumerated at `_audit/SURFACE_ENGINE_TRACE.md` §5.2 case (b) and queued for the AE-V11-04 backfill pack: ~25 UX Design rows, ~10 retired KB Engineering Spec rows (where the spec content survived in §22), ~8 Pricing companion rows.

### M.2 Process Gates

The following gates bind every subsequent integration phase and every post-v7.1 surface authoring change.

1. **Surface/Engine row required on every engine-concept addition.** Any change that introduces a new entity, role, state-machine state, capability, plan-gated feature, webhook, API endpoint, or named engine concept anywhere in the Master Spec MUST add a corresponding row to Appendix M in the same change. The row may be an "Internal-only, never surfaced" entry if the concept is engine-only — but the entry MUST exist. Phases that author new surfaces (14.4, 14.5, 14.6, 14.7, 14.8, and beyond) MUST update the relevant Appendix M row from "forward reference" status to a tightened, surface-bound description in the same change that authors the surface.

2. **First-30-Seconds Test as surface-authoring quality gate.** Every UX surface authored in `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` (or any future surface-authoring artifact) MUST be evaluated against the First-30-Seconds Test (§3.13 Acid Test): "Would a panicked first-timer understand this surface element in the first 30 seconds with no training?" Surfaces that fail the test are returned for redesign before being approved into the spec. The test itself is authored in Phase 14.17.

3. **Adversarial review pass — Appendix M coverage as a P0 check.** The adversarial review pass authored in Phase 14.19 audits Appendix M coverage as a priority-0 check. Any engine concept enumerated in §13.10, §17.8, §20.7, §22.17, §27, §34, §44, or any other acceptance-criteria block that is not represented by a row in Appendix M is a P0 review failure.

4. **CI gate: `appendix_m_engine_to_surface_completeness`.** A deploy-time validator (authored in Phase 14.18) traverses the Master Spec, extracts every engine concept (entities in §4.x; roles in §5.x; state-machine entries in Appendices A, D, E, L; capabilities in §21.4 / §22.10; plan-gated features in §34.1; webhooks in §31; API endpoints in §32; PostHog events in Appendix G) and asserts that each one resolves to either (a) a row in Appendix M with a surface metaphor, or (b) a row in Appendix M flagged "Internal-only, never surfaced." A concept absent from Appendix M is a CI failure.

5. **CI gate: `appendix_m_no_inline_engine_concepts_in_ux_spec`.** `UX_Design_of_Sourcera.md` and any subsequent surface-authoring artifact MUST cite the relevant Appendix M row by anchor for every surface it authors. A surface that names an engine concept inline (e.g., "the user sees their `pipeline_stage_id`") without an Appendix M cross-reference is a CI failure.

6. **Tier visibility integrity.** The "Hidden from tier(s)" column in Appendix M is the canonical contract for surface-level tier gating. The §5.11 Feature Access Matrix governs *who can act* on a surface; this column governs *who sees the surface at all*. A surface that appears for a tier listed in this column is a P0 defect. Phase 14.18 ships a smoke-test pack that flips a test Org through every tier and asserts the surface is hidden where Appendix M says it should be hidden.

7. **Forward-reference rows expire on phase landing.** Rows marked "Forward reference. Row will be tightened when Phase X.Y lands." MUST be updated in the same commit that authors Phase X.Y. A forward-reference row that survives past its phase landing is a documentation defect.

### M.3 Authored Extension Note

Appendix M is an Authored Extension introduced in Phase 14.2 of the v7.1.0 integration program. The Process Gates in M.2 describe future Phase 14.18 / 14.19 / 14.17 enforcement artifacts that have not yet been authored at the time Appendix M lands. The forward references stand as binding authoring constraints; the artifacts implementing them (the CI validator, the adversarial review checklist, the First-30-Seconds Test rubric) land in their respective phases. Until those artifacts ship, Appendix M is enforced through code review and authoring discipline. Human sign-off on M.1 row coverage is required before Appendix M is considered binding for downstream phases.

### M.4 CI Gate — Appendix M Coverage {#appendix-m-ci-gate}

M.4 specifies the deploy-time enforcement contract for M.2 gates #1, #4, and #7. Authored in Phase 14.18 of the v7.1.0 integration program; hardened against firewall-bypass, trigger-scope, and audit-trail-completeness defects in the Phase V11 remediation pass (closed 2026-05-11). Binds every PR that touches `Sourcera_Master_Spec.md` from this phase forward. Runtime status: `runtime_active` at v7.1.0 (stamped 2026-04-28; M.4 wiring landed in implementation pack M02.3, GitHub Actions workflow `.github/workflows/spec-lint.yml` with detector script `tools/spec-lint/appendix_m_coverage_on_diff.ts`).

#### M.4.1 Scope {#m-4-1-scope}

Every pull request that modifies `Sourcera_Master_Spec.md` and introduces a new engine concept MUST include a corresponding row in Appendix M (§M.1) in the same diff. The CI gate `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` runs against every PR that touches the Master Spec and blocks merge until coverage is satisfied or an explicit override is applied per §M.4.4. The gate is registered as a required check in GitHub branch-protection on `main`; repository administrators cannot bypass the check without invoking the override path. The gate is identically catalog-bound in Appendix M.5 (`Gate ID = appendix_m_coverage_on_diff`, `row_class = spec_tree_lint`, `runtime_status = runtime_active`).

#### M.4.2 Triggers — concept classes that require an Appendix M row {#m-4-2-triggers}

The lint check enforces presence of an Appendix M row update when the PR diff introduces any of the following concept classes. Detection runs over the post-edit Master Spec Markdown parse tree (the spec-repo's `remark-parse`-derived tree, with code-fence and frontmatter blocks elided) against a snapshot of the pre-edit parse tree fetched from the merge-base commit:

1. **Entity.** A new entity field table under §4.x (any of §4.2, §4.3 Buyer Console, §4.4 Seller Console, §4.5 Marketplace, §4.6 Audit, §4.7 Cross-Console Bridge, §4.8 Billing & AI Accounting). Detected by a new `## 4.N.M {Entity Name} {#4.N.M-...}` heading or an inserted `Field | Type | Constraints | Notes` table whose anchor was absent in the pre-edit snapshot.
2. **Entity field.** A new field row inserted into an existing §4.x entity table whose `Field | Type | Constraints | Notes` cell tuple was absent in the pre-edit snapshot AND whose field name is not in the canonical infrastructure-field allow-list (`id`, `org_id`, `console`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `deleted_at`). Per §4.7.1 forward-compatibility rule.
3. **AIOperation.** A new `AIOperation` capability — a new `CapabilityRegistryEntry` row in §4.8.2; a new `capability_id` value referenced anywhere in §22.10 / §34.10 / §44.6; or a new `cost_center` / `model_tier` combination registered against a new capability. Detected by a new row in §4.8.2's capability table or a new `capability_id` literal anywhere in an AIOperation-emitting section.
4. **Capability (non-AI).** A new role capability surfaced in §5 RBAC; a new feature capability under §13–§30 acceptance-criteria blocks; a new tool entry in §22.10 KB tool catalog or §21.4 Sourcera AI Agents tool catalog. Detected by a new row in §5.11 Feature Access Matrix; a new `### N.N {Feature}` or `### N.N.N {Capability}` heading under feature sections §13–§30 (now expanded to include §13.11 Defense View, §13.12 EvalStarter intake, §22.20 Seller Maya Surface Polish, §50.10–§50.17 Ops Console subsections, §51.3–§51.6 Product Usage Analytics dashboards); or a new tool entry in the §22.10 / §21.4 catalogs.
5. **Enum value.** A new enum value registered in Appendix J (Controlled Vocabulary Registry). Detected by a new row in any Appendix J enum table whose `value` cell was absent in the pre-edit snapshot.
6. **State-machine state.** A new state or transition row inserted into Appendix A (Workspace State Machine), Appendix D (Bid Workspace State Machine), Appendix E (DSAR Lifecycle State Machine), or Appendix L (Defense View / Per-Vertical EvalStarter / Solo Tier state machines). Detected by a new row in any `From | To | Trigger | Conditions | Notes` table whose tuple was absent in the pre-edit snapshot.
7. **Plan-tier feature.** A new plan-gated feature surfaced in §34.1 Plan Tier Definitions; §34.8 Entitlement Matrix; §34.13 Pro Trial Seat allocation; or §39 Object Size Constraints. Detected by a new row OR new column OR new cell value in §34.1.1 / §34.1.2 / §34.1.3 / §34.8.x / §39.x tables.
8. **Webhook event.** A new webhook event kind registered in §31 Webhook Event Catalog or Appendix C Notification Event Catalog. Detected by a new row in §31 catalog table or Appendix C registry whose `event_kind` cell was absent in the pre-edit snapshot.
9. **Notification event.** A new in-app or email notification kind registered in §20 Pulse / §29 In-App Notifications / §41 Email or Appendix C. Detected by a new row in Appendix C with `kind=notification`, a new template entry in §41, or a new `### 29.N` toast / banner / modal sub-section.
10. **PostHog event.** A new PostHog event registered in Appendix G (PostHog Event Taxonomy) or §51 Product Usage Analytics instrumentation. Detected by a new row in Appendix G whose `event_name` cell was absent in the pre-edit snapshot.
11. **API endpoint.** A new endpoint added to §32 Endpoint Catalog. Detected by a new sub-section heading of the form `### 32.N.M {METHOD} /v1/{...}` or by a new row in the §32.5 / §32.8 / §32.9 endpoint inventory tables.
12. **Named CI gate (catalog-self-reference).** Any new `\`<gate_id>\` (Appendix M.5; ...)` inline citation in the Master Spec body MUST resolve to an existing §M.5 catalog row. New gate IDs that are cited inline but absent from §M.5 fail the gate. This sub-trigger closes the D-11.3-002 13-orphan-cross-reference pattern. Implementation: regex `/Appendix M\.5\s+\`([a-z0-9_]+)\`/g` over the post-edit Master Spec body; matched gate IDs are checked against the §M.5 catalog gate-ID set extracted at parse time.

The detector operates on the post-edit Master Spec parse tree relative to the pre-edit merge-base snapshot. Cosmetic edits — header-level changes that do not alter heading text; anchor-slug renames where the canonical anchor remains discoverable via the alias-redirect table at §M.4.2.1; prose rewrites that introduce no new heading, table row, or enum value; whitespace-only changes; comment-only changes — are filtered by the parser. The cosmetic-edit filter rule is published in `tools/spec-lint/cosmetic_edit_filter.ts` and version-tied to this M.4 contract; filter-rule amendments require an explicit `appendix_m_cosmetic_filter_amended` Authored Extension row.

##### M.4.2.1 Anchor-slug alias-redirect table {#m-4-2-1-anchor-aliases}

Maintained at `tools/spec-lint/anchor_aliases.json` in the spec repo. Each alias row is `{deprecated_anchor, canonical_anchor, retired_in_phase, retired_at}`. The detector treats a deprecated anchor as resolving to the canonical anchor for trigger-detection purposes. The alias-redirect table is itself a versioned Authored Extension (AE-V11-05); amendments require ledger sign-off.

#### M.4.3 Failure mode {#m-4-3-failure-mode}

When the gate detects a triggering concept introduction without a corresponding Appendix M row update in the same diff, the PR check fails with one of the following deterministic statuses:

| Status | Trigger | Override-eligible |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff: missing_row` | One or more triggered concepts have no Appendix M.1 row in the post-edit snapshot. | Yes — via §M.4.4 |
| `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff: invalid_override_rationale` | A `@appendix-m-internal-only:` annotation is present but malformed (missing required substring, missing prefix colon, missing concept_name token, missing required cross-class qualifier per §M.4.4.1). | No — must fix annotation |
| `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff: override_target_not_flagged_by_detector` | A `@appendix-m-internal-only:` annotation passes rationale parsing BUT the annotation's `{concept_name}` does NOT match any concept the §M.4.2 trigger detector flagged in the same PR (i.e., the author is attempting to admit an `Internal-only, never surfaced` row for an identifier that does not appear in the diff). Per §M.4.4.2.A detector-flag pre-merge cross-validation. Authored in the v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 remediation pass (closed 2026-05-15; D-11.2-004 P0 firewall-bypass closure). | No — override is rejected; the annotation must reference a detector-flagged concept_name in the same PR OR the M.1 row must be authored directly |
| `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff: override_target_customer_visible` | A `@appendix-m-internal-only:` annotation passes rationale parsing AND detector-flag cross-validation BUT the customer-surface-reachability cross-validation step in §M.4.4.2.B–§M.4.4.2.E detects that the override target is reachable from a customer surface (any of: console enum, RBAC, plan-tier, surface-class non-internal). | No — override is rejected; row must be authored with an explicit surface metaphor |
| `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff: orphan_inline_gate_reference` | An inline `Appendix M.5 \`<gate_id>\`` citation resolves to a gate ID absent from the §M.5 catalog gate-ID set. | No — must add catalog row |
| `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff: parse_error` | The post-edit Markdown parse tree cannot be constructed (malformed table; orphan anchor; broken frontmatter). | No — must fix parse error |
| `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff: pass` | No triggered concept; or every triggered concept has a coverage row or accepted override (grammar + detector-flag + customer-surface cross-validation all pass). | n/a |

For `missing_row` and `orphan_inline_gate_reference` failures, the gate posts an inline review comment using the canonical comment template (see `tools/spec-lint/comment_templates.ts`). Comment template for missing-row:

> **Appendix M coverage missing.** This PR introduces the following engine concept(s) without a corresponding row in Appendix M (§M.1):
>
> - `{concept_class}` `{concept_name}` at `{spec_anchor}` (line {line_number})
>
> Add a row to §M.1 in the same diff binding the engine concept to a surface metaphor, OR apply the `@appendix-m-internal-only:` override per §M.4.4 if the concept is genuinely internal-only. See §M.2 gate #1 and §M.4 for the authoring contract. Gate run ID: `{gate_run_id}` (see audit trail at `tools/spec-lint/run-logs/{gate_run_id}.json`).

For `orphan_inline_gate_reference`:

> **Appendix M.5 catalog gap.** This PR cites the following CI gate(s) by name with an `Appendix M.5` placement claim, but the gate is absent from the §M.5 catalog row set:
>
> - `{gate_id}` cited at `{spec_anchor}` (line {line_number})
>
> Add a §M.5 catalog row for each cited gate in the same diff, or remove the inline `Appendix M.5` placement claim. See §M.5 catalog header for the authoring contract. Gate run ID: `{gate_run_id}`.

The PR is blocked from merge until the comment resolves. The gate is a GitHub branch-protection required check; repository administrators cannot bypass it without invoking the override path.

##### M.4.3.1 Third-party degradation {#m-4-3-1-third-party-degradation}

If the GitHub API is degraded and the gate cannot post the inline review comment, the gate falls **closed** (fail-secure): the gate run is marked `comment_post_failed` and the PR is blocked from merge until either the comment post succeeds on retry (exponential backoff: 1s / 4s / 16s / 64s / 256s; max 5 retries) or the spec-ops oncall manually unblocks via an explicit `@ci-gate-comment-post-bypass:` annotation (which is itself logged to the M.4.5 audit trail with `gate_outcome = comment_post_bypass_applied`). The fail-closed posture is required to prevent the gate's enforcement from being trivially defeated by a coincident GitHub outage.

#### M.4.4 Override path — `@appendix-m-internal-only:` annotation {#m-4-4-override-path}

For engine concepts that are genuinely internal-only and never surfaced (reactivity machinery, internal cache TTL fields, deployment-only flags, internal-IPC headers, internal property-test seeds), the PR author applies the override by including the literal annotation `@appendix-m-internal-only:` in the PR description, followed by a one-line justification.

##### M.4.4.1 Override grammar {#m-4-4-1-override-grammar}

Canonical form (machine-parseable; the parser uses regex `/^@appendix-m-internal-only:\s+(?P<concept_name>[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)\s+—\s+(?P<rationale>.+)$/m`):

```
@appendix-m-internal-only: {concept_name} — {rationale}
```

Rationale grammar requirements (enforced cumulatively by the parser):

1. **Substring requirement.** Rationale MUST contain the literal substring `internal-only construct, not surfaced` (case-sensitive, exact match) to assert that the author has affirmatively considered and confirmed the no-surface decision.
2. **Minimum length.** Rationale MUST be ≥ 60 characters total (raised from §M.4.4-v1's 30-character minimum after V11 hardening; the longer floor mitigates the D-11.2-004 P0 firewall-bypass attack by forcing the author to write a substantive justification beyond the required substring).
3. **Concept-name token.** `{concept_name}` MUST be a unique identifier across the override block. Identical `{concept_name}` tokens on different override lines are a `multiple_override_same_concept_name` parser failure.
4. **Cross-class qualifier (new in V11).** If the triggered concept class is `entity_field`, `enum_value`, `webhook_event`, `notification_event`, `posthog_event`, `api_endpoint`, or `named_ci_gate` (the seven classes most associated with customer-visible surfaces), the rationale MUST additionally include one of the following affirmative qualifiers, each of which scopes the internal-only claim to a specific exclusion class:
   - `not_in_pricing_api` — the concept is not reachable from `GET /v1/pricing` or `GET /v1/pricing.capabilities[]` (per §32.8 Public Pricing API).
   - `not_in_seller_serializer` — the concept does not appear in any seller-console serializer per §22.20.x surface integrity contract.
   - `not_in_buyer_serializer` — the concept does not appear in any buyer-console serializer.
   - `not_in_marketplace_serializer` — the concept does not appear in any §27 marketplace public-page serializer.
   - `not_in_webhook_payload` — the concept does not appear in any §31 webhook payload schema.
   - `not_in_email_template` — the concept does not appear in any §41 Loops.so email template variable.
   - `not_in_posthog_payload` — the concept does not appear in any Appendix G PostHog event property.

Multiple qualifiers may be listed in a single rationale (e.g., `not_in_pricing_api, not_in_seller_serializer, not_in_webhook_payload`).

##### M.4.4.2 Cross-validation step (V11 firewall hardening; v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 extension) {#m-4-4-2-cross-validation}

Before auto-generating an `Internal-only, never surfaced` Appendix M.1 row, the gate performs a **two-part cross-validation** on the override target: a pre-merge detector-flag check (§M.4.4.2.A) and a customer-surface-reachability check across four orthogonal predicates (§M.4.4.2.B–§M.4.4.2.E). The two parts compose: detector-flag failure short-circuits the predicate evaluation, and ANY predicate evaluating `true` causes the gate to reject the override.

This cross-validation step closes the D-11.2-004 (P0) firewall-bypass vulnerability that allowed an author to ship a customer-visible field disguised as internal-only via a syntactically valid override rationale. The V11 remediation pass (closed 2026-05-11) authored the four V11 predicates (surface-section / plan-gating / public-API / serializer reachability). The v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 remediation pass (closed 2026-05-15) (a) prepended the detector-flag pre-merge cross-validation at §M.4.4.2.A — closing the residual D-11.2-004 P0 attack where an author submits a syntactically valid override for a concept that does not appear in the diff at all — and (b) re-organized the customer-surface-reachability predicates around the canonical access-axes vocabulary (console enum / RBAC / plan-tier / surface-class non-internal) per `_audit/REMEDIATION_BACKLOG.md §2 → P0 #5` recommendation. The v7.2.0-REM predicate set strictly subsumes the V11 set: each V11 predicate's coverage is preserved as a sub-check inside one of the four v7.2.0-REM predicates. Coverage is non-decreasing — no V11-detected leak class can pass the v7.2.0-REM check.

**Acceptance condition.** The override is honored if and only if (a) §M.4.4.2.A passes (the annotation's `{concept_name}` matches a concept the §M.4.2 trigger detector flagged in the same PR diff) AND (b) all four customer-surface-reachability predicates §M.4.4.2.B / §M.4.4.2.C / §M.4.4.2.D / §M.4.4.2.E evaluate **false**.

###### M.4.4.2.A Detector-flag pre-merge cross-validation {#m-4-4-2-a-detector-flag}

The gate verifies that every `@appendix-m-internal-only: {concept_name} — {rationale}` annotation references a concept that the §M.4.2 trigger detector flagged in the same PR diff. The detector emits a `triggered_concepts[]` array per gate run (see §M.4.5.1 record schema, `concept_name` field per row); the cross-validator joins each annotation row to that array on the `concept_name` token.

The join is performed under the following matching rules:

1. **Exact ASCII match.** `annotation.concept_name == detected_concept.concept_name` (case-sensitive, byte-equal). The §M.4.4.1 grammar restricts `{concept_name}` to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`, so canonicalization-by-NFC is not required.
2. **Anchor-alias resolution.** If the annotation's `concept_name` resolves to a deprecated anchor per `tools/spec-lint/anchor_aliases.json` (§M.4.2.1 alias-redirect table), the canonical anchor's concept_name is used for the join. Alias resolution is applied to both sides symmetrically (annotation and detected) to prevent rename-during-PR drift from breaking the cross-validation.
3. **Concept-class filter.** The match requires the detected concept's `concept_class` (per the §M.4.2 12-class enumeration) to be in the §M.4.4.1 cross-class qualifier-eligible set (`entity_field`, `enum_value`, `webhook_event`, `notification_event`, `posthog_event`, `api_endpoint`, `named_ci_gate`) OR in the broader §M.4.4.1 set (`entity`, `aioperation`, `capability_non_ai`, `state_machine_state`, `plan_tier_feature`). The override path is not available for concept classes outside this 12-class set; the annotation is rejected at the grammar layer per §M.4.4.1 before reaching this step.
4. **Multi-annotation cardinality.** If a single PR carries N annotations and the detector flagged M concepts, the cross-validator runs an N×M join. Annotations that fail the join after exhausting all candidates are aggregated into a single rejection comment per PR (see §M.4.4.2.G).

If the join fails — i.e., no detected concept matches the annotation's `concept_name` under the rules above — the gate rejects the override with status `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff: override_target_not_flagged_by_detector` (registered in Appendix I `Spec-Lint CI Gate Internal Failure Modes`, error code `override_target_not_flagged_by_detector`). The PR is blocked from merge.

**Rationale for the pre-merge detector-flag step.** Without this step, an author could append `@appendix-m-internal-only: arbitrary_engine_name — internal-only construct, not surfaced (not_in_pricing_api ...)` to a PR description that introduces no engine concept at all — and the auto-row generator at §M.4.4.3 would seed Appendix M.1 with the `arbitrary_engine_name` row, untethered from any spec authoring. The seeded row would carry the canonical `Internal-only, never surfaced` sentinel, defeating downstream §M.5 `appendix_m_engine_to_surface_completeness` traversal because the row appears resolved even though no spec body cites it. The detector-flag step makes the override path strictly downstream of the trigger detector: the override can only admit concepts the detector itself flagged.

**Counterfactual coverage.** Three realistic failure modes the detector-flag step closes:
- **Adversarial-input failure mode 1: orphan annotation.** A PR with a no-op spec edit (typo fix, comment-only change) carrying an override annotation for `customer_visible_field_xyz`. §M.4.4.2.A rejects with `override_target_not_flagged_by_detector` because the detector flagged zero concepts. (V11 §M.4.4.2 predicates would have rejected on the customer-surface predicate if `customer_visible_field_xyz` appeared in §3 / §32 / §31, but in the V11 implementation an orphan name that did not match any predicate's spec-section reach would pass V11 unconditionally — a residual P0 gap.)
- **Adversarial-input failure mode 2: typo'd concept name.** A PR introducing engine concept `solo_envelope_throttle_threshold_value_cents` with an override annotation for `solo_envelope_throttle_threshold` (typo: missing `_value_cents`). §M.4.4.2.A rejects because the annotation's concept_name does not exactly match the detected concept's name. The author must either fix the typo (causing the join to succeed and then run §M.4.4.2.B–§M.4.4.2.E) or author the §M.1 row directly. This eliminates the silent-typo bypass that would otherwise admit an `Internal-only` row for a name no engine concept ever uses.
- **Adversarial-input failure mode 3: prefix-substring near-match.** A PR introducing engine concept `kb_export_archive_integrity_check_aux` with an override annotation for `kb_export_archive_integrity_check`. The exact ASCII match rule rejects the join (substring matching is not permitted). The author authors the §M.1 row directly or amends the annotation to the full concept_name.

###### M.4.4.2.B Predicate 1 — Console enum reachability {#m-4-4-2-b-console-enum}

**Definition.** The override target's `concept_name` is **console-reachable** if any spec-side cite of the concept resolves to a `console` enum value in `{buyer, seller, marketplace_public}`, OR if the concept is named in a feature section whose canonical console binding is non-internal.

**Operationalization.** Predicate 1 evaluates `true` if ANY of the following sub-checks is `true`:

1. **Inline appearance in customer-surface sections.** The concept_name appears (as `` `<name>` ``, `${name}`, `{{name}}` template token, or unbracketed identifier-shape ASCII match) anywhere in §3 (Design System), §11 (Buyer Console nav), §12 (Buyer Console pages), §13 (Buyer Workspace surfaces; including §13.11 Defense View + §13.12 Buyer Maya Intake), §14 (Evaluation Scenarios), §15 (TCO), §16 (Selection Report), §17 (Marketplace Surfaces — buyer side), §19 (Templates), §20 (Pulse), §22 (Seller-Console surfaces), §22.18.6 (Post-Close Outcome Debrief), §22.20 (Seller Maya Surface Polish), §26 (Public Seller Pages), §27 (Marketplace Listings), §29 (In-App Notifications surfaces), §38 (Mobile surfaces), §41 (Email templates — Loops.so variables), §44.6 (Solo-Tier Surface Treatment), §48 (Growth surfaces — referral / KB share / Hero Moment), §51.3–§51.6 (Product Usage dashboards). Ops Console surfaces (§50.10–§50.17) are bound to `console=internal_ops` and are excluded from this sub-check; see §M.4.4.2.E sub-check 4 instead.
2. **Bound to a `console`-tagged entity table.** The concept_name appears as a `Field` cell in any §4.3 (Buyer Console), §4.4 (Seller Console), §4.5 (Marketplace), or §4.7 (Cross-Console Bridge) entity table. Bridge entities are the firewall surface and explicitly count as customer-visible by Predicate 1 — the Bridge serializer projects fields to both consoles per §4.7.1.
3. **Cited as a serializer field reachable from non-internal endpoint.** The concept_name appears in any spec-side mention of a Convex query / mutation handler, GraphQL schema field, REST response key, or webhook payload cited in §32.5 / §32.8 / §32.9 / §31, where the endpoint's declared `auth_scope` per §32.2 includes any of `buyer_*`, `seller_*`, `marketplace_*`, `public_pricing_*`, `webhook_subscriber_*`. Endpoints scoped to `ops_*` or `internal_*` do NOT count by Predicate 1.
4. **Cited as a Loops.so email template variable.** The concept_name appears in any §41 transactional or lifecycle email template's variable list (e.g., `{{ workspace_name }}` in a Hero Moment email). Email templates are customer-surface by §41.0 convention.

If any of sub-checks 1–4 returns `true`, Predicate 1 evaluates `true` and the override is rejected.

###### M.4.4.2.C Predicate 2 — RBAC reachability {#m-4-4-2-c-rbac-reachability}

**Definition.** The override target's `concept_name` is **RBAC-reachable** if it appears as a row, column, or cell in §5.11 Feature Access Matrix; OR as a capability binding for any non-internal role in §5; OR as a permission cited in §5.2 / §5.3 / §5.5 / §5.6 role definitions.

**Operationalization.** Predicate 2 evaluates `true` if ANY of the following sub-checks is `true`:

1. **§5.11 Feature Access Matrix row.** The concept_name appears as a row identifier, column header (other than the canonical plan-tier columns), or cell value in §5.11.
2. **Non-internal role grant.** The concept_name appears in any §5.2 (Buyer roles), §5.3 (Workspace roles), §5.5 (Seller roles), or §5.6 (Marketplace roles) role-permission table as a granted capability for any role other than `ops_*` (the §5.7 / §50.3 Ops role family). Specifically, presence in any of: `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `billing_admin`, `buyer_evaluator`, `buyer_stakeholder`, `buyer_guest`, `buyer_solo_owner`, `workspace_owner`, `workspace_admin`, `workspace_editor`, `workspace_viewer`, `use_case_lead`, `seller_admin`, `seller_responder`, `seller_observer`, `seller_solo_owner`, `marketplace_publisher`, `marketplace_visitor`.
3. **Capability registry binding.** The concept_name is, or directly references, a `capability_id` registered in §21.4 (Sourcera AI Agents catalog), §22.10 (KB tool catalog), or §4.8.2 (CapabilityRegistryEntry) whose `console_applicability` enum value is not exclusively `ops` (i.e., any binding to `buyer`, `seller`, or `marketplace_public`).
4. **Permission identifier in §5.2.1.x operation table.** The concept_name appears in the §5.2.1.1 / §5.2.1.2 / §5.2.1.3 / §5.2.1.4 operation-by-operation permission lists for any non-Ops role.

If any of sub-checks 1–4 returns `true`, Predicate 2 evaluates `true` and the override is rejected. The §50.3.x Ops Role Kind tables and §50.X Ops Console surface tables are explicitly excluded from this predicate; see §M.4.4.2.E sub-check 4.

###### M.4.4.2.D Predicate 3 — Plan-tier reachability {#m-4-4-2-d-plan-tier}

**Definition.** The override target's `concept_name` is **plan-tier-reachable** if it appears as a row, column, or cell in any plan-tier-governing section.

**Operationalization.** Predicate 3 evaluates `true` if ANY of the following sub-checks is `true`:

1. **§34.1 Plan Tier Definitions cell value.** The concept_name appears in §34.1.1 (Buyer plan tiers), §34.1.2 (Seller plan tiers), or §34.1.3 (Solo plan tier — symmetric) as a row, column, or cell value (including the canonical 6-tier-per-console plan grid).
2. **§34.8 Entitlement Matrix row.** The concept_name appears in §34.8.x entitlement-matrix rows binding a capability_id to a plan-tier × subscription-tenure cell.
3. **§34.10 / §34.13 wallet / trial-seat allocation.** The concept_name appears in §34.10 wallet contract, §34.13 Pro Trial Seat allocation, or §34.14 / §34.15 rate-card seed tables.
4. **§39 Object Size Constraints row.** The concept_name appears in any §39.x object-size-constraint table as a `Field` cell or limit citation.
5. **§44 envelope or rate-card cell.** The concept_name appears in §44.1 (Performance / Latency / Rate-limit envelope), §44.2 (Cost envelope), §44.4 (Throughput envelope), §44.5 (Quality envelope), or §44.6 (Solo-Tier Surface Treatment) as a row, column, or cell value bound to a plan tier.
6. **Public Pricing API field.** The concept_name appears in `GET /v1/pricing` or `GET /v1/pricing.capabilities[]` per §32.8 Public Pricing API response schema.

If any of sub-checks 1–6 returns `true`, Predicate 3 evaluates `true` and the override is rejected.

###### M.4.4.2.E Predicate 4 — Surface-class non-internal {#m-4-4-2-e-surface-class}

**Definition.** The override target's `concept_name` carries a **non-internal surface class** if it is NOT in the canonical internal-only allowlist AND does not satisfy the spec-side internal-only attestation pattern.

**Operationalization.** Predicate 4 evaluates `true` if NONE of the following affirmative internal-only sub-checks is `true` — i.e., the predicate defaults to `true` (= "non-internal") and falls back to `false` (= "internal-only confirmed") only on affirmative evidence. Sub-checks (any matching sub-check forces Predicate 4 to `false`, exempting the concept from this predicate):

1. **Canonical internal-only concept-class allowlist match.** The concept_name's detected concept_class (per the §M.4.2 12-class enumeration) is bound to one of the canonical internal-only construct kinds via the spec-side internal-only attestation pattern below. The canonical kinds are: `internal_cache_ttl_field`, `reactivity_machinery_field`, `internal_ipc_header_field`, `deployment_only_flag`, `internal_property_test_seed`, `dr_drill_fixture_field`, `chaos_synthetic_fixture_field`, `release_orchestration_signal_field`, `convex_cron_internal_state_field`, `audit_chain_internal_field`, `spec_lint_internal_field`. Bindings are registered in `tools/spec-lint/internal_only_concept_class_allowlist.json` (versioned; amendments are an Authored Extension).
2. **Ops-Console-exclusive surface.** The concept_name appears EXCLUSIVELY in §50 (Ops Console) sections AND in entities whose `console` enum value is `internal_ops`. (Note: this excludes the concept from Predicate 1 sub-check 1 reach, but does NOT excuse a §22 / §22.20 / §27 customer-surface reach concurrently.)
3. **Spec-side internal-only attestation paragraph.** The concept_name's introducing section carries a paragraph of the canonical form `**Internal-only construct.** {concept_name} is an internal {kind} that is never serialized to any customer console, webhook payload, email template, or public API response. ...` (regex `/\*\*Internal-only construct\.\*\*\s+\b{concept_name_quoted}\b.+never serialized to any customer console/`). The attestation paragraph is the spec-side companion of the override annotation: it must appear in the section that introduces the concept.
4. **Explicit serializer-redaction lock.** The concept_name appears in `tools/spec-lint/serializer_redaction_locks.json` as a closed-set member with explicit `redacted_from: ["buyer_console", "seller_console", "marketplace_public", "webhook_payload", "email_template"]` coverage (all five must be present). The locks file is a versioned Authored Extension; entry additions require AE-row ratification.

If NONE of sub-checks 1–4 returns `true`, Predicate 4 defaults to `true` (= "non-internal") and the override is rejected. The default-deny posture is required to prevent silent non-attestation: an author who genuinely intends an internal-only construct must affirm via one of the four sub-checks.

###### M.4.4.2.F Override acceptance condition {#m-4-4-2-f-acceptance}

The override is accepted (and §M.4.4.3 auto-row generation proceeds) if and only if:

- §M.4.4.1 grammar all checks pass (substring + min length + concept-name token + cross-class qualifier), AND
- §M.4.4.2.A detector-flag pre-merge cross-validation passes (the `{concept_name}` matches a detector-flagged concept in the same PR), AND
- §M.4.4.2.B Predicate 1 (Console enum reachability) evaluates `false`, AND
- §M.4.4.2.C Predicate 2 (RBAC reachability) evaluates `false`, AND
- §M.4.4.2.D Predicate 3 (Plan-tier reachability) evaluates `false`, AND
- §M.4.4.2.E Predicate 4 (Surface-class non-internal) evaluates `false`.

Any failure in any of the above eight gates causes rejection with the corresponding failure-mode status from §M.4.3 and the corresponding inline comment from §M.4.4.2.G.

###### M.4.4.2.G Rejection comment templates {#m-4-4-2-g-rejection-comments}

The cross-validator emits one of the following inline PR review comments depending on which check failed. All comments include the `gate_run_id` (per §M.4.5) and a deep link to the audit-trail JSON record at `tools/spec-lint/run-logs/{gate_run_id}.json` for post-mortem investigation.

**`override_target_not_flagged_by_detector` (§M.4.4.2.A failure):**

> **Override rejected — annotation target not flagged by detector.** The `@appendix-m-internal-only:` annotation for `{concept_name}` cannot be honored: the §M.4.2 trigger detector did not flag any concept matching `{concept_name}` in this PR's diff. The override path is strictly downstream of the trigger detector — overrides can only admit concepts the detector itself flagged in the same PR.
>
> Detected concepts in this PR: `{detected_concept_list}` (count: {detected_count}).
> Annotation concept_name: `{annotation_concept_name}`.
> Closest detected matches by Levenshtein distance < 5: `{near_match_list}`.
>
> Resolution paths: (a) Fix the annotation's `{concept_name}` to exactly match one of the detected concepts above; (b) Author the §M.1 row directly without invoking the override path; (c) If the concept is genuinely internal-only AND the PR is a no-op for the trigger detector, the override path is not available — the §M.1 row must be authored directly with the `Internal-only, never surfaced` sentinel in the `Tier visibility` cell.
>
> Gate run ID: `{gate_run_id}` (audit trail at `tools/spec-lint/run-logs/{gate_run_id}.json`).

**`override_target_customer_visible` (§M.4.4.2.B–§M.4.4.2.E failure):**

> **Override rejected — target appears customer-visible.** The `@appendix-m-internal-only:` annotation for `{concept_name}` cannot auto-generate an `Internal-only, never surfaced` Appendix M.1 row because the concept is reachable from a customer surface per cross-validation predicate {predicate_id} ({predicate_human_name}).
>
> Predicate {predicate_id} sub-check that failed: {sub_check_id} — {sub_check_human_name}.
> Evidence cite: `{evidence_anchor}` at line `{evidence_line_number}`. Excerpt: `{evidence_excerpt_120_chars}`.
> Predicate evaluation snapshot (per-predicate result): `Predicate 1 (Console enum reachability): {p1_result}` / `Predicate 2 (RBAC reachability): {p2_result}` / `Predicate 3 (Plan-tier reachability): {p3_result}` / `Predicate 4 (Surface-class non-internal): {p4_result}`.
>
> Resolution paths: (a) Author an explicit §M.1 row with a surface metaphor + `Tier visibility` cell value listing the tiers that see the surface, instead of using the override; (b) If the customer-surface reach is incidental (e.g., the concept is named in a surface section as a cross-reference but not actually rendered), file a follow-up Authored Extension to amend the §M.4.4.2 predicate-sub-check set OR rename the concept to break the heuristic match; (c) If the concept genuinely should NOT be reachable from the customer surface, fix the upstream spec-side cite at `{evidence_anchor}` instead of adding the override.
>
> Gate run ID: `{gate_run_id}` (audit trail at `tools/spec-lint/run-logs/{gate_run_id}.json`).

Override-rejection appeals route through the §M.4.5 audit-trail emitter (`gate_outcome ∈ {fail_target_not_flagged_by_detector, override_target_customer_visible}`) and are flagged for human review at the §M.2 gate #3 Phase 14.19 adversarial review pass. The spec-ops oncall (per §M.4.6.2) triages override-rejection appeals within 2 business days; the audit-trail JSON record is the canonical source-of-truth for the rejection decision.

###### M.4.4.2.H V11-to-v7.2.0-REM predicate coverage map {#m-4-4-2-h-v11-coverage-map}

The v7.2.0-REM predicate set strictly subsumes the V11 predicate set. The table below maps each V11 predicate to the v7.2.0-REM predicate(s) that absorb it; coverage is non-decreasing.

| V11 predicate | v7.2.0-REM absorber | Coverage note |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| V11 Predicate 1 (Surface-section reachability) | §M.4.4.2.B sub-check 1 + §M.4.4.2.E sub-check 2 | Inline appearance in customer-surface sections is now Predicate 1 sub-check 1; Ops-Console-exclusive surfaces are explicitly excluded from Predicate 1 reach but checked under Predicate 4 sub-check 2. |
| V11 Predicate 2 (Plan-gating reachability) | §M.4.4.2.D (entirety) | Plan-tier reachability is the entirety of Predicate 3; expanded to cover §39 / §44 / Public Pricing API per v7.2.0-REM. |
| V11 Predicate 3 (Public-API reachability) | §M.4.4.2.B sub-check 3 + §M.4.4.2.D sub-check 6 | Public-API serializer reach is Predicate 1 sub-check 3 (auth-scope-bound to non-internal); pricing-API reach is Predicate 3 sub-check 6. |
| V11 Predicate 4 (Serializer reachability) | §M.4.4.2.B sub-check 3 + §M.4.4.2.E (default-deny) | Serializer fields cited in §32 / §22 / §44 are covered by Predicate 1 sub-check 3 when the endpoint is non-internal-scoped; the Predicate 4 default-deny posture (§M.4.4.2.E sub-checks 1–4) catches any remaining serializer cite that the §M.4.4.2.B sub-check 3 heuristic missed. |

The Phase V11 hardening's protective effect is preserved verbatim; no V11-detected leak class can pass the v7.2.0-REM check. The v7.2.0-REM additions are: (a) the §M.4.4.2.A detector-flag pre-merge cross-validation (orthogonal to the V11 predicate set — closes the orphan-annotation attack); and (b) the §M.4.4.2.E default-deny posture (forces the author to affirmatively attest internal-only status rather than relying on heuristic absence).

##### M.4.4.3 Override acceptance — auto-row generation {#m-4-4-3-auto-row-generation}

When all M.4.4.1 grammar checks AND the M.4.4.2 cross-validation pass, the gate auto-generates the corresponding Appendix M.1 row with:

- `Engine concept` cell: `{concept_name}` (verbatim from the annotation).
- `Spec home` cell: `{spec_anchor}` (inferred by the detector from the parse-tree location of the triggered concept).
- `Surface metaphor` cell: `Internal-only, never surfaced`.
- `Tier visibility` cell: `Internal-only, never surfaced` (canonical sentinel value per the §M.1 legend amendment in Phase V11 remediation; replaces the prior `Hidden from tier(s)` column header semantics — see §M.1 preamble).
- `Notes` cell: `Override auto-generated via @appendix-m-internal-only: annotation on PR #{pr_id}. Rationale: "{rationale}". Qualifiers: [{qualifier_list}]. Auto-generated; flagged for Phase 14.19 adversarial review pass per §M.2 gate #3.`

The auto-generated row is placed under the appropriate spec-area group banner inferred from the concept's spec anchor; the author retains responsibility for moving the row if the auto-placement is imprecise.

Multiple overrides may appear in a single PR description (one per missing concept). Each override line MUST include the exact `@appendix-m-internal-only:` prefix; lines without the prefix are ignored.

##### M.4.4.4 Concurrent-PR merge-conflict resolution {#m-4-4-4-concurrent-pr-merge-conflicts}

When two PRs A and B each invoke `@appendix-m-internal-only:` on different concepts and both target the same Appendix M.1 area-group banner, the second PR to merge will encounter a structural Markdown-table merge conflict on M.1. Resolution rule: the second PR's author rebases on the first PR's post-merge `main` and re-runs the gate; auto-row-generation re-applies idempotently against the post-rebase state. The gate's auto-row generator detects existing rows by `(Engine concept, Spec home)` tuple and skips re-emission for tuples already present. No author intervention required beyond the rebase.

##### M.4.4.5 Sibling override annotation for non-Appendix-M gates {#m-4-4-5-sibling-override}

For CI gates other than `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff`, the override grammar is the `@ci-gate-override:` annotation. Definitionally:

```
@ci-gate-override: {gate_id} — {rationale}
```

Rationale grammar requirements (single canonical specification — replaces the three-way drift between §M.4.4-v1, §M.5 line 49567-v1, and AE-14.18.1-02-v1 captured as D-11.2-011; hardened in v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 with explicit failure-mode error codes per Counterfactual #1 / #2 / #3):

1. **Minimum length.** Rationale MUST be ≥ 60 characters (harmonized with §M.4.4.1 floor). A rationale below the floor is rejected with status `override_rationale_too_short` (registered in Appendix I `Spec-Lint CI Gate Internal Failure Modes`). The 60-character floor is canonical; per-row tightening to a higher floor is permissible via the `Override path` cell but the floor is never relaxed. The parser counts characters after stripping the `@ci-gate-override: {gate_id} — ` prefix; surrogate pairs count as a single character per Unicode-normalization-form-C; ASCII whitespace at the rationale's leading and trailing edges is trimmed before counting.
2. **Gate-ID match.** `{gate_id}` MUST exactly match a `Gate ID` value in the §M.5 catalog (case-sensitive, ASCII snake_case). A `{gate_id}` absent from the catalog is rejected with status `override_unknown_gate` (registered in Appendix I `Spec-Lint CI Gate Internal Failure Modes`). The parser loads the §M.5 catalog gate-ID set at boot from the post-edit Master Spec parse tree (the `Gate ID` column values across §M.5.4 / §M.5.5 / §M.5.10 / §M.5.12 / §M.5.13 / §M.5.14 / §M.5.NN catalog blocks); the set is computed deterministically per the §M.5.3 schema. Closest-match suggestions (Levenshtein < 5) are surfaced in the rejection comment to disambiguate typos.
3. **Row-level prohibition supersedes default.** If the §M.5 catalog row's `override_path` column declares `not_permitted` (or any `not_permitted_<rule>` form per §M.5.2), the override is rejected with status `ci_gate_override_not_permitted` regardless of grammar conformance. The status carries the `<rule>` token in the rejection comment for the author's resolution path. This rule is canonical and operates at the parser layer before any other validation; the row-level cell value is the authoritative source of truth. Row-level prohibition is checked after `{gate_id}` resolves to the catalog row but before §M.4.4.5 ¶1 / ¶4 / ¶5 checks (so an `override_unknown_gate` rejection precedes the `not_permitted` rejection in the precedence chain).
4. **Coupled-gate annotation requirement.** If the §M.5 catalog row's `override_path` column declares a `coupled_with:<other_gate_id>` constraint, the override annotation for the cited gate alone is sufficient; the coupled gate's enforcement runs at deploy-validator time via the coupled-gate runtime artifact (per the D-11V-004 remediation; e.g., `s3_replication_policy_residency_bound` is coupled with `s3_cross_region_replica_dpa_approval_required`). The cited `<other_gate_id>` MUST itself resolve to a §M.5 catalog row; an `override_path` cell that names a non-existent coupled gate is rejected at catalog-load time with status `override_coupled_gate_unknown` (registered in Appendix I `Spec-Lint CI Gate Internal Failure Modes`). This rule is checked at gate boot (when the catalog is loaded) AND at override-apply time (to defend against catalog hot-edit races); the boot-time check is the authoritative source-of-truth and runs as part of the `appendix_m5_self_consistency` meta-gate cluster per §M.5.4 Phase V11 cluster.
5. **Substantive-prerequisite annotation.** If the §M.5 catalog row's `override_path` column declares `requires_audit_event:<event_kind>`, the override is accepted only if the named AuditEvent has been emitted prior to the override application; verified by the runtime artifact at deploy-validator time. The override annotation alone is necessary but not sufficient. The cited `<event_kind>` MUST itself be a value in the Appendix J `audit_event_kind` enum; an `override_path` cell that names a non-existent event_kind is rejected at catalog-load time with status `override_requires_audit_event_kind_unknown` (registered in Appendix I `Spec-Lint CI Gate Internal Failure Modes`; same precedence chain as ¶4).

#### M.4.5 Audit trail {#m-4-5-audit-trail}

Every gate run — pass, fail, or override-applied — emits a structured audit record. The record is serialized as JSON conforming to schema `tools/spec-lint/gate_run_record.schema.json` and propagated to four destinations:

1. **Spec-repo run logs.** Persisted at `tools/spec-lint/run-logs/{gate_run_id}.json` (git-LFS; per-PR retention until PR is merged or closed + 90 days for closed-without-merge). Permits CI-pipeline retrospective audit.
2. **Convex `AuditEvent` table (§4.6.1).** Inserted with `action_class = ci_gate`, `actor_type = system_agent`, `system_agent_id = system_agent_spec_lint_pipeline`, `user_id = NULL`, `target_type = pull_request`, `target_id = pr_id`, `metadata` containing the full record. PII in the rationale text (rare; the substring requirement and qualifier set discourage PII inclusion) is swept by the §6.8.4.5 sweep registry on cascade per Pattern A; the record itself follows §40.2 AuditEvent retention (7 years).
3. **PostHog event** (`spec_lint.appendix_m_gate_run` — registered in Appendix G; per Appendix G PostHog Taxonomy). Properties include `gate_outcome`, `triggered_concept_count`, `override_count`, `override_target_customer_visible_count`, `parse_error_count`, `pr_id`, `commit_sha`. Permits product-team observability on override-rejection rates and gate-trigger frequency.
4. **Datadog log** (service tag `spec-lint`; log level `info` for pass, `warn` for override_applied, `error` for fail_*). Permits SRE alerting on gate failure spikes per §42.6 ops observability.

##### M.4.5.1 Record schema {#m-4-5-1-record-schema}

```json
{
  "gate_run_id": "uuid",
  "pr_id": 12345,
  "pr_repository": "sourcera/sourcera-spec",
  "commit_sha": "git-sha-40",
  "merge_base_sha": "git-sha-40",
  "gate_outcome": "pass | fail_missing_row | override_applied | fail_invalid_override | override_target_not_flagged_by_detector | override_target_customer_visible | orphan_inline_gate_reference | parse_error | comment_post_failed | comment_post_bypass_applied",
  "triggered_concepts": [
    {
      "concept_class": "entity | entity_field | aioperation | capability_non_ai | enum_value | state_machine_state | plan_tier_feature | webhook_event | notification_event | posthog_event | api_endpoint | named_ci_gate",
      "concept_name": "string",
      "spec_anchor": "string",
      "spec_line_number": "integer",
      "coverage_resolved_by": "m1_row | override_internal_only | unresolved",
      "covering_row_anchor": "string?"
    }
  ],
  "override_annotations": [
    {
      "concept_name": "string",
      "rationale": "string",
      "qualifiers": ["not_in_pricing_api | not_in_seller_serializer | ..."],
      "cross_validation_outcome": "pass | rejected_detector_flag | rejected_predicate_1_console_enum | rejected_predicate_2_rbac | rejected_predicate_3_plan_tier | rejected_predicate_4_surface_class",
      "cross_validation_detector_flag_outcome": "pass | not_flagged_by_detector | near_match_only",
      "cross_validation_failed_predicate_sub_check": "string?",
      "cross_validation_evidence_anchor": "string?",
      "cross_validation_evidence_line_number": "integer?"
    }
  ],
  "auto_generated_rows": [
    {
      "concept_name": "string",
      "m1_row_anchor": "string",
      "area_group_banner": "string"
    }
  ],
  "actor": "github_user_login",
  "ran_at_utc": "iso-8601",
  "detector_version": "semver"
}
```

The `gate_outcome` enum is registered in Appendix J as `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff_outcome` (per Phase V11 remediation; was the unregistered `gate_outcome` enum filed in D-11.2-006; v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 added the `override_target_not_flagged_by_detector` value). The `concept_class` enum is registered in Appendix J as `appendix_m_concept_class`. The `cross_validation_outcome` enum is registered in Appendix J as `appendix_m_cross_validation_outcome` (v7.2.0-REM Phase 2 expanded from 5 values to 6: added `rejected_detector_flag`; renamed `rejected_predicate_N` → `rejected_predicate_N_<axis>` to encode the canonical axis per §M.4.4.2 predicate set). The `cross_validation_detector_flag_outcome` enum is registered in Appendix J as `appendix_m_detector_flag_outcome` (v7.2.0-REM Phase 2; 3 values: `pass`, `not_flagged_by_detector`, `near_match_only`).

##### M.4.5.2 Retention and DSAR cascade {#m-4-5-2-retention-and-dsar}

- **Convex AuditEvent retention:** 7 years per §40.2 AuditEvent row (no retention-singleton drift introduced).
- **Spec-repo run-logs retention:** PR-lifetime + 90 days after close per `tools/spec-lint/retention.json`. Not §40.2-bound because the spec repo is not a Convex deployment; this is an explicit divergence point documented inline and registered as a new §40.2 row (`SpecLintRunLog | spec_repo_git_lfs | pr_lifetime + 90 days after close | per V11 remediation`).
- **DSAR cascade behavior:** the `actor` field (GitHub username) is User-attribution but does NOT map to a §4.2.3 User row (GitHub users are not Sourcera Users); the field is exempt from DSAR cascade per §6.8.4.3 Cascade Class Coverage Registry row (added in V11 remediation: `Class = exempt`, `Pattern = github_attribution_exempt`, `rationale = GitHub Login is not a Sourcera-attributable User; cascade is governed by GitHub's own data-deletion contract`).
- **PII redaction in rationale text:** the `rationale` field is swept by the §6.8.4.5 free-text-PII sweep at AuditEvent ingest using the §48.4.4 PII detector; detected spans are replaced with `[REDACTED_PII]` sentinels and `redaction_verification_hash` is recomputed per §4.7.1.1 (cross-console-bridge convention re-used for catalog audit hygiene).
- **Data-residency behavior:** the AuditEvent is written to the residency partition of the Sourcera-internal `meta_org` (§50.2 Ops separation architecture); spec-repo run-logs and digests are non-residency-bound platform artifacts.

##### M.4.5.3 Idempotency on re-run {#m-4-5-3-idempotency}

Re-runs of the gate on the same `commit_sha` are idempotent: the record is updated in place keyed on `(pr_id, commit_sha)`. Re-runs on a different commit_sha (post-push or post-rebase) emit a new record; the prior record is retained for audit. The auto-row-generator is idempotent against existing `(Engine concept, Spec home)` tuples per §M.4.4.4 concurrent-PR rule.

#### M.4.6 Nightly digest {#m-4-6-nightly-digest}

A nightly aggregator job (Convex cron `appendix_m_gate_nightly_digest` at 09:00 UTC daily; runtime in `convex/crons/appendix_m_gate_nightly_digest.ts`) aggregates the prior 24h of `override_applied` and `override_target_customer_visible` runs and posts a digest for human review.

##### M.4.6.1 Digest destinations {#m-4-6-1-digest-destinations}

Primary: Sourcera Slack workspace, channel `#spec-ops`. Channel ID configured via Convex env var `SLACK_SPEC_OPS_CHANNEL_ID` (default: `C0SPECOPS01` for the production Sourcera Slack workspace; the placeholder is replaced at deploy time via the existing Slack integration per §43.4.2). Bot identity: `@sourcera-spec-bot` (the same GitHub App identity used for inline PR comments).

Fallback: if the Slack post fails (rate-limit, 5xx, or channel-deletion), the digest is queued to Loops.so via the existing `@spec-ops-digest` distribution list (Loops.so List ID: `lo_spec_ops_digest`). The Loops.so fallback is documented in `convex/crons/appendix_m_gate_nightly_digest.ts` and runs on the same cron tick.

Secondary archive: all digests are persisted to a Convex `SpecLintDigest` table (org-scoped to the Sourcera-internal `meta_org` per §50.2 Ops separation architecture) for retrospective audit. Retention: 2 years per §40.2 (added in V11 remediation as a new row in §40.2 retention table).

##### M.4.6.2 Reviewer rotation {#m-4-6-2-reviewer-rotation}

Reviewer rotation is owned by the spec-ops oncall rotation in PagerDuty schedule `spec-ops-oncall-rotation` (rotation cadence: weekly; primary + secondary). The Convex cron tags the primary oncall in the Slack post; SLA is 2 business days to triage every `override_applied` and `override_target_customer_visible` entry. Missed-SLA escalation fires a SEV-3 PagerDuty page to the spec-ops secondary oncall.

##### M.4.6.3 Failed-job alarming {#m-4-6-3-failed-job-alarming}

If the nightly cron itself fails (Convex execution error, Slack 5xx + Loops 5xx, Datadog alert pipeline degraded), a Datadog monitor `monitor:appendix_m_gate_nightly_digest_failed` fires a SEV-2 alert to `spec-ops-oncall-rotation` within 15 minutes of cron-tick failure.

##### M.4.6.4 Digest template {#m-4-6-4-digest-template}

Slack post template:

> **Appendix M gate — nightly override digest ({date})**
>
> Period: {start_utc} → {end_utc}
>
> Override applied: {applied_count} runs
> Override rejected (customer-visible): {rejected_count} runs
> Parse errors: {parse_error_count} runs
>
> **Top override targets by rationale qualifier:**
> {qualifier_breakdown_table}
>
> **Override targets requiring review:**
> {target_review_table}
>
> Primary oncall: @{primary_login}. SLA: 2 business days.
>
> Full digest: {convex_digest_url}

### M.5 CI Gate Catalog {#appendix-m-ci-gate-catalog}

§M.5 is the canonical registry of every CI gate authored as a forward-reference during the v7.1.0 Surface-Abstraction & Dual-Maya Integration program (Phases 14.1 through 14.10 plus 14.17), the audit-remediation passes (Phase 2V / 3V / 3V+ / V8.4 / V9), and the Phase V11 catalog-completeness remediation (closed 2026-05-11). Each gate carries a structured contract — `Gate ID`, `Source phase`, `Row class`, `Runtime status`, `Scope`, `Execution context + Assertion`, `Failure mode + Override path`, `Runbook`, `Authority anchor` — at §M.4 fidelity.

#### M.5.1 Authoring contract {#m-5-1-authoring-contract}

Each gate row below is an **engine-side contract** the spec asserts. The runtime wiring (lint detector, deploy-time validator, schema-validation test, Playwright fixture, Datadog monitor, synthetic chaos test) is owned by the implementation pack referenced in the row's `Runtime status` cell. A gate is `runtime_active` when (a) the runtime artifact exists in the CI / production pipeline; (b) the gate has run on the most recent main-branch commit (for spec-tree gates) or the most recent deploy (for runtime gates) or the most recent scheduled run (for synthetic monitors); and (c) the run record has been ingested by the §42 observability stack. Until that point, the gate is `spec_binding_pending_pack_<id>` and enforced through code-review and authoring discipline per §M.3 and §M.4.7.

##### M.5.1.1 Runtime-wiring acceptance criteria {#m-5-1-1-runtime-wiring-acceptance-criteria}

Every §M.5 row whose `Runtime status` is `spec_binding_pending_pack_<id>` inherits the acceptance criteria below unless a stricter row-local authoring contract supersedes it:

1. **Pack artifact.** The owning pack named by `<id>` MUST land a concrete runtime artifact in the matching path family: M02.3 spec-tree lint in `.github/workflows/spec-lint.yml` / `tools/spec-lint/`; M11.3 runtime, deploy-validator, or UI tests in `.github/workflows/test-strategy.yml`, `convex/deploy_validators/`, or `tests/integration/`; M21.3 marketplace / abuse / analytics validators in the marketplace runtime test or deploy-validator pack; M24.3 Stripe, metering, committed-spend, or reconciliation validators in the billing runtime test pack; release-orchestration gates in `tools/release/stamp_gate.ts`.
2. **Positive fixture.** The pack MUST include at least one positive fixture, live-run assertion, or golden-spec example that exercises the row's `Assertion` and produces the expected ACCEPT / PASS outcome.
3. **Negative fixture.** The pack MUST include at least one negative fixture, fault injection, or counterfactual spec example that violates the row's `Assertion` and fails closed with the row's named failure mode, Appendix I error code when applicable, PR comment, alert, or release-stamp rejection.
4. **Observability evidence.** The first successful run MUST emit the §M.4.5 audit event and §42 observability record for the gate run. Runbook links MUST resolve unless the row explicitly declares `n/a (spec-tree-lint; no runtime paging path)`.
5. **Same-change promotion.** A row may transition from `spec_binding_pending_pack_<id>` to `runtime_active` only in the same PR, release record, or stamp record that lands the runtime artifact, the positive fixture, the negative fixture, and the observability evidence. `v7_1_1_stamp_gate_runtime_status_audit` rejects any promotion missing one of those four evidence classes.
6. **Pending-window discipline.** Until the criteria above are satisfied, the row remains `spec_binding_pending_pack_<id>` and may be enforced only through code review and authoring discipline; no release checklist may count it as `runtime_active`.

#### M.5.2 Severity and override discipline {#m-5-2-severity-and-override}

Every gate is a hard PR block (for spec-tree / lint gates) or a hard deploy block (for runtime gates) unless the row's `Override path` cell declares otherwise. The override grammar is canonical per §M.4.4.5:

- `appendix_m_coverage_on_diff` overrides use `@appendix-m-internal-only: {concept_name} — {rationale}` per §M.4.4.1.
- All other gates use `@ci-gate-override: {gate_id} — {rationale}` per §M.4.4.5.
- Rationale ≥ 60 characters; Gate ID literal match; row-level `not_permitted` supersedes default.

Override classes available per row (enumerated in the `Override path` cell):

- `default_ci_gate_override` — standard §M.4.4.5 grammar; rationale ≥ 60 chars; flagged in nightly digest.
- `not_permitted_<rule>` — override is rejected at parser layer; the `<rule>` token names the binding contract (e.g., `not_permitted_gdpr_art_17`, `not_permitted_console_firewall`, `not_permitted_residency_lock`, `not_permitted_hero_moment_integrity`, `not_permitted_solo_surface_integrity`, `not_permitted_billing_singleton`).
- `coupled_with:<other_gate_id>` — override of this gate alone is sufficient; the coupled gate's enforcement runs separately.
- `requires_audit_event:<event_kind>` — override is accepted only if the named AuditEvent is on record prior to override application; verified at deploy-validator time.
- `requires_phase_12_3_contrast_qualifier` — Appendix-K-glossary-canonicality-specific override class admitting deliberate Phase-12.3 contrast paragraphs.

#### M.5.3 Schema {#m-5-3-schema}

Per Phase V11 remediation, each catalog row carries the following columns:

| Column | Definition | Cardinality |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `Gate ID` | ASCII snake_case identifier; unique across catalog. Must not contain Unicode characters (`§` rename per D-11.3-009). | 1 per row |
| `Source phase` | Authoring phase / audit remediation phase / V11 phase. | 1 per row |
| `Row class` | Enum: `per_feature_gate`, `cross_feature_invariant`, `spec_tree_lint`, `runtime_property_test`, `synthetic_monitor`, `deploy_validator`, `chaos_synthetic`, `release_stamp_gate`, `meta_catalog_invariant`. Registered in Appendix J as `ci_gate_row_class`. | 1 per row |
| `Runtime status` | Enum: `runtime_active`, `spec_binding_pending_pack_<id>`, `spec_binding_release_gate_only`. Registered in Appendix J as `ci_gate_runtime_status`. | 1 per row |
| `Scope` | The spec section, file, or runtime artifact under enforcement. | 1 per row |
| `Execution context` | Enum: `pr_lint`, `deploy_validator`, `runtime_test`, `synthetic_monitor`, `quarterly_chaos`, `release_stamp`, `nightly_cron`. Registered in Appendix J as `ci_gate_execution_context`. | 1 per row |
| `Assertion` | The invariant the gate enforces (as a falsifiable claim). | 1 per row |
| `Failure mode` | The observable failure (test/lint/build/synthetic), error code if applicable, and severity escalation. | 1 per row |
| `Override path` | One of the override classes from §M.5.2. | 1 per row |
| `Runbook` | URL or anchor to the on-call runbook page (operations repo convention: `runbooks.sourcera.com/ci-gates/<gate_id>`). For spec-tree-lint gates with no on-call dimension, value is `n/a (spec-tree-lint; no runtime paging path)`. | 1 per row |
| `Authority anchor` | Spec section and defect / AE row that the gate enforces or remediates. | 1 per row |

The full multi-column row representation appears in §M.5.5 (per-gate detail records). The §M.5.4 catalog index table below is the **7-column overview** at v7.2.0-REM Phase 3 fidelity for backward-compatibility with existing cross-references; the index lists `Gate ID | Source phase | Runtime status | Scope | Trigger | Failure mode | Authority anchor`. The `Runtime status` column landed at v7.2.0-REM Phase 3 closure (2026-05-18, this remediation pass) per D-11.3-001 P0; the remaining AE-V11-03 column extensions (`Row class`, `Execution context` / `Assertion` split, `Runbook`, `Override path`) remain staged for successive remediation phases per `_audit/REMEDIATION_BACKLOG.md` v7.1.1 stamp-gate inheritance set, with per-cluster `Override path` cells already authored in-line in the existing `Failure mode` cell (per the §M.5.2 row-level override-class set). Phase V11 amendments mark rows that received Phase V11 hardening with a trailing `[V11]` tag in the `Source phase` cell. The `Runtime status` column is the canonical per-row carrier for the §M.5.5 per-row runtime-status assignment table — when the two diverge, §M.5.4 per-row cells are authoritative (§M.5.5 is the default-by-phase-cluster mapping that informs per-row defaults but does not override an explicit per-row declaration).

For every closed Appendix-J enum (rows under §J that declare a finite, comma-separated value set without an open-extension annotation), every inline Master Spec body reference of shape `<enum_name>\s*=\s*` `` ` `` `<value>` `` ` `` or `<enum_name>\s*∈\s*\{[^}]*\}` MUST resolve `<value>` (resp. every value inside the set-literal) to an exact match in the enum's registered value set. Inline references to non-registered values (sentinels like `not_applicable`, `n/a`, `none`, `unset`, `pending`, or any ad-hoc value not in the registered set) fail. Exemption set: (a) Appendix J authoring sections themselves where the enum is defined; (b) §M.4 / §M.5 grammar placeholders (`<gate_id>`, `<rule>`, `<id>` and similar); (c) the literal `null` where the field-table schema declares Nullable; (d) Glossary entries that explicitly cite the retired-sentinel-history for D-2.2-042 v7.1.0 pre-remediation wording (allow-listed by the §M.4.2.1 anchor-alias-redirect table). Detector regex set (case-sensitive on enum_name; case-insensitive on the natural-language pattern): (i) ``/`([a-z_]+)`\s*=\s*`([a-z0-9_]+)`/g`` resolved against Appendix-J registered-value set per `<enum_name>`; (ii) ``/`([a-z_]+)`\s*∈\s*\{[^}]+\}/g`` resolved against same; (iii) ``/sentinel\s+`([a-z_]+)\s*=\s*([a-z0-9_]+)`/gi`` matches the D-2.2-042 anti-pattern explicitly. Closes D-2.2-042 P0 firewall_leakage; closes D-V72REM-PH1-001 P0 sibling (HeatMapAggregationCard). | `not_permitted_closed_enum_integrity` — enum-bound erosion is a P0-class firewall invariant; admitting a sentinel against any closed Appendix-J enum opens the same gateway exploited by D-2.2-042. Override is rejected at parser layer regardless of grammar conformance. The §M.4.4.5 row-level `not_permitted` rule applies. | `runbooks.sourcera.com/ci-gates/enum_bound_no_inline_sentinel_admission` | M02.3 |

The §4.4.16 HeatMapCell data-model table is the canonical field-allowlist for the entity per the *Vendor-Identity-Free Aggregate Invariant*. The detector parses the §4.4.16 field table on every PR; if a new row introduces (a) any FK column resolving to a Seller-side entity (`seller_org_id`, `seller_software_id`, `seller_user_id`, `seller_profile_id`), (b) any `vendor_opt_out_*` column, (c) any column whose Notes cell references the Opt-Out Registry, (d) any column whose Constraints cell references the §4.4.8 closed enum, OR (e) any column whose name matches the regex `/^(seller_|vendor_|sw_|product_|software_id|owner_user_)/`, the PR fails with `heat_map_cell_vendor_identity_field_forbidden_drift` and is blocked. The detector also asserts the converse: removal of any field currently in the allowlist (`id`, `category_id`, `region_code`, `industry_code`, `company_size_band`, `period_start`, `period_end`, `signal_count`, `k_anon_floor`, `k_anon_satisfied`, `demand_index`, `demand_trend`, `prior_period_signal_count`, `contributing_source_hash`, `last_refreshed_at`, `refresh_cadence_days`, `next_scheduled_refresh_at`, `publication_status`, `residency_region_scope`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`) requires an Authored-Extension annotation in the PR description. Closes the §4.4.16 D-2.2-042 remediation AC #4 binding. **Authoring contract for v7.2.0-REM Phase 1.** The two gates above MUST be wired into the implementation pack M02.3 spec-lint workflow (`.github/workflows/spec-lint.yml`) before v7.1.0a hot-patch stamps. Detector sources live at `tools/spec-lint/enum_bound_sentinel.ts` and `tools/spec-lint/heat_map_cell_field_allowlist.ts` respectively. The wiring landing is registered as AE-V72REM-01 dependency (v7.1.0a stamp) per `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md → v7.2.0-REM Program`. The §M.5.5 per-row runtime-status assignment for both gates is `spec_binding_pending_pack_m02_3` at the v7.2.0-REM Phase 1 closure point; the v7.1.0a stamp gate audit (`v7_1_1_stamp_gate_runtime_status_audit` extended to a v7.1.0a-hot-patch sibling per AE-V72REM-07) re-evaluates both gates for promotion to `runtime_active` at hot-patch stamp time.

**Closed-enum registry binding.** The detector at `tools/spec-lint/enum_bound_sentinel.ts` parses Appendix J for closed-enum rows at boot. The detector's enum-registry-load path consumes the §J.\*.\* sub-headings as enum names and the comma-separated value lists in the section body as registered values. Any enum row containing an explicit `extensible: true` annotation (currently: `console_bridge_event_kind` per the §4.7.1 extension-governance contract; `appendix_m_concept_class` per the §M.4.2 governance) is excluded from the closed-set assertion. The closed-enum registry is the union of all non-extensible enums; at v7.2.0-REM Phase 1 closure that includes `vendor_opt_out_scope_kind` (5 values), `vendor_opt_out_scope_ref_type` (9 values), `vendor_opt_out_page_type_filter` (8 values), `vendor_opt_out_reason_code` (6 values), `vendor_opt_out_ops_review_status` (5 values), `vendor_opt_out_retro_backfill_status` (5 values), and the broader Appendix-J non-extensible set.

**Counterfactual coverage (verification against the D-2.2-042 attack surface).** The `enum_bound_no_inline_sentinel_admission` gate's detector MUST fail on each of the following adversarial inputs:
1. **The retired v7.1.0 sentinel.** A PR re-introducing the literal string ``sentinel `scope_kind=not_applicable` record in the registry`` anywhere in the Master Spec body — pattern (iii) matches and merge is blocked.
2. **An ad-hoc sentinel against a sibling enum.** A PR adding `` `scope_ref_type=heat_map_cell_aggregate` `` to §4.4.8 prose, where `heat_map_cell_aggregate` is not in the §4.4.8 `vendor_opt_out_scope_ref_type` registered value set — pattern (i) matches and merge is blocked.
3. **A set-literal admission against a closed enum.** A PR adding `` `reason_code ∈ {legal, competitive, accuracy_dispute, ops_override}` `` where `ops_override` is not in the registered set — pattern (ii) matches and merge is blocked.
4. **A bypass attempt via the override annotation.** A PR carrying `@ci-gate-override: enum_bound_no_inline_sentinel_admission — rationale ≥ 60 chars` — rejected at parser layer per the row-level `not_permitted_closed_enum_integrity` override class.

**Detector residency and audit trail.** Detector runs emit an entry to the §M.4.5.1 AuditEvent table with `action_class = ci_gate`, `actor_type = system_agent`, `system_agent_id = system_agent_spec_lint_pipeline`, `target_type = pull_request`. Nightly digest (§M.4.6) aggregates the prior-24-hour run count and any failure-mode breakdown into Slack `#spec-ops` per the §M.4.6.1 destinations. PII in offending strings is rare (gate scope is enum-value strings, not free text); when present (e.g., a sentinel literal inadvertently containing a contributor email), the §6.8.4.5 sweep registry handles cascade redaction per §M.4.5.2.
