**Counterfactual coverage (verification against the D-EM-001 attack surface).** The `entitlement_matrix_registry_binding_completeness` gate MUST fail on each of the following adversarial inputs:

1. **The retired v7.1.0 condition.** A PR that lands the v7.1.0 Master Spec snapshot (with `qa_suggestion_seller` in §34.8.5 but no `qa_suggestion_buyer` registry row, AND with the canonical-form lock note referencing `qa_suggestion_buyer` as if registered) — the reverse-pass detector identifies `qa_suggestion_buyer` (referenced in the canonical-form lock note matched by the gate's secondary lock-note scanner — see §M.5.14 supplementary detector contract) but absent from §21.4, and fails with `entitlement_matrix_unbound_capability_id`.
2. **A future §34.8.5 PR adds a capability_id not in §21.4.** A PR adding a new row to the seller proactive block (e.g., `seller_revops_recommender`) without authoring the corresponding §21.4.1 or §21.4.2 `CapabilityRegistryEntry` row — the reverse-pass detector identifies the orphan and fails with `entitlement_matrix_unbound_capability_id`. The PR author is directed to author the registry row in the same PR per the §34.8.5 maintenance rule.
3. **A new §21.4 customer-billed capability ships without a §34.8.5 row.** A PR adding `kb_summary_synthesis` as a new `customer_billed` row in §21.4.2 Extended Capabilities, but failing to add a §34.8.5 matrix row — the forward-pass detector identifies the orphan and fails with `capability_registry_active_capability_missing_matrix_row`. The PR author is directed to add the matrix row in the same PR per the §34.8.5 maintenance rule.
4. **A bypass attempt via the override annotation.** A PR carrying `@ci-gate-override: entitlement_matrix_registry_binding_completeness — rationale ≥ 60 chars` — rejected at parser layer per the row-level `not_permitted_entitlement_registry_binding_integrity` override class.
5. **An exemption-class abuse.** A PR claiming a customer-billed AI capability falls under exemption class (a) (platform-internal aggregation) by appending `_aggregation` to its `capability_id` (e.g., `qa_suggestion_buyer_aggregation`) — the exemption classifier additionally asserts `enforcement_mode = n/a (sourcera_owned)` per §34.8.5 line 29755 inline fix F-3.1.A; a row with `enforcement_mode = hard` cannot satisfy the exemption predicate and falls through to standard binding enforcement.

**Detector residency and audit trail.** Detector and validator runs emit an entry to the §M.4.5.1 AuditEvent table with `action_class = ci_gate`, `actor_type = system_agent`, `system_agent_id = system_agent_spec_lint_pipeline` (for PR-lint) OR `system_agent_id = system_agent_deploy_validator` (for deploy-time half), `target_type = pull_request` OR `target_type = deployment`. Nightly digest (§M.4.6) aggregates the prior-24-hour run count and any failure-mode breakdown into Slack `#spec-ops` per the §M.4.6.1 destinations. PII risk: nil (gate scope is `capability_id` strings, which are platform-scoped identifiers with no subject PII).

**Supplementary detector contract.** The `entitlement_matrix_registry_binding_completeness` detector also performs a **secondary lock-note scan**: it parses the §34.8.5 canonical-form lock note paragraph (anchored at the "Canonical-form lock" `**` bold marker) for any backtick-quoted `capability_id` string referenced as if registered (regex: `` /`([a-z_]+_(?:buyer|seller))`\s+(?:as|under|per|with|in)/g ``) and confirms each match resolves to a §21.4 row OR to one of the registered exemption classes. This sub-detector catches the D-EM-001 P0 attack pattern explicitly: the v7.1.0 canonical-form lock note cited `qa_suggestion_buyer` as if registered but had no §21.4 row; the secondary scan would have failed-closed on that condition.

**Sibling-of-sibling-of-family-root coverage.** Beyond the `qa_suggestion_family` split, the `entitlement_matrix_registry_binding_completeness` gate covers the analogous `org_intelligence_family` (tri-split: `org_intelligence_vendor_history` / `org_intelligence_full` / `org_intelligence_suggestions`) and `kb_suggestion_family` (dual-split: `kb_suggestion_buyer` / `kb_suggestion_seller`) family-rooted patterns. Sibling cardinality assertions for those families are registered as separate gates (`org_intelligence_family_cardinality`, `kb_suggestion_family_cardinality`) under the v7.1.0a stamp-gate audit; both are listed at `spec_binding_pending_pack_m11_3` pending their own runtime wiring per the §M.5.5 per-row runtime-status assignment table. The `not_permitted_capability_family_integrity` override class applies uniformly across all three sibling-cardinality gates.

**Authoring contract for v7.2.0-REM Phase 6 (§M.5.18 closure).** The five gates above MUST be wired into implementation pack M02.3 (spec-tree-lint cluster, `.github/workflows/spec-lint.yml`) before the v7.1.1 stamp. Detector sources: `tools/spec-lint/appendix_c_webhook_catalog_completeness.ts`, `tools/spec-lint/appendix_c_to_appendix_g_coverage.ts`, `tools/spec-lint/appendix_c_to_appendix_f_retry_class_coverage.ts`, `tools/spec-lint/webhook_default_retry_class.ts`, `tools/spec-lint/appendix_j_enum_completeness.ts`. Each emits a §M.4.5.1 AuditEvent (`action_class = ci_gate`) and aggregates to the §M.4.6 nightly digest. The §M.5.5 per-row runtime-status table is extended by 5 rows (all `spec_binding_pending_pack_m02_3`). Wiring landing registered as AE-V72REM-PH6-02 dependency per `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md → v7.2.0-REM Program`.

**Counterfactual coverage (verification against the catalog-completeness attack surface).**

1. **A future PR adds a webhook event (e.g., a new `marketplace.*` event named in §27 body) without the Appendix C row.** `appendix_c_webhook_catalog_completeness` parses the body for the new back-ticked event token, finds no matching Appendix C table row, and **fails closed** at PR-lint with a comment naming the unregistered event. The same PR would also trip `appendix_c_to_appendix_g_coverage` and `webhook_default_retry_class` once the Appendix C row is added without a G mirror / retry-class binding — the three gates compose to force a complete C+G+F registration. Detection class: §M.5.18 `appendix_c_webhook_catalog_completeness`. Override: `not_permitted_catalog_completeness`.
2. **A future PR adds an Appendix J enum value without a consumer in §1–§51.** `appendix_j_enum_completeness` direction (b) scans §1–§51 for at least one consumer of the new value, finds none, and **fails closed** at PR-lint with a comment naming the orphan value. Conversely, a body reference `See Appendix J <name>` with no registry entry fails direction (a). Detection class: §M.5.18 `appendix_j_enum_completeness`. Override: `not_permitted_catalog_completeness`.
3. **A future PR introduces a third webhook retry class inline (e.g., a `console_bridge_standard`-style curve) without authoring §F.x + an Appendix J `webhook_retry_class` value.** `webhook_default_retry_class` resolves the Appendix C `Retry Curve` cell against the `webhook_retry_class` enum, finds an unregistered class, and **fails closed**. This is the regression guard for the D-6.1-012 closure. Detection class: §M.5.18 `webhook_default_retry_class`. Override: `not_permitted_retry_class_binding`.

**Detector residency and audit trail.** Same pattern as §M.5.14–§M.5.17 (AuditEvent emission with `action_class = ci_gate` per §M.4.5.1; nightly digest to Slack `#spec-ops` via the `appendix_m_gate_nightly_digest` Convex cron per §M.4.6 with Loops.so `lo_spec_ops_digest` fallback; Datadog service `spec-lint`; PostHog `spec_lint.appendix_catalog_completeness.gate_run`; nil PII — the detectors read only the Master Spec parse tree).
